records.text: Accused: Pre-Arrest Bail - S. 498 CrPc - Offence u/s 489(f) Punishment is up to 3 years, offence not falling within the prohibitory clause, bail confirmed. 2026 MLD 88 Lah (Justice Amber Gul)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed in a section 406 PPC case
records.text: Accused: Pre-Arrest Bail - Offence u/s 406 PPC Bail Confirmed. 2026 MLD Lah 187 (Justice Tanvir Ahmad Sheikh)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed in a cross-version case
records.text: Accused: Pre-Arrest Bail - S. 498 CrPc - Offence u/s 324, 337 (f)(6) Cross version case, Pre- Arrest Confirmed. 2026 SCMR 442 titled Manaan Ali etc. Vs The State.
records.title: Manaan Ali etc. Vs The State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Merits can be examined at the pre-arrest bail stage; co-accused found innocent
records.text:
Accused: Pre-Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 2021 SCMR 130 Titled Khair Muhammad Etc. Vs The State
a. During investigation co-accussed was found innocent, matter of further inquiry.
b. Merits of the case can be discussed at the stage of pre-arrest bail as well. Bail Confirmed. Reliance: PLD 2021 SC 708 -where further details are;
1. Merits of the case can be discussed even at the stage of Pre-Arrest Bail. (2022 SCMR 1427)
2. It is difficult to prove mala fide of the complainant, in each and every case. It can be inferred from the record.
3. If a case of post-arrest bail is made out, then there is no harm to confirm a pre-arrest bail petition.
records.title: Khair Muhammad Etc. Vs The State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed
records.text: Accused: Pre-Arrest Bail 2024 YLR 359 titled Raza Muhammad Vs The State. Bail confirm
records.title: Raza Muhammad Vs The State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Non-cognizable offence: no investigation without the Magistrate's permission
records.text: Accused: Pre-Arrest Bail - Offence u/a 155(c) Police order 2002 Zeeshan Thaheem SI, Jani Gill SHO (unreported) Offence is non-cognizable, hence investigation cannot be conducted without permission of magistrate u/s 155 CrPc. Bail confirmed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail may be filed directly in the High Court where the accused fears for his life in the Sessions Court
records.text: Accused: Pre- Arrest Bail 2019 YLR 183, 2019 PCRLJ 436 LAH, PLD 2004 SC 1, PLD 97 SC 582, 2022 SCMR 676, 2022 MLD 1845 Balochistan Pre Arrest bail can be directly filed in High Court, where accused feels apprehension of murder in session court.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail refused: cheque of a huge amount
records.text: Complainant: Pre-Arrest Bail offence u/s 489(f) PPC PLJ 2018 CrC Lah 304, 2016 SCMR 2064, 2013 SCMR 1669, 2011 SCMR 170, PLD 2009 SC 427 Cheque of huge amount, accused is not entitled for the extra-ordinary relief of Pre-Arrest Bail. Dismissed. Reliance: 2016 SCMR 2064, 2013 SCMR 1669, 2011 SCMR 170, PLD 2009 SC 427

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Hurt case: pre-arrest bail confirmed where the injured did not appear before the medical board
records.text: Accussed: Pre-Arrest offence of hurt case 2010 MLD 950 LAH, 2012 SCMR 646 Injured did not appear before the medical board, Pre- Arrest bail confirmed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Hurt case: pre-arrest bail refused where the accused is named with a specific role
records.text: Complainant: Pre-Arrest offence of hurt case 2022 SCMR 273 Accused nominated in FIR, specific role of causing injury. Bail Dismissed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail has a narrow scope and is not a matter of right
records.text: Complainant: Pre-Arrest offence of hurt case 2022 MLD 104 ISB; Reliance: 2021 MLD 1226, 2019 SCMR 1129, 2021 SCMR 449 Bail should not be granted in every case, as a run of mill. It cannot be claimed as a right. Pre-Arrest bail has a narrow scope. BAIL DISMISSED.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Plea of alibi can be considered at the pre-arrest bail stage
records.text: Accussed: Pre-Arrest offence u/s 302 PPC 1978 SCMR 242 Ground of plea of alibi can be considered at the stage of pre-arrest bail as well, if there are reasonable grounds pre-arrest bail can be confirmed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Counter-version cases: bail is the rule, refusal the exception
records.text: Accussed: 2024 SCMR 1605 / PLJ 2024 SC CrC 267 In case of counter-version, bail would be granted as a rule; refusal is an exception.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where the cheque was issued as a guarantee
records.text: Accused: Pre-Arrest offence u/s 489(f) 2024 SCMR 1567 - Cheque was issued as a guarantee; pre-arrest bail was confirmed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is limited to cases of mala fide implication
records.text: Accused: Pre-Arrest offence u/s 498 CrPc 2026 MLD 309 - Pre-arrest bail has limited scope only in cases where the court comes to the conclusion that the accused has been implicated on the basis of mala fide, and the accused has to prove that he is not a habitual offender or proclaimed offender, and he has approached the court of session first.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Bail cannot be withheld merely because the accused was a proclaimed offender
records.text: Post Arrest Bail of Proclaimed Offender: Offence u/s 87, 88 CRPC Mere on the basis of proclaimed offender, bail cannot be withheld, Bail Allowed. 2025 SCMR 318 (h)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Narcotics: each accused liable only for the quantity recovered from him
records.text: Post Arrest Bail: 3.2 kgs Ice recovered from 3 accused, accused would not be vicariously liable, he would be responsible only to the extent of recovered substance. Bail Allowed. 2026 SCMR 115

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Statutory ground: bail after one year in custody without conclusion of trial
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail on Statutory Ground- 497 CrPc- 2026 PCRLJ 7 Lah (Justice Amjad Rafiq) Offences u/s 394, 411- Accused is behind the bar, for the last 1 year, trial not concluded, bail allowed. Reliance, PLD 2024 SC 73, PLD 2024 Lah 12

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Section 324 PPC: aerial firing, co-accused declared innocent, rule of consistency
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 324 PPC: Allowed 2026 MLD 521 GB titled Hasnain Ahmad Vs The State Co-Accussed were declared innocent, aerial firing, offence u/s 324 PPC is not attracted, rule of consistency. Allowed. Reliance: 2021 YLR Note 150 pg 147, 2020 MLD 1187, 2018 MLD 724, 2019 MLD 724, 2022 YLR 2082.
records.title: Hasnain Ahmad Vs The State Co

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed in a PECA 2016 case
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence under PECA 2016, s. 3,4, 13, 14, 16 & 420, 468, 471, 109 PPC. Bail Allowed. 2026 MLD 542 Lah

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed in a PECA 2016 case
records.text: Accussed: Post Arrest Bail offence under PECA 2016, s.3, 4, 21 2022 SCMR 592/ 1467 Bail Allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Bail allowed: offence outside the prohibitory clause, nine-month unexplained delay in FIR, no recovery
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest bail offence u/s 2023 SCMR 734, 679 Offence not falling under prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, 9 month delay in lodging of FIR, without explanation. Nothing was recovered during physical remand. bail allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Bail refused although the offence fell outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: Complainant: Post Arrest 2022 SCMR 526/1477, 1511 Offence not falling within the prohibitory clause, even then post-arrest bail dismissed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Two versions: police opinion that the accused did not fire
records.text:
Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302, 324, 436, 452, 109 PPC 2026 MLD 97 Lah (Justice Jawad Zafar) Police Opinion - According to FIR, there was an allegation of firearm injury, but according to police the accused did not make a fire, case of two version, Allowed.
Reliance: 2012 SCMR 1137, 2019 SCMR 1458, PLD 2024 SC 1241, 2022 SCMR 663.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Hurt to the mouth: whether section 337-U or 334 PPC applies is for the trial court
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 337 (u), 337 (a) or 334 PPC. 2026 MLD 108 Lah (Justice Chaudhary Shehram Sarwar) Allegation of pistol’s butt blow, on the mouth of injured. His lips were ruptured, teeth were broken, trial court will see whether offence 337 (u) is made out, or s. 334 PPC. Bail Allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Murder: bail allowed where empties did not match the weapon
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 2026 SCMR 220 Empties recovered from place of occurrence were not matched with weapons of offense, Bail Allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Narcotics: bail allowed where 3.2 kg of ice was recovered from secret cavities
records.text: Further - Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 9-C 2026 SCMR 115/ 135 titled Muhammad Dawood Vs The State 3.2 KG of ICE (Meth) was recovered from the secret cavities. Bail Allowed. Reliance: 2021 SCMR 324/ 1804, PLD 2016 SC 471, 2020 SCMR 356.
records.title: Muhammad Dawood Vs The State 3.2 KG of ICE

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Murder: new facts in investigation made it a case of two versions
records.text:
Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 PPC 2022 SCMR 976 Titled Zafar Iqbal Vs The State During investigation, new facts came on record, case of two-version. Bail Allowed.
Reliance: 2012 SCMR 1137, 2023 PCRLJ 468 Lah
records.title: Zafar Iqbal Vs The State During investigation

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Statutory ground: bail where the trial was not completed within the stipulated period
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail (Statutory ground) 2026 PCRLJ 7, titled Sunny Hakim Vs The State; Justice Amjad Rafiq The trial was not completed within the stipulated period, and the accused was released on statutory grounds. Reliance: 2022 SCMR 1, PLD 2022 SC 112, 2026 PCRLJ 389 SC AJ&K.
records.title: Sunny Hakim Vs The State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Murder: general role and unmatched empties make a case of further inquiry
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 220 General role, empties were not matched, matter of further inquiry, bail allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Murder: vicarious liability, delay in trial and rule of consistency
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 PPC, 324 PPC 2026 SCMR 99 Vicarious liability, delay in conclusion of trial, rule of consistency, bail allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Cheque case: unexplained delay in FIR and no proof of the transaction
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 489(f) PPC 2023 SCMR 748 Delay in registration of FIR without any explanation, there was no proof of transaction of money to the accused, matter doubtful, case of further inquiry. Bail Granted.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Murder: indiscriminate firing by many accused but a single injury is a case of further inquiry
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 PPC 2021 SCMR 63 Allegation of bland thrifty firing of many accused, but one fire hit to the deceased, no PW was injured. And only four empties were taken into possession from the place of occurrence. Case of further inquiry. Bail Allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Murder: bail refused where the accused is nominated, the FIR is prompt and the trial has commenced
records.text: Complainant: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 PPC 2021 SCMR 176, 2007 SCMR 1798, 1980 SCMR 230, 1990 SCMR 307 Titled Noor Sultan Vs The State Accused nominated, FIR registered promptly, trial of the case commenced, if the role of accused is discussed, then prosecution case will be prejudiced. Bail Dismissed.
records.title: Noor Sultan Vs The State Accused nominated

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Cheque case: business transaction and six and a half months in custody
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 489(f) PPC 2022 SCMR 592 There is a business transaction between the complainant and the accused, the accused is behind bars for 6 and a half months, an offence not falling within the prohibitory clause. Bail Allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Bail allowed where the chemical examiner's and DNA reports did not match
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s s.377, 377(b), 367 (a) PPC 2022 SCMR 1447 Report of chemical examiner and DNA report not matched, Bail Allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Murder: general role of firing with no specific injury attributed
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 PPC 2022 SCMR 198 Titled Sikander Hayat Vs The State General role of firing, no specific role was attributed as to who fired at the deceased and where it hit, according to the PFSA report, twenty seven empties were matched from one weapon, case of further inquiry. Bail Allowed.
records.title: Sikander Hayat Vs The State General role of firing

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Murder: no role or weapon attributed and no recovery; abscondence of a co-accused is no ground to refuse bail
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 PPC 2021 SCMR 138 Accused nominated in FIR, prompt FIR but neither any role nor any weapon has been attributed to the accused, nothing was recovered from the accused, mere abscondance of the co-accussed, no ground for refusal of bail. Bail Allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: An accused in jail may furnish surety from a different city
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 302 PPC 1992 PCRLJ 916 - If accused in jail, can still give zamanat from a different city.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Cheque issued as security or in a business transaction is a case of further inquiry
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence u/s 489-F PPC 2026 MLD 951 - Offence does not fall within the prohibitory clause of Section 497 CrPC. If the cheque was issued as a security or business transaction, the case becomes one of further enquiry. Allowed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Registration of many cases is not by itself a ground to refuse bail
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail 2012 SCMR 573 - mere registration of many casses is not a ground for refusal of bail, if otherwise case is made out.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail
records.heading: Bail cancelled where it was obtained by concealing facts
records.text:
Complainant- cancellation of bail u/s 497(5) CrPc. 2021 SCMR 111 Accused of violating the Zubeir Case(PLD 1986 SC 173) with concealment of facts, obtained post-arrest bail, complainant filed cancellation of bail, which was allowed.
Reliance: PLD 2015 SC 66, 2020 SCMR 937 2008 SCMR 1556-, 2006 SCMR 1217, 1993 SCMR 550

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 154 CrPc- Registration of the case
records.heading: Police cannot hold an inquiry before registering the case
records.text: 2017 YLR 1584-DB, PLD 2016 581- Police cannot hold the inquiry prior to registration of the case.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S.205(initial stage magistrate) s. 540-A CrPc (during trial)(trial in absentia)- Dispensation of attendance of the accused
records.heading: Court may dispense with the attendance of one of several accused
records.text:
2014 PCRLJ 224: If there are more than one accused, then the court has the power to dispense with the attendance of one of the accused.
Reliance: 1980 PCRLJ 1

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPc- Examination of Accussed
records.heading: Evidence not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used against him
records.text: 2025 SCMR 1558: (E) s 342 CRPC, portion of evidence which was not put in 342 crpc, cannot be used against the accused. Accused Acquitted. Reliance on 2020 SCMR 687/ 321

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPc- Examination of Accussed
records.heading: Evidence not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be read against him
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ 159: which portion of evidence was not put to the accused, u/s 342 CrPc. cannot be read out against him. Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 417 CrPc - Appeal against acquittal (High Court)- read with S.249-A (Acquittal by Magistrate)& 265(k) CrPc(acquittal by Session).
records.heading: Appeal against acquittal under section 417 CrPC allowed
records.text: 2025 SCMR 562 - Appeal against acquittal u/s 417 CRPC, appeal allowed. Offence 324, 337 (d).

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 417 CrPc - Appeal against acquittal (High Court)- read with S.249-A (Acquittal by Magistrate)& 265(k) CrPc(acquittal by Session).
records.heading: Appeal under section 417 CrPC lies against every acquittal, including under sections 249-A and 265-K
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ 1828, Reliance: 2000 YLR 629, PLD 2004 SC 298, 2008 PCRLJ 1064 - In case of acquittal after full trial or u/s 249(a) and 265(k) CrPc., in all cases appeal u/s 417 CrPc. would be maintainable.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 410 CrPc - Appeal against conviction
records.heading: Time-barred jail appeal: delay of 2,511 days condoned on a plausible explanation
records.text: 2025 SCMR 744: offence u/s 302- Time barred jail appeal, u/s 410 CrPc, jail appeal was filed with the delay of 2511 days with plausible explanation, delay was condoned, and appeal was allowed.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 410 CrPc - Appeal against conviction
records.heading: Appeal of a proclaimed offender should be decided on merits in his absence
records.text: PLD 2015 Lah 1 - although accused was proclaimed offender but court should decide the appeal on merit in absence of accused as well.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: 497(5) CrPc - Cancellation of Bail
records.heading: Bail cancelled where it was obtained by concealing facts
records.text: 2021 SCMR 111- Accused by violating the Zubeir Case(PLD 1986 SC 173) with concealment of facts, obtained post-arrest bail, complainant filed cancellation of bail, which was allowed. Reliance: PLD 2015 SC 66, 2020 SCMR 937

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 167 CrPc (Physical Remand of accused )Read with S. 63 CrPc(power of magistrate to discharge the accused)
records.heading: Discharge by the Magistrate set aside and the accused sent on physical remand
records.text: PLD 2026 HC AJ&K 1- Police requested for physical remand but area magistrate discharged the accused, complainant assailed said order in High Court, Petition was allowed and accused was again sent on Physical remand.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Submission of Report 173 CrPC
records.heading: Jail authorities cannot withhold release because a section was added after the section 173 report
records.text: PLD 2026 ISB 35 - report of 173 CrPc was submitted in the court and after that I.O added a new section, due to the addition of a new section, jail authorities did not release the accused. The Act of Jail Authorities was declared illegal, Writ Petition allowed.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561(a) CrPc- Inherent powers of HC/ Quashing of F.I.R
records.heading: A bank cannot lodge an FIR under section 489-F PPC; FIR quashed
records.text: PLD 2026 Lah 69-Bank has no authority to get lodged F.I.R u/s 489 (f) PPC, F.I.R quashed.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561(a) CrPc- Inherent powers of HC/ Quashing of F.I.R
records.heading: Article 155(c) Police Order offences are non-cognizable; FIR quashed
records.text: 2012 YLR 828 Lah, Titled Muhammad Shafi vs The State, 2011 YLR 294 Lah- Offence u/a 155(c) Police Order 2002, are non-cognizable, directly FIR cannot be registered, FIR quashed. (Further: case of Zeeshan Thaheem SI)
records.title: Muhammad Shafi vs The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561(a) CrPc- Inherent powers of HC/ Quashing of F.I.R
records.heading: Quashment may be sought directly in the High Court without first applying under section 249-A or 265-K
records.text: 2021 MLD 278 Isb- Quashment can be directly filed in high court without submitting application u/s 249(a) or 265(k) CrPc. Reliance: 2021 PCRLJ 398 HC AJ&K, 2005 YLR 3193, 2018 YLR 2532, 2011 PCRLJ 1153, 2006 PCRLJ 263, 2009 SCMR 141, 2015 SCMR 1575, 2020 PCRLJ 335

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561(a) CrPc- Inherent powers of HC/ Quashing of F.I.R
records.heading: Criminal proceedings may be stayed until the civil court decides
records.text: 2021 PCRLJ 564, 2008 SCMR 839: Criminal proceeding can be stayed till the decision of civil court.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561(a) CrPc- Inherent powers of HC/ Quashing of F.I.R
records.heading: Partial quashment is permissible
records.text: 2003 CRLJ 733 SC - Partial quashment can be done.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Investigation after submission of report u/s 173 CrPc
records.heading: Investigation can be transferred even after the section 173 report
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ 427, PLD 2020 LAH 434, 2004 SCMR 1924, 2014 SCMR 474 Even after submission of a report of 173 CrPc, investigation can be transferred.(S. 18(6) Police Order 20002)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: 22-A CrPc- Registration of Case
records.heading: Justice of Peace cannot direct registration of a case for a non-cognizable offence
records.text: Child Marriage Restriant Act, 2026 MLD 525 Lah (Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh) - Justice of Peace cannot issue direction for registration of the case offense is non-cognizable and police cannot register the case. Rel. 2018 PCRLJ 50 (registration of case against public servant, no power of Justice of Peace)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: 22-A CrPc- Registration of Case
records.heading: Justice of Peace must call for police comments before ordering registration of a case
records.text: 2026 YLR 222 - It is necessary for the Justice of Peace to call comments from police. Without comments, an order for registration of a case is illegal.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: 22-A CrPc- Registration of Case
records.heading: Justice of Peace must apply a judicial mind and not act as a postman
records.text: 2024 SCMR 985 - Justice of Peace should not issue directions for registration of the case without applying his judicial mind, and he should not pass the order as a postman.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: 22-A CrPc- Registration of Case
records.heading: Justice of Peace looks only at whether the petition discloses a cognizable offence
records.text: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 20 - Justice of Peace will not assess the background of the case. He will see whether the contents of the petition make out cognizable offences, then he will issue directions for registration of the case.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S.200 CrPc.- Private Complaint
records.heading: Private complaint for a cognizable, non-compoundable offence cannot be dismissed for non-prosecution
records.text: PLJ 2023 CrC, Note 4, pg. 4, Lah; 2006 PCRLJ 1101- Dismissal of private complaint due to non Prosecution. If the offence is non-compoundable & congizable, then the court cannot dismiss a private complaint due to non-prosecution. Order Illegal.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S.200 CrPc.- Private Complaint
records.heading: Private complaint cannot be dismissed for non-prosecution once the accused is summoned
records.text: 2011 SCMR 720 - If accused is summoned in private complaint, it cannot be dismissed due to non-prosecution.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S.200 CrPc.- Private Complaint
records.heading: Summoning in a private complaint requires only prima facie evidence
records.text: 2026 PCrLJ 597 - Detail for summoning of accused in private complaint under Section 200 CrPC read with 204: court will see prima facie evidence on record and in-depth court will assess the evidence at the time of trial. Summoning order upheld.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S.200 CrPc.- Private Complaint
records.heading: Where a private complaint and a State case are both pending, the complaint is tried first
records.text: PLD 2025 Lahore 137 - If a private complaint and state case are under trial, then the first private complaint would be tried, and during the proceedings, no further investigation would be allowed to avoid unnecessary delay and complication in the trial.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S.200 CrPc.- Private Complaint
records.heading: Private complaint wrongly dismissed for failure to supply certified copies in time
records.text: 2018 PCRLJ LAH 63 - U/s 265-e & 204(3) - Private complaint dismissed by lower courts on the basis that the complainant did not provide certified copies to the accused within the stipulated period. Overturned on appeal by HighCourt.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 204 CrPc- Summoning of accused in private complaint
records.heading: Revision allowed and accused summoned where prima facie evidence was available
records.text: 2026 MLD 575 Lah (Justice Shehbaz Ali Rizvi) Crim. Revision: Private Complaint was dismissed, offence u/s 302, 324 PPC. Revision was allowed as prima facie reasonable evidence is available. Revision allowed, Accused Summoned.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 204 CrPc- Summoning of accused in private complaint
records.heading: Accused may be summoned in a private complaint on prima facie evidence
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ 1437: if there is a prima facie evidence against the accused in a private complaint, the court can summon the accused to face trial, u/s 204 CrPc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC- Summoning of Witness
records.heading: Accused's application to summon the investigating officer as a court witness dismissed
records.text: 2026 MLD 118 Lah (DB) (Justice Shehram Sarwar, Justice Sardar Akbar Ali Dogar) Accused submitted application in the trial court to summon the investigating officer, as CW, u/s 540 CrPc, which was dismissed. Criminal Revision also dismissed.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC- Summoning of Witness
records.heading: A witness given up by the prosecution may be summoned on the accused's application
records.text: PLJ 2005 Lah CrC 395: Prosecution gave up the PW, but the accused submitted an application for his summoning, and he confronted his statement u/s 161 CrPc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC- Summoning of Witness
records.heading: A witness named in the FIR may be summoned although his section 161 statement was not recorded
records.text: 2022 SCMR 1882: Witness was cited in FIR, but his statement u/s 161 was not recorded. In spite of the fact, he can be summoned as a witness.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC- Summoning of Witness
records.heading: A surprise witness not on the list of prosecution witnesses cannot be produced
records.text: 2021 PCRLJ 915-DB SINDH: Name of the witness not included in the list of PWs, surprising witness cannot be produced. Application Dismissed. Summoning order illegal. Reliance: PLD 2018 SC 178, 2005 YLR 212, PLD 2022 LAH 319, 2018 YLR 2490, 2018 PCRLJ 2490, PLD 2009 SC 669, 2022 YLR 478, 2020 MLD 942

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 494 CrPc- Withdrawal of the case
records.heading: Prosecution may withdraw under section 494 CrPC even after evidence is recorded
records.text: 2026 PCRLJ 152 Pesh: Even after recording of evidence, prosecution can withdraw its case under S. 494 CrPc at any stage.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265(c) CrPc- Delivery of copies
records.heading: Copies of case diaries can be delivered to the accused
records.text: PLD 1996 Lah 277: Copies of case diaries can be delivered to the accused.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345 CrPc- Compromise, S. 338(e)
records.heading: Honour killing: on compromise, death sentence altered to life imprisonment
records.text: 2026 SCMR 480 Titled Sanober Khan Vs The State, offence u/s 302 PPC, 311 PCC(honour killing)- Fasaad fil Arz- Compromise effected, death sentence altered into life imprisonment.
records.title: Sanober Khan Vs The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345 CrPc- Compromise, S. 338(e)
records.heading: Compromise in non-compoundable offences
records.text: 2023 PCRLJ 749, PLJ 2022 SC 40, 2002 SCMR 184, 2013 PCRLJ 398, 1998 SCMR 466, 2011 MLD 1468: Compromise in non-compoundable offences

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345 CrPc- Compromise, S. 338(e)
records.heading: Compromise through a power of attorney for a legal heir abroad
records.text: 2016 MLD 631 Lah - compromise through power of attorney. All the legal heirs entered into compromise, father was also one of the legal heirs of the deceased but was outside the country, application for seeking compromise through power of attorney was allowed, and accussed were acquitted.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 161 CrPc- Statement of PWs , read with S. 172 CrPc( Confrontation)
records.heading: The investigating officer can be cross-examined on the case diary and section 161 statements
records.text: 2018 PCRLJ 553- I.O can be cross examined on case diary and statement of PWs u/s 161 CrPc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S.176 CrPC- Judicial Inquiry into cause of death by Magistrate
records.heading: Judicial inquiry under section 176 CrPC determines only the cause of death
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ Lah 860 - In judicial inquiry, a magistrate can only ascertain the case of death and is not competent to declare any person guilty or innocent. This is a judicial order, revision can be filed against such order in session court.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 412 CrPc- No right to Appeal if defendant pleads guilty
records.heading: Right of appeal where a plea of guilty was made under coercion or inducement
records.text:
2022 PCRLJ 878- although there is no provision of appeal under s.412 CrPc, in case of confession before the court, however, if at the time of framing of charge, accused denied the charges, but subsequently confessed the guilt, and confession is not
independent, that is under coercion or inducement, then accused has a right to file the appeal. (Appeal by Naseer Ahmad Thaheem in 1998, J. Basheer A. Mujahid and Naeem Ullah Sherwani - procedure of confession must be adopted, and not under inducement).

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 439 CrPc- Revisional Powers of High Court & Session Court
records.heading: Charge amended on arrest of a third accused: evidence must be recorded afresh
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ 705 Sindh - De Novo Trial : trial of two accused started, evidence recorded in the meanwhile third accused was arrested and charge was amended, on relying previous evidence, all the three accused were convicted, according to law, evidence was again to be recorded by the trial court. Case Remanded in revision petition and trial again started. Powers of revision, under 439 CrPc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial: factors to be considered
records.text: Retrial factors to be considered. (a) Facts of case, (b) harassment already undergone by accused, (c) expenditure incurred in defence, (d) circumstances of the case. 67 adjournments during 5 years of trial. Retrial not ordered. PLJ 1980 Cr.C. (Pesh.) 409 Mir Zaman v. Khalil-ur-Rehman.
records.title: Mir Zaman v. Khalil-ur-Rehman

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial not to be ordered where it would deny the benefit of doubt
records.text: Retrial not to be ordered when it amounts to the denial of principle of doubt and leading to injustice. The Court before ordering retrial should consider the view of the trial Court regarding evidence before it, magnitude of apprehended miscarriage of justice if retrial not ordered, chances of conviction and expenses of retrial. 1988 SCMR 1691 Haji Muhammad etc. v. Muhammad Ibrahim etc.
records.title: Haji Muhammad etc. v. Muhammad Ibrahim etc

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial proper where the High Court analyses the case without binding the trial court
records.text: Retrial proper where High Court's order for retrial (in acquittal case) attempting exhaustive analysis of the case and expressing opinion "not lacking in directness" but at the same time cautioning lower Court against treating such opinion as binding". (SC) PLD 1962 SC 249 Abdur Rashid.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Section 198-A CrPC and offences by public servants in the course of duty
records.text: Offence by Public Servants committed by them during the performance of their official duties, held, Sec. 198-A Cr.P.C. is operative inspite of repeal of Act XXV of 1974 by Ordinance XXVII of 1981. PLJ 1997 Cr.C. (Pesh) 1430, Zil-e-Hussain Shah v. Asif Jan.
records.title: Zil-e-Hussain Shah v. Asif Jan

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial ordered where witnesses were not cross-examined on vital police statements
records.text: Witnesses not cross-examined in Court as to vital statement before police. Retrial ordered. (DB) PLD 1967 Dacca 566 Ansar Sardar. Retrial proper where trial Court's conclusion (in judgment of acquittal) not supported by balanced statement of relevant facts or by truly reasoned arguments. (SC) PLD 1962 SC 249 Abdur Rashid.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Murder case decided on special oath: illegality not curable, retrial ordered
records.text: Murder case decided on special oath, held the procedure was illegal not curable u/S. 537, Cr.P.C. Case remanded for retrial. (DB) PLJ 1991 Cr.C. (Lah.) 76 Elahi Bux.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial order set aside where the acquittal followed six years without evidence
records.text: Retrial. Where trial Court acquits the accused when the case remained pending for 6 years for lack of evidence, High Court ordered retrial. Supreme Court set aside the High Court's order. 1992 SCMR 2328, Karm Ali Shah v. Mazhar Hussain etc.
records.title: Karm Ali Shah v. Mazhar Hussain etc

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial ordered in revision seven years after the occurrence
records.text: Retrial after 7 years of occurrence ordered in revision from acquittal. 1972 P.Cr.LJ 664 Muhammad Din v. Haider etc. 1972 P.Cr.LJ 657 Khadam Hussain v. Ilyas etc.
records.title: Muhammad Din v. Haider etc

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial can be ordered from any stage, even for arguments only
records.text: Retrial ordered after 19 years of occurrence, only for hearing arguments. Neither de novo trial nor fresh evidence was to be recorded. Retrial by High Court can be ordered from any stage of proceedings, u/S. 439 Cr.P.C. PLJ 1996 SC 313, Abdul Latif v. Bagga Khan etc.
records.title: Abdul Latif v. Bagga Khan etc

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: State-appointed defence counsel given too little time to prepare: case remanded
records.text: Defence counsel engaged at State expense in case under section 302, P.P.C. given only 2« hours to prepare the case of the accused. Prejudice alleged by the accused. Case remanded for trial. (DB) 1971 P.Cr.LJ 1047 Bhasia Kiri Ghara.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Accused prejudiced in defence by the investigating officer's deposition: retrial ordered
records.text:
Prejudice in defence. Accused failing to produce defence evidence relying on deposition of Investigating Officer that he could not swear that they had participated in murder. Held, accused prejudiced in defence. Retrial ordered.
(SC) PLD 1958 SC (Pak.) 275 Moonda etc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Bias suggested by the judge's remarks: retrial before a different judge
records.text: Bias in Judge. Judge making unfounded remarks in judgment suggesting bias, Retrial entrusted to different Judge. PLD 1957 Kar. 814 M. Faridi.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial may be ordered from a particular point in the proceedings
records.text: Retrial may be ordered from a particular point in proceeding of a case. (SC) PLD 1958 SC (Pak.) 275 Moonda etc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial to be heard by another judge where the first has expressed an opinion on merits
records.text: Retrial case to be heard by another Judge, as the Sessions Judge had already expressed opinion on merits of the case. (DB) PLD 1958 Kar. 18 Chutto.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial may be ordered for all accused although the ground concerns only some
records.text: Retrial for all the accused ordered although ground for retrial appeared to be only for some of the accused. (SC) PLD 1958 SC (Pak.) 275 Moonda etc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Mere delay in prosecution is no ground to refuse retrial
records.text: Mere delay in prosecution is no ground for not ordering retrial. (DB) PLD 1964 Lah.1 State v. Muhammad Shafi.
records.title: State v. Muhammad Shafi

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial is not barred where the acquittal was on a technical defect
records.text: Acquittal not on merits, retrial is not illegal. The accused was acquitted on a technical defect in sanction for prosecution. PLD 1956 Lah. 87 Salahuddin v. Crown.
records.title: Salahuddin v. Crown

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Acquittal without jurisdiction operates as a discharge; retrial not barred
records.text: Acquittal to operate as discharge where the orders are passed without jurisdiction. Retrial is therefore, not barred. (PC) PLD 1949 PC 108 Yousaf Ali v. King.
records.title: Yousaf Ali v. King

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Want of sanction for prosecution: retrial not barred
records.text: Sanction for prosecution wanting therefore Court not of competent jurisdiction. Retrial not barred. PLD 1951 Lah. 430 Ishan Elahi v. Crown.
records.title: Ishan Elahi v. Crown

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial is a continuation of the same trial, not double jeopardy
records.text: Retrial is not a second but continuation of same trial and not within principle of double jeopardy. (FC) PLD 1955 FC 185 Anwar.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial ordered where the evidence on record was very slight
records.text: Evidence on record very slight. Appellant could not have offered evidence against it. Retrial ordered. (PC) 1 MIA 67 Janoki Das v. Brinda Ban.
records.title: Janoki Das v. Brinda Ban

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Discharge for non-attendance of prosecution witnesses held illegal; retrial ordered
records.text: Discharge for non-attendance of prosecution witnesses on about 40 hearings and the Magistrate issuing coercive process against the PWs in a cognizable warrant and non-compoundable case, is illegal. Retrial ordered. 1975 P.Cr.LJ 816 Piyare Muhammad.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Offence admitted by misapprehension: retrial cannot be resisted
records.text: Offence admitted by misapprehension, request for retrial cannot be resisted, 196 IC 553 in re: S.S. Pattabi Rama Iear.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: A third trial may be ordered in a proper case
records.text: Third trial. The fact that the accused has been retried on the same charge is no reason for refusing to order a third trial in a proper case, if the evidence is of such a nature as to make another trial desirable for the ends of justice. (DB) 45 Cr.LJ 99 Emp. v. Lal Mia. 209 IC 206.
records.title: Emp. v. Lal Mia

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial order set aside 11 years after acquittal and 21 years after the FIR
records.text: Retrial after 11 years of acquittal and 21 years after FIR was registered. Retrial order set aside. 1987 SCMR 237 Sultan Khan etc. 1972 SCMR 95 Phulail Khan.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial not ordered after a long lapse of time
records.text: Long time elapse since trial. Retrial not ordered. (SC) PLD 1976 SC 1 Dosa. PLJ 1976 SC 20.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial not justified ten years after the offence
records.text: Retrial long time elapsed between commission of offence and hearing of appeal. Retrial not justified. (Occurrence 9-1-71 appeal 1-4-81). (PC) 1982 PSC 307 Ajodha.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: No retrial after nine years
records.text: No retrial after 9 years. Revision petition filed in 1973, came up for hearing in 1981. Retrial not ordered. PLJ 1981 Cr.C. (Lah.) 543 Abdul Ghafoor v. Sultan Ali etc.
records.title: Abdul Ghafoor v. Sultan Ali etc

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Protracted trial: retrial not justified
records.text: Protracted trial. Order for retrial is not justified. PLD 1962 Q.51. Umed Ali etc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Trial in suspense for seven years: retrial not justified
records.text: Trial kept in suspense for 7 years. Retrial is not justified. PLD 1962 Dac. 61 Bassanta Kumar Chaudhri.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Prosecution pending for four years: retrial not ordered
records.text:
Prosecution hanging for four years. Retrial not ordered. PLD 1962 Kar. 753 State
v. Abrar Hussain Shah.
records.title:
State
v. Abrar Hussain Shah

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Accused long in custody: not a fit case for retrial
records.text: Accused in custody for a long time. The offence was committed in 1947 and the accused was placed on trial in 1949. He was in custody for a long time during the trial. Held, not a fit case for retrial. (FC) PLD 1953 FC 125 Asir-ud-Din v. Crown.
records.title: Asir-ud-Din v. Crown

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial refused after a six-year trial and two years in jail
records.text: Retrial refused because trial extended over 6 years and accused remained in jail for 2 years. 1970 P.Cr.LJ 515 Zabte Khan.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial not ordered after a protracted trial and long sentences in connected cases
records.text: Retrial not ordered because of previous protracted trial and long terms of punishment in connected cases. (DB) 1970 P.Cr. LJ 649 State v. Jagmal Singh.
records.title: State v. Jagmal Singh

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial order set aside where the accused spent four years in custody awaiting it
records.text: Retrial order set aside by Supreme Court because incident took place on 4-8-1966 and the accused was acquitted on 13-12-1967, Supreme Court heard the case on 22-10-1971. Accused in custody for 4 years waiting retrial. Witnesses may not be available. (SC) 1972 SCMR 95 Shah Wali.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial is not to fill the gaps in the prosecution case
records.text: Not to supplement deficiencies of prosecution. It is not the function of the court to supplement the deficiencies of the prosecution by remanding the case for proper trial. To comply with the request for retrial would be exposing the accused to a further ordeal and expenses to which the Crown has no right to expose him. The subject cannot be made to suffer because of the neglect or omissions of the Crown in the mode in which it conducts a criminal proceeding. (DB) ILR 5 Lah. 404 Crown v. Jaswant Rai & Co.
records.title: Crown v. Jaswant Rai & Co

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial refused where sought mainly to fill gaps in the prosecution case
records.text: Retrial not ordered. Offence committed more than 2 years and 4 months before hearing of appeal. Crown's request for retrial based mainly on desire to fill up gaps in the prosecution. Retrial not ordered. (FC) PLD 1952 FC 63 Aminul Haq v. Crown.
records.title: Aminul Haq v. Crown

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial order set aside where the appellate court itself doubted guilt
records.text: Retrial order set aside. Appellate Court doubtful of accused's guilt, yet ordering retrial. Order set aside. (FC) PLD 1954 FC 120 Abdus Sattar v. Crown.
records.title: Abdus Sattar v. Crown

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial after long delay only when absolutely necessary
records.text: Long time intervening between acquittal and hearing of revision did not by itself stand in the way of ordering a retrial. It should be ordered only when it is absolutely necessary and unavoidable. (DB) PLD 1956 BJ 24 Crown v. Ismail.
records.title: Crown v. Ismail

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial in revision from acquittal not barred after seven years
records.text:
Retrial after revision from acquittal; not a bar even after 7 years of occurrence. 1972 P.Cr.LJ 657 Khadim Hussain v. Ilyas etc. 1972 P. Cr. LJ 664 Muhammad Din
v. Haider etc.
records.title: Khadim Hussain v. Ilyas etc

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Retrial not ordered where it would amount to an order to convict
records.text: Retrial not ordered where it would practically amount to an order to convict the accused. (DB) PLD 1955 Lah. 271 Crown v. Mirza Khan.
records.title: Crown v. Mirza Khan

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: High Court may order retrial from any stage under section 439 CrPC
records.text: Retrial from any stage can be ordered by the High Court u/S. 439, Cr.P.C. PLD 1996 SC 152, Abdul Latif v. Bagga Khan.
records.title: Abdul Latif v. Bagga Khan

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: On remand, the trial court need not record evidence afresh
records.text: De novo trial on remand of the case by High Court, the Trial Court is not required to record evidence de novo but judgment already recorded by it may be reconsidered. PLJ 1995 SC 526, Muhammad Abbas v. Saghir Ahmed.
records.title: Muhammad Abbas v. Saghir Ahmed

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 423, Cr.P.C.- Power of appellate court in disposing of appeal RETRIAL
records.heading: Unsoundness of mind is judged at the time of the offence, not the trial
records.text: The unsound mind of the accused is to be determined whether it was so when the crime was committed; not the state of mind of the accused at the time of the trial. Case remanded for trial of the offence u/S. 302 PPC. 1994 SCMR 1517, Abdul Wahid.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: 45. Retrial not ordered after 14 years of the commission of the offence,
records.heading: Retrial not ordered after 14 years
records.text: 1977 P.Cr.LJ 12 Sultan Ali.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: 45. Retrial not ordered after 14 years of the commission of the offence,
records.heading: Partial retrial is lawful where co-accused were rightly acquitted
records.text: Partial retrial of accused is perfectly legal when the appellate Court is of the view that the co-accused have been rightly acquitted such cases should not be ordered to be retried against all the accused. NLR 1991 Cr. 214 Shahmand etc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: 45. Retrial not ordered after 14 years of the commission of the offence,
records.heading: An acquitted accused cannot be retried without an appeal or revision against his acquittal
records.text: Retrial of acquitted accused when no appeal or revision against his acquittal in the High Court, held he cannot be retried because of section 403, Cr.P.C. just because the co-accused was remanded for retrial. PLJ 1991 Cr. C. (Lah.) 448 Muhammad Riaz.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Medical Board
records.heading: Medical board may be constituted even 21 days after the first medico-legal certificate
records.text:
PLJ 2018 CrC Lah 770 (Justice Kasim Khan), 2017 MLD 1828 Lah (J. Ch Abdul Aziz), 2009 PCRLJ Lah pg. 1281, 2023 PCRLJ 1373, 2004 MLD 1401, 2023 PCRLJ 222. A medical board can be constituted even after 21 days of the date of first MLC.
Against: 2026 YLR 208

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S.145 Crpc- Attachment of property
records.heading: Property sealed under section 145 CrPC without hearing the other party: order set aside
records.text: 1987 SCMR 1371 - Magistrate sealed the disputed property, without hearing the second party, order illegal, set aside.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sections of CRPC relative to Fard E Jurm & High Court Rules
records.heading: Framing of charge: relevant sections of the CrPC
records.text: 241, 241-A CrPc., 242, 221-223/ 7(C), 221 (7), Previously convicted- 245(a) CrPc.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 145 CrPc. Immovable property and powers of magistrate
records.heading: A mosque cannot be sealed under section 145 CrPC
records.text: PLJ 2013 718 - Mosque cannot be sealed under section 145 CrPC.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 528 CrPC - Transfer of Case
records.heading: After trial begins, only the High Court can transfer the case
records.text: PLD 2025 Lahore 98 - After commencement of trial, the Session Judge has no power to transfer the trial or bail from one court to another court; only the High Court has the power to do so.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.heading: Section 342 statement carries more weight than a section 164 confession
records.text: 2015 SCMR 423 - Examination of the accused under section 342 CrPC is more valuable according to law for the purpose of decision of the case as compared to a confessional statement under section 164 CrPC.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CRPC - Confessional Statement
records.heading: Confession in police custody or before the media has no evidentiary value
records.text: PLD 2019 SC 196- confession recorded under custody of police by the accused or before any media has no evidentiary value.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345 Crpc- Compromise
records.heading: A complainant who has forgiven the accused cannot proceed with the case again
records.text: 2026 SCMR 480 - In criminal cases, if once the complainant forgave the accused, he cannot again further proceed the case.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 249-A CrPc- Appeal Against Acquittal
records.heading: Acquittal under section 249-A CrPC: appeal lies under section 417, not revision
records.text: 2025 PCrLJ 1095 - If the accused is acquitted under Section 249-A CrPC, then the appeal would be filed under Section 417 CrPC in the High Court; criminal revision is not maintainable.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 173, s. 190, s. 63 CrPc., s.169 crpc - Discharge cancellation report
records.heading: Sections 173, 190, 63 and 169 CrPC: authorities
records.text: 1999 SCMR 733, PLD 2001 LAH 271 titled Ashiq Hussein Vs State, 1983 PCRLJ 2187, 1999 SCMR 12, 1993 PCRLJ 1593, PLD 1980 LAH 80, PLD 1985 SC 62, 2006 SCMR 1920, 2005 PCRLJ 1165, PLD 1981 (Abdul Waheed Case), PLD 1987 (Muhammad Zain Case).
records.title: Ashiq Hussein Vs State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Art. 13 Const. Read with s. 403 CrPc (no double trial for convicted person)
records.heading: Double jeopardy: Article 13 of the Constitution and section 403 CrPC
records.text: Double Jeopardy PLD 2012 SC 179 + PLD 2006 SC 365

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO (Identification Parade)
records.heading: No identification parade needed where the accused is clearly visible on CCTV
records.text: 2026 YLR 564 -The accused was visible in CCTV camera footage clearly, no need to hold an identification parade.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO (Identification Parade)
records.heading: Identification parade not held according to the settled principles: acquittal
records.text: 2025 SCMR 50 titled Subha Sadiq Vs The State - Principle of Identification parade - identification was not held according to the principle, case doubtful, accused acquitted.
records.title: Subha Sadiq Vs The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO (Identification Parade)
records.heading: Identification parade held after seven days has no evidentiary value
records.text: 2011 SCMR 537 - identification parade held after 7 days, it has no evidentiary value, accused acquitted.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO (Identification Parade)
records.heading: Identification parade has no value where the accused's features were not given in the FIR
records.text: 1995 SCMR 585/2585- features of the accused were not given in FIR, identification parade has no legal value, accused acquitted.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO (Identification Parade)
records.heading: Identification parade held 26 days after arrest has no value
records.text: 2011 SCMR 387 - Identification parade held 26 days after arrest, has no value. Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO (Identification Parade)
records.heading: Identification parade alone cannot sustain a conviction
records.text: 2009 SCMR 4 - Although Identification parade is a corroborative piece of evidence but merely on the basis of conducting of identification parade u/a 2(c) QSO, one cannot be convicted.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO (Identification Parade)
records.heading: Evidence not challenged in cross-examination is deemed admitted
records.text: 1991 CLC note. 329 pg 252, 1991 SCMR 2300, 1998 SCMR 879- if some portion of evidence which is not challenged during cross-examination, that amounts to admitted.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO (Identification Parade)
records.heading: Evidence recorded in one case cannot be used in another unless exhibited
records.text: PLJ 2004 Kar 613 - evidence recorded in one case cannot be used in other case, until unless that is exhibited according to law. Rel. 2004 PCRLJ 371

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art 150. Hostile Witness
records.heading: When a witness may be declared hostile
records.text: 2025 PCRLJ 942 - Witness recorded his examination in chief, according to statement u/s 161 CRPC, but during cross examination, he resiles or tries to give benefit to the accused, then he can be declared hostile witness and right of cross examination can be given to the prosecution. Reliance: 2025 SCMR 547, 2023 SCMR 670.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art 150. Hostile Witness
records.heading: Only the State counsel, not private counsel, may cross-examine a hostile witness
records.text: 1968 PCRLJ 321 Lah/ 68 - Only government lawyer can cross examine a hostile witness, private counsel cannot.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 140/ 153 QSO
records.heading: FIR of a complainant who died before cross-examination cannot be used as corroboration
records.text: 2025 SCMR 762: (a)Complainant died before recording of evidence, F.I.R was exhibited as Exhibit PA, but cross examination could not be conducted, said F.I.R cannot be used as a corroborative piece of evidence against the accused, and accused cannot be convicted on the basis of said evidence. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: AIR 1957 SC 366, 1979 SCMR 155

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 38 QSO.
records.heading: Confession before the police has no evidentiary value
records.text: PLD 1965 SC 366 - Art. 38 QSO. Accussed: Confession before police has no evidentiary value, accused intimated the police that he has committed an offence, his such statement cannot be used against him. Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 140 QSO read with 10-A Constitution of Pakistan, read with s. 162 CrPc
records.heading: The author of a document can be confronted with its contents
records.text:
2026 PCRLJ 277 ISB, titled Muhammad Shoaib Hassan Vs The State- The author of the document can be confronted with the contents of the document (2012 PCRLJ 614 Balochsitan (DB), 2006 PCRLJ 639 Kar (DB)).Further facts and details of case: Offence u/s 302, I.O took into possession video clip from the mobile of accused, and accused submitted application to confront said video, application dismissed, revision also dismissed. Reliance: PLD 2019 SC 675, 2012 PCRLJ 614 Balochsitan
(DB), 2006 PCRLJ 639 Kar (DB).
records.title: Muhammad Shoaib Hassan Vs The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 172 QSO- Cross Examination on Investigating Officer
records.heading: The investigating officer must answer every question in cross-examination
records.text:
2018 PCRLJ 553-I.O is duty bound to reply on each and every question put in cross- examination, even counsel for accused through IO can see some portion of case diaries. Revision Allowed, case was remanded, and IO was again summoned to give the opportunity of cross-examination.
Further detail: I.O can be cross examined on case diary and statement of PWs u/s 161 CrPc. Court under art. 15 QSO, can force the I.O to reply to the cross-examination. According to Art. 49 QSO statement under s. 161 CrPc is a public document.
Reliance: PLD 2003 Lah 290 (J. Tassaduq Jillani, J. Asif Saeed Khosa, J. Khawaja Shareef)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 133 QSO - Cross-Examination
records.heading: Evidence of a witness who was not cross-examined has no evidentiary value
records.text:
1995 SD pg. 485- if the witness is not cross-examined, it has no evidentiary value.
Reliance: PLJ 1986 CRC 383, 1993 PCRLJ 1729

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 13 QSO( Production of the title deed of witness) & Art. 129(g) ( Withhold of best evidence)
records.heading: High Court cannot disturb concurrent findings of fact unless perverse or illegal
records.text:
PLD 2024 SC 771- High court cannot give its own view regarding disputed questions of facts, and cannot interfere into the concurrent findings of the courts below until and unless it deems that the judgments of the courts below are perverse and illegal.
Reliance: 2009 CLD 610 titled State Life Vs Jaffar Hussein, 2006 SCMR 152 titled Allies Books Vs Sultan Ahmad.
records.title: State Life Vs Jaffar Hussein

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 27 QSO ( First Version of accused)
records.heading: The first version of the accused is admissible
records.text: PLD 2020 SC 523 The first version of the accused is admissible.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Oath Act- QSO, s. 8
records.heading: Evidence given by a Muslim witness without oath is inadmissible
records.text: 1995 CRLJ 282, 1990 PCRLJ 445 If the muslim witness gives any evidence in court, without oath according to s.8 oath act, such evidence is not admissible.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO- Discovery of facts
records.heading: After acquittal, further police investigation requires the Magistrate's permission
records.text: 1991 PCRLJ 1755- If the accused is acquitted by the magistrate, then on orders of DIG, the DSP cannot conduct investigation without magistrate’s permission.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 72-78 read with S. 461/ 537 CrPc - Exhibition of documents
records.heading: The court may look at documents that have not been exhibited
records.text: 1987 CRLJ 32 - documents can be viewed by court even though they have not been exhibited.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art 46(1) - Dying Declaration
records.heading: Dying declaration is weak evidence where the person who recorded it is not produced
records.text: 2026 PCrLJ 134 - Dying declaration can be recorded in presence of any person. If the witness before whom the dying declaration was recorded is not produced in the court and he is not examined, then such like evidence would be presumed a weak type of evidence.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 73 QSO- Primary Evidence
records.heading: Oral evidence has no value against documentary evidence
records.text: 2015 CLC 1387 - In the presence of documentary evidence, oral evidence has no value.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 73 QSO- Primary Evidence
records.heading: High Court should not consider documents never produced or exhibited below
records.text: 1989 CLC 382 - The highcourt should not consider documentary evidence which has not been presented in the trial court, nor been exhibited neither presented in the appealent court.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 73 QSO- Primary Evidence
records.heading: Photographs and video recordings are documentary evidence
records.text: 2002 PCRLJ 1765- Photography and videographs are also considered to be documentary evidence.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 73 QSO- Primary Evidence
records.heading: An unchallenged document is preferred over oral evidence
records.text: PLD 2004 LAH 115 - If any document has not been confronted or challenged, then it should be preferred over oral evidence.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.heading: Section 182 PPC: only the police officer who received the false information can initiate proceedings
records.text:
2026 SCMR 77- S. 182 PPC, read with s. 173, s. 190 and s. 195 CrPc: accused acquitted in FIR, but cannot proceed against complainant u/s 182 PPC, only the police officer before whom false application was submitted is competent to initiate proceedings against the complainant. reliance on 1968 PCRLJ 215, AIR 2017 SC 391
AGAINST: CP No. 42 K/ 2017, 2024 SCMR 1123

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 84 PPC- Unsound Mind
records.heading: A person of unsound mind cannot be convicted
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ Isb 1739 Accussed- if an unsound mind commits any offence, he cannot be convicted. (Mens Rea)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 489-F PPC | Security Cheque
records.heading: Security cheque: no conviction without proof of dishonest intent
records.text: 2024 SCMR 1567 - Supreme Court held the principles of security cheque; if the cheque was issued as a security, then without proving the dishonest intent of the accused he cannot be convicted.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 489-F PPC | Security Cheque
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC applies only to a cheque issued with dishonest intention
records.text: 2026 PCrLJ 1175 - Offence under Section 489-F attracts only the cheque that was issued with dishonest intention.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 489-F PPC | Security Cheque
records.heading: Bank fraud and forgery: complainant must produce CCTV footage or a handwriting expert's report
records.text: 2026 PCrLJ 158 - During trial in bank fraud, forgery, and corruption cases, the complainant is bound to produce evidence like CCTV footage or the report of a handwriting expert. If there are dishonest improvements, then the evidence is not reliable and the accused is acquitted.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 452 PPC
records.heading: Entering a relative's house is not an offence under section 452 PPC
records.text: 2009 PCrLJ 1259 - Entry into the house of a relative does not constitute an offence under section 452 PPC.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Trial | Hurt
records.heading: Broken teeth in a fight: section 334 PPC applies
records.text: PLJ 2022 CrC 1385 In a fight, if teeth of the injured are broken then Section 334 PPC would be applicable, while in Section 337U PPC the amount of arsh has been mentioned.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Hurt | Section 337-D PPC
records.heading: Section 337-D PPC applies only to injuries to the body trunk, not the neck
records.text: 2026 SCMR 715 - Section 337-D PPC would be applicable only in a case where the injury goes in depth in the body trunk. An injury caused on a neck would not attract Section 337-D as the neck does not include the body trunk; hence, the sentence awarded under Section 337-D PPC to the accused is acquitted, only sentence would be upheld in other sections.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Motive not proved: benefit of doubt and acquittal
records.text:
Accused: 2025 SCMR 1339 / 780 - Motive not proved, benefit of doubt, Accused acquitted.
Reliance: 2023 PCRLJ 917, 2020 SCMR 305, 2021 SCMR 780/ 810/ 736, 2024 SCMR 1427

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Medical and ocular evidence in conflict; night occurrence with no source of light
records.text:
Accused: 2025 SCMR 944- Medical and ocular evidence in conflict, occurrence of night time, and no source of light was mentioned in FIR. Accused Acquitted.
Reliance: 2019 SCMR 129, 2022 SCMR 1567, 2022 PCRLJ 109 LAH( DB), 2025 SCMR 1580 (Medical & Ocular in conflict )

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Delay in post-mortem gives the benefit of doubt
records.text: Accused: 2021 SCMR 810 - delay in conducting post mortem, benefit of doubt, Accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Delayed FIR, unproved motive, and conflict between site plan and medical evidence
records.text:
Accused: (Main Case Law) 2021 PCRLJ 449 Lah (Multan Bench)
(d) Delayed FIR, reliance on PLD 2019 SC 64
(e) motive not proved, 2006 SCMR 1846, 2010 SCMR 846, 2012 SCMR 327, 2015 SCMR 315
(f) scaled site plan, and medical evidence in conflict, Accused Acquitted

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Confession before the Magistrate made under coercion and without proper procedure
records.text: Accused: 2025 SCMR 1344 - Confession before magistrate under coercion, and proper procedure was not adopted. Accused confessed his guilt first, but subsequently denied the charge, neither there was a thumb impression on the first page of confession nor accused was given time to think. Contradiction in the statement of PWs, Accused Acquitted. Reliance on 2019 SCMR 129

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Evidence of witnesses without enmity should still not be believed blindly
records.text: Accussed: 2025 SCMR 281 - Although there was no enmity of the witnesses with the accused, however, their evidence should not be blindly believed. Registration of FIR was shown promptly, which was not possible. Benefit of doubt. Accused Acquitted

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Delayed FIR, contradictions and doubtful presence of witnesses
records.text: Accussed: 2025 SCMR 1087 - Delayed FIR, contradiction in the statement of PWs, presence of the PWs doubtful, accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Medical and ocular evidence in conflict, delayed post-mortem, night occurrence
records.text: Accussed: 2025 SCMR 1110 (h) - Medical and ocular in conflict, delayed Post Mortem, occurrence night time, benefit of doubt. Accused Acquitted

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Previous enmity, delayed FIR and related witnesses
records.text: Accussed: 2025 SCMR 1024 -Previous enmity, delayed FIR, relative witnesses, Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Conflict between medical and ocular evidence shows the witnesses did not see the occurrence
records.text: Accussed: 2025 SCMR 1053- Medical and Ocular in conflict, it means that the witnesses have not seen the occurrence with their own eyes. Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: A matching forensic report alone does not prove the prosecution case
records.text: Accussed: 2025 SCMR 1082 - mere matching of Forensic report does not prove prosecution case, if other evidence is not in line, then Accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Exculpatory statement of a co-accused cannot be used against another accused
records.text: Accussed: 2025 SCMR 552 - Exculpatory statement of Co-Accussed cannot be used against the co-accussed. Recovery effected from open place, motive introduced with delay, benefit of doubt, Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form a connected chain
records.text:
Accussed: 2025 SCMR 1558
(A) Circumstantial Evidence must be connected with one another, accused was implicated, on the statement of co-accused, Accused Acquitted.
Further: 2011 SCMR 1127 - mere circumstantial evidence cannot be basis for conviction. reliance on; 1992 SCMR 1047, 1996 SCMR 188, 1999 SCMR 1034, 2008 SCMR 1103
(C) Confession was not recorded according to law, the accused cannot be convicted.
Reliance on 2008 SCMR 649/ 329, 2017 SCMR 898, 1992 SCMR 196
(E) s 342 CRPC, portion of evidence which was not put in 342 CrPc, cannot be used against the accused. Accused Acquitted. Reliance on 2020 SCMR 687/ 321.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Recovery and chain of custody not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC
records.text: PLD 2026 Lah 47 (DB) u/s 342 CRPC: it was not put to the accused u/s 342, when recovery was affected, when the case property was deposited in Police Station, when was it sent for forensic, when the sample were deposited in Maal Khana, and when they were sent for further sampling in laboratory, and which PWs deposited the case property in Maal Khaana, and which PWs deposited the case property in laboratory. Appeal allowed, Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Delayed section 161 statements of related and interested witnesses
records.text:
Accussed: 2025 SCMR 1408, 2024 SCMR 1085,2008 SCMR 1556, 2006 SCMR 1217, 1993 SCMR 550-- offence u/s 302, 324 PPC: Delayed statement of PWs u/s 161 CrPc were recorded, after meeting with the police office , witnesses relative of the complainant, interested witness, previous enmity. Benefit of Doubt, Accused Acquitted.
AGAINST: 2021 PCRLJ 647 (DB) GB The witness statement of PWs recorded with delay is not fatal or detrimental for prosecution.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Dishonest improvements, weapon not sent for comparison, injured witness not examined
records.text: Accussed: 2025 SCMR 45 - 302 PPC, dishonest improvements, empties were recovered, weapon was not sent for comparison, injured witness was not medically examined, medical and ocular in conflict. Motive introduced with delay and was not proved(2025 SCMR 552). Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Time-barred jail appeal: delay of 2,511 days condoned on a plausible explanation
records.text: Accused: 2025 SCMR 744 - offence u/s 302. Time barred jail appeal, u/s 410 CRPC, jail appeal was filed with the delay of 2511 days with plausible explanation, delay was condoned, and appeal was allowed.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Distinguishing suicide from homicide on the medical signs
records.text:
Accused: 2025 SCMR 730 - Difference of Suicide and Homicide (Murder)
If there are no wounds around the neck, and eyes were closed, ribs were not fractured, and palms were not closed, it means it was suicide. If these symbols are not found, there is a murder. Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Attached property of a proclaimed offender: limitation runs from the date of knowledge
records.text: Accused: 2025 PCRLJ 93 Balochistan- offence u/s 302, 324 PPC, s. 89, 88 CRPC, Accused proclaimed offender, property attached, subsequently arrested, with the delay of 2 years, submitted application for de-attachment of the property, limitation of 2 year is from the date of knowledge, not from the date of attachment, revision allowed.

records.heading: Improvements and omissions, medical conflict, and motive attributed to a co-accused
records.text:
Accused: 2025 PCRLJ 1675 LAH
(e) Improvements and omission not reliable, reliance on 2019 SCMR 631, 2021 SCMR 810,
(f) Medical and ocular in conflict
(i) Motive attributed to co-accussed Benefit of doubt, appeal allowed, Accused Acquitted
