records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: No conviction merely for being a proclaimed offender
records.text:
Accused: 2026 SCMR 47
(A) Conviction of Absconder No one can be convicted merely on the basis of being proclaimed offender Reliance: 2026 PCRLJ 105 Lah, PLD 2008 SC 298, 2003 SCMR 611
(A)Motive not proved
(B) Pistol and Empties were sent together, recovery not reliable. Reliance 2023 SCMR 1278/ 670.
(C)Chance witnesses,
(D) General role of firing with different weapons, 8 injuries, size of entry and exit same, matter doubtful, acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Mere abscondence is not proof of guilt in a murder case
records.text:
Accused: ABSCONDANCE- offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 257, titled Laeq Shah Vs The State
Mere abscondance of the accused in murder case, is not proof of guiltiness of accused, if other evidence does not support. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: 2026 SCMR 47, 2026 PCRLJ 105 Lah, PLD 2008 SC 298, 2003 SCMR 611
Further detail on; 2026 PCRLJ 105 Lah: Offence u/s 302, 109 PPC;
A. FIR was registered with the delay of 9 hours and 25 minutes.
H. Mere on the basis of absconding, sentence cannot be upheld. Accused Acquitted.
Reliance: 2025 SCMR 888, 2010 SCMR 566, 1999 SCMR 1220.
records.title: Laeq Shah Vs The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Brother of a deceased complainant may pursue the case; dishonest improvements unreliable
records.text:
Accused: Change of Complainant: 2026 SCMR 182- Offence u/s 302 PPC
(a) After the death of the complainant, his brother was allowed to pursue the criminal case, u/s 417 CRPC. Allowed.
(b) Dishonest improvements of the PWs, to bring in line ocular evidence to medical evidence. Unreliable. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: 2008 SCMR 6, 2010 SCMR 385, 2022 PCRLJ Lah 1811, 2022 PCRLJ note 94 pg. 142, 2022 PCRLJ note 32 pg. 146.
(c)Near the place of occurrence, CCTV cameras were installed, but the prosecution did not produce CCTV footage in the court, in this way according to Art. 129 (g) QSO, best evidence was withheld. Accused Acquitted. Reliance on; 2006 SCMR 1846, 2010 SCMR 846, 2009 SCMR 230, 2024 SCMR 1146/ 1224.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Co-accused found innocent, contradictions, and post-mortem delayed by ten hours
records.text:
Accused: 2026 SCMR 60
(a) Co-accussed were found innocent during investigation, and the trial court acquitted the accused.
(b) There was a contradiction in the statement of PWs.
(c) Post-Mortem was conducted with the delay of 10 hours. It means the occurrence was unseen. Reliance on; 2020 SCMR 192, 2019 SCMR 1978/ 1068, 2018 SCMR 1549, & 2011 SCMR 1190, 2026 SCMR 1122,
(d) Co-Accussed were acquitted, hence the appellant cannot be convicted on the same evidence. Reliance, 2024 SCMR 156/ 929, 2022 SCMR 393, 2021 SCMR 612.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Unexplained delay in FIR and unnatural conduct of the witnesses
records.text:
Accused: 2026 PCRLJ Lah 105
U/S 302 PPC. Delay of 9 hours 25 minutes in registration of case, in spite of availability of the mobile, neither complainant or PWs called at 15 or Rescue 1122. Conduct of PWs in unnatural, medical and ocular evidence is in conflict. Accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Dying declaration signed by the deceased and not put to the accused under section 342
records.text: Accused: 2026 PCRLJ 134 Lah (DB-Multan) (Justice Waheed Khan) (Justice Jawad Zafar) Dying Declaration: Art. 64 QSO. There are signatures of the deceased on the dying declaration which is against the law and not admissible. Dying declaration was not put on the accused under s. 342 CrPc, magistrate was not informed regarding dying declaration. Such dying declarations cannot be exhibited under Art. 46 QSO. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: 2025 PCRLJ 311, 1997 SCMR 1011, 1996 SCMR 777, 2025 LHC 752 Titled Hafeez Ahmad Vs The State.
records.title: Hafeez Ahmad Vs The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dying Declaration
records.heading: Procedure for recording a dying declaration
records.text:
2026 MLD 65 Lah (Justice Waheed Khan)- S. 174-A CrPc Procedure of recording of dying declaration, offence u/s 302 PPC, Art. 46 QSO, Art. 21 & 25 Police Rules 1934, High Court Rule No. 8 - If some injured intends to record his dying declaration, then it is a requirement of the law that soon after it, police or medical officers be informed in this regard and they must record his statement and after this, magistrate be informed regarding this. If till the arrival of the magistrate, the injured is able to give the statement, or he is alive, then the magistrate will record his statement again.
Against: 2010 SCMR 55, 2001 SCMR 1474: SC held that above mentioned procedure is not necessary.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dying Declaration - accused
records.heading: Dying declaration without a doctor's certificate has no value
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ note 123 pg 190 Lah: certificate of doctor was not obtained, dying declaration has no value, acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Confession before the media is illegal; no conviction on chance witnesses without corroboration
records.text:
Accused: PLD 2026 SC 126 titled Shahid Ali Vs State. Offence u/ 302 PPC, Art. 39, 40 QSO, S. 164 CrPc.
(a) Confession before Media illegal
(1) Without any strong and corroborative evidence, no one can be convicted on evidence of chance witnesses.
(2) During the investigation, the accused confessed his guilt before media persons, which was played on different TV channels. The trial court awarded the death sentence which was confirmed by the High Court. The Supreme Court held that such evidence is not admissible and the accused were acquitted. Reliance: 2024 SCMR 1782, PLD 2021 SC 600.
(b) Last Seen Evidence If the accused and the deceased were seen together and soon after that, the deceased was murdered, then it can be presumed that the accused may be the actual culprit. If there is a long delay/ duration between last seen occurrence and time of death then such like last seen evidence is not reliable. Reliance on, PLD 2018 SC 813, 2000 SCMR 1784, 1997 SCMR 1416, PLD 1996 SC 305
records.title: Shahid Ali Vs State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Appeal against acquittal dismissed: doubtful timing of the FIR
records.text:
Accused: Appeal Against Acquittal, S. 417 CrPc, Dismissed. 2026 YLR 513 Lah (DB) CJ Aalia Neelum, Justice Abber Gul, titled Muhammad Arshad Vs State, offence u/s 302 PPC.
(A) Delay of 2 hours in lodging F.I.R, according to inquest report I.O after receiving the 15 call reached at the place of occurrence at 5:10 Pm, while F.I.R was registered at 7:05 PM, occurrence was stated at 5:10 PM, I.O recorded the statement of complainant after reaching at the place of occurrence, it means F.I.R was registered with deliberation and consultation. Accused Acquitted.
Reliance; 2021 SCMR 23.
(B) The witnesses who identified the dead body were not witnesses of the F.I.R, and there was a difference in the statement of witnesses, regarding firearm injuries, and the witnesses were not residents near the place of occurrence, and they did not identify the dead body, even did not explain the reason for their presence at the place of occurrence.
(C) Nil
(D) Medical evidence was in conflict with ocular evidence, the medical officer noted 11 injuries, but there was allegation of only 7 fire injuries. Accused Acquitted. Reliance on; PLD 2009 SC 53, 2008 SCMR 1103
(E) Motive not proved, empties were recovered on the day of occurrence but were sent after recovery of the pistol, in laboratory, although were matched but have no evidentiary value, and the I.O did not mention in column no. 22 and 23 of the inquest report.
(F) A pistol and 2 live bullets were allegedly shown to be recovered from the accused but bullets were not sent to the laboratory, and the accused acquitted.
Reliance: 2024 PCRLJ 617, 2016 SCMR 1605, 2018 SCMR 577.
records.title: Muhammad Arshad Vs State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Eyewitnesses did not identify the body at the post-mortem: case doubtful
records.text: Accused: 2024 SCMR 1449 titled Iftikhar Vs State. Offence u/s 302 PPC: Eye witnesses of FIR did not identify the dead body, at the time of post-mortem. Case doubtful, accused acquitted.
records.title: Iftikhar Vs State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Police opinion is not binding, but its benefit can go to the accused
records.text: Accused: Ipsi-Dixit of Police (Police Opinion)- Although police opinion is not binding on court but benefit of such opinion can be given to the accused. Accused Acquitted. 2001 YLR 674; PLD 2000 LAH 216; PLD 1994 FSC 34; 1996 MLD 1484.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Unnatural conduct of witnesses who did not help the injured
records.text: Accused: 2026 YLR 397 DI Khan (Pesh) DB titled Saqib Vs State Unnatural conduct of PWs, instead of rescuing the injured, they went to his house for information, that is unreliable. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: 2017 SCMR 2007, 2023 YLR 903, 2023 PCRLJ 17.
records.title: Saqib Vs State Unnatural conduct of PWs

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: No recovery memo of the body and no witnesses from the locality
records.text:
Accused: 2025 SCMR 762 -(b) recovery memo of dead body was not prepared, nor the people of locality were associated, only iron box in which dead body was found, its recovery memo was prepared, death sentence was awarded to the accused, in connection with murder of his wife. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: 2024 SCMR 1310/ 1507, 2017 SCMR 898
(c)Medical evidence is only corroborative piece of evidence, it describes the nature of injury, kind of weapon and seat of injury, but does not confirm, about the accused.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Inmates of the house not joined in the investigation: best evidence withheld
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC. 2024 SCMR 1310/ 1507 The inmates of the house were not associated with the investigation, it means they were not going to support the prosecution case, and best evidence was withheld, accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Night occurrence: light bulb neither seized nor checked
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC. 2026 SCMR 434 Night occurrence, neither the I.O taken into possession electric bulb, nor I.O chequeed the same whether that was in working condition or not. Case of further inquiry. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: 2025 SCMR 1599

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Conflict between medical and ocular evidence: appeal allowed
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC. 2026 PCRLJ 426 Balochistan Conflict in medical and ocular evidence, appeal allowed. Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Recovery in violation of section 103 CrPC and empties not matched
records.text:
Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC, 324 PPC, 34 PPC 2026 MLD Lah 420/ 466. Justice Sadiq Mahmood Khurram Violation of 103CrPc in recovery preceding of rifle, as private witnesses were not associated, empties were not matched. Appeal Allowed. Accused Acquitted.
Reliance: 2019 SCMR 2006, 2020 SCMR 219/ 305.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: High Court's direction to record additional evidence and decide again held illegal
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC, 423 CrPc , 428 CrPc 2026 SCMR 308. Titled: Waseem Hassan Khan Vs The State Additional Evidence - the High Court issued direction to the trial court to again record additional evidence and then to decide the case. Such direction is illegal.
records.title: Waseem Hassan Khan Vs The State Additional Evidence

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: No conviction on CCTV footage without a forensic report
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 350 Titled: Fazal Mahmood Etc. Vs The State The accused was convicted on the basis of CCTV footage, he cannot be convicted on the basis of CCTV, without a forensic report. Accused Acquitted.
records.title: Fazal Mahmood Etc. Vs The State The accused was convicted on the basis of CCTV footage

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Delayed post-mortem and rigor mortis: time of death doubtful
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 251, titled Ghulam Sarwar Vs The State Post Mortem was conducted with delay, rigor mortis had started developing after 2-4 hours of the death, and till 12 hours remain on peak. After this, rigor mortis starts to loose effect. During cross examination, doctor stated the duration between death and psot-mortem 16-18 hours, which does not support the time of occurrence according to FIR. Contradiction in statement of PWs, and unnatural conduct of the PWs. Appeal Allowed. Accused Acquitted.
records.title: Ghulam Sarwar Vs The State Post Mortem was conducted with delay

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Motive not proved: acquittal
records.text:
Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 350
Motive not proved, Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Constable who received the complaint not produced: best evidence withheld
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2019 SCMR 326, 2024 PCRLJ 1421 (DB) The constable who took the complaint was not produced as a witness, the best evidence was upheld (Art. 129 (g) QSO), case doubtful, Accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: FIR registered after a preliminary inquiry; unexplained delay in post-mortem
records.text:
Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 PCRLJ 362 Lah, titled Muhammad Riaz Vs The State, ((Justice Shehbaz Ali Rizvi, Justice Jawad Zafar)
A. Offence u/s 302 PPC, FIR was registered after preliminary inquiry, and statements of PWs were recorded prior to registration of case. B.Delay in conducting of Post-Mortem without any explanation
F. Empties were sent with delay in the laboratory. Case Doubtful, Accused Acquitted.
records.title: Muhammad Riaz Vs The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Light source not seized; hatchet and clothes not sent for DNA comparison
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 434 Bulb was not taken into possession, blood stained hatchet and blood stained clothes of the deceased were not sent for DNA comparison, case doubtful. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: 2025 SCMR 1599, 2023 SCMR 781

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Doubtful time of death, negative forensic report and delayed post-mortem
records.text:
Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2023 PCRLJ 402 Time of death doubtful, PFSA report negative, empties not matched, presence of witnesses and complainant at the time of occurrence doubtful, post-mortem conducted with delay. Accused Acquitted.
Reliance ; 2023 PCRLJ NOTE 43, 2017 YLR 1189, PLD 2009 SC 64, 2023 YLR 24 LAH, 2021 SCMR 736, 2015 PCRLJ Pesh 1123

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: A single ground of doubt is sufficient for acquittal
records.text:
Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2023 SCMR 241 Benefit of doubt, only one ground of doubt is sufficient to acquit the accused.
Reliance ; 2022 PCRLJ 173, PLD 2009 SC 64, 2021 PCRLJ 449(B)(DB), 2021 YLR 1745
(DB), 2012 SCMR 327, 2019 SCMR 129/64/1306, 2014 SCMR 1698

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Medical evidence in conflict with ocular evidence: benefit of doubt
records.text:
Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2022 SCMR 393 Medical evidence is in conflict with ocular, benefit of doubt, accused acquitted.
Reliance: 2019 SCMR 1306/129/1150/1308 , 2021 YLR 1745-DB, 2021 PCRLJ 449, 2019 SCMR 64, 2021 YLR 1745, 2014 SCMR 1698, 2021 SCMR 736

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Delay in post-mortem: authorities by length of delay
records.text:
Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2022 PCRLJ Note 96 Lah Delay in Post-Mortem. Accused Acquitted.
1. Delay of 9 hours: 2022 YLR 424, 1995 SCMR 610, 2017 SCMR 54/1115
2. Delay of 6 hours: 2022 PCRLJ 109, 2011 SCMR 323/1190
3. Delay of 12 hours: 2021 PCRLJ 449, 2017 SCMR 486
4. Delay of 33 hours and 25 mins: 2022 PCRLJ Lah 1852

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Source of light neither mentioned nor seized: case doubtful
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2021 SCMR 736 Source of light not mentioned, nor taken into possession, case doubtful. Accused Acquitted. Reliance: PLD 2020 SC 523, 2020 YLR 589 Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2022 PCRLJ 705 Sindh- De Novo Trial : trial of two accused started, evidence recorded in the meanwhile third accused was arrested and charge was amended, on relying previous evidence, all the three accused were convicted, according to law, evidence was again to be recorded by the trial court. Case Remanded in revision petition and trial again started. Powers of revision, under 439 CrPc.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive
records.heading: Motive not proved and no DNA test: acquittal
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - Motive 2023 YLR note 17, 2025 SCMR 1339 Titled Khizar Hayat Vs State Motive not proved. DNA was not conducted, acquitted.
records.title: Khizar Hayat Vs State Motive not proved

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Co-accused acquitted on the same evidence: appellant also acquitted
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2022 PCRLJ Lah 1811 Co-accussed acquitted on the same set of evidence, evidence cannot be believed up to the extent of the appellant, appeal allowed, accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Empties and pistol sent together for comparison: recovery unbelievable
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC 2023 SCMR 670, 2022 PCRLJ Lah 591 Crime empties and pistols were sent together for comparison in PFSA, recovery unbelievable, accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Benefit of doubt in a murder case
records.text: Accussed: offence u/s 302 PPC 2023 PC RLJ 781 Benefit of doubt.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Scaled site plan in conflict with medical evidence on firing distance
records.text: Accussed: offence u/s 302 PPC 2022 PCRLJ Lah 891 Scaled site plan and medical evidence in conflict, according to scaled site plan, accused were shown at the distance of 5, 6 and 8 Qarams(1 Qaram= 5.5 Ft.) , while according to post-mortem report, there was a blackening, which can only be caused at the distance 6-12 inches(4 ft.). Accused Acquitted. Reliance: 2011 SCMR 323, 2015 PCRLJ 111.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured witness
records.heading: An injury alone does not prove a witness's presence at the scene
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - Injured witness 2022 PCRLJ 1260 Mere on the basis of injured witness, does not prove that he was present at the place of occurrence, if other evidence does not support the prosecution. Accused Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must be appraised with great care and caution
records.text: Accussed Side: Offence u/s 302, 276 PPC - 2025 SCMR 1399 - although Conviction can be awarded on the basis of Circumstantial evidence, but it should be appreciated with great care and caution. Acquitted. Reliance: 2013 SCMR 374.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: No simultaneous conviction under sections 302 and 201 PPC
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC, 201 PPC 2015 SCMR 993 - Accused cannot be convicted at the same time u/s 302 & 201 PPC.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery weapon of offence
records.heading: Complainant as recovery witness of the weapon: recovery loses its sanctity
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - Recovery weapon of offence 1993 SCJ 568- in murder case, complainant is recovery witness of weapon of offence, looses its sanctity, and evidence is not admissable, accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Self cross-examination by the accused not accepted
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - 2010 PCRLJ 812 (a) - Self cross of accused not accepted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Cross-Version Cases
records.heading: FIR and cross-version cases are to be tried and decided together
records.text: PLD 2016 SC 70 F.I.R and cross-version cases would be tried and decided simultaneously.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Deceased entered the accused's house with bad intention: section 302(c), not 302(b)
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - 2021 MLD 362 - If deceased entered into the house of the accused with bad intention and resultantly he is murdered, then the accused will be convicted under section 302-C instead of 302-B PPC.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Acquittal under section 265-K CrPC is possible even after charge and evidence
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - 2026 PCrLJ 152 - Even after framing of charge and recording of the statement of witnesses, the court has the power to acquit the accused under section 265-K CrPC in an offence under Section 302-B PPC.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Age Determination
records.heading: No ossification test needed where a birth certificate exists
records.text: 2025 PCrLJ 482 / PLJ 2024 CrC 1175 - In presence of a birth certificate of the accused, there is no need for an ossification test.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in FIR
records.heading: Prosecution must explain delay in the FIR
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - DELAY IN FIR 2026 YLR 266 - F.I.R was registered with delay. Prosecution is duty-bound to explain such delay. Accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Accused Conduct
records.heading: Conduct of the accused: case doubtful
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - ACCUSED CONDUCT 2026 PCrLJ 134 - Unnatural conduct of the accused is doubtful. Acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence
records.heading: Last-seen witnesses introduced with delay: case doubtful
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - LAST SEEN EVIDENCE 2026 SCMR 621 - Witnesses of last seen evidence introduced with delay, contradiction in statements, matter doubtful, accused acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Site Plan
records.heading: Site plan that does not tally with the witnesses makes the case doubtful
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - SITE PLAN 2026 SCMR 798 - If the site plan does not tally with the statement of witnesses, the case becomes doubtful and the accused becomes acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Statement
records.heading: Delayed statement of a prosecution witness has no value
records.text: Accused: offence u/s 302 PPC - DELAYED STATEMENT 2023 SCMR 1140 - Statement of a prosecution witness recorded with delay has no value, and the accused will be acquitted.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence appraised with caution; sentence maintained
records.text: Complainant side: 2013 SCMR 274 - Death sentence awarded by trial court, and confirmed by High Court, circumstantial evidence is required to read and appreciate with great caution and care. Partial appeal allowed, but sentence maintained.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Motive not proved: death sentence reduced to life imprisonment
records.text: Complainant side: 2025 SCMR 74 -Motive not proved, conviction maintained, however, on the basis of mitigation, death sentence converted into life imprisonment.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Husband's conduct after wife's murder: conviction upheld, death reduced to life
records.text: Complainant side: 2025 SCMR 1591 - Accused was under allegation of being the murderer of his wife, did not attend funeral, remained missing for 37 days, and did not report the incident to the police. Death Sentence, converted to life imprisonment. Conviction Upheld. reliance on 2015 SCMR 710, 2005 SCMR 1524, 2017 SCMR 724, PLD 2017 SC 681.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Appeal against acquittal under section 417 CrPC allowed
records.text: Complainant side: 2025 SCMR 562 Appeal against acquittal u/s 417 CRPC, appeal allowed. Offence 324, 337 (d).

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Minor contradictions are natural and do not benefit the accused
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 PCRLJ 93 SC AJ&K- Minor contradictions are natural and benefits cannot be given to the accused. Conviction upheld. Reliance: 2025 SCMR pg. 1368/1360 titled Iftikhar Kiyani Urf Khara Vs The State
records.title: Iftikhar Kiyani Urf Khara Vs The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Related witnesses cannot be discarded merely for their relationship
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 466 - Accused nominated in FIR, all the witnesses corroborated the occurrence, merely on the basis of relationship with the complainant, their evidence cannot be rebutted. Single fire, but there is no chance of substitution. Conviction Upheld.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Accused nominated and medical evidence in line with ocular: conviction upheld
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 PCRLJ HC AJ&K 563 - accused nominated in FIR, medical evidence in line of ocular, conviction upheld. Appeal dismissed.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: A single fire shot is not a mitigating circumstance
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 205 titled Muhammad Kamran Vs The State Accused nominated in FIR, medical evidence in line with ocular, single fire does not fall in mitigation, appeal dismissed. Conviction Upheld. Reliance: 2005 SCMR 427
records.title: Muhammad Kamran Vs The State Accused nominated in FIR

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Minor conflict between medical and ocular evidence does not upset the conviction
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 317 Titled Muhammad Ali Vs The State Minor contradiction, in medical and occular evidence, post-mortem was conducted with delay. And it was impossible for the PWs to give photo-picture evidence regarding injuries. Conviction Upheld. Appeal Dismissed. Reliance: 2003 SCMR 522; 2017 SCMR 54 , 2018 SCMR 326
records.title: Muhammad Ali Vs The State Minor contradiction

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Motive not proved: death sentence reduced to life imprisonment
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 365 Motive not proved, death sentence converted into life imprisonment. Conviction Upheld.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Parties known to each other and prompt FIR: conviction upheld
records.text:
Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC 2026 SCMR 333/ 262
Occurrence of murder took place after sunset, accused and complainants are previously known to each other, prompt registration of FIR. Conviction upheld, appeal dismissed.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Daylight occurrence, prompt FIR and matching forensic report: death sentence upheld
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 2025 SCMR 445/205 titled Muhammad Raees vs The State Daylight occurrence, prompt FIR, medical in line with ocular evidence, forensic report matched, death sentence upheld.
records.title: Muhammad Raees vs The State Daylight occurrence

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: No identification parade needed where the accused is clearly visible on CCTV
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 2026 YLR 564 The accused was visible in CCTV camera footage clearly, no need to hold an identification parade(Art. 22 QSO) . Conviction upheld.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Juvenile claim: school and late-entered birth certificates are unreliable
records.text:
Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC Declaration of Juvenile under Juvenile Justice System 2018 2009 SCMR 1073 Titled Muhammad Anwar Vs Muhammad Sufyan Etc.
(a) School certificates regarding proof of birth are not reliable.
(B) Birth certificate was entered with a delay, is not reliable. The opinion of the medical board will be preferred. s.8 Juvenile Justice System, opinion of the medical board will be preferred on the documents.
Reliance: 2025 MLD Lah 367 Tilted Kamran Mushtaq Vs The State (J. Amjad Rafiq), PLD 2020 SC 356, 2017 SCMR 633, 2018 YLR 1605, 2003 YLR 315, PLD 2004 SC 758, PLD 2024 SC 843, PLD 2022 SC 551, 2002 SCMR 446, 2012 SCMR 1400.
records.title: Muhammad Anwar Vs Muhammad Sufyan Etc

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Doctor describing the injury as superficial does not affect the case
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PPC PLJ 1983 CRC Lah 84 It does not affect anything, if the doctor declares the injury as superficial.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Diyat is assessed at the rate prevailing at the time of decision
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PLJ 2010 SC 231 - Diyat (Blood money) will be ascertained according to the schedule at the time of decision, and not according to that of the time of occurrence.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: A close relative may pursue the murder case after the complainant's death
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 2026 SCMR 182 - In case of death of a complainant, a close relative of the complainant, especially an injured or eyewitness, can pursue the murder case.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Medical board may be constituted 21 days after the first examination
records.text: Complainant side: 2026 YLR 208 Lahore - Medical board can be constituted after 21 days of the first medical examination.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested Witness
records.heading: A related witness is not necessarily an interested witness
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 - INTERESTED WITNESS 2026 PCrLJ 344 - Mere relative witness does not fall in the category of interested witness. Sentence maintained.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Contradictions in evidence
records.heading: Minor contradictions are natural
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 - Contradictions in evidence 2026 PCrLJ 93 Minor contradictions are natural. The court would not like an overly tutored prosecution witness. Conviction upheld.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Juvenile
records.heading: Life imprisonment for a juvenile upheld
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302- Juvenile 2022 MLD 915 Pesh (Musarat Hilali J.)& 2026 YLR 901 LHC Life imprisonment for juvenile upheld

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Minor discrepancies; ocular and medical evidence in conformity
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 2026 SCMR 317 - Minor discrepancies, ocular and medical in conformity, appeal against conviction dismissed.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: CCTV footage confirmed by forensic analysis: death sentence maintained
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 PLD 2026 SC 251 (Noor Muqadam Case) CCTV footage was submitted to forensic for analysis, report of PFSA confirmed the presence of accused in CCTV. No motive was set by the complainant. Death Sentence Maintained.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Facts discovered on the accused's disclosure are admissible
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 2026 YLR 1044 LHC Recovery of new facts on the disclosure of the accused are admissible and can be used against the accused.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Matching recoveries support the prosecution; related witnesses with natural presence are reliable
records.text:
Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 2026 MLD 649 LHC, 2026 PCRLJ 344 BALOCHISTAN
- Recovery of crime weapon, blood stained earth and clothes matched PFSA, support prosecution case.
- Interested/relative witnesses are reliable witnesses if their presence at the place of occurrence was natural and in this situation, evidence cannot be discarded.
- If ocular account narrate the complete story in line and other evidence corroborate the same, even despite of lengthy cross examination, it will be presumed that prosecution proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Recovery of the weapon of offence is not necessary
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 2011 SCMR 872 Recovery of weapon of offence is not necessary. Sentence maintained.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.heading: Delay in recording witness statements is not fatal to the prosecution
records.text: Complainant side: Offence u/s 302 2021 PCRLJ 647 (DB) GB The witness statement of PWs recorded with delay is not fatal or detrimental for prosecution.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.heading: Rape: father's evidence of the victim's account to him is admissible
records.text: Complainant: PLD 2026 Bal 16 Art 19 QSO Victim stated the occurance of rape to her father and her father appeared as PW in the court. Evidence of her father is admissible according to Law. Conviction maintained, appeal dismissed. Reliance; 2024 PCRLJ 1048/ 1783/ 1881, 2024 MLD 1073, PLD 2020 SC 295, 2022 SCMR 544.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.heading: Rape charge: conviction under section 496-B PPC where the relations were consensual
records.text: PLD 2026 SC 187 - If in a rape case forcible element is not proved and it is established that the victim and accused were having relations with consent, then under section 238(2) CrPC court can award the sentence to the accused under section 496B PPC instead of section 376 PPC.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.heading: Rape allegation doubtful: 18 days with the accused without complaint, no violence, no DNA
records.text: 2026 SCMR 393 - Allegation of rape. The victim remained with the accused for a period of 18 days at different places with the accused but she did not make any hue and cry to seek the help of the public. There was no mark of violence on the body of the victim, no DNA was conducted, and no CDR was available on record. Allegation of abduction and rape doubtful. The accused was acquitted.

records.subject: Family Law
records.heading: Wife entitled to maintenance after nikah even without rukhsati
records.text: 2026 SCMR 1 - Maintenance: After Nikkah, Rukshati did not take place, but wife is entitled for the maintenance

records.subject: Family Law
records.heading: Family court may grant relief not claimed; maintenance according to the husband's means
records.text:
2026 CLC 474 ISB
(C) to protect the rights of the parties, the court can award the relief which was not sought in the suit.
(D) Maintenance: Suit for maintenance can be decreed according to the economical status of the Defendant. Suit for dissolution of marriage on basis of khula decreed, dowry articles returned.

records.subject: Family Law
records.heading: Present market value may be decreed where the gold cannot be returned
records.text: 2026 SCMR 494: If the actual gold cannot be returned then its present market value could be decreed.

records.subject: Family Law
records.heading: Dissolution sought on another ground cannot be decreed as khula
records.text: PLD 2026 SC 91 -Dissolution of Marriage The lady filed suit for dissolution of marriage, as she wants to carry her education abroad, but the trial court decreed for dissolution of marriage on the basis of khula, which is illegal. Order Recalled, suit decreed only up to the extent of dissolution of marriage.

records.subject: Family Law
records.heading: Claim for a daughter's marriage expenses dismissed
records.text: PLD 2026 SC 122 - Suit for Maintenance & expenses for marriage of her daughter. Suit up to the extent of the daughter's marriage expense was dismissed.

records.subject: Family Law
records.heading: Marriage during iddat is irregular
records.text: PLD 2021 BALOCHISTAN 28 - Marriage during the period of iddat falls in the category of irregular marriage, but it is not against shariah. Reliance: 1992 SCMR 1273 titled Abida Khanum Vs Sarfraz.
records.title: Abida Khanum Vs Sarfraz

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Succession Certificate under Succession Act s. 372, 373
records.heading: Succession certificate proceedings are summary and do not determine rights
records.text: This is summary procedure, and rights cannot be determined through it, and civil court has power to hear the proceeding. Reliance: 2015 CLC 1719, PLD 2015 Isb 30, PLD 2011 Lah 192,

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Child Marriage Restraint Act
records.heading: Child Marriage Restraint Act offence is non-cognizable; no FIR
records.text: 2026 MLD 525 - Violation of Child Marriage Restraint Act is a non-cognizable offence; F.I.R cannot be registered. Even a Justice of Peace cannot issue directions for registration of cases. Only on the complaint of the union council can the family court proceed.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Right of Maintenance
records.heading: Daughter's suit for maintenance after the age of 19
records.text: PLJ 2006 SC 449- Daughter after attaining the age of 19 years cannot file a suit for maintenance.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Guardian and Wards
records.heading: Mother's second marriage: father entitled to custody of the minor girl
records.text: 2018 CLC 453- If the mother contracts a second marriage, then the father who is a natural guardian would be entitled to the custody of the minor girl.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Divorce
records.heading: Imposing conditions on the husband's right of divorce is illegal
records.text: 2024 CLC 2129- To impose conditions in case of divorce on the husband is illegal.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: DNA | Adoption
records.heading: Only the adoptive parent can challenge the parentage he recorded
records.text: PLD 2019 SC 449- If the person adopted a child and got entered his own parentage in the documents, then only that person can amend or challenge the documents. No other person is competent to challenge his parentage or the conduction of DNA.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961
records.heading: Second marriage and polygamy fall outside the family court's jurisdiction
records.text: 2025 CLC 863 & 2024 MLD 786- In case of second marriage, polygamy does not fall under the jurisdiction of the family court; the matter would be trialed by the criminal court only. Under Section 6 Family Law, second marriage without permission is no offence.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Iddat
records.heading: No iddat where only nikah was solemnised without rukhsati
records.text: PLD 1996 Lahore 65- If rukhsati did not take place and only nikkah was solemnized, then there is no period of iddat.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Articles | Limitation
records.heading: Dowry and maintenance suit filed six years after the husband's death dismissed as time-barred
records.text: 2025 CLC 1030- Wife filed a suit for recovery of dowry articles and a suit for maintenance mentioned in column no. 17 after 6 years of the death of her husband, so it was dismissed. Suit can be filed only within 3 years.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikkah Registration | MFLO 1961
records.heading: Nikah registrar must fill in every column of the nikahnama
records.text:
PLD 2026 SC 20- Nikkah registrar is duty-bound to fill all the columns of Nikkah Nama according to the amendment in Muslim Family Law Ordinance 1961 in the
year 2015. If the Nikkah registrar does not fill all the columns of Nikkah Nama, then penal proceedings can be initiated against him.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikkah Nama
records.heading: A registered nikahnama is sufficient proof
records.text: 2025 SCMR 1454- Registered Nikkah Nama is sufficient to prove the case; no need to produce further witnesses.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance and Marriage Expenditure
records.heading: Maintenance and a daughter's marriage expenses are distinct claims
records.text: PLD 2026 SC 122- Suit for maintenance and suit for recovery of marriage expenditure of the daughter are two different nature cases. Suit for maintenance is maintainable, but until unless the date of marriage of the daughter is not fixed and the father does not refuse to pay marriage expenditure, she cannot file the suit; this is premature.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Ex-Parte Decree
records.heading: Ex parte decree upheld where notice went to the address in the nikahnama
records.text: 2010 SCMR 1840- Wife filed a suit and sent notices to the address of the husband written in Nikkah Nama. Suit was ex-parte decreed. No excuse regarding receiving of notices. Application to set aside the ex-parte decree was dismissed.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula | Dower (Haq-Ul-Mehar)
records.heading: Khula: wife must return the dower whether or not rukhsati took place
records.text: 2026 SCMR 561- Wife filed a suit for dissolution of marriage on the basis of khula. Whether rukhsati took place or not, in both cases the wife is duty-bound to return Haq-ul-Mehar.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance
records.heading: No maintenance where the wife fails to prove she was turned out or deserted
records.text: 2016 CLC 932 - If the wife fails to prove that she was forcibly ousted or deserted from her house by the husband, then she is not entitled to maintenance.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Guardian and Wards | Custody of Minor
records.heading: Parents who hand over custody by consent lose the right of custody
records.text: PLJ 2026 Lahore 43 - If real parents with their consent handed over the custody of their minor child, they lose the right of custody.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dual Nikkah Nama
records.heading: Two claimants to nikah: the girl goes with the one she acknowledges
records.text: 2018 SCMR 747- There are two claimants of Nikkah. The girl should be sent to the person whom she claimed Nikkah instead of sending her to Dar-ul-Aman, and the family court will decide about the dispute of Nikkah Namas.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Law | Cross-Examination
records.heading: Family court may restore a closed right of cross-examination
records.text: 2012 CLC 292 - Family court after closing the right of cross-examination of a party recalled it by providing again the right of cross-examination.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Parents
records.heading: Disabled parents can sue their sons for maintenance
records.text: PLD 2026 Lahore 181 - Disabled parents can file the suit for maintenance against their sons.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Articles
records.heading: Dowry articles: receipts need not be proved
records.text: 2017 CLJ 121 - Every parent according to his status gives dowry articles to their daughter, and there is no need to prove receipts of articles; suit decreed.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance | Bait-Ul-Maal
records.heading: Bait-ul-Maal may be ordered to pay maintenance where the father cannot
records.text: 2014 SCMR 481- If the father is financially weak and is unable to pay the maintenance to the children, then the court can issue an order to the Bait-ul-Maal to pay the maintenance to the children.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Guardian and Wards | Jurisdiction
records.heading: Guardian petition: where the mother may file
records.text: PLD 2012 SC 66 - Mother can file a guardian petition in the court where the child is living permanently with his father or in the court from whose jurisdiction the mother was deprived.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Limitation
records.heading: Suit for dowry articles and gold ornaments: limitation is three years
records.text: 2016 CLC 313 - the limitation for Suit of recovery of dowry article and gold ornaments is 3 years.

records.subject: Election Appeal
records.heading: Election appeal: authorities

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.heading: Illegal Dispossession Act does not apply against a co-sharer
records.text: Accused: Illegal disposition act does not apply against co-sharer. Appeal against acquittal dismissed. 2025 SCMR 787, 2016 SCMR 1931, PLD 2024 SC 1152, 2003 SCMR 477

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.heading: Illegal Dispossession Act: accused has a right of appeal against conviction or fine
records.text: 2022 PCRLJ 1828 Lah- Under s.8(a) of the act, in case of conviction or fine, right of appeal has been given to the accused.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings under Order VI Rule 17 CPC has a wide scope
records.text:
2026 CLC 458 RWP (Justice Jawad Hassan) Order 6, Rule 17 CPC- there is a wide scope regarding permission to amend the suit. Writ Petition allowed.
Reliance: 2018 SCMR 82, 2016 SCMR 1621, 2008 SCMR 1682

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.heading: Blocking of an identity card on a civil court decree is illegal
records.text: 2026 CLC 496 SINDH: Blockage of ID Card in result of degree of civil court - Order Illegal, Writ Allowed. Reliance: 2024 CLC 1068; PLD 2000 LAH 290, PLD 2021 ISB 305.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.heading: Specific performance: the beneficiary must prove the agreement through marginal witnesses
records.text: 2026 CLC 520 Lah (Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad): Specific suit for performance- the beneficiary party is under obligation to prove its case and marginal witnesses are necessary to prove the suit. Civil Revision Allowed.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.heading: An agreement to sell alone does not confer ownership
records.text: 2026 CLC 463 SINDH: Only on the basis of agreement to sell, no one can claim or consider as an owner of the property.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Order 37: Suit for recovery on basis of Cheque
records.heading: Order XXXVII suit on a cheque said to be issued as security
records.text: 2026 MLD 409 Lah (Justice Anwar Hussein) There was business dealing between plaintiff and defendant, cheque was issued as a security, which was the liability of the defendant to prove it. Suit dismissed. Appeal Allowed.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.heading: Ex parte decree passed without proper procedure set aside
records.text: 2021 MLD 67 Isb Setting aside ex-parte proceeding- s. 151 CPC, Order 9 Rule 13 : The trial court, without adopting coercion measures/ proper procedure, passed an ex-parte decree, which was assailed by the defendant, and an application for setting aside ex-parte proceeding was allowed.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Contract Act - Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Agreement to sell is doubtful without full particulars of the witnesses
records.text: PLD 2026 SC 42 - Particulars of witnesses necessary ID card no, name, parentage, and complete address of the witness is necessary. Without the above-mentioned details, the agreement to sell is doubtful.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Law of Inheritance
records.heading: Issueless deceased: children of predeceased siblings do not inherit
records.text: 2026 MLD 807 Balochistan - Person died issueless; his brothers and sisters are alive. If some brothers and sisters died prior to the death of the said person, property would not be given as a right of inheritance to the children of already dead brothers and sisters under Section 4.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Pleadings may be amended at any stage if the nature of the case is unchanged
records.text: 2026 CLC 458- Court can allow to amend the suit and written statement at any stage if the category of the case is not changed.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summoning of Witnesses
records.heading: A necessary witness may be summoned although not named in the list of witnesses
records.text: 2016 CLC Note 127 - No party can be deprived to produce the witnesses whose evidence is necessary for the decision of the case on the ground that their names are not included in the list. Court can summon the witnesses under Section 14 CPC and Order 16 Rule 2.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Decree - Civil Prison
records.heading: Civil prison in execution is a coercive measure, not a conviction
records.text: 2026 SCMR 521 - After decretal of civil suits, in result of execution if someone is sent to civil prison, then it would not fall in the category of conviction. Only conviction is in criminal cases, but in civil cases, it amounts to coercive measures for the satisfaction of the decree.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution Court | CNIC Blocking
records.heading: Executing court cannot block the judgment debtor's CNIC in a money decree
records.text: PLD 2026 SC 280- In money decree cases, the executing court has no power under Section 51-E of CPC to block the CNIC of the judgment debtor. No citizen can be deprived of his identity.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Necessary Party
records.heading: Relief cannot be refused merely for non-joinder of a necessary party
records.text: 2017 CLC 495- Court cannot refuse to give relief to the plaintiff on the ground that he has not impleaded the necessary party in the suit. No one should be knocked out on the basis of technicalities.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Gift (Hiba)
records.heading: Gift of the whole property to sons to deprive daughters is illegal
records.text: 2026 SCMR 587 - If parents, by depriving their daughters, alienate the whole property in the name of their sons, such like Hiba/gift is illegal.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Injunction (Stay)
records.heading: A party who concealed earlier suits is not entitled to an injunction
records.text: 2019 YLR 815 - The party who concealed previous suits is not entitled to get stay.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Lis Pendens
records.heading: A purchaser during the suit may be joined as a party
records.text: 2026 CLC 109 - During the proceeding of the suit, the purchaser of the property can also become a party in a suit, and lis pendens cannot apply.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC
records.heading: Decree obtained by fraud or without jurisdiction: remedy is section 12(2) CPC, not a fresh suit
records.text: 2010 SCMR 1097 / PLD 2007 Peshawar 66 - If the decree was passed on the basis of forgery, fraud, misrepresentation, and want of jurisdiction, that decree can be challenged under Section 12(2) CPC. No independent suit would be filed.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit for Possession | Co-Owner
records.heading: No suit for possession against a co-owner; the remedy is partition
records.text: 2019 SCMR 84 - Against a co-owner, a suit for possession cannot be filed; only a partition application would be filed against them.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revenue Law | Jurisdiction
records.heading: Orders of revenue officers cannot be challenged directly in the civil court
records.text: PLD 2026 26- Order of revenue officers would not be challenged directly in civil court, but that can be challenged in High Court.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revenue Law | Partition
records.heading: Revenue authorities may partition a joint khewat partly used for residence
records.text: 2026 CLC 684 - In joint khewat, if some portion of the property is still in the use for agriculture purposes, then revenue authorities have power for its partition, although some of the portion of said land is being used for residential purposes.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Value of Paid Utility Bills & Tax Reciepts
records.heading: Paid utility bills and tax receipts do not prove ownership
records.text: 2013 MLD 1818 -Mere on the basis of paid utility bills and tax receipts no one can be held as owner of the said property.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.heading: A wrongly filed appeal can be converted into a revision
records.text: NLR 2004 Civil 177, 2007 SCMR 866- Conversion of Appeal into revision allowed. Wrongly filed appeal can be converted into revision.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.heading: Civil procedure: authorities (entry incomplete)
records.text: 2007 CLC 1413 Lah, 2010 CLC 1438 Lah - Court can

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.heading: Revenue court cannot cancel old mutations
records.text: 2026 CLC 407: Old Mutations cannot be cancelled by the revenue court.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.heading: Concurrent findings of the courts below are not to be interfered with lightly
records.text: 2026 SCMR 31- Concurrent findings of the courts below cannot be interfered straight away. Order Set Aside.

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.heading: Passport Control List: stopping a previously deported traveller at the airport held illegal
records.text: Petitioner was deported from Iran some time ago, was travelling again for Oman, but he was restrained at Airport on the pretext that his name is existing in PCL. Writ Allowed, act of airport authority is illegal. PLD 2026 ISB 15 (Muhammad Iqbal Vs Federation of Pakistan)

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.heading: Travel cannot be restricted for alleged illegal travel without a show-cause notice
records.text: Rule 21 & 22: Allegation of illegal travelling without giving show cause notice, movement of any person/ citizen, cannot be curtailed. Writ Allowed. 2026 MLD 125 Bal (DB ) Titled: Laal Baksh vs Federation of Pakistan. Reliance: 2017 SCMR 1179, 2018 MLD 579.
records.title: Laal Baksh vs Federation of Pakistan

records.subject: DNA Test
records.heading: DNA test application made directly to the trial court without first applying during investigation
records.text:
2026 MLD 182 Sindh: S. 265 (f) (7), S. 94, S. 540, S. 510 and 561 (a) CrPc Accused neither submitted application during Investigation to I.O, nor Submitted application in the court of Area Magistrate, for DNA. He directly filed an application in the trial court which was dismissed and he assailed the order through revision petition, which was also dismissed by the High Court. Reliance: PLD 2019 SC 669.
AGAINST: 2015 YLR 1776, PLD 2012 FSC 114, 2017 MLD 1611

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Exhumation | DNA
records.heading: Exhumation is to determine the cause of death, not to take a DNA sample
records.text: PLD 2014 Balochistan 50 - Exhumation cannot be done for the purpose of taking a sample for DNA. The only purpose of exhumation is to determine whether the death of the person was natural or unnatural.

records.subject: Character Certificate
records.heading: Acquitted accused: criminal record to be removed from the police character certificate
records.text: PLD 2026 Lah 84 (Justice Abber Gul) AbdulRehman Vs GOP Offence of Kite flying- Accussed was acquitted u/s 249-A CrPc, head of the police was directed to exclude the criminal record of the accused from police character certificate. Writ Allowed. Reliance: PLD 2023 Lah 512, PLD 2025 Pesh 67

records.subject: Service Matters
records.heading: No dismissal from service without a regular inquiry and a hearing
records.text: 2026 SCMR 576: without regular inquiry and without giving the opportunity of hearing to the public servant, cannot be dismissed from service. Reliance: 2023 SCMR 1135/ 603.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Appeal | Limitation
records.heading: Service appeal filed in the wrong forum and returned is not time-barred
records.text: 2025 SCMR 64- If a public servant filed an appeal on the wrong forum and the case is returned to file at the proper forum, the appeal would not be considered as a time-barred appeal.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Constitutional Law
records.heading: Right to a fair trial under Article 10-A extends to every public servant
records.text: 2026 SCMR 692 - Article 10A Constitution of Pakistan 1973, right of fair trial is the right of every public servant.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Promotion
records.heading: Promotion is governed by the rules in force when the civil servant became eligible
records.text: 2026 SCMR 558 - If the public servant is eligible for promotion and ultimately the department adjourns the proceeding and amends the laws (such like amendments in the way of promotion), he will be promoted according to laws which were applicable at the time of his eligibility.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension
records.heading: Limitation does not apply to pension matters
records.text: PLJ 2026 SC 254 - Law of limitation would not apply to pension matters.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Contract Employees
records.heading: A contract employee has no right to confirmation in service
records.text: 2021 SCMR 977- Khushal Khan Khattak University Vs. Jibran Ali Etc. Contract employee cannot claim as a matter of right for his confirmation in service.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Promotion
records.heading: Once promoted, rightly or wrongly, a civil servant cannot be reverted
records.text: 2020 PCRLJ CS 352, 2018 PLC CS 292 (locus potentia) - Once rightly or wrongly promoted, cannot be reverted.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.heading: FIA has no authority to block or freeze a citizen's bank account
records.text: PLD 2026 ISB 63 (DB) (ICA) FIA has no authority to block or freeze the bank account of any citizen.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Anti-Corruption
records.heading: Special Judge Anti-Corruption cannot suspend a public servant
records.text: 2026 PCrLJ 1- Special judge anti-corruption has no power to suspend any public servant.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.heading: Narcotics hidden in a truck: passenger may have had no knowledge; bail allowed
records.text: Accused: Post Arrest Bail offence CNSA 2026 SCMR 217 15 Kg Chars (Hash) and Ice (meth) was recovered from the secret cavities of the truck. Petitioner was travelling in that truck, there is a possibility that he has no knowledge about narcotics. Bail Allowed.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.heading: Narcotics trial: application for call data records of police witnesses who used phones at the scene
records.text:
Accused-Trial offence CNSA 2022 PCRLJ LAH 59-DB (J. Sohail Nasir & J. Ali Zia Bajwa) During cross-examination police officials-PWs admitted that they were using the mobile phones at the time of occurrence, and the accused submitted an application in the trial court for summoning of CDR of PWs, which was dismissed. Accused Assailed the order in revision petition in high court, which was allowed and trial court was directed to summon the CDR of police officials.
Reliance: PLD 2014 SC 232, PLD 2021 SC 600, PLD 2020 SC 334.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.heading: Narcotics: failure to prove safe custody of the case property leads to acquittal
records.text: 2026 YLR 1058, PLJ 2026 Cr.C. 83. Crl. Appeal 55608/23-Shafqat Iqbal alias Bilalu Vs The State etc. By now it is also well settled that if safe custody of allegedly recovered substance or parcel of sample/case property has not been proved then, there is no need to discuss other merits of the case and it straightaway leads to the acquittal of the accused.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.heading: Section 9(c) CNSA: an independent private witness is necessary
records.text: Accused-Trial offence CNSA 2025 SCMR 1657 It is necessary to produce an independent private witness in trial under Section 9C CNSA 1997. No one can be convicted on the basis of evidence of police officials or spy informations.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Medical Jurisprudence (Modi) page 535 - Firearm range
records.heading: Range and velocity of a 12-bore gun
records.text: Generally the range of a 12 bore gun is 30-40 yards, sometimes it can go up to 200 yards as well. Low velocity up to 1200 feet. medium velocity 1200-2500 feet, and high velocity 3500 feet.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Sections of CRPC relative to Fard E Jurm & High Court Rules
records.heading: Framing of charge: relevant sections of the CrPC
records.text: 241, 241-A CrPc., 242, 221-223/ 7(C), 221 (7), Previously convicted- 245(a) CrPc.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Police Powers
records.heading: Police have no power to interfere in citizens' business matters
records.text: 2009 PCrLJ 290 - The police have no power to interfere in the business matters of citizens.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Police Powers
records.heading: Police cannot register cases against couples found in hotels
records.text: 2024 PCrLJ 1972 - Police cannot register the case against the couples from the hotels.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Dispute Resolution Council (DRC)
records.heading: Forcible dispossession by a Dispute Resolution Council is illegal
records.text: PLJ 2026 Lahore 16- Forceful dispossession of any person by the DRC is illegal. All the proceedings must be according to Sections 16 and 17.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: NADRA Ordinance | CNIC Cancellation
records.heading: NADRA will not cancel a CNIC once issued
records.text: 2025 CLC 558 - Once NADRA issued CNIC, then NADRA will not cancel the same.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Relevant sections to Contempt of Court
records.heading: Contempt of court: relevant provisions
records.text: Art. 204 Cons. 1973, s. 480, s. 175, s. 178, s. 179, s. 180, s. 228, s.482 CrPc., & s. 3& 4 of Contempt of Court Act 1976.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Lodging in Dar Ul Aman
records.heading: A woman cannot be lodged in Dar-ul-Aman indefinitely
records.text: 1998 PCRLJ 1675 Lady cannot be lodged in Dar Ul Aman for indefinite period, she should be produced 1 or 2 months a month in court.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail
records.heading: Cancellation of bail: when bail may be recalled
records.text: Cancellation of bail in appellate jurisdiction: bail may be recalled where the accused misuses the concession (tampering with evidence, influencing or threatening witnesses, a fresh offence, breach of bail conditions, non-appearance without cause) or where new facts change the basis of the grant. Otherwise the court interferes with a bail-granting order only if it is perverse on its face or made in clear disregard of the principles of the law of bail. Only a tentative assessment of the record is made at the bail stage. Ref: Rab Nawaz v. Shehzad Hassan (Crl.P.253-L/2025, decided 26.03.2025).
records.title: Rab Nawaz v. Shehzad Hassan (Crl.P.253-L/2025, decided 26.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Juvenility: Age Determination (s. 8 JJSA 2018)
records.heading: Juvenility: documents must be verified and tested before acceptance
records.text: Documents produced to prove juvenility must be verified and tested under the Qanun-e-Shahadat before acceptance. The inquiry under s. 8 Juvenile Justice System Act 2018 is akin to a trial within a trial; the court should call the record and authors of the documents as witnesses. An accused charged with murder who claims juvenility bears the burden of proving it on genuine documents. Ref: 2025 MLD 367, PLJ 2025 CrC 149; Kamran Mushtaq v. The State (Crl. Revision 56647/24); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kamran Mushtaq v. The State (Crl. Revision 56647/24)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: Related chance witnesses who did not identify the body are unreliable
records.text: Eye-witnesses who are close relatives of the deceased, give no reason for following the deceased that day, and did not identify the body at the inquest or post-mortem are interested and chance witnesses whose evidence is unreliable. Medical evidence only corroborates the injury and weapon, not the identity of the assailant. Recovery of the weapon from the accused's house 16 days after the occurrence held implausible. Accused acquitted on benefit of doubt. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 171; Muhammad Dilshad v. The State (Jail Appeal 59174/19).
records.title: Muhammad Dilshad v. The State (Jail Appeal 59174/19)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Dispensation of Attendance of Accused
records.heading: Earning a livelihood abroad justifies dispensing with the accused's attendance
records.text: Earning a livelihood abroad is a valid reason to dispense with the personal attendance of the accused. The judgment also explains the difference between a conviction and a sentence and the lasting consequences of a conviction for the person concerned. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 181; Rai Muhammad Aslam v. The State (Crl. Misc. 40397/24).
records.title: Rai Muhammad Aslam v. The State (Crl. Misc. 40397/24)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death of Wife Inside House: Onus on Husband
records.heading: Wife's unnatural death in the bedroom: Article 122 QSO puts an onus on the husband to explain
records.text: Where a wife dies an unnatural death inside the bedroom at night and the husband alone had access and exclusive knowledge of what happened, Art. 122 QSO places an onus on him to explain the circumstances. In such cases the first version of the accused has persuasive value, and the conduct of the surviving spouse is a relevant circumstance; strict principles of circumstantial evidence are relaxed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 197; The State v. M. Waqas (Murder Reference 215-19).
records.title: The State v. M. Waqas (Murder Reference 215-19)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Recovery Memo
records.heading: Recovery memo must be prepared at the spot and attested by the witnesses
records.text: A recovery memo must be prepared at the spot and attested by the witnesses so as to exclude fabrication. Where the evidence showed the recovery memo was prepared after registration of the FIR, no legal sanctity attaches to it. Ref: 2025 YLR 75, PLJ 2025 CrC 207; Nayyar Abbas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 549 of 2023).
records.title: Nayyar Abbas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 549 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Gift (Hiba) under Muslim Law
records.heading: Essentials of a valid gift; heirs cannot dispute a gift the donor accepted in his lifetime
records.text: Explains the essentials of a valid gift (hiba) under Muslim law: declaration by the donor, acceptance by the donee and delivery of possession, with an immediate and unconditional transfer. Where the donor accepted the gift and its validity in his lifetime, his legal heirs have no standing to dispute it after his death. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 339; Syed Masood Ali v. Mst. Feroza Begum (Civil Petitions 552-K of 2021 & 1108-K of 2023).
records.title: Syed Masood Ali v. Mst. Feroza Begum (Civil Petitions 552-K of 2021 & 1108-K of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Paternity: DNA Test and Art. 128 QSO
records.heading: Child born in wedlock: husband's DNA application in a maintenance suit rightly refused
records.text: Under Art. 128 QSO a child born during a valid marriage is conclusive proof of legitimacy. An application by the husband for DNA analysis in a suit for maintenance of the minor was rightly refused; DNA testing must not be used to harass the mother or delay maintenance. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 332, PLJ 2025 Lah 244; Sakhawat Hussain v. ADJ Bhalwal (WP 22286/23).
records.title: Sakhawat Hussain v. ADJ Bhalwal (WP 22286/23)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Enhancement after Marriage
records.heading: Enhancement of dower agreed after marriage is lawful and enforceable
records.text: An enhancement of dower agreed after the marriage is lawful and executable. It is not an unlawful condition imposed to keep the parties in the marriage. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 359, PLJ 2024 Lah 273; Syed Sibt Hassan v. Saba Batool (WP 38567/22).
records.title: Syed Sibt Hassan v. Saba Batool (WP 38567/22)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Transfer of Family Case
records.heading: Transfer of a family case from one court to another
records.text: Supreme Court judgment on transfer of a family case from one court to another (summary in the post is in Urdu only; holding to be read from the report). Ref: PLD 2025 SC 310; Mst. Sidra Hameed v. Syed Abdul Mateen (C.M.A. 100/2024).
records.title: Mst. Sidra Hameed v. Syed Abdul Mateen (C.M.A. 100/2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Talaq Notice: Territorial Jurisdiction of Union Council
records.heading: Talaq notice: the Union Council where the wife was residing has jurisdiction
records.text: The Union Council (or its Chairman) with jurisdiction over a talaq notice is the one within whose territory the wife was residing when the divorce was pronounced. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 340, PLJ 2024 Lah 214.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Documents Tendered in Statement of Counsel
records.heading: Documents produced through counsel's statement are inadmissible
records.text: Documents produced through the statement of counsel are not validly tendered. They are inadmissible and cannot be relied upon as evidence; documents must be produced through the mode prescribed by law. Ref: 2025 MLD 573.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Addition of Offences after Bail
records.heading: No arrest on addition of offences unless the earlier bail is first cancelled
records.text: Where an accused already holds pre-arrest or post-arrest bail in a case, he cannot be arrested merely because further offences are added in the same case unless the earlier bail is first cancelled under s. 497(5) CrPC. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1568, PLJ 2024 CrC 532; Mujtaba Saleem Butt v. Incharge Investigation AVLS (Crl. Misc. 10162/24).
records.title: Mujtaba Saleem Butt v. Incharge Investigation AVLS (Crl. Misc. 10162/24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Closure of Evidence: Indolent Party
records.heading: Evidence closed where a party failed to produce it despite several opportunities
records.text: A party given several opportunities and a warning to produce evidence, who fails to do so, cannot be allowed to delay proceedings; closure of his evidence upheld. The law helps the vigilant, not the indolent. Ref: 2025 SCMR 624; Muhammad Asim v. Dr. Abdul Hamid Jan (C.P.L.A. 277-Q/2024, decided 16.01.2025); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Asim v. Dr. Abdul Hamid Jan (C.P.L.A. 277-Q/2024, decided 16.01.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula before Rukhsati
records.heading: Khula before rukhsati: dower received must be restored to the husband
records.text: Under s. 10(4) West Pakistan Family Courts Act 1964, where rukhsati has not taken place and the wife will not live with the husband, the court dissolving the marriage by khula at the pre-trial stage must restore the dower received to the husband rather than try the issue of cruelty. A wife granted khula is not entitled to a decree for dower and maintenance, and if the marriage was not consummated she need not observe iddat. Ref: 2020 YLR Sindh 1558, PLD 2014 Pesh 226.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Statutory Delay
records.heading: Statutory delay bail is a right and cannot be refused because other cases are registered
records.text: Bail on the statutory ground of delay in conclusion of trial under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC is a right. It cannot be withheld merely because other cases, not relating to terrorism, are registered against the accused. Accused in custody for about one year and ten months; bail allowed. Ref: 2025 MLD 132, 2025 MLD 610, PLJ 2024 CrC 1219; Muhammad Rauf v. The State (Crl. Misc. 16105-B/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Rauf v. The State (Crl. Misc. 16105-B/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Punjab Animal Slaughter Control Act 1963
records.heading: Bail court may itself consider what offence the facts disclose
records.text: Possession of dead meat is punishable under the Punjab Animal Slaughter Control Act 1963. While deciding a bail petition the court may itself consider what offence the facts disclose. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 627; Naveed Tariq v. The State (Crl. Misc. 38478/24).
records.title: Naveed Tariq v. The State (Crl. Misc. 38478/24)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness
records.heading: An injured witness is not reliable merely because of his injury
records.text: Injuries on a witness show his presence but do not make his testimony reliable. An injured witness cannot be believed merely because of his injury if his evidence is not otherwise confidence-inspiring. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 762; Allah Rakha v. The State (Crl. Appeal 17661/19).
records.title: Allah Rakha v. The State (Crl. Appeal 17661/19)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Fake Police Encounters
records.heading: Zero tolerance for fake police encounters and custodial killings
records.text: Zero tolerance must be shown towards fake police encounters and custodial killings. Police officials cannot justify such killings under the guise of self-defence. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 726, PLJ 2024 CrC 1211; Mst. Farzana Bibi v. C.C.P.O. Lahore (Crl. Misc. 36448/24).
records.title: Mst. Farzana Bibi v. C.C.P.O. Lahore (Crl. Misc. 36448/24)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Rule 17-A: Deceased Employee Quota
records.heading: End of the deceased-employee quota (Rule 17-A) applies prospectively
records.text: The Supreme Court decision ending the policy of appointing children of deceased or retired civil servants (omission of Rule 17-A, Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment & Conditions of Service) Rules 1974) applies prospectively from the date of that decision. Cases where the parent died or retired on medical grounds before then remain covered. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 389; Muhammad Zaman v. Government of the Punjab (WP 12771-24).
records.title: Muhammad Zaman v. Government of the Punjab (WP 12771-24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Reinvestigation after Cancellation of FIR
records.heading: Reinvestigation after cancellation of an FIR needs the Magistrate's permission
records.text: After an FIR is cancelled, the police may reinvestigate the case, but only with the permission of the Magistrate concerned. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 398, 2024 MLD 1796; Muhammad Aslam Khan v. Judicial Magistrate Ferozewala (Crl. Proceedings 9158/24).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam Khan v. Judicial Magistrate Ferozewala (Crl. Proceedings 9158/24)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Family Pension: Unmarried Daughter; Succession Certificate
records.heading: Family pension passes from the eldest unmarried daughter to the next on her marriage
records.text: Under the pension rules as amended in 1999, the eldest unmarried daughter of a deceased government servant draws her share of family pension until marriage, after which it passes to the next unmarried daughter. Proceedings for a succession certificate under the Succession Act 1925 are summary, and a second application was wrongly held barred by Order II Rule 2 CPC. Ref: 2025 SCMR 579, PLJ 2025 SC 183; Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public (C.P.L.A. 256-Q/2020).
records.title: Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public (C.P.L.A. 256-Q/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Remedy against Revisional Decree on Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Remedy against a revisional decree on rejection of a plaint
records.text: Explains the remedy available where a District Court, in revisional jurisdiction, passes a decree on rejection of a plaint, and the need for a real link between an alleged procedural irregularity and the substantive rights of the parties. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 24, PLJ 2025 SC 207; Misree Khan v. Abdul Ghafoor (C.P.L.A. 81-P/2019).
records.title: Misree Khan v. Abdul Ghafoor (C.P.L.A. 81-P/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Time as Essence of Contract
records.heading: Whether time is of the essence depends on the agreement and the parties' intention
records.text: Whether time is of the essence depends on the wording of the agreement and the intention of the parties, and is a question of fact. Where time is not of the essence, failure to perform by the date fixed does not make the agreement voidable; the promisee is left to compensation. Ref: 2025 SCMR 495, PLJ 2025 SC 188; Zeeshan Pervez v. Muhammad Nasir (C.P.L.A. 812-K/2022).
records.title: Zeeshan Pervez v. Muhammad Nasir (C.P.L.A. 812-K/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive; Hanging and Strangulation
records.heading: Motive is a double-edged weapon and cannot alone establish guilt
records.text: Motive is a double-edged weapon that may explain either real or false implication; an accused cannot be held guilty on the basis of motive alone. The judgment also sets out the medical differences between hanging and strangulation. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1507, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 73; Muhammad Ijaz alias Billa v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz alias Billa v. The State

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Common Intention, Abetment, Honour Killing
records.heading: Common intention, abetment and honour killing
records.text: S. 34 PPC does not require each accused to act with his own hand; a prearranged plan and participation in furtherance of the common intention suffice. S. 109 PPC: an abettor is punishable as for the offence abetted where it is committed in consequence of the abetment. Honour killing (karo-kari) is murder simpliciter, not permitted by law or religion, and an offence committed on the pretext of honour falls within "fasad-fil-arz" under s. 299(ee) PPC. The judgment also explains the term "sui juris". Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 87; Muhammad Ali Mahar v. The State (Crl. P. 201-K of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ali Mahar v. The State (Crl. P. 201-K of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 426 CrPC: Absconding Convict
records.heading: An absconding convict must surrender before any application is entertained
