records.text: Where a family court did not give adequate opportunity to file a written statement, another chance should be given. Speed must not lead to hurried decisions; justice delayed is denied, but justice hurried is buried. Ref: 2026 CLC 489; Muhammad Waqas v. Judge Family Court (WP 71055/25).
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. Judge Family Court (WP 71055/25)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: PECA 2025 Amendment Prospective
records.heading: PECA 2025 amendment making offences non-bailable applies prospectively
records.text: The 2025 amendment to s. 43 PECA making offences under ss. 13 and 14 non-bailable is substantive, not procedural, and applies prospectively, because bail in a bailable offence is a vested right. Ref: 2026 MLD 542; Muhammad Rizwan v. The State (Crl. Misc. 10519-B-24).
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan v. The State (Crl. Misc. 10519-B-24)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Evidence Not Wholly Discarded
records.heading: Evidence of a hostile witness is weighed with caution, not wholly discarded
records.text: The evidence of a hostile witness is not wholly discarded; it is weighed with caution and the test is independent corroboration and consistency with the rest of the evidence. On the facts it was unsafe to base a capital conviction on it. Ref: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 264-J/2023; M.R. 21/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 264-J/2023; M.R. 21/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Limitation: Common Question of Law
records.heading: Time-barred case may be heard on merits where the common question of law is already decided
records.text: Where a common question of law has been decided in one case, another case on the same point that is time-barred may be heard on merits. Ref: 2026 MLD 507; Benish Ghaffar v. ADJ (WP 1829-24).
records.title: Benish Ghaffar v. ADJ (WP 1829-24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Party Impleaded at Appellate Stage: Remand
records.heading: Party impleaded at the appellate stage: case to be remanded for trial
records.text: When a party is impleaded at the appellate stage under O. I R. 10 CPC, natural justice requires remand to the trial court so that the new party can plead, lead evidence and contest. Ref: 2026 YLR 536; Naeem Abbas v. Altaf Hussain (RFA 47-25).
records.title: Naeem Abbas v. Altaf Hussain (RFA 47-25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: CNIC Cannot Be Blocked by Civil Court
records.heading: Civil courts cannot attach, impound or block a CNIC
records.text: A CNIC is not the holder's movable property; it belongs to the Federal Government under s. 18 NADRA Ordinance 2000. Civil courts cannot attach, impound, cancel or block it as a coercive measure; only NADRA may act, on the grounds in s. 18. Ref: Muhammad Ali Ansari v. Federation of Pakistan (WP 8895 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Ali Ansari v. Federation of Pakistan (WP 8895 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summoning Defendant as Plaintiff's Witness
records.heading: Plaintiff may not summon the defendant as his own witness
records.text: Plaintiffs may not summon the defendant as their own witness to compel her into the box; this puts examination and cross-examination in the wrong hands and hinders a fair trial. Refusal upheld. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 976.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth: School Record
records.heading: School admission register is reliable evidence of date of birth
records.text: An entry in the school admission register, made when the plaintiff was ten, is reliable evidence of date of birth; the defendants did not dispute her documents. Concurrent findings set aside in revision and the suit for correction decreed. Ref: 2025 YLR 40.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody Not Proved: Acquittal
records.heading: Narcotics: broken chain of custody leads to acquittal
records.text: Recovery of 1005 grams of ice and 6000 grams of charas: contradictions in the witnesses' accounts of custody and transmission of the samples and case property broke the chain of custody. Conviction under ss. 9(d) and 11(c) of the 2019 Act set aside; petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 937; Attique Ullah v. The State (Criminal Petition 1753).
records.title: Attique Ullah v. The State (Criminal Petition 1753)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cross-Firing: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Cross-firing between two groups: who fired the fatal shot is a matter of further inquiry
records.text: Cross-firing between two groups in which a minor died; the minor's heirs compromised with the rival group, and a joint role was attributed to both sides. Who caused the fatal shot was a matter of further inquiry; post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 914; Asad Khalil v. The State (Criminal Petition 868 of 2025).
records.title: Asad Khalil v. The State (Criminal Petition 868 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Oral Gift: Revocation and Title Documents
records.heading: Oral gift against a later registered gift deed: possession of the title documents decisive
records.text: Dispute between a donee under an oral gift (1984), confirmed in writing and by mutation, and a later registered gift deed by the donor to his wife after revoking the oral gift. Possession of the original title documents was treated as decisive of ownership. Order of the single judge restored; appeal allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 929; Ghulam Asghar Khan v. Muhammad Arif Khan (Civil Appeal 8-K of 2020).
records.title: Ghulam Asghar Khan v. Muhammad Arif Khan (Civil Appeal 8-K of 2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 337-N(2) PPC at Bail Stage
records.heading: Prohibitory clause alone is no ground to refuse bail; section 337-N(2) PPC considered
records.text: Even where the offence falls within the prohibitory clause, bail cannot be refused on that ground alone; s. 337-N(2) PPC may be considered at the bail stage, and the gravity of the offence is no substitute for punishment. Post-arrest bail granted. Ref: 2026 SCMR 917; Muzamil Hussain v. The State (Criminal Petition 974-L of 2025).
records.title: Muzamil Hussain v. The State (Criminal Petition 974-L of 2025)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Supreme Court Judgments Not Binding on FCC
records.heading: Supreme Court judgments are not binding on the Federal Constitutional Court
records.text: Under Art. 189 of the Constitution, Supreme Court judgments are not binding on the Federal Constitutional Court; they may be treated as persuasive. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 114; Muhammad Farhan v. Province of Punjab (F.C.P.L.A. 16 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Farhan v. Province of Punjab (F.C.P.L.A. 16 of 2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt as of Right
records.heading: Benefit of doubt goes to the accused as of right
records.text: Where there is doubt in the prosecution case, its benefit goes to the accused as of right. Ref: 2026 SCMR 891; Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition 473 of 2018).
records.title: Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition 473 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt; Co-accused Acquitted; Negative Forensic Report
records.heading: Co-accused acquitted on the same evidence and pistol not matched with the empties
records.text: Even slight doubt benefits the accused. Witnesses attributed firing to five persons, three unknown in the FIR; co-accused were acquitted on the same evidence; the pistol recovered from the appellant did not match the empties. Appellant acquitted. Ref: 2026 SCMR 921; Muhammad Amjad v. The State (Criminal Appeal 220-L of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Amjad v. The State (Criminal Appeal 220-L of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Interfaith Marriage after Conversion: Custody Not Illegal
records.heading: Daughter's declaration of conversion to Islam sufficient; marriage upheld
records.text: A father sought recovery of his daughter, claiming she was a minor Christian and her marriage void. Her declarations of conversion to Islam were sufficient and further probing into her faith was unwarranted; her marriage under the 1961 Ordinance stood, and her birth documents were not conclusive given her apparent age in court. Custody with her husband not illegal absent a court declaration otherwise; leave refused. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Action after Acquittal
records.heading: Departmental action after acquittal depends on whether it rests on independent evidence
records.text: Where departmental proceedings rest on independent evidence of misconduct, acquittal in the criminal case does not end them. Where they rest only on the registration of an FIR, acquittal removes their basis and any penalty is unsustainable. Ref: 2026 SCMR 843, PLJ 2026 SC 118; Ghulam Murtaza v. District Police Officer, Gujrat (C.P. 4757 of 2024).
records.title: Ghulam Murtaza v. District Police Officer, Gujrat (C.P. 4757 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Blocking CNIC, Passport and Bank Accounts of Absent Witness
records.heading: Trial court cannot block a witness's CNIC, passport or bank accounts for non-appearance
records.text: A trial court cannot order blocking of a complainant-witness's CNIC, passport or bank accounts for non-appearance: only NADRA may cancel or impound a CNIC (s. 18 NADRA Ordinance 2000), passports are governed by s. 8 Passports Act 1974, and NADRA cannot direct banks to block accounts. Order set aside; petitioner directed to appear. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 388; Abdul Rehman v. The State (Criminal Revision 205 of 2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. The State (Criminal Revision 205 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Document Not Produced: Reference in Cross-Examination
records.heading: A document never produced in evidence remains unproved
records.text: A document on which a claim is founded, if never produced in evidence, remains unproved; mere reference to it in cross-examination cannot replace strict proof. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 269, PLJ 2026 SC 322; Province of Punjab v. Zulfiqar (C.P.L.A. 1600-L of 2014).
records.title: Province of Punjab v. Zulfiqar (C.P.L.A. 1600-L of 2014)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: CNIC of Judgment-Debtor Cannot Be Blocked
records.heading: Executing court cannot block the judgment debtor's CNIC under section 51 CPC
records.text: Section 51 CPC sets out the modes of executing a decree; the residuary clause (e) does not allow an executing court to block the judgment-debtor's CNIC. Doing so is not a proper exercise of discretion or statutory power, and the High Court erred in upholding it. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 280, PLJ 2026 SC 298; Agha Abid Majeed Khan v. Idrees Ahmed (C.P.L.A. 3744/2023).
records.title: Agha Abid Majeed Khan v. Idrees Ahmed (C.P.L.A. 3744/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth in Educational Record
records.heading: Correction of date of birth in the educational record
records.text: Authority on correction of date of birth in educational record. Ref: 2020 SCMR 316.

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.topic: ECL: FIR Alone Not Enough
records.heading: A name cannot be placed on the Exit Control List merely because an FIR is registered
records.text: A name cannot be placed on the Exit Control List merely because an FIR has been registered. Ref: 2026 MLD 250.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Freezing Bank Account of Accused
records.heading: Neither NCCIA nor FIA can freeze the bank account of an accused
records.text: Neither NCCIA nor FIA has authority to freeze the bank account of an accused. Ref: PLD 2026 Islamabad 63.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Court Jurisdiction after Tenancy Ends
records.heading: Civil court is the forum for disputes arising after the tenancy ends
records.text: Civil courts may try all suits of a civil nature unless expressly or impliedly barred (s. 9 CPC). The Rent Tribunal has no jurisdiction over disputes arising after the tenancy ends, so the civil court is the proper forum for them. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 640; Fauzia Qayyum v. Additional District Judge (WP 55743/25).
records.title: Fauzia Qayyum v. Additional District Judge (WP 55743/25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Recall of Ad-Interim Injunction: Not a Final Order
records.heading: Recall of an ad-interim injunction for repeated adjournments is not a final order
records.text: Recalling an ad-interim injunction because of repeated adjournment requests, to secure the petitioner's presence for arguments, regulates procedure and is not a final order; it is not ordinarily open to challenge unless perverse, illegal or without jurisdiction. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 610; Kaneez Begum v. Additional District Judge (Misc. Writ 75498/25).
records.title: Kaneez Begum v. Additional District Judge (Misc. Writ 75498/25)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Registered in Non-Cognizable Offence
records.heading: Course to follow where an FIR is registered for a non-cognizable offence
records.text: Traces the legislative history of the "book" prescribed under ss. 154 and 155 CrPC and sets out the course to follow where an FIR has been registered for a non-cognizable offence: preliminary investigation with the SP's direction, or a police report under s. 173 CrPC on which the magistrate may take cognizance under s. 190(1)(a) or (b). After preliminary investigation the accused may be arrested only on a warrant (s. 155(3) CrPC); on summons the magistrate may take a bond under s. 91 or commit to custody under s. 351 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 663; Muhammad Ahsan v. The State (WP 25543/24).
records.title: Muhammad Ahsan v. The State (WP 25543/24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Gift Excluding Other Heirs (Zarar)
records.heading: Gift of the whole estate to the child who cared for the donor is valid
records.text: A gift made only to deprive other heirs out of malice may be invalid as zarar. But where the excluded children had distanced themselves and litigated against their father while the donee cared for him in old age, a gift of the whole estate to the donee is valid. Liaqat Ali v. Shahnaz Akhtar (2025 LHC 693) distinguished. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 630; Muhammad Naseem v. Asghar Ali Tabassum (Civil Revision 55105/23).
records.title: Muhammad Naseem v. Asghar Ali Tabassum (Civil Revision 55105/23)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Special Oath by Third Person
records.heading: A third person's refusal to take a special oath is no ground to dismiss a suit
records.text: A third person's refusal to take a special oath is not a ground to dismiss a suit. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 627; Mst. Nasreen Akhtar v. ADJ (WP 724-20).
records.title: Mst. Nasreen Akhtar v. ADJ (WP 724-20)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Registered Document: Presumption of Correctness
records.heading: A registered document carries a presumption of correctness
records.text: A document must be presented for registration within the prescribed time. A registered document carries strong evidentiary value and a presumption of correctness because it passes through verification. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 304.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: NAB Cases Transferred to Federal Constitutional Court
records.heading: Pending NAB cases stand transferred to the Federal Constitutional Court
records.text: The Supreme Court has no jurisdiction in NAB cases under Art. 175F(a) of the Constitution read with ss. 32 and 32A NAO 1999. All pending NAB petitions and appeals stand transferred by fiction of law to the Federal Constitutional Court (judgment of 24 July 2026). Ref: PLD 2026 SC 424; Chairman NAB v. Adeel Ahmed (Crl.P.L.A. 316/2018).
records.title: Chairman NAB v. Adeel Ahmed (Crl.P.L.A. 316/2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Limitation: State Must Comply
records.heading: The State must comply with limitation and cannot plead internal delays
records.text: Limitation under the Supreme Court Rules 2025 is substantive. The State must meet the time limits and cannot rely on internal file movement, committee schedules or staff shortages as sufficient cause. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 376; Federation of Pakistan v. Farid Ullah (C.P.L.A. 4430/2025).
records.title: Federation of Pakistan v. Farid Ullah (C.P.L.A. 4430/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower Property Payable on Demand
records.heading: Dower property payable on demand must be kept available for transfer
records.text: Where property is entered in the nikahnama as dower payable on demand, the husband must keep it available for transfer whenever the wife demands it. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 371; Sajid Hussain v. Additional District Judge, Vehari (CPLA 1330-L of 2025).
records.title: Sajid Hussain v. Additional District Judge, Vehari (CPLA 1330-L of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Conversion to Islam: Marriage to Non-Muslim Husband
records.heading: Marriage of a non-Muslim woman to her non-Muslim husband after her conversion to Islam
records.text: Considers the legal and Shariah status of the marriage of a non-Muslim woman to her non-Muslim husband after her conversion to Islam. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 617; Noor Fatima v. Station House Officer (WP 622/2025).
records.title: Noor Fatima v. Station House Officer (WP 622/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dissolution: Second Marriage without Permission
records.heading: Second marriage without permission entitles the wife to dissolution
records.text: A wife is entitled to dissolution of marriage if the husband contracts a second marriage in breach of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 302, PLD 2026 SC 91, PLD 2025 SC 262.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Geo-Fencing and CDR of Witnesses
records.heading: Accused may seek geo-fencing data and call records of witnesses under section 94 CrPC at any stage
records.text: Under s. 94 CrPC an accused may seek production of any document, including geo-fencing data and CDR of prosecution witnesses, at any stage to test their claimed presence, if the court finds it necessary or desirable. The discretion must be exercised judiciously to reach a just decision. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1334.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Road Certificate: Documentary Proof of Dispatch
records.heading: Road certificate entry can be negated only by a document, not oral evidence
records.text: An entry in the road certificate about dispatch of case property can be negated only by a document of superior value, not by oral evidence. Where the investigating officer and the moharrar gave conflicting accounts of who took the sample parcel to the PFSA, safe transmission was not proved. Road certificates must record the required details expressly. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1639, PLJ 2026 CrC 669; Naseem alias Seemay Shah v. The State (Crl. A. 68455/23).
records.title: Naseem alias Seemay Shah v. The State (Crl. A. 68455/23)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Dispute Not Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: A dowry dispute between spouses is not criminal breach of trust
records.text: A dispute between spouses over dowry articles is for the Family Court and cannot be turned into an offence under s. 406 PPC merely by calling the articles "amanat". Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 678; Muhammad Umair Riaz v. The State (Crl. Misc. 9787/26).
records.title: Muhammad Umair Riaz v. The State (Crl. Misc. 9787/26)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Infirmity a Separate Ground for Bail
records.heading: Infirmity is a ground for bail separate from sickness
records.text: S. 497 CrPC recognises "infirmity" as a ground for bail separate from sickness, even in heinous offences. Infirmity covers frailty from age, congenital limitation or non-fatal disease restricting mobility. If the court itself finds the prisoner infirm it may grant bail without further medical inquiry. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 707; Iftikhar Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 33164/26).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 33164/26)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A CrPC: Transfer between Justices of Peace
records.heading: Sessions Judge cannot transfer a section 22-A application from one Justice of Peace to another
records.text: A Sessions Judge acting administratively may entrust an application under s. 22-A(6) CrPC to an Ex-Officio Justice of the Peace, but cannot later transfer it to another Ex-Officio Justice of the Peace. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 581; Faisal Manzoor v. District & Sessions Judge (WP 41376/26).
records.title: Faisal Manzoor v. District & Sessions Judge (WP 41376/26)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Succession Certificate Appeal: Forum
records.heading: Appeal in succession certificate matters lies to the District Judge whatever the value
records.text: The forum of appeal against a grant or refusal of a succession certificate is governed by ss. 384 and 388 Succession Act 1925, not pecuniary limits. An appeal from a Civil Judge with delegated powers under s. 388 lies to the District Judge whatever the value of the estate; returning it was a jurisdictional error. Appeal restored. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 606; Sheikh Imam Baksh v. Mst. Gulzar Begum (Civil Revision 35921/25).
records.title: Sheikh Imam Baksh v. Mst. Gulzar Begum (Civil Revision 35921/25)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Doubtful Fracture
records.heading: Doubtful medical evidence of a fracture: pre-arrest bail
records.text: Doubtful medical evidence of a finger fracture with no injury to the rest of the hand suggested a friendly-hand injury, making out a case for pre-arrest bail. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 658; Umar Farooq v. The State (Crl. Misc. 15322/26).
records.title: Umar Farooq v. The State (Crl. Misc. 15322/26)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Arrest of Judgment-Debtor: S. 51 and O. XXI R. 40 CPC
records.heading: Arrest of a judgment debtor in a money decree is an exceptional mode of execution
records.text: Arrest and detention of a judgment-debtor in execution of a money decree is an exceptional mode, available only on strict compliance with the safeguards in s. 51 and O. XXI R. 40 CPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 642; Naseer Ahmad Nasir v. Ali Sher (WP 31402/26); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Naseer Ahmad Nasir v. Ali Sher (WP 31402/26)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Referral of Public Functionary for Departmental Action
records.heading: Court may refer an obstructing public functionary for departmental action
records.text: Where a public functionary appears to obstruct execution of judicial orders, the court may refer the matter to the competent authority for departmental action. Such a referral is recommendatory, makes no finding of guilt, and is not ordinarily interfered with in writ jurisdiction. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 658; Muhammad Sufyan v. Additional District Judge (Misc. Writ 12495/26).
records.title: Muhammad Sufyan v. Additional District Judge (Misc. Writ 12495/26)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Oral Extension of Tenancy
records.heading: An oral extension of tenancy operates at most for one month
records.text: An oral extension of tenancy, unless the other side concedes it, operates at most for one month; a claimed oral extension of 15 years could not be assumed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 663; Khizar Hayyat v. ADJ (WP 7652-26).
records.title: Khizar Hayyat v. ADJ (WP 7652-26)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Muharram Processions and Majalis: Licence
records.heading: Licence for a Muharram procession or majlis needed only where there is a threat to the peace
records.text: A licence for a Muharram procession or majlis is needed only where the police judge it to threaten the peace; restrictions on such assemblies are otherwise unjustified. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 668; Syed Wasi Haider v. CPO (WP 7251-26).
records.title: Syed Wasi Haider v. CPO (WP 7251-26)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor: Factors
records.heading: Maintenance of a minor is fixed on the child's needs and the father's means
records.text: In fixing a minor's maintenance the court considers the child's reasonable needs and the father's means, income and status. Higher courts interfere with the amount only if it is arbitrary, unreasonable or contrary to law. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 518; Mst. Shaheen Nawaz v. Raheel Khan (C.P.L.A. 316-K/2026).
records.title: Mst. Shaheen Nawaz v. Raheel Khan (C.P.L.A. 316-K/2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Counsel's Concession under Wakalatnama
records.heading: A concession made by counsel in open court cannot be disowned for convenience
records.text: Under O. III R. 4 CPC and s. 22(3) Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act 1973, a wakalatnama does not give unlimited authority to compromise or withdraw. But a statement or concession made in open court by duly engaged counsel cannot be disowned as a matter of convenience without proof of lack of authority or fraud; a party cannot approbate and reprobate. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 521; Muhammad Ashraf v. Akber Ali (C.P.L.A. 49-K/2026).
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. Akber Ali (C.P.L.A. 49-K/2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Rent Proceedings: Delay and Dilatory Tactics
records.heading: Rent cases must be decided speedily; dilatory tactics discouraged
records.text: Rent laws are a special summary code for speedy decision. Courts must not let rent cases drag through repeated applications, revisions and appeals for decades; statutory timelines must be followed and mala fide adjournments and applications discouraged. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1995, PLJ 2026 SC 546; Muhammad Jahangir v. Haji Muhammad Ashraf (C.A. 2555/2016).
records.title: Muhammad Jahangir v. Haji Muhammad Ashraf (C.A. 2555/2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR
records.heading: A prompt FIR secures the earliest account; delay invites embellishment
records.text: Prompt lodging of the FIR secures the earliest account of the time, culprits, roles, weapons and witnesses. Delay often leads to embellishment as an afterthought. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 740; Musharaf Habib v. The State (Crl. Appeal 821 of 2017).
records.title: Musharaf Habib v. The State (Crl. Appeal 821 of 2017)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Land Acquisition: Self-Contained Regime
records.heading: Land acquisition is governed by the self-contained regime of the 1894 Act
records.text: Land acquisition for a public purpose is governed by the self-contained regime of the Land Acquisition Act 1894; parties must seek relief under that Act. Ref: PLJ 2026 FCC 111; C.P.L.A. 3912 of 2025, C.P.L.A. 1449 of 2025 and C.M.A. 1142-L of 2025.
records.title: C.P.L.A. 3912 of 2025, C.P.L.A. 1449 of 2025 and C.M.A. 1142-L of 2025

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Strict Proof Despite Seriousness
records.heading: Narcotics: seriousness of the offence does not lower the standard of proof
records.text: Narcotics enforcement mostly reaches street-level peddlers, not the principal traffickers. The seriousness of the offence does not lower the standard of proof; because punishments are harsh, courts must insist on strict proof of recovery, custody, sampling, transmission and conscious possession. Judgment circulated to IGPs, Prosecutors General and DPOs. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 273; Mehmood Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 1544 of 2025).
records.title: Mehmood Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 1544 of 2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Punjab Food Authority: Release of Seized Items
records.heading: Punjab Food Authority: seized food or premises may be released on a surety bond
records.text: The Punjab Food Authority Act 2011 sets up three regimes: the Food Safety Officer, the Food Authority and the Special Court, each with distinct powers (ss. 7, 12, 13 and 39). Seized food or premises may be released during proceedings against a surety bond, without prejudice to the final decision, as with case property under the CrPC. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 744; Abdul Qadeer v. The State (WP 10163 of 2026).
records.title: Abdul Qadeer v. The State (WP 10163 of 2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 26-A CPC: Penal Action for Late Written Statement
records.heading: Late written statement: the defendant's conduct must be examined before penal action under section 26-A CPC
records.text: S. 26-A CPC aims to shorten litigation, but before penal consequences are imposed the defendant's conduct must be examined; where he acted in good faith or was prevented by genuine circumstances from filing the written statement in time, strict penal action may not be warranted. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 734.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summary Suit: Death of Drawer; Execution against Heirs
records.heading: Summary suit survives the drawer's death where his legal representatives contest on merits
records.text: A summary suit under O. XXXVII CPC validly filed against the drawer in his lifetime does not fail on his death where his legal representatives were impleaded, adopted his written statement and contested on merits; they cannot raise maintainability under ss. 29 and 29-A Negotiable Instruments Act for the first time in appeal. Under s. 50 CPC the decree is executable against them only to the extent of the estate inherited. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 716, PLJ 2026 Lah 534.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minors: Inquisitorial Role
records.heading: Court takes an inquisitorial role in fixing maintenance for minors
records.text: When fixing maintenance for minors, the court takes an inquisitorial role. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 767, PLJ 2026 Lah 260; Muhammad Saeed Anwar v. Judge Family Court (WP 26445/22).
records.title: Muhammad Saeed Anwar v. Judge Family Court (WP 26445/22)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: No Change of Investigation after Charge
records.heading: No change of investigation after the charge is framed
records.text: Investigation cannot be changed after the charge has been framed. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1759; Maryam Bibi v. The State (WP 45328/25).
records.title: Maryam Bibi v. The State (WP 45328/25)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Delay in Registration of FIR: Duty of Police
records.heading: Delay in registering the FIR gives room for false implication
records.text: The FIR is not substantive evidence, but delay in registering it gives room for false implication and manipulation of evidence. Prompt registration lets the police secure the scene and evidence; the Court stressed police accountability for proper investigation. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1409; Mir Muhammad alias Kurary v. The State (Criminal Appeal 40-K of 2022).
records.title: Mir Muhammad alias Kurary v. The State (Criminal Appeal 40-K of 2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Gravity of Offence No Bar Where Further Inquiry
records.heading: Gravity of the offence alone does not justify refusing bail in a case of further inquiry
records.text: The gravity or atrocity of an offence alone does not justify refusing bail, pre-arrest or post-arrest, where the evidence leaves the case one of further inquiry; bail cannot be withheld as punishment. Like cases should be treated alike, after assessing each accused's role. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1422; Kashif Tanveer v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 562-L of 2025).
records.title: Kashif Tanveer v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 562-L of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Annual Increase in Maintenance: Not Compounded
records.heading: Annual increase in maintenance is calculated on the original decreed amount
records.text: Where a maintenance decree is silent on compounding, the annual increase (here 20%) is calculated on the originally decreed amount, not on the enhanced amount of the previous year. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1582, PLJ 2026 SC 429; Muhammad Waqar Wasi v. Mst. Amber Abid (C.P.L.A. 3204 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Waqar Wasi v. Mst. Amber Abid (C.P.L.A. 3204 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Juvenility: Documents Preferred over Ossification
records.heading: Juvenility: documentary proof of age preferred over an ossification test
records.text: Documentary proof of age is preferred over an ossification test in an inquiry under s. 8 Juvenile Justice System Act 2018, and the trial court has ample power to hold that inquiry. Ref: 2026 LHC 5998; Ali Shair alias Malhi v. Additional Sessions Judge (Crl. Revision 49478/26, decided 17.09.2026); Justice Amir Ajam Malik.
records.title: Ali Shair alias Malhi v. Additional Sessions Judge (Crl. Revision 49478/26, decided 17.09.2026)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Collection without Due Process
records.heading: Collecting DNA without due process violates privacy and dignity
records.text: Collecting a person's DNA without due process violates privacy, dignity and liberty under Art. 9 of the Constitution, given the sensitivity of genetic information. An arbitrary demand for DNA in an anti-corruption case was not sustainable. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1780; Khalid Hameed v. Special Judge Anti-Corruption, Pakpattan (Crl.P.L.A. 106/2023).
records.title: Khalid Hameed v. Special Judge Anti-Corruption, Pakpattan (Crl.P.L.A. 106/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Judicial Confession: Unnatural Detail; Retraction
records.heading: A judicial confession with unnatural detail raises doubt about its voluntariness
records.text: A judicial confession setting out exact dates, times and places of many murders in a structured way looked prepared rather than spontaneous, raising serious doubt about its voluntariness and truth; it could not safely sustain a capital conviction. The judgment also covers the value of a retracted confession and the fair trial guarantee in Art. 10-A. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 308; Ahmed Saeed alias Bharam alias Nagori v. The State (Criminal Appeal 649/2022 in J.P. 385/2019).
records.title: Ahmed Saeed alias Bharam alias Nagori v. The State (Criminal Appeal 649/2022 in J.P. 385/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: S. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: Sudden loss of self-control: case falls under section 302(c) PPC
records.text: Where the accused lost self-control and the occurrence happened on the spur of the moment, the case fell within s. 302(c) PPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 316; Muhammad Nasir Hussain v. The State (Jail Petition 459 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Nasir Hussain v. The State (Jail Petition 459 of 2022)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Minor Victim; Negative DNA; Potency Test
records.heading: Minor victim's testimony can sustain a conviction; negative DNA report is only corroborative
records.text: The identity of rape victims must be protected. The testimony of a minor victim can by itself sustain a conviction. A negative DNA report is only corroborative, and a potency test shows capacity, not commission. Ref: 2026 MLD 1618.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Counsel Cannot Tender Documents in Evidence
records.heading: Counsel cannot tender documents in evidence through his own statement
records.text: Counsel may file and present documents under O. XIII CPC, but documents must be proved through witnesses; counsel cannot tender them in evidence through his own statement, including in family cases. A decree does not bind on paternity a person who was not a party. Ref: 2026 MLD 1693; Naeem Niaz Awan v. Additional District Judge (WP 71795/2023).
records.title: Naeem Niaz Awan v. Additional District Judge (WP 71795/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: First Petition Time-Barred (Art. 181)
records.heading: First execution petition must be filed within three years
records.text: A decree-holder must file the first execution petition within three years under Art. 181 Limitation Act 1908. If he fails, the right to execute is lost and cannot be revived by a later petition under s. 48 CPC. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1785, PLJ 2026 SC 580; Rasheed (deceased) v. Muhammad Azam Khan (Civil Petition 4530 of 2024).
records.title: Rasheed (deceased) v. Muhammad Azam Khan (Civil Petition 4530 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Unauthorised Improvements: No Compensation
records.heading: No compensation for improvements made on another's property without consent
records.text: A person who builds on or improves another's property without the owner's consent, such as a tenant or permissive occupant, does so at his own risk and gains no title or right to compensation. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1967, PLJ 2026 SC 478; Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal 140-P of 2018).
records.title: Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal 140-P of 2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Registered Power of Attorney: Authority to Sell
records.heading: Authority to sell under a registered power of attorney includes an agreement to sell
records.text: A registered power of attorney is presumed duly executed under Art. 95 QSO. Authority to sell includes authority to enter into an antecedent agreement to sell. The High Court erred in revision by reversing concurrent findings on a restrictive reading of the power; appeals allowed and trial and appellate decrees for specific performance restored. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1978; Saad Younis v. Ghulam Bari (C.A. 435-L/2012).
records.title: Saad Younis v. Ghulam Bari (C.A. 435-L/2012)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Co-owner Eviction; Bona Fide Need of Family
records.heading: One co-owner may seek eviction; personal need extends to the landlord's family
records.text: One co-owner can seek eviction on behalf of all. Bona fide personal need extends to the landlord's co-sharers, children and family, and the landlord may choose which premises suit him. Eviction orders upheld; leave refused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1825; Najeeb Ullah v. Syed Shams-ud-Din (Civil Petitions 300-Q, 303-Q to 312-Q of 2025).
records.title: Najeeb Ullah v. Syed Shams-ud-Din (Civil Petitions 300-Q, 303-Q to 312-Q of 2025)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Landlord Sole Judge of Need
records.heading: The landlord is the sole judge of his need and choice of premises
records.text: The landlord is the sole judge of his requirement and choice of premises. His sworn testimony alone can prove bona fide personal need if consistent with the ejectment application. High Court's order set aside for misreading evidence; eviction restored, tenant given six months to vacate. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1931; Nafees Ahmed v. Mst. Shaheen Begum.
records.title: Nafees Ahmed v. Mst. Shaheen Begum

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: PFSA Report: Protocols Requirement Directory
records.heading: Chemical examiner's report: the "full protocols" requirement is directory
records.text: Larger bench (five judges): the requirement to state "full protocols" in a chemical examiner's report under unamended rule 6 of the 2001 Rules is directory; non-compliance does not by itself invalidate the report under s. 36(2) CNSA. Under amended rule 6, naming the recognised tests listed in its Explanation is sufficient compliance. No retrospective effect. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1862, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 337; Baz Khan v. The State (Crl.A. 43/2020).
records.title: Baz Khan v. The State (Crl.A. 43/2020)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Contempt: Non-Implementation of Appointment Order
records.heading: Contempt: conditional and delayed steps are not compliance with an appointment order
records.text: In contempt proceedings over non-implementation of an order to appoint the petitioner as Sub-Inspector in the Punjab Police, the department's conditional and delayed steps were not genuine compliance. The department was warned to implement within 30 days, with liberty to the petitioner to pursue contempt if it did not. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 771.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Challenge to Long-Standing Revenue Entries
records.heading: Challenge to long-standing revenue entries: limitation and the civil court bar
records.text: A suit to restore 1956-57 revenue entries and undo later mutations, after third-party rights had arisen, raised limitation and the civil court bar in s. 172 West Pakistan Land Revenue Act 1967. The courts below reappraised evidence without deciding maintainability; petition converted into appeal and allowed, suit dismissed, respondents left to the revenue hierarchy. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1817, PLJ 2026 SC 415; Nadeem Akhtar (deceased) v. Manzoor Ahmad (C.P.L.A. 1086/2019).
records.title: Nadeem Akhtar (deceased) v. Manzoor Ahmad (C.P.L.A. 1086/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: New Plea before Supreme Court; Unproved Document
records.heading: No new case before the Supreme Court; unproved panchayat nama cannot defeat a sanctioned mutation
records.text: A party cannot set up a new case for the first time before the Supreme Court, and evidence beyond pleadings is of no effect. An unproved panchayat nama could not defeat title shown in a sanctioned mutation; a scribe's evidence cannot replace proof through attesting witnesses. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1905, PLJ 2026 SC 443; Anwar Ali Shah v. Sadiq Ali Shah (C.A. 1410 of 2019).
records.title: Anwar Ali Shah v. Sadiq Ali Shah (C.A. 1410 of 2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 360 CrPC: Correcting Evidence Recorded by Video Link
records.heading: Disputed record of video-link evidence must be compared with the recording and corrected
records.text: S. 360(1) CrPC requires a completed deposition to be read over and corrected; s. 360(2) lets a witness object and requires a memorandum with the correct version. Where a witness disputes the written record of her video-link evidence, the trial court must compare it with the recording and record any correction. Orders refusing this set aside (Art. 10-A). Ref: PLD 2026 SC 498, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 283; Mst. Nayab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1033/2024).
records.title: Mst. Nayab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1033/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay: Substantive Right
records.heading: Statutory delay bail is a substantive right defeated only by concerted delay by the accused
records.text: The third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC gives a substantive right to bail if trial is not concluded in time. Only a visible and concerted effort by the accused to delay the trial defeats it; ordinary adjournments or isolated requests do not. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1834; Muhammad Iqbal v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 449-L/2026).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 449-L/2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Conscious Possession; Custody of Case Property
records.heading: Narcotics in secret cavities: conscious possession and custody of case property not proved
records.text: 27 kg of charas allegedly found in secret cavities of a vehicle: the vehicle and cavities were not produced, ownership was not proved through excise records, the investigating officer and moharrir contradicted each other on who handed over the case property, and no malkhana register or road certificate was produced. Conscious possession and safe custody not proved; acquitted. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1830, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 279; Alam Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 51 of 2023).
records.title: Alam Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 51 of 2023)

records.subject: Character Certificate
records.topic: Minor Conviction on Plea of Guilt
records.heading: Minor conviction on a plea of guilt should not stigmatise a police clearance certificate for all time
records.text: The petitioner was convicted on his own plea of guilt under the Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance 1981 and fined Rs. 1,000. Showing that minor conviction in his police clearance certificate for all time stigmatised him; respondents directed to issue the certificate accordingly. Ref: PLD 2026 Pesh 226.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Gold Ornaments Gifted to Bride
records.heading: Gold ornaments gifted to the bride by her parents are her personal property
records.text: Gold ornaments gifted to the bride by her parents for her exclusive use are her personal property; their retention by the husband or his family can be remedied through the Family Court. Reduction of the decree from 87 to 44 tolas left undisturbed; leave refused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1838.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Child Victim: Testimony; Sentence
records.heading: Child victim's testimony can sustain a conviction; death sentence converted to life
records.text: The testimony of a child victim with a firm core on identity, place, force and threat can sustain a conviction; a restrained narration does not weaken it. On sentence, the court held that proof of guilt does not settle the choice between death and life imprisonment; conviction maintained, death sentence converted to imprisonment for life. Directions issued to protect child victims. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1842.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Tazkiya-tul-Shahood: Credibility of Witness in Qisas
records.heading: A witness in a qisas case must satisfy tazkiya-tul-shahood before being relied upon
records.text: In a case liable to qisas, a witness must satisfy tazkiya-tul-shahood. The Judge must inquire into the witness's credentials, openly or confidentially, through credible persons of the same walk of life, and may use modern technical assistance for this purpose. Ss. 302(a) and 304 PPC. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1187.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 302(b) PPC and Meaning of Tazir
records.heading: Section 302(b) PPC prescribes tazir, with court discretion between death and life imprisonment
records.text: Section 302(b) PPC provides death or life imprisonment as tazir and differs from s. 302(a); strict compliance with s. 304 PPC or Art. 17 QSO is not required. Tazir is punishment other than qisas, not prescribed by the Quran or Sunnah, and the court has discretion between the sentences, subject to giving reasons. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1187.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Scope of Section 302(c) PPC
records.heading: Section 302(c) PPC covers culpable homicide without mens rea, premeditation or ill design
records.text: Section 302(c) PPC covers culpable homicide not amounting to murder, committed without mens rea, premeditation or ill design. The sentence may extend to 25 years at the discretion of the court, and the offender's state of mind, surrounding circumstances and mode of commission are relevant. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1187.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd Committed Due to Provocation
records.heading: Provocation in qatl-i-amd requires four elements and loss of self-control is judged subjectively
records.text: Provocation requires four elements: provoking circumstances, resulting loss of self-control, capacity of the provocation to make an ordinary person lose self-control, and proportionate retaliation. Loss of self-control is judged subjectively. The Court observed that deliberate insult to religious feelings extends the scope of sudden provocation. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1187.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Common Intention or Common Object: Duty of Trial Court
records.heading: Trial court must record a definite finding on common intention or common object
records.text: Where there are several assailants, the court must record a definite finding on s. 34 PPC (common intention) or ss. 148/149 PPC (common object), at the framing of charge and at judgment. Deciding on individual liability after finding common intention is contrary to law. If that finding is negative but guilt is proved, conviction follows the overt act of each assailant. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1187.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Public Confidence in the Judicial Process
records.heading: Public confidence in courts rests on fair and non-discriminatory dispensation of justice
records.text: Courts gain public confidence by fair, equitable and just dispensation of justice, free from discrimination on grounds of gender, race, religion, colour, caste, creed, status or language. Judges must discharge this task with great care and caution so that public confidence is preserved. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1187.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Common Intention or Object: Trial Court Guidelines
records.heading: Trial court must examine the record before charge to decide on common intention
records.text: The Supreme Court directed the trial court to follow ss. 265-C and 265-D CrPC before charge, then to examine the crime report, s. 161 statements, s. 173 report and other documents to decide whether s. 34 or ss. 148/149 PPC applies. If the offence is one of individual liability, s. 302(c) PPC applies and each accused is dealt with according to the allegation, with judicial reasoning. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1187.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Investigation Distinguished from Verification: Police Order 2002
records.heading: Verification under Art. 18(10) of the Police Order 2002 is distinct from investigation
records.text: Tariq Saleem J held that investigation is distinct from verification under Art. 18(10) of the Police Order 2002, and that the scope of verification is limited. Verification is not a synonym of investigation or reinvestigation, which implies collecting evidence to find how the occurrence took place and who was involved. Ref: Muhammad Afzal v. The State etc. (W.P. No. 8830 of 2019); Justice Tariq Saleem.
records.title: Muhammad Afzal v. The State etc. (W.P. No. 8830 of 2019)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 63-A Reference: Detailed Dissent of Mazhar Alam Miankhel J
records.heading: Authority containing the detailed dissent of Mazhar Alam Miankhel J on Art. 63-A
records.text: Authority containing the 17-page detailed dissenting judgment of Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel J in the Art. 186 reference on Art. 63-A and Constitution Petitions Nos. 2 and 9 of 2022. The short order of 17 May 2022 was by a 3 to 2 majority. The post gives no holding of the dissent. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 488; Reference No. 1 of 2022 (Art. 63-A); Constitution Petition No. 2 of 2022; Constitution Petition No. 9 of 2022; Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel.
records.title: Reference No. 1 of 2022 (Art. 63-A); Constitution Petition No. 2 of 2022; Constitution Petition No. 9 of 2022

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Res Gestae and Credibility of Witnesses
records.heading: Statement of the deceased was res gestae and a related eyewitness is not discredited
records.text: Under Art. 19 QSO, a fact so connected with a fact in issue as to form part of the same transaction is relevant, and the statement of the deceased was spontaneous. A witness not named in the FIR is not disbelieved by universal rule, and variations without substantial bearing do not impair credibility. Relationship with the deceased does not by itself defeat an eyewitness. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 66.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death After 19/20 Days: Conviction Under Ss. 324/337-D
records.heading: Death 19 or 20 days after the stabbing did not attract section 302 PPC
records.text: As the deceased died 19/20 days after the occurrence, the court held it unsafe to attribute the death to the stab injuries, so s. 302 PPC was not attracted. The appellant was convicted under ss. 324/337-D PPC and the appeal was partly allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 66.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: Presence at Scene Unproved
records.heading: Eyewitnesses living elsewhere who give no reason for presence are chance witnesses
records.text: Eyewitnesses who were residents of other houses, gave no reason or physical proof of their presence at the scene and did not identify the body at post-mortem are chance witnesses and cannot be relied upon, following Supreme Court authority cited in the judgment. Delay in post-mortem and want of motive were also considered under s. 302(b) PPC. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1159; Fakhar Abbas v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 209 & M.R. No. 7 of 2019), heard 13.10.2021; Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Fakhar Abbas v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 209 & M.R. No. 7 of 2019), heard 13.10.2021

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Circumstance Sufficient
records.heading: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to the benefit of doubt
records.text: For benefit of doubt it is unnecessary to show many circumstances. A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt in the mind of a prudent person suffices, and the benefit is extended to the accused as a matter of right. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1159; Fakhar Abbas v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 209 & M.R. No. 7 of 2019), heard 13.10.2021; Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Fakhar Abbas v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 209 & M.R. No. 7 of 2019), heard 13.10.2021

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Theft of Electricity: Ss. 462-H to 462-M and Cognizance
records.heading: Electricity theft offences are cognizable but the court takes cognizance only on a complaint
records.text: Offences under ss. 462-H to 462-M PPC (Chapter XVII-B, inserted in 2016) were made cognizable and non-bailable, so an FIR may be registered. Under s. 462-O the court takes cognizance only on a complaint, which must be filed with the s. 173 CrPC report, and prosecutors must scrutinise both before forwarding them to the court. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1152.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 145 CrPC: Actual Possession Only
records.heading: Section 145 CrPC Magistrate decides only actual possession, not entitlement to property
records.text: Under s. 145 CrPC the Magistrate determines only actual physical possession on the relevant date and cannot decide entitlement to the property. A dispute concerning land, water or boundaries must give rise to a breach of peace, and apprehension alone does not suffice. As the parties were already litigating before a competent court, the application was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1137.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report: Administrative Order Not Revisable
records.heading: Direction to submit a challan after a cancellation report is administrative and not revisable
records.text: A Magistrate's direction to submit a s. 173 CrPC report after disagreeing with a police cancellation report is an administrative order under the Police Rules 1934 (Rr. 24.7 and 25.7) and the High Court Rules and Orders, and is not revisable, though its validity can be examined under s. 561-A CrPC. A summoning order is judicial, and revision against it is maintainable. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1128.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape by a Child: Maturity of Understanding
records.heading: Child assessed at 10 to 12 years protected by section 83 PPC
records.text: A convicted appellant assessed by the medical board as 10 to 12 years old was protected by s. 83 PPC, as no evidence showed he had attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature of the offence under s. 376 PPC. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and the appellant was acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1123.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Appeal: Eyewitnesses, Alibi, Non-Production of Witnesses
records.heading: Murder conviction upheld despite non-production of every witness and an unproved alibi
records.text: Conviction under s. 302 PPC was upheld. The FIR gave full details of the occurrence and roles, two eyewitnesses remained on the prosecution record after the complainant died, and the prosecution need not produce every witness. The accused's unexplained long disappearance and plea of alibi carried no weight. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1091.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Defect in Charge: Failure of Justice Required
records.heading: A defective charge is fatal only if the accused were misled and justice failed
records.text: An omission by the trial court in framing the charge under ss. 221, 222, 223, 225, 232 and 239 CrPC is fatal to the prosecution only if the accused show that they were misled in their defence and that a failure of justice resulted. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1091.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Section 489-F PPC
records.heading: Delay in FIR is not always fatal in a section 489-F PPC bail case
records.text: In pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC for an offence under s. 489-F PPC, delay in FIR is not always fatal. The executant of a promissory note bearing the firm's stamp cannot avoid personal liability by adding words showing representative capacity. 'Dishonestly' in s. 489-F means a fraudulent act or intent to defraud, especially creditors. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1083.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 265-D CrPC: Scrutiny Before Framing Charge
records.heading: Before charge the court must scrutinise the police report and may discharge the accused
records.text: Before framing charge the court must examine the police report and documents under s. 265-D CrPC, frame charge if sufficient material exists and otherwise discharge the accused. A discharged accused may be summoned later if evidence emerges. Prosecutors must scrutinise police reports under s. 9(5) of the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service Act 2006. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1074.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Major Penalty on CCTV Footage Without Forensic Audit
records.heading: A major penalty cannot rest solely on unverified and uncorroborated CCTV footage
records.text: A major penalty for taking a bribe cannot rest solely on CCTV footage that was never sent for forensic examination, was not produced before the Service Tribunal and was uncorroborated, where no regular inquiry was held and the alleged bribe givers were not associated. The Service Tribunal rightly set aside the penalties of compulsory retirement and reduction in rank. Ref: 2022 PLC (C.S.) 474, 2021 SCMR 1077.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supply of Section 161 Statements to Accused
records.heading: The accused is entitled to section 161 statements recorded as daryaft under Article 10A
records.text: Under the right to fair trial (Art. 10A), an accused is entitled to inculpatory and exculpatory material, including s. 161 CrPC statements recorded as 'daryaft' in police diaries from persons who are not prosecution witnesses. Supply of such statements was directed. Ref: 2022 MLD 523; Tahir Zahoor Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Revisions Nos. 68 and 69 of 2021).
records.title: Tahir Zahoor Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Revisions Nos. 68 and 69 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Copy of CCTV Footage Not Within Section 265-C
records.heading: A copy of CCTV footage is not a document under section 265-C CrPC
records.text: A copy of CCTV footage does not fall within the documents listed in s. 265-C CrPC and, even if it did, supply may be withheld in the public interest. As the prosecution offered a transcript and the accused can view the footage at trial and answer under s. 342 CrPC, no prejudice arose and the request was refused. Ref: 2022 MLD 523; Tahir Zahoor Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Revisions Nos. 68 and 69 of 2021).
records.title: Tahir Zahoor Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Revisions Nos. 68 and 69 of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage and CDR: Admissibility
records.heading: Blurred CCTV footage and an unproved call data record were not relied upon
records.text: CCTV footage without clear visuals and with blurred features of the culprits was discarded. Call Data Record was inadmissible because no record keeper of the cellular company appeared to prove it. The appeal was dismissed with modification of sentences. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 664; Rashed alias Chand v. State.
records.title: Rashed alias Chand v. State

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Report: Significance in Establishing Identity
records.heading: DNA match between crime scene sample and suspect helps establish identity
records.text: DNA can be taken from biological material such as blood, semen, saliva or hair, and a match between a crime scene sample and the suspect's profile generally indicates the same biological origin. As DNA is resilient to tampering, it is of great help where the identity of the accused is in doubt. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 664; Rashed alias Chand v. State.
records.title: Rashed alias Chand v. State

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Margalla Hills National Park: Illegal Construction
records.heading: Margalla Hills construction declared illegal and armed forces cannot engage in business activity
records.text: The Islamabad High Court, in its detailed judgment, declared construction in the Margalla Hills National Park illegal, including the Navy Golf Course and the lease between the Army Farms Directorate and the Monal restaurant. The armed forces have no authority to engage directly or indirectly in business activity outside their remit.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Deputy Speaker's Ruling on No-Confidence Motion Unconstitutional
records.heading: Deputy Speaker's ruling rejecting the no-confidence motion was unconstitutional
records.text: In the detailed 86-page judgment authored by the Chief Justice, the Supreme Court unanimously held the Deputy Speaker's Art. 5(1) ruling rejecting the no-confidence motion unconstitutional. Under Art. 95(2) the Speaker was bound to hold the vote. The Court was unpersuaded by the foreign interference plea. Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel and Jamal Khan Mandokhail JJ added separate notes. Ref: Suo motu case on ruling of Deputy Speaker National Assembly (Qasim Suri) under Art. 5(1); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Suo motu case on ruling of Deputy Speaker National Assembly (Qasim Suri) under Art. 5(1)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Res Judicata in Section 22-A(6) CrPC Proceedings
records.heading: Res judicata applies to section 22-A(6) CrPC applications but not to a private complaint
records.text: The principle of res judicata applies to applications under s. 22-A(6) CrPC seeking a direction to register an FIR under s. 154 CrPC, so a second application is not maintainable. It does not bar a private complaint, which is an independent statutory remedy. Ref: Shahzad v. Ex-officio Justice of Peace etc. (W.P. No. 80439/2021, decided 30.03.2022).
records.title: Shahzad v. Ex-officio Justice of Peace etc. (W.P. No. 80439/2021, decided 30.03.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Limited Estate of Muslim Female: Succession on Termination
records.heading: Limited estate of a Muslim female passes to the last owner's Shariat heirs
records.text: On the death or marriage of a Muslim female holding a limited interest under custom, succession opens in favour of those who would have inherited the last full owner had Shariat law applied at his death, and an heir who died meanwhile is represented by his own heirs. The post discusses s. 3 of the West Punjab Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1948 and the 1962 Act. Ref: Faiz Ullah and others v. Dilawar Hussain and others (Civil Appeal No. 97/2003).
records.title: Faiz Ullah and others v. Dilawar Hussain and others (Civil Appeal No. 97/2003)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Section 4 MFLO: Inheritance of Grandchildren
records.heading: Section 4 MFLO remains law and grandchildren of a predeceased child may inherit
records.text: Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 remains subsisting law, so children of a predeceased son or daughter are entitled to inherit, until the Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court upholds the Federal Shariat Court decision in the Allah Rakha case or dismisses the appeal. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1352, PLJ 2024 SC 20; Mst. Kalsoom Begum v. Peran Ditta, etc. (Civil Appeal No. 1348 of 2014).
records.title: Mst. Kalsoom Begum v. Peran Ditta, etc. (Civil Appeal No. 1348 of 2014)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: Leave Granted: Section 20 PECA and Freedom of Speech
records.heading: Leave granted to consider whether section 20 PECA violates Article 19
records.text: Leave to appeal was granted to consider whether s. 20 PECA violates Art. 19, whether criminalising defamation dilutes freedom of speech and the defence of truth, how parallel civil and criminal defamation proceedings affect Art. 10A, and whether petitioners could approach the Supreme Court without filing an ICA. The post records no decision. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1267.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Witness Turning Hostile
records.heading: A witness resiling from her statement is no ground for post-arrest bail
records.text: A witness resiling from her s. 161 CrPC statement and filing a private complaint with a different story is not a ground for post-arrest bail under s. 497(2) CrPC. The High Court's bail order was illegal and perverse, so the petition was converted into appeal, allowed and bail cancelled. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1299.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sudden Occurrence: Conversion to Section 302(c) PPC
records.heading: Sudden occurrence without premeditation fell under section 302(c) PPC
records.text: Where the occurrence was sudden without premeditation, the accused side was also injured, the head injury role was enlarged to three accused in the private complaint (two acquitted) and medical evidence showed one head injury, the case fell under s. 302(c) PPC. The petitioner was convicted under s. 302(c) and sentenced to the period already undergone, over 15 years. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1328.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Affirmative Action for Overseas Pakistanis
records.heading: Overseas Pakistanis form a distinct class justifying affirmative action under Article 25
records.text: Overseas Pakistanis cannot pursue cases as efficiently as local residents and so form a distinct class on an intelligible differentia (Art. 25). Public institutions may take affirmative action and make special provisions to protect their lawful rights. The Court appreciated the Lahore High Court's administrative measures and the Punjab legislation. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1282.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Buyer's Obligation to Tender Balance Sale Consideration
records.heading: A buyer must prove readiness to pay the balance or deposit it in court
records.text: A buyer's primary obligation is to pay the balance consideration. If the seller refuses payment, the buyer must show the money was kept ready, for example by pay order or cashier cheque, or deposit it in court. The petitioners had done neither. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1216.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 84 QSO: Comparison of Signatures
records.heading: Article 84 QSO permits comparison of signatures but no presumption arises from omission
records.text: Article 84 QSO enables the court to compare signatures, but if the court did not do so, no presumption arises from that omission. Counsel could not show that the disputed signature was sent with admitted signatures for forensic examination. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1216.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Power of Attorney: Construction and Attorney's Dealing With Property
records.heading: An attorney dealing with the principal's property for himself must first obtain consent
records.text: A power of attorney is construed strictly, and the principal may revoke it at any time unless it is coupled with consideration (s. 2 Powers of Attorney Act 1882; s. 202 Contract Act). An attorney who sells or gifts the principal's property to himself or his next of kin, or buys it for his own benefit, must first consult the principal and obtain consent after disclosing all material circumstances. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1398.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 117, 95, 79, 129 QSO and Registration Act
records.heading: Authority on Articles 117, 95, 79 and 129 QSO and the Registration Act
records.text: Authority discussing Arts. 117, 95, 79 and 129 QSO and ss. 32 and 33 of the Registration Act in a suit for declaration, and noting that surrender presupposes possession or ownership of the thing given up while release is the discharge of a right of action. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1398.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Husband Accused of Wife's Murder: Acquittal on Doubts
records.heading: Husband's conviction for killing his wife set aside on doubts and acquittal ordered
records.text: A husband's conviction under s. 302(b) PPC for killing his wife was set aside. The absence of the deceased's father as a witness, an autopsy showing no ligature mark with an intact hyoid bone, four eyewitnesses who did not intervene and an unchallenged co-accused acquittal raised doubts. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1358.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 122 QSO: Onus on Husband for Wife's Death
records.heading: Husband must explain his wife's homicidal death in his house under Article 122 QSO
records.text: In incidents of domestic violence, especially the homicidal death of a wife in her husband's house, a heavy onus lies on the husband to explain satisfactorily the circumstances leading to the tragedy, under Art. 122 QSO. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1358.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Right of Cross-Examination: Defence Cannot Be Struck Off
records.heading: Defence cannot be struck off in criminal proceedings and cross-examination cannot be denied
records.text: The concept of striking off the defence is alien to criminal proceedings. Under Art. 10A, depriving an accused of the opportunity to cross-examine a witness deposing against him violates the fundamental right to fair trial. The petition was converted into appeal and allowed, and the trial court was directed to afford cross-examination of PWs 3 to 5 within one month. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1360.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Constabulary Punishments, Fair Trial and Double Jeopardy
records.heading: Authority on constabulary punishments, fair trial, natural justice and double jeopardy
records.text: Authority discussing r. 17 of the North West Frontier Constabulary Rules 1958 with ss. 8 to 13 of the Constabulary Act 1915 on punishments, the right to fair trial under Art. 10A, natural justice, double jeopardy under Art. 13 and the maxims nemo bis punitur and interest reipublicae. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1387.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Poast Recovery: Chemical Examiner Report and Sentence
records.heading: Poast is a narcotic only at 0.2 percent morphine, so sentence was reduced
records.text: Poast in mixture form is a narcotic substance under s. 2(t)(iii) CNSA only if it contains 0.2 percent morphine. The Chemical Examiner's report gave no percentage and no quantity of sack, so the applicable limb of s. 9 could not be determined. Conviction for 1650 kg was maintained but life imprisonment was reduced to the period undergone. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1375.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Power of Attorney: Agent's Duties and Repudiation
records.heading: An agent owes fiduciary duties and the principal may repudiate undisclosed self-dealing
records.text: The relation of principal and agent is fiduciary. The agent must act for the principal's benefit, take his instructions at every stage and avoid conflict of interest. Where the agent deals on his own account without consent and conceals material facts, or the dealing is disadvantageous to the principal, the principal may repudiate it under s. 215 Contract Act and courts may rescind it. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1262.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Private University Not Amenable to Writ Jurisdiction
records.heading: A private university is not amenable to writ jurisdiction under Article 199
records.text: The University of Management and Technology, Lahore, being a private sector university, does not perform functions in connection with the affairs of the Federation, a Province or a local authority under Art. 199(1)(a), and is therefore not amenable to judicial review. Ref: 2022 CLC 1328.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Section 284 Punjab Local Government Act: Power to Seal Premises
records.heading: Section 284 allows sealing of premises only for public health, safety or welfare
records.text: Under s. 284 of the Punjab Local Government Act 2019, the Inspector or Enforcement Officer may seal premises only if satisfied that it is in the interest of public health, safety, convenience or welfare, or to avoid danger to life or property. Sealing shops merely for unapproved construction, without a serious threat, was prima facie unjustified and encroached on fundamental rights. Ref: 2022 CLC 1261.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Sealing of Shops: Inquiry and Hearing Required
records.heading: A running business cannot be sealed without proper inquiry and hearing
records.text: A running business cannot be sealed without proper inquiry and hearing. A bare notice does not satisfy audi alteram partem. The power under s. 284 is not unbridled, must be used sparingly after inquiry and notice, and must rest on rational reasons. Ref: 2022 CLC 1261.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Defamation: Proper Apology Under Section 5(e)
records.heading: An apology published after judgment to avoid damages is not a proper apology
records.text: For the defence of proper apology under s. 5(e) of the Defamation Ordinance 2002, the offer to tender and publish the apology must be voluntary. An apology published after the trial court's judgment to avoid payment of damages is not a proper apology. The appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2010 CLD 1175.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutation Attested During Donee's Minority
records.heading: A gift mutation attested without the minor donee required determination of her age
records.text: A gift mutation attested on the donor's statement alone, without the donee who claimed to be a minor, required determination of her age. A person under eighteen is a minor under s. 3 Majority Act 1875 and cannot contract under s. 11 Contract Act. Under s. 6 Limitation Act 1908 she had to sue within the period after attaining majority. Ref: 2022 LHC 5316; Hayat etc. v. Fateh Khatoon (Civil Revision 495-13, decided 20.06.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Hayat etc. v. Fateh Khatoon (Civil Revision 495-13, decided 20.06.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Confession After Plea of Not Guilty at Charge
records.heading: Court cannot convict on a later confession after a plea of not guilty
records.text: Where the accused pleads not guilty at charge and claims trial, the court has no discretion to record his confession later and convict without prosecution evidence. After denial under s. 242 CrPC, s. 243 becomes inoperative and the court proceeds under s. 244. The confession was held not to be voluntary. Ref: Muhammad Alamgir v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 316 of 2015, decided 14.06.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Alamgir v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 316 of 2015, decided 14.06.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 382-B CrPC Benefit After Decision of Appeal
records.heading: Court may extend section 382-B CrPC benefit under section 561-A even after appeal is decided
records.text: Under s. 561-A CrPC the court has inherent power to extend the benefit of s. 382-B CrPC in appropriate cases even after the appeal is decided. The test is whether the trial court considered relevant facts in withholding it. Since 'shall' replaced 'may' in 1979, the provision is mandatory. Ref: Naseer Ahmad v. The State and two others (W.P. No. 4822 of 2022, decided 21.06.2022).
records.title: Naseer Ahmad v. The State and two others (W.P. No. 4822 of 2022, decided 21.06.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 540 CrPC: Summoning Court Witness
records.heading: A section 540 CrPC application cannot be dismissed summarily as belated
records.text: Section 540 CrPC gives the court wide power to examine any witness at any stage, with a discretionary and an obligatory part. An application cannot be dismissed summarily as belated or as filling a lacuna without considering whether the witness's examination is essential for a just decision. Ref: The State v. Ahmed Yar (Criminal Appeal No. 297 of 2022, decided 07.06.2022).
records.title: The State v. Ahmed Yar (Criminal Appeal No. 297 of 2022, decided 07.06.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Witnesses Unharmed Despite Motive: Presence Doubtful
records.heading: Witnesses unharmed despite the accused's motive and firing range are doubtfully present
records.text: Where the accused had a motive against the complainant or witnesses but caused them no harm although they were within firing range, this indicates that the witnesses were not present at the place of occurrence. Ref: Muhammad Maqbool alias Allah Wasaya and another v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 122 of 2020; Murder Reference No. 07 of 2020), heard 07.06.2022.
records.title: Muhammad Maqbool alias Allah Wasaya and another v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 122 of 2020; Murder Reference No. 07 of 2020), heard 07.06.2022

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unproved Light Source and Unharmed Witnesses
records.heading: Failure to prove a light source at the scene is fatal to the prosecution
records.text: Failure to prove a light source at the place and time of occurrence is fatal to the prosecution case, and the court cannot presume one. Where the accused had a motive against the witnesses but did not harm them within firing range, they had not witnessed the occurrence. Ref: Javaid v. The State and another (Crl. A.
