No. 240557 of 2018; Murder Reference No. 323 of 2018), heard 25.05.2022.
records.title: Javaid v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 240557 of 2018; Murder Reference No. 323 of 2018), heard 25.05.2022

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade and Art. 22 QSO
records.heading: Identification parades serve prosecution and accused alike under Article 22 QSO
records.text: Under Art. 22 QSO, facts establishing the identity of a person whose identity is relevant are always relevant. Identification has a twofold object, to satisfy the investigators and then the court. Identification parades serve the prosecution and the accused alike and are held for persons concerned with the offence. Ref: Shakeel Shah and another v. The State (Crl. A. No. 53076-J of 2019; Murder Reference No. 207 of 2019), heard 19.05.2022.
records.title: Shakeel Shah and another v. The State (Crl. A. No. 53076-J of 2019; Murder Reference No. 207 of 2019), heard 19.05.2022

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 265-C CrPC: Supply of DVD and Fair Trial
records.heading: Non-supply of the DVD under section 265-C CrPC denied the right to fair trial
records.text: Right of fair trial was denied by non-supply of a copy of the DVD/CD under s. 265-C CrPC and by not displaying the videos and photos during prosecution evidence and the s. 342 CrPC examination. The accused must know before trial the evidence to be produced. The trial was confined to ss. 292-A/292-C PPC. Ref: Usman Ali v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No. 395 of 2022), heard 13.07.2022.
records.title: Usman Ali v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No. 395 of 2022), heard 13.07.2022

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Appeal Against Registrar's Refusal to Register Art. 184(3) Petition
records.heading: Registrar's refusal to register an Article 184(3) petition: appeal partly allowed
records.text: An appeal under O. V R. 3 Supreme Court Rules 1980 challenged the Registrar's refusal to register an Art. 184(3) petition on grounds including an individual grievance (1998 SCMR 793), defective notice and absence of public importance. The appeal was partly allowed, with the petition to be fixed before an appropriate Bench. Ref: Qausain Faisal (Advocate Supreme Court) v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Interior and others (C.M. Appeal 87/2022), decided 18.07.2022; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Qausain Faisal (Advocate Supreme Court) v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Interior and others (C.M. Appeal 87/2022), decided 18.07.2022

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Muharram Processions: Traditional and Licensed
records.heading: Authority on licensed and traditional Muharram processions
records.text: Authority on permission for Muharram processions, noting two kinds observed by Shia Muslims: the licensed procession, usually of Tazia and Zuljinnah on 10th Muharram, and the traditional procession, being any other procession. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2022 LHC 5709; Shamim Haider etc. v. Addl. Chief Secretary Home Lahore etc. (Writ Petition-Religion-1915-22), decided 19.07.2022; Justice Sohail Nasir.
records.title: Shamim Haider etc. v. Addl. Chief Secretary Home Lahore etc. (Writ Petition-Religion-1915-22), decided 19.07.2022

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Assembly Security During Election of Chief Minister
records.heading: Assembly security handles election proceedings and police are requisitioned only if appropriate
records.text: The internal security of the Assembly is responsible for security during the election proceedings. Police help may be requisitioned only when the Presiding Officer and Assembly authorities consider it appropriate on a law and order situation, and not unnecessarily, so that members do not apprehend an unfair election. Ref: 2022 LHC 5787; Muhammad Sibtain Khan v. Deputy Speaker Provincial Assembly for the Province of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 45456/22), decided 22.07.2022; Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Sibtain Khan v. Deputy Speaker Provincial Assembly for the Province of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 45456/22), decided 22.07.2022

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Promissory Note: Proof and Section 118(a) Presumption
records.heading: Authority on proof of a promissory note and the section 118(a) presumption
records.text: Authority on whether a promissory note must be proved by producing marginal witnesses, the effect of the presumption as to consideration for negotiable instruments, and how the s. 118(a) Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 presumption can be rebutted. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2022 LHC 5719; Allah Ditta v. Zulfiqar (Civil Revision 82-22), decided 18.07.2022; Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Allah Ditta v. Zulfiqar (Civil Revision 82-22), decided 18.07.2022

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Extraordinary Relief Against Abuse of Law
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is extraordinary relief against victimisation through abuse of law
records.text: Pre-arrest bail is extraordinary relief granted to protect innocent persons from victimisation and humiliation through abuse of law for ulterior motive. An accused with a good case for post-arrest bail should not be sent to jail for a few days merely at the complainant's wish by dismissing pre-arrest bail. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1254.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Marriage Without Iddat: Irregular and Not Zina
records.heading: Marriage without iddat is irregular and does not amount to zina
records.text: A marriage contracted without observing iddat is irregular, and is not void, so it does not amount to the cognizable offence of zina under s. 4 and s. 5 of the Offence of Zina (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance 1979. The petition seeking a zina case against the couple was dismissed. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1188; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 540 CrPC: Re-Summoning of Witness and Lacuna
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC permits re-summoning of a witness and prosecutor's oversight is no lacuna
records.text: Under s. 540 CrPC the court has plenary power to summon, recall or re-examine a witness at any stage if necessary for a just decision. An oversight by the prosecutor is not an irreparable lacuna, which means an inherent weakness in the prosecution case. Revision against re-summoning was dismissed. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1214.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 63-A Reference: Votes of Defecting Members
records.heading: A defecting member's vote under Article 63-A will not be counted
records.text: By a 3 to 2 majority on the presidential reference on Art. 63-A, the Supreme Court held that the vote of a defecting member will not be counted and that Parliament may legislate on the period of disqualification. The fourth question on the period was not answered and the pending Art. 186 and Art. 184(3) matters were disposed of. Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel and Jamal Khan Mandokhail JJ recorded dissenting notes. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 488; Presidential Reference under Art. 186 on interpretation of Art. 63-A; Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Presidential Reference under Art. 186 on interpretation of Art. 63-A

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Binding Effect of Supreme Court Benches
records.heading: An earlier Supreme Court Bench judgment binds smaller and equal Benches
records.text: An earlier judgment of a Supreme Court Bench binds Benches of smaller and equal strength. A Bench disagreeing must request the Chief Justice to constitute a larger Bench. A two member Bench should follow a three member Bench and, if it disagrees, refer the matter for a three member Bench, and cannot skip directly to a larger Bench. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 581.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Chief Minister Election: Interim Order on Deputy Speaker's Ruling
records.heading: Interim order on the Deputy Speaker's ruling in the Punjab Chief Minister election
records.text: In an interim written order on the petition against the Deputy Speaker's ruling in the Punjab Chief Minister election, the Supreme Court directed replies by 11 am on 25 July, fixed hearing for Monday and required production of the record, including the party head's letter. It observed that the province cannot be left without a Chief Minister and cabinet, and that Hamza Shehbaz continued as trustee Chief Minister. Ref: Chaudhary Parvez Elahi v. The Deputy Speaker Provincial Assembly of Punjab Lahore, etc. (Const. P. 22/2022), decided 23.07.2022; Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Chaudhary Parvez Elahi v. The Deputy Speaker Provincial Assembly of Punjab Lahore, etc. (Const. P. 22/2022), decided 23.07.2022

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Safe Custody and Transmission of Samples
records.heading: Prosecution must prove safe custody and transmission of sample parcels to the laboratory
records.text: In a s. 9(c) CNSA case, the prosecution must establish safe custody and safe transmission of sample parcels to the Forensic Science Laboratory. Non-production of the Moharrar Investigation and the constable who took the parcels, without plausible explanation, went to the root of the case and created serious doubt. Benefit of doubt extended to the accused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1006.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Weapon Without Empties
records.heading: Recovery of a revolver is inconsequential where no empty was recovered
records.text: Recovery of a revolver from the accused had no impact where no empty was recovered from the place of occurrence. A dent in the prosecution case was created and its benefit had to go to the accused. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1148.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Use of Evidence Recorded in Another Trial
records.heading: Evidence recorded in a co-accused's trial cannot support conviction unless exhibited
records.text: Every criminal proceeding must be decided on the material on its own record. A post-mortem report and doctor's statement recorded in the trial of a co-accused, used against the accused without being exhibited, could not support his conviction. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1148.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondment Is Not Proof of Guilt
records.heading: Abscondment is not proof of guilt and cannot alone support conviction
records.text: Abscondment cannot be viewed as proof of the crime, and an accused cannot be convicted on that basis alone. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1148.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Solitary Eye-Witness Statement
records.heading: Conviction may be recorded on the solitary statement of an eye-witness
records.text: A conviction can be recorded on the basis of the solitary statement of an eye-witness. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1148.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Scope and Right
records.heading: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt gives the accused the benefit as of right
records.text: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt in a prudent mind entitles the accused to its benefit as of right and not as a concession. Conviction must rest on unimpeachable, trustworthy and reliable evidence, and any doubt in the prosecution case is resolved in favour of the accused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1148.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Testimony of Witnesses Related to Deceased
records.heading: Relationship with the deceased alone is no ground to discard prosecution witnesses
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony, unless previous enmity or ill will to falsely implicate the accused is established on the record. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1085.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 133: Incomplete Cross-Examination
records.heading: A statement without cross-examination, where the witness became unavailable, has no evidentiary value
records.text: Where the complainant's statement was recorded, cross-examination was reserved, and he later did not make himself available despite efforts to procure his attendance, the statement without cross-examination was not a legal statement. It lost evidentiary value and could not be relied upon as unreliable evidence. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1088.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Proof of Sale Mutation and Sale Consideration
records.heading: Sale and mutation under section 54 TPA not proved and rightly held invalid
records.text: Under s. 54 Transfer of Property Act, the purported vendee failed to prove the sale and its mutation. His witnesses contradicted each other, the patwari and sanctioning revenue officer were not examined, and no reliable evidence of payment of consideration was produced. The High Court rightly held the sale and mutation invalid. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1009.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Reasonable and Natural Gift
records.heading: A gift to a daughter-in-law and granddaughters for financial security was reasonable and valid
records.text: A father whose son had remarried transferred some property to his first daughter-in-law (also his niece) and to his granddaughters for their financial security. The gift mutation appeared reasonable and natural and was held valid. Appeal partially allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1009.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 120: Accrual of Right to Sue for Declaration
records.heading: Right to sue for a declaration accrues on denial of the right
records.text: Art. 120 Limitation Act does not say when the right to sue accrues; this is read with s. 42 Specific Relief Act. The right to sue for a declaration accrues when the other party denies or is interested to deny the right. If a donor or seller does not challenge an actual denial within time despite knowledge, the claim is barred. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1009.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 18 Limitation Act: Fraud and Date of Knowledge
records.heading: Fraud and knowledge must be pleaded and proved to invoke section 18 Limitation Act
records.text: S. 18 Limitation Act postpones limitation to the date fraud first became known, but the plaintiff must plead the fraud, its particulars and date of knowledge (O. VI R. 4 CPC) and prove it. In a challenge by an heir to a 1977 gift mutation after 32 years, the donor's knowledge governed, and s. 18 did not save the suit. Appeal partially allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1009.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Law Requiring Act in Particular Manner
records.heading: What the law requires in a particular manner must be done in that manner
records.text: Where the law stipulates that something must be done in a particular manner, it must be done in that manner. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1021.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 10A: Meaning of Due Process
records.heading: Due process under Article 10A is undefined and read with the whole Constitution
records.text: The Constitution does not define due process, and its scope should not be limited by definition. Due process incorporates universally accepted standards of justice independent of any particular law and is understood holistically with the entire Constitution, which excludes arbitrary power, authoritarianism and autocratic rule. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1021.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Water Crisis Writ Petition
records.heading: Authority on a writ petition concerning a water crisis
records.text: Authority on a writ petition concerning a water crisis. The post gives only the citation and topic, without the holding. Ref: 2022 LHC 5908; Usman Ghani etc v. Rawalpindi Metropolitan RWP etc (Writ Petition 2046-22, decided 23.07.2022); Justice Sohail Nasir.
records.title: Usman Ghani etc v. Rawalpindi Metropolitan RWP etc (Writ Petition 2046-22, decided 23.07.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Against Interlocutory Order on Bank Guarantee
records.heading: Constitution petition is maintainable where no appeal or revision lies against an interlocutory order
records.text: Neither appeal nor revision lay against an interlocutory order requiring a bank guarantee and surety bond for suspension of an ex-parte decree, so a constitution petition was maintainable for want of an equally efficacious alternate remedy. The office objection was overruled, without precluding a decision on maintainability on merits at the main hearing. Ref: 2022 LHC 5931; Hafiz Muhammad Awais etc v. Learned ADSJ Lahore etc (Objection Case 106921/22, decided 20.07.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Hafiz Muhammad Awais etc v. Learned ADSJ Lahore etc (Objection Case 106921/22, decided 20.07.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Chief Minister Election: Deputy Speaker Ruling Set Aside
records.heading: Deputy Speaker's ruling in the Punjab Chief Minister election was declared void
records.text: A three-member bench accepted the petition against the Deputy Speaker's ruling of 22.07.2022 in the Punjab Chief Minister election and declared the ruling void. Parvez Elahi was declared Chief Minister, the new cabinet notification and appointments made by Hamza Shehbaz were set aside, and the Governor was directed to administer the oath. Ref: Chaudhry Parvez Elahi v. Deputy Speaker, Provincial Assembly of Punjab, Lahore and others (Constitution Petition No. 22 of 2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar.
records.title: Chaudhry Parvez Elahi v. Deputy Speaker, Provincial Assembly of Punjab, Lahore and others (Constitution Petition No. 22 of 2022)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Appealability of Contempt Orders
records.heading: Only orders finally terminating contempt proceedings are appealable
records.text: Only orders and judgments that finally terminate contempt proceedings against the contemnor are appealable. Where the court whose order is allegedly disobeyed, in its discretion, refuses to initiate contempt proceedings, that order cannot be questioned before the appellate forum. Ref: 2022 MLD 1248.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 16: Policy Banning Events and Judicial Review
records.heading: An event ban is an executive policy decision with limited judicial review
records.text: The right to assemble under Art. 16 is subject to limits. A ban on sports, festivals and cultural events is an executive policy decision, which the High Court under Art. 199 may examine only if it smacks of mala fide or offends fundamental rights. Ref: 2022 MLD 1267.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 344 CrPC: Costs on Adjournment
records.heading: The power to grant adjournment under section 344 CrPC includes imposing costs
records.text: Frequent adjournments sought by parties cause unnecessary delay in trial. The words 'on such terms' in s. 344 CrPC include power to impose costs when granting an adjournment, and this power is inherent in the court for safe administration of justice. Ref: 2022 MLD 1331.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Transfer of Execution of Family Court Decree
records.heading: A Family Court cannot send execution to another district except through the High Court
records.text: A Family Court cannot directly send execution proceedings to another district. Under s. 25-A Family Courts Act 1964, execution can go to another district only through the High Court. The District Judge may transfer execution between Family Courts within the district, and the Supreme Court may transfer it between provinces. Ref: 2022 MLD 1289.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Drawing Up of Decree Sheet: No Limitation
records.heading: No limitation applies to drawing up a decree sheet, and parties are not penalised
records.text: The court must draw up the decree sheet, and no limitation is prescribed for doing so under O. XX R. 7 CPC. A litigant need not remind the court of this duty, and a party cannot be penalised for the court's omission or neglect. Ref: 2022 MLD 1203.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: PTI Prohibited Funding Case: ECP Order
records.heading: Election Commission held that PTI received prohibited funding and issued a forfeiture show cause notice
records.text: The Election Commission held that PTI received prohibited funds from foreign individuals and companies and held accounts not disclosed. It found the Form I filed by the party chairman incorrect and the affidavit on party accounts false. A show cause notice was issued as to why the prohibited funds should not be forfeited. Ref: Akbar Sher Babar v. PTI (decided 02.08.2022).
records.title: Akbar Sher Babar v. PTI (decided 02.08.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Investigation: Art. 18A Police Order
records.heading: Article 18A Police Order 2002 prescribes the procedure for transfer of investigation
records.text: Neither the Code nor the Police Rules 1934 provide a procedure for transfer of investigation. Art. 18A Police Order 2002, inserted by the 2013 amendment, requires the first application to the Head of District Police, who seeks the DSB's opinion within seven working days, with a further route to the Regional Police Officer after RSB opinion. Courts evaluate contradictory police opinions on established principles. Ref: Afzal Ahmad v. City Police Officer, Faisalabad etc. (Writ Petition No. 21663 of 2021, decided 21.03.2022).
records.title: Afzal Ahmad v. City Police Officer, Faisalabad etc. (Writ Petition No. 21663 of 2021, decided 21.03.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 491 CrPC After Registration of FIR
records.heading: Judgment on maintainability of section 491 CrPC after registration of an FIR
records.text: Judgment on the maintainability of s. 491 CrPC after registration of an FIR, concerning recovery of a woman detenue and her child. The court discussed the legislative background on trafficking in women and contemplated a continuous mandamus to secure supervision of recovery by law enforcement agencies. Ref: Kalsoom Mai v. DPO, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 5159 of 2022, decided 29.07.2022).
records.title: Kalsoom Mai v. DPO, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 5159 of 2022, decided 29.07.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental and Criminal Proceedings: Police Dismissal
records.heading: Departmental proceedings and criminal prosecution can run concurrently with different standards of proof
records.text: Departmental disciplinary proceedings and criminal prosecution differ in standard of proof and can run concurrently. Acquittal in the criminal case does not conclusively establish suitability of the candidate. A member of a disciplined force must have utmost integrity, a spotless character and clean antecedents. Ref: Faraz Naveed v. District Police Officer, Gujrat and another (C.P. 3122/2020, decided 28.02.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Faraz Naveed v. District Police Officer, Gujrat and another (C.P. 3122/2020, decided 28.02.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Columns 13 and 16: Intention of Parties
records.heading: Nikahnama clauses are construed by the parties' intention, whatever the column heading
records.text: A Nikahnama is a marriage contract whose clauses are construed according to the intention of the parties, irrespective of the heading of the column in which a term is entered. Courts must ascertain the true intent, since Nikah registrars are mostly laymen. The High Court rightly treated four kanal of agricultural land entered in column 16 as agreed dower. Ref: Haseen Ullah v. Mst. Naheed Begum & others (C.P. 1289/2020); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Haseen Ullah v. Mst. Naheed Begum & others (C.P. 1289/2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Transfer of Execution of Family Court Decree
records.heading: A Family Court cannot send execution to another district except through the High Court
records.text: A Family Court cannot directly send execution proceedings to another district. Under s. 25-A Family Courts Act 1964, execution can go to another district only through the High Court. The District Judge may transfer execution between Family Courts within the district, and the Supreme Court may transfer it between provinces. Ref: 2022 MLD 1280.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Withdrawal of Suit Against Sale Mutation: Bar on Fresh Suit
records.heading: Withdrawal of a suit against a sale mutation bars re-agitating it in another's suit
records.text: A person who withdraws his suit challenging a sale mutation loses the cause of action to re-agitate the matter in a suit by another, whether as co-plaintiff or proforma defendant supporting the plaintiff. He may still defend his stance on the matter as a defendant. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1282.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Possession Follows Title: Section 39 Land Revenue Act
records.heading: Possession follows title under section 39 of the Land Revenue Act 1967
records.text: Under s. 39 of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Act 1967, possession follows title, and an owner is presumed to be in possession of his property unless the contrary is proved by cogent evidence. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1282.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Standard of Proof in Civil Cases
records.heading: Disputed civil facts are decided on preponderance of probability
records.text: Disputed facts in civil cases are ordinarily decided on the evidential standard of preponderance of probability. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1282.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: No Fresh Limitation Where Predecessor Time-Barred
records.heading: No fresh limitation runs where the predecessor's right to sue was time barred
records.text: Under s. 3 of the Limitation Act 1908, when the right to sue of a person from or through whom the plaintiff derives his right has become time barred, no fresh period of limitation starts for the plaintiff. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1282.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Adverse Revenue Entry: Actual Denial and Fresh Cause of Action
records.heading: Limitation runs from takeover of possession and later entries give no fresh cause
records.text: Each new adverse revenue entry is only an apprehended denial of right and gives a person in possession a fresh cause of action for declaration (Art. 120 Limitation Act; s. 42 Specific Relief Act). Where the beneficiary of a sale or gift mutation takes over possession, that is actual denial, limitation runs from it, and later repeated entries give no fresh cause of action. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1282.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Poast: Poppy Plant Parts and Morphine Content
records.heading: Only the sack of the whole poppy plant is poast containing morphine
records.text: Only the sack, pouch or basket of the whole poppy plant is poast and contains morphine, excluding the seeds. Cultivation of poppy straw cannot be considered criminal unless it is proved to be for the sole purpose of extracting narcotics by a proper method. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1375.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 133: Cross-Examination Where Accused Lacks Counsel
records.heading: Where an accused lacks counsel the court should cross-examine the witnesses itself
records.text: Where the accused did not produce counsel to cross-examine prosecution witnesses, the Trial Court should ask the accused to cross-examine himself. If he refuses, the court should cross-examine the witnesses itself, rather than closing the right of cross-examination. Ref: 2022 MLD 1331.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Murderous Assault: Further Inquiry and Doubt at Bail Stage
records.heading: Bail granted under section 497(2) CrPC where the murderous assault case called for further inquiry
records.text: Bail was granted under s. 497(2) CrPC as the case called for further inquiry: unexplained nine-hour delay in the FIR, injury dimensions inconsistent with the alleged weapon, a single shot at a non-vital part, no weapon recovered, and over ten months in custody. Benefit of doubt in the prosecution version may be given at the bail stage. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1245.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Specific Role and Medical Support
records.heading: Bail cancelled where the accused had a specific role supported by medical evidence
records.text: Bail was cancelled where the accused was nominated with a specific allegation of firearm injuries to the abdomen, the occurrence was in broad daylight between persons known to each other, medical evidence supported the injuries, and the offence fell within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Bail had been granted ignoring bail principles. Appeal allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1229.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Further Inquiry in Breach of Trust
records.heading: Bail granted in a section 406 PPC case where entrustment and mens rea were absent
records.text: Bail was granted under s. 497(2) CrPC in a s. 406 PPC case. The only material was a co-accused's inadmissible statement, entrustment and misappropriation with mens rea were absent, nothing was recovered, and the offence did not fall within the prohibitory clause. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1223.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Payment Outside Court to Unauthorised Person
records.heading: Payment outside court to an unauthorised attorney did not satisfy the conditional decree
records.text: Under s. 12 Specific Relief Act, payment outside court to an alleged attorney of the vendors who was not competent to receive it did not satisfy the condition of the conditional decree. Once the petitioners' suit stood dismissed, they could not resist the respondents' suit, which only the vendors could resist. Revision petitions dismissed. Ref: 2022 MLD 1378.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Mala Fide
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail may be confirmed where the case is registered with mala fide intention
records.text: Under s. 498 CrPC, where a case is registered with mala fide intention and ulterior motives and no sufficient evidence exists against the accused, bail before arrest can be confirmed if arrest is sought on that footing. Ref: 2022 MLD 1373.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Female Accused, Forest Fire Video
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed for a woman accused over a forest fire video
records.text: Ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed for a female accused charged over a forest fire seen in her social media video. The Investigation Officer conceded no evidence that she set the fire, most sections were bailable, and an FIR under s. 188 PPC needs a written complaint of the public servant under s. 195 CrPC. Ref: 2022 MLD 1373.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Custody of Judicial Records: Missing Documents
records.heading: A Presiding Officer must act at once to recover or reconstruct missing record
records.text: Under Vol. IV, Chap. 16, Part-D, Cl. (4) of the High Court (Lahore) Rules and Orders, if a document or part of the record is found missing, the Presiding Officer must immediately act to recover or reconstruct it and fix responsibility on the custodian or the relieved official. Ref: 2022 CLC 1368.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Email Printout as Primary Evidence
records.heading: An email printout is primary evidence under Article 73 QSO
records.text: A printout of an email is output of an automated information system working without active human intervention. It is primary evidence under Art. 73 Qanun-e-Shahadat read with s. 3 Electronic Transactions Ordinance 2002, unless the system is proved not to have been working at the material times. Ref: 2022 CLC 1337.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Scope of Constitutional Jurisdiction
records.heading: Constitutional jurisdiction is extraordinary and discretionary and needs gross misreading or jurisdictional error
records.text: Constitutional jurisdiction is extraordinary and discretionary. The petitioner must show gross misreading or non-reading of evidence, jurisdictional error or legal infirmity causing miscarriage of justice. Interference may be called for on misreading, erroneous assumption of facts, misapplication of law, or excess or abuse of jurisdiction. Ref: 2022 CLC 1337.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Reciprocal Promises and Proof by Email
records.heading: Emails with undenied dispatch and receipt may be relied upon in a reciprocal promises dispute
records.text: In a Higher Education Commission suit against a scholarship student, the Deed of Agreement comprised reciprocal promises (ss. 51 and 52 Contract Act) and the Commission was to make funds available first. Emails whose dispatch and receipt neither party denied could be relied upon. The High Court set aside the judgments below and remanded the matter. Ref: 2022 CLC 1337.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance Is Discretionary Relief
records.heading: Specific performance under section 12 is discretionary even where the agreement is proved
records.text: Specific performance under s. 12 Specific Relief Act is discretionary. Even if the agreement is proved, the court is not bound to decree the suit and may consider other relevant factors. Ref: 2022 CLC 1300.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell Creates No Title: S. 53-A TPA
records.heading: A mere agreement to sell creates no title and cannot restrict the owner
records.text: A mere agreement to sell creates no title and cannot restrict the owner's rights unless proved. If the holder proves execution, s. 53-A Transfer of Property Act protects his rights; otherwise the owner's right to enjoy the property cannot be curtailed. Ref: 2022 CLC 1300.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Proof of Execution of Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Existence of a document does not prove execution where its contents are denied
records.text: Mere existence of a document does not prove execution. Where contents are specifically denied, especially by a Parda observing lady or illiterate person, the beneficiary must prove free consent, knowledge of contents and payment of consideration. The High Court set aside concurrent decrees for misreading of evidence. Ref: 2022 CLC 1300.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: S. 47 CPC: Execution of Ejectment Order and Joint Khata
records.heading: In execution of an ejectment order, joint khata status of the property is irrelevant
records.text: In execution of an ejectment order, the petitioner had to return possession of the rented property, and it was irrelevant whether the property formed part of a joint khata. The petitioner had challenged the dismissal of his application under s. 47 read with O. XIII R. 10 CPC. Ref: 2022 CLC 1296.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 133: Order of Examination of Witnesses
records.heading: Article 133 QSO prescribes examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination in that order
records.text: Art. 133 Qanun-e-Shahadat prescribes the order of examination: examination-in-chief by the calling party, cross-examination by the adverse party if desired, then re-examination by the calling party if desired. It governs how witnesses are dealt with at trial by both prosecution and accused. Ref: 2022 YLR 1742.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Power to Summon or Recall Witness
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC power to summon or recall applies where evidence is essential
records.text: S. 540 CrPC covers three cases: a person not examined and not present, a person present in court though not summoned, and a person already examined who may be recalled and re-examined. The power may be exercised if the evidence appears essential to the just decision of the case. Ref: 2022 YLR 1742.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Meaning of Already Examined
records.heading: A witness is already examined under section 540 CrPC only after examination is complete
records.text: A witness is 'already examined' under s. 540 CrPC only when the Art. 133 procedure has been followed and examination is complete. The Trial Court erred in recalling a witness whose cross-examination had been reserved, before its conclusion. Revision allowed and the order set aside. Ref: 2022 YLR 1742.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Articles Suit: Belated Plea for Additional Issues
records.heading: Husband's belated application for additional issues in a dowry articles suit was refused
records.text: In a wife's suit for dowry articles including a vehicle, the husband's application for additional issues on ownership, made during the appeal after about three years of suit and one and a half years of appeal, came after fatal delay. The Family Court had already dealt with the question. Writ petition dismissed. Ref: 2022 YLR 1678.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXII CPC: Death of Party and S. 12(2)
records.heading: Failure to bring legal representatives on record is not fatal absent serious prejudice
records.text: Failure to bring legal representatives of a deceased party on record is not fatal unless it causes serious prejudice. Daughters of a deceased defendant sought annulment of the appellate decree under s. 12(2) CPC; the other defendants and counsel were also bound to inform the court, and the case did not fall within s. 12(2). Revision dismissed. Ref: 2022 YLR 1665.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Conceding Written Statement by Superseded Counsel
records.heading: A conceding written statement filed by superseded counsel may be discarded on prompt application
records.text: In a suit for specific performance, the previous counsel, despite being superseded by new counsel, filed a conceding written statement. The High Court held the prompt application to discard it could not be summarily declined, set aside the orders and allowed the petition, so a fresh written statement could be filed and the case decided on merits. Ref: 2022 YLR 1660.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1: Second Suit Filed Before Withdrawal of First
records.heading: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC bars suits filed after withdrawal of an earlier suit
records.text: The bar of O. XXIII R. 1 CPC applies to a suit instituted after withdrawal of a previous suit. It does not bar a suit already pending when the earlier suit is withdrawn. Rejection of the plaint was set aside, revision allowed, and the suit held deemed pending before the Trial Court. Ref: 2022 YLR 1536.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1: Withdrawal of Suit with Liberty
records.heading: Withdrawal with liberty to sue afresh is allowed only to cure a formal defect
records.text: Permission to withdraw a suit with liberty to file afresh is granted only to cure an apparent or formal defect, not a latent defect touching merits, and sufficient grounds are a condition precedent. An application under O. XXIII R. 1(2) CPC to circumvent O. VII R. 11 CPC is defective and mala fide. Ref: 2022 YLR 1629.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 129(g): Withholding of Best Evidence
records.heading: Withholding best evidence under Article 129(g) QSO weighed against the plaintiff
records.text: In a claim on a promissory note, a partner-witness failed to produce the account reconciliation agreement and another witness did not produce the accounts he claimed to have seen. Withholding best evidence under Art. 129(g) Qanun-e-Shahadat weighed against the plaintiff, and the appeal was allowed. Ref: 2022 YLR 1583.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summary Suit on Promissory Note: Denial and Proof
records.heading: Denial of a promissory note leaves the section 118 presumption of little avail
records.text: Where execution of a promissory note and consideration were categorically denied, the s. 118 Negotiable Instruments Act presumption was of little avail. Non-disclosure of the note by the plaintiff in a previous suit damaged its probability. Execution and consideration were unproved, so handwriting expert opinion needed no discussion. Appeal allowed. Ref: 2022 YLR 1583.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence
records.heading: Additional evidence under O. XLI R. 27 CPC cannot be allowed to fill lacunas
records.text: Permission to produce additional evidence under O. XLI R. 27 CPC cannot be given merely to fill lacunas left by a party in its evidence. Ref: 2022 YLR 1752.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Local Government Delimitation: Non-Speaking Orders Set Aside
records.heading: Delimitation objections must be decided separately by reasoned order, and non-speaking orders are void
records.text: The Delimitation Authority had to decide each objector's objections separately within thirty days after inquiry under the Elections Rules 2017. A single evasive order without reasons violated s. 24-A General Clauses Act. The High Court declared the delimitations void and referred the petitions to the Election Commission to decide within one month. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 607.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested Witness and Related Witnesses
records.heading: Closely related witnesses of the victim are not interested witnesses
records.text: An interested witness is one who has an ulterior motive for the accused's conviction, and closely related witnesses of the victim do not fall in that category. Substitution of real culprits is a rare phenomenon where eye-witnesses lost their kith and kin before their own eyes. Ref: 2022 YLR 1357.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Policy Decision Shifting Wagon Stand
records.heading: A policy decision to shift a wagon stand was not interfered with
records.text: A Government policy decision to shift the petitioners' wagon stand to the General Bus Stand, to avoid traffic congestion and terrorism threat, was not shown to be illegal, arbitrary or mala fide and the High Court did not interfere. Respondents were directed to provide reasonable facilities for the shift. Ref: 2022 YLR 1647.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Discovery Must Reveal New Fact
records.heading: Article 40 QSO applies only where information leads to discovery of a new fact
records.text: Art. 40 applies only if information from an accused in police custody leads to discovery of a fact not previously learnt from another source. Where the prosecution already knew the details through an alleged extra-judicial confession and the body had been recovered, the later pistol recovery statement and pointing out were inadmissible. Ref: 2022 YLR 1702; Mohsin Abbas v. State.
records.title: Mohsin Abbas v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Intrinsic Worth of Evidence: Inimical Witness
records.heading: Intrinsic worth decides guilt and an inimical witness may be relied upon if corroborated
records.text: Only the intrinsic worth and probative value of evidence decide guilt or innocence. Evidence of an uninterested witness may be corrupted deliberately, while that of an inimical witness, if consistent with and corroborated by other evidence, may be relied upon. Ref: 2022 YLR 1702; Mohsin Abbas v. State.
records.title: Mohsin Abbas v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Complete Chain on Capital Charge
records.heading: A capital conviction on circumstantial evidence needs every link from body to accused
records.text: A conviction on a capital charge on circumstantial evidence needs deep scrutiny, since fabrication is not uncommon. The prosecution must provide all links in the chain, from the dead body to the accused's neck. Here many links were missing. Ref: 2022 YLR 1702; Mohsin Abbas v. State.
records.title: Mohsin Abbas v. State

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Deprivation of Females of Inheritance
records.heading: Depriving females of inheritance conflicts with the Quranic commandments
records.text: The court observed that depriving females of inheritance conflicts with the Quranic commandments, and noted that the petitioner daughter and sister had been deprived of her inheritance for about 23 years. The post gives no outcome. Ref: 2022 YLR 1597.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence
records.heading: Last seen evidence is the weakest type unless strongly supported by independent sources
records.text: Last seen evidence has always been considered the weakest type of evidence unless proved to a high standard and strongly supported by other independent sources. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 134.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Witnesses
records.heading: Silence of the deceased's brothers when he left with the accused was unnatural
records.text: Two witnesses, real brothers of the deceased, did not inform the police when he left with the accused and did not return. This silence was unnatural, affected their veracity, and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 134.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Extra-Judicial Confession: Unnatural Witness
records.heading: An extra-judicial confession before an unnatural witness could not be relied upon
records.text: An extra-judicial confession made before a close relative of the deceased, who made no effort to apprehend the accused and first spoke to the Investigating Officer two days later, was under heavy clouds of doubt and could not be relied upon. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 134.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Currency, Tablets and Utensils
records.heading: Currency notes without special marks do not prove they belonged to the deceased
records.text: Recovery of currency notes does not show they belonged to the deceased without special marks. Tablets and utensils were not sent to any expert and the Medical Officer found no poison or intoxicant, so the attempt to prove drugging failed. The prosecution failed to prove its case and the appeal was allowed. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 134.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eye-Witness Evidence and Reduction of Death Sentence
records.heading: Death sentence reduced to life imprisonment where the fatal injury could not be attributed
records.text: Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was upheld on unshaken, mutually corroborating eye-witness evidence, with the accused apprehended at the spot. As it was not discernible which accused caused the fatal injuries, the death sentence was altered to life imprisonment. Appeal dismissed with that modification. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1102.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Medical Negligence: Punjab Healthcare Commission Act Bar
records.heading: Punjab Healthcare Commission Act 2010 bars prosecution on allegations of medical negligence
records.text: A petitioner challenged an order directing the SHO to register an FIR under s. 154 CrPC for a child's death by alleged medical negligence. The Punjab Healthcare Commission Act 2010 bars prosecution on allegations of negligence, and the complainant must approach the concerned forum. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1067.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Civil and Criminal Proceedings Run Concurrently; Second FIR
records.heading: Civil and criminal proceedings can run concurrently and a second FIR on different facts proceeds
records.text: A second FIR on entirely different facts and documents is proceedable. Civil and criminal proceedings can go side by side because of differing outcomes and standards of proof, and an acquittal does not bar a civil claim. Findings of a criminal court do not bind a civil court. Revision against refusal of s. 249-A CrPC relief dismissed. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1050.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appreciation of Evidence: Eye-Witnesses and S. 342 Statement
records.heading: Conviction upheld after examining eyewitnesses' presence and the section 342 CrPC statement
records.text: In a charge under ss. 302(b) and 34 PPC, the court examined the presence of the two eye-witnesses at the scene, who were a kilometre away, without plausible explanation. It also dealt with the effect of the accused's statement under s. 342 CrPC. Appeal against conviction was dismissed. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1005.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 497(1) CrPC: Reasonable Grounds Standard
records.heading: Bail under section 497(1) CrPC requires reasonable grounds, a standard below proof beyond doubt
records.text: Every person is presumed innocent, benefit of doubt must be granted, and bail is not to be denied as punishment. S. 497(1) CrPC requires a reasonable man standard of reasonable grounds, lower than proof beyond reasonable doubt. Bail petition was dismissed on the facts, a phone having been recovered from the accused. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 981.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Double Jeopardy: Art. 13, S. 403 CrPC, S. 26 General Clauses Act
records.heading: Double jeopardy bars a second trial for the same offence after acquittal or conviction
records.text: Art. 13 of the Constitution, s. 403 CrPC and s. 26 General Clauses Act bar a second trial for the same offence after acquittal or conviction on the same facts (autrefois acquit and autrefois convict). Prosecution of the appellant on facts for which he was acquitted on appeal infringed this protection, which applies regardless of the gravity of the crime. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1022.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VIII CPC: Evasive Denial in Written Statement
records.heading: Evasive denial in a written statement is ordinarily no denial and amounts to admission
records.text: Compilation of authorities on evasive denial under O. VIII Rr. 3, 4 and 5 CPC. Most hold that evasive denial is no denial and amounts to admission of the plaint's averment. PLD 2007 SC 433 is listed for the view that evasive denial would not amount to an admission. Ref: PLD 2011 SC 119, PLD 2007 SC 433, 2020 MLD 1166, 2017 CLC 436 and others.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Husband's Suit for Return of Dowry Articles
records.heading: A husband may sue in the Family Court for return of the wife's dowry articles
records.text: A husband sued the Family Court to return the wife's dowry articles, and the Judge Family Court rejected the suit on the logic that only a wife can sue. The court noted that Serial No. 8, Part-I of the Schedule makes dowry matters triable by family courts and that s. 7 of the 1964 Act imposes no such restriction on the plaintiff. Ref: Uzair Azmat v. Judge Family Court etc. (Writ Petition No. 46842 of 2022, decided 05.08.2022).
records.title: Uzair Azmat v. Judge Family Court etc. (Writ Petition No. 46842 of 2022, decided 05.08.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Five-Step Inquiry in Murder Trial (India)
records.heading: Supreme Court of India prescribes a five-step inquiry in a murder trial
records.text: Supreme Court of India held that a five-step inquiry is necessary: whether there is a homicide, whether it is culpable, whether it amounts to murder under s. 300 or falls under s. 304 IPC, whether s. 304-A applies, and, if the culprit cannot be identified, s. 72 IPC. Earlier decisions needed no reconsideration. Appeal allowed.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Presence of Investigating Officer and Witnesses at Murder Trial (India)
records.heading: Sessions Judge must summon the absent investigating officer and act against absent witnesses
records.text: In a murder trial the Sessions Judge must summon the investigating officer if absent, whose presence is a must and who must keep witnesses present. The court must take action against absent witnesses, including bailable or non-bailable warrants. The Sessions Judge was directed to proceed day to day under s. 309 Cr.P.C. Ref: Shailendra Kumar v. State of Bihar and Others (decided 28.11.2001); Justice M.B. Shah; Justice B.N. Agrawal; Justice Arijit Pasayat.
records.title: Shailendra Kumar v. State of Bihar and Others (decided 28.11.2001)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Scope of Re-Examination of Witness (India)
records.heading: Re-examination explains matters from cross-examination and is not confined to resolving ambiguities
records.text: Re-examination under s. 138 Evidence Act is directed to explaining matters referred to in cross-examination. It is not confined to resolving ambiguities, and the party calling the witness may put any question to obtain such explanation. Appeal against conviction under s. 302 IPC was dismissed.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Judicial Confession of Juvenile Accused
records.heading: Extra caution is required in recording the judicial confession of a juvenile accused
records.text: In recording a s. 164 confession of a juvenile accused in a qatl-i-amd case, the court must take extra caution. It is desirable that the juvenile be given counselling or consultation with a natural guardian or close blood relative. The confession must be voluntary, based on true facts and corroborated. Ref: 2021 SCMR 1039.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Guidelines on Detention and Bail of Juveniles
records.heading: Juvenile detention is a last resort and trials must conclude within six months
records.text: The High Court issued directions under the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018 to safeguard juvenile accused, as detention should be a last resort and for the shortest time. The Provincial Police Officer must ensure challan or interim challan within 14 days, and trial courts must conclude juvenile trials within six months on a day-to-day basis. Ref: PLD 2021 Lah 586.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Plea of Juvenility Must Be Taken Early
records.heading: Plea of juvenility must be taken at the earliest opportunity
records.text: An accused claiming minority at the time of the offence must take that plea at the earliest available opportunity, and an adverse inference should be drawn against him if the claim is delayed. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 895.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Determination of Age of Accused
records.heading: Whether an accused is a child is determined by evidence under Qanun-e-Shahadat
records.text: Determination of whether the accused is a child requires evidence under Qanun-e-Shahadat. The Trial Court summoned school, Union Council and NADRA record, and the complainant did not allege forgery. The accused were juveniles under s. 7 of the Juvenile Justice System Ordinance 2000. Revision petition dismissed. Ref: 2021 MLD 2088.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reliability of Evidence: Injured Witness and Last Seen
records.heading: Injured witness evidence may be rejected and unblemished last seen evidence may be relied upon
records.text: No empirical parameters exist to rate evidence as strong or weak, and the court must assess the integrity of available evidence for adequacy. Even injured witness evidence may be rejected if lacking the ring of truth, while last seen evidence free from taint may be relied upon as a reliable link between offender and victim. Ref: 2021 SCMR 662; Qaisar Mehmood v. State.
records.title: Qaisar Mehmood v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Restoration of Appeal Dismissed for Non-Appearance
records.heading: Appeal dismissed for non-appearance was restored under section 561-A CrPC
records.text: A second appeal after dismissal of the first for the accused's non-appearance was incompetent and time barred. The delay was wilful, but the request to treat the second appeal as an application under s. 561-A CrPC was accepted, the dismissal order was recalled and the first appeal resurrected. Ref: 2022 YLR 1252.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 313 CrPC: Examination of Accused and Defence Version (India)
records.heading: Section 313 requires each adverse circumstance to be put to the accused separately
records.text: The purpose of s. 313 is to give the accused a reasonable opportunity to explain adverse circumstances, by putting each adverse piece of evidence as a question. Bundling circumstances defeats a fair opportunity. The courts below failed to scrutinise the defence version. Appeal allowed and conviction set aside.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Leading Questions by Prosecutor in Examination-in-Chief (India)
records.heading: A prosecutor cannot lead the witness in examination-in-chief unless the witness is declared hostile
records.text: A leading question suggests the answer the prosecutor expects. The court may permit it to draw the witness's attention to matters otherwise not reached, but a question suggesting the expected answer is not allowed unless the witness is declared hostile with permission. Appeal allowed and the appellant acquitted under s. 302 IPC.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Contradicting Defence Witnesses with Police Statements (India)
records.heading: Defence witnesses cannot be contradicted with police statements under section 162 Cr.P.C
records.text: Under s. 162 Cr.P.C. only prosecution witnesses may be contradicted by their statements to the police, not court witnesses or defence witnesses. It was wrong to allow the prosecution to cross-examine DW 1 by reference to his police statement. Ref: AIR 1975 SC 1324; Mrs. Shakila Khader and Ors. v. Nausheer Cama and Ors. (decided 10.03.1975).
records.title: Mrs. Shakila Khader and Ors. v. Nausheer Cama and Ors. (decided 10.03.1975)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Prosecution Witness Examined as Defence Witness
records.heading: Accused cannot call examined prosecution witnesses as defence witnesses under section 233(3) CrPC
records.text: The power to summon or recall a witness is discretionary. S. 233(3) CrPC does not entitle the accused to have prosecution witnesses, already examined, cross-examined and discharged, examined as defence witnesses. Such an application was frivolous and vexatious, and the trial judge ought to have refused it as made to delay proceedings or defeat the ends of justice. Ref: State Of Madhya Pradesh v. Badri Yadav & Anr, decided 31.03.2006; Justice H.K. Sema; Justice Dr. Ar. Lakshmanan.
records.title: State Of Madhya Pradesh v. Badri Yadav & Anr, decided 31.03.2006

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Public Prosecutor's Duty and Defence Witnesses
records.heading: A Public Prosecutor may skip an independent witness who will not support the prosecution
records.text: Where the prosecution cites both related and independent witnesses, the Public Prosecutor may limit the independent witnesses examined. If he has reliable information that a witness will not support the prosecution, he may say so in court and skip that witness, and the defence may then cite and examine that person as a defence witness. The prosecutor must decide fairly. Ref: Hukam Singh And Ors v. State Of Rajasthan, decided 14.09.2000.
records.title: Hukam Singh And Ors v. State Of Rajasthan, decided 14.09.2000

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Intention and Knowledge in Murder
records.heading: Intention and knowledge in murder are inferred from weapon, ferocity and multiplicity of injuries
records.text: Intention and knowledge are subjective states of mind, to be gathered from circumstances such as the weapon used, the ferocity of the attack and the multiplicity of injuries. Knowledge is bare awareness of likely consequences, whereas intention requires something more than foresight, namely the purposeful doing of an act to achieve a particular end. Appeal partly allowed and sentence of ten years rigorous imprisonment imposed. Ref: (2016) 3 SCC 317; Nankaunoo v. State of U.P. (Criminal Appeal No. 46 of 2016, decided 19.01.2016); Justice R. Banumathi; Justice T.S. Thakur; Justice A.K. Sikri.
records.title: Nankaunoo v. State of U.P. (Criminal Appeal No. 46 of 2016, decided 19.01.2016)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Thumb Impression: Expert Opinion Required
records.heading: Comparison of thumb impressions by mere observation without expert opinion is unsafe
records.text: Comparison of a thumb impression by mere observation, without expert opinion, is prone to human fallibility. Courts should seek the assistance of experts in the relevant field, particularly as forensic science has advanced, to reach a fair conclusion. Petition allowed. Ref: 2022 LHC 6028; Ahmed Mahmood alias Mahmood v. A.D.J etc (Writ Petition 4232-18, decided 01.06.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Ahmed Mahmood alias Mahmood v. A.D.J etc (Writ Petition 4232-18, decided 01.06.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Party Not Appearing as Witness; Proof of Sale Consideration
records.heading: A party aware of the facts must appear as his own witness
records.text: A party personally aware of the circumstances is bound to appear as his own witness and face cross-examination, failing which an adverse inference may be drawn. Where payment of the sale consideration is not proved, a completed sale under s. 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 cannot be inferred. Ref: 2022 LHC 6020; Muhammad Siddique v. Mukhtiar Ahmad (Civil Revision 595-16, decided 07.06.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Siddique v. Mukhtiar Ahmad (Civil Revision 595-16, decided 07.06.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Lodging FIR
records.heading: Unexplained delay in lodging the FIR is a serious lapse
records.text: Delay in lodging the FIR is a serious lapse unless plausibly explained, and delay per se is a valid ground to test the veracity of the prosecution witnesses. The Rapat was also not exhibited in evidence, so it was unclear whether the appellant was nominated in it. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1527.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 100 CPC: Scope of Second Appeal
records.heading: Second appeal under section 100 CPC does not lie to question findings of fact
records.text: A second appeal under s. 100 CPC lies only on the grounds of a decision contrary to law, failure to determine a material issue of law, or substantial procedural error or defect. It does not lie to question findings of fact. A first appellate finding at variance with the trial court is immune from interference only if supported by evidence and logical reasoning. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1433.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 12 Specific Relief Act: Discretion in Specific Performance
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary but the discretion must be exercised reasonably
records.text: Specific performance is discretionary, but the discretion must not be exercised arbitrarily or unreasonably. Under s. 12 and its explanation, breach of a contract to transfer immoveable property is presumed incapable of adequate compensation in money unless the contrary is proved. The plaintiff must show readiness and willingness, and the court may award compensation in addition to or in substitution for performance. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1433.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 27(b) Specific Relief Act: Bona Fide Purchaser Burden
records.heading: A subsequent vendee claiming bona fide purchase bears the initial onus
records.text: A subsequent vendee claiming to be a bona fide purchaser for value without notice bears the initial onus, relying on Arts. 117 and 119 QSO. Mere denial of knowledge is insufficient; he must show due diligence, such as public notice inviting objections. Once discharged, the burden shifts to the plaintiff to prove notice or a colourable or fraudulent transaction. Appellants failed to prove the plea. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1433.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Collusive Subsequent Sale Without Due Diligence
records.heading: A collusive subsequent sale without due diligence defeats the bona fide purchaser plea
records.text: The entire deal appeared collusive: the vendor, tempted by a better offer, breached the earlier agreement and transferred the land by mutation in a hurried manner before the cut-off date in that agreement. The subsequent buyers produced no evidence of public notice, objections or other inquiry made as part of due diligence. Reference made to s. 55 of the Transfer of Property Act. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1433.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Actus Curiae Neminem Gravabit: Correcting Court Errors
records.heading: The maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit requires courts to remedy their own errors
records.text: The maxim that an act of the court shall prejudice no one requires a court to remedy a patent error or oversight, which may be reviewed, and to restore the affected person to the position he would have held but for the mistake. Parties should not suffer for acts or omissions of the court or State functionaries. The judgment also discusses s. 8(5) of the Punjab Civil Servants Act 1974 and proforma promotion after retirement. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1546.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 115 CPC: Superintendence and Visitorial Powers
records.heading: Section 115 CPC powers are superintendence and visitorial powers of correction
records.text: The powers under s. 115 CPC are to be exercised as superintendence and visitorial powers of correction, unhindered by technicalities. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1522.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Framing of Issues and Additional Issues
records.heading: A party may apply for additional issues where issues are improperly framed or incomplete
records.text: Under O. XIV R. 1 CPC the court must settle proper issues after reading the pleadings (defined in O. VI R. 1 as plaint or written statement), covering the material propositions of law and fact on which the right decision depends. A party who finds that issues are improperly framed, need recasting, or that additional issues are required, may apply to the court for additional issues. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1572.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Dissemination of Proscribed Religious Material
records.heading: Bail refused where sufficient material connected the accused with disseminating proscribed religious material
records.text: Accused were alleged to have disseminated proscribed material and a defiled translation of the Holy Quran through WhatsApp, Google Drive links and email (ss. 295-B, 298-C, 120-B, 34, 109 PPC; s. 11 PECA). The prosecution had sufficient material connecting them with the offence. Bail refused, and petitions for leave to appeal dismissed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1511.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Propagation of Banned Material via WhatsApp
records.heading: Bail refused to an administrator of a WhatsApp group sharing proscribed material
records.text: The accused was a nominated administrator of a WhatsApp group in which proscribed books and banned translation of the Holy Quran were shared. Forensic analysis of the phones showed his role in adding and removing members, so sufficient incriminating material existed (ss. 295-A, 295-B, 295-C, 298-C, 34, 109 PPC; s. 11 PECA). Bail refused and leave to appeal refused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1477.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Recusal of Judge: Principles
records.heading: A judge decides on his own conscience whether to recuse
records.text: Under the Code of Conduct for Judges and Art. 209(8) of the Constitution, a judge decides on his own conscience whether to recuse. Recusal is discouraged where a litigant or counsel creates a perception of bias to move a case from a Bench seen as unfavourable to one seen as more favourable, as yielding would erode public confidence and increase the workload of the other Bench. Ref: PLD 2022 Kar 499.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Courts Act 1964: Object and Purpose
records.heading: The Family Courts Act 1964 is a special statute that avoids technicalities
records.text: The Family Courts Act, 1964 is a special statute to advance justice and avoid technicalities. A Family Court proceeds on the premise that every procedure is permissible unless clearly prohibited, and may exercise its own powers to keep justice on course. Its main object is the protection and convenience of women and children, as also shown by s. 14(3), barring appeal or revision against interim orders. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 600.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: FIA Inquiry Against Customs Officials: Board Permission
records.heading: FIA needs Board permission under Rule 5(1) before inquiring against customs officials
records.text: The FIA must apply to the Board under Rule 5(1) of the FIA Rules 2002 for permission to inquire against the petitioners, and the Board must decide by speaking order within 30 days. If approved, a de novo inquiry follows, and prosecution needs a second approval under Rule 5(2). If approval is declined, the petitioners may seek acquittal from the trial court. Prayer to quash the FIR declined. Ref: Muhammad Ahmad Zaheer etc. v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (Writ Petition No. 62575/2021, date of hearing 31.03.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Ahmad Zaheer etc. v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (Writ Petition No. 62575/2021, date of hearing 31.03.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Temporary Injunction: Three Essential Ingredients
records.heading: A temporary injunction needs a prima facie case, irreparable loss and balance of convenience
records.text: To obtain a temporary injunction the plaintiff must establish a prima facie case, possibility of irreparable loss if the injunction is refused, and a balance of convenience in his favour. A prima facie case is foundational, and the other two conditions are considered only once it is established. Ref: 2022 LHC 6070; Kashif Iqbal v. Asghar Ali Ghumman (F.A.O. 39089/22, decided 07.07.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Kashif Iqbal v. Asghar Ali Ghumman (F.A.O. 39089/22, decided 07.07.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Annual Increase in Maintenance: Effective Date
records.heading: A decreed annual maintenance increase runs from institution of the suit
records.text: A 10% annual increase in maintenance awarded by a decree runs from the date of institution of the suit and not from the date of the decree. Any ambiguity in the decree must be construed in line with the object of the Family Courts Act, 1964, a beneficial legislation that cannot be read to the detriment of a minor or female. Ref: 2022 LHC 6063; Mah Noor Azhar v. Muhammad Sohail Khan etc (Family 23991/17, decided 24.06.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mah Noor Azhar v. Muhammad Sohail Khan etc (Family 23991/17, decided 24.06.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ordinary and Additional Powers of Magistrates
records.heading: Magistrates hold ordinary powers by office under section 36 CrPC and additional powers by conferment
records.text: Ordinary powers of Magistrates arise from office under s. 36 CrPC and are listed in the Third Schedule, which includes recording statements and confessions under s. 164 for a First Class Magistrate. Additional powers may be conferred under s. 37 and the Fourth Schedule, by the Provincial Government under s. 39, and continue under s. 40 until withdrawn. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 545; Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC: Any Magistrate May Record Statement
records.heading: Any Magistrate may record a section 164 CrPC statement, including out of district
records.text: The words any Magistrate in s. 164 CrPC include Judicial Magistrates and Special Judicial Magistrates, even without jurisdiction in the case, so statements and confessions may be recorded out of district during investigation. Promptly recorded statements carry greater evidentiary value as chances of fabrication are remote. A statement recorded out of district was held admissible, relying on an Allahabad decision (AIR 1938 All 625). Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 545; Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Magistrate's Functions During Investigation Beyond Jurisdiction
records.heading: A Magistrate should not refuse to record a statement merely for lack of territorial jurisdiction
records.text: Investigation collects evidence wherever found, and Magistrates have powers in remand, warrants, search, inquest, bail and recording statements and confessions. A police officer may execute a warrant throughout Pakistan under s. 82 CrPC and, on arrest out of district, must produce the accused before the local Magistrate under ss. 84 and 85, who should not refuse to record a statement merely for lack of territorial jurisdiction. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 545; Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 102 and 91 QSO: Proof of Recorded Confession
records.heading: A confession not recorded under section 164 CrPC must be proved by evidence
records.text: Under Art. 102 QSO, a matter required by law to be in documentary form is proved by the document itself. A statement or confession not recorded under s. 164 or 364 CrPC requires evidence that it was duly made, and the Magistrate may be called. If recorded in accordance with law, its genuineness is presumed under Art. 91, and Explanation 3 of Art. 102 does not bar oral evidence of the same fact. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 545; Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Appellate Interference in Contempt Discretion
records.heading: An appellate court ordinarily will not interfere where the court declines to initiate contempt
records.text: Contempt is essentially a matter between the court and the alleged contemnor, so an appellate court ordinarily will not substitute its opinion where the court concerned declines to act or accepts an apology (s. 3 Contempt of Court Ordinance; Art. 204). The principle is not absolute, and a High Court order refusing to initiate civil contempt may be interfered with under Art. 185(3) only if arbitrary, perverse or improbable. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 546.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Contractual Obligations and Disputed Facts
records.heading: Contractual obligations and disputed facts are not decided in Article 199 jurisdiction
records.text: Contractual rights and obligations are to be enforced through the ordinary civil courts, and violation of a contract cannot be decided in constitutional jurisdiction. Superior courts should not investigate disputed questions of fact needing evidence, which is properly done in a suit. Art. 199 provides an expeditious remedy where illegality can be shown without elaborate inquiry. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 628.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-K CrPC: Acquittal at Any Stage
records.heading: Authority on section 265-K CrPC and acquittal at any stage
records.text: Authority on s. 265-K CrPC, the power of the court to acquit an accused at any stage; the judgment states the scope of the section. The post gives no further holding. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 562.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 18: Regulation of Trade
records.heading: The legislature may regulate trade through licences without changing its private character
records.text: In a welfare State the legislature may regulate trades through licences, permits and reasonable conditions, and control production, distribution and consumption of commodities. Such regulation does not change the legal relationship between contracting parties, the legal character of commercial transactions, or the private nature of the trade or business. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 562.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail: Delay Counted From Detention
records.heading: Delay under the third proviso to section 497(1) CrPC counts from detention
records.text: Under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, the period of delay in conclusion of the trial is counted from the date of the accused's detention in the case. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 551.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Hardened, Desperate or Dangerous Criminal: S. 497(1)
records.heading: A hardened, desperate or dangerous criminal cannot claim bail for delay
records.text: The accused cut the nose of his sister-in-law and her alleged paramour (ss. 336, 334, 367, 354, 342, 148, 149 PPC). The nature and manner of the offence brought him within the expression hardened, desperate or dangerous criminal in the fourth proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, so he could not claim bail for delay under the third proviso. Leave to appeal dismissed and bail refused. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 541.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 185: Interference With High Court Discretionary Orders
records.heading: Supreme Court interferes with High Court discretionary orders only if arbitrary or perverse
records.text: Discretionary orders of the High Courts are not generally interfered with by the Supreme Court but are not immune from scrutiny if found arbitrary, perverse or against settled principles of law. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 546.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Failure to Reproduce Issue in Judgment
