records.heading: Failure to reproduce an issue in the judgment is of little importance
records.text: Where the framed issue was comprehensive enough to cover the dispute, including the genuineness of the Nikahnama, and both parties led evidence, failure to caption or reproduce the issue in the judgment was of little importance as long as findings on material points were reached with judicial application of mind. Allocation of onus had no bearing where sufficient evidence was led. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 580.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Non-Framing of Issues and Composite Issues
records.heading: A composite issue does not vitiate the trial unless serious prejudice is shown
records.text: Where one party affirms and the other denies a material proposition, the court should frame an issue, and parties must also seek proper issues. A composite issue covering interconnected contradictory stances does not per se vitiate the trial, and the challenger must show serious prejudice. If evidence was led accordingly, the objection becomes inconsequential. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 580.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses: Testimony Not Discarded
records.heading: Relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard testimony
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony unless previous enmity or ill will to falsely implicate the accused is established on the record. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1577.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Substitution of Accused: Rare Phenomenon
records.heading: Substitution of the real culprit is a rare phenomenon
records.text: Substitution of the real culprit is a rare phenomenon. A complainant would not spare the real murderer of his brother and falsely involve the petitioner without reason. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1577.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Delay, Substitution and Weak Recovery
records.heading: Delay, substitution and weak recovery gave the accused the benefit of doubt
records.text: The complainant was not an eyewitness, the FIR was delayed about 18 hours without explanation, the accused was substituted for a nominated person, and the churri was not sent to the Chemical Examiner so its recovery was inconsequential. Recovery of ornaments was unsafe to rely on, and a single circumstance creating doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1515.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt at Bail and Suspension of Sentence
records.heading: Benefit of doubt may be extended even at bail and suspension of sentence stage
records.text: It is established that the benefit of doubt can be extended to the accused even at the preliminary stage of bail and suspension of sentence (ss. 426 and 497 CrPC). Ref: 2022 SCMR 1555.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Contradicting Ocular Account
records.heading: Discrepancy between medical and ocular evidence raised serious doubt on the eyewitnesses
records.text: Blackening around the wound indicated a close-range shot, yet the site plan placed the accused 18 steps away, and the doctor described the chest wound as an exit wound. This major discrepancy between medical and ocular evidence raised serious doubt on the eyewitnesses. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1567.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Circumstance
records.heading: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt gives the accused the benefit as of right
records.text: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt in a prudent mind about guilt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right and not as a matter of grace. Conviction must rest on unimpeachable, trustworthy and reliable evidence, and any doubt is resolved in favour of the accused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1567.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC Statement Before Any Magistrate
records.heading: A section 164 CrPC statement may be recorded by a Magistrate of another district
records.text: A statement under s. 164 CrPC may be recorded by any Magistrate. It is not legally necessary that it be recorded before the Magistrate having territorial jurisdiction over the police station, and it may be recorded before a Magistrate of another district. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 545, PLJ 2022 Lah 302, PLJ 2022 Lah 181, PLJ 2021 Lah 645.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution of Family Court Decrees: S. 13(4)
records.heading: Family Court decrees are executed under section 13 of the 1964 Act
records.text: On an execution petition after a Family Court decree, the court proceeds under s. 13 of the 1964 Act. S. 13(4) allows execution by the Family Court itself or by a Civil Court designated by the District Judge, which then enjoys the powers under O. XXI CPC, although s. 17 excludes the CPC (except ss. 10 and 11) and the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order from Family Court proceedings. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 600.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution Not Transferable Out of District: Precept Under S. 46 CPC
records.heading: Execution outside the district proceeds by precept under section 46 CPC
records.text: There is no need to transfer an execution petition to a court in another district where the judgment debtor resides. The executing court may send a precept under s. 46 CPC to the court where the debtor resides or owns property, to attach it and recover the decretal amount as arrears of land revenue. Directions were issued to District Judges and Family Courts in Punjab, including adherence to s. 13(3) of the Act for money decrees. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 600.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009: Affidavits and Disclosure
records.heading: Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 requires full disclosure on affidavit by both sides
records.text: The Act sets a special procedure requiring both sides to make full and fair disclosure on affidavit. S. 22(3) requires a leave to defend application to be accompanied by the tenant's affidavit, relevant documents and witness affidavits, and s. 19 requires the ejectment petition to carry a concise statement of facts with all relevant documents and witness affidavits. Where a statute prescribes a procedure, it must be followed. Ref: Abdul Malik alias Badshah Khan v. Addl. District Judge & 5 others (Writ Petition No. 5651 of 2022/BWP, date of hearing 03.08.2022).
records.title: Abdul Malik alias Badshah Khan v. Addl. District Judge & 5 others (Writ Petition No. 5651 of 2022/BWP, date of hearing 03.08.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Permission for Political Gathering; Non-Impleadment Objection
records.heading: Courts ordinarily do not interfere with permission for political gatherings
records.text: An objection that a province or party was not impleaded loses efficacy where it was impleaded in connected petitions and given reasonable opportunity of hearing. The grant or refusal of permission to hold a political public gathering lies within the domain of the relevant authority, and the court does not ordinarily interfere. Ref: 2022 LHC 6091; Amjad Shahzad v. Deputy Commissioner etc (48397/22, decided 12.08.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Amjad Shahzad v. Deputy Commissioner etc (48397/22, decided 12.08.2022)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Hearing Other Side Before FIR Direction
records.heading: Stop payment or account closure does not remove a case from section 489-F PPC
records.text: Ordinarily the original cheque, the bank return slip and a copy of the notice under s. 30 of the Negotiable Instruments Act suffice before the Justice of Peace for a direction to register an FIR. Stop payment or closure of the account does not per se take a case out of s. 489-F PPC, but it made it imperative to hear the other side on the s. 22-A(6) CrPC application. Ref: Humair Yousaf v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 46941 of 2021, date of hearing 17.06.2022).
records.title: Humair Yousaf v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 46941 of 2021, date of hearing 17.06.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Standards of Proof in Civil and Criminal Cases
records.heading: Civil and criminal cases follow different standards of proof under Article 2(4) QSO
records.text: Art. 2(4) QSO sets the prudent man standard and requires no perfect proof. Preponderance of probability applies in civil cases, proof beyond reasonable doubt in criminal cases, and clear and convincing proof in civil cases involving allegations of a criminal nature. These are three degrees of probability, evaluated in the circumstances of each case. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 353.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 167 CrPC: Physical Remand and Revision Before Sessions Judge
records.heading: Revision lies before the Sessions Judge against refusal of police remand under section 167 CrPC
records.text: A revision lies before the Sessions Judge against a Judicial Magistrate's order refusing police remand, and the Sessions Judge must decide it on merits. S. 167 CrPC permits a Magistrate, with or without jurisdiction, to authorise detention for up to 15 days in total with reasons recorded, and a police remand order should be intimated to the Sessions Court, which has supervisory jurisdiction. Ref: The State through Advocate-General, ICT v. Learned Additional Sessions Judge and 2 others (Writ Petition No. 2995 of 2022, decided 16.08.2022).
records.title: The State through Advocate-General, ICT v. Learned Additional Sessions Judge and 2 others (Writ Petition No. 2995 of 2022, decided 16.08.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Meaningful Reading of Plaint
records.heading: A plaint must be read meaningfully before rejection under O. VII R. 11 CPC
records.text: The court must do substantial justice and not non-suit a party on technicalities. When rejecting a plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC, it must give the plaint a meaningful reading. The judgment also discusses the master and servant relationship and the protective purpose of laws for fundamental human rights. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1598.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 9 CPC: Ouster of Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Ouster of civil court jurisdiction under section 9 CPC cannot be presumed
records.text: Under s. 9 CPC the ouster of civil court jurisdiction cannot be presumed unless the prerequisites laid down for it are fulfilled. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1598.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 7 ATA Not Attracted: Personal Vendetta
records.heading: Section 7 ATA is not attracted by a scuffle and personal vendetta
records.text: Where the occurrence arose from a scuffle between children and was the result of personal vendetta, without premeditation or a specific motive to create terror or insecurity in society, s. 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 is not attracted. Conviction and sentence under s. 7 set aside. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1494.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeal Without Board Resolution or Power of Attorney
records.heading: An appeal for a company without Board Resolution or power of attorney was dismissed
records.text: Authority on an appeal filed on behalf of a company petitioner without a Board Resolution or power of attorney, which was dismissed, with discussion of O. XXIX R. 1, O. VI Rr. 14 and 15, O. III R. 4 and O. XLI R. 1 CPC. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1501.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 9 CPC: Ouster of Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Civil courts may try all civil suits unless cognizance is barred expressly or impliedly
records.text: Civil Courts may try all suits of a civil nature unless cognizance is expressly or impliedly barred. Ouster cannot be inferred routinely unless the conditions are fulfilled, and lack of jurisdiction is not presumed until a specific law debars the Civil Court and provides a specific remedy within a hierarchy. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1501.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 114 QSO: Doctrine of Estoppel
records.heading: Estoppel under Article 114 QSO prevents denial of a belief intentionally induced
records.text: Under Art. 114 QSO, a person who by declaration, act or omission intentionally caused or permitted another to believe a thing true and act on it cannot deny its truth against that person. The principle rests on equity, aims to prevent fraud, and though a rule of evidence may constitute substantive rights. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1454.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Approbate and Reprobate: Benefits and Burdens
records.heading: One who approbates cannot reprobate and may not take a benefit without its burden
records.text: One who approbates cannot reprobate. This is akin to the doctrine of benefits and burdens, under which a person taking advantage under an instrument that grants a benefit and imposes a burden cannot take the former without complying with the latter. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1454.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Police Custody Confession: Arts. 39 and 40 QSO
records.heading: Confession in police custody is inadmissible and Article 40 QSO has a narrow exception
records.text: A confession made in police custody is inadmissible under Art. 39 QSO. Art. 40 is an exception admitting only information from the accused that leads to discovery of a fact perceivable through the senses and previously unknown to anyone. Any wider reading of Art. 40 is incorrect. Ref: 2022 [M] PCr.R 70.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confession of Co-Accused Cannot Alone Convict
records.heading: Confession of a co-accused cannot alone convict another accused
records.text: On the Islamic jurisprudential view that a confessing accused loses purity of deposition, the confession of a co-accused cannot solely convict another accused and can only be used against its maker. Absent other proof, it cannot support conviction of a co-accused. Ref: 2022 [M] PCr.R 70.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 43 QSO: Co-Accused Confession as Circumstantial Evidence
records.heading: A co-accused's confession is only circumstantial evidence against others under Article 43 QSO
records.text: Under Art. 43 QSO a proved confession is proof against its maker and only circumstantial evidence against other accused, after strict and cautious appraisal. A s. 164 CrPC confession need not be on oath and the co-accused cannot cross-examine its maker, so it is a weak circumstance and cannot solely found conviction of another accused. Ref: 2022 [M] PCr.R 70.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Voluntariness of Confession: Relevant Factors
records.heading: A confession is voluntary if free of duress, inducement, threat, promise or pressure
records.text: A statement is voluntary if made with specific intention and free of duress, inducement, threat, promise or pressure. Relevant factors include time between arrest and recording, warning about the right to remain silent, the Magistrate's precautions, assurance of not being returned to police, the Magistrate's satisfaction about torture, and the accused's reason for confessing. Ref: 2022 [M] PCr.R 70.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Prosecution Must Prove Judicial Confession Voluntary
records.heading: The prosecution must prove at trial that a judicial confession was voluntary and true
records.text: The prosecution must prove at trial that a judicial confession was voluntary and true. S. 164(3) CrPC requires the Magistrate to record a memorandum of his belief in voluntariness, and the Rules and Orders of the Lahore High Court Vol. III Ch. 13 stress the same precautions. Under Arts. 37, 38 and 39 QSO, confessions induced by threat or promise, or made in police custody, are inadmissible. Ref: 2022 [M] PCr.R 70.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 107 PPC: Ingredients of Abetment by Conspiracy
records.heading: Abetment by conspiracy under section 107 PPC requires instigation, engagement and intentional aid
records.text: Under s. 107 PPC, three ingredients are essential to charge a person as conspirator: instigation, engagement with co-accused, and intentional aid in respect of the act or omission for completion of the abetment. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1540.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Circumstance
records.heading: Benefit of doubt as of right arises from a single circumstance creating reasonable doubt
records.text: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt in a prudent mind about guilt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right and not as grace. Conviction must rest on unimpeachable, trustworthy and reliable evidence, and any doubt is resolved in favour of the accused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1540.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Admission by Attorney Binds Principal
records.heading: An admission by an attorney binds the principal unless lack of authority is proved
records.text: An admission made by an attorney is binding on his principal unless a contrary intention or lack of authority is proved. An unqualified admission, through an attorney, of the existence of a family settlement needs no proof, and the settlement operated as an agreement binding on the parties. Suit for declaration rightly decreed and leave to appeal refused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1532.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Unregistered Family Settlement Binding
records.heading: An unregistered family settlement that was unchallenged binds the parties and legal heirs
records.text: A written settlement unchallenged before any forum binds the parties and their legal heirs, and a charge created on property passes with the property. The objection that the settlement was unregistered was itself an admission of its existence, and as it was executed through close relatives it required no compulsory registration. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1532.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Patwari's Duty in Sanctioning Mutation
records.heading: A Patwari must sanction mutations on evidence and cannot make arbitrary entries
records.text: A Patwari must sanction mutations in accordance with the Award or Settlement before him and on evidence, and cannot make entries arbitrarily. Sanctioning a mutation on oral assertions, after taking signatures on a blank paper, against the documentary evidence was illegal and indicated mala fides. Public officials owe a fiduciary duty to the public. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1532.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Government Ownership Claim and Escheat: Art. 172
records.heading: Government claiming ownership must prove lawful acquisition or follow the Article 172 escheat procedure
records.text: A government claiming ownership must show that the property was acquired by due process or that it became owner of ownerless property under Art. 172 of the Constitution. Before taking unclaimed property by escheat, the government must follow the procedure provided by law and invite objections through a widely circulated public notice. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1428.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Unsettled Land: Possession as Proof of Ownership Against Government
records.heading: Merely unsettled land is not ownerless, and possession may prove ownership against government
records.text: Land that was merely unsettled is not ownerless property. As the government neglected its duty to conduct settlement and was neither in possession nor able to prove ownership, the respondent's possession and control sufficed as proof of ownership, in light of Arts. 23 and 24 of the Constitution. No ground was shown to interfere with the High Court's findings. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1428.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Joint Investigation Team Report: Evidentiary Value
records.heading: A JIT report is a section 173 CrPC report and inadmissible in evidence
records.text: A JIT report is the opinion of its members and can at most be treated as a report under s. 173 CrPC, which is inadmissible in evidence. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 178.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 167 CrPC Order: Judicial and Revisable
records.heading: An order under section 167 CrPC is judicial and revisable by the Sessions Court
records.text: An order passed under s. 167 CrPC is a judicial order and is revisable by the Sessions Court. Ref: KLR 2018 CrC 205, 2005 YLR 805.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Medico-Legal Examination Under Police Rules
records.heading: Rule 25.19 Police Rules governs medico-legal examination and police cannot compel an injured person
records.text: Chapter 25 of the Police Rules governs medico-legal cases. Under Rule 25.19(1) the person to be examined is produced before the highest medical authority available in the district, at the Civil Hospital rather than a branch dispensary. Rule 25.19(3) provides that police cannot compel an injured person to submit to examination and he may be examined privately at his own expense. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1293.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Trial Court Must Consider DNA Report
records.heading: A trial court must consider an exhibited DNA report before convicting
records.text: DNA testing is a gold standard for establishing identity. Where a DNA report was exhibited and put to the accused under s. 342 CrPC but the trial court did not discuss it in convicting, that conflicts with the right to fair trial under Art. 10-A of the Constitution. A court must consider all oral and documentary evidence, as defined in Art. 2(c) QSO, before judgment. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1268.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Competency of Child Witness: Art. 3 QSO
records.heading: Omitting preliminary questioning of a child witness does not exclude the deposition
records.text: Under Art. 3 QSO all persons are competent to testify unless the court considers them unable to understand questions or respond rationally. Preliminary questioning of a child witness before oath is a rule of caution and not a statutory bar, so the deposition is not excluded if it was omitted. In sexual assault of very young children, conviction may rest on other circumstances such as medical evidence, DNA and eyewitness evidence. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1396.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Setting Aside Ex Parte Decree: Two Grounds
records.heading: Proof of either non-service or sufficient cause sets aside an ex parte decree
records.text: A defendant seeking to set aside an ex parte decree must show either that summons was not duly served or that sufficient cause prevented appearance on the hearing date. Satisfying either condition is enough and both need not be shown together. The rule emphasises due service so that a party is not deprived of its right without opportunity of defence. Ref: 2022 CLC 1529.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Due Service of Summons: Order V CPC
records.heading: Defective newspaper citation instead of due service of summons does not satisfy Order V CPC
records.text: Under Order V CPC, summons is ordinarily served on the defendant personally (R. 10), or through an agent (Rr. 12, 13), or on an adult male family member residing with him if he cannot be found (R. 15). Substituted service has the same effect as personal service but requires compliance with the rules. Where notices were issued instead of summons and newspaper citation was defective, summons was held not duly served (O. V Rr. 17, 19, 20 and O. IX Rr. 6, 13). Ref: 2022 CLC 1529.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Setting Aside Ex Parte Decree
records.heading: Application to set aside an ex parte decree must be filed within thirty days
records.text: Under Art. 164 of the Limitation Act, an application to set aside an ex parte decree must be filed within thirty days. Time runs from the date of decree where summons was duly served, and from the date of knowledge of the decree where summons was not duly served. Ref: 2022 CLC 1529.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Protection of Parents Ordinance 2021: Eviction of Children
records.heading: A parent may seek eviction of a child by complaint to the Deputy Commissioner
records.text: Under s. 4(2) of the Ordinance a parent may complain in writing to the Deputy Commissioner, who after hearing the parties and being satisfied that ownership vests in the parent orders eviction irrespective of the child's defence. The order is appealable under s. 7. Ss. 200 to 240 CrPC are not made applicable, so the procedure of complaint is not followed. Eviction of parents by a child is an offence under s. 3. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 559.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Initial Burden of Proof on Plaintiff
records.heading: The initial burden of proof lies on the plaintiff
records.text: Under Arts. 117 and 118 QSO the initial burden lies on the plaintiff to prove his claim by cogent, legal, relevant and unimpeachable evidence. Weakness in the defence evidence does not relieve the plaintiff of that burden. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 589.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Sale Deed on Multiple Pages: Signature on Each Page
records.heading: Each page of a multi-page deed must be signed or its connection proved
records.text: Where a document runs to more than one page, the parties must sign or thumb-mark each page. Otherwise the plaintiff must prove by evidence that the unsigned pages are connected with the signed page and assented to by the executant. Without that connection the unsigned pages are not part of the deed and consensus ad idem is not established. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 589.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Registrar Cannot Decide Maintainability: Supreme Court Rules
records.heading: The Registrar has no power to decide maintainability of a petition or appeal
records.text: The Registrar's powers under the Supreme Court Rules 1980 (including O. III R. 10, O. V R. 1(6), O. VII R. 7 and O. XVII R. 5) are administrative and concern form and presentation. The Registrar has no power to decide maintainability of a petition or appeal, which is for the Court. The Court may discourage frivolous filings by costs under O. XVII R. 12. Ref: Muhammad Ahsan Abid v. Makhdoom Khusru Bakhtiar and others (C.M. Appeal 39/2021, decided 10.08.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Ahsan Abid v. Makhdoom Khusru Bakhtiar and others (C.M. Appeal 39/2021, decided 10.08.2022)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Civil Court Review of Board of Revenue Orders
records.heading: Civil courts may examine the legality of Board of Revenue orders despite section 36
records.text: Despite s. 36 of the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act 1912, the general jurisdiction under s. 9 CPC leaves civil courts with ultimate jurisdiction to examine the acts and orders of special tribunals and decide their legality. In such a suit, statements of the parties and the record of proceedings are ordinarily sufficient evidence of the legality of the impugned order. Ref: Nausher v. Province of Punjab, etc. (C.A. 1011/2016, decided 18.08.2022); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Nausher v. Province of Punjab, etc. (C.A. 1011/2016, decided 18.08.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Sham Sale to Defeat Family Court Decree in Execution
records.heading: A judgment debtor's sale during execution to a defence witness was held sham
records.text: In execution of a family court decree, a sale by the judgment debtor during execution proceedings to his own defence witness was held a sham transaction meant to frustrate the decree. Delay of over 12 years in execution on an inapplicable objection cannot be allowed to defeat the decree. Concurrent findings upheld and petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 667; Naeem Shehzad v. Additional District Judge, Arifwala and 2 others (W.P. No. 208019 of 2018); Justice Muhammad Shan Gul.
records.title: Naeem Shehzad v. Additional District Judge, Arifwala and 2 others (W.P. No. 208019 of 2018)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Election of Chief Minister: Defecting Members' Votes
records.heading: Recount directed excluding votes of defecting members in the Chief Minister election
records.text: Under Arts. 63-A(1)(b) and 130(4), after holding that 25 votes of defecting members could not be counted, the Court declined to quash the notification and send the matter to the Presiding Officer under the provisos. It directed the Deputy Speaker to recount excluding those votes, with further polls if no majority results, and applied the de facto doctrine to protect acts done meanwhile. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 675; Muhammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Province of the Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 30456 of 2022 and others); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch.; Justice Shahid Jamil Khan; Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi; Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Province of the Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 30456 of 2022 and others)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Defamation by Newspaper: Decree Upheld
records.heading: Defamation decree against a newspaper's editors upheld for failure to prove correctness of publication
records.text: A defamation suit against a newspaper's Chief Editor and Editor was decreed. The appellants failed to establish the factual correctness of what was published and showed no investigation of it. Notice by registered post was proved, satisfying s. 8 of the Defamation Ordinance, 2002. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 683; Chief Editor Muhammad Riaz Anjum, etc. v. Dr. Mohammad Shahbaz (R.F.A. No. 140 of 2012, decided 19.05.2022); Justice Muhammad Masood Jahangir; Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Chief Editor Muhammad Riaz Anjum, etc. v. Dr. Mohammad Shahbaz (R.F.A. No. 140 of 2012, decided 19.05.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Benefits of Widow of High Court Judge
records.heading: A High Court Judge's widow is entitled to benefits under the revised assistance package
records.text: The widow of a High Court Judge who died in service was held entitled to benefits under the office memorandum on the revised assistance package. No plausible reason was given for withdrawing the earlier memorandum, and the privileges of a Judge or spouse are not limited or restricted. The impugned memoranda were set aside and the petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 693; Mrs. Kaneez Fatima v. Islamic Republic of Pakistan and others (W.P. No. 1659 of 2021); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Mrs. Kaneez Fatima v. Islamic Republic of Pakistan and others (W.P. No. 1659 of 2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX R. 13 CPC: Defective Newspaper Citation
records.heading: An ex parte decree is set aside where newspaper citation was defective
records.text: An ex parte decree was set aside under O. IX R. 13 CPC where citation was published in a newspaper without process fee, the process server's report was unverified, the petitioner's name was wrongly reflected, no postal certificate was on file and no inquiry was held. O. V Rr. 17 and 19 were not complied with. Revision allowed and the suit restored as pending. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 715; Muhammad Hussain v. Rana Sohail Anjum etc. (C.R. No. 2020 of 2014); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Hussain v. Rana Sohail Anjum etc. (C.R. No. 2020 of 2014)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Striking Off Defence for Non-Payment of Maintenance
records.heading: Failure to pay interim maintenance justifies striking off defence under section 17-A
records.text: Under s. 17-A of the Family Courts Act, 1964 the father's right to defend was struck off for failing to pay interim maintenance as directed. The petitioner produced no document showing inability to pay, and his bank statement showed regular salary above Rs. 130,000 monthly. The concurrent judgments were unexceptionable and the petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 744; Muhammad Naveed Akhtar v. Mst. Ghazala Batool, etc. (W.P. No. 43023 of 2022); Justice Muhammad Shan Gul.
records.title: Muhammad Naveed Akhtar v. Mst. Ghazala Batool, etc. (W.P. No. 43023 of 2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Appeal Against Sentence After Confession: s. 412 CrPC
records.heading: After confession, section 412 CrPC allows challenge only to extent or legality of sentence
records.text: Where conviction rests on a confession, s. 412 CrPC allows a sentence to be challenged only as to extent or legality. An appeal is barred but revision remains available. A sentence of one year and nine months under s. 9(b) CNSA, 1997 for 680 grams of charas was found legal and the appeal was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1218, PLD 2022 Lahore 694; Qasim Ali v. State (Crl. A. No. 363 of 2020); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Qasim Ali v. State (Crl. A. No. 363 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Probation Ordinance s. 11: Conviction Not a Bar
records.heading: A conviction solely under the Probation Ordinance is disregarded for disqualification under other laws
records.text: Under s. 11 of the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960 a conviction solely under the Ordinance is not a conviction for other purposes and is disregarded under any law imposing disqualification or disability (s. 11(2)). Courts should extend probation to repenting first offenders within ss. 4 and 5. The conviction does not stand in the way of future prospects, save for being dealt with again under the Ordinance. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1218, PLD 2022 Lahore 694; Qasim Ali v. State (Crl. A. No. 363 of 2020); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Qasim Ali v. State (Crl. A. No. 363 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Power to Summon Witnesses: s. 540 CrPC
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC witnesses' statements must be supplied to the defence and complainant
records.text: Section 540 CrPC is an exception to the adversarial system and an overarching component of the criminal justice system rooted in fair trial and due process. The criminal revisions were dismissed, but the court must supply copies of the statements of such witnesses to the defence and the complainant for cross-examination so that no evidence comes on record by surprise. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1229; Waqas alias Kashi etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. Nos. 71763 & 68819 of 2021); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Waqas alias Kashi etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. Nos. 71763 & 68819 of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Res Gestae: Art. 19 QSO
records.heading: A non-eyewitness may give relevant res gestae evidence under Article 19 QSO
records.text: A witness who is not an eyewitness may still give relevant res gestae evidence under Art. 19 QSO where the victim disclosed the entire details to her on reaching home. Medical evidence was also treated as res gestae under the principle of contemporaneous physical condition, admissible as to injury and not for identifying the accused. Appeals and revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1241, PLD 2022 Lahore 645; Kamran etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 38038 & 30076 & Crl. Rev. No. 30079 of 2019); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kamran etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 38038 & 30076 & Crl. Rev. No. 30079 of 2019)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Alibi Supported by CCTV
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed where CCTV footage supported the plea of alibi
records.text: In a case under ss. 302/34 PPC, post-arrest bail was allowed under s. 497 CrPC where CCTV footage obtained by police showed the petitioner inside a bank for an hour-long clip, bank officers' statements were recorded and the police themselves appreciated the plea of alibi. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1264; Muhammad Mustafa Qureshi v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 3755-B of 2022, decided 01.07.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Mustafa Qureshi v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 3755-B of 2022, decided 01.07.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Plea of Alibi Not Raised Early
records.heading: Post-arrest bail refused where the plea of alibi was not raised early
records.text: Post-arrest bail was refused under s. 497 CrPC to a named accused with a specific role of dagger blows. The plea of alibi was not set up at the earliest stage and no details of place or time were given. Credibility of an alibi is properly considered where it is raised when the accusation is made and maintained consistently. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1308; Zahid Rasheed v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 2811-B of 2022, decided 01.06.2022); Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Zahid Rasheed v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 2811-B of 2022, decided 01.06.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Successive Fire Shots Under s. 324 PPC
records.heading: Bail under section 324 PPC is not justified by non-vital injuries after successive shots
records.text: In a s. 324 PPC case, intention manifests when the trigger is pressed, more so with successive shots. Bail cannot be granted on the plea that injuries were on non-vital parts. A single shot may stand differently. Femoral and popliteal vessels in the thigh and calf, if damaged, can cause death within five to seven minutes. Post-arrest bail dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1267; Muhammad Azam v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 23859-B of 2022, decided 17.05.2022); Justice Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Muhammad Azam v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 23859-B of 2022, decided 17.05.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Unnatural Conduct
records.heading: Eyewitnesses from other houses are chance witnesses and their account was unnatural
records.text: Eyewitnesses who lived in other houses and were not inmates of the house where the occurrence took place were declared chance witnesses not worthy of reliance. Their account that the accused waited and acted exactly as they arrived was held unnatural and opposed to the common course of human conduct, suggesting their presence was procured later. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1273; Abdul Wahid alias Budho v. State (Crl. A. No. 436-J and M.R. No. 18 of 2019); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Safdar Saleem Shahid.
records.title: Abdul Wahid alias Budho v. State (Crl. A. No. 436-J and M.R. No. 18 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Circumstance Suffices
records.heading: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt suffices for the benefit of doubt as of right
records.text: If even a single circumstance creating reasonable doubt in the mind of a prudent person is available, the benefit of it is to be extended to the accused as of right and not as a concession. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1273; Abdul Wahid alias Budho v. State (Crl. A. No. 436-J and M.R. No. 18 of 2019); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Safdar Saleem Shahid.
records.title: Abdul Wahid alias Budho v. State (Crl. A. No. 436-J and M.R. No. 18 of 2019)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance Suit on 1966 Agreement Not Maintainable
records.heading: A suit for specific performance on a 1966 agreement was not maintainable
records.text: A suit for specific performance on an agreement of 1966 was held not maintainable, the questions raised being res judicata (s. 11 and O. XXIII R. 2 CPC), limitation (Art. 113) and Arts. 17 and 79 QSO. Remand was pointless after decades of litigation. Appeal dismissed on that footing and parties left to bear their own costs. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 257; Muhammad Afzal Khan v. Muhammad Aslam (decd.) thr. LRs (C.A. No. 176 of 2016, decided 17.05.2022); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Afzal Khan v. Muhammad Aslam (decd.) thr. LRs (C.A. No. 176 of 2016, decided 17.05.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift by Pardanashin Lady: Burden of Proof
records.heading: The person upholding a gift by a pardanashin lady must prove her understanding
records.text: The burden rests on the person seeking to uphold a transaction with a pardanashin or illiterate lady to prove that she executed the document with understanding of it. Whether a lady is pardanashin or illiterate is a question of fact, and the court must exercise particular care with such documents. Civil petition dismissed and leave declined. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 265; Abdul Aziz v. Mst. Zaib-un-Nissa and others (C.P. No. 2711 of 2019, decided 10.05.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Abdul Aziz v. Mst. Zaib-un-Nissa and others (C.P. No. 2711 of 2019, decided 10.05.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revisional Jurisdiction: Suo Motu and Time Bar
records.heading: A time barred revision needs sufficient cause explaining delay for each day
records.text: Revisional jurisdiction is corrective and supervisory, and a court may act suo motu to correct jurisdictional errors, but whether to do so rests in its discretion. Where the revision was time barred and the condonation application did not explain delay for each day, it was rightly dismissed. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 274; Khan Bahadur Khan v. Khan Malook Khan (C.P. No. 1824 of 2019, decided 10.05.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Khan Bahadur Khan v. Khan Malook Khan (C.P. No. 1824 of 2019, decided 10.05.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Cancellation of Inheritance Mutation: Shariat Application
records.heading: Inheritance mutation was correctly cancelled and all legal heirs take Shariat shares
records.text: Under s. 2-A of the West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1962, an acquisition by two sons through inheritance mutation no. 2207, made after the cut-off date of 15 March 1948, could not be saved and the mutation was correctly cancelled. All legal heirs are entitled to the estate by their Shariat shares. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 281; Mst. Raj Begum (deceased) through her L.Rs and others v. Mst. Ajaib Jan (deceased) through her L.Rs and others (C.A. No. 230 of 2016, decided 19.04.2022); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Mst. Raj Begum (deceased) through her L.Rs and others v. Mst. Ajaib Jan (deceased) through her L.Rs and others (C.A. No. 230 of 2016, decided 19.04.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 63-A(1)(b): Party Head's Direction to Members
records.heading: Deputy Speaker's exclusion of votes on a party head's direction lacked lawful authority
records.text: The Deputy Speaker excluded 10 PML(Q) votes in the election of the Chief Minister of Punjab on the basis of a direction under Art. 63-A(1)(b) given by the party head. The question was whether the party head is the relevant person to issue such a direction, and the ruling was declared to be without lawful authority. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 298; Chaudhry Parvez Elahi v. Deputy Speaker, Provincial Assembly of Punjab, Lahore and others (Const. P. No. 22 of 2022, decided 26.07.2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar.
records.title: Chaudhry Parvez Elahi v. Deputy Speaker, Provincial Assembly of Punjab, Lahore and others (Const. P. No. 22 of 2022, decided 26.07.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Single Fire Shot at Spur of Moment: s. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: A single shot at the spur of the moment falls under section 302(c) PPC
records.text: Where the accused fired a single shot at the spur of the moment over a blocked passage, without premeditation or alleged motive and without repeating it despite opportunity, the case fell under s. 302(c) PPC and the sentence was reduced to fourteen years. The accused's petition was converted into appeal and partly allowed, and the other petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 118; Gul Zarin etc. v. Kamal-ud-Din and others (Crl. P. Nos. 53-Q & 66-Q of 2020, decided 09.03.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Gul Zarin etc. v. Kamal-ud-Din and others (Crl. P. Nos. 53-Q & 66-Q of 2020, decided 09.03.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Alteration of Charge: Ahmadis and ss. 295-B, 295-C PPC
records.heading: Nothing prohibits Ahmadis from professing and practising their religion in their place of worship
records.text: On a complainant's application under s. 227 CrPC to add ss. 295-B and 295-C PPC, concerning Ahmadis styling their place of worship a mosque and displaying shaair-e-Islam, the Court observed that nothing prohibits Ahmadis from professing and practising their religion in their place of worship. It stated that a statute is expounded according to the legislature's express or manifest intention. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 122; Tahir Naqash, etc. v. State, etc. (Crl. P. 916-L of 2021, decided 12.01.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Tahir Naqash, etc. v. State, etc. (Crl. P. 916-L of 2021, decided 12.01.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Acquittal: Contradictions and Unsafe Custody of Charas
records.heading: Contradictory witnesses and unsafe custody of charas led to acquittal
records.text: In a recovery of 25 kilograms of charas, the complainant and the sole recovery witness did not corroborate each other on material points, said nothing of parcels being prepared at the spot or of their custody, and there was delay in sending the sample to the FSL. Petition allowed, convictions set aside and accused acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 131; Zafar Khan and another v. State (Jail Petition No. 42 of 2017, decided 11.02.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Zafar Khan and another v. State (Jail Petition No. 42 of 2017, decided 11.02.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: ss. 302(a), 302(b), 302(c) PPC: Scope and Common Intention
records.heading: Deciding individual liability after finding common intention under section 302(b) PPC defies the law
records.text: Section 302(a) PPC reflects Qisas under the Islamic system and is a distinct provision with its own considerations. A judgment that finds an offence under s. 302(b) in furtherance of common intention or object but decides on individual liability defies the intent of the law. The appeals were allowed and the matter remanded to the trial court to conclude the trial within two months. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 136; Bashir Ahmed and others v. State etc. (Crl. P. Nos. 1371 & 1651-L of 2016 and Crl. Misc. Appln. No. 1704 of 2017, decided 26.11.2020); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Bashir Ahmed and others v. State etc. (Crl. P. Nos. 1371 & 1651-L of 2016 and Crl. Misc. Appln. No. 1704 of 2017, decided 26.11.2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 22-A CrPC: Bona Fide Claim of Right
records.heading: Removal of property under a bona fide claim of right is not theft
records.text: A petition for registration of a case was rightly refused where the movable property allegedly taken was in a house belonging to the proposed accused, and so in her possession, and she had a bona fide claim of right over it. Its removal was not theft and disclosed no cognizable offence. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Islamabad 102; Muhammad Tanveer Ahmad v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace/Additional Sessions Judge-III, Islamabad-East and 3 others (W.P. No. 440 of 2022, decided 07.04.2022); Justice Saman Rafat Imtiaz.
records.title: Muhammad Tanveer Ahmad v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace/Additional Sessions Judge-III, Islamabad-East and 3 others (W.P. No. 440 of 2022, decided 07.04.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Protecting Female Heirs; Compromise Among Co-Sharers
records.heading: Courts must take greater care to protect female heirs and a compromise binds co-sharers
records.text: Courts must take greater care to protect the rights of female legal heirs against male heirs who seek to deprive them. Between co-sharers deriving title from a common predecessor, a lenient and flexible approach applies and hyper-technicalities are avoided. Parties are bound by a compromise made before a court between legal heirs and acted upon by one side. Ref: Liaqar Zarin v. Mst. Noor-ul-Haram (W.P. No. 1120-M of 2018, decided 04.07.2022).
records.title: Liaqar Zarin v. Mst. Noor-ul-Haram (W.P. No. 1120-M of 2018, decided 04.07.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Certiorari Against Court Judgment: Jurisdictional Defect
records.heading: Certiorari against a court judgment requires excess, improper exercise or lack of jurisdiction
records.text: A person seeking a writ of certiorari against a court's order or judgment must establish excess of jurisdiction, improper exercise of jurisdiction or lack of jurisdiction, so as to warrant interference by the High Court in constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: Liaqar Zarin v. Mst. Noor-ul-Haram (W.P. No. 1120-M of 2018, decided 04.07.2022).
records.title: Liaqar Zarin v. Mst. Noor-ul-Haram (W.P. No. 1120-M of 2018, decided 04.07.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift and Enhanced Dower: No Approbate and Reprobate
records.heading: Gift and enhanced dower are different, so a party cannot approbate and reprobate
records.text: Transfer of property by gift and by enhancement of dower are different propositions, so a party cannot approbate and reprobate by alleging both. Concurrent findings of fact are not interfered with on the ground that reappraisal could yield another view, unless misreading or non-reading of evidence affecting the merits is shown, relying on 1998 SCMR 760. Ref: Mst. Bakht Begum v. Afrin Khan (C.R. No. 429-M of 2018, decided 30.06.2022).
records.title: Mst. Bakht Begum v. Afrin Khan (C.R. No. 429-M of 2018, decided 30.06.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 322 PPC: Confinement Only on Default of Diyat
records.heading: A person convicted under section 322 PPC is confined only on default of diyat
records.text: An accused convicted under s. 322 PPC on a plea of guilty or after trial may be kept in confinement only if he defaults in paying diyat. Section 382-B CrPC does not apply in such cases. Ref: Zeeshan Hafeez v. The State (Cr. MBA No. 394-A of 2022, decided 27.06.2022).
records.title: Zeeshan Hafeez v. The State (Cr. MBA No. 394-A of 2022, decided 27.06.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal: Double Presumption of Innocence
records.heading: An acquitted accused enjoys a double presumption of innocence on appeal against acquittal
records.text: An appeal against acquittal was dismissed where the complainant's account contradicted the FIR on the number of shots, the police visit to the spot was contradicted by the investigating officer and recovery memo, the second eyewitness was insufficient for a capital charge, and recovery of the pistol was not established. An acquitted accused enjoys a double presumption of innocence. Ref: State through A.G Khyber Pakhtunkhwa v. Sajid Munir (Cr.A No. 55-D of 2017, decided 27.06.2022).
records.title: State through A.G Khyber Pakhtunkhwa v. Sajid Munir (Cr.A No. 55-D of 2017, decided 27.06.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Exaggerated Number of Accused; Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Exaggeration in the number of accused affects the veracity of the evidence
records.text: Where the number of accused charged is found exaggerated, the exaggeration reacts on the veracity of the evidence. Medical evidence is confirmatory, but where the eyewitness account fails to convince on mode, manner and number of accused, the conflict with it surfaces. If it cannot be determined which accused committed the offence, the benefit goes to all. Appeal allowed. Ref: Hamayun v. The State (Cr. A No. 206-B of 2021, decided 23.06.2022).
records.title: Hamayun v. The State (Cr. A No. 206-B of 2021, decided 23.06.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: s. 4 MFLO 1961: Widow of Predeceased Son
records.heading: The widow of a predeceased son takes no share under section 4 MFLO 1961
records.text: Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 benefits only the children of a predeceased son or daughter. The widow of a predeceased son is neither sharer nor residuary in her father-in-law's or mother-in-law's estate and is not entitled to a share in it. Ref: Mst. Hayat Begum v. Rehman Malik etc. (C.R. No. 441-M of 2019, decided 23.06.2022).
records.title: Mst. Hayat Begum v. Rehman Malik etc. (C.R. No. 441-M of 2019, decided 23.06.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration Requires Corroboration
records.heading: A dying declaration is weak evidence and needs corroboration before conviction
records.text: A dying declaration is regarded as weak evidence and it is unsafe to convict on it without corroboration, as it is not made on oath or subject to cross-examination and the maker may be affected by his condition. The essential ingredients for acting on it were not established. Criminal appeal allowed. Ref: Issa Khan v. The State (Cr. A No. 26-B of 2022, decided 22.06.2022).
records.title: Issa Khan v. The State (Cr. A No. 26-B of 2022, decided 22.06.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Single Accused: Courts Must Seek Corroboration
records.heading: Courts must seek independent corroboration even where only one accused is charged
records.text: Even where only one accused is charged, courts must search for independent corroboration, and trial and appellate courts must take extra care to avoid miscarriage of justice. The objection to the complainant's presence was not accepted. Appeal partially allowed, with benefit given to co-convict Said Awal Badshah. Ref: Umer Gul etc. v. The State etc. (Cr. A. No. 151-B of 2021, decided 21.06.2022).
records.title: Umer Gul etc. v. The State etc. (Cr. A. No. 151-B of 2021, decided 21.06.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Proof of Possession, Sampling and Safe Custody
records.heading: Prosecution must prove possession, sampling, sealing and safe transmission of contraband
records.text: The prosecution must prove conscious knowledge and control of the contraband by the accused, and must prove seizure, sampling, sealing on the spot and safe transmission to the police station and the FSL. A monogram of an officer absent at recovery casts serious doubt on recovery and parcels. A single doubt suffices to acquit. Ref: Shakeel Ahmad v. The State (Cr.A No. 291-M of 2021).
records.title: Shakeel Ahmad v. The State (Cr.A No. 291-M of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dying Declaration; Conversion to s. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: A sole dying declaration needs corroboration and conviction was converted to section 302(c) PPC
records.text: The sole declaration of a dying man is hardly a ground to convict unless corroborated, and the court examined whether the deceased was capable of talking and whether the doctor certified his alertness. Appeal partially allowed: conviction under s. 302(a) PPC was set aside and the appellant convicted under s. 302(c) PPC and sentenced to 15 years rigorous imprisonment. Ref: Irfan Ullah v. The State (Cr.A No. 131-B of 2021, decided 10.05.2022).
records.title: Irfan Ullah v. The State (Cr.A No. 131-B of 2021, decided 10.05.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Shuhada Package: Siblings Outside Definition of Family
records.heading: Siblings of deceased police personnel are outside the Shuhada package definition of family
records.text: Under Rule 2(c) of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Civil Servants Pension Rules, 2021, brothers and sisters of a deceased police personnel do not fall within the definition of family. Although they may be legal heirs under Muhammadan Law, the continuation of salary under the Shuhada package is restricted to the term family as defined in the Rules.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Rule 35 Prisons Rules: Set-Off of Period in Prison
records.heading: Under Rule 35 Prisons Rules, period in prison in another FIR counts as sentence served
records.text: Under Rule 35 of the Pakistan Prisons Rules, 1978 the period not counted as sentence served is that spent out of prison without being committed to prison again. The Superintendent was directed to count the petitioner's period in prison after 15.12.2021 in another FIR as sentence served in the s. 9(c) CNSA case. Ref: Rao Fakhar Nawaz v. Superintendent, New Central Jail Bahawalpur and another (Writ Petition No. 5078 of 2022).
records.title: Rao Fakhar Nawaz v. Superintendent, New Central Jail Bahawalpur and another (Writ Petition No. 5078 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Grandfather's Liability for Maintenance of Grandchildren
records.heading: A grandfather maintains grandchildren only where parents are unable and he is well off
records.text: The judgment discusses the doctrines of parens patriae and loco parentis. A grandfather becomes liable to maintain grandchildren only on two conditions: the father is impoverished and infirm and the mother is also hard up, and the grandfather is in easy circumstances. Ref: Safiya Ishaq etc. v. Judge Family Court etc. (Writ Petition No. 68950/2021).
records.title: Safiya Ishaq etc. v. Judge Family Court etc. (Writ Petition No. 68950/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Probation Ordinance s. 11: Effect of Conviction
records.heading: A conviction solely under the Probation Ordinance is no conviction for future purposes
records.text: Under s. 11 of the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960 a conviction solely under the Ordinance is not a conviction for any purpose in future and is confined to proceedings under the Ordinance. Under s. 11(2) it is disregarded for any law imposing a disqualification or disability on a convicted person. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1218.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Medical Re-Examination Order of Magistrate: Not Revisable
records.heading: A Magistrate's order on medical re-examination is executive and not revisable
records.text: An order of a Judicial Magistrate allowing or dismissing an application for medical re-examination of an injured person, including by a District or Provincial Standing Medical Board, is an executive order and is not amenable to revisional jurisdiction. The remedy lies by writ in the High Court. Ref: PLD 2020 Lahore 77.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Electricity Theft, Complainant's Grudge
records.heading: An accused with a good post-arrest bail case should not be refused pre-arrest bail
records.text: Under s. 498 CrPC in an electricity theft case under s. 462-I PPC, an accused with a good case for post-arrest bail cannot be sent behind bars for a few days at the wish of the complainant by refusing pre-arrest bail. The petitioner had deposited the detection bill and joined investigation. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 87; Ishtiaq Ahmad v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 78492-B of 2021, decided 30.03.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Ishtiaq Ahmad v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 78492-B of 2021, decided 30.03.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Private Money Lending Act 2007
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed in a private money lending case under section 498 CrPC
records.text: Sections 3 and 4 of the Punjab Prohibition of Private Money Lending Act, 2007 prohibit private money lending in the Province. Ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed under ss. 497(2) and 498 CrPC on fresh bail bonds of Rs. 100,000 with one surety. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 84; Mst. Kiran Bibi v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8733-B of 2013, decided 13.08.2013); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Mst. Kiran Bibi v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8733-B of 2013, decided 13.08.2013)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Is Not a Substitute for Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is not a substitute for post-arrest bail
records.text: Under s. 498 CrPC, anticipatory bail cannot be granted to undermine the investigative process, which includes arrest, and pre-arrest bail is not a substitute for post-arrest bail. Counsel could not show that the intended arrest was tainted with mala fides in a case under ss. 324, 148, 149 PPC. Ad-interim bail not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 80; Sagheer Ahmad alias Safeer Ahmad, etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 73877-B of 2021, decided 09.03.2022); Justice Sardar Ahmed Naeem.
records.title: Sagheer Ahmad alias Safeer Ahmad, etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 73877-B of 2021, decided 09.03.2022)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Bar Association Elections: Writ Not Maintainable
records.heading: Writ petition against a bar association election is not maintainable
records.text: Relying on Supreme Court authority, bar councils are autonomous bodies generating their own funds without government control and are not amenable to Art. 199. Their office bearers are therefore private individuals and not public functionaries for the purpose of a constitutional petition. The writ petition was not maintainable. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah Note 96; Muhammad Aafaq v. President Lahore High Court Bar Association etc. (W.P. No. 13215 of 2021, decided 21.03.2022); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Aafaq v. President Lahore High Court Bar Association etc. (W.P. No. 13215 of 2021, decided 21.03.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 22-A(6) CrPC and the FIA: Alternative Remedy
records.heading: Writ petition was not maintainable because an alternative remedy exists under section 22-A(6) CrPC
records.text: The Court considered whether 'police authorities' in s. 22-A(6) CrPC includes the FIA, noting that s. 5(1) of the FIA Act, 1974 gives its members provincial police powers in investigation. Because an adequate alternative remedy exists under s. 22-A(6), the writ petition was not maintainable and was dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah Note 83.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Women's Inheritance: Mutation Excluding Female Heirs Void
records.heading: Inheritance mutation excluding women shareholders is void and may be reversed without a civil court
records.text: Inheritance must first be mutated in the names of all shareholders including women. A transfer made by concealing or omitting women shareholders is void and may be reversed without resort to a civil court. Applications on the issue are to be treated as execution applications under the CPC or the Contempt of Court Act 2003, or as complaints under s. 200 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2021 Quetta 172; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Kamran Mulakhail.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Relevancy, Admissibility and Proof of Evidence
records.heading: Authority on relevance, admissibility, proof and evidentiary value in the law of evidence
records.text: Authority on principles of the law of evidence: relevance, admissibility, proof and evidentiary value. A fact is relevant if logically probative of a fact in issue and admissible if relevant and not excluded by any exclusionary provision. Relief beyond the prayer may be granted by looking at the whole plaint, as O. VII R. 7 CPC empowers effective or ancillary relief. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 715.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Meaning of Terrorism: s. 6 ATA 1997
records.heading: Larger bench authority on the meaning of terrorism under section 6 ATA
records.text: Authority on the meaning, scope and import of the term terrorism defined in s. 6 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, decided by a larger bench of the Supreme Court. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 61.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: s. 342 CrPC Statement and Grave and Sudden Provocation
records.heading: Section 342 CrPC statement accepted in full established grave and sudden provocation
records.text: Where the prosecution failed to prove its case, the accused's statement under s. 342 CrPC that he killed his sister and her paramour on seeing them committing zina was to be accepted in its entirety without proof under Art. 121 QSO. Taken as a whole it established grave and sudden provocation. Illicit sex with a female family member was considered sufficient to cause such provocation. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 201.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: First Proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC: Woman Accused
records.heading: The first proviso to section 497(1) CrPC allows bail to a woman accused
records.text: Explains the scope of the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, under which the court may direct the release on bail of a person under sixteen, a woman, or a sick or infirm person accused of an offence within the prohibitory clause. Bail in non-prohibitory offences is the rule and refusal the exception. The outcome is not stated in the post. Ref: Mst. Tahira Batool v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.910/2022, decided 19.08.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Mst. Tahira Batool v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.910/2022, decided 19.08.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotic Samples
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody and transmission of narcotic samples gives the benefit of doubt
records.text: Failure of the prosecution to establish safe custody of sample parcels in the Malkhana and their safe transmission to the laboratory, for example by not producing the Moharrar or the transmitting official, gives rise to benefit of doubt. In both judgments the Supreme Court set aside the convictions and acquitted the accused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1052, 2022 SCMR 1006.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Delay in Trial: Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance
records.heading: Bail lies for trial delay over one year not caused by the accused
records.text: Concerns post-arrest bail on the ground of delay in the conclusion of trial under s. 5(6) of the Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1984, and the constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court to grant bail. The post states that an accused is entitled to bail where trial is delayed for over one year through no fault of the accused, in offences not punishable with death. Ref: Syed Raza Hussain Bukhari v. The State through D.A.G. & another (Crl.P.636/2022, decided 10.08.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Syed Raza Hussain Bukhari v. The State through D.A.G. & another (Crl.P.636/2022, decided 10.08.2022)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Cheque Given for Vani/Swara Compromise Void
records.heading: A cheque given for a vani or swara compromise is void
records.text: A cheque issued as security for a compromise in a murder case, under which a girl was to be married into the victim's family (vani/swara), rests on unlawful consideration and is void under s. 24 of the Contract Act, 1872. The payee can neither sue on it nor invoke s. 489-F PPC. The compromise was void ab initio, and the Justice of Peace order was set aside as slipshod. Ref: Gul Sher v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 67567 of 2021, heard 23.02.2022).
records.title: Gul Sher v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 67567 of 2021, heard 23.02.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Torture and Physical Remand: Shahbaz Gill Petition
records.heading: Authority on torture and physical remand from the Islamabad High Court's detailed judgment
records.text: Authority on a constitutional petition against alleged torture and physical remand of the accused. The post only announces that the Islamabad High Court issued its detailed judgment on 22 August 2022 and does not state the holding. Ref: Muhammad Shahbaz Shabeer v. Additional Sessions Judge and others (Writ Petition No.3035 of 2022, decided 22.08.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Shahbaz Shabeer v. Additional Sessions Judge and others (Writ Petition No.3035 of 2022, decided 22.08.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Registers and s. 172 CrPC Privilege
records.heading: The trial court misconstrued section 172 CrPC in refusing to summon police registers
records.text: The right to fair trial under the CrPC is elevated by Art. 10-A of the Constitution. The trial court had refused to summon registers Nos. 2, 19 and 21 under the Police Rules, 1934 as privileged under s. 172 CrPC. The High Court examined the scope of s. 172, held the trial court had misconstrued it, and set aside its findings as illegal and erroneous. Ref: 2022 LHC 6197; Subhan Allah v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 43716/22, decided 14.07.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Subhan Allah v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 43716/22, decided 14.07.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ss. 16 and 17 CPC: Properties in Different Jurisdictions
records.heading: A suit over properties in different jurisdictions may be filed where any one lies
records.text: The words any portion of the property in ss. 16 and 17 CPC are not confined to one property. Where relief is sought over immovable properties in different court jurisdictions, the suit may be filed in any court within whose limits one of them lies, provided the cause of action is the same. Section 17 aims to avoid conflicting decisions and multiplicity of litigation. Ref: Abdul Habib & others v. Mst. Noor Bibi & others (Civil Petition Nos. 189-0 & 190-0 of 2017, decided 26.07.2022).
records.title: Abdul Habib & others v. Mst. Noor Bibi & others (Civil Petition Nos. 189-0 & 190-0 of 2017, decided 26.07.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Trust Property Board: Power to Sell Property
records.heading: A sale by the Evacuee Trust Property Board without Federal Government approval is void
records.text: Examines the authority of the Evacuee Trust Property Board to sell property under the Evacuee Trust Properties (Management & Disposal) Act, 1975, including ss. 3, 4 and 6 and the 1984 amendment inserting s. 4(2)(d). The High Court was held right that the sale deed, made without Federal Government approval, was illegal and void ab initio. Ref: Raja Ali Zaman (deceased) thr. LRs and another v. Evacuee Trust Property Board and another (Civil Appeal No.668 of 2022, decided 04.08.2022).
records.title: Raja Ali Zaman (deceased) thr. LRs and another v. Evacuee Trust Property Board and another (Civil Appeal No.668 of 2022, decided 04.08.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Time for Paying Cost of Certified Copies: s. 12 Limitation Act
records.heading: Exclusion under section 12 Limitation Act applies only after the copy application is submitted
records.text: Considers whether time taken by a litigant in paying the cost of certified copies is excluded under the newly added s. 12(5) of the Limitation Act. The post records the settled view that exclusion of time requisite under s. 12 applies only after the application for copies is submitted and covers time taken by court officials in preparing and issuing the copies. Ref: Pak Leather Crafts Limited and others v. Al-Barka Bank Pakistan Limited (Civil Appeal No. 24-K of 2019, decided 04.08.2022).
records.title: Pak Leather Crafts Limited and others v. Al-Barka Bank Pakistan Limited (Civil Appeal No. 24-K of 2019, decided 04.08.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint and Fresh Plaint
records.heading: Rejection under clause (d) of O. VII R. 11 CPC permits no fresh plaint
records.text: Under O. VII R. 11 CPC, defects under clauses (a), (b) and (c) may be cured and a fresh plaint presented, subject to limitation. Where a plaint is rejected under clause (d) because the suit is barred by law, a fresh plaint is not envisaged, and withdrawal with permission to file afresh cannot be allowed. A suit filed after limitation must be dismissed unless exclusion of time is pleaded. Ref: Muhammad Anwar (decd) through his LRs. etc. v. Abdul Hameed and others (Civil Petitions No. 3950 & 4047 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Anwar (decd) through his LRs. etc. v. Abdul Hameed and others (Civil Petitions No. 3950 & 4047 of 2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Presumption as to Thirty Year Old Documents
records.heading: The thirty year old document presumption is discretionary and requires the original before the court
records.text: The presumption of genuineness of a thirty year old document is discretionary and requires the original to be before the court. The court must not presume every document and signature genuine without considering the relevant factors under Art. 100 QSO. The agreement here was exhibited through a witness with no connection to it, proper custody was not shown, and the findings below were set aside. Ref: Abdul Habib & others v. Mst. Noor Bibi & others (Civil Petition Nos. 189-0 & 190-0 of 2017).
records.title: Abdul Habib & others v. Mst. Noor Bibi & others (Civil Petition Nos. 189-0 & 190-0 of 2017)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal Under ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC
records.heading: Applications under sections 249-A and 265-K may be taken at any stage of the trial
records.text: Applications under ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC may be taken up at any stage of the trial, but if there is even a slight probability of conviction the court should record evidence and decide on merits. The presumption of double innocence does not attach to acquittals under these provisions. Ref: Model Customs Collectorate, Islamabad v. Aamir Mumtaz Qureshi (Criminal Petition No.209 of 2018 and Crl. Misc. Application No.392 of 2018, decided 13.07.2022).
records.title: Model Customs Collectorate, Islamabad v. Aamir Mumtaz Qureshi (Criminal Petition No.209 of 2018 and Crl. Misc. Application No.392 of 2018, decided 13.07.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: Delayed s. 164 CrPC Identification
records.heading: Delayed naming in a section 164 CrPC statement called for further inquiry and bail
records.text: The accused was not nominated in the FIR and was named in a s. 164 CrPC statement made a month later, no source was disclosed, nothing was recovered from him and empties found were fired from different weapons. The alleged video confession had no prima facie evidentiary value. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC requiring further inquiry, and bail was granted. Ref: Abdul Wahid v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 103-P of 2022, decided 27.07.2022).
records.title: Abdul Wahid v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 103-P of 2022, decided 27.07.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses and Minor Discrepancies
records.heading: Relationship of witnesses is no ground to discard testimony, and minor discrepancies are ignored
records.text: Relationship of witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony unless previous enmity or ill will is shown. Substitution of the real culprit is a rare phenomenon, and minor discrepancies that do not shake the salient features of the prosecution case are to be ignored. Absence of blood at the scene was explained by the post-mortem findings. Ref: Azhar Hussain Hafl Ghous Bakhsh v. The State & others (Petition No. 190 of 2017, decided 16.08.2022).
records.title: Azhar Hussain Hafl Ghous Bakhsh v. The State & others (Petition No. 190 of 2017, decided 16.08.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence
records.text: Where ocular evidence is trustworthy and confidence inspiring it is preferred over medical evidence, and casual discrepancies between the two are possible. Relationship of witnesses with the deceased does not by itself discredit them absent previous enmity or ill will. The presence of the witnesses at the scene was natural, and development of rigor mortis in cold weather was not surprising. Ref: Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020, decided 31.05.2022).
records.title: Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020, decided 31.05.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Art. 12: Protection Against Retrospective Punishment at Bail Stage
records.heading: Article 12 protection against retrospective punishment is available even at the bail stage
records.text: Protection against retrospective punishment under Art. 12 of the Constitution is available to an accused even at the bail stage. Ref: 2022 LHC 6207; Khalid Mattoo v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 43237/22, decided 18.08.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Khalid Mattoo v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 43237/22, decided 18.08.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Exemption From Personal Appearance of Accused (Indian Supreme Court)
records.heading: A Magistrate may exempt an accused from personal appearance in rare summons cases
records.text: Indian Supreme Court guidelines. A Magistrate may in rare instances dispense with the personal appearance of an accused in a summons case where attendance would cause enormous hardship, taking the precautions stated. If the court considers that the accused or counsel is delaying the trial, it may direct appearance on each date under s. 205(2) CrPC. Appeal disposed of accordingly.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Transcripts: Evidentiary Value
records.heading: Call data record without transcripts or recordings is not worth reliance
records.text: Relying on Mian Khalid Pervaiz, CDR without transcripts or end to end recordings is not worth reliance, and the callers must be shown to be the persons concerned. The prosecution must also produce the competent witness who generated the CDR and show the SIM was owned by the accused. The CDR here was inconclusive, and its value was next to nothing. Ref: 2022 YLR 1822; Jamshaid alias Bablu v. State.
records.title: Jamshaid alias Bablu v. State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Orders Under s. 36 CPC
records.heading: Section 36 CPC allows a court to execute an executable order
