records.text: A court may get an executable order executed, as s. 36 CPC applies the provisions on execution of decrees to orders so far as applicable. In the case at hand no such executable order existed. Ref: 2022 YLR 1867.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Joint Identification Parades
records.heading: Joint identification parades are not barred and are not discarded merely for being joint
records.text: Joint identification is not prohibited by the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders, although separate proceedings are preferred as a rule of prudence. Where the proceedings are otherwise impeccable, they cannot be discarded solely because they were held jointly for more than one accused, particularly when each suspect stood in a separate row with the required dummies. Ref: 2022 YLR 1924.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in s. 324 PPC: Injury on Non-Vital Part
records.heading: Intention is apparent from successive shots, so bail on a non-vital part is unjustified
records.text: Amended s. 324 PPC punishes an act aimed at taking life with imprisonment up to ten years. Where successive shots are fired, intention is apparent, and granting bail because the victim was hit on a non-vital part unduly stretches the law. Single shot cases and club, hatchet or knife attacks may be treated differently. Ref: 2022 MLD 1531.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: s. 489-F PPC: Liability of Authorised Agent
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC requires dishonest issue and an authorised agent is liable only if dishonest
records.text: The elements of s. 489-F PPC are a valid cheque, dishonest intent, issue for repayment of a loan or fulfilment of an obligation, and dishonour. An authorised agent who draws the cheque may be liable, but the prosecution must establish his dishonesty. No material showed dishonest issue by the accused, so pre-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: 2022 MLD 1444.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Delay in FIR in s. 489-F Cases
records.heading: Delay in FIR is of little consequence in a section 489-F PPC case
records.text: Delay in registration of an FIR is not always fatal for the prosecution, particularly in white collar crimes or where the evidence is documentary. In an offence under s. 489-F PPC, which rests on dishonour of a cheque, delay is of little consequence. Ref: 2022 MLD 1444.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: ss. 16 and 17 Specific Relief Act 1877
records.heading: Section 16 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 is an exception to section 17
records.text: Section 16 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 is an exception to s. 17, which bars specific performance of part of a contract. Failure to fulfil a condition to construct did not defeat enforceability, and the case fell under s. 16. Section 14 was not attracted. Possession had been delivered and no steps were taken to cancel or terminate the agreement, so the decree was upheld. Ref: 2022 MLD 1474.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: s. 17-A(3) Family Courts Act: No Retrospective Effect
records.heading: Section 17-A(3) of the Family Courts Act does not operate retrospectively on final decrees
records.text: Section 17-A(3) of the Family Courts Act, 1964 (Punjab Amendment) does not operate retrospectively to reopen final decrees. Vested rights cannot be impaired by a new law unless it is expressly or by necessary intendment retrospective. The decree, which had disallowed annual increment and attained finality, could not be altered, and the constitutional petition was allowed. Ref: 2022 MLD 1523.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Revision Barred by Punjab Amendment to s. 115 CPC
records.heading: After the Punjab Amendment civil revision is not maintainable and a constitutional petition lies
records.text: After the Punjab Amendment Act XIV of 2018 added sub-section (5) to s. 115 CPC, a civil revision is not maintainable and a constitutional petition should be filed. The court may convert one type of proceeding into another and converted the revision into a constitutional petition, subject to payment of court fee. Ref: 2022 MLD 1411.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wife's Murder: Art. 122 QSO and Recovery of Body
records.heading: Recovery of the body from the accused's house hardly connects him with the crime
records.text: Where all other prosecution evidence is unreliable, an accused cannot be convicted of murdering his wife on supposition and failure to discharge the onus under Art. 122 QSO. Mere recovery of the body from his house, unsupported by any inmate, hardly connects him with the crime. Ref: 2022 YLR 1844.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXIX R. 2B CPC Omitted: Interim Injunction
records.heading: Interim injunction cannot be refused after omission of O. XXXIX R. 2B CPC
records.text: After omission of O. XXXIX R. 2B CPC, dismissal of an application for interim injunction on the ground that relief was being extended beyond one year of the initial order was per incuriam and unjustified, especially as no earlier interim order had been made for the applicant. Ref: 2022 LHC 6212; Ameer Ali v. S.E West Circles Motor Canal etc. (Civil Revision 47469/22, decided 04.08.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Ameer Ali v. S.E West Circles Motor Canal etc. (Civil Revision 47469/22, decided 04.08.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Mandatory or Directory Provisions: Tests
records.heading: Legislative intent is the ultimate test of whether a provision is mandatory or directory
records.text: The ultimate test for whether a provision is mandatory or directory is legislative intent. The word shall is one indicator, along with penal consequences, the object and purpose of the enactment, and whether non-compliance causes inconvenience or injustice. The post also refers to s. 7(5) of the Act requiring an application for leave to defend to be accompanied by supporting documents. Ref: Syed Haider Ali v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited etc. (R.F.A No.12451/2022, heard 23.06.2022).
records.title: Syed Haider Ali v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited etc. (R.F.A No.12451/2022, heard 23.06.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mortgage: Rights of Mortgagor and Mortgagee
records.heading: Mortgagor and mortgagee hold independent proprietary rights of redemption and possession
records.text: Discusses the nature of a mortgage and the independent proprietary rights of mortgagor (redemption) and mortgagee (possession on default), which may be transferred to others. Refers to s. 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and the Punjab Redemption and Restitution of Mortgaged Lands Act, 1962. The post does not give the outcome. Ref: Dadu Khan (decd.) thr. LRs and 3 others v. Ghulam Abbas and 23 others (Civil Appeal No.339 of 2016, decided 23.08.2022).
records.title: Dadu Khan (decd.) thr. LRs and 3 others v. Ghulam Abbas and 23 others (Civil Appeal No.339 of 2016, decided 23.08.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Intimidation and Overt Act: s. 506 PPC
records.heading: Where criminal intimidation results in an overt act, section 506 PPC does not apply
records.text: Under ss. 503 and 506 PPC, where criminal intimidation results in an overt act, the provision on criminal intimidation (s. 506) does not apply and only the offence constituted by the overt act remains. Ref: Rana Muhammad Imran Nasrullah v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition No 358-L of 2022).
records.title: Rana Muhammad Imran Nasrullah v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition No 358-L of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical v Ocular Discrepancies and Related Witnesses
records.heading: Casual discrepancies between medical and ocular evidence do not discredit related witnesses
records.text: Casual discrepancies between medical and ocular evidence are possible, as witnesses under firing make only tentative assessments of where shots landed. Relationship of witnesses with the deceased is no ground to reject them absent enmity, substitution is rare, and minor discrepancies are ignored. Absence of a recovered empty made the rifle recovery inconsequential. Ref: Shamsher Ahmad v. The State (Jail Petition No. 154 of 2016 and Criminal Petition No. 108-1 of 2016).
records.title: Shamsher Ahmad v. The State (Jail Petition No. 154 of 2016 and Criminal Petition No. 108-1 of 2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Circumstance Sufficient
records.heading: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to benefit as of right
records.text: Any doubt in the prosecution case is resolved in favour of the defence. A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt in a prudent mind about guilt entitles the accused to the benefit as a matter of right. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1328.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Delimitation: Object and Purpose
records.heading: Delimitation must be a fair and neutral exercise by a neutral body
records.text: Delimitation is an indispensable stage of the electoral process, as it fashions the weight of a vote. It must be a fair and neutral exercise by a neutral body, since partisan political intervention leads to gerrymandering and erodes confidence in elections. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 607.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Judicial Review of Delimitation
records.heading: High Court jurisdiction to review delimitation orders under Article 199 is not barred
records.text: Constitutional courts do not readily surrender jurisdiction where an order is illegal and no alternate remedy is prescribed. The High Court's jurisdiction to review orders, notifications and acts of the Delimitation Authority and Delimitation Committee is not barred. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 607.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Arts. 218 and 219: Electoral Rolls and Objections
records.heading: Election Commission prepares electoral rolls under Article 219(a) and must hear objections
records.text: The Election Commission prepares electoral rolls under Art. 219(a), including for local government elections, and must give an opportunity to deal with objections. Art. 218 requires it to conduct elections justly, fairly and in accordance with law, including all arrangements before Election Day. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 607.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Witnesses Exonerating Co-Accused
records.heading: Witnesses exonerating a co-accused cast serious doubt on their credibility
records.text: The FIR was registered after 11 days. The injured witnesses and the complainant later exonerated a co-accused who had been ascribed a dagger blow, and the case against the appellant rested on the same evidence. This conduct cast serious doubt on their credibility, and a single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right (ss. 302(b), 337-F(ii) PPC). Ref: 2022 SCMR 1527.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Judge Must Know and Apply the Law
records.heading: A judge is expected to know and apply the law correctly
records.text: Justice must be administered according to the law even where the parties are misdirected or misplaced in that regard. A judge is expected to know all the laws of the country, and failure of counsel to advise properly is not a complete excuse for applying the wrong law. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1546.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-i-Ishhad and Talb-i-Muwathibat Requirements
records.heading: Talb-i-Ishhad notice must be served on the vendor by registered post with acknowledgment due
records.text: Notice of Talb-i-Ishhad must be served on the vendor through registered post with acknowledgment due. The pre-emptor, claiming as Shafi Jar, failed to prove common irrigation or passage and had contradictory evidence on the making of Talb-i-Muwathibat. All courts below correctly found the legal requirements unfulfilled. Leave to appeal refused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1522.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Stage: No Deeper Appraisal of Evidence
records.heading: At the bail stage the court does not dig deep into the evidence
records.text: At the bail stage under s. 497 CrPC the court is not meant to dig deep into the evidence or scrutinise factual aspects of the case. That is the responsibility of the trial court, after evidence is adduced by both sides. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1511.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Robbery s. 392 PPC: Unreliable Recovery Evidence
records.heading: Section 392 PPC conviction cannot stand without reliable recovery or identification evidence
records.text: The complainant admitted he did not see the snatching, concealment of cash by digging while chased appeared impossible, no recovery or identification of the mobile phone or looted articles was established, and the motorcycle could not be used against the accused. Conviction under s. 392 PPC could not be sustained. Appeal partly allowed and robbery conviction set aside. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1577.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Single Witness: Quality Over Quantity
records.heading: In a section 302(b) PPC case quality of evidence matters more than quantity
records.text: In a s. 302(b) PPC case the quality and not the quantity of evidence is considered. The evidence of one person, if confidence inspiring, is sufficient to sustain conviction. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1577.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Reliance Not Safe
records.heading: A dying declaration recorded by the investigating officer without disclosing time and place is unsafe
records.text: A dying declaration recorded by the investigating officer, without disclosure of its time and place and without producing that officer in court, could not be given credence (Art. 46 QSO; s. 302(b) PPC). The police were present at hospital yet did not record the statement at the first opportunity. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1515.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Pistol Inconsequential on Negative Forensic Match
records.heading: Pistol recovery is inconsequential where forensic match with crime empties is negative
records.text: A .30 bore pistol recovered on the accused's pointation was sent to the Forensic Science Agency, but the match with crime empties was negative, so the recovery became inconsequential (s. 302(b) PPC). Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1567.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Plea of Alibi Established
records.heading: Plea of alibi established through verification by the Commanding Officer led to acquittal
records.text: The accused pleaded he was visiting a cousin at a military Battalion in another city. The investigating officer found the plea true and obtained a verification letter from the Commanding Officer, and a serving member of the forces deposed in support. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1567.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved
records.heading: Motive is not proved where the prosecution does not produce the person involved
records.text: The alleged motive was a previous quarrel between a co-accused and the complainant's son, but the prosecution did not produce the son, so the motive was not proved. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1567.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion Cannot Be Sole Basis of Conviction
records.heading: Absconsion cannot be the sole basis of conviction
records.text: Absconsion cannot be viewed as proof of the crime, and an accused cannot be convicted only on that basis. The prosecution must prove its case independently beyond any reasonable shadow of doubt. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1567, 2022 SCMR 1148.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Joint Recovery and Delayed Crime Empties Inadmissible
records.heading: Joint recovery of weapons from an open place has no evidentiary value
records.text: A joint recovery of weapons by several accused from an open place, with no indication of who first led to it, has no evidentiary value. Crime empties neither kept in safe custody nor sent to the Chemical Examiner for over two months without explanation were inadmissible. Appeals allowed and convictions under s. 13(e) of the Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965 set aside. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1494.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rule of Consistency: Acquitted Co-Accused
records.heading: Rule of consistency applies where acquitted co-accused also fired at the deceased
records.text: Co-accused who also fired at the deceased had all been acquitted, the locale of their shots was undescribed, and any of them could have caused the chest injuries. The s. 173 CrPC report found the accused involved only through mobile phone contact with co-accused, so nothing distinguished his case (ss. 302(b), 109 PPC). Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1540.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documentary Evidence Over Oral Evidence
records.heading: Documentary evidence takes precedence over conflicting oral evidence
records.text: Documentary evidence takes precedence over oral evidence, especially where oral assertions are in direct conflict with documentary evidence. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1532.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Family Settlement: Charge and Registration
records.heading: A family settlement deed needs no compulsory registration and the charge passes with property
records.text: A charge created on property through a family settlement passes with the property to the legal heirs (s. 100). Where a family settlement is in the form of a deed and not a regular partition deed, it does not require compulsory registration (s. 17). Ref: 2022 SCMR 1532.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Entries in Revenue Record: Patwari's Duty
records.heading: A Patwari must make revenue entries on evidence and cannot make arbitrary entries
records.text: A Patwari has no power to make arbitrary entries in the relevant register and must make entries based on the evidence before him (s. 42 as cited in the headnote). Ref: 2022 SCMR 1532.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Second Appeal: Interference with Findings of Fact
records.heading: Interference in second appeal under section 100 CPC needs a decision contrary to law
records.text: The High Court normally does not interfere in second appeal under s. 100 CPC unless the decision below is contrary to law or fails to determine a material issue of law. Once it entertains the appeal, it may determine an issue of fact if the conditions of s. 103 CPC are met, as concurrent findings of fact are not sacrosanct. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 589.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Scribe Is Not an Attesting Witness: Art. 79
records.heading: A scribe is not an attesting witness under Article 79 QSO
records.text: Under Art. 79 QSO the deposition of a scribe cannot be equated with that of an attesting witness. In a suit for possession and injunction on an alleged sale deed, execution of unsigned pages and the second marginal witness were not proved and the plaintiff's brother was produced as scribe. The second appeal was allowed and the concurrent decrees were set aside. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 589.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unproved Motive as Mitigating Circumstance in Qatl-i-Amd
records.heading: Unproved motive is a mitigating circumstance on sentence under section 302(b) PPC
records.text: Absence of motive, or failure to prove an alleged motive, is a sufficient mitigating circumstance for the quantum of sentence under s. 302(b) PPC. The prosecution bears the burden of proving motive alleged in the FIR. Conviction was maintained but the death sentence was converted to life imprisonment. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1608; Muhammad Shoban v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Shoban v. State

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Safe Custody and Transmission of Samples
records.heading: Prosecution failed to prove safe custody and transmission of narcotic samples
records.text: The prosecution failed to prove safe custody and transmission of sample parcels, as neither the Moharrar nor the depositing constable was produced and the parcels reached the laboratory three days after recovery. The vehicle was also never produced. Benefit of doubt was given, the appeal was allowed and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1422.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Government Department and Condonation of Delay
records.heading: A government department is treated as an ordinary litigant when seeking condonation of delay
records.text: A government department is treated as an ordinary litigant when seeking condonation of delay. A restoration application barred by limitation required sufficient cause explained in the condonation application, and the counsel's affidavits and lack of medical certificate did not show it. Limitation is not a mere technicality because valuable rights accrue on its expiry. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1615; SKB-KNK Joint Venture Contractor v. Water and Power Development Authority.
records.title: SKB-KNK Joint Venture Contractor v. Water and Power Development Authority

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revisional Jurisdiction on Divergent Findings
records.heading: High Court must re-appraise the whole evidence where trial and appellate findings diverge
records.text: Where the trial court and appellate court reach divergent findings, the High Court in revisional jurisdiction must re-appraise the entire evidence to determine which court's findings rest on proper appraisal of evidence and appreciation of law. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1625; Mst. Azra Gulzar v. Muhammad Farooq.
records.title: Mst. Azra Gulzar v. Muhammad Farooq

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: NAB Bail: Pick and Choose Among Co-Accused
records.heading: Supreme Court declined to allow NAB to pick and choose among co-accused
records.text: Where co-accused whose role was prima facie worse had not been arrested, and NAB gave no intelligible differentia for the classification, the Supreme Court declined to perpetuate it despite s. 24(a) NAO. Leave petitions were converted into appeals and allowed, ad-interim bail was confirmed and others received post-arrest bail. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1612.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Cancellation of Appointments: Vested Rights and Natural Justice
records.heading: Appointments cannot be cancelled by omnibus order without reasons, hearing or show cause notice
records.text: Appointment letters were cancelled by an omnibus order without reasons, hearing or show cause notice. The court noted they were issued after codal formalities and no ground based on R. 9(6) of the 2009 Rules was shown, and that action should lie against officials who violated rules, not low paid appointees. Describes the doctrine of vested rights. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1583.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Illegal Order Creates No Perpetual Rights
records.heading: Employees gain no perpetual rights from an illegal order
records.text: If an order is illegal, employees cannot gain perpetual rights on the basis of it. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1583.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: No Vested Right to Antedated Seniority
records.heading: No employee has a vested right to antedated seniority
records.text: No antedated seniority can be claimed as a vested right. No one has a vested right to a particular promotion or seniority, which are governed by the applicable rules and regulations. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1618.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Challenge to Inheritance Mutation: Acquiescence and Limitation
records.heading: A long delayed challenge to an inheritance mutation after third party rights arise fails
records.text: An heir who sits idly by and challenges a long standing inheritance mutation only after third party rights are created must show lack of awareness, cogent reasons for delay, and collusion or knowledge on the buyer's part. The plaintiffs allowed third party interest, including 444 plot allottees, to arise, and the suit was dismissed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1558.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Daughters Deprived of Inheritance on Custom
records.heading: Daughters excluded from inheritance on custom are entitled to Shariat shares
records.text: Sons who relied on a 1956 inheritance mutation excluding their sisters did not establish acquisition in accordance with the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Acts, even if the father died before 15 March 1948. All legal heirs were entitled to shares under Islamic shariat, the appeal was dismissed, and the records were directed to be corrected. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1394.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Who Is Complainant After Death
records.heading: A power of attorney executed by a deceased complainant does not exist in law
records.text: On the complainant's death, a power of attorney executed by the deceased did not exist in law. Initiation of prosecution lies with the aggrieved person under s. 154 CrPC and withdrawal with the Public Prosecutor under s. 494 CrPC. The extended definition of aggrieved person under the 1990 Ordinance covers only bodily harm, not ss. 448 and 380 PPC. Pre-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1115.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental and Criminal Proceedings Concurrently
records.heading: Disciplinary proceedings do not depend on the outcome of concurrent criminal proceedings
records.text: The outcome of disciplinary proceedings does not depend on the outcome of concurrent criminal proceedings. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1520.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Consequential Relief Where Main Relief Time-Barred
records.heading: Consequential relief is of no avail where the main relief is time-barred
records.text: When the main relief sought in a suit is barred by limitation, the consequential relief, even if within time, is of no legal avail. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1481.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Merits and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Merits may be touched in pre-arrest bail and further inquiry justified granting it
records.text: Merits may be touched upon when granting the extraordinary relief of pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC. Here no one was injured, the accused was unarmed, his son had received bail, and false implication in a civil dispute was possible. The case fell under s. 497(2) CrPC and pre-arrest bail was granted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1424.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Attempt to Commit Qatl-i-Amd: s. 324 PPC Ingredients
records.heading: Guilt under section 324 PPC turns on the act, intention and surrounding circumstances
records.text: In a s. 324 PPC case, the nature of the act done, the intention of the offender and the circumstances leading to the occurrence are the essential matters to be examined in deciding guilt. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1424.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in s. 489-F PPC: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail in a section 489-F PPC case outside the prohibitory clause is the rule
records.text: Bail in offences outside the prohibitory clause is the rule and refusal the exception, and registration of another FIR does not disentitle an accused with a prima facie case. The accused had been in custody over four months, the maximum sentence was three years, and whether the cheque was issued was for the trial court. Bail was granted under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1467.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Purpose of s. 489-F PPC
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC is not a means of recovering an alleged amount
records.text: Section 489-F PPC is not intended by the Legislature as a means of recovering an alleged amount. Civil proceedings, including under O. XXXVII CPC, provide the remedies for recovery. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1467.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Sodomy Case: Medical and DNA Reports
records.heading: Bail granted in a sodomy case where medical and DNA reports raised further inquiry
records.text: The prompt medico-legal report found no injury and a normal anus, and the DNA report could not override it. With the FIR lodged two days after the occurrence, the case called for further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Leave was converted into appeal and bail was allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1447.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Contradictory Medical Evidence on Accused's Injury
records.heading: Contradictory medical evidence on the accused's injury called for further inquiry and bail
records.text: Medical evidence on the injury attributed to the accused was contradictory, and it appeared superficial compared with the firearm injury of a co-accused and the stated cause of death. Common intention under s. 34 PPC was for trial. The case required further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC and bail was allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1444.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Judge's Widow: Benefits Under Office Memorandum 2015
records.heading: A Judge's widow is entitled to benefits under the Office Memorandum of 2015
records.text: The widow of a Judge who died in service is entitled to the benefits of the office memorandum of 4 December 2015, including rent of a hired house until superannuation age and a lump sum in lieu of a plot if none was allotted. The impugned 2020 office memoranda were set aside and the petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 693.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Rules 197-A to 197-C Punjab Motor Vehicles Rules: Previous Publication
records.heading: Government must follow the previous publication requirement when making Motor Vehicles Rules
records.text: Considered whether publication of draft rules, without re-publication, substantially complied with s. 119 of the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 and s. 22 of the Punjab General Clauses Act, given two decades of enforcement. The declaration was confined to the case, and the Government must follow the previous publication requirement in future. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 569.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Duty of Trial Judge on Admissibility of Evidence
records.heading: A trial judge must check admissibility while recording evidence and decide objections at once
records.text: A trial judge must check the admissibility of evidence while recording it, without waiting for an objection from either side, and must decide an admissibility objection then and there rather than deferring it to the end of the trial. Ref: 2018 SCMR 2092.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Criminal History: Acquitted Cases Not to Be Listed
records.heading: Acquitted cases must not be listed in a person's criminal history
records.text: Listing cases ending in acquittal in a petitioner's criminal history violates his fundamental rights and misleads the court. Criminal history must reflect only convictions, including suspended sentences, and pending FIRs in which he stands arraigned. Police were directed to comply with instructions of the Additional IG (Investigation). Ref: 2022 LHC 6253; Zulfiqar Ali v. JOP etc. (Criminal Proceedings 47617/22, decided 18.08.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Zulfiqar Ali v. JOP etc. (Criminal Proceedings 47617/22, decided 18.08.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Late Submission of s. 173 CrPC Police Report
records.heading: Late submission of section 173 CrPC police reports violates the right to fair trial
records.text: Late submission of police reports under s. 173 CrPC causes miscarriage of justice and violates Arts. 4, 9 and 10A of the Constitution, as pre-trial proceedings fall within fair trial. The High Court issued directions for timely submission, with failure by an investigating officer to be reported to his superiors for action. Ref: 2022 LHC 6257; Muhammad Razzaq v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 23198/22, decided 18.08.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Razzaq v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 23198/22, decided 18.08.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Court Fee Default: O. VII R. 11(c) CPC
records.heading: Continuous default in court fee forfeits leniency and attracts O. VII R. 11(c) CPC
records.text: Court fee exists to secure State revenue, not to give a litigant a technical weapon, and the law favours flexibility in curing deficiencies. A litigant who shows continuous default or delinquent conduct in making good the deficiency forfeits that leniency, and O. VII R. 11(c) CPC applies. Ref: Muhammad Azeem v. Noor Muhammad (deceased) (Civil Revision No.1365-D/2016, decided 16.05.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Azeem v. Noor Muhammad (deceased) (Civil Revision No.1365-D/2016, decided 16.05.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Sexual Harassment at Workplace: PTV Controller
records.heading: Sexual harassment at PTV was proved and complaints are decided irrespective of reporting delay
records.text: The Supreme Court held that sexual harassment of women at PTV was proved and ordered the respondent to pay Rs 500,000 to each of six women. It welcomed the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace amendments and stated that complaints are decided on merits irrespective of delay in reporting. Ref: Ather Farooq Buttar v. Federation of Pakistan thr. its Secretary M/o Information, Broadcasting and National Heritage, Islamabad & others (C.P.1347/2019, decided 27.07.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Ather Farooq Buttar v. Federation of Pakistan thr. its Secretary M/o Information, Broadcasting and National Heritage, Islamabad & others (C.P.1347/2019, decided 27.07.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Investigation of Offences Relating to Religion
records.heading: Investigation of Chapter XV PPC offences must follow the law and require corroboration
records.text: The Supreme Court directed that its order go to the prosecution departments of all provinces and Islamabad so that investigation of Chapter XV PPC offences follows the law. It noted that false allegations are often made to settle scores, that s. 295-C carries only death, that corroboration is required and that proof must remain beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: Salamat Mansha Masih v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 883-L of 2022, decided 23.08.2022).
records.title: Salamat Mansha Masih v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 883-L of 2022, decided 23.08.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail of Woman Under KP Narcotics Act
records.heading: Sections 497 and 498 CrPC apply to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa narcotics offences
records.text: Sections 497 and 498 CrPC apply to offences under the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Control of Narcotic Substances Act 2019. Under the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, bail is the rule even in prohibitory clause offences, and a woman's petition is also examined under that proviso if s. 497(2) does not assist. The nature of an offence may indicate likelihood of repetition. Ref: Mst. Fursan v. The State through Addl. Advocate General, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Crl.P.994/2022, decided 26.08.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Mst. Fursan v. The State through Addl. Advocate General, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Crl.P.994/2022, decided 26.08.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Voluntary Retirement and Pension: Amended s. 12
records.heading: Amended section 12 applies prospectively and does not affect earlier retirement orders
records.text: Amended s. 12 applies prospectively and does not affect retirement orders lawfully passed before its commencement, even if retirement takes effect after leave preparatory to retirement. The Finance Department had no authority to clarify otherwise. An accrued vested right to retire and receive pension is protected by the doctrine of locus poenitentiae. Ref: 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1156.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Deputationist: Status and Repatriation
records.heading: A deputationist has no vested right to tenure and may be repatriated
records.text: A civil servant working as an officer of the Punjab Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education on deputation does not lose civil servant status. A deputationist has no vested right to the tenure of deputation and may be repatriated by the competent authority. A repatriation order is not open to challenge under Art. 199 in this manner. Ref: 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1209.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Document Outside Challan Produced in Cross-Examination
records.heading: A relevant document produced in cross-examination and exhibited may be considered by the court
records.text: A document not part of the challan, produced by a witness at defence counsel's request in cross-examination and exhibited, can be considered. The court cannot refuse a relevant document, as search for truth is its primary duty. The post also notes no express right to State-funded counsel outside capital cases. Ref: 2015 PCrLJ 1566.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: No Right to Appointment Against Vacated Posts
records.heading: Unsuccessful candidates have no right to appointment against posts that fall vacant
records.text: A Public Service Commission need not maintain a list of unsuccessful candidates or a waiting list. Absent a legal provision requiring it, candidates who were not recommended acquire no legal or constitutional right to appointment against posts that fall vacant, and High Court jurisdiction could not be invoked. Ref: 2022 SCMR 650, 2022 PLC (C.S.) 877.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Filling Posts Vacated After Selection: Principles
records.heading: Posts vacated after selection should be re-advertised and waiting lists used only exceptionally
records.text: Competitive examinations by Public Service Commissions form one selection and all vacancies are to be filled in one go. Posts left vacant because candidates did not join or quit should be re-advertised for open competition. Use of a waiting list is limited to exceptional circumstances and only where the governing rules permit. Ref: 2022 SCMR 650, 2022 PLC (C.S.) 877.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Substitute Candidate for Vacated Post: Punjab PSC Regulations
records.heading: Substitute from the merit list is recommended only if the department requests it
records.text: Regulations 59 and 62 of the Punjab Public Service Commission Regulations, 2016 allow a substitute from the merit list during its validity if the department so requests. The obligation to recommend is conditional on that request, and an unselected candidate has no automatic right of appointment. Ref: 2020 SCMR 976, 2020 PLC (C.S.) 753.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Waiting List Candidates for Unfilled Posts
records.heading: Departments must consider remaining waiting list candidates when selected candidates refuse to join
records.text: Where selected candidates refuse to join and posts remain vacant, the department must consider remaining waiting list candidates, as posts cannot be kept vacant until the next recruitment while selected candidates remain available on the waiting list. Ref: 2022 SCMR 739.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape Victim's Testimony; Consent Immaterial Below Age
records.heading: A rape victim's single testimony suffices to uphold conviction
records.text: A rape victim stands on a higher pedestal than an injured witness and her single testimony suffices to uphold conviction. Under s. 375 PPC consent is immaterial where the victim is below the age of consent. Force need not be physical restraint, as fear of violence suffices, and absence of cries or immediate disclosure did not dislodge the prosecution case. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1241, PLD 2022 Lahore 645; Kamran etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 38038 & 30076 & Crl. Rev. No. 30079 of 2019); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kamran etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 38038 & 30076 & Crl. Rev. No. 30079 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification Distinguished from Recognition
records.heading: Recognition of a previously known person needs no identification parade
records.text: Identification and recognition differ. Recognising someone previously known, such as by profession or from the workplace or neighbourhood, does not require knowing his name or parentage, and a formal identification parade is unnecessary for such a person. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1241, PLD 2022 Lahore 645; Kamran etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 38038 & 30076 & Crl. Rev. No. 30079 of 2019); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kamran etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 38038 & 30076 & Crl. Rev. No. 30079 of 2019)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail Granted by ATC
records.heading: Section 497(5) CrPC does not apply to cancellation of bail granted by an ATC
records.text: The High Court may examine the correctness, legality and propriety of a bail order under ss. 435 and 439 CrPC read with s. 561-A CrPC. As bail for ATC-triable accused is granted under s. 21-D ATA, s. 497(5) CrPC does not apply to cancellation of such bail. Ref: Malik Tariq Ayub & another v. Raja Arshad Mehmood & another (Criminal Misc. No.326-BC of 2019, decided 19.04.2022).
records.title: Malik Tariq Ayub & another v. Raja Arshad Mehmood & another (Criminal Misc. No.326-BC of 2019, decided 19.04.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness of Plaintiff
records.heading: Specific performance requires equitable conduct and readiness and willingness of the plaintiff
records.text: Specific performance under ss. 12 and 22 of the Specific Relief Act is discretionary and requires equitable conduct. Under s. 24(b) it cannot be granted to a person who has become incapable of performing or who violates an essential term, so the plaint must state compliance and readiness to pay the balance. Omission may invite O. VII R. 11(d) CPC consequences. Ref: Abdus Salam Khan Barki, etc. v. Mian Pervaiz Akhtar, etc. (RFA No. 51 of 2013, decided 22.02.2022).
records.title: Abdus Salam Khan Barki, etc. v. Mian Pervaiz Akhtar, etc. (RFA No. 51 of 2013, decided 22.02.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: No-Fault Dissolution and Haq Mehr
records.heading: A wife may obtain khula without proving fault
records.text: A wife may seek no-fault dissolution without proving cause, and this does not contradict Islamic jurisprudence. Where she is unwilling to stay in the marriage at pre-trial reconciliation, the Family Court must pronounce dissolution forthwith. Questions of fault and return of Haq Mehr are decided separately by issues and evidence, and do not revive a dissolved marriage on appeal. Ref: Shaza Tehseen v. Tehseen Butt, etc. (Writ Petition No. 4332 of 2021, decided 21.02.2022).
records.title: Shaza Tehseen v. Tehseen Butt, etc. (Writ Petition No. 4332 of 2021, decided 21.02.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Preliminary Decree in Partition
records.heading: A preliminary decree in partition is executable and gives the auction purchaser vacant possession
records.text: A preliminary decree under the Partition Act, 1893 is a decree under s. 2 CPC and is executable. A co-sharer is not a tenant and cannot claim adverse possession against a court auction purchaser, who is entitled to vacant possession without separate ejectment proceedings. A co-sharer who later buys other shares stands as a third party purchaser. Ref: Syed Ali Asim Jaffari, etc. v. Qamar Abbas, etc. (Civil Revision No. 67 of 2021, decided 15.08.2022).
records.title: Syed Ali Asim Jaffari, etc. v. Qamar Abbas, etc. (Civil Revision No. 67 of 2021, decided 15.08.2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Probational Release Under Good Conduct Prisoners Act 1926
records.heading: Explanation of release on licence under the Good Conduct Prisoners Probational Release Act 1926
records.text: Explains ss. 2 to 6 of the Good Conduct Prisoners Probational Release Act, 1926, covering release on licence for likely good conduct, duration of the licence, counting of licence time as sentence served, and revocation. It also refers to the rules on rolls examined by the Assistant Director. The outcome is not stated. Ref: Muhammad Imran v. Assistant Director, Reclamation and proclamation, ICT, Islamabad etc. (W.P. NO.2131-2022, decided 24.08.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Assistant Director, Reclamation and proclamation, ICT, Islamabad etc. (W.P. NO.2131-2022, decided 24.08.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Primary and Secondary Evidence: Proof of Documents
records.heading: Documents are proved by primary evidence and admission in evidence does not prove them
records.text: Under Arts. 72 to 76 QSO, contents of documents are proved by primary evidence, with secondary evidence admissible only in the exceptional circumstances in Art. 76. Admission of a document in evidence does not by itself prove it, because the method of proof is distinct from adducing it. Ref: Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem, etc. (W.P. No.2163/2019, decided 07.06.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem, etc. (W.P. No.2163/2019, decided 07.06.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Breach of Trust: Ingredients of s. 405 PPC
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust under section 405 PPC requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation
records.text: Criminal breach of trust under s. 405 PPC requires entrustment of property or dominion over it and dishonest misappropriation, conversion or disposal in violation of trust. The property must belong to someone other than the accused, and the prosecution must prove mens rea, dishonesty being defined in s. 24 PPC. Ref: Muhammad Ibrar Khan v. Mian Muhammad Ramzan etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 67 of 2020, decided 20.05.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Ibrar Khan v. Mian Muhammad Ramzan etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 67 of 2020, decided 20.05.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal Under s. 249-A CrPC Must Be Reasoned
records.heading: An acquittal under section 249-A CrPC must give reasons based on the evidence
records.text: Reasons for acquitting an accused even at an initial stage under s. 249-A CrPC must flow from analysis of the prosecution evidence and the law on the subject. Ref: Muhammad Ibrar Khan v. Mian Muhammad Ramzan etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 67 of 2020, decided 20.05.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Ibrar Khan v. Mian Muhammad Ramzan etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 67 of 2020, decided 20.05.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Breach of Agreement to Sell Not Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: Breach of an agreement to sell is not criminal breach of trust
records.text: Breach of a term of an agreement to sell, created under the Contract Act, 1872, does not meet the ingredients of criminal breach of trust under s. 406 PPC. Payment of money is not entrustment of property, and remedies lie under the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Ref: Muhammad Musawar Abbasi v. The State and another (Criminal Misc. No.787-BC of 2022, decided 20.06.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Musawar Abbasi v. The State and another (Criminal Misc. No.787-BC of 2022, decided 20.06.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: PEMRA Blanket Ban on Live Speeches
records.heading: PEMRA cannot impose a blanket ban on live speeches under section 27
records.text: PEMRA counsel could not satisfy the court that a blanket prohibition on live speech could be passed under s. 27 of the PEMRA Ordinance, 2002. The Urdu headline reports the court set aside the PEMRA order of 20.08.2022. PEMRA may proceed against licencees failing to implement the delay mechanism. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority & another (Civil Misc. Appeal No.102/2022, decided 05.09.2022); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority & another (Civil Misc. Appeal No.102/2022, decided 05.09.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Phased Acceptance of Resignations of Assembly Members
records.heading: Court cannot review the Speaker's satisfaction on phased acceptance of resignations of Assembly members
records.text: Per the Urdu report, the Islamabad High Court dismissed the petition against phased acceptance of PTI members' resignations, holding it cannot review the Speaker's satisfaction on the 11 accepted resignations or interfere in parliamentary matters. It declared the Deputy Speaker's earlier order accepting 123 resignations illegal. Ref: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf through its Secretary General Mr Asad Umar v. Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan through its Secretary National Assembly Sectt. & 126 others (W.P. No.2892/2022, decided 06.09.2022); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf through its Secretary General Mr Asad Umar v. Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan through its Secretary National Assembly Sectt. & 126 others (W.P. No.2892/2022, decided 06.09.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: PEMRA Directions on Code of Conduct and Sub Judice Matters
records.heading: PEMRA must enforce the Electronic Media Code of Conduct 2015 on sub judice discussion
records.text: The Supreme Court issued mandamus to PEMRA to enforce the Electronic Media Code of Conduct, 2015, which protects Arts. 19 and 19A while ensuring sub judice discussion does not prejudice Arts. 4 and 10A. Licensees were to receive reminders of editorial oversight obligations. The Supreme Court or High Court may act under Art. 204. Cited by the Islamabad High Court. Ref: PLD 2019 SC 1.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Mere Accompaniment and Proof of Possession
records.heading: Mere accompaniment of a co-accused does not prove possession of recovered narcotics
records.text: Where narcotics are recovered from a co-accused, mere accompaniment of the principal accused does not show active possession or knowledge. Accomplice evidence is ordinarily viewed with suspicion and needs corroboration. The prosecution must prove the accused knowingly controlled the contraband, and s. 29 CNSA 1997 was enacted for such circumstances. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1466.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIA as Police Authority under s. 22-A(6) CrPC
records.heading: The FIA is a police authority within section 22-A(6) CrPC
records.text: The FIA falls within the expression 'the police authorities' in s. 22-A(6) CrPC and is amenable to the jurisdiction of the Ex-officio Justice of Peace, including when it acts under PECA. The Justice of Peace is not obliged to direct registration of an FIR in every case, since the direction must be 'appropriate' to the circumstances. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 664.

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: PECA Complaints: Inquiry Before FIR under Rule 7
records.heading: A PECA complaint is first registered as an inquiry before any FIR
records.text: Under s. 29(2) PECA and Rule 7 of the Investigation Rules, a cybercrime complaint is first registered as an inquiry. An FIR is lodged only if a cognizable offence is found and Rule 7(4) is complied with; for non-cognizable offences court permission is sought. Registration of an FIR is not a condition precedent to investigation, and the special law prevails over ss. 154 and 155 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 664.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Petition in Absence of Petitioner
records.heading: A bail petition cannot be decided in the absence of the petitioner
records.text: If the petitioner is not present before the Court, his bail petition cannot be proceeded with and cannot be decided on merits. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1525.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Sulphuric Acid Not a Controlled Substance Specified
records.heading: Sulphuric acid is not a controlled substance under the CNS Act 1997
records.text: Sulphuric acid is not a narcotic drug under s. 2(s) and is not listed in the Schedule of psychotropic substances under s. 2(za) CNS Act 1997. Possession for industrial, medical or scientific use is excepted under s. 6, subject to licensing. The Court directed the D.G. ANF and Secretary MNC to frame a policy on its possession and use. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1492.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: S. 29 CNSA: Primary Burden on Prosecution
records.heading: Primary burden under section 29 CNSA remains on the prosecution to prove a nexus
records.text: Despite the negative wording of s. 29 CNS Act 1997, the primary onus remains on the prosecution to prove its case, including a strong nexus between the recovered substance and the accused. Only once that tie is established does s. 29 operate against the accused. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1492.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Forfeiture of Bail Bond under s. 514 CrPC
records.heading: Forfeiture of a bail bond under section 514 CrPC requires recorded grounds of proof
records.text: Before releasing a person on bail s. 499 CrPC requires a bond. Under s. 514 CrPC the court must first satisfy itself that the bond has been forfeited, then record the grounds of proof for that conclusion; for a bond for appearance it may refer to its own record showing non-appearance on the fixed date. Ref: Muhammad Rasheed v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 411 of 2022, heard 21.07.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Rasheed v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 411 of 2022, heard 21.07.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Leave to Appeal: Supreme Court Not Ordinary Appellate Court
records.heading: The Supreme Court does not act as an ordinary appellate court in granting leave
records.text: In granting leave to appeal the Supreme Court does not act as an ordinary court of appeal. Leave is justified only if an important question of law arises, or the finding of fact results from gross misreading or non-reading of material evidence or is so shocking or improbable that no reasonable person could have reached it. Ref: Ghulam Rasool v. The State (J.P. 249/2018, decided 01.09.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Ghulam Rasool v. The State (J.P. 249/2018, decided 01.09.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Common Intention: Mere Presence Insufficient
records.heading: Mere presence with the principal accused does not establish common intention
records.text: The criminal act must be done in furtherance of common intention. Mere presence of an accused with another accused who commits the crime does not establish common intention, unless there is evidence of his own criminal act committed in furtherance of that intention. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1187; Bashir Ahmed v. State.
records.title: Bashir Ahmed v. State

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Enforcement of Arbitral Award
records.heading: Authority on enforcement of an arbitral award
records.text: Authority on enforcement of an arbitration award. The post gives only the subject heading and no holding. Ref: Shahin Shah v. The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa thr. Secretary Irrigation Department, Peshawar and others (C.A. 315/2022, decided 20.06.2022); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan.
records.title: Shahin Shah v. The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa thr. Secretary Irrigation Department, Peshawar and others (C.A. 315/2022, decided 20.06.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: PEMRA Council of Complaints: Open Selection Process
records.heading: Public appointments, even honorary ones, require an open selection process
records.text: Public appointments, including to honorary positions such as membership of the PEMRA Council of Complaints, require an open selection process. Headhunting can form part of an open selection process. Ref: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority, Islamabad and another v. ARY Communications Limited, Karachi and others (C.P. 1716/2022, decided 25.07.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority, Islamabad and another v. ARY Communications Limited, Karachi and others (C.P. 1716/2022, decided 25.07.2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: S. 153(1)(c) Income Tax Ordinance: Labour and Carriage Services
records.heading: Interpretation of section 153(1)(c) Income Tax Ordinance on labour and carriage services
records.text: Interprets s. 153(1)(c) of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 with regard to the rendering of labour and carriage services. The Court also stressed the necessity of the Federal Board of Revenue maintaining a data bank of cases. Ref: Commissioner Inland Revenue, Chenab Zone, Faisalabad v. Abdul Hameed Labour Contractor C/o M/s Punjab Beverages Company Pvt Ltd Faisalabad (C.P. 6309/2021, decided 31.08.2022); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Commissioner Inland Revenue, Chenab Zone, Faisalabad v. Abdul Hameed Labour Contractor C/o M/s Punjab Beverages Company Pvt Ltd Faisalabad (C.P. 6309/2021, decided 31.08.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 27(1) of the Constitution and Its Provisos
records.heading: Interpretation of Article 27(1) of the Constitution and its three provisos
records.text: Interprets Art. 27(1) of the Constitution and the three provisos to it. The post gives only the subject and no holding. Ref: Muhammad Tayyab Bukhari v. Dr. Anees-ur-Rehman and others (C.A. 49/2022, decided 05.09.2022); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Muhammad Tayyab Bukhari v. Dr. Anees-ur-Rehman and others (C.A. 49/2022, decided 05.09.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: Meaning and Principles
records.heading: Last seen evidence alone is insufficient for conviction under section 302 PPC
records.text: Last seen together evidence rests on probability and requires cogent reasons for the deceased accompanying the accused, proximity of the crime scene, a short time gap, no possibility of third party interference, and motive. It is not by itself sufficient for conviction under s. 302 PPC without linking evidence such as recovery, and must be scrutinised with great caution. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 813; Muhammad Abid v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Abid v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Last Seen Witnesses: Acquittal
records.heading: Delayed last seen witnesses who were chance witnesses were unreliable and the accused was acquitted
records.text: Last seen witnesses related to the complainant, who stayed silent for over a week and gave an unsupported explanation for the delay, were unreliable and were also chance witnesses. The Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court acquitted the accused of all charges and set aside the conviction and sentences. Ref: 2015 SCMR 155; Imran alias Dully v. The State.
records.title: Imran alias Dully v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Unbroken Chain Required
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form an unbroken chain from the body to the accused
records.text: Where a case rests entirely on circumstantial evidence, each piece must form one unbroken chain from the dead body to the neck of the accused. A missing link breaks the chain, and conviction cannot safely be recorded, especially on a capital charge. Courts must exercise great caution. Ref: 2015 SCMR 155; Imran alias Dully v. The State.
records.title: Imran alias Dully v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: Fundamental Principles
records.heading: Last seen evidence requires cogent reasons, proximity, close timing and motive for conviction
records.text: A conviction based on last seen evidence requires the prosecution to show cogent reasons for the deceased accompanying the accused, proximity of the crime scene, close timing between sighting and murder, a reason for the journey together, and motive. Recovery of the weapon and expert opinion must be transparent. The court must also consider any contributory role of the deceased if the murder was not planned. Ref: 2017 SCMR 2026.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Unbroken Chain and Scrutiny
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence needs an unbroken chain and deep scrutiny because fabrication is not uncommon
records.text: Reliance on circumstantial evidence requires an unbroken chain of links from the dead body to the accused, proof beyond reasonable doubt, and deep scrutiny because fabrication is not uncommon. Where evidence falls short of that standard it is better to discard it so that an innocent person is not sent to the gallows. Ref: 2017 SCMR 2026.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: Further Linking Evidence Required
records.heading: Last seen with the accused is not sufficient without incriminating recoveries
records.text: That the deceased was last seen with the accused is not by itself sufficient to sustain a murder charge, and further evidence such as incriminating recoveries is needed. Circumstantial evidence must be incompatible with innocence and accepted with great caution. If last seen shortly before death near the scene, an inference of responsibility can easily be drawn. Ref: PLD 2003 SC 704.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Standard of Care
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must be narrowly examined before an adverse inference is drawn
records.text: Circumstantial evidence must always be narrowly examined, and the circumstances ascertained with minute care before an adverse inference is drawn. A mere concurrence of circumstances supported by defective evidence can create a specious appearance. The court must be watchful against the investigating officer's design and satisfy itself that the evidence was fairly and genuinely collected. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 600.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Sufficiency for Conviction
records.heading: Conviction is possible only if no hypothesis consistent with innocence can be suggested
records.text: If no hypothesis consistent with innocence can be suggested on the proved circumstances, conviction is possible. If they can be reconciled with any reasonable hypothesis of innocence, the case is one of insufficient evidence and ends in acquittal. The chain must be unbroken, and a missing link makes conviction unsafe, especially on a capital charge. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 600.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence in Capital Cases: Unbroken Chain
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence in capital cases must form a single unbroken chain
records.text: In capital cases circumstantial evidence must form a single unbroken chain from the dead body to the neck of the accused, and a missing link renders it unreliable for conviction. Courts must take extra care because evidence can be fabricated, and must guard against deliberate design by the investigating agency. Failure to do so is a failure of justice. Ref: 2017 SCMR 986.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Reliance and Scope
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence founds conviction only if incompatible with innocence
records.text: Guilt can be deduced from circumstances, but where they are tampered with or contrived they cannot be accepted without careful and critical analysis. Circumstantial evidence can found a conviction only if it is incompatible with innocence and incapable of explanation on any other reasonable hypothesis than guilt. Ref: 2016 SCMR 1144.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence in Capital Crimes: Missing Link
records.heading: A missing link in circumstantial evidence bars conviction in crimes entailing capital punishment
records.text: Pieces of circumstantial evidence must make an unbroken chain from the dead body to the neck of the accused, and any missing link bars conviction in crimes entailing capital punishment. Courts must take extraordinary care, and where the evidence lacks the required quality the safe course is not to rely on it. Ref: 2016 SCMR 274.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower Suit against Father-in-Law as Wakeel
records.heading: A father-in-law who signed as Wakeel of bridegroom is liable in a dower suit
records.text: A suit for recovery of dower is competent against the father-in-law who signed the Nikahnama as 'Wakeel of bridegroom' in the prescribed column, and he cannot escape liability on that footing. The decree for deferred dower and dismissal of appeal were upheld, no illegality being shown. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 137.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Sample of a Free Woman and Art. 128 QSO
records.heading: A free woman cannot be compelled to give a DNA sample under Article 14
records.text: Under Art. 128 QSO only a putative father, within the time prescribed, may challenge the paternity of a child. A free woman cannot be compelled to give a DNA sample, as forcible taking would violate her liberty, dignity and privacy under Art. 14 of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2019 SC 449.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Legitimacy of Child Born in Marriage
records.heading: A child born in a valid marriage is conclusively legitimate
records.text: A child born during a valid marriage, or within two years of its dissolution with the mother remaining unmarried, is conclusively legitimate. The husband never disowned the child in his lifetime, and a dubious late birth entry did not displace the presumption. Revision was dismissed. Ref: 2018 CLC Note 18.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Legitimacy of Child and Principle of Farash
records.heading: A child born during marriage follows the bed and legitimacy cannot be questioned
records.text: A child born during the subsistence of marriage follows the bed, and its legitimacy could not be questioned where the wife remained with the husband. The Family Court rightly held that the presumption of legitimacy applied, and the husband's refusal to offer a DNA test raised doubt about his claim. Ref: 2017 MLD 1228.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Paternity of Minor: Only Civil Court Can Decide
records.heading: Only a civil court can decide the paternity of a minor
records.text: Neither the Family Court nor the appellate court is a court of civil jurisdiction, so the question of a minor's paternity cannot be determined by them. The appellate court exceeded its jurisdiction in remanding a maintenance suit to determine paternity, which only a civil court can adjudicate. Ref: PLD 2016 Lahore 536.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Denial of Paternity: Time Limit under Muslim Personal Law
records.heading: Paternity must be denied immediately after birth or within the post natal period
records.text: Under Muslim Personal Law paternity must be denied immediately after birth, or within the post natal period of at most 40 days according to Imam Muhammad and Imam Yousaf. No lawful denial can be made afterwards. Art. 128 QSO read with s. 2 of the West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1962 secures unchallengeable legitimacy despite scientific evidence. Ref: PLD 2015 SC 327.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Legitimacy: Conclusive Proof from Birth in Marriage
records.heading: Birth during marriage or within two years of dissolution is conclusive proof of legitimacy
records.text: A child born during a valid marriage, not earlier than six lunar months from the marriage or within two years after its dissolution, is conclusive proof of legitimacy, provided the mother remained unmarried. Ref: 2008 SCMR 1707.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Legitimacy: Presumption in Favour of Child
records.heading: Disowning a child born in wedlock needs tangible proof because every presumption favours legitimacy
records.text: Legitimacy is a vital issue and must not be decided in a cavalier manner. Disowning a child born in wedlock must be substantiated by tangible proof and credible evidence, and mere denial cannot remove legitimacy since the child follows the bed. Every presumption favours legitimacy. Ref: PLD 2008 Lahore 302.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test to Disprove Legitimacy Not Proper
records.heading: A DNA test to disprove legitimacy was not a proper direction
records.text: In view of the practice of denying legitimacy to avoid maintenance or exclude a child from inheritance, a direction for a DNA test was not proper. The Court noted lack of skills and facilities in Pakistan, the stigma of any error on the child, and that error in results cannot be ruled out. Ref: PLD 2010 Lahore 422.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Challan under s. 512 CrPC: Legal Status
records.heading: Practice of mentioning challan under section 512 CrPC was directed to be discontinued
records.text: Authority on the legal status of a challan described as under s. 512 CrPC. The Special Court has no power under s. 19 of the Act to constitute a JIT or direct the Government to do so, and the practice of mentioning 'Challan under Section 512 Cr.PC' was directed to be discontinued, with copies sent to all judicial officers in Punjab. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 268.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Death of Wife in Accused's House: Onus
records.heading: A husband bears part of the onus for his wife's unnatural death at home
records.text: Where a wife or vulnerable dependent dies an unnatural death in the accused's house, part of the onus lies on him to explain the circumstances. If the prosecution case is demolished or wholly unbelievable, the accused cannot be convicted merely for failing to explain, and the entire burden cannot be shifted to him. Ref: 2019 SCMR 1451, PLD 2019 SC 592, 2018 SCMR 787, PLD 2017 SC 681 and others.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Inquiry Before FIR by Anti-Corruption Establishment
records.heading: Anti-Corruption Establishment must hold an inquiry before an FIR is lodged
records.text: The Anti-Corruption Establishment is to hold an inquiry before an FIR is lodged. The Sessions Judge's order directing registration of the FIR without formal and independent inquiry was without jurisdiction and was set aside, and the Establishment was to proceed under the Anti-Corruption Establishment Rules 2014 after hearing the accused. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 197.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Stamp Vendor as Public Servant
records.heading: A stamp vendor appointed by the District Collector is a public servant
records.text: A stamp vendor appointed by the District Collector, who obtains stamps from the government treasury and receives commission from public revenue, serves the government in a public duty and is a 'public servant' under s. 21, clause ninth PPC and s. 2 of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947. Ref: 2012 PCrLJ 255.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Registration of Case against Public Servant: R. 8 Punjab ACE Rules
records.heading: Registration against a public servant requires prior inquiry and orders under Rule 8
records.text: Where a public servant is alleged to have committed a scheduled offence jointly with private persons, a case can be registered only on the orders of the officers named in R. 8 of the Punjab Anti-Corruption Establishment Rules 1985, after a thorough prior inquiry. The inquiry protects public servants from false and frivolous cases. Ref: 2016 PCrLJ 1216.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Deaf and Dumb Witness: Competency under Art. 3 QSO
records.heading: A deaf and dumb witness is competent unless he cannot understand or answer rationally
records.text: Although no provision matches s. 119 of the Indian Evidence Act, the evidence of a deaf and dumb witness can be recorded by necessary implication of Arts. 3 and 59 QSO read with s. 543 CrPC. A witness is incompetent only if the court definitely concludes that he can neither understand questions nor give rational answers, and the record showed no such satisfaction. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 1086.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Deaf and Dumb Witness: Interpreter and Oath
records.heading: Failure to assess comprehension or administer oath to a deaf witness vitiated the conviction
records.text: The trial court did not assess the witness's comprehension, did not show the interpreter was versed in the witness's signs, did not clarify whether the interpreter acted under s. 543 CrPC or as an expert under Art. 59 QSO, and did not administer an oath. Because of these violations the conviction and sentence were set aside. Ref: 2019 SCMR 64.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Discharge of Accused before Framing of Charge: s. 265-D
records.heading: Framing of charge is not automatic and the court may discharge under section 265-D CrPC
records.text: Framing of charge is not automatic, and the Trial Court need not merely endorse the police version. If the record is insufficient the court may discharge the accused under s. 265-D CrPC. Here the accused lady was discharged because the complainant disclosed no source for her alleged involvement, and the petition against discharge was dismissed. Ref: 2021 MLD 1532.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Safe Custody in Narcotics Cases
records.heading: Chain of safe custody must be established in narcotics cases
records.text: Acquittal in a s. 9(c) CNS Act case where recovery of heroin was made but the chain of safe custody was not established by the prosecution. Cases carrying harder sentences need credible evidence and a transparent process, and a single circumstance creating reasonable doubt suffices. The judgment provides guidelines for maintaining the chain of safe custody. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 492; Nadeem Akhtar v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 94 of 2017, heard 13.10.2021); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa; Justice Muhammad Shan Gul.
records.title: Nadeem Akhtar v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 94 of 2017, heard 13.10.2021)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Trial in Absentia
records.heading: Section 19(10)(b) ATA on trial in absentia was declared ultra vires Article 10
records.text: Discusses trial in absentia as an exception to the audi alteram partem principle, with reference to Art. 14(3)(d) ICCPR and national law. Section 19(10)(b) of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997 (since deleted) was declared ultra vires Art. 10 of the Constitution, while the rest of s. 19 was held intra vires. Ref: Muhammad Umair v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 364/2022, heard 26.05.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Umair v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 364/2022, heard 26.05.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Appeal by Father: Maintenance Below Rs. 5000 per Child
records.heading: Appealability of maintenance below Rs. 5000 per child referred for larger bench
records.text: The question whether a father may appeal a family decree where each minor's maintenance is below Rs. 5000 per month but the aggregate exceeds Rs. 5000 was referred to the Chief Justice to consider a Larger Bench because of conflicting judgments. Ref: 2020 (M) CLR 673.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeal under s. 13 Gas (Theft Control and Recovery) Act 2016
records.heading: Section 13(3) Gas Act 2016 requires a reasoned order for admission of an appeal
records.text: Section 13(3) of the Gas (Theft Control and Recovery) Act 2016 requires a reasoned order for admission of an appeal in part or whole. Where no reason or ground for admission is given, the appeal is dismissed in limine. Ref: 2022 LHC 6389; Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited etc. v. Farman Ali (Deceased) through LRs etc. (R.F.A. 51934/22, decided 07.09.2022); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited etc. v. Farman Ali (Deceased) through LRs etc. (R.F.A. 51934/22, decided 07.09.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inordinate Delay in Post-Mortem
records.heading: Inordinate delay in post-mortem suggests concocting of the prosecution story
records.text: A delay of 12 to 24 hours between death and post-mortem indicated that time was consumed in manoeuvring and concocting the prosecution story and managing eyewitnesses. The prosecution failed to prove its case under ss. 302 and 34 PPC, and the appeal was allowed with acquittal. Ref: 2022 MLD 1603.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements and Defence Plea of Accidental Fire
records.heading: Dishonest improvements by an eyewitness made his evidence unsafe to rely upon
records.text: An eyewitness who made dishonest material improvements, confronted in cross-examination, could not be safely relied upon. The accused's plea that the shot fired accidentally in a scuffle was corroborated by medical and investigating officer evidence, with no premeditation or motive. The prosecution failed to prove its case and the accused was acquitted. Ref: 2022 MLD 1603.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Dying Declaration: Art. 46 QSO
records.heading: A dying declaration inconsistent with the FIR and left with blank space is doubtful
records.text: The dying declaration was inconsistent with the FIR version, as it named only the accused and did not mention the eyewitnesses. It also appeared doubtful because a blank space was left after it, with an incomplete thumb impression suggesting it was taken on blank paper. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2022 MLD 1577.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay of Sixteen Hours in FIR
records.heading: Unexplained delay of sixteen hours in lodging the FIR is fatal
records.text: The occurrence took place at about Maghrib time and the police were informed after about sixteen hours with no explanation in the FIR. Such unexplained delay in lodging the FIR was fatal to the prosecution case. Ref: 2022 MLD 1577.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII R. 2 CPC: Summary Suit against Legal Heirs on Cheque
records.heading: Legal heirs of a cheque executant cannot be sued in a summary suit
records.text: Legal heirs of the executant who are not makers, drawers, endorsers or acceptors of the cheque cannot be sued in a summary suit under O. XXXVII R. 2 CPC, so the suit was not maintainable. Only the person who signed or thumb-marked the cheque is liable. The writ petition was accepted and the plaint directed to be returned.
