Ref: 2022 MLD 1555, 2022 CLD 900; Bushra Bibi and others v. Additional District Judge and others (WP No. 22594 of 2019).
records.title: Bushra Bibi and others v. Additional District Judge and others (WP No. 22594 of 2019)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Estoppel under Art. 114 QSO: Non-Deposit of Consideration
records.heading: Estoppel under Article 114 QSO prevents a litigant from taking inconsistent pleas
records.text: Estoppel under Art. 114 QSO is an equitable rule that prevents a litigant from taking inconsistent pleas and blowing hot and cold. The plaintiff, who had expressed willingness to pay the enhanced consideration, could not retract, and the cross-objection was dismissed with the defendant's appeal deemed accepted. Ref: 2022 CLC 1461.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Juvenility: Burden of Proving Age on Accused
records.heading: The accused must prove his claimed age by positive evidence to claim juvenility
records.text: It is for the accused to prove his claimed age through positive evidence, otherwise he cannot claim the benefit of juvenile legislation. The claim is an assertion of fact, and the burden lies heavily on the person asserting it. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1662.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Concurrent Departmental and Criminal Proceedings
records.heading: Departmental and criminal proceedings may run concurrently because standards of proof differ
records.text: Departmental and criminal proceedings can run concurrently, as they involve different standards of proof. Acquittal on benefit of doubt does not bar disciplinary action, and a police official found guilty after inquiry of a heinous crime was rightly dismissed. A disciplined force requires persons with spotless character and clean antecedents. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1770, 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1445; Faraz Naveed v. District Police Officer Gujrat and another.
records.title: Faraz Naveed v. District Police Officer Gujrat and another

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Contract Employees: No Right to Regularisation
records.heading: Contract employees have no vested right to regularisation without statutory backing
records.text: Contract employees in a master and servant relationship have no vested right to regularisation without statutory backing. The petitioner, found over age in the fresh recruitment, never sought age relaxation under the Rules. Regularisation cannot be directed unless the employee was appointed under the rules against a regular sanctioned vacant post. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1680.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Deciding Suit on Failure to Produce Evidence
records.heading: O. XVII R. 3 CPC does not permit dismissal without examining the record
records.text: The expression 'to decide the suit forthwith' in O. XVII R. 3 CPC does not mean decide or dismiss there and then. The court may examine the record, and can ask the failing party to record its statement and then proceed. The Trial Court's dismissal without touching the merits was set aside and the case remanded for decision within three months. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1793.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotic Samples
records.heading: Any break in the chain of custody of narcotic samples makes the analyst's report unreliable
records.text: Representative samples must be kept in safe custody and safely transmitted from recovery to the Government analyst. Any break in the chain makes the analyst's report unreliable and incapable of sustaining conviction. The conviction of the petitioner was set aside and he was acquitted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1641.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Binding Effect of Earlier Supreme Court Bench Decisions
records.heading: An earlier Bench judgment binds smaller and equal Benches of the Supreme Court
records.text: An earlier Bench judgment of the Supreme Court binds smaller Benches and Benches of equal strength. A co-equal Bench that wishes to take a contrary view must request the Chief Justice to constitute a larger Bench. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1641.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Rule 22(1) ATIR Rules Ultra Vires s. 132(2)
records.heading: Part of Rule 22(1) ATIR Rules 2010 was struck down as ultra vires
records.text: A portion of Rule 22(1) of the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue Rules 2010 was struck down as ultra vires s. 132(2) of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1787.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Registrar's Powers on Maintainability of Petition
records.heading: The Registrar has no power to decide maintainability of a petition
records.text: The Registrar under the Supreme Court Rules 1980 has no power to decide maintainability of a petition. An appeal under O. V R. 3 against refusal to register an Art. 184(3) petition was partly allowed, and the appellant was to meet the Registrar's objections within two weeks, after which the petition would be registered and fixed before a Bench. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 675.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Courts Decide on Established Facts
records.heading: Courts decide disputes on established facts, free of surmise or conjecture
records.text: Courts decide disputes on the strength of established facts and not on surmises or conjectures. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 574.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Deputy Speaker's Ruling under Art. 5(1): Suo Motu Case
records.heading: Deputy Speaker's ruling under Article 5(1) examined in the suo motu case
records.text: Detailed judgment in the suo motu case on the ruling issued by the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly under Art. 5(1) of the Constitution at the time of the no-confidence motion against the former Prime Minister. The post also refers to an additional note by Justice Mazhar Alam Miankhel. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 574; Justice Mazhar Alam Miankhel.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Columns 13 and 16: Intention of Parties
records.heading: Nikahnama entries are read by the parties' intention and not the column headings
records.text: Entries in columns 13 and 16 of the Nikahnama are interpreted by the intention of the parties and not the column headings, especially where the value or items of dower are disputed. The Nikahnama is a contract to be construed like others, and the wife's claim to the agricultural land in column 16 was upheld. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 686.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cross-Version and Further Inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC
records.heading: A cross-version alone does not justify further inquiry under section 497(2) CrPC
records.text: Mere existence of a cross-version is not a ground for further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC unless the record supports it and, on tentative assessment, the court finds it prima facie true or cannot tell which party was the aggressor. The bail granting order was set aside, the bail petition dismissed and the accused directed to surrender. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 694.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Pre-Arrest Bail after Dismissal for Non-Appearance
records.heading: A second pre-arrest bail petition after dismissal for non-appearance needs a satisfactory explanation
records.text: If a pre-arrest bail petition is dismissed for non-appearance under s. 498-A CrPC, a second petition is maintainable only if the petitioner gives a satisfactory explanation for his absence. If the explanation is unsatisfactory, the second petition is not maintainable and is dismissed without examining merits. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 894.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Pre-Arrest Bail after Withdrawal of First
records.heading: Withdrawing a pre-arrest bail petition to file another without explanation is an abuse of process
records.text: Withdrawing a pre-arrest bail petition after enjoying ad interim bail, to file another and obtain the same benefit without lawful explanation, is an abuse of process. A successive petition is not maintainable unless the accused gives a satisfactory explanation for the withdrawal and the fresh filing. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 892.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Personal Presence of Accused under s. 498-A
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail cannot be granted under section 498-A CrPC to an absent accused
records.text: Under s. 498-A CrPC the court cannot grant pre-arrest bail to an accused who is not personally present, and the petition is to be dismissed. If a satisfactory explanation is given, the court may exempt presence for that day and adjourn briefly, but cannot examine the merits in his absence. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 886.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Sedition Case: Absence of Solid Material
records.heading: Bail should not be denied in a sedition case without solid material
records.text: The Islamabad High Court granted bail in a case of incitement to sedition against Shahbaz Gill on bail bonds of Rs. 500,000. The Chief Justice remarked that bail should not be denied without solid material, and the trial court remains competent to pass orders to ensure attendance at trial. Ref: Muhammad Shahbaz Shabbir Gill v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 1104-B/2022, decided 15.09.2022); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Muhammad Shahbaz Shabbir Gill v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 1104-B/2022, decided 15.09.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation against Co-Sharers in Inheritance Claims
records.heading: No limitation runs against a co-sharer, but lifetime transfers by the propositus are different
records.text: No limitation runs against a co-sharer, and a mutation creates no title, so a heir may seek declaration under s. 42 Specific Relief Act. Limitation cannot be ignored where the propositus transferred property by sale or gift in his lifetime and heirs challenge it after considerable delay. The Court distinguished earlier limitation cases on that basis. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1647.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance Opens on Death: Heirs Become Co-Sharers
records.heading: Heirs become co-sharers from the date of death and each is presumed in possession of the whole
records.text: Under Muslim Personal Law inheritance opens just after death, and all entitled heirs become owners and co-sharers to the extent of their shares from the date of death. Section 3 of Act IX of 1948 gives implied retrospective effect, and each co-sharer is presumed in possession of every inch of the joint property until partition. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1647.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of Proceedings: Art. 199 and s. 249-A CrPC
records.heading: Quashing under Article 199 is unusual where sections 249-A and 265-K CrPC provide a remedy
records.text: The High Court's Art. 199 jurisdiction is extraordinary, and ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC ordinarily provide an adequate remedy, so quashing under Art. 199 or s. 561-A CrPC is not usual. The bar is not absolute, and the Court may intervene in exceptional cases, such as where interpretation of Art. 19 and the FIA's jurisdiction are in issue. Ref: Usman Zulfiqar Khan v. The State etc. (Writ Petition No. 19711/2022).
records.title: Usman Zulfiqar Khan v. The State etc. (Writ Petition No. 19711/2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sudden Provocation: Outraging Religious Feelings
records.heading: Deliberate insult to a class's religion can extend the scope of sudden provocation
records.text: A deliberate and malicious act intended to outrage the religious feelings of a class of people by insulting its religion or religious rituals, through derogatory remarks, extends the scope of cases falling within sudden provocation under ss. 302(b) and 302(c) PPC. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 136; Bashir Ahmed and others v. State etc. (Crl. P. Nos. 1371 & 1651-L of 2016 and Crl. Misc. Appln. No. 1704 of 2017, decided 26.11.2020); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Bashir Ahmed and others v. State etc. (Crl. P. Nos. 1371 & 1651-L of 2016 and Crl. Misc. Appln. No. 1704 of 2017, decided 26.11.2020)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Civil Court Review of Revenue Authority Orders
records.heading: Civil courts may use summary procedure to review the legality of revenue authority orders
records.text: Describes the summary procedure for suits in which the legality of orders of administrative authorities such as revenue authorities is challenged within the limited jurisdiction of Civil Courts. The statements of the parties and the record are ordinarily sufficient evidence. The respondents objected to jurisdiction under s. 36 of the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act 1912. Ref: Nausher v. Province of Punjab etc. (C.A. 1011/2016, decided 18.08.2022); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Nausher v. Province of Punjab etc. (C.A. 1011/2016, decided 18.08.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 4 MFLO: Inheritance of Predeceased Son's Children
records.heading: Section 4 MFLO benefit to widows of predeceased children and exemplary costs against delay
records.text: Concerned whether widows of predeceased children can benefit from s. 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961. Only a preliminary decree had been passed, so the suit remained pending. The Court held that appellants sought to protract litigation and that exemplary costs should be imposed on parties who deprive heirs of their inheritance. Ref: PLJ 2022 Islamabad 143.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 203-D(2)(b): Effect of Federal Shariat Court Decision
records.heading: A Federal Shariat Court decision does not take effect while an appeal is pending in the Supreme Court
records.text: A decision of the Federal Shariat Court declaring a law or provision repugnant to Islamic injunctions does not take effect before disposal of an appeal against it preferred before the Supreme Court. Ref: PLJ 2022 Islamabad 143.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dissolution of Marriage and Repayment of Haq Mehr
records.heading: A wife who obtains dissolution for cruelty cannot be made to return haq mehr
records.text: Under s. 10(4) Family Courts Act a decree for dissolution is contingent on repayment of haq mehr. Where the wife obtains dissolution on the ground of cruelty, she cannot be burdened with returning dower. Under s. 14(2) the only appealable part is the finding determining civil liabilities for haq mehr upon dissolution. Ref: PLJ 2022 Islamabad 129.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Interim Injunction in Specific Performance Suit: Three Essentials
records.heading: Interim relief should follow the three essentials and the trial court must consider the respondents' documents
records.text: The trial court refused interim relief without considering the respondents' averments and documents, while the three essentials for interim relief favoured the respondents. The High Court may convert a civil revision into a writ petition on payment of court fee. The appellate order was modified to allow petitioners to sell 50% of plots, and the petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 791.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Blocking CNIC to Compel Appearance in Execution
records.heading: A CNIC cannot be blocked to compel appearance in execution or surrender in a criminal case
records.text: Section 18 of the NADRA Ordinance 2000 does not allow blocking a person's CNIC to compel him to appear before an executing court or to surrender in a criminal case. A CNIC is essential to fundamental rights and cannot be withdrawn without due process, and under s. 18(1) it may be cancelled or impounded only after a show cause notice. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 803.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Customs Reference: Scope of High Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: In customs reference jurisdiction the High Court decides only questions of law
records.text: In reference jurisdiction under the Customs Act 1969 the High Court confines itself to questions of law and does not decide factual controversies. It interferes with the Appellate Tribunal only for an illegality or jurisdictional defect going to the root, and may decline to answer a question that would be merely academic. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 810.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor: Concurrent Findings Not Disturbed
records.heading: Concurrent findings fixing a minor's maintenance are not disturbed in constitutional jurisdiction
records.text: Concurrent findings fixing maintenance after considering the minor's needs and the father's financial status were not disturbed in constitutional jurisdiction, and the delivery expenses claim was rightly dismissed. The petitioners may apply to the trial court to increase maintenance. Under s. 5 Family Courts Act the Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction over scheduled matters. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 815.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Illegal Water Hydrants and Water Shortage
records.heading: A writ against illegal water hydrants is disposed of once action is initiated against the respondents
records.text: Writ concerning an illegal business of water hydrants run without permission, with no effective mechanism to restrict them, under the Development of Cities Act 1976. The Court noted the seriousness of water shortage, and as action had been initiated against the private respondents the grievance was redressed. Copies were sent to officials for compliance. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 819.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Presumption of Consideration under s. 118 NIA
records.heading: A proved negotiable instrument raises a presumption of consideration until the contrary is proved
records.text: Once a negotiable instrument is brought on record and its execution proved, a presumption of valid consideration arises under s. 118 Negotiable Instruments Act 1881, and it remains until the party disputing consideration proves the contrary. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 831.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Promissory Note: No Attestation Required, Art. 79 QSO
records.heading: A promissory note needs no attestation or witnesses to prove its execution
records.text: A promissory note needs no attestation and no witnesses to prove its execution, since Art. 79 QSO applies only to documents required by law to be attested. It need only be signed by the maker. The petitioner failed to rebut the presumption under s. 118(a) NIA, and the decree was upheld. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lahore 831.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Business Partnership Dispute
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is confirmed in a civil partnership dispute where entrustment is missing
records.text: Where the dispute between business partners was civil, a suit for accounts had been filed, and the element of entrustment under s. 405 PPC was missing, pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC was confirmed. The proper course for an aggrieved partner was to sue for accounts, and s. 406 PPC is not attracted to partnership property. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1314.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Breach of Trust: Essential Ingredients
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation, not mere breach of trust
records.text: The ingredients of criminal breach of trust under s. 406 PPC are entrustment of property or dominion and dishonest misappropriation or conversion to own use. Breach of trust simpliciter is a civil wrong, and criminal liability arises when it is associated with dishonesty. Even temporary misappropriation may attract s. 405 PPC. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1314.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Identification Parade and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: An identification parade is necessary where unknown accused are identified on a dark night
records.text: In a dark night rape case where the accused were not previously known to the witnesses, an identification parade was necessary. The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, and a single circumstance creating doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right. Ocular account found unsynchronised with medical account (Ss. 376, 452, 384 PPC). Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1321.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Disbelieved Witnesses and Co-Accused
records.heading: Witnesses disbelieved against one co-accused need independent corroboration against the others
records.text: Where prosecution witnesses are disbelieved regarding one co-accused, they cannot be relied upon against other co-accused unless supported by independent and unimpeachable corroboration. Such corroboration was not available in the case. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1321.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Fair Trial and Defence Evidence
records.heading: Fair trial under Article 10-A includes a fair opportunity to produce defence evidence
records.text: In a case under Ss. 302/324/337-F(iii)/34 PPC, the Court dealt with summoning of Rescue 15 record with its custodian under s. 540 CrPC. It stressed that fair trial under Art. 10-A includes a fair and adequate opportunity to the accused, and directed the trial Court to allow the petitioner to produce defence evidence. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1328.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Collection and Transmission of Firearms to FSL
records.heading: Firearms must be collected, preserved and transmitted to the laboratory in a provable chain
records.text: Drawing on case law, the judgment lists the steps for collecting, preserving and transporting firearms and tool marks. The recovery must be recorded in s. 161 CrPC statements, kept in the Malkhana with entry, the Malkhana in-charge examined, and safe transmission to the Forensic Science Laboratory proved through police evidence. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1365.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Broken Teeth: Itlaf-i-Udw under S. 334 PPC
records.heading: Broken teeth are not a fracture and amount to itlaf-i-udw under section 334 PPC
records.text: Teeth are not bone, so breaking them is not a fracture under s. 337-A(iii) PPC. It is itlaf-i-udw under s. 334 read with s. 337-U PPC, and arsh for one tooth is one-twentieth of the diyat. The conviction was maintained with the sentence altered accordingly. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1385.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Proof Beyond Reasonable Doubt and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Guilt must be proved beyond reasonable doubt and a single infirmity gives the benefit of doubt
records.text: A criminal judgment must state the points for determination, the decision and the reasons. Guilt must be proved beyond reasonable doubt and not by probabilities, the prosecution case must be shown to be true and not merely possibly true, and a single infirmity entitles the accused to the benefit of doubt. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1394.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 365-A PPC Not Attracted in Rape Case
records.heading: Section 365-A PPC is not attracted where abduction was for sexual intercourse and not extortion
records.text: Section 365-A PPC requires kidnapping or abduction for extortion or for a demand to secure release of the abductee. Those elements were absent in the FIR, and the words any other demand cannot be extended to compelling a woman to sexual intercourse, which is dealt with by ss. 365-B and 376 PPC. Revision allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Cr.C. 1411.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Substitution of Accused Is Rare
records.heading: Substitution of an innocent person for the real culprit is a rare occurrence
records.text: Substitution of an innocent person for the real culprit is a rare phenomenon, because even interested witnesses would not normally let the real culprits of the murder of their relatives go free by involving innocent persons. Ref: PLJ 2022 Cr.C. 1418.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C CrPC: Supply of Copies to Accused
records.heading: Failure to supply copies under section 265-C and a defective section 342 examination vitiate conviction
records.text: Section 265-C CrPC is to be construed liberally, and copies of all oral and documentary evidence must be supplied to the accused, even where he conceded the omission. Examination under s. 342 CrPC is a mandatory duty and not a formality. Denial of these rights breached fair trial, and the conviction could not be sustained. Ref: PLJ 2022 Cr.C. 1443.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Further Inquiry in Rape Case
records.heading: Absence of violence marks and divergent statements make a rape case one of further inquiry
records.text: Medical evidence showing no mark of violence and divergent statements of the alleged victim made the case one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC (Ss. 376, 496-A, 420, 468, 471 PPC). The petitioner was no longer required for investigation and bail cannot be withheld as punishment. The factum of Nikah is to be determined by the Family Court. Ref: PLJ 2022 Cr.C. 1455.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Belated Challenge to Inheritance Mutation
records.heading: A belated challenge to an inheritance mutation after third party rights arise faces limitation
records.text: A distinction exists between an heir whose share was omitted and who sues promptly, and one who acquiesces in long-standing mutation entries and sues only after third party rights are created. Other heirs with the same interest should have been impleaded. Article 120 of the Limitation Act prescribes six years from knowledge (Ss. 39 and 42 Specific Relief Act). Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 308.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 2 CPC: Limitation in Fresh Suit
records.heading: A fresh suit under Order XXIII Rule 2 CPC remains bound by limitation
records.text: In a fresh suit instituted with permission granted under the preceding rule of O. XXIII R. 2 CPC, the plaintiff remains bound by the law of limitation as if the first suit had not been instituted. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 308.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Double Transfer Punishment Without Inquiry
records.heading: Two punishments for one alleged offence without inquiry or hearing are contrary to the Constabulary Rules
records.text: Two punishments of transfer and loss of seniority were imposed for the same alleged offence without show-cause notice, inquiry or personal hearing, contrary to R. 17 of the NWFP Constabulary Rules, 1958. No decision affecting a person's rights may be taken without hearing him. Appeal disposed of. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 332.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 10-A: Right to Fair Trial
records.heading: The right to a fair trial under Article 10-A is fundamental and justice is not defeated by technicalities
records.text: Under Art. 10-A the right to a fair trial is a fundamental right, and the Court must examine in each case whether it was afforded. The expression complete justice is wide and means that justice is not to be distorted by mere technicalities. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 332.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Registrar's Powers: Objections to Art. 184(3) Petition
records.heading: The Registrar cannot decide maintainability or merits of an Article 184(3) petition
records.text: Under O. V R. 3 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980, the Registrar performs administrative and ministerial functions and cannot decide maintainability or merits of an Art. 184(3) petition. Objections touching those questions were overruled for judicial determination by the Court, while two administrative objections were sustained. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 339.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift: Acceptance and Burden of Proof on Donees
records.heading: Donees bear the burden of proving a gift, including acceptance and delivery of possession
records.text: The burden of proving a gift and its validity lies on the donees as beneficiaries, and evidence cannot go beyond what they pleaded. They failed to prove acceptance, so the gift deed and mutation could not be sustained, and the minor granddaughter inherited her share under s. 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. A valid gift requires declaration, acceptance and delivery of possession. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 357.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal: Delayed s. 161 Statements and FSL Mismatch
records.heading: Delayed section 161 statements and a forensic mismatch support acquittal on benefit of doubt
records.text: In a s. 302(b) PPC case, delay in recording s. 161 CrPC statements reduced their value, witnesses resiled, and the pistol did not match the empties. Abscondence was not put to the accused under s. 342 CrPC. A single circumstance creating doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right. Appellant acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 161.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Delay Attributable to Accused
records.heading: Bail is refused where trial delay is mostly attributable to the accused's own applications
records.text: Bail was dismissed where the applicant was specifically nominated for a firearm injury, the trial delay was mostly attributable to his own applications, and prosecution evidence was almost complete. Bail cannot be claimed as of right under s. 497 CrPC even where delay is not attributable to the accused. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 167.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed: Co-Accused on Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is confirmed where co-accused has unchallenged post-arrest bail and no forensic test exists
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was confirmed under s. 498 CrPC where no forensic test of the alleged forged signature had been conducted and the co-accused had been granted unchallenged post-arrest bail. Pre-arrest and post-arrest bail rest on different footings, and after arrest the petitioner would be entitled to consideration for post-arrest bail. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 170.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed: Co-Accused on Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is confirmed where the co-accused has already been granted post-arrest bail
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was confirmed under s. 498 CrPC because the co-accused had been granted post-arrest bail, and after arrest the petitioner would in any case become entitled to consideration for post-arrest bail. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 170.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ss. 302(b) and 302(c) PPC: Definite Finding Required
records.heading: A definite finding on common intention or individual liability is required to apply section 302(b) or (c) PPC
records.text: In murder cases under s. 302 PPC the trial Court must evaluate whether the act was committed in furtherance of common intention or by individual liability, and give a definite finding to apply s. 302(b) or 302(c) PPC. The case was remanded for re-writing of the judgment. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 173.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail Refused: Proscribed Religious Material
records.heading: Post-arrest bail is refused where forensic analysis and group activity support the allegation of banned material
records.text: Post-arrest bail was dismissed in a case under Ss. 295-A, 295-B, 295-C, 298-C PPC and s. 11 PECA, where forensic analysis of phones, recoveries and the petitioners' role in a WhatsApp group of banned material were relied upon. Petitions dismissed as without merit. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 191.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Safe Transmission of Samples
records.heading: Safe custody and safe transmission of samples must be proved through the Moharrar and constable
records.text: In a s. 9(c) CNSA case the prosecution failed to prove safe custody because the Moharrar was not produced, and safe transmission because the transmitting constable was not produced. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 201.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Lady Police Officer in Rape Investigation
records.heading: A lady police officer should be associated with investigation of rape where women are complainants or witnesses
records.text: A lady police officer should be associated with investigation where the complainant or witnesses are women who may not be forthcoming before male officers. The Court noted the Punjab SOP for Investigation of Rape Cases of 2013 and suggested a similar one for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It also discussed qazf. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 205.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Elderly Accused and Further Inquiry
records.heading: An accused over seventy in a case of further inquiry is admitted to bail
records.text: The petitioner was over seventy years old and the case was one of further inquiry. Petition was converted into an appeal and allowed, admitting the petitioner to bail. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 205.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission: Withheld Witnesses
records.heading: Failure to produce the Moharrar and constable defeats proof of safe custody and transmission
records.text: In a s. 9(c) CNSA case the Moharrar who kept the sample parcels and the constable who took them to the laboratory were not produced, so safe custody and transmission were not established. Conviction set aside and the accused acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 203.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail Refused: Murder of Wife, Plea of Suicide
records.heading: Bail is refused where medical findings contradict suicide and the husband must explain his wife's death
records.text: Bail was dismissed where the medical findings, including a ligature mark and petechial haemorrhage with an intact hyoid bone, were inconsistent with suicide. Under Art. 122 QSO the husband had to explain what befell his wife who spent the night with him, and witnesses spoke of acrimony between the spouses. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 210.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 7 ATA Not Attracted: Personal Vendetta
records.heading: Section 7 ATA is not attracted where an occurrence arises from personal enmity without intent to terrorise
records.text: Where the occurrence arose from a scuffle between children, previous enmity or a personal act of ghairat, without intent to create terror or insecurity in society, s. 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 is not attracted. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 216.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal: Delayed FIR and Exoneration of Co-Accused
records.heading: Delayed FIR and exoneration of a co-accused on the same evidence raise doubt warranting acquittal
records.text: In a case under Ss. 302/337-F(ii)/34 PPC, the FIR was delayed by 11 days, the Rapat was not exhibited, and injured witnesses later exonerated a co-accused who was acquitted on the same evidence. A shadow of doubt arose, and the benefit goes to the appellant as of right. Appeal allowed and appellant acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 224.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: PPSC Recommendation and Locus Poenitentiae
records.heading: A civil servant appointed on PPSC recommendation cannot be terminated simpliciter after appointment letters issue
records.text: PPSC does not become functus officio after sending its recommendation (Regs. 26 and 63, PPSC Regulations, 2016). After appointment letters are issued, a civil servant cannot be terminated simpliciter under the principle of locus poenitentiae. The Art. 212 bar applies only to terms and conditions of service or disciplinary matters. Ref: 2021 LHC 7833; Chand Iqbal etc v. POP etc (Service 26883/21, decided 14.07.2021); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Chand Iqbal etc v. POP etc (Service 26883/21, decided 14.07.2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Shifting Burden of Proof: Art. 122 QSO
records.heading: The evidential burden shifts as proceedings progress and Article 122 QSO governs facts within a person's knowledge
records.text: The evidential burden shifts as proceedings progress. Under Art. 122 QSO, a fact especially within a person's knowledge must be proved by him, and where a plaintiff has produced the best evidence available and taken the necessary steps, the burden of producing record in the defendant's custody shifts to the defendant. Ref: 1996 MLD 1064.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Burden of Proof, Best Evidence and CPC Tools
records.heading: The legal burden stays on a party while the evidential burden shifts and adverse inference follows withholding
records.text: Burden of proof has a legal facet that stays on a party and an evidential facet that shifts. Parties must produce all material evidence in their power or face an adverse inference, disclosure by public bodies is treated more liberally, and the trial court should use the CPC as a toolkit, including O. 15 R. 3, to discover the truth. Ref: M/s Naseem & Company and others v. Capital Development Authority and others (Writ Petition No. 3159 of 2020, decided 25.03.2022).
records.title: M/s Naseem & Company and others v. Capital Development Authority and others (Writ Petition No. 3159 of 2020, decided 25.03.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested Relative Witnesses and Doubtful Presence
records.heading: Relationship alone does not warrant rejecting a witness but doubtful presence cannot be cured by corroboration
records.text: Relationship alone does not warrant rejecting a witness, but the testimony must be free from doubt and infirmity. Where presence of the eye-witnesses is doubtful, corroborative evidence cannot cure the defect and becomes worthless. Ref: Muhammad Imran v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 54463/2019).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 54463/2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing FIR: Age of Abductee Girl Disputed
records.heading: The age of an abductee is for the trial court and not for quashing under Article 199
records.text: Where no material exists to decide the age of the abductee or whether she was sui juris to marry, that question is for the trial court after evidence and not for the High Court in constitutional jurisdiction. A minor cannot make a valid proposal or acceptance of marriage. The High Court refused to quash the FIR. Ref: 2022 LHC 6452; Danish Farooq v. SHO etc (Criminal Proceedings 49970/22, decided 19.09.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Danish Farooq v. SHO etc (Criminal Proceedings 49970/22, decided 19.09.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Marriage of Minor Under 18 Is Invalid
records.heading: A girl under 18 cannot validly contract marriage and guardians cannot do so on her behalf
records.text: The Islamabad High Court held that a girl under 18 cannot validly contract marriage, as the legal age of majority is 18 and guardians cannot contract a physical relationship on her behalf. A 16 year old girl was returned to her mother, and the lack of clarity in the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance was referred to the Cabinet Division and Parliament. Ref: PLD 2022 Islamabad 228; Justice Babar Sattar.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 221 CrPC: Contents and Object of Charge
records.heading: A charge must state the offence and the law violated so that it gives the accused notice
records.text: A charge must state the offence and the law and section violated. Its object is to give the accused notice of the precise accusation, and a charge that does not mislead the accused in his defence has no material defect. Under s. 265-D the charge is framed after perusing the police report or complaint and documents. Ref: 2022 MLD 1046.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Declaration to Change Date of Birth
records.heading: Consistent school records prevail over a later NADRA birth certificate in a suit to change date of birth
records.text: In a suit under s. 42 Specific Relief Act for change of date of birth, the date consistently recorded in school and matriculation records prevailed. The High Court erred in upsetting concurrent findings and directing the Board to change the date on the basis of a later NADRA birth certificate. Appeal allowed and suit dismissed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 912.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Declaring a Witness Hostile: Art. 150 QSO
records.heading: A witness is declared hostile only for unwillingness to tell the truth and a withheld witness raises adverse presumption
records.text: A witness may be declared hostile under Art. 150 QSO only where his manner of giving evidence shows he is unwilling to tell the truth, and he is then cross-examined by both parties. A witness cited but not produced is not hostile but withheld, and an adverse presumption arises against the party withholding him. Ref: 2003 YLR 2958.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination of Resiling Witness: Art. 140 QSO
records.heading: A witness who resiles from a recorded section 161(3) statement can be cross-examined under Article 140 QSO
records.text: The words reduced into writing in s. 161(3) CrPC and Art. 140 QSO are identical, indicating that a witness who resiles from a previous statement reduced into writing under s. 161(3) can be cross-examined under Art. 140 QSO. Ref: 2003 YLR 2958.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Return of Case from ATC to Regular Court
records.heading: Maltreatment and snatching of a phone is not terrorism and the case returns to the regular court
records.text: Maltreatment of a maid and snatching of her mobile phone was not an act of terrorism. The Anti-Terrorism Court rightly returned the case to the regular court before framing of charge, as the ingredients of s. 365-A PPC were not met. Constitutional petition dismissed. Ref: 2014 PCrLJ 754.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Court's Duty to Control Cross-Examination
records.heading: The trial court must control cross-examination and protect the dignity of the witness
records.text: The trial Court must be vigilant in controlling cross-examination (Arts. 132(2), 133, 141 QSO), ensure the witness understands the question, disallow lengthy and irrelevant questions, and be conversant with the case facts. It must also protect the dignity of the witness from insult by counsel. Ref: 2006 PCrLJ 1294; Ali Asghar v. State.
records.title: Ali Asghar v. State

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Definition and Types of Contempt of Court
records.heading: Contempt of court is civil, criminal or judicial and the law should operate with restraint on free speech
records.text: The judgment explains that contempt is defined in Art. 204 of the Constitution and s. 3 of the Ordinance, and divides it into civil, criminal and judicial contempt. It emphasises restraint so that contempt law operates least restrictively of freedom of speech under Art. 19. The application for contempt proceedings was dismissed. Ref: Saleem Ullah Khan, Advocate v. Fowad Ahmed Chaudhary (Criminal Original No. 157 of 2022).
records.title: Saleem Ullah Khan, Advocate v. Fowad Ahmed Chaudhary (Criminal Original No. 157 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Executing Court Cannot Appoint Local Commission
records.heading: An executing court has no power to appoint a local commission
records.text: The power to appoint a local commission under s. 75 and O. XXVI R. 9 CPC is restricted to proceedings in the suit. An application under O. XXI R. 32 is an execution proceeding, so the executing court has no power to appoint a local commission. Ref: 2022 CLC 1719.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: Out-of-Court Payment under O. XXI R. 1 and 2
records.heading: Out-of-court payment in execution must be by bank or money order or in writing and certified to the court
records.text: The executing court cannot go behind the decree beyond s. 47 CPC. An out-of-court payment is acceptable only if made through a bank or postal money order or evidenced in writing signed by the decree-holder, and must be certified to the court under O. XXI Rr. 1 and 2. A disputed receipt did not satisfy these requirements. Ref: 2022 CLC 1684.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Presumption of Truth of Revenue Record
records.heading: Revenue record entries carry a presumption of truth until rebutted though a mutation is not a title deed
records.text: A mutation is not a title deed, but revenue record entries carry a presumption of truth under s. 52 of the Land Revenue Act, 1967 until rebutted. Record of Rights is public record under Art. 150 of the Constitution, and demanding thirty years of record from an unchallenged owner imposes a higher onus than the law requires. Ref: 2022 CLC 1703.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Strict Proof of Talb-i-Muwathibat
records.heading: Talb-i-Muwathibat must be strictly proved with date, time and place or the pre-emption claim fails
records.text: Talb-i-Muwathibat is the foundation of the right of pre-emption under s. 13 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1991, and its date, time and place must be proved by cogent evidence. Strict proof of the talbs is required, and failure to prove it defeats the pre-emption claim. Ref: 2022 CLC 1628.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Investigation under Art. 18A Police Order
records.heading: Transfer of investigation under Article 18A is not routine and cannot be ordered to favour a party
records.text: Transfer of investigation under Art. 18A of the Police Order, 2002 is not routine. It is ordered when further relevant material is needed and not to favour one party. Re-investigation or further investigation may be conducted after conclusion of a private complaint depending on the fate of the trial. Ref: Dilshad Akbar v. Inspector General of Police, Punjab, Lahore & others (Writ Petition No. 18153 of 2022).
records.title: Dilshad Akbar v. Inspector General of Police, Punjab, Lahore & others (Writ Petition No. 18153 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: A chance witness must give a satisfactory explanation for his presence or his testimony is rejected
records.text: A chance witness, who is not ordinarily expected to be at the scene, must be scrutinised with great care and accepted only if he gives a satisfactory explanation for his presence, failing which his testimony is liable to be rejected. Ref: Muhammad Irfan Haider & 2 others v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No. 344 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan Haider & 2 others v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No. 344 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Legal Burden and Evidential Burden
records.heading: The legal burden of proving every element of the offence rests on the prosecution throughout
records.text: The legal burden of proving all elements of the offence beyond reasonable doubt rests on the prosecution, and the court decides at the end of the trial whether it was discharged. The evidential burden is a separate concept. Ref: Muhammad Irfan Haider & 2 others v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No. 344 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan Haider & 2 others v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No. 344 of 2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Cannot De-Exhibit Documents
records.heading: A Family Court cannot review its earlier order to de-exhibit documents
records.text: Neither the CPC nor the Qanun-e-Shahadat applies to proceedings under the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964, and the Family Court cannot review its earlier order to de-exhibit exhibited documents. Such an order is without jurisdiction and may be set aside by the High Court in constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: 2002 CLC 1801.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Unproved Iqrar Nama Cannot Be Tendered
records.heading: A private document must be proved through its scribe and attesting witnesses before it is tendered
records.text: Only documents proved in accordance with the QSO may be tendered in evidence. A private document must be proved through its scribe and attesting witnesses, and presenting it in examination-in-chief, without it forming part of the investigation or prosecution evidence, does not make it admissible. Ref: PLJ 2016 CrC 708.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: No De-Exhibiting of Documents under CPC
records.heading: The CPC provides no power to de-exhibit a document once it is marked as an exhibit
records.text: The CPC does not define or provide for de-exhibiting, and apart from O. XIII R. 9 CPC there is no provision to remove a document from record once marked as an exhibit. Its evidentiary value remains open to challenge, so the Trial Court rightly declined to de-exhibit the documents. Ref: 2018 CLC 1569.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Resiling from Recorded Compromise
records.heading: Petitioners cannot resile from a compromise recorded in the order by relying on section 12(2) CPC
records.text: Where a compromise was recorded in the order during arguments, the petitioners cannot resile from it by asserting that the matter was part heard or that the decision resulted from misrepresentation. Such assertions fall outside s. 12(2) CPC, particularly when counsel who appeared did not support them by affidavit. Ref: 2022 LHC 6552; Muhammad Yousaf v. Mst. Bashiran Bibi etc (Civil Petition/CM-U/S. 12(2) C.P.C. 22-C-22, decided 12.09.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Mst. Bashiran Bibi etc (Civil Petition/CM-U/S. 12(2) C.P.C. 22-C-22, decided 12.09.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement Securing Loan Is Not Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A document securing a loan with a penal clause is not an agreement to sell
records.text: An agreement securing a loan with a penal clause on default is not an agreement to sell, and the substance of a document governs over its label. A document may be construed as security for a loan, and vague, unconscionable or lopsided agreements cannot be specifically enforced. A beneficiary must strongly prove that an illiterate executant understood the document. Ref: Khalid Mehmood v. Dilawar Khan (C.R. No. 318 of 2015, decided 21.09.2022).
records.title: Khalid Mehmood v. Dilawar Khan (C.R. No. 318 of 2015, decided 21.09.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal: Double Presumption
records.heading: An accused acquitted enjoys a double presumption of innocence that an appellate court disturbs sparingly
records.text: In an appeal against acquittal the accused enjoys a double presumption of innocence, which the appellate court should disturb sparingly and only where the conclusion is not based on a fair reading of the evidence, or is perverse, arbitrary or wholly unreasonable. Mere possibility of another view is not enough. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 146.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Legal and Evidential Burden: Arts. 117 and 122 QSO
records.heading: The legal burden of proving guilt stays on the prosecution and Article 122 QSO operates only afterwards
records.text: The legal burden of proving guilt under Art. 117 QSO rests on the prosecution and cannot shift unless the legislature expressly provides. Art. 122 QSO operates only after the prosecution has discharged that burden, whereupon the accused bears the evidential burden of creating doubt. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 146.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Child Witness: Rationality Test
records.heading: A child witness must be able to understand and answer questions rationally throughout testimony
records.text: Under Art. 3 QSO a child witness must have the capacity to understand questions and respond rationally. The rationality test applied at the start of examination should continue throughout the testimony, with remedial measures or adjournment if the child shows hindrance or reluctance. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 146.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ingredients of S. 201 PPC
records.heading: Section 201 PPC requires knowledge of an offence, causing disappearance of evidence and intent to screen the offender
records.text: The offence under s. 201 PPC requires proof that the accused knew or had reason to believe an offence had occurred, caused evidence of it to disappear or gave false information, and acted with the intention of screening the offender from punishment. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 146.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Cruelty to Child: S. 328-A PPC
records.heading: Cruelty to a child under section 328-A PPC requires a wilful act or omission causing actual harm
records.text: The offence under s. 328-A PPC requires an act of commission or omission, that is wilful, and that results in actual physical or psychological harm to the child. Mens rea for acts of commission is judged by objective societal standards, and for omissions by a subjective fault criterion. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 146.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: Ss. 302(b) and 302(c) PPC
records.heading: Grave and sudden provocation is judged objectively and unproved allegations of bad character do not amount to it
records.text: Grave and sudden provocation is judged by objective criteria as a question of fact and not by the offender's state of mind. An unproved allegation of bad character, or merely seeing the wife in a man's company, did not amount to provocation, so the case did not fall under s. 302(c) PPC. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 620.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation Rejected
records.heading: Fetching a shotgun and reloading broke any loss of self-control so provocation was rejected
records.text: Fetching a shotgun broke any loss of self-control, and the accused reloaded and fired repeatedly. There was no evidence of what caused sudden provocation, so Exception 1 to the erstwhile s. 300 PPC was not attracted. Convictions maintained and leave refused. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 419.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Opinion on Distance of Firearm Blackening
records.heading: A medical doctor may note blackening but the distance of fire is for a forensic expert
records.text: A medical doctor may state whether a wound shows blackening but may not be qualified to determine the distance of fire, which falls within the expertise of a firearm forensic expert. The prosecution case under s. 324 PPC was held proved. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 419.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Honour Killing Distinguished from Grave and Sudden Provocation
records.heading: Honour killing is premeditated murder and differs from sudden loss of self-control under provocation
records.text: Murder in the name or on the pretext of honour under the first proviso to s. 302(c) PPC is a calculated, premeditated murder, whereas Exception 1 to the erstwhile s. 300 PPC covers a sudden, unpremeditated loss of self-control. The two phrases address different situations and must not be confused. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 840.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Penalty under S. 302(b) PPC: Relevant Factors
records.heading: The death penalty under section 302(b) PPC follows where the killing was brutal and discretion to withhold it needs care
records.text: Death penalty is to be imposed where the manner and method of the incident show the deceased was killed brutally. Courts must consider the heinousness of the act and proceed with care when exercising discretion to withhold the death penalty. Ref: 2012 SCMR 1195.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: Verbal Abuse and Burden
records.heading: Verbal abuse and threats are not sufficient for grave and sudden provocation and the burden is on the accused
records.text: Mere verbal abuse and threats are not sufficient for grave and sudden provocation. The burden of proving circumstances bringing the case within provocation lies on the accused, and the plea must be considered as a whole and not piecemeal. Ref: 2012 SCMR 1195.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: Nature and Test
records.heading: Provocation must be one that would upset a person of ordinary sense and calmness and not one sought by the accused
records.text: The benefit of grave and sudden provocation is available only if the accused did not seek the provocation. It must be such as would upset a person of ordinary sense and calmness and not merely a hot-tempered or hypersensitive one. Ref: 2011 SCMR 613.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: Adequate Cause
records.heading: Grave and sudden provocation must be shown distinctly with an adequate cause for the loss of control
records.text: Grave and sudden provocation must be shown distinctly, including that the act was done under a feeling that took away the accused's control over his actions and that the feeling had an adequate cause. Ref: PLD 2010 SC 669.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ghairat Distinguished from Grave and Sudden Provocation
records.heading: An accused pleading ghairat with premeditation may not rely on grave and sudden provocation
records.text: Commission of an offence due to ghairat or family honour must be distinguished from grave and sudden provocation. The plea of provocation may not be available to an accused who pleads ghairat and committed the crime with premeditation. Ref: PLD 2006 SC 283.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Provocation Plea Corroborated by Witnesses
records.heading: Witnesses not understanding the words spoken does not defeat corroboration of the provocation plea
records.text: In a s. 302 PPC case, the fact that witnesses did not understand the Pushto words spoken by the deceased did not mean their evidence failed to corroborate the plea of sudden provocation. Words said to be capable of causing provocation could be a mitigating circumstance relevant to a lesser penalty. Ref: PLD 1996 SC 1.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Arts. 117 and 121 QSO
records.heading: He who asserts must prove, and an accused pleading an exception must prove the circumstances
records.text: Under Art. 117 QSO he who asserts must prove. Under Art. 121 QSO an accused who pleads a general or special exception has the burden of proving the circumstances bringing the case within it, and the Court presumes their absence. Ref: PLD 1996 SC 1.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Fresh Ground: Complainant Retracts
records.heading: A complainant's retraction after compromise is a fresh ground for bail even in a non-compoundable offence
records.text: Although the offence was not compoundable, where the complainant and witnesses were unwilling to depose against the accused after a compromise, no other evidence would suffice for conviction. The case became arguable on a fresh ground and bail was allowed. Ref: 2012 YLR 1606.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Islamic Jurisprudence in Administration of Justice
records.heading: Courts in Pakistan must seek guidance from Islamic jurisprudence in administering civil and criminal justice
records.text: Courts in Pakistan must seek guidance for the administration of justice in civil and criminal cases from the principles enunciated by the Holy Prophet, the four Caliphs, Imams and eminent Qazis, and give them overriding effect over Western principles. Ref: 1996 SCMR 973.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Succession: Classes of Heirs under Muslim Law
records.heading: Muslim heirs are sharers, residuaries and distant kindred and the nearer in blood excludes the remote
records.text: Muslim inheritance is governed by Shariah, with heirs divided into sharers, residuaries and distant kindred, and the nearer in blood inheriting before the remote. Collaterals inherit after sharers and residuaries, and a claimant must prove his connection with the deceased and the absence of heirs with a preferential right. Ref: PLD 2005 SC 511.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Application of Precedent in Criminal Cases
records.heading: A ruling in one criminal case must be carefully considered before it is cited as precedent in another
records.text: Hardly any criminal case is identical on all fours to another, and background and causes of the offence differ. A ruling in one criminal case must therefore be carefully considered before it is cited as a precedent in another. Ref: 2009 SCMR 1273.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Tendering a Document and Its Probative Value
records.heading: Tendering a document is a mode of proving its existence and does not mean the court accepted it
records.text: Tendering a document is the mode of proving its existence and does not mean the court has accepted it or its contents (Arts. 72, 73, 74, 79 QSO). Probative value is assessed after existence or execution is established, and where the objection concerns contents and not execution, production cannot be denied. Ref: PLD 2022 Sindh 222.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Trichotomy of Powers and Statutory Interpretation
records.heading: Courts interpret a statute only where it is unclear and must give effect to legislative intent
records.text: The Constitution rests on a trichotomy of powers among the legislature, executive and judiciary. Courts interpret a statute only where it is unclear, vague or opposed to the Constitution, must give effect to legislative intent, and cannot substitute their own views for it. Ref: PLD 2022 Sindh 440.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: NAO: Bond under S. 91 CrPC Where No Arrest Directed
records.heading: Where no arrest is directed under the NAO the accused is bound over by a section 91 CrPC bond
records.text: Where no direction for arrest was pending under s. 24(a) of the National Accountability Ordinance, 1999, nor later issued under s. 24(c), the Accountability Court was to require the accused to execute a bond with or without sureties under s. 91 CrPC to assure his appearance. Majority view. Ref: PLD 2022 Sindh 440.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Cross-Versions Must Be Tried Together
records.heading: Cross-version cases must be tried together by the same court with simultaneous judgments
records.text: Counter cases must be tried side by side by the same court and judgments pronounced simultaneously, since the question of who was the aggressor cannot be decided without examining the evidence of both. The impugned judgments were set aside and the case remanded for decision afresh. Ref: 2022 MLD 1589.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC Appeal: Complainant Must Be Heard
records.heading: The complainant must be impleaded and heard in an appeal arising from a section 489-F PPC acquittal
records.text: Where an accused appeals against acquittal grounds without impleading the complainant, the appellate court must direct impleading and issue notice. It must also allow the complainant to produce the original cheque or prove the reasons for non-production under the QSO. Appeal allowed and case remanded. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1545.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Judicial Record and Secondary Evidence: Art. 76 QSO
records.heading: A criminal court cannot summon judicial record and only certified copies are admissible as secondary evidence
records.text: The Criminal Procedure Code, 1898 has no provision for a court to summon judicial record, by analogy with O. XIII R. 10 CPC. Only certified copies may be produced as secondary evidence under Art. 76 QSO. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1545.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 and R. 13 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Rejection of a plaint under Order VII Rule 11 leaves the plaintiff free to file a fresh plaint
records.text: O. VII R. 11 CPC must be read with O. VII R. 13, under which rejection of a plaint leaves the plaintiff free to present a fresh plaint on the same cause of action. This distinguishes rejection from a suit finally decided after evidence, to which res judicata under s. 11 CPC applies. Ref: Hadayat Ullah deceased through Legal Heirs etc. v. Province of the Punjab etc. (Civil Revision No. 3587-2011).
records.title: Hadayat Ullah deceased through Legal Heirs etc. v. Province of the Punjab etc. (Civil Revision No. 3587-2011)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Challenging Cabinet Size under Art. 92(1)
records.heading: A writ challenging the size of the cabinet under Article 92(1) was dismissed in limine
records.text: A petition under Art. 199 sought a declaration that the appointment of Federal Ministers and Ministers of State violated Art. 92(1). The Court declined to exercise its extraordinary discretionary jurisdiction and dismissed the petition in limine. Ref: Sheikh Rasheed Ahmad v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division & 74 others (W.P. No. 3593/2022, decided 27.09.2022); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Sheikh Rasheed Ahmad v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division & 74 others (W.P. No. 3593/2022, decided 27.09.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Plea of Alibi Found Correct
records.heading: A plea of alibi found correct during investigation makes the case one of further inquiry for bail
records.text: Where the plea of alibi was found correct during investigation, the case is one of further inquiry for post-arrest bail. Courts must make a tentative assessment of all material with great care in capital cases, and benefit of doubt goes to the accused even at the bail stage. Ref: 2022 LHC 6592; Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 2293/22, decided 16.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 2293/22, decided 16.09.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Christian Marriage Act 1872: Marriage of Minors
records.heading: The Christian Marriage Act 1872 governs marriage of minors and prevails over church precepts
records.text: The Christian Marriage Act, 1872 and the Divorce Act, 1869 are the principal family laws for Christians and prevail over church precepts in case of conflict. The Act defines a minor as a person under twenty one years who is not a widow or widower, and s. 19 provides for consent of the father, guardian or mother to a minor's marriage. Ref: Nasreen Bibi v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 63301/2021).
records.title: Nasreen Bibi v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 63301/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC Suit on Cheque: Presentment Required
records.heading: A summary suit on a cheque requires presentment to the bank and dishonour
records.text: A suit under O. XXXVII CPC on a cheque requires that the cheque was presented to the bank and dishonoured, as that gives the cause of action. Without presentment the cheque is only evidence of the loan transaction, and the summary suit is not maintainable. Ref: Ghulam Mustafa, etc. v. Muhammad Musharaf Hussain, etc. (Regular First Appeal No. 104 of 2015, decided 15.09.2022).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa, etc. v. Muhammad Musharaf Hussain, etc. (Regular First Appeal No. 104 of 2015, decided 15.09.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marking of s. 164 and s. 27 Statements
records.heading: Omnibus marking of section 164 statements and confessions should be avoided and only admissible portions proved
records.text: Indian Supreme Court guidance that omnibus marking of a s. 164 CrPC statement should be deprecated, and the relevant portions used for contradiction or corroboration under ss. 145/157 of the Evidence Act marked separately. Only the admissible portion of a confession under s. 27 should be extracted in the recovery memo or proved by the Investigating Officer, and wholesale marking of the entire confession should be avoided. Ref: In Re: To Issue Certain Guidelines Regarding Inadequacies and Deficiencies in Criminal Trials (Suo Motu Writ (Crl.) No. 1 of 2017, decided 30.03.2017); Justice S.A. Bobde; Justice L. Nageswara Rao.
records.title: In Re: To Issue Certain Guidelines Regarding Inadequacies and Deficiencies in Criminal Trials (Suo Motu Writ (Crl.) No. 1 of 2017, decided 30.03.2017)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance Decree is Preliminary: Extension of Time
records.heading: A specific performance decree is preliminary and the court may extend time for payment of the price
records.text: A decree for specific performance of an agreement to sell is preliminary in nature, since the vendee must still deposit the price and the seller must execute the conveyance. The court retains seisin of the lis and may enlarge the time for payment of the purchase price under s. 148 CPC. Ref: Muhammad Sidique v. Syed Riaz Shah (Civil Revision No.150/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Sidique v. Syed Riaz Shah (Civil Revision No.150/2022)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Avenfield Reference: Acquittal Appeals Allowed
records.heading: The Islamabad High Court allowed the Avenfield acquittal appeals by short order with reasons to follow
records.text: The Islamabad High Court issued a one page short order allowing the appeals against the judgment of 6 July 2018, acquitting Maryam Nawaz of the charges in the reference and setting aside her sentence. The sentence of Capt. (R) Safdar was also set aside. Detailed reasons were to follow. Ref: Maryam Nawaz v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 122 of 2018); Capt. (R) Muhammad Safdar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 123 of 2018).
records.title: Maryam Nawaz v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 122 of 2018); Capt. (R) Muhammad Safdar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 123 of 2018)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Cheque Must be Issued by Accused
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC applies only where the accused himself issued the cheque
records.text: Section 489-F PPC applies only where the cheque was issued by the accused himself, as shown by the word 'his' in the later part of the section. Even if the petitioner may have cheated or committed breach of trust, s. 489-F PPC was held not attracted on the facts. Ref: 2014 YLR 882.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Transit/Protective Bail Granted Till 07.10.2022
records.heading: Transit bail was granted until a stated date to enable appearance before the competent court
records.text: The petitioner was granted transit or protective bail till 07.10.2022 on bail bonds of Rs. 10,000 with one surety, to enable him to appear before the court of competent jurisdiction. The order was to expire automatically after that date. Counsel's request for exemption from personal appearance was accepted. Ref: Imran Ahmed v. The State and another (Cri. Misc. No.1240/B/2022).
records.title: Imran Ahmed v. The State and another (Cri. Misc. No.1240/B/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Investigation: Art. 18A Police Order
records.heading: Article 18A of the Police Order provides a tiered regime for transfer of investigation
records.text: Neither the Code nor the Police Rules 1934 provide a procedure for transfer of investigation. Art. 18A of the Police Order 2002 (inserted in 2013) sets a tiered regime: the Head of District Police, then the Regional Police Officer, then the Provincial Police Officer, each within stated time limits and after opinion of the relevant standing board. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 721.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partition Suit: Local Commission
records.heading: In a partition suit the court appoints a local commission at its discretion and must protect every sharer
records.text: In a partition suit the parties are those who already have established ownership, and the court must ensure no sharer is deprived of his entitlement. A local commission is appointed at the court's discretion under O. XXVI R. 1 CPC, and the parties may object to its proposal. A second commission appointed before the referee provision of the Partition Act 2012 was held valid. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 766.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Determination of Compensation for Acquired Land
records.heading: Compensation for acquired land is assessed at market value as a prudent man would assess it
records.text: The Land Acquisition Act 1894 is a complete scheme that protects the owner, who is to receive gold for gold and not copper for gold. Market value is to be assessed as a prudent man would, on all available evidence, including loss from severance and injurious affection. Future value, sale deeds, mutation entries, delay and credible oral evidence may be considered. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 730.

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: Vires of S. 20 PECA: Defamation
records.heading: Section 20 PECA protecting a person's dignity was held intra vires the Constitution
records.text: Section 20 PECA, which protects the dignity of a natural person, was held intra vires. It conforms to Art. 14 of the Constitution and is justified by the Harm Principle. The Explanations and Exceptions of s. 499 PPC are read into it through ss. 28 and 50 PECA, and it does not violate Arts. 4 and 25. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Single Trial of CNSA, PPC and ATA Offences in ATC
records.heading: Offences arising from one transaction under CNSA, PPC and ATA are tried together by the Anti-Terrorism Court
records.text: Where recovery of narcotics (s. 9(c) CNSA), murder (s. 302 PPC) and an offence under s. 7 ATA arose from one transaction, both s. 173 CrPC reports were to go to the Anti-Terrorism Court for a single trial. 'Distinct offence' in s. 233 CrPC means offences having no nexus. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 700.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 17A(1) Family Courts Act: Interim Maintenance Mandatory
records.heading: The Family Court must fix interim maintenance on the defendant's first appearance under section 17A(1)
records.text: Under s. 17A(1) of the Family Courts Act 1964, the word 'shall' makes it imperative for the Family Court to fix interim monthly maintenance on the defendant's first appearance. Default in payment is sanctioned by striking off the defence. The writ petition was dismissed in limine. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 715.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 17A(3) Family Courts Act: Automatic Annual Increase
records.heading: The annual increase in maintenance under section 17A(3) is mandatory and automatic and needs no decree
records.text: The annual increase under s. 17A(3) of the Family Courts Act applies where the court omits to prescribe it, is mandatory and automatic, and needs no decree. It is recoverable by the executing court, at ten percent each year on the constant base maintenance, for as long as the entitlement lasts. It does not operate retrospectively. Ref: 2022 MLD 1762.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Expunction of Judge's Remarks Against Prosecutors
records.heading: Derogatory remarks by a judge against public prosecutors without material were expunged
records.text: The High Court allowed a writ petition by public prosecutors and ordered expunction of derogatory remarks made against prosecutors by an Anti-Terrorism Court judge. There was no material for such remarks, and the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service Act 2006 gives prosecutors independent powers from the registration of the FIR. The court also referred to judicial restraint. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1594.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 14 Family Courts Act: Appeal Against Interim Order
records.heading: An order dismissing an interim protection application under the Family Courts Act is appealable under section 14
records.text: Dismissal of an application under s. 21A of the Family Courts Act for interim protection of property during a dower suit is 'a decision given' and appealable under s. 14. An interlocutory order to which finality attaches for a particular purpose is likewise challengeable. A direct writ without availing that remedy was not maintainable. Ref: 2022 MLD 1621.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Execution of Document
records.heading: Execution of a document is a series of acts and exhibiting a document is not proving it
records.text: Execution of a document means a series of acts, not mere signing or a thumb impression. It must be shown that it was written, read over and understood in the presence of witnesses, and the executants identified by reliable evidence. An unproved document is inadmissible unless strict proof is waived, and exhibiting a document differs from proving it. Ref: 2022 MLD 1734.

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Petition Against Dead Respondent
records.heading: A contempt petition against a sole respondent who has died is not proceedable
records.text: An order against an official by designation binds the incumbent despite change of office holder. A contempt petition filed against a sole respondent who has died is not proceedable, being equivalent to a stillborn suit, and the successor cannot be substituted, though a fresh petition may be filed. Ref: 2022 LHC 6729; Muhammad Majid v. Dr Shahid Iqbal MS Jinnah Hospital (Criminal Original (Writ) 29909/22, decided 15.09.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Majid v. Dr Shahid Iqbal MS Jinnah Hospital (Criminal Original (Writ) 29909/22, decided 15.09.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 17A(4) Family Courts Act: Procedure for Fixing Maintenance
records.heading: Family Courts must follow the section 17A(4) procedure when fixing maintenance and avoid arbitrary amounts
records.text: The High Court addressed the procedure for fixing maintenance under s. 17A(4) of the Family Courts Act 1964, which Family Courts frequently ignore, resulting in arbitrary amounts and stereotyped orders. It refers to the Schedule under s. 5 and binding precedent under Arts. 189 and 201. Copies were directed to Punjab judges and the Punjab Judicial Academy. Ref: Marriam Bibi and others v. Azhar Iqbal and others (Writ Petition No.359 of 2022).
records.title: Marriam Bibi and others v. Azhar Iqbal and others (Writ Petition No.359 of 2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Transfer is Not a Right of Employee
records.heading: An employee cannot claim transfer to a place of his choice as a right
