records.text: An employee cannot, under any circumstances, claim transfer from one place to another of his choice as a right. Ref: 2022 LHC 6795; Ms. Farzana Liaqat v. Program Director etc. (Writ Petition 5653-22, decided 29.09.2022); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Ms. Farzana Liaqat v. Program Director etc. (Writ Petition 5653-22, decided 29.09.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Full Sisters: Sharers or Residuaries
records.heading: Full sisters who do not become residuaries take two thirds as sharers and Radd does not apply
records.text: Relying on the tables in Mulla's Principles of Mohammadan Law, full sisters who do not meet the conditions for becoming residuaries take 2/3 as sharers. The principle of Return (Radd) does not apply, and the residue left after the sharers is distributed among the petitioners as residuaries. Ref: 2022 LHC 6784; Muhammad Tufail etc. v. Begum Munawar Sadique etc. (Civil Revision 1362-18, decided 22.09.2022); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Tufail etc. v. Begum Munawar Sadique etc. (Civil Revision 1362-18, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII R. 3: Substitution of Security for Bank Guarantee
records.heading: Title documents of equivalent value may be substituted for a bank guarantee condition on leave to defend
records.text: Where leave to defend a summary suit was conditional on a bank guarantee equal to the claim, substitution of original title documents of property of equivalent value ought to have been allowed. The orders of the courts below were set aside and the matter remanded. Ref: 2014 SCMR 1830.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII: Leave to Defend and Summoning Bank Record
records.heading: On leave to defend the court may probe the defence and summon bank record held by a third party
records.text: In deciding leave to appear and defend in a suit on a dishonoured cheque, the court must not act mechanically and may probe the genuineness and plausibility of the defence. The plaintiff may seek summoning of a document in a third party's custody, and the Trial Court rightly summoned bank record supported by an affidavit. Ref: 2021 MLD 1473.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Witness Statement Not Recorded by Police: s. 161(3)
records.heading: Police need not record statements of all witnesses under section 161(3) and the accused is not prejudiced by absence
records.text: Under s. 161(3) CrPC it is not obligatory for the police to record statements of all witnesses examined. If recorded and the witness is to be examined, the accused is entitled to a copy. Absence of a previous statement does not prejudice the accused, as the court appreciates the witness's evidence as a whole for trustworthiness. Ref: P.A. Shaduly @ Haris v. State (decided 11.04.2017); Justice C.K. Abdul Rehim; Justice Shircy V..
records.title: P.A. Shaduly @ Haris v. State (decided 11.04.2017)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: SDR, CDR and Tower Location: Certificate Requirement
records.heading: Electronic evidence such as CDR and CCTV needs a section 65B(4) certificate to be relied upon
records.text: The Bombay High Court agreed that the trial court rightly refused to rely on CCTV footage, CDR, SDR and tower location of the accused because the electronic evidence was not supported by a certificate under s. 65B(4) of the Indian Evidence Act. Ref: State of Maharashtra v. Sagar Vishwanath Borkar (Criminal Confirmation Case No. 01 of 2020).
records.title: State of Maharashtra v. Sagar Vishwanath Borkar (Criminal Confirmation Case No. 01 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Conviction Under s. 34 IPC Without Charge
records.heading: An accused charged under section 149 IPC may be convicted under section 34 absent failure of justice
records.text: Indian Supreme Court discussion of whether an accused charged under s. 149 IPC may be convicted under s. 34 IPC where no s. 34 charge was framed. Relying on (1998) 6 SCC 554, s. 464(1) CrPC provides that no finding is invalid merely for absence of or error in a charge unless a failure of justice has in fact occurred. Appeals dismissed.

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Right to Maternity Leave
records.heading: The right to maternity leave entitles working women to paid leave or benefits around childbirth
records.text: The right to maternity leave entitles working women to paid leave or social security benefits around childbirth, and may be justified under Arts. 3 and 11 of the Constitution. The post refers to the Mines Maternity Benefit Act 1941 and the Revised Leave Rules of 1980 and 1981. Ref: Sabeen Asghar etc. v. Province of the Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 51488/2022).
records.title: Sabeen Asghar etc. v. Province of the Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 51488/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Execution: Determining Value of Land
records.heading: Whether an executing court may fix an alternate value of land without fact-finding is raised
records.text: Concerns whether an executing court may determine and specify an alternate value of land on its own assumptions, without any fact-finding exercise to ascertain the market value. The post states only the question. Ref: Ahmad Khan v. ADJ, etc. (W.P. No. 50484 of 2022).
records.title: Ahmad Khan v. ADJ, etc. (W.P. No. 50484 of 2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Preliminary Decree and Local Commission in Partition
records.heading: A local commission only prepares partition by the shares in the preliminary decree and cannot decide rights
records.text: A preliminary decree determines the shares of all interested parties, and whether the property is joint is decided before it. The local commission only prepares the mode of partition according to the shares fixed in the decree and cannot determine any party's right or share. Ref: Zia ud Din etc. v. Malik Humayun Irfan etc. (Civil Revision No.364-D of 2010).
records.title: Zia ud Din etc. v. Malik Humayun Irfan etc. (Civil Revision No.364-D of 2010)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marked But Unproved Document is Not Evidence
records.heading: A document that is marked but not proved cannot be treated as legal evidence
records.text: A document that has only been marked, and not produced and proved in evidence, cannot be taken into account by the courts as legal evidence of a fact. Ref: Zia ud Din etc. v. Malik Humayun Irfan etc. (Civil Revision No.364-D of 2010).
records.title: Zia ud Din etc. v. Malik Humayun Irfan etc. (Civil Revision No.364-D of 2010)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Scope of Art. 128 QSO
records.heading: The scope of Article 128 QSO is noted without a stated holding
records.text: Authority on the scope of Art. 128 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order 1984. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2022 LHC 6828; Shahida Parveen v. POP etc. (Civil Revision 1007157.460-09, decided 21.09.2022); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Shahida Parveen v. POP etc. (Civil Revision 1007157.460-09, decided 21.09.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Proclaimed Offender: Bail Stands Cancelled
records.heading: Declaration as a proclaimed offender or issue of non-bailable warrants cancels bail under section 497(5) CrPC
records.text: Under s. 497(5) CrPC, when an accused on bail is subsequently declared a proclaimed offender or non-bailable warrants of arrest are issued against him, that declaration or issuance ipso facto amounts to cancellation of his bail. Ref: 2019 SCMR 1641.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Second Appeal: Scope Under s. 100 CPC
records.heading: A second appeal under section 100 CPC lies only on the grounds stated in that section
records.text: A second appeal under s. 100 CPC lies only on the grounds stated there: decision contrary to law, failure to determine a material issue of law, or substantial procedural defect. Section 101 bars other grounds, and High Courts should not treat second appeals as first appeals or reverse findings merely because another view is possible. Ref: Zafar Iqbal & others v. Naseer Ahmed & others (C.A.775/2015); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Zafar Iqbal & others v. Naseer Ahmed & others (C.A.775/2015)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail to Woman Accused: First Proviso to s. 497(1)
records.heading: A woman accused may be released on bail under the first proviso to section 497(1) even in prohibitory offences
records.text: The first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC lets the court release a woman on bail even in offences within the prohibitory clause. Bail is refused only where the accused is likely to abscond, tamper with prosecution evidence or witnesses, or repeat the offence. Bail was granted on bond of Rs. 50,000 with two sureties, subject to cancellation under s. 497(5) CrPC for misuse. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 764.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Trust Property Board: Authority to Sell Property
records.heading: A sale of evacuee trust property without Federal Government approval is illegal and void ab initio
records.text: Discusses the statutory framework of the Evacuee Trust Properties (Management and Disposal) Act 1975 governing the Board's powers of sale. A sale deed obtained without the approval of the Federal Government was held illegal and void ab initio, and the High Court was held to have rightly so concluded. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 726.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Registrar Cannot Decide Maintainability Under Supreme Court Rules
records.heading: The Registrar's powers are administrative and he cannot decide maintainability of a petition or appeal
records.text: Under the Supreme Court Rules 1980 the Registrar's powers are administrative and cover form and presentation only. He has no power to decide the maintainability of a petition or appeal, which is for the Court alone. Frivolous filings may be discouraged by costs under O. XVII R. 12. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 712.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Court Review of Revenue Authority Orders
records.heading: Civil courts may review administrative tribunal orders for lawfulness but cannot re-decide as an appellate court
records.text: Under s. 9 CPC civil courts may examine whether an administrative tribunal's order is lawful, even where jurisdiction is barred, but cannot take fresh evidence and re-decide as an appellate court. They may set aside findings based on no evidence. Grounds include jurisdiction, statutory basis, reasons, fair hearing and evidence. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 699.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summary Procedure O. XV Rr. 3, 4 CPC in Suits Against Tribunal Orders
records.heading: A civil court may use summary procedure in suits challenging tribunal orders and treat the record as evidence
records.text: In suits challenging orders of administrative tribunals, a civil court may use the summary procedure of O. XV Rr. 3 and 4 CPC and treat the complete record of the tribunal proceedings as sufficient evidence. Statements of the plaintiff and the defendant or record custodian are ordinarily enough to decide legality. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 699.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Delay: Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance 1984
records.heading: An accused is entitled to bail if trial is delayed over one year through no fault of his own
records.text: Addresses post-arrest bail for delay in trial of offences under the Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance 1984, including s. 5(6) and the High Court's constitutional jurisdiction. Under the third proviso (a) to s. 497(1) CrPC, an accused is entitled to bail if trial is delayed over one year, through no fault of the accused, in offences not punishable with death. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 743.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Investigation of Religion Offences: Supreme Court Directions
records.heading: Investigation of offences against religion must follow law and need corroboration of oral testimony
records.text: The Supreme Court directed that copies of the order go to the prosecution departments of all provinces and Islamabad so that investigation of offences under Chapter XV PPC follows law and the Constitution. It noted adverse publicity, false allegations to settle scores, the gravity of s. 295-C, and the need for corroboration of oral testimony. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 751.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ghairat and Grave Provocation: s. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: Murders under ghairat and grave and sudden provocation fall within section 302(c) PPC and mitigate sentence
records.text: The defence need only show a glimpse that its version is true. Where the murders were committed under the impulse of ghairat and grave and sudden provocation after the accused saw the deceased together in an amorous pursuit, the doctrine of diminished liability applied and the case fell within s. 302(c) PPC, mitigating the sentence. Ref: Sabtain Haider v. The State (Jail Petition No. 34 of 2020, decided 21.09.2022).
records.title: Sabtain Haider v. The State (Jail Petition No. 34 of 2020, decided 21.09.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Breach of Trust: Ingredients of s. 405 PPC
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation and entrustment is for the trial court
records.text: An offence under s. 405 PPC, punishable under s. 406 PPC, requires entrustment of property and dishonest misappropriation, conversion or disposal in violation of law or contract. Whether there was entrustment, as asserted by the petitioner, was left for the Trial Court to decide after recording evidence. Ref: Muhammad Ali v. Samina Qasim Tarar and others (Civil Petition No. 3130 of 2020, decided 29.09.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Ali v. Samina Qasim Tarar and others (Civil Petition No. 3130 of 2020, decided 29.09.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Vehicle Registration Scam, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail is allowed as further inquiry where the petitioner had no nexus with the scam
records.text: In a bogus vehicle registration scam of 2015 to 2018, one petitioner was posted as ETO only in 2019 and the Investigating Officer stated that he had no nexus with the scam so far. The case was held covered by s. 497(2) CrPC, calling for further inquiry, as detention for an indefinite period was unwarranted. Ref: Naeem Qadir Sheikh and Muhammad Zaigham Ali v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition Nos. 1086-L & 1143-L of 2022, decided 30.09.2022).
records.title: Naeem Qadir Sheikh and Muhammad Zaigham Ali v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition Nos. 1086-L & 1143-L of 2022, decided 30.09.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Abetment s. 107 PPC and CDR Not Conclusive
records.heading: Abetment is prima facie missing without specifics and call data record alone is not conclusive of guilt
records.text: No specific date, time or place of the alleged conspiracy was given, and the three ingredients of abetment under s. 107 PPC were prima facie missing. Call Data Record without concrete material is not conclusive of guilt, and there was no evidence that the phone or SIM belonged to the petitioner. Guilt is for the Trial Court after evidence. Ref: Shameem Bibi v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition No. 982-L of 2022, decided 22.09.2022).
records.title: Shameem Bibi v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition No. 982-L of 2022, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Meaning of 'Conjointly' in ss. 391 and 396 PPC
records.heading: The word conjointly in sections 391 and 396 PPC requires jointness of action among the robbers
records.text: The word 'conjointly' in ss. 391 and 396 PPC, used nowhere else in the PPC, indicates jointness of action, with each robber acting with the knowledge, consent and aid of the others under an agreement or understanding. The post also restates the three ingredients of abetment under s. 107 PPC. Ref: Muhammad Ali, Khurram Shahzad, Muhammad Sajjad, complainant v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal Nos. 363 to 366 of 2021, decided 22.09.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Ali, Khurram Shahzad, Muhammad Sajjad, complainant v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal Nos. 363 to 366 of 2021, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Transposition of Previous Statements in Criminal Trial
records.heading: Previous statements must be proved before use and a criminal court cannot transpose copies from its own record
records.text: Previous statements under Arts. 46 and 47 QSO must first be proved before corroboration or contradiction. The trial court's practice of transposing copies of earlier statements from its own record was held unwarranted, as the CrPC has no provision for transposition, unlike O. XIII R. 10 CPC for civil proceedings. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1753.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Concurrent Sentences: ss. 35 and 397 CrPC
records.heading: Courts should liberally order concurrent running of sentences under sections 35 and 397 CrPC absent aggravating factors
records.text: Absent aggravating circumstances, courts should liberally use ss. 35 and 397 CrPC to order concurrent running of sentences in one trial and consolidation with earlier sentences in a subsequent trial. Penal provisions are to be read in favour of liberty, and consecutive sentences would not serve the interest of justice. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1641.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Blocked CNIC or Passport: Recourse to Embassy
records.heading: A citizen abroad with a blocked CNIC or passport may approach the embassy for relief
records.text: A Pakistani abroad whose CNIC was blocked after being declared a proclaimed offender in 2014 petitioned the High Court. The court upheld the office objection that counsel's power of attorney was not embassy attested, held that the embassy may be approached where CNIC or passport is blocked, and that an embassy cannot reject a citizen's application for emergency travel documents. Ref: 2022 CLC 1950; Justice Shujaat Ali Khan.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 47 CPC: Executing Court's Jurisdiction
records.heading: Section 47 CPC vests the executing court with all questions on execution and requires a fair hearing
records.text: Section 47 CPC empowers the executing court to finally determine all questions on execution, discharge or satisfaction of a decree and bars a separate suit, and it becomes functus officio once the decree is discharged. An order finally accepting an objection petition without fair hearing violated Art. 10-A of the Constitution. Ref: 2022 CLC 1925.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Delay in Leave to Defend: Art. 159 Limitation Act
records.heading: An application for leave to defend after an ex parte decree must be filed within ten days of knowledge
records.text: Art. 159 of the Limitation Act 1908 allows 10 days for an application for leave to appear and defend from service or knowledge of the decree. The petitioner knew of the ex parte decree on 09.09.2015 but filed on 12.11.2015 and did not explain the delay. His plea against his former counsel was unsubstantiated and rightly discarded. Ref: 2022 CLC 1871.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Special Law Limitation: s. 5 Limitation Act Inapplicable
records.heading: Section 5 of the Limitation Act cannot condone delay beyond the period fixed by a special law
records.text: The Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act 1997 is a special law, so delay beyond the period under s. 38(3) of the Act cannot be condoned under s. 5 of the Limitation Act 1908, by virtue of s. 29(2)(b) of that Act. Ref: 2022 CLC 1992.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Challenge to s. 144 CrPC Imposition in Islamabad
records.heading: A petition against section 144 imposition was dismissed where the court may intervene only for misuse of power
records.text: The Islamabad High Court dismissed Asad Umar's petition against s. 144 in the capital. The party had parliamentary representation and an alternate forum, law and order is the executive's domain, and the court may intervene only for misuse of power. The petitioner was not aggrieved by any executive act, and imposition alone does not violate fundamental rights. Ref: Justice Athar Minallah.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 138 NI Act: Cheque Presented Without Endorsing Part Payment
records.heading: No section 138 NI Act offence arises where a cheque is presented for the full amount despite part payment
records.text: Indian Supreme Court held that no offence under s. 138 NI Act is made out where a cheque is presented for the full amount without endorsing a part payment made after issue, as the sum is not a legally enforceable debt. Part payments must be endorsed under s. 56 NI Act, after which the balance may be presented.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Official Accommodation: Bar on Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Official accommodation matters are challengeable only before the forums provided, failing which under Article 199
records.text: Orders made or proceedings taken regarding official accommodation under the applicable rules and policies cannot be challenged before any court except the forums provided therein. Where no forum is provided, a High Court may exercise power under Art. 199 of the Constitution if satisfied. Ref: Govt of Pakistan, Ministry of Housing & Works through Joint Estate Officer, Peshawar v. Malik Safeer Ahmed (C.P. 361-P/2018, decided 18.08.2022); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Govt of Pakistan, Ministry of Housing & Works through Joint Estate Officer, Peshawar v. Malik Safeer Ahmed (C.P. 361-P/2018, decided 18.08.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive and Sentence in Brutal Murder
records.heading: Weak motive loses significance in a brutal murder and the death sentence may be awarded
records.text: Weakness or non-proof of motive loses significance in a barbarous murder, and the alternate sentence of life imprisonment under s. 302(b) PPC is not inflexible where the killing displayed brutality. Homicides committed out of human frailty differ from ferocious killings, and in a proved brutal murder courts should not hesitate to award the death sentence. Ref: Muhammad Faisal v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 76 of 2020; Murder Reference No. 14 of 2020, heard 14.09.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Faisal v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 76 of 2020; Murder Reference No. 14 of 2020, heard 14.09.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 9 CPC and Cooperative Society Act
records.heading: Jurisdiction of civil courts under section 9 CPC and the Cooperative Society Act is noted without a holding
records.text: Authority on the jurisdiction of civil courts under s. 9 CPC read with s. 17 of the Undesirable Cooperative Society Act, 1993. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2022 LHC 6948; Harmooz Khan etc v. Abdul Azeem Khan etc (Civil Revision 115692/17, decided 27.09.2022); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Harmooz Khan etc v. Abdul Azeem Khan etc (Civil Revision 115692/17, decided 27.09.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeal Against Consent Decree: Exceptions
records.heading: A consent decree is appealable only in the stated exceptional cases
records.text: A consent decree is appealable in stated exceptions: appeal by a non-party to the compromise, no consent or no compromise at all, invalidity such as want of jurisdiction, dispute on the nature of compromise, decree exceeding the agreement, consent given under mistake or procured by fraud, or non-compliance with O. XXIII R. 3 CPC. Ref: 2022 LHC 6940; Asif Naeem v. Mst Bilqees Fatima etc (Civil Revision 60443/22, decided 04.10.2022); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Asif Naeem v. Mst Bilqees Fatima etc (Civil Revision 60443/22, decided 04.10.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 157 CrPC Cannot Bar Registration of FIR
records.heading: The SHO has no discretion to refuse registration of an FIR on information of a cognizable offence
records.text: Section 157 CrPC read with Rule 24.4 of the Police Rules cannot be employed before registration of a case under s. 154 CrPC. On information of a cognizable offence the SHO has no discretion to inquire into its credibility and refuse registration, and must register the case and then investigate. Ref: 2022 LHC 6953; Arsalan Raza v. JOP Gujrat etc (Criminal Proceedings 9549/21, decided 07.09.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Arsalan Raza v. JOP Gujrat etc (Criminal Proceedings 9549/21, decided 07.09.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Exhibition of Document Is Not Proof
records.heading: Exhibition of a document is distinct from its proof and the relying party must prove it under the QSO
records.text: Under Art. 72 QSO, exhibition of a document is distinct from its proof. A document does not stand proved merely because it was exhibited, even without objection, and the party relying on it must prove it under the Qanun-e-Shahadat. A document passes through three stages: filing, admission in evidence, and proof or disproof. Ref: 2022 CLC 686.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Transgender Person's Entitlement to Family Pension
records.heading: A transgender person is entitled to family pension as the unmarried daughter of the deceased
records.text: A transgender person, being the unmarried daughter of the deceased father, is entitled to family pension under s. 2(e) of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Civil Servant (Pension) Rules, 2021, with reference to Arts. 4 and 25 of the Constitution and ss. 4 and 16 of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2018. Ref: Rukhsar v. Government of KP (W.P. No. 1277-A of 2021, decided 22.09.2022).
records.title: Rukhsar v. Government of KP (W.P. No. 1277-A of 2021, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Attestation of Financial Instruments: Arts. 17 and 79
records.heading: Instruments on financial obligations must be attested by two men or one man and two women
records.text: Under Art. 17(2)(a) QSO, an instrument reduced to writing on financial or future obligations must be attested by two men or one man and two women. Art. 79 QSO prescribes the procedure for proving execution of a document required by law to be attested. Ref: 2022 LHC 6959; Niamat Bibi v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 1148-13, decided 29.09.2022); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Niamat Bibi v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 1148-13, decided 29.09.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Arts. 117 and 122 QSO
records.heading: The burden stays on the prosecution and Article 122 QSO operates only after the elements are proved
records.text: Under Art. 117 QSO the accused is presumed innocent and the burden stays on the prosecution. Art. 122 operates only after the prosecution proves the elements of the offence, and then requires only evidence of facts especially within the accused's knowledge sufficient to create doubt. It cannot relieve the prosecution of its duty. Ref: Muhammad Arslan v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 584 of 2022; Murder Reference No. 46 of 2022, decided 04.10.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arslan v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 584 of 2022; Murder Reference No. 46 of 2022, decided 04.10.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 122 QSO Does Not Shift Prosecution Burden
records.heading: Article 122 QSO does not relieve the prosecution of its burden of proving guilt
records.text: In a criminal case the burden is on the prosecution and Art. 122 QSO does not relieve it of that duty. The Article covers exceptional cases where facts are especially within the accused's knowledge, and it cannot undermine the rule that the prosecution must prove guilt subject to express statutory exception. Ref: Muhammad Arslan v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 584 of 2022; Murder Reference No. 46 of 2022, decided 04.10.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arslan v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 584 of 2022; Murder Reference No. 46 of 2022, decided 04.10.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 63-A: Defection and Presidential Reference
records.heading: A vote cast against party direction by a defecting member is not counted under Article 63-A
records.text: In the Art. 186 reference on Art. 63-A, objections to maintainability were rejected. The majority held that a vote cast against party direction by a defecting member is not counted, that Parliament is to fix the period of disqualification, and that party direction comes from the parliamentary party, not the party head. Short order issued 17.05.2022. Ref: Reference No. 1 of 2022 (Reference by the President under Article 186 seeking interpretation of Article 63-A); Constitution Petition No. 9 of 2022 (short order 17.05.2022); Justice Munib Akhtar.
records.title: Reference No. 1 of 2022 (Reference by the President under Article 186 seeking interpretation of Article 63-A); Constitution Petition No. 9 of 2022 (short order 17.05.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Direct Appeal Against Acquittal Treated as Special Leave
records.heading: A direct appeal against acquittal may be treated as a petition for special leave under section 561-A CrPC
records.text: A complainant who filed a direct appeal against acquittal without seeking special leave under s. 417(2) CrPC, admitted by the High Court, could be rescued under s. 561-A CrPC and the appeal treated as an application for special leave from the date of admission. A litigant should not suffer for the mistake of counsel or the court office. Ref: 2021 YLR 1641.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Appellate Court's Duty on Burden of Proof
records.heading: The appellate court must examine the burden of proof and the prosecution must stand on its own legs
records.text: In appeal the High Court must examine every aspect in light of Arts. 117 to 122 QSO on the burden of proof. Even if the defence version fails, the prosecution has to stand on its own legs. Ref: 2021 YLR 1641.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Arts. 117 and 122 QSO
records.heading: The burden of proving guilt cannot shift unless the legislature expressly provides and Article 122 applies afterwards
records.text: The accused is presumed innocent and the burden of proving guilt beyond doubt lies on the prosecution and cannot be shifted unless the legislature expressly so provides. Once the prosecution establishes the elements of the offence, the burden shifts under Art. 122 QSO to produce evidence of facts especially within the accused's knowledge. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 857.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Arts. 117 and 122 QSO
records.heading: The prosecution bears the burden of proving guilt and Article 122 QSO applies only to exclusive knowledge
records.text: The burden of proving guilt beyond doubt lies on the prosecution and cannot be shifted to the accused unless the legislature expressly so commands. If the prosecution establishes the elements of the offence, the burden shifts under Art. 122 QSO to produce evidence of facts especially within the accused's exclusive knowledge. Ref: 2021 YLR Note 102.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Contents of Documents: Art. 72
records.heading: The contents of a document are best proved by the document itself under Article 72 QSO
records.text: Under Art. 72 QSO the contents of a document may be proved by primary or secondary evidence. The best evidence of the contents is the document itself, and law requires its production in proof of its contents. Ref: 2022 SCMR 842.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Petitioners Left on Bail Pending Leave
records.heading: Petitioners who surrendered may remain on earlier bail bonds pending leave to appeal against cancellation
records.text: Where the High Court had cancelled bail granted by the Additional Sessions Judge in a s. 302/34 PPC case and the order needed further examination, petitioners who surrendered before the Supreme Court were allowed to remain on their earlier bail bonds during the pendency of the petition for leave to appeal. Ref: PLD 1991 SC 382.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Magistrate Disagreeing with Cancellation Report
records.heading: A Magistrate's order disagreeing with a cancellation report is judicial and revisable
records.text: A Magistrate's order disagreeing with a cancellation report and summoning the accused is a judicial act, revisable under ss. 435 and 439 CrPC and open to review under Art. 199. A s. 173 report is only the Investigating Officer's opinion and does not bind the court. Constitutional petition dismissed. Ref: 2011 YLR 2587.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Cannot Decide Guilt or Cancel FIR
records.heading: Police cannot decide guilt or cancel an FIR without a Magistrate's order
records.text: Investigation under s. 4(1) CrPC means only collection of evidence, and determining guilt or innocence rests with the courts. Section 63 CrPC and Rule 24.7 of the Police Rules, 1934 bar discharge or cancellation of an FIR without a Magistrate's order. The High Court order based on the Investigating Officer's opinion was set aside and the appeal allowed. Ref: PLD 2006 SC 316.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report Order Not Revisable
records.heading: A Magistrate's order on cancellation of a case pending investigation is administrative and not revisable
records.text: A Magistrate's order on discharge of an accused or cancellation of a case pending investigation is an administrative order, not revisable under ss. 435 and 439-A CrPC. A Magistrate acts judicially when he forms an opinion on summoning an accused under s. 204 CrPC. The Additional Sessions Judge's order was set aside as without jurisdiction. Ref: 2016 PCrLJ 1783.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Revision Against Order Agreeing with Cancellation Report
records.heading: Revision is not maintainable against a Magistrate's executive order agreeing with a cancellation report
records.text: A criminal revision is not maintainable against the executive order of a Judicial Magistrate agreeing with the police cancellation report in an FIR under s. 406 PPC. The order passed in revision was not sustainable. Ref: 2018 PCrLJ 823.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Discharge Under S. 63 CrPC Distinguished from Cancellation
records.heading: Discharge of an accused under section 63 CrPC differs from cancellation of a case and needs reasons
records.text: Cancellation of a case, which ends police investigation, differs from discharge of an accused under s. 63 CrPC. A Magistrate ordering discharge must apply his mind to the allegations, the evidence and the defence plea, examine police diaries and record reasons. Subject to R. 6 of the Lahore Rules and Orders, he may discharge suo motu when the accused is produced for remand under s. 167 CrPC. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1393.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Magistrate Must Apply Mind to Cancellation Report
records.heading: A Magistrate must apply his mind to a cancellation report and pass a speaking order
records.text: A Magistrate acting under s. 173(3) CrPC on a cancellation report must not pass a mechanical order or merely stamp police proceedings, and must show on what material he agrees and check compliance with R. 24.7 of the Police Rules, 1934. The petition was allowed and the Magistrate directed to pass a fresh speaking order. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1038.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Governing Principles
records.heading: Exceptionally strong reasons are required to cancel bail granted on a tentative assessment
records.text: Once bail is granted on a tentative assessment of evidence, exceptionally strong reasons are required to cancel it. Grounds include a patently illegal or erroneous bail order causing miscarriage of justice, misuse of bail, interference with prosecution witnesses or investigation, likelihood of absconding, repetition of offence, and fresh incriminating material. Ref: 2022 SCMR 660.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Non-Appearance and Fresh Bonds
records.heading: Cancellation of bonds for non-appearance needs only fresh bail bonds where a superior court granted bail
records.text: Where the High Court granted pre-arrest bail in a s. 324/34 PPC case and the trial court later cancelled bonds for non-appearance, the only requirement was fresh bail bonds, since the trial court could not recall a superior court's bail. The accused came from a far flung area, and the complainant had no objection. Appeal allowed and pre-arrest bail granted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 660.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documentary Evidence Preferred Over Oral Evidence
records.heading: Where evidence conflicts, oral evidence gives way to documentary evidence
records.text: Documentary evidence carries much weight, and where there is a contest the oral evidence gives way to the documentary evidence. Ref: 2021 YLR 2245.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Evidence Includes Cross-Examination
records.heading: Evidence in section 342 CrPC includes cross-examination and its incriminating circumstances must be put to the accused
records.text: The word evidence in s. 342 CrPC means examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination under Arts. 2(c), 71 and 132 QSO. Circumstances appearing in cross-examination or re-examination that are against the accused must also be put to him. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 1147.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Evidence Includes Cross-Examination
records.heading: Circumstances in cross-examination and re-examination against the accused must be put to him under section 342
records.text: The word evidence in s. 342 CrPC covers examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination under Arts. 2(c), 71 and 132 QSO. Circumstances in cross-examination or re-examination that are against the accused must be put to him to enable him to explain. Ref: 2020 MLD 1202.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hearsay Evidence Cannot Sustain Conviction
records.heading: Hearsay evidence cannot be the basis of a conviction for qatl-i-amd
records.text: In a reappraisal of evidence in a qatl-i-amd case under s. 302(b) PPC, hearsay evidence under Art. 71 QSO cannot be made the basis of a conviction. Ref: 2019 SCMR 872.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Defective S. 342 Statement: Retrial
records.heading: Failure to put incriminating evidence under section 342 CrPC vitiates trial and is not curable
records.text: All incriminating evidence, including circumstances in cross-examination and re-examination, must be put to the accused under s. 342 CrPC. Failure to do so illegally vitiates the trial and is not curable under s. 537 CrPC. The judgment in a s. 396 PPC case was set aside and the case remanded for retrial from the stage of s. 342 statements. Ref: 2017 YLR 2284.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Party Producing Witness: Presence During Evidence
records.heading: A party wishing to be present during his witness's evidence must testify first or be excluded
records.text: Under Arts. 130 and 133 QSO, a person who wishes to be present while the evidence of his witness is recorded must either record his own statement and be cross-examined first or be excluded while other witnesses' evidence is recorded. Ref: 2021 PLC 224.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Order of Witnesses and Cross-Examination: Consent Order
records.heading: Evidence by affidavit and cross-examination proceeded on a consent order within the time fixed
records.text: Under Art. 130 QSO and O. XIX CPC, the Supreme Court directed the matter to proceed on a consent order for affidavits-in-evidence and cross-examination of witnesses preferably on the same date, without undue adjournments, within the three months fixed by the High Court. Petition converted into appeal and disposed of. Ref: 2019 SCMR 1104.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Audio or Video Recording of Evidence: No Present Need
records.heading: A mere wish for audio or video recording of evidence does not justify judicial innovation on procedure
records.text: The procedure of Chap. XXV CrPC for recording evidence in writing is comprehensive and time-tested, and a mere desire for audio or video recording without urgency and utility does not justify judicial innovation. The issue needs thorough examination of feasibility and resources, and any procedure adopted would have to apply generally. Ref: PLD 2006 Kar 629.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Recording Evidence Through Modern Devices
records.heading: Evidence may also be preserved through modern devices in addition to recording under Chapter XXV CrPC
records.text: A Judge need not record evidence on audio cassette, but in appropriate cases evidence may also be preserved through modern devices in addition to recording under Chap. XXV CrPC. With the Presiding Officer controlling the device and stopping inadmissible evidence, Arts. 131 and 133 QSO are not violated. Ref: PLD 2006 Kar 629.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination by Co-Defendant
records.heading: A co-defendant adversely affected by a witness's evidence may cross-examine that witness
records.text: Under Arts. 132 and 133 QSO a party has a right to cross-examine if adversely affected, so a co-defendant may cross-examine a witness. Evidence affecting a co-defendant's interest cannot be relied on against him without giving him the opportunity to cross-examine. Ref: 2022 YLR 868.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: No Recall for Further Cross-Examination
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC permits recall for re-examination but not for further cross-examination
records.text: Section 540 CrPC allows a court to summon or recall a witness for re-examination for just adjudication, but does not provide for recalling a witness for further cross-examination, which is not permissible. The High Court set aside the lower appellate court's order re-summoning two prosecution witnesses and allowed the petition. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1558.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Examination Only on Matters in Cross-Examination
records.heading: Re-examination is limited to matters arising in cross-examination
records.text: Re-examination can be directed only to explain matters arising in cross-examination, not matters deposed in examination-in-chief. Where the Investigating Officer had not yet been cross-examined, there was no ground for re-examination and s. 540 CrPC could not be invoked. Ref: 2019 YLR 768.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Examination Before Cross-Examination Not Proper
records.heading: Cross-examination precedes re-examination under Articles 132 and 133 QSO and not the reverse
records.text: Section 540 CrPC empowers the court to re-examine a witness but does not prescribe the order, while Arts. 132 and 133 QSO prescribe the mode. The High Court directed that cross-examination be conducted first, then re-examination, with re-cross-examination allowed if the defence wished. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 883.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Indecent and Prolonged Cross-Examination
records.heading: Prolonged cross-examination of a hapless witness and insulting questions should be avoided
records.text: Under Arts. 132(2) and 146 QSO, lengthy cross-examination of a hapless witness and questions that add insult to injury should be avoided. Prolonged cross-examination to lead a witness into error should be deprecated, and courts should shun uncharitable treatment of witnesses. Ref: 2018 YLR Note 119.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Complainant's Right to Cross-Examine Court Witness
records.heading: In a complaint case police witnesses in the challan are court witnesses open to cross-examination by both parties
records.text: Where a complaint case accompanies the State case, the police witnesses listed in the challan are treated as court witnesses and both parties may cross-examine them. The trial court's refusal to let the complainant cross-examine the Sub-Inspector was set aside and he was to be treated as a court witness. Ref: 2016 MLD 1747.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confronting Witness with Previous Statement
records.heading: The defence may confront a witness with his previous statement to impeach credibility
records.text: Under Arts. 132 and 140 QSO the defence is not confined to facts stated in examination-in-chief and may question the witness to impeach credibility. The accused cannot be denied the right to confront the complainant with his previous statement, and its value is judged at final judgment. Ref: 2015 PCrLJ 26.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Suggestions in Cross-Examination Not Admissions
records.heading: Suggestions put in cross-examination by counsel of an acquitted accused are not admissions
records.text: Suggestions put in cross-examination by counsel of an acquitted accused, even if they suggest an incriminating fact, are not an admission of fact or guilt unless proved by independent evidence, and may be the result of inarticulate cross-examination. Ref: 2014 YLR 2116.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Line of Cross-Examination No Inference Against Accused
records.heading: No inference arises against an accused from the line of cross-examination without clear client instructions
records.text: Under Arts. 132 and 133 QSO, where questions are not shown to have been put on the clear instructions of the client, no inference can be drawn against the accused from the line of cross-examination, and the prosecution cannot claim any benefit. Ref: 2013 YLR 2105.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Judge's Power to Question Witnesses: Art. 161
records.heading: A trial court may question witnesses under Article 161 QSO only with caution and in aid of justice
records.text: A trial court has ample authority under Art. 161 QSO to put questions to witnesses, but must exercise it with caution and solely in aid of justice without disturbing equality in the scales. The court is responsible neither for prosecution nor defence and must stay neutral. Ref: 2021 SCMR 1725.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Court's Power to Summon Evidence: Art. 161 and S. 540
records.heading: The court may put questions and order production of necessary evidence under Article 161 and section 540
records.text: Under Art. 161 QSO and s. 540 CrPC the court may put questions or order production of necessary evidence, and failure to use them where needed may cause miscarriage of justice. Section 265-F(2) CrPC obliges the court to ascertain names of persons likely to know the facts, and the court need not confine itself to the evidence under the s. 173 report. Ref: 2012 YLR 325.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Entrusted Bail Application
records.heading: A Sessions Judge cannot withdraw or transfer an urgent bail application once entrusted to another judge
records.text: A Sessions Judge may entrust an urgent bail application to another Additional Sessions Judge under s. 17(4) or s. 193(2) CrPC but cannot withdraw it once entrusted, and an entrusted bail application cannot be transferred. The High Court retains power under s. 561-A CrPC or Art. 199. The acting Sessions Judge's transfer order was set aside. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1145.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Defamation Complaint: Cognizance by Sessions Court
records.heading: A Sessions Court cannot take cognizance of a defamation complaint unless sent up by a Magistrate
records.text: Section 193 CrPC bars the Court of Session from taking cognizance in original jurisdiction unless the case is sent up by a Magistrate under s. 190(2). Section 502-A PPC was inserted for expeditious trial of defamation under s. 500 PPC and does not alter the procedure for instituting a complaint. Leave refused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 356.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Complaint Case and Challan Case in Sessions Court
records.heading: A complaint case and a challan case in Sessions Court are consolidated and decided by one judgment
records.text: After taking cognizance, the Sessions Court must process the complaint case and the police report case under ss. 193 and 204 CrPC, dealing with them independently up to that stage, as laid down in Nur Elahi's case (PLD 1966 SC 708). The trial court was directed to proceed accordingly, with both cases consolidated and one judgment announced. Ref: 2008 MLD 728.

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Complaint Under Act Need Not Route Through Magistrate
records.heading: A complaint under the Illegal Dispossession Act is triable by the Court of Session without routing through a Magistrate
records.text: A complaint disclosing contravention of s. 3 of the Illegal Dispossession Act, 2005 is triable by the Court of Session under s. 4 and need not be routed through a Magistrate under ss. 190(2) and 193 CrPC. The CrPC applies to proceedings under the Act wherever required, subject to the Act. Ref: 2006 YLR 2686.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Judge Cannot Take Direct Cognizance
records.heading: A Sessions Judge cannot take direct cognizance of a complaint as a court of original jurisdiction
records.text: A Sessions Judge cannot take direct cognizance of a complaint as a court of original jurisdiction unless the case is sent up by a Magistrate under s. 190(2) or 190(3) read with s. 193 CrPC. The proceedings were quashed, with liberty to file a fresh complaint under s. 190 CrPC. Revision accepted. Ref: 2005 PCrLJ 1496.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supplementary Challan and Cognizance by Sessions Court
records.heading: An accused named in the first incomplete challan need not be named again in a supplementary challan
records.text: An accused named in column 2 of the first incomplete challan need not be named again in a supplementary challan, and the Sessions Court was not barred from taking cognizance under s. 193(1) read with s. 190(3) CrPC. Discharge under s. 169 CrPC is not an acquittal and does not bind the trial court. Ref: 2003 YLR 421.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cognizance by Sessions Court After Magistrate Commitment
records.heading: The Sessions Court takes cognizance under section 193 after a Magistrate sends the case for trial
records.text: Under s. 190(3) CrPC a Magistrate sends the case to the Sessions Court for trial without recording evidence, and the Sessions Court then takes cognizance under s. 193 read with s. 190(1)(a), (b) and (c) CrPC. Ref: 1997 PCrLJ 56.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Questioning of Person Named as Accused in FIR
records.heading: A person named in an FIR may be questioned by police but a confession to police is inadmissible
records.text: A person named in the FIR can be questioned by police and his statement recorded under s. 161 CrPC, and unless a person is accused he cannot claim protection of Art. 20(3) of the Indian Constitution. A confession to police is inadmissible under s. 25 of the Evidence Act, and an admission in a s. 161 statement attracts the bar of s. 162 CrPC. Ref: AIR 2019 SC 3363; Dipakbhai Jagdishchandra Patel v. State of Gujarat and Ors. (Criminal Appeal No. 714 of 2019, decided 24.04.2019); Justice Ashok Bhushan; Justice K.M. Joseph.
records.title: Dipakbhai Jagdishchandra Patel v. State of Gujarat and Ors. (Criminal Appeal No. 714 of 2019, decided 24.04.2019)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Court's Duty Towards Arbitration Agreements
records.heading: Courts should hold a party to an agreed arbitration clause and not allow it to refuse the agreed mode
records.text: Once a party has agreed to arbitration, the court should either facilitate that party in arbitration within the Arbitration Act, 1940 or compel the party to abide by the contract terms. The purpose of arbitration is defeated if a party refuses the agreed mode of dispute resolution, and such a trend must not be encouraged. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1810.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: ICC Rules Do Not Oust Pakistani Courts
records.heading: The ICC Rules do not divest Pakistani courts of jurisdiction in arbitration matters
records.text: The ICC Rules, including Art. 21, do not divest the courts in Pakistan of their jurisdiction in arbitration matters. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1810.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Notice of Filing of Award: S. 14 Arbitration Act
records.heading: Filing an award in the presence of the parties substantially meets the notice requirement under section 14
records.text: Where an award is filed in court in the presence of the parties or their authorised agents, the requirement of notice of signing and making of the award under s. 14 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 is substantially met. Issuing a formal notice is then a mere technicality that cannot vitiate the proceedings. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1810.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Composite Order Making Award Rule of Court
records.heading: A High Court cannot assume grounds not taken against a composite order making an award rule of court
records.text: Where a trial court dismissed objections as time barred and made the award rule of court, the High Court had to examine whether both parts were independently challenged on grounds under ss. 17 and 39 of the Arbitration Act, 1940. It could not assume grounds not taken, and exceeded jurisdiction. Appeal allowed and award made rule of court. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1810.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Grounds for Setting Aside Arbitration Award
records.heading: A court cannot reappraise evidence or make a roving inquiry when asked to set aside an award
records.text: A court cannot reappraise the evidence relied on by the arbitrator or conduct a roving inquiry to find infirmities in the award. Any illegality or infirmity must be apparent on the face of the award, and the court examines the award itself. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1810.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Late Filing of Award: S. 28 Arbitration Act
records.heading: The four month limit for filing an award is not absolute and section 28 allows enlargement
records.text: The four month time limit for filing an award is not absolute, and s. 28 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 allows enlargement. Where the parties were present and did not object to extensions, late filing was not misconduct and did not invalidate the award. Appeal allowed and award made rule of court. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1810.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Witness Without S. 161 Statement: Ss. 265-F and 540
records.heading: A witness without a section 161 statement may be examined under section 265-F or section 540 CrPC
records.text: A witness named in the FIR whose statement was not recorded under s. 161 CrPC may be examined under s. 265-F or s. 540 CrPC, since neither confines the court to witnesses whose s. 161 statements were recorded or who are in the calendar of witnesses. Its evidentiary value is assessed, and it may or may not be acted upon if prejudice is caused to the accused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1882; Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020).
records.title: Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses: Relationship Not a Ground to Discard
records.heading: Relationship with the deceased is no ground to discard a witness without proved enmity
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony unless previous enmity or ill will to falsely implicate the accused is established on the record. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1882; Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020).
records.title: Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Prosecution Evidence
records.heading: Minor discrepancies that do not shake the salient features of the prosecution case are not given undue importance
records.text: Courts must not attach undue importance to minor discrepancies that do not shake the salient features of the prosecution case, and the accused cannot claim a premium on them. Giving weight to insignificant inconsistencies would leave hardly any conviction. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1882; Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020).
records.title: Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Binding Precedent of the Supreme Court
records.heading: A Supreme Court decision binds only where it decides a question of law or enunciates a principle
records.text: To constitute a binding precedent, the Supreme Court must have decided a question of law, or its decision must be based upon or enunciate a principle of law. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1913, 2023 PLC (C.S.) 1.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ss. 16 and 17 CPC: Suit Over Several Properties
records.heading: A suit over several properties may be filed where one of them is situated if the cause of action is the same
records.text: The words any portion of the property in ss. 16 and 17 CPC are not limited to one property. A suit for relief over immovable properties in different court jurisdictions may be filed in any court where one of them is situated, provided the cause of action is the same. Section 17 avoids conflicting decisions and multiplicity. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1846.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: S. 21(e): Unapproved Gratuity Fund Contributions
records.heading: Contributions to an unapproved gratuity fund cannot be deducted under section 21(e) of the Income Tax Ordinance
records.text: Under s. 21(e) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, contributions to an unapproved gratuity fund cannot be deducted in computing income from business. The argument that s. 21(e) does not apply once a contribution is made was held absurd, as it would defeat the requirement of approval. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1943.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Fresh Questions of Law Before Supreme Court
records.heading: Parties cannot raise fresh questions of law in the Supreme Court that were not raised earlier
records.text: The Supreme Court is not a forum for raising fresh questions of law not raised before the Tribunal or High Court. It deprecated introducing a new question without disclosing that it was not raised earlier, and parties must confine themselves to questions raised and decided by the High Court. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1943.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ss. 16 and 17 CPC: Territorial Jurisdiction
records.heading: Sections 16 and 17 CPC allow suit in any court where one of several properties lies
records.text: The words any portion of the property in ss. 16 and 17 CPC cover more than one property. A suit may be filed in any court where one of the properties is situated, if the cause of action is the same. Section 17 aims to avoid conflicting decisions and multiplicity of litigation and gives parties a convenient choice of court. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1846; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Partial Bar of Jurisdiction
records.heading: A plaint cannot be rejected for ouster of jurisdiction where the bar applies to only one prayer
records.text: Where the jurisdiction of the civil court is barred for one prayer but not for others, the plaint cannot be rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC on the ground of ouster of jurisdiction. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1846; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: Delayed S. 164 Statement Naming Accused
records.heading: A delayed section 164 statement naming an unnominated accused without material makes the case one of further inquiry
records.text: The petitioner was not nominated in the FIR and was named by the complainant in a s. 164 CrPC statement a month later, with no source disclosed, no tangible material collected, and empties fired from different weapons. The alleged video interview confession had prima facie no evidentiary value. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, calling for further inquiry. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1954.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Prosecution Evidence
records.heading: Courts must not give undue weight to minor discrepancies and the accused cannot claim a premium on them
records.text: Courts must not attach undue importance to minor discrepancies that do not shake the salient features of the prosecution case, and the accused cannot claim a premium on them. Giving weight to insignificant inconsistencies would leave hardly any conviction. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1907.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Substitution a Rare Phenomenon
records.heading: Substitution of an innocent person for the real culprit is rare, especially without previous enmity
records.text: Substitution is a rare phenomenon, and a complainant would not spare the real culprit who murdered his daughter to falsely implicate the accused without reason, especially with no previous enmity. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was maintained on reliable ocular evidence corroborated by medical evidence. Leave refused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1907.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses: Relationship Not a Ground to Discard
records.heading: Relationship alone does not justify discarding prosecution witnesses where no plausible reason for false implication exists
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony unless previous enmity or ill will to falsely implicate the accused is established. Counsel could point to no plausible reason why the complainant would falsely implicate the convict and spare the real culprit. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1907.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mortgage: Rights of Mortgagor and Mortgagee
records.heading: A mortgage gives the mortgagor a right of redemption and the mortgagee a right to possess
records.text: Authority on the nature of a mortgage as a contract giving the mortgagor a right of redemption and the mortgagee a right to possess if the money is not repaid. These are independent proprietary interests that may be transferred. It refers to s. 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and the Punjab Redemption and Restitution of Mortgaged Lands Act, 1962. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1893.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail Under Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Narcotics Act: Ss. 497 and 498
records.heading: Sections 497 and 498 CrPC apply to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa narcotics offences and bail is the rule under the first proviso
records.text: Sections 497 and 498 CrPC apply to offences under the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2019. Under the first proviso to s. 497(1), bail is the rule even in a prohibitory clause offence, and a woman accused not entitled under s. 497(2) should also be examined under that proviso. The nature of an offence may indicate likelihood of repetition. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1950.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 506(ii) PPC Inapplicable Where Overt Act Follows
records.heading: Section 506(ii) PPC does not apply where intimidation ends in an overt act
records.text: Under ss. 503 and 506 PPC, where criminal intimidation materialises and ends in an overt act, s. 506(ii) PPC is not applicable and only the overt act committed in consequence of the intimidation remains in the field. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1946, 2023 SCMR 734.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is confirmed as further inquiry where a civil suit is pending and most offences are bailable
records.text: Ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed under s. 497(2) CrPC as the case called for further inquiry, with a declaratory suit over the plot pending, possible false implication, most offences bailable, and s. 440 PPC added belatedly. The court may touch on the merits when granting pre-arrest bail. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1946.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal Under Ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC
records.heading: Acquittal under sections 249-A and 265-K is available at any stage but not where conviction is remotely probable
records.text: Under s. 249-A a Magistrate may acquit where the charge is groundless or there is no probability of conviction, and under s. 265-K the court may acquit where there is no probability of conviction. Applications may be taken up at any stage, but if there is a remote probability of conviction the court should record evidence. Petition allowed and the case remanded for evidence. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1861.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sanctity of Acquittal Under Ss. 249-A and 265-K
records.heading: An acquittal under section 249-A or 265-K lacks the sanctity of an acquittal after full trial
records.text: In appeal or revision, an acquittal under s. 249-A or s. 265-K CrPC lacks the sanctity of an acquittal after full trial. The principles for setting aside concurrent acquittals and the presumption of double innocence do not apply, relying on 2005 SCMR 1544 and PLD 1999 SC 1063. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1861.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Rescission and Rectification Distinguished
records.heading: Rectification corrects a mistranscribed instrument while rescission cancels a correctly recorded transaction made under mistake
records.text: Rectification ensures a written instrument accurately reflects the parties' antecedent agreement where it was incorrectly transcribed. Rescission presupposes a correctly transcribed transaction entered into under a mistaken assumption of fact or law, and cancels it retroactively, restoring the parties to their original position. The post attributes this to the Supreme Court of Canada.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post-Mortem Examination
records.heading: A post-mortem delay of about eight hours did not benefit the convict
records.text: A delay of about eight hours in conducting the post-mortem examination was held not beneficial to the petitioner convict. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1931.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Substitution a Rare Phenomenon
records.heading: Substitution is rare and an explained FIR delay does not weaken a conviction on reliable evidence
records.text: Substitution is a rare phenomenon, and a complainant would not spare the real culprit who killed his son and falsely implicate the petitioner without reason. A 2 hours 45 minutes delay in the FIR was explained and the source of light was established. Conviction was maintained, the High Court having converted death to life imprisonment. Leave refused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1931.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses: Relationship Not a Ground to Discard
records.heading: Relationship with the deceased is no ground to discard testimony unless enmity or ill will is established
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony unless previous enmity or ill will to falsely implicate the accused is established on the record. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1931.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Prosecution Evidence
records.heading: Minor discrepancies in prosecution evidence do not justify acquittal and the accused gets no premium on them
records.text: Courts must not attach undue importance to minor discrepancies that do not shake the salient features of the prosecution case, and the accused cannot claim a premium on them. Giving weight to insignificant inconsistencies would leave hardly any conviction. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1931.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage as Primary Evidence
records.heading: CCTV footage stored directly on a hard drive is primary evidence and needs no section 65B certificate
records.text: CCTV footage stored directly on the computer hard drive is original, self generated media and not secondary evidence, so it needs no certification under s. 65B of the Evidence Act, relying on Anwar P.V. v. P.K. Basir ((2014) 10 SCC 473). The conviction for murder was upheld and the appeal dismissed. The post does not name the court. Ref: Justice Sanjiv Khanna; Justice R.K. Gauba.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light Must Be Proved
records.heading: In a night occurrence the prosecution must prove the source of light as a rule of caution
records.text: In a homicide in the dark hours the prosecution must prove the source of light to exclude false implication and wrong attribution of role. This is a rule of caution and not a statutory requirement. Failure to explain the source of light damaged the prosecution case. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1695.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 12(5) Limitation Act: Time for Certified Copies
records.heading: Time for certified copies excludes only the time court officials need to prepare and issue the copy
records.text: Considers whether time taken by a litigant in paying the cost of a certified copy is excluded under newly added s. 12(5) of the Limitation Act. The time requisite covers only the time taken by court officials in preparing and issuing the copy, and where a copy is not delivered on the intimated date the applicant should take a fresh date. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1868.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Common Intention Under S. 38 PPC
records.heading: Common intention under section 38 PPC turns on the material role played during the occurrence
records.text: On common intention under s. 38 PPC, omission of accused names in some recovery documents was police slackness and did not affect strong ocular evidence, and panicked witnesses cannot give photographic narration of roles. Vicarious liability varies with the facts for sentencing, and the touchstone is the material role played during the occurrence. Ref: 2022 LHC 6969; Abdul Aziz v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 547-18, decided 08.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Abdul Aziz v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 547-18, decided 08.09.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Additional Questions to Accused Under S. 342 CrPC
records.heading: Additional questions may be put under section 342 CrPC and unput evidence cannot be used against the accused
records.text: The first part of s. 342 CrPC lets the court ask the accused as many questions as it desires at any time, so additional questions may be put after his statement is recorded. Evidence not put to the accused in his s. 342 statement cannot be used against him, in line with the audi alteram partem principle. Ref: 2022 LHC 6964; Toheed Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 719-17, decided 04.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Toheed Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 719-17, decided 04.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Weapon Not Essential for Conviction
records.heading: Recovery of the weapon is not essential for conviction on trustworthy eye witness evidence
records.text: Recovery of the weapon used is not a sine qua non for conviction. A conviction can rest on a sole eye witness if trustworthy and reliable, and contradictions about the timing of the FIR are no ground to acquit where the case rests on eye witness deposition. Ref: Justice M.R. Shah; Justice Krishna Murari.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Laches in Constitutional Petitions
records.heading: Laches in constitutional petitions depends on the facts and does not bar a challenge on recurring pension rights
records.text: Compilation on the doctrine of laches in constitutional petitions. Laches is applied on the facts of each case and is not a rule of universal application. Quo warranto is discretionary and may be declined for laches. A challenge to a circular on pensionary rights is not hit by laches as pension is a recurring right. Constitutional relief is discretionary and delay is examined on equitable principles. Ref: 2022 PLC (C.S.) 288, 2021 SCMR 1313, 2019 SCMR 1720, 2019 PLC (C.S.) 1375 and others.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Polling Agents: No Verbal Instructions by Polling Officers
records.heading: Polling officers cannot issue verbal instructions on polling agents as they defy Article 218
records.text: Verbal instructions of polling officers concerning polling agents, being detrimental to a fair and transparent process, can neither be issued nor acted upon, as they defy the command of Art. 218 of the Constitution. A polling agent from outside the constituency who is not a voter must give complete identification and particulars to the Presiding Officer with the nomination if required. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 878; Doctor Yasmin Rashid v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc. (W.P. No. 44479 of 2022, heard on 16.7.2022); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Doctor Yasmin Rashid v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc. (W.P. No. 44479 of 2022, heard on 16.7.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Alleged Abduction of Minor, Habitual Litigant
records.heading: A habitual litigant's petition alleging abduction of a minor is dismissed where reports and CDRs contradict him
records.text: In a petition under Art. 199 alleging abduction of a minor, the court relied on reports of the SHO and DPO. The petitioner was found to be a habitual litigant with several criminal cases, CDRs placed the parties in Lahore instead of Jhang, there was no proof of the claimed marriage and the lady denied his claim. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 886; Muhammad Ramzan v. State and 7 others (W.P. No. 32866 of 2022, decided on 19.7.2022); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. State and 7 others (W.P. No. 32866 of 2022, decided on 19.7.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 133 CrPC: Obstructed Public Right of Way
records.heading: A conditional order under section 133 CrPC to open a blocked public right of way was upheld
records.text: Revenue reports established that a right of way in a joint khata, used by the public to reach a mosque, had been blocked by walls. The courts below were justified in making a conditional order under s. 133 CrPC to open the passage. Concurrent findings were not disturbed and the petition under Art. 199 was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 898; Ghulam Siddique v. Additional Sessions Judge, etc. (W.P. No. 18344 of 2019, heard on 1.7.2022); Justice Muhammad Shan Gul.
records.title: Ghulam Siddique v. Additional Sessions Judge, etc. (W.P. No. 18344 of 2019, heard on 1.7.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Aggrieved Person and Alternate Remedy
records.heading: Article 199 cannot be invoked by a person not aggrieved who ignores the statutory remedy
records.text: Where an FIR was registered against the petitioner's subordinates, the petitioner was not an aggrieved party or person. He gave no explanation for not using the definite, time bound statutory remedy. Art. 199 jurisdiction cannot be invoked as a matter of right or routine. Petition dismissed in limine, relying on PLD 1967 SC 569 and PLD 2019 Lahore 373. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 915; Muhammad Saqib v. SHO and another (W.P. No. 12 of 2022, decided on 5.1.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem; Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Muhammad Saqib v. SHO and another (W.P. No. 12 of 2022, decided on 5.1.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Prosecutor's Power Over Addition of Offences
records.heading: Addition of offences against accused falls within the prosecutor's exclusive domain under the Punjab Prosecution Service Act
records.text: Under s. 9(7) of the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service Act 2006, the prosecutor may scrutinise the evidence and the applicability of offences against any or all accused, and the addition or insertion of any offence falls within the prosecutor's exclusive domain. The post also notes that the Magistrate and trial court have several opportunities to rectify a mistake under s. 173 CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 915; Muhammad Saqib v. SHO and another (W.P. No. 12 of 2022, decided on 5.1.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem; Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Muhammad Saqib v. SHO and another (W.P. No. 12 of 2022, decided on 5.1.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance: Female Heir, Gift and Residuaries
records.heading: A full sister excludes descendants of the true grandfather and her post-1964 gift was valid
records.text: A full sister ranks above descendants of the true grandfather in the Table of Residuaries and excludes them. A gift made by the female heir after the 1964 Amendment was valid as she no longer held the estate as a limited owner. Appeals allowed and the trial court's dismissal of the suit restored. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 416; Abdul Khaliq (decd) thr. LRs v. Fazalur Rehman and others (C.As. No. 53 & 54 of 2015, decided on 30.6.2022); Justice Sajjad Ali Shah; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Abdul Khaliq (decd) thr. LRs v. Fazalur Rehman and others (C.As. No. 53 & 54 of 2015, decided on 30.6.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Breach of Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Breach of an agreement to sell is not criminal breach of trust as payment of money is not entrustment
records.text: Breach of a term of an agreement to sell, or a seller's failure to transfer property after receiving the sale consideration, does not constitute criminal breach of trust under s. 406 PPC, as payment of money is not entrustment of property.
