Petition against the bail granted to respondent No. 2 dismissed in limine as a tentative assessment. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1484; Muhammad Musawar Abbasi v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 787-BC of 2022, decided on 20.6.2022); Justice Tariq Mehmood Jahangiri.
records.title: Muhammad Musawar Abbasi v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 787-BC of 2022, decided on 20.6.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secondary Evidence: Memory Card, Arts. 159 and 160
records.heading: Secondary evidence of a memory card is admissible where the complainant withholds it despite notice
records.text: Where the complainant did not produce the memory card despite notice, the accused were entitled to produce secondary evidence under Arts. 159 and 160 QSO. Video clips contradicted the presence of the prosecution witnesses at the scene, raising serious doubt in a s. 302(b) PPC conviction. Appeal allowed; revision and P.S.L.A. dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1459; Muhammad Nazim etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 105079-J, Crl. Rev. No. 105522 & P.S.L.A. No. 105523 of 2017, heard on 1.2.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Nazim etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 105079-J, Crl. Rev. No. 105522 & P.S.L.A. No. 105523 of 2017, heard on 1.2.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Cross-Version Needs Tentative Assessment
records.heading: Treating every cross-version as further inquiry would encourage fabrication so the court must assess the material tentatively
records.text: In a petition for cancellation of post-arrest bail under s. 497(5) CrPC, the court held that treating every cross-version as a case of further inquiry would encourage fabricated cross-versions. Courts must tentatively assess the material on record. The fatal shot was attributed to respondent No. 2 and the material supported the offence. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 229; Muhammad Rafique v. State etc. (Crl.P. No. 301 of 2022, decided on 22.6.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. State etc. (Crl.P. No. 301 of 2022, decided on 22.6.2022)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: S. 6(5) Juvenile Justice System Act: Bail of Juvenile
records.heading: A juvenile over sixteen accused of a heinous offence may not be bailed save on the statutory delay ground
records.text: Considers s. 6(5) of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018 on post-arrest bail of a juvenile over sixteen years accused of a heinous offence such as qatl-i-amd. Such a juvenile may not be released on bail, subject to the statutory ground concerning continuous detention exceeding six months without completion of trial. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 233; Khawar Kayani v. State etc. (Crl. P. No. 345 of 2022, decided on 20.6.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Khawar Kayani v. State etc. (Crl. P. No. 345 of 2022, decided on 20.6.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Hardened, Desperate or Dangerous Criminal: Fourth Proviso s. 497(1)
records.heading: Whether an accused is a hardened criminal depends mainly on the facts and not only on previous cases
records.text: Previous convictions or pending cases may support, but are not the exclusive factor in deciding, whether an accused is a hardened, desperate or dangerous criminal under the fourth proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC. The opinion is formed mainly from the facts and circumstances, including the nature of the offence, its effects, the role of the accused, the manner of commission and his conduct. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 239; Allah Wasaya v. State etc. (Crl. P. No. 440 of 2022, decided on 20.6.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Allah Wasaya v. State etc. (Crl. P. No. 440 of 2022, decided on 20.6.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Medical Contradiction, Single Shot at Non-Vital Part
records.heading: Bail is allowed where the FIR was delayed, the injury suggests a pellet and one shot hit a non-vital part
records.text: Bail granted under s. 498 CrPC in a s. 324 PPC case. The FIR was delayed by nine hours, the 0.5 cm x 0.5 cm injury suggested a pellet and not the weapon alleged, a single shot was fired at a non-vital part (wrist) and no weapon was recovered. Bail allowed on bonds of Rs. 200,000 with one surety. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 243; Ali Raza v. State and others (Crl. P. No. 1262-L of 2021, decided on 21.3.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Ali Raza v. State and others (Crl. P. No. 1262-L of 2021, decided on 21.3.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Nominated Accused, Medical Support
records.heading: Bail is cancelled where the nominated accused had a specific role supported by medical evidence
records.text: Bail cancelled under s. 497(5) CrPC. The respondent was nominated with a specific role in the murder of his father and brother, supported by medical evidence. A witness resiling from her s. 161 CrPC statement and filing a private complaint with a different story did not justify bail. The High Court order was illegal, perverse and arbitrary. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 250; Muhammad Amjad Shahzad v. Muhammad Akhtar Shahzad and another (Crl. P. No. 124 of 2022, decided on 30.3.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Amjad Shahzad v. Muhammad Akhtar Shahzad and another (Crl. P. No. 124 of 2022, decided on 30.3.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Police and Official Witnesses Are Reliable
records.heading: Police and official witnesses are as reliable as private witnesses if unshattered and without animus
records.text: Testimony of police or official witnesses is as good as that of private witnesses, and can sustain a conviction, if it remains unshattered in cross-examination and no animus against the accused is shown. Conviction in this narcotics case was maintained. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 255; Zafar Iqbal v. State (Crl. A. No. 177 of 2022, decided on 27.5.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Zafar Iqbal v. State (Crl. A. No. 177 of 2022, decided on 27.5.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Opium (Poast) Under s. 2(t) CNSA: Sentence Reduced
records.heading: The meaning of opium under section 2(t) CNSA guided reduction of the sentence to the period undergone
records.text: The court examined what constitutes poast or opium under s. 2(t) of the Control of Narcotic Substances Act 1997 in order to fix the quantum of punishment. Conviction upheld but the sentence of imprisonment for life was reduced to the period already undergone. Appeal partly allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 255; Zafar Iqbal v. State (Crl. A. No. 177 of 2022, decided on 27.5.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Zafar Iqbal v. State (Crl. A. No. 177 of 2022, decided on 27.5.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: No Deeper Appreciation of Evidence at Bail Stage
records.heading: Courts do not dig deep into evidence at the bail stage as that is for the trial court
records.text: In a case under s. 11 PECA and ss. 295-B and 298-C PPC concerning blasphemous material shared online, the court held that at bail stage it does not dig deep into evidence or scrutinise factual aspects, which is for the trial court. Bail refused. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 262; Rohan Ahmad and others v. State and others (Crl. Ps. Nos. 1313-L, 1314-L and 1315-L of 2021, decided on 29.4.2022); Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Rohan Ahmad and others v. State and others (Crl. Ps. Nos. 1313-L, 1314-L and 1315-L of 2021, decided on 29.4.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder of Wife: Onus on Husband, Art. 122 QSO
records.heading: A wife's homicidal death in the husband's house places an onus on him but doubts in the case may justify acquittal
records.text: Although the homicidal death of a wife in her husband's house casts a heavy onus on him under Art. 122 QSO, the autopsy findings, the witnesses' conduct, the unchallenged acquittal of a co-accused and doubts in the prosecution case made the appellant's version not safely dismissible. Appeal allowed and the appellant acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 266; Shaukat Hussain v. State (Crl. A. No. 585 of 2020, decided on 14.2.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel; Justice Qazi Muhammad Amin Ahmed.
records.title: Shaukat Hussain v. State (Crl. A. No. 585 of 2020, decided on 14.2.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare of the Child Paramount
records.heading: The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in deciding custody
records.text: The paramount consideration in custody is the welfare of the minor. The court exercises parental jurisdiction and weighs the parents' ability to provide for physical and emotional needs, medical care and a safe home. There is no mathematical formula for welfare. The post also refers to the UNCRC and Arts. 9 and 12. Ref: Raja Muhammad Owais v. Mst. Nazia Jabeen and others (Civil Petition No. 240 of 2021, decided 05.10.2022).
records.title: Raja Muhammad Owais v. Mst. Nazia Jabeen and others (Civil Petition No. 240 of 2021, decided 05.10.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 149 IPC: Abatement of Appeal and Number of Convicts
records.heading: Abatement of an appeal on the death of co-convicts differs from acquittal for the purposes of section 149 IPC
records.text: Indian Supreme Court decision holding that abatement of an appeal on the death of co-convicts is different from acquittal. The effect of the number of convicts falling below five pending appeal against conviction under s. 149 IPC owing to death is therefore different from that of acquittals. Ref: Justice CT Ravikumar; Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302(b) PPC: Alternate Sentence of Life Imprisonment
records.heading: Life imprisonment is the alternate sentence under section 302(b) PPC where motive is not proved beyond doubt
records.text: Imprisonment for life is an alternate sentence under s. 302(b) PPC, and it is for the court to decide in which cases death is awarded. If the projected motive is not proved beyond doubt, the alternate sentence of imprisonment for life is to be awarded. Ref: 2022 MLD 1848.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witness: Corroboration Required
records.heading: It is unsafe to convict on the uncorroborated testimony of a chance witness on a capital charge
records.text: It is unsafe to convict on uncorroborated testimony of a chance witness, especially on a capital charge. His testimony is ordinarily not accepted unless justifiable reasons for his presence at the crime scene at the relevant time are shown, and corroboration must be sought. Ref: Liaquat Ali v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 350-J-2015, decided 22.09.2022).
records.title: Liaquat Ali v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 350-J-2015, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Compulsory Retirement: Modification of Punishment by Tribunal
records.heading: The Service Tribunal cannot modify a punishment imposed after due process unless it is unreasonable or contrary to law
records.text: Compulsory retirement was imposed after due process. The Service Tribunal cannot modify a punishment unless it is unreasonable or contrary to law, and must record reasons with proper application of mind. Travel history without approved leave was proved in the inquiry through IBMS. Ref: Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others v. Nargis Jamal (C.A. 19/2022, decided 06.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others v. Nargis Jamal (C.A. 19/2022, decided 06.10.2022)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-i-Ishhad: Non-Production of A.D. Card
records.heading: Non-production of the A.D. card gives rise to an adverse inference that Talb-i-Ishhad notice was not served
records.text: Failure of the pre-emptor to produce the A.D. card of the registered notice, or to seek leave for secondary evidence on proof of loss, led to an adverse inference that the Talb-i-Ishhad notice was not served on the vendee. The pre-emptor failed the mandatory requirement of law. Ref: 2022 LHC 7043; Muhammad Shafiq Khan v. Muhammad Waryam (Civil Revision 1082-16, decided 21.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Masood Jahangir.
records.title: Muhammad Shafiq Khan v. Muhammad Waryam (Civil Revision 1082-16, decided 21.09.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX CPC: Dismissal for Default After Evidence
records.heading: Dismissal for default under Order IX CPC is not justified where all evidence is on record and arguments were heard
records.text: Where the plaintiffs' entire evidence was already on record and the matter had been argued, dismissal of the suit for default under Order IX CPC was not justified, since the file had been requisitioned by the Appellate Court and returned without a date being fixed. Ref: 2022 LHC 7028; Khalid Iqbal etc. v. Mst. Yasmeen etc. (Civil Revision 1705-15, decided 19.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Masood Jahangir.
records.title: Khalid Iqbal etc. v. Mst. Yasmeen etc. (Civil Revision 1705-15, decided 19.09.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Admission: Art. 34 QSO, Not Conclusive Proof
records.heading: An admission under Article 34 QSO is a relevant fact and not conclusive proof against its maker
records.text: An admission made in ignorance of legal rights has no legal effect. Under Art. 34 QSO an admission is only a relevant fact and not conclusive proof against the maker. A statement agreeing to send signatures or thumb impressions to an expert was not an admission as defined. Ref: 2022 LHC 7034; Zahid Mahmood etc. v. Sabir Hussain (Civil Revision 51659/22, decided 06.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Masood Jahangir.
records.title: Zahid Mahmood etc. v. Sabir Hussain (Civil Revision 51659/22, decided 06.09.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Power of Attorney Holder as Witness in Specific Performance
records.heading: An attorney holder without personal knowledge cannot depose to the principal's acts and dealings in a specific performance suit
records.text: Indian Supreme Court summary of who may give evidence in a suit for specific performance. An attorney holder without personal knowledge can give only formal evidence. He may prove acts he himself did under the power of attorney, but cannot depose for acts and dealings of the principal of which only the principal has knowledge. Ref: Man Kaur (dead) by LRs v. Hartar Singh Sangha (Civil Appeal Nos. 147-148 of 2001, decided 05.10.2010).
records.title: Man Kaur (dead) by LRs v. Hartar Singh Sangha (Civil Appeal Nos. 147-148 of 2001, decided 05.10.2010)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Five Principles for Specific Performance
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary and equitable relief and depends on five stated considerations
records.text: Indian Supreme Court: specific performance is discretionary and equitable relief. The court considers whether a valid concluded contract exists, whether the plaintiff was and is ready and willing, whether he performed his part, whether granting relief is equitable or causes hardship to the defendant, and whether alternative relief such as refund is due. Appeal dismissed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail Versus Setting Aside Bail Order
records.heading: A perverse or illegal bail order may be set aside on grounds distinct from cancellation for misconduct
records.text: Indian Supreme Court: parameters for granting bail differ from those for cancelling it. An order of bail that is perverse, illegal or based on irrelevant material can be set aside by a superior court, which is distinct from cancellation for misconduct or supervening circumstances. The bail order there ignored the parameters under s. 439 Cr.P.C.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Fraud and Protection of Minors and Women
records.heading: Fraud vitiates the most solemn proceedings and courts must protect the rights of minors and women
records.text: Where minors and women are parties, the court must protect their rights. Fraud vitiates the most solemn proceedings and ill-gotten gains cannot be validated. An adverse finding on an issue that a party does not assail attains finality. Ref: 2022 LHC 7058; Hakim Bibi etc. v. Fateh Muhammad etc. (Writ Petition 707-11, decided 28.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Hakim Bibi etc. v. Fateh Muhammad etc. (Writ Petition 707-11, decided 28.09.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: First Responder Under s. 157 CrPC and Rule 25.10
records.heading: A first responder under Rule 25.10 may preserve the scene, secure witnesses and speak to the injured
records.text: Rule 25.10 of the Police Rules 1934 allows a first responder to preserve the scene of crime, record particulars of and secure potential witnesses and obtain information, and arrest culprits nearby until the regular investigator takes over. Speaking to the injured at the hospital was within these functions. Ref: 2022 LHC 7077; Imran v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 1065-19, decided 28.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Imran v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 1065-19, decided 28.09.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXI R. 1 and 2 CPC: Out of Court Payment
records.heading: Out of court payment under Order XXI Rule 1 CPC is valid by bank, money order or signed writing
records.text: Order XXI Rule 1(1)(b) CPC permits out of court payment by bank, postal money order or a payment evidenced in writing signed by the decree-holder or his agent. Revenue stamps are not required. Rule 2(2) is permissive ('may') and no consequence is provided for not informing the court of such payment. Ref: Muhammad Abbas v. Additional District Judge & 2 others (Writ Petition No. 3377 of 2022/BWP, heard on 03.08.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Abbas v. Additional District Judge & 2 others (Writ Petition No. 3377 of 2022/BWP, heard on 03.08.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 100 QSO: Presumption for Thirty Year Old Documents
records.heading: The presumption for a thirty year old document under Article 100 QSO is discretionary and needs conditions to be met
records.text: Before presuming genuineness of a thirty year old document under Art. 100 QSO, the court must be satisfied about its originality, age, proper custody and unsuspicious character, and the original must be before it. The presumption is discretionary and not every document and signature is to be presumed genuine. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1857.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Unperformed Agreement Does Not Create Title
records.heading: A mere agreement creates no title unless acted upon by its executant or by a decree
records.text: A mere agreement does not create title unless acted upon by its executant or by a decree of a competent court. Property not transferred in the executant's lifetime devolves on his legal heirs, so the agreement holder cannot transact as owner and a subsequent agreement to sell by him is invalid and unenforceable. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1857.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Fresh Suit After Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A fresh plaint is allowed after rejection under clauses (a) to (c) of Order VII Rule 11 but not clause (d)
records.text: Where a plaint is rejected under clauses (a) to (c) of O. VII R. 11 CPC the defect can be cured and a fresh plaint filed, subject to limitation. Where rejected under clause (d) as barred by law, a fresh plaint is not envisaged, and withdrawal with permission to file afresh cannot be allowed. High Court judgment set aside. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 716.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Elements of Defamation: Libel and Slander
records.heading: Libel is actionable per se and defamation requires a defamatory imputation referring to the claimant and published
records.text: Defamation is publication of a statement that lowers a person's reputation and takes the forms of libel and slander. Libel is actionable per se and injury is presumed. The claimant must prove that the imputation is defamatory, refers to the claimant and was published to at least one other person. Defamation is defined in s. 3 of the Defamation Ordinance, 2002. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 683; Chief Editor Muhammad Riaz Anjum, etc. v. Dr. Mohammad Shahbaz (R.F.A. No. 140 of 2012, decided 19.05.2022); Justice Muhammad Masood Jahangir; Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Chief Editor Muhammad Riaz Anjum, etc. v. Dr. Mohammad Shahbaz (R.F.A. No. 140 of 2012, decided 19.05.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 167 CrPC: Revision Against Magistrate's Remand Order
records.heading: Revision before the Sessions Judge lies against a Magistrate's order refusing further physical remand
records.text: Revision before the Sessions Judge against a Judicial Magistrate's order refusing further physical remand under s. 167 CrPC is maintainable. The Sessions Judge was directed to decide the revision on merits after hearing the parties. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Islamabad 170.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Habeas Corpus: Custody of Minor and Hizanat
records.heading: A mother has the first right of hizanat of a minor child and habeas corpus remains available despite guardian proceedings
records.text: Under s. 491 CrPC the mother of a minor aged about two had the first right of hizanat and custody was handed to her. Pendency of proceedings before the Guardian Court under s. 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act does not bar a parent lawfully holding custody from seeking recovery, and the High Court exercises parental jurisdiction. Ref: 2020 MLD 1891.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minors: Mother Preferred, Father Abroad
records.heading: Custody of minors goes to the mother where no disqualification exists and the father is abroad
records.text: No ground of disqualification of the mother under Islamic law applied, and the father was living abroad so could not be presumed able to care for the minors. No one is a better guardian than a mother. Orders under s. 491 CrPC and s. 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act were set aside and custody given to the mother. Ref: 2021 MLD 957.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Habeas Corpus: Arrest on Dubious Supplementary Statements
records.heading: Arrest of unnominated detenus on dubious supplementary statements without a manual roznamcha is not sustained in habeas corpus
records.text: In a habeas corpus petition under s. 491 CrPC, detenus who were not nominated in the FIR were arrested on supplementary statements found dubious, and no manual roznamcha was kept as Police Rules 22.3 and 22.4 require. The court stressed that courts must guard the fundamental rights under Arts. 9, 10 and 14. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 593.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Habeas Corpus: Woman in Dar-ul-Aman, Right to Liberty
records.heading: A woman in Dar-ul-Aman who is sui juris may seek release at any stage
records.text: A woman placed in Dar-ul-Aman may at any stage ask for release and cannot be kept there further. The detenue, being sui juris, could not be detained against her wishes and was set at liberty. Questions of the validity of the marriage and the husband's gender must be raised before the Family Court or a criminal court. Ref: PLD 2021 Lah 77.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: S. 9(1) Elections Act: Power to Order Recasting of Votes
records.heading: Section 9 of the Elections Act 2017 allows the Commission to order recasting of votes and not only declare an election void
records.text: Under s. 9 of the Elections Act 2017 the Commission can call on voters to recast their votes, which differs from declaring the whole election void under repealed s. 103AA of the Representation of the People Act 1976. The Explanation to s. 9(1) allows only one special case for declaring an election void. Ref: 2021 SCMR 1675; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Mushir Alam.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 218(2)(b): Office of ECP Member and Reading In
records.heading: The office of an ECP Member under Article 218(2)(b) is not quasi-judicial and reading in is available
records.text: The office of a Member of the Election Commission under Art. 218(2)(b) is not quasi-judicial. The Constitution is a living document to be given dynamic and progressive interpretation, and the doctrine of reading in is available once a constitutional defect is found. The case was to be listed for rehearing before adopting that approach. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 39.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: ECP Has No Power on Pre-Election Disqualification of Returned Candidate
records.heading: The Commission cannot decide alleged pre-election disqualification of a returned candidate but may declare a poll void
records.text: The Commission has no jurisdiction under Art. 218(3) or s. 9(1) of the Elections Act 2017 to decide alleged pre-election qualification or disqualification of a returned candidate. Its power to declare a poll void is implied in s. 9(1), and in the Explanation the word 'election' may be read as 'poll'. Ref: 2022 SCMR 42.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Appreciation of Evidence of Hostile Witness
records.heading: The evidence of a hostile witness cannot be discarded as a whole
records.text: Indian Supreme Court, summarising C. Muniappan v. State of Tamil Nadu: evidence of a hostile witness cannot be discarded as a whole, and relevant admissible parts may be used by the prosecution or the defence. Omissions and discrepancies do not justify disregarding the entire evidence.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Evidence of Hostile Witness Not Rejected in Toto
records.heading: A witness's evidence is not wholly rejected because the prosecution treated him as hostile
records.text: Evidence of a prosecution witness cannot be rejected wholly because the prosecution treated him as hostile. It is not effaced from the record and can be accepted to the extent found dependable on careful scrutiny, as summarised in C. Muniappan v. State of Tamil Nadu. Ref: Rameshbhai Mohanbhai Koli & Ors v. State of Gujarat (Criminal Appeal No. 1166 of 2009, decided 20.10.2010).
records.title: Rameshbhai Mohanbhai Koli & Ors v. State of Gujarat (Criminal Appeal No. 1166 of 2009, decided 20.10.2010)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Murderer Cannot Inherit From the Victim
records.heading: An heir who murders the person from whom he would inherit loses the right to inherit
records.text: Under the Islamic law of inheritance an heir found guilty of murdering the person from whom he would inherit loses the right to inherit. Ref: 2022 LHC 7112; Muhammad Ayub v. Muhammad Farooq (Civil Revision 889-18, decided 28.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Ayub v. Muhammad Farooq (Civil Revision 889-18, decided 28.09.2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Rectification Jurisdiction of Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue
records.heading: The Appellate Tribunal must determine the mistake, correct the original order and record reasons in rectification
records.text: The Appellate Tribunal must follow three steps in rectification: determine the mistake under the guidelines in 1992 PTD 570, correct it in the original order, and record reasons for the change of result. Ref: 2022 LHC 7179; The CIR v. M/s. Lahore Rubber Store (Sales Tax Reference 80-16, decided 17.10.2022); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: The CIR v. M/s. Lahore Rubber Store (Sales Tax Reference 80-16, decided 17.10.2022)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: S. 114 Land Revenue Act: Recovery of Microfinance Loans
records.heading: Section 114 of the Land Revenue Act gives Revenue Officers no power to recover microfinance loans
records.text: Section 114 of the Land Revenue Act 1967 gives Revenue Officers no power to recover loan amounts of microfinance institutions from defaulters. Ref: 2022 LHC 7132; Muhammad Siddique v. Govt. of the Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 7737-22, decided 18.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Siddique v. Govt. of the Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 7737-22, decided 18.10.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Second Writ After Withdrawal of First: Clean Hands
records.heading: A second writ on the same cause after withdrawal of the first is precluded and clean hands are required
records.text: A first writ petition on the same cause was withdrawn after the petitioners were confronted with legal infirmities, so a fresh petition is precluded under sub-rule (3), relying on 1996 SCMR 1433. A petitioner in constitutional jurisdiction must come with clean hands and not conceal material facts. Ref: 2022 LHC 7172; Azeem Khan etc. v. Govt. of the Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 2363-22, decided 08.09.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Azeem Khan etc. v. Govt. of the Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 2363-22, decided 08.09.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal With Liberty to Sue Afresh
records.heading: Permission to sue afresh after withdrawal requires a formal defect or sufficient grounds and cannot be mechanical
records.text: A plaintiff may withdraw a suit at any time, but permission to file afresh under O. XXIII R. 1(2) CPC requires a formal defect (a technical defect) or other sufficient grounds. Permission cannot be granted mechanically and the court must examine the application. Ref: 2022 LHC 7165; M/s Best Way Cement Ltd v. Yasir Saleem etc. (1645-21, decided 08.09.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: M/s Best Way Cement Ltd v. Yasir Saleem etc. (1645-21, decided 08.09.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Decree: No Revocation, s. 21(3) Family Courts Act
records.heading: A khula decree does not become ineffective by revocation and only by reconciliation within 90 days
records.text: Section 7(3) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 allows revocation of talaq within 90 days, but s. 21(3)(b) of the Family Courts Act 1964 does not use the word revoke. A khula decree becomes ineffective only if reconciliation is effected within 90 days by mutual arrangement of the spouses. Ref: 2022 LHC 7147; Liaqat Ali v. Chief Officer Municipal Committee etc. (Family 70550/21, decided 19.10.2022); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. Chief Officer Municipal Committee etc. (Family 70550/21, decided 19.10.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Adoption and Custody Claim by Real Parents
records.heading: Adoption does not bar the real parents from claiming custody of the child
records.text: Adoption does not bar the real parents from claiming custody of the child from the adoptive parents, as the welfare of the child lies with the real parents. Ref: 2022 LHC 7138; Mst. Shahnaz Mai v. ADJ etc. (Writ Petition 7422-22, decided 04.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Mst. Shahnaz Mai v. ADJ etc. (Writ Petition 7422-22, decided 04.10.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Possession in Specific Performance Decree Not Claimed in Plaint
records.heading: A plaintiff may claim possession in a specific performance suit under section 22 of the Specific Relief Act
records.text: Indian Supreme Court on s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act 1963, inserted on the Law Commission's recommendation, allowing a plaintiff to claim possession in a specific performance suit to avoid multiplicity. Appeal allowed, High Court order set aside, and the Executing Court to ensure the decree is executed with delivery of possession.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth in Matriculation Certificate
records.heading: A suit to correct date of birth in a Matriculation Certificate failed as time barred
records.text: Correction of the date of birth in a Matriculation Certificate was declined as the suit was barred by time and the evidence on record was grossly misread. Ref: 2022 LHC 7195; BISE Multan v. Muhammad Afzal (Civil Revision 50-22, decided 19.10.2022); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: BISE Multan v. Muhammad Afzal (Civil Revision 50-22, decided 19.10.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Surrender of Dower After Imran Anwar Khan
records.heading: Islam prescribes no ceiling on dower surrendered on khula after the Federal Shariat Court decision
records.text: Applying Imran Anwar Khan (PLD 2022 FSC 25), which struck down the ceiling in s. 10(5) and (6) of the Act as repugnant to Islam with effect from 01.05.2022, Islam prescribes no specific ceiling for dower surrendered on khula. The quantum is to be decided on the principles drawn from that judgment. Ref: 2022 LHC 7184, PLD 2025 Lah 551; Muhammad Mohsin Raza v. ADJ etc. (Writ Petition 12505-20, decided 17.10.2022); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Muhammad Mohsin Raza v. ADJ etc. (Writ Petition 12505-20, decided 17.10.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Admissibility of Video Evidence as Document
records.heading: Video evidence obtained by forensic techniques is documentary evidence subject to the rules on proof of documents
records.text: Video evidence, tapes and photographs produced by forensic techniques are documentary evidence in electronic form, so the principles governing admissibility of documents apply. The court relied on Art. 139 QSO, which allows it to ask a witness to support a statement with a document. Ref: 2022 LHC 7201; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Video and Snaps as Documentary Evidence
records.heading: Video evidence not played in court nor copied to the accused requires remand for lawful proof
records.text: Video evidence and photographs obtained through forensic techniques are documentary evidence, so the rules on proof of documents apply. Where the video was not played in court nor copied to the accused, the appeals were disposed of and the case remanded so the evidence is brought on record lawfully, with copies to the accused, in camera exhibition, cross-examination and fresh s. 342 Cr.P.C. questioning, then decision afresh within four months. Ref: 2022 LHC 7201; Numan alias Nomi v. The State (Crl. A. 364/2020, with Crl. A. 380/2020, 382/2020 and 407/2020); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Numan alias Nomi v. The State (Crl. A. 364/2020, with Crl. A. 380/2020, 382/2020 and 407/2020)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Presumptions and Evidential Burden on Accused
records.heading: A presumption places an evidential burden on the accused discharged on the balance of probabilities
records.text: A presumption provides that once a primary fact is proved, the presumed fact is taken as proved unless the opponent rebuts it. In certain situations an accused bears an evidential, not legal, burden. His standard of proof is the civil balance of probabilities, discharged through cross-examination of prosecution witnesses or defence evidence. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1005.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minors: Blood Relationship and Welfare
records.heading: Custody preference by closeness of blood relationship is departed from only for strong reasons tied to the minor's welfare
records.text: Under ss. 17 and 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act, preference by closeness of blood relationship is the general principle, and departing from it requires very strong and compelling reasons tied to the welfare of the minor. Custody with the maternal grandfather after the mother's suspicious death was maintained. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 32.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Previous Probation Conviction Not a Bar
records.heading: An earlier probation conviction under the Probation Ordinance is no ground to refuse bail
records.text: The accused, alleged to hold 510 grams of charas, had earlier been placed on probation under s. 5 of the Probation of Offenders Ordinance 1960 without breach or proceedings under s. 7. He was entitled to s. 11(2) of the Ordinance and the earlier conviction could not be a ground to refuse bail. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: 2022 MLD 1310; Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Confession s. 164 CrPC: Right to Counsel
records.heading: A Magistrate must inform the accused of the right to counsel before recording a section 164 confession
records.text: The right to counsel is part of the right to fair trial under Art. 10A and recognised in s. 340 CrPC, so before recording a confession under s. 164 the Magistrate must inform the accused of it and allow him to engage counsel. A Special Magistrate had no jurisdiction to convict on that basis. Conviction set aside and the FIR deemed pending. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 176 CrPC Inquiry Judicial and Subject to Revision
records.heading: A section 176 CrPC inquiry is judicial and revisable and cannot opine on guilt
records.text: An inquiry by a Magistrate into cause of death under s. 176 CrPC is judicial in nature, so revision before the Sessions Court is competent. The inquiry report cannot opine on guilt or innocence, and registration of an FIR or a private complaint remains an independent right not hedged by the inquiry. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 860.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Public Documents: Store-Room Register Not Duly Proved
records.heading: A public register entry without proper certification under Article 87 QSO is not duly proved
records.text: In a heroin case, a page of Register No. XIX (Store-Room Register) was produced without proper certification under Art. 87 QSO, with no police station or district named. Without formal proof, its admission was improper and the entry was rejected. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1334.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ex-Officio Justice of Peace: Directions Under s. 22-A
records.heading: The Ex-Officio Justice of Peace performs judicial functions and may direct enforcement of its earlier order
records.text: A direction of the Ex-Officio Justice of Peace to the Regional Police Officer to enforce an earlier order under ss. 22-A and 22-B CrPC and proceed against the SHO under the Police Order 2002 rests on lawful authority. The functions are judicial and not executive, administrative or ministerial. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1779.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Electricity Theft: FIR and Conditional Cognizance s. 462-O
records.heading: An FIR may be registered for electricity theft but the court takes cognizance conditionally under section 462-O
records.text: Offences in Chapter XVII-B PPC on electricity theft are cognizable and non-bailable, so an FIR may be registered, but s. 462-O introduces conditional cognizance by the court. Cognizance is a later stage than FIR and investigation, and the technical report on theft requires expert opinion. Ref: 2022 MLD 1091.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Object and Scope of Summoning Witnesses
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC serves fair trial and due process under Article 10-A as an exception to the adversarial system
records.text: Section 540 CrPC is an exception to the adversarial system, with an inquisitorial element. Its object is to serve as an overarching part of the criminal justice system rooted in the right to fair trial and due process under Art. 10-A of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 319.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Witnesses Not in Calendar
records.heading: The trial court may summon any person as a witness at any stage under section 540 CrPC
records.text: The trial court may summon any person as a witness at any stage under s. 540 CrPC, with discretion at preliminary stages and a duty where evidence is essential to a just decision. The witness keeps his prosecution or defence character. The trial court's course was upheld and it must supply copies of the statements to the accused and complainant for cross-examination. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 319.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Plea of Self-Defence Not Established
records.heading: A self-defence plea fails where the other party was unarmed and repeated shots showed excess force
records.text: The accused admitted the occurrence but his self-defence version failed as the complainant party carried no weapon and repeated shots showed excess force. He did not appear as his own witness under s. 340(2) CrPC nor file a written statement under s. 265-F. The prosecution had proved its case. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 591.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Non-Appearance of Witness: Call as Court Witness
records.heading: A court should call a non-appearing witness as a court witness and not rely only on presumption
records.text: In a criminal trial the court should not rely merely on presumption for non-appearance of a witness but should call him as a court witness to obtain direct testimony. Art. 129(g) QSO is more akin to civil proceedings than criminal ones. Ref: 2022 YLR 805.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Falsus in Uno, Falsus in Omnibus
records.heading: Witnesses disbelieved against one set of accused cannot be accepted against others save by abundant caution
records.text: If witnesses are disbelieved against one set of accused, their testimony cannot be accepted against other accused on the principle of falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus, yet under the principle of abundant caution an accused can be singled out. The post is cut short. Ref: 2022 YLR 805.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post Mortem Examination
records.heading: Delay in post mortem due to administrative reasons or unavailability of a doctor does not benefit the accused
records.text: Delay in conducting the post mortem examination may be due to an administrative issue or unavailability of a doctor. In such circumstances the benefit cannot be extended to the accused and the prosecution cannot be held responsible. Ref: 2022 YLR 805.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Corroboration and Standard of Proof
records.heading: Corroboration needs independent evidence implicating the accused in a material particular and the standard is proof beyond reasonable doubt
records.text: Corroboration needs relevant, credible, admissible and independent evidence implicating the accused in a material particular, and not confirmation of every circumstance. The standard before a criminal court is proof beyond reasonable doubt, and the post discusses the formulations 'sure of guilt' and a 'floating standard'. Ref: 2022 YLR 805.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Meaning of Motive
records.heading: Motive is the emotion that led to the act and not the external exciting cause
records.text: Motive in the correct sense is the emotion supposed to have led to the act. The external fact sometimes called the motive is merely the possible exciting cause of that motive and is not identical with it. Ref: 2022 YLR 805.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 149 IPC Misuse: Allahabad High Court Bail
records.heading: Section 149 IPC should not be applied unless the circumstances show a common object of all accused
records.text: The Allahabad High Court observed that s. 149 IPC is among the most misused provisions in investigation, and, finding on the facts that the ingredients were not made out, considered the bail plea. Courts should not implicate accused unless circumstances show all shared a common object of the unlawful assembly. Ref: Sanjeev @ Kallu Sethiya v. State of U.P. (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 18458 of 2022); Justice Siddharth.
records.title: Sanjeev @ Kallu Sethiya v. State of U.P. (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 18458 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Reference to Provincial Standing Medical Board
records.heading: A vague allegation of political pressure on the Medical Board is rejected and a reference to the Provincial Board is necessary
records.text: Under ss. 464 and 465 CrPC, an allegation that political pressure was exerted on the District Standing Medical Board was rejected as vague and unsubstantiated for want of details. The Board's opinion was found deficient and a reference to the Provincial Standing Medical Board was held necessary to reach the truth. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1293.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inquest Report Under R. 25.39 Police Rules
records.heading: The inquest report is prepared in the prescribed format and given to the doctor before post-mortem
records.text: Under R. 25.39 of the Police Rules, 1934, the inquest report is prepared in the prescribed format and given to the doctor before the post-mortem to counter tampering with police record. The court also found the recovered .12 bore carbine of no help to the prosecution because the PFSA report showed no match with the crime empties. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1695.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A: Police Harassment of Unlicensed Oil Depot
records.heading: A licence is mandatory for an oil depot and the High Court made no finding on illicit acts
records.text: The petitioner ran an oil depot but showed no licence, which is mandatory under R. 28 of the Pakistan Oil Rules 2016, and the matter fell within OGRA and its inspection officers. Section 285 PPC was not attracted to sale of adulterated petroleum. The High Court made no finding on illicit acts and left him free to take legal proceedings. Ref: 2022 YLR 2102.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Framing of Charge: Object and Scope
records.heading: The framing of charge begins the trial and tells the accused precisely what the prosecution intends to prove
records.text: The trial commences on framing of charge, whose purpose is to tell the accused precisely what the prosecution intends to prove against him. The charge is the foundation of the prosecution case. A trial in contravention of mandatory provisions on its conduct is vitiated. Ref: 2022 YLR 2123.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Bail Refused: Cheque Issued Under Compromise Deed
records.heading: Bail is refused where a cheque under a compromise deed filed in court was drawn on a closed account
records.text: Bail was refused in a s. 489-F PPC case where the cheque was issued under a compromise deed filed in court to obtain bail, drawn on an account already closed or closed afterwards, which defeats a solemn undertaking to the court. Bail in a non-bailable offence is a concession. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2022 YLR 2176; Justice Sardar Ejaz Ishaq Khan.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Outside Prohibitory Clause: Rule and Exceptions
records.heading: Outside the prohibitory clause bail is the rule and refusal the exception
records.text: In offences not within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC bail is the rule and refusal the exception, which operates where there is likelihood of absconding, tampering with evidence or repetition of the offence, or where the accused is a previous convict. Ref: 2022 YLR 2176; Justice Sardar Ejaz Ishaq Khan.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Striking Off Right to Lead Evidence
records.heading: A court may strike off the right to lead evidence of a party deliberately prolonging the matter
records.text: A court may strike off the right to produce evidence of a party deliberately avoiding it and prolonging the matter, under O. XVII R. 3 CPC. A last opportunity order is a firm promise of no further adjournment that the court must enforce. Dismissal of the suit was upheld. Ref: 2022 YLR 2174.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: No Appeal Against Interim Order of Family Court
records.heading: No appeal or revision lies against an interim order of the Family Court
records.text: The Family Courts Act 1964 is a special law that provides one appeal against the final order, so no appeal or revision lies against an interim order of the Family Court or Executing Court. The CPC and Qanun-e-Shahadat do not apply to Family Court proceedings. The Additional District Judge erred in entertaining the appeal. Ref: 2022 YLR 2114.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Uncertain Time of Occurrence: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Inconsistent and unestablished time of occurrence gives the accused the benefit of doubt
records.text: In a s. 302(b) PPC case, the prosecution was unsure of and failed to establish the time of occurrence. The FIR application, the complainant's evidence, the inquest report, the post-mortem report and the Investigating Officer's cross-examination gave inconsistent times. Charge not proved beyond doubt; appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 YLR 2086.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Non-Compliance After Leave to Defend
records.heading: Non-compliance with a surety bond direction after leave to defend justifies recall of leave and decree of the suit
records.text: In a summary suit on a dishonoured cheque under O. XXXVII Rr. 2 and 3 CPC, leave to defend was granted on a direction to furnish a surety bond. The defendant did not comply, so the Trial Court recalled the leave and decreed the suit. The appellate court found no illegality or irregularity in the decree. Ref: 2022 CLC 1815.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Incriminating Evidence Not Put
records.heading: Failure to put incriminating material to the accused under section 342 CrPC is fatal to conviction
records.text: Examination under s. 342 CrPC is a bounden duty of the Trial Court and not a formality. Evidence or circumstances not put to the accused cannot be used against him. In a s. 9(c) CNSA case (1500 grams of charas), failure to put incriminating material, including the charas, was fatal and the conviction was not upheld. Ref: 2022 MLD 1805.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Presence of Eyewitnesses: Acquittal
records.heading: Doubtful presence of eyewitnesses living away from the scene supports acquittal and the acquittal was not perverse
records.text: In a murder case under ss. 302, 324, 109 and 148 PPC, the injured witnesses lived away from the place of occurrence and the complainant was not a witness to the inquest or post-mortem reports, so their presence was doubtful. The acquittal was not perverse, and benefit of doubt goes to the accused, relying on 2010 SCMR 491. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1830.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: No Justification for Presence
records.heading: A complainant with no plausible reason for presence at the spot is a chance witness and the accused is acquitted
records.text: In a s. 302/34 PPC case, the complainant lived a kilometre from the spot and gave no plausible reason for being there, so he was a chance witness. Witnesses did not intervene against two empty-handed accused, and evidence disbelieved against a co-accused could not be believed against the present accused. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1804.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report: Revision Against Magistrate Order
records.heading: Only judicial orders of a Magistrate are revisable and administrative orders may be examined under section 561-A
records.text: Only judicial orders of a Judicial Magistrate are revisable under s. 439 CrPC. Administrative orders are not revisable and may be examined under s. 561-A CrPC. The post notes that in declining the s. 173 cancellation report the Magistrate summoned no accused and only directed submission of a s. 173 report. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1770.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Juvenile Exactly Sixteen: Bail Under S. 6(3)
records.heading: An accused exactly sixteen at the time of the offence is treated as accused of a bailable offence
records.text: An accused who was exactly sixteen on the date of the offence is not 'more than sixteen years of age', so s. 6(3) of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018 applies and he is treated as accused of a bailable offence. Juvenility is judged by the date of the crime and not the date of arrest. Appeal allowed and bail granted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1806.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Challenge to S. 124-A PPC Dismissed
records.heading: A petition challenging the vires of section 124-A PPC is not maintainable where the petitioner was not charged
records.text: A petition under Art. 199 challenging the vires of s. 124-A PPC (sedition) was dismissed as not maintainable. The petitioner's counsel stated she had not been charged under s. 124-A. The petitioner was left to raise the matter in Parliament if so advised. Ref: Dr Shireen Mehrunnisa Mazari v. Federation of Pakistan (W.P. No.3549/2022, decided 23.09.2022); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Dr Shireen Mehrunnisa Mazari v. Federation of Pakistan (W.P. No.3549/2022, decided 23.09.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 302(b) PPC: Reliable Ocular Account Upheld
records.heading: Conviction under section 302(b) PPC is maintained on a reliable ocular account corroborated by medical and forensic evidence
records.text: Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was maintained where the ocular account was reliable and the witnesses' presence natural, medical evidence corroborated it, no reason for false implication was shown, and the Forensic Science Laboratory report matched the crime empty to the pistol recovered. The High Court had converted death to life imprisonment, and no further leniency was shown. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1882; Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020).
records.title: Sajid Mehmood v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 398 of 2020)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Notice for Violating Order of 25 May
records.heading: The Supreme Court declined an interim order against the long march and sought a reply in contempt proceedings
records.text: The Supreme Court again declined the Federal Government's request for an interim order restraining the long march and sought a reply from Imran Khan in contempt proceedings for alleged violation of its order of 25 May. A five-member bench heard the matter. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior v. Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi (Criminal Original Petition No.148/2022 in Const.P.19/2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Syed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior v. Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi (Criminal Original Petition No.148/2022 in Const.P.19/2022)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Revision Against Orders of Anti-Terrorism Court
records.heading: A revision lies against orders of the Special Court under the Anti-Terrorism Act
records.text: Authority for the proposition that a revision lies against orders of the Special Court under the Anti-Terrorism Act. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 427, PLD 2019 Lah 436, PLD 2018 Lah 836.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 188: Scope of Review Jurisdiction
records.heading: Review under Article 188 succeeds only where the error alters the outcome and makes the judgment bad law
records.text: Review jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Art. 188 operates in a limited area. A review does not succeed merely because a material error has crept into the judgment. It is allowed only when the error alters the outcome and renders the judgment bad law. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Meaning of Service of Pakistan
records.heading: Service of Pakistan is wider than civil service and covers functions connected with the affairs of the Federation
records.text: The terms service of Pakistan and civil servant are not synonymous; service of Pakistan is wider and civil service is a sub-category. A person is in the service of Pakistan if performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Federation. An employing entity must exercise public or sovereign power, be under effective government control and be mainly government financed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Art. 240: Merit in Appointments to Service
records.heading: Article 240 requires appointments to the service of Pakistan to follow law and merit
records.text: Art. 240 is the bedrock for appointments to the service of Pakistan, and appointing authorities must ensure appointments strictly accord with the relevant laws. The principles of merit, non-discrimination, transparency and fairness also emanate from fundamental rights, especially Art. 18. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 25: Reasonable Classification
records.heading: Article 25 permits classification resting on an intelligible differentia with a rational nexus to its object
records.text: Art. 25 permits differential treatment of persons not similarly placed under a reasonable classification. The classification must rest on an intelligible differentia having a rational nexus with the object sought to be achieved. Only if this test is met can distinct treatment be sustained. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Legislative History as Aid to Construction
records.heading: Legislative history is an aid to construction only where the statute is ambiguous or leads to absurdity
records.text: Reference to legislative history is permissible only as an aid where the statute is ambiguous or obscure, or its literal meaning leads to an absurdity. The post also states that the Supreme Court ordinarily does not enter into purely academic exercises. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Prospective or Retrospective Effect of Supreme Court Judgments
records.heading: Supreme Court judgments operate prospectively unless declared to operate retrospectively
records.text: Supreme Court judgments operate prospectively but may operate retrospectively if so declared. There is no binding rule that all judgments take effect only from the date of pronouncement. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Separation of Powers: Minority View
records.heading: Separation of powers means reciprocal checks and balances and is the source of judicial review
records.text: Minority view: no branch of government is omnipotent and each acts within the Constitution. Separation of powers means reciprocal checks and balances, not walls between branches. Legislative authority does not include passing unconstitutional laws, so the principle is the source of judicial review. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial Review of Legislation: Minority View
records.heading: Courts should try to save the constitutionality of legislation before striking it down
records.text: Minority view: courts must tread carefully in reviewing legislation. They should first try to save its constitutionality by tools such as reading down or reading out, and interfere only where the law opposes constitutional values and fundamental rights. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Pro Negante Rule and Equally Divided Bench
records.heading: The pro negante rule does not apply to the final decision of a case by an equally divided Supreme Court
records.text: Minority view: the rule that an equal division of appellate judges affirms the lower court's judgment does not apply to the final decision of a case by the Supreme Court, because of the second proviso to O. XI R. 1 of the Supreme Court Rules 1980. The rule is confined to division on a point of law where a majority agrees on the final decision. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Judgment in Rem: Notice to Affected Persons
records.heading: A judgment in rem binds non-parties and public notice may be ordered so affected persons can intervene
records.text: Minority view: a judgment in rem binds parties and non-parties alike. Separate notice to every likely affected person is neither practicable nor required by law. For fair trial and due process, the court may order public notice through the press or another mode so affected persons may seek to intervene. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Parliamentary Debates as Aid to Interpretation
records.heading: Parliamentary debates may be referred to for ascertaining the mischief and purpose of legislation
records.text: Minority view: parliamentary debates, especially the speech of the mover of the Bill or the Standing Committee chairman or members, may be referred to for ascertaining the mischief the legislation sought to remedy and its object and purpose. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 25(1): Scope of Reasonable Classification
records.heading: Article 25(1) allows reasonable classification and the challenger must show it is arbitrary
records.text: Minority view: Art. 25(1) does not prohibit reasonable classification based on an intelligible differentia with a rational nexus to the object of the law. Such classification is not offended by lack of mathematical nicety or some resulting inequality. The challenger bears the burden of showing it is arbitrary. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Presumption of Constitutionality of Statutes
records.heading: A law is presumed constitutional and construed to save its validity with severance where possible
records.text: Minority view: there is a presumption in favour of the constitutionality of a law, and a law should be construed to save its validity. The challenger bears the burden of showing violation. Where possible, the offending part is severed and the remainder sustained unless the Legislature would not have enacted it independently. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Disinheritance (Aaq) Unknown to Islamic Law
records.heading: Islamic law has no disinheritance and an Aaq Nama does not disentitle a child from inheritance
records.text: Islamic law has no institution of abandonment (aaq) depriving a son or daughter of inheritance. Even if parents disinherit a child, the child remains entitled to a share on their death, and an Aaq Nama does not disentitle a person from inheritance. Ref: PLD 2013 Lah 464, 2011 YLR 697.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Review of Judgment on Dismissed Government Employees
records.heading: A five-member bench heard review petitions on the restoration of dismissed government employees with a dissent
records.text: Review petitions against the judgment of 17.08.2021 in C.A. No.491 of 2012 were heard by a five-member bench, with Syed Mansoor Ali Shah J dissenting. The Urdu summary states that the Court restored government employees dismissed between 1996 and 1999. The report includes majority and minority views on review, Art. 25 and judicial review. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1691; Hadayat Ullah and others v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Civil Review Petitions Nos. 292 to 302, 351 to 432, 442 to 456 of 2021, decided 17.12.2021); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Sajjad Ali Shah; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Qazi Muhammad Amin Ahmed; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Hadayat Ullah and others v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Civil Review Petitions Nos. 292 to 302, 351 to 432, 442 to 456 of 2021, decided 17.12.2021)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Power to Summon Witnesses and Record
records.heading: Family Courts may summon any witness or record in the interest of justice beyond the parties' lists
records.text: Under the proviso to s. 7(2) read with ss. 15 and 17(4) of the Act, Family Courts may summon any witness or record in the interest of justice. Their powers are not confined to the witnesses and record in the lists tendered by the parties. Ref: Mst. Shehla Tahir and another v. Learned Judge Family Court, Lahore and another (W.P. No.17989 of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Shehla Tahir and another v. Learned Judge Family Court, Lahore and another (W.P. No.17989 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance: Quantum Depends on Husband's Income
records.heading: The quantum of maintenance depends on the known and other sources of the husband's income
records.text: In maintenance matters, fixation of the quantum of maintenance depends on the known sources and other sources of income of the husband or father. Ref: Mst. Shehla Tahir and another v. Learned Judge Family Court, Lahore and another (W.P. No.17989 of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Shehla Tahir and another v. Learned Judge Family Court, Lahore and another (W.P. No.17989 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report Only Through Superintendent of Police
records.heading: A cancellation report must reach the Magistrate through the Superintendent of Police under Rule 24.7
records.text: A cancellation report must be sent to the Magistrate through the Superintendent of Police, who alone is authorised to send it. Rule 24.7 of the Police Rules 1934 is mandatory, and what the law requires in a particular manner must be done in that manner. The Magistrate's power to cancel a case derives from s. 173(3) CrPC. Ref: 2022 LHC 7240; Ehsan Ullah Chaudhary v. The State etc. (52999/22, decided 22.09.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Ehsan Ullah Chaudhary v. The State etc. (52999/22, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Examination of Injured by Standing Medical Board
records.heading: Lahore High Court directions govern re-examination of an injured person by the Standing Medical Board
records.text: Authority on directions of the Lahore High Court to Magistrates, police and the health department regarding re-examination of an injured person through the District or Provincial Standing Medical Board. Ref: PLJ 2018 CrC 770.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345 CrPC: Compromise at Bail Stage
records.heading: A compromise at bail stage in section 345(1) offences remains effective at trial even if the complainant resiles
records.text: For offences in s. 345(1) CrPC, a compromise made at the bail stage remains effective at trial and entitles the accused to acquittal even if the complainant later resiles. For offences in s. 345(2), it is effective only for bail, and acquittal requires the complainant or injured to make the compromise statement before the Trial Court. Ref: PLD 2016 SC 347.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: One FIR Per Incident
records.heading: A separate FIR cannot be registered for every new version of the same incident
records.text: After the first information of a cognizable offence is registered as an FIR, the matter becomes a case, and every later step in the investigation is a step in that case. A separate FIR cannot be registered for every new version of the same incident. Reliance is placed on R. 24.5 of the Police Rules 1934. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 595.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Arrest Not Mandatory After FIR
records.heading: Arrest is not mandatory after registration of an FIR unless the situation on the ground warrants it
records.text: Arrest of the accused is not mandatory after registration of an FIR. Unless the situation on the ground warrants, arrest is to be deferred until sufficient material or evidence is available prima facie satisfying the investigating officer of the correctness of the allegations or the suspect's involvement. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 595.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Summoned Accused Need Not Seek Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: An accused summoned under section 204 CrPC cannot apply for pre-arrest bail
records.text: An accused summoned by a court under s. 204 CrPC in a private complaint is not arrested by issue of summons and has no apprehension of arrest, so cannot apply for pre-arrest bail. The court may require a bond for future appearance under s. 91 CrPC, with or without sureties. Ref: 2014 SCMR 1762.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Qisas and Ta'zir: Distinct Regimes
records.heading: Qisas and Ta'zir are separate regimes and sections 306 to 311 PPC apply only to Qisas cases
records.text: A case is one of Qisas under s. 304 PPC only on a voluntary and true confession before a competent court, or the requisite witnesses established through tazkiya-tul-shuhood under Art. 17 QSO. Other cases are Ta'zir. Qisas and Ta'zir are separate, mutually exclusive regimes, and ss. 306 to 311 PPC apply only to Qisas cases. Ref: PLD 2015 SC 77.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Compounding Murder: Capacity of Deceased Heir
records.heading: An heir's capacity to compound a Ta'zir case ends on his death and does not pass to his heirs
records.text: In a Ta'zir case, an heir's capacity to compound is exhausted on that heir's death and does not pass to his own heirs, who are not heirs of the victim. Only surviving direct heirs of the victim may compound, and their compromise is effective even if the deceased heir's heirs do not agree. Ref: PLD 2019 SC 461.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 203 and 204 CrPC Orders: Remedy Is Revision
records.heading: Orders under sections 203 and 204 CrPC are judicial and challengeable by revision and not by writ
records.text: Orders under s. 203 CrPC dismissing a direct complaint, and orders under s. 204 CrPC taking cognizance and issuing summons or warrants, are judicial orders. They are challengeable by revision and not by writ or appeal. Ref: PLD 2016 SC 55.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Complete Chain Required
records.heading: On circumstantial evidence the chain must be complete and point only to the guilt of the accused
records.text: In circumstantial evidence cases the chain of circumstances must be complete and lead only to the irresistible conclusion that the accused alone committed the crime, each circumstance being conclusive and consistent only with guilt. Under s. 30 of the Indian Evidence Act a co-accused's confession is not substantive evidence, and conduct alone under s. 8 cannot found a conviction. Ref: Subramanya v. State of Karnataka (Criminal Appeal No. 242 of 2022, decided 13.10.2022).
records.title: Subramanya v. State of Karnataka (Criminal Appeal No. 242 of 2022, decided 13.10.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11(d) CPC: Plaint Rejection and Res Judicata
records.heading: Only the plaint is considered under Order VII Rule 11(d) and a res judicata plea needing examination falls outside it
records.text: Under O. VII R. 11(d) CPC only the statements in the plaint are considered, not the written statement or other material, and no evidence or disputed question is entered into. A res judicata plea needing examination of the pleadings, issues and decision in the previous suit is beyond the scope of R. 11(d). Ref: Srihari Hanumandas Totala v. Hemant Vithal Kamat (Civil Appeal No. 4665 of 2021, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 565).
records.title: Srihari Hanumandas Totala v. Hemant Vithal Kamat (Civil Appeal No. 4665 of 2021, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 565)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Against Rent Tribunal Order for Fraud
records.heading: An order of the Rent Tribunal obtained by fraud may be challenged under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: Since s. 31 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 allows the Rent Tribunal to invoke the CPC, a person aggrieved by a Tribunal order obtained by fraud may challenge it by an application under s. 12(2) CPC. The ouster in ss. 26 and 34 of the Act does not apply. Ref: Ghulam Ali v. Rana Babar Khan etc. (W.P. No.49479 of 2020, heard 26.10.2022).
records.title: Ghulam Ali v. Rana Babar Khan etc. (W.P. No.49479 of 2020, heard 26.10.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Negligence of Public Functionaries: S. 337-H(1)
records.heading: A public functionary is criminally liable for negligence only if grossly negligent and the act is the causa causans
records.text: A public functionary or employee incurs criminal liability for negligence only if grossly negligent to a degree amounting to a criminal act or omission, and the act occasioning injury is causa causans. Where a thunderstorm damaged a pole and the police report negated negligence, s. 337-H(1) PPC was not attracted. Petition accepted and the impugned order set aside. Ref: Muhammad Irfan etc. v. ASJ/Ex-officio Justice of Peace etc. (Writ Petition No. 46486/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan etc. v. ASJ/Ex-officio Justice of Peace etc. (Writ Petition No. 46486/2021)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Change of Advocate in Review Petition
records.heading: The scope of Order XXVI Rule 6 of the Supreme Court Rules on change of advocate is noted without a holding
records.text: Authority on the scope of O. XXVI R. 6 of the Supreme Court Rules 1980 regarding change of advocate in a review petition. The post lists the matter as a suit for declaration and states no holding. Ref: Amjad Hussain v. Nazir Ahmad & others (C.M.A.3610/2022, decided 24.10.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Amjad Hussain v. Nazir Ahmad & others (C.M.A.3610/2022, decided 24.10.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Admissibility and Probative Value
records.heading: Admissibility and probative value of a dying declaration are noted without a stated holding
records.text: Authority on admissibility and probative value of a dying declaration. The appeal arose from a High Court judgment setting aside a conviction under ss. 302, 376, 341 and 448 of the Indian Penal Code in which the victim was set on fire. The extract gives no holding. Ref: State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai @ Pandav Rai (Criminal Appeal No. 1441 of 2022); Justice Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud.
records.title: State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai @ Pandav Rai (Criminal Appeal No. 1441 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal: Limited Interference
records.heading: An acquittal is reversed only in the rarest cases of absolutely wrong or perverse reasoning
records.text: Under Art. 136 of the Indian Constitution the Supreme Court is cautious in interfering with an acquittal, especially one confirmed up to the High Court. It reverses only in rarest cases where the High Court acquitted on an absolutely wrong process of reasoning, a legally erroneous and perverse approach, ignoring vital facts. Ref: Subramanya v. State of Karnataka (Criminal Appeal No. 242 of 2022).
records.title: Subramanya v. State of Karnataka (Criminal Appeal No. 242 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Tests for Conviction on Circumstantial Evidence
records.heading: Circumstances must be firmly established and form a chain so complete that only the accused could have committed the crime
records.text: No straightjacket formula governs circumstantial evidence, but the circumstances must be cogently and firmly established, of definite tendency unerringly pointing to guilt, and conclusive. Cumulatively they must form a chain so complete that within all human probability the crime was committed by the accused alone.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Examination of Informant and Weapon Recovery
records.heading: Non-examination of the informant and non-recovery of the weapon do not justify discarding an eyewitness
records.text: Non-examination of the original complainant does not justify discarding the testimony of an eyewitness. Recovery of the weapon is not a sine qua non for conviction where there is direct eyewitness evidence, and contradictions about the timing of the FIR do not justify acquittal. Appeals allowed and the accused directed to surrender. Ref: State through the Inspector of Police v. Laly and Ors. (Criminal Appeal Nos. 1750-1751 of 2022, decided 14.10.2022); Justice M.R. Shah; Justice Krishna Murari.
records.title: State through the Inspector of Police v. Laly and Ors. (Criminal Appeal Nos. 1750-1751 of 2022, decided 14.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appeal Against Conviction Under S. 302/149 IPC
records.heading: A conviction under section 302/149 IPC was confirmed and the appeal dismissed
records.text: The appellant, tried with others under ss. 302/149, 307/149, 147 and 148 IPC and convicted under s. 302/149 IPC with life imprisonment, appealed against the High Court's dismissal of his appeal. The Supreme Court found the High Court justified in confirming conviction and sentence and dismissed the appeal. Ref: Gurmail Singh & Anr. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. (Criminal Appeal No. 965 of 2018, decided 17.10.2022); Justice C.T. Ravikumar; Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia.
records.title: Gurmail Singh & Anr. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. (Criminal Appeal No. 965 of 2018, decided 17.10.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Restoration of Execution Petition Under S. 151 CPC
records.heading: An Executing Court may restore an execution petition dismissed for non-prosecution under section 151 CPC
records.text: Although no specific CPC provision covers it, an Executing Court may restore an execution petition dismissed for non-prosecution in exercise of its inherent powers under s. 151 CPC. Absence of an express provision does not curtail the court's jurisdiction to meet the ends of justice. Ref: Muhammad Inam Bhatti v. Syed Muhammad Sibtain (C.R.No.52637 of 2020, heard 04.10.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Inam Bhatti v. Syed Muhammad Sibtain (C.R.No.52637 of 2020, heard 04.10.2022)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt: Non-Compliance of Court Order
records.heading: A contempt matter on non-compliance of a court order is listed without a stated holding
