records.text: Listed under contempt of court and non-compliance of a court order, in the matter of the Federation against Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi. The post states no holding. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior v. Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi (Crl.O.P.148/2022, decided 02.11.2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior v. Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi (Crl.O.P.148/2022, decided 02.11.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Impleading Legal Heirs in Service Appeal
records.heading: The conditions for impleading legal heirs in a service appeal are discussed without a stated holding
records.text: Authority discussing s. 2(b) of the Civil Servants Act 1973, ss. 2(a) and 4 of the Service Tribunals Act 1973, the maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona, and O. XXII R. 1 CPC on the conditions for impleading legal heirs in a service appeal. The post gives no holding. Ref: Azra Bibi v. General Manager, Personnel (CPO), Pakistan Railways HQ, Lahore & others (C.P.2628/2019, decided 10.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Azra Bibi v. General Manager, Personnel (CPO), Pakistan Railways HQ, Lahore & others (C.P.2628/2019, decided 10.10.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial Restraint in Educational Institution Matters
records.heading: Courts leave disciplinary and administrative matters of educational institutions to their professional expertise
records.text: In educational matters, disciplinary, administrative and policy matters are best left to the professional expertise of those running the institutions, unless there is a blatant violation of fundamental rights or the law. Ref: Aina Haya v. Principal Peshawar Model Girls High School-I, Peshawar & others (C.P.2824/2019, decided 20.01.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Aina Haya v. Principal Peshawar Model Girls High School-I, Peshawar & others (C.P.2824/2019, decided 20.01.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Proportionality in Dismissal: Five Passports
records.heading: Dismissal of a civil servant who travelled on five passports is proportionate and reviewable for reasonableness
records.text: The court may judicially review an executive decision on grounds of proportionality and reasonableness. A civil servant who travelled without NOC on five passports, deceiving and impersonating a businessman, also committed an offence under s. 6 of the Passports Act 1974. No latitude was shown for conversion of the penalty. Ref: Ijaz Badshah v. The Secretary, Establishment Division, Govt. of Pakistan, Islamabad & others (C.P.3813/2019, decided 12.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ijaz Badshah v. The Secretary, Establishment Division, Govt. of Pakistan, Islamabad & others (C.P.3813/2019, decided 12.10.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Upgradation of Post Is Not a Vested Right
records.heading: Upgradation of a post is a policy matter and not a vested right
records.text: Upgradation of a post is not a vested right but stems from a policy decision for a particular set of employees under a scheme, and is distinct from promotion. To justify it, the competent authority must establish that the department needs restructuring or reform, or that service exigency in the public interest requires it. Ref: Amanullah Khan v. Hospital Director, KTH(MTI), Peshawar & others (C.P.2092/2019, decided 12.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Amanullah Khan v. Hospital Director, KTH(MTI), Peshawar & others (C.P.2092/2019, decided 12.10.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Dismissal for Fraud and Misappropriation of Public Money
records.heading: Proved fraud and misappropriation of public money justify dismissal despite long service
records.text: Where fraud and misappropriation of public money are proved, the delinquent cannot be exonerated. Long service is no ground to convert dismissal into compulsory retirement, and the punishment was proportionate to the misconduct. Ref: Allah Ditta v. Deputy Postmaster General (Admn), Office of the Postmaster General, Northern Punjab Circle, Rawalpindi & another (C.P.2602/2019, decided 05.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Allah Ditta v. Deputy Postmaster General (Admn), Office of the Postmaster General, Northern Punjab Circle, Rawalpindi & another (C.P.2602/2019, decided 05.10.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Union Council Jurisdiction Over Divorce Notice
records.heading: The Union Council with jurisdiction over a divorce notice is where the wife resided at pronouncement
records.text: The issue was a Union Council Chairman's assumption of jurisdiction over a divorce notice while proceedings were pending in a US court, with reference to ss. 2(b) and 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 and Rule 3(b) of the West Pakistan Rules. The post indicates the relevant Union Council is that where the wife resided at pronouncement of divorce, and notes the respondent resided in the USA. Ref: Dr. Hassan Shahryar v. Sana Waqar and 2 others (Civil Revision No.13538 of 2020, heard 27.09.2022).
records.title: Dr. Hassan Shahryar v. Sana Waqar and 2 others (Civil Revision No.13538 of 2020, heard 27.09.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Statutory Ground of Delay: Abscondence
records.heading: Statutory delay for bail is counted from arrest and earlier abscondence does not bar bail
records.text: For the statutory ground of delay in conclusion of trial under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, the period is counted from the date of the accused's arrest. Where the accused has been in custody over five years without fault on his part, earlier abscondence does not bar bail on this ground. Ref: 2022 LHC 7296; Riaz Shah v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 40039/22, decided 27.10.2022); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Riaz Shah v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 40039/22, decided 27.10.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 25 and Art. 37(c): MBBS/BDS Admission Marks Improvement
records.heading: Candidates who improved their marks cannot be discriminated against for not ticking a check box
records.text: Candidates who improved their marks in a special examination cannot be discriminated against, in violation of Art. 25 read with Art. 37(c), merely because they did not select the check box showing intent to improve marks in the online MBBS/BDS admission application. Ref: 2022 MLD 1922.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Art. 17(2)(a) QSO: Attestation of Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Article 17 QSO is satisfied where an agreement to sell was made before witnesses and later reduced to writing
records.text: Under Art. 17(2)(a) QSO a written instrument of financial or future obligations is to be attested by two men or one man and two women. Where the agreement to sell was made before witnesses, later reduced to writing and possession delivered, Art. 17 was satisfied. Art. 79 QSO governs proof of attested documents. The courts' decree for specific performance was endorsed. Ref: 2022 MLD 1945.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Judicial Confession: Voluntariness and S. 164 CrPC
records.heading: A judicial confession must be proved voluntary and true and the magistrate must record his belief under section 164(3)
records.text: To make a judicial confession credible, the prosecution must prove it was voluntary and true. Under s. 164(3) CrPC the magistrate must record a memorandum of his belief that it was voluntary. Lahore High Court Rules and Orders, Vol. III, Ch. 13 aim to ensure it is free from duress, threat, promise or inducement. Ref: 2022 YLR 2259.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Discovery of Fact
records.heading: Information from an accused in custody is relevant under Article 40 QSO only if it leads to discovery of a fact
records.text: Information furnished by an accused in police custody is relevant under Art. 40 QSO where it leads to discovery of a fact perceivable through the human senses and previously not within anyone's knowledge. Any other interpretation of Art. 40 is described as incorrect. Ref: 2022 YLR 2259.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Defence Applications and Fair Trial
records.heading: Dismissal of defence applications to summon record without valid reasons denied a fair trial
records.text: After the prosecution closed its evidence and the s. 342 statement was recorded, the Trial Court dismissed the accused's applications to correct a clerical mistake and summon the Rescue 15 record and its custodian, without valid reasons. This prejudiced the accused and denied fair trial under Art. 10-A. Petition allowed and the accused to be given an opportunity to produce defence evidence. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 198.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Abscondence Not a Bar to Bail
records.heading: Mere abscondence is not proof of guilt and cannot alone justify refusing bail
records.text: Mere abscondence is not proof of guilt and cannot alone be a ground to refuse bail where the accused otherwise has a case on merits, including further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Disappearance after a murder is natural whether the accused is rightly or wrongly involved. 2021 SCMR 2017 adds that abscondence is a circumstance that cannot invariably be ignored. Ref: 2022 SCMR 547, 2021 SCMR 1295, 2021 SCMR 2017, 2020 SCMR 956.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Will Executed and Acted Upon in Lifetime
records.heading: A will acted upon in the testator's lifetime becomes an inter vivos instrument with its own requirements
records.text: A will operates after death, so a will executed and acted upon in the testator's lifetime ceases to be a will and becomes an inter vivos instrument such as a gift, with its own requirements and standards of proof. The parties admitted the wills were so acted upon, which questions their validity under s. 2(h) of the Succession Act 1925. The post also records that s. 41 TPA 1882 protected the purchasers. Ref: Shams-ui-Islam Khan and others v. Samash--ui-Islam Khan and others (Civil Appeals No.10-0 and 1273 of 2021, decided 06.10.2022).
records.title: Shams-ui-Islam Khan and others v. Samash--ui-Islam Khan and others (Civil Appeals No.10-0 and 1273 of 2021, decided 06.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Convict: Conversion to S. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: A minor convict acting at the spur of the moment is convicted under section 302(c) PPC
records.text: Minor discrepancies from lapse of memory do not benefit the accused, and the eyewitness evidence was reliable. However, as the petitioner was a minor, the occurrence was at the spur of the moment without premeditation, and the weapon was ordinarily attached to a motorcycle or cycle, he was convicted under s. 302(c) PPC and sentenced to the period already undergone. Ref: Muhammad Usama v. The State (Jail Petition No. 496 of 2019, decided 20.10.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Usama v. The State (Jail Petition No. 496 of 2019, decided 20.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Forensic Report and Delayed Recovery of Churri
records.heading: A duplicate forensic report and a month-old recovery of a churri are of no help to the prosecution
records.text: The prosecution tendered only a duplicate forensic report showing human blood on the churri without leading the original or seeking leave for secondary evidence. The recovery was made about a month after the occurrence, and human blood would have disintegrated in about three weeks, so the recovery was inconsequential. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 192.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Private Recovery of Dead Body: Acquittal
records.heading: A private recovery of a dead body without an independent witness does not help the prosecution
records.text: Where the complainant made no effort to search for the missing deceased, the dead body was recovered privately without an independent witness, and no proof showed the accused lived in the house, the recovery was of no help to the prosecution. Falsus in uno falsus in omnibus did not justify conviction where co-accused were acquitted on the same evidence. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 192.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Presence of Eyewitnesses at Taxi Stand
records.heading: Eyewitnesses at a place that is not their residence must give a solid reason for being present
records.text: The incident occurred at a taxi stand that was not the eyewitnesses' residence, so they had to give a solid reason for being present. The complainant's own account suggested the brother-in-law arrived after the occurrence, and co-accused were acquitted on disbelief of the same eyewitnesses. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2022 YLR 2466.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay, Chance Witness and Withheld Evidence
records.heading: Unexplained delay, a chance complainant and withheld evidence make eyewitnesses doubtful and defeat the prosecution case
records.text: Unexplained FIR delay of about two hours ten minutes, post-mortem delay, conflict between ocular and medical evidence, and a chance complainant made the eyewitnesses doubtful. Non-production of the deceased's father, an inmate of the house, allowed adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO. The recovery of a pistol was immaterial without crime empties. Prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 201.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Rape Bail: Consensual Zina and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Whether an act was rape or consensual zina is a matter of further inquiry justifying bail
records.text: Despite a DNA report that the accused could not be excluded, the question was whether it was rape or consensual zina, a bailable offence. With no allegation of forcible abduction, no medico-legal support for intoxication and no recovery of the bottle, the case needed further probe. The co-accused had been released and the accused was on par. Bail allowed. Ref: 2022 YLR 2323.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC: Ingredients of Interim Injunction
records.heading: A temporary injunction requires a prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable loss
records.text: The ingredients for a temporary injunction are a prima facie arguable case, balance of convenience and irreparable loss or injury. Where the plaintiffs could not make out a prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable loss did not favour them. The appellate court's dismissal of the injunction application stood. Ref: 2022 YLR 2479.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Lis Pendens: Alienation During Suit
records.heading: Alienation of suit property during the pendency of the suit is subject to lis pendens
records.text: If defendants shown as owners alienate the suit property during the pendency of the suit, the transaction is subject to the principle of lis pendens, which safeguards the plaintiffs' rights. Validating pendente lite alienation affecting the opponent's rights would start endless litigation. Ref: 2022 YLR 2479.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Recovery Suit on Lost Cheque: Contradictory Evidence
records.heading: A recovery suit on a lost cheque fails where the plaintiff's evidence is materially discrepant
records.text: In a recovery suit on a cheque, the plaintiff's evidence was materially discrepant. He claimed to be taking to encash on 02.05.2012 a cheque due on 07.05.2012 and lost it, and the police report and testimony gave four different dates of loss. He failed to prove his case. Ref: 2022 YLR 2354.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Lost Cheque: Proof of Loss Before Secondary Evidence
records.heading: The plaintiff must prove loss of a negotiable instrument without his own default before secondary evidence is considered
records.text: In a suit on a lost negotiable instrument, the plaintiff must first prove the loss, bearing a heavy onus to show it was not due to his own default or negligence, before secondary evidence is considered. Without such proof, secondary evidence is valueless. The suit was dismissed and the appeal allowed. Ref: 2022 YLR 2354.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell by Mother of Minor Without Guardian Court Permission
records.heading: An agreement to sell a minor's property by his mother without Guardian Court permission is void ab initio
records.text: An agreement to sell a minor's property made by his mother without prior permission of the Guardian Court under s. 29 of the Guardians and Wards Act 1890 is void ab initio and cannot be enforced against the minor. In revision under s. 115 CPC the High Court could not interfere with concurrent findings. Ref: 2022 YLR 2293.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Court to Determine Jurisdiction and Limitation First
records.heading: A court must first determine jurisdiction and limitation before proceeding further in a suit
records.text: A court seized of a matter must first determine whether it has jurisdiction over the subject matter and whether the suit was filed within the limitation prescribed by law, before proceeding further. Ref: 2022 YLR 2450.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Challenge to Fraudulent Mutation After 11 Years
records.heading: A mutation procured by fraud can be challenged at any time and is not barred by limitation
records.text: A mutation challenged 11 years after sanction is not barred by limitation, because a document procured by fraud can be challenged at any time. Ref: 2022 YLR 2383.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale Mutation: Summary Nature of Mutation Proceedings
records.heading: Mutation proceedings are summary and fiscal and do not determine right or title to immovable property
records.text: Mutation proceedings are initiated for fiscal purposes, to collect land revenue and maintain the record. They are summary and are not judicial proceedings determining right or title to immovable property. The case concerned a woman's challenge to an oral sale mutation allegedly attested by thumb-impression. Ref: 2022 YLR 2383.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Admission of Price Before Attesting Officer
records.heading: An admission of receipt of price before the Attesting Officer is not conclusive proof
records.text: A mere admission as to receipt of the sale price before the Attesting Officer in sale mutation proceedings cannot be taken as conclusive proof. Ref: 2022 YLR 2383.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Thumb-Impression Expert Opinion: Weak Evidence
records.heading: Expert opinion on a thumb-impression is weak evidence and cannot substitute for available direct evidence
records.text: Expert opinion is always a weak type of evidence and not conclusive. Expert testimony on a thumb-impression cannot substitute for available direct evidence, and the court cannot base findings merely on an expert's opinion. Ref: 2022 YLR 2383.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Roznamcha Waqiati Does Not Confer Title
records.heading: Roznamcha Waqiati is not a document conferring title and proof of contents matters more than exhibition
records.text: Roznamcha Waqiati is not per se admissible and is not a document conferring title. Exhibition of a document and proof of its contents are different aspects, and the latter is more relevant and important. Ref: 2022 YLR 2383.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Readmission After Dismissal for Non-Prosecution
records.heading: Article 168 of the Limitation Act applies to readmission of an appeal dismissed for want of prosecution
records.text: Art. 168 of the Limitation Act 1908 applies to readmission of an appeal dismissed for want of prosecution. In the absence of a specific provision for readmission of a miscellaneous petition, Art. 181 applies. Ref: 2022 YLR 2376.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Unregistered Power of Attorney and Privity in Specific Performance
records.heading: A specific performance suit fails where the exhibited power of attorney was unregistered and privity was not established
records.text: In a suit for specific performance on an agreement made through an attorney, the plaintiff did not give details of the power of attorney or produce it, and the exhibited power of attorney was unregistered though compulsorily registrable. The plaintiff failed to establish privity with the respondent, and the suit failed. Ref: 2022 YLR 2399.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Recording Evidence Through Video Link
records.heading: Evidence by video link under Article 164 QSO requires the witness to be under judicial or executive supervision
records.text: Courts may record evidence by video conferencing under Art. 164 QSO, but the witness must be under the supervision of a judicial or executive officer, and the same law applies as to a physically present witness. A WhatsApp call lacks such supervision. The cases were remanded for recording witnesses physically or by video link following the guidelines. Ref: PLD 2021 Pesh 105.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Video Link Evidence Under Art. 164 QSO
records.heading: The CrPC does not prohibit video link evidence and Article 164 QSO empowers its admission
records.text: The CrPC does not provide for evidence by video conference but does not prohibit it. Art. 164 QSO empowers the court to admit evidence made available by technological advancement and can be invoked for video link evidence, and s. 10 of the Punjab Witness Protection Act 2018 could also be invoked. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 1184.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Admissibility and Proof of Audio and Video Recordings
records.heading: The requirements for admissibility and proof of audio and video recordings are stated as authority
records.text: Authority on the requirements for admissibility of an audio tape or video in evidence and the mode and manner of proving it before a court. Ref: PLD 2019 SC 675; Ishtiaq Ahmed Mirza and others v. Federation of Pakistan and others.
records.title: Ishtiaq Ahmed Mirza and others v. Federation of Pakistan and others

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Remand: Magistrate May Direct Addition or Deletion of Offence
records.heading: A Magistrate at remand may direct addition or deletion of an offence but not dictate the section 173 report
records.text: At the time of remand, a Magistrate may direct the Investigating Officer to add, delete or substitute an offence in the FIR if circumstances warrant. He cannot direct the SHO to submit the s. 173 CrPC report in a particular manner, against persons or for offences of his choosing. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 293.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Accused Called as Court Witness: Art. 13
records.heading: Calling the accused as a court witness contravenes Article 13 of the Constitution
records.text: Calling the accused as a court witness by the Trial Court was against the mandate of Art. 13 of the Constitution and the Islamic principle that no one can be compelled to be a witness against himself. Ref: 2016 YLR Note 147.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Student Struck Off: 66 Percent Attendance Requirement
records.heading: A student below the required 66 percent attendance is ineligible for the board examination and sympathy cannot override the law
records.text: A student struck off from a Peshawar school for non-payment of fees and absence was held ineligible for the board examination because her attendance was below the required 66 percent. The Urdu summary states the court cannot grant relief on sympathy by violating clear law, and the petition was dismissed. Ref: Aina Haya v. Peshawar Model School.
records.title: Aina Haya v. Peshawar Model School

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Factors for Assessing Reliability of Identifying Witness
records.heading: Reliability of an identifying witness is assessed by five stated factors
records.text: Reliability of a witness identifying a suspect is assessed by five factors: opportunity to view the suspect at the time of the crime, degree of attention, accuracy of prior description, certainty shown at the confrontation in court, and time between the crime and the confrontation. Ref: 2019 SCMR 956.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 100 PPC: Self-Defence Not Pleaded
records.heading: The court may infer self-defence from the evidence though it was not explicitly pleaded
records.text: Even if the plea of self-defence was not explicitly taken at trial, in the s. 342 CrPC statement or in cross-examination, it remains open to the court to infer it from the evidence led at trial. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 170.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Private Defence Inferred From Evidence
records.heading: Private defence may be inferred from the evidence though not specifically pleaded at trial
records.text: There is no bar to raising private defence though not specifically pleaded at trial, and the court may infer it from the evidence if tenable. For a convict sentenced to death on a murder charge, his conduct during the occurrence must fall within the parameters of the right of private defence in the PPC. Ref: 2009 SCMR 929.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Self-Defence Benefit Without Specific Plea
records.heading: The benefit of self-defence may be extended without a specific plea where the circumstances suggest it
records.text: If the accused did not specifically plead self-defence but the circumstances and prosecution evidence suggest he acted in self-defence, its benefit may be extended to him. Ref: 2018 PCrLJ 1563.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Purpose and Limits of Cross-Examination
records.heading: Cross-examination is not meant to hound a witness and is exercised within Articles 141 and 151 QSO
records.text: The purpose of cross-examination is not to hound or harass a witness. The accused's right to cross-examine is valuable and is to be exercised within the framework of Arts. 141 and 151 QSO. Ref: 2018 PCrLJ 1193.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Prolonged Cross-Examination Deprecated
records.heading: Prolonged cross-examination aimed at leading a witness into error is deprecated and the court must check it
records.text: Prolonged cross-examination aimed at leading a witness into error is deprecated. The court is bound to check it and to protect a party against irrelevant and scandalous questions, acting under Art. 146 QSO and relying on PLD 1967 SC 167. Ref: 1996 SCMR 3.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Downloaded Judgments Not Part of Judicial Record
records.heading: A downloaded copy of a judgment cannot ordinarily be made part of the judicial record
records.text: An electronically generated or downloaded copy of a judgment uploaded on the Court's official website cannot ordinarily be made part of the judicial record. The office should object, and the court decides case by case whether to retain it. If produced at arguments, the court considers its relevance and admissibility. Ref: 2022 LHC 7414; Akeel Ahmad v. Chairman, Punjab Public Service Commission, Lahore etc. (149609/22, decided 12.10.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Akeel Ahmad v. Chairman, Punjab Public Service Commission, Lahore etc. (149609/22, decided 12.10.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Suit for Jactitation of Marriage Decreed
records.heading: A suit for jactitation of marriage is decreed where no valid marriage with her free will is proved
records.text: A suit for jactitation of marriage was decreed where the petitioner's claim was in negative form and she proved that no valid and lawful marriage had taken place with her free will and accord. Ref: 2022 LHC 7466; Bakhtawar Bibi v. ADJ etc. (2523918.5819-17, decided 31.10.2022); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Bakhtawar Bibi v. ADJ etc. (2523918.5819-17, decided 31.10.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: High Court Jurisdiction Over Civil Servant Service Terms
records.heading: The High Court has no jurisdiction over a civil servant's terms of service including suspension
records.text: The High Court has no jurisdiction to entertain a dispute about the terms and conditions of a civil servant's service, including transfer, posting and disciplinary matters such as suspension. The petition of the CCPO Lahore against his suspension was dismissed. Ref: 2022 LHC 7480; Ghulam Mahmood Dogar v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (70222/22, decided 08.11.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Ghulam Mahmood Dogar v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (70222/22, decided 08.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Parity Versus Further Inquiry in Bail
records.heading: Parity treats like cases alike while further inquiry rests on a tentative assessment creating doubt
records.text: The doctrine of parity means like cases are treated alike, while further inquiry rests on a tentative assessment creating doubt about involvement. The case involved ss. 365 and 337-L(2) PPC with no specific role assigned to the petitioner. Under s. 497 CrPC the court may hold detention unjustified without detailed discussion of facts. Ref: Muhammad Nadim v. The State, etc. (Crl.P.1072-L/2022, decided 08.11.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Nadim v. The State, etc. (Crl.P.1072-L/2022, decided 08.11.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 295-A PPC: Ingredients and Mental Illness
records.heading: Section 295-A PPC requires deliberate and malicious intent to outrage religious feelings and the standard is high
records.text: S. 295-A PPC requires a deliberate and malicious intent to outrage the religious feelings of a class of citizens by insulting or attempting to insult their religion or beliefs, by words, signs or visible representations. The standard is high. The post observes that blasphemy accused often have mental conditions and refers to the legal insanity defence. Ref: Nasrullah Khan v. Station House Officer, Police Station Saddar, Mianwali, etc. (Writ Petition No. 60241/2021).
records.title: Nasrullah Khan v. Station House Officer, Police Station Saddar, Mianwali, etc. (Writ Petition No. 60241/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Transfer of Suit: Notice of Parvee Required
records.heading: The transferee court must issue notice of parvee to the parties when a suit is transferred administratively
records.text: Where a suit is transferred under an administrative order, the transferee Court must issue notice of parvee to the parties under Para 6, Chapter XIII, Vol. I of the High Court Rules and Orders. A suit dismissed for want of evidence without such notice or warning is harshly treated, and the High Court may correct the irregularity in revision under s. 115 CPC. Revision allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 993, 2023 MLD 551; Noor Zaman v. Mst. Gullan (deceased) through L.Rs. (C.R. No. 70819 of 2021, decided 12.01.2022); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Noor Zaman v. Mst. Gullan (deceased) through L.Rs. (C.R. No. 70819 of 2021, decided 12.01.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Striking Off Right to File Written Statement
records.heading: A defendant whose right to file a written statement was struck off and unchallenged is left without a defence
records.text: Where a defendant, despite repeated opportunities, defied the requirement to file a written statement and the order striking off his right to do so was never challenged and attained finality, he was left without a defence. The Court stressed that the law helps the vigilant and not the indolent. The decree of dower was left to be executed as per law. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 984; Sahibzada Haroon Ali Syed v. Additional District Judge and others (W.P. No. 3405 of 2019, decided 12.01.2022); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Sahibzada Haroon Ali Syed v. Additional District Judge and others (W.P. No. 3405 of 2019, decided 12.01.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Revision against a remand order lies only where the remand is perfunctory, perverse or illegal
records.text: In a declaratory suit against gift deeds and mutations in favour of an adopted son, the appellate Court rightly set aside the rejection of the plaint on limitation and remanded the case. Revision against a remand order lies only where the remand is perfunctory, perverse or illegal, and a trial was necessary. Civil revisions dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 974; Abdul Waheed, etc. v. Mst. Rubina Shaheen (C.R. No. 52-D of 2022, decided 20.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Shan Gul.
records.title: Abdul Waheed, etc. v. Mst. Rubina Shaheen (C.R. No. 52-D of 2022, decided 20.01.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Presence of Accused Mandatory
records.heading: An accused abroad cannot obtain pre-arrest bail as his presence before the court is mandatory
records.text: Pre-arrest bail is an order restraining the police from arresting the accused, and the accused must be present before the Court for it to be granted. An accused who is abroad cannot obtain protective ad-interim pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Lah 970; Abid Farooq v. Federation of Pakistan, etc. (W.P. No. 79717 of 2021, decided 12.01.2022); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Abid Farooq v. Federation of Pakistan, etc. (W.P. No. 79717 of 2021, decided 12.01.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partition of Agricultural Land: Revenue Authorities
records.heading: Partition of agricultural land with other shareholders belongs to the Revenue Authorities and not the Civil Court
records.text: A preliminary decree for the house attained finality where the co-sharer agreed to and received consideration for her share. For agricultural land with other shareholders, the Civil Court could only determine shares, and partition belongs to the Revenue Authorities, so the Civil Court could not order it. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 Islamabad 214; Syed Ali Asim Jaffari, etc. v. Qamar Abbas, etc. (C.R. No. 67 of 2021, decided 31.08.2022); Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Syed Ali Asim Jaffari, etc. v. Qamar Abbas, etc. (C.R. No. 67 of 2021, decided 31.08.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F(vii) CrPC: Summoning Record in Defence
records.heading: The accused may summon record or witnesses under section 265-F(vii) only after closure of prosecution evidence
records.text: The accused has a right under s. 265-F(vii) CrPC to have record or witnesses summoned after closure of prosecution evidence. An application to summon CDRs made earlier was premature, and the accused had not availed the right after his statement was recorded. Dismissal of the application did not call for interference. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 182; Asad Sarwar Bhatti v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 24647 of 2021, decided 11.05.2022); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Asad Sarwar Bhatti v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 24647 of 2021, decided 11.05.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Physical Remand: Supervision by Senior Police Officer
records.heading: Police remand custody ordered in revision is to be supervised by an officer not below the rank of SSP
records.text: In a writ against an order granting 48 hours of police remand in revision, the Court held that the legality of proceedings, including want of sanction, is to be examined when cognizance is taken. No interference was made with the revisional order, but remand custody was to be supervised by an officer not below the rank of SSP. Petition disposed of. Ref: PLJ 2022 Islamabad 200; Muhammad Shahbaz Shabeer v. Additional Sessions Judge and others (W.P. No. 3035 of 2022, decided 22.08.2022); Justice Aamer Farooq.
records.title: Muhammad Shahbaz Shabeer v. Additional Sessions Judge and others (W.P. No. 3035 of 2022, decided 22.08.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint: Ss. 200 to 204 CrPC
records.heading: A Magistrate may issue process on a private complaint if satisfied of a prima facie case after examining the complainant
records.text: A private complaint gives an aggrieved person direct access to set the law in motion. After examining the complainant on oath, the Magistrate may issue process if satisfied of a prima facie case, and may proceed on the allegations in the complaint. The impugned order was set aside and the matter remanded for further enquiry. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 181; Rubina Subtain alias Fazeela Bibi v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 09 of 2021, decided 02.06.2021); Justice Sardar Ahmed Naeem.
records.title: Rubina Subtain alias Fazeela Bibi v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 09 of 2021, decided 02.06.2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Statutory Delay: S. 497(1)(a) CrPC
records.heading: An accused who did not cause delay and has long custody earns bail on statutory delay
records.text: Where the statutory period under s. 497(1)(a) CrPC had matured, the accused had not contributed to the delay and had been in custody about two years and eight months without substantial progress in the trial, he earned a right to bail on statutory delay. Bail allowed, with a direction to conclude the trial within six months. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 170; Sikandar Hayat v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 65647-B of 2021, decided 23.02.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Sikandar Hayat v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 65647-B of 2021, decided 23.02.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Joint Identification Parade of Several Accused
records.heading: A joint identification parade is not invalid where each suspect stood in a separate row with dummies
records.text: Identification proceedings should ordinarily be held separately as a rule of prudence, but this is not mandatory. Proceedings that are otherwise impeccable cannot be discarded solely because they were held jointly for several suspects, where each was placed in a separate row with dummies. Relying on 2020 SCMR 342. The appeal was dismissed with alterations and the death sentence was not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1603; Hamza Yaqoob and others v. State and another (Crl. A. Nos. 776 & 956, M.R. No. 71 of 2018, decided 13.01.2022); Justice Raja Shahid Mehmood Abbasi; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Hamza Yaqoob and others v. State and another (Crl. A. Nos. 776 & 956, M.R. No. 71 of 2018, decided 13.01.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal: Division Bench Jurisdiction
records.heading: Appeals against acquittal are to be decided by a Division Bench under the High Court Rules and Orders
records.text: Under the High Court Rules and Orders, Vol. V, Chapter 3, Part B, appeals against acquittal are to be decided by a Division Bench, which may also direct fixation of connected matters. Fixing such an appeal before a Single Bench was against the spirit of the Rules, and the office was directed to fix it before a Division Bench. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1599; Manzoor Khan v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 750 of 2020, decided 30.05.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Manzoor Khan v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 750 of 2020, decided 30.05.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Complainant Satisfied With Investigation
records.heading: A complainant who does not challenge the Investigating Officer's opinion shows satisfaction with the investigation
records.text: Where the accused was placed in column No. II by the Investigating Officer and the complainant neither challenged that opinion nor filed a private complaint, this showed satisfaction with the investigation. Even for bail the law is not stretched in favour of the prosecution, and any doubt goes to the accused. Post-arrest bail allowed despite s. 497(1) CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1595; Muhammad Ijaz v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 8802-B of 2021, decided 26.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 8802-B of 2021, decided 26.01.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Arts. 117 and 122 QSO
records.heading: The burden of proving guilt stays on the prosecution and shifts under Article 122 QSO only after the elements are established
records.text: Art. 117 QSO embodies the presumption of innocence, and the burden to prove guilt beyond doubt lies on the prosecution and cannot shift to the accused unless the legislature expressly says so. Only after the prosecution establishes the elements of the offence does the burden shift under Art. 122 QSO, regarding facts especially within the accused's knowledge. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1568; State v. Muhammad Zeeshan (M.R. No. 58 of 2016); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: State v. Muhammad Zeeshan (M.R. No. 58 of 2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witness, Source of Light and Identification Parade
records.heading: A chance witness, missing source of light and doubtful identification lead to acquittal in a night dacoity murder
records.text: In a night-time dacoity murder, no source of light was mentioned in the FIR, the two site plans conflicted on lighting, and the sole eye-witness, a security supervisor, was a chance witness whose identification of the appellants was doubtful. The appeals were accepted and the accused were to be released. Murder Reference answered in the negative as to Abdul Hameed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1555; Abdul Hameed alias Kora and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 711, 658 & M.R. No. 6 of 2021, heard 07.06.2022); Justice Raja Shahid Mehmood Abbasi; Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Abdul Hameed alias Kora and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 711, 658 & M.R. No. 6 of 2021, heard 07.06.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Conditional Bail on Deposit of Arsh: S. 337-N(2) PPC
records.heading: An accused pleading nolo contendere may be bailed on deposit of Arsh or Daman and bail may carry conditions
records.text: An accused who pleads nolo contendere may be released on bail on deposit of Arsh or Daman under s. 337-N(2) PPC. A criminal Court may impose conditions when granting bail, as bail restricts liberty, and conditional bail orders are now common even under special laws. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1549; Bilal Azam v. Muhammad Haq Nawaz, etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 22527 of 2020, heard 17.06.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Bilal Azam v. Muhammad Haq Nawaz, etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 22527 of 2020, heard 17.06.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Suspension of Short Sentence Pending Appeal: S. 426 CrPC
records.heading: A short sentence may be suspended under section 426 CrPC where the appeal is unlikely to be decided soon
records.text: Once an accused is convicted the presumption of innocence vanishes, but where the sentence is short and the appeal is unlikely to be decided soon, the whole sentence may be served before the appeal is heard. Sentence suspended under s. 426 CrPC for one appellant, relying on 2019 SCMR 516 and 2007 SCMR 246. Petition partially allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 1543; Talib Hussain and another v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 181 of 2022, decided 05.07.2022); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar; Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Talib Hussain and another v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 181 of 2022, decided 05.07.2022)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Colonization Act S. 30(2): Resumption of Government Land
records.heading: The Board of Revenue may resume Government land acquired by fraud and Civil Courts may strike down unlawful orders
records.text: The Board of Revenue, Punjab is vested under s. 30(2) of the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act, 1912 with power to resume Government land acquired by fraud or misrepresentation. Civil Courts lack jurisdiction where Revenue Authorities acted lawfully, but may strike down orders passed without lawful authority. A High Court may be approached under Art. 199. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 425; Nausher v. Province of Punjab through District Collector, Khanewal and another (C.A. No. 1011 of 2016, decided 18.08.2022); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Nausher v. Province of Punjab through District Collector, Khanewal and another (C.A. No. 1011 of 2016, decided 18.08.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Trust Property: Notification Before Sale
records.heading: Evacuee land must be notified in the Official Gazette before any sale under the 1977 Scheme
records.text: Evacuee properties vested in the Federal Government under s. 6 of the Evacuee Trust Properties Act, 1975. Before any evacuee land or property can be sold, it must be notified in the Official Gazette by the relevant Member Board of Revenue under para 3 of the 1977 Scheme. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 436; Raja Ali Zaman (deed.) thr. LRs and another v. Evacuee Trust Property Board and another (Civil A. No. 668 of 2022, decided 04.08.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Raja Ali Zaman (deed.) thr. LRs and another v. Evacuee Trust Property Board and another (Civil A. No. 668 of 2022, decided 04.08.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Challenge to PTO or PTD: Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: A person with locus standi challenging a PTO or PTD must approach the Civil Court
records.text: A person with locus standi who wishes to challenge a provisional transfer order or PTD issued under repealed evacuee laws must approach the Civil Court, a court of plenary jurisdiction. The case concerned a suit for declaration under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the validity of a PTD. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 450; Muhammad Din v. Deputy Settlement Commissioner and others (C.A. No. 730 of 2015, decided 08.03.2022); Justice Sajjad Ali Shah; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Muhammad Din v. Deputy Settlement Commissioner and others (C.A. No. 730 of 2015, decided 08.03.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance: Proof of Collateral Residuary Heir
records.heading: A collateral residuary claimant must prove his link to the deceased
records.text: A claimant to a share as collateral consanguine male residuary must prove his connection to the deceased. The fatwa and pedigree table produced did not establish the appellant's link to the deceased or an entitlement as residuary to half the estate. Appeal dismissed with no order as to costs. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC 461; Muhammad Sharif v. Mst. Niamat Bibi (C.A. No. 954 of 2014, decided 24.06.2021); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Muhammad Sharif v. Mst. Niamat Bibi (C.A. No. 954 of 2014, decided 24.06.2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 396 PPC: No Overt Act Required
records.heading: Section 396 PPC does not require proof of a specific overt act
records.text: The prosecution relied on ocular account, medical evidence, identification parade and recovery of the weapon. For s. 396 PPC no one can be distinguished by role, and the prosecution need not prove a specific overt act by each accused. The High Court judgment was well reasoned and the appeals were dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 295; Muhammad Ali and others v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 363 to 366 of 2021, decided 22.09.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Muhammad Ali and others v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 363 to 366 of 2021, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ghairat and Grave and Sudden Provocation: S. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: Double murder under ghairat and provocation falls under section 302(c) PPC
records.text: In a double murder committed under ghairat and grave and sudden provocation, the eye-witnesses and medical evidence were reliable, and mere relationship with the deceased did not discredit them. The conviction was altered to s. 302(c) PPC and the sentence reduced to the period already undergone. Petition converted into appeal and partly allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 288; Sabtain Haider v. State (J.P. No. 34 of 2020, decided 21.09.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Sabtain Haider v. State (J.P. No. 34 of 2020, decided 21.09.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed: Role and Co-Accused Parity
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where the accused had no nexus and a co-accused had bail
records.text: Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC was confirmed in a vehicle registration fraud case where the Investigating Officer stated the petitioner had no nexus with the scam, the verification of files lay with the inspector, and a co-accused with a similar role had obtained post-arrest bail. Petitions converted into appeals and allowed. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 284; Naeem Qadir Sheikh and another v. State etc. (Crl. P. Nos. 1086-L & 1143-L of 2022, decided 30.09.2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Naeem Qadir Sheikh and another v. State etc. (Crl. P. Nos. 1086-L & 1143-L of 2022, decided 30.09.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Abetment and CDR Evidence
records.heading: Bail granted to a woman implicated later; a CDR alone does not prove guilt
records.text: A woman not named in the crime report and implicated later by a supplementary statement was granted bail. Abetment under s. 107 PPC requires instigation, engagement with co-accused and intentional aid, and a Call Data Record without other concrete material is not conclusive evidence of guilt. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 281; Shameem Bibi v. State etc. (Crl. P. No. 982-L of 2022, decided 22.09.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Shameem Bibi v. State etc. (Crl. P. No. 982-L of 2022, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotic Samples
records.heading: A broken chain of custody makes the chemical examiner's report unreliable
records.text: Where parcels reached the chemical examiner seven days after recovery and no witness proved safe custody and transmission, the chain was broken. Any break makes the chemical examiner's report worthless and unreliable to support conviction under s. 9(c) CNSA. Conviction set aside and accused acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 276; Qaiser and another v. State (J.P. No. 587 of 2016 along with Crl. S.M.R.P. No. 14 of 2022, decided 02.06.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Qaiser and another v. State (J.P. No. 587 of 2016 along with Crl. S.M.R.P. No. 14 of 2022, decided 02.06.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Delay in Sending Sample: Moharrar Not Produced
records.heading: Acquittal where the Moharrar and carrying constable were not produced
records.text: In a case of 50 kilograms of charas, the sample parcel reached the FSL after five days. Neither the Moharrar who kept it in the Malkhana nor the constable who carried it was produced, so safe custody and transmission was not established. Accused acquitted under s. 9(c) CNSA. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2022 SC CrC 274; Akhtar Gul v. State (J.P. No. 343 of 2018, decided 31.03.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Akhtar Gul v. State (J.P. No. 343 of 2018, decided 31.03.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: No Cash Deposit Condition Beyond Sureties
records.heading: A court granting bail cannot impose a cash deposit beyond sureties
records.text: The accused furnishes a bail bond under s. 499 CrPC to secure attendance, and a Court granting bail cannot impose a further condition of depositing money. Default is met by forfeiture of the bond under s. 514 CrPC. Imposing any condition other than sureties contravenes the Supreme Court's dictum. Ref: Javed Iqbal v. The State through D.A.G., Islamabad & another (Criminal Petition No. 1251 of 2022, decided 01.11.2022).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State through D.A.G., Islamabad & another (Criminal Petition No. 1251 of 2022, decided 01.11.2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Advance Tax on Persons Not Required to File Return
records.heading: Non-adjustable advance tax on persons not required to file returns is unconstitutional
records.text: Collecting non-adjustable advance tax from persons without taxable income, who are not required to file a return, is unconstitutional. The Court found the procedure in Rule 2 of the Tenth Schedule impracticable and unreasonable for withholding agents, and absence from the active taxpayer list is not equal to being a non-filer. Ref: Rao Tariq Islam, etc. v. Federation of Pakistan, etc. (W.P. No. 228757 of 2018); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Rao Tariq Islam, etc. v. Federation of Pakistan, etc. (W.P. No. 228757 of 2018)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Murree Tragedy: Directions to Government Departments
records.heading: No criminal case in the Murree deaths, but Government must enhance compensation
records.text: On the deaths of 22 persons in Murree on 7 January 2022, the Court held that no criminal case was warranted, but the Government of Punjab bore responsibility for mishandling by departments and was directed to enhance the Rs. 800,000 paid to each victim's family. NDMA and PDMA were directed to devise disaster management plans. Petitions disposed of. Ref: Rizwan Ellahi & another v. Province of Punjab & 8 others (announced 07.11.2022).
records.title: Rizwan Ellahi & another v. Province of Punjab & 8 others (announced 07.11.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Adoption: Legal Position and Declaration for Adult
records.heading: Questions on adoption and an adult's declaration of adoption were framed
records.text: Judgment on whether adoption is permitted under the laws of Pakistan, what rights accrue to an adopted child and adopting parents, and whether an adult can obtain a declaration of adoption nearly three decades later where no adoption deed was executed. The post gives the questions framed and not the holding. Ref: Malik Mohammad Rafiq and 2 others v. Public at Large and others (R.F.A. No. 620 of 2022); Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Malik Mohammad Rafiq and 2 others v. Public at Large and others (R.F.A. No. 620 of 2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Art. 212: Administrative Courts and Tribunals
records.heading: Article 212(1) allows Administrative Courts and Tribunals with exclusive jurisdiction over service matters
records.text: Art. 212(1) opens with a non-obstante clause and empowers the Federation and Provinces to create Administrative Courts or Tribunals with exclusive jurisdiction, including over terms and conditions of persons in the service of Pakistan. The Court confined its discussion to para (a) and said it applies mutatis mutandis to other such Tribunals. Ref: Dean / Chief Executive, Gomal Medical College, Medical Teaching Institution, D.I. Khan v. Muhammad Armaghan Khan and others (Civil Appeal No. 1474 of 2021, decided 15.11.2022).
records.title: Dean / Chief Executive, Gomal Medical College, Medical Teaching Institution, D.I. Khan v. Muhammad Armaghan Khan and others (Civil Appeal No. 1474 of 2021, decided 15.11.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Exhibiting a Document: Role of the Court
records.heading: Assigning an exhibit number is the duty of the Court, not the witness
records.text: An exhibit is a document or object produced before the Court for inspection or shown to a witness. Assigning the exhibit number is the sole duty of the Court, not the witness. Questions on admissibility must be decided when the document is tendered and before it is marked, and proof is a separate matter. Ref: PLD 2018 Lah 132.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Reliability and Credibility
records.heading: Reliable circumstantial evidence is distinguished from credible evidence
records.text: Judgment on circumstantial evidence in criminal cases, discussing its definition, guiding principles and requirements. It distinguishes reliable evidence, which depends on the witness's capacity and the legality of the process of collection, from credible evidence, which concerns the witness's character. Ref: 2022 LHC 7641; State v. Muhammad Shahid etc (Murder Reference 55-18, decided 25.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: State v. Muhammad Shahid etc (Murder Reference 55-18, decided 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Person Impeaching a Fictitious Sale
records.heading: The person impeaching a fictitious sale bears the burden of proving it
records.text: If the party on whom the burden lies produces no evidence, the issue is decided against him. The burden of proving a deceitful transaction rests on the person who impeaches it, so in a declaratory suit alleging a fictitious sale the plaintiff must prove it. Where his evidence is self-contradictory or the case is doubtful, the defendant succeeds. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1054.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation: Burden of Proof on Claimant of Title
records.heading: A party relying on a disputed mutation must prove it and the transaction
records.text: A mutation does not itself confer or extinguish title. A person deriving title through a mutation must prove that the transferor parted with ownership and that the mutation was duly entered and attested, and where the mutation is disputed the onus of proving it and the genuineness of the transaction lies on the party relying on it. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1054.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance: Burden on Exclusive Claimant
records.heading: A person claiming exclusively against Shari'ah shares must prove that claim
records.text: On the death of a Muslim, property devolves on the legal heirs in Shari'ah shares, and possession by one heir is possession by all. A person who lays exclusive claim to the property or a part of it, contrary to the Shari'ah shares, bears the burden of establishing that claim. Ref: 2022 SCMR 13.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Suit to Claim Legal Character Including Paternity
records.heading: A person denied legal character, including paternity, may sue to claim it
records.text: A person whose legal character, including paternity, is denied may file a suit to claim it, but the Court held that the case before it was not of that kind. Ref: Munir Hussain, etc. v. Riffat Shamim, etc. (Civil Misc. Application No. 3492/2022 in Civil Petition No. Nil/2022, decided 14.11.2022).
records.title: Munir Hussain, etc. v. Riffat Shamim, etc. (Civil Misc. Application No. 3492/2022 in Civil Petition No. Nil/2022, decided 14.11.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Ban on Motorcycles on Motorways: S. 45 Ordinance
records.heading: Section 45 of the Ordinance permits a ban on motorcycles on motorways
records.text: Section 45 of the National Highways Safety Ordinance, 2000 deals with traffic control in the interest of public safety or convenience, and imposing a ban on motorcyclists on motorways is permissible under it. The judgment also addresses Arts. 4 and 9 of the Constitution and judicial review versus judicial overreach. Ref: Federation of Pakistan thr. Secretary M/o Communications, Islamabad & another v. Shuja Sharif & others (C.P. 303/2019, decided 24.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan thr. Secretary M/o Communications, Islamabad & another v. Shuja Sharif & others (C.P. 303/2019, decided 24.10.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Injunction Based Only on Possession
records.heading: Mere possession cannot ground an injunction for an indefinite period
records.text: Mere possession of the suit property cannot be the basis for granting an injunction for an indefinite period, unless a legal right to continue in possession is established on the record. Ref: 2022 LHC 7679; Muhammad Rafique v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ 71147/22, decided 14.11.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ 71147/22, decided 14.11.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Application: Limitation Under Art. 181
records.heading: An application under section 12(2) CPC is limited to three years under Article 181
records.text: Under Art. 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908 the limitation for an application under s. 12(2) CPC is three years from the date of the impugned decision based on fraud. If fraud kept the applicant from knowledge of the decision, s. 18 extends the start to the date of knowledge. Fraud must be pleaded specifically with particulars. Ref: PLD 2019 SC 504.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC Is Not a Recovery Provision
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC is meant to punish, not to recover money
records.text: Prima facie s. 489-F PPC is not intended by the legislature to recover an alleged amount, but to determine guilt and award sentence, fine or both. Recovery of money lies through civil proceedings such as O. XXXVII CPC. Ref: 2022 SCMR 592; Abdul Saboor v. State.
records.title: Abdul Saboor v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Cheque Case: S. 497(2) CrPC Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail in a cheque case after long custody: further inquiry under section 497(2)
records.text: The accused issued a cheque to settle a loan and had been in custody six and a half months, while the maximum punishment under s. 489-F PPC is three years and the offence is outside the prohibitory clause. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC calling for further inquiry. Leave converted into appeal and allowed; bail allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 592; Abdul Saboor v. State.
records.title: Abdul Saboor v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Withdrawal Under S. 494 CrPC and Honourable Acquittal
records.heading: Withdrawal under section 494 CrPC yields acquittal simpliciter, not a lesser kind of acquittal
records.text: Withdrawal under s. 494 CrPC results in discharge if made before charge and acquittal if after. The distinction between clean acquittal and acquittal on benefit of doubt, or honourable acquittal, is a self-coined notion alien to the Code, and an acquittal is an acquittal simpliciter with all the consequences of a pure acquittal. Ref: PLD 2002 SC 1060.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: All Acquittals Are Honourable
records.heading: All acquittals are honourable; none can be termed dishonourable
records.text: All acquittals are honourable, and there can be no acquittal that is termed dishonourable. Ref: 2001 SCMR 269.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Recording Civil Evidence by Video Conference
records.heading: Civil evidence may be recorded by video conference under Order XVIII Rule 4
records.text: The Court considered whether a witness not physically present can give evidence in a civil case by video conference, in the light of O. XVIII R. 4 CPC and whether 'attendance' there includes virtual attendance. The Urdu heading states that civil evidence may be recorded by video conference. The Court also applied updating construction of statutes. Ref: Meera Shafi (Meeshah Shafi) v. Ali Zafar (C.P. 1795/2022, decided 21.11.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Meera Shafi (Meeshah Shafi) v. Ali Zafar (C.P. 1795/2022, decided 21.11.2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Grant of Leave to Appeal by Supreme Court
records.heading: Leave to appeal is granted only on important questions of law or gross misreading of evidence
records.text: In granting leave to appeal the Supreme Court does not act as an ordinary appellate court. Leave is justified only where an important question of law arises, or the finding of fact results from gross misreading or non-reading of evidence or is so shocking or improbable that no reasonable person could have reached it. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 806.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Fixing Maintenance: S. 17A(4) Family Courts Act
records.heading: Family Courts must not fix maintenance mechanically, ignoring section 17A(4) procedure
records.text: The Court held that Family Courts were fixing maintenance mechanically and arbitrarily, ignoring the procedure in s. 17A(4) of the Family Courts Act, 1964, causing miscarriage of justice. Copies of the judgment were directed to be sent to all Punjab judges and the Punjab Judicial Academy. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 840; Justice Jawad Hassan.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Guardian of Disabled Person: Accounts and Inventory
records.heading: The Court may still consider a guardian's need for funds despite late accounts
records.text: The Court is guardian of minors and disabled persons, and the intent of the legislation is their welfare. Where a mother appointed guardian filed her statement of expenditure late and no inventory under s. 37, the Court must still consider her stated need for withdrawing funds and may enquire into correctness. Petition allowed; application to be decided afresh. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 833.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Scope of Terrorism Under Anti-Terrorism Act
records.heading: Not every grievous hurt or endangering act amounts to terrorism
records.text: The Anti-Terrorism Act is a special law to be read in light of its preamble and object. Not every case of grievous hurt, damage to private property or act endangering life amounts to terrorism. The Supreme Court allowed the appeals and acquitted all accused, including the main accused, in the Shahzeb Khan murder case. Ref: Nawab Siraj Ali S/o Nawab Imdad Ali Talpur & another v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.A. 400/2019, decided 18.10.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Nawab Siraj Ali S/o Nawab Imdad Ali Talpur & another v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.A. 400/2019, decided 18.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appraisal of Prosecution Case Before Accused's Statement
records.heading: Prosecution evidence is assessed first; an exculpatory statement must be accepted as a whole
records.text: The Court should first assess the prosecution evidence independently, then the accused's version. If the prosecution evidence is rejected, the statement under s. 342 or 340(2) CrPC must be accepted as a whole, and an exculpatory statement leads to acquittal. The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, and exculpatory parts of a confession cannot be rejected. Ref: Javed Iqbal v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Crl.A. 139/2022, decided 25.10.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood.
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Crl.A. 139/2022, decided 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ingredients of Criminal Breach of Trust: S. 406 PPC
records.heading: Section 406 PPC requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation or disposal of property
records.text: The essential ingredients of s. 406 PPC are entrustment, dishonest misappropriation or conversion to own use by the person trusted, and dishonest use or disposal of property in violation of a direction of law or of a legal contract. Ref: Malik Zulfiqar Ahmed v. The State and 02 others (Writ Petition No. 1413-Q of 2022, decided 27.10.2022).
records.title: Malik Zulfiqar Ahmed v. The State and 02 others (Writ Petition No. 1413-Q of 2022, decided 27.10.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift to Daughter-in-Law: Hiba-bil-Ewaz
records.heading: A bride's gift from her father-in-law cannot be undone for want of possession
records.text: Courts have held that a gift made to a bride at her wedding by the groom's father cannot be undone because it was not made by the groom or because possession was not handed over, and the father-in-law is treated as holding possession for her benefit. Where the nikahnama property belongs to a parent-in-law, the bride's claim depends on proving a contract of guarantee. Ref: Mst. Asima Bibi and another v. Mst. Naeema Akhtar and others (Writ Petition No. 449 of 2021, decided 11.11.2022).
records.title: Mst. Asima Bibi and another v. Mst. Naeema Akhtar and others (Writ Petition No. 449 of 2021, decided 11.11.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Alienation by Widow Holding Life Estate
records.heading: A widow holding a life estate cannot alienate against the reversioner
records.text: The dispute concerned land inherited in 1929 by a widow as a life owner without a right to alienate, and her later alienation, which an earlier suit decreed void against the reversioner. The Court found no misreading or non-reading of evidence or legal or jurisdictional defect, and declined to interfere with the impugned judgment. Ref: Shahray Khan (decd.) through LRs etc. v. Qadir Bakhsh (decd.) through LRs etc. (Civil Petition No. 2658 of 2019).
records.title: Shahray Khan (decd.) through LRs etc. v. Qadir Bakhsh (decd.) through LRs etc. (Civil Petition No. 2658 of 2019)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 186A: Transfer of Case Between High Courts
records.heading: Transfer between High Courts under Article 186A is discretionary and used sparingly
records.text: The power under Art. 186A to transfer a case from one High Court to another is discretionary and exercised in the interest of justice, a concept varying with the facts of each case. It is a constitutional safeguard ensuring a fair hearing and fair trial, to be used with caution in compelling circumstances. Ref: Muhammad Saleem Baig, Chairman Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA), Islamabad v. M/s Labbaik (Pvt) Limited through Executive Admin Bol TV Quetta and others (Constitution Petition No. 10 of 2020, decided 06.06.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Saleem Baig, Chairman Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA), Islamabad v. M/s Labbaik (Pvt) Limited through Executive Admin Bol TV Quetta and others (Constitution Petition No. 10 of 2020, decided 06.06.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Local Commission Report: S. 75 and O. XXVI CPC
records.heading: A Local Commission report is not lightly ruled out but cannot alone decide a suit
records.text: Under s. 75 read with O. XXVI CPC the Court may appoint a Local Commission for local investigation, and its report cannot lightly be ruled out. A suit cannot be decided on the report alone, but where the Commission was appointed by mutual consent with an undertaking to abide by its findings and objections were rejected, the Court may decide on it. Ref: Abdul Rasheed v. Province of the Punjab etc. (Civil Revision No. 237171 of 2018, decided 16.11.2022).
records.title: Abdul Rasheed v. Province of the Punjab etc. (Civil Revision No. 237171 of 2018, decided 16.11.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Fornication: Complaint Under S. 203-C CrPC
records.heading: A complaint under section 203-C is mandatory to convict for fornication
records.text: A complaint under s. 203-C CrPC is mandatory for convicting a person of fornication. A male alone cannot be convicted of the offence, and the consenting female cannot be believed as a witness against him. No criminal revision lies against an acquittal under s. 439(5) CrPC. Ref: 2022 LHC 7745; Rashid Ahmad v. State etc. (decided 11.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Rashid Ahmad v. State etc. (decided 11.10.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Self-Projection by Politicians on Government Records
records.heading: Placing the Chief Minister's image on sanads is impermissible self-projection
records.text: The Court held that placing the Chief Minister's image on sanads of proprietary rights, so as to present him as benefactor, amounts to self-projection and self-aggrandisement at public expense, which is not permissible. It referred to the Quaid-e-Azam's directions to civil servants to stay away from party politics. Ref: Deputy Administrator Evacuee Trust Property, Rawalpindi v. Sakhi Muhammad Kiani (Civil Petition No. 4734 of 2018).
records.title: Deputy Administrator Evacuee Trust Property, Rawalpindi v. Sakhi Muhammad Kiani (Civil Petition No. 4734 of 2018)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Struck-Off Defence: Cross-Examination and Evidence Allowed
records.heading: A defendant whose defence is struck off may still cross-examine and lead evidence
records.text: The Family Courts Act has no specific provision to strike off a defendant's defence, but for contumacious default the Family Court may make an order in the nature of O. VIII R. 10 CPC. Even so, the defendant may cross-examine the plaintiff's witnesses, lead evidence to disprove the plaint and take part in final arguments. Ref: 2022 LHC 7759; Raja Ibadat Sajjad Khan v. Shehnaz Kousar etc. (Family 13531/22, decided 21.11.2022); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Raja Ibadat Sajjad Khan v. Shehnaz Kousar etc. (Family 13531/22, decided 21.11.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Tribunal Interference With Quantum of Punishment
records.heading: A Tribunal needs strong reasons to interfere with the quantum of punishment
records.text: Imposing penalty lies in the domain of the Inquiry or Authorized Officer, and a Tribunal needs strong reasons to reduce it. Its power to modify punishment is not unbridled, and it should not substitute its own view unless the penalty rests on unreasonable or extraneous considerations or is against the law. Given the seriousness of the charges, no leniency was shown. Ref: 2022 LHC 7781; Tahir Jamil Butt v. The Lahore High Court, Lahore through its Registrar (decided 07.10.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Tahir Jamil Butt v. The Lahore High Court, Lahore through its Registrar (decided 07.10.2022)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Removal of Lamberdar: Grounds Under Rule 18
records.heading: Removal of a lamberdar is confined to the grounds in rule 18
records.text: The grounds for removal of a lamberdar are those enumerated in rule 18, and the concurrent orders of the revenue hierarchy were set aside. Ref: 2022 LHC 7808; Temoor Sheikh v. MBR etc. (W.P. 13222-17, decided 16.11.2022); Justice Ch. Muhammad Masood Jahangir.
records.title: Temoor Sheikh v. MBR etc. (W.P. 13222-17, decided 16.11.2022)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Admission of Right of Pre-emption and Price Determination
records.heading: An admission of the right of pre-emption cannot be retracted when price is disputed
records.text: The right of pre-emption and the determination of sale price are severable. Failure of vendee and pre-emptor to agree on price does not wipe out a compromise acknowledging the right, and an admission once made cannot be retracted, since price may be determined under s. 27 of the Act. Ref: 2022 LHC 7824; Ch. Mohammad Saleem v. Ch. Abdul Razzaq (Regular Second Appeal, decided 05.10.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Ch. Mohammad Saleem v. Ch. Abdul Razzaq (Regular Second Appeal, decided 05.10.2022)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: NAB Amendment 2022: Accused Left Remediless
records.heading: No person can be left remediless where life and liberty are involved
records.text: After the National Accountability (Amendment) Act, 2022, s. 5(o) and (s) took petitioners outside the Ordinance as the alleged amount was below Rs. 500 million, leaving a lacuna and no remedy for them. The Court, as custodian of fundamental rights under Arts. 9 and 10, held that no person can be left remediless where life and liberty are involved. Ref: 2022 LHC 7771; Muhammad Alam Khilji etc v. Learned Judge Accountability Court No.1 Rwp etc (W.P. 3197-22, decided 17.11.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Alam Khilji etc v. Learned Judge Accountability Court No.1 Rwp etc (W.P. 3197-22, decided 17.11.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Sale Mutation by Brother Against Illiterate Sister
records.heading: A brother taking an oral sale mutation from an illiterate sister must prove it
records.text: Where the beneficiary of an oral sale mutation was the plaintiff's brother and she was an illiterate village woman, he had to prove the underlying transaction and that it was free of undue influence, coercion or fraud. Depriving women of inheritance by gifts and mutations is deprecated, relying on 2021 SCMR 179. Ref: 2022 LHC 7837; Hayyat Ali v. Mst. Khatoon Begum etc. (Civil Revision 419-18, decided 25.10.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Hayyat Ali v. Mst. Khatoon Begum etc. (Civil Revision 419-18, decided 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Visitation Schedule for Minors Under Guardian and Wards Act
records.heading: A non-custodial parent should have frequent visitation in a homely environment
records.text: The Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 prescribes no set visitation pattern. Limited meetings within Court premises are inappropriate, and the non-custodial parent should meet the child in a homely environment frequently and regularly under a balanced annual plan. Overnight stay should be granted in appropriate cases. Ref: 2022 LHC 7798; Shahid Wazeer v. ADJ etc. (Writ Petition 17366-21, decided 06.10.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Shahid Wazeer v. ADJ etc. (Writ Petition 17366-21, decided 06.10.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Heroin Case: Unproduced Witnesses and No Arrest Evidence
records.heading: Acquittal in a heroin case where arrest and recovery were not proved
records.text: In a case of 12 kg of heroin, material witnesses were not produced and none of six prosecution witnesses described the date, place or manner of arrest, and no recovery memo of personal search existed. The prosecution must prove its case beyond doubt even in heinous cases, and the benefit of doubt led to acquittal. Ref: 2022 LHC 7816; Abdul Hamid v. State (Crl. Appeal 684-19, decided 01.11.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Abdul Hamid v. State (Crl. Appeal 684-19, decided 01.11.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Father's Liability for Maintenance and Marriage Expenses
