records.heading: A father must pay reasonable maintenance and marriage expenses of his daughter
records.text: A father is bound to pay reasonable maintenance and the marriage expenses of his daughter. Maintenance includes food, clothing, lodging, medical and education expenses and other needs for well-being, and under Para 370(1) of Muhammadan Law a father maintains his daughter until marriage. It is not a courtesy. Ref: 2022 LHC 7788; Muhammad Riaz Ahmad v. Shaheen Akhtar etc. (Family 40877/21, decided 10.11.2022); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Riaz Ahmad v. Shaheen Akhtar etc. (Family 40877/21, decided 10.11.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Police Independence: Art. 184(3) Petition
records.heading: Police cannot be an instrument for vested interests; integrity and independence are crucial
records.text: The Court observed that the police force cannot be made an instrument for vested or elite interests and that integrity, independence and trustworthiness are crucial. Notices were issued to Provincial Police Officers, Home Secretaries and the ICT administration to furnish eight years of data, and Punjab was to file its reply. Ref: Rana Tahir Saleem v. Province of Punjab through Chief Secretary to the Government of Punjab Lahore and others (Const.P. 34/2022, decided 23.11.2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Rana Tahir Saleem v. Province of Punjab through Chief Secretary to the Government of Punjab Lahore and others (Const.P. 34/2022, decided 23.11.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ of Quo Warranto: Conditions for Issuance
records.heading: Quo warranto may be sought by any bona fide member of the public
records.text: A writ of quo warranto tests whether a holder of a public office holds it lawfully. The petitioner need not be an aggrieved person, and it suffices that the relator is a member of the public acting bona fide, who may be a whistle blower without special interest. Ref: Jawad Ahmad Mir v. Prof. Dr. Imtiaz Ali Khan, Vice Chancellor, University of Swabi, District Swabi, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and others (C.P. 3944/2019, decided 18.10.2022).
records.title: Jawad Ahmad Mir v. Prof. Dr. Imtiaz Ali Khan, Vice Chancellor, University of Swabi, District Swabi, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and others (C.P. 3944/2019, decided 18.10.2022)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Appointment of Village Headman: Marks Under Rule 17
records.heading: Appointment of a village headman is essentially an administrative function of revenue authorities
records.text: The Court considered whether marks for hereditary claims under rule 17(1)(a) must be awarded in full or whether the Collector may withhold them. It stressed that appointment of a headman is essentially an administrative function belonging to the revenue authorities, who are better placed than Courts of general jurisdiction. Ref: Ahsan Khan v. Government of the Punjab etc. (I.C.A. No. 71340/2021, decided 31.10.2022).
records.title: Ahsan Khan v. Government of the Punjab etc. (I.C.A. No. 71340/2021, decided 31.10.2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Workers' Welfare Fund: Not a Tax, Not Retrospective
records.heading: The Workers' Welfare Fund is not a tax and the ruling is not retrospective
records.text: Following PLD 2017 SC 28, the Fund cannot be equated with tax and is not adjustable against a tax refund. That judgment cannot be applied retrospectively to recover WWF which FBR bona fide allowed to be adjusted under the relevant provisions. Ref: 2022 LHC 7886; MS Synthetic Products Enterprises Limited etc v. FBR through Chairman etc (Tax (Writ) 62961/21, decided 11.11.2022); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: MS Synthetic Products Enterprises Limited etc v. FBR through Chairman etc (Tax (Writ) 62961/21, decided 11.11.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A(6) CrPC: Justice of Peace and Registration of FIR
records.heading: A Justice of the Peace need not blindly direct registration of an FIR
records.text: Information of a cognizable offence falls under s. 154 CrPC. Section 22-A(6) CrPC does not oblige an ex-officio Justice of the Peace to issue a direction to register a case blindly whenever a complaint is filed. The judgment also examines the nature of the JOP's functions and how applications should be decided. Ref: 2022 LHC 7848; Ghulam Sarwar v. JOP etc. (39257/21, decided 16.11.2022); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Ghulam Sarwar v. JOP etc. (39257/21, decided 16.11.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Opinion of Police Not Binding on Court
records.heading: The opinion of the police does not bind the court
records.text: The opinion of the police is not binding on the court. The court must decide the case on the evidence produced before it, which must be admissible and reliable. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Stay of Criminal Proceedings During Civil Litigation
records.heading: Stay of criminal proceedings during civil litigation is discretionary and depends on prejudice
records.text: Stay of criminal proceedings pending civil litigation is discretionary, and no universal rule requires a stay merely because the subject matter is the same. The guiding test is whether the accused is likely to be prejudiced, for instance where criminal liability depends on or is intimately connected with the civil result. The High Court may stay under Art. 199 or s. 561-A CrPC. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Investigation of Non-Cognizable Offence: Effect on Cognizance
records.heading: Investigation of a non-cognizable offence without permission does not necessarily vitiate cognizance
records.text: Police cannot investigate a non-cognizable offence without Magistrate's permission under s. 155 CrPC. However, if a police officer acted through bona fide error and a competent court took cognizance under s. 190(1)(a) or (b) CrPC, cognizance is not necessarily vitiated absent serious prejudice or miscarriage of justice. There is no blanket protection for dishonest or mala fide police acts. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Not Condition Precedent to Investigation
records.heading: Registration of an FIR is not a condition precedent to investigation
records.text: Registration of an FIR under s. 154 CrPC is not a condition precedent to the commencement of investigation. Police may of their own motion investigate where they genuinely believe a cognizable offence has been committed, as s. 157 CrPC supports. The FIR provisions aim at obtaining early information and recording circumstances before they are forgotten or embellished. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Interpretation: 'By', 'Under', 'Not in Derogation Of'
records.heading: Prescribed by law differs from prescribed under it; not in derogation of means in addition to
records.text: Something provided in the main text of a statute is prescribed 'by' the law, whereas something provided through rules is 'under' the parent enactment, so the word 'under' leaves room for either route. The phrase 'and not in derogation of' means the same as 'in addition to'. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Principles for Examining Vires of a Statute
records.heading: Courts presume a statute is constitutional when examining its vires under Article 199
records.text: Under Art. 199 the court presumes a statute to be constitutional and prefers a valid interpretation where two are possible. Invalidity must be beyond reasonable doubt, narrower grounds are preferred to constitutional questions, the court is not concerned with wisdom of legislation, and mala fides are not attributed to the legislature. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 14: Dignity and Right to Reputation
records.heading: The right to reputation forms part of human dignity under Article 14
records.text: Human dignity is a cherished and inviolable value under Art. 14 of the Constitution, and it includes the right to reputation. A good name is an inherent personal right and an integral part of dignity. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 19: Freedom of Expression and Defamation
records.heading: Freedom of expression under Article 19 is subject to reasonable restrictions and defamation law
records.text: Explains freedom of speech and expression under Art. 19 as a fundamental right serving self-fulfilment, the search for truth and democracy, subject to reasonable restrictions. The post also lists considerations, such as the tone and circumstances of publication, relevant to defamation and qualified privilege. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: PECA Investigation Rules 2018: Non-Cognizable Offences
records.heading: Irregular investigation of non-cognizable PECA offences is cured by section 537 absent prejudice
records.text: Rule 6(3) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Investigation Rules 2018 allows complaints to a Cybercrime Reporting Centre, and r. 7 retains the cognizable and non-cognizable distinction. Non-cognizable offences are dealt with under s. 155 CrPC and need court permission. Any irregularity in investigation is cured by s. 537 CrPC absent prejudice or malice. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: S. 20 PECA: Offences Against Dignity
records.heading: Section 20 PECA is constitutional and consistent with Article 14
records.text: Section 20 PECA covers offensive and derisive language as well as defamation, and the Explanations and Exceptions of s. 499 PPC are read into it through ss. 28 and 50 PECA. The argument that it stifles free speech was rejected, and it was held not unconstitutional but in conformity with Art. 14. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 19: Legislative Competence for S. 20 PECA
records.heading: Parliament was competent to enact section 20 PECA even under amended Article 19
records.text: Fundamental rights protect against the State, and defamation is a private wrong. Parliament was competent to enact s. 20 PECA even under the amended Art. 19, and the section is also justifiable because defamation may endanger public order or incite an offence. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Quashing FIR: Vires Challenge and s. 249-A CrPC
records.heading: A vires challenge to quash an FIR cannot be decided by a Magistrate under section 249-A
records.text: Where the accused seeking quashing of an FIR challenged the vires of a statutory provision and raised questions of interpretation of the Constitution and statute, such questions could not be decided by a Magistrate in an application under s. 249-A CrPC. The constitutional petition was held competent. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of FIR: Alternate Remedy ss. 249-A, 265-K
records.heading: The High Court ordinarily does not quash proceedings where sections 249-A and 265-K provide a remedy
records.text: Art. 199 jurisdiction is extraordinary and available only where no adequate alternate remedy exists. Sections 249-A and 265-K CrPC ordinarily provide that remedy, so the High Court does not normally quash proceedings under Art. 199 or s. 561-A CrPC, though in exceptional circumstances it may intervene. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: PECA s. 20 and ss. 499, 500 PPC: Not Discriminatory
records.heading: Section 20 PECA and sections 499, 500 PPC satisfy reasonable classification under Article 25
records.text: PECA is lex specialis for cybercrimes and does not override the PPC, since s. 28 applies PPC provisions unless inconsistent. Section 20 PECA and ss. 499 and 500 PPC do not overlap and satisfy the test of reasonable classification under Art. 25 of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 773.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Conflicting Judgments: Appellate Findings Preferred
records.heading: Where trial and appellate judgments conflict, the appellate findings are preferred
records.text: Where the judgments of the Trial Court and the appellate court conflict, the findings of the appellate court are to be preferred and respected unless the record shows they are unsupported by evidence. Ref: 2022 YLR 2479.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Service Benefits Not Part of Tarka
records.heading: Group insurance, provident and benevolent funds are not tarka and not heritable
records.text: Group insurance, provident and benevolent funds are service benefits that mature only after the employee's death, so they are not tarka and not heritable. Salary due at death may be heritable. The revocation application was rightly dismissed, since the nominee's rights cannot be determined under the Succession Act, 1925 and lie before a Court of general jurisdiction. Ref: 2022 CLC 2030.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Interpretation of Provisos: Legislative Intent
records.heading: The purpose of a proviso is determined from legislative intent
records.text: Where a proviso appears in a law, its purpose must be determined from the intent of the legislature. Ref: 2022 CLC 2045.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Nomination Papers: Rectification of Defects, S. 62 Elections Act
records.heading: A Returning Officer must allow a non-substantial defect in nomination papers to be remedied
records.text: Under s. 62(9)(d)(ii) of the Elections Act, 2017 the Returning Officer shall not reject nomination papers for a defect that is not substantial and may allow it to be remedied. A candidate who pointed out the omission himself and applied within the ECP's timeframe was entitled to rectification. No illegality or perversity was found. Ref: 2022 CLC 2045.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Co-Sharer Cannot Change Nature of Joint Property
records.heading: A co-sharer in possession cannot change the nature of joint property before partition
records.text: Suit for declaration is not maintainable inter se co-owners, and no restriction can be placed on a co-sharer's right to sell his share. A co-sharer in possession of joint property cannot change its nature unless partition takes place by metes and bounds. Appellate Court's reversal of rejection of plaint upheld under Ss. 42 and 54 Specific Relief Act. Ref: 2022 YLR 2491.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: High Court Cannot Assume Jurisdiction in Matter Pending Before Supreme Court
records.heading: The High Court cannot assume Article 199 jurisdiction in a matter pending before the Supreme Court
records.text: Under Art. 199 of the Constitution, the High Court cannot assume constitutional jurisdiction in a matter that is already pending before the Supreme Court. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 817.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Term of Office and Tenure of Office: Local Government
records.heading: Term of office under section 30(1) is fixed and not extendable
records.text: Term of office is the fixed period set by the Constitution or statute, while tenure of office is the period actually held, which is variable. The word 'term' in s. 30(1) of the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 is fixed and not extendable; for representatives whose first meeting was held on 01.01.2017, the five years expired on 31.12.2021. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 817.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Judicial Estoppel: Inconsistent Positions
records.heading: Judicial estoppel bars a party from taking inconsistent positions before the Court
records.text: Judicial estoppel is an equitable doctrine precluding a party from taking inconsistent positions before the Court. A party who succeeds on a position of fact in one case is estopped from asserting a different position on the same facts in a later case. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 817.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Leave to Defend Needs Affidavit
records.heading: An application for leave to defend that raises disputed facts needs an affidavit
records.text: Where an application for leave to defend in a summary suit under Order XXXVII CPC requires resolution of disputed facts, it must be accompanied by an affidavit, failing which the Court is justified in dismissing it. Ref: 2022 LHC 7900; Muhammad Basheer v. Syed Imdad Ali Shah (Civil Revision 6746/20, decided 24.11.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Basheer v. Syed Imdad Ali Shah (Civil Revision 6746/20, decided 24.11.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation: Mixed Question of Law and Fact
records.heading: Limitation is a mixed question of law and fact the Court must decide
records.text: Limitation is a mixed question of law and fact, and the Court must decide it whether or not it has been raised as a defence. Ref: 2022 LHC 7900; Muhammad Basheer v. Syed Imdad Ali Shah (Civil Revision 6746/20, decided 24.11.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Basheer v. Syed Imdad Ali Shah (Civil Revision 6746/20, decided 24.11.2022)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: PECA S. 20 and PPC Ss. 499-500: Defamation
records.heading: PECA is lex specialis and section 20 PECA survives the discrimination challenge
records.text: PECA is lex specialis for cybercrime and does not override the PPC; S. 28 PECA applies the PPC to PECA offences unless inconsistent. S. 20 PECA and Ss. 499 and 500 PPC do not overlap and satisfy the reasonable classification test under Art. 25 of the Constitution, so the challenge of discrimination failed.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Stay of Criminal Proceedings Pending Civil Suit
records.heading: Criminal proceedings are stayed only where the accused is likely to be prejudiced
records.text: There is no universal rule that criminal proceedings must be stayed whenever a civil suit and criminal case share a subject-matter; stay is discretionary. The guiding principle is whether the accused is likely to be prejudiced. If criminal liability depends on, or is intimately connected with, the civil outcome so that conflicting decisions risk grave injustice, criminal proceedings must be held in abeyance. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 773.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Remission for Period Spent on Bail
records.heading: A convict on bail cannot count that period as sentence served
records.text: Under Rule 35 of the Pakistan Prisons Rules, 1978, the period an accused spends out of prison and is not again committed to prison is not counted as sentence served. A convict who remained on bail is not entitled to count that period as sentence served or to remissions for it. Ref: 2022 LHC 7905; Nasreem Akhtar Siddiqui v. Govt of Punjab etc (Criminal Proceedings 69955/21, decided 22.11.2022); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Nasreem Akhtar Siddiqui v. Govt of Punjab etc (Criminal Proceedings 69955/21, decided 22.11.2022)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Ingredients and S. 118 NIA Presumption
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC requires a cheque issued dishonestly towards an obligation and dishonoured
records.text: S. 489-F PPC is not attracted to every dishonour. Its elements are: the cheque was duly issued, with dishonest intent, towards repayment of a loan or fulfilment of an obligation, and was dishonoured on presentation. The presumption under s. 118 Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 favours the holder and can be rebutted at a regular trial. Ref: Ahmad Faran Sabir v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8564/M/2022).
records.title: Ahmad Faran Sabir v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8564/M/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Cheque: S. 118 NIA Presumption and Handwriting Comparison
records.heading: A defendant may rebut the section 118 presumption by evidence of non-payment of consideration
records.text: In a recovery suit on a cheque, the petitioner had not denied his signature on the cheque and had admitted its issuance in his written statement. A defendant may discharge the burden under s. 118 Negotiable Instruments Act by reliable evidence of non-payment of consideration, or by pointing to flaws in the plaintiff's evidence to show the presumption is rebutted. Ref: 2022 MLD 1955.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Column 16: House Undertaking After Khula
records.heading: Delivery of one room does not satisfy the column 16 house undertaking
records.text: Where column 16 of the nikahnama records the husband's undertaking to give the wife a house, delivery of one room does not satisfy the special condition. The case concerns enforcement of that condition after a decree of khula with badl-e-khula, the husband contending the house was given in lieu of dower; the father had earlier acknowledged the entry in a compromise. Ref: 2022 MLD 1982.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Quantum of Maintenance for Minor
records.heading: A father must maintain his child and the Family Court rightly fixed the quantum
records.text: A father is legally and morally bound to maintain his child. Considering the father's salary, the child's school-going status, rising expenses and the parties' status, the Family Court rightly fixed the quantum of maintenance, and the concurrent findings on evidence were upheld. Writ petition dismissed. Ref: 2022 MLD 1995.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Blocking CNIC to Compel Appearance Unlawful
records.heading: Section 18 NADRA Ordinance does not permit blocking a CNIC to compel appearance
records.text: S. 18 of the NADRA Ordinance, 2000 must be strictly construed, and does not permit blocking or digital impounding of a CNIC to compel a judgment-debtor's appearance in family execution or an accused's surrender. The Executing Court's order directing NADRA to block the CNIC was declared without legal authority and set aside; petition accepted. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 756.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Blasphemy Bail: Preaching Not a Crime, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Preaching is not a crime; blasphemy bail granted as a case of further inquiry
records.text: A Christian accused of preaching and blasphemy under ss. 295-A, 295-B and 295-C PPC. Preaching is not a crime given the right to profess and propagate religion, the book mentioned in the FIR had no blasphemous material, and the complainant took eight hours to inform the police. The case was treated as one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 751.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identity of Accused: Alias in FIR
records.heading: An alias in the FIR does not raise doubt about the identity of the accused
records.text: A discrepancy between the name in the FIR (Rasool Bakhsh, with alias Rasoola) and the convict's name (Ghulam Rasool) raised no doubt about identity, as the parties lived in the same vicinity, identity was never questioned and rural people are commonly known by aliases. Leave to appeal declined and petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 806.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Habeas Corpus: Case Diaries and Police Misconduct
records.heading: Case diaries are not an officer's property; police misconduct warranted an FIR against officers
records.text: A detenu was recovered from a police station without his arrest being recorded in the Roznamcha, and no case diary could be produced. Case diaries are not the investigating officer's personal property and must be maintained under the Police Rules, 1934. The SHO and investigating officer committed gross misconduct under the Police Order, 2002, and the High Court directed registration of an FIR against them. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 224.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Probation and Community Service Order, S. 5(2)
records.heading: A community service order has positive aspects under the Probation of Offenders Ordinance
records.text: Under S. 5(2) of the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960, the Court listed the positive aspects of a community service order, including restricting growth of prison numbers, reducing prison expenditure and enabling offenders to make reparation. The petition was converted into an appeal and partly allowed. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 795.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Protection of Women Against Violence Act 2016 Upheld
records.heading: The Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act 2016 is not repugnant to Islam
records.text: The Federal Shariat Court held that the Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act 2016 contains no provision repugnant to the Quran and Sunnah, and dismissed the petitions challenging it as without merit. Judgment dated 29.11.2022. Ref: Justice Syed Muhammad Anwer; Justice Khadim Hussain M. Sheikh.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Environmental Protection Act: Action Against Brick Kilns
records.heading: Brick kiln action must follow the statutory procedure, with remedy before the Environmental Tribunal
records.text: The Court explained the procedure under the Punjab Environmental Protection Act, 1997 for action against brick kilns not using zigzag technology. The agency, instead of following the statutory procedure, took extreme steps, which was deprecated; a person aggrieved by non-compliant proceedings has a remedy before the Environmental Tribunal under Ss. 21 and 22. Ref: 2022 LHC 7950; Nemat Ullah v. POP etc (Writ Petition 17916-22, decided 30.11.2022); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Nemat Ullah v. POP etc (Writ Petition 17916-22, decided 30.11.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal Powers and Admission: O. XII R. 6 CPC
records.heading: A Service Tribunal may decide on an unambiguous admission by analogy with Order XII Rule 6
records.text: Under S. 5(2) of the Service Tribunals Act, 1973 the Tribunal is deemed a Civil Court with CPC powers. Its judgment based on the Department's admission in its comments is considered by analogy with decree on admission under O. XII R. 6 CPC, which requires an unambiguous and unequivocal admission of liability. The doctrine of approbate and reprobate is also noted. Ref: Divisional Superintendent Postal Services Faisalabad v. Khalid Mahmood and others (C.P. 1874/2022, decided 06.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Divisional Superintendent Postal Services Faisalabad v. Khalid Mahmood and others (C.P. 1874/2022, decided 06.10.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Conveyance Allowance for Teachers During Vacations
records.heading: Conveyance allowance for teachers cannot be stopped during vacations
records.text: Conveyance allowance to teachers cannot be stopped during summer or winter vacations; doing so is illegal and discriminatory. Under S. 23 of the Civil Servants Act, 1973 terms and conditions of service cannot be varied to the civil servant's disadvantage. Ref: Government of K.P. through Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others v. Maqsad Hayat (C.P. 84-P/2020, decided 07.07.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Government of K.P. through Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others v. Maqsad Hayat (C.P. 84-P/2020, decided 07.07.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Declaration Suit Barred: Art. 120 and Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A declaration suit is limited to six years under Article 120 and limitation must be examined
records.text: The limitation for a declaration suit under Art. 120 of the Limitation Act is six years, and under S. 3 the Court must examine limitation whether or not raised. A declaration based on an agreement to sell from a non-title holder was also not maintainable. Revision dismissed and plaint rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC. Ref: 2022 LHC 7960; Muhammad Anwer Jawed v. Ghulam Muhammad etc (Civil Revision 58436/22, decided 28.09.2022); Justice Ch. Muhammad Masood Jahangir.
records.title: Muhammad Anwer Jawed v. Ghulam Muhammad etc (Civil Revision 58436/22, decided 28.09.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 476 CrPC: Limits on Proceedings
records.heading: Section 476 CrPC proceedings require an offence under section 195(1)(b) or (c)
records.text: Before proceeding under s. 476 CrPC, the Court must see that the complaint discloses an offence under s. 195(1)(b) or (c). The provision is not to be used for private vengeance or personal scores, and process is not to be issued routinely on every application by a litigant. Ref: Mehmood Ahmad v. ASJ etc (W.P. 73916/2022, decided 23.11.2022).
records.title: Mehmood Ahmad v. ASJ etc (W.P. 73916/2022, decided 23.11.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recall Order Not Revocable for Non-Deposit
records.heading: A recall order cannot be revoked merely for non-deposit of the imposed amount
records.text: Once the Court concluded the accused had not been afforded sufficient opportunity to cross-examine and ordered recall of witnesses, that order could not be recalled merely because the accused failed to deposit the Rs. 1,000 imposed within the specified time. Ref: 2004 MLD 1018.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Re-Investigation by Director General: R. 19 ACE Rules
records.heading: The Director General cannot sit in appeal over his own order directing a challan
records.text: Under R. 19 of the Punjab Anti-Corruption Establishment Rules, 1985, the Governor, Chief Secretary and Director may call for records and give directions. The Director General had no justification to sit in appeal against his own earlier order directing submission of challan, so the re-investigation order was declared illegal and without jurisdiction. Ref: 2009 MLD 337.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: S. 202 CrPC Applies to Special Judge Anti-Corruption
records.heading: Section 202 CrPC applies to a Special Judge Anti-Corruption
records.text: S. 202 CrPC begins with 'any Court' and so includes a Special Judge, and is not inconsistent with the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. Under Ss. 5 and 6 of that Act, the CrPC procedure applies to proceedings before the Special Judge (Central), who could therefore entrust inquiry of a private complaint. Ref: 2009 PCrLJ 235.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Court and Discharge Report: Re-Investigation
records.heading: On a discharge report the Trial Court may disagree with the investigating officer and direct trial
records.text: On a discharge report under S. 173 CrPC, the Trial Court may examine the material and disagree with the investigating officer's findings and direct trial. The order for re-investigation was set aside, with a direction to give definite findings on whether it agreed or disagreed with the discharge report. Ref: 2013 PCrLJ 1835.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning of Witnesses
records.heading: A plea under section 540 CrPC cannot be allowed to prolong the trial
records.text: The object of S. 540 CrPC is to serve the interest of justice, and a plea to summon a witness cannot be allowed to prolong the trial. Where the complainant had admitted execution of the power of attorney, summoning the Magistrate and the Forensic Science Laboratory official was unnecessary. Application dismissed and revision dismissed. Ref: 2013 PCrLJ 1043.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Defective Charge and S. 342 Examination: De Novo Trial
records.heading: A defective charge and missing certificate of inability required retrial
records.text: Failure to charge the accused according to the acts alleged against them under the penal provisions caused grave injustice, and a certificate of inability was mandatory where the Trial Court had not recorded evidence itself. Convictions and sentences were set aside and the case remanded for trial afresh. Appeal allowed. Ref: 2014 PCrLJ 1640.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Special Judge Cannot Direct Local Police to Investigate
records.heading: A Special Judge cannot direct local police to investigate an Anti-Corruption Establishment case
records.text: A Special Judge Anti-Corruption, invoking S. 5(6) of the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, wrongly directed local police to investigate a case within the ambit of the Anti-Corruption Establishment. High Court set aside that part of the order. Petition allowed. Ref: 2015 PCrLJ 379.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Criminal Breach of Trust: Acquittal on Evidence
records.heading: Conviction for criminal breach of trust set aside where evidence was wanting
records.text: In a prosecution under S. 409 PPC for misappropriation of forest trees, the evidence was found wanting: the co-accused witness was not independent, no evidence showed misappropriation of 35 trees, and evidence on a matter with no charge framed was a nullity. Conviction set aside and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2015 PCrLJ 1293.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Order Under S. 204: Revision Only
records.heading: An order summoning the accused under section 204 is challenged only by revision
records.text: A Magistrate's order disagreeing with a cancellation report and summoning the accused under S. 204 CrPC is a judicial order. It can be challenged only through criminal revision, and constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court cannot be invoked against it. Ref: 2015 PCrLJ 1103.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-K: Acquittal When Complainant Exonerates Accused
records.heading: Acquittal under section 265-K is proper where the complainant exonerates the accused
records.text: Where the complainant in a bribery case swore a statement exonerating the accused, the Special Judge committed no illegality in acquitting under S. 265-K CrPC, even though it was argued that S. 249-A applied. Appeal against acquittal dismissed in limine. Ref: 2016 PCrLJ 286.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Precedents in Criminal Cases Not Strictly Applied
records.heading: Precedents in criminal cases cannot be applied strictly as each case has its own facts
records.text: Precedents in criminal cases cannot be applied strictly, as each criminal case has its own peculiar facts and circumstances. Ref: 2016 PCrLJ 286.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Consolidated Trial of Thirty Transactions Under One Charge
records.heading: A single charge covering thirty transactions caused no prejudice under section 234 CrPC
records.text: Where a Postmaster misappropriated money from thirty savings accounts, the amended single charge covering all transactions was explicit and not vague. No prejudice resulted from consolidation under S. 234 CrPC, and the trial was not vitiated. Ref: 2017 PCrLJ Note 165.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Withdrawal from Prosecution: Court Must Examine Bona Fides
records.heading: The Court must examine whether withdrawal from prosecution is bona fide
records.text: Withdrawal of sanction three years after grant, without reasons and during trial, was mala fide. The Court must apply its mind to whether a request for withdrawal under S. 494 CrPC is bona fide and intended to foster justice, and not made to favour the accused. Revision dismissed. Ref: 2005 YLR 1669.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Cooperative Society Officers as Public Servants: Sanction
records.heading: Cooperative society office bearers are public servants for sanction purposes under section 65-B
records.text: Office bearers of a cooperative housing society are deemed public servants under S. 65-B of the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925. The Special Judge's order dismissing the complaint and acquitting for want of sanction was set aside, and the complaint was deemed pending before the Special Judge to proceed afresh. Ref: 2009 PCrLJ 875.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Binding Force of Supreme Court Decisions: Art. 189
records.heading: A Supreme Court decision binds all other courts under Article 189
records.text: Under Art. 189 of the Constitution, a decision of the Supreme Court is binding on all other courts. Ref: 2009 PCrLJ 875.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Cooperative Society Officers: Special Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Misappropriation by cooperative society officers is triable by the Special Court Anti-Corruption
records.text: Every officer of a society, including a co-operative bank, is deemed a public servant within S. 21 PPC under S. 65-B of the Co-operative Societies Act. Matters involving alleged misappropriation of public money are exclusively triable by the Special Court Anti-Corruption, and the jurisdictional objections were repelled. Ref: 2020 YLR 321.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal: S. 417 CrPC Principles
records.heading: Interference with an acquittal requires grave irregularity causing miscarriage of justice
records.text: The principles for an appeal against acquittal differ from those for an appeal against conviction. Interference with an acquittal is justified only where the Trial Court committed grave irregularity causing miscarriage of justice. Ref: 2020 YLR 321.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Person's Appeal Against Special Judge Acquittal
records.heading: A private person has no right of appeal against a Special Judge's acquittal
records.text: S. 417(1) CrPC gives a private person no right of appeal against acquittal by a court other than the High Court, and a prosecution witness is not an aggrieved person under S. 417(2-A). The right of appeal is statutory and cannot be inferred by implication, so the appeal against the Special Judge's acquittal was dismissed in limine. Ref: 2012 PCrLJ 420.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: No Appeal by Complainant Against Special Court Acquittal
records.heading: A complainant cannot appeal against a Special Court acquittal where the special law is silent
records.text: Where a special law is silent on appeal, the right cannot be inferred from the general law. The right of an aggrieved person under S. 417(2-A) CrPC does not extend to private persons in Special Court cases on scheduled offences, and a barred appeal cannot be converted into a petition under S. 561-A. Complainant's appeal dismissed. Ref: PLD 2006 Lahore 147.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift: Proof of Original Transaction Under S. 122 TPA
records.heading: The original transaction of a gift must be proved under section 122 TPA
records.text: Under S. 122 Transfer of Property Act, the original transaction of gift must be established as required by law, irrespective of whether it is evidenced by a registered deed. The case concerned a suit challenging a gift deed, general power of attorney and mutation. Ref: 2022 CLC 1973.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Does Not Run Against Co-Sharers in Inheritance
records.heading: Limitation does not run against co-sharers to deprive a legal heir of inheritance
records.text: Under S. 3 of the Limitation Act, limitation does not run against co-sharers and cannot be used to deprive a legal heir of his share in the inheritance. Ref: 2022 CLC 1973.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Surrender Before Hearing of Appeal: Inconsistent Practice
records.heading: Courts have been inconsistent on whether surrender before the court suffices before appeal
records.text: Commentary noting that the Lahore High Court, relying on 2012 SCMR 997, treated surrender before the court as sufficient, overruled the office objection and suspended a sentence. In a later case on similar facts, relying on 2015 SCMR 1570, the objection was maintained and surrender to police was required before the appeal would be heard. Ref: Deputy Commissioner Mandi Bahauddin v. Member Punjab Bar Council.
records.title: Deputy Commissioner Mandi Bahauddin v. Member Punjab Bar Council

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Appeal Against Special Judge's Order: Who May File
records.heading: Any aggrieved person may appeal to the High Court against a Special Judge's order
records.text: Under S. 10(1) of the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, the High Court is the forum for appeal and revision against a Special Judge's order. Any aggrieved person, including the Federal or Provincial Government, accused or complainant, may approach it against conviction, acquittal or for enhancement of sentence. Ref: PLD 2015 SC 348.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Suppression of Co-Accused's Bail Refusal
records.heading: Suppressing a co-accused's bail refusal reflects adversely and justifies cancellation of bail
records.text: Counsel who filed a bail application before the same High Court Judge without disclosing that the same relief had been refused to a co-accused only days earlier suppressed a material fact, which reflected adversely on the accused's bona fides. Bail allowed by the High Court was cancelled. Ref: PLD 2015 SC 242.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Custody Within Fifteen Days of Arrest: S. 167
records.heading: Total detention under section 167 CrPC cannot exceed fifteen days
records.text: A Judicial Magistrate may authorise detention in police or judicial custody from time to time, but total detention under S. 167 CrPC cannot exceed fifteen days. Within that period custody may be changed between police and judicial more than once. An Executive Magistrate may authorise detention for one week only. Appeals dismissed.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Return of Surety Documents Before Bond Executed
records.heading: Documents offered by a proposed surety must be returned until a bond is executed
records.text: A written declaration, even on oath, of readiness to stand surety does not make a person a surety. The offer must be accepted by the court and followed by execution of a bond, with verification of the surety's documents. Until then the return of offered documents cannot be refused. Application allowed. Ref: PLD 2017 Sindh 67; Aijaz-ul-Haq v. The State (Bail Application No. 1449 of 2008, decided 14.03.2016); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Aijaz-ul-Haq v. The State (Bail Application No. 1449 of 2008, decided 14.03.2016)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Delay in Acquisition Proceedings and Property Rights
records.heading: The executive may not sleep over acquisition proceedings and keep citizens waiting
records.text: Art. 24 of the Constitution protects property rights, and property may be acquired only for a public purpose with due compensation under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Where the law prescribes no time for an act, the executive may not sleep over the matter and keep citizens waiting in agony. Ref: 2022 LHC 7991; Shahid Mehmood etc v. District Collector etc (Writ Petition 2439-21, decided 17.11.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Shahid Mehmood etc v. District Collector etc (Writ Petition 2439-21, decided 17.11.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1(3) CPC: Bar on Subsequent Suit
records.heading: Whether a subsequent suit during an earlier suit is barred under Order XXIII Rule 1(3)
records.text: The post poses the question whether a subsequent suit instituted during the pendency of an earlier suit is hit by the bar in Order XXIII Rule 1(3) CPC. No holding is stated. Ref: Malik Zarin Khan v. Adnan Ali Malik etc (C.R. No. 3659 of 2016).
records.title: Malik Zarin Khan v. Adnan Ali Malik etc (C.R. No. 3659 of 2016)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Proforma Promotion of Retired District Judge
records.heading: A retired judge is entitled to proforma promotion from the date his junior was promoted
records.text: Since the appellant had retired while his matter was pending before the Performance Evaluation Committee, he is entitled to proforma promotion as District and Sessions Judge from the date his junior was promoted, with consequential benefits as per law. Ref: Muhammad Afzal Khan v. The Lahore High Court (Service Appeal No. 09 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Afzal Khan v. The Lahore High Court (Service Appeal No. 09 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Copy-Pasting Evidence from Main Case
records.heading: Copying evidence from a main case into an offshoot case is illegal
records.text: The High Court observed that copying evidence from the main case and pasting it into the evidence of an offshoot case is illegal and unlawful and must be stopped. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ Note 10.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Breach of Trust: Entrustment Under S. 405 PPC
records.heading: Section 405 PPC requires entrustment in a broad sense and dishonest misappropriation
records.text: S. 405 PPC requires entrustment of property and dishonest misappropriation, conversion or use in breach of law or contract. 'Entrustment' is used in a broad sense and 'trust' is comprehensive, covering relationships such as trustee and beneficiary, bailor and bailee, master and servant, and pledger and pledgee. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2001.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Concurrent Civil and Criminal Remedies
records.heading: Civil and criminal remedies for the same cause may be pursued concurrently
records.text: Remedies for the same cause may be pursued under both criminal and civil law. An act does not lose its criminal nature because it also gives rise to civil liability, and it is wrongly presumed that a challenge to civil liability makes criminal prosecution unsustainable. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2001.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of FIR in Constitutional Jurisdiction Set Aside
records.heading: The High Court wrongly quashed an FIR for breach of trust in constitutional jurisdiction
records.text: The High Court quashed an FIR for criminal breach of trust in constitutional jurisdiction, ignoring the contents of the crime report and the alternative remedy under the CrPC. As challan was not yet submitted, further material could be collected, and entrustment is for the Trial Court after evidence. Appeal allowed and judgment set aside. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2001.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Further Inquiry, Bogus Vehicle Registration
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail granted as further inquiry in a bogus vehicle registration case
records.text: An Excise officer posted in 2019 for a scam of 2015 to 2018, against whom the Investigating Officer found no nexus, and a data entry operator whose role did not include verification, were covered by S. 497(2) CrPC as cases of further inquiry. Pre-arrest bail granted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2068.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Abetment: Ingredients of Conspiracy Under S. 107 PPC
records.heading: Conspiracy under section 107 PPC requires instigation, engagement and intentional aid
records.text: Three ingredients are essential to treat a person as a conspirator under S. 107 PPC: instigation, engagement with co-accused, and intentional aid to the act or omission for the purpose of completing the abetment. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2077; Shameem Bibi v. State.
records.title: Shameem Bibi v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Not Conclusive Evidence
records.heading: A Call Data Record without concrete material is not conclusive evidence of guilt
records.text: In the absence of concrete material, the Call Data Record is not a conclusive piece of evidence to ascertain the guilt or otherwise of an accused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2077; Shameem Bibi v. State.
records.title: Shameem Bibi v. State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Scope of Second Appeal Under S. 100 CPC
records.heading: A second appeal lies only on the grounds in section 100 CPC
records.text: A second appeal lies only on the grounds in S. 100 CPC, and S. 101 bars any other ground. High Courts must not decide second appeals as first appeals, and in second appeal have no jurisdiction to reweigh witness testimony or reverse findings merely because another view is possible. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2006.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction Altered to S. 302(c) PPC: Minor, Spur of Moment
records.heading: Conviction altered to section 302(c) where the accused was a minor acting on the spur of the moment
records.text: The accused was a minor aged about 14, the occurrence was at the spur of the moment without premeditation, and the weapon was a motorcycle wire lock. Conviction under S. 302(b) PPC was altered to S. 302(c) PPC and life imprisonment reduced to the period already undergone. Petition converted into appeal and partly allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2143.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Eye-Witness Statements
records.heading: Minor discrepancies in eye-witness statements are inevitable and do not help the accused
records.text: Because of lapse of memory over time, minor discrepancies in eye-witness statements are inevitable and the accused cannot claim their benefit. Eye-witnesses who narrated the occurrence naturally were reliable enough to sustain the conviction. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2143.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Bona Fide Purchaser from Ostensible Owner: S. 41 TPA
records.heading: Purchasers who checked revenue records from ostensible owners are protected by section 41 TPA
records.text: Sons were ostensible owners through mutations sanctioned on unchallenged wills, and purchasers who checked the revenue records acted in good faith with reasonable care. S. 41 Transfer of Property Act applied and they were entitled to its equitable protection, without inquiring into consent of all legal heirs. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2130.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Will Executed and Acted Upon in Lifetime
records.heading: A will executed and acted upon in the testator's lifetime becomes an inter vivos instrument
records.text: A will operates after death, and ceases to be a will if executed and acted upon during the testator's lifetime. It then takes the guise of an inter-vivos instrument such as a gift, with its own requirements and standards of proof. S. 2(h) of the Succession Act is referred to. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2130.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody: Welfare of the Minor as Paramount
records.heading: The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in custody
records.text: The paramount consideration in custody is the welfare of the minor. The court exercises parental jurisdiction and considers the parents' ability to provide for physical and emotional needs, medical care and a safe home. There is no mathematical formula, and welfare covers physical, mental and emotional wellbeing. The post also refers to the UNCRC. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2123.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Abetment: Ingredients of Conspiracy Under S. 107 PPC
records.heading: Conspiracy under section 107 PPC requires instigation, engagement and intentional aid
records.text: Three ingredients are essential to treat a person as a conspirator under S. 107 PPC: instigation, engagement with co-accused, and intentional aid to the act or omission for completion of the abetment. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2024.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Dacoity with Murder: Meaning of 'Conjointly', S. 396 PPC
records.heading: Conjointly in sections 391 and 396 PPC means jointness of action and understanding
records.text: The word 'conjointly' in Ss. 391 and 396 PPC indicates jointness of action and understanding among the dacoits. S. 396 applies where five or more persons commit dacoity and any one commits murder, making all of them responsible for dacoity with murder and exposing them to its penalties. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2024.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Diminished Liability: Ghairat and Grave and Sudden Provocation
records.heading: Killing under ghairat and sudden provocation attracts section 302(c) through diminished liability
records.text: Diminished liability absolves an accused of part of the liability where his state of mind substantially impairs responsibility. Murder of the sister's alleged paramour, seen with her in an objectionable position, under ghairat and grave and sudden provocation attracted S. 302(c) PPC. Conviction under S. 302(b) was altered and sentence reduced to the period undergone. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2012.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Petition: O. XXIII R. 8 Supreme Court Rules
records.heading: The first proviso bar did not apply to a petition for recall of pre-arrest bail
records.text: The bar in the first proviso to R. 8, O. XXIII, Supreme Court Rules 1980 did not apply, as no order of imprisonment or fine was challenged; the matter concerned recall of pre-arrest bail. The second proviso applied, and the applicants undertook to appear and surrender. Registrar's office objection overruled. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2055.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Exclusive Jurisdiction Clause in Agreement
records.heading: An agreement selecting a particular court with jurisdiction is lawful and not against public policy
records.text: Parties cannot be barred from enforcing their rights in an ordinary court, but a mutual agreement selecting a particular court with territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction is lawful and not contrary to public policy. Ss. 16 and 17 CPC. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2044.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 10 CPC: Return of Plaint, Exclusive Jurisdiction
records.heading: An exclusive jurisdiction clause justifies return of the plaint under Order VII Rule 10
records.text: Although both courts had jurisdiction, a clause granting exclusive jurisdiction to the civil courts of place L bound the parties. Application under O. VII R. 10 CPC allowed, plaint to be returned for filing at place L, and the orders of the Civil Court and High Court set aside. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2044.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: No Arbitrary Relief Without Legal Authority
records.heading: No court may grant arbitrary relief without a power conferred by law
records.text: No court has jurisdiction to grant arbitrary relief unsupported by a power conferred by the Constitution or the law. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2114.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Act Must Be Done in Prescribed Manner
records.heading: Where the law prescribes a manner of doing a thing, it must be done that way
records.text: Where the law prescribes a particular manner of doing a thing, it must be done in that manner or not at all. Anything done contrary to it is illegal, ex facie erroneous and unsustainable. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2080.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Merits May Be Touched
records.heading: A court deciding pre-arrest bail may touch upon the merits of the case
records.text: It is established that while deciding pre-arrest bail the court may touch upon the merits of the case, relying on PLD 1989 SC 347, PLD 2021 SC 898, PLD 2022 SCMR 1424 and 2022 SCMR 1271. Ref: 2020 SCMR 2040.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Consistency With Co-Accused
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail follows consistency where a co-accused with the same role has bail
records.text: Where the petitioners' role cannot be distinguished from that of a co-accused already granted unchallenged post-arrest bail, refusing pre-arrest bail on the technical ground of different standards would be futile, since they would become entitled to post-arrest bail on consistency soon after arrest. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2040.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Cross-Examination by Prosecution Witness
records.heading: The prosecution may impeach its own witness who departs from his earlier statement
records.text: The prosecution may be permitted to impeach its own witness where his examination-in-chief departs from his earlier statement or is adverse to the prosecution, but not on the basis of answers given in defence cross-examination. A mere prosecution witness, not a legal heir, had no locus standi to apply. Arts. 133 and 151 QSO. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1026.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Surprise Evidence and Chance Witness
records.heading: A chance witness appearing first at trial without earlier statements casts doubt on the prosecution
records.text: A complainant's son, not named in her statement and who gave no statement during investigation, appeared first at trial. S. 265-C CrPC guards against surprise evidence, and Art. 151 QSO allows impeachment by former statements. The complainant's account shifted and lacked corroboration. Appeal accepted, conviction set aside, murder reference answered in the negative. Ref: 2019 YLR 2831; Muhammad Yasin v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Yasin v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 150 and 151 QSO: Hostile Witness
records.heading: Permission to question one's own witness is discretionary and requires equivocation or animosity
records.text: A court may permit a party to put questions to its own witness, but this is not a right, and the discretion must be exercised with caution. The party must show equivocation, variation, suppression of truth or animosity. The Investigating Officer, who only narrated his investigation, was not declared hostile and the revision was dismissed. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 1475.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Arts. 150 and 151 QSO
records.heading: Evidence of a hostile witness may ordinarily be ignored, subject to Article 150
records.text: Evidence of a hostile witness may ordinarily be ignored, subject to Art. 150 QSO. Art. 151 applies where the witness prevaricates, is animus towards the calling party or gives unfavourable evidence, and the witness is declared hostile with the court's permission. It also lists grounds for impeaching credit. Ref: 2019 YLR 18.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Evidence Beyond Pleadings; Cross-Examination
records.heading: What is not pleaded cannot be proved and inconsistent evidence is ignored
records.text: A recalled witness who was not confronted with his previous statement or pleadings and answered yes to every question gave evidence on matters not pleaded. What is not pleaded cannot be proved, and evidence inconsistent with the pleadings is ignored. Arts. 132(2), 140 and 141 QSO. Ref: 2005 YLR 1995.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC Statement as Evidence
records.heading: A section 164 statement is evidence only if made in the accused's presence with cross-examination
records.text: A witness's statement recorded under s. 164 CrPC can be treated as evidence only if it was made in the presence of the accused, who was given an opportunity to cross-examine. Art. 133 QSO. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 286.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC: Cross-Examination During Investigation
records.heading: Cross-examination during investigation does not prejudice the accused's right to cross-examine at trial
records.text: The right of cross-examination under s. 164 CrPC does not prejudice the accused's right to cross-examine the witness at trial. The statement remains a piece of investigation evidence either way and may be used for contradiction under Art. 140 QSO, in line with fair trial under Art. 10-A. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1564.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 133(3) QSO: Right to Re-Examine Witness
records.heading: The producing party has an absolute right to re-examine where explanation is needed
records.text: Re-examination arises after cross-examination and aims to clear ambiguity or explain a matter raised in it. The word 'shall' in Art. 133(3) QSO gives the producing party an absolute right to re-examine where explanation is needed. New matter requires leave of the court, and the adverse party may then cross-examine on it. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 537; Muhammad Shahid v. Aqeel and 5 others (Criminal Revision No. 01/2020/BWP).
records.title: Muhammad Shahid v. Aqeel and 5 others (Criminal Revision No. 01/2020/BWP)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed FIR: Tampering and Inquest Report
records.heading: A careful reading of the inquest report can show that an FIR was delayed and tampered
records.text: The court observed that police tamper with the FIR Register and Station Diary so that delayed reports appear spontaneous. A careful perusal of the inquest report prepared under the Police Rules, 1934 can show that the case was not registered at the time stated in the FIR. Ref: Hafeez Ahmed & another v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 113 of 2020).
records.title: Hafeez Ahmed & another v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 113 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Cannot Discharge Accused After Challan
records.heading: Police cannot discharge an accused after a complete challan and cognizance
records.text: After a complete challan under s. 173 CrPC is submitted and cognizance taken, the police cannot discharge the accused on re-investigation or file a supplementary challan. Only the trial court can consider a discharge report. The police discharge order was declared illegal and quashed. Ref: 2000 PCrLJ 1551.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Amended Promotion Rules Not Retrospective
records.heading: Amended promotion rules cannot apply retrospectively
records.text: Amended promotion rules cannot apply retrospectively. Employees who completed PIPFA before the DPC met had to be considered under the Recruitment Rules notified by S.R.O. 639(I)/2014 and not under S.R.O. 690(I)/2020. Ref: Controller General of Accounts, Government of Pakistan, Islamabad and another v. Abdul Waheed (C.P. 1775/2022, decided 28.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Controller General of Accounts, Government of Pakistan, Islamabad and another v. Abdul Waheed (C.P. 1775/2022, decided 28.09.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Reko Dik Presidential Reference: Short Opinion
records.heading: The new Reko Dik agreement contained nothing unlawful, in the Court's short opinion
records.text: In its short opinion on a reference under Art. 186, the Court held that the new Reko Dik agreement contained nothing unlawful, was not contrary to the 2013 judgment, and that provinces may amend mineral laws. It noted that the Constitution does not permit agreements over national assets contrary to law. Ref: Presidential Reference No. 2 of 2022; Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Presidential Reference No. 2 of 2022

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial Review of Judicial Commission Decisions
records.heading: Judicial Commission decisions are reviewable under Article 199 only within its limited scope
records.text: Art. 199 confers power in the nature of certiorari, directing a court under the High Court's superintendence to correct errors of law or jurisdiction. Judicial review of Judicial Commission of Pakistan decisions under Art. 175A requires analysis of the scope of Art. 199. The constitutional petition was bound to fail. Ref: Muhammad Azim Khan Afridi v. The President of Pakistan thr. the Principal Secretary, Islamabad & others (C.P. 3413/2017, decided 22.08.2022); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan.
records.title: Muhammad Azim Khan Afridi v. The President of Pakistan thr. the Principal Secretary, Islamabad & others (C.P. 3413/2017, decided 22.08.2022)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction Petition Between Co-Owners
records.heading: An eviction petition between co-owners fails without partition by metes and bounds
records.text: An eviction petition by one co-owner against another is not maintainable without partition by metes and bounds, particularly where such partition has not been proved in accordance with law. Ref: 2022 MLD 2051.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses in Murder Trials
records.heading: Calling independent witnesses chance witnesses does not make their evidence suspect
records.text: Describing independent witnesses as chance witnesses does not make their evidence suspicious or their presence doubtful. Murders are not committed with notice to witnesses, and inmates of a house or passers-by in a street are natural witnesses. Their evidence cannot be brushed aside on that ground alone. Ref: AIR 1953 SC 459; Puran v. The State of Punjab.
records.title: Puran v. The State of Punjab

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F(7) CrPC: Process for Defence Evidence
records.heading: Process for defence evidence may be refused only for vexation, delay or defeating justice
records.text: The court may refuse process for a defence witness or document only if the application is for vexation, delay or defeating justice. The accused need show only that the evidence is admissible and prima facie relevant. Refusal to summon the police register was contrary to ss. 94 and 265-F(7) CrPC and Art. 10-A. Ref: 2020 MLD 62; Muhammad Tanveer v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Tanveer v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F(6) CrPC: Right to Adduce Defence Evidence
records.heading: The word shall in section 265-F(6) obliges the court to allow defence evidence
records.text: The word 'shall' in s. 265-F(6) CrPC places an obligation on the trial court to let the accused adduce defence evidence, and ss. 340(2) and 265-F(6) are mandatory, in line with Art. 10-A. The refusal to allow earlier trial statements and judgment was set aside, and the revision accepted. Ref: 2017 MLD 1611; Asif v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 844 of 2015).
records.title: Asif v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 844 of 2015)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Prosecution Witnesses Without Cursory Statements
records.heading: The trial court may summon witnesses in a private complaint without cursory statements
records.text: In a private complaint, ss. 244(2) and 265-F CrPC give the trial court wide power to summon persons likely to know the facts. Recording a cursory or s. 161 statement is not a legal requirement. The revisional order was set aside and the trial court's order restored. Ref: 2016 PCrLJ 599; Muhammad Anwar v. Additional Sessions Judge Mian Channu and 7 others (W.P. No. 14300 of 2011).
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. Additional Sessions Judge Mian Channu and 7 others (W.P. No. 14300 of 2011)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Record Keeper of Excise Office
records.heading: Refusing to summon the Excise record keeper for delay denied a fair trial
records.text: The trial court could not refuse to summon the Excise record keeper to prove ownership of the motorcycle on the ground of delay, since the office was in the same city. The order denied fair trial under Art. 10-A, and the High Court directed the record keeper to be summoned. Ref: 2015 YLR 782.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Late Production of Documents by Prosecution
records.heading: Documents produced late through the Public Prosecutor are not inadmissible for that reason alone
records.text: Documents produced through the Public Prosecutor under s. 493 CrPC are not inadmissible merely because they were not produced under s. 265-F at an earlier stage. Where genuineness is not questioned, the court may admit them later if necessary for a just decision, and may then assess their intrinsic value. Ref: 2012 PCrLJ 73.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Police Officer as Defence Witness
records.heading: A court must issue process for a defence witness unless it records grounds for refusal
records.text: Under s. 265-F(7) CrPC the court must issue process for a defence witness, and may refuse only for vexation, delay or defeating justice, with reasons recorded. The trial court gave no solid reason for refusing to summon the investigating police officer. The High Court directed that he be summoned. Ref: 2007 PCrLJ 24.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 265-A and 265-F(2) CrPC: Who Names Prosecution Witnesses
records.heading: In a complaint case only the complainant names witnesses under section 265-F(2)
records.text: In cases on police report the court ascertains from the Public Prosecutor the persons to be produced as witnesses. The word complainant in s. 265-F(2) CrPC means the complainant in a complaint case, who alone may name witnesses in a private complaint. Ref: 2004 PCrLJ 1353.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Rapt on Which FIR Was Based
records.heading: Discretion to summon the Rapt behind an FIR must be exercised judiciously
records.text: The complainant sought to summon the Rapt on which the FIR was recorded, and the Magistrate and Sessions Judge refused it as not part of the challan or police file. The post notes that the FIR itself was based on the Rapt and that discretion under ss. 244 and 265-F CrPC must be exercised judiciously. Ref: 2004 MLD 1040.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Belated Application to Summon Court Witness
records.heading: A belated application to summon a court witness without new facts was rightly refused
records.text: An application to summon a court witness after charge and recording of prosecution evidence, with no new fact and no earlier request, was rightly refused under s. 540 CrPC. S. 265-F(3) also allows refusal where summoning is for vexation or delay. The revision court could not interfere with the reasoned order. Ref: 2003 YLR 2101.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Investigating Officer for Opinion
records.heading: A court rightly refused to summon an officer for his opinion as police opinion does not bind
records.text: The complainant sought to summon the later Investigating Officer for his opinion, although he had recorded no s. 161 statement and collected no material. The trial court rightly refused under s. 265-F(3) CrPC, as police opinion does not bind the court. The constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: 2003 YLR 1178.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Process for Defence Witness: Reasons Required
records.heading: Refusal of process for a defence witness requires written reasons
records.text: A trial court may refuse process for a defence witness under s. 265-F(7) CrPC only if the purpose is vexation, delay or defeating justice, and must record the grounds in writing. Refusal for extraneous reasons was set aside, with a direction to summon the witness who had supported the alibi. Ref: 2003 PCrLJ 416.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Eye-Witnesses Not Named in FIR
records.heading: Eye-witnesses not named in the FIR may be summoned under section 540 CrPC
records.text: The trial court wrongly dismissed the complainant's application to summon two claimed eye-witnesses because they were not named in the FIR or supplementary statements. Under s. 540 CrPC the court may summon any person whose evidence is essential for a just decision. The trial court was directed to summon them. Ref: 2003 MLD 1296.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recall of Witness by Prosecution
records.heading: The court must call a witness whose evidence is necessary, even before closure of the prosecution case
records.text: The prosecution may bring evidence omitted through human error before it closes its case, and s. 540 CrPC gives wide power to call a witness. The court is bound to call a witness whose statement is necessary for a just decision. Refusal before closure of the prosecution case was illegal. Ref: 2001 YLR 746.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Production of Documents Not Listed With Challan
records.heading: Documents on ownership not listed with the challan may be admitted at trial
records.text: Receipts about ownership of ornaments were not listed with the challan under s. 265-C CrPC, but ownership of property could be proved at trial under Arts. 18 to 45 QSO. The trial court rightly allowed the documents on record as admissible. Ref: 1998 PCrLJ 271.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F(3) CrPC: Refusal to Summon Won-Over Witnesses
records.heading: Won-over witnesses given up in haste need not be summoned under section 265-F(3)
records.text: Where witnesses were given up in haste without proper steps to serve them, and the Investigating Officer stated that the FIR witnesses had resiled and another set was introduced, the trial court rightly refused to summon the won-over witnesses under s. 265-F(3) CrPC. Ref: 1986 PCrLJ 2157.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Independent Witnesses as Court Witnesses
records.heading: Failure to examine material independent witnesses as court witnesses causes miscarriage of justice
records.text: The petitioner, placed in Column No. 2 of the challan but summoned by the trial court, sought to call three independent witnesses examined by police. They were material to a just decision under s. 540 CrPC, and failure to examine them as court witnesses occasioned a miscarriage of justice. Ref: 1980 PCrLJ 1119.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Injured Witness Not Named in Calendar of Witnesses
records.heading: An injured witness not in the calendar of witnesses caused no prejudice to the accused
records.text: An injured witness named in the FIR and examined at trial, without defence objection and after lengthy cross-examination, caused no violation of law although not in the calendar of witnesses and no s. 161 copy was supplied. The accused was not prejudiced. The post also explains the object of ss. 265-C and 265-F CrPC. Ref: 2007 SCMR 1631.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-D CrPC: Discharge of Accused
records.heading: The trial court must examine all prosecution material before discharging an accused under section 265-D
records.text: Before exercising the power of discharge under s. 265-D CrPC, the trial court must examine the entire material placed on record by the prosecution. Ref: PLD 2005 SC 408.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Investigation, Prosecution and Trial: Roles Under CrPC
records.heading: Investigation, prosecution and trial are distinct roles; the officer's opinion on guilt is outside his domain
records.text: Investigation, prosecution and trial are three pillars of the criminal justice system. The Investigating Officer's opinion on guilt is outside his domain. Where evidence is lacking he submits a negative final report under ss. 173 and 169 CrPC, and the trial court may acquit under s. 265-K or 249-A where conviction is improbable. Ref: 2010 PCrLJ 182.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-D CrPC: Framing of Charge
records.heading: For framing a charge the court consults only the material specified in section 265-D
records.text: For framing a charge the court consults only the police report, complaint, documents and prosecution statements under s. 265-D CrPC. The trial court wrongly deleted offences under ss. 367-A, 377 and 511 PPC despite prima facie material. Revision allowed and the trial court directed to proceed according to law. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 1358.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Temporary Injunction: Three Ingredients
records.heading: A temporary injunction requires a prima facie case, irreparable loss and balance of convenience
records.text: A plaintiff seeking a temporary injunction must show a prima facie case, possible irreparable loss if it is refused, and a balance of convenience in his favour. The prima facie case is foundational, and the other two conditions are considered only once it is established. O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC. Ref: 2022 CLC 2094.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Restoration of Restoration Application: Limitation
records.heading: A second restoration application is governed by Article 181 with three years
records.text: An application to restore an earlier restoration application, both dismissed for non-prosecution, is not an application under O. XLI R. 19 CPC with 30 days under Art. 168. It is an application under s. 151 CPC governed by residuary Art. 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908, with three years. The vague, non-speaking order could not be sustained. Ref: 2022 CLC 2007.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: S. 24 Pre-emption Act: Deposit of Zar-e-Soim
records.heading: A pre-emptor cannot be penalised where the court passed no deposit order
records.text: Under s. 24 of the Pre-emption Act the court must require the pre-emptor to deposit one third of the sale price within a period fixed by it, capped at 30 days from filing by the first proviso. If the court passes no deposit order, the pre-emptor cannot be penalised, since no one is prejudiced by an act of the court. Ref: 2022 CLC 2126.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Promissory Note: Essentials and Proof
records.heading: A proved promissory note carries a presumption once execution and contents are established
records.text: A promissory note requires an unconditional undertaking to pay a certain sum of money to a certain person or order or to bearer, signed by the maker. Once its existence, execution and contents are proved under Arts. 72, 75 and 79 QSO, the presumption attaches. The respondent proved the note, and the appellant's inadmissibility contention failed. Ref: 2022 CLC 2115.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: S. 118 Negotiable Instruments Act: Presumption of Consideration
records.heading: The person denying consideration under section 118 must allege and prove it
records.text: Under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act the instrument is presumed to be made for consideration. The presumption is rebuttable, and the onus lies on the person denying consideration to allege and prove it. Absent satisfactory evidence, the presumption operates. Ref: 2022 CLC 2115.
