records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Adverse Revenue Entry: When Right to Sue Accrues
records.heading: The right to sue accrues on actual denial, not on apprehended denial of a right
records.text: Authority on the principles for deciding when the right to sue accrues to a donor or owner seeking a declaration of ownership after an adverse entry in the revenue record (Jamabandi), distinguishing actual denial of right from apprehended or threatened denial. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1282.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Specific Performance Suit Barred by Res Judicata and Limitation
records.heading: A specific performance suit was barred by res judicata and limitation
records.text: A suit of 1992 for specific performance of a 1966 agreement was barred by res judicata under s. 11 CPC, since the vendor's earlier unchallenged decree bound the vendee, and was beyond the period of limitation under Art. 113. The lower courts and High Court had not considered these objections. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1275.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation in Inheritance Suits: Accrual of Cause of Action
records.heading: In inheritance disputes the cause of action accrues when a legal heir is denied rights
records.text: In inheritance disputes the cause of action accrues only when a legal heir is denied his or her rights, and time runs from then. The defendant heirs bear the burden of proving this. Limitation becomes relevant where the claimant's conduct shows acquiescence, especially when third party interests were created. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 812.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Against Void Orders
records.heading: Limitation runs even against a void order and date of knowledge must be proved
records.text: Limitation runs even against a void order, and delay cannot be condoned on that ground alone. A person making a belated claim must plead and prove by cogent evidence his date of knowledge to bring the claim within time. Ref: 2020 SCMR 2046.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fraud in Inheritance: Limitation
records.heading: Limitation never runs against fraud, particularly in female inheritance rights
records.text: Limitation never runs against fraud, particularly in matters involving the inheritance rights of a female. Ref: 2020 SCMR 352.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Suit Pleaded as Inheritance but Not Proved
records.heading: The bar of limitation applies fully where an inheritance claim is not proved
records.text: Where a suit is pleaded to concern inheritance but the plaintiff fails to prove that it does, the law and bar of limitation apply fully. Ref: 2020 SCMR 668.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fraud or Misrepresentation and Expiry of Limitation
records.heading: A transaction resulting from fraud cannot be protected by expiry of limitation
records.text: A transaction or document resulting from fraud or misrepresentation cannot be perpetuated or protected on the ground that limitation has expired, whenever it is assailed in court. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 338.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Between Co-Sharers
records.heading: No question of limitation arises between co-sharers in possession of joint property
records.text: No question of limitation arises in litigation between co-sharers, as every co-sharer is presumed to be in possession of every inch of the joint property. Ref: 2019 SCMR 567.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Lahore High Court Directions on Rape Cases
records.heading: Lahore High Court directions on the investigation and trial of rape cases
records.text: Authority on the Lahore High Court's latest directions for the investigation and trial of rape cases. Ref: 2022 LHC 8114; Muhammad Aamar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 54853/22, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Aamar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 54853/22, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence in Appeal
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal cannot be used to patch up weak parts of a case
records.text: O. XLI R. 27 CPC has limited scope. An appellate court may admit additional evidence where it cannot pronounce judgment owing to lacunas or defects in the evidence, but a party cannot use it to patch up weak parts of its case or fill omissions left before the trial court. Ref: 2022 LHC 8093; Altaf Ahmed v. Muhammad Anwar (Civil Revision 599-83, decided 26.10.2022); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Altaf Ahmed v. Muhammad Anwar (Civil Revision 599-83, decided 26.10.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation in Inheritance Cases: Third Party Interest
records.heading: Limitation is relevant in inheritance cases where a third party interest has been created
records.text: The law of limitation is relevant in inheritance cases where a third party interest has been created in the property. The post gives only this proposition with the listed citations and no facts or outcome. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1558, PLD 2022 SC 353, PLD 2021 SC 812.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Fraud Vitiates the Most Solemn Proceedings
records.heading: Fraud vitiates the most solemn of proceedings
records.text: Fraud vitiates the most solemn of proceedings. The post lists authorities for the proposition without facts or outcome. Ref: 2022 SCMR 595, 2022 PLC (C.S.) 745, PLD 2022 SC 85, 2011 SCMR 986 and others.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Case Diary: Ss. 172 and 162 CrPC
records.heading: Police diaries under section 172 aid inquiry but are not evidence
records.text: Police diaries under s. 172 CrPC may be sent for by the court as an aid to inquiry or trial, not as evidence, and the accused cannot call for or see them merely because the court referred to them. The police officer may refresh memory from them if the court used them for contradiction. Revision disposed of. Ref: 2014 PCrLJ 1236.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 161 and 172 CrPC: Witness Statement in Case Diary
records.heading: A witness statement in a case diary keeps its character as a section 161 statement
records.text: A witness statement embodied in the case diary instead of being recorded separately is at best a procedural lapse by the Investigating Officer. It keeps its character as a s. 161 CrPC statement and does not become part of the case diary under s. 172. Ref: 2021 SCMR 1914.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused's Right to Copies of Police Statements
records.heading: The accused is entitled to copies of all police statements, including those in case diaries
records.text: Statements of all persons examined by police, whether or not cited as witnesses, and whether or not described as recorded under s. 161 CrPC, must be supplied to the accused before trial. This includes statements embodied in a case diary under s. 172 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2017 Lahore 228.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 161 and 172 CrPC: Privilege of Case Diaries
records.heading: Only case diaries are privileged; section 161 statements are not
records.text: S. 161 CrPC is independent of s. 172. Only the case diaries are privileged, and this privilege is not absolute. Statements under s. 161 are not privileged even if recorded in a case diary, and are public documents under Art. 49 QSO. Under Art. 15 QSO the court may make the Investigating Officer consult the diaries. Ref: PLD 2003 Lahore 290.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 172(2) CrPC: Police Diary and Injunctions of Islam
records.heading: A section 172 police diary is not evidence and no judgment can rest on it
records.text: Information under s. 172 CrPC is not evidence, is not admissible and is not on par with a s. 161 statement. The diary records only the investigation procedure, and no judgment can rest on it even if the court consults it. The Shariat petition against s. 172(2) was dismissed. Ref: PLD 2014 FSC 15.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Definition of Sale and Limitation for Pre-emption Suit
records.heading: Section 31 gives 120 days from registration of the sale deed for a pre-emption suit
records.text: The post sets out the definition of sale in s. 2(d) of the Act as a permanent transfer of ownership of immovable property for valuable consideration, and s. 31, which gives 120 days from the date of registration of the sale deed for a pre-emption suit. Ref: Syed Asad Hussain & others v. Syed Ghulam Khitab (Civil Appeal No. 232-P of 2014, decided 24.11.2022).
records.title: Syed Asad Hussain & others v. Syed Ghulam Khitab (Civil Appeal No. 232-P of 2014, decided 24.11.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Proof of Agreement to Sell and Payment
records.heading: A plaintiff must prove an agreement to sell through two marginal witnesses and prove payment
records.text: A plaintiff must prove the agreement to sell through two marginal witnesses and prove payment of consideration. Oral proof of payment contradicting the agreement must be pleaded and strongly proved. Where execution is denied, the plaintiff should seek signature or thumb impression comparison. A party can prove only what it has pleaded. Ref: Muhammad Ghaffar (deceased) through LRs and others v. Arif Muhammad (C.P.L.A. No. 1511 of 2022, decided 24.11.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Ghaffar (deceased) through LRs and others v. Arif Muhammad (C.P.L.A. No. 1511 of 2022, decided 24.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Liberty and Merits
records.heading: Liberty cannot be taken away on bald and vague allegations
records.text: Liberty is a constitutionally guaranteed right that cannot be taken away on bald and vague allegations. The first pre-arrest bail petition was dismissed for non-appearance although counsel had informed the court, and the second petition was then dismissed. While granting pre-arrest bail, the merits of the case can be touched upon. Ref: Muhammad Tanveer etc v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 1442 of 2022, decided 01.12.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Tanveer etc v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 1442 of 2022, decided 01.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Abetment Allegation, Suckling Child, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail granted where the abetment allegation lacked particulars and the case needed further inquiry
records.text: The abetment allegation lacked date, time, place or witnesses, and the ingredients of s. 107 PPC were prima facie missing. A call data record is not conclusive without other material. The petitioner had a suckling child in jail and the case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC as one of further inquiry, so bail was granted. Ref: Mst. Asiya v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 1267 of 2022, decided 18.11.2022).
records.title: Mst. Asiya v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 1267 of 2022, decided 18.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Two Possible Views of Forensic Report
records.heading: Where a forensic report allows two views, the one favouring the accused is adopted
records.text: Where the Forensic Science Agency report allows two views, the one favouring the accused must be adopted. Heinousness not proved to the hilt is no ground for punishment, and a single doubt suffices for the benefit of doubt. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: Saghir Ahmed v. The State etc (Jail Petition No. 300 of 2022, decided 28.11.2022).
records.title: Saghir Ahmed v. The State etc (Jail Petition No. 300 of 2022, decided 28.11.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeal by Non-Party: Separate Application for Leave
records.heading: A non-party must file a separate application for leave to appeal
records.text: A person who was not a party to the proceedings below must file a separate application for leave to appeal the judgment, decree or order along with the memorandum of appeal. Ref: Kanwar Arif Ali Khan v. Danis Ali (C.P. 3509/2021, decided 01.12.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Kanwar Arif Ali Khan v. Danis Ali (C.P. 3509/2021, decided 01.12.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Public Servant Distinguished From Civil Servant
records.heading: All civil servants are public servants but not all public servants are civil servants
records.text: Civil servant and government servant have almost the same meaning, whereas public servant under s. 21 PPC has wider scope and applies only for penal and related procedural law. All civil servants are public servants, but not all public servants are civil servants. Employees of a statutory corporation are not civil servants under the Civil Servants Act 1973. Ref: Muhammad Naeem v. Federation of Pakistan thr. Secretary M/o Finance Division, Islamabad & others (C.P. 4294/2019, decided 25.11.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Naeem v. Federation of Pakistan thr. Secretary M/o Finance Division, Islamabad & others (C.P. 4294/2019, decided 25.11.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Amendment of Pleadings: Interest of Justice
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings is allowed in the interest of justice to decide the real controversy
records.text: In deciding an application to amend pleadings, the court keeps the interest of justice in view so that the real controversy is decided. Amendment may be allowed despite delay, at any stage and in some cases in appeal or revision, if it is expedient for determining the real questions and does not change the nature of the pleadings. Ref: Ahmad Bakhsh v. Imam Bakhsh & others (Civil Revision No. 950 of 2019, decided 08.12.2022).
records.title: Ahmad Bakhsh v. Imam Bakhsh & others (Civil Revision No. 950 of 2019, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Inheritance: Recurring Cause of Action
records.heading: No limitation runs in inheritance matters with a recurring cause of action
records.text: No limitation runs in inheritance matters with a recurring cause of action, and a party may claim an inherited right at any time unless guilty of gross negligence and abandonment. A transaction resulting from misrepresentation cannot be protected by limitation. Adverse revenue entries give fresh cause of action and, if unchallenged, do not extinguish the right. Ref: Allah Ditta v. Ali Shah (deceased) through Legal Heirs & others (Civil Revision No. 1095-D of 2010, decided 08.12.2022).
records.title: Allah Ditta v. Ali Shah (deceased) through Legal Heirs & others (Civil Revision No. 1095-D of 2010, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Liability of Company and Signatory
records.heading: A company can be prosecuted under section 489-F but a signatory's liability needs proof
records.text: The word whoever in s. 489-F PPC covers natural and juristic persons, and s. 11 PPC defines person to include a company, so a company can be prosecuted for a dishonoured cheque. The offence is not one of strict liability and requires proof of dishonesty. A signatory's liability requires proof that he was in charge of the company's operations at the time. Ref: Kabeer Akbar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 52233/B/2022, decided 08.12.2022).
records.title: Kabeer Akbar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 52233/B/2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Mandamus or Quo Warranto: Release of Officer to Federal Government
records.heading: A request to relieve an officer for Federal service is mandamus, not quo warranto
records.text: Where an outsider seeks a direction to the Provincial Government to relieve a government officer so that he may join the Federal Government, the relief is in the nature of mandamus and not quo warranto. The petitioner must therefore show that he is an aggrieved party. Ref: 2022 LHC 8172; Mohsin Rasool v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 68367/22, decided 01.11.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Mohsin Rasool v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 68367/22, decided 01.11.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: Future Maintenance and Procedure
records.heading: A Family Court may grant future maintenance for a child even if unclaimed
records.text: A Family Court may grant future maintenance for a child even if unclaimed, acting in its parental capacity, and procedural convenience must be resolved in favour of women and children. The failure to formally implead the child caused no miscarriage of justice. Under s. 17 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 the CPC applies only as to ss. 10 and 11. Ref: Arif Fareed v. Bibi Sara and others (C.P. 5601/2021, decided 06.12.2022); Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Arif Fareed v. Bibi Sara and others (C.P. 5601/2021, decided 06.12.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Abatement of Criminal Appeal on Death of Accused
records.heading: A criminal appeal abates on the death of the accused except as to a fine
records.text: An appeal against a sentence of death or imprisonment abates on the death of the accused and survives only as to a sentence of fine. Compensation of Rs. 500,000 under s. 544-A CrPC cannot be considered a fine. The court also explained the legal consequence of abatement in answer to the argument about loss of service benefits. Ref: 2022 LHC 8195; Khuda Bakhsh v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 1164-18, decided 14.11.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Khuda Bakhsh v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 1164-18, decided 14.11.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Domicile Distinguished From Residence
records.heading: Residence involves permanency and differs from domicile, which requires animus manendi
records.text: Animus manendi means the intention of remaining. Residence involves an element of permanency and does not mean occasional or intermittent dwelling for a particular period. The post also notes the doctrine of legitimate expectation. Ref: District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.P. 448-P/2017, decided 16.12.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.P. 448-P/2017, decided 16.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XI CPC: Striking Off Defence for Failure to Answer Interrogatories
records.heading: A defendant who fails to answer interrogatories may have his defence struck out
records.text: Under O. XI Rr. 8, 9 and 21 CPC, the defendant must answer interrogatories within seven days or the time fixed by the court. On default the court has jurisdiction to strike out his right of defence, as in a suit for damages under ss. 4 and 9 of the Defamation Ordinance. Ref: 2022 LHC 8204; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Mian Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif (Civil Revision 76628/22, decided 07.12.2022); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Mian Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif (Civil Revision 76628/22, decided 07.12.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade Loses Strength on Court Identification
records.heading: An identification parade loses its strength if the accused is identified in court
records.text: An identification parade loses its strength if the accused persons are identified during the proceedings before the Trial Court. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2024.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Weapon Without FSL Report
records.heading: Recovery of a weapon is inconsequential if neither it nor the empty is sent to the FSL
records.text: Recovery of the weapon of offence is inconsequential where neither the crime empty nor the weapon is sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2012.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Prima Facie Case for Temporary Injunction
records.heading: A prima facie case exists where the plaintiff's case is on a better footing
records.text: Prima facie means at first sight. The court tentatively examines pleadings, affidavits, counter-affidavits and documents, and infers a prima facie case if the plaintiff's case is on a better footing and relief is likely at trial. O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC. Ref: 2022 CLC 2094.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Injunction Based on Agreement to Sell
records.heading: An agreement to sell creates no right in immovable property to ground an injunction
records.text: An agreement to sell creates no right in immovable property, and its weight is assessed by tentative examination of the circumstances. The appellant paid about 98.75 percent of the price in cash without proof of means or of possession, and failed to show a prima facie case. Injunction refused and appeal dismissed. Ref: 2022 CLC 2094.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Promissory Note Suit: Admissions in Cross-Examination
records.heading: Admissions in cross-examination defeated the defence in a promissory note suit
records.text: In a suit on a promissory note under O. XXXVII CPC, the defendant admitted borrowing the money, putting thumb impressions on documents and that the loan was for his own use. These admissions demolished his defence, and mere denials also operated against him. The decree was upheld. Ref: 2022 CLC 2115.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotic Samples
records.heading: Guilt is not established where safe custody and transmission of narcotics is not proved
records.text: Where the prosecution fails to establish safe custody of the recovered narcotic substance and its safe transmission from the police station to the Chemical Examiner, guilt cannot be held established beyond the shadow of doubt against the accused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2149, 2022 SCMR 2121, 2022 SCMR 2105, 2022 SCMR 2093.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cross-Versions: Not Sufficient Ground for Bail
records.heading: The mere existence of a cross-version is not sufficient ground for bail
records.text: The mere existence of a cross-version cannot alone be treated as a sufficient ground to grant bail to an accused. The case concerned murderous assault under s. 302 PPC and bail under s. 497 CrPC. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2111.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Meaning of Judgment Varied, Upheld or Set Aside
records.heading: A judgment varies a ruling only where it changes, alters or modifies it
records.text: A judgment varies the ruling below only where it changes, alters or modifies it. Where a judgment is upheld or set aside, the ruling is accepted in toto or reversed absolutely. A judgment partially upheld and partially reversed, where only the maintained part is challenged, is treated as upheld to one extent and set aside as to the rest. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2034.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Laches and Condonation of Delay
records.heading: A litigant who sleeps on his rights cannot claim relief and each day's delay must be explained
records.text: A litigant who sleeps on his rights has no right to claim relief under the doctrine of laches. For condonation of delay, each day's delay must be explained with proper justification. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2089.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeal Incompetent After Daman Deposited and Sentence Executed
records.heading: A convict who deposits the daman and secures release has executed his sentence
records.text: A convict who deposits the daman immediately and secures release has executed his sentence, so his appeal is not maintainable. Allowing deposit under protest is unlawful except as required by s. 337-Y(1a) PPC. The order directing the injured witness to return the daman was set aside and the application allowed. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1793.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Right of Appeal Is Statutory: Ss. 404, 382-A, 426 CrPC
records.heading: The right of appeal is statutory and cannot be exercised by analogy
records.text: The right of appeal is statutory and cannot be exercised by analogy unless expressly conferred (s. 404 CrPC). A convict may appeal while on bail by postponement of sentence under s. 382-A, or seek bail under s. 426 during appeal while in custody. Unless one of these applies, no appeal against conviction can be entertained. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1793.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Break in Safe Transmission of Samples
records.heading: Acquittal in a narcotics case where transmission of samples was not proved
records.text: The Lahore High Court acquitted a foreign model sentenced to eight and a half years for narcotics. It found that transmission of the samples to the laboratory was not proved, the sample weight had increased, the recovery memo lacked a monogram and the lady constable who searched the suitcase was not produced. Prosecution lacunae were held fatal. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1846.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Decree Without Monetary Value Executable
records.heading: A dowry decree is executable even if it states no monetary value
records.text: O. XX R. 10 CPC does not strictly apply to family court decrees in view of s. 17 of the Family Courts Act, 1964, which has no corresponding provision. A decree for dowry articles including gold ornaments is lawful and executable even if it states no monetary value payable should the movable property not be delivered. Ref: 2022 MLD 2077.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution of Dowry Decree: Alternate Price
records.heading: The wife's claim for alternate price in execution of a dowry decree was not to be declined
records.text: In execution of a decree for return of dowry articles, the wife refused the gold ornaments as not pure and claimed alternate price, and the husband had paid the price for seven tolas. The High Court set aside the Executing Court's direction that she receive the articles per the annexed list and decline her claim for alternate price. Ref: 2022 MLD 2077.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Compounding of Qatl-i-Amd by Legal Heirs
records.heading: Legal heirs may compound qatl-i-amd under section 345 after a Ta'zir conviction
records.text: Where conviction and sentence for qatl-i-amd have been passed under Ta'zir, the surviving legal heirs of the deceased are competent to effect a compromise within the meaning of s. 345 CrPC. Ref: 2022 MLD 2006.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Closely related eye-witnesses who stood by silently acted unnaturally and were unreliable
records.text: Closely related eye-witnesses who stood as silent spectators 13 feet away while the accused armed only with a churri inflicted nine injuries, and did not intervene or apprehend him, acted unnaturally. Their presence was doubtful and their evidence unreliable. Prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1852.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Acquittal where neither alleged motive was proved
records.text: Neither alleged motive was proved: no suit or application on the property dispute was produced, and the ex-wife's evidence on the marriage motive was self-contradictory. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1852.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses at Scene of Occurrence
records.heading: Eye-witnesses without a valid reason for presence at the scene were chance witnesses
records.text: Both eye-witnesses were not residents of the house where the murder occurred and could give no valid reason for their presence, since the family members were away at a wedding. They were chance witnesses, the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt, and the accused was acquitted. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1852.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements to Match Medical Evidence
records.heading: Dishonest improvements by eye-witnesses to match medical evidence made them unreliable
records.text: The FIR alleged one churri injury while the post-mortem showed nine. Both eye-witnesses made dishonest improvements, exposed in cross-examination, to match the medical evidence. Their evidence was not worthy of reliance and the accused was acquitted. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1852.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Churri From Public Place
records.heading: A weapon recovered from a public place after delay is of no avail to the prosecution
records.text: A churri recovered 16 days after the occurrence from a street accessible to the public, and sent to the Forensic Science Agency over a month after the occurrence, was of no avail to the prosecution despite a positive report. Accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1852.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post-Mortem Examination
records.heading: A long delay in post-mortem suggested time spent procuring eye-witnesses
records.text: A delay of 33 hours and 25 minutes in the post-mortem, with police papers received only the next day, suggested the time was spent procuring fake eye-witnesses. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt and the accused was acquitted. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1852.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Right of Appeal Is Statutory
records.heading: The right of appeal is statutory and cannot be imported or inferred
records.text: The right of appeal is statutory and not inherent. Under s. 404 CrPC, unless a special law gives a right of appeal it cannot be imported or inferred. The posts also set out the functions of appeals, including protecting against miscarriages of justice and correcting error. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1828.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal: Appeal Under S. 417, No Revision
records.heading: An acquittal is challenged only by appeal under section 417 and not by revision
records.text: An acquittal, whether after full trial or under ss. 249-A or 265-K CrPC, can be challenged only by appeal to the High Court under s. 417. Revision lies on legality and propriety, but cannot be filed against acquittal because s. 439(4)(a) prohibits converting acquittal into conviction. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1828.

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: S. 8-A: No Appeal or Revision Against Acquittal
records.heading: Section 8-A does not give appeal or revision against acquittal
records.text: The word "any" in s. 8-A of the Illegal Dispossession Act cannot be read to include an order of acquittal. Revision against acquittal has no room in law, so the complainant can at most assail the acquittal through a constitutional petition under Art. 199 where no other efficacious remedy exists. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1828.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Meaning of the Remedy of Appeal
records.heading: Appeal is a request to a superior court to change a decision for erroneous application of law
records.text: Authority on the concept of appeal as a request to a superior court to change a previous decision, resorted to by an unsuccessful party on the ground of erroneous application of law. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1828.

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: No Appeal Against Interlocutory Orders: Revision Remedy
records.heading: No appeal lies against interlocutory orders under the Illegal Dispossession Act; revision is the remedy
records.text: The Legislature did not provide an appeal against all orders under the Illegal Dispossession Act, 2005, such as dismissal under s. 203 CrPC, cognizance, attachment, eviction or rejection of an s. 265-K application. The suitable remedy is revision in the High Court. S. 8-A was inserted to give appeal against conviction. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1828.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Separate Suits for Each Finance Facility
records.heading: Each finance facility may found a separate suit not barred by Order II Rule 2
records.text: Each finance facility may give rise to an independent cause of action, so separate suits under s. 9 of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001 are not barred by O. II R. 2 CPC. The Banking Court rightly decreed the suit as no substantial question was raised in the leave application. Ref: 2022 CLD 1494.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Execution Limitation Not Extended by Pendency of Appeal
records.heading: Pendency of an appeal without stay does not extend limitation for execution
records.text: Mere filing of an appeal does not stay the decree. Time is excluded under s. 15 of the Limitation Act only where a stay was granted, and none was. The bank's execution petition was time barred under Art. 181 and was held not maintainable. Ref: 2022 CLD 1454.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witness: No Justification for Presence
records.heading: A complainant living a kilometre away with no reason for presence was a chance witness
records.text: The complainant, who lived one kilometre away and had no job there, was a chance witness with no plausible reason for presence. The prosecution case that the accused were empty handed made non-intervention by the witnesses doubtful, and the post-mortem supported absence. Appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1811.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Witness
records.heading: A witness who makes a dishonest improvement is liable to be thrown away
records.text: If a witness introduces a dishonest improvement, his statement does not remain reliable and is liable to be thrown away. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1811.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Vague Conspiracy Allegation
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail where the conspiracy allegation lacked details and incriminating contact
records.text: Where the FIR and s. 161 statements lacked details of an alleged conspiracy to murder, and contact between the accused-petitioner and her husband and son was not an incriminating circumstance, the allegation lacked support. Observations in a bail order are tentative and do not prejudice either party at trial (ss. 497, 498 CrPC). Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1806.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Scrutiny of Nomination Papers: S. 62 Elections Act
records.heading: A voter who objects late has no locus standi before the Election Tribunal
records.text: The appellant knew of the scrutiny held in his presence a day before the last date, yet objected only 24 hours later, so he had no locus standi before the Election Tribunal. S. 62 of the Elections Act, 2017 allows a voter to object before the Returning Officer. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2022 CLC 1842.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Fraud With Overseas Pakistani
records.heading: Bail refused where sufficient material existed in a fraud case, so section 497(2) was not attracted
records.text: Bail was refused to an accused charged under ss. 420, 468, 471, 406 and 489-F PPC for taking money on an agreement to sell land he did not own, selling the complainant's plots and issuing a dishonoured cheque. Sufficient material existed, so s. 497(2) CrPC was not attracted. Leave to appeal dismissed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2040.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Recall of Medical Officer for Re-Examination
records.heading: A medical officer must be recalled where his durations of injuries differ and need explanation
records.text: The medical officer gave different durations for the deceased's injuries in examination-in-chief and cross-examination, and the discrepancy needed explanation. Refusing re-examination would prejudice the petitioner. Petition allowed, the order set aside and the trial court directed to recall the Medical Officer. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 537; Muhammad Shahid v. Aqeel and 5 others (Criminal Revision No. 01/2020/BWP).
records.title: Muhammad Shahid v. Aqeel and 5 others (Criminal Revision No. 01/2020/BWP)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Appeal Not Heard on Merits Without Surrender
records.heading: Without surrender, a contempt appeal cannot be heard on merits
records.text: The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal of a Punjab Bar Council member advocate in a contempt of court case and held that, without surrender, the case cannot be heard on merits.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Additional Witnesses Not to Suit Complainant
records.heading: Additional witnesses cannot be summoned under section 540 merely to suit the complainant
records.text: The discretion under the first part of s. 540 CrPC must be exercised judicially on sound material and not as a rule. Additional witnesses could not be summoned to fulfil the complainant's desire, and the complainant had not shown they appeared during investigation. The High Court set aside the Trial Court's order. Ref: 2013 PCrLJ 1623.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Summoning Witnesses: Art. 10-A Fair Trial
records.heading: Fair trial under Article 10-A justified re-summoning witnesses not cross-examined by State counsel
records.text: Where State-appointed defence counsel did not cross-examine certain prosecution witnesses, the right to fair trial under Art. 10-A made delay and lacunae ignorable technicalities. The High Court directed the Trial Court to re-examine those witnesses within seven days. Ref: 2014 MLD 69.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Re-Summoning Injured Child Witness
records.heading: The Trial Court erred in refusing to re-summon the sole injured child witness
records.text: S. 540 CrPC has a discretionary first part and a mandatory second part. Where the complainant gave up the sole injured child eyewitness, the Trial Court erred in dismissing the application to re-summon her, as there was material suggesting reckless conduct or collusion to stifle the prosecution case. Ref: 2014 PCrLJ 1803.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: No Filling of Lacuna by Re-Summoning
records.heading: Neither side may fill a lacuna by re-summoning witnesses under section 540
records.text: Neither defence nor prosecution may fill a lacuna by re-summoning witnesses under s. 540 CrPC, as trials would never end. The accused had full opportunity to cross-examine, and the High Court declined interference in a constitutional petition. Ref: PLD 2015 Lahore 26.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Carbon Copies of Recovery Memos as Primary Evidence
records.heading: Carbon copies made by a uniform process are admissible as primary evidence
records.text: Carbon copies made by a uniform process in performing official duty are admissible as primary evidence. The Trial Court wrongly refused the carbon copies of recovery memos, which prejudiced the prosecution, and could have requisitioned the originals if doubtful. The order was set aside. Ref: 2015 PCrLJ 1354.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Accused's Application for CDR
records.heading: An accused may use the same CDR the prosecution relies on to prove innocence
records.text: Where the prosecution case rested on call detail records, the accused had every right to use the same CDR to prove innocence. The court could not summarily dismiss an s. 540 CrPC application for additional evidence. The Anti-Terrorism Court order was set aside and the application accepted. Ref: 2016 PCrLJ Note 77.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Re-Examination of Doctor to Fill Lacuna
records.heading: The prosecution cannot re-examine a doctor under section 540 to fill a lacuna
records.text: After the defence had cross-examined the doctor and brought out matters in its favour, the prosecution could not be permitted to mutilate them. It could not fill the lacuna, such as missing X-ray reports and operation notes, at a belated stage by re-examining the doctor under s. 540 CrPC. Ref: 2016 YLR Note 86.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Material Witness for Defence
records.heading: A witness who narrated facts to the investigating officer may be examined as a defence witness
records.text: A witness who appeared before the investigating officer and narrated facts became relevant and important. The Trial Court wrongly dismissed the accused's application under s. 540 CrPC, so the order was set aside and the witness was allowed to be examined as a defence witness. Ref: 2016 YLR Note 129.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recalling a Formal Witness
records.heading: A formal witness was rightly not recalled where no miscarriage of justice would result
records.text: S. 540 CrPC has a discretionary first part and a mandatory second part, aimed at digging out the truth. The accused could not explain why he did not cross-examine a formal witness, and not recalling him would cause no miscarriage of justice, so the application was rightly dismissed. Ref: PLD 2016 Lahore 533.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Wide Powers to Summon Evidence
records.heading: Section 540 gives the Trial Court wide power to summon evidence at any stage
records.text: The Trial Court has a duty to dig out the truth and wide discretion under the first part of s. 540 CrPC to summon relevant evidence at any stage. Under the second part it is compulsory to summon evidence essential for a just decision. Ref: 2017 YLR Note 243.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Defence Witnesses: Complainant's Undertaking on Timeline
records.heading: The High Court took account of the complainant's undertaking on trial timeline for defence witnesses
records.text: During trial the accused sought to summon four defence witnesses. The complainant had no objection provided the trial concluded within 30 days, and the High Court took the statements of the parties into account. Ref: 2017 MLD 185.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Re-Examination of Injured Witness Refused
records.heading: Section 540 cannot be used to fill lacunae or protract the trial
records.text: The injured witness had been cross-examined by defence counsel, and the accused's application to re-summon her under s. 540 CrPC was dismissed. S. 540 cannot be used by a party to fill the lacunae of its case or to protract the trial. Ref: 2017 YLR 1042.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Re-Summoning Investigating Officer
records.heading: Re-summoning the investigating officer was refused as section 540 cannot fill lacunae
records.text: The complainant appeared interested in protracting the trial, and the investigating officer had already given an exhaustive statement. S. 540 CrPC cannot be used to let a party fill the lacunae in its case. Ref: 2017 YLR 1636.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Examination of Witness at Any Stage
records.heading: A court may recall a witness at any stage if justice requires, but not to fill a lacuna
records.text: A court may at any stage recall a witness for re-examination, on its own or at a party's request, if justice requires, to obtain explanation or remove doubt or ambiguity. It cannot be allowed to fill a lacuna causing prejudice to the other side, who may cross-examine after re-examination. Ref: PLD 2018 Lahore 13.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning of Material Documents and Witnesses
records.heading: Courts may examine anyone whose evidence is necessary for a just decision under section 540
records.text: The law empowers courts to examine anyone whose evidence is necessary for a just decision under s. 540 CrPC. In a case of an allegedly bogus matric certificate, not all material and witnesses allowed by the Trial Court were essential, but the NADRA District Registrar might be important. Revision was partly accepted. Ref: 2018 YLR 151.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Two Parts, Discretionary and Mandatory
records.heading: Section 540 has a discretionary first part and a mandatory second part
records.text: The first part of s. 540 CrPC confers wide discretion to summon, examine or recall witnesses, while the second part obliges the court to do so if the evidence is essential to a just decision. The complainant's daughter, who had made a s. 161 statement, was an essential witness. Revision allowed. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 1436.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recalling Witness Not to Fill Lacunas
records.heading: Witnesses may be recalled where justice demands but not to fill lacunas
records.text: Witnesses may be recalled where justice demands or to rectify an obvious mistake, but not to fill lacunas or protract the trial. An accused cannot recall witnesses for further cross-examination as of right when opportunity was afforded, particularly where the petition was vague on the points not cross-examined. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 1113; Muhammad Safdar alias Bhooma v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Safdar alias Bhooma v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Evidence Essential for Just Decision
records.heading: Section 540 power depends on evidence being essential, and an oversight is not a lacuna
records.text: The power under s. 540 CrPC is conditioned on the evidence being essential to a just decision, not to fill an inherent weakness in the prosecution case. An oversight by prosecutor or defence in producing a document or eliciting an answer is not a lacuna. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 1135.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Necessary Evidence, Lacuna Irrelevant
records.heading: Where evidence is necessary for a just decision, objections about lacunae become irrelevant
records.text: Where evidence is necessary for a just decision, it is mandatory to summon it and objections about curing lapses or filling lacunae become irrelevant. The criminal justice system is inquisitorial, and delay in applying is immaterial. Re-examination of the complainant to produce documents already on record was upheld. Ref: 2021 YLR 2096.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Late Application for Record and Fair Trial
records.heading: A late section 540 application was allowed on fair trial grounds
records.text: The accused applied under s. 540 CrPC to summon the Rescue 15 record and custodian after prosecution evidence closed, which the Trial Court declined. The High Court allowed the petition on fair trial grounds, set aside the order and directed that the petitioner be given an opportunity to produce defence evidence. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 198.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Challan Witnesses in Private Complaint
records.heading: Declining to summon challan witnesses in a parallel private complaint was proper
records.text: The challan case and the private complaint were proceeding side by side, so declining to summon two challan witnesses as court witnesses was a proper exercise of discretion. The accused could examine them as defence witnesses if he wished. Ref: 2022 MLD 70.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: No Second Chance to Improve Evidence
records.heading: Section 540 gives no second chance to improve evidence at a belated stage
records.text: Where evidence is essential for a just decision, the court must allow it, but it cannot let a party fill lacunas or take a second chance to improve its case. An application to produce additional evidence at a very belated stage, only to fill lacunas, was rightly dismissed. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 649.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Witness Not in Calendar of Witnesses
records.heading: A witness need not be named in the calendar of witnesses to be summoned under section 540
records.text: For summoning a witness under s. 540 CrPC, the witness's name need not appear in the calendar of witnesses. The test is that his evidence is necessary for just decision of the case. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1349.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Second Medical Board for Injured: Not Permissible
records.heading: A second Medical Board should not be directed absent strong grounds of mala fide
records.text: The first medical examination enjoys a presumption of genuineness under Art. 129(e) QSO and Art. 150. Absent very strong grounds of mala fide against the Medical Officer, a second Medical Board should not be directed. The Magistrate's order was set aside in the constitutional petition. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1822.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Medico-Legal Certificate Not Per Se Admissible
records.heading: A medico-legal certificate is not per se admissible without the Medical Officer's testimony
records.text: Neither the MLC nor a Medical Board's re-examination report is per se admissible, as neither is protected by s. 510 CrPC. The Medical Officer must appear before the Trial Court as a witness to verify its contents. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1822.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Complete Statement of Witness in One Session
records.heading: A witness's complete statement should ordinarily be recorded in one session
records.text: A witness's complete statement comprises examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination. Once a witness has entered the box, it is legally desirable to record his statement in full in one session under Art. 133 QSO, and fragmentary recording should be avoided subject to well-reasoned exceptions. Ref: 2020 CLC 900.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Forfeiture of Right to Cross-Examine: Art. 133 QSO
records.heading: A court cannot forfeit an accused's right to cross-examine with unseemly haste
records.text: Re-examination under Art. 133 QSO is allowed only to explain matters from cross-examination or, with permission, a new matter, and cannot be used to rectify errors. A court cannot forfeit an accused's right to cross-examine with unseemly haste, particularly in a murder case. Ref: 2017 YLR Note 342.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed: Fabrication of Injury
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where the complainant's injury may have been fabricated
records.text: The complainant's injury was opined by the District Standing Medical Board to possibly be fabricated, he did not appear before the Provincial Board, and the accused's own injuries were suppressed. A prima facie doubt arose, so the case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, and ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 264.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Case of Two Versions
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail allowed in a case of two versions where the injured avoided the Medical Board
records.text: The injured did not appear before the District Standing Medical Board despite notices, requiring further inquiry into guilt and into whether a non-bailable offence was committed. With two versions of the occurrence, the aggressor was for the Trial Court to determine, and pre-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Complainant Evading Medical Board
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail allowed where the complainant deliberately evaded the Medical Board
records.text: The injured complainant deliberately did not appear before the District Standing Medical Board, and the co-accused sons already had pre-arrest bail. Possible fabrication of injury and false implication made it a case of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC, and bail was allowed. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 1571.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed: Delayed FIR and Two Versions
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed after delayed FIR, two versions and completed investigation
records.text: With a six day delay in the FIR, a case of two versions, the injured not appearing before the Medical Board, investigation complete and challan submitted, no useful purpose was served by custody. False implication could not be ruled out, and ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2018 YLR Note 110.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation Distinguished from Honour Killing
records.heading: Grave and sudden provocation is committed on the spur of the moment, unlike honour killing
records.text: In honour killing the murder is well thought out, calculated and premeditated, while under grave and sudden provocation the act is committed on the spur of the moment without planning or deliberation. Family honour may underlie both, yet the two differ. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 201.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: Meaning and Scope
records.heading: Grave and sudden provocation must deprive the offender of self-control and be proportionate
records.text: The provocation must be so grave and sudden as to deprive the offender of self-control, per Exception 1 to the erstwhile s. 300 PPC. It consists of the act of provocation, loss of self-control and a proportionate reaction, tested against what a reasonable person of that society would do. Their relationship in time decides whether passion had time to cool. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 201.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Doctrine of Diminished Responsibility
records.heading: Diminished responsibility absolves an accused of part of the liability where abnormality of mind impairs responsibility
records.text: Diminished responsibility absolves an accused of part of the liability if an abnormality of mind substantially impairs responsibility, here an act committed due to love and affection and injury to reputation. It is a mitigating defence where mental defect does not wholly exclude criminal responsibility, and is most often asserted in murder cases. Ref: 2022 SCMR 18.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Diminished Responsibility: Crimes Under Mental Compulsion
records.heading: A crime committed under mental compulsion or ghairat attracts diminished liability
records.text: A crime committed due to mental or psychological compulsion falls within diminished liability, which absolves an accused of part of the liability. Where an act is committed under the impulses of ghairat, the doctrine is squarely attracted as mitigation. Ref: 2022 SCMR 976.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: Sentence Converted to S. 302(c)
records.heading: Sentence converted to section 302(c) on grave and sudden provocation
records.text: The accused claimed grave and sudden provocation after the deceased allegedly attempted to rape his sister and abused his mother. Eye-witness testimony was not discarded merely for relationship and was supported by medical evidence. The sentence was converted from life under s. 302(b) to ten years under s. 302(c) PPC. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 523; Justice Mansoor Ali Shah.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Annual Increment on Maintenance: Compound Basis Question
records.heading: Amici were appointed on whether annual increment on maintenance is compound
records.text: Interim order appointing two Advocates Supreme Court as amici curiae to assist on whether the annual increment on maintenance allowance under s. 17-A of the Family Courts Act, 1964 is calculated on the principal amount fixed or on a compound basis. The matter was relisted for 02.02.2023. No decision on the question appears. Ref: Sohaib Umar Ilyas v. Judge Family Court (W.P. No. 15888/2021, order dated 14.12.2022); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Sohaib Umar Ilyas v. Judge Family Court (W.P. No. 15888/2021, order dated 14.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution Petitions and Proceedings
records.heading: Execution petitions and proceedings were considered; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on execution petitions and proceedings, decided by Muhammad Ali Mazhar J. The post gives only the topic and case details without stating the holding. Ref: Summit Bank Limited, Lahore v. M/s M.M. Brothers Proprietorship Concern, Lahore and others (C.P. 2056/2022, decided 04.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Summit Bank Limited, Lahore v. M/s M.M. Brothers Proprietorship Concern, Lahore and others (C.P. 2056/2022, decided 04.10.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. V R. 20 CPC: Substituted Service
records.heading: Substituted service under Order V Rule 20 is as effectual as personal service
records.text: The court may order substituted service under O. V R. 20 CPC where the other side is avoiding service or summons cannot be served ordinarily, by affixation, electronic means, courier, beat of drum, press publication or other mode. Such service is as effectual as personal service. Writ jurisdiction cannot bypass the remedy of appeal. Ref: Sana Jamali v. Mujeeb Qamar & another (C.P. 32-Q/2019, decided 05.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Sana Jamali v. Mujeeb Qamar & another (C.P. 32-Q/2019, decided 05.10.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 195 CrPC: Pendency of Suit Bars Initiation of Proceedings
records.heading: Pendency of a suit bars initiation of proceedings for false information under section 195
records.text: The petitioner sought action under ss. 193, 419, 420 PPC and s. 476 CrPC against the plaintiff of an Order 37 suit for alleged false information. The court held the competent court decides at final disposal of the suit, so pendency of the suit bars initiation. Revisional jurisdiction under ss. 435 and 439 CrPC is not exercised absent illegality or perversity. Ref: 2022 LHC 8214; Nadeem Ahmad v. Shafqat Parvaze etc. (Crl. Revision 78903/22, decided 13.12.2022); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Nadeem Ahmad v. Shafqat Parvaze etc. (Crl. Revision 78903/22, decided 13.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Revision: Suit Not Dismissed for Want of Jurisdiction
records.heading: A court deciding a section 12(2) application cannot dismiss the suit itself for want of jurisdiction
records.text: In allowing a civil revision against dismissal of an application under s. 12(2) CPC, the High Court held that, by entertaining a plea of want of jurisdiction, it could not dismiss the suit itself. Ref: 2022 LHC 8228; Sajjad Hussain etc. v. Mst. Mumtaz etc. (Civil Revision CM-1-540-04, decided 14.12.2022); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Sajjad Hussain etc. v. Mst. Mumtaz etc. (Civil Revision CM-1-540-04, decided 14.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Specific Performance Decree: Limitation
records.heading: Limitation for execution of a specific performance decree depends on first or later application
records.text: A decree holder already in possession under a specific performance decree need not file execution for possession, and may file execution on the judgment debtor's refusal to perform the rest. The first execution application is governed by Art. 181 of the Limitation Act (three years) and later ones by s. 48 CPC (six years). Ref: Mst. Iqbal Bibi, etc. v. Additional District Judge, etc. (Civil Revision 1620/2016, decided 29.11.2022).
records.title: Mst. Iqbal Bibi, etc. v. Additional District Judge, etc. (Civil Revision 1620/2016, decided 29.11.2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Constitution of Benches: Order XI Supreme Court Rules
records.heading: Constitution of benches under Order XI of the Supreme Court Rules; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on constitution of benches under Order XI of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980, decided by Muhammad Ali Mazhar J. The post gives only the topic and case details without stating the holding. Ref: State Bank of Pakistan v. Mohammad Naeem & others (C.R.P. 35-K/2020, decided 10.11.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: State Bank of Pakistan v. Mohammad Naeem & others (C.R.P. 35-K/2020, decided 10.11.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dissolution on Ground of Cruelty
records.heading: Cruelty requires acts beyond trivial matters that no reasonable person can endure
records.text: For dissolution on the ground of cruelty, the court must judge the intensity and ruthlessness of the acts and whether they exceed trivial day-to-day matters and are such that no reasonable person can endure. Where a husband claims conjugal rights in answer to a suit for dissolution, dower, dowry and maintenance, the court must see whether he sincerely fulfils his obligations. Ref: Mst. Tayyeba Ambareen & another v. Shafaqat Ali Kiyani & another (C.P. 3209/2019, decided 03.11.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mst. Tayyeba Ambareen & another v. Shafaqat Ali Kiyani & another (C.P. 3209/2019, decided 03.11.2022)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Commission Cannot Act Against Officers for Misconduct
records.heading: The Election Commission cannot act against officers for misconduct; their departments can
records.text: The Lahore High Court set aside the Election Commission's action against officers over alleged irregularities in the Daska by-election and allowed their petitions. It held that the relevant departments, and not the Election Commission, have authority to act against officers for misconduct. Ref: Asif Hussain v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc. (W.P. 32915/2022, decided 21.12.2022); Justice Shujaat Ali Khan.
records.title: Asif Hussain v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc. (W.P. 32915/2022, decided 21.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Service by Publication: O. V R. 20 CPC and Ex Parte Decree
records.heading: Service by publication is presumed to be personal service, a rebuttable presumption
records.text: Substituted service by publication is presumed to be personal service under O. V R. 20(2) CPC, a rebuttable presumption. The court must first see whether the conditions were met and ordinary modes of service exhausted. The petitioner applied promptly to set aside the ex parte decree, so the application was not time barred and the courts below erred in dismissing it. Ref: Naeem Shehzad v. Mst. Sarran Bibi & others (Civil Revision 358/2022, decided 13.12.2022).
records.title: Naeem Shehzad v. Mst. Sarran Bibi & others (Civil Revision 358/2022, decided 13.12.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Confronting Witness With E-mail in Custody Case
records.heading: A witness's e-mail may be treated as a previous statement and confronted in cross-examination
records.text: The Qanun-e-Shahadat does not strictly apply before the Family Court, but basic evidentiary principles do. E-mail or digital communication of a witness may be treated as a previous statement and confronted in cross-examination, subject to relevancy. The orders refusing confrontation were set aside. Ref: 2020 CLC 1029.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 164 QSO: Modern Devices as Evidence
records.heading: Article 164 QSO allows modern devices as evidence subject to integrity of the process
records.text: Art. 164 QSO provides a wide mechanism to bring on record evidence by visual, audio, digital, sonic or biological means, subject to the integrity of the process. The video footage was confirmed by forensic report as having integrity. Ref: PLD 2019 Lahore 366.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Gang Rape Recorded on Phone: Consent and Submission
records.heading: The victim's conduct in a recorded gang rape showed submission and not consent
records.text: In a prosecution for rape by two or more persons with a video of the assault, the Trial Court rightly placed implicit reliance on the prosecution evidence. The victim's conduct was held to show submission and not consent, and no interference with the guilty verdict was called for. Ref: PLD 2019 Lahore 366.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Riaz Ahmad v. The State: Petition Disposed
records.heading: A criminal petition on qatl-e-khata was disposed of; no holding is given
records.text: Case status page showing a criminal petition instituted on 27.03.2019 and disposed of on 20.12.2022. The caption refers to a Supreme Court hearing at Lahore on a murder by axe blows that the High Court had treated as qatl-e-khata, reducing life imprisonment to five years. The image gives no holding. Ref: Riaz Ahmad v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 360-L/2019, disposed 20.12.2022).
records.title: Riaz Ahmad v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 360-L/2019, disposed 20.12.2022)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Disqualification for False Statement: Art. 63(1)(c)
records.heading: A member making a false statement is disqualified for the term of the assembly only
records.text: The Supreme Court held the member admitted a false statement about renouncing foreign citizenship, so Art. 63(1)(c) applied and he stood disqualified for the term of the assembly, but could contest future elections. It held the Election Commission cannot disqualify a candidate before election and set aside the lifetime disqualification. Ref: Muhammad Faisal Vawda v. Election Commission of Pakistan, through its Secretary and others (CMA 751/2022 in C.P. 397/2022, decided 25.11.2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Muhammad Faisal Vawda v. Election Commission of Pakistan, through its Secretary and others (CMA 751/2022 in C.P. 397/2022, decided 25.11.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence in Appeal
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal must bear directly on the point in issue
records.text: O. XLI R. 27 CPC lets the appellate court take additional evidence needed to pronounce judgment or for any substantial cause. The evidence must bear directly on the point in issue, and the test is whether a just decision can be reached without it. Where the vires of a mutation is challenged, the other party must prove its valid basis. Ref: Mst. Ilyas Akhtar v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Civil Revision 251/2017, decided 13.12.2022).
records.title: Mst. Ilyas Akhtar v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Civil Revision 251/2017, decided 13.12.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Converted to Life: Doubts on Weapon Recovery
records.heading: Death sentence converted to life where weapon recovery details were missing
records.text: The appeal against conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was dismissed as the FIR was prompt, the eye-witness account matched medical evidence and the defence indirectly admitted motive. The death sentence was converted to life imprisonment as the motorcycle details were missing and no crime empty was recovered. Ref: 2022 LHC 8343; Riaz v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 43590/19, decided 14.11.2022); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Riaz v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 43590/19, decided 14.11.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Chief Minister Restored on Undertaking Not to Dissolve Assembly
records.heading: The Chief Minister was restored on his undertaking not to advise dissolution of the Assembly
records.text: The Lahore High Court restored the Chief Minister and the Punjab cabinet on his undertaking not to advise dissolution of the Assembly. Notices were issued to all parties for 11 January, and the court said it was not obliging him to take a vote of confidence.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Chief Minister De-Notified by Governor: Interim Order
records.heading: The Governor's orders de-notifying the Chief Minister were held in abeyance
records.text: The petitioner challenged the Governor's orders under Art. 130(7) of the Constitution and rule 22(7) of the Assembly Rules declaring he lacked majority confidence. The five member bench held the impugned orders in abeyance till the next hearing, without precluding the petitioner from taking a vote of confidence on his own accord. Ref: Chaudhary Pervez Elahi v. Governor Punjab etc. (W.P. 82603/2022, decided 23.12.2022); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh; Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh; Justice Asim Hafeez; Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal; Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Chaudhary Pervez Elahi v. Governor Punjab etc. (W.P. 82603/2022, decided 23.12.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Intimidation: Ss. 503 and 506 PPC
records.heading: A bare threat is not criminal intimidation unless it aims to compel an act or omission
records.text: A bare threat does not constitute criminal intimidation under ss. 503 and 506 PPC unless it is meant to make the person threatened do an act he is not legally bound to do, or omit one he is entitled to do, to avoid the threat. As the FIR mentioned no such element, s. 506(b) PPC was doubtful. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1254.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Quo Warranto: Appointment of Provincial Police Officer
records.heading: Quo warranto fails where the appointee's lack of qualification or fatal defect is not shown
records.text: The petitioner did not show the appointee was unqualified or that a procedural defect, such as lack of federal and provincial consensus, went to the root of the matter. Suitability is for the appointing authority, and quo warranto is a discretionary jurisdiction, relying on 2019 SCMR 1720. The appointment was not held unlawful. Ref: 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1594.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Transfer Matters: Tribunal Jurisdiction and Persons With Disabilities
records.heading: Transfer matters fall within service terms and the Service Tribunal has exclusive jurisdiction
records.text: Transfer matters fall within terms and conditions of service, and the Service Tribunal has exclusive jurisdiction under Art. 212. The objection was overruled because the case involved interpretation of fundamental rights of persons with disabilities. The Chief Minister was directed to consider the proposals on the Transfer Policy expeditiously. Ref: 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1523.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Written Statement to I.O. as S. 161 CrPC Statement
records.heading: A written statement transcribed by the investigating officer substantially follows section 161
records.text: Where witnesses handed written statements that the investigating officer transcribed into the case diary in their presence, with further questions and answers recorded, the s. 161 CrPC procedure was substantially followed. S. 161 statements serve only for contradiction, and "orally" includes audio video recording. The application was rejected.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Intimidation: Ingredients of S. 506 PPC
records.heading: Section 506 PPC requires a threat intended to cause harm or compel an act or omission
records.text: To prove s. 506 PPC, the prosecution must show the accused threatened a person with injury to person, reputation or property, intending to cause harm or to make him do or omit an act, as a means of avoiding execution of the threat. The intended threat may be of death, grievous hurt or destruction of property by fire. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 199.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Counter-Version FIRs: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Where there are two versions of the occurrence, section 497(2) is attracted
records.text: Where there are two versions of the occurrence, s. 497(2) CrPC is squarely attracted and calls for further probe into the occurrence. Ref: 2022 SCMR 547.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: S. 497(2) CrPC
records.heading: Where a second view of the material is possible, the accused is entitled to bail
records.text: The term further inquiry in s. 497(2) CrPC requires that guilt be established on reasonable grounds. Where a second view of the material on record is possible, the accused is entitled to bail in the spirit of s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: 2021 SCMR 63.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Settled Principles
records.heading: Bail granted in disregard of settled principles or on incorrect facts may be recalled
records.text: Under s. 497(5) CrPC, bail granted in disregard of settled principles of law, or on a factually incorrect premise, is by itself a justification to recall it. Bail is discretionary relief, but the discretion must rest on sound judicial principles and conform to statutory parameters. Ref: 2022 SCMR 849.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Not Substitute for Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail cannot substitute for post-arrest bail
records.text: Pre-arrest bail cannot be used as a substitute or alternative for post-arrest bail. Ref: 2022 SCMR 707.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Grant and Cancellation of Bail Distinguished
records.heading: Grant and cancellation of bail rest on entirely different considerations
records.text: The considerations for grant of bail and for its cancellation are entirely different. Courts are generally reluctant to interfere with a bail-granting order, even if it appears unsustainable in law, where nothing shows that the accused misused the concession. Ref: 2022 SCMR 676.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Abscondment and Bail
records.heading: Abscondment is not conclusive of guilt and does not by itself bar bail
records.text: Abscondment is not conclusive proof of guilt and its value depends on the facts of each case. Bail may be granted to an absconder who has a good case on merits, and mere abscondment does not deprive an accused of bail. Ref: 2022 SCMR 419.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Concealment of Criminal Case in Police Recruitment
records.heading: Concealing a criminal case in police recruitment justifies rejection despite later acquittal
records.text: Candidates for the post of constable were rejected for concealing their involvement in a criminal case, although they were later acquitted. The Court stressed the high standards required for police appointments under Rule 12.12 of the Police Rules, 1934, and held that one who makes a false statement for recruitment cannot be expected to perform duties honestly. Ref: 2022 LHC 8404; Mirza Shahzeb v. C.P.O etc (W.P. 1891-20, decided 16.12.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Mirza Shahzeb v. C.P.O etc (W.P. 1891-20, decided 16.12.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Wheat Quota Notification and Article 25
records.heading: Clause VII of the wheat quota notification violated Article 25
records.text: Clause VII of the notification dated 19.05.2022 regarding allocation of the wheat quota was declared unconstitutional in terms of Art. 25 of the Constitution. Ref: 2022 LHC 8416; Rana Abdul Basit Khan v. Province of Punjab etc (W.P. 81071/22, decided 27.12.2022); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Rana Abdul Basit Khan v. Province of Punjab etc (W.P. 81071/22, decided 27.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Land Reforms: Res Judicata and S. 144 CPC
records.heading: A second revision before the Federal Land Commission is barred by res judicata
records.text: The Federal Land Commission cannot entertain a second revision on the same subject, which is barred by res judicata and liable to summary rejection under O. VII R. 11 CPC where the Supreme Court has finally decided the matter. If possession is changed in violation of a status quo order, the court that passed the order may restore the position under s. 144 CPC. Ref: 2022 LHC 8424; Province of Punjab through Secretary v. Federal Land Commission etc (W.P. 26860/21, decided 24.11.2022); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Province of Punjab through Secretary v. Federal Land Commission etc (W.P. 26860/21, decided 24.11.2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Section 175 Income Tax Ordinance, 2001
records.heading: Scope and effect of section 175 of the Income Tax Ordinance; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the scope and effect of s. 175 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2022 LHC 8442; Ms Outfitters Stores Pvt. Ltd. v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. 68823/22, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Ms Outfitters Stores Pvt. Ltd. v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. 68823/22, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Stamp Vending Licences: Structured Discretion
records.heading: Unstructured discretion in granting stamp vending licences must be structured by policy guidelines
records.text: Unfettered and unstructured discretion in granting stamp vending licences under the Stamp Act, 1899 and Stamp Rules, 1934 must be structured by instructions of the Board of Revenue. The Senior Member, Board of Revenue was directed to frame policy guidelines, and pending that any fresh licence must be granted after newspaper advertisement. Ref: 2022 LHC 8488; Mubashir Ali Awan v. Commissioner RWP etc (W.P. 2803-20, decided 28.11.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mubashir Ali Awan v. Commissioner RWP etc (W.P. 2803-20, decided 28.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Reliable Eyewitnesses in Murder
records.heading: An FIR lodged within one hour and forty five minutes was held prompt
records.text: An FIR lodged one hour and forty five minutes after the occurrence, with a 20 kilometre distance to the police station, was held prompt. Daylight occurrence between known parties excluded misidentification, and the consistent ocular witnesses were not unnatural. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was maintained but death sentence was altered to imprisonment for life. Ref: Ali Asghar @ Aksar v. The State (Crl. A. 190 of 2020, decided 07.12.2022).
records.title: Ali Asghar @ Aksar v. The State (Crl. A. 190 of 2020, decided 07.12.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Common Intention versus Individual Liability in Qatl-i-Amd
records.heading: The trial court must find whether qatl-i-amd was by common intention or individual liability
records.text: In qatl-i-amd cases the trial court must give a definite finding whether the act was committed in furtherance of common intention or object, or on individual liability. A conviction under s. 302(b) PPC based on common intention but sentencing on individual liability defies the law.
