If common intention is not established, each accused is dealt with according to individual role. Ref: Shafqat Hussain v. The State and another (Cr.P. 614 & 618 of 2017, decided 30.11.2022).
records.title: Shafqat Hussain v. The State and another (Cr.P. 614 & 618 of 2017, decided 30.11.2022)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: FIA Powers and AMLA Account Seizure
records.heading: FIA powers are not unfettered and AMLA seizure of accounts needs prior court permission
records.text: FIA powers under s. 5(5) of the Act of 1974 are not unfettered and must be used sparingly. Possession of local money is no crime without proof of a predicate offence, and s. 14(2) AMLA, 2010 requires prior court permission before seizure of bank accounts. S. 25 AMLA does not empower the FIA to order seizure of accounts. Ref: 2022 LHC 8535; Uzma Adil Khan v. FIA through DG etc (Criminal Proceedings 72202/21, decided 23.12.2022); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Uzma Adil Khan v. FIA through DG etc (Criminal Proceedings 72202/21, decided 23.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Unsigned List of Witnesses: Party Not to Suffer
records.heading: A party should not suffer for the court's failure to sign the list of witnesses
records.text: A party should not suffer for an act of the court, so the Presiding Officer's failure to sign the list of witnesses cannot be attributed to the plaintiff. Following the liberal view in 1981 SCMR 150, the record showed the plaintiff intended the proposed person to be his witness. The courts below also erred in declining production of SMS record referred to in the O. VII R. 14 CPC form. Ref: 2022 LHC 8499; Ghulam Hafeez etc v. Abdul Hadi etc (W.P. 491-19, decided 31.10.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Ghulam Hafeez etc v. Abdul Hadi etc (W.P. 491-19, decided 31.10.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Fraud in General Power of Attorney and Pardanashin Plea
records.heading: A plaintiff alleging fraud in a GPA must prove her case independently
records.text: A plaintiff alleging fraud in a registered GPA and the sale based on it must prove her case independently and cannot rely on weaknesses in the defendants' evidence. The pardanashin plea must be proved by cogent reasons, and on the facts the GPA carried a presumption of correctness. The purchaser acquired valid title and the civil revision was allowed. Ref: 2022 LHC 8509; Muhammad Umair Pasha etc v. The District Collector etc (C.R. 103-22, decided 08.11.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Umair Pasha etc v. The District Collector etc (C.R. 103-22, decided 08.11.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confronting Witness With Police Report: Art. 140 QSO
records.heading: A report lodged by a witness at the police station is a previous statement under Article 140
records.text: A report lodged by a prosecution witness at the police station is a previous statement under Art. 140 QSO, and he may be cross-examined on it. The trial court wrongly disallowed the question. Revision allowed. Ref: 2015 YLR 782.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 140 QSO: Cross-Examination on Previous Statement
records.heading: A witness may be cross-examined on a previous written statement without first producing it
records.text: Under Art. 140 QSO a witness may be cross-examined on a relevant previous statement in writing without that document first being produced or exhibited. The trial court cannot disallow such questions unless irrelevant. The order was set aside in a s. 561-A CrPC application and the criminal revision was allowed. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 77.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Witness Denying Police Statement: Art. 140 QSO
records.heading: A witness who denies a police statement deprives the accused of cross-examination and is unreliable
records.text: Cross-examination is a fundamental right of the accused, and a witness examined but not cross-examined cannot be considered against him. A witness who denies making a statement to police deprives the accused of cross-examination, becomes unreliable, and his evidence against the accused must be excluded. Ref: 2020 PCrLJ 415.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Complainant's Request for Accused's First Version
records.heading: A complainant was rightly refused the accused's first version to confront him as defence witness
records.text: A complainant's request for a copy of the first version of an accused, recorded under s. 161 CrPC, to confront him when he appeared as a defence witness was rightly declined. Qisas requires confession or the prescribed standard of proof, and the primary responsibility to prove the charge rests on the prosecution. Ref: PLD 2016 Lahore 482.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Use of Previous Admission: Art. 140 QSO
records.heading: A previous admission cannot be used unless the witness was confronted with specific portions
records.text: Where a party's witness-box statement runs counter to a previous admission, the admission cannot be used as legal evidence against that party unless the witness was confronted with the specific portions in cross-examination as required by Art. 140 QSO. Ref: 2008 PCrLJ 1383.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Procedure to Prove Contradictions with S. 161 Statement
records.heading: A contradiction with a section 161 statement is proved through the Investigating Officer if denied
records.text: To establish contradiction with a s. 161 CrPC statement, the witness's attention is drawn to the portion and an explanation obtained if admitted. If denied, the question is put to the Investigating Officer, and the contradiction is then exhibited and used in assessing the witness (Art. 140 QSO). Ref: 2006 PCrLJ 639.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Contradiction Only by Confronting Previous Statement
records.heading: A witness may be contradicted by an earlier statement only by confronting him with it
records.text: Where a witness is to be contradicted by an earlier statement or admission, that can be done only by confronting him with that previous statement (Art. 140 QSO). Ref: 2006 YLR 28.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Given Up Witness Confronted with Police Statement
records.heading: A given up witness examined under section 540 may be confronted with his police statement
records.text: A witness examined under s. 540 CrPC keeps his character as prosecution or defence witness, and s. 540 cannot be read to defeat other provisions of the Code. A given up prosecution witness examined under s. 540 may be confronted with his police statement under s. 162 CrPC, and the trial court's order was upheld. Ref: 2005 PCrLJ 1022; Tahir Waheed v. The State.
records.title: Tahir Waheed v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Pleadings Are Not Previous Statements for Confrontation
records.heading: Pleadings in the same suit are not previous statements for confrontation under Article 140
records.text: Pleadings in the same suit are not previous statements attracting the rule of confrontation under Art. 140 QSO. Ref: 2005 YLR 2838.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supply of Police Statements to Accused: S. 265-C
records.heading: The accused may obtain copies of police statements whether the case is a challan or complaint
records.text: A person examined by police during investigation and called as a prosecution witness may be contradicted with his statement under Art. 140 QSO, so the accused may seek a copy, whether the case is a challan or a complaint case. S. 265-C CrPC protects accused by requiring copies seven days before trial, and revision was allowed directing the police to furnish copies. Ref: 2005 YLR 933; Muhammad Ashiq v. Muhammad Anwar.
records.title: Muhammad Ashiq v. Muhammad Anwar

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Log Book on Accused's Application
records.heading: Summoning a Log Book on the accused's application in a murder trial; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on summoning a Log Book on the accused's application, on the ground of the right to cross-examine the Investigating Officer, in a murder trial involving ss. 162 and 265-C CrPC and Art. 140 QSO. The complainant opposed. The post does not state the holding. Ref: 2004 YLR 2407; Shaukat Mahmood v. Ghazanfar and others.
records.title: Shaukat Mahmood v. Ghazanfar and others

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Preventive Detention: S. 11-EEE ATA by Provincial Government
records.heading: The Provincial Government may exercise preventive detention power under section 11-EEE ATA
records.text: Given the definition of government in s. 2(i) ATA, s. 11-EEE does not restrict the power of preventive detention to the Federal Government. The Provincial Government may exercise it in its own right without delegation under s. 33. The case also concerned compliance with the Punjab Government Rules of Business 2011. Ref: PLD 2022 Lahore 61.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Art. 212 Bar: Inquiry into Initial Appointment
records.heading: The Article 212 bar applies where compulsory retirement flows from a probe into initial appointment
records.text: The bar under Art. 212 of the Constitution applies where compulsory retirement flows from a probe into the civil servant's initial appointment. Appointment under s. 4 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974 is part of the terms and conditions of service, and the law makes no distinction between probes into induction and later conduct. Ref: 2022 LHC 8562; Sultan Mehmood v. Province of Punjab etc (W.P. 3821-22, decided 27.12.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Sultan Mehmood v. Province of Punjab etc (W.P. 3821-22, decided 27.12.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Habeas Corpus: Nature and Purpose
records.heading: Habeas corpus tests the validity of imprisonment and frees a person illegally restrained
records.text: Discusses habeas corpus as rooted in personal liberty and human dignity, the means by which the validity of imprisonment is tested, and the duty of courts to free a person whose restraint is illegal. The post gives no outcome. Ref: Abid Hameed v. Additional Sessions Judge etc (W.P. 66114 of 2022).
records.title: Abid Hameed v. Additional Sessions Judge etc (W.P. 66114 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Case Diary: S. 172 CrPC
records.heading: A case diary under section 172 lets courts check the method of investigation
records.text: S. 172 CrPC requires a police officer to maintain a case diary recording the time of information, start and close of investigation, places visited and circumstances ascertained. Its object is to let courts check the method of investigation. The Investigating Officer's opinion does not decide sufficiency of grounds, which the magistrate determines under s. 173(3) CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2021 SC CrC 216.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Property: Sale to Non-Muslim and Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: A civil court has no jurisdiction over matters relating to evacuee property
records.text: Land sold by a Muslim owner to a non-Muslim on receipt of full consideration is a complete sale, and after the vendees' migration it became settlement pool property. The civil court has no jurisdiction to adjudicate matters relating to evacuee property. Ref: 2022 LHC 8570; Najib Aslam (deceased) through his Legal Heirs Umair Najeeb etc v. The State through District Collector Faisalabad etc (W.P. 27129/21, decided 07.12.2022); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Najib Aslam (deceased) through his Legal Heirs Umair Najeeb etc v. The State through District Collector Faisalabad etc (W.P. 27129/21, decided 07.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: PECA S. 11, WhatsApp Post
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed in a section 11 PECA case over a WhatsApp post
records.text: Post-arrest bail was sought in an FIR registered at FIA Cyber Crime Circle, Multan, alleging an offence under s. 11 PECA (maximum seven years) over an Arabic post in a WhatsApp group. The petitioner was admitted to bail on a bond of Rs 100,000 with one surety, and the petition was converted into an appeal and allowed. Ref: Zahid Zafar v. The State and another (Cr.P. 1501 of 2022, decided 16.12.2022); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Zahid Zafar v. The State and another (Cr.P. 1501 of 2022, decided 16.12.2022)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Postponement of Islamabad Local Government Elections
records.heading: Notification postponing Islamabad local government elections was suspended and elections directed
records.text: The Islamabad High Court allowed the petitions, suspended the notification postponing the Islamabad local government elections and directed the Election Commission to hold them on 31 December. A short order was announced with the detailed judgment to follow. Ref: Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail to Elderly Woman: Abetment and CDR, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail to an elderly woman where abetment ingredients were missing and further inquiry was needed
records.text: An elderly woman not named in the crime report, implicated later by a supplementary statement alleging abetment without specific date, time or place, had a case calling for further inquiry under S. 497(2) CrPC. The ingredients of abetment were prima facie missing and the CDR alone did not advance the case. Bail granted. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2077; Shameem Bibi v. State.
records.title: Shameem Bibi v. State

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Compensation to Daughters Deprived of Inheritance
records.heading: Brothers who sold inherited property must pay sisters their shares with mark-up
records.text: Where brothers sold inherited property to bona fide purchasers and deprived their sisters of their shares, the sons were directed to pay the daughters the equivalent of their shares of the sale consideration with mark-up at bank rate from the date of sale. Other estate transactions devolve per Sharia shares. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2130.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sharia-Compliant Will Not an Ex-Ante Instrument
records.heading: A Sharia-compliant will does not regulate heirs' shares before the estate opens
records.text: A Sharia-compliant will does not operate as an ex-ante instrument regulating the inheritable shares of legal heirs before the testator's estate opens, even where the ultimate value received by each heir equals the Quranic share. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2130.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody to Mother Despite Second Marriage: Children's Wishes
records.heading: Custody to the mother is proper despite remarriage and children's wishes are relevant
records.text: Custody was rightly awarded to the mother, an educated woman running a school and living in her own house, although she had remarried. The children's expressed wish to live with her is a relevant factor, though not the sole one. Petition for leave to appeal dismissed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2123.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Prosecution Case
records.heading: Minor discrepancies do not frustrate the prosecution case unless they shatter its salient features
records.text: Minor discrepancies do not frustrate the prosecution case unless something directly shatters its salient features. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2024.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Related Witnesses: Relationship Alone Not Ground to Discard
records.heading: Relationship of witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard testimony without enmity
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony unless previous enmity or ill will to falsely implicate the accused is established on record. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2012.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Reappraisal, Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Conviction for qatl-i-amd maintained on consistent ocular and corroborating medical evidence
records.text: Both eye-witnesses survived lengthy cross-examination, were consistent and explained their presence, and the medical evidence corroborated their account. The motive, admitted by the accused in his S. 342 CrPC statement, was suspicion of illicit relations. Conviction for qatl-i-amd maintained; petition partly allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2012.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Competent Authority and Inquiry Committee Recommendations
records.heading: The competent authority is not invariably bound by an inquiry committee's recommendations
records.text: The competent authority is not invariably bound by the recommendations of an inquiry committee, but must scrutinise the inquiry proceedings and report with application of mind. Where charges are proved and a fair opportunity of defence was given, it may impose punishment in accordance with law, considering the gravity of the charges. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2114.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Compulsory Retirement: Unauthorised Foreign Travel
records.heading: The Tribunal lacked a basis to reduce compulsory retirement for unauthorised foreign travel
records.text: The respondent travelled abroad without approval and offered no justification, document or NOC. The Tribunal had no analytical basis to reduce compulsory retirement to reversion to a lower post. Appeal allowed, the Tribunal's judgment set aside and compulsory retirement restored. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2114.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal: Power to Modify Punishment
records.heading: The Tribunal may modify punishment only carefully and with cogent reasons
records.text: Awarding punishment is primarily the function of the competent authority, and the Tribunal's role is secondary unless the penalty is unreasonable or contrary to law. The Tribunal may modify penalties, but must do so carefully, judiciously and with cogent reasons. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2114.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused Despite Cross-Version
records.heading: Bail refused despite a cross-version where the accused had a specific firing role
records.text: Bail was refused to an accused nominated in a promptly lodged FIR with a specific firing role at the head of the deceased, supported by medical evidence, three injured witnesses and weapon recovery. The cross-version did not place him at the scene or claim private defence. Leave to appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2111.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Art. 185(2)(d) Appeal: Competence Where Part Unchallenged
records.heading: An Article 185(2)(d) appeal is incompetent where the appellant challenges only part
records.text: Where the High Court varied the lower court's judgment in the appellant's favour and the appellant challenged only the portion dismissing his claim, a civil appeal under Art. 185(2)(d) of the Constitution was not competent. A civil petition for leave to appeal under Art. 185(3) was required. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2034.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Provisional Appointment Subject to Character Verification
records.heading: A provisional appointee booked in a murder case before joining has no right to appointment
records.text: An appointee who was provisionally offered a police post but never joined, and whose letter was subject to verification of character, could not claim a right to appointment, having been booked in a murder case before joining. Each department may make rules and induct people according to its own standards. Leave to appeal was refused. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2089.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Deputationists and Special Allowance
records.heading: Deputationists had no legal right to a special allowance not provided in the memorandum
records.text: Deputationists in the National Highway and Motorway Police are distinct from regular employees. As the office memorandum on their terms did not provide the special allowance of one month's pay, they had no legal right to claim it. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2047.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth in Service Book
records.heading: The competent authority may inquire into and correct a wrong date of birth in a service book
records.text: R. 12-A of the Sindh Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1974 does not stop the competent authority inquiring into interpolations or incorrect dates of birth in the service book. After due inquiry correction may be made, and a civil servant cannot treat a wrong entry as sacrosanct. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2050.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: PM Assistance Package 2014: Not for Statutory Body Employees
records.heading: The 2014 Assistance Package did not extend to employees of statutory bodies
records.text: The 2014 Prime Minister's Assistance Package was meant for families of government employees. Employees of PESCO and WAPDA are not government servants, so the High Court could not direct payment to widows under it. Appeals were allowed and the High Court judgments set aside. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2058.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Territorial Jurisdiction under Art. 199: Company's Head Office
records.heading: Territorial jurisdiction under Article 199 lies where the company's head office is
records.text: PESCO is regulated by the Companies Ordinance, 1984, so the relevant High Court under Art. 199 read with s. 7 of that Ordinance was the Peshawar High Court, where its head office is, and not the Islamabad High Court. Appeal was allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2058.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: WAPDA Own Assistance Package and Art. 212 Bar
records.heading: A second assistance package is unconscionable and barred by Article 212
records.text: WAPDA had granted its own assistance package and compensated the widow, and that assessment was never challenged and attained finality. Claiming a second package would be unconscionable, and the matter, forming part of the terms of service, was subject to the Art. 212 bar. Appeal was allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2058.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Official Accommodation Allotment: Civil Suit Not Maintainable
records.heading: A civil suit against cancellation of official accommodation is not maintainable
records.text: Allotment or cancellation of official accommodation relates to terms and conditions of service. Orders under the applicable rules cannot be questioned before any court except the forums provided, though the High Court may act under Art. 199 if no forum exists. A civil suit against the Estate Officer's cancellation was not maintainable and the plaint was to be returned. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2073.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Proforma Promotion for Administrative Delay
records.heading: A person missing promotion through administrative delay has a legitimate expectation of proforma promotion
records.text: A person who misses consideration for promotion through administrative oversight or delay and retires before promotion has a legitimate expectation of proforma promotion with consequential benefits. Competent authorities should fix timelines for the committees concerned. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2020.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Move-Over Policy Is Not Promotion
records.heading: Move-over treats the higher scale as an extension and is not promotion
records.text: Move-over is not promotion to a higher pay scale but treats the higher scale as an extension of the existing scale. It was devised for employees who, not being promoted, are stagnant at the maximum of their scale, under the Establishment Code 2007 criteria. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2020.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Dismissal of Teacher for Bogus Transfer Orders
records.heading: A teacher who procured bogus transfer orders was rightly dismissed and her challenge was barred by laches
records.text: A government school teacher who procured bogus transfer orders and failed to give a plausible defence to show cause notices was dismissed after codal formalities. Her challenge to the withdrawal of appointment after about 19 years was hit by laches. The Service Tribunal's reinstatement was set aside and the appeal allowed. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2096.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Appeal as Prerequisite to Service Appeal
records.heading: A departmental appeal is a prerequisite to a service appeal before the Tribunal
records.text: To avail a remedy before the Service Tribunal a departmental appeal must first be filed before the competent forum. Without it, a subsequent service appeal is not maintainable. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2096.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Customs Refund: Manufacturer's Certificate for HS Code
records.heading: A customs refund failed because the HS Code certificate did not come from the manufacturer
records.text: A refund claim for over-paid duties on an imported Hummer limousine failed because the HS Code classification required certification by the manufacturer, General Motors, and the certificate produced came from a seller. The Customs decision rejecting the refund was restored. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2107.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Transmission of Samples: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Acquittal where safe transmission of samples was not established
records.text: Safe transmission of samples to the Chemical Examiner was not established because the Head Constable who delivered them was not produced, permitting an adverse presumption under Art. 129(g) QSO. With no clarity on who was driving among four persons in the truck, the accused was acquitted on benefit of doubt. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2121.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Observations in Bail Orders Do Not Affect Merits
records.heading: Observations in bail orders have no effect on the merits in later proceedings
records.text: Observations made in a bail granting or bail refusing order under ss. 497 and 498 CrPC have no effect on the merits of the case in any subsequent proceedings. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2142.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Proceedings Despite Criminal Acquittal
records.heading: Acquittal in a criminal case does not bar departmental proceedings against a civil servant
records.text: A civil servant cannot escape departmental proceedings or their consequences because of acquittal on a criminal charge. The department may still consider continued service inexpedient and can assess suitability through an inquisitorial fact finding method free of the heavier procedural requirements of criminal trial. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2147.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Transmission of Samples: S. 9(c) Acquittal
records.heading: Acquittal on benefit of doubt where delivery of sample parcels was not proved
records.text: The Moharrar did not say to whom he handed the sample parcels, and no witness proved delivery intact to the laboratory. Safe transmission was not established and tampering could not be excluded, so the appeal was allowed and the accused acquitted on benefit of doubt. Ref: 2022 SCMR 2149.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Promotion of Senior Most from Date of Vacancy
records.heading: The senior most official is entitled to promotion from the date of vacancy
records.text: The senior most official became entitled to promotion to a BPS-17 post vacated by retirement on 12 May 2015, and denial of it was held unlawful and arbitrary by the Tribunal. The case concerned whether promotion took effect from the date of vacancy or later. Ref: 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1481.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Regular Inquiry versus Fact Finding Inquiry
records.heading: A regular inquiry differs from a fact finding inquiry as to procedure and purpose
records.text: A regular inquiry follows a show cause notice and statement of allegations, and requires a fair opportunity of defence and cross-examination. A fact finding inquiry is an internal initial step to see whether a prima facie case of misconduct exists to start disciplinary proceedings. Ref: 2022 SCMR 745, 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1562.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal's Duty to Give Reasons
records.heading: The Service Tribunal must give reasons and discuss evidence before altering a penalty
records.text: Where an order based on an inquiry report is challenged, the Service Tribunal must give reasons and discuss the evidence on record before confirming, reducing or setting aside the penalty. Ref: 2022 SCMR 745, 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1562.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Appointments to Honorary Public Offices: PEMRA COC
records.heading: Honorary public offices must be filled through an open and competitive process
records.text: Appointments to honorary public offices such as the PEMRA Council of Complaints must be made through an open and competitive process including advertisement. The Ordinance and Rules require citizens of eminence, whom the Government must identify through headhunting. The Court issued directions for filling the posts. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1923, 2022 PLC (C.S.) 1577.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Registration of FIR and Prosecution Distinguished
records.heading: Registration of an FIR and prosecution of the offence are entirely distinct
records.text: Registration of an FIR under s. 154 CrPC and prosecution of the offence, with reference to s. 204 CrPC, are entirely distinct phenomena. Ref: 2022 YLR 1131.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Advocate General and Assistant Advocate General
records.heading: The Advocate General is a constitutional appointee while Assistant Advocates General are appointed under statute or rules
records.text: The Advocate General holds a constitutional appointment. An Assistant Advocate General is appointed under statute or rules, which also apply to the Additional Advocate General. Ref: 2022 YLR 1131.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Art. 155 Police Order 2002: Cognizable Offence
records.heading: The offence under Article 155 of the Police Order 2002 is cognizable
records.text: The offence under Art. 155 of the Police Order, 2002 is cognizable, as the Order does not oust the Code of Criminal Procedure on this question. The High Court declined to interfere with the Ex-officio Justice of Peace's direction to record the complainant's version under s. 154 CrPC. Ref: 2022 YLR 1131.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Administrators and Development Projects Without Local Government
records.heading: Administrators cannot carry out development projects on MNA or MPA recommendation
records.text: Local government development projects cannot be carried out by an Administrator on an MNA's or MPA's recommendation, and Administrators may only continue public service. Appointment of Administrators without Cabinet approval was without lawful authority. Grants to MNAs and MPAs for local government work were declared illegal, and the Election Commission was directed to hold elections. Ref: 2022 LHC 8584; M/S Malik Mazhar Hussain v. GOP etc (W.P. 18004-22, decided 23.12.2022); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: M/S Malik Mazhar Hussain v. GOP etc (W.P. 18004-22, decided 23.12.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Husband's Suit to Revoke Gift to Wife: Burden of Proof
records.heading: A husband alleging collusion in a gift to his wife bears the burden of proof
records.text: A husband alleging collusion in a gift mutation to his wife bore the burden under Art. 117 QSO, and the court could not rely on the defendants' weaknesses until it was discharged. Concurrent dismissal was upheld and heavy costs were imposed under s. 35-A CPC. Ref: PLD 2021 Lahore 33.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Declaratory Judgments Art. 184 and O. I R. 10 CPC
records.heading: The Supreme Court may give declaratory judgments under Article 184 in disputes between governments
records.text: Authority on the power to give declaratory judgments under Art. 184 of the Constitution in disputes between governments. The object of O. I R. 10 CPC is to enable the court to adjudicate completely upon all questions between necessary and proper parties. Ref: Province of the Punjab thr. Deputy Commissioner/District Collector, Rawalpindi & another v. Muhammad Akram & others (C.P. 3760/2019, decided 01.12.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Province of the Punjab thr. Deputy Commissioner/District Collector, Rawalpindi & another v. Muhammad Akram & others (C.P. 3760/2019, decided 01.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: Benefit of Doubt at Bail Stage
records.heading: Further inquiry presupposes a tentative assessment creating doubt, and benefit of doubt applies at bail stage
records.text: The expression further inquiry presupposes a tentative assessment creating doubt about the accused's involvement. Every accused is presumed innocent, and benefit of doubt may be extended even at the bail stage. The court looks only at the material before it to see whether tangible evidence exists, without probing the merits. Ref: Fahad Hussain & another v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P. 167-K/2022, decided 28.12.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Fahad Hussain & another v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P. 167-K/2022, decided 28.12.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 306 and 308 PPC: Larger Bench Reference
records.heading: Sections 306 and 308 PPC question for tazir cases was referred to a larger bench
records.text: Case law holds ss. 306 and 308 PPC apply only to qatl-i-amd liable to qisas under s. 302(a), yet this creates an anomaly for tazir cases. Noting Khalil-uz-Zaman and Zahid Rehman, the bench referred the question to the Chief Justice for a larger bench. Ref: Muhammad Nasir v. The State (J.P. 351/2017, decided 03.01.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Nasir v. The State (J.P. 351/2017, decided 03.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXI R. 98 CPC: Resistance in Execution
records.heading: A person may be detained for resistance in execution only after inquiry proves it
records.text: On resistance in execution the court may proceed under O. XXI R. 98 CPC, and may detain a person only after an inquiry proves resistance. The executing court wrongly relied on the bailiff's report without recording his statement or an affidavit, so the impugned order was not sustainable. Ref: 2022 LHC 8611; Kousar Bibi Niazi v. The Learned Civil Judge etc (W.P. 5777-22, decided 01.11.2022); Justice Safdar Saleem Shahid.
records.title: Kousar Bibi Niazi v. The Learned Civil Judge etc (W.P. 5777-22, decided 01.11.2022)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Interim Restraint on ECP Proceedings Against Party Chairman
records.heading: The Election Commission was restrained from proceeding against the party chairman
records.text: The Lahore High Court restrained the Election Commission, for a second time, from proceeding to remove Imran Khan from the party chairmanship, issuing notice and seeking its reply. The petition challenged the Commission's action as beyond its powers. Ref: 2023 LHC 1; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Election Commission of Pakistan (W.P. 332/23, decided 05.01.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Election Commission of Pakistan (W.P. 332/23, decided 05.01.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Transfer of Cases: Art. 186A
records.heading: Inconvenience is no ground for transfer of cases under Article 186A
records.text: The Supreme Court's power under Art. 186A to transfer cases is discretionary and exercised in the interest of justice to secure a fair hearing. Inconvenience to a petitioner is no ground, and he must face litigation before courts of competent jurisdiction. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 27.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Controversial Tweets Case
records.heading: Post-arrest bail was granted in the controversial tweets case
records.text: The Islamabad High Court granted post-arrest bail to Senator Azam Swati in the controversial tweets case. The post gives only the title of the decision. Ref: Muhammad Azam Khan Swati v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Azam Khan Swati v. The State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Controversial Tweets Case
records.heading: Post-arrest bail was granted in the controversial tweets case
records.text: The Islamabad High Court granted post-arrest bail to Senator Azam Swati in the controversial tweets case. The post gives only the title, case number and date. Ref: Muhammad Azam Khan Swati v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 1644-B/2022, decided 02.01.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Azam Khan Swati v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 1644-B/2022, decided 02.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Supreme Court Rules: Explaining Documents Filed
records.heading: Documents filed with an application must be explained under Order XVIII Rule 1
records.text: An application or concise statement must state the purpose of filing under O. XVIII R. 1 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980, which also applies to supplemental proceedings. Documents filed through them, save exhibits or pleadings, must be explained in the application, concise statement or supporting affidavit. Ref: Naeem Tahir & others v. Jahan Shah alias Shah Jehan & others (C.P. 2633/2019, decided 04.01.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Naeem Tahir & others v. Jahan Shah alias Shah Jehan & others (C.P. 2633/2019, decided 04.01.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Federal Shariat Court: Policy Guidelines and Indexation
records.heading: Policy guidelines and indexation fall outside the Federal Shariat Court's jurisdiction
records.text: Giving policy guidelines to government to mould a sector according to Islam is not the Federal Shariat Court's task, and indexation falls outside its jurisdiction as no law presently deals with it. Such matters are for Parliament, the State Bank or the Government. Shariat petitions were allowed. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 47.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Federal Shariat Court Jurisdiction over Fiscal Laws
records.heading: The Federal Shariat Court may examine fiscal laws against the Injunctions of Islam
records.text: The Federal Shariat Court may examine any law, including fiscal laws, against the Injunctions of Islam irrespective of any link to a constitutional Article. The Riba petitions were not merely a prayer to implement Art. 38(f) and were maintainable. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 47.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Insurance and Takaful under Islamic Injunctions
records.heading: Insurance is not un-Islamic per se but Takaful follows Shariah compliant modes
records.text: Insurance is not un-Islamic per se, and its permissibility depends on the business modes used. Insurance linked to Riba, al-Gharar or al-Qimar is prohibited, while Takaful, which follows Shariah compliant modes, is based on Islamic Injunctions. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 47.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Bank Interest as Riba
records.heading: Bank interest on loans and deposits is Riba and prohibited in all forms
records.text: Interest charged by banks on loans and interest paid on deposits are Riba and prohibited in all forms. The prohibition is absolute irrespective of the purpose of the loan, whether consumption or commercial. Shariat petitions were allowed. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 47.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Banking Transactions and Shariah Compliance
records.heading: A bank transaction involving interest in any form is prohibited
records.text: A bank transaction involving interest in any form or percentage is prohibited, even if made in the name of business. Banking is neither permissible nor impermissible per se, and the nature of the transaction decides, so doubtful or non Shariah compliant transactions are impermissible. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 47.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 10-A: Due Process Not Available Repeatedly
records.heading: A person who elects not to be heard cannot repeatedly claim due process under Article 10-A
records.text: Due process under Art. 10-A is afforded to a person whose rights are being determined, but one who elects not to avail the opportunity of being heard cannot benefit from it. Giving repeated opportunities undermines the rights of other parties in the litigation. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 34.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Political Parties as Right Holders under Art. 17(2)
records.heading: Political parties are themselves right holders under Article 17(2)
records.text: Political parties are themselves right holders under Art. 17(2), not placeholders for their members, and the rights inhere in each party in equal measure. A plurality of competing parties is an integral aspect of Art. 17(2). Ref: PLD 2023 SC 42.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 63A Reference: Defector's Vote Disregarded
records.heading: A defector's vote against the party direction is disregarded immediately under Article 63A
records.text: On a Presidential reference under Art. 186 seeking interpretation of Art. 63A, a defector's vote is to be disregarded immediately and automatically once cast against the parliamentary party's direction, with no further act required. A conscientious objector may resign instead of defecting. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 42.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act 2016 Upheld
records.heading: The Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act 2016 is not repugnant to Islam
records.text: Urdu report: the Federal Shariat Court held the Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act, 2016 is not repugnant to the Injunctions of Islam, finding no provision contrary to the Quran and Sunnah, and dismissed the petitions challenging it. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 1; Justice Syed Muhammad Anwer; Justice Khadim Hussain M. Shaikh.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 45 Pardon and Prisoners' Right to Dignity
records.heading: Convicts keep their fundamental rights and ill prisoners may be considered for premature release
records.text: Art. 45 empowers the President to grant pardon, reprieve and remission. Under Art. 9 convicts keep their fundamental rights, including humane treatment, and seriously ill, old or infirm prisoners have a right to be considered for premature release, reported by Jail Superintendents through the Inspector General of Prisons. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 19.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Change of Advocate in Review Petition: O. XXVI R. 6
records.heading: A review application must be drawn by the advocate who appeared at the original hearing
records.text: Under O. XXVI R. 6 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980 a review application must be drawn by the Advocate who appeared in the original hearing. Substitution needs special leave, granted only if earlier counsel's appearance is impossible by unavoidable circumstances. The applications were rejected and the review petitions not entertained. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 22.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: ASC Engaged by AOR: Client's Wish Insufficient
records.heading: Only an ASC instructed by an AOR may represent a party
records.text: Under O. IV R. 6 of the Supreme Court Rules only an ASC instructed by an AOR may represent a party. An AOR engaging another ASC because the client wished it, without special leave, was not sufficient reason to disregard the Rules, and the review petition was dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 19.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: AOR Cannot Withdraw Without Leave
records.heading: An Advocate-on-Record cannot withdraw without leave, even for non-payment of fees
records.text: Under O. IV R. 24 of the Supreme Court Rules, an Advocate-on-Record once engaged cannot withdraw from the case without leave of the Court, and can never do so because his fee, costs or charges were not paid. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 19.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 63A(1)(b): Parliamentary Party Direction and De-Seating
records.heading: The power to issue a direction under Article 63A(1)(b) belongs to the parliamentary party
records.text: The power to issue a direction under Art. 63A(1)(b) belongs to the parliamentary party and cannot be delegated to anyone, including the Party Head. A member who votes against the direction is not ipso facto de-seated, as the Party Head has discretion whether to make a declaration of defection. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 42.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Penal Provisions Construed Strictly
records.heading: A penal provision is construed strictly and its scope is not extended
records.text: A penal provision is construed strictly and its scope is not extended unless clear language or necessary intendment requires it. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 42.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Adoption in Islamic Law
records.heading: A child may be adopted but his real parentage cannot be changed
records.text: Under Surah Al-Ahzab verses 4 and 5, one may adopt a child but cannot change his parentage. The adopted child must be addressed by his real father's name, and if that is unknown he is treated as a brother in Islam and a friend. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 1.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Suspension and Remission of Sentences: Ss. 401 to 402D CrPC
records.heading: Sections 401 to 402-D set the powers to suspend, remit and commute sentences
records.text: S. 401(1) CrPC lets the Provincial Government suspend or remit sentences, and s. 402 allows commutation without consent. S. 402-A gives the President power in death sentences, and s. 402-B limits the Provincial Government after presidential relief. S. 402-C requires victim or heirs' consent in Chapter XVI PPC cases, and s. 402-D bars relief in rape cases. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 19.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Parole of Seriously Ill Prisoner: Probational Release Act
records.heading: Section 2 of the Probational Release Act does not bar parole of a seriously ill prisoner
records.text: S. 2 of the Good Conduct Prisoners Probational Release Act, 1926 imposes no condition barring parole of a seriously ill prisoner. The Director General cannot give instructions that limit the Act's scope or conflict with it. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 19.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 173 CrPC: Completion of Investigation and Interim Report
records.heading: Section 173 CrPC requires prompt investigation and an interim report within fourteen days
records.text: S. 173 CrPC requires investigation without unnecessary delay and a report through the Public Prosecutor to the magistrate. If not finalised within 14 days of the FIR, an interim report must follow within three days, and the court should then commence trial unless there are reasons to postpone. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Investigation: Art. 18A Police Order
records.heading: Article 18A of the Police Order provides the regime for transfer of investigation
records.text: Neither the Code nor the Police Rules, 1934 provided a procedure for transferring investigation between police officers. The Police Order, 2002 addressed this, and the Police Order (Amendment) Act, 2013 introduced Art. 18A with a new regime for transfer of investigation. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Conflicting Supreme Court Judgments: Larger Bench Prevails
records.heading: Where Supreme Court judgments conflict, the larger bench judgment prevails
records.text: Where Supreme Court judgments conflict, the one rendered by the larger bench prevails. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Reasoned Recommendations and Orders under Art. 18A
records.heading: Orders under Article 18A must show reasons and examination of the case file
records.text: Administrative authorities must act in accordance with law and exercise discretion reasonably, failing which courts may set aside the action in judicial review. Under Art. 18A the DSB, RSB and Review Board must show examination of the case file, and the police heads must record reasons and not merely reproduce recommendations, or the order is arbitrary. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ingredients of S. 182 PPC
records.heading: Section 182 PPC requires false information given to a public servant with intent to cause wrongful action
records.text: S. 182 PPC requires giving information to a public servant, known or believed by the giver to be false, with intent to cause or knowing it likely to cause the public servant to act or omit wrongly, or to use his lawful power to injure or annoy another. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 56.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 195 CrPC: Bar on Cognizance of S. 182 PPC
records.heading: Section 195(1)(a) bars cognizance of section 182 PPC except on the public servant's complaint
records.text: S. 195(1)(a) CrPC absolutely bars cognizance of an offence under s. 182 PPC except on written complaint of the public servant concerned or his superior. Cognizance taken by the Sessions Judge himself under s. 476 CrPC on no such complaint was disapproved, and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 56.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Scope of S. 476 CrPC
records.heading: Section 476 CrPC applies only to offences in section 195(1)(b) and (c)
records.text: S. 476 CrPC applies only to offences in s. 195(1)(b) and (c) CrPC and not to those in s. 195(1)(a). A court therefore has no jurisdiction to make a complaint under s. 476 for an offence outside s. 195(1)(b) and (c), though it may complain to the jurisdictional Magistrate. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 56.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint: Summoning on Sufficient Ground
records.heading: Summoning on a private complaint requires only sufficient ground under section 204
records.text: For issuing process on a private complaint, s. 204 CrPC requires only sufficient ground and not reasonable ground, which is a different standard from s. 497(1) CrPC. At that stage the court looks at the relevance of the material, not its admissibility or weight. A complaint may be filed against persons not named in the FIR. Revision against summoning dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 93.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 184(3): Prerequisites for Original Jurisdiction
records.heading: Article 184(3) needs a Fundamental Right violation and a matter of public importance
records.text: To invoke the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Art. 184(3), the petitioner must show violation of his Fundamental Right(s) whose enforcement is a matter of public importance. If either element is absent, the petition cannot be entertained. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 32.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Additional Judges: No Right to Confirmation
records.heading: Additional High Court Judges have no right to confirmation or extension
records.text: Additional High Court Judges have no constitutional tenure, as the President determines their period and confirmation depends on the approval of the Judicial Commission. They cannot claim confirmation as Permanent Judges or an extension on the strength of judicial independence or access to justice, since that would render Art. 197 redundant. No Fundamental Right was infringed, so the petition failed. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 32.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Partial Re-Poll or Fresh Election in Constituency
records.heading: The Election Commission may order a partial re-poll or fresh elections in a constituency
records.text: The post concerns the power of the Election Commission to declare a poll void and order either a partial re-poll or fresh elections in the whole constituency. The judgment states the factors the Commission must bear in mind in choosing between the two. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 1.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Materially Affected Test for Declaring Poll Void
records.heading: A poll is voided where grave illegalities materially affected the result
records.text: In deciding whether to order a re-poll, the Election Commission must ask whether grave illegalities or violations have materially affected the result in one or more polling stations or the whole constituency. Two methods may be used: the numerical tally, or an assessment of the gravity and extent of the violations. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 1.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Advocate's Strike Cannot Prejudice Detained Accused
records.heading: A detained accused must not suffer because his advocate strikes
records.text: A detained accused must not suffer because his advocate strikes, including in solidarity with colleagues. Under the Pakistan Bar Council Canons, an advocate must appear when a matter is called or make alternative arrangements. The court need not wait for the complainant's advocate, as State counsel is required to prosecute. Ref: Shahbaz Akmal v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab, Lahore and another (Crl.P.1496/2022, decided 05.01.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Shahbaz Akmal v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab, Lahore and another (Crl.P.1496/2022, decided 05.01.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Repeat Bail Application on Statutory Delay Ground
records.heading: An accused who withdraws a bail application on statutory delay cannot refile on that ground
records.text: According to the Urdu note in the post, an accused who files a bail application on the ground of statutory delay in trial and then withdraws it cannot file a fresh application on the same ground. Ref: Shahbaz Akmal v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab, Lahore and another (Crl.P.1496/2022, decided 05.01.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Shahbaz Akmal v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab, Lahore and another (Crl.P.1496/2022, decided 05.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Change of Advocate in Review Petition
records.heading: Changing counsel in review applications without justifiable reasons is condemnable
records.text: Order XXVI of the Supreme Court Rules 1980 governs review practice and stresses the role of the advocate who draws the application. Under r. 6 the review is drawn by the advocate who appeared at the original hearing. Filing review applications by changing counsel without justifiable reasons or unavoidable circumstances is condemnable. Ref: Muhammad Iqbal (deceased) v. Ahmad Din (deceased) through his L.Rs., etc (C.M.A.1609-L/2021, decided 30.12.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal (deceased) v. Ahmad Din (deceased) through his L.Rs., etc (C.M.A.1609-L/2021, decided 30.12.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit by Unauthorised Person: Curable Defect
records.heading: A suit filed by an unauthorised person is a curable defect
records.text: A suit filed by an unauthorised person is a curable defect. Under O. III R. 1 CPC an act in court may be done by the party, his recognised agent or his pleader, but signing and verifying pleadings falls under O. VI Rr. 14 and 15 CPC, which expressly provide otherwise. The post also refers to O. IV, VIII and XXIX R. 1 CPC. Ref: SDO/AMO Hasth Nagri Sub Division PESCO, Peshawar & others v. Khawazam Zad (C.P.1159/2019, decided 06.12.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: SDO/AMO Hasth Nagri Sub Division PESCO, Peshawar & others v. Khawazam Zad (C.P.1159/2019, decided 06.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Ipse Dixit of Investigating Officer
records.heading: A second Investigating Officer's ipse dixit carries no persuasive value for cancelling bail
records.text: The opinion of a second Investigating Officer carries no persuasive value unless based on cogent and concrete material. Accepting such ipse dixit as the ground for bail would discredit the eye witnesses' version at the initial stage. The accused was nominated for a firearm injury on the head of the deceased, supported by medical evidence. Ref: Amir Faraz v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl.P.475/2022, decided 09.01.2023); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood.
records.title: Amir Faraz v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl.P.475/2022, decided 09.01.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Public Interest Litigation
records.heading: Public interest litigation was considered; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on public interest litigation. The post gives only the case title, the writ petition number and the hearing date of 23.12.2022, without a holding. Ref: Mazhar Rasool Hashmi v. Government of the Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 81608/2022).
records.title: Mazhar Rasool Hashmi v. Government of the Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 81608/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Compassionate Release and Terminal Illness: S. 401 CrPC
records.heading: Compassionate release allows terminally ill prisoners to be released before completing their sentence
records.text: Compassionate release allows terminally ill and some other very sick prisoners to be released before completing their sentence, on the basis that a change in health may alter the justification for imprisonment. The post also defines terminal illness, with advanced cancer and heart disease as examples. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 19.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Restoration of Appeal Dismissed Without Listing
records.heading: An appeal dismissed on a date when it was not listed is void
records.text: An appeal dismissed for non-prosecution before the record summoned by the court was received, and on a date when it was not listed, is not an order under O. XLI R. 17(1) CPC and is void. The restoration application was not time barred, so its dismissal as barred was a nullity. The High Court in revision set aside both orders. Ref: PLD 2023 Sindh 23.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Place of Trial: Offence in Two Districts
records.heading: Courts of each area have concurrent jurisdiction where an offence is committed in parts
records.text: Where an offence is committed in parts in different areas, courts of each area have concurrent jurisdiction. The more suitable court is chosen under r. 3, Chapter 26, Vol. III of the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders. Abduction and murder cases were tried together in the district where the parties and witnesses resided, and the case was transferred under s. 526 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 1.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 4 MFLO: Widow of Predeceased Son
records.heading: The widow of a predeceased son is not entitled under section 4 MFLO
records.text: Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 benefits only the sons and daughters of a predeceased son or daughter. The widow of a predeceased son is neither sharer nor residuary and is not entitled to the legacy of her father-in-law or mother-in-law. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 6.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 4 MFLO Subject to Shariat Shares
records.heading: Section 4 MFLO is subject to Shariat shares and cannot reduce other descendants' shares
records.text: Section 4 MFLO 1961 removes the hardship of grandchildren but cannot reduce the shares of other descendants. Despite its non-obstante clause it is read with s. 2 of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1962, and where the two overlap or conflict, Shariat prevails. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 6.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Commissioner's Written Opinion under S. 17(4)
records.heading: The Commissioner's opinion on urgency must be expressed in a written order
records.text: The Commissioner must form an opinion that the urgency provisions apply, and it must be expressed in a written order and not presumed. Before acting under s. 17(4) he must reach it on material before him, with a direct nexus to the power, having regard to Rr. 10 and 11 of the Punjab Land Acquisition Rules 1983 on preserving agricultural economy. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 1.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Urgency Acquisition: Right of Hearing under S. 5-A
records.heading: The section 5-A right of hearing is inviolate even in urgency acquisition
records.text: Even in urgency under s. 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act 1894, ss. 5 and 5-A and all steps up to the s. 9 notice must be complied with, and possession can be taken only after that notice. The s. 5-A right of hearing is inviolate. The notifications under ss. 4, 17(4) and 6 were struck down. Urgency connotes immediate steps. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 1.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Shia Divorce: Reading of Seeghajaat
records.heading: A Shia male may divorce by reading the Seeghajaat directly or through a wakeel
records.text: Under Fiqah-e-Jafria a Shia male can pronounce divorce by reading the Seeghajaat, directly or through a wakeel, in the presence of the wife or her wakeel, after which the divorce takes effect. This could be done in the present case even with retrospective effect, where a Family Court had dissolved the marriage by khula. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 38.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Determining Tentative Rate of Rent
records.heading: Rent Controller factors for fair rent may fix tentative rent under the Punjab Act
records.text: The factors a Rent Controller uses to fix fair rent under s. 8(1) and (2) of the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance 1979, such as rent of similar premises nearby, rise in construction and repair costs and annual value, can be applied to determine tentative rent under s. 24 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 47.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction for Default in Tentative Rent
records.heading: Eviction follows default in paying tentative rent fixed by the Rent Tribunal
records.text: The tenant did not deny the rate of rent and defaulted in paying the tentative rent fixed by the Rent Tribunal, so eviction was ordered under s. 24 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009. The Tribunal rightly directed monthly deposit by the 10th, adjustable against dues at the final stage. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 47.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Late Challenge to Inheritance Mutation
records.heading: Later heirs cannot challenge an inheritance mutation after long delay and many transfers
records.text: Where a legal heir deprived of inheritance lived for a considerable period without challenging it, later heirs have no locus standi to challenge the mutation after the property has changed many hands. The suit filed in 2006 was barred by time. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 12.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: No Suo Motu Jurisdiction of High Court under Art. 199
records.heading: The High Court has no suo motu jurisdiction under Article 199
records.text: The High Court has no suo motu jurisdiction under Art. 199, which is vested only in the Supreme Court under Art. 184(3). Banning imports or exports lies in the executive domain, and the High Court could not fix prices. It could at most direct the Government to perform its legal duty. Ref: M/s Sadiq Poultry Pvt Ltd Rawalpindi v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through its Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others (C.P.5646/2021, decided 27.09.2022); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan.
records.title: M/s Sadiq Poultry Pvt Ltd Rawalpindi v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through its Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others (C.P.5646/2021, decided 27.09.2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Sales Tax Act Judgment
records.heading: A sales tax matter was decided; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on a sales tax matter, described in the Urdu note as highly informative. The post gives no holding. Ref: The Commissioner Inland Revenue Z-II, LTP v. M/s Attock Cement Pakistan Limited (C.A.1422/2019, decided 12.01.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: The Commissioner Inland Revenue Z-II, LTP v. M/s Attock Cement Pakistan Limited (C.A.1422/2019, decided 12.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Reliable Ocular Account
records.heading: A report made four hours after the incident was prompt and the ocular account reliable
records.text: A report made about four hours after the incident, with the police station 25 kilometres away, was prompt. The related eye witnesses remained consistent under cross-examination and the medical evidence matched their account. The petitioners were convicted under s. 302(c) PPC and sentenced to 14 years, a lenient view being warranted. Ref: Muhammad Abbas and Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Petition No. 355 of 2018, decided 02.01.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Abbas and Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Petition No. 355 of 2018, decided 02.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone sustains conviction
records.text: Where ocular evidence is trustworthy and confidence inspiring, it is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices to sustain conviction, relying on 1996 SCMR 908, PLD 2003 SC 396, 2010 SCMR 1025 and 2011 SCMR 460. Medical evidence and recovery are corroborative only. Ref: Nasir Ahmed v. The State (Jail Petition No. 865 of 2017, decided 12.12.2022).
records.title: Nasir Ahmed v. The State (Jail Petition No. 865 of 2017, decided 12.12.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Ban on Motorcycles on Motorways
records.heading: Section 45 permits a ban on motorcyclists on motorways without violating fundamental rights
records.text: Section 45 of the National Highways Safety Ordinance 2000 permits prohibiting or restricting motor vehicles in the interest of public safety or convenience, including a ban on motorcyclists on motorways. The ban was within the law and did not violate any fundamental right to life or liberty. Leave converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 129.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat
records.heading: A statute is construed to be effective and cannot be read down into meaninglessness
records.text: A statute must be construed so as to make it effective and operative, and the presumption favours constitutionality. A court can strike down an unconstitutional law but cannot, by reading down, render a provision meaningless or inoperative. Ref: 2023 SCMR 129.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 25: Reasonable Classification
records.heading: Reasonable classification requires an intelligible differentia rationally related to the object of the law
records.text: Persons may be classified into groups and treated differently if there is a reasonable basis. Classification must rest on an intelligible differentia that distinguishes those grouped together from others left out, and the differentia must have a rational relationship with the object of the law. Ref: 2023 SCMR 129.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Scope of Judicial Review
records.heading: Judicial review must stay distinct from judicial overreach
records.text: Judicial review lets courts examine the lawfulness of legislative and executive action, on grounds such as ultra vires acts, unreasonableness, breach of natural justice or statutory procedure, and breach of legitimate expectation. Courts must draw a line between judicial review and judicial overreach and remain within the confines of the dispute and the Constitution. Ref: 2023 SCMR 129.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: ATA: Not Every Grievous Offence Is Terrorism
records.heading: Not every grievous offence amounts to terrorism under the Anti-Terrorism Act
records.text: The Anti-Terrorism Act is a special law to be read in light of its preamble and object. Relying on a seven member bench, not every case of grievous bodily harm, damage to property or endangering life amounts to terrorism. The Urdu note says the Court accepted the appeals and acquitted all accused, including Shah Rukh Jatoi, in the Shahzeb Khan murder case. Ref: 2023 SCMR 16.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX R. 13 CPC: Setting Aside Ex-Parte Decree
records.heading: A vague application under Order IX Rule 13 cannot succeed through the party's own negligence
records.text: An application under O. IX R. 13 CPC alleging an unproved compromise was deficient in material facts and vague, giving no details of the compromise or instructions to counsel, nor why the defendant did not confirm withdrawal of the suit. A party cannot take advantage of his own negligence. Leave to appeal refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 159.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial Commission Decisions and Art. 199
records.heading: Judicial Commission decisions under Article 175A are not reviewable by constitutional petition
records.text: Decisions of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan under Art. 175A are not open to judicial review through constitutional petitions under Art. 199, as the Commission is not a Court under High Court superintendence for certiorari. Even if reviewable, the decision in question had no legal or jurisdictional defect. Ref: 2023 SCMR 68.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Additional Judge: No Vested Right to Confirmation
records.heading: An Additional Judge has no vested right to confirmation on recommendation alone
records.text: An Additional Judge has no vested right to confirmation merely because the Chief Justice recommended him. The recommendation is procedural and must be deliberated and voted on by the Judicial Commission. The petition against non-confirmation was rightly dismissed, and leave to appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 68.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Scope of Certiorari under Art. 199
records.heading: In certiorari the High Court does not sit as a court of appeal
records.text: In constitutional jurisdiction the High Court does not sit as a court of appeal. Certiorari directs a court under its superintendence to correct errors of law or jurisdiction, and although a prerogative under Art. 199, it remains a discretionary power. Ref: 2023 SCMR 68.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ of Quo Warranto: Scope and Prerequisites
records.heading: Quo warranto lies at the instance of any bona fide member of the public
records.text: Quo warranto tests whether a holder of public office occupies it in accordance with law. The relator need not be an aggrieved person and it suffices that he is a member of the public acting bona fide. It lies where the holder lacks qualification, the appointing authority was not competent or the prescribed procedure was not followed, and the burden then lies on the appointee. Ref: 2023 SCMR 162.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Stopgap Appointment and Additional Charge
records.heading: A stopgap or additional charge arrangement confers no right and may be withdrawn without reasons
records.text: A stopgap arrangement, such as ad hoc appointment or look-after, acting or additional charge, is temporary and the incumbent does not hold the post substantively. It confers no claim to benefit and may be withdrawn by the competent authority at any time without reasons. Ref: 2023 SCMR 162.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence over Medical; Blackening Discrepancy
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence prevails over medical evidence despite blackening discrepancies
records.text: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence. Blackening depends on factors such as the target surface, body structure and gunpowder quality, and the victim was not static. Casual discrepancies between medical and ocular accounts about distance and location of shots are possible, since witnesses can only make a tentative assessment. Ref: 2023 SCMR 190.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses; Substitution Rare
records.heading: Relationship with the deceased is no ground to discard prosecution witnesses
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony. Substitution is a rare phenomenon, and a complainant would not spare the real killer of his brother to falsely implicate the petitioner without reason. Ref: 2023 SCMR 190.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: ASI Not Authorised to Investigate Murder
records.heading: An Assistant Sub-Inspector is not authorised to investigate a murder case under section 302 PPC
records.text: Under the law, an Assistant Sub-Inspector is not authorised to investigate a murder case falling within s. 302 PPC. Ref: 2023 SCMR 190.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction Sustained Without Motive and Recovery
records.heading: Conviction stands on sufficient evidence even where motive and recovery are discarded
records.text: Even if motive and recovery are discarded, sufficient evidence remains to sustain the conviction. As recovery was inconsequential and motive unproved, the High Court rightly took a lenient view in converting death to imprisonment for life, and no further leniency could be shown. Ref: 2023 SCMR 190.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Joint Confession of Co-Accused
records.heading: A confession made jointly by co-accused has no legal sanctity and is inadmissible
records.text: A confessional statement made jointly by all the co-accused has no legal sanctity and is inadmissible in evidence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 190.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Doctrine of Parity and Rule of Consistency
records.heading: Bail follows parity: accused with the same role as bailed co-accused are treated alike
records.text: Where the role of the accused is the same as that of co-accused already bailed, like cases should be treated alike, after accurate assessment of each role. Accused with a composite role like two bailed co-accused, and no ransom alleged in the FIR, was granted bail under s. 497(2) CrPC, and the petition was converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 184.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry and Right to Expeditious Trial
records.heading: Further inquiry rests on tentative doubt, and detention is not punishment
records.text: Further inquiry requires a tentative assessment of the record creating doubt about involvement of the accused. The object of detention is to make the accused face trial and not to punish him, and he is entitled to a fair and expeditious trial. Reasonable grounds under s. 497 CrPC must be legally tenable, admissible and appealing to a reasonable judicial mind, relying on 2016 SCMR 18 and PLD 2014 SC 760. Ref: 2023 SCMR 184.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Reasonable Doubt: Better on Bail than in Jail
records.heading: Where reasonable doubt exists about involvement, the accused is better kept on bail
records.text: Where reasonable doubt arises about the accused's participation or the prosecution case, he should not be denied bail and it is better to keep him on bail during trial. If the prosecution places no material showing involvement, the court may hold detention unjustified without dilating on the facts. Ref: 2023 SCMR 184.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Benami Transaction: Proof and Pleading
records.heading: A benami claim must be decided on legal grounds, not suspicion, and properly pleaded
records.text: In a benami claim the court must decide on legal grounds and not on suspicion or conjecture, applying the ordinary course of human conduct. A benami transaction involves the seller, the real owner and the benamidar, with a contract between real owner and benamidar. The appellants' pleadings and evidence fell short of the material facts, which alone sufficed to reject their claim. Ref: Muhammad Yousaf and others v. Muhammad Ishaq Rana (deceased) through L.Rs and others (C.A.801/2021); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf and others v. Muhammad Ishaq Rana (deceased) through L.Rs and others (C.A.801/2021)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Incorrect Statutory Provision Cited in Order
records.heading: Citing the wrong statutory provision in an order does not invalidate it where the power exists
records.text: Even if the authority making the impugned order did not mention the correct statutory provision, the court will consider the matter under it if the relevant power or jurisdiction has been conferred. Ref: 2023 SCMR 179.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Removal of Chief Minister Punjab: Notification Declared Void
records.heading: Notification removing the Punjab Chief Minister declared void after the Governor withdrew his own
records.text: According to the Urdu post, the Governor Punjab withdrew his notification removing Chaudhry Pervaiz Elahi as Chief Minister. The Court declared void the Chief Secretary's notification of 22 December and disposed of the petition. Ref: 2023 LHC 8; Ch. Pervaiz Ellahi v. Governor Punjab etc. (W.P. 82603/22, decided 12.01.2023); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Ch. Pervaiz Ellahi v. Governor Punjab etc. (W.P. 82603/22, decided 12.01.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Shia Divorce: Seeghajaat and Retrospective Effect
records.heading: Shia divorce takes effect on reading the Seeghajaat in the wife's presence
records.text: Under Fiqa Jafria a divorce takes effect when the Seeghajaat are read, directly or through a representative, in presence of the wife or her representative. The recent amendment to s. 7 MFLO accords with precedent, and the exercise can be undertaken now even with retrospective effect. The petitioner had not denied the respondent's presence in court. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 2.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
