records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Consent Decree Under Settlement
records.heading: A party who consents to a decree under a settlement cannot later attack it under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: By consenting to the respondent's suit being decreed and withdrawing her own suit under a settlement agreement, the petitioner is deemed to have accepted his plea. The decree was not obtained by fraud. The writ petition was an abuse of process and was dismissed with costs throughout. Ref: PLJ 2023 Islamabad 21; Mrs. Rubina Amjad v. Javaid Shafique Saddiqui and 9 others (W.P. No. 1412 of 2020, decided 21.09.2022); Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Mrs. Rubina Amjad v. Javaid Shafique Saddiqui and 9 others (W.P. No. 1412 of 2020, decided 21.09.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Police Deployment in Punjab Assembly for CM Election
records.heading: The Speaker may be assisted by the Sergeant at Arms in deploying police for the election
records.text: The petition challenged the Deputy Speaker's order deploying police in the Punjab Assembly for the election of the Chief Minister. Rule 210(5) of the Assembly Rules authorises the Speaker to be assisted by the Sergeant at Arms, as the Assembly has its own internal security system. Petitions disposed of. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 1; Muhammad Sibtain Khan v. Deputy Speaker, Provincial Assembly for the Province of Punjab through Secretary Punjab Assembly and others (W.P. No. 45456 of 2022, decided 22.07.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Sibtain Khan v. Deputy Speaker, Provincial Assembly for the Province of Punjab through Secretary Punjab Assembly and others (W.P. No. 45456 of 2022, decided 22.07.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Oral Sale and Limitation
records.heading: A suit filed beyond three years from withdrawal of the earlier suit is time barred
records.text: The plaintiff failed to discharge the onus on the key issues and both courts below misread and non-read the evidence. A suit filed beyond three years from withdrawal of the earlier one was time barred, as compliance with the statutory period is mandatory. Revision allowed, decrees set aside and suit dismissed with costs. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 13; Muhammad Ayub (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Hashim Khan (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (C.R. No. 180 of 2006, heard 12.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Masood Jahangir.
records.title: Muhammad Ayub (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Hashim Khan (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (C.R. No. 180 of 2006, heard 12.01.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Waiting List Candidate Not Penalised for Department's Lapse
records.heading: A waiting list candidate cannot be penalised for the department's lapse in omitting him
records.text: The petitioner stood at Sr. No. 4 in the waiting list and could have been appointed when recommended candidates did not join. His omission from PPSC's revised recommendations was a lapse for which he cannot be penalised. The impugned order was unsustainable, petition allowed and his grievance to be decided within thirty days. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 34; Asad Abbas v. Government of the Punjab through Secretary Co-operative Societies Department, Lahore and others (W.P. No. 55270 of 2020, decided 20.09.2021); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Asad Abbas v. Government of the Punjab through Secretary Co-operative Societies Department, Lahore and others (W.P. No. 55270 of 2020, decided 20.09.2021)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Vague General Power of Attorney
records.heading: A vague general power of attorney not identifying the property cannot support an agreement to sell
records.text: A general power of attorney that did not identify the suit property or authorise an agreement to sell made the transaction doubtful, as a power of attorney must be free from vagueness. Failure to cross-examine on a witness's statement amounts to admission, and a photocopy of the power of attorney was produced without proving non-availability of the original. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 39; Muhammad Ashraf (deceased) through L.Rs., and etc. v. Muhammad Yousaf, etc. (C.R. No. 225-D of 2002, decided 29.06.2022); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf (deceased) through L.Rs., and etc. v. Muhammad Yousaf, etc. (C.R. No. 225-D of 2002, decided 29.06.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension Withheld on Life Imprisonment
records.heading: Pension is withheld on imprisonment and restored only on acquittal in appeal
records.text: Good conduct is an implied condition of pension. On a pensioner's sentence to imprisonment, the pension is suspended and restored only if he is acquitted on appeal. The petitioner was merely on bail with sentence suspended, so withholding of his pension was justified. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 69; Akhtar Ali v. Post Master General (W.P. No. 2738 of 2018, decided 23.06.2022); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Akhtar Ali v. Post Master General (W.P. No. 2738 of 2018, decided 23.06.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Wife's Suit for Personal Belongings: Family Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: A wife's suit for personal belongings and property bought after marriage lies before the Family Court
records.text: A suit by a wife for personal belongings or property purchased after marriage while residing with her husband falls within the jurisdiction of the Family Court under the Family Courts Act 1964, subject to proof. Both courts below erred in ousting her on jurisdiction. Petition accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 76; Suriya Nafees v. Muhammad Ramzan Shahid etc. (W.P. No. 9545 of 2016, heard 18.01.2022); Justice Safdar Saleem Shahid.
records.title: Suriya Nafees v. Muhammad Ramzan Shahid etc. (W.P. No. 9545 of 2016, heard 18.01.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Regularisation: Subsequent Policy Cannot Defeat Vested Right
records.heading: A later policy cannot defeat a vested right to regularisation
records.text: Refusal to regularise a Junior Auditor appointed in 2013 on the ground of a changed qualification under a revised policy was unjustified. A right accrued cannot be taken away by a later notification, which applies prospectively absent legal sanction. Petition allowed and the impugned order set aside. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 79; Muhammad Tariq v. Controller General of Accounts, Islamabad and 3 others (W.P. No. 66323 of 2020, heard 06.06.2022); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Muhammad Tariq v. Controller General of Accounts, Islamabad and 3 others (W.P. No. 66323 of 2020, heard 06.06.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell by Guardian Without Court Permission
records.heading: A guardian mother cannot sell a minor's property without Guardian Court permission under section 29
records.text: A mother appointed guardian cannot alienate a minor's property without permission of the Guardian Court under s. 29 of the Guardians and Wards Act 1890. Her agreement to sell is void and cannot be enforced by a suit for specific performance. Concurrent findings were sound and the civil revision was dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 83; Afzaal Ahmad Buttar and another v. Muhammad Yousaf (C.R. No. 520 of 2022, decided 11.01.2022); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Afzaal Ahmad Buttar and another v. Muhammad Yousaf (C.R. No. 520 of 2022, decided 11.01.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Contract Employee Not Meeting Eligibility: Estoppel
records.heading: Respondents are estopped from calling a recruitment illegal after their committee recommended the employee
records.text: The petitioner did not meet the eligibility criterion but committed no fraud or misrepresentation, and the Recruitment Committee scrutinised her record and recommended her. Respondents were estopped from calling the recruitment illegal, and she acquired the qualification within the period in her appointment letter. Termination was unjustified and the petition accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 86; Salma Karamat v. District Education Officer (M-EE), Narowal, etc. (W.P. No. 20794 of 2021, heard 13.05.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Salma Karamat v. District Education Officer (M-EE), Narowal, etc. (W.P. No. 20794 of 2021, heard 13.05.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Voluntary Retirement and Amended S. 12: No Retrospectivity
records.heading: Amended section 12 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act does not apply retrospectively
records.text: A statute does not apply retrospectively unless expressly stated. A Finance Department clarification had no lawful basis as officials cannot interpret, modify or add to a provision of law. The retirement order was issued before the amended s. 12 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act 1974 commenced. Petition accepted and pension case to be processed within thirty days. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 91; Muhammad Faheem Zafar v. Government of the Punjab and 3 others (W.P. No. 17603 of 2021, heard 18.01.2022); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Muhammad Faheem Zafar v. Government of the Punjab and 3 others (W.P. No. 17603 of 2021, heard 18.01.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Declaration Suit: Preponderance of Probability and Revisional Limits
records.heading: A revisional court exceeds jurisdiction by disturbing concurrent findings of preponderance of probability
records.text: In a s. 42 Specific Relief Act suit, the appellants' evidence created a high degree of probability of their relationship with Nasir-ud-Din, shifting the evidential burden to the respondents. The trial and appellate courts rightly found preponderance of probability, and the revisional court appears to have exceeded its jurisdiction by setting aside their findings. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 8; Salamat Ali and others v. Muhammad Din and others (C.A. No. 849 of 2015, decided 20.01.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Salamat Ali and others v. Muhammad Din and others (C.A. No. 849 of 2015, decided 20.01.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata: Reopening Decided Inheritance Dispute
records.heading: Res judicata bars a fresh suit reopening a dispute finally decided earlier
records.text: Under s. 11 CPC, public policy requires that disputes finally decided should not be reopened. A 1958 judgment was never challenged by the party or her legal heirs, and a fresh suit on the same cause of action in 1997 was impermissible. Not every observation in a Supreme Court judgment creates a binding precedent. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 29; Muhammad Shifa and others v. Meherban Ali and others (C.A. No. 1389 of 2014, decided 03.02.2022); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Muhammad Shifa and others v. Meherban Ali and others (C.A. No. 1389 of 2014, decided 03.02.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Jurisdiction over Suit Concerning Property in USA
records.heading: Civil courts at Sahiwal lacked jurisdiction over a suit on income from land in the USA
records.text: A suit for recovery of income from inherited land in the USA, against a respondent residing there, fell outside s. 10 CPC, and on the plaint's averments the civil courts at Sahiwal lacked jurisdiction. The suit was also filed at least 28 years later without valid justification. The High Court's judgment was upheld and the appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 32; Rana Muhammad Hanif Khan (deceased) through LRs v. Saddiq Khan (deceased) through LRs (C.A. No. 997 of 2010, decided 14.02.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Rana Muhammad Hanif Khan (deceased) through LRs v. Saddiq Khan (deceased) through LRs (C.A. No. 997 of 2010, decided 14.02.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 115 CPC: High Court and Remand Orders
records.heading: Under section 115 CPC the High Court is not confined to affirming or repeating a remand
records.text: The appellate court remanded the case on an impleadment application without considering the record or evidence. The High Court under s. 115 CPC was not confined to affirming the remand or remanding again, and rightly found no basis for remand as the issue stood decided. The parties had litigated for over twenty years. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 39; Noor Muhammad (deceased) through L.Rs. and others v. Muhammad Ashraf and others (C.A. No. 1296 of 2013, decided 07.02.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Noor Muhammad (deceased) through L.Rs. and others v. Muhammad Ashraf and others (C.A. No. 1296 of 2013, decided 07.02.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post-Mortem and Strangulation
records.heading: Delay in post-mortem suggests absence of witnesses, and strangulation is distinguished from hanging
records.text: Relying on 2012 SCMR 327, delay in post-mortem examination reflects the absence of witnesses and is meant to procure their presence and advance a false narrative. Strangulation is compression of the neck by a force other than hanging, and throttling by fingers leaves thumb and finger marks on either side of the neck. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 50; Muhammad Naeem v. State (Crl. A. No. 467-J & M.R. No. 22 of 2019, heard 12.01.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Naeem v. State (Crl. A. No. 467-J & M.R. No. 22 of 2019, heard 12.01.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 117 QSO: Burden of Proof
records.heading: Article 117 QSO presumes innocence until the prosecution proves guilt by sufficient evidence
records.text: Article 117 QSO enshrines the foundational principle that the accused is presumed innocent unless proved guilty. The burden on the accused arises only when the prosecution has proved guilt by sufficient evidence, apart from facts under Art. 122 QSO. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 50; Muhammad Naeem v. State (Crl. A. No. 467-J & M.R. No. 22 of 2019, heard 12.01.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Naeem v. State (Crl. A. No. 467-J & M.R. No. 22 of 2019, heard 12.01.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Copy of Video Hard Disk of Crime Scene
records.heading: A video hard disk of the crime scene is a document and the accused may obtain a copy
records.text: A video film on a hard disk of the crime scene is a document under Art. 2(1)(b) QSO, and the accused's application for a copy was covered by s. 265-C CrPC. Excluding it from evidence because a person hardly relevant failed to make copies was unlawful. Revision allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 85; Javed Iqbal v. State, etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 307 of 2021, heard 26.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. State, etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 307 of 2021, heard 26.01.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Earlier Probation under S. 5 Ordinance
records.heading: An earlier conviction with probation, without breach, was considered in a post-arrest bail case
records.text: In a s. 9 CNSA case with recovery of 510 grams charas, the court considered the accused's earlier drug conviction with one year's probation under s. 5 of the Probation of Offenders Ordinance 1960. No breach of the bond was alleged, no s. 7 proceedings were initiated and he was never sentenced for the original offence. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 88; Abid alias Chirri v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 411-B of 2022, decided 08.04.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Abid alias Chirri v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 411-B of 2022, decided 08.04.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Disbelieved Witnesses and Dishonest Improvements
records.heading: Witnesses disbelieved against some accused cannot convict others without strong independent corroboration
records.text: Where the same witnesses are disbelieved against some accused, they cannot found conviction of the rest without strong independent corroboration. Injuries on a witness do not make him truthful, and a witness who makes dishonest improvements is unworthy of reliance without such corroboration. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 94; Bagga etc. v. State etc. (Crl. As. Nos. 441-J & 442-J & C.S.R. No. 3 of 2018, decided 11.01.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Bagga etc. v. State etc. (Crl. As. Nos. 441-J & 442-J & C.S.R. No. 3 of 2018, decided 11.01.2022)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Powers of DG Anti-Corruption and Speaking Orders
records.heading: An order of the DG Anti-Corruption without reasons is not a speaking order
records.text: Rule 15(2) of the Punjab Anti-Corruption Establishment Rules 2014 empowers the DG to peruse the record of a pending investigation and give directions for fair and speedy investigation. An order without reasons is not a speaking order. The order was set aside and the application remitted to the DG for fresh decision with reasons. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 22; Nisar Ahmad Afzal v. D.G. Anti-Corruption, etc. (W.P. No. 43868 of 2022, heard 15.07.2022); Justice Muhammad Shan Gul.
records.title: Nisar Ahmad Afzal v. D.G. Anti-Corruption, etc. (W.P. No. 43868 of 2022, heard 15.07.2022)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 7 ATA Not Compoundable: Acquittal on Appeal
records.heading: Section 7 ATA is non-compoundable, yet the Supreme Court acquitted the appellants on appeal
records.text: After a compromise with the legal heirs, the High Court set aside the convictions under ss. 302/109/34 PPC but maintained conviction under s. 7 ATA as non-compoundable. The occurrence arose from an indecent joke with the complainant's daughter. The Supreme Court allowed the appeals and acquitted the appellants. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 1; Nawab Siraj Ali and others v. State through A.G. Sindh (Crl. A. Nos. 400, 401 and 402 of 2019, decided 18.10.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Nawab Siraj Ali and others v. State through A.G. Sindh (Crl. A. Nos. 400, 401 and 402 of 2019, decided 18.10.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Refused: Fraud and Cheque Allegations
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail refused where oral and documentary material showed fraud over an agreement to sell
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was refused in a case under ss. 406, 489-F, 420, 468 and 471 PPC where the petitioner took Rs. 4.4 million on an agreement to sell land and promised part refund. Sufficient oral and documentary material existed against him. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 18; Malik Muhammad Tahir v. State and another (Crl. P. No. 287 of 2022, decided 22.09.2022); Justice Ijaz Ul Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Malik Muhammad Tahir v. State and another (Crl. P. No. 287 of 2022, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Confession Must Be Read as a Whole
records.heading: A confession must be accepted or rejected as a whole, not in part
records.text: A confession must be accepted or rejected as a whole, and the court cannot rely on the inculpatory part while rejecting the exculpatory part. The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt whatever plea the accused takes. Appeal allowed and the accused acquitted on benefit of doubt in a case of 25 kilograms of charas. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 21; Javed Iqbal v. State (Crl. A. No. 139 of 2022, decided 25.10.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. State (Crl. A. No. 139 of 2022, decided 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cross Version and Further Inquiry
records.heading: A cross version alone does not make a case one of further inquiry
records.text: Mere existence of a cross version is not a ground for holding a case one of further inquiry under s. 497 CrPC. Where the court cannot even tentatively tell which party was the aggressor, the case against both falls within further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Treating every cross version as further inquiry without tentative assessment would encourage concocted versions. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 31; Muhammad Rafique v. State and others (Crl. P. No. 301 of 2022, decided 22.06.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. State and others (Crl. P. No. 301 of 2022, decided 22.06.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Confession Read in Toto, Not in Pieces
records.heading: A confession must be read in toto and cannot be split into inculpatory and exculpatory parts
records.text: A judicial or extra-judicial confession must be considered as a whole and accepted or rejected as a whole. The court cannot select the inculpatory passage and discard the exculpatory part. Where the prosecution fails to prove its case, a conviction may rest on the confession only if it is taken in toto. Ref: 2023 SCMR 139; Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 139 of 2022).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 139 of 2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: S. 9(c) CNSA: Safe Custody and Transmission of Samples
records.heading: The prosecution must prove every link in safe custody and transmission of narcotic samples
records.text: In a s. 9(c) CNSA case the prosecution must establish every step from recovery, sealing of sample parcels, safe custody and safe transmission to the laboratory. If any link is missing, the benefit of doubt goes to the accused. Here the custody of the parcels between recovery and receipt by the Chemical Examiner was unexplained, and the accused was acquitted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 139, 2022 SCMR 2149, 2022 SCMR 2121, 2022 SCMR 2105 and others; Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 139 of 2022).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 139 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Undertaking Recorded in Compromise
records.heading: A recorded undertaking in a compromise remains enforceable in execution despite dismissal of the suit
records.text: A tenant sued for permanent injunction and, on compromise, undertook before the court to vacate within six months. The Lahore High Court held that a party who fails to honour his recorded undertaking remains bound by it despite dismissal of the suit, and execution may be filed against him. Provisions on execution of decrees apply to orders, s. 36 CPC. Revision dismissed. Ref: 2018 CLC 1833.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Bare Denial of Agreement to Sell Insufficient
records.heading: A bare denial of an agreement to sell is insufficient, and later admission departs from pleadings
records.text: A simple denial that a document is fake is legally insufficient unless the facts are proved on record. The defendants first denied the agreement to sell and receipt, then admitted the signatures and thumb impression with a different explanation, a deviation from pleadings the appellate court overlooked. The appellate judgment was set aside, the trial court decree restored and the suit decreed. Ref: 2022 LHC 8645; Mst. Shamim Akhtar etc v. Muhammad Younas Khan etc (62-18, decided 13.09.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mst. Shamim Akhtar etc v. Muhammad Younas Khan etc (62-18, decided 13.09.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Institutional Autonomy in Recruitment: Overqualified Candidates
records.heading: A recruiting institution has autonomy, and an overqualified candidate has no automatic right to appointment
records.text: A recruiting institution has autonomy in its recruitment process. A person who is overqualified for a post is not necessarily entitled to appointment to a post that requires a lower qualification. Ref: Waqas Aslam & others v. Lahore Electric Supply Company Ltd, Lahore thr. its Legal Director & others (C.P. 4806/2019, decided 07.12.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Waqas Aslam & others v. Lahore Electric Supply Company Ltd, Lahore thr. its Legal Director & others (C.P. 4806/2019, decided 07.12.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 25: Equal Protection Does Not Extend to Illegality
records.heading: Article 25 gives no right to equal treatment in illegality
records.text: Art. 25 guarantees equal protection of law and cannot be invoked to perpetuate an unlawful act or claim equal treatment with illegalities. It applies where persons similarly placed are denied a benefit lawfully granted to others. The petitioners could not challenge the refusal of the permission sought on the ground of equal treatment. Ref: Muhammad Yasin v. The Director General Pakistan, Post Office, Islamabad & another (C.P. 688/2020, decided 09.01.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Yasin v. The Director General Pakistan, Post Office, Islamabad & another (C.P. 688/2020, decided 09.01.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Rights of Persons with Disabilities: Transfer of Incapacitated Employee
records.heading: Authority on transfer of an incapacitated employee and rights of persons with disabilities; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the rights of persons with disabilities and the transfer of an incapacitated employee during service to another post. The post gives the topic only and does not state the holding. Ref: Divisional Superintendent, Pakistan Railways, Multan & another v. Umar Daraz (C.P. 4618/2019, decided 28.11.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Divisional Superintendent, Pakistan Railways, Multan & another v. Umar Daraz (C.P. 4618/2019, decided 28.11.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Office of Attorney-General Cannot Be Left Vacant
records.heading: The office of Attorney-General is constitutional and cannot be left vacant or held in an acting capacity
records.text: The Attorney-General for Pakistan is a constitutional post and cannot be left vacant. The Constitution makes no mention of an acting Attorney-General. The Attorney-General and the Federal Law Secretary were directed to attend on the next date. Ref: Federation of Pakistan thr. M/o Defense v. Mrs. Ajmal Samia (decd) thr. her LRs & others (C.A. 1621/2017, decided 11.01.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan thr. M/o Defense v. Mrs. Ajmal Samia (decd) thr. her LRs & others (C.A. 1621/2017, decided 11.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Witnesses Disbelieved as to Co-Accused
records.heading: Witnesses disbelieved against one co-accused cannot be relied on against another without unimpeachable corroboration
records.text: Once prosecution witnesses are disbelieved with respect to one co-accused, they cannot be relied upon against another co-accused unless supported by independent and unimpeachable corroboration. The maxim falsus in uno falsus in omnibus was applied and the prosecution was held to have failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Failure to Prove Motive Set Up by Prosecution
records.heading: If the prosecution sets up a motive and fails to prove it, the prosecution bears the consequence
records.text: The prosecution need not establish motive in every murder case, but if it sets up a motive and fails to prove it, the prosecution and not the accused must suffer the consequence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: A Single Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single doubt suffices to entitle the accused to the benefit of doubt
records.text: It is better that guilty persons escape than that an innocent person suffer. To earn the benefit of doubt it is not necessary that many circumstances create uncertainty, and a single doubt entitles the accused to its benefit. The post lists supporting Supreme Court authorities. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 426(2-B) CrPC: Suspension of Sentence Pending Appeal
records.heading: Section 426(2-B) CrPC sets two conditions for suspension of sentence after special leave to appeal
records.text: S. 426(2-B) CrPC lays down two conditions for suspension of sentence: the High Court must be satisfied that the convict has been granted special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court, and it must think fit that the sentence or order appealed against be suspended. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 139.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 63A Interpretation: Defector's Vote (Urdu Report)
records.heading: Under Article 63A a defector's vote against party direction is not counted, per the majority
records.text: Urdu report of the majority judgment authored by Justice Munib Akhtar. A defector's vote cast against party direction is not counted, Parliament is to fix the period of disqualification, and the Constitution refers to the parliamentary party and not the party head. Objections to maintainability of the Presidential reference were rejected. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 42; Justice Munib Akhtar.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 195 and S. 476 CrPC: Complaint Requirement
records.heading: Section 195 CrPC requires a written complaint before cognizance, and section 476 applies only to clauses (b) and (c)
records.text: Section 195 CrPC is an exception to the general rule that any person may set the law in motion, and a court cannot take cognizance of the offences it lists without the written complaint it requires. Under s. 195(1)(a), offences under ss. 172 to 188 PPC need a written complaint of the public servant concerned or his superior. Section 476 CrPC applies only to s. 195(1)(b) and (c) offences. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 56.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Delay in Filing Private Complaint
records.heading: No period is prescribed for a private complaint, and delay alone is not fatal
records.text: No time period is prescribed by law for filing a private complaint, which is often filed as a last resort after approaching the police and the Ex-Officio Justice of Peace under s. 22-A(6) CrPC. Delay by itself is not fatal to evidence that is otherwise credible, and is examined on the facts of each case. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 93.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eye-Witnesses at Scene Doubtful
records.heading: Doubtful presence of interested eye-witnesses at the scene led to acquittal on appeal
records.text: The presence of the complainant and two injured witnesses was doubtful. Their houses were not near the scene, and the complainant was not a witness to the inquest or post-mortem reports and did not escort the body to hospital. The witnesses were interested and not trustworthy, their evidence was discarded and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Recording Eye-Witness Statements
records.heading: Unexplained delay of one or two days in recording eye-witness statements is fatal
records.text: An unexplained delay of one or two days in recording the statements of eye-witnesses is fatal, and their testimony cannot be safely relied upon. Here the police first met the witnesses two days after the occurrence and the prosecution was held to have failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvement by Complainant
records.heading: A dishonest improvement by the complainant over the FIR justifies discarding the statement
records.text: The FIR showed that the witnesses reached the scene after the firing and after the injuries had been sustained, whereas the private complaint stated that they were present and witnessed the occurrence. This was a dishonest improvement, the statement was discarded and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Medical Evidence
records.heading: An ocular account contradicted by medical evidence on the level of wounds defeats the prosecution
records.text: The prosecution alleged a downward shot from a balcony at a victim on the ground, but the medical officer stated that the entry and exit wounds were at the same level. This was a material contradiction between ocular and medical evidence, and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Weapon and Empties: Corroboratory Value
records.heading: Recovery of a weapon is corroboratory only and cannot sustain a capital conviction
records.text: Recovery of a pistol is purely corroboratory and cannot sustain a conviction on a capital charge. The Forensic Science Agency report showed that the crime empties were not fired from the recovered .30 bore pistol, so the recovery was inconsequential and unhelpful to the prosecution. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Suspension of Sentence: S. 9(c) CNSA, Leave Granted
records.heading: Sentence under section 9(c) CNSA suspended where leave was granted on custody and transmission of samples
records.text: Leave had been granted by the Supreme Court to reappraise evidence on safe custody and safe transmission of samples to the Chemical Examiner. The prosecution case might fall through, and the accused had been in jail since 2011. Sentences under s. 9(c) CNSA were suspended pending the Supreme Court appeal and the petition was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 139.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR Excludes False Implication
records.heading: A prompt FIR lodged on learning of the crime rules out false implication
records.text: The father of the deceased lodged the FIR within half an hour of learning of the robbery-murder from an eye-witness, although he was not an eye-witness himself. There was no delay, which by itself rules out false implication, and the prosecution proved its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 11.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion as Corroborative Circumstance
records.heading: Long absconsion without explanation indicates guilt when read with ocular and circumstantial evidence
records.text: The accused was declared a proclaimed offender under ss. 87 and 88 CrPC and remained a fugitive for over six years. He neither took the plea of ignorance, nor examined himself on oath, nor produced any witness to explain his whereabouts. This conduct indicated guilt when considered with the ocular and circumstantial evidence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 11.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Proved; Eye-Witness Testimony Unshaken
records.heading: Unshaken eye-witnesses, an immediate FIR and a proved motive sustain the prosecution case
records.text: The motive was an attempt to snatch the deceased's motorcycle. The eye-witnesses emerged unscathed from lengthy cross-examination and the defence could not establish their interestedness. The complainant directly charged the accused in an immediate FIR, and the prosecution proved its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 11.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eye-Witnesses on the Spot
records.heading: Eye-witnesses who adhered to their version at the spot inspection were present on the spot
records.text: Both eye-witnesses were present at the spot inspection and adhered to their version, so their presence was not doubtful. Their evidence could not be brushed aside on the bald allegation that they were labourers of the deceased. There is no rule that all persons under firearm attack must receive injuries. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 11.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Recovery of Crime Weapon
records.heading: Non-recovery of the crime weapon is immaterial where the accused absconded for over six years
records.text: The nominated accused absconded and was arrested after more than six years. Under those circumstances non-recovery of the crime weapon had no adverse impact on the prosecution case. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 11.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses on Public Thoroughfare
records.heading: Passers-by on a public thoroughfare are not mere chance witnesses if they explain their presence
records.text: A chance witness is one who is present at the scene incidentally. Where the crime occurs on a public thoroughfare or a place frequented by the public, passers-by cannot be rejected as mere chance witnesses, unless they give no satisfactory explanation of their presence or their testimony has an inherent weakness or contradiction. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 11.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Empties Not Sent to Ballistic Expert
records.heading: Non-sending of empties to a ballistic expert is immaterial where the accused absconded
records.text: Where no crime weapon was recovered because of the accused's own absconsion, non-sending of empties to the ballistic expert has no adverse impact. No hard and fast rule governs the weight of expert opinion, and lack of it matters little where the case is proved by reliable evidence. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 11.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Unbroken Chain
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form an unbroken chain, and a missing link benefits the accused
records.text: Circumstantial evidence must form a continuous chain with all circumstances linked, one end touching the dead body and the other the neck of the accused. If any link is missing, the benefit goes to the accused. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved in Murder of Minor Niece
records.heading: Absence of any proved motive for the murder of a minor niece left the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: The accused was the paternal uncle of the four-year-old deceased. No motive was stated in the FIR, the supplementary statement or the evidence, and no reason was shown why the accused would murder his niece. The prosecution could not prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Not Supporting Prosecution Case
records.heading: Medical evidence that did not support the alleged cause of death raised doubt about the prosecution case
records.text: The medical officer could not determine the cause of death and did not opine that death was by drowning as claimed. No seminal material was found on the swabs and no allegation of sexual offence was made. The prosecution case did not support the medical evidence, and doubt arose. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Extra-Judicial Confession: Reliability of Witnesses
records.heading: Extra-judicial confession witnesses who gave no time or place and delayed statements were unreliable
records.text: The witnesses to the extra-judicial confession gave no time or place, one recorded his s. 161 statement 18 days later and the other never did. Two witnesses made no attempt to apprehend the lone accused after hearing of a heinous crime. Their evidence was not worthy of reliance and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Pointation of Place by Accused Without Recovery
records.heading: Pointation of a place by the accused is of no avail where nothing was recovered
records.text: The complainant deposed that the accused pointed out the canal where he threw the girl, but nothing was recovered from the place and the body had already been recovered by the police. The evidence of pointation was of no avail to the prosecution. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: CCTV Footage: Recovery and Custody Doubtful
records.heading: Contradictions on recovery and custody of CCTV footage left the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: The shopkeeper could not say who checked and took the CCTV recording, and he denied joining the investigation, contrary to the Investigating Officer. The complainant never stated in court that he saw the recording. Glaring contradictions on recovery and safe custody of the CD left the prosecution unable to prove its case beyond doubt. Appeal allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: Proximity of Time and Place
records.heading: Last seen evidence requires close proximity of time and place to the recovery of the body
records.text: To believe last seen evidence there must be close proximity between the time and place of last seeing the deceased with the accused and the place and time of recovery of the body or occurrence. No such proximity or specific date and time was shown, so the last seen evidence was not reliable. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witnesses: Injuries Show Presence Only
records.heading: Injuries on a witness show presence at the scene but do not make his account true
records.text: The injured witnesses did not disclose the name or weapon of any accused to the medical officer, and the medico-legal certificate did not record a firearm injury. Injuries only indicate presence at the scene and do not make everything the injured witness says gospel truth. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 2.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Ingredients of Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: Section 406 PPC requires entrustment, dishonest misappropriation and use contrary to law or contract
records.text: The ingredients of criminal breach of trust under s. 406 PPC are entrustment, dishonest misappropriation or conversion by the person trusted, and dishonest use or disposal of property in violation of a direction of law or of a legal contract. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 149.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Breach of Agreement to Sell Is Not Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: Breach of an agreement to sell is not criminal breach of trust under section 406 PPC
records.text: Breach of a term of an agreement to sell does not attract s. 406 PPC. Payment of money under such an agreement is not entrustment, and a seller who takes consideration and fails to transfer the property commits no misappropriation. The remedy lies under the Specific Relief Act. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 149.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Reluctance to Interfere
records.heading: Cancellation of bail requires very strong and exceptional grounds as it curtails liberty before trial
records.text: Superior courts are ordinarily reluctant to interfere with an order granting bail. Very strong and exceptional grounds are required to disturb the concession, because cancellation curtails the liberty of an accused before completion of trial. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 149.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in PECA Offences: Retweeting, Ss. 9, 10, 11
records.heading: Bail allowed for retweeting under PECA sections 9, 10 and 11, which fall outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: Ss. 9, 10 and 11 PECA 2016 do not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC and prescribe fine as an alternative punishment. The State showed no material that the accused, who had retweeted, intended to glorify a proscribed organization, which could not be concluded without further inquiry. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 114.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Where Fine Is Alternative Punishment: Art. 9
records.heading: Where fine is an alternative punishment, bail considers the lesser penalty in light of Article 9
records.text: For offences carrying fine as an alternative punishment, the lesser punishment is considered when deciding bail under s. 497 CrPC. Time spent in prison where the trial court may impose only a fine would breach the right to liberty under Art. 9 of the Constitution, and the loss of liberty could not be recompensed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 114.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence: Arts. 9, 10-A and 14
records.heading: Presumption of innocence and Articles 9, 10-A and 14 protect liberty pending trial
records.text: An accused is deemed innocent until proven guilty. The right to liberty and dignity under Arts. 9 and 14 and the right to fair trial under Art. 10-A are protected, and there is no mechanism to restore liberty lost pending trial if the accused is found innocent. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 114.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Remand: Caution and Sessions Judge Supervision
records.heading: Police remand must be ordered with great caution, for the minimum time and reported to the Sessions Court
records.text: Remand to police custody must be ordered with great caution as it deprives a citizen of liberty. It may be granted for the minimum necessary time where custody is essential to the investigation, after examining the police diaries, and the order must be intimated to the supervising Sessions Court. The High Court set aside the Magistrate's order and remanded the matter to the Sessions Court. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 83.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Special Law Prevails Over General Law
records.heading: A special law prevails over a general law, which applies only where the special law is silent
records.text: A special provision overrides a general provision and a special enactment prevails over a general one. The procedure of the special law must be followed, and recourse to general law is permissible only where the special law is silent and the general provision is not inconsistent with it. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 38.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010: Object and Scope of S. 4
records.heading: The Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010 fills a gap in general law and courts must apply its intent
records.text: The Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010 meets a special need by giving subsequent conversion of crime proceeds a distinct meaning, filling a gap where general law was silent. Courts must apply the legislative intent in its natural way. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 38.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Interpretation: Unambiguous Statutory Language
records.heading: Unambiguous statutory language must be given its clear meaning without deviation
records.text: Where the language of a statute is unambiguous and its meaning clear, it must be given that clear meaning without deviation or departure. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 38.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of Second FIR under Anti-Money Laundering Act
records.heading: A second FIR under the Anti-Money Laundering Act was not quashed as no ground for quashing was shown
records.text: The petitioner sought quashing of a second FIR under s. 4 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010 on the same facts. An FIR may be quashed only where no offence appears on its face, there is no legal authority to register it, or it is mala fide and an abuse of process. The High Court declined to quash it and dismissed the petition. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 38.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Appeal by Legal Heirs Before Service Tribunal After Death
records.heading: Legal heirs cannot file a fresh Service Tribunal appeal after the civil servant's death
records.text: Only the civil servant himself may appeal to the Service Tribunal under s. 4 of the Service Tribunals Act 1973, and legal heirs cannot file a fresh appeal after his death. A pending appeal may be continued for monetary dues such as pension or gratuity. The widow's appeal was incompetent and leave was refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 46.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Conveyance Allowance of Teachers During Vacations
records.heading: Conveyance allowance of teachers cannot be stopped during vacations, as that is illegal and discriminatory
records.text: Conveyance allowance of teachers cannot be stopped during summer or winter vacations, and doing so is illegal and discriminatory. Under s. 23 of the Civil Servants Act 1973 the terms and conditions of service cannot be varied to the disadvantage of civil servants. Ref: 2023 SCMR 8.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Objections to Admissibility During Recording of Evidence
records.heading: An admissibility objection may be decided in the final judgment, but a stamp duty objection must be decided first
records.text: When an admissibility objection is raised during evidence, the trial court may note it, mark the document tentatively as an exhibit and decide the objection in the final judgment, excluding the evidence if the objection is sustained. An objection of deficient stamp duty must be decided before proceeding further. Ref: Justice K.T. Thomas; Justice R.P. Sethi; Justice B.N. Agarwal.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 46 QSO: Dying Declaration
records.heading: A dying declaration is admissible under Article 46 QSO but is weak evidence needing close scrutiny
records.text: A dying declaration is a statement by a homicide victim on the cause of his death, relevant and admissible under Art. 46 QSO, with no particular mode of recording prescribed. It is a weak type of evidence akin to that of an interested witness and requires close scrutiny. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 19.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: State Functionaries Must Act in Accordance with Law
records.heading: A state functionary must act in accordance with law and not on whim or caprice
records.text: A state functionary must act in accordance with law and follow the prescribed procedure, and not on whim or in a capricious and arbitrary manner, as nobody is above the law. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 31.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: S. 9(a)(vi) NAO: Misuse of Authority; Handwriting Expert Report
records.heading: Conviction under section 9(a)(vi) NAO upheld for misuse of authority in selling association plots
records.text: The President of an association and its record custodian were convicted for misusing authority in selling association plots. The handwriting expert confirmed the signatures were the accused's, the prosecution witnesses stood firm and no material contradictions were shown. The appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 31.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Confession Before Assistant Commissioner After FATA Merger
records.heading: Conviction on a confession before an Assistant Commissioner in former FATA set aside for de novo trial
records.text: The accused was convicted under s. 302(b) PPC on a confession recorded before an Assistant Commissioner exercising powers of Additional District Magistrate in the former FATA, and challenged that jurisdiction. The delay in appeal was condoned, the conviction and sentence were set aside and the case was remanded for de novo trial. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 65.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Sexual Harassment of Minor Girl, S. 354 PPC
records.heading: Bail refused to an accused nominated with a specific role in harassment of a minor girl
records.text: Bail was refused where the FIR was prompt, the accused was nominated with a specific role, the victim was medically examined the same day and the witnesses supported the allegations. There were sufficient grounds to connect him with offences falling within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 73.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Sedition Case: Anti-State Comments
records.heading: Bail is the rule where most sedition-related sections fall outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: The applicability of ss. 153-A, 131, 124-A, 120-A and 120-B PPC and ss. 6, 7 and 11 ATA required further probe into guilt. The remaining sections did not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so bail was the rule and refusal the exception. Bail allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 100.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 153-A PPC: Promoting Enmity Between Groups
records.heading: Section 153-A PPC addresses promoting enmity between groups and classes to prevent breaches of public tranquillity
records.text: S. 153-A PPC addresses promoting enmity between groups and classes. It is meant to prevent attacks on a community and conflict between classes through mutual abuse, and to prevent breaches of public tranquillity from enmity between religious, racial or language groups, castes or communities. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 100.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 131 PPC: Abetting Mutiny and Meaning of Mutiny
records.heading: Section 131 PPC punishes abetting mutiny, which implies collective insubordination in the armed forces
records.text: S. 131 PPC applies where an offender abets mutiny by, or attempts to seduce from duty, an officer, soldier, sailor or airman of the armed forces. Mutiny is not defined in the PPC and implies collective insubordination, revolt or refusal to obey lawful command in the military and naval services. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 100.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 124-A PPC: Sedition
records.heading: Section 124-A PPC punishes seditious disaffection aimed at overthrowing government by force or violence
records.text: S. 124-A PPC provides measures to protect the Government from seditious activities, namely actual or attempted disaffection by speech or advocacy aimed at overthrowing the Central or Provincial Government by force or violence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 100.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 11-X ATA: Civil Commotion
records.heading: Section 11-X(2) and (3) ATA apply to calls for action or shut down enforced by threats or force
records.text: Subsections (2) and (3) of s. 11-X ATA apply when an accused makes a call for action or shut down imposed through threats or force resulting in damage to property or injury to a person. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 100.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 7 ATA: Nexus with S. 6 Required
records.heading: Section 7 ATA applies only where the offence has a nexus with the objects in section 6 ATA
records.text: For s. 7 ATA to apply, the ingredients of the alleged offence must have a nexus with the object of the case as contemplated in s. 6 ATA. This is judged from the allegations in the crime report, the record and the surrounding circumstances. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 100.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Franchise Official to Verify CDR
records.heading: Under section 540 CrPC a franchise official may be summoned to verify a call data record copy
records.text: The accused sought verification of a photostat copy of the complainant's call data record to show he was elsewhere at the time of the incident. Verification would cause no prejudice to the prosecution, so the Trial Court was directed to summon an official of the relevant mobile company franchise. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 111.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Chemical Examiner on Weight Discrepancy
records.heading: Under section 540 CrPC the incumbent Chemical Examiner may be summoned on a weight discrepancy
records.text: Re-weighing of the narcotics showed a discrepancy, and the original Chemical Examiner had died. Whether the incumbent Chemical Examiner is examined as a prosecution or a court witness is immaterial, as his opinion on the discrepancy matters. The Trial Court was directed to summon him. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 111.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Free-Will Marriage Defence; Non-Joining of Alleged Husband
records.heading: Failure to join the alleged husband in investigation of a free-will marriage defence raised doubt
records.text: The accused relied on an affidavit of free will and a habeas corpus application by a man claiming to be the victim's husband. The police did not associate that man in the investigation and the complainant did not seek to join him as an accused or to falsify the marriage. This created doubt and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 121.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Contradictions in Three Statements of Victim
records.heading: Contradictions among the victim's three statements and the FIR date raised doubt and led to acquittal
records.text: The victim made three statements: before the High Court in a habeas corpus petition, to the police under s. 161 CrPC and at trial. An allegation made in the first statement was absent from the later ones, and the FIR date was also inconsistent with the stated dates. Doubt arose and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 121.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Shortcomings in Prosecution Evidence of Abduction and Rape
records.heading: Gaps in evidence of abduction and rape, including unsent clothes and no independent witness, led to acquittal
records.text: No independent witness was produced although the abduction was alleged on a highway in daylight. The victim's last worn clothes were collected but not sent for chemical analysis for semen, and the Investigator could not trace the other culprits. The prosecution failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt and the appeal was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 121.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 426 CrPC: Not a Hardened, Desperate or Dangerous Criminal
records.heading: A convict alleged to have conspired by calls from abroad was not a hardened, desperate or dangerous criminal
records.text: Where the convict was alleged to have made telephone calls from abroad and hatched a conspiracy to murder three persons, the Supreme Court observed that he was not a hardened, desperate or dangerous criminal for the purpose of suspension of sentence under s. 426 CrPC. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 132.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 426(1-A)(c) CrPC: Suspension of Sentence for Delay in Appeal
records.heading: A convict has a statutory right to suspension of sentence under section 426(1-A)(c) if he did not cause delay
records.text: S. 426 CrPC first asks whether delay in deciding the appeal was caused by the convict or someone on his behalf. If not, he has a statutory right to suspension of sentence under s. 426(1-A)(c), subject to the proviso. It may be refused if he is a hardened, desperate or dangerous criminal or is accused of terrorism punishable with death or life imprisonment. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 132.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Refused: Mala Fide Not Shown
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is refused unless the intended arrest is shown to be actuated by mala fide
records.text: Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC is not allowed unless the court is satisfied that the intended arrest is actuated by mala fide of the complainant party or police. The accused were nominated with a specific role of damaging a government watercourse, the witnesses supported the prosecution and no ill will was shown. Pre-arrest bail refused. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 161.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Order Observations Are Tentative
records.heading: Observations in a bail order under section 497(2) CrPC are tentative and do not bind the trial court
records.text: Observations made in a bail order under s. 497(2) CrPC are tentative and do not influence the trial court when deciding the case on merits. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 161.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Confiscation of Vehicle: Ss. 32 and 33 CNSA
records.heading: A vehicle used to carry narcotics is liable to confiscation where the appellant proved no ownership
records.text: Under the CNSA the narcotic, utensils and the vehicle or conveyance used to carry them are liable to confiscation. The appellant never claimed ownership of the vehicle during investigation or trial, relied only on a purchase slip while the vehicle was registered to another, and filed the appeal four months late. The appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 164.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor: Onus on Father to Prove Income
records.heading: The father must prove his income in a maintenance claim, failing which an adverse inference is drawn
records.text: A minor is not burdened with proving the financial status or payment capacity of his father to be entitled to maintenance. It is for the father to prove his financial sources, and if he fails or does not disclose his income, an adverse inference is drawn against him. Ref: 2023 CLC 161.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Past Maintenance: Six Years under Art. 120 Limitation Act
records.heading: A suit for past maintenance falls under Article 120 of the Limitation Act, giving six years
records.text: A suit for recovery of past maintenance falls under the residuary Art. 120 of the Limitation Act 1908, giving six years. Past maintenance may be allowed for more than three but not more than six years before the suit. Interim maintenance paid during the suit is adjusted against the amount fixed in the final decree. Ref: 2023 CLC 161.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift Must Be Proved Before Written Gift Deed
records.heading: An oral gift must be proved with full particulars before a written gift deed can stand
records.text: Where an oral gift is later reduced into a written deed, the beneficiary must first prove the oral gift, pleading its complete details in the plaint, including the day, venue, witnesses, time and consideration. Failing that, the written deed falls with it. The petitioners also did not prove offer, acceptance and delivery of possession, and the revision was dismissed. Ref: 2023 CLC 122.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Climate Justice: Arts. 3, 9 and 38
records.heading: Articles 3, 9 and 38 support climate justice and the right to life free from environmental hazards
records.text: Art. 3 requires the State to eliminate exploitation, which needs meaningful measures against environmental degradation and for climate justice. The right to life under Art. 9 includes life free from environmental hazards, and Art. 38 obliges the State to secure the people's well-being, so a climate crisis jeopardises Art. 9 rights. Ref: 2023 CLC 1.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Cheque with Part Payment, S. 56 NIA
records.heading: After part payment of a cheque, a summary suit on the full amount is not maintainable without endorsement
records.text: Where part of the cheque amount was paid before suit, the payee cannot present the cheque for the full sum without an endorsement under s. 56 Negotiable Instruments Act, nor sue under O. XXXVII CPC for the cheque amount. He must sue for the balance in an ordinary civil court. The appeal was allowed and the plaint returned under O. VII R. 10 CPC. Ref: 2023 CLC 193.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witnesses: Injuries Show Presence Only
records.heading: Injuries on a witness show presence at the scene but do not make his account true
records.text: The injured witnesses did not disclose the name or weapon of any accused to the medical officer, and the medico-legal certificate did not record a firearm injury. Injuries only indicate presence at the scene and do not make everything the injured witness says gospel truth. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 2.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Premature Transfers of Police Officers: Police Order 2002
records.heading: The Supreme Court directed implementation of the Police Order 2002 against premature transfers of police officers
records.text: The Supreme Court directed the Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governments to implement the Police Order 2002 and refrain from transferring police officers before the period prescribed by law. If an early transfer is unavoidable, reasons must be recorded, and no officer is to be removed without consulting a senior police officer. Notice was issued on applying these principles to Sindh and Balochistan. Ref: Rana Tahir Saleem v. Province of Punjab through Chief Secretary to the Government of Punjab Lahore and others (Const.P. 34/2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Ayesha A. Malik; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Rana Tahir Saleem v. Province of Punjab through Chief Secretary to the Government of Punjab Lahore and others (Const.P. 34/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Binding Effect of Accepted Special Oath
records.heading: A party who offers a special oath cannot resile once the other side accepts and takes it
records.text: Under s. 17(2) of the Family Courts Act 1964, ss. 8 to 11 of the Oaths Act 1873 apply before the Family Court. A party who offers to be bound by a special oath cannot resile once the other side accepts and takes the oath, as a binding agreement then exists. Leave to appeal refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 153.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Pre-Arrest Bail: Perversity
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail may be cancelled where the grant is perverse and contrary to judicial directions
records.text: Bail granted to an accused may be recalled on grounds including perversity of the order, meaning a decision contrary to judicial and statutory directions. Having examined the incriminating material collected by the police, the High Court set aside the order and cancelled the pre-arrest bail in a murder case. Ref: 2023 LHC 20; Haji Arshad Mehmood v. Farrukh Imtiaz Khokhar etc (Crl. Misc. 2759-B/22, decided 11.01.2023); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Haji Arshad Mehmood v. Farrukh Imtiaz Khokhar etc (Crl. Misc. 2759-B/22, decided 11.01.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Delay in FIR: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Unexplained delay of nine months in reporting a robbery made out a case of further inquiry
records.text: An unexplained delay of over nine months in reporting a robbery, with no recovery despite physical remand, and a bare allegation of criminal intimidation under s. 503 PPC, made out a case of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. The offence was also outside the prohibitory clause, and grant of bail is the rule. Ref: Muhammad Nawaz alias Karo v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.P. 1392/2022, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz alias Karo v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.P. 1392/2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Case of Two Versions
records.heading: Two versions of an incident, with a doubtful cross-version injury, make a case of further inquiry
records.text: Where the court is faced with two versions of the incident, including a cross-version lodged later with a doubtful injury attribution, the case falls within s. 497(2) CrPC as one of further inquiry. The Investigating Officer's opinion on the overt act is to be assessed after evidence is recorded. Ref: Muhammad Umar Waqas Barkat Ali v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 352-L/2022, decided 23.11.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Umar Waqas Barkat Ali v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 352-L/2022, decided 23.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Reliability of Ocular Account
records.heading: An FIR lodged two hours after a daylight occurrence at a distant police station is not delayed
records.text: An FIR lodged two hours after a daylight occurrence, at a police station 13.5 kilometres away, was not delayed. The ocular witnesses, though not locals, reasonably explained their presence, and the parties were known to each other. The life sentence substituted by the High Court was left undisturbed. Ref: Aman Ullah v. The State (Crl.A. 75-L/2021, decided 15.11.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Aman Ullah v. The State (Crl.A. 75-L/2021, decided 15.11.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Conviction Set Aside: No Link to Narcotics Consignment
records.heading: Conviction under section 9-C CNSA set aside where no knowledge of the narcotics consignment was shown
records.text: The prosecution failed to show that the appellant knew of the narcotics or facilitated booking the parcels with fake documents, and its witnesses did not support its case. Art. 150 QSO allows the court to permit the calling party to put cross-examination type questions at any stage. Conviction under s. 9-C CNSA set aside and appeal allowed.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Child Nutrition: Policy and Legislation Directions
records.heading: Court directed legislation and a national policy on child malnutrition in public interest litigation
records.text: The Food and School Education Departments have a mandate under the Second Schedule of the Punjab Government Rules of Business 2011 to frame policy and legislation on the issue. In public interest litigation the Court directed the respondents to legislate on children's fundamental rights, formulate a national policy addressing malnutrition, and ensure its implementation. Ref: 2022 LHC 8686; Zafar Khizer v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (W.P. 505/22, decided 11.10.2022); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Zafar Khizer v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (W.P. 505/22, decided 11.10.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Deposit of Balance Sale Consideration: Guidelines
records.heading: Courts must order deposit of balance sale consideration with no more than two opportunities
records.text: Under s. 24 of the Specific Relief Act 1877, civil courts are to order the vendee-plaintiff to deposit the balance sale consideration within a stipulated time, with no more than two opportunities, the last order stating that failure will lead to dismissal. In the case reported, the appellant was given a final chance of seven days and the appeal was allowed on that basis. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 372; Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed; Justice Shahid Karim.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness
records.heading: Specific performance requires the plaintiff to prove readiness and willingness and to tender the balance consideration
records.text: Specific performance under s. 24 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 is an equitable relief. The plaintiff must allege and prove readiness and willingness from the date of the agreement to the decree, and show capacity by offering or tendering the balance consideration to the vendor or in court, failing which adverse consequences follow. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 372.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Divorce Certificates for Christian Community
records.heading: The Provincial Government must frame rules for registering divorces of the Christian community
records.text: Registration of births, deaths, marriages and divorces is a local government function, now vested in the Union Council under s. 33(1)(j) PLGA 2022. No rules have been framed for registering divorces of the Christian community. The Court directed the Provincial Government to frame rules and, until then, NADRA to accommodate the community under its Registration Policy. Ref: 2022 LHC 8696; Mst Shumaila Sharif v. The Secretary etc (W.P. 66288/22, decided 16.12.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Mst Shumaila Sharif v. The Secretary etc (W.P. 66288/22, decided 16.12.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Trial Cannot Be Adjourned Sine Die
records.heading: A Sessions Court cannot adjourn a trial sine die because Chapter XXII-A has no such provision
records.text: Chapter XXII-A of the CrPC, which governs Sessions trials, has no provision for adjourning a trial for an indefinite period without a date. S. 249 CrPC permits this only to a First Class Magistrate and only in State cases, not complaint cases. A Sessions Court cannot therefore adjourn a trial sine die. Ref: 2022 LHC 8703; Nadeem Sultan etc v. Hamza Shamim etc (Crl. Revision 91-22, decided 22.07.2022); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Nadeem Sultan etc v. Hamza Shamim etc (Crl. Revision 91-22, decided 22.07.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness, Willingness and Deposit
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary, and readiness is judged from conduct before and after filing the suit
records.text: Specific performance under s. 24 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 is discretionary and must be exercised on settled principles. The plaintiff's readiness and willingness is judged from conduct before and after filing the suit. Where a deposit in court is ordered, the consequences of non-compliance should be stated clearly in advance. Ref: M/s DW Pakistan Private Limited Lahore v. Begum Anisa Fazl-i-Mahmood and others (C.P. 3989/2022, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: M/s DW Pakistan Private Limited Lahore v. Begum Anisa Fazl-i-Mahmood and others (C.P. 3989/2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Death Certificate: Copy and Best Evidence
records.heading: A death certificate not proved as an attested copy was excluded and an adverse inference followed
records.text: Production of a document and its proof are separate matters. A death certificate bearing signatures of the Union Council Secretary and Nazim was not an attested copy without a certificate of correctness, and its signatories were not examined. The copy was excluded, the custodian of the register was withheld, an adverse inference followed, and the revision was dismissed. Ref: 2017 YLR 2229.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Proactive Role of Trial Courts; Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Trial courts should act proactively, and prosecution silence on a material aspect gives the defence the benefit of doubt
records.text: Trial courts should adopt a proactive approach to dispensing justice and not merely rely on the material produced by the parties. The extract concludes that the prosecution's silence on a material aspect raised serious doubt about the veracity of its version, the benefit of which went to the defence. Ref: Zeeshan Iftikhar alias Shani v. The State, etc. (Crl. Appeal 14750 of 2022); Zaheer-ud-Din Babar v. Zeeshan Iftikhar etc. (Crl. Rev. 14749 of 2022).
records.title: Zeeshan Iftikhar alias Shani v. The State, etc. (Crl. Appeal 14750 of 2022); Zaheer-ud-Din Babar v. Zeeshan Iftikhar etc. (Crl. Rev. 14749 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ambiguous Order and Closure of Evidence
records.heading: Penal consequences such as closure of evidence should not follow non-compliance with an ambiguous order
records.text: A court must pass orders in clear terms. Where an earlier order is ambiguous, a later order imposing penal consequences for non-compliance, such as closure of evidence, should not be passed. Ref: 2023 LHC 36; Manzoor Ahmad etc v. Khalid Hassan Khan etc. (R.F.A. 7238/22, decided 10.01.2023); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Manzoor Ahmad etc v. Khalid Hassan Khan etc. (R.F.A. 7238/22, decided 10.01.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Vice Chancellor: No Vested Right to Extension
records.heading: A Vice Chancellor who has completed his tenure has no vested right to extension
records.text: Under s. 12 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Universities Act 2012, a Vice Chancellor who has completed his tenure cannot claim extension as a vested right if the competent authority is not interested in extending it for a legitimate reason. Ref: 2023 SCMR 162.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Wrong Symbol on Ballot Papers: Re-Poll
records.heading: The Election Commission may order a re-poll for the whole constituency after a wrong symbol was printed
records.text: Under s. 9(1) of the Elections Act 2017, the Election Commission printed a tap instead of the allotted hand pump symbol in a local government election. The two are easily distinguishable, and given the close result the poll was materially affected. The Commission was within its jurisdiction to order a re-poll for the whole constituency. Ref: 2023 SCMR 179.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Presumption of Regularity of Judicial Acts
records.heading: Judicial and official acts are presumed regular, although the presumption is rebuttable
records.text: The court may presume that judicial and official acts were regularly performed, although the presumption is rebuttable. The appellant had not objected when the order was dictated and had not sought review to assert that consent was not given. Ref: 2023 CLC 161.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: s. 489-F: Cancellation of Pre-Arrest Bail Refused
records.heading: Dishonesty under section 489-F PPC needs evidence of lack of commercial integrity, assessed at trial
records.text: Dishonesty under s. 489-F PPC needs evidence of absence of commercial integrity, which can be assessed at trial. The accused pleaded that the complainant had not performed his side of a share purchase agreement. The petition to cancel pre-arrest bail was dismissed and leave refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Perverse Order
records.heading: Bail is cancelled where the order is perverse on its face or disregards a principle of bail law
records.text: The Supreme Court ordinarily cancels bail on two grounds: the order is perverse on its face, or it was made in clear disregard of a principle of the law of bail. A perverse order is one passed against the weight of the material, ignoring it, without applying the relevant criteria, or without reasons. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Abscondence Alone Does Not Bar Bail
records.heading: Abscondence by itself is not sufficient to withhold bail from an accused otherwise entitled to it
records.text: Mere abscondence by itself is not sufficient to withhold the concession of bail when the accused otherwise becomes entitled to it. Ref: 2023 SCMR 172.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Elopement Case: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Undisclosed sources of information in the FIR and late witnesses made an elopement case one of further inquiry
records.text: The FIR did not disclose the complainant's source of information about the accused's involvement, the two witnesses examined under s. 161 CrPC were late and also did not disclose their source, and the wife was not arrested. This brought the case within further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Leave was converted into appeal and bail granted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 172.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Disbelieved Recovery and Sentence of Life Imprisonment
