records.heading: Where recovery is disbelieved as inconsequential, life imprisonment is justified and no further leniency is due
records.text: The courts below rightly disbelieved the recovery of a churri because no independent witness joined and the blood stained weapon was not sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory. With the recovery inconsequential, life imprisonment was justified and no further leniency was due. Leave refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 117.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Relationship of Witnesses with Deceased
records.heading: Mere relationship of ocular witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony
records.text: Mere relationship of the ocular witnesses with the deceased is not a ground to discard their testimony. Ref: 2023 SCMR 117.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Evidence
records.heading: Minor discrepancies on trivial matters are ignored where the evidence as a whole inspires confidence
records.text: Courts should ignore minor discrepancies on trivial matters where the material aspects of the evidence have a ring of truth. The test is whether the evidence read as a whole inspires confidence. A discrepancy going to the root of the matter may be used by the defence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 117.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Quota for Minorities and Persons with Disabilities
records.heading: The Supreme Court upheld the quota for minorities and persons with disabilities in grade 17 posts
records.text: The Supreme Court upheld the Lahore High Court and retained the quota for minorities and persons with disabilities in grade 17 posts in Punjab. The Constitution makes both groups equal citizens and gives them extra care and protection. The Public Service Commission was told not to use the word disabled for special persons. Ref: Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Seniority: Retrospective Regularisation Amendment
records.heading: A retrospective deeming clause cannot override vested rights of Public Service Commission selectees beyond the parent Act
records.text: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Ad hoc Appointments) (Amendment) Act 2014 sought to give the appellants a retrospective advantage at the expense of vested rights of respondents who were selected by the Public Service Commission. Citing Art. 25(1) of the Constitution, the Court held the deeming clause went beyond the 1994 Act and was valid only to the extent it conformed to it. Ref: 2023 SCMR 174.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Redemption of Mortgage: Second Application Barred
records.heading: A second redemption application is barred where no suit was filed after the first was rejected
records.text: Under the Punjab Redemption and Restitution of Mortgaged Lands Act 1964, the Board of Revenue cannot extend limitation to revive time barred claims. A second application under s. 3 was barred by s. 8, as no suit for redemption was filed after the first application was rejected in 1972. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 124.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reappraisal of Evidence: Qatl-i-Amd Conviction Upheld
records.heading: A report to the police about two hours after a daylight occurrence is without inordinate delay
records.text: A report to the police about two hours after a daylight occurrence, at a station 4.5 kilometres away, was without inordinate delay. The witnesses were consistent, explained their presence and were corroborated by medical evidence. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was maintained and leave refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 117.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Single Witness
records.heading: A murder conviction can rest on a single reliable witness, as evidence is weighed and not counted
records.text: A murder conviction can rest on the testimony of a single witness whom the court finds reliable. Evidence is judged by quality and not quantity, and it is the statement and not the person giving it that is assessed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 117.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy and confidence inspiring ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence
records.text: Where the ocular evidence is trustworthy and confidence inspiring, it is given preference over medical evidence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 117.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Determination of Compensation under s. 23(1)
records.heading: Compensation under section 23(1) reflects present and near-future beneficial use, and revenue entries are not conclusive
records.text: In assessing compensation under s. 23(1) of the Land Acquisition Act 1894, the court considers both present use and any more beneficial use reasonably available in the near future, and not a use in the distant future. Compensation is the price a willing vendor may expect from a willing purchaser, and revenue entries on land nature are not conclusive. Ref: 2023 SCMR 102.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Enhancement of Compensation: Commercial Land Evidence
records.heading: Unchallenged Patwari, valuer and Local Commission evidence established commercial land and enhanced compensation
records.text: Unchallenged testimony of the Patwari, a professional evaluator's evidence and the Local Commission's report established the land as commercial. The appeal was partly allowed and compensation enhanced from Rs.1200 to Rs.40,000 per marla, with statutory benefits including compulsory acquisition charges and compound interest. Ref: 2023 SCMR 102.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Local Commission under O. XXVI R. 9 CPC
records.heading: Courts should use suo motu power under O. XXVI R. 9 CPC to obtain a Commission report on land value
records.text: As Art. 24 of the Constitution gives the landowner a right to fair compensation, the court is not limited to the parties' evidence and should use its suo motu power under O. XXVI R. 9 CPC to obtain a Commission's report on the location, type, use and market value of the land. Ref: 2023 SCMR 102.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Special Costs for Frivolous Litigation
records.heading: Special costs may be imposed on frivolous litigation that wastes court time
records.text: Under O. XXVIII R. A(3) of the Supreme Court Rules 1980, costs may be imposed on frivolous litigation, which wastes court time and offends Arts. 9 and 37(d) of the Constitution. The CDA's challenge, based on its own repeated transfers, was frivolous and special costs of Rs.500,000 were imposed. Leave refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 61.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Sub-Campuses of Universities Outside Charter Territory
records.heading: The Supreme Court endorsed the HEC in treating sub-campuses outside a university's charter territory as illegal
records.text: The HEC regarded sub-campuses set up outside the territory of a university's charter as illegal. The Supreme Court endorsed all lawful acts of the HEC to maintain uniform education standards and directed the Federal and Provincial Governments to cooperate fully in enforcing them. Ref: 2023 SCMR 58.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: s. 42: Suit Challenging Paternity of Child
records.heading: A plaintiff seeking a negative declaration on a child's paternity lacks standing under section 42
records.text: A plaintiff who seeks a negative declaration that a child is not another's daughter does not assert his own legal character under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act 1877, and so lacks standing. The suit was filed only after the father's death and the mother testified to paternity. Petition for leave dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 6.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction Not Barred by Suit for Specific Performance
records.heading: An agreement to sell or a suit for specific performance does not bar eviction under the Rented Premises Act
records.text: Under the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009, an agreement to sell or a suit for specific performance does not bar eviction under s. 15. Title cannot be decided in eviction proceedings, and an unwritten tenancy presumes the owner is landlord and the occupier tenant. The constitutional petitions were dismissed. Ref: 2023 CLC 86.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Closure of Evidence under Punjab Rented Premises Act
records.heading: The Punjab Rented Premises Act is a special law prevailing over the CPC, with two evidence opportunities per side
records.text: The Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 is a special law requiring conclusion within four months, and under ss. 25 and 27 it prevails over the CPC. Only two opportunities are to be given to each side to adduce evidence. Ref: 2023 CLC 86.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secondary Evidence: Uncertified Copy of Revenue Order
records.heading: An uncertified copy of a revenue order is inadmissible as secondary evidence without meeting Articles 76 and 77 QSO
records.text: Respondents relied on an uncertified copy of a Tehsildar's order without producing the original. Arts. 76 and 77 QSO require the admissibility test to be met before secondary evidence, and repeated reference to the order in other orders does not excuse that. Respondents withheld best evidence. Revision allowed and case remanded to the appellate court. Ref: 2023 CLC 138.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: NAB References: Transfer Is Not Acquittal
records.heading: Transfer of NAB references to the competent courts is not acquittal or discharge
records.text: Under s. 4(3) of the 1999 Ordinance, pending matters must be transferred to the competent courts and the law does not envisage return of references to NAB. Transfer is not acquittal or discharge. Where new facts emerge, NAB may seek the Accountability Court's permission to file supplementary references. Ref: Adam Amin Chaudhry & another v. National Accountability Bureau (NAB) Islamabad through its Chairman & 29 others (W.P. 3787-2022, decided 19.01.2023); Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir.
records.title: Adam Amin Chaudhry & another v. National Accountability Bureau (NAB) Islamabad through its Chairman & 29 others (W.P. 3787-2022, decided 19.01.2023)

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Retrenched Workmen: Dues and Re-employment Preference
records.heading: Retrenched workmen are entitled to dues and to preference in re-employment after completion of BMR
records.text: The impugned Labour Court order protected the interests of retired and retrenched employees by entitling them to dues and benefits and compensation under the Payment of Wages Act for delay. After completion of BMR, no new workmen were to be inducted without preference to retrenched workmen, with contempt proceedings before the Labour Court for breach. Ref: All Workmen Employed by Dandot Cement Company Pvt. Ltd v. M/s. Dandot Cement Company Pvt. Ltd. and others (Writ Petition No.2162 of 2022).
records.title: All Workmen Employed by Dandot Cement Company Pvt. Ltd v. M/s. Dandot Cement Company Pvt. Ltd. and others (Writ Petition No.2162 of 2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Exemption on Import of Hybrid Electric Vehicles
records.heading: Exemption clauses on import of Hybrid Electric Vehicles are interpreted in favour of the assessee
records.text: Concerns exemption from customs duty, sales tax and withholding tax on import of Hybrid Electric Vehicles. An exemption clause is interpreted in favour of the assessee. The judgment also discusses the Pakistan Climate Change Act 2017 and the Pakistan Environmental Protection Act 1997. Ref: Collector of Customs, Model Customs Collectorate, Peshawar v. Wasifullah and another (C.P. 389/2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Collector of Customs, Model Customs Collectorate, Peshawar v. Wasifullah and another (C.P. 389/2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Tax on Foreign Assets: Finance Act 2022
records.heading: Tax on foreign assets under section 8(2)(b) of the Finance Act 2022 is a lawful exercise of legislative power
records.text: Tax on foreign assets imposed by s. 8(2)(b) of the Finance Act 2022 is a lawful exercise of Parliament's legislative power under Entry 50 of the Federal Legislative List. Ref: 2022 LHC 8733; Zaka Uddin Malik v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Tax Writ 50314/22, decided 22.12.2022); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Zaka Uddin Malik v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Tax Writ 50314/22, decided 22.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: s. 337-G PPC Exhaustive
records.heading: Section 337-G PPC is exhaustive on imprisonment, so the added sections were inapt and bail was confirmed
records.text: S. 337-G PPC is exhaustive on imprisonment, so adding ss. 334, 336, 337-F(i) and 337-F(v) PPC to the FIR was inapt. The offence is bailable under Schedule II CrPC, and ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2023 MLD 107.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Suspension of Sentence of Juvenile Pending Appeal
records.heading: Section 426 CrPC governs suspension of a juvenile's sentence pending appeal, and juvenility does not alter the two year period
records.text: The Juvenile Justice System Act 2018 has no provision for suspending the sentence of a convicted juvenile, so s. 426 CrPC applies through s. 18. The two year period under s. 426(1-A)(c) CrPC is unchanged by juvenility, and the bail ground for juveniles during trial does not extend after conviction. Ref: 2023 MLD 60.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: No Jurisdiction over Inheritance Claim
records.heading: The Family Court has no jurisdiction over a claim to inheritance or tarka
records.text: The Schedule to the Family Courts Act 1964 does not empower the Family Court to adjudicate a claim to inheritance or tarka. A sister suing the widower for the deceased's dowry articles had no locus standi before the Family Court and must approach the competent Civil Court. Ref: 2023 MLD 92.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused of Unsound Mind: Voir Dire and Trial
records.heading: Section 465 CrPC requires a trial within a trial on unsoundness of mind before the case proceeds
records.text: Fair trial under Art. 10-A requires the accused's mental presence. S. 465 CrPC requires the court first to try the fact of unsoundness through a trial within a trial, and the case cannot proceed until the accused is declared fit. If bail is not granted under s. 466(1), safe custody is ordered under s. 466(2). Ref: 2023 LHC 76; Muhammad Hanif v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 173-22, decided 10.01.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 173-22, decided 10.01.2023)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Quashing of FIR under s. 489-F PPC
records.heading: FIRs under section 489-F PPC on dishonoured cheques considered for quashing where issuance and dishonour were undenied
records.text: Concerns quashing of FIRs under s. 489-F PPC arising from dishonoured post-dated cheques given for business obligations. The extract records that issuance and dishonour were not denied and that earlier FIRs on other cheques were compromised after payment. Ref: 2019 MLD 636.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Petition to Supreme Court Without Filing ICA
records.heading: A petition directly to the Supreme Court is ordinarily not maintainable where an intra court appeal lies
records.text: Where an ICA lies to the High Court under s. 3 of the Law Reforms Ordinance, a petition directly to the Supreme Court is ordinarily not maintainable. This is a rule of practice and does not oust jurisdiction. Exceptions include questions of great public importance, constitutional interpretation, validity of provincial statutes, and fundamental rights, where the objection is raised belatedly. Ref: Federal Board of Revenue thr. its Chairman, Islamabad & others v. M/s Hub Power Company Ltd & others (C.P. 3739/2019, decided 20.01.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Federal Board of Revenue thr. its Chairman, Islamabad & others v. M/s Hub Power Company Ltd & others (C.P. 3739/2019, decided 20.01.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Restoration of Civil Revision: Art. 181
records.heading: An application to restore a civil revision is governed by three years under Article 181
records.text: The limitation period for an application for restoration of a civil revision is three years under Art. 181 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act 1908. Ref: Mst. Jameela Bibi (decd) through LRs v. Mst. Fatima Bibi (decd) through LRs (C.P. 3125/2020, decided 19.01.2023).
records.title: Mst. Jameela Bibi (decd) through LRs v. Mst. Fatima Bibi (decd) through LRs (C.P. 3125/2020, decided 19.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: A Single Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single doubt suffices, and heinousness of an unproved offence is no ground to punish
records.text: Heinousness of an offence that is not proved to the hilt is no ground to punish. It is better that many guilty persons are let off than one innocent suffers. A single doubt suffices, and its benefit goes to the accused. Ref: Amir Muhammad Khan v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 297 of 2020, decided 18.01.2023).
records.title: Amir Muhammad Khan v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 297 of 2020, decided 18.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Firearm Injuries on Head: Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Injuries on different parts of the head do not contradict ocular and medical evidence
records.text: The head is not a stationary part of the body, and a victim may turn it to protect himself. Injuries on different parts of the head therefore do not show a contradiction between the ocular and medical evidence. Ref: 2011 SCMR 429.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Legitimate Expectation and Concealment of Criminal Case
records.heading: Concealing a criminal case when seeking appointment defeats any legitimate expectation of joining duty
records.text: Legitimate expectation arises from a promise, assurance, practice or policy of a public authority, and it is for the court to decide whether it is legitimate. As the respondent had concealed his involvement in a criminal case when seeking appointment under the son quota, the Bank was within its domain in not allowing him to join duty. Ref: President National Bank of Pakistan and others v. Waqas Ahmed Khan (Civil Appeal No. 441 of 2021, decided 16.01.2023).
records.title: President National Bank of Pakistan and others v. Waqas Ahmed Khan (Civil Appeal No. 441 of 2021, decided 16.01.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Guidelines for Magistrates on Remand
records.heading: Magistrates must grant remand sparingly with recorded reasons under the Lahore High Court Rules
records.text: The Lahore High Court Rules on remand are reproduced for Magistrates. In the first 15 days judicial custody may be liberal, but police custody only on strong exceptional grounds for the shortest period. Reasons must be recorded, and after 15 days the police must submit a challan or the accused is released on bail. Remand is not to be granted mechanically. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 293.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Writ Against Interim Order of Family Court
records.heading: Examines whether a writ lies against an interim order of the Family Court given section 5 limits
records.text: Examines whether a writ petition lies against an interim order of a Family Court, noting that its jurisdiction under s. 5 of the Family Courts Act 1964 is confined to matters in Part I of the Schedule. The extract refers to the Supreme Court judgment in Moon Enterprises CNG Station v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines (2020 SCMR 300). Ref: Arshad Mehmood v. Judge Family Court and another (Writ Petition No. 11512 of 2019, decided 24.01.2023).
records.title: Arshad Mehmood v. Judge Family Court and another (Writ Petition No. 11512 of 2019, decided 24.01.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 476 CrPC Discretion and Costs for Frivolous Litigation
records.heading: The power under section 476 CrPC is discretionary, and costs may curb frivolous litigation
records.text: The power under s. 476 CrPC to take cognizance of offences relating to proceedings before the court is discretionary and must be exercised judiciously, with prime regard to whether it is expedient in the interests of justice. The Court also stressed imposing costs to curb frivolous and vexatious litigation. Ref: Qazi Naveed ul Islam v. District Judge, Gujrat and others (C.P. 3127/2020, decided 12.01.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Qazi Naveed ul Islam v. District Judge, Gujrat and others (C.P. 3127/2020, decided 12.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Naqeebullah Mehsud Case: Acquittal of Rao Anwar
records.heading: Judgment acquitting all accused in the Naqeebullah Mehsud murder case; the post states no reasoning
records.text: Judgment acquitting SSP Rao Anwar and all other accused in the Naqeebullah Mehsud murder case. The post only shares the judgment file and states no reasoning. Ref: The State v. Rao Anwar Ahmed Khan etc..
records.title: The State v. Rao Anwar Ahmed Khan etc.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Comparison of Signatures and Thumb Impressions by Expert
records.heading: Courts should take a liberal view of requests for expert comparison of signatures and thumb impressions
records.text: Courts should take a liberal view of requests for comparison of signatures or thumb impressions, as no express provision allows refusal and the expert report supplements the evidence. Refusal on the ground that it would delay proceedings was misconceived, and the courts below failed to exercise their jurisdiction. Ref: Aashiq Hussain v. Fida Hussain & others (Writ Petition No.6404 of 2020).
records.title: Aashiq Hussain v. Fida Hussain & others (Writ Petition No.6404 of 2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 152 CPC: Correction of Clerical Mistakes
records.heading: Section 152 CPC allows correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes and accidental slips at any time
records.text: Under s. 152 CPC the court may at any time correct clerical or arithmetical mistakes in a judgment, decree or order, and also errors from an accidental slip or omission. The two limbs are disjunctive. Technicalities should not defeat substantial justice. Ref: Shabbir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Multan, etc. (Writ Petition No.3227 of 2022, decided 19.01.2023).
records.title: Shabbir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Multan, etc. (Writ Petition No.3227 of 2022, decided 19.01.2023)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Land Acquisition: National Highway Authority
records.heading: Land acquisition case involving the National Highway Authority; the post states no holding
records.text: Authority on land acquisition. The post gives only the case title, number and judge, and states no holding. Ref: National Highway Authority v. Mazhar Siddique and others (C.P. 819/2017, decided 03.01.2023); Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan.
records.title: National Highway Authority v. Mazhar Siddique and others (C.P. 819/2017, decided 03.01.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Declaration of Assets in Local Government Nomination Papers
records.heading: A returning officer may allow a substantial defect in asset declaration to be remedied under Rule 18(3)
records.text: A candidate must declare assets in the nomination papers under the Sindh Local Government Act 2013, and again after success as required by s. 23. A sustained objection to the declaration may lead the Returning Officer to reject nomination, but he has discretion to allow a substantial defect to be remedied under Rule 18(3) proviso (ii) of the Sindh Local Councils (Election) Rules 2015. Ref: 2023 SCMR 206.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption Limitation: Registered Sale Deed and s. 31
records.heading: Pre-emption limitation on a registered sale deed runs four months from registration
records.text: Where the sale is by registered deed, limitation for a pre-emption suit is four months from registration. S. 31 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act 1991 does not control limitation, as ss. 30 and 31 are independent. The suit was barred by time. Ref: 2023 CLC 201.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: s. 30 Pre-emption Act: Clauses Independent
records.heading: Section 30 of the Pre-emption Act gives four independent events, and clause (d) is residual
records.text: S. 30 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act 1991 gives four independent events for computing limitation. Clause (d) is a residual provision that applies only if none of clauses (a), (b) and (c) is attracted. Ref: 2023 CLC 201.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Execution: Decree Holder Bank Purchasing Attached Property
records.heading: A decree holder bank may purchase attached property at auction with the bid set off against the decree
records.text: The decree holder Bank became successful bidder after higher bidders failed to deposit 25 percent. The High Court approved the auction, found no irregularity, treated permission as impliedly dispensing with the O. XXI R. 84(2) CPC deposit, and set off the bid money against the decree, subject to the Bank's undertaking to pay any other bank holding a charge. Ref: 2023 CLD 154.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Alteration, Novation and Rescission of Contract
records.heading: Novation substitutes a new contract, while alteration modifies the original and is read into it
records.text: Novation wholly substitutes a new contract, while alteration modifies the original and is read into it, original terms surviving unless inconsistent. A modified contract with independent force rescinds the original. After the compromise agreement the bank's depositor was entitled to the agreed 15 percent profit, and the fresh suit was not hit by O. XXIII R. 1(3) CPC. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 61, 2023 CLD 14.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Reciprocal Promises: Compensation under s. 54
records.heading: A promisor who fails to perform reciprocal promises cannot claim specific performance and owes compensation under section 54
records.text: Where a contract consists of reciprocal promises and one cannot be performed, a promisor who fails to perform the other cannot claim specific performance and must pay compensation for the resulting loss under s. 54 of the Contract Act 1872. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 61, 2023 CLD 14.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Signed Document Binding over Prior Correspondence
records.heading: A signed document of agreed terms binds the parties over earlier correspondence
records.text: When the parties sign a document containing agreed terms, the preceding invitation to treat or correspondence has no precedence and the signed document binds the parties. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 61, 2023 CLD 14.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Late Filing of List of Witnesses: Decide on Merits
records.heading: Late filing of a list of witnesses was cured by one further opportunity on costs
records.text: In a suit for specific performance of an oral agreement to sell, the defendant missed the deadline for the list of witnesses. The High Court allowed the petition and directed the Trial Court to grant one opportunity on costs, failing which it should proceed in accordance with law. Ref: 2023 YLR 37.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Identification Parade
records.heading: Related eye-witnesses who gave no justification for their presence were chance witnesses, and the identification parade failed
records.text: Related eye-witnesses who gave no justification for their presence, came back home, stayed silent for a month and were absent from inquest and post-mortem records were chance witnesses. Their evidence, and the identification parade resting on it, lacked value. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2023 YLR 24.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved
records.heading: A motive that shifted between versions without evidence was discarded
records.text: The prosecution shifted from a motive of threatening calls to one of illicit relations, and produced no oral or documentary evidence for either. Silence on the details of the motive led to it being discarded. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2023 YLR 24.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Defective Investigation: Threatening Calls
records.heading: Defective investigation of threatening call SIMs contributed to failure to prove the case
records.text: The police arrested the owner of one SIM used for threatening calls but did not have him identified by the eye-witnesses, and the owner of the other SIM was never traced. This defective investigation contributed to the failure to prove the case beyond doubt. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2023 YLR 24.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Pistol on Pointation Inconsequential
records.heading: Recovery of a pistol on pointation was inconsequential where witnesses were disbelieved
records.text: Recovery witnesses were closely related to the deceased and already disbelieved, and the crime empty and pistol were sent together to the Forensic Science Agency. The recovery was inconsequential and the positive forensic report lost significance. Ref: 2023 YLR 24.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light Not Proved
records.heading: Without proof of a source of light in a night occurrence, availability of light cannot be presumed
records.text: No source of light was described in the FIR or rough site plan, and the bulb shown in the scaled site plan was not taken into possession by the Investigating Officer. Availability of light could not be presumed. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2023 YLR 24.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: Presence at Spot Not Justified
records.heading: A complainant who lived far from the scene and gave no explanation was an interested chance witness
records.text: The complainant lived 2 to 2.5 kilometres from the scene, gave no abuttals and said the FIR was lodged on the next day, so she was an interested chance witness. The co-eye-witness was also disbelieved. Prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Withholding Best Evidence: Art. 129(g) QSO
records.heading: Withholding natural witnesses in a populated area justifies an adverse inference under Article 129(g) QSO
records.text: The incident occurred in a populated commercial area, yet natural witnesses such as the daughter-in-law, the sweet shop owner and hotel workers were not produced. This was withholding of best evidence, justifying an adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO. Appeal against convictions allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: An ocular account not in line with medical evidence leaves the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: The witnesses described a firearm injury below the chest which the Medical Officer did not record, and the left flank injury was an exit wound. The ocular account was not in line with the medical evidence, so the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR: Claim of Promptitude Rejected
records.heading: A prompt FIR was rejected as registered after deliberation by an unexplained informant
records.text: Although the FIR was lodged within about one and a half hours, the record showed it was written by a school teacher from another chak, the informant was unknown and no reason explained his presence. The FIR was found to have been registered after deliberation, as the eye-witnesses were not present. Appeal against convictions allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Joint Role of Firing Attributed to Two Assailants
records.heading: A joint firing role without showing whose shot hit which part makes the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: A joint firing role was attributed to the accused and an absconding co-accused, but the record did not show which assailant's shot hit which part of the deceased. This made the prosecution case highly doubtful. Appeal against convictions allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of Over 13 Hours in Post-Mortem
records.heading: Unexplained post-mortem delay of over 13 hours casts serious doubt on the prosecution story
records.text: Post-mortem was conducted after a delay of 13 hours and 45 minutes with no explanation. Such delay typically arises from consultation and inquiry about the culprits in unwitnessed cases and cast serious doubt on the prosecution story. Appeal against convictions allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light Not Established
records.heading: Without an established source of light the night witnesses could not have identified the culprits
records.text: The occurrence was at night and the Investigating Officer did not take into possession any source of light, nor did the witnesses produce it. Without an established light source the witnesses could not have identified the culprits. Appeal against convictions allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved: Silence on Details
records.heading: A motive not reported and silent on details was rightly disbelieved by the Trial Court
records.text: No direct motive was attributed to the accused, and the earlier quarrel was never reported to the police. Silence on the details of the motive led the Trial Court to rightly disbelieve it. Appeal against convictions allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Police Opinion of Innocence in Successive Investigations
records.heading: Police opinion of innocence may be considered where successive investigations rest on cogent material
records.text: The police view is not binding on the court but may be considered if based on cogent material. Two investigations found the accused absent from the scene, and independent local witnesses supported him. The police opinion was reliable. Appeal against convictions allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Dishonest improvements by eye-witnesses make their statements doubtful and unreliable
records.text: The complainant and eye-witness improved on their earlier accounts by adding hits on the right shoulder and other body parts. This deliberate and dishonest improvement made their statements doubtful and unreliable. Appeal against convictions allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 12(2) CPC: Issues and Evidence Not Mandatory
records.heading: Framing issues and recording evidence is not mandatory in deciding an application under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: It is not mandatory to frame issues and record evidence to decide an application under s. 12(2) CPC. The court regulates its procedure according to the nature of the allegations, since mandatory issues would defeat the object of avoiding protracted litigation. Ref: 2023 YLR 200.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Suit After 18 Years; Unproved Agreement
records.heading: A specific performance suit after 18 years on an unproved agreement with best evidence withheld fails
records.text: The plaint omitted the date of the alleged 1983 agreement and persons present, the suit was filed in September 2001, possession was disputed, and a co-purchaser was not examined, which was withholding of best evidence. The revision petition was allowed. Ref: 2023 YLR 176.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Executory Agreement Does Not Confer Ownership
records.heading: An executory agreement confers no ownership and must first be proved
records.text: Ownership cannot be claimed on the basis of an executory agreement whose enforcement is sought. The agreement must first be proved before any rights under it are claimed. Art. 79 QSO is cited. Ref: 2023 YLR 176.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit for Damages: Malicious Civil Prosecution
records.heading: A suit for damages for malicious civil prosecution is maintainable where earlier proceedings lacked probable cause
records.text: A suit for damages for malicious civil litigation is maintainable where the earlier civil proceedings against the plaintiff failed and were instituted without probable cause. The application under O. VII R. 11 CPC was rightly dismissed. Revision dismissed, with a direction to the Trial Court to decide the suit expeditiously on merits. Ref: 2023 MLD 191.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A plaint may be rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC only on the grounds listed
records.text: A plaint may be rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC only for want of jurisdiction, lack of cause of action, bar by law or non-payment of court fee. Where the assertions require evidence, the plaint cannot be summarily rejected on the whim of the opposite party. Revision dismissed. Ref: 2023 MLD 191.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Declaration Suit: Interpolated Sale Deed and Limitation
records.heading: A declaration suit on an interpolated sale deed was within limitation under Article 120
records.text: Heirs sued for a declaration that their deceased father was the owner under a 1963 sale deed in which the defendant allegedly interpolated his own name. The suit, filed in 2000 after the father died in 1997 and the interpolation came to light, was held to be within limitation under Art. 120 of the Limitation Act, 1908. Ref: 2023 MLD 175.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Presumption Attached to Thirty-Year-Old Document
records.heading: The presumption for a document over 30 years old is rebuttable
records.text: In a dispute over an alleged benami sale deed in favour of the deceased father, the presumption of validity attaching to a document more than 30 years old is rebuttable. The deed did not mention the respondent's name. Ref: 2023 MLD 175.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Proof of Oral Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A disputed oral agreement to sell must be proved by cogent, corroborated and confidence inspiring evidence
records.text: An oral agreement to sell is permissible, but if its existence is questioned it must be proved by cogent, corroborated and confidence inspiring evidence. Omission of time, place and witnesses from the plaint is fatal. Plaintiffs who produced no cheque or bank statement and contradicted themselves failed, and the revision was dismissed. Ref: 2023 MLD 145.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Discretion of Court
records.heading: A decree for specific performance lies in the Court's discretion even where the plaintiff proves his case
records.text: Under s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act, a decree for specific performance lies within the exclusive discretion of the Court, which may refuse the relief on equitable principles even if the plaintiff has proved his case. Ref: 2023 MLD 145.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Judicial Notice Under Art. 112 QSO
records.heading: Judicial notice under Article 112 QSO is exhaustive and covers neither parental finances nor Pathan dowry custom
records.text: The instances of judicial notice in Art. 112 QSO are exhaustive, and no other fact may be assumed or treated as proved without evidence. The financial status of a girl's parents and the custom of Pathans regarding dowry are not judicially noticeable facts and could not found a judgment. Ref: 2023 MLD 51.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Presumption of Dowry Delivery After Rukhsati
records.heading: Delivery of dowry is presumed after rukhsati, but presumptions based on custom or family size are unwarranted
records.text: Where rukhsati took place, delivery of dowry articles is to be presumed, as parents customarily give dowry to daughters. Presumptions based on a large family or Pathan custom are legally unwarranted. The question of return of dowry was left for the Family Court to decide on the evidence, and the constitutional petition was partially allowed. Ref: 2023 MLD 51.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Prompt and Deferred Dower in Nikahnama
records.heading: A Nikahnama is presumed correct, and prompt dower differs from deferred dower by its terms
records.text: A Nikahnama carries a presumption of correctness. The Rs.1000 entered in column 13 was prompt dower payable on demand, while the 16 kanal of land entered in column 16 was deferred dower payable only on separation or the husband's death. Ref: 2023 YLR 193.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Hundi Business Inferences Insufficient
records.heading: Post-arrest bail cannot be withheld on mere inferences without confidence inspiring material linking the accused
records.text: Post-arrest bail under s. 497 CrPC cannot be withheld on mere inferences and presumptions. The prosecution must collect confidence inspiring material reasonably connecting the accused with the offence. Screenshots from a laptop were not mentioned in the FIR or s. 161 statements. Bail allowed in a hundi/hawala money laundering case. Ref: 2023 YLR 166.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Money Laundering: Proceeds of Crime Must Be Proved
records.heading: Section 4 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act requires proof that the property is proceeds of crime
records.text: To attract s. 4 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010, the prosecution is primarily required to prove that the property in question is proceeds of crime. Ref: 2023 YLR 166.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 79 QSO: Two Attesting Witnesses for Gift Memo
records.heading: A document creating financial obligation needs two attesting witnesses under Article 79 QSO
records.text: A document entailing future or financial obligation must be proved through two attesting witnesses under Art. 79 QSO, which is mandatory and inflexible. Only one of two attesting witnesses to the unregistered memo of gift was examined, so the memo remained unproved and inadmissible in evidence. Ref: 2023 YLR 118.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Unregistered Memo of Gift Confers No Title
records.heading: An unregistered memo of gift confers no title to immovable property
records.text: An unregistered memo of gift does not confer title to immovable property. The plaintiff did not disclose when or where the oral gift was offered and accepted or when possession changed, and the donor lived about two years after the memo without any registered transfer. Revision accepted and the dismissal of the suit restored. Ref: 2023 YLR 118.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 59 QSO: Signature Comparison and Adverse Presumption
records.heading: Failure to seek expert signature comparison of a disputed gift document raises an adverse presumption
records.text: A beneficiary relying on an alleged unregistered gift document, which the other side calls forged, may seek comparison of the donor's signatures through an expert. By not doing so, the plaintiff incurred an adverse presumption against himself. Ref: 2023 YLR 118.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Compounding Offence Under s. 420 PPC
records.heading: An offence under section 420 PPC can be compounded by the person cheated with the Court's permission
records.text: Under s. 345 CrPC, an offence under s. 420 PPC can be compounded with the permission of the Court by the person cheated. Ref: 2023 YLR 250.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 420 PPC: Delivery of Property Not Proved
records.heading: Section 420 PPC is not made out without proof of delivery of property by cheating
records.text: Where the prosecution produced no receipt signed by the accused and did not produce the form issued to the complainant, receipt of any amount by cheating was not proved and the ingredients of s. 420 PPC were missing. Criminal revision accepted and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2023 YLR 250.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Compensation for Acquired Land With Potential Value
records.heading: Land with potential value on a main road earns enhanced fair compensation under the Constitution
records.text: Acquisition must conform to Art. 24(2) and (3) of the Constitution, and the owner must receive adequate, fair and just compensation. Under s. 23(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, value is assessed at the s. 4 notification. Land on a main road near a bypass had potential value, and compensation was enhanced from Rs.12,000 per marla to Rs.40,000. Ref: 2023 YLR 222.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Consumer Court Orders Must Give Reasons
records.heading: A Consumer Court order must show independent application of mind and give reasons
records.text: A final order of a Consumer Court under s. 31 of the Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005 must show independent application of mind and reasons, as reasons are essential to any judgment. The order determined no pivotal issues and gave no reasoning, so the High Court set it aside and remanded the matter for fresh decision. Ref: 2023 YLR 130.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Objection to Admissibility of Document: Decide Immediately
records.heading: An objection to admissibility of a document must be decided immediately, not deferred to judgment
records.text: An objection to the admissibility of a document in evidence must be decided then and there. It cannot be deferred until the end of the trial or the passing of the final judgment. Ref: 2023 CLD 135.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell Without Proprietary Rights
records.heading: A person without proprietary rights over State land cannot execute a sale deed, so the agreement to sell fails
records.text: A person who is not owner of property held by the State cannot execute a sale deed until he obtains proprietary rights, and any transaction remains suspended until then. The plaintiff admitted the Settlement Department had conferred no proprietary rights and did not implead it. Revision allowed and the suit dismissed. Ref: 2023 YLR 86.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Section 115 CPC: Interference With Perverse Concurrent Decrees
records.heading: Under section 115 CPC the High Court may interfere with perverse concurrent decrees
records.text: In revisional jurisdiction under s. 115 CPC, the High Court has jurisdiction to interfere with perverse concurrent judgments and decrees of the lower fora. Ref: 2023 YLR 86.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Section 115 CPC: Concurrent Findings of Fact
records.heading: Concurrent findings of fact in revision stand unless they suffer from misreading or non-reading of evidence
records.text: In revision under s. 115 CPC, concurrent findings of fact cannot be disturbed unless they suffer from misreading or non-reading of evidence. Ref: 2023 MLD 115.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Arts. 4 and 10-A: Fair Trial and Treatment According to Law
records.heading: Article 10-A guarantees fair trial and Article 4 the right to be treated in accordance with law
records.text: Art. 10-A of the Constitution provides the right to fair trial and due process. Art. 4 states the inalienable right of every citizen to be treated in accordance with law, and no action detrimental to reputation, life or liberty may be taken except as per law. No Court may disregard Art. 4. Ref: 2023 YLR 236.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Unfair Practice in Public Tenders
records.heading: Unfair practice by public functionaries in a general tender may be challenged under Article 199
records.text: Violation of law and unjust or partial practice by public functionaries that adversely affects the right of citizens to participate lawfully in obtaining contracts through general tender is unconstitutional, and jurisdiction under Art. 199 can be invoked in such cases. Ref: 2023 YLR 236.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Duty of Courts to Protect Minor Litigants
records.heading: A minor litigant is under the Court's protection and must be duly represented and defended
records.text: Under Art. 10-A, a minor litigant is under the protection of the Court, which must watch over the minor's interests and ensure he is duly represented and defended in the proceedings. Ref: 2023 YLR 78.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX R. 13 CPC: Ex Parte Decree Against Minors
records.heading: An ex parte decree against minors obtained by fraud or misrepresentation can be set aside under O. IX R. 13
records.text: Petitioners who were minors when the ex parte decree for specific performance was passed proved by reliable evidence that it was obtained by fraud or misrepresentation. The courts below had decided the issue routinely against the minors, and the High Court had jurisdiction to reverse the perverse concurrent findings. Ref: 2023 YLR 78.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Fundamental Rights Cannot Be Diluted by Administrative Instructions
records.heading: Administrative instructions without statutory backing cannot dilute fundamental rights
records.text: Law' means law made by Parliament or a Provincial Assembly, and administrative instructions, SOPs or guidelines without statutory backing cannot dilute fundamental rights. Regulation of a right can never mean total prohibition, and regulations so intrusive as to deny enjoyment of the right cannot be imposed even by law. Ref: 2023 YLR 64.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Freedom of Religion: Majlis-e-Aza Permission
records.heading: Refusing permission for a Majlis-e-Aza on non-statutory guidelines unduly restricts freedom of religion under Article 20
records.text: Authorities denied a Fiqa-e-Jafria petitioner permission to hold a Majlis-e-Aza on his property on the basis of guidelines with no statutory backing, which unduly restricted his right under Art. 20. The order was set aside and the matter remanded to the Deputy Commissioner for fresh consideration after hearing the petitioner. Petition allowed. Ref: 2023 YLR 64.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Speaking Orders: Independent Reasons Required
records.heading: Decisions, especially statutory ones, must contain independent reasons for the conclusion
records.text: Any reasonable exercise of decision making, especially one mandated by statute, must contain independent reasons for the conclusion. Reasons explain the justification for a decision and assure the affected person it is not fanciful, whimsical or arbitrary. Ref: 2023 YLR 64.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 25: Discriminatory Refusal of Thesis Extension
records.heading: Refusing a thesis extension while granting it to similarly placed students violates Article 25
records.text: A University that refused a PhD scholar an extension to submit his thesis, while granting extension to similarly placed students in the same meeting, violated Art. 25. The High Court directed the Syndicate to consider awarding him an honorary degree under s. 22(2)(xxii) of the UET Taxila Act, 1994, after hearing all concerned. Ref: 2023 YLR 203.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitrator's Report: Objections Before Making Award Rule of Court
records.heading: Parties must be allowed to file objections to an arbitrator's award before it is made rule of Court
records.text: Where parties referred a dispute to the village Lambardar as arbitrator, the Trial Court dismissed the suit on his report without giving the parties an opportunity to file objections to the award. The Appellate Court ignored this omission. Civil revision allowed and the case remanded, the suit to be treated as pending from the stage of filing of the award. Ref: 2023 YLR 57.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Conviction and Sentence Distinguished
records.heading: A conviction is the guilty verdict, while a sentence is the punishment awarded under it
records.text: A conviction is the guilty verdict, whereas a sentence is the form of punishment, either fine or imprisonment, awarded in pursuance of that verdict. Ref: 2023 YLR 6.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sentencing: Retribution and Just Deserts
records.heading: Sentences must be proportionate to the crime, so first offenders who served nearly four years had theirs reduced
records.text: Retribution is based on just deserts and requires proportionality between sentence and crime. First offenders with no criminal history or proven link to proscribed organisations, who had served almost four years, deserved different treatment. Convictions were maintained and sentences reduced to the period already served. The prosecutor raised no objection to the request for reduction. Ref: 2023 YLR 6.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Nomination Rejected: Proposer Not on Constituency Roll
records.heading: A nomination is rightly rejected where the proposer is not a voter on the constituency roll
records.text: Under the Elections Act, 2017, a candidate must be proposed by a voter on the electoral roll of that constituency. Nomination papers were rightly rejected where the proposer was from another constituency, and the Appellate Tribunal acting under s. 63 is bound by the Supreme Court's interpretation under Art. 189. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 MLD 132.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blind Murder: Delayed Nomination and Uncorroborated Confession
records.heading: In a blind murder, a delayed nomination, unproved motive and contradicted confession left the case doubtful
records.text: In an unseen murder, the accused was nominated by a supplementary statement recorded 21 days after the FIR, the motive was not proved, and the s. 164 CrPC confession contradicted the medical evidence and did not comply with mandatory requirements. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 YLR 89.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Confiscation of Vehicle: Owner Not Involved
records.heading: A vehicle is not liable to confiscation where its registered owner had no nexus with the offence
records.text: A vehicle was not liable to confiscation under the narcotics law where the registered owner was not an accused, had no nexus with the offence, and his knowledge or connivance was not established. The order returning the vehicle was upheld and the prosecution's appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 YLR 63.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Intra Court Appeal: Quashing of FIA FIR
records.heading: An intra court appeal against refusal to quash an FIA FIR fails where no error of law is shown
records.text: An intra court appeal against refusal to quash an FIR registered by the FIA was dismissed in view of the proviso to s. 3(2) of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972, as no error of law was shown. S. 13(3) of the Official Secrets Act, 1923 bars no investigation, and the Efficiency and Discipline Rules, 2020 concern only departmental action. Ref: 2023 MLD 47.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Section 99 CPC: Non-Framing of Issues
records.heading: Non-framing of issues causes no miscarriage of justice where the plaintiff led all his evidence
records.text: A plaintiff who led all his evidence without issues being framed could not complain after losing, as s. 99 CPC applied and no miscarriage of justice occurred. The ground was not raised in appeal, and Art. 199 jurisdiction does not permit reappraisal of evidence. Constitutional petition dismissed. Ref: 2023 MLD 180.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Recovery of Weapon and Eye-Witness Presence
records.heading: Non-recovery of the weapon does not harm the prosecution where the accused absconded for over six years
records.text: In a murder during robbery, where the nominated accused absconded for over six years, non-recovery of the crime weapon had no adverse effect on the prosecution case. The presence of both eye-witnesses at the spot was not doubted, and minor contradictions after a long lapse were insignificant. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 11.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 19-A QSO: Statement Soon After Incident
records.heading: A statement made soon after the incident is relevant under Article 19-A QSO if part of the same transaction
records.text: A statement of the accused made soon after the incident is relevant under Art. 19-A QSO because of its spontaneity and immediacy, but it must form part of the same transaction. If there was an interval sufficient for fabrication, the statement is not relevant. Ref: Shazam Ali v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.26723-J of 2019; Murder Reference No.82 of 2019).
records.title: Shazam Ali v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.26723-J of 2019; Murder Reference No.82 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence and Minor Discrepancies
records.heading: In circumstantial cases the Court weighs quality of evidence, and minor discrepancies are expected after a long gap
records.text: Where no ocular account exists and circumstantial evidence is produced, the Court looks at the quality rather than the quantity of evidence. Minor discrepancies, contradictions and omissions are to be expected when witnesses are examined after a long gap. Ref: Shazam Ali v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.26723-J of 2019; Murder Reference No.82 of 2019).
records.title: Shazam Ali v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.26723-J of 2019; Murder Reference No.82 of 2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Audio CD Copied From Phone Lacks Authenticity
records.heading: An audio CD copied from a phone lacks authenticity as the original device was not examined
records.text: An audio or video recording cannot be relied upon until proved genuine and untampered. A CD prepared by a witness by copying audio from the complainant's mobile phone was not the original recording device and lost authenticity. The police should have taken the phone and had it forensically tested against the accused's voice. Ref: 2023 LHC 115; Rana Muhammad Yousaf Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 61551/22, decided 13.01.2023); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Rana Muhammad Yousaf Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 61551/22, decided 13.01.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Powers Under ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC
records.heading: The Trial Court's powers under sections 249-A and 265-K CrPC are similar to those under section 561-A
records.text: The powers of the Trial Court under ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC are similar to the powers of the High Court under s. 561-A CrPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 115; Rana Muhammad Yousaf Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 61551/22, decided 13.01.2023); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Rana Muhammad Yousaf Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 61551/22, decided 13.01.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Punjab Election Date Petition: Notice Issued
records.heading: Lahore High Court issued notice on a petition seeking a date for the Punjab Assembly election
records.text: The Lahore High Court admitted for hearing the petition of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaaf seeking a date for the Punjab Assembly election, counsel arguing that the Governor must announce it within 90 days of dissolution. The Election Commission was to be joined as party, and notice was ordered to the Attorney General and Advocate General under O. XXVII-A CPC. Ref: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaaf through its General Secretary Asad Umar v. Governor of Punjab and another (Writ Petition No.5851 of 2023, order dated 30.01.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaaf through its General Secretary Asad Umar v. Governor of Punjab and another (Writ Petition No.5851 of 2023, order dated 30.01.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Ear Injury: Helix and Cartilage Not Organ or Limb
records.heading: Helix and cartilage of the ear is not an organ or limb under section 334 PPC, supporting bail
records.text: Helix and cartilaginous tissue of the ear is not an organ or limb attracting iflaf-i-udw under s. 334 PPC, and the doctor did not identify the limb affected. The remaining s. 337-F(iii) PPC offence does not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so a case for bail on further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC was made out. Ref: 2023 YLR Note 1.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Supreme Court and Interim Orders
records.heading: The Supreme Court does not readily interfere in interim orders
records.text: Authority that the Supreme Court does not readily interfere in interim orders. Ref: Attiq ur Rehman v. Sh. Tahir Mehmood and others (C.P.600/2020, decided 26.01.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Attiq ur Rehman v. Sh. Tahir Mehmood and others (C.P.600/2020, decided 26.01.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Joint Trial of PECA s. 11 and Blasphemy Offences
records.heading: PECA section 11 and blasphemy offences from the same transaction can be tried together
records.text: Offences under s. 11 PECA, 2016 and ss. 295-A, 295-B, 295-C and 298-C PPC arising from the same transaction can be tried together at one trial under ss. 235 and 4(c) CrPC, as their ingredients are interlinked and not inconsistent. Separate trials would risk conflicting decisions. Ref: 2022 LHC 8819; Shiraz Ahmed etc v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 69407/22, decided 09.12.2022); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Shiraz Ahmed etc v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 69407/22, decided 09.12.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Call Data Record (CDR)
records.heading: A call data record is proved like other primary evidence and only the authorised officer may obtain it
records.text: A CDR is tendered and proved like any other primary evidence. Under the SOP, only the authorised officer can generate or obtain a CDR from the automated system, and he cannot delegate this by giving his email to a subordinate or anyone else. He must also maintain confidentiality of the CDR. Ref: Mst. Saima Nareen v. State etc (Crl. Appeal CM/2/59829/21, decided 31.01.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Mst. Saima Nareen v. State etc (Crl. Appeal CM/2/59829/21, decided 31.01.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Call Data Record (CDR)
records.heading: A call data record is proved like other primary evidence and only the authorised officer may obtain it
records.text: A CDR is tendered and proved like any other primary evidence. Under the SOP, only the authorised officer can generate or obtain a CDR from the automated system, and he cannot delegate this by giving his email to a subordinate or anyone else. He must also maintain confidentiality of the CDR. Ref: Mst. Saima Nareen v. State etc (Crl. Appeal CM/2/59829/21, decided 31.01.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Mst. Saima Nareen v. State etc (Crl. Appeal CM/2/59829/21, decided 31.01.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Pakistan Railways Land Lease for Public Use
records.heading: A Supreme Court bench permitted Pakistan Railways to lease land for public use with conditions
records.text: A three member special bench of the Supreme Court permitted Pakistan Railways to lease land for public use. It directed that the status of leased land not be changed, that no construction be raised on railway land used as a park, and that Railways obtain legislation on its lands from Parliament or the Cabinet. Ref: Matter regarding implementation of the order of this Court dated 28.6.2019 (C.M.A.7139/2019, decided 26.01.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Matter regarding implementation of the order of this Court dated 28.6.2019 (C.M.A.7139/2019, decided 26.01.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift: Particulars to Be Pleaded and Proved
records.heading: A person claiming an oral gift must plead and prove time, place, possession and witnesses
records.text: A person claiming an oral gift must plead in detail the time, date and place of the declaration and acceptance, the transfer of possession, and the names of the witnesses in whose presence it was made, and then prove these by producing witnesses. Ref: Muhammad Arif v. Province of Punjab and others (C.R. No.23580 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. Province of Punjab and others (C.R. No.23580 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Producing Adversary as Witness; Art. 131 QSO
records.heading: The CPC neither bars nor permits producing an adversary as one's own witness, and the practice is disapproved
records.text: The CPC neither bars nor permits a party to produce his adversary as its own witness, and the practice has not been approved as it causes unnecessary embarrassment. Art. 131 QSO empowers the court to disallow irrelevant or inadmissible evidence and to regulate the production of evidence. Ref: Muhammad Arif v. Province of Punjab and others (C.R. No.23580 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. Province of Punjab and others (C.R. No.23580 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Unregistered Award and Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A plaint cannot be rejected where an award made rule of Court needed evidence on its registration
records.text: Where the award was made rule of the Court subject to registration and no registration was shown, the parties had to be allowed to lead evidence on its registration, its effect on partition and on the later khangi taqseem nama. Rejection of the plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC was held erroneous and the orders of the courts below annulled. Ref: Mahboob Ahmad and others v. Ayub Ahmad and others (C.R. No.2494 of 2022).
records.title: Mahboob Ahmad and others v. Ayub Ahmad and others (C.R. No.2494 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor Daughters: Welfare Lies With Mother
records.heading: Welfare of the minors is paramount, and custody of daughters was given to the educated mother
records.text: Welfare of the minors is the paramount consideration in custody. Daughters need the company of their real mother, and on the evidence custody with the educated mother, living in a joint family with the maternal grandmother, was in the best interest of the minors. The father was availing the agreed visitation. Ref: Mst. Alia Sehr v. Mushtaq Ahmed and others (W.P. No.61653 of 2020).
records.title: Mst. Alia Sehr v. Mushtaq Ahmed and others (W.P. No.61653 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report: Duty of Magistrate
records.heading: A Magistrate must examine police diaries and give reasons before accepting a cancellation report
records.text: On a police cancellation report, the Magistrate must thoroughly examine the police diaries and record his reasons. The Judicial Magistrate treated the report casually, and the impugned order was bereft of reasoning and showed no application of mind. Ref: Madiha Ammad v. The State etc. (Writ Petition No. 21725/2021).
records.title: Madiha Ammad v. The State etc. (Writ Petition No. 21725/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Regular Second Appeal (Citation Only)
records.heading: Regular second appeal decided by the Lahore High Court on 24.01.2023; the post states no holding
records.text: Authority on a regular second appeal decided by the Lahore High Court on 24.01.2023. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 171; Mubashar Ahmad Ayaz v. Manzoor Ahmad Chinioti etc (Regular Second Appeal 46-09, decided 24.01.2023); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Mubashar Ahmad Ayaz v. Manzoor Ahmad Chinioti etc (Regular Second Appeal 46-09, decided 24.01.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Prohibited Funding Case: Petition Premature
records.heading: A petition against the Election Commission in the prohibited funding case was premature before the show cause process ended
records.text: A larger bench of the Islamabad High Court dismissed PTI's petition against the Election Commission as premature. PTI may respond to the show cause notice and, if aggrieved at the end of that process, seek remedies including judicial review. The ECP's tentative findings referred to the Federal Government were held to be of no consequence. Ref: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) v. ECP (Writ Petition-2998-2022, decided 02.02.2023); Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) v. ECP (Writ Petition-2998-2022, decided 02.02.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Punjab Election Date: Ninety Day Requirement
records.heading: Lahore High Court remarked that elections must be held within 90 days and questioned the economic plea
records.text: In the petition seeking a date for the Punjab Assembly election, the Lahore High Court remarked that the Constitution requires elections within 90 days and questioned the plea of a poor economic situation. The Governor's counsel was given time to file a reply and the hearing was adjourned to 9 February. Ref: 2023 LHC 198; Pakistan Tehreek e Insaaf through Asad Umar v. Governor Punjab through Principal Secretary (Writ Election Miscellaneous 5851/23, 03.02.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Pakistan Tehreek e Insaaf through Asad Umar v. Governor Punjab through Principal Secretary (Writ Election Miscellaneous 5851/23, 03.02.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Partition Act s. 6: Written Statement Within 30 Days
records.heading: Section 6 of the Punjab Partition Act is mandatory and requires a written statement within 30 days
records.text: S. 6 of the Punjab Partition of Immovable Property Act, 2012 is mandatory. A defendant must file the written statement within 30 days of first appearance, the Court cannot extend the period, and on default the defence must be struck off and the defendant cannot lead evidence. Delay caused by time granted by the Trial Court did not help the petitioners. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 81.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Deputy Commissioner Cannot Declare Title or Correct Record
records.heading: The Deputy Commissioner cannot declare title or correct revenue record under the Civil Administration Act
records.text: Ss. 15 and 19 of the Punjab Civil Administration Act, 2017 deal with public order and safeguarding property and do not empower the Deputy Commissioner to declare title or correct revenue record. He cannot go beyond his statutory functions. The High Court declined to interfere and dismissed the constitutional petition. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 97.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 526 CrPC: Transfer From Ex-Officio Justice of Peace
records.heading: An ex-officio Justice of Peace is not a court, so section 526 CrPC does not allow transfer
records.text: S. 526 CrPC empowers the High Court to transfer cases pending before criminal courts only. An ex-officio Justice of Peace acting under ss. 22-A and 22-B is not a court within s. 20 PPC read with s. 4(2) CrPC, so a transfer petition from one such Justice of Peace to another was dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 86.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Vested Right: Meaning and Scope
records.heading: A vested right is absolute, complete and unconditional and cannot be taken away without consent
records.text: A right that so completely and definitely belongs to a person that it cannot be impaired or taken away without his consent is a vested right. It is absolute, complete and unconditional, immediate and perfect in itself and not dependent on a contingency. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 103.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Arts. 7 and 8: State Cannot Take Away Fundamental Rights
records.heading: Article 8 bars the State, including Parliament, from enacting a law that takes away a fundamental right
records.text: Art. 8 prohibits the State from enacting a law that takes away a fundamental right conferred on a citizen. The State, as defined in Art. 7, includes Parliament as part of the legislature. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 103.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Deeming Clause as Legal Fiction
records.heading: A deeming clause is a legal fiction that cannot be extended beyond the language creating it
records.text: A deeming clause is a legal fiction that the Court accepts as reality, placing an artificial construction on a word or phrase. It is a fiction and cannot be extended beyond the language of the section creating it or by importing another fiction. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 103.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Interpretation of Statutes: Legislative Intent
records.heading: Courts give statutory words their plain meaning to discover legislative intent regardless of consequences
records.text: The Court's function is to discover the true legislative intent, giving words their plain and ordinary meaning irrespective of consequences. Where the language is unambiguous and capable of one construction only, no question of construction arises, and the Court is not concerned with policy or harsh results. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 103.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ of Quo Warranto: Object and Scope
records.heading: Quo warranto tests whether a holder of public office holds it in accordance with law
records.text: A writ of quo warranto under Art. 199(1)(b)(ii) is in the nature of laying information before the Court against a person who usurps an office. Its object is to determine whether the holder of a statutory or constitutional office holds it in accordance with law. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 103.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC: Effect of Injunction
records.heading: An injunction under O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC remains in force until final adjudication or recall
records.text: An injunctive order under O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC is passed after application of mind to the facts and circumstances. It remains in force until final adjudication or until the Court recalls or vacates it. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 103.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Essential Elements of a Legal Right
records.heading: A legal right has an owner, a bound person, an obligatory act, an object and a title
records.text: The essential elements of a legal right are: an owner of the right, a person bound by a correlative duty, an obligatory act or omission as its content, an object or subject matter, and a title consisting of the facts or events by which the right vested in its owner. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 103.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Trial: Chapter XXII-A Legislative Background
records.heading: Authority on sessions trial under Chapter XXII-A CrPC and its legislative background; no further holding stated
records.text: Authority on trial before the Court of Session under Chapter XXII-A (ss. 265-A to 265-N) CrPC. The judgment details the legislative background of sessions trial. The post states no further holding.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Extra-Judicial Confession: Principles of Appraisal
records.heading: An extra-judicial confession is weak evidence needing an unimpeachable source and corroboration
records.text: Extra-judicial confession is a weak piece of evidence and not direct evidence. It can be used against an accused only if it comes from an unimpeachable source and is corroborated in material particulars, and a capital conviction cannot rest on it alone. The Court must be satisfied that it was made, was voluntary and was true. Ref: 2021 YLR 2210, 2021 MLD 1415; Shafqat Masih v. State.
records.title: Shafqat Masih v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Preparation of Site Plan Under Police Rules
records.heading: Under Police Rules R. 25.13(2)(i) a Patwari or draftsman prepares the scene map in heinous crimes
records.text: Under R. 25.13(2)(i) of the Police Rules, in heinous crimes the investigating officer who needs an accurate map of the scene summons the Patwari or a qualified draftsman to prepare it in duplicate, one for the Court with the report and one for police use. Responsibilities of the Patwari, draftsman and police officer must be clearly defined. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC Note 52.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Ombudsman Entertaining Time-Barred Complaint
records.heading: The Ombudsman may entertain a time-barred complaint only after stating the special circumstances
records.text: The Ombudsman may entertain a time-barred complaint only if he states the special circumstances making it proper to do so. His order mentioned none in entertaining the respondent's time-barred pension complaint. The orders of the Ombudsman and the President were set aside and the matter remanded for fresh decision of the review application. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Islamabad 61; Allama Iqbal Open University (AIOU), through Registrar v. Federation of Pakistan through D.G. Legal for President of Pakistan and 2 others (W.P. No. 1086 of 2021, decided 22.11.2022); Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Allama Iqbal Open University (AIOU), through Registrar v. Federation of Pakistan through D.G. Legal for President of Pakistan and 2 others (W.P. No. 1086 of 2021, decided 22.11.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 22-A CrPC: Dishonoured Cheque Claimed as Security
records.heading: A claim that a dishonoured cheque was security was not credible without proof of repayment
records.text: The Ex-officio Justice of Peace committed no illegality in directing registration of a case on a dishonoured cheque.
