The petitioner's claim that the cheque was lying as security and misused after repayment was not credible, as no receipt of repayment was placed on record. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 19; Abdul Shakoor v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace and 2 others (W.P. No. 7903 of 2021, decided 15.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Abdul Shakoor v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace and 2 others (W.P. No. 7903 of 2021, decided 15.09.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Suit on Cheque Issued to Attorney
records.heading: A summary suit on cheques issued to an attorney without nexus to the claim was dismissed
records.text: A suit for recovery under O. XXXVII CPC was dismissed because the cheques were issued in the name of the attorney, who had no nexus with the claim, and no evidence of the respondent's liability was produced. The plaintiff had no locus standi or cause of action. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 20; Chaudhry Shaukat Ali through Special Attorney v. Irshad Ahmad (R.F.A. No. 1544 of 2014); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Chaudhry Shaukat Ali through Special Attorney v. Irshad Ahmad (R.F.A. No. 1544 of 2014)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation After Withdrawal of Earlier Suit
records.heading: Withdrawal of an earlier suit gives no fresh cause of action and does not extend limitation
records.text: After withdrawal of an earlier suit, limitation is reckoned from the filing of the earlier proceedings. Withdrawal, even with permission, gives no fresh cause of action and does not extend limitation, so the plaintiff proceeds as if the first suit was never filed. The third suit for cancellation of GPA and sale deeds was time barred. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 21; Mirza Mushtaq v. Athar Rasul and 11 others (C.R. No. 24602 of 2019, decided 12.09.2022); Justice Muhammad Masood Jahangir.
records.title: Mirza Mushtaq v. Athar Rasul and 11 others (C.R. No. 24602 of 2019, decided 12.09.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII R. 4 CPC: Setting Aside Decree on Promissory Note
records.heading: A decree on a promissory note is not set aside where the defendant shows no special circumstances
records.text: An application to set aside a decree on a promissory note failed because the defendant, who admitted execution, gave lame excuses and did not make out special circumstances. His plea that he executed it as surety was unproved and he filed no application under s. 12(2) CPC. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 22; Zulfiqar Ali v. Ahmad Nawaz (F.A.O. No. 32850 of 2021); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Zulfiqar Ali v. Ahmad Nawaz (F.A.O. No. 32850 of 2021)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift Mutation: Proof and Pardanashin Lady
records.heading: An oral gift mutation by a pardanashin lady must be proved through attesting witnesses or secondary evidence
records.text: In a suit to cancel an oral gift mutation, the plaintiff had to bring on record death entries of the signatories and seek leave to lead secondary evidence of attestation by marginal witnesses and revenue officials, which was not done. The mutation concerned an illiterate lady entitled to pardanashin protection. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 25; Muhammad Ashraf v. ADJ etc. (C.R. No. 830 of 2017); Justice Muhammad Masood Jahangir.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. ADJ etc. (C.R. No. 830 of 2017)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor Children: Liability of Father
records.heading: A father is liable to maintain his minor children, and an uncross-examined assertion stands
records.text: A father is liable to maintain his minor children. The wife's categorical assertion that he expelled her from the house was not cross-examined, and the Family Court rightly granted maintenance. The concurrent decrees did not call for interference and the petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 26; Muhammad Amin v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and 4 others (W.P. No. 41183 of 2022, decided 29.06.2022); Justice Shams Mehmood Mirza.
records.title: Muhammad Amin v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and 4 others (W.P. No. 41183 of 2022, decided 29.06.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: High Court Not an Appellate Court
records.heading: In constitutional jurisdiction the High Court is not an appellate court and checks only jurisdictional errors
records.text: In constitutional jurisdiction under Art. 199, the High Court does not act as an appellate court and need only oversee jurisdictional errors of inferior courts. Judgments free from misreading and non-reading of evidence are not interfered with. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 26; Muhammad Amin v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and 4 others (W.P. No. 41183 of 2022, decided 29.06.2022); Justice Shams Mehmood Mirza.
records.title: Muhammad Amin v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and 4 others (W.P. No. 41183 of 2022, decided 29.06.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Sheesha Cafes and Smoking in Public Places
records.heading: The Federal Government must notify rules on smoking in sheesha bars and public places within six months
records.text: Under ss. 5 and 17 of the Prohibition of Smoking and Protection of Non-Smokers Health Ordinance, 2002, the Federal Government was directed to notify rules within six months. The Chief Commissioner ICT was to stop smoking in sheesha bars and public places until designated areas are notified. Petition disposed of. Ref: PLJ 2023 Islamabad Note 29; Yassa Khan v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary M/o NHSRC and 2 others (W.P. No. 4242 of 2021); Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani.
records.title: Yassa Khan v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary M/o NHSRC and 2 others (W.P. No. 4242 of 2021)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Agreement and Habeas Remedy
records.heading: An agreement to hand over custody of a minor has no value in law
records.text: An agreement to hand over custody of a minor has no value in law, and an agreement by a female that is unconscionable on its face is presumed to be the result of coercion and undue influence. The Guardian Court decides custody finally, yet a parent lawfully holding custody who is deprived of it may seek a remedy. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 30; Mst. Farzana Parveen v. City Police Officer and 4 others (W.P. No. 14457 of 2022, decided 12.10.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Mst. Farzana Parveen v. City Police Officer and 4 others (W.P. No. 14457 of 2022, decided 12.10.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Surety Bond in Execution of Maintenance Decree
records.heading: A surety in execution of a maintenance decree is bound to the extent of his undertaking
records.text: In execution of a maintenance decree, the surety was bound to the extent of Rs.200,000 undertaken by him. The revisional court's order refusing his discharge was in accordance with law and needed no interference under Art. 199. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 32; Muhammad Irfan v. Additional District Judge and 5 others (W.P. No. 61371 of 2020); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Muhammad Irfan v. Additional District Judge and 5 others (W.P. No. 61371 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-e-Amd: Delay in Reporting and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Unexplained delay in reporting to the police supports an inference of fabrication and benefit of doubt
records.text: Unexplained delay in reporting the matter to the police speaks against the prosecution version and supports an inference that the interval was used to fabricate a story. Medical evidence may confirm the ocular account but cannot connect the accused with the crime. Appeal allowed and the accused acquitted, and the complainant's revision for enhancement was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 32; Shahid Pervaiz alias Farooq alias Farooqi etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 27738-J & Crl. Rev. No. 14608 of 2021); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Shahid Pervaiz alias Farooq alias Farooqi etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 27738-J & Crl. Rev. No. 14608 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint: Ss. 200 to 204 CrPC
records.heading: A Magistrate may issue process on a private complaint on the allegations alone if a prima facie case exists
records.text: A private complaint gives an aggrieved person direct access to set the law in motion. After examining the complainant on oath, the Magistrate may issue process on the allegations in the complaint alone if satisfied that a prima facie case exists. The impugned order was set aside and the matter remanded for further enquiry. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 43; Rubina Subtain alias Fazeela Bibi v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 09 of 2021, decided 02.06.2021); Justice Sardar Ahmed Naeem.
records.title: Rubina Subtain alias Fazeela Bibi v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 09 of 2021, decided 02.06.2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning CDRs Under s. 265-F(vii) CrPC
records.heading: An application to summon CDRs was premature as the right under section 265-F(vii) arises after prosecution evidence
records.text: An application to summon CDRs was premature, as the accused had the right under s. 265-F(vii) CrPC to have record summoned after the prosecution evidence. He recorded his statement without moving any such application. The dismissal of the application required no interference and the revision was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 44; Asad Sarwar Bhatti v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 24647 of 2021, decided 11.05.2022); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Asad Sarwar Bhatti v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 24647 of 2021, decided 11.05.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness: Testimony Tested Like Any Other
records.heading: An injured witness is present at the scene but his testimony is tested like any other
records.text: The presence of an injured witness at the scene cannot be disputed, but his injuries do not stamp his testimony with credence. His statement must be tested on the principles applied to any other prosecution witness, relying on 1981 SCMR 795, 1996 SCMR 1411 and 1995 SCMR 127. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 46; Muhammad Younas v. State and another (Crl. Rev. No. 285 of 2021, decided 30.11.2021); Justice Sohail Nasir.
records.title: Muhammad Younas v. State and another (Crl. Rev. No. 285 of 2021, decided 30.11.2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Attempt to Commit Qatl-e-Amd: Single Empty Recovered
records.heading: The prosecution account was doubted where only one empty was found despite multiple fires alleged
records.text: In a case under ss. 324 and 337-F(iii) PPC, the Court doubted the prosecution account where no witness said the petitioner reloaded the gun after each fire and only one empty was found at the scene despite multiple fires alleged. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 46; Muhammad Younas v. State and another (Crl. Rev. No. 285 of 2021, decided 30.11.2021); Justice Sohail Nasir.
records.title: Muhammad Younas v. State and another (Crl. Rev. No. 285 of 2021, decided 30.11.2021)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Ten Kilograms of Bhang
records.heading: With ten kilograms of bhang the sentence must be commensurate with quantity, supporting post-arrest bail
records.text: Under s. 9(1)(c) of the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997 as amended in 2022, the sentence must be commensurate with the quantity recovered. With 10 kilograms of bhang there was least likelihood of the maximum punishment, and the petitioner had been in custody for over one and a half months. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 47; Muhammad Adnan v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7786-B of 2022, decided 23.11.2022); Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Adnan v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7786-B of 2022, decided 23.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Scope and Further Stretching
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is narrow but may be stretched where an innocent person faces arrest for a tainted purpose
records.text: The scope of pre-arrest bail is narrow but should not be narrowed further on flimsy grounds, and should be stretched where an innocent person faces arrest for a tainted purpose. The ocular account contradicted the medical history, and the petitioner had joined investigation, so no useful purpose lay in sending him to jail. Ad interim bail confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 50; Saleem Sarwar v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8229-B of 2020, decided 16.02.2021); Justice Raja Shahid Mehmood Abbasi.
records.title: Saleem Sarwar v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8229-B of 2020, decided 16.02.2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Delay and Mala Fide
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail granted where FIR delay was unexplained, offences were bailable and mala fide was possible
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was granted where the FIR was delayed by about eight days without explanation, s. 436 PPC was prima facie not attracted, the remaining offences were bailable, and mala fide of the police could not be ruled out. Liberty is a precious constitutional right. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 52; Abdul Sattar and others v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 44738-B of 2022, decided 14.09.2022); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch..
records.title: Abdul Sattar and others v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 44738-B of 2022, decided 14.09.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Criminal History Not a Bar
records.heading: Criminal history does not bar bail under section 497(2) CrPC where the case is one of further inquiry
records.text: Criminal history of two similar cases does not prevent bail under s. 497(2) CrPC if the case is otherwise one of further inquiry. Nobody may be detained as advance punishment, and there was doubt in the recovery of charas. The embargo in s. 5 of the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997 was not attracted. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 53; Muhammad Jalal v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 6746-B of 2022, decided 13.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Jalal v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 6746-B of 2022, decided 13.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses Require Cautious Scrutiny
records.heading: Chance witnesses are accepted only if they satisfactorily explain their presence at the scene
records.text: The testimony of chance witnesses requires cautious scrutiny and cannot be accepted unless they satisfactorily explain their presence at or near the place of occurrence at the relevant time, relying on PLD 2021 SC 600. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 54; Samran Babar v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 57592 of 2019); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch..
records.title: Samran Babar v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 57592 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive, Recovery and Medical Evidence in Unwitnessed Murder
records.heading: In an unwitnessed murder, motive is double edged, recovery is corroborative and medical evidence cannot point to the accused
records.text: Motive is a double edged weapon, as it may also explain false involvement. Recovery is merely corroborative and relevant only if the ocular account inspires confidence. Medical evidence in an unwitnessed murder cannot point to the accused. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt and the appeal was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 54; Samran Babar v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 57592 of 2019); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch..
records.title: Samran Babar v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 57592 of 2019)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Delay in Medical Examination
records.heading: Bail granted where the injured was medically examined about twenty days after a single knee shot
records.text: Bail after arrest granted under s. 497 CrPC where the injured, hit once on the knee by a single shot, was medically examined only about twenty days later. The question of intention to kill is for the trial Court, and the petitioner is no longer required for investigation. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 56; Muhammad Yousaf v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7120-B of 2021, decided on 8.11.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7120-B of 2021, decided on 8.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: No Mala Fide Shown
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail declined where medico-legal certificates supported the allegation and no mala fide was shown
records.text: Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC declined where the allegation of causing injuries was supported by medico-legal certificates and statements under s. 161 CrPC, and no mala fide or ulterior motive against the complainant, injured or investigating officer could be shown. Bail dismissed and ad interim bail recalled. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 57; Shahzad Ahmed and another v. The State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 43019-B of 2021, decided on 26.9.2022); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Shahzad Ahmed and another v. The State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 43019-B of 2021, decided on 26.9.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Doubtful Identification Parade
records.heading: An accused said to be known to the complainant but unnamed in the FIR makes the identification parade doubtful
records.text: In a robbery case the complainant said the accused was known to him yet did not name him in the FIR, which made the worth of the identification parade a matter for the trial Court. The case became one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 59; Muhammad Rizwan alias Raju v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 3331-B of 2022, decided on 22.6.2022); Justice Shakil Ahmed.
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan alias Raju v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 3331-B of 2022, decided on 22.6.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Role of Prosecution in Criminal Cases
records.heading: The Prosecution Service is an independent agency and not a post office for investigating officers
records.text: The Prosecution Service is an independent agency whose role is to check the working of investigating officers at the right time, and it is not that of a post office. A court may agree or disagree with a prosecutor's opinion but cannot sit over the powers of prosecutors. The impugned order could not be sustained and the petition was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 121; Shagufta Sarwar, ADPP and another v. Special Judge Anti-Terrorism Court and others (W.P. No. 17809 & Crl. Rev. No. 311 of 2021, decided on 15.11.2021); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad; Justice Sohail Nasir.
records.title: Shagufta Sarwar, ADPP and another v. Special Judge Anti-Terrorism Court and others (W.P. No. 17809 & Crl. Rev. No. 311 of 2021, decided on 15.11.2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Res Judicata: Repeat s. 22-A Application
records.heading: Res judicata applies to a repeat section 22-A application but does not bar a private complaint
records.text: The Ex-officio Justice of Peace exercises quasi-judicial functions under s. 22-A(6) CrPC, so the principle of res judicata applies to a second application seeking registration of an FIR on the same facts. It does not bar a private complaint, which is an independent statutory remedy. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 129; Shahzad v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace etc. (W.P. No. 80439 of 2021); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Shahzad v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace etc. (W.P. No. 80439 of 2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Religious Processions: Permission and Licensing
records.heading: Processions are licensed or traditional, and permission was regulated under section 30 of the Police Act 1861
records.text: Processions are of two kinds, the Licensed Procession (usually the Tazia and Zuljinnah of 10th Muharram) and the Traditional Procession (all others). Before the Police Order, permission and licences for religious processions were regulated under s. 30 of the Police Act, 1861. The post also notes the purpose of the Punjab Civil Administration Act, 2017. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 135; Shamim Haider and 6 others v. Additional Chief Secretary (Home) and 5 others (W.P. No. 1915 of 2022); Justice Sohail Nasir.
records.title: Shamim Haider and 6 others v. Additional Chief Secretary (Home) and 5 others (W.P. No. 1915 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance: Concealed Income of Husband
records.heading: A husband who hides his income to avoid maintaining his minor children cannot succeed
records.text: In a suit for dissolution of marriage and maintenance under ss. 8 and 9 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, the husband who produced no document of his financial status and hid his income to avoid maintenance of the minors could not succeed. Findings of fact of the Courts below were left undisturbed and both writ petitions were dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 143; Zia Hussain v. Additional District Judge and others (W.P. No. 2832 of 2018); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Zia Hussain v. Additional District Judge and others (W.P. No. 2832 of 2018)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Remission for Period Spent on Bail
records.heading: A convict released on bail and not confined in jail earns no remission for that period
records.text: Under R. 35 of the Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978, a convict who was released on bail and not confined in jail is not entitled to remissions for that period, and the period is not counted as sentence served. The petition for remission was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 149; Nasreen Akhtar Siddiqui v. Government of the Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 69955 of 2021); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Nasreen Akhtar Siddiqui v. Government of the Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 69955 of 2021)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Mother During Suckling Period
records.heading: A mother feeding a suckling baby is entitled to maintenance for that period under section 9 MFLO
records.text: Under s. 9 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, a mother who feeds a suckling baby cannot be deprived of maintenance, and she is entitled to it for the period in which she fed the minor. The Family Court decree was modified accordingly, the rest of the maintenance fixed was upheld, and the petition was partially allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 154; Mst. Farida Bibi etc. v. Judge Family Court etc. (W.P. No. 18625 of 2016); Justice Safdar Saleem Shahid.
records.title: Mst. Farida Bibi etc. v. Judge Family Court etc. (W.P. No. 18625 of 2016)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 22-A CrPC: Civil Dispute over Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Genuineness of an agreement to sell is for the Civil Court, not the Justice of Peace under section 22-A
records.text: Where the dispute concerns an agreement to sell, its genuineness is for the Civil Court after evidence, and the Ex-officio Justice of Peace rightly declined to order an FIR. Writ jurisdiction should not be invoked when an adequate remedy exists. Petition dismissed in limine, with liberty to use the alternate remedy. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 161; Mehmood Ahmad v. ASJ, etc. (W.P. No. 73916 of 2022, decided on 23.11.2022); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Mehmood Ahmad v. ASJ, etc. (W.P. No. 73916 of 2022, decided on 23.11.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Proof of Agreement to Sell and Mutation
records.heading: Failure to prove an agreement to sell and payment defeated the mutation and the appellate judgment
records.text: The respondents failed to prove the agreement to sell and the payment of consideration, as the lambardar, union council members and Tehsildar did not appear to support the mutation, and a diary entry is not primary evidence unless the revenue officer produces it and faces cross-examination. The appellate judgment was set aside and the trial Court decree restored. Revision allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 172; Mst. Kaneeza Bibi and 4 others v. Sabir Hussain and 3 others (C.R. No. 296-D of 2012); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Mst. Kaneeza Bibi and 4 others v. Sabir Hussain and 3 others (C.R. No. 296-D of 2012)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Arts. 117 and 122 QSO
records.heading: In criminal cases the burden lies on the prosecution and never shifts, notwithstanding Article 122 QSO
records.text: In a criminal case the burden lies on the prosecution and never shifts, and Art. 122 QSO does not relieve it of that duty. The burden shifts only after the prosecution proves the elements of the offence, and then the accused need only produce evidence creating doubt about facts within his especial knowledge. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 113.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Benefit of Doubt at Bail Stage
records.heading: Benefit of doubt may be extended at the bail stage where a land dispute makes false implication possible
records.text: At the bail stage only a tentative assessment is made, but benefit of doubt can be extended if the facts warrant. The injury attributed to the petitioner was on a non-vital part and not the cause of death, and a land dispute made false implication a possibility. The case was one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Bail accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 156; Hassan Iqbal v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 73828-B of 2021, decided on 18.1.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Hassan Iqbal v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 73828-B of 2021, decided on 18.1.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Extra-Judicial Confession: Weak Evidence
records.heading: An extra-judicial confession is weak evidence needing utmost care and corroboration
records.text: Extra-judicial confession is weak evidence and needs utmost care and corroboration by reliable evidence. Here the witness's account of a confession before the police in the complainant's presence, which the complainant did not mention in his application, shook the prosecution case. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC set aside and the appellant acquitted by benefit of doubt. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 160; Manzoor Ahmad v. The State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 454-J of 2021/BWP); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Manzoor Ahmad v. The State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 454-J of 2021/BWP)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Plea of Alibi
records.heading: A plea of alibi backed by disinterested witnesses cannot be ignored at the bail stage
records.text: A plea of alibi supported by the affidavit of a disinterested medical practitioner and the statements of two non-partisan hotel and bank managers cannot be ignored at the bail stage. The opinion of the investigating agency does not bind the Court. Case of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC made out. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 170; Muhammad Aslam v. The State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 2293/B of 2022, decided on 16.9.2022); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 2293/B of 2022, decided on 16.9.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested and Chance Witnesses
records.heading: Relationship does not make an eyewitness unworthy, and a witness who explains his presence is not a chance witness
records.text: Relationship with the deceased does not make an eyewitness unworthy of credence, and the defence must show enmity giving a likelihood of false implication. Chicken suppliers who explained their presence were not chance witnesses, and even a passerby who explains his presence cannot be discarded. Appeal dismissed and death sentence confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 174; Muhammad Faisal v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 76 of 2020 & M.R. No. 14 of 2020); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz; Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Faisal v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 76 of 2020 & M.R. No. 14 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 342 CrPC: Additional Questions to Accused
records.heading: Section 342 CrPC allows additional questions to the accused at any stage, even after his statement
records.text: The first part of s. 342 CrPC allows the Court to put questions at any stage, so additional questions may be put even after the accused's statement was recorded. Evidence not put to the accused cannot be used against him, and the Court can put additional questions instead of recording the statement afresh or remanding. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 195, 2023 PCrLJ 805; Tauheed Abbas v. The State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 719 of 2017, heard on 4.10.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Tauheed Abbas v. The State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 719 of 2017, heard on 4.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Supporting Ocular Account
records.heading: Medical evidence matching the site plan distances supports the ocular account, and panic excludes photographic narration
records.text: Where two witnesses were firm on the roles of the appellants and the doctor's opinion on firearm injuries matched the distances shown in the site plan, medical evidence supported the ocular account. Witnesses in panic cannot be expected to give a photographic narration. Appeals partly allowed and death sentence not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 200; Abdul Aziz, etc. v. The State, etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 547-J, 551-J, 546-J of 2018 & M.R. No. 47 of 2018); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Abdul Aziz, etc. v. The State, etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 547-J, 551-J, 546-J of 2018 & M.R. No. 47 of 2018)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Common Intention: Material Role of Accused
records.heading: Vicarious liability for sentence under common intention depends on the material role of each accused
records.text: Motive plays a vital role in fixing liability where common intention is alleged. Vicarious liability for sentencing is determined by the material role each accused played during the occurrence, as persons react differently in a crime episode and their reflexes cannot be punished. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 200; Abdul Aziz, etc. v. The State, etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 547-J, 551-J, 546-J of 2018 & M.R. No. 47 of 2018); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Abdul Aziz, etc. v. The State, etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 547-J, 551-J, 546-J of 2018 & M.R. No. 47 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Untrustworthy Witness: Dishonest Improvements
records.heading: A witness who makes dishonest improvements on a material aspect is untrustworthy
records.text: A witness who makes dishonest improvements on a material aspect to fill gaps in the prosecution case or align his statement with other evidence is untrustworthy. Delay in postmortem is usually due to incomplete police papers. Appeal accepted, the appellant acquitted, and death sentence not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 222; Muhammad Saleem and another v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 237968 & M.R No. 340 of 2018); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch.; Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Saleem and another v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 237968 & M.R No. 340 of 2018)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: s. 489-F PPC: Meaning of 'or' in Punishment
records.heading: The word or in section 489-F PPC is disjunctive, so a fine alone may be imposed
records.text: The word 'or' in s. 489-F PPC is disjunctive, so the punishments of imprisonment, fine or both are alternatives. A sentence of imprisonment is not mandatory and the Court may impose a fine only. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 228; Rao Ghulam Mustafa v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 41311-B of 2022, decided on 14.9.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Rao Ghulam Mustafa v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 41311-B of 2022, decided on 14.9.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 161 CrPC: Oral Examination and Written Record
records.heading: Section 161 CrPC allows oral examination, but once recorded in writing each statement needs a separate record
records.text: Under s. 161 CrPC a witness may be examined orally, and reducing the statement into writing is optional, but once it is reduced into writing a separate record of each statement must be made. The use of 'may' and 'shall' in s. 161(3) is meaningful. Appeals dismissed with modification and death sentence not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 232; Imran and others v. The State (Crl. A. Nos. 1065-J, 691 & M.R. No. 96/2019, heard on 28.9.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Imran and others v. The State (Crl. A. Nos. 1065-J, 691 & M.R. No. 96/2019, heard on 28.9.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 10 CPC: Exclusive Jurisdiction Clause
records.heading: Parties may by agreement choose a court that has territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction
records.text: Parties cannot confer jurisdiction on a Court that has none, but they may by agreement choose a Court having territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction. Clause 25 of the agreement signed at Lahore was binding. The application under O. VII R. 10 CPC was allowed and the plaint returned for filing in the civil Court at Lahore. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 55; Eden Builders (Pvt) Limited, Lahore v. Muhammad Aslam and others (C.M.A. No. 12587/2021 in/and C.P. No. 5925 of 2021, decided on 13.9.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Eden Builders (Pvt) Limited, Lahore v. Muhammad Aslam and others (C.M.A. No. 12587/2021 in/and C.P. No. 5925 of 2021, decided on 13.9.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail to Woman: Abetment and CDR
records.heading: Bail granted to a woman implicated by supplementary statement where the ingredients of abetment were missing
records.text: A 50 year old woman not named in the crime report and implicated through a supplementary statement was granted bail, as no date, time or place of the alleged conspiracy was given and the ingredients of s. 107 PPC were missing. There was no evidence the phone or SIM was hers, and the CDR alone did not advance the prosecution case. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 42; Shameem Bibi v. The State and others (Crl. P. No. 982-L of 2022, decided on 22.9.2022); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Shameem Bibi v. The State and others (Crl. P. No. 982-L of 2022, decided on 22.9.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail After Cancellation: Office Objection
records.heading: The office bar in Rule 8 does not apply to recall of pre-arrest bail granted by the trial Court
records.text: The bar in R. 8 applies only where an order of imprisonment or fine is challenged, and here the matter concerned recall of pre-arrest bail granted by the trial Court. The applicants were willing to surrender before the Supreme Court, so the office objection was overruled and the office directed to entertain and fix the bail petition. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 47; Atif Ali and others v. Abdul Basit and another (Crl. Misc. A. No. 30 of 2022 in Crl. P. No. Nil of 2022, decided on 27.9.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Atif Ali and others v. Abdul Basit and another (Crl. Misc. A. No. 30 of 2022 in Crl. P. No. Nil of 2022, decided on 27.9.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NEPRA Fuel Price Adjustment: Improperly Constituted Authority
records.heading: NEPRA demands made by an authority not fully constituted under section 3 were declared illegal and coram non judice
records.text: The demand of Fuel Price Adjustment, Quarter Tariff Adjustment and change of tariff status from industrial to commercial by NEPRA, not constituted fully under s. 3 of the NEPRA Act, 1997, was declared illegal, without lawful authority and coram non judice. Directions were issued to NEPRA and to the Federal Government, including maximum subsidy for domestic consumers up to 500 units a month. Ref: Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (W.P. No. 50725 of 2022, decided on 06.02.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (W.P. No. 50725 of 2022, decided on 06.02.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. V R. 20 CPC: Substituted Service
records.heading: Substituted service under O. V R. 20 CPC requires reason to believe the other side evades service
records.text: O. V R. 20 CPC gives wide freedom as to the mode of substituted service when summons cannot be served personally. The remedy can be used only if the Court is satisfied there is reason to believe that the other side is keeping out of the way to avoid service. Ref: 2023 SCMR 316.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Alternate Remedy and Exhaustion
records.heading: Article 199 cannot bypass an equally efficacious alternate remedy such as a Family Court appeal
records.text: Art. 199 enforces a clear right and cannot be used to bypass an equally efficacious alternate remedy. A constitutional petition against a Family Court decree, instead of an appeal under s. 14 of the Family Courts Act, 1964, was not maintainable, as the High Court must relegate parties to the special forum. Ref: 2023 SCMR 316.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Ubi Jus Ibi Remedium
records.heading: Where there is a right there is a remedy, even where the law seems to give none
records.text: The maxim that where there is a right there is a remedy is an elementary principle of law. A person with a right has a corresponding remedy to sue in Court unless jurisdiction is barred, and the principle can be invoked even where the law seems to give no remedy. Ref: 2023 SCMR 316.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XII R. 6 CPC: Decree on Admission
records.heading: A decree on admission under O. XII R. 6 CPC is discretionary and needs an unambiguous admission
records.text: The Court has a discretionary power under O. XII R. 6 CPC to decree on admissions without determining other questions, but the admission must be unambiguous and unequivocal. Under s. 5(2) of the Service Tribunals Act, 1973 the Tribunal has the powers of a Civil Court, and the post draws an analogy with O. XII R. 6. Ref: 2023 SCMR 354.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Back Benefits: Admission and Approbate and Reprobate
records.heading: Departments that admitted regularisation before the Tribunal cannot resile before the Supreme Court
records.text: The departments admitted before the Service Tribunal that the employees' services were regularised from initial appointment and promised arrears of pay when funds were available. Nothing remained for the Tribunal to decide, and their plea before the Supreme Court was hit by the doctrine of approbate and reprobate. Leave refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 354.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXI CPC: Court Auction and Proclamation
records.heading: Court auctions under O. XXI CPC require proper publicity, including proclamation in a widely circulated newspaper
records.text: The scheme of O. XXI CPC aims at proper publicity so that the best possible price is realised at court auctions. Competitive bidding under Rr. 66 and 67(2) requires at least two potential bidders, and the executing Court should order publication of the proclamation in at least one widely circulated daily newspaper. Ref: 2023 SCMR 374.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Definition of Public Servant: ss. 21 and 161 PPC
records.heading: The definition of public servant in sections 21 and 161 PPC confers no civil status
records.text: The definition of public servant in s. 21 PPC, and the extended definition in the Explanation to s. 161 PPC, apply only for the substantive criminal law and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. They do not confer any civil status, capacity or position on the persons covered. Ref: 2023 SCMR 301.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Equality in Appointment: Eligibility Criteria
records.heading: A candidate must meet eligibility criteria and cannot claim equality with another who was wrongly allowed
records.text: Under Arts. 4, 5 and 25 of the Constitution, an unlawful act cannot be made a standard for enforcing the right to equality. A candidate must meet the eligibility criteria in the relevant law and cannot be excused because another person who did not meet them was allowed to compete or was appointed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 394.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: False Affidavit on Foreign Nationality: Undertaking to Resign
records.heading: A parliamentarian who filed a false foreign nationality affidavit was bound to resign immediately
records.text: A parliamentarian admitted that his nomination affidavit wrongly claimed renunciation of foreign nationality, which was disqualifying under Art. 63(1)(c), and undertook to resign from the Senate. The Supreme Court held him bound to resign immediately and said he would not be disqualified in a subsequent election on the basis of this matter. Ref: 2023 SCMR 370.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Commission: No Jurisdiction on Pre-Election Disqualification
records.heading: The Election Commission has no jurisdiction over pre-election disqualification of a returned candidate
records.text: Under Art. 218(3) of the Constitution read with s. 8(c) or 9(1) of the Elections Act, 2017, the Election Commission has no jurisdiction to inquire into and decide the pre-election qualification or disqualification of a returned candidate. Ref: 2023 SCMR 370.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Ocular Account and Missing Corroboration at Bail
records.heading: At the bail stage, absence of corroboration cannot discard an ocular account recorded on the day
records.text: At the bail stage, absence of corroboratory evidence cannot discard an ocular account recorded on the day of the occurrence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 308.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Trial Commenced and Misuse
records.heading: Cancellation of bail is not barred merely because trial has begun, and misuse justified recall
records.text: No fixed rule bars cancellation of bail merely because trial has begun, and the question is whether the accused is entitled to bail under s. 497 CrPC on the facts. Where the fatal injury was attributed to the accused, was supported by medical evidence and the accused hampered the trial, bail was recalled. Ref: 2023 SCMR 308.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Opinion of Investigating Officer at Bail Stage
records.heading: The investigating officer's opinion carries persuasive value only if based on strong and concrete material
records.text: The opinion of the investigating officer has persuasive value only if based on strong and concrete material, which the Court must examine. In the absence of material or data, no credit can be given to the opinion as the officer's ipse dixit. Ref: 2023 SCMR 308.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Reasonable Grounds and Standard of Proof at Bail
records.heading: At bail the prosecution must show reasonable grounds that appeal to a reasonable judicial mind
records.text: The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt at all stages, including when deciding bail. Reasonable grounds for believing the accused guilty are those that appeal to a reasonable judicial mind rather than capricious, irrational or illusory ones, and cannot be decided in a vacuum. Ref: 2023 SCMR 364.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: Delayed FIR and Unexplained Narrative
records.heading: A nine day FIR delay and an unexplained narrative made the case one of further inquiry
records.text: Further inquiry must have a nexus with the result of the case and presupposes a tentative assessment creating doubt about involvement. FIR lodged nine days after the incident, with no details of the alleged protest and no villager named, made the case one of further inquiry. Ad interim pre-arrest bail confirmed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 364.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail to Wife Accused of Abetment: Suckling Baby
records.heading: A wife accused of abetment with a suckling baby and no conspiracy details was entitled to bail
records.text: A wife accused of abetting the murder of her husband, implicated by a s. 164 CrPC statement after 15 days, with no date, time or place of conspiracy given and a suckling baby of 17 months, was entitled to bail. The case fell within the first proviso to s. 497(1) and s. 497(2) CrPC. Bail granted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 383; Mst. Asiy v. The State.
records.title: Mst. Asiy v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record: Evidentiary Value
records.heading: Without concrete material, a Call Data Record is not conclusive evidence of guilt
records.text: In the absence of any concrete material, the Call Data Record is not conclusive evidence for ascertaining the guilt or otherwise of an accused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 383; Mst. Asiy v. The State.
records.title: Mst. Asiy v. The State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cross-Versions: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Two versions of an incident bring the case squarely within further inquiry under section 497(2) CrPC
records.text: Where two versions are before the Court, the case falls squarely within further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. The accused's father had lodged an earlier FIR supported by medico-legal certificates, and the complainant lodged the cross-version six days later. Ad interim pre-arrest bail confirmed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 330.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Merits Can Be Touched
records.heading: The merits of the case may be touched upon when deciding pre-arrest bail
records.text: The merits of the case can be touched upon when deciding the extraordinary relief of pre-arrest bail. Ref: 2023 SCMR 330.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Rape Case: Delay and Medical Findings
records.heading: Bail granted in a rape case on unexplained delay, absence of violence marks and no DNA testing
records.text: Bail granted under s. 497(2) CrPC where the alleged rape had no specific date, the delay in lodging the FIR was unexplained, the medical report showed no violence marks, no DNA or semen grouping test was done, and the FSL report showed the video was created about seven months before the FIR. Accused had been in custody a year. Ref: 2023 SCMR 397.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Solitary Statement of Rape Victim
records.heading: In rape cases the victim's statement alone suffices if it appears independent, unbiased and straightforward
records.text: In rape cases the statement of the victim alone is sufficient to prove the charge, on the strict condition that it appears independent, unbiased and straightforward in establishing the accusation. Ref: 2023 SCMR 397.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single doubt suffices, and where two views are possible the one favouring the accused is adopted
records.text: For the accused to receive benefit of doubt, many doubtful circumstances are unnecessary and a single doubt suffices. If two views are possible on the evidence, one of guilt and one of innocence, the view favourable to the accused is to be adopted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 241.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: s. 377 PPC: Sodomy with Minor, Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Benefit of doubt in a section 377 PPC case where reports gave no definite finding of sodomy
records.text: The heinousness of an offence that is not proved to the hilt is no ground to punish. The medical and Forensic Science reports gave no definite finding of sodomy and only said the victim may have been victimised, so they were read in favour of the accused, who received benefit of doubt. Ref: 2023 SCMR 241.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dissolution of Marriage on Ground of Cruelty
records.heading: A wife may obtain dissolution for cruelty under the 1939 Act, and it was wrongly converted into khula
records.text: A wife may sue for dissolution of marriage under s. 2(viii)(a) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 on grounds of physical or mental cruelty, including cruelty at the in-laws' home. The Supreme Court set aside the appellate Court and High Court decisions that converted the dissolution into khula and restored the Family Court judgment. Ref: 2023 SCMR 246; Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Restitution of Conjugal Rights Used as Weapon
records.heading: A husband's claim for restitution of conjugal rights must be in good faith and not defeat maintenance or dower
records.text: When a husband claims restitution of conjugal rights in response to the wife's suit for dissolution, dower, dowry and maintenance, the Court must see whether he sincerely fulfils his obligations. The claim must be made in good faith to reconcile and must not be used to defeat the claim of maintenance or dower. Ref: 2023 SCMR 246; Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ex Debito Justitiae: Rectifying Court's Mistake
records.heading: Every court may rectify its own mistake ex debito justitiae so that no party suffers for it
records.text: Every court may rectify its own judgment ex debito justitiae to prevent abuse of process and patent oversights, and no person should suffer for a Court's mistake. A party prejudiced by a Court's error should be restored to the position he would have had but for the mistake. Ref: 2023 SCMR 334.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Amendment of Statute: Clarificatory Amendment
records.heading: An amendment that is merely explanatory or clarificatory does not change the state of the law
records.text: An amendment of a statutory provision is generally made to change the state of the law, but this does not hold where the amendment is merely explanatory or clarificatory. Ref: 2023 SCMR 279.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Prospective and Retrospective Application of New Law
records.heading: Procedural law applies to pending proceedings, while substantive law affecting rights applies prospectively unless stated
records.text: A new procedural law that does not affect rights or liabilities applies to pending and future proceedings, while a substantive law affecting rights or liabilities applies prospectively unless expressly stated. A rebuttable presumption belongs to the procedural law of evidence and so applies retrospectively. Ref: 2023 SCMR 261.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Special Law Prevails over General Law
records.heading: Where both a special law and a general law apply, the special law prevails
records.text: Where both a special law and a general law apply to a matter, the special law prevails. Ref: 2023 SCMR 273.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Court Must Consider Limitation Suo Motu
records.heading: The Court must consider limitation on its own motion even if no party raises it
records.text: The Court must independently examine limitation and take cognizance of delay even if no party raises it as a defence. Failure to file within the period creates a right in favour of the opposite party. Limitation law bars enforcement after the period and does not create a right where none exists. Ref: 2023 SCMR 291.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Domicile Certificate Preferred over CNIC Address
records.heading: For domicile specific posts, the domicile certificate takes preference over the CNIC address
records.text: For domicile specific posts, the domicile certificate is the parent document for recruitment and is to be given weight and preference over the address on the CNIC. Considering only the CNIC address would cause complications for persons who move temporarily or live in rented houses. Ref: 2023 SCMR 217.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Domicile and Residence Distinguished
records.heading: Authority on the distinction between domicile and residence and how a domicile is acquired
records.text: Authority on the distinction between domicile and residence and the principles governing acquisition of a domicile. Ref: 2023 SCMR 217.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Proof of Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A decree under section 12 requires proof of the agreement through two marginal witnesses and of payment
records.text: For a decree under s. 12 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 the plaintiff must prove the agreement through two marginal witnesses and prove payment of the consideration. Oral evidence of payment that contradicts the agreement must be pleaded and proved by strong, consistent evidence. Contradictory evidence of execution has no weight. Ref: 2023 SCMR 344.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance is Discretionary Relief
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary and may be withheld on just and equitable grounds even if the agreement is proved
records.text: A decree for specific performance of an agreement to sell is discretionary, and the Court may withhold it for just and equitable reasons even if the agreement is proved. Ref: 2023 SCMR 344.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Uncertain Property in Agreement to Sell
records.heading: No decree for specific performance lies where the property in the agreement is uncertain
records.text: When the property in the agreement to sell is not specific, no decree can be passed in view of s. 21 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, and the Court refuses to enforce a contract suffering from uncertainty. Ref: 2023 SCMR 344.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pleadings: Secundum Allegata et Probata
records.heading: A party is bound by its pleadings and no evidence may be led on a fact not pleaded
records.text: A party is bound by its pleadings up to the Supreme Court and can only prove the case it pleaded. Under the rule secundum allegata et probata, no evidence may be led on a fact not specifically pleaded and no evidence outside the pleadings may be considered. Ref: 2023 SCMR 344.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift (Tamleeq): Onus on Beneficiary
records.heading: The beneficiary of a disputed oral gift must prove it with date, place, witnesses and possession
records.text: Where the owner disputes an oral gift, the onus lies on the beneficiary to prove the oral transaction and the mutation, including the date, time, place, witnesses and transfer of possession. The petitioners disclosed none of these and produced no witnesses, so the oral tamleeq was not proved. Ref: Raheela Begum and others v. Nargis Bano and others (C.R. No. 55453 of 2022).
records.title: Raheela Begum and others v. Nargis Bano and others (C.R. No. 55453 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII Rr. 1 to 3 CPC: Withdrawal of Suit
records.heading: Earlier pronouncements on withdrawal of a suit under O. XXIII Rr. 1 to 3 CPC expressed different views
records.text: Authority on O. XXIII Rr. 1 to 3 CPC, which deal with permission to withdraw a suit with liberty to file a fresh one on payment of costs. The post only records that earlier pronouncements expressed different views. Ref: Sh. Sajjad Umer v. Muhammad Din and others (F.A.O. No. 101195 of 2017).
records.title: Sh. Sajjad Umer v. Muhammad Din and others (F.A.O. No. 101195 of 2017)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: Further Cross-Examination and Equality of Arms
records.heading: Further cross-examination in a Family Court is refused where it would offend equality of arms
records.text: Section 11(3) of the Family Courts Act allows further examination of witnesses only to clarify an issue or clear a doubt, and not to fill lacunae in evidence. A further opportunity to cross-examine after proper opportunity was given would offend the principle of equality of arms and Art. 10A of the Constitution, so it was refused. Ref: 2023 LHC 284; Muhammad Zuhaib Ishaq v. SCJ, etc. (W.P. No. 81179 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Zuhaib Ishaq v. SCJ, etc. (W.P. No. 81179 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIV R. 1 CPC: Framing of Issues
records.heading: Failure to frame proper issues after amendment of pleadings offends O. XIV R. 1 CPC
records.text: No evidence beyond the pleadings can be considered. The trial Court did not call for a replication or frame additional issues after amendment of the pleadings, although the objection to maintainability of a suit for partial partition went to the root, so O. XIV R. 1 CPC was not followed. Proper issues are essential, as further proceedings are otherwise meaningless. Ref: 2023 LHC 295; Muhammad Yousaf (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Naila Shaheen and others (R.S.A. No. 129 of 2010).
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Naila Shaheen and others (R.S.A. No. 129 of 2010)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Forest Ordinance 2002: Non Obstante Clause and Climate Change
records.heading: Authority on the non obstante clause, the Forest Ordinance 2002 and climate change; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the construction of a non obstante clause, the object of the Forest Ordinance, 2002 and the need to preserve forests, and climate change and its Islamic dimension. The post gives no holding or outcome. Ref: Shah Zaman Khan v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Chief Secretary Khyber Pakhtunkhwa at Peshawar and others (C.A. 329/2022, decided on 07.02.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Shah Zaman Khan v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Chief Secretary Khyber Pakhtunkhwa at Peshawar and others (C.A. 329/2022, decided on 07.02.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Police Rules R. 12.2(3): Seniority from Confirmation
records.heading: Under Police Rules R. 12.2(3) seniority is reckoned from the date of confirmation
records.text: Under R. 12.2(3) of the Police Rules, 1934, seniority is to be reckoned from the date of confirmation. The judgment also discusses the concept of organizational justice. Ref: Syed Hammad Nabi & others v. Inspector General of Police Punjab, Lahore & others (C.A. 1172/2020); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Syed Hammad Nabi & others v. Inspector General of Police Punjab, Lahore & others (C.A. 1172/2020)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Pesticide Laboratory: PNAC Accreditation
records.heading: Pesticide laboratories must be accredited by PNAC and set up by the Provincial Government, not by rules
records.text: Pesticide laboratories are to be accredited and certified by the Pakistan National Accreditation Council under the Pakistan National Accreditation Council Act, 2017, and the laboratory is set up by the Provincial Government under s. 13 of the Ordinance. Rules can only provide the procedure and cannot establish the laboratory. The concept of reading down a rule is also discussed. Ref: Province of Punjab through Secretary Agriculture Department, Lahore v. Saleem Ijaz, etc (C.P. 1336-L/2021, decided on 06-01-2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Province of Punjab through Secretary Agriculture Department, Lahore v. Saleem Ijaz, etc (C.P. 1336-L/2021, decided on 06-01-2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appellate Jurisdiction: Deference to Trial Court Findings
records.heading: An appellate court normally defers to trial court findings on witness credibility unless erroneous on their face
records.text: The Trial Court is best placed to judge the credibility of witnesses, so the Appellate Court normally defers to findings based on evidence unless they are on their face erroneous. The Appellate Court may reappraise evidence to check that the trial approach was not flawed or perverse. Ref: 2023 SCMR 246; Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Interference with Family Court Findings
records.heading: The High Court may interfere with Family Court findings in writ only for misreading, perversity or glaring legal error
records.text: Appraisal of evidence is primarily for the Trial Court, here the Family Court. In constitutional jurisdiction the High Court may interfere as a corrective measure where findings rest on misreading or non-reading of evidence, are arbitrary or perverse, or show glaring and patent errors of law or abuse of jurisdiction. Ref: 2023 SCMR 246; Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Income Tax Ordinance: ss. 122(5) and 111(1)(d)
records.heading: Authority comparing sections 122(5) and 111(1)(d) of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the comparison and application of s. 122(5) and s. 111(1)(d) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. The post gives no holding. Ref: Commissioner Inland Revenue, Lahore v. Mian Liaqat Ali Proprietor Liaqat Hospital, Lahore (C.P. 648-L/2021); Justice Munib Akhtar.
records.title: Commissioner Inland Revenue, Lahore v. Mian Liaqat Ali Proprietor Liaqat Hospital, Lahore (C.P. 648-L/2021)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: OPS Transfer and Posting: Service Tribunal Jurisdiction
records.heading: Transfer and posting orders against Own Pay and Scale fall within terms of service for Tribunal jurisdiction
records.text: Transfer and posting orders of a civil servant against Own Pay and Scale fall within the terms and conditions of service under s. 9 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974, for the purpose of the jurisdiction of the Punjab Service Tribunal. Ref: 2023 LHC 311; Hafiz Riaz Ahmad and 1 other v. Province of Punjab etc. (WP 6917/23, decided on 06.02.2023); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Hafiz Riaz Ahmad and 1 other v. Province of Punjab etc. (WP 6917/23, decided on 06.02.2023)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Revision Against Appellate Order under s. 39 Arbitration Act
records.heading: An appellate order under section 39 of the Arbitration Act can be challenged by civil revision
records.text: An appellate order under s. 39 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 can be challenged by civil revision under s. 115 CPC. The Act bars a second appeal but has no express bar on revision, and finality given by a special statute does not remove the High Court's revisional power. Ref: 2023 LHC 322; Hajra Bibi (deceased) through LRs etc v. Bashir Ahmed (deceased) through LRs etc (Misc. Writ. 57166/19, decided on 25.01.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Hajra Bibi (deceased) through LRs etc v. Bashir Ahmed (deceased) through LRs etc (Misc. Writ. 57166/19, decided on 25.01.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: SNGPL Gas Supply: ATL and Additional Security
records.heading: SNGPL is not compelled to supply subsidised gas where the consumer is absent from the ATL
records.text: SNGPL is not compelled to continue gas supply or generate subsidised bills where a consumer's name is absent from the ATL. Requiring additional security from the petitioners would operate discriminately, unjustly enrich SNGPL and take away the benefit given by the Government of Pakistan. Ref: 2023 CLC 324.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Decree for Specific Performance Passes No Title
records.heading: A decree for specific performance passes no title until a registered sale deed is executed
records.text: A decree for specific performance passes no title to the decree holder until a registered sale deed is executed in implementation of the decree. Ref: 2023 CLC 252.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pleadings Are Not Evidence: Defendant Not Appearing
records.heading: Pleadings are not evidence, and a defendant who stays out of the witness-box weakens his case
records.text: Pleadings are not a substitute for evidence, and averments carry no weight unless proved or admitted. A written statement of a defendant who was not examined cannot be used, and a defendant who files a written statement but stays out of the witness-box gives a strong basis to discard his case. Ref: 2023 CLC 252.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: s. 4 MFLO 1961: Heirs of Predeceased Daughter
records.heading: Heirs of a predeceased daughter qualify under section 4 MFLO if the propositus died after 1961
records.text: Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 has no retrospective effect, but it only requires that succession open after the Ordinance. As succession opens on the propositus's death, the legal heirs of a predeceased son or daughter qualify even where the child died before 1961, if the propositus died afterwards. Ref: 2023 CLC 355.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Medical Colleges in Punjab: Affiliation with UHS
records.heading: Medical colleges in Punjab must affiliate with UHS Lahore and no federal exemption may override this
records.text: Under s. 37 of the University of Health Sciences Ordinance, 2002, every medical college in Punjab must affiliate with UHS Lahore before starting educational activities. The Federal Government or its authorities have no jurisdiction to grant exemption, a No Objection Certificate or a notification contrary to this requirement. Ref: University of Health Sciences v. Government of Pakistan etc. (29214-11, decided on 10-02-2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: University of Health Sciences v. Government of Pakistan etc. (29214-11, decided on 10-02-2023)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Companies Ordinance 1984: Inspection and Investigation
records.heading: Authority on the difference between inspection and investigation under the Companies Ordinance 1984; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the difference between the power of inspection and the power of investigation under the Companies Ordinance, 1984. The post gives no holding. Ref: Saif Power Limited, Islamabad v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law, Islamabad and others (C.P. 3263/2022); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Saif Power Limited, Islamabad v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law, Islamabad and others (C.P. 3263/2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Function Test and Statutory Rules of Service
records.heading: Employees may file a service writ under Article 199 only where their service is governed by statutory rules
records.text: Whether an organisation is a person under Art. 199(5) is decided by the function test. Employees of bodies performing functions for the federation, a province or a local authority may file a writ in service matters only if their service is governed by statutory rules, and not where it is governed by internal regulations or instructions. Ref: Bashir Ali Shahzad v. The Bank of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 10403 of 2019).
records.title: Bashir Ali Shahzad v. The Bank of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 10403 of 2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody and Guardianship of Minor
records.heading: A father's right of custody is subordinate to the minor's welfare, and a mother cannot be denied custody for lack of resources
records.text: Custody and guardianship are distinct under the Guardians and Wards Act, with the guardian definition in s. 4(2) seemingly including custody. A father remains natural guardian and is legally bound to maintain the minor, but his right of custody is subordinate to the welfare of the minor. A mother cannot be denied custody for lack of resources. Ref: Saima Nazir v. Guardian Judge (IV), Lahore and another (W.P. No.41017 of 2022, decided 03.02.2023).
records.title: Saima Nazir v. Guardian Judge (IV), Lahore and another (W.P. No.41017 of 2022, decided 03.02.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal: Reduction of Penalty and Proportionality
records.heading: Authority on reduction of penalty by the Service Tribunal and proportionality; no further holding stated
records.text: Authority on when and how the Service Tribunal may reduce the penalty imposed on a civil servant, and on the concept of proportionality, especially in cases involving moral turpitude. The post gives no further holding. Ref: Divisional Superintendent Postal Services, D.G. Khan v. Nadeem Raza and another (C.P.3855/2022, decided 17.01.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Divisional Superintendent Postal Services, D.G. Khan v. Nadeem Raza and another (C.P.3855/2022, decided 17.01.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Mandamus for Election Date: 90-Day Rule
records.heading: Whether mandamus lies to announce an election date given the 90 day constitutional requirement
records.text: The question was whether a writ of mandamus under Art. 199 can be issued to announce the date of election. The Court noted that the Constitution mandates 90 days for fixing the date of election of a Provincial Assembly after dissolution, under Arts. 105, 112 and 224(2). It also set out the constitutional role of the Governor. Ref: Munir Ahmad v. The Governor of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No.6118 of 2023, decided 10.02.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Munir Ahmad v. The Governor of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No.6118 of 2023, decided 10.02.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Reference and Criminal Appeal
records.heading: Judgment in a murder reference and criminal appeal heard on 23.01.2023; the post states no holding
records.text: Judgment in a murder reference and the connected criminal appeal, heard on 23.01.2023. The post gives only the case titles and numbers and no holding. Ref: The State v. Bilal Hassan (Murder Reference No.81 of 2019); Bilal Hassan v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.19109 of 2019).
records.title: The State v. Bilal Hassan (Murder Reference No.81 of 2019); Bilal Hassan v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.19109 of 2019)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Removal and Appointment of Punjab Law Officers
records.heading: Removal of the Advocate General Punjab was upheld but appointment of new law officers was partly set aside
records.text: The removal of the Advocate General Punjab and other law officers by notifications dated 24.01.2023 was upheld. The notification of the same date appointing new law officers was set aside to the extent it concerned law officers who had retained their offices in the government headed by Muhammad Hamza Shahbaz Sharif as Chief Minister. Ref: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal etc. v. Province of Punjab through its Secretary, Law & Parliamentary Affairs etc. (W.P. No. 5324-2023, decided 14.02.2023).
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal etc. v. Province of Punjab through its Secretary, Law & Parliamentary Affairs etc. (W.P. No. 5324-2023, decided 14.02.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Limits of Constitutional Jurisdiction over Executive Policy
records.heading: Courts in constitutional jurisdiction must not encroach on the executive domain absent a rights violation
records.text: Courts exercising constitutional jurisdiction must act with fairness, reasonableness and proportionality and must not encroach on the executive domain absent violation of fundamental rights or excess of legal limits. The High Court wrongly linked non-payment of hydel profits with tariff determination, ignored NEPRA formulae and an alternative remedy, and its findings were held erroneous. Ref: Peshawar Electric Supply v. The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) (Civil Appeals Nos.513 to 586 of 2014, decided 16.01.2023).
records.title: Peshawar Electric Supply v. The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) (Civil Appeals Nos.513 to 586 of 2014, decided 16.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suits for Damages: Governing Law and Jurisdiction
records.heading: The Civil Court may entertain suits for tortious pure economic loss where no law regulates them
records.text: Ss. 73 to 75 of the Contract Act, 1872 govern damages for breach of contract and are inapplicable where the claim does not arise from breach of contract. The Specific Relief Act, 1877 does not define suits for damages. Where no law regulates tortious breaches causing pure economic loss, the Civil Court, as a court of plenary jurisdiction, may entertain and decree such suits. Ref: Pakistan Television Corporation v. Noor Sanat Shah (Civil Appeal No.284 of 2017, decided 16.01.2023).
records.title: Pakistan Television Corporation v. Noor Sanat Shah (Civil Appeal No.284 of 2017, decided 16.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices for conviction
records.text: Trustworthy and confidence inspiring ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices for conviction. Medical evidence and recovery are corroborative. Minor discrepancies between medical and ocular accounts do not damage the prosecution case, as witnesses cannot give an exact picture of injuries. A positive forensic report on the weapon and empties was also noted. Ref: Aman Ullah; Riaz Hussain v. The State etc (Jail Petition No. 883 of 2017 and Criminal Petition No. 1793-L of 2017, decided 07.02.2023).
records.title: Aman Ullah; Riaz Hussain v. The State etc (Jail Petition No. 883 of 2017 and Criminal Petition No. 1793-L of 2017, decided 07.02.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Delay in FIR and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Unexplained FIR delay of two days and a counter FIR made the case one of further inquiry
records.text: FIR lodged after unexplained delay of two days indicates deliberation and consultation. Medical evidence prima facie supported the accused version and the injuries fell under ss. 337-F(iii) and 337-A(i) PPC. A counter FIR existed. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC as one of further inquiry into guilt, since liberty cannot be curtailed on bald allegations. Ref: Gul Muhammad v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1557 of 2022, decided 09.02.2023).
records.title: Gul Muhammad v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1557 of 2022, decided 09.02.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Delay of Five Days and Wider Net
records.heading: An unexplained five day FIR delay and a wider net of co-accused made the case one of further inquiry
records.text: FIR lodged after an unexplained delay of five days suggested deliberation and consultation. Co-accused named in the FIR had been granted pre-arrest bail and the possibility of false involvement by throwing a wider net could not be ruled out. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, entitling the petitioner to further inquiry into guilt. Ref: Abdul Rehman @ Muhammad Zeeshan v. The State and others (Criminal Petition No. 1619 of 2022, decided 02.02.2023).
records.title: Abdul Rehman @ Muhammad Zeeshan v. The State and others (Criminal Petition No. 1619 of 2022, decided 02.02.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Abetment: Ingredients under Ss. 107 to 109 PPC
records.heading: Abetment requires active complicity and substantial assistance before the offence, not mere concurrence or negligence
records.text: Abetment under s. 107 PPC requires active complicity before commission of the offence, with substantial assistance to the principal offender. Instigation, engagement with co-accused and intentional aid are the essential ingredients. Concurrence in another's criminal acts without participation, or mere negligence, is not abetment. A single doubt suffices to give the accused its benefit. Ref: Mst. Hajira Bibi @ Seema, Mst. Shaina Hameed and Abdul Qaseem v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 39-K of 2022, Criminal M.A. No. 113-K of 2022 and Criminal Petition No. 613 of 2022, decided 06.02.2023).
records.title: Mst. Hajira Bibi @ Seema, Mst. Shaina Hameed and Abdul Qaseem v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 39-K of 2022, Criminal M.A. No. 113-K of 2022 and Criminal Petition No. 613 of 2022, decided 06.02.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appreciation of Evidence: Prompt FIR and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: An FIR lodged within one hour is not delayed, and a single doubt suffices for benefit of doubt
records.text: Each criminal case turns on its own facts, and motive, time, manner of occurrence and subsequent events must be examined. The FIR was lodged within one hour of the occurrence without inordinate delay. The post restates that for the benefit of doubt it is not necessary to have many doubts, and a single doubt suffices. Ref: Sarfraz and Allah Ditta v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 560 of 2020).
records.title: Sarfraz and Allah Ditta v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 560 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561-A CrPC: Quashment of FIR and Costs
records.heading: Authority on the scope of section 561-A CrPC and costs for vexatious petitions; no further holding stated
records.text: Authority on the scope of s. 561-A CrPC, the grounds for quashment of an FIR, and the justification for imposing costs under Order 28 Rule 3 of the Supreme Court Rules 1980 where petitions are vexatious and frivolous. The post gives no further holding. Ref: F.I.A. thr. Director General, F.I.A. HQ, Islamabad & others v. Syed Hamid Ali Shah & others (C.P.1257/2020, decided 06.02.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: F.I.A. thr. Director General, F.I.A. HQ, Islamabad & others v. Syed Hamid Ali Shah & others (C.P.1257/2020, decided 06.02.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Interim Custody under S. 12 Guardians and Wards Act
records.heading: An appeal lies against an interim custody order under section 12, where the minor's welfare controls
records.text: After insertion of Guardianship in the First Schedule of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964, an appeal lies against an order under s. 12 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. Welfare of the minor controls interim custody under s. 12 as it does under s. 25. A minor aged four should not be deprived of the mother's care at the interim stage.
