Ref: 2023 LHC 434; Ayesha Tahir v. ADJ Lahore etc (Family 36910/22, decided 19.01.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Ayesha Tahir v. ADJ Lahore etc (Family 36910/22, decided 19.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXII CPC: Minors Cannot Be Proceeded Against Ex-Parte
records.heading: Ex parte proceedings against minors without a guardian ad litem contravene O. XXXII R. 3 read with R. 11
records.text: Where minors are sued without a guardian ad litem being appointed, ex-parte proceedings and decree against them contravene O. XXXII R. 3 read with R. 11 CPC. Even if an appointed guardian fails in his duty, the Court must appoint its own official as guardian. The revisional court wrongly reversed the trial court, which had set aside the ex-parte decree. Ref: 2023 LHC 444; Ariba Naeem etc. v. A.D.J RWP etc (Writ Petition-Miscellaneous-Civil Suit 1222-17, decided 08.02.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Ariba Naeem etc. v. A.D.J RWP etc (Writ Petition-Miscellaneous-Civil Suit 1222-17, decided 08.02.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Treatment of Absence Period Does Not Undo Penalty
records.heading: Treatment of the period of absence does not undo a penalty already imposed
records.text: Treatment given to the period of absence from duty after a penalty is imposed has no bearing on the penalty and does not undo it. Unauthorised absence is misconduct, and where a penalty lesser than dismissal or removal is imposed the authority must make an incidental administrative order on how the absence period is treated. Ref: Ijaz Akbar v. The Director General (ext) L & DD, Punjab, Lahore & others (C.P.4835/2019, decided 30.01.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Ijaz Akbar v. The Director General (ext) L & DD, Punjab, Lahore & others (C.P.4835/2019, decided 30.01.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Interpretation of Punitive Law in Favour of Liberty
records.heading: Punitive law is interpreted in favour of liberty unless the statute clearly directs otherwise
records.text: In interpreting punitive law, courts must prefer the interpretation that favours liberty unless the statute clearly directs otherwise. An interpretation curtailing liberty is construed strictly, and where two equal interpretations are possible the one favourable to the accused is adopted. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 169.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Concurrent Running of Sentences in Hardship Cases
records.heading: Sections 35 and 397 CrPC allow concurrent running of sentences, which must be seriously considered in hardship cases
records.text: S. 397 CrPC, besides s. 35, gives the court discretion to direct that sentences from the same or different trials run concurrently, and in hardship cases this must be seriously considered. The petitioner had served over 24 years and total sentences came to 50 years, so the High Court directed concurrent running and allowed the petition. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 169.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 23 ATA: Stage for Determining Jurisdiction
records.heading: A jurisdictional objection under section 23 ATA may be decided at any stage, even in the final judgment
records.text: A jurisdictional objection goes to the authority of the tribunal and must be decided at the earliest. The question of jurisdiction under s. 23 ATA arises after the Anti-Terrorism Court takes cognizance, has no outer limit, and may be decided even at final judgment, after which the case must be transferred to a competent court if no scheduled offence is made out. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 203.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Act of Terrorism: Fear Alone Not Determinant
records.heading: Fear alone does not make an act terrorism, and intent distinguishes private from State sanction
records.text: Cultivation of fear alone does not determine whether an act is terrorism, and intent distinguishes private from State sanction. The ATC order refusing transfer misapplied s. 6 ATA. No offence under ss. 6 and 7 ATA was made out, so the High Court set it aside and under s. 23 transferred the trial to the Sessions Court. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 203.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Role of Judges: Interpreting Law as It Is
records.heading: Judges state what the law is, giving statutory words their meaning from promulgation
records.text: Judges lay down what the law is and not what it ought to be. When giving meaning to statutory words, the court states the meaning attributable to those words from the time the statute was promulgated. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 203.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Certainty of Punishment and Expeditious Disposal
records.heading: Certainty of punishment rather than severity deters crime, and expeditious disposal builds faith in the rule of law
records.text: Certainty of punishment, rather than severity, deters crime, and expeditious disposal of cases by ordinary courts builds public faith in the rule of law. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 203.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Medical Examiner's Opinion Requires Reasons
records.heading: A medical examiner's opinion on fabrication given without reasons has no probative value
records.text: An opinion of a medical examiner on possibility of fabrication, given by ticking yes or no without cogent reasons, has no probative or evidentiary value. Every examiner must give reasons, and space should be provided in the medico-legal certificate. The Court criticised the inadequate qualification of examiners as offending fair trial under Art. 10-A, and disposed of the petition under s. 22-A CrPC with directions. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 222.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Jurisdiction over Nikahnama Terms
records.heading: Only the Family Court can decide matters relating to the terms and conditions of the Nikahnama
records.text: Under s. 5 read with s. 20 of the Family Courts Act, 1964, only the Family Court can decide matters relating to the terms and conditions of the Nikahnama, and the genuineness of a permission letter to contract a second marriage touches those conditions. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 265.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of FIR: Art. 199 and S. 561-A
records.heading: The High Court may quash an FIR under Article 199 or section 561-A, though the power is used sparingly
records.text: The High Court may quash an FIR or pending proceedings under Art. 199 or s. 561-A CrPC, though this inherent power is used sparingly. Subordinate courts may acquit under ss. 265-K and 249-A CrPC, but if they do not, the High Court may intervene, and one need not always approach the trial court first. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 265.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Cancellation and Second FIR
records.heading: Subordinate courts cannot quash an FIR, but a party may file a private complaint after police cancellation
records.text: Subordinate criminal courts cannot quash an FIR, though police may cancel it under the Police Rules, 1934. Under s. 154 CrPC all versions are recorded in the same FIR, and if the first FIR was cancelled the party may file a private complaint or apply for review of the cancellation order. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 265.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Object of FIR: Not Conclusive Evidence
records.heading: An FIR gives information of a cognizable offence and is not conclusive evidence
records.text: An FIR is meant to give information of a cognizable offence and cannot be treated as conclusive evidence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 276.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 249-A CrPC: Acquittal Must Consider Investigation Material
records.heading: On an application under section 249-A CrPC the court must consider investigation material, not the FIR alone
records.text: On an application under s. 249-A CrPC the trial court must consider the material collected during investigation, and exclusive reliance on the FIR is unjust and arbitrary. The High Court set aside the acquittal in a criminal breach of trust case and remanded the application for fresh decision. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 276.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Protective Bail: Nature and Scope
records.heading: Protective bail has no CrPC provision, is limited in purpose and duration and is not pre-arrest bail
records.text: The CrPC has no provision for protective bail, and High Courts grant it under s. 561-A CrPC and Art. 199 without touching the merits. It is limited in purpose and duration, is not pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC, and gives no right to pre-arrest bail when the accused appears before the concerned court. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 290; Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Transitory Bail on Arrival from Abroad
records.heading: The High Court may grant transitory bail under Article 199 to a petitioner returning from abroad to surrender
records.text: Under Art. 199 the High Court has ample power to protect from arrest on arrival a petitioner abroad who wishes to surrender and face pending proceedings. Transitory bail was justified because without it he could remain a fugitive. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 290; Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transitory Remand: Ss. 60, 61 and 167 CrPC
records.heading: Transitory remand is lawful where the arrested person is produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours
records.text: A person arrested must be produced before the Magistrate without unnecessary delay under s. 60 and cannot be detained beyond 24 hours without a Magistrate's order under ss. 61 and 167 CrPC. The petitioner arrested in another jurisdiction was produced within 24 hours and transitory remand was lawful. The petition was dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 305.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC: Second Statement Declined
records.heading: A second statement under section 164 CrPC is allowed only in exceptional circumstances, not mechanically
records.text: The word may in s. 164(1) CrPC makes the Magistrate's power discretionary. Permission to record a second statement cannot be given mechanically and requires exceptional circumstances. The Magistrate rightly declined to record a second statement of the alleged abductee, no coercion or duress being shown, and the petition was dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 316.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Question by Party to Own Witness
records.heading: Permission under Article 150 QSO to question one's own witness is discretionary and not a right
records.text: Under Art. 150 QSO, permission to put questions to one's own witness is in the court's discretion and not a right. It requires showing that the witness equivocates, varies his statement, suppresses the truth or bears animosity. Being unfavourable is not enough to declare a witness hostile. The petition was dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 326.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Transmission of Sample: Chain of Evidence
records.heading: Failure to prove safe transmission of a narcotics sample cuts the chain of evidence and creates doubt
records.text: In a case of 4000 grams of opium under s. 9(c) CNSA, the prosecution did not examine the Head Constable who took the sample to the Chemical Examiner and did not prove safe transmission. This cut the chain of evidence, created serious doubt and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 331.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Delay in Sending Sample and Safe Custody
records.heading: Unexplained delay of nine days in sending a sample, with no proof of safe custody, is fatal
records.text: A delay of about nine days in sending the sample, against the 72 hours under R. 4(2) of the Control of Narcotic Substances (Government Analysts) Rules, 2001, without explanation was fatal. The prosecution also failed to prove safe custody in the malkhana, so the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 331.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Framing of Charge: Purpose
records.heading: A charge gives precise information of the accusation so the accused may focus on the allegations
records.text: A charge is precise information of the specific accusation, telling the accused what the prosecution intends to prove. Its purpose is also to let the accused focus on the allegations to be faced. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 14.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Prompt Post-Mortem
records.heading: An FIR lodged within 15 minutes with full details and a prompt post-mortem rule out false involvement
records.text: An FIR lodged within 15 minutes of the occurrence with full details ruled out false involvement. The post-mortem was also prompt, as the body reached hospital within an hour and the post-mortem was done soon after. The trial court rightly convicted the accused. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 14.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Number of Witnesses: Quality over Quantity
records.heading: The prosecution need not produce every witness, as quality prevails over quantity
records.text: The prosecution is not bound to produce every witness, and quality and not quantity of witnesses prevails in reaching a just decision. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 14.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Natural Presence of Independent Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Independent eye-witnesses living nearby were naturally present despite prior enmity between the parties
records.text: Despite prior enmity between the parties, eye-witnesses proved independent, unrelated to the complainant and living in the vicinity, and their presence at 5:15 p.m. was natural. Cross-examination did not shake their reliability, so conviction was rightly recorded. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 14.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Lapses in Witness Statements
records.heading: Minor lapses are natural where eye-witnesses testify years later because the accused absconded
records.text: Eye-witnesses testified about three years and four months after the occurrence because the accused absconded, so minor lapses were natural. Doubt arising from witness statements must be genuine and not artificial to justify acquittal. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 14.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Forensic Matching Report of Empties
records.heading: A forensic report on matching of empties is corroborative and not conclusive
records.text: A forensic report on matching of empties with recovered pistols is corroborative and not conclusive. Even a negative report would not adversely affect the testimony of two eye-witnesses. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 14.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion as Corroboration of Ocular Account
records.heading: Long unexplained disappearance of the accused may corroborate the ocular account even if absconsion is not formally proved
records.text: Even if absconsion was not proved in accordance with law, the long disappearance of the accused and avoidance of process of justice without explanation could be used as corroboration of the ocular account. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 14.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Plea of Alibi: Timing and Proof
records.heading: A plea of alibi must be taken at the first opportunity and proved by cogent evidence
records.text: A plea of alibi is a special plea that must be taken at the first available opportunity and proved by cogent and concrete evidence. Raising it only after two years and nine months, at arrest, and not producing the person said to be with him, left the plea unsubstantiated. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 14.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: FIR Not Prompt: Registered After Deliberation
records.heading: An FIR contradicted on promptness was found registered after deliberation, weakening the prosecution case
records.text: The claimed promptness of the FIR was contradicted by the application for its registration and the complainant's own cross-examination. The FIR was found to have been registered after due deliberation and consultation, which weakened the prosecution case on benefit of doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Filing Private Complaint
records.heading: A private complaint filed after unexplained delay was treated as filed after deliberation to fill lacunas
records.text: A private complaint filed after an unexplained delay of two months and twenty one days, following dissatisfaction with police investigation, was treated as filed after deliberation to fill lacunas in the FIR. The prosecution could not prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Post-Mortem Creates Doubt
records.heading: Unexplained post-mortem delay of over 13 hours casts serious doubt on the prosecution story
records.text: A post-mortem delay of 13 hours and 45 minutes without explanation cast serious doubt on the prosecution story, as such delay is normally due to consultation and inquiry about culprits in an unwitnessed occurrence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Withholding Best Evidence: Art. 129(g) QSO
records.heading: Withholding natural witnesses without cause leads to an adverse inference under Article 129(g) QSO
records.text: Natural and material witnesses in a thickly populated area, such as the daughter-in-law and shop and hotel workers, were not produced. Though the prosecution need not produce many witnesses, withholding them without cause led to an adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Joint Role of Firing Attributed
records.heading: A joint firing role without showing whose shots hit which part makes the prosecution case highly doubtful
records.text: Where a joint role of firing was attributed to the accused and an absconding co-accused and it was not shown which assailant's shots hit which part of the deceased, the prosecution case became highly doubtful. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light Not Established
records.heading: Without proof of a source of light the witnesses had no occasion to identify the culprits at night
records.text: For an occurrence at 8:15 p.m., the Investigating Officer did not take into possession any source of light and none was produced. Without proof of the source of light the witnesses had no occasion to identify the culprits, and involvement was not free from doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Police Opinion of Innocence in Successive Investigations
records.heading: Police opinion of innocence may be considered if based on cogent material and independent witnesses
records.text: The opinion of the police is not binding on the court but may be considered if based on cogent and convincing material. Two successive investigations found the accused absent from the scene, supported by independent local witnesses, so the opinion was reliable. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Asserted but Not Proved
records.heading: An asserted motive that is not proved may react against the prosecution on a murder charge
records.text: No direct motive was attributed to the accused and the motive incident was not reported to the police, so the trial court rightly disbelieved the motive. Failure to prove an asserted motive may react against a sentence on a murder charge. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 16.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Fair Value Compensation Irrespective of Revenue Classification
records.heading: The landowner must receive the fair value of acquired land irrespective of revenue classification
records.text: The right to compensation in acquisition cases has a constitutional foundation. Revenue classifications are not relevant to compensation, and the landowner must receive the fair value of the acquired land. Ref: Federal Govt. of Pakistan thr. M/o. Defence Rawalpindi and another v. Mst. Zakia Begum and another (C.A.2150/2019); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Federal Govt. of Pakistan thr. M/o. Defence Rawalpindi and another v. Mst. Zakia Begum and another (C.A.2150/2019)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Production and Exhibition of Case Property at Trial
records.heading: Case property must be produced and exhibited at trial under the CrPC, Police Rules and High Court Rules
records.text: The judgment discusses why and under which laws case property must be produced and exhibited at trial, including the Criminal Procedure Code, Narcotics Rules, Police Rules and High Court Rules and Orders. It sets out R. 22.16 of the Police Rules, 1934 on seizure, marking and sealing of case property. Ref: Ahmad Ali and another v. The State (Crl.A.48/2021); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood.
records.title: Ahmad Ali and another v. The State (Crl.A.48/2021)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Delay in Punjab Elections Referred to Chief Justice
records.heading: A two member bench referred the delay in Punjab elections to the Chief Justice
records.text: A two-member bench noted that the Punjab Assembly was dissolved on 14 January, that the Constitution requires elections within 90 days, and that no progress had been made, so delay was a risk. The matter not being directly before it, the bench referred the file to the Chief Justice for appropriate orders. Ref: Ghulam Mehmood Dogar v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Government of Pakistan, Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (C.P.3988/2022, decided 16.02.2023); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan.
records.title: Ghulam Mehmood Dogar v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Government of Pakistan, Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (C.P.3988/2022, decided 16.02.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift by Father to Minor Son: Irrevocable, No Possession Needed
records.heading: A father's gift to his minor son under Muhammadan Law is irrevocable and needs no transfer of possession
records.text: A gift of immovable property by a father to his minor son under Muhammadan Law cannot be revoked, and no transfer of possession is needed for a gift by a father to a minor child or by a guardian to a ward. Ss. 123 and 129 of the Transfer of Property Act do not apply to hiba. A gift between persons within prohibited degrees cannot be revoked. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 395.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Pre-Arrest Bail on Default of Compromise
records.heading: Bail granted on compromise is cancelled where the accused defaults on the agreed balance
records.text: In an s. 489-F PPC case, pre-arrest bail granted on compromise was cancelled because the accused paid part of the amount and defaulted on the balance of Rs.1,400,000. The bail was conditional on performance. Under s. 497(5) CrPC the State, or any person vitally interested, may seek cancellation of wrongly granted bail. Ref: Azeem-ud-Din v. Feroze Khan etc. (Crl. Misc. No.60014/CB/2022, decided 20.01.2023).
records.title: Azeem-ud-Din v. Feroze Khan etc. (Crl. Misc. No.60014/CB/2022, decided 20.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Conversion of Suit and Procedure
records.heading: A plaint alleging a decree obtained by fraud may be treated as an application under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: A plaint alleging a decree obtained by fraud may be treated as an application under s. 12(2) CPC. Framing issues and recording evidence is not mandatory in every case, as s. 12(3) governs the procedure. Limitation for the application is governed by Art. 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908. Ref: 2023 LHC 479; Muhammad Sharif etc v. Muhammad Ramzan etc (Civil Revision 1600864.192-14, decided 13.02.2023); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Muhammad Sharif etc v. Muhammad Ramzan etc (Civil Revision 1600864.192-14, decided 13.02.2023)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Bail of Juvenile as of Right: S. 6 JJSA 2018
records.heading: A juvenile is granted bail as of right under section 6(3) JJSA 2018 save for stated exceptions
records.text: Under s. 6(3) of the Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018 a juvenile accused of a major or minor offence is granted bail as of right, unless release may bring him in association with criminals or expose him to danger. In heinous offences bail may be declined only if he is over 16. S. 6(4) does not overlap s. 6(3). Ref: 2023 LHC 472; Muhammad Manzoor @ Dani v. State etc (Crl. Misc.-Post-arrest Bail 261-B-23, decided 07.02.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Manzoor @ Dani v. State etc (Crl. Misc.-Post-arrest Bail 261-B-23, decided 07.02.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Appeal under S. 70(13) Anti-Dumping Duties Act: Which High Court
records.heading: High Court in section 70(13) of the Anti-Dumping Duties Act means the Islamabad High Court
records.text: The Anti-Dumping Duties Act, 2015 does not define High Court in s. 70(13). Since Islamabad High Court exercises jurisdiction over the Islamabad Capital Territory, the term corresponded to the Islamabad High Court, and the Lahore High Court lacked territorial jurisdiction to examine the decision of the Appellate Tribunal. Ref: 2023 LHC 484; M/S Ashfaq Brothers etc v. Anti-Dumping Appellate Tribunal etc (F.A.O. 74-22, decided 08.02.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: M/S Ashfaq Brothers etc v. Anti-Dumping Appellate Tribunal etc (F.A.O. 74-22, decided 08.02.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Petition: Verification and Notary under Elections Act 2017
records.heading: An election may be questioned only by a candidate's election petition signed and verified as the CPC requires
records.text: Under s. 139 of the Elections Act, 2017 an election may be questioned only by an election petition filed by a candidate. S. 144(4) requires the petition and annexures to be signed and verified as the CPC requires for pleadings. The Court discussed the notary, who is appointed under the Notaries Ordinance, 1961 by the Provincial Government. Ref: 2023 LHC 503; Col.(R) Muhammad Shabir Awan v. Raja Saghir Ahmed etc (Election Petition 1-22, decided 26.01.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Col.(R) Muhammad Shabir Awan v. Raja Saghir Ahmed etc (Election Petition 1-22, decided 26.01.2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tentative Rent Order under S. 17(8) on Denial of Relationship
records.heading: The Rent Controller cannot travel beyond the Act when passing a tentative rent order on denial of relationship
records.text: The Court examined whether the Rent Controller may pass a tentative rent order under s. 17(8) of the Act, 1963 where the relationship of landlord and tenant is denied. The Rent Controller cannot travel beyond the Act, whose object is to regulate matters between landlord and tenant. Ref: 2023 LHC 495; Muhammad Nazeer v. Ch Ghulam Hussain etc (Writ Petition-Miscellaneous-Rent 3843-21, decided 19.01.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Nazeer v. Ch Ghulam Hussain etc (Writ Petition-Miscellaneous-Rent 3843-21, decided 19.01.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Upgradation of Post Distinguished from Promotion
records.heading: Upgradation is a higher pay scale for the same post, differs from promotion and is not a vested right
records.text: Promotion is advancement in rank or grade, whereas upgradation only gives a higher pay scale to relieve stagnation, with the same post and duties. Upgradation is personal to incumbents, is not a vested right, and stems from a policy decision. The Government must show a need for restructuring, reform or service exigency. Ref: 2023 SCMR 418.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Inquiry and Proportionality of Punishment
records.heading: The competent authority decides punishment, and the Tribunal interferes only if it is unreasonable or disproportionate
records.text: Award of punishment belongs to the competent authority, and the Service Tribunal or Court has a secondary role unless the punishment is unreasonable, disproportionate or illegal. Deterrent punishment is justified for gross misconduct. Dismissal was proportionate here, so conversion to compulsory retirement was refused and the petition for leave to appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 407.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Delay in Oath of Newly Elected Chief Minister
records.heading: Delay of 25 days in administering the Chief Minister's oath was against the constitutional scheme
records.text: Under the Constitution, prompt formation of governments is contemplated, and administration of oath by the President, Governor or their nominee is mandatory. Delay of the Chief Minister's oath for 25 days was against the constitutional scheme. The High Court advised the Governor to complete the process, referred to the President's role, and allowed the petition. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 124.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: High Court as Custodian of the Constitution under Art. 199
records.heading: The High Court is custodian of the Constitution under Article 199 and no one is above the law
records.text: The High Court is custodian to protect, observe and defend the Constitution, and is justified in exercising powers under Art. 199 for supremacy of law, as no one, however highly placed, is above the law. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 124.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: No Cash Deposit Condition for Bail Beyond Surety
records.heading: A court may not impose a cash deposit condition on bail beyond a bond and surety
records.text: To ensure attendance the accused submits a bail bond under s. 499 CrPC, and the court may not impose a further condition of depositing money. Default is met by forfeiture under s. 514 CrPC. The High Court condition of depositing Rs.3.5 million had no legal backing and was set aside, while bail on Rs.500,000 with one surety was maintained. Ref: 2023 SCMR 401.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses and Ocular Evidence over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Related witnesses with natural presence may support capital punishment, and ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence
records.text: Mere relationship of witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony if their presence is natural and evidence confidence inspiring, and it can support capital punishment. Ocular evidence preferred over medical evidence suffices alone. Medical evidence is corroborative, and minor discrepancies are immaterial. Ref: Imran Mehmood v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 82 of 2022, decided 13.02.2023).
records.title: Imran Mehmood v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 82 of 2022, decided 13.02.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Suits Involving Children: Procedural Technicalities
records.heading: In family suits involving children, procedural technicalities are resolved in favour of women and children
records.text: A decree of maintenance could be given to a minor daughter not formally named as plaintiff, as her claim was pleaded in the plaint and prayer. In family disputes involving children, procedural convenience must be resolved in favour of women and children, and technicalities of normal procedure are unsuitable. Ref: 2023 SCMR 413.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: High Courts and Constitutional Petitions in Family Cases
records.heading: High Courts should not use Article 199 as a substitute for appeal or revision in family cases
records.text: The Family Courts Act, 1964 gives no second appeal, so the legislature intended finality after the appellate court. The Supreme Court observed that High Courts routinely use Art. 199 as a substitute for appeal or revision, defeating expeditious disposal, and should constitute special Family benches. Ref: 2023 SCMR 413.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: University Barred from Cancelling Degree after Three Years
records.heading: A university cannot cancel a degree three years after the result gazette
records.text: Under Chapter VI of the Calendar of the University of the Punjab 1998, once the result gazette is issued and three years have lapsed, the University is debarred from quashing a student's result card, certificate or degree. Arising in a revision under s. 115 CPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 510; University of Punjab Through Controller Examinations v. Abdul Majeed etc (Civil Revision 78898/21, decided 02.02.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: University of Punjab Through Controller Examinations v. Abdul Majeed etc (Civil Revision 78898/21, decided 02.02.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI R. 1 CPC: Witnesses Outside the List
records.heading: Witnesses outside the Order XVI Rule 1 list need good cause to be called
records.text: Under O. XVI R. 1(2) CPC, as amended by the Lahore High Court, a party cannot call or produce witnesses whose names are not in the list filed under sub-rule (1). The provision is mandatory, and a defaulting party may be allowed only on showing good cause, not as of right or on a bald excuse. Ref: 2023 YLR 431.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Alibi Found Correct in Investigation: Further Inquiry
records.heading: An alibi found correct in investigation makes the case one of further inquiry
records.text: Where the plea of alibi was found correct by the investigating agency, the case is one of further inquiry for post-arrest bail. Courts must exercise extraordinary care in capital cases, make a tentative assessment, and give the benefit of doubt to the accused even at the bail stage. Ref: 2023 YLR Note 9.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Only Statutory Grounds Considered
records.heading: Only the statutory grounds in section 12(2) CPC may be considered on such an application
records.text: Only the grounds mentioned in s. 12(2) CPC may be considered when deciding an application under it, and other merits are irrelevant. Non-impleading of a claimed owner in a suit for possession under s. 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 does not suffice, as such suit lies against the persons who dispossessed the plaintiff. Ref: 2023 YLR 355.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Fair Trial: Opportunity to Lead Evidence in Civil Cases
records.heading: Every party must have a full opportunity to prove its case by evidence
records.text: Every party must be given an open field to prove his stance by evidence, in accordance with the Qanun-e-Shahadat and the CPC, as Art. 10-A guarantees fair trial and due process. Where an out of court settlement is alleged and the respondents stepped back, the petitioner can prove it by leading evidence. Ref: 2023 YLR 452.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Appellate Interference with Trial Discretion
records.heading: An appellate court should not disturb trial court discretion in specific performance without perversity
records.text: In a suit for specific performance of an agreement to sell, the appellate court must consider the evidence of both sides in its entirety. It should not interfere with the trial court's discretion unless exercised perversely, arbitrarily or against judicial principles, and must firmly conclude that the agreement was proved without relying on gaps in the defendant's testimony. Ref: 2023 YLR 309.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Remand under Ss. 167 and 344 CrPC; Case Diaries
records.heading: Physical remand under section 167(3) CrPC requires recorded justification and personally prepared case diaries
records.text: An Investigating Officer cannot have case diaries drafted by subordinates, as that delegates his power. Under s. 167(3) CrPC the Magistrate must record justification for granting physical remand, which was missing here. The post also distinguishes remand to police custody under s. 167 from judicial custody under s. 344. Ref: 2023 YLR 382.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supplementary Statement Not an FIR
records.heading: A supplementary statement is not an FIR and has no basis in the CrPC
records.text: The CrPC has no provision for a supplementary statement, and a supplementary statement cannot be equated with the FIR. Ref: 2023 YLR 382.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Further Investigation Distinguished from Re-investigation
records.heading: Further investigation continues the earlier inquiry, whereas re-investigation starts afresh
records.text: Further investigation is a continuation of the earlier investigation to find more concrete evidence, whereas re-investigation starts afresh. Investigation is the domain of the police, and directing investigation derives from ss. 155, 156, 157, 159 and 202 CrPC. Transfer of investigation requires written reasons. Ref: 2023 YLR 264.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof after De-consolidation of Suits
records.heading: After de-consolidation, plaintiffs must prove their case afresh on the new issues
records.text: After de-consolidation of a suit and framing of fresh issues, plaintiffs bear the onus to prove their case with affirmative, corroborative and trustworthy evidence. Merely tendering a witness statement recorded in another suit is not valid proof, and the issue must be proved afresh. Regular second appeal under s. 100 CPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 517; Mst. Rajan Bibi etc v. Muhammad Saddique etc (Regular Second Appeal 67-13, decided 24.01.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Mst. Rajan Bibi etc v. Muhammad Saddique etc (Regular Second Appeal 67-13, decided 24.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Interrogatories under Order XI CPC
records.heading: Interrogatories under Order XI CPC: authority on meaning and scope, no further holding
records.text: Authority on the meaning and scope of interrogatories under Order XI CPC, arising from an appeal against closing the defendant's right of defence in a defamation suit for damages. The post gives no further holding. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Main Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif (C.P.3436-L/2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Main Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif (C.P.3436-L/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 162 CrPC: Confronting Defence Witness with S. 161 Statement
records.heading: A defence witness cannot be confronted with his section 161 statement beyond section 162 CrPC
records.text: S. 162 CrPC contains an absolute bar on using a s. 161 statement for any purpose other than contradicting the witness as Art. 140 QSO allows, and Art. 140 is controlled by s. 162. The complainant could not confront a defence witness with his s. 161 statement. The High Court maintained the trial court order. Ref: PLD 2013 Lah 8; Muhammad Sarwar v. Muhammad Afzal.
records.title: Muhammad Sarwar v. Muhammad Afzal

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Confronting Hostile Witness with S. 161 Statement
records.heading: A hostile witness cannot be confronted with his section 161 statement by the prosecution
records.text: Under ss. 161 and 162 CrPC, the prosecution cannot be permitted to confront a witness with his s. 161 statement to contradict him, even after he has been declared hostile. Ref: PLD 2013 SC 386.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Waiting List and Legitimate Expectation in Recruitment
records.heading: A waiting list is a contingency reserve and delay in appointments cannot be blamed on the candidate
records.text: A waiting list is a contingency reserve to fill vacancies when selected candidates do not join or leave early. Authorities must complete initial appointments within the validity period. As the process was not completed within 90 days, delay could not be attributed to the petitioner, who had a legitimate expectation, and the authorities were directed to process his case. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 8.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Wilful Absence: No Regular Inquiry Needed; Penalty Modified
records.heading: Admitted absence needs no regular inquiry, but the penalty was reduced to removal from service
records.text: Where absence from duty is admitted, no regular inquiry is needed before a major penalty. For 23 months of absence without leave, the authority's enhancement of the penalty from removal to dismissal was unsustainable, and given length of service the penalty was modified to removal from service. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 69.

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Election Commission Power to Punish for Contempt
records.heading: Election Commission contempt notices challenged: proceedings continue but no final order until decision
records.text: The petitioner challenged contempt notices issued by the Election Commission, arguing that under Arts. 175(2) and 204 only the Supreme Court or High Court may punish contempt and that the notices were issued by the wrong officers. The High Court issued notice and let proceedings continue but barred any final order until the petition is decided. Ref: 2023 CLC 239.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Seniority and Current Charge Postings in LESCO
records.heading: Current charge posting of a junior referred to the Federal Government with directions on rules
records.text: A junior was posted on current charge instead of the petitioner, and the authorities pleaded lack of statutory rules. The matter involved seniority and eligibility, and possible mala fide could not be ruled out. The High Court sent the petition to the Federal Government and directed strict compliance with rules and policy in transfers and postings. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 81.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Good Governance: Discretion Must Be Exercised Lawfully
records.heading: Administrative discretion must be exercised lawfully, fairly, transparently and without bias
records.text: Discretion vested in authorities must be exercised in accordance with law, and in an independent, transparent and unbiased manner. Administrative authorities must act fairly and on a reasonable basis, and unreasonable or arbitrary use of discretion defeats good governance. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 81.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Suit for Specific Performance of Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Suit for specific performance of an agreement to sell: topic only, no holding
records.text: Authority on a suit for specific performance of an agreement to sell. The post gives only the topic and case details and no holding. Ref: Zafar Iqbal v. Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ferozewala & others (C.P.715/2020, decided 17.02.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Zafar Iqbal v. Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ferozewala & others (C.P.715/2020, decided 17.02.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Cipher Inquiry: Executive Domain and Separation of Powers
records.heading: Courts cannot assume executive power over external affairs or order a cipher inquiry
records.text: External affairs fall within the executive authority of the Federation under Art. 97 and the Federal Legislative List, and the then Prime Minister elected not to order an inquiry under the Act. The Court cannot assume executive powers, and Art. 175(3) requires separation of the Judiciary from the Executive. Ref: Zulfiqar Ahmed Bhutta Advocate Supreme Court of Pakistan at Islamabad v. The Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Law & Justice Division, Islamabad (C.M.Appeal 44/2022, decided 22.02.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Zulfiqar Ahmed Bhutta Advocate Supreme Court of Pakistan at Islamabad v. The Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Law & Justice Division, Islamabad (C.M.Appeal 44/2022, decided 22.02.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Suo Motu: Date of Provincial Assembly Elections
records.heading: Suo motu bench constituted on who must appoint the date for provincial assembly elections
records.text: Order under Art. 184(3) constituting a nine-member bench to hear a suo motu case on elections to the Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assemblies. The questions referred concern who holds constitutional responsibility for appointing the election date after dissolution, how and when it is to be discharged, and the duties of the Federation and Province. Ref: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Successive Applications and Review by Appellate Court
records.heading: A litigant cannot raise the same ground through successive applications in execution
records.text: A litigant cannot agitate the same ground through successive applications once an executing court order has been upheld on appeal, as this abuses the process and offends public policy. The appellate court had no jurisdiction to review its earlier order dismissing the claim for alternate value of dowry articles, so the impugned order could not stand. Ref: 2023 LHC 560; Muhammad Abu Sufyan v. Additional District Judge etc (22694/22, decided 06.02.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Abu Sufyan v. Additional District Judge etc (22694/22, decided 06.02.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 408(b) CrPC: Appeal from Magistrate's Sentence
records.heading: A sentence by any class of Magistrate is appealable to the Court of Session in Punjab
records.text: Under s. 408(b) CrPC as amended for Punjab, a sentence passed by any class of Magistrate, including one empowered under s. 30, is appealable to the Court of Session. A direct appeal to the High Court is not maintainable. Ref: PLD 2016 Lah 255, 2013 MLD 1054, 2006 YLR 1718, 2005 PCrLJ 1435.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail to Women Accused: S. 497(1) Proviso
records.heading: A woman accused in a prohibitory clause offence is covered by the first proviso to section 497(1)
records.text: A woman accused charged with an offence within the prohibitory clause, such as s. 302 PPC, falls under the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, so bail is the rule and refusal the exception, as in non-prohibitory offences. Under s. 497(1) the availability of sufficient incriminating material is not a relevant consideration, which distinguishes it from s. 497(2). Ref: Mst. Ghazala v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P. 54/2023, decided 22.02.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Mst. Ghazala v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P. 54/2023, decided 22.02.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Registration and Investigation Duties of Police
records.heading: Police must register an FIR on information of a cognizable offence and investigate impartially
records.text: An FIR under s. 154 CrPC must be registered once information of a cognizable offence is received, and refusal attracts disciplinary proceedings against the officer and his superior. The investigator must collect both inculpatory and exculpatory evidence without preset notions. In rape and sexual violence cases the directions in PLD 2020 Sindh 611 and the Judicial Inquiry Report are to be followed. Ref: Legal Aid Foundation for Victims of Rape and Sexual Assault and others v. Federal Government, etc. (Writ Petition 3555/2019).
records.title: Legal Aid Foundation for Victims of Rape and Sexual Assault and others v. Federal Government, etc. (Writ Petition 3555/2019)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Ingredients and Valid Defence
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC requires proof of its ingredients and is defeated by arranging funds with the bank
records.text: Section 489-F PPC is attracted only if the prosecution proves issuance of the cheque, dishonest intention, issuance to repay a loan or fulfil an obligation, and dishonour on presentation. The accused has a valid defence if he proves he arranged with his bank that the cheque would be honoured. Appeal dismissed as the concurrent findings required no interference. Ref: 2010 SCMR 806; Muhammad Sultan v. The State (Criminal Appeal 233-L of 2009 in Criminal Petition 546-L of 2009, decided 15.12.2009); Justice Khalil-ur-Rehman Ramday; Justice Mahmood Akhtar Shahid Siddiqui; Justice Rahmat Hussain Jafferi.
records.title: Muhammad Sultan v. The State (Criminal Appeal 233-L of 2009 in Criminal Petition 546-L of 2009, decided 15.12.2009)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 539-B CrPC: Local Inspection Cannot Be Delegated
records.heading: Local inspection under section 539-B CrPC is for the trial Judge and cannot be delegated
records.text: Section 539-B CrPC empowers the trial Judge or Magistrate to inspect the place of occurrence after notice to the parties. This power cannot be delegated to a subordinate officer to visit as a Commission, so the appointment of a Magistrate as Commission to test the site plan was improper. Ref: 2016 SCMR 2084.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage: Proof of Genuineness
records.heading: CCTV footage must be proved genuine through the person who prepared it
records.text: Merely producing CCTV footage in court is insufficient to rely on it unless it is proved genuine. The party relying on it must examine the person who prepared the footage from the CCTV system. Ref: 2016 SCMR 2084.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Open Transfer Deed: Vehicle Ownership
records.heading: An open transfer deed does not transfer vehicle ownership and is void after 30 days
records.text: An open transfer deed is not a valid title document and does not transfer ownership of a vehicle under the Ordinance. If the transferee does not apply to the Motor Registering Authority for change of ownership within 30 days of the transaction, the transfer is null and void under s. 32 of the Ordinance. Ref: Muhammad Akram v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 51580/M/2022, decided 18.01.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 51580/M/2022, decided 18.01.2023)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Meaning of Dishonestly in S. 489-F PPC
records.heading: Dishonestly in section 489-F PPC is a state of mind distinct from fraudulently
records.text: Section 489-F PPC uses the word dishonestly, which differs from fraudulently. Dishonesty is a state of mind (mens rea) that the court determines from the course of action adopted, applying subjective and objective tests, with wrongful gain and loss understood under s. 23 PPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 580; Maqbool Ahmed v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal against Acquittal 32-19, decided 08.02.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Maqbool Ahmed v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal against Acquittal 32-19, decided 08.02.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 47 CPC: Executing Court and Ancillary Questions
records.heading: An executing court cannot go behind the decree but must decide ancillary questions under section 47
records.text: An executing court cannot go behind the decree but must decide ancillary questions arising from it under s. 47 CPC. Where the agreement to sell specified only 13 plots, the executing court should have determined which plots were covered and whether the decree was executable. The impugned orders were not sustainable. Ref: 2023 MLD 339.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Father's Reluctance and Welfare
records.heading: Custody of a minor restored to the mother where the father was unable and reluctant to maintain her
records.text: Custody of the minor daughter was restored to the mother, who had raised her since birth, because the father's inability and reluctance to maintain her through inadequate means, lack of interest and irregular payment of meagre maintenance were proved. The lower appellate court had misread the evidence, and the Family Court judgment was restored. Ref: 2023 MLD 218.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Hizanat: Welfare of Minor Overrides Prescribed Principles
records.heading: The welfare of the child overrides the prescribed principles of hizanat
records.text: Welfare of a child is an overarching concept covering material, intellectual, moral and spiritual well-being and is determined on the evidence of each case. The prescribed principles of hizanat can be departed from in the supreme interest of the child, and neither parent has an absolute right to custody. Ref: 2023 MLD 218.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Limited Scope, No Merits Review
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC is limited to fraud, misrepresentation and want of jurisdiction, not merits
records.text: An application under s. 12(2) CPC is limited to fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction, and the court cannot sit in appeal on the merits of the decree. An educated woman who accepted Rs.25 million in a family settlement could not rely on a later rise in property value as fraud. The High Court declined to interfere. Ref: 2023 MLD 201.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 7 MFLO: Powers of Chairman Union Council
records.heading: The Chairman Union Council cannot declare whether a talaq was validly pronounced
records.text: Under s. 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 the Chairman Union Council may only attempt reconciliation and issue a certificate of effectiveness of talaq. He cannot declare whether a talaq was validly pronounced, which is for a court of competent jurisdiction. Ref: 2023 MLD 354.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revision: Interference with Concurrent Findings
records.heading: In revision the High Court disturbs concurrent findings only for misreading or patent violation of law
records.text: The High Court generally does not disturb concurrent findings of the courts below in revision. It must intervene where there is a wrong exercise of jurisdiction tainted by misreading or non-reading of evidence or a patent violation of law apparent on the surface. Ref: 2023 MLD 383.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Setting Aside Ex Parte Proceedings: Liberal Approach
records.heading: Applications to set aside ex parte orders should be considered liberally to allow decision on merits
records.text: Courts should avoid technicalities when deciding an application to set aside an order proceeding ex parte, particularly where nothing material has happened afterwards. Generous consideration should be given so that parties obtain a decision on merits. Ref: 2023 MLD 264.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Service by Publication: O. V Rr. 15 to 19 CPC
records.heading: Mechanical service by publication without compliance with Order V is invalid and voids ex parte proceedings
records.text: Substituted service ordered mechanically, without diligent compliance with O. V Rr. 15 to 19 CPC, a report verified on oath by the process server, recording of his statement, or a court declaration why ordinary service failed, is not lawful or effective. Ex parte proceedings founded on such service cannot stand. Ref: 2023 MLD 264.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 181: Application to Set Aside Ex Parte Proceedings
records.heading: A defendant appearing before final hearing with good cause may be heard despite an Article 181 objection
records.text: Under O. IX R. 7 CPC a defendant who appears before the final hearing and shows good cause may be heard. The objection that the application to set aside ex parte proceedings was time-barred under Art. 181 of the Limitation Act 1908 was held unsustainable. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2023 MLD 264.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Recovery of Dower: Jirga Settlement Not Binding
records.heading: A jirga settlement not approved by a court does not bind the wife in a dower claim
records.text: A respondent relying on an affidavit signed in jirga proceedings had to prove it through at least two marginal witnesses, which he failed to do. A settlement through local intervention not approved by any court does not bind the wife as law. Constitutional petition allowed and the Trial Court decree restored. Ref: 2023 MLD 279.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Forum of Appeal: Value in Plaint
records.heading: The forum of appeal depends on the value of the suit as stated in the plaint
records.text: Under s. 18 of the Punjab Civil Courts Ordinance 1962 the forum of appeal depends on the value of the original suit as stated in the plaint. Where an application under s. 20 of the Arbitration Act 1940 gave no valuation, the amount claimed was merely the disputed sum, so the appeal lay to the District Judge, who was directed to decide it on merits. Ref: 2023 MLD 362.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345 CrPC: Compounding Qatl-i-amd, Minors' Diyat
records.heading: Differential diyat is not payable to minors whose guardian already drew the diyat without objection
records.text: On a compromise under s. 345 CrPC, differential diyat was not payable to minor legal heirs whose guardian had already received the diyat in 2012 and raised no objection, since enhancement of diyat is not a legal right once it has been drawn. The compromise reaffirmed the earlier one. Application accepted, appeal allowed and accused acquitted. Ref: 2023 MLD 395.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Elections to Provincial Assemblies Within 90 Days
records.heading: Provincial Assembly elections must be held within 90 days of dissolution
records.text: Report of the Supreme Court judgment in the suo motu case stating that elections to the Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assemblies must be held within 90 days of dissolution. The Governor announces the date where he dissolved the Assembly, otherwise the President does, and the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was held to have defaulted by not announcing a date. Ref: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023, decided 01.03.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023, decided 01.03.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Transfer of Execution by Family Court: Larger Bench
records.heading: A Family Court has the CPC powers to transfer execution proceedings and execute its decree
records.text: A three-member Larger Bench resolved the conflict between single bench decisions and held that a Family Court has the CPC powers to transfer execution proceedings and execute the decree. Once a decree is executable under s. 13 of the Family Courts Act, the executing court may use any mode of execution under the CPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 590, 2023 CLC 1300; Mst. Amman Gul v. Judge Family Court Rwp etc (Transfer Application (Civil) 31-22, decided 15.02.2023).
records.title: Mst. Amman Gul v. Judge Family Court Rwp etc (Transfer Application (Civil) 31-22, decided 15.02.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 25 Family Courts Act: Transfer of Execution
records.heading: Only the High Court may transfer execution between districts under section 25, later doubted by a Larger Bench
records.text: Under s. 25 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act 1964 only the High Court may transfer a suit, appeal or execution from one district to another, and a Family Court cannot do so itself. The post notes that a three-judge Larger Bench of the same court later took the contrary view. Ref: 2023 LHC 736; Ishrat Bano & 1 Other v. Fateh Muhammad (Objection Case (Civil) 16605, decided 09.02.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Ishrat Bano & 1 Other v. Fateh Muhammad (Objection Case (Civil) 16605, decided 09.02.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Constitution of Benches and Fixation of Cases
records.heading: Constitution of benches and fixation of cases at the Supreme Court: views of two Justices
records.text: Authority on the constitution of benches and the fixation of cases at the Supreme Court, setting out the views of Justice Qazi Faez Isa and Justice Yahya Afridi. Ref: Muhammad Imtiyaz v. Ch. Muhammad Naeem and others (C.P. 3380/2020, decided 01.03.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Muhammad Imtiyaz v. Ch. Muhammad Naeem and others (C.P. 3380/2020, decided 01.03.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Governor Refusing to Administer Oath to Chief Minister
records.heading: Where the Governor refuses to administer the oath, the President may nominate another person under Article 104
records.text: The Governor of the Punjab informed the court through the Advocate General that he would not administer the oath to the newly elected Chief Minister. The High Court directed its order to be sent to the President for exercise of power under Art. 104 to nominate another person to administer the oath, and disposed of the writ petition. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 136; Justice Muhammad Ameer Bhatti.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Commission to Announce Date of Provincial Election
records.heading: The Election Commission must announce the provincial election date within the 90 day period
records.text: The Constitution mandates a 90-day period for elections after dissolution of a Provincial Assembly under Arts. 105, 112 and 224(2). Read with Arts. 218(3), 219(d) and 220, the duty to announce the date falls within the penumbra of these provisions on the ECP, which was directed to announce the Punjab election date after consulting the Governor. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 179.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Election of Chief Minister Punjab
records.heading: The Deputy Speaker was directed to hold the Chief Minister election on the date fixed
records.text: The prayer to shorten the session date was declined, and the Deputy Speaker was directed to hold the Chief Minister election on 16.04.2022 under Art. 130(3) and Rule 20 of the Rules of Procedure, with all concerned acting impartially. The order withdrawing the Deputy Speaker's powers was set aside as contrary to Art. 53(3). Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 193.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII Suit: District Judge May Entrust to ADJ
records.heading: A District Judge may entrust an Order XXXVII suit to an Additional District Judge
records.text: Under Chapter 13, Vol. I of the High Court (Lahore) Rules and Orders a Civil Judge may refer a suit to the District Judge for entrustment to another competent court. The District Judge, as supervisory authority, may entrust an O. XXXVII suit to an Additional District Judge under s. 15 of the Punjab Civil Courts Ordinance 1962 and s. 24 CPC. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 149.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: CPC Applicability in Gas Theft Recovery Suits
records.heading: Failure to file a witness list does not bar evidence in a gas theft recovery suit
records.text: The CPC applies to a suit under s. 6 of the Gas (Theft Control and Recovery) Act 2016 on matters where no special procedure is provided. A list of witnesses is required under O. XVI R. 1 CPC, but failure to file it does not bar a party from producing its own witnesses and documents on the date fixed for evidence. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 139.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 130(7): Governor's Vote of Confidence Orders
records.heading: Challenge to Governor's orders on loss of confidence closed after the vote of confidence
records.text: The Chief Minister challenged the Governor's orders under Art. 130(7) declaring that he lacked majority confidence, and their operation was held in abeyance on his undertaking. After he obtained a vote of confidence the High Court declined to interfere because the petition had borne fruit. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 154.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance Decree: Possession Already with Decree-Holder
records.heading: A decree-holder in possession under a specific performance decree need not execute for possession
records.text: A suit for specific performance is always a suit for possession, so a decree-holder already in possession need not file execution for possession of the land. She may execute for the remaining part on the judgment-debtor's refusal to perform. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 157.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Execution Petitions: Art. 181 and S. 48 CPC
records.heading: The first execution application falls under Article 181 and later ones under section 48 CPC
records.text: The limitation law prescribes no period for execution. After the Law Reforms Ordinance 1972 the first execution application is governed by residuary Art. 181 of the Limitation Act 1908 (three years), and any subsequent application by s. 48 CPC (six years). Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 157.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Sale Deed: Secondary Evidence
records.heading: A sale deed is not proved without the prescribed mode of proof for secondary evidence
records.text: The petitioners failed to prove the admissibility and execution of the sale deed through the prescribed mode of proof for secondary evidence. Ref: 2023 LHC 773; Ghulam Yasin etc v. Hussain Bakhsh etc (Civil Revision 1053-D-04, decided 21.02.2023); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Ghulam Yasin etc v. Hussain Bakhsh etc (Civil Revision 1053-D-04, decided 21.02.2023)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Honorifics Not to Be Used for Courts
records.heading: Honorifics such as honourable should not be used for courts
records.text: Honorifics such as honourable should not be used for courts. Litigants, counsel and Judges should aim for clarity and brevity and avoid appearing obsequious. Ref: Shaukat Ali v. State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan thr. its Chairman and another (C.P. 1743/2020, decided 03.03.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Shaukat Ali v. State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan thr. its Chairman and another (C.P. 1743/2020, decided 03.03.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Consensus Ad Idem and Caveat Emptor
records.heading: Consensus ad idem and the doctrine of caveat emptor in sale and specific performance
records.text: Authority on ss. 42 and 22 of the Specific Relief Act, s. 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, Art. 113 of the Limitation Act 1908 and s. 10 of the Contract Act. It discusses consensus ad idem, meaning a meeting of the minds, and the effect of the doctrine of caveat emptor. Ref: Rao Abdul Rehman v. Muhammad Afzal, etc (C.P. 1133-L/2016, decided 16.01.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Rao Abdul Rehman v. Muhammad Afzal, etc (C.P. 1133-L/2016, decided 16.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Procedural Technicalities Versus Merits
records.heading: Courts prefer decisions on merits over procedural technicalities
records.text: Courts lean towards deciding matters on merits rather than stifling them on procedural formalities. Rules of procedure facilitate enforcement of rights and cannot be used to cause a miscarriage of justice, so securing the ends of justice outweighs strict adherence to them. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 174.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Misjoinder of Parties: Curable Defect
records.heading: Misjoinder of parties is a curable procedural defect that does not affect the merits
records.text: Misjoinder of parties does not affect the merits or the jurisdiction of the court (s. 99 CPC) and is a procedural error curable by striking out the names under O. I R. 10 CPC at any stage, including appeal or revision. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 174.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Authority to Institute Suit Versus Signing and Verifying Plaint
records.heading: Authority to institute a suit is distinct from signing and verifying the plaint
records.text: Presenting a plaint or written statement may be done only by the party in person, a recognised agent or a pleader under O. III R. 1 CPC. O. VI Rr. 14 and 15 and O. XXIX R. 1 govern signing and verification and cannot establish authority to institute or defend. The headnote also lists curability of defects in authority. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 174.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: CPC Procedure Presumed Permissible Unless Prohibited
records.heading: Every procedure is permissible in civil proceedings unless the law prohibits it
records.text: Courts should treat every procedure as permissible until shown to be prohibited by law, rather than as prohibited unless the CPC expressly provides for it. Prohibition cannot be presumed as a general principle. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 211.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Evidence by Video Conference in Civil Cases
records.heading: Evidence in civil cases may be recorded through video conference
records.text: The Urdu header states that evidence in civil cases can be recorded through video conference. The extract considers whether the attendance of witnesses under O. XVIII R. 4 CPC extends to virtual attendance, and refers to Arts. 46, 47 and 71 QSO and ss. 503 and 512 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 211.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Meaning of Judgment: Reasons Required
records.heading: A judgment requires reasons as well as the result
records.text: Pronouncing a judgment means giving the reasons as well as the result. Announcing only the result after hearing, before the grounds are written, is not a judgment or decision. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 241.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Dating of Judgments and Belated Writing
records.heading: A judgment must state its date and litigants should not suffer for belated writing
records.text: Every judgment must state the date when it is written, signed and pronounced, and litigants should not suffer for belated writing or missing dates. The Supreme Court deprecated belated writing, and Judges who do not write judgments within a reasonable time may be guilty of misconduct. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 241.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitration Agreement: Negative Undertaking
records.heading: An arbitration agreement carries a positive duty to arbitrate and a negative undertaking not to sue elsewhere
records.text: An arbitration agreement imposes a positive obligation to proceed with a dispute and also a negative undertaking not to bring claims within its scope in any forum other than arbitration. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 116.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Jirga Limits and Vani/Swara: Art. 8(1)
records.heading: A jirga must act within the law and vani or swara is void under Article 8(1)
records.text: A jirga or panchayat must act within the law and cannot make arbitrary, unjust or illegal decisions or ones contrary to fundamental rights. The custom of vani or swara falls within Art. 8(1) of the Constitution, is void and cannot be practised (see s. 310-A PPC). Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 171.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Gender-Based Violence and Women's Fundamental Rights
records.heading: Gender-based violence impairs the fundamental rights of women and girls to life and dignity
records.text: Gender-based violence impairs the fundamental rights of women and girls, particularly life and dignity. The Constitution guarantees women equal rights and prohibits sex discrimination, and the Principles of Policy require the State to ensure their full participation in national life and protect marriage, family, mother and child. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 171.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Children's Fundamental Rights: Nutrition and Education
records.heading: Provincial departments must legislate or enforce policy on children's nutrition and education
records.text: The Provincial Food and School Education Departments have the mandate under the Second Schedule of the Punjab Government Rules of Business 2011 to make policy or legislation on children's rights to nutritious food, development and education. The petition was disposed of with directions to legislate or enforce existing law, formulate a policy and implement it. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 164.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Attorney-General for Pakistan: Post Cannot Be Vacant
records.heading: The office of Attorney-General for Pakistan cannot be left vacant
records.text: The Attorney-General for Pakistan is a constitutional post that cannot be left vacant. The Constitution does not mention an acting Attorney General, and neither a Deputy nor an Additional Attorney-General is a substitute. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 183.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Supreme Court Rules: Explaining Documents Filed
records.heading: Documents filed in supplemental proceedings must be explained as Order XVIII Rule 1 requires
records.text: An application or concise statement must state the purpose of filing, as Order XVIII R. 1 of the Supreme Court Rules 1980 requires, and this applies to supplemental proceedings. Documents filed through them, other than exhibits or pleadings, must be explained there or in a supporting affidavit. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 209.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Review Petition: Change of Advocate, O. XXVI R. 6 SC Rules
records.heading: A review petition is to be drawn by the original Advocate unless unavoidable circumstances prevent it
records.text: Under O. XXVI R. 6 of the Supreme Court Rules 1980 a review application is to be drawn by the Advocate who appeared at the original hearing. A change of counsel is allowed only where the earlier counsel cannot appear due to unavoidable circumstances, and the practice of changing counsel without justification is condemnable. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 185.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Maintainability of Appeal under Art. 212(3)
records.heading: Maintainability of appeals under Article 212(3): authority on service tribunal jurisdiction
records.text: Authority on the maintainability of appeals under Art. 212(3) of the Constitution. It discusses Art. 212(1)(a), under which Administrative Courts or Tribunals may be created for terms and conditions of persons in the service of Pakistan, including disciplinary matters. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 190.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Direct Petition to Supreme Court Without ICA
records.heading: A direct petition to the Supreme Court without an intra-court appeal is ordinarily not maintainable
records.text: Where an intra-court appeal lies to the High Court under s. 3 of the Law Reforms Ordinance, a petition to the Supreme Court without exhausting it is ordinarily not maintainable, as this is a rule of practice. It is entertained in exceptional cases such as important questions of public importance, constitutional interpretation or fundamental rights, particularly where the objection is raised late. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 207.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F: Cheque Issued as Security for Vani Settlement
records.heading: A cheque given as security for a vani settlement is void and cannot found section 489-F
records.text: A cheque given as security for a compromise requiring a daughter's marriage under the custom of vani or swara had an unlawful consideration and was void under s. 24 of the Contract Act. The respondent could neither sue on it nor invoke s. 489-F PPC. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 171.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody: Poverty Does Not Disqualify Father as Guardian
records.heading: A father is not unfit as guardian merely because he is poor or uneducated
records.text: A father cannot be declared unfit as guardian merely because he is poor or uneducated or because others are better off. The relevant consideration is the bond of love and willingness to care, and appointing another guardian breached ss. 19(b) and 41(1)(e) of the Guardians and Wards Act 1890. The father was declared sole guardian. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 83.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Non-Parent Guardian: Continuing Court Oversight and Test
records.heading: A non-parent guardian needs continuing court review and a parent is displaced only on risk of harm
records.text: Where a Family Court appoints a guardian other than a biological parent, it must keep reviewing the child's welfare, at least annually, and rely on professional assessment of the child's needs. A parent is displaced only on the test in s. 16 of the Islamabad Capital Territory Child Protection Act 2018, namely risk of significant harm, abuse or exploitation, or abandonment. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 83.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: No Suo Motu Jurisdiction of High Court under Art. 199
records.heading: A High Court has no suo motu jurisdiction under Article 199 and cannot fix prices
records.text: A High Court has no suo motu jurisdiction under Art. 199. Fixing prices of dairy and poultry products and policy matters belong to the Executive, and the High Court cannot fix prices or devise a pricing formula. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 236.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Wife Embracing Islam: Marriage During Iddat and Procedure
records.heading: A marriage during iddat after conversion is fasid, and the wife must petition for dissolution
records.text: A marriage contracted during iddat after the wife's conversion was declared fasid, not batil, and she was released from Darul Amman and could marry afresh. A married non-Muslim woman who embraces Islam is to petition the Family Court for dissolution, which summons the husband, offers him Islam and awaits his response until iddat expires. Ref: PLD 2023 Sindh 53.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Filing of Award in Court: S. 14(2) Arbitration Act
records.heading: A dispute over who filed an award is resolved by notice to the arbitrator, not remission
records.text: Where the award was made in the parties' presence and filed in court, but it was disputed whether the arbitrator or the respondent's counsel filed it under s. 14(2) of the Arbitration Act 1940, the dispute could be resolved by notice to the arbitrator seeking clarification. Remitting the award to the arbitrator was not the proper course. Ref: 2021 SCMR 1137.

records.subject: Arbitration
