records.topic: Award Must Be Appraised Before Being Made Rule of Court
records.heading: The court must scrutinise an award for apparent errors before making it Rule of Court
records.text: The court cannot send a matter to an arbitrator for grant of a decree, and even if treated as an irregularity the trial court had to assess the award for apparent errors before making it Rule of the Court. Remand to the trial court was rightly ordered, and leave to appeal was refused. Ref: 2020 SCMR 850.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Award Made Rule of Court on Conceding Statement
records.heading: A decree on an award by conceding statement stands where it was never challenged in his lifetime
records.text: Whether a decree on an award based on a father's conceding statement was fraudulently obtained depended on whether he actually appeared and conceded. He never challenged the decree in his lifetime and a mutation had been effected, so the application under s. 12(2) CPC was rightly dismissed. Ref: 2017 SCMR 385.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 31(1) Arbitration Act: Court for Filing Award
records.heading: Section 31(1) fixes one court for all arbitration matters, with jurisdiction at both work and proceedings places
records.text: Section 31(1) of the Arbitration Act 1940 defines the jurisdiction of the court in which an award is filed, so that one court handles all arbitration matters. Read with s. 2(c), it gave jurisdiction under ss. 14 and 17 to the civil courts at both the place of the work and the place of the proceedings. Ref: PLD 2017 SC 53.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitrator Appointed in Contravention: Ss. 11 and 5
records.heading: An arbitrator appointed in contravention of the Act is not appointed in law
records.text: An arbitrator appointed in contravention of the Arbitration Act 1940 has not been appointed in law. An application to remove him under s. 11, or to revoke his authority under s. 5, is therefore not sustainable. Ref: PLD 2016 SC 121.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Irregular Appointment of Sole Arbitrator: Participation Under Protest
records.heading: Participation under protest before an irregularly appointed arbitrator is not consent
records.text: Participation under protest in proceedings before an irregularly appointed sole arbitrator is not consent, and the party may approach the court to set aside the appointment. An arbitrator not appointed in accordance with the agreement and the Act lacks jurisdiction, so his award cannot be deemed valid. Ref: PLD 2016 SC 121.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 20: Existing Dispute as Prerequisite
records.heading: An existing dispute is a prerequisite for filing an arbitration agreement under section 20
records.text: An existing dispute within the arbitration agreement is a sine qua non for invoking s. 20 of the Arbitration Act 1940, and its absence is sufficient cause under s. 20(4) to decline filing the agreement. A full and final settlement received without a dispute raised may therefore defeat the application. Ref: PLD 2015 SC 154.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 17 Cannot Substitute Ss. 30 and 33
records.heading: Section 17 cannot be used to set aside an award on grounds under sections 30 and 33
records.text: While exercising jurisdiction under s. 17 of the Arbitration Act 1940, an award cannot be set aside on grounds falling under ss. 30 and 33. Section 17 cannot replace those sections or be given overriding effect. Ref: 2014 SCMR 1268.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Objections to Award: No Appellate Review; Pre-Decree Interest
records.heading: A court cannot sit in appeal on an award and pre-decree interest needs agreement, usage, statute or equity
records.text: On objections the court cannot sit as an appellate court on the award or substitute its view, and may set it aside only for an error apparent on its face or misconduct. An arbitrator cannot award interest before the date of decree absent agreement, usage, statute or equity, and s. 34 CPC does not apply. Ref: 2014 SCMR 1268.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Chairman Appointed by Arbitrators Is an Arbitrator
records.heading: A chairman chosen by two arbitrators is an arbitrator and not an umpire
records.text: A chairman selected by two arbitrators is an arbitrator, not an umpire under s. 10 of the Arbitration Act 1940. He may agree with the reasons of one arbitrator without recording independent reasons, as he sat throughout the proceedings. The Arbitration Committee was properly constituted. Ref: PLD 2014 SC 494.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Ss. 30 and 33: Court Not a Court of Appeal
records.heading: On objections to an award the court does not sit in appeal or search for latent errors
records.text: In dealing with objections to an award under ss. 30 and 33 of the Arbitration Act 1940, the court does not sit as a court of appeal and does not search for latent errors in the proceedings or the award. Ref: PLD 2011 SC 506.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Oral Arbitration Agreement Not Recognised
records.heading: Only a written arbitration agreement is recognised under section 2(a) of the Arbitration Act
records.text: Section 2(a) of the Arbitration Act recognises only a written arbitration agreement, so an oral agreement cannot support an application under s. 14 to make an award Rule of the Court. A written agreement need not be signed by both parties if intention to arbitrate is manifest. Both courts below dismissed the application. Ref: PLD 2021 Lah 398.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 34: Conditions for Stay of Legal Proceedings
records.heading: A stay under section 34 requires no step taken after appearance and readiness to arbitrate
records.text: A stay under s. 34 of the Arbitration Act 1940 requires that proceedings were commenced by a party to the agreement over a matter agreed to be referred. The applicant must have taken no step after appearance and have been ready and willing to arbitrate throughout, and the court must find no sufficient reason against referral. Ref: 2021 CLC 965.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Writ Petition Barred by Arbitration Clause
records.heading: An arbitration clause bars a writ petition challenging termination or seeking specific performance
records.text: Where the contract contains an arbitration clause, a writ petition under Art. 199 cannot be used to challenge termination or seek specific performance. The LPG dispute was to be resolved under the agreement, and the constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: 2021 CLC 1992.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Unfiled Award: Interim Relief and Monetary Loss
records.heading: An award not before the court cannot be treated as binding and monetary loss is not irreparable
records.text: An award not before the court cannot be treated as binding on presumptions. The company could have placed it before the court under R. 10, Chap. 4-B, Part B, Vol. I of the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders and sought interim relief there. Monetary loss is not irreparable, and the High Court declined to interfere for concealment of facts. Ref: 2021 CLC 1244.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 20: Principles for Referring Dispute to Arbitration
records.heading: Principles for referring a dispute to arbitration under section 20: authority, no further holding
records.text: Authority on the principles for referring a dispute to arbitration under s. 20 of the Arbitration Act 1940. Ref: 2022 CLC 294.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Plea of Fraud Against Alleged Arbitration Agreement and Award
records.heading: Alleged fraud in an arbitration agreement and award: same-date stamp papers and no dispute noted
records.text: The petitioner alleged that his thumb impressions on blank papers were misused to fabricate the arbitration agreement and award. The court noted that the stamp papers for appointing arbitrators and for the Faisla Salsi bore the same date, and that no dispute could exist over three independently held properties. Ref: 2022 MLD 818.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Supreme Court Interference in Interim Orders of High Court
records.heading: The Supreme Court does not readily interfere with High Court interim orders unless arbitrary or abusive
records.text: The Supreme Court's settled policy is not to readily interfere with interim orders of the High Court, as piecemeal adjudication is undesirable. The exception is interim relief that is arbitrary, unreasonable or an abuse of power resulting in miscarriage of justice. Ref: 2023 SCMR 501.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Interim Orders of High Court: Interference by Supreme Court
records.heading: The Supreme Court normally does not interfere with High Court interim orders
records.text: The Supreme Court normally does not interfere with interim orders of the High Court except in exceptional circumstances. Ref: 2023 SCMR 459.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Leave-Refusing Orders Are Not Binding Precedent
records.heading: A leave-refusing order that decides no question of law is not binding precedent
records.text: A leave-refusing order that decides no question of law and enunciates no principle under Art. 189 is not a binding precedent. It does not endorse the impugned order's statements of law, since a case is authority only for what it decides. Ref: 2023 SCMR 584.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Police Service Disputes: Limited Judicial Interference
records.heading: Service disputes among police officers call for limited judicial interference
records.text: Disputes among police officers should first be resolved by the Inspector General of Police or his representatives. Courts should interfere only in cases of legal interpretation or blatant abuse of the process under the Police Order or Police Rules 1934, so that the force keeps its autonomy and efficiency. Ref: 2023 SCMR 584.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Seniority of Punjab Police Inspectors
records.heading: Seniority of Punjab Police Inspectors is reckoned from date of confirmation, not appointment
records.text: The final seniority list of Inspectors in the Punjab Police is reckoned from the date of confirmation and not from the date of appointment. Ref: 2023 SCMR 584.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Repeated Bail Applications on Same Ground
records.heading: A bail application on the same ground cannot be repeated before the same court
records.text: A further bail application on the same ground cannot be repeated before the same court. If a bail application is withdrawn while the ground subsists, it cannot be taken again. Ref: 2023 SCMR 421.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Lawyers' Strikes and Rights of Accused
records.heading: Lawyers' strikes that postpone trials negate the accused's right to the protection of law
records.text: When advocates strike and trials are postponed, the accused's right to the protection of law is negated, and added incarceration of a detained accused later acquitted harms his liberty. Advocates should not strike for a lesser cause than defending the Constitution in the public interest. Ref: 2023 SCMR 421.

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Jurisdiction Not a Substitute for Execution
records.heading: High Court use of contempt jurisdiction as a substitute for execution is undesirable
records.text: The Supreme Court observed that use of contempt jurisdiction by the High Court as a substitute for execution proceedings is undesirable. Ref: 2023 SCMR 493.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay Not to Be Assumed
records.heading: Condonation of delay cannot be assumed where there is no valid reason for it
records.text: Decisions must be challenged within the prescribed period, and it should not be assumed that delay will be condoned where there is no valid reason for condoning it. Ref: 2023 SCMR 476.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Restoration of Civil Revision: Three Years under Art. 181
records.heading: Restoration of a civil revision dismissed in default is governed by three years under Article 181
records.text: The limitation for restoring a civil revision dismissed in default is three years under Art. 181 of the Limitation Act 1908. The Supreme Court noted that restoration of a suit or appeal has only 30 days and found the logic of the difference unclear. Leave was converted into an appeal and allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 485; Mst. Jameela Bibi (decd) through LRs v. Mst. Fatima Bibi (decd) through LRs (C.P. 3125/2020).
records.title: Mst. Jameela Bibi (decd) through LRs v. Mst. Fatima Bibi (decd) through LRs (C.P. 3125/2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Merits May Be Touched Upon
records.heading: The court may touch upon the merits while granting pre-arrest bail
records.text: While granting pre-arrest bail, the court may touch upon the merits of the case. Ref: 2023 SCMR 581.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Crop Destruction and Pending Civil Suit
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where a pending civil suit suggested false implication in a crop destruction FIR
records.text: Where a civil suit over the land was pending before the FIR for destroying a standing crop, false implication to pressurise the accused could not be ruled out. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, requiring further inquiry. Leave converted into appeal and allowed, and ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 581.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed FIR and Contradicted Sole Eyewitness
records.heading: Unexplained FIR delay and a contradicted sole eyewitness gave the accused the benefit of doubt
records.text: In a s. 302(b) PPC case, an unexplained delay of over five hours in reporting a crime 21 kilometres from the police station showed deliberation. The sole eyewitness account was contradicted by medical evidence and the investigating officer, and the accused's documented stance was overlooked. Benefit of doubt was given, the appeal allowed and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 566.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: A Single Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single doubt is enough for the accused to receive its benefit
records.text: For the accused to receive the benefit of the doubt, many doubtful circumstances are unnecessary. A single doubt entitles him to its benefit. Ref: 2023 SCMR 566.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Heinousness of Offence Not a Ground to Punish
records.heading: The heinousness of an offence not proved to the hilt is no ground to punish
records.text: The mere heinousness of an offence, if not proved to the hilt, is not a ground to punish an accused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 566.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reappraisal of Evidence: Prompt FIR, Ocular Account
records.heading: An FIR lodged two hours after a daylight murder is prompt given the distance to the police station
records.text: In a murder appeal under s. 302(b) PPC, an FIR lodged about two hours after the incident, given the distance to the police station, was not delayed. Daylight occurrence between persons known to each other excluded misidentification, and the eyewitnesses reasonably explained their presence. Conviction sustained and appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 527.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Reliable Ocular Account, FSL Match
records.heading: A prompt FIR, reliable ocular account and matching FSL report sustained a qatl-i-amd conviction
records.text: FIR lodged within about one hour and forty five minutes, given a 20 kilometre distance, was prompt. The ocular account of witnesses resident in the locality was reliable after lengthy cross-examination, and the Forensic Science Laboratory report matched the crime empties with the recovered weapon. Sufficient material existed to sustain the conviction. Ref: 2023 SCMR 596.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Recovery and Quantum of Sentence
records.heading: Crime empties and weapon sent together to the FSL make the recovery doubtful
records.text: Where the crime empties and the weapon were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory together, the recovery was doubtful and rightly disbelieved. As the High Court had already reduced death to imprisonment for life, the Supreme Court found no room for further interference with the sentence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 527.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Established: Death Sentence Reduced
records.heading: An unproved motive may be a mitigating circumstance reducing death to life imprisonment
records.text: If the prosecution alleges a specific motive, it must establish it through cogent and confidence inspiring evidence, failing which the motive may be treated as a mitigating circumstance. Where the real motive related to a servant and the actual motive remained a mystery, the death sentence under s. 302(b) PPC was altered to imprisonment for life. Ref: 2023 SCMR 596.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Prosecution Case
records.heading: Minor discrepancies that do not affect the salient features of the prosecution case are ignored
records.text: Minor discrepancies that do not hamper the salient features of the prosecution case should be ignored, and the accused cannot claim benefit of them. Ref: 2023 SCMR 527.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies: Ring of Truth Test
records.heading: Minor discrepancies are ignored where evidence has a ring of truth, but omissions going to the root help the defence
records.text: Courts should ignore minor discrepancies where the material aspects of the evidence have a ring of truth. The test is whether the witness inspires confidence, though an omission or discrepancy going to the root of the matter benefits the defence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 596.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence
records.text: Where ocular evidence is found trustworthy and confidence inspiring, it is given preference over medical evidence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 596, 2023 SCMR 527, 2023 SCMR 478.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Prosecution Witnesses
records.heading: Mere relationship with the deceased is no ground to discard prosecution witnesses
records.text: Mere relationship of the prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony. Ref: 2023 SCMR 596.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Prompt Report and Corroborated Ocular Account
records.heading: A report thirty minutes after the occurrence is prompt and a corroborated ocular account sustains a capital charge
records.text: A report made thirty minutes after the occurrence, with a six kilometre distance to the police station, was prompt. The daylight ocular account of the complainant and a close relative was natural and corroborated by medical evidence, and with motive sufficed for the capital charge. Leave to appeal was refused and the death sentence maintained. Ref: 2023 SCMR 478.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inconsequential Recovery and Death Sentence
records.heading: Inconsequential weapon recovery is no ground for a lesser sentence where the ocular account is trustworthy
records.text: Where the ocular account is believed to be confidence inspiring and trustworthy, the mere fact that recovery of the weapon is inconsequential is no ground for imposing a lesser penalty than death. Ref: 2023 SCMR 478.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Witness Evidence
records.heading: Trivial discrepancies do not justify rejecting prosecution evidence, but omissions going to the root benefit the defence
records.text: Courts should ignore minor discrepancies where the material aspects of the evidence have a ring of truth. Discrepancies on trivial matters that do not shake the salient features of the prosecution case should not lead to rejection of the evidence, but an omission going to the root of the matter benefits the defence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 478.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Discrepancies Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Casual discrepancies between ocular and medical evidence do not harm the prosecution case
records.text: Casual discrepancies between medical evidence and the ocular version are possible, since witnesses to live firing cannot state the location of shots with exactitude. Immaterial conflict that makes no dent in the prosecution version has no adverse effect on its case. Ref: 2023 SCMR 478.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: A trustworthy ocular account is preferred over medical evidence and alone sustains conviction
records.text: Where the ocular account is trustworthy and confidence inspiring, it is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices to sustain a conviction. Ref: 2023 SCMR 478.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Spur of the Moment: s. 302(b) Altered to s. 302(c)
records.heading: A spur of the moment killing without premeditation falls under section 302(c), not 302(b)
records.text: Where the occurrence took place at the spur of the moment without premeditation, with no repetition of knife blows and no deep rooted enmity, conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was altered to s. 302(c) PPC. Life imprisonment was reduced to fourteen years rigorous imprisonment each, and the petition was converted into an appeal and partly allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 487.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Eyewitness Evidence
records.heading: Minor discrepancies in eyewitness statements from lapse of time give the accused no benefit
records.text: Owing to lapse of memory over time, minor discrepancies in eyewitness statements occur naturally, and the accused cannot claim benefit of them. Ref: 2023 SCMR 487.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Prosecution Witnesses
records.heading: Mere relationship with the deceased is no ground to discard prosecution witnesses
records.text: Mere relationship of the prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony. Ref: 2023 SCMR 487.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness, Willingness, Deposit of Balance
records.heading: Specific performance requires readiness and willingness throughout, and is discretionary
records.text: Specific performance under s. 12 of the Specific Relief Act is discretionary, to be exercised on settled principles and not arbitrarily. The plaintiff must show readiness and willingness to perform from the date the balance consideration became payable until decision of the suit, which is a condition precedent, and deposit of the balance in court is the practice discussed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 555; M/s DW Pakistan Private Limited Lahore v. Begum Anisa Fazl-i-Mahmood and others (C.P. 3989/2022).
records.title: M/s DW Pakistan Private Limited Lahore v. Begum Anisa Fazl-i-Mahmood and others (C.P. 3989/2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Vendee's Cheque for Balance Deposited in Profit Bearing Account
records.heading: A vendee's balance consideration may be deposited in a profit bearing account pending trial
records.text: The vendee tendered a cheque for the balance consideration with a bank statement, and the High Court directed its deposit in a profit bearing account so that either party could take the benefit at the end of trial. No illegality or perversity was found, and leave to appeal was refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 555; M/s DW Pakistan Private Limited Lahore v. Begum Anisa Fazl-i-Mahmood and others (C.P. 3989/2022).
records.title: M/s DW Pakistan Private Limited Lahore v. Begum Anisa Fazl-i-Mahmood and others (C.P. 3989/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Art. 45 Constitution and s. 402-C CrPC
records.heading: The President's power under Article 45 is not restricted by section 402-C CrPC
records.text: The President's authority under Art. 45 of the Constitution is separate from the Code of Criminal Procedure and is not subject to its restrictions. Section 402-C Cr.P.C., insofar as it clogs that authority, is ultra vires the Constitution and of no force. Ref: Mubarik Ali alias Makhan v. Government of the Punjab etc. (W.P. 27557/2021).
records.title: Mubarik Ali alias Makhan v. Government of the Punjab etc. (W.P. 27557/2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Aurat March: Lahore High Court Decision
records.heading: Aurat March: Lahore High Court decision on a writ against the Deputy Commissioner, no holding
records.text: Authority on the Aurat March, decided by the Lahore High Court in a writ petition against the Deputy Commissioner. The post gives no holding. Ref: Khawar Mumtaz etc. v. Deputy Commissioner etc. (W.P. 15163/2023, heard 07.03.2023).
records.title: Khawar Mumtaz etc. v. Deputy Commissioner etc. (W.P. 15163/2023, heard 07.03.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Scope and Application of s. 302(a) and (b) PPC
records.heading: Scope and application of section 302(a) and (b) PPC: authority, no holding
records.text: Authority on the scope and application of s. 302(a) and s. 302(b) PPC, in a criminal appeal with the connected murder reference. The post gives no holding. Ref: Khalid Mehmood v. The State (Crl. A. 253/2019; Murder Reference 16/2019, heard 08.12.2022).
records.title: Khalid Mehmood v. The State (Crl. A. 253/2019; Murder Reference 16/2019, heard 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: PTI Long March: Civil Administration and Police Powers
records.heading: Powers of civil administration and police over the PTI Long March under the Punjab Civil Administration Act
records.text: Decision on the PTI Long March from Liberty Chowk Lahore to Islamabad, examining the powers of the civil administration and police under the Punjab Civil Administration Act 2017 in dealing with law and order, and sit-ins. Ref: 2023 LHC 845; Sheikh Muhammad Hafeez v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (W.P. 3256-22, decided 08.03.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Sheikh Muhammad Hafeez v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (W.P. 3256-22, decided 08.03.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sexual Abuse under ss. 377A and 377B PPC
records.heading: Sexual abuse under sections 377A and 377B PPC: authority, no further holding
records.text: Authority on the offence of sexual abuse under ss. 377A and 377B PPC, with a note on language, sentence range and the doctrine of merger. The post gives no further holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 888; Muhammad Sajid v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 301-21, decided 08.02.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Sajid v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 301-21, decided 08.02.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation in Inheritance Claims
records.heading: Inheritance claims are not free of limitation and the right is forfeited if not asserted in time
records.text: A sweeping statement that no limitation applies to inheritance would amount to rewriting the law of limitation. Public interest requires an end to litigation, and a person disputing the presumption must do so within the period provided by law or forfeit the right. Ref: Mst. Resham Begum (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Kenth etc. (Civil Revision 907/2015, decided 22.02.2023).
records.title: Mst. Resham Begum (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Kenth etc. (Civil Revision 907/2015, decided 22.02.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Local Commission Report Appointed by Consent
records.heading: A party who consented to a local commission cannot later challenge its report
records.text: Under s. 75 and Order XXVI CPC a court may appoint a local commission, and where it was appointed by mutual consent with an undertaking to abide by its findings, the court may decide on its report. A party whose objections were rejected cannot later challenge the report. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 293, 2023 CLC 1846; Abdul Rasheed v. Province of the Punjab etc. (C.R. 237171/2018, heard 16.11.2022); Justice Shujaat Ali Khan.
records.title: Abdul Rasheed v. Province of the Punjab etc. (C.R. 237171/2018, heard 16.11.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: ss. 12, 21(c) and 22
records.heading: Specific performance fails where contract terms cannot be found with reasonable certainty
records.text: A contract whose terms the court cannot find with reasonable certainty cannot be specifically performed (s. 21(c)). Relief under s. 12(b) and (c) is discretionary and available where no standard exists to assess damages or compensation is inadequate, and discretion under s. 22 must be exercised judiciously. Art. 150 gives full faith and credit to public record absent contrary evidence. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 259.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Withdrawal by Advocate, Power of Attorney
records.heading: An engaged advocate binds the party by withdrawing an appeal, and merits grounds fall outside section 12(2)
records.text: An advocate duly engaged binds the party by a statement of withdrawal of an appeal, and the death of the executant of a power of attorney does not end the authority to represent the company. The grounds pertained to merits and fell outside s. 12(2) CPC, so the application to recall the withdrawal was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 249; Adam Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Cane Commissioner Punjab etc. (C.M. 10910/2021/BWP in ICA 4/2019-BWP, decided 13.01.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir; Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Adam Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Cane Commissioner Punjab etc. (C.M. 10910/2021/BWP in ICA 4/2019-BWP, decided 13.01.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Contradictory Order Closing Evidence: Remand
records.heading: A party cannot be blamed for a contradictory order closing evidence, as an act of court prejudices no one
records.text: Where an order closing evidence in a suit for specific performance was contradictory and unclear about what occurred, the party could not be blamed, since an act of court prejudices no one. The appeal under s. 96 CPC was allowed and the case remanded to give the appellants another opportunity to produce evidence. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 234; Manzoor Ahmad etc. v. Khalid Hassan Khan etc. (R.F.A. 7238/2022, heard 10.01.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal; Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Manzoor Ahmad etc. v. Khalid Hassan Khan etc. (R.F.A. 7238/2022, heard 10.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 152 CPC: Correction of Accidental Slip or Omission
records.heading: Section 152 CPC permits correcting accidental omissions of relief from a decree
records.text: A court under s. 152 CPC may correct clerical or arithmetical mistakes and also errors arising from accidental slip or omission. Reliefs of specific performance and perpetual injunction omitted from the decree could be incorporated, and the petition was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 225, 2023 MLD 448; Shabbir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Multan etc. (W.P. 3227/2022, decided 19.01.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Shabbir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Multan etc. (W.P. 3227/2022, decided 19.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Attachment Before Judgment; Doctrine of Limine Control
records.heading: A civil court cannot refer a dispute over immovable property rights to the Anti-Corruption Establishment
records.text: A civil court has no jurisdiction to refer a civil matter on rights in immovable property to the Anti-Corruption Establishment. Finding no infirmity in the concurrent findings, the High Court applied the doctrine of limine control and dismissed the constitutional petition in limine. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 212; Mst. Seema Yousaf etc. v. District Judge etc. (W.P. 20144/2021, decided 19.01.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mst. Seema Yousaf etc. v. District Judge etc. (W.P. 20144/2021, decided 19.01.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Consolidation of Suits by District Judge
records.heading: A District Judge may club a recovery suit with a cancellation suit to avoid conflicting judgments
records.text: A suit for recovery and a suit for cancellation of a pronote were rightly clubbed together by the District Judge, which avoids conflicting judgments on the same subject matter. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 199; Doud Khan v. Muhammad Rashid etc. (C.R. 884/2021, heard 20.01.2022); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Doud Khan v. Muhammad Rashid etc. (C.R. 884/2021, heard 20.01.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Delay in Filing Complaint: s. 22-A(6) CrPC
records.heading: Delay in filing a complaint after a section 22-A(6) application is not by itself fatal
records.text: It is common for an aggrieved person to approach the police, then apply under s. 22-A(6) Cr.P.C., and file a complaint as a last resort. Delay in filing a complaint is not by itself fatal and is judged on the facts of each case. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 329; Muhammad Yar and 4 others v. Ghulam Haider and 2 others (Crl. Rev. 1177/2015, heard 12.04.2022); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Yar and 4 others v. Ghulam Haider and 2 others (Crl. Rev. 1177/2015, heard 12.04.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Standard of Proof
records.heading: The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and cannot rely on preponderance of probability
records.text: In a case under ss. 302(b) and 452 PPC, the prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and cannot discharge that burden by meeting the civil standard of preponderance of probability. Where reasonable doubt remains, the accused receives its benefit as of right, not as a concession. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 299; Liaquat Ali v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 350-J/2015, heard 22.09.2022); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Liaquat Ali v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 350-J/2015, heard 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Evidence Essential for Just Decision
records.heading: Evidence essential to a just decision must be brought on record whichever party it favours
records.text: The criminal justice system is inquisitorial, and evidence essential for a just decision, here comparison of disputed cheque signatures with admitted signatures through the Punjab Forensic Science Agency, must be brought on record whichever party it favours. Revision accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 290; Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court etc. (Crl. Rev. 23556/2022, heard 31.01.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court etc. (Crl. Rev. 23556/2022, heard 31.01.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Suspension of Sentence: s. 426 CrPC
records.heading: Sentence suspended under section 426 CrPC where the investigating officer found the petitioner did not fire
records.text: Sentence was suspended under s. 426 Cr.P.C. in a case under ss. 302/34 PPC, where the investigating officer, relying on USB evidence, stated that the petitioner did not fire, and he had been in custody for one year. Petition allowed on bail bonds of Rs. 1,00,000 until final disposal of the appeal. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 268; Munir Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 530 and Crl. Misc. 1/2022, decided 09.01.2023); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Munir Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 530 and Crl. Misc. 1/2022, decided 09.01.2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Sodomy: Delay in Medical Examination, Negative DNA
records.heading: A four day delay in medical examination with negative DNA reports destroyed the prosecution case
records.text: In an appeal under s. 376-A PPC, the victim's brother was not an eyewitness, and a four day delay in medical examination with negative DNA reports was destructive to the prosecution. The judgment also discusses the legal and evidential burdens. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 244; Muhammad Irfan Haider and 2 others v. The State and another (Crl. A. 344 & 365/2019, heard 13.09.2022); Justice Sohail Nasir.
records.title: Muhammad Irfan Haider and 2 others v. The State and another (Crl. A. 344 & 365/2019, heard 13.09.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Reliable Ocular Account, Life Sentence Upheld
records.heading: A reliable daylight ocular account corroborated by medical evidence upheld a life sentence
records.text: Matter was reported without inordinate delay, the daylight ocular account was reliable and its witnesses explained their presence, and medical evidence corroborated it. Life imprisonment under ss. 302/34 PPC was maintained, petitions were dismissed and leave to appeal refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 55; Muhammad Bashir and another v. The State etc. (J.P. 557/2016 and Crl. P. 1391-L & 1392-L/2016, decided 31.10.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Bashir and another v. The State etc. (J.P. 557/2016 and Crl. P. 1391-L & 1392-L/2016, decided 31.10.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Unexplained Delay in FIR
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed where the FIR was lodged after nine months without explanation
records.text: Post-arrest bail under s. 497 Cr.P.C. was allowed where the FIR was lodged after nine months and sixteen days, the record was silent on when the complainant learned of the petitioner's role, and no recovery was made despite physical remand. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 68; Muhammad Nawaz @ Karo v. The State (Crl. P. 1392/2022, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz @ Karo v. The State (Crl. P. 1392/2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Juvenile Age Sixteen: Bail under s. 6 JJSA 2018
records.heading: An accused aged sixteen at the offence is treated under section 6(3) JJSA 2018 regardless of arrest date
records.text: An accused exactly sixteen at the time of the offence is dealt with under s. 6(3) of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018, treated as accused of a bailable offence for a minor or major offence. The law on the date of commission applies and the date of arrest is immaterial. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 70; Sahib Ullah v. The State through A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl. P. 546/2021, decided 28.06.2021); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Sahib Ullah v. The State through A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl. P. 546/2021, decided 28.06.2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Prompt FIR, Ocular Account, Life Sentence Upheld
records.heading: An FIR two hours after a daylight occurrence was prompt and the life sentence was upheld
records.text: An FIR lodged about two hours after a daylight occurrence was prompt, the witnesses reasonably explained their presence, and the ocular account was reliable and corroborated by medical evidence. The life sentence under s. 302(b)/34 PPC was upheld and the appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 73; Amanullah v. The State and another (Crl. A. 75-L/2021, decided 15.11.2022); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Amanullah v. The State and another (Crl. A. 75-L/2021, decided 15.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Cross-Version and Overt Act
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed in a cross-version case where the complainant's stance was untrue in investigation
records.text: Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 Cr.P.C. was confirmed in a cross-version case where the petitioner's father had lodged the first FIR, the cross-version came six days later, and the complainant's stance was found untrue in investigation. The investigating officer's opinion on the overt act is to be tested after evidence. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 79; Muhammad Umar Waqas Barkat Ali v. The State and another (Crl. P. 352-L/2022, decided 23.11.2022); Justice Ijaz Ul Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Umar Waqas Barkat Ali v. The State and another (Crl. P. 352-L/2022, decided 23.11.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Audio and Video Clips as Documentary Evidence
records.heading: Audio and video clips are documentary evidence in electronic form and need proof by a witness
records.text: Video, tapes and photographs obtained through forensic techniques are documentary evidence in electronic form, so the principles on admissibility of documents apply. Such a clip has a dual character as electronic document and real evidence, and is proved through a witness who recorded or watched it. Art. 139 QSO permits its use to corroborate the complainant and victim. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 320, 2023 PCrLJ 1394; Numan alias Nomi and others v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 364, 380, 382 & 407/2020, heard 19.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Numan alias Nomi and others v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 364, 380, 382 & 407/2020, heard 19.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis and Time of Death
records.heading: Where medical evidence does not confirm the time of occurrence, the prosecution must suffer
records.text: The extract explains rigor mortis as a medical phenomenon and holds that where the time of occurrence is not confirmed by medical evidence, the prosecution must suffer. It also states that a witness who denies admitted facts cannot be termed reliable. Ref: Muhammad Afzal v. The State (Crl. A. 64331-J/2019, heard 06.03.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Afzal v. The State (Crl. A. 64331-J/2019, heard 06.03.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Son Quota Appointment: Concealment of Criminal Case
records.heading: Concealing a criminal case when seeking son quota appointment counts against the candidate despite alleged false FIR
records.text: A respondent seeking appointment under the son quota had concealed his involvement in a criminal case. Even if FIR allegations are admitted to be false, it cannot be said without recording evidence that there was no probability of conviction. Appeal allowed and the Peshawar High Court judgment set aside. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 103; President National Bank of Pakistan and others v. Waqas Ahmed Khan (C.A. 441/2021, decided 16.01.2023); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: President National Bank of Pakistan and others v. Waqas Ahmed Khan (C.A. 441/2021, decided 16.01.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NBP Employees: Statutory Corporation and Art. 199
records.heading: National Bank of Pakistan employees are of a statutory corporation and may invoke Article 199
records.text: The National Bank of Pakistan is a body corporate under s. 3(2) of its Ordinance 1949, and its employees are employees of a statutory corporation, not of the Federal Government. The NBP is amenable to writ jurisdiction under Art. 199, and its employees governed by statutory rules may also invoke it. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 106; Muhammad Naeem v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (C.P. 4294/2019, heard 25.11.2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Naeem v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (C.P. 4294/2019, heard 25.11.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Art. 185(2)(d): Appeal Against Partly Modified Judgment
records.heading: An appellant who accepted a partial modification must seek leave and cannot appeal under Article 185(2)(d)
records.text: An appellant who accepted a modification favouring him and challenged only the part dismissing his appeal could not file an appeal under Art. 185(2)(d) and had to petition for leave to appeal. The appeal was also time barred and was dismissed, as was the connected petition. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 115; Asadullah Khan and another v. Muslim Commercial Bank Ltd. and another (C.A. 8-Q & 11-Q and C.P. 32-Q of 2017, decided 28.07.2022); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Asadullah Khan and another v. Muslim Commercial Bank Ltd. and another (C.A. 8-Q & 11-Q and C.P. 32-Q of 2017, decided 28.07.2022)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Compensation: Commercial Nature of Acquired Land
records.heading: Land in a commercial area is commercial for compensation even without proof of current use
records.text: A landowner has a fundamental right to fair and just compensation for acquired land. Land situated in a commercial area is commercial in nature even without evidence of its use at the time of acquisition, and compensation is determined accordingly. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 121; Malik Tariq Mahmood and others v. Province of Punjab and others (C.A. 914-L/2013, decided 29.11.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Malik Tariq Mahmood and others v. Province of Punjab and others (C.A. 914-L/2013, decided 29.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis: Determining Time of Death
records.heading: Complete rigor mortis indicates a time between death and post mortem of about fourteen hours
records.text: Rigor mortis started two hours after death in September and was complete in twelve hours. As it had completed in the body, the time between death and post mortem might be fourteen hours. Ref: 2012 SCMR 172.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis Belies Time of Occurrence
records.heading: Complete rigor mortis in hot weather contradicted the stated time of occurrence
records.text: Where the occurrence was stated at 10.00 a.m. and autopsy was at 5.00 p.m., complete rigor mortis in hot weather belied the time of assault given in the crime report. Ref: 2019 SCMR 1327.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis Belies Time of Occurrence
records.heading: Rigor mortis in all corpses within a short span contradicted the stated time of occurrence
records.text: Where the occurrence was stated at 2.00 p.m. and autopsies began at 4.30 p.m., rigor mortis in all corpses within so short a span in March meant the occurrence did not appear to have taken place at the time stated in the crime report. Ref: 2019 SCMR 1156.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Revision: Title Only
records.heading: Civil revision heard on 7 February 2023: title only, no holding stated
records.text: Civil revision between M/s Gulistan Group of Companies and Waseem Javed Khand, heard on 07.02.2023. The post states no holding. Ref: M/s Gulistan Group of Companies v. Mr. Waseem Javed Khand (Civil Revision 25850/2022, heard 07.02.2023).
records.title: M/s Gulistan Group of Companies v. Mr. Waseem Javed Khand (Civil Revision 25850/2022, heard 07.02.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marking Document in Cross-Examination Does Not Prove It
records.heading: Marking a document in cross-examination does not dispense with proof of it
records.text: Marking as an exhibit a document referred to in cross-examination is a practice of convenience for locating and identifying it. It does not dispense with proof of execution, contents and genuineness in accordance with the law of evidence unless the witness admits them. Ref: Geeta Marine Services Pvt Ltd v. The State & Another, decided 22.09.2008; Justice A.S. Oka.
records.title: Geeta Marine Services Pvt Ltd v. The State & Another, decided 22.09.2008

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 367 CrPC: Points for Determination and Reasons
records.heading: A judgment must state points for determination and reasons under section 367(1) CrPC
records.text: Under s. 367(1) Cr.P.C. every judgment must state the points for determination, the decision and the reasons. Failure to specify the points is not curable under s. 537, and want of reasons is an illegality that prejudices the accused. Ref: Muhammad Shah v. The State (Crl. A. 124/2021, decided 08.03.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Shah v. The State (Crl. A. 124/2021, decided 08.03.2023)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Interference in Award; Costs for Frivolous Litigation
records.heading: Interference with an arbitrator's award and costs for frivolous litigation: authority, no further holding
records.text: Authority on the scope of interference with the award of an arbitrator and on the imposition of costs for frivolous and vexatious litigation. The post gives no further holding. Ref: National Highway Authority through its Chairman, Islamabad v. M/s Sambu Construction Co. Ltd. Islamabad and others (C.P. 3767/2020, decided 13.02.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: National Highway Authority through its Chairman, Islamabad v. M/s Sambu Construction Co. Ltd. Islamabad and others (C.P. 3767/2020, decided 13.02.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: No Appeal or Revision Against Interim Family Court Order
records.heading: An interim order of the Family Court is not open to appeal, revision or review
records.text: An interim order of the Family Court is not subject to revision, appeal or review, since s. 14(3) of the Family Courts Act 1964 bars them. The High Court declined to interfere with the interim order of the Guardian Judge, final custody being left to the application under s. 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act. Ref: 2023 YLR 497.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Father as Natural Guardian; Grandmother's Custody Application
records.heading: The father is natural guardian and the grandmother's custody application was dismissed
records.text: A maternal grandmother applied for custody of minors who lived with her, and the father contested, asserting she had no standing in his presence. The Guardian Court and appellate court dismissed her application, and the father was held to be natural guardian of the minors. Ref: 2023 YLR 497.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ex-Officio Justice of Peace: Direction to Arrest
records.heading: An Ex-officio Justice of Peace cannot direct police to arrest where there is no police inaction
records.text: In a cross-version case, a direction by the Ex-officio Justice of Peace to arrest the petitioners was set aside as without lawful authority, there being no police inaction and the Justice of Peace having only jurisdiction to direct police to look into the matter. The investigating officer may defer arrest if not satisfied of involvement. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 340.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Not Precondition to Investigation; s. 157 CrPC
records.heading: An FIR is not a precondition to investigation and registration does not oblige arrest
records.text: An FIR is not a condition precedent for police investigation, and even where an FIR is recorded the investigating officer may refuse to investigate under s. 157 Cr.P.C. Registration of an FIR does not oblige the investigating officer to arrest the accused. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 340.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction Petition: Tenancy Requires Premises and Rent
records.heading: A tenancy requires premises and agreed rent, and the ejectment petitioner must prove his own case
records.text: For an eviction petition under the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 to succeed, the ejectment petitioner must establish his own case independently of the respondent's failure to challenge title. Premises and agreed rent are necessary constituents of a tenancy, so where possession was given without fixation of rent there is no tenancy relationship. Ref: 2023 YLR 729.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Remand Not Ordered Where Evidence Sufficient
records.heading: Remand should not be ordered where the appellate court can decide on the evidence
records.text: Remand should not be ordered lightly where the appellate court can decide the case itself. Where issues were framed and evidence led, and the first appellate court upheld the trial court's reasons, there is no case for remand under O. XLI R. 23 CPC. Ref: 2023 YLR 532.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Judgment under s. 2(9) CPC; Appellate Findings
records.heading: A trial court must decide every issue but an appellate court need not record findings issue-wise
records.text: A judgment under s. 2(9) CPC requires a statement of grounds for the decision. A trial court must decide every issue, but an appellate court need not record findings issue-wise and commits no illegality by recording findings on all points raised before it. Ref: 2023 YLR 532.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Declaratory Decree: Pre-Existing Right; Uncertain Oral Agreement
records.heading: A declaratory decree needs a pre-existing denied right, and an uncertain oral agreement is void
records.text: A declaratory decree under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act may be passed only for a pre-existing right that is denied. An alleged oral agreement of 1970 with undetailed particulars was void for uncertainty under s. 29 of the Contract Act and unenforceable under s. 21(c) of the Specific Relief Act. Ref: 2023 YLR 687.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Admissibility and Recording
records.heading: A dying declaration free from tutoring may found a conviction even if its maker does not testify
records.text: A dying declaration is admissible although its maker does not testify, and may found a conviction if free from prompting and tutoring and proved to be made by the deceased. Under Police Rules 1934 it is to be recorded by a Magistrate, or before a gazetted police officer, or otherwise before two or more unconcerned reliable witnesses. Ref: 2023 YLR 585.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Arts. 117 and 122 QSO
records.heading: The burden of proving guilt stays on the prosecution and Article 122 applies only after guilt is proved
records.text: Under Art. 117 QSO the burden of proving guilt lies on the prosecution and does not shift. Art. 122 applies only after the prosecution proves guilt, for facts especially within the accused's knowledge, and an accused cannot be convicted merely for failing to explain how the deceased lost his life. Ref: 2023 YLR 585.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Rule of Consistency: Concession to Co-Accused
records.heading: A concession by the Investigating Officer to a co-accused cannot distinguish between accused persons
records.text: Under the rule of consistency, a concession extended by the Investigating Officer to a co-accused cannot create a distinction between accused persons. Ref: 2023 YLR Note 61.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 336 PPC: Intention to Hurt, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Section 336 PPC requires intention or knowledge of hurt, and its absence makes a case of further inquiry
records.text: An offence under s. 336 PPC requires intention to cause hurt or knowledge that hurt is likely, which was prima facie missing. The petitioner's culpability required determination by the trial court, making the case one of further inquiry. Ref: Muhammad Hamza v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 11382-B/2023, decided 16.03.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Hamza v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 11382-B/2023, decided 16.03.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Where Nikah Performed Without Rukhsati
records.heading: A wife is entitled to maintenance from the date of Nikah without rukhsati or consummation
records.text: Under ss. 5 and 9 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, no condition of rukhsati or consummation is required for maintenance. Where the husband was at fault for not seeking rukhsati and the wife was willing, she is entitled to maintenance from the date of Nikah. Ref: Ahsan Nawaz v. Judge Family Court etc. (W.P. 355/2023, heard 15.03.2023).
records.title: Ahsan Nawaz v. Judge Family Court etc. (W.P. 355/2023, heard 15.03.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Valid Gift: Offer, Acceptance, Delivery; Pleadings
records.heading: A valid gift needs offer, acceptance and delivery, and the plaint must plead them
records.text: The ingredients of a valid gift are offer, acceptance and delivery of possession. A plaint that omits description of the offer and acceptance and the names of witnesses is deficient, since a party cannot lead evidence beyond its pleadings. Ref: 2023 CLC 543.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Award Cancelling Joint Venture and Tenancy Agreements
records.heading: An award cancelling a joint venture and tenancy for material breach was made rule of Court
records.text: An arbitrator rightly appreciated the evidence and found the appellant in material breach of a Joint Venture Agreement, cancelling it and the tenancy agreement, and the award was made rule of the Court. The award was modified in part under s. 24 read with s. 21 of the Arbitration Act 1940, and the connected Appeal 64/2019 was allowed. Ref: 2022 LHC 9025; Shahid Muneer Sattar v. Mst. Mamoona Asad Raza etc. (F.A.O. 59-19, decided 22.12.2022).
records.title: Shahid Muneer Sattar v. Mst. Mamoona Asad Raza etc. (F.A.O. 59-19, decided 22.12.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Remand of Time-Barred Appeal: Writ Maintainable
records.heading: A remand of a clearly time-barred appeal is an error apparent, so a writ is maintainable
records.text: Where the respondent's appeal was clearly time barred and the appellate court remanded without addressing limitation, the remand order is an error apparent on the face of the record, so the constitutional petition is maintainable. Ref: 2023 LHC 975; Beenish v. ADJ etc. (Family 16930/20, decided 01.03.2023).
records.title: Beenish v. ADJ etc. (Family 16930/20, decided 01.03.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Toshakhana Case: Warrants Cancelled, Arrest Restrained
records.heading: Islamabad High Court cancelled warrants and restrained arrest in the Toshakhana case
records.text: Written decision of the Islamabad High Court in the Toshakhana case, cancelling the warrants against Imran Khan and restraining his arrest. The post gives only this description.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Different Criteria
records.heading: The criteria for cancelling bail differ from those for granting it
records.text: The criteria for granting bail and for cancelling it differ. An Additional Sessions Judge had no occasion to recall a well-reasoned bail order of a Magistrate where no club injury was shown. Revision allowed and the bail granting order restored. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 86; Bashir Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. 98/2021, decided 14.02.2022); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Bashir Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. 98/2021, decided 14.02.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Unexplained Delay in FIR, Merits
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed on unexplained FIR delay of two months and bail to a co-accused
records.text: Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 Cr.P.C. was confirmed where the FIR delay of almost two months was unexplained, a co-accused had been granted bail, and the petitioners' side had earlier registered a case against the complainant party. Merits may be touched upon at the pre-arrest stage. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 67; Muhammad Usman Haider etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 3790-B/2022, decided 13.07.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Usman Haider etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 3790-B/2022, decided 13.07.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: s. 489-F PPC, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC falls outside the prohibitory clause, so ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed
records.text: Grounds available in post-arrest bail may be considered for pre-arrest bail, and merits can be touched upon. The s. 489-F PPC offence did not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 Cr.P.C., so ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 64; Farooq Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 4980-B/2022, decided 04.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Farooq Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 4980-B/2022, decided 04.10.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Right to Cross-Examine Prosecution Witnesses
records.heading: The right to cross-examine prosecution witnesses cannot be closed on the day of examination in chief
records.text: Where the trial court closed the right to cross-examine on the day examination in chief was recorded, the High Court allowed the revision with the Deputy Prosecutor General not objecting. One opportunity was granted to cross-examine PW-2 and PW-3 on costs of Rs. 5,000 for each witness. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 63; Muhammad Akram v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. 415/2022, decided 08.11.2022); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. 415/2022, decided 08.11.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Minimum Age of Marriage: Not Against Islam
records.heading: A statutory minimum age of marriage is not against the injunctions of Islam
records.text: Fixing a minimum age for marriage by State legislation, as in s. 2(a) of the Sindh Child Marriages Restraint Act 2013, is not against the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran and Sunnah. Ref: Ali Azhar v. The Province of Sindh and others (Shariat Petition 05-I of 2022, decided 06.03.2023).
records.title: Ali Azhar v. The Province of Sindh and others (Shariat Petition 05-I of 2022, decided 06.03.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Chemical Examiner Report Not Put to Accused
records.heading: Incriminating material not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used against him
records.text: Incriminating material, here the chemical examiner's report, must be put to the accused when examined under s. 342 Cr.P.C. If it is not, it cannot be considered as evidence against him. Ref: Faheem v. The State (Crl. Rev. 03-K/2022, decided 03.02.2023).
records.title: Faheem v. The State (Crl. Rev. 03-K/2022, decided 03.02.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Dishonestly and Fraudulently: ss. 24 and 25 PPC
records.heading: Misappropriation induced by alluring offers is fraudulent and outside criminal breach of trust
records.text: A dishonest act may be done for the doer's own interest causing wrongful loss or gain, while a fraudulent act involves deception against a particular person to deprive him of property. Misappropriation of property induced by alluring offers is fraudulent and falls outside criminal breach of trust. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 487.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report: Complainant's Right of Hearing
records.heading: A complainant must be heard by the Magistrate when police seek cancellation of a case
records.text: A complainant is entitled to be informed and heard by the Magistrate when police seek cancellation of a case, under Arts. 4 and 10A of the Constitution. The Magistrate must apply his mind and examine the police diaries, and a casual, unreasoned order was remanded for fresh decision. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 372.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Investigation After Submission of Challan
records.heading: Transfer or further investigation after submission of the challan is not barred
records.text: No embargo exists on transfer of investigation or on further or fresh investigation after challan is submitted. Under Art. 18A(1) of the Police Order 2002, the District Standing Board's opinion is inclusive and not conclusive, and the District Police Officer must examine the facts and give reasons in writing. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 427.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Adna and Ala Milkiat Abolished; Adverse Possession
records.heading: Adna and Ala Milkiat were abolished in 1964 and adverse possession is repugnant to Islam
records.text: Adna Milkiat, Ala-Milkiat and similar interests were abolished after promulgation of MLR 1964. A claim of adverse possession is repugnant to the injunctions of Islam. Ref: 2023 LHC 998; Muhammad Naseem etc. v. POP etc. (Civil Revision, decided 02.03.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Naseem etc. v. POP etc. (Civil Revision, decided 02.03.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Decree Dissolving Marriage: Executability
records.heading: A khula order subject to return of dower is a decree under section 13 and is executable
records.text: As the Family Courts Act 1964 does not define decree, recourse is had to s. 2(2) CPC. An order dissolving marriage on khula subject to return of dower was a decree under s. 13 of the Act and was executable. Ref: 2023 LHC 992; Muhammad Suqrat v. A.D.J. RWP etc. (W.P. 2827-16, decided 02.03.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Suqrat v. A.D.J. RWP etc. (W.P. 2827-16, decided 02.03.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 365 PPC: Secret Confinement Required
records.heading: Section 365 PPC requires intent to confine the victim secretly and wrongfully
records.text: Section 365 PPC applies only where the abduction is with intent to confine the victim secretly and wrongfully. Where the FIR shows the victim was taken in the complainant's presence, tied and tortured, with police arriving on a call, the offence falls under s. 342 PPC and s. 365 is not attracted. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 468.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Merits May Be Touched
records.heading: The merits may be touched upon while granting pre-arrest bail, as held in Meeran Bux
records.text: Although the merits for pre-arrest and post-arrest bail differ, the Supreme Court has held in Meeran Bux v. The State (PLD 1989 SC 347) that the merits of the case can be touched upon while granting pre-arrest bail. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 468.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: No Limitation for Execution of Family Decree
records.heading: Execution of a family dower decree is not subject to limitation
records.text: Section 13 of the Family Courts Act 1964 provides no limitation for filing an execution petition in family cases. A dower decree may be executed whenever the wife approaches the court, and postponing recovery during the marriage does not bar execution. Family Courts, as trial or executing courts, are governed by equity, justice and fair play, free of CPC technicalities. Ref: Mirza Muhammad Akbar Baig v. Add. District Judge etc. (W.P. No. 6002 of 2022).
records.title: Mirza Muhammad Akbar Baig v. Add. District Judge etc. (W.P. No. 6002 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Entry Suits Are Family Suits
records.heading: A suit challenging a Nikahnama entry is a family suit triable by the Family Court
records.text: Any suit challenging an entry of the Nikahnama, whether instituted before the 2015 amendment of the Family Courts Act and pending, or filed after it, is deemed a family suit. It is to be tried by, or transferred to, the Family Court, or deemed so transferred if already being tried there. Ref: Muhammad Yousaf v. Addl. District Judge, Multan and others (Civil Petition No. 6482 of 2021, decided 08.02.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Addl. District Judge, Multan and others (Civil Petition No. 6482 of 2021, decided 08.02.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Consistency and Merits
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail should not be refused where a similarly placed co-accused has post-arrest bail
records.text: Where a co-accused with a similar role has been granted post-arrest bail, refusing pre-arrest bail on the technical ground that the two stand on different footing would serve little purpose, since the petitioner would obtain post-arrest bail on consistency after arrest. It is established that the merits can be touched upon while granting pre-arrest bail. Ref: Muhammad Imran v. The State etc. (Crl. Petition No. 1212-L of 2022, decided 01.03.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State etc. (Crl. Petition No. 1212-L of 2022, decided 01.03.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Order on Execution Objections Appealable, S. 14
records.heading: An order on objections to execution of a family decree is appealable under section 14
records.text: An order refusing to recall warrants of arrest and deciding the objection petition against execution of a family decree is a decision given under s. 14 of the Family Courts Act 1964 and is appealable. In view of the alternate remedy, the writ petition under Art. 199 was dismissed as premature and not maintainable. Ref: PLJ 2021 Lah 40; Jabran Mustafa v. Judge Family Court etc. (W.P. No. 69574 of 2020, decided 01.01.2021); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Jabran Mustafa v. Judge Family Court etc. (W.P. No. 69574 of 2020, decided 01.01.2021)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation in Female Heirs' Declaratory Suits
records.heading: A female heir's declaratory suit over inherited share is governed by Article 120 with six years
records.text: No specific Article of the Limitation Act 1908 covers a suit under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 for a declaration of ownership, so residuary Art. 120 applies, giving six years from accrual of the right to sue. The rule applies to a female legal heir's suit for a declaration of her share in inherited property. Ref: Saadat Khan and others v. Shahid-ur-Rehman and others (C.P. 262-P/2017, decided 23.09.2021); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Saadat Khan and others v. Shahid-ur-Rehman and others (C.P. 262-P/2017, decided 23.09.2021)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Premature Petition on Holding Elections
records.heading: A petition on holding elections was premature once the schedule had been issued
records.text: Nothing on record showed that the Inspector General of Police or Chief Secretary Punjab was reluctant to hold elections within the time directed, or that the Election Commission was failing to act under Arts. 218 and 220. As the schedule had been issued, the petition was premature and based on apprehensions, and was dismissed. Ref: 2023 LHC 1082; Munir Ahmad v. Province of Punjab etc. (W.P. 18733/23, decided 22.03.2023); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Munir Ahmad v. Province of Punjab etc. (W.P. 18733/23, decided 22.03.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post Mortem
records.heading: An unexplained post-mortem delay of thirty one hours cast doubt on the prosecution case
records.text: An unexplained delay of about thirty one hours in conducting the autopsy suggests the police used the time to procure and plant eye witnesses and prepare a story. Together with the other circumstances, the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 43.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: Presence Not Established
records.heading: Eye witnesses who were chance witnesses failed to establish their presence at the scene
records.text: Both eye witnesses were not residents of the house of occurrence and the site plans did not show their houses nearby. They were chance witnesses who failed to establish their presence at the scene with the reasons they gave. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 43.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Pistol and Cash on Pointation
records.heading: Pistol recovery is inconsequential without a positive forensic report matching the crime empties
records.text: Recovery of a pistol on the accused's pointation was inconsequential without a positive Forensic Science Agency report matching the crime empties with it. Recovery of cash on pointation was, in the peculiar circumstances, not believable. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 43.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of 21 Hours in FIR: Art. 129 QSO
records.heading: An unexplained twenty one hour FIR delay and a withheld witness raise an adverse presumption under Article 129
records.text: The explanation for a twenty one hour delay in lodging the FIR was that the accused locked the eye witnesses in the house and a person freed them next day. The prosecution withheld that material witness, so an adverse presumption under Art. 129 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat 1984 could be drawn. The explanation was disbelieved and the prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 43.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in FIR: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Documentary times contradicting the stated time of reporting left the FIR delay unexplained
records.text: The prosecution claimed the incident was reported soon after it occurred at about 5 or 6 a.m., but the written application and FIR bore times of 9.45 and 10.10 a.m. Documentary evidence contradicted the stated time of reporting and the delay was unexplained. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt, the appeal was allowed and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 402.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Eye Witness
records.heading: Dishonest improvements by an eye witness on matters absent from his section 161 statement create doubt
records.text: An eye witness who made improvements in court on matters not recorded in his s. 161 Cr.P.C. statement, when confronted with it, created doubt about his credibility and truthfulness. It was not safe to rely on the prosecution witnesses. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 402.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: No Justification for Presence
records.heading: Chance witnesses with conflicting reasons for being at the scene cannot be relied upon
records.text: The place of occurrence was a thoroughfare away from the village and the witnesses gave conflicting accounts of why they were there, producing no warabandi record. As chance and interested witnesses, their presence at the scene became doubtful. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 402.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inquest and Post-Mortem Timings: Time of Death
records.heading: Inconsistent inquest and post-mortem timings made the time of death and FIR doubtful
records.text: The inquest report recorded information of death at 8.00 a.m., altered in different ink, and the post-mortem timings suggested death around 7 or 8 a.m. These contradicted the prosecution's account that police reached the scene within 30 to 45 minutes of an incident at 5 or 6 a.m. The time of death and of the incident became doubtful and the FIR appeared ante dated. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 402.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: FIA Jurisdiction over OGRA Ordinance Offences
records.heading: FIA has no jurisdiction over OGRA Ordinance offences, so bail was allowed as further inquiry
records.text: The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority Ordinance 2002 is not a scheduled offence under the FIA Act 1974 and has its own complaint mechanism with overriding effect, so the FIA had no jurisdiction. The company had paid the fine, the accused had been in jail about three months and were no longer needed for investigation. The case required further inquiry and bail was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 456.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fraud, Void Transactions and Limitation
records.heading: Fraud vitiates the most solemn transaction and limitation does not run against a void transaction
records.text: Fraud vitiates even the most solemn transaction, a transaction based on fraud is void, and limitation does not run against a void transaction. Under s. 9 CPC civil courts may try all civil suits unless jurisdiction is barred, and proceedings challenged as coram non judice are not covered by the exceptions. The post also discusses the bar on civil court jurisdiction over settlement authority orders after repeal of the evacuee property laws. Ref: Safdar Yar Khan etc. v. Mohammad Iqbal Khan etc. (R.S.A. No. 56 of 2005).
records.title: Safdar Yar Khan etc. v. Mohammad Iqbal Khan etc. (R.S.A. No. 56 of 2005)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension Matters: Service Tribunal Jurisdiction
records.heading: Pension claims fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Service Tribunal, not Article 199
records.text: Art. 212(1)(a) vests exclusive jurisdiction over terms and conditions of service, including those of persons who have held a civil post, in the service tribunal. A pension claim falls within the Punjab Service Tribunal's jurisdiction under ss. 2(b), 3 and 4 of the Tribunal Act, so the High Court has no jurisdiction under Art. 199. Ref: Abdus Salam v. Assistant Commissioner, Murree & 5 others (I.C.A. No. 53 of 2021).
records.title: Abdus Salam v. Assistant Commissioner, Murree & 5 others (I.C.A. No. 53 of 2021)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Acting Charge and Regular Promotion: APT Rules 1974
records.heading: Acting charge cannot continue for an unlimited period under the APT Rules 1974
records.text: Authority discussing Rules 6-A, 7, 7A and 8A of the APT Rules 1974, acting charge versus promotion on regular basis, and consideration for regularization. It states that acting charge cannot be continued for an unlimited period. Ref: The Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary & others v. Ghulam Shabbir (C.A. 52-K/2022, decided 30.12.2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: The Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary & others v. Ghulam Shabbir (C.A. 52-K/2022, decided 30.12.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Rioting: Evidence of Common Intent
records.heading: Riot requires proof of disturbance of the peace by several persons with common intent
records.text: Riot requires proof of disturbance of the peace by several persons acting with common intent, shown by evidence of illegal acts at the site. Pre-concert, or circumstances uniting the persons to act with common intent on the spur of the moment, must be proved. Riot, rout and unlawful assembly are related but distinct offences. Ref: 2023 LHC 1106; Fayyaz Ahmad etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 654-22, decided 23.02.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
