records.title: Fayyaz Ahmad etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 654-22, decided 23.02.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Bullet Deflection and Ricochet in Cranial Cavity
records.heading: Bullet deflection and ricochet in the cranial cavity: authority, no holding
records.text: Authority on deflection of a bullet and the ricochet effect in the cranial cavity, in an appeal against conviction under the Pakistan Penal Code. Ref: 2023 LHC 1090; Bashir Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 223-21, decided 22.02.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Bashir Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 223-21, decided 22.02.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIV CPC: Framing Issues and Partial Partition
records.heading: Issues are framed from both sides' pleadings and partial partition is not allowed
records.text: Under O. XIV Rr. 1 and 2 CPC issues are framed from the material propositions of law and fact raised in the pleadings of both sides, not only those in the plaint. Where the dispute extends to other joint or benami properties, they must be included, since partial partition is not allowed regardless of possession. Ref: Aila Azhar and another v. Ali Kuli Amin-ud-Din and others (W.P. No. 21798 of 2022, decided 09.03.2023).
records.title: Aila Azhar and another v. Ali Kuli Amin-ud-Din and others (W.P. No. 21798 of 2022, decided 09.03.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Mob Violence: Identity of Accused Not Proved
records.heading: Failure to prove the identity of accused in a spontaneous mob outburst led to acquittal
records.text: In a trial before the Anti-Terrorism Court arising from a spontaneous mob outburst, the prosecution failed to establish the identity of the appellants by ocular account or other means. Co-accused on the same evidence had already been acquitted, and one reasonable doubt suffices for acquittal. Appeal allowed and the appellants acquitted. Ref: 2023 LHC 1106; Fayyaz Ahmad etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 654/2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Fayyaz Ahmad etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 654/2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Decree for Specific Performance Is Preliminary
records.heading: A decree for specific performance is generally preliminary and time for balance may be extended under section 148
records.text: A decree for specific performance of an agreement to sell is generally preliminary, as the court retains seisin and power under s. 148 CPC to extend the time for payment of the balance price. A decree may be conditional and treated as preliminary until the condition is complied with. Revision was dismissed as the courts below had acted without illegality or material irregularity. Ref: 2023 MLD 404.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Decree Becomes Final on Lapse of Payment Period
records.heading: A decree becomes final when the payment period lapses and the court is then functus officio
records.text: Where the decree required the balance consideration within two months and provided that the suit would be deemed dismissed on default, it was preliminary until that period expired. After it lapsed it became final, no further steps were contemplated, and the court was functus officio when the application was filed over three and a half months later. Ref: 2023 MLD 404.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 35(c) Specific Relief Act: Rescission
records.heading: A court may rescind a contract under section 35(c) even after a specific performance decree
records.text: Even where a suit for specific performance is decreed, the contract may be rescinded by the court. Under s. 35(c) of the Specific Relief Act 1877 the court may, in the suit in which the decree was made and not complied with, rescind the contract as regards the defaulting parties or altogether, as justice requires. Ref: 2023 MLD 404.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Defamation: Libel, Slander and Required Elements
records.heading: Defamation requires a defamatory imputation referring to the claimant and published to another person
records.text: Defamation is publication of a statement that lowers a person's reputation, and takes the form of libel and slander. The claimant must prove that the imputation is defamatory, refers to the claimant and was published to at least one other person. Defamation is defined in s. 3 of the Ordinance 2002, and no one has an unbridled right of expression. Ref: 2023 MLD 525.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Contract Between Counsel and Client: Agency
records.heading: A counsel is an agent of the client under section 182 of the Contract Act
records.text: A counsel acts for his client under the ordinary rules of principal and agent, and falls within the definition of agent in s. 182 of the Contract Act 1872. The contract between advocate and client is governed by the general rules of contract, and a power of attorney is construed strictly. Ref: 2023 MLD 483.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC and S. 151 CPC
records.heading: Section 151 CPC cannot be used where Order XXIII Rules 1 and 2 expressly apply
records.text: A plaintiff may withdraw a suit at any stage under O. XXIII R. 1 CPC, but if he seeks liberty to file a fresh suit he must state the defect in the earlier suit. Inherent powers under s. 151 CPC cannot be used where an express provision applies, so O. XXIII Rr. 1 and 2 governed and s. 151 was inapplicable. Ref: 2023 MLD 541.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Withdrawal of Suit: Liberty Without Notice
records.heading: Liberty to file a fresh suit cannot be given without notice to the defendants
records.text: The plaintiff was entitled to withdraw the suit under O. XXIII R. 1 CPC, but permission to file a fresh suit could not be given where no specific notice was issued to the defendants and they were not present before the court on that date. Ref: 2023 MLD 541.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Benami Transaction: Essential Elements and Pleading
records.heading: A benami claim must plead and prove both complementary contracts by legal testimony
records.text: A benami transaction involves the seller, the real owner and the ostensible owner, and two complementary contracts: one between the real and ostensible owner, and one between the benamidar and the seller. The plaintiff must plead both in detail and prove them by legal testimony, and failure to do so is fatal. Courts must decide on legal grounds, not suspicion or conjecture. Ref: 2023 SCMR 572.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale by Attorney Through Oral Mutation: Burden of Proof
records.heading: Vendees relying on an attorney's oral sale mutation must prove the power of attorney and the sale
records.text: Where property was sold by a general attorney through oral sale mutation, the vendees must prove the power of attorney, the ingredients of sale and the execution of the mutation by cogent evidence. Transactions involving illiterate women are treated like those of pardanasheen ladies, and attestation of mutation alone does not prove a sale. The onus lies on the beneficiary. Ref: 2023 LHC 1158; Mst. Irshad Bibi v. Ghulam Mustafa etc. (Civil Revision 970-12, decided 24.03.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Mst. Irshad Bibi v. Ghulam Mustafa etc. (Civil Revision 970-12, decided 24.03.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-K Cr.P.C.: Prosecution's Right to Lead Evidence
records.heading: Section 265-K CrPC cannot deprive the prosecution of the chance to lead evidence
records.text: The prosecution cannot be deprived of the opportunity to produce evidence through s. 265-K Cr.P.C., especially where the allegations require recording of evidence. Ss. 249-A and 265-K are an exception to the general rule that guilt or innocence is decided after full opportunity to both sides. The summoning of an accused under s. 204(1) is not mechanical. Ref: 2022 LHC 9073; State v. Muhamamd Shahid @ Shada (Crl. Appeal 1026-16, decided 01.06.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: State v. Muhamamd Shahid @ Shada (Crl. Appeal 1026-16, decided 01.06.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Method of Exhibiting a Document in Evidence
records.heading: A document may be exhibited only when relevant and admissible, as decided by the trial court
records.text: A document can be exhibited only when it is relevant and admissible in evidence, and the trial court must decide its admissibility before exhibiting it. The judgment sets out the method of exhibiting a document. Ref: 2022 LHC 9067; Aziz Khan v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 39152/19, decided 27.09.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Aziz Khan v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 39152/19, decided 27.09.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Disclosure of Toshakhana Gifts and Record
records.heading: Failure to disclose Toshakhana gifts is culpable wrongdoing and the Government was directed to disclose them
records.text: Ownership of gifts vests in the Government unless the prescribed procedure for acceptance and disposal is followed, and failure to disclose the identity of gifts is a culpable wrongdoing. The Government was directed to disclose the providers of gifts from 1990 to 13 March 2023 and the Toshakhana record from 1990 to 2001, within seven days of receipt of the certified copy. Ref: 2023 LHC 1180; Munir Ahmad v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (W.P. 80733/22, decided 22.03.2023); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Munir Ahmad v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (W.P. 80733/22, decided 22.03.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 184(3) Jurisdiction and Provincial Elections Suo Motu
records.heading: Scope of Article 184(3) while the matter is pending in High Courts: suo motu elections case
records.text: Judgment in the suo motu case on provincial assembly elections addressing the scope of Art. 184(3) while the matter is pending in the High Courts, the constitutional bar on using it against a High Court's judicial pronouncement, res judicata for Art. 199 decisions, federalism, political dialogue, and the need for rules regulating Art. 184(3) and bench constitution. Ref: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023, decided 01.03.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023, decided 01.03.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Dissent: Regulating Chief Justice's Bench Powers
records.heading: Dissent: the Chief Justice's power over benches needs regulation and a bench cannot be changed after the cause list
records.text: In their detailed dissenting judgment, the judges held that the petitions on Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa elections be dismissed, the suo motu proceedings closed and the High Courts decide pending petitions within three days. They held that the Chief Justice's power over benches needs regulation and that, once the cause list is issued, he cannot change a bench. Ref: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023, decided 01.03.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023, decided 01.03.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail in Controversial Tweets Case
records.heading: Islamabad High Court allowed post-arrest bail to a PTI Senator in the tweets case
records.text: The Islamabad High Court allowed post-arrest bail to a PTI Senator in the controversial tweets case. The post gives only the citation and the outcome. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 350.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift: Declaration, Acceptance and Possession
records.heading: A donee must prove declaration, acceptance and possession with time, place and witnesses
records.text: To prove a gift the donee must allege and prove three mandatory ingredients: declaration, acceptance and transfer of possession. The time, place and names of the persons in whose presence these were performed must also be specifically stated. Ref: Shehzad Nawaz and others v. Mst. Raaj Begum and others (R.S.A. No. 25 of 2015).
records.title: Shehzad Nawaz and others v. Mst. Raaj Begum and others (R.S.A. No. 25 of 2015)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Change of AOR and ASC Without Consent
records.heading: Change of AOR and ASC without consent of the earlier AOR or permission: authority, no holding
records.text: Authority on change of Advocate on Record and Advocate Supreme Court without the consent of the earlier AOR or permission of the Court, together with restoration. The post gives no further holding. Ref: Fakhar Nawaz v. Administrative Secretary/Senior Member Board of Revenue, Peshawar & others (C.M.A. 10945/2022, decided 20.03.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Fakhar Nawaz v. Administrative Secretary/Senior Member Board of Revenue, Peshawar & others (C.M.A. 10945/2022, decided 20.03.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: PEMRA Regulations 2002 Void Ab Initio
records.heading: PEMRA Regulations 2002 were void ab initio and the Ordinance gives no power to levy surcharge
records.text: The PEMRA (TV/Radio Broadcast Operations) Regulations 2002 did not derive their power from the PEMRA Ordinance 2002, so they were void ab initio and non est. The Ordinance gives no power to levy and recover surcharge on late payment of the annual fee. Ref: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) through its Chairman & another v. Pakistan Broadcasters Association, Karachi & others (C.A. 1518/2013, decided 24.02.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) through its Chairman & another v. Pakistan Broadcasters Association, Karachi & others (C.A. 1518/2013, decided 24.02.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 184(3) Hearings Postponed Pending Art. 191 Rules
records.heading: Article 184(3) cases should be postponed until rules under Article 191 are enacted
records.text: The judgment held that hearing of this case and all other Art. 184(3) cases should be postponed until the rules under Art. 191 are enacted. It also held that judges remain accountable to the people, valid criticism cannot be prohibited, and PEMRA's blanket prohibition order offends the Constitution. The case concerned additional marks for Hafiz-e-Quran in MBBS and BDS admissions. Ref: S.M.C. 4/2022 (decided 29.03.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: S.M.C. 4/2022 (decided 29.03.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 124-A PPC (Sedition) Declared Void
records.heading: Section 124-A PPC on sedition declared void by the Lahore High Court
records.text: On petitions against the registration of sedition cases over speeches against the government, the Lahore High Court announced its reserved judgment declaring s. 124-A PPC void. Ref: Sulaiman Abuzar Niazi and others (petitions); Justice Shahid Karim.
records.title: Sulaiman Abuzar Niazi and others (petitions)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Constitution of Supreme Court Benches: Review Petitions
records.heading: A review petition should be heard by the same bench, including dissenting judges
records.text: A review petition should, as far as practicable, be heard by the same bench that decided the case. Judges who dissented, subject to availability, are necessary members of the review bench with the same judicial power as the others. No litigant or lawyer may demand a bench of choice, as constituting benches is the Chief Justice's privilege and duty. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 119, PLD 2021 SC 327.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Dissenting Note on Stay of Art. 184(3) Cases
records.heading: Dissenting note on the order staying Article 184(3) suo motu cases until rules are made
records.text: Five page dissenting note by Justice Shahid Waheed from the 2 to 1 order of the three member bench, which had stayed hearing of all suo motu cases until rules were made. The post does not state his reasoning. Ref: S.M.C. 4/2022 (decided 30.03.2023); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: S.M.C. 4/2022 (decided 30.03.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift: Heavy Burden on Donee
records.heading: A donee claiming an oral gift of inheritable property bears a heavy burden of proof
records.text: A donee claiming an oral gift of inheritable property to the exclusion of other heirs bears a heavy burden to prove it and must stand on his own evidence. Unpleaded witnesses, unproduced witnesses and a doubtful acknowledgment deed defeated the claim, so the appeal was allowed and the suit dismissed. Ref: 2023 CLC 543.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Second Appeal: Concurrent Findings and Misreading of Evidence
records.heading: Concurrent findings based on misreading of evidence may be set aside in second appeal
records.text: Where concurrent findings of the courts below rest on misreading of the parties' evidence, the High Court may set them aside in second appeal. Ref: 2023 CLC 543.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Investigation as Vital Component of Criminal Justice
records.heading: Investigation is a vital component of criminal justice and police must unearth the truth
records.text: Investigation is a vital component of the criminal justice system and rule of law, and the police must unearth the truth, collect all available evidence on indictable conduct and locate suspected persons. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 372.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Special Oath Offered by Counsel Binds Party
records.heading: A special oath offered and accepted through counsel binds the party under the Oaths Act
records.text: The word party in ss. 8 and 9 of the Oaths Act 1873 includes the party's advocate, so an offer of special oath may be made and accepted through counsel. An offer made by the husband's counsel and accepted by the wife became a binding agreement, and the wife's dowry suit was decreed on her special oath. The constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: 2023 MLD 483.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 3 Limitation Act: Bar Applies Without Objection
records.heading: A time-barred claim must be dismissed under section 3 even if the opposite party raises no objection
records.text: Compliance with the statutory period for exercising a right is mandatory under s. 3 of the Limitation Act 1908, and the court cannot ignore it even if the opposite party raised no objection. Ref: 2023 CLC 504.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 5 Limitation Act: Condonation of Delay
records.heading: Delay is condoned under section 5 only where beyond the litigant's control with a plausible reason
records.text: The law of limitation bars suits, appeals and remedies to save parties from endless litigation. Delay may be condoned under s. 5 only where the circumstances were beyond the litigant's control and a plausible reason is given. Ref: 2023 CLC 504.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 47 and 75 QSO: Deceased Witnesses' Earlier Statements
records.heading: Evidence discarded by a competent court cannot be revived through a withdrawn appeal
records.text: Statements of deceased witnesses from an earlier suit dismissed by the Civil Court, and then withdrawn in appeal, could not found success in a later suit, since evidence discarded by a competent court cannot be revived. Simple withdrawal of the appeal did not wash away the reasoned determination. Copies of a deceased witness's statement may be admitted as secondary evidence, but only following the proper procedure. Ref: 2023 CLC 504.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 8 Specific Relief Act: Possession Includes Ownership Declaration
records.heading: In a suit for possession, a declaration of ownership is an inbuilt relief
records.text: In a suit for possession, a declaration of ownership is an inbuilt relief. Once the plaintiff is held entitled to possession, he is taken to have been declared the title holder. Ref: 2023 CLC 504.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fresh Suit After Withdrawal: Limitation
records.heading: A fresh suit filed over three years after withdrawal in appeal is time barred
records.text: Where an earlier suit was withdrawn in appeal with liberty to file afresh, the fresh suit instituted more than three years after the withdrawal was beyond limitation and time barred. The case concerned a challenge to an oral sale mutation and a claimed earlier sale contract. Ref: 2023 CLC 504.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Scope of High Court's Revisional Jurisdiction
records.heading: In revision the High Court interferes only with illegal or perverse judgments and decrees
records.text: The High Court in revision interferes only with judgments and decrees found illegal, unlawful or perverse, resulting from misreading or non-reading of evidence or excess of jurisdiction by the courts below. Ref: 2023 CLC 504.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Fraud Vitiates Solemn Proceedings
records.heading: Fraud vitiates the most solemn proceedings and ill-gotten gain cannot be validated
records.text: Fraud vitiates the most solemn proceedings, any edifice raised on a fraudulent transaction stands automatically dismantled, and ill-gotten gain obtained by fraud cannot be validated under any law. Ref: 2023 CLC 471.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Construction by Co-Sharer During Partition Appeal
records.heading: Co-sharers may build at their own risk while a final partition decree is under appeal
records.text: Where a final partition decree was under appeal under s. 161 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act 1967, respondent co-sharers could build at their own risk and cost. The petitioner's right was safeguarded, since if the appeal succeeded they could claim no compensation for improvements. The constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: 2023 CLC 430.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitrator's Interpretation of Contract: Limits of Interference
records.heading: A court cannot interfere with a reasoned arbitrator's interpretation merely because it would differ
records.text: Where an arbitrator interprets a contract clause in a reasoned manner, the court cannot interfere merely because it might have interpreted it differently. Neither the trial court nor the High Court can sit in judgment over the arbitrator's interpretation when deciding misconduct under s. 30. Ref: 2023 CLC 493.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Making Award Rule of Court: Judicial Function
records.heading: Making an award rule of court is a judicial function requiring scrutiny despite no objections
records.text: The power to make an award a rule of court under the Arbitration Act 1940 is judicial, not ministerial, and absence of objections does not relieve the court of scrutinising the award. The petitioner failed to prove execution of the reference deed. The High Court declined to interfere in revision and dismissed it. Ref: 2023 CLC 582.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed in a section 489-F PPC case with pending civil litigation over the cheque
records.text: The complainant was a special attorney, the principal had not joined the investigation, and the FIR gave no date or purpose for the money. Civil litigation over the cheque was pending, the accused was a first offender and no longer required for investigation, and a large amount did not enlarge the punishment. Post-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 499.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Alternative Punishments, S. 497(1)
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC punishments are alternative and the offence is outside section 497(1) prohibition
records.text: The punishments under s. 489-F PPC are in the alternative, as the word or is used, so a sentence of imprisonment is not mandatory and a fine alone may be imposed. The offence is not covered by the prohibition in s. 497(1) Cr.P.C. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 499.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 Cr.P.C.: Re-Summoning Witnesses for Cross-Examination
records.heading: Counsel's unavailability for cross-examination justifies one more opportunity under section 540
records.text: Where cross-examination could not be conducted because defence counsel was unavailable, asking the unrepresented accused to cross-examine was no substitute for counsel's cross-examination. The High Court held it proper to give counsel one more opportunity, allowed the revision and directed the trial court to allow the accused one more chance. Ref: 2023 MLD 559.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Suit on Oral Agreement to Sell: Maintainability
records.heading: A declaratory suit on an oral agreement to sell without a prayer for possession is not maintainable
records.text: A court must examine at the outset the form and maintainability of a suit. A declaratory suit based on an oral agreement to sell cannot be entertained as an ordinary suit and must state payment of consideration and, if possession is claimed, how, when and before whom it was given. A suit on an agreement to sell without a prayer for possession is not maintainable. Ref: 2023 MLD 511.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Co-Sharer's Suit for Injunction Without Partition
records.heading: A co-sharer may sue for injunction to protect his rights without seeking partition
records.text: A co-sharer may sue for permanent injunction to protect his rights without seeking partition, relying on Fazal v. Ghulam Muhammad (2003 SCMR 999). Each co-sharer owns every inch of the joint property until partition, and none may change its nature or build without consent. The courts below erred in dismissing the suit as not maintainable. Ref: 2023 LHC 1297; Fazal Karim etc. v. Mehboob Khan (Civil Revision 212-18, decided 15.03.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Fazal Karim etc. v. Mehboob Khan (Civil Revision 212-18, decided 15.03.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Subsequent Vendee with Notice: No Protection
records.heading: A subsequent vendee with notice of an earlier agreement is not a bona fide purchaser
records.text: A person who bought through sale mutation knowing of the vendor's earlier agreement over the same land is not a bona fide purchaser and cannot claim protection under s. 27 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 or s. 41 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882. An alternate prayer for compensation does not amount to withdrawing the claim for specific performance. Ref: 2023 LHC 1319; Malik Zulfiqar Ahmad etc. v. Mosaddaq Parvaiz etc. (Civil Revision 49148/20, decided 21.02.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Malik Zulfiqar Ahmad etc. v. Mosaddaq Parvaiz etc. (Civil Revision 49148/20, decided 21.02.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Expired Pesticides: Substandard Under S. 3(rr)
records.heading: Expired pesticides are substandard under section 3(rr) and attract section 21(2)(b)
records.text: The term expired pesticide is not defined in the Ordinance or the Punjab Agriculture Pesticides Rules 2018. Expired pesticides are included in part (a) of the definition of substandard in s. 3(rr) of the Ordinance, so s. 21(2)(b) applies when a person sells expired pesticides. Ref: 2023 LHC 1346; Muhammad Farman v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 72710/22, decided 07.02.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Farman v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 72710/22, decided 07.02.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Dissenting Note on Recusal in Elections Case
records.heading: Dissenting note: a judge declined to remain on a bench where the order was dictated in his absence
records.text: In his note the judge said he declined to remain on the bench because the order was dictated in his absence without consultation. He wished the dispute over the ratio of the 1 March order to be resolved first, and the majority order of that date had not been issued. Ref: Mohammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Election Commission of Pakistan through Chief Election Commissioner Islamabad and others (Const.P. 5/2023, decided 31.03.2023); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Mohammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Election Commission of Pakistan through Chief Election Commissioner Islamabad and others (Const.P. 5/2023, decided 31.03.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 184(3) Maintainability When Matter Pending in High Court
records.heading: Suo motu proceedings were not maintainable where the election matter was pending in High Courts
records.text: In his seven page note, the judge held the suo motu proceedings dismissed and the suo motu and constitutional petitions not maintainable, as the election matter was pending in the Lahore and Peshawar High Courts. He noted the Supreme Court has held it does not interfere when a matter is before a High Court, and should refrain when political matters are at their height. Ref: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023, decided 31.03.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Suo Motu Regarding Holding of General Elections to the Provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (S.M.C. 1/2023, decided 31.03.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: ICJ: Certain Iranian Assets, Jurisdiction and Admissibility
records.heading: ICJ upheld the objection to jurisdiction over treaty claims but rejected the admissibility objection
records.text: The International Court of Justice, by ten votes to five, upheld the United States' objection to jurisdiction over claims under Arts. III, IV and V of the 1955 Treaty relating to Bank Markazi. By thirteen votes to two it rejected the objection to admissibility on exhaustion of local remedies. The Urdu text says the US was held liable to compensate Iran for freezing assets. Ref: Certain Iranian Assets (Islamic Republic of Iran v. United States of America).
records.title: Certain Iranian Assets (Islamic Republic of Iran v. United States of America)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Punjab Rented Premises Act: Procedure on Ejectment Petitions
records.heading: Landlord and tenant must disclose fully on affidavit and the Tribunal cannot take ex parte title evidence
records.text: Under ss. 19 and 22 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 both landlord and tenant must make full disclosure on affidavit with all documents at the time of pleading. The Rent Tribunal could not reject the leave application and then take ex parte evidence on the landlord's title. The ejectment orders were set aside and the matter remanded for fresh decision. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 225.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Costs Against Frivolous and Vexatious Litigation
records.heading: Costs under Order 28 Rule 3 may curb frivolous and vexatious litigation
records.text: Frivolous and vexatious litigation burdens the courts and should be curbed by imposing costs under Order 28 Rule 3 of the Supreme Court Rules 1980. Actual costs, above nominal costs, may be awarded in an appropriate case, and such costs serve the requirement of fair trial under Art. 10A. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 298.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 476 Cr.P.C.: Discretionary Cognizance
records.heading: Cognizance under section 476 CrPC is discretionary and must not serve private vengeance
records.text: The power under s. 476 Cr.P.C. to take cognizance of offences committed in relation to proceedings before a court is discretionary, indicated by the words may take cognizance. The court must exercise it judiciously, considering whether it is expedient in the interests of justice, and ensure it is not used by a litigant to wreak private vengeance. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 298.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI CPC: Dismissal of Appeal for Non-Prosecution
records.heading: An appeal dismissed for non-appearance is untenable where sufficient cause for absence is shown
records.text: Appeals from original decrees are governed by s. 96 and O. XLI CPC, and under R. 11(2) an appeal may be dismissed if the appellant does not appear. The applicants showed sufficient cause for non-appearance, so the dismissal order was not tenable. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 216.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Restoration of Dismissed Appeal: Art. 181
records.heading: Restoration of a dismissed appeal here fell under residuary Article 181 with three years
records.text: Art. 168 of the Limitation Act 1908 gives thirty days for re-admission of an appeal dismissed for non-prosecution under O. XLI R. 17(1) CPC. In this case the residuary Art. 181, giving three years, applied, so the restoration application was within time. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 216.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 10-A: Right to Be Heard and Fair Trial
records.heading: The right to be heard extends to pre-trial proceedings including investigation under Article 10-A
records.text: Audi alteram partem is enshrined in the Constitution, and the right to be heard is read into every statute affecting a person's rights, particularly after Art. 10-A. Pre-trial proceedings including investigation fall within the right to a fair trial. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 233.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report Only Through Superintendent of Police
records.heading: A cancellation report must go to the Magistrate through the Superintendent of Police, not a DSP
records.text: Under R. 24.7 of the Police Rules 1934 a cancellation report under s. 173 Cr.P.C. must be sent to the Magistrate by the Superintendent of Police, who must apply his independent mind. The word shall in R. 24.7, against may in Art. 18(10) of the Police Order 2002, shows the rule is mandatory. A report forwarded by a DSP was not valid. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 233.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: S. 24-A General Clauses Act: Reasoned Orders
records.heading: Section 24-A General Clauses Act imposes a duty to give reasons after hearing all parties
records.text: Section 24-A of the General Clauses Act 1897 places an affirmative duty on a court, authority or forum to pass an order or judgment with reasons, after giving all parties an opportunity to present their submissions. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 233.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing FIR and Investigation Under Art. 199
records.heading: The High Court may quash an FIR and investigation as without lawful authority under Article 199
records.text: Registration of an FIR and investigation are acts amenable to High Court jurisdiction under Art. 199(1)(a)(ii). The High Court may declare them without lawful authority and of no legal effect and make consequential orders, such as quashing the FIR and investigation. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 265.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Contents Decide Whether Offence Is Cognizable
records.heading: The contents of the FIR, not the mere section cited, decide whether an offence is cognizable
records.text: The contents of an FIR must be examined to see whether the allegations disclose a cognizable offence. Merely mentioning a particular section of the PPC or other law in the FIR is not determinative. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 265.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Production of Original Documents During Trial
records.heading: The prosecution may produce original documents at trial even if only copies were given to police
records.text: In a s. 489-F PPC trial the prosecution may produce original documents during evidence even if only copies were given to the police in investigation. Under Art. 18 QSO the court must allow evidence that proves a fact in issue, and no provision of the Code of Criminal Procedure bars receiving a relevant document at a late stage. The trial court could not discard them; the revisional order was upheld. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 124; Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supply of Statements and Documents to Accused
records.heading: The accused must receive free copies of FIR, police report and statements before trial
records.text: Before a trial under Chap. XXIIA CrPC on a police report, the accused must be given free copies of the FIR, police report, statements under ss. 161 and 164 and the inspection and recovery notes at least 7 days before trial. In Magistrate trials under Chap. XX, copies of the s. 161 and 164 statements and the first inspection note are to be supplied in the same way, except in summary cases or offences punishable with fine or up to six months. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 124; Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Standard of Proof in Civil and Criminal Cases
records.heading: Civil cases need preponderance of probability whereas criminal cases need proof beyond all reasonable doubt
records.text: The degree of proof differs between civil and criminal cases. In civil cases a preponderance of probability suffices and the benefit of reasonable doubt need not necessarily go to the defendant. In criminal cases guilt must be established beyond all reasonable doubt to a moral certainty. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 124; Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Exhibiting a Document Does Not Prove It
records.heading: Exhibiting a document neither proves it nor bars objection to its admissibility
records.text: Marking a document as an exhibit does not bar the other party from challenging its admissibility and does not dispense with proof of it, which must follow the QSO. Admission in evidence neither fixes its evidentiary value nor makes admissibility final. There is no concept of de-exhibition under Art. 18 QSO; objections are decided by the trial court when adjudicating the case. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 124; Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Primary and Secondary Evidence of Documents
records.heading: Document contents are proved by primary evidence, with secondary evidence only in the cases in Article 76
records.text: Contents of documents may be proved by primary or secondary evidence. Art. 73 QSO defines primary evidence, Art. 74 lists the forms of secondary evidence, and Art. 75 requires proof by primary evidence except in the exceptional cases in Art. 76, where notice to produce is generally needed before secondary evidence is given. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 124; Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Suleman v. Muhammad Saad Naseem (Writ Petition No. 2163 of 2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561-A CrPC: Quashing of FIR or Investigation
records.heading: The High Court cannot quash an FIR or investigation under section 561-A CrPC
records.text: The High Court has no power under s. 561-A CrPC to quash an FIR or an investigation. It may quash a judicial proceeding pending before a subordinate court under that section. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 265.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Compensation: Potential Value of Entire Acquired Area
records.heading: Compensation for a large acquired area must reflect the potential value of the whole area
records.text: Under R. 4 of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Assessment Rules, 1968, where a large area of differently classified land is acquired for one project, compensation must reflect the potential value of the whole area. Valuing small parcels by ownership and revenue classification disadvantages the landowners. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 277.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Compensation: Factors for Potential Value of Land
records.heading: Factors for the potential value of acquired land under Rule 4: authority
records.text: Authority on compensation for acquired land under R. 4 of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Assessment Rules, 1968, which states the factors to be considered in determining the potential value of the land. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 277.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Punishment of Rajm Under Zina Ordinance
records.heading: The Federal Shariat Court held the repugnancy question on rajm closed by an earlier decision
records.text: A Shariat petition contended that rajm under s. 5 of the Offence of Zina (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance, 1979 is repugnant to Islam because the punishment is 100 stripes. The Federal Shariat Court held the question closed, having been decided in Federation of Pakistan v. Hazoor Bakhsh (PLD 1983 FSC 255), which held rajm to be in accordance with Shariah. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 261.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Honorifics for High Courts and Supreme Court
records.heading: Honorifics such as honourable, learned or Apex should not be used for superior courts
records.text: The Supreme Court deprecated prefixes such as honourable, hon'ble and learned, and the terms August or Apex, when referring to the High Courts or Supreme Court. The Constitution uses none of them, so advocates and judges should prefer the language of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 260.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Constitution of Benches and Fixation of Cases
records.heading: No provision empowers the Registrar or Chief Justice to constitute benches or fix cases
records.text: No provision of the Constitution or the Supreme Court Rules, 1980 empowers the Registrar or the Chief Justice to constitute Benches, change or reduce their members, or fix cases. Preferential or out of turn fixing without justification may suggest favour to one party, and transparency and fairness are needed to preserve the Court's independence. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 306.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Change of Counsel at Review Stage
records.heading: Substitution of counsel at review stage is refused absent compelling circumstances
records.text: Substitution of counsel at the review stage was refused where there were no compelling circumstances and the previous counsel was available. Loss of confidence in counsel is hardly a ground, and liberal permission would defeat R. 6 of O. XXVI of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980 and encourage endless litigation. Application dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 273.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Frivolous Litigation: Costs Under O. XXVIII R. 3
records.heading: Litigation to settle a private grudge is frivolous and attracts costs under Order XXVIII Rule 3
records.text: Litigation started by a person with no interest in the matter to settle a private grudge is frivolous and vexatious and burdens the courts. Such practice may be curbed by costs under O. XXVIII R. 3 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980. Leave to appeal was dismissed with costs of Rs.100,000. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 298.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Vexatious Petition: Costs on FIA Inspector Personally
records.heading: Costs for a vexatious petition were imposed personally on the FIA Inspector who registered the FIR
records.text: Where an FIR was registered and investigated without lawful authority, a petition continuing the harassment of the respondents was held meritless and vexatious. Leave to appeal was declined with costs of Rs.100,000, to be paid from his own pocket by the FIA Inspector who registered the FIR, deposited within 30 days and paid to the respondents. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 265.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Versus Medical Evidence in Murder Appeal
records.heading: Conflict between ocular and medical evidence and timing discrepancies in a murder jail appeal
records.text: Jail appeal against a death sentence under s. 302(b) PPC. The post records a conflict between the ocular account and medical evidence, unexplained discrepancies in the timings of the inquest report, omission of the names of those who identified the body, and that the eye-witnesses were close relatives of the deceased. The outcome is not given. Ref: 2023 LHC 1385; Asjad Mehmood v. The State (Jail Appeal 44525/19, decided 15.03.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Asjad Mehmood v. The State (Jail Appeal 44525/19, decided 15.03.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Postponement of Punjab and KP Elections
records.heading: Supreme Court set aside the Election Commission decision and ordered Punjab and KP elections for 14 May
records.text: Judgment in Constitution Petition No. 5 of 2023 dated 04.04.2023. The file title states that the Election Commission's decision was set aside and elections in KP and Punjab were ordered for 14 May. No further reasoning is given in the post.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Commission Cannot Extend 90 Day Period: Art. 224(2)
records.heading: The Election Commission cannot extend the election date beyond the 90 days in Article 224(2)
records.text: The Election Commission's order of 22.03.2023 was declared unconstitutional, void ab initio and quashed, as neither the Constitution nor the law lets the Commission extend the date of elections beyond the 90 days in Art. 224(2). The Punjab Assembly Election Programme under s. 57(2) of the Elections Act, 2017 was revived with modifications to stages 6 to 11. Ref: Mohammad Sibtain Khan v. Election Commission of Pakistan (Constitution Petition No. 5 of 2023, decided 04.04.2023).
records.title: Mohammad Sibtain Khan v. Election Commission of Pakistan (Constitution Petition No. 5 of 2023, decided 04.04.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Postponement of Punjab Elections Declared Unconstitutional
records.heading: The postponement of Punjab elections was declared unconstitutional and the President's date restored
records.text: The Supreme Court declared the Election Commission's order of 22 March, postponing Punjab Assembly elections to 8 October, unconstitutional, in excess of jurisdiction and unlawful. The President's date was restored, polling in Punjab was ordered for 14 May, and election programme stages 6 to 11 were restored. The Court said its decision was unaffected by the order of 29.03.2023 in SMC 4/2022. Ref: Mohammad Sibtain Khan v. Election Commission of Pakistan (Constitution Petition No. 5 of 2023, decided 04.04.2023).
records.title: Mohammad Sibtain Khan v. Election Commission of Pakistan (Constitution Petition No. 5 of 2023, decided 04.04.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Suo Motu Case on Extra Marks for Hafiz-e-Quran
records.heading: Larger bench on suo motu notice on extra marks for Hafiz-e-Quran and bench constitution
records.text: A larger bench was constituted to consider the order of 15.03.2023, announced on 29.03.2023, which the bench described as a fresh suo motu invocation of jurisdiction on bench constitution and the power of the Chief Justice as master of the roster. The Urdu text reports that the suo motu notice on additional 20 marks was disposed of as infructuous and that the earlier two member decision had no legal status. Ref: Suo Motu Case on Additional 20 Marks to Hafiz-e-Quran in MBBS/BDS Admission (decided 04.04.2023); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan.
records.title: Suo Motu Case on Additional 20 Marks to Hafiz-e-Quran in MBBS/BDS Admission (decided 04.04.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Environmental Approvals for Small-Scale Mining
records.heading: The Mining and Mineral Department obtains environmental approvals for small-scale mining
records.text: The Mining and Mineral Department is responsible for obtaining environmental approvals for small-scale mining licences and leases. Ref: Public Interest Law Association of Pakistan, Karachi v. Province of Punjab (C.P. 55/2020, decided 02.02.2023); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Public Interest Law Association of Pakistan, Karachi v. Province of Punjab (C.P. 55/2020, decided 02.02.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 148: Limitation for Redemption of Mortgage
records.heading: A mortgagor has sixty years under Article 148 running from accrual of the right to redeem
records.text: Under Art. 148 of the Limitation Act, 1908 a mortgagor has sixty years to redeem or recover possession, running from when the right to redeem or recover accrues. That date depends on the terms of the mortgage agreement, for example where a date is fixed for payment of the mortgage debt. Petitions dismissed and leave refused. Ref: Khan Afsar v. Mst. Qudrat Jan (Civil Petitions No. 3573 and 3574 of 2020, decided 10.03.2023).
records.title: Khan Afsar v. Mst. Qudrat Jan (Civil Petitions No. 3573 and 3574 of 2020, decided 10.03.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Suit Over Wrong Revenue Entries, Not Dower
records.heading: A suit over wrong revenue entries is governed by six years and is not a dower claim
records.text: The respondent never denied receiving dower and claimed to enjoy the property's proceeds, so the dispute concerned wrong entries in the revenue record and not dower under Arts. 103 and 104 of the Limitation Act. Relying on 2000 SCMR 1574 and Arts. 120 and 144, six years run from when the right to sue accrued, so the suit was not time barred and the Family Court was not the forum. Ref: Pirzada Noor-ul-Basar v. Mst. Pakistan Bibi (Civil Appeal No. 23-P of 2017, decided 29.03.2023).
records.title: Pirzada Noor-ul-Basar v. Mst. Pakistan Bibi (Civil Appeal No. 23-P of 2017, decided 29.03.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Delay Over One Year, Further Inquiry
records.heading: An accused detained over a year without attributable delay is entitled to bail under the third proviso
records.text: Under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, an accused in a non-bailable offence not punishable with death, detained over a year without the delay being attributable to him, must be released on bail. A co-accused with a similar role had been granted bail, and the case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC as one of further inquiry. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: Noor Kamal v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1720 of 2022, decided 30.03.2023).
records.title: Noor Kamal v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1720 of 2022, decided 30.03.2023)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Acquisition Under Ordinance 1960 and Non-Joinder of Province
records.heading: Non-joinder of the Province was fatal in a petition on acquisition under the 1960 Ordinance
records.text: Land acquired for Jet Airport extension under the 1960 Ordinance was governed by that Ordinance's independent mechanism, to which the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was alien. The respondents' constitutional petition omitted the Province of Punjab despite Art. 174, which went to the root of their case. The post does not give the final outcome. Ref: 2023 LHC 1435; Civil Aviation Authority v. Haji Pervez Khan etc. (ICA (Writ) 296-10, decided 05.04.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Civil Aviation Authority v. Haji Pervez Khan etc. (ICA (Writ) 296-10, decided 05.04.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Definition of Employee Under KP Regularization Act 2009
records.heading: Definition of employee under the KP Regularization Act 2009: discussion, no holding
records.text: Discussion of the definition of employee under ss. 2(b) and 3 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Employees (Regularization of Services) Act, 2009, and of the doctrines of estoppel, finality and res judicata. The post gives no holding or outcome. Ref: Muhammad Raqeeb v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (C.A. 1414/2021, decided 02.03.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Raqeeb v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (C.A. 1414/2021, decided 02.03.2023)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 23 ATA: Premature Transfer to Ordinary Court
records.heading: Transfer to the ordinary court under section 23 ATA after charge was framed was premature
records.text: The trial court had summoned the accused under s. 204 CrPC and framed a charge under s. 365-A PPC, and neither order was challenged. Invoking s. 23 ATA to send the case to the ordinary court at that stage was a premature exercise, neither permissible nor appreciable. Petition allowed and the Anti-Terrorism Court's order set aside. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 662.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C: Copies of Hard Disks to Accused
records.heading: Copies of seized hard disks must be supplied to the accused under section 265-C CrPC
records.text: Supply of copies of hard disks seized in investigation is mandatory under s. 265-C CrPC. Asking a constable in court to copy them was improper, and the disks should have gone to an IT department of the investigating agency. Revision allowed and the order excluding the disks was set aside, with copies to be prepared by a reliable police laboratory or PFSA. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 690; Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 307 of 2021).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 307 of 2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Presence of Accused Mandatory
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail cannot be granted unless the accused is present before the court
records.text: Under ss. 498 and 498-A CrPC the accused must be present before the court for pre-arrest bail, and without his presence it cannot be granted, even protective ad-interim bail. The accused was abroad and the petition was dismissed as not maintainable. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 678.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Kinds of Pre-Arrest Bail Explained
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail may be ad-interim, confirmed or protective, subject to section 498-A requirements
records.text: Pre-arrest bail is an order restraining the police or investigating agency from arresting the accused. It may be ad-interim, confirmed or protective (transitory) ad-interim bail, and s. 498-A CrPC now governs the basic requirements for maintainability of a pre-arrest bail petition. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 678.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Defective Charge: Remand for Re-framing of Charge
records.heading: A charge omitting one of two murders is defective and requires remand to re-frame the charge
records.text: Accused were charged twice, each time only with the murder of the female deceased, and never for the murder of the male deceased, so their conviction or acquittal did not attach to that death. Under ss. 221 and 225 CrPC the convictions and sentences were set aside and the case remanded to re-frame the charge, re-examine under s. 342 and decide afresh. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 625.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Plea of Mental Illness of Accused Not Determined
records.heading: A plea of mental illness must be determined by the trial court before trial proceeds
records.text: The accused was charged with murdering his wife and the defence pleaded mental illness. The trial court noted abnormality and obtained a Medical Board report suggesting schizophrenia, yet held him fit to stand trial and its judgment was silent on the plea. Appeal allowed and remanded for fresh comprehensive reports and a determination of his capability to face trial. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 567.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Withholding Best Evidence: Art. 129(g) QSO
records.heading: Withholding the best available witness raises an adverse inference under Article 129(g) QSO
records.text: The owner of a tractor present at the scene was never cited as an eye-witness, so the prosecution withheld the best available evidence and an adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO arose. With other doubts about the recoveries and the forensic report, the prosecution failed to prove its case under s. 302(b) PPC. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 532.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion Not Conclusive Proof of Guilt
records.heading: Absconsion is not conclusive proof of guilt and is only a suspicious circumstance
records.text: Absconsion of the accused is not conclusive proof of guilt and is only a suspicious circumstance. Suspicion cannot take the place of proof, its value depends on the facts of each case, and it may be consistent with guilt or innocence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 532.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint Dismissed After Cursory Inquiry Under S. 202
records.heading: A private complaint cannot be dismissed on cursory inquiry where a prima facie cognizable offence exists
records.text: The private complaint was dismissed after cursory statements of witnesses. After considering the material under s. 202 CrPC the trial court must issue process if sufficient ground exists, and the High Court found a prima facie cognizable offence that the trial court ignored. Revision allowed and remanded for a speaking, well-reasoned order. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 600.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Dishonest Improvements
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail granted where later statements were dishonest improvements against the accused
records.text: In a rash driving and murder case the FIR was lodged against an unknown accused, although the parties came from the same vicinity, and later statements were improvements made to tighten the screw on the accused. Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC was granted. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 517.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Futile Where Post-Arrest Bail Due
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail should not be refused where post-arrest bail would follow
records.text: Once the court concludes that on dismissal of pre-arrest bail the accused would be entitled to post-arrest bail, sending him to prison is a futile exercise. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 517.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Memory of Eye-Witness: No Photographic Recall Expected
records.heading: An eye-witness cannot be expected to recall events with photographic precision
records.text: People generally cannot accurately recall the sequence of events in a short span and remember only the main purport. A witness cannot be expected to be a human tape-recorder or video camera, or to narrate with mathematical niceties. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 1775.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: S. 7E Income Tax Ordinance Read Down
records.heading: Section 7E of the Income Tax Ordinance is read down as market value is not income
records.text: The market value of immovable property cannot be presumed to be income under Entry 47 of the Constitution. S. 7E of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 is read down to save taxation on the capital value of assets, and the exclusion of persons from chargeability under it is discriminatory and ultra vires. Ref: 2023 LHC 1548; Muhammad Usman Gul v. Federation of Pakistan (Tax Writ 52559/22, decided 06.04.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Usman Gul v. Federation of Pakistan (Tax Writ 52559/22, decided 06.04.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540-A CrPC: Exemption From Personal Appearance
records.heading: Incapability under section 540-A CrPC includes absence for employment abroad
records.text: Incapability in s. 540-A CrPC is not confined to physical incapability and includes, for example, absence due to employment abroad. No prejudice to the complainant was shown and counsel had undertaken to appear on every date, so the revision was allowed and the accused were exempted from personal appearance. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 596.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 22-A and 22-B: Successive Petitions With False Affidavits
records.heading: Repeated section 22-A and 22-B petitions with false first-petition certificates: holding not stated
records.text: Concerns a petitioner who filed repeated applications under ss. 22-A and 22-B CrPC, each with a certificate that it was the first petition on the subject, in several districts. The post is cut before the holding and the outcome is not stated. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 640; Khurram Imtiaz v. Additional Sessions Judge, Islamabad.
records.title: Khurram Imtiaz v. Additional Sessions Judge, Islamabad

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Clean Hands for Discretionary Relief
records.heading: Discretionary relief under Article 199 requires the petitioner to come with clean hands
records.text: Relief under the discretionary and equitable constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court under Art. 199 requires as a pre-condition that the parties approach the court with clean hands. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 640; Khurram Imtiaz v. Additional Sessions Judge, Islamabad.
records.title: Khurram Imtiaz v. Additional Sessions Judge, Islamabad

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 124-A PPC Sedition Struck Down
records.heading: Section 124-A PPC on sedition struck down as unconstitutional, per the file title
records.text: The file title states that s. 124-A PPC (sedition) was declared unconstitutional and contrary to fundamental rights, struck down, and removed from the Pakistan Penal Code. No reasoning is given in the post. Ref: 2023 LHC 1450.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 124-A PPC Violates Arts. 19 and 19A
records.heading: Section 124-A PPC violates Articles 19 and 19A and is void as a whole
records.text: S. 124-A PPC is unconstitutional and offends the fundamental rights in Arts. 19 and 19A of the Constitution. Being inconsistent with and in derogation of fundamental rights, it is void as a whole and struck down. Ref: Haroon Farooq v. Federation of Pakistan (W.P. No. 59599 of 2022, decided 30.03.2023).
records.title: Haroon Farooq v. Federation of Pakistan (W.P. No. 59599 of 2022, decided 30.03.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Where Offence Not Within Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Bail is the rule and refusal the exception outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: For offences not falling within the prohibition in s. 497 CrPC, grant of bail is the rule and refusal the exception. Ref: 2023 SCMR 679, 2023 SCMR 734.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: Delay of Nine Months in FIR
records.heading: A nine month FIR delay and no recovery made the case one of further inquiry
records.text: In a dacoity, wrongful confinement and criminal intimidation case, the crime report was lodged after nine months and sixteen days with an unacceptable explanation. No recovery was made despite physical remand and the accused had been in custody over five months. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, and the accused was admitted to bail. Ref: 2023 SCMR 734.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Rule of Consistency
records.heading: Bail granted on the rule of consistency where the sim belonged to a bailed co-accused
records.text: The accused was nominated for transmitting objectionable photographs and videos, but the sim used belonged to a co-accused who had already been granted bail. He became entitled to bail on the rule of consistency, and he had no previous criminal record. Appeal allowed and bail granted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 679.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 113 Limitation Act: Specific Performance
records.heading: Three years under Article 113 run from the date fixed for performance in the agreement
records.text: Where the agreement fixes a date for performance, the three years under Art. 113 of the Limitation Act, 1908 run from that date, and only if none is fixed from the date of refusal being noticed. Here the transaction was to be completed by 15.10.2002, so the first part applied, suit was due by 14.10.2005 and the suit filed on 30.7.2008 was late. Ref: Mazhar Hussain v. Mst. Jantan Bibi (C.R. No. 20075 of 2023, decided 27.03.2023).
records.title: Mazhar Hussain v. Mst. Jantan Bibi (C.R. No. 20075 of 2023, decided 27.03.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: NEPRA Alone Determines Tariff and Subsidies
records.heading: Only NEPRA can determine tariff and adjust electricity based subsidies
records.text: Only NEPRA can determine the tariff and adjust electricity based subsidies in the tariff. Ref: K-Electric Limited v. Federation of Pakistan (C.A. 1011/2020, decided 19.01.2023); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: K-Electric Limited v. Federation of Pakistan (C.A. 1011/2020, decided 19.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Compliance With Procedure and Discretion on Penal Provisions
records.heading: Penal provisions are applied on wilful default and not mechanically, with condonation absent deliberate disregard
records.text: Compliance with procedural rules is fundamental to the course of litigation. In construing penal provisions the court's discretion must rest on sound reasons, and non-compliance may be condoned where there was no deliberate disregard of an order. Penal provisions are to be applied thoughtfully, on wilful failure and deliberate default, and not mechanically. Ref: 2023 SCMR 636.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XI Rr. 1 and 2 CPC: Interrogatories
records.heading: Interrogatories are to be used fairly and abuse to prolong trial must be curbed
records.text: Interrogatories shorten litigation if fairly used, but abuse to prolong the trial must be curbed heavily. The trial court's power under R. 1 of O. XI to examine and reject irrelevant interrogatories is permissive, and the party should seek examination by application under R. 7 or by answering and objecting under R. 6. Ref: 2023 SCMR 636.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 1 CPC: Adjournments Discretionary
records.heading: Adjournment under Order XVII Rule 1 is discretionary and not interfered with absent perversity
records.text: The trial court's power under R. 1 of O. XVII CPC to grant an adjournment on sufficient cause is discretionary. An appellate court cannot interfere with an order granting or refusing an adjournment unless the discretion was exercised perversely or arbitrarily. Ref: 2023 SCMR 636.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Striking Out Defence for Failure to Answer Interrogatories
records.heading: An order striking out a defence for unanswered interrogatories was set aside and remanded
records.text: In a defamation suit the defendant repeatedly delayed the case and did not answer interrogatories despite many opportunities. Per the majority view, the trial court committed no irregularity in rejecting his objections. The order striking out his defence was nevertheless set aside and the case remanded to allow him a reasonable opportunity to answer the interrogatories. Ref: 2023 SCMR 636; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XI R. 21 CPC: Wilful Default and Contumacious Conduct
records.heading: Penal action under Order XI Rule 21 requires wilful, deliberate default and contumacious conduct
records.text: Penal action under R. 21 of O. XI CPC for default in answering interrogatories or giving discovery is strictly construed and requires wilful, deliberate default. Conduct is material, and contumacy may be shown by disregard of a specific order after sufficient opportunity or by a series of inordinate delays at different stages. Ref: 2023 SCMR 636.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XI R. 21 CPC: Suo Motu Penal Action
records.heading: The court may take penal action under Order XI Rule 21 suo motu after a last opportunity warning
records.text: Penal action under R. 21 of O. XI CPC may be taken by the court on a party's application and also suo motu. The trial court may act on its own if its order is not complied with despite a warning of last opportunity. Ref: 2023 SCMR 636.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XI R. 21 CPC: Oral Application Sufficient
records.heading: An oral application suffices for action under Order XI Rule 21 CPC
records.text: The expression apply in R. 21 of O. XI CPC includes an oral application or request, and the application need not necessarily be in writing. Ref: 2023 SCMR 636.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Arts. 10A and 37(d): Adjournments and Case Management
records.heading: Unjustified adjournments defeat timelines and peremptory orders must be followed by consequences
records.text: Leniency by trial judges in granting unjustified adjournments, at the cost of statutory timelines, is unwarranted. A peremptory order with a last opportunity warning must be followed by the legal consequences of non-compliance, and rules with time limits should be observed. A court-controlled case management system is needed to conclude litigation within a reasonable time. Ref: 2023 SCMR 636.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: R. 22 Punjab Agricultural Pesticides Rules 2018: Read Down
records.heading: Rule 22 of the 2018 Pesticides Rules is read down to require PNAC accredited standards
records.text: Laboratories in Pakistan can be accredited or certified only by PNAC. R. 22 of the 2018 Rules, requiring ISO certification, was irreconcilable with s. 13 of the Agricultural Pesticides Ordinance, 1971 and s. 4 of the PNAC Act, 2017, and the Supreme Court saved it by reading it down to require compliance with standards accredited by PNAC. Ref: 2023 SCMR 774.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 9 CPC: Civil Court Jurisdiction for Pure Economic Loss
records.heading: A civil court may try a damages suit for pure economic loss against a State corporation
records.text: A civil court did not lack jurisdiction to try a suit for damages against a State corporation for tortious breach causing pure economic loss to its employee. Where no law regulates such breaches, the civil court as a court of plenary jurisdiction may entertain, adjudicate and decree the suit. Ref: 2023 SCMR 616.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Tort of Economic Loss: Burden of Proof and Sovereign Immunity
records.heading: The claimant must prove economic loss and sovereign immunity has been done away with
records.text: In a suit arising from an employment dispute the damage was mainly economic and the claimant bears the burden of proving it. The respondent discharged it by documentary evidence of legal fees aggregating Rs.310,000. The post also records that sovereign immunity has been done away with, relying on PLD 1962 SC 28. Ref: 2023 SCMR 616.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. I R. 10 CPC: Addition and Striking Out of Parties
records.heading: Under Order I Rule 10 the court may add or strike out parties at any stage
records.text: Under O. I R. 10 CPC the court may at any stage, on application or without, strike out a party improperly joined and add a party who ought to have been joined or whose presence is necessary for complete adjudication. The object is to bring all persons concerned on record, avoid protraction and multiplicity of proceedings. Ref: 2023 SCMR 755.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Amendment of Plaint After Conclusion of Evidence
records.heading: Amendment of the plaint after evidence was refused where it was an abuse of process
records.text: In a suit for specific performance of an oral agreement the vendees sought amendment of the plaint after evidence to allege that an impleaded defendant was not the vendor's son. The Supreme Court held their interest was better protected with him remaining a defendant, given the s. 12(2) CPC risk. Appeal allowed, the amendment orders set aside, with costs for abuse of process. Ref: 2023 SCMR 613.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Son Quota Appointment: Concealed Criminal Case
records.heading: Acquittal under section 265-K does not show no probability of conviction for a concealed case
records.text: The respondent was acquitted under s. 265-K CrPC of murdering his wife, but without evidence it cannot be said there was no probability of conviction. The Bank refused to let him join as cashier, a post of importance, and acted within its domain. Appeal allowed and the High Court's direction to allow him to join was set aside. Ref: 2023 SCMR 766.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Misappropriation of Public Money: Refund and Long Service No Mitigation
records.heading: Refund of misappropriated public money and long service are no mitigation for dismissal
records.text: A civil servant cannot claim leniency merely because he refunded misappropriated money, nor treat embezzlement of public money as minor misconduct. Long service is no ground to convert dismissal into compulsory retirement, as such leniency would license misconduct near retirement. Ref: 2023 SCMR 770.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Non-Production of Narcotics Case Property at Trial
records.heading: Failure to produce narcotics case property at trial without explanation defeats the prosecution
records.text: The prosecution must produce and exhibit the recovered narcotics and vehicle in court. If destroyed under s. 516-A CrPC, destruction requires notice to the accused and must occur in his presence or his representative's, with samples and the Magistrate's certificate exhibited. The case property was not produced without explanation, so the prosecution failed and the accused were acquitted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 781.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: S. 489-F PPC, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail allowed in a section 489-F case with delayed FIR and unproved payment
records.text: The accused himself stopped payment of the cheque, claiming it was removed from his cheque book without authority. The FIR was lodged after unexplained delay and no proof was yet shown that the complainant paid the amount. This made the case one of further inquiry, so the petition was converted into an appeal and pre-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 748.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 516-A CrPC: Superdari of Vehicle to Registered Owner
records.heading: The registered owner is prima facie entitled to superdari of the vehicle under section 516-A
records.text: The registered owner of a vehicle is prima facie entitled to its temporary custody (superdari) under s. 516-A CrPC unless a court of competent jurisdiction decides a dispute as to title. Ref: 2023 SCMR 711.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Right to Cross-Examine in Inquiry: Art. 10A
records.heading: An accused in an inquiry has a right to cross-examine witnesses under Article 10A
records.text: The accused in an inquiry has a vested right to defend and to cross-examine witnesses, as trustworthiness can be tested only by cross-examination. Denying cross-examination of the departmental representative who led evidence and produced documents is against Art. 10A of the Constitution. Ref: 2023 SCMR 603.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Remand to Lower Fora Not a Vested Right
records.heading: Remand is not a vested right and requires a material error causing serious prejudice
records.text: Remand cannot be claimed as a vested right. The court or tribunal must first determine whether a material error or defect adversely affected the corpus of the case and caused serious prejudice on essential questions of law or fact. Ref: 2023 SCMR 603.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Pedigree Table Alone Does Not Prove Relationship
records.heading: A pedigree table on a mutation does not prove relationship without independent evidence
records.text: A pedigree table on a mutation is not proof of relationship unless proved by witnesses or independent evidence. Producing it through counsel without corroboration cannot show that a party was unrelated to the deceased. The sisters were held illegally excluded from inheritance and the mutation invalid. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 730; Rustam v. Jehangir (deceased) through LRs (Civil Appeal No. 106-L of 2010, decided 19.12.2022); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Rustam v. Jehangir (deceased) through LRs (Civil Appeal No. 106-L of 2010, decided 19.12.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Common Intention or Common Object in Qatl-i-amd
records.heading: The court must ascertain common intention or object among multiple assailants in qatl-i-amd
records.text: Authority on the duty of the court, where there are multiple assailants in qatl-i-amd, to ascertain common intention or common object at the time of framing the charge and sentencing the accused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 750.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Crime Empties Sent With Weapon to FSL
records.heading: A positive FSL report loses value where crime empties were sent together with the weapon
records.text: Where crime empties are sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory after the accused's arrest or together with the crime weapon, the positive report loses its evidentiary value. Sending them together is unsafe for sustaining conviction and suggests foul play by the Investigating Officer. Ref: 2023 SCMR 670.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: One Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single doubt entitles the accused to its benefit
records.text: For the benefit of doubt, many circumstances creating uncertainty are unnecessary, and a single doubt entitles the accused to its benefit. Ref: 2023 SCMR 670.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive: Prosecution Must Prove Alleged Motive
records.heading: An alleged motive must be proved by cogent evidence or the failure favours the accused
