records.text: If the prosecution alleges a specific motive, it must establish it through cogent and confidence-inspiring evidence, failing which the failure goes in favour of the accused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 670.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reappraisal of Evidence: Acquittal in Qatl-i-amd
records.heading: Distant, unlit and unreliable ocular witnesses led to acquittal in a qatl-i-amd appeal
records.text: The complainant was a distant relative living 6 kilometres away, the deceased's son who allegedly witnessed the occurrence was given up, no source of light was mentioned for a night occurrence, and both ocular witnesses lived 5 to 6 kilometres away. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Appeal allowed and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 670.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Minor conflicts between ocular and medical evidence are possible and should be ignored
records.text: Minor conflicts between ocular and medical evidence are quite possible, since witnesses at a momentary glance cannot state the number and location of injuries exactly. Minor discrepancies on trivial matters that do not shake the salient features of the prosecution case should be ignored. Ref: 2023 SCMR 795.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence, which is only corroborative
records.text: Trustworthy and confidence-inspiring ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices to sustain conviction. Medical evidence and recovery are corroborative in nature and alone cannot sustain conviction. Ref: 2023 SCMR 795.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Eyewitnesses Not Discarded Merely for Relationship
records.heading: Related eyewitnesses whose presence was natural can be relied on even for capital punishment
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony. If their presence was natural and their evidence straightforward and confidence-inspiring, it can safely be relied on even to award capital punishment. Ref: 2023 SCMR 795.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Premeditated Murder: Death Sentence Upheld
records.heading: A prompt FIR, independent eyewitnesses and a confession upheld the death sentence for premeditated murder
records.text: The FIR was lodged within an hour at the hospital, the occurrence was in daylight between known persons, and the ocular witnesses included two independent Family Court bailiffs. Medical evidence, motive, a positive Forensic Science Laboratory report and a confession before the Magistrate also supported the case. Premeditation was indicated, so the appeal was dismissed and the death sentence upheld. Ref: 2023 SCMR 795.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Preferred; Medical Evidence Corroborative
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred and medical evidence and recovery are only corroborative
records.text: Trustworthy ocular evidence is given preference over medical evidence and alone suffices to sustain conviction in qatl-i-amd cases. Medical evidence and recovery are always corroborative and alone cannot sustain conviction. Ref: 2023 SCMR 723.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Medical Discrepancies Do Not Negate Direct Evidence
records.heading: Minor medical discrepancies on injuries do not negate direct evidence
records.text: Minor discrepancies in medical evidence on the nature of injuries do not negate direct evidence, as witnesses are not expected to give a photographic picture of the ocular account. Ref: 2023 SCMR 723.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Relationship of Witnesses With Deceased
records.heading: Mere relationship with the deceased is no ground to discard prosecution witnesses
records.text: Mere relationship of prosecution witnesses with the deceased cannot be a ground to discard their testimony. Ref: 2023 SCMR 723.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reappraisal of Evidence: Prompt FIR and Natural Witnesses
records.heading: A same day FIR after hospital treatment is prompt and the conviction was maintained
records.text: The FIR was lodged on the same day after the injured were first taken to hospital, which showed promptitude. The occurrence was in daylight between known persons and the witnesses' presence was natural. The weapon was recovered at the accused's instance and the Forensic Science Laboratory report was positive. Conviction under ss. 302(b), 324 and 337-D PPC was maintained. Ref: 2023 SCMR 723.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Reduced to Life: Motive Not Established
records.heading: A motive discarded after a compromise justified reducing the death sentence to life imprisonment
records.text: The alleged motive, a love marriage two years earlier, was rightly discarded by the High Court because the grievance had been redressed by a compromise. As the motive was disbelieved, the High Court rightly converted the death sentence to life imprisonment. Petitions for leave to appeal dismissed and leave refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 723.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Two Member Bench Cannot Alter High Court Judgment Without Leave
records.heading: A two member bench cannot modify a High Court judgment without granting leave
records.text: A two member Supreme Court bench could grant leave or dismiss a petition under O. XI of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980 but could not modify a High Court Division Bench judgment without granting leave, which needed a three member bench. The review petition was allowed and the petition for leave restored for hearing before a three member bench. Ref: 2023 SCMR 737.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Precedent: Same or Similar Law Interpreted
records.heading: A precedent arises only where the law interpreted is the same or similar
records.text: To constitute a precedent, the law interpreted must be the same as or similar to that in the case in hand. Ref: 2023 SCMR 681.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Reasonable Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single reasonable doubt entitles the accused to acquittal as of right and not of grace
records.text: For the benefit of doubt, multiple infirmities are unnecessary and a single or slightest reasonable doubt in the prosecution case suffices, as a matter of right and not of grace. The judgment relies on a long list of earlier Supreme Court decisions. Ref: 2023 SCMR 781.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recall of Witness to Fill Lacuna
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC cannot be used to recall a witness merely to fill a lacuna
records.text: A prosecution witness cannot be summoned for re-examination merely to fill a lacuna, or trials would never end. S. 540 CrPC gives wide power but is not for filling lacunae or protracting proceedings. The witness had already been examined twice, refusal caused no miscarriage of justice, and revision lies only in exceptional circumstances. Ref: Ghulam Madni v. The State and five others (Crl. Revision No. 203 of 2022, decided 17.11.2022).
records.title: Ghulam Madni v. The State and five others (Crl. Revision No. 203 of 2022, decided 17.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Common Intention and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Common intention and further inquiry in pre-arrest bail: discussion, no outcome
records.text: Discussion of constructive liability in sharing a common intention to commit a criminal act, and of further inquiry, which presupposes a tentative assessment that may create doubt about the accused's involvement. The post gives no outcome. Ref: Ahtisham Ali v. The State (Crl.P. 13-K/2023, decided 22.03.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ahtisham Ali v. The State (Crl.P. 13-K/2023, decided 22.03.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 382-B CrPC: Mandatory Benefit of Pre-Conviction Detention
records.heading: Section 382-B CrPC is mandatory and requires credit for pre-conviction detention
records.text: After substitution of shall for may in 1979, s. 382-B CrPC is mandatory, and courts must give the accused credit for time spent in jail before conviction, to compensate for delay in trial. It also applies where a death sentence was set aside and the accused convicted under s. 302(c) PPC and sentenced to fifteen years. Ref: Muhammad Aslam v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 6795-M of 2022, decided 06.10.2022).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 6795-M of 2022, decided 06.10.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 94 and 540 CrPC: Summoning Custodian of Documents
records.heading: Documents cannot be produced without summoning their custodian or the person who prepared them
records.text: Under ss. 94 and 540 CrPC the court may summon a person holding documents or a witness essential to a just decision, but cannot allow production of documents without summoning the custodian or the person who prepared them. The petitioner had sought neither, so the Special Judge's order contained no illegality. Ref: Ch. Noman Haseeb v. The Learned Special Judge Anti-Corruption Court, Bahawalpur and four others (Criminal Revision No. 217 of 2022).
records.title: Ch. Noman Haseeb v. The Learned Special Judge Anti-Corruption Court, Bahawalpur and four others (Criminal Revision No. 217 of 2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 182 PPC: False Information to Public Servant
records.heading: Section 182 PPC has three ingredients and only the public servant may proceed against the informant
records.text: The post sets out the three ingredients of s. 182 PPC: information to a public servant, the informant's knowledge that it is false, and intent to cause the public servant to act or omit to the injury or annoyance of another. It is for the public servant to move against the informant, and no other authority can direct the police officer to proceed against the first informant. Ref: Umair Afzal v. The Additional Sessions Judge/Justice of Peace, Bahawalpur and three others (Writ Petition No. 9774 of 2022).
records.title: Umair Afzal v. The Additional Sessions Judge/Justice of Peace, Bahawalpur and three others (Writ Petition No. 9774 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence in Murder Reference
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence in a murder reference: authority, no holding
records.text: Authority on circumstantial evidence, arising from a murder reference and the accused's criminal appeal. The post gives no holding or outcome. Ref: Abdul Jabbar v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 351-J of 2022; Murder Reference No. 14 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Jabbar v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 351-J of 2022; Murder Reference No. 14 of 2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Gas Utility Court Exclusive Jurisdiction Over Gas Theft
records.heading: The Gas Utility Court has exclusive jurisdiction over gas theft cases
records.text: The Gas Utility Court has exclusive jurisdiction to decide gas theft cases. Ref: Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority v. Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (C.P. 797/2021, decided 31.01.2023); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority v. Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (C.P. 797/2021, decided 31.01.2023)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test Without Consent Violates Arts. 9 and 14
records.heading: A DNA test without consent violates Articles 9 and 14 and civil law gives no power for it
records.text: A DNA test without consent infringes privacy, personal liberty and Arts. 9 and 14 of the Constitution. Only certain criminal provisions permit it, and civil law gives no such power. It is unnecessary where paternity is consistently documented or the father never denied it. The request in a paternity dispute over property was rejected. Ref: Muhammad Nawaz v. Additional District and Session Judge, Gujranwala (C.P. 2414-L/2015, decided 05.04.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. Additional District and Session Judge, Gujranwala (C.P. 2414-L/2015, decided 05.04.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Vague and Multifarious Constitutional Petition Not Maintainable
records.heading: A vague and multifarious constitutional petition needing a roving inquiry is not maintainable
records.text: A constitutional petition resting on jumbled, incoherent and vague facts, raising multifarious grounds needing a roving inquiry, with undisclosed results of remedies sought elsewhere, was dismissed as not maintainable. Ref: 2023 YLR 767.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: PEMRA Prohibition: Opinion of Councils of Complaints
records.heading: PEMRA must consider the opinion of the Councils of Complaints before a prohibition order
records.text: PEMRA must consider the opinion of the Councils of Complaints before passing a prohibition order under s. 27(a) of the PEMRA Ordinance, 2002. The judgment also discusses tolerance under the Constitution, the scope of freedom of expression and the right to information, and the commonly accepted standard of decency. Ref: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority v. M/s ARY Communication Private Limited (C.P. 3506/2020, decided 12.04.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority v. M/s ARY Communication Private Limited (C.P. 3506/2020, decided 12.04.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Bar Associations Are Private Bodies: Writ Not Maintainable
records.heading: Bar Associations are private bodies and a writ against them is not maintainable
records.text: District and Tehsil Bar Associations are private organisations, and their Executive and Auction Committees, awarding contracts, are private parties not performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Federation. A constitutional petition against them is not maintainable. Ref: 2023 YLR 809.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell by Father of Minors
records.heading: A father cannot sell minors' immovable property without a guardian of property certificate
records.text: A father, though legal guardian, cannot sell the immovable property of minors without a certificate or appointment as guardian of property under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, save in the exceptional cases it provides (ss. 29, 359, 362). The purchasers' payment to an unauthorised person and their three years of inaction made their version doubtful. Ref: 2023 YLR 854.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Unbroken Chain Required
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete and unbroken chain to the accused
records.text: Where the occurrence was unwitnessed and the prosecution relies on circumstantial evidence, a weak type of evidence, each circumstance must link to the next in a complete, continuous and unbroken chain firmly connecting the accused with the offence. If any link is missing, the benefit goes to the accused. Ref: 2023 YLR 901; Syed Ali Akbar v. The State.
records.title: Syed Ali Akbar v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Cannot Identify the Culprit
records.heading: Medical evidence cannot connect the accused with the commission of the crime
records.text: Medical evidence may confirm the ocular account as to the seat, nature and duration of injuries and the kind of weapon used, but it cannot connect the accused with the commission of the crime. Ref: 2023 YLR 901; Syed Ali Akbar v. The State.
records.title: Syed Ali Akbar v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Burden on Prosecution and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: The prosecution must prove its case beyond doubt and a single doubt gives the accused the benefit
records.text: The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, and failing that the accused gets the benefit of doubt. Multiple doubts are unnecessary, as even a single circumstance creating doubt in a prudent mind suffices, and the benefit is a matter of right. Ref: 2023 YLR 793.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Defence Plea Accepted or Rejected in Toto
records.heading: A defence plea is accepted or rejected as a whole and the prosecution cannot rely on its weakness
records.text: The prosecution must establish its case independently and cannot rely on weaknesses of the defence. A defence plea is accepted or rejected as a whole, and picking only the sentences favouring the prosecution is prohibited. Ref: 2023 YLR 793.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 63(1)(n) & (o): Cutoff Date for Clearing Dues
records.heading: The cutoff date for clearing dues under Article 63(1)(n) and (o) is the last date for nominations
records.text: The cutoff date for clearing loans, government dues and utility expenses under Art. 63(1)(n) and (o) of the Constitution is the last date for filing nomination papers. The non obstante clause of s. 62(10) of the Elections Act, 2017 applies only where the candidate shows he was unaware of the liability when filing nomination papers. Ref: 2023 LHC 2096; Faisal Aziz v. Returning Officer PP-82 (Election Appeal 24133/23, decided 11.04.2023); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Faisal Aziz v. Returning Officer PP-82 (Election Appeal 24133/23, decided 11.04.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: No Further Investigation in a Concluded Case
records.heading: No further investigation or section 161 statement is possible in a concluded case
records.text: No law permits recording a statement under s. 161 Cr.P.C. once a case is decided. After the Supreme Court ruling in Sughran Bibi, all versions after the FIR are recorded under s. 161 Cr.P.C., so reinvestigation or further investigation in a concluded case is impossible. Ref: Zubaida Khanum v. District Police Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 18561/2021).
records.title: Zubaida Khanum v. District Police Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 18561/2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act Suspended
records.heading: The Supreme Court suspended the Practice and Procedure Act as prima facie interfering with judicial independence
records.text: The Supreme Court suspended operation of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act until further orders, observing that it prima facie interferes with judicial independence and internal affairs. The order notes the President returned the Bill under Art. 75, and political parties may join as parties. Matter fixed for 02.05.2023. Ref: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan (Const.P.6/2023, decided 13.04.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan (Const.P.6/2023, decided 13.04.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Direct Release of Election Funds to ECP
records.heading: State Bank directed to release Punjab election funds directly to the Election Commission
records.text: The Supreme Court directed the acting Governor of the State Bank to release funds for the Punjab elections directly to the Election Commission of Pakistan. Ref: Mohammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Election Commission of Pakistan (Const.P.5/2023, decided 14.04.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Mohammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Election Commission of Pakistan (Const.P.5/2023, decided 14.04.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Place of Sessions Trial: Option to Accused
records.heading: The accused must be offered a choice of sub-division trial in sessions cases under section 190
records.text: Sessions cases (excluding Hadood cases) are normally tried at the District Headquarters, but when the accused appears before the Magistrate under s. 190 Cr.P.C. he must be given and the record must show the choice of trial at the sub-division. Mechanical forwarding without offering this choice was irregular. The Sessions Judge was directed to conclude the trial within six months. Ref: Muhammad Waqar alias Fauji v. The State (Crl. Misc. No.76558/T/2022, decided 07.03.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Waqar alias Fauji v. The State (Crl. Misc. No.76558/T/2022, decided 07.03.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Returning Officer Cannot Declare Under Art. 62(1)(f)
records.heading: A Returning Officer cannot make an Article 62(1)(f) declaration in summary proceedings
records.text: A Returning Officer has no power to issue a declaration in summary proceedings. The Art. 62(1)(f) declaration against the appellant was made on 20.03.2023 without recording evidence and without giving reasons for invoking disqualification. Ref: Kashif Mehmood v. Election Commission of Pakistan and 2 others (Election Appeal No.6 of 2023/BWP, heard 13.04.2023).
records.title: Kashif Mehmood v. Election Commission of Pakistan and 2 others (Election Appeal No.6 of 2023/BWP, heard 13.04.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 62(1)(f): Specific Declaration Required
records.heading: Disqualification under Article 62(1)(f) requires a specific declaration by a court
records.text: Disqualification under Art. 62(1)(f) of the Constitution requires a specific declaration by a court. General directions to the Election Commission to initiate criminal proceedings against persons accused of corrupt practices or forgery cannot be treated as such a declaration to debar a person for life. Ref: Muhammad Rizwan Nowaiz Gill v. The Returning Officer PP-77, Sargodha-VI (Election Appeal No.24144/2023, heard 12.04.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan Nowaiz Gill v. The Returning Officer PP-77, Sargodha-VI (Election Appeal No.24144/2023, heard 12.04.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: GPF and Gratuity as Tarka
records.heading: GPF and gratuity of a deceased are tarka and pass to the legal heirs
records.text: General Provident Fund and gratuity of a deceased were held to be tarka that goes to the legal heirs, and the real sister, as the only legal heir, was entitled to the amount. Ref: 1999 CLC 806, 1999 PLC (C.S.) 793.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recalling Witnesses for Re-examination
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC allows recalling any witness whose evidence is essential to a just decision
records.text: Under s. 540 Cr.P.C. the trial court may summon any person, or recall and re-examine any witness, whose evidence appears essential to a just decision, and is not confined to listed witnesses, provided there is no delay or defeat of justice. The prosecution gave plausible reasons, so the order allowing re-examination was justified. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 635.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Pension and Service Benefits Shared Among Heirs
records.heading: Pension benefits of a civil servant with two widows must be shared among all heirs
records.text: On the death of a civil servant leaving two widows and children, the pension benefits, Group Insurance and Benevolent Fund inherited by one widow and her daughter are to be shared with the other widow and her children. The Division Bench directed payment to both widows and other heirs, with recovery of any excess received. Ref: 2018 CLC 392.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Omission of Spouse's Assets in Nomination Papers
records.heading: Omission of a wife's assets in nomination papers is not fatal absent bad faith
records.text: Under s. 62(9)(c) of the Elections Act, 2017 false statements may lead to rejection of nomination papers, but omission of the wife's assets and liabilities is not equivalent to omission of the candidate's own or his dependants'. The wife is under no legal duty to disclose them to him, so the omission is not fatal unless made in bad faith to gain undue benefit. Ref: 2023 LHC 2156; Sheikh Muhammad Akram v. The Returning Officer PP-126 (Election Appeal 24497/23, decided 14.04.2023); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Sheikh Muhammad Akram v. The Returning Officer PP-126 (Election Appeal 24497/23, decided 14.04.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutation Challenged by Minor: Limitation
records.heading: A suit by a minor challenging a gift mutation is within six years of attaining majority
records.text: A person under eighteen is a minor under s. 3 of the Majority Act, 1875 and cannot contract (s. 11 Contract Act, 1872). A suit challenging a gift mutation attested in her absence while a minor had to be filed within six years, and by s. 6 of the Limitation Act, 1908 within that period after attaining majority. Ref: 2023 MLD 665.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. II R. 1 and 2 CPC: Splitting of Claims
records.heading: A suit must include the whole claim and omitted portions cannot be sued on later
records.text: Under O. II R. 2 CPC every suit must include the whole claim arising from the cause of action, and a portion omitted or relinquished cannot be sued on afterwards. Cause of action means the bundle of facts the plaintiff must prove. The plaintiff was criticised for splitting claims between the High Court and the Civil Court, creating multiplicity of proceedings. Ref: Dr. Muhammad Amin v. Zarai Taraqiati Bank Ltd (C.P.2933/2019); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Dr. Muhammad Amin v. Zarai Taraqiati Bank Ltd (C.P.2933/2019)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: S. 234(5) Elections Act: Alternate Remedy Bars Writ
records.heading: An alternate remedy under section 234(5) of the Elections Act bars a constitutional petition
records.text: Under s. 234(5) of the Elections Act, 2017 'any person' aggrieved by the order of the nominated officer may appeal, including a contesting candidate seeking disqualification of rivals. A constitutional petition is therefore not maintainable in view of the alternate remedy, absent extraordinary circumstances. Ref: 2023 MLD 602.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Vertebral Injury in Medical Evidence
records.heading: Failure to explain a vertebral fracture left the cause of injury a mystery
records.text: The doctor failed to explain the nature of the vertebral fracture, whether compressed, crushed or dislocated, to report skin discolouration to gauge the time of injury, or to say whether it resulted from a direct blow or a fall. The absence of symptoms expected from a blunt weapon left the causation of injury No. 1 a mystery. Ref: 2023 MLD 629.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Documents Produced After Plaint: O. XIII R. 2 CPC
records.heading: Documents may be received after the plaint on good cause under Order XIII Rule 2
records.text: Failure to file documents with the plaint or at the first hearing is not fatal, as O. XIII R. 2 CPC allows the court to receive documentary evidence later on good cause. A document admitted without objection is deemed waived as to production, though the court may still examine its validity. Certified copies of revenue record are public documents and omission from the list of reliance did not justify de-exhibiting them. Ref: 2023 CLC 713.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: De-exhibiting Documents: O. XIII CPC
records.heading: The CPC does not provide for de-exhibiting documents once received and marked
records.text: The term de-exhibit does not appear in the CPC. O. XIII R. 3 allows rejection of irrelevant or inadmissible documents, but it was not intended that documents be removed after being received and marked as exhibits. The party may take back the document under O. XIII R. 9. Compliance with O. XIII R. 4 on marking exhibits is mandatory. Ref: 2023 CLC 713.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit Treated as S. 12(2) CPC Application
records.heading: A suit alleging fraud in a decree may be treated as a section 12(2) CPC application
records.text: Procedural laws advance justice and courts favour adjudication on merits. Where the plaint alleged that the decree was obtained by fraud, the appellate court was justified in treating the suit as an application under s. 12(2) CPC, and no prejudice was caused to the defendants. Ref: 2023 CLC 782.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Issues and Evidence Not Mandatory
records.heading: Framing issues and recording evidence is not mandatory for a section 12(2) CPC application
records.text: It is not mandatory in every case to frame issues and record evidence to decide an application under s. 12(2) CPC, as s. 12(3) governs the procedure. The appellate court's direction, issued without first allowing the civil court an opportunity, was unwarranted and liable to interference. Ref: 2023 CLC 782.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for S. 12(2) CPC Application: Art. 181
records.heading: A section 12(2) CPC application is governed by Article 181 of the Limitation Act
records.text: The period of limitation for an application under s. 12(2) CPC is governed by Art. 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908. Ref: 2023 CLC 782.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 145 CPC: Liability of Surety for Decree
records.heading: A surety is liable in execution only to the extent stated in the surety bond
records.text: Under s. 145 CPC a decree may be executed against a surety only to the extent he has rendered himself personally liable, so the stipulations in the surety bond must be examined to ascertain the extent of liability. Ref: 2023 CLC 702.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Automatic Rent Increase under S. 5-A
records.heading: The rent increase under section 5-A is automatic and no landlord notice is required
records.text: A tenant must increase rent by 25% every three years as the statute requires, and failure is wilful default under s. 13(2)(i), allowing the Special Judge (Rent) to order eviction. The increase under s. 5-A is automatic, and no separate notice by the landlord is needed or is a condition precedent to jurisdiction. Ref: 2023 CLC 738.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Money Decree Cannot Be Sold in Execution
records.heading: A money decree cannot be sold in execution and must follow Order XXI Rule 53(2)
records.text: A money decree cannot be sold in execution, and once such a decree is attached the procedure in O. XXI R. 53(2) CPC must be followed. Ref: 2023 CLC 756.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 164: Setting Aside Ex Parte Decree
records.heading: Article 164 gives 30 days to set aside an ex parte decree and displaces Article 181
records.text: Art. 164 of the Limitation Act gives 30 days to apply to set aside an ex parte decree. Time runs from the decree where the defendant appeared or service of the first summons is undisputed, and from knowledge of the decree where summons were not served. The residuary Art. 181 cannot apply where another article provides the period. Ref: 2023 CLC 768.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Policy Decisions: Subsidised Wheat Price
records.heading: Fixing the subsidised wheat price is a policy matter and courts interfere only if arbitrary or mala fide
records.text: Fixing or increasing the subsidised price of wheat for mills is within the Government's policy domain, and the High Court ordinarily does not interfere unless the decision is manifestly arbitrary, mala fide, patently illegal or unreasonable. Ref: 2023 LHC 2208; Syed Faisal G. Meeran v. Province of Punjab etc. (Local Government 19723/23, decided 04.04.2023); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Syed Faisal G. Meeran v. Province of Punjab etc. (Local Government 19723/23, decided 04.04.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Struck-off Written Statement: Defendant May Still Cross-examine
records.heading: A defendant with a struck-off written statement may still cross-examine and lead rebuttal evidence
records.text: Although the Family Courts Act, 1964 has no express provision, a Family Court may in contumacious default make an order in the nature of O. VIII R. 10 CPC. Even without a written statement the defendant may cross-examine witnesses, lead rebuttal evidence and join final arguments. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 315; Raja Ibadat Sajjad Khan v. Mst. Shehnaz Kousar etc. (W.P. No. 13531 of 2022, heard 21.11.2022); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Raja Ibadat Sajjad Khan v. Mst. Shehnaz Kousar etc. (W.P. No. 13531 of 2022, heard 21.11.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII: Affidavit with Leave to Defend
records.heading: An application for leave to defend a summary suit on disputed facts needs an affidavit
records.text: Where an application for leave to defend in a summary suit needs resolution of disputed facts, it must be accompanied by an affidavit, failing which dismissal is justified. An affidavit may be unnecessary where the claim rests only on a question of law. Here the plea that cheques were issued as guarantee and misused needed an affidavit. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 330, 2023 YLR 1341; Muhammad Bashir v. Syed Imdad Ali Shah (C.R. No. 6746 of 2020, decided 24.11.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Bashir v. Syed Imdad Ali Shah (C.R. No. 6746 of 2020, decided 24.11.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Magistrate's Power of Discharge: Ss. 63 and 173
records.heading: A Magistrate may discharge an accused under section 63 during investigation and under section 173(3) after the report
records.text: Magistrates may discharge an accused after an FIR at two stages, under s. 63 Cr.P.C. during investigation and under s. 173(3) after the police final report. The Court noted conflicting authority on discharge under s. 63 at the s. 167 remand stage, and stressed the Magistrate's duty to safeguard liberty. The impugned order was set aside and the petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 345; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State etc. (W.P. No. 253 of 2022, heard 26.1.2022); Justice Muhammad Shan Gul.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State etc. (W.P. No. 253 of 2022, heard 26.1.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Superdari and Sealing Power under Punjab Food Authority Act
records.heading: The Food Safety Officer's sealing power under the Punjab Food Authority Act was declared ultra vires
records.text: On a petition concerning superdari under s. 516-A Cr.P.C., the Court found the sealing power of the Food Safety Officer under s. 13(1)(c) of the Punjab Food Authority Act, 2011 lacks guidelines, any remedy or any de-sealing mechanism, and is ex facie discriminatory. The proceedings were declared ultra vires and the seized whey powder bags were ordered handed to the petitioner. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 370; Wajid Ali v. Learned Judicial Magistrate etc. (W.P. No. 12205 of 2021, decided 21.11.2022); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Wajid Ali v. Learned Judicial Magistrate etc. (W.P. No. 12205 of 2021, decided 21.11.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Executing Court Can Undo Transfer to Defeat Decree
records.heading: An executing court may cancel a transfer made to frustrate a decree
records.text: Where a judgment debtor transferred property by disputed gift mutations after his writ petition against a maintenance decree was dismissed, the transfer was an attempt to frustrate the decree. The executing court had jurisdiction to undo it and rightly cancelled the mutations. The appellate court erred and the revision was accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 374, 2024 YLR 550; Mst. Robina Shehnaz v. Mukhtar Begum (C.R. No. 2701 of 2016, heard 24.1.2023); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Mst. Robina Shehnaz v. Mukhtar Begum (C.R. No. 2701 of 2016, heard 24.1.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Jactitation of Marriage: Burden of Proof
records.heading: A woman denying free consent to a marriage cannot be burdened to prove the negative
records.text: Where a woman's claim is in negative form, that she did not freely enter a marriage and the Nikahnama is forged, she cannot be burdened to prove it by further evidence. The respondent failed to establish her free consent. The petition was allowed, the judgments set aside and the suit for jactitation of marriage decreed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 376; Bakhtawar Bibi v. Additional District Judge and 2 others (W.P. No. 5819 of 2017, heard 31.10.2022); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Bakhtawar Bibi v. Additional District Judge and 2 others (W.P. No. 5819 of 2017, heard 31.10.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Comparison of Thumb-Impressions of Witnesses
records.heading: A party asserting thumb-impressions that witnesses deny must seek expert comparison
records.text: Where witnesses deny their thumb-impressions on a document, the party asserting them bears a heavy burden and must seek expert comparison with admitted impressions. Courts must take a liberal view of such requests, and delay is no ground to refuse. The petition was allowed and the trial court directed to decide the suit within two months of the expert report. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 384; Aashiq Hussain v. Fida Hussain and others (W.P. No. 6404 of 2020, heard 24.1.2023); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Aashiq Hussain v. Fida Hussain and others (W.P. No. 6404 of 2020, heard 24.1.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Fornication: Complaint under S. 203-C Mandatory
records.heading: A conviction for fornication requires a complaint under section 203-C CrPC
records.text: A conviction for fornication requires a complaint under s. 203-C Cr.P.C., and a private complaint under s. 376(ii) PPC is not competent for that offence. A male alone cannot be convicted of fornication, and the consenting female cannot be believed as a witness against him. Appeal accepted and the appellant acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 348, 2023 YLR 2412; Rashid Ahmed etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. A. No. 185 & Crl. Rev. No. 242 of 2015, heard 11.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Rashid Ahmed etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. A. No. 185 & Crl. Rev. No. 242 of 2015, heard 11.10.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint: Ss. 200 and 203 CrPC Procedure
records.heading: A Magistrate must examine a private complainant on oath and give brief reasons to dismiss under section 203
records.text: On receiving a private complaint the Magistrate must immediately examine the complainant on oath under s. 200 Cr.P.C. and record and sign the statement. A complaint under s. 203 may be dismissed only after considering the grounds with brief reasons. The revision was allowed and the matter remanded for a speaking order. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 361; Sajjad Ali v. Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Mandi Baha-ud-Din and 12 others (Crl. Rev. No. 56556 of 2020, decided 13.5.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Sajjad Ali v. Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Mandi Baha-ud-Din and 12 others (Crl. Rev. No. 56556 of 2020, decided 13.5.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Pre-Arrest Bail: Perverse Order
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail was cancelled where the order was perverse and call data linked co-accused to the scene
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was cancelled under ss. 497(5)/498 Cr.P.C. as the order was perverse. Call data record prima facie placed co-accused at the crime scene and the material connected the respondent with the murder offence. Mala fide false implication can be gathered from circumstances. The petition was accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 397; Haji Arshad Mehmood v. Farrukh Imtiaz Khokhar etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 2759-CB of 2022, decided 11.1.2023); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Haji Arshad Mehmood v. Farrukh Imtiaz Khokhar etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 2759-CB of 2022, decided 11.1.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused of Unsound Mind: Ss. 465 and 466 CrPC
records.heading: Unsoundness of mind must first be tried by voir dire under sections 465 and 466 CrPC
records.text: Ss. 465 and 466 Cr.P.C. are mandatory. The court must first try the fact of unsoundness by voir dire, a trial within a trial, in keeping with Art. 10-A. Schizophrenia is not a permanent mental disorder, so the application was rightly rejected. If found of unsound mind, the court orders bail or safe custody under s. 466. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 412, 2023 PCrLJ 1546; Muhammad Hanif v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 173 of 2022, decided 10.1.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 173 of 2022, decided 10.1.2023)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Petition Against a Dead Respondent
records.heading: A contempt petition against a respondent who had died and held no post then is not maintainable
records.text: A contempt petition under the Contempt of Court Ordinance, 2003 filed against a Medical Superintendent who had died two years earlier, and who held the post neither when the order was issued nor when the petition was filed, is not maintainable, as he had not disobeyed the order. The petition was dismissed, with liberty to file afresh against the incumbent. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 423; Muhammad Majid v. Dr. Muhammad Shahid Iqbal (Crl. Org. No. 29909 of 2022, decided 15.9.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Majid v. Dr. Muhammad Shahid Iqbal (Crl. Org. No. 29909 of 2022, decided 15.9.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Trial Cannot Be Adjourned Sine Die
records.heading: A Sessions trial cannot be adjourned sine die under Chapter XXII-A
records.text: Chapter XXII-A governing Sessions trials has no provision for adjourning a trial for an indefinite period. S. 249 Cr.P.C. allows it only to a Magistrate of the First Class and only in State cases, not complaint cases. The order of the Additional Sessions Judge dated 22.04.2022 was set aside and the revision allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 404.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record: Procedure for Proof and SOP
records.heading: A Call Data Record is proved as primary evidence and only the authorised officer may generate it
records.text: Leading three-judge bench authority on Call Data Record. A CDR is tendered and proved like other primary evidence, and the Investigating Officer receives it by recovery memo, treating it as primary evidence under Explanations 3 and 4 of Art. 73 QSO. Only the authorised officer may generate a CDR under the SOP and he cannot delegate that power. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 371, PLD 2024 Lahore 522; Mst. Saima Nareen v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal CM/2/59829/21).
records.title: Mst. Saima Nareen v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal CM/2/59829/21)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Father's Duty to Pay Daughter's Marriage Expenses
records.heading: A father must pay his daughter's marriage expenses according to his financial status
records.text: A father must provide reasonable maintenance to his daughter and also bear her marriage expenses according to his financial status. The appellate court's award was not excessive in view of the father's means and social norms, so the constitutional petition was dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 323; Muhammad Riaz Ahmad v. Mst. Shaheen Akhtar etc. (W.P. No. 40877 of 2021, decided 10.11.2022); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Riaz Ahmad v. Mst. Shaheen Akhtar etc. (W.P. No. 40877 of 2021, decided 10.11.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal Power to Impose Special Costs
records.heading: The Service Tribunal can impose special costs in a civil servant's appeal
records.text: The Service Tribunal can impose special costs while deciding the service appeal of a civil servant. Ref: Zakir Mehmood v. Secretary, Ministry of Defence (D.P) Pakistan Secretariat, Rawalpindi and others (C.P.2712/2020, decided 12.04.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Zakir Mehmood v. Secretary, Ministry of Defence (D.P) Pakistan Secretariat, Rawalpindi and others (C.P.2712/2020, decided 12.04.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Tribunal Cannot Direct Decision on Representation
records.heading: The Service Tribunal cannot direct a decision on a representation undecided for 90 days
records.text: Once it hears the service appeal, the Service Tribunal cannot direct the departmental authority to decide the civil servant's representation that remained undecided for 90 days before the appeal was filed. Ref: Dr. Sayyid Abdul Samad Pirzada v. The Chief Secretary Govt of Punjab Lahore & others (C.P.2009/2020, decided 13.04.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Dr. Sayyid Abdul Samad Pirzada v. The Chief Secretary Govt of Punjab Lahore & others (C.P.2009/2020, decided 13.04.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Order on Simultaneous Elections: 4 April Order Unaffected
records.heading: The 4 April order for Punjab elections stood unaffected by political dialogue on simultaneous elections
records.text: In its written order the Supreme Court issued notices to the Federation, the Election Commission and political leaderships on applications for simultaneous elections. It held the 4 April order for Punjab elections unaffected and in accord with the Constitution, which requires elections within 90 days of dissolution, and that political dialogue does not excuse duties under Arts. 112 and 224. Ref: Mohammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Election Commission of Pakistan (C.M.A.2769/2023, decided 19.04.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Mohammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Election Commission of Pakistan (C.M.A.2769/2023, decided 19.04.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail to Woman Accused of Abetment: Burnt Unidentified Body
records.heading: Bail granted to a woman accused of instigating murder where the body was burnt and unidentified
records.text: Bail was granted under s. 497 Cr.P.C. to a woman accused of instigating her husband's murder. The body was burnt and unidentified, with DNA report awaited, and she was implicated by a s. 164 statement recorded after 15 days. She was also a lady with a suckling child. The Peshawar High Court order was set aside. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 83; Mst. Asiya v. The State and another (Crl. P. No. 1267 of 2022, decided 18.11.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Mst. Asiya v. The State and another (Crl. P. No. 1267 of 2022, decided 18.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices for conviction
records.text: Where ocular evidence is trustworthy and confidence inspiring, it is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices for conviction. Casual discrepancies between the two are possible, witnesses cannot give an exact photographic account of injuries, and non-material conflicts do not damage the prosecution case. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 87.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Abetment under S. 109 PPC: Ingredients Required
records.heading: Abetment under section 107 PPC requires active complicity and substantial assistance before the offence
records.text: Abetment requires active complicity before the offence and substantial assistance to the principal culprit. The three ingredients of s. 107 PPC were missing, and a WhatsApp voice message between the appellants and the principal accused was insufficient. The second wife and step daughter were acquitted, and the complainant's petition against the High Court judgment was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 93; Mst. Hajira Bibi @ Seema and others v. Abdul Qaseem and another (Crl. A. No. 39-K, Crl. M.A. No. 113-K & Crl. P. No. 613 of 2022, decided 6.2.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Mst. Hajira Bibi @ Seema and others v. Abdul Qaseem and another (Crl. A. No. 39-K, Crl. M.A. No. 113-K & Crl. P. No. 613 of 2022, decided 6.2.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Cross-Version
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where the cross-version FIR came later and the complainant's stance was untrue
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was confirmed under s. 498 Cr.P.C. where the petitioner's father had lodged the first FIR, the cross-version was lodged six days later, and the complainant's stance was found untrue in investigation. This raised serious doubt about his allegations, and the investigating officer's opinion on the overt act needed evidence. The petition was converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 100; Muhammad Umar Waqas Barkat Ali v. The State and another (Crl. P. No. 352-L of 2022, decided 23.11.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Umar Waqas Barkat Ali v. The State and another (Crl. P. No. 352-L of 2022, decided 23.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Contradictory Account of Investigation and Night Occurrence
records.heading: Contradictory witness accounts of the investigation in a night occurrence led to acquittal
records.text: In a night occurrence with no source of light, PW-1's account of how the case was registered and the police proceedings was squarely contradicted by PW-2. The prosecution case was found doubtful, the appeal was allowed, the death sentence conviction set aside and the appellants acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 103; Sarfraz and another v. The State (Crl. A. No. 560 of 2020, decided 2.1.2023); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Sarfraz and another v. The State (Crl. A. No. 560 of 2020, decided 2.1.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reliable Ocular Account; Sentence under S. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: A provoked spur of the moment killing warranted modifying the sentence under section 302(c)
records.text: The ocular account was reliable and in line with the medical evidence, so conviction was sustained. As the occurrence took place at the spur of the moment without premeditation after something provoked the petitioners, the sentence was modified. The petition was converted into appeal and partly allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 112; Muhammad Abbas and another v. The State (J.P. No. 355 of 2018, decided 2.1.2023); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Abbas and another v. The State (J.P. No. 355 of 2018, decided 2.1.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 18 Limitation Act: Fraud and Fresh Limitation
records.heading: Section 18 of the Limitation Act is unavailable where fraud and date of knowledge are not pleaded
records.text: In a suit for declaration against a gift mutation by the plaintiff's father, who lived about 23 years after it, the plaintiff neither pleaded nor proved fraud, nor gave a date of knowledge. The benefit of s. 18 of the Limitation Act, 1908 for computing limitation was therefore unavailable. The Court also addressed s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 185; Mst. Rabia Gula and others v. Muhammad Janan and others (C.A. No. 139-P of 2013, decided 25.2.2022); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Mst. Rabia Gula and others v. Muhammad Janan and others (C.A. No. 139-P of 2013, decided 25.2.2022)

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Trade Union Registration by Trans-Provincial Establishment
records.heading: Registration of a trade union by a trans-provincial establishment under the Industrial Relations Act 2012
records.text: The Court considered the forum and law for registration of a trade union by a trans-provincial establishment. It noted the Industrial Relations Act, 2012 applies to persons employed in establishments in the Islamabad Capital Territory or carrying on business in more than one province. Ref: 2023 LHC 2257; M/S Independent Newspapers Corporation v. Province of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 3383-22, decided 10.04.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: M/S Independent Newspapers Corporation v. Province of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 3383-22, decided 10.04.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Purchase from Co-sharer Does Not Bar Execution
records.heading: A vendee from a co-sharer acquires no better title and cannot defeat a final decree for possession
records.text: A vendee from a co-sharer in a joint khata steps into the vendor's shoes and acquires no better title, and without formal partition the co-sharer cannot put the vendee in possession. The vendee's right is subject to partition. The purchase does not defeat a final decree for possession, and the executing court cannot go beyond the decree. Ref: 2023 LHC 2290; Mst Kaneez Batool v. Allah Buksh (Civil Revision 40110/22, decided 16.03.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mst Kaneez Batool v. Allah Buksh (Civil Revision 40110/22, decided 16.03.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Service of Summons under S. 8 Family Courts Act
records.heading: Personal service under section 8 of the Family Courts Act is not shown by a postal receipt alone
records.text: Personal service under s. 8 of the Family Courts Act, 1964 was not established where the process server was not produced and service was presumed only from a postal receipt without acknowledgment due. Reliance on publication was unsafe without showing personal service was impossible, particularly as the respondent described her as an illiterate villager. Ref: 2023 LHC 2265; Sadaf Rasheed v. Senior Civil Judge etc. (Family 81201/22, decided 25.01.2023); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Sadaf Rasheed v. Senior Civil Judge etc. (Family 81201/22, decided 25.01.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Relinquishment and Discretion
records.heading: Relinquishment of specific performance is decided on conduct and the relief remains discretionary
records.text: Relinquishment of the right to seek specific performance is decided on the conduct of the parties and the evidence led. Specific performance is discretionary and equitable, under s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, and may be declined if unjust and inequitable even where lawful to grant. Ref: 2023 LHC 2269; Asim Jamshed v. Shahzad Iqbal Malik etc. (Regular Second Appeal 64508/22, decided 28.03.2023); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Asim Jamshed v. Shahzad Iqbal Malik etc. (Regular Second Appeal 64508/22, decided 28.03.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: FIR Not Substantive Evidence
records.heading: An FIR is not substantive evidence and cannot found a conviction
records.text: An FIR is not substantive evidence and cannot be relied upon as such. Although an entry in a public or official register is admissible as a relevant fact under Art. 49 QSO, a conviction cannot be based on the FIR. Ref: 2023 LHC 2276; Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 255528/18, decided 10.04.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 255528/18, decided 10.04.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Polygraph Test as Investigative Technique
records.heading: The polygraph test as a useful investigative technique and medical evidence on the weapon used
records.text: Authority on the polygraph test as a useful investigative technique. The judgment also examines the medical evidence on close-range blackening and absence of an exit wound, and whether a pistol or rifle caused the injury, noting that matching the recovered bullet with the weapon would settle it. Ref: 2023 LHC 2276; Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 255528/18, decided 10.04.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 255528/18, decided 10.04.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Parity and Rule of Consistency in Bail
records.heading: Parity in bail requires comparable roles and consideration of tangible evidence against the accused
records.text: The rule of parity or consistency rests on treating like cases alike, with comparable roles or overt acts of co-offenders. To decide whether reasonable grounds exist for bail, courts must consider tangible evidence available against the accused. Ref: Bakhti Rahman v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P.207/2023, decided 15-03-2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Bakhti Rahman v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P.207/2023, decided 15-03-2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Order on Consensual Election Date Talks
records.heading: The Punjab election date of 14 May stood while leaders negotiated a consensual election date
records.text: The Supreme Court recorded the political leaders' positive statements on simultaneous general elections and their fidelity to the Constitution. Negotiations were to focus on a one-point agenda of a consensual election date. The Punjab election date of 14.05.2023 fixed in Const.P.5/2023 on 04.04.2023 stood, and the matter was listed for 27.04.2023. Ref: Sardar Kashif Khan v. Federation of Pakistan (Const.P.9/2023, decided 20.04.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Sardar Kashif Khan v. Federation of Pakistan (Const.P.9/2023, decided 20.04.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 18 Limitation Act: Fraud in Inheritance Suits
records.heading: Fraud under section 18 affects only limitation and must be pleaded with particulars and proved
records.text: Fraud under s. 18 of the Limitation Act relates only to concealing, not creating, the right to sue and so affects only limitation. The plaintiff must plead the fraud with particulars and date of knowledge under O. VI R. 4 CPC and prove it, and the benefit is unavailable against a bona fide purchaser for value. When a co-sharer's land is sold and possession transferred, the right to sue accrues from that sale. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 353.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Admission to MBBS: Art. 25-A and Late Intimation
records.heading: Late intimation by a university deprived a qualified candidate of admission in violation of Article 25-A
records.text: Courts ordinarily refrain from interfering in the internal affairs of educational institutions, but this is not a rule of universal application. The petitioner qualified MDCAT and was on the open merit list but was deprived of admission by late intimation from the university, violating Art. 25-A. Petition allowed and admission directed in first year MBBS 2022-23. Ref: 2023 LHC 2338; Muhammad Usman Farooq v. RWP Medical University etc. (Writ Petition 1132-23, decided 19-04-2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Usman Farooq v. RWP Medical University etc. (Writ Petition 1132-23, decided 19-04-2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI R. 1 CPC: Late List of Witnesses
records.heading: A late witness list needs good cause with recorded reasons under Order XVI Rule 1
records.text: O. XVI R. 1 CPC requires the list of witnesses within seven days of settlement of issues, and a party omitting it must obtain the court's permission by showing good cause, with reasons recorded. A list sought after the other side's evidence closed, on an unsupported plea lacking affidavit, was not excused, relying on 2020 SCMR 2155 and PLD 2013 SC 255. Ref: Muhammad Azam v. Muhammad Anwar Khan and 6 others (Civil Revision No. 50670 of 2020, heard 03.04.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Azam v. Muhammad Anwar Khan and 6 others (Civil Revision No. 50670 of 2020, heard 03.04.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Not a Punishment; No Onerous Conditions
records.heading: Bail is not a punishment and cannot carry conditions that make it ineffective
records.text: Bail cannot be withheld as punishment. Wrongful incarceration of an accused later acquitted cannot be repaired, and where entitlement to bail is found, it cannot be made subject to conditions that render it ineffective. Bail rests on the presumption of innocence, and its primary purpose is to secure attendance. Ref: Muhammad Taimur v. Chairman, National Accountability Bureau NAB Headquarters, Islamabad & others (Civil Petition No.278 of 2023, decided 17-04-2023).
records.title: Muhammad Taimur v. Chairman, National Accountability Bureau NAB Headquarters, Islamabad & others (Civil Petition No.278 of 2023, decided 17-04-2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Bribe-Giver and Bribe-Taker Both Liable
records.heading: Both bribe-giver and bribe-taker can be prosecuted subject to section 165-B PPC
records.text: Subject to s. 165-B PPC, both bribe-giver and bribe-taker can be prosecuted. Accepting money to procure a public servant's favour through personal influence falls within s. 163 PPC, whether or not the accused could in fact do the favour. A bribe-giver's claim for return of the bribe is entertained only where the taker agreed to pay it back. Ref: Salman Mushtaq v. Ex-officio Justice of Peace etc. (Writ Petition No. 58123/2022, heard 7.4.2023).
records.title: Salman Mushtaq v. Ex-officio Justice of Peace etc. (Writ Petition No. 58123/2022, heard 7.4.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Hatchets: Joint Recovery Inadmissible
records.heading: Recovery of non blood stained hatchets and a joint recovery are of no use to the prosecution
records.text: Recovery of hatchets that were not blood stained, both made from the accused's house on the same day, was of no use. A hatchet separated and shown as recovered on one accused's lead as the weapon of offence was a plantation, and a joint recovery was inadmissible. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 MLD 629.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eyewitnesses Doubted: Unnatural Conduct
records.heading: Unnatural conduct of claimed eyewitnesses made their presence doubtful
records.text: The claimed eyewitnesses' presence was doubted because of the dent to the ocular account when one accused was declared innocent, their failure to chase or intervene, and contradictions with the medical time of death. Their unnatural conduct showed they were not present, so their testimony was not credible and the prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: 2023 MLD 629.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance Mutation Obtained by Uncle: Declared Void
records.heading: An inheritance mutation in favour of an uncle over the legal heir daughter is void
records.text: In a daughter's suit, the inheritance mutation sanctioned in favour of her deceased father's brother was declared null and void. The revenue authorities lacked jurisdiction to decide inheritance, and the Collector had no discretion to grant proprietary rights to another person in the presence of the legal heir. The suit was concurrently decreed. Ref: 2023 CLC 673.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Does Not Run on Inheritance Mutation
records.heading: Limitation does not run on an inheritance mutation sanctioned by concealment
records.text: In the case of an inheritance mutation, limitation does not run, especially where evidence shows it was sanctioned by concealment or the other side compensated the legal heir with produce or money. Ref: 2023 CLC 673.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Arrest and Detention of Judgment Debtor in Execution
records.heading: Arrest of a judgment debtor requires show cause notice, inquiry and opportunity to lead evidence
records.text: Before ordering arrest and detention of a judgment debtor in civil prison, the court must issue a show cause notice, satisfy itself through inquiry and allow the parties an opportunity to lead evidence. Without these preconditions the order cannot be passed. Ref: 2023 CLC 796.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Audi Alteram Partem and Revision Jurisdiction
records.heading: Dismissing suits in revision without hearing the plaintiffs offends audi alteram partem
records.text: The High Court had dismissed the suits while allowing revisions against dismissal of s. 12(2) applications, without hearing the plaintiffs, offending audi alteram partem. It had no jurisdiction to dismiss the suits, so it modified its judgment, remanded the matter to the lower appellate court to decide the appeals afresh and allowed the applications. Ref: 2023 CLC 806.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 129(g) QSO: Withholding Vendors in Oral Sale
records.heading: Withholding the vendors in an oral sale raises an adverse inference under Article 129(g)
records.text: In proving an oral sale, the vendors who had transferred their shares to the plaintiffs were the best witnesses, but they were withheld. An adverse inference under Art. 129, illustration (g) of the Qanun-e-Shahadat, 1984 was drawn that their evidence would have negated the plaintiffs' stance. Ref: 2023 MLD 654.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Oral Sale: Essential Details Must Be Pleaded
records.heading: An oral sale plaint must plead time, date, venue and witnesses or it fails
records.text: In a suit for specific performance of an oral contract, the plaintiff must specifically plead the time, date, venue and names of witnesses of the transaction, to discourage frivolous litigation and surprise evidence. Their omission from the plaint was fatal, and inconsistent evidence failed to prove the oral sale. Ref: 2023 MLD 654.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay: Counsel's Unavailability
records.heading: Unavailability of counsel is not a good ground for condonation of delay
records.text: Unavailability of counsel is not a good ground for condonation of delay. A litigant must keep abreast of the case and pursue it diligently, and where counsel is unavailable the party must itself be present. A communication gap between counsel and client is no ground, and an indolent litigant is entitled to no relief. Ref: 2023 MLD 739.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appellate Findings Preferred Over Trial Court
records.heading: Where trial and appellate findings conflict, the appellate court's findings are preferred
records.text: Where the findings of the trial court and the appellate court are inconsistent, the findings of the appellate court are to be preferred unless there is a cogent reason to the contrary. Ref: 2023 SCMR 815.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Court Cannot Make a Contract for Parties
records.heading: A court cannot make a contract for the parties under section 10 of the Contract Act
records.text: Under s. 10 of the Contract Act, where the parties have not structured an effective and enforceable contract, the court cannot make one for them and decides the lis on the terms actually agreed. A decree for specific performance may be refused where the substratum of the contract suffers from legal infirmities rendering it unenforceable. Ref: 2023 SCMR 815.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: Proof and Delay
records.heading: Specific performance failed for unverified title, thirteen years of delay and defective agreements
records.text: A suit for specific performance and declaration failed where the vendee did not verify the vendor's title to an undivided jointly owned property, sued about 13 years after the agreements, gave no reason for the delay, and the agreements lacked a proper description of the property and were not signed by the other co-owner. The Appellate Court rightly held the agreements not proved. Ref: 2023 SCMR 815.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Reliable Ocular Account
records.heading: An FIR within 1 hour 25 minutes at 25 kilometres is prompt and consistent ocular accounts sustained conviction
records.text: In a s. 302(b) PPC case, an FIR lodged within 1 hour 25 minutes at a distance of 25 kilometres was prompt, excluding deliberation. Consistent ocular accounts by an injured complainant and another resident witness, daylight, known parties and corroborating medical evidence sustained the conviction. Leave to appeal was refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 831; Aqil v. The State.
records.title: Aqil v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone sustains conviction
records.text: Medical evidence and recovery are corroborative in nature and alone cannot sustain a conviction. Where ocular evidence is trustworthy and confidence inspiring, it is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices to sustain a conviction. Ref: 2023 SCMR 831; Aqil v. The State.
records.title: Aqil v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Reduced: Motive Disbelieved
records.heading: Death sentence converted to life imprisonment where the alleged motive was disbelieved
records.text: Recovery of the weapon was inconsequential as no crime empty was recovered, and the motive based on a divorce two years earlier was disbelieved. The High Court rightly took a lenient view and converted the death sentence into imprisonment for life. Leave to appeal was refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 831; Aqil v. The State.
records.title: Aqil v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Related Witness Distinguished from Interested Witness
records.heading: A related witness is not equivalent to an interested witness
records.text: The term related is not equivalent to interested. A witness is interested only if he or she derives some benefit from the accused being punished, and a natural witness who is the only possible eye-witness cannot be called interested. Ref: 2023 SCMR 831; Aqil v. The State.
records.title: Aqil v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Testimony of Injured Eye-Witness
records.heading: The testimony of an injured eye-witness carries greater evidentiary value
records.text: The testimony of an injured eye-witness carries greater evidentiary value. Ref: 2023 SCMR 831; Aqil v. The State.
records.title: Aqil v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Contradictions and Minor Discrepancies
records.heading: A contradiction may be fatal to the prosecution but a minor discrepancy is not
records.text: A contradiction in a witness's statement may be fatal to the prosecution, whereas a minor discrepancy does not make the case doubtful. Whether a discrepancy is minor depends on the circumstances, the witnesses' social status and the environment of testimony, and parrot-like statements are discredited. Ref: 2023 SCMR 831; Aqil v. The State.
records.title: Aqil v. The State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Adjournments and Costs: Court's Discretion
records.heading: Court's discretionary power to grant adjournments and impose costs, and the governing principles
records.text: Authority on the court's power to grant time and adjourn hearings, the costs of adjournment, and the principles governing exercise of that discretion. Ref: 2023 MLD 708.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 516-A CrPC: Superdari of Vehicle Used for Narcotics
records.heading: Superdari of a vehicle used for narcotics refused on self-contradictory pleas
records.text: Superdari of a vehicle from which narcotics were recovered was refused where the appellant took self-contradictory pleas about who had possession and produced no convincing evidence of lack of knowledge. Prima facie he knew the vehicle was used to carry a large quantity of narcotics. Ref: 2023 MLD 793.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell and Mere Declaration
records.heading: An agreement to sell creates no interest in property and a mere declaration suit is limited
records.text: Under s. 54 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 a contract for sale of immovable property does not of itself create any interest in or charge on the property. A suit for mere declaration is permissible only as provided by s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act 1877, and the proviso bars a declaration where the plaintiff can seek further relief and omits to do so. Ref: 2023 SCMR 815.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 113: Limitation for Specific Performance
records.heading: Limitation for specific performance under Article 113 runs from the date fixed or knowledge of refusal
records.text: Specific performance under s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act is discretionary and must be exercised on sound legal principles. Under Art. 113 of the Limitation Act 1908, limitation runs from the date fixed for performance where time is of the essence, and otherwise from knowledge of refusal by the executant. Ref: 2023 SCMR 815.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Consensus ad Idem and Oral Contracts
records.heading: Consensus ad idem is required and an oral contract needs the clearest evidence
records.text: Consensus ad idem denotes a meeting of minds on the terms of the contract. Section 10 of the Contract Act 1872 does not exclude enforcement of an oral contract, but the court requires the clearest and most satisfactory evidence of it. Ref: 2023 SCMR 815.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Definition and Essentials of a Contract
records.heading: A contract is an enforceable agreement and the court cannot make one for the parties
records.text: Relying on Black's Law Dictionary, Anson and Treitel, the Court describes a contract as an agreement creating legally enforceable obligations, with essentials including competent parties, subject matter, legal consideration and mutuality. The court cannot make a contract for the parties, and specific performance may be refused where the contract suffers from legal infirmities. Ref: 2023 SCMR 815.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Caveat Emptor in Sale of Property
records.heading: Under caveat emptor a buyer who does not examine title bears the risk
records.text: The maxim caveat emptor obliges a buyer to scrutinise the status and title of the property before purchase. A buyer who purchases without examining title does so at his own risk, and the law will not help him escape the bargain unless there was fraud or a special covenant or warranty. Ref: 2023 SCMR 815.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Time Not Essence in Contracts for Immovable Property
records.heading: Time is not of the essence in contracts for immovable property unless intended
records.text: In contracts for immovable property time is not of the essence unless the intention of the parties shows otherwise, and a fixed time limit alone does not make it so. Failure to pay the balance consideration by the fixed date is not by itself a ground to refuse specific performance, and a plaintiff need not prove willingness where the defendant is in breach. Ref: Ishtiaq Saleem v. Syed Zulfiqar Ali Shah (deceased) through L.Rs & others (Civil Revision No. 618-D of 2009/BWP, heard 11.04.2023).
records.title: Ishtiaq Saleem v. Syed Zulfiqar Ali Shah (deceased) through L.Rs & others (Civil Revision No. 618-D of 2009/BWP, heard 11.04.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Constitutional Petition Against Federation (No Holding Stated)
records.heading: Constitutional petition against the Federation: only title, number and date recorded, no holding stated
records.text: The post records only the title, number and date of a constitutional petition against the Federation through the Law and Justice Division. No holding is stated. Ref: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad and others (Const.P. 6/2023, decided 02.05.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad and others (Const.P. 6/2023, decided 02.05.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Belated Statements and Unforensic Audio
records.heading: Post-arrest bail: belated witness statement and unforensic audio recording raise further inquiry
records.text: A prosecution witness statement recorded at a belated stage loses its sanctity, and a USB audio recording not sent for forensic examination is unsafe to rely on, relying on PLD 2019 SC 675. In a circumstantial evidence case the facts must be incompatible with innocence, and benefit of doubt may be extended at the bail stage. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, calling for further inquiry. Ref: Salman Zahid v. The State through P.G. Sindh (Crl.P. 263/2023, decided 27.04.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Salman Zahid v. The State through P.G. Sindh (Crl.P. 263/2023, decided 27.04.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Types of Court Orders During Proceedings
records.heading: A court passes regulatory, adjudicatory and regulatory cum adjudicatory orders during proceedings
records.text: During a case a court ordinarily passes three types of orders. The first is regulatory, managing or controlling the proceedings. The second is adjudicatory, a formal decision on a claim or dispute. The third is regulatory cum adjudicatory, containing a decision on an issue together with a direction for further progress of the case. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 387.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) Application Treated Under S. 151 CPC
records.heading: An application under section 12(2) CPC may be treated as one under section 151
records.text: Where a suit was withdrawn on a compromise based on a cheque that was dishonoured, the trial court rightly used inherent powers under s. 151 CPC, as an application under s. 12(2) CPC may be converted into one under s. 151 to protect valuable rights. The revisional court's order was set aside and the petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 375.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Government Appointment Without Advertisement
