records.heading: Government appointment without advertisement and fair selection violates the constitutional guarantee
records.text: The liberty to work is the essence of Arts. 9, 18, 27 and 38(c) of the Constitution, and denial of a government job is a serious blow to a citizen. Appointment to a government post without advertisement and a proper selection giving all eligible candidates a fair chance violates the constitutional guarantee. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 271.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Right to Property: Art. 23 Constitution
records.heading: The right to property under Article 23 is fundamental but subject to reasonable restrictions
records.text: The right to property is a fundamental right but is neither unfettered nor unbridled. Art. 23 gives every citizen the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property anywhere in Pakistan, subject to the Constitution and reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 245.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Commission Cannot Extend 90 Day Period
records.heading: The Election Commission cannot extend elections beyond the 90 days in Article 224(2)
records.text: Neither the Constitution nor the law empowers the Election Commission to extend the date of elections beyond the 90 days provided in Art. 224(2). The Commission's order delaying elections to the Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assemblies was declared unconstitutional and void, and the Punjab election programme was restored with modifications. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 406.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 184(3) Cases: Rules Under Art. 191
records.heading: Article 184(3) cases postponed until rules are framed under Article 191
records.text: Order XXV of the Supreme Court Rules 1980 deals only with formal applications under Art. 184(3), and no procedure exists for suo motu cases or cases of immense constitutional importance. The Court postponed hearing of all Art. 184(3) cases until rules on listing, bench constitution and selection of judges are made under Art. 191. Ref: PLD 2003 SC 387.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 148 Limitation: Redemption of Mortgage
records.heading: The limitation period to redeem a mortgage under Article 148 is sixty years
records.text: Under Art. 148 of the Limitation Act 1908 the period against a mortgagee to redeem or recover possession is sixty years, running from when the right to redeem accrues. Accrual depends on the terms of the mortgage agreement. The suit was held within limitation, and the petitions were dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 359.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Without Husband's Consent: S. 10(4) Family Courts Act
records.heading: Khula under section 10(4) of the Family Courts Act without husband's consent was already decided
records.text: The question whether khula granted under s. 10(4) of the Family Courts Act 1964 without the husband's consent is repugnant to Islam had already been decided in PLD 2014 FSC 43. That decision held that courts may decree khula where the husband refuses and reconciliation fails. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 286.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula and Talaq: Effect and Halala
records.heading: Khula operates as a single irrevocable divorce and needs no halala for remarriage
records.text: According to Shariah, khula operates as a single irrevocable divorce, so the spouses may remarry by mutual consent without halala. Iddat is required if the wife wishes to marry another person. Halala is required only after a third talaq becomes final. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 286.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ouster of Civil Court Jurisdiction: Strict Construction
records.heading: A provision ousting the jurisdiction of civil courts is construed strictly
records.text: A provision ousting civil court jurisdiction is construed strictly and cannot disturb established rights, deprive anyone of property, or create injustice or hardship, though it retains legal effect. Availability of an alternative remedy for those affected is a relevant factor. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 340.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Mala Fide Against Public Functionary
records.heading: Mala fide cannot be attributed to a functionary acting under a legal mandate without cogent material
records.text: Mala fide cannot be attributed to an executive or government functionary performing functions under a legal mandate. Without cogent and convincing material supporting the plea, the action is presumed not to be tainted with mala fide. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 245.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Intra Court Appeal: Bar Under Law Reforms Ordinance
records.heading: No intra court appeal where the applicable law provided an appeal, revision or review
records.text: Under the proviso to s. 3(2) of the Law Reforms Ordinance 1972, an intra court appeal is not available where the Art. 199 petition arose from proceedings in which the applicable law provided at least one appeal, revision or review. The employee had challenged orders of the competent, appellate and revisional authorities, so the appeal was dismissed as not maintainable. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 241.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Care in Legislative Drafting
records.heading: Special care is required in legislative drafting because one word may defeat the purpose
records.text: The State cannot afford even slight errors in drafting laws, as a mistake of one word may defeat the purpose of legislation. The Federal Shariat Court directed the Secretary Law and Justice to ensure special care in legislative drafting. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 283.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Development Funds to MNAs and MPAs Through Local Government
records.heading: Development projects not approved by the local government were without lawful authority
records.text: New development projects not approved by the defunct local government, whether recommended by MNAs and MPAs or otherwise, were without lawful authority. Appointment of administrators under the Chief Minister's notification of 21.10.2022 without Cabinet approval was also without lawful authority. The Election Commission was directed to hold local government elections forthwith after delimitation. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 257; M/s. Mazhar Hussain v. Government of Punjab, etc.
records.title: M/s. Mazhar Hussain v. Government of Punjab, etc

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Right to Information: Substantially Financed by Government
records.heading: Substantial government financing under the Right to Information Act need not exceed fifty percent
records.text: Under s. 2(h)(iv) of the Punjab Transparency and Right to Information Act 2013, financing need not be measured in percentage and need not exceed fifty percent. It suffices that government assistance is material and important or has an essential role in the body's existence. The High Court declined to interfere with the Commissioner's order against the club. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 278.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Female Heirs' Declaration Suit
records.heading: Article 120 governs a female heir's declaration suit and time runs from actual denial
records.text: No specific article covers a s. 42 Specific Relief Act suit for declaration of ownership, so residuary Art. 120 of the Limitation Act 1908 applies, giving six years from when the right to sue accrues. For a female heir suing her brother, time runs from actual denial of her rights. The Court treats differently property still held by the defrauding brothers and property alienated to good faith transferees for value. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 362.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Transactions by Hard of Hearing Non-Verbal Persons
records.heading: Transactions by a hard of hearing non-verbal person need safeguards on consideration and payment
records.text: A transaction affecting the rights of a person of unsound mind or intellectually disabled must be made through a next friend or guardian under O. XXXII R. 15 CPC. For a person who is hard of hearing and non-verbal but not intellectually disabled, the Court laid down safeguards for the transaction, including checks that the consideration equals the value of the property and was actually paid. Ref: Zafar Afzal and others v. Ashiq Hussain (C.A. 415/2018, decided 12.04.2023); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Zafar Afzal and others v. Ashiq Hussain (C.A. 415/2018, decided 12.04.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ex Parte Proceedings: Court Must Not Act Mechanically
records.heading: After proceeding ex parte, the court must not act mechanically
records.text: After proceeding ex parte, the court may decide with or without evidence, but despite the defendant's absence it should not act mechanically and must consider the legal and factual aspects of the case on the material before it. A decree includes rejection of a plaint under s. 2(2) CPC. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Defence, Rawalpindi and another v. M/s Farrukh International (Pvt) Ltd through its Proprietor, Karachi (C.P. 3185/2020, decided 06.02.2023); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Defence, Rawalpindi and another v. M/s Farrukh International (Pvt) Ltd through its Proprietor, Karachi (C.P. 3185/2020, decided 06.02.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 17(2)(a) and 79 QSO: Attestation by Two Witnesses
records.heading: A financial document needs two attesting witnesses to prove its execution under Articles 17 and 79
records.text: A document relating to financial or future obligations must be attested by at least two witnesses under Art. 17(2)(a) QSO. Under Art. 79 it cannot be used as evidence unless two attesting witnesses appear to prove its execution, and here this condition precedent was not satisfied. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Defence, Rawalpindi and another v. M/s Farrukh International (Pvt) Ltd through its Proprietor, Karachi (C.P. 3185/2020, decided 06.02.2023); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Defence, Rawalpindi and another v. M/s Farrukh International (Pvt) Ltd through its Proprietor, Karachi (C.P. 3185/2020, decided 06.02.2023)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: SCBA Challenge to Pakistan Bar Council Action
records.heading: SCBA challenge to Pakistan Bar Council removal of office bearers: no holding stated
records.text: The Supreme Court Bar Association challenged in the Supreme Court the Pakistan Bar Council's removal of its Secretary and Additional Secretary and the show cause notices issued on allegations of misconduct. The post gives no holding. Ref: Supreme Court Bar Association, through its Vice-President, Islamabad and others v. Pakistan Bar Council, through its Secretary, Islamabad and another (Const.P. 13/2023, decided 05.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association, through its Vice-President, Islamabad and others v. Pakistan Bar Council, through its Secretary, Islamabad and another (Const.P. 13/2023, decided 05.05.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 176 CrPC: Disinterment Order Is Judicial, Revisable
records.heading: An order on disinterment of a corpse under section 176 CrPC is judicial and revisable
records.text: An order of the area magistrate accepting or declining disinterment of a corpse for post mortem examination under s. 176 CrPC is a judicial order amenable to revisional jurisdiction. According to the Urdu note, revision lies before the Sessions Court. Ref: 2023 LHC 2489; Mohmad v. SHO PS Arrotee etc (70407/21, decided 27.04.2023); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Mohmad v. SHO PS Arrotee etc (70407/21, decided 27.04.2023)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Quashing of FIR: Illegal Upgradations Case
records.heading: FIR quashed where violation of service terms was held not to be criminal misconduct
records.text: The High Court quashed an FIR under ss. 409/109 PPC and s. 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947 concerning illegal upgradations, holding that violation of service terms of CDA employees was not criminal misconduct, although FIA had found prima facie abuse of authority. The extract does not state the Supreme Court's final outcome. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 247; FIA through Director General, FIA and others v. Syed Hamid Ali Shah and others (C.P. 1257 of 2020, decided 06.02.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: FIA through Director General, FIA and others v. Syed Hamid Ali Shah and others (C.P. 1257 of 2020, decided 06.02.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Denied Agreement Must Be Proved
records.heading: A plaintiff must prove an agreement to sell denied by the vendor through signature comparison
records.text: Where the vendor categorically denied execution of an agreement to sell, the plaintiff had to seek comparison of signatures or thumb impressions, which was never requested. With inconsistencies in the area and unproved earnest money, execution was not established. The appeal was allowed and the suit dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 255; Muhammad Ghaffar (deceased) through LRs and others v. Arif Muhammad (C.P.L.A. 1517 of 2022, decided 22.11.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Ghaffar (deceased) through LRs and others v. Arif Muhammad (C.P.L.A. 1517 of 2022, decided 22.11.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 476 CrPC: Discretionary Power and Abuse of Process
records.heading: The power under section 476 CrPC is discretionary and must not serve private vengeance
records.text: The power under s. 476 CrPC to take cognizance of offences committed in relation to proceedings is discretionary and must not be abused by a litigant pursuing private vengeance or a grudge. The petition was held frivolous and vexatious, and the Court also discussed the objectives of imposing costs. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 265; Qazi Naveed-ul-Islam v. District Judge, Gujrat, etc. (C.P. 3127 of 2020, decided 12.01.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Qazi Naveed-ul-Islam v. District Judge, Gujrat, etc. (C.P. 3127 of 2020, decided 12.01.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashment of FIR: Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust needs entrustment and misappropriation, and a disputed civil liability does not bar prosecution
records.text: Criminal breach of trust requires entrustment and misappropriation. In using inherent powers the High Court must decide whether continuing proceedings would be a gross abuse of process, and it is wrong to presume that prosecution is unsustainable merely because a civil liability is disputed. Petition allowed, the High Court judgment set aside and the challan directed to be submitted to the trial court. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 286; Muhammad Ali v. Samina Qasim Tarar and others (C.P. 3130 of 2020, decided 29.09.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Ali v. Samina Qasim Tarar and others (C.P. 3130 of 2020, decided 29.09.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 169: Restoration of Civil Revision
records.heading: An application to restore a civil revision has three years under Article 169
records.text: Under Art. 169 of the Limitation Act 1908, an application with no period prescribed elsewhere has three years from when the right to apply accrues. A petitioner therefore has three years to apply for restoration of a civil revision dismissed for non-prosecution. The impugned order was set aside and the petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 291; Mst. Jameela Bibi (decd) through LRs v. Mst. Fatima Bibi (decd) through LRs (C.P. 3125 of 2020, decided 19.01.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Jameela Bibi (decd) through LRs v. Mst. Fatima Bibi (decd) through LRs (C.P. 3125 of 2020, decided 19.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Plaint rejected where an earlier suit on the same relief had failed and no new cause arose
records.text: Respondents had earlier sued for specific performance on the same subject matter and relief, and that suit and appeal were dismissed. Proprietary rights were never granted and the land remained with the Province, so no new cause of action arose. The civil revision was allowed and the plaint rejected under O. VII R. 11 read with R. 13 CPC. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 391; Hadayat Ullah deceased through Legal Heirs etc. v. Province of the Punjab etc. (C.R. 3587 of 2011, heard 30.03.2022); Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Hadayat Ullah deceased through Legal Heirs etc. v. Province of the Punjab etc. (C.R. 3587 of 2011, heard 30.03.2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Failure to Decide Additional Issues: Remand
records.heading: Failure to decide additional issues framed by the trial court requires remand
records.text: Where the trial court framed additional issues but ignored them when writing the judgment, the fate of the case could not be finally decided without deciding them. The appeal was accepted, the judgments set aside and the matter remanded for fresh decision. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 436; Mubashar Ahmad Ayaz v. Late (Moulana) Manzoor Ahmad Chinioti through L.Rs. etc. (R.S.A. 46 of 2009, heard 24.01.2023); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Mubashar Ahmad Ayaz v. Late (Moulana) Manzoor Ahmad Chinioti through L.Rs. etc. (R.S.A. 46 of 2009, heard 24.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 152 CPC: Correction of Decree Omitting Reliefs
records.heading: A decree omitting pleaded and proved basic reliefs may be corrected under section 152 CPC
records.text: Law favours adjudication on merits, and technicalities should not defeat justice. Reliefs of specific performance and perpetual injunction, pleaded and supported by evidence, were basic reliefs omitted from the ex parte decree. The application for correction was allowed and the trial court directed to incorporate them. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 439; Shabbir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Multan, etc. (W.P. 3227 of 2022, heard 19.01.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Shabbir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Multan, etc. (W.P. 3227 of 2022, heard 19.01.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: S. 9-C CNSA: No Connection of Appellant With Consignment
records.heading: Appellant released where prosecution witnesses found no connection with the narcotics consignment
records.text: The appellant, CEO of a logistics company, was charged over heroin recovered from a cloth consignment. Prosecution witnesses stated that investigation found no connection of the appellant with it or his knowledge of any narcotics, and they were not declared hostile. The appeal was accepted and release ordered. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 438; Shuja-ul-Haq Malik v. State etc. (Crl. A. 51188 of 2022, heard 09.01.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Shuja-ul-Haq Malik v. State etc. (Crl. A. 51188 of 2022, heard 09.01.2023)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Liability of Company and Signatory
records.heading: A company and its cheque signatory in charge of operations may be prosecuted under section 489-F
records.text: Corporations cannot claim immunity from prosecution because they lack mens rea, and the word whoever in s. 489-F PPC includes juristic persons, so a company can be prosecuted. A director or CEO cannot rely on separate legal identity, and the cheque signatory is liable if shown in charge of operations. The offence is not one of strict liability, as dishonesty must be proved. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 446; Kabeer Akbar v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 52233-B of 2022, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Kabeer Akbar v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 52233-B of 2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Comparison of Signatures: S. 94 CrPC and Art. 161 QSO
records.heading: Signature comparison should be allowed under section 94 CrPC and Article 161 QSO
records.text: Where the dispute turns on alleged forgery of a deceased father's signatures on cheques, any evidence essential to a just decision must be brought on record, and ss. 94 CrPC and Art. 161 QSO are relevant. The complainant's application for comparison of signatures was wrongly dismissed, and the revision was accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 461; Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court, etc. (Crl. Rev. 23556 of 2022, heard 31.01.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court, etc. (Crl. Rev. 23556 of 2022, heard 31.01.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 249-A CrPC: Acquittal Application Dismissed
records.heading: An acquittal application under section 249-A fails where the presumption of consideration for the cheque stands
records.text: Section 249-A CrPC is an exception to the normal rule that acquittal follows a full trial. The Investigating Officer's sole opinion cannot negate the presumption that every cheque was made for consideration, and the petitioner did not deny his signature. The inherent jurisdiction was not exercised and the petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 469; Ahmad Faran Sabir v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8564-M of 2022, heard 26.05.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Ahmad Faran Sabir v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8564-M of 2022, heard 26.05.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Falsus in Uno, Falsus in Omnibus
records.heading: Witnesses disbelieved against one set of accused cannot be accepted against the others
records.text: On the principle of falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus, if witnesses are disbelieved against one set of accused their testimony cannot be accepted against the others, though under abundant caution an accused may be singled out. The appeals and revision were dismissed, the murder reference answered in the negative and the death sentence not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 481; Ghulam Yasin etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. 199788, 211790 & Crl. Rev. 211791 of 2018, heard 16.06.2022); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ghulam Yasin etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. 199788, 211790 & Crl. Rev. 211791 of 2018, heard 16.06.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Melee: Distance and Blackening Around Wounds
records.heading: In a melee, witnesses cannot recall exact distance and blackening around wounds is not abnormal
records.text: In a melee witnesses cannot be expected to recall the exact distance between accused and victim, and the parties would not remain stagnant. Even at six feet, a shot fired with a stretched arm would reduce the range so that blackening around the wounds is not abnormal medical evidence. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 481; Ghulam Yasin etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. 199788, 211790 & Crl. Rev. 211791 of 2018, heard 16.06.2022); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ghulam Yasin etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. 199788, 211790 & Crl. Rev. 211791 of 2018, heard 16.06.2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 403 PPC: Misappropriation and Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: Section 403 PPC lacks the words fraudulently and entrustment, which convert misappropriation into breach of trust
records.text: The judgment compares a misappropriation provision of another enactment with s. 403 PPC, noting that the words fraudulently and entrustment are missing in s. 403 and that s. 403 is confined to moveable property. Entrustment converts dishonest misappropriation into criminal breach of trust. The appeal was allowed and the appellant acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 491; Amir Hayat v. State (Crl. A. 51224 of 2017, decided 06.06.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Amir Hayat v. State (Crl. A. 51224 of 2017, decided 06.06.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular and Medical Contradiction: Chance Witness
records.heading: Conviction fails where ocular and medical evidence conflict and the chance witness is unproved
records.text: Conviction under ss. 302/34 PPC failed where the ocular account conflicted with the medical evidence, the postmortem showed two entry wounds attributed to no accused, and PW-2, a chance witness, failed to prove his presence. The murder reference was answered in the negative, the death sentences were not confirmed, and the complainant's appeal against acquittal of respondents was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 507; Sajid Hussain v. State etc. (Crl. A. 717, 771 & M.R. 95 of 2018, heard 31.10.2022); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch..
records.title: Sajid Hussain v. State etc. (Crl. A. 717, 771 & M.R. 95 of 2018, heard 31.10.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula by Courts: S. 10(4) Family Courts Act
records.heading: Khula by ordinary courts under section 10(4) was already decided and needs no halala
records.text: The grant of khula by ordinary courts under s. 10(4) of the Family Courts Act 1964 had already been decided by the Full Bench in Saleem Ahmad. Khula is a unique right of women and operates as a single irrevocable divorce, so remarriage needs no halala. The Shariat petition was dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 513; Khurram Shehzad v. Federation of Pakistan through Ministry of Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Shariat Petition 11-I of 2022, decided 07.02.2023); Justice Syed Muhammad Anwer; Justice Khadim Hussain M. Shaikh.
records.title: Khurram Shehzad v. Federation of Pakistan through Ministry of Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Shariat Petition 11-I of 2022, decided 07.02.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Recovery of Dead Body Not Exclusive Knowledge
records.heading: Recovery of a dead body already known to others is not a discovery under Article 40
records.text: Recovery of the dead body at the accused's pointing out was inadmissible under Art. 40 QSO as a discovery, because an application for disinterment had already been moved and the police, doctor and complainant knew of it. Exclusive knowledge did not arise. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and the appeal was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 518, 2023 YLR 2207; Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay Ground Lost After Withdrawal of Bail Application
records.heading: Statutory delay ground cannot be raised again after withdrawing a bail application while it subsisted
records.text: Under the third proviso, cl. (b), to s. 497 CrPC, a bail application withdrawn while the ground of statutory delay subsisted cannot be taken again on that ground, as endorsed by a five-member bench in Muhammad Aslam. The petition was not maintainable and was dismissed, with the trial court directed to conclude the trial within two months. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 117; Shahbaz Akmal v. State through Prosecutor General Punjab, Lahore and another (Crl. P. 1496 of 2022, decided 09.01.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Shahbaz Akmal v. State through Prosecutor General Punjab, Lahore and another (Crl. P. 1496 of 2022, decided 09.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Corroborated by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Medical evidence corroborating the ocular account defeats minor discrepancies on distances and locations
records.text: In a s. 302(b) PPC case, the medical evidence corroborated the ocular account on nature, time, locale and impact of injuries. Witnesses firing live shots can only make a tentative assessment of distances and locations, and minor discrepancies in medical evidence do not undermine the ocular account. The petition was dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 123; Nasir Ahmed v. State (J.P. 865 of 2017, decided 12.12.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Nasir Ahmed v. State (J.P. 865 of 2017, decided 12.12.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appreciation of Ocular Account and Discrepancies
records.heading: A reliable ocular account corroborated by medical evidence sustains conviction despite trivial discrepancies
records.text: A reliable and confidence inspiring ocular account corroborated by medical evidence sustained the conviction under s. 302(b) PPC. The test is whether the evidence read as a whole has a ring of truth, and minor discrepancies on trivial matters should not lead to rejection of the evidence. The appeal was partly allowed and the judgment modified. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 130; Ali Asghar @ Aksar v. State (Crl. A. 190 of 2020, decided 07.12.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Ali Asghar @ Aksar v. State (Crl. A. 190 of 2020, decided 07.12.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Common Object Ignored: Conviction on Individual Role
records.heading: Convicting on individual roles while ignoring common object in a section 149 charge is illegal
records.text: Where all accused were charged under ss. 148/149 PPC, the courts below ignored common object and convicted on individual roles, which was held illegal. The appeals were allowed and the trial court was directed to rewrite the judgment on the available evidence within one month after hearing both parties. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 136; Muhammad Iqbal and others v. State and another (Crl. P. 614 & 618 of 2017, decided 30.11.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal and others v. State and another (Crl. P. 614 & 618 of 2017, decided 30.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Post-Arrest Bail: Perverse Order
records.heading: Bail granted on the police ipse dixit after charge was perverse and was cancelled
records.text: Under s. 497 CrPC, bail may be cancelled where the bail granting order is erroneous and causes a miscarriage of justice. Bail granted after charge was framed on the ipse dixit of the police, which would discredit the eye-witnesses at the initial stage, was perverse. The petition was converted into an appeal and allowed, and bail was recalled. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 141; Amir Faraz v. State (Crl. P. 475 of 2022, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Amir Faraz v. State (Crl. P. 475 of 2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 14 Limitation Act: Due Diligence and Good Faith
records.heading: Exclusion of time under section 14 requires due diligence and good faith in the wrong forum
records.text: To obtain exclusion of time under s. 14 of the Limitation Act 1908, a litigant must show that he prosecuted his remedy with due diligence and in good faith in a court unable to entertain it for defect of jurisdiction. Due diligence means the care a reasonable person would take in choosing the forum. Ref: 2023 SCMR 866.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Runs Even Against a Void Order
records.heading: Limitation runs even against a void order
records.text: Limitation runs even against a void order, and an aggrieved party must approach the competent forum within the period of limitation provided by law. Ref: 2023 SCMR 866.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conspiracy: Absence of Date, Time and Place
records.heading: Alleged conspiracy fails where no date, time or place was disclosed in the crime report
records.text: The crime report gave no specific date, time or place of the alleged conspiracy, and the later prosecution witnesses also failed to reveal them. The transcript of WhatsApp voice messages produced by the prosecution did not constitute any offence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 870.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Abetment: Substantial Assistance Required
records.heading: Abetment requires substantial assistance to the principal offender, and mere concurrence or negligence is insufficient
records.text: The essence of abetment is that the abettor substantially assists the principal culprit in committing the offence. Mere concurrence in another's criminal act without participation is not culpable, and mere negligence does not amount to abetment. Ref: 2023 SCMR 870.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: A Single Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single doubt in the prosecution case entitles the accused to its benefit
records.text: Any doubt in the prosecution case is to be resolved in favour of the accused. It is not necessary that many circumstances create uncertainty, and a single doubt entitles the accused to its benefit. Ref: 2023 SCMR 870.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Delayed FIR and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where the unexplained FIR delay made the case one of further inquiry
records.text: An FIR lodged after five days without explanation showed deliberation and consultation. Co-accused named in the FIR had already received pre-arrest bail, and the accused was a young man with no criminal history. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC as one of further inquiry, and ad-interim bail was confirmed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 884.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Court May Touch Merits
records.heading: A court granting pre-arrest bail may touch upon the merits of the case
records.text: While granting pre-arrest bail the court may touch upon the merits of the case. Ref: 2023 SCMR 884.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail to Women Accused: First Proviso to S. 497(1) CrPC
records.heading: Bail is the rule for a woman, a minor under sixteen or a sick accused
records.text: The first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC places the court's power to grant bail to a woman, a person under sixteen or a sick or infirm accused on the same footing as in non-prohibitory offences. Bail is the rule and refusal the exception, justified only by likelihood of absconding, tampering with evidence or witnesses, or repeating the offence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 887.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Under S. 497(1) and S. 497(2) CrPC Distinguished
records.heading: Bail under section 497(2) is a right while section 497(1) is discretionary
records.text: Bail under s. 497(2) CrPC is granted as of right where there are no reasonable grounds for believing the accused committed the offence and there are sufficient grounds for further inquiry. In exercising discretion under s. 497(1), the availability of sufficient incriminating material connecting the accused is not a relevant consideration. Ref: 2023 SCMR 887.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Injured Witnesses
records.heading: An FIR two hours after the occurrence is prompt and injured witnesses support conviction
records.text: An FIR lodged two hours after the occurrence at five kilometres from the police station was prompt. Two injured eye-witnesses with no relationship or animosity gave full details supported by medical evidence, and the motive was not seriously disputed. The jail petitions were dismissed, leave refused and the death sentences maintained. Ref: 2023 SCMR 900.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Testimony of Police Witnesses
records.heading: Police witnesses are as reliable as private witnesses unless animus is proved
records.text: The testimony of police officials is as good as that of any private witness unless animus against the accused is proved. Police witnesses can be relied upon if their testimony remains unshattered in cross-examination. Ref: 2023 SCMR 900.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Confidence inspiring ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone sustains conviction
records.text: Trustworthy and confidence inspiring ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices to sustain a conviction. Discrepancies in medical evidence on the nature of injuries do not negate direct evidence, as witnesses are not expected to give a photographic account. Ref: 2023 SCMR 900.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Evidence
records.heading: Minor discrepancies on trivial matters should be ignored unless they go to the root
records.text: Where the material aspects of the evidence have a ring of truth, minor discrepancies on trivial matters not affecting the salient features of the prosecution case should be ignored. The defence can take advantage of an omission or discrepancy only if it goes to the root of the matter. Ref: 2023 SCMR 900.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification of Unknown Accused Through Parade
records.heading: Identification of unknown accused upheld where parade formalities were observed and the injured witness was consistent
records.text: The accused were unknown but their features were given in the crime report. The injured witness's presence was proved by his injuries, his account was consistent, the identification parade formalities were observed and the accused had remained a considerable time in the complainant's house. The medical evidence corroborated the ocular account. Ref: 2023 SCMR 929.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Discrepancies Distinguished from Contradictions
records.heading: Discrepancies must be distinguished from contradictions, which alone may be fatal
records.text: Discrepancies must be distinguished from contradictions. A contradiction may be fatal to the prosecution, but minor discrepancies that do not go to the root of the story or shake its salient features need not be given much importance. Ref: 2023 SCMR 929.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Test Identification Parade Is Corroborative Only
records.heading: An identification parade is only corroborative and its omission is not fatal
records.text: An identification parade must be conducted fairly according to the exigencies of the case and is not an unchangeable ritual. It is merely corroborative, and if a witness identifies the accused in court with confidence-inspiring and consistent testimony, non-holding of a parade is not fatal. Ref: 2023 SCMR 929.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Dacoity With Murder: Meaning of Conjointly
records.heading: Conjointly in dacoity means joint action and all members are guilty if one commits murder
records.text: The word conjointly in ss. 391 and 396 PPC means that five or more dacoits act with knowledge and consent, in aid of one another or under an agreement. If any one of them commits murder during the dacoity, all members are guilty of dacoity with murder under s. 396 PPC. Ref: 2023 SCMR 929.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed: Mala Fide of Complainant
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where the complainant suppressed facts, indicating mala fide
records.text: The complainant suppressed his relationship with the accused, an ex parte dowry decree and the bailiff's visit when lodging the FIR, indicating mala fide and ulterior motive. The accused was at par with a co-accused whose bail was confirmed and had joined the investigation. The petition was converted into an appeal and allowed, and pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 967.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Refused: No Mala Fide Shown
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail refused in a non-bailable case where no specific mala fide was alleged
records.text: An FIR by a father against his son alleging attempted qatl-i-amd and theft was supported by eye-witnesses and medical evidence, and the offences under ss. 324 and 380 PPC were non-bailable. The accused alleged no specific mala fide or ulterior motive. The petition was dismissed, leave declined and pre-arrest bail refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 975.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 34 PPC: Common Intention
records.heading: Section 34 PPC does not require an act by one's own hand, only prior concert
records.text: An offence under s. 34 PPC does not require that a person perform an act with his own hand, as common intention presupposes prior concert and a pre-arranged plan. One who aids by presence or other act in furtherance of the common intention is held to have done the act himself. Ref: 2023 SCMR 975.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Extraordinary Relief
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is extraordinary relief to protect the innocent from mala fide cases
records.text: Pre-arrest bail is an extraordinary relief granted in extraordinary situations to protect innocent persons from cases lodged with mala fide intention. The petitioner must satisfy the court of the basic conditions under s. 497 CrPC, namely reasonable grounds to believe he is not guilty and that the case is one of further inquiry. Ref: 2023 SCMR 975.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotics Samples
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody and transmission of narcotics samples defeats the prosecution case
records.text: Neither safe custody nor safe transmission of the sealed samples to the Forensic Science Laboratory was established, as the Moharrar and the depositing Constable were not produced and the samples were received three days after recovery with no account of where they remained. Tampering was apparent, so the prosecution case was not proved beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2023 SCMR 986.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift: Burden of Proof on Donee
records.heading: A donee relying on a gift against female heirs must prove it
records.text: The donee who relies on a gift to defeat female heirs must prove it. A photocopy of the sub-registrar's register, with no certified copy and no sub-registrar or official examined, is no evidence, and mutation made on such a basis is unlawful. Depriving female heirs of inheritance constitutes fraud. Costs of Rs.500,000 imposed on the appellant. Ref: 2023 SCMR 988; Muhammad Rafiq v. Mst. Ghulam Zoharan Mai & another (Civil Appeal No. 2613 of 2016).
records.title: Muhammad Rafiq v. Mst. Ghulam Zoharan Mai & another (Civil Appeal No. 2613 of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata: Scope and Rationale
records.heading: Res judicata gives finality to judgments and prevents multiplicity of proceedings
records.text: The doctrine of res judicata gives finality to judgments between the parties and prevents multiplicity of proceedings on the same cause of action. A final judgment cannot be reopened unless fraud, mistake or lack of jurisdiction is pleaded and established. Ref: 2023 SCMR 992.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Cross-Version FIRs, Delay in Trial
records.heading: Post-arrest bail: counter FIR, general role and delay in trial call for further inquiry
records.text: Only a general role was ascribed to the accused in an offence under ss. 324 and 34 PPC, there was a counter FIR, no repeat fire, and the trial had not concluded after more than 22 months. A co-accused with a similar role had been granted bail by the Supreme Court. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, calling for further inquiry. Ref: 2023 SCMR 999.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: SCBA v. PBC: De-Seating and Show Cause Notices
records.heading: Show cause notices and de-seating orders challenged for want of due process; settlement recorded
records.text: Petitioners alleged that show cause notices and de-seating orders were issued without due process and in violation of Rules 118 and 125 of the Pakistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Council Rules, 1976. The post also records that the terms of settlement of all disputes were agreed in Court by representatives of the PBC and the SCBA. Ref: Supreme Court Bar Association, through its Vice-President, Islamabad and others v. Pakistan Bar Council, through its Secretary, Islamabad and another (Const.P. 13/2023, decided 09.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association, through its Vice-President, Islamabad and others v. Pakistan Bar Council, through its Secretary, Islamabad and another (Const.P. 13/2023, decided 09.05.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Right of Access to Justice; Sanctity of Court
records.heading: Order on the right of access to justice and the sanctity of the Court, no holding stated
records.text: The order deals with the right of access to justice and the sanctity and safety of the Court. The post gives no further holding. Ref: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. The State and others (Crl.P. 519/2023, decided 11.05.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. The State and others (Crl.P. 519/2023, decided 11.05.2023)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Essential Elements and S. 118 NIA Presumption
records.heading: Section 489-F is not attracted to every dishonoured cheque and section 118 raises a presumption
records.text: Section 489-F PPC is not attracted to every dishonour. Its elements are a duly issued cheque, dishonest intent, issue towards repayment of a loan or fulfilment of an obligation, and dishonour on presentation. Section 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 raises a presumption of consideration and holder in due course. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 469; Ahmad Faran Sabir v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8564-M of 2022, heard 26.05.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Ahmad Faran Sabir v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8564-M of 2022, heard 26.05.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance of Survival and Hospital Death Not Mitigating
records.heading: Chances of survival and death in hospital are not mitigating circumstances
records.text: Mere chances of survival do not reduce the liability of the accused, and death in hospital after some time cannot be treated as a mitigating circumstance. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 481; Ghulam Yasin etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. 199788, 211790 & Crl. Rev. 211791 of 2018, heard 16.06.2022); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ghulam Yasin etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. 199788, 211790 & Crl. Rev. 211791 of 2018, heard 16.06.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Principles and Leading Rules
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form a chain incompatible with innocence and any reasonable doubt favours the accused
records.text: Reliability depends on the capacity of the witness and legality of the process, whereas credibility touches the witness's character. Circumstantial evidence works cumulatively, and the inculpatory facts must be clearly proved, incompatible with innocence and incapable of explanation on any other reasonable hypothesis than guilt. Any reasonable doubt entitles the accused to acquittal. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 518, 2023 YLR 2207; Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Counter FIR and Delayed Registration
records.heading: Post-arrest bail: counter FIR and unexplained delay of two days call for further inquiry
records.text: Medical evidence prima facie supported the accused's version, a counter FIR existed and the FIR was lodged after unexplained delay of two days, indicating deliberation. Whether s. 324 PPC applied was for the trial court. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, calling for further inquiry. Ref: 2023 SCMR 857.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Power of Attorney: Strict Construction and Ratification
records.heading: A power of attorney is strictly construed but the principal may ratify unauthorised acts
records.text: A power of attorney is construed strictly and operates prospectively, but ss. 196, 197 and 199 of the Contract Act allow the principal to ratify an act not expressly authorised, expressly or by implication. Once ratified, the agent's act binds the principal as if done by the principal. Ref: 2023 CLC 854.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII R. 3 CPC: Leave to Defend
records.heading: Leave to defend under Order XXXVII is not warranted for bald and vague allegations
records.text: Under O. XXXVII R. 3(2) CPC the trial court has discretion to grant leave unconditionally or on terms of payment or security, guided by the quality and plausibility of the defence. Leave application based on bald and vague allegations or a baseless defence does not warrant even conditional leave. Ref: 2023 CLC 880.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Promissory Note: Attestation and Art. 79 QSO
records.heading: A promissory note needs no attesting witnesses because the Negotiable Instruments Act requires only the maker's signature
records.text: Art. 79 QSO requires two witnesses only for documents required by law to be attested, and Art. 17(2) excludes this where a special law provides otherwise. The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (s. 4) requires only the maker's signature, so no attesting witnesses are needed to prove a promissory note. Ref: 2023 CLC 905.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Negotiable Instruments: Presumption of Consideration s. 118
records.heading: Section 118 raises a presumption of consideration once execution of a negotiable instrument is proved
records.text: Section 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 raises a presumption of consideration once execution is proved, until the contrary is proved by the party disputing it. Absent rebuttal, no independent document or separate receipt is needed to establish consideration. Ref: 2023 CLC 905.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Headman Appointment: Marks under Rule 17
records.heading: No vested right to headman appointment arises and the appointment is administrative
records.text: The court considered whether maximum marks for hereditary claims under r. 17(1)(a) of the Rules are mandatory. It observed that no vested right to appointment as headman arises for villagers, and that such appointment is an administrative function lying with the revenue authorities. Ref: 2023 CLC 825.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Arrest of Accused from Court Premises
records.heading: Police may not arrest an accused from the verandah of a court room
records.text: Police, though bound to apprehend culprits, may not lower the dignity of the Court by arresting an accused from the verandah of the court room. The Additional Sessions Judge's order releasing the accused and directing that no arrest be made in court premises disclosed no illegality; revision disposed of accordingly. Ref: 1997 PCrLJ 309; Muhammad Nawaz v. Kazim Ali Malik, Additional Sessions Judge.
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. Kazim Ali Malik, Additional Sessions Judge

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Inquiry: Denial of Cross-Examination
records.heading: Compulsory retirement after an inquiry denying cross-examination is contrary to natural justice and Article 10-A
records.text: Compulsory retirement imposed after an inquiry in which the petitioner was not allowed to cross-examine witnesses was defective, contrary to natural justice and Art. 10-A of the Constitution, relying on 2022 SCMR 745 and 2023 SCMR 603. Acceptance of gratuity and pension does not bar the challenge. Petition converted into appeal and allowed; de novo inquiry directed within two months and reinstatement subject to refund of dues. Ref: Raja Muhammad Shahid v. The Inspector General of Police & others (C.P. 545-K of 2021, decided 20.04.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Raja Muhammad Shahid v. The Inspector General of Police & others (C.P. 545-K of 2021, decided 20.04.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Detention under MPO without Criminal Cases
records.heading: Detention under the MPO without registering criminal cases was criticised
records.text: Riots are to be suppressed under ss. 127 to 132 CrPC. Detaining citizens under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 without registering criminal cases after the events of 9 May 2023 was criticised, and persons considered miscreants should be proceeded against by registration of criminal cases. Right to dignity is subject to no qualification. Ref: 2023 LHC 2661; Abu Bakar Siddiq Bhutta v. Government of Punjab etc. (32441/23, decided 18.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Abu Bakar Siddiq Bhutta v. Government of Punjab etc. (32441/23, decided 18.05.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Withdrawal of Suit with Permission to Refile
records.heading: Permission to file a fresh suit is presumed where the withdrawal request was not declined
records.text: Where a suit was allowed to be withdrawn on the plaintiff's counsel's statement seeking permission to file a fresh suit, and that request was not declined, permission to file a fresh suit is presumed to have been granted even though the order does not say so expressly. Ref: 2018 CLC Note 106.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Stay of Criminal Proceedings Pending Civil Suit
records.heading: Civil and criminal proceedings are independent and stay of the criminal case is discretionary
records.text: Civil and criminal proceedings are independent. The High Court may stay criminal proceedings under Art. 199 or s. 561-A CrPC where civil litigation is pending, but there is no universal rule of automatic stay and the decision rests in the court's discretion, guided by whether the accused would be prejudiced. Ref: Mian Tariq Aziz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60825/M/2021).
records.title: Mian Tariq Aziz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60825/M/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 510 CrPC: Expert Report Not Conclusive
records.heading: An expert report under section 510 CrPC is admissible but not conclusive
records.text: A report mentioned in s. 510 CrPC is admissible without examining the expert, but it is not conclusive evidence. Its probative value depends on the circumstances and must be evaluated by the court. Ref: Mian Tariq Aziz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60825/M/2021).
records.title: Mian Tariq Aziz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60825/M/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Court-Fee: Appeal Decided Before Payment
records.heading: An appellate court should not decide an appeal before court-fee is paid
records.text: Non-payment or belated payment of court-fee does not adversely affect the opposite party, unlike sale consideration in specific performance or the deposit in pre-emption. The appellate court should not have decided the appeal before court-fee was paid. Ref: Syed Zahid Hussain Shah v. Mumtaz Ali and others (Civil Appeal No. 2015 of 2022, decided 09.05.2023).
records.title: Syed Zahid Hussain Shah v. Mumtaz Ali and others (Civil Appeal No. 2015 of 2022, decided 09.05.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Transgender Persons Act 2018: Shariat Petition Judgment
records.heading: Judgment on the Shariat petition challenging the Transgender Persons Act 2018, no summary given
records.text: Authority on the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2018, being the judgment on the Shariat petition challenging it. The post shares the judgment file without a summary. Ref: Hammad Hussain v. FOP (Shariat Petition 05-I of 2020).
records.title: Hammad Hussain v. FOP (Shariat Petition 05-I of 2020)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Transgender Act: Provisions Declared Against Islam
records.heading: Provisions of the Transgender Persons Act 2018 declared against the injunctions of Islam
records.text: The Federal Shariat Court declared s. 2(f) (definition of gender identity), s. 2(n)(iii), s. 3 and s. 7 of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2018 against the injunctions of Islam, to cease to have legal effect immediately. The related provisions of the 2020 Rules also cease to have effect. The Shariat petitions were accepted.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Transgender Act: Gender Identity and Biological Sex
records.heading: Gender follows biological sex, while transgender persons keep all constitutional rights
records.text: The Federal Shariat Court held that gender follows biological sex, that a person cannot self-identify as male or female contrary to it, and that inheritance shares follow sex. It held that transgender persons are entitled to all constitutional rights and that the whole of s. 2 is not against Shariah, while ss. 2(f) and 3 and related Rules were declared void. Ref: Justice Syed Muhammad Anwar; Justice Khadim Hussain.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Actual Denial of Co-Sharer's Rights
records.heading: Actual denial of a co-sharer's rights is not readily inferred from possession by another
records.text: Because co-sharers stand in a relationship of trust, possession by one is regarded as on behalf of all, and actual denial of a co-sharer's rights is not readily inferred. Mere disputes over use and sharing of profits, without an overt act ousting a co-sharer from ownership, are not actual denial and do not require a declaratory suit. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 362.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI R. 1(2) CPC: List of Witnesses
records.heading: Only witnesses listed within seven days of settlement of issues may be called
records.text: The word call in O. XVI R. 1(2) CPC means calling a witness under the authority of the Court. A list of witnesses must be presented within seven days of settlement of issues, and only witnesses so listed may be called or produced in evidence. Ref: 1999 SCMR 799.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Despite Unproved Motive
records.heading: Unproved motive may justify life imprisonment, but a brutal murder warrants death
records.text: Weakness or failure to prove motive may justify the alternate sentence of life imprisonment under s. 302(b) PPC, but the rule is flexible and loses significance where the murder is brutal. In a proved brutal murder the Courts should not hesitate to award death. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 174, 2023 MLD 1298; Muhammad Faisal v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 76 of 2020 & M.R. No. 14 of 2020); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz; Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Faisal v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 76 of 2020 & M.R. No. 14 of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Proof of Payment Despite Nikahnama Entry
records.heading: The husband must prove payment of dower despite a Nikahnama entry that it was paid
records.text: Despite a Nikahnama entry that dower was paid, the husband had to prove by evidence how the land stated as dower was transferred to the wife. Entries in columns 13 and 14 showing a small cash sum and gold ornaments could not be stretched to mean the entire dower was paid. Ref: 2018 CLC Note 108.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Transfer Before Two-Year Tenure: Local Government
records.heading: Mass transfers before the two-year tenure without written reasons are unsustainable
records.text: Transfers and postings must be exercised judiciously, and a tenure fixed by law cannot be varied except for compelling reasons recorded in writing. The two-year tenure for local government employees accords with Art. 140A. Transfer of 193 employees together, without regard to s. 186 of Act XXXIII of 2022 or reasons in writing, was found wanting. Ref: 2023 LHC 2668; Ashfaq Ahmad v. Government of Punjab etc. (Service 27705/23, decided 17.05.2023); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad v. Government of Punjab etc. (Service 27705/23, decided 17.05.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Decreed Against Grandfather as Father
records.heading: A maintenance decree treating the grandfather as father is unsustainable and was remanded
records.text: A Family Court decree for maintenance that treated the minor's grandfather as the father proceeded on a wrong premise and offended the principle of fair trial, so it was not sustainable. The case was remanded for fresh decision. Ref: 2023 YLR 1106.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Alienation of Minor's Property by De Facto Guardian
records.heading: Alienation of a minor's immovable property by a de facto guardian, no holding stated
records.text: Authority on alienation of a minor's immovable property by a de facto guardian, arising in a suit for specific performance. The post gives no holding. Ref: Muhammad Aqil v. Muhammad Amir and others (C.A. 32-K/2018); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan.
records.title: Muhammad Aqil v. Muhammad Amir and others (C.A. 32-K/2018)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Disciplinary Proceedings: Limits on Authorised Officer
records.heading: An authorised officer cannot direct the competent authority how to decide disciplinary proceedings
records.text: The authorised officer cannot direct the competent authority to decide disciplinary proceedings in a particular manner, nor direct a de novo inquiry where the proceedings were dropped or filed after due consideration. Ref: Fida Hussain v. Chief Secretary, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar and others (C.P. 1777/2020, decided 07.04.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Fida Hussain v. Chief Secretary, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar and others (C.P. 1777/2020, decided 07.04.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appreciation of Evidence and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: The prosecution must prove guilt on its own strength and reasonable doubt favours the accused
records.text: In a criminal case the burden of proving guilt lies on the prosecution, which must stand on its own strength. The standard of proof differs from civil cases, and if there is real and reasonable doubt the accused is entitled to its benefit. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 126, PLJ 2022 CrC 186.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 367 CrPC: Contents of Judgment
records.heading: A judgment under section 367 CrPC must state the points, the decision and reasons
records.text: Under s. 367 CrPC a judgment must contain the points for determination, the decision and the reasons. The trial judge deviated entirely from this requirement. A judgment must rest on critical analysis of the relevant facts, and be transparent, unambiguous and intelligible. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 126, PLJ 2022 CrC 186.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Admissibility and Reliability
records.heading: A dying declaration is admissible and reliable if the maker could identify assailants without prompting
records.text: A dying declaration is admitted despite the hearsay rule because a dying person has little incentive to fabricate. Its reliability is tested by whether the maker could identify the assailants, whether misidentification was possible, and whether it was free from outside prompting. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 126, PLJ 2022 CrC 186.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Discovery of Known Place of Occurrence
records.heading: Disclosure of an already known place of occurrence is not a discovery under Article 40
records.text: Under Art. 40 QSO the word distinctly means a fact not known to anyone before the accused disclosed it. The place of occurrence pointed out by the appellants was not secret, so the disclosure had no legal value and could not be used as incriminating evidence. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 724.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade: Value and Requirements
records.heading: An identification parade is corroborative, a rule of prudence, and cannot alone sustain conviction
records.text: An identification parade is relevant under Art. 22 QSO but is only a method of testing an eye-witness and is corroborative, not substantive, evidence. It is a rule of prudence, cannot as a rule alone sustain a conviction, and is governed by the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders and Police Rules, 1934. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 724.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 141 QSO: Object of Cross-Examination
records.heading: The object of cross-examination is to test credibility and obtain help for one's own case
records.text: Art. 141 QSO concerns questions lawful in cross-examination. The object of cross-examination is to test the credibility of a witness and obtain something helpful to one's own case, and the modes of shaking credibility depend on the facts of each case. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 646, PLJ 2021 CrC 1565.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 94 CrPC: Production of Documents
records.heading: Section 94(1) CrPC allows production of documents at any stage if the court finds it necessary
records.text: Section 94(1) CrPC empowers the court to direct production of any document or thing it considers necessary for a just decision. Its scope is wide and may be invoked at any stage of inquiry or trial, the only precondition being that the applicant satisfies the court that production is necessary. Ref: PLJ 2022 CrC 646, PLJ 2021 CrC 1565.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Grandfather's Liability for Maintenance; Execution
records.heading: A grandfather's maintenance liability is conditional, and execution cannot shift to him merely on the father's default
records.text: Under para 370 of Mulla's Muhammadan Law, a grandfather's duty to maintain grandchildren arises only if the father is poor and infirm, the mother cannot maintain, and the grandfather is in easy circumstances. The Family Court may use CPC procedure to execute its decree, and execution cannot shift to the grandfather merely because the father did not satisfy it. Ref: 2023 LHC 2702; Muhammad Siddique v. Amna Bibi etc. (Family 52429/20, decided 10.05.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Siddique v. Amna Bibi etc. (Family 52429/20, decided 10.05.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Acceptance of Resignations of Members National Assembly
records.heading: Notifications accepting resignations of 72 National Assembly members were set aside as without lawful authority
records.text: Notifications issued by the National Assembly Secretariat accepting the resignations of 72 members, and the consequent ECP notifications, were held to be without lawful authority and set aside. The Speaker was directed to complete his inquiry and hear the petitioners afresh. Ref: 2023 LHC 2719; Muhammad Riaz Khan Fatyana & 42 others v. Speaker National Assembly Islamabad etc. (8360/23, decided 19.05.2023); Justice Shahid Karim.
records.title: Muhammad Riaz Khan Fatyana & 42 others v. Speaker National Assembly Islamabad etc. (8360/23, decided 19.05.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Female Minors: Mother's Right of Hizanat
records.heading: A mother is entitled to custody of her female children until puberty
records.text: Section 17 of the Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 requires the court to consider the welfare of the minor, with regard to age, gender and religion. Under Muhammadan Law the mother is entitled to custody (Hizanat) of her female children until puberty. Ref: 2023 MLD 1000.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody and Guardianship Distinguished
records.heading: Custody and guardianship are distinct and custody is subordinate to the welfare of the minor
records.text: The Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 distinguishes custody, meaning the right of upbringing, from guardianship. The father remains natural guardian and must maintain the child even where the mother has custody. Custody is subordinate to the welfare of the minor, and the mother cannot be denied custody for lack of resources. Ref: 2023 MLD 1000.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Territorial Jurisdiction of Family Court: Maintenance
records.heading: Territorial jurisdiction of the Family Court in maintenance depends on cause of action or residence
records.text: Under Art. 175(2) of the Constitution, jurisdiction exists only as conferred by law. The Family Court's jurisdiction over maintenance arises under s. 5 and the Schedule to the Family Courts Act, 1964, and under R. 6 of the Family Court Rules, 1965 the competent court is where the cause of action arose in whole or part, or where the parties reside or last resided together. Ref: 2023 MLD 914.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Construction of Nikahnama Stipulations
records.heading: Nikahnama stipulations are construed according to the parties' intentions, whatever the column
records.text: The petitioner was held entitled to dower, reversing concurrent judgments. The inquiry report on a false Nikahnama entry had no legal basis, and stipulations in a Nikahnama are construed according to the parties' intentions irrespective of the column in which they appear. Ref: 2023 LHC 2744; Mst. Aniza etc. v. ADJ etc. (Family 38446-16, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Mst. Aniza etc. v. ADJ etc. (Family 38446-16, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 22-A CrPC: Breach of Trust and FIO 2001
records.heading: The 2001 Ordinance applies only between customer and financial institution, not to the proposed accused here
records.text: The Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001 applies only where the parties stand as customer and financial institution. The proposed accused in a bank pledge case were not customers, and a surveyor appointed by the bank became its agent. The s. 22-A application concerned s. 409 PPC. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 697.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Interference in Criminal Investigation
records.heading: Under Article 199 the High Court cannot act as an appellate court over investigation
records.text: The High Court cannot hear a petition under Art. 199 like an appeal and substitute its findings. It determines only whether there is an error of law or jurisdiction, and no court may interfere in investigation except in certain circumstances. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 810.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Physical Remand: s. 167 CrPC Revision
records.heading: Revision lies against a section 167 CrPC remand order, which must not be mechanical
records.text: A revision lies against a s. 167 CrPC order. Remand must not be granted mechanically or refused on conjecture, and is decided on the record including police diaries. A further 48 hours of police custody to recover a mobile phone was upheld and the High Court declined to interfere. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 810.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording Witness Statement
records.heading: Delay in recording a witness statement without cogent reason impairs credibility
records.text: Where a witness's statement was recorded with delay without cogent reason, its credibility is impaired. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 850.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Single Unbroken Chain
records.heading: In circumstantial evidence cases any missing link in the chain destroys the prosecution case
records.text: In a case of circumstantial evidence the prosecution must show the pieces of evidence are inter-linked into one chain, of a quality incompatible with the accused's innocence. Any missing link destroys the entire prosecution case. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 850.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 265-C CrPC: Copies of Hard Disks
records.heading: Supply of copies of hard disks to the accused under section 265-C is mandatory
records.text: It is mandatory under s. 265-C CrPC to supply the accused copies of hard disks. The trial court's course of having a constable in court prepare copies was unwarranted, and it should have sent them to the investigating agency's IT department. The order excluding the disks was set aside and the revision allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 690.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 342 CrPC: Re-Recording Statement of Accused
records.heading: Evidence not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used against him
records.text: The first part of s. 342 CrPC allows the court to ask questions at any time, and evidence not put to the accused cannot be used against him, in line with audi alteram partem. The petition was dismissed with a direction that the trial court put additional questions on the available evidence and treat them as part of the earlier statement. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 805.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Superdari of Non-Customs Paid Vehicles
records.heading: Police cannot seize non-custom paid vehicles, which is a matter for Customs Officers
records.text: No FIR was registered and there was no basis to seize the vehicle under s. 550 CrPC. Police have no power to seize non-custom paid vehicles, as that lies with Customs Officers, and good faith police acts are protected by Art. 171 of the Police Order, 2002. The petition was allowed, leaving Customs to pursue lawful remedies. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 834.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Disbelieved Prosecution Evidence: No Need for Defence Version
records.heading: If prosecution evidence is disbelieved, the court need not consider the defence version
records.text: If the prosecution's evidence is not believed, the trial court need not even consider the defence story and should acquit the accused. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 87.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower Payable on Demand is Prompt
records.heading: Dower stated as payable on demand is prompt dower
records.text: Where the Nikahnama does not state whether dower is prompt or deferred and says only that it is payable on demand, it is not deferred dower and is payable on demand during the subsistence of marriage. Ref: 2023 LHC 2773; Samina v. ADJ etc. (Family 5278/21, decided 24.05.2023); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Samina v. ADJ etc. (Family 5278/21, decided 24.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Rectification of Sale Deed: Limitation and Minority
records.heading: A suit to rectify a sale deed succeeded within limitation despite the minority of two respondents
records.text: Concurrent findings were reversed and the suit for rectification of a sale deed decreed. The suit was within limitation, execution was proved under s. 68 of the Evidence Act, and the minority of two respondents was not fatal as their interest was safeguarded and they did not sue within three years of disability ceasing (ss. 6 and 8, Art. 91 Limitation Act, 1908). Ref: 2023 LHC 2786; Abdur Rehman etc. v. Manzoor Ahmad etc. (Civil Revision 1933-12, decided 17.05.2023); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Abdur Rehman etc. v. Manzoor Ahmad etc. (Civil Revision 1933-12, decided 17.05.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Audio Leaks Inquiry Commission Suspended
records.heading: The audio leaks inquiry commission was suspended and consultation with the Chief Justice is mandatory
records.text: The Supreme Court suspended the notification of 19 May 2023 constituting the audio leaks inquiry commission and restrained its proceedings. It observed that the government cannot interfere in judicial matters and that consultation with the Chief Justice on nominating judges to such a commission is mandatory. Next hearing was fixed for 31 May. Ref: Abid Shahid Zuberi, Advocate Supreme Court of Pakistan, Karachi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 14/2023, decided 26.05.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Abid Shahid Zuberi, Advocate Supreme Court of Pakistan, Karachi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 14/2023, decided 26.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Cancellation v. Declaration of Document: Void or Voidable
records.heading: Cancellation lies for a voidable document, while a void document allows either remedy
records.text: A suit for cancellation under s. 39 and one for declaration under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 differ according to whether the document is void or voidable. For a voidable document (consent by coercion, fraud and the like) only cancellation lies. For a void one (forgery or deceit as to its nature) either remedy is open. Ref: 2021 SCMR 198.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Delegation of Commissioner's Powers under s. 122(5A)
records.heading: The Commissioner's powers under section 122(5A) can be delegated to the Additional Commissioner
records.text: The Commissioner's powers under s. 122(5A) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 can be delegated to the Additional Commissioner Inland Revenue under s. 210 of the Ordinance. Ref: Allied Bank Limited v. The Commissioner of Incom Tax, Lahore, etc. (C.P. 6-L/2023, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Allied Bank Limited v. The Commissioner of Incom Tax, Lahore, etc. (C.P. 6-L/2023, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Informing Advocates of Fixation of Cases
records.heading: Order on informing advocates of the fixation of cases, no holding stated
records.text: The order concerns the mode and manner of informing advocates about the fixation of cases by the Supreme Court. The post gives no further holding. Ref: Mehtab Publications (Pvt) Ltd thr. Raja Mehtab Ahmed, Islamabad v. Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) thr. its Chairman, Islamabad & others (C.M.A. 9009/2022, decided 26.05.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
