records.title: Mehtab Publications (Pvt) Ltd thr. Raja Mehtab Ahmed, Islamabad v. Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) thr. its Chairman, Islamabad & others (C.M.A. 9009/2022, decided 26.05.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Double Taxation Treaties and Review Jurisdiction
records.heading: Judgment on double taxation treaties, the Vienna Convention and review jurisdiction under Article 188
records.text: The judgment discusses ss. 107, 109 and 44 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, avoidance of double taxation under double taxation treaties, Art. 31 of the Vienna Convention 1969, and review jurisdiction under Art. 188 of the Constitution read with Order XXVI of the Supreme Court Rules 1980 and O. XLVII R. 1 CPC. Ref: Commissioner Inland Revenue Z-III v. M/s. MSC Switzerland Geneva & others (C.R.P. 432-K/2022, decided 09.02.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Commissioner Inland Revenue Z-III v. M/s. MSC Switzerland Geneva & others (C.R.P. 432-K/2022, decided 09.02.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Consumer Protection Act: Limitation and Expert Evidence
records.heading: The 30 day period under the Consumer Protection Act runs from knowledge of defect, and denied defects need expert evidence
records.text: The 30 day period under s. 28(4) of the Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005 runs from knowledge of the defect, after written notice under s. 28(1) and 15 days to respond under s. 28(2). Where technical defects are denied, the consumer must bring expert evidence, and the Consumer Court must be satisfied that it suffices. Ref: M/s Pak Suzuki Motors Company, Ltd. thr. its Manager v. Faisal Jameel Butt and another (C.A. 797/2017, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: M/s Pak Suzuki Motors Company, Ltd. thr. its Manager v. Faisal Jameel Butt and another (C.A. 797/2017, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: House-Breaking by Night: Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: House-breaking by night under section 458 PPC falls within the prohibitory clause
records.text: The facts alleged prima facie constituted house-breaking by night after preparation for hurt under s. 458 PPC rather than s. 452. That offence carries up to fourteen years and falls within the prohibitory clause of s. 497(1) CrPC. The sanctity of home under Art. 14 of the Constitution calls for strict enforcement of such laws. Ref: Hilal Khattak v. The State through Attorney General for Pakistan and another (Crl.P. 461/2023, decided 24.05.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Hilal Khattak v. The State through Attorney General for Pakistan and another (Crl.P. 461/2023, decided 24.05.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Articles: Alternate Value and Appreciation
records.heading: A risen value of a dowry article is assessed at the date of realisation of the decree
records.text: In a suit for return of dowry, the alternate value is ordinarily assessed with depreciation for wear and tear. Where an article such as a car has risen in value, the claimant is entitled to its market value as on the date of realisation of the decree, not the price paid in 2017. Ref: 2023 LHC 2845; Muhammad Afzal v. ADJ etc. (WP Family 57778/22, decided 26.04.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Afzal v. ADJ etc. (WP Family 57778/22, decided 26.04.2023)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Intra-Court Appeal Against Refusal to Initiate Contempt
records.heading: Interference with refusal to initiate contempt requires a serious legal question or grave miscarriage of justice
records.text: An appellate court may interfere with an order refusing to initiate contempt proceedings only where a serious question of law arises or grave miscarriage of justice is shown, such as findings that are arbitrary, perverse, ridiculous or improbable. Ref: 2023 LHC 2854; Muhammad Ali v. Dr. Ali Raza (I.C.A. 118-23, decided 22.05.2023); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Ali v. Dr. Ali Raza (I.C.A. 118-23, decided 22.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Valid Contract Elements; Enforcing Unsigned Agreement
records.heading: An unsigned agreement may be enforced if its necessary ingredients are proved
records.text: Under ss. 2(h) and 10 of the Contract Act, a valid agreement needs consent, consideration, capacity and a lawful object, judged by objective manifestations of intent. Where the parties did not intend to be bound until a signed writing, neither is bound, but an unsigned agreement may be enforced if its necessary ingredients are proved. Ref: Said Rasool v. Maqbool Ahmed (deceased) through his L.Rs., etc. (C.A. 102-L/2017, decided 17.05.2023); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Said Rasool v. Maqbool Ahmed (deceased) through his L.Rs., etc. (C.A. 102-L/2017, decided 17.05.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wajtakar Witnesses and Res Gestae
records.heading: Wajtakar evidence of witnesses who heard the shot is reliable under res gestae
records.text: Prosecution witnesses who heard the gunshot and saw the petitioner flee with a pistol gave wajtakar evidence, reliable under the doctrine of res gestae in Art. 19 QSO. Being residents of the locality, their presence was natural, and cross-examination yielded nothing. Minor discrepancies not going to the root of the case carry little weight. Ref: Muhammad Ijaz v. The State (J.P. 206/2019, decided 08.05.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz v. The State (J.P. 206/2019, decided 08.05.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Two Possible Views: Benefit to Accused; Cancellation
records.heading: Where two views are possible, the view favourable to the accused is adopted
records.text: Where two views are possible on the evidence, the view favourable to the accused is adopted. The post also introduces guidelines for cancellation of bail, which it does not reproduce. Ref: Saeed Ullah S/o Jumma Khan and others v. The State through A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P. 245/2023, decided 04.05.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Saeed Ullah S/o Jumma Khan and others v. The State through A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P. 245/2023, decided 04.05.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest and Post-Arrest Bail: Same Role, s. 497(2)
records.heading: Same role for pre-arrest and post-arrest bail petitioners makes the case one of further inquiry
records.text: The injuries were on non-vital parts and no repeat fire was made, so applicability of s. 324 PPC was for the trial court. Both petitioners having the same role, one on interim pre-arrest bail and the other seeking post-arrest bail, the case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC calling for further inquiry. Ref: Jamaluddin & Juma v. The State (Crl.P. 41-K/2023, decided 29.05.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Jamaluddin & Juma v. The State (Crl.P. 41-K/2023, decided 29.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Cancellation v. Declaration of Document: Void or Voidable
records.heading: Cancellation of a voidable document and declaration for a void document are distinguished
records.text: A suit for cancellation under s. 39 and one for declaration under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 are distinguished by whether the document is void or voidable. For a voidable document only cancellation lies. For a void document, such as a forgery, either remedy is available. Ref: 2021 SCMR 1986.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: FIR Registration Irregularities and Delay: Acquittal
records.heading: Irregularities in FIR registration and delay cast doubt on the prosecution and led to acquittal
records.text: Delay in lodging the FIR, non-entry of the oral complaint in the FIR register as Rule 24.5 of the Police Rules, 1934 requires, non-production of the computer operator who typed the FIR, and unexplained delay in postmortem cast doubt on the prosecution. Conviction could not be sustained and the appeal was allowed. Ref: 2023 LHC 2869; Ali Ahsan Sunny v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 193932/18, decided 22.05.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Ali Ahsan Sunny v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 193932/18, decided 22.05.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII CPC: Unilateral Statement is No Compromise
records.heading: A unilateral statement made in the opponent's absence is not a compromise under Order XXIII
records.text: A compromise needs mutual concessions and satisfaction of the Court under O. XXIII R. 3 CPC. A unilateral statement made in the opponent's absence and unsupported by a document, in order to withdraw a suit, has no binding effect. The trial court's rejection of plaint was restored and the appeal allowed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 344.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Widow of Judge: Benefits under Office Memorandum
records.heading: A Judge's widow is entitled to the benefits under the office memorandum of 2015
records.text: The widow of a Judge who died in service is entitled to the benefits under the office memorandum of 4 December 2015, namely rent of hired house until superannuation age and a lump sum grant in lieu of plot if no plot was allotted. The contrary office memoranda of 2020 were set aside and the petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 324.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Punjab Bar Council: Writ Not Maintainable
records.heading: A writ against the Punjab Bar Council is not maintainable as it is an autonomous private body
records.text: The Punjab Bar Council is an autonomous private body without Government control, though constituted under the Act, so a constitutional petition against it is not maintainable. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 313.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sine Die Adjournment of Sessions Trial
records.heading: A Sessions trial cannot be adjourned sine die merely because a co-accused is unarrested
records.text: No express provision permits adjourning a Sessions trial indefinitely, and s. 249 CrPC is confined to First Class Magistrates in State cases. Adjourning sine die solely because a co-accused is unarrested was not justified, as the accused has a right to an expeditious decision. The impugned order was set aside and the revision accepted. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 334; Nadeem Sultan and another v. Hamza Shamim (Criminal Revision No. 91 of 2022).
records.title: Nadeem Sultan and another v. Hamza Shamim (Criminal Revision No. 91 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 265-D CrPC: Discharge is a Legal Requirement
records.heading: Discharge under section 265-D is a legal requirement and section 249 does not apply to private complaints
records.text: Charge and discharge must be decided with care, as involving a person in criminal process without sufficient evidence offends Art. 4 of the Constitution. Discharge under s. 265-D CrPC is a legal requirement, and s. 249 CrPC applies only to cases instituted on police report, not private complaints. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 291; Muhammad Usman Ghani v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 5 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Usman Ghani v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 5 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Right of Confrontation and Cross-Examination
records.heading: The right to confront and cross-examine witnesses is part of fair trial under Article 10-A
records.text: The right to confront witnesses is part of fair trial under Art. 10-A of the Constitution, and cross-examination is a statutory right under Art. 133 QSO. Evidence relied on against an accused must be put to him for challenge. The trial court must ensure the accused is not under-represented by inexperienced counsel. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 300; Fayyaz Hussain v. The State.
records.title: Fayyaz Hussain v. The State

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Competition Act 2010: Passing-Off and Confusing Similarity
records.heading: Competition Act 2010: passing-off, confusing similarity and no locus standi for an adjudicatory body
records.text: The judgment addresses free and fair competition as part of the right to freedom of trade under Art. 18 of the Constitution, codification of passing-off and injurious falsehood, s. 10(2)(a) and (d) of the Competition Act 2010, confusing similarity in labelling and packaging, and the lack of locus standi of an adjudicatory body to defend its quasi-judicial decision. Ref: Competition Commission of Pakistan v. A. Rahim Foods (PVT.) Limited & Another (C.A. 444/2017, decided 10.05.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Competition Commission of Pakistan v. A. Rahim Foods (PVT.) Limited & Another (C.A. 444/2017, decided 10.05.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 21 PPC: Public Servant
records.heading: Section 21 PPC and the status of a public servant, no holding stated
records.text: Authority on s. 21 of the Pakistan Penal Code, arising from a petition against the Executive Officer of the Cantonment Board Quetta. The post gives no holding. Ref: Dr. Abdul Nabi v. Executive Officer Cantonment Board Quetta (C.P. 47-Q/2016, decided 21.03.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Dr. Abdul Nabi v. Executive Officer Cantonment Board Quetta (C.P. 47-Q/2016, decided 21.03.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Closing of Right of Cross-Examination
records.heading: An accused cannot hijack the trial, and counsel at State expense may be appointed
records.text: An accused cannot hijack the trial under the guise of fair trial or linger on proceedings to tamper with evidence. The trial court was not helpless and could proceed without violating the right to confront. If the accused did not engage counsel by the next date, counsel at State expense should be appointed under the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders and the trial concluded expeditiously. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 300; Fayyaz Hussain v. The State.
records.title: Fayyaz Hussain v. The State

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale Mutation: Proof of Consideration by Witnesses
records.heading: Payment of consideration in a sale mutation must be shown by witnesses who saw it
records.text: Payment of consideration must be shown by reliable witnesses who saw it made. The preferred witnesses under s. 42 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 were absent, the revenue officer did not depose, and the witnesses and deed writer had not seen payment. The appellate decree was set aside and the trial court's decree upheld. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 380.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Court-Fee: Deficiency and Deciding Appeal First
records.heading: A court should first attend to court-fee and late payment does not prejudice the opposite party
records.text: A court should first attend to court-fee, and non-payment may lead to rejection of the plaint, a principle applying equally to memoranda of appeal. The appellate court adopted a course the law did not provide by allowing the appeal subject to payment within thirty days. Non-payment or belated payment does not adversely affect the opposite party. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 470.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Land Transactions by Hard of Hearing Non-Verbal Persons
records.heading: Land transactions by a hard of hearing non-verbal person need safeguards against fraud and undervaluation
records.text: Transactions of persons of unsound mind or intellectually disabled must proceed through a next friend or guardian under O. XXXII R. 15 CPC. For a person who is hard of hearing and non-verbal but not intellectually disabled, safeguards must ensure freedom from influence, misrepresentation or fraud, and that consideration equals value and was paid. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 456.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test Without Consent in Civil Cases
records.heading: In civil cases a DNA test cannot be ordered without consent
records.text: In civil cases a DNA test cannot be ordered without consent, as it infringes the rights to liberty and privacy under Arts. 9 and 14 of the Constitution. If the party bearing the onus withholds consent, the court may draw an adverse presumption under Art. 129(g) QSO, which is permissive. The request for DNA testing was refused. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 461; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Despite Alternate Remedy: Mala Fide Order
records.heading: A writ may be entertained despite an alternate remedy where the order is mala fide or unauthorised
records.text: A writ petition may be entertained despite an alternate remedy where the statutory body's order is without lawful authority, unjust or mala fide. Not exhausting the remedy of revision is not fatal to a constitutional petition. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 392.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Grandfather's Maintenance Liability; Bait-ul-Mal Directions
records.heading: Grandchildren's maintenance upheld with Bait-ul-Mal directed to pay each minor monthly
records.text: In a Hindu personal law matter the grandfather challenged a maintenance order in favour of minor grandchildren. The Court stressed the State's duty to protect the family and directed Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal to register the minors as beneficiaries and pay Rs.10,000 monthly to each until marriage, increasing by 10 percent annually, through their mother. Ref: PLD 2023 Sindh 214.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Directions for Protection of Child Sexual Abuse Survivors
records.heading: Directions for protection of child sexual abuse survivors during investigation and custody
records.text: The High Court directed medico legal officers to follow Standard Operating Procedures and that the Zainab Alert Act, 2020, the ICT Child Protection Act, 2018 and the Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018 be implemented. Sexual offences against children should be investigated by a female or sensitised officer, no child survivor held overnight in police custody, and child survivors never placed in the accused's presence. Ref: PLD 2023 Islamabad 195.

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Defining Sexual Harassment at the Workplace
records.heading: Judgment defining sexual harassment under the 2010 Workplace Harassment Act, no further holding
records.text: The judgment defines sexual harassment under the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010. The post gives no further holding. Ref: Nadia Naz v. The President of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Islamabad & others (C.R.P. 255/2021, decided 06.06.2023); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Nadia Naz v. The President of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Islamabad & others (C.R.P. 255/2021, decided 06.06.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chain of Custody of Weapons and Tool Marks
records.heading: Firearm and tool mark inferences require recorded statements, Malkhana custody and proof of safe transmission
records.text: Inferences drawn on firearms and tool marks require that the investigating officer record s. 161 CrPC statements identifying the parcel, the weapon be kept in the Malkhana with an entry produced in court, the Malkhana in-charge be examined, and safe transmission to the Forensic Science Laboratory be proved through police evidence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 735.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Firing in Court Premises: Triable by ATC
records.heading: Firing within court premises is triable only by the Anti-Terrorism Court
records.text: Firing within court premises is an offence in the Third Schedule of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 and is triable only by the Anti-Terrorism Court, even where it arises from personal vendetta. A court of ordinary jurisdiction receiving such a challan should return it to the prosecution for presentation before the ATC, as s. 190 CrPC limits a magistrate's cognizance. Ref: 2023 LHC 2898; Ali Nawaz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8329/23, decided 25.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ali Nawaz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8329/23, decided 25.05.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Effect of Criminal Sentence on Government Service
records.heading: Effect of a criminal sentence on government service, no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the after effects of a sentence in a criminal case on the government service of a public servant. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 2911; Iftikhar Ahmed v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 340-13, decided 10.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmed v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 340-13, decided 10.05.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: NAB Pre-Arrest Bail: Requirements for Court
records.heading: Requirements for granting pre-arrest bail in NAB cases, no holding stated
records.text: The case concerns the requirements a court must consider when granting pre-arrest bail in NAB cases, in a petition by the Chairman NAB seeking cancellation of bail. The post gives no holding. Ref: Chairman, National Accountability Bureau, Islamabad v. Yar Muhammad Solangi & others (C.P. 101/2020, decided 29.03.2023); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Chairman, National Accountability Bureau, Islamabad v. Yar Muhammad Solangi & others (C.P. 101/2020, decided 29.03.2023)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Cheque Given as Security; Quashing of FIR
records.heading: A plea that a cheque was given as security is a defence and does not justify quashing
records.text: The plea that the cheque was given as security is a defence and a question of fact, so an FIR cannot be quashed under Art. 199 unless the facts are admitted. Civil and criminal liability for dishonour are independent. Liability under s. 489-F PPC generally arises only for cheques issued to discharge an accrued or determined liability, unless the one-transaction or continuing act theory applies. Ref: Hayat Kimya Pakistan (Private) Limited v. Humair Yusuf and others (Writ Petition No. 3103/2023).
records.title: Hayat Kimya Pakistan (Private) Limited v. Humair Yusuf and others (Writ Petition No. 3103/2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Discretionary Relief and Conduct
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary and may be declined on the purchaser's conduct
records.text: Relinquishment of the right to specific performance depends on the parties' conduct and evidence. Specific performance is discretionary and equitable under s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, and may be declined where unjust. The courts below refused it to a purchaser who paid only 8 percent as earnest money, and the High Court upheld the refusal. Ref: 2023 CLC 1100; Asim Jamshaid v. Shahzad Iqbal Malik.
records.title: Asim Jamshaid v. Shahzad Iqbal Malik

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Summons Without Plaint, Limitation
records.heading: In a summary suit, time to seek leave to defend runs only after the plaint copy is supplied
records.text: In a summary suit under O. XXXVII CPC, summons must be on Form IV with a copy of the plaint and annexures. Without them service is not proper, and the ten day limitation under Art. 159 of the Limitation Act, 1908 for leave to defend does not run until the copy is supplied. Ref: 2023 CLC 1131.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tentative Rent Order on Denial of Relationship
records.heading: The Rent Controller cannot go beyond the Act when the landlord-tenant relationship is denied
records.text: The question was whether, where the relationship of landlord and tenant is denied, the Rent Controller may pass a tentative rent order under s. 17(8) of the Act, 1963. The Rent Controller cannot travel beyond the ambit of that Act, which regulates matters between landlord and tenant. Ref: 2023 CLC 1070.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prosecution Not Bound to Produce All Witnesses
records.heading: The prosecution is not bound to produce all witnesses
records.text: The prosecution is not bound to produce all witnesses. If the appellants believed the withheld witnesses would not support the prosecution, they could examine them in defence or seek to have them summoned as Court witnesses, and confidence inspiring prosecution evidence cannot be discarded on that basis alone. Ref: Muhammad Anwar v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 204964/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 204964/2018)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Exhaustion of Remedies; Merger of Interim Orders
records.heading: Exhaustion of alternate remedies before writ jurisdiction and merger of interim orders into final orders
records.text: The judgment addresses invoking High Court writ jurisdiction without availing alternate remedies, under the doctrine of exhaustion of remedies, and the merger of interim orders into final orders. Ref: Mian Azam Waheed v. The Collector of Customs thr. Addl. Collector of Customs, Model Customs Collectorate of Appraisement (East), Karachi (C.P. 3215/2021); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mian Azam Waheed v. The Collector of Customs thr. Addl. Collector of Customs, Model Customs Collectorate of Appraisement (East), Karachi (C.P. 3215/2021)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Money Laundering Requires Predicate Offence
records.heading: A predicate offence is a necessary element of money laundering
records.text: Commission of a predicate offence is a necessary element of money laundering, since it gives rise to the proceeds of crime. Without a predicate offence there can be no offence of money laundering. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1030.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Arts. 10 and 10A: Right to Fair Trial
records.heading: Articles 10 and 10A guarantee arrest safeguards and a fair trial however heinous the crime
records.text: Arts. 10 and 10A of the Constitution guarantee safeguards on arrest and detention and a fair trial with due process. An arrested person must be told the grounds of arrest and the charge, may consult and be defended by a lawyer, may cross-examine witnesses, explain the evidence against him and produce defence evidence. The guarantee under Art. 10A cannot be taken away however heinous the crime. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 92.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C CrPC: Supply of Documents to Accused
records.heading: Non-supply of documents under section 265-C CrPC vitiates the whole trial
records.text: The accused is entitled to know the case against him, so s. 265-C CrPC is to be construed liberally and copies of all oral and documentary evidence must be supplied before trial. Non-compliance vitiates the whole trial even if the accused conceded the omission. A statement written in the s. 172 diary instead of under s. 161 CrPC must also be supplied. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 92.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Examination of Accused
records.heading: Examination of the accused under section 342 is a mandate and every incriminating piece must be put
records.text: Examination of the accused under s. 342 CrPC is a mandate, not a formality, based on the maxim audi alteram partem. Every incriminating piece of evidence that may be used for conviction must be put to the accused, and deviation from this duty renders the conviction invalid. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 92.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Purpose of Criminal Proceedings: Discovering Truth
records.heading: The purpose of criminal proceedings is to discover the truth and reach a just decision
records.text: The sole purpose of judicial proceedings in a criminal case is to discover the truth and reach a just decision, meaning one that is right, fair and well founded. The court should ensure that no aspect of the case is left unattended before the final verdict. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 92.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C CrPC: Supply of Statements and Documents
records.heading: Copies of DVD or CD evidence must be supplied to the accused under section 265-C
records.text: S. 265-C CrPC cannot be read in isolation from the proviso to Art. 164 QSO, so courts must supply copies of modern-device evidence such as DVD or CD material. Where such material was never supplied or shown to the accused, conviction was set aside and the case remanded to the Trial Court. Courts may also direct supply of copies at other stages if justice demands. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 92.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Set Up but Not Proved
records.heading: If the prosecution sets up a motive and fails to prove it, the prosecution suffers
records.text: The prosecution need not establish motive in every murder case, but if it sets up a motive and fails to prove it, the prosecution must suffer the consequences and not the accused. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 917.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Simultaneous Civil and Criminal Proceedings
records.heading: Civil and criminal proceedings on the same matter ordinarily proceed together
records.text: Civil and criminal proceedings on the same matter may ordinarily proceed together. A criminal trial may be postponed only where criminal liability depends on or is intimately connected with the civil outcome and a bona fide claim cannot be separated from the alleged offence. It will not be stayed where the subject matters are distinct or the civil suit is mala fide. Ref: Salman Ashraf v. Additional District Judge, Lahore, etc. (C.P. 2000-L/2020, decided 26.05.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Salman Ashraf v. Additional District Judge, Lahore, etc. (C.P. 2000-L/2020, decided 26.05.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Consolidation of Causes from Different Jurisdictions
records.heading: Causes from different jurisdictions, or civil, criminal and family matters, cannot be consolidated
records.text: Causes emanating from different jurisdictions cannot be consolidated in a single proceeding. A civil matter cannot be consolidated with a criminal matter or with a family matter. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1002.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Suit Challenging Nikahnama Entry: Family Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: A suit challenging a Nikahnama entry is triable exclusively by the Family Court
records.text: A suit challenging the validity of an entry in the Nikahnama is to be tried exclusively by the Family Court. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1002.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Contradictions in Ocular Account: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Contradictions between the complainant and eye-witness led to benefit of doubt and acquittal
records.text: In a case under ss. 302(b), 109 and 34 PPC, the complainant and the eye-witness contradicted each other on the identity of a witness, relationships and timings. Their evidence was found untruthful and discarded, the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt, and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 896.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Recovery of Weapon of Offence
records.heading: Weapon recovery in doubtful circumstances is merely corroborative and gives the prosecution no help
records.text: Recovery of a pistol from the house of a person related to both parties, in a densely populated locality and without any family member present, was doubtful. Such recovery is merely corroborative and offers no help to the prosecution without trustworthy eye-witness evidence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 896.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: A glaring conflict between ocular and medical evidence shows the eye-witnesses were not present
records.text: Where the injury described by eye-witnesses as an entry wound was an exit wound per the post mortem report, and injury directions were inconsistent with their account, the glaring conflict showed that the eye-witnesses were not present. The ocular account was tainted and could not be given legal credence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 896.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved
records.heading: Motive was not proved where the enmity did not involve the deceased
records.text: Where the alleged enmity was between the accused and the complainant, the deceased had nothing to do with it, and no evidence of motive was tendered, the prosecution failed to prove the motive. The complainant being present and spared made the alleged motive improbable. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 896.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unscathed Eye-Witnesses: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Eye-witnesses left unscathed while at the accused's mercy raise benefit of doubt
records.text: The accused allegedly fired repeatedly at the deceased, yet the complainant and eye-witnesses were not scratched although at his mercy. The prosecution could not prove its case beyond doubt and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 896.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. II Rr. 1 and 2 CPC: Splitting of Causes of Action
records.heading: A suit must include the whole claim and causes of action should not be split
records.text: Every suit must include the whole claim arising from the cause of action (O. II R. 2 CPC). A dismissed employee should have united the challenge to the rejection of the departmental appeal and to the dismissal order, instead of splitting them between a writ petition and a civil suit, which caused overlapping and multiplicity of proceedings. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1083.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ex Parte Proceedings: Court Not to Act Mechanically
records.heading: Despite the defendant's non-appearance, the court must not act mechanically
records.text: Despite non-appearance of the defendant, the court should not act mechanically and must consider the legal and factual aspects on the basis of the material before it. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1118.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Financial Document: Two Marginal Witnesses
records.heading: A party relying on a financial document must produce its two marginal witnesses, even in ex parte cases
records.text: Where execution and attestation of a document relating to financial or future obligations is put in issue, the party relying on it must produce its two marginal witnesses. The rule applies equally where the defendant has been proceeded against ex parte. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1118.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence in Appeal
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal is allowed only in the two exceptions under Order XLI Rule 27
records.text: Under O. XLI R. 27 CPC no evidence is generally produced at the appellate stage. There are two exceptions: where the lower court refused to admit evidence it ought to have admitted, or where the appellate court requires a document to pronounce judgment. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1155.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 92 QSO: Presumption of Genuineness of Documents
records.heading: A properly proved document raises a rebuttable presumption of genuineness of its contents
records.text: Once a document is proved in accordance with law, the genuineness of its contents may be presumed (acta probant sese ipsa). Documentary evidence cannot ordinarily be overridden by oral evidence, but the presumption is rebuttable by cogent and reliable evidence to the contrary. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1155.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Fresh Plea Not Raised Before Supreme Court
records.heading: The Supreme Court does not decide a fresh plea not raised in the lower courts
records.text: In its appellate jurisdiction the Supreme Court generally does not decide a ground or question of fact not pleaded or raised before the lower court and High Court. An appellant has no right to raise an entirely new plea on the pretext of doing complete justice. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1072.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Dower Limitation: Revenue Entries Dispute
records.heading: A dispute over revenue entries while the wife possessed the land is not a dower matter
records.text: The dispute concerned wrong entries in the revenue record while the wife was in possession and receiving the proceeds, so it was not a dower matter. The six year period runs from when the right to sue accrued, and the suit was held not barred by time nor required to be filed in the Family Court, relying on 2000 SCMR 1574. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1072.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Transmission of Samples to FSL Not Proved
records.heading: Safe transmission of samples is unproved where the delivering constable was not produced and delay was unexplained
records.text: Where the constable who delivered the sample parcels to the Forensic Science Laboratory was not produced and the delay of twelve days was unexplained, safe transmission was not established. The prosecution could not be held to have proved its case beyond reasonable doubt, giving the accused the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1009.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Samples: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Unexplained delay and missing witnesses defeat safe custody of samples and give benefit of doubt
records.text: Samples reached the laboratory four days after recovery without explanation, and neither the Moharrar nor the delivering constable was produced, so safe custody and transmission were not established. The prosecution also failed to prove ownership of the vehicle. The accused were given the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1144, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 29; Aid Wazir v. State.
records.title: Aid Wazir v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Purpose of Bail
records.heading: The primary purpose of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused
records.text: The primary purpose of bail is to ensure the attendance of the accused before the court. It also enables the accused, who is presumed innocent, to pursue normal activities essential to life such as earning a livelihood and caring for the family. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1093.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Belatedly Recorded Witness Statements
records.heading: A prosecution witness statement recorded at a belated stage loses its sanctity
records.text: A statement of a prosecution witness recorded at a belated stage loses its sanctity. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1140, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 25; Salman Zahid v. State through P.G. Sindh.
records.title: Salman Zahid v. State through P.G. Sindh

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Test for Guilt
records.heading: In circumstantial evidence cases the facts must be incompatible with innocence and unexplainable on any other hypothesis
records.text: In a case resting on circumstantial evidence, the incriminating facts must be incompatible with the innocence of the accused and incapable of explanation on any reasonable hypothesis other than guilt. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1140, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 25; Salman Zahid v. State through P.G. Sindh.
records.title: Salman Zahid v. State through P.G. Sindh

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: House-Breaking by Night: S. 458 PPC and Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: House-breaking by night under section 458 PPC falls within the prohibitory clause and bail was declined
records.text: Facts alleged in the FIR prima facie constituted house-breaking by night after preparation for hurt under s. 458 PPC, punishable up to fourteen years, which falls within the prohibitory clause of s. 497(1) CrPC. Leave to appeal was refused and bail was declined. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1182, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 31; Hilal Khattak v. State and another.
records.title: Hilal Khattak v. State and another

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Non-Prohibitory Clause Offences: Three Exceptions to Bail
records.heading: Outside the prohibitory clause bail is a rule but may be refused on three grounds
records.text: In offences outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497(1) CrPC bail is a rule but not a right. It may be refused where the accused is likely to abscond, tamper with evidence or influence witnesses, or repeat the offence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1182, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 31; Hilal Khattak v. State and another.
records.title: Hilal Khattak v. State and another

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Risk of Absconding and Harm to Abductee
records.heading: Bail refused where there was risk of absconding and harm to the abductee
records.text: The accused, the father of the alleged abductee, appeared to have the real motive, most co-accused were absconders and the abductee had not been recovered. There was a likelihood of absconding, harming her or influencing her evidence, so almost all three exceptions applied and bail was declined. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1182, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 31; Hilal Khattak v. State and another.
records.title: Hilal Khattak v. State and another

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sanctity of Home: Ss. 455 and 458 PPC
records.heading: House-breaking offences under sections 455 and 458 PPC protect the sanctity of home under Article 14
records.text: House-breaking after preparation for hurt is categorised as a grave offence under s. 455 PPC (day) and s. 458 PPC (night) because of the sanctity and privacy of home guaranteed by Art. 14 of the Constitution. All State organs, including the judiciary, should enforce these protections strictly. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1182, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 31; Hilal Khattak v. State and another.
records.title: Hilal Khattak v. State and another

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay Bail: Delay Caused by Accused
records.heading: Statutory delay bail requires the court to find the delay was not caused by the accused
records.text: On a bail plea based on statutory delay in trial, the court must first form an opinion that the delay was not caused by the accused or those acting for him. Where the accused sought repeated adjournments when witnesses were present, bail was refused and leave to appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1131, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 36; Muhammad Ali v. State and another.
records.title: Muhammad Ali v. State and another

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Further Inquiry, Property Dispute
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where a land dispute and delayed FIR made false implication possible
records.text: In a case of theft of crop arising from a dispute over ownership and possession of land, false implication could not be ruled out. The FIR was delayed by 16 days, only a general role was ascribed and similarly placed co-accused were exonerated or bailed. The case fell under s. 497(2) CrPC and ad interim bail was confirmed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1152.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Weapon Recovery Not Sent to FSL
records.heading: Recovery of a weapon not sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory is inconsequential
records.text: Where the weapon of offence is recovered from the accused but is not sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory, the recovery is inconsequential. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1097.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Reliable Ocular Account: Conviction Maintained
records.heading: An FIR within one hour excludes deliberation and a reliable ocular account sustains conviction
records.text: An FIR lodged within one hour showed promptitude and excluded deliberation. The ocular account of the complainant and two witnesses was reliable and corroborated by medical evidence, so conviction under ss. 324 and 337-F(v) PPC was maintained. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1097.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sentence Reduced: Spur of the Moment, Single Shot
records.heading: Sentence reduced where the offence arose on the spur of the moment from a single shot
records.text: The occurrence arose on the spur of the moment from a quarrel, with a single fire shot on a non vital part, indicating no intention to kill. Conviction was maintained but the five year sentence under s. 324 PPC was reduced to the period already undergone, with Daman payable in instalments. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1097.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-i-Ishhad: Notice Served on One of Two Vendees
records.heading: A pre-emption suit fails if any Talb is skipped or unproved, including defective notice to vendees
records.text: If any Talb is skipped or not proved, a suit for possession through pre-emption fails. Notices of Talb-i-Ishhad received by another vendee on behalf of the others were not service in the eyes of law, so the suit was rightly dismissed and the appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1113.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 79 QSO: Proof of Contract in Ex Parte Suit
records.heading: A contract on financial obligations must be proved under Article 79 even in an ex parte suit
records.text: A contract concerning financial and future obligations must be proved even where the defendant is ex parte. Production through a representative who neither prepared nor attested it, without the original record or marginal witnesses (Art. 79 QSO), failed to prove execution. Leave to appeal was dismissed with costs of Rs. 100,000. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1189.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Test Identification Parade: LHC Directives
records.heading: Lahore High Court directives require a test identification parade within 48 hours of the order
records.text: The Lahore High Court issued directives to protect the rights of the accused under Arts. 4, 9, 10, 10A and 14 of the Constitution. A magistrate committing an accused to jail for a TIP must forward the order to the Sessions Judge, who deputes a magistrate to conduct the TIP within 48 hours. The same applies to Special and Anti-Terrorism Courts. Ref: 2023 LHC 3274; Muhammad Ramzan v. State etc (Writ Petition 9139-23, decided 06.06.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. State etc (Writ Petition 9139-23, decided 06.06.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation as Mixed Question in Summary Suit
records.heading: Limitation is a mixed question of law and fact that the court must decide in a summary suit
records.text: Limitation is a mixed question of law and fact which the court must decide even if not raised as a defence. If its resolution needs disputed facts, an affidavit may be required with the leave application. If it can be decided on admitted or undisputed facts, the court may decide it on its own, whether or not leave to defend is granted. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lahore 330, 2023 YLR 1341; Muhammad Bashir v. Syed Imdad Ali Shah (C.R. No. 6746 of 2020, decided 24.11.2022); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Bashir v. Syed Imdad Ali Shah (C.R. No. 6746 of 2020, decided 24.11.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Sale Mutation in Favour of Brother: Burden of Proof
records.heading: A brother benefiting from an oral sale mutation by an illiterate sister must prove the transaction
records.text: Where the beneficiary of an oral sale mutation was the real brother of an illiterate female plaintiff, he had to prove the transaction and show it was free of undue influence, coercion or fraud. Deprivation of women of inheritance through gifts and mutations is deprecated, relying on 2021 SCMR 179. Ref: 2023 YLR 1521.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Punjab Partition Act 2012: Ss. 7 and 8, Interim Mesne Profits
records.heading: Whether section 8 overrides section 7 so as to bar interim mesne profits, no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the import of ss. 7 and 8 of the Punjab Partition of Immovable Property Act, 2012. The questions posed are whether s. 8 overrides s. 7 so as to bar the trial court from directing deposit of interim mesne profits until the dispute on title or share is resolved. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2023 YLR 1362.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Preliminary Inquiry in Complaint: No Defence Hearing
records.heading: At the initial stage of a complaint the accused has no right of audience
records.text: At the initial stage the trial court makes a tentative assessment of the cursory evidence of the complainant party, and the accused has no right of audience, so the defence version cannot be discussed. Summoning an accused to answer the charge does not infringe his right but gives him an opportunity to explain his position. Ref: 2022 LHC 9616; Sajjad Ali v. ASJ etc (Crl. Revision 56556/20, decided 13.05.2022); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Sajjad Ali v. ASJ etc (Crl. Revision 56556/20, decided 13.05.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Closure of Right of Cross-Examination
records.heading: Criminal cases are decided on the totality of impressions and not on cross-examination of a single witness
records.text: Where the accused was given ample opportunities but cross-examined no prosecution witness and the trial court closed his right with cogent reasons, it was held that criminal cases are decided on the totality of impressions drawn from the circumstances, and not on the restricted basis of a witness's cross-examination or a specific fact disclosed by him. Ref: 2023 LHC 3342; Muhammad Tasleem v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 544-15, decided 01.06.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Tasleem v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 544-15, decided 01.06.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Intra-Court Appeal and Writ Against National Police Foundation
records.heading: An intra-court appeal is a statutory remedy and the National Police Foundation may be amenable to writ jurisdiction
records.text: Under Art. 175(2) jurisdiction may be conferred by the Constitution or law; an intra-court appeal is a statutory remedy and does not take away the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction, which in appropriate cases will not insist on it first being availed. The National Police Foundation is in certain cases amenable to writ jurisdiction under Art. 199. Ref: Dr. Mohammad Aslam Khaki v. Khawja Khalid Farooq Khan and others (C.P. 3203/2017, decided 19.06.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Dr. Mohammad Aslam Khaki v. Khawja Khalid Farooq Khan and others (C.P. 3203/2017, decided 19.06.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Plot Allotment: Single Plot and Parks
records.heading: More than one plot cannot be allotted to an individual and parks cannot be allotted
records.text: More than a single plot cannot be allotted to an individual. Parks and green areas cannot be converted to residential use or allotted. Ref: Dr. Mohammad Aslam Khaki v. Khawja Khalid Farooq Khan and others (C.P. 3203/2017, decided 19.06.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Dr. Mohammad Aslam Khaki v. Khawja Khalid Farooq Khan and others (C.P. 3203/2017, decided 19.06.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 340(2) CrPC: Accused Not Appearing on Oath
records.heading: An accused who pleads specifically but does not testify on oath withholds the best evidence
records.text: An accused who takes a specific plea but does not appear on oath under s. 340(2) CrPC and only produces defence witnesses withholds the best evidence, which lowers the sanctity of the defence version. Under Art. 119 QSO the burden lies on the party asserting a fact, and once the prosecution discharges its burden the accused must prove his specific plea. Ref: Nazir Ahmed v. The State (Jail Petition 169/2021, decided 01.06.2023).
records.title: Nazir Ahmed v. The State (Jail Petition 169/2021, decided 01.06.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 53-A Transfer of Property Act: Limitation
records.heading: The right of a transferee in possession under section 53-A is not extinguished by limitation
records.text: S. 53-A creates a right in the transferee in possession under part performance to retain possession, which is an existing equitable title. Limitation does not extinguish it, and does not bar a transferee in possession who sues as plaintiff to preserve that right. Ref: Rahmat Wali Khan & another v. Ghulam Muhammad & others (C.A. 226-P/2018, decided 11.04.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Rahmat Wali Khan & another v. Ghulam Muhammad & others (C.A. 226-P/2018, decided 11.04.2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Ejectment and Determination of Fair Rent
records.heading: Ejectment and determination of fair rent, with only case details given and no holding
records.text: Authority on rent matters, concerning ejectment and determination of fair rent. The post gives only the heading and case details, without the holding. Ref: Akhtar Kamran deceased through his legal heirs & others v. Pervaiz Ahmed & others (C.P. 492-K/2023, decided 26.04.2023); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Akhtar Kamran deceased through his legal heirs & others v. Pervaiz Ahmed & others (C.P. 492-K/2023, decided 26.04.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses and Primacy of Ocular Evidence
records.heading: Related witnesses with natural presence can sustain conviction and ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence
records.text: Related witnesses whose presence is natural and whose evidence is straightforward and confidence inspiring can sustain a conviction, and substitution is rare. Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence, which with recovery is only corroborative. Ref: Abdul Wahid v. The State (Crl. A. 446/2020, decided 06.06.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Abdul Wahid v. The State (Crl. A. 446/2020, decided 06.06.2023)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Age Determination: Ossification Test
records.heading: Where age documents conflict, the ossification test is the best way to determine age
records.text: Date of birth is ordinarily proved by documents, but where the birth certificate and NADRA record conflict, the ossification test is the best way to determine age. The trial court rightly constituted a medical board, and under s. 510 CrPC an expert report may be used in evidence without calling the expert. Ref: Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Crl. P. 1617/2022, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Crl. P. 1617/2022, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 10(5) Family Courts Act: Khula and Surrender of Dower
records.heading: On khula the wife may be directed to surrender part of her dower under section 10(5)
records.text: Under s. 10(5) of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964, on khula the Family Court may direct the wife to surrender up to fifty percent of deferred dower or twenty-five percent of admitted prompt dower. A house in the Nikahnama being deferred dower, the wife was bound to surrender fifty percent of it. Ref: Syed Amir Raza v. Mst. Rohi Mumtaz and others (C.P. 2865/2022, decided 05.05.2023); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Syed Amir Raza v. Mst. Rohi Mumtaz and others (C.P. 2865/2022, decided 05.05.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Cross-Examination in Departmental Enquiry
records.heading: The right of cross-examination in a departmental enquiry is a vested right
records.text: The right of cross-examination is a vested right of the accused in a departmental enquiry. Mere acceptance of dues is no ground to nonsuit the petitioner. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1135.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Pakistan Bar Council: De-Seating and Settlement with SCBA
records.heading: Dispute over de-seating by the Pakistan Bar Council and settlement with the SCBA, no outcome stated
records.text: Authority on a dispute where petitioners contended that show cause notices and de-seating orders were issued without due process, in violation of rr. 118 and 125 of the Pakistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Council Rules, 1976. The terms of settlement agreed by PBC and SCBA representatives in court are also noted. The post gives no outcome. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1123.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 149 Limitation Act: Government Controlled Statutory Body
records.heading: A Government controlled statutory body is not an alter ego of Government for Article 149
records.text: A Government controlled statutory body such as the Higher Education Commission is not an alter ego of the Government, so it is not governed by Art. 149 of the Limitation Act, 1908. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1077.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Rule of Consistency (Parity) in Bail
records.heading: The rule of consistency treats like cases alike but requires comparable roles
records.text: The rule of consistency requires that like cases be treated alike, so a benefit extended to one accused applies to a co-accused whose case is analogous. It requires comparability of roles or overt acts, and where roles differ due allowance cannot be extended. Courts must consider tangible evidence against the accused when assessing reasonable grounds. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1068, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 11; Bakhti Rahman v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl. P. 207/2023).
records.title: Bakhti Rahman v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl. P. 207/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Shajjah Injuries and Prohibitory Clause: Ss. 337-A(ii) and (iii) PPC
records.heading: Shajjah-i-hashimah under section 337-A(iii) falls within the prohibitory clause of section 497
records.text: S. 337 PPC describes six kinds of shajjah. Shajjah-i-mudihah under s. 337-A(ii) carries arsh and up to five years ta'zir, and shajjah-i-hashimah under s. 337-A(iii) carries arsh and up to ten years ta'zir, which falls within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1068; Bakhti Rahman v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl. P. 207/2023).
records.title: Bakhti Rahman v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl. P. 207/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Stage: Tentative Assessment and Reasonable Grounds
records.heading: At the bail stage the court makes a tentative assessment looking for tangible evidence
records.text: At the bail stage the court tentatively assesses the material without deeper appreciation, looking for tangible evidence connecting the accused. Under s. 497(2) CrPC the court must be satisfied there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty. The mere possibility of further inquiry exists in almost every case, and overwhelming evidence connecting the accused defeats bail. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1068; Bakhti Rahman v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl. P. 207/2023).
records.title: Bakhti Rahman v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl. P. 207/2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal: No Direction to Decide Representation
records.heading: A Service Tribunal cannot direct the department to decide a representation pending before the appeal
records.text: A Service Tribunal hearing a service appeal cannot direct the departmental authority to decide a civil servant's representation that remained undecided for 90 days before the appeal was filed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1087.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Polygamy: S. 6 Muslim Family Laws Ordinance
records.heading: A second marriage without written permission of the Arbitration Council attracts dower liability and a criminal complaint
records.text: Under s. 6(1) of the Ordinance no man may contract another marriage during an existing one without prior written permission of the Arbitration Council. S. 6(5) makes him liable to pay all dower due immediately and creates a complaint-based offence punishable with up to one year's simple imprisonment and fine. S. 20 of the Family Courts Act deems the Family Court a magistrate of first class for such offences. Ref: Muhammad Nazeer v. ADJ, Sialkot etc. (Writ Petition 30090, decided 20.06.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Nazeer v. ADJ, Sialkot etc. (Writ Petition 30090, decided 20.06.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC: Recording by Magistrate Without Jurisdiction
records.heading: Any Magistrate under section 164 CrPC includes one without jurisdiction in the case
records.text: The expression any Magistrate in s. 164 CrPC includes Judicial and Special Judicial Magistrates under s. 4(ma), even if they lack jurisdiction in the case, and they may record statements or confessions during investigation or before inquiry or trial begins. Writ petition allowed, and the petitioner may approach the Magistrate at Lahore to have her statement recorded. Ref: PLD 2022 Lah 545; Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mst. Hira Bibi v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 1556 of 2022, decided 24.01.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Civil Imprisonment for Non-Payment of Maintenance Decree
records.heading: Civil imprisonment for maintenance default is governed by the CPC unless the Family Court orders otherwise
records.text: The special procedure in s. 13(3) of the Family Courts Act, 1964, applies only if the Family Court specifically orders it. Absent such an order, execution follows the CPC, so the term of civil imprisonment is governed by s. 55 read with O. XXI CPC and not by s. 82 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act. Ref: PLD 2021 Lah 624; Adnan v. Superintendent Jail, Gujrat and 3 others (Writ Petition 22688/2021); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Adnan v. Superintendent Jail, Gujrat and 3 others (Writ Petition 22688/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Withdrawal Slip Not Negotiable Instrument
records.heading: A withdrawal slip is not a negotiable instrument and legal representatives who did not sign it cannot be sued
records.text: A withdrawal slip attributed to a deceased person was not a negotiable instrument, and his legal representatives who did not sign it could not be sued under O. XXXVII R. 2 CPC. The appeal was allowed and the parties directed to appear before the District Judge, Muzaffargarh. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 485; Ghulam Mustafa v. Muhammad Musharaf Hussain (R.F.A. 104/2015, decided 28.09.2022); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. Muhammad Musharaf Hussain (R.F.A. 104/2015, decided 28.09.2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Not Conditional on Rukhsati
records.heading: A wife's claim to maintenance is not conditional on rukhsati
records.text: A wife's claim to maintenance is not conditional on rukhsati or consummation. Where the nikah was solemnised and the husband neither asked for rukhsati nor performed marital obligations though the wife was willing, she became entitled to maintenance. The constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 496; Ahsan Nawaz v. Judge Family Court etc (W.P. 355/2023); Justice Faisal Zaman Khan.
records.title: Ahsan Nawaz v. Judge Family Court etc (W.P. 355/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: S. 324 PPC Applicability for Trial
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed as section 324 PPC applicability is for the trial after a single shot
records.text: The petitioner fired one shot hitting the complainant's leg, the injury being under s. 337-F(iii) PPC, and did not cause further injury though the complainant was at his mercy. Applicability of s. 324 PPC was for the trial to decide, investigation was complete and post-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 539; Tasawar Abbas v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 4254-B/2022, decided 22.09.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Tasawar Abbas v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 4254-B/2022, decided 22.09.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Conditional Pre-Arrest Bail on Default
records.heading: Conditional pre-arrest bail is cancelled where the accused defaults on the compromise undertaking
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was granted on a compromise in a s. 489-F PPC case, the accused paying part and undertaking to pay Rs. 1,400,000 within six months but defaulting. As the bail was conditional on due performance of his obligations, it was recalled and cancelled. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 543, 2024 PCrLJ 1364; Azeem-ud-Din v. Feroze Khan etc (Crl. Misc. 60014/CB/2022, decided 20.01.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Azeem-ud-Din v. Feroze Khan etc (Crl. Misc. 60014/CB/2022, decided 20.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained FIR Delay and Chain of Custody: Acquittal
records.heading: Unexplained FIR delay and broken chain of custody of crime empties led to acquittal
records.text: Unexplained delay of about two and a half hours in reporting, material contradictions and omissions suggested the prosecution withheld the true genesis. The PFSA report could not corroborate the case without producing the team members who collected the crime empties to prove the chain of custody. Appeal accepted and the death sentence not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 559; Arshad Ali and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 47011-J & M.R. 159/2019); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Arshad Ali and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 47011-J & M.R. 159/2019)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: Joint Trial of S. 11 PECA and Ss. 295-A, 295-B, 295-C, 298-C PPC
records.heading: Offences under PECA and sections 295 to 298-C PPC from the same transaction can be tried together
records.text: Offences under s. 11 PECA and ss. 295-A, 295-B, 295-C and 298-C PPC arising from the same transaction can be tried together under ss. 4(c) and 235 CrPC. Their ingredients are interlinked and not inconsistent, and separate trials risk conflicting decisions. The revision was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 575, 2024 PCrLJ 1098; Sheraz Ahmad etc v. State etc (Crl. Rev. 69407/2022, decided 09.12.2022); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Sheraz Ahmad etc v. State etc (Crl. Rev. 69407/2022, decided 09.12.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 139 QSO: Best Evidence Rule
records.heading: Documentary evidence is the best evidence and Article 139 requires disclosure of recorded facts
records.text: Under Art. 139 QSO a witness must disclose whether the fact deposed to is recorded in a document, and the court may require its production. Documentary evidence is the best evidence and the best evidence rule excludes oral assertions. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 581; Maqbool Ahmed v. State etc (Crl. A. 32/2019); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Maqbool Ahmed v. State etc (Crl. A. 32/2019)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Three Essential Elements
records.heading: Section 489-F requires a dishonestly issued cheque for repayment of a loan or obligation
records.text: Not every dishonoured cheque constitutes an offence. S. 489-F PPC requires that the cheque be issued dishonestly, for repayment of a loan or to fulfil an obligation, and the obligation must be closely related to a loan. The appeal was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 581; Maqbool Ahmed v. State etc (Crl. A. 32/2019); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Maqbool Ahmed v. State etc (Crl. A. 32/2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 249-A CrPC: Acquittal Where Only CD Evidence
records.heading: Acquittal under section 249-A where the prosecution relied solely on an unverified CD
records.text: The prosecution relied solely on a CD of call data. No mobile phone or SIM was taken into possession and no forensic report on the CD's genuineness existed. An s. 249-A application may be filed at any stage, and it was allowed, the trial proceedings quashed and the accused acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 593; Rana Muhammad Yousaf Khan Advocate v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 61551-M/2022); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Rana Muhammad Yousaf Khan Advocate v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 61551-M/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 377 PPC: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: A single loophole in the prosecution case gives the accused the benefit of doubt
records.text: Where two views are possible, the one favourable to the accused is adopted, and a single loophole such as conflict between ocular and medical evidence or doubtful presence of eye-witnesses benefits the accused. Conviction must rest on unimpeachable, reliable evidence. The petition was converted into appeal and allowed, and the petitioner acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 149; Saghir Ahmed v. State and others (J.P. 300/2022, decided 28.11.2022); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Saghir Ahmed v. State and others (J.P. 300/2022, decided 28.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Rule of Consistency and Delay
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed on delay and the rule of consistency, since post-arrest bail would follow
records.text: The FIR was delayed by 16 days, only a general role was ascribed, two co-accused were declared innocent and a similarly placed co-accused had post-arrest bail. Refusing pre-arrest bail on a technical ground would be futile since post-arrest bail would follow on consistency. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC and ad interim bail was confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 154; Muhammad Imran v. State etc (Crl. P. 1212-L/2022, decided 01.03.2023); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. State etc (Crl. P. 1212-L/2022, decided 01.03.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reliable Ocular Account Corroborated by Medical Evidence
records.heading: A reliable ocular account corroborated by medical evidence sustains conviction even if one witness is discarded
records.text: In a s. 302(b) PPC case, the ocular account was reliable and confidence inspiring and the medical evidence corroborated it. Even if one eye-witness is discarded, the complainant's evidence alone sufficed to sustain conviction. The appeal was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 157; Sajid Mehmood v. State (Crl. A. 398/2020); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Sajid Mehmood v. State (Crl. A. 398/2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Pre-Arrest Bail: Dishonesty in S. 489-F PPC
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail in a section 489-F case is cancelled only if dishonesty is presently indicated
records.text: Dishonesty is an ingredient of s. 489-F PPC, and commercial integrity is an ethical standard needing evidence, assessable at trial. Cancellation of pre-arrest bail requires that dishonesty be presently indicated by the accused's conduct. No such ground was shown and leave to appeal was declined. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 166; Ahmed Shakeel Bhatti and others v. State and others (Crl. P. 1197-L and 1263-L and C.P. 1596-L of 2021, decided 16.03.2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Ahmed Shakeel Bhatti and others v. State and others (Crl. P. 1197-L and 1263-L and C.P. 1596-L of 2021, decided 16.03.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Rule of Consistency
records.heading: Post-arrest bail granted on the rule of consistency where co-accused with similar roles were on bail
records.text: In a case under ss. 365 and 337-L(2) PPC with no specific role assigned to the petitioner, two co-accused in similar general roles were already on bail. The benefit extended to one accused should extend to the co-accused, the case was one of further inquiry, and the petition was converted into appeal and bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 171; Muhammad Nadim v. State and another (Crl. P. 1072-L/2022, decided 08.11.2022); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Nadim v. State and another (Crl. P. 1072-L/2022, decided 08.11.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Case Property Not Produced: Safe Custody, Police Rules
records.heading: Failure to produce case property and prove safe custody led to acquittal under the CNSA
records.text: Under s. 9(c) CNSA, the Police Rules, 1934 (rr. 22.16, 22.18 and others) govern sealing, custody and production of case property. Where the case property was not produced and safe custody and transmission were not established, the appeal was allowed and the appellants acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 176; Ahmed Ali and another v. State (Crl. A. 48/2021); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Ahmed Ali and another v. State (Crl. A. 48/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Superdari of Vehicle: Open Transfer Deed and MRA Jurisdiction
records.heading: The Motor Registering Authority cannot decide ownership disputes and an open transfer deed is not valid title
records.text: The Motor Registering Authority has no power to decide an application challenging ownership or to suspend or cancel registration over a dispute. An open transfer deed is not a valid title document, and a transferee who does not apply to the MRA for change of ownership within 30 days makes the transfer null and void under s. 32 of the Ordinance. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 601; Muhammad Akram v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 51580/M/2022, decided 27.02.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 51580/M/2022, decided 27.02.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Handwriting Expert's Opinion: Weak Evidence
records.heading: A handwriting expert's opinion is relevant but weak evidence and not conclusive proof
records.text: A handwriting expert's opinion is relevant but is a weak type of evidence and should not be treated as conclusive proof of a fact. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 601; Muhammad Akram v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 51580/M/2022, decided 27.02.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 51580/M/2022, decided 27.02.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partition and Declaration: Ordinary Course of Human Conduct
records.heading: Fair trial requires applying the law to a transaction in light of ordinary human conduct
records.text: In proceedings under s. 4 of the Punjab Partition of Immovable Property Act, 2012 and s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, it was held that fair trial requires the law to be applied to a transaction in light of the ordinary course of human conduct. The appellants' claim was unsupported by their evidence. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 319; Muhammad Yousaf and others v. Muhammad Ishaq Rana (deceased) through LRs and others (C.A. 801/2021, decided 14.12.2022); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf and others v. Muhammad Ishaq Rana (deceased) through LRs and others (C.A. 801/2021, decided 14.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Delayed Supplementary Statement
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where the petitioner was nominated only in a belated supplementary statement
records.text: The petitioner was nominated in a robbery case only through a third supplementary statement recorded after three months and twenty days, without disclosing the source. Mala fide can be inferred from the facts and circumstances, and the credibility of the statement is for the trial court. Pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 155; Muhammad Rafique v. State (Crl. Misc. 8731-B/2022, decided 16.01.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. State (Crl. Misc. 8731-B/2022, decided 16.01.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Judge Cannot Decide Paternity in Bail Matter
records.heading: A Sessions Judge hearing a bail application cannot determine paternity of a child
records.text: While hearing a pre-arrest bail application, the Additional Sessions Judge had no authority to determine the paternity of a child, a matter for the civil court. The order was beyond jurisdiction and was set aside, and the bail application was to be decided on merits. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 158; Muhammad Yaqoob v. State etc (Crl. Rev. 36/2023, decided 08.02.2023); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Muhammad Yaqoob v. State etc (Crl. Rev. 36/2023, decided 08.02.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: No Seminal Material, Mala Fide
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where medical examination showed no seminal material and false involvement was possible
records.text: In a case under s. 377-B PPC, the medical examination after 14 hours showed nothing indicating the offence and no seminal material was found, so no DNA examination was done. False involvement by the complainant could not be ruled out, and interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 162; Muhammad Younas v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 8151-B/2022, decided 06.12.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Younas v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 8151-B/2022, decided 06.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Delay and Extra Judicial Confession
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where theft was reported after delay and the extra judicial confession lacked detail
records.text: In a theft case under s. 380 PPC reported after a month's delay, the alleged joint extra judicial confession gave no detail of time or place. Sending the petitioners behind bars would serve no useful purpose, and ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 164; Peer Bakhsh and 2 others v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 5155-B/2022, decided 12.09.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Peer Bakhsh and 2 others v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 5155-B/2022, decided 12.09.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Recovery of Bhang
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed for a small quantity of bhang because the sentence must match the quantity
records.text: Under s. 9(1)-1(c) CNSA as amended in 2022, the sentence must be commensurate with the quantity recovered. With a small quantity of bhang, no similar previous case against the accused and more than one and a half months in custody, the maximum punishment was unlikely. Post-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 183; Muhammad Adnan v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 7786-B/2022, decided 23.11.2022); Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Adnan v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 7786-B/2022, decided 23.11.2022)

records.subject: Bail
