records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Distilled Liquor under Prohibition Order 1979
records.heading: An offence of distilled liquor under Article 4 of the 1979 Order is bailable
records.text: Where 101 litres of distilled liquor with distilling articles were recovered and nothing showed sale, the offence under Art. 4 of the Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979 is bailable and Art. 3 does not fall within the prohibitory clause. Post-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 182; Muhammad Sabir v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 8733-B/2022, decided 05.01.2023); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Muhammad Sabir v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 8733-B/2022, decided 05.01.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Unbroken Chain of Safe Custody of Samples
records.heading: Gaps in the chain of custody of bhang samples defeat the prosecution case
records.text: In a prosecution under s. 9(c) CNSA for bhang recovery, failure to prove safe custody of the case property and the transmission of samples to the Forensic Science Agency, and the unexplained gaps in the chain, defeated the prosecution case. Benefit of doubt was extended, the appeal was allowed and the accused were acquitted. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1233.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Pesticide Dealer, Substandard Stock
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed for a licensed pesticide dealer where the manufacturer bore the main liability
records.text: A licensed pesticide dealer, against whom no tampering with seals was alleged, was only a dealer and the main liability lay on the manufacturer, who had not been arrayed. The offence did not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC and the case was one of mala fide. Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC was confirmed. Ref: 2018 YLR 214.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Army Joint Venture over State Land Declared Unlawful
records.heading: The Army joint venture over State land was held unconstitutional and unlawful
records.text: The joint venture between the Pakistan Army and the Caretaker Punjab Government over more than one million acres of State land for corporate farming, approved under s. 10(2) of the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act, 1912, was held unconstitutional and unlawful under Art. 245 of the Constitution and s. 230 of the Elections Act, 2017. The petitions were allowed and the impugned decisions and the JVA were set aside. Ref: 2023 LHC 3403; Public Interest Law Association of Pakistan v. Federation of Pakistan (W.P. 20906/23); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Public Interest Law Association of Pakistan v. Federation of Pakistan (W.P. 20906/23)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Limited Judicial Review of Arbitration Award
records.heading: Courts do not sit in appeal over an arbitration award and interfere only under section 30
records.text: The arbitrator is the final judge of the quality and quantity of evidence, and the court does not sit in appeal over an award or search for latent errors of law or fact. Interference is warranted only where a clear case under s. 30 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 is made out, on jurisdictional, procedural or substantive grounds. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1103.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Misconduct of Arbitrator: Meaning
records.heading: Misconduct of an arbitrator is failure of essential duty causing substantial miscarriage of justice
records.text: Misconduct of an arbitrator in the judicial sense means failure to perform his essential duty, or conduct inconsistent with his duties, resulting in substantial miscarriage of justice between the parties. It is a ground for setting aside an award. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1103.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Costs for Vexatious Litigation Against Award
records.heading: Costs of Rs. 300,000 imposed for vexatious litigation against an arbitration award
records.text: The petitioner had pursued an award through the courts for over ten years, which amounted to frivolous and vexatious litigation that clogged the courts. The Supreme Court imposed costs of Rs. 300,000 payable to the respondent within a month, recoverable as a money decree on default. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1103.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction Requires Landlord-Tenant Relationship
records.heading: Eviction requires the landlord first to establish that the person is his tenant
records.text: Under ss. 13 and 15 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009, eviction is available only where the landlord first establishes that the person sought to be evicted is his tenant, as every ground in s. 15 requires a violation by a tenant. The Rent Tribunal's jurisdiction does not extend to claims of possession through partition or disputed title, which belong to the civil courts. Ref: Abdul Rehman v. Additional District Judge and 2 Others (W.P. 25062/2020).
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. Additional District Judge and 2 Others (W.P. 25062/2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Decided on Charge Framed
records.heading: Bail is decided on the offence in the framed charge, and a bailable charge gives bail as of right
records.text: Once the Trial Court has framed a charge, the bail application must be decided on the allegations in the charge and not on other penal provisions the police or complainant consider attracted. Where the charge was framed only under s. 341 PPC, a bailable offence, bail was a matter of right and pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Bail allowed. Ref: 2001 PCrLJ 1082.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supplementary Statement Cannot Be Exhibited Independently
records.heading: A supplementary statement of the complainant cannot be exhibited independently
records.text: A supplementary statement of the complainant given to the Investigating Officer is treated as a statement under s. 161 CrPC and may be used by the defence for contradiction under s. 162 CrPC. The complainant may depose in court on its contents, but no provision permits its independent exhibition. The revision was allowed and the order of the Trial Court was set aside. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 504; Tahir Abbas v. The State and 2 others (Crl. Revision 72656/2019, decided 21.01.2020); Justice Muhammad Qasim Khan; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Tahir Abbas v. The State and 2 others (Crl. Revision 72656/2019, decided 21.01.2020)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: CEO and Board of Public Sector Company: Separate Powers
records.heading: The CEO, chairman and Board of a public sector company hold separate powers, and the CEO's removal needs a three fourth majority
records.text: The offices of CEO, chairman and Board members of a public sector company are separate and independent in appointment, removal, powers and functions under mandatory law. The CEO of SNGPL can be removed only under s. 190 of the Companies Act, 2017 by a three fourth Board majority, so the Board's decisions withdrawing his powers and appointing an Acting CEO were unlawful. Ref: 2023 LHC 3681; Syed Ali Javaid Hamdani v. Federation of Pakistan (W.P. 12660/23), decided 05.06.2023; Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Syed Ali Javaid Hamdani v. Federation of Pakistan (W.P. 12660/23), decided 05.06.2023

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Recusal of Judge: Relative Among Petitioners
records.heading: A Judge recused himself from military trial petitions because a petitioner is his relative
records.text: Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah recused himself from the bench hearing petitions against the trial of civilians by military courts, as one petitioner, a former Chief Justice, is his relative. He relied on Art. IV of the Code of Conduct of the Judges of the Supreme Court and the principle that justice must manifestly be seen to be done. Ref: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 26.06.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 26.06.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Reference Against Former Chief Justice: Petition Dismissed
records.heading: Petition seeking continuation of the Supreme Judicial Council reference was dismissed, with no reasoning given
records.text: The Supreme Court dismissed the petition seeking continuation of the Supreme Judicial Council reference against former Chief Justice Saqib Nisar. The post gives no reasoning. Ref: Afiya Shehrbano Zia and others v. The Hon'ble Supreme Judicial Council and others (Const.P. 19/2020, decided 27.06.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar.
records.title: Afiya Shehrbano Zia and others v. The Hon'ble Supreme Judicial Council and others (Const.P. 19/2020, decided 27.06.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Place of Registration and Investigation of FIR
records.heading: A case is ordinarily registered and investigated where the offence occurred, with joint investigation pending settlement
records.text: Under ss. 156(1) and 177 CrPC, a case should ordinarily be registered and investigated by the police station within whose limits the offence occurred, with exceptions in ss. 178 to 185 CrPC, of which s. 179 CrPC is relevant here. A cognizable offence may also be investigated where its consequences ensue. Pending settlement of jurisdiction, joint investigation by both police stations is indicated. Ref: 2023 LHC 3761; Sakina Bibi v. ASJ Pakpattan (Crl. Proceedings 56691/22), decided 01.06.2023; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Sakina Bibi v. ASJ Pakpattan (Crl. Proceedings 56691/22), decided 01.06.2023

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Substituted Service by Publication: O. V R. 20 CPC
records.heading: Substituted service by publication is valid only if ordinary modes were exhausted and failed
records.text: Proper service is the foundation of the court's jurisdiction. Substituted service by publication under O. V R. 20 CPC is only a rebuttable presumption of personal service and is valid only if ordinary modes were exhausted and verified to have failed. The petitioner resided abroad, was not properly served, and his application to set aside the ex parte decree was within time. Revision allowed. Ref: 2023 MLD 1167.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Property: Sale to Non-Muslim, Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Civil courts have no jurisdiction over evacuee property and a sale to a non-Muslim was complete
records.text: Land sold by a Muslim owner to a non-Muslim after receipt of full consideration is a complete sale, and after the vendee's migration to India the property became settlement pool property. The civil court has no jurisdiction over matters relating to evacuee property. Ref: 2023 MLD 1061.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Amendment of Pleadings: Real Controversy
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings is allowed at any stage to determine the real controversy
records.text: In deciding an application for amendment of pleadings, the court keeps in view the interest of justice and the determination of the real controversy. Amendment may be allowed despite delay, at any stage, even in appeal or revision, if it does not change the nature of the pleadings. A change in relief based on the same averments does not ordinarily change the character of the suit. The plaintiff's request for amendment could not have been refused. Ref: 2023 MLD 1076.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Second Revision Barred: O. VII R. 11 and s. 144 CPC
records.heading: A second revision on the same subject is barred by res judicata and Supreme Court decisions bind all organs
records.text: A decision of the Supreme Court on excess land under the Land Reforms Ordinance, 1978 binds all organs of the State under Art. 189. A second revision before the Federal Land Commission on the same subject is barred by res judicata and liable to rejection under O. VII R. 11 CPC. The court that issued a status quo order may restore possession under s. 144 CPC if it was changed in violation of that order. Ref: 2023 MLD 1023.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Joinder of Charges: s. 234 CrPC Is Discretionary
records.heading: Joinder of charges under section 234 CrPC is permissive and neither side may claim it as of right
records.text: Under s. 233 CrPC every offence requires a separate charge and trial, subject to exceptions including s. 234 CrPC. Section 234 is permissive and not mandatory, allowing joinder of up to three offences of the same kind within twelve months. Neither side can claim joinder as of right, and the accused cannot insist on it unless separate trials would prejudice him or amount to an illegality such as double jeopardy. Ref: Saira Fatima v. The State (Crl. Misc. 31686/2023, decided 30.05.2023).
records.title: Saira Fatima v. The State (Crl. Misc. 31686/2023, decided 30.05.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused of Unsound Mind: s. 466 CrPC Release
records.heading: An accused of unsound mind may be released on security under section 466 CrPC
records.text: Where an accused is found of unsound mind and incapable of making his defence, the court may under s. 466(1) CrPC release him on sufficient security for his care and appearance, whether or not the offence is bailable. Under s. 466(2) CrPC, if security is not given, he is detained in safe custody and a report is made to the Provincial Government. Ref: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Crl. Revision 33626/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Crl. Revision 33626/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail for Delay in Trial: S. 497(1) Third Proviso
records.heading: Statutory bail accrues if trial is not concluded within one year from detention
records.text: Under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, in an offence not punishable with death the trial must conclude within one year from the date of detention, failing which the accused has a statutory right to bail. The period runs from detention and not from framing of charge. The exception for a dangerous accused requires material showing a serious threat to society if released. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail for Delay: Scope of Third and Fourth Provisos
records.heading: Statutory bail accrues on expiry of the detention period, subject to delay by the accused and the fourth proviso
records.text: The third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC ensures that pre-conviction detention does not exceed two years in offences punishable with death and one year in other cases, counted from the date of detention. Statutory bail accrues on expiry of that period, subject to two exceptions, one being delay caused by the accused and the other under the fourth proviso concerning a hardened or dangerous offender. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 112.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX R. 13 CPC: Defective Service on Parda Ladies
records.heading: An ex parte decree against parda ladies not properly served may be set aside with limitation running from knowledge
records.text: Where the process server's report was not on oath and did not state that a copy of the summons was delivered, the defendants, who were parda observing ladies, were not properly served and limitation for the application to set aside the ex parte decree ran from knowledge. Revision was accepted and the case remanded to the trial court for fresh trial. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 99; Mst. Zohran Bibi and others v. Ghulam Qadir and others (C.R. 14/2016, decided 20.09.2021); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Mst. Zohran Bibi and others v. Ghulam Qadir and others (C.R. 14/2016, decided 20.09.2021)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Appointment of Divorced Daughter of Deceased Employee
records.heading: Intra Court Appeal on appointment of a divorced daughter allowed by consent and remitted for fresh decision
records.text: The appellant, a divorced daughter of a deceased government employee, had her application under s. 17-A of the Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1974 declined. With consent of counsel, the Intra Court Appeal was allowed and the matter remitted to the Deputy Commissioner, Vehari, for fresh decision. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 97; Mst. Nadia Hameed v. Government of Punjab through Deputy Commissioner Vehari and 3 others (ICA 41 in W.P. 1008/2021, decided 10.03.2021); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal; Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Mst. Nadia Hameed v. Government of Punjab through Deputy Commissioner Vehari and 3 others (ICA 41 in W.P. 1008/2021, decided 10.03.2021)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Balance Consideration: Deposits Made with DHA
records.heading: Undisputed deposits made with DHA must be credited against the balance consideration
records.text: In a suit for specific performance, the revisional court's direction to deposit the full balance consideration of Rs. 36,400,000 without crediting amounts the petitioner had deposited with DHA was set aside, as the quantum and fact of those deposits were undisputed and required before transfer. The petition was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 93; Abdul Rehman v. Syed Iqbal Hassan Kazmi and others (W.P. 9264/2023, decided 05.04.2023); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. Syed Iqbal Hassan Kazmi and others (W.P. 9264/2023, decided 05.04.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Arrears of Maintenance in Execution
records.heading: An executing court correctly awarded arrears of maintenance from the date of desertion pleaded
records.text: The executing court correctly interpreted the Family Court decree in holding the wife entitled to arrears of maintenance from 02.12.2013, as the plaint pleaded desertion by the husband. No jurisdictional defect or procedural impropriety was shown and the constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 88; Mst. Fazeelat Hassan and another v. Muhammad Shakeel Anjum and 2 others (W.P. 17385/2021, decided 07.11.2022); Justice Faisal Zaman Khan.
records.title: Mst. Fazeelat Hassan and another v. Muhammad Shakeel Anjum and 2 others (W.P. 17385/2021, decided 07.11.2022)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Rent Registrar Order Does Not Bar Eviction Petition
records.heading: An administrative order of the Rent Registrar does not bar the Tribunal from entertaining eviction
records.text: The Rent Registrar has no power to conclusively determine the status of the parties, which is a judicial function of the Rent Tribunal. An order under s. 5 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009 made in an administrative capacity does not preclude the Tribunal from entertaining an eviction petition. Ref: 2023 LHC 3780; Khurram Shahzad v. Zeeshan Nawaz (Misc. Writ 31543/21), decided 16.06.2023; Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Khurram Shahzad v. Zeeshan Nawaz (Misc. Writ 31543/21), decided 16.06.2023

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Judge Power to Transfer Cases: s. 528 CrPC
records.heading: The powers of a Sessions Judge and an Additional Sessions Judge under section 528 were held synonymous, later overruled
records.text: Concerns the Sessions Judge's power under s. 528 CrPC to transfer cases, arising from a post-arrest bail application in a murder case transferred repeatedly and adjourned at least 44 times. The bench held that the powers of a Sessions Judge and an Additional Sessions Judge are synonymous and that 'Assistant Sessions Judge' in s. 528 does not mean Additional Sessions Judge. Later overruled by a five-judge bench. Ref: PLD 2020 Lah 382.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Minor's Contract Without Court-Appointed Guardian Void
records.heading: A minor's contract to dispose of property without a court-appointed guardian is void
records.text: A minor is disqualified from contracting to dispose of his property without a guardian appointed by a court of competent jurisdiction. Any such transaction is void ab initio and has no binding force. Ref: Muhammad Nadir Khan (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Muhammad Usama and others (Civil Revision 42577/2023, decided 22.06.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Nadir Khan (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Muhammad Usama and others (Civil Revision 42577/2023, decided 22.06.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation: Not a Document of Title, Burden of Proof
records.heading: A mutation is not a document of title and the relying party must prove the original transaction
records.text: Section 42(7) of the Land Revenue Act, 1967 requires the Revenue Officer to ensure the presence of the person whose right is acquired, identified by two respectable persons. A mutation is not a document of title, and once challenged the party relying on it must prove the original transaction behind it. Ref: Muhammad Younis and others v. Mst. Dolat Bibi and others (Civil Revision 620/2014).
records.title: Muhammad Younis and others v. Mst. Dolat Bibi and others (Civil Revision 620/2014)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fraud: Art. 95 Limitation Act, Three Years from Knowledge
records.heading: Limitation for relief on the ground of fraud is three years from knowledge
records.text: Under Art. 95 of the Limitation Act, 1908, where relief is sought on the ground of fraud, the limitation period is three years, computed from the date of knowledge. Ref: Muhammad Younis and others v. Mst. Dolat Bibi and others (Civil Revision 620/2014).
records.title: Muhammad Younis and others v. Mst. Dolat Bibi and others (Civil Revision 620/2014)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Medical Bail on Suspension of Sentence: NAO Conviction
records.heading: Bail on medical grounds granted to an Accountability Court convict on suspension of sentence
records.text: A convict of the Accountability Court sentenced to seven years under ss. 9(a)(v) and 14(c) NAO was admitted to bail on suspension of sentence for six weeks on medical grounds, given consistent medical opinion on cardiac, kidney and other ailments. Conditions included a bond of Rs. 5 million, no leaving the country and voluntary surrender on expiry. Ref: 2019 SCMR 734.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Toshakhana Case: Islamabad High Court Decision
records.heading: Islamabad High Court decision in a Toshakhana criminal revision, no holding stated
records.text: Decision of the Islamabad High Court dated 04.07.2023 in a criminal revision arising from the Toshakhana case against the District Election Commissioner. The post gives no holding. Ref: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. District Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Crl. Rev. 75-2023, decided 04.07.2023).
records.title: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. District Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Crl. Rev. 75-2023, decided 04.07.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Judicial Inquiry into Custodial Death or Torture: Art. 106 Police Order
records.heading: Article 106 provides a judicial inquiry into death or serious injury in police custody
records.text: Art. 106 of the Police Order, 2002 provides for a judicial inquiry, by a judge not below District and Sessions Judge appointed on request to the Chief Justice of the High Court, into death, rape or serious injury in police custody. A police offence under Art. 155(1)(c) and (d) is cognizable but prosecution under Art. 155(2) needs sanction by written report of the authorised officer. Ref: 2023 LHC 3905; Hafeez Ullah v. Additional Sessions Judge (WP 10957/23), pronounced 05.06.2023; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Hafeez Ullah v. Additional Sessions Judge (WP 10957/23), pronounced 05.06.2023

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Supreme Court Judgments Have Retrospective Effect
records.heading: A Supreme Court judgment interpreting a provision applies from the date the provision was enacted
records.text: A Supreme Court judgment declares the correct interpretation of an existing provision and does not lay down law for the first time. The interpretation therefore applies from the date the provision was enacted and not from the date of the judgment. Ref: The State v. Shakil-ur-Rehman (CSR 2-N/2018), decided 20.06.2023.
records.title: The State v. Shakil-ur-Rehman (CSR 2-N/2018), decided 20.06.2023

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Forensic Report Without Test Protocols Is Inconclusive
records.heading: A forensic report without full test protocols is inconclusive and attracts no presumption
records.text: A forensic report that does not describe the full protocols of the tests applied, as required by Rule 6 of the Rules, is inconclusive, defective and unreliable. It does not attract the evidentiary presumption attached to a Government Analyst's report under s. 36(2) CNSA, 1997. Ref: The State v. Shakil-ur-Rehman (CSR 2-N/2018), decided 20.06.2023.
records.title: The State v. Shakil-ur-Rehman (CSR 2-N/2018), decided 20.06.2023

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: No Deemed Proof from Absence of Cross-Examination in Criminal Cases
records.heading: No fact is deemed proved from absence of cross-examination in criminal cases
records.text: The rule that a fact is deemed proved if the witness was not cross-examined on it applies to civil cases and not to criminal cases. A criminal case is decided on the totality of impressions gathered from the circumstances and not on whether a witness was cross-examined on a particular fact. Art. 133 QSO. Ref: PLD 2019 SC 64, PLJ 2019 SC CrC 1.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination: Civil and Criminal Cases Distinguished
records.heading: Deemed proof from non-cross-examination applies in civil cases and not in criminal cases
records.text: The principle that a fact is deemed proved if the witness stating it was not cross-examined applies to civil cases and not to criminal cases. A criminal case is decided on the totality of impressions from the circumstances and not on the narrow ground of cross-examination on a particular fact. Ref: 2018 SCMR 149.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Arrest from High Court Premises: Detailed Judgment
records.heading: Arrest from High Court premises: manner of arrest wrong but arrest lawful, per detailed judgment
records.text: Detailed judgment on the 9 May 2023 arrest of the petitioner by Rangers from the Islamabad High Court premises, where he had sought pre-arrest bail in the Al-Qadir Trust case. The post records that the High Court Chief Justice found the manner of arrest wrong but the arrest lawful, and that the Court observed that tolerating such arrests would turn court premises into hunting grounds for law enforcement. Ref: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. The State and others (Crl.P. 519/2023), short order 11.05.2023, detailed judgment 07.07.2023; Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. The State and others (Crl.P. 519/2023), short order 11.05.2023, detailed judgment 07.07.2023

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Exclusive Jurisdiction over Custody of Minors
records.heading: The Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction over custody and guardianship of minors despite the Mental Health Ordinance
records.text: Under the Family Courts Act, 1964 the Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction over custody and guardianship of minors (Entries 5 and 6, Part I of the Schedule). The Mental Health Ordinance, 2001 does not repeal that jurisdiction, even for a minor with mental disability, as repeal by implication is not lightly presumed and s. 60 of the Ordinance operates only in case of conflict. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 433.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Meaning of Minor, Guardian and Ward
records.heading: Section 4 defines minor, guardian and ward under the Guardians and Wards Act
records.text: Under s. 4 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, a minor is a person who has not attained majority under the Majority Act, 1875, a guardian is a person having care of the minor's person or property or both, and a ward is a minor for whom there is a guardian. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 433.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody and Guardianship Distinguished: Father's Duty to Maintain
records.heading: Custody and guardianship differ and the father must maintain the child even where the mother has custody
records.text: Custody involves the right to upbringing, while guardianship involves care of the minor even without possession of the child. The father remains natural guardian and must maintain the child even where the mother has custody. His right of custody is subordinate to the welfare of the minor, and the mother cannot be deprived of custody for lack of resources. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 433.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Constitutional Petition Against Interim Custody Order under S. 12
records.heading: A constitutional petition against an interim custody order under section 12 is maintainable
records.text: A constitutional petition against an order granting interim custody under s. 12 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 is maintainable, since no appeal lies against such an order under s. 14(3) of the Family Courts Act. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 433.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Mother's Entitlement to Custody of Minor Girls
records.heading: A mother is entitled to custody of minor girls unless disentitled by the record
records.text: The mother of minor girls is entitled to their custody unless the record contains something disentitling her. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 433.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Jurisdiction Without Mental Health Ordinance Prerequisites
records.heading: Mental Health Ordinance prerequisites do not apply to the Family Court's jurisdiction over custody
records.text: Appointment of a guardian under ss. 32 and 33 of the Mental Health Ordinance, 2001 is governed by ss. 29 to 31, requiring possession of property and written consent of the Advocate General Punjab. Those prerequisites do not apply to the Family Court's jurisdiction over custody of minors under the Family Courts Act, 1964, as no minor can be left without a guardian and custodian. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 443.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Liability of Wakeel or Surety for Dower
records.heading: A surety or wakeel who signed the Nikahnama is liable for dower
records.text: A person who stands surety or guarantor for dower may be impleaded in a suit for recovery of dower and is as liable as the bridegroom. A father who acted as wakeel of the bridegroom and signed the Nikahnama cannot escape liability absent express repudiation of that authority, as Islamic law departs from the general agency rule in marriage. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 446.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikah Through Wakeel Is Valid
records.heading: A nikah solemnised through a wakeel is valid
records.text: Nikah is a civil contract that may be solemnised through an agent or wakeel. All Islamic schools of thought recognise a nikah performed through a wakeel as valid. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 446.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Due Service and Fair Trial in Custody Proceedings
records.heading: An ex parte custody decree without proper service and hearing offends Article 10-A
records.text: A mother's application to set aside an ex parte custody decree was allowed by the High Court. The process server was not produced, service was presumed from a postal receipt without acknowledgment due, and publication was relied on without establishing that personal service failed. Without proper service and hearing, the welfare determination does not meet Art. 10-A. The father's custody application is to be decided afresh. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 412.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Welfare of Minor Paramount in Custody
records.heading: The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in custody
records.text: A decision on custody of a minor girl must, as far as practicable, be made on merit, with her welfare as the paramount consideration in law. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 412.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Intra Court Appeal Not Maintainable in Custody Matter
records.heading: An Intra Court Appeal does not lie against a Judge in Chambers' order in constitutional jurisdiction
records.text: An order on an application under s. 12 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 changing custody is appealable under s. 14(1) of the Family Courts Act, 1964. By the proviso to s. 3(2) of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972, an Intra Court Appeal does not lie against a Judge in Chambers' order in constitutional jurisdiction. The appeal was dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 453.

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Right to Maternity Leave as Fundamental Right
records.heading: Safe motherhood is a fundamental right and maternity leave cannot be denied to internees
records.text: Maternity leave is the basic element of maternity protection and safe motherhood is a fundamental right, justifiable under Arts. 3 and 11 of the Constitution. Internees of the Punjab Workers Welfare Board could not be denied maternity leave under the Internship Policy, 2014, and were entitled to paid leave without impact on their careers. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 416.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Right to Safe Motherhood: Arts. 25 and 14
records.heading: Neglect of maternity care is sex discrimination infringing Articles 25 and 14
records.text: Neglect of women's health needs such as maternity care is sex discrimination. Violation of the right to safe motherhood infringes Art. 25 of the Constitution and offends the right to dignity under Art. 14(1). Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 416.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Transgender Persons Act 2018: Declared Against Islam
records.heading: Provisions of the Transgender Persons Act 2018 declared against Islam, with gender tied to biological sex
records.text: The Federal Shariat Court held provisions of ss. 2, 3 and 7 of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2018 against the injunctions of Islam, and the corresponding Rules of 2020 ceased to have effect. Gender is tied to biological sex and not to self-perception, while transgender persons remain entitled to all fundamental rights. Ref: PLD 2023 FSC 301; Justice Syed Muhammad Anwar; Justice Khadim Hussain.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Challenge to JIT for Zaman Park Violence Dismissed
records.heading: Petitions challenging the Joint Investigation Team for Zaman Park violence were dismissed
records.text: A three-member Full Bench dismissed petitions challenging the constitution of a Joint Investigation Team to probe petrol bomb attacks and violence against police at Zaman Park. The JIT was constituted in accordance with law and each petitioner may approach the trial court individually. Ref: Ch. Fawad Ahmad and others v. Government of the Punjab and others (W.P. 24153/2023), decided 10.07.2023; Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh; Justice Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ch. Fawad Ahmad and others v. Government of the Punjab and others (W.P. 24153/2023), decided 10.07.2023

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Muslim Owner's Rights Unaffected by Custom
records.heading: Custom cannot restrict a Muslim owner's use or disposal of inherited property
records.text: Property vested in a Muslim by inheritance according to the principles of Islam carries no restriction on its utilisation or disposal. Any regional usage or custom to the contrary is inconsequential and ineffective regarding that right. Ref: 2023 MLD 1061.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift: Proof and Prerequisites
records.heading: A valid oral gift requires offer, acceptance and delivery of possession, proved in detail by the donees
records.text: A valid oral gift requires explicit offer, acceptance and voluntary delivery of possession, and absence of proof of any element invalidates it. Where a daughter alleges fraud to deny her inheritance, the donees must plead and prove the gift in detail. A sanctioned mutation creates no right unless the gift itself is proved. Revision allowed and the declaratory suit decreed. Ref: 2023 CLC 1171.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: No Limitation Against Female Heir Deprived of Inheritance
records.heading: No limitation runs against a female heir deprived of her inheritance
records.text: In matters where female heirs are deprived of their share in inheritance, no limitation runs against the heir. Ref: 2023 CLC 1171.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Gift Mutation: Non-Production of Attesting Witnesses
records.heading: Failure to produce attesting witnesses of a gift mutation is fatal
records.text: Under Arts. 17 and 79 QSO the beneficiaries had to produce the attesting witnesses of the oral gift and mutation, and failure was fatal. Not producing the Patwari and Tehsildar who entered and sanctioned the mutation amounted to withholding material evidence, raising the presumption under Art. 129(g) QSO against them. Ref: 2023 CLC 1171.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documents Produced Through Statement of Counsel Invalid
records.heading: Documents tendered through the statement of counsel are an invalid mode of proof
records.text: Documents tendered through the statement of counsel are an invalid mode of proof. A party must produce documents it relies on in evidence itself, giving the other side a fair opportunity to cross-examine, and documents so produced cannot be relied on. Ref: 2023 CLC 1171.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Interpretation of Contractual Documents
records.heading: A document is read as a whole to find the parties' intention
records.text: A document is read as a whole and construed according to the language used, to find the parties' intention, without implying terms inconsistent with its express terms. Ordinary meanings are preferred to far fetched ones, though the court may resolve ambiguity by considering commercial purpose and factual background. Ref: 2023 CLC 1021.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Service of Summons: Affixation and Substituted Service
records.heading: Defective affixation and publication of summons made dismissal of the leave to defend application unsustainable
records.text: Where a defendant refuses service, the process server must record the name and address of the person who identified the house, and the court must examine the serving officer on oath where the return is not on affidavit. In an O. XXXVII suit on a cheque, defective affixation and publication made the dismissal of the leave to defend application unsustainable. Ref: 2023 MLD 1118.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Time for Leave to Appear and Defend
records.heading: Leave to appear and defend must be sought within ten days of service or knowledge
records.text: In a suit for recovery of money, the period for filing an application for leave to appear and defend is ten days from the date of service of summons or the date of knowledge. Ref: 2023 MLD 1118.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Setting Aside Ex Parte Decree: Promissory Note Suit
records.heading: Ex parte decree on a promissory note stands where nothing rebuts the plaintiff's stance
records.text: In a suit on a promissory note, the defendant admitted execution but claimed it was a surety against divorcing the plaintiff's sister, then absented himself and his right to produce evidence was closed. The court noted that nothing on record rebutted the plaintiff's stance in considering the application to set aside the ex parte decree. Ref: 2023 MLD 1182.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Sales Tax Act 1990: Strict Construction, Retroactivity, SROs
records.heading: Sales Tax Act 1990: strict construction, retroactivity and SROs, no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the Sales Tax Act, 1990 (ss. 2, 3, 4, 8 and 71), discussing strict construction of taxing statutes, the doctrine of ultra vires, retroactive application of curative and remedial legislation, and the effect of SROs. The post gives no holding. Ref: M/s. Rajby Industries and Association of Persons, Karachi v. The Federation of Pakistan through Secretary M/o Finance, Islamabad and others (C.P. 4700/2021); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: M/s. Rajby Industries and Association of Persons, Karachi v. The Federation of Pakistan through Secretary M/o Finance, Islamabad and others (C.P. 4700/2021)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Juvenile Accused in Terrorism Case: Juvenile Court Alone Competent
records.heading: A juvenile accused of terrorist offences must be tried by the Juvenile Court
records.text: A juvenile accused of terrorist offences must be tried by the Juvenile Court and not the Anti-Terrorism Court, as the Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018 takes precedence under ss. 4(4) and 23, and its safeguards are available only there. The High Court transferred the trial to the Juvenile Court, which proceeds from the stage reached. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 110.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Requires Delivery of Possession
records.heading: A gift without delivery of possession is void even if made through a registered document
records.text: Delivery of possession by the donor and taking of possession by the donee is essential to a valid gift, which takes effect from delivery. Without it the gift is void even if made through a registered document. Ref: 2023 CLC 1217.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof When Attesting Witness Not Found: Art. 80 QSO
records.heading: Where no attesting witness is found, Article 80 requires proof that the witnesses died or cannot be traced
records.text: Art. 80 QSO prescribes the procedure for proof when no attesting witness is found, and the party relying on it must prove that the witnesses have died or cannot be traced. Ref: 2023 CLC 1217.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Special Law Limitation and Office Objections
records.heading: Section 5 is unavailable under a special law unless made applicable, and uncured office objections can time bar a petition
records.text: Where the governing statute prescribes no limitation period, the Limitation Act, 1908 applies, but if it prescribes one, s. 5 is unavailable unless made applicable under s. 29(2). A petition with office objections not removed within the time allowed becomes time barred if limitation expires meanwhile, as limitation is not a mere technicality. Ref: 2023 CLC 1217.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1(3) CPC: Subsequent Suit During Pendency
records.heading: A subsequent suit filed while an earlier suit is pending and not withdrawn is maintainable
records.text: O. XXIII R. 1(3) CPC bars a fresh suit only where the plaintiff has withdrawn or abandoned an earlier suit without permission. A subsequent suit on the same subject matter filed while the earlier suit is pending, and not withdrawn, is maintainable. A suit not decided on merits does not operate as res judicata. Ref: 2023 CLC 1368.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Accepted Resignation Cannot Be Withdrawn
records.heading: A resignation accepted by the competent authority cannot be recalled
records.text: Once a resignation is accepted by the competent authority, the employee who tendered it is precluded from recalling it. Ref: 2023 LHC 4073; Ali Ashtar Naqvi v. Lahore High Court, Lahore through its Registrar and another (Service Appeal 10-18), decided 20.06.2023; Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Ali Ashtar Naqvi v. Lahore High Court, Lahore through its Registrar and another (Service Appeal 10-18), decided 20.06.2023

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Time-Barred Departmental Appeal Taints Service Appeal
records.heading: A time-barred departmental appeal makes the service appeal time-barred as well
records.text: Where the departmental appeal or representation is barred by time, the appeal before the Service Tribunal is hit by limitation even if filed within time. Ref: 2023 LHC 4073; Ali Ashtar Naqvi v. Lahore High Court, Lahore through its Registrar and another (Service Appeal 10-18), decided 20.06.2023; Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Ali Ashtar Naqvi v. Lahore High Court, Lahore through its Registrar and another (Service Appeal 10-18), decided 20.06.2023

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Listing in Fourth Schedule of ATA 1997: Criteria
records.heading: Criteria for listing a person in the Fourth Schedule of the Anti-Terrorism Act, no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the criteria and pre-requisites for listing a person in the Fourth Schedule of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997. The post gives no holding. Ref: Ghulam Abbas v. Government of Punjab etc. (Crl. Appeal 67693/22), decided 13.07.2023; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ghulam Abbas v. Government of Punjab etc. (Crl. Appeal 67693/22), decided 13.07.2023

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Extracting Data from Personal Phone Without Court Permission
records.heading: Extracting data from a personal phone without court permission is unconstitutional and illegal
records.text: Spying over or extracting data from the personal phone of an individual or suspect is unconstitutional and illegal, except with the permission of the court. Ref: Muhammad Rahmat Ullah v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 73676/22), decided 13.06.2023; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Rahmat Ullah v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 73676/22), decided 13.06.2023

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: No Arrest in Blind FIRs or Pending Inquiries
records.heading: No arrest in blind FIRs or pending inquiries before a statement of allegations and hearing
records.text: The petitioner was not to be arrested in any blind or unknown FIRs, or in pending inquiries, until completed after giving a statement of allegations and hearing under the Punjab Anti-Corruption Rules, 2014 or the FIA Act, 1974. Causing trauma through arrest after arrest to extort information or confession is an offence under s. 337K PPC. Ref: Parvez Elahi v. Care Taker Govt. of Punjab etc. (Criminal Proceedings 45360/23), pronounced 13.07.2023; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Parvez Elahi v. Care Taker Govt. of Punjab etc. (Criminal Proceedings 45360/23), pronounced 13.07.2023

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence and Extra-Judicial Confession
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain consistent only with guilt, and a confession must be voluntary
records.text: In a circumstantial case, circumstances must be fully established, form a complete chain consistent only with guilt, and exclude every other hypothesis, as suspicion cannot replace proof beyond reasonable doubt. An extra-judicial confession must be shown to be true and voluntary. Absence of a ballistic expert was a glaring defect. Benefit of doubt was given and the accused were acquitted. Ref: Pritinder Singh @ Lovely v. The State of Punjab (Crl. Appeals 1635 and 1714 of 2010, decided 05.07.2023).
records.title: Pritinder Singh @ Lovely v. The State of Punjab (Crl. Appeals 1635 and 1714 of 2010, decided 05.07.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Nature, Scope and Recovery
records.heading: The court awards the entire contractual dower and deferred dower without a fixed time falls due on death or divorce
records.text: Dower is a sum or property due to the wife from the husband in consideration of marriage, and a court should award the entire sum fixed in the contract unless legislation provides otherwise. Where deferred dower has no fixed time for payment, it falls due on death or divorce. The High Court also directed that other beneficial conditions be recorded in a separate instrument and not mixed with the dower entries of the Nikahnama (s. 5 MFLO 1961, R. 8 Muslim Family Laws Rules, 1961).

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Test Identification Parade: Dock Identification Admissible
records.heading: Failure to hold a test identification parade does not make dock identification inadmissible
records.text: Identification tests are not substantive evidence and serve only to guide the investigation. Failure to hold a test identification parade, or non-identification by a witness, does not render identification in court inadmissible or vitiate the prosecution case. The weight of such identification is for the courts of fact, which may accept it without corroboration in appropriate cases. Ref: AIR 2018 SC 3592; Raju Manjhi v. State of Bihar (Criminal Appeal No. 1333 of 2009).
records.title: Raju Manjhi v. State of Bihar (Criminal Appeal No. 1333 of 2009)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Minor's Share Sold by De Facto Guardian
records.heading: A de facto guardian cannot sell a minor's share, so specific performance fails to that extent
records.text: Where there is no evidence that the adult co-sharer was ever appointed guardian of the minor co-sharer, a de facto guardian cannot sell the minor's share. A suit for specific performance of the agreement to sell therefore cannot be decreed to the extent of the minor's share. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1032.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Curative Review Against Justice Qazi Faez Isa Withdrawn
records.heading: Curative review against a Supreme Court Judge was allowed to be withdrawn and disposed of
records.text: The Supreme Court allowed the application to withdraw the curative review filed in 2021 against Justice Qazi Faez Isa and disposed of the matter on that basis. The Registrar's office had earlier objected that the law does not provide for a curative review. The withdrawal followed Federal Cabinet and presidential approval. Ref: The President of Pakistan & others v. Justice Qazi Faez Isa (C.M.A. 2012/2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: The President of Pakistan & others v. Justice Qazi Faez Isa (C.M.A. 2012/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Recording in Nikahnama Column 13
records.heading: Agreed dower must be recorded only in column 13 of the Nikahnama and other conditions separately
records.text: Dower is an obligation on the husband and, absent legislation, the court awards the entire contractual sum. Nikah Registrars were directed to comply with Rules 7 to 13 of the Muslim Family Laws Rules, 1961 and record agreed dower only in column 13. Governments were directed to amend column 13 to specify cash, moveable and immovable property, and other conditions are to be in a separate instrument. Ref: 2023 CLC 1021; Wasif Ali etc. v. Mrs. Fakhra Jabeen etc. (W.P. 2111/2013, decided 05.10.2021).
records.title: Wasif Ali etc. v. Mrs. Fakhra Jabeen etc. (W.P. 2111/2013, decided 05.10.2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Arts. 9 and 10: Security of Person and Arrest Safeguards
records.heading: Article 9 guarantees security of person and Article 10 provides safeguards on arrest
records.text: Life and liberty are fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution. Article 9 guarantees security of person and Art. 10 provides safeguards as to arrest and detention. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1185.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording Statement under S. 161 CrPC
records.heading: Delay in recording a section 161 statement without explanation casts serious suspicion on credibility
records.text: The credibility of a witness is viewed with serious suspicion where his statement under s. 161 CrPC was recorded with delay and no plausible explanation is offered. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 108.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of Twelve Hours in Post-Mortem Examination
records.heading: A post-mortem delay of twelve hours in an unwitnessed murder was normally occasioned by incomplete police papers
records.text: A delay of about twelve hours and fifteen minutes in the post-mortem of the deceased, in an unwitnessed murder case, was held to be normally occasioned by incomplete police papers while the complainant and police were consulting and making preliminary inquiry about the culprits. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 108.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion, Warrant and Proclamation as Corroboration
records.heading: Warrant, proclamation and absconsion are only corroborative, and unproved documents are stray papers
records.text: Warrant, proclamation and absconsion serve only to corroborate the prosecution case. Where the contents of the warrant and proclamation are deficient and their execution is not proved, those documents are mere stray papers with no legal consequence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1103.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Standard of Proof: Beyond Reasonable Doubt
records.heading: Guilt must be proved beyond reasonable doubt and not by preponderance of probabilities
records.text: A strict standard of proof applies to guilt, which cannot rest on a preponderance of probabilities and must be proved beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 104.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Withholding of Star Witness: Adverse Inference
records.heading: Withholding the star witness raises an adverse inference and a single circumstance gives benefit of doubt
records.text: The injured widow, the star direct witness, was not produced, which led to an adverse inference against the prosecution. Where ocular evidence is unreliable, corroborative evidence such as recoveries cannot cure the deficiency. Benefit of doubt goes to the accused as of right and a single circumstance suffices. Convictions for qatl-i-amd were set aside. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1054.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: A chance witness is presumed absent unless justifiable reasons for presence are shown
records.text: The testimony of a chance witness is ordinarily not accepted unless justifiable reasons for his presence at the scene are shown, and the presumption is that he was absent. It may be relied upon only if convincing explanations are offered, otherwise it is suspect evidence to be accepted with caution. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 110.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Classification of Evidence
records.heading: An item of judicial evidence may attract more than one label
records.text: An item of judicial evidence may attract more than one label. The principal labels are testimony (direct evidence), hearsay (indirect evidence), documentary evidence, real evidence (including material things such as case property) and circumstantial evidence (relevant facts such as motive, preparation, opportunity and identity). Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1156; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Relevancy and Admissibility of Evidence
records.heading: Relevant evidence is usually admissible subject to exclusionary rules based on policy
records.text: Relevant evidence is usually admissible, subject to exclusionary rules of evidence which rest on policy considerations. Admissibility concerns only whether the law of evidence permits relevant evidence of a given kind to be received. Hearsay, confessions made in police custody and previous bad character of the accused are examples of relevant evidence that is excluded. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1156; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Additional Witnesses and Doubtful Admissibility
records.heading: Article 18 makes the QSO exhaustive and doubtful admissibility is resolved in favour of admission
records.text: A charge must be proved through evidence as defined in Art. 2(c) QSO, and Art. 18 makes the QSO exhaustive on what may be proved. The court should note the gist of evidence, objection and decision before admitting it. Where doubt exists on admissibility, the court should decide in favour of admissibility, the value being reviewable under Art. 162. The Trial Court was directed to continue recording the two additional prosecution witnesses. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1156; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Military Trial of Civilians: Order of 21 July 2023
records.heading: Supreme Court order on military trials of civilians, with assurances from the Attorney General
records.text: The Supreme Court issued its written order on the challenge to military trials of civilians, giving the Attorney General time to take instructions on the right of appeal and listing the matter for 1 August. The Attorney General gave assurances, including that no military trial would begin without prior notice to the Court, that evidence would be recorded as in ordinary courts and that detailed reasons would be given. Ref: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan (Const.P.24/2023, decided 21.07.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan (Const.P.24/2023, decided 21.07.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Constitutional Jurisdiction Against Appellate Decisions in Family Cases
records.heading: Scope of High Court constitutional jurisdiction against appellate decisions in family cases, no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the scope of the constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court when hearing petitions against appellate decisions, particularly in family cases. Ref: M. Hamad Hassan v. Mst. Isma Bukhari and others (C.P.1418/2023, decided 17.07.2023); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: M. Hamad Hassan v. Mst. Isma Bukhari and others (C.P.1418/2023, decided 17.07.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved: Caution in Ocular Evidence
records.heading: If motive is not proved, ocular evidence must be evaluated with great caution
records.text: If motive is not proved, the ocular evidence must be evaluated with great caution. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1054.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy last seen evidence corroborated by CCTV proves the case but unproved motive reduces the death penalty
records.text: Last seen evidence from an independent named witness, who was not a chance witness and was not dented in cross-examination, was held trustworthy and was corroborated by CCTV footage. The prosecution proved its case, but as motive was not proved the death penalty was reduced to imprisonment for life. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1071.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage on USB: Safe Custody and Reliance
records.heading: CCTV footage on a USB with established safe custody is reliable even through a related witness
records.text: Where the USB holding CCTV footage was not seriously disputed or alleged to be tampered with and its safe custody was established, the safeguards could be relaxed on the facts. The evidence of the witness who viewed the footage was held reliable, even though he was related to the deceased, as no enmity was shown. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1071.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Production of Documents Without Board Authorisation
records.heading: The investigator needs no court or Board authorisation to collect documents under section 94 from a non-banking company
records.text: Under s. 94 CrPC the Trial Court and the investigator may collect required documents, and the investigator needs no court authorisation where the document is held by a company other than a banking company. The accused's objection that production needed Board of Directors authorisation was rightly rejected. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1110.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration Recorded by Investigating Officer
records.heading: A dying declaration may be recorded by the Investigating Officer as no specified forum is required
records.text: No specified forum is necessary before whom a dying declaration may be made. The statement of the injured recorded by the Investigating Officer with the doctor's permission was not illegal and matched the FIR. The appeal was dismissed, with the death sentence altered to imprisonment for life. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1200.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of Over 24 Hours in FIR Not Fatal
records.heading: Mere delay in lodging the FIR does not disbelieve the prosecution case if the evidence is trustworthy
records.text: Mere delay in lodging the FIR is not sufficient to disbelieve the prosecution case. It puts the court on notice to scrutinise the evidence closely, and if the evidence is trustworthy and convincing the delay may be ignored. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1200.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Falsus in Uno, Falsus in Omnibus
records.heading: Witnesses disbelieved against one set of accused cannot be accepted against others, save for abundant caution
records.text: If witnesses are disbelieved against one set of accused, their testimony cannot be accepted against other accused under the principle of falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus. Under the principle of abundant caution, however, an accused can be singled out from the others. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1200.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Melee, Blackening and Death After Hospital Treatment
records.heading: In a melee exact distance cannot be recalled and death after hospital treatment is not mitigating
records.text: In a melee witnesses cannot be expected to recall the exact distance between accused and victim, and blackening around the wounds showed no abnormality in the medical evidence. Mere chances of survival, or death in hospital after some time, do not reduce the accused's liability or amount to a mitigating circumstance. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1200.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Benami Transaction: Burden and Proof
records.heading: A person alleging a benami transaction bears a heavy burden to show the owner was a name lender
records.text: The burden lies heavily on the person claiming against the tenor of the document to show the ostensible owner was a mere name lender. It is discharged by the recognised criteria, including source of purchase money, possession, relationship of the parties, motive, custody of title deed and conduct. The evidence must be reliable and withstand strict scrutiny. Ref: 2023 SCMR 572.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Admission of Right of Pre-emption and Disagreement on Price
records.heading: Admission of the right of pre-emption cannot be retracted merely because the parties disagreed on price
records.text: The right of pre-emption and determination of the sale price are severable. Failure of vendee and pre-emptor to agree on price does not undo a compromise acknowledging the right of pre-emption, and the admission cannot be retracted. The price can be determined under s. 27 of the Act. Ref: 2023 YLR 1568.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 337-N(2) PPC: Daman and Imprisonment as Ta'zir
records.heading: Daman and imprisonment as ta'zir may be awarded together under section 337-F(vi) PPC
records.text: The non-obstante clause in s. 337-N(2) PPC does not apply to kinds of hurt for which no arsh is provided. Daman is a distinct punishment under s. 53 and s. 299(b) PPC, so imprisonment of up to seven years as ta'zir alongside daman under s. 337-F(vi) PPC was lawfully awarded by the trial court. Ref: 2023 YLR 1649; Talib Hussain and another v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 181 of 2022).
records.title: Talib Hussain and another v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 181 of 2022)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Ex Parte Award: Objections Under S. 30 Arbitration Act
records.heading: An objection under section 30 of the Arbitration Act carries no weight without substantial grounds
records.text: Merely filing an objection under s. 30 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 carries no weight unless substantial grounds for setting aside the award are alleged. The petitioner had ample opportunity to join the proceedings and showed no misconduct by the Arbitrator. Leave to appeal was refused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1361.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Non-Interference With Arbitrator's Decision
records.heading: An arbitrator's decision is not lightly interfered with until a clear case under section 30 is made out
records.text: The decision of an arbitrator should not be lightly interfered with while deciding objections, until a clear and definite case within s. 30 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 is made out. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1361.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitrator's Impartiality and Moral Misconduct
records.heading: An arbitrator must act in good faith and deliberate departure from the contract may be misconduct
records.text: An arbitrator must act in good faith, be disinterested and impartial and stand indifferent between the parties. He is sole and final judge of law and fact but cannot act arbitrarily or independently of the contract, and a deliberate departure from the contract may amount to misconduct or mala fide action vitiating the award. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1361.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Legal Misconduct by Arbitrator
records.heading: An arbitrator commits legal misconduct through procedural defects, excess of jurisdiction or an award without evidence
records.text: An arbitrator misconducts the proceedings where there is a defect in procedure, breach or neglect of duty, action contrary to equity and good conscience, absence or excess of jurisdiction, action beyond the reference, reliance on extraneous circumstances, disregard of material documents, or an award based on no evidence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1361.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Bar of Jurisdiction
records.heading: A bar on the jurisdiction of civil courts must be created by statute and not imported from foreign jurisprudence
records.text: A bar on the jurisdiction of civil courts or on maintainability of a suit under s. 9 or O. VII R. 11(d) CPC must be created expressly or impliedly by a statute enacted by the legislature. Courts in Pakistan cannot import an implied bar from another country's jurisprudence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1292.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance of Unsigned Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Whether an unsigned agreement to sell can be specifically enforced, question only, no holding stated
records.text: Authority on whether an unsigned agreement to sell immoveable property is valid and whether its specific performance can be ordered. The post gives the question only and does not state the holding. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1390.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Unsoundness of Mind: Time of Execution and Pleading
records.heading: A plea of unsoundness of mind must state the time of execution and cannot be cured by evidence
records.text: Where unsoundness of mind is pleaded, the crucial point is the time of execution of the contract. Plaintiffs had to state in the plaint when the executant's paralysis occurred, and could not cure the omission through evidence. Suits for declaration were rightly dismissed by the lower courts, and the appeals were allowed (ss. 11 and 12 Contract Act). Ref: 2023 SCMR 1339; Muhammad Munir and others v. Umar Hayat and others (Civil Appeals Nos. 1731, 1732 of 2021, decided 24.05.2023); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Muhammad Munir and others v. Umar Hayat and others (Civil Appeals Nos. 1731, 1732 of 2021, decided 24.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Time as Essence of Contract in Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Time was of the essence where the agreement provided for cancellation and forfeiture of earnest money on default
records.text: Time was of the essence where the agreement stated the date for performance and provided for cancellation and confiscation of earnest money on default. The vendee, who admittedly failed to arrange the balance and pleaded incorrectly, was not entitled to the discretionary relief of specific performance. Appeal allowed and suit dismissed (s. 55 Transfer of Property Act, s. 12 Specific Relief Act 1877). Ref: 2023 SCMR 1371.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Further Inquiry Where Two Views Possible
records.heading: Bail allowed where applicability of section 324 PPC was for the Trial Court and two views were possible
records.text: If two views are possible on the evidence, the view favourable to the accused is adopted. Where only a general role was ascribed, injuries were on non-vital parts and over 37 empties were recovered, the applicability of s. 324 PPC was for the Trial Court after evidence. Bail allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1397.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed: Delay and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where an FIR delay of three days made the case one of further inquiry
records.text: An FIR lodged after about three days with an unconvincing explanation, and injuries on non-vital parts without repeated fire, made the case one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC, with s. 324 PPC left to the Trial Court. Ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed and the co-accused was admitted to post-arrest bail. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1243.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Consistency Between Pre-Arrest and Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail should not be refused on a technical ground where post-arrest bail would follow on consistency
records.text: Where two petitioners are ascribed the same role, refusing pre-arrest bail on the ground that its considerations differ would be defeated by consistency, since the arrested petitioner would obtain post-arrest bail soon after. A person should not be sent to custody on a technical ground. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1243.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Contradictions in Prosecution Evidence
records.heading: Minor discrepancies are ignored where the evidence has a ring of truth
records.text: Courts should ignore minor discrepancies where the material aspects of the evidence have a ring of truth. The test is whether the witness inspires confidence, and only an omission or discrepancy going to the root of the matter benefits the defence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1299.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Evidence Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices for conviction
records.text: Where ocular evidence is trustworthy and confidence inspiring, it is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices to sustain a conviction. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1278.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reliance on Witnesses Related to Deceased
records.heading: Related witnesses with natural presence and confidence inspiring evidence can sustain conviction
records.text: If the presence of related witnesses at the occurrence is natural and their evidence is straightforward and confidence inspiring, it can safely be relied upon to sustain a conviction. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1278.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Surrender of Deferred Dower Under S. 10(5)
records.heading: On khula the wife may be directed to surrender up to half of deferred dower
records.text: Under s. 10(5) of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964, on dissolution by khula the Family Court may direct the wife to surrender up to fifty percent of deferred dower or up to twenty-five percent of admitted prompt dower. The house recorded as deferred dower was held to be reduced to fifty percent in her favour. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1394.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Concurrent Civil and Criminal Proceedings: Stay
records.heading: Civil and criminal proceedings may ordinarily proceed together, and stay is warranted only in limited cases
records.text: Civil and criminal proceedings on the same matter may ordinarily proceed together. A criminal trial may be postponed where criminal liability depends on or is intimately connected with the civil result, but not where the subject matters are distinct or the civil suit is mala fide. The standards of proof differ, so divergent findings are possible. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1292.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 42 Declaration: Fraud in Registered Deeds Not Proved
records.heading: A plea of fraud in registered deeds fails where the Sub-Registrar proved the executant presented them
records.text: A plea that a registered sale deed and exchange deed were obtained by fraud was not established, as the Sub-Registrar testified that the executant himself presented the documents and acknowledged receipt of consideration. Suits for declaration were rightly dismissed by the Trial Court and First Appellate Court, and the appeals were allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1339; Muhammad Munir and others v. Umar Hayat and others (Civil Appeals Nos. 1731, 1732 of 2021, decided 24.05.2023); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Muhammad Munir and others v. Umar Hayat and others (Civil Appeals Nos. 1731, 1732 of 2021, decided 24.05.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Reappraisal of Evidence in Qatl-i-Amd
records.heading: An FIR lodged within two hours from the hospital was prompt and excluded deliberation
records.text: An FIR lodged one hour and fifty-five minutes after the incident, from the hospital to which the deceased was first taken, was prompt, which excluded deliberation and consultation. The eye-witnesses explained their presence, the accused was known and medical evidence corroborated the ocular account. Appeal against conviction dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1278.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Eye-Witness Statements
records.heading: Minor discrepancies not going to the root of the prosecution story need not be given much importance
records.text: Discrepancies of a minor character that do not go to the root of the prosecution story or shake its salient features need not be given much importance. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1375.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wajtakar Witnesses, Res Gestae and Prompt FIR
records.heading: Wajtakar evidence rests on res gestae and absconsion of over five years is corroboratory
records.text: An FIR lodged about three and a half hours after the incident, with the police station 18 kilometres away, was prompt. The evidence of witnesses who heard the shot and saw the accused flee with a pistol was wajtakar evidence resting on res gestae under Art. 19 QSO. Medical evidence corroborated, and absconsion of over five years was corroboratory. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1375.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Related Witness Versus Interested Witness
records.heading: A related witness is not interested in all circumstances but becomes so where tainted with malice
records.text: A related witness is not an interested witness in all circumstances and may be a natural witness, especially where the offence occurs in the presence of family members. A related witness becomes interested when his evidence is tainted with malice, and the evidence of a near relative of the victim must be closely scrutinised. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1375.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Doctrine of Binding Precedent
records.heading: Binding precedent promotes certainty, consistency and organic development of the law
records.text: The doctrine of binding precedent promotes certainty and consistency in judicial decisions and ensures an organic and systematic development of the law. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1232.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Interim Orders Do Not Survive Final Decision
records.heading: Interim orders merge into the final order and do not survive final adjudication
records.text: No interlocutory order survives after the original proceeding ends. Interim orders are made in aid of the final order and merge into it, and do not survive final adjudication. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1247.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption: No Partial Decree
records.heading: A pre-emptor must ordinarily take the whole bargain and pay the entire price
records.text: Since the right of pre-emption is one of substitution, the pre-emptor must ordinarily take over the whole bargain and pay the entire price, and the vendor's defective title is not a limitation. Partial pre-emption on proportionate price is permitted only where the right extends to part of the property or only part is capable of pre-emption. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1305, PLJ 2024 SC 40; Muhammad Riaz v. Muhammad Ramzan, etc (C.P.446-L/2014).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Muhammad Ramzan, etc (C.P.446-L/2014)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Proof of Talb-i-Muwathibat and Talb-i-Ishhad
records.heading: A pre-emption suit fails where Talb-i-Muwathibat and Talb-i-Ishhad were not proved by the witnesses
records.text: The pre-emptor's two witnesses gave no date for Talb-i-Muwathibat or Talb-i-Ishhad and knew nothing of the notice's contents or signatories. No acknowledgement receipt was produced and the postman was not examined. The suit for possession through pre-emption was rightly dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1305, PLJ 2024 SC 40; Muhammad Riaz v. Muhammad Ramzan, etc (C.P.446-L/2014).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Muhammad Ramzan, etc (C.P.446-L/2014)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Vendee's Obligation to Prove Valid Transaction
records.heading: A vendee must establish title of the seller, offer and acceptance, consideration and delivery of possession
records.text: A vendee must establish that the transaction was with a title holder, that an offer was made and accepted, that the parties had no incapacity, that there was consensus ad idem, valid consideration and delivery of possession. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 550.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Attorney Selling to Self or Relatives
records.heading: An attorney selling to himself or relatives must first obtain the principal's informed consent
records.text: An attorney acts as agent of the principal and must take the principal into confidence before converting the principal's property into personal use or for his near relatives. If he intends to sell to himself or his next of kin, he must first obtain the principal's consent after disclosing all material circumstances. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 550.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fraud Vitiates Transaction: Limitation Does Not Run
records.heading: Fraud vitiates the transaction and limitation does not run against a void transaction
