records.text: Fraud vitiates even the most solemn transaction, which is void, and limitation does not run against a void transaction. Mere lapse of time does not extinguish a party's right, and the matter may be considered on merit notwithstanding the bar of limitation so that fraud is not perpetuated. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 550.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Delay in Identification Parade During Pre-Trial Detention
records.heading: Petition for an early identification parade after MPO detention, with no outcome stated
records.text: Petitioners initially detained under the MPO were arrested under s. 54 CrPC after revocation of the detention order. They sought a direction under Art. 199 for an early test identification parade, alleging deliberate delay by the Government. The post does not state the outcome. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 605; Muhammad Ramzan etc. v. State etc. (W.P. No. 9139 of 2023, decided 06.06.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan etc. v. State etc. (W.P. No. 9139 of 2023, decided 06.06.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Qatl Shibh-i-Amd: Ss. 315 and 316 PPC
records.heading: An injury not likely to cause death is qatl shibh-i-amd punishable under section 316
records.text: Where the injury caused by the accused is not likely to cause death in the ordinary course of nature, the case falls within qatl shibh-i-amd under s. 315 PPC and the sentence is that provided by s. 316 PPC. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 196.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witness and Inconsequential Recovery
records.heading: A chance witness unconfirmed by medical evidence and a non-functional pistol recovery do not sustain conviction
records.text: The complainant, whose ocular account was not confirmed by medical evidence and who gave no plausible reason for his presence, was a chance witness whose evidence was suspect. Recovery of a non-functional pistol, without recovered empties, gave no corroboration. The appeal against conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was allowed and the revision for enhancement dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 639; Muhammad Afzal & others v. State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 64331-J & Crl. Rev. No. 43121 of 2019, decided 06.03.2023); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Afzal & others v. State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 64331-J & Crl. Rev. No. 43121 of 2019, decided 06.03.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: S. 336 PPC Further Inquiry
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed as intention or knowledge under section 336 PPC was prima facie missing
records.text: Intention or knowledge of likely hurt is a necessary requirement of the offence under s. 336 PPC and was prima facie missing. With a month's unexplained delay in the FIR, culpability required determination by the Trial Court, making it a case of further inquiry. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 654; Muhammad Hamza v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 11382-B of 2023, decided 16.03.2023); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Hamza v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 11382-B of 2023, decided 16.03.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Second Marriage Without Permission: Sentence Reduced
records.heading: Sentence for second marriage without permission reduced to the period undergone
records.text: In a criminal revision on conviction for second marriage without written permission (s. 6(5)(b) MFLO 1961), the court considered the first wife's acquiescence in not filing a complaint promptly. The revision was dismissed and the sentence already undergone was considered sufficient. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 656; Muhammad Rafiq v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 6973 of 2023, decided 04.04.2023); Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.
records.title: Muhammad Rafiq v. State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 6973 of 2023, decided 04.04.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 173 CrPC Report: Prosecutor's Opinion in ICT
records.heading: In Islamabad the prosecutor examines the section 173 report as no equivalent of the Punjab Act exists
records.text: The criteria laid down by the Lahore High Court for examining a s. 173 CrPC report arose from interpretation of a Punjab statute. In the Islamabad Capital Territory there is no equivalent Act of 2006, and the prosecutor generally examines the s. 173 report and certifies its suitability for trial. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 685; Ammad Yousaf v. Ghulam Murtaza Chandio & another (Crl. Rev. No. 07 of 2023, decided 14.02.2023); Justice Aamer Farooq.
records.title: Ammad Yousaf v. Ghulam Murtaza Chandio & another (Crl. Rev. No. 07 of 2023, decided 14.02.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 243 CrPC Inoperative After Denial of Charge
records.heading: Section 243 CrPC is inoperative once a charge is framed and denied under section 242
records.text: Once a formal charge is framed and denied under s. 242 CrPC, the provisions of s. 243 CrPC become inoperative, and trial proceeds under s. 244 CrPC. Here the appellant had pleaded not guilty and later asked to confess before any prosecution evidence was recorded. Appeal allowed (s. 31-A Drugs Act 1976). Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 735; Muhammad Sohail Asim v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 407 of 2015); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Sohail Asim v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 407 of 2015)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: FIR Not Entered in Register: Doubt on Timing
records.heading: Failure to enter the FIR in the register casts doubt on timing and benefits the accused
records.text: Under s. 154 CrPC and R. 24.5(1) Police Rules, the substance of information must be entered in the FIR register. Entering the complaint on a computer without the register entry, and with no explanation, indicated that the document was prepared later and cast doubt on the prosecution story, the benefit going to the accused. Appeal accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 709, 2024 MLD 359; Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift: Failure to Produce Deed or Certified Copy
records.heading: A beneficiary of a denied gift must prove it, and a photocopy of the register is no proof
records.text: Neither the gift deed nor a certified copy was produced, and a photocopy of the sub-registrar's register was relied on without any official testifying to it. Since the gift was denied, the beneficiary had to establish it and failed to do so. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 452; Muhammad Rafiq v. Mst. Ghulam Zoharan Mai and another (C.A. No. 2613 of 2016, decided 17.03.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Rafiq v. Mst. Ghulam Zoharan Mai and another (C.A. No. 2613 of 2016, decided 17.03.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Rule of Consistency
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed on the rule of consistency where a co-accused had been granted bail
records.text: Where a co-accused had been granted bail and the transmission used a SIM owned by the co-accused, the petitioner became entitled to bail on the rule of consistency, the offences being outside the prohibition in s. 497 CrPC. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 203; Shahzad v. State and another (Crl. P. No. 1353 of 2022, decided 06.12.2022); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Shahzad v. State and another (Crl. P. No. 1353 of 2022, decided 06.12.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Related Witnesses in Qatl-i-Amd
records.heading: Mere relationship of witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony
records.text: An FIR lodged with promptitude, with the police station seven kilometres away, excluded deliberation and consultation. Mere relationship of witnesses with the deceased is no ground to discard their testimony, and medical evidence corroborated the ocular version. Life imprisonment upheld and appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 205; Imran Mehmood v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 82 of 2022, decided 13.02.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Imran Mehmood v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 82 of 2022, decided 13.02.2023)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Misconduct of Arbitrator and Setting Aside Award
records.heading: Misconduct of an arbitrator as a ground for setting aside an award under the Arbitration Act
records.text: Authority on arbitration under ss. 13, 30 and 35 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, noting that arbitration often resolves disputes faster than litigation, and discussing what constitutes misconduct of an arbitrator for setting aside an award. Ref: Anjum Aqeel v. Latif Mohammad Chaudhry and another (C.P.3059/2021, decided 18.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Anjum Aqeel v. Latif Mohammad Chaudhry and another (C.P.3059/2021, decided 18.05.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Accused May Seek Production Before Defence Stage
records.heading: An accused may apply before the defence stage for production of a document under section 94
records.text: The meaning and scope of s. 94 CrPC were explained. Even before the defence evidence stage, an accused may apply to the trial court to direct the prosecution or complainant to produce a document in its possession if production is necessary or desirable for the trial. Ref: The State thr. Dr. Hafsa Karam Elahi, DRAP, Islamabad v. Chaudhry Muhammad Usman (Crl.P.112/2020, decided 15.06.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: The State thr. Dr. Hafsa Karam Elahi, DRAP, Islamabad v. Chaudhry Muhammad Usman (Crl.P.112/2020, decided 15.06.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Breaking of Tooth: S. 334 and S. 337-U PPC
records.heading: Section 337-U PPC is only explanatory and itlaf of a tooth is punishable under section 334
records.text: Section 337-U PPC is not an offence in Schedule II CrPC and is only an explanatory and controlling provision. Itlaf of a tooth is punishable under s. 334 PPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 4300; Sajjad Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 25688/23, decided 27.06.2023); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Sajjad Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 25688/23, decided 27.06.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Leave Petitions in Pre-Arrest Bail Matters
records.heading: The law of limitation applies fully to leave petitions in pre-arrest bail matters
records.text: The law of limitation applies fully to petitions for leave to appeal in pre-arrest bail matters, as in other criminal petitions under Art. 185(3). Delay must be supported by an application for condonation showing sufficient cause, and the Supreme Court should be approached promptly after dismissal by the High Court. Ref: Zafar Iqbal v. The State, etc (Crl.P.497-L/2023, decided 31.07.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Zafar Iqbal v. The State, etc (Crl.P.497-L/2023, decided 31.07.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Punjab Elections on 14 May: Detailed Judgment
records.heading: Detailed Supreme Court judgment on holding Punjab elections on 14 May, holding not stated
records.text: The Supreme Court issued its detailed 25-page judgment in the case concerning holding elections in Punjab on 14 May, authored by Justice Munib Akhtar. The post does not state the holding. Ref: Mohammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Election Commission of Pakistan through Chief Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Constitution Petition No. 5 of 2023); Justice Munib Akhtar.
records.title: Mohammad Sibtain Khan and others v. Election Commission of Pakistan through Chief Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Constitution Petition No. 5 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 41 Transfer of Property Act: Ostensible Owner
records.heading: Section 41 protects a transferee who acted in good faith after dealing with an ostensible owner
records.text: Protection under s. 41 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 requires that the transferor is the ostensible owner, by the express or implied consent of the real owner, the transfer is for consideration, and the transferee acted in good faith after taking reasonable care to ascertain the transferor's power to transfer. Ref: PLD 2022 SC 699.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Board Opinion Preferred Over First Medical Officer
records.heading: A Medical Board's collective opinion is preferred over that of the single first examining doctor
records.text: Where the opinion of the doctor who first examined the injured differs from that of a subsequently constituted Medical Board of senior doctors, the Board's collective opinion is given preference over the single initial examiner. Ref: 2022 SCMR 946.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Application Before Rent Tribunal
records.heading: A person aggrieved by a fraudulent Rent Tribunal order may apply under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: Since s. 31 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 lets the Rent Tribunal exercise CPC provisions, a person aggrieved by a Tribunal order obtained by fraud may apply under s. 12(2) CPC, and the ouster in ss. 26 and 34 of the Act does not apply. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 507.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Criminal History: Acquitted Cases Not to Be Listed
records.heading: Acquitted cases must not be listed in the criminal history of a petitioner
records.text: Listing cases ending in acquittal in the criminal history of a petitioner is violative of his fundamental rights. The criminal history submitted to the High Court in bail, harassment and habeas corpus petitions must reflect only convictions, suspended sentences and pending FIRs, with true and updated status. Related directions to police were issued (ss. 491 and 497 CrPC, Art. 199). Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 512.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Necessary Party and Proper Party Distinction
records.heading: A necessary party is needed for a binding decree while a proper party is needed to adjudicate all issues
records.text: A necessary party is one without whom no final and binding decree can be passed, whereas a proper party is one whose presence is needed to adjudicate all issues. Non-impleadment of a necessary party makes the suit bad, but non-impleadment of a proper party does not. A co-sharer whose rights would not be prejudiced by a decree of specific performance was held neither a necessary nor a proper party, and the impleadment application was dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 503.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Vendee from Co-sharer: Rights and Possession
records.heading: A vendee from a co-sharer steps into the vendor's shoes and keeps possession until partition
records.text: A vendee from a co-sharer of undivided joint property steps into the shoes of the vendor to the extent of the area purchased, provided it does not exceed the vendor's share. Alienation of a specific portion only entitles the vendee to retain ostensible possession until actual partition by metes and bounds takes place among the co-sharers. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 503.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Bald Denial of Agreement to Sell; Resiling from Pleadings
records.heading: A bald denial of a document is insufficient and resiling from pleadings is impermissible
records.text: A simple denial of a document as fake is legally insufficient unless the facts are proved on record. The defendants first evasively denied the agreement to sell and receipt, then admitted the signatures and thumb impression with an unproved explanation, a deviation from pleadings the appellate court overlooked. Appellate judgment set aside, trial court judgment restored and suit decreed. Ref: 2023 MLD 1372.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Judicial Council: Judge Retired or Resigned
records.heading: Article 209 does not apply to a person who has retired or resigned as a Judge
records.text: Art. 209 of the Constitution does not apply to a person who has retired or resigned from the office of a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court. The only action open to the Council and the President is removal from office, so the Article applies only to a Judge still in office at the relevant time. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 510.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Conflicting Medical Board Age Reports: Benefit to Accused
records.heading: Where medical board age opinions conflict, the view favourable to the accused is adopted
records.text: Where a medical board gave conflicting age opinions (18 to 20 years from one department and 16 to 18 years from another), the view favourable to the accused is to be adopted if two views are possible. The Trial Court rightly declared the accused a juvenile at the time of the offence. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 536.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Ossification Test in Determining Age
records.heading: Where age documents vary, the ossification test is the best way to determine age
records.text: Age is ordinarily proved by documents such as a birth certificate, educational records and the National Identity Card. Where the date of birth is disputed and varies across these, the ossification test, based on the degree of fusion of bones seen on X-ray, is the best way to determine age, though results vary with individual factors such as climate, diet and heredity. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 536.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Unregistered Sale Deed Preferred over Registered Deed
records.heading: An unregistered sale deed with delivery of possession may be preferred over a registered deed
records.text: An unregistered sale deed can be preferred over a registered one where possession was delivered under it. The first proviso to s. 50 of the Registration Act, 1908 allows protection of such rights under s. 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and a vested right so created cannot be defeated on technicalities. Decree for declaration and permanent injunction upheld. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 506.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Signature Comparison by PFSA: Not Lacuna Filling
records.heading: Signature comparison by the Forensic Science Agency was necessary for a just decision and is not lacuna filling
records.text: In a complaint before the Special Court (Offences in Respect of Banks) alleging forged signatures on cheques, the complainant's application to send the bank record to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency for comparison with specimen signature card signatures was necessary for a just decision. Ss. 94 and 540 CrPC and Art. 161 QSO were relied on. Revision allowed and Trial Court directed to send the record to PFSA. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 528; Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court (Criminal Revision No. 23556 of 2022).
records.title: Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court (Criminal Revision No. 23556 of 2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ of Certiorari: Object, Scope and Grounds
records.heading: Certiorari corrects errors of jurisdiction in a supervisory capacity and cannot substitute for appeal
records.text: Under Art. 199(1)(a)(ii), certiorari corrects errors of jurisdiction and annuls acts of inferior bodies without lawful authority, in a supervisory and not appellate capacity. It lies for want or excess of jurisdiction, failure to exercise it, breach of natural justice, or error apparent on the face of the record. It cannot substitute for appeal or revision. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 536.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Evacuee Trust Property: Cancellation of Lease for Public Purpose
records.heading: The Federal Government may eject a lessee from evacuee trust property required for a public purpose
records.text: Under s. 25 of the Evacuee Trust Properties (Management and Disposal) Act, 1975, the Federal Government may eject any person from evacuee trust property required for a public purpose, and suitability is for the executive. A lessee has no vested right enforceable in constitutional jurisdiction, and a plea of malice in fact is a factual question. Cancellation of lease was not without lawful authority and the petition failed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 536.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mandatory or Directory Provision: Penal Consequences
records.heading: A provision is mandatory only where non-compliance carries penal consequences
records.text: A provision of law can be termed mandatory only where non-compliance carries penal consequences. In the absence of penal consequences, the provision can generally be treated as directory. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 536.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Tribunal Interference with Departmental Penalty
records.heading: A Tribunal should not interfere with a departmental penalty unless it is unreasonable or disproportionate
records.text: Imposition of penalty lies within the domain of the Inquiry or Authorised Officer, and a Tribunal needs strong justifiable reasons to lessen it. A Court or Tribunal should not substitute its view unless the punishment rests on unreasonable or extraneous considerations, is against law, or alarmingly disproportionate to the charges. The appellant, facing serious charges proved in a regular inquiry, deserved no leniency. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 921.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. I R. 10 CPC: Addition of Party Without Hearing
records.heading: An application to add a party under Order I Rule 10 should be decided after hearing him
records.text: Under O. I R. 10(2) CPC, the test is whether the person's presence is necessary to enable the Court to adjudicate all questions effectively and completely. An application seeking to add a purchaser of the suit property should have been decided after hearing him, as he had filed a detailed counter affidavit. The order was set aside and the matter remanded for fresh decision. Ref: PLD 2023 Sindh 293.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Declaring Witness Hostile
records.heading: A witness cannot be declared hostile once cross-examination by the defence has commenced
records.text: Art. 150 QSO gives the Trial Court discretion to permit the calling party to put cross-examination questions to its own witness. Once cross-examination by the defence has commenced, the witness no longer remains the witness of the prosecution or complainant, so a request to declare him hostile cannot then be entertained. The Trial Court rightly dismissed the application. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 130.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of Multiple FIRs for Same Incident
records.heading: Multiple FIRs on one occurrence burden the accused who cannot defend in several courts
records.text: On a petition under the High Court's inherent jurisdiction, the Court considered multiple FIRs on similar allegations arising from one occurrence, with one case already pending in another province. It observed that it was neither possible nor convenient for the petitioner to seek bail and defend in several courts for the same offence, and that a Magistrate must carefully examine justification before depriving a citizen of liberty. Ref: PLD 2023 Quetta 85.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Private Medical Colleges: Mid-Course Fee Enhancement Illegal
records.heading: Private medical colleges cannot raise tuition fees during a study programme
records.text: Enhancement of tuition fee and other charges by private medical colleges during a study programme was declared illegal. Colleges must charge the tuition fee stated at admission for session 2022 and later, and PMDC must ensure compliance and report within 45 days to the Deputy Registrar. Ref: 2023 LHC 4329; Judicial Activism Panel through Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Federation of Pakistan etc (26651/23, decided 08.06.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Judicial Activism Panel through Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Federation of Pakistan etc (26651/23, decided 08.06.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Urdu Translation of Judgments Directed
records.heading: The Lahore High Court Registrar was directed to prepare proposals for Urdu translation of judgments
records.text: The Registrar of the Lahore High Court was directed to prepare a summary with proposals to create or enhance capacity to translate judgments into Urdu and publish them, with the author Judge's permission, so that common citizens can understand decisions on their rights. The Urdu post adds that the language barrier obstructs the constitutional right to information. Ref: 2023 LHC 4329; Judicial Activism Panel through Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Federation of Pakistan etc (26651/23, decided 08.06.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Judicial Activism Panel through Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Federation of Pakistan etc (26651/23, decided 08.06.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Art. 25: Intelligible Differentia and Classification
records.heading: Differential treatment under Article 25 is permitted if classification rests on intelligible differentia with a rational nexus
records.text: Differential treatment of persons not similarly placed is permitted under Art. 25 of the Constitution if the classification is reasonable, based on an intelligible differentia with a rational nexus to the object sought. A fiscal statute is interpreted by textualism, according to its plain meaning and not legislative history. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 471; Service Global Footwear Limited and another v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 58683 of 2022, decided 27.06.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Service Global Footwear Limited and another v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 58683 of 2022, decided 27.06.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: S. 74 ITO 2001: Special Tax Year
records.heading: A special tax year needs written application to the Commissioner and cannot evade tax in a normal year
records.text: Both normal and special tax years are twelve months under s. 74 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001. A special tax year requires written application to the Commissioner under s. 74(3) and is subject to s. 74(5). It exists to accommodate a category of taxpayers and not to evade tax due in a normal tax year. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 471; Service Global Footwear Limited and another v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 58683 of 2022, decided 27.06.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Service Global Footwear Limited and another v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 58683 of 2022, decided 27.06.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ of Certiorari: Object and Scope
records.heading: Certiorari annuls acts without lawful authority in a supervisory and not appellate jurisdiction
records.text: Under Art. 199(1)(a)(ii) the High Court, by certiorari, corrects errors of inferior courts and tribunals and annuls acts taken without lawful authority. It acts in supervisory and not appellate jurisdiction, and may interfere in all cases of excess of jurisdiction, including by executive or administrative bodies performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Federation. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 536; Atif Riaz v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Religious Affairs, Islamabad and 6 others (Writ Petition No. 2571 of 2021, decided 11.02.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Atif Riaz v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Religious Affairs, Islamabad and 6 others (Writ Petition No. 2571 of 2021, decided 11.02.2022)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Before Rent Tribunal
records.heading: A Rent Tribunal order obtained by fraud may be challenged under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: Given s. 31 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009, the Rent Tribunal may exercise the powers of a Civil Court under the CPC when executing its orders. A person aggrieved by a Tribunal order obtained by fraud may apply under s. 12(2) CPC, and the ouster in ss. 26 and 34 does not apply. Constitutional petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 507; Ghulam Ali v. Rana Babar Khan and 3 others (Writ Petition No. 49479 of 2020); Justice Faisal Zaman Khan.
records.title: Ghulam Ali v. Rana Babar Khan and 3 others (Writ Petition No. 49479 of 2020)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Consumer Complaint: Accrual of Cause of Action
records.heading: In a consumer complaint the cause of action accrues on the company's denial of the claim
records.text: Under ss. 25 and 28 of the Punjab Consumer Protection Act 2005, where the company denied the consumer's claim after notice, the cause of action accrued on the date of that denial. A complaint filed about fourteen days later was within the time in s. 28(4). Order to replace the defective engine maintained and appeal dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 516; The Indus Motor Company Limited v. Abdul Khalid Gill and another (F.A.O. No. 03 of 2018/BWP, decided 08.02.2021); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: The Indus Motor Company Limited v. Abdul Khalid Gill and another (F.A.O. No. 03 of 2018/BWP, decided 08.02.2021)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Age Determination: Ossification Test
records.heading: Where age documents vary, the ossification test is the best way under the Juvenile Justice System Act
records.text: Under s. 8(1) of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018, age is ordinarily proved by documents such as birth certificate, educational records and NIC. Where the date of birth is disputed and varies across them, the ossification test, based on fusion of bone, is the best way to determine age. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 536; Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Criminal Petition No. 1617 of 2022, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Criminal Petition No. 1617 of 2022, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Conflicting Medical Board Reports on Age
records.heading: Conflicting medical board reports on age are resolved in favour of the accused
records.text: Where the medical board's opinions on age conflict, the view favourable to the accused is adopted, as where two views are possible on the evidence. The Trial Court rightly declared the accused a juvenile at the time of the offence. Leave to appeal refused and petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 536; Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Criminal Petition No. 1617 of 2022, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Criminal Petition No. 1617 of 2022, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Certiorari Not a Substitute for Appeal
records.heading: Certiorari cannot be used as a substitute for appeal or revision
records.text: Writ of certiorari cannot be used as a substitute for appeal or revision, as its scope is limited. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 536; Atif Riaz v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Religious Affairs, Islamabad and 6 others (Writ Petition No. 2571 of 2021, decided 11.02.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Atif Riaz v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Religious Affairs, Islamabad and 6 others (Writ Petition No. 2571 of 2021, decided 11.02.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Evacuee Trust Property: Ejectment of Lessee
records.heading: A lessee of evacuee trust property has no vested right to enforce lease terms through a constitutional petition
records.text: Under s. 25 of the Evacuee Trust Properties (Management and Disposal) Act 1975 the Federal Government decides whether property is required for public purpose, and a lessee has no vested right to enforce lease terms through a constitutional petition. Questions of fact such as malice cannot be determined under Art. 199. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 536; Atif Riaz v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Religious Affairs, Islamabad and 6 others (Writ Petition No. 2571 of 2021, decided 11.02.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Atif Riaz v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Religious Affairs, Islamabad and 6 others (Writ Petition No. 2571 of 2021, decided 11.02.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Summoning Evidence: Specimen Signature Comparison
records.heading: Evidence essential for a just decision, including signature comparison, must be brought on record
records.text: The criminal justice system is inquisitorial, and evidence essential for a just decision must be brought on record even if it favours one party, and a lacuna may be filled. Under s. 540 CrPC, s. 94 CrPC and Art. 161 QSO the Court should obtain the signature comparison. Special Court order set aside and record directed to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency. Revision allowed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 528; Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court and others (Criminal Revision No. 23556 of 2022, heard 31.01.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court and others (Criminal Revision No. 23556 of 2022, heard 31.01.2023)

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.topic: Blacklisting of Accused Abroad: Right to Return
records.heading: Blacklisting of an accused abroad and his right to return to Pakistan, judgment opening only
records.text: Page shows the start of the judgment. A criminal case was registered against the petitioner's husband under s. 22 of the Emigration Ordinance 1979, and the petition concerned his blacklisting under the Passport and Visa Manual 2006 and his right to return to Pakistan to face proceedings, with reference to Arts. 4, 9 and 15. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 522; Rukhsana Bibi v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 33181 of 2023, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Rukhsana Bibi v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 33181 of 2023, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Impleadment of Co-sharer in Suit for Specific Performance
records.heading: A co-sharer is neither a necessary nor a proper party in a suit for specific performance
records.text: In a suit for specific performance of an agreement to sell, a co-sharer in joint khewat is neither a necessary nor a proper party under O. I R. 10 CPC where a decree would not harm his ownership rights and his presence is not needed to resolve the dispute. Impleadment application dismissed and constitutional petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 503; Muhammad Yousaf v. Additional District Judge, Ferozewala and others (Writ Petition No. 30112 of 2021); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Additional District Judge, Ferozewala and others (Writ Petition No. 30112 of 2021)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Rent Tribunal: Applicability of CPC and S. 12(2)
records.heading: Sections 26 and 34 of the Rented Premises Act oust the CPC and the Tribunal executes orders as a decree
records.text: The Rent Tribunal passed an eviction order in proceedings in which the petitioner was not impleaded, and his application alleging fraud was treated as requiring a s. 12(2) CPC application. Held that ss. 26 and 34 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 oust the CPC apart from what s. 26 mentions, and under s. 31 the Tribunal executes its orders as a decree. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 507; Ghulam Ali v. Rana Babar Khan and 3 others (Writ Petition No. 49479 of 2020, heard 26.10.2022); Justice Faisal Zaman Khan.
records.title: Ghulam Ali v. Rana Babar Khan and 3 others (Writ Petition No. 49479 of 2020, heard 26.10.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 161 QSO: Court Powers to Obtain Proof
records.heading: Court powers to obtain proof and fill lacunae under Article 161 QSO, judgment opening only
records.text: Page shows the start of the judgment. Complainant alleged that signatures on cheques drawn on his late father's bank accounts were forged and sought comparison with specimen signatures by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency. The headnote concerns summoning and examining evidence and filling lacunae under Art. 161 QSO and ss. 94 and 540 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 528; Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court and others (Criminal Revision No. 23556 of 2022, heard 31.01.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zaheer Ahmed v. Judge, Special Court and others (Criminal Revision No. 23556 of 2022, heard 31.01.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Consumer Court: Expert Evidence Not Necessary
records.heading: Expert evidence is unnecessary in a consumer case where the company did not deny the malfunction
records.text: Under s. 25 of the Punjab Consumer Protection Act 2005, expert evidence is not necessary where the company did not deny malfunction of the engine. Order to replace the defective engine without charge maintained and appeal dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 516; The Indus Motor Company Limited v. Abdul Khalid Gill and another (F.A.O. No. 03 of 2018/BWP, decided 08.02.2021); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: The Indus Motor Company Limited v. Abdul Khalid Gill and another (F.A.O. No. 03 of 2018/BWP, decided 08.02.2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Consumer Damages Under S. 10 PCPA 2005
records.heading: A consumer must prove financial loss and mental agony through independent evidence to obtain damages
records.text: A consumer must prove financial loss and mental agony through independent and reliable evidence. Where the consumer suffered no damage from the vehicle beyond loss of utility, s. 10 of the Punjab Consumer Protection Act 2005 limits relief, and the award of damages was not justified. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 516; The Indus Motor Company Limited v. Abdul Khalid Gill and another (F.A.O. No. 03 of 2018/BWP, decided 08.02.2021); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: The Indus Motor Company Limited v. Abdul Khalid Gill and another (F.A.O. No. 03 of 2018/BWP, decided 08.02.2021)

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.topic: Blacklisted Accused: Return to Face Trial
records.heading: A fugitive accused keeps the right to return and surrender to face proceedings
records.text: A fugitive accused loses some rights but not the right to return and surrender before the Court to face proceedings, under Arts. 4, 9 and 15. The husband's name had wrongly been placed on the blacklist. The High Court directed removal and issue of a fifteen-day single sheet emergency passport under Cl. 33 of the Passport and Visa Manual 2006. Petition disposed of. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 522; Rukhsana Bibi v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 33181 of 2023, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Rukhsana Bibi v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 33181 of 2023, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Super Tax Rate Reduced: Discrimination
records.heading: A discriminatory super tax rate was reduced from ten percent to four percent
records.text: Petitioners challenged the super tax of 10% under s. 4C and Division IIB of Part I of the First Schedule to the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 as discriminatory. Applying textualism and the documents produced, the High Court declared the First Proviso to Division IIB discriminatory, reduced the rate from 10% to 4% and allowed the constitutional petition. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 471; Service Global Footwear Limited and another v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 58683 of 2022, decided 27.06.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Service Global Footwear Limited and another v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 58683 of 2022, decided 27.06.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Necessary Party and Proper Party Distinction
records.heading: Non-joinder of a necessary party is fatal to a suit, but not of a proper party
records.text: A suit in which a necessary party is not impleaded is bad, while a suit in which a proper party is not impleaded is not bad (O. I R. 10 CPC). Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 503; Muhammad Yousaf v. Additional District Judge, Ferozewala and others (Writ Petition No. 30112 of 2021); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Additional District Judge, Ferozewala and others (Writ Petition No. 30112 of 2021)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Vendee of Co-sharer: Rights in Joint Property
records.heading: A vendee of a co-sharer steps into the vendor's shoes until partition by metes and bounds
records.text: A vendee from a co-sharer holds the same rights as the vendor, no more or less. Where the vendor was in exclusive possession of a portion and transferred it, the vendee steps into the vendor's shoes to the extent of the vendor's share, and keeps ostensible possession until partition by metes and bounds. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 503; Muhammad Yousaf v. Additional District Judge, Ferozewala and others (Writ Petition No. 30112 of 2021); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Additional District Judge, Ferozewala and others (Writ Petition No. 30112 of 2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Consumer Warranty: Defective Engine of Vehicle
records.heading: Plea of improper maintenance failed, so replacement of the defective engine under warranty was upheld
records.text: Under s. 25 of the Punjab Consumer Protection Act 2005, the company's plea of improper maintenance and substandard lubricants failed on the documentary evidence. The Warranty Booklet imposed no burden to maintain through authorised dealers, and the engine was covered by the warranty. Replacement of the defective engine was upheld. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 516; The Indus Motor Company Limited v. Abdul Khalid Gill and another (F.A.O. No. 03 of 2018/BWP, decided 08.02.2021); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: The Indus Motor Company Limited v. Abdul Khalid Gill and another (F.A.O. No. 03 of 2018/BWP, decided 08.02.2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Criminal History Lists in Bail and Habeas Petitions
records.heading: Police commonly produce lists of registered cases to show a petitioner's criminal antecedents
records.text: Page shows the start of the headnote. Under ss. 491 and 497 CrPC and Art. 199, the High Court noted it is common police practice to produce a list of cases registered against a petitioner during bail, harassment and habeas corpus petitions, to establish his criminal antecedents. The rest of the holding is not shown. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 512; Zulfiqar Ali v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace and others (Writ Petition No. 47617 of 2022, decided 26.10.2022); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Zulfiqar Ali v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace and others (Writ Petition No. 47617 of 2022, decided 26.10.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Unregistered Sale Deed With Possession: S. 53-A TPA
records.heading: An unregistered sale deed backed by delivery of possession is protected under section 53-A TPA
records.text: An unregistered sale deed can be preferred over a later registered deed where possession was delivered under it, as the vendor admitted execution, payment and delivery. Rights are protected under s. 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 and the first proviso to s. 50 of the Registration Act 1908. Decree for declaration and injunction upheld and appeal dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 506; Rehmat Wali Khan and another v. Ghulam Muhammad and others (Civil Appeal No. 226-P of 2018, decided 11.04.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Rehmat Wali Khan and another v. Ghulam Muhammad and others (Civil Appeal No. 226-P of 2018, decided 11.04.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mandatory and Directory Provisions: Penal Consequences
records.heading: A provision is mandatory only where non-compliance carries penal consequences, otherwise it is generally directory
records.text: A provision of law can be termed mandatory only where non-compliance carries penal consequences. In the absence of penal consequences, such a provision can generally be treated as directory. The page also notes the meaning of the word 'eject', relying on law dictionaries. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 536; Atif Riaz v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Religious Affairs, Islamabad and 6 others (Writ Petition No. 2571 of 2021, decided 11.02.2022); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Atif Riaz v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Religious Affairs, Islamabad and 6 others (Writ Petition No. 2571 of 2021, decided 11.02.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance Opens on Death: Living Heirs Entitled
records.heading: Under Islamic law inheritance opens on death and heirs then living become entitled to shares
records.text: Under Islamic law the legacy of a Muslim opens the moment he dies, and all legal heirs living on the day of death become entitled to their respective shares. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 88.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Proof of Divorce Against Widow's Share
records.heading: A Talaq-Nama not independently proved cannot defeat a widow's share in succession
records.text: A widow's share in succession was resisted on the plea of a Talaq-Nama in the husband's lifetime. The scribe and Notary Public did not know the deceased, and his identity was established only through his son, a beneficiary, without independent evidence. The High Court in revision set aside the concurrent judgments, held the widow entitled to her Shari share and directed a fresh succession certificate. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 88.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Written Talaq: Effectiveness Governed by S. 7 MFLO
records.heading: Pronouncement and effectiveness of Talaq, including written Talaq, are regulated by section 7 MFLO
records.text: Pronouncement of Talaq and its effectiveness, whether by Talaq-Nama or oral Talaq reduced into writing, together with ancillary consequences, is regulated by s. 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 88.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Talaq in Death Illness: Widow's Inheritance
records.heading: A widow keeps her inheritance where the husband dies before her Iddat ends after revocable or death-bed Talaq
records.text: A revocable Talaq (Ahsan or Hasan) does not affect the widow's right to a share in the legacy if the husband dies before completion of her Iddat. The same applies to a Talaq given on the death bed where the husband dies before her Iddat ends. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 88.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Witness Dropped by Prosecution
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC lets the court summon a dropped material witness, but only for cogent reasons
records.text: Where the prosecution has dropped a material witness whose evidence may bear directly on the result, the Court has wide power under s. 540 CrPC to summon and examine him to discover the truth. The power must not be exercised at random, and a written request showing cogent reasons is required. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 28.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Inquisitorial Role; Court Witnesses
records.heading: Court witnesses under section 540 CrPC belong to neither side, as the court's role is inquisitorial
records.text: The Court's role under s. 540 CrPC is inquisitorial, aimed at discovering truth suppressed by either party and securing the ends of justice. Witnesses examined under it are Court witnesses, not witnesses for the prosecution or defence, so neither party can claim a right to them. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 28.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Power to Summon Material Witness
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC empowers the court to examine any person at any stage, even without an application
records.text: S. 540 CrPC gives the Court wide power to examine any person as a Court witness at any stage, even without a formal application from either side, and to recall and re-examine witnesses. Where the investigation is found defective, the Court cannot sit idle and must use all enabling provisions, including s. 540, to discern the truth. Ref: PLD 2013 SC 160.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused Refusing Cross-Examination: Defence Counsel at State Expense
records.heading: Accused refusing state defence counsel and cross-examination must still get a fair opportunity, so de novo trial was ordered
records.text: Where accused refused state-provided defence counsel, declined to cross-examine and stayed mute under s. 342 CrPC, their conduct was disorderly, but statements recorded without cross-examination risk substantial injustice and reasonable opportunity should be given. Judgments of the courts below were set aside and the case remitted for de novo trial. Ref: 2011 SCMR 735.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Court Witnesses Called at Instance of Accused
records.heading: Calling witnesses under section 540 CrPC at the accused's instance was not an imminent requirement of the case
records.text: In a s. 302/34 PPC trial, persons were examined as Court witnesses at the accused's instance under s. 540 CrPC although they were not abandoned prosecution witnesses. Nothing in cross-examination inferred their presence, and the Court was not constrained to summon them suo motu. Calling them was not an imminent requirement of the case and carried a risk. Ref: PLD 2003 SC 662.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Accused's Application on Date of Arrest
records.heading: Conflicting dates of arrest warranted summoning the named witnesses as Court witnesses under section 540 CrPC
records.text: The prosecution and defence gave conflicting dates of arrest, a crucial matter. Had the Trial Court accepted the accused's s. 540 CrPC application, the controversy could have been resolved. Conviction and sentence were set aside and the case remanded to summon the named witnesses as Court witnesses and decide afresh. Ref: 2001 SCMR 308.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Wheat Recovery, Nothing More to Recover
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail allowed in a foodstuff case where nothing more remained to be recovered
records.text: In a case under ss. 3 and 6 of the Punjab Foodstuff (Control) Act, 1958, pre-arrest bail was allowed because the Investigating Officer submitted that nothing more was to be recovered from the petitioner. Sending him behind bars would serve no useful purpose and harm his reputation. Observations were tentative. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 120; Muhammad Akbar v. State and another (W.P. No. 7012 of 2023, decided 29.5.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Akbar v. State and another (W.P. No. 7012 of 2023, decided 29.5.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Principle of Return (Radd) to Surviving Sister
records.heading: A sole surviving sister takes a half share and the remainder returns to her by Radd
records.text: After the death of the propositus, his only surviving sister took a half share and, under para 66 of Muhammadan Law, the remaining half returned to her by Radd. The revision was allowed, the decrees of the courts below set aside and the plaintiffs' suit dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 118; Muhammad Yasin and 2 others v. Munir Hussain and 10 others (C.R. No. 2285 of 2015); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Yasin and 2 others v. Munir Hussain and 10 others (C.R. No. 2285 of 2015)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Tender of Documents by Party, Not Counsel
records.heading: Documents on which a suit rests must be tendered by the party, not through counsel's statement
records.text: Documents on which a suit rests must be produced in evidence by the party itself, with fair opportunity to the other side to cross-examine. Production of the challenged sale deed and mutations through counsel's statement was not a valid tender in evidence. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 118; Muhammad Yasin and 2 others v. Munir Hussain and 10 others (C.R. No. 2285 of 2015); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Yasin and 2 others v. Munir Hussain and 10 others (C.R. No. 2285 of 2015)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-examination of Injured by Medical Board
records.heading: Re-examination of an injured person by a medical board cannot be ordered routinely without cogent reasons
records.text: A medico-legal certificate can be challenged and a medical board constituted, but re-examination cannot be asked for as a matter of routine or ordered without cogent reasons where no violation of medical jurisprudence is shown. The High Court may endorse the reasoning of the court below. Petition dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah Note 119; Zeeshan Ali v. State and 3 others (W.P. No. 38548 of 2023, decided 8.6.2023); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zeeshan Ali v. State and 3 others (W.P. No. 38548 of 2023, decided 8.6.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Sexual Abuse of Minor, S. 377-B PPC
records.heading: Bail allowed in a section 377-B PPC case as the sentence and the act alleged called for trial
records.text: Bail was allowed on a charge under ss. 377-B and 506(ii) PPC of sexual abuse of a minor boy. The sentence of 20 years, not less than 14, was seen as possibly disproportionate where an act less than an attempt was prima facie visible, a matter for trial. The Ministry of Law was directed to prescribe rules under s. 19 of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 228; Hamad v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 722-B of 2023, decided 31.5.2023); Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani.
records.title: Hamad v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 722-B of 2023, decided 31.5.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Pointing Out and Recovery of Body
records.heading: Pointing out the place of occurrence and the concealed body is relevant information under Article 40 QSO
records.text: Where the accused was apprehended soon after the FIR and pointed out the place of occurrence and where the body was concealed, the lead and recovery are relevant information under Art. 40 QSO, known only to the assailants, relying on 1971 SCMR 412 and PLJ 2006 SC 931. Appeal dismissed with modification of conviction and sentence, and death sentence not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 224; Ahmad Shoaib v. State etc. (Crl. A. 648 & Capital Sentence Reference No. 5-T of 2019, heard on 4.10.2021); Justice Raja Shahid Mehmood Abbasi; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Ahmad Shoaib v. State etc. (Crl. A. 648 & Capital Sentence Reference No. 5-T of 2019, heard on 4.10.2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: ATM Withdrawal, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Unexplained ATM withdrawal without the PIN made the case one of further inquiry for bail
records.text: Bail after arrest was allowed where the complainant never said she disclosed the ATM PIN to the petitioner, and how he withdrew Rs. 14,500 without it was unexplained, making the case one of further inquiry. Offences under ss. 420 and 471 PPC were also noted as bailable. Petition accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 223; Muhammad Amir Yousaf v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 2895-B of 2023, decided 9.5.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Amir Yousaf v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 2895-B of 2023, decided 9.5.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence and Wajtakkar: Weak Evidence
records.heading: Last seen evidence is weak and wajtakkar evidence needs independent corroboration
records.text: Last seen evidence is weak and wajtakkar evidence is not believable without independent corroboration. The conduct of the two witnesses was improbable, and no single piece of evidence connected the appellants to the crime. Appeal allowed, convictions and death sentences set aside, appellants acquitted and Murder Reference answered in the negative. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 220; Rizwan Akhtar alias Razi Bawa and another v. State etc. (Crl. A. 1112-J & M.R. 290 of 2015, heard on 18.5.2021); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Rizwan Akhtar alias Razi Bawa and another v. State etc. (Crl. A. 1112-J & M.R. 290 of 2015, heard on 18.5.2021)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: 320 Grams Charas, Net Weight in Doubt
records.heading: Net weight of 320 grams of charas awaits evidence, so post-arrest bail was allowed
records.text: Recovery of 320 grams of charas, contained in a plastic bag, placed the case under s. 9(1) CNSA as amended in 2022. Net weight, and so the applicable category, would be determined only after evidence. Bail after arrest allowed, with liberty to the Trial Court to cancel it for delay or misuse. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 210; Ghulam Shabbir v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 2639-B of 2023, decided 15.5.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Ghulam Shabbir v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 2639-B of 2023, decided 15.5.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Fertilizer Control Act: Conviction Set Aside in Revision
records.heading: Conviction for storing adulterated fertilizer was set aside where the prosecution failed to make out its case
records.text: Storing adulterated fertilizer is an offence under s. 18(1) of the Fertilizer Control Act, 1973, but the raid had no private witness, the petitioner was a long-standing first offender and a seller, not a manufacturer. Prosecution failed to make out a case, and conviction and sentence were set aside. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 205; Muhammad Arshad v. State and another (Crl. Rev. 415 of 2013, decided 8.5.2023); Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.
records.title: Muhammad Arshad v. State and another (Crl. Rev. 415 of 2013, decided 8.5.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Belated Supplementary Statement Not Further Inquiry
records.heading: A belated supplementary statement alone does not create further inquiry unless the investigation is mala fide
records.text: A mere belated supplementary statement of the complainant under s. 161 CrPC does not create a case of further inquiry unless police investigation is shown to be mala fide. The petitioner was named with specific roles and the post-mortem supported the ocular account. Post-arrest bail dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC Note 201; Muhammad Kashif Yaseen v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 39693-B of 2022, decided 19.9.2022); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Muhammad Kashif Yaseen v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 39693-B of 2022, decided 19.9.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ for Details of Criminal Cases and Inquiries
records.heading: Petition for details of FIRs and inquiries allowed, with medical and transport requests forwarded for decision
records.text: The petitioner sought details and copies of FIRs and inquiries against him, protection from arrest in unknown cases, a medical scan and a well-ventilated vehicle for court appearances. Petition allowed, and the medical scan and transport request were forwarded to the Additional Chief Secretary (Home) for decision in accordance with law. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 688; Parvez Elahi v. Care Taker Government of Punjab etc. (W.P. No. 45360 of 2023, decided 13.7.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Parvez Elahi v. Care Taker Government of Punjab etc. (W.P. No. 45360 of 2023, decided 13.7.2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Rent Tribunal: Late Production of Documents, S. 19(3)
records.heading: Rent Tribunal litigants must produce all documents at the outset, and further evidence is not a right
records.text: Under the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009, litigants must produce all documents they rely on at the outset, and further evidence is not a matter of right. Inadvertent defects may be cured exceptionally with reasons. Permission to produce a voice recording DVD after closing evidence lacked sufficient grounds, and that part of the Tribunal's order was set aside. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 679, 2024 CLC 230; Nasira Bibi v. Special Judge Rent, Lahore and another (W.P. No. 80035 of 2022, decided 5.7.2023); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Nasira Bibi v. Special Judge Rent, Lahore and another (W.P. No. 80035 of 2022, decided 5.7.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mandatory and Directory Enactments: Compliance
records.heading: Mandatory enactments need strict compliance while directory provisions need only substantial compliance
records.text: Mandatory enactments require strict compliance and acts in breach are invalid. A directory provision requires substantial compliance, and minor deviations may be overlooked in the interest of justice. Courts must examine the scheme of the Act to give effect to legislative intent. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 679, 2024 CLC 230; Nasira Bibi v. Special Judge Rent, Lahore and another (W.P. No. 80035 of 2022, decided 5.7.2023); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Nasira Bibi v. Special Judge Rent, Lahore and another (W.P. No. 80035 of 2022, decided 5.7.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 42: Declaration on Dower Deed, Pardanashin Lady
records.heading: Supreme Court upheld the High Court's findings on a pardanashin lady's declaration suit on a dower deed
records.text: A pardanashin lady sued for a declaration of ownership of land under a dower deed not entered in the revenue record. The Supreme Court found that the High Court had scrutinised the evidence in its true perspective, with well reasoned findings. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 466; Pirzada Noor-ul-Basar v. Mst. Pakistan Bibi and others (C.A. No. 23-P of 2017, decided 29.3.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Pirzada Noor-ul-Basar v. Mst. Pakistan Bibi and others (C.A. No. 23-P of 2017, decided 29.3.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: A chance witness needs a convincing explanation for presence at the scene, failing which testimony is suspect
records.text: A chance witness is one not normally expected at the scene without a convincing explanation. The eyewitnesses' presence was a laboured story, and their testimony was suspect, as was their inconsistent evidence about blood on their clothes. Appeal allowed, the accused acquitted and the complainant's revision for enhancement dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 746; Mansab Ali and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 220945-J & Crl. Rev. 218894 of 2018, heard on 6.6.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Mansab Ali and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 220945-J & Crl. Rev. 218894 of 2018, heard on 6.6.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 300 PPC: Reasons for Non-Application of S. 302
records.heading: Trial court must give reasons on the prosecution material when holding that section 302 PPC does not apply
records.text: In forming an opinion that s. 302 PPC does not apply, the Trial Court must give reasons on the material the prosecution put forward, particularly the Commission report holding the airline responsible for endangering passengers. Criminal revision allowed, with observations confined to the adequacy of the impugned order. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 757; Abid Rehman v. Farooq Umar Bhoja and others (Crl. Rev. 8 of 2020, decided 20.5.2022); Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir.
records.title: Abid Rehman v. Farooq Umar Bhoja and others (Crl. Rev. 8 of 2020, decided 20.5.2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Re-summoning Witness to Fill Lacunae
records.heading: Application to re-summon the investigating officer to fill lacunae under section 540 CrPC was rightly dismissed
records.text: The complainant's application to re-summon the investigating officer for further re-examination, apparently to bring on record a statement of a Court witness, was rightly dismissed by the Trial Court as there was no reason for it. Revision dismissed and the order upheld, as interference is warranted only in exceptional circumstances. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 782; Ghulam Madni v. State and 5 others (Crl. Rev. 203 of 2022, decided 17.11.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Ghulam Madni v. State and 5 others (Crl. Rev. 203 of 2022, decided 17.11.2022)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Changing Counsel to Avoid Bench: Mala Fide
records.heading: Changing counsel to avoid a Bench is mala fide and the power of attorney was not accepted
records.text: In a second bail petition under s. 489-F PPC, replacing the earlier counsel by an advocate blocked by the Bench was held an ulterior and mala fide step to avoid hearing before that Bench. His power of attorney was not accepted, the office was directed not to accept it where he sought to supersede earlier counsel, and the petitioner was free to engage another advocate. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 786; Muhammad Talha v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 27751-B-2023, decided 7.6.2023); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Muhammad Talha v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 27751-B-2023, decided 7.6.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Government Analyst Report Without Test Protocols
records.heading: A Government Analyst report omitting the full test protocols is unreliable and attracts no presumption under section 36(2) CNSA
records.text: A forensic report that does not describe the full protocols of tests applied, as required by R. 6 of the Control of Narcotic Substances (Government Analysts) Rules, 2001, is inconclusive, defective and unreliable and does not attract the presumption under s. 36(2) CNSA. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 791, 2023 YLR 2654; Shakil-ur-Rehman v. State (Crl. A. 182346 & 197051 & CSR No. 2-N of 2018, heard on 20.6.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Shakil-ur-Rehman v. State (Crl. A. 182346 & 197051 & CSR No. 2-N of 2018, heard on 20.6.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 228 PPC: Intentional Insult to Public Servant
records.heading: Mens rea is a necessary ingredient of the offence of intentional insult under section 228 PPC
records.text: Mens rea, meaning intention to insult or interrupt, is a necessary ingredient of an offence under s. 228 PPC, and criminal liability attaches to acts coupled with a guilty mind. Appeal accepted, the conviction and sentence set aside and the appellant acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 798; Ahmad Muneel v. State etc. (Crl. A. 669 of 2023, heard on 26.6.2023); Justice Safdar Saleem Shahid.
records.title: Ahmad Muneel v. State etc. (Crl. A. 669 of 2023, heard on 26.6.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Appeal: Close-Range Fire and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Close-range fire, site plan distance and absence of exit wound led to acquittal in a murder appeal
records.text: In a s. 302(b) PPC appeal, the Court examined blackening on the wound, indicating close-range fire, against the 11 feet distance in the site plan and the absence of an exit wound. The Urdu post describes the judgment as covering polygraph tests in detail. Appeal allowed, the accused acquitted and the complainant's revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 765; Muhammad Aslam etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. 255528 of 2018 and Crl. Rev. 255777 of 2018, decided 10.4.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. 255528 of 2018 and Crl. Rev. 255777 of 2018, decided 10.4.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: No Mala Fide Alleged
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail refused where no specific mala fide was alleged and offences were non-bailable
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was refused where no specific details of mala fide or ulterior motive were alleged, the offences under ss. 324 and 380 PPC were non-bailable, and there were serious allegations of a false agreement to sell. Under s. 498 CrPC the petitioner must satisfy the Court on mala fide. Petition dismissed, leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 212; Ahtisham Ali v. State (Crl. P. 13-K of 2023, decided 22.3.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ahtisham Ali v. State (Crl. P. 13-K of 2023, decided 22.3.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotics Samples
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody and transmission of narcotics samples led to acquittal
records.text: Neither safe custody nor safe transmission of the sealed sample parcels to the laboratory was proved. The Moharrar and the Constable who deposited the parcels were not produced, and the three day gap between recovery and receipt was unexplained. Appeal allowed and the accused acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 217; Muhammad Hazir v. State (Crl. A. 285 of 2022, decided 1.3.2023); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Muhammad Hazir v. State (Crl. A. 285 of 2022, decided 1.3.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Injured Witness Testimony
records.heading: A prompt FIR, injured witness and medical corroboration supported conviction despite minor discrepancies
records.text: An FIR registered within one hour and 25 minutes at a police station 25 kilometres away, detailed witness accounts, an injured witness whose injuries prove her presence, and corroborating medical evidence supported the conviction. Minor discrepancies were immaterial. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 221; Aqil v. State (J.P. 553 of 2017, decided 16.2.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Aqil v. State (J.P. 553 of 2017, decided 16.2.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness, Identification Parade and Recovery
records.heading: Injured witness, identification parade and recovery of weapons supported conviction despite minor discrepancies
records.text: An FIR on the same day, an injured witness whose injuries prove his presence, unambiguous identification, an identification parade and recovery of weapons supported conviction under ss. 302, 324 and 396 PPC. Minor discrepancies do not make the prosecution case doubtful. Petitions dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 228; Ansar and others v. State and others (J.P. 405 of 2021 and Crl. P. 946 of 2021, decided 2.3.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ansar and others v. State and others (J.P. 405 of 2021 and Crl. P. 946 of 2021, decided 2.3.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail to Woman Accused: First Proviso to S. 497(1)
records.heading: For women under the first proviso to section 497(1) CrPC, bail is the rule even in murder cases
records.text: For women and others in the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, bail is the rule and refusal the exception, whatever the category of the offence, as for offences outside the prohibitory clause. Bail was granted to the petitioner in a case under s. 302 PPC. Bail granted. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 238; Mst. Ghazala v. State and another (Crl. P. 54 of 2023, decided 22.2.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Mst. Ghazala v. State and another (Crl. P. 54 of 2023, decided 22.2.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Belated Supplementary Statement
records.heading: Post-arrest bail granted where a belated statement, unexamined recording and the petitioner's age cast doubt
records.text: The complainant recorded a further s. 161 CrPC statement 12 days after the FIR, suspecting the petitioner. The alleged audio recording on a USB was not sent for forensic examination, and the petitioner was 18 or 19 years old and reportedly a heart patient. The cumulative effect doubted the prosecution version and he was admitted to bail. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 241; Salman Zahid v. State through P.G. Sindh (Crl. P. 263 of 2023, decided 27.4.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Salman Zahid v. State through P.G. Sindh (Crl. P. 263 of 2023, decided 27.4.2023)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Explosive Substances: Police Witnesses and Minor Discrepancies
records.heading: Police witnesses are as good as private witnesses, and minor discrepancies do not justify rejecting evidence
records.text: In a case under ss. 4 and 5 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 and s. 7 ATA, police witnesses are as good as private witnesses, and minor discrepancies on trivial matters should not lead to rejection of evidence. The petitioner did not appear on oath under s. 340(2) CrPC. Petition refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 245; Nazir Ahmed v. State (Jail P. 169 of 2021, decided 1.6.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Nazir Ahmed v. State (Jail P. 169 of 2021, decided 1.6.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Statutory Delay and Rule of Consistency
records.heading: Bail granted on a general role, trial delay not caused by the accused and consistency with a co-accused
records.text: Bail was granted where only a general role was ascribed to the petitioners, the trial delay was not caused by them, and a co-accused with a similar role had been granted post-arrest bail by the Supreme Court. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 250; Noor Kamal and another v. State and another (Crl. P. 1720 of 2022, decided 30.3.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Noor Kamal and another v. State and another (Crl. P. 1720 of 2022, decided 30.3.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Abductee Not Recovered
records.heading: Post-arrest bail refused where the abductee was not recovered after about five months
records.text: Post-arrest bail was refused where the petitioner, father of the alleged abductee, appeared to have the real motive, and non-recovery of the abductee after about five months was a serious matter. The Inspector General of Police was directed to look into it personally and depute an officer to ensure recovery. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 252; Hilal Khattak v. State and another (Crl. P. 461 of 2023, decided 24.5.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Hilal Khattak v. State and another (Crl. P. 461 of 2023, decided 24.5.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Remedy Against Recall of Bail: Revision, Not S. 498
records.heading: Recall of bail under section 497(5) CrPC is challenged by revision, not by a petition under section 498
records.text: Where bail is recalled under s. 497(5) CrPC, the remedy is revision and a petition under s. 498 CrPC is not competent. A Magistrate cannot cancel bail granted by a higher forum but may issue non-bailable warrants and proceed against the surety under s. 514 CrPC, which amounts to cancellation. Ref: 2023 LHC 4390; Muhammad Moosa v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 2163-B-23, decided 16.06.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Moosa v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 2163-B-23, decided 16.06.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Recovery of Weapon on Disclosure, Art. 40 QSO
records.heading: A weapon recovered on the accused's disclosure and pointation is relevant under Article 40 QSO
records.text: A weapon recovered on the disclosure and pointation of the accused is relevant under Art. 40 QSO. Such recovery gains credence if witnessed by two witnesses, who need not live in the same neighbourhood, as the place was within the exclusive knowledge of the accused. The objection based on s. 103 CrPC was rejected. Ref: 2023 MLD 1298, PLJ 2023 CrC 174; Muhammad Faisal v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 76 of 2020 & M.R. No. 14 of 2020); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz; Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Faisal v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 76 of 2020 & M.R. No. 14 of 2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Guidelines for Cancellation of Bail
records.heading: Bail may be cancelled for illegality, misuse, absconding, interference or fresh material showing guilt
records.text: Bail may be cancelled where the grant order is patently illegal or has caused miscarriage of justice, the accused misused the concession, hampered prosecution evidence, is likely to abscond, interfered with the investigation, committed a similar offence, or where fresh material tending to establish guilt has emerged. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1397.

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Karachi Nallah Affectees: Compensation Payment Mechanism
records.heading: Consent payment mechanism recorded for Karachi Nallah affectees in contempt proceedings against the Chief Minister
records.text: In a contempt application against the Chief Minister, Sindh over non-payment of compensation to affectees of Gujjar, Orangi and Mehmoodabad Nallahs, a consent mechanism was recorded for 6932 affectees. Cheques were to be prepared within 7 days, paid in two tranches of Rs. 90,000, collectable within 30 days, and construction cost paid per Pakistan Engineering Council standards for 80 square yard houses. Ref: Shehri-Citizens for a Better Environment & others v. Murad Ali Shah (Crl.O.P. 4-K/2023, decided 17.08.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Shehri-Citizens for a Better Environment & others v. Murad Ali Shah (Crl.O.P. 4-K/2023, decided 17.08.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pleading and Proof of Fraud
records.heading: A party alleging fraud must plead it clearly and again state it clearly in examination-in-chief
records.text: A party asserting fraud must narrate it clearly in its pleadings and again clearly in examination-in-chief. A bald statement of fraud has no legal consequence. Ref: 2023 YLR 1576.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Proactive Trial Court; Withholding of Witness
