records.heading: Trial courts should be proactive, and a withheld witness raises doubt that benefits the defence
records.text: Trial courts should adopt a proactive approach to justice rather than sit idle and depend only on the material the parties produce. The prosecution's retention of its cards close to its chest gave rise to serious doubt about its version, the benefit of which goes to the defence. Ref: 2023 YLR 1691; Zeeshan Iftikhar alias Shani v. State.
records.title: Zeeshan Iftikhar alias Shani v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Witness
records.heading: A witness who dishonestly improves his version has testimony of no worth to the prosecution
records.text: The complainant's FIR said two accused fired and hit the injured on the mouth, but in examination-in-chief he improved this to joint firing with one accused's shot hitting the lips, and offered no explanation when confronted. An important witness who improves his version to align with other statements has testimony of no worth to the prosecution. Ref: 2023 YLR 1585.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Deaf and Dumb Accused Understanding Proceedings: S. 341
records.heading: Section 341 CrPC did not apply to an accused who understood the proceedings through interpreters
records.text: S. 341 CrPC did not apply to an accused claiming to be deaf and dumb because he could understand the proceedings through interpreters, namely his elder brother and a school headmistress, who conveyed the Court's questions and his replies. The Trial Court had taken care of the relevant provisions. Ref: 2023 YLR 1727.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Own Pay Scale Appointments Declared Unlawful
records.heading: Own Pay Scale appointments were declared unlawful and alien to law by the Lahore High Court
records.text: The Lahore High Court declared Own Pay Scale (OPS) appointments alien to law, in violation of Arts. 4 and 25, the PCS Act and PCS Rules, and without legal basis per S&GAD notifications of 17.05.1982 and 01.05.2000. Posts are to be filled under recruitment rules, with stop-gap arrangements under PCS Rules. The Chief Secretary was directed to review 183 appointments within 30 days. Ref: Tanveer Sarwar v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 63900/2021); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Tanveer Sarwar v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 63900/2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Marriage of Girl Under Sixteen: Bail Refused
records.heading: The statutory marriage age of sixteen for females is strictly enforced, and bail was refused
records.text: The statutory age of sixteen for a female's marriage under the Act of 1929 and allied laws is to be strictly enforced, preferred over uncodified divergent religious opinions, in line with Arts. 4, 9, 14 and 25 and Pakistan's UNCRC obligations. Under s. 375(d) PPC the consent of a female below sixteen is immaterial. Bail dismissed. Ref: 2023 LHC 4435; Shahid Imran v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 33583/23, decided 31.05.2023); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Shahid Imran v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 33583/23, decided 31.05.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Actus Curiae Neminem Gravabit: Correction of Court's Error
records.heading: No person should suffer for the Court's fault, and a patent error may be corrected by review
records.text: No person should suffer from the fault of the Court. A patent and obvious error of the Court may be reviewed, and where the Court has erred it must remedy the injury promptly and, by the principle of restitution, restore the party to the position he would have held but for the mistake. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1451.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Scope of High Court Constitutional Jurisdiction
records.heading: Authority on the scope of High Court constitutional jurisdiction and the meaning of alternate remedy
records.text: Authority on the scope and purpose of the High Court's constitutional jurisdiction, disputed questions of fact, and the meaning of the expression alternate remedy. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1442.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Statutory Ground of Delay
records.heading: An accused in custody beyond the one year statutory period without fault is entitled to bail on delay
records.text: In a murderous assault case the statutory period was one year, while the accused had been in custody over two years. Charge was first framed on 17-01-2023 and no delay was attributable to the accused thereafter, so he became entitled to bail on the statutory ground of delay. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1450.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199 Against Appellate Decisions, Family Cases
records.heading: Article 199 against appellate decisions in family cases is limited to jurisdictional errors and procedural impropriety
records.text: Art. 199 jurisdiction is limited against appellate decisions and cannot substitute for appeal or revision. The High Court cannot reappraise evidence or re-examine facts decided by lower courts, especially in family cases where the legislature intended to avoid prolonging disputes. Its role is limited to correcting jurisdictional errors and procedural impropriety. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1434.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Directory and Mandatory Provisions: Distinction
records.heading: Whether a provision is mandatory or directory depends on the scheme of the Act and its substance
records.text: Whether a provision is mandatory or directory depends on the scheme of the Act and Rules, and the Court looks at substance and fundamental nature, not just form. A provision conferring both a power and a duty is mandatory. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1502.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutation: Proof and Limitation
records.heading: A suit challenging a gift mutation filed almost 15 years later was time-barred
records.text: Donees proved the gift (tamleek) through revenue record and witnesses. The suit challenging the 1981 mutation, filed almost 15 years later, was time-barred, and the appellants had no locus standi to allege fraud when the donor never challenged the mutation in her lifetime. Suit for declaration and permanent injunction rightly dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1402.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Toshakhana Case: Ex Parte Conviction, Court Awaits High Court
records.heading: In the Toshakhana case the Supreme Court decided to await the High Court's decision first
records.text: Order records that the trial court proceeded ex parte on 05.08.2023, convicted the petitioner under ss. 167 and 173 of the Elections Act, 2017 with three years' imprisonment, and had earlier refused his request to produce defence witnesses at the s. 342 CrPC stage. The Supreme Court decided to await the High Court's decision first. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. District Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Crl.P.921/2023, decided 23.08.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. District Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Crl.P.921/2023, decided 23.08.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Toshakhana Case: Court Awaits High Court Order
records.heading: Supreme Court awaits the High Court order and seeks a report on the petitioner's jail conditions
records.text: As proceedings were in progress before the High Court on the matters in issue, the Supreme Court considered it appropriate to await that order before proceeding. The Attorney General was directed to file a report on the petitioner's living conditions in jail by 28.08.2023 for perusal by the Bench in Chambers. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. District Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Crl.P.921/2023, decided 24.08.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. District Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Crl.P.921/2023, decided 24.08.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Lodging FIR
records.heading: An FIR lodged after unexplained delay of over six hours carries no evidentiary value
records.text: An FIR lodged more than six hours after the occurrence, when police were already in contact with the complainant party through a constable who brought the injured to hospital, carried no sanctity or evidentiary value without explanation. It could not corroborate the prosecution, which failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1235.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Witnesses who change the location of injuries to match the postmortem report are not truthful
records.text: Where the complainant and injured witnesses changed the location of injuries on the deceased to align the ocular account with the postmortem report, the improvements were dishonest. Witnesses who make such improvements are not reliable or truthful, and their testimony is not confidence inspiring. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1235.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness: Presence of Injury
records.heading: The mere presence of an injury on a witness does not make him truthful
records.text: The mere presence of an injury on the person of a prosecution witness does not stamp him as a truthful witness. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1235.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Suppression of Injuries to Another Person
records.heading: Suppression of injuries to another person in the FIR left the prosecution case unproved
records.text: The complainant party suppressed in the FIR and complaint the firearm injury to another person who later died, and admitted it only in court. Where injuries are suppressed or unexplained, the prosecution case lacks proof beyond doubt, and the ocular account was discarded as unreliable. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1235.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Where Ocular Account Disbelieved
records.heading: Motive does not assist the prosecution once the ocular account is disbelieved
records.text: Once the ocular account is disbelieved as to the accused, motive does not assist the prosecution. Motive is a double edged weapon and may also explain false implication. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1235.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Defective Warrant and Proclamation: Absconsion
records.heading: A defective warrant and proclamation give no corroboration, and absconsion does not prove the charge
records.text: The warrant was addressed to no police officer for execution, the proclamation gave no date for surrender, and the process server's report lacked details of the accused's house. Both were defective and gave no corroboration. Absconsion is not proof of the charge and does not help where the ocular account is disbelieved. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1235.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Framing of Charge: Ss. 265-D and 265-K CrPC
records.heading: At the charge stage the court does not examine the veracity of documents, as that would be a trial within a trial
records.text: At the charge stage the court does not examine the veracity or admissibility of documents or statements, as that would amount to a trial within a trial. Under s. 265-D CrPC the report under s. 173 and accompanying material need only provide a prima facie basis to proceed. S. 265-K allows discharge or acquittal where there is no probability of conviction. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1256.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: No Justification for Presence
records.heading: Chance witnesses with no plausible reason for presence were held not to be at the scene
records.text: The complainant and his brother, who did not reside in the vicinity, gave no plausible reason for being at the scene. They were chance witnesses, and their conduct after the death (not witnessing the inquest, not escorting the body or being named in the postmortem report) showed they were not present at the time and place of occurrence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1262.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Alleged Conspiracy Not Proved
records.heading: A claim that relatives overheard a conspiracy during a condolence visit was not credible
records.text: The claim that relatives overheard the accused party hatching a conspiracy while visiting them for condolence was not credible. The relatives did not tell the complainant or the deceased, and visiting the accused's house in another city despite an existing dispute did not appeal to a prudent mind. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1262.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Material contradiction between the FIR injuries and medical evidence made the eye-witnesses unsafe to rely on
records.text: The FIR described injuries on the abdomen, chest and thigh that the medical evidence did not support, as some were exit wounds and no abdominal injury existed. This material contradiction made it unsafe to rely on the eye-witnesses. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1262.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Pistol Recovery on Pointation Inconsequential
records.heading: A purely corroboratory pistol recovery cannot alone sustain a conviction on a capital charge
records.text: A recovery that is purely corroboratory cannot alone sustain a conviction on a capital charge. No independent witness was associated and the forensic report only showed the pistol was in mechanical operating condition, so the recovery was inconsequential. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1262.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Set Up but Not Proved
records.heading: If the prosecution sets up a motive and fails to prove it, the prosecution suffers
records.text: The prosecution need not establish motive in every murder case, but if it sets up a motive and fails to prove it, the prosecution suffers and not the accused. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1262.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion: Corroborative Value Only
records.heading: Absconsion alone cannot sustain a capital conviction and is only corroborative of the ocular account
records.text: Absconsion alone cannot sustain a conviction on a capital charge and may only corroborate or confirm the ocular account. Its relevance to guilt or innocence depends on the overall facts of the case. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1262.

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Promissory Note and O. XXXVII CPC Suit
records.heading: A promissory note forming part of a finance agreement supports a suit under Order XXXVII CPC
records.text: Discussion of s. 2(i) and s. 6 of the Microfinance Institutions Ordinance, 2001 and ss. 3 and 4 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. A promissory note is an instrument containing an unconditional undertaking, and as it was an integral part of the finance agreement, the suit was maintainable under O. XXXVII CPC. Ref: Telenor Microfinance Bank Limited v. Shamim Bano & others (C.P.329-K/2022, decided 28.04.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Telenor Microfinance Bank Limited v. Shamim Bano & others (C.P.329-K/2022, decided 28.04.2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Victim Testimony, Credibility and Inconclusive DNA
records.heading: A sole victim's testimony may suffice if reliable, but credibility problems and inconclusive DNA gave the benefit of doubt
records.text: The sole testimony of a sexual assault victim may suffice if independent, unbiased and straightforward, otherwise corroboration may be sought. The victim's earlier similar case ended in compromise, damaging her credibility, and the DNA report was not conclusive against the petitioner. A single doubt suffices for the benefit of doubt. Ref: Atta ul Mustafa v. The State, etc (Crl.P.596-L/2022, decided 11.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Atta ul Mustafa v. The State, etc (Crl.P.596-L/2022, decided 11.08.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Consistency and Fraud Allegation
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail may rest on consistency, and a huge fraud allegation alone is no ground to refuse it
records.text: Where the principal accused has been granted post-arrest bail, refusing pre-arrest bail on a technical ground would be limited to arrest, as the petitioner would then get bail on consistency. Mere fraud of a huge amount, or registration of other cases, is no ground to decline bail where a prima facie case exists on merits. Merits may be touched in pre-arrest bail. Ref: Ch. Saeed Ahmad Khalil v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.701/2023, decided 11.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Ch. Saeed Ahmad Khalil v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.701/2023, decided 11.08.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Non-Prohibitory Clause and Consistency
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail follows consistency with a co-accused, and bail is the rule outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: Where a co-accused ascribed a similar role has been granted post-arrest bail, pre-arrest bail would be consistent with the likely post-arrest outcome. Bail in offences outside the prohibitory clause is the rule and refusal the exception, and merits may be touched in pre-arrest bail. Ref: Munawar Bibi v. The State (Crl.P.90-K/2023, decided 03.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Munawar Bibi v. The State (Crl.P.90-K/2023, decided 03.08.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revision under S. 115 CPC: Scope
records.heading: Revision under section 115 CPC corrects jurisdictional errors and does not ordinarily reach findings of fact
records.text: Revisional powers under s. 115 CPC are exercised within clauses (a) to (c) and serve to correct jurisdictional errors of subordinate courts. Erroneous findings of fact are ordinarily not revisable unless based on no evidence or inadmissible evidence and so perverse that grave injustice results. Ref: Shamshad Bibi v. Riasat Ali, etc (C.P.1692-L/2022, decided 25.05.2023); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Shamshad Bibi v. Riasat Ali, etc (C.P.1692-L/2022, decided 25.05.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal under Order XLI Rule 27 CPC needs reasons and a document not easily fabricated
records.text: O. XLI R. 27 CPC allows additional evidence in appeal after recording reasons, in three situations in clauses (a) to (c), with procedure under R. 28. Before allowing it, the court must be satisfied that the document is not of a kind that could easily be fabricated, tampered with or manufactured. Ref: Shamshad Bibi v. Riasat Ali, etc (C.P.1692-L/2022, decided 25.05.2023); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Shamshad Bibi v. Riasat Ali, etc (C.P.1692-L/2022, decided 25.05.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in S. 489-F PPC: Tenant and Cheque
records.heading: Bail is the rule in a section 489-F PPC case outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: The petitioner was the complainant's tenant, and a rent claim falls within the Rent Controller's domain. Whether the cheque was issued towards a loan or obligation under s. 489-F PPC is for the trial court. The offence carries a maximum of three years and falls outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so bail is the rule. Other cases do not bar bail. Ref: Zafar Nawaz v. The State (Crl.P.717 of 2023, decided 22.08.2023).
records.title: Zafar Nawaz v. The State (Crl.P.717 of 2023, decided 22.08.2023)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: Recovered Mobile Phones and Forensic Extraction as Evidence
records.heading: Recovered phones and forensic extraction proved a charge of making a nude video of a minor
records.text: Recovery of a pistol, mobile phone and SIMs, with a forensic extraction summary showing thousands of images and videos of minors and the accused, established the prosecution case beyond reasonable doubt on a charge of making a nude video of a minor and blackmailing him. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1310.

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: Sexual Exploitation of Minors: Technical Evidence
records.heading: Forensically confirmed technical evidence of sexual exploitation of minors means not every victim need be summoned
records.text: Where technical evidence of obscene photographs or videos is available from an information technology system and confirmed by forensic reports, all victims need not be summoned. Acquittal on the rape charge under s. 377 PPC did not absolve the accused of the crime of seducing, exploiting and blackmailing minors. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1310.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Medical Board for Accused: Application to Health Secretary
records.heading: A Special Medical Board arranged on the complainant's application to the Secretary was declared without lawful authority
records.text: The accused's father was an aggrieved person under Art. 199 and the petition was maintainable. The Prisons Rules do not prescribe a procedure for a Medical Board, and Rule 197 was flagrantly violated when the accused was shifted without the Inspector General's order. The complainant's application to the Secretary was incompetent, and the Special Board and its report were declared without lawful authority. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1373.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Prison Rules: Court Regulates Custody of Under-Trial Prisoner
records.heading: The court regulates custody of an under-trial prisoner, so medical board requests go to it
records.text: Rules 197, 397 and 981 of the Prison Rules, 1978 govern treatment of prisoners, including removal to hospital outside the jail with the Inspector General's permission. The magistrate or court regulates the custody of a prisoner, so requests for examination or re-examination by a medical board should be made to it. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1373.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: Admission of Execution
records.heading: Admitted execution of an agreement to sell needs no proof, so the onus on execution was discharged
records.text: The respondent examined her attorney and an attesting witness, and the appellant's attorney conceded execution of the agreement to sell. Admitted facts need not be proved, so the onus on execution was discharged and nothing prevented execution of the sale deed. Ref: 2023 CLC 1411.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Penalty Clause Does Not Bar Specific Performance
records.heading: A penalty clause on breach does not by itself bar specific performance under section 20
records.text: Specific performance is discretionary under s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, but the discretion must rest on reason and fairness. Under s. 20, a stipulation for payment of a penalty on breach does not by itself prevent specific performance. The first appellate court rightly decreed specific performance and the second appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2023 CLC 1411.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Second Appeal under S. 100 CPC: Limited Scope
records.heading: A second appeal under section 100 CPC has very limited scope and the first appellate judgment is preferred
records.text: A regular second appeal under s. 100 CPC has very limited scope. Where the courts below differ, preference ordinarily goes to the first appellate court's judgment unless it offends law, and it cannot be interfered with absent a procedural defect materially affecting its findings. Ref: 2023 CLC 1411.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Striking Off Right to File Written Statement
records.heading: Striking off the right to file a written statement was upheld after ten opportunities over eight months
records.text: The CPC provisions cited (Rr. 1, 1A and 10 as reported) allow thirty days and not more than two opportunities for a written statement. Defendants who took ten opportunities over eight months without cause showed negligence. Striking off the right was less penal than pronouncing judgment, they could still cross-examine, and the constitutional petition was dismissed in limine. Ref: 2023 CLC 1453.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Joint Venture of State Land with Army Unlawful
records.heading: A joint venture of State land between the Army and a Caretaker Government was unconstitutional and unlawful
records.text: A joint venture over more than one million acres of State land for corporate agriculture farming between the Pakistan Army and the Caretaker Punjab Government, under a notification of 20.02.2023 under s. 10(2) of the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act, 1912, was unconstitutional and unlawful under Art. 245 and s. 230 of the Elections Act, 2017. Petitions allowed and the transaction set aside. Ref: 2023 CLC 1535; Justice Abid Hussain Chattah.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Challenged for Fraud: Burden on Beneficiary
records.heading: Where a gift is challenged for fraud, the beneficiary must prove the deed or mutation and the original transaction
records.text: A valid gift needs offer, acceptance and delivery of possession. Where its sanctity is challenged for fraud or misrepresentation, the beneficiary must prove both the gift deed or mutation and the original transaction. No adverse order may be passed against an unimpleaded owner. Concurrent findings were not disturbed under s. 115 CPC absent misreading or non-reading of evidence. Ref: 2023 MLD 1405.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Preventive Detention under West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance
records.heading: A preventive detention order under section 3 cannot rest on conjecture and was declared unlawful
records.text: An order under s. 3 of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 cannot rest on conjecture and must be supported by cogent material satisfying a prudent person. The detention order and arrest were declared unlawful, release was directed on the petitioner's undertaking, and arrest in another case was restrained for two days to allow him to seek bail. Ref: 2023 MLD 1417.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Additional Evidence by DNA Test Refused in Revision
records.heading: Additional evidence by DNA test was refused in revision as it was raised late and lacked bona fides
records.text: The High Court declined an application for additional evidence by DNA testing to prove the petitioner was the deceased owner's daughter, as it was not raised before the trial and appellate courts and lacked bona fides. Concurrent findings against relationship were not disturbed in revision, which was dismissed. Ref: 2023 MLD 1445.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Not Proved in Accordance with Law
records.heading: A call data record received by e-mail without verification was not proved in accordance with law
records.text: A call data record received by a constable by e-mail, without sender or recipient address, signature of a service provider representative or subscriber details, was not proved in accordance with law. No company official was produced, the record did not support the prosecution version, and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2023 MLD 1490; Muhammad Shahzad v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Shahzad v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Recovery on Disclosure: Art. 40 QSO
records.heading: Recovery of unidentified stolen articles from an open shop after five months did not prove possession by the accused
records.text: Admissibility of a disclosure statement to police leading to discovery under Art. 40 QSO depends on how the prosecution proves it. The stolen articles were not identified by the complainant, and recovery after more than five months from an open, accessible shop not belonging to the accused was insufficient to prove he held the stolen goods. Ref: 2023 MLD 1490; Muhammad Shahzad v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Shahzad v. State

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 4 MFLO: Inheritance of Predeceased Children's Issue
records.heading: Section 4 MFLO protects orphan grandchildren, and the Federal Shariat Court verdict stands suspended on appeal
records.text: Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 protects orphan grandchildren, who take the share their predeceased parent would have inherited from the grandfather. Although the Federal Shariat Court declared s. 4 repugnant to Islam, that verdict stands suspended automatically on the filing of an appeal before the Supreme Court. Ref: 2023 MLD 1484.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 382-B CrPC: Mandatory Set-Off of Detention
records.heading: Credit for pre-conviction detention under section 382-B CrPC is mandatory since the word shall replaced may
records.text: Since the word 'shall' replaced 'may' in s. 382-B CrPC, giving credit for pre-conviction detention is mandatory, including where a death sentence is later reduced. The benefit compensates for delay in trial. Invoking s. 561-A CrPC, the petition was allowed and the accused was declared entitled to the benefit. Ref: 2023 MLD 1545.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Improvement in Statement: Witness Untrustworthy
records.heading: A witness who improves his statement on material aspects is untrustworthy
records.text: A witness who improves his statement on material aspects of the case is untrustworthy. Ref: 2023 MLD 1568.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion Not Conclusive Proof of Guilt
records.heading: Absconding after the occurrence is not conclusive proof of guilt without independent corroboration
records.text: Absconding after the occurrence is not conclusive proof of guilt. The trial court convicted eight accused on the same evidence on which it acquitted seven co-accused, and the High Court set aside the convictions for want of independent corroborating evidence. Ref: 2023 MLD 1568.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report: Fair Investigation, Art. 10-A
records.heading: A cancellation report without efforts to compel attendance breaches fair investigation under Article 10-A
records.text: Fair investigation is mandatory for a fair trial under Art. 10-A. A cancellation report prepared merely because the complainant and witnesses did not join investigation, without showing process for compelling attendance, was defective. The High Court set aside the trial court's order, remanded for fresh decision and allowed the constitutional petition. Ref: 2023 MLD 1593.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: First Responder: S. 157 CrPC and Rule 25.10 Police Rules
records.heading: A first responder may preserve the scene, record witnesses and arrest culprits under Rule 25.10 Police Rules
records.text: Under Rule 25.10 of the Police Rules, 1934 a first responder may preserve the crime scene, record particulars of potential witnesses including the injured and obtain information, and arrest culprits available near the scene until the regular investigator takes over. Ref: 2023 YLR 2084.

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Acquisition under 1960 Ordinance and Non-Joinder of Province
records.heading: Land acquired under the 1960 Ordinance falls outside the 1894 Act, and non-joinder of the Province was fatal
records.text: Land acquired by an award of 25.05.1966 for Jet Airport extension under the 1960 Ordinance, which has its own independent acquisition mechanism, is not governed by the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Failure to implead the Province of Punjab in the writ petition, contrary to Art. 174, went to the root of the case. Property rights are subject to reasonable restrictions in the public interest. Ref: 2023 YLR 2030.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 4 MFLO: Share of Daughter of Predeceased Son
records.heading: Under section 4 MFLO the daughter of a predeceased son takes her father's share
records.text: Under s. 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 the daughter of a predeceased son takes her father's share in the grandfather's estate, here one third of the property. The findings of the courts below on her share were found to accord with Mst. Zainab v. Kamal Khan alias Kamla (PLD 1990 SC 1051). Ref: 2023 YLR 1961.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence Not to Fill Lacunae
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal under Order XLI Rule 27 CPC cannot be used to fill lacunae
records.text: O. XLI R. 27 CPC contemplates few circumstances for additional evidence in appeal. A party cannot use it to patch up weak parts of its case or fill omissions. The petitioner failed to show the documents were available but could not be produced for reasons beyond his control, so the case fell outside the Rule. Ref: 2023 YLR 1972.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in S. 489-F PPC: Not for Recovery of Money
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC is not meant for recovery of money, and bail is the rule
records.text: Section 489-F PPC is not intended for recovery of an alleged amount, for which civil remedies such as O. XXXVII CPC exist. Whether cheques were issued towards a loan or obligation is for the trial court. The offence carries a maximum of three years, outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so bail is the rule. Absconsion alone is not proof of the offence. Ref: Noman Khaliq v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.714/2023, decided 11.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Noman Khaliq v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.714/2023, decided 11.08.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Purchaser of Stolen Goods, Consistency
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail granted to an alleged purchaser of stolen goods on delay in the FIR and consistency
records.text: The only allegation was that the petitioner bought stolen goods from co-accused over four years with no specific dates, and the FIR was lodged 13 days late without explanation. Applicability of s. 381 PPC was for the trial court. As co-accused had post-arrest bail, consistency applied, and a prima facie case was made out for pre-arrest bail. Ref: Muhammad Aziz @ Mana v. The State, etc (Crl.P.62-L/2023, decided 23.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Aziz @ Mana v. The State, etc (Crl.P.62-L/2023, decided 23.08.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Intimidation (S. 503) and S. 506 PPC
records.heading: Where criminal intimidation has materialised into an overt act, section 506 PPC does not apply
records.text: Where criminal intimidation under s. 503 PPC has materialised into an overt act, s. 506 PPC does not apply, and only the overt act committed in consequence of the intimidation remains in the field. Ref: Abdul Rehman v. The State, etc (Crl.P.611-L/2023, decided 11.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. The State, etc (Crl.P.611-L/2023, decided 11.08.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Cheques Given as Surety, Delayed FIR
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail granted where cheques were given as surety and the FIR was lodged after three years
records.text: The petitioner said the dishonoured cheques of 2019 were given as surety within a business relationship and filed a suit for rendition of accounts. The complainant's silence for three years before lodging the FIR prima facie supported that stance. A prima facie case was made out for pre-arrest bail. Ref: Abdul Rasheed v. The State, etc (Crl.P.294-L/2023, decided 24.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Abdul Rasheed v. The State, etc (Crl.P.294-L/2023, decided 24.08.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Poppy Straw: Meaning of Poast (Doda)
records.heading: Only the doda contains the narcotic in poppy straw, and the prosecution failed to prove its case
records.text: Under the CNSA definition all parts of the mowed poppy plant except seeds are poppy straw, but relying on Taimoor Khan v. State (2016 SCMR 621) and Muhammad Imran v. The State (2011 SCMR 1954), only the basket or pouch (doda), excluding seeds, holds the narcotic, and poppy straw may be other parts. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: Barkhurdar v. The State, etc (Crl.P.733-L/2018, decided 09.06.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Barkhurdar v. The State, etc (Crl.P.733-L/2018, decided 09.06.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Delayed FIR and Non-Vital Injuries: S. 497(2) CrPC
records.heading: A delayed FIR and injuries on non-vital parts made the case one of further inquiry under section 497(2) CrPC
records.text: The FIR was lodged about three days late with an unimpressive explanation, injuries were on non-vital parts and no repeat fire was made despite opportunity. Applicability of s. 324 PPC was for the trial court, and the case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, calling for further inquiry. Ref: Jamaluddin & Juma v. The State (Crl.P.41-K/2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Jamaluddin & Juma v. The State (Crl.P.41-K/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Nomination, Absconsion and Surrender
records.heading: Mere nomination in the crime report does not make a person an accused, and absconsion is not proof of the offence
records.text: Mere nomination in the crime report does not make a person an accused unless investigation confirms the accusation. Absconsion is not proof of the offence, relying on PLJ 1995 SC 477. The petitioner surrendered and joined investigation, so he could not be held in custody indefinitely, and merits may be touched in pre-arrest bail. Ref: Saad Zia v. The State, etc (Crl.P.150-L/2023, decided 20.06.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Saad Zia v. The State, etc (Crl.P.150-L/2023, decided 20.06.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revisional Jurisdiction under S. 115 CPC
records.heading: Concurrent findings based on misreading of evidence are not sacrosanct in revision under section 115 CPC
records.text: Concurrent findings based on misreading or non-reading of evidence are not sacrosanct. Revisional jurisdiction is pre-eminently corrective and supervisory, and under s. 115 CPC the court may even act suo motu to correct jurisdictional errors to ensure safe administration of justice. Ref: Mst. Faheeman Begum (decd.) thr. LRs. & others v. Islam-ud-Din (decd.) thr. LRs. & others (C.A.1300/2019, decided 03.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mst. Faheeman Begum (decd.) thr. LRs. & others v. Islam-ud-Din (decd.) thr. LRs. & others (C.A.1300/2019, decided 03.05.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Bail on Fresh Ground of Delay in Trial
records.heading: Delay in trial after rejection of a first bail application on that ground is a fresh ground for second bail
records.text: The third proviso to s. 497 CrPC operates once a year passes without conclusion of a trial of an offence not punishable with death, for no fault of the accused. Delay occurring in the year after rejection of a first bail application on that ground is a fresh ground for a second bail application. Ref: Syeda Ayesha Subhani v. The State, etc (Crl.P.588-L/2023, decided 28.08.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Syeda Ayesha Subhani v. The State, etc (Crl.P.588-L/2023, decided 28.08.2023)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Petition Against Deceased Sole Respondent
records.heading: A contempt petition against a deceased sole respondent is not proceedable, but a fresh petition may be filed
records.text: An order against an official by designation binds the incumbent despite change of the holder. A contempt petition filed against a sole respondent who had died is not proceedable, being equivalent to a stillborn suit, and the successor cannot be substituted, but a fresh petition may be filed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 585.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Delegated Legislation: Rules of 1969 and Right of Appeal
records.heading: The Rules of 1969 including the appeal provision were validly framed under section 96 of the 1965 Ordinance
records.text: Under the Ordinance of 1965, s. 80 deals with parking places and halting stations in Chapter VII, and s. 96 with s. 96(2)(f) authorises rules on parking places and stands. The Rules of 1969, including the appeal provision for Chapter VIII matters, were framed under s. 96, so the delegated legislative power was rightly exercised. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 572.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Fraud During Court Proceedings
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC applies only to fraud practised during the court proceedings and relating to the subject matter of the suit
records.text: An application under s. 12(2) CPC lies only where fraud or misrepresentation relates to the subject matter of the suit in which the decree was passed, as s. 12(1) bars an independent suit. The fraud or misrepresentation must have been practised during the proceedings in court and not outside it. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 555.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. II R. 2 CPC: Bar on Splitting Claims
records.heading: Order II Rule 2 CPC bars a later suit for a claim omitted or relinquished from the first
records.text: Order II Rule 2 requires every suit to include the whole claim for a cause of action. A plaintiff who omits or relinquishes a claim, or omits a relief without leave of the court, cannot sue for it later. The rule guards against the defendant being vexed twice on the same cause of action. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 601.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Cause of Action, Claim and Relief under O. II R. 2
records.heading: The bar in Order II Rule 2 is against splitting the claim, not the cause of action
records.text: Cause of action is the set of material facts constituting a right and its infringement that entitles a person to sue. The bar in O. II R. 2 is against splitting the claim and not the cause of action. Claim and relief are distinct terms, and the cause of action is also relevant to limitation, forum and locus standi. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 601.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Joinder of Parties and Causes of Action
records.heading: Order II CPC must be read with the joinder rules so all matters are settled in one action
records.text: Order II cannot be understood without the principles of joinder of parties and causes of action in O. I Rr. 1 and 3 and O. II Rr. 3 and 4. The Code provides a fairly liberal regime so that all matters at issue between the parties are settled shortly and speedily in one action. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 601.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata (S. 11) Distinguished from O. II R. 2
records.heading: Order II Rule 2 CPC needs no decision on merits, unlike res judicata under section 11
records.text: Res judicata under s. 11 CPC requires a decision in the prior suit, whereas O. II R. 2 bars a second suit where the plaintiff omitted or relinquished a claim or relief in the first, without needing a final decision on merits. A suit barred under O. II R. 2 is dealt with by rejection of plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 601.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Registers 2, 19 and 21 Are Public Documents
records.heading: Police Registers 2, 19 and 21 are public documents not privileged under section 172 CrPC
records.text: Registers No. 2, 19 and 21 under the Police Rules, 1934 are public documents, not privileged under s. 172 CrPC, and the accused may have them summoned. The trial court wrongly dismissed the application on the basis of s. 172, and the revision was allowed, leaving admissibility and evidentiary value to the trial court. The Court also referred to the fair trial right under Art. 10-A. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 578; Subhan Allah v. The State and another (Criminal Revision No. 43716 of 2022).
records.title: Subhan Allah v. The State and another (Criminal Revision No. 43716 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Framing Issues and Recording Evidence
records.heading: Issues and evidence on a section 12(2) CPC application are needed only where it raises a matter requiring evidence
records.text: Framing issues and recording evidence on a s. 12(2) application is obligatory only where it raises a matter needing evidence. It is unnecessary where the application can be decided without complicated questions of fact, such as a limitation point resolvable on law. This depends on the satisfaction of the court of first instance. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 555.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Court as Court of Ultimate Jurisdiction
records.heading: The civil court is the court of ultimate jurisdiction and may interfere where illegality has been committed
records.text: Under the rule that courts try all suits unless barred, the civil court is the court of ultimate jurisdiction and may interfere in matters where illegality has been committed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 564.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court Judgment as Solemn and Final Decision
records.heading: A Supreme Court judgment is presumed a solemn and final decision on all points arising in the case
records.text: Every Supreme Court judgment is presumed to be a solemn and final decision on all points arising in the case. If the Court has not taken a conscious and deliberate decision on a point of fact or law, this is a material irregularity amounting to an error apparent on the face of the judgment. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 621.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Curative Review: Second Review Barred, Withdrawal Allowed
records.heading: A second review is barred by Order XXVI Rule 9, but withdrawal of curative review petitions was allowed
records.text: Order XXVI R. 9 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980 bars a second review, so the appellants were precluded from reviewing the subject judgment, which finally disposed of the review petitions. The right of parties to withdraw is recognised, and the applications were allowed and the curative review petitions dismissed as withdrawn. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 621.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Sale by Attorney of Illiterate Pardanashin Women
records.heading: Sale of an illiterate pardanashin woman's property requires safeguards, which bind a general attorney too
records.text: A transaction with a pardanashin woman carries a principle of caution: she must be aware of it, have independent advice, there must be witnesses to the sale and payment, and it must be explained in a language she understands. These duties bind a general power of attorney holder too. The alleged vendee here produced no witnesses to the sale or payment. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 628; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Pardanashin Women: Safeguards in Property Transactions
records.heading: Transactions with a pardanashin woman require her awareness, independent advice, witnesses and explanation in her language
records.text: In a transaction with a pardanashin woman, she must be fully aware, have independent advice, there must be witnesses to the sale and receipt of consideration, and it must be explained in a language she understands, relying on 2016 SCMR 862 and 2021 SCMR 19. A power of attorney holder must also ensure this. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 628.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Fabricated Narcotics Case and Delayed Challan
records.heading: Bail allowed in a fabricated narcotics case where the challan was wilfully delayed
records.text: Subordinate police officials booking persons with previous records in narcotics cases on fabricated evidence to make a crackdown successful cannot be endorsed. Wilful delay in submitting the challan prima facie infringed the fair trial right and suggested mala fide, making this a case of further inquiry. Bail allowed. Ref: 2023 LHC 4526; Shehzad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.34710/23, decided 21.06.2023); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Shehzad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.34710/23, decided 21.06.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Female Heirs and Tenancy Rights in Bahawalpur
records.heading: The Colonization Act 1912 does not bar female heirs from inheriting tenancy rights in Bahawalpur
records.text: In succession to tenancy before 1951 in Bahawalpur, the Colonization Act, 1912 does not prevent female heirs from inheriting tenancy rights, as Shariah law prevails. Ref: Muhammad Boota (decd.) thr. LRs. & others v. Mst. Fatima & others (C.A.419/2011, decided 05.09.2023); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Muhammad Boota (decd.) thr. LRs. & others v. Mst. Fatima & others (C.A.419/2011, decided 05.09.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness
records.heading: A plaintiff in a specific performance suit must plead and prove readiness and willingness to perform
records.text: Under Forms 47 and 48 in Appendix A of the First Schedule to the CPC, the plaintiff must plead that he applied to the defendants to perform, or tendered the amount and demanded transfer. In a suit for specific performance he must plead and prove readiness and willingness to perform his obligations. Ref: Ijaz-ul-Haq v. Mrs. Maroof Begum Ahmed & others (C.A.1121/2018, decided 16.08.2023); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Ijaz-ul-Haq v. Mrs. Maroof Begum Ahmed & others (C.A.1121/2018, decided 16.08.2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Anti-Rape Act: Purposive Interpretation and Special Units
records.heading: The Anti-Rape Act is to be construed purposively, and Special Sexual Offences Investigation Units are to be set up
records.text: The Anti-Rape Act must be interpreted liberally and purposively, adopting the construction that advances its objectives. Section 9 provides a special investigation procedure, with the Anti-Rape (Investigation) Rules 2022. If Special Sexual Offences Investigation Units have not been set up, they are to be constituted immediately and police officers trained. Ref: 2023 LHC 4535; Sumaira v. The State etc. (Criminal Proceedings 75596/22, decided 31.08.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Sumaira v. The State etc. (Criminal Proceedings 75596/22, decided 31.08.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth Requires Civil Court Declaration
records.heading: Correction of a date of birth requires a declaration by a civil court of competent jurisdiction
records.text: For alteration or correction of a date of birth, a declaration is indispensable, and it can only be issued by a civil court of competent jurisdiction on evidence produced during proceedings about authenticity. Ref: Abdul Nafey v. Muhammad Rafique & Others (C.P.173-Q/2023, decided 09.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Abdul Nafey v. Muhammad Rafique & Others (C.P.173-Q/2023, decided 09.08.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift under Muhammadan Law: Ingredients and Revocation
records.heading: A Muslim gift needs offer, acceptance and delivery of possession, and may be revoked only before delivery
records.text: A gift (hiba) is an immediate transfer without exchange, accepted by the donee. Its requisites are offer, acceptance and delivery of possession, and a Muslim may make it orally, though writing serves as proof. Under s. 167 of the Muhammadan Law it may be revoked only before delivery of possession. Ref: Hayat Muhammad thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Riaz (C.A.1551/2017, decided 07.08.2023); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Hayat Muhammad thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Riaz (C.A.1551/2017, decided 07.08.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Child Witness Competence and Withholding Best Evidence
records.heading: Giving up a witness because she was a minor is unjustified, and withheld best evidence favoured the appellants
records.text: Giving up a witness as unnecessary is the prosecution's prerogative, but giving her up because she was a minor has no legal justification. A child may depose subject to capacity and understanding, which the court decides under Arts. 3 and 17 QSO after voir dire. Best evidence was withheld, so the benefit went to the appellants. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 412, 2023 PCrLJ 1546; Muhammad Hanif v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 173 of 2022, decided 10.1.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 173 of 2022, decided 10.1.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Trial Court Not a Silent Umpire
records.heading: The trial court may use section 540 CrPC to summon withheld evidence but may not craft new evidence
records.text: The trial court is not a silent spectator and may use s. 540 Cr.P.C. to summon or recall evidence to find the truth where a party withholds it. Summoning already available but withheld evidence is permissible, but crafting new evidence is prohibited in an adversarial system. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 412, 2023 PCrLJ 1546; Muhammad Hanif v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 173 of 2022, decided 10.1.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. The State etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 173 of 2022, decided 10.1.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Decree: No Revocation, Only Reconciliation
records.heading: A khula decree has no revocation and becomes ineffective only on reconciliation within 90 days
records.text: Section 7(3) MFLO allows revocation of talaq within 90 days, but s. 21(3)(b) of the Family Courts Act, 1964, a non obstante clause, omits revocation. A khula decree becomes ineffective only if within 90 days the spouses reconcile by mutual arrangement. Ref: 2023 CLC 1673.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revision under S. 115 CPC: Concurrent Findings
records.heading: The High Court in revision cannot upset concurrent findings of fact by re-examining evidence
records.text: The High Court in revision cannot upset concurrent findings of fact by re-examining evidence. Interference is justified only where the decision is perverse, suffers a jurisdictional error, or involves misreading or non-reading of evidence and is contrary to law. A mere erroneous decision does not call for interference. Ref: 2023 CLC 1777.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Sham Transfer to Defeat Maintenance Decree
records.heading: A sham transfer to relatives to defeat a maintenance decree did not make a section 12(2) CPC application maintainable
records.text: A transfer by a judgment debtor to close relatives to avoid paying maintenance decreed to his wife and children is a sham transaction. An application under s. 12(2) CPC succeeds only on fraud, misrepresentation or lack of jurisdiction, and non-impleadment alone is insufficient, so the application was not maintainable. Ref: 2023 CLC 1750.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Company and Signatory Liability under S. 489-F PPC
records.heading: A company can be prosecuted under section 489-F PPC, and a signatory is liable only if in charge of operations
records.text: Under s. 11 PPC, 'person' includes a company, and 'whoever' in s. 489-F covers juristic persons, so a company can be prosecuted. The signatory may be liable only if the prosecution proves he was in charge of the company's operations at the time. The offence is not one of strict liability, and dishonesty must be proved. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1588.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Impleading Revenue Officials in Civil Suits
records.heading: Where connivance of revenue officials in a mutation is alleged, the Province and officials are necessary parties
records.text: Impleading revenue officials is not a universal rule and depends on the case. Where connivance of revenue officials in attesting a mutation is alleged in a civil suit, the Province of the Punjab and those officials are necessary parties, as no finding can be recorded against them in their absence. Ref: 2023 LHC 4556; Fatima Noon v. Zain ul Haq Noon etc. (Misc. Writ 12264/22, decided 03.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Fatima Noon v. Zain ul Haq Noon etc. (Misc. Writ 12264/22, decided 03.05.2023)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitration Clause and Cantonments Act Remedies
records.heading: Authority on arbitration agreements under the Arbitration Act 1940 and Cantonments Act remedies, holding not stated
records.text: Authority on arbitration agreements, discussing ss. 16, 19, 30, 32, 33 and 35 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, Art. 4 of the Constitution, and ss. 260 to 265 of the Cantonments Act, 1924. The post lists the provisions discussed without stating the holding. Ref: Cantonment Board Peshawar & another v. M/S Raco Advertiser & another (C.A.1137/2014, decided 13.06.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Cantonment Board Peshawar & another v. M/S Raco Advertiser & another (C.A.1137/2014, decided 13.06.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Double Taxation and Meaning of Royalties
records.heading: Authority on double taxation, the concept of royalties and the rule of interpretation, holding not stated
records.text: Authority on double taxation, the concept of royalties and the rule of interpretation. The post gives the subject only and does not state the holding. Ref: The Commissioner of Income Tax v. M/s. Inter Quest Informatics Services (C.A.94/2008, decided 08.09.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: The Commissioner of Income Tax v. M/s. Inter Quest Informatics Services (C.A.94/2008, decided 08.09.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Audio Leaks Commission: Objection to Bench
records.heading: Federal government objections to the bench hearing the audio leaks commission petition were rejected as lacking legal significance
records.text: The Supreme Court rejected the federal government's objections to the bench hearing the petition against the audio leaks commission. It held that the objections to three judges had no legal significance and that the application against the bench was filed to harass rather than in good faith, and it criticised the government's conduct towards court decisions. Ref: Abid Shahid Zuberi, Advocate Supreme Court of Pakistan, Karachi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Islamabad and others (C.M.A.3932/2023, decided 08.09.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial.
records.title: Abid Shahid Zuberi, Advocate Supreme Court of Pakistan, Karachi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Islamabad and others (C.M.A.3932/2023, decided 08.09.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Writ Jurisdiction in Local Government Election Disputes
records.heading: Authority on High Court writ jurisdiction in local government election disputes, holding not stated
records.text: Authority on the writ jurisdiction of the High Court in election disputes, the expressions coram non judice, per incuriam and functus officio, ss. 37, 38, 39 and 41 of the Balochistan Local Government Act, 2010, ss. 139 and 140 of the Elections Act, 2017 and the Balochistan Local Government (Election) Rules, 2013. No holding is stated in the post. Ref: Jameel Qadir v. Government of Balochistan Local Government Rural Development and Agrovilles Department, Quetta through its Secretary (C.P.2270/2023, decided 27.07.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Jameel Qadir v. Government of Balochistan Local Government Rural Development and Agrovilles Department, Quetta through its Secretary (C.P.2270/2023, decided 27.07.2023)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Addendum to s. 4 Notification: Time and Valuation
records.heading: An addendum to a section 4 notification must issue within reasonable time and before steps in the acquisition
records.text: An addendum or corrigendum to a s. 4 notification under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 must issue within a reasonable time and cannot issue after steps have been taken in furtherance of the acquisition. Compensation under s. 23 is assessed on the market value on the date of the addendum notifying the complete and final land. Ref: (CP 1441 of 2021, decided 11.09.2023).
records.title: (CP 1441 of 2021, decided 11.09.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Conspiracy to Topple Government: Officers' Sentences Upheld
records.heading: Supreme Court maintained the sentences of military officers convicted of conspiring to overthrow the government
records.text: The Supreme Court maintained the sentences of the military officers convicted of involvement in a conspiracy to overthrow the government of former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and dismissed the appeals of the accused. Ref: Ex.Col.Muhammad Azad Minhas v. Federation of Pakistan thr. Secy. M/o Deffence, Rawalpindi (C.A.1191/2016, decided 12.09.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Ex.Col.Muhammad Azad Minhas v. Federation of Pakistan thr. Secy. M/o Deffence, Rawalpindi (C.A.1191/2016, decided 12.09.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Art. 199: Appointment Offered to Different Post
records.heading: Offering a different post from the one applied for violated recruitment terms and the writ was maintainable
records.text: Respondents applied for the post of customer service executive, qualified the test and interview, but were offered data entry operator posts without reason, which violated the recruitment terms. The writ petition was maintainable and the High Court rightly granted relief. Petitions dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 525; National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) through its Chairman, Islamabad and others v. Jawad Khan and 2 others (C.Ps. No. 596 to 598 of 2021, decided 08.05.2023); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) through its Chairman, Islamabad and others v. Jawad Khan and 2 others (C.Ps. No. 596 to 598 of 2021, decided 08.05.2023)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-e-Ishhad Proved: Interference with Concurrent Findings
records.heading: Talb-e-Ishhad was proved, and the High Court had identified no substantial question of law
records.text: Witnesses consistently proved that the right of pre-emption was announced immediately on knowledge of the sale, and the acknowledgement receipt of the notice of Talb-e-Ishhad established timely service. The High Court had identified no substantial question of law in second appeal. Appeal allowed and the Regular Second Appeal remanded for fresh decision. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 562; Muzafar Iqbal v. Mst. Riffat Parveen and others (C.A. No. 307 of 2017, decided 29.03.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muzafar Iqbal v. Mst. Riffat Parveen and others (C.A. No. 307 of 2017, decided 29.03.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A party seeking rejection of a plaint under Order VII Rule 11 must show the law barring the suit
records.text: A party seeking rejection of a plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC must show the law by which the suit is expressly or impliedly barred. The petitioner pointed to no provision of the NAB Ordinance conferring exclusive jurisdiction on the Accountability Court to enforce civil obligations. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 573; Salman Ashraf v. Additional District Judge, Lahore, etc. (C.P. No. 2000-L of 2020, decided 26.05.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Salman Ashraf v. Additional District Judge, Lahore, etc. (C.P. No. 2000-L of 2020, decided 26.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Minor's Property: Agreement Without Court-Appointed Guardian
records.heading: A minor's property cannot be contracted away without a court-appointed guardian, and such a transaction is void
records.text: A minor cannot contract to dispose of property without a guardian appointed by a competent court, and such a transaction is void ab initio. A father not so appointed was incompetent to enter the sale agreements, and suits against minors without a next friend or guardian are not maintainable. Revision dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 705; Muhammad Nadir Khan (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Muhammad Usama and others (C.R. No. 42577 of 2023, decided 22.06.2023); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Nadir Khan (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Muhammad Usama and others (C.R. No. 42577 of 2023, decided 22.06.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 148 CPC: Extension of Time under Conditional Decree
records.heading: Whether the civil court remained seised to extend time under a conditional decree was decided in favour of extension
records.text: The question was whether the civil court, after a conditional decree for specific performance requiring deposit of the balance within ten days failing which the plaintiff would be non-suited, remained seised of the matter and could extend time. Revision allowed, the appellate judgment set aside and the trial court order of 20.12.2016 restored. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 709; Muhammad Bilal and another v. Muhammad Ayub (C.R. No. 388 of 2018/BWP, decided 12.06.2023); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Muhammad Bilal and another v. Muhammad Ayub (C.R. No. 388 of 2018/BWP, decided 12.06.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Caretaker Government: Limits on Major Policy Decisions
records.heading: A caretaker government cannot take major policy decisions on non-urgent matters under section 230(2)(a)
records.text: A caretaker government is restrained from major policy decisions except on urgent matters (s. 230(2)(a) Elections Act, 2017). Suspending the notification of an elected government creating the new district of Wazirabad was a major policy decision on a non-urgent matter. Petitions allowed and the notification of 15.02.2023 set aside. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 714; Ikhlaq Haider Chattha v. Caretaker Chief Minister Punjab and others (W.P. No. 10992 of 2023); Justice Shahid Karim.
records.title: Ikhlaq Haider Chattha v. Caretaker Chief Minister Punjab and others (W.P. No. 10992 of 2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Rent Registrar's Refusal Does Not Bar Ejectment
records.heading: The Rent Registrar's refusal to register a tenancy does not bar the Rent Tribunal from ordering ejectment
records.text: Refusal of the Rent Registrar to register a tenancy agreement or to reduce an oral tenancy into writing does not preclude the Rent Tribunal from entertaining a landlord's ejectment application under the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 719; Khurram Shahzad v. Zeeshan Nawaz, etc. (W.P. No. 31543 of 2021, decided 16.06.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Khurram Shahzad v. Zeeshan Nawaz, etc. (W.P. No. 31543 of 2021, decided 16.06.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. II R. 2 CPC: Second Suit on Same Cause of Action
records.heading: A second suit on the same cause of action was barred by Order II Rule 2 CPC
records.text: Both suits concerned the right of inheritance and its denial, and the petitioners could have sought the relief of declaration in the first suit. The second suit challenging the family settlement was therefore barred by O. II R. 2 CPC. The result of the order of the Additional District Judge was right and the writ petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 735; Kamila Aamir and another v. Additional District & Session Judge and others (W.P. No. 27395 of 2021, decided 19.06.2023); Justice Shams Mehmood Mirza.
records.title: Kamila Aamir and another v. Additional District & Session Judge and others (W.P. No. 27395 of 2021, decided 19.06.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Wheat Quota: No Vested Right of Mill Owners
records.heading: Flour mill owners have no vested right to an enhanced wheat quota, which is an executive policy matter
records.text: Flour mill owners have no vested right to an enhanced wheat quota. Fixation of quota is an executive policy function, and the court in constitutional jurisdiction cannot abridge the executive's power to frame policy. Art. 18 does not extend to promoting the business of mill owners. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 764; Muhammad Ibrar, etc. v. Government of Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 940 of 2023, decided 11.07.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Ibrar, etc. v. Government of Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 940 of 2023, decided 11.07.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: S. 11(1) and 11(6) Sales Tax Act: No Inconsistency
records.heading: Sections 11(1) and 11(6) of the Sales Tax Act 1990 are not inconsistent as they serve different purposes
records.text: Section 11(1) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 can be invoked only against a registered person required to file a return. There is no apparent inconsistency between s. 11(1) and s. 11(6), which serve different purposes, so the plea based on the non obstante clause failed. Petition dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 771; M/s. Abdullah Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Federation of Pakistan, etc. (W.P. No. 42272 of 2023, decided 21.06.2023); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: M/s. Abdullah Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Federation of Pakistan, etc. (W.P. No. 42272 of 2023, decided 21.06.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Better Class Facility for Under-Trial Prisoner
records.heading: Better class facility to an under-trial prisoner cannot be denied by misapplying Rule 242 of the Prison Rules
records.text: The Prison Rules contain no express restriction on under-trial prisoners seeking better class facility. Rule 242(2)(c)(v) Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978 covers s. 395 PPC but not s. 7 Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, so its application was a misapplication of law and discriminatory where similarly placed prisoners received the facility. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 777; Rabia Sultan v. Province of Punjab and 2 others (W.P. No. 43904 of 2023, decided 06.07.2023); Justice Ali Baqar Najafi; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Rabia Sultan v. Province of Punjab and 2 others (W.P. No. 43904 of 2023, decided 06.07.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 426(1A)(c) CrPC: Statutory Right to Suspension of Sentence
records.heading: Proviso (c) to section 426(1A) CrPC gives a statutory right to bail where an appeal is pending over four years
records.text: Where a convict's appeal has remained pending for more than four years without his fault, proviso (c) to s. 426(1A) CrPC gives him a statutory right to release on bail. The sentence was suspended and he was released on bail, petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 806; Sajid alias Saji v. State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 241575-J of 2018, decided 10.04.2023); Justice Muhammad Ameer Bhatti.
records.title: Sajid alias Saji v. State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 241575-J of 2018, decided 10.04.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Superdari of Vehicle Declared Tampered
records.heading: A purchaser who buys a vehicle without due care is not a bona fide purchaser and superdari was refused
records.text: A purchaser who bought a vehicle without due care and compliance with law cannot claim to be a bona fide purchaser and at most can claim damages from his seller. The vehicle had been found tampered by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency. Petition under s. 561-A CrPC for superdari dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 808; Ahmad Ali v. Additional Sessions Judge, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60827-M of 2022, decided 17.04.2023); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Ahmad Ali v. Additional Sessions Judge, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60827-M of 2022, decided 17.04.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: S. 7 CNSA: Transportation Requires Permit under Rules
records.heading: Transporting narcotics under section 7 CNSA requires a permit under the Rules
records.text: Section 7 CNSA prohibits transportation of narcotic drugs except in conformity with rules under s. 7(2) and any required permit, and contravention is an offence under s. 9. The Control of Narcotic Substances Rules 2001 required a permit for transporting ketamine, and although SRO 1350(I)/2021 was not retrospective the petitioner had to comply with the Rules. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 814; Liaquat Ali v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 7517/B of 2023, decided 29.03.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Liaquat Ali v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 7517/B of 2023, decided 29.03.2023)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Admissibility of DNA Evidence: Arts. 59 and 164 QSO
records.heading: DNA evidence is admissible as expert opinion under Articles 59 and 164 QSO
records.text: DNA evidence is evaluated under Arts. 59 and 164 QSO, the former making expert opinion relevant and the latter allowing evidence from modern devices and techniques. A technician conducting DNA examination is an expert whose opinion is admissible, and s. 9(3) Punjab Forensic Science Agency Act, 2007 reaffirms this. The judgment also notes the risk of sample contamination. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 824; Muhammad Imran alias Aamir v. State (Crl. A. No. 462 & M.R No. 17 of 2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Imran alias Aamir v. State (Crl. A. No. 462 & M.R No. 17 of 2022)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 7 ATA: Relationship with Substantive Offence
records.heading: Section 7 ATA is ancillary to the substantive offence, and the prosecution failed to prove it
records.text: The provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 are co-related and ancillary to the substantive offence, here s. 302 PPC, and the gravity of that offence guides whether the Act is attracted. As a special law it must be read in light of its own object. The court found that the prosecution had not proved the offences under s. 7. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 857; Khateeb Hussain and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 43-ATA, 34-ATA & C.S.R. No. 2 of 2021); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Khateeb Hussain and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 43-ATA, 34-ATA & C.S.R. No. 2 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Failure to Prove Motive: ss. 302(b) and 324 PPC
records.heading: An unproved motive and a witness shown to have arrived after the occurrence weakened the prosecution case
records.text: The alleged motive concerning a dispute over watering of lands was not proved, as the complainant produced no documentary evidence and the Investigating Officer admitted that motive could not be proved. One prosecution witness who claimed presence at the occurrence was shown to have arrived after it was complete. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 895; Muhammad Shahbaz and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 254 of 2021, 729-J of 2017, 36 of 2018 and M.R No. 09 of 2021); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Shahbaz and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 254 of 2021, 729-J of 2017, 36 of 2018 and M.R No. 09 of 2021)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift by Brother to Sister: Proof of Offer and Acceptance
records.heading: A gift from a brother to a sister fails without reliable proof of offer, acceptance and mutation
records.text: A gift from a brother to his sister was not proved where there was no reliable evidence of offer and acceptance, apart from an admission of possession. Proof of the revenue entry cannot substitute proof of the original transaction, and the mutation was not proved in line with Art. 79 QSO as only one witness was examined. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1645.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Entries: Scope and Evidentiary Value
records.heading: A mutation carries no presumption of correctness and is not a document of title
records.text: Mutation is sanctioned in summary proceedings to keep the record updated under s. 42 Land Revenue Act, 1967. It carries no presumption of correctness before incorporation in the record of rights and must be independently proved by affirmative evidence. A mutation is not itself a document of title and cannot vest title in immovable property. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1645.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Adna Maliks under MLR 1959: Contradictory Stance
records.heading: Appellants cannot claim tenants and self-cultivation at once, and rights had accrued to respondents as Adna Maliks
records.text: Appellants claimed that the respondents were their tenants while also claiming before the High Court to be self-cultivating the land, a contradictory stance. The Jamabandi of 1943-44 predated MLR 1959, so rights had accrued to the respondents as Adna Maliks before it. The suit for declaration was rightly decreed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1635.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Trials of Civilians under Army Act: Formation of Bench
records.heading: Authority on trials of civilians under the Army Act and on the formation of the bench
records.text: Authority on the constitutionality of trials of civilians under the Pakistan Army Act, 1952, and on the formation of the bench, including non-consultation of the two senior most judges, delay in petitions against the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023, special benches and a judge's recusal. Observations of bench members on the constitution of the bench are noted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1732.

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Counsel Misleading the Court: Costs
records.heading: Counsel who misleads the Court on an earlier decision was ordered to pay costs
records.text: Counsel for the review petitioner twice claimed that the matter had been decided in an earlier round of litigation, which was incorrect and amounted to misrepresentation. The review petition was dismissed with costs of Rs. 10,000 under O. XVII R. 12 and O. XXVIII R. 3 Supreme Court Rules, 1980, to be paid by counsel to a charitable organisation. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1709.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Objections to Liability Close after Limitation
records.heading: Objections to liability and its discharge close after the limitation period lapses
