records.text: All objections regarding liability and its discharge come to a close after the lapse of the limitation period. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1660.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 5 Limitation Act: Condonation of Delay Discretionary
records.heading: The power to condone delay under section 5 of the Limitation Act is discretionary
records.text: The power to condone delay and extend time under s. 5 of the Limitation Act is discretionary. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1665.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay in Connected Petition
records.heading: Delay of seven days was condoned in a petition connected with others raising the same question of law
records.text: Where several connected civil petitions for leave to appeal raised the same question of law, the Supreme Court condoned the delay of seven days in one of them on the ground that it was a connected petition. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1716.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Production of Documents Before Trial
records.heading: An accused may apply under section 94 CrPC for production of a document before the defence stage
records.text: Even before the trial begins or the defence is entered, an accused may apply under s. 94 CrPC for production of a document not covered by s. 265-C that is necessary or desirable for the inquiry or trial, despite s. 265-F(7). Section 94 sets no limit on the stage of exercise. Appeal partly allowed and the respondent's application remitted for fresh decision. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1676; The State v. Chaudhry Muhammad Usman (Criminal Petition No. 112 of 2020).
records.title: The State v. Chaudhry Muhammad Usman (Criminal Petition No. 112 of 2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Non-Prohibitory Clause: Bail the Rule
records.heading: For offences outside the prohibitory clause of section 497 CrPC, bail is the rule
records.text: For offences not falling within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, grant of bail is the rule and refusal an exception. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1773.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Theft and Receiving Stolen Property
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail granted for purchase of stolen articles where the FIR was delayed and co-accused were on bail
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was granted where the FIR was delayed by 13 days, the only allegation was purchase of stolen articles, co-accused had post-arrest bail and the maximum punishment under s. 411 PPC does not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Mere allegation of huge loss is no ground to refuse bail. Appeal allowed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1773.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Murderous Assault: Bail Refused
records.heading: Bail refused in a murderous assault where a specific role was ascribed and a common object could not be ruled out
records.text: Bail was refused where a specific role was ascribed to the petitioner in the ocular account, all accused were armed with firearms, a common object could not be ruled out, and the one day delay in the FIR was not fatal. A co-accused with a similar role was refused pre-arrest bail. The alibi plea lacked proper details. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1724.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Registration of Other Cases Inconsequential
records.heading: Registration of another criminal case does not disentitle an accused with a prima facie case to bail
records.text: Mere registration of another criminal case against an accused does not disentitle him to bail if on merits he has a prima facie case. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1712.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Non-Prohibitory Offences: Further Inquiry, Pre-Arrest Bail Confirmed
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail was confirmed in a delayed theft case as one of further inquiry
records.text: Grant of bail in offences outside the prohibitory clause is the rule. In a theft case with an FIR delayed over three months, a co-accused in a similar role on bail and an elderly female accused, the case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC as one of further inquiry. Ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1729.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Court May Touch Merits
records.heading: The court may touch upon the merits of the case while granting pre-arrest bail
records.text: While granting pre-arrest bail, the court may touch upon the merits of the case. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1712, 2023 SCMR 1729, 2023 SCMR 1773.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: A Single Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single doubt suffices, and its benefit must go to the accused
records.text: For an accused to be given the benefit of doubt it is not necessary that many circumstances create uncertainty. If there is only one doubt, its benefit must go to the accused. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1698, 2023 SCMR 1791.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Poppy Straw: Only Doda Contains Narcotic
records.heading: Only the doda contains the narcotic in poppy straw, and the unproved recovery raised doubt
records.text: Relying on Taimoor Khan (2016 SCMR 621) and Muhammad Imran (2011 SCMR 1954), only the basket, sack or pouch (doda), excluding seeds, contains narcotic substance, and poppy straw is not necessarily doda. The prosecution did not show what was recovered or how much was doda, which raised doubt. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and the petitioner acquitted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1791, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 45; Barkhurdar v. The State, etc (Crl.P.733-L/2018); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Barkhurdar v. The State, etc (Crl.P.733-L/2018)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Implausible Version and Inconclusive DNA
records.heading: A rape victim's implausible account and an inconclusive DNA report led to reappraisal in the accused's favour
records.text: On reappraisal in a s. 376 PPC case, the victim's account that she was made unconscious and raped in front of the accused's mother and sisters was held implausible. No intoxicant was recovered or found in her blood, and the DNA report was inconclusive and showed her allegation was not entirely true. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1698.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Sole Testimony of Rape Victim
records.heading: Courts may convict on the sole testimony of a sexual assault victim if it is independent and straightforward
records.text: Absent compelling reasons, courts may convict on the sole testimony of a victim of sexual assault, provided it is independent, unbiased and straightforward. If the court finds her version difficult to accept, it may seek corroboration from evidence lending assurance to it. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1698.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Report in Rape Cases: Corroboration Only
records.heading: A DNA report in a rape case is not primary evidence and serves only for corroboration
records.text: In a s. 376 PPC case, a DNA report cannot be treated as primary evidence and can be relied upon only for corroboration. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1698.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ss. 96 and 100 CPC: Appellate Judgments
records.heading: Appellate judgments must state points and reasons, and section 100 CPC covers only substantial questions of law
records.text: An appellate judgment must state the points for determination and the reasons for the decision (O. XLI CPC). The High Court's jurisdiction under s. 100 CPC is to decide substantial questions of law and not pure questions of fact, which distinguishes it from appellate jurisdiction under s. 96. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1652.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NAB Amendments: Maintainability and Voided Provisions
records.heading: The NAB amendments on the monetary threshold and public office holder exceptions were declared void ab initio
records.text: The petition was held maintainable for violation of Arts. 9, 14, 24 and 25. The Rs. 500 million threshold inserted in s. 5(o) NAB Ordinance and the exceptions for holders of public office added to s. 4 were declared void ab initio as regards references against elected holders of public office and persons in the service of Pakistan. Justice Mansoor Ali Shah recorded a dissenting note. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const.P.21/2022, decided 15.09.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const.P.21/2022, decided 15.09.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NAB Amendments: Dissent on Parliament's Legislative Power
records.heading: In dissent, what Parliament has done it can undo, as its legislative power is never exhausted
records.text: In his dissenting note, Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah observed that what Parliament has done it can undo, and its legislative power is never exhausted. If Parliament can enact the NAB law, it can repeal the entire law or amend it. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const.P.21/2022, decided 15.09.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const.P.21/2022, decided 15.09.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Preferred over Site Plan and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Reliable ocular evidence prevails over the site plan and medical evidence where they conflict
records.text: Where ocular witnesses contradict the distance in the site plan, the witnesses prevail, since a site plan is not substantive evidence. Ocular account is the principal evidence and expert evidence is confirmatory, so a conflict with medical evidence on the number of injuries is resolved in favour of reliable ocular testimony. Ref: Muhammad Hanif v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 528 of 2019 in Jail Petition No. 327 of 2018, decided 05.09.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 528 of 2019 in Jail Petition No. 327 of 2018, decided 05.09.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Physical Remand: Detention Without Formal Arrest
records.heading: A remand order was set aside where detenus were held without formal arrest and the application omitted arrest details
records.text: Where detenus were held at the police station without formal arrest and the application for physical remand omitted the rapat number, date and time of arrest, the remand order was set aside under s. 561-A CrPC. One detenu was discharged and the other given protective bail. Directions were issued to the IGP Punjab, DG Anti-Corruption and DG FIA to frame a mechanism on case diaries. Ref: 2023 LHC 4601; Mst. Nasreen Bibi v. DPO etc. (W.P. 6566-23, decided 08.09.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Mst. Nasreen Bibi v. DPO etc. (W.P. 6566-23, decided 08.09.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 203: Protection of District Judiciary
records.heading: High Courts must protect the district judiciary from executive intrusion under Article 203
records.text: The High Courts' duty to protect district judges is inherent in their power of supervision and control under Art. 203 of the Constitution, and they must protect the district judiciary from executive intrusion that weakens its independence. An additional note prescribes safeguards for district judges in relation to criminal cases. Ref: Sultan Ahmed v. Registrar, Balochistan High Court, Quetta and others (Crl.A.633/2019, decided 07.06.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Sultan Ahmed v. Registrar, Balochistan High Court, Quetta and others (Crl.A.633/2019, decided 07.06.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Revision Against Magistrate's Remand Order
records.heading: A Magistrate's order on physical remand is judicial and can be challenged by revision before the Sessions Judge
records.text: An order of a Magistrate refusing remand is a judicial function, and under s. 435 CrPC the superior court may exercise revisional jurisdiction. In anti-corruption cases, a challenge to the Judicial Magistrate's grant or refusal of physical remand lies by revision before the Sessions Judge. The Special Judge's jurisdiction under s. 4 Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is also discussed. Ref: Parvez Elahi v. Additional Sessions Judge and 3 others (Crl. Misc. No. 40242-M of 2023).
records.title: Parvez Elahi v. Additional Sessions Judge and 3 others (Crl. Misc. No. 40242-M of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance: Constructive Possession of Heirs
records.heading: An heir in possession holds constructive possession for all heirs, and relinquishment needs a positive act
records.text: Under Islamic law succession opens on the owner's death, and a wrong mutation confers no right as revenue record serves fiscal purposes. An heir in possession is in constructive possession for all heirs, so brothers' possession is that of their sisters unless there is express repudiation. Relinquishment of an interest needs a positive and affirmative act. Ref: Noor Din deceased through LRs v. Peruaiz Akhtar & others (Civil Appeal No. 130 of 2016, decided 01.08.2023).
records.title: Noor Din deceased through LRs v. Peruaiz Akhtar & others (Civil Appeal No. 130 of 2016, decided 01.08.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Foreigners Act: Asylum Seeker Fleeing Afghanistan
records.heading: A person who comes to Pakistan to save her life cannot be prosecuted for lack of a visa
records.text: The Islamabad High Court accepted the petition and quashed the FIR registered under s. 14 Foreigners Act against an Afghan Hazara woman who entered without a visa. She had strong evidence of grave and immediate threat to her life after the Taliban takeover, verified by UNHCR. A person who comes to Pakistan to save life cannot be prosecuted for lack of a visa. Ref: Rahil Azizi v. The State & others (Writ Petition No. 1666 of 2023); Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Rahil Azizi v. The State & others (Writ Petition No. 1666 of 2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Stare Decisis and Binding Precedent
records.heading: Courts should honour prior decisions, with vertical stare decisis stronger than horizontal
records.text: Courts should honour prior decisions on the same subject to maintain harmony and uniformity. Under vertical stare decisis decisions of higher courts take precedence over lower courts, while horizontal stare decisis, binding courts at the same level, is generally less forceful. The doctrine of binding precedent rests on public policy. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad v. Mr. Fazal-e-Subhan & others (C.P.2314/2022, decided 30.05.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad v. Mr. Fazal-e-Subhan & others (C.P.2314/2022, decided 30.05.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: PEEDA: Essential Elements of Show Cause Notice
records.heading: A PEEDA show cause notice must contain the prescribed elements, or the right to a defence is frustrated
records.text: A show cause notice under PEEDA must be in writing, state the charge with date, place and responsibility, quote the clause of PEEDA, indicate the proposed penalty, give the time for a written explanation, bear the competent authority's signature and state the time, date and place of inquiry with the inquiry officer's name. Failure frustrates the right to a defence and fair trial. Ref: Sanaullah Sani v. Secretary Education Schools, Government of Punjab, School Education Department, Lahore & another (C.P.1276/2020, decided 17.08.2023); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Sanaullah Sani v. Secretary Education Schools, Government of Punjab, School Education Department, Lahore & another (C.P.1276/2020, decided 17.08.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proving Fraud and Collusion
records.heading: A person alleging fraud, cheating or collusiveness must prove it
records.text: A person who alleges fraud, cheating or collusiveness is required to prove it. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 628.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Roznamcha Entries and Mutation: Mode of Proof
records.heading: Roznamcha entries not proved to be made at the vendor's instance carry no evidentiary value
records.text: Under s. 42 Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 an acquisition of right is reported to the Patwari, recorded in the Roznamcha and entered in the register of mutations. Entries in the Roznamcha not proved to have been made at the instance of the vendor or signed by him carry no evidentiary value. Ref: Nazeer Ahmad v. Muhammad Sadiq (deceased) through L.Rs. and 2 others (C.R. No. 174/2017, decided 15.09.2023).
records.title: Nazeer Ahmad v. Muhammad Sadiq (deceased) through L.Rs. and 2 others (C.R. No. 174/2017, decided 15.09.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Consumer Court: Nature of Appeal
records.heading: The nature of an appeal from a Consumer Court depends on whether the proceeding is civil or criminal
records.text: Proceedings before a Consumer Court may be civil or criminal, and this determines the nature of the appeal. If the proceeding is based on s. 32(1) of the Punjab Act, the appeal is criminal, and in other cases it is civil. Ref: Shaista Jamil v. Daraz and another (Criminal Appeal No. 559/2023).
records.title: Shaista Jamil v. Daraz and another (Criminal Appeal No. 559/2023)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 21-E ATA: Physical Remand Discretionary
records.heading: Physical remand under section 21-E ATA is discretionary, not mandatory, and needs recorded reasons
records.text: Under s. 21-E ATA the grant of physical remand is discretionary, not mandatory, and cannot be granted routinely. The remand period should be as short as possible, and the Special Court, deemed a Magistrate, must record reasons under s. 167(3) CrPC and not act as a post office. The remand granted by the ATC was upheld. Ref: 2023 LHC 4674; State v. Muswar Hussain Shah, etc. (Crl. Revision No. 57693/2023, decided 14.09.2023).
records.title: State v. Muswar Hussain Shah, etc. (Crl. Revision No. 57693/2023, decided 14.09.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Second Petition After Withdrawal Without Permission
records.heading: A second petition after withdrawal without permission and with concealment disentitles the petitioner to relief under Article 199
records.text: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC applies mutatis mutandis to constitutional petitions. A second petition filed at a High Court bench after withdrawal of the first without the required permission, with concealment of the circumstances of withdrawal, disentitles the petitioners to discretionary relief under Art. 199. Petition dismissed in limine with costs of Rs. 100,000. Ref: 2023 MLD 1611.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Roznamcha and Mutation Require Independent Proof
records.heading: A transaction in the Roznamcha and a mutation must each be independently proved
records.text: A transaction recorded in the Roznamcha and a mutation must be independently proved. Under s. 42 Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 acquisitions are reported to the Patwari and entered in the Roznamcha and mutation register, and entries not proved to have been made at the vendor's instance or signed by him carry no evidentiary value. Ref: Nazeer Ahmad v. Muhammad Sadiq (deceased) through L.Rs. and 2 others (C.R. No. 174/2017, decided 15.09.2023).
records.title: Nazeer Ahmad v. Muhammad Sadiq (deceased) through L.Rs. and 2 others (C.R. No. 174/2017, decided 15.09.2023)

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Harassment under s. 2(h) Workplace Harassment Act
records.heading: Harassment under section 2(h) includes sex-based discrimination affecting the workplace, not only sexual advances
records.text: Harassment under s. 2(h) Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 is not limited to sexual advances and includes sex-based discrimination that affects the workplace environment and interferes with the victim's work. Justice Yahya Afridi described sexually demeaning attitudes as harassment rooted in gender-based discrimination. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 588; Justice Ayesha A. Malik; Justice Yahya Afridi.

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Harassment: Victim's Perspective and Reasonable Woman Standard
records.heading: In harassment cases the reasonable woman standard and the victim's perspective apply
records.text: In harassment cases the victim's perspective is relevant, rather than the notion of acceptable behaviour. The standard of a reasonable woman applies to decide whether the workplace was rendered hostile, with all factors viewed objectively and subjectively. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 588.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Officer's Undisclosed Opinion on Cause of Death
records.heading: An undisclosed medical opinion on the cause of death, given first in court, could not be considered
records.text: The Medical Officer prepared the postmortem report a month later, gave no official opinion on cause of death in it and recorded no time of death. His exaggerated court version of death by firearm could not be considered, as the accused was unaware of that opinion and had not been given a copy. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 518, 2023 YLR 2207; Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Hoe, Shoes and Pistol Without Forensic Support
records.heading: Recoveries not forensically tested or doubtful added no quality to the prosecution case
records.text: Recovery of a hoe and shoes was of no avail as they were not sent for testing, and the pistol recovery was doubtful because police had visited the place earlier, only a functionality report existed and no casings were collected. The recovery added no quality to the prosecution case. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 518, 2023 YLR 2207; Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Forensic Parcels
records.heading: Safe transmission of parcels to the Forensic Science Agency was not established
records.text: Safe transmission of parcels from the Medical Officer to the Forensic Science Agency was not established, as the Investigating Officer did not depose to depositing the parcels despite appearing twice as a witness. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 518, 2023 YLR 2207; Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Tayyab and another v. State and another (Crl. A. 778, 492 & M.R. 55 of 2018, heard 25.10.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Reliable and Credible Evidence
records.heading: Reliability and credibility of evidence differ, as examined in the law on circumstantial evidence
records.text: Reliable and credible evidence differ, as reliability depends on the capacity of a witness to depose, legality of processes and competency, whereas credibility touches the character of the witness. The Urdu note describes the Lahore High Court decision as a detailed discussion of the definition, guiding principles and legal requirements of circumstantial evidence in criminal cases. Ref: 2023 YLR 2207, PLJ 2023 CrC 518.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 59 and 84 QSO: Comparison of Thumb Impressions
records.heading: Refusing comparison of disputed thumb impressions and signatures under Articles 59 and 84 QSO negates justice
records.text: Arts. 59 and 84 QSO are enabling provisions where the genuineness of signatures or thumb impressions is disputed. Refusal to allow comparison of thumb impressions and signatures amounts to negation of justice. Reports of fingerprint and handwriting experts remain open to objection by either side. Ref: 2023 YLR 2304.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Fraud Against Registered Tamleek Deed: Proof and Necessary Parties
records.heading: Bare allegation of fraud against a registered deed fails, and necessary parties had to be impleaded
records.text: A plaintiff alleging fraud against a registered tamleek deed without particulars, relying only on his self-serving statement, failed to discharge his onus. The Province and Sub-Registrar were necessary parties but were not impleaded, and bare words cannot dislodge the presumption for a registered document. Concurrent judgments were set aside and the matter remanded to the Trial Court. Ref: 2023 YLR 2304.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Appeal Not Against All Decree-Holders: Minor Not Impleaded
records.heading: A defendant who appealed a maintenance decree without impleading the minor was taken to admit the findings for the minor
records.text: A defendant who appealed against a Family Court maintenance decree without making the minor a respondent was taken to have admitted the findings in favour of the minor, and could not later claim before the High Court that he had challenged the decree as a whole. Ref: 2023 YLR 2233.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor: Poverty of Father
records.heading: The father's poverty is no ground to interfere with a reasonable maintenance decree for a minor
records.text: Mere poverty of the father, a driver without stable income, is no ground to interfere with a Family Court decree for maintenance of Rs. 10,000 per month, which was neither exorbitant nor unreasonable given inflation. Constitutional petition dismissed. Ref: 2023 YLR 2233.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Striking Off Defence for Non-Payment of Interim Maintenance
records.heading: Striking off a defence for non-payment of interim maintenance arrears was upheld
records.text: A defendant has no vested right to multiple opportunities to comply with an order to pay arrears of interim maintenance. Striking off his defence for non-compliance was upheld, and non-compliance disentitled him to discretionary relief from the High Court. Ref: 2023 YLR 2233.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: QSO Applies to Criminal Proceedings Before Family Court
records.heading: The Qanun-e-Shahadat applies to criminal proceedings before the Family Court under Part II or section 20
records.text: Section 17(1) Family Courts Act, 1964 excludes the Qanun-e-Shahadat only for matters in Part I of the Schedule. It does not apply to criminal proceedings for offences in Part II or s. 20, including s. 6(5) Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, so the Qanun-e-Shahadat, 1984 applies in such proceedings. Ref: 2023 YLR 2140.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court as Judicial Magistrate: Polygamy Offence
records.heading: The Family Court is deemed a Judicial Magistrate for offences under the MFLO, including a second marriage without permission
records.text: Section 20 Family Courts Act, 1964 deems the Family Court a Judicial Magistrate of the first class for cognizance and trial of offences including those under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. Cognizance is on complaint of the Union Council, Arbitration Council or aggrieved party, and trial follows the summary procedure of Chapter XXII CrPC. Contracting a second marriage without Arbitration Council permission is an offence under s. 6. Ref: 2023 YLR 2140.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence at Appeal
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal cannot fill lacunae, and unexplained delay of ten years defeated the application
records.text: O. XLI R. 27 CPC does not allow additional evidence to fill lacunae or supply a party's deficiency, and gives no unfettered discretion. A petitioner who sought to produce 39 documents after ten years of litigation and failed to explain the delay did not satisfy the court, and discretion is not exercised for a party who remained indolent. Ref: 2023 YLR 2364.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification of Dead Body Not Proved
records.heading: Failure to prove the identity of the skeleton as the deceased meant the charge was not proved
records.text: The prosecution failed to prove the identity of the skeleton as the deceased. The DNA report lost its efficacy, the complainant and witness did not depose to identifying the body, and the identification of clothes was in doubt through interpolation. When the basic fact in issue was not proved, further material could not be used, and the charge was not proved beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2207.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 120 Limitation Act: Declaration Suit Time-Barred
records.heading: A declaration suit is governed by Article 120 with a six year period, and the court must examine limitation itself
records.text: A suit for declaration is governed by Art. 120 Limitation Act, 1908 with a six year period, and under s. 3 the court must examine limitation even if no party raises it. A suit founded on an agreement to sell from a non-title holder is not maintainable. Revision dismissed and the plaint rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC. Ref: 2023 CLC 1725.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account: Omissions in Police Memos and Panic of Witnesses
records.heading: Omissions in police memos are mere slackness and do not affect strong, consistent ocular evidence
records.text: Omission of the accused's name against the word Banam in some documents is at most slackness by the police and does not affect strong, consistent ocular evidence, as the Police Rules, 1934 prescribe no format for spot recovery memos. A witness in panic cannot be expected to state each accused's role with photographic precision. Ref: 2023 YLR 2120.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Common Intention under s. 38 PPC
records.heading: Common intention under section 38 PPC turns on the material role played by each accused
records.text: The judgment discusses common intention and vicarious liability under s. 38 PPC, holding that since each person may act or withdraw differently, reflexes cannot be punished and the touchstone is the material role played by each accused during the occurrence. Ref: 2023 YLR 2120.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Female Minor Aged 10 to 15
records.heading: A girl's preference for her father cannot alone decide custody, and the mother's second marriage is no sole bar
records.text: A minor's preference for the father cannot be the sole criterion of welfare, especially for a girl aged 10 to 15, who needs her natural mother most given puberty and privacy. A mother's second marriage is not the sole ground to deprive her of custody, and nothing on record showed a disability of the mother. Ref: 2023 LHC 4682; Kamran Saeed v. ASJ Mianwali etc. (WP 15564/23, decided 13.09.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Kamran Saeed v. ASJ Mianwali etc. (WP 15564/23, decided 13.09.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Police Recruitment: Candidate Acquitted After FIR
records.heading: A police candidate cannot be debarred merely because an FIR was registered and ended in acquittal
records.text: A candidate for police employment cannot be debarred merely because an FIR was registered after his application, particularly where he was acquitted by a competent court. Registration of an FIR does not make a person guilty, and a judicial finding on the non-constitution of an offence carries more authority than the investigation's finding of guilt. Ref: 2023 LHC 4701; Syed Ali Hassan Naqvi v. Senior Superintendent of Police etc. (WP 50582/22, decided 12.09.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Syed Ali Hassan Naqvi v. Senior Superintendent of Police etc. (WP 50582/22, decided 12.09.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Police Official on Deputation to FIA: Disciplinary Power
records.heading: A police official on deputation to the FIA stays a civil servant and the parent department may take disciplinary action
records.text: A police official on deputation to the FIA remains a civil servant under s. 2(1)(b) Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974, particularly where the misconduct does not relate to duties assigned by the borrowing agency. Rule 11 of the Police Rules (E&D) Rules, 1975 delegates suspension and proceedings to the borrowing agency but does not prevent the parent department from initiating disciplinary proceedings. Ref: 2023 LHC 4690; Muzammal Hayat v. IGP Punjab Lahore etc. (WP 42703/23, decided 26.09.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muzammal Hayat v. IGP Punjab Lahore etc. (WP 42703/23, decided 26.09.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Locus Poenitentiae: Withdrawal of Health Allowance
records.heading: Locus poenitentiae barred unilateral withdrawal of a health allowance that conferred a vested right
records.text: Payment of health allowance conferred a vested right, so the executive was barred by locus poenitentiae from unilaterally rescinding it. Withdrawal of pay protection was declared without lawful authority and of no legal effect, with both parties bound by the contract terms settled between them. Ref: 2023 PLC (C.S.) 1176.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 42 Specific Relief Act: Pre-Existing Right Required
records.heading: No decree for declaration of ownership under section 42 can be passed without a pre-existing right or title
records.text: Without a pre-existing right or title, no decree for declaration of ownership can be passed under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Ref: 2023 LHC 4751; PMDC v. Govt of Punjab etc. (Civil Revision 506-09, decided 05.09.2023); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: PMDC v. Govt of Punjab etc. (Civil Revision 506-09, decided 05.09.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Evidence Led After Closure of Plaintiff's Evidence
records.heading: Further evidence led by a plaintiff after closing his evidence without permission is liable to be ignored
records.text: Where the plaintiff tendered only documents and closed affirmative evidence without reserving a right to lead more, and the defendant's right was then closed under O. XVII R. 3 CPC without adverse evidence, any further evidence led by the plaintiff without the court's permission is liable to be ignored. Ref: 2023 LHC 4751; PMDC v. Govt of Punjab etc. (Civil Revision 506-09, decided 05.09.2023); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: PMDC v. Govt of Punjab etc. (Civil Revision 506-09, decided 05.09.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Early Rejection and Date of Knowledge of Fraud
records.heading: Order VII Rule 11 CPC ends incompetent suits early, and the date of knowledge of fraud must be pleaded and proved
records.text: The object of O. VII R. 11 CPC is to end an incompetent suit at inception, and the court must examine the plaint thoroughly at the outset. The date of knowledge of alleged fraud must be explicitly pleaded and proved, which was lacking in this case. Ref: 2023 LHC 4763; Muhammad Yasin v. Muhammad Ismail etc. (Civil Revision 62703/23, decided 26.09.2023); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Yasin v. Muhammad Ismail etc. (Civil Revision 62703/23, decided 26.09.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Service Benefits as Tarkah
records.heading: A service benefit due in the employee's lifetime forms part of his tarkah and is inheritable
records.text: A service benefit due or payable to an employee in his lifetime forms part of his tarkah and is inheritable by all legal heirs per personal law. A benefit not fallen due in his lifetime, or in the nature of a grant or compensation, goes only to those entitled under the service rules or applicable law, which must not conflict with Shariah. Ref: PLD 2023 Sindh 321.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Tarkah: Nominee and Scope of Estate
records.heading: Only property owned by the deceased forms tarkah, and a nominee is merely a trustee
records.text: Only property owned by the deceased at death, or to which he had acquired an absolute right in law during his lifetime, forms tarkah and is inheritable. A nominee confers no title and is merely a trustee, so nomination does not entitle the nominee to take tarkah exclusively. Ref: PLD 2023 Sindh 321.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Sugar Price Control: Provincial Competence
records.heading: Price control of sugar and essential foodstuffs lies within provincial legislative competence
records.text: The power to fix prices of sugar and essential foodstuffs lies with the provincial government, and legislation on price control is for the Provincial Assembly. The 1977 Act was declared ultra vires the powers of Parliament to the extent it applies to price control. The petitions and the intra-court appeal were allowed. Ref: 2023 LHC 4778; Ms Hamza Sugar Mills Pvt Ltd etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Misc. Writ 61692/21, decided 05.10.2023); Justice Shahid Karim.
records.title: Ms Hamza Sugar Mills Pvt Ltd etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Misc. Writ 61692/21, decided 05.10.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Decree Holder Includes Successful Defendant
records.heading: A successful defendant in whose favour rights are determined is also a decree holder
records.text: A decree conclusively determines the rights of the parties, whether plaintiff or defendant. A defendant in whose favour rights are determined is therefore also a decree holder and may execute the decree. A narrow reading confined to plaintiffs would force repeated adjudication. Ref: Saif-ur-Rehman v. Ijaz and another (C.A.1573/2017, decided 20.09.2023); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Saif-ur-Rehman v. Ijaz and another (C.A.1573/2017, decided 20.09.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Succession to Tenancy under Colonization Act
records.heading: A widow succeeds to the tenancy under section 20 of the Colonization Act in the absence of male descendants
records.text: Under s. 20 of the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912, a widow succeeds to the tenancy in the absence of male lineal descendants, holding a limited estate until death or remarriage. Daughters succeed only under clause (c) when no male descendant or widow survives. A mutation sanctioned to the exclusion of legal heirs was a waste paper contrary to Shariah. Ref: 2023 LHC 4826; Mst. Saddan v. Muhammad Yousaf etc (Civil Revision 270-97, decided 20.09.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Mst. Saddan v. Muhammad Yousaf etc (Civil Revision 270-97, decided 20.09.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution of Maintenance Decree: Future Maintenance
records.heading: Future maintenance not yet accrued cannot be treated as arrears for auction of the father's property
records.text: Future maintenance not yet accrued cannot be treated as notional arrears for auction of the judgment-debtor father's property in execution. The sale to the mother herself, revival of execution and proceedings without notice to the father reflected arm-twisting, and the minors lost in both eventualities. Ref: 2023 LHC 4846; Muhammad Waqas v. Executing Court Judge Family Court etc (WP 25771/22, decided 04.09.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. Executing Court Judge Family Court etc (WP 25771/22, decided 04.09.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Deficient Court Fee: Section 149 CPC
records.heading: The Court must ascertain deficiency in court fee under section 149 CPC and avoid technicalities
records.text: The judgment discusses the powers of the Court under s. 149 CPC, ss. 4 and 6 of the Court Fees Act, 1870, the combined effect of O. VII R. 11 and s. 149 CPC, and the distinction between ss. 148 and 149 CPC. The Court is bound to ascertain any deficiency in court fee and technicalities should be avoided. Ref: Meeru Khan v. Mst. Naheed Aziz Siddiqui & others (C.P.609/2020, decided 13.09.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Meeru Khan v. Mst. Naheed Aziz Siddiqui & others (C.P.609/2020, decided 13.09.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Compliance with Procedural Law; Justice Seen Done
records.heading: Procedural laws must be complied with, and justice must be seen to be done
records.text: Procedural laws must be complied with, otherwise the judicial system will enter chaos. A fundamental rule of dispensing justice is that justice must not only be done but should be seen to be done. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 661.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Live Streaming of Court Proceedings and Technology
records.heading: Technology serves the judicial system as a tool, and the live streaming request was wrongly filed as a miscellaneous matter
records.text: The judicial system should respond to technology that enhances transparency, while remembering that technology is a tool and a servant, not the master, and a sober approach is preferable. On the application seeking live streaming of review proceedings, the majority view of Munib Akhtar J. was that it raised a new prayer with no nexus to review jurisdiction and appeared wrongly filed as a miscellaneous matter. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 661.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 19A: Matters of Public Importance
records.heading: Matters of public importance under Article 19A affect the public at large and are interpreted liberally
records.text: Matters of public importance under Art. 19A are those affecting the public at large or a whole community, as opposed to individuals or small groups. Art. 19A is to be interpreted progressively and liberally, and cases heard under Art. 184(3), including review petitions arising therein, are matters of public importance. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 661.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Additional Evidence in Civil Revision
records.heading: Additional evidence is ordinarily not recorded in civil revision but may be in exceptional cases
records.text: Ordinarily no additional evidence is recorded in civil revision, but in exceptional cases a High Court may record or admit it to determine whether the lower court acted illegally or with material irregularity under s. 115(1)(c) CPC. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 643.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence
records.heading: Order XLI Rule 27 CPC is not for filling lacunas and is used cautiously and sparingly
records.text: The power under O. XLI R. 27 CPC is not meant to fill lacunas, cure deficiencies or allow a new plea, and is to be exercised cautiously and sparingly. The court must be satisfied that the document sought to be adduced is not of a kind that could easily be fabricated or tampered with. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 643.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Court Jurisdiction: Plenary and Ouster
records.heading: A civil court has plenary jurisdiction, and the party pleading ouster must establish it
records.text: A Civil Court has plenary jurisdiction and may determine jurisdictional facts concerning its own jurisdiction on the averments in the plaint. The party pleading ouster of jurisdiction must establish that fact. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 677.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Bail: Fresh Ground of Trial Delay
records.heading: Further delay after rejection of a first bail application on trial delay is a fresh ground for second bail
records.text: The third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC operates when a year passes without conclusion of trial in a non-capital offence for no fault of the accused. Further delay for no fault of the accused after rejection of the first bail application on that ground is a fresh ground for a second bail application. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 648.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Criminal Statute: Interpretation Favouring Accused
records.heading: Where two interpretations of a criminal statute are possible, the one favouring the accused is preferred
records.text: Where two interpretations of a provision of a criminal statute are reasonably possible, the one favourable to the accused is to be preferred over the one favouring the prosecution. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 648.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Articles: Appreciation and Depreciation
records.heading: Alternate price of dowry articles reflects depreciation for wear and tear and appreciation for gaining articles
records.text: In fixing the alternate price of dowry articles, depreciation applies to articles subject to wear and tear, while appreciation must be considered for articles such as vehicles and gold that gain value. The wife was held entitled to the market value of the car on the date of realisation of the decree. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 669.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Articles: Engagement Gifts Excluded
records.heading: Gifts given to the groom at engagement are not dowry, which comprises only articles given to the bride
records.text: Gifts given to the groom at the time of engagement are not dowry, as ownership vests in the husband. Dowry comprises only articles given to the bride at the time of marriage. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 669.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Courts Act s. 9: Late Filing of Documents
records.heading: The word shall in section 9 of the Family Courts Act is directory, so late filing of documents may be allowed
records.text: The word shall in s. 9(2) and (4) of the Family Courts Act, 1964 is directory, as no penal consequence is prescribed. The Family Court retains discretion to permit a defendant to file and produce documents belatedly, and the discretion exercised by the courts below was not arbitrary, so no interference was warranted. Ref: 2023 LHC 4878; Muhammad Nawaz v. ADJ Hafizabad etc (WP 65227/23, decided 05.10.2023); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. ADJ Hafizabad etc (WP 65227/23, decided 05.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Difference Between s. 154 and s. 161 Statements
records.heading: A suppressed statement to police after the occurrence is the FIR, and a later application may be a section 161 statement
records.text: A statement given by the complainant to the police immediately after the occurrence, though suppressed, is the FIR under s. 154 CrPC. A later application for registration of the case may be treated as a statement under s. 161 CrPC, even though the FIR was recorded on it. Ref: 2023 LHC 4882; Faisal v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 66322/19, decided 03.10.2023); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Faisal v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 66322/19, decided 03.10.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC against Writ of Mandamus
records.heading: A section 12(2) CPC application against a writ of mandamus directing a decision on an application is not maintainable
records.text: An application under s. 12(2) CPC to set aside a High Court writ of mandamus directing the FDA to decide a pending application was dismissed as not maintainable. The direction only required the authority to perform its duty within the law and favoured neither party. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 694.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula as a Right of Women
records.heading: Khula is a woman's fundamental right and needs no proof of maltreatment
records.text: Khula is a fundamental right of a woman under the Quran and Sunnah to claim dissolution of marriage from the court, and that right cannot be denied. Allegations of maltreatment are not necessary to obtain a decree of khula. Ref: Haji Saif-ur-Rahman Shaheen v. Islamic Republic of Pakistan (Shariat Petition No. 16/I of 2022, decided 06.10.2023).
records.title: Haji Saif-ur-Rahman Shaheen v. Islamic Republic of Pakistan (Shariat Petition No. 16/I of 2022, decided 06.10.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Decree against Surety
records.heading: A decree can be executed against a surety to the extent he made himself personally liable
records.text: A decree can be executed against a surety to the extent he has made himself personally liable, in line with s. 128 of the Contract Act, 1872 and s. 145 CPC. After default there was no reason to absolve the petitioner of liability for the agreed amount. Ref: 2023 LHC 4866; Ghulam Shabbir v. Mst. Tanzeela Nusrat etc (Writ Petition-2669-23, decided 12.09.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Ghulam Shabbir v. Mst. Tanzeela Nusrat etc (Writ Petition-2669-23, decided 12.09.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: CCTV Footage Considered at Bail Stage
records.heading: CCTV footage free from tampering is admissible under Articles 46-A and 164 QSO and may be considered at bail stage
records.text: CCTV visuals found by PFSA to be free from editing and tampering are admissible under Arts. 46-A and 164 QSO and may be considered even at bail stage. The police opinion based on them was that the complainant side was the aggressor, and bail has been granted in precedents to accused attributed firearm injuries.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Crossed Entry in Nikahnama Column 15
records.heading: A crossed prompt dower entry in Column 15 cannot be read against the wife, and the husband must prove payment
records.text: Only deferred dower falls due on death or divorce. Where an entry on prompt dower in Column 15 of the nikahnama is crossed off, it cannot be read against the wife, and the burden of proving payment lies on the husband through positive evidence. Ref: 2023 LHC 4933; Hira Masood v. Additional District Judge etc (WP 35641/19, decided 15.09.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Hira Masood v. Additional District Judge etc (WP 35641/19, decided 15.09.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023 Upheld
records.heading: The Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023 was upheld by majority, with the retrospective appeal clause struck down
records.text: By a majority of 10 to 5 the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023 was held in accordance with the Constitution. Prospective right of appeal under s. 5(1) was upheld by 9 to 6, while the clause granting appeal retrospectively was declared ultra vires by 8 to 7. Reasons were to follow. Ref: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division (Constitution Petitions No. 6 to 8, 10 to 12, 18 to 20 and 33/2023, decided 11.10.2023).
records.title: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division (Constitution Petitions No. 6 to 8, 10 to 12, 18 to 20 and 33/2023, decided 11.10.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 149 PPC: Common Object and Bail
records.heading: Under section 149 PPC a common object cannot be ruled out at bail stage where all accused were armed
records.text: Under s. 149 PPC every member of an unlawful assembly is accountable where the offence is committed with a common object, and a nexus between the common object and the offence is required. All accused were armed and assigned specific roles, with ocular support, so a common object could not be ruled out at the bail stage. Ref: Allah Dewayo Shahani v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.52-K/2023, decided 17.08.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Allah Dewayo Shahani v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.52-K/2023, decided 17.08.2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Medical Examination of Rape Victims: Directions
records.heading: Directions on medical examination of rape victims prohibit the two-finger test and comment on past sexual history
records.text: Directions issued that medical opinion conform to s. 375 PPC, examinations follow s. 164-A and DNA testing s. 164-B CrPC, and the two-finger test be prohibited under s. 13(1) of the Anti Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021. Examiners must not comment on past sexual history, and SOPs are to be updated per WHO guidelines. Ref: 2023 LHC 4974; Muhammad Akram v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.20609/23, decided 13.04.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.20609/23, decided 13.04.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Criminal Liability and Arrest of Judges
records.heading: Judicial office gives no immunity for non-judicial acts, but arrest of district judicial officers follows safeguards
records.text: Judicial office gives no immunity for non-judicial acts, so a judge can be arrested and held criminally liable. Where a district judicial officer is to be arrested, the nominee of the High Court is to be informed, a formal arrest may be made if urgent, and the officer is not to be taken to a police station or handcuffed without proper cause. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1955.

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Protection and Security of District Judiciary
records.heading: The district judiciary should have independent security, and High Courts must protect it under Article 203
records.text: The district judiciary should have its own security personnel independent of the district administration and police. High Courts have a duty under Art. 203 to protect district judges from intrusion on their independence, and should act against executive officers involved in illegal confrontation under the Contempt of Court Ordinance, 2003. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1955.

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Assault on Qazi by Assistant Commissioner
records.heading: An Assistant Commissioner who raided and assaulted a Qazi without an FIR committed contempt
records.text: An Assistant Commissioner who raided a Qazi's residence, assaulted and arrested him without any FIR and confined him for about six hours committed contempt by undermining district courts. The High Court's conviction, treating his early unqualified apology and young age only as mitigation, was upheld. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1955.

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Unqualified Apology in Contempt Proceedings
records.heading: An early unqualified apology in contempt ordinarily leads to discharge, though the court may still convict
records.text: An unqualified apology at an early stage amounts to an admission of guilt, removes the need for framing a charge and recording evidence, and ordinarily leads to discharge with a warning. This is not absolute, and in peculiar circumstances the court may convict and treat the apology only as mitigation. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1955.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Public Institutions and Verbal Orders
records.heading: Public institutions do not function on verbal orders, and opinions must be recorded in writing
records.text: Public institutions do not function on verbal orders, and every opinion formed by the institution must be recorded and reduced to writing. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1991.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Tenancy Succession in Bahawalpur Before 1951
records.heading: Before 1951 Shariah governed succession of Muslims in Bahawalpur unless a consistent custom was established
records.text: Even before s. 19-A was inserted in the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act, 1912 in 1951, Shariah governed succession of Muslims in Bahawalpur, unless a consistent custom was established. The Punjab Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1948 applied there, so Shariah prevails over custom or s. 20 of the 1912 Act.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 187(1): Complete Justice Power
records.heading: Article 187(1) confers power only in a competently pending case and gives no independent jurisdiction
records.text: Art. 187(1) is subject to Art. 175(2) and confers power to issue directions only in a case competently pending before the Court. It gives no independent jurisdiction and cannot be invoked where the matter is finally concluded. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1843.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Second Review and Curative Review Not Maintainable
records.heading: Only one review is allowed, so a second or curative review petition is not maintainable
records.text: Art. 188 and the Supreme Court Rules, 1980 allow only one review of a judgment or order. A second review petition, including one styled a curative review, is not maintainable. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1843.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Exhaustion of Remedies in Art. 199 Jurisdiction
records.heading: A litigant must exhaust statutory remedies before Article 199 jurisdiction can be invoked
records.text: Under the doctrine of exhaustion of remedies a litigant cannot approach a new forum until the statutory remedy is exhausted. Art. 199 jurisdiction is extraordinary and cannot be reduced to an ordinary remedy for all grievances or used to bypass the statute. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1919.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Per Incuriam: Meaning
records.heading: A decision rendered in ignorance of a statute or rule having statutory force is per incuriam
records.text: A decision becomes per incuriam when it is rendered in ignorance of a statute or a rule having the force of statute. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1919.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Coram Non Judice: Meaning and Effect
records.heading: An act done by a court without jurisdiction is coram non judice, null and void
records.text: Coram non judice means an act done by a court without jurisdiction. A suit brought in a court lacking jurisdiction, or a judgment given without jurisdiction over the parties, is null and void and may be disregarded. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1919.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Absconsion Not Proof of Offence
records.heading: Absconsion is not proof of the offence and alone is no ground to refuse bail
records.text: Absconsion is not proof of the offence and alone cannot be a ground to refuse bail. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1948.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Other Criminal Cases Do Not Bar Bail
records.heading: Registration of other criminal cases does not bar bail where a prima facie case exists on merits
records.text: Mere registration of other criminal cases against an accused does not disentitle him to bail if he has a prima facie case on merits. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1977.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Non-Prohibitory Clause: Bail is the Rule
records.heading: For offences outside the prohibitory clause of section 497 CrPC, bail is the rule and refusal the exception
records.text: For offences not falling within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, grant of bail is the rule and refusal the exception. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1948, 2023 SCMR 1977.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Bail and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail in a section 489-F PPC case: whether the cheque was for a loan is for the trial court
records.text: The accused was a tenant of the complainant, and whether the cheque was issued for repayment of a loan or to discharge an obligation under s. 489-F PPC was for the trial court. The maximum punishment is three years, outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, and the accused had been in custody about six months. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1977.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Absconsion Not a Ground to Refuse Bail
records.heading: Mere absconsion cannot justify refusing bail, as disappearance after a murder is natural
records.text: Absconsion is not proof of the offence, and mere absconsion cannot justify refusing relief, since disappearance after the occurrence is natural for a person involved in a murder case rightly or wrongly. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1898, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 38; Saad Zia v. The State, etc (Crl.P.150-L/2023).
records.title: Saad Zia v. The State, etc (Crl.P.150-L/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Merits Can Be Touched
records.heading: Mere nomination does not make a person an accused, and merits may be touched in pre-arrest bail
records.text: Mere nomination in the crime report does not make a person an accused until investigation confirms the accusation. An accused who surrendered and joined investigation should not be kept in custody indefinitely before trial, and merits may be touched upon while granting pre-arrest bail. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1898, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 38; Saad Zia v. The State, etc (Crl.P.150-L/2023).
records.title: Saad Zia v. The State, etc (Crl.P.150-L/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Further Inquiry, No Overt Act
records.heading: An empty handed accused with no overt act made out a case of further inquiry for pre-arrest bail
records.text: The petitioner was empty handed, assigned no overt act and placed in column 2 of the s. 173 CrPC report, and he surrendered and joined investigation. The case fell under s. 497(2) CrPC as one of further inquiry. Leave was converted into appeal, allowed, and ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Statutory Interpretation: Redundancy
records.heading: Redundancy of a statutory provision is not lightly imputed, and interpretations producing it are avoided
records.text: Redundancy of a statutory provision is not to be lightly imputed, and an interpretation that produces it should be avoided where possible. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1980.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Legal Heir in Possession: Constructive Possession
records.heading: A legal heir in possession holds constructive possession on behalf of all heirs
records.text: A legal heir in possession is considered in constructive possession on behalf of all the heirs despite his exclusive possession. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1928.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation in Challenge to Inheritance Mutation
records.heading: A daughter's heirs who learned of the mutation in 2004 were not time-barred as she never relinquished her share
records.text: Limitation is relevant where the claimant's conduct shows acquiescence, particularly when third party interests arise. Where the daughter never relinquished her share, the cause of action accrued on denial of her right, and the suit by her heirs filed after learning of the entry in 2004 was not time barred. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1928.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: No Limitation against Female Heirs Defrauded
records.heading: No limitation runs against a female heir defrauded of inheritance by her family
records.text: No limitation runs against a female whose inheritance right has been defrauded by her family, or against a co-sharer denied inheritance, where the denial gives the cause of action. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1901.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: PEEDA Act s. 21: Proceedings against Retired Employee
records.heading: Section 21 PEEDA mandates finalising proceedings against a retired employee within two years of retirement
records.text: The proviso to s. 21 of the PEEDA Act, 2006 mandatorily requires proceedings against a retired employee to be finalised within two years of retirement, and s. 20 gives the Act overriding effect. Proceedings begun three years after retirement were unlawful, and the petition for leave to appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1951.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Expunction of Strictures against NAB Officers
records.heading: Strictures against NAB officers who were not parties and had no notice were expunged
records.text: Strictures recorded by the High Court against NAB officers who were not parties and had no notice condemned them unheard and infringed their right to a fair trial. The petitions were converted into appeals and allowed to the extent of expunging the strictures. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1914.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Non-Presentation of Cheque: O. XXXVII Suit
records.heading: No cause of action arises for an Order XXXVII suit on a cheque never presented for payment
records.text: Where a cheque was never presented for payment, there was no refusal by the drawer or bank under ss. 72 and 84 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. No cause of action accrued for a suit under O. XXXVII CPC, which was therefore not maintainable. Ref: 2014 CLC 995.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Patwaris: Private Offices and Munshis
records.heading: A Patwari is a public servant, and Patwaris were barred from private buildings and private staff
records.text: A Patwari is a public servant liable to departmental and anti-corruption proceedings, while a Munshi hired through his private arrangement is a private person. The Lahore High Court barred Patwaris from using private buildings and private staff, and directed the Senior Member Board of Revenue and DG Anti-Corruption Punjab to act. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1623.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Right to Information from Supreme Court Registrar
records.heading: Access to information is a citizen's right under Article 19A, and the Right to Information Act does not apply to the Supreme Court
records.text: The Supreme Court allowed the request for details of its employees and directed the Registrar to supply the information within 7 days. It held that access to information is a citizen's right under Art. 19A and that the Right to Information Act does not apply to the Supreme Court. Ref: Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No.3532/2023, decided 16.10.2023).
records.title: Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No.3532/2023, decided 16.10.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Custodial Death: Qatl Shibh-i-Amd by Police
records.heading: Police officials were rightly convicted under section 316 PPC for a custodial death caused by torture
records.text: Police officials in whose custody the deceased died, with torture matching medical evidence and no medical care given, were rightly convicted under s. 316 PPC, with wrongful confinement under s. 344 PPC. The High Court declined to interfere with conviction and sentence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1650.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: MPO Detention: Alternate Remedy Not Efficacious
records.heading: The section 3(6) representation against an MPO detention is not an efficacious remedy ousting constitutional jurisdiction
records.text: The representation under s. 3(6) of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 is an alternate remedy but not efficacious enough to oust constitutional jurisdiction. The detention order did not meet the requirements of s. 3, was set aside and release was ordered, with a bond under s. 3(9) available for future concerns. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1646.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: FIA Jurisdiction: Impersonation in Recruitment Test
records.heading: The FIA may investigate scheduled PPC offences with a nexus to the Federal Government, such as impersonation in its recruitment test
records.text: The FIA may register and investigate scheduled PPC offences where there is a nexus with the Federal Government. Impersonating a candidate in an FIA recruitment test prima facie disclosed such offences against a federal agency, and no mala fides were shown, so the petition to quash the FIR was dismissed. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1688.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation against Wrong Revenue Entry
records.heading: There is no blanket exemption from limitation for challenging a wrong revenue entry
records.text: There is no blanket exemption from limitation for challenging a wrong entry. Each new ownership entry in the periodical record gives a fresh cause of action, and a plaintiff must show the last wrong entry came to his knowledge for the suit to be within time. Ref: Shah Fakhr-e-Alam and others v. Mst. Shaukat Ara and others (C.A.998/2020); Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Shah Fakhr-e-Alam and others v. Mst. Shaukat Ara and others (C.A.998/2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 196 CrPC: FIRs for Political Speech Offences
records.heading: FIRs for political speech offences registered without following section 196 CrPC are illegal
records.text: FIRs under ss. 121-A, 124, 153-A and 505 PPC registered without following s. 196 CrPC are illegal, since cognizance requires a complaint by the Federal or Provincial Government or an authorised officer. The Government must tolerate criticism and avoid malicious or frivolous prosecution. Ref: Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.225/2023, decided 14.09.2023); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.225/2023, decided 14.09.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examining Doctor on Medico-Legal Report
records.heading: The defence may question the doctor on the medico-legal examination of accused persons
records.text: The defence may question the doctor about the medico-legal examination of accused persons, under Arts. 152, 155 and 156 QSO read with s. 265-F(7) CrPC. The defence must put its case to the witness during cross-examination, and the medical officer may refresh memory before testifying. Ref: 2023 LHC 5014; Muhammad Aslam v. The State and another (Crl. Revision 206, decided 12.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State and another (Crl. Revision 206, decided 12.10.2023)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption Decree: Mutation and Limitation
records.heading: Revenue authorities must sanction mutation on a pre-emption decree and cannot refuse it for non-execution within limitation
records.text: Revenue authorities must sanction mutation on the basis of a Civil Court decree and cannot refuse it because the decree was not executed within limitation. The Member Board of Revenue's contrary view conflicted with the Supreme Court's dictum, and a decree under O. XX R. 14(1) CPC is of a peculiar nature. Ref: 2023 LHC 5072; Mahmood (deceased) through LRs etc v. Siraj Ahmad (deceased) through LRs etc (Civil Revision-1463-23, decided 10.10.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Mahmood (deceased) through LRs etc v. Siraj Ahmad (deceased) through LRs etc (Civil Revision-1463-23, decided 10.10.2023)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption: Date, Time and Place
records.heading: Authority on pre-emption concerning date, time and place, with no further holding given
records.text: Authority on pre-emption concerning the date, time and place; the post gives no further holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 5083; Muhammad Anwar v. Atta Ullah (Civil Revision 1200-D-02, decided 03.10.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. Atta Ullah (Civil Revision 1200-D-02, decided 03.10.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Proof of Common Intention
records.heading: Proving common intention requires evidence of pre-concert, failing which attending circumstances are considered
records.text: Proving common intention requires evidence of pre-concert or consultation between the accused, and in its absence the attending circumstances may be considered to decide whether common intention existed. Ref: 2023 LHC 5037; Muhammad Tanvir etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 66363/19, decided 10.10.2023); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Tanvir etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 66363/19, decided 10.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Arrest on Mere Suspicion in Habeas Corpus
records.heading: Strong suspicion or an undisclosed source is not legal evidence and cannot alone justify arrest
records.text: Arrest cannot be made without evidence. A complainant's strong suspicion or firm belief, or an undisclosed reliable source or landlord's clue, is not legal evidence and cannot alone justify arrest. Ref: 2023 LHC 5052; Rashida Bibi v. SHO etc. (Crl. Misc. Habeas Corpus 4043-H-23, decided 10.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Rashida Bibi v. SHO etc. (Crl. Misc. Habeas Corpus 4043-H-23, decided 10.10.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Samples
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody and transmission of samples gave the accused the benefit of doubt
records.text: The prosecution failed to establish safe custody of the recovered contraband in the malkhana and safe transmission of samples to the Chemical Examiner. The report could not be linked to the seized substance, giving the accused the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1720.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chemical Examiner Report: Protocols Not Stated
records.heading: A chemical report omitting protocols, tests and quantity violates the Rules and cannot support conviction
records.text: A report that does not state the protocols and tests applied or the quantity tested violates Rr. 5 and 6 of the Control of Narcotic Substances (Government Analysts) Rules, 2001. It loses sanctity under s. 36 CNSA and cannot support conviction. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1720.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Contradictions in Complainant IO Evidence
records.heading: Contradictions between the complainant and the IO on weighing and sampling time touched the root of the case
records.text: The complaint was recorded at 9:30 a.m. with weight and sampling details, though the complainant and IO admitted that weighing and sampling took 5 to 6 hours. The contradiction touched the root of the case and created a dent in the prosecution case. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1720.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Return of Mobile Phone and De-freezing of Accounts
records.heading: A phone seized on arrest must be reported to the Magistrate, and its prolonged retention was unjustified
records.text: A phone seized on arrest is property taken under s. 51 CrPC, and the investigating officer must report the seizure to the Magistrate under s. 523 CrPC. Its prolonged retention and the freezing of small bank balances were unjustified, so the FIA was directed to return the phone and unfreeze the accounts. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1763.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Jinnah House and Askari Tower Cases
records.heading: Lahore High Court allowed post-arrest bail in the Jinnah House attack and Askari Tower arson cases
records.text: The Lahore High Court allowed the post-arrest bail applications of the accused in the Jinnah House attack and Askari Tower arson cases. Ref: Khadija Shah v. The State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No.64830-B of 2023).
records.title: Khadija Shah v. The State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No.64830-B of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 426(2B) CrPC: Remedy and High Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Authority on the remedy under section 426(2B) CrPC and High Court jurisdiction, with no further holding given
records.text: Authority on the remedy under s. 426(2B) CrPC, its legislative history and the jurisdiction of the High Court; the post gives no further holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 5119; Muhammad Iqbal etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 3200-M-23, decided 06.09.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 3200-M-23, decided 06.09.2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Unregistered Tenancy Agreement: Penalty under s. 9
records.heading: The Rent Tribunal may direct payment of the section 9 penalty for an unregistered tenancy agreement
records.text: Where a tenancy agreement relied on in an application for leave to contest is unregistered or non-conforming under the 2009 Act, the Rent Tribunal may halt proceedings and direct payment of the s. 9 penalty. If paid in time the application proceeds, and s. 9 applies to applications by either landlord or tenant. Ref: 2023 LHC 5158; Irshad Ahmed v. Shaukat Hussain Kiyani etc (Writ Petition-1215-20, decided 10.10.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Irshad Ahmed v. Shaukat Hussain Kiyani etc (Writ Petition-1215-20, decided 10.10.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Restoration of Bail Applications Dismissed for Non-Prosecution
records.heading: Bail applications dismissed for non-prosecution were restored and remanded for fresh hearing
records.text: The Islamabad High Court restored nine bail applications of the petitioner, set aside the trial courts' orders dismissing them for non-prosecution, and remanded them for fresh hearing. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State etc (CRL. REV. NO.127-2023, decided 02.10.2023).
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State etc (CRL. REV. NO.127-2023, decided 02.10.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Protective Bail on Consent of NAB
records.heading: Protective bail granted from arrest on arrival as NAB consented and did not contest
records.text: As NAB consented and did not contest, the petitioner was protected from arrest on arrival in Pakistan until he surrenders before the Court on 24.10.2023. Ref: Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif v. State (W.P. No.3333 of 2023, decided 19.10.2023).
records.title: Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif v. State (W.P. No.3333 of 2023, decided 19.10.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Missing Person: Representation by Legal Heirs
records.heading: Legal heirs of a person proved missing may represent him in a suit against him
records.text: Legal heirs of a person proved to have gone missing may represent him in a suit against him, in terms of Arts. 123 and 124 QSO. Ref: 2023 LHC 5180; Muhammad Sufyan Qasim through 4 legal heirs v. Manzoor Ahmad etc (Misc. Writ.7834/23, decided 18.10.2023); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Muhammad Sufyan Qasim through 4 legal heirs v. Manzoor Ahmad etc (Misc. Writ.7834/23, decided 18.10.2023)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitration Award: Opportunity of Hearing, ss. 30 and 34
records.heading: Objection of no hearing before the arbitrator failed where the petitioner appeared before the arbitrator
