records.text: Objections under s. 30 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 alleging no opportunity before the arbitrator failed, as the petitioner was contacted by telephone and appeared before the arbitrator. No irregularity or perversity was found in the High Court judgment, the petitions were dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 656; Injum Aqeel v. Latif Muhammad Chaudhry, etc. (C.Ps. No. 3059 & 3060 of 2021); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Injum Aqeel v. Latif Muhammad Chaudhry, etc. (C.Ps. No. 3059 & 3060 of 2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: DNA Test in Appeal
records.heading: Additional evidence by DNA test in appeal was not warranted, as the power is used sparingly
records.text: The power under O. XLI R. 27 CPC is not to fill lacunas or allow a new plea and is used sparingly. No application was made in the trial court and no exceptional circumstances existed. The petitioner had proved on balance of probabilities that she was the daughter, and the petition was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 600; Shamshad Bibi, etc. v. Riasat Ali, etc. (C.P. No. 1692-L of 2022, decided 25.05.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Shamshad Bibi, etc. v. Riasat Ali, etc. (C.P. No. 1692-L of 2022, decided 25.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness
records.heading: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must prove breach and readiness and willingness, including availability of funds
records.text: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must prove the defendant's breach and that he was always ready and willing to perform, including evidence that funds were available to pay in time. Failure to prove this bars the relief. The appeal was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC 641; Liaquat Ali Khan v. Muhammad Akram & another (C.A. No. 431 of 2021, decided 07.07.2023); Justice Ijaz-ul-Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Liaquat Ali Khan v. Muhammad Akram & another (C.A. No. 431 of 2021, decided 07.07.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower Payable on Demand
records.heading: Dower recorded as payable on demand is not deferred dower and may be claimed during marriage
records.text: Where the nikahnama column records dower as payable on demand, without calling it prompt or deferred, it is not deferred dower and may be claimed during the marriage. The petition was partially allowed and the decree modified to award Rs. 500,000 dower. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 844; Samina v. Additional District Judge etc. (W.P. No. 5278 of 2021); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Samina v. Additional District Judge etc. (W.P. No. 5278 of 2021)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Failure to Deposit Balance
records.heading: A specific performance suit was rightly dismissed for failure to deposit the balance consideration despite two opportunities
records.text: A suit for specific performance was rightly dismissed where the plaintiff failed, despite two opportunities, to deposit the balance sale consideration as directed to test his bona fides. Specific performance is discretionary, and the civil revision was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 820, 2024 CLC 268; Nasir Abbas Bhatti v. Abid Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 9463 of 2022); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Nasir Abbas Bhatti v. Abid Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 9463 of 2022)

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: CCTV Footage as Evidence in Disciplinary Inquiry
records.heading: CCTV footage emailed to the Inquiry Officer without producing the retriever did not meet the criteria of proof
records.text: Footage emailed to the Inquiry Officer by the company's representative, without producing the person who retrieved it from the computer, did not meet the criteria for proving CCTV contents. The inquiry was not fair or transparent, and the writ petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 824; Coca Cola Beverages Pakistan Ltd. v. Ghulam Abbas etc. (W.P. No. 22538 of 2022); Justice Shujaat Ali Khan.
records.title: Coca Cola Beverages Pakistan Ltd. v. Ghulam Abbas etc. (W.P. No. 22538 of 2022)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Fourth Schedule: Proscription under s. 11-EE
records.heading: Listing in the Fourth Schedule requires credible information beyond suspicion, and none was shown against the appellant
records.text: Before listing a person in the Fourth Schedule the authority must hold credible information in more than one form, beyond suspicion, and keep periodic records for the courts. No material was shown against the appellant, so the appeal was allowed and both orders were set aside. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 934; Ghulam Abbas v. Government of Punjab, etc. (Crl. A. No. 67693 of 2022, decided 13.07.2023); Justice Ali Baqar Najafi; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ghulam Abbas v. Government of Punjab, etc. (Crl. A. No. 67693 of 2022, decided 13.07.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 94 and 540 CrPC: Production of Documents
records.heading: An application under sections 94 and 540 CrPC to produce copies without summoning a witness did not fit those provisions
records.text: An application under ss. 94 and 540 CrPC to produce document copies as prosecution evidence, without seeking to summon their custodian or any witness who prepared them, did not fit those provisions. The Special Judge's order was upheld and the revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 942; Ch. Noman Haseeb v. Learned Special Judge Anti-Corruption Court, Bahawalpur and 4 others (Crl. Rev. No. 217 of 2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Ch. Noman Haseeb v. Learned Special Judge Anti-Corruption Court, Bahawalpur and 4 others (Crl. Rev. No. 217 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Reference: Contrived FIR and Unproved Motive
records.heading: A contrived FIR, delay and an unproved motive made the prosecution witnesses' presence doubtful
records.text: The complainant's written application was held not prompt or natural but contrived. Delay in reporting suggested the witnesses were absent at the scene, the alleged motive was unproved, and their photographic account of the occurrence was improbable. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 978; Muhammad Ishaq and 4 others v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 205 & M.R. No. 8 of 2022); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Ishaq and 4 others v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 205 & M.R. No. 8 of 2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Rape of Minor, Nominated Accused
records.heading: Post-arrest bail refused where a nominated accused faced a specific allegation of rape of a minor
records.text: Post-arrest bail under s. 497 CrPC refused in a case under ss. 365-B/376 PPC. The accused was nominated with a specific allegation, the minor victim supported the prosecution in her s. 161 CrPC statement, and the medical officer opined that the possibility of rape could not be ruled out. Bail dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 948; Muhammad Aamar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 54853/B/2022, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Aamar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 54853/B/2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Suspension of Short Sentence: Elections Act Conviction
records.heading: A three year sentence is a short sentence, and suspension under section 426 CrPC needs no deeper merits appreciation
records.text: Where the sentence awarded by the trial court is three years' simple imprisonment with fine, it qualifies as a short sentence, and a deeper appreciation of the merits is not warranted at the stage of suspension. The sentence was suspended under s. 426 CrPC and the applicant was released on bail on furnishing bonds. Application allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 929; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. District Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Crl. A. 273/2023, decided 28.08.2023); Justice Aamer Farooq; Justice Tariq Mehmood Jahangiri.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. District Election Commissioner, Islamabad (Crl. A. 273/2023, decided 28.08.2023)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Determination of Age: Ossification Test and NADRA Record
records.heading: The respondent was a juvenile on any view of the date of birth, and the ossification test case was distinguished
records.text: Even if the date of birth in the NADRA record is accepted, the respondent was 16 years 2 months and 19 days old at the time of the offence, so he was a juvenile in all eventualities. The case relied on by the petitioner was distinguished because no ossification test had been conducted there. Reference was made to s. 510 CrPC on expert reports. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 257; Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Crl. P. 1617/2022, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Crl. P. 1617/2022, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Explosive Substances: Official Witnesses and Minor Discrepancies
records.heading: Official witnesses are as good as private witnesses unless animus is proved, and minor discrepancies are ignored
records.text: Testimony of official witnesses is as good as that of any private witness unless animus against the accused is proved. Courts should ignore minor discrepancies where the material aspects of the evidence have a ring of truth. Conviction under ss. 4/5 of the Explosive Substances Act and s. 7(ii) ATA was upheld, petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 260; Nazir Ahmed v. The State (J.P. 169/2021, decided 01.06.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Nazir Ahmed v. The State (J.P. 169/2021, decided 01.06.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses and Ocular Evidence Over Medical
records.heading: Natural and confidence inspiring related witnesses and trustworthy ocular evidence can alone sustain a conviction
records.text: Where the presence of related witnesses is natural and their evidence is straightforward and confidence inspiring, it can safely sustain a conviction. Trustworthy ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence and alone suffices for conviction under s. 302(b) PPC. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 265; Abdul Wahid v. The State (Crl. A. 446/2020, decided 06.06.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Abdul Wahid v. The State (Crl. A. 446/2020, decided 06.06.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: s. 324 PPC, Injuries on Non-Vital Parts
records.heading: Whether section 324 PPC applies is for trial, so pre-arrest bail was allowed for injuries on non-vital parts
records.text: Injuries were on non-vital parts and the petitioners did not repeat the fire despite opportunity, and there was delay in the FIR. Whether s. 324 PPC applies is for the trial court after evidence, so a case for pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC was made out. Ad interim bail of one petitioner confirmed and the other admitted to bail. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 271; Jamaluddin and another v. The State (Crl. P. 41-K & 42-K/2023, decided 29.05.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Jamaluddin and another v. The State (Crl. P. 41-K & 42-K/2023, decided 29.05.2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Implausible Story and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: An implausible rape account by a married woman gave the accused the benefit of doubt
records.text: The victim's account that the accused's mother and sisters gave her an intoxicating drink and that rape was then committed was found implausible. She was a married woman with an old ruptured hymen, and benefit of doubt was extended to the accused. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and the accused acquitted of charges under ss. 376-II/337-J PPC. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 275; Atta-ul-Mustafa v. The State and another (Crl. P. 596-L/2022, decided 11.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Atta-ul-Mustafa v. The State and another (Crl. P. 596-L/2022, decided 11.08.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: s. 489-F PPC, Cheque for Rent
records.heading: Bail granted under section 497(2) CrPC in a section 489-F PPC case involving a cheque for rent
records.text: Section 489-F PPC carries three years and does not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Whether the cheque was issued towards repayment of a loan or fulfilment of an obligation is a question for the trial court after evidence, and a rent claim prima facie lies before the Rent Controller. Bail granted under s. 497(2) CrPC. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 281; Zafar Nawaz v. The State and another (Crl. P. 717/2023, decided 22.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Zafar Nawaz v. The State and another (Crl. P. 717/2023, decided 22.08.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: s. 489-F PPC, Delay in FIR
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where cheques dishonoured in 2019 led to an FIR after about three years
records.text: Cheques dated 2019 were dishonoured in 2019 yet the FIR was lodged after about three years, and a suit for rendition of accounts was pending. Whether the cheques were issued towards a loan or an obligation under s. 489-F PPC is for the trial court. A prima facie case for pre-arrest bail was made out and ad interim bail confirmed. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 287; Abdul Rasheed v. The State and another (Crl. P. 294-L/2023, decided 24.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Abdul Rasheed v. The State and another (Crl. P. 294-L/2023, decided 24.08.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Principles of Appreciation (Indian Supreme Court)
records.heading: There is no hard and fast rule for accepting a dying declaration, which the court must be convinced is true
records.text: The Supreme Court of India held that there is no hard and fast rule for accepting a dying declaration, and the court must be fully convinced of its truthfulness on the facts. Factors such as expectation of death, first opportunity, tutoring, proper recording, opportunity to observe and consistency go to weight and not admissibility. The two declarations were found doubtful on the surrounding circumstances. Ref: Irfan @ Naka v. The State of Uttar Pradesh (Crl. A. 825-826/2022, decided 23.08.2023).
records.title: Irfan @ Naka v. The State of Uttar Pradesh (Crl. A. 825-826/2022, decided 23.08.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeals Dismissed for Non-Appearance: Right to Seek Revival
records.heading: Appeals dismissed for non-appearance, with liberty to seek a decision on merits on surrender or arrest
records.text: The Islamabad High Court dismissed both appeals of Nawaz Sharif in the Avenfield and Al-Azizia references for non-appearance, noting that he left the country despite being on bail after a fair trial. The court allowed him to apply for decision of the appeals on merits if he surrenders or is arrested. Appeals dismissed. Ref: PLD 2022 Islamabad 13; Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif v. State through Chairman, National Accountability Bureau, Islamabad (Criminal Appeals 1/2019 and 121/2018).
records.title: Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif v. State through Chairman, National Accountability Bureau, Islamabad (Criminal Appeals 1/2019 and 121/2018)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Avenfield Reference: Acquittal of Maryam Nawaz and Safdar
records.heading: Acquittal in the Avenfield reference as the prosecution failed to prove its case and NAB could not shift the burden
records.text: The Islamabad High Court set aside the judgment of 6 July 2018 as to the appellants and acquitted them under s. 9(a) of the National Accountability Ordinance 1999. The prosecution failed to prove its case, NAB could not shift the burden of proof onto the accused, and its investigation was described as disappointing. Appeals allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 1; Maryam Nawaz Sharif (Maryam Safdar) v. The State (Crl. As. 122 & 123/2018, decided 29.09.2022); Justice Aamer Farooq; Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani.
records.title: Maryam Nawaz Sharif (Maryam Safdar) v. The State (Crl. As. 122 & 123/2018, decided 29.09.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Trial of Civilians by Military Courts: Army Act Provisions Ultra Vires
records.heading: Army Act provisions enabling trial of civilians by military courts were declared ultra vires the Constitution
records.text: By short order, s. 2(1)(d) (both sub-clauses) and s. 59(4) of the Pakistan Army Act 1952 were declared ultra vires the Constitution and of no legal effect. The trials of about 103 civilians and others similarly placed in relation to the events of 9 and 10 May 2023 are to be held by criminal courts of competent jurisdiction under ordinary or special law. Ref: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 23.10.2023); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 23.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Nature and Purpose of the FIR
records.heading: The FIR is not substantive evidence and only sets criminal law in motion and gives a clue for investigation
records.text: The FIR is not substantive evidence unless used as a dying declaration. Its purpose is to set the criminal law in motion and give a clue for investigation under s. 154 CrPC, and it need not contain every minute detail of the occurrence. After registration the Investigating Officer must find out the truth. Ref: 2023 LHC 5215; Niaz Abbas Muhammad Nawaz etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 36092/2019, decided 03.10.2023); Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Niaz Abbas Muhammad Nawaz etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 36092/2019, decided 03.10.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Petitions for General Elections Within 90 Days: Order of 23 October
records.heading: Authority on the order of 23 October 2023 in petitions for general elections within 90 days, no holding given
records.text: Authority on the written order of the hearing of 23 October 2023 in the petitions seeking holding of general elections within 90 days. The post gives no holding. Ref: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 32/2023, decided 23.10.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 32/2023, decided 23.10.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Special Oath Under Oaths Act 1873
records.heading: A special oath accepted under the Oaths Act 1873 binds the person who made the offer and is conclusive proof
records.text: Under s. 9 of the Oaths Act 1873 the court may communicate an offer of a special oath to the other party, and under s. 10 may administer the oath on acceptance. Under s. 11 the evidence so given binds the person who made the offer and is conclusive proof of the matter stated. Ref: 2023 LHC 5286; Fayyaz Ahmad through Special Attorney Muhammad Aamer Munir v. Sube Deen (Civil Revision 66481/2023, decided 11.10.2023); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Fayyaz Ahmad through Special Attorney Muhammad Aamer Munir v. Sube Deen (Civil Revision 66481/2023, decided 11.10.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Importance and Requirement of Site Plan
records.heading: Rule 25.13 Police Rules requires two accurately prepared site plans by a qualified officer, and failure violates it
records.text: A site plan is to be prepared by a qualified police officer or other suitable agency or patwari, but not by a patwari for an inhabited enclosure or land inside a town or village site, under Rule 25.13 of the Police Rules 1934. Two site plans are required, one on the officer's own observation and one with references from witness statements, and the failure to prepare it accurately was held a violation of the rule. Ref: Sajid Hussain v. The State (Crl. Appeal 289/2019); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Sajid Hussain v. The State (Crl. Appeal 289/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Entry Wound Bigger Than Exit Wound
records.heading: Circumstances in which an entry wound may be bigger than an exit wound in a bullet injury
records.text: Also considers the circumstances in which an entry wound may be bigger than an exit wound in a bullet injury, with reference to Parikh's Textbook of Medical Jurisprudence, Forensic Medicine and Toxicology. Ref: Sajid Hussain v. The State (Crl. Appeal 289/2019); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Sajid Hussain v. The State (Crl. Appeal 289/2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Under s. 9 Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961
records.heading: A wife may apply under section 9 MFLO in addition to other remedies, and the Arbitration Council may fix maintenance
records.text: Read with ss. 5 and 21 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act 1964, nothing prevents a wife from applying under s. 9 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 in addition to any other remedy. Her right to invoke s. 9 cannot be taken away by proceedings before another forum, and the Arbitration Council could fix maintenance with arrears when issuing a certificate of talaq. Ref: 2023 MLD 1928.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Further Cross-Examination in Family Court: Equality of Arms
records.heading: Further cross-examination in Family Court cannot fill lacunae caused by a party's negligence, given equality of arms
records.text: Section 11(3) of the Family Courts Act is for clarifying doubts in a witness's statement, not for filling lacunae caused by a party's negligence. Allowing further cross-examination after a proper opportunity would put the petitioner at an advantage, contrary to equality of arms and Art. 10A of the Constitution, and could not be allowed. Ref: 2023 MLD 1968.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Abatement of Criminal Appeal on Death of Accused
records.heading: An appeal against a sentence of death or imprisonment abates on the accused's death but continues as to any fine
records.text: An appeal against a sentence of death or imprisonment abates on the death of the accused but continues as to any fine. Compensation of Rs.500,000 under s. 544-A CrPC cannot be considered a fine. The court explained the legal consequences of abatement, including the contention of loss of service benefits by a deceased civil servant. Ref: 2023 MLD 1983.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Denial of Appointment Merely on FIR Declared Illegal
records.heading: Denial of an appointment merely on account of an FIR, without a determined criminal record, was illegal
records.text: Denial of an appointment letter despite recommendation by the Punjab Public Service Commission, on account of an FIR and without determining that the candidate has a criminal record, was declared illegal. The rule applied was held contrary to the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Faraz Naveed. Ref: 2023 LHC 5412; Syed Ali Raza and 1 other v. Chairman PPSC through its Secretary etc. (WP 43082/23, decided 17.10.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Syed Ali Raza and 1 other v. Chairman PPSC through its Secretary etc. (WP 43082/23, decided 17.10.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Ephedrine Quota Case: Acquittal on Appeal
records.heading: The Lahore High Court set aside the sentence and acquitted the accused in the ephedrine quota case
records.text: The Lahore High Court set aside the sentence of 25 years' imprisonment and fine imposed on Hanif Abbasi in the ephedrine quota case and acquitted him on his appeal. Ref: 2023 LHC 5352; Muhammad Hanif Abbasi v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 663/2018, decided 18.10.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif Abbasi v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 663/2018, decided 18.10.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Earnest Money and Vendor's Reciprocal Obligation
records.heading: Earnest money is forfeited if the vendee fails to pay, but the vendor's own reciprocal default makes him the aggrieved party
records.text: Earnest money forms part of the price if the sale completes and is forfeited if the vendee fails to pay the balance on time. Here the respondent had failed from the outset to install the gas meter as the agreement required, so the petitioner was the aggrieved party who could seek performance or avoid the contract and recover damages. Ref: 2023 LHC 5404; Muhammad Afzal v. Asia Zaheer (Civil Revision 5252/2, decided 04.10.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Afzal v. Asia Zaheer (Civil Revision 5252/2, decided 04.10.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Presumption, Readiness and Willingness
records.heading: Breach of a contract to transfer immovable property is presumed not adequately compensable in money
records.text: Under the explanation to s. 12 of the Specific Relief Act 1877, breach of a contract to transfer immovable property is presumed not adequately compensable in money, and the burden to dislodge this lies on the party averring otherwise. A plaintiff who pleads readiness and willingness and deposits the balance price as directed is not incapable under s. 24(b), so the suit cannot be dismissed. Ref: 2023 CLC 1892.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Late Payment Charges: s. 74 Contract Act Penalty Clauses
records.heading: Late payment charges of Rs.1000 per day were penal, so reasonable compensation was awarded under section 74
records.text: Section 74 of the Contract Act 1872 allows reasonable compensation not exceeding the stipulated amount or penalty. Late payment charges at Rs.1000 per day were held oppressive and penal, so the defendants were awarded Rs.150,000 for the delay. The specific performance decree was maintained subject to payment of that compensation. Ref: 2023 CLC 1892.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Jurisdiction to Declare Contract Terms Repugnant to Islam
records.heading: Only the Federal Shariat Court can declare a law repugnant to Islam, not the Appellate Court
records.text: Under Art. 175(2) of the Constitution and Arts. 203D and 203G, only the Federal Shariat Court can declare a law repugnant to the injunctions of Islam. The Appellate Court lacked jurisdiction to declare a provision of the agreement or allotment letter so repugnant, and its validity is to be tested under s. 74 of the Contract Act 1872. Ref: 2023 CLC 1892.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Private Medical Colleges: No Fee Increase During Study
records.heading: Private medical colleges cannot increase tuition fees during a study programme
records.text: Enhancement of tuition fee and other charges by private medical colleges during a study programme was declared illegal. Colleges must charge the tuition fee notified at admission for session 2022 onwards, and PMDC must ensure compliance with a report to the Deputy Registrar within 45 days. Ref: 2023 CLC 1947; Justice Shahid Jamil.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Urdu Translation of Judgments
records.heading: The Registrar was directed to propose capacity for Urdu translation of judgments, as language barriers hinder access to information
records.text: The Registrar was directed to send a summary with proposals to the Chief Justice for building capacity to translate judgments into Urdu, with the permission of the author Judge. The court observed that language barriers hinder the constitutional right to information. Ref: 2023 CLC 1947; Justice Shahid Jamil.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeal Against Consent Decree: Exceptions
records.heading: A consent decree is appealable in listed exceptions such as no consent, fraud, or non-compliance with Order XXIII Rule 3
records.text: A consent decree is appealable in listed exceptions, including appeal by a non-party to the compromise, no consent or no compromise, invalidity such as lack of jurisdiction, a decree travelling beyond the agreement, consent given under mistake of fact or obtained by fraud on the court, and non-compliance with O. XXIII R. 3 CPC. Ref: 2023 CLC 1962.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Restoration of Execution Petition Under s. 151 CPC
records.heading: An Executing Court may restore an execution petition dismissed for non-prosecution under its inherent powers in section 151 CPC
records.text: An Executing Court can restore an execution petition dismissed for non-prosecution in exercise of its inherent powers under s. 151 CPC. The section is enabling, there is no prohibition, and absence of an express provision does not curtail the court's jurisdiction to meet the ends of justice. Ref: 2023 CLC 1811.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Preliminary Decree in Partition Suit
records.heading: A preliminary decree in a partition suit must determine the shares, failing which it is defective and not executable
records.text: Under O. XX R. 18 CPC a preliminary decree in a partition suit determines the rights and shares of the interested parties, and whether the property is joint is decided before it. A preliminary decree without determination of shares is defective and neither sustainable nor executable. Ref: 2023 CLC 1875.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Powers of Local Commission in Partition
records.heading: A Local Commission cannot determine shares and only prepares the mode of partition per the preliminary decree
records.text: A Local Commission has no power to determine the right or share of any party in a partition suit. It only prepares the mode of partition on the spot according to the shares fixed in the preliminary decree, and a mode of partition prepared where shares were not determined is not sustainable. Ref: 2023 CLC 1875.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marked Document Not Proved in Evidence
records.heading: A document only marked and not proved in evidence cannot be taken as legal evidence
records.text: A document which has been only marked and not produced and proved in evidence cannot be taken into account by the courts as legal evidence of fact. Ref: 2023 CLC 1875.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Illegal Basic Decree: Superstructure Falls
records.heading: When the basic decree is illegal or void, the entire superstructure built on it falls
records.text: When the basic order, judgment or decree is found illegal or void, the entire superstructure built on it falls automatically. Ref: 2023 CLC 1875.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Appeal: Conviction Upheld, Death Sentence Reduced
records.heading: Murder conviction upheld, but the death sentence was reduced to life imprisonment on benefit of doubt
records.text: The FIR was prompt, the eyewitness account was corroborated by medical evidence, and the law does not require proof with arithmetical accuracy. Because the motorcycle number and ownership were not established and no crime empty was recovered, the death sentence was converted into imprisonment for life, benefit of doubt being an extenuating circumstance. Appeal under s. 302(b) PPC otherwise dismissed. Ref: 2023 YLR 2471.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence in Appeal
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal under Order XLI Rule 27 is allowed where a just decision cannot be reached without it
records.text: Order XLI Rule 27 CPC enables the appellate court to take additional evidence needed to pronounce judgment or for any other substantial cause. The test is whether a just decision can be reached without it, and the evidence must bear directly on the point in issue. The petitioner was allowed to bring documents and oral evidence on record in the interest of justice. Ref: 2023 YLR 2441.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Retrospective Effect of Supreme Court Judgments
records.heading: Supreme Court interpretation of a provision applies from the time of its enactment, not from the date of judgment
records.text: Supreme Court judgments declare the correct interpretation of an existing provision, so the interpretation applies from the time the law or provision was enacted and not from the date of the judgment. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 791, 2023 YLR 2654; Shakil-ur-Rehman v. State (Crl. A. 182346 & 197051 & CSR No. 2-N of 2018, heard on 20.6.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Shakil-ur-Rehman v. State (Crl. A. 182346 & 197051 & CSR No. 2-N of 2018, heard on 20.6.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift (Tamleek): Onus on Beneficiary
records.heading: Where an oral gift is disputed by the owner, the beneficiary must prove the transaction and the mutation
records.text: Where an oral gift is disputed by the owner, the onus shifts to the beneficiary to prove the oral transaction and the mutation, including date, time, place, witnesses and transfer of possession as a constitutive element. The petitioners failed to prove these, and oral tamleek was not proved by admissible evidence. Ref: 2023 YLR 2619.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Conditions for Conviction
records.heading: Conviction on circumstantial evidence needs conclusive circumstances forming a chain leaving no hypothesis of innocence
records.text: To sustain conviction on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances must be established by cogent and convincing evidence, be of conclusive nature, and form a chain so compact that no reasonable hypothesis of innocence remains and the crime was authored by the accused and none else. Ref: 2023 YLR 2538.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: Weak Corroborative Evidence
records.heading: Last seen evidence is weak and cannot sustain capital punishment without corroboration
records.text: Last seen evidence is weak and insufficient to sustain capital punishment without corroboration. The prosecution must prove proximity in time and place between last being seen alive with the accused and death, and eliminate the possibility that the deceased met anyone else in the interval. Ref: 2023 YLR 2538.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Pointation of Known Place of Occurrence: Art. 40 QSO
records.heading: Pointation of a place of occurrence already known to the investigating officer is not a discovery under Article 40 QSO
records.text: Pointation of a place of occurrence already known and inspected by the investigating officer is not a discovery of a new fact under Art. 40 QSO, as it is hit by Arts. 38 and 39. It is inadmissible against the appellant. Ref: 2023 YLR 2538.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Guidelines for Medico-Legal Postmortem Examination
records.heading: Guidelines for medico-legal postmortem examination were listed from a forensic medicine textbook
records.text: The court listed guidelines for postmortem examination drawn from a textbook on forensic medicine, including a written order before autopsy, careful reading of the police report, a complete examination of the skull, thorax and abdomen. Autopsy should follow filing of eyewitness statements and information of weapon and injuries to police, to exclude later tampering. Ref: 2023 YLR 2503, PLJ 2024 CrC Note 2; Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: False Implication of Family Members in Homicide
records.heading: The court observed a trend in Punjab of implicating many family members of the accused in homicide cases
records.text: The court observed a trend in Punjab of implicating as many members of the accused's family as possible in homicide cases to pressure them to give up pursuing the actual culprit, and that false witnesses may be planted where the murder is unwitnessed. Ref: 2023 YLR 2503, PLJ 2024 CrC Note 2; Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Data From Automated Systems: Arts. 46-A and 164 QSO
records.heading: Data from automated systems tendered by a defence witness was validly brought on record under Articles 46-A and 164 QSO
records.text: Data generated by an automated information system and collected through modern devices, tendered by a defence witness, was legitimately brought on record under Arts. 46-A and 164 QSO. Courts can use such data to ascertain the truth of a fact. Ref: 2023 YLR 2503, PLJ 2024 CrC Note 2; Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Proof of Guilt and Appraisal of Witness Evidence in Entirety
records.heading: A conviction must rest on proved guilt, and a witness's evidence is scrutinised in its entirety without cherry-picking
records.text: A conviction requires guilt to be proved by the prosecution, and a verdict driven by sentiment or emotion is not justice. A witness's evidence must be scrutinised in its entirety and cannot be appraised by cherry-picking. Ref: 2023 YLR 2503, PLJ 2024 CrC Note 2; Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Police Recruitment: Candidates With Criminal Antecedents
records.heading: A Magistrate's parole observation cannot nullify the departmental bar on police appointment of candidates with criminal antecedents
records.text: Standing Order No. 06/2015 of the Police Department bars appointment of candidates with criminal antecedents. A Magistrate's observation on releasing an offender on parole under s. 11 of the Probation of Offenders Ordinance 1960 that it would not affect government service cannot nullify that departmental policy for the police force. Ref: 2023 LHC 5453; Akash Masih v. SSP Operation etc. (WP 59263/2022, decided 12.10.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Akash Masih v. SSP Operation etc. (WP 59263/2022, decided 12.10.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cipher Case: Bail and Quashment Refused
records.heading: The Islamabad High Court rejected bail and quashment applications in the cipher case
records.text: The Islamabad High Court issued its detailed judgment rejecting the bail application and the application for quashment of the case of the Chairman PTI in the cipher case. The post gives no further reasoning.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Court Witness: Order of Cross-Examination
records.heading: The prosecution questions a court witness first, and the accused may then cross-examine if incriminated
records.text: The prosecution is to put questions to a court witness first, and the accused may then cross-examine if an incriminating circumstance emerges against him. The trial court's finding that the accused must cross-examine first was incorrect. Ref: 2002 PCrLJ 614.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NAB Amendments: Dissenting Note on Judicial Review of Legislation
records.heading: In dissent, judicial review of legislation is limited to conflict with fundamental rights, so the NAB amendments stood
records.text: In his dissenting note, the Judge held that the judiciary may review legislation only where it conflicts with fundamental rights. The challenged NAB amendments fall within the policy domain of Parliament and do not take away or abridge fundamental rights, so he would dismiss the petition on merits in view of Art. 8(2). Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const.P. 21/2022, dissenting note dated 30.10.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const.P. 21/2022, dissenting note dated 30.10.2023)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Mutation Register and Record of Rights: Presumption of Correctness
records.heading: The mutation register is distinct from the record of rights and carries no presumption of truth
records.text: Under Rule 7.1 of the Land Record Manual and ss. 33(3) and 34 of the Land Revenue Act, the mutation register is distinct from the record of rights and carries no presumption of truth. Section 52 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act 1967 gives a presumption of correctness only to entries in records of rights and periodical records made as per law. Ref: Hasham Khan (decd) through his LRs v. Waheed Ahmed (C.A. 170/2017, decided 07.06.2023); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Hasham Khan (decd) through his LRs v. Waheed Ahmed (C.A. 170/2017, decided 07.06.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Unbroken Chain of Circumstances
records.heading: In circumstantial evidence cases the circumstances must form an unbroken chain, failing which the accused gets the benefit
records.text: In circumstantial evidence cases every circumstance must link with the others to form a continuous chain, with one end touching the dead body and the other the neck of the accused. If any link is missing, the benefit goes to the accused. Ref: 2023 LHC 5484; The State v. Shabana Kausar (Murder Reference, decided 17.10.2023); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: The State v. Shabana Kausar (Murder Reference, decided 17.10.2023)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Scheme of Arbitration Under Arbitration Act 1940
records.heading: The Arbitration Act 1940 provides a scheme of arbitration without court intervention, aimed at finality
records.text: Describes the scheme of arbitration without court intervention under the Arbitration Act 1940, covering appointment and removal of arbitrators (ss. 8 to 12), their powers (s. 13), the award and its filing (s. 14), modification or remission (ss. 15 and 16) and judgment according to the award (s. 17). The object of the provisions is to expedite and simplify arbitration and obtain finality. Ref: Haji Shinkai v. Abdul Shakoor and others (Civil Appeal 23-Q/2017, decided 19.10.2023).
records.title: Haji Shinkai v. Abdul Shakoor and others (Civil Appeal 23-Q/2017, decided 19.10.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Presumption of Sunni Faith and Its Rebuttal
records.heading: Every Muslim in the sub-continent is presumed Sunni unless evidence to the contrary is produced
records.text: Every Muslim in the sub-continent is presumed to be Sunni unless good evidence to the contrary is produced. Rebuttal is judged on preponderance of evidence, and with no strict criteria courts consider way of life, parental faith and the faith of close relatives. Ref: Mst. Nawab Bibi (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Hakim Ali and others (Civil Revision 2312/2014, heard 04.10.2023).
records.title: Mst. Nawab Bibi (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Hakim Ali and others (Civil Revision 2312/2014, heard 04.10.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Husband's Absolute Right of Talaq
records.heading: A husband has an absolute right to divorce his wife, with no condition prescribed
records.text: A husband has an absolute right to divorce his wife, with no condition prescribed in Shariah or in codified law. Reference is made to s. 7(1) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 and s. 105 of the Code of Muslim Personal Laws. Ref: Muhammad Awais v. Zahida Parveen (Civil Revision 44034/2019, heard 05.10.2023).
records.title: Muhammad Awais v. Zahida Parveen (Civil Revision 44034/2019, heard 05.10.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXI Rr. 1 & 2 CPC: Out of Court Payment of Decree
records.heading: Out of court payment of a decree is permitted by Order XXI Rule 1, with no requirement of revenue stamps
records.text: Order XXI Rule 1(1)(b) CPC permits out of court payment by bank, postal money order or a payment evidenced in writing and signed by the decree-holder or his agent, with no requirement of revenue stamps. The decree-holder must certify payment under R. 2(1), and the judgment-debtor 'may' apply under R. 2(2), with no stated consequence for not informing the court. Ref: 2023 CLC 1974.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Gap in Law No Excuse for Not Enforcing Fundamental Rights
records.heading: A gap in law is no excuse for non-enforcement of fundamental rights, which the High Court may enforce
records.text: Absence or gap in law cannot excuse non-enforcement of fundamental rights. The High Court has unabridged powers under Art. 199(2) of the Constitution to direct enforcement of fundamental rights. Ref: 2023 LHC 5568; Judicial Activism Panel through its Chairman Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Government of Pakistan etc. (WP 67863/2021, decided 31.10.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Judicial Activism Panel through its Chairman Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Government of Pakistan etc. (WP 67863/2021, decided 31.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal on Compromise Is an Honourable Acquittal
records.heading: All acquittals, including acquittal on compromise, are honourable and carry the consequences of a pure acquittal
records.text: All acquittals, including acquittal on compromise, are honourable, and the law draws no distinction between types of acquittal. An unchallenged acquittal attains finality and carries all consequences of a pure acquittal, erasing the alleged guilt and any sentence. Ref: 2023 LHC 5587; Rizwan Ali Sayal v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (WP 1938/2023, decided 19.09.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Rizwan Ali Sayal v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (WP 1938/2023, decided 19.09.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Date: Delimitation Timeline and ECP Proposal
records.heading: The ECP stated the delimitation timeline and proposed 11 February 2024 for the election
records.text: The ECP counsel stated that delimitation would conclude on 30 November 2023, with final publication by 5 December and the election programme under s. 57(2) of the Elections Act 2017 concluding on 29 January 2024. The ECP proposed Sunday 11 February 2024, and it was directed to meet the President to settle a date. Ref: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 32/2023, decided 02.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 32/2023, decided 02.11.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Discretion and Art. 185(3) Interference
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary, and the Supreme Court will not interfere under Article 185(3) absent grave injustice
records.text: A decree of specific performance under s. 12 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 is discretionary. Where three courts below dismissed the suit for the plaintiff's own serious default, the Supreme Court will not interfere under Art. 185(3) unless misuse of discretion causing grave injustice is shown. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2017 SCMR 516; Malik Imam Bakhsh v. Muhammad Boota (deceased) through legal heirs (Civil Petition 2280/2015, decided 18.08.2016); Justice Amir Hani Muslim; Justice Dost Muhammad Khan.
records.title: Malik Imam Bakhsh v. Muhammad Boota (deceased) through legal heirs (Civil Petition 2280/2015, decided 18.08.2016)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Protecting Identity of Sexual Violence Victims
records.heading: Courts must protect the identity of sexual violence victims and identify them by acronyms in judgments
records.text: Under the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act 2021 the Courts are obliged to protect the identity of victims of sexual violence. Judgments must identify victims by acronyms instead of full names, and District and Sessions Judges in the Punjab are to ensure compliance. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 757, PLJ 2023 CrC 948; Muhammad Aamar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 54853/B/2022, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Aamar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 54853/B/2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Directions on Medical Examination of Rape Victims
records.heading: Directions on medical examination in rape cases prohibit the two-finger test and comment on past sexual history
records.text: Directions for medical examination in rape cases: medical opinion must follow the current definition in s. 375 PPC, examinations must follow s. 164-A CrPC and DNA testing s. 164-B CrPC, and the two-finger test is prohibited under s. 13(1) of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act 2021. Examiners must not comment on past sexual history, and SOPs are to be updated to WHO Guidelines. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 757, PLJ 2023 CrC 948; Muhammad Aamar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 54853/B/2022, decided 08.12.2022); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Aamar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 54853/B/2022, decided 08.12.2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Price Control of Foodstuffs: Provincial Legislative Field
records.heading: The 1977 Act was struck down as price control of essential foodstuffs lies in the provincial legislative field
records.text: The 1977 Act was declared ultra vires Parliament to the extent it applies to price control of essential foodstuffs and anti-profiteering in the Punjab, and actions taken under it were declared ultra vires and non est. The Act and the 2021 Order were struck down, since price control of essential food commodities lies within the Provincial Assembly's legislative field. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 736.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Order Without Hearing: Audi Alteram Partem
records.heading: An order passed without a hearing offends audi alteram partem and was defective
records.text: Superior courts cannot approve inaction or dubious acts of executive functionaries that are against the law, the Constitution and natural justice. The impugned order was defective because the petitioner was not given an opportunity of showing cause or of hearing, contrary to audi alteram partem. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 703, PLJ 2023 Lah 785.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Jurisdiction Over Concluded Contracts
records.heading: The High Court may strike down an order on a concluded contract for mala fides or arbitrariness where no disputed facts arise
records.text: The High Court under its constitutional jurisdiction can examine and strike down an order on a concluded contract for mala fides, arbitrariness, lack of transparency or discrimination, if challenged promptly and no contentious questions of fact arise. Routine contractual disputes are not open to scrutiny, but breaches involving no controversial facts can be addressed, and the remedy is more efficacious than a suit or arbitration. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 703, PLJ 2023 Lah 785.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction: Landlord Must Prove Tenancy Under Rented Premises Act 2009
records.heading: To invoke the Rented Premises Act 2009 the landlord must prove the person occupies as tenant
records.text: To invoke the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 the landlord must establish that the person whose eviction is sought occupies the premises as tenant, that is, one who undertook or is bound to pay rent. Where the relationship was denied, the landlord had to prove it. Constitutional petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 720.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale Mutations: Burden on Beneficiaries
records.heading: The burden of proving sales and sale mutations lies on the beneficiaries, and failure may amount to fraud
records.text: The burden to establish the sales and sale mutations lay upon the beneficiaries, and failure to discharge it may be said to constitute fraud. The Supreme Court ordered possession of five squares of land to be given to the respondent and costs to be paid to her. Ref: Mehmood Khan and others v. Sara Akhtar and others (C.P. 3030/2021, decided 26.10.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Mehmood Khan and others v. Sara Akhtar and others (C.P. 3030/2021, decided 26.10.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt as of Right
records.heading: The benefit of doubt is a right, not a concession, and even a single doubt entitles the accused to it
records.text: Conviction must rest on unimpeachable, trustworthy evidence, and the burden of proof is always on the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The benefit of doubt is a right and not a concession, and even a single doubt entitles the accused to it. Ref: Maqsood Alam v. The State etc. (Crl. P. 1710-L/2017, decided 12.10.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Maqsood Alam v. The State etc. (Crl. P. 1710-L/2017, decided 12.10.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minors: Grandfather's Liability and Quantum
records.heading: A grandfather must maintain the children only where the father cannot and the mother is also poor
records.text: A grandfather who is affluent is obliged to maintain the children only when the father is poor, infirm and incapable of earning and the mother is also poor. In fixing quantum, the Family Court must balance the minors' needs against the father's means, without unjust enrichment or oppression of the father. Ref: 2023 LHC 5606; Ayesha Hashmat and 2 others v. ADJ etc. (WP 27381/2023, decided 01.11.2023); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Ayesha Hashmat and 2 others v. ADJ etc. (WP 27381/2023, decided 01.11.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Locus Poenitentiae: Cancellation of Tender After Acceptance
records.heading: Cancelling a tender after acceptance was illegal as locus poenitentiae protected the successful bidder's accrued right
records.text: Under the principle of locus poenitentiae a right accrued to the successful bidder, which the authorities could not take away unilaterally. No provision allowed cancellation after acceptance and the reasons given were extraneous to the bid documents. The cancellation order was declared illegal, and the authorities were directed to finalise the tender under the applicable rules. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 703, PLJ 2023 Lah 785.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 149 CPC: Deficiency of Court Fee
records.heading: Section 149 CPC is an interim power to allow time to make up deficient court fee, not an exemption
records.text: Section 149 CPC is an exception to ss. 4 and 6 of the Court Fees Act 1870. It is an interim power to allow time to make up deficient court fee on plausible grounds, and does not exempt payment altogether. Courts should check court fee at admission. The petition was converted into appeal, allowed and the second appeal remanded to the High Court for decision on merits. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 912.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Procedure as Handmaid of Justice
records.heading: Procedure is the handmaid of justice, and technicalities are avoided unless essential on public policy grounds
records.text: Procedure is mere machinery whose object is to facilitate and not obstruct the administration of justice. The CPC should be considered liberally and must not undermine substantial justice, and technicalities are to be avoided unless essential on grounds of public policy. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 912.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Counsel's Authority to Withdraw Suit: O. III R. 1 CPC
records.heading: A suit withdrawn on the statement of counsel holding a power of attorney was validly withdrawn
records.text: The suit was withdrawn on the statement of counsel who held a power of attorney authorising any statement, and a plaintiff was present when it was recorded. The Appellate Court had misconstrued the law, so the High Court under Art. 199 set aside its order and maintained the trial court's dismissal of the restoration application. Petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 699.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NAB Amendments Appeals: Interim Order on Trials
records.heading: Trial courts may continue trials in NAB cases but may not decide them until the intra-court appeals are decided
records.text: In the intra-court appeals against the judgment striking down the NAB amendments, trial courts were allowed to continue trials but restrained from deciding them until final decision of the appeals. The appeals are to be fixed after the Full Court issues detailed reasons on the Practice and Procedure Act, and notice was issued to the Attorney General and the Advocates General. Ref: Islamic Republic of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice, Govt. of Pakistan, Islamabad v. Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and another (I.C.A.2/2023, decided 31.10.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Islamic Republic of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice, Govt. of Pakistan, Islamabad v. Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and another (I.C.A.2/2023, decided 31.10.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Petitions for General Elections Within 90 Days
records.heading: Judgment on petitions for general elections within 90 days, with only the opening paragraphs reproduced and no holding
records.text: Judgment on Constitution Petitions seeking general elections within 90 days, filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association and others, together with related miscellaneous appeals by PTI and another. The post reproduces only the opening paragraphs, recording the parties and the dissolution of the National Assembly, and gives no holding. Ref: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P.32/2023, decided 03.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P.32/2023, decided 03.11.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Date: 90 Days and Seventh Census
records.heading: The judgment records agreement on 8 February 2024 for elections and the need for the seventh census
records.text: The judgment records that the President and the Election Commission agreed on 8 February 2024 for the general elections. It states that the President should have announced a date within 90 days of dissolution, and that elections were not held in time because the seventh census, approved by the Council of Common Interests under Art. 154, was needed as a constitutional requirement under Art. 51. Ref: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P.32/2023, decided 03.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P.32/2023, decided 03.11.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Past Maintenance Before Arbitration Council: s. 9(1) MFLO
records.heading: Section 9(1) MFLO does not curtail the Arbitration Council's power to grant past maintenance
records.text: Section 9(1) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 does not curtail the power of the Arbitration Council to grant past maintenance. The husband's duty to maintain arises with the marriage and is enforceable for the past period even if not claimed then, subject to limitation and the circumstances of the case. Ref: 2023 MLD 1928.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Review Petition Does Not Operate as Stay
records.heading: Filing a review petition under Article 188 does not operate as a stay of the judgment under review
records.text: Under Art. 188 of the Constitution, mere filing of a review petition before the Supreme Court does not operate as a stay of the judgment under review. As the High Court judgment on inheritance had not been implemented, the District Collector (Revenue) was directed to ensure immediate entries in the revenue record in accordance with it. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 910.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Special Appellate Court: Amenable to Art. 199
records.heading: The Special Appellate Court under the Smuggling Act is not immune from High Court jurisdiction under Article 199
records.text: The Special Appellate Court under the Prevention of Smuggling Act 1977 is distinct from the High Court, and its presiding High Court Judge acts as persona designata. The bar in Art. 199(5) is therefore not attracted, and its acts, orders and judgments are not immune from High Court jurisdiction under Art. 199. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 907.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Review Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court: Principles
records.heading: Review jurisdiction is limited, as the Supreme Court does not rehear a case as in appeal
records.text: Review jurisdiction attaches to the finality of Supreme Court judgments, which can be reopened only on limited grounds. The Court does not rehear the case as in appeal. Its scope is defined by O. XLVII R. 1 CPC, and Art. 188 deliberately uses the word review and not appeal, unlike Art. 185. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 825.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 187: Power Distinguished from Jurisdiction
records.heading: Article 187 gives power to do complete justice in a matter competently before the Court but confers no jurisdiction
records.text: Art. 187 does not confer jurisdiction on the Supreme Court. It gives power to do complete justice and can be used only in a matter competently before the Court, without creating an independent right to initiate proceedings. Jurisdiction is the capacity to decide a dispute, while the power of the Court means the orders it may pass after assuming jurisdiction. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 825.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Striking Down Statutes: Caution Required
records.heading: The power to strike down a statute must be used with caution where a harmonising interpretation is available
records.text: Constitutional courts may rule on the vires of laws, but the power to strike down must be exercised with great care and caution. A law should not be struck down unless no alternate interpretation is available that harmonises the statute with the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 825.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination by Non-Adverse Co-Defendant
records.heading: Only a party with an obvious conflict of interest may cross-examine the witnesses of other parties
records.text: Under Arts. 132 and 133 QSO, only a party with an obvious conflict of interest may cross-examine the witnesses of other parties. A co-defendant whose interest is the same as that of the party calling the witness cannot cross-examine, so as to prevent abuse of process and filling of lacunas. Writ petition dismissed. Ref: 2023 MLD 1875.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Withdrawn Suit: No Deduction of Time for Second Suit
records.heading: Time spent on a withdrawn suit is not deducted for a second suit under Order XXIII Rule 2 CPC
records.text: Where a suit for specific performance was withdrawn with conditional permission to file afresh, O. XXIII R. 2 CPC governs the second suit and the time spent on the withdrawn suit is not deducted. Once limitation starts running it cannot be stopped, and equity cannot override it. Concurrent rejection of the plaint as time-barred was upheld. Ref: 2023 MLD 1819.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Proof of Offence under s. 462-C PPC
records.heading: Authority on proof of an offence under section 462-C PPC on a bail application, with no further holding given
records.text: Authority on the evidential requirement for proof of an offence under s. 462-C PPC and the duty of the prosecution, decided on a post-arrest bail application under s. 497 CrPC. The post gives no further holding or outcome. Ref: 2023 LHC 5653; Muhammad Hassan v. The State (Crl. Misc. 3535-B/2023, decided 30.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Hassan v. The State (Crl. Misc. 3535-B/2023, decided 30.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Securing Attendance of Accused: Bond or Detention
records.heading: A bond under section 91 CrPC or detention under section 351 secures the attendance of an accused
records.text: A bond under s. 91 CrPC and, in contrast, detention under s. 351 CrPC are the methods to secure the attendance of an accused for trial. Decided in a criminal revision against interim orders. Ref: 2023 LHC 5661; Muhammad Aslam v. State etc (Crl. Revision 255-23, decided 24.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. State etc (Crl. Revision 255-23, decided 24.10.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Evidence of Witness Read as a Whole
records.heading: A witness's evidence must be read as a whole, and cross-examination prevails where the examination-in-chief is not defended
records.text: Under Arts. 132 and 133 QSO, a witness's evidence must be read as a whole, especially the cross-examination, and a single sentence cannot be torn out of context. If the witness cannot defend his examination-in-chief in cross-examination, the Court cannot rely on it and must decide on the basis of the cross-examination. Ref: 2023 CLC 1933.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination: Scope and Documents Not Proved
records.heading: Documents cannot be considered unless the witness is tested in cross-examination, which carries equal importance
records.text: Documents filed with the evidence or relied on in the written statement cannot be considered unless the witness enters the witness box and is tested in cross-examination. The purpose of cross-examination is to test the veracity of the examination-in-chief, so equal importance must be given to it when evaluating a witness's evidence. Ref: 2023 CLC 1933.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Courts: CPC and QSO Not Strictly Applicable
records.heading: The CPC and QSO apply only loosely in Family Courts, and property recorded in the Nikahnama is the wife's
records.text: The provisions of the CPC and the Qanun-e-Shahadat 1984 are not strictly applicable in Family Court proceedings, and the Family Court has power to adopt its own procedure. In a dower dispute, property recorded in the Nikahnama without any condition imposed by the husband is the personal property of the wife. Constitutional petition dismissed. Ref: 2023 CLC 1926.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Interpretation of Columns of Nikahnama
records.heading: Column 17 of the Nikahnama cannot be read as concerning conditions after divorce
records.text: The Nikah Form is a very important document for resolving spousal disputes under the Family Courts Act 1964. Its columns follow a systematic sequence, and Column 17 cannot be read as concerning conditions after divorce, because Column 18 begins the subject of divorce and divorce conditions are separately recorded. Ref: 2023 CLC 1926.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Jurisdiction and Purpose of Family Courts
records.heading: Family Courts have exclusive jurisdiction over Schedule matters and wide powers including reconciliation efforts
records.text: Under s. 5 of the Family Courts Act 1964, Family Courts have exclusive jurisdiction over matters in the Schedule, subject to the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 and the Conciliation Courts Ordinance 1961. The Act replaced the lengthy Civil Court procedure and gives Family Court Judges wide powers, including efforts at reconciliation and reunion of spouses. Ref: 2023 CLC 1926.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Doctrine of Election
records.heading: A party that elects one of several concurrent remedies is precluded from proceedings seeking contrary relief
records.text: A party may choose one of several concurrent remedies before a competent forum, but once the election is made it is precluded from launching other proceedings seeking relief contrary to the first. The doctrine rests on waiver and abandonment, O. II R. 2 CPC, estoppel and res judicata. Ref: 2023 CLC 380.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Presumption of Possession of Gold Ornaments
records.heading: Gold ornaments are generally presumed to be possessed by females, and the wife failed to prove the husband took them
records.text: In a suit for deferred dower in gold ornaments, the wife did not say who held the ornaments and failed to prove that the husband had snatched them. The general presumption is that gold ornaments are possessed by females and only exceptionally by males. The Appellate Court's findings were set aside and those of the Family Court upheld. Ref: 2019 CLC 1008.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Limitation for Suit for Dowry Articles
records.heading: A suit for dowry articles must be filed within three years under Article 49 of the Limitation Act
records.text: A suit for recovery of dowry articles is a suit for specific movable property and must be filed within three years under Art. 49 of the Limitation Act, from divorce or from refusal of a specific demand. A suit filed 26 years after divorce, with no date of refusal asserted, was barred, and the delay raised a presumption that the articles were taken back. Ref: 2016 MLD 693.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Removal of Lamberdar on Mere Registration of Cases
records.heading: A lamberdar cannot be removed merely because criminal cases were registered and ended in acquittal
records.text: A lamberdar with 24 years of unblemished service was removed by the Revenue Hierarchy merely because criminal cases were registered, though he was never convicted and was acquitted or exonerated in all of them. The removal was not backed by any ground in the relevant Rules. The respondent's appointment was declared of no legal effect and the petitioner was restored. Ref: 2023 CLC 1995.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Interpretation of the Law of Limitation: Salient Features
records.heading: Limitation is a statute of repose, strictly construed, and equity does not override it
records.text: Under ss. 3 and 5 of the Limitation Act 1908, limitation is a statute of repose, strictly construed, and justice, equity and good conscience do not override it. Hardship or imagined inherent discretion cannot cross the hurdle of limitation, and unexplained delay or laches of those with access to legal assistance is not to be countenanced. Ref: PLD 2016 SC 872.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Adoption as Legal Character: s. 42 Declaration
records.heading: Adoption is a legal character for a section 42 declaration, but a collusive suit without evidence of adoption fails
records.text: Adoption is a legal character for the purposes of s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act 1877, and an adoptive parent or adopted child may seek a declaration of it. A mere declaration cannot be sought where further consequential relief is available. The suit was found collusive for lack of evidence that the child lived as the adopted son, and the appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2023 CLC 1916.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI CPC: Memorandum of Appeal and Forum Defects
records.heading: An appeal filed in a court lacking jurisdiction should be returned promptly to the appellant to elect the right forum
records.text: Discussion of O. XLI Rr. 1, 3 and 9 CPC and ss. 5 and 14 of the Limitation Act on the form of the memorandum of appeal. Where an appeal is filed in a court lacking territorial or pecuniary jurisdiction, the memorandum should be promptly returned to the appellant to elect the right forum, to avoid a decision coram non judice. The maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit is also considered. Ref: Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi, etc (C.P.1877-L/2016, decided 26.09.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi, etc (C.P.1877-L/2016, decided 26.09.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Deferred Dower: Limitation under Art. 104
records.heading: A bare plea of earlier talaq does not effect divorce, so the dower suit under Article 104 was within time
records.text: A bare plea in a written statement that talaq was pronounced earlier does not itself effect divorce, and the alleged pronouncement was not shown to be backed by notice or Arbitration Council proceedings. Divorce became effective at the latest on the date of the earlier judgment finding the wife divorced, so the three-year period under Art. 104 ran from that date and the suit was within time. Ref: 2005 YLR 1518.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Past Maintenance Under Compromise Beyond Three Years
records.heading: A husband who undertook past maintenance by compromise for over three years bears the onus of proving payment
records.text: Where the husband undertook by compromise to pay past maintenance for more than three years, the onus to prove payment lay on him and he failed to discharge it. The High Court repelled his plea that maintenance could not be allowed beyond three years, since he had voluntarily signed the compromise, and the decree was upheld. Ref: 2005 YLR 106.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Withdrawn Suit for Dower: Section 14 Limitation Act
records.heading: Section 14 of the Limitation Act excludes time spent in previous litigation on a withdrawn dower suit
records.text: O. XXIII R. 2 CPC does not apply to suits under the West Pakistan Family Courts Act 1964 because of s. 17 of that Act. Even if applied, the words law of limitation include sections as well as articles, and s. 14 of the Limitation Act excludes the time spent in previous litigation. The benefit of s. 14 was therefore available to the petitioner. Ref: 2005 MLD 376.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Nikah Nama Entries as Proof of Transfer of Property
records.heading: Nikah Nama entries suffice to prove transfer of property given in dower without registration
records.text: Entries in the Nikah Nama are sufficient proof of transfer of property given in dower, and no registration or other document is required to complete the transfer. A transfer of the suit property made during the pendency of the suit cannot be held bona fide under the principle of lis pendens. Ref: 2005 MLD 376.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Delegated Divorce Without Notice: Dower Limitation
records.heading: Delegated divorce without notice to the Arbitration Council never took effect, so the dower suit was within time
records.text: Where the wife exercised her delegated right of divorce but sent no notice to the Chairman Arbitration Council under ss. 7 and 8 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, the ninety-day period never started and her divorce never took effect. The husband's later divorce took effect on expiry of ninety days, so her dower suit was within time. The decrees were set aside and the suit decreed. Ref: 2007 CLC 1009.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Blasphemy: Digital Forensic Evidence and Recoveries
records.heading: Digital forensic evidence under Articles 46-A and 164 QSO proved a blasphemy case despite non-association of private witnesses
records.text: In a prosecution under ss. 295-A, 295-B and 295-C PPC, non-association of private witnesses in the recovery of computers and laptops was inconsequential. The blasphemous material extracted by digital forensic examination was backed by Arts. 46-A and 164 QSO, and the prosecution was held to have proved its case against the accused. Ref: 2023 YLR 2663.

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Dispute Between Co-Sharers Outside s. 3
records.heading: A land dispute between co-sharers pending in a civil suit falls outside section 3 of the Illegal Dispossession Act
records.text: The land dispute was already pending in a civil suit before the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 was enacted, the accused were co-sharers with a mutation on file, and nothing linked them to land grabbers. A co-sharer is presumed in possession of every inch of joint property, so the dispute fell outside s. 3 of the Act and the accused received the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2023 YLR 2691.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Victim's Version Need Not Be Corroborated
records.heading: A rape victim's version need not be corroborated in material particulars in every case
records.text: It is not the law that in every case the version of the complainant or victim must be corroborated in material particulars by independent evidence.
