The two prosecution witnesses were consistent on the salient features, their deposition was straightforward and confidence-inspiring, and lengthy cross-examination caused no serious crack in the prosecution case. Ref: The State v. Muhammad Rafique (Capital Sentence Reference No. 13-T of 2020); Muhammad Rafique v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 67706-J of 2020).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Rafique (Capital Sentence Reference No. 13-T of 2020); Muhammad Rafique v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 67706-J of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Decree Against Father Not Executable Against Grandfather
records.heading: A maintenance decree against a father cannot be executed against the grandfather
records.text: A maintenance decree passed against a child's father cannot be executed against the grandfather. If no property of the father is found, the child must institute a suit for maintenance against the grandfather under the Family Courts Act, as due process under Art. 4 of the Constitution requires, since the claim operates against the grandfather's property. Ref: Bashir Ahmad (decd) through LRs v. Additional District Judge, Hafizabad and others (C.P.5918/2021, decided 03.11.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Bashir Ahmad (decd) through LRs v. Additional District Judge, Hafizabad and others (C.P.5918/2021, decided 03.11.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Rule of Consistency in Bail: Benchmark
records.heading: The rule of consistency in bail rests on Article 25 and looks at the investigation material as well as the FIR role
records.text: The rule of consistency in bail under s. 497(2) CrPC rests on equality before the law under Art. 25. The benchmark for applying it is not only the role attributed to the accused in the FIR but also the material collected in the investigation. Ref: Mohammad Atif v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl.P.298/2023, decided 31.10.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Mohammad Atif v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl.P.298/2023, decided 31.10.2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Deposit of Arrears and Rent During Rent Appeal
records.heading: Question whether the Appellate Court can direct deposit of arrears and rent during a rent appeal, holding not given
records.text: The post states only the question decided: whether an Appellate Court, admitting an appeal from eviction proceedings where the respondent denies the landlord and tenant relationship, can direct the appellant to deposit arrears adjudicated by the Rent Tribunal and regular monthly rent during the appeal. The holding is not given. Ref: 2023 LHC 5703; Muhammad Irfan v. ADJ etc (Misc. Writ.50434/23, decided 17.10.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Irfan v. ADJ etc (Misc. Writ.50434/23, decided 17.10.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Abuse of Process by Plaintiffs in Possession
records.heading: Plaintiffs in illegal possession for 14 years who drag out litigation abuse process and violate Article 23
records.text: Leave to appeal was declined as no illegality was pointed out. Plaintiffs who remained in illegal possession for 14 years while dragging out litigation violated the owners' right under Art. 23. Courts must remain vigilant against abuse of process, impose costs where required and stem frivolous litigation, and possession was to be handed over immediately. Ref: Javed Hameed, etc v. Aman Ullah, etc (Civil Petition No.1990-L of 2017).
records.title: Javed Hameed, etc v. Aman Ullah, etc (Civil Petition No.1990-L of 2017)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Evacuee Land: Status Changed Only by Custodian
records.heading: The status of evacuee land can be changed only by the Custodian of Evacuee Properties
records.text: Evacuee land vested in the State on migration of non-Muslims to India, and its status can be changed only by the Custodian of Evacuee Properties in accordance with law. The Custodian's notification of 10.02.1948 granting such land to the Forest Department was upheld by the Supreme Court. The concurrent decrees of the two courts below had no backing in law and were reversed. Ref: 2023 LHC 5726; Province of Punjab through Collector etc v. Mst. Sughran Bibi etc (Civil Revision 115655/17, decided 01.11.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Province of Punjab through Collector etc v. Mst. Sughran Bibi etc (Civil Revision 115655/17, decided 01.11.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Chief Justice in Chamber Cannot Exceed the Rules
records.heading: Neither the Chief Justice nor a Judge in Chambers alone can pass an order beyond the Rules
records.text: Neither the Chief Justice nor a Judge in Chambers alone can pass an order beyond what the Rules provide, so the former Chief Justice's proceedings in the matter had no legal effect. The Human Rights Cell may only forward complaints meeting the Art. 184(3) test, and since the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023 the Committee under s. 2(1) decides whether a matter is fixed. Ref: Application in respect of Property Dispute (H.R.C.82928/2018, decided 08.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Application in respect of Property Dispute (H.R.C.82928/2018, decided 08.11.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 184(3): Caution and Alternative Forums
records.heading: Article 184(3) is to be exercised cautiously, and an alternative forum should address the grievance first
records.text: Art. 184(3) is an original jurisdiction to be exercised cautiously, and where another forum can address the grievance it should do so first. Direct intervention may affect the rights of others and High Court decisions can come to the Court under Art. 185. The applicant was left to complain to the Ministry of Defence, which the AAG assured would be considered, and to pursue other remedies. Ref: Application in respect of Property Dispute (H.R.C.8157-P/2023, decided 08.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Application in respect of Property Dispute (H.R.C.8157-P/2023, decided 08.11.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Decree Subject to Return of Dower: Execution
records.heading: A khula decree subject to return of dower is a decree for all purposes and executable
records.text: A decree dissolving marriage on the basis of Khula subject to return of dower is a compound decision under s. 10(4) of the Family Courts Act 1964. Under Rr. 16 and 17 of the Family Courts Rules 1965 and s. 13 of the Act it is a decree for all purposes, so the husband's execution petition for return of dower is maintainable. Ref: 2023 CLC 1285.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Frivolous Litigation by Government Against Property Owners
records.heading: Frivolous litigation by the Government against property owners over land of little financial significance was condemned
records.text: The Court condemned the Government of Punjab's frivolous litigation over land of little financial significance, contrary to the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property under Arts. 23 and 24 and the rule that compulsory deprivation requires compensation. Public resources and court time were wasted, and the order was sent to the Chief Secretary, Punjab. Ref: Province of Punjab through the Deputy Commissioner/Collector District Gujranwala & others v. Zulfiqar Ali & another (C.P.386-L/2021, decided 13.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Province of Punjab through the Deputy Commissioner/Collector District Gujranwala & others v. Zulfiqar Ali & another (C.P.386-L/2021, decided 13.11.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Same Handwriting on Complaint, Recovery Memo and Site Plan
records.heading: Admitted same handwriting on the complaint, recovery memo and site plan led to the accused's acquittal
records.text: The complainant and a prosecution witness admitted in cross-examination that the complaint, recovery memo, rough site plan and s. 161 CrPC statements were in the same handwriting, although the Investigating Officer denied it. The trial court's examination of the documents confirmed this. The accused was acquitted, according to the post. Ref: 2023 LHC 5785; Ijaz Hussain @ Jajay Shah v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 214-21, decided 05.10.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Ijaz Hussain @ Jajay Shah v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 214-21, decided 05.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Grounds of Arrest: Art. 10 and Police Compliance
records.heading: Police must provide grounds of arrest under Article 10, and Magistrates must ensure compliance at remand
records.text: The police were disregarding Art. 10 of the Constitution and earlier directions on providing grounds of arrest to the accused. Failure warranted contempt proceedings, but a lenient view was taken and directions were reissued. Magistrates hearing physical remand under s. 167 CrPC must ensure grounds of arrest are provided and made part of the police file. Ref: 2023 LHC 5817; Mst. Shehnaz Bibi etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 2945-B-23, decided 13.11.2023); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Mst. Shehnaz Bibi etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 2945-B-23, decided 13.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Record Before Defence Stage: s. 265-F(7)
records.heading: An accused may summon record or witnesses under section 265-F(7) CrPC only on entering his defence
records.text: The accused's application to summon the Rescue-15 audio record before cross-examining prosecution witnesses was dismissed. Under s. 265-F(7) CrPC the accused may summon record or witnesses only when his turn comes on entering his defence, and not before. The criminal revision was rejected. Ref: 2023 LHC 5822; Raja Asad Kiani v. ADJ etc (Crl. Revision 265-23, decided 08.11.2023); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan.
records.title: Raja Asad Kiani v. ADJ etc (Crl. Revision 265-23, decided 08.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused of Unsound Mind: Release on Security s. 466
records.heading: An accused of unsound mind should as a rule be released on security rather than detained
records.text: An accused of unsound mind who is incapable of making his defence should as a rule be released on sufficient security under s. 466 CrPC. An order for detention in safe custody is the exception, made only when there is apprehension that he would not be properly cared for or would injure himself or others. Ref: Zaigham Hassan Khan v. The State, etc (Crl.P.172-L/2023, decided 07.11.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Zaigham Hassan Khan v. The State, etc (Crl.P.172-L/2023, decided 07.11.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Fraudulent Transfer of Woman's Land: Costs
records.heading: A purported sale of a woman's land in derogation of section 42 attracted costs of one million rupees
records.text: The purported sale of a woman's land was effected in derogation of s. 42 of the Land Revenue Act 1967 and the judgments requiring extra care over women's property, and violated Art. 24(1). Revenue officers were complicit or incompetent. The petitioners were directed to pay one million rupees as costs, constituting a charge on their landholding until paid. Ref: Muhammad Mumtaz Khan (decd) thr. LRs & others v. Mst. Siraj Bibi (decd) thr. LRs (C.M.A.6336/2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Muhammad Mumtaz Khan (decd) thr. LRs & others v. Mst. Siraj Bibi (decd) thr. LRs (C.M.A.6336/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Faizabad Dharna Review: Delay in Fixing Petitions
records.heading: The Court recalled its judgment as review petitions were not fixed, and present incumbents were not held responsible
records.text: The Court recalled its judgment of 6 February 2019 warning of orchestrated violent protests, noting that review petitions were not fixed for hearing, which hindered implementation. It acknowledged the manipulation involved in not fixing them, and held that present incumbents should not be held responsible for predecessors, given that they showed a wish to implement the decision. Ref: Review Petition by Sh. Rasheed Ahmed, Chairman, Awami Muslim League (C.M.A.3577/2019, decided 15.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Review Petition by Sh. Rasheed Ahmed, Chairman, Awami Muslim League (C.M.A.3577/2019, decided 15.11.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Representation Against Discharge Under Police Rules
records.heading: A civil servant discharged under Rule 12.21 may make representation under section 21 and then approach the Service Tribunal
records.text: Discussion covers the doctrine of ex debito justitiae and the right of representation under s. 21 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act 1974 against discharge from service under Rule 12.21 of the Police Rules 1934. An adverse decision on representation can be challenged under s. 4 of the Punjab Service Tribunals Act. Ref: Junaid Wazir v. Superintendent of Police, PRU/Dolphin Police, Lahore and another (C.P.3186/2020, decided 05.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Junaid Wazir v. Superintendent of Police, PRU/Dolphin Police, Lahore and another (C.P.3186/2020, decided 05.10.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Discontinuing Use of Sahib for Public Servants
records.heading: Adding the word sahib to the job titles of public servants should be discontinued
records.text: In a criminal petition over the murder of a child, the Court observed that adding the word sahib to the job titles of public servants should be discontinued, as it elevates their status unnecessarily and may foster a perception of unaccountability. A copy of the order was sent to the Inspector General of Police, the Home Secretary and the Advocate General, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Ref: Javid Khan v. Arshid Khan and another (Crl.P.149-P/2023, decided 15.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Javid Khan v. Arshid Khan and another (Crl.P.149-P/2023, decided 15.11.2023)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Reference Under s. 18: Jurisdictional Conditions
records.heading: A written application within time is a jurisdictional condition precedent to a reference under section 18
records.text: Before the Collector can make a reference under s. 18 of the Act, a written application must be made by a person interested who does not accept the award, stating grounds of objection and filed within the period in the provisos to s. 18. These are jurisdictional facts and conditions precedent, and without them the Court has no jurisdiction over the reference. Ref: Gul Zaman v. Dy. Commissioner/Collector Gwadar & others (C.A.13-Q/2020, decided 14.11.2023); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Gul Zaman v. Dy. Commissioner/Collector Gwadar & others (C.A.13-Q/2020, decided 14.11.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Belated s. 161 Statement of Injured Complainant
records.heading: A belated and unexplained section 161 statement of an injured complainant made the prosecution story doubtful
records.text: The complainant's statement under s. 161 CrPC was recorded at a belated stage, with no evidence of his incapacity and no plausible explanation for the delay, and was reproduced from a computer-generated paper. This made the prosecution story doubtful, and the prosecution failed to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2023 YLR 2562.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 161 QSO: Court's Power to Question Witnesses
records.heading: The court may question any witness under Article 161 QSO and section 540 CrPC but must not act as prosecutor
records.text: Art. 161 QSO and s. 540 CrPC empower and oblige the court to ask any witness any question at any stage to reach the truth. The judge must not act as prosecutor, cross-examine, intimidate or favour either side, and must use the power with caution and only where necessary, relying on 2021 SCMR 1725 and 2018 SCMR 141. Ref: 2023 YLR 2562.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 265-F(2) and 540 CrPC: Summoning Material Witnesses
records.heading: The court must summon material witnesses under sections 265-F(2) and 540 CrPC but cannot advance either side's case
records.text: Under s. 265-F(2) CrPC the court must ascertain from the prosecutor or complainant the names of persons acquainted with the facts and summon them. Under s. 540 CrPC the court must summon or recall a person whose evidence is essential for a just decision, but cannot use the power to advance the case of either prosecution or defence. Ref: 2023 YLR 2562.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Owner Presumed Landlord; Claim of Ownership No Defence
records.heading: The owner is presumed to be the landlord, and a bare claim of ownership is no defence to eviction
records.text: Ownership is not essential to the relationship of landlord and tenant, but absent contrary evidence the owner is presumed landlord and the person in possession a tenant. Tenancy may be oral or implied. A person cannot remain in rented premises merely by asserting ownership and filing a suit for declaration. Ref: Nasir Khan v. Nadia Ali Butt and others (C.P.2885/2022, decided 08.11.2023); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Nasir Khan v. Nadia Ali Butt and others (C.P.2885/2022, decided 08.11.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Police Confession Inadmissible, Further Inquiry
records.heading: A confession to the police is not provable against the accused, so the case required further inquiry for bail
records.text: Bail cannot be withheld as punishment, and the prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt at all stages including bail. Under Arts. 38 and 39 QSO a confession made to the police or in police custody is not provable against the accused. The case therefore required further inquiry into guilt, to be resolved at trial. Ref: Akhtar v. Khwas Khan and another (Crl.P.1054/2023, decided 23.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Akhtar v. Khwas Khan and another (Crl.P.1054/2023, decided 23.10.2023)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Award After Withdrawal of Suit Without s. 21 Reference
records.heading: An award after withdrawal of a suit is not illegal merely because no reference was obtained under section 21
records.text: The post distinguishes the jurisdiction of the Civil Court under s. 9 CPC from that under s. 2(c) of the Arbitration Act 1940. An award made after withdrawal of an ordinary suit cannot be held illegal merely because the order of reference was not obtained under s. 21 of the Arbitration Act 1940. Ref: 2023 LHC 5844; Sakhi Mohammad (deceased) etc. v. Mst. Maridan etc. (Civil Revision 4290-16, decided 18.10.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Sakhi Mohammad (deceased) etc. v. Mst. Maridan etc. (Civil Revision 4290-16, decided 18.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Habeas Corpus: Fabricated Supplementary Statements and Case Diary
records.heading: Supplementary statements recorded to justify illegal confinement were fabricated, and case diary guidelines were issued
records.text: In a habeas petition under Art. 199 and s. 491 CrPC, arrest of the detenues was shown only after the production order, and supplementary statements were recorded to justify illegal confinement. The case diary should follow Rule 25.54 of the Police Rules 1934, with numbered, stamped sheets. The petition was disposed of with directions and guidelines. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 854; Mst. Nasreen Bibi v. District Police Officer etc (W.P. No. 6566 of 2023, decided 08.09.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Mst. Nasreen Bibi v. District Police Officer etc (W.P. No. 6566 of 2023, decided 08.09.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Female Minor: Mother's Preferential Right
records.heading: A mother has the better right to custody of a female minor unless she remarries, and remarriage is no impediment
records.text: Under ss. 17 and 25 of the Guardian and Wards Act 1890, a mother has the better right to custody on separation unless she remarries, and remarriage is not itself an impediment. A minor's preference for the father cannot be the sole criterion for a girl aged 10 to 15, who needs her natural mother most. Petition dismissed, with extended visitation on long weekends expected. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 912; Kamran Saeed v. Additional District Judge etc (W.P. No. 15564 of 2023, heard 13.09.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Kamran Saeed v. Additional District Judge etc (W.P. No. 15564 of 2023, heard 13.09.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Disputed Dower Entry in Nikahnama: Burden of Proof
records.heading: The burden of proving a disputed dower entry false lies on the party disputing it
records.text: The burden to prove that a disputed dower entry in the Nikahnama was false or later inserted lay on the party disputing it, who relied only on an inquiry report and produced no evidence. Where no mode of payment is specified, the whole dower is payable on demand. The wife was held entitled to Rs. 500,000 dower and the husband's petition was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 923; Mst. Aniza and another v. Additional District Judge and 2 others (W.P. Nos. 38446 & 35820 of 2016, heard 23.05.2023); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Mst. Aniza and another v. Additional District Judge and 2 others (W.P. Nos. 38446 & 35820 of 2016, heard 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Worship Place and Continuing Offence
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail allowed as the accused committed no continuing act constituting the actus reus
records.text: The prosecution invoked the doctrine of continuing offence over a Qadiani worship place built in 1922. Its design violated no law then in force and the accused committed no continuing act constituting the actus reus now, even if ss. 298-B and 298-C PPC are strict liability offences. Petition for pre-arrest bail accepted. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 1019; Imran Hameed etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 5151/B of 2023, decided 10.04.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Imran Hameed etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 5151/B of 2023, decided 10.04.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Kidnapping for Extortion: Delay in Reporting Crime
records.heading: A delay of two and a half months in reporting a kidnapping for extortion was disastrous for the prosecution
records.text: In a case under s. 365-A PPC read with s. 7(e) ATA involving extortion of a large sum, a delay of two and a half months in reporting the crime to the police was disastrous for the prosecution. Guilt remained unproved on insufficient evidence, and the appeals were allowed with release of the appellants. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 1028; Muhammad Rizwan etc v. State and another (Crl. A. Nos. 57199, 57200, 57201 & 57203 of 2019, heard 22.12.2021); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan etc v. State and another (Crl. A. Nos. 57199, 57200, 57201 & 57203 of 2019, heard 22.12.2021)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Juvenile Accused: Transfer from ATC After Ordinance Lapse
records.heading: An Ordinance stands repealed after 120 days, so the juvenile's trial was transferred to the Juvenile Court
records.text: The Anti-Terrorism Court relied on Ordinance No. V of 2012 and s. 24 of the General Clauses Act. The Court noted that under Art. 89 an Ordinance stands repealed after 120 days, being temporary legislation. Revision allowed, and the trial of the juvenile was transferred to the Juvenile Court at Peshawar to resume from the stage reached, under s. 23 ATA. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 1053; Saeedullah v. Lal Sher and another (Crl. Rev. No. 70-P of 2022, decided 10.04.2023); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Saeedullah v. Lal Sher and another (Crl. Rev. No. 70-P of 2022, decided 10.04.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Breaking of Tooth as Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw
records.heading: Breaking a tooth is Itlaf-i-salahiyyat-i-udw punishable under section 336 PPC, as teeth are not bones
records.text: Teeth are not bones, and breaking a tooth constitutes Itlaf-i-salahiyyat-i-udw, punishable under s. 336 PPC with Qisas, or Arsh and up to ten years Ta'zir where Qisas is not executable. Section 337-U sets the scale of Arsh for teeth, and ss. 332, 335, 336 and 337-U are read together. Pre-arrest bail application dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 1070, 2024 YLR 1339; Sharafat Ali v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 10982/B of 2023, decided 08.03.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Sharafat Ali v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 10982/B of 2023, decided 08.03.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Bail on Statutory Ground of Trial Delay
records.heading: A second post-arrest bail application on the statutory ground of trial delay under the third proviso to section 497 CrPC
records.text: Concerns a second post-arrest bail application on the statutory ground of delay under the third proviso to s. 497 CrPC, after an earlier one was dismissed by the High Court and the Supreme Court, and the petition to cancel bail granted by the High Court. The post records that delay was mainly due to a video-link defect and the accused's illness on some dates. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 290; Syeda Ayesha Subhani v. State, etc (Crl. P. 588-L of 2023, decided 28.08.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Syeda Ayesha Subhani v. State, etc (Crl. P. 588-L of 2023, decided 28.08.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Breaking of Tooth: S. 334 and S. 337-U PPC
records.heading: Breaking of a tooth attracts section 334 PPC, with arsh under section 337-U
records.text: Urdu compilation note: breaking of a tooth attracts s. 334 PPC, while s. 337-U PPC provides the arsh for a tooth. Citations are listed without any holding text. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 1074, PLJ 2023 CrC 1070, PLJ 2022 CrC 1385.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: s. 164 Statement as Evidence Under s. 265-J CrPC
records.heading: A section 164 CrPC statement is evidence under section 265-J only on strict conditions
records.text: Under s. 265-J CrPC a witness's s. 164 CrPC statement is evidence only if recorded in the presence of the accused, with prior notice, with an opportunity of cross-examination, and if the witness is produced and examined at trial. Examination under Art. 133(1) QSO includes cross-examination when desired, so examination-in-chief alone is insufficient. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 1028; Muhammad Rizwan etc v. State and another (Crl. A. Nos. 57199, 57200, 57201 & 57203 of 2019, heard 22.12.2021); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan etc v. State and another (Crl. A. Nos. 57199, 57200, 57201 & 57203 of 2019, heard 22.12.2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Theft Outside Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed for an illiterate woman accused of theft outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was confirmed for an illiterate woman accused under s. 379 PPC, an offence outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. The FIR was lodged after over three months, a co-accused with a similar role had post-arrest bail, and no useful purpose would be served by incarceration. The petition was converted into an appeal and allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 296; Munawar Bibi v. State (Crl. P. No. 90-K of 2023, decided 03.08.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Munawar Bibi v. State (Crl. P. No. 90-K of 2023, decided 03.08.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Fraud Without Specific Dates
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed in a fraud case with no specific dates and further inquiry
records.text: Pre-arrest bail was confirmed in a case under ss. 420, 468 and 471 PPC where no specific dates of the fraud were given and a supplementary statement had widened the net. A co-accused had pre-arrest bail and the principal accused had post-arrest bail. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC, calling for further inquiry. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 311; Ch. Saeed Ahmed Khalil v. State etc (Crl. P. No. 701 of 2023, decided 11.08.2023); Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Ch. Saeed Ahmed Khalil v. State etc (Crl. P. No. 701 of 2023, decided 11.08.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Broad Daylight Murder: Two Places One Transaction
records.heading: Firing at two places 1.5 kilometres apart was one transaction in a daylight murder
records.text: The occurrence took place in broad daylight, the nominated accused were previously known to the witnesses, and the two eyewitnesses were unanimous on the salient features. Firing at two places 1.5 kilometres apart was presumed to be one and the same transaction. The appeal against conviction under s. 302(b) PPC and s. 7 ATA, with life imprisonment, was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 299; Muhammad Hanif v. State (Crl. A. No. 528 of 2019 in J.P. No. 327 of 2018, announced 05.09.2023); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. State (Crl. A. No. 528 of 2019 in J.P. No. 327 of 2018, announced 05.09.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wajtakar Witnesses and Medical Corroboration
records.heading: Consistent wajtakar witnesses with medical corroboration sustain a murder conviction
records.text: Two witnesses from the same locality heard the gunshot and saw the accused fleeing with a pistol, which is wajtakar evidence. They were consistent on every material point, the matter was reported the same day and medical evidence corroborated them. The petition under s. 302 PPC was dismissed and leave to appeal refused. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 338; Muhammad Ijaz v. State (J.P. No. 206 of 2019, decided 08.05.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz v. State (J.P. No. 206 of 2019, decided 08.05.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR and Reliable Ocular Account
records.heading: An FIR lodged after one hour and fifty-five minutes is prompt
records.text: An FIR lodged after one hour and fifty-five minutes was prompt, which prima facie shows truthfulness and excludes deliberation and consultation. The ocular witness explained his presence, was consistent and confidence-inspiring, and medical evidence corroborated him. The appeal against conviction under s. 302 PPC with life imprisonment was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 343; Abdul Wahid v. State (Crl. A. No. 446 of 2020, decided 06.06.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Abdul Wahid v. State (Crl. A. No. 446 of 2020, decided 06.06.2023)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Determination of Juvenile Age: Conflicting Medical Board Report
records.heading: Juvenile age is ordinarily determined on documents despite conflicting medical board estimates
records.text: Under s. 8 of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018, date of birth is ordinarily determined on documentary proof such as birth certificate, educational records and national identity card. The Medical Board gave conflicting estimates (radiology 18 to 20 years, dental 16 to 18 years). The petition against the declaration of the accused as juvenile was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 349; Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Crl. P. No. 1617 of 2022, decided 23.05.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi.
records.title: Gufran Ali v. Haseeb Khan and another (Crl. P. No. 1617 of 2022, decided 23.05.2023)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Suo Motu Contempt: Raid on Judicial Officer's Residence
records.heading: Raiding and confining a judicial officer attracts suo motu contempt punishment
records.text: Appeal against a High Court conviction in suo motu contempt under the Contempt of Court Ordinance 2003, with imprisonment till rising of the court and a fine of Rs. 5000. The appellant had raided a Qazi's residence, assaulted him and confined him for about six hours without a case. The headnote mentions unqualified apology and public confidence in the district judiciary. Ref: PLJ 2023 SC CrC 321; Sultan Ahmed v. Registrar, Balochistan High Court, Quetta and others (Crl. A. No. 633 of 2019, decided 07.06.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Sultan Ahmed v. Registrar, Balochistan High Court, Quetta and others (Crl. A. No. 633 of 2019, decided 07.06.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Annual Increase in Maintenance: Effective Date
records.heading: An annual increase in maintenance runs from the decree unless a retrospective date is justified
records.text: A Family Court decreeing maintenance may also fix an annual increase. If the increase is to apply retrospectively it must give a categoric finding justifying a particular date. Otherwise, where no date is given or no increase is suggested, the increase is deemed applicable from the date of decree. Ref: 2023 LHC 5893; Samia Zaman v. Asad Zaman etc (WP 8786/21, decided 15.11.2023); Justice Faisal Zaman Khan.
records.title: Samia Zaman v. Asad Zaman etc (WP 8786/21, decided 15.11.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: PFSA Protocols: Premature Acquittal under s. 265-K
records.heading: Acquittal under section 265-K CrPC for unrecorded PFSA protocols was premature
records.text: The trial court acquitted the accused under s. 265-K CrPC because protocols were not recorded in the PFSA report. The High Court accepted the appeal against acquittal and remanded the case, holding that the veracity of protocols in a narcotics analysis report can be assessed only once it is tendered in evidence, and premature termination of the prosecution is deprecated. Ref: 2023 LHC 5933; State v. Shafique Ahmad (Crl. Appeal 166-20); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: State v. Shafique Ahmad (Crl. Appeal 166-20)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Additional Note: Elections Within 90 Days of Dissolution
records.heading: Elections were constitutionally due within 90 days, and the President fixes the date under Article 48(5)
records.text: In his additional note, Justice Athar Minallah stated that after dissolution of the National Assembly elections were constitutionally due by 7 November, that fixing the date is the President's power under Art. 48(5), and that fixing 8 February breached the Constitution. He added that the Election Commission cannot be a silent spectator when the President or Governors fail to act. Ref: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P.32/2023, decided 23.11.2023); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P.32/2023, decided 23.11.2023)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Device Versus Disguise in Evading Pre-emption
records.heading: A lawful device to evade pre-emption is permitted but a disguise is not
records.text: A device is permitted but a disguise is not. Where a transaction is given a false colour to evade third party rights, the Court must remove the veil and determine its true character. A person is equally entitled to evade the law of pre-emption by lawful and legitimate devices such as gift or exchange. Ref: Amir Waheed Shah & others v. Ajmal Khan & others (C.A.271/2015, decided 24.11.2023); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Amir Waheed Shah & others v. Ajmal Khan & others (C.A.271/2015, decided 24.11.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Promissory Note: Attestation and Art. 79 QSO
records.heading: A promissory note needs no attestation, so non-production of one attesting witness does not exclude it
records.text: A promissory note meeting the four ingredients of s. 4 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 is not subject to the attestation requirement of Art. 17(2)(a) QSO, so non-production of one attesting witness under Art. 79 does not exclude it. Attestation does not convert it into a bond. The s. 118 presumption of consideration is only prima facie and may be displaced by a probable defence. Ref: Mehr Noor Muhammad v. Nazir Ahmed (C.A.317-L/2011, decided 24.11.2023); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mehr Noor Muhammad v. Nazir Ahmed (C.A.317-L/2011, decided 24.11.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: CSS Examination: Women Quota and Open Merit
records.heading: Women qualifying on open merit are adjusted against open merit seats before the women quota
records.text: On an appeal under s. 7(3)(d) of the Federal Public Service Commission Ordinance 1977, women candidates who qualify the CSS competitive examination on open merit must first be adjusted against open merit seats. The seats of the 10% women quota are then filled from the other women candidates according to merit. Ref: 2023 LHC 5972; Usama Bin Malik v. Federal Public Service Commission etc (F.A.O. 80183/21, decided 08.11.2023); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Usama Bin Malik v. Federal Public Service Commission etc (F.A.O. 80183/21, decided 08.11.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Columns 13 to 16: Dower
records.heading: Unspecified dower is payable on demand and the section 10 presumption needs positive evidence to rebut
records.text: Columns 13 to 16 of the nikahnama record the dower and other property given or to be given by the husband to the wife. Where dower is unspecified it is payable on demand, and the presumption under s. 10 of the Ordinance is rebuttable only by positive evidence. The decision considers whether a house noted against column 16 forms prompt or deferred dower. Ref: 2022 MLD 416.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Decree on Award: S. 12(2) CPC or S. 30
records.heading: Whether a decree on an award is challenged under section 12(2) CPC or section 30
records.text: Authority on whether a decree founded on an award under the Arbitration Act can be challenged by an application under s. 12(2) CPC or only under s. 30 of the Act, and on whether an oral gift needs proof where an award followed it and affects female legal heirs. The post gives the questions only and no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 5982; Shamsa Hameed v. ASJ Khushab etc (Misc. Writ 46285/17, decided 17.11.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Shamsa Hameed v. ASJ Khushab etc (Misc. Writ 46285/17, decided 17.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Criminal Proceedings Through Attorney
records.heading: Criminal proceedings cannot be initiated or evidence recorded through an attorney
records.text: Criminal proceedings cannot be initiated through a general or special attorney. An attorney does not speak of his own knowledge and is neither a witness nor a complainant, so he cannot file an FIR or a criminal complaint, and criminal law has no provision for recording evidence through an attorney. Ref: Khawar Mehmood v. Gul Faraz Ahmed and another (Criminal Appeal No. 44 of 2023, decided 13.11.2023).
records.title: Khawar Mehmood v. Gul Faraz Ahmed and another (Criminal Appeal No. 44 of 2023, decided 13.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 367 CrPC: Reasons for Alternative Sentence
records.heading: Failure to give reasons under section 367(5) CrPC for not awarding death warrants remand
records.text: Only three persons were booked, so the case fell outside dacoity with murder under s. 396 PPC, which needs five or more. The trial court failed to give reasons under s. 367(5) CrPC for not awarding the death sentence. Appeals accepted, judgment set aside and case remanded for rewriting of the judgment, to be concluded preferably within one month. Ref: Saddam Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 01-QOF2022, decided 16.11.2023).
records.title: Saddam Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 01-QOF2022, decided 16.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Purpose and Checks of Police Investigation
records.heading: Police investigation must be fair and impartial and aims to place the truth before the court
records.text: Ss. 157, 160, 161 and related provisions CrPC provide checks and balances so that investigation is fair and impartial, free of political or other pressure. Its aim is to find the truth and place it before the court through evidence collected. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 1475.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: S. 9(c) CNSA: Safe Custody and Transmission of Samples
records.heading: A missing link in the safe custody chain entitles the accused to the benefit of doubt
records.text: In s. 9(c) CNSA cases the prosecution must prove each step from recovery to sample parcel preparation, safe custody and safe transmission to the laboratory. A missing link entitles the accused to the benefit of doubt, as guilt cannot then be held established beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2023 SCMR 139; Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 139 of 2022).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 139 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC: Principles of Judicial Confession
records.heading: A confession must be read as a whole and cannot be split into parts
records.text: A confession, judicial or extra-judicial, must be read as a whole and cannot be split to rely only on the inculpatory part. A solitary confession forming the basis of conviction is accepted or rejected in toto, and it inculpates only its maker. Where other believable prosecution evidence exists, a portion may be rejected in light of that evidence. Ref: 2023 SCMR 139; Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 139 of 2022).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 139 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Art. 150 QSO and Recall
records.heading: A witness is hostile under Article 150 QSO only if he equivocates or suppresses the truth
records.text: To invoke Art. 150 QSO it must be shown that the witness equivocated, varied his statement, tried to suppress the truth or bore animosity to the calling party. An unfavourable witness is not necessarily hostile, and conflict with other witnesses is no ground to treat a witness as hostile. The order allowing the prosecution to recall a witness lacked reasons. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLD 2019 Lah 594.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint Against Police: Defective Investigation
records.heading: A private complaint alleging defective investigation is not maintainable against police officials
records.text: A private complaint under ss. 200 and 204 CrPC alleging defective investigation is not maintainable against police officials. Prosecution can proceed only on a written report by an authorised officer under Art. 155 of the Police Order 2002, or the complainant may approach the police hierarchy. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 1172.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Remissions: S. 9A CNSA Not Retrospective
records.heading: The bar on remissions in section 9A CNSA is prospective only
records.text: S. 9(A)(1) of the Amendment Act 2022, barring remissions, is prospective and cannot be applied retrospectively to a convict arrested, indicted or convicted before its insertion. The Superintendent Jail was directed to grant remissions in accordance with law and rules. Ref: 2023 LHC 6047; Imran Mustafa v. GOP etc (Writ Petition 16629-23, decided 21.11.2023); Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Imran Mustafa v. GOP etc (Writ Petition 16629-23, decided 21.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A(6) CrPC: Justice of Peace Powers
records.heading: A Justice of Peace must not act mechanically or ignore a police report without lawful reasons
records.text: The functions of an Ex-Officio Justice of Peace under s. 22-A CrPC are quasi-judicial and the powers are not unbridled. After requisitioning a police report he must not proceed mechanically or brush the report aside without lawful reasons, in light of the guidelines in Younas Abbas v. Additional Sessions Judge, Chakwal (PLD 2016 SC 581). Ref: 2023 LHC 6035; Ch. Abdul Majeed v. Justice of Peace etc (Writ Petition 3343-23, decided 15.11.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Ch. Abdul Majeed v. Justice of Peace etc (Writ Petition 3343-23, decided 15.11.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Doctrine of Exhaustion of Remedies
records.heading: A litigant must exhaust remedies in the original forum before seeking relief elsewhere
records.text: The doctrine of exhaustion of remedies prevents a litigant from seeking a remedy in a new court or jurisdiction until all claims or remedies have been pursued as fully as possible in the original one. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2075.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitration Act 1940: Writ Not Maintainable Against Award
records.heading: A writ is not maintainable against an award where the Arbitration Act 1940 gives an alternate remedy
records.text: Where parties agreed to a single arbitrator, the Arbitration Act 1940 governs and not the Committee of Arbitration under ss. 260 to 265 of the Cantonments Act 1924. The Arbitration Act provides an alternate remedy, so a writ petition to upset the award was not maintainable. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2075.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Setting Aside Lower Courts' Findings: Reasons
records.heading: A higher court that disagrees with lower courts' findings must examine them and give reasons
records.text: A higher court dissatisfied with the findings of lower courts must examine and discuss them, give reasons for disagreeing, and support its own findings with valid reasons based on the evidence and the law. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2103.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revisional Jurisdiction of High Court: S. 115 CPC
records.heading: The High Court should not substitute its own reading of evidence in revision under section 115
records.text: Revisional jurisdiction is meant to rectify errors, illegalities and material irregularity of subordinate courts. Where the trial court and first appellate court have taken a view of the evidence, the High Court under s. 115 CPC should generally not substitute its own reading, unless the lower courts' view is clearly unreasonable or contradicts settled legal principles. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2103, 2023 SCMR 2133.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Wrong Revenue Entry: Fresh Cause of Action
records.heading: Each new revenue entry may give a fresh cause of action but limitation is not blanketly excused
records.text: Each new ownership entry in the periodical revenue record may give a fresh cause of action, but the plaintiff must show that the last wrong entry came to his knowledge. There is no blanket exemption from limitation for those challenging an admitted wrong entry. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2103.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: Executing Court Cannot Go Behind Decree
records.heading: An executing court must execute a decree as it stands and cannot go behind it
records.text: An executing court must execute a decree as it stands and cannot go behind it. Exceptions: it may decide whether the decree or a severable part is executable, look at the judgment to identify the property if the decree is silent, and refuse execution of a decree that is a nullity, without jurisdiction or in violation of law. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2133.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Meaning of Decree-Holder
records.heading: A decree-holder is anyone entitled to enforce a right under the decree, not only a plaintiff
records.text: A decree determines the rights of the parties, so a decree-holder is any person entitled to enforcement of a right under the decree. This includes defendants and even strangers on whom the decree confers rights, and is not confined to plaintiffs. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2133.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Fraud on the Court
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC applies only to fraud on the court, not fraud between the parties
records.text: S. 12(2) CPC applies only where fraud or misrepresentation was practised on the court and the order was obtained through it. Concealment by a seller that he sold the land during the pendency of an appeal is, at best, fraud between the parties. The purchasers' applications failed, and lis pendens made their purchase subject to the outcome of the litigation. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2158; Sheikh Muhammad Iftikhar Ahmad v. Faiz Ahmad.
records.title: Sheikh Muhammad Iftikhar Ahmad v. Faiz Ahmad

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Doctrine of Lis Pendens
records.heading: A purchaser from a party during a suit is bound by the final decision
records.text: Lis pendens applies when a person purchases from a party during a suit concerning the same property. The parties are bound by the final decision notwithstanding any intermediate alienation. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2158; Sheikh Muhammad Iftikhar Ahmad v. Faiz Ahmad.
records.title: Sheikh Muhammad Iftikhar Ahmad v. Faiz Ahmad

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 155(2) CrPC: Magistrate and Non-Cognizable Investigation
records.heading: A Magistrate may order investigation of a non-cognizable offence only after applying his judicial mind
records.text: S. 155(2) CrPC does not expressly empower a Magistrate to order investigation of a non-cognizable offence, but the police may report and the Magistrate may order it. He must apply his judicial mind and be satisfied that reasonable grounds exist for believing an offence was committed, failing which the order is arbitrary. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2058; Sheikh Humayun Nazir v. State.
records.title: Sheikh Humayun Nazir v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Bail, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC is not for recovery of money and bail follows as further inquiry
records.text: S. 489-F PPC is not meant for recovery of money, for which civil remedies such as O. XXXVII CPC exist. Whether the cheques were issued for a loan or an obligation is for the trial court. The maximum punishment of three years falls outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so s. 497(2) applies. Appeal allowed and bail granted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2122, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 42; Noman Khaliq v. State.
records.title: Noman Khaliq v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Land Dispute, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed in a land dispute where false implication cannot be ruled out
records.text: Where the primary dispute concerns ownership and possession of land, false implication cannot be ruled out. The FIR was lodged after 62 days without explanation, ascribed only a general role to seven accused, and two nominated co-accused were found innocent. The case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC and ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2081.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Valid Gift: Ingredients and Revocation
records.heading: A valid gift needs offer, acceptance and delivery of possession and is revocable only before delivery
records.text: A valid gift requires offer by the donor, acceptance by the donee and delivery of possession, and comes into existence once all three are complete. Under s. 167 of Muhammadan Law a gift can be revoked only before delivery of possession. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2012.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Cancellation of Gift by Donor's Successors
records.heading: A donor's successors cannot cancel a gift the donor confirmed and whose fraud was unproved
records.text: The donor's sworn statement in an earlier pre-emption suit and his signing of the mutation before the revenue authorities confirmed a valid gift. He proved no fraud, so his successors were not entitled to cancellation or revocation of the gift. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2012; Hayat Muhammad v. Muhammad Riaz.
records.title: Hayat Muhammad v. Muhammad Riaz

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 295-B PPC: Acquittal Upheld
records.heading: Acquittal in a section 295-B PPC case upheld for contradictions and false implication
records.text: Leave to appeal against acquittal was declined. The prosecution evidence had material contradictions, a land dispute indicated false implication, independent witnesses were abandoned, the torn pieces of the Holy Quran were not produced, and the accused was an abnormal person. The prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2109.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Preferred Over Medical Evidence
records.heading: Reliable ocular evidence is preferred over medical evidence where the two conflict
records.text: In a qatl-i-amd case ocular evidence is the principal evidence if the witnesses are independent, reliable and confidence inspiring, while expert evidence is confirmatory. If the two conflict on the number of injuries, preference is given to the ocular account. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2016.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Site Plan Versus Ocular Account
records.heading: Witnesses' statements prevail over a site plan, which is not substantive evidence
records.text: Where witnesses' statements about the distance between accused and victim contradict the site plan, the witnesses' statements take precedence. A site plan is not substantive evidence and only explains the occurrence to help the court appreciate the facts. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2016.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 235 CrPC: Offence in Two Phases
records.heading: An occurrence in two phases and places in continuation is one transaction under section 235 CrPC
records.text: An occurrence that began in the court premises and ended 1.5 kilometres away at a tea stall, in continuation of the accused's act, is one transaction covered by s. 235 CrPC. The objection that the occurrence took place away from the court premises had no force. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2016.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: Proof by Attesting Witnesses
records.heading: An agreement to sell is proved by attesting witnesses and the stamp vendor, and cross-examination did not shake it
records.text: Attesting witnesses and the stamp vendor proved the agreement, payment of consideration and delivery of possession, and cross-examination shook none of it. The other legal heirs admitted the transaction, and the petitioner failed to discharge the onus of showing that no agreement was executed. Leave to appeal declined. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2162; Jamshed Ali Shah v. Irshad Hussain Shah.
records.title: Jamshed Ali Shah v. Irshad Hussain Shah

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Temporary Injunction: Three Ingredients
records.heading: A temporary injunction needs a prima facie case, irreparable loss and balance of convenience
records.text: A plaintiff seeking a temporary injunction must establish a prima facie case, irreparable loss if the injunction is refused, and balance of convenience in his favour. A prima facie case is foundational, and the other two conditions are considered only once it is established. Ref: 2023 LHC 6069; Asmat Bibi v. ADJ Ferozwala etc (Misc. Writ 50316/23, decided 15.11.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Asmat Bibi v. ADJ Ferozwala etc (Misc. Writ 50316/23, decided 15.11.2023)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Physical Remand: Principles Under S. 21-E ATA
records.heading: Remand in ATC cases needs an independent mind and a speaking order, as police custody is the exception
records.text: Remand in ATC-triable cases is governed by s. 21-E ATA, with s. 167 CrPC applying so far as consistent. Remand needs the accused to be produced before the Magistrate, who must apply an independent mind, examine the case diaries and pass a speaking order, since police custody is an exception and not the rule. Ref: 2023 LHC 6054; Mansha Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 67181/23, decided 24.10.2023); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mansha Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 67181/23, decided 24.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Trial of Challan Case and Private Complaint
records.heading: A private complaint on the same allegations as the FIR is tried before the challan case
records.text: The Nur Elahi procedure (PLD 1966 SC 708) is generally recommended, with departures for two categories. Where the FIR lodger files a private complaint on the same allegations against the same accused, the complaint is tried first and the challan case held back. Cross-cases with different versions and different accused must be tried together by the same court. Ref: 2023 LHC 6074, PLJ 2024 CrC 795; Asfand Yar etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 37-23, decided 11.10.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Asfand Yar etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 37-23, decided 11.10.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Photographing Narcotics Recovery: Bail Granted
records.heading: Police must photograph narcotics recoveries and bail was allowed for delayed challan
records.text: The Court directed police and ANF officials to photograph or record the narcotics, accused and scene using mobile phones, as admissible evidence under Art. 164 QSO, and to conduct searches before respectable persons of the locality. Bail was allowed on a bond of Rs. 100,000 for delay in the challan and failure to collect evidence in accordance with law. Ref: Zahid Sarfaraz Gill v. The State thr. A.G., Islamabad (Crl.P.1192/2023, decided 22.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Zahid Sarfaraz Gill v. The State thr. A.G., Islamabad (Crl.P.1192/2023, decided 22.11.2023)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: NAB Trial Delay: Right to Expeditious Trial
records.heading: Delay in a NAB trial beyond one year not attributable to the accused is abuse of process
records.text: S. 16 of the National Accountability Ordinance 1999, as amended in 2022, requires the trial to be completed within one year. Delay not attributable to the accused amounts to abuse of process, and every accused has an inalienable right to an expeditious and fair trial guaranteed by Art. 10-A, relying on PLD 2022 SC 497. Ref: 2023 LHC 6132; Ghulam Qadir Khan v. NAB etc (Writ Petition 2366-23, decided 23.11.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Ghulam Qadir Khan v. NAB etc (Writ Petition 2366-23, decided 23.11.2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Consensual Intercourse: Fornication, Not Rape
records.heading: Consensual intercourse is fornication and not rape, and needs a complaint under section 203-C CrPC
records.text: Consensual intercourse falls under fornication, s. 496-B PPC, and not rape. Cognizance of fornication can be taken only on a complaint under s. 203-C CrPC, and a police report is not a complaint. The conviction under s. 376 PPC was set aside and the proceedings declared coram non judice. Ref: 2023 LHC 6139; Muhammad Saleem v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 395-21, decided 25.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Saleem v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 395-21, decided 25.10.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absence of Premeditation and Motive: Sentence
records.heading: Absence of premeditation and unproved motive may mitigate a capital sentence
records.text: Where there is no premeditation to commit murder and the prosecution does not prove motive, this may be treated as a mitigating factor to reduce the sentence in capital punishment cases. Ref: Muhammad Yasin v. The State, etc (Crl.P.476-L/2018, decided 01.11.2023); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan.
records.title: Muhammad Yasin v. The State, etc (Crl.P.476-L/2018, decided 01.11.2023)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Use of the Word August Before Supreme Court
records.heading: The Constitution names the Court as the Supreme Court of Pakistan without any prefix
records.text: The Court observed the repeated use of the word august before the Supreme Court of Pakistan. The Constitution names the Court as the Supreme Court of Pakistan without any prefix or adjective, and all should follow that description. Ref: M. Taimoor Ali v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.1294/2023, decided 28.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: M. Taimoor Ali v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.1294/2023, decided 28.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Fresh Ground: Counsel Should Not Withdraw Petition
records.heading: Counsel should insist on a decision on merits instead of withdrawing a petition with a fresh ground
records.text: If a fresh ground became available before the impugned order, counsel should not withdraw the petition and should insist on a decision on merits, the position being settled by Nazir Ahmad v. State (PLD 2014 SC 241) and Muhammad Aslam v. State (PLD 2015 SC 41). The petition was dismissed as withdrawn. Ref: M. Taimoor Ali v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.1294/2023, decided 28.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: M. Taimoor Ali v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.1294/2023, decided 28.11.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: A chance witness who gives no plausible reason for his presence gives suspect testimony
records.text: An eye-witness who lived 5 or 6 km away, had no business there and gave no plausible reason for his presence was a chance witness whose testimony was suspect. His account of the wounds was also unconfirmed by medical evidence, so the ocular account was unreliable and the prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1834.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion: Defective Warrant and Proclamation
records.heading: Absconsion must be proved and a defective warrant and proclamation fail to prove it
records.text: Absconsion must be proved like any other fact. The warrant was not addressed to a police officer or public servant and the proclamation stated no period or date for surrender, so both were defective and absconsion was not proved. Absconsion is in any case not proof of the charge. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1834.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Non-Functional Pistol
records.heading: Recovery of a non-functional pistol with no empty is inconsequential and gives no corroboration
records.text: Recovery of a pistol that the Forensic Science Agency found non-functional, with no empty recovered from the place of occurrence, was inconsequential and gave no corroboration to the prosecution. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1834.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Contradicting Time of Death
records.heading: A medical time-of-death estimate contradicted by rigor mortis is ipse dixit and fails the prosecution
records.text: Death was immediate, so rigor mortis began later and lasted longer. As rigor mortis was fully developed, the interval between death and post-mortem could not be under twelve hours, and the medical officer's estimate of five to six hours was ipse dixit. The alleged time of occurrence was not proved and the prosecution case fell. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1834.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Unsupported by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Wounds described by eye-witnesses but absent in the post-mortem report are fatal to the prosecution
records.text: The complainant described entry wounds on the front of the abdomen and left rib, but the post-mortem report found none. Where eye-witnesses themselves state the exact locale of wounds and medical evidence does not confirm it, the prosecution must bear the consequence. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1834.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Contradictions on Place of Occurrence and FIR
records.heading: Contradictions on where the complainant's statement was recorded place the occurrence under a cloud
records.text: The place where the complainant's statement was recorded was under a cloud because the SI gave a different account. The exact position of the deceased was not stated, no blood or firearm marks were found, and her clothes bore no holes or blood. The exact place of occurrence was therefore also under a cloud. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1834.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved
records.heading: A motive attains vital importance in a killing by a closely related person but is lost once the ocular account fails
records.text: Where a person is killed by a closely related person, any motive alleged attains vital importance. The alleged grudge over a maintenance decree was undermined because the decree was conditional on rehabilitation with the accused. Also, once the ocular account is disbelieved, motive loses efficacy. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1834.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: FSA Report Not Exhibited: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: An unexhibited FSA report cannot sustain a conviction and a prosecutor's statement cannot cure it
records.text: In a s. 9(c) case involving 10 kg 200 g of charas, the Forensic Science Agency report was on the record but was never exhibited, and a prosecutor's unsworn statement could not cure this. The report could not be considered to maintain the conviction, recovery became inconsequential and the prosecution case fell. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1806.

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.topic: Removal of Name From Passport Control List
records.heading: Placing a name on the Passport Control List on police recommendation was unlawful
records.text: The Islamabad High Court held that placing the petitioner's name on the Passport Control List, on the recommendation of Islamabad Police, was unfair and unlawful. It ordered the DG Immigration to remove her name within one week and report to the Deputy Registrar. Ref: Dr. Shireen M. Mazari v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Interior, Ministry of Interior, Islamabad and another (Writ Petition No. 2212 of 2023).
records.title: Dr. Shireen M. Mazari v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Interior, Ministry of Interior, Islamabad and another (Writ Petition No. 2212 of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody Agreements and Mother's Remarriage
records.heading: Custody agreements between parents are unenforceable and remarriage alone does not bar a mother's custody
records.text: Agreements between parents about custody of children are against public policy and unenforceable. Remarriage of the mother is not a stand-alone ground to deprive her of custody, relying on Raja Muhammad Owais v. Nazia Jabeen (2022 SCMR 2123). The Family Court must also evaluate the adverse effects of separating siblings. Ref: 2023 LHC 6165; Imtiaz Hussain v. District Judge etc (Family 244677/18, decided 13.11.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Imtiaz Hussain v. District Judge etc (Family 244677/18, decided 13.11.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence and Fair Trial
records.heading: A fair trial and the presumption of innocence require proof beyond reasonable doubt
records.text: The right to a fair trial is an integral limb of safe administration of criminal justice and is crucial to avoid erroneous verdicts. Every person is presumed innocent until proven guilty, the prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, and doubt is resolved in favour of the accused. Ref: Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad, etc (Crl.P.290-L/2015, decided 27.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad, etc (Crl.P.290-L/2015, decided 27.11.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Age Relaxation for Assistant Conservator of Forests
records.heading: Questions on the blanket age relaxation for Assistant Conservator of Forests under rule 12(1)
records.text: Authority on the blanket 15 year age relaxation notification for the post of Assistant Conservator of Forests, under rule 12(1) of the Rules, and on the selection of stipendiary candidates not mentioned in the advertisement. The post lists the questions framed and gives no holding. Ref: Ayaz and others v. Mustafa Saeed and others (C.P.231/2022, decided 27.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Ayaz and others v. Mustafa Saeed and others (C.P.231/2022, decided 27.11.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Declaring a Witness Hostile or Unfavourable
records.heading: Only the court can declare a witness hostile, and unfavourable evidence is not itself vindictive
records.text: A witness can be declared hostile only by the court, generally at the request of counsel, having regard to demeanour and credibility. The court may treat a witness as merely unfavourable, and unfavourable evidence does not by itself show vindictiveness. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 1026.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 155 QSO: Refreshing Memory
records.heading: A witness may refresh memory under Article 155 QSO only after indicating a lapse or need
records.text: A witness may refresh his memory under Art. 155 QSO only after indicating a memory lapse or need for a document, and the court must follow the proper procedure. The trial court allowed unrestricted access to the police file and the witness recited from it. His earlier recorded statement was held inadmissible and of no legal effect. Ref: PLD 2023 Pesh 160.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 493 CrPC: Private Counsel and Hostile Witness
records.heading: Private counsel may seek to declare a witness hostile where the Public Prosecutor does not object
records.text: A privately engaged counsel need not sit aloof and may seek to have a witness declared hostile and cross-examine him, as the Public Prosecutor did not object and consent is presumed. Under s. 493 CrPC and Art. 150 QSO there is no harm in the court permitting it. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLD 2020 Sindh 596.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Hostile Versus Unfavourable Witness
records.heading: A witness giving unfavourable evidence in an unguarded moment is not hostile under Article 150 QSO
records.text: A witness who in an unguarded moment gave unfavourable evidence, with nothing to show deliberate suppression of truth, cannot be treated as hostile. A hostile witness resiles from an earlier statement and damages the calling party, whereas an unfavourable witness has no hostile intention. Hostility can be allowed only during examination-in-chief. Petition allowed. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 1472.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Memo of Appearance and Dead Defendant
records.heading: A memo of appearance is no authorisation and a decree against a dead person is a nullity
records.text: A memo of appearance is not an authorisation to represent a litigant and at most intimates that a power of attorney will follow. A decree against a dead person is a nullity. Concurrent orders under s. 12(2) read with O. IX R. 13 CPC setting aside a specific performance decree were upheld and the petition dismissed in limine with costs of Rs. 50,000. Ref: 2021 CLC 684; Justice Ch. Muhammad Masood Jehangir.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Request to Declare Witness Hostile
records.heading: A request to declare a witness hostile should be made when the adverse statement is given
records.text: Where a witness makes an adverse statement, a request to declare him hostile can be made at that moment so that the truth is drawn out through cross-examination. The requirement of law cannot be excused. Ref: 2021 CLC 684; Justice Ch. Muhammad Masood Jehangir.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Mehr Payable on Demand: Compensatory Costs
records.heading: Mehr is payable when the wife demands it and non-payment attracts compensatory costs
records.text: Mehr (dower) must be paid when the wife demands it. Compensatory costs were imposed for failure to pay it. Ref: Khalid Pervaiz v. Samina, etc (C.P.2734-L/2023, decided 20.11.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Khalid Pervaiz v. Samina, etc (C.P.2734-L/2023, decided 20.11.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Bail Petition: Same Grounds Not Competent
records.heading: A second bail petition on the same or earlier available grounds is not competent
records.text: A second bail petition repeating earlier grounds, or grounds available earlier, is not competent, except for entitlement on statutory grounds under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC. Delay caused by the accused defeats that right, and recording the last witness's statement does not mean the trial is complete. Ref: Muhammad Usman v. The State through P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.P.1233/2023, decided 30.11.2023); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. The State through P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.P.1233/2023, decided 30.11.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale by Minor Void
records.heading: A minor cannot enter a sale contract, so sales made by him are void
records.text: A minor is incompetent to enter into a legal sale contract of his property, so the sale transactions made were void. Ref: Noorullah & Others v. Ghulam Murtaza & Others (C.A.17-Q/2023, decided 10.11.2023); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Noorullah & Others v. Ghulam Murtaza & Others (C.A.17-Q/2023, decided 10.11.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Deposit and Readiness to Pay
records.heading: A vendee seeking specific performance must deposit the price and show readiness to pay
records.text: Where the vendor refuses to accept the sale consideration, the vendee seeking specific performance must deposit the amount in court. He must show he was at all times ready and willing to pay and had the amount available, since he cannot enforce the vendor's obligation without showing his own willingness and capability. Ref: Masood Ahmad Bhatti and another v. Khan Badshah and another (C.P.5632/2021, decided 16.11.2023); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Masood Ahmad Bhatti and another v. Khan Badshah and another (C.P.5632/2021, decided 16.11.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Grandchildren's Share Under S. 4 of the Ordinance 1961
records.heading: Grandchildren take their deceased parent's share under section 4 where succession opened after the Ordinance
records.text: Under s. 4 of the Ordinance 1961 grandchildren take a share equal to that of their deceased parent, whether the parent died before or after the promulgation. The only condition is that the succession opened after the promulgation of the Ordinance. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 900.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Proof of Parentage: Acknowledgment or Treatment
records.heading: Parentage is presumed from the father's acknowledgment or course of treatment in his lifetime
records.text: Where parentage of a child cannot easily be ascertained, it is generally presumed from the father's express acknowledgment or from a course of treatment given by him in his lifetime. Ref: 2023 LHC 6187; Zainab Bibi v. Abdul Aziz (Civil Revision 479-D-01, decided 25.10.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Zainab Bibi v. Abdul Aziz (Civil Revision 479-D-01, decided 25.10.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Private Partition: S. 147 Land Revenue Act 1967
records.heading: A private partition confers no right without affirmation by the revenue officer under section 147
records.text: A party pleading a private partition under a family settlement must apply to the revenue officer for affirmation under s. 147 of the Land Revenue Act 1967. Without an order of affirmation, the party relying on the private partition cannot claim any right under it. Ref: 2023 LHC 6202; Mubarak Ahmad v. Muhammad Hayat etc (Civil Revision 341-17, decided 16.11.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Mubarak Ahmad v. Muhammad Hayat etc (Civil Revision 341-17, decided 16.11.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Limitation and Arts. 102, 103 QSO
records.heading: Oral evidence cannot vary a documented contract and limitation for specific performance runs from the fixed date
records.text: Arts. 102 and 103 QSO exclude oral evidence to prove or vary the terms of a documented contract. For specific performance, limitation runs from the date fixed for performance or, if none, from notice of refusal. On concurrent findings the suit was filed over three years late and the petitioner was not entitled to relief. Ref: 2023 LHC 6245; Robina Kausar v. Umar Majeeb Shami (Civil Revision 75693/22, decided 05.12.2023); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: Robina Kausar v. Umar Majeeb Shami (Civil Revision 75693/22, decided 05.12.2023)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-e-Muwathibat: Strict Proof
records.heading: Pre-emption is extinguished unless Talb-e-Muwathibat is strictly proved with credible evidence
records.text: Under s. 13 of the Act, the right of pre-emption is extinguished unless Talb-e-Muwathibat, Talb-e-Ishhad and Talb-e-Khasoomat are made. For Talb-e-Muwathibat the pre-emptor must prove who informed him of the sale, when and where, who was present in the Majlis, and his immediate declaration, by credible and independent evidence. Ref: 2023 LHC 6235; Muhammad Munir (Deceased) through LRs Kashif Munir and 6 others v. Muhammad Zia Ullah etc (Civil Revision 63814/23, decided 04.12.2023); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: Muhammad Munir (Deceased) through LRs Kashif Munir and 6 others v. Muhammad Zia Ullah etc (Civil Revision 63814/23, decided 04.12.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Marz-ul-Maut: Burden of Proof
records.heading: The plea of marz-ul-maut failed for want of medical or other proof
records.text: The plea that the deceased was suffering from marz-ul-maut was not proved by any medical or other evidence worthy of consideration. Ref: 2023 LHC 6258; Mst. Samina Kausar etc v. Mst. Nasreen Bibi etc (Civil Revision 661-12, decided 28.11.2023); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: Mst. Samina Kausar etc v. Mst. Nasreen Bibi etc (Civil Revision 661-12, decided 28.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 145 CrPC: Nature and Scope
