records.heading: Section 145 CrPC proceedings are executive and aim to prevent a breach of the peace
records.text: Proceedings under s. 145 CrPC are executive in nature and do not adjudicate ownership or possession. Their purpose is to prevent a likely breach of the peace and maintain status quo. The dispute must concern land or water within the Magistrate's jurisdiction, and the Magistrate's satisfaction on these pre-conditions must be reflected in the preliminary order. Ref: Aminullah & others v. Syed Haji Muhammad Ayub & others (C.P.116/2020, decided 07.12.2023); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Aminullah & others v. Syed Haji Muhammad Ayub & others (C.P.116/2020, decided 07.12.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed FIR, Suspect Witnesses, Medical Evidence
records.heading: An unexplained delayed FIR and suspect witnesses are fatal and medical evidence cannot identify the assailant
records.text: An FIR not promptly recorded without reasonable explanation is fatal to the prosecution. Witnesses who cannot explain their arrival at the scene at odd hours give suspect evidence. Medical evidence is only supportive and cannot identify the assailant. Ref: 2023 LHC 6219; Mst. Gulnaz Ajmal v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 72371/19, decided 23.11.2023); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Mst. Gulnaz Ajmal v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 72371/19, decided 23.11.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Ex-Parte Decree: Limitation Under S. 9(7) Family Courts Act
records.heading: The 30 day period to set aside an ex-parte family decree runs from service under section 9(7)
records.text: Under the Family Courts Act 1964 the 30 day limit for applying to set aside an ex-parte decree runs from service of notice under s. 9(7), added by Ordinance LV of 2002. Where a rule is inconsistent with the statute, the statute prevails. Ref: 2023 LHC 6270; Fazal Hussain v. Razia Begum etc (Writ Petition 2998-18, decided 23.11.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Fazal Hussain v. Razia Begum etc (Writ Petition 2998-18, decided 23.11.2023)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Avenfield Reference: Acquittal Appeal Allowed
records.heading: Appeal allowed and the appellant acquitted in the Avenfield Reference
records.text: Appeal allowed and the appellant acquitted. The Court noted observations in Criminal Appeal No. 122/2018 that NAB had not proved its case as no document established guilt, and that no appeal had been preferred against that judgment. Detailed reasons were to follow. Ref: Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif v. The Chairman, NAB (Crl. Appeal No. 121/2018, decided 29.11.2023).
records.title: Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif v. The Chairman, NAB (Crl. Appeal No. 121/2018, decided 29.11.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Will: Nature, One-Third Limit and Heirs' Consent
records.heading: A will operates after death up to one third and heirs' help with mutation proves their consent
records.text: A will is a disposition taking effect after death and is rescindable, and it does not bind the testator before death. Bequests are permissible up to one third. If other heirs help the legatee to effect mutation or allow exclusive possession after the testator's death, that is proof of the heirs' consent. Ref: 2023 LHC 6276; Mst. Kaniz Fatima v. Ghulam Hussai (Civil Revision 751-D-04, decided 03.10.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Mst. Kaniz Fatima v. Ghulam Hussai (Civil Revision 751-D-04, decided 03.10.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Registered Deed: Mutation Cannot Be Cancelled Unheard
records.heading: A revenue officer cannot cancel a mutation on a registered deed without hearing the purchaser
records.text: The revenue officer was bound to incorporate the registered deed in the revenue record and could not cancel the mutation without notice and hearing to the purchaser. A registered document is notice to the public, and revenue entries are made for fiscal purposes and are not foundation of title. Ref: 2023 LHC 6290; Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93, decided 31.05.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93, decided 31.05.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 41 Transfer of Property Act: Ostensible Owner
records.heading: Section 41 Transfer of Property Act protection fails if any one ingredient is missing
records.text: A person claiming protection under s. 41 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 must show the transferor was an ostensible owner, the transfer was with the real owner's express or implied consent, it was for consideration, and the transferee acted in good faith with reasonable care. Failure of any one ingredient defeats the protection. Ref: 2023 LHC 6290; Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93, decided 31.05.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93, decided 31.05.2023)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test Mandatory in Rape Cases
records.heading: A DNA test and preservation of DNA evidence is mandatory in rape cases
records.text: In rape cases administration of a DNA test and preservation of DNA evidence is mandatory. Ref: Salman Mushtaq and another v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.1121/2023, decided 08.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Salman Mushtaq and another v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.1121/2023, decided 08.11.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Further Inquiry and Reasonable Grounds
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail turns on harassment or malice and gravity alone does not justify refusal
records.text: Pre-arrest bail turns on whether arrest would cause humiliation or harassment for ulterior motives or the prosecution is malicious. The gravity of an offence alone does not justify refusing bail where the evidence creates doubt. Where there are no reasonable grounds to believe the accused committed the offence, further inquiry is made out. Ref: Salman Mushtaq and another v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.1121/2023, decided 08.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Salman Mushtaq and another v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.1121/2023, decided 08.11.2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Marriage of Girl Under 16: Not Rape
records.heading: Marriage of an underage girl is punishable under the 1929 Act and is not rape
records.text: Marriage of an underage girl is punishable only under the Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929, which does not declare such marriage void. The offence in s. 375 PPC cannot be equated with consensual consummation of marriage with a legally wedded girl who has attained puberty, though below the minimum age. Ref: Nazar Muhammad v. DPO Okara etc. (Criminal Proceedings 57371/23, order pronounced 19.10.2023); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Nazar Muhammad v. DPO Okara etc. (Criminal Proceedings 57371/23, order pronounced 19.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Judicial Versus Administrative Orders of Magistrate
records.heading: A judicial order of a Magistrate attracts res judicata while an administrative order does not
records.text: A judicial order involves power to hear and determine a controversy and make a binding decision, attracts res judicata and functus officio, and is conclusive in collateral proceedings. An administrative order can be attacked for any error in direct or collateral proceedings, cannot be res judicata and may be rescinded by the body making it. Ref: PLD 2020 Lah 77.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Columns 5, 5-A and 21-A: No Criminal Liability
records.heading: Nikahnama columns did not require disclosure of the groom's status, so no criminal liability arose
records.text: Column 5-A required the number and names of children only if the bride was a widow or divorcee with children, and did not require disclosure of her status. The form used had no column expressly requiring disclosure that the groom was a widower or divorcee, so respondents 5 to 8 could not be burdened with criminal liability. Ref: 2023 MLD 2016.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Deliberate Default in Family Suit
records.heading: A petitioner who deliberately disappeared from a family suit after fair opportunities was in default
records.text: The petitioner was given fair opportunities to file a written statement and pursue the case but deliberately disappeared without valid justification. The Court also noted that the Act was enacted because female litigants previously waited years for dower, maintenance and dissolution. Ref: 2023 MLD 2073.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 182 PPC: Show Cause Notice and Justice of Peace
records.heading: A Justice of Peace cannot direct police to initiate action under section 182 PPC
records.text: Before action under s. 182 PPC, the person to be prosecuted should receive a show cause notice and an opportunity to explain. An Ex-officio Justice of Peace can direct the police, but they are not subordinate to him under s. 195(1)(a) CrPC, so he cannot direct a police officer to initiate action under s. 182 PPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 6369; Shoaib Sohail v. Learned JoP etc (Criminal Proceedings 598/23, decided 09.01.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Shoaib Sohail v. Learned JoP etc (Criminal Proceedings 598/23, decided 09.01.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Trial Court Sending Entire Material to PFSA
records.heading: A trial court cannot direct sending the entire material to PFSA to let the prosecution fill lacunas
records.text: Of 35 packets opened, samples were drawn from only two. The trial court's direction to send the entire material to the PFSA gave the prosecution a premium to fill lacunas, which is contrary to the adversarial system and violates the fundamental right to fair trial and due process. Ref: 2023 LHC 6365; Asad Ullah v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 654-23, decided 20.07.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Asad Ullah v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 654-23, decided 20.07.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Attorney's Power to Sell Excludes Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A power to sell does not include a power to enter into an agreement to sell
records.text: A power to sell does not include a power to enter into an agreement to sell, which binds the principal to future performance. Without a specific power, the attorney cannot bind the principal, so the agreement to sell sought to be enforced was bad. Ref: 2023 LHC 6374; Sughran Bibi etc v. Muhammad Nawaz etc (Civil Revision 2401-14, decided 30.10.2023); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Sughran Bibi etc v. Muhammad Nawaz etc (Civil Revision 2401-14, decided 30.10.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution Against Surety: S. 145 CPC
records.heading: A decree can be executed against a surety to the extent of his personal liability
records.text: Under s. 145 CPC a decree can be executed against a surety to the extent of his personal liability, and after default he cannot escape the agreed amount, per s. 128 of the Contract Act 1872. The surety could not wriggle out of his own undertaking, but the Executing Court was directed to decide his objection on the amount paid after framing issues and taking evidence. Ref: 2023 CLC 2169.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Plea of Guilt at Any Stage of Trial
records.heading: A plea of guilt may be recorded at any stage but a capital trial needs evidence
records.text: There is no prohibition on recording a plea of guilt at any stage of trial, even if the accused denied the charge at framing. The court must examine why guilt is admitted, and a trial for a capital offence must not end on an admission alone, as evidence must be recorded. Ref: 2023 LHC 6388; State v. Muhammad Altaf (Crl. Appeal 482-22, decided 14.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: State v. Muhammad Altaf (Crl. Appeal 482-22, decided 14.11.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Suspension of Single Bench Judgment: In Personam Effect
records.heading: A Single Bench judgment suspended by a Division Bench is suspended only in personam
records.text: A Single Bench judgment suspended by a Division Bench is suspended only in personam for that case. Interpretation based on unambiguous provisions and Supreme Court judgments remains binding in rem, as law cannot be suspended, relying on Federation of Pakistan v. Aitzaz Ahsan (PLD 1989 SC 61). Ref: 2023 LHC 6408; MS Hadi Developers Private Limited through Zafar Iqbal v. Government of the Punjab etc (WP 70681/23, decided 15.11.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: MS Hadi Developers Private Limited through Zafar Iqbal v. Government of the Punjab etc (WP 70681/23, decided 15.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Order under s. 204 CrPC
records.heading: Issuing process under section 204 CrPC needs only a tentative assessment and not proof of guilt
records.text: For issuing process under s. 204 CrPC, evidence sufficient to establish guilt is not required; only a tentative assessment showing sufficient ground to proceed, and detailed reasons are not needed. The revisional court went beyond its limits by relying on an earlier FIR that was not before the summoning court. The accused's proper course was an application under s. 249-A CrPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 6412; Muhammad Akbar Ali v. Addl. Sessions Judge Zafarwal etc. (Crl. Misc. 43746/23, decided 01.12.2023); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Akbar Ali v. Addl. Sessions Judge Zafarwal etc. (Crl. Misc. 43746/23, decided 01.12.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Civil Appeal 981 of 2018 Order
records.heading: Order in Civil Appeal 981 of 2018 decided on 11.12.2023, with no holding
records.text: Order in Civil Appeal 981 of 2018 decided on 11.12.2023. The post gives only the case details and no holding. Ref: Sardar Confcius Imam Qasrani v. Sardar Mir Badshah Khan Qaisarani & another (C.A. 981/2018, decided 11.12.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Sardar Confcius Imam Qasrani v. Sardar Mir Badshah Khan Qaisarani & another (C.A. 981/2018, decided 11.12.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail allowed where the ingredients of criminal breach of trust were not made out
records.text: The ingredients of criminal breach of trust under s. 406 PPC are entrustment, and dishonest misappropriation, conversion, use or disposal of the property in violation of a legal direction or contract. The ingredients of s. 405 PPC were not made out on the record. Pre-arrest bail allowed. Ref: 2023 LHC 6463; Ghulam Nazik etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 7916-B/2023, decided 06.11.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Ghulam Nazik etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 7916-B/2023, decided 06.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recall of Witness, Second PFSA Report
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC cannot be used to let the prosecution fill lacunas with a second PFSA report
records.text: Power under s. 540 CrPC to recall a witness must not be used to give one party an illegal advantage. Allowing the prosecution to submit a second PFSA report, or to have the analyst conduct a fresh test under s. 510 CrPC, would let it fill lacunas in its case. The court must remain a neutral arbiter and not assume the role of prosecutor. Ref: 2023 LHC 6420; Muhammad Ramzan v. State etc (Crl. Revision 352/2023, decided 04.12.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. State etc (Crl. Revision 352/2023, decided 04.12.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Accused Declared Innocent by Police
records.heading: A person found innocent by the police is not an accused, and bail allowed as further inquiry
records.text: A person cannot be termed an accused unless the investigating officer finds him involved and orders his arrest. The police finding of innocence, placing him in column No. II of the report, though not binding on the court, was based on cogent material and brought the case within further inquiry for bail. Offence under s. 302 PPC. Bail allowed. Ref: 2023 LHC 6448; Muhammad Imran v. The State (Crl. Misc. 5878-B/2023, decided 12.10.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State (Crl. Misc. 5878-B/2023, decided 12.10.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail on Medical Grounds: Blindness
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed on medical grounds where the accused is blind
records.text: Post-arrest bail allowed on medical grounds, the accused suffering from loss of eyesight or blindness. Ref: 2023 LHC 6429; Muhammad Akmal v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 1554-B/2023, decided 11.09.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Akmal v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 1554-B/2023, decided 11.09.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ex-Officio Justice of Peace Functus Officio
records.heading: An Ex-Officio Justice of Peace is functus officio after passing an order
records.text: After passing an order, the Ex-Officio Justice of Peace becomes functus officio and cannot recall his earlier order at the time of its implementation. Ref: 2023 LHC 6438; Mst. Robina Khatoon v. ASJ etc (Writ Petition 5109/2020, decided 20.11.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Mst. Robina Khatoon v. ASJ etc (Writ Petition 5109/2020, decided 20.11.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Claim Against Paternal Uncle
records.heading: A paternal uncle cannot replace the grandfather as defendant in a maintenance claim
records.text: Mulla's Muhammadan Law is neither a statute nor a custom or usage and so does not bind the courts. A claim of maintenance from a grandfather and one from a paternal uncle rest on different principles of Islamic jurisprudence, so the uncle could not replace the grandfather as defendant after the grandfather's death. Ref: 2023 LHC 6415; Mahnoor Shabbir through Sajida Safdar v. ADJ etc (Family 62482/2022, decided 12.12.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Mahnoor Shabbir through Sajida Safdar v. ADJ etc (Family 62482/2022, decided 12.12.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Duty Magistrate: Discharge at Physical Remand
records.heading: A Duty Magistrate can discharge an accused produced for physical remand
records.text: A Duty Magistrate can discharge an accused who is produced before him for physical remand. Ref: 2023 LHC 6453; Muhammad Bilal v. State etc (Writ Petition 15198/2023, decided 25.10.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Bilal v. State etc (Writ Petition 15198/2023, decided 25.10.2023)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Bail of Juvenile in Heinous Offence
records.heading: A juvenile connected with a heinous offence by reasonable grounds does not deserve bail on juvenility alone
records.text: Where reasonable grounds on the record connect the petitioner with a heinous offence, he does not deserve the concession of bail even on the ground of juvenility, in light of s. 4(6) of the Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018. Ref: 2023 LHC 6469; Abdul Rehman v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 62271/2023, decided 13.12.2023); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 62271/2023, decided 13.12.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Bhutto Reference: Points for Consideration
records.heading: Order identifying the first points for consideration in the Bhutto Presidential Reference
records.text: Order of 12.12.2023 identifying the first points for consideration in the Presidential Reference under Art. 186: maintainability, whether a factual inquiry is needed, the legitimacy of the trial and appeal, and whether judges were removed to secure a result. Two former judges were appointed amici curiae to assist, with submissions due by 5 January 2024. Ref: Reference by the President of Islamic Republic of Pakistan Under Article 186 of the Constitution to revisit the case of Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto (Reference 1/2011, decided 12.12.2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Reference by the President of Islamic Republic of Pakistan Under Article 186 of the Constitution to revisit the case of Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto (Reference 1/2011, decided 12.12.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Right to Privacy: Media Filming of Citizens
records.heading: Media filming and questioning citizens in the presence of officials intrudes on the right to privacy
records.text: Persons with cameras and microphones who film citizens and question them about licences and documents, in the presence of public functionaries, intrude on the constitutional right to privacy, respect and dignity, and no one is bound to answer them. Public functionaries are directed not to facilitate such illegality, and officials who aid the violation are liable. Ref: Vishal Ahmad Shakir v. Federation of Pakistan (Writ Petition 80758/2023, decided 13.12.2023).
records.title: Vishal Ahmad Shakir v. Federation of Pakistan (Writ Petition 80758/2023, decided 13.12.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Public Safety Commissions under Police Order 2002
records.heading: The Provincial Government must notify Safety Commissions under section 37 of the Police Order 2002
records.text: The Provincial Government is directed to notify Provincial and District Safety Commissions under s. 37 of the Police Order 2002, within 30 days according to the Urdu report. The court held that failure of a public authority to perform its legal duty violates the law and Constitution, and that there cannot be a gap in governance through chosen representatives, read with Art. 140A. Ref: 2023 LHC 6402; Muhammad Razzaq etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Misc. Writ 5973/2017, decided 16.11.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Razzaq etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Misc. Writ 5973/2017, decided 16.11.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Intra Court Appeals: Military Trial of Civilians
records.heading: First interlocutory order in intra court appeals on military trial of civilians, suspending the earlier decision
records.text: First interlocutory order in intra court appeals under s. 5 of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023 against the order of 23.10.2023 declaring s. 2(1)(d) and s. 59(4) of the Pakistan Army Act, 1952 ultra vires the Constitution. The Urdu caption states that the order suspended that decision. Ref: Shuhada Forum, Balochistan through its Patron in Chief, Nawabzada Jamal Raisani, Quetta Cantt and others v. Justice (R) Jawwad S. Khawaja and others (I.C.A. 5/2023, decided 13.12.2023); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Mussarat Hilali; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Shuhada Forum, Balochistan through its Patron in Chief, Nawabzada Jamal Raisani, Quetta Cantt and others v. Justice (R) Jawwad S. Khawaja and others (I.C.A. 5/2023, decided 13.12.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sara Inam Murder: Conviction and Death Sentence
records.heading: Trial court convicted the accused under section 302(b) PPC and imposed the death sentence
records.text: The trial court held the prosecution had proved the case and convicted the accused under s. 302(b) PPC for killing the victim by repeated blows with a heavy dumbbell. Death sentence with fine of Rs 1 million payable to the heirs. The co-accused Samina Shah was not named in the FIR and no evidence of abetment was produced against her. Ref: Justice Nasir Javed Rana.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal in Murder Case and Weapon Recovery Case
records.heading: An accused acquitted in the murder case is entitled to acquittal in the weapon recovery case
records.text: Urdu and English note: an accused acquitted in the main murder case is also entitled to acquittal in the separately registered case under s. 13/20/65 for recovery of the unlicensed weapon used in the murder. Only citations are listed. Ref: 2021 YLR 1906, 2014 MLD 1561, 2012 MLD 1315, PLD 1996 Karachi 345.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Preventive Detention under s. 3 MPO
records.heading: Preventive detention under section 3 MPO without sufficient and cogent material violates Article 9
records.text: An order of preventive detention passed without sufficient and cogent material violates Art. 9 of the Constitution. The authority issuing an order under s. 3 of the MPO must satisfy itself that the material before it is sufficient to justify the detention, and the power cannot be used on grounds other than those the law provides. Ref: Saghir Razzaq v. Deputy Commissioner, Layyah etc. (Writ Petition 19212/2023, decided 14.12.2023).
records.title: Saghir Razzaq v. Deputy Commissioner, Layyah etc. (Writ Petition 19212/2023, decided 14.12.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 140 and 151 QSO: Previous Statement of Witness
records.heading: Article 140 QSO lets a witness explain inconsistency with his previous statement
records.text: Art. 140 QSO serves to give the witness an opportunity to explain inconsistency with his previous statement and to equip the other side to impeach his credibility. It is read with Art. 151(3), which permits impeaching credit by former inconsistent statements but does not provide the manner of proof, which Art. 140 supplies. Ref: PLD 1996 Lah 512.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Executive Officers as DROs and ROs: Interim Suspension
records.heading: Executive officers' appointment as election officers suspended pending a larger bench decision
records.text: A challenge to ss. 50(1)(b) and 51(1) of the Elections Act 2017 under Arts. 218(3) and 220 was referred to the Chief Justice for a larger bench. Meanwhile the ECP notifications of 11.12.2023 appointing District Returning Officers, Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers from the executive were suspended. Ref: Barrister Umair Khan Niazi v. Election Commission of Pakistan, etc. (W.P. No. 80828/2023), decided 13.12.2023; Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.
records.title: Barrister Umair Khan Niazi v. Election Commission of Pakistan, etc. (W.P. No. 80828/2023), decided 13.12.2023

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Concurrent Findings in Family Execution: No Interference
records.heading: The High Court will not disturb concurrent findings of Family Courts that accord with law and evidence
records.text: The High Court in constitutional jurisdiction would not interfere with concurrent findings of the Family Court and appellate court that accorded with law and evidence, where no jurisdictional error or irregularity in proceedings was shown. Ref: 2023 CLC 2169.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIV R. 5 CPC: Framing of Additional Issues
records.heading: The court must frame the correct issues under Order XIV Rule 5 CPC at any stage
records.text: Framing of issues is a vital stage of trial. The power under O. XIV R. 5 CPC can be exercised at any stage before final disposal, even by the appellate court. The court is bound to frame correct issues necessary to determine the real controversy even if the parties have not pointed them out, and a party cannot suffer for the court's inaction. Ref: 2023 CLC 2071.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Additional Issues and Production of Mutation Copy
records.heading: Failure to frame a material issue and consider a mutation copy makes the orders a nullity
records.text: Where the plaint raised a material proposition of fact and law that the written statements denied, a proper issue had to be framed and the trial court failed to do so. Both courts below also failed to consider the request to produce a copy of a mutation, which was essential for just decision, making their orders a nullity in the eye of law. Ref: 2023 CLC 2071.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Withdrawal of Suit: Disclosure of Formal Defect
records.heading: Withdrawal of a suit with liberty to file afresh needs disclosure of a formal defect
records.text: A plaintiff seeking permission to withdraw a suit and file afresh must disclose a formal defect of such a nature that the suit must fail, and the court must be satisfied of this. Absent such disclosure the civil court rightly refused permission, and the revisional court transgressed its powers. The High Court set aside the appellate order under Art. 199. Ref: 2023 CLC 2042.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Instances of Formal Defect in Suit
records.heading: Formal defects in a suit include misjoinder, wrong valuation and non-impleading of a necessary party
records.text: Instances of formal defect include misjoinder of parties or causes of action leading to failure of the suit, erroneous valuation of the subject matter, insufficient description of the property, failure to disclose a cause of action, a material document not properly stamped, non-impleading of a necessary party, and the form of the suit. Ref: 2023 CLC 2042.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ of Mandamus: Scope under Art. 199(1)(a)(i)
records.heading: Mandamus under Article 199(1)(a)(i) directs functionaries to do what the law requires and no more
records.text: A writ in the nature of mandamus under Art. 199(1)(a)(i) is a direction to a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Federation, a Province or a Local Government to do what the law requires. The High Court's jurisdiction is limited to ensuring state functionaries do what the law requires, and it oversteps if it directs beyond that. Ref: 2023 CLC 2156.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Visitation Schedule: Welfare of Minor
records.heading: Minor's welfare is paramount and a father may be given overnight visitation to build a bond
records.text: In guardian proceedings the welfare of the minor is paramount. Limited meetings within court premises do not allow a bond to develop with the non-custodial parent. Where the mother had remarried and the minor lived with maternal relatives, the father, who had relinquished custody, was entitled to more time, including overnight stays, to develop a fatherly bond. Ref: 2023 CLC 2110.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Divorce: Jurisdiction of Union Council
records.heading: For a wife abroad, divorce under section 7 MFLO goes before the Pakistan Mission officer, not a Lahore Chairman
records.text: Under s. 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 the Union Council with jurisdiction is the one where the wife resides at the time of pronouncement of divorce. As she was abroad, under S.R.O. 1086(K)/61 dated 09.11.1961 officers of Pakistan Missions abroad discharge the Chairman's functions, so the Chairman Union Council at Lahore had no authority. Ref: 2023 CLC 2025.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant's Estoppel: Art. 115 QSO
records.heading: A tenant cannot question the landlord's title without first surrendering possession
records.text: A tenant cannot question the landlord's title as it stood at the commencement of tenancy. He must first surrender possession and then dispute it, and Art. 115 QSO bars denial of his status once tenancy is proved. A tenant who purchases a share from a co-owner does not cease to be a tenant. Eviction under the Punjab Rented Premises Act upheld. Ref: 2023 CLC 2140.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 24 CPC: Transfer of Cases by District Judge
records.heading: A District Judge may transfer a case under section 24 CPC, which specifies no ground
records.text: A District Judge, on his own or on an application, may transfer a case from one subordinate court to another or hear it himself. S. 24 CPC specifies no ground for transfer. The contention that he went beyond the application and showed personal interest was held misconceived, and remarks about the petitioner's reservations against the Additional District Judges were not to be read as part of the order. Ref: 2023 LHC 6496; Madrissa Tul Madina & Gumbad e Khizra v. Lahore Development Authority etc (Civil Revision 74007/2023, decided 08.12.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Madrissa Tul Madina & Gumbad e Khizra v. Lahore Development Authority etc (Civil Revision 74007/2023, decided 08.12.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Defective Pleadings: Non-Compliance with CPC
records.heading: Pleadings often fail to comply with Orders VI, VII and VIII CPC and judges overlook the defects
records.text: The Supreme Court noted that pleadings often fail to comply with Orders VI, VII and VIII CPC: no prayer clause, no verification under O. VI R. 15, no list of legal heirs, and no statements on jurisdiction, cause of action, valuation or court fees. Judges overlook these defects. Bar Councils were called upon to assist and may submit written proposals. Ref: Fazeelat Nasreen and another v. Maqsood Begum and others (Civil Review Petition 410/2023 in Civil Appeal 310/2021).
records.title: Fazeelat Nasreen and another v. Maqsood Begum and others (Civil Review Petition 410/2023 in Civil Appeal 310/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supply of Documents to Accused: s. 94 and Art. 10-A
records.heading: Documents not appended to the section 173 report cannot be used as surprise evidence against the accused
records.text: Documents on which the prosecution is to be structured must be supplied to the accused in good time. The CDR and recovery memo collected by the I.O. but not appended to the s. 173 CrPC report cannot be used as surprise evidence, as due process under Art. 10-A requires a fair opportunity to prepare the defence. The trial court may summon documents under s. 94 CrPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 6503; Sabir Hussain v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 200/2023, decided 13.12.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Sabir Hussain v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 200/2023, decided 13.12.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: S. 130(2) ITO 2001: Appointment of Tribunal Members
records.heading: Prime Minister in section 130(2) of the Income Tax Ordinance is read down to Federal Government
records.text: The words Prime Minister in s. 130(2) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 are read down to mean Federal Government. Appointments of the Chairman and Members of the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue made by the Prime Minister under the 2020 Appointment Rules are declared ultra vires. Ref: 2023 LHC 6550; Lahore Tax Bar Association v. Federation of Pakistan etc (27339/23, decided 18.12.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Lahore Tax Bar Association v. Federation of Pakistan etc (27339/23, decided 18.12.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: General Elections Cannot Be Delayed After Election Programme
records.heading: General elections cannot be delayed or derailed after announcement of the Election Programme
records.text: In a democracy general elections cannot be delayed or derailed after announcement of the Election Programme. Ref: Gul Khan and others v. Saeed ur Rehman and others (C.P. 4305/2023, decided 18.12.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Gul Khan and others v. Saeed ur Rehman and others (C.P. 4305/2023, decided 18.12.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 29(2) Limitation Act: Appeal Against Acquittal under CNSA
records.heading: Section 5 Limitation Act does not apply to delay in a CNSA appeal against acquittal
records.text: S. 29(2) of the Limitation Act excludes the application of s. 5 for condonation of delay in filing an appeal against acquittal under s. 48 of the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997. Ref: 2023 LHC 6572; State v. Muhammad Imran (Crl. Appeal 275/2020, decided 12.12.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: State v. Muhammad Imran (Crl. Appeal 275/2020, decided 12.12.2023)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Advocate as PCB Election Commissioner: Rule 108-O
records.heading: Challenge to a practising advocate's appointment as PCB Election Commissioner under Rule 108-O
records.text: Challenge to the appointment of a practising advocate as Election Commissioner for the PCB Chairman election, on the ground that he had not suspended his licence under Rule 108-O of the Pakistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Rules, 1976, and to his mandate on composition of the Board of Governors. The court read the mandate as the conduct of the Chairman's election to complete the BoG composition. Ref: 2023 LHC 6592; Muhammad Faisal Labar v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (80447/23, decided 15.12.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Faisal Labar v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (80447/23, decided 15.12.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Rules of Cross-Examination: Lengthy Cross-Examination
records.heading: The judgment lays down rules for cross-examination and deprecates lengthy cross-examination
records.text: The judgment lays down essential rules for cross-examining witnesses and deprecates lengthy cross-examination. Ref: 2023 LHC 6578; Muhammad Zafar alias Ghulabi v. The State (Crl. Appeal 71/2022, decided 29.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Zafar alias Ghulabi v. The State (Crl. Appeal 71/2022, decided 29.11.2023)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Re-allotment of Surrendered Land in Prohibited Zone
records.heading: Surrendered land in a prohibited zone cannot be re-allotted and such orders are void ab initio
records.text: Under para. 18(3) of MLR 115/1972, surrendered or resumed state land within the prohibited zone of a Municipal Committee can neither be allotted nor have proprietary rights granted. Any such order is void ab initio. Writ petition allowed, all re-allotments and grants of proprietary rights cancelled, and Tawan to be recovered from sitting occupants. Ref: 2023 LHC 6607; Faiz Ahmad etc v. Chairman Federal Land Commission etc (254943/18, decided 07.12.2023); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Faiz Ahmad etc v. Chairman Federal Land Commission etc (254943/18, decided 07.12.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Undecided Application for Additional Evidence
records.heading: A pending undecided application for additional evidence justified setting aside the appellate judgment
records.text: An application for permission to record additional evidence goes to the root of the matter. Pendency of such an undecided application was enough to set aside the appellate court's judgment, as the court failed to exercise its jurisdiction and prejudiced the petitioner. Ref: 2023 LHC 6602; Amjad Amin Lodhi v. ADJ etc (Writ Petition 9272/2021, decided 13.12.2023); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Amjad Amin Lodhi v. ADJ etc (Writ Petition 9272/2021, decided 13.12.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 503/506 PPC: Intimidation and Overt Act
records.heading: Section 506 PPC does not apply once a section 503 threat has materialised into an overt act
records.text: Where a threat of criminal intimidation under s. 503 PPC has materialised into an overt act, s. 506 PPC does not apply. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2081, PLJ 2023 SC CrC 315.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Sexual Abuse of Minor under s. 377-A PPC
records.heading: Bail allowed for sexual abuse of a minor where a 14 year minimum appeared disproportionate
records.text: No medical examination of the minor was done as the allegation was of mere attempt. S. 377-A PPC covers a wide range of acts but carries a minimum of 14 years, which appeared disproportionate where less than an attempt was prima facie visible, a matter for trial. Bail allowed, with directions to the SHO and I.O. to take measures for safeguarding the victim and his family. Ref: 2023 MLD 2082.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Age of Victim and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Rape conviction set aside where the victim's age was unproved and the evidence defective
records.text: No evidence showed the victim was under age, the question was not put to the accused under s. 342 CrPC, and the medico-legal report gave no basis for the stated age. The victim's account was unsupported by DNA or medical evidence and the prosecution was marked by defects and contradictions. Benefit of doubt extended, conviction set aside and accused acquitted. Ref: 2023 MLD 2037.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cartridge Cases: Comparison with Weapon at PFSA
records.heading: Cartridge cases must be sent to PFSA and redeposited for later comparison with an absconder's weapon
records.text: Cartridge cases are to be submitted to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency, Lahore for comparison with the weapon. If any accused is an absconder, the cartridge cases, after exhibition in the trial of another accused, are to be deposited again with the PFSA until compared with the weapon later recovered from the absconder.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Jail Trial in Cypher Case: Notification Set Aside
records.heading: The notification ordering a jail trial in the cypher case was declared void
records.text: The detailed judgment of 19.12.2023 declares void the notification of 29 August ordering a jail trial of the accused in the cypher case. The short order was issued on 21.11.2023 and the 59 page detailed judgment was authored by Mian Gul Hassan Aurangzeb J. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan and others (I.C.A. 367/2023, decided 19.12.2023); Justice Mian Gul Hassan Aurangzeb; Justice Saman Rafat Imtiaz.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan and others (I.C.A. 367/2023, decided 19.12.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 180 PPC: Refusal to Sign Statement
records.heading: Procedure for trial of a section 180 PPC offence on refusal to sign a statement
records.text: Authority on the procedure for trial of an offence under s. 180 PPC upon refusal to sign the statement or charge sheet. Ref: 2023 LHC 6660; Kashif Nawaz etc v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 531/2023, decided 19.12.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kashif Nawaz etc v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 531/2023, decided 19.12.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Defamation and Perjury: Route of Trial
records.heading: Different routes of trial for defamation and perjury, and judicial proceeding during investigation
records.text: Authority on the different routes of trial for defamation and perjury, and on the concept of judicial proceeding during investigation. Appeal against acquittal. Ref: 2023 LHC 6664; Sumera Rasheed v. The State etc (PSLA 7/2023, decided 27.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Sumera Rasheed v. The State etc (PSLA 7/2023, decided 27.11.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal Powers as Civil Court
records.heading: A Service Tribunal deciding an appeal is deemed a civil court with the same powers
records.text: Discusses ss. 20 and 26 of the Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2010 and ss. 16 and 19 of the Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability Act, 2006. For deciding an appeal the Service Tribunal is deemed a civil court with the same powers as such a court. Ref: Rafaqat Ali v. Chief Secretary, Government of the Punjab, Lahore and others (C.P. 460/2022, decided 21.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Rafaqat Ali v. Chief Secretary, Government of the Punjab, Lahore and others (C.P. 460/2022, decided 21.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 512 CrPC: Statements Against Absconding Accused
records.heading: Evidence recorded against an absconding accused under section 512 CrPC may be used in a later trial
records.text: S. 512 CrPC preserves the record of evidence given in the absence of an absconding accused. A deposition so recorded can be used if the deponent is dead or his evidence cannot be procured without delay, expense or inconvenience. Documents exhibited in the statement form part of it and need no re-exhibition in the later trial of a co-accused. Ref: Abdul Moeen v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 04-I/2022, decided 07.12.2023).
records.title: Abdul Moeen v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 04-I/2022, decided 07.12.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Level Playing Field: Duty of ECP
records.heading: Petition on a level playing field disposed of, recording the duty of the ECP
records.text: Petition under Art. 184(3) by the PTI Chairman alleging arrests, harassment and snatching of nomination papers of its members, seeking that the ECP ensure free and fair elections with a level playing field. The order records the duty of the ECP in this regard. Petition disposed of. Ref: Gohar Ali Khan v. Federation of Pakistan through its Secretary, Ministry of Interior Government of Pakistan, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 47/2023, decided 22.12.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Gohar Ali Khan v. Federation of Pakistan through its Secretary, Ministry of Interior Government of Pakistan, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 47/2023, decided 22.12.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail under Official Secrets Act: Cypher Case
records.heading: Offences under section 5(1) of the Official Secrets Act are bailable and bail was granted to both accused
records.text: Offences under s. 5(1)(a) to (d) of the Official Secrets Act, 1923 are generally punishable under s. 5(3)(b) with up to two years, and are bailable under s. 12(1)(b). The court considered that the treatment of political dissidents during elections calls for favourable consideration of bail as a rule. Bail granted to both accused. Ref: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. The State through D.A.G. & another (Crl.P. 1276/2023, decided 22.12.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. The State through D.A.G. & another (Crl.P. 1276/2023, decided 22.12.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: PTI Intra-Party Elections: Election Symbol
records.heading: Election Commission declared PTI ineligible for its election symbol after defective intra-party elections
records.text: The Election Commission held that PTI failed to hold intra-party elections in accordance with its constitution, rejected the certificate dated 4 December 2023 and Form 65, and invoked s. 215 of the Elections Act, 2017 to declare PTI ineligible to obtain the election symbol it applied for.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Caretaker Government and Approved Development Projects
records.heading: A caretaker government may fund projects already approved by the elected government
records.text: A caretaker government may expend funds on projects already determined and approved by the elected government, relying on PLD 2023 Lahore 257. The interim government was directed to publish details of previously sanctioned projects and those initiated by it within 15 days. Ref: 2023 LHC 6820; Nouman Arshad v. The Director General LDA etc (2977/21, decided 21.12.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Nouman Arshad v. The Director General LDA etc (2977/21, decided 21.12.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Transit Anticipatory Bail: s. 438 CrPC (India)
records.heading: Transit anticipatory bail may be granted under section 438 CrPC for an FIR registered outside jurisdiction
records.text: The High Court or Court of Session may grant limited anticipatory bail as interim protection under s. 438 CrPC for an FIR registered outside its territorial jurisdiction, subject to conditions. These include notice to the investigating officer and public prosecutor on the first hearing and recorded reasons for the apprehension of inter-state arrest. Ref: Priya Indoria v. State of Karnataka and Ors. (Criminal Appeal arising out of SLP (Crl.) Nos. 11423-11426 of 2023, decided 20.11.2023); Justice B.V. Nagarathna; Justice Ujjal Bhuyan.
records.title: Priya Indoria v. State of Karnataka and Ors. (Criminal Appeal arising out of SLP (Crl.) Nos. 11423-11426 of 2023, decided 20.11.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence and DNA in Homicide
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form an unbroken chain and DNA evidence only corroborates for the prosecution
records.text: In homicide cases resting on circumstantial evidence, each incriminating circumstance must be clearly established and all must be interwoven into an unbroken chain, one end touching the corpse and the other proving the accused's guilt. DNA evidence can only corroborate for the prosecution, while it has probative value for disproving the charge. The post refers to failure to prove proper sampling of anal swabs. Ref: 2023 LHC 6692; The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55/2019, decided 30.11.2023); Justice Abdul Aziz.
records.title: The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55/2019, decided 30.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Execution on Accused's Statement in Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: An Additional District Judge cannot begin execution on an accused's statement in a pre-arrest bail petition
records.text: An Additional District Judge cannot initiate execution proceedings on the basis of a statement of an accused person recorded by him during pendency of a pre-arrest bail petition. Petition allowed and the order for attachment of property set aside. Ref: 2023 LHC 6744; Muhammad Arif v. ASJ etc (Writ Petition 10312/2023, decided 12.12.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. ASJ etc (Writ Petition 10312/2023, decided 12.12.2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Prison Rules Judgment
records.heading: Prison rules judgment noted by its Urdu caption, with no holding given
records.text: Authority on prison rules, according to the Urdu caption. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 6711; Razia Bibi v. Province of Punjab etc (24030/22, decided 25.07.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Razia Bibi v. Province of Punjab etc (24030/22, decided 25.07.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Punishments under s. 53 PPC: Arsh, Daman, Diyat
records.heading: Section 53 PPC punishments include qisas, diyat, arsh, daman and ta'zir
records.text: Explains the punishments a court may impose under s. 53 PPC, including qisas, diyat, arsh, daman and ta'zir, and the definitions of arsh, daman and diyat in s. 299 PPC. Daman under s. 337-Y PPC may be paid in a lump sum or in instalments over five years. Ref: 2023 LHC 6754; Manzoor Hussain v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 40476/19, decided 07.11.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Manzoor Hussain v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 40476/19, decided 07.11.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Recorded Conversation: CD
records.heading: A recorded conversation on a CD is not proved without the mobile phone and forensic analysis
records.text: A conversation recorded on a mobile phone and converted into a CD cannot be proved by producing the CD alone, without producing the mobile phone and forensic analysis of the conversation. Ref: 2023 LHC 6759; Abu Bakar Samoosa etc etc. v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 228667/18, decided 19.12.2023); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Abu Bakar Samoosa etc etc. v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 228667/18, decided 19.12.2023)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Self-Cheque and Bearer Cheque under s. 489-F PPC
records.heading: A cheque payable to self only does not attract section 489-F PPC
records.text: A cheque made payable to self only does not attract s. 489-F PPC, since a person cannot dishonestly issue a cheque to pay himself. Where it is payable to self or bearer and bearer is not scored off, a holder in due course under s. 9 NIA may initiate action under s. 489-F. The police officer cannot judge the veracity of allegations when registering an FIR. Ref: 2023 LHC 6808; Tariq Mehmood v. ASJ JOP etc (Criminal Proceedings 68498/22, decided 15.12.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Tariq Mehmood v. ASJ JOP etc (Criminal Proceedings 68498/22, decided 15.12.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Vires of Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023
records.heading: Detailed judgment on the vires of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023
records.text: Detailed judgment on the constitution petitions challenging the vires of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023. The post gives only the case details and no holding. Ref: Constitution Petitions No. 6 to 8, 10 to 12, 18 to 20 and 33 of 2023.
records.title: Constitution Petitions No. 6 to 8, 10 to 12, 18 to 20 and 33 of 2023

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: 3 MPO Powers in Islamabad Capital Territory
records.heading: Federal Cabinet alone acts for the ICT, so the Deputy Commissioner cannot issue 3 MPO orders
records.text: The Federal Government is both Federal and Provincial Government for the ICT, and following Mustafa Impex any government decision or action for the ICT can only be taken by the Federal Cabinet as collegium. The Presidential Orders of 1980, 1987 and 1990 and notifications declaring the Administrator or Chief Commissioner to be Provincial Government were declared ultra vires. The Urdu report says the Deputy Commissioner cannot issue 3 MPO orders. Ref: Shehryar Afridi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior & others (Writ Petition 2491/2023); Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Shehryar Afridi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior & others (Writ Petition 2491/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Intra Court Appeal Against Art. 199 Order
records.heading: Whether an intra court appeal lies against a Single Judge's order under Article 199
records.text: The matter concerns whether a statutory right of intra court appeal under the Law Reforms Ordinance 1972 can lie against a Single Judge's order under Art. 199. One Judge issued notices under O. XXVII-A CPC and proposed referral to the Chief Justice. The post indicates the other view was that the case should be decided first and the question left for other proceedings. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2058; Sheikh Humayun Nazir v. State; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Sheikh Humayun Nazir v. State

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Delimitation of Constituencies: Objections
records.heading: Election Commission rejected objections to the draft delimitation of constituencies PP-8 and PP-9
records.text: Petitioners' objections to the draft delimitation of constituencies PP-8 and PP-9 were rejected by the Election Commission on 26.11.2023. The judgment reviews the Election Commission's role under Art. 218 of the Constitution and ss. 19 and 20 of the Elections Act, 2017 on the manner and principles of delimitation. Ref: 2023 LHC 6842; Waheed Mehmood v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 4099/2023, decided 14.12.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Waheed Mehmood v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 4099/2023, decided 14.12.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation: Arts. 56 and 115 and s. 14
records.heading: Which Limitation Act Article governs a suit and whether section 14 excludes Ombudsman time
records.text: The question was which Article of the Limitation Act governs a suit, Art. 56 for price of work done or Art. 115 for compensation for breach of contract, and whether time spent before the Federal Ombudsman could be excluded under s. 14 for a suit filed in 2006. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 6823; Pakistan Railways etc. v. Misri Khan etc (Civil Revision 661/2017, decided 06.12.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Pakistan Railways etc. v. Misri Khan etc (Civil Revision 661/2017, decided 06.12.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pending Miscellaneous Application Before Final Judgment
records.heading: A final judgment given with a miscellaneous application pending is a nullity
records.text: A court must decide a pending miscellaneous application before finalising the lis. Failure to do so renders the final judgment a nullity in the eye of law, relying on 1991 SCMR 1232. Ref: 2023 LHC 6830; Sabira Bibi etc v. Mst. Safura Jan etc (Writ Petition 1475/2023, decided 07.12.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Sabira Bibi etc v. Mst. Safura Jan etc (Writ Petition 1475/2023, decided 07.12.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. V R. 20 CPC: Substituted Service
records.heading: Order V Rule 20 CPC prescribes substituted service, and ex-parte proceedings followed publication
records.text: Order V CPC governs issuance and service of summons, and O. V R. 20 CPC prescribes the mode of substituted service. The case concerned ex-parte proceedings ordered after substituted service by newspaper publication. Ref: 2023 LHC 6855; Muhammad Aurangzeb etc v. ADJ etc (Writ Petition 4158/2023, decided 13.12.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Aurangzeb etc v. ADJ etc (Writ Petition 4158/2023, decided 13.12.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Alternate Remedy and Election of Remedy
records.heading: A party who opts for a statutory remedy cannot abandon it under the doctrine of election
records.text: Art. 199 powers are not unbridled. Despite an alternate remedy the High Court may exercise jurisdiction where circumstances demand, but not in an omnibus fashion. A party who opts for a statutory remedy against an order cannot abandon it, and such a trend offends the doctrine of election, relying on PLD 1992 SC 847. Ref: 2023 LHC 6836; Syeda Farzana Batool etc v. Iltaf Hussain Shah etc (Writ Petition 2154/2022, decided 13.12.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Syeda Farzana Batool etc v. Iltaf Hussain Shah etc (Writ Petition 2154/2022, decided 13.12.2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Concurrent Departmental and Criminal Proceedings
records.heading: Acquittal in a criminal trial does not bar concurrent disciplinary proceedings
records.text: Acquittal in a criminal trial is no embargo against disciplinary proceedings, and the two may proceed concurrently without one impinging on the other. An acquittal may be considered in the disciplinary proceedings but cannot be the sole determining factor in deciding their outcome. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2111; Manzar Abbas v. District Police Officer, Sargodha.
records.title: Manzar Abbas v. District Police Officer, Sargodha

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Police Officials: Dismissal for Gross Misconduct
records.heading: Police officials' misuse of position on a motorway was held gross misconduct by majority
records.text: The majority view held that convincing material showed police officials in uniform travelling in a private car on a motorway without permission and abusing their position, amounting to gross misconduct. Another part of the headnote records that on one allegation the inquiry officer collected no evidence and that, even if true, dismissal was not warranted. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2111; Manzar Abbas v. District Police Officer, Sargodha; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Manzar Abbas v. District Police Officer, Sargodha

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Order of Acquittal under s. 249-A: Revision and Writ
records.heading: Neither revision nor a writ lies against an acquittal order under section 249-A CrPC
records.text: Against an order of acquittal under s. 249-A CrPC, a criminal revision under s. 439 CrPC is not competent. A writ petition against the acquittal order is also not competent in light of s. 417(2) CrPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 6869; Hajra Javaid Makhdoom v. Muhammad Tehmas Nasir etc (Criminal Proceedings 59534/22, decided 19.12.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Hajra Javaid Makhdoom v. Muhammad Tehmas Nasir etc (Criminal Proceedings 59534/22, decided 19.12.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Jaifah under s. 337-D PPC
records.heading: Jaifah under section 337-D PPC needs a cavity injury directly caused by the trauma
records.text: For s. 337-D PPC, the injury in the body cavity must be a direct consequence of the trauma inflicted by the perpetrator and not its fall-out or by-product. The court criticised the medical officer's incorrect opinion and expected the Secretary (Health), Punjab to sensitise medical officers to the importance of their opinions in criminal cases. Ref: 2023 LHC 6876; Rashid v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 3229-B/2023, decided 20.12.2023); Justice Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Rashid v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 3229-B/2023, decided 20.12.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: PTI Symbol Case: Writ Not Maintainable
records.heading: A writ on the PTI symbol was not maintainable where the same proceedings were pending elsewhere
records.text: A writ against the ECP decision on PTI intra-party elections and the election symbol was held not maintainable, as the same proceedings were pending before different benches of the Peshawar High Court. Dismissed in limine under the doctrine of Limine Control, relying on PLD 2019 Lah 407. Ref: 2024 LHC 1; Umar Aftab Dhillon and 1 other v. ECP etc (287/24, decided 03.01.2024); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Umar Aftab Dhillon and 1 other v. ECP etc (287/24, decided 03.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 62(1)(f): Period of Disqualification
records.heading: Article 62(1)(f) disqualification lasts as long as the court declaration remains in force
records.text: Where a court declaration against a candidate implies dishonesty, breach of trust or similar failings, the consequent incapacity under Art. 62(1)(f) lasts as long as the declaration remains in force. If the declaration attains finality, the embargo has permanent effect. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 405; Sami Ullah Baloch and others v. Abdul Karim Nosherwani and others; Justice Mian Saqib Nisar; Justice Azmat Saeed; Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Sajjad Ali Shah.
records.title: Sami Ullah Baloch and others v. Abdul Karim Nosherwani and others

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 62(1)(f): Duration of Disqualification
records.heading: Article 62(1)(f) disqualification lasts while the declaration stands and is permanent once final
records.text: Disqualification under Art. 62(1)(f) of the Constitution lasts as long as the court declaration of lack of sagacity, honesty or trustworthiness remains in force, and becomes permanent once that declaration is final. It is distinct from the five year disqualification under Art. 63(1)(h), and does not unreasonably curtail Art. 17(2). Ref: PLD 2018 SC 405; Sami Ullah Baloch and others v. Abdul Karim Nosherwani and others (Civil Appeal 233/2015 and connected matters, decided 13.04.2018); Justice Mian Saqib Nisar; Justice Sh. Azmat Saeed; Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Sajjad Ali Shah.
records.title: Sami Ullah Baloch and others v. Abdul Karim Nosherwani and others (Civil Appeal 233/2015 and connected matters, decided 13.04.2018)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Interpreting Conflicting Constitutional Provisions
records.heading: Constitutional provisions are read harmoniously and only irreconcilable ones yield
records.text: The Constitution is an organic document to be read as a whole, with each provision applied harmoniously. Only where two provisions are irreconcilable, and one was inserted while the Constitution was in abeyance, does that provision yield, provided the other was enforced by parliamentary will and is closer to the Preamble. Ref: PLD 2018 SC 405; Sami Ullah Baloch and others v. Abdul Karim Nosherwani and others (Civil Appeal 233/2015 and connected matters, decided 13.04.2018); Justice Mian Saqib Nisar; Justice Sh. Azmat Saeed; Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Sajjad Ali Shah.
records.title: Sami Ullah Baloch and others v. Abdul Karim Nosherwani and others (Civil Appeal 233/2015 and connected matters, decided 13.04.2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Interim Injunction: Unregistered Trade Marks
records.heading: An interim injunction for unregistered trade marks is not granted as a matter of course
records.text: An interim injunction is a preventive relief preserving the status quo until the suit concludes. After a prima facie case, the court must examine balance of convenience and irreparable loss. For unregistered marks it should not be granted as a matter of course, and suits when the right by prior use and its infringement are shown with some clarity. Ref: 2023 LHC 6883; Ms Samsara Couture House Pvt Ltd etc v. Syeda Khadija Batool etc (F.A.O. 7892/20, decided 13.12.2023); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Ms Samsara Couture House Pvt Ltd etc v. Syeda Khadija Batool etc (F.A.O. 7892/20, decided 13.12.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct and Accused's Statement Read in Toto
records.heading: The accused's statement is accepted or rejected in toto once the prosecution fails
records.text: The prosecution must first prove its case. If it fails, the statement of the accused is to be accepted or rejected in toto, and it is not permissible to accept the inculpatory part and reject the exculpatory part. The post also lists unnatural conduct of witnesses and conflict between ocular and medical evidence on the number of injuries. Ref: 2023 LHC 6893; Rafaqat Ali v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 36587/19); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Rafaqat Ali v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 36587/19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eye Witness Account: Number of Injuries
records.heading: An eye witness cannot give an exact picture of each injury amid the panic of firing
records.text: An eye witness cannot give an exact picture of each injury sustained by the deceased given the panic caused by firing. The occurrence was in broad daylight so mis-identification was unlikely, and the two eye witnesses, not shaken in cross-examination, corroborated each other and were confidence inspiring. Ref: 2023 LHC 6917; Muhammad Sarwar v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 56707/19, decided 02.11.2023); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Sarwar v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 56707/19, decided 02.11.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Accused's Statement Accepted in Toto: s. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: If the accused's statement is accepted in toto, the case falls under section 302(c) PPC
records.text: If prosecution evidence is disbelieved, the statement of the accused is to be accepted or rejected in toto. If the appellant's statement is accepted in toto, to his extent the case falls under s. 302(c) PPC and not s. 302(b) PPC. The post also lists delay in post mortem, unnatural conduct of witnesses and no source of light. Ref: 2023 LHC 6928; Muhammad Rafique etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 5537/22); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 5537/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Delay in FIR and Post Mortem
records.heading: Delayed FIR and post mortem with chance witnesses suggest an unseen occurrence
records.text: Delay in lodging the FIR and in the post mortem suggests the occurrence was unseen and the time was used to procure false eye witnesses. Witnesses who could not justify their presence were chance witnesses, and their conduct as silent spectators was unnatural, so their evidence was not worthy of reliance. Ref: 2023 LHC 6950; Imran Ali v. The State etc (Criminal Appeal No. 68692-J of 2020); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Imran Ali v. The State etc (Criminal Appeal No. 68692-J of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Body, Chance Witnesses, Adverse Inference
records.heading: Recovery of a body from the accused's house alone cannot support a capital conviction
records.text: Mere recovery of a dead body from the accused's house is not sufficient for a capital conviction without reliable corroboration. The eye witnesses were chance witnesses with unnatural conduct, there was delay in FIR and post mortem and conflict with medical evidence, and an adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO was drawn for withholding the best evidence. Ref: 2023 LHC 6967; Haq Nawaz v. The State (Jail Appeal 64474/22); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Haq Nawaz v. The State (Jail Appeal 64474/22)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Polygamy: s. 6 MFLO and Abetment
records.heading: Section 6 MFLO penalises only the man who remarries and does not create abetment
records.text: S. 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance penalises only the man who contracts another marriage without the Arbitration Council's permission. It does not make registration of such a marriage an offence nor create inchoate offences, so abetment under s. 109 PPC cannot be read into s. 6(5). Ref: 2023 LHC 6888; Mst. Sidra-Tul-Muntaha v. ASJ Lahore etc (WP 84511/23, decided 21.12.2023); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Mst. Sidra-Tul-Muntaha v. ASJ Lahore etc (WP 84511/23, decided 21.12.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Improvements Contradicting Medical Evidence
records.heading: Witnesses' improvements on the number of injuries, conflicting with medical evidence, make them unreliable
records.text: Prosecution witnesses improved their statements at trial on the number of injuries to the deceased's chest and shoulder, in conflict with the medical evidence, so their evidence was not worthy of reliance. The post also lists chance witnesses and delay in post mortem. Ref: 2023 LHC 6940; Qasim Ali v. The State (Jail Appeal 80274/22); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Qasim Ali v. The State (Jail Appeal 80274/22)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023: Additional Note
records.heading: Additional note on the topics raised by the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023
records.text: Note of Muhammad Ali Mazhar J on the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023, covering legislative competence, intra vires and ultra vires, retrospective right of appeal, Arts. 184 and 199, reading down, change of counsel in review, master of the roster, effect on decided cases and hearing by full court. The post gives only the topics. Ref: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad and others (Const.P. 6/2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad and others (Const.P. 6/2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Substitution of Returning Officer by ECP
records.heading: The ECP had justifiable reasons to substitute a returning officer and its discretion was lawful
records.text: The Supreme Court held the ECP had justifiable reasons to substitute the returning officer and its discretion was not illegal. The ad-interim ex-parte order of the Peshawar High Court, passed without notice to the ECP, was set aside by converting the petition into an appeal, and the writ dismissed. Scrutiny of nomination papers to proceed on a fresh schedule. Ref: Election Commission of Pakistan v. Dawood Shah and others (C.P. 4522/2023, decided 02.01.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Election Commission of Pakistan v. Dawood Shah and others (C.P. 4522/2023, decided 02.01.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Missing Persons: Directions to Commission
records.heading: The Commission was directed to submit details of missing persons to the Attorney-General
records.text: The Commission was directed to collate and submit details of missing persons, including who reported them, when they went missing, whether recovered and efforts made, and the production orders not complied with. The information goes to the Attorney-General within ten days, who is to respond within twenty days thereafter. Ref: Civil Petitions No. 1503, 1504 & 1505 of 2022 and Civil Petition No. 4333 of 2021 (decided 03.01.2024).
records.title: Civil Petitions No. 1503, 1504 & 1505 of 2022 and Civil Petition No. 4333 of 2021 (decided 03.01.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Accused's First Version to Police: Arts. 27 and 38 QSO
records.heading: The accused's first version to police is admissible if used in his own favour
records.text: A statement made by the accused to the investigating officer after arrest or during investigation is covered by s. 161 CrPC. The first version is relevant and admissible under Art. 27 QSO and not barred by Art. 38 or s. 162 CrPC if used by the accused in his own favour. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 523; Justice Mansoor Ali Shah.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 31 CPC: Appellate Judgment Requirements
records.heading: An appellate judgment must state points, decision, reasons and relief under Order XLI Rule 31
records.text: O. XLI R. 31 CPC requires an appellate judgment to state the points for determination, the decision, the reasons, and the relief where the decree is reversed or varied. Non-adherence can be fatal and is ignored only where there is substantial compliance. Ref: 2023 LHC 6984; Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849/2011).
records.title: Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849/2011)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Compromise in s. 489-F Cases at Bail Stage
records.heading: Lahore High Court directions on compromise in section 489-F cases at the bail stage
records.text: Lahore High Court judgment giving detailed directions on the procedure and effect of compromise in s. 489-F PPC cheque cases at the pre-arrest or post-arrest bail stage, per the Urdu caption. Ref: PLD 2020 Lah 97.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Reinstatement after Acquittal on Compromise
records.heading: A civil servant acquitted on compromise is entitled to reinstatement
records.text: A civil servant convicted under s. 302 PPC was acquitted in appeal on compromise, and the Supreme Court held him entitled to reinstatement, per the Urdu caption. The headnote records that his Service Tribunal appeal was not time barred, as it was unjust to penalise him for not appealing departmentally before earning his acquittal. Ref: PLD 2010 SC 695.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Compromise with Deceased Convict in Murder Appeal
records.heading: The High Court accepted a compromise with a convict who died during his appeal
records.text: A convict sentenced to life under s. 302(b) PPC died during his appeal, and his heirs sought a merits hearing. The victim's heirs then compromised with and forgave the deceased convict. The High Court accepted the compromise, allowed the appeal and acquitted him. Ref: Hukam Khan v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 93 of 2014).
records.title: Hukam Khan v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 93 of 2014)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 62(1)(f): Lifetime Disqualification Overruled
records.heading: Lifetime disqualification under Article 62(1)(f) was overruled and the period is five years
records.text: By six to one, the Supreme Court overruled Sami Ullah Baloch, holding Art. 62(1)(f) not self-executory and lifetime disqualification inconsistent with fundamental rights. Until legislation, it is to be read like Art. 62(1)(d), (e) and (g), and s. 232(2) of the Elections Act sets five years. Yahya Afridi J dissented, holding disqualification lasts while the declaration remains in force. Ref: Hamza Rasheed Khan v. Election Appellate Tribunal, Lahore High Court, Lahore & others (C.A. 982/2018, decided 08.01.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Hamza Rasheed Khan v. Election Appellate Tribunal, Lahore High Court, Lahore & others (C.A. 982/2018, decided 08.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Disqualification: Mere Registration of Case or Abscondence
records.heading: Mere registration of a case or abscondence does not disqualify a candidate under Article 63
records.text: Mere registration of a criminal case against a candidate, or his purported abscondence, is not a disqualification to contest election under Art. 63 of the Constitution, relying on 2016 SCMR 733. The judgment also reviews the nomination process under ss. 60 and 62 of the Elections Act, 2017. Ref: 2024 LHC 36; Eman Waseem v. Returning Officer etc (Election Appeal 16/24, decided 04.01.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Eman Waseem v. Returning Officer etc (Election Appeal 16/24, decided 04.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Meaning of Default in Art. 63
records.heading: Default in Article 63 means a wilful and deliberate failure to fulfil an obligation
records.text: The word default in Art. 63 of the Constitution does not bear its ordinary meaning. It connotes a wilful and deliberate failure to fulfil an obligation and negligence in performing the duty, relying on 1999 PTD 1302 and 2018 CLC 1330. Ref: 2024 LHC 32; Raja Ahmed Aziz Bhatti v. Returning Officer (Election Appeal 5/24, decided 04.01.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Raja Ahmed Aziz Bhatti v. Returning Officer (Election Appeal 5/24, decided 04.01.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Common Witnesses for Conviction and Acquittal of Co-Accused
records.heading: A common set of witnesses may be used to acquit and convict co-accused of the same offence
records.text: A common set of witnesses may be used to record acquittal and conviction against accused persons charged with the same offence. The post is a compilation of authorities on this proposition. Ref: 2023 YLR 585, 2022 YLR Note 19, 2021 YLR Note 88, 2021 YLR Note 71 and others.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
