records.topic: Two Versions: Complaint Case Taken First
records.heading: In a two versions case where police discard the FIR version, the private complaint is taken first
records.text: Where police discard the complainant's FIR version and challan other persons with new witnesses, the case is one of two versions and the private complaint is to be taken up first. The trial court's order staying the challan case, with the complaint proceeding, had no legal infirmity (ss. 173 and 200 CrPC). Ref: 2013 MLD 1599; Muhammad Sajjad v. Rab Nawaz.
records.title: Muhammad Sajjad v. Rab Nawaz

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Witnesses: Use of Evidence from Another Case
records.heading: A witness's deposition in one criminal case cannot be used in another without calling him
records.text: The law has no concept of using the deposition of one set of witnesses of a criminal case in another case without calling them, or of placing certified copies of statements on another case record. Adopting such evidence without examination and cross-examination would be serious. The Anti-Terrorism Court orders were set aside and the criminal revisions allowed. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 417; Ghulam Mustafa v. State.
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. State

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Rejection of Nomination Papers: Conviction and Sentence
records.heading: Conviction and sentence are distinct and section 426 CrPC relieves the sentence but keeps the conviction
records.text: The Election Tribunal dismissed the appeal against rejection of nomination papers for NA-89 Mianwali and upheld the Returning Officer's decision, per the Urdu report. Conviction and sentence are distinct, and s. 426 CrPC is an enabling provision that relieves the convict of the sentence but keeps the conviction intact. Ref: 2024 LHC 76; Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. Returning Officer etc (Election Appeal 151-24, decided 10.01.2024); Justice Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. Returning Officer etc (Election Appeal 151-24, decided 10.01.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Station Diary: Soft Copy and Maintenance
records.heading: A soft copy of the Station Diary must be kept in addition to the manual record
records.text: A soft copy of the Station Diary (Roznamcha) must be prepared in addition to the manual record. The Station Diary, kept under Art. 167 of the Police Order and Rules 22.48 and 22.49, is the most significant police station document and checks police powers. Directions on its maintenance were issued. Ref: Jamila Bibi v. S.H.O P.S Baghban Pura Lahore etc. (Criminal Proceedings 79470/23, decided 11.12.2023); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Jamila Bibi v. S.H.O P.S Baghban Pura Lahore etc. (Criminal Proceedings 79470/23, decided 11.12.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Trial of Civilians by Court Martial: s. 2(1)(d) Army Act
records.heading: Trial of civilians by court martial under section 2(1)(d) Army Act is ultra vires the Constitution
records.text: Detailed judgment declaring trial of civilians by court martial under s. 2(1)(d) of the Pakistan Army Act, 1952 ultra vires the Constitution. The short order was issued on 23.10.2023. Ref: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan, etc (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 10.01.2024); Justice Munib Akhtar.
records.title: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan, etc (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 10.01.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Military Trial of Civilians: Additional Note
records.heading: Additional note of Ayesha A. Malik J on military trial of civilians
records.text: Additional note of Ayesha A. Malik J in the detailed judgment declaring military trial of civilians unconstitutional. Ref: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan, etc (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 10.01.2024); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan, etc (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 10.01.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Military Trial of Civilians: Additional Note
records.heading: Additional note of Yahya Afridi J on trial of civilians by military courts
records.text: Additional note of Yahya Afridi J in the detailed judgment on the trial of civilians by military courts. The post gives only the case details and no holding. Ref: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan, etc (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 10.01.2024); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan, etc (Const.P. 24/2023, decided 10.01.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Bhutto Reference: Appearance of Counsel and Amici
records.heading: Order in the Bhutto Reference recording counsel and amici and fixing the hearing for February 2024
records.text: Order in the Presidential Reference under Art. 186 of the Constitution on the Bhutto death sentence. The Court recorded the representation of the family members, the withdrawal and appointment of amici after disclosures, and fixed the Reference for hearing in the third week of February 2024. Ref: Reference No. 1 of 2011 (Reference by the President under Article 186), order of 08.01.2024.
records.title: Reference No. 1 of 2011 (Reference by the President under Article 186), order of 08.01.2024

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Decree Against Father Not Executable Against Grandfather
records.heading: A maintenance decree against a father cannot be executed against the grandfather
records.text: A maintenance decree against a child's father cannot be executed against the grandfather. If no property of the father is found, the child must sue the grandfather separately under the Family Courts Act 1964, so that he receives the prescribed procedure in line with Art. 4 of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 67; Bashir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Hafizabad and others.
records.title: Bashir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Hafizabad and others

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 63(1)(h): Moral Turpitude and Tosha Khana Concealment
records.heading: Concealing Tosha Khana gifts is moral turpitude barring a convicted person under Article 63(1)(h)
records.text: A convicted person involved in a case of moral turpitude cannot contest elections under Art. 63(1)(h) of the Constitution. Concealment of the fact of obtaining gifts from Tosha Khana falls within moral turpitude. The appeal against rejection of nomination papers was dismissed and the Returning Officer's decision upheld. Ref: 2024 LHC 100; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The Returning Officer NA-122 Lahore-VI etc (Election Appeal 831/24, decided 10.01.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The Returning Officer NA-122 Lahore-VI etc (Election Appeal 831/24, decided 10.01.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal on Compromise Is an Honourable Acquittal
records.heading: An acquittal on compromise is as honourable as any other acquittal
records.text: All acquittals, including an acquittal based on compromise, are honourable, as the law draws no distinction between types of acquittal. An acquittal not challenged before a higher forum attains finality and removes the stigma of the allegation and any adjudged guilt. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 54; Rizwan Ali Sayal v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. 1938/2023).
records.title: Rizwan Ali Sayal v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. 1938/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Writ of Quo Warranto Only in Exceptional Cases
records.heading: A writ of quo warranto under Article 199 should issue only in exceptional cases
records.text: A writ of quo warranto under Art. 199 should be issued only in exceptional cases and not casually, especially where the candidate's qualifications were thoroughly examined at the time of appointment. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 54; Rizwan Ali Sayal v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. 1938/2023).
records.title: Rizwan Ali Sayal v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. 1938/2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Discontinuing the Word Sahib for Public Servants
records.heading: Adding the word sahib to a public servant's job title should be discontinued
records.text: In a bail matter arising from the murder of a child, the Court observed that adding the word sahib to a job title should be discontinued, as it elevates public servants and may foster a perception of unaccountability contrary to the public interest. The judgment was directed to be sent to the IG, the Advocate General and the Home Department of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 73; Javid Khan v. Arshid Khan and another (Crl.P. 149-P/2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Javid Khan v. Arshid Khan and another (Crl.P. 149-P/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Prosecution Must Prepare Case Before Coming to Court
records.heading: The prosecution must prepare its case before coming to court and not in court
records.text: The Court criticised the practice of preparing the case in court despite prior notice to the State, which turns the Court into an office of the prosecution. Investigating officers travelled to bring documents that could have been sent electronically, which would have assisted in deciding the bail application. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 73; Javid Khan v. Arshid Khan and another (Crl.P. 149-P/2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Javid Khan v. Arshid Khan and another (Crl.P. 149-P/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Promissory Note: Attestation Not Required
records.heading: A promissory note meeting section 4 NIA ingredients needs no attestation under Article 17(2)(a) QSO
records.text: An instrument meeting the four ingredients of s. 4 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 is a promissory note, and the attestation requirement of Art. 17(2)(a) QSO does not apply to it. Attestation by witnesses does not change its character. The presumption of consideration under s. 118 is only prima facie and may be displaced by a probable defence. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 45; Mehr Noor Muhammad v. Nazir Ahmed (C.A. 317-L/2011).
records.title: Mehr Noor Muhammad v. Nazir Ahmed (C.A. 317-L/2011)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 466 CrPC: Release of Accused of Unsound Mind
records.heading: An accused of unsound mind should as a rule be released on security under section 466 CrPC
records.text: An accused of unsound mind who cannot make his defence should as a rule be released on sufficient security under s. 466 CrPC. Detention in safe custody is an exception, justified only where there is apprehension of improper care or of injury to himself or others. The accused suffered from schizophrenia and was charged under s. 295-C PPC. Petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 75, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 61; Zaigham Hassan Khan v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 172-L/2023, decided 07.11.2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Zaigham Hassan Khan v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 172-L/2023, decided 07.11.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Release of Schizophrenic Accused on Security Pending Trial
records.heading: A schizophrenic accused was released on security as no exceptional circumstance justified detention
records.text: A schizophrenic accused was released on bail under s. 466 CrPC because his family was ready to furnish security and care for him. There was no past record of injury to others and the incident was not violent, so no exceptional circumstance justified detention in a mental health hospital. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 75; Zaigham Hassan Khan v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 172-L/2023).
records.title: Zaigham Hassan Khan v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 172-L/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Release of Lunatic Pending Investigation or Trial
records.heading: Release of an accused of unsound mind is the rule and safe custody the exception
records.text: An accused of unsound mind who cannot make his defence should as a rule be released on sufficient security under s. 466 CrPC. An order for detention in safe custody is made only as an exception, where there is apprehension of improper care or of injury to himself or others. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 75; Zaigham Hassan Khan v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 172-L/2023).
records.title: Zaigham Hassan Khan v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 172-L/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI R. 1 CPC: Late List of Witnesses
records.heading: A late list of witnesses needs good cause supported by an affidavit under Order XVI Rule 1
records.text: O. XVI R. 1 CPC requires the list of witnesses within seven days of settlement of issues. If it is omitted, the Court's permission is needed and the party must show good cause, with reasons recorded. An unsupported plea, without an affidavit, raised a year after the time given and after the plaintiff's evidence closed, was rejected. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 47; Muhammad Azam v. Muhammad Anwar Khan and 6 others (Civil Revision 50670/2020).
records.title: Muhammad Azam v. Muhammad Anwar Khan and 6 others (Civil Revision 50670/2020)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Injunction Against Encashment of Unconditional Bank Guarantee
records.heading: An unconditional bank guarantee cannot be injuncted on mere allegations of breach
records.text: An unconditional bank guarantee is an independent contract and payment must be made regardless of the dispute between the contracting parties. Mere allegations of breach or unfair conduct do not justify an interim injunction, and the applicant must meet the fraud exception and show damages are inadequate. The injunction application was rightly dismissed and the dispute is for the arbitrator. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 1; Messrs Paragon Technologies v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and others (W.P. 4534/2023).
records.title: Messrs Paragon Technologies v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and others (W.P. 4534/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 184(3): Maintainability and Alternate Remedy
records.heading: Article 184(3) is to be exercised cautiously and not where another forum can attend to the grievance
records.text: Art. 184(3) is an original jurisdiction to be exercised cautiously. Where another forum exists it should first attend to the grievance, appeals from High Courts lie under Art. 185, and direct intervention may affect the rights of others. An application alleging misuse of office by ISI and Rangers personnel was held not maintainable, and the applicant may complain to the Ministry of Defence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 40; H.R.C. 8157-P/2023.
records.title: H.R.C. 8157-P/2023

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: General Elections Within 90 Days: Date Fixed
records.heading: Court recorded agreement fixing general elections on 8 February 2024
records.text: In petitions for holding general elections within 90 days, the Court recorded the agreement between the President and the Election Commission to hold elections to the National and Provincial Assemblies on 8 February 2024 and issued orders accordingly. The matters were allowed in those terms. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1; Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 32/2023).
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 32/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Deed: Pre-requisites Not Established, Cancellation
records.heading: A gift deed failed where the donor and heirs kept possession and the deed was unilateral
records.text: The pre-requisites of a valid gift were not established. The donor and then his heirs remained in possession and the gift deed was unilateral. The Court allowed the appeals, decreed the donor's suit and cancelled the gift deed, setting aside the possession decree granted to the donee. Ref: 2024 SCMR 24; Mst. Tahira Samina and others v. Javed Saeed Tariq and others (Civil Petitions 723 and 724 of 2021).
records.title: Mst. Tahira Samina and others v. Javed Saeed Tariq and others (Civil Petitions 723 and 724 of 2021)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Challenging Gift Deed: Cause of Action
records.heading: Limitation to challenge a gift deed runs from when the donee first used it against the plaintiff
records.text: A suit filed 20 years after registration of a gift deed was within time because the cause of action accrued when the donee first used the gift against the plaintiff, by entering mutation in the Cantonment record just before the suit. Ref: 2024 SCMR 24; Mst. Tahira Samina and others v. Javed Saeed Tariq and others (Civil Petitions 723 and 724 of 2021).
records.title: Mst. Tahira Samina and others v. Javed Saeed Tariq and others (Civil Petitions 723 and 724 of 2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: No Prejudice to Anyone From Court's Fault
records.heading: No one should suffer prejudice from a fault, act or omission of the Court
records.text: In the administration of justice, no injury or prejudice should be caused to anyone by any fault, act or omission of the Court. Ref: 2024 SCMR 107; Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi and others (Civil Petitions 1877-L and 1878-L of 2016).
records.title: Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi and others (Civil Petitions 1877-L and 1878-L of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Jurisdiction Cannot Be Conferred or Taken Away by Consent
records.heading: Parties cannot by consent confer jurisdiction on a court or take away its jurisdiction
records.text: Parties cannot by mutual consent take away the jurisdiction vested in a court by law, nor confer on a court jurisdiction that the law does not give it. Ref: 2024 SCMR 107; Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi and others (Civil Petitions 1877-L and 1878-L of 2016).
records.title: Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi and others (Civil Petitions 1877-L and 1878-L of 2016)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Wrong Forum for Appeal: Duty of Court Staff
records.heading: Court staff must raise jurisdictional objections on first presentation of an appeal to protect limitation
records.text: Under ss. 3 and 5 of the Limitation Act, counsel must ensure an appeal is filed before the right forum, but court staff must also examine the memo of appeal on first presentation and raise jurisdictional objections immediately, so that the residual limitation period is not lost. Delay condonation was wrongly refused. Appeals allowed and the matter remanded to the High Court. Ref: 2024 SCMR 107; Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi and others (Civil Petitions 1877-L and 1878-L of 2016).
records.title: Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi and others (Civil Petitions 1877-L and 1878-L of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI Rr. 1, 3, 9 CPC: Scrutiny of Memo of Appeal
records.heading: The Court and staff must scrutinise the memo of appeal and promptly return it if filed at the wrong forum
records.text: O. XLI Rr. 1, 3 and 9 CPC place a duty on the Court and its staff to examine the memo of appeal and supporting documents before admission and to raise doubts on jurisdiction. If the appeal is at the wrong forum, the memo should be returned promptly so that the decision is not coram non judice. Ref: 2024 SCMR 107; Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi and others (Civil Petitions 1877-L and 1878-L of 2016).
records.title: Faqir Muhammad v. Khursheed Bibi and others (Civil Petitions 1877-L and 1878-L of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Challenge to Decision Does Not Suspend Compliance
records.heading: A decision does not become ineffective merely because it has been challenged before a higher forum
records.text: A decision does not become ineffective, and may not be left uncomplied with, merely because it has been challenged before a higher forum. Ref: 2024 SCMR 142; Khalid Pervaiz v. Samina and others (Civil Petition 2734-L of 2023).
records.title: Khalid Pervaiz v. Samina and others (Civil Petition 2734-L of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Recovery of Dower: Compensatory Costs on Husband
records.heading: Mehr is payable on demand and the husband's frivolous litigation attracted compensatory costs
records.text: Mehr must be paid whenever the wife demands it, including during the marriage. The husband's untenable defence and frivolous litigation of six and a half years led the Court to impose compensatory costs of Rs. 100,000 in addition to costs throughout, with execution by the Family Court if mehr and costs are unpaid. Ref: 2024 SCMR 142; Khalid Pervaiz v. Samina and others (Civil Petition 2734-L of 2023).
records.title: Khalid Pervaiz v. Samina and others (Civil Petition 2734-L of 2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Sale by Minor Void; Proof of Mutation and Sale
records.heading: A sale by a minor is void and a mutation needs proof through attesting witnesses
records.text: A sale to or by a person who was a minor at the time was void under s. 11 of the Contract Act. The claimants adduced no documentary proof or witness of the sale and failed to prove the mutation by summoning the two attesting witnesses under Arts. 17(2)(a) and 79 QSO. The High Court rightly held the mutation and sale void. Ref: 2024 SCMR 150; Noorullah and others v. Ghulam Murtaza and others (Civil Appeal 17-Q, Civil Petition 257-Q of 2023).
records.title: Noorullah and others v. Ghulam Murtaza and others (Civil Appeal 17-Q, Civil Petition 257-Q of 2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Deposit of Balance Consideration in Court
records.heading: A vendee seeking specific performance must deposit the balance consideration in court
records.text: Where the vendor refuses the balance consideration, the vendee seeking specific performance must deposit it in court. He must show that he was always ready and willing and that the money was available, since he cannot enforce the vendor's obligation without showing capability as well as willingness. Ref: 2024 SCMR 168; Masood Ahmad Bhatti and another v. Khan Badshah and another.
records.title: Masood Ahmad Bhatti and another v. Khan Badshah and another

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Refusal of Pay Orders by Vendor
records.heading: A vendor's objection to pay orders not on the vendee's own account was an afterthought
records.text: The vendor's objection that pay orders for the balance were not drawn on the vendee's personal account was an afterthought, as the agreement had no such condition and earlier payments through other accounts were accepted. The vendee had deposited the balance in court, and the trial court rightly decreed specific performance. Ref: 2024 SCMR 168; Masood Ahmad Bhatti and another v. Khan Badshah and another.
records.title: Masood Ahmad Bhatti and another v. Khan Badshah and another

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale Mutations Denied: Burden on Beneficiaries, Fraud
records.heading: Beneficiaries of sale mutations must prove the sale where the landowner denies it
records.text: Where the landowner denied selling her land or receiving consideration, the burden to prove the sale lay on the beneficiaries of the sale mutations. Failure to discharge it constituted fraud. Leave to appeal was dismissed and revenue authorities were directed to deliver exclusive possession to the respondent. Ref: 2024 SCMR 178; Mehmood Khan and others v. Sara Akhtar (Civil Petition 3030 of 2021).
records.title: Mehmood Khan and others v. Sara Akhtar (Civil Petition 3030 of 2021)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Change of Village Name: Objections Must Be Invited
records.heading: Objections of inhabitants must be invited before a village is renamed
records.text: The Provincial Government's notification renaming a village, and the consequential renaming of a school, was held void. Although the 1994 Rules cover roads and public places and not villages, objections and suggestions of the inhabitants had to be invited before notification under Para 7.69 of the Land Records Manual. The High Court's declaration was upheld. Ref: 2024 SCMR 199; Jehanzeb and others v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others (Civil Appeal 1444 of 2013).
records.title: Jehanzeb and others v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others (Civil Appeal 1444 of 2013)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Autonomy Principle and Fraud Exception for Guarantees
records.heading: Payment under an unconditional bank guarantee is independent of disputes, except for fraud by the beneficiary
records.text: Under ss. 13 and 5 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, payment under an unconditional bank guarantee or letter of credit depends on documentary demands and not on any dispute between the parties (pay first, sue later). The only exception is fraud alleged against the beneficiary of which the bank has notice. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 1; Messrs Paragon Technologies v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and others (W.P. 4534/2023).
records.title: Messrs Paragon Technologies v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and others (W.P. 4534/2023)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Comparative Law on Injunctions Against On-Demand Bonds
records.heading: Survey of Singapore, Indian and English law on injunctions against on-demand bonds
records.text: The judgment surveys the jurisprudence of Singapore on unconscionability, of India on restraining realisation of unconditional bank guarantees, and of England on calls upon autonomous demand bonds, in relation to the power to grant interim injunctions. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 1; Messrs Paragon Technologies v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and others (W.P. 4534/2023).
records.title: Messrs Paragon Technologies v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and others (W.P. 4534/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Fair Trial and Due Process: Duty of Courts
records.heading: Every person is entitled to a fair trial and due process before courts at every level
records.text: Courts from top to bottom must deal with matters of life, liberty, body, reputation or property in accordance with law, and every person before them is entitled to a fair trial and due process in the determination of civil rights and obligations or any criminal charge. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 67; Bashir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Hafizabad and others.
records.title: Bashir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Hafizabad and others

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Grandfather's Liability for Maintenance of Minor
records.heading: A grandfather is liable for a minor's maintenance only if the father is poor and he is affluent
records.text: A maintenance decree against the father cannot be executed against the grandfather, and the child must sue the grandfather separately. The grandfather is liable only if the father is poor with no resources and the grandfather is in easy circumstances. The Family Court may grant interim maintenance if both conditions are prima facie met. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 67; Bashir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Hafizabad and others.
records.title: Bashir Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Hafizabad and others

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Member of Parliament as Public Servant under S. 21 PPC
records.heading: A Member of Parliament is a public servant under section 21 PPC
records.text: A Member of Parliament is an officer performing a public duty and remunerated by fees (salary and allowances), and so falls within clause ninth of s. 21 PPC. He is therefore triable as a public servant for corruption and criminal misconduct under the PPC and the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 102; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const. P. 21 of 2022).
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const. P. 21 of 2022)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 41 Arbitration Act: Interim Injunction and Three Tests
records.heading: Interim injunctions remain available after reference to arbitration subject to the usual tests
records.text: Cl. 4 of the Second Schedule of the Arbitration Act 1940 empowers the Court to grant interim injunctions even after reference to arbitration, and s. 41 makes the grant governed by the CPC (O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2). The applicant must satisfy the established tests, including a prima facie case and the balance of convenience. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 1; Messrs Paragon Technologies v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and others (W.P. 4534/2023).
records.title: Messrs Paragon Technologies v. Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and others (W.P. 4534/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Abduction: Further Inquiry, Pre-Arrest and Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Bail in an abduction case where the abductee was sui juris and married to an accused
records.text: Where the alleged abductee, said to be sui juris, had a registered marriage with one accused and the marriage-related suits were pending, it was a matter of further inquiry whether her brother was involved in the abduction. Ad-interim pre-arrest bail of two accused was confirmed and the brother was granted post-arrest bail. Ref: 2024 SCMR 14; Salman Mushtaq and others v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1121 and 1128 of 2023).
records.title: Salman Mushtaq and others v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1121 and 1128 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Humiliation, Harassment and Malice
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail turns on humiliation, harassment or malice and injury to reputation and liberty
records.text: The paramount factors for pre-arrest bail are whether arrest would cause humiliation, unwarranted persecution or harassment for ulterior motives, or whether the prosecution is malicious and would irreparably injure the accused's reputation and liberty. Ref: 2024 SCMR 14; Salman Mushtaq and others v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1121 and 1128 of 2023).
records.title: Salman Mushtaq and others v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1121 and 1128 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Gravity of Offence Alone Insufficient to Refuse Bail
records.heading: The gravity of the offence alone does not justify refusing bail where evidence creates doubt
records.text: For pre-arrest or post-arrest bail, the gravity or viciousness of the offence is not by itself sufficient to refuse bail where the evidence creates some doubt about the veracity of the prosecution case. Ref: 2024 SCMR 14; Salman Mushtaq and others v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1121 and 1128 of 2023).
records.title: Salman Mushtaq and others v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1121 and 1128 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 497 CrPC: Meaning of Reasonable Grounds
records.heading: Reasonable grounds under section 497 CrPC must be legally acceptable and not imaginative
records.text: Reasonable grounds under s. 497 CrPC oblige the prosecution to show sufficient material that the accused committed an offence within the prohibitory clause. The accused must show the evidence gives rise to clear suspicion about his involvement. Courts must tentatively apply a judicious mind, and reasonable grounds must be legally acceptable and not imaginative or presumptuous. Ref: 2024 SCMR 14; Salman Mushtaq and others v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1121 and 1128 of 2023).
records.title: Salman Mushtaq and others v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1121 and 1128 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Murder: Further Inquiry under S. 497(2) CrPC
records.heading: Murder bail granted as further inquiry where the petitioner was named in neither section 164 statement
records.text: The petitioner's name appeared in neither of the two s. 164 CrPC statements, including the co-accused's confession, and there was no other circumstantial evidence beyond an earlier application by the deceased. The case called for further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and bail granted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 20; Fahad v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 495 of 2023).
records.title: Fahad v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 495 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Bail Application: Fresh Grounds
records.heading: A second bail petition needs fresh grounds, except statutory delay in the conclusion of trial
records.text: A second bail petition repeating earlier grounds is not competent, and grounds available when the earlier petition was filed or withdrawn are not fresh grounds. The exception is entitlement to bail on the statutory ground of delay in conclusion of trial. Ref: 2024 SCMR 28, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 16; Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 1233 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 1233 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Third Proviso to S. 497(1) CrPC: Statutory Delay Ground
records.heading: Statutory delay bail under the third proviso accrues as of right unless the accused hindered the trial
records.text: The right to bail under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC is not discretionary and accrues on fulfilment of its conditions, but not where the accused's act or omission hindered conclusion of trial. If the accused afterwards corrects himself, a fresh ground arises. The fresh petition was competent and bail was granted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 28, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 16; Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 1233 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 1233 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay: Co-Accused Abscondence Not Attributable
records.heading: A co-accused's abscondence is not attributable to the accused for statutory delay bail
records.text: The third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC confines the delay to acts or omissions of the accused or persons acting on his behalf. An accused cannot be made liable for a co-accused's acts, whatever the relationship, unless the prosecution shows his complicity on undisputed facts. Bail was granted after more than two years of incarceration. Ref: 2024 SCMR 28; Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 1233 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 1233 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay: Calculating Delay Attributable to Accused
records.heading: Delay attributable to the accused is assessed by cumulative effect and not by excluding adjournment dates
records.text: In assessing delay attributable to the accused, the court considers the cumulative effect on disposal and not a mathematical exclusion of dates on which the defence sought adjournments. The main factor is whether the defence caused delay in the attendance of witnesses. Recording of the last witness does not defeat the right. Ref: 2024 SCMR 28; Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 1233 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition 1233 of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Non-Prohibitory Offences: Enmity and Delay in Trial
records.heading: Bail granted in non-prohibitory offences where there was enmity and long custody without trial conclusion
records.text: The accused was nominated in two FIRs for offences outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. There was previous enmity over an FIR and he had been in custody over five months without conclusion of trial. Petitions converted into appeals and allowed, and bail granted in both FIRs. Ref: 2024 SCMR 43; Faheem Ullah v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1174 and 1202 of 2023).
records.title: Faheem Ullah v. The State through P.G. Punjab and another (Criminal Petitions 1174 and 1202 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal Upheld: Doubtful Witnesses and Defective Investigation
records.heading: Acquittal upheld where eyewitnesses were distant, light was unproved and the investigation was defective
records.text: Acquittal was upheld where the eyewitnesses lived 30 to 35 kilometres away, no source of light was established for a night incident, the accused was implicated after two and a half months without an identification parade, the site plan was defective and the ocular account conflicted with the medical evidence. Leave was refused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 51; Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Presence of Eyewitnesses: Testimony Excluded
records.heading: Ocular testimony should be excluded where the eyewitnesses' presence at the scene is doubtful
records.text: Where the presence of the eyewitnesses at the scene is doubtful, their ocular testimony should be excluded from consideration. Ref: 2024 SCMR 51; Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: A Single Circumstance Suffices
records.heading: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to its benefit
records.text: Several doubtful circumstances are not required, and even one circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to its benefit. If two sensible conclusions can be drawn from the evidence, the one favouring acquittal must be preferred. Ref: 2024 SCMR 51; Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal: Double Presumption of Innocence
records.heading: An acquittal carries a double presumption of innocence that is not lightly displaced on appeal
records.text: An acquittal carries a double presumption of innocence that cannot be lightly displaced. An appellate court interferes only where the acquittal is perverse, in gross violation of law, or marked by grave misreading or non-reading of evidence, and not merely because another view is possible. Ref: 2024 SCMR 51; Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 10-A: Accused as Favourite Child of Law
records.heading: The accused as favourite child of law is a safeguard of fair trial and not an indulgence
records.text: The phrase that the accused is the favourite child of law does not mean the Court should grant unwarranted favour or indulgence. It is a safeguard for fair-minded justice, an even-handed right of defence and a fair trial under Art. 10-A, supporting the presumption of innocence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 51; Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Khurram Shehzad (Criminal Petition 290-L of 2015)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Conviction Maintained on Reliable Ocular Account
records.heading: Murder conviction maintained where the ocular account matched the medical evidence
records.text: The ocular account was in line with the medical evidence and the prosecution witnesses were not shattered in cross-examination. Guilt was proved beyond doubt for murder and for injuries to the deceased's son. Conviction maintained, jail petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 67; Sohail Akhtar and another v. The State and another (Jail Petition 345 of 2017 and Criminal Petition 465 of 2017).
records.title: Sohail Akhtar and another v. The State and another (Jail Petition 345 of 2017 and Criminal Petition 465 of 2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Enhancement of Sentence Refused: Inconsequential Recovery
records.heading: Enhancement of sentence refused as recovery was inconsequential and crime empties were sent late
records.text: The High Court rightly treated the recovery as inconsequential because crime empties were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory after the convict's arrest. Its reduction of the death sentence to life imprisonment was upheld, and the complainant's petition for enhancement was dismissed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 67; Sohail Akhtar and another v. The State and another (Jail Petition 345 of 2017 and Criminal Petition 465 of 2017).
records.title: Sohail Akhtar and another v. The State and another (Jail Petition 345 of 2017 and Criminal Petition 465 of 2017)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Costs for Protracted Litigation to Retain Possession
records.heading: Heavy costs were imposed for protracted frivolous litigation to retain illegal possession
records.text: Plaintiffs who dragged out a suit for seven years and filed a frivolous petition to keep illegal possession violated the defendants' right under Art. 23 of the Constitution. Courts must impose costs to stem frivolous litigation. Leave was dismissed with costs of one million rupees as a charge on the property, and possession was to be handed over. Ref: 2024 SCMR 89; Javed Hameed and others v. Aman Ullah and others (Civil Petition 1990-L of 2017).
records.title: Javed Hameed and others v. Aman Ullah and others (Civil Petition 1990-L of 2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unproved Motive as Mitigating Factor: Death to Life
records.heading: Absence of premeditation and unproved motive may reduce a death sentence to life imprisonment
records.text: Where there is no premeditation and the prosecution fails to prove motive, this may be a mitigating factor reducing a death sentence to imprisonment for life under s. 302(b) PPC, in line with Art. 6 ICCPR. The High Court's reduction of sentence was upheld and leave refused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 128; Muhammad Yasin v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 476-L/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Yasin v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 476-L/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Conviction Upheld, No Deliberate Delay
records.heading: Murder conviction upheld where the victim was taken to hospital and eyewitnesses were consistent
records.text: There was no deliberate delay in reporting, as the victim was taken to hospital and died there. The three eyewitnesses were consistent, there was no prior enmity and the medical evidence corroborated them. The conviction was rightly upheld, and the jail petition was dismissed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 128; Muhammad Yasin v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 476-L/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Yasin v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 476-L/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Doubtful Ocular Account and Acquitted Co-Accused
records.heading: Benefit of doubt extended where the ocular account was doubtful and a similar co-accused was acquitted
records.text: Benefit of doubt was extended where the ocular account was doubtful, a co-accused with a similar role stood acquitted on the same evidence, the complainant's presence was contradicted by an attendance register, the recovery was inconsequential and motive was vague. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 156; Maqsood Alam v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 1710-L/2017).
records.title: Maqsood Alam v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 1710-L/2017)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 145 CrPC: Nature and Object of Proceedings
records.heading: Section 145 CrPC proceedings are executive and need material showing imminent breach of the peace
records.text: Proceedings under s. 145 CrPC are essentially executive and do not decide ownership or possession rights. Their object is to prevent a likely breach of the peace and maintain the status quo. Mere existence of a dispute is insufficient, and there must be material showing imminent danger of a breach of the peace. Ref: 2024 SCMR 136; Aminullah and others v. Syed Haji Muhammad Ayub and others (Civil Petition 116 of 2020).
records.title: Aminullah and others v. Syed Haji Muhammad Ayub and others (Civil Petition 116 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 145 CrPC: Judicial Magistrate Lacks Jurisdiction in Balochistan
records.heading: A Judicial Magistrate lacks jurisdiction under section 145 CrPC in Balochistan after the 2010 Amendment
records.text: After the Balochistan Amendment Act 2010, s. 145 CrPC powers lie with the District Magistrate, Sub-Divisional Magistrate or a specially empowered Executive Magistrate, so the Judicial Magistrate lacked jurisdiction. The jurisdictional requirement of likely breach of the peace was also absent. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and the High Court judgment set aside. Ref: 2024 SCMR 136; Aminullah and others v. Syed Haji Muhammad Ayub and others (Civil Petition 116 of 2020).
records.title: Aminullah and others v. Syed Haji Muhammad Ayub and others (Civil Petition 116 of 2020)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: High Court Writ Despite Supreme Court Cognizance of Special Court Trial
records.heading: A High Court writ against a trial of which the Supreme Court had taken cognizance was set aside
records.text: The Lahore High Court entertained and allowed a writ petition challenging the Special Court trial at Islamabad, although the Supreme Court had taken cognizance of that trial and given directions. The applications were allowed, and the Lahore High Court's office file was to be requisitioned and put up with the petitions before the Supreme Court. Ref: 2024 SCMR 63; Taufiq Asif v. Genl. (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf & others (C.M.A. 677/2020).
records.title: Taufiq Asif v. Genl. (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf & others (C.M.A. 677/2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Special Court Appeal: Office Objection on Non-Surrender
records.heading: A convict's appeal cannot be refused numbering for non-surrender as appeal is a right
records.text: An appeal under s. 12(3) of the Criminal Law Amendment (Special Court) Act 1976 was filed in time but not numbered because the appellant had not surrendered. The C.M. Appeal against that office objection was allowed, as appeal is the right of every convict, and the appeal was ordered numbered and set for hearing with the Special Court record. Ref: 2024 SCMR 60; General (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Criminal Misc. Appeal 6/2020 in Criminal Appeal Nil/2020).
records.title: General (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Criminal Misc. Appeal 6/2020 in Criminal Appeal Nil/2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeal Abated on Death of Convict Appellant
records.heading: An appeal against Special Court conviction abates on the appellant's death and the conviction subsists
records.text: The appeal against conviction by the Special Court under s. 12(3) of the 1976 Act was dismissed as abated, as the appellant had died and no legal heir came forward. The conviction by the Special Court therefore subsists. Ref: General (R) Pervez Musharraf v. The Federation of Pakistan and others (Crl.A. 785/2020, decided 10.01.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: General (R) Pervez Musharraf v. The Federation of Pakistan and others (Crl.A. 785/2020, decided 10.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: PTI Electoral Symbol (Bat): Peshawar High Court Detailed Judgment
records.heading: Peshawar High Court detailed judgment on PTI's writ concerning the bat electoral symbol
records.text: Detailed judgment of the Peshawar High Court in the writ petition of PTI against the Election Commission concerning the return of the bat electoral symbol. The post gives the dates of hearing and signing but no reasoning. Ref: Pakistan Tehreek Insaf (PTI) etc v. Election Commission of Pakistan (W.P. 6173 of 2023, decided 10.01.2024).
records.title: Pakistan Tehreek Insaf (PTI) etc v. Election Commission of Pakistan (W.P. 6173 of 2023, decided 10.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Intra-Party Elections: S. 208 Elections Act 2017, Bat Symbol
records.heading: The Election Commission's order was upheld after PTI failed to hold valid intra-party elections
records.text: The Court upheld the Election Commission's order of 22 December 2023 after PTI failed to hold valid intra-party elections required by s. 208 of the Elections Act 2017. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and the Peshawar High Court judgment in W.P. 6173-P/2023 set aside. Detailed reasons were to follow. Ref: Election Commission of Pakistan through Special Secretary, Islamabad v. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Islamabad through its authorized person and others (Civil Petition 42/2024, decided 13.01.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Election Commission of Pakistan through Special Secretary, Islamabad v. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Islamabad through its authorized person and others (Civil Petition 42/2024, decided 13.01.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Family Court Jurisdiction over Wife Residing Abroad
records.heading: A Pakistani Family Court has jurisdiction over a khula suit by a wife ordinarily resident abroad
records.text: Under the proviso to R. 6 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Rules 1965, the word ordinarily differs from permanent residence. A Pakistani Family Court had jurisdiction over a khula suit by a dual-citizen wife living in the USA who regularly visited Pakistan and her family. Where the proviso is met, the Court has no option but to dissolve the marriage. Ref: Sohail Ahmed v. Mst. Samreena Rasheed Memon & others (C.P. 488-K/2023, decided 20.12.2023); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Sohail Ahmed v. Mst. Samreena Rasheed Memon & others (C.P. 488-K/2023, decided 20.12.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A CrPC: No FIR for Non-Cognizable S. 498-A PPC
records.heading: No FIR can be ordered for non-cognizable section 498-A PPC under section 22-A CrPC
records.text: Under Schedule II CrPC, s. 498-A PPC is non-cognizable, so an FIR cannot be ordered for it. The Ex-Officio Justice of Peace may refuse to direct registration of a case and competently dismiss an application under s. 22-A(6) CrPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 7096; Muhammad Ajmal v. JOP etc (W.P. 15477/2021); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Ajmal v. JOP etc (W.P. 15477/2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Detention under MPO and Liberty as Fundamental Right
records.heading: Liberty is inalienable and the Punjab MPO operates subject to constitutional guarantees
records.text: Liberty is an inalienable right under Arts. 4 and 9 of the Constitution, and detention of a citizen violates fundamental rights. The Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance 1960 operates subject to constitutional guarantees. Political parties are important institutions, and the right to form and operate them is a guaranteed right. Ref: 2023 LHC 7103; Adnan Sami Khan v. GOP etc (W.P. 6977/2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Adnan Sami Khan v. GOP etc (W.P. 6977/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Adoption Has No Legal Effect in Shariah
records.heading: Adoption has no legal effect in Shariah and creates no inheritance rights
records.text: Adoption in Islam has no legal consequence and creates no new legal relationship or inheritance rights between adopted child and adoptive parents. The child is attributed to the natural parents, and NADRA registration must record known natural parentage. Ref: 2023 LHC 7114; Mst. Arzu v. DPO etc (W.P. 12826/2023, decided 11.09.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Mst. Arzu v. DPO etc (W.P. 12826/2023, decided 11.09.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Reference and Connected Criminal Appeals
records.heading: Lahore High Court murder reference with connected criminal appeals, case numbers only
records.text: Murder reference with connected criminal appeals decided by the Lahore High Court. The post gives only the case numbers and no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 7123; The State v. Ghulam Shabbir and Begum Bibi (Murder Reference 51 of 2019).
records.title: The State v. Ghulam Shabbir and Begum Bibi (Murder Reference 51 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Art. 129 QSO: Implausible Conduct of Assailants Sparing Witnesses
records.heading: Implausible conduct of assailants sparing witnesses showed that the witnesses did not see the occurrence
records.text: It was implausible that assailants with a direct dispute with a witness would spare him and the other witnesses, who could depose against them. Applying Art. 129 QSO on natural human conduct, the Court concluded that the witnesses did not witness the occurrence. Ref: 2023 LHC 7173; The State v. Irfan alias Punna (Murder Reference 64 of 2018).
records.title: The State v. Irfan alias Punna (Murder Reference 64 of 2018)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F CrPC: Production of Witnesses Before Accused's Examination
records.heading: Under section 265-F CrPC the accused is examined only after the prosecution witnesses
records.text: Under s. 265-F CrPC, if the accused does not plead guilty, the Court hears the complainant, takes the prosecution evidence and summons the persons the complainant names as acquainted with the facts. The accused is examined only after the witnesses are examined. Ref: 2023 LHC 7438; Mst. Haseena Mai v. State etc (Crl. Revision 336/2023, decided 22.11.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Mst. Haseena Mai v. State etc (Crl. Revision 336/2023, decided 22.11.2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: S. 14(2) Anti-Rape Act 2021: Cross-Examination by Counsel
records.heading: Section 14(2) of the Anti-Rape Act is mandatory and cross-examination must be by counsel
records.text: S. 14(2) of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act 2021 is mandatory because of the word shall. The opportunity to cross-examine the victim must be given to the accused's counsel and not to the accused, and non-compliance invalidates the act. Ref: 2023 LHC 7300; Abbas Ali v. State etc (W.P. 16927/2023, decided 14.11.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Abbas Ali v. State etc (W.P. 16927/2023, decided 14.11.2023)

records.topic: Murder Reference and Connected Criminal Appeals
records.heading: Lahore High Court murder reference with an appeal and special leave petition, case numbers only
records.text: Murder reference with a criminal appeal and a petition for special leave to appeal decided by the Lahore High Court. The post gives only the case numbers and no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 7265; The State v. Muhammad Arif (Murder Reference 135 of 2019).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Arif (Murder Reference 135 of 2019)

records.topic: Murder Reference and Connected Appeal and Revision
records.heading: Lahore High Court murder reference with an appeal and a revision, case numbers only
records.text: Murder reference with a criminal appeal and a criminal revision decided by the Lahore High Court. The post gives only the case numbers and no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 7307; The State v. Muhammad Nadeem (Murder Reference 28 of 2019).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Nadeem (Murder Reference 28 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Reference and Connected Criminal Appeals
records.heading: Lahore High Court murder reference with an appeal and special leave petition, case numbers only
records.text: Murder reference with a criminal appeal and a petition for special leave to appeal decided by the Lahore High Court. The post gives only the case numbers and no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 7348; The State v. Moula Bakhsh (Murder Reference 31 of 2020).
records.title: The State v. Moula Bakhsh (Murder Reference 31 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Reference and Connected Criminal Appeals

records.topic: Murder Reference and Connected Criminal Appeals
records.heading: Lahore High Court murder reference with two criminal appeals, case numbers only
records.text: Murder reference with two criminal appeals decided by the Lahore High Court. The post gives only the case numbers and no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 7232; The State v. Shahid alias Shahra (Murder Reference 11 of 2019).

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: KP Pre-emption Act 1987: Talb-e-Ishhad Notice on Printed Form
records.heading: Questions on the KP Pre-emption Act 1987 and talb-e-ishhad notice on a printed form
records.text: Authority on ss. 2(d), 6 and 13 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pre-emption Act 1987, the construction of the terms sitting, meeting and majlis, the interpretation of words in parentheses, and the effect of a talb-e-ishhad notice on a printed or stereotyped form. The post gives no holding. Ref: Amanullah v. Muhammad Shareef Khan (C.A. 179/2016, decided 31.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Amanullah v. Muhammad Shareef Khan (C.A. 179/2016, decided 31.10.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court Judge's Constitution Petition Against Federation
records.heading: Constitution petition by a Supreme Court Judge against the Federation, with no holding
records.text: Constitution petition filed by a Judge of the Supreme Court against the Federation of Pakistan and others. The post gives only the title and the name of the Judge and no holding. Ref: Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi, Judge Supreme Court of Pakistan v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Law and Justice, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 43/2023); Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi, Judge Supreme Court of Pakistan v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Law and Justice, Islamabad and others (Const.P. 43/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Extrajudicial Confession, Foot Tracker and Last Seen: Acquittal
records.heading: Acquittal where the extrajudicial confession, foot tracker and last seen evidence were not credible
records.text: Circumstantial evidence is weak. The extrajudicial confession was not credible, the foot tracker evidence did not meet R. 26 of Chapter XXV of the Punjab Police Rules 1934, safe custody of moulds was unproved, the forensic report was partially negative and the last seen witnesses did not justify their presence. Appeal accepted and accused acquitted. Ref: 2023 LHC 7518; Muhammad Nadeem v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 151/2016, decided 29.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Nadeem v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 151/2016, decided 29.11.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutation: Particulars of Fraud and Proof of Original Transaction
records.heading: A party pleading fraud must give particulars and a mutation is not a document of title
records.text: Under O. VI R. 4 CPC a party pleading fraud must give particulars, and the plaint lacked them. A mutation is not a document of title but an acknowledgment of the original transaction, which the person relying on it must first establish. Ref: 2023 LHC 7553; Mst. Munawar Jan etc v. Mst. Shufaidan Jan etc (Civil Revision 934/2012, decided 07.12.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Mst. Munawar Jan etc v. Mst. Shufaidan Jan etc (Civil Revision 934/2012, decided 07.12.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Unproved Motive
records.heading: Related chance eyewitnesses who cannot explain their presence are not believed, and unproved motive hurts the prosecution
records.text: Closely related eyewitnesses who were chance witnesses and failed to explain their presence were not believed. The mouth of the deceased being open, their absence from identification of the body and the lack of blood on their clothes showed they were not present. If the prosecution sets up a motive and fails to prove it, the prosecution suffers. Ref: 2023 LHC 7536; State v. Ashfaq Hussain (Murder Reference 51/2022, decided 06.12.2023); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: State v. Ashfaq Hussain (Murder Reference 51/2022, decided 06.12.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Grandfather's Liability and Quantum of Maintenance of Minors
records.heading: An affluent grandfather must maintain grandchildren only if the father and mother are both poor
records.text: A grandfather who is affluent is obliged to maintain grandchildren only where the father is poor, infirm and incapable of earning and the mother is also poor. Quantum must balance the needs of the minors against the father's finances, without unjust enrichment or oppression of the father. Ref: 2024 CLC 141; Ayesha Hashmat and 2 others v. ADJ etc (WP 27381/23).
records.title: Ayesha Hashmat and 2 others v. ADJ etc (WP 27381/23)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Cricket Board Management and Politically Motivated Decisions
records.heading: Cricket Board management should not be influenced by politically motivated decisions
records.text: The management of the Cricket Board should not be influenced by politically motivated decisions. Its Board of Governors should include representation of elected stakeholders from the grass roots, and election of the Chairman from the Prime Minister's nominees as Patron is deprecated. Ref: 2024 CLC 171; Naveed Mushtaq Abbasi v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 2376/2023).
records.title: Naveed Mushtaq Abbasi v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 2376/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination of Co-Defendant by a Defendant
records.heading: A defendant may seek the Court's permission to cross-examine a co-defendant whose statement is against his interest
records.text: The QSO has no specific provision allowing a defendant to cross-examine a co-defendant, but where a co-defendant's statement is against his interest, he may seek the Court's permission to cross-examine. Permission should be refused if the object is to cover a lacuna in the evidence. Ref: 2024 CLC 57; Atta Muhammad v. ASJ etc (Misc. Writ 25275/22).
records.title: Atta Muhammad v. ASJ etc (Misc. Writ 25275/22)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Undue Adjournments for Evidence
records.heading: A party granted time to produce evidence must act efficiently or the Court may decide under Order XVII Rule 3
records.text: Where a date is fixed or time granted to produce evidence or secure attendance of witnesses, the party must take efficient steps to comply. If the party avoids the order, the Court under O. XVII R. 3 CPC may proceed and decide the case in appropriate circumstances. Ref: 2024 CLC 29; Atta Ellahi v. Allah Bachaya etc (Civil Revision 554-20).
records.title: Atta Ellahi v. Allah Bachaya etc (Civil Revision 554-20)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Transfer by Administrative Order: Notice Parvee
records.heading: A transferee Court must issue notice parvee before a penal order after an administrative transfer
records.text: Where a case is transferred under an administrative order and not under s. 24-A(2) CPC, the transferee Court must issue notice parvee to the parties and counsel before passing a penal order such as absolute last opportunity. Dismissal of the suit under O. XVII R. 3 CPC was set aside in revision under s. 115 CPC and the case remanded for two clear opportunities to produce evidence. Revision allowed. Ref: 2024 CLC 49; Muhammad Yaqoob v. Raheela Yousaf (Civil Revision No. 18764 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Yaqoob v. Raheela Yousaf (Civil Revision No. 18764 of 2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Intra Court Appeal under Law Reforms Ordinance
records.heading: No intra court appeal lies where the original proceedings already provided an appeal, revision or review
records.text: Section 3 of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972 provides an Intra Court Appeal in certain cases, but none lies where the Art. 199 petition arises from proceedings in which the applicable law provided at least one appeal, revision or review against the original order. Ref: 2024 CLC 114; Reham Dad v. Province of Punjab (Intra Court Appeal No. 13 of 2021).
records.title: Reham Dad v. Province of Punjab (Intra Court Appeal No. 13 of 2021)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Extraction of Data from Personal Phone
records.heading: Extracting data from a personal phone without Court permission is unconstitutional and illegal
records.text: Spying on or extracting data from the personal phone of an individual or suspect is unconstitutional and illegal except with the permission of the Court. The prosecution story of distributing hate material was not proved by cogent evidence, and the conviction under ss. 11-F(2), 11-G and 11-W ATA was set aside, the accused being acquitted by benefit of doubt. Appeal allowed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1, PLJ 2024 CrC 287; Muhammad Rahmat Ullah v. The State (Crl. A. No. 73676 of 2022); Justice Ali Baqar Najafi; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Rahmat Ullah v. The State (Crl. A. No. 73676 of 2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail: Delay Caused by Court
records.heading: An accused detained over two years in a capital case is entitled to statutory bail unless he caused the delay
records.text: Under the third proviso to s. 497 CrPC an accused in a capital offence detained continuously for over two years must be released on bail unless the delay is caused by the accused or the fourth proviso applies. The right rests also on Arts. 4, 9 and 10A of the Constitution, and indefinite pre-trial detention is not permitted. Ref: Rohan Ahmad v. The State (Crl.P. 894-L/2023); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Rohan Ahmad v. The State (Crl.P. 894-L/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Marriage During Iddat is Void
records.heading: A marriage contracted during Iddat is invalid
records.text: A marriage contracted during the period of Iddat is invalid. Muslim jurists term it Batil (void), and even if treated as irregular (Fasid) it remains an invalid marriage. Ref: 1992 SCMR 1273; Allah Dad v. Mukhtar and another.
records.title: Allah Dad v. Mukhtar and another

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Illegal Act Not Legitimised by Lapse of Time
records.heading: No illegal act or wrong entry is legitimised by the passage of time
records.text: No illegal act or wrong entry can be legitimised by the passage of time, however long it may be. Ref: 2024 CLC 106; Allah Ditta v. Ali Shah (deceased) through Legal Heirs (Civil Revision No. 1095-D of 2010).
records.title: Allah Ditta v. Ali Shah (deceased) through Legal Heirs (Civil Revision No. 1095-D of 2010)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Licences for SMGs and Prohibited Bore Weapons
records.heading: Questions on licences for SMGs and prohibited bore weapons sent to a separate Article 184(3) petition
records.text: The Court framed questions on the authority to issue licences for SMGs and other prohibited bore weapons, their compatibility with Arts. 25 and 9, and the number of licences issued. The office was directed to register a separate constitution petition under Art. 184(3), with notices to the Attorney General and Advocates General under O. XXVIIA CPC. Ref: Kashif v. Imran and another (Crl.P. 188-P/2023, decided 17.01.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Kashif v. Imran and another (Crl.P. 188-P/2023, decided 17.01.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Agreement Waiving Mother's Right of Hizanat
records.heading: An agreement waiving the mother's right of Hizanat is unlawful and unenforceable
records.text: A mother is entitled to custody of a male child until seven years and a female child until puberty. Any iqrarnama or agreement by which the mother waives her right of Hizanat is unlawful and unenforceable, relying on PLD 2020 SC 508. Ref: Mst. Haseena Bibi v. Abdul Haleem (C.A. 1227/2016, decided 15.11.2023); Justice Mussarat Hilali.
records.title: Mst. Haseena Bibi v. Abdul Haleem (C.A. 1227/2016, decided 15.11.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Challenge to Registered Document
records.heading: Mere denial by the executant of a registered sale deed does not shift the burden to the beneficiary
records.text: The standard of evidence differs between challenging a registered and an unregistered document. Mere denial by the executant of a registered sale deed does not shift the burden to the beneficiary to prove execution. The burden rules in Arts. 117 to 122 QSO apply, and execution is proved under Art. 79 QSO. Ref: Mst. Nazeeran v. Ali Bux (deceased) through L.Rs (C.A. 81-K/2022, decided 05.12.2023); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Mst. Nazeeran v. Ali Bux (deceased) through L.Rs (C.A. 81-K/2022, decided 05.12.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Essential Ingredients of a Valid Gift
records.heading: A valid gift requires declaration, acceptance and delivery of possession
records.text: A valid gift requires three ingredients: declaration of the gift, acceptance of the gift, and delivery of possession of the subject of the gift. Ref: 2022 SCMR 1352, PLJ 2024 SC 20; Mst. Kalsoom Begum v. Peran Ditta, etc. (Civil Appeal No. 1348 of 2014).
records.title: Mst. Kalsoom Begum v. Peran Ditta, etc. (Civil Appeal No. 1348 of 2014)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt at Bail Stage
records.heading: Benefit of doubt can be extended even at the bail stage
records.text: Benefit of doubt can be extended even at the bail stage. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1140, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 25; Salman Zahid v. State through P.G. Sindh.
records.title: Salman Zahid v. State through P.G. Sindh

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Non-Prohibitory Offences: Rule
records.heading: In non-prohibitory offences bail is the rule and refusal is the exception
records.text: In offences not falling within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2122, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 42; Noman Khaliq v. State.
records.title: Noman Khaliq v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Absconsion and Bail
records.heading: Absconsion is not proof of the offence and alone is no ground to refuse bail
records.text: Absconsion cannot be viewed as proof of the offence and alone cannot be a ground to refuse the relief of bail. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2122, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 42; Noman Khaliq v. State.
records.title: Noman Khaliq v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Registration of FIR Despite Territorial Jurisdiction Doubt
records.heading: Information of a cognizable offence cannot be neglected for doubt about territorial jurisdiction
records.text: Information of a cognizable offence cannot be neglected on the pretext of lack of territorial jurisdiction. A case may be registered where the offence is committed or its consequences ensue, and where the station lacks jurisdiction the information is recorded in the daily diary and forwarded, with lawful measures taken meanwhile, under Police Rules 1934, Rr. 25.1 to 25.8. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 1; Sakina Bibi v. Additional Sessions Judge (W.P. No. 56691 of 2022, decided 01.06.2023); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Sakina Bibi v. Additional Sessions Judge (W.P. No. 56691 of 2022, decided 01.06.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Time-Barred Appeal Against Common Judgment
records.heading: A time-barred appeal against a common judgment is not dismissed while other appeals are pending
records.text: Where more than one appeal arises from a common judgment, an appeal that is barred by time cannot be dismissed on limitation if one or more of the other appeals are pending. Ref: 2024 CLC 1; National Command Authority through D.G. SPD, Rawalpindi v. Zahoor Azam.
records.title: National Command Authority through D.G. SPD, Rawalpindi v. Zahoor Azam

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Ephedrine Quota Case: Acquittal on Appeal
records.heading: Ephedrine quota conviction set aside and the appellant acquitted for want of material evidence
records.text: In the Ephedrine quota case the High Court set aside the conviction and 25 year sentence and acquitted the appellant. A quota of 500 kg was lawfully allotted to him and the prosecution brought no material evidence against him. The acquittal of co-accused was not interfered with, an acquittal carrying a double presumption of innocence. Ss. 9, 14 and 15 CNSA. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1; Muhammad Hanif Abbasi v. The State (Crl. A. No. 663 of 2018, decided 18.10.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif Abbasi v. The State (Crl. A. No. 663 of 2018, decided 18.10.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Revision Against Refusal of Remand
records.heading: Revision lies under section 435 CrPC against a Magistrate's refusal of remand
records.text: An order of a Magistrate refusing remand is a judicial function, and under s. 435 CrPC the superior Court can exercise revisional jurisdiction. The Urdu summary adds that in anti-corruption cases revision against the Judicial Magistrate's grant or refusal of physical remand lies before the Sessions Judge. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 55, PLJ 2024 CrC 66; Parvez Elahi v. Additional Sessions Judge and 3 others (Crl. Misc. No. 40242-M of 2023).
records.title: Parvez Elahi v. Additional Sessions Judge and 3 others (Crl. Misc. No. 40242-M of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Medical Evidence and Motive
records.heading: Medical evidence does not connect the accused with the offence and unproved motive hurts the prosecution
records.text: Medical evidence may confirm the seat and nature of injury and the weapon but does not connect the accused with the offence. If the prosecution sets up a motive and fails to prove it, the prosecution suffers. Reasonable doubt must be resolved in the accused's favour as of right, not concession. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 50; Abdul Ghaffar v. The State (Crl. Appeal 245-21).
records.title: Abdul Ghaffar v. The State (Crl. Appeal 245-21)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Physical Remand under s. 21-E ATA
records.heading: Physical remand under section 21-E ATA is discretionary and needs recorded reasons
records.text: The power under s. 21-E ATA to grant physical remand of not less than fifteen days is discretionary. Remand is not to be granted routinely, should be as short as possible, and the Court, deemed a Magistrate, must record reasons under s. 167(3) CrPC. The Anti-Terrorism Court rightly granted remand for a period it deemed appropriate. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 73; The State v. Muswar Hussain Shah (Crl. Revision No. 57693/2023).
records.title: The State v. Muswar Hussain Shah (Crl. Revision No. 57693/2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Fabricated Recovery and Belated Challan
records.heading: Fabricated narcotics cases and wilful delay in the challan make bail a case of further inquiry
records.text: Police officials fabricating narcotics cases against persons with previous records to make a crackdown appear successful cannot be endorsed. Wilful delay in submitting the challan infringed the right to fair trial and showed prima facie mala fide, making the case one of further inquiry. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 79; Shehzad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 34710/23); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Shehzad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 34710/23)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Photographing Narcotics Recovery; Bail
records.heading: Police must photograph or video narcotics recoveries and bail was allowed for delayed challan
records.text: The Court directed that police and ANF officials should photograph or video the recovered narcotics, the accused and the scene, which is admissible evidence, and that searches be conducted in the presence of respectable locals. Bail was allowed on a bond of Rs. 100,000 owing to delay in submitting the challan and failure to collect evidence as required by law. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 8; Zahid Sarfaraz Gill v. The State (Crl.P. 1192/2023).
records.title: Zahid Sarfaraz Gill v. The State (Crl.P. 1192/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 114 QSO: Doctrine of Estoppel
records.heading: Article 114 QSO bars a person from denying what he caused another to believe
records.text: Art. 114 QSO incorporates estoppel: a person who by declaration, act or omission intentionally caused or permitted another to believe a thing true and act on it, cannot deny its truth against that person or his representative in a suit or proceeding. The judgment also covers approbation and reprobation and presumption of service under Art. 129 QSO and s. 27 General Clauses Act. Ref: 2023 SCMR 1305, PLJ 2024 SC 40; Muhammad Riaz v. Muhammad Ramzan, etc (C.P.446-L/2014).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Muhammad Ramzan, etc (C.P.446-L/2014)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inquest Report Under Rule 25.35 Police Rules
records.heading: An inquest report under Rule 25.35 can show that the case was not registered at the stated time
records.text: The inquest report under Rule 25.35 of the Police Rules 1934 can show that the case was not registered at the time stated in the FIR. Its details must be given to the medical officer before autopsy, so that witness statements are recorded before the postmortem, and later statements allow the ocular account to be adjusted to the medical evidence. Appeal allowed and conviction set aside. Ref: 2023 YLR 2503, PLJ 2024 CrC Note 2; Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 113, 190, Crl. Rev. 63 & M.R. 34/2020, heard 22.11.2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account in Conflict With Medical Evidence
records.heading: An ocular account inconsistent with medical evidence warrants rejecting the eyewitnesses' version
