records.text: Medical evidence helps the court test the deposition of an eyewitness. If the ocular account is inconsistent with the medical evidence, rejection of the eyewitnesses' version is warranted. The court need not give alternative reasoning for a lacuna in medical evidence. Ref: 2023 YLR 2503, PLJ 2024 CrC Note 2; Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State.
records.title: Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Eyewitnesses: Credibility Still to Be Tested
records.heading: An injured witness's credibility must still be tested and injuries show only presence at the spot
records.text: Injuries received by a witness indicate at most presence at the spot, and his evidence must still be tested on the settled principles of appraisal of evidence. There is no rule that an injured witness speaks only the truth, and credibility makes a witness reliable. Ref: 2023 YLR 2503, PLJ 2024 CrC Note 2; Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State.
records.title: Hafeez Ahmed and another v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Justice of Peace under s. 22-A(6) CrPC: Scope
records.heading: The Justice of Peace under section 22-A(6) only examines whether a cognizable offence is disclosed
records.text: The office of the ex-officio Justice of Peace is a quasi-judicial forum. Its only jurisdiction under s. 22-A(6) CrPC is to examine whether the information disclosed a cognizable offence and to direct the SHO to register an FIR without going into the veracity of the information. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 1; Sakina Bibi v. Additional Sessions Judge (W.P. No. 56691 of 2022, decided 01.06.2023); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Sakina Bibi v. Additional Sessions Judge (W.P. No. 56691 of 2022, decided 01.06.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Motive and Time of Death
records.heading: Doubt over time of death and unproved motive entitle the accused to the benefit of doubt
records.text: The medical opinion on the interval between death and post mortem cast deep doubt on the prosecution case. Motive was not proved by any independent witness, and tainted evidence cannot corroborate tainted evidence. A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to the benefit of doubt as of right. Ss. 302(b) and 374 PPC. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 87; Abdul Jabbar v. The State (Crl. A. No. 351-J and M.R. No. 14 of 2022, heard 08.03.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Abdul Jabbar v. The State (Crl. A. No. 351-J and M.R. No. 14 of 2022, heard 08.03.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Arrest After Arrest in Successive Cases
records.heading: Arrest after arrest in successive cases offends due process and liberty
records.text: Arrest after arrest or successive remands in different cases denies the fundamental rights to life and liberty and offends due process. An accused on interim pre-arrest bail in one case who is arrested in another should not have his petition dismissed for want of appearance. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 43; Parvez Elahi v. Care Taker Government of Punjab (W.P. No. 45360 of 2023, decided 13.07.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Parvez Elahi v. Care Taker Government of Punjab (W.P. No. 45360 of 2023, decided 13.07.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witnesses: Credibility and Delay
records.heading: Injuries on a witness prove presence but not truthfulness, and delay and improvements gave benefit of doubt
records.text: Injuries on a witness prove presence at the scene but do not guarantee truthful testimony, and credibility decides reliability. Delay in recording statements, doubt over the injured witness's medical examination, dishonest improvements and doubt about the statement recorded at the spot led to the benefit of doubt. S. 302 PPC. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 6; Saeed Fareed v. The State (Crl. A. Nos. 335, 1003 of 2019, heard 10.10.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Saeed Fareed v. The State (Crl. A. Nos. 335, 1003 of 2019, heard 10.10.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Mala Fide and Discrepancies
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where discrepancies raised doubt and complainant's mala fide could not be ruled out
records.text: Discrepancies in the dates of occurrence and medical examination, together with a minor little finger injury, raised serious doubts and mala fide of the complainant could not be ruled out. Interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed under s. 498 CrPC on fresh bonds of Rs. 100,000. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 22; Dilshad v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 3925-B of 2023, decided 04.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Dilshad v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 3925-B of 2023, decided 04.10.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Generalised Allegations
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where allegations were generalised and involvement appeared mala fide
records.text: Allegations against the petitioner were generalised, with no injury statement, no record of the alleged messages or calls and no specification of the stolen articles. Her involvement appeared to rest on mala fide, and pre-arrest bail was confirmed under s. 498 CrPC. Observations are tentative. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 13; Mst. Sumaira Bibi v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 4094-B of 2023, decided 13.06.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Mst. Sumaira Bibi v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 4094-B of 2023, decided 13.06.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 371-A/371-B PPC and Brothel Copulation
records.heading: Sections 371-A and 371-B PPC are not attracted by copulation in a brothel house
records.text: Sections 371-A and 371-B PPC are not attracted against copulation in a brothel house. Ref: 2024 LHC 150; Khalida Bibi v. The State (Crl. Misc. 885/24, decided 15.01.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Khalida Bibi v. The State (Crl. Misc. 885/24, decided 15.01.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Suit for Specific Performance
records.heading: Authority on a suit for specific performance, with no holding given
records.text: Authority on a suit for specific performance. The post gives no holding. Ref: Matloob Ellahi Paracha v. Raja Arshad Mahmood and another (C.A. 1877/2016); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Matloob Ellahi Paracha v. Raja Arshad Mahmood and another (C.A. 1877/2016)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Exemption Extends to Similarly Situated Persons
records.heading: An exemption granted to a class extends to all similarly situated persons
records.text: When an exemption is granted to a particular class of persons, its benefit extends to all similarly situated persons. Ref: Commissioner Inland Revenue Zone-IV, Karachi v. M/s A.P. Moller Maersk (C.P. 560-K/2019, decided 12.01.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Commissioner Inland Revenue Zone-IV, Karachi v. M/s A.P. Moller Maersk (C.P. 560-K/2019, decided 12.01.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Environment, Water Resources and Tree Plantation
records.heading: Lahore High Court order on environment, water resources and tree plantation, with no holding
records.text: Authority on a Lahore High Court order concerning the environment, water resources and tree plantation. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2023 LHC 7619; Haroon Farooq v. Government of Punjab (Misc. Writ 227807/18, decided 19.12.2023); Justice Shahid Karim.
records.title: Haroon Farooq v. Government of Punjab (Misc. Writ 227807/18, decided 19.12.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Adjournments: O. XVII R. 3 CPC
records.heading: Courts must not grant adjournments liberally and must stand by a last opportunity
records.text: Frequent adjournment requests in lower courts abuse the process and cause backlog, and courts must not grant adjournments liberally without compelling reasons. O. XVII R. 3 CPC empowers the court to decide forthwith if a party granted time fails to produce evidence, and a court that gives a last opportunity must stand by its order. Ref: Duniya Gul v. Niaz Muhammad (C.P. 920-P/2023, decided 16.01.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Duniya Gul v. Niaz Muhammad (C.P. 920-P/2023, decided 16.01.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Meaning of Lien in Service Law
records.heading: Lien in service law is a civil servant's right to hold a post and return to his original one
records.text: In service law, lien has a statutory connotation and is the right of a civil servant to hold a post to which promoted or transferred while retaining a right to his original post, and so to return to it, on the conditions set by the applicable rules. Dictionary definitions cannot be applied strictly. Ref: Muhammad Saleem v. Govt. of Balochistan through Chief Secretary and another (C.M.A. 145-Q/2022, decided 21.12.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Muhammad Saleem v. Govt. of Balochistan through Chief Secretary and another (C.M.A. 145-Q/2022, decided 21.12.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Cross-Cases
records.heading: Bail in cross-cases is ordinarily granted as further inquiry and alike for both sides
records.text: Principles of bail in cross-cases depend on the facts of each case. A cross-case needs a tentative finding that the parties, venue and transaction point to a single incident narrated differently, and bail is ordinarily granted as a rule on the ground of further inquiry, refusal being the exception. Where one side gets bail, the other should be treated alike. S. 497 CrPC. Ref: Ahmad Ali v. The State through A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar and another (Crl.P. 183-P/2022, decided 07.03.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Ahmad Ali v. The State through A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar and another (Crl.P. 183-P/2022, decided 07.03.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 295-B PPC: Ingredients
records.heading: Section 295-B PPC covers wilful defiling or derogatory use of the Holy Qur'an
records.text: S. 295-B PPC covers two scenarios: wilful defiling, damaging or desecrating a copy of the Holy Qur'an or an extract, and wilful use of it in a derogatory manner or for unlawful purposes. For the first, the act must be done of the person's own will and must defile, damage or desecrate the copy or extract. The punishment is life imprisonment. Ref: Muhammad Zafran v. The State (Crl.A. 597/2018); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Muhammad Zafran v. The State (Crl.A. 597/2018)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Deprived Heir and Limitation Where Third-Party Rights Arise
records.heading: A deprived heir is not barred by limitation unless third-party rights have been created
records.text: An heir deprived of his shari share at the time of inheritance mutation is not hindered by limitation, as possession of one heir is constructive possession for all and the cause of action arises on denial. Where third-party rights have been created, limitation applies and the claimant heir bears the burden of showing lack of awareness and giving cogent reasons. Ref: Khaleelullah v. Muhaim Khan (C.A. 25-Q/2018, decided 19.12.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Khaleelullah v. Muhaim Khan (C.A. 25-Q/2018, decided 19.12.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: PTI Intra-Party Elections and Bat Symbol
records.heading: Supreme Court detailed judgment on PTI intra-party elections and the bat symbol, with no holding given
records.text: Detailed 38 page judgment of the Supreme Court on the intra-party elections of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf and the bat electoral symbol, issued on 25.01.2024 after the short order of 13.01.2024. The post gives no holding. Ref: Election Commission of Pakistan through Special Secretary, Islamabad v. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Islamabad (Civil Petition No. 42/2024, decided 13.01.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Election Commission of Pakistan through Special Secretary, Islamabad v. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Islamabad (Civil Petition No. 42/2024, decided 13.01.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Art. 212(3): Appeals from Provincial Administrative Tribunals
records.heading: Appeals from Provincial Administrative Tribunals lie to the Supreme Court under Article 212(3)
records.text: The proviso to Art. 212(2) does not apply to Art. 212(3), so appeals against orders of Provincial Administrative Tribunals lie to the Supreme Court under Art. 212(3). The view that such decisions are challenged under Art. 199 absent a Parliamentary law is incorrect. Gomal Medical College v. Armaghan Khan (PLD 2023 SC 190) overruled. Ref: Syed Asghar Ali Shah v. Kaleem Arshad (C.P. 167-P/2022, decided 15.01.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Syed Asghar Ali Shah v. Kaleem Arshad (C.P. 167-P/2022, decided 15.01.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Arrest in Another Case
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is not dismissed for non-prosecution if the accused is jailed in another case
records.text: If an accused granted ad-interim pre-arrest bail is arrested and confined in jail in another case, his pre-arrest bail petition will not be dismissed for non-prosecution and will be decided after procuring his attendance. Concerns the restoration of interim bail of the petitioner. Ref: 2024 LHC 175; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Anti-Terrorism Court (Crl. Revision 54056/23, decided 23.01.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Anti-Terrorism Court (Crl. Revision 54056/23, decided 23.01.2024)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: ICJ Provisional Measures: South Africa v. Israel
records.heading: ICJ held it had jurisdiction and ordered Israel to prevent acts of genocide but no ceasefire
records.text: The International Court of Justice held that it had jurisdiction and rejected Israel's request to dismiss the case. It ordered Israel to take all measures to prevent acts of genocide in Gaza, to punish incitement and to preserve evidence, and to report within one month. It did not order a ceasefire. Ref: South Africa v. Israel (Application of the Convention on Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in Gaza Strip, decided 26.01.2024); Justice Gevorgian; Justice Tomka; Justice Abraham; Justice Bennouna; Justice Yusuf; Justice Xue; Justice Bhandari; Justice Robinson; Justice Salam; Justice Iwasawa; Justice Nolte; Justice Charlesworth; Justice Brant; Justice Barak; Justice Moseneke; Justice Sebutinde.
records.title: South Africa v. Israel (Application of the Convention on Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in Gaza Strip, decided 26.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Rejection of Nomination Papers: National Assembly
records.heading: Authority on rejection of nomination papers for the National Assembly, with no holding
records.text: Authority on rejection of nomination papers for the National Assembly. The post gives no holding. Ref: Tahir Sadiq v. Faisal Ali and others (C.P. 150/2024, decided 26.01.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Tahir Sadiq v. Faisal Ali and others (C.P. 150/2024, decided 26.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Proclaimed Offender Contesting Election
records.heading: A proclaimed offender is not disqualified from contesting an election without backing of law
records.text: As neither the Constitution nor the Elections Act makes a proclaimed offender disqualified from contesting an election, courts cannot create such a disqualification without backing of law. The Supreme Court allowed Umar Aslam Khan to contest from NA-87 Khushab. Ref: Umar Aslam Khan v. Election Commission of Pakistan through Chief Election Commissioner (C.P. 159/2024, decided 26.01.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Umar Aslam Khan v. Election Commission of Pakistan through Chief Election Commissioner (C.P. 159/2024, decided 26.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Rejection of Nomination Papers on Trivial Grounds
records.heading: Nomination papers should not be rejected on trivial grounds as participation is core to democracy
records.text: Participation is at the core of democracy, and disenfranchisement by rejection of nomination papers on trivial grounds must be avoided. The Supreme Court allowed Parvez Elahi to contest from PP-32 Gujrat. Ref: Parvez Elahi through attorney Qaisra Elahi v. Election Commission of Pakistan (C.P. 181/2024, decided 26.01.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Parvez Elahi through attorney Qaisra Elahi v. Election Commission of Pakistan (C.P. 181/2024, decided 26.01.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Abscondence as Corroborative Evidence
records.heading: Abscondence is corroborative evidence to be read with the substantive evidence
records.text: Abscondence of an accused is a corroborative piece of evidence that cannot be read in isolation and must be read with the substantive evidence. Ref: 2024 YLR 94; Jan Muhammad alias Jani v. The State.
records.title: Jan Muhammad alias Jani v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eye-Witnesses Not Proved
records.heading: Eye-witnesses were not proved present given unexplained presence, delayed report and delayed post mortem
records.text: Eye-witnesses who gave no explanation for their presence, delayed reporting for about three and a half hours, did not name the appellant in the complainant's oral statement and were followed by a post mortem delayed over nine hours were held not proved present. The delay was used to procure their attendance. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2024 YLR 94; Jan Muhammad alias Jani v. The State.
records.title: Jan Muhammad alias Jani v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recovery Without Local Witnesses: s. 103 CrPC
records.heading: A recovery made without local witnesses violates section 103 CrPC and is excluded
records.text: Recovery of a Kalashnikov rifle made without joining any witness of the locality violated s. 103 CrPC and was evidence obtained by illegal means, hit by the exclusionary rule. The forensic report was of no use because the rifle was not compared with the empties. Appeal allowed. Ref: 2024 YLR 94; Jan Muhammad alias Jani v. The State.
records.title: Jan Muhammad alias Jani v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light
records.heading: An electric bulb never produced to investigators means no source of light for a night occurrence
records.text: Where eye-witnesses claim to have seen a night occurrence by an electric bulb that was never produced to the Investigating Officer or the Trial Court, the inference is that no source of light existed to identify the assailants and their roles. Ref: 2024 YLR 94; Jan Muhammad alias Jani v. The State.
records.title: Jan Muhammad alias Jani v. The State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint, Cause of Action
records.heading: A specific performance suit filed before confirmation of the vendors' proprietary rights has no cause of action
records.text: A suit for specific performance of an agreement to sell state land was filed before the Province confirmed proprietary rights to the vendors, so no cause of action had arisen. The High Court set aside the concurrent decrees and rejected the plaint under O. VII Rr. 11 and 13 CPC. Ref: 2024 YLR 56; Ghulam Hussain (deceased) v. Sher Muhammad (deceased).
records.title: Ghulam Hussain (deceased) v. Sher Muhammad (deceased)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Challenge to Old Mutations: Inheritance of Tenancy Rights
records.heading: Old mutations accorded with the applicable law and must be challenged within the time allowed
records.text: Mutations of 1935 and 1937 sanctioned under ss. 20(b) and 21(b) of the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act, 1912 accorded with the applicable law, and the predecessor of the plaintiffs was rightly excluded. A person wishing to dispute them must act within the period provided by law, otherwise the right is forfeited, as litigation must end. Ref: 2024 YLR 40; Mst. Resham Begum (deceased) v. Kenth.
records.title: Mst. Resham Begum (deceased) v. Kenth

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Defects in Ocular Account of Double Murder
records.heading: Unnatural witness conduct, no light and conflict with medical evidence undermined a double murder case
records.text: Unnatural conduct of witnesses, conflict between the ocular account and the medical evidence, no source of light in a 4.45 a.m. occurrence, and post mortem delays of about 15 hours undermined the prosecution evidence. A five and a half hour FIR delay with a 12 km distance was not fatal by itself. Ref: 2024 YLR 23; Muhammad Rafique v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Blood-Stained Weapon After One Month
records.heading: Recovery of a blood-stained weapon after one month on pointation is doubtful
records.text: Recovery of a blood-stained kappa on the accused's pointation after one month and three days was not free from doubt, since the accused had time to wash it and the blood would have disintegrated. Ref: 2024 YLR 23; Muhammad Rafique v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. The State

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: s. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: Killing on grave and sudden provocation converted a section 302(b) conviction to section 302(c)
records.text: The accused admitted in his s. 342 CrPC statement killing his sister and the other deceased on grave and sudden provocation after finding them in an objectionable condition. The s. 311 PPC honour amendment was not retrospective to the 2013 occurrence. S. 302(b) PPC was converted to s. 302(c) with fourteen years, and the co-accused was acquitted. Ref: 2024 YLR 23; Muhammad Rafique v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Pardahnashin Lady: Shifting of Onus
records.heading: The onus shifts to beneficiaries only if the lady is a Pardahnashin unable to transact worldly affairs
records.text: In a sale deed executed by an attorney, the burden shifts to the beneficiaries to prove the sale and payment only if the lady qualifies as a Pardahnashin lady unable to transact worldly affairs because of seclusion. Ref: 2024 YLR 1; Muhammad Umair Pasha v. District Collector, Jhelum.
records.title: Muhammad Umair Pasha v. District Collector, Jhelum

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Fraud: Pleading and Proof; Power of Attorney
records.heading: Fraud must be pleaded and proved and a plaintiff who admits executing a power of attorney cannot plead ignorance
records.text: Fraud must be specifically pleaded and proved. A plaintiff who admits executing a general power of attorney cannot seek to set aside a registered sale deed founded on it by pleading ignorance of its contents. The High Court set aside concurrent findings in revision and dismissed the suit. Ref: 2024 YLR 1; Muhammad Umair Pasha v. District Collector, Jhelum.
records.title: Muhammad Umair Pasha v. District Collector, Jhelum

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Minor Contradictions: Evidence Read as a Whole
records.heading: Evidence is read as a whole and minor contradictions do not defeat lawful rights
records.text: Evidence must be read as a whole to determine its preponderance, and minor contradictions or weaknesses in the statements of parties cannot deprive them of their lawful rights. Ref: 2024 YLR 1; Muhammad Umair Pasha v. District Collector, Jhelum.
records.title: Muhammad Umair Pasha v. District Collector, Jhelum

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular-Medical Conflict and Delays in Wife's Murder
records.heading: Ocular-medical conflict and unexplained delays cast serious doubt in a wife's murder case
records.text: The throttling account was negated by the post mortem findings that the hyoid bone and cartilages were intact. A nine hour twenty minute post mortem delay and an unexplained seven and a half hour FIR delay over 12 km cast serious doubt. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 214; Muhammad Saleem v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Saleem v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Withholding Material Witnesses: Art. 129(g) QSO
records.heading: Withholding the accused's children as witnesses invites an adverse inference under Article 129(g) QSO
records.text: Five children of the accused and deceased were present, the eldest aged 12 or 13, yet none was produced. This invited an adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO, and a party withholding the best evidence is presumed to have a sinister motive. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 214; Muhammad Saleem v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Saleem v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Witness
records.heading: A witness who dishonestly improves a material aspect is untrustworthy
records.text: A witness is untrustworthy if he makes dishonest improvements on a material aspect to fill gaps in the prosecution case or to align his statement with other prosecution evidence. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 214; Muhammad Saleem v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Saleem v. The State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Amended Written Statement Cannot Resile from Admission
records.heading: A defendant cannot resile from an admission in his earlier written statement by amending it
records.text: A defendant cannot resile from an admission made in his earlier written statement by amending it. In a suit for specific performance the defendant reversed his stance on willingness to perform in the amended written statement, and this, with transfer of the property to his wife, showed ill intention. Ref: 2024 CLC 205; Malik Muhammad Altaf v. Muhammad Ashraf (deceased) through Legal Heirs and another (R.S.A. No. 226 of 2016).
records.title: Malik Muhammad Altaf v. Muhammad Ashraf (deceased) through Legal Heirs and another (R.S.A. No. 226 of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Amendment of Pleadings: O. VIII R. 9 and O. VI R. 17
records.heading: Parties cannot alter pleadings on their own and amendment needs the Court's leave under Order VI Rule 17
records.text: O. VIII R. 9 CPC bars further pleadings after the written statement without leave unless it contains a set-off, and O. VI R. 17 CPC lets the Court permit amendment on just terms when necessary to determine the question in controversy. Parties cannot alter pleadings on their own. Ref: 2024 CLC 205; Malik Muhammad Altaf v. Muhammad Ashraf (deceased) through Legal Heirs and another (R.S.A. No. 226 of 2016).
records.title: Malik Muhammad Altaf v. Muhammad Ashraf (deceased) through Legal Heirs and another (R.S.A. No. 226 of 2016)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: Closing Right to File Written Statement
records.heading: Failure to file a written statement in a Family Court strikes off the defence under Order VIII Rule 10
records.text: Although the Family Courts Act, 1964 has no specific provision on failure to file a written statement, failure within time entails striking off the defence under O. VIII R. 10 CPC. The defendant may still cross-examine and lead evidence. A defendant who did not challenge the order was estopped from raising the point first in constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: 2024 CLC 187; Raja Ibadat Sajjad Khan v. Mst. Shehnaz Kousar.
records.title: Raja Ibadat Sajjad Khan v. Mst. Shehnaz Kousar

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI R. 1 CPC: Delay in Filing List of Witnesses
records.heading: A late list of witnesses needs good cause and a false plea of misplacement showed none
records.text: A list of witnesses is due within seven days of settlement of issues, and later filing needs the Court's permission on showing good cause, with reasons recorded. A false plea that the list was misplaced by the Ahalmad showed no good cause, and the High Court declined to interfere with refusal. Ref: PLD 2024 Lahore 49; Muhammad Azam v. Muhammad Anwar Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Azam v. Muhammad Anwar Khan

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Unregistered Compulsorily Registrable Document Inadmissible
records.heading: An unregistered compulsorily registrable document is inadmissible and confers no rights
records.text: A document that must be registered under s. 17 of the Registration Act, 1908 but is not registered is inadmissible, cannot confer rights even if exhibited, and cannot be produced as secondary evidence. An unregistered exchange deed of immovable property was inadmissible, and the High Court set aside the concurrent decrees. Ref: 2024 MLD 90; Khalid Mehmood v. Sardaran Bibi.
records.title: Khalid Mehmood v. Sardaran Bibi

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Declaration Suit on Unregistered Deed: ss. 42, 49 SRA
records.heading: A declaration suit based on an unregistered deed is not maintainable
records.text: An unregistered document creates no title, right or interest in the property under s. 49 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, so a suit for declaration under s. 42 on its basis is not maintainable. Ref: 2024 MLD 90; Khalid Mehmood v. Sardaran Bibi.
records.title: Khalid Mehmood v. Sardaran Bibi

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marginal Witnesses: Arts. 17 and 79 QSO
records.heading: Failure to produce the required marginal witnesses of an exchange deed is fatal and withholds best evidence
records.text: Under Arts. 17 and 79 QSO the beneficiary must prove the exchange deed by producing the marginal witnesses. Failure to produce the required number is non-compliance with a mandatory provision, is fatal, and amounts to withholding best evidence under Art. 129(g) QSO. Ref: 2024 MLD 90; Khalid Mehmood v. Sardaran Bibi.
records.title: Khalid Mehmood v. Sardaran Bibi

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Waiver of Minor's Maintenance by Agreement
records.heading: Neither a mother nor a relative can waive a minor's right to maintenance
records.text: Neither a mother nor any relative can waive a minor's right to maintenance, so an agreement by the mother not to claim it has no legal value and does not bar fixation of past and future maintenance for the minor and the mother. The mother had fed the child and could not be deprived. Ref: 2024 MLD 145, PLJ 2023 Lahore 154; Mst. Farida Bibi v. Judge Family Court (W.P. No. 18625 of 2016).
records.title: Mst. Farida Bibi v. Judge Family Court (W.P. No. 18625 of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ad Interim Injunction: Refusal Not a Case Decided
records.heading: Refusal of an ad interim injunction does not amount to a case decided
records.text: Ad interim means for the meantime, whereas temporary means for a fixed period, so refusal of an ad interim injunction does not amount to a case decided. The High Court directed the Trial Court to decide the O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC application within ten days after hearing the parties. Ref: 2024 MLD 32; Shariq Builders and Property Advisors v. Dr. Muhammad Faisal Murad (F.A.O. No. 54 of 2023).
records.title: Shariq Builders and Property Advisors v. Dr. Muhammad Faisal Murad (F.A.O. No. 54 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Criticism of Courts: Action Against Journalists
records.heading: Criticism of courts is a citizen's right and no action lies where it is only criticism
records.text: Criticism is the right of every citizen and journalist, and if the matter is only criticism no action is to be taken. The Court restrained action against the summoned journalists, directed the DG FIA to meet them, and required a federal government report on violence against journalists within two weeks. Ref: Suo Moto Action regarding Highhandedness by FIA (S.M.C. 5/2021, decided 29.01.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Suo Moto Action regarding Highhandedness by FIA (S.M.C. 5/2021, decided 29.01.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revision Against Interlocutory Orders: Case Decided
records.heading: Revision does not lie against interlocutory orders that are not a case decided
records.text: The High Court should not readily interfere with interlocutory orders unless clauses (a), (b) or (c) of s. 115(1) CPC are involved. Apprehensions of wrong exercise of jurisdiction, orders of adjournment or orders fixing a case for arguments are not a case decided to sustain revision under s. 115 CPC. Ref: 2024 MLD 55; Falak Sher v. Abdul Aziz (deceased) through L.Rs (Civil Revision No. 36424 of 2023).
records.title: Falak Sher v. Abdul Aziz (deceased) through L.Rs (Civil Revision No. 36424 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Parda Nasheen Lady: Sale Mutation Cancelled
records.heading: A sale mutation by a Parda Nasheen lady was cancelled as knowledge, advice and payment were not shown
records.text: In a suit to cancel a mutation transferring a sister's share to her brother, the evidence did not show her knowledge of the transaction or independent advice, payment was not proved, and the fingerprint expert found the thumb-impression did not match hers. No infirmity was found in the concurrent decrees. Ref: 2024 CLC 181; Syed Iqbal Hussain Shah v. Mst. Kalsoom Bibi.
records.title: Syed Iqbal Hussain Shah v. Mst. Kalsoom Bibi

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Proclaimed Offender: Right to Contest Election
records.heading: A proclaimed offender's right to contest election is not abridged absent a contrary provision
records.text: The right to form or be a member of a political party under Art. 17(2) includes the right to contest and to vote. Courts should approach electoral matters with circumspection, and absent contrary provision a person's civil right to contest is not abridged by being a proclaimed offender. Tahir Sadiq was allowed to contest from NA-49 Attock. Ref: Tahir Sadiq v. Faisal Ali and others (C.P. 150/2024, decided 29.01.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Tahir Sadiq v. Faisal Ali and others (C.P. 150/2024, decided 29.01.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale Mutation: Burden on Beneficiary; Thumb Impression
records.heading: The beneficiary of a sale mutation bears the burden and a mismatched thumb impression defeated it
records.text: The burden to prove a sale mutation lay on the beneficiary and was not discharged. The respondent had her thumb impression sent to the Provincial Finger Print Bureau, whose report and witness established that the impression on the mutation was not hers. The Supreme Court directed the petitioners to hand the land back. Ref: 2024 SCMR 202; Ghulam Fareed (deceased) v. Daulan Bibi.
records.title: Ghulam Fareed (deceased) v. Daulan Bibi

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Shamlat Deh and Chiragah: Protection of Character
records.heading: Land declared Chiragah cannot have its character changed and must be protected
records.text: Land declared Chiragah under Shart Wajib-ul-Arz cannot have its character changed, and the district administration must protect it. Claims on khasra numbers converted by housing schemes go to the Member Board of Revenue and Chief Commissioner, Islamabad, who should act against encroaching schemes and restore the land. Ref: 2024 CLC 125; Raja Tahir Mahmood v. Chief Commissioner, Islamabad.
records.title: Raja Tahir Mahmood v. Chief Commissioner, Islamabad

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Protective Bail: Discretion and Repeated Applications
records.heading: Protective bail is a discretionary remedy and a repeated application without explanation was refused
records.text: Protective bail is a Court-developed discretionary remedy rooted in s. 498-A CrPC, lacking crystallised rules, to enable access to the competent Court. The petitioner's second application, after about three months without a satisfactory explanation for not approaching the Quetta Court, was refused. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 30; Kamal Kumar v. The State.
records.title: Kamal Kumar v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Seizure of Vehicles as Case Property; Alternate Remedy
records.heading: Functionaries cannot defeat Article 199 jurisdiction by citing alternate remedies for their own illegal acts
records.text: Public functionaries cannot defeat the High Court's Art. 199 jurisdiction by pointing to alternate remedies where their own illegal acts are in issue. Vehicles seized under s. 550 CrPC and later made case property were not backed by valid reason, the seizure was struck down and the police directed to return them. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 113; Sheikh Rasheed Ahmed v. SHO Police Station Kohsar, Islamabad.
records.title: Sheikh Rasheed Ahmed v. SHO Police Station Kohsar, Islamabad

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Case Property under s. 516-A CrPC
records.heading: Case property under section 516-A CrPC includes property used in or evidencing the offence
records.text: Interim custody, interim disposal and superdari are used interchangeably. Case property is property used in the offence, property in respect of which the offence appears committed, stolen property recovered from the accused, or property that is itself evidence of the offence. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 113; Sheikh Rasheed Ahmed v. SHO Police Station Kohsar, Islamabad.
records.title: Sheikh Rasheed Ahmed v. SHO Police Station Kohsar, Islamabad

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal under s. 249-A CrPC Before Key Evidence
records.heading: A hasty acquittal under section 249-A CrPC before key evidence denied the complainant due process
records.text: The Trial Court acted hastily in acquitting the accused under s. 249-A CrPC mid-trial without the doctor's and Investigating Officer's evidence, since conviction was not remotely improbable and reasons were required. It denied the complainant due process under Art. 10-A. The case was remanded and the s. 417 appeal allowed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 76; Waheed Gul v. Rokhan Shah.
records.title: Waheed Gul v. Rokhan Shah

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-K CrPC: Quashing in Extraordinary Circumstances
records.heading: Proceedings quashed in an extraordinary case where the accused claimed ownership of the house
records.text: Where the accused claims ownership of the house and has long been in litigation over it with the person on whose behalf the complainant claims tenancy, no offence of trespass lies against an occupant or claimed purchaser, even if the claim is under litigation. This was an extraordinary case and the proceedings against the accused were quashed under s. 561-A CrPC. Petition allowed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 223; Abdul Rehman alias Rehman v. The State.
records.title: Abdul Rehman alias Rehman v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC: Ingredients and Co-Accused
records.heading: Sections 249-A and 265-K CrPC apply only in exceptional circumstances where the charge is groundless
records.text: Ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC are part of the Code and cannot be treated as non-existent, but they depart from the normal course and apply only in exceptional circumstances, where the charge is groundless or there is no probability of guilt even if the case is taken as correct. Dismissal of a co-accused's application is no ground to dismiss another accused's application. Petition under s. 561-A allowed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 223; Abdul Rehman alias Rehman v. The State.
records.title: Abdul Rehman alias Rehman v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Pointation Not Discovery under Arts. 39 and 40 QSO
records.heading: A pointation recorded after the site plan is not a discovery under Articles 39 and 40 QSO
records.text: A disclosure or pointation recorded after the site plan was already prepared is not a discovery within Arts. 39 and 40 QSO. Police practice of presenting such disclosures as discovery was held wrong and illegal. The recovery of the pistol, the empties and the FSL report had no legal value. The prosecution failed to prove the charge of qatl-i-amd s. 302 PPC and the appellant was given the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 20; Mst. Rainaz v. The State.
records.title: Mst. Rainaz v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confession of Illiterate Accused Before Magistrate
records.heading: A magistrate's confession must be voluntary and truthful and an illiterate accused's uncorroborated one failed
records.text: A confession before a Magistrate must be proved to be voluntary and truthful. The only evidence was the confession of an illiterate accused, recorded by the Magistrate in Urdu on a computer from her Pushto statement, and no independent corroboration was available. The High Court set aside the life sentence and conviction under s. 302 PPC and acquitted the appellant. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 20; Mst. Rainaz v. The State.
records.title: Mst. Rainaz v. The State

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Co-Sharer Limitation, Fraud and Mutation
records.heading: No limitation runs against a co-sharer and time for fraud runs from knowledge
records.text: No limitation runs against a co-sharer, who is presumed in possession of every part of the joint property until partition. Under s. 18 of the Limitation Act, time runs from knowledge of fraud. Mutation confers no title and mainly serves fiscal record purposes. Roznamcha Waqiati is not part of the record of rights. Ref: 2023 LHC 7640; Khushi Muhammad v. Mst. Raj Bibi (Civil Revision 295-13, decided 25.10.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Khushi Muhammad v. Mst. Raj Bibi (Civil Revision 295-13, decided 25.10.2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Polling Stations: Judicial Review of ECP Order
records.heading: The High Court may review an ECP polling station order only for a grave and patent violation of law
records.text: Establishing polling stations under s. 59 of the Elections Act 2017 primarily lies with the Election Commission, but the High Court may use judicial review to cure a grave and patent violation of law. The ECP order of 15 January 2024 was set aside and the ECP was directed to restore the polling station at the named school. Petition allowed. Ref: 2024 LHC 193; Riaz Ahmed Khan v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 195-24, decided 26.01.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Riaz Ahmed Khan v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 195-24, decided 26.01.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Detention Beyond 24 Hours: Art. 10(2) and S. 61
records.heading: An arrested person cannot be kept in police custody beyond 24 hours without a Magistrate's authority
records.text: Under Art. 10(2) of the Constitution and s. 61 CrPC an arrested person cannot be kept in police custody beyond 24 hours, excluding journey time to the Magistrate, without the Magistrate's authority. Detention beyond that period is illegal. Ref: 2024 LHC 187; Muhammad Waqas v. ASJ Lahore etc (Criminal Proceedings 79261/23, decided 17.01.2024); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. ASJ Lahore etc (Criminal Proceedings 79261/23, decided 17.01.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Father's Duty to Pay Daughter's Education Expenses
records.heading: A father must maintain his daughter until she completes graduation and obtains employment
records.text: The judgment considers whether a Muslim father must pay his daughter's educational expenses and whether maintenance of a child includes them, noting that the family statutes do not define maintenance. It concludes that the father must maintain the daughter until she completes her graduation studies and obtains employment to support herself. Ref: Qudrat Ullah v. Additional District Judge, Renala Khurd District Okara, etc (C.P. 8-L/2023, decided 25.01.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Qudrat Ullah v. Additional District Judge, Renala Khurd District Okara, etc (C.P. 8-L/2023, decided 25.01.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: NADRA Regulations: No Statutory Force
records.heading: NADRA regulations made without Federal Government approval lack statutory force and cannot be enforced by petition
records.text: Rules made by the Federal Government under s. 44 of the NADRA Ordinance 2000 have statutory force. Regulations, including service terms and promotion policy, made by the Authority under s. 45 without Federal Government approval do not, so a constitutional petition to enforce them is not maintainable. Ref: 2024 PLC (C.S.) 33; Amir Shahzad etc v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior Islamabad etc (113414/17).
records.title: Amir Shahzad etc v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior Islamabad etc (113414/17)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension Claim: Service Tribunal Jurisdiction, Art. 212
records.heading: Pension disputes of civil servants lie exclusively with the Service Tribunal and not the High Court
records.text: Pension is a term and condition of service of a civil servant, falling within Chapter II of the Civil Servants Act and within Art. 212(1)(a) of the Constitution. Disputes about it lie exclusively with the Service Tribunal, and the High Court has no jurisdiction under Art. 199. Ref: 2024 PLC (C.S.) 1; Abdus Salam v. Assistant Commissioner, Murree & 5 others (I.C.A. No. 53 of 2021).
records.title: Abdus Salam v. Assistant Commissioner, Murree & 5 others (I.C.A. No. 53 of 2021)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Recruitment: Interference Needs Proof of Malafide
records.heading: Courts should not interfere in recruitment without clear evidence of favouritism or mala fides
records.text: In the absence of specific evidence of favouritism, political interference, departure from merit or mala fides established through clear evidence, the courts should not interfere in the recruitment process. Ref: 2024 PLC (C.S.) 68; Madeeha Munir v. Government of the Punjab and 06 Others (ICA No. 56780 of 2020).
records.title: Madeeha Munir v. Government of the Punjab and 06 Others (ICA No. 56780 of 2020)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension as a Right under Art. 9
records.heading: Pension is a right earned by service and protected by Article 9, not a bounty
records.text: Pension is like salary and is a right earned by satisfactory service, not a bounty or ex-gratia payment. It cannot be arbitrarily abridged, reduced or refused except as the rules provide. As a regular source of livelihood it is protected by the right to life under Art. 9 of the Constitution. Ref: 2024 PLC (C.S.) 116; Muhammad Maqsood Aslam v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Writ Petition No. 66920 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Maqsood Aslam v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Writ Petition No. 66920 of 2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail After Arrest: Two Versions of the Occurrence
records.heading: Bail after arrest where the FIR version differed from the State's fresh investigation
records.text: Where the complainant's version in the FIR differs from the version found by the State after fresh investigation under an SP and approved by the DPO, the case of the petitioners falls within s. 497(2) CrPC. Bail granted. Ref: Mujahid Hussain S/o Ghulam Muhammad and another v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl.P. 1329/2023, decided 19.01.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Mujahid Hussain S/o Ghulam Muhammad and another v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl.P. 1329/2023, decided 19.01.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeal by Person Directly Affected by Decree
records.heading: A person directly affected by a decree can appeal against it
records.text: A person directly affected by a decree can prefer an appeal against it. The post gives only this heading. Ref: 2024 YLR 251; Mian Javed Akthar etc. v. Rana Muhammad Ismail etc. (Regular Second Appeal 37-17).
records.title: Mian Javed Akthar etc. v. Rana Muhammad Ismail etc. (Regular Second Appeal 37-17)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording S. 161 CrPC Statements
records.heading: Unexplained delay in recording section 161 CrPC statements impinges on witnesses' credibility
records.text: Where prosecution witnesses recorded their s. 161 CrPC statements three days after the incident without explanation, the delay impinges on their credibility. Ref: 2024 YLR 270; The State v. Muhammad Anwar (Murder Reference 4-14).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Anwar (Murder Reference 4-14)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence Not Conclusive Proof of Guilt
records.heading: Abscondence alone is not conclusive proof of guilt and cannot support conviction
records.text: Abscondence by itself is not conclusive proof of guilt, and without other convincing evidence an accused cannot be convicted and sentenced merely on that basis. Ref: 2024 YLR 270; The State v. Muhammad Anwar (Murder Reference 4-14).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Anwar (Murder Reference 4-14)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Single Circumstance Creating Doubt Entitles Acquittal
records.heading: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt in a prudent mind entitles the accused to acquittal
records.text: It is not necessary that many circumstances create doubt about guilt. A single circumstance that creates reasonable doubt in the mind of a prudent person entitles the accused to acquittal. Ref: 2024 YLR 270; The State v. Muhammad Anwar (Murder Reference 4-14).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Anwar (Murder Reference 4-14)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Improbable Conspiracy at Public Place
records.heading: It does not appeal to a prudent mind that many would gather publicly to plot a murder
records.text: The court observed that it does not appeal to a prudent mind that many people would assemble at a public place to hatch a conspiracy for a murder. Ref: 2024 YLR 270; The State v. Muhammad Anwar (Murder Reference 4-14).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Anwar (Murder Reference 4-14)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Suit for Damages for Medical Negligence
records.heading: A patient may sue a doctor in the Civil Court for damages for proven medical negligence
records.text: Besides proceedings under the Punjab Healthcare Commission Act 2010 (s. 4(7)), a patient may sue a doctor for damages for proven medical negligence, and the Civil Court has jurisdiction to award reasonable compensation, including for medical expenses, loss of earning, loss of amenities and pain and suffering. Appeal partially allowed and compensation enhanced. Ref: 2024 LHC 205; Mariam Sajjad v. Prof. Dr. Rasool Ahmed Chaudhary (Regular First Appeal 70634/23, decided 01.02.2024); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Mariam Sajjad v. Prof. Dr. Rasool Ahmed Chaudhary (Regular First Appeal 70634/23, decided 01.02.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Nikah During Iddat: Petitions to Dismiss Complaint Rejected
records.heading: Islamabad High Court rejected petitions to dismiss the complaint over a nikah during iddat
records.text: Full judgment of the Islamabad High Court rejecting the petitions of Bushra Bibi and Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi seeking dismissal of the case concerning a nikah allegedly contracted during iddat. The post does not set out the reasoning. Ref: Bushra Bibi v. The State etc (W.P. No. 171-2024, decided 31.01.2024); Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State & Another (Crl. Misc. No. 99-2024, decided 31.01.2024).
records.title: Bushra Bibi v. The State etc (W.P. No. 171-2024, decided 31.01.2024); Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State & Another (Crl. Misc. No. 99-2024, decided 31.01.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Jail Trial in Toshakhana and 190 Million Pound References
records.heading: A jail trial based on threats to the petitioner's life was held not mala fide
records.text: A Division Bench dismissed the petitions against the jail trial of the Toshakhana and 190 million pound references. It held the jail trial was based on threats to the petitioner's life and was not mala fide, and upheld reliance on a 1931 Bombay High Court decision on the executive's power to determine the place of hearing. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. No. 198-2024; W.P. No. 199-2024); Justice Aamer Farooq; Justice Tariq Mahmood Jahangiri.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. No. 198-2024; W.P. No. 199-2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Cypher Case: Conviction under Official Secrets Act
records.heading: Special Court convicted two accused in the cypher case under the Official Secrets Act 1923
records.text: The Special Court held Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and Shah Mehmood Qureshi guilty under ss. 5(3)(a), 5(1)(c), 5(1)(d) and 9 of the Official Secrets Act 1923 read with s. 34 PPC. Imran Khan received 10 years rigorous imprisonment under s. 5(3)(a) and 2 years with a fine of Rs. 10 lakh under each of ss. 5(1)(c) and 5(1)(d) punishable under s. 5(3)(b). Ref: The State v. Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and Makhdoom Shah Mehmood Qureshi (FIR No. 06/2023, dated 15.08.2023).
records.title: The State v. Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and Makhdoom Shah Mehmood Qureshi (FIR No. 06/2023, dated 15.08.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summons in Complaint: Ss. 496 and 496B PPC
records.heading: Summons under section 496B PPC set aside for defective procedure while section 496 summons stood
records.text: Petitions against summoning in an iddat nikah complaint were partly allowed. Summons for s. 496B PPC were set aside because the requisite procedure was not followed. Summons for s. 496 PPC stood, as issuance of process does not itself infringe rights and the objections went to merits, so the trial continues. Ref: Bushra Bibi v. The State etc. (W.P. No. 171-2024) and Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State & Another (Crl. Misc. No. 99-2024), decided 31.01.2024.
records.title: Bushra Bibi v. The State etc. (W.P. No. 171-2024) and Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State & Another (Crl. Misc. No. 99-2024), decided 31.01.2024

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Use of 'August Court' for Supreme Court
records.heading: The Constitution describes the Court as the Supreme Court of Pakistan without any prefix or adjective
records.text: The Supreme Court observed that the Constitution describes it as the Supreme Court of Pakistan without any prefix or adjective, and that everyone should abide by that description rather than repeatedly using 'august' or 'August Court'. Ref: 2024 SCMR 209; M Taimoor Ali v. State.
records.title: M Taimoor Ali v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Bail Application: Fresh Grounds After Withdrawal
records.heading: Counsel should insist on a merits decision instead of withdrawing a bail petition with a fresh ground
records.text: If a fresh ground had arisen before the High Court's order, counsel should have insisted on a decision on merits instead of withdrawing the bail petition. The position is settled by Nazir Ahmad v. State (PLD 2014 SC 241) and Muhammad Aslam v. State (PLD 2015 SC 41). The petition was not pressed before the Supreme Court. Ref: 2024 SCMR 209; M Taimoor Ali v. State.
records.title: M Taimoor Ali v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Police Opinion on Guilt Not Binding
records.heading: The police opinion on an accused's guilt is ipse dixit and does not bind the court
records.text: The ipse dixit of the police on the guilt or innocence of an accused cannot be relied on, as that is for the Trial Court to decide on the evidence. Leave converted into appeal and allowed, and the petitioner admitted to bail. Ref: 2024 SCMR 205; Naveed Sattar v. State.
records.title: Naveed Sattar v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Identification Parade After Nomination by Complainant
records.heading: An identification parade held after the complainant nominated the accused is prima facie open to question
records.text: Where the identification parade was held after the complainant had nominated the petitioner, the sanctity of the parade is prima facie open to question. Leave converted into appeal and allowed, and the petitioner admitted to bail. Ref: 2024 SCMR 205; Naveed Sattar v. State.
records.title: Naveed Sattar v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Call Data Record Not Conclusive Evidence
records.heading: A Call Data Record without supporting material is not conclusive evidence of guilt or innocence
records.text: Without concrete supporting material, a Call Data Record is not conclusive evidence of the guilt or innocence of an accused. Leave converted into appeal and allowed, and the petitioner admitted to bail. Ref: 2024 SCMR 205; Naveed Sattar v. State.
records.title: Naveed Sattar v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: Delayed Nomination in Supplementary Statements
records.heading: Nomination only in a fourth supplementary statement made bail a case of further inquiry
records.text: The complainant nominated the petitioner only in a fourth supplementary statement, over four months after the occurrence, and kept changing her stance. With no direct evidence and the petitioner in custody for over 20 months, the case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC for further inquiry. Bail granted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 205; Naveed Sattar v. State.
records.title: Naveed Sattar v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Photographs Not Sent for Forensic Examination
records.heading: Photographs not sent for forensic examination are unsafe to rely on as evidence
records.text: Where nothing shows that photographs allegedly connecting the petitioner with the crime were sent for forensic examination, it is unsafe to rely on them as evidence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 205; Naveed Sattar v. State.
records.title: Naveed Sattar v. State

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Identification Parade, Speedy Justice and Frivolous Litigation
records.heading: The State must ensure expeditious justice under Article 37(d) and curb frivolous litigation
records.text: The State must ensure inexpensive and expeditious justice under Art. 37(d), and judges must protect fundamental rights with an open mind. The Government should curb false and frivolous litigation and courts should discourage it. The prosecution case rested on an identification parade held in jail and recovery of money. The outcome is not stated in the post. Ref: Mehboob Hassan v. Akhtar Islam, etc (Crl.P. 235-L/2015, decided 27.10.2023); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Mehboob Hassan v. Akhtar Islam, etc (Crl.P. 235-L/2015, decided 27.10.2023)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Multiple Post-Dated Cheques: Single FIR Only
records.heading: Only one FIR can be registered for several cheques issued together for staged payment
records.text: Where several cheques of different dates were issued together for staged payment, only one FIR can be registered for their dishonour, and later dishonoured cheques are dealt with in that case. A second FIR on the same transaction is an abuse of process, and the High Court quashed it. Ref: 2022 MLD 31; Hamid Khan v. The State and 2 others.
records.title: Hamid Khan v. The State and 2 others

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikah During Iddat: Trial Court Judgment
records.heading: Senior Civil Judge's judgment on a second nikah within the iddat of the first
records.text: The Senior Civil Judge's detailed judgment records findings that the accused had contact before the nikah of 1 January 2018 and that their lengthy meetings in the complainant's absence were unjustified. It notes that the woman's version on iddat is normally preferred but was rejected by the complainant, and that a second nikah could not take place within the iddat of the first. Ref: Complainant v. Imran Khan Niazi and others (decided 03.02.2024); Justice Qudratullah.
records.title: Complainant v. Imran Khan Niazi and others (decided 03.02.2024)
records.court: Court of Senior Civil Judge, Islamabad

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Challenge to Paternity: No Negative Declaration
records.heading: No negative declaration on paternity can be sought under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act
records.text: No negative declaration on paternity can be sought under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, only a positive one. Under Art. 128 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order 1984 even a father cannot deny paternity beyond the prescribed period, and third parties have no locus standi. The bar protects dignity and privacy under Art. 14. Ref: Shafqat Hussain v. Abdul Hameed and others (Writ Petition No. 2775-Q of 2023, decided 22.01.2024).
records.title: Shafqat Hussain v. Abdul Hameed and others (Writ Petition No. 2775-Q of 2023, decided 22.01.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 189: Conflicting Supreme Court Judgments
records.heading: Where Supreme Court judgments conflict, the judgment of the larger Bench prevails under Article 189
records.text: Under Art. 189 of the Constitution, where Supreme Court judgments conflict on a point of law, the judgment of the larger Bench prevails. Ref: 2024 CLC 114; Reham Dad v. Province of Punjab.
records.title: Reham Dad v. Province of Punjab

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Evasive Denial in Written Statement
records.heading: An evasive denial in a written statement is an admission of the fact
records.text: An evasive denial in a written statement is an admission of the fact by the defendant. Ref: 2024 CLC 1; National Command Authority through D.G. SPD, Rawalpindi v. Zahoor Azam.
records.title: National Command Authority through D.G. SPD, Rawalpindi v. Zahoor Azam

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Civil Awards: Procedure for Conferment under Art. 259(2)
records.heading: The President confers civil awards under Article 259(2) on recommendation through a set procedure
records.text: Under Art. 259(2) of the Constitution read with the Act, the President confers civil awards on recommendation, following a set procedure through the Cabinet Division and a Committee. The contention that the Committee has no authority to confer the award had no force, and Art. 4 rights are balanced by the duty to obey the law under Art. 5(2). Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 86; Khushdil Khan Malik v. Federation of Pakistan and others (W.P. No. 3542/2022).
records.title: Khushdil Khan Malik v. Federation of Pakistan and others (W.P. No. 3542/2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: No Right to Civil Award Without Nomination; Delay
records.heading: There is no right to a civil award without nomination through the Cabinet Division
records.text: Nominations for civil awards go through the nominating agency to the Cabinet Division and the Awards Committees, and then to the President. The petitioner never approached the Cabinet Division because his agency had not forwarded his nomination, so he could not claim the award as of right. He also approached the Court after unexplained delay of about five months. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 86; Khushdil Khan Malik v. Federation of Pakistan and others (W.P. No. 3542/2022).
records.title: Khushdil Khan Malik v. Federation of Pakistan and others (W.P. No. 3542/2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 23 Specific Relief Act: Decree on Compromise, Third Party Fraud
records.heading: Even on compromise the court must check legality before decreeing specific performance, and a third party may join
records.text: The discretion to decree specific performance is exercised on sound legal principles, and even on a compromise or conceding statement the court must check legality and genuineness. A decree is redundant against a contesting third party where fraud or misrepresentation is alleged. The impugned order was set aside, the petitioner was allowed to join the suit as a necessary party, and the petition was allowed.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Import Restrictions on Law Books: National Security Discretion
records.heading: Import restrictions on law books driven by national security are not reviewable on narrow rationality grounds
records.text: Discretion under s. 3(1) of the 1950 Act must be exercised by rules of reason and justice, but where the decision is largely driven by national security and foreign affairs, it cannot be reviewed on narrow rationality grounds. The impugned SRO and Para were held valid, the right to read was held to be a fundamental right, and the Federal Government was directed to appoint an officer to hear review or revision. Ref: 2024 LHC 254; Kashif Law Book House etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Misc. Writ 34660/20, decided 26.01.2024); Justice Shahid Karim.
records.title: Kashif Law Book House etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Misc. Writ 34660/20, decided 26.01.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation of Sale: Roznamcha Entry and Proof
records.heading: A Roznamcha entry is a ministerial act and not an admission, and mutation is sanctioned under section 42(6)
records.text: A Roznamcha entry of a change in rights is a ministerial act of the Patwari that starts the transfer process, and it is not an admission by the person recording it. A mutation is sanctioned by the Revenue Officer under s. 42(6) of the Punjab Land Revenue Act 1967 in the presence of the person whose right is acquired. Ref: 2024 MLD 18; Nazeer Ahmad v. Muhammad Sadiq (deceased) through L.Rs and 2 others (C.R. No. 174 of 2017).
records.title: Nazeer Ahmad v. Muhammad Sadiq (deceased) through L.Rs and 2 others (C.R. No. 174 of 2017)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Widow's Suit for Dower: Art. 104 Limitation
records.heading: A widow's dower claim is time-barred if filed more than three years after the husband's death
records.text: Art. 104 of the Limitation Act 1908 allows three years for a claim of dower where marriage is dissolved by death or divorce. The widow sued four years after her husband's death, so her suit was rightly dismissed as time-barred. Ref: 2024 MLD 51; Hameeda v. Khan Muhammad and 2 others (C.P. (t) 157 of 2022).
records.title: Hameeda v. Khan Muhammad and 2 others (C.P. (t) 157 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Jurisdiction: Widow's Share in Husband's Property
records.heading: A widow's claim to a share in her husband's property is outside Family Court jurisdiction
records.text: A widow's claim to a share in property left by her husband is outside the jurisdiction of the Family Court under s. 5(1) and Part I of the Schedule to the Family Courts Act 1964. The suit was not maintainable, and the constitutional petition was dismissed in limine. Ref: 2024 MLD 51; Hameeda v. Khan Muhammad and 2 others (C.P. (t) 157 of 2022).
records.title: Hameeda v. Khan Muhammad and 2 others (C.P. (t) 157 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Minor's Maintenance Cannot Be Waived
records.heading: A minor's right to maintenance cannot be waived by the mother or blood relatives
records.text: A minor's right to maintenance cannot be waived by the mother or blood relatives. A Punchayat Nama signed by the grandfather, under which the mother would not claim maintenance in return for custody, did not disentitle the minor. The Family Court's award was upheld. Ref: 2024 MLD 145; Farida Bibi v. Judge Family Court (WP 18625 of 2016).
records.title: Farida Bibi v. Judge Family Court (WP 18625 of 2016)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Mother's Maintenance for Fostering Period
records.heading: A mother who feeds the minor during the fostering period is entitled to maintenance from the father
records.text: Although a wife who leaves the marital home without reason may be refused maintenance, a mother who feeds the minor during the fostering period is entitled to maintenance from the father, as the welfare of the minor is supreme. The High Court granted her past maintenance for the fostering period at the rate awarded to the minor. Ref: 2024 MLD 145; Farida Bibi v. Judge Family Court (WP 18625 of 2016).
records.title: Farida Bibi v. Judge Family Court (WP 18625 of 2016)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Enhancement of Minor's Maintenance: S. 151 CPC Application
records.heading: The Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction under section 151 CPC to enhance a minor's maintenance
records.text: The Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction on an application under s. 151 CPC to enhance a minor's maintenance even after the final decree. The mother should apply there instead of invoking constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: 2024 MLD 145; Farida Bibi v. Judge Family Court (WP 18625 of 2016).
records.title: Farida Bibi v. Judge Family Court (WP 18625 of 2016)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Substandard Meat under Punjab Food Authority Act
records.heading: Bail allowed as further inquiry in a substandard meat case outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: The nature and degree of substandard meat and the applicable standard were not described, a valid Punjab Food Authority certificate covered the date of occurrence, there was no complaint, and the Veterinary Officer's report was missing. The offence did not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Bail allowed as a case of further inquiry. Ref: 2024 YLR 161; Rehmat Ullah v. The State (47143-B of 2023).
records.title: Rehmat Ullah v. The State (47143-B of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance and Dowry Articles: Remand to Confront USB
records.heading: Dowry articles decree set aside and remanded to confront witnesses with the USB
records.text: In a wife's suit for maintenance and dowry articles, the courts below had decreed maintenance and dowry. The High Court set aside the judgments on recovery of dowry articles and remanded the case to the Trial Court for fresh decision after confronting witnesses with the USB produced by the petitioner. Ref: 2024 YLR 265; Babar Rasool v. ADJ Ssrgodha (WP 23372 of 2020).
records.title: Babar Rasool v. ADJ Ssrgodha (WP 23372 of 2020)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Maintainability of Appeal under S. 19 Contempt Ordinance
records.heading: Contempt proceedings give an aggrieved person no vested right and appeal maintainability is discretionary under section 19
records.text: S. 19 of the Contempt of Court Ordinance 2003, read with Art. 204, gives the appellate court broad discretion on maintainability, depending on the order appealed against. Contempt proceedings are between the contemnor and the Court and give no vested right to an aggrieved person, so if proceedings are terminated not even the State or an informer can agitate them in appeal. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 109; Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020).
records.title: Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Offences Against Religion and Prolonged Pre-Trial Detention
records.heading: No one may be charged for an act that was not an offence when done
records.text: The Supreme Court regretted that in offences against religion facts give way to emotions and individual complainants supplant the State. It stressed that freedom of faith is a tenet of Islam and that no one may be charged for an act that was not an offence when done. The petitioner had been imprisoned during trial for longer than he could be punished if found guilty. Ref: Mubarak Ahmad Sani v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 1054-L/2023, decided 06.02.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Mubarak Ahmad Sani v. The State, etc (Crl.P. 1054-L/2023, decided 06.02.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Special Oath under Oaths Act 1873, Ss. 8 to 11
records.heading: A special oath under the Oaths Act 1873 binds the person who made the offer
records.text: Under s. 9 of the Oaths Act 1873 the court may communicate a party's offer of a special oath to the other party. On acceptance, s. 10 allows administration of the oath, and under s. 11 the evidence so given binds the person who made the offer and is conclusive proof of the matter stated. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 70; Fayyaz Ahmad through Special Attorney Muhammad Aamer Munir v. Sube Deen (Civil Revision 66481/23).
records.title: Fayyaz Ahmad through Special Attorney Muhammad Aamer Munir v. Sube Deen (Civil Revision 66481/23)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Power Is a Power to Punish
records.heading: The contempt power is a power to punish and not a means of enforcing orders
records.text: The contempt power is a power to punish and is not a mechanism for execution or enforcement of court orders. Proceedings may be initiated suo motu or at the instance of a party. The Division Bench declined to interfere with the order of the Judge in Chambers dropping the contempt proceedings. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 109; Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020).
records.title: Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Civil Contempt Distinguished from Other Forms
records.heading: Civil contempt needs a duly served order and wilful, mala fide non-compliance by a party
records.text: Civil contempt differs from criminal and judicial contempt. It alone concerns an order within s. 2(a) of the Contempt of Court Ordinance 2003, and includes undertakings recorded by a court. It requires a duly served order and wilful, mala fide non-compliance by a contemnor who is a party in his personal capacity. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 109; Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020).
records.title: Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: No Exercise of Jurisdiction for Academic Purposes
records.heading: A court's jurisdiction cannot be exercised for mere academic discussion or a futile purpose
records.text: The court's jurisdiction cannot be invoked or exercised for mere academic discussion or a futile purpose. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 109; Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020).
records.title: Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Purpose of the Right of Appeal
records.heading: The remedy of appeal exists to correct orders and eliminate miscarriage of justice
records.text: The remedy of appeal exists to examine the correctness and validity of orders of the court below and to eliminate chances of miscarriage of justice. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 109; Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020).
records.title: Dr. Manzoor Hussain Malik and another v. Mahar Muhammad Khalid Ahmad, Additional Commissioner (Revenue), Bahawalpur and 2 others (I.C.As. Nos. 174 of 2021 and 81 of 2020)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Registrar Cannot Initiate Litigation for Supreme Court
records.heading: The Registrar of the Supreme Court has no power to initiate litigation without the Court's approval
records.text: Under O. III R. 1 of the Supreme Court Rules 1980 the Registrar is executive head of the office but has no power to initiate litigation, and the Rules do not envisage it. The Registrar could not be given this responsibility nor undertake it without the Court's approval. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 192; Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No. 3532 of 2023).
records.title: Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No. 3532 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 19A: Right to Information and the Supreme Court
records.heading: The Right of Access to Information Act 2017 does not apply to the Supreme Court but Article 19A does
records.text: The Right of Access to Information Act 2017 applies only to public bodies as defined in s. 2(ix), which does not include the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court remains within Art. 19A, and information of public importance can be sought subject to regulation and reasonable restrictions. Legislature cannot grant a public entity outright exclusion from the right. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 192; Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No. 3532 of 2023).
records.title: Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No. 3532 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 19A: Right to Know Replaces Need to Know
records.heading: Article 19A replaced need-to-know with a right to know and shifted the burden to those concealing
records.text: Art. 19A has turned access to information from a need-to-know basis into a right-to-know, shifting the burden to those who wish to conceal information. Access is a fundamental right and no longer a discretion. It guards against corruption and promotes participatory governance. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 192; Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No. 3532 of 2023).
records.title: Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No. 3532 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
