records.topic: Information on Supreme Court Staff, Vacancies and Service Rules
records.heading: Supreme Court issued directions on a request for staff and vacancy information under Article 19A
records.text: The petitioner sought from the Registrar information on sanctioned staff strength, vacancies, daily-wage and contract staff, new posts since 2017, female staff and similar matters, under Art. 19A. The Supreme Court issued directions on the request, including refund of the court fee paid on the petition and the intra-court appeal. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 192; Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No. 3532 of 2023).
records.title: Mukhtar Ahmad Ali v. The Registrar, Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad and another (Civil Petition No. 3532 of 2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Delimitation Disputes Deferred Until After General Elections
records.heading: Delimitation disputes should be addressed after general elections, on the principle of proportionality
records.text: On the principle of proportionality, general elections have primacy and delimitation disputes should be addressed after them. The High Court interfered with the ECP's delimitation order about three days before notification of the Election Programme, which was held improper. The case was to be fixed after the General Elections 2024. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 207; Gul Khan and other v. Saeed ur Rehman and others (Civil Petition No. 4305 of 2023).
records.title: Gul Khan and other v. Saeed ur Rehman and others (Civil Petition No. 4305 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: PEMRA: Delegation of Powers to Chairman
records.heading: PEMRA delegation of powers must be reasonable and the Chairman lacked validly delegated authority
records.text: PEMRA may delegate its powers under the PEMRA Ordinance 2002 subject to rules, and rules of delegation must be reasonable, non-arbitrary and consistent with the statutory purpose. In this case the Chairman had no validly delegated authority to approve the recommendation of the Council of Complaints. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 230; Messrs Fun Infotainment (Pvt.) Limited / Neo T.V., Lahore v. Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority through its Chairman, Islamabad and others (Civil Petition No. 5438 of 2021).
records.title: Messrs Fun Infotainment (Pvt.) Limited / Neo T.V., Lahore v. Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority through its Chairman, Islamabad and others (Civil Petition No. 5438 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Army Act: Conviction Under Alternative Charge
records.heading: An accused may be convicted of an alternative offence if the principal charge fails
records.text: Under s. 111(5) of the Pakistan Army Act 1952, Rr. 21(4) and 51(7) and (8) of the Army Act Rules 1954, and ss. 236 and 237 CrPC, an accused may be convicted of an alternative offence he might have been charged with if the principal charge fails. The convictions on the alternative charge stood. Appeal and constitutional petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 235; Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas and another v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence and others (Civil Appeal No. 1191 of 2016 and Constitution Petition No. 18 of 2000).
records.title: Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas and another v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence and others (Civil Appeal No. 1191 of 2016 and Constitution Petition No. 18 of 2000)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial Review of Court Martial Decisions
records.heading: Court Martial decisions are reviewable only for mala fides, want of jurisdiction or coram non judice
records.text: Orders and sentences of a Court Martial or other forums under the Pakistan Army Act 1952 (s. 97) are reviewable by the High Courts and Supreme Court under Arts. 199 and 184(3) only for mala fides including malice in law, want of jurisdiction or coram non judice. Absent mala fides, the Field General Court Martial convictions were not coram non judice. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 235; Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas and another v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence and others (Civil Appeal No. 1191 of 2016 and Constitution Petition No. 18 of 2000).
records.title: Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas and another v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence and others (Civil Appeal No. 1191 of 2016 and Constitution Petition No. 18 of 2000)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Laches in Constitutional Jurisdiction: Delay Defeats Equity
records.heading: Delay defeats equity and constitutional petitions must be brought promptly or fail for laches
records.text: Delay defeats equity, and a right not enforced within the time allowed becomes unenforceable. Limitation does not strictly apply to proceedings under Arts. 199 and 184(3), but they must be brought promptly. A party guilty of contumacious lethargy or gross negligence may be non-suited on the ground of laches. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 235; Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas and another v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence and others (Civil Appeal No. 1191 of 2016 and Constitution Petition No. 18 of 2000).
records.title: Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas and another v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence and others (Civil Appeal No. 1191 of 2016 and Constitution Petition No. 18 of 2000)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Dismissed Army Officer: Loss of Housing Scheme Benefits
records.heading: Dismissal from the army removes housing scheme benefits without double jeopardy
records.text: Dismissal from service takes away perks, privileges and amenities conferred on army personnel, including housing scheme membership and plots. Withdrawal of these benefits does not amount to double jeopardy, as the case falls outside Art. 13 of the Constitution and s. 403 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 235; Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas and another v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence and others (Civil Appeal No. 1191 of 2016 and Constitution Petition No. 18 of 2000).
records.title: Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas and another v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence and others (Civil Appeal No. 1191 of 2016 and Constitution Petition No. 18 of 2000)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Appeals of Army Officers Dismissed, Sentences Upheld
records.heading: Supreme Court upheld sentences of army officers in the conspiracy case, per the Urdu post
records.text: According to the Urdu post, the Supreme Court upheld the sentences of army officers convicted in the conspiracy to topple the Benazir Bhutto government and dismissed their appeals. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 235; Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas v. Federation of Pakistan thr. Secy. M/o Defence, Rawalpindi (C.A. 1191/2016).
records.title: Ex. Col. Muhammad Azad Minhas v. Federation of Pakistan thr. Secy. M/o Defence, Rawalpindi (C.A. 1191/2016)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Intra-Party Elections: PTI Ineligible for Election Symbol
records.heading: A bare certificate of intra-party elections does not suffice when challenged, and PTI's ineligibility was upheld
records.text: A bare certificate that intra-party elections were held does not suffice when challenged, though the ECP should not concern itself with minor irregularities. No prima facie evidence of any election was produced and the complaints of fourteen members were wrongly brushed aside. The ECP declaration that PTI was ineligible to obtain the election symbol was upheld. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 267; Election Commission of Pakistan through Special Secretary, Islamabad v. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Islamabad through authorized person and others (Civil Petition No. 42 of 2024).
records.title: Election Commission of Pakistan through Special Secretary, Islamabad v. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Islamabad through authorized person and others (Civil Petition No. 42 of 2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 62(1)(f): Lifetime Disqualification Ended
records.heading: Lifetime disqualification under Article 62(1)(f) conflicts with fundamental rights and Sami Ullah Baloch was overruled
records.text: By a 6 to 1 majority in a judgment by Qazi Faez Isa CJ, the Supreme Court overruled Sami Ullah Baloch, holding that lifetime disqualification under Art. 62(1)(f) conflicts with fundamental rights, and that until legislation it is to be read like Art. 62(1)(d), (e) and (g). The five year period under s. 232(2) of the Elections Act applies. Yahya Afridi J dissented. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 256; Hamza Rasheed Khan v. Election Appellate Tribunal, Lahore High Court, Lahore & others (C.A. 982/2018); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Hamza Rasheed Khan v. Election Appellate Tribunal, Lahore High Court, Lahore & others (C.A. 982/2018)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Counsel and Client; Removal of Law Officers
records.heading: A client need not give reasons for withdrawing a brief and the Chief Minister may remove Law Officers
records.text: A client need not give reasons for withdrawing a brief, and a lawyer is a spokesman and adviser, not an agent. The Chief Minister is the competent authority to appoint and remove the Advocate General and other Law Officers, who cannot be treated as public servants whom the Government must retain despite lack of confidence. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 129; Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023).
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Care-Taker Government: Meaning and Role
records.heading: A care-taker government is temporary and expected to refrain from important policy decisions
records.text: A care-taker is one who looks after matters in the owner's absence. A care-taker government is temporary, holds office until an election is held, carries on routine business and is expected to refrain from important policy decisions. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 129; Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023).
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Care-Taker Government: Removal of Advocate General Upheld
records.heading: A care-taker government may remove Law Officers who do not help create an impression of impartiality
records.text: The sole purpose of a care-taker government is fair and free elections, and it may dispense with Law Officers who do not help create an impression of impartiality. The notification removing the Advocate General Punjab and other Law Officers was upheld. The notification appointing new Law Officers was set aside to the extent they had served in the preceding political government. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 129; Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023).
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Later Special Law Prevails: Leges Posteriores Maxim
records.heading: Of two conflicting special laws with overriding clauses, the later generally prevails
records.text: Where two special laws with overriding clauses conflict, the later statute generally prevails over the earlier one, on the maxim leges posteriores priores contrarias abrogant. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 129; Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023).
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Meaning of Public Interest in Statutes
records.heading: Public interest takes its colour from the statute and in elections means honest, free and fair elections
records.text: Public interest has no strict meaning and takes its colour from the statute in which it occurs. In the election context it covers ensuring honest, just, free and fair elections in accordance with law, in line with Arts. 218 to 224 and 224-A of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 129; Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023).
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Law Officers of Earlier Governments: Public Interest and S. 230 Elections Act
records.heading: Appointing care-taker Law Officers from earlier political governments was ultra vires section 230 of the Elections Act
records.text: Appointing as care-taker Law Officers persons who had served in earlier political governments could not be justified in the public interest and would defeat the aim of free and fair elections. The notification was declared ultra vires s. 230 of the Elections Act 2017 to that extent, and the constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 129; Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023).
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Care-Taker Government Is Sui Generis
records.heading: A care-taker government is sui generis and differs from an elected government
records.text: A care-taker government is sui generis. The Constitution distinguishes between an elected and a care-taker Chief Minister in obligations, responsibilities, powers and functions. An elected government answers to the Assembly, whereas a care-taker government works in the absence of an Assembly. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 129; Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023).
records.title: Ashfaq Ahmad Kharal and 21 others v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Law and Parliamentary Affairs and others (Writ Petitions Nos. 5324, 5343, 5055 and 6545 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Framing of Issues Discretionary
records.heading: On a section 12(2) CPC application the court need not always frame issues and record evidence
records.text: On an application under s. 12(2) CPC the court is not bound in every case to frame issues and record evidence as in a suit. It decides, on the nature of the fraud or misrepresentation alleged, whether issues and evidence are needed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 262; Hafiz Malik Kamran Akbar and others v. Muhammad Shafi (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (Civil Petition No. 2341-L of 2016).
records.title: Hafiz Malik Kamran Akbar and others v. Muhammad Shafi (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (Civil Petition No. 2341-L of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Who May Apply
records.heading: Any person adversely affected may apply under section 12(2) CPC to the court that passed the judgment
records.text: Fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction is raised by application under s. 12(2) CPC to the court that passed the judgment, not by separate suit. The word person is not limited to the judgment-debtor or successors and includes anyone adversely affected, whether or not a party to the original proceedings. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 262; Hafiz Malik Kamran Akbar and others v. Muhammad Shafi (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (Civil Petition No. 2341-L of 2016).
records.title: Hafiz Malik Kamran Akbar and others v. Muhammad Shafi (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (Civil Petition No. 2341-L of 2016)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Art. 204 and Contempt Ordinance: Compliance with High Court Judgment
records.heading: The High Court should have ensured compliance with its own judgment under Article 204
records.text: Authority on Art. 204 of the Constitution and ss. 2, 3 and 5 of the Contempt of Court Ordinance 2003. A court should neither assume a jurisdiction not vested in it nor renounce one that is, and the High Court should have ensured compliance with its own judgment instead of leaving it ineffectual. Ref: Muhammad Ishaque & others v. M/s. Zeal Pak Cement Factory Ltd. (C.P. 175-K/2022, decided 22.12.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Ishaque & others v. M/s. Zeal Pak Cement Factory Ltd. (C.P. 175-K/2022, decided 22.12.2023)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Stamp Act 1899: Object and Purpose
records.heading: The Stamp Act 1899 ensures payment of dues on instruments and protects the exchequer
records.text: The Stamp Act 1899 ensures payment of dues on documents and instruments for registration and protects the national exchequer. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 94; Nestle Pakistan Limited through Authorized Signatory v. Sub-Registrar, Nishtar Town, Lahore and another (Writ Petition No. 53187 of 2022).
records.title: Nestle Pakistan Limited through Authorized Signatory v. Sub-Registrar, Nishtar Town, Lahore and another (Writ Petition No. 53187 of 2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Local Commission Cannot Impound Document for Short Stamp Duty
records.heading: A Local Commission cannot impound a document for short stamp duty and must report to the Sub-Registrar
records.text: A Local Commission is paid fees by the party, not from the exchequer, and is not in charge of a public office under the Stamp Act 1899. He cannot impound documents and must report omissions to the Sub-Registrar. The petitioner was not liable for stamp duty on service charges, and the Sub-Registrar was directed to register the lease deed. Petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 94; Nestle Pakistan Limited through Authorized Signatory v. Sub-Registrar, Nishtar Town, Lahore and another (Writ Petition No. 53187 of 2022).
records.title: Nestle Pakistan Limited through Authorized Signatory v. Sub-Registrar, Nishtar Town, Lahore and another (Writ Petition No. 53187 of 2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Redundancy Principle in Statutory Interpretation
records.heading: A word or phrase in a provision is presumed deliberate and not redundant
records.text: It is presumed that the legislature chooses its words carefully, and a word or phrase added to a provision is not to be treated as redundant. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 94; Nestle Pakistan Limited through Authorized Signatory v. Sub-Registrar, Nishtar Town, Lahore and another (Writ Petition No. 53187 of 2022).
records.title: Nestle Pakistan Limited through Authorized Signatory v. Sub-Registrar, Nishtar Town, Lahore and another (Writ Petition No. 53187 of 2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Fiscal Charging Provision: Interpretation Favouring Individual
records.heading: A fiscal charging provision with two possible meanings is read in favour of the individual
records.text: When a charging provision of a fiscal statute has two possible interpretations, the one favouring the individual should be applied. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 94; Nestle Pakistan Limited through Authorized Signatory v. Sub-Registrar, Nishtar Town, Lahore and another (Writ Petition No. 53187 of 2022).
records.title: Nestle Pakistan Limited through Authorized Signatory v. Sub-Registrar, Nishtar Town, Lahore and another (Writ Petition No. 53187 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Short Adjournments and Day-to-Day Trial: Art. 10-A
records.heading: Short adjournments or day-to-day trial do not per se violate Article 10-A
records.text: Short adjournments or day-to-day trial do not per se deny Art. 10-A of the Constitution, so long as every right of the accused remains intact and every objection is dealt with in accordance with law. Ref: PLD 2024 Islamabad 41; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State through Attorney General Office, Islamabad and another (Diary No. 18047 of 2023).
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State through Attorney General Office, Islamabad and another (Diary No. 18047 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supply of Documents: Signatures on Order Sheet
records.heading: Copies of section 173 documents must be supplied; order sheet signatures only prove compliance
records.text: Copies of documents appended to the s. 173 CrPC report must be given so the accused knows the case against him. Signatures of the accused on the order sheet are only proof that ss. 265-C or 241-A CrPC was complied with. Ref: PLD 2024 Islamabad 41; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State through Attorney General Office, Islamabad and another (Diary No. 18047 of 2023).
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State through Attorney General Office, Islamabad and another (Diary No. 18047 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Official Secrets Act: Supply of Cypher and Documents to Accused
records.heading: Accused may receive copies of statements and documents, subject to public interest exclusions
records.text: An accused may receive copies of statements under ss. 161 and 164 CrPC and other documents, subject to exclusion of parts whose disclosure is inexpedient in the public interest. All documents forming part of the s. 173 report were supplied. The effect of any other fundamental document is for the Trial Court. The High Court directed compliance with Art. 10-A and declined to interfere. Ref: PLD 2024 Islamabad 41; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State through Attorney General Office, Islamabad and another (Diary No. 18047 of 2023).
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State through Attorney General Office, Islamabad and another (Diary No. 18047 of 2023)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Withdrawal from Acquisition After Possession: No Funds
records.heading: Acquisition cannot be withdrawn after possession merely because the department lacked funds
records.text: Once possession was taken under an award under s. 11 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894, the acquisition was closed and the Commissioner could not withdraw under s. 48 merely because the department lacked funds. The withdrawal was invalid, illegal and without jurisdiction, and could not be held bona fide. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 218; Government of Pakistan v. Akhtar Ullah Khattak (CA No. 538 of 2022).
records.title: Government of Pakistan v. Akhtar Ullah Khattak (CA No. 538 of 2022)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Commissioner's Power to Withdraw Ends on Possession
records.heading: Power to withdraw from acquisition ends once actual possession is taken
records.text: The Commissioner's power to withdraw from acquisition is unfettered until possession is taken, after which acquisition is complete. Possession must be actual, not notional or on paper, and taken under s. 16 or 17. After possession the land vests in the Government and earlier notifications cannot be cancelled under s. 21 of the General Clauses Act 1897. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 218; Government of Pakistan v. Akhtar Ullah Khattak (CA No. 538 of 2022).
records.title: Government of Pakistan v. Akhtar Ullah Khattak (CA No. 538 of 2022)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: NAB Amendments 2022 Declared Void
records.heading: NAB amendments of 2022 declared void and affected proceedings restored
records.text: The Court held the petition under Art. 184(3) maintainable and declared the National Accountability (Amendment) Act 2022 and Second Amendment Act 2022 void. Proceedings closed or returned under them were restored, and NAB and other fora were to return the records within seven days to proceed from the same stage. Justice Mansoor Ali Shah dissented. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 102, PLJ 2023 SC 665; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const. P. 21 of 2022); Justice Umar Ata Bandial; Justice Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Law and Justice Division, Islamabad and another (Const. P. 21 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Non-Compliance with Art. 46(1) QSO
records.heading: Dying declaration not meeting Article 46(1) QSO conditions cannot sustain a conviction
records.text: If the conditions for recording a dying declaration under Art. 46(1) QSO and Rule 25.21 of the Police Rules 1934 are not met, it can at most be treated as a s. 161 CrPC statement, and a conviction cannot rest on it. Ref: 2024 LHC 369; Ghulam Abbas Agha v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 78701/19, decided 30.01.2024); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Ghulam Abbas Agha v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 78701/19, decided 30.01.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Second Marriage Complaint under S. 6 MFLO Through Attorney
records.heading: Complaint under section 6 MFLO for second marriage cannot proceed through a special attorney
records.text: A wife's complaint under s. 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 for a second marriage without Arbitration Council permission was dismissed as not proceedable through a special attorney. The post refers to the Rules 1961 under s. 11 governing trial and to a 1976 notification substituting the words aggrieved party for Union Council. The outcome in the High Court is not stated. Ref: 2024 LHC 381; Sonia Sharief v. ADJ etc (Writ Petition 97-24, decided 25.01.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Sonia Sharief v. ADJ etc (Writ Petition 97-24, decided 25.01.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Presumption of Subsisting Marriage: Art. 129 QSO
records.heading: A marriage is presumed to subsist until death unless divorce is proved
records.text: A marriage is presumed to subsist until the husband's death unless divorce is established by evidence or other material, in view of Illustration (d) of Art. 129 QSO, under which a state of things shown to exist is presumed to continue. Ref: Syed Saqlain Shahana through Legal Heirs v. ADJ Okara etc (Misc. Writ 8728/23, decided 09.02.2023); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Syed Saqlain Shahana through Legal Heirs v. ADJ Okara etc (Misc. Writ 8728/23, decided 09.02.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unintentional Occurrence Remark Not a Specific Plea
records.heading: A remark that the occurrence was unintentional is not a specific plea
records.text: The accused's passing remark in cross-examination and in his s. 342 CrPC statement that the occurrence was unintentional is not a specific plea and does not shift the burden. The case is judged on the prosecution evidence. The post also notes a lost bullet in the body and no spent shell for a single 12 bore shot. Ref: 2024 LHC 390; Amir Shahzad v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 38881/19, decided 25.01.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Amir Shahzad v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 38881/19, decided 25.01.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Witness Disbelieved in Earlier Trial
records.heading: A witness disbelieved in an earlier trial may be relied on later if natural
records.text: A witness disbelieved or found exaggerating in an earlier trial may be relied on in a later trial if his testimony is straightforward and natural. Under Art. 3 QSO only a person convicted of perjury or false evidence is barred, subject to repentance. Ref: 2024 LHC 406; Ihsan Ullah Munshi etc. v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 53656/19, decided 17.01.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ihsan Ullah Munshi etc. v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 53656/19, decided 17.01.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence as Corroborative Evidence
records.heading: Long abscondence is corroborative evidence but not a sole ground of conviction
records.text: Abscondence of about 13 or 14 years is a relevant fact under Art. 21 QSO and corroborative evidence, though not a sole ground of conviction. The life sentences under s. 302(b) PPC were upheld, both appellants having a joint role in firing. Ref: 2024 LHC 406; Ihsan Ullah Munshi etc. v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 53656/19, decided 17.01.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ihsan Ullah Munshi etc. v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 53656/19, decided 17.01.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Writ Against Election Results: Remedy Before ECP
records.heading: Writ against election results is not maintainable; the remedy lies before the ECP
records.text: The Lahore High Court dismissed petitions against election results of 18 constituencies as not maintainable. The petitioners may file a representation before the ECP under ss. 8, 9, 15 and 95 of the Elections Act 2017 read with Art. 218(3), and the ECP should decide promptly, including on consolidation of results.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Gravity of Allegation Not a Bar
records.heading: Gravity of the allegation alone does not bar pre-arrest bail
records.text: The gravity of the allegation alone does not prevent pre-arrest bail where reasonable grounds exist on a tentative appraisal of the evidence. The court must assess the accused's precise role and whether the accusation aims to injure or disgrace him. The post also notes inconsistencies between the FIR and the medico-legal report and a Medical Board finding of fabricated injuries. Ref: Mir Muhammad v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A. 705/2023, decided 22.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mir Muhammad v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A. 705/2023, decided 22.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Court Does Not Monitor Police Investigation
records.heading: The court does not monitor police investigation absent mala fides or illegality
records.text: Investigation is the responsibility of the police and the IO. The court does not monitor it unless it appears mala fide, an abuse of power or in violation of the Cr.P.C., so judicial intervention during investigation is restricted and limited. Ref: Mir Muhammad v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A. 705/2023, decided 22.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mir Muhammad v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A. 705/2023, decided 22.11.2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Further Investigation or Transfer After Challan and Charge
records.heading: Further investigation or transfer is allowed after challan and charge on compelling justification
records.text: Further investigation, re-investigation or transfer of investigation is allowed until the trial concludes, even after challan, framing of charge or a pending private complaint, but only with compelling justification and where justice requires. The court may hold the challan case in abeyance but cannot halt further investigation absent exceptional circumstances. S. 56(e) of the Specific Relief Act bars injunctions against criminal investigation. Ref: 2024 LHC 420; Zain Ali and another v. Additional Inspector General of Police and others (Writ Petition No. 65602/2022).
records.title: Zain Ali and another v. Additional Inspector General of Police and others (Writ Petition No. 65602/2022)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Court May Order Accused's DNA Test under Punjab Forensic Act
records.heading: A court may order an accused's DNA test under the Punjab forensic law
records.text: S. 10 of the Punjab Act 2007 lets a court send forensic material to the PFSA for analysis, and a DNA sample falls within the definition of forensic material in s. 2(1)(g). The court may therefore order an accused's DNA test and its comparison with samples from the victim. Ref: 2023 LHC 7687; Shakeel Akhtar v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 71205/21, decided 06.07.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Shakeel Akhtar v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 71205/21, decided 06.07.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification Parade: Objection of Accused Seen by Witnesses
records.heading: Magistrate must decide the accused's objection that witnesses saw him before the identification parade
records.text: Police must prevent witnesses from seeing the accused in lock-up or custody before an identification parade, and must prove the precautions taken. Where the accused objects before the Magistrate that witnesses saw them in lock-up, the Magistrate must record and decide the objection before proceeding. Here the Magistrate ignored it and completed the parade.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 426(2B) CrPC: Suspension of Sentence After Leave
records.heading: Suspension of sentence under section 426(2B) CrPC requires a High Court certificate
records.text: Suspension of sentence under s. 426(2B) CrPC applies only where the High Court certifies a substantial question of law on interpretation of the Constitution, giving a right to special leave to appeal in the Supreme Court. If the High Court refuses the certificate, leave to appeal under O. XXIII R. 2 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980 is available instead. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 252; Muhammad Iqbal and others v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 55 of 2013).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal and others v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 55 of 2013)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody of Seized Narcotics
records.heading: Prosecution must prove an unbroken chain of custody of seized narcotics
records.text: The prosecution must establish an unbroken, safe and secure chain of custody from recovery of the drug to dispatch of samples to the Narcotics Testing Laboratory. Any break or lapse in control of the samples casts doubt on the Government Analyst's report and makes it incapable of sustaining a conviction. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 385; Shahadat Ali v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 1303 of 2019).
records.title: Shahadat Ali v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 1303 of 2019)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chemical Examiner Report: Rules 5 and 6
records.heading: An analyst report omitting tests, quantity and protocols cannot support a conviction
records.text: Rules 5 and 6 of the Control of Narcotic Substances (Government Analysts) Rules, 2001 prescribe a complete procedure for the analyst's report. A report that omits the required tests, the quantity tested and the protocols is not a proper report under s. 36 CNSA 1997, loses its sanctity and cannot support a conviction. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 385; Shahadat Ali v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 1303 of 2019).
records.title: Shahadat Ali v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 1303 of 2019)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Confiscation of Vehicle: S. 32 and S. 74 CNSA
records.heading: An innocent vehicle owner is entitled to its return, and prosecution must prove knowledge
records.text: S. 74 CNSA concerns temporary custody of the vehicle, while s. 32 governs final confiscation or release after trial. An innocent owner is entitled to return of the vehicle and the burden lies on the prosecution to prove the owner's knowledge, which must be established by evidence. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 385; Shahadat Ali v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 1303 of 2019).
records.title: Shahadat Ali v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 1303 of 2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Registration of FIR: S. 154 and S. 157 CrPC
records.heading: SHO must register a case on information of a cognizable offence before investigating
records.text: S. 157 CrPC read with Rule 24.4 of the Police Rules cannot be invoked before a case is registered under s. 154. On information of a cognizable offence the SHO has no discretion to inquire into its reliability and refuse registration; he must register the case and then investigate. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 351; Arsalan Raza v. JOP Gujrat etc (Criminal Proceedings 9549/21).
records.title: Arsalan Raza v. JOP Gujrat etc (Criminal Proceedings 9549/21)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Primacy of Question of Jurisdiction
records.heading: Jurisdiction is the foremost question and the cornerstone of a fair legal process
records.text: The question of jurisdiction of a court or forum is the foremost and pivotal consideration, as it determines which court is competent, where the case is to be heard and what cases it may address. Its determination is the cornerstone of a fair legal process. Ref: 2024 SCMR 298; Muslim Commercial Bank Limited v. Muhammad Anwar and others (Civil Appeal No. 377 of 2014).
records.title: Muslim Commercial Bank Limited v. Muhammad Anwar and others (Civil Appeal No. 377 of 2014)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Retrospective Effect of Procedural Law
records.heading: Procedural law has retrospective effect unless the contrary is provided
records.text: Procedural law has retrospective effect unless the contrary is provided expressly or by implication. Ref: 2024 SCMR 298; Muslim Commercial Bank Limited v. Muhammad Anwar and others (Civil Appeal No. 377 of 2014).
records.title: Muslim Commercial Bank Limited v. Muhammad Anwar and others (Civil Appeal No. 377 of 2014)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Special Law and General Law: Precedence
records.heading: General laws apply to fill the vacuum where no special law exists
records.text: In the absence of a special law, the ordinary or general laws apply to fill the vacuum. Ref: 2024 SCMR 298; Muslim Commercial Bank Limited v. Muhammad Anwar and others (Civil Appeal No. 377 of 2014).
records.title: Muslim Commercial Bank Limited v. Muhammad Anwar and others (Civil Appeal No. 377 of 2014)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 32 Arbitration Act 1940: Suit to Enforce Award
records.heading: Award must be made a rule of court, not enforced by suit
records.text: A suit to enforce an award raises the question of its existence, effect or validity and is barred by s. 32 of the Arbitration Act, 1940. The expression 'effect of the award' is wide enough to cover a suit for enforcement. The proper course is to have the award made a rule of the Court and then execute it. Ref: 2024 SCMR 344; Haji Shinkai v. Abdul Shakoor and others (Civil Appeal No. 23-Q of 2017).
records.title: Haji Shinkai v. Abdul Shakoor and others (Civil Appeal No. 23-Q of 2017)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Moulding of Relief in Incompetent Suit
records.heading: Court cannot grant unrequested loan recovery in an incompetent suit for declaration
records.text: In a suit for declaration and injunction found incompetent, the High Court could not grant recovery of a loan amount that the plaintiff neither prayed for nor was interested in, and that was not the subject of the framed issue. The modification of the decree under ss. 42 and 55 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 was not justified. Ref: 2024 SCMR 344; Haji Shinkai v. Abdul Shakoor and others (Civil Appeal No. 23-Q of 2017).
records.title: Haji Shinkai v. Abdul Shakoor and others (Civil Appeal No. 23-Q of 2017)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Proof of Shafi Sharik Right of Pre-emption
records.heading: Pre-emptor claiming as co-owner must prove the right by documentary evidence
records.text: A pre-emptor claiming as co-owner must prove his right by documentary evidence. His name appeared only in Khana Kafiyat and not in the ownership column of the khata, and the Jamabandi did not show him as co-owner. The right was not proved, appeals were allowed and the pre-emption suit dismissed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 353; Hasham Khan (deceased) through LRs v. Waheed Ahmed (C.As. Nos. 170 and 171 of 2017).
records.title: Hasham Khan (deceased) through LRs v. Waheed Ahmed (C.As. Nos. 170 and 171 of 2017)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Presumption of Truth: Khana Kafiyat Entries
records.heading: Presumption of correctness does not attach to Khana Kafiyat entries
records.text: Presumption of correctness under s. 52 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 attaches only to the ownership and possession columns of the record of rights, not to the Lagan column or Khana Kafiyat. A party relying on Khana Kafiyat must prove the entry by independent evidence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 353; Hasham Khan (deceased) through LRs v. Waheed Ahmed (C.As. Nos. 170 and 171 of 2017).
records.title: Hasham Khan (deceased) through LRs v. Waheed Ahmed (C.As. Nos. 170 and 171 of 2017)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Proof of Talb-i-Ishhad Notice
records.heading: Talb-i-Ishhad notice must be proved through witnesses and the Advocate who issued it
records.text: The plaintiff did not prove performance of the Talbs. Witnesses of the Talb-i-Ishhad notice were not named in the plaint and the Advocate who issued the notice was not produced to prove it. The notice was sent to a village address although the vendee lived abroad. Appeals allowed and suit dismissed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 353; Hasham Khan (deceased) through LRs v. Waheed Ahmed (C.As. Nos. 170 and 171 of 2017).
records.title: Hasham Khan (deceased) through LRs v. Waheed Ahmed (C.As. Nos. 170 and 171 of 2017)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Appealability of Maintenance Decree: Per Head Amount
records.heading: Appealability of a maintenance decree is judged by the amount per plaintiff
records.text: A Full Bench held that appealability under s. 14(2)(c) of the Family Courts Act, 1964 is judged by the amount decreed per plaintiff and not the aggregate. A decree for less than Rs. 5,000 per month to each plaintiff is not appealable, even if the total exceeds that sum. Ref: 2024 LHC 438; Muhammad Aslam v. Judge Family Court, Ferozewala, etc. (Writ Petition No. 126306 of 2017, decided 13.02.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. Judge Family Court, Ferozewala, etc. (Writ Petition No. 126306 of 2017, decided 13.02.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 426(2B) CrPC: Legislative History, Discretion
records.heading: Section 426(2B) CrPC suspension is discretionary and unnecessary where the Supreme Court grants leave
records.text: Traces the history of s. 426(2B) CrPC, introduced in 1946 for convicts granted special leave to appeal to His Majesty in Council. Where leave is granted by the Supreme Court there is no need to seek suspension of sentence from the High Court. The word 'may' makes the grant of bail discretionary and the High Court may refuse it. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 252; Muhammad Iqbal and others v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 55 of 2013).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal and others v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 55 of 2013)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Site Plan Contradicting Prosecution Version
records.heading: Site plan contradicting the prosecution version leaves the case doubtful
records.text: A site plan is not substantive evidence but is important for fixing the locations of the incident and witnesses where their presence is challenged. Here the site plans did not match the claimed ownership, ploughing and crop position, so the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 306; Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witness: No Reason for Presence
records.heading: A witness giving no reason for being at the scene is a chance witness
records.text: A witness who lived in another village and gave no reason for being at the scene or visiting the deceased or complainant is a chance witness, not a natural witness. His testimony could not establish the prosecution case beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 306; Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Medical evidence contradicting the ocular account on firing distance leaves the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: The site plan showed the accused three feet from the deceased, yet none of the sixteen firearm wounds carried blackening, burning, charring or tattooing. The medical evidence contradicted the ocular account on distance and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 306; Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal of Co-accused on Same Evidence
records.heading: Acquittal of co-accused on the same evidence requires strong corroboration against others
records.text: Where the evidence was discarded against five acquitted co-accused, including the one said to have fired the shots, strong independent corroboration of the ocular account was required to sustain conviction. Previous enmity is a double edged weapon, as a motive for the accused and for false implication. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 306; Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence Not Proved: Proclamation Proceedings
records.heading: Abscondence is not established without proof of proclamation proceedings under sections 87 and 88
records.text: Abscondence was not established where no process server was produced and no report on execution of notices was on record. The prosecution failed to prove proclamation proceedings under ss. 87/88 CrPC as required by law, so the evidence of abscondence was of no avail. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 306; Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Weapon Recovery Without Matching Forensic Report
records.heading: Weapon recovery gives no corroboration without a matching forensic report
records.text: Recovery of a 12 bore repeater from the accused was inconsequential as the forensic report only confirmed its working condition and there was no matching report with the crime empties. It gave no corroboration to the ocular account. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 306; Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Azam and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeals Nos. 132397, 135890 and Murder Reference No. 9 of 2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 47 CPC: Questions Before Executing Court
records.heading: Execution, discharge and satisfaction questions between parties go to the executing court
records.text: Under s. 47 CPC all questions between the parties or their representatives relating to execution, discharge or satisfaction of the decree must be decided by the executing court and not by a separate suit. The remedy requires that the question relates to execution, discharge or satisfaction and that it arises between the parties to the suit. Ref: 2024 LHC 560; Ghulam Mustafa v. Muhammad Mushtaq, etc. (Civil Revision No. 390 of 2020).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. Muhammad Mushtaq, etc. (Civil Revision No. 390 of 2020)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Bar and Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A time barred suit must be rejected at once without issues or evidence
records.text: Limitation is not a mere technicality, since a right accrues to the other side on its expiry. A question of law may be considered even at appellate or revisional stage. Art. 113 of the Limitation Act, 1908 gives three years, and a time barred suit must be rejected at once without issues or evidence. Ref: 2024 LHC 551; Muhammad Akram v. Province of Punjab through Collector and others (Civil Revision No. 5690 of 2024, decided 26.01.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. Province of Punjab through Collector and others (Civil Revision No. 5690 of 2024, decided 26.01.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Substituted Service Only After Ordinary Service Fails
records.heading: Substituted service is illegal unless ordinary service is verified to have failed
records.text: Substituted service cannot be resorted to unless all efforts to effect service in the ordinary manner are verified to have failed. Resort to it otherwise is an illegality and a nullity in law. Ref: 2024 LHC 546; Chairman, National Highway Authority through its G.M. & another v. Abdul Hameed and another (F.A.O. No. 5549 of 2023).
records.title: Chairman, National Highway Authority through its G.M. & another v. Abdul Hameed and another (F.A.O. No. 5549 of 2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Readiness and Willingness: Deposit of Balance Price
records.heading: Deposit of balance price is not required on filing; readiness must be proved
records.text: The Specific Relief Act, 1877 does not require deposit of the balance consideration on filing. Since the relief is discretionary, the vendee must plead and prove readiness and willingness with supporting evidence, and the court may direct deposit to test his capacity and intention. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 820, 2024 CLC 268; Nasir Abbas Bhatti v. Abid Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 9463 of 2022); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Nasir Abbas Bhatti v. Abid Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 9463 of 2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Banking Court Proceedings and Readiness to Perform
records.heading: Pending Banking Court proceedings do not relieve a plaintiff of proving readiness and willingness
records.text: Pending Banking Court proceedings over the property, subject to s. 23 of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001, do not relieve a plaintiff seeking specific performance of the burden to prove readiness and willingness. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 820, 2024 CLC 268; Nasir Abbas Bhatti v. Abid Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 9463 of 2022); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Nasir Abbas Bhatti v. Abid Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 9463 of 2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Equity and Fairness in Specific Performance
records.heading: Want of equity and fairness may justify refusing specific performance even absent fraud
records.text: Even absent fraud, want of equity and fairness may justify refusing specific performance, judged on the terms and all surrounding circumstances. The plaintiff paid a small earnest sum, property values rose and he failed to deposit the balance, which showed unwillingness and risked unfair advantage. Ref: PLJ 2023 Lah 820, 2024 CLC 268; Nasir Abbas Bhatti v. Abid Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 9463 of 2022); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Nasir Abbas Bhatti v. Abid Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 9463 of 2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Time Barred Declaration: Consequential Reliefs Fail
records.heading: When the main declaration is time barred, consequential reliefs also fail
records.text: When the main relief of declaration of ownership is time barred, consequential reliefs even if within time are of no avail. A co-owner who knows of an actual denial of his right and does not sue within limitation loses the right to challenge it, and later Jamabandi entries creating third party interest give no fresh cause of action. Ref: Ghulam Mustafa v. Mst. Mah Begum and others (Civil Appeal No. 43-Q of 2018).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. Mst. Mah Begum and others (Civil Appeal No. 43-Q of 2018)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Blasphemy Allegation: S. 295-C PPC Not Made Out
records.heading: Section 295-C PPC not made out even on the complainant's allegations in full
records.text: Even on the complainant's allegations in full, the capital offence under s. 295-C PPC was not made out, and the particulars of any offence against religion must be clearly stated. The police entry into the petitioner's house without a warrant was illegal and cast doubt on any recovery from it. Ref: Zubair Saeed Sabri/Sain Zubair Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1359 of 2023, date of hearing 14.02.2024).
records.title: Zubair Saeed Sabri/Sain Zubair Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1359 of 2023, date of hearing 14.02.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 9 Family Courts Act: Late Filing of Documents
records.heading: Family Court has discretion to permit late filing of documents under section 9
records.text: Although ss. 9(2) and 9(4) of the Family Courts Act, 1964 use 'shall', they are not mandatory as no penal consequence is prescribed. The Family Court has discretion to permit a defendant to file and produce a document not filed with the written statement. Ref: 2024 CLC 375; Muhammad Nawaz v. ADJ Hafizabad etc (WP 65227/23).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. ADJ Hafizabad etc (WP 65227/23)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Exclusion of Time Spent Before Wrong Forum
records.heading: Time before a wrong forum is excluded only under section 5 on sufficient cause
records.text: Where a plaint or appeal is returned under O. VII R. 10 CPC it is treated as a fresh institution. A request to exclude time spent before a court lacking jurisdiction falls under s. 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908, requiring sufficient cause, and the principles of s. 14 may inform that assessment. The application for excluding about one year was dismissed. Ref: 2024 CLC 357; Ayaz Mehmood v. Musadaq Riaz and 2 others (R.F.A. No. 51 of 2023).
records.title: Ayaz Mehmood v. Musadaq Riaz and 2 others (R.F.A. No. 51 of 2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Burden on Applicant: Due Diligence and Good Faith
records.heading: Applicant seeking exclusion of time must plead and show due diligence and good faith
records.text: A litigant seeking exclusion of time spent before a forum without jurisdiction must plead the facts and reasonably show due diligence and good faith. The initial burden to establish these elements lies on the applicant. Ref: 2024 CLC 357; Ayaz Mehmood v. Musadaq Riaz and 2 others (R.F.A. No. 51 of 2023).
records.title: Ayaz Mehmood v. Musadaq Riaz and 2 others (R.F.A. No. 51 of 2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Wrong Advice of Counsel and Wrong Forum
records.heading: Wrong advice of counsel cannot justify enlarging time spent before the wrong forum
records.text: Wrong advice of counsel cannot be the foundation for enlarging time consumed in pursuing a remedy before the wrong forum. Ref: 2024 CLC 357; Ayaz Mehmood v. Musadaq Riaz and 2 others (R.F.A. No. 51 of 2023).
records.title: Ayaz Mehmood v. Musadaq Riaz and 2 others (R.F.A. No. 51 of 2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Is Not a Mere Technicality
records.heading: Sections 5 and 14 do not reward carelessness or excuse lack of vigilance
records.text: Availing a remedy within the period provided by law is not a mere technicality. Ss. 5 and 14 of the Limitation Act, 1908 do not reward carelessness or validate lack of vigilance, so the plea that cases be decided on merits was misconceived. Ref: 2024 CLC 357; Ayaz Mehmood v. Musadaq Riaz and 2 others (R.F.A. No. 51 of 2023).
records.title: Ayaz Mehmood v. Musadaq Riaz and 2 others (R.F.A. No. 51 of 2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 17 Specific Relief Act: Partial Performance
records.heading: Partial specific performance is barred unless within sections 14 to 16
records.text: S. 17 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 bars decree of part performance unless the case falls squarely within ss. 14 to 16. Splitting a contract is not permitted, and under s. 16 the part must stand on a separate and independent footing. Specific performance is discretionary and the suit was dismissed. Ref: 2024 CLC 301; Mian Abdul Ghaffar v. Mst. Kishwar Iqbal and 5 others (Civil Revision No. 369 of 2021).
records.title: Mian Abdul Ghaffar v. Mst. Kishwar Iqbal and 5 others (Civil Revision No. 369 of 2021)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Petition to Annul General Elections 2024 Dismissed
records.heading: Petition to annul General Elections 2024 dismissed with a fine of Rs. 500,000
records.text: A three member bench dismissed a petition seeking investigation of alleged rigging and fresh general elections 2024. The petitioner did not appear and had emailed a request to withdraw. The Court imposed a fine of Rs. 500,000 on the petitioner. Ref: Ali Khan v. Government of Pakistan through A.G. Islamabad and another (C.U.O. 18/2024, decided 21.02.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Ali Khan v. Government of Pakistan through A.G. Islamabad and another (C.U.O. 18/2024, decided 21.02.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Judicial Council Proceedings After Resignation
records.heading: Supreme Judicial Council proceedings do not abate on the Judge's resignation or retirement
records.text: Appeals partially allowed by a 4 to 1 majority: once proceedings have begun before the Supreme Judicial Council against a Judge, they do not abate on his resignation or retirement. It is for the Council to proceed accordingly. Delay in filing was condoned and reasons were to follow. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary, Ministry of Law & Justice Islamabad v. The Honourable Supreme Judicial Council through its Secretary, Supreme Court Building, Islamabad and others (I.C.A. 1/2024, decided 21.02.2024).
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary, Ministry of Law & Justice Islamabad v. The Honourable Supreme Judicial Council through its Secretary, Supreme Court Building, Islamabad and others (I.C.A. 1/2024, decided 21.02.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Blasphemy Allegation: S. 295-C PPC Not Made Out
records.heading: Section 295-C PPC not made out even on the complainant's allegations in full
records.text: Even on the complainant's allegations in full, the capital offence under s. 295-C PPC was not made out, and the particulars of any offence against religion must be clearly stated. The police entry into the petitioner's house without a warrant was illegal and cast doubt on any recovery from it. Ref: Zubair Saeed Sabri/Sain Zubair Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1359 of 2023, date of hearing 14.02.2024).
records.title: Zubair Saeed Sabri/Sain Zubair Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1359 of 2023, date of hearing 14.02.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Enforceability of Agreement Increasing Dower
records.heading: An agreement increasing dower is enforceable and is no restraint on marriage
records.text: An agreement proved by the beneficiary wife and marginal witnesses, increasing dower payable on divorce or second marriage, is enforceable, as a husband may increase dower after marriage and such a term is not a restraint on marriage under s. 26 of the Contract Act, 1872, relying on cited authorities. The award of Rs.4,000,000 as dower was upheld and both petitions dismissed. Ref: 2024 LHC 572; Syed Sibt Hassan v. Saba Batool etc. (W.P. 38567/2022, with W.P. 75369/2021); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Syed Sibt Hassan v. Saba Batool etc. (W.P. 38567/2022, with W.P. 75369/2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Granted to Ahmadi Accused
records.heading: Supreme Court bail order for an Ahmadi accused; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on a bail order of the Supreme Court in favour of an Ahmadi accused, the subject of wide discussion on social media. The Court also issued the judgment in Urdu. The post gives no holding or provisions. Ref: Mubarak Ahmad Sani v. The State, etc (Crl. P.L.A. 1054-L/2023, decided 06.02.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Mubarak Ahmad Sani v. The State, etc (Crl. P.L.A. 1054-L/2023, decided 06.02.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A(6) CrPC: Ex-Officio Justice of Peace Powers
records.heading: Ex-Officio Justice of Peace must not act mechanically or brush aside the police report
records.text: The functions of the Ex-Officio Justice of Peace under s. 22-A CrPC are quasi-judicial and not unbridled. He must not act mechanically and cannot brush aside the police report without lawful reasoning, relying on PLD 2016 SC 581. Petition allowed and the impugned order set aside. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 73; Chaudhary Abdul Majeed v. Learned Ex-Officio Justice of Peace Rawalpindi and 6 others (W.P. No. 3343 of 2023, heard 15.11.2023); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Chaudhary Abdul Majeed v. Learned Ex-Officio Justice of Peace Rawalpindi and 6 others (W.P. No. 3343 of 2023, heard 15.11.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: S. 9(A)(1) CNSA: No Retrospective Bar on Remissions
records.heading: Section 9(A)(1) CNSA is prospective and does not bar remissions of earlier convicts
records.text: S. 9(A)(1) CNSA 1997, inserted by the Amendment Act 2022, is prospective. It cannot bar remissions for a convict arrested, indicted or convicted before its insertion. The convict was entitled to earn remissions and the Superintendent Jail was directed to grant them. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 63, 2024 PCrLJ 1487; Imran Mustafa v. Government of Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 16629 of 2023, decided 21.11.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar; Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Imran Mustafa v. Government of Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 16629 of 2023, decided 21.11.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution Against Surety: S. 128 Contract Act
records.heading: A decree surety is liable in execution to the extent of his bond
records.text: A person who stands surety for satisfaction of a decree may be proceeded against in execution to the extent of his personal liability under his surety bond (s. 128 Contract Act, s. 145 CPC). The High Court in writ jurisdiction does not disturb concurrent findings of fact without compelling reasons. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 82; Ghulam Shabbir v. Mst. Tanzeela Nusrat etc. (W.P. No. 2669 of 2023, heard 12.9.2023); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Ghulam Shabbir v. Mst. Tanzeela Nusrat etc. (W.P. No. 2669 of 2023, heard 12.9.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Temporary Injunction: Plaintiff as Dominus Litis
records.heading: A plaintiff cannot be compelled to implead persons against whom he seeks no relief
records.text: A plaintiff is dominus litis and cannot be forced to sue a person against whom he seeks no relief. Dismissal of an O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC application because the siblings were not impleaded was wrong, as the petitioner claimed no right against them. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 92; Asmat Bibi v. Additional District Judge, etc. (W.P. No. 50316 of 2023, decided 15.11.2023); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Asmat Bibi v. Additional District Judge, etc. (W.P. No. 50316 of 2023, decided 15.11.2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: 9 May Cases: Challenge to Detention Dismissed
records.heading: Writ petitions challenging 9 May detentions dismissed where cases were registered
records.text: A Division Bench dismissed writ petitions seeking to declare the detention of Khadija Shah and others in the 9 May events illegal. Cases had been registered and the law was taking its course. Legal procedure cannot be bypassed and remedies remain available. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 109; Justice Ali Baqar Najafi; Justice Amjad Rafiq.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Suits Challenging Nikahnama Entries Are Family Suits
records.heading: Suits challenging Nikahnama entries are family suits triable by the Family Court
records.text: Any suit challenging an entry in the Nikahnama, pending or filed after the 2015 amendment to the Family Courts Act, 1964, is deemed a family suit to be tried by the Family Court, or deemed transferred to it. Leave to appeal was refused and the petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC 69; Muhammad Yousaf v. Additional District Judge, Multan and others (C.P. No. 6482 of 2021, decided 8.2.2023); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Additional District Judge, Multan and others (C.P. No. 6482 of 2021, decided 8.2.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Failure to Pay Balance on Due Date
records.heading: Vendee unable to pay balance on due date is not entitled to discretionary specific performance
records.text: The plaintiff admitted he could not arrange the balance consideration on the date of performance or for three months after, and the suit was decreed about 13 years after the agreement. He was not entitled to discretionary relief under s. 12 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Appeal allowed and suit dismissed; earnest money confiscated. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC 105; Muhammad Aslam and others v. Muhammad Anwar (C.A. No. 781 of 2017, decided 4.5.2023); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam and others v. Muhammad Anwar (C.A. No. 781 of 2017, decided 4.5.2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Tamleek Proved by Revenue Record and Witnesses
records.heading: Tamleek proved by revenue record and witnesses defeats a co-owner's declaration suit
records.text: In a suit for declaration and injunction by a co-owner of undivided agricultural land (ss. 42 and 54 Specific Relief Act, 1877), the respondents proved tamleek through revenue record and witnesses. Counsel could not show error, perversity or jurisdictional defect warranting interference. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC 75; Mst. Faheeman Begum (deceased) through L.Rs and others v. Islam-ud-Din (deceased) through L.Rs and others (C.A. No. 1300 of 2019, decided 3.5.2023); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mst. Faheeman Begum (deceased) through L.Rs and others v. Islam-ud-Din (deceased) through L.Rs and others (C.A. No. 1300 of 2019, decided 3.5.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Injuries on Non-Vital Parts
records.heading: Whether section 324 PPC applies to non-vital injuries is for the trial court
records.text: Where injuries were on non-vital parts and the petitioners did not repeat fire despite opportunity, applicability of s. 324 PPC was for the trial court after evidence. Ad interim pre-arrest bail of one petitioner was confirmed and the other was admitted to bail (ss. 498 and 498-A CrPC). Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 50; Jamaluddin and another v. State (Crl. P. Nos. 41-K & 42-K of 2023, decided 29.5.2023); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Jamaluddin and another v. State (Crl. P. Nos. 41-K & 42-K of 2023, decided 29.5.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Prompt FIR, Related Witnesses, Sentence
records.heading: Prompt FIR and consistent related eyewitnesses supported by medical evidence sustain conviction
records.text: The prompt FIR excluded consultation, and two related eyewitnesses were consistent and had no motive to implicate the petitioner. The ocular account was supported by medical evidence, and the High Court rightly disbelieved the motive and mitigated the sentence on recognised grounds. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 54; Maskeen Ullah and another v. State and another (J.P. No. 816 of 2017 & Crl. P. No. 775-L of 2016, decided 14.6.2023); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Maskeen Ullah and another v. State and another (J.P. No. 816 of 2017 & Crl. P. No. 775-L of 2016, decided 14.6.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail on Statutory Ground: Delay in Trial
records.heading: Delay in trial not caused by the accused entitles him to statutory bail
records.text: The petitioner had been in custody over two years and the charge was framed only recently, with no fault of his in the delay before that. He became entitled to bail on the statutory ground under s. 497 CrPC. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 60; Muhammad Umer Shahzad v. State and others (Crl. P. No. 1618-L of 2022, decided 6.6.2023); Justice Sardar Tariq Masood; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Umer Shahzad v. State and others (Crl. P. No. 1618-L of 2022, decided 6.6.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved as Mitigating Factor
records.heading: Absence of premeditation and unproved motive may mitigate sentence in capital cases
records.text: Where there is no premeditation and motive is not proved, that may be a mitigating factor reducing the sentence in capital cases. Under s. 302(b) PPC, with consistent ocular account and corroborating medical evidence, life imprisonment stood and leave to appeal was refused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 128, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 79; Muhammad Yasin and another v. State, etc. (Crl. P. No. 476-L of 2018 and J.P. No. 337 of 2018, decided 1.11.2023); Justice Ijaz ul Ahsan; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Yasin and another v. State, etc. (Crl. P. No. 476-L of 2018 and J.P. No. 337 of 2018, decided 1.11.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Second Bail Petition: Fresh Ground Required
records.heading: A second bail petition is maintainable only on a fresh ground
records.text: A second bail petition is maintainable only on a fresh ground, meaning one not available or in existence when the earlier application was decided. It is barred even if the earlier petition was withdrawn, or a ground then available was abandoned. The petitioner's pre-arrest bail petition under s. 498 CrPC was considered for fresh grounds. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 163, 2024 YLR 2847; Sarfraz Ali v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 82227-B of 2022, decided 10.2.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Sarfraz Ali v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 82227-B of 2022, decided 10.2.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail Refused: Classified Cipher Case
records.heading: Post-arrest bail refused in an Official Secrets Act case over a classified cipher
records.text: Post-arrest bail under s. 497 CrPC was refused in a case under the Official Secrets Act, 1923 (ss. 5 and 9). The allegation was that the petitioner shared a twisted version of the contents of a classified cipher with unauthorised persons. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 230; Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 1354-B & W.P. No. 2448 of 2023, decided 27.10.2023); Justice Aamer Farooq.
records.title: Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 1354-B & W.P. No. 2448 of 2023, decided 27.10.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eyewitnesses Doubtful: Corroboration
records.heading: Unexplained presence of eyewitnesses at early hours makes the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: No evidence explained why the witnesses went to the scene at early hours, making their presence doubtful. Relationship alone does not discredit a witness, but as a matter of prudence and not of law the Court should seek corroboration. The prosecution case under s. 302(b) PPC was doubtful. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 252, 2025 YLR 116; Khalil Ahmad and 2 others v. State (Crl. A. No. 78847-J, M.R. No. 375 of 2019, heard 14.9.2023); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch.; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Khalil Ahmad and 2 others v. State (Crl. A. No. 78847-J, M.R. No. 375 of 2019, heard 14.9.2023)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Engaging Blocked Advocate to Transfer Bail Case
records.heading: Engaging a blocked advocate to procure transfer of a bail case is mala fide
records.text: Engaging an advocate whom the bench had blocked, to procure transfer of a bail case, was a calculated move coloured with mala fide. The advocate's acceptance was unprofessional, and the office was directed not to accept his power of attorney before this bench where he supersedes earlier counsel. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 269; Muhammad Talha v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 27751-B of 2023, decided 7.6.2023); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Muhammad Talha v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 27751-B of 2023, decided 7.6.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Delayed Postmortem, Conflicting Witnesses
records.heading: Delayed postmortem and conflicting witnesses entitle the accused to the benefit of doubt
records.text: Witnesses conflicted on whom the first fire hit, and the postmortem was delayed 11 hours 45 minutes without explanation, casting doubt on the FIR. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC could not be sustained. Appeal accepted and the murder reference answered in the negative. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 273; Bilal Hassan and another v. State (Crl. A. No. 19109 & M.R. No. 81 of 2019, heard 23.1.2023); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Bilal Hassan and another v. State (Crl. A. No. 19109 & M.R. No. 81 of 2019, heard 23.1.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Witness Conduct: Art. 129 QSO
records.heading: Unnatural conduct of witnesses and medical contradictions show the charge was not proved
records.text: Conduct of witnesses contrary to natural human conduct, assessed under Art. 129 QSO, together with contradictions between ocular and medical evidence, showed the prosecution failed to prove the charge. Motive is only corroborative, and a tainted piece of evidence cannot corroborate another. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 201; Khuda Bakhsh and another v. State and others (Crl. A. No. 244, Crl. Rev. No. 166 & M.R. 8 of 2021, heard 24.1.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Khuda Bakhsh and another v. State and others (Crl. A. No. 244, Crl. Rev. No. 166 & M.R. 8 of 2021, heard 24.1.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Postmortem and Reporting: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: One circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right
records.text: A contrived written application and delay in postmortem and in reporting to the police suggested the witnesses were absent at the occurrence. A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right, not as a concession. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 171; Mahnaz Ali v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 68 & M.R. No. 6 of 2022, heard 18.1.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mahnaz Ali v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 68 & M.R. No. 6 of 2022, heard 18.1.2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution of Maintenance Decree: Cancellation of Mutation
records.heading: Executing court may cancel a mutation by which a judgment debtor alienated property
records.text: In execution of a maintenance decree, the executing court cancelled a mutation by which the judgment debtor had alienated property, so the property reverted to the original owner. The decree ceases against him on death but his property remains liable for the decretal amount. Petition dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah Note 19; Tahir Mahmood v. Additional District Judge, Burewala, etc. (W.P. No. 11802 of 2023, decided 26.10.2023); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Tahir Mahmood v. Additional District Judge, Burewala, etc. (W.P. No. 11802 of 2023, decided 26.10.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Charas Sentencing Zone
records.heading: Bail for 1000 to 4999 grams of charas considers the lesser sentence zone
records.text: Under the amended law the sentencing zone for 1000 to 4999 grams of charas is nine to fourteen years. For bail the lesser sentence is considered, so the quantity did not attract the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. With no criminal history the case was one of further inquiry. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 52; Ashir Nisar v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8185-B of 2022, decided 8.12.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ashir Nisar v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8185-B of 2022, decided 8.12.2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Bald Allegation of Theft
records.heading: A bald allegation of theft without linking evidence justifies pre-arrest bail
records.text: No direct or indirect evidence linked the petitioners to the alleged theft of bricks, and the complainant did not disclose how he knew they were the culprits. A bald allegation under s. 379 PPC is insufficient. Ad interim pre-arrest bail confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 49; Muhammad Ayub and another v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7043-B of 2023, decided 8.11.2023); Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Ayub and another v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7043-B of 2023, decided 8.11.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: S. 489-F PPC, No Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC carries no prohibitory clause, so post-arrest bail may be allowed
records.text: S. 489-F PPC carries a maximum of three years, so no prohibitory clause applies, and bail is a procedural relief unconnected with the final decision.
