The FIR was delayed and the case rested on documentary evidence in the prosecution's possession. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 46; Muhammad Arshad v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8049-B of 2023, decided 14.11.2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Arshad v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8049-B of 2023, decided 14.11.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Strong Grounds Required
records.heading: Bail once granted is recalled only on strong and exceptional grounds
records.text: Nomination in the FIR or a prohibitory clause offence does not bar pre-arrest bail by itself. Considerations for grant and cancellation differ, and bail once granted is recalled only on strong and exceptional grounds such as misuse, tampering with witnesses, repetition, absconding or an arbitrary order. Petition dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 44; Masaub Haider v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 6284-CB of 2022, decided 22.9.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Masaub Haider v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 6284-CB of 2022, decided 22.9.2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas Conviction: Sentence Reduced
records.heading: Sentence for charas reduced for a first offender with satisfactory jail conduct
records.text: The appellant was a first offender with satisfactory jail conduct, and charas is less harmful than narcotics such as heroin. A lenient view was taken on quantum of sentence under s. 9 CNSA. The sentence was reduced, conviction maintained and the appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 42; Sher Zaman v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 208731 of 2018, decided 18.5.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Sher Zaman v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 208731 of 2018, decided 18.5.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: 1440 Grams Charas
records.heading: Continued detention for 1440 grams of charas without trial in sight justified bail
records.text: For possession of 1440 grams of charas, within the 1000 to 4999 gram zone, continued detention for an indefinite period was unfair where conclusion of trial was not in sight. Post-arrest bail under s. 497 CrPC allowed, relying on PLJ 2018 SC 812. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 40; Zohaib alias Majid Ali v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 3741-B of 2023, decided 12.9.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Zohaib alias Majid Ali v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 3741-B of 2023, decided 12.9.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Attempt to Murder: Modification of Sentence and Fine
records.heading: Sentence under section 324 PPC modified and fine reduced on regret and prosecution non-objection
records.text: The petitioner expressed regret and said he was sole breadwinner, and the prosecution did not object to a reduced sentence. The sentence under s. 324 PPC was modified and the fine reduced from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 30,000, with 15 days simple imprisonment in default. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 36; Nasrullah alias Pehlwan v. State and another (Crl. Rev. No. 112960 of 2017, decided 18.5.2023); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Nasrullah alias Pehlwan v. State and another (Crl. Rev. No. 112960 of 2017, decided 18.5.2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: 1000 Grams Charas After 2022 Amendment
records.heading: Lesser sentence is considered for bail in 1000 to 4999 gram charas cases
records.text: The 2022 amendment prescribes a minimum of nine years for 1000 to 4999 grams of charas. For bail the lesser sentence is kept in mind in offences with alternate sentences, and police act as complainant and investigator under the Act. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 35; Muhammad Mansha v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7078-B of 2023, decided 11.10.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Mansha v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7078-B of 2023, decided 11.10.2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Blasphemy Appeal: Suspicion Cannot Replace Proof
records.heading: Suspicion, however grave, cannot replace proof beyond reasonable doubt in a blasphemy case
records.text: The judgment surveys Quranic injunctions on respect for the Holy Prophet and the liability of contemners. It affirms that suspicion, however grave, cannot substitute the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt in a criminal case. The post does not state the outcome. Ref: 2024 LHC 587; Muhammad Kashif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 285-20, decided 06.02.2024); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Kashif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 285-20, decided 06.02.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Compromise in Ta'zir: Who Are Legal Heirs
records.heading: Brother and sister are not legal heirs for compromise where wife, son and daughters survive
records.text: Where the deceased leaves a wife, son and daughters, his brother and sister are not legal heirs for the purpose of compromise in a case where the punishment was awarded as Ta'zir. Ref: 2024 LHC 579; Zafar v. The State (Jail Appeal 79782/22, decided 20.02.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zafar v. The State (Jail Appeal 79782/22, decided 20.02.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 84 QSO: Late Application for Thumb Impression Comparison
records.heading: No time limit applies to an application under Article 84 QSO for expert comparison
records.text: No time limit is prescribed under Art. 84 QSO for an application to compare signatures or thumb impressions through an expert. Moving it after evidence is recorded is not a cogent reason to dismiss it, as a litigant may seek assistance of the Court to discharge his burden of proof. Ref: Sabir Hussain v. Additional District Judge etc. (W.P. No. 993/2022, date of hearing 30.01.2024).
records.title: Sabir Hussain v. Additional District Judge etc. (W.P. No. 993/2022, date of hearing 30.01.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Attesting Witnesses: Arts. 17, 79 and 81 QSO
records.heading: Admitted execution by the executant exempts proof through two attesting witnesses under Article 81
records.text: Proof of a document under Art. 17 QSO needs two attesting witnesses under Art. 79, but where execution is admitted by the executant, Art. 81 exempts this requirement. Admission in a prior suit made non-production of both marginal witnesses non-fatal. Ref: Muhammad Islam v. Bagh Ali (deceased) through LRs (RSA No. 230/2016, date of hearing 23.01.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Islam v. Bagh Ali (deceased) through LRs (RSA No. 230/2016, date of hearing 23.01.2024)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mubarik Ahmad Sani Review: Notices to Religious Institutions
records.heading: Supreme Court issued notices to the Attorney General and religious institutions in the review petition
records.text: In the review petition the Supreme Court issued notices to the Attorney General and ten religious institutions, including the Council of Islamic Ideology, seeking assistance. Further applications to be joined were to be fixed with the case. Written opinions were invited within three weeks. Ref: The State through Prosecutor General Punjab v. Mubarik Ahmad Sani and another (Crl. R.P. 2/2024, decided 26.02.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: The State through Prosecutor General Punjab v. Mubarik Ahmad Sani and another (Crl. R.P. 2/2024, decided 26.02.2024)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape and PECA Charges: Trial by Special Court
records.heading: Rape cases joined with PECA charges are tried by the court trying rape cases
records.text: Where rape charges are joined with ss. 21 or 22 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016, the case is tried by the court trying rape cases under s. 2(f), (g), (h) of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021. The FIA court has no jurisdiction.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape and PECA Charges: Trial by Special Court
records.heading: Rape cases joined with PECA charges are tried by the court trying rape cases
records.text: Where rape charges are joined with ss. 21 or 22 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016, the case is tried by the court trying rape cases under s. 2(f), (g), (h) of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021. The FIA court has no jurisdiction.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Framing of Issues and Particulars of Fraud
records.heading: Court need not frame issues on every section 12(2) application; fraud must be particularised
records.text: On an application under s. 12(2) CPC the Court is not bound to frame issues in every case and may decide after considering the nature of the allegations whether issues and evidence are needed. Full particulars of fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction must be pleaded, not vague allegations. Ref: Hafiz Malik Kamran Akbar, etc v. Muhammad Shaif (deceased) through LRs, etc (C.P.L.A. 2341-L/2016, decided 02.01.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Hafiz Malik Kamran Akbar, etc v. Muhammad Shaif (deceased) through LRs, etc (C.P.L.A. 2341-L/2016, decided 02.01.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance Vests on Death: Invalid Revenue Entry
records.heading: Muslim heirs inherit by operation of law and a contrary revenue entry is worthless
records.text: On the death of a Muslim, all legal heirs automatically become owners of his estate by operation of law. An unauthorised revenue entry contrary to the law of inheritance has no legal worth. Civil revision allowed. Ref: 2024 LHC 726; Mehwish Mughal & 1 Other v. Amira Bukhari etc (Civil Revision 16524/23, decided 14.02.2024); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Mehwish Mughal & 1 Other v. Amira Bukhari etc (Civil Revision 16524/23, decided 14.02.2024)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Lumberdari Grant of State Charagah Land
records.heading: Charagah land cannot be allotted under a Lumberdari grant
records.text: State Charagah land cannot be converted into state land and sold to the occupant, nor allotted under a Lumberdari grant, as Charagah lands are excluded from grants of proprietary rights. A successor of a Lambardar who obtained land earlier cannot claim a second Lumberdari grant in his personal capacity. Ref: 2024 LHC 737; Bakhsh v. Member Judicial BOR Punjab etc (WP 56073/20, decided 20.02.2024); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Bakhsh v. Member Judicial BOR Punjab etc (WP 56073/20, decided 20.02.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower Agreed at Nikah: Binding and Payable
records.heading: Dower agreed at nikah is binding and wholly payable on demand after consummation
records.text: An agreement for dower made at solemnisation of marriage is binding. If the marriage was consummated, the wife is entitled to immediate payment of the whole unpaid dower, prompt and deferred, relying on para 336(2) of Mulla's Principles of Muhammadan Law. An amount payable on a future event counts as deferred dower. Ref: 2024 LHC 676; Muhammad Ghause v. Additional District Judge, Bahawalpur & 02 others (W.P. No. 7630 of 2018, date of hearing 06.02.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Ghause v. Additional District Judge, Bahawalpur & 02 others (W.P. No. 7630 of 2018, date of hearing 06.02.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 118: Presumptions on Negotiable Instruments Rebuttable
records.heading: Section 118 presumptions on negotiable instruments are rebuttable by a probable defence
records.text: In a recovery suit on a negotiable instrument, the statutory presumptions under s. 118 on consideration, date and time are rebuttable. The defendant may rebut them by a probable defence, shown from the plaintiff's evidence or circumstances, that consideration is improbable or doubtful, judged by natural human conduct. Ref: 2024 LHC 651; Shaukat Ali v. Abdul Ghaffar (RFA No. 245/2017, date of hearing 24.01.2024).
records.title: Shaukat Ali v. Abdul Ghaffar (RFA No. 245/2017, date of hearing 24.01.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIV CPC: Framing of Issues
records.heading: A case may be decided on a preliminary issue of law under Order XIV
records.text: Issues may be of fact, of law or mixed. Under O. XIV R. 2 CPC a case may be disposed of on a preliminary issue of law concerning jurisdiction or a statutory bar. The object of framing issues is to identify the real dispute, and an appellate court may frame an issue and refer it for trial without remanding the whole case. Ref: 2024 LHC 660; Abdul Rahman and others v. Muhammad Farooq and others (R.F.A. No. 14953 of 2022, date of hearing 20.02.2024).
records.title: Abdul Rahman and others v. Muhammad Farooq and others (R.F.A. No. 14953 of 2022, date of hearing 20.02.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Writ Enforces Rights, Subject to Law
records.heading: A writ enforces fundamental rights but cannot create entitlements contrary to law
records.text: A writ is for enforcement of fundamental rights, not for creating entitlement, and equitable relief can be granted only subject to the relevant law. The right under Art. 4 to be treated in accordance with law is subject to the duty under Art. 5 to obey the law, here the SOP issued under the Food Department policy. Ref: 2004 MLD 203; Al-Khalid Flour Mills v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 3042 of 2022).
records.title: Al-Khalid Flour Mills v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 3042 of 2022)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption: Re-Sale to Ex-Owner and Talbs
records.heading: Pre-emption suit fails where land was resold to the original owner before institution
records.text: A pre-emption suit is not maintainable where the pre-empted land was sold back to the original owner before institution of the suit. Non-performance of the Talbs under s. 13 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1991 is fatal. The High Court has supervisory jurisdiction under s. 115 CPC. Ref: 2024 MLD 396; Zahid Khan etc. v. Muhammad Ahsan etc. (Civil Revision 550-16).
records.title: Zahid Khan etc. v. Muhammad Ahsan etc. (Civil Revision 550-16)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Breach of Trust: Ss. 405 and 406 PPC
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation under section 405 PPC
records.text: Criminal breach of trust under s. 405 PPC requires that the accused was entrusted with property or dominion over it, and dishonestly misappropriated or converted it or disposed of it in violation of a trust. Punishment for ordinary cases is under s. 406, with aggravated forms in ss. 407 to 409. Ref: 2024 MLD 309, PLJ 2022 CrC 1314; Muhammad Saleem etc v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 69238/B/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Saleem etc v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 69238/B/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Executing Court Going Behind Decree: Nullity
records.heading: Executing court may go behind a decree that is a nullity in law
records.text: If a decree is inexecutable because of a nullity in law, the executing court can go beyond it. Part of the pre-emptible property was mortgaged and redeemed before the pre-emption decree, so the vendees of the pre-emptors had no valid title and the objection petition was rightly accepted. Ref: 2024 YLR 482; Bakhsha v. Sh. Qadir Bakhsh (Civil Revision 138-D-06).
records.title: Bakhsha v. Sh. Qadir Bakhsh (Civil Revision 138-D-06)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Appeal: Chance Witnesses, Delayed Postmortem
records.heading: Chance witnesses and delayed postmortem leave the murder case unproved
records.text: The complaint was unreliable as the investigating officer admitted taking the complainant's thumb impression on blank paper. Witnesses were chance witnesses with no proven visibility at night, the site plans gave no light source, and delayed postmortem pointed to a belated FIR. SIM recovery was inconsequential. Ref: 2024 YLR 509; Maqsood Ahmad etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal 991-12).
records.title: Maqsood Ahmad etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal 991-12)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Vakalatnama: No Implied Power to Compromise
records.heading: A vakalatnama does not impliedly authorise counsel to compromise or consent to a decree
records.text: A power of attorney is construed strictly and confers only powers expressly given or arising by necessary implication. A vakalatnama does not impliedly authorise counsel to compromise, withdraw the suit or consent to a decree, so such an act has no legal consequence at the option of the party concerned. Ref: 2024 LHC 755; Falak Sher v. Hashmat Bibi (Writ Petition 3631-15, decided 21.02.2024); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Falak Sher v. Hashmat Bibi (Writ Petition 3631-15, decided 21.02.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Arrest After Addition of Offences Requires Cancellation
records.heading: An accused on bail cannot be arrested on added offences without cancelling bail first
records.text: An accused already granted pre-arrest or post-arrest bail by a competent court cannot be arrested merely because further offences are added to the case. The earlier bail must first be cancelled under s. 497(5) CrPC. Ref: 2024 LHC 771; Mujtaba Saleem Butt v. Incharge Investigation AVLS etc (Crl. Misc. 10162/24, decided 20.02.2024); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mujtaba Saleem Butt v. Incharge Investigation AVLS etc (Crl. Misc. 10162/24, decided 20.02.2024)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt for Defying Orders Against MPO Detentions
records.heading: Officials faced contempt proceedings for defying orders declaring MPO detentions illegal
records.text: The District Magistrate, SSP, DPO and SHO faced contempt proceedings for disregarding High Court orders that declared MPO detention orders illegal and for obstructing access to justice. Per the file title, the DC was sentenced to six months and the SSP and SHO to four months each. Ref: The State v. Irfan Nawaz Memon, District Magistrate and three others (Criminal Original No. 197-W/2023); Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: The State v. Irfan Nawaz Memon, District Magistrate and three others (Criminal Original No. 197-W/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Alternate Remedy Not a Bar
records.heading: Alternate remedy is no bar to a writ where it is cumbersome or delayed
records.text: Where the procedure for relief through other proceedings is too cumbersome, or relief cannot be had without delay and expense, or delay would make relief meaningless, the High Court will issue a writ under Art. 199 to a party found entitled to it, even though another course was open. Ref: 2024 CLC 385; Imran Abbas Bhatti v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 31899 of 2023).
records.title: Imran Abbas Bhatti v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 31899 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Preventive Detention: Requirement of Sound Material
records.heading: Preventive detention for prejudice to public peace requires sound supporting material
records.text: An order of preventive detention for prejudice to public peace must rest on sound material showing the detenu was engaged in activity prejudicial to public safety or order, such as electronic records, call records or speeches. No such material was produced, so the detention orders violated s. 3 of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, were set aside and release was directed. Ref: 2024 CLC 385; Imran Abbas Bhatti v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 31899 of 2023).
records.title: Imran Abbas Bhatti v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 31899 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partition Suit: Failed Internal Auction and Willingness
records.heading: A co-owner showing no willingness for internal auction causes it to be declared failed
records.text: In a suit for partition under the Punjab Partition of Immovable Property Act, 2012, a co-owner who sought adjournments for about nine months and did not appear showed no willingness for the internal auction. The Civil Court rightly declared the internal auction failed and moved to external auction. Constitutional petition dismissed in limine. Ref: 2024 CLC 251; Awais Gohar v. Sumaira Adnan and others (Petition No. 65237 of 2023).
records.title: Awais Gohar v. Sumaira Adnan and others (Petition No. 65237 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partition Act 2012: Six Month Time Limit
records.heading: Section 14 fixes six months for partition suits and delay defeats the Act's purpose
records.text: Section 14 of the Punjab Partition of Immovable Property Act, 2012 fixes six months from institution to complete partition suits. The petitioner defeated the Act's purpose of expeditious partition by delaying the internal auction, while the respondent lady kept appearing. No illegality was found in the orders below and the petition was dismissed. Ref: 2024 CLC 251; Awais Gohar v. Sumaira Adnan and others (Petition No. 65237 of 2023).
records.title: Awais Gohar v. Sumaira Adnan and others (Petition No. 65237 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eye-Witnesses at Scene Not Proved
records.heading: Eye-witnesses not named in the inquest report were doubtfully present at the scene
records.text: The inquest report did not name or bear the signatures of the complainant or eye-witness, and the complainant arranged two witnesses before reporting, one from 70 to 80 kilometres away. This suggested the witnesses were not present at the scene and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 709, 2024 MLD 359; Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Post-Mortem
records.heading: Unexplained delay in post-mortem contributes to the failure of the prosecution case
records.text: An unexplained delay of about ten hours and forty-five minutes between registration of the FIR and the post-mortem contributed to the finding that the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 709, 2024 MLD 359; Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested and Inimical Related Witnesses
records.heading: Closely related and inimical witnesses had reasons to implicate the accused falsely
records.text: The prosecution witnesses were closely related to the deceased and inimical towards the accused, given earlier criminal cases lodged by the complainant against the accused's family. They had reasons to implicate the accused falsely, and the prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 709, 2024 MLD 359; Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Pistol and Empties Inconsequential
records.heading: Broken chain of custody makes recovery of pistol and empties inconsequential
records.text: Inconsistencies in the chain of custody of the crime empties and the recovered 9MM pistol sent for forensic examination meant that safe custody was not established, so the recoveries were inconsequential and the benefit went to the accused. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 709, 2024 MLD 359; Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Bullet Recovered at Post-Mortem Not Sent for Forensics
records.heading: Failure to send a recovered bullet for forensic comparison draws an adverse inference
records.text: A bullet recovered from the deceased's lung and handed to the police was neither sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory for comparison nor exhibited. An adverse inference was drawn that the report would have been unfavourable to the prosecution. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 709, 2024 MLD 359; Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. A. No. 27767, M.R. No. 241 & P.S.L.A. No. 41181 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Proved: Afterthought
records.heading: A vague motive without documentary support is an afterthought and unproved
records.text: The alleged motive, a grudge over property left by a deceased police officer, was vague and not supported by documentary evidence. The widow was not interrogated or produced, and the motive was held an afterthought not proved by credible evidence. Ref: 2024 MLD 359; Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. Appeal No. 27767, P.S.L.A. No. 41181 and Murder Reference No. 241 of 2019).
records.title: Taha Azaam Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl. Appeal No. 27767, P.S.L.A. No. 41181 and Murder Reference No. 241 of 2019)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Special Court Act s. 9 and Territorial Jurisdiction of LHC
records.heading: Authority on section 9 Special Court Act and territorial jurisdiction; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on the following issues: territorial jurisdiction of the Lahore High Court, availability of an alternate adequate remedy, decision on merits by the High Court, relief granted that was not sought, constitutionality of s. 9 of the Special Court Act, misapplication of Mustafa Impex, and violation of earlier directions of the Court. The post gives no holding. Ref: Taufiq Asif v. General (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf & others (C.P.L.A. 3797/2020); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Taufiq Asif v. General (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf & others (C.P.L.A. 3797/2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Framing of Charge: Duty of Trial Court
records.heading: Framing of charge is the foundation of trial and must be proper and unambiguous
records.text: Framing of charge is the foundation of trial. Section 221 CrPC prescribes the procedure and the Trial Judge must ensure a proper and unambiguous charge. An incomplete, defective or vague charge may mislead the accused and cause a failure of justice, though under s. 225 CrPC an error or omission is not material unless the accused was misled and a failure of justice resulted. Ref: Zain Shahid v. The State & another (Crl.P.L.A. 29-K/2022); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Zain Shahid v. The State & another (Crl.P.L.A. 29-K/2022)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: PECA s. 19: Dishonest Intention and Uploaded Material
records.heading: Dishonest intention is presumed where private material is uploaded without a known source
records.text: Where private audio or video is uploaded to social media without a known source or legal purpose, dishonest intention is presumed and the burden of proof lies on the person responsible. The regulator should act promptly and then seek discharge of that burden. Electronic evidence is admissible but must meet higher standards than ordinary evidence. The authorities were directed to publish the measures taken. Ref: 2024 MLD 243; Hamna Qaiser v. Chairman, PEMRA and others (Writ Petition No. 5076 of 2023).
records.title: Hamna Qaiser v. Chairman, PEMRA and others (Writ Petition No. 5076 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Wheat Milling SOP Clause VI: Validity and Art. 18
records.heading: Challenge to Clause VI of the wheat milling SOP failed
records.text: A flour mill's challenge to Clause VI of the SOP of 21.09.2022 under the Wheat Release Milling Policy 2022-2023 failed. Mills grinding for the Army must submit a monthly grinding schedule approved by the Ministry of Defence to receive subsidised quota. The petitioner showed no solid reasons to hold the SOP issued without lawful authority or violative of Art. 18. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2024 MLD 203; Al-Khalid Flour Mills v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 3042 of 2022).
records.title: Al-Khalid Flour Mills v. Government of Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 3042 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 462-J PPC: Unexplained Delay in Complaint
records.heading: Unexplained delay in lodging an electricity theft complaint left the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: In an electricity theft case, a three day delay in lodging the complaint required explanation. The complainant had not gone to the place of occurrence and reported on hearsay from the surveillance team, and no reason for the delay was shown. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 MLD 276; Ghulam Jaffar v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 29417 of 2022).
records.title: Ghulam Jaffar v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 29417 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 462-J PPC: Non-Recovery of Connecting Wire
records.heading: Non-recovery of the connecting wire made the section 462-J PPC case doubtful
records.text: Where witnesses said only the meter was removed and the wire connected to the main line was not taken into possession, and the attesting witnesses to the recovery memo were not examined or cited, the prosecution case on s. 462-J PPC was doubtful. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 MLD 276; Ghulam Jaffar v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 29417 of 2022).
records.title: Ghulam Jaffar v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 29417 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 462-J PPC: Defective Recovery Memo and Ownership
records.heading: Defective recovery memo and unproved ownership left the section 462-J PPC case unproved
records.text: The undated recovery memo did not say where the meter was installed, who removed it or whether it was sealed, and the meter number and consumer name had been altered with whitener. The connection was in the name of the accused's son and no proof was given that the premises belonged to the accused. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 MLD 276; Ghulam Jaffar v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 29417 of 2022).
records.title: Ghulam Jaffar v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 29417 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Withholding Best Evidence: Art. 129(g) QSO
records.heading: Failure to produce the connecting wire is withholding best evidence under Article 129(g)
records.text: The prosecution must place before the Court all material witnesses and case properties secured in investigation. The surveillance team did not secure or produce the wire allegedly connected to the main line, so the prosecution withheld the best evidence under Art. 129(g) QSO. The case was not proved beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 MLD 276; Ghulam Jaffar v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 29417 of 2022).
records.title: Ghulam Jaffar v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 29417 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower of Immovable Property: Possession and Produce
records.heading: Dower in immovable property is not discharged until possession or produce is given
records.text: Dower consisting of immovable property is not discharged until possession is given to the wife or her share of the produce is paid. A husband who delays payment and denies possession on the plea that he need only transfer the land shows contumacious conduct, which the High Court would not countenance in constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: Muhammad Ali Khan v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 15918/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Ali Khan v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 15918/2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Presidential Reference on Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Trial
records.heading: Presidential reference opinion: Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto did not receive a fair trial
records.text: In its unanimous opinion on the Art. 186 reference, the Supreme Court said Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto did not receive a fair trial as required by the Constitution and that his fundamental right was not observed. The Court declined to answer the question on which it received no assistance. Ref: Reference by the President of Pakistan under Article 186 to revisit the case of Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto (Reference 1/2011, decided 06.03.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Reference by the President of Pakistan under Article 186 to revisit the case of Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto (Reference 1/2011, decided 06.03.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023: Constitutionality
records.heading: Concurring note on constitutionality of the Supreme Court Practice and Procedure Act 2023
records.text: Authority on the constitutionality of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023, in a concurring note endorsed by a majority of the Bench. It addresses the meaning of 'subject to law' in Art. 191, entries 55 and 58 of the Federal Legislative List, separation of powers, the scope of s. 3, and the status of benches and decisions during suspension of the Act. Ref: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division and others (C.P. 6/2023, decided 07.03.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division and others (C.P. 6/2023, decided 07.03.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Modern Devices Evidence and Voice Samples
records.heading: Courts may use data from modern devices, including matched voice samples, as evidence
records.text: Courts may use data from modern devices to ascertain facts under Arts. 46-A and 164 QSO. Voice samples on CD matched the voice recorded on USB, strengthening the prosecution case. An identification parade by the four year old abductee was not essential. Conviction and sentence under s. 365-A PPC maintained. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 215; Muhammad Farrukh etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 68886 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Farrukh etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 68886 of 2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Discovery on Disclosure by Accused
records.heading: A fact discovered on disclosure by the accused is admissible under Article 40 QSO
records.text: Discovery of a fact not known to anyone has legal significance and the fact so discovered is admissible under Art. 40 QSO. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 215; Muhammad Farrukh etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 68886 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Farrukh etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 68886 of 2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit Challenging Mutation: Revenue Officials Necessary Parties
records.heading: Revenue officials and the Provincial Government are necessary parties in a suit alleging connivance
records.text: Where a suit alleges that a mutation was attested through connivance of revenue officials, the Provincial Government and those officials are necessary parties. Without them no valid adjudication or finding of connivance can be made against them. Ref: 2020 SCMR 214; Sikandar Hayat and another v. Sughran Bibi and 6 others (Civil Appeal No. 146-L of 2018).
records.title: Sikandar Hayat and another v. Sughran Bibi and 6 others (Civil Appeal No. 146-L of 2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Un-Cross-Examined Portion of Witness Statement
records.heading: A material portion of testimony left uncross-examined is presumed accepted
records.text: If a material portion of a witness's statement is not cross-examined, it is presumed that the opposite party accepted that portion. Ref: 2020 SCMR 214; Sikandar Hayat and another v. Sughran Bibi and 6 others (Civil Appeal No. 146-L of 2018).
records.title: Sikandar Hayat and another v. Sughran Bibi and 6 others (Civil Appeal No. 146-L of 2018)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutation in Favour of Minor Donee
records.heading: A minor donee need not independently prove offer, acceptance and delivery for a gift mutation
records.text: A donee who was a minor, about six years old, when his father attested the gift mutation was not required to prove offer, acceptance and delivery of possession independently. The donee's side proved attestation through revenue officials, the record keeper and attesting witnesses, and the gift mutation was held valid. Ref: 2020 SCMR 214; Sikandar Hayat and another v. Sughran Bibi and 6 others (Civil Appeal No. 146-L of 2018).
records.title: Sikandar Hayat and another v. Sughran Bibi and 6 others (Civil Appeal No. 146-L of 2018)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 196 PPC: Complaint, Delegation and Quashing
records.heading: Cognizance of section 196 PPC offences requires a complaint, and a delegate cannot redelegate
records.text: Where a law prescribes a manner of doing something, it must be done in that manner. Cognizance of s. 196 PPC offences requires a complaint by the Government or an empowered officer. The Secretary, being a delegate, could not redelegate, and no complaint was filed against the petitioner. Appeal allowed, proceedings quashed and petitioner acquitted. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 273; Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023).
records.title: Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-D CrPC: Framing of Charge
records.heading: Trial court must consider the record under section 265-D before framing charge
records.text: The provisions of Chapter XXII-A CrPC are mandatory. Under s. 265-D the Trial Court must consider the FIR, police report, documents and witness statements before framing charge, and frame it only if it has jurisdiction and prima facie grounds exist. Otherwise it should refrain, to avoid purposeless and frivolous prosecution. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 273; Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023).
records.title: Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC: Acquittal at Any Stage
records.heading: Sections 249-A and 265-K CrPC allow acquittal at any stage, used sparingly
records.text: Sections 249-A and 265-K CrPC empower trial courts to acquit at any stage, before or after charge or after some evidence, for recorded reasons after hearing the parties. The power applies where there is no jurisdiction, insufficient material, a groundless charge or no probability of conviction, and must be used sparingly and judiciously. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 273; Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023).
records.title: Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Politically Motivated FIRs for Offences Against State
records.heading: Supreme Court observed on the adverse consequences of politically motivated FIRs against citizens
records.text: The Supreme Court recorded observations on the adverse consequences of politically motivated FIRs against politicians, political workers, media persons and human rights activists, and on how they deprive citizens of their fundamental rights. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 273; Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023).
records.title: Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Special Damages: Proof Required
records.heading: A claim for special damages fails without proof of actual damages under any head
records.text: A plaintiff claiming special damages of over Rs. 524 million from a housing society, after being allotted plots elsewhere than originally balloted, failed to prove actual damages under any head. The Trial Court rightly decreed the suit only in part. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 204; Ejaz Hussain Rathore v. Bahria Town Pvt. Ltd. etc. (R.F.A. 8-18).
records.title: Ejaz Hussain Rathore v. Bahria Town Pvt. Ltd. etc. (R.F.A. 8-18)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Sub Judice: S. 10 CPC
records.heading: Section 10 CPC bars proceeding with a later suit on a matter already in issue
records.text: A party cannot agitate the same matter before two courts at once. Section 10 CPC bars the court in which a later case is filed from proceeding where the matter in issue is directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted case. Simultaneous pursuit before two High Courts undermines the rule of law. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 295; Election Commission of Pakistan through Special Secretary, Islamabad v. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Islamabad through its authorized person and others.
records.title: Election Commission of Pakistan through Special Secretary, Islamabad v. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Islamabad through its authorized person and others

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Prosecution Under S. 196 PPC by Complaint Only
records.heading: Offences under section 196 PPC may be prosecuted only upon complaint, not an FIR
records.text: Offences mentioned in s. 196 PPC may be prosecuted only upon a complaint before a Judicial Magistrate by the Government or an empowered officer, not through an FIR. Offences outside s. 196 may be initiated by FIR under s. 154 CrPC. Where law prescribes a manner, it must be followed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 273; Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023).
records.title: Ammad Yousaf v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 225/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower Cannot Be Waived by Agreement
records.heading: Dower cannot be waived by agreement, and no estoppel operates against a statute
records.text: The wife's right to dower has its footing in s. 5 of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939. She cannot be estopped from it, and any iqrarnama, agreement or compromise waiving it, registered or not, is void. There is no estoppel against a statute or rules with statutory force. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 291; Mst. Haseena Bibi v. Abdul Haleem & others (C.A. 1227/2016).
records.title: Mst. Haseena Bibi v. Abdul Haleem & others (C.A. 1227/2016)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Claim and Entitlement to Dower
records.heading: A wife's khula statement does not bar her claim to dower
records.text: A wife's statement seeking dissolution on the basis of khula did not bar her dower claim, since the Family Court expressly deferred the dower dispute to evidence and she was willing to rejoin her husband if her rights under the marriage deed were met. The husband's conduct, including a second marriage, counted against him. Decree for dower upheld and petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2024 Pesh 25; Tauheed Farooqi v. Faiqa Anmol.
records.title: Tauheed Farooqi v. Faiqa Anmol

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Kabeen Nama Admitted: Arbitration Suspension Unproved
records.heading: Plea of suspension of the Kabeen Nama by arbitration admitted its execution
records.text: The husband's plea that an arbitration decision suspended the Kabeen Nama amounted to admission of its execution. He did not prove the suspension by examining any witness or the arbitrator, so the document stood admitted and the dower decree was upheld. Ref: PLD 2024 Pesh 25; Tauheed Farooqi v. Faiqa Anmol.
records.title: Tauheed Farooqi v. Faiqa Anmol

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Jurisdiction Over Gold Ornaments in Marriage Deed
records.heading: Family Court has jurisdiction over gold ornaments claimed under a Kabeen Nama
records.text: A Kabeen Nama is a matrimonial document and is not an independent contract amounting to an actionable claim under s. 3 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. The wife's claim to gold ornaments under it was a consideration of marriage, so the Family Court had jurisdiction. Ref: PLD 2024 Pesh 25; Tauheed Farooqi v. Faiqa Anmol.
records.title: Tauheed Farooqi v. Faiqa Anmol

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Group Insurance Proceeds Not Part of Estate
records.heading: Group insurance proceeds are not part of the estate and are not distributable
records.text: Group Insurance Proceeds do not form part of a deceased's estate, so they are not distributable among legal heirs, a suit for administration does not lie, and a succession certificate is not required. The father's succession application was not maintainable. The Division Bench set aside the Single Judge's order. Ref: PLD 2024 Kar 89; Nusrat Fareed v. Ahmed Mujahid.
records.title: Nusrat Fareed v. Ahmed Mujahid

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: What Constitutes Estate of Deceased (Tarka)
records.heading: The estate comprises only property or rights owned or absolutely claimable at death
records.text: The estate comprises moveable and immoveable assets, rights or benefits the deceased owned and controlled or could claim and transfer. Heirs inherit only from the estate. Only property or rights owned at death, or in which an absolute right to claim had been acquired in life, form the estate. Ref: PLD 2024 Kar 89; Nusrat Fareed v. Ahmed Mujahid.
records.title: Nusrat Fareed v. Ahmed Mujahid

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Trial of Civilians by Court Martial
records.heading: Trial of civilians by court martial under the Army Act is ultra vires the Constitution
records.text: The Supreme Court declared trial of civilians by court martial under s. 2(1)(d) of the Pakistan Army Act 1952 ultra vires the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 337; Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan, etc (Const.P. 24/2023).
records.title: Jawwad S. Khawaja v. Federation of Pakistan, etc (Const.P. 24/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Dishonest Investigation and Role of Investigating Officer
records.heading: Authority on dishonest investigation and the Investigating Officer's role; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on dishonest investigation and the role of the Investigating Officer. The provisions listed include ss. 166, 375, 376 and 511 PPC, s. 4(l) CrPC with Rule 25.2 of the Police Rules 1934, s. 22 of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act 2021, the Sindh Police (E & D) Rules 1988 and Arts. 4 and 155 of Police Order 2002. No holding is given. Ref: Ikramuddin Rajput v. The Inspector General of Police Sindh & others (C.P.L.A. 940-K/2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ikramuddin Rajput v. The Inspector General of Police Sindh & others (C.P.L.A. 940-K/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Pardon to Accused Requires Prosecution on Board
records.heading: A court cannot tender pardon to an accused without taking the prosecution on board
records.text: A court cannot tender pardon to an accused without taking the prosecution on board. Ref: 2024 LHC 866; Muhammad Asif v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 12454/22, decided 22.02.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 12454/22, decided 22.02.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI CPC: Court Witness and List of Witnesses
records.heading: Court may summon a non-party witness on its own motion under Order XVI
records.text: The proviso to O. XVI R. 1 CPC allows the court to condone default in filing the witness list within seven days for sufficient cause. An application to summon a Treasury record keeper as a court witness attracted O. XVI R. 14 CPC, under which the court may of its own motion summon a non-party to give evidence or produce documents, with diet money paid as the court directs. Ref: 2024 LHC 850; Muhammad Akram v. Haji Ilam Din (deceased) through L.Rs and others (W.P. No. 48863 of 2023, decided 01.03.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. Haji Ilam Din (deceased) through L.Rs and others (W.P. No. 48863 of 2023, decided 01.03.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 24(b) Specific Relief Act: Readiness and Reciprocal Promises
records.heading: Specific performance cannot be enforced in favour of a person violating an essential term
records.text: Under s. 24(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 specific performance cannot be enforced in favour of a person who violates an essential term remaining to be performed. The vendee failed to prove readiness, time was of the essence, and under s. 54 of the Contract Act reciprocal promises require the first promise to be performed. The Specific Relief Act does not require the vendee to deposit the balance consideration on filing the suit. Ref: 2024 LHC 802; Mst. Qamar Bibi (Late) through her Legal Heirs v. Shahab-ud-Din & another (Civil Revision No. 233690 of 2018).
records.title: Mst. Qamar Bibi (Late) through her Legal Heirs v. Shahab-ud-Din & another (Civil Revision No. 233690 of 2018)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Disputed Mutation and Pardanasheen Lady
records.heading: A disputed mutation confers no title and its beneficiary must prove the original transaction
records.text: A mutation confers no title, and once challenged the party relying on it must prove the original transaction. Old and illiterate ladies receive the same protection as pardanasheen ladies. Failure to seek thumb impression comparison or to produce the witnesses and revenue officer raised an adverse presumption under Art. 129(g) QSO. Ref: 2024 LHC 894; Rasheed Ahmad v. Azra Parveen (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (Civil Revision No. 11729 of 2019).
records.title: Rasheed Ahmad v. Azra Parveen (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (Civil Revision No. 11729 of 2019)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 118 NIA Presumptions and Rebuttal
records.heading: Section 118 presumptions on negotiable instruments are rebuttable by a probable defence
records.text: In a recovery suit on a negotiable instrument, s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act raises rebuttable presumptions on consideration, date and time. The defendant may rebut them with a probable defence supported by confidence-inspiring evidence or circumstances. Art. 129 QSO allows presumption of facts in the common course of events. Ref: Abdul Ghaffar v. Muhammad Iqbal (RFA No. 1181 of 2016).
records.title: Abdul Ghaffar v. Muhammad Iqbal (RFA No. 1181 of 2016)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Reasonable Grounds and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail is not withheld as punishment and reasonable doubt on involvement supports bail
records.text: Bail cannot be withheld as punishment, and the accused is presumed innocent, with the prosecution bound to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt even at the bail stage. Reasonable doubt about involvement supports bail, and further inquiry requires a tentative assessment creating such doubt. Ref: 2023 SCMR 476; Akhtar v. Khwas Khan and another (Crl.P. 1054/2023).
records.title: Akhtar v. Khwas Khan and another (Crl.P. 1054/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Confession to Police: Arts. 38 and 39 QSO and Further Inquiry
records.heading: A confession to police or in police custody cannot be proved, raising further inquiry
records.text: Under Arts. 38 and 39 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order 1984 a confession to a police officer, or made in police custody outside a Magistrate's presence, cannot be proved against the accused. The case therefore required further inquiry into guilt, to be resolved on evidence at trial. Ref: 2023 SCMR 476; Akhtar v. Khwas Khan and another (Crl.P. 1054/2023).
records.title: Akhtar v. Khwas Khan and another (Crl.P. 1054/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Punjab Food Authority Act: Rule 52 Sample Quantity Mandatory
records.heading: Minimum sample quantity under Rule 52 of the Punjab Food Rules is mandatory
records.text: Rule 52 of the Punjab Food Rules 2011, prescribing minimum sample quantities for a Public Analyst's report, is mandatory, since breach prejudices the accused and the fair trial right under Art. 10-A. The offence under s. 22(1) of the PFA Act does not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 7721; Muhammad Ashraf v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 17013/23, decided 10.04.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 17013/23, decided 10.04.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Abscondence Not a Bar to Bail
records.heading: Abscondence alone does not justify keeping an accused in custody indefinitely
records.text: Abscondence is a relevant factor in bail but must not be considered in isolation to keep a person in custody indefinitely. A person named in a murder case, rightly or wrongly, who becomes a fugitive acts naturally. Ref: 2024 SCMR 464; Said Nabi v. Ajmal Khan and another (Criminal Petition No. 104-P of 2023).
records.title: Said Nabi v. Ajmal Khan and another (Criminal Petition No. 104-P of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Intra Court Appeal: Proviso to S. 3(2) Law Reforms Ordinance
records.heading: Intra court appeal barred where the law provides an appeal, review or revision
records.text: To invoke the proviso to s. 3(2) of the Law Reforms Ordinance 1972, the test is whether the law provides at least one appeal, review or revision against the original order. If it does, s. 3(2) applies whether or not that remedy is available to the person filing the intra court appeal. Ref: 2024 SCMR 472; International Islamic University, Islamabad through Rector and another v. Syed Naveed Altaf and others (Civil Petition No. 835 of 2021).
records.title: International Islamic University, Islamabad through Rector and another v. Syed Naveed Altaf and others (Civil Petition No. 835 of 2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Habeas Corpus in Child Custody: Exceptional Remedy
records.heading: Habeas corpus for child custody issues only where no adequate remedy exists
records.text: A writ of habeas corpus issues only if the High Court is satisfied that no adequate remedy exists, such as under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890, and that production and custody are in the child's best interests. It should be an exception, reserved for criminality, forced removal or abduction, as the Guardian Court has the powers to decide custody. Ref: 2024 SCMR 486; Mst. Qurat-ul-Ain v. Station House Officer, Police Station Saddar Jalalpur Jattan, District Gujrat and others (Civil Petition No. 3718 of 2023).
records.title: Mst. Qurat-ul-Ain v. Station House Officer, Police Station Saddar Jalalpur Jattan, District Gujrat and others (Civil Petition No. 3718 of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Habeas Corpus by Grandmother or Friend of Minor
records.heading: A paternal grandmother must show why a habeas corpus writ is needed for a minor
records.text: A paternal grandmother is not a parent and must show why a writ is needed, including authority from the father or capacity as friend of the minor, which she did not. A friend must show that no person entitled to custody exists or is available, and that the friend is interested in the child's welfare. Appeal allowed and the Guardian Court directed to proceed expeditiously. Ref: 2024 SCMR 486; Mst. Qurat-ul-Ain v. Station House Officer, Police Station Saddar Jalalpur Jattan, District Gujrat and others (Civil Petition No. 3718 of 2023).
records.title: Mst. Qurat-ul-Ain v. Station House Officer, Police Station Saddar Jalalpur Jattan, District Gujrat and others (Civil Petition No. 3718 of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Mother's Second Marriage and Custody
records.heading: A mother's remarriage does not automatically remove her from custody of her children
records.text: A mother's remarriage does not automatically remove her from the custody of her children. A reading of Islamic principles, the Convention on the Rights of the Child and CEDAW shows no legal justification for separating a mother from her child because she remarries. Ref: 2024 SCMR 486; Mst. Qurat-ul-Ain v. Station House Officer, Police Station Saddar Jalalpur Jattan, District Gujrat and others (Civil Petition No. 3718 of 2023).
records.title: Mst. Qurat-ul-Ain v. Station House Officer, Police Station Saddar Jalalpur Jattan, District Gujrat and others (Civil Petition No. 3718 of 2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 295-B PPC: Ingredients of Defiling the Holy Quran
records.heading: Section 295-B PPC covers wilful defiling of the Holy Quran or its derogatory use
records.text: Section 295-B PPC covers two scenarios: wilful defiling, damaging or desecrating a copy of the Holy Quran or an extract, and wilful use of it in a derogatory manner or for unlawful purposes. For the former, the offence requires that the person acted of his own will and defiled, damaged or desecrated a copy or extract. Punishment is life imprisonment. Ref: 2024 SCMR 548; Muhammad Zafran v. The State (Crl.A. 597/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Zafran v. The State (Crl.A. 597/2018)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Dacoity: Further Inquiry, No Description in FIR
records.heading: No description of the accused in a dacoity FIR makes bail a further inquiry case
records.text: In a dacoity case, absence of the accused's description in the FIR questioned the identification parade, and none of the stolen goods was recovered from him. This made the case one of further inquiry. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and bail granted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 589; Kashif v. Imran and another (Criminal Petition No. 188-P of 2023).
records.title: Kashif v. Imran and another (Criminal Petition No. 188-P of 2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Licences for Prohibited Bore Weapons: Issuing Authority
records.heading: Court questioned the legal authority behind licences for prohibited bore weapons
records.text: In the bail petition the Court observed that the complainant showed only a paper issued by a Deputy Inspector General of Police as a licence for a sub-machine gun, a prohibited bore weapon, and that exemptions existed for certain categories of persons. It raised questions on the legal authority for such licences and directed registration of a constitution petition under Art. 184(3) for the Committee under the 2023 Act. Ref: 2024 SCMR 589; Kashif v. Imran and another (Criminal Petition No. 188-P of 2023).
records.title: Kashif v. Imran and another (Criminal Petition No. 188-P of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Misuse and Threats to Complainant
records.heading: Bail is cancelled where an influential accused threatens the complainant and misuses it
records.text: Bail was cancelled where the accused was nominated with a specific role, the weapon was recovered from him, medical and ocular evidence supported the prosecution, the investigation was partisan, and he, as an influential person, threatened the complainant, which amounted to misuse of bail. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and bail recalled. Ref: 2024 SCMR 594; Shaukat Ali and another v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore and another (Criminal Petitions Nos. 528-L and 1068-L of 2023).
records.title: Shaukat Ali and another v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore and another (Criminal Petitions Nos. 528-L and 1068-L of 2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 81 QSO: Admitted Execution and Attesting Witnesses
records.heading: Admitted execution makes examination of attesting witnesses unnecessary under Article 81 QSO
records.text: Where the executant himself admits execution of a document, examination of the attesting witnesses is unnecessary under Art. 81 QSO. Admitted facts need not be proved, so production of two attesting witnesses was not required. Ref: Amer Saleem v. Nadeem Akhtar Mirza and another (R.F.A. No. 23090 of 2017).
records.title: Amer Saleem v. Nadeem Akhtar Mirza and another (R.F.A. No. 23090 of 2017)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Claim Against Paternal Uncle
records.heading: A paternal uncle cannot be substituted for a deceased grandfather in a maintenance claim
records.text: Mulla's Muhammadan Law is not a statute, custom or usage and is not binding on courts. Maintenance from a grandfather and from a paternal uncle rest on different principles, so after the grandfather's death the paternal uncle could not be substituted as defendant. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 135; Mahnoor Shabbir v. Additional District Judge, etc. (W.P. No. 62482 of 2022, decided 12.12.2023); Justice Shahid Jamil Khan.
records.title: Mahnoor Shabbir v. Additional District Judge, etc. (W.P. No. 62482 of 2022, decided 12.12.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Deposit of Balance After Partial Withdrawal
records.heading: After withdrawal against one defendant, balance deposit must be recomputed with clear consequences of default
records.text: After the plaintiff withdrew the suit against one defendant, the trial court had to deduct that defendant's share and direct deposit of a specific balance with clear consequences of default. Dismissal for non-deposit of the whole amount was erroneous. Civil revision accepted and parties directed to appear before the Senior Civil Judge, Faisalabad. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 143; Dr. Asghar Ali v. Muhammad Ali (C.R. No. 42583 of 2022, heard 10.05.2023); Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Dr. Asghar Ali v. Muhammad Ali (C.R. No. 42583 of 2022, heard 10.05.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Concurrent Findings on Proof of Agreement
records.heading: Concurrent findings decreeing specific performance stand where the agreement and payment were proved
records.text: The buyer proved the agreement to sell and the receipt of balance consideration through two attesting witnesses to each document and the bank manager. The seller's successors could not resile from his commitment. With no misreading or non-reading of evidence shown, concurrent findings decreeing specific performance stood and the revision was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 146; Abdul Shakoor deceased through his Legal Heirs etc. v. Rana Abid Mahmood etc. (C.R. No. 63321 of 2020, heard 13.04.2023); Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Abdul Shakoor deceased through his Legal Heirs etc. v. Rana Abid Mahmood etc. (C.R. No. 63321 of 2020, heard 13.04.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Failure to Withdraw Ejectment Petition
records.heading: Sellers who did not withdraw the ejectment petition could not resist specific performance
records.text: Sellers who agreed to withdraw their ejectment petition but, after receiving payment, did not withdraw it and appealed its dismissal could not resist specific performance. Courts below granted relief on conduct and equity, and with no misreading or non-reading of evidence shown, the revision was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 151; Naveed Ahmed etc. v. Sheikh Amjad Saeed deceased through his Legal Heirs etc. (C.R. No. 3093 of 2012, heard 01.03.2023); Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Naveed Ahmed etc. v. Sheikh Amjad Saeed deceased through his Legal Heirs etc. (C.R. No. 3093 of 2012, heard 01.03.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Bare Allegation of Fraud
records.heading: Mere allegation of fraud without material does not warrant inquiry under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: The petitioner alleged under s. 12(2) CPC that he received no notice and filed no written statement, but the record showed he filed a wakalatnama and written statement and the suit was decreed on merits. Mere allegations of fraud without material do not warrant inquiry. Application dismissed and the petition dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 156; Ijaz Ahmad Khan v. Muhammad Bootay Khan deceased through his Legal Heirs etc. (C.R. No. 78446 of 2023, decided 05.12.2023); Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Ijaz Ahmad Khan v. Muhammad Bootay Khan deceased through his Legal Heirs etc. (C.R. No. 78446 of 2023, decided 05.12.2023)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Firing in Court Premises: Exclusive Jurisdiction of ATC
records.heading: Firing in court premises is triable only by the Anti-Terrorism Court
records.text: Firing in court premises is a Third Schedule offence under the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997 and is triable only by the Anti-Terrorism Court, even if it arose from personal enmity. An ordinary court receiving a challan disclosing a scheduled offence returns it to the prosecution for presentation before the ATC, relying on s. 190 CrPC, and s. 346 CrPC allows sending cases to the proper court. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 314; Ali Nawaz v. The State Etc (Crl. Misc. 8329/23).
records.title: Ali Nawaz v. The State Etc (Crl. Misc. 8329/23)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Protective or Transitory Bail
records.heading: Protective bail is granted by High Courts for a fixed time without touching merits
records.text: The CrPC has no provision for protective bail, but High Courts grant it under s. 561-A CrPC and Art. 199 for a fixed time without touching merits. It differs from pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC and does not entitle the accused to it. As it rests on fundamental rights, the High Court must judicially assess a second request.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Judicial Council Inquiry and Retirement of Judge
records.heading: Supreme Judicial Council inquiry does not abate on the judge's retirement
records.text: Once the Supreme Judicial Council initiates an inquiry into the conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge, it does not abate on the judge's retirement during pending proceedings. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary, Ministry of Law & Justice Islamabad v. The Honourable Supreme Judicial Council through its Secretary, Supreme Court Building, Islamabad and others (I.C.A. 1/2024, short order 21.02.2024).
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary, Ministry of Law & Justice Islamabad v. The Honourable Supreme Judicial Council through its Secretary, Supreme Court Building, Islamabad and others (I.C.A. 1/2024, short order 21.02.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail of Fake Advocate
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail of a person posing as an advocate was cancelled
records.text: The High Court cancelled pre-arrest bail granted by the Additional Sessions Judge to a person posing as an advocate, holding that this is a serious offence against the whole legal system. Pre-arrest bail is an extraordinary concession needing reasonable grounds and mala fide of the complainant or police. Bail granted ignoring sufficient material is liable to be recalled. Ref: 2024 LHC 938; Muhammad Rafie v. Ghaneem Aabir, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 73505-CB/2023, decided 13.03.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Rafie v. Ghaneem Aabir, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 73505-CB/2023, decided 13.03.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial Review of Executive Policy Decisions
records.heading: Courts review executive policy only for constitutional or statutory violation or arbitrariness
records.text: In reviewing government policy the court cannot act as an appellate authority on its propriety or adequacy, nor as an adviser to the executive. Its object is to ascertain whether the policy violates fundamental rights, conflicts with the Constitution or a statute, or is demonstrably arbitrary or discriminatory. Courts must stay within constitutional limits to avoid judicial activism. Ref: 2024 SCMR 581, PLJ 2024 SC 234; Senior General Manager, Pakistan Railways and others v. Muhammad Pervaiz (Civil Appeal No. 512 of 2021).
records.title: Senior General Manager, Pakistan Railways and others v. Muhammad Pervaiz (Civil Appeal No. 512 of 2021)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Diyat Recoverable From Estate on Death of Convict
records.heading: Unpaid diyat is recoverable from the offender's estate on his death
records.text: Corporal punishments end with the offender's death, but monetary punishment is recoverable from his assets, as s. 386 CrPC shows. Diyat under s. 299(e) PPC, if unpaid, is recoverable from the offender's estate on his death under s. 331(3) PPC. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and the appeal deemed pending before the High Court for decision on merits. Ref: 2019 SCMR 1144; Muhammad Shamoon (decd) through his L.Rs v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 303-L/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Shamoon (decd) through his L.Rs v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 303-L/2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Doctrine of Election Between Concurrent Remedies
records.heading: An aggrieved person must elect between concurrent remedies and cannot hop between them
records.text: An aggrieved person must elect among available concurrent or coexistent remedies. Once the election is made, he cannot launch another proceeding seeking relief contrary to what the other remedy could achieve, and cannot hop from one remedy to another. The post cites s. 11 and O. II R. 2 CPC and Art. 114 QSO. Ref: 2024 SCMR 518; Chief Executive Officer NPGCL, GENCO-III, TPS Muzafargarrah v. Khalid Umar Tariq Imran and others (Civil Petition No. 1787-L of 2022).
records.title: Chief Executive Officer NPGCL, GENCO-III, TPS Muzafargarrah v. Khalid Umar Tariq Imran and others (Civil Petition No. 1787-L of 2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Principles of Limitation Law
records.heading: Limitation gives certainty to disputes and is not a mere technicality
records.text: The law of limitation provides certainty and quietus to legal disputes and requires persons to approach courts with due diligence. Limitation is not a mere technicality, since valuable rights accrue to the other party when the period expires. Ref: 2024 SCMR 518; Chief Executive Officer NPGCL, GENCO-III, TPS Muzafargarrah v. Khalid Umar Tariq Imran and others (Civil Petition No. 1787-L of 2022).
records.title: Chief Executive Officer NPGCL, GENCO-III, TPS Muzafargarrah v. Khalid Umar Tariq Imran and others (Civil Petition No. 1787-L of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Defective Investigation and Duties of Investigating Officer
records.heading: A botched or dishonest investigation contaminates the judicial process
records.text: A botched or dishonest investigation impedes justice and contaminates the judicial process. Under s. 4(l) CrPC and Rule 25.2 of the Police Rules 1934 the Investigating Officer must find the truth without prematurely committing to any view. Section 166(2) PPC punishes improper or negligent investigation by a public servant, and s. 27 of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997 is also noted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 510; Ikramuddin Rajput v. The Inspector General of Police Sindh & others (C.P.L.A. 940-K/2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ikramuddin Rajput v. The Inspector General of Police Sindh & others (C.P.L.A. 940-K/2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Inquiry and Criminal Trial: Standard of Proof
records.heading: A departmental inquiry applies the balance of probabilities, unlike a criminal trial
records.text: Disciplinary proceedings determine whether misconduct is proven so as to impose a penalty under service law, whereas criminal prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. The standard in a departmental inquiry is balance of probabilities or preponderance of evidence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 510; Ikramuddin Rajput v. The Inspector General of Police Sindh & others (C.P.L.A. 940-K/2022); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ikramuddin Rajput v. The Inspector General of Police Sindh & others (C.P.L.A. 940-K/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Entries: Duty of Nikah Registrar
records.heading: Nikah Registrar must accurately fill all nikahnama columns with the parties' answers
records.text: Under s. 6(2A) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 the Nikah Registrar or solemnizer must accurately fill all nikahnama columns with the specific answers of the bride or bridegroom. Under s. 5(5) the form and registers are as prescribed. A defaulting Nikah Khawan or Registrar should be held accountable. The Court also noted the custom of agriculturist families giving dowry on first or second marriage. Ref: 2024 LHC 920; Irfan Mohsin v. Additional District and Sessions Judge & others (Writ Petition No. 4265 of 2020).
records.title: Irfan Mohsin v. Additional District and Sessions Judge & others (Writ Petition No. 4265 of 2020)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Award: Court's Duty Under S. 17 Despite Limitation
records.heading: Court must examine an award under section 17 despite a time barred application
records.text: Once an award is before the court, s. 17 of the Arbitration Act 1940 requires the court to examine it for patent illegality or cause to remit, even if the opposite party's application was time barred. The court cannot dismiss objections yet refuse to make the award a rule of court merely because the application was out of time. Ref: 2024 LHC 989; Sultan Mehmood v. Naeem Ahmad (Civil Revision 931-18, decided 19.02.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Sultan Mehmood v. Naeem Ahmad (Civil Revision 931-18, decided 19.02.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Presumption on Cheque Rebutted
records.heading: Presumption on a cheque is rebutted by the plaintiff's admission that payment was cleared
records.text: The presumption of correctness attached to a cheque was refuted where the plaintiff admitted in criminal proceedings (Exh.D-1) that the amount had been cleared and recorded in a voucher. The Trial Court erroneously ignored that statement, which constituted a probable defence. Ref: 2024 LHC 998; Malik Muhammad Ashraf v. Muhammad Asif etc (Regular First Appeal 258-22, decided 23.02.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Malik Muhammad Ashraf v. Muhammad Asif etc (Regular First Appeal 258-22, decided 23.02.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Willingness and Readiness of Plaintiff
records.heading: Specific performance is refused to a plaintiff who disregards directions to pay the balance
records.text: Specific performance is discretionary, equitable relief and is not granted to a plaintiff who showed contumacious conduct by not complying with repeated directions to pay the balance sale consideration. The court must find which party failed to perform. A vendee is expected to sue promptly on refusal, showing readiness and willingness to deposit the balance. Ref: 2024 LHC 1015; Sh. Khalid Javaid v. Shams ud Din Chishti (Civil Revision 323-22, decided 28.02.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Sh. Khalid Javaid v. Shams ud Din Chishti (Civil Revision 323-22, decided 28.02.2024)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: FIA Act 1974: Powers and Inquiry v. Investigation
records.heading: Inquiry and investigation under the FIA Act 1974 have distinct meanings
records.text: The FIA Act 1974 empowers the FIA to inquire into and investigate scheduled offences. Section 5(1) gives members police-like powers of search, arrest and seizure throughout Pakistan, and s. 5(6) punishes contravention of a s. 5(5) order. The Act uses 'inquiry' and 'investigation' without definition, and they have distinct meanings. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 422; Hamza Khalid v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 72452/B/2023).
records.title: Hamza Khalid v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 72452/B/2023)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: FIA Act s. 5(5): Limits on Seizure and Search
records.heading: An officer acting under section 5(5) of the FIA Act has no unfettered seizure power
records.text: An officer acting under s. 5(5) of the FIA Act has no unfettered power. He must act in good faith, there must be circumstances requiring swift action, and the seized property must have a nexus with the investigation. The FIA must follow Chapter VII CrPC for searches unless a special law prescribes otherwise, and aggrieved persons may seek redress from the competent court. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 422; Hamza Khalid v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 72452/B/2023).
records.title: Hamza Khalid v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 72452/B/2023)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: FIA Cases Distinct From Tax Authority Cases
records.heading: Criminal cases under the FIA Act must be treated distinctly from tax authority cases
records.text: Criminal cases under the FIA Act differ from those handled by tax authorities and must be dealt with distinctively. The principles in Justice Qazi Faez Isa's case apply to them. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 422; Hamza Khalid v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 72452/B/2023).
records.title: Hamza Khalid v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 72452/B/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sentencing Discretion and Concurrent Sentences
records.heading: Sentencing is discretionary and sentencing decisions are not strict binding precedent
records.text: Sentencing rests in the discretion of the sentencing judge, and sentencing decisions are examples of how a particular offender was dealt with rather than binding precedent in the strict sense.
