Uniformity of sentencing is desirable. Having regard to the peculiar facts, the sentences were directed to run concurrently. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 578; Talib v. Government of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 25111/2019).
records.title: Talib v. Government of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 25111/2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Life Imprisonment Term and s. 382-B Benefit
records.heading: Benefit of section 382-B CrPC for under-trial detention is mandatory and ordinarily cannot be refused
records.text: Under s. 57 PPC life imprisonment is reckoned as 25 years for fractions of terms, and Rule 140 of the Prison Rules is to the same effect; with remissions the minimum a lifer serves is 15 years. Section 35 CrPC governs sentences on conviction of several offences at one trial. The benefit of s. 382-B CrPC for under-trial detention is mandatory and ordinarily cannot be refused. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 578; Talib v. Government of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 25111/2019).
records.title: Talib v. Government of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition No. 25111/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Fresh Plaint After Rejection
records.heading: Withdrawal cannot be allowed to file afresh after rejection under Order VII Rule 11(d)
records.text: Under clauses (a) to (c) of O. VII R. 11 CPC the defects can be cured and a fresh plaint presented, subject to limitation. Where rejection is under clause (d) because the suit is barred by law, a fresh plaint is not envisaged unless that finding is reversed, so withdrawal with permission to file afresh cannot be allowed. Under O. XXIII R. 2 CPC the plaintiff remains bound by limitation as if the first suit had not been filed. Ref: 2024 CLC 524; Muhammad Nawaz and others v. Province of Punjab through Additional Collector and others (Civil Revision No. 176407 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz and others v. Province of Punjab through Additional Collector and others (Civil Revision No. 176407 of 2018)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Mandatory Duty to Decide Limitation: s. 3
records.heading: Section 3 obliges the court to dismiss a time barred suit even if unpleaded
records.text: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 allows condonation only for applications, appeals, reviews and revisions on sufficient cause. For suits, s. 3 is mandatory and the court must dismiss a time barred suit even if limitation is not pleaded, and may only exclude time under ss. 4 to 25 where the plaint sets up such a ground. Limitation is not a mere technicality and a right accrues on its expiry. A waiver does not relieve the court of deciding limitation. Ref: 2024 CLC 524; Muhammad Nawaz and others v. Province of Punjab through Additional Collector and others (Civil Revision No. 176407 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz and others v. Province of Punjab through Additional Collector and others (Civil Revision No. 176407 of 2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. III CPC: Recognized Agent Has No Right of Audience
records.heading: A recognized agent under Order III has no right of audience to plead
records.text: Under O. III Rules 1 and 2 CPC an attorney or recognized agent may appear, file applications and act for the party, but these words do not include pleading. The right to plead belongs to the pleader under O. III R. 4 CPC, so a recognized agent has no right of audience in court. Ref: 2024 CLC 550; Sana Aslam v. Ali Imran etc (Review 18987/22).
records.title: Sana Aslam v. Ali Imran etc (Review 18987/22)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Setting Aside Ex Parte Proceedings Order
records.heading: Article 181 governs limitation for setting aside an order of ex parte proceedings
records.text: Articles 163 and 164 of the Limitation Act, 1908 apply to restoration of a suit or setting aside an ex parte decree and do not cover an application to set aside an order of ex parte proceedings. As no article specifically provides for it, the residuary Article 181 applies, giving three years from accrual of the right to sue. Ref: 2024 CLC 563; Rana Karamat v. Farhan Haider etc (Misc. Writ 53269/21).
records.title: Rana Karamat v. Farhan Haider etc (Misc. Writ 53269/21)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Express Request and Consent of Wife
records.heading: Khula can be granted only on the wife's express request and with her consent
records.text: Khula is a basic right of a woman under Muslim family law. The court can grant it only if she seeks it in express terms, and her consent is vital for its grant. Ref: Ibrahim Khan thr. Attorney Muhammad Zaheer v. Mst. Saima Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 4657/2022, decided 15.02.2024); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Ibrahim Khan thr. Attorney Muhammad Zaheer v. Mst. Saima Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 4657/2022, decided 15.02.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Distinguished from Dissolution under DMMA
records.heading: Khula needs no ground but requires dower waiver, unlike dissolution under the DMMA
records.text: Khula is a basic right of a woman, grantable only on her express request and with her consent. Unlike dissolution under s. 2 DMMA, khula needs no ground, requires waiver of dower, and a decree follows immediately once pre-trial reconciliation fails under s. 10 of the Family Courts Act, 1964. Dissolution under the DMMA preserves dower under s. 5 and requires evidence under s. 11 FCA. Ref: Ibrahim Khan thr. Attorney Muhammad Zaheer v. Mst. Saima Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 4657/2022, decided 15.02.2024); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Ibrahim Khan thr. Attorney Muhammad Zaheer v. Mst. Saima Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 4657/2022, decided 15.02.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inquest Report: Omissions and Pistol Recoveries
records.heading: Omission of eyewitnesses from the inquest report suggests their names were not then known
records.text: The inquest report, prepared under Chapter 25 Rule 35 of the Police Rules, 1934, guards against later fabrication. Omission of the eyewitnesses and the accused and of any summary of facts without explanation supports an inference that their names were not known then. Recovery of pistols on pointing out of the appellants, in the presence of a negative report, draws adverse inference. Ref: 2024 LHC 1060; Ghaffar Abbas @ Ghaffar Ahmed etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 435-22, decided 13.03.2024); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan.
records.title: Ghaffar Abbas @ Ghaffar Ahmed etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 435-22, decided 13.03.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chemical Reaction of Potassium Nitrate, Sulfur and Carbon
records.heading: The judgment records the chemical reaction of potassium nitrate, sulfur and carbon
records.text: The judgment records that potassium nitrate, sulfur and carbon react to form nitrogen, carbon dioxide, heat and potassium sulfide, and the heat makes the gases expand rapidly, producing an explosive force and propelling action. Ref: 2024 LHC 1076; Muhammad Hanif Tayyab v. Insha Ullah etc (Crl. Appeal 10214/22, decided 12.03.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif Tayyab v. Insha Ullah etc (Crl. Appeal 10214/22, decided 12.03.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: SJC Removal of Judge: Art. 211 and Art. 10A
records.heading: Article 211 bar does not apply to mala fide acts or acts without jurisdiction
records.text: The bar under Art. 211 does not apply to mala fide acts, acts coram non judice or acts without jurisdiction. The SJC must hold an inquiry before forming its opinion on misconduct, and Art. 10A fair trial requirements were not met. The SJC report and the notification of 11 October 2018 were set aside, and Justice Shaukat Aziz Siddiqui is deemed retired as a Judge of the Islamabad High Court. Ref: Shaukat Aziz Siddiqui v. Federation of Pakistan, Secty M/o Law and Justice and another (C.P. 76/2018, decided 22.03.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Shaukat Aziz Siddiqui v. Federation of Pakistan, Secty M/o Law and Justice and another (C.P. 76/2018, decided 22.03.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Rights of Arrested Accused: Grounds and Family Contact
records.heading: Accused must be promptly told the grounds of arrest and allowed to contact family
records.text: The detaining authority must promptly inform the accused of the grounds of arrest, in accordance with due process. The accused must also be allowed to contact his family after arrest. Compliance by police and Magistrates must be ensured and properly documented in the police record. Ref: 2024 LHC 1065; Muhammad Imran v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc (Criminal Proceedings 8709/24, decided 20.02.2024); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc (Criminal Proceedings 8709/24, decided 20.02.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Videography of Narcotics Arrests and Recoveries
records.heading: Narcotics arrests and recoveries must be video recorded to promote transparency
records.text: Complaints of false implication are frequent, and videography promotes transparency in narcotics cases. The court directed that arrest, recovery and related proceedings be video recorded, and that detailed reasons be stated in the supplementary statement where this is not possible. The government was directed to supply body-worn and dashboard cameras to police and ANF within six months. Ref: 2024 LHC 1103; Kousar Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 5175-B-23, decided 28.02.2024); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Kousar Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 5175-B-23, decided 28.02.2024)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Section 18 Limitation Act: Fraud and Knowledge of Right
records.heading: Section 18 starts limitation from when fraud concealing the right to sue became known
records.text: Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1908 postpones the start of limitation where a person is kept by fraud from knowledge of his right to sue, so that time runs from when the fraud first became known. A seller or donor who does not challenge an actual denial of his right within limitation, despite knowledge, is barred. Ref: 2002 SCMR 1009; Mst. Rabia Gula, etc. v. Muhammad Janan, etc. (Civil Appeal No. 139-P of 2013).
records.title: Mst. Rabia Gula, etc. v. Muhammad Janan, etc. (Civil Appeal No. 139-P of 2013)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Challenging Adverse Revenue Entry
records.heading: Failure to challenge a known adverse entry within limitation bars the suit
records.text: A seller or donor who has knowledge of an adverse entry and does not challenge the actual denial within limitation is barred, and repetition of the entry in a later Jamabandi gives no fresh cause of action. Failure to challenge the entry during the donor's lifetime despite knowledge is hit by limitation. Ref: 2024 LHC 1120; Muhammad Azram v. Muhammad Altaf etc (Civil Revision 573-14, decided 29.02.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Azram v. Muhammad Altaf etc (Civil Revision 573-14, decided 29.02.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Declaration Without Possession: s. 42 Specific Relief Act
records.heading: Bare declaration cannot be claimed under section 42 without possession being sought
records.text: The judgment considers the scope of s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Where possession admittedly is not with the plaintiff, he cannot claim a bare declaration unless the relief of possession is also sought. Ref: 2024 LHC 1120; Muhammad Azram v. Muhammad Altaf etc (Civil Revision 573-14, decided 29.02.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Azram v. Muhammad Altaf etc (Civil Revision 573-14, decided 29.02.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Showing Arrest in Other FIRs; Physical Remand
records.heading: Investigating agency must show arrest in all known cases and may seek physical remand
records.text: When an accused is arrested in one case, the investigating agency must show his arrest in all registered cases known to it. Even after he is lodged in judicial custody, police may obtain his physical remand in FIRs registered at other police stations, districts or provinces with the permission of the Magistrate or court concerned. Ref: 2024 LHC 1111; Syed Faheem ul Hassan v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc. (W.P. No. 1075/24, decided 06.03.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Syed Faheem ul Hassan v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc. (W.P. No. 1075/24, decided 06.03.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Mentally Ill Accused: Trial and Execution
records.heading: Authority on trial of mental illness pleas and execution of mentally ill prisoners
records.text: Authority of a five member Supreme Court bench on three questions: how a trial court should deal with a plea of mental illness at the time of the offence, how it should deal with a claim that the accused is incapable of making a defence due to mental illness, and whether a mentally ill condemned prisoner should be executed. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 488; Mst. Safia Bano and another v. Home Department Government of Punjab through Secretary and others.
records.title: Mst. Safia Bano and another v. Home Department Government of Punjab through Secretary and others

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Time Barred Suit: Rejection of Plaint Without Evidence
records.heading: A suit barred by limitation must be rejected at once without evidence or issues
records.text: If a suit is found to be barred by limitation, the plaint has to be rejected forthwith without recording evidence or framing any issue. Ref: 2024 YLR 573; Ghulam Hussain v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Civil Revision No. 69554 of 2023).
records.title: Ghulam Hussain v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Civil Revision No. 69554 of 2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Not a Technicality; Law Points at Revision
records.heading: Limitation is not a mere technicality and law points may be raised at revision
records.text: Limitation is not a mere technicality, and on its expiry a right accrues in favour of the other side that cannot lightly be taken away. A question of law, even if not raised by the opposite party, can be considered by the courts at the appellate and revisional stage. Ref: 2024 YLR 573; Ghulam Hussain v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Civil Revision No. 69554 of 2023).
records.title: Ghulam Hussain v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Civil Revision No. 69554 of 2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Cross-Examination of Own Witness
records.heading: Prosecution may cross-examine its own witness who turns hostile under Article 150 QSO
records.text: Art. 150 QSO does not confine the court's power to permit the party calling a witness to put questions that might be put in cross-examination to any stage of the examination. It is wide and discretionary, so where a witness supports the prosecution in chief but turns hostile in cross-examination, the prosecution may cross-examine him. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 261, 2024 YLR 745; Shuja ul Haq Malik v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 51188/22).
records.title: Shuja ul Haq Malik v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 51188/22)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Police Opinion of Innocence and CCTV
records.heading: CCTV footage found unedited by PFSA is admissible even at the bail stage
records.text: A routine ipse dixit of the police without supporting reasoning does not suffice for post-arrest bail in a homicide case, but an opinion in favour of the accused based on confidence inspiring material can be used on tentative assessment. CCTV footage found by PFSA to be unedited is admissible under Arts. 46-A and 164 QSO even at the bail stage. Ref: 2024 YLR 762; Usman Ali Maqbool v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 47792/23).
records.title: Usman Ali Maqbool v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 47792/23)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Cross Version Cases
records.heading: Bail is generally granted in cross version cases, leaving aggression to trial
records.text: Bail is generally granted where there are two versions of the incident, absent extraordinary circumstances, especially when the accused's counter version is supported by record and investigation. Courts lean towards post-arrest bail in cross version cases and leave the question of who initiated aggression to the trial court. Ref: 2024 YLR 762; Usman Ali Maqbool v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 47792/23).
records.title: Usman Ali Maqbool v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 47792/23)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 2 CPC: Fresh Suit and Limitation
records.heading: Time in a withdrawn suit counts against the plaintiff in a fresh suit
records.text: On a fresh suit filed with permission after withdrawal, time runs against the plaintiffs from the institution of the first suit. Under O. XXIII R. 2 CPC the plaintiff is bound by limitation as if the first suit had not been instituted, and the time consumed in the former suit is counted against him. Ref: 2024 YLR 793; Dost Muhammad Khan (deceased) through L.Rs v. Fareed Muhammad Khan and others (C.R. No. 12352 of 2022).
records.title: Dost Muhammad Khan (deceased) through L.Rs v. Fareed Muhammad Khan and others (C.R. No. 12352 of 2022)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Denial of Tenancy: Proof of Ownership Suffices
records.heading: Proof of ownership establishes the landlord tenant relationship where the tenant denies it
records.text: Where the alleged tenant denies the landlord and tenant relationship and the landlord proves his ownership of the property, that suffices to establish the relationship. Because of the denial, the tenant's default in payment of rent is also taken as proved. Ref: 2024 YLR 824; Abdul Wahid v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 53442/2020).
records.title: Abdul Wahid v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 53442/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pleadings Are Not Evidence
records.heading: Pleadings are not evidence and must be proved by evidence
records.text: Mere pleadings of the parties are not evidence in themselves. To substantiate the facts pleaded, evidence has to be produced that corroborates and proves the contentions. Ref: 2024 YLR 824; Abdul Wahid v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 53442/2020).
records.title: Abdul Wahid v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 53442/2020)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: No s. 53-A Protection in Ejectment
records.heading: An agreement to sell gives a tenant no section 53-A protection in ejectment
records.text: A mere agreement to sell confers no ownership, so a vendee tenant in ejectment proceedings cannot claim protection under s. 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. The landlord retains his status, and possession is re-transferred if the tenant later succeeds in a suit for specific performance. Ref: 2024 YLR 824; Abdul Wahid v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 53442/2020).
records.title: Abdul Wahid v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 53442/2020)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 71 QSO: Oral Evidence Means Personal Testimony
records.heading: Oral evidence under Article 71 QSO means personal testimony of the perceiving witness
records.text: Having regard to the language of the first proviso to Art. 71 QSO, the oral evidence contemplated by that article is personal testimony based on the memory of the person who has seen, heard or perceived the fact. Ref: 2024 LHC 1184; Muhammad Asif v. The State (Jail Appeal 6732/19, decided 15.03.2024); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Jail Appeal 6732/19, decided 15.03.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Guardian ad Litem for Person of Unsound Mind: O. XXXII
records.heading: Authority on guardian ad litem for a person of unsound mind under Order XXXII
records.text: Authority on the appointment of a guardian in the suit under Order XXXII CPC for a person of unsound mind, and on the scope of the Mental Health Ordinance, 2001 in this regard. Ref: Malik Arshad Hussain Awan v. M/s United Bank Limited (C.P.L.A. 1393-L/2020, decided 22.02.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Malik Arshad Hussain Awan v. M/s United Bank Limited (C.P.L.A. 1393-L/2020, decided 22.02.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Disputed Documents Cannot Be Tendered Through Counsel
records.heading: Disputed documents must be proved by sworn witnesses, not tendered through counsel
records.text: Disputed documents must be brought on record by the party or its witnesses on oath so that they are subject to cross-examination. Documents submitted through the unsworn statement of counsel cannot be considered as evidence. Ref: Muhammad Ashraf and others v. Azhar Ahmad and others (Civil Revision No. 17685 of 2024, decided 26.03.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf and others v. Azhar Ahmad and others (Civil Revision No. 17685 of 2024, decided 26.03.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance Vests on Death; Daughter and Illegal Mutation
records.heading: A daughter cannot be deprived of her inherited share by an illegal mutation
records.text: Legal heirs inherit to the extent of their shares the moment the predecessor dies. A daughter of the deceased landlord cannot be deprived of her inherited share by an illegal mutation sanctioned at the behest of male heirs. Ref: Mst. Sehat Bibi v. Bahar Khan s/o late Daulat Khan & 2 others (Civil Appeal No. 26-Q of 2017).
records.title: Mst. Sehat Bibi v. Bahar Khan s/o late Daulat Khan & 2 others (Civil Appeal No. 26-Q of 2017)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 184(3) Petition Against General Elections 2024: Costs
records.heading: Article 184(3) petition against General Elections 2024 dismissed as withdrawn with costs
records.text: A petition under Art. 184(3) to declare the General Elections 2024 void was withdrawn. The Court found abuse of process and waste of court time, noting the petitioner did not disclose that he had been court martialed and used his former army rank. The petition was dismissed as withdrawn with costs of Rs. 500,000, payable in equal shares to the Pakistan Bar Council and the Supreme Court Bar Association within thirty days, failing which recoverable as arrears of land revenue. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 486; Ali Khan v. Government of Pakistan through A.G., Islamabad and another (C.U.O. 18/2024 in C.P. NIL of 2024).
records.title: Ali Khan v. Government of Pakistan through A.G., Islamabad and another (C.U.O. 18/2024 in C.P. NIL of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution Limitation: Which Decree Is Executable
records.heading: Once the court of last instance passes a decree, only that decree is executable
records.text: Until an appeal or revision is filed, or while pending without stay, the decree remains executable, but once the court of last instance passes a decree only that decree can be executed, whether it affirms, reverses or modifies the lower decree. Where no petition for leave to appeal was filed before the Supreme Court, Bakhtiar Ahmed v. Mst. Shamim Akhtar (2013 SCMR 5) did not apply, the execution application was not time barred, and leave was declined. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 489; Anjuman Ghulaman Mustafa v. Darul Islamia Society and others (C.P.L.A. No. 6052 of 2021).
records.title: Anjuman Ghulaman Mustafa v. Darul Islamia Society and others (C.P.L.A. No. 6052 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Abatement of Appeal on Death of Convict: Musharraf
records.heading: Appeal abates on the convict's death and the Special Court conviction subsists
records.text: The appellant, convicted by the Special Court, was required to surrender but did not, and died on 5 February 2023. As none of his legal heirs came forward, the appeal under s. 12(3) of the Criminal Law Amendment (Special Courts) Act, 1976 was dismissed as abated, with s. 431 CrPC referred to, and the conviction by the Special Court subsists. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 497; General (R) Pervez Musharraf v. The Federation of Pakistan and others (Crl.A. 785/2020); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: General (R) Pervez Musharraf v. The Federation of Pakistan and others (Crl.A. 785/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ex Parte Decree: Improper Service Under O. V R. 16
records.heading: Service of summons without the defendant's signature is improper under Order V Rule 16
records.text: In an O. XXXVII suit, service was held improper where the process server did not obtain the defendant's signature when delivering the summons, as O. V R. 16 CPC requires, and no inquiry under O. V R. 19 CPC examined the serving officer. Revision was allowed. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 233; Asad Mumtaz Warraich v. Ali Mumtaz Warraich (Civil Revision No. 60871 of 2023).
records.title: Asad Mumtaz Warraich v. Ali Mumtaz Warraich (Civil Revision No. 60871 of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Public Safety Commissions: Government Directed to Notify
records.heading: Government directed to notify Public Safety Commissions; absence of elected representatives no excuse
records.text: The government was directed to notify the Provincial and District Public Safety Commissions within 30 days under s. 37 of the Police Order, 2002. The excuse of absence of elected representatives was rejected, since there cannot be a gap in governance through chosen representatives, relying on the Preamble read with Art. 140A of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 238; Muhammad Razzaq etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Misc. Writ 5973-17); Justice Shahid Jameel.
records.title: Muhammad Razzaq etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Misc. Writ 5973-17)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail: Delay Caused by the Court
records.heading: Capital accused detained over two years gets bail unless he caused the delay
records.text: Under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC a court shall release an accused in an offence punishable with death detained for over two years, unless the delay was caused by the accused or the fourth proviso applies. The right rests also on Arts. 4, 9 and 10A of the Constitution. Petition converted into appeal and allowed, and bail granted. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 492; Rohan Ahmad v. The State, etc (Crl. P. 894-L of 2023).
records.title: Rohan Ahmad v. The State, etc (Crl. P. 894-L of 2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Presidential Reference on Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Case
records.heading: Presidential reference opinion: Bhutto was not afforded a fair trial
records.text: In a Presidential Reference under Art. 186 to revisit the Bhutto case, the Supreme Court gave a unanimous opinion that Bhutto was not afforded a fair trial in accordance with the Constitution and that a fundamental right was not observed in his trial. On the question regarding the doctrine of repentance the Court gave no opinion for want of assistance. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 509; Reference by the President of Islamic Republic of Pakistan under Article 186 of the Constitution to revisit the case of Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto (Reference 1/2011); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Reference by the President of Islamic Republic of Pakistan under Article 186 of the Constitution to revisit the case of Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto (Reference 1/2011)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Rule of Consistency in Bail: Benchmark
records.heading: Under the rule of consistency, bail considers the FIR role together with investigation material
records.text: The rule of consistency rests on equality before the law under Art. 25 of the Constitution. The benchmark for applying it under s. 497(2) CrPC is the role attributed in the FIR together with the material collected in the investigation, and not the FIR role alone. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1071, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 1; Mohammad Atif v. The State (Crl. P. 298/2023).
records.title: Mohammad Atif v. The State (Crl. P. 298/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 145 CrPC: Title Disputes and Breach of Peace
records.heading: Title disputes cannot be decided in section 145 CrPC proceedings
records.text: Questions of title or separation of a share in land cannot be determined in proceedings under s. 145 CrPC. Such proceedings require a dispute over land, water or boundaries likely to cause a breach of peace. Property disputes not likely to cause breach of peace fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the civil court. Ref: PLD 2024 Pesh 35; Gul Zada v. Hazrat Gul and others (Cr.M.Q.P. No. 54-M of 2017).
records.title: Gul Zada v. Hazrat Gul and others (Cr.M.Q.P. No. 54-M of 2017)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Attachment Before Judgment: Intent to Obstruct Decree
records.heading: Attachment before judgment requires intent to obstruct or delay execution of a decree
records.text: Attachment before judgment requires the court to be satisfied that the defendant is disposing of or removing property with intent to obstruct or delay execution of a future decree. No person is barred from dealing with property merely because a suit is filed. The court may examine conduct before the suit and surrounding circumstances. The Division Bench declined to interfere with the order requiring security. Ref: PLD 2024 Kar 112; Ghulamali P. Allana v. Louis Dreyfus Commodities Suisse SA and 3 others (High Court Appeal No. 62 of 2023).
records.title: Ghulamali P. Allana v. Louis Dreyfus Commodities Suisse SA and 3 others (High Court Appeal No. 62 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Rejection of Plaint and Presentation of Fresh Plaint
records.heading: Rejection of a plaint on limitation or res judicata is prima facie incurable
records.text: Rejection of a plaint does not bar a fresh plaint if the defect is cured or curable, but rejection on limitation or res judicata is prima facie incurable. The court must first decide whether proceedings are within time, whether or not objection is taken, and limitation creates vested rights. The High Court in revision set aside the appellate order and restored the trial court order. Ref: PLD 2024 Kar 121; Ali Mardan Shah and 3 others v. V Mushtaque through L.Rs. and others (R.A. No. 165 of 2010).
records.title: Ali Mardan Shah and 3 others v. V Mushtaque through L.Rs. and others (R.A. No. 165 of 2010)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Intra Court Appeal Under s. 3 Law Reforms Ordinance
records.heading: Intra court appeal is not maintainable even if a party had no right of appeal
records.text: An intra court appeal is not maintainable under s. 3 of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972 even if one of the parties to the proceedings had no right of appeal against the original order. Ref: National Bank of Pakistan through its President, Head Office, Karachi, etc v. Muhammad Adeel (C.P.L.A. 1800-L/2018, decided 13.03.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: National Bank of Pakistan through its President, Head Office, Karachi, etc v. Muhammad Adeel (C.P.L.A. 1800-L/2018, decided 13.03.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Suspension of Sentence: Co-Accused Acquitted
records.heading: Acquittal of a similarly placed co-accused warrants suspension of sentence
records.text: Where a co-accused with a similar or more effective role has been acquitted and there is no corroboration, conviction of the accused on the same evidence calls for reappraisal of evidence, which warrants suspension of execution of his sentence. Ref: 2024 LHC 1346; Muhammad Waseem v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal CM/1/20219/23, decided 05.04.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Waseem v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal CM/1/20219/23, decided 05.04.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift: Donor's Capacity and Attorney's Power
records.heading: An attorney cannot make a gift of the principal's property without express permission
records.text: The judgment deals with the concept of an oral gift (hiba) and requires that the donor be compos mentis. A power of attorney cannot be used by the attorney to make a gift without the principal's express permission. An attorney who intends to sell or gift to himself or his next of kin must consult the principal and seek permission. Ref: Babar Anwar v. Muhammad Ashraf and another (C.P.L.A. 5972/2021, decided 24.01.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Babar Anwar v. Muhammad Ashraf and another (C.P.L.A. 5972/2021, decided 24.01.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: Closure of Right to Written Statement
records.heading: Negligent defendant gets no relief against closure of his right to written statement
records.text: Family Courts exist for expeditious disposal of family disputes. The defendant and counsel had no lawful excuse for negligence in noting the hearing date and filing the written statement. Allowing the constitutional petition would defeat the object of the Family Courts Act, 1964, and it was dismissed in limine. Ref: 2022 CLC 391; Qaiser-ur-Rehman v. Civil Judge.
records.title: Qaiser-ur-Rehman v. Civil Judge

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ex Parte Proceedings on Adjourned Date: O. IX R. 6
records.heading: Ex parte proceedings are authorised only on the date fixed in the summons
records.text: Order IX R. 6 CPC authorises ex parte proceedings only on the date fixed in the summons for hearing and not on an adjourned date. Proceeding ex parte after adjournments on the earlier publication, without fresh notice or publication, was a grave illegality. Ref: 2021 CLC 2119; Abdul Majeed Hussain Bibi.
records.title: Abdul Majeed Hussain Bibi

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: No Oral Acknowledgement of Liability: s. 19
records.heading: Oral acknowledgement of liability does not extend limitation under section 19
records.text: Law does not recognise oral acknowledgement of liability for the benefit of s. 19 of the Limitation Act, 1908, and none was shown in writing. The suit for recovery on a cheque, filed about ten years after the amount fell due, was barred under Art. 64-A, and the High Court declined to interfere. Ref: 2024 MLD 603; Manzoor Ahmad v. Azam Ali.
records.title: Manzoor Ahmad v. Azam Ali

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Conditional Bail: s. 401(4-A) CrPC
records.heading: A court may impose a reasonable condition on bail under section 401(4-A) CrPC
records.text: Under s. 401(4-A) CrPC a criminal court may pass a conditional order restricting liberty. A condition may be imposed on bail if circumstances warrant, provided it is neither illegal nor unreasonable and is one the accused can fulfil independently of another's will. The case concerned release on deposit of arsh under s. 337-N(2) PPC. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 645; Bilal Azam v. Muhammad Haq Nawaz.
records.title: Bilal Azam v. Muhammad Haq Nawaz

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Production of Driver Who Shifted Body
records.heading: Non-production of the driver and unreported shifting of the body cast doubt on eyewitnesses
records.text: Eyewitnesses took the already dead deceased to hospital instead of reporting to police, could not give the registration number or driver's name of the vehicle, and the prosecution did not produce the driver. This cast doubt on their presence and gave rise to an adverse inference, so the prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 617; Mansab Ali v. State.
records.title: Mansab Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blood Stained Clothes of Eyewitnesses Not Produced
records.heading: Eyewitnesses failing to produce claimed blood stained clothes strikes at the prosecution case
records.text: Eyewitnesses claimed their clothes were smeared with the deceased's blood but produced none and then said they had washed them. This omission struck at the root of the prosecution case and showed a false claim. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 617; Mansab Ali v. State.
records.title: Mansab Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: Close Relatives at Scene
records.heading: Close relatives at a distant scene without explanation are chance witnesses
records.text: The complainant mother and her brother were closely related to the deceased and were chance witnesses, as the occurrence was far from their homes and no independent evidence established the reason for their presence. Their presence appeared a laboured story. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 617; Mansab Ali v. State.
records.title: Mansab Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Co-Accused Acquitted on Same Evidence
records.heading: Witnesses disbelieved against an acquitted co-accused need independent corroboration against others
records.text: Where a co-accused was acquitted on the same evidence and the acquittal was not challenged, witnesses disbelieved as to him cannot be relied upon against the other accused without independent, unimpeachable corroboration. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 617; Mansab Ali v. State.
records.title: Mansab Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Contradiction between eyewitness account and postmortem injuries raises reasonable doubt
records.text: Eyewitnesses spoke only of firearm injuries, while the postmortem showed fifteen injuries, nine firearm and six by blunt weapons, with no accused alleged to carry a blunt weapon. Eyewitnesses were also not mentioned in the inquest report. This contradiction raised reasonable doubt under ss. 302(b) and 34 PPC. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 617; Mansab Ali v. State.
records.title: Mansab Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Postmortem Casts Doubt on Prompt FIR
records.heading: Delayed postmortem casts doubt on the promptness of the FIR
records.text: A postmortem conducted 6 to 7 hours after death, with the body at the dead house from 12.00 p.m. until 4.00 p.m., cast serious doubt on the promptness of the FIR. An inference arose that the time was used to fabricate the story and procure eyewitnesses. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 617; Mansab Ali v. State.
records.title: Mansab Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Unproved: Undetailed Quarrel
records.heading: An undetailed quarrel motive without corroboration remains unproved
records.text: The alleged motive, a quarrel between the deceased and the accused, had no details in the complaint or inquest report, was not reported to police or a panchayat and had no independent corroboration, so it remained unproved. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 617; Mansab Ali v. State.
records.title: Mansab Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recoveries Attested by Eyewitnesses Inconsequential
records.heading: Eyewitnesses cannot corroborate themselves by attesting recoveries
records.text: Eyewitnesses cannot corroborate themselves by acting as attesting witnesses to recoveries, since corroboration must come from independent sources. The recoveries were of no efficacy, and the inquest report showed no crime empties although the recovery memo and site plan did. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 617; Mansab Ali v. State.
records.title: Mansab Ali v. State

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Firing in Court Premises: Exclusive ATC Jurisdiction
records.heading: Firing in court premises is exclusively triable by the Anti-Terrorism Court
records.text: Under Entry 4, serial (iii) of the Third Schedule of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, firing in court premises is exclusively triable by the Anti-Terrorism Court even where it results from personal vendetta. A Magistrate lacking jurisdiction should send the case on, as s. 346 CrPC contemplates. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 658; Ali Nawaz v. State (Crl. Misc. 8329/23).
records.title: Ali Nawaz v. State (Crl. Misc. 8329/23)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 12(2) CPC: Substituted Service by Publication
records.heading: Ex parte decree not following due course of law was rightly set aside under section 12(2)
records.text: Where summons could not issue because the plaintiffs did not deposit process fee, the trial court resorted to newspaper publication instead of proceeding against the plaintiffs. The ex parte proceedings and decree were not the outcome of due course of law. The s. 12(2) application was rightly allowed. Ref: 2024 MLD 455; Muhammad Aurangzeb v. Additional District Judge, Rawalpindi.
records.title: Muhammad Aurangzeb v. Additional District Judge, Rawalpindi

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Scope of Writ of Certiorari Art. 199(1)(a)(ii)
records.heading: Certiorari under Article 199(1)(a)(ii) has limited scope and needs material illegality
records.text: A writ of certiorari under Art. 199(1)(a)(ii) of the Constitution has a very limited scope. The petitioner must show that the order assailed is without lawful authority and suffers from material illegalities. Ref: 2024 MLD 455; Muhammad Aurangzeb v. Additional District Judge, Rawalpindi.
records.title: Muhammad Aurangzeb v. Additional District Judge, Rawalpindi

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Personal Need Not a Ground Under Punjab Rented Premises Act
records.heading: Personal need is not a ground of eviction under the Punjab Rented Premises Act
records.text: Requirement of property for personal use is not a ground of eviction under the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009. The other grounds depended on the landlord and tenant relationship, which the petitioner failed to prove by dependable evidence. Ref: 2024 MLD 413; Abdul Rehman v. Additional District Judge.
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. Additional District Judge

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction Requires Proof of Landlord Tenant Relationship
records.heading: Eviction requires the landlord first to establish the tenant relationship
records.text: Reading ss. 13 and 15 with ss. 2(d) and 2(l) of the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009, eviction is available only if the landlord first establishes that the person to be evicted is his tenant. Other claims must be resolved by civil courts. The constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: 2024 MLD 413; Abdul Rehman v. Additional District Judge.
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. Additional District Judge

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Oral Tenancy: Proof by Independent Evidence
records.heading: An oral tenancy needs independent proof and contradictory witnesses cannot establish it
records.text: The petitioner claimed an oral tenancy arising from the previous owner's statement on sale, but named no witnesses in the petition, and his later witnesses contradicted him. The oral tenancy could not be proved by receipt or independent evidence. Ref: 2024 MLD 413; Abdul Rehman v. Additional District Judge.
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. Additional District Judge

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Withdrawal With Permission: O. XXIII R. 2 and Limitation
records.heading: Permission to file afresh does not exempt the plaintiff from limitation
records.text: Under s. 9 of the Limitation Act, 1908 time once running is not stopped. Under O. XXIII R. 2 CPC, permission to file a fresh suit does not exempt the party from limitation. A specific performance suit filed after over five years was barred under Art. 113, which prescribes three years, and the court should decide limitation first. Ref: 2024 MLD 485; Javaid Iqbal Butt v. Riffat Mahmood Ghauri.
records.title: Javaid Iqbal Butt v. Riffat Mahmood Ghauri

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Failure to Prove Attendance Before Sub-Registrar
records.heading: Plaintiff failing to prove attendance before the Sub-Registrar cannot obtain specific performance
records.text: The plaintiff failed to prove his appearance before the Sub-Registrar on the target date, producing neither the Sub-Registrar nor staff and not showing he had the balance consideration. The High Court in revision declined to disturb the concurrent findings, which showed no misreading or non-reading of evidence. Ref: 2024 MLD 467; Muhammad Sarwar alias Babar v. Muhammad Yasin (deceased).
records.title: Muhammad Sarwar alias Babar v. Muhammad Yasin (deceased)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest and Post-Arrest Bail: Merits
records.heading: Merits required for pre-arrest and post-arrest bail differ under sections 498 and 497
records.text: The merits required for bail before arrest and after arrest under ss. 498 and 497 CrPC differ, but even the merits of the case can be touched upon when granting pre-arrest bail. Ref: 2024 MLD 502; Mohammad Ali Farhan Hameed v. State.
records.title: Mohammad Ali Farhan Hameed v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Breach of Trust and FIR Delay
records.heading: A broken promise is not criminal breach of trust, supporting pre-arrest bail
records.text: An unexplained FIR delay of over a year made false implication possible, and s. 406 PPC was hardly attracted as no entrustment was shown. A mere broken promise is not criminal breach of trust. Ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2024 MLD 502; Mohammad Ali Farhan Hameed v. State.
records.title: Mohammad Ali Farhan Hameed v. State

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance: Pedigree Table Not Proved
records.heading: Collaterals who failed to prove their pedigree table had no locus standi
records.text: Collaterals claimed the estate of an issueless owner against his widow. Their pedigree table was issued in India in an Indian language and translated by a private person, and was not shown to be obtained in accordance with law (Art. 89(5) QSO). They failed to prove their relationship and had no locus standi. Ref: 2024 MLD 534; Mst. Badami v. Mst. Budhee.
records.title: Mst. Badami v. Mst. Budhee

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eyewitnesses at Scene in Rural Setting
records.heading: Presence of a relative visiting from another village is not unusual in rural settings
records.text: The presence of a relative visiting from another village eight miles away was not unusual, as in rural settings close kin visit and stay without specific purpose, and daytime travel is normal. The complainant's testimony was in any event natural and confidence inspiring. Appeal against conviction of two accused was dismissed. Ref: 2024 MLD 576; Zulfiqar Ali v. State.
records.title: Zulfiqar Ali v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail Refused: Rape of Minor
records.heading: Bail refused in rape of a minor where reasonable grounds connect the petitioner
records.text: Bail was refused where the victim supported the prosecution in her ss. 161 and 164 CrPC statements and a USB containing video of the act was secured. Reasonable grounds connected the petitioner to the offences, and punishment for rape of a minor attracts the prohibition in s. 497 CrPC. Ref: 2024 MLD 597; Shahbaz v. State.
records.title: Shahbaz v. State

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics Bail: Non-Association of Private Witnesses and Videography
records.heading: Failure to associate private witnesses in narcotics recoveries supports further inquiry and bail
records.text: Police in narcotics recoveries often neither associate private witnesses nor explain the omission, and should use modern devices and videography under Art. 164 QSO. The case was one of further inquiry, and bail was granted on tentative assessment although the offence was grave. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 652; Imdad Ullah v. State.
records.title: Imdad Ullah v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Contradictions in Witness Evidence
records.heading: Minor contradictions and embellishments do not affect the core of the prosecution case
records.text: Minor contradictions, inconsistencies or insignificant embellishments, which may arise from lapse of memory or lapse of time, do not affect the core of the prosecution case and are no ground to reject its evidence. The prosecution proved its case. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 632; Sadoro Mirbahar v. State.
records.title: Sadoro Mirbahar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Supported by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Ocular account supported by a matching wound proves the prosecution case
records.text: The complainant and two injured eyewitnesses assigned the accused the role of firing at the deceased, and the postmortem found a matching wound. The defence version was not put to the prosecution witnesses in cross-examination. The prosecution proved its case. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 632; Sadoro Mirbahar v. State.
records.title: Sadoro Mirbahar v. State

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Element of Terrorism: Aerial Firing and Police Murder
records.heading: Aerial firing and murder of a police constable justified Anti-Terrorism Act charges
records.text: Terrorism was present as the accused and accomplices fired in the air, harassing the area and making people flee, and murdered a police constable, which justified charges under the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 632; Sadoro Mirbahar v. State.
records.title: Sadoro Mirbahar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Weapon With Rubbed Number
records.heading: A rubbed pistol number consistently noted shows the weapon recovered was the one examined
records.text: The pistol recovered from the accused had a rubbed number, noted consistently in the FIR, recovery memo and Forensic Science Laboratory report, showing the weapon recovered was the one the laboratory received. The recovery was relied upon. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 632; Sadoro Mirbahar v. State.
records.title: Sadoro Mirbahar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses: Reliance
records.heading: Relationship alone does not make a witness interested or discard trustworthy evidence
records.text: Mere relationship with the deceased does not discard otherwise trustworthy evidence where there is no ill will or enmity with the accused, and relationship alone does not make a witness interested. It was unlikely the complainant would free the real culprit and implicate innocents without reason. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 632; Sadoro Mirbahar v. State.
records.title: Sadoro Mirbahar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Pistol and Empties
records.heading: Sealed case property received sealed by the laboratory proves safe custody and transmission
records.text: The case property was sealed on the spot and the Forensic Science Laboratory noted the parcels were received sealed. Safe custody and transmission to the expert were not disputed by the defence, so the prosecution proved its case. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 632; Sadoro Mirbahar v. State.
records.title: Sadoro Mirbahar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Corroboration: Direct Evidence as Rule of Caution
records.heading: Natural direct evidence needs no corroboration beyond a rule of abundant caution
records.text: Direct evidence is material to decide the charge, and its failure suffices to hold the charge not proved. Where direct evidence is natural and confidence inspiring, independent corroboration is only a rule of abundant caution and not a mandatory rule. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 605; Kifayatullah v. State.
records.title: Kifayatullah v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested Witness: Intrinsic Value of Statement
records.heading: Belief in a witness depends on the intrinsic value of his statement
records.text: Belief in a witness depends on the intrinsic value of his statement. No universal rule requires an interested witness to be disbelieved or a disinterested one believed, as it depends on prudence and reasonableness. An illogical statement is not believed despite the witness's reputation. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 605; Kifayatullah v. State.
records.title: Kifayatullah v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Is Not Corroboration of Identity
records.heading: Medical evidence supports direct evidence but does not establish the accused's identity
records.text: Medical evidence supports or explains direct or circumstantial evidence, confirming matters such as the seat and nature of injury, cause of death and weapon used. It does not establish the identity of the accused and cannot corroborate his involvement. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 605; Kifayatullah v. State.
records.title: Kifayatullah v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Sole Eyewitness
records.heading: Conviction may rest on a single confidence inspiring eyewitness
records.text: The sole evidence of a material eyewitness suffices to establish guilt if confidence inspiring and trustworthy, as the law weighs quality rather than quantity of evidence. An accused may be convicted on one reliable eyewitness. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 605; Kifayatullah v. State.
records.title: Kifayatullah v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder in Court Premises: Independent Witnesses and CCTV
records.heading: Murder in court premises proved by eyewitnesses, pistol recovery, CCTV and admitted motive
records.text: The accused shot an under trial prisoner outside a courtroom in the sight of police officials and an independent prisoner, a pistol was recovered, CCTV footage showed the shooting, and he admitted the motive in his s. 342 CrPC statement. The prosecution proved its case and the judgment was upheld. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 605; Kifayatullah v. State.
records.title: Kifayatullah v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 78 QSO: Disputed Documents Through Counsel
records.heading: Disputed documents cannot be proved through counsel's statement under Article 78 QSO
records.text: Art. 78 QSO lays down the mode of proving execution of a document, and a document brought on record without following it is inadmissible. Disputed documents cannot be tendered through counsel's statement, as the opposing party is then deprived of cross-examination on authenticity. Such papers were mere stray papers. Ref: 2024 LHC 1349; Khawaja Javed Mehmood v. PSIC Rawalpindi etc (Civil Revision 33-22, decided 21.03.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Khawaja Javed Mehmood v. PSIC Rawalpindi etc (Civil Revision 33-22, decided 21.03.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Postmortem Report: Doctor Must Prove Contents
records.heading: A postmortem report's contents cannot be read unless the doctor verifies them
records.text: A postmortem report is expert opinion, and its contents cannot be read unless the doctor appears to verify it. Where he is unavailable, secondary evidence may be given through a person who saw it prepared, knows his handwriting, another doctor or hospital record keeper. Under Art. 78 QSO, proof of execution does not prove the truth of contents. Ref: 2024 LHC 1366; Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22, decided 18.03.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22, decided 18.03.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Marriage With Sister of Wife: Criminal Liability
records.heading: Marrying two sisters concurrently attracts tazir; most Hanafi jurists impose no hadd
records.text: The judgment addresses marrying two real sisters concurrently and marrying a divorced wife's sister during her iddat. On criminal liability, most Hanafi jurists hold that hadd is not imposed, but they are unanimous that the matter is serious and tazir must be inflicted. Ref: Musawar Hussain v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 67328/B/2023).
records.title: Musawar Hussain v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 67328/B/2023)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Conviction of Advocate: Six Months
records.heading: Advocate convicted of wilful contempt of court and sentenced to six months
records.text: The Chief Justice found, after considering the oral and documentary evidence, that the respondent advocate had committed wilful contempt of the court of a Judge under ss. 3 and 11 of the Contempt of Court Ordinance 2003 read with Art. 204 of the Constitution. He was convicted under s. 5 and sentenced to six months simple imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 100,000, and taken into custody. Recording and circulation of video of the incident in the court room was referred to FIA Lahore for inquiry. Ref: The State v. Zahid Mehmood Goraya, Advocate (Crl. Org. (Suo Moto) No. 20741-W of 2024, decided 08.04.2024); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: The State v. Zahid Mehmood Goraya, Advocate (Crl. Org. (Suo Moto) No. 20741-W of 2024, decided 08.04.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Voice Record
records.heading: Call Data Record without voice recording is not relevant to prove prosecution case
records.text: Production of the Call Data Record alone, without voice recording, transcript or conversation details, was not relevant to prove any fact supporting the prosecution case in a murder charge. Ref: 2022 YLR 1702; Mohsin Abbas v. State.
records.title: Mohsin Abbas v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 265-C and 265-E CrPC: Disclosure of Prosecution Case
records.heading: Prosecution must disclose its case under section 265-C at least seven days before trial
records.text: The prosecution must disclose its case and the court must supply relevant documents, including witness statements, free of cost at least seven days before trial begins. The accused need not disclose his defence at the initial stage, since s. 265-E CrPC requires him only to be asked at charge whether he is guilty or has a defence. Ref: 2020 MLD 62; Muhammad Tanveer v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Tanveer v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Blasphemous SMS: CDR, Handset and Confession
records.heading: Blasphemous SMS conviction fails without proof of handset use and authorship
records.text: Conviction required proof that the handset used to send the SMS belonged to or was used by the accused and that he authored the texts. The CDR was not obtained through prescribed channels, and the confession was hit by Art. 38 QSO and recorded in English. Prosecution failed, the judgment was set aside and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2021 MLD 1415; Shafqat Masih v. State.
records.title: Shafqat Masih v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Call Data Record: Scope and Limits
records.heading: A Call Data Record alone is not conclusive proof of the accused's involvement
records.text: In a murder case, a Call Data Record showing only caller and recipient numbers, location and duration of calls, with no evidence of the conversation, is not conclusive proof of involvement of the accused. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt, the appeal was allowed and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2023 YLR 901; Syed Ali Akbar v. The State.
records.title: Syed Ali Akbar v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Call Data Record: Evidentiary Value
records.heading: A Call Data Record is not conclusive proof of involvement in the crime
records.text: A CDR shows only caller and recipient numbers, location and duration, and is not conclusive proof of involvement in the crime. Where the registered owner of the SIM was not established, no voice transcript was produced and the document lacked attestation, the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 917; Akbar alias Mohsin v. State.
records.title: Akbar alias Mohsin v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: CCTV Footage Not Sent to Forensic Agency
records.heading: CCTV footage not sent for forensic opinion on authenticity is inconsequential
records.text: CCTV footage on CD and USB seized from the Bank Manager was discarded by the Trial Court as inconsequential because the Investigating Officer did not send it to the Forensic Science Agency for an expert opinion on authenticity. The prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: 2023 YLR 1691; Zeeshan Iftikhar alias Shani v. State.
records.title: Zeeshan Iftikhar alias Shani v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: CCTV Footage as Evidence: Art. 164 QSO
records.heading: CCTV footage with the ocular account is reliable evidence under Article 164 QSO
records.text: CCTV footage secured through USB on the trial court's order, together with the ocular account, was reliable, confidence inspiring and trustworthy under Art. 164 QSO. The accused was convicted under s. 302(c) PPC instead of s. 302(b), reducing the sentence. Ref: 2022 YLR 901; Raja Fahad v. State.
records.title: Raja Fahad v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: CCTV Footage Not Proved: Inconclusive Forensic Report
records.heading: Unproved CCTV footage and an inconclusive forensic comparison are of no avail to the prosecution
records.text: The petrol pump owner who produced the CCTV footage was neither joined in investigation nor produced at trial, and the footage was not played for identification. The forensic comparison was inconclusive, so the footage was of no avail to the prosecution. Ref: 2023 YLR Note 82; Muhammd Safdar v. State.
records.title: Muhammd Safdar v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Unproved CCTV Footage
records.heading: CCTV footage is not gospel truth until proved at trial, supporting pre-arrest bail
records.text: CCTV footage is not the gospel truth unless its veracity, contents and timing are proved at trial, and the complainant must prove it was not tampered with. Two differing forensic reports raised doubt, so involvement needed further probe under s. 497(2) CrPC and ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 569; Arjamand Shahzadi v. State.
records.title: Arjamand Shahzadi v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of CCTV Footage: Gaps in Shopkeeper's Evidence
records.heading: Vague shopkeeper evidence weakens the recovery of CCTV footage in a murder case
records.text: In a murder of a minor after abduction, the shopkeeper's evidence on the CCTV recording was vague, as he did not name the person who checked the cameras and took his USB, nor state that police were present. The judgment examines these deficiencies in the recovery of the footage. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8; Muhammad Arshad alias Accha v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Arshad alias Accha v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Call Data Record of Deceased Not Produced
records.heading: Failure to produce Call Data Record of the deceased's call weakened the prosecution case
records.text: In a murder trial, the complainant did not give the mobile numbers involved nor produce Call Data Record to prove the deceased's call that took the witnesses to the scene. The Investigating Officer collected no such evidence and the phone was never produced. These gaps weakened the prosecution case. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 463; Muhammad Arslan v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Arslan v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Availability of Call Data Record
records.heading: Call Data Record is the best evidence of an alleged call to the deceased
records.text: Where the prosecution alleged that a co-accused called the deceased, the Call Data Record was the best evidence and its absence was a further difficulty for the prosecution. The co-accused who made the call had been acquitted, which destroyed the basic story and undermined the conviction of the accused. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 83; Tahir v. State.
records.title: Tahir v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Call Data Record for Defence
records.heading: Trial court erred in refusing to summon Call Data Record sought for defence
records.text: In a narcotics case entailing a capital sentence, the accused must get every chance to defend himself. The Trial Court erred in refusing to summon the Call Data Record of the personal mobile numbers of the raiding party witnesses. The High Court directed the Trial Court to summon the record. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 59; Muhammad Asif Ali Usama v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Asif Ali Usama v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Availability of Call Data Record in Ransom Case
records.heading: Absence of Call Data Record and unverified ownership led to acquittal under section 365-A PPC
records.text: In a case of kidnapping for ransom and murder, no Call Data Record of the accused's phone was collected and its ownership was not verified. Given this deficiency of evidence, the Trial Court acquitted the accused of the offence under s. 365-A PPC. Ref: 2022 YLR Note 39; Muhammad Ejaz v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Ejaz v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Failure to Produce Deceased's Mobile Phone
records.heading: Failure to produce the deceased's phone or its Call Data Record caused prosecution failure
records.text: The deceased allegedly received a call that took him to the scene, but his phone was not taken by the Investigating Officer, produced by witnesses, found by the doctors or at the scene, and no Call Data Record was collected. Failure to produce the phone had repercussions resulting in failure of the prosecution case. Ref: 2021 YLR Note 161; Muhammad Hanif v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Phone and SIM Without Call Record
records.heading: Recovered phone and SIMs prove no relevant fact without call records
records.text: In a suicide blast case, no voice call record or transcript was brought on record for the recovered mobile phone and SIM cards. The Investigating Officer admitted obtaining no record of where calls were made or received. Mere recovery of the phone and SIMs proved no relevant fact. Ref: 2021 YLR Note 88; Qari Ahmed Khan v. State.
records.title: Qari Ahmed Khan v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Voice Record
records.heading: Call Data Record without voice record or transcript is not relevant to prove a fact
records.text: Production of Call Data Record without any voice record or transcript, and without disclosure of the conversations, was not relevant to prove any fact supporting the prosecution. Doubt arose in the prosecution case and its benefit went to the accused. Ref: 2021 YLR Note 71; Muhammad Imran v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Voice Transcript
records.heading: Bare production of Call Data Record without conversation details is not relevant against the accused
records.text: A constable produced the Call Data Record of the deceased and the accused, but no voice record or transcript was on record. Bare production of the record without the details of conversations was not relevant to prove any fact against the accused, and the resulting doubt benefited him. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ Note 70; Muhammad Faidous Raza v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Faidous Raza v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Call Data Record Without Transcript
records.heading: Call Data Record without voice transcript gives no ground to cancel a wife's bail
records.text: Petition under s. 497(5) CrPC for cancellation of post-arrest bail of a wife accused of colluding in her husband's murder. Delayed and unnatural witness statements on extra-judicial confession and a Call Data Record without voice transcript were of no avail. No reason existed to set aside the bail order. Ref: 2020 MLD 1896; Muhammad Asif Javed v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Asif Javed v. State

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Call Data Record: Ownership of SIMs Not Proved
records.heading: Call Data Record without proof of SIM ownership cannot establish telephonic communication with the accused
records.text: In an extortion case, the prosecution did not prove ownership or registration of the numbers, nor link the recovered phones to the SIM cards. Mere availability of Call Data Record without a link between the numbers and the accused could not establish telephonic communication. The offence under s. 25-D Telegraph Act 1885 was not attracted. Ref: 2021 YLR Note 54; Muhammad Ilyas Mughal v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Ilyas Mughal v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Failure to Collect Call Data Record
records.heading: Failure to collect Call Data Record to support an alleged luring call weakens the prosecution
records.text: The complainant said the deceased was lured by a call from a lady co-accused, yet no phone numbers appeared in the FIR or evidence and the police collected no Call Data Record to support the story. With this and other circumstances, the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2021 YLR Note 67; Syed Saqlain Shah v. State.
records.title: Syed Saqlain Shah v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record: Cellular Company Official Not Examined
records.heading: Call Data Record adds nothing where the cellular company official is not examined
records.text: Call Data Record added nothing where the concerned official of the cellular company was not produced, the record bore no sign or stamp of the issuing authority and did not name the deceased or appellants. It was neither substantive nor corroborative evidence and served only to locate the mobile. Ref: 2020 YLR 195; Gohar Khan v. State.
records.title: Gohar Khan v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Authorised Signature
records.heading: A Call Data Record lacking an authorised signature cannot be safely relied upon
records.text: A Call Data Record lacking the signature of an authorised officer of the company could not be safely relied upon, and it was doubtful whether the Investigating Officer generated it himself. There was no transcript or proof of SIM issuance in the accused's name, and the car recovery had no nexus with the accused. Ref: 2018 YLR 2363; Kaleem Ullah v. State.
records.title: Kaleem Ullah v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Not Proved in Accordance with Law
records.heading: A Call Data Record not proved in accordance with law is inadmissible
records.text: The Call Data Record on record did not connect the accused with the crime and was inadmissible and not proved in accordance with law. The prosecution conceded it would not rely on it, as no mobile phone of the deceased was recovered. Ref: 2020 YLR Note 102; Zahid Hussain v. State.
records.title: Zahid Hussain v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CDRs as Computer Generated Documents: Proof
records.heading: Unsigned, unstamped computer generated CDRs not issued by the cellular company cannot be believed
records.text: CDRs that were computer generated and neither issued nor endorsed by the cellular company, bearing no signature, stamp or seal and not even naming the company, could not be believed. The prosecution could have proved them by examining an official or representative of the company but did not. Ref: 2018 MLD 1573; Tariq Hussain etc v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 08-I of 2018).
records.title: Tariq Hussain etc v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 08-I of 2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Evidentiary Value of Call Detail Record Data
records.heading: Call Detail Record data without call transcripts or audio is not worthy of reliance
records.text: Mere production of CDR data without call transcripts or end to end audio recording is not worthy of reliance as evidence. It must also be established that the callers at both ends were the persons whose call data is used. Courts must take extra care because such data can easily be edited. Ref: 2021 SCMR 522; Mian Khalid Perviz v. State.
records.title: Mian Khalid Perviz v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Call Detail Record for Defence
records.heading: Accused may use in defence the same Call Detail Record the prosecution relies on
records.text: Where the prosecution relied on Call Detail Record to connect the accused with a ransom kidnapping, the accused had equal right to use the same record in defence. The Trial Court could not summarily dismiss an application under s. 540 CrPC. The Anti-Terrorism Court order was set aside and the record was to be summoned. Ref: 2016 PCrLJ Note 77; Abdul Razzaq v. State.
records.title: Abdul Razzaq v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C CrPC: Supply of Videos and Documents to Accused
records.heading: Copies of video material must be supplied to the accused under section 265-C CrPC
records.text: No copy of the DVD or CD was supplied to the accused and the material was not shown during witness examination. After the proviso to Art. 164 QSO, s. 265-C CrPC cannot be read in isolation and courts must supply copies of such material at the relevant stage. Supply of copies of evidence is a valuable right. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 92; Usman Ali v. State.
records.title: Usman Ali v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C: Statement Recorded in Case Diary
records.heading: A witness statement recorded in the case diary must also be supplied under section 265-C
records.text: Where the police officer does not record a witness statement as required by s. 161 CrPC but writes it in the diary under s. 172 CrPC, a copy of it should also be given to the accused under s. 265-C CrPC. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 92; Usman Ali v. State.
records.title: Usman Ali v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C: Statutory Right to Witness Statements
records.heading: Accused has a statutory right to all witness statements, and omission vitiates the trial
records.text: The accused has a statutory right under s. 265-C CrPC to the statements of all witnesses recorded under ss. 161 and 164 CrPC. Omission to comply vitiates the whole trial, since the accused cannot set up his defence without the record. Ref: 2017 YLR 1999; Muhammad Tariq v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Tariq v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C: Purpose and Seven Day Period in ATA Trials
records.heading: Seven day period under section 265-C does not apply to Anti-Terrorism Special Courts
records.text: The purpose of s. 265-C CrPC is to let the accused know the prosecution case and meet the allegations. The seven day period does not apply to Anti-Terrorism Act Special Courts, but the accused must still get proper opportunity to prepare his defence under Art. 10-A of the Constitution. Ref: 2022 PCrLJ 421; Malik Zafar Iqbal v. State.
records.title: Malik Zafar Iqbal v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Confronting Witness with s. 161 Statement on Denial
records.heading: Defence cannot be barred from confronting a witness who denies his section 161 statement
records.text: Where a witness denied making a statement to the police, the Trial Court wrongly barred the defence from confronting him with it. Statements under s. 161 CrPC and their use under s. 162 CrPC are safeguards against surprise. Denial merely places an onus on the defence to prove the statement through the Investigating Officer. Ref: 2017 YLR Note 286; Asghar Ali Ramay v. State.
records.title: Asghar Ali Ramay v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C: Object of Supplying Copies
records.heading: Non-supply of copies under section 265-C before framing of charge vitiates the trial
records.text: Copies under s. 265-C CrPC inform the accused of the charges so that he can answer at the framing of charge and defend himself. He has a statutory right to them before the charge is framed, even in a complaint case. Omission to supply them vitiates the whole trial. Ref: 2009 YLR 1007; Muhammad Siddique v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Siddique v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C: Statements of Uncited Witnesses
records.heading: Copies of section 161 statements of uncited witnesses must be supplied under section 265-C
records.text: Under s. 265-C(1)(c) CrPC the Trial Court must supply copies of statements of all witnesses recorded under s. 161 CrPC, whether or not cited in the calendar of witnesses. The dismissal of the accused's application was erroneous. Revision allowed and supply directed. Ref: 2006 YLR 1558; Nasir Khan v. State.
records.title: Nasir Khan v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Eye-Witnesses Produced at Trial Without s. 161 Statements
records.heading: Eye-witnesses without section 161 statements at a belated stage are excluded from consideration
records.text: Two eye-witnesses, daughters of the deceased, were produced at a belated stage, absent from the complaint and without s. 161 CrPC statements. Examination under s. 161 CrPC and supply of copies are fundamental safeguards that cannot be dispensed with, and their statements were excluded from consideration. Ref: 2015 YLR 2694; Nusrat Bibi v. State.
records.title: Nusrat Bibi v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supplementary Statement and the FIR
records.heading: A supplementary statement is not a continuation or expansion of the FIR
records.text: A supplementary statement is neither a continuation of the FIR nor can it be read in expansion of it. The use of a statement under s. 161 CrPC is controlled by s. 162 CrPC, and a written supplementary statement cannot be admitted in evidence. Ref: 2015 YLR 2694; Nusrat Bibi v. State.
records.title: Nusrat Bibi v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Improvements by Witness: Ss. 161 and 162 CrPC
records.heading: Material dishonest improvements by a witness may lead to his statement being discarded
records.text: Where a prosecution witness deviates from his earlier statement and is duly confronted under Art. 153 QSO and s. 162 CrPC, the statements may be thrown out of consideration if material, dishonest or crafty improvements were made. Ref: 2014 YLR 201; Syed Ghulam Abbas Bokhari v. Raja Mushtaq Ahmad.
records.title: Syed Ghulam Abbas Bokhari v. Raja Mushtaq Ahmad

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Complainant's Application as s. 161 Statement
