records.heading: A complainant's application after the FIR may be treated as a section 161 statement
records.text: An application given by the complainant to the Investigating Officer after the FIR can be treated as a statement under s. 161 CrPC, usable only for contradiction under s. 162 CrPC. The Trial Court could not exhibit it and its order doing so was set aside. Ref: 2008 YLR 1092; Naseer Haider v. State.
records.title: Naseer Haider v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Object and Purpose of S. 162 CrPC
records.heading: Section 162 CrPC allows police statements only to contradict a witness, not to corroborate
records.text: Section 162 CrPC protects the accused against use of police statements at trial. They may be used only to contradict a witness under Art. 140 QSO and not for corroboration. Art. 140 is controlled by s. 162 and its prohibition cannot be defeated. Evidence where the prosecution used such a statement is inadmissible. Ref: 2005 MLD 1470; Shaukat Ali v. State.
records.title: Shaukat Ali v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Confrontation with Previous Statement Disallowed
records.heading: Barring confrontation of a witness with his previous statement is an incurable illegality
records.text: A witness's denial of a previous statement is no ground for barring cross-examination on it. The defence may lead evidence of the statement through the police officer who recorded it. Disallowing confrontation was an incurable illegality and procedural unfairness warranting quashing of the conviction. Ref: 2002 YLR 220; Muhammad Akhtar v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Akhtar v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Confronting Accused Witness with First Version
records.heading: An accused testifying on oath may be cross-examined on his first version to police
records.text: An accused who testifies on oath under s. 340(2) CrPC is a witness and may be cross-examined on his earlier version given to police, relying on the first proviso to s. 162 CrPC and Art. 140 QSO. The Trial Court was directed to supply the version and recall him for confrontation. Ref: 2001 PCrLJ 698; Sarfraz Talib v. Abdul Waheed.
records.title: Sarfraz Talib v. Abdul Waheed

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Meaning of Any Person in Ss. 160 to 162 CrPC
records.heading: Any person in sections 160 to 162 CrPC includes accused persons and suspects
records.text: The expression any person in ss. 160, 161 and 162 CrPC includes persons who are or ultimately are found to be accused and suspects. Interrogating an accused and recording his version aims at acquiring true facts, and the accused may place his own oral and documentary material before the Investigating Officer. Ref: 1999 PCrLJ 1198; Maqbool Ahmed v. Station House Officer, Police Station Changa Manga, District Kasur.
records.title: Maqbool Ahmed v. Station House Officer, Police Station Changa Manga, District Kasur

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Witness Denying s. 161 Statement
records.heading: A witness denying his section 161 statement makes his credibility doubtful
records.text: The accused may confront a witness with his s. 161 CrPC statement. A witness who denies making a statement before the police tries to deprive the accused of this right, which makes his credibility doubtful. He may be presumed not to have seen the occurrence or to have had nothing to say, unless rebutted by the record. Ref: PLD 1996 Lahore 286; Sajjad Hussain v. The State.
records.title: Sajjad Hussain v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Statements in Zimnies as s. 161 Statements
records.heading: Statements recorded in Zimnies or the Diary are section 161 statements to be supplied
records.text: Witness statements recorded in the Zimnies, in detail or gist, or in the body of the Diary are to be treated as statements under s. 161 CrPC. The accused may demand copies subject to s. 162 CrPC. The Sessions Court order for supply was upheld. Ref: PLD 1996 Lahore 277; Nazar Muhammad v. Mushtaq Ahmed.
records.title: Nazar Muhammad v. Mushtaq Ahmed

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supply of Police Diary Statements to Accused
records.heading: Accused is entitled to all investigation material, subject to section 162, before trial begins
records.text: The accused, presumed innocent and entitled to equal protection of law, is entitled to all material collected against him or in his favour in investigation before trial begins, subject to s. 162 CrPC. The Trial Court was directed to supply copies of the statements of five persons recorded in the police diary. Ref: PLD 1995 Lahore 632; Muhammad Aslam v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Judgment Against Advocate; Bar Appearances
records.heading: Contempt lies between the Court and contemnor, so only three advocates could appear
records.text: Judgment in contempt proceedings against an advocate, described in the headline as imposing a sentence. The Court observed that contempt lies between the Court and the contemnor, so only three advocates were allowed to appear for the respondent, as mass appearances by Bar office bearers create an impression of pressure. Ref: 2024 LHC 1450; The State v. Zahid Mehmood Goraya (Advocate) (Criminal Original 20741/24, decided 08.04.2024).
records.title: The State v. Zahid Mehmood Goraya (Advocate) (Criminal Original 20741/24, decided 08.04.2024)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Child Victim Testimony and Hearsay in Sexual Abuse Cases
records.heading: Absence of corroboration does not automatically discredit a child victim of sexual abuse
records.text: Absence of corroboration does not automatically discredit a child victim of sexual abuse, since age, demeanour and unlikelihood of tutoring may make it unnecessary. Abuse may be penetrative or non-penetrative, and the latter carries a higher risk of false accusation. Hearsay under the tender years exception may only corroborate the child's court testimony. Ref: 2024 LHC 1462; Imdad Ullah v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 448-22, decided 15.01.2024); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Imdad Ullah v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 448-22, decided 15.01.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 476 CrPC: Limits on Complaint Procedure
records.heading: Section 476 CrPC must not be used to settle personal scores
records.text: Section 476 CrPC is meant to keep the course of justice free of impurities in respect of offences under s. 195(1)(b) or (c) CrPC. Before proceeding, the court must see that the complaint makes out such an offence. The provision must not be used to wreak private vengeance or settle personal scores, and process is not to be issued as a matter of routine on every application of a litigant. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 786, PLJ 2023 Lah 161; Mehmood Ahmad v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (W.P. No. 73916/2022).
records.title: Mehmood Ahmad v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (W.P. No. 73916/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eye Witnesses
records.heading: Eye witnesses standing by as silent spectators while injuries were inflicted acted unnaturally
records.text: Where the accused were armed only with dandas and the eye witnesses stood by as silent spectators while 17 injuries were inflicted, without trying to rescue the deceased or apprehend the accused, their conduct was held highly unnatural. This showed that they were not present at the spot at the relevant time. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 696; Rafaqat Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 36587 of 2019).
records.title: Rafaqat Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 36587 of 2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Refusal to Register FIR: Alternative Remedies
records.heading: Writ is undesirable where remedies for refusal to register an FIR were not fully used
records.text: Where police refuse to register an FIR, the aggrieved party may approach the Sessions Judge as Ex-Officio Justice of Peace under s. 22-A(6) CrPC, the Magistrate under s. 156(3) CrPC, or file a direct complaint under s. 200 CrPC. Where the petitioner used only the first remedy and did not avail the other two, invoking writ jurisdiction despite an adequate remedy was held not desirable. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 786, PLJ 2023 Lah 161; Mehmood Ahmad v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (W.P. No. 73916/2022).
records.title: Mehmood Ahmad v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (W.P. No. 73916/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Accused's Statement: Inculpatory and Exculpatory Parts
records.heading: Inculpatory part of an accused's statement cannot be accepted while rejecting the exculpatory part
records.text: It is the first duty of the prosecution to prove its case. If it fails, the statement of the accused must be accepted or rejected in toto. It is legally not permissible to accept the inculpatory part of an accused's statement and reject the exculpatory part. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 696; Rafaqat Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 36587 of 2019).
records.title: Rafaqat Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 36587 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Postmortem: Eye Witnesses Not Present
records.heading: Postmortem delayed 10 hours 40 minutes suggests eye witnesses were not present
records.text: Postmortem examination conducted 10 hours and 40 minutes after the occurrence was held suggestive that the prosecution eye witnesses were not present at the spot. The delay was taken to have been consumed in procuring the attendance of fake eye witnesses. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 696; Rafaqat Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 36587 of 2019).
records.title: Rafaqat Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 36587 of 2019)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 337-H(1) PPC: Criminal Negligence of Public Functionary
records.heading: Section 337-H(1) PPC requires gross negligence amounting to a criminal act or omission
records.text: A public functionary or organisation employee incurs criminal liability for negligence only where grossly negligent to a degree amounting to a criminal act or omission, and where the act causing injury is causa causans. Where a thunderstorm damaged an electricity pole and the feeder was shut down on learning of it, s. 337-H(1) PPC was not attracted. The petition was accepted and the Justice of Peace's order set aside. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 685; Muhammad Irfan etc. v. ASJ/Ex-officio Justice of Peace etc. (Writ Petition No. 46486/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan etc. v. ASJ/Ex-officio Justice of Peace etc. (Writ Petition No. 46486/2021)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Documents Before Justice of Peace
records.heading: In section 489-F cases cheque, return slip and notice normally suffice for registration
records.text: In s. 489-F PPC cases it is normally enough for the aggrieved person to produce the original cheque, the bank's return slip and a copy of the s. 30 Negotiable Instruments Act notice before the Justice of Peace seeking registration of an FIR. Stop payment or closure of account does not per se take a case outside s. 489-F, but on the facts it made hearing the other side imperative. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 756; Humair Yousaf v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 46941 of 2021).
records.title: Humair Yousaf v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 46941 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Justice of Peace: No Minitrial on Non-Registration
records.heading: A Justice of Peace cannot hold a minitrial on a complaint of non-registration
records.text: A Justice of Peace cannot conduct a minitrial when hearing a complaint of non-registration of a criminal case. A mandate to hold detailed inquiry into the veracity of allegations would militate against the scheme of the Code. Relying on Khizer Hayat's case, proceedings before the Justice of Peace are summary and need not be treated as regular lis with elaborate orders resembling a judgment. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 756; Humair Yousaf v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 46941 of 2021).
records.title: Humair Yousaf v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 46941 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A(6) CrPC: Hearing the Accused
records.heading: Justice of Peace has no absolute duty to hear the accused under section 22-A(6)
records.text: A Justice of Peace does not have an absolute duty to hear the accused when deciding an application under s. 22-A(6) CrPC. He may afford audience only if the circumstances demand, and no hard and fast rule can be laid down in that respect. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 756; Humair Yousaf v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 46941 of 2021).
records.title: Humair Yousaf v. Station House Officer etc. (Writ Petition No. 46941 of 2021)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 365-A PPC: Ransom Required, Not Sexual Demand
records.heading: Section 365-A PPC requires a ransom demand and does not cover a sexual demand
records.text: Abduction and demand of ransom for release, whether of property, cash or otherwise, must be present to attract s. 365-A PPC. Where no ransom was demanded, the words any other demand could not be stretched to cover compelling a woman to sexual intercourse, which falls under ss. 365-B and 376 PPC. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 671, PLJ 2022 CrC 1411; Mansab Ali v. The State (Crl. Revision No. 17417/2022).
records.title: Mansab Ali v. The State (Crl. Revision No. 17417/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Territorial Jurisdiction When Wife Resides Abroad
records.heading: A wife abroad with regular visits and links to Pakistan is within the Rule 6 proviso
records.text: Under Rule 6 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Rules 1965, the word ordinarily in the proviso differs in meaning from permanent residence. The proviso relaxes the territorial rule in favour of a wife suing for dissolution of marriage, and a wife living in the USA who regularly visits and has links with Pakistan was held within it. Ref: 2024 SCMR 634; Sohail Ahmed v. Mst. Samreena Rasheed Memon & others (C.P. 488-K/2023).
records.title: Sohail Ahmed v. Mst. Samreena Rasheed Memon & others (C.P. 488-K/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift by Attorney Without Principal's Consent
records.heading: A gift by a general attorney needs the principal's express permission to be valid
records.text: A gift of the principal's property made by his general attorney, with no proof that the attorney sought the principal's permission or consent, was not validated. Love and affection as consideration must proceed from the real owner, and an attorney may gift only on the principal's express permission and instructions. The concurrent findings were upheld. Ref: 2024 SCMR 734, PLD 2024 SC 373; Babar Anwar v. Muhammad Ashraf and another (C.P.L.A. 5972/2021).
records.title: Babar Anwar v. Muhammad Ashraf and another (C.P.L.A. 5972/2021)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Pre-requisites of a Valid Gift Under Muslim Law
records.heading: A valid gift under Muslim law requires tender, acceptance and possession
records.text: The donor must be of sound mind, of age, owner of the property and free from coercion, and the thing gifted must exist and be lawful. The constituents of a valid gift are tender, acceptance and possession. The donor must divest himself of ownership, state his intention unambiguously and deliver possession. Ref: 2024 SCMR 734, PLD 2024 SC 373; Babar Anwar v. Muhammad Ashraf and another (C.P.L.A. 5972/2021).
records.title: Babar Anwar v. Muhammad Ashraf and another (C.P.L.A. 5972/2021)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Identification Parade, Expeditious Justice and Frivolous Litigation
records.heading: Court stressed the State's duty to ensure expeditious justice and curb frivolous litigation
records.text: Petition against acquittal under the Anti-Terrorism Act resting on an identification parade and recovery. The Court stressed the State's duty under Art. 37(d) of the Constitution to ensure expeditious justice and the judges' duty to protect fundamental rights. Government should curb false and frivolous litigation, and courts should use existing powers to discourage it. Ref: 2024 SCMR 757; Mehboob Hassan v. Akhtar Islam, etc (Crl.P. 235-L/2015).
records.title: Mehboob Hassan v. Akhtar Islam, etc (Crl.P. 235-L/2015)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Civil and Criminal Proceedings on Same Subject: Stay
records.heading: Criminal proceedings must stop where criminal liability depends on the fate of civil lis
records.text: Where the ultimate criminal liability depends on the fate of the civil lis, the criminal proceedings are, by operation of law, required to be stopped. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 786; Mehmood Ahmad v. Additional Sessions Judge (W.P. 73916 of 2022).
records.title: Mehmood Ahmad v. Additional Sessions Judge (W.P. 73916 of 2022)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Pauper Counsel: Duty to Prepare or Seek Adjournment
records.heading: Counsel accepting a dock-brief must prepare the case or seek an adjournment
records.text: Counsel who accepts a dock-brief for a state-paid fee and undertakes to defend a prisoner without trying to know anything about the case offends against the tradition of the profession. If not ready, it is his duty to ask for time and, if necessary, adjournment. Unseemly hurry makes defence in important cases impossible and is likely to affect the result of the trial. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 772; Munir Ahmed v. State.
records.title: Munir Ahmed v. State

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare of Child Paramount
records.heading: Welfare of the child is paramount in deciding custody between mother and father
records.text: The father is natural guardian, while the mother has custody of a male child to seven years and a female child to puberty, and this continues after divorce. The mother's financial inability does not deprive her of custody, and the father's duty to maintain remains. These rules are not absolute and the welfare of the child is paramount. The headline states that remarriage alone does not forfeit the mother's custody. Ref: Shaista Habib v. Muhammad Arif Habib and others (C.P.L.A. 3801/2022, decided 06.03.2023); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Shaista Habib v. Muhammad Arif Habib and others (C.P.L.A. 3801/2022, decided 06.03.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Fabricated Injuries and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Fabricated injuries found by a Special Medical Board justify confirming pre-arrest bail
records.text: The FIR assigned a firearm injury to the petitioner, but the medico-legal report described a sharp cutting object and a Special Medical Board found the injuries fabricated. The Investigating Officer also found the petitioner not guilty. This created further inquiry and possible mala fide, so ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 805; Mir Muhammad v. State.
records.title: Mir Muhammad v. State

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Proclaimed Offender: Rejection of Nomination Papers
records.heading: A person cannot be treated as a proclaimed offender without proceedings under section 87
records.text: A person cannot be treated as a proclaimed offender without proceedings under s. 87 CrPC, and no proclamation was shown against the petitioner. The disadvantage of being a proclaimed offender ordinarily relates only to that case. Neither the Constitution nor s. 62(9) of the Elections Act lets Returning Officers reject nomination papers on this ground. Ref: 2024 SCMR 775; Tahir Sadiq v. Faisal Ali.
records.title: Tahir Sadiq v. Faisal Ali

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Police Promotion: Training Under Rule 19.25 Police Rules
records.heading: Training under Rule 19.25 Police Rules is mandatory for promotion of upper subordinates
records.text: For promotion of upper subordinates in the police, training under Rule 19.25 of the Police Rules 1934 is mandatory, and promotion takes effect once the requirement of law is fulfilled. The Court urged a culture of knowledge, skill and performance to reduce litigation over promotion. Ref: The Inspector General of Police, Punjab Lahore, etc v. Waris Ali, ASI, deceased through L.Rs, etc (C.A. 3-L/2016).
records.title: The Inspector General of Police, Punjab Lahore, etc v. Waris Ali, ASI, deceased through L.Rs, etc (C.A. 3-L/2016)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Court Not to Monitor Police Investigation
records.heading: Court does not monitor investigation absent mala fides, abuse of power or CrPC violation
records.text: Investigation is the responsibility of the police and the IO plays a vital and dominant role. It is not the duty of the court to monitor the investigation unless it appears mala fide, an abuse of power or in violation of the CrPC, so the court's intervention during investigation is restricted and limited. Ref: 2024 SCMR 805; Mir Muhammad v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 705/2023).
records.title: Mir Muhammad v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 705/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Principles and Grounds
records.heading: Authority on principles and grounds for grant of pre-arrest bail
records.text: Authority on the principles and grounds for grant of pre-arrest bail, which the judgment states. Ref: 2024 SCMR 805; Mir Muhammad v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 705/2023).
records.title: Mir Muhammad v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 705/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 265-C and 342 CrPC: Non-Supply and Non-Display of Video Evidence
records.heading: Authority on non-supply and non-display of video evidence; holding not stated
records.text: Authority on three points: non-supply of a copy of the DVD/CD to the appellant under s. 265-C CrPC, non-display of videos and photos during prosecution witnesses' statements, and non-display of them while examining the appellant under s. 342 CrPC. The holding is not stated in the post.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Commission: Recount After Declaration of Returned Candidate
records.heading: Authority on Election Commission jurisdiction to order recount after declaration; holding not stated
records.text: Authority on the jurisdiction of the Election Commission to order a recount after the declaration of the returned candidate. The holding is not stated in the post. Ref: 2024 LHC 1720; Abdul Rehman Kanju v. Rana Muhammad Faraz Noon etc. (ICA Election 29-24, decided 16.04.2024); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Abdul Rehman Kanju v. Rana Muhammad Faraz Noon etc. (ICA Election 29-24, decided 16.04.2024)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Negative DNA Report Not Fatal to Prosecution
records.heading: A negative DNA report does not defeat a prosecution case with compelling other evidence
records.text: A negative forensic or DNA report does not by itself defeat the prosecution case where other evidence is compelling, relying on Abdul Ghani v. The State (2022 SCMR 544). The conviction under s. 377 read with s. 511 PPC of a juvenile appellant was upheld, s. 377-A PPC not being alleged or proved. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2024 LHC 1706; Muhammad Saleem v. The State and another (Crl. A. 422/2023); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Saleem v. The State and another (Crl. A. 422/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Fuel Price Adjustment and Tariff Charges in Electricity Bills
records.heading: Fuel adjustment and tariff demands by an improperly constituted NEPRA declared illegal
records.text: Writ petitions disposed of declaring the demand of Fuel Price Adjustment, Quarter Tariff Adjustment and change of tariff from Industrial to Commercial by NEPRA, not constituted fully under s. 3 of the NEPRA Act 1997, illegal and coram non judice. Directions were issued to NEPRA and the Federal Government on billing, tariffs and subsidy. Ref: 2024 CLC 744; Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. 50725 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Federation of Pakistan etc (W.P. 50725 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Against Family Court Decree
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC may be invoked against a Family Court judgment and decree
records.text: Section 12(2) CPC can be invoked to challenge a judgment and decree passed by a Family Court under the Family Courts Act 1964. Ref: Fozia Mazhar v. Additional District Judge, Jhang, etc. (C.P.L.A. 1737-L/2020, decided 26.04.2024); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Fozia Mazhar v. Additional District Judge, Jhang, etc. (C.P.L.A. 1737-L/2020, decided 26.04.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Justice of Peace, Investigation and S. 561-A CrPC
records.heading: Authority on Justice of Peace powers, Investigating Officer duties and section 561-A; holdings not stated
records.text: Authority on the power and function of the Justice of Peace under s. 22-A CrPC, ss. 154, 155, 169 and 173 CrPC, the responsibilities of the Investigating Officer, and the jurisdiction of the High Court under s. 561-A CrPC. The holdings are not stated in the post. Ref: Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A. 99-K/2018).
records.title: Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A. 99-K/2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Conduct of Examination in Chief of Witness
records.heading: Public Prosecutor must conduct examination in chief following international best practices
records.text: The examination in chief of a witness is to be conducted by the Public Prosecutor, who is required to follow the pattern suggested by international best practices so as to help the witness recollect the facts. The story of a prosecution witness must be elicited through techniques including signposting and piggybacking. Ref: 2024 LHC 1817; Rao Hamayun Waqas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 10549/21).
records.title: Rao Hamayun Waqas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 10549/21)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Order to Deposit Balance Sale Consideration
records.heading: An order to deposit balance consideration without stated consequences does not prejudice the plaintiff
records.text: In a suit for specific performance, a discretionary order directing the plaintiff to deposit the balance consideration, without stating consequences of non-deposit, does not prejudice his rights when issues were framed and evidence was to follow. The High Court refused to interfere in revision. Ref: 2024 MLD 667; Ghulam Hussain v. Manzoor Hussain (Civil Revision 25657/19).
records.title: Ghulam Hussain v. Manzoor Hussain (Civil Revision 25657/19)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: MBBS Admission: Late Intimation and Art. 25-A
records.heading: Late intimation by a University deprived a qualified candidate of education under Article 25-A
records.text: Courts ordinarily keep their hands off internal affairs of educational institutions, but this is not a rule of universal application. A candidate who qualified MDCAT and was on the open merit list was deprived of education under Art. 25-A by the University's late intimation. The petition was allowed and admission to MBBS first year 2022-23 directed. Ref: 2024 MLD 638; Muhammad Usman Farooq v. RWP Medical University etc (W.P. 1132-23).
records.title: Muhammad Usman Farooq v. RWP Medical University etc (W.P. 1132-23)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale Mutation: S. 42(7) Land Revenue Act and Proof
records.heading: Mutation attested without the transferor's presence and identification violates section 42(7)
records.text: Under s. 42(7) of the Land Revenue Act 1967 the Revenue Officer must ensure the presence and identification of the transferor. A mutation is no document of title, and its beneficiary must prove the original transaction. The mutations were attested in violation of s. 42(7), the judgments below were set aside and the suit decreed. Ref: 2024 MLD 728; Muhammad Younis and others v. Mst. Dolat Bibi and others (Civil Revision 620 of 2014).
records.title: Muhammad Younis and others v. Mst. Dolat Bibi and others (Civil Revision 620 of 2014)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 95 Limitation Act: Fraud, Three Years from Knowledge
records.heading: Article 95 prescribes three years from knowledge for relief based on fraud
records.text: Under Art. 95 of the Limitation Act 1908, where relief is sought on an allegation of fraud, the limitation period is three years, computed from the date of knowledge. Ref: 2024 MLD 728; Muhammad Younis and others v. Mst. Dolat Bibi and others (Civil Revision 620 of 2014).
records.title: Muhammad Younis and others v. Mst. Dolat Bibi and others (Civil Revision 620 of 2014)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Re-allotment of Surrendered Land in Prohibited Zone
records.heading: Re-allotment of surrendered land in a prohibited zone is void ab initio
records.text: Under para 18(3) of MLR 115/1972, surrendered or resumed state land within the prohibited zone of a Municipal Committee can be neither allotted nor granted proprietary rights. Any such grant is void ab initio. The writ petition was allowed, re-allotments cancelled and Tawan to be recovered from occupants. Ref: 2024 MLD 756; Faiz Ahmad etc v. Chairman Federal Land Commission etc (254943/18).
records.title: Faiz Ahmad etc v. Chairman Federal Land Commission etc (254943/18)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Witnesses Spared Despite Motive Against Them
records.heading: Witnesses spared despite a motive against them suggests they did not see the occurrence
records.text: Where the motive was against the complainant or witnesses and the accused caused them no harm although they were within firing range, this shows the witnesses had not witnessed the occurrence. Ref: 2024 YLR 841; State v. Muhammad Sharif (Murder Reference 45-18).
records.title: State v. Muhammad Sharif (Murder Reference 45-18)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post-Mortem Examination
records.heading: Unexplained post-mortem delay shows the claimed eye-witnesses were absent
records.text: Inordinate, unexplained delay in the post-mortem examination and in sending police papers to the Medical Officer shows that the claimed eye-witnesses were absent, and the delay was used to procure their presence and build a false account, as repeatedly held by the Supreme Court. Ref: 2024 YLR 841; State v. Muhammad Sharif (Murder Reference 45-18).
records.title: State v. Muhammad Sharif (Murder Reference 45-18)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Burden of Proof and Particulars of Fraud in Pleadings
records.heading: Particulars of fraud must be pleaded and the asserted facts proved
records.text: Art. 117 QSO requires a person seeking judgment on a legal right dependent on asserted facts to prove them. O. VI R. 4 CPC requires particulars, with dates and items, to be stated in the pleadings where misrepresentation, fraud, breach of trust, default or undue influence is relied on. Ref: 2024 YLR 989; Roshan Iqbal v. Nazar Muhammad etc (Civil Revision 2584-14).
records.title: Roshan Iqbal v. Nazar Muhammad etc (Civil Revision 2584-14)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rupture of Hymen and Healing of Hymenal Injuries
records.heading: Authority on causes of hymen rupture and healing time; holding not stated
records.text: Authority on the causes of rupture of the hymen and the healing time of hymenal injuries. The holding is not stated in the post. Ref: 2024 LHC 1934; Amjad Ali v. The State etc. (Appeal 195087/18, decided 15.04.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Amjad Ali v. The State etc. (Appeal 195087/18, decided 15.04.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Examination-in-Chief: Signposting and Piggybacking
records.heading: Signposting and piggybacking are permissible techniques in examination-in-chief
records.text: Signposting and piggybacking are two techniques the prosecution may follow in examination-in-chief. Signposting alerts the witness to a particular part of his testimony and is permissible per international best practice, while piggybacking frames the next question using part of the previous answer. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1156; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Objection to Admissibility to Be Decided at Once
records.heading: An objection to admissibility must be decided at once, not at the end of trial
records.text: An objection by any party on the admissibility of evidence must be attended to and decided by the court then and there before proceeding. It should not be reserved for decision at the end of the trial. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1156; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Relevancy and Admissibility of Evidence
records.heading: Relevant evidence is usually admissible, subject to exclusionary rules based on policy
records.text: Relevant evidence is usually admissible, subject to exclusionary rules that rest on policy considerations. Admissibility depends on whether the law of evidence permits relevant evidence of a particular kind to be received. Hearsay, custodial confessions and previous bad character of the accused are excluded although relevant. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ 1156; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Suo Motu Case on Six Islamabad High Court Judges' Letter
records.heading: Supreme Court sought proposals on the institutional response to the six judges' letter
records.text: Written order of the first hearing of 3 April 2024. The Supreme Court sought proposals from the Pakistan Bar Council, Supreme Court Bar and Federation on the judiciary's institutional response. Justice Athar Minallah disagreed with paras 1 to 12 and said whether the Prime Minister may be summoned is for the full court. Ref: In the matter of letter dated 25th March 2024 of the Six Judges of the Islamabad High Court (S.M.C. 1/2024); Justice Athar Minallah; Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: In the matter of letter dated 25th March 2024 of the Six Judges of the Islamabad High Court (S.M.C. 1/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Case: Mere Apprehension of Bias
records.heading: Mere apprehension of bias is no ground for recusal or transfer of a case
records.text: Mere apprehension or bias is no ground to seek recusal of a Judge or transfer of a case, apart from personal interest as mentioned in s. 556 CrPC. Ref: 2024 LHC 1980; Mehmood v. The State etc (T.A. (Crl) 10-T-24, decided 29.04.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mehmood v. The State etc (T.A. (Crl) 10-T-24, decided 29.04.2024)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Sterling Witness: Evidence of Prosecutrix
records.heading: A victim of exceptional quality and credibility may be relied on without corroboration
records.text: Where witnesses are neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable, the court should seek the true genesis of the incident. A victim may be relied on as a sterling witness without corroboration if her quality and credibility are exceptionally high and her version is consistent throughout. An unreliable account marked by flaws makes conviction difficult. Ref: Nirmal Premkumar and Ors. v. State Rep. by Inspector of Police (Criminal Appeal No. 1098 of 2024, decided 11.03.2024).
records.title: Nirmal Premkumar and Ors. v. State Rep. by Inspector of Police (Criminal Appeal No. 1098 of 2024, decided 11.03.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Examination in Chief Without Accused's Advocate
records.heading: Recording examination in chief without the accused's advocate is illegal
records.text: Recording examination in chief of prosecution witnesses in the absence of the accused's advocate, without recording cross-examination, is illegal. The trial court should have provided a legal aid advocate, and the accused's advocate has a right to object to leading or irrelevant questions. Section 242(3) of the Indian Cr.PC is an exception. Ref: Ekene Godwin & Anr. v. State of Tamil Nadu (Criminal Appeal Nos. 1664-1665 of 2024, decided 18.03.2024).
records.title: Ekene Godwin & Anr. v. State of Tamil Nadu (Criminal Appeal Nos. 1664-1665 of 2024, decided 18.03.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Suo Motu on Letter of Six IHC Judges
records.heading: Seven member bench takes up six IHC judges' letter under Article 184(3)
records.text: Order of a seven-member bench taking up under Art. 184(3) the letter of six Islamabad High Court judges alleging interference in judicial work. It records the Attorney-General's account of the steps taken by the Government, including the inquiry commission and its head's recusal. A separate note by one judge recuses from the bench, citing restraint and the High Courts' own powers. Ref: In the matter of letter dated 25 March 2024 of the Six Judges of the Islamabad High Court (Suo Motu Case No. 1/2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Athar Minallah; Justice Musarrat Hilali; Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: In the matter of letter dated 25 March 2024 of the Six Judges of the Islamabad High Court (Suo Motu Case No. 1/2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Audio Leaks Case: Recusal Applications Held Mala Fide
records.heading: Recusal applications by PTA, FIA, IB and PEMRA held mala fide and dismissed with costs
records.text: The Islamabad High Court held the four applications by PTA, FIA, IB and PEMRA seeking recusal of the judge mala fide and dismissed them with Rs. 500,000 costs each. Preliminary contempt notices were issued to the DG IB, DG FIA and Chairman PTA. The Court said it was giving all parties full opportunity on phone tapping. Ref: Bushra Imran Khan v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior and Secretary Ministry of Defence & others (Writ Petition No. 2758/2023); Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Bushra Imran Khan v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Interior and Secretary Ministry of Defence & others (Writ Petition No. 2758/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Interference with Concurrent Findings
records.heading: Supreme Court does not ordinarily interfere with concurrent findings of fact and law
records.text: Where the courts below have made concurrent findings of fact and law, the Supreme Court ordinarily does not interfere unless exceptional circumstances warrant it. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 600; Khaleelullah & others v. Muhaim Khan & others (C.A. 25-Q/2018).
records.title: Khaleelullah & others v. Muhaim Khan & others (C.A. 25-Q/2018)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Cause of Action for Denial of Inheritance
records.heading: Cause of action for inheritance accrues on actual denial of the heir's share
records.text: The cause of action of an heir accrues when the co-sharer in possession actually denies or threatens to deny his share. Transfer to a third party by sale or gift is an actual denial, while a mere annotation in the revenue records is only a threatened or apprehended denial. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 600; Khaleelullah & others v. Muhaim Khan & others (C.A. 25-Q/2018).
records.title: Khaleelullah & others v. Muhaim Khan & others (C.A. 25-Q/2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Guardian in the Suit for Person of Unsound Mind
records.heading: Authority on guardian in suit for a person of unsound mind under Order XXXII
records.text: Authority on appointment of a guardian in the suit under Order XXXII CPC for a person of unsound mind and the scope of the Mental Health Ordinance 2001 in this regard. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 595; Malik Arshad Hussain Awan v. M/s United Bank Limited (C.P.L.A. 1393-L/2020).
records.title: Malik Arshad Hussain Awan v. M/s United Bank Limited (C.P.L.A. 1393-L/2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Appealability of Maintenance Decree: Per Head Amount
records.heading: Appealability of a maintenance decree is determined by maintenance per claimant
records.text: A Lahore High Court full bench of three judges held that appealability of a maintenance decree is determined by the maintenance per claimant. If the Family Court decrees Rs. 4,500 monthly for each of four claimants, no appeal lies even though the total is Rs. 18,000 monthly. Ref: PLD 2024 Lahore 300, PLJ 2024 Lahore 178; Muhammad Aslam v. Judge Family Court, Ferozewala, etc (Writ Petition No. 126306 of 2017).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. Judge Family Court, Ferozewala, etc (Writ Petition No. 126306 of 2017)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Pension Is Not Tarka
records.heading: A pension does not fall within the definition of tarka
records.text: A person's pension does not fall within the definition of tarka, as it is governed by the departmental pensionary rules of that department. Ref: PLD 2024 FSC 22; Noor Aisha v. Federation of Pakistan (Shariat Petition No. 06/I of 2023).
records.title: Noor Aisha v. Federation of Pakistan (Shariat Petition No. 06/I of 2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats: Proportional Representation, Leave Granted
records.heading: Leave granted on proportional representation for reserved seats for women and non-Muslims
records.text: Leave to appeal was granted to consider the meaning and scope of proportional representation for reserved seats for women and non-Muslims under Arts. 51(6)(d) and (e) and 106(2)(c). The headline reports that the decision allocating the Sunni Ittehad Council's reserved seats to other parties was suspended. Ref: Sunni Ittehad Council, Faisalabad and another v. Election Commission of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others (C.P.L.A. 1328/2024, decided 06.05.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Sunni Ittehad Council, Faisalabad and another v. Election Commission of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others (C.P.L.A. 1328/2024, decided 06.05.2024)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Court's Duty to Consider Limitation Under S. 3
records.heading: Trial and appellate courts must decide limitation under section 3 even if unraised
records.text: Even if no party raises limitation, the trial court and appellate court must consider and decide it under s. 3 of the Limitation Act. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 600; Khaleelullah & others v. Muhaim Khan & others (C.A. 25-Q of 2018).
records.title: Khaleelullah & others v. Muhaim Khan & others (C.A. 25-Q of 2018)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Issues: Territorial Jurisdiction and S. 9 Special Court Act
records.heading: Authority on writ jurisdiction issues and section 9 Special Court Act; no holding stated
records.text: Authority on issues listed as territorial jurisdiction of the Lahore High Court, alternate adequate remedy, decision on merits, relief granted that was not sought, constitutionality of s. 9 of the Special Court Act, misapplication of Mustafa Impex and violation of Supreme Court directions. The post gives no holding. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 610; Taufiq Asif v. General (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf (C.P.L.A. 3797/2020).
records.title: Taufiq Asif v. General (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf (C.P.L.A. 3797/2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence and Proof Beyond Reasonable Doubt
records.heading: The prosecution bears the whole burden and the presumption of innocence continues
records.text: The prosecution bears the whole burden of proof, and the accused need not refute its claims. Presumption of innocence remains until guilt is proved beyond reasonable doubt, and the two concepts are linked as a unit. Ref: Imtiaz Latif, etc v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1690-L/2016, decided 27.03.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Imtiaz Latif, etc v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1690-L/2016, decided 27.03.2024)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Kidnapping for Ransom Not Terrorism: Mens Rea
records.heading: Kidnapping for ransom is not terrorism where two fold mens rea is missing
records.text: Where the abductee was released on payment of ransom and the petitioners had no prior criminal history, the case did not meet the criteria for terrorism because the two fold mens rea was missing. Ref: Imtiaz Latif, etc v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1690-L/2016, decided 27.03.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Imtiaz Latif, etc v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1690-L/2016, decided 27.03.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Order of Appraisal: Prosecution Evidence and S. 342 Statement
records.heading: Court should assess prosecution evidence first, then the accused's statement and defence evidence
records.text: The court should first assess the prosecution evidence independently, then the statements under s. 342 and s. 340(2) CrPC and defence evidence. If prosecution evidence is disbelieved, the accused's statement is accepted as a whole, and an exculpatory statement leads to acquittal. With counter versions, a plea that might reasonably be true must be accepted. Ref: Muhammad Imtiaz Baig, etc v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1288-L/2017, decided 29.03.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Imtiaz Baig, etc v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1288-L/2017, decided 29.03.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXI R. 90 CPC: Setting Aside Execution Sale
records.heading: Setting aside an execution sale under Order XXI Rule 90 requires irregularity and substantial injury
records.text: O. XXI R. 90 CPC requires material irregularity or fraud, substantial injury to the applicant and deposit of twenty percent of the sum realised at the sale or security. O. XXI is an exhaustive scheme, and the Trial Court rightly treated the objections as falling under r. 90 and not r. 84. Ref: Tariq Zubair Khan v. Mst. Tabassum Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 4194/2023, decided 19.04.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Tariq Zubair Khan v. Mst. Tabassum Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 4194/2023, decided 19.04.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023: Dissent of Shahid Waheed
records.heading: Dissenting judgment of Justice Shahid Waheed on the Supreme Court Practice and Procedure Act
records.text: Authority comprising the dissenting judgment of Justice Shahid Waheed in the challenge to the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023. The post does not state the reasoning. Ref: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad and others (C.P. 6/2023, decided 07.05.2024); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad and others (C.P. 6/2023, decided 07.05.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023: Dissent of Ayesha A. Malik
records.heading: Dissenting judgment of Justice Ayesha A. Malik on the Supreme Court Practice and Procedure Act
records.text: Authority comprising the dissenting judgment of Justice Ayesha A. Malik in the challenge to the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act 2023. The post does not state the reasoning. Ref: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad and others (C.P. 6/2023, decided 07.05.2024); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Raja Amer Khan and another v. The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law and Justice Islamabad and others (C.P. 6/2023, decided 07.05.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Hizanat: Mother's Right to Custody of Minor
records.heading: Mother's preferential right of hizanat is not lost by waiver on one occasion
records.text: The mother has a preferential right of hizanat, distinct from the father's guardianship, and waiver on one occasion does not bind her in law. Custody of a minor under two years was regulated in favour of the mother by way of recovery order under Art. 199 of the Constitution, subject to final determination by the Guardian Court. Petition disposed of. Ref: 2024 LHC 2076; Sadia Aziz v. DPO etc. (W.P. 3109-H/2024, decided 02.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Sadia Aziz v. DPO etc. (W.P. 3109-H/2024, decided 02.05.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination of Investigating Officer on Case Diary
records.heading: Investigating Officer may be cross-examined on case diaries once he consults them
records.text: The Investigating Officer is no formal witness, and once he has consulted the police file to refresh his memory he is amenable to cross-examination. The defence may see the relevant portion of the case diaries and question on it. The Investigating Officer was ordered re-summoned for cross-examination. Ref: 2018 PCrLJ 553; Kalimullah v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 27-B of 2017).
records.title: Kalimullah v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 27-B of 2017)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 46 QSO: Statements of Dead Persons as Exceptions
records.heading: Article 46 QSO clauses are exceptions to the rule that oral evidence be direct
records.text: The clauses of Art. 46 QSO are exceptions to the rule that oral evidence must be direct, as the maker of the statement is not examined and safeguards of oath and cross-examination are absent. A dying declaration or confession under Art. 46(3) must be proved by the normal procedure before reliance. Ref: PLD 2003 Karachi 618; Kaka Kishanchand v. The State.
records.title: Kaka Kishanchand v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 155 QSO: Witness Refreshing Memory from Affidavit
records.heading: A witness may refresh his memory from his affidavit under Article 155 QSO
records.text: Under Art. 155(1) and (3) QSO a witness may refresh his memory from a document he executed or read, with court permission, whether his examination in chief is oral or based on an affidavit. Arts. 155 to 157 make no distinction between private and official witnesses. Ref: 2014 CLC 798.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry and Reasonable Grounds Under S. 497 CrPC
records.heading: Further inquiry is a tentative assessment creating doubt about the accused's involvement
records.text: Further inquiry is a tentative, exploratory assessment that may create doubt about the accused's involvement. The prosecution must show reasonable grounds, being tenable, admissible and appealing to a reasonable judicial mind, that the accused committed an offence within the prohibitory limb of s. 497 CrPC. The headline also refers to parity. Ref: Attaullah v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 35-K/2024, decided 04.04.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Attaullah v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 35-K/2024, decided 04.04.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 115 CPC: Scope of Revisional Jurisdiction
records.heading: Revisional jurisdiction under section 115 CPC corrects jurisdictional errors and irregular exercise
records.text: Under s. 115 CPC the revisional court examines jurisdictional errors, including exercise of jurisdiction not vested, failure to exercise jurisdiction vested, or illegal or materially irregular exercise. It may also act suo motu to ensure superintendence and correct errors free of technicalities. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 588; Haji Musharraf Mahmood Khan v. Sardarzada Zafar Abbas (CP No. 423-L of 2018).
records.title: Haji Musharraf Mahmood Khan v. Sardarzada Zafar Abbas (CP No. 423-L of 2018)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Court's Duty to Address Limitation Under S. 3
records.heading: Court must independently decide limitation under section 3 whether or not raised
records.text: The law of limitation bars enforcement of stale rights after a certain period and does not confer a right. Under s. 3 of the Limitation Act 1908 the court must independently consider and decide limitation as a primary duty, whether or not the other party raises it. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 588; Haji Musharraf Mahmood Khan v. Sardarzada Zafar Abbas (CP No. 423-L of 2018).
records.title: Haji Musharraf Mahmood Khan v. Sardarzada Zafar Abbas (CP No. 423-L of 2018)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Restoration of Revision Dismissed in Default: Art. 181
records.heading: Article 181 governs restoration of a revision dismissed for non-prosecution
records.text: Neither the CPC nor the Limitation Act gives a specific period for restoring a revision dismissed for non-prosecution. The residuary Art. 181 of the Limitation Act applies, allowing three years from when the right to apply accrues. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 588; Haji Musharraf Mahmood Khan v. Sardarzada Zafar Abbas (CP No. 423-L of 2018).
records.title: Haji Musharraf Mahmood Khan v. Sardarzada Zafar Abbas (CP No. 423-L of 2018)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Pre-requisites of S. 34 PPC: Common Intention
records.heading: Section 34 PPC requires proof of a pre-arranged plan and common intention
records.text: S. 34 PPC requires proof that a criminal act was done by several persons in furtherance of common intention, under a pre-arranged plan and in concert. Strong circumstances must show common intention, and common intention must be distinguished from similar intention. Ref: 2024 LHC 2091; M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 78896/2019, decided 08.04.2024).
records.title: M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 78896/2019, decided 08.04.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F CrPC: Witness Without s. 161 Statement
records.heading: Section 265-F CrPC does not bar testimony of a witness without a section 161 statement
records.text: S. 265-F CrPC does not prohibit the court from recording testimony of a person whose s. 161 CrPC statement was not recorded. An injured witness named in the calendar of witnesses, whose injury was confirmed, could not be excluded on that ground, and other confidence inspiring evidence could not be discarded. Ref: 2024 LHC 2091; M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 78896/2019, decided 08.04.2024).
records.title: M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal No. 78896/2019, decided 08.04.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minors: Liability of Uncles
records.heading: Uncles are liable for two thirds of minors' maintenance when minors lack means
records.text: Where minors have no property or insufficient income, their uncles are liable on account of kinship to pay two thirds of the maintenance fixed by the court and the mother contributes the remaining one third. The headline says the uncle who inherited the grandfather's estate was held liable. Ref: 2024 LHC 2111; Muhammad Maroof and others v. Mst. Mariam Farooq and others (Writ Petition No. 50 of 2024, decided 22.04.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Maroof and others v. Mst. Mariam Farooq and others (Writ Petition No. 50 of 2024, decided 22.04.2024)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: O. XXI R. 90 Second Proviso and S. 19(7) FIO 2001
records.heading: Supreme Court overruled earlier authority on the second proviso to Order XXI Rule 90
records.text: The Supreme Court expounded the meaning and scope of the second proviso to O. XXI R. 90 CPC and s. 19(7) of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance 2001. Habib and Company v. MCB (PLD 2020 SC 227) and P.I.C.I.C v. Govt. of Pakistan (2002 CLD 1) were overruled. Ref: Mst. Samrana Nawaz, etc v. MCB Bank Ltd., etc (C.P.L.A. 2646-L/2018, decided 10.05.2024).
records.title: Mst. Samrana Nawaz, etc v. MCB Bank Ltd., etc (C.P.L.A. 2646-L/2018, decided 10.05.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Legal Status of Adopted Child in Islam
records.heading: Adoption has no legal effect in Shariah and the adopted child is not an heir
records.text: Adoption has no legal effect in Shariah and creates no new legal relationship, and the child is attributed to the natural parents. An adopted child is not an heir of the adoptive parent under the Succession Act 1925. NADRA must record the parentage of a child of known parentage as natural parents. Ref: 2024 YLR 1073; Mst. Arzu v. DPO etc (WP 12826-23).
records.title: Mst. Arzu v. DPO etc (WP 12826-23)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Effect of Criminal Sentence on Police Service
records.heading: Dismissal from police service on a compensatory sentence requires a departmental inquiry
records.text: Punishment on a judicial sentence is not automatic and requires a departmental inquiry under Rule 16.24 of the Police Rules. Rule 16.2(2) turns on sentence, not conviction, and the petitioner was sentenced only to Arsh and Daman, compensatory punishments. He should not have been dismissed without a departmental inquiry. Ref: 2024 YLR 1052; Iftikhar Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 340-13).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 340-13)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: PEEDA Act 2006 Not Applicable to Police
records.heading: PEEDA Act 2006 does not apply to police employees governed by the Police Rules
records.text: The PEEDA Act 2006 does not apply to police employees, who are governed by Chapter XVI of the Police Rules 1934. An adverse order passed behind the petitioner's back can be challenged under the law. Ref: 2024 YLR 1052; Iftikhar Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 340-13).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 340-13)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: S. 6(3) JJSA 2018: Bailable Offences and Pre-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Offences punishable up to seven years are bailable for juveniles, including pre-arrest bail
records.text: Under s. 6(3) of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018, offences punishable up to seven years are bailable for a juvenile accused, and this provision applies to pre-arrest bail as well. Ref: Manzoor Ahmad v. Muhammad Umar Farooq etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 78015/CB/2023).
records.title: Manzoor Ahmad v. Muhammad Umar Farooq etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 78015/CB/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXI R. 90 CPC: Deposit of Twenty Percent
records.heading: Twenty percent deposit under Order XXI Rule 90 is made on the court's direction
records.text: A larger bench held that the deposit under the second proviso to O. XXI R. 90 CPC need not accompany the objection application and is to be made on the direction of the court. The Banking Court erred in dismissing the objection for non-deposit. Appeal allowed; the court must fix the amount and allow time to deposit, failing which the objection is dismissed. Ref: Mst. Samrana Nawaz v. MCB Bank Ltd (C.P. 2646-L/2018, C.A. 17-L/2019 and C.A. 364-L/2020, decided 10.05.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Mst. Samrana Nawaz v. MCB Bank Ltd (C.P. 2646-L/2018, C.A. 17-L/2019 and C.A. 364-L/2020, decided 10.05.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification of Dead Body Seen Thrown in Canal
records.heading: A witness who saw a person thrown into a canal must identify the recovered body
records.text: Where a witness claims to have seen the accused throw an unknown person into a canal, identification of the recovered dead body by that witness is necessary. Ref: 2024 YLR 1099; Asif Ali v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 1503/2023).
records.title: Asif Ali v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 1503/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Witnesses Unharmed and Blackening Distance in Murder
records.heading: Sparing close relative witnesses and blackening at 5.5 feet cast doubt on the account
records.text: It is unbelievable that an accused killing a man before his close relatives would not injure the witnesses. The post-mortem noted blackening at the entrance wound though the firing distance was 5.5 feet, whereas by Modi's treatise blackening occurs within about three feet for a shotgun and two feet for a pistol. Ref: Riasat Ali and Fakhar Zaman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 708-L of 2018, decided 10.05.2024).
records.title: Riasat Ali and Fakhar Zaman v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 708-L of 2018, decided 10.05.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Call Data Record Shows Tower Area Only
records.heading: Call Data Record shows only cell tower area and not who carried the SIMs
records.text: Ownership of the mobile phones and SIMs was not proved. Call Data Record only shows SIMs within a cell tower's area and not who carried them or that the users were together. Mere Call Data Record without voice transcript was of no avail to the prosecution. Ref: 2024 YLR 1099; Asif Ali etc v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 1503/2023).
records.title: Asif Ali etc v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 1503/2023)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 34 Arbitration Act 1934: Stepping into Proceedings
records.heading: Whether adjournment and a power of attorney amount to stepping into proceedings under section 34
records.text: Considers whether seeking adjournment and filing a power of attorney or an application under s. 34 amounts to taking a step in the proceedings. It notes that where parties agreed to arbitration, that forum is preferred and a party who sues in disregard of it may face a stay application. The post does not give the conclusion. Ref: Waqas Yaqub v. Adeel Yaqub and another (F.A.O. No. 88 of 2023, heard 07.05.2024).
records.title: Waqas Yaqub v. Adeel Yaqub and another (F.A.O. No. 88 of 2023, heard 07.05.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording Eye-Witness Statements Under S. 161
records.heading: Unexplained delay in recording eye-witness statements under section 161 is fatal
records.text: Even one or two days of unexplained delay in recording the s. 161 CrPC statements of eye-witnesses is fatal, and their testimony cannot be safely relied upon. Ref: 2017 SCMR 486; Muhammad Asif v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Police Examination of Witnesses
records.heading: Unexplained police delay in recording a witness's section 161 statement is fatal to the prosecution
records.text: Delay by the police in recording a witness's s. 161 CrPC statement without plausible explanation is fatal to the prosecution case, and the witness's statement is not to be relied upon. Ref: 2010 SCMR 584; Rahat Ali v. State.
records.title: Rahat Ali v. State

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Bilateral Agreement: Deposit of Balance Consideration
records.heading: Buyer cannot be directed to deposit the entire price where the seller has not performed
records.text: In a bilateral agreement to sell, the parties perform their parts step by step. Where the seller had not provided the sales records on which the buyer's next payment depended, the buyer could not be directed to deposit the entire price. The High Court set aside the Trial Court's order as the amount was uncertain. Ref: 2023 MLD 838; Premium Developers through Chief Executive v. Muhammad Tariq.
records.title: Premium Developers through Chief Executive v. Muhammad Tariq

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Non-Deposit of Balance Consideration Despite Last Opportunity
records.heading: Failure to deposit balance despite last opportunity brings dismissal of the suit
records.text: An order to deposit the balance sale consideration tests the vendee's bona fides and protects the vendor. Where the vendee failed to deposit despite repeated and last opportunities, the penal consequence had to follow, and the suit was rightly dismissed, relying on 2017 SCMR 2022. Ref: 2023 CLC 926; Khairat Ali v. Saqib Ashfaq.
records.title: Khairat Ali v. Saqib Ashfaq

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Release Deed, Gift Deed and Sale Deed Distinguished
records.heading: The character of the transaction decides whether a deed is release, gift or sale
records.text: The character of the transaction and the rights created decide whether an instrument is a release deed, gift deed or sale deed. By a release deed a co-sharer or heir separates from joint property, and accepting consideration for a share and releasing it estops the heir from later claims based on spes successionis. Ref: 2024 SCMR 916; Mst. Farzana Zia & others v. Mst. Saadia Andaleeb & others (C.A. 1012/2018).
records.title: Mst. Farzana Zia & others v. Mst. Saadia Andaleeb & others (C.A. 1012/2018)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Under Muslim Law and Transfer of Property Act
records.heading: Transfer of Property Act sections 123 and 129 do not govern Muslim law gifts
records.text: Release deeds and gift deeds are distinct and not interchangeable. Ss. 123 and 129 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 do not apply to gifts under Muslim law, where the constituents are tender, acceptance and possession. The donor must be of sound mind and free from coercion, and any property may be gifted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 916; Mst. Farzana Zia & others v. Mst. Saadia Andaleeb & others (C.A. 1012/2018).
records.title: Mst. Farzana Zia & others v. Mst. Saadia Andaleeb & others (C.A. 1012/2018)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Revenue Authorities and Women's Land
records.heading: Revenue authorities must protect women's land and officials complicit in deprivation face action
records.text: Revenue authorities must take care over the land of women. Officials who through complicity or incompetence help deprive women of land should face action, and where land remains illegally retained, substantial compensatory costs must be imposed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 978; Muhammad Mumtaz Khan v. Mst. Siraj Bibi (C.M.A. 6336/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Mumtaz Khan v. Mst. Siraj Bibi (C.M.A. 6336/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Framing of Charge: S. 221 and S. 225 CrPC
records.heading: A charge omission is material only if the accused was misled and justice failed
records.text: Framing of charge is the foundation of trial, and under s. 221 CrPC the Trial Judge must ensure a proper, unambiguous charge. A charge omitting ingredients or framed vaguely may mislead the accused. Not every omission is a material illegality unless the accused was misled and failure of justice resulted, as provided by s. 225 CrPC. Ref: 2024 SCMR 843; Zain Shahid v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 29-K/2022).
records.title: Zain Shahid v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 29-K/2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance Vests on Death; Illegal Mutation
records.heading: A daughter cannot be deprived of her inherited share by an illegal mutation
records.text: Legal heirs inherit their shares the moment the predecessor dies. A daughter of a deceased landlord cannot be deprived of her share in inherited property by an illegal mutation sanctioned at the instance of male heirs. Ref: 2024 SCMR 938; Mst. Sehat Bibi v. Bahar Khan s/o late Daulat Khan & 2 others (Civil Appeal No. 26-Q of 2017).
records.title: Mst. Sehat Bibi v. Bahar Khan s/o late Daulat Khan & 2 others (Civil Appeal No. 26-Q of 2017)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Photographs of Recovery in Narcotics Cases
records.heading: Police and ANF must photograph or video record narcotics recoveries, the accused and the scene
records.text: The Court directed police and ANF officials in narcotics cases to photograph or video record the recovered narcotics, the accused and the scene, observing that such recordings are admissible evidence under the law of evidence. Bail was allowed on bonds of Rs. 100,000 owing to delay in submitting the challan and failure to collect evidence in accordance with law. Ref: 2024 SCMR 934, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 8; Zahid Sarfaraz Gill v. The State thr. A.G., Islamabad (Crl.P. 1192/2023).
records.title: Zahid Sarfaraz Gill v. The State thr. A.G., Islamabad (Crl.P. 1192/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 22-A & 22-B CrPC: Mala Fide Applications
records.heading: Courts must not entertain mala fide section 22-A and 22-B applications mechanically
records.text: An application under ss. 22-A and 22-B CrPC was held tainted with mala fide where the parties were lawyers with admitted animosity from bar elections and counsel conceded the respondent was absent at the occurrence. Courts must not entertain such applications lightly or decide them mechanically by directing the police to register an FIR. The dismissal by the trial court, upheld by the High Court, was maintained. Ref: 2024 SCMR 985; Munawar Alam Khan v. Qurban Ali Mallano & others (Crl.P.L.A. 31-K/2022).
records.title: Munawar Alam Khan v. Qurban Ali Mallano & others (Crl.P.L.A. 31-K/2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Delay in Sending Samples to Laboratory: Bail
records.heading: Delay in sending charas samples with no custody record raises further inquiry for bail
records.text: In a case of 1420 grams of charas, a delay of over a month in sending samples to the Forensic Science Laboratory, with no record of who held them in safe custody, made the case one of further inquiry despite Rule 4(2) of the Control of Narcotic Substances (Government Analysts) Rules, 2001 requiring dispatch within seventy-two hours. The maximum sentence of fourteen years did not attract the bar of s. 51 CNSA. Bail allowed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 913; Sagheer Ahmed v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1241-L/2023).
records.title: Sagheer Ahmed v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1241-L/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Judicial Council: Misconduct and Removal of Judge
records.heading: Supreme Judicial Council found a Supreme Court Judge guilty of misconduct and recommended removal
records.text: The Supreme Judicial Council, acting under Art. 209(6) of the Constitution, found a Judge of the Supreme Court guilty of misconduct and recommended his removal from office. Ref: 2024 SCMR 880; Re: Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi, Judge, Supreme Court of Pakistan (Complaint 586/2023).
records.title: Re: Justice Sayyed Mazahar Ali Akbar Naqvi, Judge, Supreme Court of Pakistan (Complaint 586/2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: No Limitation in Inheritance; Fraud Vitiates
records.heading: Limitation does not run in inheritance matters and fraud vitiates the foundational transaction
records.text: Limitation does not run where a question of inheritance is involved. Where the foundational transaction rests on fraud and mala fide, the superstructure built upon it cannot stand. Ref: 2024 CLC 895, PLJ 2024 Lahore 160; Mst. Nawab Bibi v. Hakim Ali (C.R. No. 2312 of 2014).
records.title: Mst. Nawab Bibi v. Hakim Ali (C.R. No. 2312 of 2014)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 17-A Family Courts Act: Striking Off Defence
records.heading: Striking off defence under section 17-A Family Courts Act cannot be exercised mechanically
records.text: Although s. 17-A of the Family Courts Act, 1964 empowers the Family Court to strike off the defence and decree the suit for non-payment of interim maintenance, the power cannot be exercised mechanically. Before invoking this penal provision the Court must consider whether it was vested with power to pass the interim maintenance order, which was not done here. Ref: 2024 CLC 863; Bashir Masih v. Suneela Nadeem etc (WP 38-14).
records.title: Bashir Masih v. Suneela Nadeem etc (WP 38-14)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: No Limitation for Execution of Family Court Decree
records.heading: No limitation applies to execution of a Family Court decree
records.text: No limitation is provided for filing an execution petition in family cases under s. 13 of the Family Courts Act, 1964, and a decree of dower may be executed whenever the wife moves the Court, even if recovery was postponed during the marriage. Proceedings of the Family Court, as trial or executing court, are governed by equity, justice and fair play. Ref: 2024 CLC 979; Mirza Muhammad Akbar Baig v. Add. District Judge, etc. (Writ Petition No. 6002 of 2022).
records.title: Mirza Muhammad Akbar Baig v. Add. District Judge, etc. (Writ Petition No. 6002 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Order VII Rule 11 CPC aims to bury an incompetent suit at inception
records.text: The object of O. VII R. 11 CPC is to bury an incompetent suit at its inception, and the Court must examine the plaint thoroughly at the outset. The date of knowledge of the alleged fraud must be pleaded explicitly and proved, which was lacking here. Ref: 2024 CLC 922, PLJ 2023 Lahore 896; Muhammad Yasin v. Muhammad Ismail etc (Civil Revision 62703/23).
records.title: Muhammad Yasin v. Muhammad Ismail etc (Civil Revision 62703/23)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Quantum of Children's Maintenance
records.heading: There is no fixed formula for children's maintenance, which turns on needs and father's means
records.text: A father is obliged to maintain his children, and there is no fixed formula for the quantum. The Court must consider the minors' education, status and expenses and the father's ability to pay, and a bare plea of limited resources does not discharge him. The aim is that the minors are maintained with dignity and the mother is not left to bear the burden. Ref: Syed Zain Muntazar Mehdi v. Mst. Sara Naqvi etc. (Writ Petition No. 370 of 2024).
records.title: Syed Zain Muntazar Mehdi v. Mst. Sara Naqvi etc. (Writ Petition No. 370 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Special Oath under the Oath Act
records.heading: A special oath accepted and administered binds the parties and the court
records.text: An offer to be bound by the oath statement of the opposite party, once accepted and the special oath administered, binds the parties and the Court must decide on that basis. The Oath Act prescribes no formal procedure: ss. 8 to 10 require an offer, its communication and acceptance, then oath and statement, and under s. 11 the statement is conclusive proof against the person who made the offer. Ref: Abdul Sattar Khan v. Muhammad Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (R.S.A. No. 08 of 2012, decided 09.04.2024).
records.title: Abdul Sattar Khan v. Muhammad Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs. and others (R.S.A. No. 08 of 2012, decided 09.04.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secondary Evidence Without Prior Application
records.heading: Secondary evidence may be led without a prior application for leave
records.text: A party may lead secondary evidence before the trial court without filing a prior application for leave, since such applications lead either to the evidence being ignored or considered twice. The other side may object when the evidence is tendered, and the Court may decide the objection then or record it and decide at final adjudication. Ref: 2024 LHC 2256; Bagh Ali v. ADJ Pakpattan etc (Misc. Writ 11458/24, decided 18.04.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Bagh Ali v. ADJ Pakpattan etc (Misc. Writ 11458/24, decided 18.04.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Territorial Jurisdiction of Trial; FIA Act Schedule
records.heading: The court within whose territory the occurrence took place conducts the trial
records.text: Where a question arises between courts of two districts over taking cognizance and trial, the High Court decides it, and the court within whose territory the occurrence took place conducts the trial. Even if an offence appears in the schedule of the FIA Act, 1974, the court established under the parent statute of that offence tries the case. Ref: 2024 LHC 2316; Riasat Ali v. The State etc (WP 30611/24, decided 16.05.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Riasat Ali v. The State etc (WP 30611/24, decided 16.05.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Extension of Time to Deposit Balance Sale Price
records.heading: Trial court may extend time for balance deposit unless directed at vendor's instance
records.text: In a suit for specific performance, where the direction to deposit the balance consideration is not at the instance of the vendor, the trial court has power to extend the time. Where the direction was at the vendor's instance, the Court ordinarily becomes functus officio. Ref: 2024 LHC 2268; Humayon Sajjad v. Aslam Khan (R.F.A. 45873/23, decided 15.05.2024); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Humayon Sajjad v. Aslam Khan (R.F.A. 45873/23, decided 15.05.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Discharge Order Set Aside: Misreading of Evidence
records.heading: A discharge order based on misreading and non-reading of evidence is perverse and set aside
records.text: In a petition under Art. 199, the order of a Judicial Magistrate discharging the accused for insufficient material was held perverse and the result of misreading and non-reading of evidence. The order was set aside and the matter sent to the Sessions Judge to assign to another Magistrate to decide afresh after notice to all concerned. Ref: 2024 LHC 2265; Rasoolan Bibi v. The State etc (WP 82843/23, decided 14.05.2024); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Rasoolan Bibi v. The State etc (WP 82843/23, decided 14.05.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supplementary Statement: Arrest and Remand Directions
records.heading: Accused must not be arrested on a supplementary statement alone without incriminating material
records.text: A supplementary statement naming an accused without disclosing the source of information is not per se admissible, and the Investigating Officer should insist on the source. The accused must not be arrested on that statement alone before incriminating material is collected, and any remand request must carry the Prosecutor's opinion on sufficiency of material.
