Directions issued to police, prosecutors and magistrates. Ref: 2024 LHC 229; Mst. Najma Bibi v. S.H.O. P.S. City Daska etc. (Crl. Misc. 27821/24, decided 13.05.2024); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Mst. Najma Bibi v. S.H.O. P.S. City Daska etc. (Crl. Misc. 27821/24, decided 13.05.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Arrest in One Case Presumed Arrest in All Cases
records.heading: An accused arrested in one case is presumed arrested in all cases requiring arrest
records.text: To stop successive arrests in different cases after bail, an accused arrested in one case is presumed arrested in all cases against him where arrest was required. If arrest in an earlier case was omitted, the Investigating Officer must apply in writing to the Magistrate or Court with the Prosecutor's opinion, and approval must be given by reasoned order and not mechanically. Ref: 2024 LHC 2287; Shahida Bibi v. I.G.P. etc. (Crl. Misc. 27670/24, decided 13.05.2024); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Shahida Bibi v. I.G.P. etc. (Crl. Misc. 27670/24, decided 13.05.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination of Medical Officer on Accused's MLCs
records.heading: Defence may cross-examine the prosecution medical officer on the accused's medico-legal certificates
records.text: The defence may cross-examine the prosecution's medical officer on the medico-legal examination of the accused. Under Art. 155 QSO the officer may refresh memory from the medico-legal certificates and radiologist report, and the prosecution may seek permission to question him under Art. 150. The defence may later tender those documents in its defence evidence. Revision allowed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 808; Muhammad Aslam v. The State and another (Crl. Rev. 206-2021).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State and another (Crl. Rev. 206-2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 91 and 351 CrPC: Securing Accused's Attendance
records.heading: Court may require a bond under section 91 or commit to custody under section 351
records.text: The Court may require an accused summoned for trial to furnish a bond under s. 91 CrPC, or commit him to custody under s. 351 CrPC if evidence is available against him. Such detention is regulated under s. 344 CrPC and bail under s. 497 CrPC may be considered at an appropriate stage. When a bond is taken under s. 91 the question of bail does not arise. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 977, PLJ 2024 CrC 435; Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 255 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 255 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supply of CDR and Documents to Accused
records.heading: A CDR collected but not appended to the section 173 report must be supplied
records.text: A CDR collected by the Investigating Officer but not appended to the s. 173 CrPC report must be supplied to the accused, who cannot be met with surprise evidence, as Art. 10-A requires a fair opportunity. Under Art. 160 QSO the prosecution cannot use a CDR it fails to produce on the accused's notice. The only privileged material is the investigation diary under s. 172 CrPC. Ref: 2024 MLD 886; Sabir Hussain v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 200-23).
records.title: Sabir Hussain v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 200-23)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeal or Reference of Convict of Unsound Mind
records.heading: Appeal of a convict of unsound mind should be postponed until he recovers
records.text: Deciding an appeal, or a reference under s. 374 CrPC, while the convict is of unsound mind denies him a hearing. The appellate court or High Court should postpone the hearing until the convict recovers, but may proceed if the case is one in which he would be acquitted. Ref: 2024 MLD 846; Iqbal Ansari v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 2066/2016).
records.title: Iqbal Ansari v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 2066/2016)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Judicial Inquiry into Custodial Death or Rape: Police Order
records.heading: Article 106 of Police Order 2002 provides judicial inquiry into custodial death, rape or serious injury
records.text: Art. 106 of the Police Order 2002 provides for a judicial inquiry, through a request to the Chief Justice of the High Court, where a person in police custody dies, is raped or is seriously injured. An FIR for police dereliction can be registered under Art. 155(1)(c) and (d), but Art. 155(2) requires sanction for prosecution. Establishment of the Provincial Police Complaints Authority is essential. Ref: 2024 MLD 951; Hafeez Ullah v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (WP 10957/23).
records.title: Hafeez Ullah v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (WP 10957/23)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination Rules and Lengthy Cross-Examination
records.heading: Lahore High Court states guiding rules for cross-examination and deprecates lengthy cross-examination
records.text: A Lahore High Court judgment stating essential guiding rules for cross-examining witnesses and strongly deprecating lengthy cross-examination. Ref: 2024 MLD 919; Muhammad Zafar alias Ghulabi v. The State (Crl. Appeal against Conviction-PPC 71-22).
records.title: Muhammad Zafar alias Ghulabi v. The State (Crl. Appeal against Conviction-PPC 71-22)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Heroin Bail: Weight Including Wrapping, Amended S. 9
records.heading: Heroin weighed in a shopping bag raises further inquiry on quantity for bail
records.text: Since the 2022 amendment to s. 9 CNSA prescribes separate sentences for each narcotic, the lesser punishment is considered at the bail stage. The 1080 grams of heroin were weighed in a shopping bag and nothing showed the contraband was weighed without wrapping, so further inquiry arose on whether the quantity attracted the higher punishment. Directions were also given to the ICT police on training in narcotics investigations. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 868; Muhammad Naseer v. The State (Criminal Miscellaneous No. 1225-B of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Naseer v. The State (Criminal Miscellaneous No. 1225-B of 2023)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test for Paternity Requires Consent
records.heading: A DNA test to determine paternity requires the consent of the parties
records.text: A DNA examination to determine a child's paternity requires the consent of the parties. If consent is withheld, the trial court may draw an adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO and decide paternity on the evidence produced, and physiognomy is good circumstantial evidence of paternity. Ref: 2024 LHC 2358; Kaneez Fatima and 1 other v. Senior Civil Judge etc (WP 75322/22, decided 15.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kaneez Fatima and 1 other v. Senior Civil Judge etc (WP 75322/22, decided 15.05.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Decided Despite Arrest in Another Case
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail may be decided on merits though the accused is arrested elsewhere
records.text: A pending petition for pre-arrest bail can be decided on merits in the accused's absence even though he is under arrest in another case. Ref: 2024 LHC 2349; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 46363/23, decided 13.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 46363/23, decided 13.05.2024)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: ICJ Order on Rafah Operation: South Africa v. Israel
records.heading: ICJ orders Israel to halt its Rafah military operation and open the crossing
records.text: On South Africa's request to modify the order of 28 March 2024, the International Court of Justice, by majority, ordered Israel to halt its military operation in Rafah, to report on compliance within a month, to open the Rafah crossing for aid and to allow access to UN fact-finding missions in Gaza. Ref: Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip (South Africa v. Israel) (General List No. 192, decided 24.05.2024).
records.title: Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip (South Africa v. Israel) (General List No. 192, decided 24.05.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Polygamy: Private Complaint Against Second Wife and Others
records.heading: Complaint of polygamy disclosed no prima facie offence against the second wife and Nikah participants
records.text: A complaint must state facts disclosing both the unlawful act and the criminal intent. The Family Court summoned only the husband accused of a second marriage without Arbitration Council permission, and counsel could not show any offence prima facie made out in the complaint against the second wife, Nikah witnesses, reciter or registrar. Ref: 2024 MLD 786; Mst. Sidra-tul-Muntaha v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (Writ Petition No. 84511 of 2023).
records.title: Mst. Sidra-tul-Muntaha v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (Writ Petition No. 84511 of 2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Release of Vehicle Seized Under CNSA
records.heading: Seized vehicle of a lawful owner without nexus to the accused may be released
records.text: The CNSA is lex specialis, so articles connected with narcotics are dealt with under ss. 32 and 33 and the proviso to s. 74. A seized vehicle is not liable to confiscation, and its lawful owner with no nexus to the accused may seek release, while the prosecution may show the applicant knew of the offence. Release on acquittal is not an absolute rule and each case turns on its facts. Ref: 2024 LHC 2375; Muhammad Akram v. ASJ etc (Crl. Appeal 460-23, decided 06.03.2024); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. ASJ etc (Crl. Appeal 460-23, decided 06.03.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Return of Deposited Balance: Actus Curiae Neminem Gravabit
records.heading: Court inaction in not recording a deposit order cannot prejudice the plaintiff
records.text: Where the trial court allowed the plaintiff's application to deposit the balance consideration but failed to record this in the order sheet, the omission is the Court's inaction and cannot prejudice the plaintiff, applying the maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit. Courts must not act mechanically, and there was no adverse claimant of the amount. Ref: 2024 LHC 2443; Saima Batool v. ADJ etc (Writ 57749/23, decided 30.04.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Saima Batool v. ADJ etc (Writ 57749/23, decided 30.04.2024)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Disputing Landlord Status: Once a Tenant
records.heading: Once a tenant, always a tenant applies against a tenant who disputes landlord status
records.text: The tenant was inducted by the respondent's deceased father and the respondent, as legal heir, succeeded to the premises, a status the tenant did not dispute. The tenant neither approached the Rent Tribunal to deposit rent nor filed an interpleader suit, and the settled principle is that once a tenant, always a tenant. Ref: 2024 LHC 2437; Sohail Niaz Khan v. Bilal Rizwan etc. (Writ 79017/23, decided 06.05.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Sohail Niaz Khan v. Bilal Rizwan etc. (Writ 79017/23, decided 06.05.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Damages After Acquittal in Criminal Prosecution
records.heading: Acquittal does not automatically entitle the accused to damages for prosecution
records.text: Acquittal may give rise to a rebuttable presumption that there was no reasonable cause for prosecution, but failure of a prosecution does not automatically entitle the accused to damages. The nature of the acquittal must be taken into account. Ref: 2024 LHC 2425; Tariq Mehmood v. Tahir Farooq (R.F.A. 80927/22, decided 16.05.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Tariq Mehmood v. Tahir Farooq (R.F.A. 80927/22, decided 16.05.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Concealment of Facts: Unclean Hands, Costs
records.heading: A petitioner concealing material facts approaches the Court with unclean hands and incurs costs
records.text: A petitioner who concealed that the impugned order had been implemented and that he had joined of his own volition approached the Court with unclean hands. Fraud vitiates solemn proceedings, such a litigant may be thrown out at any stage with costs, and the petition was dismissed with costs of Rs. 100,000. Ref: 2024 LHC 2433; Muhammad Shehzad v. Province of Punjab etc. (WP 27923/24, decided 21.05.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Shehzad v. Province of Punjab etc. (WP 27923/24, decided 21.05.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Guardianship: Welfare of Minor, Least Detrimental Option
records.heading: Court may choose the guardian least detrimental to the minor's welfare
records.text: The welfare of a minor is a relative consideration, and the Court may choose the guardian who is least detrimental to the minor. Custody was given to the mother, who was accused of murdering the minor's father, by restoring the Guardian Judge's order, as the paternal grandmother had dealt with the minor's property without authority in a clandestine manner. Ref: 2024 LHC 2451; Hina Imtiaz v. ADJ etc (Family 3513/23, decided 24.05.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Hina Imtiaz v. ADJ etc (Family 3513/23, decided 24.05.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Healthcare Commission and Consumer Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Authority on jurisdiction of the Healthcare Commission Punjab and the Consumer Court
records.text: Authority on the jurisdiction of the Healthcare Commission Punjab and the Presiding Officer of the Consumer Court, which operate in their respective spheres. Ref: 2024 LHC 2418; Dr. Omar Chughtai etc v. Province of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 2863-24, decided 13.05.2024); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Dr. Omar Chughtai etc v. Province of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 2863-24, decided 13.05.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Counsel's Authority to Compromise Under Vakalatnama
records.heading: A vakalatnama does not impliedly authorise counsel to compromise, withdraw or suffer a decree
records.text: A power of attorney is construed strictly and confers only the authority expressly given or necessarily implied. A vakalatnama does not impliedly authorise counsel to compromise, withdraw the suit or suffer a decree, and such an act without specific authority has no legal consequence at the option of the party concerned. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 262, PLJ 2024 Lahore 322, PLD 2025 Lahore 414; Falak Sher v. Hashmat Bibi (Writ Petition-3631-15).
records.title: Falak Sher v. Hashmat Bibi (Writ Petition-3631-15)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI CPC: Summoning Court Witness
records.heading: Order XVI Rule 14 lets the court summon a non-party witness on its own motion
records.text: The proviso to O. XVI R. 1 CPC allows condonation of delay in filing the witness list for sufficient cause. An application seeking to summon a Treasury record keeper as a court witness attracted O. XVI R. 14 CPC, under which the Court may summon a non-party witness of its own motion, with diet money payable by the party the Court directs under the Lahore High Court amendment. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 302; Muhammad Akram v. Haji Ilam Din (deceased) through L.Rs and others (W.P. No. 48863 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. Haji Ilam Din (deceased) through L.Rs and others (W.P. No. 48863 of 2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Guarantee Cheque Misused After Payment of Dues
records.heading: Cheque issued as guarantee and misused after dues were cleared cannot support a recovery decree
records.text: A cheque issued as a guarantee for a wheat purchase, with no date specified, was misused after the amount due was admittedly cleared. The trial court misread evidence and erred in decreeing the recovery suit under O. XXXVII CPC and dismissing the suit for cancellation under s. 39 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 310, 2025 CLC 1913; Malik Muhammad Ashraf v. Muhammad Asif, etc. (R.F.A. No. 258 of 2022).
records.title: Malik Muhammad Ashraf v. Muhammad Asif, etc. (R.F.A. No. 258 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Procedure for Cancellation Reports
records.heading: Cancellation reports require complainant notice, independent reasons and a hearing by the Magistrate
records.text: Guidelines on cancellation reports under s. 173 CrPC: the complainant must be informed and sign the report under Rule 25.57, the Superintendent of Police must forward it with independent reasons, and no prosecutor may forward it otherwise. The Magistrate must issue notice to all concerned and hear them before deciding it, in line with audi alteram partem. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 315; Ali Mansoor Khan v. Learned ADJ etc (58171/23).
records.title: Ali Mansoor Khan v. Learned ADJ etc (58171/23)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 148 PPC: Common Object, No Corroboration
records.heading: Forensic report on weapons gives no corroboration; common object is essential under section 148 PPC
records.text: Where appellants caused no injury and were alleged only to have fired ineffectively, a forensic report on the working condition of weapons or matching of empties gives no corroboration. Common object is a necessary ingredient of s. 148 PPC, read with s. 141 PPC, and none was established. Appeals allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 553, 2024 MLD 1672; Asif alias Asad and 3 others v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 245 & 409 of 2016); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Asif alias Asad and 3 others v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 245 & 409 of 2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Heinous Nature of Offence Irrelevant to Appraisal of Evidence
records.heading: Gruesome nature of an offence is irrelevant to appraisal of evidence
records.text: In a four-fold murder case, the gruesome nature of the offence may bear on sentence but is irrelevant to appraising evidence, which must decide guilt without sentiment. The accused is presumed innocent until proved guilty beyond reasonable doubt. Appeal allowed, death sentence not confirmed, and the complainant's petition against acquittal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 562; Umer Draz and others v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 44377, M.R. No. 223, P.S.L.A. No. 55094 & Crl. Rev. No. 55096 of 2019); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Umer Draz and others v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 44377, M.R. No. 223, P.S.L.A. No. 55094 & Crl. Rev. No. 55096 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Site Plan; S. 510 CrPC
records.heading: Ocular account contradicted by site plan and forensic reports gives benefit of doubt
records.text: Oral testimony contradicting the unscaled site plan and the forensic reports gave benefit of doubt. Under s. 510 CrPC reports of experts such as the chemical examiner, serologist and forensic scientist are admissible per se without examining the expert. The investigation was criticised as tainted and a copy sent to the CCPO. Appeal accepted. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 571; Muhammad Bilal etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 56380 & Crl. Rev. No. 42144 of 2021, decided 20.02.2024); Justice Aalia Neelum.
records.title: Muhammad Bilal etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 56380 & Crl. Rev. No. 42144 of 2021, decided 20.02.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345(2) CrPC: Who May Compromise Qatl-i-Amd
records.heading: Only direct surviving legal heirs may compromise Qatl-i-Amd under section 345(2) CrPC
records.text: Direct surviving legal heirs of the deceased may compromise under s. 345(2) CrPC where the punishment was Ta'zir. The legal heirs of a mother who died after the occurrence are not legal heirs of the deceased for this purpose. Appeals accepted and the appellants acquitted under s. 345(6) CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 609; Zafar and others v. State (Crl. A. No. 79782-J, 79783-J & 79784-J of 2022); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zafar and others v. State (Crl. A. No. 79782-J, 79783-J & 79784-J of 2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Pre-Arrest Bail: Fake Advocate
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail to a person posing as an advocate cancelled as perverse
records.text: Pre-arrest bail granted to a person accused of posing as an advocate and committing fraud was held perverse, arbitrary and contrary to settled principles, since investigation had established material connecting him with the offences under ss. 420, 468 and 471 PPC and s. 58 of the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act. Petition allowed under s. 497(5) CrPC, observations being tentative. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 627; Muhammad Rafie v. Ghaneem Aabir, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 73505-CB of 2023, decided 13.03.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Rafie v. Ghaneem Aabir, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 73505-CB of 2023, decided 13.03.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Joint Extra-Judicial Confession; Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Joint extra-judicial confession is doubtful where witnesses did not react to it
records.text: In a circumstantial evidence case, a joint extra-judicial confession was doubtful as the deceased's brothers, the witnesses, did not react to it. A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right, and the accused were acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 638; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 526-J & 527-J & M.R. No. 33 of 2021); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram; Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi etc. v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 526-J & 527-J & M.R. No. 33 of 2021)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Appointment of Election Tribunals: Chief Justice Prevails
records.heading: Chief Justice's opinion prevails over the ECP in appointing Election Tribunals
records.text: In appointing Election Tribunals under s. 140 of the Act, the opinion of the High Court Chief Justice prevails over a contrary view of the ECP, which must appoint the Judges nominated by him. Assigning areas of jurisdiction to the Tribunals lies with the Chief Justice. The petitions seeking additional tribunals in Punjab were allowed. Ref: 2024 LHC 2466; Salman Akram Raja v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc (Election 28985/24, decided 29.05.2024); Justice Shahid Karim.
records.title: Salman Akram Raja v. Election Commission of Pakistan etc (Election 28985/24, decided 29.05.2024)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Custodial Torture and Death: Exclusive FIA Jurisdiction
records.heading: The FIA has exclusive jurisdiction to investigate custodial torture, death and rape
records.text: Jurisdiction to investigate custodial torture, death and rape lies exclusively with the FIA under the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act, 2022. Police were directed to cease investigating such matters, and the implementation of the Act was referred to the Punjab Chief Minister and the Federal Interior Ministry. Ref: 2024 LHC 2550; Mst. Sarriya Bibi v. RPO Sheikhupura etc. (WP 61743/23, decided 09.04.2024); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mst. Sarriya Bibi v. RPO Sheikhupura etc. (WP 61743/23, decided 09.04.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Punjab Food Authority Act: Rule 52 Sample Quantity Mandatory
records.heading: Rule 52 of the Punjab Food Rules on minimum sample quantity is mandatory
records.text: Rule 52 of the Punjab Food Rules, 2011, prescribing the minimum sample quantity for the Public Analyst's report, is mandatory, since prosecution under Chapter IV of the PFA Act depends on that report and Art. 10-A guarantees a fair trial. The offence under s. 22(1) of the PFA Act does not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Ref: 2024 YLR 1182; Muhammad Ashraf v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 17013/23); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 17013/23)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 337-D PPC: Jaifah Injury Must Be Direct Result
records.heading: Section 337-D PPC applies only where the body cavity injury is a direct result
records.text: An injury to the body cavity attracts s. 337-D PPC only if it is the direct consequence of the trauma inflicted by the perpetrator and not its fall-out or by-product. The Court criticised an incorrect medical opinion and confirmed ad interim pre-arrest bail on fresh bonds of Rs. 100,000. Ref: 2024 YLR 1194, PLJ 2024 CrC 829; Rashid v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 3229-B-23).
records.title: Rashid v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 3229-B-23)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics Analysis Report: Protocols Assessed at Trial
records.heading: Protocols in a narcotics analysis report are assessed only when tendered at trial
records.text: The veracity of protocols in a narcotics analysis report can be assessed only once it is tendered in evidence, and premature termination of the prosecution is deprecated. The acquittal under s. 265-K CrPC was set aside on the State's appeal and the case remanded. Ref: 2024 YLR 1174; State v. Shafique Ahmad (Crl. Appeal-Against Acquittal 166-20).
records.title: State v. Shafique Ahmad (Crl. Appeal-Against Acquittal 166-20)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: S. 510 CrPC: Handwriting Expert Report Not Conclusive
records.heading: A handwriting expert report is admissible per se but not conclusive
records.text: After the 2022 amendment, s. 510 CrPC makes the reports of forensic scientists and handwriting experts admissible per se without calling them, though the Court may summon the expert. Admissibility is distinct from probative value, and such an opinion is not conclusive and must be evaluated by the Court. Ref: 2024 YLR 1264; Mian Tariq Aziz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60825/M/2021).
records.title: Mian Tariq Aziz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60825/M/2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 61, 78 and 100 QSO: Handwriting and Signatures
records.heading: Articles 61, 78 and 100 QSO govern proof of handwriting and signatures
records.text: Art. 61 QSO makes the opinion of a person acquainted with a person's handwriting a relevant fact. Art. 78 requires proof of signature or handwriting where it is questioned, and Art. 100 attaches presumptions to thirty-year-old documents. Ref: 2024 YLR 1264; Mian Tariq Aziz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60825/M/2021).
records.title: Mian Tariq Aziz v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 60825/M/2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Contradiction Between Medical and Ocular Evidence
records.heading: Medical evidence on the bullet track contradicted the prosecution claim of a frontal shot
records.text: The medical evidence on the track of the bullet, entering from the left side of the chest without exit from the back, contradicted the prosecution claim of a frontal chest shot. The unusual size of the entry wound compared with the exit wound was another doubtful feature of the medical evidence. Ref: 2024 YLR 1349; Sajid Hussain v. State (Crl. Appeal 289-19).
records.title: Sajid Hussain v. State (Crl. Appeal 289-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Site Plan: Requirement Under Police Rules
records.heading: Rule 25.13 of the Police Rules requires a site plan by a qualified police officer
records.text: Under Rule 25.13 of the Police Rules, 1934 a site plan is prepared by a qualified police officer or suitable agency, and not by a patwari for an inhabited enclosure or village or town land. Two plans are required, the first of the officer's own observations and the second, not sent to court, of witness statements. The expert and the investigating officer failed in this duty. Ref: 2024 YLR 1349; Sajid Hussain v. State (Crl. Appeal 289-19).
records.title: Sajid Hussain v. State (Crl. Appeal 289-19)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Is Not a Title Document
records.heading: A mutation does not create title and may be challenged before the Civil Court
records.text: Mutations do not create title, are not part of the record of right and are sanctioned only for fiscal purposes, and may be challenged before the Civil Court. A mutation sanctioned to exclude the legal heirs of the deceased is a waste paper contrary to Shariah. Ref: 2024 YLR 1394.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: No Limitation Against Wrong Entry in Inheritance
records.heading: No limitation runs against a wrong entry in matters of inheritance
records.text: No limitation runs against a wrong entry, and a mutation is not a starting point of limitation. In matters of inheritance, limitation does not bar a person from obtaining his share. Ref: 2024 YLR 1394.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Grandchildren's Share Under S. 4 of Ordinance 1961
records.heading: Grandchildren take their deceased parent's share under section 4 of the 1961 Ordinance
records.text: Under s. 4 of the Ordinance, 1961, grandchildren receive the share their deceased parent would have taken, whether the parent died before or after the Ordinance, provided succession opened after its promulgation. Ref: 2024 YLR 1394.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Breaking of Tooth: S. 334 PPC, Not S. 337-U
records.heading: Breaking of a tooth is punishable under section 334 PPC and not section 337-U
records.text: S. 337-U PPC is not listed as an offence in Schedule II of the CrPC and is merely an explanatory and controlling provision. Itlaf of a tooth is punishable under s. 334 PPC. Ref: 2024 YLR 1321, PLJ 2023 CrC 1074; Sajjad Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 25688/23).
records.title: Sajjad Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 25688/23)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Open Transfer Deed Does Not Transfer Vehicle Ownership
records.heading: An open transfer deed does not transfer ownership of a vehicle
records.text: An open transfer deed is not a valid title document and does not transfer ownership of a vehicle under the Ordinance. If the transferee does not apply to the Motor Registering Authority for change of ownership within 30 days, the transfer is null and void under s. 32 of the Ordinance. Ref: 2024 YLR 1382; Muhammad Akram v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 51580/M/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 51580/M/2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail for Delay in Trial; Abscondence
records.heading: Statutory bail for delay in trial is a right and abscondence does not bar it
records.text: The period for statutory bail on delay in concluding the trial is counted from the date of the petitioner's arrest. Under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, which uses the word shall, bail on this ground is a right, so earlier abscondence cannot bar it. Ref: 2024 YLR 1369; Riaz Shah v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 40039/22).
records.title: Riaz Shah v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 40039/22)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Evidence: Corroborative Value Only for Prosecution
records.heading: DNA evidence is only corroborative for the prosecution but may disprove the charge
records.text: The prosecution bears a heavier burden than the accused, who may create doubt. DNA evidence can be used by the prosecution only as corroboratory evidence, while it has probative value for disproving the charge. Failure to prove proper sampling of internal anal swabs was noted. Ref: 2024 YLR 1127; The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55-19).
records.title: The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55-19)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 38 to 40 QSO: Discovery Statements of Accused
records.heading: Article 40 QSO admits only the portion of an accused's statement leading to discovery
records.text: Under Arts. 38 and 39 QSO a confession to a police officer is inadmissible, and Art. 40 admits only the portion of an accused's statement leading to discovery of a fact, not his confession of the crime. The fact must be previously unknown, perceivable by the senses and related to the fact in issue, and a disclosure memo must be prepared. Ref: 2024 YLR 1127; The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55-19).
records.title: The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: Proximity of Time and Distance
records.heading: Last seen evidence requires proof of proximity of time and distance
records.text: To rest a conviction on circumstantial evidence, the prosecution must prove proximity of time and of distance in last seen evidence. Even if proved, it gives rise only to a probability of involvement and must be considered with other circumstances and strong corroboration. Ref: 2024 YLR 1127; The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55-19).
records.title: The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Need for Caution
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence is valid but courts must evaluate it with vigilance
records.text: Circumstantial evidence is recognised in Islamic law as Alqarain, with reference to the account of Prophet Yusuf in Surah Yousaf. Courts must still be vigilant in evaluating it, as it may be crafted by planting false witnesses. Ref: 2024 YLR 1127; The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55-19).
records.title: The State v. Nadeem Shah (Murder Reference 55-19)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Consistency, Fraud, Other Cases
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail follows consistency where the principal accused has post-arrest bail
records.text: Where the principal accused has post-arrest bail, refusing pre-arrest bail on technical grounds would be futile given consistency. Mere fraud of a huge amount is no ground to refuse bail, merits may be touched on in pre-arrest bail, and registration of other cases does not disentitle an accused with a prima facie case. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 124; Ch. Saeed Ahmad Khalil v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab another (Crl.P. 701/2023).
records.title: Ch. Saeed Ahmad Khalil v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab another (Crl.P. 701/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Leading Questions: Arts. 136 and 137 QSO
records.heading: Leading questions under Articles 136 and 137 QSO during examination of a witness
records.text: Authority on leading questions under Arts. 136 and 137 QSO, covering the guidelines and parameters and their admissibility during examination of a witness. Ref: Ishaq v. The State etc (Criminal Revision No. 311-P of 2023, decided 13.05.2024).
records.title: Ishaq v. The State etc (Criminal Revision No. 311-P of 2023, decided 13.05.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama: Presumption of Truth for Two Parts Only
records.heading: Only the first and fourth parts of a nikahnama enjoy a presumption of truth
records.text: A nikahnama is a public document with a presumption of truth, but only the first and fourth parts, kept with the Nikah Khawan in the register and forwarded to the Union Council, enjoy that presumption, as they are in official custody. Ref: 2021 LHC 9385; Ejaz Iqbal v. ADJ etc (Writ Petition-3075-21, decided 23.11.2021); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Ejaz Iqbal v. ADJ etc (Writ Petition-3075-21, decided 23.11.2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pendency in Higher Court Does Not Stay Proceedings
records.heading: A petition in the Supreme Court does not automatically stay lower court proceedings
records.text: Under O. XX R. 1 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980, execution and trial proceedings do not stay automatically on filing a petition in the Supreme Court without an injunctive order. A trial court that stays or adjourns sine die without such an order faces the consequences of that illegal order. Ref: Rashid Baig, etc v. Muhammad Mansha, etc (C.P.L.A. 925-L/2018, decided 29.04.2024); Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Rashid Baig, etc v. Muhammad Mansha, etc (C.P.L.A. 925-L/2018, decided 29.04.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Live Broadcast of Court Proceedings
records.heading: Whether to allow live broadcast of proceedings lies exclusively with the Court
records.text: A request to live broadcast or live-stream proceedings may be made and objected to, but as matters stand it lies in the exclusive domain of the Court to allow or decline it. Ref: Islamic Republic of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice, Govt. of Pakistan, Islamabad v. Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and another (I.C.A. 2/2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Islamic Republic of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice, Govt. of Pakistan, Islamabad v. Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and another (I.C.A. 2/2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Challenge to Registered Power of Attorney: Specific Pleadings
records.heading: A registered power of attorney can be challenged only on specific pleadings
records.text: A document can be challenged only on specific pleadings. The plaintiff denied ever appointing an attorney, yet his own witness from the Sub-Registrar office produced the registration record confirming the executor's and witnesses' signatures. The petition was converted into an appeal and accepted, so the trial court's dismissal of the suit stood. Ref: Shah Madar Khan v. Tariq Daud and others (C.P.L.A. 3877/2023, decided 09.05.2024); Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Shah Madar Khan v. Tariq Daud and others (C.P.L.A. 3877/2023, decided 09.05.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marking of Exhibit Does Not Dispense With Proof
records.heading: Marking a document as an exhibit does not dispense with proving it
records.text: Marking a document as an exhibit does not dispense with proving it, and documents not brought on record through witnesses cannot be considered. Reading documents in evidence without observing Art. 76 QSO is illegal, and the trial court exceeded its jurisdiction in recording documentary evidence. Ref: 2024 YLR 1199; Muhammad Aslam v. Muhammad Ismail (Civil Revision No. 22357 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. Muhammad Ismail (Civil Revision No. 22357 of 2020)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Inheritance Claims After Third-Party Rights Created
records.heading: Heirs must be vigilant once third-party rights have been created in good faith
records.text: Where third-party rights have been created in good faith for consideration, heirs must be vigilant, and the claimant bears the burden of proving he was unaware of being deprived of his share. A suit by an heir disregarded in the inheritance mutation is easier than one brought after third-party rights arose. If the injured person does not sue in time, no fresh limitation arises for his heirs. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 600; Khaleelullah v. Muhaim Khan (Civil Appeal No. 25-Q of 2018).
records.title: Khaleelullah v. Muhaim Khan (Civil Appeal No. 25-Q of 2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification of Recovered Articles Before Magistrate
records.heading: Recovered articles must be identified before a Magistrate and kept sealed
records.text: The PFSA's role is to help police collect and package articles with biological stains or fingerprints, not to take them for analysis. Recovered articles must be identified before a Magistrate like a suspect, under Art. 22 QSO, and witnesses must not see them after recovery. Property should be sealed on recovery and kept sealed until produced. Ref: 2024 LHC 2718; Muhammad Umar etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 58520/20, decided 14.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Umar etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 58520/20, decided 14.05.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 129(g) QSO: Adverse Inference for Withheld Witnesses
records.heading: Withholding key witnesses attracts an adverse inference under Article 129(g) QSO
records.text: Under Art. 129(g) QSO the Court may presume that evidence which could be produced but is withheld would be unfavourable to the party withholding it. Key witnesses on the abductee's narration and the ransom calls were not produced, so an adverse inference was drawn and the prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1146; Abdul Qadeer v. The State (J.P. 238/2008).
records.title: Abdul Qadeer v. The State (J.P. 238/2008)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade Without Role of Accused
records.heading: Identification of an accused without reference to his role has no evidentiary value
records.text: Identification of an accused without reference to the role he played in the occurrence has no evidentiary value. Here the accused objected that he had been shown to the abductee at a police office, and the parade memo did not specify his role. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1146; Abdul Qadeer v. The State (J.P. 238/2008).
records.title: Abdul Qadeer v. The State (J.P. 238/2008)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Kidnapping for Ransom: Unproved Recovery and Missing CDR
records.heading: Kidnapping for ransom not proved without bank record, CDR or independent corroboration
records.text: The prosecution failed to prove kidnapping for ransom as no bank record or CDR was produced, the cash recovery lacked independent corroboration, and the FIR was delayed two days. The abductee and complainant made improvements, so the charge was not proved beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1146; Abdul Qadeer v. The State (J.P. 238/2008).
records.title: Abdul Qadeer v. The State (J.P. 238/2008)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. II R. 2 CPC: Second Suit for Earnest Money
records.heading: A second suit for earnest money is not barred by Order II Rule 2 CPC
records.text: A second suit for recovery of earnest money, based on alleged cancellation of the agreement to sell by mutual consent, had a different cause of action from the earlier withdrawn suit for specific performance founded on illegal cancellation. It was not barred by O. II R. 2 CPC. Appeal allowed and the trial court directed to decide the second suit on merits. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 663.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 6 ATA: Ingredients of Terrorism
records.heading: Offences driven by personal or financial motives are not terrorism under section 6 ATA
records.text: Whether an offence falls within s. 6 ATA is determined from the FIR, the record and surrounding circumstances, examining motivation, objective, design or purpose and whether public fear and insecurity was instilled. Offences driven by personal or financial motives, however heinous, are not terrorism. A short kidnapping for ransom by financially motivated accused lacked the required mens rea. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1169, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 299; Imtiaz Latif v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1690-L/2016).
records.title: Imtiaz Latif v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1690-L/2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Defence Plea and Statement under S. 342 CrPC
records.heading: A defence plea must be accepted if it might reasonably be true
records.text: The Court should first assess the prosecution evidence independently and then the s. 342 statement, s. 340(2) statement and defence evidence. Where versions conflict, the defence plea must be weighed against the accusation. Even if the accused fails to establish the plea to the Court's satisfaction, the plea must be accepted if it might reasonably be true. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1191; Muhammad Imtiaz Baig v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1288-L/2017).
records.title: Muhammad Imtiaz Baig v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1288-L/2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested Witnesses: Unexplained Presence at Scene
records.heading: Interested witnesses with unexplained presence cannot support a capital sentence without corroboration
records.text: Testimony of interested witnesses must be scrutinised with care and needs independent corroboration, and capital punishment cannot rest on uncorroborated interested testimony. Here the closely related eye-witnesses had unexplained presence at the scene, the complainant brother was uninjured, and the ocular account was contradictory. The prosecution failed to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1085, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 178; Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl.P.L.A.887-L/2013).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl.P.L.A.887-L/2013)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Weapon Without Forensic Report
records.heading: A weapon recovery carries no significance without a forensic report linking it to the crime
records.text: Recovery of the sota six days after the occurrence, unstained with blood and with nothing on record showing it was sent to the forensic science laboratory, carried no significance as it was not established as the murder weapon. The Investigating Officer should have sent it for forensic examination. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1085; Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl.P.L.A.887-L/2013).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl.P.L.A.887-L/2013)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Importance of Forensic Science in Criminal Justice
records.heading: Forensic science provides objective evidence essential to the criminal justice system
records.text: The Court emphasised the importance of forensic science in the criminal justice system, describing it as the application of scientific techniques to provide objective, circumstantial evidence for the detection and prosecution of crime and for assessing the degree of guilt of a suspect. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1085; Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl.P.L.A.887-L/2013).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl.P.L.A.887-L/2013)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Fair Investigation and Art. 10A Due Process
records.heading: Article 10A requires fair investigation and prosecution of the accused
records.text: Effective functioning of the investigating agency and prosecution is the cornerstone of criminal justice, and Art. 10A requires that the accused be fairly investigated and prosecuted. The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. The Court observed that faulty investigation erodes public confidence and that investigation should be specialised and separated from other police duties. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1085, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 178; Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl.P.L.A.887-L/2013).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl.P.L.A.887-L/2013)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikah Nama Entries: Free Consent of Bride
records.heading: Ambiguity in a Nikah Nama entry is resolved in favour of the wife
records.text: In interpreting a Nikah Nama, courts must consider the bride's free consent and freedom to settle its terms with informed understanding. Ambiguity or doubt in an entry must be resolved in favour of the wife unless the evidence preponderantly shows she was informed, understood each column and freely negotiated the terms. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1078; Muhammad Yousaf v. Huma Saeed and others (C.P.L.A.2673/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Huma Saeed and others (C.P.L.A.2673/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Column 17 of Nikah Nama: Plot Granted to Wife
records.heading: Courts cannot read a condition into column 17 of a Nikah Nama
records.text: The form and headings of a Nikah Nama are not conclusive and the intent of the parties governs. Column 17 described a plot explicitly with no stipulated condition, and courts cannot read in a condition not expressly provided. The High Court rightly held the divorced wife entitled to the plot. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1078; Muhammad Yousaf v. Huma Saeed and others (C.P.L.A.2673/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Huma Saeed and others (C.P.L.A.2673/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A CrPC: Limited Role of Justice of Peace
records.heading: A Justice of Peace under section 22-A CrPC cannot conduct a full inquiry
records.text: Under s. 22-A CrPC the Justice of Peace need only see whether a cognizable case is made out from the application and may then direct recording of the statement under s. 154. He cannot conduct a full inquiry or act as investigator or prosecutor. A person refused registration of an FIR may approach the Justice of Peace, who must examine the application after hearing the parties. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1123; Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A.99-K/2018).
records.title: Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A.99-K/2018)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 169 and 173 CrPC: Registration of FIR and Arrest
records.heading: Mere registration of an FIR does not justify arrest without tangible evidence
records.text: Mere registration of an FIR does not imply conviction. Section 169 CrPC requires release of the accused where investigation discloses insufficient evidence or reasonable ground, and s. 173 governs the police report. The proposed accused should not be arrested without tangible evidence, and a false FIR may expose the complainant to action under s. 182 CrPC. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1123; Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A.99-K/2018).
records.title: Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A.99-K/2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Adjournments: O. XVII R. 3 CPC
records.heading: Courts must not grant adjournments liberally and may decide the suit forthwith on default
records.text: Frequent adjournment requests in lower courts amount to abuse of process and contribute to backlog, and courts must not grant adjournments liberally without compelling reasons. Order XVII R. 3 CPC empowers the court to decide the suit forthwith where a party granted time fails to act. A court giving a last opportunity must stand by its commitment. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 672; Duniya Gul and another v. Niaz Muhammad and others (C.P.920-P/2023).
records.title: Duniya Gul and another v. Niaz Muhammad and others (C.P.920-P/2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Proposed Amendment: Refund of Earnest Money in Specific Performance Suit
records.heading: Supreme Court proposes amending the Specific Relief Act to allow refund of earnest money
records.text: After 19 years of two rounds of litigation arising from one sale agreement, the Supreme Court proposed amendment of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 so that a plaintiff suing for specific performance of a contract for transfer of immovable property may also seek possession or partition, or other relief including refund of earnest money if specific performance is refused. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 663; Matloob Ellahi Paracha v. Raja Arshad Mahmood and another (Civil Appeal No.1877 of 2016, decided 14.11.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Matloob Ellahi Paracha v. Raja Arshad Mahmood and another (Civil Appeal No.1877 of 2016, decided 14.11.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 97 Limitation Act: Recovery of Earnest Money
records.heading: Article 97 Limitation Act governs a suit for earnest money after failure of consideration
records.text: A suit to recover earnest money after the first suit for specific performance was withdrawn is governed by Art. 97 Limitation Act, 1908, for money paid on consideration that afterwards fails. Limitation of three years runs from failure of consideration, here the dismissal of the first suit as withdrawn. The second suit was within time and the trial court was directed to decide it on merits. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 663.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare Principle
records.heading: The welfare of the minor is the foundational principle in custody disputes
records.text: The welfare and best interests of the minor are the foundational principle in custody disputes. A custody decision made without assessing and determining the child's welfare, considering the relevant factors, cannot be sustained and the exercise of discretion is not lawful. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 629.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Mother's Second Marriage Not Bar to Custody
records.heading: A mother's second marriage is not a bar to custody of her child
records.text: A mother's second marriage is not a bar to custody. The minor, mature enough to form preferences, regarded his father as a stranger and was comfortable with his mother and step father, and the father had made no serious effort to build a relationship. The Court expected the parents to settle the custody dispute amicably with a visitation schedule serving the child's welfare. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 629.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation: Government Departments Not Entitled to Preferential Treatment
records.heading: Government departments get no preferential treatment on limitation and condonation of delay
records.text: Limitation is not a mere technicality, as expiry of the period vests valuable rights in the other party. Under ss. 3 and 5 of the Limitation Act, delay by governments, departments or autonomous bodies can be condoned only on sufficient grounds, and absent such grounds they are treated like ordinary litigants. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 698.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Articles Construed by Plain Language
records.heading: Articles of the Limitation Act are construed according to their plain language
records.text: The law of limitation is a disabling provision, so its various Articles are to be construed according to their plain language. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 663.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Woman Must Expressly Seek It
records.heading: A court cannot grant khula unless the wife expressly seeks it
records.text: Khula is the exclusive and absolute right of the woman, who must unambiguously offer before the court to seek release from the marriage by waiving her dower. A court cannot grant a decree of khula on its own where she has not sought it, as her consent is vital. Here the wife had sought dissolution on the ground of cruelty and claimed her dower. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 645, PLJ 2024 SC 505; Ibrahim Khan v. Mst. Saima Khan and others (C.Ps. No. 4657 to 4659 of 2022, decided 15.2.2024); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Ibrahim Khan v. Mst. Saima Khan and others (C.Ps. No. 4657 to 4659 of 2022, decided 15.2.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula and Re-marriage Without Halala
records.heading: A woman dissolving marriage by khula may re-marry the same man without halala
records.text: Khula is a special right of the woman not available to a man. A woman who obtains dissolution by khula can re-marry the same man without an intervening marriage (halala). Ref: PLD 2024 SC 645; Ibrahim Khan v. Mst. Saima Khan and others (C.Ps. No. 4657 to 4659 of 2022, decided 15.2.2024); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Ibrahim Khan v. Mst. Saima Khan and others (C.Ps. No. 4657 to 4659 of 2022, decided 15.2.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 517 CrPC: Disposal of Case Property on Acquittal
records.heading: Disposal of case property on acquittal is regulated by the lower court under section 517 CrPC
records.text: Unless the High Court directs otherwise on acquittal, disposal of case property is regulated by the lower Court under s. 517 CrPC. Ref: 2024 LHC 2802; Muhammad Shamoon v. The State (Crl. Revision 31115/21, decided 16.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Shamoon v. The State (Crl. Revision 31115/21, decided 16.05.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Reasonable Grounds Under s. 497(2) CrPC: Tentative Assessment
records.heading: Reasonable grounds under section 497(2) CrPC require tentative appraisal of the whole record
records.text: Whether reasonable grounds exist for believing the accused committed the offence under s. 497(2) CrPC requires tentative appraisal of the whole material on record, and cannot be decided by examining the FIR alone. The tentative assessment of evidence collected in investigation, both for and against the accused, is determinative. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1071, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 1; Muhammad Atif v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Atif v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Grounds of Bail in Prohibitory Clause Offences
records.heading: Post-arrest bail in prohibitory clause offences rests on three recognised grounds
records.text: In offences within the prohibitory clause of s. 497(1) CrPC, post-arrest bail is granted on three grounds: the first proviso (minor, woman, or sick or infirm person), the third proviso (delay in trial beyond the prescribed period through no fault of the accused), and s. 497(2) (no reasonable grounds, but sufficient grounds for further inquiry). Ref: 2024 SCMR 1071, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 1; Muhammad Atif v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Atif v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 154 and 155 CrPC: Duty to Register FIR
records.heading: A police officer cannot inquire into the truth of information before registering an FIR
records.text: No provision, including ss. 154 or 155 CrPC, authorises an Officer Incharge of a Police Station to inquire into the truth of the information before reducing it into writing. The condition for recording an FIR is information of a cognizable offence. A direct complaint cannot replace the s. 154 mechanism, though it may be availed in exceptional circumstances. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1123; Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A.99-K/2018).
records.title: Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A.99-K/2018)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Maintenance of Police Station Diary
records.heading: The Station Diary must be maintained under the Police Order and Rules, including a soft copy
records.text: The Station Diary (Roznamcha) is the most significant document at a police station, designed to check police powers, and is maintained under Art. 167 of the Police Order and Rules 22.48 and 22.49 of the Police Rules. A soft copy must be prepared in addition to the manual record and directions on its maintenance were issued. The District Police Officer should inspect diaries regularly under Art. 167(2). Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1014; Jamila Bibi v. S.H.O P.S Baghban Pura Lahore etc. (Criminal Proceedings 79470/23).
records.title: Jamila Bibi v. S.H.O P.S Baghban Pura Lahore etc. (Criminal Proceedings 79470/23)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Alternate Remedy and Proof of Mala Fide Against Government
records.heading: A person alleging mala fide against government must plead particulars and bears the onus
records.text: Courts show restraint and direct parties to the alternative efficacious remedy under the maxim ubi jus ibi remedium. A person alleging mala fide against government bears the onus, as official acts are presumed regular, must plead particulars of the mala fide, and cannot be allowed a roving enquiry into government files. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1037, PLJ 2024 CrC 109; Mian Arif Said v. Province of Punjab.
records.title: Mian Arif Said v. Province of Punjab

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Decree on Attorney's Statement
records.heading: A decree on an attorney's purported no-objection statement was not sustainable
records.text: A suit for specific performance was decreed four days after filing, before the return date of summons, on the purported no-objection statement of the defendant's attorney, without ante-dating or proper consideration. The decree was not sustainable, and the defendant's application under s. 12(2) CPC was maintainable and rightly allowed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1106; Ejaz Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Pasroor.
records.title: Ejaz Ahmad v. Additional District Judge, Pasroor

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Deficient Court Fee: Conditional Order and Extension of Time
records.heading: Extension of time for deficient court fee without request or time frame was unjustified
records.text: Time to make good the Court fee deficiency was allowed under s. 149 CPC on condition that the plaint would be deemed rejected on default. The Trial Court's later extension, without a request and without fixing a time frame, was perfunctory, unjustified and unwarranted. The Revisional Court rightly set it aside and the High Court rightly maintained that. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1059; Kh. Muhammad Fazil v. Mumtaz Munnawar Khan Niazi.
records.title: Kh. Muhammad Fazil v. Mumtaz Munnawar Khan Niazi

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 149 CPC: Discretion to Allow Payment of Deficient Court Fee
records.heading: Section 149 CPC allows payment of deficient court fee on plausible grounds
records.text: Section 149 CPC is an exception to ss. 4 and 6 of the Court Fees Act, 1870. Discretion is generally exercised in favour of a litigant showing plausible reasons such as bona fide miscalculation, unavailability of stamps or circumstances beyond control, and only where sufficient grounds for non-payment are made out. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1059; Kh. Muhammad Fazil v. Mumtaz Munnawar Khan Niazi.
records.title: Kh. Muhammad Fazil v. Mumtaz Munnawar Khan Niazi

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 13 CPC: Fresh Plaint After Rejection for Court Fee
records.heading: Rejection of a plaint for court fee does not bar a fresh plaint within limitation
records.text: Under O. VII R. 13 CPC rejection of a plaint does not of its own force preclude presenting a fresh plaint on the same cause of action. Where rejection is for non-payment of Court fee and not for another cause such as limitation, the plaintiff may present a fresh plaint within limitation. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1059; Kh. Muhammad Fazil v. Mumtaz Munnawar Khan Niazi.
records.title: Kh. Muhammad Fazil v. Mumtaz Munnawar Khan Niazi

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 148 CPC: Enlargement of Time
records.heading: Time may be enlarged under section 148 CPC after expiry but only judiciously
records.text: The Court may enlarge time under s. 148 CPC even after the original period has expired, but this discretion must be exercised reasonably and judiciously, and not arbitrarily, capriciously or whimsically. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1059; Kh. Muhammad Fazil v. Mumtaz Munnawar Khan Niazi.
records.title: Kh. Muhammad Fazil v. Mumtaz Munnawar Khan Niazi

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal: Double Presumption of Innocence
records.heading: Interference in an appeal against acquittal is narrow because of the double presumption of innocence
records.text: Interference in an appeal against acquittal is narrow and limited because acquittal adds to the presumption of innocence. Courts interfere only if the judgment is perverse, in gross violation of law, or suffers from grave misreading or non-reading of evidence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1116; Sardaran Bibi v. The State.
records.title: Sardaran Bibi v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Doubt Sufficient
records.heading: A single doubt is enough to extend the benefit of doubt to the accused
records.text: For giving benefit of doubt many circumstances are not required, as a single doubt is enough to extend the benefit to the accused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1116; Sardaran Bibi v. The State.
records.title: Sardaran Bibi v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 302(b) PPC: Acquittal Upheld on Doubtful Evidence
records.heading: Acquittal under section 302(b) PPC upheld where improvements and doubtful motive left the case doubtful
records.text: The High Court rightly acquitted where witnesses made marked improvements inconsistent with medical evidence, the complainant's statements varied, the incident occurred in darkness, two female witnesses were not produced and the motive was doubtful. The case was fraught with doubts, and the acquittal did not warrant interference. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1116; Sardaran Bibi v. The State.
records.title: Sardaran Bibi v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Concurrent Running of Sentences in Different Cases
records.heading: Section 397 CrPC permits sentences in different cases to run concurrently
records.text: Section 397 CrPC gives the Court wide discretion to direct that sentences of a convict in different trials run concurrently, and the Court should not deny this benefit in a suitable case. The High Court's jurisdiction under s. 561-A CrPC may be invoked where the appellate Court has not consciously denied the benefit. Sentences were directed to run concurrently. Ref: 2024 LHC 2860; Sher Afzal v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 729-M-24, decided 29.05.2024); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan.
records.title: Sher Afzal v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 729-M-24, decided 29.05.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 497 CrPC: Bail to Woman Under First Proviso
records.heading: The first proviso to section 497 CrPC is beneficial legislation for women, subject to their conduct
records.text: The first proviso to s. 497 CrPC is beneficial legislation permitting bail to a woman in offences within the prohibitory clause. In granting such bail the Court should also consider the applicant's conduct and whether she has a criminal record or is a habitual offender. Vicarious liability may be examined at the bail stage where the FIR shows preconcert or common intention. Ref: Mst. Ishrat Bibi v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.L.A.243/2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mst. Ishrat Bibi v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.L.A.243/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unproved Motive as Mitigating Circumstance
records.heading: Failure to prove motive may mitigate the quantum of sentence
records.text: Under settled principles, failure of the prosecution to prove the alleged motive can be considered a mitigating circumstance for reducing the quantum of sentence. Ref: Khalid v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.668/2019, decided 05.06.2024); Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: Khalid v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.668/2019, decided 05.06.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Pleadings may be amended at any stage if necessary to decide the real controversy
records.text: Under O. VI R. 17 CPC pleadings may be amended at any stage where necessary to decide the real question in controversy. Amendment is allowed where it avoids multiplicity of suits, does not alter the subject matter or cause of action, takes away no accrued right and causes no injustice. The list is not exhaustive. Ref: 2024 LHC 2864; Iftikhar Ahmad v. Muhammad Anwar, etc (C.R. No.20763 of 2024).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmad v. Muhammad Anwar, etc (C.R. No.20763 of 2024)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 6 ATA: Heinousness Alone Not Terrorism
records.heading: An act is not terrorism under section 6 ATA however heinous if an ingredient is absent
records.text: Where any ingredient of s. 6 ATA 1997 is absent, an act does not fall within terrorism, however heinous and whether or not it causes terror or a sense of fear and insecurity in society. Ref: 2024 SCP 195; Javed Iqbal v. The State (J.P.233/2015, decided 26.03.2024); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State (J.P.233/2015, decided 26.03.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitnesses Not Accompanying Deceased to Hospital
records.heading: Eyewitnesses who did not accompany the deceased to hospital were probably absent from the scene
records.text: The real father and brother of the deceased, claiming to be eyewitnesses, did not accompany the deceased to hospital and were not mentioned in the inquest or post-mortem reports as identifiers of the body. This fact alone strongly suggests their absence from the scene. Ref: 2024 SCP 197; Iftikhar Hussain @ Kharoo v. The State (J.P.195/2017, decided 08.05.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Iftikhar Hussain @ Kharoo v. The State (J.P.195/2017, decided 08.05.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence and Burden of Proof
records.heading: The presumption of innocence continues until guilt is proved beyond reasonable doubt
records.text: The presumption of innocence remains until the prosecution proves guilt beyond reasonable doubt, and the burden never shifts except in cases under Art. 121 QSO. The accused need not produce evidence, and the presumption alone warrants acquittal unless the Court is fully convinced of guilt. Ref: 2024 SCP 197; Iftikhar Hussain @ Kharoo v. The State (J.P.195/2017, decided 08.05.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Iftikhar Hussain @ Kharoo v. The State (J.P.195/2017, decided 08.05.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Art. 46 QSO
records.heading: A dying declaration under Article 46 QSO must be scrutinised with great care
records.text: A dying declaration under Art. 46 QSO must be evaluated with great care and caution on the facts of each case. It may be made before a private person but must be free from influence, and that person must be examined. The Court must ascertain that it was honest, the maker was fit of mind, free from outside influence, fearing death and truthful. Ref: 2024 SCP 190; Muhammad Saeed v. The State thr. A.G, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A.968/2017, decided 20.05.2024); Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: Muhammad Saeed v. The State thr. A.G, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A.968/2017, decided 20.05.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody in CNSA Cases
records.heading: A missing link in the chain of custody of narcotics samples benefits the accused
records.text: The prosecution must establish every step from recovery, preparation and safe custody of sample parcels to their safe transmission to the laboratory, and a missing link benefits the accused. The witness who transmitted the samples must be produced. Rule 4(2) of the 2001 Government Analysts Rules requires dispatch within seventy two hours of seizure, and Rule 22.70 Police Rules governs Register No. XIX. Ref: 2024 SCP 192; Asif Ali S/o Zafar Ali & another v. The State P.G. Punjab (Crl.P.L.A.1602/2023, decided 22.05.2024); Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: Asif Ali S/o Zafar Ali & another v. The State P.G. Punjab (Crl.P.L.A.1602/2023, decided 22.05.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Order of Acquittal Under S. 249-A: Revision and Writ Not Competent
records.heading: Neither revision nor writ is competent against an acquittal order under section 249-A CrPC
records.text: Against an order of acquittal under s. 249-A CrPC, a criminal revision under s. 439 CrPC is not competent. A writ petition against such an order is also not competent in light of s. 417(2) CrPC. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1081, PLJ 2024 Lahore 362; Hajra Javaid Makhdoom v. Muhammad Tehmas Nasir etc (Criminal Proceedings 59534/22).
records.title: Hajra Javaid Makhdoom v. Muhammad Tehmas Nasir etc (Criminal Proceedings 59534/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Cannot Identify Assailant
records.heading: Medical evidence is confirmatory and cannot identify the assailant
records.text: Medical evidence is supportive and confirmatory. It can show the locale, nature, magnitude of injury and kind of weapon but cannot identify the assailant, and so was of no help to the prosecution on the facts. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1054; Mst. Gulnaz Ajmal v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 72371/19).
records.title: Mst. Gulnaz Ajmal v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 72371/19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recording Blood Group in Post-Mortem Report
records.heading: Recording the deceased's blood group in the post-mortem report aids forensic matching and DNA testing
records.text: Where the doctor notes the deceased's blood group in the post-mortem report, it helps ascertain the blood group on blood stained cotton from the scene, the deceased's clothes and the weapon, and assists DNA testing. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1054; Mst. Gulnaz Ajmal v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 72371/19).
records.title: Mst. Gulnaz Ajmal v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 72371/19)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Condonation of Delay in Appeal Against Acquittal Under CNSA
records.heading: Section 5 of the Limitation Act does not apply to appeals against acquittal under CNSA
records.text: Section 29(2) of the Limitation Act excludes the application of s. 5 for condonation of delay in filing an appeal against acquittal under s. 48 CNSA 1997. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1111; State v. Muhammad Imran (Crl. Appeal-Against Acquittal-CNSA 275-20).
records.title: State v. Muhammad Imran (Crl. Appeal-Against Acquittal-CNSA 275-20)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 249-A CrPC: Acquittal Application at Any Stage
records.heading: An accused may apply for acquittal under section 249-A CrPC at any stage
records.text: Section 249-A CrPC places no embargo on the accused applying for acquittal at any stage. The Court must hear the prosecutor and the accused and, if the charge is groundless or conviction improbable, acquit by a reasoned order. The powers under ss. 249-A and 265-K are similar to the High Court's powers under s. 561-A. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1143; Rana Muhammad Yousaf Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 61551/22).
records.title: Rana Muhammad Yousaf Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 61551/22)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cross-Version After Conclusion of Trial
records.heading: After trial concludes, a person with a cross-version may only file a private complaint
records.text: No law permits recording a statement under s. 161 CrPC once a case is decided. Sughran Bibi prohibits only a second FIR, so a cross-version may be permitted while the trial is pending. After the original FIR has run its course, the remedy for a person seeking to prosecute on a cross-version is a private complaint. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1168; Zubaida Khanum v. District Police Officer etc. (WP No. 18561/2021).
records.title: Zubaida Khanum v. District Police Officer etc. (WP No. 18561/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Belated Recording of Witness Statements Under S. 161 CrPC
records.heading: Belated recording of witness statements under section 161 CrPC casts serious doubt on the prosecution
records.text: The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that recording the statements of witnesses under s. 161 CrPC at a belated stage casts serious doubt on the prosecution version. Ref: Khiyal Muhammad v. The State (Crl.A.36/2023, decided 23.05.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Khiyal Muhammad v. The State (Crl.A.36/2023, decided 23.05.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift: Limitation Where Donor Does Not Challenge Adverse Entry
records.heading: A donor who does not challenge an adverse entry within limitation is barred
records.text: If a purported seller or donor, with knowledge, does not challenge denial of his right within limitation, the claim is barred, and repetition of the wrong entry in later revenue records gives no fresh cause of action. Failure of a donor to challenge an adverse entry in her or his lifetime is hit by limitation. Ref: 2024 CLC 1137; Muhammad Azram v. Muhammad Altaf etc (Civil Revision-573-14).
records.title: Muhammad Azram v. Muhammad Altaf etc (Civil Revision-573-14)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 42 Specific Relief Act: Declaration Without Possession
records.heading: A plaintiff out of possession cannot seek a bare declaration without seeking possession
records.text: Where possession is admittedly not with the plaintiff, he is precluded from claiming a bare declaration unless he also seeks the relief of possession. The post also refers to the scope of s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Ref: 2024 CLC 1137; Muhammad Azram v. Muhammad Altaf etc (Civil Revision-573-14).
records.title: Muhammad Azram v. Muhammad Altaf etc (Civil Revision-573-14)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 6 Ordinance 1961: Complaint for Second Marriage
records.heading: Section 6 of the 1961 Ordinance restricts a second marriage without Arbitration Council permission
records.text: Section 6 of the 1961 Ordinance restricts a second marriage without the prior written permission of the Arbitration Council, and contravention is punishable under s. 6(5) with simple imprisonment up to one year and a fine of five hundred thousand rupees. The case concerns a wife's complaint filed through a special attorney, dismissed as not proceedable through an attorney, and the Rules framed under s. 11. Ref: 2024 CLC 1170; Sonia Sharief v. ADJ etc (WP 97-24); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Sonia Sharief v. ADJ etc (WP 97-24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Leave to Appear and Defend
records.heading: Limitation for a leave to defend application under Order XXXVII runs from appearance
records.text: Order XXXVII CPC is a special summary procedure for suits on negotiable instruments, where the defendant must seek leave to appear and defend under Rule 3 and, once leave is granted, the suit becomes a regular suit. Limitation for the leave application runs from the day the defendant enters appearance, so the trial court erred in dismissing it as time barred and decreeing the suit. Ref: 2024 CLC 1184; Muhammad Ali Khalid v. Muhammad Talha (RFA No. 6825 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Ali Khalid v. Muhammad Talha (RFA No. 6825 of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Reconciliation in Khula and Dissolution of Marriage Cases
records.heading: Lahore High Court judgment on reconciliation in khula and dissolution of marriage cases
records.text: Authority on reconciliation in cases of khula and dissolution of marriage, described as a detailed Lahore High Court judgment in a family writ petition. Ref: 2024 LHC 2988; Syed Asif Hussain Shah v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 167-24, decided 29.04.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Syed Asif Hussain Shah v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 167-24, decided 29.04.2024)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Margalla Hills National Park: Restaurants to Be Vacated
