records.heading: Restaurants within the Margalla Hills National Park must be vacated within three months
records.text: Margalla Hills National Park must be protected and conserved, and all restaurants operating within it are to be vacated within three months. The Wildlife Management Board is to be assisted by CDA. Kiosks must obtain a licence from the Board, remove their garbage outside the Park and keep fire extinguishers where stoves are used. The Urdu note adds that the restaurant leases were declared void. Ref: The Monal Group of Companies, Islamabad v. Capital Development Authority through its Chairman, Islamabad and others (C.P.L.A.304/2022, decided 11.06.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: The Monal Group of Companies, Islamabad v. Capital Development Authority through its Chairman, Islamabad and others (C.P.L.A.304/2022, decided 11.06.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX CPC, O. V R. 20 CPC and Arts. 163, 164, 181 Limitation Act
records.heading: Authority on Order IX, Order V Rule 20 CPC and Limitation Act Articles 163, 164 and 181
records.text: Authority discussing Order IX Rules 6 to 9 and 13 CPC, Order V Rule 20 CPC and Arts. 163, 164 and 181 of the Limitation Act. The post gives no holding. Ref: Muhammad Yousuf Bhindi v. M/s. A.G.E. & Sons (Pvt) Ltd. & others (C.P.L.A.1032-K/2023, decided 08.04.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Yousuf Bhindi v. M/s. A.G.E. & Sons (Pvt) Ltd. & others (C.P.L.A.1032-K/2023, decided 08.04.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Fake Police Encounters: Zero Tolerance
records.heading: Fake police encounters cannot be permitted in the guise of self-defence
records.text: Zero tolerance should be shown against fake police encounters, which cannot be permitted in the guise of self-defence by police officials. Ref: 2024 LHC 3047; Mst. Farzana Bibi v. C.C.P.O. Lahore etc (Crl. Misc.36448/24, decided 13.06.2024); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mst. Farzana Bibi v. C.C.P.O. Lahore etc (Crl. Misc.36448/24, decided 13.06.2024)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: S. 118 NI Act: Presumption on Mutilated Cheque
records.heading: A mutilated cheque keeps the section 118 presumption if key details are undamaged
records.text: The mutilated or torn condition of a negotiable instrument does not by itself remove the presumption of correctness under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, if key information such as payee, date, amount and signatures is undamaged. Ref: 2024 LHC 3063; Liaqat Ali v. Noor Ahmad (Regular First Appeal-338-21, decided 29.05.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. Noor Ahmad (Regular First Appeal-338-21, decided 29.05.2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Bail of Juvenile: S. 6(5) Juvenile Justice System Act 2018
records.heading: Delay ground for juvenile bail under section 6(5) applies only in heinous offences
records.text: The Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018 focuses on diversion, social reintegration and the best interest of the child. Since minor and major offences are bailable under s. 6(3), the ground of delay in conclusion of trial in s. 6(5) for bail applies only to juveniles detained for a heinous offence. Ref: Mehran v. Ubaid Ullah and others (Crl.P.L.A.80-P/2024, decided 29.05.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Mehran v. Ubaid Ullah and others (Crl.P.L.A.80-P/2024, decided 29.05.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Deposit of Balance Sale Consideration in Specific Performance
records.heading: The Specific Relief Act does not require deposit of balance consideration unless the court orders
records.text: The Specific Relief Act contains no provision requiring deposit of the balance sale consideration in Court unless so ordered. The plaintiff bears the initial burden of showing unequivocal readiness and willingness under Form 47, Appendix A, First Schedule CPC. The Court also noted the need to decide commercial and industrial cases with a proactive approach on priority. Ref: Mr. Meer Gul v. Mr. Raja Zafar Mehmood & others (C.A.51-K/2021, decided 04.04.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mr. Meer Gul v. Mr. Raja Zafar Mehmood & others (C.A.51-K/2021, decided 04.04.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive as Double-Edged Weapon and Delayed Post-Mortem
records.heading: Motive is double-edged and unexplained delay in post-mortem calls for careful scrutiny
records.text: Motive is a double-edged weapon that may support real or false involvement. Unexplained delay in the post-mortem calls for careful scrutiny of the prosecution evidence, as the natural inference is preliminary investigation and consultation to nominate the accused and plant eye-witnesses. The Court also discussed differences between hanging and strangulation. Ref: Muhammad Ijaz @ Billa v. The State (Crl.A.169/2023, decided 22.05.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz @ Billa v. The State (Crl.A.169/2023, decided 22.05.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Guilt Not Based on High Probabilities
records.heading: Guilt cannot rest merely on high probabilities inferred from the evidence
records.text: A finding of guilt cannot be based merely on high probabilities inferred from the evidence. Otherwise the golden rule of benefit of doubt, a dominant feature of criminal justice in this country, would be reduced to naught. Ref: Muhammad Ijaz @ Billa v. The State (Crl.A.169/2023, decided 22.05.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz @ Billa v. The State (Crl.A.169/2023, decided 22.05.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC: Statement of Accused Before Magistrate
records.heading: An accused's section 164 CrPC statement is not substantive evidence
records.text: If the investigating officer does not record the accused's statement according to his stance, he may appear before a Magistrate and have it recorded under s. 164 CrPC. The section authorises Magistrates to record statements before commencement of inquiry or trial, and the accused's s. 164 statement is not substantive evidence and its facts must be proved under the Qanun-e-Shahadat. Ref: Muhammad Asghar Ali Shah v. The State etc. (Writ Petition No. 3962/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asghar Ali Shah v. The State etc. (Writ Petition No. 3962/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail on Medical Grounds: Loss of Eyesight
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed in a murder case on medical grounds of total loss of sight
records.text: Post-arrest bail under s. 497 CrPC was allowed in a s. 302 PPC case on medical grounds, the accused having lost sight of both eyes in jail, as assessed by a five member Board. The observations were tentative, and the trial court was directed to conclude the trial without delay. Petition accepted. Ref: 2024 YLR 1619, PLJ 2024 CrC 852; Muhammad Akmal v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 1554-B of 2023, decided 11.9.2023); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Akmal v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 1554-B of 2023, decided 11.9.2023)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Bail of Juvenile in Heinous Offence: S. 4(6) JJSA 2018
records.heading: A juvenile connected with a heinous offence on reasonable grounds is not entitled to bail
records.text: Where reasonable grounds on the record connect the petitioner with a heinous offence, he does not deserve bail even on the ground of juvenility, in light of s. 4(6) of the Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018. Ref: 2024 MLD 1147, PLJ 2024 CrC 679; Abdul Rehman v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 62271/23).
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 62271/23)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Mobile Phone Conversation Through CD
records.heading: A mobile phone conversation cannot be proved merely by producing a CD
records.text: A conversation recorded on a mobile phone and converted into a CD cannot be proved merely by producing the CD, without production of the mobile phone and forensic analysis of the conversation. Ref: 2024 YLR 1510, PLJ 2024 CrC 720; Abu Bakar Samoosa etc v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 228667/18).
records.title: Abu Bakar Samoosa etc v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 228667/18)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused's Option of Place of Trial: District Headquarters or Sub-Division
records.heading: The Magistrate must offer the accused a choice of trial at the sub-division
records.text: Sessions cases should normally be tried at District Headquarters, but under Letter No. 7886/RHC/MIT dated 25.5.1999 the Magistrate must offer the accused a choice of trial at the sub-division when they appear under s. 190 CrPC and record that fact. The right to choose could not be denied. The Sessions Judge was directed to conclude the case within six months. Ref: 2024 MLD 1015; Muhammad Waqar alias Fauji v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No.76558/T/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Waqar alias Fauji v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No.76558/T/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Arrest in All Known Cases and Physical Remand in Other FIRs
records.heading: Police must show arrest in all known cases and may seek physical remand in other FIRs
records.text: When an accused is arrested, the investigating agency must show his arrest in all cases registered against him within its knowledge. Even after he is in judicial custody in one case, police may obtain his physical remand in FIRs at other police stations, districts or provinces with the permission of the concerned Magistrate or Court. Ref: 2024 YLR 1628, PLJ 2024 Lahore 404; Syed Faheem ul Hassan v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc. (W.P. No. 1075/24).
records.title: Syed Faheem ul Hassan v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc. (W.P. No. 1075/24)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Marrying Sister of Divorced Wife During Iddat: Bail Refused
records.heading: Marrying a divorced wife's sister during iddat carries criminal liability; pre-arrest bail declined
records.text: Marriage with the sister of a divorced wife before completion of her iddat parallels marrying two sisters together and carries criminal liability, though most Hanafi jurists hold hadd is not attracted and tazir must be inflicted. The petitioner's unproved divorce deed and added charges under ss. 420, 468 and 471 PPC weighed against him, and pre-arrest bail was declined. Ref: 2024 YLR 1653; Munawar Hussain v. The State and another (Criminal Miscellaneous No. 67328-B of 2023).
records.title: Munawar Hussain v. The State and another (Criminal Miscellaneous No. 67328-B of 2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Readiness and Willingness in Specific Performance
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary and may be refused for failure to pay the balance
records.text: Specific performance is discretionary and equitable, and may be refused to a plaintiff who contumaciously fails to comply with repeated directions to pay the balance consideration. The Court must find which party has not performed. A vendee is expected to sue promptly on refusal, showing readiness and willingness to deposit the balance, and performance is not judged from a date convenient to the plaintiff. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 351, 2025 CLC 513; Sh. Khalid Javaid v. Shams Ud Din Chishti (Civil Revision-323-22).
records.title: Sh. Khalid Javaid v. Shams Ud Din Chishti (Civil Revision-323-22)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutation: Fraud Particulars and Proof of Original Transaction
records.heading: A party pleading fraud must give particulars, and a mutation is not a title document
records.text: A party pleading fraud must give particulars under O. VI R. 4 CPC. A mutation is not a document of title but only an acknowledgment of the original transaction, which the person relying on it must establish first. The post also refers to Art. 113 QSO on admissions and to the declaratory suit provision. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 340, 2025 MLD 87; Mst. Munawar Jan etc v. Mst. Shufaidan Jan etc (Civil Revision 934-12).
records.title: Mst. Munawar Jan etc v. Mst. Shufaidan Jan etc (Civil Revision 934-12)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Hizanat and Walayat: Mother's Right of Custody
records.heading: A mother has a prior right of hizanat, distinct from the father's guardianship
records.text: Walayat (guardianship) differs from hizanat (custody). The father is natural guardian, but the mother has a prior right of custody until the prescribed age, to which the guardian's claim gives way. Waiver of hizanat has no binding force, and a mother does not lose the right on divorce except in the situations in Para 354 of Muhammadan Law, subject to the Guardian Court's determination. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lahore 413, PLD 2025 Lahore 540; Sadia Aziz v. DPO etc. (WP (habeas) 3109-24).
records.title: Sadia Aziz v. DPO etc. (WP (habeas) 3109-24)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Suspension of Sentence: Co-Accused Acquitted on Same Evidence
records.heading: Acquittal of a co-accused on the same evidence supports suspension of sentence
records.text: Where a co-accused with a similar or more effective role has been acquitted, conviction of the accused on the same evidence without corroboration requires reappraisal of the evidence, resulting in suspension of execution of the sentence. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 718; Muhammad Waseem v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal CM/1/20219/23).
records.title: Muhammad Waseem v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal CM/1/20219/23)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Videography of Narcotics Recoveries and Arrests
records.heading: Narcotics arrests and recoveries must be video recorded, with cameras for police and ANF
records.text: Noting frequent false implication in narcotics cases, the Court directed that arrest, recovery and other proceedings in narcotics cases be video recorded, with detailed reasons in a supplementary statement where that is impossible. The Government was directed to provide body worn and dashboard cameras to the police and ANF within six months, and compliance by Special Courts was ordered. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 736; Kousar Bibi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.-Post-arrest Bail 5175-B-23).
records.title: Kousar Bibi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.-Post-arrest Bail 5175-B-23)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cartridge Cases and Comparison by PFSA Where Accused Absconds
records.heading: Cartridge cases must be redeposited with PFSA for comparison where an accused absconds
records.text: Cartridge cases are to be submitted to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency, Lahore for comparison with the weapon. Where an accused is an absconder, the cartridge cases, after exhibition in the trial of another accused, are to be deposited again with PFSA until compared with the weapon recovered from the absconder. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 745; Abid Ali etc v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 29270/19).
records.title: Abid Ali etc v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 29270/19)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Arrest Requires Evidence: Suspicion or Reliable Source Insufficient
records.heading: Arrest cannot rest on suspicion or an undisclosed reliable source without evidence
records.text: Arrest cannot be made without evidence. A complainant's strong suspicion or firm belief, or a claim that he learned of involvement from an undisclosed reliable source or landlord's clue, is not legal evidence and arrest cannot rest solely on it. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 700; Rashida Bibi v. SHO etc. (Crl. Misc.-Habeas Corpus 4043-H-23).
records.title: Rashida Bibi v. SHO etc. (Crl. Misc.-Habeas Corpus 4043-H-23)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt by Advocate: Role of Bar Associations
records.heading: Contempt is between the Court and the contemnor; mass bar appearance gives an impression of pressure
records.text: In contempt proceedings against an advocate, the Court observed that contempt is a matter between the Court and the contemnor and allowed only three advocates to appear for him, noting that mass appearance of bar office bearers gives an impression of pressure. It expected Bar Associations to discourage strikes and lock downs of Courts. The Urdu heading refers to the advocate's punishment. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 762; The State v. Zahid Mehmood Goraya (Advocate) (Criminal Original 20741/24).
records.title: The State v. Zahid Mehmood Goraya (Advocate) (Criminal Original 20741/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Illegal Detention Without Formal Arrest: Physical Remand Set Aside
records.heading: Detention without formal arrest and irregular remand led to discharge and set aside of remand
records.text: A detenu held at a police station without formal arrest, not nominated in the FIR, with irregularities in the remand application and undated case diaries, was discharged. The physical remand order was set aside under s. 561-A CrPC. Arrest cannot be made without sufficient incriminating material, a confession before police is inadmissible, and directions were issued including that a reliable source or landlord's clue is not legal evidence. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 700; Rashida Bibi v. SHO etc. (Crl. Misc.-Habeas Corpus 4043-H-23).
records.title: Rashida Bibi v. SHO etc. (Crl. Misc.-Habeas Corpus 4043-H-23)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats Case: Additional Note of Justice Athar Minallah
records.heading: Additional note on the reserved seats case and the Election Commission's duty of a level playing field
records.text: In an additional note in the reserved seats case concerning Sunni Ittehad, the judge said the interpretation of a Supreme Court judgment prima facie appeared wrong and removed a major political party from the electoral process. He said the case concerns voters' fundamental rights and that the Election Commission must show a level playing field was provided to all parties before, during and after the general elections. Ref: Justice Athar Minallah.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conjectures and Inferences in Criminal Law
records.heading: Conjecture has no place in criminal law, while logical inference does
records.text: Conjecture has no place in criminal law, whereas an inference plays an important role because it rests on logical deduction from circumstances available on the record. Ref: 2018 SCMR 1590; Lal Khan v. Qadeer Ahmed.
records.title: Lal Khan v. Qadeer Ahmed

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Surrender Before Filing Leave Petition Against Conviction
records.heading: A convict must surrender before a leave petition against conviction is maintainable
records.text: A convict challenging conviction and a sentence of imprisonment must first surrender to undergo the sentence for his petition for leave to appeal before the Supreme Court to be maintainable under the Supreme Court Rules, 1980. An accused seeking bail before arrest need not surrender to the police but may undertake to surrender at the hearing. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 639, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 174; Mehboob-ur-Rehman and Jawar v. The State.
records.title: Mehboob-ur-Rehman and Jawar v. The State

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Distribution and Waiver of Diyat Among Offenders
records.heading: Diyat is divided equally among offenders and a waiver as to one is borne by the others
records.text: Where several offenders commit Qatl-e-Amd, diyat is divided equally among them. If recovery from one offender is waived, the remaining diyat is paid by the others according to their shares. S. 338-F PPC requires the court to be guided by the Qur'an and Sunnah, and the trial court is to fix the value of diyat under s. 323 PPC. Ref: PLD 2003 Kar 277; Muhammad Sharif v. The State (Criminal Revision Application No. D-59 of 2002).
records.title: Muhammad Sharif v. The State (Criminal Revision Application No. D-59 of 2002)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare as Foundational Principle
records.heading: Custody is decided on the welfare of the child, not the mother's financial inability
records.text: A custody decision made without assessing the child's welfare and best interests cannot be sustained, and welfare is the foundational principle in custody disputes. The father is natural guardian, while the mother is entitled to hizanat of a male child to seven years and of a female child until puberty. The mother's financial inability does not defeat custody, as the father's duty of maintenance continues. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 629, PLJ 2024 SC 537; Shaista Habib v. Muhammad Arif Habib and others (Civil Petition No. 3801 of 2022).
records.title: Shaista Habib v. Muhammad Arif Habib and others (Civil Petition No. 3801 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. II R. 2 CPC: Splitting of Cause of Action
records.heading: Order II Rule 2 CPC does not require suing on all causes of action from one transaction
records.text: Order II R. 2 CPC prevents splitting of a cause of action and multiplicity of suits, but does not require suing on all causes of action arising from one transaction. A second suit to recover earnest money had a cause of action different from the first suit for specific performance. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 663; Matloob Ellahi Paracha v. Raja Arshad Mahmood and another (Civil Appeal No.1877 of 2016, decided 14.11.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Matloob Ellahi Paracha v. Raja Arshad Mahmood and another (Civil Appeal No.1877 of 2016, decided 14.11.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Adjournments: Discouraging Adjournment Culture
records.heading: Frequent adjournment requests abuse the process of the court and add to backlog
records.text: Frequent adjournment requests in the lower courts amount to an abuse of the process of the court and add to the backlog of litigation. Courts must not grant adjournments liberally or without compelling reasons, and the post refers to O. XVII R. 3 CPC in this regard. Leave refused and petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 672; Duniya Gul and another v. Niaz Muhammad and others (Civil Petition No. 920-P of 2023).
records.title: Duniya Gul and another v. Niaz Muhammad and others (Civil Petition No. 920-P of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Possession of Dead Meat: Animal Slaughter Control Act
records.heading: Possession of dead meat is also culpable under the Punjab Animal Slaughter Control Act
records.text: Possession of dead meat is also culpable under the Punjab Animal Slaughter Control Act, 1963. While deciding a bail petition the court may consider what offence is made out from the facts and circumstances of the case. Ref: 2024 LHC 3301; Naveed Tariq & 1 Other v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 38478/24, decided 25.06.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Naveed Tariq & 1 Other v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 38478/24, decided 25.06.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Scope of Section 249 CrPC
records.heading: Section 249 CrPC lets a Magistrate stop proceedings by a reasoned, revisable order
records.text: S. 249 CrPC allows a Magistrate to stop proceedings at any stage, other than those begun by private complaint, and release the accused without a verdict. The order must be reasoned, is revisable, and does not require a bond. The section is not a remedy for staying criminal proceedings, and civil and criminal proceedings differ in standard of proof so res judicata and double jeopardy do not apply. Ref: 2024 LHC 3306; Zahid Maqsood Butt v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 3568/24, decided 07.06.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Zahid Maqsood Butt v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 3568/24, decided 07.06.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion: Corroborative Value Only
records.heading: Absconsion is only corroborative and cannot by itself found a conviction
records.text: Mere absconsion cannot be the basis of conviction. It is a relevant fact usable only as corroboration alongside substantive evidence, is a suspicious circumstance that cannot take the place of proof, and cannot cure defects in the prosecution case. Its value depends on the facts of each case. Ref: Rafaqat Ali @ Foji v. The State (J.P. 234/2017).
records.title: Rafaqat Ali @ Foji v. The State (J.P. 234/2017)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 506(b) PPC: Criminal Intimidation Ingredients
records.heading: A bare threat without a condition does not establish criminal intimidation under section 506(b) PPC
records.text: A bare threat does not establish criminal intimidation unless it is meant to cause, or causes, the person threatened to do an act he is not legally bound to do, or to omit an act he is legally entitled to do, to avoid the threat. As the FIR mentioned no such condition, it was doubtful whether s. 506(b) PPC was made out. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 162; Amjad Shabab alias Amjad Hussain v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 1879-B of 2024).
records.title: Amjad Shabab alias Amjad Hussain v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 1879-B of 2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Qatl-bis-sabab Punishable with Diyat
records.heading: Qatl-bis-sabab is punishable with diyat only, so pre-arrest bail was confirmed
records.text: Qatl-bis-sabab under s. 322 PPC is punishable with diyat only, and an accused charged with it cannot be sent to prison, though he may be imprisoned if he fails to pay diyat. The petitioner's child died after unintentionally firing a gun, and the mother declined to proceed against him. Pre-arrest bail confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 160; Muhammad Ramzan v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 9776-B of 2023, decided 24.01.2024); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 9776-B of 2023, decided 24.01.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Recovery of Weapon
records.heading: Arrest is not necessary for weapon recovery where search warrants can achieve it
records.text: Arrest of the petitioner is not necessary for recovery of the weapon of offence, as that purpose can be achieved by the Investigating Officer obtaining search warrants. Relied on in a pre-arrest bail petition under s. 498 CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 137; Qaiser Abbas and 4 others v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 9281-B of 2023).
records.title: Qaiser Abbas and 4 others v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 9281-B of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Appreciation of Evidence in Qatl-i-Amd Appeal
records.heading: Appreciation of evidence in a Qatl-i-Amd appeal and murder reference
records.text: Appeal and murder reference under ss. 302/109/34 PPC. The headnote records that eye-witnesses left unharmed by the shooter were taken to be present, that the FIR was prompt and the post mortem followed within three and a half hours. It also lists delay in sending crime empties to PFSA, recovery, motive and benefit of doubt. The final outcome is not shown in the excerpt. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 141; Muhammad Asif etc. v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 992 of 2021, Crl. A. No. 42 & M.R. No. 5 of 2022, decided 23.04.2024); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Asif etc. v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 992 of 2021, Crl. A. No. 42 & M.R. No. 5 of 2022, decided 23.04.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay Ground: Accused Contributing to Delay
records.heading: Statutory delay ground for bail is unavailable to an accused who contributed to the delay
records.text: Bail on the ground of expiry of the statutory period is available only to an accused who has not contributed to delay in the trial. The petitioners sought adjournments on crucial dates when prosecution witnesses were present, and the Supreme Court judgments relied on were distinguished. Criminal revision under ss. 435 and 439 CrPC dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 143; Waseem and 2 others v. State and another (Crl. Rev. No. 84195 of 2023, decided 18.01.2024); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Waseem and 2 others v. State and another (Crl. Rev. No. 84195 of 2023, decided 18.01.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Absconsion and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Absconsion alone cannot deny bail once further inquiry is made out
records.text: Once a case is found to attract further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC, the accused cannot be denied bail solely because of absconsion. The petitioner, arrested after about a decade, had earlier sought pre-arrest bail, joined investigation and surrendered. Bail allowed in a murder case. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 144; Rustam v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 336-B of 2024, decided 23.02.2024); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Rustam v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 336-B of 2024, decided 23.02.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Honour Killing: Sui Juris Woman and Fasad-fil-Arz
records.heading: A major Muslim woman is sui juris with the same rights and liberties as a man
records.text: A major Muslim woman, like a major man, is sui juris and entitled to the same rights and liberties, a view supported by Art. 9 of the Constitution. The judgment also addresses karo-kari, fasad-fil-arz under ss. 299(ee), 302(c), 305, 311, 337-N and 338-E PPC and s. 345 CrPC, and the expression mastermind. Ref: Muhammad Ali Mahar & another v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 201-K/2023, decided 11.06.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Ali Mahar & another v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 201-K/2023, decided 11.06.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Tender of Pardon to Accomplice: Consent Required
records.heading: A court cannot tender pardon to an accomplice without the prosecution and his written consent
records.text: The court cannot tender pardon to an accused without taking the prosecution on board. Under s. 338 CrPC pardon may be tendered by the court before judgment, but the accomplice must first volunteer to become approver, and his written consent was missing on record. The order was contrary to Art. 13 of the Constitution and was set aside. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 459, PLJ 2024 CrC 543; Muhammad Asif v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision No. 12454 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision No. 12454 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Registration of Divorce of Christians: Union Council
records.heading: Divorces of Christians are registered by the Union Council and NADRA accommodates them meanwhile
records.text: Registering divorces and issuing certificates is a function of local government, now of the Union Council under s. 33(1)(j) of the Punjab Local Government Act 2022. No rules have been framed for divorces of the Christian community. Until the Provincial Government frames rules, NADRA is to accommodate the community under its Registration Policy, which allows change of marital status on affidavit. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 443; Mst Shumaila Sharif v. The Secretary etc (WP 66288/22).
records.title: Mst Shumaila Sharif v. The Secretary etc (WP 66288/22)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Medical Negligence: Guidelines on FIR Registration
records.heading: Criminal prosecution for medical negligence requires a supporting technical expert report
records.text: A healthcare professional can be criminally prosecuted for negligence only if a technical expert report from IHRA or PMDC supports it. On a complaint of medical negligence the SHO must record it in the daily diary, seek expert reports from IHRA and PMDC, and lodge an FIR only after a negative report. Guidelines issued for ss. 200, 22-A and 22-B CrPC applications. Ref: Dr. Farhat Ullah Bakhsh v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace/ASJ-III (East), Islamabad and others (W.P. No. 3431-2023, heard 05.06.2024).
records.title: Dr. Farhat Ullah Bakhsh v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace/ASJ-III (East), Islamabad and others (W.P. No. 3431-2023, heard 05.06.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Surety in Execution: Extent of Liability
records.heading: A surety is liable only to the extent he clearly undertook in the bond
records.text: A surety's liability is co-extensive with that of the judgment debtor but is limited to what he clearly undertook, and the bond is strictly construed from its words and recitals. The petitioner stood surety for Rs. 400,000 only, and had paid that sum, so he had discharged his liability. Ref: 2024 LHC 3367; Masood ul Hassan v. ADJ etc (WP 5215-22, decided 02.07.2024); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Masood ul Hassan v. ADJ etc (WP 5215-22, decided 02.07.2024)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Ingredients and Bail
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC falls outside the prohibitory clause, so bail is the rule
records.text: The elements of s. 489-F PPC are dishonest issuance of a cheque towards repayment of a loan or an obligation, and dishonour. Whether the cheque was for an obligation is for the trial court. The maximum punishment of three years is outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so bail is the rule, and other registered cases do not bar bail if a prima facie case exists on merits. Ref: 2024 SCP 234; Ali Anwar Paracha v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 240/2024, decided 04.06.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Ali Anwar Paracha v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 240/2024, decided 04.06.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Counter Versions: Bail as Rule on Further Inquiry
records.heading: Counter versions of one incident make bail the rule on further inquiry
records.text: Where the complainant and the opposite party give counter versions of the same incident, bail is granted as a rule on the ground of further inquiry, since the correct version and the aggressor are to be decided after pro and contra evidence at trial. Refusal of bail is the exception. Ref: 2024 SCP 233; Khizar Hayat v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1345-L/2023, decided 30.05.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Khizar Hayat v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 1345-L/2023, decided 30.05.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CDR Without Transcripts Not Reliable Evidence
records.heading: Call data records without transcripts or audio recordings are not reliable evidence
records.text: Mere production of call data records without transcripts or complete audio recordings is not reliable evidence. It must also be established that the persons at both ends of the call are those whose data is produced, and courts must be cautious given the ease of editing recordings. The judgment also stresses a thorough investigation in kidnapping for ransom cases. Ref: 2024 SCP 231; Asmat Ullah Khan v. The State (J.P. 431/2016, decided 15.05.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Asmat Ullah Khan v. The State (J.P. 431/2016, decided 15.05.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Abatement of Appeal on Death: Sentence of Fine
records.heading: On an appellant's death the appeal against the sentence of fine does not abate
records.text: On the death of an appellant, the appeal as to the sentence of imprisonment abates. The appeal as to the sentence of fine, which affects the appellant's property, does not abate and is to be heard on merits according to the settled principles of criminal justice. Ref: 2024 SCP 231; Asmat Ullah Khan v. The State (J.P. 431/2016, decided 15.05.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Asmat Ullah Khan v. The State (J.P. 431/2016, decided 15.05.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: No Suo Motu Jurisdiction Under Article 199
records.heading: The High Court cannot exercise suo motu jurisdiction under Article 199
records.text: The High Court cannot exercise suo motu jurisdiction under Art. 199 of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 780; Hafsa Habib Qureshi v. Amir Hamza and others (C.P.L.A. 3747/2023).
records.title: Hafsa Habib Qureshi v. Amir Hamza and others (C.P.L.A. 3747/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Conversion of Proceedings by High Court
records.heading: The High Court may convert one type of proceeding into another in constitutional jurisdiction
records.text: In its constitutional jurisdiction the High Court may convert one type of proceeding into another. It may then decide the matter itself if it has jurisdiction over the issue, or remit it to the competent authority, forum or court for decision on merits. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 780; Hafsa Habib Qureshi v. Amir Hamza and others (C.P.L.A. 3747/2023).
records.title: Hafsa Habib Qureshi v. Amir Hamza and others (C.P.L.A. 3747/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Interference in Concurrent Findings of Family Courts
records.heading: The High Court does not interfere in writ with concurrent findings of Family Courts
records.text: In writ jurisdiction under Art. 199 the High Court does not interfere with findings of fact on controversial questions. Review is limited to misreading or non-reading of evidence, or findings based on no evidence, and the writ cannot substitute for revision or appeal. Findings of the District Court on appeal under the Family Courts Act 1964 are ordinarily final. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 771; Fozia Mazhar v. Additional District Judge, Jhang, etc (C.P.L.A. 1737-L/2020).
records.title: Fozia Mazhar v. Additional District Judge, Jhang, etc (C.P.L.A. 1737-L/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Against Family Court Decrees
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC can be invoked against a decree of a Family Court
records.text: A Family Court may apply the general principles of the CPC, including entertaining an application challenging a judgment, decree or order on the ground of fraud or misrepresentation. S. 12(2) CPC can therefore be invoked against a decree passed by a Family Court under the Family Courts Act 1964. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 771; Fozia Mazhar v. Additional District Judge, Jhang, etc (C.P.L.A. 1737-L/2020).
records.title: Fozia Mazhar v. Additional District Judge, Jhang, etc (C.P.L.A. 1737-L/2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Conversion of Acquittal Appeal into Criminal Revision
records.heading: The High Court may convert an appeal against acquittal into a criminal revision
records.text: Under ss. 417(2A) and 439 CrPC the High Court may in its discretion convert an appeal against acquittal into a criminal revision, particularly where substantial questions of law are raised. The conversion order in this case was held to suffer from no illegality or irregularity. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 805; Noman Mansoor alias Nomi v. The State thr. AG, Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A. 894/2021).
records.title: Noman Mansoor alias Nomi v. The State thr. AG, Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A. 894/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 439(2) CrPC: Notice Before Enhancing Sentence
records.heading: Notice under section 439(2) CrPC is required before enhancing sentence in revision
records.text: After a direct revision or conversion of an appeal into a revision, notice under s. 439(2) CrPC must be issued to the other side. The High Court may enhance sentence in revision only after giving the accused a hearing. No notice was issued here, so the matter was sent back for fresh decision after hearing all concerned. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 805; Noman Mansoor alias Nomi v. The State thr. AG, Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A. 894/2021).
records.title: Noman Mansoor alias Nomi v. The State thr. AG, Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A. 894/2021)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats: ECP Order Declared Ultra Vires
records.heading: The ECP order on reserved seats was declared ultra vires the Constitution
records.text: In a short order the Supreme Court set aside the Full Bench judgment dated 25.03.2024 to the extent inconsistent with it. It declared the ECP order dated 01.03.2024 ultra vires the Constitution and of no legal effect, and quashed from 06.05.2024 the notifications declaring returned candidates for reserved seats for women and minorities. Ref: Sunni Ittehad Council through its Chairman, Faisalabad and another v. Election Commission of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others (Civil Appeals No. 333 and 334 of 2024 and C.M.A. No. 2920 of 2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Ayesha A. Malik; Justice Athar Minallah; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Sunni Ittehad Council through its Chairman, Faisalabad and another v. Election Commission of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others (Civil Appeals No. 333 and 334 of 2024 and C.M.A. No. 2920 of 2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats Case: Majority Decision Reported
records.heading: Majority held PTI a political party entitled to reserved seats proportionately
records.text: Eight judges allowed the appeal and five dissented. The ECP decision of March was held to be outside the Constitution, and the High Court decision upholding it was set aside. PTI was and remains a political party and is entitled to reserved seats proportionately, to submit its list within 15 days, and independents must file affidavits of party affiliation for ECP verification. Ref: Sunni Ittehad Council v. Election Commission of Pakistan; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Sunni Ittehad Council v. Election Commission of Pakistan

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Adjournments Cannot Be Claimed as of Right
records.heading: Adjournments cannot be demanded as of right or used as a delaying tactic
records.text: Adjournments have become a plague on the justice system and deny litigants speedy justice. They cannot be used as a delaying tactic or demanded as of right. The post refers to O. XVII R. 3 CPC, under which the court may decide the suit forthwith if a party fails to perform an act necessary for its progress despite time allowed. Ref: Lutfullah Virk v. Muhammad Aslam Sheikh (C.P.L.A. 2849-L/2015, decided 03.07.2024); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Lutfullah Virk v. Muhammad Aslam Sheikh (C.P.L.A. 2849-L/2015, decided 03.07.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Rash and Negligent Driving: Proof and S. 342 Statement
records.heading: Driving fast is no offence unless rashness or negligence is proved
records.text: Driving fast on a highway is no offence unless speed above the limit and rashness or negligence are proved. Evidence not put to the accused under s. 342 CrPC cannot be used against him, and his statement must be accepted or rejected as a whole. Conviction resting only on his statement was unsustainable as he did not admit rash driving. Ref: Syed Fida Hussain Shah v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 134/2024, decided 04.07.2024).
records.title: Syed Fida Hussain Shah v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 134/2024, decided 04.07.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Repeated Nomination in Similar Cases: Mala Fide
records.heading: Repeated nomination and re-arrest in similar cases showed mala fide and led to release
records.text: The Lahore High Court ordered immediate release of the petitioner. Repeatedly naming her in similar cases and re-arresting her after release showed mala fides, the Investigating Officer had no evidence against her, and she was discharged. Detention orders issued while she was in jail were criticised, and remand courts were told to consider fundamental rights. Ref: 2024 LHC 3408; Mst. Sanam Javed v. Learned Special Judge Anti Terrorism Court Gujranwala etc (Crl. Revision 39439/24, decided 10.07.2024); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Mst. Sanam Javed v. Learned Special Judge Anti Terrorism Court Gujranwala etc (Crl. Revision 39439/24, decided 10.07.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: Proof Through Marginal Witnesses
records.heading: An agreement to sell must be proved through marginal witnesses under Articles 17 and 79 QSO
records.text: The beneficiary of an agreement to sell must prove its genuineness through marginal witnesses under Arts. 17 and 79 QSO 1984, and non-compliance renders it inadmissible. The plaintiff produced one marginal witness but not for cross-examination and gave no death certificate. The courts below were held to have rightly dismissed the suit. Ref: 2024 MLD 1176; Muhammad Sharif v. Rana Muhammad Sharif (Civil Revision No. 2827 of 2016).
records.title: Muhammad Sharif v. Rana Muhammad Sharif (Civil Revision No. 2827 of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Special Oath: Binding Effect of Voluntary Offer
records.heading: A voluntary offer of special oath, once accepted, binds the party and cannot be resiled from
records.text: Disposal of a suit on an agreed special oath is a lawful compromise and cannot be challenged through appeal. An offer of special oath made voluntarily by the petitioner and accepted by the respondent was binding on the petitioner, who could not resile from it. Ref: 2024 MLD 1156; Rehana Shafqat v. Afira Butt and others (Civil Revision No. 49064 of 2022).
records.title: Rehana Shafqat v. Afira Butt and others (Civil Revision No. 49064 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Pension Heirs: Unproved Divorce of Second Wife
records.heading: Alleged divorce of a second wife was unproved, so the pension order was upheld
records.text: The petitioner claimed the deceased had divorced his second wife, but two divorce deeds of different dates existed and she could not produce the witnesses after the respondent's denial and special oath. The Appellate Court rightly upheld the Trial Court order, and no interference was warranted in revisional jurisdiction. Ref: 2024 MLD 1156; Rehana Shafqat v. Afira Butt and others (Civil Revision No. 49064 of 2022).
records.title: Rehana Shafqat v. Afira Butt and others (Civil Revision No. 49064 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 1 and 2 CPC: Particulars of Claim
records.heading: Particulars of a claim must be pleaded under Order VII Rules 1 and 2 CPC
records.text: Particulars of the claim must be pleaded under O. VII Rr. 1 and 2 CPC. The plaintiff claimed only an accumulated sum for allowances, gratuity and compensation without breaking it down by head, so the pleading was ambiguous. Ref: 2024 MLD 1111; M/S Gulistan Group of Companies through Director v. Waseem Javed Khand (Civil Revision No. 25850 of 2022).
records.title: M/S Gulistan Group of Companies through Director v. Waseem Javed Khand (Civil Revision No. 25850 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Documents Produced Through Counsel's Statement
records.heading: Disputed documents must be produced through their author or witnesses, not counsel's statement
records.text: Disputed documents must be brought on record through their author or witnesses connected with them, and not through the statement of counsel. Documents produced in evidence beyond those relied on under O. VII R. 14 and O. XIII R. 1 CPC must not be considered by the courts. Ref: 2024 MLD 1111; M/S Gulistan Group of Companies through Director v. Waseem Javed Khand (Civil Revision No. 25850 of 2022).
records.title: M/S Gulistan Group of Companies through Director v. Waseem Javed Khand (Civil Revision No. 25850 of 2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Superdari of Vehicle: Owner Without Knowledge
records.heading: An owner without knowledge of narcotics use may obtain superdari of his vehicle
records.text: If the owner of a vehicle used to carry narcotics is not an accused and had no knowledge of the use, s. 74 CNSA 1997 does not bar release of the vehicle on superdari. The appellant, with valid ownership documents, was entitled to custody on surety bonds and an affidavit not to dispose of it. Ref: 2024 MLD 1070; Commissionerate of Afghan Refugees v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 74897 of 2023).
records.title: Commissionerate of Afghan Refugees v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 74897 of 2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Leave to Contest: Computing Ten Days Limitation
records.heading: The first day of appearance is excluded in computing the ten days for leave to contest
records.text: In computing the ten days under s. 22(2) of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 for a leave to contest application, the first day of appearance is excluded by s. 8 of the Punjab General Clauses Act 1956. Ref: 2024 LHC 3422; Ms Phipsons Company Pvt Limited v. Zahid Moyeen etc (WP: 1913/20, decided 11.07.2024); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Ms Phipsons Company Pvt Limited v. Zahid Moyeen etc (WP: 1913/20, decided 11.07.2024)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Unregistered Lease and Mutwalli as Landlord
records.heading: An unregistered lease over twelve months is a monthly tenancy, and a mutwalli is a landlord
records.text: Under s. 5(4) of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 the duty to register is not removed, so an unregistered lease beyond 12 months is treated as a month to month tenancy terminable by notice. A mutwalli who receives rent is a landlord under s. 2(d), so his ejectment petition is maintainable. Ref: 2024 LHC 3422; Ms Phipsons Company Pvt Limited v. Zahid Moyeen etc (WP: 1913/20, decided 11.07.2024); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Ms Phipsons Company Pvt Limited v. Zahid Moyeen etc (WP: 1913/20, decided 11.07.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Abetment and Section 107 PPC
records.heading: Ingredients of abetment by conspiracy were missing, so pre-arrest bail was confirmed
records.text: The petitioner's name appeared only in a supplementary statement and not in the FIR. The three ingredients of abetment by conspiracy under s. 107 PPC, namely instigation, engagement with co-accused and intentional aid, were prima facie missing, and no other evidence was collected. Pre-arrest bail confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 167; Muhammad Maqsood Ahmad v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 10070-B of 2023, decided 18.03.2024); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Maqsood Ahmad v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 10070-B of 2023, decided 18.03.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Facilitating Escape, No Overt Act
records.heading: Merely helping the principal accused escape with no overt act supports post-arrest bail
records.text: The petitioner was nominated but stood 147 feet away and only helped the principal accused escape on a motorcycle, with no overt act or link to the motive. The ingredients of s. 107 PPC were prima facie missing, and the police opinion of guilt does not bind the court. Post-arrest bail granted. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 168; Waheed Akhtar v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 522-B of 2024, decided 12.03.2024); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Waheed Akhtar v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 522-B of 2024, decided 12.03.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas 2120 Grams: Lesser Sentence at Bail Stage
records.heading: Charas of 2120 grams does not attract the prohibitory clause at bail stage
records.text: For 1000 to 5000 grams of charas the sentence under s. 9(c) CNSA ranges from nine to 14 years, and the lesser sentence is considered at bail stage. The 2120 grams recovered did not attract the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Criminal history is no handicap if the case is one of further inquiry. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 172; Muhammad Asghar v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 7664-B of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Asghar v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 7664-B of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unattended Body Casts Doubt on Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: A body left unattended at autopsy casts doubt on the presence of eye-witnesses
records.text: The doctor found the deceased's eyes semi-open and mouth open at autopsy, suggesting the body remained unattended after the occurrence. Had the claimed eye-witnesses, including the complainant, been present they would have attended the body, which doubts their presence. Relying on a Supreme Court case where open eyes and mouth led to disbelief of eye-witnesses. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 174; Muhammad Azeem etc. v. State (Crl. A. Nos. 78686-J, 70240 & M.R. No. 339 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Azeem etc. v. State (Crl. A. Nos. 78686-J, 70240 & M.R. No. 339 of 2019)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Illegal Detention Without Production Before Magistrate
records.heading: Detention beyond 24 hours without production before a Magistrate supports bail
records.text: The petitioner, arrested with 1280 grams of charas, was not produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours, and no remand order existed. The police explanation of a lawyers' issue was unacceptable, as he was illegally detained for two days before being sent to jail. Post-arrest bail granted on surety bonds. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 175; Ghulam Nabi alias Gama v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 71128-B of 2023, decided 16.04.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Ghulam Nabi alias Gama v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 71128-B of 2023, decided 16.04.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas 1460 Grams: Not Within Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Charas of 1460 grams does not attract the prohibitory clause of section 497 CrPC
records.text: Under s. 9(1)(c) CNSA as amended in 2022, 1000 to 4999 grams of charas carries up to 14 years but not less than nine, so the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC is not attracted as the lesser sentence is considered at bail stage. Criminal history in other cases is no handicap if the case is one of further inquiry. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 179; Vikki Masih v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 86078-B of 2023).
records.title: Vikki Masih v. State, etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 86078-B of 2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Ground: Two Years Detention Without Conclusion of Trial
records.heading: Two years of detention without conclusion of trial gives a right to bail
records.text: Where charge was framed for the first time and the petitioners had been detained over two years without conclusion of trial, a right to bail accrued under s. 497 CrPC. It can be denied only if the delay was caused by the accused or acts on their behalf, or if they are convicted of a death or life offence. Bail allowed, trial court told to expedite. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 185; Naseer Ahmad and another v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 728-B of 2024, decided 05.04.2024); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Naseer Ahmad and another v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 728-B of 2024, decided 05.04.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ex-Officio Justice of Peace: Functus Officio After Order
records.heading: An Ex-Officio Justice of Peace becomes functus officio after passing an order
records.text: Proceedings under ss. 22-A and 22-B CrPC are quasi-judicial in nature. Once the Ex-Officio Justice of Peace passes an order he becomes functus officio and cannot recall it when asked to implement it. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 476; Mst Robina Khatoon v. ASJ etc (WP: 5109-20).
records.title: Mst Robina Khatoon v. ASJ etc (WP: 5109-20)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Grounds of Arrest: Article 10 and Police Compliance
records.heading: Police must give grounds of arrest under Article 10 and Magistrates must ensure compliance
records.text: The court noted that police were disregarding Art. 10 of the Constitution and earlier directions on providing grounds of arrest. Failure would warrant contempt proceedings but a lenient view was taken, directing future compliance. Magistrates deciding physical remand under s. 167 CrPC must ensure grounds of arrest are made part of the police file. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 809.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 180 PPC: Refusal to Sign Charge Sheet
records.heading: Refusal to sign the charge sheet is not an offence under section 180 PPC
records.text: Obtaining the accused's signature on the charge sheet is not a legal requirement under ss. 243 or 265-E CrPC, so an accused who refuses to sign cannot be convicted under s. 180 PPC. The appeal was allowed and the conviction and sentence set aside. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 813; Kashif Nawaz etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. A. No. 531 of 2023, heard 19.12.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kashif Nawaz etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. A. No. 531 of 2023, heard 19.12.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Police Opinion of Innocence: Further Inquiry
records.heading: A police opinion of innocence based on cogent material supports further inquiry for bail
records.text: A police opinion favouring the accused does not bind the court but creates doubt about the prosecution case and has persuasive value if based on cogent material. It brought the case within further inquiry. A person is not an accused until the Investigating Officer finds him involved. In a s. 302 PPC case, bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 817; Muhammad Imran v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 5878-B-23); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 5878-B-23)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Deposit of Arsh and Daman Under Protest Impermissible
records.heading: A convict cannot be released by depositing arsh or daman under protest
records.text: A sentence of imprisonment must be carried out unless deferred or suspended under s. 382-A or s. 426 CrPC. The trial court cannot allow a convict to deposit diyat, arsh or daman under protest for release, and such an order is illegal and without jurisdiction. The order was set aside and the petition accepted. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 822, 2024 PCrLJ 2036; Manzoor Hussain v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 40476/19).
records.title: Manzoor Hussain v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 40476/19)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Physical Remand by Anti-Terrorism Court: Principles
records.heading: Principles on grant of physical remand by the ATC and the 24 hour rule
records.text: The High Court may under s. 439 CrPC examine the vires of proceedings in revision. A police officer cannot hold an arrestee beyond 24 hours without a Magistrate's order under s. 167 CrPC, and remand to the investigating officer hands custody to the investigating agency for further investigation. Principles on grant or refusal of physical remand by the ATC were elaborated. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 837; Mansha Ali v. State & another (Crl. Rev. No. 67181 of 2023, heard 24.10.2023); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch.; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mansha Ali v. State & another (Crl. Rev. No. 67181 of 2023, heard 24.10.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Variance with Ocular Account
records.heading: An eye-witness account at variance with medical evidence gives rise to doubt
records.text: Medical evidence confirms the ocular account, and an eye-witness statement at variance with it gives rise to doubt whose benefit cannot be denied to the accused. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Appeal allowed, convictions set aside, and the murder reference answered in the negative. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 857; Muhammad Atif Naveed etc. v. State (Crl. A. Nos. 827, 698 & M.R. No. 41 of 2022, heard 16.04.2024); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Muhammad Atif Naveed etc. v. State (Crl. A. Nos. 827, 698 & M.R. No. 41 of 2022, heard 16.04.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence Chain and Judicial Confession
records.heading: Inadmissible evidence breaks the chain of circumstantial evidence; confession safeguards under section 164(3) CrPC
records.text: Each link in a chain of circumstantial evidence must be admissible, as inadmissible evidence breaks the chain. For confessions under s. 164(3) CrPC the precautions in the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders, Vol. III, Ch. 13 aim to ensure voluntariness. Appeal accepted, convictions set aside, and the murder reference answered in the negative. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 873; Adnan Pervaiz and another v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 349 & M.R. No. 25 of 2019, heard 30.09.2021); Justice Raja Shahid Mehmood Abbasi; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Adnan Pervaiz and another v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 349 & M.R. No. 25 of 2019, heard 30.09.2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recovery Memo and Framing of Charge: Fair Trial
records.heading: The recovery memo is mandatory for framing of charge and a fair trial
records.text: The recovery memo has a deep nexus with the charge to be framed against an accused, and is a mandatory requirement for a fair trial under Art. 10-A of the Constitution. Ref: 2024 LHC 3449; Nayyar Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 549-23, decided 13.02.2024); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Nayyar Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 549-23, decided 13.02.2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Guidelines for Implementing Juvenile Justice System Act 2018
records.heading: Guidelines issued for implementing the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018, including interrogation by Sub-Inspector
records.text: Guidelines were issued for swift implementation of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018. A juvenile may be interrogated only by a police officer not below Sub-Inspector, under supervision of an SP or SDPO and assisted by a probation or social welfare officer. The Prosecutor General Punjab must ensure strict compliance. Ref: 2024 LHC 3460; Rehana Nazir v. DPO Gujrat etc (WP: 40169/24, decided 19.07.2024); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Rehana Nazir v. DPO Gujrat etc (WP: 40169/24, decided 19.07.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Who May Apply for Cancellation of Bail: S. 497(5) CrPC
records.heading: Wrongly granted bail may be challenged by the State, interested persons or the court itself
records.text: It is the State's duty to ensure bail is not wrongly granted, so the prosecution should seek correction under s. 497(5) CrPC. Any person vitally interested in the case may also contest such an order, and the court may act on its own initiative. S. 497(5) confers powers similar to revisional powers under ss. 435 and 436 CrPC. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1364, PLJ 2023 CrC 543; Azeem-ud-Din v. Feroze Khan etc (Crl. Misc. 60014/CB/2022, decided 20.01.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Azeem-ud-Din v. Feroze Khan etc (Crl. Misc. 60014/CB/2022, decided 20.01.2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 462-C PPC: Proof and Prosecution Duty
records.heading: Post-arrest bail case on proof of an offence under section 462-C PPC
records.text: Post-arrest bail petition under s. 497 CrPC which addresses the evidential requirement for proof of an offence under s. 462-C PPC and the duty of the prosecution. The post gives no further holding. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1341, PLJ 2024 CrC 440; Muhammad Hassan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 3535-B-23).
records.title: Muhammad Hassan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 3535-B-23)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Doctrine of Merger of Lower Court Order
records.heading: Under the doctrine of merger a lower court order is deemed the higher court's order
records.text: If the order of a lower court merges in the order of the higher court, the lower court order is deemed to be an order of the higher court. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1390; Muhammad Aslam v. Molvi Muhammad Ishaq (C.A. 1429/2014).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. Molvi Muhammad Ishaq (C.A. 1429/2014)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Application: Three Years Under Art. 181
records.heading: An application under section 12(2) CPC is governed by the three year period in Article 181
records.text: The Limitation Act 1908 prescribes no specific period for an application under s. 12(2) CPC, so the residuary Art. 181 applies, giving three years. Applications filed in 1990 after a compromise of 1979 were time barred even if counted from 1987. Appeals allowed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1390; Muhammad Aslam v. Molvi Muhammad Ishaq (C.A. 1429/2014).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. Molvi Muhammad Ishaq (C.A. 1429/2014)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: No Deeper Appraisal of Evidence at Bail Stage
records.heading: At the bail stage the court cannot deeply appraise the evidence
records.text: At the bail stage the court cannot deeply appraise the material on record and must decide only tentatively by looking at that material. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1284.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry and Reasonable Grounds
records.heading: Further inquiry rests on tentative doubt while reasonable grounds must be legally tenable material
records.text: Further inquiry presupposes a tentative assessment creating doubt about the accused's involvement, while reasonable grounds are legally tenable, admissible and appealing to a reasonable judicial mind. The prosecution must show sufficient material under the prohibitory limb of s. 497 CrPC, and the accused must show material creating reasonable doubt. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1210; Attaullah v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 35-K/2024).
records.title: Attaullah v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 35-K/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Rule of Consistency in Bail
records.heading: Under the rule of consistency, bail to a co-accused with the same role extends to the accused
records.text: Under the rule of consistency or parity, where the role ascribed to the accused is the same as that of a co-accused, the benefit extended to one should extend to the other. The court must first assess the constituents of the role assigned to the accused before applying parity. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1210; Attaullah v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 35-K/2024).
records.title: Attaullah v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 35-K/2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Improvements, Contradictions and Adverse Inference
records.heading: Dishonest improvements make a witness untrustworthy and unproduced witnesses attract an adverse inference
records.text: Dishonest improvements by a witness make his statement untrustworthy, and material contradictions create doubt in the prosecution case. An adverse inference arises under Art. 129(g) QSO that two witnesses not produced by the prosecution would not have supported its version. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1310; Mst. Saima Noreen and Muhammad Shafiq v. The State (Jail Petition No. 181 of 2016 with Criminal Petition No. 154-L of 2016).
records.title: Mst. Saima Noreen and Muhammad Shafiq v. The State (Jail Petition No. 181 of 2016 with Criminal Petition No. 154-L of 2016)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 17-A: Striking Off Defence for Non-Payment of Interim Maintenance
records.heading: A Family Court may strike off the defence for non-payment of interim maintenance
records.text: Under s. 17-A of the Family Courts Act 1964 the Family Court may strike off the defence and decree the suit where the father fails to pay interim maintenance by the fourteenth of each month, after notice. The quantum was not arbitrary, and costs of Rs. 100,000 were imposed on the father for disregarding the order. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1292; Shahzad Amir Farid v. Mst. Sobia Amir Farid and others (Civil Petition No. 3155-L of 2023).
records.title: Shahzad Amir Farid v. Mst. Sobia Amir Farid and others (Civil Petition No. 3155-L of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody: Interference with Interim Orders Under Art. 185(3)
records.heading: Interim custody orders of the High Court are ordinarily not interfered with under Article 185(3)
records.text: Interim orders of the High Court are ordinarily not interfered with under Art. 185(3) of the Constitution, save in exceptional cases of flagrant violation of law, wrongful exercise of jurisdiction or grave injustice. Petitions against interim custody orders, while the s. 25 Guardians and Wards Act application was pending, were not maintainable. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1295; Khawaja Adnan Zafar v. Hina Bashir, etc (C.P.L.A. 1708-L/2022).
records.title: Khawaja Adnan Zafar v. Hina Bashir, etc (C.P.L.A. 1708-L/2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: De Facto Guardian Cannot Transfer Minor's Property
records.heading: A de facto guardian cannot transfer a minor's immovable property
records.text: Under Muslim law a de facto guardian of a minor has no power to transfer any right or interest in the minor's immovable property. The principle of estoppel is inapplicable against a minor. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1271; Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Fraud: Burden on Party Alleging
records.heading: A party alleging fraud must prove it, and bald assertions do not shift the burden
records.text: Fraud vitiates all actions. No special quantum or number of witnesses is needed to prove it, and the court must be satisfied on reliable evidence. A party alleging fraud must prove it, and bald or generalised assertions do not shift the initial burden. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1271; Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Legal Burden and Evidential Burden Distinguished
records.heading: The legal burden stays on the plaintiffs while the evidential burden may shift
records.text: The legal burden is fixed by law and pleadings and stays on the plaintiffs throughout the trial. The evidential burden shifts once sufficient evidence raises a presumption, and that evidence may be circumstantial or based on presumptions of law or fact. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1271; Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Art. 117 QSO and Preponderance
records.heading: Civil issues are decided on preponderance and burden matters only where evidence is evenly balanced
records.text: Civil issues are decided on preponderance of evidence, and burden matters only where evidence is evenly balanced. Under Art. 117 QSO the burden lies on the person asserting the affirmative, until discharged the other party need not prove his case, and admitted facts need no proof. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1271; Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Challenging a Registered Document: Mere Denial Insufficient
records.heading: Mere denial by the executant does not displace the presumption for a registered document
records.text: The standard of evidence differs for registered and unregistered documents. A registered document carries a presumption of genuineness under Arts. 85(5) and 129(e) QSO, and mere denial by the executant does not shift the burden to the beneficiary to prove valid execution. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1271; Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint to Magistrate: Cognizance by Sessions Court
records.heading: A Sessions Court cannot take cognizance of a private complaint unless the Magistrate sends it
records.text: A private complaint must be filed before the Magistrate unless the law permits otherwise. A Sessions Court cannot take cognizance of an offence as a court of original jurisdiction unless the Magistrate sends the case under s. 190(2) CrPC. Ref: 2023 LHC 7767; Umar Hasnain etc v. State etc (Crl. Revision 148-23, decided 16.06.2023); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Umar Hasnain etc v. State etc (Crl. Revision 148-23, decided 16.06.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Doubtful Eye-Witnesses and Acquittal
records.heading: Doubtful eye-witnesses contradicted by medical and site map evidence led to acquittal
records.text: The alleged eye-witnesses did not inform the police, were contradicted by the Medical Officer and the site map, gave no convincing reason for their presence, and made no attempt to save the deceased. The prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond doubt. Petitions converted into appeals and allowed, and both accused were acquitted under ss. 302(b) and 34 PPC. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1310, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 319; Mst. Saima Noreen and Muhammad Shafiq v. The State (Jail Petition No. 181 of 2016 with Criminal Petition No. 154-L of 2016).
records.title: Mst. Saima Noreen and Muhammad Shafiq v. The State (Jail Petition No. 181 of 2016 with Criminal Petition No. 154-L of 2016)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mubarik Ahmad Sani Review Case Decision
records.heading: Decision on the State's review petition in the Mubarik Ahmad Sani matter
records.text: Decision in the review petition filed by the State through the Prosecutor General Punjab in the Mubarik Ahmad Sani matter. The post gives only the case title and date, with no holding. Ref: The State through Prosecutor General Punjab v. Mubarik Ahmad Sani and another (Crl.R.P. 2/2024, decided 24.07.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Illegal Dispossession Act: Family Members and S. 7(1)
records.heading: Authority on the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 and family members under section 7(1)
records.text: Authority on the applicability of the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 to family members and the conditions for s. 7(1) of the Act. The post lists the issues without stating the holding. Ref: Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A. 66-K/2024, decided 15.07.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A. 66-K/2024, decided 15.07.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Scope and Grounds of S. 265-K CrPC
records.heading: Authority on the scope and grounds of acquittal under section 265-K CrPC
records.text: Authority on the scope and grounds of acquittal under s. 265-K CrPC. The post notes that these were discussed without stating the holding. Ref: Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A. 66-K/2024, decided 15.07.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A. 66-K/2024, decided 15.07.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Challenge to Registered Power of Attorney: Specific Pleading
records.heading: Challenge to a registered power of attorney needs specific pleading and a suit for cancellation
records.text: A challenge to a document requires specific pleadings. Where a registered power of attorney was proved, the plaintiff should have sued for cancellation under s. 39 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 and a s. 42 declaration suit was inapt. The plaintiff failed to discharge his initial onus. Petition converted to appeal and allowed, and the trial court's dismissal of the suit restored. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1319; Shah Madar Khan v. Tariq Daud and others (C.P.L.A. 3877/2023).
records.title: Shah Madar Khan v. Tariq Daud and others (C.P.L.A. 3877/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXI R. 90 CPC: Setting Aside Execution Sale
records.heading: Setting aside an execution sale requires irregularity or fraud, substantial injury and deposit
records.text: Setting aside an execution sale under O. XXI R. 90 CPC requires material irregularity or fraud, substantial injury to the applicant, and deposit of twenty percent of the sum realized at the sale or security as directed. The trial court rightly held the objections fell within r. 90. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1218; Tariq Zubair Khan v. Mst. Tabassum Khan (C.P.L.A. 4194/2023).
records.title: Tariq Zubair Khan v. Mst. Tabassum Khan (C.P.L.A. 4194/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: No Automatic Stay on Pendency Before Higher Court
records.heading: Pendency before a higher court does not automatically stay trial or execution proceedings
records.text: Under O. XX R. 1 of the Supreme Court Rules 1980, trial and execution proceedings do not stay automatically on filing a petition in the Supreme Court without an injunctive order. A trial court that stays proceedings or adjourns them sine die without such an order will face the consequences of the illegal order. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1385, PLJ 2024 SC 874; Rashid Baig, etc v. Muhammad Mansha, etc (C.P.L.A. 925-L/2018).
records.title: Rashid Baig, etc v. Muhammad Mansha, etc (C.P.L.A. 925-L/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Site Plan and Crime Empties Discrepancies
records.heading: Site plan and crime empties discrepancies left the murder charge unproved
records.text: The site plan did not show the point from which seven crime empties were said to be recovered, none was recovered near the point of the accused's alleged firing, and the firearm expert linked only two empties to a 222 caliber rifle. The prosecution failed to prove murder beyond reasonable doubt. Petition converted into appeal and allowed; accused acquitted under s. 302(b) PPC. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1224; Abdul Hameed v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 194/2024).
records.title: Abdul Hameed v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 194/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Conflicting with Prosecution Version
records.heading: A blackened entrance wound conflicted with a rifle shot from 5.5 feet
records.text: The postmortem showed a blackened and burnt area around the entrance wound, which conflicted with the claim of a rifle shot fired from 5.5 feet, and the prosecution witnesses gave no explanation. The prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt. Petition converted into appeal and allowed; accused acquitted under s. 302(b) PPC. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1224; Abdul Hameed v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 194/2024).
records.title: Abdul Hameed v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 194/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account and Unnatural Conduct of Witnesses
records.heading: Unnatural conduct of witnesses and an inaccurate site map left the ocular account unproved
