records.text: The site map omitted the horse stable and the deceased's haveli, the person whose haveli the deceased was shown occupying was not produced, and the witnesses' conduct towards the injured persons lying at the scene was unnatural. The ocular account was not proved and the charge under s. 302(b) PPC failed. Petition converted into appeal and allowed; accused acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1224; Abdul Hameed v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 194/2024).
records.title: Abdul Hameed v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 194/2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Mubarik Sani Review: Finality of Prophethood
records.heading: Review of the Mubarik Ahmad Sani order accepted in part and dismissed in part
records.text: Per the Urdu judgment extract, the Court held that its order of 6 February 2024 did not depart from binding precedent, citing PLD 1985 FSC 8 and 1993 SCMR 1718, and that the fundamental right to freedom of religion is subject to law, public order and morality. Review Petition No. 2 of 2024 was accepted and Review Petitions Nos. 3 and 4 were dismissed. Ref: The State through Prosecutor-General, Punjab v. Mubarik Ahmad Sani and another (Criminal Review Petition No. 2 of 2024 in Crl.P. 1054-L of 2023), decided 24.07.2024; Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan; Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: The State through Prosecutor-General, Punjab v. Mubarik Ahmad Sani and another (Criminal Review Petition No. 2 of 2024 in Crl.P. 1054-L of 2023), decided 24.07.2024

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Acquittal and Departmental Disciplinary Proceedings
records.heading: Acquittal in a criminal case does not bar disciplinary penalties
records.text: An acquittal in a criminal case does not absolve a person from penalties imposed in disciplinary proceedings, because proof beyond reasonable doubt is a stricter standard than the balance of probabilities applied in disciplinary proceedings. Ref: Mumtaz Uddin Shaikh v. Chief Post Master GPO Hyderabad & others (C.P.L.A. 516-K/2022, decided 19.07.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Mumtaz Uddin Shaikh v. Chief Post Master GPO Hyderabad & others (C.P.L.A. 516-K/2022, decided 19.07.2024)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Laches Judged by Conduct of the Person
records.heading: Laches is judged in the light of the conduct of the person concerned
records.text: The question of laches or delay in invoking a right is always considered in the light of the conduct of the person concerned. Ref: Mumtaz Uddin Shaikh v. Chief Post Master GPO Hyderabad & others (C.P.L.A. 516-K/2022, decided 19.07.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Mumtaz Uddin Shaikh v. Chief Post Master GPO Hyderabad & others (C.P.L.A. 516-K/2022, decided 19.07.2024)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Scope of Section 5: Inquiry and Investigation
records.heading: Distinction between inquiry and investigation under section 5 of the Illegal Dispossession Act
records.text: Authority on the scope of s. 5 of the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 for inquiry and investigation. An inquiry reviews an allegation to determine whether it is responsible, which law may have been breached and whether an investigation is warranted; the investigation stage follows where a breach is substantiated and responsibility is not accepted or other issues warrant it. Ref: Noor Khan etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 2454/22, decided 27.06.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Noor Khan etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 2454/22, decided 27.06.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Mala Fide and s. 489-F
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is extraordinary relief granted only on proof of mala fide and further inquiry
records.text: Whether a cheque was issued in fulfilment of an obligation under s. 489-F PPC is a question for the Trial Court after evidence. Pre-arrest bail is extraordinary relief, available only where the conditions of s. 497(2) CrPC are met and reasonable grounds for further inquiry are shown, and it is granted only if mala fide of the complainant or police is established. Ref: Azhar Pervaiz Bukhari v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 619-L/2024, decided 01.07.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Azhar Pervaiz Bukhari v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A. 619-L/2024, decided 01.07.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Costs on Frivolous Litigation
records.heading: Frivolous litigation must be discouraged and may be met with costs
records.text: Frivolous litigation must be rooted out and strongly discouraged. One way to curb frivolous and vexatious cases is the imposition of costs under Order XXVIII, Rule 3 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1990. The Court noted about 2.2 million cases pending before all courts in the country. Ref: Asma Haleem v. Abdul Haseeb Chaudhry and others (C.P.L.A. 3300/2024, decided 30.07.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Asma Haleem v. Abdul Haseeb Chaudhry and others (C.P.L.A. 3300/2024, decided 30.07.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Defective Investigation Report and s. 173 Directions
records.heading: A defective investigation report differs from a defective investigation; section 173 directions issued
records.text: Distinguishes a defective investigation report from a defective investigation. Directions are issued for timely submission of investigation reports to ensure strict compliance with s. 173 CrPC, requiring investigating officers, prosecutors, judges, magistrates and jail superintendents to follow the principles in Hakeem Mumtaz and the instructions of the Directorate of District Judiciary. Ref: 2024 LHC 3574; Rahat Abbas etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 1979-B-24, decided 09.05.2024); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Rahat Abbas etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 1979-B-24, decided 09.05.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats: Dissenting Note on PTI Entitlement
records.heading: Dissenting note held reserved seats for PTI would be relief created by the Court
records.text: In their detailed dissenting note, two judges held that granting reserved seats to PTI would be relief created by the Court itself, requiring departure from Arts 175 and 185 and suspension of Arts 51, 63 and 106. They noted PTI was not a party and the Sunni Ittehad Council did not contest the election as a political party. Ref: (Civil Appeal No. 333/2024 and connected matters, detailed reasons of short order announced 12.07.2024); Justice Aminuddin Khan; Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: (Civil Appeal No. 333/2024 and connected matters, detailed reasons of short order announced 12.07.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Regularisation: Contract Increments as Personal Allowance
records.heading: Regularisation is a fresh appointment, and contract increments are payable as Personal Allowance
records.text: Regularisation is a fresh appointment with immediate effect, relying on 2024 SCMR 527, 2021 SCMR 760 and 2021 SCMR 767. Increments earned in contract service are payable as Personal Allowance under cl. 6 of the Punjab notification of 19.10.2009, but do not form part of emoluments for pension. Review allowed and earlier order of 08.02.2021 recalled. Ref: Chief Secretary, Government of the Punjab, Lahore, etc. v. Parveen Shad (C.R.P. 30-L/2021 in C.P.L.A. 1641-L/2018 etc.), decided 08.07.2024; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Chief Secretary, Government of the Punjab, Lahore, etc. v. Parveen Shad (C.R.P. 30-L/2021 in C.P.L.A. 1641-L/2018 etc.), decided 08.07.2024

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Right of Appeal in Family Cases
records.heading: Authority on the right of appeal in family cases
records.text: Authority on the right of appeal in family cases. The post gives no holding. Ref: Syed Raheel Ahmed v. Mst. Syeda Zona Naqvi and others (C.P.L.A. 473-K/2024, decided 26.07.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Syed Raheel Ahmed v. Mst. Syeda Zona Naqvi and others (C.P.L.A. 473-K/2024, decided 26.07.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: High Court as Appellate Court in Constitutional Jurisdiction
records.heading: Authority on whether the High Court may resolve factual controversies as an appellate court
records.text: Authority on whether the High Court can sit as a court of appeal to address factual controversies in its constitutional jurisdiction. The post gives no holding. Ref: Syed Raheel Ahmed v. Mst. Syeda Zona Naqvi and others (C.P.L.A. 473-K/2024, decided 26.07.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Syed Raheel Ahmed v. Mst. Syeda Zona Naqvi and others (C.P.L.A. 473-K/2024, decided 26.07.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance on Oral Agreement: Proof
records.heading: An oral agreement of sale must be proved by the clearest evidence and pleaded in detail
records.text: An oral agreement is valid and enforceable but must be proved by the clearest and most satisfactory evidence. A party seeking specific performance of a sale of immovable property on an oral agreement bears the onus of proving mutual consensus on the terms, and must plead them in detail. No evidence can be considered on a plea of fact not raised in the pleadings. Ref: Hafiz Qari Abdul Fateh v. Miss Urooj Fatima & others (C.P.L.A. 174-K/2022, decided 24.07.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Hafiz Qari Abdul Fateh v. Miss Urooj Fatima & others (C.P.L.A. 174-K/2022, decided 24.07.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Samples
records.heading: Parcels sent beyond seventy two hours and a missing transmitter witness led to acquittal
records.text: The prosecution must establish every step from recovery to sealing, safe custody and safe transmission of sample parcels to the laboratory, and a missing link benefits the accused. Here the parcels were sent beyond seventy two hours contrary to Rule 4(2) of the Control of Narcotic Substances (Government Analysts) Rules 2001 and the transmitting Sub-Inspector was not produced. Appeal allowed; accused acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1408.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody: Non-Production of Moharrar
records.heading: Non-production of the Moharrar means safe custody of contraband parcels is not established
records.text: The Moharrar of the police station was not produced, so safe custody of the contraband parcels (146.20 kilograms of charas) and the sample parcel was not established. The prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt. Petition converted into appeal and allowed; accused acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1571.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion: Corroborative Value Only
records.heading: Absconsion is only a suspicious circumstance and cannot found a conviction
records.text: Mere absconsion is not conclusive proof of guilt and is only a suspicious circumstance that cannot take the place of proof. It may corroborate substantive evidence but must be read along with it, cannot cure defects in the prosecution case and cannot by itself found a conviction. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1579.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion of Accused: Effect
records.heading: Abscondence is corroborative only and cannot remedy defects in the prosecution case
records.text: Abscondence may be used as corroborative evidence but must be read with substantive evidence. It has no value without other evidence, cannot remedy defects in the prosecution case and cannot alone sustain a conviction. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1449.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Hanging Versus Strangulation: Medical Evidence
records.heading: Absence of strangulation marks made the claim of death by throttling doubtful
records.text: The judgment lists distinguishing marks of death by hanging and death by strangulation. The medical officer admitted there were no scratches or injury marks usually found in strangulation, so, applying Modi's Medical Jurisprudence and Toxicology, the claim that death was caused by throttling was doubtful. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1507.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Non-Prohibitory Clause Offences: Bail as Rule
records.heading: Bail is the rule and refusal the exception outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: For offences not falling within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1596.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Registration of Other Cases Not a Bar
records.heading: Registration of other cases does not bar bail where a prima facie case exists
records.text: Mere registration of other criminal cases against an accused does not disentitle him to bail if he has a prima facie case on merits. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1596.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Rule of Consistency and Doctrine of Parity
records.heading: Bail to a co-accused with the same role extends to the accused on parity
records.text: Where the role ascribed to the accused is the same as that of a co-accused who has received bail, the same benefit should be extended, on the principle that like cases are treated alike. The Court must first assess the accused's role and then decide whether parity is made out. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1528.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: First Proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC: Women Accused
records.heading: The first proviso to section 497(1) CrPC is welfare legislation to be read purposively
records.text: The first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC permits conditional release on bail of an accused under sixteen years, a woman, or a sick or infirm person. It is welfare legislation to be interpreted purposively, having regard to the circumstances of each case, including the absence of criminal record or habitual offending, and the interests of children of women accused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1528.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Female Accused: Further Inquiry and Consistency
records.heading: A female accused with a co-accused's bail and no mastermind role gets bail on consistency
records.text: All other co-accused, including the main accused who fired on the deceased, had been granted bail, and nothing showed the female petitioner to be the mastermind. She made out a case of further inquiry and was entitled to bail under the rule of consistency and the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC. Petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1528.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Better to Err in Granting Bail
records.heading: It is better to err in granting bail than in refusing it
records.text: It is better to err in granting bail than in refusing it, because ultimate conviction and sentence can repair the wrong resulting from a mistaken grant of bail. Liberty is a precious right guaranteed by the Constitution. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1525, 2024 SCMR 1567, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 7.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Prohibitory Clause, Specific Role
records.heading: Bail refused where a specific firing role is supported by ocular, medical and recovery evidence
records.text: The petitioner was nominated with a specific role of firing at the deceased and injured person, with ocular account, medical evidence, recovery of empties and recovery of a pistol on his pointation supporting the prosecution. The case fell within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Petition dismissed, leave declined and bail refused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1576.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Ground of Delay in Trial
records.heading: A single section 265-K application does not show deliberate delay barring statutory bail
records.text: Bail on the statutory ground of delay in conclusion of trial is a right unless the delay is caused by the accused's own conduct, such as repetitive irrelevant applications. Moving a single application under s. 265-K CrPC does not show deliberate delay. Petition converted into appeal and allowed; post-arrest bail granted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1479.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Scope of Terrorism under Section 6 ATA
records.heading: Terrorism under section 6 ATA requires the action and its intent to meet the statutory nexus
records.text: An offence is terrorism only if the action falls within s. 6(2) ATA 1997 and its intent, motivation, object, design or purpose has a nexus with s. 6(1)(b) and (c). This is determined from the FIR, investigation material and evidence as a whole. Without these ingredients, heinousness or terror caused in society does not make an act terrorism. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1437.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Kidnapping for Ransom: Personal Vendetta Not Terrorism
records.heading: Kidnapping for ransom from personal vendetta is an offence under section 365-A PPC, not terrorism
records.text: Kidnapping for ransom falls under s. 6(2)(e) ATA only if done with the intent or purpose of terrorism. An act for personal vendetta is an offence under s. 365-A PPC, triable by the ATC only for speedy trial, and the accused is charged under s. 365-A PPC. Convictions under s. 7(e) ATA were converted to s. 365-A PPC with life imprisonment. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1437.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Murder of Police Raiding Party Not Terrorism
records.heading: Firing on a raiding party to avoid arrest inside a house was not terrorism
records.text: Firing by the petitioners on a raiding party, to avoid arrest, inside a house with no evidence of the public being present, lacked the intent or object of terrorism and any sense of fear in society. Convictions under s. 7 ATA were set aside, while convictions under ss. 302(b), 34 and 324 PPC of two petitioners were maintained. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1437.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Jurisdiction of ATC over Heinous Offences
records.heading: Section 13 ATA lets the ATC try Third Schedule heinous offences outside terrorism
records.text: Section 13 ATA 1997 empowers the ATC to try offences under the Act and also heinous offences that do not fall within the definition of terrorism but are included in the Third Schedule by the government. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1437.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Cannot Identify the Culprit
records.heading: Medical evidence cannot identify the culprit where the eye-witness account is unreliable
records.text: Medical evidence by its nature cannot identify a culprit in an unwitnessed incident. Where the eye-witness account relied on by the prosecution is unreliable, a conviction cannot be sustained on medical evidence alone. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1449.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Doubt Suffices
records.heading: A single loophole in the prosecution case entitles the accused to the benefit of doubt
records.text: A single loophole or lacuna in the prosecution case entitles the accused to its benefit. It is unnecessary that many circumstances create uncertainty, and any doubt is resolved in favour of the accused, including one circumstance sufficient to suggest the evidence was fabricated to procure conviction. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1427, 2024 SCMR 1490, 2024 SCMR 1507.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Corroboratory Evidence and Unreliable Witness
records.heading: Corroboratory evidence cannot make an unreliable witness reliable
records.text: Corroboratory evidence does not convert an unreliable witness or unreliable evidence into a reliable one. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1427.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Heinousness Not a Ground for Conviction
records.heading: Heinousness alone is no ground to punish an accused where the case is not proved
records.text: Mere heinousness of an offence, if the case is not proved to the hilt, is not a ground to punish the accused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1490.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder Conviction Upheld: Recovery and Forensic Match
records.heading: Murder conviction upheld on pistol recovery, forensic match and a witness seeing him flee
records.text: The petitioner, who surrendered, disclosed the .30 bore pistol and it was recovered on his pointation. The Forensic Science Laboratory matched two crime cartridges from the scene to it, and a witness saw him fleeing the scene. The case under s. 302(b) PPC was proved. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1413.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: s. 489-F: Proof of Loan or Obligation; Further Inquiry
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC requires material showing a loan or obligation behind the cheque
records.text: Mere issuance and dishonour of a cheque is insufficient under s. 489-F PPC; there must be material showing a loan or obligation for which it was issued. Where the record did not show when, why and before whom the Rs 32,00,000 was paid, applicability of s. 489-F needed further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Bail granted. Ref: 2024 MLD 1363.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: s. 489-F PPC Not a Recovery Tool; Bail as Rule
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC punishes dishonest issuance and is not a recovery tool; bail is the rule
records.text: Section 489-F PPC is meant to punish dishonest issuance of a cheque, not to recover money. Its punishment of up to three years, fine or both falls outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so bail is the rule and refusal the exception, even for a large amount. Ref: 2024 MLD 1363.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Proclaimed Offender: Thirty Day Proclamation Period
records.heading: A person arrested before the thirty day proclamation period expires is not a proclaimed offender
records.text: The period for appearance in a proclamation cannot be less than 30 days. The petitioner was arrested about 21 days after the proclamation was issued, before expiry of the period, so he could not be termed a proclaimed offender for proceedings under ss. 512 and 173 CrPC. Ref: 2024 MLD 1363.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence and Chance Witnesses
records.heading: Last seen evidence from unnamed chance witnesses with inconsistent accounts is not reliable
records.text: The last seen witness was not named in the FIR or the complainant's supplementary statement, the witnesses gave inconsistent accounts of where the deceased was last seen, and all lived 17 to 21 kilometres away so were chance witnesses. They gave no reason for being present. The last seen evidence was not worthy of reliance. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1310.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 84 QSO: Court's Visual Comparison of Signatures
records.heading: The Court may visually compare signatures itself under Article 84 QSO
records.text: In certain eventualities the Court has plenary power to compare signatures with other relevant material itself to resolve the controversy. A visual comparison of signatures on sale deeds by the Trial Court under Art. 84 QSO is in consonance with the law. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1271.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Deposit of Balance Sale Consideration
records.heading: Deposit of balance sale consideration is required only under a Court order
records.text: The Specific Relief Act 1877 has no provision requiring the plaintiff to deposit the balance sale consideration in Court automatically; a deposit is required only under a Court order with a timeline. The plaintiff bears the initial burden of showing readiness and willingness, and may offer to deposit. Appeal allowed and the case remanded to the High Court. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1496; Meer Gul v. Raja Zafar Mehmood (Civil Appeal No. 51-K of 2021).
records.title: Meer Gul v. Raja Zafar Mehmood (Civil Appeal No. 51-K of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements and False Implication
records.heading: Uninjured witnesses making dishonest improvements and enmity left the charge unproved
records.text: Two witnesses claimed to be with the deceased yet received no injury, which was not believable, and both made dishonest improvements at trial. Their ocular testimony lacked corroboration and false implication due to previous enmity could not be ruled out. The prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1579.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Failure to Collect Blood Stained Earth
records.heading: Failure to collect blood stained earth casts doubt on the place of occurrence
records.text: No blood stained earth was collected from the alleged place of occurrence and no explanation was offered by any prosecution witness or the Investigating Officer. This created serious doubt about the place of occurrence as narrated by the prosecution witnesses. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1579.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eye-Witnesses Doubtful
records.heading: Eye-witnesses who did not take the deceased to hospital were doubtful and unreliable
records.text: The deceased's father and brother neither shifted him to hospital nor accompanied him, the delay in the postmortem and the identification of the body by two other persons cast doubt on their presence at the scene, and their testimony had material contradictions. Their evidence was unreliable and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1449.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Wire and Pistol Inconsequential
records.heading: Recovery of a wire and pistol is relevant only if the ocular account inspires confidence
records.text: Recoveries of an electric wire and the pistol are corroborative evidence and are relevant only when the ocular account inspires confidence. The ocular account here was full of contradictions. Appeals allowed and both appellants acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1507.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Lodging FIR
records.heading: Unexplained sixteen hour delay in lodging the FIR makes the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: The formal FIR was registered over sixteen hours after the incident although the police station was 16 km away, and the prosecution gave no explanation. The delay showed dishonesty, deliberation and consultation by the complainant and made the prosecution case doubtful. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1427.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Double-Edged Motive and Interested Complainant
records.heading: Motive from enmity cuts both ways and an interested complainant raises doubt
records.text: Motive arising from enmity of murder between the parties cuts both ways and may explain false implication. The complainant, unrelated to the deceased, pursued a private complaint even after the police found the petitioner innocent, which raised doubt over his motives and the prosecution case. The High Court rightly disbelieved the motive. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1427.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Weapon Recovery Without Forensic Report
records.heading: Gun recovery without a positive firearm expert report is rightly disbelieved
records.text: Recovery of a single barrel gun on the accused's pointation was rightly disbelieved without a positive firearm expert report. Recovery is corroborative evidence, relevant only when the ocular account inspires confidence, which it did not here. Jail petition converted into appeal and allowed; accused acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1427.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay of Fifteen Hours in FIR
records.heading: Unexplained fifteen hour delay in the FIR shows deliberation and consultation
records.text: The matter was reported over fifteen hours after the incident although the police station was one furlong away, and the prosecution did not explain the delay. The delayed FIR showed dishonesty and that it was lodged with deliberation and consultation. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1490.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Star Witnesses Not Named in FIR; Belated s. 161 Statements
records.heading: Eye-witnesses not named in the FIR and examined late under section 161 CrPC are doubtful
records.text: The two alleged eye-witnesses were not named in the FIR and their statements under s. 161 CrPC were recorded after a delay of 16 hours, without plausible explanation. This cast serious doubt on the prosecution version, and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1490.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconsion Not Conclusive Proof of Guilt
records.heading: Abscondence is not conclusive proof of guilt and cannot take the place of proof
records.text: Mere abscondence is not conclusive proof of guilt, its value depends on the facts of each case, and it cannot take the place of proof unless the case is otherwise proved by cogent and reliable evidence. Here the accused explained they feared a fake police encounter as the deceased's son was a policeman. Ref: 2024 YLR 1924; Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22).
records.title: Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Postmortem Report: Doctor Must Appear
records.heading: A postmortem report cannot be read unless the doctor appears to authenticate it
records.text: A postmortem report is expert opinion whose contents cannot be read unless the doctor appears to authenticate it, and Art. 78 QSO requires proof of execution. Where the doctor had died and a clerk merely tendered the reports, they were of no use to the prosecution, as the doctor was not tested by cross-examination. Ref: 2024 YLR 1924; Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22).
records.title: Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documents Exhibited Through Statement of Counsel
records.heading: Documents cannot be admitted solely through counsel's statement as it denies cross-examination
records.text: Documents cannot be admitted into evidence solely through the statement of counsel, as this compromises the opposing party's right of cross-examination. Documents exhibited that way without opportunity for cross-examination do not meet the standards of admissibility. Ref: 2024 CLC 1246.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Tests of Reliability
records.heading: A dying declaration must be shown to be honest, voluntary and made by a fit person
records.text: A dying declaration is a question of fact decided on the circumstances of each case. It may be made before a private person, who must be examined, and it must be shown that it was made honestly, by a person in a fit state of mind, free from outside influence, fearing death and making a truthful statement.

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: PECA 2016 and ETO 2002: Offences Before Commencement
records.heading: PECA 2016 does not apply to conduct that occurred before it came into force
records.text: The alleged threatening and blackmailing through personal pictures occurred about a year before PECA 2016 came into force on 18.08.2016, so PECA was not attracted. Sections 36 and 37 of the Electronic Transactions Ordinance 2002 were also not attracted, and both courts below committed no illegality. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1520.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Expectancy of Life: Long Incarceration on Death Sentence
records.heading: Long incarceration under a death sentence may justify reduction to life imprisonment
records.text: Where a convict under sentence of death has served custody equal to or more than a full term of life imprisonment during his remedies, expectancy of life may be considered with other circumstances to reduce the sentence. The petitioner spent 16 years in the death cell with delay not attributable to him. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC maintained; death sentence reduced to life imprisonment. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1474.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unproved Motive as Mitigating Circumstance
records.heading: Failure to prove motive is a mitigating circumstance for reducing a death sentence
records.text: Failure of the prosecution to prove the alleged motive, here enmity over land and matrimonial relations, can be a mitigating circumstance for reducing the sentence. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC maintained, death sentence converted to imprisonment for life. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1474.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Mitigating Circumstances for Lesser Sentence
records.heading: Unproved motive and a single stab wound justified a life sentence
records.text: The High Court rightly disbelieved the recovery of the knife from an open place, and rightly treated absence of motive in the FIR, the unproved motive set up at trial and a single stab wound as mitigating circumstances warranting imprisonment for life. Petition dismissed, leave refused and the life sentence maintained. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1421.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Foundational Elements of s. 489-F PPC
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC requires dishonest issuance towards a loan or obligation and dishonour
records.text: The foundational elements of an offence under s. 489-F PPC are issuance of the cheque with dishonest intent, issuance towards repayment of a loan or fulfilment of an obligation, and dishonour of the cheque. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1596.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Implausible Sequence of Events
records.heading: An implausible sequence of events and few empties made the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: Eye-witnesses said ten armed accused kept up indiscriminate firing yet the witnesses escaped by taking cover behind trees, a sequence that did not appeal to reason. The claim was also negated by the recovery of only eleven empty cartridges. The prosecution case was doubtful. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1427.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Sending Weapon for Forensic Analysis
records.heading: Unexplained delay of over 19 days in sending weapons for forensic analysis led to acquittal
records.text: A pistol, live cartridges and empty shells were sent for forensic examination after an unexplained delay of more than 19 days. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Appeal allowed, judgments of the Trial Court and High Court set aside and the appellant acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1490.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction Upheld: Statement of Injured and Postmortem
records.heading: Conviction upheld on the injured's statement to those who responded and the postmortem
records.text: The unnatural death by a stab wound was undisputed, two witnesses responded to the deceased's cries and she named the petitioner as inflicting churri blows, and the postmortem showed she survived about one hour 35 minutes. Petition dismissed, leave refused and life imprisonment maintained. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1421.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Recount Petitions: Returning Officer's Duty
records.heading: A Returning Officer has power to recount votes under section 95(5) of the Elections Act
records.text: In the majority detailed judgment (2 to 1), the Court held that the High Court overlooked s. 95(5) of the Elections Act 2017, as amended on 5 August 2023, giving the Returning Officer power to recount votes. It stated that the election dispute forum is the Election Tribunal and that a Returning Officer cannot surrender authority to a crowd or neglect duty. Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi dissented. Ref: (Civil Petitions No. 1573, 1673, 1729, 1767 and 2433 of 2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan; Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: (Civil Petitions No. 1573, 1673, 1729, 1767 and 2433 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIA, Justice of Peace and Torture and Custodial Death Act 2022
records.heading: A complaint before the FIA is competent under the Torture and Custodial Death Act 2022
records.text: The Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act 2022 is lex specialis, so a complaint before the FIA is competent even if local police have registered an FIR. The FIA is a police force under s. 5 FIA Act and falls within the jurisdiction of the Justice of Peace under s. 22-A CrPC, who may direct it.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: List of Authorities
records.heading: Compilation of Supreme Court and Lahore High Court judgments on last seen evidence
records.text: Compilation of Supreme Court and Lahore High Court judgments on last seen evidence. The post gives citations without holdings. Ref: 2021 SCMR 873, 2021 SCMR 662, 2019 SCMR 1317, 2019 SCMR 1224 and others.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Vendee of Co-Sharer Steps into Vendor's Shoes
records.heading: The vendee of a co-sharer steps into the vendor's shoes up to his share
records.text: The vendee of a co-sharer owning an undivided khata has the same rights as the vendor, no more and no less. Until partition, the vendee steps into the vendor's shoes for ownership of the area purchased, provided it does not exceed the vendor's share in the whole property. Ref: Zafar Iqbal and others v. Muhammad Rafiq and others (Civil Appeal No. 477-L of 2011, date of hearing 02.07.2024).
records.title: Zafar Iqbal and others v. Muhammad Rafiq and others (Civil Appeal No. 477-L of 2011, date of hearing 02.07.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Accused Arrested in Another Case
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is not dismissed for non-prosecution if the accused is jailed in another case
records.text: If an accused granted ad-interim pre-arrest bail in one case is arrested and confined in jail in another case, his pre-arrest bail petition is not dismissed for non-prosecution. It is decided after procuring his attendance. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 486; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Anti-Terrorism Court etc. (Crl. Revision 54056/23).
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. Anti-Terrorism Court etc. (Crl. Revision 54056/23)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Habeas Corpus: Nature and Purpose
records.heading: Habeas corpus tests the validity of imprisonment and protects personal liberty
records.text: Habeas corpus, meaning 'you have the body', has its roots in personal liberty and human dignity and is the means by which the validity of imprisonment is tested. If restriction on a person is illegal, the courts should step in to free him. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 476; Abid Hameed v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 66114 of 2022).
records.title: Abid Hameed v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 66114 of 2022)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 63(1)(h): Moral Turpitude and Tosha Khana Gifts
records.heading: Concealing Tosha Khana gifts is moral turpitude disqualifying under Article 63(1)(h)
records.text: A convicted person cannot contest elections under Art. 63(1)(h) of the Constitution if involved in a case of moral turpitude. Concealment of the fact of obtaining gifts from Tosha Khana falls within the definition of moral turpitude. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 502; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The Returning Officer NA-122 Lahore-VI etc (Election Appeal 831/24).
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The Returning Officer NA-122 Lahore-VI etc (Election Appeal 831/24)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Kidnapping for Ransom: Terrorism Intent Required
records.heading: Kidnapping for ransom is terrorism only if done with the intent of terrorism
records.text: Kidnapping for ransom was placed in the Third Schedule ATA 1997 for heinousness and speedy trial by the ATC only. It is terrorism under s. 6(2)(e) only if done with the design, purpose or intent of terrorism; otherwise it is an offence under s. 365-A PPC, and the accused is charged and tried only under s. 365-A PPC. Ref: Rizwan Rasheed & another v. The State (J.P. 193 of 2016, date of hearing 21.03.2024).
records.title: Rizwan Rasheed & another v. The State (J.P. 193 of 2016, date of hearing 21.03.2024)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Possession of Explosives: Shifting of Onus
records.heading: The onus on the accused to justify possession of explosives arises only after the prosecution proves possession
records.text: A statutory presumption in a penal enactment must be strictly construed. The onus shifts to the accused to prove lawful justification for possession of explosive substance only after the prosecution first proves his possession. Absent evidence of justification, the contrary is proved, in line with the purpose requirement of s. 6(1)(c) ATA. Ref: Muhammad Asjad v. The State, etc. (Criminal Petition No. 809-L of 2017).
records.title: Muhammad Asjad v. The State, etc. (Criminal Petition No. 809-L of 2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence and Proof Beyond Reasonable Doubt
records.heading: The presumption of innocence remains until guilt is proved beyond reasonable doubt
records.text: The presumption of innocence remains until the prosecution proves guilt beyond reasonable doubt, which requires evidence that convinces a prudent person. The presumption of innocence is adequate to warrant acquittal unless the court is fully convinced of guilt. Ref: Muhammad Jahangir Muhammad Lateef v. The State (Jail Petition No. 514/2016 & Crl. P. 1011-L/2016, date of hearing 06.05.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Jahangir Muhammad Lateef v. The State (Jail Petition No. 514/2016 & Crl. P. 1011-L/2016, date of hearing 06.05.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Habeas Corpus: Minor's Custody and Visitation Rights
records.heading: Visitation rights of a minor lie exclusively with the Guardian Court, not in habeas corpus
records.text: In habeas corpus proceedings under s. 491 CrPC, the father's custody of the minor was lawful and in the minor's welfare. The Additional Sessions Judge exceeded jurisdiction by enforcing a meeting schedule for the step-sister, since determining visitation rights lies exclusively with the Guardian Court. The orders enforcing meetings were set aside. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 476; Abid Hameed v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 66114 of 2022).
records.title: Abid Hameed v. Additional Sessions Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 66114 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Disclosure Leading to Recovery
records.heading: Article 40 QSO needs a disclosure in custody, preferably written before witnesses, leading to discovery
records.text: To attract Art. 40 QSO, the prosecution must prove that the accused in police custody conveyed information, which should be in writing and before witnesses, leading to discovery of a new fact. Discovery alone is insufficient. The investigating officer did not record the appellant's disclosure in writing before a witness, so the dagger recovery was immaterial. Ref: (Criminal Appeal No. 577/2019 & Crl. P. 596/2016).
records.title: (Criminal Appeal No. 577/2019 & Crl. P. 596/2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Witnesses
records.heading: Witnesses who made no attempt to save the deceased have doubtful presence
records.text: The prosecution witnesses did not try to save the deceased, which was unnatural conduct, so their presence at the time of the crime was doubtful and the occurrence appeared unseen. Such witnesses must be scrutinised with greater care and circumspection. Ref: (Criminal Appeal No. 577/2019 & Crl. P. 596/2016).
records.title: (Criminal Appeal No. 577/2019 & Crl. P. 596/2016)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Family Settlement: Principles and Significance
records.heading: A genuine and bona fide family settlement is upheld and cannot be revoked by a party who benefited
records.text: A family settlement must be genuine and bona fide, aimed at resolving family disputes and conflicting claims, and courts uphold such arrangements made in good faith to discourage litigation. The judgment sets out principles drawn from Pakistani, Indian and English case law, including that a party who took material benefits under the arrangement cannot seek to revoke it. Ref: Bashir Ahmed (deceased) through his L.Rs., etc v. Nazir Ahmad, etc (C.A. 197-L/2019, decided 19.08.2024); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Bashir Ahmed (deceased) through his L.Rs., etc v. Nazir Ahmad, etc (C.A. 197-L/2019, decided 19.08.2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Rationale of the Juvenile Justice System
records.heading: The juvenile justice system is rehabilitative and restorative and rests on the best interest of the child
records.text: The juvenile justice system treats juveniles differently from adults because of their immaturity and amenability to rehabilitation. It is rehabilitative and restorative rather than retributive, and is built on the best interest of the child, in line with international conventions such as the UNCRC. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 843; Mehran v. Ubaid Ullah and others (Crl.P.L.A. 80-P/2024).
records.title: Mehran v. Ubaid Ullah and others (Crl.P.L.A. 80-P/2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Juvenile Bail: s. 6(4) and 6(5) JJSA 2018
records.heading: Section 6(5) of the JJSA 2018 gives juveniles a distinct bail ground for delay in trial
records.text: Section 6(4) of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018 governs bail on merits, while s. 6(5) gives a distinct ground of bail for a juvenile detained over six months whose trial is incomplete, unless the delay is caused by the juvenile. Delay caused by the co-accused's absence cannot be attributed to the petitioner. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 843, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 270; Mehran v. Ubaid Ullah and others (Crl.P.L.A. 80-P/2024).
records.title: Mehran v. Ubaid Ullah and others (Crl.P.L.A. 80-P/2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Adequate Alternate Remedy
records.heading: The alternate remedy rule under Article 199 regulates the exercise, not the existence, of jurisdiction
records.text: The High Court will not ordinarily entertain a petition under Art. 199 where an adequate remedy exists, but this rule regulates exercise and not existence of jurisdiction. Exceptions include orders palpably without jurisdiction, manifestly mala fide, void or coram non judice. Bypassing a statutory remedy is discouraged, and the Court must consider whether the remedy is illusory. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 838; Muhammad Safeer and others v. Muhammad Azam and others (Civil Petition No. 888 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Safeer and others v. Muhammad Azam and others (Civil Petition No. 888 of 2024)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Scope of Review under s. 8 Board of Revenue Act 1957
records.heading: Review under section 8 of the Board of Revenue Act is limited to prescribed grounds
records.text: Review is a statutory power limited to the conditions the legislature prescribes and is distinct from appeal. Section 8(1) of the Board of Revenue Act 1957 allows review only on new and important matter or evidence, a mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or any other sufficient reason, which does not extend to every ground. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 838; Muhammad Safeer and others v. Muhammad Azam and others (Civil Petition No. 888 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Safeer and others v. Muhammad Azam and others (Civil Petition No. 888 of 2024)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: ANF Not a Person Aggrieved under s. 43 Prevention of Smuggling Act
records.heading: The ANF as complainant is not a person aggrieved entitled to appeal under section 43
records.text: The Anti-Narcotic Force as complainant is not a 'person aggrieved' entitled to appeal under s. 43 of the Prevention of Smuggling Act 1977 against a Special Judge's order. The right of appeal is statutory and cannot be implied. Its appeal was rightly held not maintainable. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 810; The State through A.N.F., Rawalpindi v. Obaid Khan (Civil Appeal No. 277 of 2014).
records.title: The State through A.N.F., Rawalpindi v. Obaid Khan (Civil Appeal No. 277 of 2014)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Declaring a Witness Hostile
records.heading: A witness disowning his section 161 statement may be declared hostile under Article 150 QSO
records.text: A prosecution witness who disowns his s. 161 CrPC statement, or whose answers conflict with other evidence, may be declared hostile and cross-examined by the prosecution in the Court's discretion. The Trial Court wrongly refused because the statement lacked his signature. Petition allowed and the Trial Court directed to reconsider. Ref: PLD 2024 Balochistan 123.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Right of Appeal: Person Adversely Affected
records.heading: Where an appeal is given without specifying who may use it, any aggrieved person may appeal
records.text: Where a right of appeal is given from a judgment, decree or order without specifying who may use it, every person adversely affected and aggrieved by it may appeal. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 830; M/s. Tanveer Cotton Mills (Pvt.) Ltd. Lahore v. Summit Bank Limited, etc (C.P.L.A. 1422-L/2021).
records.title: M/s. Tanveer Cotton Mills (Pvt.) Ltd. Lahore v. Summit Bank Limited, etc (C.P.L.A. 1422-L/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 539-B CrPC: Local Inspection by Court
records.heading: The power of local inspection under section 539-B CrPC cannot be delegated
records.text: The power of spot inspection under s. 539-B CrPC cannot be delegated by the Trial Court to any other officer, and cannot substitute for collecting evidence. The order appointing a local commission after final arguments was not sustainable. Petition allowed and the Trial Court directed to decide on the evidence brought on record. Ref: PLD 2024 Peshawar 140.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Quantum of Maintenance of Minors
records.heading: A father must maintain his children at a reasonable standard according to his ability
records.text: A father must maintain his children, and the quantum is set at a reasonable standard considering education, status, expenses and the minors' needs, with no fixed formula. The main consideration is the father's ability, and merely claiming lack of resources does not discharge the obligation. The mother should not bear the burden. Ref: 2024 CLC 1580; Syed Zain Muntazar Mehdi v. Mst. Sara Naqvi etc. (Writ Petition No. 370 of 2024).
records.title: Syed Zain Muntazar Mehdi v. Mst. Sara Naqvi etc. (Writ Petition No. 370 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Doubtful Source of Light
records.heading: Identification at night is doubtful where the source of light is not proved
records.text: The occurrence was at 10:30 p.m. with only a torch, which was not taken into possession, and moonlight, which was not proved as it was the sixth night of the Islamic month. Insufficient light cast doubt on the witnesses' identification of the assailants and their roles. Ref: 2024 YLR 1924; Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22).
records.title: Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Witnesses Doubtful: Unnatural Conduct
records.heading: Witnesses unfamiliar with the place and passive against armed assailants had doubtful presence
records.text: The complainant was not a resident of the place and could not name persons cultivating the land, and the deceased's son also failed to show familiarity with the area. Against natural conduct, they did not try to capture hatchet-armed assailants. Their presence was not established and their testimony could not be used against the accused. Ref: 2024 YLR 1924; Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22).
records.title: Allah Ditta etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 82543/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Defective Investigation: Inquest Report Discrepancies
records.heading: Inquest report discrepancies and unexplained investigation lapses left the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: The inquest report recorded the time of information of death and inquest inconsistently with the prosecution timeline, and the Investigating Officer gave no plausible explanation. He also left the drawing of the body's position blank. His conduct was not above board and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 YLR 1892; Asjad Mehmood v. State.
records.title: Asjad Mehmood v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Witnesses who stood as silent spectators showed unnatural conduct and unreliable evidence
records.text: Several adult male relatives and others present did not try to save the deceased or apprehend the accused, who was armed only with a churri and inflicted 11 injuries. They stood as silent spectators, so their conduct was unnatural and their evidence unworthy of reliance. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2024 YLR 1868; Imran Ali v. State.
records.title: Imran Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: Presence Not Proved
records.heading: Chance witnesses with an unexplained presence and a belated female witness are doubtful
records.text: The complainant and one eye-witness lived in another district, and the story explaining their presence at the village was absent from the FIR and so appeared concocted. They were chance witnesses. A female eye-witness who first made her statement two days after the occurrence was also doubtful. Ref: 2024 YLR 1868; Imran Ali v. State.
records.title: Imran Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Ocular Account and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Eye-witnesses speaking of one injury against eleven injuries found were probably not present
records.text: All eye-witnesses spoke of a single injury, but the medical officer and postmortem report showed eleven injuries. This conflict between ocular and medical evidence suggested the witnesses were not present at the spot. Ref: 2024 YLR 1868; Imran Ali v. State.
records.title: Imran Ali v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Withholding of Independent Witnesses
records.heading: The prosecution need not produce all named witnesses where other evidence inspires confidence
records.text: The prosecution is not bound to produce all witnesses named in the FIR. Giving up two independent witnesses did not allow other overwhelming and confidence inspiring evidence to be discarded, since the defence was free to examine them or seek their summoning as Court witnesses. Appeal against conviction dismissed. Ref: 2024 YLR 1745; Muhammad Anwar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Postmortem Not Fatal
records.heading: A postmortem delay of 17 to 24 hours is not fatal absent deliberate delay
records.text: A delay of 17 to 24 hours in conducting postmortem examinations was not fatal where the investigating officer promptly sent the dead and injured to hospital, so there was no deliberate delay. Belated autopsy attributable to hospital practice gave no benefit to the accused. Ref: 2024 YLR 1745; Muhammad Anwar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Complainant at Scene Proved
records.heading: The complainant's presence at the scene was proved by a valid reason and firm testimony
records.text: The complainant gave a valid reason for being with the deceased and remained firm and consistent in lengthy cross-examination. Her not being injured did not shake her presence in view of the background enmity described. Her testimony and that of the injured witness proved guilt beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 YLR 1745; Muhammad Anwar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inconsequential Weapon Recovery: No Mitigation
records.heading: Weapon recovery not matching the empties is no ground for a lesser punishment
records.text: Recovery of Kalashnikovs that did not match the crime empties was no ground for lesser punishment, as the accused were arrested after long periods and could have handed over different weapons. Non-recovery from other accused who absconded for 9 months to 3 years was immaterial where the ocular account was confidence inspiring. Ref: 2024 YLR 1745; Muhammad Anwar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording Statements of Injured Witnesses
records.heading: A two day delay in recording injured witnesses' statements was not consequential
records.text: A delay of two days in recording s. 161 CrPC statements of injured witnesses was not consequential, as the male members of the complainant party were dead or hospitalised. The medical officer found no fabrication and the medico-legal reports were not challenged, so the injuries were taken as sustained in the occurrence. Ref: 2024 YLR 1745; Muhammad Anwar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light Not Proved
records.heading: Failure to prove a source of light in a night occurrence made the case doubtful
records.text: In a night occurrence at about 7.30 pm, no witness stated that any light source was lit at the scene. The complainant's later claim of cricket bulbs was contradicted by his admission that no match was on and by the site plans, and the investigating officer had to arrange light herself. Absence of a proved light source made the prosecution case doubtful. Ref: 2024 YLR 1686; Rashid v. State.
records.title: Rashid v. State

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Cannot Hear Civil Suits
records.heading: Family Courts cannot adjudicate civil disputes outside Part I of the Schedule
records.text: A District Judge has no authority under ss. 12 or 15 of the Punjab Civil Courts Ordinance 1962 to entrust civil claims to a court beyond its jurisdiction, and Family Courts cannot adjudicate civil disputes other than those in Part I of the Schedule to the Family Courts Act 1964. Revision allowed and the District Judge directed to transfer the cases to a competent Civil Judge. Ref: 2024 CLC 1331; Aun Akhter and another v. Ahmad Abdul Rehman and others (Civil Revision No. 54194 of 2023).
records.title: Aun Akhter and another v. Ahmad Abdul Rehman and others (Civil Revision No. 54194 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Joinder of Charges: s. 234 CrPC Directory
records.heading: Joinder of charges under section 234 CrPC is directory and cannot be claimed as of right
records.text: Joinder of charges under s. 234 CrPC is procedural and directory, and cannot be claimed as of right by the accused or the prosecution. The accused must show prejudice or illegality, such as double jeopardy, from separate trials. Where the cases had different complainants and witnesses, refusal of joinder was upheld and the petition dismissed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1289; Mst. Saira Fatima v. The State and 3 others (Crl. Misc. No. 31686 of 2023).
records.title: Mst. Saira Fatima v. The State and 3 others (Crl. Misc. No. 31686 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit on Cheque: Burden of Proof on Plaintiff
records.heading: A plaintiff suing on a cheque must state the particulars of the underlying agreement
records.text: In a suit for recovery on a cheque under O. XXXVII CPC, the plaintiff did not state in the plaint or in his statement the date, time and place of the alleged lease agreement on which the claimed amount rested. Appeal accepted, the decree set aside and the suit dismissed. Ref: 2024 YLR 1810; Muhammad Asghar v. Sikandar Mehmood Dai (R.F.A. No. 207 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Asghar v. Sikandar Mehmood Dai (R.F.A. No. 207 of 2018)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mubarik Ahmad Sani: Contested Paragraphs Expunged
records.heading: The Supreme Court expunged the contested paragraphs from its Mubarik Ahmad Sani judgments
records.text: The Supreme Court allowed the applications of the Punjab Government and the Federation for correction and, in a short order, expunged the contested paragraphs from its judgments of 6 February and 24 July 2024. The report records submissions by religious scholars and party representatives during the hearing. Ref: The State through Prosecutor General Punjab v. Mubarik Ahmad Sani and another (Crl.M.A.1113/2024, decided 22.08.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: The State through Prosecutor General Punjab v. Mubarik Ahmad Sani and another (Crl.M.A.1113/2024, decided 22.08.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal under Order XLI Rule 27 needs a valid reason or sufficient cause
records.text: Additional evidence in appeal is allowed only where the trial court improperly refused admissible evidence, or the appellate court requires the document or witness to pronounce judgment, or for any other substantial cause. The application to place a 2004 notification on record disclosed no valid reason or sufficient cause and was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 563; Iqbal Hussain etc. v. Government of the Punjab etc. (R.F.A. No. 10887 of 2021, decided on 19.3.2024); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan; Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Iqbal Hussain etc. v. Government of the Punjab etc. (R.F.A. No. 10887 of 2021, decided on 19.3.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Fraud Not Substantiated
records.heading: An application under section 12(2) CPC fails if fraud allegations are not substantiated
records.text: An application under s. 12(2) CPC alleging fraud and misrepresentation failed because the applicants did not substantiate the allegations or rebut the documentary and oral evidence on which the courts found Respondent No. 1 to be the lawful wife and her son born of the marriage. Concurrent findings stood and the applications were dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 584; Muhammad Siddique v. Rabia Rafique etc. (C.M. No. 7-C of 2023/BWP, decided on 5.4.2024); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Siddique v. Rabia Rafique etc. (C.M. No. 7-C of 2023/BWP, decided on 5.4.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Visitation Rights of Non-Custodial Parent
records.heading: A non-custodial parent has a right of access supported by a proper visitation schedule
records.text: A non-custodial parent has a right of access to the minor, and a properly framed visitation schedule is needed for effective participation in upbringing and to prevent emotional deprivation. Under s. 25 of the Guardian and Wards Act 1890, the petition was partly allowed and the visitation schedule amended. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 601, 2025 CLC 960; Fayyaz-ul-Hassan Anwar v. Mst. Shehla Khalid etc. (W.P. No. 46618 of 2021, heard on 21.3.2024); Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Fayyaz-ul-Hassan Anwar v. Mst. Shehla Khalid etc. (W.P. No. 46618 of 2021, heard on 21.3.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 22-A and 22-B CrPC: FIR Application Dismissed
records.heading: A Justice of Peace may refuse to direct registration where material facts were concealed
records.text: The Justice of Peace rightly refused to direct registration of a case where the petitioner concealed material facts, the police found no supporting evidence and the cited eyewitness was on judicial remand on the date of occurrence. Petition dismissed, with liberty to file a private complaint. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 607; Ghulam Sarwar v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace etc. (W.P. No. 39257 of 2021, heard on 16.11.2022); Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Ghulam Sarwar v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace etc. (W.P. No. 39257 of 2021, heard on 16.11.2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift by Attorney Requires Express Permission
records.heading: An attorney cannot gift the principal's property to himself without the principal's express permission
records.text: An attorney cannot transfer the principal's property to himself or his kith and kin without specific permission of the principal, and a gift through an attorney attracts strict proof. The petitioners failed to plead and prove the power of attorney, the offer, acceptance and delivery of possession, and the principal's express permission. Civil revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 618, 2025 MLD 286; Rab Nawaz deceased son of Abdul Haq through his Legal Heirs etc. v. Mst. Samra Andleeb (C.R. No. 44182 of 2024, decided on 12.7.2024); Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Rab Nawaz deceased son of Abdul Haq through his Legal Heirs etc. v. Mst. Samra Andleeb (C.R. No. 44182 of 2024, decided on 12.7.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Justice of Peace: Registration of Case
records.heading: No authority may inquire into the correctness of information before the SHO records it
records.text: No authority is vested in an officer in charge of a police station or anyone else to inquire into the correctness of information conveyed to the SHO for recording. Petition allowed and the SHO directed to implement the Justice of Peace order of 06.10.2015 and act strictly in accordance with law. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 216; Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl. P. No. 99-K of 2018, decided on 2.4.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh and others (Crl. P. No. 99-K of 2018, decided on 2.4.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Upheld, Sentence Reduced
records.heading: Related eyewitnesses corroborated by medico-legal evidence proved the charge, but long death cell custody reduced the sentence
records.text: Unshaken testimony of two related eyewitnesses, corroborated by medico-legal evidence, recovery of four empties and blood stains and a positive expert report, proved the charge under ss. 302/324/34 PPC, with no inordinate delay in the FIR. Taking mitigating circumstances into account, including long custody in the death cell, the sentence was reduced and s. 382-B CrPC benefit extended. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 225; Khalid v. State through PG Sindh (Crl. P. No. 668 of 2019, heard on 21.5.2024); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: Khalid v. State through PG Sindh (Crl. P. No. 668 of 2019, heard on 21.5.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Immediate Statement of Injured
records.heading: A woman's immediate statement to those who responded to her cries supported conviction
records.text: The injured woman, who had been stabbed in her house, told witnesses who responded to her cries about the churri blows by the convict, and was taken promptly to hospital. A claim by PW-8 to have seen the stabbing was a dishonest improvement. No illegality was found in the appellate judgment, so the petitions were dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 230; Muhammad Saeed and another v. State and others (Crl. P. Nos. 968 and 891 of 2017, heard on 20.5.2024); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: Muhammad Saeed and another v. State and others (Crl. P. Nos. 968 and 891 of 2017, heard on 20.5.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Supplementary Statement: Arrest and Remand Directions
records.heading: A supplementary statement without a disclosed source is not per se admissible evidence
records.text: A supplementary statement naming an accused without disclosing the source of information is not per se admissible evidence. The investigating officer must first collect incriminating material before arrest, and remand requests must carry the prosecutor's opinion on sufficiency of material. Directions issued to police, prosecutors and magistrates to protect liberty. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 964, 2024 MLD 1693; Mst. Najma Bibi v. S.H.O., etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 27821-H of 2024).
records.title: Mst. Najma Bibi v. S.H.O., etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 27821-H of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 397 CrPC: Concurrent Running of Life Sentences
records.heading: Section 397 CrPC allows life sentences from two trials to run concurrently
records.text: Section 397 CrPC, read with s. 497, empowers the court to direct that sentences of a convict in two different trials run concurrently, unless a superior appellate court has consciously denied that benefit. The petitioner's life sentences in two murder cases were directed to run concurrently with benefit of s. 382-B CrPC. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 973; Sher Afzal v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 729-M of 2024, heard on 29.5.2024); Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Sher Afzal v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 729-M of 2024, heard on 29.5.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Prolonged Death Cell Detention
records.heading: Prolonged death cell detention beyond the convict's control is a ground in his favour
records.text: Detention up to or beyond a life term, including 24 years in a death cell in inhuman conditions, was treated as a ground in favour of the convict under s. 302(b) PPC. The delay was due to the system and beyond his control, so he could not be penalised for the act of the Court or the Executive. Ref: Ghulam Shabbir v. The State & another (Crl.R.P.103/2017, decided 27.08.2024); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Ghulam Shabbir v. The State & another (Crl.R.P.103/2017, decided 27.08.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Arrest in One Case Deemed Arrest in All
records.heading: An accused arrested in one case is presumed arrested in all cases requiring arrest
records.text: To stop successive arrests in different cases after bail, an accused arrested in one case is presumed arrested in all cases where arrest was required. If arrest was not made earlier, the investigating officer must seek permission from the Area Magistrate or Court with the prosecutor's opinion, and approval must be by reasoned order. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 976, 2024 PCrLJ 1669; Shahida Bibi v. Inspector General of Police, Punjab etc..
records.title: Shahida Bibi v. Inspector General of Police, Punjab etc.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Civil Burden of Proof: Preponderance and Art. 117
records.heading: Civil issues are decided on preponderance and the person asserting a fact must prove it
records.text: Civil issues are decided on preponderance of evidence, and burden of proof matters only where evidence is evenly balanced. Under Art. 117 QSO the person asserting a fact must prove it. The High Court was held to have rightly exercised its s. 115 CPC jurisdiction in setting aside the first appellate judgment and upholding the trial court. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1271; Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux and others (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Nazeeran and others v. Ali Bux and others (Civil Appeal No. 81-K of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Power of Attorney: Presumption under Art. 95 QSO
records.heading: A consulate attested and registered power of attorney carries a presumption under Article 95 QSO
records.text: The party alleging that a power of attorney was fraudulent bears the burden of proving the fraud. A power of attorney attested by the Consulate General of Pakistan in Malaysia and registered in Pakistan attracts the presumption of execution and authenticity under Art. 95 QSO, and nothing showed forgery. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1233; Mst. Iqbal Bibi and others v. Kareem Hussain Shah and others (Civil Appeal No.1229 of 201).
records.title: Mst. Iqbal Bibi and others v. Kareem Hussain Shah and others (Civil Appeal No.1229 of 201)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documents Cannot Be Exhibited Through Counsel's Statement
records.heading: Disputed documents cannot be tendered through counsel's statement as it denies cross-examination
records.text: Disputed documents cannot be tendered in evidence through the statement of counsel, because this deprives the opposing party of the right to test authenticity by cross-examination. Documents must be produced in evidence by the party itself, with opportunity to the other side to cross-examine. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 715, 2022 YLR 1634; Mst. Akhtar Sultana v. Major Retd. Muzaffar Khan Malik.
records.title: Mst. Akhtar Sultana v. Major Retd. Muzaffar Khan Malik

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Honour Killing: Compromise Does Not Warrant Bail
records.heading: Compounding by all legal heirs does not entitle an honour killing accused to bail
records.text: An offence in the name or on the pretext of honour falls outside qatl-i-amd as defined in s. 302(c) PPC and is treated as fasad-fil-arz under s. 299(ee) PPC. Under ss. 345(2-A) and 345(7) CrPC and s. 311 PPC, compounding by all legal heirs did not entitle the accused to bail. Bail refused. Ref: 2024 LHC 3700; Bilal Sikandar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.47663/24, decided 21.08.2024); Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Bilal Sikandar v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.47663/24, decided 21.08.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension as Vested Right, Not Charity
records.heading: Pension is a vested right and not charity from the employer
records.text: Pensionary benefits are a vested right and not charity, alms or donation by the employer. The Supreme Court set aside the Sindh High Court order for not reflecting the correct exposition of law and disposed of the matter on assurance that the petitioner would be paid pension within three weeks after adjustment of 811 earned leaves. Ref: Muhammad Yousaf v. Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary, Government of Sindh & others (C.P.L.A.982-K/2023, decided 12.06.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Syed Hassan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary, Government of Sindh & others (C.P.L.A.982-K/2023, decided 12.06.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody: Stepmother and Working Mother
records.heading: A stepmother is not presumed a substitute for the mother and a working mother is not disqualified
records.text: Unless proved by cogent evidence, a stepmother cannot be presumed a substitute for the real mother in upbringing a minor. A mother cannot be disqualified from custody because she works, as welfare of the minor remains the primary consideration. A minor is not always the best judge of where welfare lies. Ref: 2024 CLC 1520; Dr. Muhammad Asif Mirani v. ADJ Layyah, etc..
records.title: Dr. Muhammad Asif Mirani v. ADJ Layyah, etc.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody Distinguished from Guardianship
records.heading: Custody concerns upbringing, guardianship concerns care, and both remain subject to the minor's welfare
records.text: Under the Guardian and Wards Act 1890, custody involves the right to upbringing of a minor, while guardianship concerns taking care of the minor even without control over the child. The father is natural guardian and legally bound to maintain the minor, but this duty is not a decisive factor for custody, which remains subordinate to welfare of the minor. Ref: 2024 CLC 1520; Dr. Muhammad Asif Mirani v. ADJ Layyah, etc..
records.title: Dr. Muhammad Asif Mirani v. ADJ Layyah, etc.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1(3) CPC: Fresh Suit After Withdrawal
records.heading: Whether a fresh suit after unconditional withdrawal is barred by Order XXIII Rule 1(3) CPC
records.text: The judgment considers whether a second suit pending when the first was unconditionally withdrawn is barred by O. XXIII R. 1(3) CPC, and whether its institution was a ploy to defeat the object of the provision. It reviews O. II Rr. 1 to 3 and notes that trial courts can curb non-disclosure of an earlier suit. Ref: 2024 CLC 1468; Muhammad Zulfiqar Ali v. Rashid Mehmood Sidhu (F.A.O No. 72708 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Zulfiqar Ali v. Rashid Mehmood Sidhu (F.A.O No. 72708 of 2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Cancellation (S. 39) Distinguished from Declaration (S. 42)
records.heading: Section 39 applies where the instrument is void or voidable, while section 42 seeks a declaration
records.text: Section 39 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 presupposes that the instrument is void or voidable qua the plaintiff, while s. 42 lets a person entitled to a character or right to property seek a declaration against denial of it. Where the plaintiffs challenged the validity of the deeds, the suit fell under s. 39. Ref: 2024 CLC 1415; Abdul Ghafoor etc. v. Babar Sultan Jadoon etc. (RFA 71-21).
records.title: Abdul Ghafoor etc. v. Babar Sultan Jadoon etc. (RFA 71-21)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Power of Attorney: Scope of S. 202 Contract Act
records.heading: A power of attorney is strictly construed and an agent needs specific permission to deal for himself
records.text: A power of attorney must be strictly construed according to its recitals, and the principal may revoke it at any time, with termination of agency governed by s. 201 of the Contract Act 1872. An agent dealing for himself or his kith and kin must obtain the principal's specific permission, and s. 202 is an exception to these general rules. Ref: 2024 CLC 1415; Abdul Ghafoor etc. v. Babar Sultan Jadoon etc. (RFA 71-21).
records.title: Abdul Ghafoor etc. v. Babar Sultan Jadoon etc. (RFA 71-21)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Revenue Decision No Bar to Civil Suit; Gift Proof
records.heading: A revenue decision does not bar a civil suit alleging fraud, and a gift needs detailed proof
records.text: A decision on the revenue side does not bar a subsequent civil suit, particularly where fraud is alleged, because revenue proceedings are summary and their jurisdiction over fraud is barred. The gift defence also lacked detail, as neither the time of offer and acceptance was pleaded nor any witness produced. Ref: 2024 CLC 1451; Muhammad Rashid etc. v. Muhammad Ismail (Civil Revision 1090-09).
records.title: Muhammad Rashid etc. v. Muhammad Ismail (Civil Revision 1090-09)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Miscellaneous Application Decided Before Appeal
records.heading: A pending miscellaneous application must be decided before the appeal by a separate judgment
