records.text: A pending miscellaneous application, such as one for additional evidence under O. XLI R. 27 CPC, must be decided first and the appeal then decided by a separate judgment. Deciding both together would give a premium to dismissing the application. The matter was remanded to the appellate court. Ref: 2024 CLC 1538; Mst. Ghulam Fatima etc. v. Pahar Khan etc. (CR 194-12).
records.title: Mst. Ghulam Fatima etc. v. Pahar Khan etc. (CR 194-12)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 78 QSO: Documents Through Counsel's Statement
records.heading: A document not proved under Article 78 QSO is inadmissible and counsel's statement cannot substitute
records.text: Article 78 QSO prescribes the mode of proof of execution of documents, and a document brought on record without complying with it is inadmissible. Disputed documents cannot be tendered through the statement of counsel, as this denies the opposing party cross-examination. The exhibit and undertaking were stray papers in law. Ref: 2024 CLC 1503; Khawaja Javed Mehmood v. PSIC Rawalpindi etc. (Civil Revision-33-22).
records.title: Khawaja Javed Mehmood v. PSIC Rawalpindi etc. (Civil Revision-33-22)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Extension of Time for Balance Sale Consideration
records.heading: Courts cannot extend time for the balance sale consideration contrary to the agreement
records.text: Courts cannot extend the time for depositing the balance sale consideration contrary to the agreement, as that rewrites the contract. A buyer must show he was ready, able and willing to pay, or that he offered payment or prepared a pay order or deposited the amount in court. An exception may arise where the balance is a small portion of the price. Ref: Abdil Ali v. A.D.J. Gojra, etc. (C.P.L.A.2293-L/2016, decided 02.09.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Abdil Ali v. A.D.J. Gojra, etc. (C.P.L.A.2293-L/2016, decided 02.09.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NAB Amendments Restored in Intra-Court Appeals
records.heading: The Supreme Court restored the NAB amendments in intra-court appeals
records.text: A five member bench of the Supreme Court unanimously allowed the intra-court appeals and restored the NAB amendments, holding that the earlier three member bench judgment did not prove them to be contrary to the Constitution. The Court stressed caution by the judiciary and legislature in respecting each other's domains. Ref: Islamic Republic of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice, Govt. of Pakistan, Islamabad v. Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and another (I.C.A.2/2023); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Athar Minallah; Justice Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Islamic Republic of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice, Govt. of Pakistan, Islamabad v. Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi and another (I.C.A.2/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Female Accused Attributed Lalkara
records.heading: Attributing a joint lalkara to a female relative made false implication possible, so bail was allowed
records.text: Mere heinousness of the offence is no ground to refuse bail, and a person's liberty cannot be curtailed on bald allegations. Attributing a joint lalkara to a female relative of the co-accused made false implication a possibility, and vicarious liability is for the trial court, so the case called for further inquiry. Bail allowed. Ref: 2024 LHC 3790; Bilqious Bibi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.5564/24, decided 02.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Bilqious Bibi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.5564/24, decided 02.05.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Sale of Drone and Co-Accused's Confession
records.heading: Sale of a drone is not prohibited, and a co-accused's confession cannot be used against another
records.text: Sale of a drone is not prohibited in Pakistan, so a person cannot be made an accused because a co-accused used it to transport narcotics. The extra-judicial confession of a co-accused cannot be used against another accused. Bail granted. Ref: 2024 LHC 3779; Salman Hamid v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.17244/24, decided 02.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Salman Hamid v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.17244/24, decided 02.05.2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Age: Birth Certificate and Ossification Test
records.heading: An ossification test is unnecessary to determine age where a birth certificate is available
records.text: Where a birth certificate is available, an ossification test under s. 8 of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018 is not necessary to determine age. Ref: 2024 LHC 3798; Imran Haider v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 83203/23, decided 22.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Imran Haider v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 83203/23, decided 22.05.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Infirmities in Inquest Report
records.heading: Inquest report infirmities and a missing constable cast doubt on prompt FIR registration
records.text: The inquest report under Rule 35 of Chapter 25 of the Police Rules 1934 shows how investigation proceeded on the first day and tests the claim of prompt FIR registration. Here the constable carrying the complaint was not produced, and the evidence indicated the FIR was registered after the postmortem, allowing eyewitnesses to adjust their statements. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421, PLJ 2024 CrC 857; Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Eyewitness: Testimony Must Be Scrutinised
records.heading: An injured eyewitness's testimony must still be tested on the principles of appraisal
records.text: Receipt of grievous hurt by an eyewitness supports his presence but is not conclusive proof of the truth of his deposition. His testimony must still be tested on the principles of appraisal of evidence. The saying that an injured witness seldom lies is an overstatement where there is more than one assailant. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421, PLJ 2024 CrC 857; Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Two Possible Interpretations: Benefit to Accused
records.heading: Where two interpretations of a fact are possible, the one favouring the accused is adopted
records.text: It is a well entrenched principle of appraisal of evidence that where two interpretations of the same fact are possible, the one favouring the accused is to be adopted. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421, PLJ 2024 CrC 857; Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording s. 161 CrPC Statement of Eyewitness
records.heading: A two or three day delay in recording an eyewitness's section 161 statement is fatal without explanation
records.text: A delay even of two or three days in recording the s. 161 CrPC statement of an eyewitness of a homicide is always considered fatal. Without a legally admissible explanation, the deposition of such witness is to be excluded from consideration. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421, PLJ 2024 CrC 857; Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blackening: Firearm Discharge Distance
records.heading: Blackening is found only if a firearm is discharged from within three feet
records.text: Blackening is found if a firearm is discharged from a distance of not more than three feet. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421, PLJ 2024 CrC 857; Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Evidentiary Value of Site Plan
records.heading: A site plan is not substantive evidence but may show distances and positions of eyewitnesses
records.text: A site plan is not substantive evidence, but it can be used to judge the distance between assailant and victim and the location of eyewitnesses, if proved at trial to have been prepared on the pointation of the narrators of the ocular account. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421, PLJ 2024 CrC 857; Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Atif Naveed and another v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 827 and 698 of 2022 and Murder Reference No. 41 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recalling Witness Not to Fill Lacuna
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC cannot be used to fill lacunae or give a second chance
records.text: Section 540 CrPC empowers the court to summon or recall a witness essential for just decision, but it cannot be used to fill lacunae or give a party a second chance, including a fresh forensic report. The order allowing the prosecution's applications for re-examination was set aside and the applications dismissed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1401; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 352 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 352 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F CrPC: Procedure for Prosecution Evidence
records.heading: Procedure for prosecution evidence under section 265-F CrPC where the accused does not plead guilty
records.text: Under s. 265-F CrPC, if the accused does not plead guilty, the court hears the complainant, takes the evidence produced in support of the prosecution and summons persons named by the complainant as acquainted with the facts. Examination of the accused follows examination of the witnesses. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1443; Mst. Haseena Mai v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 336 of 2023).
records.title: Mst. Haseena Mai v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 336 of 2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Expired Pesticides as Substandard Pesticides
records.heading: Expired pesticides are substandard pesticides under section 3(rr) of the Ordinance
records.text: The Ordinance and the Punjab Agriculture Pesticides Rules 2018 do not define expired pesticide, but expired pesticides fall within part (a) of the definition of substandard in s. 3(rr) of the Ordinance. Section 21(2)(b) therefore applies when a person sells expired pesticides. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1495; Muhammad Farman v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 72710/22).
records.title: Muhammad Farman v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 72710/22)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Inducted by Deceased Father: Payment to Heir
records.heading: A tenant inducted by the deceased father continues as tenant of the heir and must pay him rent
records.text: A tenant inducted by the respondent's deceased father continues as tenant of the legal heir, to whom the premises devolved. A tenant who disputes the relationship, and shows no bona fides by approaching the Rent Tribunal or filing an interpleader suit, must pay rent to that heir, as once a tenant is always a tenant. Ref: 2024 YLR 1981; Sohail Niaz Khan v. Bilal Rizwan etc. (Writ.79017/23).
records.title: Sohail Niaz Khan v. Bilal Rizwan etc. (Writ.79017/23)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Witness Disbelieved in Earlier Trial
records.heading: A witness disbelieved in an earlier trial is not necessarily untruthful in a later trial
records.text: A witness who missed or exaggerated a fact in an earlier trial cannot be termed untruthful in a later trial if his testimony is straightforward and natural. Otherwise a witness disbelieved once could never be relied upon and later accused would get a clean chit. Competency of witnesses is governed by Art. 3 QSO. Ref: 2024 YLR 2000; Ihsan Ullah Munshi etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 53656/19).
records.title: Ihsan Ullah Munshi etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 53656/19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence as Corroborative Evidence
records.heading: Abscondence of 13 or 14 years is corroborative evidence but not a sole ground for conviction
records.text: Abscondence of the accused for about 13 or 14 years is a relevant fact under Art. 21 QSO and is corroborative evidence, though not a sole ground for conviction. The trial court rightly sentenced both appellants to life imprisonment under s. 302(b) PPC, their joint role of firing being a mitigating factor. Ref: 2024 YLR 2000; Ihsan Ullah Munshi etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 53656/19).
records.title: Ihsan Ullah Munshi etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 53656/19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inquest Report Omitting Eyewitnesses and Accused
records.heading: An inquest report omitting the complainant, eyewitnesses and accused suggests an unseen occurrence
records.text: The inquest report under Chapter 25 Rule 35 of the Police Rules 1934 guards against later fabrication. Where it omitted the names of the complainant, the eyewitnesses and the accused, with no explanation, an inference arose that the occurrence was unseen and the FIR was lodged after deliberation and preparation of witnesses. Ref: 2024 YLR 2123, PLJ 2024 CrC 791; Ghaffar Abbas @ Ghaffar Ahmed etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal-435-22).
records.title: Ghaffar Abbas @ Ghaffar Ahmed etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal-435-22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery Despite Negative Report; Motive
records.heading: Recovery despite a negative report is inconsequential and chance witnesses failed to prove presence
records.text: Previous enmity as motive cuts both ways. Recovery of pistols on the accused's pointing out, in the presence of a negative report, is inconsequential and draws an adverse inference. The chance witnesses failed to establish their presence at the time and place of occurrence. Ref: 2024 YLR 2123, PLJ 2024 CrC 791; Ghaffar Abbas @ Ghaffar Ahmed etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal-435-22).
records.title: Ghaffar Abbas @ Ghaffar Ahmed etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal-435-22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Art. 46(1) QSO Conditions
records.heading: A dying declaration not meeting Article 46(1) QSO conditions is at most a section 161 statement
records.text: If the conditions for recording a dying declaration under Art. 46(1) QSO and Rule 25.21 of Chapter XXV of the Police Rules 1934 are not met, it can at most be treated as a s. 161 CrPC statement, and a conviction cannot be based on it. Ref: 2024 YLR 2222; Ghulam Abbas Agha v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 78701/19).
records.title: Ghulam Abbas Agha v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 78701/19)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Possession of One Co-Sharer
records.heading: Possession of one co-sharer is possession on behalf of all co-sharers until partition
records.text: Possession of one co-sharer is considered possession on behalf of all co-sharers. A co-sharer in possession even of a fractional share has a right, title and interest in every part of the joint land until it is partitioned by metes and bounds in accordance with law. Ref: 2024 YLR 2130; Mst. Sara Akhtar, etc. v. Mehmood Khan, etc. (Civil Revision No.1376 of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Sara Akhtar, etc. v. Mehmood Khan, etc. (Civil Revision No.1376 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 4 CPC: Particulars of Fraud
records.heading: Order VI Rule 4 CPC requires particulars of fraud and vague allegations are insufficient
records.text: Order VI Rule 4 CPC requires particulars of fraud with dates and items to be pleaded, and general or vague allegations, however strong, are insufficient. The plaint alleging a fraudulently prepared oral gift memorandum gave no particulars and the initial burden was not discharged. Appeal allowed, High Court judgment set aside and suit dismissed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1649, PLJ 2024 SC 702; Aamir Afzal and another v. S. Akmal (deceased) through his L.Rs and others (C.A.648/2022).
records.title: Aamir Afzal and another v. S. Akmal (deceased) through his L.Rs and others (C.A.648/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revisional Jurisdiction of High Court under s. 115 CPC
records.heading: The High Court should not disturb concurrent findings in revision absent gross misreading of evidence
records.text: The judgment sets out the principles and scope of revisional jurisdiction under s. 115 CPC. A High Court should not interfere with concurrent findings merely because reappraisal of evidence might suggest another view, unless there is gross misreading of evidence or material evidence was ignored. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1649, PLJ 2024 SC 702; Aamir Afzal and another v. S. Akmal (deceased) through his L.Rs and others (C.A.648/2022).
records.title: Aamir Afzal and another v. S. Akmal (deceased) through his L.Rs and others (C.A.648/2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Proof of Oral Agreement to Sell
records.heading: An oral agreement to sell must be pleaded in detail and proved by strong independent evidence
records.text: An oral agreement is valid and enforceable but must be proved by the clearest and most satisfactory evidence. A party seeking specific performance on an oral agreement to sell immovable property must plead its terms in detail with particulars such as date and time and prove mutual consensus through strong and independent evidence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1709; Hafiz Qari Abdul Fateh v. Miss Urooj Fatima & others (C.P.L.A.174-K/2022).
records.title: Hafiz Qari Abdul Fateh v. Miss Urooj Fatima & others (C.P.L.A.174-K/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: No Evidence on Unpleaded Facts
records.heading: No evidence can be considered on a plea of fact not raised in the pleadings
records.text: No amount of evidence can be considered on a plea of fact that was not raised in the pleadings, whether the plaint or the written statement. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1709; Hafiz Qari Abdul Fateh v. Miss Urooj Fatima & others (C.P.L.A.174-K/2022).
records.title: Hafiz Qari Abdul Fateh v. Miss Urooj Fatima & others (C.P.L.A.174-K/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed FIR and Unnatural Conduct of Witnesses
records.heading: A delayed FIR and unnatural conduct of witnesses left the prosecution case doubtful
records.text: The FIR was not registered promptly and the matter was reported belatedly after deliberation and consultation, so false involvement of the accused could not be ruled out. The complainant and the eye-witness did not take the injured to hospital and their conduct was unnatural, so their presence at the scene was not established. Prosecution case held doubtful. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1608; Abid Hussain v. The State (Crl.A.46-L/2020).
records.title: Abid Hussain v. The State (Crl.A.46-L/2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Failure to Prove Motive: Effect
records.heading: Failure to prove motive does not harm a prosecution case proved by reliable evidence
records.text: Mere failure to prove the alleged motive has no adverse effect on the prosecution case if the prosecution has proved its case by reliable evidence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1608; Abid Hussain v. The State (Crl.A.46-L/2020).
records.title: Abid Hussain v. The State (Crl.A.46-L/2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Testimony of Witnesses Related to Deceased
records.heading: Close relationship with the deceased is not a criterion for believing or disbelieving a witness
records.text: Close relationship of a witness with the deceased is not a criterion for believing or disbelieving the evidence of that witness. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1608; Abid Hussain v. The State (Crl.A.46-L/2020).
records.title: Abid Hussain v. The State (Crl.A.46-L/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Frivolous Litigation: Imposition of Costs
records.heading: Frivolous and vexatious litigation is discouraged and costs may be imposed under the Supreme Court Rules
records.text: Frivolous and vexatious litigation must be rooted out and discouraged, and costs may be imposed under the Supreme Court Rules for that purpose. In a partition suit where the petitioner objected to the auction report and the High Court set aside the appellate order, the petition was found frivolous, interference was declined and costs were imposed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1714, PLJ 2025 SC 132; Asma Haleem v. Abdul Haseeb Chaudhry and others (C.P.L.A.3300/2024).
records.title: Asma Haleem v. Abdul Haseeb Chaudhry and others (C.P.L.A.3300/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Cheque Dishonour s. 489-F PPC
records.heading: Whether a cheque was issued for an obligation is for the Trial Court; pre-arrest bail refused
records.text: Whether the cheque was issued in fulfilment of an obligation under s. 489-F PPC is for the Trial Court to decide after evidence. The plea that the cheque was stolen failed because the FIR lodged by the accused's relative was found false after investigation, and no mala fide was shown. Pre-arrest bail refused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1719, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 70; Azhar Pervaiz Bukhari v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.619-L/2024).
records.title: Azhar Pervaiz Bukhari v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.619-L/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Extraordinary Relief and Mala Fide
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is extraordinary relief needing reasonable grounds for further inquiry and proof of mala fide
records.text: Bail before arrest is an extraordinary relief and cannot be granted unless the applicant satisfies s. 497(2) CrPC and shows reasonable grounds for further inquiry. It can be granted only if the accused establishes mala fide on the part of the complainant or the police. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1719; Azhar Pervaiz Bukhari v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.619-L/2024).
records.title: Azhar Pervaiz Bukhari v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.619-L/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Evidence Not Put to Accused
records.heading: Prosecution evidence not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used against him
records.text: A piece of prosecution evidence not specifically put to the accused in his statement under s. 342 CrPC cannot be used against him. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1622; Syed Fida Hussain Shah v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A.134/2024).
records.title: Syed Fida Hussain Shah v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A.134/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Statement of Accused: Inculpatory and Exculpatory Parts
records.heading: An accused's statement is accepted or rejected as a whole, not in part
records.text: Where the prosecution evidence is disbelieved, the statement of an accused is to be accepted or rejected as a whole. It is not permissible to accept the inculpatory part and reject the exculpatory part. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1622; Syed Fida Hussain Shah v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A.134/2024).
records.title: Syed Fida Hussain Shah v. The State through Advocate General, Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A.134/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Counter Versions: Bail as Rule
records.heading: Where versions of one incident conflict, bail is the rule on further inquiry
records.text: Where the complainant's FIR version and the opposite party's version arise from the same incident, bail is granted as a rule on the ground of further inquiry, since the correct version and the aggressor are to be determined after evidence at trial. Refusal of bail in such cases is an exception. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1605; Khizar Hayat v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.1345-L/2023).
records.title: Khizar Hayat v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.1345-L/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained FIR Delay and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Unexplained FIR delay and acquittal of a co-accused with the same role support benefit of doubt
records.text: The FIR was lodged over two hours after the stated time of occurrence without explanation, and the body was taken to hospital late, indicating consultation and deliberation, so false involvement could not be ruled out. Co-accused attributed the same joint injuries had been acquitted. A single doubt suffices to give benefit of doubt to an accused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1731; Muhammad Nawaz v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.522-L/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.522-L/2018)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Complainant's Appeal Against Acquittal Without Special Leave
records.heading: A complainant cannot appeal to the High Court against acquittal without special leave
records.text: In a complaint case, an appeal by the complainant against an acquittal by a court subordinate to the High Court was incompetent before the High Court without grant of special leave to appeal. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1731; Muhammad Nawaz v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.522-L/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.522-L/2018)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Waiver and Compounding of Qisas by Wali
records.heading: Only an adult sane Wali may waive or compound the right of Qisas under sections 309 and 310 PPC
records.text: Under s. 309 PPC only an adult sane Wali may at any time waive the right of Qisas without compensation. Under s. 310 PPC the Wali may compound the right of Qisas on accepting badal-i-sulh. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1731; Muhammad Nawaz v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.522-L/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.522-L/2018)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Writ Jurisdiction Against Family Court Orders
records.heading: The High Court should not interfere in writ with Family Court orders unless contrary to law or perverse
records.text: The Family Courts Act created a special forum with simplified procedure and exclusive jurisdiction under s. 55, limiting family litigation to a single appeal. A High Court should not interfere under Art. 199 unless the Family Court acted contrary to law or its findings are perverse and non-interference would cause grave miscarriage of justice. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1642; Muhammad Shamim v. Mst. Asma Begum and others (C.P.L.A.263-K/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Shamim v. Mst. Asma Begum and others (C.P.L.A.263-K/2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Unregistered General Power of Attorney: Proof
records.heading: An unregistered general power of attorney must be proved under Article 79 QSO and carries no presumption
records.text: An unregistered general power of attorney was not proved under Art. 79 QSO as the attesting witnesses, notary and attorneys were not produced, and no presumption of correctness attaches under s. 49 of the Registration Act, 1908 or Art. 95 QSO. Immovable property cannot be transferred on the basis of an unregistered attorney, and the burden lay on its beneficiary. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1683; Syed Pervaiz Hussain and another v. Zikr-ur-Rehman and others (C.P.L.A.520-K/2024).
records.title: Syed Pervaiz Hussain and another v. Zikr-ur-Rehman and others (C.P.L.A.520-K/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Chain of Circumstances
records.heading: In circumstantial evidence cases a missing link in the chain benefits the accused
records.text: Where the case rests on circumstantial evidence, utmost care is required. Every circumstance must link with the others in a continuous chain, and if any link is missing the benefit goes to the accused. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1782, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 345; Rehmat-ullah v. The State (Crl.A.23-Q/2020).
records.title: Rehmat-ullah v. The State (Crl.A.23-Q/2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence in Unwitnessed Incident
records.heading: Medical evidence cannot sustain a conviction in an unwitnessed incident where eyewitness evidence is unreliable
records.text: Medical evidence by its nature cannot identify the culprit in an unwitnessed incident. Where the eyewitness account is unreliable, a conviction cannot stand on medical evidence alone. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1741; Muhammad Jahangir Muhammad Lateef v. The State (Jail Petition No.514/2016).
records.title: Muhammad Jahangir Muhammad Lateef v. The State (Jail Petition No.514/2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Witness
records.heading: Dishonest improvements by a witness deprive his evidence of significance
records.text: Where a witness makes dishonest improvements in his statement, his evidence loses its significance in the eyes of the law. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1741; Muhammad Jahangir Muhammad Lateef v. The State (Jail Petition No.514/2016).
records.title: Muhammad Jahangir Muhammad Lateef v. The State (Jail Petition No.514/2016)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Justice Delayed is Justice Denied: Timely Judgments
records.heading: Judgments must be written and delivered within a reasonable time after the hearing
records.text: Law and good practice require that judgments be written soon after the hearing, and delivery within a reasonable time is an indispensable part of dispensing justice. The post also compiles relying on PLD 2018 SC 296 (indefinitely pending criminal trials) and 2015 SCMR 15 (justice hurried is justice buried). Ref: 2024 SCMR 1656.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Vendee of Co-Sharer: Rights in Joint Khata
records.heading: The vendee of a co-sharer holds the vendor's rights in the joint khata to the area purchased
records.text: The vendee of a co-sharer steps into the shoes of the vendor with the same rights, no more and no less. Until partition, he holds ownership rights in the joint property to the extent of the area purchased, provided it does not exceed the vendor's share. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1791; Zafar Iqbal and others v. Muhammad Rafiq and others (Civil Appeal No.477-L of 2011).
records.title: Zafar Iqbal and others v. Muhammad Rafiq and others (Civil Appeal No.477-L of 2011)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Contradicting Ocular Account
records.heading: Lunar shaped injuries and a long wait contradicted the witnesses' account and made their presence doubtful
records.text: The postmortem report and doctor's statement showed the injured lay at the scene for a long time and that the injuries were lunar shaped, contradicting the witnesses' account of dagger blows. Related witnesses' testimony is not to be disregarded but needs greater scrutiny. Their conduct was unnatural and their presence doubtful. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1773, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 64.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Complainant and Eye-Witness
records.heading: Witnesses who made no attempt to avert an attack by a lone accused had doubtful presence
records.text: The complainant and eye-witness were 20 paces away and outnumbered a lone accused, yet made no attempt to avert the attack or catch him. Their conduct was unnatural, their presence at the scene was doubtful and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1773, 2024 SCMR 1608.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Disclosure Leading to Recovery
records.heading: Article 40 QSO requires a written disclosure before witnesses, so the dagger recovery was immaterial
records.text: Art. 40 QSO applies only where an accused in police custody conveys information leading to discovery of a new fact, and such information should be in writing before witnesses. The IO did not record the disclosure, so recovery of the dagger was immaterial. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1773, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 64.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Duty of Court to Examine Limitation
records.heading: The court has an inherent duty to examine limitation whether or not it is raised
records.text: Under s. 3 of the Limitation Act, 1908 it is the inherent duty of the court to examine the question of limitation, whether or not it is raised. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1675.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII R. 2 CPC: Summary Suit on Cheque
records.heading: A summary suit on a cheque must be supported by the relevant instruments and agreement
records.text: O. XXXVII R. 2 CPC allows summary suits on bills of exchange, hundies or promissory notes. A cheque is a negotiable instrument, and a summary suit must be supported by the relevant instruments and the parties' agreement. The respondent had exhibited only three documents and could not produce the agreement relied on. Ref: 2024 LHC 3895; Muhammad Waseem v. Maple Leaf Cement Factory (R.F.A.20-24), decided 09.09.2024; Justice Jawad Hassan; Justice Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Muhammad Waseem v. Maple Leaf Cement Factory (R.F.A.20-24), decided 09.09.2024

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats Case: Clarification of Short Order
records.heading: The majority clarified that the short order on reserved seats contains no ambiguity
records.text: On applications by the Election Commission and PTI, the eight-judge majority clarified that the 12 July short order contains no ambiguity, that PTI was and remains a political party, and that the Commission must comply promptly. A seat is deemed that of the party whose certificate was filed, and failure to comply carries constitutional and legal consequences. Ref: Sunni Ittehad Council through its Chairman, Faisalabad and another v. Election Commission of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others (C.A.333/2024), decided 14.09.2024; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Sunni Ittehad Council through its Chairman, Faisalabad and another v. Election Commission of Pakistan through its Secretary, Islamabad and others (C.A.333/2024), decided 14.09.2024

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Party Declining to Enter Witness Box
records.heading: A party able to testify who stays out of the witness box invites an adverse inference
records.text: It is a bad practice for a party able to give personal evidence to stay out of the witness box. Appearing without sufficient cause amounts to withholding evidence and the court may draw an inference against her. Compelling her attendance through a witness summons at the plaintiffs' instance would be objectionable and obstruct fair trial. Ref: Muhammad Ayaz and others v. Mst. Saima Saeed and others (C.P.L.A.47/2024), decided 11.09.2024; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Muhammad Ayaz and others v. Mst. Saima Saeed and others (C.P.L.A.47/2024), decided 11.09.2024

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Review Under S. 8 Punjab Board of Revenue Act
records.heading: Review under section 8 of the Punjab Board of Revenue Act is restricted to prescribed grounds
records.text: The scope of review under s. 8 of the Punjab Board of Revenue Act, 1957 is restricted to the grounds prescribed by the legislature. The High Court dismissed the Art. 199 petition holding review an adequate remedy, without adverting to the grounds the petitioners had taken. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC 612; Muhammad Safeer and others v. Muhammad Azam and others (C.P. No. 888 of 2024), decided 12.06.2024; Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Muhammad Safeer and others v. Muhammad Azam and others (C.P. No. 888 of 2024), decided 12.06.2024

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Liability of Surety in Family Execution
records.heading: A surety in family execution is liable only to the extent clearly undertaken
records.text: A surety's liability is co-extensive with that of the judgment debtor but the surety bond must be strictly construed and he is liable only to the extent clearly undertaken. The petitioner stood surety for Rs. 400,000 only and had paid it, so the appellate order was set aside and the executing court's order restored. Petition accepted. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 683, 2024 CLC 1744; Masood ul Hassan v. ADJ etc (WP 5215-22).
records.title: Masood ul Hassan v. ADJ etc (WP 5215-22)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance Decree and Mutation
records.heading: A specific performance decree must be executed under Order XXI Rule 32, not implemented by mutation
records.text: A decree for specific performance does not itself transfer title and cannot be implemented directly in the revenue record through mutation. The decree holder must execute it under O. XXI R. 32 CPC so that the sale deed is executed and possession delivered, after which revenue authorities must give effect to it. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 698, 2024 CLC 1910; Razia Begum and 5 others v. Member (Judicial-III) B.O.R., and 12 others (W.P. No. 13531 of 2018), decided 27.06.2024; Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Razia Begum and 5 others v. Member (Judicial-III) B.O.R., and 12 others (W.P. No. 13531 of 2018), decided 27.06.2024

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Defective DNA Sampling and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: No fingerprints and defective DNA sampling gave the accused benefit of doubt
records.text: In an unwitnessed double murder, no effort was made to lift fingerprints and the DNA sampling was defective, so the conviction under s. 302(b) PPC could not stand. Appeal allowed, the accused acquitted on benefit of doubt and the death sentence not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1024; Abdul Hakeem and another v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 835 & M.R No. 44 of 2022), heard 20.03.2024; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz; Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan.
records.title: Abdul Hakeem and another v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 835 & M.R No. 44 of 2022), heard 20.03.2024

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Delay in FIR and Medical Evidence in Rape
records.heading: Unexplained FIR delay, unproved place of occurrence and medical evidence not supporting forcible rape led to acquittal
records.text: Unexplained delay in reporting allowed for deliberation and consultation. The prosecution did not prove the place of occurrence, as no petrol pump witness opposite the scene was examined, and the medical evidence did not support forcible rape. Appeal allowed and the accused acquitted on benefit of doubt. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1044; Amjad Ali v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 195087 of 2018), decided 26.04.2024; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Amjad Ali v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 195087 of 2018), decided 26.04.2024

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: 1550 Grams Charas, S. 9(1)3(c) CNSA
records.heading: Charas of 1550 grams does not attract the prohibitory clause, so bail was allowed
records.text: For charas between 1000 and 4999 grams, s. 9(1)3(c) CNSA as amended in 2022 prescribes 9 to 14 years, so the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC is not attracted and the lesser sentence counts for bail. Bail after arrest allowed on surety of Rs. 200,000, with tentative observations only. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 221; Munir Akhtar v. State and another (Crl. Misc No. 2427-B of 2024), decided 15.05.2024; Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.
records.title: Munir Akhtar v. State and another (Crl. Misc No. 2427-B of 2024), decided 15.05.2024

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 512 CrPC: Transposing Evidence in Absence of Accused
records.heading: Evidence recorded in an absconder's absence may be transposed to his trial under section 512 CrPC
records.text: Section 512 CrPC preserves the record of evidence given in the absence of an absconding accused. Witness statements so recorded can be transposed to the trial of an accused later arrested, and documents exhibited in them form part of the statement without re-exhibition. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 240.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Photocopy of PFSA Report Inadmissible
records.heading: A photocopy of a PFSA report is inadmissible without proof for secondary evidence
records.text: A photocopy of the Punjab Forensic Science Agency report is inadmissible under s. 510 CrPC. Under Arts. 75 and 76 QSO a document must be proved by primary evidence, and secondary evidence requires proof of loss with permission, which was not sought. Death sentence not confirmed and the appeal dismissed with modification of sentence. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC Note 227; Ghulam Akbar v. Zulfiqar Ali etc. (Crl. A. No. 516 & M.R No. 47 of 2020), decided 27.02.2024; Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz; Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Ghulam Akbar v. Zulfiqar Ali etc. (Crl. A. No. 516 & M.R No. 47 of 2020), decided 27.02.2024

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 526 CrPC: Transfer of Criminal Case
records.heading: Mere suspicion of bias is no ground for transfer of a criminal case
records.text: Apprehension of bias is no ground for transfer of a criminal case unless supported by material or circumstances, and mere suspicion of bias is insufficient. As the Judge was conducting the trial expeditiously, alleged bias could not be anticipated. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1061; Mehmood v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 10-T of 2024), decided 29.04.2024; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mehmood v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 10-T of 2024), decided 29.04.2024

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Transcripts
records.heading: A CDR without call transcripts or complete audio recordings is not reliable evidence
records.text: Mere production of a CDR without call transcripts or complete audio recordings is not reliable evidence, and it must be shown that the persons at both ends are those whose data is produced. Courts must be cautious as recordings can be edited. The complainant's petition seeking restoration of the death sentence was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 251.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in S. 489-F PPC Offence
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC falls outside the prohibitory clause, so bail is the rule
records.text: The elements of s. 489-F PPC are dishonest issue of a cheque, towards repayment of a loan or fulfilment of an obligation, and dishonour. The offence does not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so bail is the rule, and registration of other cases does not by itself disentitle the accused. Petition admitted. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 264; Ali Anwar Paracha v. State and another (Crl. P.L.A. No. 240 of 2024), decided 04.06.2024; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Ayesha A. Malik; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Ali Anwar Paracha v. State and another (Crl. P.L.A. No. 240 of 2024), decided 04.06.2024

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail to Woman: First Proviso to S. 497 CrPC
records.heading: The first proviso to section 497 CrPC benefits women, with regard to criminal record and conduct
records.text: The first proviso to s. 497 CrPC is beneficial legislation for women, in addition to the usual test of reasonable grounds. The court should also consider the applicant's conduct and whether she has a criminal record or is a habitual offender. Bail petition allowed with directions for expeditious trial. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 279.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence Alone Cannot Sustain Conviction
records.heading: A conviction cannot rest on abscondence alone where eye-witness presence is doubtful
records.text: The presence of both eye-witnesses at the spot was highly doubtful, no motive was proved and the churri was recovered four years later without being sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory. A conviction cannot rest on abscondence alone. Acquittal. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 286; Iftikhar Hussain alias Kharoo v. State (J.P. No. 195 of 2017), decided 08.05.2024; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Iftikhar Hussain alias Kharoo v. State (J.P. No. 195 of 2017), decided 08.05.2024

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Appeal in Family Cases and Writ Jurisdiction
records.heading: Authority on appeals in family cases and the High Court's appellate role in writ
records.text: Authority on the right of appeal in family cases and on whether the High Court can sit as a court of appeal on factual controversies in its constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 902; Syed Raheel Ahmed v. Mst. Syeda Zona Naqvi and others (C.P.L.A.473-K/2024).
records.title: Syed Raheel Ahmed v. Mst. Syeda Zona Naqvi and others (C.P.L.A.473-K/2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Environment, Water Resources and Tree Plantation Order
records.heading: Lahore High Court order on the environment, water resources and tree plantation
records.text: Authority on an order of the Lahore High Court concerning the environment, water resources and tree plantation. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 637; Haroon Farooq v. Government of Punjab etc (Misc. Writ 227807/18).
records.title: Haroon Farooq v. Government of Punjab etc (Misc. Writ 227807/18)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Adjournment Culture: Not a Matter of Right
records.heading: Adjournments cannot be used as a delaying tactic or demanded as of right
records.text: Adjournments have become a plague on the justice system, given the heavy pendency of cases, and rob litigants of speedy justice. They cannot be used as a delaying tactic or demanded as of right. The court referred to the provisions allowing it to proceed to decide the suit where a party defaults. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 887, PLJ 2024 SC 905; Lutfullah Virk v. Muhammad Aslam Sheikh (C.P.L.A.2849-L/2015).
records.title: Lutfullah Virk v. Muhammad Aslam Sheikh (C.P.L.A.2849-L/2015)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: S. 124-A PPC Sedition Struck Down
records.heading: Section 124-A PPC on sedition is void for contravening Articles 19 and 19A
records.text: Section 124-A PPC is inconsistent with and in derogation of the fundamental rights in Arts. 19 and 19A of the Constitution. It was held void as a whole and struck down. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 637; Haroon Farooq v. Federation of Pakistan and others (W.P No.59599 of 2022).
records.title: Haroon Farooq v. Federation of Pakistan and others (W.P No.59599 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Rights of Accused in Custody
records.heading: An arrested person must be told the grounds of arrest and allowed to contact family
records.text: An arrested person must be promptly told the grounds of arrest and details of the accusation, and be allowed to contact his family. The duties of police and Magistrates are explained, and compliance with these safeguards must be documented in the police record. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 626; Muhammad Imran v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc (Criminal Proceedings 8709/24).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc (Criminal Proceedings 8709/24)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Liability of Partners
records.heading: Liability of a partner under section 489-F PPC depends on his role and authority
records.text: Section 489-F PPC applies to natural and juristic persons, and liability of one who issues a cheque for an entity depends on his role and authority, determined with s. 29A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. The complainant alleged no complicity of the two other partners, so the Justice of Peace order was not interfered with. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 561; Muhammad Shahid Faqir v. ASJ/Justice of Peace Bhakkar.
records.title: Muhammad Shahid Faqir v. ASJ/Justice of Peace Bhakkar

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Healing Time of Hymenal Injuries
records.heading: A hymen that healed within five days is inconsistent with forcible rape
records.text: Relying on a cited medical study, mild submucosal hemorrhages disappear within 3 to 4 days while marked ones persist for 11 to 15 days. If rape had been committed forcibly, the hymen should not have healed within five days. The post also lists other causes of rupture of the hymen. Ref: 2024 MLD 1563, PLJ 2024 CrC 1044; Amjad Ali v. State (Crl. A. No. 195087 of 2018); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Amjad Ali v. State (Crl. A. No. 195087 of 2018)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Termination of Widow on Remarriage
records.heading: A widow in contract employment cannot be terminated for remarriage
records.text: A widow given contract employment on her husband's death in service cannot be terminated for contracting a second marriage. Marriage and re-marriage is a religious and fundamental right of a woman, and the Memorandum of 15.12.2015 relied on had already been set aside by the Supreme Court. Intra Court Appeal allowed. Ref: 2024 LHC 3944; Zoya Islam v. Government of Pakistan etc (ICA 77894/22), decided 11.09.2024; Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Zoya Islam v. Government of Pakistan etc (ICA 77894/22), decided 11.09.2024

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Ala Maliks and Adna Maliks: MLR 64
records.heading: Authority on Ala Maliks and Adna Maliks under Martial Law Regulation 64
records.text: Authority on the concept of Ala Maliks and Adna Maliks with reference to Martial Law Regulation 64 and the 1960 Notification. Ref: Muhammad Ramzan and others v. Member (Judicial-II) Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore and others (C.A.936/2012), decided 16.09.2024; Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan and others v. Member (Judicial-II) Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore and others (C.A.936/2012), decided 16.09.2024

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Retrospective Legislation and S. 65B Income Tax Ordinance
records.heading: The first proviso to section 65B(1) of the Income Tax Ordinance is ultra vires Article 25
records.text: The judgment covers legislative powers of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies, principles on retrospective legislation and vested rights. It held the first proviso to s. 65B(1) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 ultra vires Art. 25 of the Constitution. Ref: The Commissioner Inland Revenue v. Mekotex (Pvt) Limited and others (C.P.L.A.824-K/2023), decided 18.09.2024; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: The Commissioner Inland Revenue v. Mekotex (Pvt) Limited and others (C.P.L.A.824-K/2023), decided 18.09.2024

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Criminal Breach of Trust s. 406 PPC
records.heading: Section 406 PPC requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation; pre-arrest bail allowed
records.text: Section 406 PPC requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation, conversion or disposal of the property in violation of law or contract. The ingredients of s. 405 PPC were not made out. Pre-arrest bail allowed. Ref: 2024 MLD 1484; Ghulam Nazik etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 7916-B-23).
records.title: Ghulam Nazik etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 7916-B-23)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Alienation of Property of Mentally Disordered Person
records.heading: A manager of a mentally disordered person's property cannot alienate it without the court's prior permission
records.text: Under ss. 2(m), 29, 32, 36 and 37 of the Mental Health Ordinance, 2001, the manager of the property and person of a mentally disordered person cannot alienate the property without explicit prior permission of the competent court. Ref: 2024 MLD 1455; Azhar Ali v. Khalid Iqbal etc (Civil Revision 18523/22).
records.title: Azhar Ali v. Khalid Iqbal etc (Civil Revision 18523/22)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Deficient Court Fee: O. VII R. 11(c) CPC
records.heading: A litigant who continuously defaults on court fee cannot claim leniency under Order VII Rule 11(c)
records.text: Court fee exists to secure revenue and not to give a litigant a technical weapon, so the law shows flexibility on deficiency. A litigant who continuously defaults in paying the fee or making good the deficiency cannot claim that leniency, and O. VII R. 11(c) CPC applies. Ref: 2024 MLD 1550; Muhammad Azeem v. Noor Muhammad (Civil Revision No.1365-D/2016).
records.title: Muhammad Azeem v. Noor Muhammad (Civil Revision No.1365-D/2016)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: FIA as Investigating Agency Only
records.heading: The FIA is only an investigating agency and does not make its court the only forum
records.text: Under ss. 2(a) and 3 of the FIA Act, 1974 the FIA is only an agency for inquiry into and investigation of scheduled offences. Inclusion of an offence in the Schedule does not make the FIA court the only forum, and the Electricity Utility Court was directed to take cognizance, try the case and decide bail.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Application to Summon Witness Declined
records.heading: A section 540 CrPC application to summon a witness on an already proved fact was rightly rejected
records.text: The complainant sought to summon the deceased's father, who had been abroad, to prove a fact already covered by the complainant's own evidence. He had been available in Pakistan and the complainant did not inform the trial court earlier, so rejection of the s. 540 CrPC application was upheld. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1443; Mst. Haseena Mai v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 336 of 2023).
records.title: Mst. Haseena Mai v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 336 of 2023)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats Case: Detailed Majority Judgment
records.heading: PTI was held a political party entitled to reserved seats despite denial of its symbol
records.text: In the detailed majority judgment, the Peshawar High Court judgment and the Election Commission decision of 1 March were set aside. PTI was held a political party entitled to reserved seats in the National Assembly, as denial of an electoral symbol does not bar a party from contesting. The Commission was to obtain signed statements from the remaining 41 MNAs within 15 days. Ref: Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Unbroken Chain Required
records.heading: A conviction on circumstantial evidence needs an unbroken chain and admissible circumstances
records.text: A conviction on circumstantial evidence requires circumstances so closely interwoven that no conclusion other than guilt is possible. Any break in the chain, or legal inadmissibility of any part, renders the evidence unworthy of credence. The CCTV report could not be used for conviction, relying on PLD 2019 SC 675. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1764; The State v. Abdul Hakeem (Murder Reference 44-22).
records.title: The State v. Abdul Hakeem (Murder Reference 44-22)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Report: Sampling, Custody and Transmission
records.heading: DNA evidence is admissible only if sampling, custody and transmission are satisfactorily proved
records.text: DNA evidence is admissible only if the prosecution satisfactorily proves sampling, packing, safe custody and onward transmission to the forensic agency. Any defect makes even a positive report doubtful and it is discarded. Here the scientist did not identify the police officer receiving the samples, and the nature of the nail swabs was not shown. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1764; The State v. Abdul Hakeem (Murder Reference 44-22).
records.title: The State v. Abdul Hakeem (Murder Reference 44-22)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Anti-Rape Act: Liberal Interpretation and SSIUs
records.heading: The Anti-Rape Act is to be interpreted liberally, and missing special investigation units must be constituted
records.text: The Anti-Rape Act creates a framework including crisis cells, special investigation units, special prosecutors and special courts, and must be interpreted liberally and purposively. Section 9 provides a special investigation procedure under the Anti-Rape (Investigation) Rules 2022. The government was directed to constitute the missing special investigation units and train police immediately. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1783; Sumaira v. The State etc (Criminal Proceedings 75596/22).
records.title: Sumaira v. The State etc (Criminal Proceedings 75596/22)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Legal Heirs for Compromise in Ta'zir Cases
records.heading: A deceased's brother and sister are not legal heirs for compromise where his wife and children survive
records.text: Where the wife, son and daughters of the deceased survive, the brother and sister of the deceased are not legal heirs for the purpose of compromise in a case where punishment was awarded as Ta'zir. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1738, PLJ 2024 CrC 609; Zafar v. The State (Jail Appeal 79782/22).
records.title: Zafar v. The State (Jail Appeal 79782/22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 71 QSO: Oral Evidence as Personal Testimony
records.heading: Oral evidence under Article 71 QSO is personal testimony based on the witness's memory
records.text: The first proviso to Art. 71 QSO shows that the evidence it contemplates is personal testimony based on the memory of the person who saw, heard or perceived the fact. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1691; Muhammad Asif v. The State (Jail Appeal 6732/19).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Jail Appeal 6732/19)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summary Suit Against Legal Heirs of Cheque Maker
records.heading: A summary suit lies only against executants, not legal heirs of a deceased cheque maker
records.text: A cheque ceases to operate as a bill of exchange on the maker's death before presentation. A summary suit lies only against executants, and legal heirs who did not sign are not liable under O. XXXVII Rr. 2 and 3 CPC. The suit was not maintainable and the plaint was ordered returned under O. VII R. 10 CPC. Ref: 2015 CLC 641; Muhammad Abaid Ullah v. Ateeq-ur-Rehman and 8 others (Civil Revision No.288 of 2010).
records.title: Muhammad Abaid Ullah v. Ateeq-ur-Rehman and 8 others (Civil Revision No.288 of 2010)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Cheque Not Presented to Bank
records.heading: A suit under Order XXXVII is not maintainable on a cheque never presented to the bank
records.text: A plaintiff must present the cheque to the bank, and a suit under O. XXXVII CPC is not maintainable on a cheque never presented. In the sixteen suits on sixteen cheques, the first suit was dismissed and the others were held barred by O. II R. 2 CPC, with plaints rejected. Ref: 2016 CLC 937; Zahoor Ahmad v. Master Mushtaq Ahmad (RFAs Nos.84 and 85 to 99 of 2006).
records.title: Zahoor Ahmad v. Master Mushtaq Ahmad (RFAs Nos.84 and 85 to 99 of 2006)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Dishonour Needed for Cause of Action
records.heading: Without dishonour of the cheque no cause of action arises for a summary suit
records.text: Where the cheque was never presented for payment, there was no refusal by the drawer or bank under ss. 72 and 84 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, so no cause of action arose for a suit under O. XXXVII CPC. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2014 CLD 995; Khalifa Azhar Mumtaz v. Ghulam Akbar (R.F.A. No. 39 of 2002).
records.title: Khalifa Azhar Mumtaz v. Ghulam Akbar (R.F.A. No. 39 of 2002)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secondary Evidence: Arts. 76 and 77 QSO
records.heading: Secondary evidence is an exception requiring the prerequisites of Articles 76 and 77 QSO
records.text: Documents must be proved by primary evidence. Secondary evidence under Art. 76 QSO is an exception for genuine need and cannot be allowed routinely without satisfying Arts. 76 and 77. The plaintiff had exhibited photocopies of the agreement, bank documents and cheque, and the judgment lacked the prerequisites. Ref: 2024 MLD 1501; Saad Muhammad Abbasi v. Syed Ejaz Ali (R.F.A. No. 286 of 2022).
records.title: Saad Muhammad Abbasi v. Syed Ejaz Ali (R.F.A. No. 286 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ex Parte Decree: Court Having No Option
records.heading: Even in ex parte proceedings the court must assess the genuineness of the plaintiff's claim
records.text: Even in ex parte proceedings or on a conceding statement, the court must assess the genuineness of the plaintiff's claim. Observing that the court had no option but to decree the suit showed a mechanical approach. The ex parte decree was set aside and the case remanded for decision on merits. Ref: 2024 MLD 1501; Saad Muhammad Abbasi v. Syed Ejaz Ali (R.F.A. No. 286 of 2022).
records.title: Saad Muhammad Abbasi v. Syed Ejaz Ali (R.F.A. No. 286 of 2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partition Suit Without Impleading All Co-Owners
records.heading: A partition suit is not maintainable where all co-owners are not impleaded
records.text: A partition suit under the Punjab Partition of Immovable Property Act, 2012 was not maintainable where all co-owners were not impleaded and no mesne profits were claimed. The petitioner's witnesses gave hearsay evidence and he did not appear in the witness box himself. Concurrent findings were not disturbed under s. 115 CPC. Ref: 2024 MLD 1508; Mubashar Ali Shah v. Muhammad Sharif (Civil Revision No 58370 of 2021).
records.title: Mubashar Ali Shah v. Muhammad Sharif (Civil Revision No 58370 of 2021)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Husband's and Father's Obligation to Maintain
records.heading: A husband must maintain his wife and a father his children under law and Sharia
records.text: A husband has a legal, moral and religious obligation to maintain his wife, and a father to maintain his children until the age fixed by law and Sharia. The Courts below holding the petitioner liable to pay maintenance did not deviate from law and Sharia. Ref: 2024 CLC 1580; Syed Zain Muntazar Mehdi v. Mst. Sara Naqvi etc. (Writ Petition No. 370 of 2024).
records.title: Syed Zain Muntazar Mehdi v. Mst. Sara Naqvi etc. (Writ Petition No. 370 of 2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Proof of Father's Income: Salary Slip
records.heading: A father must produce reliable record of his salary, and a self-produced slip is insufficient
records.text: Even though the mother could not produce the salary slip, the father had to produce reliable record of his salary. His self-produced computer generated slip lacked verification by his employer and could have been supported by bank statements or employer testimony. No ground existed to disturb the concurrent findings of the Courts below. Ref: 2024 CLC 1580; Syed Zain Muntazar Mehdi v. Mst. Sara Naqvi etc. (Writ Petition No. 370 of 2024).
records.title: Syed Zain Muntazar Mehdi v. Mst. Sara Naqvi etc. (Writ Petition No. 370 of 2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Proof of Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Specific performance fails where marginal witnesses were not produced to prove the agreement
records.text: The plaintiffs did not produce the marginal witnesses of the agreement, so execution was not proved under Arts. 17 and 79 QSO. As specific performance is discretionary, unimpeachable evidence was needed, and the relief could not be extended to them. Ref: 2024 MLD 1522; Niamat Bibi v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 1148-13).
records.title: Niamat Bibi v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 1148-13)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement Not Agitated in Executor's Lifetime
records.heading: Failure to raise any claim in the executor's lifetime casts doubt on the agreement to sell
records.text: The plaintiffs raised no claim or legal notice during the five years the executor lived after the alleged agreement to sell. This cast doubt on the veracity and authenticity of the agreement. Ref: 2024 MLD 1522; Niamat Bibi v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 1148-13).
records.title: Niamat Bibi v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 1148-13)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: Mortgagee Bank Not Impleaded
records.heading: Non-impleadment of the mortgagee bank weighed against proof of the agreement to sell
records.text: The plaintiffs pleaded that the property had been redeemed, but their witness admitted not knowing when, and the property was still mortgaged with a bank that was not impleaded. This weighed against proof of the agreement to sell. Ref: 2024 MLD 1522; Niamat Bibi v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 1148-13).
records.title: Niamat Bibi v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 1148-13)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Acquiescence in Suit for Declaration
records.heading: A plaintiff who let the respondent remain in possession and develop the property acquiesced in his title
records.text: By letting the respondent remain in possession, deal with the property as exclusive owner and develop it at his expense, the petitioner acquiesced in his title. She also failed to implead the revenue officials she alleged had colluded in the sale deed. Ref: 2024 CLC 1596; Mst. Sahib Khatoon alias Saban v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 1167).
records.title: Mst. Sahib Khatoon alias Saban v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 1167)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Suit to Cancel Registered Sale Deed: Delay
records.heading: A suit to cancel a registered sale deed filed 21 years later was time barred
records.text: A suit challenging a registered sale deed for fraud, filed about 21 years later, was outside the three years in Art. 91 and the six years in Art. 120 of the Limitation Act, 1908, and no explanation was given. Failure to claim possession while out of possession was also fatal. Ref: 2024 CLC 1596; Mst. Sahib Khatoon alias Saban v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 1167).
records.title: Mst. Sahib Khatoon alias Saban v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 1167)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Inconsistent Findings: Appellate Court Preferred
records.heading: Where trial and appellate findings are inconsistent, the Appellate Court's findings are preferred
records.text: Where the findings of the Trial Court and the Appellate Court are inconsistent, those of the Appellate Court must be preferred absent a cogent reason to the contrary. Ref: 2024 CLC 1596; Mst. Sahib Khatoon alias Saban v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 1167).
records.title: Mst. Sahib Khatoon alias Saban v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 1167)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 129(e) QSO: Presumption of Regularity
records.heading: A registered sale deed attracts a presumption of regularity, and an earlier dismissed suit barred the present one
records.text: The presumption of regularity under Art. 129(e) QSO attaches to a registered sale deed executed and attested by officials, and the plaintiff failed to rebut it or prove the alleged connivance. An earlier suit on the same subject dismissed for non-prosecution barred the present suit under O. II R. 2 and O. IX R. 9(1) CPC. Ref: 2024 CLC 1596; Mst. Sahib Khatoon alias Saban v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 1167).
records.title: Mst. Sahib Khatoon alias Saban v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 1167)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Constitution of Election Tribunals in Punjab
records.heading: Supreme Court set aside the High Court judgment on constituting Election Tribunals in Punjab
records.text: A five-member bench unanimously allowed the Election Commission's appeal and set aside the Lahore High Court single bench judgment of 12 June 2024 on constituting Election Tribunals, which could not be cited as precedent. The Commission's claim was that constituting tribunals is its power and the High Court cannot exercise it. Ref: Election Commission of Pakistan through Chief Election Commissioner, Islamabad v. Salman Akram Raja and others (C.A.842/2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Aqeel Abbasi.
records.title: Election Commission of Pakistan through Chief Election Commissioner, Islamabad v. Salman Akram Raja and others (C.A.842/2024)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Claiming Ownership Must Vacate
records.heading: A tenant asserting ownership must vacate and pursue his declaration suit
records.text: A tenant cannot retain occupancy of rented premises merely because he has filed a suit for declaration. Where the tenant asserts ownership, he must vacate, pursue the suit and regain possession if it is decided in his favour. Ref: Mst. Mussarrat Shaheen v. Mst. Verbeena Khan Afroz and another (C.P.L.A.562-K/2024).
records.title: Mst. Mussarrat Shaheen v. Mst. Verbeena Khan Afroz and another (C.P.L.A.562-K/2024)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Execution of Eviction Order: Merits Not Reopened
records.heading: Execution of an eviction order does not permit re-examination of the merits
records.text: Execution proceedings are confined to implementing judicial decisions and do not permit re-examination of the merits. The Rent Controller was bound to enforce the eviction order, and the High Court was bound by the same constraint, so their decisions were justified. Ref: Muhammad Ain-ul-Haq v. Abdul Ali and another (C.P.L.A.662-K/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Ain-ul-Haq v. Abdul Ali and another (C.P.L.A.662-K/2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Depriving Females of Inheritance: Costs
records.heading: Courts must be vigilant against depriving females of inheritance and impose substantial costs
records.text: Legal heirs of a Muslim become owners on death, yet females are often deprived of inheritance through bogus documents and fraud. Courts must be vigilant, and those who do so must pay substantial costs. A simple matter dragged on for twenty-five years was wrongly remanded on a technicality. Ref: Mst. Aksar Jan and others v. Mst. Shamim Akhtar and others (C.P.L.A.4576/2023), decided 25.09.2024; Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Mst. Aksar Jan and others v. Mst. Shamim Akhtar and others (C.P.L.A.4576/2023), decided 25.09.2024

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: General Attorney Transferring Principal's Property
records.heading: A general attorney needs the principal's special permission to transfer the principal's property
records.text: The holder of a general power of attorney must obtain special permission from the principal when transferring the principal's property, whether in his own favour or in favour of his relatives. Ref: Allah Bakhsh (deced) thr. his LRs. v. Muhammad Riaz and others (C.P.L.A.2565/2023), decided 11.09.2024; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Allah Bakhsh (deced) thr. his LRs. v. Muhammad Riaz and others (C.P.L.A.2565/2023), decided 11.09.2024

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bone Deep Injury: Shajjah-e-Khafifa or Mudihah
records.heading: A bone deep injury without exposure or fracture is shajjah-e-khafifa under section 337-A(i) PPC
records.text: An injury described as bone deep, with no exposure of bone and no fracture, is shajjah-e-khafifa under s. 337-A(i) PPC, not shajjah-e-mudihah under s. 337-A(ii) PPC. Interim bail was confirmed on fresh bail bonds, with the observations declared tentative. Ref: 2019 PCrLJ 1039.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Shajjah-i-Khafifah and Shajjah-i-Mudihah Distinguished
records.heading: A bone deep lacerated wound is shajjah-i-khafifah, a bailable and non-cognizable offence
records.text: Shajjah-i-khafifah is an injury without exposure of bone, while shajjah-i-mudihah exposes bone without fracture. A bone deep lacerated wound falls within s. 337-A(i) PPC, a bailable and non-cognizable offence, so ad interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: PLD 2014 Lah 555.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Depriving Sisters of Inheritance: Costs Imposed
records.heading: Brothers who deprived their sisters of inheritance were refused leave and ordered to pay costs
records.text: Brothers who deprived their sisters of their father's inheritance and pursued a baseless claim for decades were refused leave to appeal. The petition was dismissed with costs of Rs. 500,000 payable to the revenue authority for distribution among those deprived, and revenue authorities were directed to ensure distribution of the estate per Shariah shares. Ref: Bakht Biland Khan & others v. Zahid Khan & others (C.P.L.A.284-P/2012).
records.title: Bakht Biland Khan & others v. Zahid Khan & others (C.P.L.A.284-P/2012)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Challenging Paternity in Succession Proceedings
records.heading: A person claiming to be the deceased's brother cannot challenge paternity without a section 42 declaration suit
records.text: A person claiming to be the brother of the deceased has no legal character to challenge the paternity or legitimacy of the respondents in succession proceedings without first filing a suit under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 for a negative declaration. Ref: Moulvi Abdul Fateh v. Yar Muhammad and others (C.P.L.A.259-Q/2020).
records.title: Moulvi Abdul Fateh v. Yar Muhammad and others (C.P.L.A.259-Q/2020)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Paying Rent Outside Agreed Mode
records.heading: A tenant cannot pay rent through a mode other than the agreed one without written consent
records.text: Where the tenancy agreement requires rent to be deposited by a set date in a specified bank account, the tenant cannot pay through another mode unless the landlord agrees in writing. Courts cannot read an implied term (cash payment) that conflicts with an express clause, and no novation arose as no cash receipts existed. Ref: 2024 LHC 4099; Atif Munawar v. ADJ etc (WP 10130-24, decided 24.09.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Atif Munawar v. ADJ etc (WP 10130-24, decided 24.09.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Depriving Sisters of Inheritance: Costs Imposed
records.heading: Costs of Rs. 500,000 imposed on brothers who deprived their sisters of inheritance
records.text: The Supreme Court dismissed a petition by brothers who deprived their sisters of their father's inheritance, observing that the absence of costs had encouraged untenable litigation. Costs of Rs. 500,000 were imposed and revenue authorities were directed to distribute the estate per Shariah shares and report compliance. Ref: Bakht Biland Khan & others v. Zahid Khan & others (C.P.L.A.284-P/2012).
records.title: Bakht Biland Khan & others v. Zahid Khan & others (C.P.L.A.284-P/2012)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Reconciliation in Khula and Dissolution Cases
records.heading: Lahore High Court judgment on reconciliation in suits for khula and dissolution of marriage
records.text: Detailed Lahore High Court judgment on reconciliation (musalihat) in suits for khula and dissolution of marriage. The post gives no holding beyond the topic. Ref: 2024 CLC 1648; Syed Asif Hussain Shah v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 167-24).
records.title: Syed Asif Hussain Shah v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 167-24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Pleadings may be amended at any stage if the original character and cause of action are unchanged
records.text: Under O. VI R. 17 CPC amendment of pleadings may be allowed at any stage, including appeal or revision, where necessary to decide the real question in controversy, even ignoring delay. It must not alter the fundamental character of the original pleadings or the cause of action; the list of permissible grounds is not exhaustive. Ref: 2024 CLC 1735; Iftikhar Ahmad v. Muhammad Anwar, etc (C.R. No.20763 of 2024).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmad v. Muhammad Anwar, etc (C.R. No.20763 of 2024)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Concise Statement of Arrears; Strained Relations No Ground
records.heading: An ejectment petition for default must state the period and claim, and strained relations are no ground
records.text: Under s. 19(3) of the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009, an ejectment petition alleging default must state the period of default and the claim; omission is fatal. Strained or hostile relations arising from eviction proceedings are not a ground for eviction under s. 15 of the Act. Ref: 2024 CLC 1712; Maqsood Ahmad v. ADJ Faisalabad etc (WP 38539/23).
records.title: Maqsood Ahmad v. ADJ Faisalabad etc (WP 38539/23)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Bona Fide Purchaser: S. 41 TPA, S. 27(b) SRA
records.heading: A bona fide purchaser without notice is protected under section 41 TPA and section 27(b) SRA
records.text: Where the oral sale was not proved, the petitioner as a bona fide purchaser for consideration without notice was protected under s. 41 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and s. 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. The concurrent judgments and decrees were reversed. Ref: 2024 CLC 1764; Muhammad Siddique v. Muhammad Yaqoob etc (Civil Revision 2168-14).
records.title: Muhammad Siddique v. Muhammad Yaqoob etc (Civil Revision 2168-14)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revisional Interference with Concurrent Findings
records.heading: A High Court in revision may interfere with concurrent findings if evidence was misappreciated or overlooked
records.text: A High Court in revisional jurisdiction is reluctant to interfere with concurrent findings, but this is not a rule of thumb. It may interfere where the courts below misinterpreted or misappreciated the material on record or overlooked it. Ref: 2024 YLR 2342; Nargis Bibi v. Muhammad Amin (Civil Revision 2534-14).
records.title: Nargis Bibi v. Muhammad Amin (Civil Revision 2534-14)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Suit for Possession: Proof of Title
records.heading: A plaintiff seeking possession must prove ownership firmly by producing the title document
records.text: A plaintiff seeking possession must establish ownership beyond doubt by producing the title document. The burden of proof must be discharged firmly and not with shaky evidence. Ref: 2024 YLR 2342; Nargis Bibi v. Muhammad Amin (Civil Revision 2534-14).
