records.title: Nargis Bibi v. Muhammad Amin (Civil Revision 2534-14)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Resiling from Recorded Compromise
records.heading: Petitioners cannot resile from a compromise recorded in the order through a section 12(2) CPC application
records.text: Where a compromise was made during arguments and its terms were recorded in the order, the petitioners cannot claim that the matters were part heard or that the order rested on misrepresentation. Such assertions, unsupported by counsel's affidavit, fall outside s. 12(2) CPC and offend Art. 129 QSO. Ref: 2024 YLR 2491; Muhammad Yousaf v. Mst. Bashiran Bibi etc (Civil Petition/CM-U/S 12(2) CPC 22-C-22).
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Mst. Bashiran Bibi etc (Civil Petition/CM-U/S 12(2) CPC 22-C-22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Lost Bullet; No Specific Plea by Accused
records.heading: A passing suggestion of unintentional occurrence is not a specific plea and does not shift the burden
records.text: Authority on a lost bullet in the body and absence of a spent shell where a single 12 bore shot was fired. A passing suggestion of unintentional occurrence in cross-examination and in the s. 342 CrPC statement is not a specific plea and does not shift the burden to the accused; the case is examined on the prosecution evidence. Ref: 2024 YLR 2418; Amir Shahzad v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 38881/19).
records.title: Amir Shahzad v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 38881/19)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Applies to Inheritance Claims
records.heading: The law of limitation applies to inheritance claims and bars those who neglect their rights
records.text: The law of limitation applies to inheritance matters. Founded on the maxim that the law assists the vigilant, it requires claimants to act promptly, and those who neglect their rights for decades forfeit the ability to challenge the matter. Ref: Akhtar Nasir Ahmed v. Province of Punjab through District Collector Gujrat & others (C.P.L.A.1182-L/2018, decided 09.10.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Akhtar Nasir Ahmed v. Province of Punjab through District Collector Gujrat & others (C.P.L.A.1182-L/2018, decided 09.10.2024)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Partition Proceedings and Questions of Title
records.heading: Partition by the Revenue Officer follows sections 135-A and 141, including decision on questions of title
records.text: If co-sharers agree on a private partition scheme, the Revenue Officer affirms it under s. 135-A of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967; otherwise he commences partition and completes it within thirty days. If a question of title arises, he has jurisdiction under s. 141 of the Act to decide it after hearing the parties. Ref: 2024 LHC 4125; Ch. Muhammad Naeem & 3 Others v. Member Judicial BOR Punjab etc (WP 59198/24, decided 30.09.2024); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Ch. Muhammad Naeem & 3 Others v. Member Judicial BOR Punjab etc (WP 59198/24, decided 30.09.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Uterine Brother Inherits Issueless Half-Sister
records.heading: A uterine brother inherits the estate of his issueless half-sister
records.text: Applying Ayat 7 to 11 of Surah al-Nisa, where a male Muslim dies without male issue and his only daughter dies issueless leaving a surviving uterine brother, that brother inherits her estate. The progeny of a predeceased uncle or step father is excluded. Revision allowed and concurrent decisions reversed. Ref: 2024 LHC 4112; Manzoor Ahmad v. Chiragh Khan through LRs (Civil Revision 164468/18, decided 26.09.2024); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Manzoor Ahmad v. Chiragh Khan through LRs (Civil Revision 164468/18, decided 26.09.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Application before Family Court
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC application is maintainable before a Family Court
records.text: An application under s. 12(2) CPC is maintainable before a Family Court despite the exclusion of the Code by s. 17 of the Family Courts Act, 1964. Issues need not always be framed, but where fraud and misrepresentation are alleged and a prima facie case is made out, the application should not be dismissed summarily. Ref: 2024 LHC 4133; Misbah Iftikhar v. Aleesa etc (Writ Petition 1234-23, decided 26.09.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Misbah Iftikhar v. Aleesa etc (Writ Petition 1234-23, decided 26.09.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 17-A(3) Family Courts Act: Compound Annual Increase
records.heading: Annual 10 percent maintenance increase under section 17-A(3) is calculated on a compound basis
records.text: Section 17-A(3) of the Family Courts Act, 1964 is a beneficial provision calling for liberal interpretation. Where the decree omits annual increase or does not specify the basis, the automatic 10 percent yearly increase in maintenance is calculated on a compound basis by the Executing Court. Ref: 2024 LHC 4177; Saba Gull Shahd & 2 Others v. Additional District Judge Faisalabad etc (7340/24, decided 09.10.2024); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Saba Gull Shahd & 2 Others v. Additional District Judge Faisalabad etc (7340/24, decided 09.10.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 63A Review: Majority Judgment Set Aside
records.heading: Article 63A review allowed and the majority judgment of 17 May 2022 set aside
records.text: In the review of the Art. 63A interpretation judgment, the Supreme Court set aside the majority judgment of 17 May 2022 as contrary to the Constitution and to decisions of larger Benches. The opinions of the minority Judges were sustained. Review petition allowed. Ref: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its President v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Interior, Islamabad and others (C.R.P.197/2022, decided 10.10.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan through its President v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Interior, Islamabad and others (C.R.P.197/2022, decided 10.10.2024)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mubarak Ahmed Sani: Correction of Judgment
records.heading: Objected paragraphs deleted on correction; the 6 February order stands only as to bail
records.text: On applications for correction, the Supreme Court deleted the paragraphs objected to by the ulema (paras 7, 42 and 49) from its judgments of 6 February and 24 July 2024. The 6 February order stands only as to bail, the trial court is to proceed unaffected by earlier judgments, and this is the final decision in the matter. Ref: Federation of Pakistan and Prosecutor-General, Punjab v. Mubarak Ahmed Sani and another (Crl. Misc. Application 1113 of 2024 in Crl. Review Petition 2 of 2024).
records.title: Federation of Pakistan and Prosecutor-General, Punjab v. Mubarak Ahmed Sani and another (Crl. Misc. Application 1113 of 2024 in Crl. Review Petition 2 of 2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Insurance Policy Proceeds Form Part of Tarka
records.heading: Insurance nominee is not exclusive owner; proceeds are tarka shared by all legal heirs
records.text: A nomination under s. 72 of the Insurance Ordinance does not operate as a gift or will, and on the nominee's death the amount is payable to the legal heirs of the policy holder. The proceeds are tarka, to be shared by all legal heirs of the deceased policy holder according to their shares under Muslim law. Ref: 2024 LHC 4198; Mst. Razia Begum v. Public at Large etc (Civil Revision 44347/23, decided 01.10.2024); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Mst. Razia Begum v. Public at Large etc (Civil Revision 44347/23, decided 01.10.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Discharged Accused at Later Stage
records.heading: A discharged accused may be summoned later if evidence becomes available against him
records.text: A trial court may summon a discharged accused, even one in column No. 2 of the challan, at a later stage if evidence worth appreciating becomes available against him. Before framing charge the court must weigh the incriminating material under s. 265-D CrPC. The revision was dismissed with that direction. Ref: PLD 2023 Lahore 291; Muhammad Usman Ghani v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 5 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Usman Ghani v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 5 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Production of Further Documents
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC permits production of further documents at any stage
records.text: The complainant's application under s. 540 read with s. 94 CrPC to produce documents should not have been dismissed. The documents were prima facie important, no limitation bars the power, it may be exercised at any stage, and the evidence was incomplete so the accused were not prejudiced. Petition allowed. Ref: 2012 YLR 1192.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F: Cheques Issued as Security; Justice of Peace
records.heading: Justice of Peace rightly declined to order an FIR on cheques given as security
records.text: The Ex-officio Justice of Peace declined under s. 22-A CrPC to direct registration of an FIR on dishonoured cheques given as security. The petitioner's pleadings showed the cheques were received as security under a distribution agreement, and no jurisdictional defect was shown in the order. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2024 CLD 326; Hayat Kimya Pakistan (Private) Limited v. Humair Yusuf and others (Writ Petition 3103 of 2023).
records.title: Hayat Kimya Pakistan (Private) Limited v. Humair Yusuf and others (Writ Petition 3103 of 2023)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Cheque Payable to Cash or Bearer; S. 249-A CrPC
records.heading: A cheque payable to cash or bearer is not invalid under the Negotiable Instruments Act
records.text: A cheque bearing the words pay cash or bearer was not invalid under s. 5 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and the holder is presumed a holder in due course. The accused admitted signature and drawing on his account. The s. 249-A application and revision failed, and quashing under s. 561-A CrPC is for exceptional cases. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2024 CLD 30; Ahmad Faran Sabir v. The State and another.
records.title: Ahmad Faran Sabir v. The State and another

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Consolidation of Suits: Fresh Cross-Examination
records.heading: After consolidation of suits, the adverse party may fresh cross-examine witnesses whose earlier evidence is relied on
records.text: After consolidation of suits and framing of fresh issues, parties may rely on evidence already recorded or produce fresh evidence. If earlier witness statements are relied on, the adverse party has an unalienable right to fresh cross-examination under O. XVIII CPC. Appeal under s. 96 CPC allowed. Ref: 2024 LHC 4319; SAASA Corporation Pvt Limited v. Ms Sefam Pvt Limited (R.F.A.8394/23, decided 30.09.2024); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: SAASA Corporation Pvt Limited v. Ms Sefam Pvt Limited (R.F.A.8394/23, decided 30.09.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Adult Son
records.heading: A father may be bound to maintain an adult son who is completing basic education
records.text: A father's obligation to maintain an adult son who has not completed the basic education needed to earn a livelihood may be considered in an appropriate case. This excludes higher studies and studies abroad. The trial court must weigh the father's means, the son's age, conduct, resources, stage and performance in studies, and the education essential for livelihood. Ref: 2024 LHC 4292; Muhammad Imran v. Samina Kausar etc (WP 62571/24, decided 11.10.2024); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Samina Kausar etc (WP 62571/24, decided 11.10.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Omission of Rule 17-A: Effect on Earlier Deaths
records.heading: Omission of Rule 17-A does not prejudice heirs of civil servants who died before it
records.text: The omission of Rule 17-A of the Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1974 by notification of 24.07.2024 does not prejudice heirs where the civil servant died or was invalidated before that date. Denying them consideration was unreasonable, and the impugned order was not sustainable. Ref: 2024 LHC 4331; Syed Noor ul Hadi Shah v. GOP etc (Writ Petition 13444-24, decided 14.10.2024); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Syed Noor ul Hadi Shah v. GOP etc (Writ Petition 13444-24, decided 14.10.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 85 QSO: Proof of Registered Instrument
records.heading: A registered instrument whose execution is questioned must be proved like a private document
records.text: Under Art. 85 QSO only a registered instrument whose execution is not denied is a public document. Where its execution is questioned, the beneficiary must prove it by the modes for a private document, and mere attestation, exhibition or proof of due execution is not enough. A witness statement is read as a whole. Ref: 2024 MLD 1633; Syed Mubarak Hussain Shah v. Syed Muhammad Ayub Shah (Civil Revision 301-14).
records.title: Syed Mubarak Hussain Shah v. Syed Muhammad Ayub Shah (Civil Revision 301-14)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Void Basic Order: Superstructure Falls
records.heading: When the basic order is without lawful authority, everything built on it falls
records.text: When the basic order is without lawful authority, the entire superstructure raised on it falls to the ground automatically. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1831.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Procedure as Handmaid of Justice
records.heading: Procedure facilitates justice and technical constructions that obstruct it must be avoided
records.text: Procedure is a device to facilitate and not obstruct the administration of justice. Technical constructions of law or rules leaving no room for reasonable elasticity should be guarded against, and any construction reducing a statute to futility must be avoided. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1864; Rao Muhammad Rashid v. Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary and another (C.P.L.A.525-K/2024).
records.title: Rao Muhammad Rashid v. Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary and another (C.P.L.A.525-K/2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance is Equitable and Discretionary
records.heading: Specific performance is equitable and discretionary, not granted merely because it is lawful
records.text: Specific performance is an equitable remedy and the court is not obliged to grant it merely because it is lawful to do so, as s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 expressly provides. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1883.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness
records.heading: Specific performance barred where the vendee failed to prove readiness and willingness
records.text: The vendee failed to prove readiness and willingness to perform his obligations. The agreements imposed no duty on the vendor to obtain a No Demand Certificate, and the vendee's legal notice was unproved for want of a postal receipt. Even assuming breach by the vendor, specific performance was barred. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1883.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Extension of Time for Balance Sale Consideration
records.heading: Courts cannot extend time for depositing balance sale consideration contrary to the agreement
records.text: Courts cannot extend the time for depositing the balance sale consideration contrary to the agreement, as that rewrites it. A buyer must show he was ready, able and willing to pay, or that he offered payment and prepared a pay order or deposited the sum in court. An exception may arise where the balance is a small portion of the price. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1862.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Jactitation of Marriage: Self-Harming Statements
records.heading: In jactitation of marriage, the woman's self-harming statements carry greater evidentiary value
records.text: In a suit for jactitation of marriage where the lady disowns the marriage and says she was terrorised, her statement is critical. Self-harming statements carry greater authenticity and evidentiary value than the petitioner's evidence, which here showed a motive to avoid criminal charges. Ref: 2024 LHC 4377; Muhammad Akhtar Shah v. JFC etc (WP 3022-23, decided 03.10.2024); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Muhammad Akhtar Shah v. JFC etc (WP 3022-23, decided 03.10.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marking Weapon as P: Art. 71 QSO
records.heading: A weapon marked as P must be shown to witnesses and produced for inspection
records.text: Marking a weapon as P on the recovery memo is not a formality. As real evidence it must be shown to witnesses and produced for the court's inspection under the second proviso to Art. 71 QSO. The court should record findings on the weapon's description and calibre before using it as corroboration. Ref: 2024 LHC 4364; Fakhar Iqbal Shah v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 592-23, decided 01.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Fakhar Iqbal Shah v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 592-23, decided 01.10.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Broken Chain of Safe Custody
records.heading: No proof of custody from laboratory to court breaks the chain and leads to acquittal
records.text: Where the entire case property was sent to the laboratory and then produced in court, but no evidence showed how it travelled from the laboratory to court, the chain of safe custody stands broken. This leads to acquittal in a narcotics case. Ref: 2024 LHC 4381; Qamar Masih v. State (Crl. Appeal 203-08, decided 09.10.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Qamar Masih v. State (Crl. Appeal 203-08, decided 09.10.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Supreme Court Authorities
records.heading: Compilation of Supreme Court authorities on the principle of benefit of doubt
records.text: Compilation of Supreme Court authorities on the principle of benefit of doubt in criminal cases. The post lists the citations without stating holdings. Ref: 2024 SCMR 156, 2024 SCMR 1146, 2024 SCMR 1191, 2024 SCMR 1427 and others; Maqsood Alam and another v. The State and others; Abdul Qadeer v. The State; Muhammad Imtiaz Baig and another v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore and another; Muhammad Hassan and another v. The State and others; Khial Muhammad v. The State; Muhammad Ijaz alias Billa and another v. The State and others.
records.title: Maqsood Alam and another v. The State and others; Abdul Qadeer v. The State; Muhammad Imtiaz Baig and another v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore and another; Muhammad Hassan and another v. The State and others; Khial Muhammad v. The State; Muhammad Ijaz alias Billa and another v. The State and others

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unproved Motive and Unexamined Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Given up eye-witnesses and unproved motive meant the prosecution failed to prove its case
records.text: Material eye-witnesses were given up, the alleged motive (the deceased witnessing zina) did not stand to reason on the site plan, and the eye-witnesses behaved unnaturally. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Appeal allowed and the appellant acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1811; Imran @ Mani v. The State (Crl.Sh.A.2/2018).
records.title: Imran @ Mani v. The State (Crl.Sh.A.2/2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Joint Recovery on Pointation Inadmissible
records.heading: A joint recovery on pointation of both accused is inadmissible despite separate memos
records.text: Where weapons were recovered together from the same place, date and time on pointation of both accused, it is a joint recovery of no evidentiary value and inadmissible, even if separate memos were prepared. The weapons also did not match the crime cartridges. Appeal allowed and the appellants acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1839.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Contradictions Cast Doubt on Presence of Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Improved statements and contradictions made the presence of the eye-witnesses doubtful
records.text: The complainant improved his statement, did not explain how he saw each accused's firearm from the rear seat, and contradicted the injured eye-witness on police arrival time. Their presence at the scene was doubtful. Appeal allowed and the appellants acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1839.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive as a Double-Edged Weapon
records.heading: Where blood feud is undisputed, motive is a double-edged weapon and cannot alone convict
records.text: Where blood feud enmity is undisputed, motive may drive one side to commit a crime and may equally induce the other to falsely implicate rivals. Motive is a double-edged weapon, and the appellants could not be held responsible merely because of it. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1839.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Forgery by Public Servant Custodian of Record
records.heading: Forgery by a public servant custodian of record may be proved by documents and transactions
records.text: Where a public servant who is custodian of official record commits forgery or fraud, direct evidence is hard to find. Relevant documents and transactions can be given due weight, and the approach should be inquisitorial and not adversarial. Ref: 2024 LHC 4401; Muhammad Arif Zaman etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 909-12, decided 15.10.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Arif Zaman etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 909-12, decided 15.10.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats: Clarification on Election Amendment Act
records.heading: The Elections (Second Amendment) Act 2024 cannot render the 12 July 2024 decision ineffective
records.text: The eight majority Judges clarified that the Elections (Second Amendment) Act, 2024, including its retrospective application, cannot render the 12 July 2024 decision ineffective. As the detailed judgment had issued, no further clarification was needed and both applications were disposed of. Ref: Clarification (CMA 10247/2024 and CMA 10088/2024 in Civil Appeals 333 and 334 of 2024).
records.title: Clarification (CMA 10247/2024 and CMA 10088/2024 in Civil Appeals 333 and 334 of 2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Quota for Children of Civil Servants Unconstitutional
records.heading: Employment quotas for widows and children of civil servants without open merit are unconstitutional
records.text: Quotas and policies giving employment to the widow or children of civil servants without advertisement or open merit are inconsistent with Arts. 3, 4, 5(2), 25 and 27 of the Constitution. The Prime Minister's package and related provincial rules were declared void, governments were directed to end the policy, and the General Post Office appeal was allowed. Ref: General Post Office, Islamabad and others v. Muhammd Jalal (C.P.L.A.3390/2021, decided 18.10.2024); Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: General Post Office, Islamabad and others v. Muhammd Jalal (C.P.L.A.3390/2021, decided 18.10.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 56 NI Act: Part Payment and O. XXXVII Suit
records.heading: After part payment on a cheque, section 56 NI Act endorsement is needed before presentation
records.text: Where part payment is received against a cheque, s. 56 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 requires endorsement before the cheque is presented. Without it, the cheque cannot be presented nor an O. XXXVII CPC suit filed. The remedy is an ordinary suit, and the plaint should be returned under O. VII R. 10 CPC. Ref: 2024 CLC 1643; Muhammad Afzal v. Binyamben Sajid (R.F.A. 11759 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Afzal v. Binyamben Sajid (R.F.A. 11759 of 2021)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Family Settlement: Principles and Significance
records.heading: Family settlements made in good faith are upheld and bind those who took benefits
records.text: Courts uphold family settlements made in good faith, which must be genuine, bona fide and aim at resolving family disputes by a fair distribution. A party who took material benefits under a settlement is estopped from setting it aside. The judgment surveys Pakistani, Indian and English authority. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1984, PLJ 2024 SC 845; Bashir Ahmed (deceased) through his L.Rs. etc v. Nazir Ahmad etc (C.A.197-L/2019, decided 19.08.2024); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Bashir Ahmed (deceased) through his L.Rs. etc v. Nazir Ahmad etc (C.A.197-L/2019, decided 19.08.2024)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Occupancy Tenant and Proprietary Rights Conferment
records.heading: A tenant recorded before 21.10.1868 and in long possession is an occupancy tenant
records.text: A tenant recorded before 21.10.1868 and in possession about 20 years before the Act is an occupancy tenant, and contrary revenue entries create no right. The revenue hierarchy was directed to apply ss. 5 and 6 of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887 before conferring proprietary rights under the 2012 Act. Ref: 2024 LHC 4411; Abdul Rehman & 16 Others v. Nazir Ahmad etc (Civil Revision 59188/24, decided 30.09.2024); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Abdul Rehman & 16 Others v. Nazir Ahmad etc (Civil Revision 59188/24, decided 30.09.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: USB Containing Raid Video: Copy to Accused
records.heading: A USB with raid video is a document and the accused is entitled to a copy
records.text: A USB is a document, and where the prosecution submits a USB containing a video recording of the raid with the challan report, the accused is entitled to a copy of it. Ref: 2024 LHC 4445; Muhammad Iqbal v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 51928/24, decided 08.10.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 51928/24, decided 08.10.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Strangulation, Throttling, Mugging, Bansdola, Garrotting
records.heading: Medical jurisprudence distinguishes strangulation, throttling, mugging, bansdola and garrotting as forms of neck compression
records.text: Extract on medical jurisprudence distinguishing forms of neck compression. Strangulation is compression of the neck by a force other than hanging; throttling is by fingers and palms; mugging is by foot, knee or elbow; bansdola and garrotting are other described forms. Ref: Javed Abdul Rajjaq Shaikh v. State of Maharashtra (Criminal Appeal 1181 of 2011, decided 06.11.2019).
records.title: Javed Abdul Rajjaq Shaikh v. State of Maharashtra (Criminal Appeal 1181 of 2011, decided 06.11.2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 56 NI Act: Part Payment and O. XXXVII Suit
records.heading: After admitted part payment on a cheque, the payee must file an ordinary suit
records.text: After admitted part payment on a cheque, the payee cannot present it for encashment without the s. 56 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 procedure, nor sue under O. XXXVII CPC. He must file an ordinary suit for the balance. The first appeal was allowed on jurisdiction and the plaint directed to be returned under O. VII R. 10 CPC.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 202 to 204 CrPC: Summoning Accused on Complaint
records.heading: Before summoning an accused on complaint, the court must scrutinise the evidence under section 202 CrPC
records.text: Sections 202 to 204 CrPC require the trial court to scrutinise the evidence supporting allegations before summoning, including the purpose of the complaint and the possibility of harassment or victimisation. The s. 202 inquiry protects persons from frivolous summoning and must be weighed before issuing process. Ref: Muhammad Rajar v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh and others (Criminal Petition 165-K/2022, decided 14.10.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Rajar v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh and others (Criminal Petition 165-K/2022, decided 14.10.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wife Murder: Post-Mortem Delay and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Conviction for throttling a wife upheld; explained post-mortem delay and medical opinion prevailed
records.text: Conviction of the husband under s. 302 IPC for throttling his wife was upheld. The delay in signing the post-mortem report was explained and corroborated by the provisional death certificate, and medical opinion ordinarily prevails over inconsistency with the inquest report. Appeal dismissed. Ref: Javed Abdul Razzaq Shaikh v. The State of Maharashtra (Criminal Appeal No. 1181 of 2011, decided 06.11.2019); Justice K.M. Joseph; Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul.
records.title: Javed Abdul Razzaq Shaikh v. The State of Maharashtra (Criminal Appeal No. 1181 of 2011, decided 06.11.2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Revision for Enhancement: No Conversion of Acquittal
records.heading: Acquittal on a section 302 PPC charge cannot be converted into conviction in revision
records.text: Where the accused was convicted under s. 322 PPC and not under s. 302 PPC, he is deemed acquitted of the s. 302 charge. That acquittal cannot be converted into conviction in revision under s. 439(4)(a) CrPC, so the revision for enhancement was not maintainable and was dismissed. Ref: 2018 PCrLJ Note 79; Ghulam Mustafa v. Naeem Iqbal alias Mehnga and another (Criminal Revision 327 of 2011).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. Naeem Iqbal alias Mehnga and another (Criminal Revision 327 of 2011)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 506 PPC: No Separate First and Second Part
records.heading: The latter part of section 506 PPC is not a separate independent provision
records.text: Sections 506(ii) and 506(B) do not exist in Chapter XXII. The latter part of s. 506 PPC continues the earlier part and is not read separately. The parts differ only in the nature and gravity of the threat and the sentence, and the second part is not an independent provision. Ref: 2024 LHC 4453; Habib ur Rehman v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 56879/B/2024).
records.title: Habib ur Rehman v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 56879/B/2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Photographs and Video Clips as Evidence
records.heading: Photographs and video clips are both documents and material things for admissibility purposes
records.text: Audio or video clips and photographs are both a document and a material thing, the latter to be produced for inspection by the court. The rules on admissibility of documents apply, with the court's discretion under Art. 139 QSO. The judgment also notes that delay in reporting offences touching honour may be explained. Ref: 2024 LHC 4466; Abdul Basit v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 812-22, decided 14.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Abdul Basit v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 812-22, decided 14.10.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 302(a), (b), (c) PPC: Conversion in Revision
records.heading: Converting a finding under section 302(c) PPC to clause (a) or (b) is not enhancement
records.text: Clauses (a), (b) and (c) of s. 302 PPC are distinct offences. Converting a finding of guilt under clause (c) into one under clause (a) or (b) amounts to reversal of a finding, not enhancement of sentence within s. 439(1) CrPC. Ref: PLD 2018 Lah 139.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Ss. 371-A and 371-B PPC: Brothel Cases
records.heading: Sections 371-A and 371-B PPC need an actual sale, purchase or hiring of a woman
records.text: Persons found in sexual intercourse in a brothel are not liable under ss. 371-A or 371-B PPC, which need an actual sale, purchase or hiring of a woman for prostitution. The facts called for further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC, and bail was allowed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1972, PLJ 2024 CrC 1185; Khalida Bibi and another v. The State and others (Crl. Misc. 885-B/2024).
records.title: Khalida Bibi and another v. The State and others (Crl. Misc. 885-B/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Related Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Closely related eye-witnesses claiming to arrive by chance at the occurrence are doubtful
records.text: Closely related eye-witnesses who claimed to reach the scene by chance exactly as the occurrence took place were held to have arrived afterwards, since their story did not appeal to a prudent mind. The first post adds that a motive set up but not proved prejudices the prosecution, not the accused. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1825; State v. Ashfaq Hussain (Murder Reference 51-22).
records.title: State v. Ashfaq Hussain (Murder Reference 51-22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secondary Evidence Without Application
records.heading: A party may lead secondary evidence without a prior application for leave
records.text: A party may lead secondary evidence before the trial court without filing an application for leave. The opposing party may object when it is recorded, and the court may decide the objection at once or record the evidence under objection and decide it in the final judgment. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 695; Bagh Ali v. ADJ Pakpattan etc (Misc. Writ 11458/24).
records.title: Bagh Ali v. ADJ Pakpattan etc (Misc. Writ 11458/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recusal and Transfer: Mere Apprehension of Bias
records.heading: Mere apprehension of bias is no ground for recusal of a Judge or transfer
records.text: Mere apprehension or bias is no ground to seek recusal of a Judge or transfer of a case, except personal interest as mentioned in s. 556 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 684, PLJ 2024 CrC 1061; Mehmood v. The State etc (T.A. (Crl) 10-T-24).
records.title: Mehmood v. The State etc (T.A. (Crl) 10-T-24)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 27(b) SRA: Onus on Subsequent Bona Fide Purchaser
records.heading: A subsequent vendee under section 27(b) SRA bears the initial onus of bona fide purchase
records.text: A subsequent vendee claiming protection under s. 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 bears the initial onus. He must show he paid the price, acted in good faith without dishonest purpose, and took reasonable care to inquire as a prudent purchaser seeking good title. Ref: Faqir Syed Anwar-Ud-Din (deceased) v. Syed Raza Haider & others (C.P.L.A.3210-L/2023, decided 22.04.2024); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Faqir Syed Anwar-Ud-Din (deceased) v. Syed Raza Haider & others (C.P.L.A.3210-L/2023, decided 22.04.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing FIR on Ground of Civil Dispute
records.heading: An FIR cannot be quashed merely because the matter also involves a civil dispute
records.text: An FIR cannot be quashed merely because of a civil dispute, as civil and criminal proceedings may run simultaneously. The duty to register an FIR under s. 154 CrPC is mandatory for cognizable offences, and the ordinary course of trial should not be bypassed by invoking constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore v. Chaudhry Mohammad Khan, etc (C.P.L.A.671-L/2017, decided 27.09.2024); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore v. Chaudhry Mohammad Khan, etc (C.P.L.A.671-L/2017, decided 27.09.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Preliminary Medical Examination in Police Recruitment
records.heading: A preliminary medical examination in police recruitment is an initial screening and creates no vested right
records.text: A medical examination at the time of application is only an initial screening and is not a conclusive declaration of medical fitness under Rule 12.15 or 12.16 of the Police Rules. Vested rights arise only after enrolment, and no claim to recruitment rests on the preliminary medical examination. Ref: Government of the Punjab etc. v. Muhammad Zafar Iqbal (I.C.A. 148/2024).
records.title: Government of the Punjab etc. v. Muhammad Zafar Iqbal (I.C.A. 148/2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Diyat Payable at Rate on Date of Decision
records.heading: Diyat is payable at the rate prevailing in the year the court decides the case
records.text: The amount of diyat or arsh is imposed at the rate prevalent in the fiscal year when the court decides the case, not at the date of occurrence. Ref: 2024 LHC 4501; Shahid Ali Makhi v. State (Jail Appeal 234893/18, decided 01.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Shahid Ali Makhi v. State (Jail Appeal 234893/18, decided 01.10.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Death by Vasovagal Inhibition: S. 316 PPC
records.heading: Death by vasovagal inhibition from blunt trauma is not natural death and falls within section 316 PPC
records.text: Death due to vasovagal inhibition or shock caused by blunt trauma cannot be termed natural death, and the offence falls within s. 316 PPC. Ref: 2024 LHC 4501; Shahid Ali Makhi v. State (Jail Appeal 234893/18, decided 01.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Shahid Ali Makhi v. State (Jail Appeal 234893/18, decided 01.10.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Test Identification Parade as Evidence
records.heading: An identification parade is corroborative only and failure to hold one is not fatal
records.text: An identification parade is a method of proof under s. 22 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 and must be fair and free of collusiveness. It is only corroborative and not mandatory, so failure to hold it is not fatal where the witnesses' identification inspires confidence and is consistent. Ref: Subha Sadiq v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.786-L/2016); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Subha Sadiq v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.786-L/2016)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Lalkara and Common Intention: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Whether a lalkara was commanding and common intention existed is a matter of further inquiry
records.text: The accused was armed with a pistol and fired and raised a lalkara, but did not shoot the deceased despite no hindrance. Whether the lalkara was commanding or proverbial, and common intention and vicarious liability, need further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Bail granted. Ref: 2024 LHC 4579; Zulqarnain v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 43092/24, decided 24.10.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zulqarnain v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 43092/24, decided 24.10.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 9A: Right to Clean Environment
records.heading: Article 9A makes a clean, healthy and sustainable environment a fundamental right
records.text: Art. 9A, inserted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2024, makes a clean, healthy and sustainable environment a fundamental right. The Court stressed preserving forest cover and stopping deforestation, and disposed of the matter on the Provincial Government's statement that it would implement sustainable practices. Ref: Mehar Badshah v. Govt. of K.P. through Chief Secretary K.P, Peshawar and others (C.P.L.A.524-P/2015, decided 24.10.2024); Justice Qazi Faez Isa.
records.title: Mehar Badshah v. Govt. of K.P. through Chief Secretary K.P, Peshawar and others (C.P.L.A.524-P/2015, decided 24.10.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Mere Suit for Possession versus Declaration of Title
records.heading: Where title is disputed or clouded, the plaintiff must sue for declaration of title
records.text: Where the plaintiff is in possession but title is disputed, or the defendant claims title and threatens dispossession, the plaintiff must sue for a declaration of title and injunction. Where title is clouded and he is not in possession, he must sue for declaration, possession and injunction. Ref: Khurshid Ali & others v. Aurangzeb through LRs and others (CA 493 & 494 of 2023, decided 17.10.2024).
records.title: Khurshid Ali & others v. Aurangzeb through LRs and others (CA 493 & 494 of 2023, decided 17.10.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Second Marriage Without Permission: Dissolution of Marriage
records.heading: Second marriage without Arbitration Council permission entitles the wife to dissolution under clause (iia)
records.text: The husband admitted taking an additional wife without Arbitration Council permission under s. 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961. The Court declared the marriage dissolved under clause (iia) of s. 2 of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act 1939 and set aside the Khula and cruelty grounds and the restitution decree. Dower, dowry, maintenance and visitation decrees were upheld. Ref: Dr. Faryal Maqsood and another v. Khurram Shehzad Durrani (C.P. 308-P and 1388 of 2019, decided 23.10.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Dr. Faryal Maqsood and another v. Khurram Shehzad Durrani (C.P. 308-P and 1388 of 2019, decided 23.10.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikah Nama: Presumption of Truth and Construction
records.heading: A Nikah Nama is a public document with a strong presumption of truth
records.text: A Nikah Nama is a public document carrying a strong presumption of truth, and its columns and headings are construed by the intention of the parties. The High Court erred in ordering dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty without recording reasons. Ref: Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019, decided 23.10.2024); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019, decided 23.10.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Constitutional Action against Executive Abuse after 26th Amendment
records.heading: Maintainability of constitutional action against Executive abuse after the 26th Amendment in a transfer matter
records.text: Authority on the maintainability of a constitutional action against abuse of authority by the Executive in the context of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2024, in a service transfer and posting matter. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2024 LHC 4669; Malik Imtiaz Ahmad v. GOP etc (Writ Petition 14268-24, decided 29.10.2024); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Malik Imtiaz Ahmad v. GOP etc (Writ Petition 14268-24, decided 29.10.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Chance Witnesses; Medical Evidence Not Identifying Assailant
records.heading: Related chance witnesses who gave no reason for presence are interested and unreliable
records.text: Close relatives who gave no reason for being with the deceased, and who did not identify the body in the inquest report or at post-mortem, were interested chance witnesses. Medical evidence only supports the prosecution and does not identify the assailant. Benefit of doubt extended and the appellant acquitted. Ref: 2024 LHC 4685; Muhammad Dilshad v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 59174/19, decided 18.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Dilshad v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 59174/19, decided 18.10.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Property: Settlement Authority Functus Officio After PTD
records.heading: After a PTO or PTD is issued, the settlement authority is functus officio and re-allotment is void
records.text: After the auction was confirmed and a PTO or PTD issued to the auction purchaser, the settlement authority became functus officio. Any re-allotment of the property by the Deputy Settlement Commissioner is collusive, illegal, void and coram non judice. The subsequent allottee's appeal was dismissed. Ref: 2024 LHC 4723; Ch. Abdul Saleem v. Mst. Aziz Khatoon (R.S.A. 816178.69-06, decided 01.11.2024); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Ch. Abdul Saleem v. Mst. Aziz Khatoon (R.S.A. 816178.69-06, decided 01.11.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Proof Beyond Reasonable Doubt and Presumption of Innocence
records.heading: The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt and the accused is presumed innocent
records.text: The prosecution bears the burden of proving guilt beyond reasonable doubt and the accused is presumed innocent until then. The accused need not produce evidence, and the presumption of innocence alone warrants acquittal unless the Court is fully convinced of guilt after impartial examination of the evidence. The burden shifts only in cases falling under Art. 121 QSO. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1169, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 299; Imtiaz Latif v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1690-L/2016).
records.title: Imtiaz Latif v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1690-L/2016)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 17 Arbitration Act: Making Award Rule of Court Despite Delay
records.heading: Under section 17 of the Arbitration Act, the court must examine an award despite time bar
records.text: Under s. 17 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, once an award is before the court it must examine it for patent illegality or cause for remittal, even if the application by a party is time barred. The court cannot refuse to make the award a rule of the court solely on limitation. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 727; Sultan Mehmood v. Naeem Ahmad (Civil Revision 931-18).
records.title: Sultan Mehmood v. Naeem Ahmad (Civil Revision 931-18)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Child Marriage Restraint Act: Different Ages by Sex Struck Down
records.heading: A lower marriage age for females in the Child Marriage Restraint Act was struck down
records.text: The words in s. 2(a) of the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 prescribing a different age for females (under sixteen) were held unconstitutional, without lawful authority and struck down. The Government of Punjab was directed to issue a revised version of the Act within fifteen days. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 734, PLD 2025 Lah 1; Azka Wahid v. Province of Punjab & others (W.P. 32798 of 2023).
records.title: Azka Wahid v. Province of Punjab & others (W.P. 32798 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Mutilated Cheque: S. 118 Presumption Retained
records.heading: A mutilated cheque retains the section 118 presumption if key particulars are undamaged
records.text: The mutilated or torn condition of a cheque does not remove the presumption of correctness under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, provided key information such as payee, date, amount and signatures is undamaged. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 749; Liaqat Ali v. Noor Ahmad (Regular First Appeal 338-21).
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. Noor Ahmad (Regular First Appeal 338-21)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 498-A PPC Non-Cognizable: No FIR; S. 22-A
records.heading: Section 498-A PPC is non-cognizable so no FIR can be ordered for it
records.text: Under Schedule II CrPC, s. 498-A PPC is a non-cognizable offence, so an FIR cannot be ordered for it. The Ex-officio Justice of Peace has discretion under s. 22-A(6) CrPC and may refuse a direction to register a case. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 764; Muhammad Ajmal v. JOP etc (Writ Petition 15477-21).
records.title: Muhammad Ajmal v. JOP etc (Writ Petition 15477-21)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody Under CNSA 1997
records.heading: In narcotics cases the prosecution must prove every step of the chain of custody
records.text: In CNSA cases the prosecution must prove every step from recovery, sampling, safe custody to safe transmission to the laboratory, and a missing link benefits the accused. Under rule 4(2) of the 2001 Government Analysts Rules samples must be sent within seventy two hours, and Rule 22.70 Police Rules governs Register No. XIX. Ref: PLJ 2024 SC CrC 295; Asif Ali & another v. The State (Criminal Petition 1602 of 2023).
records.title: Asif Ali & another v. The State (Criminal Petition 1602 of 2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 22 SRA: Discretion in Decreeing Specific Performance
records.heading: Authority on the court's discretion in decreeing specific performance under section 22 SRA
records.text: Authority on the scope of clause III of s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 concerning the court's discretion in decreeing specific performance. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2024 LHC 4786; Nasir Ahmad v. Aman Ullah Khan (Regular First Appeal 267-19, decided 21.10.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Nasir Ahmad v. Aman Ullah Khan (Regular First Appeal 267-19, decided 21.10.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Sale by Attorney to Own Family: Implicit Approval
records.heading: Failure to challenge an agent's sale to his wife for years showed implicit approval
records.text: Where a son sold the principal's property to his wife in 1991 under a 1987 power of attorney, which was cancelled in 2003, and suit was filed in 2014, the general rule that an agent selling to kin needs the principal's permission did not assist the petitioner. Not challenging the transfer in 2003 showed implicit approval. Ref: 2024 LHC 4778; Mst Ayesha v. Mst Shama etc (Civil Revision 1581-19, decided 04.09.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mst Ayesha v. Mst Shama etc (Civil Revision 1581-19, decided 04.09.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Joint Account: Either or Survivor Clause
records.heading: The either or survivor clause is unislamic as to the rights of legal heirs
records.text: The either or survivor clause has been declared unislamic as to the rights of legal heirs. Account opening form stipulations are operating instructions protecting banks that pay in good faith, and the heirs may recover from the surviving holders. The bank has no unfettered power to let the survivor withdraw everything. Ref: 2024 LHC 4839; Mst Kubra Bibi v. Public at Large etc (Civil Revision 350-19, decided 27.09.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mst Kubra Bibi v. Public at Large etc (Civil Revision 350-19, decided 27.09.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Jurisdiction; Delegated Talaq
records.heading: The Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction over dissolution of marriage, including talaq-e-tafweez
records.text: Under s. 5(1) of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 and its Schedule, the Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction over dissolution of marriage, including khula and talaq-e-tafweez, so the Civil Court could not try the suit. A husband who delegates talaq to his wife does not lose his own right to pronounce talaq. Ref: 2024 LHC 4844; Shahzad Akbar v. ADJ etc (WP 13290-24, decided 17.10.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Shahzad Akbar v. ADJ etc (WP 13290-24, decided 17.10.2024)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Decree Never Dies: Limitation for Execution
records.heading: A decree never dies; limitation bars execution but does not extinguish the right
records.text: A decree never dies. Limitation bars enforcement by execution after the prescribed period but does not extinguish the right or title based on the decree. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 698, 2024 CLC 1910; Razia Begum and 5 others v. Member (Judicial-III) B.O.R., and 12 others (W.P. No. 13531 of 2018), decided 27.06.2024; Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Razia Begum and 5 others v. Member (Judicial-III) B.O.R., and 12 others (W.P. No. 13531 of 2018), decided 27.06.2024

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 148 CPC: Time to Deposit Balance Consideration
records.heading: The trial court cannot enlarge under section 148 CPC the time fixed by the decree for deposit
records.text: The trial court cannot enlarge under s. 148 CPC the one month fixed by the decree for depositing the balance consideration. After that period it becomes functus officio, and the plaintiff's remedy is an appeal, in which the appellate court may extend time on justifiable grounds. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 698, 2024 CLC 1910; Razia Begum and 5 others v. Member (Judicial-III) B.O.R., and 12 others (W.P. No. 13531 of 2018), decided 27.06.2024; Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Razia Begum and 5 others v. Member (Judicial-III) B.O.R., and 12 others (W.P. No. 13531 of 2018), decided 27.06.2024

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Custodial Torture, Death and Rape: Exclusive FIA Investigation
records.heading: The FIA has exclusive jurisdiction to investigate custodial torture, death and rape
records.text: Jurisdiction to investigate custodial torture, deaths and rapes lies exclusively with the FIA under the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act, 2022. Police were directed to cease such investigations, and the issue of implementing the Act was directed to be brought to the attention of the Chief Minister and the Federal Minister for Interior. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 789; Mst. Sarriya Bibi v. RPO Sheikhupura etc (WP 61743/23).
records.title: Mst. Sarriya Bibi v. RPO Sheikhupura etc (WP 61743/23)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Heroin Recovered from Co-Accused
records.heading: Post-arrest bail granted where the petitioner was implicated only by a co-accused's inadmissible statement
records.text: The petitioner was implicated only on the co-accused's statement, which is inadmissible, and by sale of a drone to the main accused. The contraband was not consciously in his possession. Post-arrest bail was granted on a bond of Rs. 500,000, with observations declared tentative. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1141; Salman Hamid v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 17244-B of 2024, decided 02.05.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Salman Hamid v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 17244-B of 2024, decided 02.05.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Honour Killing: Compromise Does Not Entitle to Bail
records.heading: Honour killing is excluded from qatl-i-amd and a compromise does not warrant bail
records.text: A murder in the name or on the pretext of honour is excluded from qatl-i-amd under the first proviso to s. 302(c) PPC and is fasad-fil-arz under s. 299(ee) PPC. Under s. 345(7) CrPC no offence is compounded save under s. 311 PPC, so a compromise by all legal heirs does not warrant bail. Bail refused. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1083, 2025 YLR 152; Bilal Sikandar v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 47663/24).
records.title: Bilal Sikandar v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 47663/24)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Widow's Employment Not Terminable on Remarriage
records.heading: A widow's contract employment cannot be terminated on her remarriage
records.text: A widow given contract employment on the death of her civil servant husband cannot be terminated on remarriage. Marriage or remarriage is a religious and fundamental right of a woman, and action contrary to it is illegal and ultra vires. The memorandum of 15.12.2015 relied on had already been set aside by the Supreme Court. Intra Court Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 811, 2025 PLC (C.S.) 422; Zoya Islam v. Government of Pakistan (ICA 77894/22).
records.title: Zoya Islam v. Government of Pakistan (ICA 77894/22)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Party Stealing March on Court's Final Order
records.heading: A party that steals a march on the court's final order is liable to correction
records.text: A party that acts in anticipation of the final order of a court, tries to steal a march over its adversary already before the court, or acts in a manner suggesting a race against the law is liable to correction. The court need only consider the corrective measures needed to uphold the majesty of law. Ref: 2024 CLC 1812; Abdul Sattar v. Muhammad Yaseen (Civil Revision No.2592 of 2014).
records.title: Abdul Sattar v. Muhammad Yaseen (Civil Revision No.2592 of 2014)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documentary Evidence Over Oral Deposition
records.heading: Documentary evidence takes precedence over oral deposition
records.text: It is settled law that documentary evidence takes precedence over oral deposition. Ref: 2024 CLC 1812; Abdul Sattar v. Muhammad Yaseen (Civil Revision No.2592 of 2014).
records.title: Abdul Sattar v. Muhammad Yaseen (Civil Revision No.2592 of 2014)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Transfer of Mortgaged Property to Financial Institution
records.heading: Transfer of mortgaged property to a financial institution does not become void
records.text: Under the Transfer of Property Act, 1877, a transaction regarding mortgaged property in favour of a financial institution does not become void. The institution's mortgage rights remain intact and the transferee remains obliged to pay the mortgage money to the creditor. Ref: 2024 CLC 1812; Abdul Sattar v. Muhammad Yaseen (Civil Revision No.2592 of 2014).
records.title: Abdul Sattar v. Muhammad Yaseen (Civil Revision No.2592 of 2014)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Bona Fide Purchaser versus Lis Pendens
records.heading: Where bona fide purchaser and lis pendens conflict, lis pendens prevails
records.text: Where the principles of bona fide purchaser and lis pendens conflict, lis pendens prevails. Ref: 2024 CLC 1812; Abdul Sattar v. Muhammad Yaseen (Civil Revision No.2592 of 2014).
records.title: Abdul Sattar v. Muhammad Yaseen (Civil Revision No.2592 of 2014)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Techniques for Examination in Chief
records.heading: Guidance on conducting examination in chief of prosecution witnesses
records.text: The court set out guidance on conducting examination in chief of prosecution witnesses, including aims of the exercise, preparation of witnesses, use of signposting and piggybacking, and rules on form and sequence of questions and control of the witness. Ref: 2024 YLR 2546, PLJ 2024 CrC 989; Rao Hamayun Waqas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 10549/21).
records.title: Rao Hamayun Waqas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 10549/21)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Leading Questions: Arts. 136 and 137 QSO
records.heading: Leading questions are barred in examination in chief except as Article 137 QSO permits
records.text: A prosecutor may not ask leading questions in examination in chief (Art. 136), but under Art. 137 they may be asked if the opposite party does not object, or with the court's permission where the matter is introductory, undisputed or already sufficiently proved. The five Ws technique avoids leading questions. The prosecutor need not follow the sequence of s. 161 CrPC statements. Ref: 2024 YLR 2546, PLJ 2024 CrC 989; Rao Hamayun Waqas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 10549/21).
records.title: Rao Hamayun Waqas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 10549/21)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Weak Circumstantial Evidence: Acquittal
records.heading: Weak circumstantial evidence and unproved motive led to acquittal
records.text: Circumstantial evidence is normally weak. Extrajudicial confession lacked credibility, foot tracker evidence did not meet Rule 26, Chapter XXV of the Punjab Police Rules, 1934, safe custody of moulds was unproved, the forensic report was partly negative, last seen evidence was unhelpful and motive was unproved. Appeal accepted and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2024 YLR 2521; Muhammad Nadeem v. State (Crl. Appeal-151-16).
records.title: Muhammad Nadeem v. State (Crl. Appeal-151-16)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Land: Status Changed Only by Custodian
records.heading: Evacuee land status can be changed only by the Custodian of Evacuee Property
records.text: Evacuee land vested in the State on migration of non-Muslims, and its status can only be changed by the Custodian of Evacuee Property in accordance with law. The notification of 10.02.1948 granting such land to the Forest Department was upheld by the Supreme Court. The concurrent decrees of the courts below had no backing in law and were reversed. Ref: 2024 YLR 2722; Province of Punjab v. Mst. Sughran Bibi (Civil Revision.115655/17).
records.title: Province of Punjab v. Mst. Sughran Bibi (Civil Revision.115655/17)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Competent Forum
records.heading: A section 12(2) CPC application lies before the court that passed the final order
records.text: The competent forum to challenge the validity of a judgment, decree or order under s. 12(2) CPC is the court that passed the final order. Ref: 2024 LHC 4961; Ghulam Fareed v. Muhammad Bilal (Civil Revision-574-24, decided 09.10.2024); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Ghulam Fareed v. Muhammad Bilal (Civil Revision-574-24, decided 09.10.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recall of Warrants and Proclamation: S. 75 CrPC
records.heading: A court may recall its warrants and proclamation under section 75 CrPC after surrender
records.text: A warrant issued by a court can be cancelled by the same court under s. 75 CrPC. An order issuing process, warrants or proclamation is not a judgment under s. 369 CrPC and, for valid reasons, can be recalled by the trial court after the accused surrenders. Ref: 2024 LHC 4966; Muhammad Hussain v. The State (Crl. Appeal 69556/24, decided 06.11.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Hussain v. The State (Crl. Appeal 69556/24, decided 06.11.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Proceedings After Remand: O. XLI R. 23 CPC
records.heading: On remand the trial court must follow the remand order and pre-remand evidence is not discarded
records.text: On remand the trial court must proceed in terms of the remand order, and sidetracking it can amount to defiance. O. XLI R. 23 CPC does not discard pre-remand evidence, which remains evidence after remand subject to just exceptions. The case is re-admitted on its original number in the register. Ref: 2024 LHC 4970; Shahid Hussain v. Abdul Jabbar Tassaduq (R.F.A. No. 92515 of 2017).
records.title: Shahid Hussain v. Abdul Jabbar Tassaduq (R.F.A. No. 92515 of 2017)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Internal Auction: S. 10(2) Punjab Partition Act 2012
records.heading: Section 10(2) of the Punjab Partition Act requires all co-owners at the internal auction
records.text: The Punjab Partition of Immoveable Property Act, 2012 is procedural law and each step must be followed. Under s. 10(2) the court must require all co-owners to be present in person or through authorised agents at the internal auction. Where the law requires a thing to be done in a particular manner, it must be done in that manner. Arts. 10-A and 4 of the Constitution were also referred to. Ref: 2024 LHC 4981; Naseem Bibi v. Imran Qayyum (W.P. No.57227 of 2024).
records.title: Naseem Bibi v. Imran Qayyum (W.P. No.57227 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Meaning of Disposal and Disposed Of
records.heading: Meaning of disposal and disposed of explained from dictionary definitions
records.text: Relying on dictionary definitions, the court explained the meanings of disposal and dispose of. A petition disposed of after the petitioner's counsel wished to withdraw it after arguments means that it was terminated, settled and concluded as desired by counsel after arguments and consideration of the merits. Ref: 2024 YLR 2568; Muhammad Saqlain v. The State (Crl. Misc.62426/23).
records.title: Muhammad Saqlain v. The State (Crl. Misc.62426/23)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Deciding Miscellaneous Application Before Main Lis
records.heading: A court must decide miscellaneous applications before deciding the main lis
records.text: A court must decide miscellaneous applications, such as one for comparison of thumb impressions by an expert, before deciding the main lis. Discretion to refer for expert opinion cannot justify leaving the application undecided. O. XIV CPC requires the court first to determine points of dispute and frame issues before evidence is recorded. Ref: 2024 LHC 4895; Muhammad Ismail v. Allah Wasaya (Civil Revision No.893 of 2017).
records.title: Muhammad Ismail v. Allah Wasaya (Civil Revision No.893 of 2017)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIV R. 2 CPC: Preliminary Issue of Law
records.heading: An issue of law is tried first only where deciding it can dispose of the case
records.text: O. XIV R. 2 CPC is mandatory, but an issue of law is tried first only where deciding it can dispose of the case or part of it. Issues of law going to the root of the case and decidable without evidence should be decided first. The trial court has discretion to try the legal issue first or with the factual issues. Ref: 2024 LHC 4854; Manzoor Elahi v. Rehmat Ali (C.R. No.530 of 2023).
records.title: Manzoor Elahi v. Rehmat Ali (C.R. No.530 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Livelihood Abroad: Exemption from Attendance
records.heading: Earning a livelihood abroad is a valid reason to dispense with an accused's attendance
records.text: Earning a livelihood abroad is a valid reason to dispense with the attendance of an accused. Ref: 2024 LHC 4993; Rai Muhammad Aslam v. The State (Crl. Misc.40397/24, decided 28.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Rai Muhammad Aslam v. The State (Crl. Misc.40397/24, decided 28.10.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Conviction and Sentence Distinguished
records.heading: Conviction is a guilty verdict while sentence is the punishment imposed under it
records.text: Conviction is a guilty verdict, while sentence is the imprisonment, probation or fine imposed under that verdict. Conviction is also a major obstacle to an individual's reintegration into society. Ref: 2024 LHC 4993; Rai Muhammad Aslam v. The State (Crl. Misc.40397/24, decided 28.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Rai Muhammad Aslam v. The State (Crl. Misc.40397/24, decided 28.10.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Omission of Rule 17-A: No Retrospective Effect
records.heading: Omission of Rule 17-A has no retrospective effect for children of employees who died earlier
records.text: The Supreme Court judgment in General Post Office, Islamabad v. Muhammad Jalal (Civil Petition No.3390 of 2021) does not give retrospective effect to the omission of Rule 17-A of the Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1974. Rule 17-A ended on 24 July 2024, so children of employees who died or were medically retired before that date remain entitled. Ref: 2024 LHC 5004; Muhammad Zaman v. GOP (WP: 12771-24, decided 07.11.2024); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Muhammad Zaman v. GOP (WP: 12771-24, decided 07.11.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: Proof Through Attesting Witnesses
records.heading: An agreement to sell need not be written, but non-appearance of attesting witnesses defeats proof
records.text: An agreement to sell need not be written or on stamp paper, as even an oral agreement is recognised. Where attesting witnesses do not appear, the contents and existence of the document cannot be proved in terms of Art. 17 read with Art. 79 QSO, which is mandatory. Ref: 2024 MLD 1886; Karam Elahi v. Ahmad Din (Civil Revision No.1432 of 2015).
records.title: Karam Elahi v. Ahmad Din (Civil Revision No.1432 of 2015)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Oral Contract Valid and Enforceable
records.heading: An oral contract is valid and enforceable like a written one
records.text: A contract may be written or oral, and an oral agreement is valid and enforceable like a written one provided it fulfils the requirements of a valid agreement. Ref: 2024 MLD 1886; Karam Elahi v. Ahmad Din (Civil Revision No.1432 of 2015).
records.title: Karam Elahi v. Ahmad Din (Civil Revision No.1432 of 2015)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Fraudulent Evacuee Allotments: Power to Reverse
records.heading: Earlier fraudulent evacuee allotments lack sanctity and may be investigated and reversed
records.text: The Displaced Persons (Land Settlement) Act, 1958 was repealed in 1975 and no new allotments could follow. However, earlier fraudulent allotments lack legal sanctity, and under s. 10 the Chief Settlement Commissioner may investigate and reverse them. When an allotment is reopened, the Settlement Authority can re-examine title from the inception of the claim, relying on 2016 SCMR 222. Ref: 2024 MLD 1995; Raja Abdul Ghafoor v. Province of Punjab (Civil Revision No.991-D of 2014).
records.title: Raja Abdul Ghafoor v. Province of Punjab (Civil Revision No.991-D of 2014)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Void Basic Order Taints Subsequent Transactions
records.heading: A void basic order taints all later orders and transactions built on it
records.text: When a basic order or transaction is void ab initio, the entire series of later orders and transactions and the rights built upon them fall to the ground, unless a statute or legal principle recognises the changed position of the parties. Ref: 2024 MLD 1995; Raja Abdul Ghafoor v. Province of Punjab (Civil Revision No.991-D of 2014).
records.title: Raja Abdul Ghafoor v. Province of Punjab (Civil Revision No.991-D of 2014)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Disposal of Case Property After Acquittal: S. 517 CrPC
records.heading: On acquittal by the High Court, the lower court disposes of case property under section 517 CrPC
records.text: Unless the High Court directs otherwise, on acquittal by the High Court the disposal of case property is regulated by the lower court under s. 517 CrPC, as conclusion of trial includes decision in appeal where no order on property was made. Under s. 520 the High Court may itself act if the trial court fails to. The lower court acts like an executing court under s. 47 CPC. Ref: 2024 MLD 1970, PLJ 2025 CrC Note 216; Muhammad Shamoon v. The State (Crl. Revision 31115/21).
records.title: Muhammad Shamoon v. The State (Crl. Revision 31115/21)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prolonged Death Cell Detention Beyond Life Term
records.heading: Prolonged death cell detention beyond a life term is a distinct punishment
records.text: Detention in prison up to or beyond the period of life imprisonment is a distinct punishment. The petitioner had spent twenty four years in a death cell in inhuman conditions, with delay attributable to the system and beyond his control, and was held to fulfil the criteria laid down by the Court. Prisoners in death cells retain a constitutional right to dignity. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 951; Ghulam Shabbir v. The State (Crl.R.P.103/2017).
records.title: Ghulam Shabbir v. The State (Crl.R.P.103/2017)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Cross-Cases
records.heading: In genuine cross-cases bail is granted as a rule on the ground of further inquiry
records.text: Bail in cross-cases depends on the facts of each case, and a genuine cross-case requires the same incident narrated differently. Where counter versions arise from one incident, bail is granted as a rule on the ground of further inquiry under s. 497 CrPC and refusal is the exception. Where one party gets bail, the other side is treated similarly. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 969; Ahmad Ali v. The State (Crl.P.183-P/2022).
records.title: Ahmad Ali v. The State (Crl.P.183-P/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Calling Opposite Party as Witness; Withholding Evidence
records.heading: A party avoiding the witness box invites an adverse inference, but cannot be compelled by the opponent's summons
records.text: It is a bad practice for a party to avoid the witness box when able to give personal evidence, and failure to appear without cause permits an adverse inference. However, allowing the plaintiffs to compel the defendant's attendance by witness summons is objectionable, as it places examination and cross-examination in the wrong hands. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 976; Muhammad Ayaz v. Mst. Saima Saeed (C.P.L.A. No. 47 of 2024, decided 11.09.2024); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Muhammad Ayaz v. Mst. Saima Saeed (C.P.L.A. No. 47 of 2024, decided 11.09.2024)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Art. 62(1)(f): Lifetime Disqualification Overruled
records.heading: Article 62(1)(f) is not self-executory and lifetime disqualification is overruled
records.text: By six to one, the Supreme Court held that Art. 62(1)(f) is not self-executory and overruled Sami Ullah Baloch v. Abdul Karim Nausherwani (PLD 2018 SC 405). Lifetime disqualification conflicts with fundamental rights, and until legislation is made the provision is read like Art. 62(1)(d), (e) and (g). Yahya Afridi J dissented. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1028; Hamza Rasheed Khan v. Election Appellate Tribunal, Lahore High Court, Lahore (C.A.982/2018); Justice Qazi Faez Isa; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Hamza Rasheed Khan v. Election Appellate Tribunal, Lahore High Court, Lahore (C.A.982/2018)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Property Transactions with Pardanashin or Illiterate Lady
records.heading: The beneficiary of a transaction with an illiterate or pardanashin lady must prove it with high quality evidence
records.text: Old and illiterate ladies receive the same protection as pardanashin ladies. The beneficiary of the transaction must prove with high quality evidence that she understood its nature and consequences, had independent advice, had disinterested witnesses, received the consideration, and had the deed explained in her language. The burden lies on the party relying on the deed. Revision dismissed. Ref: 2024 YLR 2629; Umar Farooq v. Irshad Bibi (Civil Revision No. 13865 of 2024).
records.title: Umar Farooq v. Irshad Bibi (Civil Revision No. 13865 of 2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Against Old Lady: Failure of Proof
records.heading: A mutation against an old lady failed for want of proof by the defendant
records.text: The defendant did not prove when and where the bargain was struck and admitted none was struck. His mother deposed against him. After the lady specifically denied her thumb impression, the defendant made no effort to have it compared, which implied admission. The courts below rightly held the defendant failed to prove his case. Ref: 2024 YLR 2629; Umar Farooq v. Irshad Bibi (Civil Revision No. 13865 of 2024).
records.title: Umar Farooq v. Irshad Bibi (Civil Revision No. 13865 of 2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Limitation and S. 53-A TPA
records.heading: Limitation does not bar specific performance on an Iqrarnama with possession after full payment
records.text: Where the suit rests on an Iqrarnama coupled with delivery of possession after full payment, limitation does not bar it, as the limitation law bars remedy and does not take away an existing right. The right under s. 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 is an existing right that no length of time extinguishes. Non-appearance of the transferors in the witness box also went against them. Ref: 2024 MLD 1810; Muhammad Afzal v. Abdul Hameed (Civil Revision No. 66888 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Afzal v. Abdul Hameed (Civil Revision No. 66888 of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Cannot Fix Exact Location
records.heading: A call data record cannot establish the exact location of the user
records.text: A CDR shows that a SIM received or made a call at a particular time within the range of a cellular tower, which is usually a sizeable area. It cannot establish the exact point where the user was present. A CDR of a witness not registered in his name, without forensically analysed voice record, cannot be a basis for summoning it. Ref: 2024 LHC 5071; Shabbir Hussain v. The State (Crl. Appeal 68635/24, decided 06.11.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Shabbir Hussain v. The State (Crl. Appeal 68635/24, decided 06.11.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Judge's Power to Transfer Criminal Case
records.heading: Five-judge Lahore High Court bench authority on a Sessions Judge's power to transfer a criminal case
records.text: Authority of a five-judge Lahore High Court bench, decided on 13 November 2024, on the powers of a Sessions Judge to transfer a criminal case. The holding is not stated in the post. Ref: Mian Zaheer Abbas Rabbani v. The State (TA (Crl) 10572/2024, decided 13.11.2024).
records.title: Mian Zaheer Abbas Rabbani v. The State (TA (Crl) 10572/2024, decided 13.11.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer Application (Crl) Before Five-Judge Bench
records.heading: Transfer application heard and disposed of by a five-judge bench on 13.11.2024
records.text: Cause list entry showing the transfer application was heard on 13.11.2024 by a bench of the Chief Justice and four named Judges and was disposed of. The reasoning is not shown. Ref: Mian Zaheer Abbas Rabbani v. The State etc. (Transfer Application (Crl) 10572/24, decided 13.11.2024); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi; Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural; Justice Farooq Haider; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mian Zaheer Abbas Rabbani v. The State etc. (Transfer Application (Crl) 10572/24, decided 13.11.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Cases by Sessions Judge: s. 528(1-A) CrPC
records.heading: Section 528(1-A) CrPC empowers a Sessions Judge to transfer cases, including bail applications before trial
records.text: A five-judge bench overruled PLD 2020 Lahore 382. Section 528(1-A) CrPC empowers the Sessions Judge to withdraw and transfer cases and appeals within the sessions division where expedient for the ends of justice, which is a judicial power. A bail application is part of the case, so before trial commences it may be so transferred. Petition disposed of. Ref: 2024 LHC 5077, PLD 2025 Lah 98, PLJ 2025 Lah 271; Mian Zaheer Abbas Rabbani v. The State (Transfer Application (Crl) 10572/24, decided 13.11.2024).
records.title: Mian Zaheer Abbas Rabbani v. The State (Transfer Application (Crl) 10572/24, decided 13.11.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
