records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence, Recovery and Last Seen
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence requires facts clearly proved and inculpatory facts incompatible with innocence
records.text: The court set out the leading rules of circumstantial evidence: facts must be clearly proved, corpus delicti must be proved, the best evidence must be adduced, inculpatory facts must be incompatible with innocence, and reasonable doubt entitles the accused to acquittal. It also dealt with recovery on disclosure under Art. 40 QSO and last seen evidence. Ref: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Criminal Appeal No 771 of 2022, decided 29.10.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Criminal Appeal No 771 of 2022, decided 29.10.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Remedy Against Decree in Revisional Jurisdiction
records.heading: Against a revisional decree of a District Court, a writ under Article 199 is the only remedy
records.text: Where a District Court issues a decree in revisional jurisdiction, a second revision, a first appeal and a second appeal are all unavailable. The aggrieved party may file a writ under Art. 199 of the Constitution, but must show more than illegality, namely that the merits were adversely affected and legal rights compromised. Ref: Misree Khan v. Abdul Ghafoor (C.P.L.A.81-P/2019, decided 14.11.2024).
records.title: Misree Khan v. Abdul Ghafoor (C.P.L.A.81-P/2019, decided 14.11.2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Proof of Juvenility: Scrutiny of Documents
records.heading: Documents offered to prove juvenility must be scrutinised and the burden lies on the accused
records.text: Documents offered to prove juvenility must pass scrutiny and be verified on admissibility rules before acceptance. The inquiry under s. 8 JJSA 2018 is like a voir dire. Absence of documents means absence of authentic and admissible documents. An accused facing the death penalty must prove juvenility on true documents, and the burden lies on him. Ref: 2024 LHC 5222; Kamran Mushtaq v. The State (Crl. Revision.56647/24, decided 08.11.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kamran Mushtaq v. The State (Crl. Revision.56647/24, decided 08.11.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Safe Custody and S. 342 CrPC
records.heading: An unbroken chain of safe custody of narcotics is essential and failure leads to acquittal
records.text: An unbroken chain of safe custody of the recovered substance and sample parcel must be proved, failing which acquittal follows. All incriminating material must be put to the accused under s. 342 CrPC. Points deposed against the prosecution by its witness, who is not re-examined or questioned under Art. 150 QSO, are treated as not denied. Ref: 2024 LHC 5214; Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State (Crl. Appeal 40132/23, decided 13.11.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State (Crl. Appeal 40132/23, decided 13.11.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Obtained by Concealing Earlier Dismissal
records.heading: Bail obtained by concealing an earlier dismissal is liable to be recalled irrespective of merits
records.text: Bail obtained through foul play, by concealing dismissal of an earlier bail application, cannot remain in the field and is liable to be recalled irrespective of merits. The conduct violated the principles in PLD 1986 SC 173, 2002 SCMR 171 and PLD 2014 SC 241. The order of the Additional Sessions Judge was set aside. Ref: 2024 LHC 5229; Ehsan Ali v. The State (Crl. Revision 72289/24, decided 18.11.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Ehsan Ali v. The State (Crl. Revision 72289/24, decided 18.11.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 43 Transfer of Property Act: Feeding the Grant
records.heading: Section 43 TPA lets the transfer operate on interest the transferor later acquires
records.text: S. 43 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 applies where a person fraudulently or erroneously represents that he is authorised to transfer immovable property. At the transferee's option the transfer operates on any interest the transferor later acquires while the contract subsists. The representation may be innocent. Ref: 2024 LHC 5203; Noora (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Province of Punjab (Civil Revision No.14536 of 2022).
records.title: Noora (deceased) through L.Rs. v. Province of Punjab (Civil Revision No.14536 of 2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Rule 17-A Appointment; Reinstatement Order Not Implemented
records.heading: Petitioner entitled to regular appointment under Rule 17-A; refusal to implement the appellate order not sustainable
records.text: The petitioner was entitled to regular appointment under Rule 17-A of the Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1974, relying on 2014 PLC (CS) 793 and 2021 PLC(CS) Note 16. The revisional order refusing to implement the Appellate Authority's order was taken on a jaundiced view and cannot sustain. Ref: 2024 LHC 5246; Muhammad Danish Sajid v. Secretary Government of Punjab (WP-2763-23, decided 04.11.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Danish Sajid v. Secretary Government of Punjab (WP-2763-23, decided 04.11.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Restitution of Conjugal Rights: Wife's Claims and Rejoinder
records.heading: A wife resisting restitution may raise Family Courts Act claims and the husband may file a rejoinder
records.text: A wife resisting a suit for restitution of conjugal rights may raise any permissible claim under the Family Courts Act, 1964. The Family Court must then give the husband an opportunity to file a rejoinder, which is treated as his written statement. Ref: 2024 LHC 5250; Nasir Sharif v. Sabeela Imtiaz (Wp 4132-23, decided 11.11.2024); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Nasir Sharif v. Sabeela Imtiaz (Wp 4132-23, decided 11.11.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Decide Application Before Appeal
records.heading: An application for additional evidence under O. XLI R. 27 must be decided before the appeal
records.text: A pending application under O. XLI R. 27 CPC for additional evidence must be decided by the appellate court before the merits of the appeal. Deciding it jointly with the appeal, or leaving it undecided, is a procedural irregularity that prejudices the party and affects the appellate process. Ref: 2024 LHC 5266; Muhammad Iqbal Gill v. Nasir Abbas (C.R. No.6830 of 2023, decided 06.11.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal Gill v. Nasir Abbas (C.R. No.6830 of 2023, decided 06.11.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution of Dowry Articles: Appeal Under S. 14
records.heading: An executing court's decision on payment of dowry articles' value is appealable under section 14
records.text: An executing court's decision directing the judgment debtor to pay the value of dowry articles, after the decree holder refused to receive the articles, is a final decision. It is appealable as a decision given under s. 14 of the Family Courts Act, 1964. Ref: 2024 LHC 5284; Muhammad Ashraf v. Judge Executing Court (WP-15322-24, decided 15.11.2024); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. Judge Executing Court (WP-15322-24, decided 15.11.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII R. 4 CPC: Special Circumstances
records.heading: A decree under O. XXXVII R. 4 CPC is set aside only on special circumstances
records.text: Under O. XXXVII R. 4 CPC a decree can be set aside only under special circumstances, which exclude ordinary circumstances and place a heavy burden on the defendant. A bare ground of non-service cannot be considered where the address in the suit and in the application is the same. Ref: Muhammad Mansab v. Muhammad Hanif (Civil Petition Nos.1970-L of 2024, decided 19.11.2024).
records.title: Muhammad Mansab v. Muhammad Hanif (Civil Petition Nos.1970-L of 2024, decided 19.11.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ss. 151, 152 CPC: Decree Conforming to Judgment
records.heading: Sections 151 and 152 CPC allow correction of mistakes and a decree must conform to the judgment
records.text: Courts may use inherent powers under s. 151 CPC for the ends of justice, and s. 152 CPC permits correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes even on the court's own motion. Under O. XX R. 6 CPC the decree must conform to the judgment. An intentional omission can only be remedied by review, appeal or revision. Ref: 2024 LHC 5288; Muhammad Hussain v. Ali Muhammad (Civil Revision No.1499 of 2012).
records.title: Muhammad Hussain v. Ali Muhammad (Civil Revision No.1499 of 2012)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CDR Alone Inconclusive Without Voice Recording
records.heading: A call data record alone is inconclusive without a forensically analysed voice recording
records.text: A CDR shows only use of a SIM within a cell tower area and does not identify the user, so a witness's admission of SIM use needs corroboration by end-to-end audio recording with forensic analysis, proved in accordance with law. Evidence known to a party but not produced at trial cannot be brought in at the appellate stage under s. 428 Cr.P.C. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 371, PLD 2024 Lahore 522; Mst. Saima Nareen v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal CM/2/59829/21).
records.title: Mst. Saima Nareen v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal CM/2/59829/21)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Copies of Witness Statements to Accused: S. 265-C
records.heading: Section 265-C CrPC entitles the accused to free copies of statements at least seven days before trial
records.text: Under s. 265-C CrPC the accused must be given copies of the specified statements and documents free of cost, no later than seven days before trial, so that the defence is not disadvantaged. The petition was accepted, the orders of the High Court and Trial Court were set aside, and the Trial Court was directed to supply the copies of the statements bearing signatures and thumb impressions. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1863.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recalling of Witness
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC allows a witness to be recalled for a just decision, not to fill gaps
records.text: S. 540 CrPC empowers the trial court to summon or recall a witness if necessary for a just decision. Re-examination clarifies matters arising from cross-examination and cannot be used to rectify flaws or fill gaps in the case. The trial court properly accepted the application to recall, and the High Court erred in overturning it. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1939.

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Pro-Mediation Bias in Arbitration Proceedings
records.heading: Mediation is a complementary and necessary component of the justice system
records.text: In proceedings concerning making an arbitral award a rule of the court, the Court observed that mediation is a complementary and necessary component of the justice system, as well as an alternative to litigation. Ref: M/s Mughals Pakistan (Pvt) Ltd. v. Employees Old Age Benefit Institution (EOBI) (C.A.256/2024, decided 06.11.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: M/s Mughals Pakistan (Pvt) Ltd. v. Employees Old Age Benefit Institution (EOBI) (C.A.256/2024, decided 06.11.2024)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction on Expiry of Tenancy Not Pleaded
records.heading: Ejectment may be ordered on expiry of tenancy during proceedings though not pleaded
records.text: Ejectment can in principle be ordered only on the grounds taken in the petition. Where tenancy expires during the proceedings, requiring the landlord to file a fresh petition on that ground would prolong the tenant's occupation without benefit, contrary to the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009, which aims at cost effective and expeditious resolution. Ref: 2024 LHC 5348; Muhammad Saleem Minhas v. Ashfaq Hussain Minhas (WP-2292-24, decided 05.11.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Saleem Minhas v. Ashfaq Hussain Minhas (WP-2292-24, decided 05.11.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Final Specific Performance Decree Voids Later Registered Deeds
records.heading: A final specific performance decree voids later registered sale deeds
records.text: Once a decree of specific performance based on an unregistered prior sale agreement attains finality, subsequently registered sale deeds become null and void. Ref: 2024 LHC 5313; Mst. Shamim Akhtar v. Abdul Hameed (Civil Revision-828-14, decided 12.11.2024); Justice Abid Hussain Chattha.
records.title: Mst. Shamim Akhtar v. Abdul Hameed (Civil Revision-828-14, decided 12.11.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution Against Surety, Not Special Attorney
records.heading: A decree can be executed against the Surety and not against the Special Attorney
records.text: A Special Attorney and a Surety are different. A decree can be executed only against the Surety, and not against the Special Attorney unless an instrument expressly makes him liable for satisfaction of the decree. Ref: 2024 LHC 5370; Muhammad Naeem v. ADJ Gujranwala (WP 65675/21, decided 25.11.2024); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Naeem v. ADJ Gujranwala (WP 65675/21, decided 25.11.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial Review of Government Policy Decisions
records.heading: Judicial review of government policy is unwarranted absent illegality, voidness or perversity
records.text: Policy decisions require political judgment and not legal interpretation. Absent illegality, voidness or perversity, judicial review of the government policy of outsourcing management of underperforming schools was unwarranted. No violation of a fundamental right or of the Punjab Free and Compulsory Education Act 2014 was shown, and the policy had cabinet approval. Ref: 2024 LHC 5390; Syed Ahsan Abbas v. GOP (WP-7707-24, decided 28.11.2024); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Syed Ahsan Abbas v. GOP (WP-7707-24, decided 28.11.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Part Patwar and Part Sarkar in Mutation
records.heading: Part Sarkar is preferred over Part Patwar and defects in attestation defeated the exchange mutation
records.text: Part Patwar records the proceedings of the Revenue Officer, while the Part Sarkar copy contains the Patwari's report, Qanungo attestation and Revenue Officer's order and is preferred over Part Patwar. Thumb impressions only on Part Patwar, sanction not in a public Jalsa-i-Aam and non-compliance with s. 42 of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Act, 1967 meant the exchange mutation could not be upheld. Ref: 2016 CLC 302.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare Paramount
records.heading: The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in custody
records.text: The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in custody under ss. 7 and 17(2) of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, including the guardian's character and capacity and the minor's age and sex. The father is natural guardian, but the court must be satisfied that welfare lies in his custody. Poverty does not disentitle the mother. The Appellate Court's arrangement was subject to reconsideration if circumstances change. Ref: Gul Sadem Khan v. Mst. Halima (C.P.L.A.421-P/2022, decided 22.11.2024); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Gul Sadem Khan v. Mst. Halima (C.P.L.A.421-P/2022, decided 22.11.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Case Cancellation Report and Prosecutor's Role
records.heading: A cancellation report is a final report under section 173 CrPC sent through the prosecutor
records.text: The Investigating Officer may recommend cancellation under Rule 24.7 of the Police Rules 1934. A cancellation report is a final report under s. 173 CrPC (Rule 25.57) and is sent through the prosecutor under s. 9(4) of the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service Act, 2006. The prosecutor applies evidential and public interest tests only if he disagrees with the police opinion. Ref: 2024 LHC 5466; Sheikh Nadeem Anwar v. Ilaqa Magistrate (Criminal Proceedings 36921/22, decided 11.11.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Sheikh Nadeem Anwar v. Ilaqa Magistrate (Criminal Proceedings 36921/22, decided 11.11.2024)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Art. 128 QSO: Legitimacy and DNA in Maintenance Suit
records.heading: Birth during a valid marriage is conclusive proof of legitimacy and DNA tests must not delay maintenance
records.text: Under Art. 128 QSO, birth during a valid marriage or within two years of its dissolution, the mother remaining unmarried, is conclusive proof of legitimacy, and under Art. 2(f)(9) no evidence may be admitted to disprove it. DNA tests should not be used as a tool of harassment or delay in child maintenance matters. Ref: 2024 LHC 5579; Sakhawat Hussain v. ADJ Bhalwal (WP 22286/23, decided 27.11.2024); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Sakhawat Hussain v. ADJ Bhalwal (WP 22286/23, decided 27.11.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Edited Nude Images Shared
records.heading: Bail refused outside the prohibitory clause where edited nude images were shared
records.text: In offences outside the prohibitory clause bail is granted as a rule, but this is not a universal rule and depends on the facts. The petitioner had victimised a young girl and her mother by sharing edited nude photographs with a close relative, which was an exceptional circumstance for refusing bail. Ref: 2024 LHC 5566; Muneeb Riaz v. The State (Crl. Misc. 63844/24, decided 30.10.2024); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Muneeb Riaz v. The State (Crl. Misc. 63844/24, decided 30.10.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Quashing: Ss. 16 of Ordinance and 341 PPC Not Attracted
records.heading: FIR quashed as section 16 of the Ordinance and section 341 PPC were not attracted
records.text: S. 16 of the Ordinance requires words or statements and a consequent fear or alarm or prejudice to public safety, but the FIR did not state what slogans were chanted. S. 341 PPC (wrongful restraint under s. 339) was also examined, and s. 144 CrPC was not alleged to be in force. The FIR was lodged in disregard of the petitioner's fundamental rights. Ref: 2024 LHC 5547; Rai Muhammad Usama Sultan v. DPO Chiniot (Criminal Proceedings 50329/24, decided 08.11.2024); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Rai Muhammad Usama Sultan v. DPO Chiniot (Criminal Proceedings 50329/24, decided 08.11.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wife's Death in Bedroom: Onus on Husband
records.heading: A wife's unnatural death in a private room puts an onus on the husband under Article 122
records.text: Where a wife dies unnaturally in a private room at night, the husband has exclusive knowledge and the onus shifts to him under Art. 122 QSO. His first version has persuasive value, and stringent principles are not applied to circumstantial evidence. Adverse inference arises if he fails to inform the police despite visible marks. The prosecution need not meet every hypothesis of the accused. Ref: 2024 LHC 5556; The State v. M. Waqas So M. Riaz (Murder Referenc.215-19, decided 12.11.2024); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: The State v. M. Waqas So M. Riaz (Murder Referenc.215-19, decided 12.11.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Adult Son for Education
records.heading: A father may be obliged to maintain an adult son to complete basic education
records.text: A father may be obliged to maintain an adult son who has not completed the basic education needed to earn his livelihood, excluding higher studies and studies abroad. The Trial Court must consider the father's capacity, the son's age, conduct, own resources, nature and stage of studies, academic performance and the education needed to earn a living. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 851; Muhammad Imran v. Samina Kausar (WP 62571/24).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Samina Kausar (WP 62571/24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Malicious Prosecution: Malice and Absence of Probable Cause
records.heading: Malicious prosecution requires proof of both malice and absence of reasonable and probable cause
records.text: A claimant for malicious prosecution must prove both malice and absence of reasonable and probable cause, which are separate requirements. Not every prosecution that ends in clearing the opponent entitles him to compensation. The appeal was allowed and the suit for Rs. 53,924,500 was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 863, 2025 MLD 1; Asghar Ali v. Muhammad Asghar (R.F.A. No. 28132 of 2023); Justice Muhammad Iqbal; Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Asghar Ali v. Muhammad Asghar (R.F.A. No. 28132 of 2023)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Charagah Land Not Available for Allotment
records.heading: Land reserved as Charagah under a scheme is not available for allotment
records.text: Where the Lambardari scheme showed that land was reserved as Charagah and not for allotment, the respondent's allotment under that scheme was cancelled. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 863, 2025 MLD 1; Asghar Ali v. Muhammad Asghar (R.F.A. No. 28132 of 2023); Justice Muhammad Iqbal; Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Asghar Ali v. Muhammad Asghar (R.F.A. No. 28132 of 2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documents Produced Through Counsel's Statement
records.heading: Documents brought on record through counsel's unsworn statement have no value in law
records.text: Documents brought on record through the statement of counsel without oath have no value in law. They must be proved by the parties' own depositions on oath or through witnesses subject to cross-examination. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 863, 2025 MLD 1; Asghar Ali v. Muhammad Asghar (R.F.A. No. 28132 of 2023); Justice Muhammad Iqbal; Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Asghar Ali v. Muhammad Asghar (R.F.A. No. 28132 of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Deferred Dower: Time of Payment
records.heading: Where no time is fixed, deferred dower becomes payable on dissolution of marriage or death
records.text: Where no period is fixed for payment of deferred dower, the wife becomes entitled on dissolution of marriage or death of a spouse. A sum agreed to be paid on a specified event becomes payable on that event. As the husband remarried and divorced the petitioner, she was entitled to a decree for dower. Petition partly allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 891; Mst. Shamim Akhtar v. Additional District Judge Rawalpindi (W.P. No. 2889 of 2020, heard on 23.10.2024); Justice Shakil Ahmad.
records.title: Mst. Shamim Akhtar v. Additional District Judge Rawalpindi (W.P. No. 2889 of 2020, heard on 23.10.2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Bailable Offences for Juveniles: S. 6(3) JJSA
records.heading: Offences punishable up to seven years are bailable for a juvenile, including on pre-arrest bail
records.text: Under s. 6(3) JJSA 2018, offences punishable up to seven years are bailable for a juvenile under 18. This benefit applies to pre-arrest bail as well as post-arrest bail, as a distinction would be arbitrary and contrary to the objectives of the Act. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 702; Manzoor Ahmad v. Muhammad Umar Farooq (Crl. Misc. No. 78015/CB/2023).
records.title: Manzoor Ahmad v. Muhammad Umar Farooq (Crl. Misc. No. 78015/CB/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Acts Under Power of Attorney After Principal's Death
records.heading: Acts under a general power of attorney after the principal's death are void
records.text: On the death of the principals the general power of attorney became redundant by operation of law, and transactions by the attorney under it are void, illegal and fraudulent. The arbitration agreement, award and the order making it a rule of the court were nullities. Petition under s. 12(2) CPC dismissed with heavy costs. Ref: 2024 LHC 5612; Mushtaq Ahmad v. Allah Ditta (Civil Revision.525-13, decided 19.11.2024); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Mushtaq Ahmad v. Allah Ditta (Civil Revision.525-13, decided 19.11.2024)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test for Paternity Requires Consent
records.heading: DNA examination to decide paternity requires the consent of the parties
records.text: Consent of the parties is essential for DNA examination to decide paternity. Without consent the trial court may draw an adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO and decide on the evidence, including physiognomy (qiyafah). The order directing DNA analysis of the minor was set aside and the writ petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2024 Lah 715, PLJ 2025 Lah 159; Kaneez Fatima v. Senior Civil Judge (WP 75322/22).
records.title: Kaneez Fatima v. Senior Civil Judge (WP 75322/22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confession Before Police in Custody Inadmissible
records.heading: A confession made before the police while in custody is inadmissible
records.text: It is well settled that the confession of an accused made before the police while in custody is inadmissible in evidence. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1782, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 345; Rehmat-ullah v. The State (Crl.A.23-Q/2020).
records.title: Rehmat-ullah v. The State (Crl.A.23-Q/2020)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Proof of SIM Ownership
records.heading: A call data record is inconsequential without proof that the SIMs belonged to the parties
records.text: The CDR was inconsequential for the prosecution because no documentary evidence showed that the SIMs belonged to the deceased or the accused, and no recording or transcript of the conversation was produced. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1782, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 345; Rehmat-ullah v. The State (Crl.A.23-Q/2020).
records.title: Rehmat-ullah v. The State (Crl.A.23-Q/2020)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Withdrawal of Complaint After Conviction
records.heading: A complainant may withdraw a complaint under section 248 CrPC after conviction in non-compoundable offences
records.text: Where offences are non-compoundable, a complainant may still withdraw the complaint under s. 248 CrPC on any consideration. The complainant, whose possession had been restored, withdrew the complaint after compromise, and the five appellants convicted under s. 3 were acquitted. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1173; Hafeez Ullah v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 974 & Crl. A. No. 609 of 2024, heard on 25.7.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Hafeez Ullah v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 974 & Crl. A. No. 609 of 2024, heard on 25.7.2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Age Determination: Documents Before Ossification Test
records.heading: Juvenility is decided first on documents and only in their absence by medical examination
records.text: Under s. 8 JJSA 2018, juvenility is decided first on documents and only in their absence by medical examination. NADRA Form-B and a birth certificate are preferred over a private school leaving certificate, and where two views of age are possible the one favouring the accused is accepted. Failure to claim juvenility earlier does not bar the claim at trial. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1175, 2025 PCrLJ 482; Imran Haider v. The State (Crl. Rev. No. 83203 of 2023, decided 22.5.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Imran Haider v. The State (Crl. Rev. No. 83203 of 2023, decided 22.5.2024)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Dismissal of Complaint Without Inquiry or Investigation
records.heading: A complaint cannot be dismissed without proper inquiry or ordering investigation
records.text: The lower court neither conducted a proper inquiry nor ordered investigation, and did not summon police record despite a cross-version FIR and possession having been given by a warrant of possession. Revision allowed, and the complaint is deemed pending for inquiry or investigation as needed. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1202; Noor Khan v. State (Crl. Rev. No. 2454 of 2022, decided 27.6.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Noor Khan v. State (Crl. Rev. No. 2454 of 2022, decided 27.6.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Fake Police Encounters: Zero Tolerance
records.heading: Fake police encounters cannot be justified as self-defence and call for zero tolerance
records.text: Zero tolerance must be shown towards fake police encounters, which cannot be allowed under the guise of self-defence by police officials. In a petition under s. 491 CrPC for recovery of a detenue who died in an encounter, the Court disposed of the petition expecting a circular on such encounters to be implemented. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 1211; Mst. Farzana Bibi v. Capital City Police Officer (Crl. Misc. No. 36448-H of 2024, decided 13.6.2024); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mst. Farzana Bibi v. Capital City Police Officer (Crl. Misc. No. 36448-H of 2024, decided 13.6.2024)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-i-Muwathibat: Two Hours Delay Fatal
records.heading: A two hour delay in making Talb-i-Muwathibat is not immediate and defeats pre-emption
records.text: The word immediate in Talb-i-Muwathibat is significant, and a delay of two hours in making the demand is not an immediate demand. Such delay is fatal to a claim of pre-emption. Ref: Late Sher Ayaz Khan v. Gul Najeeb Khan (C.P.L.A.406/2022, decided 09.12.2024); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Late Sher Ayaz Khan v. Gul Najeeb Khan (C.P.L.A.406/2022, decided 09.12.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Christian Marriage Act 1872 and Divorce Act 1869
records.heading: The Christian Marriage Act 1872 and Divorce Act 1869 prevail over church precepts in conflict
records.text: Authority on the Christian Marriage Act 1872 and Divorce Act 1869 as the principal family laws for Christians, prevailing over church precepts in conflict. It discusses the definition of minor in s. 3 (under 21 years), consent to a minor's marriage under s. 19, and the bar on marriages forbidden by the parties' personal law. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2058; Nasreen Bibi v. Station House Officer (Writ Petition No. 63301/2021).
records.title: Nasreen Bibi v. Station House Officer (Writ Petition No. 63301/2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: USB as Document; Copy to Accused
records.heading: A USB is a document under Article 2(1)(c) QSO and the accused may have a copy
records.text: A USB is a document under Art. 2(1)(c) QSO, and evidence from modern devices may be produced under Art. 164. If the prosecution files a USB containing video of the raid with the challan, the accused is entitled to a copy. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2005; Muhammad Iqbal v. The State (Crl. Appeal.51928/24).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal v. The State (Crl. Appeal.51928/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Concurrent Running of Sentences: S. 397 CrPC
records.heading: Section 397 CrPC gives wide discretion to direct sentences from separate trials to run concurrently
records.text: S. 397 CrPC gives courts wide discretion to direct that sentences from separate trials run concurrently, and in hardship cases courts should consider this seriously. Both life sentences, reached after death sentences were commuted, were treated as running concurrently. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2045, PLJ 2024 CrC 973; Sher Afzal v. State (Crl. Misc-729-M-24).
records.title: Sher Afzal v. State (Crl. Misc-729-M-24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561-A with S. 397 CrPC: Concurrent Sentences
records.heading: The High Court may order concurrent sentences under section 561-A read with section 397 CrPC
records.text: Where trial, appellate and revisional courts were silent on concurrent running of sentences, the High Court may in appropriate cases invoke its inherent jurisdiction under s. 561-A read with s. 397 CrPC, provided the superior appellate court did not consciously deny the benefit. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2045, PLJ 2024 CrC 973; Sher Afzal v. State (Crl. Misc-729-M-24).
records.title: Sher Afzal v. State (Crl. Misc-729-M-24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Partition Suit Not Barred by Res Judicata
records.heading: A partition suit is not barred by res judicata from an earlier declaratory suit
records.text: A suit for partition was wrongly rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC as res judicata, since the earlier s. 42 declaratory suit was not decided on merits. The right of partition is independent and is not barred by O. II R. 2 CPC or by any earlier suit on the same property. Ref: 2024 SCP 407; Zakirullah (decd.) v. Muhammad Rehman (C.P.L.A.159-P/2014, decided 21.11.2024); Justice Mazhar Alam Khan Miankhel.
records.title: Zakirullah (decd.) v. Muhammad Rehman (C.P.L.A.159-P/2014, decided 21.11.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution: Dower Gold Ornaments or Alternate Value
records.heading: In execution, the wife may choose either the dower gold ornaments or the alternate value
records.text: The decree entitled the wife to 7 tola gold ornaments or Rs.100,000 as alternate value. The Appellate Court travelled beyond the decree by limiting her to Rs.100,000 in execution, since the gold was primarily her dower and the word alternate offers a choice. That finding was not sustainable. Ref: 2024 LHC 5824; Mst. Zaib Un Nisa v. A.D.J (WP 3346-18, decided 20.11.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mst. Zaib Un Nisa v. A.D.J (WP 3346-18, decided 20.11.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Lodging FIR: Two Hours Thirty Five Minutes
records.heading: A two hour thirty five minute delay in lodging the FIR was consequential and needed explanation
records.text: A delay of two hours thirty five minutes in lodging the FIR, for a night occurrence about two kilometres from the police station and with a motorcycle available, was consequential. The case could not be termed promptly registered, deliberation and concoction could not be ruled out, and the prosecution had to explain the delay. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1054; Mst. Gulnaz Ajmal v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 72371/19).
records.title: Mst. Gulnaz Ajmal v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 72371/19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Not Corroborating Ocular Account
records.heading: Absence of blackening or tattooing contradicted an ocular account of close range firearm injuries
records.text: The site plan showed firearm injuries inflicted from about half a karam (2.5 feet), or less, yet the medical officer noted no blackening, tattooing or charring around the entry wounds. This contradicted the ocular account. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Complainant
records.heading: Failure to inform anyone by phone was unnatural and discredited the complainant's presence
records.text: The complainant had a mobile phone but admitted that he informed nobody of the occurrence by phone, which was contrary to natural human response for a real brother of the deceased. This was sufficient to discard his stance that he was present at the spot. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Eyewitness: Reliability Test
records.heading: An injured eyewitness's deposition must still be strictly scrutinised for credibility
records.text: Grievous hurt to an eyewitness reflects positively on his presence but does not conclusively prove his deposition, which must be tested on the principles of appraisal of evidence. It is unjust to build a conviction on an injured witness's evidence without strict scrutiny of credibility, particularly with several assailants. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of 12 Days in Statement of Injured Witness
records.heading: An unexplained delay of 12 days in recording an injured witness's statement made it unworthy of credence
records.text: A delay of about 12 days in recording the s. 161 CrPC statement of the injured lady was not satisfactorily explained. The anaesthetist's report on her condition was unsupported as he was not examined, and the medical officer found her conscious and oriented. The statement was held unworthy of credence, with a possibility of substitution of the real assailants. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1421.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage and DVR: Expert Not Summoned
records.heading: CCTV evidence was discarded where the DVR was not linked and the expert was not summoned
records.text: The DVR was not shown to be the one installed at the neighbour's house, as he was not a witness to the recovery memo and it was not exhibited in his statement. The forensic expert was not summoned, and the DVR could not be decoded, so the CCTV evidence was discarded in line with the forensic report. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1764; The State v. Abdul Hakeem (Murder Reference 44-22).
records.title: The State v. Abdul Hakeem (Murder Reference 44-22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Reporting and Ante-Timed FIR
records.heading: Delay in reporting and blanks in the inquest report showed the FIR was ante-timed
records.text: The incident at 10.00 pm was reported at the hospital emergency ward at 11.45 pm. Discrepancies and blanks in the inquest report showed that the FIR was recorded later after deliberation and consultation and was ante-timed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1691; Muhammad Asif v. The State (Jail Appeal 6732/19).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Jail Appeal 6732/19)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agent Selling Principal's Property for Own Benefit
records.heading: An agent selling the principal's property for his own benefit needs the principal's informed consent
records.text: An agent transferring the principal's property must use reasonable diligence to communicate with the principal and seek instructions where the power of attorney is doubtful. If he deals with the property on his own account, he should obtain the principal's informed consent, failing which the principal may repudiate the transaction. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1984, PLJ 2024 SC 845; Bashir Ahmed (deceased) through his L.Rs. etc v. Nazir Ahmad etc (C.A.197-L/2019, decided 19.08.2024); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Bashir Ahmed (deceased) through his L.Rs. etc v. Nazir Ahmad etc (C.A.197-L/2019, decided 19.08.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Distant Eye Witnesses and Changed Site Plan
records.heading: Distant witnesses with an intervening crop cannot credibly specify the assailants' roles
records.text: Where witnesses were at a considerable distance and standing crop intervened, their deposition specifying the roles of assailants in inflicting firearm injuries is not believable. A site plan with changed particulars annexed by the complainant did not negate the original site plan or the inquest report and was of no help. Ref: 2024 LHC 5924; Abid Ali v. The State (Jail Appeal: 79031/19, decided 20.11.2024).
records.title: Abid Ali v. The State (Jail Appeal: 79031/19, decided 20.11.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Oral Talaq Effective Without S. 7 MFLO Notice
records.heading: Oral talaq pronounced thrice takes effect even without notice under section 7 MFLO
records.text: Oral talaq pronounced thrice becomes irrevocable and effective when pronounced, even without notice under s. 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, as the Ordinance provides no such consequence and no certificate from the Chairman is needed. The appellate decree was set aside and the trial decree upheld, with the wife also entitled to maintenance for 2 and a half years for breastfeeding. Ref: 2024 MLD 1749; Khan Muhamd v. Additional District Judge, Jaranwala.
records.title: Khan Muhamd v. Additional District Judge, Jaranwala

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in FIR: Two Hours
records.heading: A two hour FIR delay was not ignorable where both witnesses claimed presence and distances were short
records.text: A delay of two hours in lodging the FIR would ordinarily be ignorable. It could not be overlooked where both prosecution witnesses claimed presence at the scene, the police station was 2 kilometres away and the hospital 1 1/4 kilometres from the police station. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1951.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inquest Report Timing Contradicts FIR
records.heading: Inquest report timing that contradicted the FIR raised doubt about the time of occurrence
records.text: The inquest report recorded receipt of information at 10:00 a.m., while the prosecution said the FIR was lodged at 2:30 p.m. and the death certificate was silent on time. The Investigating Officer did not explain this, which raised doubt about the time of occurrence and death. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1623.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Discrepancy in Deceased's Eyes: Doubt on Witnesses
records.heading: A discrepancy in the deceased's eyes between medical and inquest reports doubted the witnesses
records.text: The Woman Medical Officer noted the deceased's eyes as semi opened, while the inquest report said opened. Witnesses claimed they attended the deceased until she died in hospital, so the discrepancy created doubt about the prosecution case and the truthfulness of those witnesses. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1623.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Pistol Recovery Despite Negative Forensic Report
records.heading: Death sentence altered to life despite a negative forensic report on pistol recovery
records.text: Recovery of a .30 bore pistol at the accused's pointing out was inconsequential in the face of a negative Forensic Science Agency report on matching of empties, but was not fatal to the prosecution. The case was proved beyond doubt, and the death sentence was altered to imprisonment for life owing to mitigating circumstances. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1467.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of 1 Hour 35 Minutes in FIR
records.heading: Unexplained delay of 1 hour 35 minutes in reporting a murder was consequential
records.text: The unexplained delay in reporting a murder to a police station 4.5 kilometres away was consequential, since delay often results in consultation and deliberation and is an afterthought. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 829.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Conflict between ocular and medical evidence on the direction of the shot raised doubt
records.text: There was conflict between the ocular account and the medical evidence. The Medical Officer's report showed a shot from an upper level, whereas the witnesses said the accused fired straight and hit the deceased on the front of the chest while he stood. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 729.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of 3.5 Hours in Lodging FIR
records.heading: An unexplained delay of three and a half hours in lodging the FIR made the version doubtful
records.text: An unexplained delay of three hours and thirty minutes in reporting a night occurrence to a police station 5 to 6 kilometres away, with a severe flaw in fixing the time of reporting, cast doubt on the authenticity of the FIR and rendered the prosecution version doubtful. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 729.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of Six Hours in FIR
records.heading: A six hour fifteen minute FIR delay with a car available created doubt about the story
records.text: A delay of six hours and fifteen minutes in lodging the FIR, with the police station 5 kilometres away and the complainant having a car available that night, created doubt about the truthfulness of the prosecution story. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 696.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account v. Medical Evidence: Unexplained Injuries
records.heading: Unexplained burn and electric shock injuries meant the ocular account did not support medical evidence
records.text: Some of the 17 injuries were burn and electric shock marks which no eye-witness explained, and the postmortem report did not state the time between injury and death or death and autopsy. The ocular account therefore did not support the medical evidence. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 696.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 302(b) PPC: Death Sentence Reduced to Life
records.heading: Death sentence under section 302(b) PPC reduced to life in view of mitigating circumstances
records.text: Per the headnote, the death sentence was reduced to imprisonment for life in view of mitigating circumstances, including uncertainty about which of four assailants fired the fatal shot, a sudden occurrence amounting to a free fight without motive, and long incarceration in the death cell. Ref: 2024 SCMR 2048; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Trial or Appeal as Mitigating Circumstance
records.heading: Mere length of trial and appeal is not alone a ground to reduce the death penalty
records.text: Mere length of time taken in concluding the trial and deciding the appeal does not by itself constitute an extenuating circumstance justifying reduction of the death penalty to the lesser penalty. Ref: 2024 SCMR 2048.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Crime Empties Not Sent for Forensic Analysis
records.heading: Unexplained failure to send crime empties for forensic analysis led to acquittal
records.text: Unexplained failure to send 39 Kalashnikov and 3 twelve bore empties to the firearm expert, the complainant's doubtful presence in the absence of any firearm injury to him, improvements and non-production of injured witnesses led to failure of the prosecution case. The appellants were acquitted. Ref: 2024 SCMR 2042.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Acid Attack: Whether Act of Terrorism
records.heading: An acid attack is an act of terrorism only if it creates fear in society
records.text: An acid attack is an act of terrorism only if its actual, intended or potential effect is to create fear and insecurity in society. A personal matter between convict and victim falls outside s. 6 ATA. Where terrorism is not proved but the offence is, the Special Judge ATC convicts under the PPC, here ss. 336-B and 337-L. Ref: 2024 SCMR 2024; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Cheque Case Further Inquiry
records.heading: A disputed cheque case under section 489-F PPC fell within further inquiry; pre-arrest bail confirmed
records.text: Whether the disputed cheque was issued with dishonest intention, to repay a loan, or handed over blank as a guarantee for a business transaction was a matter for trial. The case under s. 489-F PPC fell within further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: 2024 SCMR 2066.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Brother Cannot Challenge Paternity in Succession Proceedings
records.heading: A claimed brother cannot challenge the paternity of the deceased's children without a suit for negative declaration
records.text: A person claiming to be the deceased's brother has no legal character to challenge the paternity or legitimacy of the deceased's children in succession proceedings without first filing a suit for a negative declaration under s. 42 Specific Relief Act, 1877. The children established a prima facie case on oral and documentary evidence. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1223; Moulvi Abdul Fateh v. Yar Muhammad and others (C.P.L.A.259-Q/2020).
records.title: Moulvi Abdul Fateh v. Yar Muhammad and others (C.P.L.A.259-Q/2020)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Transcripts Unreliable
records.heading: A call data record without transcripts or recordings is not reliable evidence
records.text: Mere production of a CDR, without call transcripts or audio recordings, is not reliable evidence. It must also be shown that the persons at both ends of the call are those whose data is produced. The CDR here bore no name, signature or seal of an authorised officer and could not safely be relied upon. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1119; Asmat Ullah Khan v. The State (J.P.431/2016).
records.title: Asmat Ullah Khan v. The State (J.P.431/2016)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 431 CrPC: Abatement of Appeal on Death
records.heading: A criminal appeal abates on death but an appeal against a fine does not under section 431
records.text: A criminal appeal abates on the death of the appellant, but under s. 431 CrPC an appeal against a sentence of fine does not abate. The appeal abates as to imprisonment and is heard on merits as to the fine, which affects the estate. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1119; Asmat Ullah Khan v. The State (J.P.431/2016).
records.title: Asmat Ullah Khan v. The State (J.P.431/2016)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Brothers Depriving Sisters of Inheritance
records.heading: Excluding daughters from inheritance on account of a gift of cash and dowry is against Shariah
records.text: The contention that daughters should be excluded from the inheritance mutation because of a lifetime gift of cash and dowry was against Shariah and the law. The brothers' frivolous litigation was dismissed with costs of Rs. 500,000, and the revenue authorities were directed to ensure distribution among all legal heirs per Shariah. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1273; Bakht Biland Khan & others v. Zahid Khan & others (C.P.L.A.284-P/2012).
records.title: Bakht Biland Khan & others v. Zahid Khan & others (C.P.L.A.284-P/2012)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Employment Quota for Children of Civil Servants Unconstitutional
records.heading: Employment quotas for children or widows of government employees without open merit are unconstitutional
records.text: Quotas giving employment to children or widows of government employees without advertisement or open merit were held contrary to Arts. 3, 4, 5(2), 25 and 27 of the Constitution. Provisions including s. 11-A of the Sindh Civil Servants Rules, 1974 were declared void. The GPO appeal was allowed and the Peshawar High Court judgment set aside. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1276; General Post Office, Islamabad and others v. Muhammd Jalal (C.P.L.A.3390/2021); Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan.
records.title: General Post Office, Islamabad and others v. Muhammd Jalal (C.P.L.A.3390/2021)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation in Inheritance Suits
records.heading: Limitation may bar an inheritance suit in exceptional circumstances, such as a decades late challenge
records.text: Limitation does not become irrelevant in every inheritance case, and in exceptional circumstances a suit based on inheritance may be barred by time and acquiescence. A challenge to an inheritance mutation after decades was time barred and the suit was rightly dismissed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1268; Akhtar Nasir Ahmed v. Province of Punjab through District Collector Gujrat & others (C.P.L.A.1182-L/2018).
records.title: Akhtar Nasir Ahmed v. Province of Punjab through District Collector Gujrat & others (C.P.L.A.1182-L/2018)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Applicability of IDA 2005 Beyond Qabza Mafia
records.heading: The Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 protects any lawful owner or occupier, not only against Qabza Mafia
records.text: Any lawful owner or lawful occupier illegally dispossessed may complain under ss. 3 and 4 of the Illegal Dispossession Act, 2005. The Act is not restricted to Qabza Mafia or land grabbers and covers any illegal occupant. Leave to appeal was refused. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1152; Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A.66-K/2024).
records.title: Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A.66-K/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: No Piecemeal Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A plaint cannot be rejected in part under O. VII R. 11 CPC
records.text: A plaint cannot be rejected in part under O. VII R. 11 CPC, even if only one prayer is maintainable. Only the plaint averments are examined, and weakness of proof or defendants' pleas do not justify rejection. The application must state distinctly which ground under the Rule applies. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1108; Mst. Rehmat Begum v. Mehfooz Ahmed & others (C.P.L.A.49-K/2022).
records.title: Mst. Rehmat Begum v. Mehfooz Ahmed & others (C.P.L.A.49-K/2022)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: S. 7 IDA: Interim Relief During Trial
records.heading: Interim relief under section 7 of the Illegal Dispossession Act needs only a prima facie finding
records.text: Interim relief under s. 7(1) is available only during trial, on a prima facie finding that the accused is not in lawful possession and that the complainant was owner or lawful possessor. This is a lower threshold than proof of the s. 3 offence, which awaits conclusion of trial. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1152; Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A.66-K/2024).
records.title: Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A.66-K/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Commencement of Trial: Framing of Charge
records.heading: Taking of cognizance does not commence a trial; it commences with framing of charge
records.text: Taking of cognizance does not commence a trial. The trial of a case commences with the framing of charge against the accused. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1152; Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A.66-K/2024).
records.title: Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A.66-K/2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Relief Act 1877: Ss. 5, 7, 12, 22
records.heading: Specific performance under the Specific Relief Act 1877 is equitable and discretionary
records.text: Discusses the equitable and discretionary nature of specific performance under ss. 5, 7, 12 and 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Illustrations to s. 12 are an aid to interpretation, and the court presumes that breach of a contract to transfer immoveable property cannot be adequately relieved by compensation in money. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1108; Mst. Rehmat Begum v. Mehfooz Ahmed & others (C.P.L.A.49-K/2022).
records.title: Mst. Rehmat Begum v. Mehfooz Ahmed & others (C.P.L.A.49-K/2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Repeal Includes Amendment: S. 6 General Clauses Act
records.heading: The word repeal in section 6 of the General Clauses Act includes amendment
records.text: There is no difference in principle between repeal and amendment, as an amendment inherently involves a repeal. The word repeal in s. 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 therefore includes amendment, and s. 6 applies to the amendment of a law. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1168.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Framing of Issues: O. XIV CPC
records.heading: Issues under O. XIV CPC identify the real dispute and an issue of law may be tried first
records.text: Issues under O. XIV R. 1 CPC are of fact, law or mixed. Under R. 2(1) the court may try an issue of law first if it relates to jurisdiction or a bar to the suit. The object of framing issues is to identify the real dispute. An appellate court may frame an issue and refer it for trial without remanding the whole case. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah 253; Abdul Rahman and others v. Muhammad Farooq and others (R.F.A. No.14953 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Rahman and others v. Muhammad Farooq and others (R.F.A. No.14953 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Discouraging Adjournment Culture
records.heading: Compilation of Supreme Court judgments on discouraging the culture of adjournments
records.text: Compilation of Supreme Court judgments on discouraging the culture of adjournments in court proceedings. The post lists the authorities without stating the holdings. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 887, PLJ 2024 SC 905, PLD 2024 SC 642, 2020 SCMR 300.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell Without Registration Stipulation
records.heading: An agreement to sell silent on registration still obliges the seller to execute a registered deed
records.text: Under s. 55(1)(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, absent a contrary contract, the seller is bound to execute a proper conveyance. An agreement to sell without a stipulation on registration therefore still obliged the seller to execute a registered sale deed, and the contrary appellate finding was flawed. Ref: 2024 LHC 6002; Farida Khanum v. Abdul Qayyum etc (R.S.A. 694-21, decided 27.11.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Farida Khanum v. Abdul Qayyum etc (R.S.A. 694-21, decided 27.11.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare Paramount
records.heading: Welfare of the minor overrides Muslim law preferences on age of custody
records.text: Welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in custody and is taken in its widest sense, covering mental and physical health, education, psychological well-being and moral values. Muslim law preferences on age of custody yield to the minor's welfare, judged by age, sex, environment and attending circumstances. Ref: Irfan Arshad v. Mst. Zainab Noor etc (Writ Petition No.452 of 2024).
records.title: Irfan Arshad v. Mst. Zainab Noor etc (Writ Petition No.452 of 2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Public Interest Litigation on Jail Reforms
records.heading: Recommendations on jail reforms made in public interest litigation
records.text: In public interest litigation on jail reforms, recommendations were made including women jails at Lahore, Faisalabad and Rawalpindi, open prisons with minimum security, electronic prisoner file management, digitalisation of court, prison and prosecution records, trial by video link, and revamping of probation and parole services. Ref: 2024 LHC 6036; Rida Qazi v. Govt. of Punjab (WP.16322-10, decided 18.12.2024); Justice Abid Aziz Sheikh.
records.title: Rida Qazi v. Govt. of Punjab (WP.16322-10, decided 18.12.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199 Writ and Alternate Remedy; Sealing of Petroleum Premises
records.heading: An alternate remedy does not oust Article 199 and a Deputy Commissioner cannot seal petroleum premises
records.text: Availability of an alternate remedy does not oust the High Court's discretion under Art. 199. After the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 2002 and the Pakistan Oil Rules, 2016, a Deputy Commissioner had no authority to seal premises or penalise under Rule 44 of the 1971 Rules. Ref: 2024 LHC 6021; M/S Khan Petroleum Services v. Govt of Punjab etc (WP 9424-24, decided 05.12.2024); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: M/S Khan Petroleum Services v. Govt of Punjab etc (WP 9424-24, decided 05.12.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ex Parte Decree: Implied Condonation of Delay
records.heading: Delay is impliedly condoned where an ex parte decree is set aside on an application with condonation
records.text: Where an application to set aside an ex parte decree was allowed and the courts below were aware that an application for condonation of delay was filed with it, no express order on the latter is needed. The delay is deemed impliedly condoned. Ref: 2024 LHC 6013; Muhammad Ramzan v. ADJ etc (WP15231-24, decided 14.11.2024); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. ADJ etc (WP15231-24, decided 14.11.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Tunnel Vision by Police and Prosecution
records.heading: Tunnel vision by police and prosecution has pernicious effects in criminal justice
records.text: Authority on the proposition that tunnel vision by police and prosecution has pernicious effects in the criminal justice system. Ref: 2024 LHC 6062; Usama Ali v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 77969/19, decided 04.12.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Usama Ali v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 77969/19, decided 04.12.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Unregistered Dower Deed Proved by Marginal Witnesses
records.heading: An unregistered dower deed proved by two marginal witnesses is valid under Article 79
records.text: Where the wife proves execution of the dower deed through two marginal witnesses under Art. 79 QSO, the objection that the deed is unregistered is of no significance, relying on 1989 SCMR 1871 and other authorities. The judgment also addresses recovery of deferred dower during subsistence of marriage and maintenance. Ref: Akmal Khan etc v. Mst. Noorin etc (WP. No. 883-M of 2018, decided 13.12.2024).
records.title: Akmal Khan etc v. Mst. Noorin etc (WP. No. 883-M of 2018, decided 13.12.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Constructive Res Judicata: Successive Remedies
records.heading: Constructive res judicata bars a party who exhausted one remedy from pursuing another
records.text: Where several remedies exist before different fora for the same cause, a party who exhausts one and obtains a final decision cannot pursue another, as constructive res judicata applies. A final High Court decision bars a civil suit on the same grievance, and left out grounds and reliefs cannot be raised later. Ref: Mst. Sajida Parveen v. Saqib Mushtaq & others (CR No. 576-A of 2019, decided 18.11.2024).
records.title: Mst. Sajida Parveen v. Saqib Mushtaq & others (CR No. 576-A of 2019, decided 18.11.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Art. 150 QSO and s. 161 CrPC
records.heading: A prosecution witness may be declared hostile on the basis of his section 161 statement
records.text: The term hostile is a judicial creation interpreting Art. 150 QSO. A prosecution witness may be declared hostile on the basis of his s. 161 CrPC statement and cross-examined by the prosecution. The prosecution may not confront him with that statement, except witnesses who prove their signatures or thumb impressions on documents. Ref: Shakoor Khan v. The State etc (J. Cr.A No. 1528-P of 2023, decided 12.11.2024).
records.title: Shakoor Khan v. The State etc (J. Cr.A No. 1528-P of 2023, decided 12.11.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Right of Private Defence: Ss. 96, 97, 100 PPC
records.heading: The right of private defence under sections 96, 97 and 100 PPC
records.text: Discusses the right of private defence under Chapter IV PPC, including s. 96 (nothing is an offence if done in exercise of the right), s. 97 (defence of body and property) and s. 100 (causing death or grievous hurt in specified situations of assault). Ref: Mst. Shahira Bibi v. The State and another (Cr.MBA No. 568-M of 2024, decided 08.10.2024).
records.title: Mst. Shahira Bibi v. The State and another (Cr.MBA No. 568-M of 2024, decided 08.10.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Concessions Under First Proviso to S. 497(1) CrPC
records.heading: First proviso concessions to a minor, woman or sick person should be extended at the bail stage
records.text: The special concessions in the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC for an accused under sixteen years, a woman, or a sick or infirm person should be extended at the bail stage, having regard to the facts and circumstances of each case. Ref: Mst. Shahira Bibi v. The State and another (Cr.MBA No. 568-M of 2024, decided 08.10.2024).
records.title: Mst. Shahira Bibi v. The State and another (Cr.MBA No. 568-M of 2024, decided 08.10.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Liability of Sureties in Execution: S. 145 CPC
records.heading: Sureties who undertook payment of the decretal amount are liable under section 145 CPC
records.text: Sureties who voluntarily undertook payment of the decretal amount in a surety bond are liable under s. 145 CPC and may be proceeded against as judgment debtors on the debtor's default. Production of the judgment debtor before the court does not lessen their liability. Both sureties were rightly held liable. Ref: Syed Kalam Shah & another v. Shafiq-ur-Rehman & another (C.R No. 887-P of 2022, decided 31.07.2024).
records.title: Syed Kalam Shah & another v. Shafiq-ur-Rehman & another (C.R No. 887-P of 2022, decided 31.07.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Defence of Natural Death; Art. 122 QSO
records.heading: A plea of natural death shifts the burden to the accused once strangulation is proved
records.text: Where the accused pleaded that his wife died of epilepsy, and the prosecution had discharged its burden of proving strangulation, the burden shifted to him to substantiate the plea. His failure to explain the unnatural death under Art. 122 QSO lightened the prosecution's burden. Ref: Shakir Ullah v. The State and another (Cr.A No 198-M/2022, decided 25.09.2024).
records.title: Shakir Ullah v. The State and another (Cr.A No 198-M/2022, decided 25.09.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Review: O. XLVII R. 1 and S. 114 CPC
records.heading: Review lies only for an error on the face of the record under O. XLVII R. 1
records.text: Judicial orders carry a presumption of correctness and are challenged by appeal or revision. In exceptional cases review lies under O. XLVII R. 1 and s. 114 read with s. 151 CPC, on an error on the face of the record that can be rectified without reappraisal of evidence. Ref: Syed Ali Ahmed Shah v. Syed Shoukat Hussain Shah and others (C.P.L.A.1218-K/2023, decided 16.12.2024); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Syed Ali Ahmed Shah v. Syed Shoukat Hussain Shah and others (C.P.L.A.1218-K/2023, decided 16.12.2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Inquiry: Standard of Proof and Due Process
records.heading: Departmental inquiries follow the balance of probabilities but must observe due process and natural justice
records.text: Authority on the distinction between criminal trials and departmental inquiries, balance of probabilities as the standard of proof in inquiries, and violation of due process and natural justice in ex parte inquiries held while the employee was incarcerated. Ref: The Director General, Intelligence Bureau Government of Pakistan & others v. Babar Ali Solangi (C.P.L.A.281-K/2022, decided 15.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: The Director General, Intelligence Bureau Government of Pakistan & others v. Babar Ali Solangi (C.P.L.A.281-K/2022, decided 15.10.2024)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Child Justice Approach and Best Interests of Child
records.heading: Courts must adopt a child centred approach prioritising the best interests of the child
records.text: Courts must adopt a child-centred approach prioritising the best interests of the child. Children in conflict with the law need rehabilitative rather than punitive measures, and children in contact with the law must be safeguarded. The judgment also refers to restorative justice. Ref: Malik Mahmood Ahmad Khan v. Malik Moazam Mahmood, etc (C.P.L.A.2250-L/2016, decided 19.12.2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Malik Mahmood Ahmad Khan v. Malik Moazam Mahmood, etc (C.P.L.A.2250-L/2016, decided 19.12.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX Rr. 8 and 9 CPC; Case Management
records.heading: Authority on O. IX Rr. 8 and 9 CPC and case management provisions
records.text: Authority on O. IX Rr. 8 and 9 CPC, on the principle that every procedure is permissible until prohibited by law, on Arts. 202 and 203 of the Constitution, and on inserting case management provisions in the CPC and CrPC for early disposal of backlog. Ref: Mrs. Faryal Arif Latif v. Mr. Arif Latif (Civil Petition No. 3597-L of 2023 & Civil Petition No. 8-L of 2024, decided 31.10.2024).
records.title: Mrs. Faryal Arif Latif v. Mr. Arif Latif (Civil Petition No. 3597-L of 2023 & Civil Petition No. 8-L of 2024, decided 31.10.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX Rr. 8 and 9 CPC: Dismissal for Non-Appearance
records.heading: On the plaintiff's non-appearance the suit is dismissed and restoration needs sufficient cause
records.text: Under O. IX R. 8 CPC, where the plaintiff does not appear, the suit is dismissed unless the defendant admits the claim. Under R. 9 the plaintiff cannot bring a fresh suit but may seek restoration on showing sufficient cause. The judgment also urges case management provisions in the CPC and CrPC. Ref: Mrs. Faryal Arif Latif v. Mr. Arif Latif (Civil Petition No. 3597-L of 2023 & Civil Petition No. 8-L of 2024, decided 31.10.2024).
records.title: Mrs. Faryal Arif Latif v. Mr. Arif Latif (Civil Petition No. 3597-L of 2023 & Civil Petition No. 8-L of 2024, decided 31.10.2024)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Non-Party Subsidiary Impleaded in Arbitration
records.heading: A wholly owned subsidiary is not a party to the arbitration agreement absent board resolution or novation
records.text: A company with independent corporate existence, even if a wholly owned subsidiary, could not be treated as a party to the arbitration agreement under s. 20 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, absent a board resolution or novation. The award and the decree making it rule of the Court were held invalid. Ref: 2024 CLC 2021.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Husband's Right of Talaq and Compensation Claim
records.heading: The husband's right of talaq is absolute with no condition under Shariah or codified law
records.text: In considering a claim of Rs. 500,000 as compensation in lieu of divorce, the court noted that the husband's right of talaq is absolute, with no condition described in Shariah or the codified law, citing s. 7(1) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 and s. 105 of the Code of Muslim Personal Laws. Ref: 2024 CLC 2129, PLJ 2024 Lah 165.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Entries: Gold Ornaments and Stipulation
records.heading: Nikahnama entries on gold ornaments corroborated by witnesses entitled the wife to recover them
records.text: Entries in the Nikahnama on 8 tolas of gold ornaments and a Rs. 500,000 stipulation on divorce were corroborated by witnesses and the Nikahnama is admissible. The husband led no rebuttal evidence, so the wife was rightly held entitled to recover the gold ornaments. Ref: 2024 CLC 2129, PLJ 2024 Lah 165.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor Daughters with Mother
records.heading: Custody of minor daughters was given to their educated mother in the interest of welfare
records.text: Welfare of the minors is paramount in custody. The mother is the source of unconditional affection and daughters need her company. Custody of the minors was held to lie with their educated mother living in a joint family, with the father's visitation arrangement continuing. Ref: 2024 CLC 2057; Mst. Alia Sehr v. Mushtaq Ahmed and others (W.P. No.61653 of 2020).
records.title: Mst. Alia Sehr v. Mushtaq Ahmed and others (W.P. No.61653 of 2020)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Award After Withdrawal of Suit: No S. 21 Order
records.heading: An award made after withdrawal of the suit is not illegal for want of a section 21 order
records.text: An award made after the suit was withdrawn cannot be held illegal merely because no order of reference was obtained under s. 21 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, since the suit was no longer pending. The award may be filed in the Civil Court under s. 2(c) and judgment pronounced under s. 17. Revision allowed and matter remanded. Ref: 2024 CLC 2099; Sakhi Mohammad (deceased) etc v. Mst. Maridan etc (Civil Revision 4290-16).
records.title: Sakhi Mohammad (deceased) etc v. Mst. Maridan etc (Civil Revision 4290-16)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Dower Decree: Frivolous Objection
records.heading: A third party's frivolous objection in execution of a dower decree was dismissed with costs
records.text: In execution of a decree for dower in favour of a wife, an objection by a third party claiming ownership of the attached house was dismissed. The objection petitioner's revision was dismissed with costs payable to the decree-holder, the court deprecating false and frivolous litigation. Ref: 2024 CLC 2110.

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Ss. 3 and 5 Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.heading: The Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 protects lawful owners and occupiers from property grabbers
records.text: The Act protects lawful owners and occupiers from illegal or forcible dispossession by property grabbers. S. 3 bars entry to dispossess, grab, control or occupy property without lawful authority. Under s. 5 the court directs investigation within fifteen days, tries the case day to day and decides within sixty days, and may award compensatory costs up to Rs. 500,000 for a false complaint. Ref: Aurangzaib Alamgir v. Muhammad Sajid & others (Crl.P.L.A.58-K/2023, decided 15.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Aurangzaib Alamgir v. Muhammad Sajid & others (Crl.P.L.A.58-K/2023, decided 15.10.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561-A CrPC Not a Substitute for Ss. 249-A or 265-K
records.heading: Section 561-A CrPC is curative and not a substitute for sections 249-A or 265-K
records.text: Section 561-A CrPC is curative, meant to prevent abuse of process or secure the ends of justice, and cannot be construed as an alternative or substitute for ss. 249-A or 265-K CrPC. Ref: Aurangzaib Alamgir v. Muhammad Sajid & others (Crl.P.L.A.58-K/2023, decided 15.10.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Aurangzaib Alamgir v. Muhammad Sajid & others (Crl.P.L.A.58-K/2023, decided 15.10.2024)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Charagah Land: Concept and Leasing
records.heading: Charagah land is not to be allotted, sold or exchanged and cannot be leased indefinitely
records.text: Charagah is common village grazing land, which is not to be allotted, sold or exchanged, though it may be used for public purposes. Its lease requires Board of Revenue approval for a public purpose and a specific period, and it cannot be leased for an indefinite term to a lambardar for his tenure. Ref: Muhammad Yousaf v. Member Judicial - IV, Board of Revenue, Punjab Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.3297/2024, decided 28.11.2024); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Member Judicial - IV, Board of Revenue, Punjab Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.3297/2024, decided 28.11.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Criminal Case: Fair Trial Under Art. 10-A
records.heading: A transfer application turns on assurance of a fair trial under Article 10-A
records.text: The core principle in deciding a transfer application is assurance of a fair trial under Art. 10-A of the Constitution, and a free and fair trial is a sine qua non of the criminal justice system. Ref: 2024 LHC 6096; Miss Shabnam Riaz v. Naila Karim etc (Transfer Application (Crl) 80981/24, decided 24.12.2024); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Miss Shabnam Riaz v. Naila Karim etc (Transfer Application (Crl) 80981/24, decided 24.12.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail in Rape: Consent and Victim's Testimony
records.heading: A consistent solitary statement of the victim can suffice and discrepancies are not scrutinised at pre-arrest bail
records.text: The prosecution initially bears the burden of proving absence of consent, and a trustworthy, consistent solitary statement of the victim can suffice for conviction. Absence of injuries or resistance does not indicate consent (Expl. 2 to s. 375 PPC). Scrutiny of discrepancies between the FIR and s. 164 CrPC statement is beyond a pre-arrest bail application. Ref: 2024 LHC 6099; Zain Tariq v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.56457/24, decided 31.12.2024); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Zain Tariq v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.56457/24, decided 31.12.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-K CrPC: At Any Stage, No Probability of Conviction
records.heading: Sections 249-A and 265-K CrPC apply at any stage if there is no probability of conviction
records.text: The words at any stage in ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC cover stages before or after framing of charge or some evidence, subject to hearing both parties. The court must apply a conscious judicial mind to the material to assess the probability of conviction, using the ordinary meaning of consider and probability. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1152; Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A.66-K/2024).
records.title: Niaz Ahmed and another v. Mohammad Aijaz and others (Crl.P.L.A.66-K/2024)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Binding Effect of Earlier Bench of Equal Strength
records.heading: An earlier decision of a bench of equal strength binds a later bench
records.text: An earlier decision on a question of law binds a later bench of equal strength, which cannot decide the same question contrary to it. If the later bench doubts its correctness, the matter should be referred to the Chief Justice, or the Constitution Committee in the Supreme Court, for a larger bench. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1168.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Vested Right and Past and Closed Transaction
records.heading: A vested right becomes a past and closed transaction when exercised or deemed exercised
records.text: A right vests when all facts required by law to establish it have occurred, and remains inchoate if some have not. A vested right becomes a past and closed transaction when exercised, or deemed exercised by operation of law, which depends on the facts and law of each case. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1168.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Alibi and Further Inquiry
records.heading: An alibi supported by CDR, hospital slips and CCTV made the case one of further inquiry
records.text: The petitioners' alibi of being at a hospital in another city at the time of the murderous assault was supported by CDR, hospital slips and CCTV footage, and the police placed them in Column No. 2 of the challan. The case fell within further inquiry, and ad-interim pre-arrest bail was confirmed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1241; Saeed Ahmed v. State.
records.title: Saeed Ahmed v. State

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Tarbela Dam Oustees: Proprietary Rights on Allotted Land
records.heading: Proprietary rights of a Tarbela Dam oustee accrued on allotment and were not affected by later change
records.text: Proprietary rights of a Tarbela Dam oustee, allotted land under s. 10(4) of the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act, 1912, accrued on allotment.
