A later change in the prohibited area due to upgrading of Khanewal to a district did not affect them, and denial of those rights violated Art. 24 of the Constitution. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1235.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning of Defence Witnesses After Verification Reports
records.heading: Refusing to summon defence witnesses without reasons after verification reports was arbitrary and unjust
records.text: The need to summon new witnesses arose for the accused when the trial court allowed verification of his appointment orders on the prosecution's application and then on his own. The order dismissing his application gave no reasons for four of the five witnesses and appeared arbitrary and unjust. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2014.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Compounding of Qatl-i-Amd by Incompetent Legal Heirs
records.heading: Family members who stayed aloof from the outset are incompetent to compound qatl-i-amd
records.text: Family members who stayed aloof from the outset, leaving the State to register the FIR and give evidence, were either accomplices or too frightened to question the accused, and were therefore incompetent to compound the offence. The compromise applications in the honour killing case were dismissed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2028.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Criteria for Sentencing
records.heading: Sentencing is discretionary and not a mechanical exercise
records.text: Sentencing is discretionary and not a mechanical exercise. The court considers the statutory minimum and maximum, the accused's role, gravity of the offence, loss to the State, remorse, capacity for reformation, age, health, jail conduct and time already served. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2041.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Sentence Reduced for Old Age and Poor Health
records.heading: Sentence reduced to the period undergone in view of old age and poor health
records.text: The prosecution proved misappropriation of 28261 wheat bags causing a loss of Rs. 89,183,430. In view of the accused's old age, poor health and substantial sentence already served, the sentence of fourteen years was reduced to the period undergone, with the fine maintained. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2041.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Trial in Absentia: S. 512 CrPC
records.heading: Section 512 CrPC allows prosecution evidence to be recorded in the absence of an absconding accused
records.text: Under s. 512 CrPC, where an accused absconds with no immediate prospect of arrest, the court may record prosecution evidence in his absence. Proceedings under the 2005 Act continue against absconders, while those against the accused who died abated. The petition for abatement of the entire proceedings was dismissed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2072.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Further Investigation and Re-Investigation After Challan
records.heading: Further investigation or re-investigation is permitted after challan until conclusion of trial for compelling reasons
records.text: Further investigation, re-investigation or transfer of investigation is permitted after a challan or framing of charge until conclusion of trial, if not arbitrary and supported by compelling reasons. A pending private complaint does not bar it unless exceptional circumstances exist, and s. 56(e) Specific Relief Act bars injunctions against investigations. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 2081; Zain Ali and another v. Additional Inspector General of Police and others (Writ Petition No.65602/2022).
records.title: Zain Ali and another v. Additional Inspector General of Police and others (Writ Petition No.65602/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Lis Pendens: Restored Suit and S. 52 TPA
records.heading: Restoration of a dismissed suit relates back and attracts lis pendens under section 52
records.text: If a suit is dismissed and then restored, the restoration relates back, and a transfer or sale made after dismissal and before restoration is subject to the doctrine of lis pendens in s. 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 1258.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Investigation Despite Discharge Order
records.heading: Police may reinvestigate a matter despite an order of discharge
records.text: Police authorities may reinvestigate a matter despite an order of discharge. Ref: 2024 LHC 6109; Muhammad Qaswar Hussain v. Judicial Magistrate etc (ICA Criminal 292-24, decided 23.12.2024); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Qaswar Hussain v. Judicial Magistrate etc (ICA Criminal 292-24, decided 23.12.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 182 PPC Proceedings During Pending Complaint Case
records.heading: Section 182 PPC proceedings cannot be initiated while a complaint case on the same matter is pending
records.text: While a complaint case is pending, proceedings under s. 182 PPC in a criminal case relating to the same subject matter cannot be initiated. Ref: 2024 LHC 6109; Muhammad Qaswar Hussain v. Judicial Magistrate etc (ICA Criminal 292-24, decided 23.12.2024); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Qaswar Hussain v. Judicial Magistrate etc (ICA Criminal 292-24, decided 23.12.2024)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Zar-e-Soem: Deposit Based on Sale Deed Price
records.heading: Deposit of zar-e-soem was rightly directed per the registered sale deeds and acted upon
records.text: Where a pre-emption suit is filed with an application to determine the tentative price, an inquiry is required, but here the trial court directed deposit of zar-e-soem per the registered sale deeds. The order was complied with and acted upon, and reopening it would not end the litigation. Procedural rules should make justice quickly available. Ref: 2024 MLD 2013; Muhammad Saleem v. Additional District Judge, etc. (Writ Petition No.43399/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Saleem v. Additional District Judge, etc. (Writ Petition No.43399/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIV R. 2 CPC: Preliminary Issues in Pre-emption
records.heading: Issues of law needing evidence are decided with factual issues in a pre-emption suit
records.text: Under O. XIV R. 2 CPC, issues of law that can dispose of the case are tried first, but if evidence is needed they are decided with the factual issues. The pre-emptor, having complied with the deposit order, was estopped from pressing earlier applications. Factual issues 3 and 4 could not be decided in isolation. Ref: 2024 MLD 2013; Muhammad Saleem v. Additional District Judge, etc. (Writ Petition No.43399/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Saleem v. Additional District Judge, etc. (Writ Petition No.43399/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Rejection of Plaint: Cause of Action
records.heading: A plaint is rejected only if, on proof of all allegations, no relief follows
records.text: In deciding whether a plaint discloses a cause of action, every averment is presumed true. The plaint is rejected only if, even on proof of all allegations, the plaintiff would be entitled to no relief. The suit was barred by law and disclosed no cause of action, so the lower appellate court's order was set aside. Ref: 2024 YLR 2813; Adeel Khalid Bajwa v. Bashir Ahmad Tahir and others (F.A.O. No. 81002 of 2021 and Civil Revision No. 12886 of 2022).
records.title: Adeel Khalid Bajwa v. Bashir Ahmad Tahir and others (F.A.O. No. 81002 of 2021 and Civil Revision No. 12886 of 2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Succession Certificate: Summary Procedure Under S. 373
records.heading: A succession certificate follows a summary procedure that decides only prima facie entitlement
records.text: Under s. 373 of the Succession Act, 1925 a succession certificate is granted by a summary procedure that determines only prima facie entitlement. Non-suiting the petitioner on her second application because of O. II R. 2 CPC was contrary to the Act, and the impugned judgment was not sustainable. Ref: Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public & another (C.P.L.A.256-Q/2020, decided 02.01.2025); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public & another (C.P.L.A.256-Q/2020, decided 02.01.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Meaning of Contradiction in Evidence
records.heading: Contradiction in evidence covers omissions and lacunas, not a statement set against nothing
records.text: The expression contradiction is wide and covers legal omissions, shortcomings and lacunas, and applies where acceptance of one witness's deposition requires rejection of another's. It means setting one statement against another, and not a statement against nothing. Ref: Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Exhibiting Articles: Rules and Orders LHC Vol. III
records.heading: Rules and Orders of the Lahore High Court guide the tendering and marking of incriminating articles
records.text: Guidelines on tendering incriminating articles in evidence are found in Rules and Orders of the Lahore High Court, Vol. III, Chapter 24 Part B, including Rule 14-F (every article forming part of circumstantial evidence must be produced and connected through witnesses) and Rule 14-H on marking of exhibits. Ref: Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Deposit of Balance Sale Consideration
records.heading: A direction to deposit balance consideration is not harsh and lets the vendee show readiness
records.text: A direction to deposit the balance consideration lets the vendee show readiness and willingness and safeguards the vendor, and is not harsh or oppressive. If the direction is not at the vendor's instance the trial court may extend time, otherwise it ordinarily becomes functus officio. Suit dismissed for non-deposit despite several opportunities. Ref: 2024 YLR 2826; Humayon Sajjad v. Aslam Khan (R.F.A.45873/23).
records.title: Humayon Sajjad v. Aslam Khan (R.F.A.45873/23)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Habeas Corpus for Custody of Minors: Summary Jurisdiction
records.heading: Habeas corpus for custody of minors is summary jurisdiction to be used sparingly
records.text: In habeas corpus the court may recover custody of minors from one parent and hand them to the other, but the jurisdiction is summary and extraordinary and should be sparingly used. Controversies are not tried and full evidence is not recorded, since plenary jurisdiction lies with other forums under special laws. Ref: 2025 LHC 1; Hamna Fahad v. C.C.P.O Lahore etc (WP 89/25, decided 03.01.2025); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Hamna Fahad v. C.C.P.O Lahore etc (WP 89/25, decided 03.01.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage: Admissibility Under Arts. 71 and 139 QSO
records.heading: CCTV footage not proved by an expert or played in court fails Articles 71 and 139
records.text: Video from a CD was not proved where no expert certificate or expert witness verified it, no photogrammetry test linked the accused to the footage, and it was neither played in court nor shown to a witness. CCTV footage as documentary or real evidence must meet Arts. 71 and 139 QSO. Ref: 2024 LHC 6125; Muhammad Ammar Shafi & 2 others v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 26878/24, decided 19.12.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Ammar Shafi & 2 others v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 26878/24, decided 19.12.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Investigative Lapses in Charas Recovery Case
records.heading: Investigative lapses in a charas case included no medical examination of the appellant
records.text: The post notes lapses in a charas case: the appellant, said to be a user and supplier, was not medico legally examined and no blood test was done. No intended buyer was arrested or pursued, no disclosure about dealers was obtained, and the Investigating Officer sent him to judicial custody the day after arrest without further investigation. Ref: 2024 LHC 6145; Muhammad Rizwan Ahmed alias Bablo v. The State (Crl. Appeal 631/22, decided 11.12.2024); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan Ahmed alias Bablo v. The State (Crl. Appeal 631/22, decided 11.12.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Child Witness: Competency and Voir Dire Test
records.heading: A child is competent to testify if able to understand and answer questions rationally
records.text: Under Art. 3 read with Art. 17 QSO, a child is competent to testify if capable of understanding and answering questions rationally. The court decides competency after a voir dire test, putting preliminary questions unconnected with the case. The post also notes that omissions amounting to contradictions on material particulars discredit a witness. Ref: 2024 LHC 6159; Sajjad Ahmed v. The State (Crl. Appeal 124/23, decided 27.06.2024); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Sajjad Ahmed v. The State (Crl. Appeal 124/23, decided 27.06.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Examination of Accused
records.heading: Every incriminating circumstance must be put to the accused under section 342 CrPC
records.text: Every incriminating piece of evidence or circumstance relied on against an accused must be put to him under s. 342 CrPC so that he can explain it. It is not an empty formality. Directing the trial court to examine the appellant correctly under s. 342 CrPC is not filling a lacuna in the prosecution case. Ref: 2024 LHC 6189; Muhammad Shahid Mehmood v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 243/23, decided 29.10.2024); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Shahid Mehmood v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 243/23, decided 29.10.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal: Appeal Not Revision
records.heading: Against an acquittal the remedy is appeal under section 417 and not revision
records.text: Under s. 417 CrPC an aggrieved person may appeal against an order of acquittal within 30 days. Under s. 439(5) CrPC no revision is entertained at the instance of a party who could have appealed. Ref: 2024 LHC 6200; Muhammad Sarfraz etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 6425-M-24, decided 20.11.2024); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Sarfraz etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 6425-M-24, decided 20.11.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed s. 161 CrPC Statement of Witness
records.heading: A delayed section 161 CrPC statement has no value unless plausibly explained
records.text: Delayed recording of a prosecution witness's statement under s. 161 CrPC reduces its value to nothing unless plausibly explained. No explanation was given, so no value attached to that statement. The post also treats an assailant waiting for the witnesses to arrive as contrary to natural human conduct. Ref: 2024 LHC 6207; Mst. Nadia alias Nadu Mai v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 10-J of 2021).
records.title: Mst. Nadia alias Nadu Mai v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 10-J of 2021)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Second Marriage Without Permission: Family Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Only the Family Court may try a case of second marriage without permission
records.text: Authority that the power to try a case of contracting a second marriage without permission lies only with the Family Court. Ref: 2024 LHC 6139; Muhammad Waqas v. Riffat Awan etc (Crl. Revision 1601/22, decided 27.12.2024); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. Riffat Awan etc (Crl. Revision 1601/22, decided 27.12.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Habeas Corpus Converted into Bail Petition
records.heading: Habeas corpus was converted into a bail petition where the police did not produce the record
records.text: Where the police did not produce the case record to show the detenue's connection with the offence or recoveries, the habeas corpus petition was converted into a bail petition despite the recorded arrest. He was set at liberty to approach the competent court for redress. Ref: 2025 LHC 29; Miraj Zubair v. RPO Sahiwal etc (WP 485/25, decided 08.01.2025); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Miraj Zubair v. RPO Sahiwal etc (WP 485/25, decided 08.01.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Appointment of Receiver Among Co-sharers
records.heading: Long litigation over inheritance rights is no ground to appoint a Receiver against declared co-sharers
records.text: The mere fact that parties had long been litigating over inheritance rights is no ground to appoint a Receiver or to deprive persons declared by the Supreme Court to be co-sharers to a specific extent. Ref: 2024 LHC 6272; Dost Muhammad (deceased) through 6 LRs & 13 others v. Muhammad Sarwar etc (Misc. Writ 48544/24, decided 24.12.2024); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: Dost Muhammad (deceased) through 6 LRs & 13 others v. Muhammad Sarwar etc (Misc. Writ 48544/24, decided 24.12.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 102 to 104 QSO: Documentary Terms Final
records.heading: Where terms are reduced to writing, oral evidence cannot contradict or vary the document
records.text: Under Arts. 102, 103 and 104 QSO, where parties reduce the terms of an agreement to writing, the document itself is final. No oral evidence may contradict, vary, add to or subtract from it, and the parties are bound by its terms. Ref: 2024 LHC 6286; Muhammad Arif & 1 other v. Haji Khalid Mahmood deceased through LRs (Civil Revision 45106/23, decided 29.11.2024); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: Muhammad Arif & 1 other v. Haji Khalid Mahmood deceased through LRs (Civil Revision 45106/23, decided 29.11.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 31 CPC: Appellate Judgment Requirements
records.heading: An appellate judgment without considering evidence violates O. XLI R. 31 CPC
records.text: A judgment recorded without considering the evidence cannot be approved. It violates O. XLI R. 31 CPC, which requires the appellate court to deliver a written judgment stating the points for determination, the decision on them and the reasons. Ref: 2024 LHC 6297; SNGPL v. Fazal Hussain (Civil Revision 1169-13, decided 29.11.2024); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: SNGPL v. Fazal Hussain (Civil Revision 1169-13, decided 29.11.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Court's Duty to Control Cross-Examination
records.heading: The court must control cross-examination and ensure the witness understands each question
records.text: While recording cross-examination the court must be vigilant, control it properly and ensure the witness understands each question before answering. It should not allow lengthy or irrelevant questions. In a murder trial the court must know the facts of the case so as to judge relevance of questions. Ref: 2006 PCrLJ 1294.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings may be allowed at any stage on just terms under O. VI R. 17
records.text: Under O. VI R. 17 CPC the court may at any stage allow amendment of pleadings on just terms to determine the real questions in controversy. Illustrative factors include the applicant's intention, limitation, avoiding injustice to the opponent, avoiding multiplicity of litigation, the nature of the suit and cause of action, and necessity, with the subject matter unchanged. Ref: 2024 LHC 6308; Maqbool Ahmad v. Addl. District Judge and others (Writ Petition No. 4183 of 2022, decided 24.12.2024).
records.title: Maqbool Ahmad v. Addl. District Judge and others (Writ Petition No. 4183 of 2022, decided 24.12.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof and Use of Photographs as Evidence
records.heading: A photograph is admissible if it meets QSO requirements and an inadmissible one must be disregarded
records.text: A photograph is admissible if it meets the QSO requirements. Arts. 70 and 71 allow a witness to testify on what he perceived. Art. 139 allows use of the photograph in cross-examination, Art. 140 to refresh memory, and Art. 151(3) to test credibility. An inadmissible photograph and testimony derived from it must be disregarded. Ref: 2024 LHC 6320; Awais Qarni v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 531-20, decided 07.10.2024); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Awais Qarni v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 531-20, decided 07.10.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Voluntary Statement in Cross-Examination
records.heading: A voluntary statement by a witness in cross-examination has no evidentiary value
records.text: A voluntary statement by a witness in cross-examination has no evidentiary value. A witness may not add material that does not answer or explain his answer to the question put. Such irresponsive testimony offends the rule of re-examination under Art. 133 QSO. Ref: PLD 2024 Sindh 289, 2003 YLR 406.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Retraction Distinguished from Hostility of Witness
records.heading: Mere retraction of a statement does not by itself make a witness hostile
records.text: Mere retraction of an earlier statement does not automatically make a witness hostile. Hostility means a deliberate intent to deviate from the truth or to act against the interest of the party calling the witness, whereas retraction is the withdrawal of a statement or accusation. Ref: Ghous Bakhsh v. The State (Crl.A.294/2020, decided 11.11.2024); Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Ghous Bakhsh v. The State (Crl.A.294/2020, decided 11.11.2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 191A: Validity and Bench Jurisdiction Questions
records.heading: Questions on the validity of Article 191A and bench jurisdiction were framed without a holding
records.text: The post records the two questions framed: whether Art. 191A infringes salient features of the Constitution, including judicial independence and separation of powers, and whether a bench other than the Constitutional Bench can decide its validity when jurisdiction is objected to on the basis of that Article. No holding is given. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through Revenue Division & others v. Dewan Motors (Pvt) Ltd (C.P.L.A.836-K/2020, decided 13.01.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through Revenue Division & others v. Dewan Motors (Pvt) Ltd (C.P.L.A.836-K/2020, decided 13.01.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance and Depreciation of Dowry Articles
records.heading: Depreciation of dowry articles during the suit cannot be imposed on the wife
records.text: Depreciation in value of dowry articles during a suit for their recovery cannot be imposed on the wife where the husband's denial of receiving them was evasive. A father cannot be burdened beyond his means, and maintenance may be reduced on adverse change in his means, so the appellate court erred in not letting him prove such change. Ref: 2024 LHC 6335; Mansoor Ali v. Mst. Anam Hussain etc (WP 819-20, decided 24.12.2024); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mansoor Ali v. Mst. Anam Hussain etc (WP 819-20, decided 24.12.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. I R. 10 CPC: Liberal Impleadment
records.heading: The court should exercise discretion liberally on impleadment applications under O. I R. 10
records.text: On applications under O. I R. 10 CPC the court should exercise its discretion liberally and not narrowly, especially where a party is likely to be affected by the judgment and its presence would help the court adjudicate effectively. Ref: Mr. Abdul Aziz an other v. All Pakistan Clerks Association Thru. Its Zilai President Manzoor Ahmed and others (C.P.L.A.251-Q/2024, decided 14.01.2025); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Mr. Abdul Aziz an other v. All Pakistan Clerks Association Thru. Its Zilai President Manzoor Ahmed and others (C.P.L.A.251-Q/2024, decided 14.01.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Civil Court Judgment in Criminal Proceedings
records.heading: A civil court's judgment is not admissible in criminal proceedings to prove its facts
records.text: Under Art. 57 QSO, a civil court's judgment is not admissible in criminal proceedings to establish the truth of the facts on which it is rendered. Ref: PLD 2011 Lah 246.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Bail Cancelled for Breach of Cheque Compromise
records.heading: Bail may be recalled under section 497(5) CrPC for breach of a cheque compromise
records.text: An offence under s. 489-F PPC is compoundable between the parties. Where an accused was granted bail on a compromise and later breaches its terms, his bail may be recalled on the complainant's application under s. 497(5) CrPC. The petition against the recall was dismissed in limine. Ref: 2021 MLD 947.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Stay of Criminal Proceedings Pending Civil Suit
records.heading: Criminal proceedings are stopped where criminal liability depends on the outcome of a civil lis
records.text: Where the ultimate criminal liability depends on the outcome of a civil lis, the criminal proceedings are by operation of law required to be stopped. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 786.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Remedy Against Revisional Order Rejecting Plaint
records.heading: Against a revisional decree of a District Court, only a writ under Article 199 lies
records.text: Against a decree of a District Court in revisional jurisdiction, no second revision, first appeal or second appeal lies under the CPC. The aggrieved party may file a writ under Art. 199 of the Constitution, which must show more than illegality, namely that the merits were adversely affected and legal rights compromised. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 24; Misree Khan & others v. Abdul Ghafoor & others (C.P.L.A. 81-P of 2019, decided 14.11.2024); Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Misree Khan & others v. Abdul Ghafoor & others (C.P.L.A. 81-P of 2019, decided 14.11.2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Transactions by Person of Unsound Mind
records.heading: Where a person of unsound mind transacts, the onus lies on the beneficiary to prove bona fides
records.text: Where a plaintiff proved chronic mental ailments, the onus lay on the beneficiary to prove that a property transaction under a power of attorney was bona fide. The defendants failed to discharge it, as the sale consideration was not paid to her and the other siblings did not testify. The suit through her next friend was rightly decreed. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 31; Faqir Syed Anwar-Ud-Din (deceased) v. Syed Raza Haider & others (C.P.L.A.3210-L/2023).
records.title: Faqir Syed Anwar-Ud-Din (deceased) v. Syed Raza Haider & others (C.P.L.A.3210-L/2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 27(b) SRA: Onus on Bona Fide Purchaser
records.heading: A subsequent vendee under section 27(b) SRA bears the initial onus of proving good faith
records.text: A subsequent vendee claiming protection under s. 27(b) Specific Relief Act 1877 bears the initial onus. He must show he paid due consideration to the vendor, acted in good faith without dishonest purpose, and took reasonable care to inquire as a person of ordinary prudence. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 31; Faqir Syed Anwar-Ud-Din (deceased) v. Syed Raza Haider & others (C.P.L.A.3210-L/2023).
records.title: Faqir Syed Anwar-Ud-Din (deceased) v. Syed Raza Haider & others (C.P.L.A.3210-L/2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay: Wrong Legal Advice
records.heading: Conflicting legal advice about leave petition or appeal is not sufficient cause to condone delay
records.text: Confusion or conflicting legal advice about whether a leave petition or an appeal lay is not sufficient cause for condoning delay. The appeal was time barred by 22 days, the application for condonation was dismissed, and the appeal stood dismissed. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 60; Ghulam Sarwar (deceased) thr. his L.Rs. v. Province of Punjab (C.A. 766/2021).
records.title: Ghulam Sarwar (deceased) thr. his L.Rs. v. Province of Punjab (C.A. 766/2021)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare Paramount
records.heading: The father as natural guardian is not automatically entitled to custody of a minor
records.text: Welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in custody, under ss. 7 and 17(2) of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. The father as natural guardian is not automatically entitled to custody, and poverty is not a valid ground to deny the mother custody. The custody arrangement is subject to reconsideration if circumstances change. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 47; Gul Sadem Khan v. Mst. Halima and others (C.P.L.A.421-P/2022).
records.title: Gul Sadem Khan v. Mst. Halima and others (C.P.L.A.421-P/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561-A CrPC Not Substitute for ss. 249-A, 265-K
records.heading: Section 561-A CrPC is curative and cannot substitute for sections 249-A or 265-K
records.text: Section 561-A CrPC is curative, to prevent abuse of process or secure the ends of justice. It cannot be construed as an alternative or substitute for the provisions of ss. 249-A or 265-K CrPC. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 53; Aurangzaib Alamgir v. Muhammad Sajid & others (Crl.P.L.A.58-K/2023).
records.title: Aurangzaib Alamgir v. Muhammad Sajid & others (Crl.P.L.A.58-K/2023)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Illegal Dispossession Act: Ss. 3 and 5
records.heading: The Illegal Dispossession Act protects lawful owners and occupiers with a time bound trial
records.text: The Act protects lawful owners and occupiers from illegal dispossession by property grabbers. Section 3 bars entry to dispossess or occupy without lawful authority. Under s. 5 the court directs police investigation within fifteen days, tries the case from day to day within sixty days, and may award compensatory costs up to Rs. 500,000 if the complaint is false or vexatious. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 53; Aurangzaib Alamgir v. Muhammad Sajid & others (Crl.P.L.A.58-K/2023).
records.title: Aurangzaib Alamgir v. Muhammad Sajid & others (Crl.P.L.A.58-K/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: General Attorney Alienating Property to Relatives
records.heading: A general attorney needs the principal's special permission to transfer property to himself or close relatives
records.text: The holder of a general power of attorney must obtain the principal's special permission, with prior approval and consent, before transferring the principal's property in his own favour or to his close relatives, such as his sons. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 63; Allah Bakhsh (deced) thr. his LRs. v. Muhammad Riaz and others (C.P.L.A.2565/2023).
records.title: Allah Bakhsh (deced) thr. his LRs. v. Muhammad Riaz and others (C.P.L.A.2565/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 202 to 204 CrPC: Summoning Accused
records.heading: The section 202 CrPC inquiry protects a person complained against from frivolous summoning
records.text: Under ss. 202, 203 and 204 CrPC the trial court must scrutinise the evidence behind allegations, including the purpose of bringing them and the risk of harassment or victimisation. The inquiry under s. 202 CrPC protects a person complained against from frivolous summoning and must be weighed when deciding whether to issue process. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 40; Muhammad Rajar v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 165-K/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Rajar v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 165-K/2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift (Hiba) Under Muslim Law: Essentials
records.heading: A gift under Muslim law needs declaration, acceptance and delivery, and no registration for oral immovable gifts
records.text: A gift is an immediate transfer of property without exchange. Relying on Mulla s. 149, its essentials are a clear declaration by the donor, acceptance by or for the donee, and delivery of possession. An oral gift of immovable property needs no registration or writing. A donor who affirmed the gift in his lifetime leaves his heirs no standing to dispute it. Ref: Syed Masood Ali v. Mst. Feroza Begum and another (Civil Petition No.552-K of 2021 & 1108-K of 2023, decided 26.12.2024).
records.title: Syed Masood Ali v. Mst. Feroza Begum and another (Civil Petition No.552-K of 2021 & 1108-K of 2023, decided 26.12.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 195(1)(a) CrPC: Trial Regime
records.heading: Authority on the regime of trial for offences under section 195(1)(a) CrPC
records.text: Authority on the regime of trial for offences mentioned in s. 195(1)(a) CrPC. The post gives no further holding. Ref: 2025 LHC 33; Muhammad Asif Atta v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40068/20, decided 15.01.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Asif Atta v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40068/20, decided 15.01.2025)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 181 Limitation Act: Restoration of Civil Revision
records.heading: Article 181 of the Limitation Act applies to restoring a civil revision dismissed in default
records.text: For an application to restore a civil revision dismissed in default, Art. 181 of the Limitation Act applies. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 23, PLD 2024 SC 588; Haji Musharaf Mahmood Khan v. Sardarzada Zafar Abbas (C.P.L.A.423-L/2018).
records.title: Haji Musharaf Mahmood Khan v. Sardarzada Zafar Abbas (C.P.L.A.423-L/2018)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Jactitation of Marriage: Self-Harming Statements
records.heading: A woman's self-harming statement in a jactitation suit carries more weight than the petitioner's evidence
records.text: In a suit for jactitation of marriage where the woman disowns the marriage, her statement that she acted under fear and abuse is critical. Self-harming statements carry more authenticity and weight than the petitioner's evidence, particularly where he had a motive to avoid incriminating charges in a criminal case. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 33, 2025 MLD 114; Muhammad Akhtar Shah v. JFC etc (WP 3022-23).
records.title: Muhammad Akhtar Shah v. JFC etc (WP 3022-23)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Agreement to Sell and Its Contents
records.heading: Specific performance requires proof of valid execution of the agreement and its contents
records.text: To obtain specific performance, the petitioners must prove valid execution of the agreement to sell and establish its contents by primary or secondary evidence. The post lists six modes of proving a document, including calling the signatory or a witness present, a handwriting expert, or comparing disputed with admitted signatures. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 55; Kher Din v. Mst. Hayat Bibi, etc. (C.R. No. 339-D of 2016).
records.title: Kher Din v. Mst. Hayat Bibi, etc. (C.R. No. 339-D of 2016)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Unproved Agreement to Sell: No Declaration of Title
records.heading: An agreement to sell creates no title and a declaration under section 42 was unavailable
records.text: An agreement to sell only creates a right to obtain a title document, and neither a registered deed nor oral sale mutation was executed. The petitioners could not seek a declaration under s. 42 of the Act. They failed to prove execution of the plain-paper agreement or the death of attesting witnesses, so concurrent findings were not disturbed. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 55; Kher Din v. Mst. Hayat Bibi, etc. (C.R. No. 339-D of 2016).
records.title: Kher Din v. Mst. Hayat Bibi, etc. (C.R. No. 339-D of 2016)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CDR Cannot Fix Exact Location of Caller
records.heading: A call data record shows tower range but not the exact location of the caller
records.text: A Call Data Record shows a call made or received on a SIM at a particular time within the range of a cellular tower, but not the exact location of the user. It is not conclusive evidence. Summoning CDR was refused where there was no proof the SIM was registered to the witness or any forensically analysed voice record. Appeal dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 1, 2025 PCrLJ 1184.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recall of Warrants and Proclamation Order by Trial Court
records.heading: A trial court may recall warrants and a proclamation order under section 75 CrPC
records.text: A trial court that issued warrants or declared an accused a proclaimed offender can cancel them under s. 75 CrPC. The purpose of process is to bring the accused before the court, and such an order is not a judgment under s. 369 CrPC. On cogent reasons it can be recalled after the accused surrenders. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 22, 2025 PCrLJ 915; Muhammad Hussain v. State etc (Crl. A. No. 69556 of 2024, decided 06.11.2024); Justice Farooq Haider; Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Hussain v. State etc (Crl. A. No. 69556 of 2024, decided 06.11.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Lalkara and Common Intention
records.heading: Whether a lalkara was commanding and common intention existed needs further inquiry for bail
records.text: Where the petitioner was allegedly armed with a pistol and raised a lalkara but did not fire at the deceased despite opportunity, whether the lalkara was commanding or merely proverbial, and common intention and vicarious liability, need further inquiry for trial under s. 497(2) CrPC. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 26; Zulqarnain v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 43092-B of 2024, decided 24.10.2024); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Zulqarnain v. State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 43092-B of 2024, decided 24.10.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Recalled for Concealing Earlier Dismissal
records.heading: Bail obtained by concealing an earlier dismissal is obtained by foul play and recalled at once
records.text: Bail obtained by concealing the dismissal of an earlier bail application is obtained by foul play and is liable to be recalled at once, irrespective of merits. Here the accused withdrew the first application and filed a second the next day without disclosure, relying on PLD 1986 SC 173, 2002 SCMR 171 and PLD 2014 SC 241. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 30.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Unchallenged Defence Points of Prosecution Witness
records.heading: Points deposed against the prosecution by its own witness and not challenged are taken as not denied
records.text: In a narcotics case, where a prosecution witness deposes against the prosecution on certain points and is neither re-examined nor questioned on them under Art. 150 QSO, those points are taken as not denied by the prosecution. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 35; Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40132/23, heard 13.11.2024); Justice Farooq Haider; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40132/23, heard 13.11.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody of Narcotics and s. 342 CrPC
records.heading: Broken chain of safe custody of narcotics requires acquittal and all evidence must be put under section 342
records.text: An unbroken chain of safe custody of the recovered narcotics and sample parcel must be proved, otherwise conviction is not possible and acquittal follows. All incriminating material must also be put to the accused under s. 342 CrPC. Appeal allowed and the appellant acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 35; Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40132/23, heard 13.11.2024); Justice Farooq Haider; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40132/23, heard 13.11.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Photographs as Evidence: Admissibility
records.heading: Photographs and clips are both documents and real evidence, with Article 139 regulating their use
records.text: Photographs and audio or video clips are both a document and a material thing, also called real evidence. The rules on admissibility of documents apply, with Art. 139 QSO regulating their use. They are produced to prove the information contained in them, with a witness giving the oral account. Nude pictures were held usable as evidence there. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 72, 2025 PCrLJ 589; Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Insurance Policy Proceeds Form Part of Tarka
records.heading: A nominee under the Insurance Ordinance is not exclusive owner and proceeds are tarka
records.text: Under s. 72 of the Insurance Ordinance as discussed, a nomination does not operate as a gift or will, since on the nominee's death the sum goes to the policy holder's heirs. The nominee is not exclusive owner, and all legal heirs of the deceased policy holder take the proceeds as tarka under Muslim law according to their shares. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 40, PLJ 2025 Lah 42; Mst. Razia Begum v. Public at Large etc (Civil Revision 44347/23).
records.title: Mst. Razia Begum v. Public at Large etc (Civil Revision 44347/23)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Cheque Given as Guarantee
records.heading: A cheque issued as a guarantee does not attract section 489-F PPC on tentative assessment
records.text: Not every dishonoured cheque constitutes an offence under s. 489-F PPC. The cheque was issued as a guarantee under a plot agreement and no receipt for the cash amount was produced, so on tentative assessment it was security and not issued towards an obligation. Petition converted into appeal and allowed; pre-arrest bail granted. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 7, 2024 SCMR 1567.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Delay in Trial, Third Proviso s. 497(1)
records.heading: Third proviso to section 497(1) CrPC entitles an accused detained over a year to bail
records.text: Under the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, an accused of an offence not punishable by death is entitled to bail if detained over a year and the trial delay was not caused by him or on his behalf, unless the fourth proviso applies. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 11, 2024 SCMR 1543.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Grounds of Post-Arrest Bail in Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Post-arrest bail in prohibitory clause offences lies on three grounds under section 497
records.text: In prohibitory clause offences, post-arrest bail lies on three grounds. These are the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC (minor, woman, or sick or infirm person), the third proviso (trial delay without fault of the accused), and s. 497(2) CrPC (further inquiry). On tentative assessment the case was not one of further inquiry. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 16, 2025 SCMR 129; Naeem Sajid and others v. State (Crl. P. No. 46 of 2024).
records.title: Naeem Sajid and others v. State (Crl. P. No. 46 of 2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Rule of Consistency in Bail
records.heading: The rule of consistency applies only where the cases of the accused are at par
records.text: The rule of consistency applies only where one accused's case is at par with that of the other accused whose post-arrest bail has been granted. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 16; Naeem Sajid and others v. State (Crl. P. No. 46 of 2024).
records.title: Naeem Sajid and others v. State (Crl. P. No. 46 of 2024)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Proceedings: Non-Fixation of Case, First Order
records.heading: First order in contempt proceedings over non-fixation of a case, with no holding
records.text: First order in contempt proceedings regarding non-fixation of a case before the Court. The post gives no holding. Ref: Matter regarding non-fixation of the case before the Court (Crl.O.P.1/2025, decided 21.01.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Matter regarding non-fixation of the case before the Court (Crl.O.P.1/2025, decided 21.01.2025)

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Contempt Proceedings: Non-Fixation of Case, Second Order
records.heading: Second order in contempt proceedings over non-fixation of a case, with no holding
records.text: Second order in contempt proceedings regarding non-fixation of a case before the Court. The post gives no holding. Ref: Matter regarding non-fixation of the case before the Court (Crl.O.P.1/2025, decided 22.01.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Matter regarding non-fixation of the case before the Court (Crl.O.P.1/2025, decided 22.01.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Deprivation of Females of Inheritance
records.heading: Courts must be vigilant against deprivation of females of inheritance and impose substantial costs
records.text: Legal heirs of a Muslim become owners of the estate on death. Females are often deprived of inheritance through bogus documents and fraud, and courts must be vigilant. Those who do so must pay substantial costs and may not benefit from procedural technicalities. The remand on a technicality was unjustified. Ref: 2025 SCMR 88; Mst. Aksar Jan and others v. Mst. Shamim Akhtar and others (C.P.L.A.4576/2023).
records.title: Mst. Aksar Jan and others v. Mst. Shamim Akhtar and others (C.P.L.A.4576/2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Inquiry Confined to Show Cause Notice
records.heading: A departmental inquiry cannot go beyond the allegations in the show cause notice
records.text: A regular inquiry cannot go beyond the allegations in the show cause notice. The Tribunal relied on a criminal conviction never alleged in the notice, and the inquiry was in substance ex parte. Departmental action must stay within the allegations communicated, as the accused need only answer those. Ref: 2025 SCMR 92; Faisal Ali v. District Police Officer, Gujrat, etc (C.P.L.A.3109-L/2016).
records.title: Faisal Ali v. District Police Officer, Gujrat, etc (C.P.L.A.3109-L/2016)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Suit for Possession With or Without Declaration
records.heading: A plaintiff in possession with disputed title sues for declaration and injunction, otherwise also for possession
records.text: If the plaintiff is in possession but his title is disputed or clouded, or the defendant claims title and threatens dispossession, he must sue for declaration and injunction. If out of possession with a disputed title, he must sue for declaration, possession and injunction. Ref: 2025 SCMR 34; Khurshid Ali and others v. Miangul Adnan Aurangzeb (deceased) through LRs and others (C.As. Nos.493 and 494 of 2023, decided 17.10.2024); Justice Amin ud Din Khan; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Khurshid Ali and others v. Miangul Adnan Aurangzeb (deceased) through LRs and others (C.As. Nos.493 and 494 of 2023, decided 17.10.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Unhurt With Precise Attribution of Injuries
records.heading: An unhurt eyewitness who precisely attributes each injury casts serious doubt on his presence
records.text: A witness who received no firearm injury yet attributed each injury of the deceased and injured to specific accused with specific weapons casts serious doubt on his presence. His explanation of enmity with the accused cannot be ruled out where his testimony lacks independent corroboration on material aspects. Ref: 2025 SCMR 45; Muhammad Akhtar and others, Muhammad Arshad v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 505 to 507 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Akhtar and others, Muhammad Arshad v. The State (Criminal Appeals Nos. 505 to 507 of 2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII R. 4 CPC: Special Circumstances
records.heading: A decree under O. XXXVII R. 4 CPC is set aside only on special circumstances
records.text: Under O. XXXVII R. 4 CPC a decree can be set aside only on special circumstances, which exclude ordinary circumstances, and the defendant bears a heavy burden. The petitioner filed no application for leave to defend, and a bare plea of non-service was rejected as his address in the suit and application was the same. Ref: 2025 SCMR 60, PLJ 2025 SC 134; Muhammad Mansab v. Muhammad Hanif (Civil Petition No.1970-L of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Mansab v. Muhammad Hanif (Civil Petition No.1970-L of 2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Test Identification Parade: Corroborative Value
records.heading: An identification parade is corroborative and not mandatory where identification inspires confidence
records.text: An identification parade is a mode of proof under s. 22 QSO and must be carried out fairly. It is merely corroborative and not mandatory. Not holding one is not fatal where the witness's identification inspires confidence and is consistent, and it is not required when the victim identified the accused reliably. Ref: 2025 SCMR 50; Subha Sadiq v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.786-L/2016).
records.title: Subha Sadiq v. The State, etc (Crl.P.L.A.786-L/2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minority View: Absence of Motive Not Mitigating
records.heading: Minority view that absence of motive is not a mitigating circumstance
records.text: Minority view: absence, non-proof or non-allegation of motive is not a mitigating circumstance, and the death penalty cannot be withheld on that ground alone. Delay in trial and long custody do not justify leniency in a deliberate and brutal murder. Ref: 2025 SCMR 74; Ghulam Rasool v. The State, etc (Crl.A.57/2019).
records.title: Ghulam Rasool v. The State, etc (Crl.A.57/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Majority View: Death Sentence After Prolonged Detention
records.heading: Majority view that the death sentence cannot stand after about 18 years of detention
records.text: Majority view: the appellant had been detained about 18 years, including over eleven years in the death cell, for delay due to the system and no fault of his. Executing the death penalty after that, contrary to the principle of life expectancy, would be harsh, so the death sentence under s. 302(b) PPC cannot sustain. Ref: 2025 SCMR 74; Ghulam Rasool v. The State, etc (Crl.A.57/2019).
records.title: Ghulam Rasool v. The State, etc (Crl.A.57/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Restoration of Suit: Sufficient Cause Required
records.heading: Restoration of a suit dismissed in default needs sufficient cause for non-appearance
records.text: A plaintiff seeking restoration of a suit dismissed in default must show sufficient cause for non-appearance. The costs on which an earlier restoration was conditioned were never paid, and the application gave only vague assertions without a counsel's affidavit. The Trial Court's dismissal was restored. Ref: 2020 CLC 1652.

records.subject: Contempt of Court
records.topic: Committees Cannot Undo Judicial Orders Administratively
records.heading: Committees cannot administratively undo judicial orders or withdraw a part-heard case
records.text: The show cause notice against the Additional Registrar (Judicial) was discharged. Committees under s. 2 of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act and Art. 191A cannot by administrative order undo a judicial order or withdraw a part-heard case unless the Bench refers it. Jurisdictional questions before regular Benches fall outside Art. 191A(3) and (5). Ref: Matter regarding non-fixation of the case before the Court (Crl.O.P.1/2025, decided 27.01.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Matter regarding non-fixation of the case before the Court (Crl.O.P.1/2025, decided 27.01.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Summoning Daily Diary and Register
records.heading: Accused may apply under section 94 CrPC to summon the daily diary and register
records.text: In a narcotics trial, accused sought summoning of the daily diary and Register No. 19 of Moharar Malkhana. At the stage when s. 265-F(7) CrPC applies, they remain at liberty to file applications under s. 94 CrPC even if they do not lead defence evidence, and the trial court must decide them strictly according to law on admissibility and relevancy. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 130.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Postmortem Shows Delayed FIR
records.heading: An unexplained postmortem delay indicates the FIR was recorded later than claimed
records.text: If the FIR was registered within 25 minutes, delay in the postmortem without plausible explanation indicates the FIR was recorded late, not at the time claimed. The FIR therefore cannot be used against the appellant as corroborative evidence. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 22; Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021).
records.title: Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Site Plan Used to Contradict Eyewitnesses
records.heading: A site plan is not substantive evidence but may be used to contradict eyewitnesses
records.text: A site plan is not substantive evidence under Art. 22 QSO, but it shows the crime scene and can be used to contradict or disbelieve eyewitnesses, so that the witnesses could not justify their presence at the spot. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 22; Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021).
records.title: Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Safe Custody of Case Property in Murder Case
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody of case property in a murder case gives the accused the benefit of doubt
records.text: Case property in murder cases must be kept in safe custody from seizure to production in court, with entries in the Malkhana Register on each removal and redeposit. The prosecution must produce the Register abstract. Failure to prove safe custody of the churri gave the benefit of doubt to the accused. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 22; Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021).
records.title: Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconding Creates Only Suspicion
records.heading: Absconding creates only suspicion and is not conclusive proof of guilt
records.text: Absconding creates merely a suspicion and is not conclusive proof of guilt. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 22; Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021).
records.title: Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Guidelines for Implementing Juvenile Justice System Act 2018
records.heading: Guidelines issued for implementing the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018, including interrogation by a Sub-Inspector
records.text: Guidelines issued for swift implementation of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018. Government must implement it fully, juveniles may be interrogated only by an officer not below Sub-Inspector under SP or SDPO supervision with a probation or social welfare officer, and the Prosecutor General Punjab must ensure compliance. Training sessions are advised. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1; Rehana Nazir v. DPO Gujrat etc (WP: 40169/24).
records.title: Rehana Nazir v. DPO Gujrat etc (WP: 40169/24)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Decided Despite Arrest in Another Case
records.heading: A pre-arrest bail petition can be decided in absence despite arrest in another case
records.text: Despite the accused's arrest in another case, his pending petition for pre-arrest bail can be decided on merits in his absence. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 48; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 46363/23).
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 46363/23)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Postmortem
records.heading: An unexplained postmortem delay of over seven hours suggests the police prepared a story
records.text: A postmortem delayed over seven hours from the occurrence without explanation generally suggests that the police used the time to procure eyewitnesses, involve the appellant and prepare a story before preparing the papers for the postmortem. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 109; Kashif Jamal v. State (Criminal Appeal No.865 of 2022).
records.title: Kashif Jamal v. State (Criminal Appeal No.865 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification at Night: Source of Light
records.heading: Night identification at about 88 feet without a disclosed source of light is doubtful
records.text: Identification of the appellant at night at about 88 to 90 feet, while he was facing away from the eyewitnesses, was doubtful. Later recovery of a bulb does not prove it was lit at the time unless the eyewitness disclosed the source of light in the FIR and in examination-in-chief. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 109; Kashif Jamal v. State (Criminal Appeal No.865 of 2022).
records.title: Kashif Jamal v. State (Criminal Appeal No.865 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Eyewitnesses
records.heading: Dishonest improvements by eyewitnesses shatter credibility and negate their presence
records.text: The complainant and another eyewitness improved their accounts after confrontation with their police statements, for example from one fire shot to two to match the medical evidence. Such dishonest improvements shatter credibility and negate their presence at the relevant time. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 109; Kashif Jamal v. State (Criminal Appeal No.865 of 2022).
records.title: Kashif Jamal v. State (Criminal Appeal No.865 of 2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial and Administrative Orders Distinguished
records.heading: The distinction between judicial and administrative orders must be strictly adhered to
records.text: The distinction between judicial and administrative orders must be strictly adhered to. The sanctity of judicial orders must be preserved, and they cannot be overlooked, contravened or evaded by anyone. Ref: Federation of Pakistan through Revenue Division & others v. Dewan Motors (Pvt) Ltd (C.P.L.A.836-K/2020, decided 27.01.2025); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through Revenue Division & others v. Dewan Motors (Pvt) Ltd (C.P.L.A.836-K/2020, decided 27.01.2025)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Vagrancy Ordinance Distinguished from PTPA
records.heading: The Vagrancy Ordinance applies to beggary alone, while the PTPA needs coercion, fraud or exploitation
records.text: Section 3 of the PTPA applies where coercion, fraud or exploitation by a third party is involved. Without such elements the Vagrancy Ordinance may apply, and the two must not be conflated. Beggary alone is outside the PTPA. Under s. 3 PPC, Pakistanis begging abroad may still be dealt with under domestic law. Ref: 2024 LHC 6351; Sadiq Hussain etc v. Deputy Director FIA etc (Writ Petition 12935-24, decided 17.12.2024); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Sadiq Hussain etc v. Deputy Director FIA etc (Writ Petition 12935-24, decided 17.12.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Chain of Links
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form a continuous chain and any missing link benefits the accused
records.text: Where the prosecution case rests on circumstantial evidence, utmost care is required. Every circumstance must link into a continuous chain from the dead body to the accused's neck, and if any link is missing the benefit goes to the accused. Ref: 2025 SCP 22; Sikandar Ali @ Bhola v. The State (J.P.29/2021, decided 13.01.2025); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Sikandar Ali @ Bhola v. The State (J.P.29/2021, decided 13.01.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Party Bound by Counsel's Withdrawal of Application
records.heading: A party is bound by his counsel's withdrawal of an application under a wakalatnama
records.text: By signing a wakalatnama, powers including withdrawal of a suit or application are delegated to counsel, and a party is bound by his counsel's statement unless the authority is restricted. The petitioner had withdrawn his application under s. 9(6) Family Courts Act to set aside an ex parte decree, so he acquiesced in it and was bound. Ref: 2025 SCP 21; Muhammad Ejaz v. Judge Family Court, Hafizabad, etc (C.P.L.A.2759-L/2023, decided 14.01.2025); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Ejaz v. Judge Family Court, Hafizabad, etc (C.P.L.A.2759-L/2023, decided 14.01.2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Plaintiff Must Succeed on Own Title
records.heading: A plaintiff in a suit for possession must succeed on the strength of his own title
records.text: The plaintiffs and those under whom they claimed had no title, and the gift of the shops never existed. A plaintiff in a suit for possession must succeed on the strength of his own title and cannot rely on defects in the defendants' title. The suit was dismissed and the Trial Court's decree restored. Ref: 2025 SCMR 34; Khurshid Ali and others v. Miangul Adnan Aurangzeb (deceased) through LRs and others (C.As. Nos.493 and 494 of 2023, decided 17.10.2024); Justice Amin ud Din Khan; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Khurshid Ali and others v. Miangul Adnan Aurangzeb (deceased) through LRs and others (C.As. Nos.493 and 494 of 2023, decided 17.10.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Weapon on Accused's Disclosure
records.heading: Weapon recovery was inconsequential where the forensic report did not show the sealed parcel was submitted
records.text: Recovery of the churri on the accused's pointing was inconsequential, as the forensic report did not show the sealed parcel was submitted and the property was released to the Investigating Officer before the swabs were examined. It was unclear which property was analysed. The prosecution failed to prove the charge and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 22; Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021).
records.title: Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Ocular account of front blows contradicted by medical findings of back injuries discredited the witnesses
records.text: The witnesses said a co-accused held the deceased while the accused struck churri blows on his neck and arm, but the Medical Officer found injuries on the back and none from the front. This contradiction with medical evidence went to the core of the prosecution case and discredited the witnesses. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 22; Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021).
records.title: Babar alias Jani v. The State (Murder Reference No.103 of 2021; Crl. Appeal No.43616-J of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Questions to Draftsman on Site Plan of Recovery
records.heading: The defence may not question a draftsman on a site plan he did not author
records.text: The draftsman was not the author of the site plan of the place of recovery, nor the witness on whose pointing it was made, nor an attesting witness. The trial court's refusal to allow the defence to question him on it, as irrelevant, was held sound and reasonable. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 201, PLJ 2025 CrC 129; Ali Zain v. State.
records.title: Ali Zain v. State

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Mutation Entries Remain Until Validly Substituted
records.heading: A revenue entry remains until substituted by a court decree or valid mutation
records.text: A revenue record entry remains in the field unless substituted by a court decree or a valid mutation attestation correcting rights. If entries are found unlawfully changed, the old entries are deemed to continue. Ref: 2025 SCMR 174; Muhammad Ramzan v. Member (Judicial-II) Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Member (Judicial-II) Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Shamlat Deh: Ala and Adna Maaliks
records.heading: Adna Maaliks in possession of Shamlat Deh land may claim proprietorship under MLR 64
records.text: Appellants were Adna Maaliks in possession of Shamlat Deh land and claimed ownership under MLR 64 and the 1960 Notification, relying on the Ladhoo v. B.O.R. judgments. Respondents were Ala Maaliks. The Supreme Court held the appellants' proprietorship claim based on possession was backed by law and in accordance with Supreme Court judgments. Ref: 2025 SCMR 174; Muhammad Ramzan v. Member (Judicial-II) Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Member (Judicial-II) Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance: Pending Suit Cannot Deprive Heirs
records.heading: Property of a deceased Muslim vests in the heirs and a pending partition suit does not exclude them
records.text: Property of a deceased Muslim vests in the legal heirs on death, and a pending partition suit neither affects the estate nor excludes heirs. The brother's frivolous petition was dismissed with costs of Rs. 300,000, payable equally to the sisters, who may also claim mesne profits. Ref: 2025 SCMR 98; Tanvir Sarfraz Khan v. Federation of Pakistan.
records.title: Tanvir Sarfraz Khan v. Federation of Pakistan

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay: Appeal Entertained Without Jurisdiction
records.heading: A litigant misled by the court on jurisdiction cannot be wholly blamed for resulting delay
records.text: Where a party acting with reasonable diligence is misled by the Court, or lacks timely guidance on jurisdiction, the resulting delay or error is not wholly attributable to that party. Where both the litigant and the court contributed, the litigant who approached the wrong forum cannot be deprived of legal rights. Ref: 2025 SCMR 64; Ufaid Gul v. Mst. Farkhanda Ayub Khan.
records.title: Ufaid Gul v. Mst. Farkhanda Ayub Khan

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Discretionary Relief
records.heading: A decree for specific performance is discretionary even where the agreement to sell is proved
records.text: A decree for specific performance is discretionary. It may be granted if equity leans in favour of the plaintiff, and even where the agreement to sell is proved the court may refuse the decree. Ref: 2025 SCMR 64; Ufaid Gul v. Mst. Farkhanda Ayub Khan.
records.title: Ufaid Gul v. Mst. Farkhanda Ayub Khan

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed FIR: Tampering With Police Station Record
records.heading: Prompt registration of an FIR must be examined with circumspection because station records can be tampered with
records.text: The Court observed that prompt registration of an FIR must be examined with circumspection, because police station records are prone to tampering, including holding back the FIR register and station diary so that a delayed report appears prompt. Such a practice allows witness statements to be adjusted to the medical evidence. Ref: 2024 LHC 6372; Sadaqat & another v. The State & another (Crl. Appeal 180/2021).
records.title: Sadaqat & another v. The State & another (Crl. Appeal 180/2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Duty of State Functionaries to Enforce Law
records.heading: Enforcement of a statute is a mandatory duty of every state functionary
records.text: Enforcement of a statute is a mandatory duty of every state functionary. Failure to implement law violates fundamental rights, and functionaries responsible for such negligence must be held accountable. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1; Rehana Nazir v. District Police Officer, Gujrat.
records.title: Rehana Nazir v. District Police Officer, Gujrat

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Theory Based on CCTV Footage
records.heading: Supreme Court of India authority on last seen theory resting on CCTV footage
records.text: Supreme Court of India authority on the last seen theory where it rests on CCTV footage, and on the circumstances in which such footage does not amount to last seen together evidence. The post gives no further holding. Ref: Chandrabhan Sudam Sanap v. The State of Maharashtra (Criminal Appeal 879 of 2019, decided 28.01.2025).
records.title: Chandrabhan Sudam Sanap v. The State of Maharashtra (Criminal Appeal 879 of 2019, decided 28.01.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension: Counting Contractual Period Under CSR 371-A
records.heading: A contractual period under five years followed by regularisation without gap counts towards pension
records.text: Under clause (ii) of Art. 371-A CSR, a contractual period of less than five years counts towards pension if it is followed immediately by regularisation without gap. The respondent's 4 1/2 years of contract service was continuous with regularisation, so the Service Tribunal rightly allowed his appeal. Ref: 2025 SCMR 168, 2025 PLC (C.S.) 319; Chairman/Dean Sheikh Zayed Hospital, Lahore v. Amjad Mehmood Khan.
records.title: Chairman/Dean Sheikh Zayed Hospital, Lahore v. Amjad Mehmood Khan

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Art. 212: Exclusive Jurisdiction of Service Tribunal
records.heading: Article 212 bars civil courts in service disputes even where mala fides or want of jurisdiction is alleged
records.text: The bar in Art. 212 of the Constitution applies to disputes over terms and conditions of service even where mala fides, coram non judice or want of jurisdiction is alleged. A civil servant cannot avoid the Tribunal by pleading violation of fundamental rights, and challenges to the vires of a statutory rule or notification also fall within the Tribunal's jurisdiction. Ref: 2025 SCMR 134; Muhammad Hassanullah v. Chief Secretary.
records.title: Muhammad Hassanullah v. Chief Secretary

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Quota for Sons of Retired Employees Unconstitutional
records.heading: Reserving seats or preferring children of government servants offends Articles 25 and 27
records.text: Preferring the children of government servants, or reserving seats for them, offends the prohibition of discrimination in Art. 25 and the principle of Art. 27 of the Constitution. It also detracts from merit based employment. Ref: 2025 PLC (C.S.) 34; Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa v. Tahir Mushtaq.
records.title: Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa v. Tahir Mushtaq

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Partition Proceedings and Questions of Title
records.heading: The Revenue Officer may decide questions of title in partition after hearing the parties under section 141
records.text: Where co-sharers agree on a private partition scheme, the Revenue Officer affirms it under s. 135-A of the Punjab Land Revenue Act. Otherwise he must commence and complete partition within thirty days. If a question of title arises, he may decide it after hearing the parties under s. 141 of the Act. Ref: 2025 MLD 31; Ch. Muhammad Naeem & 3 Others v. Member Judicial BOR Punjab etc (WP 59198/24).
records.title: Ch. Muhammad Naeem & 3 Others v. Member Judicial BOR Punjab etc (WP 59198/24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Malicious Prosecution: Essential Ingredients
records.heading: Malicious prosecution requires malice, absence of probable cause, termination in favour and damage, all coexisting
records.text: A plaintiff must prove malice, absence of reasonable and probable cause, prosecution on a criminal charge, termination in his favour, interference with liberty and reputation, and damage, and all must coexist. Malice alone is insufficient, and a prosecutor who honestly believes in guilt is not liable merely because he acted in anger. Ref: 2025 MLD 77; Afzaal Ahmed v. Sadia Safdar and another (R.F.A. 52942/2022).
records.title: Afzaal Ahmed v. Sadia Safdar and another (R.F.A. 52942/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Malicious Prosecution: General and Special Damages
records.heading: Damages for malicious prosecution comprise general damages and special damages
records.text: A claim for damages for malicious prosecution has two facets, general damages and special damages. General damages arise from the immediate and direct result of the wrong, while special damages follow from particular circumstances of the case. Ref: 2025 MLD 77; Afzaal Ahmed v. Sadia Safdar and another (R.F.A. 52942/2022).
records.title: Afzaal Ahmed v. Sadia Safdar and another (R.F.A. 52942/2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Readiness and Willingness: Deposit of Balance Consideration
records.heading: A plaintiff who never applied to deposit the balance consideration failed to show readiness and willingness
records.text: Although the plaintiff pleaded readiness and willingness, he never applied to the Trial Court to deposit the balance sale consideration, which was needed to substantiate his claim. The Trial Court's finding against him on readiness and willingness was not interfered with. Ref: 2025 MLD 158; Amir Sajjad v. Ghulam Murtaza (Civil Revision 15213/23).
records.title: Amir Sajjad v. Ghulam Murtaza (Civil Revision 15213/23)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secondary Evidence of Agreement to Sell: Art. 76
records.heading: Secondary evidence of an agreement to sell is barred without notice to produce under Article 76
records.text: The plaintiff had to produce the original agreement to sell, or follow Art. 76 QSO for secondary evidence if the original was with the respondent. Failing to serve a notice to produce, or to seek admission and denial under Order XII CPC, barred secondary evidence, and dismissal of the suit for specific performance was upheld. Ref: 2025 MLD 158; Amir Sajjad v. Ghulam Murtaza (Civil Revision 15213/23).
records.title: Amir Sajjad v. Ghulam Murtaza (Civil Revision 15213/23)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Conflicting Judgments: Appellate Court Preferred
records.heading: Where trial and appellate courts differ, the appellate court's view is preferred
records.text: Where the trial court and the appellate court differ, the view of the appellate court is given preference and weight. Ref: 2025 MLD 158; Amir Sajjad v. Ghulam Murtaza (Civil Revision 15213/23).
records.title: Amir Sajjad v. Ghulam Murtaza (Civil Revision 15213/23)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Revocation of Power of Attorney: Notice to Agent
records.heading: Revoking a power of attorney without notice to the agent is illegal under the Contract Act
records.text: Under ss. 202 and 206 of the Contract Act, 1872, the principal must give notice to the agent before cancelling a power of attorney, and revocation without notice is illegal. The petitioners also failed to discharge the burden of proving valid execution of the revocation deed. Ref: 2025 CLC 168; Syed Monis Raza etc v. Mst. Asia Bano etc (Civil Revision 314-15).
records.title: Syed Monis Raza etc v. Mst. Asia Bano etc (Civil Revision 314-15)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Challenge to Mutation: Locus Standi, Waiver and Acquiescence
records.heading: Petitioners cannot challenge a mutation their predecessor never challenged, owing to waiver and acquiescence
records.text: Petitioners had no locus standi to challenge a mutation that their predecessor never challenged in his lifetime. Their own inaction also attracted waiver, estoppel and acquiescence, as implied consent amounted to abandonment of rights. Ref: 2025 CLC 168; Syed Monis Raza etc v. Mst. Asia Bano etc (Civil Revision 314-15).
records.title: Syed Monis Raza etc v. Mst. Asia Bano etc (Civil Revision 314-15)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 31 CPC: Contents of Appellate Judgment
records.heading: Substantial compliance with O. XLI R. 31 CPC saves a brief but pertinent appellate judgment
records.text: O. XLI R. 31 CPC requires the appellate judgment to state the points for determination, the decision, the reasons and any relief. Non-compliance can be fatal but is ignored where there is substantial compliance. Here the brief but pertinent reasoning substantially complied and revision failed. Ref: 2025 CLC 32; Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849 of 2011).
records.title: Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849 of 2011)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Restitution Suit: Wife May Raise Family Court Claims
records.heading: A wife resisting restitution may raise Family Courts Act claims and the husband may file a rejoinder
records.text: A wife resisting a suit for restitution of conjugal rights may raise any permissible claim under the Family Courts Act, 1964. The Family Court must then allow the husband to file a rejoinder, which is treated as his written statement. Ref: 2025 CLC 5; Nasir Sharif v. Sabeela Imtiaz etc (Wp 4132-23).
records.title: Nasir Sharif v. Sabeela Imtiaz etc (Wp 4132-23)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Readiness and Willingness: Proof of Funds and Tender
records.heading: The buyer must prove readiness and willingness through funds and tender, failing which specific performance is refused
records.text: The buyer must prove readiness and willingness from the date of agreement through the suit, including funds for the balance and efforts to pay shown by banking instruments or deposit. Where he did not do so, specific performance cannot be granted. Evidence on previous litigation outside the pleadings was inadmissible. Ref: 2025 CLC 196; Ghulam Hassan etc v. Ijaz Naseer etc (R.F.A 67289/19).
records.title: Ghulam Hassan etc v. Ijaz Naseer etc (R.F.A 67289/19)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Discretion Under s. 22 Specific Relief Act
records.heading: Specific performance under section 22 is discretionary and needs proof of readiness and willingness
records.text: Under s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, a decree for specific performance is discretionary and is not granted merely because it is lawful to do so.
