The discretion must be exercised on sound judicial principles, and the buyer must prove readiness and willingness to pay the balance consideration. Ref: 2025 CLC 196; Ghulam Hassan etc v. Ijaz Naseer etc (R.F.A 67289/19).
records.title: Ghulam Hassan etc v. Ijaz Naseer etc (R.F.A 67289/19)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 102 and 103 QSO: Oral Evidence Against Written Terms
records.heading: Oral evidence cannot add to, contradict or vary the written terms of a contract
records.text: Under Art. 102 QSO, where the terms of a contract have been reduced to writing, no evidence may prove those terms except the document itself or permitted secondary evidence. Art. 103 excludes oral evidence that adds to, subtracts from, contradicts or varies the written terms. Ref: 2025 CLC 196; Ghulam Hassan etc v. Ijaz Naseer etc (R.F.A 67289/19).
records.title: Ghulam Hassan etc v. Ijaz Naseer etc (R.F.A 67289/19)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Uncertain Land Description: s. 21(c) Specific Relief Act
records.heading: Specific performance is refused where the land is not identified with reasonable certainty
records.text: Under s. 21(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, specific performance is refused where the contract terms cannot be found with reasonable certainty. An agreement to sell land must identify it by khewat, khatauni and khasra or killa numbers, failing which it is unenforceable. Ref: 2025 CLC 196; Ghulam Hassan etc v. Ijaz Naseer etc (R.F.A 67289/19).
records.title: Ghulam Hassan etc v. Ijaz Naseer etc (R.F.A 67289/19)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Free Medical Treatment for Advocates in Government Hospitals
records.heading: Practising advocates and dependents must receive free treatment in government hospitals on a Bar Council card
records.text: The Court directed the respondents to implement Notification No. SO(H&D)7-1/2018(MISC) across DHQ, THQ and RHC facilities. Practising advocates and their dependents, and advocates on government panels, must receive free treatment on par with BPS 17 and 18 officers on showing a Punjab Bar Council card. Ref: 2025 LHC 142; Adnan Mughal v. Government of Punjab etc (WP 1778-24, decided 14.01.2025); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Adnan Mughal v. Government of Punjab etc (WP 1778-24, decided 14.01.2025)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Wastewater Treatment Plant, Climate Change and Fundamental Rights
records.heading: Importance of a wastewater treatment plant for climate change and fundamental rights, with no holding
records.text: Judgment addressing the importance of a wastewater treatment plant in the context of climate change, climate finance and fundamental rights, and stressing preference for homegrown solutions. The post gives no further holding. Ref: Syed Ali Hussain etc v. Senior Member/Member (Revenue) Board of Revenue Punjab, Lahore etc (C.P.L.A.2918-L/2015, decided 31.01.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Syed Ali Hussain etc v. Senior Member/Member (Revenue) Board of Revenue Punjab, Lahore etc (C.P.L.A.2918-L/2015, decided 31.01.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Malafide Inferred From Circumstances
records.heading: Malafide is often inferred from facts and circumstances and need not be directly proved
records.text: Malafide cannot always be proved by direct evidence and is often inferred from the facts and circumstances of the case. Ref: Muhammad Saeed v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A.588/2024, decided 03.02.2025); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Muhammad Saeed v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A.588/2024, decided 03.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Duty of IO to Send Recovered Weapon for Forensics
records.heading: The Investigating Officer must send the recovered weapon for forensic examination
records.text: It was the responsibility of the Investigating Officer to present the recovered sota for forensic examination, to establish that the blows on the deceased were caused by it or to find blood or other evidence that could have strengthened the prosecution story. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1085, PLJ 2024 SC CrC 178; Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl. P. No. 887-L of 2013).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Khizar Hayat (Crl. P. No. 887-L of 2013)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR for Non-Cognizable Offence: Course to Follow
records.heading: On an FIR for a non-cognizable offence, police may file a cancellation report and the Magistrate may act
records.text: Considers the legislative history of the book referred to in s. 154 CrPC and the course open where an FIR is registered for a non-cognizable offence. Holds that police may prepare a cancellation report under Rule 24.7, and that the Magistrate may require a bond under s. 91 CrPC or commit the accused to custody under s. 351 CrPC, relying on 2024 PCrLJ 977. Ref: 2024 LHC 6439; Muhammad Ahsan v. The State etc (WP 25543/24, decided 18.12.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Ahsan v. The State etc (WP 25543/24, decided 18.12.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Belated Production of Agreement in Revision
records.heading: Belated production of an agreement in revision was an attempt to fill a lacuna
records.text: The defendants pleaded an agreement but did not produce it at trial or in appeal, and applied to produce it only in 2020, with witnesses unmentioned in the pleadings. The application was treated as an attempt to fill a lacuna and prolong proceedings, and no infirmity in the District Court judgment was shown. Ref: 2025 CLC 32; Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849 of 2011).
records.title: Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849 of 2011)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Bargain: Deficient Pleading and Proof
records.heading: An oral bargain defence failed for deficient pleading and proof of witnesses, time and place
records.text: The written statement was silent on the witnesses, time and place of the alleged oral bargain, and the defence was raised only in preliminary objections with evasive denials. A later witness, said to be a tenant, did not fill the gap, so the defence failed. Ref: 2025 CLC 32; Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849 of 2011).
records.title: Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849 of 2011)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Proof of Mutation: Lambardar and Patidar Not Produced
records.heading: Genuineness of a mutation was not proved without producing its lambardar and patidar witnesses
records.text: The mutation was witnessed by a lambardar and a patidar, whom the defendants did not produce. The lambardar appeared for the plaintiff and denied his signatures, and there was no explanation for not producing the patidar, so genuineness of the mutation was not proved. Ref: 2025 CLC 32; Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849 of 2011).
records.title: Nazir Ahmad & another v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 849 of 2011)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Leave to Defend in Summary Suits
records.heading: In a summary suit, the defendant must show a plausible defence to obtain leave to defend
records.text: Under O. XXXVII R. 2 CPC a defendant in a summary suit must first show a plausible defence to obtain leave. Without leave, the plaint allegations are deemed admitted and the plaintiff is entitled to a decree. Once leave is granted, the ordinary procedure applies, including the requirement of specific denial in O. VIII. Ref: 2025 LHC 175; Abdul Ghaffar v. Umar Farooq (RFA 27-20, decided 27.01.2025); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Abdul Ghaffar v. Umar Farooq (RFA 27-20, decided 27.01.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Remand in Appeals From Original Decree
records.heading: A case is remanded where a decree is reversed in appeal and re-trial is necessary
records.text: Under O. XLI Rr. 23, 23-A and O. XLII R. 1 CPC, a case is remanded when a decree is reversed in appeal and a re-trial is considered necessary. Ref: 2025 CLC 177; Mst. Shahida Parveen v. Muhammad Akram Baig.
records.title: Mst. Shahida Parveen v. Muhammad Akram Baig

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Additional Evidence in Appeal: O. XLI R. 27 and 28
records.heading: The appellate court must itself decide an application for additional evidence with reasons under Rule 27
records.text: Legal notices listed in the list of reliance under O. VII R. 14 CPC were allowed as additional evidence in appeal. The appellate court must itself decide the application with reasons within R. 27, and may record the evidence itself or direct the trial court to do so. Its effect is for the appellate court to consider. Ref: 2025 CLC 177; Mst. Shahida Parveen v. Muhammad Akram Baig.
records.title: Mst. Shahida Parveen v. Muhammad Akram Baig

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Inconsistent Findings: Appellate Court Preferred
records.heading: Where findings are inconsistent, the appellate court's findings are preferred absent cogent reason
records.text: Where trial and appellate findings are inconsistent, the findings of the appellate court must be preferred in the absence of a cogent reason to the contrary. Ref: 2025 CLC 140; Abdul Karim v. Mst. Ruqqia Begum.
records.title: Abdul Karim v. Mst. Ruqqia Begum

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift by Attorney: Scope and Proof
records.heading: An attorney cannot gift the principal's property without the principal's direction and clear authority
records.text: An attorney cannot gift property without the principal's intention and direction, and the document lacked a clear gifting clause. It was not proved under Art. 79 QSO as a second marginal witness was not produced, and an adverse presumption arose under Art. 129(g). The donee did not prove when, where and before whom the offer was made. Ref: 2025 CLC 140; Abdul Karim v. Mst. Ruqqia Begum.
records.title: Abdul Karim v. Mst. Ruqqia Begum

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation: Burden on Beneficiary
records.heading: A mutation is not a deed of title and the beneficiary must prove it and the original transaction
records.text: A mutation is not a deed of title and merely indicates an earlier oral transaction. When it is challenged, the beneficiary bears the burden of proving both the mutation and the original transaction. Ref: 2025 CLC 140; Abdul Karim v. Mst. Ruqqia Begum.
records.title: Abdul Karim v. Mst. Ruqqia Begum

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Postmortem Casts Doubt on FIR
records.heading: A delayed postmortem leads to the inference that the FIR was lodged late
records.text: A delayed postmortem leads to the inference that the FIR was lodged late after deliberation and consultation about implicating the accused and planting eyewitnesses. The Supreme Court in Sufyan Nawaz extended the benefit of doubt for a ten hour delay in autopsy. Ref: PLJ 2024 CrC 252, 2025 YLR 116; Khalil Ahmad and 2 others v. State (Crl. A. No. 78847-J, M.R. No. 375 of 2019, heard 14.9.2023); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch.; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Khalil Ahmad and 2 others v. State (Crl. A. No. 78847-J, M.R. No. 375 of 2019, heard 14.9.2023)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: s. 5 Illegal Dispossession Act: Inquiry and Investigation
records.heading: On a complaint under section 5 of the Illegal Dispossession Act, the Court directs police investigation
records.text: On a complaint under s. 5 of the Act, the Court may direct the officer in charge of the police station to investigate within a fixed period. Chapter 25 of the Police Rules, 1934 then applies, including statements under s. 161 CrPC, plea of the accused, site inspection and plan. On completion, a report under s. 173 CrPC goes to the Court, which then issues process or dismisses the complaint. Ref: 2025 YLR 62; Noor Khan etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 2454/22).
records.title: Noor Khan etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 2454/22)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Recovery Memo: Object and Requirements
records.heading: A recovery memo is a foundational document that must identify the seized articles beyond doubt
records.text: A recovery memo is a foundational document prepared at the spot and attested by witnesses to ensure a fair recovery and exclude fabrication or false implication. It must contain particulars identifying the seized articles beyond doubt, and it is also needed to prove the prosecution case at trial. Ref: 2025 YLR 75, PLJ 2025 CrC 207; Nayyar Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 549-23).
records.title: Nayyar Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 549-23)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Doubtful Recovery Memo of Charas
records.heading: A charas recovery memo lacking basic particulars and prepared after the FIR was doubtful
records.text: The memo for 2250 grams of charas lacked the FIR number, date, police station and place of recovery, and the recovery witness could not recall the FIR number. It appeared to have been prepared after the FIR, so the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2025 YLR 75; Nayyar Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 549-23).
records.title: Nayyar Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 549-23)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Self-Cheque and s. 489-F PPC
records.heading: A self-cheque where the drawer is also the payee attracts no offence under section 489-F PPC
records.text: A self-cheque, where the drawer is also the payee, attracts no offence under s. 489-F PPC, since a person cannot dishonestly pay himself or owe himself an obligation. A cheque payable to self or bearer may found action by a holder in due course under s. 9 NIA who proves the elements. An FIR is registered under s. 154 CrPC without testing the allegations. Ref: 2025 YLR 86; Tariq Mehmood v. ASJ JOP etc (Criminal Proceedings 68498/22).
records.title: Tariq Mehmood v. ASJ JOP etc (Criminal Proceedings 68498/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: PFSA Mandate and Duty to Dispatch Material
records.heading: The duty to dispatch articles for analysis lies with the police and not PFSA experts
records.text: The PFSA assists police in collecting and packaging articles with biological stains or fingerprints, and does not take them away for analysis. It is the legal duty of the police, and not of PFSA experts, to dispatch articles for analysis, and a breach of custody protocols makes the police liable under ss. 166 and 186(2) PPC. Ref: 2025 YLR 197, PLJ 2024 CrC 943; Muhammad Umar etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 58520/20).
records.title: Muhammad Umar etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 58520/20)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification of Recovered Articles Before Magistrate
records.heading: Identification of recovered articles must be conducted by a Magistrate with the property kept sealed
records.text: Identification of recovered articles must be conducted by a Magistrate in the same manner as for suspects, with evidentiary value governed by Art. 22 QSO. Witnesses must have had no chance to see the property after recovery, so it must be sealed on recovery and kept sealed until produced, with the result entered in the Magistrate's own hand. Ref: 2025 YLR 197, PLJ 2024 CrC 943; Muhammad Umar etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 58520/20).
records.title: Muhammad Umar etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 58520/20)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Investigating Officer at Murder Scene: PFSA and DNA Sampling
records.heading: Steps the investigating officer should take at a murder scene, including PFSA and DNA sampling
records.text: Described as an informative judgment on the steps the investigating officer should take after reaching a murder scene, covering the role of the PFSA team, circumstantial evidence and DNA sampling under the Police Rules and PFSA regulations. Ref: 2025 YLR 197, PLJ 2024 CrC 943; Muhammad Umar etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 58520/20).
records.title: Muhammad Umar etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 58520/20)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Objections to Documents: Admissibility and Mode of Proof
records.heading: An objection to mode of proof must be raised when the document is marked, or it is waived
records.text: Objections are of two kinds, inadmissibility in evidence and defects in mode of proof. An objection to mode of proof must be raised before or when the document is marked as an exhibit, failing which waiver applies. Failure to object to inadmissibility, however, is not fatal. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 124; Mst. Afia Ambrine v. Addl. District Judge, Sialkot and 14 Others (Writ Petition 10608 of 2024).
records.title: Mst. Afia Ambrine v. Addl. District Judge, Sialkot and 14 Others (Writ Petition 10608 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Exhibiting Documents Through Advocates' Unsworn Statements
records.heading: Exhibiting documents through advocates' unsworn statements deprives the opponent of cross-examination and breaches the QSO
records.text: Receiving documents through unsworn statements of advocates and marking them as exhibits deprives the opponent of cross-examination and breaches the QSO. Orders to exhibit and then de-exhibit, passed in haste in s. 12(2) CPC proceedings, should have been corrected by the revisional court by allowing an opportunity to cure the mistake. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 124; Mst. Afia Ambrine v. Addl. District Judge, Sialkot and 14 Others (Writ Petition 10608 of 2024).
records.title: Mst. Afia Ambrine v. Addl. District Judge, Sialkot and 14 Others (Writ Petition 10608 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Investigation Under Art. 18A Police Order 2002
records.heading: Transfer of investigation under Article 18A is ordered to find the truth, not to oblige a party
records.text: Art. 18A of the Police Order, 2002 empowers the Head of District Police, the Regional Police Officer and the Provincial Police Officer to transfer investigation. It is ordered where further relevant material is required to find the truth, not to oblige one party for an ulterior motive. Re-investigation or further investigation may follow conclusion of a private complaint. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 137; Dilshad Akbar v. Inspector General of Police, Punjab, Lahore & others (Writ Petition 18153 of 2022).
records.title: Dilshad Akbar v. Inspector General of Police, Punjab, Lahore & others (Writ Petition 18153 of 2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Non-Deposit of Balance Amount: Effect
records.heading: A suit cannot be dismissed for non-deposit of the balance amount at the stage of plaintiff's evidence
records.text: A suit fixed for plaintiff's evidence cannot be dismissed for non-deposit of the balance amount. Before acting under O. XVII R. 3 CPC the court must be satisfied that the party failed to comply despite reasonable time, and may extend time. The Specific Relief Act, 1877 has no provision compelling the plaintiff to deposit the balance consideration. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 171, PLJ 2025 Civil Note 25; Nasir Mahmood v. Zafar Iqbal etc (CR 49002/21).
records.title: Nasir Mahmood v. Zafar Iqbal etc (CR 49002/21)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of FIR: Partial Quashing Not Permissible
records.heading: Partial quashing of an FIR for one accused is not permissible
records.text: Partial quashing of an FIR for one accused is not permissible. The High Court may quash an FIR only in exceptional circumstances, such as allegations disclosing no cognizable offence, false allegations, civil liability converted into a criminal case, or an express legal bar. It cannot take the role of the investigating agency under Art. 199 or s. 561-A CrPC. Ref: PLD 2025 Pesh 36.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Stale Cheque: s. 489-F PPC and s. 249-A CrPC
records.heading: A stale cheque presented after six months does not attract section 489-F PPC
records.text: Under s. 84(1) NIA a cheque must be presented within a reasonable time, and one presented beyond six months is generally stale. A cheque issued in 2018 and presented in 2021, returned as stale, did not attract s. 489-F PPC. The application under s. 249-A CrPC for acquittal was allowed. Ref: PLD 2025 Kar 63.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Habeas Corpus for Minors: Interim Custody Only
records.heading: Habeas corpus for minors is limited to interim custody, leaving final custody to the Family Court
records.text: The High Court may issue habeas corpus under Art. 199(1)(b)(i) and s. 491 CrPC for minors, but only sparingly in exceptional cases such as very young children recently removed from lawful custody. Its role is limited to interim custody, leaving final custody to the Family Court, and it may intervene in international child abduction. Ref: 2024 LHC 6486; Syed Hassan Murtaza v. Mariya Bano Khan etc (WP 78185/23, decided 24.05.2024); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Syed Hassan Murtaza v. Mariya Bano Khan etc (WP 78185/23, decided 24.05.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: High Court Certiorari Jurisdiction in Family Cases
records.heading: The High Court may issue certiorari to correct jurisdictional errors of Family Courts but cannot act as appellate body
records.text: Under Art. 199(1)(a)(ii) the High Court may issue certiorari to correct jurisdictional errors of Family Courts and first appellate courts, or illegal or improper exercise of jurisdiction including denial of hearing. This jurisdiction is supervisory and the High Court cannot act as an appellate body. Ref: Muhammad Shakeel and others v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and others (C.P.L.A.4582/2023, decided 14.02.2025); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Muhammad Shakeel and others v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and others (C.P.L.A.4582/2023, decided 14.02.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 540 CrPC: Recalling Witness to Exhibit Documents
records.heading: Recalling the initial investigating officer to exhibit documents under section 540 CrPC did not fill a lacuna
records.text: Under s. 540 CrPC the court may summon or recall any witness whose evidence is essential for a just decision, but not to fill a lacuna. Re-summoning the initial investigating officer, who had omitted the early investigation in his evidence, to exhibit the documents he prepared was held not to fill a lacuna and caused no prejudice to the accused. Ref: Zeeshan Tahir, etc. v. Rafaqat Ali, etc. (Criminal Revision 134 of 2024, decided 27.01.2025).
records.title: Zeeshan Tahir, etc. v. Rafaqat Ali, etc. (Criminal Revision 134 of 2024, decided 27.01.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Review: Error on the Face of the Record
records.heading: Review lies only for an error apparent on the face of the record
records.text: Judicial orders and judgments carry a presumption of correctness and are challenged by appeal or revision. In exceptional cases they may be reviewed under O. XLVII R. 1 CPC and ss. 114 and 151 CPC on an error apparent on the face of the record, rectifiable without reappraising evidence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 361; Syed Ali Ahmed Shah v. Syed Shoukat Hussain Shah and others (C.P.L.A.1218-K/2023); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Syed Ali Ahmed Shah v. Syed Shoukat Hussain Shah and others (C.P.L.A.1218-K/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Abscondence Alone No Ground to Refuse Bail
records.heading: Mere abscondence for years is no ground by itself to refuse bail
records.text: Although the petitioner had absconded for 10 years, mere abscondence is no ground by itself to refuse bail if the accused is otherwise entitled to it on merits. Ref: 2025 SCMR 318, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 60; Mazhar Ali v. State (Crl. Petition 776 of 2024).
records.title: Mazhar Ali v. State (Crl. Petition 776 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Delay in Justice and Court Case Management
records.heading: Courts should keep internal case management systems to address delay in deciding cases
records.text: The Court stressed that delay in deciding cases is attributable to courts and also to parties and counsel, notably through adjournment applications. It said courts should keep internal case management systems, and directed that the matter be brought to the attention of the relevant authorities. Ref: 2025 SCMR 395, PLJ 2025 SC 120; Mrs. Faryal Arif Latif v. Mr. Arif Latif (Civil Petition 3597-L of 2023 & 8-L of 2024, decided 31.10.2024).
records.title: Mrs. Faryal Arif Latif v. Mr. Arif Latif (Civil Petition 3597-L of 2023 & 8-L of 2024, decided 31.10.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Procedural Technicalities and Substantial Justice
records.heading: Procedural rules advance justice and technical objections are construed liberally to avoid defeating substantial justice
records.text: The CPC is a consolidating procedural law, and its rules exist to advance justice. Procedure is machinery that facilitates and must not obstruct justice, and technical objections are construed liberally so as not to defeat substantial justice after ample hearing. Ref: 2025 SCMR 395; Mrs. Faryal Arif Latif v. Mr. Arif Latif (Civil Petition 3597-L of 2023 & 8-L of 2024, decided 31.10.2024).
records.title: Mrs. Faryal Arif Latif v. Mr. Arif Latif (Civil Petition 3597-L of 2023 & 8-L of 2024, decided 31.10.2024)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Directory and Mandatory Provisions: Ascertaining Intent
records.heading: A provision is read as directory where a mandatory reading would cause serious general inconvenience
records.text: Legislative intent on whether a provision is directory or mandatory is drawn from the whole statute, its nature, object and consequences. If a mandatory reading would cause serious general inconvenience to innocent persons without furthering the enactment's object, the provision is construed as directory. Ref: 2025 SCMR 341.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Procedural Law: Retrospective Application
records.heading: Procedural amendments apply to pending actions while laws prejudicing vested rights apply prospectively
records.text: Legislation that alters only procedure or remedies without prejudicing rights applies to pending and future actions, since there is no vested right in a procedure. Laws that affect, curtail or prejudice vested rights apply prospectively. Ref: 2025 SCMR 303.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Substantive Law and Procedural Law Distinguished
records.heading: Substantive law defines rights and obligations while procedural law governs their enforcement
records.text: Substantive law defines rights and obligations, while procedural law governs the process and remedies through which they are enforced. Substantive law determines what facts constitute a wrong, and procedure determines what facts constitute proof of it. Ref: 2025 SCMR 303.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation: Onus Where Vendor Alleges Abduction
records.heading: The onus on the beneficiary does not shift where a grown married man alleges abduction
records.text: Where a transferor denies a transaction on oath in the usual case of undue influence, the onus shifts to the beneficiary to prove the transaction and valid attestation. The Court held this case different, since a grown up married man alleged abduction and transferred property by sale to a relative of his wife. Ref: 2025 SCP 37; Muhammad Asif v. Amjad Iqbal and others (C.P.L.A.3151/2021); Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Amjad Iqbal and others (C.P.L.A.3151/2021)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutation: Dismissed Donee Suit Does Not Prove Fraud
records.heading: Dismissal of the donees' suit does not of itself establish fraud in the gift mutation
records.text: Dismissal of a suit filed by the donees does not of itself establish fraud in the gift mutation, and the petitioner must still prove fraud through evidence before a court of plenary jurisdiction. It does not become an executable decree in his favour for reversing the mutations. Ref: 2025 LHC 222; Zahida Parveen v. District Collector etc (WP. 8516/22, decided 04.02.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Zahida Parveen v. District Collector etc (WP. 8516/22, decided 04.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitnesses Attending Court Together; Inquest Report
records.heading: Eyewitnesses attending court with the injured witness in an enmity case is natural
records.text: Eyewitnesses attending court together with the injured witness in a murder enmity case is natural and not doubtful. Their not being cited as identifiers in the inquest report does not negate their presence, as they naturally accompanied the critically injured person to hospital. Ref: 2025 LHC 226; M. Waseem Iqbal, etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 51159 of 2019).
records.title: M. Waseem Iqbal, etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 51159 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in FIR Explained by Shifting Injured to Hospital
records.heading: Delay in FIR was explained by first rushing the injured to hospital
records.text: There is no hard and fast rule on delay in reporting, which depends on the facts. Delay was explained where the complainant and his injured daughter were first rushed to hospital and then referred elsewhere. Where the ocular account is confidence inspiring, inconsequential recovery is no ground for a lesser punishment. Ref: 2025 LHC 239; Ibrar v. The State (Criminal Appeal 24453 of 2021).
records.title: Ibrar v. The State (Criminal Appeal 24453 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Forged Bail Bonds: ss. 195 and 476 CrPC, Not FIR
records.heading: Forged bail bonds call for proceedings under sections 195 and 476 CrPC and not an FIR
records.text: Filing of forged bail bonds does not warrant an FIR but proceedings under ss. 195 and 476 CrPC. S. 205 PPC is non-cognizable and listed in s. 195(1)(b) CrPC, so only the court concerned can take cognizance, and the petitioners who were not sureties could at most face s. 109 read with s. 205 PPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 251; Tabinda Adnan & 2 others v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 77218/24, decided 12.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Tabinda Adnan & 2 others v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 77218/24, decided 12.02.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Territorial Jurisdiction of Family Court in Guardianship Matters
records.heading: Territorial jurisdiction of the Family Court in guardianship matters is governed by Rule 6
records.text: Under s. 5 of the Family Courts Act, 1964 the Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction over custody and guardianship, and territorial jurisdiction is governed by that Act and Rule 6, not the Guardians and Wards Act. Rule 6 turns on where the cause of action arose, where the parties reside or last resided, and for dissolution or dower suits, where the wife ordinarily resides. Ref: 2025 LHC 266; Sadia Yasmeen v. Zeeshan Ahmed etc (TA-76469/24, decided 07.02.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Sadia Yasmeen v. Zeeshan Ahmed etc (TA-76469/24, decided 07.02.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Sexual Harassment at Workplace and Power Dynamics
records.heading: Sexual harassment concerns power, and all genders have a right to a harassment free workplace
records.text: Sexual harassment concerns power and not sex or formal position. The right to a safe, harassment free workplace for all genders, including transgender persons, is rooted in constitutional guarantees of life, liberty, dignity and equality. The judgment also addresses gendered power dynamics and intersectionality. Ref: Muhammad Din v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Population Welfare, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.2541/2023, decided 12.02.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Din v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Population Welfare, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.2541/2023, decided 12.02.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Proof of Dower Deed: Art. 79 QSO Not Applicable
records.heading: Section 17 of the Family Courts Act exempts dower deed proof from the two witness rule of Article 79
records.text: Dower claims fall within the Family Courts Act, 1964, which operates outside the CPC and strict QSO standards. The requirement of two attesting witnesses under Art. 79 QSO is exempted by s. 17 of the Act. The defendants led no evidence of payment of dower, so the plaintiff was entitled to a decree. Ref: Mushtaq and others v. Mst. Fatima and others (C.P.L.A.559-P/2024, decided 31.01.2025); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mushtaq and others v. Mst. Fatima and others (C.P.L.A.559-P/2024, decided 31.01.2025)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Promissory Note: Ingredients and Attestation
records.heading: A promissory note needs the section 4 ingredients and Article 17(2)(a) attestation does not apply
records.text: Under s. 4 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 a promissory note needs an unconditional undertaking to pay, a certain sum, a certain payee or bearer, and the maker's signature. Where these are met, the attestation requirement of Art. 17(2)(a) QSO does not apply. Ref: Muhammad Adnan v. Salah-ud-Din (C.P.L.A.1618/2024, decided 17.02.2025); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Adnan v. Salah-ud-Din (C.P.L.A.1618/2024, decided 17.02.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pleadings Are Not Evidence; Evasive Denial
records.heading: Pleadings are not evidence and an evasive denial is no denial
records.text: Contents of a plaint or written statement are not evidence and must be proved by oral evidence on oath, subject to cross-examination, and by documents. Evasive denial is no denial, as Order VIII Rules 3, 4 and 5 CPC require specific denial of each allegation of fact. Ref: Muhammad Adnan v. Salah-ud-Din (C.P.L.A.1618/2024, decided 17.02.2025); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Adnan v. Salah-ud-Din (C.P.L.A.1618/2024, decided 17.02.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Principles of Natural Justice: Right of Audience
records.heading: A delinquent must be given a fair opportunity to explain and contest allegations before being found guilty
records.text: A delinquent must be given a fair opportunity to explain and contest allegations before being found guilty. Quasi-judicial, statutory and departmental authorities must act rationally and impartially, give clear reasons, and observe natural justice. Ref: 2025 SCMR 367.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Change of Date of Birth: Writ Not Maintainable
records.heading: A writ for change of date of birth is not maintainable where a civil suit is available
records.text: A constitutional petition by an employee of a Government Corporation seeking change of date of birth was incompetent. Art. 199 is meant for remedies where unlawfulness is shown without inquiry, and a civil suit was the adequate alternative remedy for controverted facts requiring evidence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 249.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Misjoinder of Causes of Action: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Causes of action cannot be joined where plaintiffs and defendants are not jointly interested
records.text: O. II R. 3 CPC does not permit joining causes of action where plaintiffs and defendants are not jointly interested. O. II R. 6 cannot cure a joinder beyond R. 3, so the plaint was rejected under O. VII R. 11(d) CPC and the plaintiffs were free to file separate suits under O. VII R. 13. Ref: PLD 2025 Kar 5; Muhammad Farhan Wazir v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Defence.
records.title: Muhammad Farhan Wazir v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Defence

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Magistrate Cannot Delete Section on Positive Police Report
records.heading: A Magistrate cannot delete a section on a positive police report; that is for the trial court
records.text: On a positive police report sending the accused for trial, the Magistrate cannot disagree by deleting a section such as s. 324 PPC on a summary review of material. Whether a particular section applies is for the trial court. The impugned order was set aside with consent and remanded for a fresh order. Ref: PLD 2025 Kar 12; Khadim Hussai v. State.
records.title: Khadim Hussai v. State

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: SHO Not an Accused for Failing to Prevent Offence: s. 107 PPC
records.heading: An SHO is not an accused merely because the offence occurred in his jurisdiction
records.text: The Court cited no material or law for making the SHO an accused merely because the offence occurred in his jurisdiction. S. 107 PPC and s. 149 CrPC apply only where the officer knew of the offence about to be committed or instigated or engaged in it. The order was set aside. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 126.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses: Unnatural Conduct
records.heading: Unnatural chance witnesses whose presence was not plausibly established led to acquittal on benefit of doubt
records.text: Eyewitnesses not named in the FIR, who lived elsewhere and went to buy a buffalo instead of reporting a brutal killing of eight police employees, were unnatural chance witnesses whose presence was not plausibly established. The petitions were converted into appeals and allowed, and the accused were acquitted on the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2025 SCMR 281.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubt on Time of Registration of FIR
records.heading: The claimed 30 minutes could not suffice for rescue and inquest, so the FIR was delayed
records.text: Rescuing bodies from debris and preparing injury statements and inquest reports could not have been done in the 30 minutes claimed. The FIR was therefore registered with considerable delay, and the time entered showed promptness wrongly. Ref: 2025 SCMR 281.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Joint Identification Parade Without Specific Roles
records.heading: A joint identification parade of two accused without specific roles carries no value in law
records.text: Identification parades of two accused held jointly, where eyewitnesses attributed no specific roles to either, carried no value in law. Ref: 2025 SCMR 281, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 45.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unreliable Eyewitness; Night Occurrence Without Light Source
records.heading: An unreliable eyewitness and no source of light in a night occurrence cast doubt on the prosecution
records.text: An eyewitness who claimed his clothes were stained with the deceased's blood was unreliable because the investigating officer never secured them. No source of light was mentioned for the night occurrence, creating a chance of mistaken identity, and the accused leaving the prime target unhurt cast doubt on the prosecution story. Ref: 2025 LHC 317; The State v. Muhammad Amjad (Murder Reference 204-21, decided 17.02.2025); Justice Sardar Akbar Ali.
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Amjad (Murder Reference 204-21, decided 17.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Heinous Nature of Offence Irrelevant to Appraisal of Evidence
records.heading: The gruesome nature of a crime is relevant only to punishment and not to appraisal of evidence
records.text: The gruesome nature of a crime is relevant only to punishment, and is irrelevant when appraising evidence to decide guilt. An accused is presumed innocent until proved guilty beyond reasonable doubt, and Art. 10-A guarantees a fair trial. Witnesses who make dishonest improvements to fill lacunae are not worthy of reliance. Ref: 2025 LHC 302; The State v. Muhammad Mohsin (Murder Reference 73-21, decided 18.02.2025); Justice Sardar Akbar Ali.
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Mohsin (Murder Reference 73-21, decided 18.02.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 79 QSO: Non-Production of Marginal Witnesses of Receipt
records.heading: A receipt not describing the property and without its marginal witnesses was not proved under Article 79
records.text: The plaintiff relied on a receipt that did not describe the property sold. He had to produce its marginal witnesses under Art. 79 QSO or explain their absence, and failing this the document was not proved. The courts below were justified in upholding the defendants' title and the mutation, gift deed and sale deed. Ref: 2025 CLC 47.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Will in Favour of an Heir: Consent and Registration
records.heading: A bequest to an heir is valid only with other heirs' consent and registration of a Will is optional
records.text: A bequest to an heir under Islamic law is valid only if the other heirs consent after the testator's death, within the one third limit. Registration of a Will is optional under the Registration Act, 1908, as s. 17 does not list it and s. 42 only permits deposit. Ref: 2025 LHC 363; Muhammad Riaz v. Arshad Ali etc (Civil Revision 41323/21, decided 13.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Arshad Ali etc (Civil Revision 41323/21, decided 13.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Eyewitnesses Without Reason for Presence; Medical Evidence
records.heading: Related eyewitnesses without reason for presence are interested chance witnesses and medical evidence cannot identify the assailant
records.text: Close relatives who gave no reason for going behind the deceased, and who did not identify the body in the inquest report or at post-mortem, were interested chance witnesses whose evidence was not worthy of reliance. Medical evidence only supports the prosecution on injuries and weapon and cannot identify the assailant. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 286; Muhammad Dilshad v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 59174/19); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Dilshad v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 59174/19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Recovery of Concealed Weapon After 16 Days
records.heading: A recovery of a concealed weapon 16 days after the occurrence did not appeal to a prudent mind
records.text: It does not appeal to a prudent mind that an accused who decided to conceal the weapon would keep it at home to hand over to the investigating officer 16 days after the occurrence. The appellant was acquitted on the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 286; Muhammad Dilshad v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 59174/19); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Dilshad v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 59174/19)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Res Gestae: Art. 19 QSO
records.heading: Res gestae under Article 19 must be spontaneous and an unexplained 12 hour FIR delay made it doubtful
records.text: Art. 19 QSO recognises res gestae, which must be so closely connected with the main occurrence as to form one transaction and be brought on record spontaneously without delay. Where the FIR rested on a res gestae event but was registered after an unexplained 12 hours, the witnesses' stance was doubtful and identity of the accused was not proved. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 262; Muhammad Sibtain v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 564-18); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Muhammad Sibtain v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 564-18)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Source of Light in Night Occurrence: Torch
records.heading: In a night murder the prosecution must prove the source of light and a torch is weak
records.text: For a night time murder the prosecution must prove the source of light to exclude mistaken identification. This is a rule of caution applied inflexibly rather than a statutory requirement, and a torch is regarded as a weak source of light. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 262; Muhammad Sibtain v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 564-18); Justice Ch. Abdul Aziz.
records.title: Muhammad Sibtain v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 564-18)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Production of Prosecution Witness
records.heading: The prosecution is not bound to produce all witnesses and other reliable evidence is not discarded
records.text: The prosecution is not bound to produce all witnesses. If the accused believed a witness would not support the prosecution, he could examine him in defence or apply to have him summoned as a court witness. Other confidence inspiring prosecution evidence cannot be discarded on that basis. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 334; M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 78896/2019).
records.title: M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 78896/2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 265-F CrPC: Injured Witness Without s. 161 Statement
records.heading: Section 265-F CrPC does not bar testimony of an injured witness whose section 161 statement was not recorded
records.text: S. 265-F CrPC does not bar recording testimony of a person whose s. 161 statement was not recorded. An injured witness named in the calendar of witnesses, whose injury was confirmed by the medical officer, cannot be excluded because the investigating officer failed to record his statement. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 334; M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 78896/2019).
records.title: M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 78896/2019)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: s. 34 PPC: Prerequisites for Common Intention
records.heading: Section 34 PPC requires a pre-arranged plan and concerted action, distinct from similar intention
records.text: S. 34 PPC requires a criminal act by several persons in furtherance of common intention, with a pre-arranged plan and concerted action. Strong circumstances must show common intention, and common intention must be distinguished from similar intention. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 334; M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 78896/2019).
records.title: M. Ihsan @ Malkoo etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 78896/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Distant Witnesses and Intervening Crop: Site Plan
records.heading: Distant witnesses with an intervening crop cannot specify roles and a changed site plan did not displace the original
records.text: Where witnesses were at a considerable distance and a grown crop intervened, their evidence specifying the assailants' roles in firearm injuries is not believable. The complainant's changed site plan did not displace the site plan of the state case or the Naqsha Khasra in column 24 of the inquest report. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 383, PLJ 2025 CrC 227; Abid Ali etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 79031/19).
records.title: Abid Ali etc. v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 79031/19)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Caution in Appreciation
records.heading: A dying declaration must be appreciated with great care and inspire confidence
records.text: Under Art. 46 QSO, a dying declaration must be appreciated with great care, since its maker cannot be cross-examined. The court must be satisfied that it inspires confidence and is not the product of tutoring or imagination, and that the deceased was fit to make it and able to identify the assailant. Medical opinion on mental fitness is usually sought. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 311; Qaiser Abbas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 250896/18).
records.title: Qaiser Abbas v. The State (Crl. Appeal 250896/18)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Denial of Paternity: Qazf and Li'an
records.heading: Denial of paternity amounts to qazf and birth within marriage is conclusive proof of legitimacy
records.text: Denial of paternity amounts to qazf, as it attributes zina to the mother, with li'an under s. 14 of the Ordinance available to a husband only while the marital bond subsists. Under Arts. 128 and 2(9) QSO, birth during a valid marriage or within two years of its dissolution, the woman remaining unmarried, is conclusive proof of legitimacy and no evidence may be led to disprove it. Ref: 2025 SCP 50; Mst. Saeeda Begum v. The State & another (Crl.Sh.R.P.2/2016, decided 27.01.2025); Justice Dr. Qibla Ayaz.
records.title: Mst. Saeeda Begum v. The State & another (Crl.Sh.R.P.2/2016, decided 27.01.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Anti-Rape Act: Scheduled Offence Opinion After Charge
records.heading: A Special Court may form its opinion on a scheduled offence only after framing of charge
records.text: A Special Court under the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021 may form its opinion on whether a scheduled offence is attracted under s. 16(3) of the Act only during the trial, that is after the framing of the charge, and not before. Ref: 2025 LHC 380; Azra Yasmin v. Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc. (Crl. Revision 1836/25, decided 25.02.2025); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Azra Yasmin v. Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc. (Crl. Revision 1836/25, decided 25.02.2025)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Cheque to Financial Institution: FIO Applies
records.heading: A cheque issued to a finance institution falls under the FIO and not section 489-F PPC
records.text: Where a cheque was issued to a finance institution for repayment of finance, the offence falls exclusively under s. 20(4) of the FIO and s. 489-F PPC does not apply. The Banking Court has exclusive jurisdiction under s. 7 of the FIO, and prosecution must be initiated by complaint before that court. Ref: 2025 LHC 385; Safeer Hussain v. CCPO Lahore etc (WP 48137/24, decided 25.02.2025); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Safeer Hussain v. CCPO Lahore etc (WP 48137/24, decided 25.02.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Barred by Law and Limitation
records.heading: Limitation falls within barred by law under O. VII R. 11(d) CPC and no separate issue is needed
records.text: Under O. VII R. 11(d) CPC, 'law' includes statutes, rules and judicial principles, so limitation falls within it. No specific issue on limitation need be framed if an issue under O. VII R. 11 is framed, as it covers clauses (a) to (d). Maintainability is a mixed question of law and fact decided after evidence. Ref: 2025 CLC 306; Manzoor Elahi v. Rehmat Ali (C.R. No. 530 of 2023).
records.title: Manzoor Elahi v. Rehmat Ali (C.R. No. 530 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIV R. 2 CPC: Preliminary Issues of Law
records.heading: An issue of law is tried first only where deciding it can dispose of the case
records.text: O. XIV R. 2 CPC is mandatory, but an issue of law is tried first only where deciding it can dispose of the case or a part of it. Where no issue is framed but allegations are met in the written statement, the court may let parties lead evidence and decide, whether or not the issue is pressed. Ref: 2025 CLC 306; Manzoor Elahi v. Rehmat Ali (C.R. No. 530 of 2023).
records.title: Manzoor Elahi v. Rehmat Ali (C.R. No. 530 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Competency of Suit During Pendency of Previous Suit
records.heading: Authority on the competency of a suit filed during the pendency of a previous suit
records.text: Authority on the competency of a suit filed during the pendency of a previous suit, with reference to s. 26, s. 12 and O. II R. 2 CPC. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2025 LHC 391; Zubair Wahid Khan v. Touseef Alam (Civil Revision 569-17, decided 12.02.2025); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Zubair Wahid Khan v. Touseef Alam (Civil Revision 569-17, decided 12.02.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: CPC and QSO Excluded; Section 64 CPC
records.heading: The QSO and CPC do not apply to Family Courts and a private transfer after attachment is void
records.text: By s. 17 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964, the QSO and the CPC do not apply to Family Court proceedings except ss. 10 and 11 CPC. The Family Court may execute its own decree under s. 13(3), and under s. 64 CPC a private transfer of attached property after attachment is void. Ref: Mst. Najma Naz and another v. Mst. Farzana Kanwal and three others (Civil Revision No. 2823 of 2019).
records.title: Mst. Najma Naz and another v. Mst. Farzana Kanwal and three others (Civil Revision No. 2823 of 2019)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Disputed Gifts Depriving Daughters of Inheritance
records.heading: Courts may scrutinise disputed gifts that deprive all daughters of inheritance
records.text: Disputed gifts that deprive all the daughters of inheritance may be scrutinised by the courts, which are not divested of power to examine the reasons and justification for such gifts so that no injustice is done. Ref: Mst. Najma Naz and another v. Mst. Farzana Kanwal and three others (Civil Revision No. 2823 of 2019).
records.title: Mst. Najma Naz and another v. Mst. Farzana Kanwal and three others (Civil Revision No. 2823 of 2019)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Forgery by Official: Res Ipsa Loquitur
records.heading: Forgery by an official holding the record may be proved on documents under res ipsa loquitur
records.text: Where forgery and cheating are committed by an official who holds the relevant record, direct evidence is hard to find and the matter surfaces late. Relevant documents and transactions may then be given due weight on the maxim res ipsa loquitur instead of insisting on oral or direct evidence. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 83; Muhammad Arif Zaman etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal.909-12); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Arif Zaman etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal.909-12)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Forgery: ss. 463, 464, 468 and 471 PPC
records.heading: Forgery under section 463 PPC requires a false document as defined in section 464
records.text: Forgery under s. 463 PPC requires the making of a false document as defined in s. 464, and the prosecution could not say under which clause of s. 464 the transaction fell. S. 468 applies to forgery for cheating and s. 471 to use of a forged document as genuine. The agreements and wakalatnamas had not been sent to a handwriting expert. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 93; Brigadier (Retired) Qaisar Shahzad v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 3153-B of 2024, decided 18.10.2024).
records.title: Brigadier (Retired) Qaisar Shahzad v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 3153-B of 2024, decided 18.10.2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody of Case Property: Charas
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody of recovered charas leads to acquittal without discussing other merits
records.text: If safe custody of the recovered substance is not proved, other merits need not be discussed and acquittal follows. An unbroken chain of safe custody and transmission of the case property and sample parcel must be proved, since recovery of narcotics constitutes the offence itself. A single dent in the prosecution case suffices for acquittal. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 99; Qamar Masih v. The State (Crl. A. No. 203 of 2008).
records.title: Qamar Masih v. The State (Crl. A. No. 203 of 2008)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas Recovery: Discrepancies in Weight and Seizure
records.heading: Discrepancies in weight and seizure of charas cast serious doubt and benefit the accused
records.text: Under s. 25 CNS Act, 1997 recovery proceedings are accepted even if s. 103 CrPC is not followed, but discrepancies casting doubt on witness presence benefit the accused. The sample was said to weigh 55 grams while the PFSA report showed 53.65 grams, and the polythene bag and tape were not seized. These anomalies created serious doubt. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 106; Muhammad Sarfraz alias Aolia v. The State (Crl. A. No. 965 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Sarfraz alias Aolia v. The State (Crl. A. No. 965 of 2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Defamation: Advocate Drafting Pleading on Instructions
records.heading: An advocate drafting a plaint on client's instructions cannot be summoned for defamation
records.text: An advocate who drafts a plaint on his client's instructions, the client verifying its contents, cannot be summoned for defamation under ss. 500 and 501 PPC, having acted in good faith without malice and being protected by Exception 9 to s. 500. The High Court will not interfere in its limited revisional jurisdiction under ss. 435 and 439 CrPC unless the order is illegal, perverse or without jurisdiction. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 109; Muhammad Musharaf Hassan v. The State, etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 16003 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Musharaf Hassan v. The State, etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 16003 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR: Withheld Witness and Inquest Report
records.heading: Non-production of the constable who carried the complaint and a defective inquest report undermined the prompt FIR
records.text: The constable who carried the complaint to the police station was not produced, and the accused were entitled to cross-examine him on the time of registration of the FIR. The inquest report prepared under Rule 35, Chapter 25, Police Rules, 1934 lacked the brief facts on page 3, which indicated that the FIR had not been registered before the autopsy. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 112; Zeeshan Ahmed and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 851 & 960 & M.R. No. 65 of 2022).
records.title: Zeeshan Ahmed and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 851 & 960 & M.R. No. 65 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Weapon Recovery as Corroboration of Doubtful Ocular Account
records.heading: Weapon recovery can only corroborate an ocular account and is unnecessary where that account is disbelieved
records.text: Recovery of pistols and a positive PFSA match with crime empties can at most corroborate an ocular account, and where the ocular account is disbelieved or suffers from multiple doubts, corroboration from other circumstances need not be sought. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 112; Zeeshan Ahmed and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 851 & 960 & M.R. No. 65 of 2022).
records.title: Zeeshan Ahmed and others v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 851 & 960 & M.R. No. 65 of 2022)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Proof of Juvenility: Scrutiny of Age Documents
records.heading: Age documents must pass QSO admissibility rules and the accused bears the burden of proving juvenility
records.text: Under s. 8 JJSA 2018, age documents must be verified and pass the admissibility rules of the QSO. Absence of documents means absence of authentic and admissible documents. Age inquiry resembles a voir dire, and an accused facing a possible death sentence must prove his claim of juvenility on true documents, the burden lying on him. Ref: 2025 MLD 367; Kamran Mushtaq v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision.56647/24); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Kamran Mushtaq v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision.56647/24)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama: Duty of Nikah Registrar
records.heading: The Nikah Registrar must fill all columns of the nikahnama accurately and may be held accountable
records.text: Under s. 6(2A) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 the Nikah Registrar must fill all columns of the nikahnama accurately with specific answers. A Nikah Khawan or Registrar who fails in this duty should be held accountable. The court also noted the custom of agriculturist families giving dowry articles at both first and second marriages. Ref: 2025 MLD 216, PLJ 2025 Lahore 251; Irfan Mohsin v. Additional District and Sessions Judge & others (Writ Petition No. 4265 of 2020).
records.title: Irfan Mohsin v. Additional District and Sessions Judge & others (Writ Petition No. 4265 of 2020)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documentary Evidence Prevails Over Oral Evidence
records.heading: Oral evidence cannot outweigh or vary documentary evidence once an agreement is in writing
records.text: Oral evidence cannot outweigh unobjected documentary evidence and cannot substitute for it. Under Art. 103 QSO, oral statements between parties to an instrument are excluded, so once an agreement is reduced to writing its terms cannot be varied by oral evidence. Ref: 2025 MLD 323; Muhammad Arif v. Javaid Khan (Civil Revision No.404-D of 2015).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. Javaid Khan (Civil Revision No.404-D of 2015)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Second Marriage Without Permission: Family Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Only the Family Court may try second marriage without permission, per the Urdu headnote
records.text: Headnote in Urdu: the power to try a case of second marriage contracted without permission lies only with the Family Court. Ref: 2025 MLD 385; Muhammad Waqas v. Riffat Awan etc (Crl. Revision 1601/22).
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. Riffat Awan etc (Crl. Revision 1601/22)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Identification Parade Needing Further Inquiry
records.heading: Identification parades after nomination in the FIR required further probe, entitling the petitioner to bail
records.text: The petitioner and his two brothers were nominated in the FIR, so the evidentiary value of identification at parades held after nomination required further probe. This entitled the petitioner to post-arrest bail. Ref: 2025 SCMR 318, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 60; Mazhar Ali v. State and another (Crl. P. No. 776 of 2024).
records.title: Mazhar Ali v. State and another (Crl. P. No. 776 of 2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Absence of Enmity Does Not Prove Witness Reliable
records.heading: Absence of enmity does not mean witnesses are to be relied upon blindly
records.text: Absence of enmity between witnesses and the accused does not mean they are to be relied upon blindly. It must still be determined whether their evidence is trustworthy or inherently unreliable. Ref: 2025 SCMR 281, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 45.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Additional Evidence at Appellate Stage
records.heading: Additional evidence may be allowed even before the apex court if inevitable for a just decision
records.text: Additional evidence may be allowed even during proceedings before the apex court, provided the party shows that non-production before the court of first instance was beyond its control and that the evidence is inevitable for a just decision of the lis. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 184; Farrukh Shahzad v. Maqbool Hussain Awan (C.R. No. 56505 of 2022).
records.title: Farrukh Shahzad v. Maqbool Hussain Awan (C.R. No. 56505 of 2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fraud Must Be Pleaded With Particulars: s. 18
records.heading: Fraud must be pleaded with full particulars from the start and then proved
records.text: Fraud must be pleaded from the start with full particulars and then proved, and a party seeking the benefit of s. 18 must allege it as a ground of attack or defence from the initial stage. A fresh ground not raised before the courts below cannot be raised for the first time, except a question of law. Ref: 2025 SCMR 231, PLJ 2025 SC 94; Taj Wali Khan v. Hukam Khan (C.A. No. 176-P/2013).
records.title: Taj Wali Khan v. Hukam Khan (C.A. No. 176-P/2013)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Sales Entered in Cultivation Column of Revenue Record
records.heading: Entering sales in the cultivation column of the revenue record allows double sales and should change
records.text: The Court criticised entries of sales in the cultivation column of the revenue record, which are not carried into the ownership column and allow double sales and collusion with revenue officials. It said the procedure should be changed, and that such transactions should be managed under the Registration Act, 1908 and not the Act of 1967. Ref: 2025 SCMR 211, PLJ 2025 SC 89; Amjad Ali and others v. Anwar Shah and others (C.P.L.A. 223-P of 2015).
records.title: Amjad Ali and others v. Anwar Shah and others (C.P.L.A. 223-P of 2015)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Section 43 Transfer of Property Act: Erroneous Representation
records.heading: Section 43 TPA applies to an erroneous representation of authority to transfer, which may be innocent
records.text: S. 43 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 applies where a person fraudulently or erroneously represents that he is authorised to transfer immovable property for consideration. At the transferee's option the transfer operates on any interest the transferor later acquires while the contract subsists, and the representation may be innocent. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 177, 2025 YLR 566; Noora through legal heirs etc v. Province of Punjab etc (Civil Revision 14536/22).
records.title: Noora through legal heirs etc v. Province of Punjab etc (Civil Revision 14536/22)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Biological Versus Legitimate Child
records.heading: Interim maintenance and section 17-A apply to a legitimate child and not automatically to a biological child
records.text: A legitimate child is born to parents lawfully married at the time of birth, while a biological child is genetically related and may be born within or outside marriage. For a legitimate child interim maintenance and s. 17-A of the Family Courts Act, 1964 apply. For a biological child the court assesses the defendant's financial capacity and the child's needs. Ref: 2025 LHC 495; Muhammad Afzal v. Judge Family Court, etc. (Writ Petition No.43280 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Afzal v. Judge Family Court, etc. (Writ Petition No.43280 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Islamabad High Court Directions for Speedy Family Cases
records.heading: Directions to remove delay in family cases, including E-Courts and E-kiosks
records.text: The Court held that the State and the Court must devise mechanisms to remove delay in family cases. It directed, among other things, special E-Courts with claim-based video statements in place of written pleadings, E-kiosks for filing, training of judges and lawyers, and implementation by the Registrar and MIT. Ref: PLJ 2025 Islamabad 6, 2024 CLC 1801; Sumaira Shaheen etc. v. Judge Family Court.
records.title: Sumaira Shaheen etc. v. Judge Family Court

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay in Civil Revision: Art. 162-A
records.heading: A civil revision filed beyond 90 days is time barred and age and ignorance are no ground for condonation
records.text: A civil revision filed after 122 days was barred by 32 days, as Art. 162-A of the Limitation Act, 2018 allows 90 days. Advanced age without medical record and ignorance of office process are no ground for condonation. Limitation cannot be bypassed to rescue an indolent party, and the petition was dismissed without merits. Ref: PLJ 2025 Civil Note 57; Muhammad Anwar v. Shahadat Ali (C.R. No. 61696 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. Shahadat Ali (C.R. No. 61696 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Penal Provision Strictly Applied
records.heading: O. XVII R. 3 CPC is penal and strictly applied after a final opportunity
records.text: O. XVII R. 3 CPC is penal and must be strictly construed and applied. A litigant who defaults after a final opportunity and a clear warning of consequences gets no concession, and the court cannot grant further time on the plea that technicalities should not defeat decisions on merits. Ref: PLJ 2025 Civil Note 53.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Further Inquiry and Mala Fide
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail granted as the injury did not correlate with the alleged weapon and mala fide may be inferred
records.text: In a s. 337-F(v) PPC case where the Medical Board found the injury did not correlate with the alleged weapon, a case of further inquiry was made out and pre-arrest bail granted. Merits may be touched upon at the pre-arrest stage, and mala fide, being a state of mind, may be inferred from circumstances. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 14; Azib Khan v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 4335-B of 2024).
records.title: Azib Khan v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 4335-B of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Medical Evidence
records.heading: A direct conflict between ocular and medical evidence raises serious doubt about eyewitness credibility
records.text: A direct conflict between ocular and medical evidence raises serious doubt about the credibility of the eyewitnesses. A witness who deliberately and mala fide improves his statement to strengthen the prosecution case is no longer reliable. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 29; Muhammad Usman alias Lillah etc. v. State (Crl. A. No. 27563-J & Crl. Rev. No. 27526 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Usman alias Lillah etc. v. State (Crl. A. No. 27563-J & Crl. Rev. No. 27526 of 2019)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas Recovery: Doubt From Weight Discrepancy
records.heading: Weight discrepancy and unseized bag raise reasonable doubt in a charas recovery
records.text: Under s. 25 CNS Act, 1997 recovery proceedings are accepted even without compliance with s. 103 CrPC. Here the shopping bag was not seized, the case property differed in form from the description, and 59 grams were said to be separated while PFSA found 47.33 grams. A reasonable doubt arose about guilt. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 28; Hukam Khan v. State (Crl. A. No. 1295 of 2023).
records.title: Hukam Khan v. State (Crl. A. No. 1295 of 2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Borderline Quantity Under s. 9(b) or 9(c) CNSA
records.heading: Recovery marginally above 1 kg is a matter of further inquiry for bail
records.text: Where 1112 grams of charas was recovered, marginally above 1 kg, it remained for the trial court to decide whether s. 9(b) or s. 9(c) CNSA, 1997 applied. This brought the case within further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 17; Khizar Hayat v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 70342-B of 2023).
records.title: Khizar Hayat v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 70342-B of 2023)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: PFSA DNA Report as Circumstantial Evidence
records.heading: A matching DNA profile on stains alone does not complete a circumstantial chain
records.text: A PFSA report is not substantive evidence, though conviction on it is lawful under the proviso to Art. 164 QSO if it has a substantive nature. Mere matching of a DNA profile from stains on the deceased's shalwar does not meet the standard for circumstantial evidence, which must form an unbroken chain to the accused. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 16.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Undertaking Not Executable as Decree or Order
records.heading: An undertaking is not a decree or order and is not executable under section 36 CPC
records.text: An undertaking is neither a decree under s. 2(2) CPC nor an order under s. 2(14) CPC, so it is not executable under s. 36 CPC. At most it could be regarded as an agreement. Ref: PLJ 2025 Peshawar 47.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Presumption Attaching to Thirty Year Old Document
records.heading: The thirty year document presumption is rebuttable and needs proper custody
records.text: The presumption of genuineness of a document over thirty years old is rebuttable and discretionary, and arises only where the document comes from proper custody under Art. 100 QSO. It extends only to a signature and parts in the handwriting of a particular person, and a dower deed produced by its scribe, who lacked proper custody, did not attract it. Ref: Muhammad Israr v. Jehanzeb & others (C.A.156-P/2013, decided 24.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui.
records.title: Muhammad Israr v. Jehanzeb & others (C.A.156-P/2013, decided 24.02.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Valid Gift: Acceptance and Withholding Best Evidence
records.heading: A gift needs offer, acceptance and delivery; withholding the acceptor harms its proof
records.text: A gift requires offer, acceptance and delivery of possession. Where acceptance was made by a person on behalf of the donee, his non-production dented the authenticity of the gift deed, as a party withholding best evidence bears the consequences. Registration alone does not prove authenticity. Ref: 2025 LHC 526; Malik Abdul Rauf v. Malik Abdul Razzaq (deceased) through L.Rs., etc. (Civil Revision No. 2363 of 2012, decided 16.02.2025).
records.title: Malik Abdul Rauf v. Malik Abdul Razzaq (deceased) through L.Rs., etc. (Civil Revision No. 2363 of 2012, decided 16.02.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Limits on Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings under O. VI R. 17 CPC is subject to limitations and conditions
records.text: Although O. VI R. 17 CPC gives courts ample power to allow amendment of pleadings, that power must be exercised subject to certain limitations and conditions. Ref: 2025 LHC 488; Iqbal Ahmad v. ADJ etc (WP 15171-22, decided 24.02.2025); Justice Syed Ahsan Raza Kazmi.
records.title: Iqbal Ahmad v. ADJ etc (WP 15171-22, decided 24.02.2025)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-e-Ishhad: Mandatory Formalities
records.heading: The formalities of Talb-e-Ishhad are mandatory and service on the vendee must be proved
records.text: Talb-e-Ishhad requires a written notice, attested by two truthful witnesses, sent under registered cover with acknowledgement due where postal facilities exist. These formalities are mandatory, and the plaintiff must prove by solid evidence that the notice was personally served on the vendee. Ref: 2025 LHC 558; Ghulam Hussain (deceased) through LRs. etc (CR No.516/D of 2022, decided 19.02.2025).
records.title: Ghulam Hussain (deceased) through LRs. etc (CR No.516/D of 2022, decided 19.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Death in House: Burden on Prosecution
records.heading: Unnatural death in the accused's house does not alone prove her guilt
records.text: The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The unnatural death of the appellant's husband in his house is a circumstance to be considered, but alone it cannot establish her guilt without other evidence connecting her to the crime. Ref: 2025 LHC 563; Palwasha Nageen v. State (Criminal Appeal No.589 of 2024, decided 24.02.2025).
records.title: Palwasha Nageen v. State (Criminal Appeal No.589 of 2024, decided 24.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Forensic Report on Blood Without Origin Finding
records.heading: A report showing only human blood on the weapon has no evidentiary value
records.text: A forensic agency report showing only the presence of human blood on the weapon, without findings on its origin or comparison with the victim's blood, has no evidentiary value. Ref: 2025 LHC 585; Ali Akbar etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 31052/23, decided 11.02.2025).
records.title: Ali Akbar etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 31052/23, decided 11.02.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Unbroken Chain of Custody in Narcotics Cases
records.heading: Failure to prove an unbroken chain of custody defeats a narcotics conviction
records.text: In CNSA cases resting on recovery and chemical analysis, the prosecution must prove an unbroken chain of custody and secure transmission to the laboratory. Failure renders the chemical examiner's report unreliable and unable to sustain conviction, and the accused gets the benefit of doubt. Ref: Muhammad Iqbal v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.828/2024, decided 17.02.2025); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.828/2024, decided 17.02.2025)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Demands on Behalf of Minor Pre-emptor
records.heading: Only the legal guardian of a minor's property may make pre-emption demands for the minor
records.text: Under ss. 3, 13 and 14 of the Pre-emption Act, read with Islamic law, only the legal guardian of the minor's property, and not a next friend under O. XXXII CPC, may exercise the right of pre-emption. A demand by a father or brother is insufficient unless previously authorised. Ref: 2025 CLC 259, PLJ 2024 Lahore 769; Ahmad Yar etc v. Chan Pir Shah etc (CR.1415-11).
records.title: Ahmad Yar etc v. Chan Pir Shah etc (CR.1415-11)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness, Willingness and Deposit
records.heading: A vendee must prove readiness and ability to pay and may be ordered to deposit
records.text: A vendee seeking specific performance must plead and prove readiness, willingness and ability to pay, for example through bank statements, and may be put to terms such as deposit at any stage. Relief is discretionary. Under s. 24(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 relief is denied to a party who violates an essential term, and the vendee there was held disentitled. Ref: 2025 CLC 352, PLJ 2024 Lahore 293; Mst. Qamar Bibi etc v. Shahab Ud Din etc (Civil Revision 233690/18).
records.title: Mst. Qamar Bibi etc v. Shahab Ud Din etc (Civil Revision 233690/18)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: Two Attesting Witnesses, Arts. 17(2) and 79
records.heading: An agreement to sell needs two attesting witnesses and a scribe cannot replace one
records.text: An agreement to sell immovable property falls within Art. 17(2) QSO and must be attested by two witnesses. Under Art. 79 it cannot be used as evidence unless two attesting witnesses are called, and a scribe cannot replace the second marginal witness. Ref: 2025 CLC 352, PLJ 2024 Lahore 293; Mst. Qamar Bibi etc v. Shahab Ud Din etc (Civil Revision 233690/18).
records.title: Mst. Qamar Bibi etc v. Shahab Ud Din etc (Civil Revision 233690/18)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 31 CPC: Appellate Judgment Requirements
records.heading: An appellate judgment reversing the trial court must comply with O. XLI R. 31 CPC
records.text: Compliance with O. XLI R. 31 CPC is mandatory. An appellate court reversing the trial court must frame points for determination, give findings on the issues and show it examined the record, so that the losing party and the higher forum can see what weighed with it. Ref: 2025 CLC 352, PLJ 2024 Lahore 293; Mst. Qamar Bibi etc v. Shahab Ud Din etc (Civil Revision 233690/18).
records.title: Mst. Qamar Bibi etc v. Shahab Ud Din etc (Civil Revision 233690/18)
