records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Mutation: Attesting Witnesses and Documentary Evidence
records.heading: Attesting witnesses need not be examined where the executant does not deny the mutation
records.text: Where the executant himself does not deny execution of a mutation, non-examination of attesting witnesses is not fatal. A document proved in accordance with law carries a presumption of genuineness, and the best evidence of its contents is the document itself, which outweighs oral evidence. Ref: 2025 CLC 228; Muhammad Khan v. Muhammad Akram (Civil Revision 1750-15).
records.title: Muhammad Khan v. Muhammad Akram (Civil Revision 1750-15)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Rent Tribunal: Application of Law of Evidence
records.heading: A Rent Tribunal must apply the general principles of evidence but not every QSO provision
records.text: A Rent Tribunal must apply the general principles of the law of evidence in the QSO, for fairness, and cannot rely on hearsay or unproved copies. It need not enforce all QSO provisions, which would defeat the expedition intended by s. 34 of the Act. A disputed tenancy agreement need not be proved under Arts. 17(2)(a) and 79. Ref: Zafar Iqbal & another v. Syed Riaz Hussain Shah and others (C.P.L.A.3854/2024, decided 25.02.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Zafar Iqbal & another v. Syed Riaz Hussain Shah and others (C.P.L.A.3854/2024, decided 25.02.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Belated Production of Public Documents: O. XIII R. 2
records.heading: Public documents of proper custody are liberally accepted despite late production under O. XIII R. 2
records.text: Under O. XIII R. 2 CPC a party producing documents late must show good cause, but where they are public documents from proper custody of undoubted authenticity, the provision is read liberally and they are ordinarily accepted. The orders allowing production were upheld and the writ petitions dismissed. Ref: 2025 CLC 223.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Habeas Corpus for Minor: Custody Is for Guardian Court
records.heading: Habeas corpus cannot resolve custody disputes, which belong to the Guardian Court
records.text: S. 491 CrPC cannot be used to declare a guardian or resolve custody disputes, which belong to the Guardians and Wards Court. Custody turns on the minor's welfare, including age, sex, religion and the guardian's character and capacity. As the minor was produced, the petition had served its purpose and permanent custody must be sought in the Guardian Court. Ref: 2025 CLC 272.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Muhammad Nasir Ismail v. Government of Punjab
records.heading: Judgment in a civil petition for leave to appeal against the Government of Punjab
records.text: Judgment in a civil petition for leave to appeal involving the Government of Punjab through the Secretary Law and Parliamentary Affairs Division. The post gives only the case number, parties, judge and date, with no holding. Ref: Muhammad Nasir Ismail v. Government of Punjab through Secretary Law and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.3062/2022, decided 25.02.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Nasir Ismail v. Government of Punjab through Secretary Law and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.3062/2022, decided 25.02.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Agreement Waiving Mother's Right of Hizanat
records.heading: A mother's agreement surrendering custody of her minor child is unenforceable
records.text: A mother's agreement surrendering custody (hizanat) of her minor child is violative of law and cannot be enforced, as para 352(5) of Muhammadan Law gives her custody of a son to age seven and of a daughter until puberty. The Court relied on PLD 2020 SC 508. Dower waivers are likewise invalid. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 291; Mst. Haseena Bibi v. Abdul Haleem & others (C.A. 1227/2016).
records.title: Mst. Haseena Bibi v. Abdul Haleem & others (C.A. 1227/2016)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 103 CrPC in Drugs Act Cases; Show Cause Notice
records.heading: Section 103 CrPC applies to Drugs Act cases and a show cause notice does not prove a hearing
records.text: S. 103 CrPC applies to cases under the Drugs Act, 1976 and the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan Act, 2012. Issuing a show cause notice does not prove a hearing unless it is shown the accused was heard at the stated time. The Board met an hour before the time stated in the notice, so the notice had no legal sanctity and the appellant was acquitted. Ref: 2025 LHC 626; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State etc (Crl.A 577-22, decided 18.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State etc (Crl.A 577-22, decided 18.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in FIR and Autopsy; CDR Not Conclusive
records.heading: Delays and missing injuries doubt eyewitness presence, and a CDR is not conclusive proof
records.text: Delays in reporting, in autopsy and in filing the private complaint, the non-nomination of the appellant in the FIR, and the absence of any described injuries to the accused cast doubt on the presence of eyewitnesses. A CDR is not conclusive proof of involvement in a crime. The appellant was acquitted. Ref: 2025 LHC 639; The State v. Atif Pervaiz (Murder Reference 23-23, decided 19.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: The State v. Atif Pervaiz (Murder Reference 23-23, decided 19.02.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Offences Outside Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Bail is the rule for offences outside the prohibitory clause absent exceptional circumstances
records.text: Offences of sexual harassment and blackmail arising from a marital dispute, punishable by at most five and three years, fall outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Grant of bail is the rule, there being no exceptional circumstance, and the petitioner, a medical professional without record, was not a flight risk. Bail granted. Ref: Syed Muhammad Ali Jaferi v. The State Thr. DAG and another (Crl. P. No. 94/2025, decided 21.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Syed Muhammad Ali Jaferi v. The State Thr. DAG and another (Crl. P. No. 94/2025, decided 21.02.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Diyat: Minors' Share and Convict's Inability to Pay
records.heading: Minors' share in diyat is protected and a convict unable to pay has statutory relief
records.text: The share of minor legal heirs in Diyat is protected in all circumstances, even after a compromise by all heirs. A convict unable to pay may seek relief under the Diyat, Arsh and Daman Fund Rules, 2007, framed under s. 338-G PPC, such as soft loans, grants, parole or jobs, or ask the trial court under s. 331 PPC for instalments. Ref: Tanvir Hussain v. The State (Crl.M.A.714/2023, decided 28.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Tanvir Hussain v. The State (Crl.M.A.714/2023, decided 28.02.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Video Recording and Private Witnesses
records.heading: Absent video recording and private witnesses, the balance tilts to the accused in narcotics bail
records.text: Given the severe punishments under the 1997 Act, the standard of proof is correspondingly high, and Art. 164 QSO stresses modern devices in evidence collection. The police made no video or photographs of the recovery and associated no private witness, and the balance tilted in favour of the petitioner. Ref: Muhammad Abid Hussain v. State (Crl.P. No 146 of 2025, decided 27.02.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Abid Hussain v. State (Crl.P. No 146 of 2025, decided 27.02.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO: Identification Parade Parameters
records.heading: Authority on the parameters of identification parades under Art. 22 QSO
records.text: Authority on the parameters under Art. 22 QSO, read with the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders, vol. 3, chapter 2, part C, and rule 26.32 of chapter 26, vol. 3 of the Police Rules, 1934. The post gives no holding. Ref: Rashid and another v. The State (Crl.A.282-L/2020, decided 18.02.2025); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Rashid and another v. The State (Crl.A.282-L/2020, decided 18.02.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Admissions: Arts. 113 and 45 QSO; Evidence Without Oath
records.heading: Parties may resile from admissions except those in pleadings, and unsworn statements are inadmissible
records.text: Parties may resile from all admissions except those made in pleadings. Art. 113 QSO governs pleading admissions and Art. 45 governs evidentiary admissions. Statements recorded without oath are inadmissible and cannot be used to the detriment of their makers. Ref: 2025 LHC 621; Muhammad Ameer v. Member (J-VII), Board of Revenue, etc. (W.P. No.234510 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Ameer v. Member (J-VII), Board of Revenue, etc. (W.P. No.234510 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Accomplice, CCTV and Video Evidence in Murder Appeal
records.heading: CCTV report without a photogrammetry test cannot establish an unknown assailant's identity
records.text: The judgment distinguishes an accomplice's statement from a co-accused's confession before police, and notes discrepancies between autopsy and crime reports. A PFSA report on CCTV footage without a photogrammetry test cannot establish an unknown assailant's identity, and the trial court's failure to assess admissibility of video evidence cannot prejudice the appellant. Ref: 2025 LHC 656; Fida Hussain etc v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-1035-23, decided 28.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar.
records.title: Fida Hussain etc v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-1035-23, decided 28.02.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics Bail: No Video Recording or Private Witness
records.heading: No video recording or private witness favours the accused in a heroin bail case
records.text: In a case of 1100 grams of heroin under s. 9(1)6(c) of the Control of Narcotic Substances Act 1997, the failure to video-record the recovery and to associate a private witness, contrary to judicial directions and Art. 164 QSO, favoured the accused. Reliance on police witnesses alone was insufficient at this stage. Petition converted into appeal and post-arrest bail allowed on bonds of Rs. 200,000. Ref: Muhammad Abid Hussain v. The State and another (Crl.P. 146/2025, decided 27.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakkar; Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Muhammad Abid Hussain v. The State and another (Crl.P. 146/2025, decided 27.02.2025)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Section 20 Arbitration Act 1940: Court Intervention
records.heading: Section 20 of the Arbitration Act 1940 provides arbitration with court intervention without a pending suit
records.text: Chapter III of the Arbitration Act, 1940 provides arbitration with court intervention where no suit is pending, and s. 20 deals with it directly. The respondents petitioned the civil court to have the agreement filed and the dispute referred to an arbitrator. Ref: 2025 LHC 669.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: FIR Not Substantive Evidence Unless Proved by Maker
records.heading: An FIR is not substantive evidence unless its maker proves it on oath
records.text: An FIR is not substantive evidence unless its maker affirms it on oath and is cross-examined. Under Arts. 140 and 153 QSO it may be used only to contradict its maker. The exception is an FIR recorded on the report of a person near death, which is a dying declaration under Art. 46 QSO but cannot corroborate another witness. Ref: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Petition No.95 of 2022, decided 20.02.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Petition No.95 of 2022, decided 20.02.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale Pendente Lite Is Not an Assignment
records.heading: A purchase during a pending suit is a sale and not an assignment
records.text: An assignment and a sale of immovable property are different, and the petitioner's claimed title came through a sale during the pendency of the second suit, not an assignment. The Court was not persuaded by the case made out and held that the case relied on had different facts. Ref: Abdul Shakoor v. Muhammad Hanif (C.P.L.A. NO.1808-L/2015, decided 25.02.2025).
records.title: Abdul Shakoor v. Muhammad Hanif (C.P.L.A. NO.1808-L/2015, decided 25.02.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Omission to Frame Charge: s. 537 CrPC
records.heading: Failure to frame a charge for a distinct offence is not curable under section 537 CrPC
records.text: Failure to frame a charge for a distinct offence goes to the root of the trial and cannot be cured under s. 537 CrPC, unlike a merely defective charge causing no prejudice. Ss. 221 and 233 require a charge for each distinct offence, and omission coupled with failure to put the accusation under s. 342 CrPC breaches fair trial. Ref: Shabeer Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.28 of 2023, decided 20.02.2025).
records.title: Shabeer Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.28 of 2023, decided 20.02.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CDR Obtained by Email From DPO Office Inadmissible
records.heading: A CDR obtained by email from a police office and not the company is inadmissible
records.text: A CDR obtained by email from the IT office of the DPO, and not from the mobile company, with no company representative appearing in court, is inadmissible in evidence. Ref: 2025 YLR 427, PLJ 2026 CrC Note 162; Usama Ali v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal.77969/19); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Usama Ali v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal.77969/19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Tunnel Vision in Police Investigation and Prosecution
records.heading: Tunnel vision in investigation and prosecution harms the criminal justice system
records.text: Tunnel vision by police and prosecution has pernicious effects on the criminal justice system. Quoting academic literature, the Court describes it as a human tendency to adopt a conclusion and filter all evidence through it, elevating supporting material and dismissing inconsistent evidence. Ref: 2025 YLR 427, PLJ 2026 CrC Note 162; Usama Ali v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal.77969/19); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Usama Ali v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal.77969/19)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Occupancy Tenant: ss. 5 and 6 Punjab Tenancy Act
records.heading: An occupancy tenant under the Punjab Tenancy Act must satisfy the statutory conditions
records.text: Under ss. 5 and 6 of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887 an occupancy tenant is one recorded in the periodical record of right before 21.10.1868 and in possession about 20 years before the Act. A tenant not meeting this cannot claim occupancy rights, and contrary revenue entries create no right. Ref: 2025 YLR 322; Abdul Rehman & 16 Others v. Nazir Ahmad etc (Civil Revision 59188/24); Justice Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Abdul Rehman & 16 Others v. Nazir Ahmad etc (Civil Revision 59188/24)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Will: Nature, Revocability and One-Third Limit
records.heading: A will takes effect after death, is revocable and is limited to one third
records.text: A will takes effect after death, is rescindable and does not bind the testator or affect his power to transfer property in his lifetime. Testamentary succession follows the will, and intestate succession applies without one. The one-third limit on bequests derives from a Hadith reported by Bukhari, not directly from the Qur'an. Ref: 2025 YLR 302; Mst. Kaneez Fatima, etc. v. Ghulam Hussain (Civil Revision No.751-D of 2004).
records.title: Mst. Kaneez Fatima, etc. v. Ghulam Hussain (Civil Revision No.751-D of 2004)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Bequest of Entire Property to Non-Heir
records.heading: An entire estate may be bequeathed to a non-heir in defined circumstances including heirs' consent
records.text: A testator may bequeath his entire property to a non-heir where a valid custom permits, there are no heirs, existing heirs consent after his death, or the only heir is a spouse whose share is unaffected. Heirs' consent may be express, oral, written or implied from conduct, such as helping the legatee obtain mutation or possession. Ref: 2025 YLR 302; Mst. Kaneez Fatima, etc. v. Ghulam Hussain (Civil Revision No.751-D of 2004).
records.title: Mst. Kaneez Fatima, etc. v. Ghulam Hussain (Civil Revision No.751-D of 2004)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift to Son Depriving Daughter of Inheritance
records.heading: A gift to a son made to deprive a daughter of inheritance is unjust
records.text: A father's gift to his son alone with the sole intention of depriving his daughter of her inheritance, made here out of anger at her love marriage, causes material and moral harm and is unjust and contrary to Islamic teachings and the objectives of Shariah. Ref: 2025 LHC 693; Liaqat Ali v. Shahnaz Akhtar (Civil Revision 58611/19, decided 18.02.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. Shahnaz Akhtar (Civil Revision 58611/19, decided 18.02.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused's Right to Cross-Examine Despite Unpaid Diet Money
records.heading: A court cannot close the accused's right to cross-examine for unpaid diet money
records.text: The CrPC has no provision allowing a court to close an accused's right to cross-examine a prosecution witness for non-payment of diet money. An order requiring Rs.10,000 from the accused contravened s. 244(3) CrPC, which exempts an accused charged with an offence punishable by over six months from bearing witness expenses. Ref: Rana Aamir Ijaz v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 187/2023).
records.title: Rana Aamir Ijaz v. The State and others (Criminal Revision No. 187/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Claim Against Paternal Uncle
records.heading: A maintenance claim against a grandfather cannot be shifted to a paternal uncle
records.text: D.F. Mulla's Muhammadan Law is a textbook and neither a statute nor custom, so its author's opinion is not binding. The granddaughter failed to prove she was a poor distant relative or that she would inherit from the uncle, and a claim against the grandfather cannot be shifted to the uncle. The lower appellate court's decision was upheld. Ref: 2024 CLC 513, PLJ 2024 Lahore 135; Mahnoor Shabbir v. Additional District Judge, etc. (W.P. No. 62482 of 2022).
records.title: Mahnoor Shabbir v. Additional District Judge, etc. (W.P. No. 62482 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pleadings Are Not Evidence
records.heading: Pleadings are not evidence and a pleaded fact must be independently proved
records.text: A plea in the pleadings has no effect without evidence and does not equate to evidence. A person asserting a fact in his pleading must prove it by independent and unimpeachable evidence. Ref: Rana Muhammad Yameen v. Muhammad Jamil (Civil Appeal No.151-P of 2013, decided 21.02.2025).
records.title: Rana Muhammad Yameen v. Muhammad Jamil (Civil Appeal No.151-P of 2013, decided 21.02.2025)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Time-Barred Civil Revisions: Suo Motu Jurisdiction and Condonation
records.heading: Authority on suo motu jurisdiction, condonation and limitation in time barred civil revisions
records.text: Authority on the scope of suo motu jurisdiction in time-barred civil revisions under s. 115 CPC, wrong advice of counsel as ground for condonation, the effect of re-insertion of Art. 162-A in the Limitation Act (Punjab Amendment), unjust enrichment, and O. XXII R. 10 CPC. The post gives no holdings. Ref: 2025 LHC 701; Haji Mehboob Alam v. Rana Khalid Mehmood etc. (Civil Revision.1214-17, decided 27.02.2025); Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: Haji Mehboob Alam v. Rana Khalid Mehmood etc. (Civil Revision.1214-17, decided 27.02.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Questions to Hostile Witness
records.heading: Art. 150 QSO allows questions to a witness who subtly contradicts his earlier statement
records.text: Under Art. 150 QSO the court may permit the party calling a witness to put questions that could be put in cross-examination, at any stage of the witness's examination, where the witness subtly contradicts his earlier statement. The accused must then be allowed to cross-examine on the answers elicited. Ref: 2025 LHC 717; Bilal Muzaffar Heera etc. v. The State etc (Jail Appeal.62458/20, decided 04.03.2025).
records.title: Bilal Muzaffar Heera etc. v. The State etc (Jail Appeal.62458/20, decided 04.03.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 12(2) CPC Application Before Family Court
records.heading: A section 12(2) CPC application is maintainable before a Family Court
records.text: An application under s. 12(2) CPC is maintainable before a Family Court despite exclusion of the CPC by s. 17 of the Family Courts Act, 1964. Issues need not always be framed, but where fraud and misrepresentation are alleged and a prima facie case exists, the application should not be dismissed summarily. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 249; Misbah Iftikhar v. Aleesa etc (Writ Petition-1234-23).
records.title: Misbah Iftikhar v. Aleesa etc (Writ Petition-1234-23)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Habeas Corpus Concerning Minors: Interim Custody Only
records.heading: Habeas corpus for minors is limited to interim custody in exceptional circumstances
records.text: The High Court may issue habeas corpus for minors under Art. 199(1)(b)(i) and s. 491 CrPC, but only in exceptional circumstances, such as very young children recently taken, no other remedy and urgency. Its role is limited to interim custody, leaving final custody to the Family Court. It may intervene in international child abduction. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 207; Syed Hassan Murtaza v. Mariya Bano Khan etc (WP 78185/23).
records.title: Syed Hassan Murtaza v. Mariya Bano Khan etc (WP 78185/23)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Execution Petitions: Art. 181 and s. 48 CPC
records.heading: Execution limitation under Art. 181 and section 48 CPC and revival of earlier petitions
records.text: Under Art. 181 an execution application must be made within three years of the decree, and s. 48 CPC sets a six year outer limit for a fresh application. An order that is merely suspensory leaves later proceedings a revival of the earlier one, and the third execution petition was held a revival of earlier timely petitions. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 286, PLJ 2024 Lahore 501; Sabir Ali v. Munawar, & others (Civil Revision No.2938 of 2022).
records.title: Sabir Ali v. Munawar, & others (Civil Revision No.2938 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Plea of Guilt Recorded Mid-Trial
records.heading: A plea of guilt may be recorded at any stage but a capital trial still needs evidence
records.text: Nothing prohibits recording a plea of guilt at any stage of trial, even after the accused denied the charge, and it does not offend fair trial if he waives it. The court must examine why he admits guilt, and a capital trial must not end on the admission alone, as evidence must be recorded. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 235; The State v. Muhammad Altaf (Crl.Appeal-482-22); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Altaf (Crl.Appeal-482-22)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of FIR Under Article 199
records.heading: Quashing an FIR under Article 199 is for exceptional cases only
records.text: Quashing an FIR under Art. 199 is for exceptional cases, where the record shows no offence can be established or the FIR is an abuse of process or without authority. It is not available where allegations disclose a prima facie case, and a pending civil dispute is no ground for quashing straightaway. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 254; The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore v. Chaudhry Mohammad Khan, etc. (C.P.L.A.671-L/2017).
records.title: The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore v. Chaudhry Mohammad Khan, etc. (C.P.L.A.671-L/2017)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Simultaneous Civil and Criminal Proceedings
records.heading: Pending civil proceedings do not bar criminal proceedings on the same matter
records.text: Criminal proceedings are not barred by pending civil proceedings, and civil and criminal proceedings can proceed simultaneously. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 254; The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore v. Chaudhry Mohammad Khan, etc. (C.P.L.A.671-L/2017).
records.title: The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab, Lahore v. Chaudhry Mohammad Khan, etc. (C.P.L.A.671-L/2017)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Second Marriage Without Arbitration Council Permission; Khula
records.heading: A second marriage without Arbitration Council permission is a ground for dissolution
records.text: Marrying again without Arbitration Council permission is a ground for dissolution under s. 2(iia) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, which any wife may invoke. Judicial khula dissolves marriage on the wife's demand, even against the husband's will, but a court cannot order it on its own when the wife has not sought it. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 262; Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019).
records.title: Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikah Nama: Presumption of Truth and Construction
records.heading: A Nikah Nama is a public document with a strong presumption of truth
records.text: The Nikah Nama is a marriage contract and a public document with a strong presumption of truth. Its columns and headings are construed in light of the parties' intention, and the court cannot imply a stipulation inconsistent with its express terms or add one merely because it seems reasonable. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 262; Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019).
records.title: Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Obligatory, Mehr-ul-Misal and Prompt Presumption
records.heading: Dower is obligatory and presumed prompt and reasonable where unspecified
records.text: Dower is an essential requirement of a valid marriage contract, and where not specified a reasonable dower, Mehr-ul-Misal, is presumed. Where the nature of payment is unspecified, dower is presumed prompt under s. 10 of the 1961 Ordinance, and it may be in cash, property or both. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 262; Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019).
records.title: Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dissolution of Marriage: Clause (iia) Survives; Cruelty
records.heading: Clause (iia) of the 1939 Act took effect and cruelty was wrongly applied for dissolution
records.text: Clause (iia) of s. 2 of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, inserted by the 1961 Ordinance, took effect and was never amended or repealed in the 1939 Act. The High Court erred in ordering dissolution on the ground of cruelty. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 262; Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019).
records.title: Dr. Faryal Maqsood & another v. Khuram Shehzad Durani & others (C.P.L.A.308-P/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Attorney's Powers: Settlement on Special Oath
records.heading: An attorney's power to contest does not extend to proposing settlement on special oath
records.text: An attorney's power to pursue a contest under para 8 of the power of attorney did not extend to proposing a settlement on special oath. Offering it transgressed her powers and amounted to surrender, and any compromise must be tested against the powers delegated. Ref: Sultan Mahmood and another v. Munir Ahmad (Civil Appeal No. 550-L of 2009 and C.M.A. No. 2063-L of 2016).
records.title: Sultan Mahmood and another v. Munir Ahmad (Civil Appeal No. 550-L of 2009 and C.M.A. No. 2063-L of 2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Claim From 500 Metres
records.heading: A claimed eyewitness view from 500 metres is far-fetched
records.text: The prosecution must establish the credibility of its witnesses, and distance of observation is critical. At 500 metres even a person with good eyesight cannot discern the details of an event, so the witnesses' graphic account was far-fetched and unacceptable. Ref: Ameeruddin v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 198/2023, decided 04.03.2025).
records.title: Ameeruddin v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 198/2023, decided 04.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Voice Identification and Retracted Confession
records.heading: Uncorroborated voice identification and a retracted confession cannot safely sustain conviction
records.text: Voice recognition lacks a standardised scientific framework and, without corroboration such as call records, witnesses or forensic analysis, is unreliable, especially where conviction carries death or life imprisonment. Any doubt favours the accused, and a retracted confession as the sole basis for conviction raises serious concern. Ref: Imtiaz and Naeem v. The State (Jail Petition No. 438/2018, decided 25.02.2025).
records.title: Imtiaz and Naeem v. The State (Jail Petition No. 438/2018, decided 25.02.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Contradicting Witness With Statement in Another Case: Art. 151(3)
records.heading: A witness may be contradicted with his statement in another case under Art. 151(3) QSO
records.text: Under Art. 151(3) QSO a witness's credit may be impeached by a former inconsistent statement, which may be used for contradiction and not as substantive evidence. A constable's statement in one narcotics case could be put to him in another, and the accused was acquitted. Ref: Muhammad Waseem v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.448 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Waseem v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.448 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance From Missing Person: Presumption of Death
records.heading: Inheritance from a missing person arises from the date of presumed death
records.text: Inheritance rights in a missing person's estate arise from the date of presumed death and not retroactively, and heirs dying earlier are disqualified. Under Arts. 123 and 124 QSO a person shown alive within thirty years is presumed alive, rebuttable by evidence. If no date is shown, death is presumed at the date the suit was instituted. Ref: Iqbal Ali Khan & others v. Naseeb Ali Khan & others (C.A.44-P/2012, decided 26.02.2025); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Iqbal Ali Khan & others v. Naseeb Ali Khan & others (C.A.44-P/2012, decided 26.02.2025)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Child Justice Approach and Restorative Justice
records.heading: Courts must adopt a child justice approach prioritising the child's best interests
records.text: Courts must adopt a child justice and child-centred approach that prioritises the best interests of the child. This covers children in conflict with the law, who need rehabilitation, and children in contact with the law, who need protection, and the post also refers to restorative justice. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 247; Malik Mahmood Ahmad Khan v. Malik Moazam Mahmood, etc. (C.P.L.A.2250-L/2016); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Malik Mahmood Ahmad Khan v. Malik Moazam Mahmood, etc. (C.P.L.A.2250-L/2016)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Scope of Revisional Powers
records.heading: Revisional jurisdiction is limited to findings unsupported by evidence or from misreading the record
records.text: Revisional jurisdiction is limited. It may be invoked where a finding of fact that influences the decision is unsupported by evidence or results from misreading or non-reading of the record, and the proceedings are before a subordinate criminal court. The High Court may then reappraise the evidence. Ref: 2025 LHC 752; Hafeez Ahmad v. State etc (Crl. Revision 400-18, decided 03.03.2025).
records.title: Hafeez Ahmad v. State etc (Crl. Revision 400-18, decided 03.03.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Non-Exhibition of Documents and Identity of Accused
records.heading: Undisclosed features in the crime report and unexplained identification leave identity unclear
records.text: The post addresses the effect of non-exhibition of articles or documents during trial. Where the petitioner's features were not disclosed in the crime report and the complainant gave no explanation of how he identified the petitioner, the identity of the petitioner remained unclear. Ref: 2025 LHC 752; Hafeez Ahmad v. State etc (Crl. Revision 400-18, decided 03.03.2025).
records.title: Hafeez Ahmad v. State etc (Crl. Revision 400-18, decided 03.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Unbroken Chain
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence needs an unbroken chain and a missing link benefits the accused
records.text: Where the prosecution case rests on circumstantial evidence, each circumstance must be linked to the next to form a complete, continuous and unbroken chain firmly connecting the accused with the offence. If any link is missing, the benefit goes to the accused. Ref: 2025 LHC 762; Muhammad Arif v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 175-21, decided 20.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 175-21, decided 20.02.2025)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Report: Safe Transmission of Sealed Parcels
records.heading: A DNA report is unreliable without proof of safe transmission of sealed parcels
records.text: A DNA report is unreliable if safe transmission of the sealed parcels to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency has not been proved. The accused was acquitted. Ref: 2025 LHC 762; Muhammad Arif v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 175-21, decided 20.02.2025); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 175-21, decided 20.02.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Breach of Trust: Essential Ingredients
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation or disposal
records.text: The offence under s. 406 PPC requires entrustment of property by a person reposing confidence, and dishonest misappropriation or conversion to own use. It is also made out where the property is dishonestly used or disposed of in violation of a legal direction or of an express or implied contract touching the discharge of the trust. Ref: 2025 LHC 788; Phaphi alias Fatima and another v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 7172-B/2025, decided 10.03.2025).
records.title: Phaphi alias Fatima and another v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 7172-B/2025, decided 10.03.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Delayed Nomination of Known Accused: Bail
records.heading: Delayed nomination of a known accused requires verification at trial and supports bail
records.text: Where the accused was related to and already known to the complainant and the injured, but was not nominated in the FIR or in the injured's statement made while medically stable, later nomination through supplementary statements requires evidential verification at trial. Bail allowed. Ref: 2025 LHC 804; Muhammad Kashif Shehzad v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 77329/24, decided 11.03.2025); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Kashif Shehzad v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 77329/24, decided 11.03.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Succession Certificate: Summary Procedure, No Bar of O. II R. 2
records.heading: Succession certificate proceedings are summary and a second application is not barred
records.text: Proceedings under the Succession Act, 1925 are summary and a special law. The Act allows more than one certificate and does not restrict a further application for an omitted claim, so the CPC, including O. II R. 2, does not bar a second application. The High Court's contrary view was unsustainable and the matter was remanded to the Trial Court. Ref: 2025 SCMR 579, 2025 PLC (C.S.) 575; Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public & another (C.P.L.A. 256-Q/2020).
records.title: Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public & another (C.P.L.A. 256-Q/2020)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Family Pension: Eldest Unmarried Daughter
records.heading: An eldest unmarried daughter may draw family pension under the amended Rules
records.text: After the 1999 amendment to the Rules, the eldest unmarried daughter of a deceased government officer may draw her share of the monthly family pension until marriage, and the next eldest unmarried daughter then becomes entitled. The High Court's decision based on the unamended Balochistan Civil Servants Pension Rules, 1989 was set aside. Ref: 2025 SCMR 579, 2025 PLC (C.S.) 575; Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public & another (C.P.L.A. 256-Q/2020).
records.title: Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public & another (C.P.L.A. 256-Q/2020)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Retraction Distinguished from Hostile Witness
records.heading: Retraction of a statement does not make a witness hostile
records.text: Mere retraction of an earlier statement by a witness does not make the witness hostile. Hostility means deliberate intent to deviate from the truth or act against the interests of the party calling the witness, whereas retraction is the withdrawal of a statement or accusation. Ref: 2025 SCMR 547; Ghous Bakhsh v. The State (Crl.A. 294/2020).
records.title: Ghous Bakhsh v. The State (Crl.A. 294/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. V CPC: Service of Summons, Audi Alteram Partem
records.heading: Service of summons under Order V CPC must respect the right to be heard
records.text: Under Order V CPC service on a defendant may be effected personally, by registered post, through an authorised agent or a male member of the family. No one should be condemned unheard, and technicalities should be avoided so that every litigant has a fair opportunity to plead and defend. Ref: 2025 SCMR 564; Hashim Khan and others v. Mst. Musarat Begum and others (C.P.L.A. 625-P/2024).
records.title: Hashim Khan and others v. Mst. Musarat Begum and others (C.P.L.A. 625-P/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Wakalatnama: Party Bound by Counsel's Acts
records.heading: A party is bound by counsel's acts under a wakalatnama unless restricted
records.text: A wakalatnama delegates to counsel all powers including withdrawal of a suit or application, and a party is bound by counsel's statement unless the power of attorney restricts it. The petitioner, who withdrew his application under s. 9(6) Family Courts Act, 1964 through engaged counsel, was held to have acquiesced in the ex parte decree. Ref: 2025 SCMR 558; Muhammad Ejaz v. Judge Family Court, Hafizabad, etc (C.P.L.A. 2759-L/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ejaz v. Judge Family Court, Hafizabad, etc (C.P.L.A. 2759-L/2023)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Charagah Land: Concept and Leasing Restrictions
records.heading: Charagah land can be leased only for a public purpose with Board of Revenue approval
records.text: Charagah is common village grazing land reserved for collective use and not to be allotted, sold or exchanged, though usable for public purposes. Under the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act 1912 it can be leased only with Board of Revenue approval, for a public purpose and for a specific period, and not indefinitely to a lambardar for his tenure. Ref: 2025 SCMR 459, PLJ 2025 SC 168; Muhammad Yousaf v. Member Judicial - IV, Board of Revenue, Punjab Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 3297/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Member Judicial - IV, Board of Revenue, Punjab Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 3297/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence and Single Doubt: Acquittal
records.heading: Without direct evidence a missing link in the circumstantial chain leads to acquittal
records.text: Where there is no direct evidence, every circumstance must link into a continuous chain, and a missing link benefits the accused. Recovery of a rope from an open place accessible to the public and a motive introduced after unexplained delay did not prove the case. Conviction for qatl-i-amd set aside and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2025 SCMR 552; Sikandar Ali @ Bhola v. The State (J.P. 29/2021).
records.title: Sikandar Ali @ Bhola v. The State (J.P. 29/2021)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partition Suit: Not Barred by Res Judicata or O. II R. 2
records.heading: A partition suit is not barred by res judicata or O. II R. 2 CPC
records.text: A suit for partition is an independent right and is not barred as res judicata by an earlier suit for declaration under s. 42 Specific Relief Act that was not decided on merits. It is also not barred by O. II R. 2 CPC, and the plaint could not be rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC. Ref: 2025 SCMR 430; Zakirullah (decd.) thr. LRs & others v. Muhammad Rehman & others (C.P.L.A. 159-P/2014).
records.title: Zakirullah (decd.) thr. LRs & others v. Muhammad Rehman & others (C.P.L.A. 159-P/2014)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Copies of Forensic Video Evidence to Accused
records.heading: Copies of audio or video evidence must be supplied to the accused beforehand
records.text: Before audio or video evidence is used, a copy must be supplied to the accused to avoid surprise evidence. As such material is collected during investigation, it falls within s. 162 Cr.P.C. and s. 265-C Cr.P.C., and copies may be provided at any stage if essential for a just decision. Art. 164 QSO gives such evidence special status. Ref: PLJ 2023 CrC 320, 2023 PCrLJ 1394; Numan alias Nomi and others v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 364, 380, 382 & 407/2020, heard 19.10.2022); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Numan alias Nomi and others v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 364, 380, 382 & 407/2020, heard 19.10.2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Willingness of Vendee
records.heading: A vendee who paid the vendor's bank liability showed readiness to perform
records.text: The vendee who paid the vendor's bank liability to obtain a no objection certificate showed continuous readiness to perform, while the vendor repeatedly tried to establish breaches. There was no breach by the vendee, so a suit for specific performance was the proper remedy. The decree was upheld and leave to appeal refused. Ref: 2025 SCMR 495; Zeeshan Pervez (Late) through Legal Heirs v. Muhammad Nasir (C.P.L.A. 812-K/2022, decided 21.05.2024); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Zeeshan Pervez (Late) through Legal Heirs v. Muhammad Nasir (C.P.L.A. 812-K/2022, decided 21.05.2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Interpretation of Contract: Contra Proferentem
records.heading: Contract meaning is found through a reasonable person and, if ambiguous, common sense
records.text: A reasonable person, considering the context of the contract, should be able to identify its meaning without ambiguity. If ambiguity persists, the meaning that accords best with common sense prevails. Ref: 2025 SCMR 495; Zeeshan Pervez (Late) through Legal Heirs v. Muhammad Nasir (C.P.L.A. 812-K/2022, decided 21.05.2024); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Zeeshan Pervez (Late) through Legal Heirs v. Muhammad Nasir (C.P.L.A. 812-K/2022, decided 21.05.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. I R. 10 CPC: Proper and Necessary Party
records.heading: Impleadment under O. I R. 10 CPC should be decided liberally where a party is affected
records.text: On applications under O. I R. 10 CPC the court should exercise its discretion liberally and without a narrow approach, especially where a party is likely to be affected by the judgment and its presence helps the court adjudicate effectively. Concurrent orders impleading the respondents were upheld. Ref: 2025 SCMR 515.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Firearm Injury at Thigh: Section 324 PPC and Bail
records.heading: A firearm injury at the thigh prima facie attracts section 324 PPC and bail is refused
records.text: An injury below the knee makes the applicability of s. 324 PPC a matter for further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. A firearm injury at the thigh, where the femoral artery lies, prima facie attracts s. 324 PPC. Bail refused. Ref: 2025 LHC 822; Nasrullah alias Nasru v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 1584/25, decided 13.03.2025); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Nasrullah alias Nasru v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 1584/25, decided 13.03.2025)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: PECA s. 43 Amendment: Prospective Application
records.heading: The 2025 amendment to section 43 PECA is substantive and applies prospectively only
records.text: The 2025 amendment to s. 43 PECA, making offences under ss. 13 and 14 non-bailable, is substantive and not merely procedural. Bail in a bailable offence is a vested right, so the amendment applies prospectively only. Ref: 2025 LHC 846; Muhammad Rizwan v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 10519-B-24, decided 11.03.2025); Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar.
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 10519-B-24, decided 11.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Autopsy, Inquest, Medico-Ocular Conflict and Identification
records.heading: Identification fails where the claimed source of light was never produced
records.text: The judgment discusses use of the autopsy and inquest report, including rigor mortis, to test whether the FIR was ante-dated, the effect of conflict between medical and ocular evidence, and the presumption under Art. 129 QSO. Identification failed where the torch said to give light was never produced or taken into possession. Ref: 2025 LHC 825; Sultan v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 328-23, decided 06.03.2025); Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar.
records.title: Sultan v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 328-23, decided 06.03.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Court Witnesses: ss. 265-F and 540 CrPC
records.heading: A court may summon a witness under section 265-F(2) CrPC unless the call is vexatious
records.text: Under s. 265-F(2) CrPC the trial court may summon a person acquainted with the facts as a witness, but may refrain where the witness is called for vexation, delay or defeating the ends of justice. The judgment also considers the purpose of court witnesses under s. 540 CrPC and the parameters of s. 103 CrPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 825; Sultan v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 328-23, decided 06.03.2025); Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar.
records.title: Sultan v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 328-23, decided 06.03.2025)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Test of Terrorism: Motivation and Design
records.heading: Terrorism is tested by motivation, object and purpose and not by consequence
records.text: Acts under s. 6(2) of the 1997 Act fall before special courts where committed with design to intimidate the government, public or a section of society. The test is the motivation, object and purpose and not the consequence. Killing of a constable was not terrorism where it was not proved he was in uniform and on duty, and gravity alone is no yardstick. Ref: Muhammad Asim v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad (Crl.A. 623/2022, decided 24.02.2025); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Muhammad Asim v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad (Crl.A. 623/2022, decided 24.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Source of Light and Medico-Ocular Conflict
records.heading: Doubtful identification at night and a medico-ocular conflict are fatal to the prosecution
records.text: Where an occurrence at night is reported without any source of light in the FIR and none was recovered, identification of the accused is doubtful. A medico-ocular conflict about the number of injuries on the deceased is fatal to the prosecution case. Ref: Chetan v. The State (Crl.A. 94/2023, decided 06.03.2025); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Chetan v. The State (Crl.A. 94/2023, decided 06.03.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotics Samples
records.heading: Safe custody of narcotics must be proved by Register XIX entries and road certificate
records.text: The prosecution must prove safe custody and transmission of case property by documentary evidence, namely the Register No. XIX entry and road certificate under the Police Rules, 1934. The bare oral statement of the muharrir or malkhana in-charge without the registers is not admissible proof. Ref: Jeehand v. The State through Prosecutor General Balochistan (Crl.P.L.A. 1187/2021, decided 14.03.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Jeehand v. The State through Prosecutor General Balochistan (Crl.P.L.A. 1187/2021, decided 14.03.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Delay in FIR in Rape Case
records.heading: Delay in reporting rape is immaterial where the victim was blackmailed and feared dishonour
records.text: A delay of one and a half months in lodging the FIR was immaterial where the victim was blackmailed over nude pictures and kept silent to protect her and her family's honour. Delay in reporting offences touching honour and reputation may deter a victim and her family from approaching the police. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 72, 2025 PCrLJ 589; Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Autopsy and Death by Vasovagal Inhibition
records.heading: Death from vasovagal inhibition is not natural death and falls under section 316 PPC
records.text: A seventeen hour delay in autopsy, explained by the unavailability of senior doctors at night, did not discredit reliable eyewitness and medical evidence. Death from vasovagal inhibition or shock due to blunt trauma is not natural death and falls under s. 316 PPC. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC altered to s. 316 PPC with ten years' rigorous imprisonment. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 555; Shahid Ali Makhi v. State (Jail Appeal 234893/18).
records.title: Shahid Ali Makhi v. State (Jail Appeal 234893/18)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Diyat Payable at Rate on Date of Decision
records.heading: Diyat is payable at the rate prevailing when the court decides the case
records.text: The amount of diyat is imposed at the rate prevalent in the fiscal year when the court decides the case, and not at the rate on the date of the occurrence. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 555; Shahid Ali Makhi v. State (Jail Appeal 234893/18).
records.title: Shahid Ali Makhi v. State (Jail Appeal 234893/18)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ex-officio Justice of Peace: Res Judicata, ss. 22-A, 22-B
records.heading: Res judicata applies to Justice of Peace applications but does not bar a private complaint
records.text: The Ex-officio Justice of Peace exercises quasi-judicial functions under s. 22-A(6) CrPC, and res judicata applies to applications seeking a direction to register an FIR under s. 154 CrPC. It does not bar a private complaint, which is an independent statutory remedy. The High Court declined to interfere. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 447.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 249 CrPC: Scope
records.heading: Section 249 CrPC lets a magistrate stop proceedings but is not a remedy for staying them
records.text: Section 249 CrPC allows a magistrate to stop proceedings at any stage, other than those on a private complaint, and release the accused without a verdict and without a bond. The order must be reasoned and is open to revision. The section is not a remedy for staying criminal proceedings. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 460, 2024 LHC 3306; Zahid Maqsood Butt v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 3568/24, decided 07.06.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Zahid Maqsood Butt v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 3568/24, decided 07.06.2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Parallel Civil and Criminal Proceedings: Stay
records.heading: Civil and criminal proceedings can run side by side without res judicata or double jeopardy
records.text: Civil and criminal proceedings can run side by side. Res judicata and double jeopardy do not apply because the standards of proof differ. Stopping proceedings is distinct from stay of proceedings and stay of prosecution, and the post notes that misappropriation and entitlement to an amount are different subject matters. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 460, 2024 LHC 3306; Zahid Maqsood Butt v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 3568/24, decided 07.06.2024); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Zahid Maqsood Butt v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 3568/24, decided 07.06.2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Death Sentence Reduced to Life
records.heading: Unknown cause of quarrel and an unsent knife justified reducing death to life imprisonment
records.text: The prosecution proved its case under s. 302(b) PPC on ocular evidence supported by medical evidence. The knife was not sent to the Forensic Science Agency and the immediate cause of the quarrel remained unknown, which were mitigating circumstances. The death sentence was converted to life imprisonment and the appeal dismissed with that modification. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 508, PLJ 2024 CrC 1240; Gulraiz v. The State (Jail Appeal 69125/20).
records.title: Gulraiz v. The State (Jail Appeal 69125/20)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Scope of Section 34 CPC
records.heading: Authority on the scope of section 34 CPC
records.text: Authority on the scope of s. 34 CPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 906; Shaheen Baig v. Zaheer Ahmed Loan (Civil Revision 69585/23, decided 20.02.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Shaheen Baig v. Zaheer Ahmed Loan (Civil Revision 69585/23, decided 20.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Meaning of Reasonable Doubt
records.heading: Reasonable doubt is one a person of common prudence would genuinely entertain
records.text: Benefit of doubt rests on a reasonable doubt, which is one a person of common prudence would entertain, genuine and inherent in the circumstances, and not artificial, imaginary or exaggerated. The judgment also states that the Western rule of falsus in uno falsus in omnibus has been modified in this jurisdiction. Ref: Sher Afzal v. The State (Crl.A. 229/2021, decided 18.03.2025); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Sher Afzal v. The State (Crl.A. 229/2021, decided 18.03.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 12(2) CPC: Locus of Legal Heirs of Donor
records.heading: Non-mention of family members in a gift suit is not fraud under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: Mere non-mention of some family members in a suit on a gift is not fraud under s. 12(2) CPC unless it alters the fundamental basis of the decision. The donor had actively participated in the proceedings and conceded the gift, which estops his legal heirs from raising belated claims of fraud. Ref: 2025 LHC 897; Bashiran Bibi & 3 Others v. Muhammad Ameen etc (C.M. (Civil) 73824/22, decided 20.02.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Bashiran Bibi & 3 Others v. Muhammad Ameen etc (C.M. (Civil) 73824/22, decided 20.02.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Minimum Sentence for the Offence
records.heading: Bail decisions must consider the minimum sentence provided for the offence
records.text: In deciding bail, the court has to consider the minimum sentence provided for the alleged offence. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 517.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Toshakhana Gift Case: Further Inquiry, Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: A later Office Memorandum is not retrospective, making the Toshakhana case one of further inquiry
records.text: The later Office Memorandum on non-deposit of gifts did not apply retrospectively, and the earlier memorandum did not attach punitive action to non-deposit, so the case was one of further inquiry. The co-accused wife already had bail, the evidence was largely documentary and trial was not near. Post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 498.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Blasphemy Offences: s. 196 CrPC Complaint Requirement
records.heading: Cognizance of section 295-A PPC offences needs a government complaint under section 196 CrPC
records.text: Under s. 196 CrPC the court cannot take cognizance of offences including s. 295-A PPC without a complaint by order or authority of the Federal or Provincial Government or an empowered officer. No such complaint had been made, which supported bail. The applicant was admitted to post-arrest bail. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 526.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Deficient Evidence in FIA Case: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Vague recovery and no company record make an FIA case one of further inquiry
records.text: No cellular company record linked the applicant to the SIM, the recovery and seizure were vague, the phone was not shown to be sealed and no call data record was obtained. The case was one of further inquiry, and the FIA was directed to expand its investigation and seek the required approvals. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 526.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Surety Amount: Reduction by Court, s. 499 CrPC
records.heading: A court has power to reduce a surety amount
records.text: The court has power to reduce a surety amount. On the peculiar facts, the Supreme Court took a lenient view and reduced the total amount to Rs.100,000, to be deposited within one month. The surety's appeal was disposed of accordingly. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 506.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Presence and Absconsion
records.heading: Absconsion alone cannot support conviction or cure defects in the prosecution case
records.text: For eyewitnesses the foremost question is whether they saw the occurrence themselves and could identify the assailants. Absconsion is a relevant circumstance but cannot alone support conviction, and it cannot make up for defects in the prosecution case. Ref: Muhammad Masood @ Mithu v. The State (J.P. 441/2017, decided 10.03.2025); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Masood @ Mithu v. The State (J.P. 441/2017, decided 10.03.2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Willingness and Non-Deposit of Balance
records.heading: Failure to deposit the balance consideration for seven years showed unwillingness to perform
records.text: Specific performance is discretionary, and the court must see whether the buyer was willing to perform at the relevant time. Failure to deposit the balance consideration until the trial court decided, after about seven years, indicated unwillingness. The post also states the limited scope of s. 100 CPC. Ref: Muhammad Azam & others v. Muhammad Aijaz (C.A. 99-K/2022, decided 20.03.2025); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Azam & others v. Muhammad Aijaz (C.A. 99-K/2022, decided 20.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Inquest Report
records.heading: An ocular account contradicted by the inquest report collapses the prosecution case
records.text: Where the ocular account says the deceased died in the hospital but column 24 of the inquest report shows the body lying in the complainant's area, the prosecution case collapses and the benefit goes to the convict. Ref: 2025 LHC 953; The State v. Ali Akbar Zia (Murder Reference 2562218.8-20, decided 11.03.2025).
records.title: The State v. Ali Akbar Zia (Murder Reference 2562218.8-20, decided 11.03.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Fraud on Court Not Proved
records.heading: A section 12(2) CPC application fails where fraud on the court is not proved
records.text: An application under s. 12(2) CPC by some legal heirs of a donor against a judgment upholding a gift was held not maintainable, as fraud was not proved by cogent evidence. The donor had himself appeared and confirmed the gift, and the dispute concerned a concluded lifetime gift and not inheritance. Application dismissed. Ref: 2025 LHC 897; Bashiran Bibi etc. v. Muhammad Aameen etc. (C.M. 73824/2022 in C.R. 1593/2005); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Bashiran Bibi etc. v. Muhammad Aameen etc. (C.M. 73824/2022 in C.R. 1593/2005)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Recruitment: Non-Disclosure of Past Acquittal
records.heading: Non-disclosure of a past acquittal is not concealment and does not bar recruitment
records.text: Non-disclosure of past involvement in a case ending in acquittal is not concealment and does not make a candidate unfit for recruitment. Mere FIR registration does not show bad character, since good character is presumed, and the right to employment is part of the right to livelihood under Arts. 9, 18, 27 and 38(c) of the Constitution. Ref: 2025 LHC 965; Umar Sheeraz v. Govt. of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 2062-23, decided 07.01.2025); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Umar Sheeraz v. Govt. of Punjab etc. (Writ Petition 2062-23, decided 07.01.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Outraging Modesty versus Sexual Abuse; Anti-Rape Act 2021
records.heading: Sexual intent, physical violation and severity mark escalation from outraging modesty to sexual abuse
records.text: The post sets out elements marking when an act under s. 354 PPC escalates to sexual abuse, namely sexual intent, physical violation, and severity and impact. Courts must interpret the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021 in line with legislative intent, and may alter or delete charges during trial. Ref: 2025 LHC 987; Kiran Bibi v. A.S.J. etc. (Crl. Revision 21000/24, decided 06.03.2025); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Kiran Bibi v. A.S.J. etc. (Crl. Revision 21000/24, decided 06.03.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Compounding s. 345(1) CrPC Before Challan
records.heading: An offence compounded before the section 173 report may end in a cancellation report
records.text: Where an offence compoundable without court permission under s. 345(1) CrPC is compromised before the s. 173 report, the police may record the compromise and submit a cancellation report. The magistrate may verify the compromise before ordering cancellation. Ref: 2024 LHC 6543; Muhammad Sajjad v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 8745-B-22, decided 19.07.2024); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Muhammad Sajjad v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 8745-B-22, decided 19.07.2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 324 PPC: Ingredients and ss. 71, 337-W
records.heading: Section 324 PPC does not require the result to be achieved and hurt is separately punishable
records.text: Section 324 PPC has two components, the act done with intention or knowledge to commit qatl-i-amd and its effect, and failure to achieve the result is immaterial. Where hurt is caused the offender may be separately convicted. Section 71 PPC limits punishment for composite offences, but s. 337-W requires separate punishment for each hurt. Ref: 2025 LHC 997; Abdul Hameed alias Meeda v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 54-20, decided 06.01.2025); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Abdul Hameed alias Meeda v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 54-20, decided 06.01.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Daily Diary: Inspection by Sessions Judge
records.heading: District and Sessions Judges may inspect police station daily diary registers
records.text: Under Art. 167 of the Police Order 2002 the District and Sessions Judge may call for and inspect police station daily diary registers. The Inspector General of Police Punjab was directed to give all District and Sessions Judges online access within three months. Ref: 2025 LHC 1007; Mst. Kosar Mai v. SHO etc (Crl. Misc. Habeas Corpus 2446-H-20, decided 28.02.2025); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Mst. Kosar Mai v. SHO etc (Crl. Misc. Habeas Corpus 2446-H-20, decided 28.02.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 and s. 12(2) CPC: Civil Servants' Cases
records.heading: Procedural law cannot prolong litigation and full CPC application would defeat speedy justice in service cases
records.text: The judgment addresses the scope of O. VII R. 11 and s. 12(2) CPC, the meaning of fraud, misrepresentation and want of jurisdiction, and the doctrine of merger. It states that procedural laws cannot be used to prolong litigation, and that full application of the CPC would defeat speedy justice in civil servants' cases. Ref: Pakistan Railways thr. its Chairman Pakistan Railways, Islamabad & another v. Muhammad Amin (deced) thr. LRS (C.P.L.A. 512/2022, decided 11.12.2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Pakistan Railways thr. its Chairman Pakistan Railways, Islamabad & another v. Muhammad Amin (deced) thr. LRS (C.P.L.A. 512/2022, decided 11.12.2024)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Doctrine of Election: Bar on Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: A party who elects a remedy under the 1977 Act cannot invoke Civil Court jurisdiction for the same relief
records.text: Appellants who invoked the remedies under the 1977 Act, including a declaration under MLR 115 and appeals to the Land Commissioner, elected that forum. Under the doctrine of election they cannot then invoke the original jurisdiction of the Civil Court for the same relief. Ref: Qazi Mumtaz Hussain v. Government of Sindh through its Secretary Revenue & others (C.A. 112-K/2022, decided 21.03.2025); Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui.
records.title: Qazi Mumtaz Hussain v. Government of Sindh through its Secretary Revenue & others (C.A. 112-K/2022, decided 21.03.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Court Witness s. 540 CrPC: Given-Up Eyewitness
records.heading: A given-up eyewitness cannot be summoned as a court witness under section 540 CrPC
records.text: A third eyewitness given up by the prosecution, whose evidence is of the same nature as the two produced, cannot be summoned as a court witness under s. 540 CrPC, though the accused may produce him as a defence witness. The accused cannot compel the prosecution to produce a witness, and the quality of eyewitness testimony matters more than number. Ref: 2025 LHC 1023; Ghulam Murtaza v. A.S.J Faisalabad etc (Crl. Revision 74970/2, decided 17.03.2025); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Ghulam Murtaza v. A.S.J Faisalabad etc (Crl. Revision 74970/2, decided 17.03.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Medical Officer Not Cross-Examined
records.heading: Absence of force in medical evidence does not defeat lack of consent from fear and intoxication
records.text: Though the medical evidence did not show force, the victim's evidence of intoxication and fear showed she could not resist, and the act was against her will and consent under s. 375 PPC. The Medical Officer was not cross-examined on the medico-legal report, and the accused was found potent. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 72, 2025 PCrLJ 589; Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Victim as Sole Eyewitness Sufficient
records.heading: A credible victim as sole eyewitness can safely support conviction
records.text: The victim was the sole eyewitness. Her account was consistent with the FIR and unshaken in cross-examination, and her admitted acquaintance with the accused supported the prosecution case. Being credible and confidence inspiring, her statement alone could safely support conviction under ss. 365-B and 376 PPC. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 72, 2025 PCrLJ 589; Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Bad Character Irrelevant; Art. 27 State of Mind
records.heading: Bad character is irrelevant but attachment to the victim is relevant to state of mind
records.text: Bad character of an accused is not relevant in criminal cases under Art. 68 QSO. However, evidence that the appellant had long been attached to the victim and wanted to marry her was relevant under Art. 27 QSO to his state of mind and intention to commit rape and prepare nude pictures. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 72, 2025 PCrLJ 589; Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Basit v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Examination of Complainant Through Video Link
records.heading: Examination of a complainant abroad through video link should be encouraged
records.text: Examination of witnesses and court proceedings through video link should be encouraged. The Trial Court's order refusing to examine a complainant residing in Germany by video link was set aside and arrangements directed, with the complainant's identity to be ascertained before his statement is recorded. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 523.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape Conviction: Confidence Inspiring Testimony and DNA
records.heading: Confidence inspiring testimony corroborated by DNA proves rape and consent from fear is no consent
records.text: The victim's confidence inspiring testimony that intercourse was forced upon her, corroborated by DNA evidence that the appellant was the biological father of her child, proved rape under s. 376 PPC beyond reasonable doubt. Consent obtained through fear is no consent under s. 90 PPC. Conviction and sentence of fourteen years confirmed and appeals dismissed. Ref: Shahzad Ahmed v. The State and another (Crl. A. 294/2022, with Jail Appeal 302/2022, announced 03.03.2025); Justice Tariq Mehmood Jahangiri; Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Shahzad Ahmed v. The State and another (Crl. A. 294/2022, with Jail Appeal 302/2022, announced 03.03.2025)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Report Corroborating Rape Victim
records.heading: A DNA report showing paternity of the victim's child corroborates her version of rape
records.text: A DNA report showing the appellant as biological father of the baby born to the victim corroborated her version of the act of intercourse. The trial court had also treated delay in reporting rape as not unnatural given the shame attached to it. The High Court confirmed the conviction. Ref: Shahzad Ahmed v. The State and another (Crl. A. 294/2022, with Jail Appeal 302/2022, announced 03.03.2025); Justice Tariq Mehmood Jahangiri; Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Shahzad Ahmed v. The State and another (Crl. A. 294/2022, with Jail Appeal 302/2022, announced 03.03.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Maintainability Versus Entitlement to Relief
records.heading: Maintainability of a case is decided before entitlement to relief
records.text: If a case is not maintainable the court does not examine its merits. Entitlement to relief concerns the claimant's substantive right to the remedy, decided on evidence and law, and is considered only after maintainability is established. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 207; Syed Hassan Murtaza v. Mariya Bano Khan etc (WP 78185/23).
records.title: Syed Hassan Murtaza v. Mariya Bano Khan etc (WP 78185/23)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Stolen Property s. 411 PPC: Onus and Bail
records.heading: Mere possession of stolen property is not an offence under section 411 PPC
records.text: Mere possession of stolen property does not constitute an offence under s. 411 PPC, and the prosecution must prove dishonest receipt or retention with knowledge or reason to believe the property was stolen. If it fails to prove the basic ingredients, bail cannot be refused. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 517.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Sole Testimony of Victim of Sexual Abuse
records.heading: The reliable sole testimony of a sexual abuse victim suffices for conviction
records.text: The independent, straightforward and reliable sole testimony of a victim of sexual abuse suffices for conviction. Corroboration linking the accused to the offence is required where there is enmity or prior grudge, and passive submission out of fear is not consent. Ref: Shahzad Ahmed v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal 294 of 2022; Jail Appeal 302 of 2022, decided 03.03.2025).
records.title: Shahzad Ahmed v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal 294 of 2022; Jail Appeal 302 of 2022, decided 03.03.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Release of Accused by Investigating Officer under s. 169 CrPC
records.heading: An Investigating Officer cannot release accused on alibi affidavits as alibi is for the trial court
records.text: The Investigating Officer discharged accused named for kidnapping and snatching of trucks on the basis of affidavits supporting alibi, without investigating or recovering the trucks. The plea of alibi is for the trial court on evidence, so the action was illegal and arbitrary and the order was set aside. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 453.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 324 PPC: Applicability Without Repeated Firing
records.heading: Section 324 PPC is attracted once the accused presses the trigger
records.text: Once an accused presses the trigger, s. 324 PPC is attracted, and its application is judged by the number of accused, the weapon and the opportunity to complete the offence. Armed accused firing straight at two injured persons at a bus stop satisfied the ingredients, and the prosecution proved its case against two accused. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 470.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution Against Several Co-Defendants
records.heading: A decree against jointly and severally liable defendants may be executed against any or all
records.text: A plaintiff with a judgment against several co-defendants who are jointly and severally liable may execute against any one of them, any combination of them or all of them. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 263.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Surety Liability: s. 128 Contract Act
records.heading: A surety's liability under section 128 Contract Act is co-extensive with the principal debtor's
records.text: Section 128 of the Contract Act, 1872 fixes the extent of a surety's liability to the creditor, which is co-extensive with the principal debtor's and no more than what the principal debtor owes. A surety may limit its liability by a special contract. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 263.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Oral Agreement: Plaint Not Rejectable under O. VII R. 11
records.heading: An oral agreement plaint is not rejectable merely because every term is not spelt out
records.text: Where an oral agreement is pleaded from conversations, the plaintiff need not spell out every term, and ambiguity can be met by particulars under O. VI R. 5 CPC. Unspelt terms do not justify rejection under O. VII R. 11 CPC. The High Court set aside the lower courts' orders and remanded for decision on merits. Ref: PLD 2025 Kar 108.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Section 12(2) CPC: Nature and Procedure
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC lets a court annul its own judgment obtained by fraud or want of jurisdiction
records.text: Section 12(2) CPC, inserted by Ordinance X of 1980, lets a court annul its own judgment obtained by fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction. No procedure is prescribed, so by s. 141 CPC the court may decide summarily or frame issues. Concurrent findings tainted by patent illegality may be set aside in constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: 2025 LHC 1046; Mumtaz Ahmed v. Amjad Niaz Abbasi etc (WP 3639-19, decided 10.03.2025).
records.title: Mumtaz Ahmed v. Amjad Niaz Abbasi etc (WP 3639-19, decided 10.03.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Non-Production of Complaint Bearer in CNSA Case
records.heading: Authority on the effect of non-production of the complaint bearer in a CNSA case
records.text: Authority on the effect of non-production of the complaint bearer in a case under the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997. Ref: 2025 LHC 1029; Mst. Bisma v. State (Crl. Appeal 664-24, decided 17.03.2025); Justice Tariq Mahmood Bajwa.
records.title: Mst. Bisma v. State (Crl. Appeal 664-24, decided 17.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Extra Judicial Confession and DNA as Corroboration
records.heading: A silent witness to an extra judicial confession is doubtful and DNA cannot corroborate nothing
records.text: A witness who hears an extra judicial confession and does not react casts doubt on his conduct and testimony, so a circumstantial case built on it fails. Where there is no substantial evidence, a DNA report as corroboration has nothing to corroborate and is of no help. Ref: 2025 LHC 1052; Muhammad Waqas v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 17977/20, decided 13.03.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 17977/20, decided 13.03.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Ipsa Loquitur: Negligence Inference
records.heading: Res ipsa loquitur permits an inference of negligence but accident alone does not prove it
records.text: Res ipsa loquitur applies where the thing causing damage was in the defendant's sole control, the occurrence would not ordinarily happen without negligence, and there is no evidence of how it occurred. It permits an inference of negligence but proof of an accident alone does not prove negligence. Ref: 2025 LHC 1065; Mst. Misbah Farooq etc v. M/s Daewoo Pakistan Express Bus Service Ltd etc (R.F.A. 1123-14, decided 04.03.2025).
records.title: Mst. Misbah Farooq etc v. M/s Daewoo Pakistan Express Bus Service Ltd etc (R.F.A. 1123-14, decided 04.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Negating Ocular Account
records.heading: Medical evidence that totally negates the ocular account makes the prosecution story improbable
