records.text: When medical evidence totally negates the ocular account, the prosecution story becomes improbable and it appears that the actual facts were suppressed or not known to the prosecution. Ref: 2025 LHC 1081; M. Ali Yasir v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 9553/21, decided 17.03.2025).
records.title: M. Ali Yasir v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 9553/21, decided 17.03.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report and Prosecutor General's Opinion
records.heading: A Prosecutor General's administrative opinion does not bind the court on a cancellation report
records.text: A cancellation report is a final report under s. 173 CrPC, sent through the prosecutor under s. 9(4) of the Punjab Criminal Prosecution Service Act, 2006. A legal opinion of the Prosecutor General in administrative capacity does not bind the court, which has discretion whether to consider it, and the Magistrate's refusal was not illegal. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 210, PLD 2025 Lah 496; Sheikh Nadeem Anwar v. Ilaqa Magistrate etc (Criminal Proceedings 36921/22).
records.title: Sheikh Nadeem Anwar v. Ilaqa Magistrate etc (Criminal Proceedings 36921/22)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Amendment of Decree: ss. 151, 152 CPC, O. XX R. 6
records.heading: Section 152 CPC corrects accidental slips only and not intentional omissions in a decree
records.text: Section 152 CPC corrects accidental or unintentional slips in a decree, while intentional omissions can only be remedied by review, appeal or revision. Under O. XX R. 6 CPC the decree must conform to the judgment and clearly state the relief granted. A plaintiff who sought only declaration could not obtain possession by amendment. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 223, PLD 2025 Lah 682; Muhammad Hussain, etc. v. Ali Muhammad, etc. (Civil Revision 1499 of 2012).
records.title: Muhammad Hussain, etc. v. Ali Muhammad, etc. (Civil Revision 1499 of 2012)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Art. 128 QSO: DNA Test to Challenge Paternity
records.heading: Birth during a valid marriage is conclusive proof of legitimacy and a DNA test is refused
records.text: Under Art. 128 QSO birth during a valid marriage or within two years of its dissolution, the mother remaining unmarried, is conclusive proof of legitimacy, and under Art. 2(f) no evidence may be given to disprove it. The ex-husband's application for a DNA test of the minor was refused and the petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 244, PLD 2025 Lah 332; Sakhawat Hussain v. Additional District Judge Bhalwal etc (WP 22286/23).
records.title: Sakhawat Hussain v. Additional District Judge Bhalwal etc (WP 22286/23)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Habeas Corpus Converted into Bail Petition
records.heading: Habeas corpus may be converted into a bail petition where police produce no linking record
records.text: Where the police did not produce the record linking the detenue to the offence or to recoveries, the habeas corpus petition was converted into a bail petition despite recorded arrest, and the detenue was set at liberty to approach the competent court. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 262, 2025 PCrLJ 1202; Miraj Zubair v. RPO Sahiwal etc (WP 485/25).
records.title: Miraj Zubair v. RPO Sahiwal etc (WP 485/25)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Habeas Corpus for Custody of Minors: Summary Jurisdiction
records.heading: Habeas corpus for custody of minors is a summary jurisdiction to be used sparingly
records.text: In habeas corpus the court may recover custody of minor children from one parent and hand it to the other, but the jurisdiction is summary and extraordinary, no full evidence is recorded, and it should be used sparingly because plenary jurisdiction lies with the special forums. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 284, 2025 CLC 1148; Hamna Fahad v. C.C.P.O Lahore etc (WP 89/25).
records.title: Hamna Fahad v. C.C.P.O Lahore etc (WP 89/25)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Vagrancy Ordinance and PTPA: Beggary and Trafficking
records.heading: Beggary alone is not trafficking and the PTPA needs coercion, fraud or exploitation
records.text: Section 3 PTPA applies where coercion, fraud or exploitation by a third party is involved. Without such elements the Vagrancy Ordinance may apply, and beggary alone is not trafficking. Section 3 PPC treats offences under Pakistani law committed abroad as if committed in Pakistan. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 300; Sadiq Hussain etc v. Deputy Director FIA etc (Writ Petition 12935-24).
records.title: Sadiq Hussain etc v. Deputy Director FIA etc (Writ Petition 12935-24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Deciding Miscellaneous Applications Before Main Lis
records.heading: Miscellaneous applications must be decided before the main case
records.text: A court must decide miscellaneous applications, such as one for comparison of thumb impressions, before deciding the main case. Under Order XIV CPC the court must first settle the points of dispute through issues, and a party cannot be taken to know the nature of the dispute where a material issue is absent. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 324; Muhammad Ismail & others v. Allah Wasaya & others (Civil Revision 893 of 2017).
records.title: Muhammad Ismail & others v. Allah Wasaya & others (Civil Revision 893 of 2017)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Free Medical Treatment for Advocates in Public Hospitals
records.heading: Practising advocates and dependents are entitled to free treatment in public hospitals
records.text: The respondents were directed to implement Notification No. SO(H&D)7-1/2018(MISC) so that practising advocates and their dependents receive free treatment in DHQs, THQs and RHCs on par with BPS 17 and 18 officers, on presentation of a Punjab Bar Council card. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 335; Adnan Mughal v. Government of Punjab etc (WP 1778-24).
records.title: Adnan Mughal v. Government of Punjab etc (WP 1778-24)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Executing Court Order on Dowry Articles: Appealability
records.heading: An executing court order for payment of dowry value is appealable under section 14
records.text: An executing court's decision directing the judgment debtor to pay the value of dowry articles, after the decree holder refused to receive them back, is a final decision appealable as a decision given under s. 14 of the Family Courts Act, 1964. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 343; Muhammad Ashraf v. Judge Executing Court etc (WP-15322-24).
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. Judge Executing Court etc (WP-15322-24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Damages After Acquittal: Malicious Prosecution
records.heading: Acquittal does not automatically entitle the accused to damages for malicious prosecution
records.text: Acquittal may give rise to a rebuttable presumption that there was no reasonable cause for prosecution, but failure of prosecution does not automatically entitle the accused to damages. The nature of the acquittal must be considered. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 346; Tariq Mehmood v. Tahir Farooq (R.F.A. 80927/22).
records.title: Tariq Mehmood v. Tahir Farooq (R.F.A. 80927/22)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Public Prosecutors: Action Requires Prosecutor General's Recommendation
records.heading: No action against public prosecutors without the Prosecutor General's recommendation
records.text: Prosecutors are public servants, and no action can be taken against them without the recommendation of the Prosecutor General, Punjab. Ref: 2025 LHC 1154; Malik Mudassar Ali etc v. Secretary PPD etc (Writ Petition 6630-22, decided 28.02.2025); Justice Anwaarul Haq Pannun.
records.title: Malik Mudassar Ali etc v. Secretary PPD etc (Writ Petition 6630-22, decided 28.02.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Chaddar and Parchi Customs Denying Women Inheritance
records.heading: Customs depriving women of inheritance are un-Islamic, illegal and void
records.text: Customs such as Chaddar or Parchi in Bannu, or any practice under any name that deprives women wholly or partly of inheritance, are declared un-Islamic, illegal and void. Perpetrators may face action under s. 498-A PPC, and State action falls under the Enforcement of Shari'ah Act, 1991. Ref: Syeda Fouzia Jalaal Shah v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Shariat Petition 10/I of 2023).
records.title: Syeda Fouzia Jalaal Shah v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Shariat Petition 10/I of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale by Village Lady: Validity of Transaction
records.heading: A vendor being a village woman alone is no ground to dispute a sale
records.text: Where both marginal witnesses corroborated the purchaser and no fraud or revenue official connivance was shown, the fact that the vendor was a villager lady cannot alone be a ground for disputing the sale. Ref: 2025 LHC 1180; Muhammad Rafique v. Mst. Suriya Bibi (Civil Revision 24-25, decided 12.03.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. Mst. Suriya Bibi (Civil Revision 24-25, decided 12.03.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Delay in Reporting Child Sexual Abuse
records.heading: Delay in reporting child sexual abuse is not treated like delay in other crimes
records.text: Delay in reporting sexual abuse cannot be equated with delay in other crimes, given trauma, fear, shame and threats. Courts do not treat the delay as material unless circumstances warrant an adverse view, especially where the victim is a child. Ref: Nazar Hussain and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal 964/J/2023).
records.title: Nazar Hussain and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal 964/J/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Chance Witness
records.heading: A chance witness is suspect unless credible reasons for presence are shown
records.text: A chance witness's testimony is suspect and generally not accepted unless credible reasons for presence at the scene are shown, though a chance witness is not necessarily false and the evidence must be scrutinised carefully. Ref: Nazar Hussain and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal 964/J/2023).
records.title: Nazar Hussain and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal 964/J/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Shamilat Share Not Presumed Transferred in Sale
records.heading: A shamilat share is not presumed transferred on sale unless the instrument mentions it
records.text: Under s. 3 of the West Pakistan Disposition (Saving and Shamlat) Ordinance, 1959, a share in shamilat land cannot be presumed transferred on sale of owned village land unless the instrument specifically mentions it. Ref: 2025 CLC 572; Allah Bakhsh v. Muhammad Hanif (Civil Revision 377-D-03).
records.title: Allah Bakhsh v. Muhammad Hanif (Civil Revision 377-D-03)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Unauthorised Revenue Entries: Recurring Cause of Action
records.heading: Each unauthorised revenue entry gives a fresh and recurring cause of action
records.text: For unauthorised entries, every new entry in the revenue record creates a fresh cause of action, so the aggrieved person has a recurring cause of action. Ref: 2025 CLC 572; Allah Bakhsh v. Muhammad Hanif (Civil Revision 377-D-03).
records.title: Allah Bakhsh v. Muhammad Hanif (Civil Revision 377-D-03)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Cancellation of Allotment After Proprietary Rights Vest
records.heading: Allotment cannot be cancelled after proprietary rights vest without fraud, notice and hearing
records.text: Once sale price is paid and possession given, revenue authorities cannot reverse the Collector's decision, and after the conveyance is registered the allottee is absolute owner. The Board of Revenue cannot cancel without proven fraud or serious breach, a show cause notice and a hearing, and the Civil Court can set aside cancellation under the Act V of 1912. Ref: 2025 CLC 434; Sarfraz Khan v. Province of Punjab & others (Civil Revision 155763 of 2018).
records.title: Sarfraz Khan v. Province of Punjab & others (Civil Revision 155763 of 2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Producing the Adversary as Own Witness
records.heading: The CPC neither bars nor permits a party producing its adversary as its own witness
records.text: The CPC neither bars nor permits a party producing its adversary as its own witness, and the practice has not been approved in the ordinary course. Article 131 QSO empowers the court to disallow irrelevant or inadmissible evidence and regulate production of evidence. Ref: 2025 CLC 420; Muhammad Arif v. Province of Punjab and others (C.R. 23580 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. Province of Punjab and others (C.R. 23580 of 2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift: Pleading and Proof of Particulars
records.heading: A party relying on an oral gift must plead and prove its particulars
records.text: A party relying on an oral gift must plead the time, date and place of declaration, acceptance and transfer of possession and the names of witnesses present, and then prove them by producing witnesses. Ref: 2025 CLC 420; Muhammad Arif v. Province of Punjab and others (C.R. 23580 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. Province of Punjab and others (C.R. 23580 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence in Appeal
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal is allowed only where a just decision cannot otherwise be reached
records.text: O. XLI R. 27 CPC enables the appellate court to take additional evidence needed to pronounce judgment or for any substantial cause. The evidence must bear directly on the point in issue, and the test is whether a just decision can be reached without it. Where a mutation is challenged, the party deriving title must prove it. Ref: 2025 CLC 452; Mst. Ilyas Akhtar v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Civil Revision 251 of 2017).
records.title: Mst. Ilyas Akhtar v. Province of Punjab, etc. (Civil Revision 251 of 2017)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agent Dealing on Own Account: s. 215 Contract Act
records.heading: An agent dealing on own account without consent may be repudiated by the principal
records.text: An attorney transferring property to himself or close relatives must obtain the principal's prior consent. Under s. 215 Contract Act, 1872 the principal may repudiate if the agent dealt on own account without consent or disclosure of material facts, and such consent need not be in writing. Ref: 2025 LHC 1238; Mohsin Lal Chaudashry v. Shoukat Ali etc (Civil Revision 423-24, decided 18.03.2025); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Mohsin Lal Chaudashry v. Shoukat Ali etc (Civil Revision 423-24, decided 18.03.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Default in Producing Evidence
records.heading: Under O. XVII R. 3 CPC the court may decide forthwith where a party fails to produce evidence
records.text: Order XVII Rule 3 CPC applies when a party fails to produce evidence, and the court may then, despite the default, decide the suit forthwith. Ref: Muhammad Feroz-ud-din Hilali v. Nadir & others (Civil Petition 473-K/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Feroz-ud-din Hilali v. Nadir & others (Civil Petition 473-K/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death in the Home: Husband's Duty to Explain, Art. 122 QSO
records.heading: A husband must explain a death inside the house and Art. 122 QSO lightens the prosecution burden
records.text: Where a death occurs inside the house in which the accused resides with other inmates, the husband must explain the circumstances, and Art. 122 QSO lightens the prosecution's burden. The court may also consider the defence's line of cross-examination, as its approach is inquisitorial. Ref: 2025 LHC 1269; Shafqat Ali v. The State (Jail Appeal 10245/22, decided 24.03.2025).
records.title: Shafqat Ali v. The State (Jail Appeal 10245/22, decided 24.03.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Married Daughter's Entitlement to Employment: Rule 10(4)
records.heading: A married daughter is equally entitled to employment in place of a deceased employee
records.text: A married daughter of a deceased government employee is equally entitled to employment in his place, and excluding her from Rule 10(4) on account of marriage denies her equal citizenship. An executive clarification cannot override statutory rules. Ref: Zahida Parveen v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary E&SE, Civil Secretariat, Peshawar and others (C.P.L.A. 566-P/2024, decided 17.03.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Zahida Parveen v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary E&SE, Civil Secretariat, Peshawar and others (C.P.L.A. 566-P/2024, decided 17.03.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas Recovery: Investigation Lapses
records.heading: Investigation lapses were noted in a charas case
records.text: The court noted lapses in a charas case: no medico-legal examination or blood test of the appellant, no attempt to arrest the intended buyer or obtain disclosure of dealers, haste in sending him to judicial custody, and case property and cash kept in the malkhana and never produced before the DPO or any court. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 216; Muhammad Rizwan Ahmed alias Bablo v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 631-22); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan Ahmed alias Bablo v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 631-22)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Wilful Absence and Tribunal's Power to Modify Penalty
records.heading: Admitted wilful absence needs no regular inquiry and the Tribunal may modify punishment
records.text: Wilful absence means failing to report for duty without informing the competent authority; where absence is admitted, no regular inquiry is needed. The Service Tribunal, as final fact-finding forum, may modify punishment for cogent recorded reasons. The Supreme Court under Art. 212(3) considers only substantial questions of law of public importance. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 145; Muzammal Khan v. Inspector General of Police Punjab, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 1354/2023).
records.title: Muzammal Khan v. Inspector General of Police Punjab, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 1354/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Not a Tool for Delay
records.heading: O. VII R. 11 CPC is no licence to prolong proceedings
records.text: Order VII Rule 11 CPC gives no licence to be invoked in every suit merely to prolong proceedings, and courts should not permit such tactics. The post also lists legal character under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the rule that concurrent findings cannot shield erroneous decisions from correction. Ref: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024, decided 28.03.2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024, decided 28.03.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Parties Bound by Their Pleadings
records.heading: Parties are bound by their pleadings and cannot prove a case beyond them
records.text: Parties are bound by their pleadings and a plea not raised initially cannot be introduced later. The suit was framed on a plea of gift, not purchase, and no plea of purchase was in the plaint. A plaintiff cannot prove a case beyond the pleadings, and evidence outside them can be ignored. Ref: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024, decided 28.03.2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024, decided 28.03.2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 21(c) Specific Relief Act: Certainty of Terms
records.heading: A contract with terms uncertain to the court cannot be specifically enforced
records.text: Section 21(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 does not allow enforcement of a contract whose terms the court cannot find with reasonable certainty; an agreement not describing the property by metes and bounds was refused enforcement. A claimant must assert a valid enforceable contract and clearly plead its terms. Ref: 2025 LHC 1367; Muhammad Asif v. Ch. Muhammad Hanif (R.S.A. 69 of 2014).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Ch. Muhammad Hanif (R.S.A. 69 of 2014)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Offence Abroad: Ss. 188 and 403 CrPC and S. 3 PPC
records.heading: An offence abroad may be tried in Pakistan and an FIR is not barred by section 188 CrPC
records.text: Under s. 3 PPC a person committing abroad an offence under the PPC may be tried in Pakistan as if committed here. Section 188 CrPC does not bar registration of an FIR under s. 154 against a Pakistani citizen for an offence abroad, and s. 403 protection requires a prior trial by a competent court ending in conviction or acquittal that stands. Ref: 2025 LHC 1359; Muhammad Irshad v. State (Crl. Misc. 7151-B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Irshad v. State (Crl. Misc. 7151-B/2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift: Heavy Onus on Beneficiary and Three Ingredients
records.heading: The beneficiary of an immovable property gift bears a heavy onus to prove three ingredients
records.text: The Lahore High Court judgment is described as a comprehensive treatment of gift (hiba/tamleek) law. The beneficiary of a gift of immovable property bears a heavy onus to prove it, and must plead and prove the three mandatory ingredients of gift, namely offer by the donor, acceptance and delivery of possession. Ref: 2025 LHC 1405; Mst. Sadiqan Begum v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 27145 of 2017).
records.title: Mst. Sadiqan Begum v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision 27145 of 2017)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Legal Character under S. 42 Specific Relief Act
records.heading: Authority on the requirement of legal character under section 42 Specific Relief Act
records.text: Authority on the requirement of legal character under s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The post gives only the topic. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 302; Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024).
records.title: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Not a Licence to Delay
records.heading: O. VII R. 11 CPC does not license delay tactics
records.text: Order VII Rule 11 CPC does not give a licence to be invoked in every lawsuit merely to prolong proceedings, and courts should not permit such tactics aimed at delay. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 302; Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024).
records.title: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Concurrent Findings Open to Correction
records.heading: Concurrent findings cannot shield erroneous decisions from correction
records.text: Concurrent findings of the courts below cannot shield erroneous decisions from correction. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 302; Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024).
records.title: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Parties Bound by Their Pleadings
records.heading: Parties are bound by their pleadings and a plea not raised initially cannot be added later
records.text: Parties are bound by their pleadings and a plea not raised initially cannot be introduced later. The suit was framed on a plea of gift, not purchase, and no plea of purchase was in the plaint. A plaintiff cannot prove a case beyond the pleadings, and evidence outside them can be ignored. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 302; Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024).
records.title: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint Principles
records.heading: Rejection of a plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC requires no subsisting cause of action
records.text: In rejecting a plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC the court may consider other material on record admitted by the plaintiff, but mixed questions of law and fact should go to trial. Piecemeal rejection is not allowed if one prayer is maintainable. The court may act suo motu without awaiting a written statement. The plaintiff must show a subsisting cause of action. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 302; Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024).
records.title: Ahmed Ali Talpur v. Sub-Registrar (C.P.L.A. 290-K/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Accused Placed in Column No. 2 of Police Report
records.heading: The Magistrate is not bound by the police view on an accused placed in Column No. 2
records.text: Police may release an accused on bond under s. 169 CrPC for insufficient evidence, but this power is not analogous to the trial court's evaluation of evidence. Under s. 173(3) CrPC the Magistrate is not bound by the police view and must independently assess the record. As the challan was already submitted, the matter was left to the forum seized of it. Ref: PLD 2025 Peshawar 62.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower Agreement: Proof of Execution by Beneficiary Wife
records.heading: A wife must prove execution of a dower agreement and may discharge it by her own evidence
records.text: Although the QSO and CPC do not apply to family matters under s. 17 of the Family Courts Act, 1964, the wife as beneficiary of a dower agreement initially bore the burden of proving its execution. She discharged it through her own evidence and marginal witnesses, and the husband's claim of theft of the stamp paper was unsupported. The agreement was held validly executed. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 359.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XL CPC: Appointment of Receiver
records.heading: A receiver is appointed sparingly and not on the applicant's mere apprehension
records.text: A receiver is to be appointed sparingly and not on the applicant's apprehension. The trial court gave no persuasive reasons under O. XL CPC and relied on emails not proved under the Electronic Transactions Ordinance, 2002 and Arts. 46-A and 78-A QSO. If the application has substance, an inquiry may be ordered and a receiver appointed on a report of waste or peril. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 366.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance of Issueless Daughter: Uterine Brother
records.heading: A uterine brother inherits the estate of an issueless daughter of a Muslim male
records.text: Applying Ayat 7 to 11 of Surah Nisa, where a Muslim male dies without male issue and his only daughter dies issueless leaving a living uterine brother, that brother inherits her estate, and progeny of her predeceased uncle or step father are excluded. Revision allowed and concurrent decisions granting shares to the step father's sons reversed. Ref: 2025 MLD 573; Manzoor Ahmad v. Chiragh Khan through LRs (Civil Revision 164468/18).
records.title: Manzoor Ahmad v. Chiragh Khan through LRs (Civil Revision 164468/18)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 25 Guardian and Wards Act: Custody and Welfare
records.heading: Under section 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act the minor's welfare is paramount
records.text: Section 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act deals with return of a minor who leaves or is removed from the guardian's custody. The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration, and the Guardian Court must record a definite finding, considering age, sex, environment, circumstances, position of parties and the law governing the minor. Ref: 2025 MLD 401.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody: Biological Parents v. Adoptive or Relatives
records.heading: Biological parents prevail over relatives or adoptive parents in custody of a minor
records.text: After the minor had been voluntarily handed over for six years, the real parents sought her custody. In the presence of the biological parents, custody cannot go to the petitioners, who were the maternal uncle and aunt or adoptive parents, as the minor's welfare lies best with her real parents. Writ petition dismissed. Ref: 2025 LHC 2015; Nazir Ahmad & 1 other v. ADJ Kasur etc. (WP 62973/24, decided 20.02.2025); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Nazir Ahmad & 1 other v. ADJ Kasur etc. (WP 62973/24, decided 20.02.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Forgery of Sale Deed: S. 467 PPC and Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Forgery of a sale deed attracts section 467 PPC and the prohibitory clause
records.text: Forgery of a sale deed, a valuable security, attracts s. 467 PPC, punishable with life imprisonment or up to ten years. Even if the Investigating Officer omitted it, the court may consider it at the bail stage, and the offence fell within the embargo of s. 497 CrPC. A forgery can be reported by any member of the public, not only the person directly affected. Ref: 2025 LHC 2094; Riaz Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8612-B/2025, decided 26.03.2025).
records.title: Riaz Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 8612-B/2025, decided 26.03.2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: No Prima Facie Case for Interim Relief
records.heading: A disputed agreement to sell does not make a prima facie case for interim relief
records.text: A prima facie case cannot be assumed where the claim rests on a disputed agreement to sell alleged to be forged, which creates no title and only a right to seek specific performance if proved. Balance of convenience favoured the respondent owners, who would suffer more from interim relief than the petitioner tenant would from its refusal. Ref: 2025 LHC 2082; Ejaz Ahmad v. ADJ Ferozewala District Sheikhupura etc. (Misc. Writ 14946/25, decided 12.03.2025); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Ejaz Ahmad v. ADJ Ferozewala District Sheikhupura etc. (Misc. Writ 14946/25, decided 12.03.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Mother's Remarriage and Custody
records.heading: A mother's remarriage does not by itself disqualify her from custody
records.text: A mother's remarriage does not by itself make her ineligible for custody of the minor. Writ petition allowed and the concurrent findings of the lower courts reversed. Ref: 2025 LHC 2078; Nazia Saddique v. ADJ etc. (WP 3974-24, decided 09.04.2025); Justice Syed Ahsan Raza Kazmi.
records.title: Nazia Saddique v. ADJ etc. (WP 3974-24, decided 09.04.2025)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Nature and Purpose of Rent Proceedings; AI in Judging
records.heading: Authority on rent proceedings and the use of artificial intelligence in judging
records.text: Authority on the nature and purpose of rent proceedings. The judgment also discusses the use of artificial intelligence for judicial and administrative efficiency, its gaps and cautions in judging and fair trial, and the continuing role of mediation and ADR. The post gives headings only. Ref: Ishfaq Ahmed v. Mushtaq Ahmed, etc. (C.P.L.A. 1010-L/2022).
records.title: Ishfaq Ahmed v. Mushtaq Ahmed, etc. (C.P.L.A. 1010-L/2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302 PPC: Death or Life under Clause (b)
records.heading: Under section 302(b) PPC the court chooses between death and imprisonment by circumstances
records.text: Section 302 PPC has three distinct punishments. Clause (a) leaves no discretion beyond death as qisas, clause (c) gives wide discretion, while under clause (b) the court chooses between death and imprisonment as tazir according to the circumstances. The power to enhance a trial court's sentence must be exercised sparingly unless needed to prevent a grave miscarriage of justice. Ref: Fida Hussain @ Saboo v. The State (Crl. Appeal 530 of 2022).
records.title: Fida Hussain @ Saboo v. The State (Crl. Appeal 530 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Closing of Evidence after Last Opportunities
records.heading: Evidence was rightly closed after last opportunities were ignored under O. XVII R. 3 CPC
records.text: The petitioner was given absolute last opportunities with clear warnings to produce evidence but ignored them, and law favours the vigilant and not the indolent. The Supreme Court upheld the order closing his right to produce evidence. Under O. XVII R. 3 CPC, evidence cannot be closed unless adjournment was granted at the party's request and the party defaulted. Ref: Muhammad Akram v. Shafaqat Ali (C.P.L.A. 1033-L of 2024, decided 27.03.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. Shafaqat Ali (C.P.L.A. 1033-L of 2024, decided 27.03.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Transfer of Judges to Islamabad High Court
records.heading: Petitions challenge the notification transferring judges to the Islamabad High Court
records.text: Seven petitions under Art. 184(3) challenge the notification of 1 February 2025 issued under Art. 200 transferring judges to the Islamabad High Court. The petition by five sitting IHC judges on seniority was treated as the leading petition. Office objections on maintainability were deferred and notice issued on stay applications for 17.04.2025. Ref: Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, Judge, Islamabad High Court, Islamabad and others v. The President of Pakistan, Pak Secretariat, Islamabad and others (C.P. 22/2025, decided 14.04.2025).
records.title: Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, Judge, Islamabad High Court, Islamabad and others v. The President of Pakistan, Pak Secretariat, Islamabad and others (C.P. 22/2025, decided 14.04.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Registrar's Jurisdiction under S. 54 Co-operative Societies Act
records.heading: The Registrar cannot adjudicate disputes on title to immovable property under section 54
records.text: The Registrar's jurisdiction under s. 54 of the Co-operative Societies Act is limited to disputes touching the business of the society. Disputes on ownership and title of immovable property lie exclusively with the civil courts and cannot be adjudicated by the Registrar. Ref: Sikander Ahmed Ghouri v. Syed Raffat Abbas Jafferi & others (C.P.L.A. 1220-K/2022, decided 21.03.2025); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Sikander Ahmed Ghouri v. Syed Raffat Abbas Jafferi & others (C.P.L.A. 1220-K/2022, decided 21.03.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Testimony of Victims with Intellectual Disabilities
records.heading: Testimony of a victim with intellectual disability should not be rejected outright
records.text: In criminal cases the testimony of a victim with a cognitive or intellectual disability should not be rejected outright. Procedural accommodations must be made for meaningful participation, and the duty extends to police, prosecutors and courts, who must exhaust reasonable means so that disability is no barrier to legal redress. Ref: 2025 LHC 2184; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal 692/2022); Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Criminal Appeal 704/J/2022); Mst. Nawaz Bibi (Criminal Revision 26/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal 692/2022); Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Criminal Appeal 704/J/2022); Mst. Nawaz Bibi (Criminal Revision 26/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift, Mutation and Fraud
records.heading: An oral gift is permissible and a party relying on a disputed mutation must prove the transaction
records.text: An oral gift is legally permissible, and an entry in the Rozenamcha Waqiati is not itself the instrument of gift. Mutation is an administrative act that does not confer title, so a party relying on a disputed mutation must prove the original transaction. Fraud unravels any transaction, and the court examined whether limitation barred rectification of fraud. Ref: 2025 SCP 117; Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc. (C.A. 113-L/2010); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc. (C.A. 113-L/2010)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Application Time Barred
records.heading: A hopelessly time barred section 12(2) CPC application cannot succeed
records.text: The law of limitation is preventive in nature and requires a person to seek legal remedies with due diligence and within the prescribed time. The application under s. 12(2) CPC was held hopelessly time barred. Ref: 2025 CLC 684, PLJ 2024 Lah 156; Ijaz Ahmad Khan v. Muhammad Bootay Khan (C.R. No. 78446 of 2023); Justice Masud Abid Naqvi.
records.title: Ijaz Ahmad Khan v. Muhammad Bootay Khan (C.R. No. 78446 of 2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 79 QSO: Two Attesting Witnesses
records.heading: An attested document cannot be used as evidence until two attesting witnesses are called
records.text: Under Art. 79 QSO, a document required by law to be attested cannot be used as evidence until at least two attesting witnesses have been called to prove execution, if two are alive, subject to the process of the court and capable of giving evidence. Ref: 2025 CLC 670; Akhtar Gul etc. v. Muhammad Ashiq etc. (Civil Revision 663-12).
records.title: Akhtar Gul etc. v. Muhammad Ashiq etc. (Civil Revision 663-12)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness
records.heading: A buyer who never paid or deposited the balance is refused specific performance
records.text: Specific performance is discretionary. The buyer must prove readiness and willingness to perform from execution until the date fixed for paying the balance price, and that he took necessary steps. The petitioner never paid, tendered or deposited the balance consideration, so discretion was rightly refused and the concurrent dismissal of the suit upheld. Ref: 2025 CLC 638; Muhammad Alam v. Darbari Khan (C.R. No. 40284 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Alam v. Darbari Khan (C.R. No. 40284 of 2020)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 84 QSO: Comparison of Thumb Impressions
records.heading: Art. 84 QSO sets no time limit for applying for comparison of thumb impressions
records.text: Art. 84 QSO prescribes no time for applying for expert comparison of signatures or thumb impressions, so filing after evidence is recorded is not a cogent ground for dismissal. A defendant had conceded no objection to comparison, and the High Court set aside the orders of the courts below and allowed the application. Ref: 2025 CLC 785; Sabir Hussain v. Additional District Judge/MCAC, Layyah.
records.title: Sabir Hussain v. Additional District Judge/MCAC, Layyah

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC Application Decided Before Appeal
records.heading: An O. XLI R. 27 CPC application must be decided before the appeal's merits
records.text: A pending miscellaneous application, such as one under O. XLI R. 27 CPC for additional evidence, must be decided by the appellate court before the merits of the appeal. Deciding both together without first disposing of the application is a procedural irregularity that vitiates the appellate process. Ref: 2025 CLC 727; Muhammad Iqbal Gill, etc. v. Nasir Abbas, etc. (C.R. No. 6830 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal Gill, etc. v. Nasir Abbas, etc. (C.R. No. 6830 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Challenged: Shifting of Onus
records.heading: Onus shifts to the beneficiary where a transferor denies a transaction on oath alleging undue influence
records.text: Where a transferor denies a transaction on oath and undue influence is alleged, as with an aged parent or wife, the onus shifts to the beneficiary to prove it. The court held the circumstances different where a grown-up married man claimed he was abducted and denied a sale to a relative of his wife, with no circumstances of undue influence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 667; Muhammad Asif v. Amjad Iqbal and others (C.P.L.A. 3151/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Amjad Iqbal and others (C.P.L.A. 3151/2021)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Civil Service, Penalties and Proportionality
records.heading: Authority on the civil service, penalties under service laws and proportionality
records.text: Authority on the role of the civil service in ensuring continuity, stability and efficiency in governance, the importance of penalties under service laws, and the principle of proportionality. The post gives headings only. Ref: 2025 SCMR 708; Muhammad Nasir Ismail v. Government of Punjab through Secretary Law and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 3062/2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Nasir Ismail v. Government of Punjab through Secretary Law and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 3062/2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: FIR Not Substantive Evidence
records.heading: An FIR is not substantive evidence unless its maker affirms it on oath
records.text: An FIR is not substantive evidence unless its maker affirms its contents on oath and faces cross-examination. Under Arts. 140 and 153 QSO it is a previous statement usable only to contradict its maker. A dying declaration FIR is admissible under Art. 46 QSO but cannot corroborate another witness. Ref: 2025 SCMR 762; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Petition 95 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Petition 95 of 2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Qazf: Denial of Paternity and Li'an
records.heading: Denial of a child's paternity is qazf and Art. 128 QSO makes legitimacy conclusive
records.text: Denial of a child's paternity is qazf, as it attributes zina to the mother. Li'an under s. 14 of the Ordinance applies where the allegation is made while the marital bond is intact. Art. 128 QSO makes birth during marriage or within two years after dissolution conclusive proof of legitimacy. For hadd, the complainant must not withdraw the complaint, and silence creates shubhah. Ref: 2025 SCMR 676; Mst. Saeeda Begum v. The State & another (Crl. Sh. R.P. 2/2016).
records.title: Mst. Saeeda Begum v. The State & another (Crl. Sh. R.P. 2/2016)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Diyat: Minors' Share and Inability to Pay
records.heading: Minors' share in diyat is protected and a convict unable to pay may seek instalments
records.text: The share of minor legal heirs in diyat remains protected under all circumstances, even where all heirs compromise. A convict unable to pay may approach the administrative committee under the Diyat, Arsh and Daman Fund Rules, 2007 framed under s. 338-G PPC, or the trial court under s. 331 PPC to pay diyat in instalments. Ref: 2025 SCMR 776; Tanvir Hussain v. The State (Crl.M.A. 714/2023).
records.title: Tanvir Hussain v. The State (Crl.M.A. 714/2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Application of QSO to Rent Tribunal Proceedings
records.heading: A Rent Tribunal must apply general principles of evidence and cannot rely on hearsay
records.text: Although the QSO does not strictly apply to rent proceedings, a Rent Tribunal must apply its general principles of evidence and cannot rely on hearsay or unproved copies of documents. It need not enforce all QSO provisions, and a disputed tenancy agreement need not be proved under Arts. 17(2)(a) and 79 QSO. Ref: 2025 SCMR 690; Zafar Iqbal & another v. Syed Riaz Hussain Shah and others (C.P.L.A. 3854/2024); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Zafar Iqbal & another v. Syed Riaz Hussain Shah and others (C.P.L.A. 3854/2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody of Narcotics
records.heading: The prosecution must prove an unbroken chain of custody in narcotics cases
records.text: Where conviction under the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997 rests on recovery and chemical analysis, the prosecution must prove an unbroken chain of custody and safe transmission to the laboratory. Failure makes the chemical examiner's report unreliable and the accused is entitled to the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2025 SCMR 704; Muhammad Iqbal v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.P.L.A. 828/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh (Crl.P.L.A. 828/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Corroborative; Motive Not Attributed
records.heading: Medical evidence is only corroborative and does not identify the assailant
records.text: Medical evidence is only corroborative, confirms injury, weapon and timing but does not identify the assailant, and matters only if the ocular account inspires confidence. Motive was attributed to co-accused who had been discharged without challenge, not directly to the petitioner. Ref: 2025 SCMR 730; Muhammad Ehsan Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 231/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Ehsan Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 231/2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Husband's Silence on Wife's Death: Art. 121 QSO
records.heading: A husband's silence on his wife's death gives no adverse presumption under Art. 121 QSO
records.text: The complainant did not witness the occurrence, and rejection of the petitioner's plea of suicide does not relieve the prosecution of proving its case. His failure to explain what happened to his wife under the same roof gives no adverse presumption under Art. 121 QSO, so maintaining the conviction was unsafe. Ref: 2025 SCMR 730; Muhammad Ehsan Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 231/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Ehsan Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 231/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Judgments in Rem and in Personam
records.heading: Authority on the distinction between judgments in rem and in personam
records.text: Authority on the distinction between judgments in rem and judgments in personam. The post gives the topic only. Ref: 2025 SCMR 790; Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Finance Division, Islamabad v. Muhammad Atiq ur Rahman (C.P.L.A. 687/2022).
records.title: Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Finance Division, Islamabad v. Muhammad Atiq ur Rahman (C.P.L.A. 687/2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Assignment and Sale of Immovable Property Distinguished
records.heading: An assignment and a sale of immovable property are different
records.text: An assignment and a sale of immovable property are different. The leave petitioner's interest came by sale during the pendency of the second suit, so it was a divestment of the vendor's whole interest. The court was not persuaded by his case, and Surraya Begum v. Suban Begum (1992 SCMR 652) was held factually different. Ref: 2025 SCMR 770; Abdul Shakoor v. Muhammad Hanif (C.P.L.A. 1808-L/2015).
records.title: Abdul Shakoor v. Muhammad Hanif (C.P.L.A. 1808-L/2015)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Wastewater Treatment and Climate Change
records.heading: Authority on wastewater treatment, climate change and fundamental rights
records.text: Authority on the importance of a wastewater treatment plant in the context of climate change, climate finance and fundamental rights, and on giving preference to homegrown solutions. The post gives headings only. Ref: 2025 SCMR 606; Syed Ali Hussain, etc. v. Senior Member/Member (Revenue) Board of Revenue Punjab, Lahore, etc. (C.P.L.A. 2918-L/2015); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Syed Ali Hussain, etc. v. Senior Member/Member (Revenue) Board of Revenue Punjab, Lahore, etc. (C.P.L.A. 2918-L/2015)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Inquiry Procedure under E&D Rules 1999
records.heading: Authority on departmental inquiry procedure under the Punjab E&D Rules 1999
records.text: Authority on Rule 7 of the Punjab Civil Servants (E&D) Rules, 1999 and the Punjab Estacode, 2013 on departmental inquiries. It covers procedure for the inquiry officer or committee, consequences of not recording evidence and denying cross-examination, discreet versus regular inquiry, and the purpose of a de novo inquiry. The post gives headings only. Ref: 2025 SCMR 632; Aamir Akbar v. Additional Superintendent of Police, Bahawalpur, etc. (C.P.L.A. 921-L/2017); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Aamir Akbar v. Additional Superintendent of Police, Bahawalpur, etc. (C.P.L.A. 921-L/2017)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Rights of Persons with Disabilities and Regularization
records.heading: Authority on rights of persons with disabilities and the regularization policy
records.text: Authority on effective implementation of laws protecting disabled persons, the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, implementation of the regularization policy, equal protection without discrimination and elimination of exploitation. The post gives headings only. Ref: 2025 SCMR 612; Chairman, NADRA Headquarter Islamabad and others v. Abdul Majeed and another (C.P.L.A. 6059/2021); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Chairman, NADRA Headquarter Islamabad and others v. Abdul Majeed and another (C.P.L.A. 6059/2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Voice Recognition and Retracted Confession
records.heading: Voice recognition and a retracted confession cannot safely sustain a death or life sentence
records.text: Voice recognition lacks a standardised scientific framework and, without corroboration such as call records, witnesses or forensic analysis, is unreliable for sustaining a death or life sentence. Any doubt favours the accused. A retracted confession as the sole basis of conviction raises serious concerns. Ref: 2025 SCMR 744; Imtiaz and Naeem v. The State (Jail Petition 438/2018).
records.title: Imtiaz and Naeem v. The State (Jail Petition 438/2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pleadings Not Evidence; Evasive Denial
records.heading: Pleadings are not evidence and evasive denial is no denial
records.text: Contents of a plaint or written statement are not evidence and must be proved by oral evidence on oath with cross-examination and by documents. Evasive denial is no denial, since O. VIII Rules 3, 4 and 5 CPC require specific denial of each allegation of fact. Ref: 2025 SCMR 653, PLJ 2025 SC 621; Muhammad Adnan v. Salah-ud-Din (C.P.L.A. 1618/2024); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Adnan v. Salah-ud-Din (C.P.L.A. 1618/2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Video Recording of Narcotics Recovery and Private Witnesses
records.heading: Absent video recording and private witnesses, the balance tilts to the petitioner in narcotics cases
records.text: As the 1997 Act prescribes severe punishments, the standard of proof is correspondingly high. Art. 164 QSO stresses use of modern devices, and the police collected no video or photographs of the recovery and associated no private witness. Failure to follow judicial directives tilted the balance in favour of the petitioner. Ref: 2025 SCMR 721, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 116; Muhammad Abid Hussain v. State (Crl.P. 146 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Abid Hussain v. State (Crl.P. 146 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry and Bridal Gifts Vest Absolutely in Bride
records.heading: Dowry and bridal gifts vest absolutely in the bride, who may sue to recover them
records.text: All property given to the bride as dowry, bridal gifts or presents vests absolutely in her, and she may sue for its recovery. Arts. 23, 24, 25 and 35 of the Constitution support this view. The court discourages dowry unless voluntary and free from social pressure. Ref: Muhammad Sajid v. Mst. Shamsa Asghar, etc. (C.P.L.A. 3284-L/2022, decided 15.04.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Sajid v. Mst. Shamsa Asghar, etc. (C.P.L.A. 3284-L/2022, decided 15.04.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: PPC Section Prevails over Schedule II CrPC Entry
records.heading: A PPC section prevails over a conflicting Schedule II CrPC entry
records.text: Where the text of a section of the PPC conflicts with the entry in Schedule II of the CrPC, the section of the PPC prevails. Ref: 2025 LHC 2421; Muhammad Waqas v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 2020-B-25, decided 15.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 2020-B-25, decided 15.04.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Widows' Right to Employment and Equality
records.heading: Widows are entitled to employment, dignity and equality without discrimination
records.text: Widows, like all citizens, are entitled to employment, dignity, equality and autonomy without discrimination or reprisal. Widowhood is a life circumstance deserving dignity, protection and equal opportunity. Ref: The Chief Commissioner Regional Tax Office, Bahawalpur and others v. Shaheen Yousaf (C.P.L.A. 808/2023, decided 16.04.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: The Chief Commissioner Regional Tax Office, Bahawalpur and others v. Shaheen Yousaf (C.P.L.A. 808/2023, decided 16.04.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Theft: Physical Possession and Civil Rights
records.heading: For theft physical possession is key and civil rights do not stifle investigation
records.text: For the offence of theft, physical possession is the key point. Civil rights or co-ownership are not a valid ground to stifle a criminal investigation or discharge the accused where the complainant had peaceful, uninterrupted, long physical possession. Ref: 2025 LHC 2426; Khan Muhammad v. Judicial Magistrate etc. (WP 782-25, decided 10.04.2025); Justice Tariq Mahmood Bajwa.
records.title: Khan Muhammad v. Judicial Magistrate etc. (WP 782-25, decided 10.04.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secondary Evidence on Accused's Refusal to Produce
records.heading: The prosecution may tender secondary evidence if the accused refuses to produce a document
records.text: If the accused refuses to produce a document to be used against him, the prosecution may tender secondary evidence of that document. Ref: 2025 LHC 2439; Munawar Ali v. ASJ etc. (Crl. Misc. 620-M-24, decided 17.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Munawar Ali v. ASJ etc. (Crl. Misc. 620-M-24, decided 17.04.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Decree against Surety
records.heading: A decree can be executed against a surety whose liability is joint and several
records.text: A decree can be executed against a surety, whose liability is joint and several with the judgment debtor, and arrest of the judgment debtor does not absolve him. Surety can be proceeded against under s. 45 CPC, and unambiguous words in a surety bond are read in their ordinary meaning. Ref: 2025 LHC 2512; Mehboob Alam v. Additional District Judge etc. (WP 29329/20, decided 15.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Mehboob Alam v. Additional District Judge etc. (WP 29329/20, decided 15.04.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Conditional Decree; Limitation for Revision
records.heading: A conditional decree makes the court functus officio on the target date
records.text: Where a decree is conditional and states the consequence of non-fulfilment, the court becomes functus officio on the target date. The judgment also considers whether the Limitation Act, 1908 prescribes any period for filing a revision application. The post gives the points only. Ref: 2025 LHC 2552; Adeel Khaleel v. Shahid Hassan etc. (WP 3048-18, decided 16.04.2025); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Adeel Khaleel v. Shahid Hassan etc. (WP 3048-18, decided 16.04.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 341 CrPC: Accused Unable to Understand Proceedings
records.heading: If the accused cannot understand proceedings the trial judge must forward them to the High Court
records.text: If the judge doubts the accused's physical or mental capacity, the s. 341 CrPC procedure applies. If the accused cannot understand the proceedings, the trial judge cannot pass a sentence and must forward the proceedings to the High Court for such orders as it thinks fit. Ref: 2025 LHC 2548; The State v. Saqib Hussain Qureshi (Reference under Section 341 Cr.P.C. 69061/20, decided 16.04.2025).
records.title: The State v. Saqib Hussain Qureshi (Reference under Section 341 Cr.P.C. 69061/20, decided 16.04.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Minor Rape Victim's Testimony; Negative DNA Report
records.heading: A minor victim's testimony can alone sustain conviction and a negative DNA report is not conclusive
records.text: The identity of rape victims must be protected. A minor victim's testimony stands on a higher pedestal and can alone sustain conviction. A negative DNA report is merely corroborative and not conclusive, and a potency test shows only capacity, not commission of rape. Ref: 2025 LHC 2497; Bilal Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Appeal 859-21, decided 10.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar.
records.title: Bilal Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Appeal 859-21, decided 10.04.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Surety's Liability after Judgment Debtor's Death
records.heading: The judgment debtor's death does not release the surety absent a contrary stipulation
records.text: The death of the judgment debtor does not release the surety from his obligation where the bond has no stipulation to that effect. Section 145 CPC allows a decree to be executed against a surety to the extent he made himself personally liable. Ref: 2025 LHC 2559; Rasheed Ahmad v. Additional District Judge (WP 63942 of 2024, decided 17.03.2025).
records.title: Rasheed Ahmad v. Additional District Judge (WP 63942 of 2024, decided 17.03.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail where Post-Arrest Bail Is Certain
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail should not be denied where post-arrest bail is certain
records.text: Ss. 337-F(i), 337-A(i) and 337-L(2) PPC are bailable, and s. 337-F(vi) falls outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Where the accused would in any case get post-arrest bail, denying pre-arrest bail and requiring incarceration is a mere procedural formality without purpose. Ref: Muhammad Akhtar v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition 310 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Akhtar v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition 310 of 2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Counter Versions: Aggressor and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Counter versions of the same incident support bail as a rule on further inquiry
records.text: The prime consideration is which party was the aggressor, and the number or seat of injuries is only indicative. Where the FIR and the opposite party give counter versions of the same incident, bail is granted as a rule on grounds of further inquiry, and refusal is an exception. Ref: Zulqarnain Haider alias Zain v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.L.A. 332/2025, decided 22.04.2025); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Zulqarnain Haider alias Zain v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.L.A. 332/2025, decided 22.04.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 12A and S. 14(3) Family Courts Act: Speedy Trial
records.heading: A family suit must be decided within six months and interlocutory orders are challenged later
records.text: Section 12A of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 obliges the trial court to decide a family suit within six months, and the right to cross-examine does not extend to repeated adjournments. Section 14(3) bars challenge to interlocutory orders, which may be raised with the final order. Ref: Khalid Pervaiz ul Haq and another v. Mst. Minha Asif and another (Civil Petition 930 of 2024).
records.title: Khalid Pervaiz ul Haq and another v. Mst. Minha Asif and another (Civil Petition 930 of 2024)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Entry No. 4, Third Schedule ATA: Kidnapping for Ransom
records.heading: Entry No. 4 offences of the ATA are heinous but not per se terrorism
records.text: Offences in entry No. 4 of the Third Schedule to the ATA, 1997 are heinous offences triable by an ATC without per se being terrorism, and the ATC punishes only for that offence. An ordinary s. 365-A PPC case is merely triable by an ATC, but kidnapping for ransom with a purpose in s. 6(1)(b) or (c) also attracts s. 7(e) ATA. Ref: Muhammad Yamin and Muhammad Ameer v. State (Jail Petition 621 of 2017, decided 09.04.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Yamin and Muhammad Ameer v. State (Jail Petition 621 of 2017, decided 09.04.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitnesses, Minor Discrepancies and Motive
records.heading: Substitution of real culprits is rare and trivial discrepancies do not damage the prosecution case
records.text: Substitution of real culprits is rare where eyewitnesses lost their kin before their eyes, and an interested witness is one with an ulterior motive for conviction. Trivial discrepancies do not damage the prosecution case, only material ones do. Motive was not proved, and the death sentence was altered to imprisonment for life. Ref: Munir Ahmad v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 80 of 2023, decided 09.04.2025).
records.title: Munir Ahmad v. The State etc. (Criminal Appeal 80 of 2023, decided 09.04.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dark Hours Identification and Complainant's Conduct
records.heading: No source of light and unnatural conduct of the complainant doubt identification at night
records.text: The semi-open eyes and mouth of the body suggested it lay unattended, and the complainant mentioned no source of light for identifying the assailant at night. No bulb was taken into possession and his silent conduct was unnatural. The absence of marks on the body doubted the dragging version. Ref: Waqas Ahmad v. The State (Jail Petition 539 of 2017, decided 09.04.2025).
records.title: Waqas Ahmad v. The State (Jail Petition 539 of 2017, decided 09.04.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive as Double-Edged Weapon; Delay in FIR
records.heading: Motive is a double-edged weapon usable by either side
records.text: Motive is a double-edged weapon that can be used either way and by either side, for real or false involvement. The post also lists delay in lodging the FIR as a point. Ref: Manzar Abas and Ali Afzal v. State (Criminal Appeals 438 and 439 of 2023, decided 13.03.2025).
records.title: Manzar Abas and Ali Afzal v. State (Criminal Appeals 438 and 439 of 2023, decided 13.03.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Circumstance Not Put to Accused
records.heading: A circumstance not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used against him
records.text: A piece of evidence or circumstance not put to the accused when recording his statement under s. 342 CrPC cannot be considered against him for conviction. Ref: Ghulam Mustafa v. State (Crl.A. 23 of 2020, decided 13.03.2025).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. State (Crl.A. 23 of 2020, decided 13.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness Not Examined under S. 161 CrPC
records.heading: An injured witness never examined under section 161 CrPC raises the question of prejudice
records.text: An injured witness was never examined under s. 161 CrPC and first appeared before the trial judge six months after the occurrence. Mere failure to examine does not bar admissibility, but the question is prejudice to the accused under s. 265-C CrPC, and the irregularity seriously undermined the evidence. Injuries do not by themselves establish truth. Ref: Muhammad Abras v. The State (Crl. A. No. 655/2020, decided 12.03.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Abras v. The State (Crl. A. No. 655/2020, decided 12.03.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Punjab Assembly Recruitment Case
records.heading: Bail was allowed in the Punjab Assembly recruitment case
records.text: The post announces the full judgment of the Lahore High Court allowing the bail application of the accused in the Punjab Assembly recruitment case. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 685; Ch. Parvez Elahi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 20737/24).
records.title: Ch. Parvez Elahi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 20737/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR for Slogans: S. 16 of Ordinance and S. 341 PPC
records.heading: An FIR for slogans fails where it does not state the slogans chanted
records.text: Section 16 of the Ordinance needs words or reports causing fear or alarm to the public or prejudice to public safety, and the FIR did not state what slogans were chanted, so it was not attracted. The court also considered s. 341 PPC and the petitioner's right of peaceful assembly, noting no s. 144 CrPC order was alleged. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 392; Rai Muhammad Usama Sultan v. DPO Chiniot etc. (Criminal Proceedings 50329/24).
records.title: Rai Muhammad Usama Sultan v. DPO Chiniot etc. (Criminal Proceedings 50329/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Discharge Set Aside: Civil and Criminal Standards of Proof
records.heading: Civil and criminal standards of proof differ and findings in one do not bind the other
records.text: Civil cases are decided on preponderance of evidence, while in criminal cases the prosecution must prove its case beyond doubt, and findings in one proceeding do not bind the other. The Magistrate's discharge order was perverse and set aside, and the matter was sent to the Sessions Judge for assignment to another Magistrate to decide afresh. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 403, 2025 PCrLJ 1983; Rasoolan Bibi v. The State etc. (WP 82843/23).
records.title: Rasoolan Bibi v. The State etc. (WP 82843/23)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Guidelines for Pre-Arrest Bail under S. 498 CrPC
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is extraordinary relief and no substitute for post-arrest bail
records.text: Pre-arrest bail is an extraordinary relief to protect innocent persons from abuse of law and is no substitute for post-arrest bail. The applicant must meet the conditions of s. 497(2) CrPC, show that arrest is sought for ulterior motives such as humiliation, and have no disentitling conduct such as a criminal record or absconding. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 87; Muhammad Ali Mahar and another v. State (Crl. P. No. 201-K of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ali Mahar and another v. State (Crl. P. No. 201-K of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift (Tamleek): Beneficiary's Heavy Onus
records.heading: The beneficiary of a challenged gift bears a heavy onus and courts scrutinise closely
records.text: Where gifts or tamleek by a deceased propositus are used to defeat lawful shares in inheritance, courts must scrutinise the evidence closely. The beneficiary of a challenged gift or transfer of immovable property bears a heavy onus to prove the transaction. Ref: Hidayat Khan and others v. Mst. Nasreen and others (C.P.L.A. 287-P/2025, decided 24.04.2025); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Hidayat Khan and others v. Mst. Nasreen and others (C.P.L.A. 287-P/2025, decided 24.04.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Abscondance Disentitles Accused to Bail
records.heading: Unexplained abscondance disentitles an accused to bail irrespective of merits
records.text: Unexplained noticeable abscondance disentitles a person to bail irrespective of the merits, as it thwarts the investigation and loses evidence such as recoveries. Three categories of absconder are described: one who fled before conviction, one whose sentence was suspended under s. 426 CrPC and who then absconded, and one convicted on appeal who has not surrendered. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 661.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Registered Tamleek Deeds: Identity of Donee and Donor's Denial
records.heading: A donor's denial does not void a registered tamleek deed whose execution is proved
records.text: Mere denial of a gift or tamleek by the donor, even if alive, does not render a registered deed void where its execution is admitted or proved. Courts must examine the document and its context, including donor and donee relationship and absence of fraud, to identify the actual donee. Ref: 2025 LHC 2682; Muhammad Nawaz etc. v. Muhammad Farrukh Rauf etc. (Civil Revision 1-15, decided 10.04.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz etc. v. Muhammad Farrukh Rauf etc. (Civil Revision 1-15, decided 10.04.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC Grounds; Art. 113 Limitation
records.heading: A plaint is rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC only on the stated grounds
records.text: A plaint may be rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC only where it discloses no cause of action, is barred by law, or is undervalued or insufficiently stamped and the deficiency is not made up in time, which was not the case here. Art. 113 of the Limitation Act, 1908 gives three years for specific performance. Ref: 2025 LHC 2719; Muhammad Iqbal etc. v. Muhammad Ashraf etc. (Civil Revision 2164-11, decided 25.04.2025); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal etc. v. Muhammad Ashraf etc. (Civil Revision 2164-11, decided 25.04.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Press Clipping as Material at Bail Stage
records.heading: A press clipping may be considered relevant material at the bail stage
records.text: A press clipping, being explanatory evidence, can be considered relevant material at the bail stage. Ref: 2025 LHC 2726; Samar Abbas v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 699-B-25, decided 22.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Samar Abbas v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 699-B-25, decided 22.04.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody: Father Abroad and Mother's Second Marriage
records.heading: A father abroad cannot claim custody merely as natural guardian where the mother remarried
records.text: A father who has never met his minor daughter and lives abroad cannot claim custody merely as natural guardian where the mother has remarried. A mother's second marriage does not itself disqualify her. On remarriage of either parent the court weighs circumstances and the minor's attachment, with welfare paramount under Art. 3(1) UNCRC. Ref: Asjad Ullah v. Mst. Aisa Bano and others (C.P.L.A. 3920/2024, decided 22.04.2025).
records.title: Asjad Ullah v. Mst. Aisa Bano and others (C.P.L.A. 3920/2024, decided 22.04.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Talaq-e-Biddat and Inheritance During Iddat
records.heading: A written talaq by post is not final if the husband dies within ninety days
records.text: Where a husband sent a written divorce by post and died within ninety days, the talaq had not become final under s. 7(3) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, so the wife remained his lawful widow and was entitled to inherit. Succession opens on death, relying on 1988 SCMR 1812. Petition dismissed and leave declined. Ref: Aziz Ahmad and others v. Mst. Musarat (C.P.L.A. 181 of 2023, decided 09.04.2025); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui; Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Aziz Ahmad and others v. Mst. Musarat (C.P.L.A. 181 of 2023, decided 09.04.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail Refused in Drowning Murder
records.heading: Post-arrest bail was refused where postmortem and histopathology corroborated drowning
records.text: Post-arrest bail was refused under s. 497 CrPC in a case under ss. 302, 148 and 149 PPC. The accused was named in the FIR, two witnesses supported the case under s. 161 CrPC, and the postmortem and forensic histopathology report of ante-mortem drowning corroborated the ocular account. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 672.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Civil Court Jurisdiction over Government Colony Land
records.heading: Section 36 bars the civil court from Government colony land vested in the revenue hierarchy
records.text: Where land is owned by the Provincial Government, s. 36 of the Colonization of Government Lands (Punjab) Act, 1912 bars the civil court from entering into the vested right of the revenue hierarchy. Ref: 2024 CLC 1193.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Review of Mutation after Fifty Years
records.heading: Revenue authorities cannot review a mutation after more than fifty years
records.text: Correction of revenue entries and of a mutation sanctioned in 1948 after more than fifty years is not within the powers of revenue authorities, especially in review proceedings, where the original persons never agitated the matter in their lifetime. The constitutional petition was dismissed. Ref: 2023 YLR 1182.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Civil Servants and Art. 199 Writ Jurisdiction
records.heading: Civil servants cannot invoke Art. 199 jurisdiction on terms of service given Art. 212
records.text: Civil servants cannot invoke the High Court's constitutional jurisdiction on terms and conditions of service by challenging laws or notifications, given Art. 212 and the requirement of no other adequate remedy under Art. 199. Ref: 2025 LHC 2787; Tassawar Ali Khan etc. v. POP etc. (WP 42822/21, decided 29.04.2025); Justice Malik Waqar Haider Awan.
records.title: Tassawar Ali Khan etc. v. POP etc. (WP 42822/21, decided 29.04.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Rule 17-A Appointments and Retrospective Effect
records.heading: Appointment processes concluded before Rule 17-A was omitted are closed
records.text: Appointment processes concluded before Rule 17-A of the Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1974 was omitted on 24.07.2024 are closed. The Supreme Court judgment in General Post Office, Islamabad v. Muhammad Jalal applies retrospectively to those whose appointment process was underway until its pronouncement on 18.10.2024. Ref: 2025 LHC 2777; Province of Punjab etc. v. Syed Muhammad Ali Raza Shah (ICA No. 2407/25); Justice Malik Waqar Haider Awan.
records.title: Province of Punjab etc. v. Syed Muhammad Ali Raza Shah (ICA No. 2407/25)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Military Trial of Civilians: Intra Court Appeals Allowed
records.heading: Provisions of the Pakistan Army Act on military trial of civilians were restored on appeal
records.text: By majority of five judges the intra court appeals were allowed in a short order, the impugned judgment set aside, and ss. 2(1)(d)(i) and (ii) and s. 59(4) of the Pakistan Army Act, 1952 restored. Those provisions could not be declared ultra vires on the basis of Art. 8(5) of the Constitution. Detailed reasons were reserved. Ref: Shuhada Forum, Balochistan through its Patron in Chief, Nawabzada Jamal Raisani, Quetta Cantt and others v. Justice (R) Jawwad S. Khawaja and others (I.C.A. 5/2023, decided 07.05.2025); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Musarrat Hilali; Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Shuhada Forum, Balochistan through its Patron in Chief, Nawabzada Jamal Raisani, Quetta Cantt and others v. Justice (R) Jawwad S. Khawaja and others (I.C.A. 5/2023, decided 07.05.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Domicile Certificate Determines Permanent Residence
records.heading: The domicile certificate and not the CNIC address determines permanent residence
records.text: The domicile certificate, and not the CNIC address, determines a candidate's permanent residence for employment. Candidates who passed competitive examinations and held valid domicile certificates could not be denied appointment on technical grounds, relying on the distinction between domicile and residence and the doctrine of legitimate expectation. Ref: District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.R.P. 5/2023, decided 25.04.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.R.P. 5/2023, decided 25.04.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Scope of Review before Supreme Court; Costs
records.heading: Review before the Supreme Court is limited and frivolous reviews attract costs
records.text: The judgment addresses the scope of review before the Supreme Court, deprecates the practice of filing a review in every matter, and directs imposition of costs in every frivolous and vexatious matter that wastes the court's time. Ref: District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.R.P. 5/2023, decided 25.04.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.R.P. 5/2023, decided 25.04.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification Parade and Recovery from Open Place
records.heading: A parade after a prior sighting has no value and open place recovery is unsafe
records.text: Where the accused may have been seen by the identifying witness before the test identification parade, the proceedings carry no evidentiary value. Reliance on a recovery from an open and accessible place is unsafe, as it cannot be said to be from the accused's exclusive possession. Ref: Usman Ahmed v. The State (Crl.A. 566/2020, decided 15.04.2025); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Usman Ahmed v. The State (Crl.A. 566/2020, decided 15.04.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Promotion Committee Cannot Question Vires of Rules
records.heading: A Departmental Promotion Committee cannot sit in judgment over the vires of rules
records.text: A Departmental Promotion Committee must act in accordance with law and cannot sit in judgment over the vires of the law or rules. The judgment also discusses the role of the civil service in a democratic state. Ref: Aatika Hina Mushtaq v. Secretary Special Education Government of the Punjab, Special Education Department Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 3116/2022, decided 21.04.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Aatika Hina Mushtaq v. Secretary Special Education Government of the Punjab, Special Education Department Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 3116/2022, decided 21.04.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Livelihood Abroad as Ground to Dispense with Attendance
records.heading: Earning a livelihood abroad is a valid reason to dispense with attendance
records.text: Earning a livelihood abroad is a valid reason to dispense with the accused's attendance. The judgment also distinguishes conviction, a guilty verdict, from sentence, the punishment imposed under it. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 405, PLJ 2025 CrC 181; Rai Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 40397/24).
records.title: Rai Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 40397/24)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Sexual Harassment and Safe Workplace
