records.heading: A harassment free workplace rests on constitutional guarantees of life, dignity and equality
records.text: Sexual harassment concerns power rather than sex or formal position. The right to a harassment-free workplace for men, women and transgender persons rests on constitutional guarantees of life, liberty, dignity and equality. The judgment also considers gendered power dynamics, social reinforcement and intersectionality. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 354; Muhammad Din v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Population Welfare, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 2541/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Din v. Province of Punjab through Secretary, Population Welfare, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A. 2541/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance of a Missing Person
records.heading: Inheritance in a missing person's estate arises from presumed death and not disappearance
records.text: Inheritance rights in a missing person's estate arise from the date he is presumed dead and not from disappearance, and an heir dying before that date is disqualified. Under Hanafi law he is presumed alive up to ninety years from birth. Arts. 123 and 124 QSO apply, and absent proof of a date, death is presumed at the institution of the suit. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 387; Iqbal Ali Khan & others v. Naseeb Ali Khan & others (C.A. 44-P/2012).
records.title: Iqbal Ali Khan & others v. Naseeb Ali Khan & others (C.A. 44-P/2012)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Account from 500 Metres
records.heading: Distance of observation is critical and a view from 500 metres is far-fetched
records.text: The prosecution must establish the credibility of its witnesses, and the distance from which they claim to have seen the incident is critical. At 500 metres even persons of excellent eyesight cannot discern specific details of an event, so the witnesses' claim was far-fetched. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 383; Ameeruddin v. The State (Criminal Appeal 198/2023).
records.title: Ameeruddin v. The State (Criminal Appeal 198/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Medical Treatment Included in Maintenance
records.heading: Medical treatment forms part of maintenance and cannot be capped
records.text: Maintenance for a wife and children is of wide connotation, inclusive of many heads without being exhaustive, and cannot be limited by a cap. Medical treatment forms part of maintenance, within the husband's means. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 367; Muhammad Irfan v. Additional District Judge Ferozwala District Sheikhupura & others (C.P.L.A. 3179-L/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan v. Additional District Judge Ferozwala District Sheikhupura & others (C.P.L.A. 3179-L/2023)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Trial Court's Power to Order Accused's DNA Test
records.heading: A trial court may order the accused's DNA test under the Punjab forensic science Act
records.text: Section 10 of the Punjab forensic science Act of 2007 lets a court send forensic material to the PFSA for analysis, and a DNA sample falls within the definition in s. 2(1)(g). The trial court may therefore order the accused's DNA test and comparison with samples taken from the victim. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 430; Shakeel Akhtar v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 71205/21).
records.title: Shakeel Akhtar v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 71205/21)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation in Inheritance Claims: Exceptions
records.heading: Limitation, waiver and acquiescence are not irrelevant in every inheritance claim
records.text: Limitation, waiver and acquiescence cannot be treated as irrelevant in every inheritance claim. Where a predecessor did not challenge, in his or her lifetime, a transaction depriving the share and third party rights were created, a simple claim of inheritance does not avoid limitation. Limitation has been disregarded only in exceptional cases, such as suits by female heirs within their lifetime alleging fraud, and cases where acquiescence and waiver are absent. Ref: 2025 LHC 2832; Muhammad Hafeez v. Muhammad Ramzan etc (WP 10459/19), decided 23.04.2025; Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: Muhammad Hafeez v. Muhammad Ramzan etc (WP 10459/19), decided 23.04.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Concealment by Eye Witnesses; Medical Evidence on Time
records.heading: Eyewitnesses who conceal vital facts cannot be relied on for conviction
records.text: If the complainant and injured eye witnesses conceal vital facts of the occurrence, they cannot be relied upon for conviction. Where medical evidence is uncertain about the interval between injury and death and between death and autopsy, it cannot support the ocular account on the time of occurrence or death. Ref: 2025 LHC 2815; Ghulam Qadir v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 79724/21), decided 30.04.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Ghulam Qadir v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 79724/21), decided 30.04.2025

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Public Institutions and Frivolous Petitions: Costs
records.heading: Public institutions must avoid frivolous petitions and may face costs
records.text: Public institutions must avoid filing meritless petitions. Costs may be imposed on meritless and frivolous petitions, and there should be internal accountability within the institution for filing them. Public institutions should maintain a robust internal scrutiny system to prevent frivolous and repetitive petitions. Ref: Federal Public Service Commission through its Secretary, Islamabad v. Kashif Mustafa and others (C.R.P.292/2024), decided 08.05.2025; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Federal Public Service Commission through its Secretary, Islamabad v. Kashif Mustafa and others (C.R.P.292/2024), decided 08.05.2025

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Articles as Tarka: Family Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: The Family Court has no jurisdiction over a Tarka claim to dowry articles
records.text: A Family Court's jurisdiction is limited to the matters listed in s. 5 and the Schedule and does not extend to claims of inheritance or Tarka. Parents of a deceased wife who claimed a share in her dowry articles as Tarka had no locus standi to sue in the Family Court, and the suit was not maintainable. Ref: PLD 2025 Balochistan 49.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Executability of Decree: Cost of Funds Award
records.heading: Executability of a decree can be raised in execution and a decree without jurisdiction is void
records.text: Questions on the executability of a decree can be raised in execution proceedings, and a decree passed by a court or forum without jurisdiction over the subject matter is void. The Division Bench set aside the Executing Court's order as the decree was not executable to the extent of the award of cost of funds. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 425.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Memory Lapses and Slips of Tongue of Witnesses
records.heading: Memory lapses and a mere slip of tongue do not destroy testimony
records.text: With the passage of time human memory fails and facts cannot be repeated photographically, particularly where the occurrence was in 2019 and cross-examination in 2021. A mere slip of tongue by a witness cannot destroy the evidentiary value of testimony or render it unreliable. Ref: 2025 LHC 2952; Muhammad Amir alias Aneel v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 83064/23), decided 29.04.2025.
records.title: Muhammad Amir alias Aneel v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 83064/23), decided 29.04.2025

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Enforcement of Court Undertakings in Execution
records.heading: A court undertaking is enforceable in execution as if it were a decree
records.text: An undertaking given before a court is enforceable in execution proceedings as if it were a decree. The Executing Court may use all permissible means, including coercive measures, to ensure compliance. Ref: 2025 LHC 3050; Sher Muhammad v. Karam Hussain etc (Civil Revision 883-16), decided 06.02.2025; Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Sher Muhammad v. Karam Hussain etc (Civil Revision 883-16), decided 06.02.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Changed Place of Occurrence; Identification Parade
records.heading: Changing the place of injury at trial is fatal and a parade on appearance alone is ineffective
records.text: If the prosecution changes the venue of receipt of the deceased's injuries during trial, that is fatal to its case. Where identification of an unknown accused rests on external appearance without details of facial features, an identification parade has no legal efficacy. Ref: 2025 LHC 2992; Yasir Shaban v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 39118/21), decided 06.05.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Yasir Shaban v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 39118/21), decided 06.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Eye Witnesses: Substitution Improbable
records.heading: Relationship alone does not discredit consistent eyewitnesses and substitution is improbable
records.text: Substitution of the real culprit for an innocent person is improbable where close relatives are killed in the presence of family members. Absent mala fide or ulterior motive for false implication, consistent and confidence inspiring eye witness testimony cannot be discredited merely because of relationship with the deceased. Ref: Altaf Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.507 of 2023), decided 07.05.2025.
records.title: Altaf Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.507 of 2023), decided 07.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Witness Testimony
records.heading: Minor discrepancies not going to the root of the case are inconsequential
records.text: Minor discrepancies and omissions that do not go to the root of the prosecution case are inconsequential, and only material discrepancies striking at its heart help the defence. Credibility depends on the intrinsic worth of the testimony as a whole, not the status of the witness, relying on 2011 SCMR 208. Ref: Iftikhar Kiyani alias Khara v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 703 of 2020), decided 28.04.2025.
records.title: Iftikhar Kiyani alias Khara v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 703 of 2020), decided 28.04.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive: Failure to Prove Once Alleged
records.heading: Once motive is alleged the prosecution must prove it or bear the consequences
records.text: The prosecution need not prove motive in every case, but once a motive is set up it must be established. If the prosecution fails to prove it, the prosecution must bear the consequences and not the defence. Ref: Khizar Hayat v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 181/2022), decided 28.04.2025.
records.title: Khizar Hayat v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 181/2022), decided 28.04.2025

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Unbroken Chain of Custody
records.heading: A lacuna in the chain of custody renders the chemical examiner's report unreliable
records.text: In narcotics cases the prosecution must establish an unbroken, secure and reliable chain of custody from seizure to receipt at the forensic laboratory. Any lacuna or discrepancy makes the process suspect and renders the chemical examiner's report inadmissible or at least unreliable. Ref: Zakir Ali v. The State (Jail Petition No.343 of 2023), decided 24.04.2025.
records.title: Zakir Ali v. The State (Jail Petition No.343 of 2023), decided 24.04.2025

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Evidence Not Put to Accused
records.heading: Evidence not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used against him
records.text: Evidence that was not put to the accused in his statement under s. 342 CrPC, so as to give him a chance to meet it in his defence, cannot be used against him. Ref: Obaid Ullah v. The State (JP 14 & 17 of 2020), decided 02.05.2025.
records.title: Obaid Ullah v. The State (JP 14 & 17 of 2020), decided 02.05.2025

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody of Narcotics and Sample Parcel
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody of case property and sample parcel leads to acquittal
records.text: An unbroken chain of safe custody of the recovered case property and sample parcel must be proved, as recovery of narcotics constitutes the offence itself. If safe custody is not proved, acquittal follows. Ref: 2025 YLR 867, PLJ 2025 Cr.C 35; Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40132/23).
records.title: Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40132/23)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Putting Incriminating Material
records.heading: All incriminating material must be put to the accused under section 342 CrPC
records.text: For conviction and sentence it is mandatory to put the entire incriminating material to the accused under s. 342 CrPC to obtain his explanation. Failure amounts to a violation of audi alteram partem. Ref: 2025 YLR 867, PLJ 2025 Cr.C 35; Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40132/23).
records.title: Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 40132/23)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested and Disinterested Witnesses: Quality over Quantity
records.heading: Interested witnesses are not automatically disbelieved and evidence is tested on quality
records.text: There is no universal rule that interested witnesses must be disbelieved or disinterested witnesses believed. It depends on prudence and reasonableness. Prosecution evidence is tested on quality and not quantity, and it is the statement and not the person that must be judged. Ref: 2025 SCMR 935; Akbar Saeed v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.P.L.A.1366/2018).
records.title: Akbar Saeed v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.P.L.A.1366/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies: Ring of Truth Test
records.heading: Minor discrepancies are ignored where the evidence has a ring of truth
records.text: Where the material aspects of the evidence have a ring of truth, minor discrepancies should be ignored. The test is whether the evidence inspires confidence when read as a whole. Only an omission or discrepancy going to the root of the prosecution case can be taken advantage of by the defence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 935; Akbar Saeed v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.P.L.A.1366/2018).
records.title: Akbar Saeed v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.P.L.A.1366/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification at Night: Source of Light Not in FIR
records.heading: Identification at night is doubtful where the FIR mentions no source of light
records.text: Where the occurrence took place at night and the FIR mentions no source of light, and no such source was recovered, identification of the accused in darkness is not free from doubt. Ref: 2025 SCMR 944; Chetan v. The State (Crl.A.94/2023).
records.title: Chetan v. The State (Crl.A.94/2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302(b) PPC: Death or Life Imprisonment Discretion
records.heading: The two punishments under section 302(b) PPC are alternate and reasons must be recorded
records.text: The two punishments under s. 302(b) PPC are distinct and alternate, and the court must exercise sentencing discretion with care, recording under s. 367(5) CrPC the reasons for a sentence other than death. Mitigating factors are relevant, and the list is not exhaustive. Enhancement of sentence must be exercised sparingly, only to prevent grave miscarriage of justice. Ref: 2025 SCMR 993, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 128; Fida Hussain @ Saboo v. The State (Crl.Appeal No 530 of 2022).
records.title: Fida Hussain @ Saboo v. The State (Crl.Appeal No 530 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Photo Account Cheque: Suit under O. XXXVII
records.heading: A Photo Account cheque dishonoured in the holder's absence gives no cause for an O. XXXVII suit
records.text: Under cl. 1.5 of State Bank Circular 10 dated 29.03.2003, a Photo Account cheque presented unilaterally without associating the account holder and dishonoured in his absence gives an invalid dishonour. It does not create a cause of action for a suit under Order XXXVII CPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 3273; Salamat Ali v. Sabohi Naz (R.F.A 27359/24), decided 05.05.2025; Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Salamat Ali v. Sabohi Naz (R.F.A 27359/24), decided 05.05.2025

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Thirty Years Old Document: Presumption of Genuineness
records.heading: The thirty year presumption of genuineness is rebuttable and age does not prevail over doubt
records.text: A dower deed over thirty years old carries a rebuttable presumption of genuineness, which rests on its unsuspicious character and proper custody. If execution or custody is prima facie disputed, the court must determine genuineness, and age alone does not prevail over doubt. The Supreme Court declined to re-appraise evidence. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2025 SCMR 841.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Declaratory Suit: Accrual of Right to Sue
records.heading: The right to sue for a declaration accrues on denial and each denial gives fresh cause
records.text: A suit for declaration of title is based on a continuing right that subsists while the plaintiff holds rights in the property. The right to sue accrues when the opposing party denies or challenges the right or unequivocally threatens it. Successive acts of denial give rise to a fresh cause of action each time. Ref: 2025 SCMR 955; Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift: Donor Need Not Give Reasons
records.heading: A donor need not explain a gift but courts may scrutinise its motives
records.text: A donor is not legally obliged to explain the decision to make a gift. Gifts are often made to disadvantage female family members and defeat their inheritance, so courts may scrutinise the motives and circumstances of a gift to protect rightful ownership and established lines of inheritance. Ref: 2025 SCMR 955; Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fraudulent Transactions: Limitation No Bar
records.heading: Fraud unravels a transaction regardless of limitation
records.text: Fraud unravels all aspects of a transaction however solemnly it was conducted, and a transaction born of deceit must be declared void and judged on its merits. This prevents entrenchment of fraudulent acts regardless of limitation issues. Ref: 2025 SCMR 955; Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Does Not Confer Title
records.heading: Mutation does not confer title and the party relying on it must prove the original transaction
records.text: Mutation does not confer title and is only a record for fiscal purposes, and illegal approval of a mutation by a Revenue Officer has no bearing on title. An oral gift is permissible, and where a mutation is challenged the parties relying on it must prove the original transaction behind it. Ref: 2025 SCMR 955; Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Fingerprints: Dactyloscopy as Forensic Tool
records.heading: Fingerprint identification is widely accepted and an indispensable forensic tool
records.text: Fingerprint identification (dactyloscopy) is widely accepted and an indispensable tool in law. It rests on the principle that no two fingerprints are alike and that an individual's patterns remain constant throughout life. Ref: 2025 SCMR 955; Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Ramzanoon Bibi v. Ibrahim (deceased) through L.Rs, etc (C.A.113-L/2010)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Maxim: Interest Reipublicae Ut Sit Finis Litium
records.heading: It is in the interest of the State that litigation should end
records.text: The maxim interest reipublicae ut sit finis litium means that it is in the interest of the State that there should be an end to litigation. Ref: 2025 SCMR 819.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Maxim: Communi Observantia Non Est Recedendum
records.heading: What the law requires done in a particular manner must be done accordingly
records.text: When the law requires a thing to be done in a particular manner it must be done accordingly, and if the prescribed procedure is not followed it is presumed that the act was not done in accordance with law. Ref: 2025 SCMR 923.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 154 CrPC: Prosecution Story Must Be Natural
records.heading: The prosecution story must be natural, convincing and free from inherent improbability
records.text: The prosecution story is the foundation of the case and must stand to reason, be natural and convincing and free from inherent improbability. It is unsafe to believe a story that fails this standard, and a conviction cannot rest on an improbable story. Ref: 2025 SCMR 880; Muhammad Qasim v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Qasim v. State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Pleadings Are Not Evidence
records.heading: A plea in pleadings is not evidence and must be proved independently
records.text: A plea raised in pleadings has no effect without evidence in proof, and does not equate to evidence. The party asserting a fact in pleadings must prove it by independent and unimpeachable evidence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 860, PLJ 2025 SC 494; Rana Muhammad Yameen v. Muhammad Jamil (Civil Appeal No.151-P of 2013), decided 21.02.2025.
records.title: Rana Muhammad Yameen v. Muhammad Jamil (Civil Appeal No.151-P of 2013), decided 21.02.2025

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 22 QSO and Police Rules: Parameters
records.heading: Authority on the parameters of identification under Art. 22 QSO and the Police Rules
records.text: Authority on the parameters under Article 22 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order 1984, the Rules and Orders of the Lahore High Court Vol. 3 Ch. 2 Part C and rule 26.32 of Ch. 26 Vol. 3 of the Police Rules 1934. Ref: 2025 SCMR 868; Rashid and another v. The State (Crl.A.282-L/2020).
records.title: Rashid and another v. The State (Crl.A.282-L/2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Omission to Frame Charge: Not Curable by S. 537
records.heading: Omission to frame a charge for a distinct offence is not curable under section 537
records.text: Failure to frame a charge for a distinct offence goes to the root of the trial and cannot be cured under s. 537 CrPC, unlike a merely defective charge. Ss. 221 and 233 CrPC require a charge for each distinct offence, and s. 237 is subject to s. 236. Omission of a charge together with failure to put the accusation under s. 342 is a grave irregularity. Ref: 2025 SCMR 802; Shabeer Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.28 of 2023).
records.title: Shabeer Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.28 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive in Cases of Direct Evidence
records.heading: Motive holds greater value where there is direct evidence
records.text: Motive holds even greater value where there is direct evidence, and it provides the final supporting element for the prosecution at the conclusion of its case. Ref: 2025 SCMR 894; Sher Afzal v. The State (Crl.A.229/2021).
records.title: Sher Afzal v. The State (Crl.A.229/2021)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Junaid Hafeez Blasphemy Trial Court Judgment
records.heading: The trial court judgment of 21 December 2019 in the Junaid Hafeez blasphemy case
records.text: The post shares the trial court judgment dated 21 December 2019 sentencing Junaid Hafeez to death for blasphemy. It urges those who criticise the decision on social media to read the judgment carefully before forming a view. Ref: The State v. Junaid Hafeez, decided 21.12.2019.
records.title: The State v. Junaid Hafeez, decided 21.12.2019

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Potency Test under S. 53-A CrPC
records.heading: Failure to produce a potency test under section 53-A CrPC creates serious doubt
records.text: S. 53-A CrPC underlines the significance of a potency test of the accused in sexual offences under ss. 376, 377 and 377-B PPC. Where the prosecution did not produce this material evidence, it could not establish that the appellant was potent, which creates serious doubt about its case. Ref: PLJ 2025 Cr.C. 360; Rizwan Sami Khan v. State etc (Crl. A. No. 41759 of 2022).
records.title: Rizwan Sami Khan v. State etc (Crl. A. No. 41759 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Forensic Report of Human Blood on Weapon
records.heading: A report of human blood alone on the weapon has no evidentiary value
records.text: A forensic agency report showing only human blood on the weapon, without findings on the origin of the blood or its comparison with the victim's blood, has no evidentiary value. Ref: PLJ 2025 Cr.C. 326; Ali Akbar etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 31052/23).
records.title: Ali Akbar etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 31052/23)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. I R. 10 CPC: Liberal Approach to Impleadment
records.heading: Impleadment under O. I R. 10 CPC should be approached liberally and not pedantically
records.text: On applications under Order I Rule 10 CPC the court should exercise discretion liberally and not narrowly or pedantically, especially where a party is likely to be affected by the judgment and its presence would enable effective adjudication. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 283; Abdul Aziz and others v. All Pakistan Clerks Association (CPLA No. 251-Q of 2024).
records.title: Abdul Aziz and others v. All Pakistan Clerks Association (CPLA No. 251-Q of 2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: S. 29 CNSA: Presumption and Prosecution Burden
records.heading: The section 29 presumption does not relieve the prosecution of proving its case
records.text: The presumption under s. 29 against the accused on recovery of contraband does not relieve the prosecution of proving its case beyond doubt. The burden shifts to the accused only if recovery, nexus with the accused and the contraband origin are proved without ambiguity. Contradictions in the prosecution case led to acquittal. Ref: 2025 YLR 888; Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Procedure for Exhibiting Case Property Articles
records.heading: Case property forming circumstantial evidence must be produced, marked and connected by witnesses
records.text: Guidelines for tendering articles in evidence are in Rules and Orders of the Lahore High Court Vol. III Ch. 24 Part B, including Rules 14-F and 14-H. Articles forming part of circumstantial evidence must be produced and connected by witnesses, and exhibits must be marked and labelled. Exhibiting allows the accused to cross-examine on the article. Ref: 2025 YLR 888, PLJ 2025 CrC 485; Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Meaning of Contradiction in Evidence
records.heading: Contradiction means setting one statement against another and covers legal omissions
records.text: The expression contradiction is wide and covers legal omissions, shortcomings and lacunas, and applies where acceptance of one witness's deposition requires rejection of another's. It means setting one statement against another and not a statement against nothing, relying on P Ramanatha Aiyar's Advanced Law Lexicon. Ref: 2025 YLR 888; Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.628 of 2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift of Immovable Property: Onus on Beneficiary
records.heading: The beneficiary of an immovable property gift must plead and prove its three ingredients
records.text: The beneficiary of a gift or transfer of immovable property bears a heavy onus to prove the transaction. The beneficiary must plead and prove the three mandatory ingredients of a gift. The post describes the judgment as an extensive review of Supreme Court authority on gifts. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 526, 2025 CLC 1158; Mst. Sadiqan Begum v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision No. 27145 of 2017).
records.title: Mst. Sadiqan Begum v. Muhammad Siddique (Civil Revision No. 27145 of 2017)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Framing of Charge: Scope of Judicial Scrutiny
records.heading: At charge framing the court sifts investigation material without assessing probative value
records.text: At the stage of framing charge the court considers only material collected during investigation that can legally become evidence, and cannot assess its probative value. The judge is not a post office for the prosecution and must sift material to see if there is strong suspicion of guilt. The final test of guilt is not applied. Ref: 2025 LHC 3194; Shiraz Ahmad v. State (Crl. Revision No. 39743 of 2024, date of hearing 14.05.2025).
records.title: Shiraz Ahmad v. State (Crl. Revision No. 39743 of 2024, date of hearing 14.05.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recording of Evidence in Presence of Accused
records.heading: Examination in chief must be recorded in the presence of the accused
records.text: Recording of evidence is a solemn duty of the trial court, and the examination-in-chief of witnesses must be recorded in the presence of the accused. S. 353 CrPC permits recording in the accused's presence, or in the presence of counsel if the court dispenses with the accused's attendance. Ref: 2025 LHC 3197; Shiraz Ahmad v. State (Crl. Revision No.37104 of 2024, date of hearing 14.05.2025).
records.title: Shiraz Ahmad v. State (Crl. Revision No.37104 of 2024, date of hearing 14.05.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal Breach of Trust: Entrustment and Loan
records.heading: A loan is not entrustment and criminal breach of trust needs entrustment and dishonesty
records.text: Criminal breach of trust under ss. 405 and 406 PPC requires entrustment of property and dishonest misappropriation. Entrustment creates a fiduciary relationship in which the same property must be returned, and a loan does not qualify as entrustment because the relationship is purely contractual. The judgment also distinguishes quashment of proceedings from quashment of an FIR. Ref: Ayesha Tayyab v. Station House Officer, Police Station Cantt., District Sialkot and others (C.P.L.A.1575/2024), decided 13.05.2025; Justice Sardar Tariq Masood.
records.title: Ayesha Tayyab v. Station House Officer, Police Station Cantt., District Sialkot and others (C.P.L.A.1575/2024), decided 13.05.2025

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Misuse in Loan and Business Disputes
records.heading: Section 406 PPC needs entrustment as amanat and dishonest misappropriation, not loan disputes
records.text: The Supreme Court expressed concern at FIRs under s. 406 PPC registered in loan or business transactions. Criminal breach of trust needs entrustment of property as amanat, and dishonest misappropriation or conversion, or use or disposal in violation of law or a legal contract. Both elements must be present. Ref: Muhammad Amjad Naeem v. The State through P.G Punjab, Lahore and another (Crl.P.L.A.170-L/2025), decided 19.05.2025; Justice Sardar Tariq Masood.
records.title: Muhammad Amjad Naeem v. The State through P.G Punjab, Lahore and another (Crl.P.L.A.170-L/2025), decided 19.05.2025

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Best Interests of the Child in Custody
records.heading: The child's welfare is read as the child's best interests and the child's voice matters
records.text: The judgment holds that the welfare of the child is to be read as the best interests of the child, applies the doctrine of updating construction of statutes, and addresses the voice and participation of the child in court proceedings. Ref: Dr. Muhammad Asiif v. Dr. Sana Sattar and others (C.R.P.458/2024), decided 16.05.2025; Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Dr. Muhammad Asiif v. Dr. Sana Sattar and others (C.R.P.458/2024), decided 16.05.2025

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Punjab Partition Act 2012: Internal Auction S. 10(2)
records.heading: Under the Punjab Partition Act every step is mandatory including co-owners' presence at auction
records.text: The Punjab Partition of Immoveable Property Act 2012 is procedural law and each step must be followed. Under s. 10(2) the court must require all co-owners to be present, in person or through authorised agents, on the date of internal auction. Where the law requires a thing to be done in a particular manner, it must be done in that manner. Ref: 2025 CLC 813; Naseem Bibi, etc. v. Imran Qayyum, etc. (W.P. No.57227 of 2024).
records.title: Naseem Bibi, etc. v. Imran Qayyum, etc. (W.P. No.57227 of 2024)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance on Oral Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A decree on an oral agreement to sell cannot rest on an irregular local commission report
records.text: A decree for specific performance of an oral agreement to sell cannot rest on a local commission report full of irregularities or on weaknesses in the defendant's case. Here the agreement was not concluded before an independent witness and the plaintiff's witnesses contradicted each other on its execution. Ref: 2025 CLC 885; Nasir Ali v. Mst. Raheela Mahdi (Civil Revision-241-22).
records.title: Nasir Ali v. Mst. Raheela Mahdi (Civil Revision-241-22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eye Witness Not Resident of Place of Occurrence
records.heading: A witness not resident at the scene may be believed given a plausible explanation
records.text: That the place of occurrence was not the witness's abode is not a universal rule for disbelieving his presence. If the witness gives a plausible explanation that appeals to a prudent mind, it must be given weight regardless of whether he lived in that vicinity. Ref: 2025 YLR 1001; The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19).
records.title: The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Collection of Blood Stained Earth
records.heading: Non-collection of bloodstained earth is at most an irregularity and gives no premium to the accused
records.text: Non-collection of blood stained earth from the crime scene is at most an irregularity on the part of the Investigating Officer, and no premium can be extended to the appellant on that basis. Ref: 2025 YLR 1001; The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19).
records.title: The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Accused Shifting Residence Before Occurrence
records.heading: Shifting of the accused's family before the occurrence gives no clean chit against eyewitnesses
records.text: Where two eye witnesses saw the appellant commit the murder and identified him in court, the mere shifting of his family to another place before the occurrence is no ground to give him a clean chit. Ref: 2025 YLR 1001; The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19).
records.title: The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Collection of CDR of Accused
records.heading: A CDR does not show who used the SIM so its non-collection does not assist the defence
records.text: A CDR only shows that a SIM registered to a person was used within the area of a specific tower. Without forensically evaluated voice record transcript or audio or video recording, it does not show who was using the SIM, so non-collection of the CDR does not assist the defence. Ref: 2025 YLR 1001; The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19).
records.title: The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence: Shifting Deceased to Hospital
records.heading: Shifting the deceased to hospital in hope of survival does not undermine medical evidence
records.text: Although the doctor opined that the interval between injuries and death was immediate, eye witnesses who shifted the deceased to hospital are ordinary people who cannot be presumed to judge death on the spot. Shifting an injured person to hospital in hope of survival is not unusual, and medical evidence supported the ocular account. Ref: 2025 YLR 1001; The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19).
records.title: The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis: Onset and Duration Vary
records.heading: The onset and duration of rigor mortis vary between individuals
records.text: Medical jurisprudence texts give typical timings for onset and completion of rigor mortis, but there is consensus that onset and duration vary between individuals owing to factors such as body condition, age, temperature, physical activity and illness. In sudden death a late onset and long duration is normal. Ref: 2025 YLR 1001; The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19).
records.title: The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Evidence Weighed and Not Counted
records.heading: Evidence is weighed and not counted and no particular number of witnesses is required
records.text: The law requires no particular number of witnesses to prove or disprove a fact. It is a time honoured principle that evidence must be weighed and not counted. Ref: 2025 YLR 1001; The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19).
records.title: The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Criminal Appeal No.78457 of 2019, MR.300-19)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Extra-Judicial and Judicial Confession
records.heading: An extra-judicial confession is weak and cannot found a capital conviction without strong corroboration
records.text: An extra-judicial confession is a weak piece of evidence and cannot found a conviction on a capital charge unless strongly corroborated by tangible evidence from an unimpeachable source. Art. 2(4) QSO sets the standard of a prudent man for the probative effect of evidence, and proof need not be absolute certainty. Ref: Bashir-ud-Din and Sharif-ud-Din v. The State (Crl.A.26/2021), decided 08.05.2025; Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Bashir-ud-Din and Sharif-ud-Din v. The State (Crl.A.26/2021), decided 08.05.2025

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Parents' Agreement and Welfare
records.heading: Custody of a minor cannot be settled by private compromise and welfare governs
records.text: Custody of a minor cannot be settled by private compromise or arbitration and must be decided on the principle of welfare of the minor. An agreement on custody in derogation of the child's right, or a divorced mother's second marriage, is no impediment to her retaining custody. No illegality was found in the concurrent judgments. Ref: 2025 MLD 773; Amjad Ali v. Additional District Judge, Pattoki and 2 others (WP Petition No. 76865).
records.title: Amjad Ali v. Additional District Judge, Pattoki and 2 others (WP Petition No. 76865)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sentencing: Single Fatal Shot Not Mitigating
records.heading: A single fatal shot does not mitigate sentence
records.text: Shooting a woman in the chest is not mitigated by the plea that only one shot was fired, as a single fatal shot shows lethal intent. The court agreed there were no mitigating circumstances for a lighter sentence in a killing arising from refusal of marriage, and condemned gender-based violence. Ref: Muhammad Kamran v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.A.91/2024), decided 16.05.2025; Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Muhammad Kamran v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.A.91/2024), decided 16.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis: Estimating Time Since Death
records.heading: Rigor mortis gives only a rough estimate of the time since death
records.text: Rigor mortis results from fusion of myosin and actin filaments into a stiff gel. In the Indian subcontinent it commences 2 to 3 hours after death, takes about 12 hours to develop, persists another 12 hours and takes about 12 hours to pass off. Its presence, extent or absence gives a rough estimate of time since death. Ref: 2025 LHC 3468; Ali Hassan v. The State (Jail Appeal 20548/22), decided 22.05.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Ali Hassan v. The State (Jail Appeal 20548/22), decided 22.05.2025

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: Time Between Injury and Death Not Stated
records.heading: An unstated interval between injury and death with uncertain cause makes a case of further inquiry
records.text: If the postmortem report does not state the time between injury and death, and the Medical Officer's opinion leaves the cause of death uncertain and the manner undetermined, the case falls within further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 3484; Maryam v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 9980/25), decided 29.05.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Maryam v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 9980/25), decided 29.05.2025

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Military Trial of Civilians: Dissenting Opinion
records.heading: Civilians not otherwise subject to the Army Act cannot be tried by courts martial, per dissent
records.text: In a detailed dissenting judgment in an intra-court appeal, Justice Jamal Mandokhail held that civilians not otherwise subject to the Pakistan Army Act, accused of offences under s. 2(1)(d) of that Act, cannot be tried by courts martial in the context of the 1973 Constitution and the injunctions of Islam. Ref: Justice Jamal Mandokhail.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness Needs Confidence-Inspiring Deposition
records.heading: An injured witness cannot be relied on merely for injuries if the deposition lacks confidence
records.text: An injured witness is a stamped witness, but cannot be relied on merely because he bears injuries if his deposition is not confidence inspiring. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 762, PLJ 2025 CrC 286; Allah Rakha etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 17661/19).
records.title: Allah Rakha etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 17661/19)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 196 CrPC: Complaint Needed at Cognizance Stage
records.heading: The section 196 CrPC complaint is needed at cognizance and not for registering the FIR
records.text: S. 196 CrPC concerns the stage of taking cognizance, which follows the s. 173 report. Its condition precedent is not mandatory for registering the FIR or starting investigation, but is required when the s. 173 report is submitted. If no government complaint accompanies the report, the court follows s. 230 CrPC and stays proceedings until it is received. Ref: Umair Altaf v. State (Criminal Misc. No.3033-B/2025), decided 15.05.2025.
records.title: Umair Altaf v. State (Criminal Misc. No.3033-B/2025), decided 15.05.2025

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Torture and Custodial Death Act 2022: FIA Investigation
records.heading: Only the FIA may investigate complaints under the Torture and Custodial Death Act 2022
records.text: Under s. 5 of the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act 2022, which begins with a non obstante clause, only the FIA may investigate complaints against public officials, supervised by the National Commission for Human Rights. Custodial rape is investigated by the FIA, and the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act 2021 is given secondary applicability. Ref: Zubaida Bibi v. District Police Officer and 02 others (Writ Petition No. 4926-HB of 2025, date of hearing 21.05.2025).
records.title: Zubaida Bibi v. District Police Officer and 02 others (Writ Petition No. 4926-HB of 2025, date of hearing 21.05.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Extra Judicial Confession: Witness Not Reacting
records.heading: A witness who does not react to an extra judicial confession is doubtful and DNA cannot corroborate nothing
records.text: A witness who does not react on hearing an extra judicial confession raises doubt about his conduct and testimony, and a circumstantial case built on it fails. Where there is no substantial evidence, a DNA report is of no help as corroboratory evidence, since there is nothing to corroborate. Ref: PLJ 2025 Cr.C 375; Muhammad Waqas v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 17977/20).
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 17977/20)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Place of Death: Hospital versus Inquest Report
records.heading: An ocular account of death in hospital contradicted by the inquest report benefits the convict
records.text: Where the ocular account says the deceased died in hospital but column 24 of the inquest report shows the body lying in the complainant's area, the prosecution case falls like a house of cards and the benefit goes to the convict. Ref: PLJ 2025 Cr.C 365; The State v. Ali Akbar Zia (M.R.8-20).
records.title: The State v. Ali Akbar Zia (M.R.8-20)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Number Absent in Inquest Report
records.heading: Absence of the FIR number in the inquest report suggests an ante-timed FIR
records.text: If the prosecution claims the FIR was recorded before the inquest report, the FIR number must appear on the first page of the inquest report. Its absence suggests the FIR was recorded with delay and ante-timed, which reduces its evidentiary value and is fatal to the prosecution. Ref: PLJ 2025 Cr.C 350; Zafar Iqbal Ilam Din v. The State (Jail Appeal 27878/22).
records.title: Zafar Iqbal Ilam Din v. The State (Jail Appeal 27878/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Close-Range Gunshot Effects: Medico-Legal Signs
records.heading: Burning, tattooing and blackening on entry wounds are signs of close-range discharge
records.text: Burning, scorching, singeing, blackening and tattooing on entry wounds are medico-legal signs of close-range discharge, and exit wounds are free from them. These signs help estimate firing distance and test the prosecution's factual account. The judgment draws on standard forensic medicine texts. Ref: 2025 LHC 3516; Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 22010/22), decided 15.05.2025; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 22010/22), decided 15.05.2025

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Appeal under S. 14: Restoration After Default Dismissal
records.heading: An appellate court may restore an appeal dismissed for non-prosecution on sufficient cause
records.text: An appellate court hearing an appeal under s. 14 of the Act, 1964 has inherent power to dismiss it for non-prosecution and can also restore it on sufficient cause being shown by the appellant. Ref: 2025 LHC 3536; Ahmed Amin v. District Judge etc (WP-2787-19), decided 29.04.2025; Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Ahmed Amin v. District Judge etc (WP-2787-19), decided 29.04.2025

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sudden Fight: Conviction Altered to S. 302(c)
records.heading: A sudden fight exceeding self-defence justifies conviction under section 302(c) PPC
records.text: The occurrence was at the spur of the moment without premeditation. The deceased, who was unarmed, initiated the confrontation, so firing exceeded lawful self-defence but justified conviction under s. 302(c) PPC. The sentence was reduced to fourteen years rigorous imprisonment and compensation to the heirs stood. Ref: Amir Khan v. The State (J.P.149/2018), decided 12.05.2025; Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Amir Khan v. The State (J.P.149/2018), decided 12.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Circumstantial Evidence
records.heading: Conviction on circumstantial evidence needs an unbroken chain excluding every innocent hypothesis
records.text: Even in capital cases conviction can rest on circumstantial evidence if it excludes every hypothesis of innocence, but it must be accepted with great caution and scrutinised minutely. The prosecution must prove every circumstance independently, forming an unbroken chain that leads to no inference other than guilt. Ref: Muhammad Wajid v. The State (Crl.A.212/2023), decided 15.05.2025; Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Muhammad Wajid v. The State (Crl.A.212/2023), decided 15.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt to Non-Appealing or Absconding Accused
records.heading: Benefit of doubt may extend to a non-appealing or absconding co-accused
records.text: If an appellate court concludes in the appeal of one accused that the prosecution evidence is doubtful and untrustworthy, the benefit of doubt can also be extended to a convict who filed no appeal and even to an absconding accused. Ref: Ghulam Mustafa alias Raja Buledi v. The State (Crl.A.199/2023), decided 12.05.2025; Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa alias Raja Buledi v. The State (Crl.A.199/2023), decided 12.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wife Killed in Husband's House: Duty to Explain
records.heading: A husband must explain a wife's unnatural death in his house after absconding
records.text: Where the wife, a vulnerable dependent, died unnaturally in the appellant's house, and he absconded for 37 days, did not report the matter and gave no plausible explanation, part of the onus shifted to him. Absence of explanation is considered in deciding whether a remote alternative theory should be disregarded. Ref: Muhammad Ijaz @ Jajj v. The State (Crl.A.345/2020), decided 07.05.2025; Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz @ Jajj v. The State (Crl.A.345/2020), decided 07.05.2025

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitration Award: Limited Court Interference under S. 30
records.heading: Court interference with an arbitration award is limited to the grounds in section 30
records.text: After an award is filed, parties may object within thirty days of service of notice under Art. 158 of the Limitation Act 1908 First Schedule. Courts do not act as appellate bodies over awards, and interference is limited to the grounds in s. 30 of the Arbitration Act 1940: jurisdictional error, proven misconduct or a patent legal mistake on the face of the record. Ref: Pakistan Railways through Chief Controller of Purchase Pakistan Railways, Lahore v. CRRC Ziyang Co.Limited, Lahore (C.P.L.A.813-L/2024), decided 29.04.2025; Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Pakistan Railways through Chief Controller of Purchase Pakistan Railways, Lahore v. CRRC Ziyang Co.Limited, Lahore (C.P.L.A.813-L/2024), decided 29.04.2025

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marking Weapon as P: Art. 71 QSO Inspection
records.heading: A weapon marked P must be shown to witnesses and produced for inspection under Art. 71 QSO
records.text: Marking a weapon as P on the recovery memo is not a formality. As real evidence it must be shown to witnesses for identification, and under the second proviso to Art. 71 QSO material things must be produced for the court's detailed inspection, with the court recording findings on description and calibre. Rule 14-F Ch. 24-B Vol. III LHC Rules and Orders is cited. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 802; Fakhar Iqbal Shah v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 592-23).
records.title: Fakhar Iqbal Shah v. State etc (Crl. Appeal 592-23)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested Witness and Abscondence
records.heading: An interested witness needs independent corroboration and abscondence alone cannot convict
records.text: Testimony of an interested witness must be scrutinised with care and needs independent corroboration. Abscondence is not by itself proof of guilt but can be corroborative, and a conviction cannot rest solely on abscondence without trustworthy substantive incriminating evidence. Ref: Fateh Khan v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.A.379/2021), decided 04.06.2025; Justice Naeem Akhter Afghan.
records.title: Fateh Khan v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.A.379/2021), decided 04.06.2025

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Injury Statement under Police Rules 25.39
records.heading: An injury statement describes injuries and does not record the injured person's account
records.text: An injury statement is prepared by a police official under rule 25.39 of the Police Rules 1934 to describe injuries and the suspected manner of causing them. It is not meant to record the injured person's account of the occurrence, which is recorded in the FIR under s. 154 CrPC, with its substance in the Daily Diary. Ref: 2025 LHC 3644; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Appeal 16787/22), decided 20.05.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Appeal 16787/22), decided 20.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Bloodstained Clothes Corroborate Eye Witnesses
records.heading: Bloodstained clothes of witnesses corroborate their presence at the scene
records.text: If bloodstained clothes of the complainant and cited eye witnesses are produced during investigation, they strongly corroborate the ocular account about the witnesses' presence at the time and place of occurrence. Ref: 2025 LHC 3644; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Appeal 16787/22), decided 20.05.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Appeal 16787/22), decided 20.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Extra Judicial Confession: Witness Not Reacting
records.heading: A witness who does not react to an extra judicial confession is doubtful and DNA cannot corroborate nothing
records.text: A witness who does not react on hearing an extra judicial confession raises doubt about his conduct and testimony, and a circumstantial case built on it fails. Where there is no substantial evidence, a DNA report is of no help as corroboratory evidence, since there is nothing to corroborate. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 841, PLJ 2025 Cr.C 375; Muhammad Waqas v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 17977/20).
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 17977/20)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Place of Death: Hospital versus Inquest Report
records.heading: An ocular account of death in hospital contradicted by the inquest report benefits the convict
records.text: Where the ocular account says the deceased died in hospital but column 24 of the inquest report shows the body lying in the complainant's area, the prosecution case falls like a house of cards and the benefit goes to the convict. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 893, PLJ 2025 Cr.C 365; The State v. Ali Akbar Zia (M.R.8-20).
records.title: The State v. Ali Akbar Zia (M.R.8-20)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Examination of Accused
records.heading: Every incriminating piece of evidence must be put to the accused under section 342 CrPC
records.text: S. 342 CrPC has two parts, permitting questions at any stage and requiring general questioning before the defence. Every incriminating piece of evidence must be put to the accused, one by one, to enable him to explain it. It is not an inane formality. Directing correct examination under s. 342 is not filling a lacuna in the prosecution case. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 922; Muhammad Shahid Mehmood v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-243-23).
records.title: Muhammad Shahid Mehmood v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-243-23)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Questions by Party Calling Witness
records.heading: Under Art. 150 QSO the calling party may put cross-examination questions to a witness
records.text: Under Art. 150 QSO the court may permit the party calling a witness to put questions that might be put in cross-examination, at any stage including examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination. This applies where a witness subtly contradicts in cross-examination what he stated earlier, provided the accused can cross-examine on the answers elicited. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 942; Bilal Muzaffar Heera etc. v. The State etc (Jail Appeal.62458/20).
records.title: Bilal Muzaffar Heera etc. v. The State etc (Jail Appeal.62458/20)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Tatima Shajra Irregularity: No Criminal Offence
records.heading: A Tatima shajra irregularity is open to departmental action and is not a criminal offence
records.text: Where a transaction rests on a registered deed, the Revenue Officer must ensure Kanungo and Patwari visit the spot and prepare Tatima shajra, and whether Tatima can be carved out of a joint khata is for Civil or Revenue Courts. The petitioner's act was at most an irregularity open to departmental action, and not a criminal offence for Anti-Corruption investigation. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 874; Arshad Abbas v. Anti-Corruption Establishment Sargodha (Writ Petition No.53631/Q/2024).
records.title: Arshad Abbas v. Anti-Corruption Establishment Sargodha (Writ Petition No.53631/Q/2024)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Mutation Not an Instrument: Art. 91 Limitation Act
records.heading: A mutation is not an instrument for Article 91 of the Limitation Act
records.text: A mutation is not an instrument for the purposes of attracting Article 91 of the Limitation Act 1908. Ref: 2025 LHC 3677; Muhammad Manzoor v. Muhammad Shafi etc (Civil Revision.3483-14), decided 03.06.2025; Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Muhammad Manzoor v. Muhammad Shafi etc (Civil Revision.3483-14), decided 03.06.2025

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Oral Rescission of Written Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A written agreement to sell cannot be rescinded orally without clear and cogent proof
records.text: A written agreement to sell cannot be rescinded orally unless rescission is proved by clear, cogent and credible evidence. Stating the time, place and witnesses of oral rescission does not offend O. VI R. 2 CPC. A buyer's deposit of money in his own account without proof of source does not prove refund of consideration. Ref: 2025 LHC 3768; Zafar Ali deceased through 11 LRs v. Ghulam Mustafa Chaudhary etc (Civil Revision 33211/23), decided 20.05.2025; Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Zafar Ali deceased through 11 LRs v. Ghulam Mustafa Chaudhary etc (Civil Revision 33211/23), decided 20.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording Statement of Oriented Injured
records.heading: Recording an oriented injured witness's statement after a month is fatal to the prosecution
records.text: Where the Medical Officer noted that the injured was well oriented and gave a history recorded on the medicolegal certificate, recording the injured witness's statement by the Investigating Officer after about one month is fatal for the prosecution. Ref: 2025 LHC 3719; Karamat Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 5394/22), decided 02.06.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Karamat Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 5394/22), decided 02.06.2025

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Art. 212 Constitution: Writ When Tribunal Non-Functional
records.heading: Writ entertained during a Tribunal's non-functionality is a stop-gap remedy
records.text: Under Art. 212(2) of the Constitution read with s. 8 of the Punjab Service Tribunals Act 1974, pending proceedings before any court abate once the Tribunal is established. Entertaining a writ petition during the Tribunal's non-functionality is a stop-gap remedy that ends when the Tribunal becomes functional. Ref: 2025 LHC 3760; Muhammad Sarfraz v. Secretary Specialized Health Care & Medical Education Department Lahore etc (WP 43029/24), decided 29.05.2025; Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Sarfraz v. Secretary Specialized Health Care & Medical Education Department Lahore etc (WP 43029/24), decided 29.05.2025

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Separation of Powers: Executive and Binding Judgments
records.heading: The Executive cannot sit over a binding judgment under separation of powers
records.text: Authority on separation of powers and the judicial prerogative of interpreting law. The principle of separation of powers is a central guarantee of just government, and the Executive cannot sit over a binding judgment. Ref: 2025 LHC 3791; Ayesha Iftikhar etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 220388/18), decided 22.05.2025; Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: Ayesha Iftikhar etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 220388/18), decided 22.05.2025

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody: Register No. XIX and Road Certificate
records.heading: Missing Register XIX entries and road certificate make safe custody dubious
records.text: Neither the investigating officer nor the Moharrer stated that entries were made in Register No. XIX or Roznamcha about handing over the case property and sample parcels, nor was any road certificate produced. These gaps in safe custody and transmission made the prosecution case dubious. Ref: 2025 LHC 3670; Sakina Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal-177-24), decided 07.05.2025; Justice Raja Ghazanfar Ali Khan.
records.title: Sakina Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal-177-24), decided 07.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Substitution of Real Culprits Is Rare
records.heading: Substitution of real culprits is rare where eyewitnesses lost kin before their eyes
records.text: It is well settled that substitution of the real culprits is a rare phenomenon, especially where the eye-witnesses lost their kith and kin before their own eyes. The post cites this case together with Muhammad Ijaz v. The State (2023 SCMR 1375). Ref: 2023 SCMR 831; Aqil v. The State.
records.title: Aqil v. The State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Urdu Translation of Evidence Recorded in English
records.heading: Urdu translation of English evidence should be prepared at once before the witness and accused
records.text: The Lahore High Court directed Punjab judges that when evidence is recorded in English, an Urdu translation should be prepared at the same time in the presence of the witness, judge and accused, so any ambiguity can be removed immediately in light of the translation. Ref: 2025 LHC 3801; The State v. Muhammad Irfan Pomi (Murder Reference.221-21), decided 29.04.2025; Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Irfan Pomi (Murder Reference.221-21), decided 29.04.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Reading One Sentence of Evidence in Isolation
records.heading: A court cannot read one sentence of evidence in isolation in the accused's favour
records.text: The court cannot pick one sentence from the evidence and read it in isolation in the appellant's favour. The word us in the complainant's cross-examination was a typographical error by the Presiding Officer, and the complainant had stated in chief that the appellant fired the shots that hit the deceased. Ref: 2025 LHC 3801; The State v. Muhammad Irfan Pomi (Murder Reference.221-21), decided 29.04.2025; Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Irfan Pomi (Murder Reference.221-21), decided 29.04.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Capital Punishment on Circumstantial Evidence
records.heading: Conviction, even capital, may rest solely on a complete and unbroken circumstantial chain
records.text: Conviction, including for capital punishment, may rest exclusively on circumstantial evidence, subject to rigorous standards. The evidence must be inconsistent with innocence and form a complete and unbroken chain linking the accused to the offence. The Supreme Court upheld the death sentence in the Noor Mukadam murder case. Ref: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State through A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A.467/2023), decided 20.05.2025; Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State through A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A.467/2023), decided 20.05.2025

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage as Primary Evidence
records.heading: CCTV footage passing the two-fold test is primary evidence needing no corroboration
records.text: CCTV footage that passes the two-fold test laid down in Ahmad Omar Sheikh is primary evidence and requires no corroboration. Ref: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State through A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A.467/2023), decided 20.05.2025; Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State through A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A.467/2023), decided 20.05.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Relationship of Eye Witnesses with Deceased
records.heading: Relationship of eyewitnesses with the deceased is no ground to disbelieve trustworthy evidence
records.text: Mere relationship of eye witnesses with the deceased is no ground to disbelieve their evidence where it is trustworthy and confidence inspiring and they have no animosity with the accused, relying on the cited Supreme Court judgments. Ref: 2023 SCMR 487, 2023 SCMR 527, 2023 SCMR 596, 2023 SCMR 723 and others.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. I R. 10 CPC: Impleadment at Appellate Stage
records.heading: A party impleaded at the appellate stage requires remand to the trial court
records.text: When a party is impleaded at the appellate stage under Order I Rule 10 CPC, natural justice requires remand to the trial court so the new party can file pleadings, lead evidence and fully contest the matter. Ref: 2025 LHC 3823; Naeem Abbas etc v. Altaf Hussain etc (RFA 47-25), decided 14.05.2025; Justice Syed Ahsan Raza Kazmi.
records.title: Naeem Abbas etc v. Altaf Hussain etc (RFA 47-25), decided 14.05.2025

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikah Nama: Proof and Marginal Witnesses
records.heading: Where marriage is admitted non-production of Nikah marginal witnesses is not fatal
records.text: Where the marriage is admitted and execution of Nikah is not denied, non-production of the marginal witnesses is not fatal to the wife's suit and her entitlement to dower is established. A Nikah Nama is a public document under s. 5 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 with a presumption of truth under Art. 85 QSO, and mere verbal denial has no legal value. Ref: Mst. Khalida Bibi v. Naeem Khan and others (C.P.L.A.252-P/2025), decided 04.06.2025; Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Mst. Khalida Bibi v. Naeem Khan and others (C.P.L.A.252-P/2025), decided 04.06.2025

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Production of Documents at Any Stage
records.heading: Section 94 CrPC allows production of documents at any stage of inquiry or trial
records.text: S. 94 CrPC imposes no limit on the stage of inquiry or trial at which the court may order production of a document, the only condition being that production is necessary or desirable. The word whenever indicates any stage. The court acts as neutral arbiter, and it is immaterial whether the document supports the prosecution or the accused. Ref: 2025 LHC 3828; Muhammad Shafiq v. The State, etc. (Crl. Revision No.45 of 2025, date of hearing 23.04.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Shafiq v. The State, etc. (Crl. Revision No.45 of 2025, date of hearing 23.04.2025)

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.topic: Passport Control List: Mere Registration of Case
records.heading: Mere registration of a criminal case does not justify placing a citizen on the Passport Control List
records.text: Mere registration of or involvement in a criminal case does not justify placing a citizen on the Passport Control List under Rule 22(2)(b) of the Passport Rules 2021 or restricting international travel, especially where the accused has been admitted to bail by a competent court.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR Recorded After Earlier Narration to Police
records.heading: A later FIR after an earlier narration to police cannot carry the weight of a prompt FIR
records.text: If the complainant narrates the whole occurrence to a police official immediately after it, but it is not recorded then and the FIR is recorded later on a written application or statement at another place, it is not an FIR under s. 154 CrPC in the strict sense and cannot carry the weight of a prompt FIR. Ref: 2025 LHC 3872; Ali Raza v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 33146/22), decided 04.06.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Ali Raza v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 33146/22), decided 04.06.2025

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Place of Occurrence: Human Blood Report Absent
records.heading: The place of occurrence is not proved without a report of human blood on the earth
records.text: If there is no report confirming that earth secured from the place of occurrence was stained with human blood, the place of occurrence is not proved in the strict sense. Ref: 2025 LHC 3872; Ali Raza v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 33146/22), decided 04.06.2025; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Ali Raza v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 33146/22), decided 04.06.2025

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Husband Denying Paternity in Maintenance Suit: Qazf
records.heading: A husband denying a child's paternity in his written statement faces qazf proceedings
records.text: According to the Urdu heading, if a husband, in his written statement to a suit for dowry and maintenance, denies that the minor is his daughter, qazf proceedings will follow against him. Ref: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No.01-L of 2025), announced 15.05.2025.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No.01-L of 2025), announced 15.05.2025

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Written Divorce: Effective from Date of Execution
records.heading: A written divorce takes effect from the date of its execution
records.text: When a divorce is pronounced in clear, unambiguous terms and documented in writing, it takes effect from the date of its execution. A written divorce deed bearing a specific date and validated on oath establishes that date as the effective date of divorce. Ref: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No.01-L of 2025), announced 15.05.2025.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No.01-L of 2025), announced 15.05.2025

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Right of Appeal Is Substantive: Act Not Rules
records.heading: The right of appeal is substantive and should be provided in the Act and not the Rules
records.text: The right of appeal is a substantive right and not a mere matter of procedure, and should be provided in the Act and not in the Rules. An appeal is a continuation of the original proceedings. Ref: Muhammad Dawood v. Mst. Sakeena Farooque @ Aziza & others (C.P.L.A.479-K/2023), decided 26.03.2025; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Dawood v. Mst. Sakeena Farooque @ Aziza & others (C.P.L.A.479-K/2023), decided 26.03.2025

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift: Strict Proof Despite Non-Registration
records.heading: A donee must strictly prove an oral gift even where registration is optional
records.text: Even where registration of a gift is relaxed or optional, the donee is not absolved from strictly proving the factum of the gift or the declaration of an oral gift under challenge. Ref: Muhammad Dawood v. Mst. Sakeena Farooque @ Aziza & others (C.P.L.A.479-K/2023), decided 26.03.2025; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Muhammad Dawood v. Mst. Sakeena Farooque @ Aziza & others (C.P.L.A.479-K/2023), decided 26.03.2025

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Trial Court Cancelling Bail Granted by Supreme Court
records.heading: Trial courts may cancel bail granted by constitutional courts for breach of conditions
records.text: The Supreme Court of India held that trial courts have authority to cancel bail granted by constitutional courts, including the Supreme Court itself, where bail conditions are violated. The CBI alleged witness tampering by the accused, who had been granted bail with conditions. Ref: The State of Karnataka through the CBI v. Vinay Rajashekharappa Kulkarni (SLP(Crl) No. 7865/2025).
records.title: The State of Karnataka through the CBI v. Vinay Rajashekharappa Kulkarni (SLP(Crl) No. 7865/2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Non-Muslim Heirs Cannot Inherit from Muslim
records.heading: A non-Muslim cannot inherit from the estate of a Muslim relative
records.text: A non-Muslim (Qadiani person) is not entitled to inherit from the estate of a Muslim relative as successor or predecessor, and Art. 260(3) of the Constitution applies retrospectively. The judgment refers to s. 2 of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1937. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 491; Tariq Mehmood etc v. Fateh Muhammad etc (Civil Revision.3843-14).
records.title: Tariq Mehmood etc v. Fateh Muhammad etc (Civil Revision.3843-14)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Child Sexual Abuse: Child Witness, Hearsay, Res Gestae
records.heading: Absence of corroboration does not automatically discredit a child victim's testimony
records.text: In evaluating a child victim's testimony in sexual abuse cases, absence of corroboration does not automatically discredit it, and tender age with other circumstances may make corroboration unnecessary. Abuse may be penetrative or non-penetrative. The tender years exception allows hearsay only to corroborate the child's in-court testimony. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 512; Imdad Ullah v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal-Against Conviction-Anti-Rape Act 448-22).
records.title: Imdad Ullah v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal-Against Conviction-Anti-Rape Act 448-22)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings at any stage must be allowed with caution and in furtherance of justice
records.text: Although O. VI R. 17 CPC permits amendment at any stage of the proceeding, the discretion must be exercised with caution and only in furtherance of justice. Ref: Muhammad Arif Tarar v. Matloob Ahmad Warraich and others (C.P.L.A.746-L/2025), decided 12.06.2025; Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Arif Tarar v. Matloob Ahmad Warraich and others (C.P.L.A.746-L/2025), decided 12.06.2025

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22 Anti-Rape Act: No FIR Registration
records.heading: Proceedings under section 22 of the Anti-Rape Act cannot begin with an FIR
records.text: Proceedings under s. 22 of the Anti-Rape Act cannot be initiated by registering an FIR. Schedule II CrPC classes offences under other laws by punishment, and offences punishable with exactly three years are treated as non-cognizable. The Act does not declare the s. 22 offence cognizable, so no FIR can be registered. Ref: 2025 LHC 4030; Syed Rizwan Haider v. A.S.J etc (WP-1142-25), decided 27.05.2025; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Syed Rizwan Haider v. A.S.J etc (WP-1142-25), decided 27.05.2025

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Transfer of Judges to Islamabad High Court: Art. 200
records.heading: A transfer of High Court judges under Art. 200(1) is distinct from a fresh appointment
records.text: By a 3 to 2 majority, the Constitutional Bench held that the President's power to transfer High Court judges under Art. 200(1) is distinct from the Judicial Commission's powers, and a transfer is not a fresh appointment. Justice Sardar Sarfraz Dogar continues as acting Chief Justice of the Islamabad High Court, and whether the transfer is permanent or temporary and the seniority of transferred judges are remitted to the President. Ref: Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, Judge, Islamabad High Court, Islamabad and others v. The President of Pakistan, Pak Secretariat, Islamabad and others (C.P.22/2025, decided 19.06.2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Shahid Bilal; Justice Salahuddin Panhwar; Justice Naeem Afghan; Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, Judge, Islamabad High Court, Islamabad and others v. The President of Pakistan, Pak Secretariat, Islamabad and others (C.P.22/2025, decided 19.06.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Reduced: Mitigating Circumstances of Enmity
records.heading: Mutual enmity and personal vendetta may justify life imprisonment in place of death
records.text: Where the offence arose from mutual enmity and personal vendetta, such mitigating circumstances may justify life imprisonment in place of the death penalty, relying on 2014 SCMR 1034 that a single mitigating circumstance may suffice. The Court considered a reduced lawful penalty adequate to meet the ends of justice. Ref: Muhammad Ikram & 2 others v. The State (J.P.23/2023, decided 05.06.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Muhammad Ikram & 2 others v. The State (J.P.23/2023, decided 05.06.2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Sale by Village Lady: Validity of Transaction
records.heading: A vendor being a village woman is not by itself a ground to impeach a sale
