records.text: Where both marginal witnesses appeared and corroborated the purchaser and no fraud or connivance of revenue officials was substantiated, the fact that the vendor is a village woman cannot by itself be a ground to impeach the sale. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 552; Muhammad Rafique v. Mst. Suriya Bibi (Civil Revision-24-25).
records.title: Muhammad Rafique v. Mst. Suriya Bibi (Civil Revision-24-25)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 21(c) Specific Relief Act: Uncertain Contract Terms
records.heading: A contract with uncertain terms cannot be specifically enforced under section 21(c)
records.text: Under s. 21(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, a contract whose terms the Court cannot ascertain with reasonable certainty cannot be specifically enforced. A claimant must plead a valid and enforceable contract and its terms clearly, and an agreement not describing the property by metes and bounds was refused enforcement in the case relied on. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 565, PLD 2025 Lah 572; Muhammad Asif v. Ch. Muhammad Hanif (R.S.A. No. 69 of 2014).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Ch. Muhammad Hanif (R.S.A. No. 69 of 2014)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Nature and Procedure
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC lets the court nullify its own judgment obtained by fraud
records.text: Section 12(2) CPC, inserted by Ordinance X of 1980, lets the court that passed a judgment, decree or order nullify it if obtained by fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction. No procedure is prescribed, so by s. 141 CPC the court may decide the application summarily or after framing issues. Concurrent findings tainted by patent illegality can be set aside in constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 597; Mumtaz Ahmed v. Amjad Niaz Abbasi etc (WP.3639-19).
records.title: Mumtaz Ahmed v. Amjad Niaz Abbasi etc (WP.3639-19)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 215 Contract Act: Agent Dealing on Own Account
records.heading: An attorney dealing on own account without prior consent may be repudiated by the principal
records.text: An attorney transferring the principal's property to himself or close relatives must obtain the principal's prior consent. Under s. 215 of the Contract Act, 1872 the principal may repudiate such dealing if the agent acted on his own account without prior consent, without disclosing material circumstances, or with dishonest concealment or disadvantage to the principal. Consent need not be in writing and may be oral. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 613, 2025 MLD 1268; Mohsin Lal Chaudashry v. Shoukat Ali etc (Civil Revision-423-24).
records.title: Mohsin Lal Chaudashry v. Shoukat Ali etc (Civil Revision-423-24)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Child Custody: Father Abroad, Mother Remarried
records.heading: A father abroad cannot claim custody merely as natural guardian where the mother remarried
records.text: A father who has never met his minor daughter and lives abroad cannot claim custody merely as natural guardian where the mother has remarried. On remarriage of either parent the Court weighs the circumstances of both, and the welfare of the minor (Art. 3(1) UNCRC) is paramount. The mother's second marriage does not by itself disqualify her. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 307; Asjad Ullah v. Mst. Aisa Bano and others (C.P.L.A.3920/2024).
records.title: Asjad Ullah v. Mst. Aisa Bano and others (C.P.L.A.3920/2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Domicile Certificate versus CNIC Address for Appointment
records.heading: The domicile certificate and not the CNIC address determines permanent residence for appointment
records.text: For employment purposes the domicile certificate, and not the CNIC address, determines a candidate's permanent residence. Relying on the doctrine of legitimate expectation, candidates who passed the competitive examination and held valid domicile certificates could not be denied appointment on technical grounds. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 364, PLD 2025 SC 720; District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.R.P.5/2023).
records.title: District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.R.P.5/2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Review Before Supreme Court: Scope and Costs
records.heading: Review before the Supreme Court is limited and frivolous reviews attract costs
records.text: The judgment also addresses the scope of review before the Supreme Court, deprecates the practice of filing a review in every matter, and directs costs in frivolous and vexatious matters that waste the Court's time. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 364, PLD 2025 SC 720; District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.R.P.5/2023).
records.title: District Education Officer (Female), Charsadda and others v. Miss Sonia Begam (C.R.P.5/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 324 PPC: Firearm Injury on Thigh
records.heading: A firearm injury at the thigh prima facie attracts section 324 PPC
records.text: A firearm injury below the knee makes s. 324 PPC a matter for further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. An injury above the knee at the thigh, where the femoral artery lies, prima facie attracts s. 324 PPC because damage may cause amputation or death by blood loss. Bail refused. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 418, 2025 PCrLJ 1839; Nasrullah alias Nasru v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.1584/25).
records.title: Nasrullah alias Nasru v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.1584/25)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Given-Up Eyewitness as Court Witness
records.heading: A given-up uninjured eyewitness cannot be summoned as a court witness under section 540 CrPC
records.text: Where the prosecution gives up a third eyewitness whose evidence is of the same nature as two examined, and who is not injured, he cannot be summoned as a Court Witness under s. 540 CrPC, though the accused may produce him as a defence witness. The accused cannot compel the prosecution to produce a witness. An injured eyewitness stands on a higher footing. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 422; Ghulam Murtaza v. A.S.J Faisalabad etc (Crl. Revision 74970/2).
records.title: Ghulam Murtaza v. A.S.J Faisalabad etc (Crl. Revision 74970/2)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eyewitnesses
records.heading: Related eyewitnesses who stood by silently acted unnaturally and their presence is doubtful
records.text: Closely related eyewitnesses who stood as silent spectators while one unarmed-with-firearm accused inflicted eight injuries, from 21 and 26 feet away, and neither saved the deceased nor apprehended the accused, acted unnaturally. This shows they were not present at the spot, so their evidence is not worthy of reliance. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 108; Muhammad Ashraf v. State (Crl. A. No. 188 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. State (Crl. A. No. 188 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Cutting Both Ways: Land Dispute
records.heading: A motive based on a land dispute cuts both ways
records.text: A motive based on a land dispute cuts both ways. The same background that could drive the accused to attack could equally push the complainant party to implicate innocent members of the accused party widely. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 105; Ghulam Mustafa v. State (Crl. A. No. 23 of 2020).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. State (Crl. A. No. 23 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Evidence Not Put to Accused
records.heading: A circumstance not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot support conviction
records.text: Evidence or a circumstance not put to the accused when his statement is recorded under s. 342 CrPC cannot be considered against him for the purpose of conviction. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 105; Ghulam Mustafa v. State (Crl. A. No. 23 of 2020).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. State (Crl. A. No. 23 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Torture and Custodial Death Act 2022: FIR and FIA
records.heading: An FIR by local police for a Torture and Custodial Death Act offence must be transferred to the FIA
records.text: An FIR registered by local police under general penal laws for an offence within the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act, 2022 must be cancelled and the matter transferred to the FIA, if cognisance has not yet been taken. Once a competent court has taken cognisance, the earlier irregularity of an FIR by an unauthorised agency does not vitiate the trial. Ref: 2025 LHC 5084; Aftab Mehmood v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.81211/24, decided 28.04.2025); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Aftab Mehmood v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.81211/24, decided 28.04.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Successive Suit on Same Cause of Action Barred
records.heading: A successive suit on the same cause of action is barred
records.text: A plaintiff who omits to claim relief arising from the same cause of action in an earlier suit is barred from a later suit for it. A third suit on the same facts and agreement, after two earlier suits were dismissed, is barred, and non-disclosure of the earlier litigation is material suppression undermining bona fides. Ref: 2025 LHC 4309; Dr. Tehsin Mazhar Sheikh v. Additional District Judge etc (Writ Petition No. 77145/2019).
records.title: Dr. Tehsin Mazhar Sheikh v. Additional District Judge etc (Writ Petition No. 77145/2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 79 and 113 QSO: Admitted Agreement to Sell
records.heading: Where execution is admitted Art. 113 QSO makes production of both attesting witnesses unnecessary
records.text: Although Art. 79 QSO requires two attesting witnesses for a document required by law to be attested, where the executant admits execution before a competent court together with delivery of possession, the facts stand admitted under Art. 113 and production of both attesting witnesses loses significance. Ref: 2025 LHC 4314; Muhammad Rafique, etc. v. Mst. Jamshed Bibi, etc. (RSA No.50 of 2014).
records.title: Muhammad Rafique, etc. v. Mst. Jamshed Bibi, etc. (RSA No.50 of 2014)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in FIR and Doubtful Presence of Complainant
records.heading: Unexplained delay in the FIR and dishonest improvements make the prosecution case unreliable
records.text: Unexplained delay in recording the FIR is fatal to the prosecution case, a complainant whose presence at the scene is not established gives suspect evidence, and witnesses making dishonest improvements cannot be relied on. A bloodstained brick recovered over two months later from a vacant place was of no avail, as human blood disintegrates within about three weeks. Ref: 2025 LHC 4352; Ali Hassan and three others v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No.78438 of 2022).
records.title: Ali Hassan and three others v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No.78438 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 462-O PPC: Complaint Required Before Sessions Trial
records.heading: A section 462-O PPC complaint is required before Sessions trial of a section 462-I offence
records.text: An offence under s. 462-I PPC is triable by the Court of Session, so the Magistrate sends the s. 173 CrPC report to it under s. 190(2) CrPC. If the report lacks the complaint required by s. 462-O PPC, the prosecution must obtain it from an officer not below Grade 17. Section 462-O is read with s. 230 CrPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 4418; The State through Deputy Prosecutor General Punjab, Multan (Writ Petition No. 14839 of 2024, decided 04.06.2025).
records.title: The State through Deputy Prosecutor General Punjab, Multan (Writ Petition No. 14839 of 2024, decided 04.06.2025)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 12 Limitation Act: Time for Obtaining Copy
records.heading: Time for obtaining a copy is excluded from limitation but not counted from delivery of the order
records.text: Under s. 12(2) and (5) of the Limitation Act, 1908 the time requisite for obtaining a copy runs from the application for the copy to the day intimated as ready for delivery. It is excluded in computing limitation, but the provision does not say that limitation is counted from the date of delivery of the order. Ref: 2025 LHC 4495; Muhammad Imran v. Shahbaz Ali Khan and others (Writ Petition No.2913 of 2024, decided 26.06.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Shahbaz Ali Khan and others (Writ Petition No.2913 of 2024, decided 26.06.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Framing of Charge: Lesser and Graver Offences
records.heading: An accused charged with a lesser offence cannot be convicted of a graver one without amendment
records.text: Charge is framed on the prima facie allegations in the FIR, s. 161 statements and s. 173 report. An accused charged with a lesser offence cannot be convicted of a graver one unless the charge is amended and evidence is given again, whereas conviction for a lesser offence of the same family is possible. Ss. 382 and 395 PPC are of the same family. Ref: 2025 LHC 4520; Muhammad Sajid and 04 others v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 3762-M of 2025, decided 06.05.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Sajid and 04 others v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 3762-M of 2025, decided 06.05.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Missing Roznamcha Entry and Safe Custody
records.heading: A missing Register II entry dents the evidence of safe custody
records.text: Under r. 22.48 of the Police Rules, 1934 the arrival and departure of police officials and station events must be entered in Register No. II. Where law requires a thing to be done in a particular manner and the procedure is not followed, it is presumed not to have been done lawfully, which dents the evidence of safe custody. Ref: 2025 LHC 4524; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 979-J of 2023, hearing 24.06.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 979-J of 2023, hearing 24.06.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody: Delay in Sending Charas Samples
records.heading: Unexplained delay in sending charas samples to the laboratory breaks the chain of custody
records.text: Unexplained delay in handing over sealed sample parcels of Charas to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency casts doubt on safe custody and makes the report doubtful. The report must be duly proved, which includes proving safe custody and transmission. A break in the chain vitiates the report and the prosecution failed to prove guilt. Ref: 2025 LHC 4537; Muhammad Tanveer Tannu v. State (Criminal Appeal No. 571 of 2024, hearing 26.06.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Tanveer Tannu v. State (Criminal Appeal No. 571 of 2024, hearing 26.06.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 94, 265-F(7), 540 CrPC: Summoning Court Witness
records.heading: A Control Room Wireless Operator Moharrar may be summoned as a court witness with the record
records.text: The Control Room Wireless Operator Moharrar may be summoned as a Court witness with the record. Under s. 265-F(7) CrPC the court shall issue process for the accused's witnesses after he enters his defence unless the application is to delay or defeat justice, and refusal is an incurable irregularity. Section 540 CrPC empowers summoning any person essential for a just decision. Ref: 2025 LHC 4548; Majid Javed alias Javed Ali v. State (Criminal Revision No.242 of 2025, decided 25.06.2025).
records.title: Majid Javed alias Javed Ali v. State (Criminal Revision No.242 of 2025, decided 25.06.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Safe Custody of Narcotics
records.heading: The prosecution must prove the recovered material is a narcotic through an unbroken chain of custody
records.text: In a conviction under the Act of 1997, the prosecution must prove beyond reasonable doubt that the recovered material is a narcotic drug. The analyst's report depends on proving recovery and the unbroken chain of custody from recovery through storage at the police station to delivery of samples to the chemical examiner. Ref: Ameenullah and Khairullah v. The State & another (Crl.a.525 of 2022, decided 18.04.2025).
records.title: Ameenullah and Khairullah v. The State & another (Crl.a.525 of 2022, decided 18.04.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Discrepancy in Number of Firearm Injuries
records.heading: Discrepancies in the number of firearm injuries cannot be stressed strictly
records.text: In firearm injuries a witness cannot be expected to give a photographic account, since the bullet strikes before its sound is heard. In the confusion of the occurrence, discrepancies in the number and location of injuries cannot be stressed strictly. Ref: 2025 LHC 4602; Muhammad Arif v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.39441-J/2022; Murder Reference No.163/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.39441-J/2022; Murder Reference No.163/2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade and CCTV Evidence: Arts. 22, 164 QSO
records.heading: An identification parade is not required where CCTV footage establishes identity
records.text: An identification parade is not required in every case, as any fact establishing identity is relevant under Art. 22 QSO. CCTV footage showing the accused is admissible under Art. 22 and is evidence from a modern device under Art. 164, subject to genuineness and authenticity, so no parade was needed. Ref: Shahbaz Mustafa and another v. State (Crl. Misc. No.15084-B/2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Mustafa and another v. State (Crl. Misc. No.15084-B/2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ingredients of Criminal Breach of Trust: S. 406 PPC
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust requires fiduciary entrustment followed by dishonest misappropriation or disposal
records.text: The offence under s. 406 PPC requires entrustment of property to the accused in a fiduciary capacity, followed by dishonest misappropriation, conversion, or use or disposal in violation of law or a legal contract. Entrustment carries its legal meaning, and the property must be held for another until a contingency arises or disposed of on stated terms. Ref: 2025 LHC 4774; Majid Ali v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 12913-B of 2025).
records.title: Majid Ali v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 12913-B of 2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Reduced: Heat of Passion
records.heading: A crime in the heat of passion without premeditation reduces death to life imprisonment
records.text: The occurrence was not premeditated and took place in the heat of passion after a dispute over sale of the house, a mitigating factor under s. 302(b) PPC. The death sentence was converted to imprisonment for life, the other sentences and compensation were maintained, and the Murder Reference was answered in the negative. Ref: 2025 LHC 4602; Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. A. 39441-J/2022, with Murder Reference 163/2022, decided 30.06.2025); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. A. 39441-J/2022, with Murder Reference 163/2022, decided 30.06.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Competent Forum
records.heading: The court which passed the final order is the competent forum under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: The competent forum to challenge the validity of a judgment, decree or order under s. 12(2) CPC is the court which passed the final order. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 575; Ghulam Fareed v. Muhammad Bilal etc (Civil Revision-574-24).
records.title: Ghulam Fareed v. Muhammad Bilal etc (Civil Revision-574-24)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NAB Writ Petitions: Fixation Before Single Judge
records.heading: Writ petitions against NAB must be fixed before a Single Judge
records.text: Writ petitions against NAB seeking mandamus, certiorari or prohibition must be fixed before a Single Judge under the Rules and precedent, since matters in constitutional jurisdiction are heard by a Single Judge unless law, the Rules or a special order of the Chief Justice provides otherwise. The Additional Registrar (Judicial) was directed to list such cases accordingly. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 563; Aamir Nawaz Minhas and others v. National Accountability Bureau and others (WP No.1027 of 2025).
records.title: Aamir Nawaz Minhas and others v. National Accountability Bureau and others (WP No.1027 of 2025)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation, Waiver and Acquiescence in Inheritance Claims
records.heading: A bare inheritance claim does not escape limitation where a predecessor did not challenge a transaction
records.text: Limitation, waiver and acquiescence cannot be ignored in every inheritance claim. If a predecessor did not challenge in her lifetime a transaction depriving her of a share, and third-party rights were created, a bare inheritance claim does not escape limitation. Limitation has been disregarded only in exceptional cases, such as fraud against female heirs in their lifetime. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 581; Muhammad Hafeez v. Muhammad Ramzan etc (WP 10459/19).
records.title: Muhammad Hafeez v. Muhammad Ramzan etc (WP 10459/19)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Declined: Pending Petition Is No Stay
records.heading: A pending petition before the Supreme Court is no stay of arrest after pre-arrest bail is declined
records.text: Once a competent court declines pre-arrest bail, the accused is exposed to lawful arrest. Police must not treat the mere filing of a petition before the Supreme Court as an implied stay or bar to arrest, since no stay exists unless granted, and pendency of higher-forum proceedings is no excuse for inaction. Ref: Zahid Khan, etc. v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another (Criminal Petition No. 645-L of 2025, decided 25.06.2025).
records.title: Zahid Khan, etc. v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another (Criminal Petition No. 645-L of 2025, decided 25.06.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in FIR, Motive, Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Delay in the FIR and possible false implication on a blood feud give benefit of doubt
records.text: Motive is a double-edged weapon usable for real or false involvement. Where the eyewitnesses were close relatives and procured, time spent in consultation delayed the FIR, and false implication on a blood-feud motive could not be ruled out, the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt suffices, as of right. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1024; Manzar Abas and Ali Afzal v. State (Criminal Appeals No. 438 and 439 of 2023).
records.title: Manzar Abas and Ali Afzal v. State (Criminal Appeals No. 438 and 439 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Pre-Conditions
records.heading: Evidence cannot be closed under O. XVII R. 3 CPC unless its pre-conditions coexist
records.text: Evidence cannot be closed under O. XVII R. 3 CPC for non-production where the previous adjournment was not at the party's request. Six conditions must coexist: adjournment at the party's request for the rule's purposes, default in the act, presence or deemed presence, material on record for a merits decision, and decision of the suit forthwith. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1032; Muhammad Akram v. Shafaqat Ali (C.P.L.A.No.1033-L of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. Shafaqat Ali (C.P.L.A.No.1033-L of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Closing of Evidence After Final Opportunities
records.heading: A litigant who ignored final opportunities cannot complain when evidence is closed
records.text: Where the plaintiff was given absolutely last and final opportunities with clear warnings to produce evidence and ignored them, an indolent litigant cannot seek favour of law. The decision closing his right to produce evidence was upheld. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1032; Muhammad Akram v. Shafaqat Ali (C.P.L.A.No.1033-L of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. Shafaqat Ali (C.P.L.A.No.1033-L of 2024)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Object of Laws and Procedural Rules for Litigants
records.heading: Litigants must follow procedural rules and cannot burden courts or delay rival parties
records.text: Laws and rules streamline institutions and courts. Litigants who proceed without following procedural rules increase the burden on courts and erode public trust, and they cannot take courts for granted or cause agony to rival parties through delay. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1032; Muhammad Akram v. Shafaqat Ali (C.P.L.A.No.1033-L of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. Shafaqat Ali (C.P.L.A.No.1033-L of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 516-A CrPC: Interim Custody of Vehicle on Superdari
records.heading: Interim custody of a vehicle on superdari does not prejudice the trial
records.text: Interim custody of a vehicle on superdari neither prejudices the trial nor gives the accused a clean chit, nor exempts the recipient from pending proceedings. Custody may continue on bond and surety until the final decision, and the recipient must attend, participate and produce the vehicle when directed. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1041; Ahsan Ali Dawach v. The State (Civil Petition No. 256-K of 2024).
records.title: Ahsan Ali Dawach v. The State (Civil Petition No. 256-K of 2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 5 Dowry and Bridal Gifts Act 1976: Absolute Vesting
records.heading: Dowry and bridal gifts vest absolutely in the bride but not items given to the groom's family
records.text: Under s. 5 of the Dowry and Bridal Gifts (Restriction) Act, 1976 property given to the bride as dowry, bridal gifts or presents vests absolutely in her, unaffected by separation or divorce. Recoverable property is confined to what was intended for the bride, so items given to the groom's family as presents could not be decreed in her favour. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 461, PLJ 2025 SC 467; Muhammad Sajid v. Mst. Shamsa Asghar (C.P.L.A. No. 3284-L of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Sajid v. Mst. Shamsa Asghar (C.P.L.A. No. 3284-L of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay of Four Hours in FIR
records.heading: An unexplained delay of four hours in the FIR creates doubt for the accused
records.text: An occurrence at about 3 or 4 AM reported at 7 AM without any plausible explanation for the delay creates doubt in the prosecution case, the benefit of which goes to the accused. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1087; Waqas Ahmad v. State (Jail Petition No.539 of 2017).
records.title: Waqas Ahmad v. State (Jail Petition No.539 of 2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Postmortem and Medical Signs Belie Time of Occurrence
records.heading: Delayed postmortem and medical signs belie the stated time of occurrence
records.text: A postmortem held 3 hours 30 minutes after the report without explanation, with rigor mortis and semi-digested food in the stomach, belied the stated time of occurrence. Semi-open eyes and mouth suggested the body lay unattended, making the complainant's presence at the spot doubtful. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1087; Waqas Ahmad v. State (Jail Petition No.539 of 2017).
records.title: Waqas Ahmad v. State (Jail Petition No.539 of 2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light Not Proved
records.heading: Identification in the dark is highly doubtful where no light source was established
records.text: Where the occurrence took place in the dark hours and the Investigating Officer neither took a bulb into possession nor was any electricity source established, identification of the assailants is highly doubtful. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1087; Waqas Ahmad v. State (Jail Petition No.539 of 2017).
records.title: Waqas Ahmad v. State (Jail Petition No.539 of 2017)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561-A CrPC: Quashing Proceedings versus FIR
records.heading: Section 561-A CrPC allows quashing of proceedings but not of an FIR or investigation
records.text: The High Court may quash criminal proceedings under s. 561-A CrPC but cannot quash police acts such as registration of an FIR or investigation under that section. The power should not be used routinely, and ordinarily the remedy under s. 249-A or 265-K CrPC should be exhausted first, save in exceptional circumstances. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1117; Ayesha Tayyab v. Station House Officer (C.P.L.A.1575/2024).
records.title: Ayesha Tayyab v. Station House Officer (C.P.L.A.1575/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Absence of Source of Light
records.heading: Identification at night is questionable where the FIR mentions no source of light
records.text: In a night-time murder case, where no source of light is mentioned in the FIR and none is recovered, identification of the accused becomes questionable. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1110; Imtiaz Hussain Shah v. State (Crl. A 201-L and 202-L of 2020).
records.title: Imtiaz Hussain Shah v. State (Crl. A 201-L and 202-L of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Presence of Eyewitnesses and Abandoned Material Witness
records.heading: Delay, unnatural conduct and conflicting wounds doubt eyewitnesses and an abandoned witness invites adverse presumption
records.text: Inordinate delay in postmortem, unnatural conduct as silent spectators, and a conflict between four entrance wounds in the ocular account and three in the medical evidence made the eyewitnesses' presence doubtful. The prosecution abandoned an impartial material witness without reason, inviting the presumption under Art. 129(g) QSO. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1110; Imtiaz Hussain Shah v. State (Crl. A 201-L and 202-L of 2020).
records.title: Imtiaz Hussain Shah v. State (Crl. A 201-L and 202-L of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: A conflict between ocular and medical evidence shows eyewitnesses were not present
records.text: Eyewitnesses spoke of two injuries by the petitioner but the medical evidence showed four incised wounds, two unexplained by them. This conflict showed that the eyewitnesses were not present at the spot. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1053; Muhammad Nawaz v. State (J.P. No 555 of 2017).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. State (J.P. No 555 of 2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Closely Related Eyewitnesses
records.heading: Related eyewitnesses who watched silently from a distance acted unnaturally
records.text: Related eyewitnesses who stood as silent spectators about 20 to 22 paces away while a lone accused armed with a Kassi inflicted repeated blows, and who did not try to save the deceased or apprehend him, acted unnaturally. Their presence at the scene was highly doubtful. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1053; Muhammad Nawaz v. State (J.P. No 555 of 2017).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. State (J.P. No 555 of 2017)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 506 PPC Inapplicable Where Overt Act Follows
records.heading: Section 506 PPC is inapplicable where intimidation ends in an overt act
records.text: Under ss. 503 and 506 PPC, whenever criminal intimidation materialises and ends in an overt act, s. 506 PPC is not applicable and only the overt act committed in consequence of the intimidation remains in the field. Ref: 2023 SCMR 734, 2022 SCMR 1946.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wife's Death in Privacy of Room: Husband's Onus
records.heading: A husband must explain a wife's unnatural death in the privacy of their bedroom
records.text: Where a wife dies an unnatural death inside the privacy of a bedroom at night, the husband, as the only person with access, has exclusive knowledge and bears an onus to explain under Art. 122 QSO, although the initial burden stays on the prosecution. Failure to explain is an additional factor of guilt, and his first version carries much significance. Ref: 2025 YLR 1609, PLJ 2025 CrC 197; The State v. M. Waqas (Murder Reference 215-19).
records.title: The State v. M. Waqas (Murder Reference 215-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive, Extra Judicial Confession and First Version
records.heading: Extra judicial confession and the accused's first version proved motive in a privacy of room death
records.text: Motive was held proved through the complainant's evidence, two witnesses of extra judicial confession and the accused's first version on arrest, which kept persuasive value despite his later denial under s. 342 CrPC. In privacy-of-room deaths, stringent principles are not applied to circumstantial evidence and the surviving partner's conduct is an additional factor. Ref: 2025 YLR 1609, PLJ 2025 CrC 197; The State v. M. Waqas (Murder Reference 215-19).
records.title: The State v. M. Waqas (Murder Reference 215-19)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Deposit of Balance Sale Consideration in Specific Performance
records.heading: A vendee must deposit the balance consideration in Court and a surety bond is no substitute
records.text: A vendee seeking specific performance must show readiness, willingness and ability to perform, and is bound to deposit the balance sale consideration in Court. Offering a surety bond in its place was fatal, and dismissal of the suit for non-deposit was consistent with law. The direction tests seriousness and protects the vendor. Ref: 2025 YLR 1144; Malik Faisal Mehmood v. Shahid Ali (RFA No 93 of 2023).
records.title: Malik Faisal Mehmood v. Shahid Ali (RFA No 93 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Challenge to Gift Deeds in Favour of Minor Nephews
records.heading: A daughter's challenge to gifts to her minor nephews failed on her concessions and delay
records.text: A daughter claiming a 1/6 share challenged gift deeds and mutations in favour of her brother and minor nephews. Her claim was rejected concurrently, as she conceded the nephews' minority and possession, gave no reason for the delayed litigation and acknowledged the disputed transactions. Ref: 2025 YLR 1217; Safia Bibi v. Muhammad Tufail (Civil Revision 30346 of 2024).
records.title: Safia Bibi v. Muhammad Tufail (Civil Revision 30346 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 4 CPC: Particulars of Fraud
records.heading: A party alleging fraud must plead full particulars under O. VI R. 4 CPC
records.text: A party alleging fraud must prove it and plead full particulars under O. VI R. 4 CPC. A vague assertion of fraud, without the circumstances and without proof of the father's incapacity, is a whimsical attribution of no consequence. Ref: 2025 YLR 1217; Safia Bibi v. Muhammad Tufail (Civil Revision 30346 of 2024).
records.title: Safia Bibi v. Muhammad Tufail (Civil Revision 30346 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Trend of Defence Cross-Examination Considered
records.heading: The trend of defence cross-examination may be considered as the court's approach is inquisitorial
records.text: Where the defence has taken a specific plea and the prosecution has proved its case, the trend of the accused's cross-examination of prosecution witnesses may also be considered, because the court's approach is inquisitorial rather than adversarial. Ref: 2025 YLR 1187, PLJ 2025 CrC 386.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 164 CrPC: Statement of Accused Before Magistrate
records.heading: An accused may have his statement recorded under section 164 CrPC but it is not substantive evidence
records.text: Where the investigating officer misrecords or alters the accused's version, the accused may himself have his statement recorded before a Magistrate under s. 164 CrPC. Such a statement is not substantive evidence, and the facts in it must be proved under the Qanun-e-Shahadat. Ref: PLJ 2024 Lah Note 57; Muhammad Asghar Ali Shah v. The State etc (Writ Petition No. 3962/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asghar Ali Shah v. The State etc (Writ Petition No. 3962/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Special Attorney Distinguished from Surety in Execution
records.heading: A decree cannot be executed against a special attorney unlike a surety
records.text: A special attorney differs from a surety. A decree can be executed only against the surety, and not against the special attorney, unless an instrument explicitly makes him liable for satisfaction of the decree. Ref: 2025 CLC 1124; Muhammad Naeem v. ADJ Gujranwala etc (WP 65675/21).
records.title: Muhammad Naeem v. ADJ Gujranwala etc (WP 65675/21)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 11(5) Punjab Partition of Immoveable Property Act 2012
records.heading: Non-payment of the 20 per cent deposit by the highest bidder voids the sale and requires resale
records.text: Under s. 11(5) of the Punjab Partition of Immoveable Property Act, 2012 the highest bidder must deposit 20 per cent at once and the balance within seven days. This is mandatory, non-payment renders the sale void, and the court must order resale under s. 11(10). It is not an irregularity under O. XXI R. 19 CPC, and the Court cannot enlarge the time. Ref: 2025 CLC 1062, PLJ 2024 Lah 519; Adnan Anwar v. Ijaz Ahmad etc (Civil Revision 72449/23).
records.title: Adnan Anwar v. Ijaz Ahmad etc (Civil Revision 72449/23)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower in Gold: Executing Court Cannot Vary Decree
records.heading: An Appellate Court cannot limit execution of a dower decree for gold to a lesser value
records.text: Where gold ornaments given as dower were taken back and the decree allowed recovery of the ornaments or Rs.100,000 as alternate value, the Appellate Court travelled beyond the decree in limiting execution to Rs.100,000. The wife may recover the ornaments or their market value and cannot be compelled to accept the nikahnama value. Ref: 2025 CLC 1048; Mst. Zaib Un Nisa and others v. Additional District Judge, Taxila and others (Writ Petition No. 3346 of 2018).
records.title: Mst. Zaib Un Nisa and others v. Additional District Judge, Taxila and others (Writ Petition No. 3346 of 2018)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Deferred Dower on Khula Due to Husband's Conduct
records.heading: A wife retains deferred dower where the husband's conduct compelled her to seek khula
records.text: Deferred dower is a contractual obligation of the husband, and seeking khula does not by itself nullify it. A wife seeking khula through mere dislike loses deferred dower as with prompt dower, but she retains it where the husband's conduct compelled her to seek dissolution. Ref: 2025 CLC 1074; Asif Mehmood v. Additional District Judge, etc (Writ Petition No.68712 of 2024).
records.title: Asif Mehmood v. Additional District Judge, etc (Writ Petition No.68712 of 2024)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Limitation for Pre-emption Suit: S. 30 Punjab Pre-emption Act
records.heading: A pre-emption suit must be filed within four months of attestation of mutation
records.text: Under s. 30 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1991 the suit must be instituted within four months from the date of attestation of mutation, and not from the date of knowledge alleged in the plaint. Ref: 2025 CLC 1109; Adil Khalil Sattar v. Saad Nasim Khan (Civil Revision-212-21).
records.title: Adil Khalil Sattar v. Saad Nasim Khan (Civil Revision-212-21)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 145 CPC: Surety Liable After Judgment Debtor's Death
records.heading: A surety remains liable under section 145 CPC after the judgment debtor's death
records.text: The death of the judgment debtor does not release the surety from his obligation unless the bond so stipulates. Under s. 145 CPC the decree can be executed against a surety to the extent of his personal liability. Ref: 2025 MLD 1156; Rasheed Ahmad v. Additional District Judge (WP. 63942 of 2024).
records.title: Rasheed Ahmad v. Additional District Judge (WP. 63942 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Enforcement of Court Undertaking in Execution
records.heading: An undertaking before a court is enforceable in execution as if it were a decree
records.text: An undertaking given by a party before a court is enforceable by the Executing Court as if it were a decree, and the Executing Court may use all permissible means, including coercive measures, to secure compliance. Ref: 2025 MLD 1144; Sher Muhammad v. Karam Hussain etc (Civil Revision 883-16).
records.title: Sher Muhammad v. Karam Hussain etc (Civil Revision 883-16)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Power of Attorney Void After Principal's Death; S. 12(2) CPC
records.heading: A power of attorney ends on the principal's death and later transactions by the attorney are void
records.text: On the principal's death a general power of attorney becomes redundant by operation of law, so later transactions by the attorney, including an arbitration agreement, award and decree against the dead, are void and a nullity. The s. 12(2) CPC application was rightly accepted, the petition dismissed and special costs imposed. Ref: 2025 MLD 1012; Mushtaq Ahmad etc v. Allah Ditta etc (Civil Revision.525-13).
records.title: Mushtaq Ahmad etc v. Allah Ditta etc (Civil Revision.525-13)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Postmortem, Ocular-Medical Conflict, Unproved Motive
records.heading: Delays, ocular-medical conflict and unproved motive give benefit of doubt as a right
records.text: A nine-hour delay in postmortem and a five-month delay in filing the private complaint cast doubt on the prosecution case. Conflict between ocular and medical evidence doubts the eyewitnesses, injured witnesses are tested by the rule of prudence, and a failure to prove asserted motive reacts against the prosecution. Benefit of doubt is a right. Ref: 2025 MLD 1165, PLJ 2025 CrC 44; Muhammad Nawaz v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 83167/23).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 83167/23)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Anti-Rape Act 2021: Scheduled Offence Opinion After Charge
records.heading: A Special Court may form its opinion on a scheduled offence only after framing the charge
records.text: A Special Court under the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021 may form its opinion on the applicability of a scheduled offence under s. 16(3) only during the trial, after framing of the charge, and not before. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1121, PLJ 2025 CrC 345; Azra Yasmin v. Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc (Crl. Revision.1836/25).
records.title: Azra Yasmin v. Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc (Crl. Revision.1836/25)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Acquittal by Magistrate: Appeal under S. 417, No Revision
records.heading: An acquittal by a Magistrate is challenged by appeal under section 417 and not by revision
records.text: A person aggrieved by an acquittal by a court other than a High Court may appeal within 30 days under s. 417 CrPC, and the Public Prosecutor may also appeal. Under s. 439(5) CrPC no revision lies at the instance of a party who could have appealed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1095; Muhammad Sarfraz etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc.-6425-M-24).
records.title: Muhammad Sarfraz etc v. State etc (Crl. Misc.-6425-M-24)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Proof of Dower Deed: Art. 79 QSO Not Applicable
records.heading: Art. 79 QSO is exempted in Family Court proof of a dower deed
records.text: Dower claims fall within the Family Courts Act, 1964, and Family Courts are not bound by CPC or strict QSO standards. The Art. 79 QSO requirement of two attesting witnesses is exempted by s. 17 of the Act. The defendants offered no evidence of payment, so the plaintiff was entitled to the decree. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 434, PLJ 2025 SC 567; Mushtaq and others v. Mst. Fatima and others (C.P.L.A.559-P/2024).
records.title: Mushtaq and others v. Mst. Fatima and others (C.P.L.A.559-P/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Heinous Nature of Crime Irrelevant to Appraisal of Evidence
records.heading: The heinous nature of a crime is irrelevant in appraising evidence of guilt
records.text: The gruesome nature of an offence may be relevant to sentence but is irrelevant in appraising evidence of guilt. The accused is presumed innocent until proved guilty beyond reasonable doubt on admissible, trustworthy evidence, and Art. 10-A fair trial rights remain regardless of how heinous the crime. Ref: 2025 YLR 1259; The State v. Muhammad Mohsin (M.R.No.73 of 2021; Crl.A.No.27259-J of 2021).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Mohsin (M.R.No.73 of 2021; Crl.A.No.27259-J of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Witnesses
records.heading: A witness who dishonestly improves his statement on material aspects is unreliable
records.text: A witness who deliberately and mala fide improves his statement on material aspects to strengthen the prosecution case or fill its lacunas becomes unreliable and is not worthy of reliance. Ref: 2025 YLR 1259; The State v. Muhammad Mohsin (M.R.No.73 of 2021; Crl.A.No.27259-J of 2021).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Mohsin (M.R.No.73 of 2021; Crl.A.No.27259-J of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery of Hatchet: Blood Disintegration Over Time
records.heading: Blood origin cannot reliably be detected on a hatchet analysed after a long delay
records.text: A hatchet recovered after the occurrence, received by the Forensic Science Agency on 27.03.2019 and analysed on 08.11.2019, could not reliably retain blood. It was scientifically impossible to detect the origin of blood after such a long period. Ref: 2025 YLR 1467.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Competency of Injured Child Witness: Art. 3 QSO
records.heading: An injured child witness is competent if intelligent and capable of making a statement
records.text: An injured child witness is competent if found intelligent and capable of making a statement in accordance with Art. 3 QSO. Death sentence upheld. Ref: 2025 YLR 1568; Ali Hassan Achoo v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 71917/19).
records.title: Ali Hassan Achoo v. The State etc (Jail Appeal 71917/19)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Infertility Allegation No Ground to Deny Dower or Maintenance
records.heading: Alleged infertility is no ground to withhold dower or maintenance
records.text: Infertility is no ground for a husband to withhold dower or maintenance, and humiliating a wife in litigation by such allegations is not tolerated. The husband's allegations were refuted by medical reports, concurrent findings were upheld, and costs of Rs.500,000 were imposed on him. Ref: Saleh Muhammad and another v. Mst. Mehnaz Begum and others (C.P.L.A.354-P/2025, decided 30.06.2025); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Saleh Muhammad and another v. Mst. Mehnaz Begum and others (C.P.L.A.354-P/2025, decided 30.06.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Child Maintenance After Dissolution of Marriage
records.heading: A father's duty to maintain his child survives divorce and loss of custody
records.text: A father's duty to maintain his child is grounded in lineage, lasts until a son's puberty and a daughter's marriage, and continues for a son unable to earn. It is independent of the duty to maintain a wife, survives divorce and loss of custody, and may devolve on a financially able mother and then the paternal grandfather. Ref: Muhammad Imran Baqir v. Mst. Zarnain Arzoo and others (C.P.L.A.5009/2024, decided 10.07.2025); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Imran Baqir v. Mst. Zarnain Arzoo and others (C.P.L.A.5009/2024, decided 10.07.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Prohibitory Clause and Rule of Consistency
records.heading: The rule of consistency applies only where the accused's case is at par
records.text: The rule of consistency applies only where the accused's case is at par. Bail in prohibitory clause cases is limited to the first and third provisos of s. 497(1) CrPC and further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. A co-accused's confession may be tentatively assessed only if corroborated by independent incriminating material. Ref: Ghazi Arab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1425/2024, decided 22.07.2025); Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi.
records.title: Ghazi Arab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1425/2024, decided 22.07.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ on Non-Fixation of Wheat Prices in Punjab
records.heading: Authority on a writ concerning non-fixation of wheat prices in Punjab
records.text: Authority on a constitutional petition concerning the non-fixation of wheat prices in the Province of Punjab, decided by the Lahore High Court on 25 July 2025. The post does not state the holding. Ref: 2025 LHC 5153; Zafar Hussain Khan v. Federal Government Through Ministry of National Food Security & Research etc (Writ 20539/25, decided 25.07.2025); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Zafar Hussain Khan v. Federal Government Through Ministry of National Food Security & Research etc (Writ 20539/25, decided 25.07.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Beneficial Interpretation and Execution of Dower Decree
records.heading: Family laws are interpreted liberally for women and a dower decree must be fully executed
records.text: Family laws are beneficial legislation and are interpreted liberally in favour of women. The Executing Court must implement a decree in full and not limit it. The wife owns the gold and any appreciation, and the husband's tactics to delay or reduce satisfaction amount to abuse of process. Ref: 2025 CLC 1048; Mst. Zaib Un Nisa and others v. Additional District Judge, Taxila and others (Writ Petition No. 3346 of 2018).
records.title: Mst. Zaib Un Nisa and others v. Additional District Judge, Taxila and others (Writ Petition No. 3346 of 2018)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Family Pension of Divorced Daughter
records.heading: A divorced daughter has the same family pension entitlement as an unmarried daughter
records.text: A daughter's entitlement to the family pension of a deceased civil servant is the same whether she is unmarried or divorced. A circular making entitlement depend on marital status at the time of the pensioner's death is contrary to the Act of 1973 and the Rules, since circulars cannot override or curtail a statute or rules. Ref: Province of Sindh v. Mst. Sorath Fatima (C.P.L.A.616-K/2025, decided 10.07.2025); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Province of Sindh v. Mst. Sorath Fatima (C.P.L.A.616-K/2025, decided 10.07.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medico-Legal Signs of Close-Range Firearm Discharge
records.heading: Burning, scorching and tattooing on entry wounds are signs of close-range discharge
records.text: Burning, scorching, singeing, blackening and tattooing on entry wounds are medico-legal signs of close-range discharge, while exit wounds are free from them. They help estimate firing distance and test the prosecution's factual account, as explained from standard forensic medicine texts. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1391; Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 22010/22).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 22010/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Lapse of Memory and Slip of Tongue of Witnesses
records.heading: A slip of tongue and lapse of memory over time do not destroy testimony
records.text: With the passage of time memory fails and facts cannot be repeated photographically. Where the occurrence was in 2019 and cross-examination in 2021, a mere slip of tongue does not destroy the evidentiary value of the testimony. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1368; Muhammad Amir alias Aneel v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 83064/23).
records.title: Muhammad Amir alias Aneel v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 83064/23)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recording of Evidence in Presence of Accused: S. 353 CrPC
records.heading: Examination in chief must be recorded in the accused's presence under section 353 CrPC
records.text: Recording evidence is a solemn duty of the trial court and not a ritual, and the examination-in-chief of witnesses must be recorded in the accused's presence. Section 353 CrPC allows recording in the accused's presence, or in the presence of counsel if his attendance is dispensed with. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1310, PLJ 2025 CrC 569; Shiraz Ahmad v. State (Crl. Revision No.37104 of 2024).
records.title: Shiraz Ahmad v. State (Crl. Revision No.37104 of 2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Rape and Consent
records.heading: A trustworthy solitary statement of the victim can suffice and pre-arrest bail is refused
records.text: In a rape case the prosecution initially bears the burden of showing absence of consent, and a trustworthy, consistent solitary statement of the victim can suffice. Absence of injuries does not by itself indicate consent (Expl. 2 to s. 375 PPC), and threats or coercion invalidate consent. Scrutiny of inconsistencies between the FIR and the s. 164 CrPC statement is beyond a pre-arrest bail application. Pre-arrest bail dismissed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1354; Zain Tariq v. The State (Crl. Misc. 56457/B of 2024).
records.title: Zain Tariq v. The State (Crl. Misc. 56457/B of 2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused in Non-Prohibitory Offence: Exceptional Circumstances
records.heading: Bail may be refused outside the prohibitory clause where exceptional circumstances exist
records.text: Bail in offences outside the prohibitory clause is a rule in many cases but is not a universal rule and depends on the facts of each case. The petitioner circulated edited nude photographs of a young girl and her mother to a close relative, which was held to be an exceptional circumstance justifying refusal of bail. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1318; Muneeb Riaz v. The State (Crl. Misc. 63844/24).
records.title: Muneeb Riaz v. The State (Crl. Misc. 63844/24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Leave to Defend in Summary Suits
records.heading: A defendant in an O. XXXVII summary suit must first obtain leave to defend
records.text: Under O. XXXVII R. 2(2) CPC a defendant must first obtain leave to appear and defend by showing a plausible defence, failing which the plaint allegations are deemed admitted and the plaintiff is entitled to a decree. Once leave is granted, the procedure of ordinary suits applies, including O. VIII CPC on written statements. Ref: 2025 CLC 1253, PLJ 2025 Lah 354; Abdul Ghaffar v. Umar Farooq (RFA 27-20).
records.title: Abdul Ghaffar v. Umar Farooq (RFA 27-20)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Limitation for Appeal to Board of Revenue; Writ Restraint
records.heading: An appeal to the Board of Revenue filed after ninety days is time barred
records.text: Under s. 162 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 an appeal against a Commissioner's order to the Board of Revenue must be filed within ninety days, and s. 167 applies the Limitation Act. The court must consider limitation under s. 3 even if not raised. A delay of one year and 21 days was fatal. Art. 199 jurisdiction is discretionary. Petition dismissed. Ref: 2025 CLC 1217, PLJ 2025 Lah 1011; Muazzam Ali Goraya v. Member (Judicial-I) (W.P. No. 4078 of 2021, decided 21.01.2025); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Muazzam Ali Goraya v. Member (Judicial-I) (W.P. No. 4078 of 2021, decided 21.01.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 79 and 81 QSO: Attesting Witnesses and Admitted Execution
records.heading: Where the executant admits execution Art. 81 QSO makes both attesting witnesses unnecessary
records.text: Two attesting witnesses must ordinarily be examined under Arts. 17 and 79 QSO, but where execution is admitted by the executant, Art. 81 makes this unnecessary. An agreement admitted in a prior suit could be proved without both marginal witnesses, and a decree on an agreement to sell can be passed in such a case. Ref: 2025 CLC 1291; Muhammad Islam v. Bagh Ali (RSA No. 230/2016).
records.title: Muhammad Islam v. Bagh Ali (RSA No. 230/2016)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Order for Registration of Case Set Aside
records.heading: The order directing registration of a case was set aside by the Chief Justice
records.text: The Chief Justice of the Lahore High Court set aside the order of the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Lahore directing registration of a case against Salman Shahbaz Sharif. The post gives no further reasoning. Ref: 2025 LHC 5178; Salman Shahbaz Sharif v. Ex-Officio JOP ASJ etc (WP 43328/25, decided 31.07.2025).
records.title: Salman Shahbaz Sharif v. Ex-Officio JOP ASJ etc (WP 43328/25, decided 31.07.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Asphyxia: Medical Definition and Appearances
records.heading: Asphyxia is a severe oxygen deficiency and the appellant was acquitted on benefit of doubt
records.text: The judgment sets out the medical definition of asphyxia as a severe deficiency of oxygen caused by interference with breathing, and describes the post-mortem appearances of a body in such cases. The appeal was accepted, the conviction and sentence set aside, and the appellant acquitted on the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2020 YLR 2018; Criminal Appeal No. 207-J of 2016/BWP.
records.title: Criminal Appeal No. 207-J of 2016/BWP

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Asphyxia and Manual Strangulation: Medical Extract
records.heading: Medical extract on asphyxia and strangulation; appeal accepted and appellant acquitted
records.text: Extract describing asphyxia, strangulation and neck anatomy relevant to the clinical features of a strangled victim. The appeal was accepted, the conviction and sentence set aside, and the appellant acquitted.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade Not Always Required: CCTV Evidence
records.heading: An identification parade is not always required where CCTV footage shows the accused
records.text: Holding an identification parade is not a legal requirement in every case. Any fact establishing identity is relevant under Art. 22 QSO, and CCTV clips showing the accused are admissible and also considered under Art. 164 QSO, subject to genuineness and authenticity. No parade was needed where such footage was available. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 470; Shahbaz Mustafa and another v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 15084-B/2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Mustafa and another v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 15084-B/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Medical and Ocular Evidence
records.heading: Eyewitness testimony cannot be accepted without reasons despite a conflict with medical evidence
records.text: Accepting eyewitness testimony despite a noticeable conflict with medical evidence, without reasons, discards the medical expert and encourages false witnesses. Medical evidence enables the court to test the truth of eyewitness accounts in murder and hurt cases, and a consistent judicial view acquits where ocular and medical evidence materially vary. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 531.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Evidentiary Value of Site Plan
records.heading: A site plan gains evidentiary value only if prepared on the witness's pointation
records.text: A site plan cannot contradict eyewitnesses unless it is proved to have been prepared on their pointation. Where it is so proved, as when the witness admitted pointing out the scene, it gains evidentiary value and shows the crime scene, witness locations and distances, and helps the court understand the genesis of the occurrence. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 531.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Examination of Witnesses: Arts. 132, 133, 137 QSO
records.heading: Examination of witnesses under Articles 132, 133 and 137 QSO: leading questions barred in chief
records.text: Art. 132 QSO divides the examination of a witness into examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination, with the sequence under Art. 133. Leading questions in examination-in-chief are barred on objection under Art. 137(1), and a party may cross-examine its own witness in the dock under Art. 150 only if the court permits. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 531.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Cross-Examining Own Witness, Hostile Witness
records.heading: A party may cross-examine its own witness under Article 150 QSO only with court permission
records.text: Cross-examination of a witness by the party calling him under Art. 150 QSO rests on the court's discretion, exercisable only in compelling circumstances and by a reasoned order on an application. Once permitted, Art. 141 questions may be put. Declaring hostile a police officer who repeats in court a view favourable to the accused given during investigation is a fallacious approach. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 531.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in s. 489-F PPC: Exceptional Circumstances
records.heading: Bail under section 489-F PPC may be refused in exceptional circumstances such as forgery and fraud
records.text: Although s. 489-F PPC does not attract the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC and bail is normally allowed, it is not a universal rule, and bail may be refused where exceptional circumstances exist. The petitioner obtained Rs. 1,204,600 on a false promise of a bank loan, handing over a forged bank letter and then a cheque. Bail refused and petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 481.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Refused: Viral Video Shared on Social Media
records.heading: Bail refused for a viral video shared on social media in exceptional circumstances
records.text: The petitioner was named for making and sharing a viral video clip, and his phone contained the content. An offence outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC does not become bailable, and bail may be refused where exceptional circumstances exist and the offence is shocking to public morality. No case for further inquiry was made out. Bail declined. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 473.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Simultaneous Civil and Criminal Proceedings
records.heading: Civil and criminal proceedings on the same matter may run together, with discretionary postponement
records.text: There is no bar to simultaneous civil and criminal proceedings on the same matter. Where criminal liability depends on the civil outcome and a bona fide claim cannot readily be distinguished from the criminal act alleged, the trial court may, in its discretion, postpone the criminal proceedings until the civil proceedings conclude. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 483.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation Not a Mere Technicality: Condonation of Delay
records.heading: Limitation is not a mere technicality and every day of delay must be explained
records.text: Limitation is not a mere technicality, and rights accrued through limitation cannot be taken away without sufficient cause. Limitation runs even against void orders. To condone delay in filing a revision, every day of delay must be explained and shown to have arisen from causes beyond the litigant's control. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 692.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Is Not an Instrument: Art. 91
records.heading: A mutation is not an instrument under Article 91 and is not a document of title
records.text: A mutation is not an instrument for the purposes of Art. 91. It records the effect of a change in ownership caused by a legal transaction and is evidence of title, not a document of title. It follows the transaction as its effect and does not precede it. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 699.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Influence of Elders as Mitigating Plea
records.heading: Influence of elders mitigates only for impressionable offenders, not accused of mature age
records.text: The principle of influence of elders applies only to offenders of impressionable age living under the influence of elders. An accused of mature age and comprehension cannot be taken to have acted on instigation, and elders, including a father, have no universal authority to command brutal and wanton murder. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 113.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Counter Version and Report Under s. 173 CrPC
records.heading: A section 173 CrPC report cannot be discarded on a belated counter version without examining the material
records.text: Where a counter version was introduced after inordinate delay, and neither court below examined the entire material or identified any error in the investigation, discarding the s. 173 CrPC report was unjustified. The criminal petition was converted into an appeal and allowed, and the Lahore High Court order was set aside. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 120.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Conviction on Uncorroborated Single Statement
records.heading: Conviction cannot rest on a single statement disbelieved against a co-accused without corroboration
records.text: A conviction cannot rest solely on the testimony of a witness that has been disbelieved against a co-accused. A single witness is relied on only if reliable and unimpeachable, and corroboration remains necessary in serious charges even though falsus in uno is no longer strictly applied. The medical certificate showed no recent penetration. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 139.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 341 CrPC: Accused Unable to Understand Proceedings
records.heading: Where an accused cannot understand proceedings, section 341 CrPC bars sentence by the trial judge
records.text: Where an accused cannot understand the proceedings, s. 341 CrPC applies. Unless he is insane the trial may proceed, but on conviction the trial judge must forward the proceedings to the High Court and cannot pass sentence. The reference was made without complying with s. 341, so the case was remanded to the trial court and the reference answered in the negative. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 550; The State v. Saqib Hussain Qureshi.
records.title: The State v. Saqib Hussain Qureshi

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed FIR, Suspect Complainant and Stale Recovery
records.heading: Delayed FIR, doubtful complainant and stale recovery undermine the prosecution case
records.text: An FIR not promptly recorded undermines the prosecution, and unexplained delay in reporting is fatal. A complainant whose presence is unproven and who makes inconsistent statements cannot be relied on, nor can witnesses who dishonestly improve. A bloodstained brick recovered after more than two months was of no use. Medical evidence is only confirmatory, and motive is double-edged. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 613, 2025 PCrLJ 1675; Ali Hassan and three others v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 78438 of 2022).
records.title: Ali Hassan and three others v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 78438 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Triple Talaq: Widow's Inheritance During Iddat
records.heading: A wife divorced by triple talaq inherits if her husband dies during her iddat
records.text: A wife divorced by triple talaq in a single sitting inherits from her husband if he dies during her iddat period. The judgment notes that s. 7(3) of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 requires ninety days after notice to the Union Council Chairman before talaq takes effect, and that treating talaq-e-biddat as immediately effective undermines that safeguard. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 444, PLD 2025 SC 469; Aziz Ahmad and others v. Mst. Musarat and another (C.P.L.A.181/2023).
records.title: Aziz Ahmad and others v. Mst. Musarat and another (C.P.L.A.181/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Discretionary Summons for Production
records.heading: Section 94 CrPC gives the court discretion to summon documents unless the application is vexatious
records.text: S. 94 CrPC gives the court discretion to issue process for production of documents or things on the application of the prosecution or the accused. On an accused's application the judge issues it unless, for recorded reasons, it is made for vexation, delay or defeating justice. The word 'may' means the court is under no obligation to compel production. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 169.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance Decree Implies Possession
records.heading: A decree for specific performance impliedly carries the right to possession
records.text: A suit for specific performance is always a suit for possession, so a decree for specific performance, including a compromise decree, implicitly carries the right to possession even if not expressly sought. Where a compromise decree does not cover the terms agreed, it cannot be executed as it stands and a fresh suit is required. Ref: PLD 2025 Sindh 242.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 47 CPC: Executing Court and Possession
records.heading: Possession follows a specific performance decree in execution even if not expressly prayed for
records.text: Plaintiffs who succeeded in a suit against the Karachi Development Authority over cancelled plots were refused possession in execution because possession was not specifically prayed for. The High Court, as a court of record with supervisory powers, set aside both orders and directed the authority to hand over physical possession forthwith. Constitutional petition allowed. Ref: 2025 CLC 858.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift and Tamleek: Onus and Principles of Proof
records.heading: The beneficiary of a challenged gift bears a heavy onus to prove it
records.text: Where a gift or transfer by a deceased owner is challenged by a lawful heir, the court must scrutinise the evidence closely. The beneficiary of the impugned gift bears the heavy onus of proving the transaction. The Supreme Court set out principles on the requisites and proof of gift, relying on earlier authorities. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 474, PLD 2025 SC 502; Hidayat Khan and others v. Mst. Nasreen and others (C.P.L.A.287-P/2025); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Hidayat Khan and others v. Mst. Nasreen and others (C.P.L.A.287-P/2025)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Challenge to Award: Consent and No Misconduct
records.heading: A party that consented to the umpire and participated without objection cannot successfully challenge the award
records.text: A party to an arbitration agreement or award may challenge its existence or validity by an independent application or in reply to an application to make the award a rule of court. The respondent consented to the Naib Tehsildar as umpire and participated without objection, and no misconduct was proved. Civil revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 778; Tafazzal Abbas v. Saif-ur-Rehman (C.R. No. 1525 of 2015, heard 16.10.2024); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Tafazzal Abbas v. Saif-ur-Rehman (C.R. No. 1525 of 2015, heard 16.10.2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 118 NI Act Presumption in O. XXXVII Cheque Suit
records.heading: The section 118 presumption arises on admitted execution and must be strongly rebutted, even after leave
records.text: The presumption under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act arises whenever execution of the instrument is admitted, and the defendant must rebut it strongly, even after leave to defend is granted. A cheque dishonoured for insufficient funds leaves the issuer no other ground. The appellant produced nothing showing the cheque was invalid or obtained by force. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 798, 2026 CLC 252; Tahir Javed v. Muhammad Sharif (R.F.A. No. 23970 of 2025, decided 02.07.2025); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad; Justice Hassan Nawaz Makhdoom.
records.title: Tahir Javed v. Muhammad Sharif (R.F.A. No. 23970 of 2025, decided 02.07.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Omitted Rule 17-A: No Right to Appointment
records.heading: No appointment can be claimed under a rule omitted and declared unconstitutional before appointment
records.text: The petitioner sought appointment under R. 17-A of the Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment and Conditions of Services) Rules, 1974 after his father's medical retirement. The rule was omitted and declared unconstitutional before his appointment, so no entitlement survived. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 828; Usama Zahoor v. District & Sessions Judge, Multan (W.P. No. 1601 of 2025, heard 22.05.2025); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Usama Zahoor v. District & Sessions Judge, Multan (W.P. No. 1601 of 2025, heard 22.05.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Against Interlocutory Order Refusing Interim Injunction
records.heading: A writ petition against refusal of an ad interim injunction is not maintainable
records.text: A constitutional petition against refusal of an ad interim injunction under O. XXXIX Rr. 1 and 2 CPC is not maintainable, as such an interlocutory order is not final and an adequate remedy exists. The proper course is to await the trial court's decision, since interim orders remain open in appeal. Ownership rights prevail over easement claims. Petition dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 832, 2026 CLC 168; Arshad Iqbal Rana v. Salman Sajjad (W.P. No. 42046 of 2025, decided 08.07.2025); Justice Malik Waqar Haider Awan.
records.title: Arshad Iqbal Rana v. Salman Sajjad (W.P. No. 42046 of 2025, decided 08.07.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Unexhibited Document Cannot Be Relied Upon
records.heading: A document not produced and exhibited in evidence cannot be read or relied upon
records.text: A document which was not produced and exhibited in evidence cannot be read and relied upon. Ref: 2025 MLD 1165; Muhammad Nawaz v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 83167/23).
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 83167/23)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Termination of Widow on Remarriage: Gender Discrimination
records.heading: Terminating a widow on remarriage alone is sex discrimination contrary to Article 25
records.text: A widow appointed as clerk under a compassionate package for families of deceased employees was terminated on remarriage. The disqualification singled out widows with no corresponding restriction on widowers, which is direct discrimination on the basis of sex contravening Arts. 25(1) and 25(2) of the Constitution. Ref: 2025 PLC (C.S.) 844; The Chief Commissioner Regional Tax Office, Bahawalpur v. Shaheen Yousaf.
records.title: The Chief Commissioner Regional Tax Office, Bahawalpur v. Shaheen Yousaf

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Photographic Narration by Eyewitnesses at Night
records.heading: Detailed night-time eyewitness accounts of each accused's injury are improbable without proof of light
records.text: Detailed narration by two eyewitnesses assigning a specific injury to each accused in a panic situation is highly improbable, especially at night where the street light claimed to illuminate the scene was not collected by the Investigating Officer. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 176.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Case Property: R. 22.16 Police Rules and Sealing
records.heading: Case property must be marked, sealed and kept safely under Rule 22.16 of the Police Rules
records.text: R. 22.16 of the Police Rules, 1934 requires seized articles to be marked or labelled, parcels sealed and kept in safe custody, and sent to headquarters or the magistrate when ordered. Under the High Court Rules and Orders, case property exhibited in open court is resealed with the court's seal and this is recorded, to preserve it for the appellate forum. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 177.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Recovery Not Video Recorded Despite Available Camera
records.heading: Bail allowed where the arrest and recovery were not video recorded despite an available camera
records.text: The arresting officer had a mobile phone with a camera but neither he nor the Investigating Officer recorded the arrest and recovery. Art. 164 QSO permits modern devices, and such footage would have been the best evidence against the petitioner. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 182.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Confession Corroborated by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Conviction may rest on a confession corroborated by medical evidence and a chain of circumstances
records.text: With no direct evidence, a conviction under s. 302(b) PPC rested on the appellant's confession. Medical evidence corroborated the confession, and the corroborative circumstances together formed a strong chain pointing to the appellant. The conviction and sentence were maintained and the appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 187; Muhammad Ilyas v. The State (Crl. A. No. 113 of 2024, decided 28.08.2024); Justice Rozi Khan Barrech; Justice Abdullah Baloch.
records.title: Muhammad Ilyas v. The State (Crl. A. No. 113 of 2024, decided 28.08.2024)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: FIA Jurisdiction: PPC Offences Related to PECA
records.heading: The FIA has no jurisdiction over PPC offences merely because the conduct also relates to PECA
records.text: The FIA, as designated agency under s. 29 PECA, has no jurisdiction to investigate allegations attracting PPC offences merely because the conduct also relates to a PECA offence. The complainant may approach the police to register an FIR under the CrPC for the PPC offences. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 Civil Note 157; Javad Khan v. State and 2 others (W.P. No. 4047 of 2022, decided 17.02.2023); Justice Babar Sattar.
records.title: Javad Khan v. State and 2 others (W.P. No. 4047 of 2022, decided 17.02.2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summoning Income Tax Record: S. 216 Income Tax Ordinance
records.heading: Section 216 of the Income Tax Ordinance bars summoning a deceased non-party's tax record
records.text: S. 216 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 prohibits requisitioning an individual's income tax record except in specified cases. None applied to the tax record of a deceased person who was not a party to the damages suit. The trial court rightly refused the application, and the civil revision was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 Islamabad 298; Basit Shuja v. Rauf Klasra (C.R. No. 32 of 2025, decided 29.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Azam Khan.
records.title: Basit Shuja v. Rauf Klasra (C.R. No. 32 of 2025, decided 29.04.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Malicious Prosecution Damages: Scope of Second Appeal
