records.heading: A second appeal under section 100 CPC lies only for error of law or procedural defect
records.text: A suit for damages for malicious prosecution after acquittal was decreed and the appeal dismissed on concurrent findings, the appellant having led no evidence connecting the respondent to the offence and failed to appear for deposition. A second appeal under s. 100 CPC lies only where the decision is contrary to law or involves a substantial error or defect in procedure. Ref: PLJ 2025 Karachi 130.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A plaint may be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 only on the stated grounds
records.text: A plaint may be rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC only if it discloses no cause of action, is barred by law, or is undervalued or insufficiently stamped and the deficiency is not made good in time. Art. 113 of the Limitation Act, 1908 gives three years for specific performance from the fixed date or from notice of refusal. Ref: 2025 MLD 1284; Muhammad Iqbal etc v. Muhammad Ashraf etc (Civil Revision 2164-11).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal etc v. Muhammad Ashraf etc (Civil Revision 2164-11)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Benami Transaction: Meaning and Burden of Proof
records.heading: A benami plea must be proved by unimpeachable evidence by the party raising it
records.text: A benami transaction is one in the name of another person who holds the property as ostensible owner. The party raising the plea of benami must prove it by unimpeachable evidence. Ref: Mst. Nasira Ansari and others v. Late Tahira Begum through legal heirs and others (C.A.41-K/2021, decided 17.07.2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mst. Nasira Ansari and others v. Late Tahira Begum through legal heirs and others (C.A.41-K/2021, decided 17.07.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Criminal Breach of Trust, s. 405 PPC
records.heading: Entrustment and a master-servant relationship under section 405 PPC are questions for trial evidence
records.text: The ingredients of criminal breach of trust under s. 405 PPC are entrustment of property or dominion over it, and dishonest misappropriation, conversion or disposal in violation of the trust. Whether a master-servant relationship existed and whether entrustment took place are factual questions for determination after evidence at trial. Ref: 2025 MLD 1374; Danish Riaz Dar v. The State (Crl. Misc. Pre-Arrest Bail 1832-B-25).
records.title: Danish Riaz Dar v. The State (Crl. Misc. Pre-Arrest Bail 1832-B-25)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage: Proof and Admissibility
records.heading: CCTV footage not proved by expert certificate or witness cannot be relied upon
records.text: CCTV video from the Safe City Authority was not proved where no expert certificate or witness verified its genuineness, no photogrammetry test was done, and the footage was neither played in court nor shown to a witness. Arts. 71 and 139 QSO were not met. A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt suffices for acquittal, relying on 2024 SCMR 1507. Ref: 2025 YLR 1681; Muhammad Ammar Shafi and 2 others v. The State (Crl. Appeal 26878/24).
records.title: Muhammad Ammar Shafi and 2 others v. The State (Crl. Appeal 26878/24)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Concealment by Eyewitnesses; Uncertain Medical Timing
records.heading: Complainant and injured witnesses who conceal vital facts cannot be relied on for conviction
records.text: A complainant and injured eyewitnesses who conceal vital facts of the occurrence cannot be relied on for conviction. Medical evidence uncertain about the interval between injury and death and between death and autopsy cannot support the ocular account on the time of occurrence or death. Ref: 2025 YLR 1911; Ghulam Qadir v. The State (Crl. Appeal 79724/21).
records.title: Ghulam Qadir v. The State (Crl. Appeal 79724/21)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Partial Decree on Selective Evidence
records.heading: A partial decree resting on fragments of evidence, ignoring material facts, cannot be sustained
records.text: A partial decree cannot be sustained where it relies on fragments of evidence and disregards material facts and documents. Courts must examine all relevant evidence holistically, and a decree rendered without evaluating the totality of the evidence amounts to a miscarriage of justice. Ref: 2025 YLR 1802; Akhtar Munir v. Gul Said etc (R.F.A. 147-24).
records.title: Akhtar Munir v. Gul Said etc (R.F.A. 147-24)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Attribution of Quantity to Each Co-Accused
records.heading: At the bail stage each accused is attributed only the narcotic quantity recovered from him
records.text: At the bail stage, unless confidence inspiring material shows each accused knew of the others' possession of narcotics, the total quantity cannot be attributed to each, and each is attributed only the quantity recovered from him or on his pointation. Total quantity may be attributed only after evidence proves conscious knowledge. Ref: Muhammad Daud v. The State through Special Prosecutor A.N.F. and another (Crl.P.L.A.537/2025, decided 19.06.2025); Justice Aamer Farooq.
records.title: Muhammad Daud v. The State through Special Prosecutor A.N.F. and another (Crl.P.L.A.537/2025, decided 19.06.2025)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Pension Claim: Recurring Cause of Action
records.heading: Pension is a recurring cause of action, so delay does not automatically defeat the claim
records.text: Pension constitutes a recurring cause of action. Claims for payment of lawful dues recur, so delay does not automatically vitiate the claim. Ref: 2025 SCMR 168, 2025 PLC (C.S.) 319; Chairman/Dean Sheikh Zayed Hospital, Lahore v. Amjad Mehmood Khan.
records.title: Chairman/Dean Sheikh Zayed Hospital, Lahore v. Amjad Mehmood Khan

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension Is a Vested Right, Not Charity
records.heading: Pension is a vested right and not charity, and cannot be withheld without hearing
records.text: Pension is a vested right and compensation for services rendered, not charity, and delaying or denying it without lawful justification or a hearing is unacceptable. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court order upholding withholding of pensionary benefits for absence without leave and ensured payment to the civil servant. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1689, 2024 PLC (C.S.) 1178; Muhammad Yousaf v. Province of Sindh.
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Province of Sindh

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence: Rarest of Rare Doctrine
records.heading: Death sentence maintained under the rarest of rare doctrine for a brutal murder of a wife
records.text: Under the rarest of rare doctrine, death may be imposed where the offence is exceptionally brutal, shocks the collective conscience and requires deterrence. The appellant murdered his wife in the matrimonial home before their young children and deserved no leniency. Death sentence maintained. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 510; Abid Hussain v. The State (Crl.A.131/2023).
records.title: Abid Hussain v. The State (Crl.A.131/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Mediation: Pro-Mediation Approach of Courts
records.heading: Courts should adopt a pro-mediation approach, especially early in litigation
records.text: Mediation is a non-adversarial process built on collaboration, confidentiality and party autonomy, reducing cost and court burden. Courts should adopt a pro-mediation approach, especially early in litigation, and the ADR Mediation Accreditation (Eligibility) Rules, 2023 and Mediation Practice Direction (Civil) Rules, 2023 consolidate mediation as a mainstream tool. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 499; Muhammad Naseer Butt v. Additional District Judge, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.3519/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Naseer Butt v. Additional District Judge, Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.3519/2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Military Trial of Civilians: Intra Court Appeals Allowed
records.heading: Intra court appeals allowed by majority: Army Act provisions on trial of civilians restored
records.text: By a majority of five to two, the Supreme Court allowed the intra court appeals, set aside the impugned judgment and restored s. 2(1)(d)(i) and (ii) and s. 59(4) of the Pakistan Army Act, 1952, holding they could not be declared ultra vires on the basis of Art. 8(5) of the Constitution. Two judges dismissed the appeals. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 482; Shuhada Forum, Balochistan through its Patron in Chief, Nawabzada Jamal Raisani, Quetta Cantt and others v. Justice (R) Jawwad S. Khawaja and others (I.C.A.5/2023, majority short order dated 07.05.2025); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi; Justice Musarrat Hilali; Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Naeem Akhter Afghan.
records.title: Shuhada Forum, Balochistan through its Patron in Chief, Nawabzada Jamal Raisani, Quetta Cantt and others v. Justice (R) Jawwad S. Khawaja and others (I.C.A.5/2023, majority short order dated 07.05.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Transfer of High Court Judges: Art. 200 Constitution
records.heading: The President's power to transfer judges under Article 200(1) is separate from the Judicial Commission's powers
records.text: By a majority of three to two, the Constitutional Bench held that the President's power to transfer judges under Art. 200(1) is separate from the powers of the Judicial Commission, and a transfer is not a new appointment. The questions whether the transfer is permanent or temporary and the judges' seniority were referred to the President. Two judges allowed the petitions and set aside the notification of 01.02.2025. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 516; Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, Judge, Islamabad High Court, Islamabad and others v. The President of Pakistan, Pak Secretariat, Islamabad and others (C.P.22/2025, decided 19.06.2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar; Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan; Justice Salahuddin Panhwar; Justice Naeem Akhter Afghan; Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, Judge, Islamabad High Court, Islamabad and others v. The President of Pakistan, Pak Secretariat, Islamabad and others (C.P.22/2025, decided 19.06.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Extra-Judicial and Judicial Confessions
records.heading: An extra-judicial confession is weak evidence and needs strong corroboration for a capital conviction
records.text: Pakistani law recognises extra-judicial and judicial confessions. An extra-judicial confession is weak evidence and cannot found a capital conviction unless strongly corroborated by tangible evidence from an unimpeachable source. Art. 2(4) QSO sets the prudent man standard. A confession that shifts blame to others while casting the maker as an unwilling spectator is not acceptable. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1380, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 160; Bashir-ud-Din and Sharif-ud-Din v. The State (Crl.A.26/2021).
records.title: Bashir-ud-Din and Sharif-ud-Din v. The State (Crl.A.26/2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Discrepancies in Witness Testimony
records.heading: Minor discrepancies not going to the root of the case are inconsequential
records.text: Minor discrepancies and omissions not going to the root of the case are inconsequential and are inbuilt proof of truthfulness. Only discrepancies on material aspects benefit the defence. Credibility depends on the intrinsic worth and coherence of the testimony and not on the status of the witness. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1360; Iftikhar Kiyani alias Khara v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 703 of 2020).
records.title: Iftikhar Kiyani alias Khara v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 703 of 2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Right of Appeal Is Substantive: Must Be Statutory
records.heading: The right of appeal is substantive and must be conferred by the Act, not the Rules
records.text: The right of appeal is a substantive right and a continuation of the original proceedings, not a mere matter of procedure. It should be provided in the Act and not in the Rules. Substantive law defines rights, while procedural law governs the modes and conditions of their application. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1229; Muhammad Dawood v. Mst. Sakeena Farooque @ Aziza and others (C.P.L.A.479-K/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Dawood v. Mst. Sakeena Farooque @ Aziza and others (C.P.L.A.479-K/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift of Immovable Property: Ss. 122, 123, 129 TPA
records.heading: A Muslim gift of immovable property needs tender, acceptance and delivery of possession, which the donee must prove
records.text: S. 123 of the Transfer of Property Act requires a registered instrument attested by two witnesses for a gift of immovable property, but s. 129 saves Muslim law, under which a valid gift needs tender, acceptance and delivery of possession, with the donor divesting himself of ownership. Relaxation or optional registration does not relieve the donee of strictly proving the gift. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1229; Muhammad Dawood v. Mst. Sakeena Farooque @ Aziza and others (C.P.L.A.479-K/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Dawood v. Mst. Sakeena Farooque @ Aziza and others (C.P.L.A.479-K/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Circumstantial Evidence
records.heading: Conviction on circumstantial evidence needs an unbroken chain excluding every hypothesis of innocence
records.text: A conviction, even in a capital case, may rest on circumstantial evidence if it excludes every hypothesis of innocence, but such evidence must be accepted with great caution and minutely scrutinised. The prosecution must prove each circumstance independently, forming an unbroken chain leading to no inference other than guilt. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1399; Muhammad Wajid v. The State (Crl.A.212/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Wajid v. The State (Crl.A.212/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Grounds and Scope of Interference
records.heading: Bail is cancelled for misconduct undermining justice, and interference with a bail order is limited
records.text: Bail may be cancelled for conduct undermining the administration of justice, such as influencing witnesses, tampering with evidence, committing another offence, breaching conditions, or absconding. An appellate court interferes with a bail-granting order only if it is perverse on its face or made in clear disregard of a principle of bail law. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1357; Rab Nawaz v. Shehzad Hassan etc (Crl.P.253-L/2025).
records.title: Rab Nawaz v. Shehzad Hassan etc (Crl.P.253-L/2025)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Company Judge Jurisdiction Under 1984 Ordinance
records.heading: The Company Judge may resolve disputed questions of fact where necessary
records.text: The jurisdiction of the Company Judge under the Companies Ordinance, 1984 includes the power to resolve disputed questions of fact where necessary. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1307; Sher Asfandyar Khan v. Neelofar Shah and others (C.A.1843/2019).
records.title: Sher Asfandyar Khan v. Neelofar Shah and others (C.A.1843/2019)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Promotion Committee Cannot Test Vires of Rules
records.heading: A Departmental Promotion Committee cannot sit in judgment on the vires of rules
records.text: A Departmental Promotion Committee must act in accordance with law and cannot sit in judgment over the vires of the law or rules. The judgment also discusses the role of the civil service in a democratic state. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1221; Aatika Hina Mushtaq v. Secretary Special Education Government of the Punjab, Special Education Department Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.3116/2022).
records.title: Aatika Hina Mushtaq v. Secretary Special Education Government of the Punjab, Special Education Department Lahore and others (C.P.L.A.3116/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata: S. 11 CPC
records.heading: Section 11 CPC bars retrial of matters directly and substantially decided in a former suit
records.text: S. 11 CPC bars a court from trying a suit or issue directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, litigating under the same title, in a competent court and finally decided. It rests on the principle that one judicial contest is sufficient for the same cause of action. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1262; Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022).
records.title: Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 2(2) CPC: Definition of Decree
records.heading: A decree under section 2(2) CPC is a formal conclusive adjudication of the parties' rights
records.text: Under s. 2(2) CPC a decree is the formal expression of an adjudication conclusively determining the rights of the parties on matters in controversy, and may be preliminary or final. It includes rejection of a plaint, but excludes adjudications appealable as orders and dismissals for default. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1262; Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022).
records.title: Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC read with S. 149: Court Fee Deficiency
records.heading: A suit cannot be dismissed for deficient court fee without identifying it and allowing time to pay
records.text: Rejection of a plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC must follow careful examination of cause of action, valuation, stamping and any bar of law. O. VII R. 11 and s. 149 CPC are read together, so a suit or appeal cannot be dismissed for deficient court fee without identifying the deficiency and allowing time to pay. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1262; Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022).
records.title: Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Ss. 148 and 149 CPC: Enlargement of Time, Court Fee
records.heading: Court fee deficiency may be made good at any stage, including in appeal, under section 149 CPC
records.text: S. 148 CPC permits the court to enlarge time fixed by it, and s. 149 permits court fee deficiency to be made good at any stage, an exception to ss. 4 and 6 of the Court Fees Act, 1870. The expression at any stage allows the appellate court to order the deficiency cured in appeal. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1262; Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022).
records.title: Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Duty of Judge to Apply Correct Law
records.heading: It is the judge's duty to know and apply the correct law
records.text: Parties need not engage lawyers, and it is the judge's duty, not the litigant's, to know and apply the correct law. Relevant provisions cannot be avoided because the parties did not bring them to the court's notice, and counsel's failure to advise properly is not a complete excuse. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1262; Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022).
records.title: Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Concurrent Findings Not Sacrosanct if Erroneous
records.heading: Concurrent findings are not sacrosanct if contrary to law or based on misreading of evidence
records.text: Concurrent findings that violate the law or rest on misreading or non-reading of evidence are not sacrosanct and may be reversed by the High Court in revision, constitutional jurisdiction or second appeal. Appellate courts do not re-weigh evidence but must examine whether the judgment accords with law and evidence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1262; Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022).
records.title: Habib Rehman and others v. Abdul Karim deceased through legal heirs and others (C.P.L.A.770-K/2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal: Execution of Its Own Judgments
records.heading: The Service Tribunal, as a civil court, can execute its own judgments
records.text: Under s. 5 of the Service Tribunals Act 1973 the Tribunal is deemed a civil court. Even if no rules for execution are framed under s. 8 of the Civil Servants Act 1973, the Tribunal can execute its judgments as a civil court. The judgment also addresses s. 9(1) of the Act and the effect of F.R. 17 on proforma promotion. Ref: 2025 SCMR 819; Ahmed Owais Peerzada v. Principal Secretary (C.P.L.A.44/2022).
records.title: Ahmed Owais Peerzada v. Principal Secretary (C.P.L.A.44/2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade Without Role Has No Value
records.heading: An identification parade without the role of each accused has no evidentiary value
records.text: An identification parade in which witnesses identify the accused without stating the role played by each is not in line with Art. 22 QSO and has no evidentiary value. CCTV footage showing only the back of the culprit does not support conviction, and where recovery of the weapon is disbelieved the firearm expert's positive report loses value. Ref: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (J.P.213/2024, decided 05.06.2025); Justice Naeem Akhter Afghan.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (J.P.213/2024, decided 05.06.2025)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Delay in Banking Cases: Case Management and AI
records.heading: Unexplained delay in banking cases is a governance failure requiring modern case management
records.text: The Supreme Court criticised unexplained delay in deciding banking cases in the High Court, describing delay as a structural challenge of judicial governance. It called for a modern case management system with non-discriminatory early fixation, no queue-jumping, age-tracking of dormant cases and judicious use of AI tools for scheduling and triage. Ref: Abdul Salam Khan v. M/s Bank Al-Habib Ltd (C.P.L.A.88-P/2022, decided 18.07.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Abdul Salam Khan v. M/s Bank Al-Habib Ltd (C.P.L.A.88-P/2022, decided 18.07.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 59 & 84 QSO: Fingerprint Evidence
records.heading: Fingerprint analysis is an accepted forensic tool under Articles 59 and 84 QSO
records.text: Under Arts. 59 and 84 QSO, fingerprint analysis (dactyloscopy) is widely accepted as an indispensable forensic tool, based on the principle that no fingerprints are alike and that patterns remain constant through life. Ref: 2025 SCMR 955; Mst. Ramzanu Bibi v. Ibrahim (C.A. No. 113-L of 2010).
records.title: Mst. Ramzanu Bibi v. Ibrahim (C.A. No. 113-L of 2010)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation of Gift: Threefold Burden on Beneficiary
records.heading: Beneficiaries of a challenged gift mutation bear the threefold burden of proving the transaction
records.text: Where a mutation of gift is challenged for fraud, its beneficiaries must prove the original transaction, discharging the burdens of pleading, of producing evidence and of persuasion. The plaintiff was justified in delaying action until the threat became overt, and her suit was within limitation. The concurrent findings were set aside and the suit decreed. Ref: 2025 SCMR 955; Mst. Ramzanu Bibi v. Ibrahim (C.A. No. 113-L of 2010).
records.title: Mst. Ramzanu Bibi v. Ibrahim (C.A. No. 113-L of 2010)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Scope of Writ Proceedings
records.heading: Article 199 provides an expeditious remedy where illegality is shown without elaborate enquiry
records.text: Proceedings under Art. 199 of the Constitution redress actual infringement of rights and provide an expeditious remedy where illegality can be shown without elaborate enquiry. The Court also observed that innocent employees in low pay scales are made scapegoats while the actual wrongdoers escape. Ref: Arab and another v. Province of Sindh through Secretary Health Department and others (C.P.L.A.933-K/2023, decided 04.06.2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Arab and another v. Province of Sindh through Secretary Health Department and others (C.P.L.A.933-K/2023, decided 04.06.2025)

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Restoration of Election Petition Dismissed for Non-Prosecution
records.heading: The Election Tribunal may restore an election petition dismissed for non-prosecution
records.text: The Election Tribunal has power to restore an election petition dismissed for non-prosecution. The contrary view in 2018 CLC 1040 is not persuasive in light of the Larger Bench of the Lahore High Court holding that such power lies with the Tribunal. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 692; Muhammad Yar v. Naveed Aslam Khan Lodhi etc (WP.65282/24).
records.title: Muhammad Yar v. Naveed Aslam Khan Lodhi etc (WP.65282/24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Ipsa Loquitur: Negligence in Civil Suit
records.heading: Res ipsa loquitur permits an inference of negligence only on its stated conditions
records.text: Res ipsa loquitur permits an inference of negligence where the event ordinarily does not occur without negligence, the instrumentality was in the defendant's exclusive control, and there is no evidence of how it happened. Proof of an accident alone is not proof of negligence, and a claim that a vehicle was mechanically unfit must be proved by specific evidence. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 661, PLJ 2025 Lah 632; Mst. Misbah Farooq etc v. M/s Daewoo Pakistan Express Bus Service Ltd etc (R.F.A.1123-14).
records.title: Mst. Misbah Farooq etc v. M/s Daewoo Pakistan Express Bus Service Ltd etc (R.F.A.1123-14)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Judicial System
records.heading: Supreme Court judgment on the use of artificial intelligence in the judicial system
records.text: Detailed Supreme Court judgment, arising from rent proceedings, on the use of artificial intelligence in the courts. The headings cover AI for judicial and administrative efficiency, gaps in AI systems, AI and fair trial, a note of caution on judging with AI, and the continuing role of mediation and ADR. The post gives no specific holdings. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 582; Ishfaq Ahmed v. Mushtaq Ahmed (C.P.L.A. No. 1010-L/2022).
records.title: Ishfaq Ahmed v. Mushtaq Ahmed (C.P.L.A. No. 1010-L/2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Certiorari Against Family Court Orders
records.heading: Certiorari lies against Family Court orders only for jurisdictional error or clear error of law
records.text: Under Art. 199(1)(a)(ii) the High Court may issue certiorari to correct jurisdictional errors of Family Courts and first appellate courts, including orders made without hearing a party or against natural justice. The jurisdiction is supervisory. The High Court cannot re-weigh evidence or sit as an appellate court, and relief lies only for a clear error of law on the face of the record. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 572, PLJ 2025 SC 572; Muhammad Shakeel and others v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and others (C.P.L.A. 4582/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Shakeel and others v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and others (C.P.L.A. 4582/2023)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Ss. 15 and 15-A SRPO: Personal Bona Fide Need
records.heading: A landlord seeking ejectment for personal need must prove good faith, failing which possession may be restored
records.text: A landlord seeking ejectment for personal bona fide need must prove good faith. Section 15-A SRPO maintains a check and balance between good faith and bad faith. Where ejectment is obtained on a false ground of personal need, possession of the premises may be restored to the tenant. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 612; Parveen Ara v. Muhammad Hanif.
records.title: Parveen Ara v. Muhammad Hanif

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Quantum Meruit and Administrative Acquiescence
records.heading: Quantum meruit under section 70 supports compensation; recovery of fifteen years' salary without fraud was disproportionate
records.text: The doctrine of quantum meruit, recognised by s. 70 of the Contract Act 1872, entitles a person to reasonable compensation for services rendered where the other party has enjoyed the benefit. Although termination for irregular appointment may be sustainable, a direction to recover fifteen years' salary without allegation or proof of fraud or mala fide was held disproportionate, inequitable and untenable. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 560; Shahbaz Latif v. DIG Pakistan Railways (C.P.L.A. 2646/2023).
records.title: Shahbaz Latif v. DIG Pakistan Railways (C.P.L.A. 2646/2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement Executed Under Custody: Coercion and Duress
records.heading: An agreement made in custody without free consent is voidable for coercion or duress
records.text: An agreement made while the party is in custody or detention may be treated as procured by coercion, duress or undue influence where free consent is absent. Such an agreement is voidable at the option of the affected party. A contract procured under duress is void, and any benefit received must be restored and the loss made good. Ref: Muhammad Zaffar Khan & another v. Syeda Shumaila Zaidi & others (C.A.209/2025, decided 08.05.2025); Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.
records.title: Muhammad Zaffar Khan & another v. Syeda Shumaila Zaidi & others (C.A.209/2025, decided 08.05.2025)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Maintainability Despite Pending Civil Proceedings
records.heading: A complaint on illegal dispossession is maintainable despite pending civil proceedings
records.text: The sessions court under the 2005 Act assesses whether illegal dispossession is made out and does not adjudicate complex questions of title. A complaint is maintainable while civil proceedings are pending, and summary dismissal solely for that reason is untenable unless the complaint is an abuse of process. Co-ownership of unpartitioned land does not bar inquiry into dispossession. Ref: Qaiser Jabbar v. Syed Mati Ullah Shah and others (Crl.P.L.A. 1121/2021, decided 08.08.2025); Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Qaiser Jabbar v. Syed Mati Ullah Shah and others (Crl.P.L.A. 1121/2021, decided 08.08.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Post-Arrest Bail, Non-Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC falls within the non-prohibitory clause, so post-arrest bail is the rule
records.text: An offence under s. 489-F PPC falls within the non-prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so bail is favourably considered as a rule and refused only in exceptional cases such as likelihood of abscondence, tampering with evidence or repetition of the offence. The amount involved is not an exception, and s. 489-F is not meant as a recovery mechanism. The post also notes that the offence required further probe. Ref: Aqeel Ahmed Khan v. The State thr. Federal P.G Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 960/2025, decided 12.08.2025); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Aqeel Ahmed Khan v. The State thr. Federal P.G Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 960/2025, decided 12.08.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotics
records.heading: No conviction can be recorded without evidence of safe custody and transmission of narcotics
records.text: Conviction cannot be recorded where there is no evidence of safe custody and transmission of the narcotic substances. Ref: Zahid Nawaz v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.L.A. 433/2025, decided 16.06.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Zahid Nawaz v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab and another (Crl.P.L.A. 433/2025, decided 16.06.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: May 9 Cases: Post-Arrest Bail to Imran Khan
records.heading: Supreme Court grants post-arrest bail in eight May 2023 FIRs against Imran Khan
records.text: The Supreme Court heard petitions against the Lahore High Court orders of 24.06.2025 refusing post-arrest bail in eight FIRs registered in May 2023, involving offences under the PPC read with s. 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997 and other laws. Per the Urdu headline, bail was granted in all eight cases, on bonds with one surety in each case. Ref: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1184/2025, decided 21.08.2025); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1184/2025, decided 21.08.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay of 14 Hours in Lodging FIR
records.heading: Unexplained delay of 14 hours in lodging an FIR suggests deliberation before registration
records.text: A delay of about 14 hours in reporting an occurrence, with the police station about nine miles away and no justifiable explanation, means that deliberations before lodging the FIR cannot safely be ruled out. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1339.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Torch Not Secured
records.heading: Night identification without a torch secured in investigation is accepted only with caution
records.text: Where the occurrence was at night and a torch was mentioned but none was secured in investigation, the eyewitnesses' claim to identify culprits with graphic detail can be accepted only with a lump of salt. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1339.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive: Consequences of Failure to Prove
records.heading: Once the prosecution sets up a motive it must prove it or bear the consequences
records.text: The prosecution need not prove motive in every case, but once it sets up a motive it must establish it. If it fails, the prosecution and not the defence must suffer the consequences. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1339.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Prosecution Witnesses
records.heading: Conduct of the complainant party contrary to normal human conduct casts doubt on their account
records.text: The conduct of the complainant party, given the numbers present, was contrary to normal human conduct. In the ordinary course, witnesses would not let the perpetrators go free after the killing of their loved ones. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1339.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Irreconcilable Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Irreconcilable ocular and medical evidence is resolved in favour of the accused
records.text: When ocular and medical evidence are in material conflict and cannot be harmonised, the inconsistency is resolved in favour of the accused, who receives the benefit of the doubt. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1391; Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 22010/22).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 22010/22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 76 QSO: Secondary Evidence
records.heading: Non-compliance with Article 76 QSO on secondary evidence vitiates the findings below
records.text: Failure to comply with Art. 76 QSO on secondary evidence vitiates the evidentiary basis of the findings of the courts below and calls for intervention by the Supreme Court. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1307; Sher Asfandyar Khan v. Neelofar Shah and others (C.A.1843/2019).
records.title: Sher Asfandyar Khan v. Neelofar Shah and others (C.A.1843/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 and 2 CPC: Withdrawal for Formal Defect
records.heading: Withdrawal with liberty to refile requires a genuine formal defect not going to the root of the case
records.text: Withdrawal of a suit with liberty to file afresh requires a genuine formal defect, such as misdescription of parties, incorrect valuation or technical procedural errors that do not affect the merits. Defects going to the root of the case are not formal. Plaintiffs could not identify any such defect, and the Supreme Court declined to interfere with the High Court. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1066.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Interested Witness: Meaning and Scope
records.heading: An interested witness is one interested in the accused's conviction for an ulterior motive
records.text: An interested witness is one who is interested in the conviction of the accused for some ulterior motive. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1123.

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: S. 6 Juvenile Justice System Act 2018: Bail of Juveniles
records.heading: Bail of juveniles under section 6 of the 2018 Act, including release after six months' detention
records.text: Section 6 of the 2018 Act governs bail of juveniles. Under s. 6(4), a juvenile over sixteen arrested for a heinous offence may be refused bail where reasonable grounds exist to believe involvement. Under s. 6(5), even in heinous offences the juvenile must be released if detained continuously for over six months, trial is incomplete and he is not responsible for the delay. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1279; Muhammad Latif alias Kala v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 1629-B of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Latif alias Kala v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 1629-B of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Last Opportunity: Enforcement Under O. XVII R. 3 CPC
records.heading: A last opportunity to produce evidence must be enforced under Order XVII Rule 3 CPC
records.text: The practice of granting 'last opportunity', then 'absolute last opportunity', is deprecated. Where a last opportunity to produce evidence is granted with a warning of consequences, the court must enforce its order, using O. XVII R. 3 CPC, to check adjournments on frivolous grounds and restore confidence in the system. Ref: 2025 MLD 1201; Raza Khan v. Malik Muhammad Munir (R.F.A. 42140 of 2022).
records.title: Raza Khan v. Malik Muhammad Munir (R.F.A. 42140 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Husband Accused of Killing Wife: Onus
records.heading: Where a wife dies in the husband's house, part of the onus shifts to him but the prosecution's remains
records.text: Where a wife dies an unnatural death in the husband's house, part of the onus shifts to him to explain the circumstances. However, the initial onus remains on the prosecution, and where all other prosecution evidence is unreliable the accused cannot be convicted on supposition merely because he did not discharge part of that onus. Ref: 2025 YLR 1934.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 161 CrPC: Delay in Recording Witness Statement
records.heading: A belated section 161 CrPC statement of a witness casts serious doubt on the prosecution version
records.text: Recording the statement of a witness under s. 161 CrPC at a belated stage casts serious doubt on the prosecution version. Ref: 2025 YLR 1934.

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 489-F and 406 PPC: Simultaneous Charge; Mistaken Credit
records.heading: Sections 489-F and 406 PPC may be charged together; mistaken bank credit may amount to entrustment
records.text: Offences under ss. 489-F and 406 PPC may be charged together. Money credited to a bank account by mistake is normally not entrustment under s. 405 PPC unless there is dishonest intention. Here the petitioner was bound to return the funds to the bank, and by using them dishonestly he caused wrongful gain to himself and wrongful loss to the bank. Ref: 2025 LHC 5337; Tariq Rehman Chohan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 43725/25, decided 18.08.2025); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Tariq Rehman Chohan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 43725/25, decided 18.08.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail: Hardened, Desperate or Dangerous Criminal
records.heading: A desperate criminal for statutory bail is judged on the mode and manner of the offence
records.text: A person seeking bail on the statutory ground may be treated as a desperate criminal on the basis of the mode and manner of the offence. Relying on Shakeel Shah's case, the phrase denotes a person likely to injure others without caring for consequences and posing a serious threat if released. The court may consider previous record and the gravity of the offence. Ref: 2025 LHC 5332; Aqsa Noureen alias Asima Bibi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 34187/25, decided 18.08.2025); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Aqsa Noureen alias Asima Bibi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 34187/25, decided 18.08.2025)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: S. 52 Land Revenue Act: Presumption of Truth
records.heading: Entries in the record of rights carry a presumption of truth under section 52
records.text: Under s. 52 of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Act 1967, a presumption of truth attaches to entries in the record of rights and periodical records. Ref: 2025 CLC 1456.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Further Investigation After Accepted Cancellation Report
records.heading: No further investigation is permitted once the Magistrate accepts a cancellation report
records.text: Once a cancellation report has been prepared and agreed to by the Magistrate, no further investigation can be carried out, as no criminal case remains in the field, and a transfer of investigation is of no legal effect. Magistrates dealing with remand or pre-trial matters must examine the record closely so that their orders do not legitimise an illegality. Ref: 2025 LHC 5342; Muhammad Sarfraz v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 764-B-25, decided 27.02.2025); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Sarfraz v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. 764-B-25, decided 27.02.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings is permitted at any stage on just terms to decide the real controversy
records.text: Order VI R. 17 CPC permits amendment at any stage on just terms to determine the real questions in controversy. Illustrative factors include the applicant's intention, limitation, avoidance of injustice to the opponent, avoidance of multiplicity of litigation, the nature of the suit and cause of action, and whether the subject matter of the suit remains unchanged. Ref: 2025 CLC 1439; Maqbool Ahmad v. Addl. District Judge and others (Writ Petition No. 4183 of 2022).
records.title: Maqbool Ahmad v. Addl. District Judge and others (Writ Petition No. 4183 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 100 QSO: Presumption for Old Documents
records.heading: Courts should apply the Article 100 QSO presumption to old documents with great care
records.text: Courts should be very careful in applying the presumption under Art. 100 QSO 1984 to old documents produced in suits asserting proprietary rights. The court may in its discretion refuse the presumption where evidence in proof of the document has been produced and disbelieved. Ref: 2025 CLC 1497; Muhammad Ramzan v. Muhammad Sharif (deceased) and Others (Civil Revision No. 65806 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Muhammad Sharif (deceased) and Others (Civil Revision No. 65806 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII R. 3 CPC: Conditional Leave to Defend
records.heading: Failure to meet conditions of leave to defend nullifies the leave and warrants a decree
records.text: The court may grant leave to defend under O. XXXVII R. 3(2) CPC subject to conditions, as a matter of discretion. If the defendant fails to comply with the conditions, the leave is nullified and he cannot defend the suit on any ground, so the court passes a decree for the plaintiff on the facts and documents before it. Ref: 2025 CLC 1580; Muhammad Irsalan Faraz v. Habib Ul Rehman (Civil Revision No. 609 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Irsalan Faraz v. Habib Ul Rehman (Civil Revision No. 609 of 2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Interference With Concurrent Findings
records.heading: Concurrent findings are not disturbed in constitutional jurisdiction absent patent illegality on the record
records.text: Concurrent findings of courts of competent jurisdiction are not interfered with in constitutional jurisdiction unless patent illegality appears on the face of the record. The High Court exercises restraint over orders passed in revisional jurisdiction and intervenes only for perversity or legal infirmity resulting in failure of justice. The petitioner failed to show any illegality. Ref: 2025 CLC 1599; Adeel Khaleel v. Shahid Hassan (Writ Petition No. 3048 of 2018).
records.title: Adeel Khaleel v. Shahid Hassan (Writ Petition No. 3048 of 2018)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345(2A) CrPC and S. 311 PPC: Honour Offences Compromise
records.heading: Life imprisonment under section 311 PPC remains compulsory for honour offences even after compromise
records.text: Section 345(2A) CrPC governs whether a compromise in an honour-related offence may be accepted, while s. 311 PPC governs the penal consequence. Even after a compromise is accepted, life imprisonment under s. 311 PPC remains compulsory if the offence was committed in the name of honour. Where fasad-fil-arz is not attracted and the compromise is genuine and voluntary, the court may acquit. Ref: 2025 LHC 4536; Jamshed and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 36924/J/2022).
records.title: Jamshed and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 36924/J/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Offence Punishable with Three Years: Non-Cognizable
records.heading: An offence punishable with exactly three years is non-cognizable, so no FIR can be registered
records.text: Under Schedule II Cr.P.C., an offence under another law punishable exactly with three years is deemed non-cognizable and bailable unless the special statute provides otherwise. As the Anti-Rape Act does not make s. 22 cognizable, an FIR cannot be registered under it, and the Additional Sessions Judge was not authorised to direct registration. Impugned direction set aside. Ref: 2025 LHC 4030; Syed Rizwan Haider v. The Additional Sessions Judge etc. (W.P. 1142/2025, decided 27.05.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Syed Rizwan Haider v. The Additional Sessions Judge etc. (W.P. 1142/2025, decided 27.05.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cognizability of s. 22 Anti-Rape Act: Schedule II
records.heading: Section 22 of the Anti-Rape Act is cognizable as Schedule II covers three years and upward
records.text: The State's review was allowed after verification showed that Schedule II CrPC reads offences punishable with imprisonment for 03 years and upward but less than 07 years as cognizable, so the earlier finding of non-cognizability of s. 22 of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act 2021 rested on a misprinted text. The order of 27.05.2025 was recalled and the Sessions Judge's direction restored. Ref: The State through Prosecutor General Punjab v. Syed Rizwan Haider SI (Review Petition No. 10 of 2025 in Writ Petition No. 1142 of 2025), decided 02.07.2025; Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: The State through Prosecutor General Punjab v. Syed Rizwan Haider SI (Review Petition No. 10 of 2025 in Writ Petition No. 1142 of 2025), decided 02.07.2025

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 345(2A) CrPC and S. 311 PPC: Honour Offences Compromise
records.heading: Life imprisonment under section 311 PPC remains compulsory for honour offences even after compromise
records.text: Section 345(2A) CrPC governs whether a compromise in an honour-related offence may be accepted, while s. 311 PPC governs the penal consequence. Even after a compromise is accepted, life imprisonment under s. 311 PPC remains compulsory if the offence was committed in the name of honour. Where fasad-fil-arz is not attracted and the compromise is genuine and voluntary, the court may acquit. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1480; Jamshed and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 36924/J/2022).
records.title: Jamshed and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 36924/J/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Reinvestigation After Discharge; S. 182 PPC Proceedings
records.heading: Police may reinvestigate despite discharge, and section 182 PPC proceedings cannot run during a complaint case
records.text: Police may reinvestigate a matter despite an order of discharge. While a complaint case is pending, proceedings under s. 182 PPC in a criminal case on the same subject matter cannot be initiated. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1566; Muhammad Qaswar Hussain v. Judicial Magistrate etc. (ICA Criminal 292-24).
records.title: Muhammad Qaswar Hussain v. Judicial Magistrate etc. (ICA Criminal 292-24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Framing of Charge: Scope of Material Considered
records.heading: At the charge stage the court asks whether strong suspicion exists, not whether guilt is proved
records.text: At the stage of framing charge the court considers only material collected in investigation which can be legally translated into evidence. The judge is not a post office and must sift the material, but cannot assess its probative value and treats the prosecution material as true. The question is whether a strong suspicion of an offence exists, not final proof of guilt. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1555; Shiraz Ahmad v. State (Crl. Revision No. 39743 of 2024).
records.title: Shiraz Ahmad v. State (Crl. Revision No. 39743 of 2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Ingredients of Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust under section 406 PPC requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation
records.text: Criminal breach of trust under s. 406 PPC requires entrustment by a person reposing confidence, and dishonest misappropriation, conversion, use or disposal of the property in violation of law or contract. 'Entrust' bears its legal meaning, and the accused must hold the property in a fiduciary capacity otherwise than for himself. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1543; Majid Ali v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 12913-B of 2025).
records.title: Majid Ali v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 12913-B of 2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Theft: Physical Possession and Co-Ownership
records.heading: For theft, physical possession is the key and co-ownership does not stifle investigation
records.text: For the offence of theft, physical possession is the key point. Civil rights or co-ownership are not a valid ground to stifle a criminal investigation or to discharge the accused where the complainant had peaceful, uninterrupted and long physical possession. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1535; Khan Muhammad v. Judicial Magistrate etc. (WP 782-25).
records.title: Khan Muhammad v. Judicial Magistrate etc. (WP 782-25)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Arbitration Act 1940: S. 20 Application Not Convertible to S. 8
records.heading: An application under section 20 of the Arbitration Act cannot be treated as one under section 8
records.text: The trial court erred in treating an application under s. 20 of the Arbitration Act 1940 as one under s. 8, as they belong to different regimes. Under s. 8 the court is functus officio after appointing the arbitrator, whereas under s. 20 it must first determine existence of the agreement, then order its filing and make the reference under sub-s. (4). The matter was remanded to be decided afresh. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 848; Bilal Siddique v. Muhammad Naeem (F.A.O. 46205/24).
records.title: Bilal Siddique v. Muhammad Naeem (F.A.O. 46205/24)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording Statement of Injured Witness
records.heading: Recording an injured witness's statement after a month despite fitness is fatal for the prosecution
records.text: Where the Medical Officer records that the injured was well oriented and gave a history at the hospital, recording the statement of the injured witness by the Investigating Officer after about one month is fatal for the prosecution. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 645; Karamat Ali v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 5394/22).
records.title: Karamat Ali v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 5394/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: FIR: Information Narrated to Police but Recorded Later
records.heading: Information narrated immediately but recorded later is not an FIR in the strict sense
records.text: Where the complainant narrates the full occurrence to a police official immediately but the FIR is recorded later on a written application or statement taken elsewhere, it is not an FIR within s. 154 CrPC in the strict sense and carries no weight as a promptly recorded FIR. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 635; Ali Raza v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 33146/22).
records.title: Ali Raza v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 33146/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Place of Occurrence: Blood-Stained Earth Report
records.heading: The place of occurrence is not proved without a report confirming human blood on the earth
records.text: Where there is no report confirming that earth secured from the place of occurrence was stained with human blood, the place of occurrence is not proved in the strict sense. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 635; Ali Raza v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 33146/22).
records.title: Ali Raza v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 33146/22)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Welfare of Minor as Best Interests of the Child
records.heading: Welfare of the minor under section 17 means the best interests of the child
records.text: The phrase 'welfare of the minor' in s. 17 of the Guardians and Wards Act 1890 must be read as the 'best interests of the child' under Art. 3 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. The child's right to be heard under Art. 12 is read into the inquiry, so that the child participates in proceedings according to age and maturity. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 597, PLD 2026 SC 238; Dr. Muhammad Asiif v. Dr. Sana Sattar and others (C.R.P. 458/2024, decided 16.05.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Dr. Muhammad Asiif v. Dr. Sana Sattar and others (C.R.P. 458/2024, decided 16.05.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery Witness, Medical Evidence and Motive
records.heading: A recovery witness cannot corroborate his own account, and medical evidence cannot identify the assailant
records.text: No one can corroborate his own version, so a recovery witness cannot corroborate his own ocular account. Medical evidence is supportive only and cannot establish the identity of the assailant. Motive is a double-edged weapon which may equally be a reason for false implication. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 635; Ali Raza v. State (Crl. A. No. 33146 & M.R. No. 155 of 2022).
records.title: Ali Raza v. State (Crl. A. No. 33146 & M.R. No. 155 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Firearm Injuries: Discrepancy in Number and Locale
records.heading: Discrepancy in the number and location of firearm injuries cannot be emphasised strictly
records.text: A witness cannot be expected to give a photographic account of a firearm occurrence, as the bullet strikes before its sound is heard. In the confusion of firing, discrepancy regarding the number and location of injuries cannot be emphasised in the strict sense. Ref: 2025 YLR 2472, PLJ 2025 CrC 703; Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. A. No. 39441-J & M.R. No. 163 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. A. No. 39441-J & M.R. No. 163 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint: Mens Rea and Issue of Process
records.heading: A complainant must disclose actus reus and mens rea before process issues on a private complaint
records.text: A complainant must disclose both actus reus and mens rea. Before issuing process the court must satisfy itself that sufficient grounds exist, as examination of the complaint under s. 200 CrPC protects the public from false and vexatious complaints. Admission of the private complaint was held a misuse of the process of law. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 667; Muhammad Ashraf etc. v. ASJudge etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 17582 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf etc. v. ASJudge etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 17582 of 2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 53-A Transfer of Property Act: Part Performance
records.heading: Part performance under section 53-A requires a written contract and a transferee ready and willing to perform
records.text: Section 53-A requires a written contract for transfer of immovable property for consideration, possession taken or retained in part performance, and some act in furtherance of the contract. The transferee must be completely and unconditionally ready and willing to perform his part, and a person who refuses to honour his commitments cannot claim the protection. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 905; Muhammad Irshad v. Muhammad Ramzan (R.F.A. No. 206 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Irshad v. Muhammad Ramzan (R.F.A. No. 206 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 491 CrPC: Habeas Corpus Principles and Orders
records.heading: Under section 491 CrPC a major in illegal detention must be set at liberty forthwith
records.text: On finding illegal or improper detention under s. 491 CrPC, the court may hand a minor to the guardian, while a major must be set at liberty forthwith. The status quo ante cannot be restored against the detenue's wishes, as that would offend Art. 9. The post also lists settled principles, including that habeas corpus is a writ of right. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 193; Sultan Ahmad v. District Police Officer etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 54755/H/2021).
records.title: Sultan Ahmad v. District Police Officer etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 54755/H/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Right of Cross-Examination and Defence Counsel at State Expense
records.heading: The right to cross-examine is part of fair trial, with counsel appointed at State expense if needed
records.text: The right to cross-examine is part of fair trial, and cross-examination by the accused himself cannot substitute for that by counsel. No CrPC provision allows the court to cut off this right, but where the accused deliberately avoids producing his lawyer, the court may appoint defence counsel at State expense and proceed with the trial. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 191; Muhammad Tariq and 6 others v. State (Crl. Rev. No. 292 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Tariq and 6 others v. State (Crl. Rev. No. 292 of 2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Recovery: Family Court Jurisdiction Over Non-Spouses
records.heading: Family Court jurisdiction depends on the subject matter, not the identity of the parties
records.text: Jurisdiction of the Family Court depends on the subject matter of the suit under the Schedule to the Family Courts Act 1964, and does not depend on the identity of the parties. A suit for recovery of dowry articles against the ex-husband's brother and wife was therefore maintainable, and the decree against them stood. The post also distinguishes necessary and proper parties. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 572; Muhammad Shakeel and others v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and others (C.P.L.A. 4582/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Shakeel and others v. Additional District Judge, Faisalabad and others (C.P.L.A. 4582/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Court Fees Act 1870: Strict Construction
records.heading: The Court Fees Act 1870 is construed strictly, with substantial justice preferred over technicality
records.text: The Court Fees Act 1870, like other fiscal legislation, is construed strictly. Its purpose is to secure revenue for the State and it does not give litigants a technicality to burden adversaries. A balance is struck between the State's interest in fees and fairness, with substantial justice preferred over technical compliance. Ref: Province of Punjab through the District Collector, Bhakkar v. Muhammad Chiragh, etc (C.P.L.A. 385-L/2021, decided 22.08.2025); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Province of Punjab through the District Collector, Bhakkar v. Muhammad Chiragh, etc (C.P.L.A. 385-L/2021, decided 22.08.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence Application
records.heading: An additional evidence application in appeal may be decided with the appeal depending on the facts
records.text: No rule requires an application for additional evidence at the appellate stage to be decided by a separate order before the main appeal. Whether to decide it first or together with the appeal depends on the facts of each case and the need for a complete adjudication. Where the evidence could affect the outcome, a conjoint decision promotes judicial economy. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 704.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Wife's Maintenance Not Conditional on Rukhsati
records.heading: A Muslim wife's right to maintenance is not conditional on rukhsati
records.text: The right of a Muslim wife to maintenance flows unconditionally from solemnization of a valid marriage and is a binding legal duty. Rukhsati is a customary practice with no independent legal status under Islamic or statutory law, so maintenance cannot be made conditional on it. Ref: Ambreen Akram v. Asad Ullah Khan etc. (Civil Petition No. 1107-L of 2015 and Civil Appeal No. 247-L of 2017, decided 11.09.2025).
records.title: Ambreen Akram v. Asad Ullah Khan etc. (Civil Petition No. 1107-L of 2015 and Civil Appeal No. 247-L of 2017, decided 11.09.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Murder: Accused Who Clasped the Deceased
records.heading: An accused who clasped the deceased while co-accused stabbed him shared the common intention
records.text: An accused who clasped the deceased and so made him helpless while co-accused inflicted two fatal knife blows shared the common intention. Sections 34, 35 and 37 PPC were attracted with s. 302 PPC, and there were prima facie grounds to connect him with the offence. Bail was refused. Ref: 2008 MLD 547.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Accused Who Raised Lalkara
records.heading: Bail for an accused who raised a lalkara is not automatic where he dominated the co-accused
records.text: An accused alleged to have shouted Lalkara is generally granted bail, but this is not an inflexible rule. The court tentatively considers the background, his interest in the crime and his influence over co-assailants under s. 497(1) CrPC. Where the accused dominated his co-accused and ignited the situation, bail was refused and the petition dismissed. Ref: 2021 PCrLJ 47.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Further Investigation or Transfer After Framing of Charge
records.heading: Further investigation or transfer after charge is ordered sparingly in exceptional cases only
records.text: Further investigation, reinvestigation or transfer of investigation must not be ordered routinely or merely because a party is dissatisfied with the Investigating Officer. It may be ordered sparingly in exceptional cases, such as where basic elements of the offence were not investigated, new evidence emerged, a proclaimed offender was arrested, or vital defects in the investigation are shown. Ref: 2025 LHC 5459; Maryam Bibi v. The State etc. (WP 45328/25, decided 26.08.2025); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Maryam Bibi v. The State etc. (WP 45328/25, decided 26.08.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Reaction to Injuries to Family: Mitigation of Sentence
records.heading: Firing in reaction to injuries to father and brother mitigates sentence to life imprisonment
records.text: Relying on the maxim that no one should gain advantage from his own wrong, where the accused may have fired on seeing his father and brother injured, and the deceased was hit as a result, this is a mitigating factor justifying imprisonment for life rather than death. Ref: 2025 MLD 1404, PLJ 2025 CrC 585.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Change of Venue of Occurrence; Identification Parade
records.heading: A change of venue of injury by the prosecution is fatal, and a parade without facial details is ineffective
records.text: If the prosecution changes the venue where the deceased received injuries during trial, it is fatal to its case. Where identification of an unknown accused rests on external appearance, an identification parade without details of facial features has no legal efficacy. Ref: 2025 MLD 1448, PLJ 2025 CrC 602; Yasir Shaban v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 39118/21).
records.title: Yasir Shaban v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 39118/21)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint: Ingredients and S. 200 CrPC Examination
records.heading: A private complaint must state every ingredient of the offence, and process needs a prima facie case
records.text: A complaint must state facts showing every ingredient of the offence, including actus reus and mens rea. Before issuing process the court must be satisfied that sufficient grounds exist, as examination under s. 200 CrPC protects the public from false and vexatious complaints, and process cannot issue without a prima facie case. Ref: 2025 MLD 1589.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Bail Not Universal Rule
records.heading: Bail in section 489-F PPC cases is normal but not a universal rule
records.text: An offence under s. 489-F PPC does not attract the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC and bail is normally allowed. It is not a rule of universal application, each case turns on its circumstances, and bail may be refused in exceptional circumstances even outside the prohibitory clause. Ref: 2025 MLD 1577, PLJ 2025 CrC 481.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Liability of Surety Limited to Attendance
records.heading: A surety's liability is limited to ensuring the accused's attendance and ends on appearance
records.text: The responsibility of a surety is limited to ensuring the accused's attendance in the case for which the bond was given. Once the accused appears before the court, the surety's liability ends and the matter lies between the court and the accused. Ref: 2025 MLD 1565; Kameer Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 13684/22).
records.title: Kameer Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 13684/22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of CDR: Photocopy Without Company Witness
records.heading: Call data records proved only by photocopy without a company witness are inconsequential
records.text: Prosecution evidence of call data records was held inconsequential where only a photocopy was produced, with no company officer or attested CDR, no permission for secondary evidence, no proof of SIM ownership, no CDR of the appellant's own SIM and no transcript of conversation with the alleged hired assassins. Ref: Sikandar Ali Lashari v. The State thr. PG Sindh (Crl.A. 343/2023, decided 10.09.2025).
records.title: Sikandar Ali Lashari v. The State thr. PG Sindh (Crl.A. 343/2023, decided 10.09.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 154 CrPC: Refusal or Delay in Registering FIR
records.heading: Refusal or delay in registering an FIR breaches the officer's statutory duty under section 154 CrPC
records.text: The Supreme Court noted the widespread refusal or delay in registering FIRs contrary to the statutory duty of the officer in charge of a police station under s. 154 CrPC, especially for vulnerable classes. Registration is an executive function and breach has serious consequences. The judgment was directed to the Secretary Interior and Chief Secretaries. The headline also refers to chance witnesses.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence as Corroborative Evidence
records.heading: Abscondence is only corroborative and cannot alone sustain a conviction
records.text: Abscondence is not proof of guilt in itself but can be taken as corroborative evidence. Without trustworthy and confidence-inspiring substantive incriminating evidence, conviction cannot rest solely on abscondence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1408; Fateh Khan v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.A. 379/2021).
records.title: Fateh Khan v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.A. 379/2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Interested Witness: Need for Independent Corroboration
records.heading: The testimony of an interested witness needs careful scrutiny and independent corroboration
records.text: The testimony of an interested witness must be scrutinised with care and caution, and independent corroboration is essential to test its validity and credibility. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1408; Fateh Khan v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.A. 379/2021).
records.title: Fateh Khan v. The State thr. P.G. Punjab & another (Crl.A. 379/2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Improbable Exact Details of Each Accused's Role
records.heading: Exact details of each accused's position and role in firing were held improbable and unnatural
records.text: The exact details in the FIR and trial testimony about the position of each nominated accused with specific firearms and the specific role of each in firing at each deceased were held highly improbable and unnatural in such an occurrence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1408; Fateh Khan v. State (Crl. Appeal No 379 of 2021).
records.title: Fateh Khan v. State (Crl. Appeal No 379 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness: Stamp of Injury and Credibility
records.heading: The stamp of a firearm injury does not by itself lend credence to a witness's testimony
records.text: The mere stamp of a firearm injury on a prosecution witness does not by itself lend credence to his testimony. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1408; Fateh Khan v. State (Crl. Appeal No 379 of 2021).
records.title: Fateh Khan v. State (Crl. Appeal No 379 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light and Identification
records.heading: The source of light must be proved for night identification, and inconsistent accounts create doubt
records.text: For an unseen night-time occurrence at about 11:48 p.m. with no substantial moonlight, the source of light enabling identification of fleeing accused had to be proved. The witnesses gave inconsistent accounts of the source (bulb, torch), creating doubt about identification. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1599; Khair Muhammad and other v. State (Crl.P. 132 of 2018).
records.title: Khair Muhammad and other v. State (Crl.P. 132 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wife Killed in Husband's House: Onus to Explain
records.heading: Where a wife dies in the husband's house, absence of explanation and abscondence were considered
records.text: The prosecution bears the burden of proof, but where a vulnerable dependent wife dies an unnatural death in the husband's house, part of the onus shifts to him to explain the circumstances. Absence of explanation, together with his abscondence for about 37 days and failure to report or attend the last rites, was considered. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1591; Muhammad Ijaz v. State (Crl. Appeal No 345 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz v. State (Crl. Appeal No 345 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Evidence Not Put to Accused
records.heading: Evidence not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used against him
records.text: Evidence not put to the accused in his statement under s. 342 CrPC, so as to give him a chance to explain it, cannot be used against him. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1558; Obaid Ullah v. The State (JP 14 & 17 of 2020).
records.title: Obaid Ullah v. The State (JP 14 & 17 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recovery From Open and Accessible Place
records.heading: A recovery from an open and accessible place is unsafe to rely on
records.text: Reliance on a recovery made from an open and accessible place is unsafe, because it cannot be said that the recovery was effected from the exclusive possession of the accused. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1442; Usman Ahmed v. The State (Crl.A. 566/2020).
records.title: Usman Ahmed v. The State (Crl.A. 566/2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification Parade After Prior Sight of Accused
records.heading: Identification proceedings have no value if the accused may have been seen by the witness earlier
records.text: Where the accused may have been seen by the identifying witness before the test identification parade, the identification proceedings carry no evidentiary value. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1442; Usman Ahmed v. The State (Crl.A. 566/2020).
records.title: Usman Ahmed v. The State (Crl.A. 566/2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Eyewitnesses and Substitution of Culprit
records.heading: Related eyewitnesses are not discredited by relationship, as substituting the real culprit is improbable
records.text: Substituting the real culprit with an innocent person, particularly where close relatives are killed in front of family members, is improbable. Absent mala fide or ulterior motive, consistent and confidence-inspiring eyewitness testimony cannot be discredited merely because the witnesses are related to the deceased. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1427; Altaf Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 507 of 2023).
records.title: Altaf Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 507 of 2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302(c) PPC: Sudden Fight and Excess of Self-Defence
records.heading: A sudden quarrel without premeditation justified section 302(c) PPC and a reduced sentence
records.text: The occurrence arose at the spur of the moment without premeditation. Firing at an unarmed deceased exceeded the bounds of self-defence, but the lack of premeditation and the sudden quarrel justified treatment under s. 302(c) PPC. The sentence was reduced to rigorous imprisonment for fourteen years, with the compensation direction left intact. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1572; Amir Khan v. The State (J.P. 149/2018).
records.title: Amir Khan v. The State (J.P. 149/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blank Recovery Memos, Inquest Report and Malkhana Entry
records.heading: Blank recovery memos, a deficient inquest report and a missing malkhana entry raise reasonable doubt
records.text: A trial court should be inquisitorial in searching for truth. Recovery memos leaving the accused's name blank raise reasonable doubt that the accused was not yet finalised, an inquest report lacking the occurrence details suggests the story was not finalised, and a missing malkhana entry for re-deposit of case property casts doubt on recovery and safe custody. Ref: 2025 LHC 5669; Muhammad Imtiaz etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 24423/22, decided 08.09.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Imtiaz etc. v. The State (Jail Appeal 24423/22, decided 08.09.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 265-D and 265-K CrPC: Framing of Charge and Acquittal
records.heading: Chapter XXII-A CrPC is mandatory, and the power to acquit under section 265-K needs utmost caution
records.text: Chapter XXII-A CrPC is mandatory. Section 265-D requires the trial court to consider, at minimum, the FIR, the s. 173 report, accompanying documents and witness statements before framing charge. The power to acquit under s. 265-K must be exercised with utmost caution and careful application of mind to the facts of the case. Ref: State v. Dawood Jan (Cr.A No. 454-P of 2018, decided 25.06.2025).
records.title: State v. Dawood Jan (Cr.A No. 454-P of 2018, decided 25.06.2025)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Bar Association Notice Barring Advocates From Appearing
records.heading: A Bar Association notice barring advocates from appearing offends legal ethics and Article 10A
records.text: A notice of DBA Mardan dated 10.05.2025 directing advocates to abstain from representing the complainant was held to strike at legal ethics and the independence of the Bar, to obstruct justice and to offend the fair trial right under Art. 10A. The judgment was sent to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Bar Council and Bar Associations. Ref: Shabir v. The State (T.A No. 34-P of 2025, decided 20.06.2025).
records.title: Shabir v. The State (T.A No. 34-P of 2025, decided 20.06.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Quo Warranto Against Judge: Interim Order Suspended
records.heading: Supreme Court suspends the Islamabad High Court order in a quo warranto matter against a judge
records.text: Petitioner's counsel relied on Malik Asad Ali (PLD 1998 SC 161) that quo warranto lies against a superior court judge but no interim order can be passed. The Supreme Court issued notice, including to the Attorney General under O. XXVII-A CPC, and suspended operation of the Islamabad High Court order of 16.09.2025 meanwhile. Ref: Justice Tariq Mehmood Jahangiri v. Mian Dawood, Advocate High Court and others (C.P.L.A. No. 4247/2025, decided 29.09.2025).
records.title: Justice Tariq Mehmood Jahangiri v. Mian Dawood, Advocate High Court and others (C.P.L.A. No. 4247/2025, decided 29.09.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Marriage of a 15-Year-Old Girl: Islamabad Child Marriage Act
records.heading: A 15-year-old married girl allowed to stay with her husband; marriage below 18 remains an offence
records.text: The Islamabad High Court allowed a 15-year-old girl, who wished to stay with her husband, to live with him. Child marriage is not void in Shariah, but marriage below 18 is an offence under the Islamabad Child Marriage Restraint Act 2025. The court made recommendations on harmonising laws, nikah registrar duties and NADRA age verification. Ref: Muhammad Riaz v. Learned District & Sessions Judge (East) Islamabad, etc. (W.P. No. 2494 of 2025); Justice Azam Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Learned District & Sessions Judge (East) Islamabad, etc. (W.P. No. 2494 of 2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Trial of Offences Under S. 195(1)(a) CrPC
records.heading: A Judge or Magistrate cannot try section 195 offences committed before himself under section 487 CrPC
records.text: Offences under ss. 172 to 188 PPC are ordinarily tried under Chapter XX CrPC on a complaint.
