Under s. 487 CrPC, a Judge or Magistrate other than a High Court Judge must not try s. 195 offences committed before himself. The conviction under s. 174 PPC was set aside, as a thing required to be done in a particular manner must be done in that manner. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1730, PLJ 2025 CrC 264; Muhammad Asif Atta v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 40068/20).
records.title: Muhammad Asif Atta v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 40068/20)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Parallel Civil and Criminal Proceedings: Postponement
records.heading: The trial court may postpone a criminal case where a civil dispute over the Nikah Nama is pending
records.text: There is no bar to simultaneous civil and criminal proceedings on the same matter. Where criminal liability depends on civil proceedings and a bona fide claim is hard to separate from a criminal act, the trial court may postpone the criminal case. As the Nikah Nama was in civil dispute, the trial court should not finalise the case before the civil and family cases. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1798, PLJ 2025 CrC 483; Abida Siddique v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 6881/25).
records.title: Abida Siddique v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 6881/25)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: S. 11 PECA with Ss. 295-A to 298-C PPC: Trial Forum
records.heading: Section 11 PECA and blasphemy offences under the PPC are triable by the court under section 44
records.text: Offences under s. 11 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 and ss. 295-A, 295-B, 295-C and 298-C PPC are interlinked and are triable by the court under s. 44(1) of that Act. Section 196 CrPC does not apply to proceedings before a court under a special statute inconsistent with it. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1791; Shiraz Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 39709/24).
records.title: Shiraz Ahmad v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 39709/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 44 CrPC: Medical Officer's Duty to Inform Police
records.heading: A medical officer must inform the police of a medico-legal case under section 44 CrPC
records.text: Under s. 44 CrPC, a medical officer attending an injured person must inform the police of the arrival of a medico-legal case. Failure may lead to prosecution under s. 187 or s. 202 PPC. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1664; Waqas Viki v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 59064/20).
records.title: Waqas Viki v. The State etc. (Jail Appeal 59064/20)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 405 PPC Illustration (f): Misappropriating Article Entrusted for Delivery
records.heading: Misappropriating an article entrusted for delivery attracts illustration (f) to section 405 PPC
records.text: Where the accused obtains an article to carry and deliver to another person but misappropriates it instead, illustration (f) to s. 405 PPC applies and the offence of criminal breach of trust, punishable under s. 406 PPC, is attracted. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1751; Sohail v. SHO PS Saddar Gujranwala etc. (WP 13839/25).
records.title: Sohail v. SHO PS Saddar Gujranwala etc. (WP 13839/25)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: No Apprehension of Arrest
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail requires a reasonable apprehension of mala fide arrest, absent where the IO says arrest is unneeded
records.text: The sine qua non for pre-arrest bail is a reasonable apprehension of arrest motivated by mala fide or ulterior motives. Where the Investigating Officer said arrest was not required, the court should have disposed of the application on that stance without confirming bail on merits. The respondents were left free to apply afresh if arrest became necessary. Ref: 2025 LHC 5784; Muhammad Ishaque v. Zafar Iqbal etc. (Crl. Misc. 36163/25, decided 25.09.2025); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Ishaque v. Zafar Iqbal etc. (Crl. Misc. 36163/25, decided 25.09.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Circumstance Not Put to Accused
records.heading: A circumstance not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used for conviction
records.text: A piece of evidence or circumstance not put to the accused when recording his statement under s. 342 CrPC cannot be considered against him for conviction. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1633; Ghulam Mustafa v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 23/2020).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 23/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Belated Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: A belated amendment introducing a new factual assertion without justification cannot be allowed
records.text: Order VI R. 17 CPC allows amendment at any stage but with caution and to further justice. An amendment introducing a new factual assertion after inordinate delay, without justification and prejudicing the opposing party, cannot be allowed, and such requests need heightened scrutiny. In a suit on an oral agreement, the petitioners' conduct did not merit indulgence. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 691; Muhammad Arif Tarar v. Matloob Ahmad Warraich and others (C.P.L.A. 746-L/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Arif Tarar v. Matloob Ahmad Warraich and others (C.P.L.A. 746-L/2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay Bail: Third and Fourth Provisos, S. 497(1) CrPC
records.heading: The third proviso to section 497(1) CrPC confers a right to bail on trial delay, subject to the fourth proviso
records.text: The 3rd proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC creates a right to bail on delay in conclusion of trial when its conditions are met, subject to the three exceptions in the 4th proviso. The ground rests solely on delay, and an accused charged with a death-punishable offence becomes entitled on continuous detention exceeding the stipulated period. Ref: Noor Agha v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 27-K of 2025).
records.title: Noor Agha v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 27-K of 2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Hardened, Desperate or Dangerous Criminal: 4th Proviso S. 497 CrPC
records.heading: The hardened criminal exception differs from the merits test, so refusal on merits does not bar delay bail
records.text: The exception of a hardened, dangerous or desperate criminal in the 4th proviso is distinct from the merits test under s. 497(1) CrPC. Bail refused on merits does not bar a fresh claim on statutory delay. The three words are disjunctive, and the prosecution must show the accused is not an ordinary criminal but a substantial risk of harm to others. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1679; Noor Agha v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 27-K of 2025).
records.title: Noor Agha v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 27-K of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Closure of Evidence After Adjournments
records.heading: The court may close evidence under Order XVII Rule 3 CPC after repeated adjournments and default
records.text: The petitioner's Illegal Dispossession Act complaint and later civil suit, with appeals, were dismissed. He sought repeated adjournments and failed to produce evidence, and the court may proceed under O. XVII R. 3 CPC despite default. The Supreme Court did not interfere with the concurrent findings of the three courts below. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1702.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Sale Deed Denied by Elderly Illiterate Lady: Burden of Proof
records.heading: An elderly illiterate woman denying a registered sale deed need not prove fraud; beneficiaries prove genuineness
records.text: Where an elderly illiterate woman denied executing a registered sale deed, she was not required to prove fraud, and the beneficiaries had to establish the genuineness of the transaction. The presumption for a registered deed is rebuttable. The High Court judgment was set aside and the trial and district court decrees restored. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1694; Mst. Rahim Khatoon v. Muhammad Yasin (Civil Appeal No. 671-L of 2013).
records.title: Mst. Rahim Khatoon v. Muhammad Yasin (Civil Appeal No. 671-L of 2013)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Meaning of 'Post' and 'Vacancy'
records.heading: A post is a position in a cadre, while a vacancy is a vacant post available for appointment
records.text: Post' denotes the number of posts in a cadre, whether filled or vacant. 'Vacancy' means a vacant post available for appointment through recruitment or promotion, arising on creation of a post or on retirement, death, resignation or removal of the incumbent.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Methamphetamine Samples
records.heading: Gaps in safe custody and transmission make the Chemical Examiner's report unsafe for conviction
records.text: In a case of 1800 grams of methamphetamine, gaps and contradictions in safe custody and transmission, including non-examination of the police official who took the property to the station, and missing chain-of-custody registers, made the Chemical Examiner's report unsafe as the sole basis for conviction. Appeal allowed. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1644.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody of Charas: Unproduced Constable
records.heading: Non-production of the constable who carried charas samples to the laboratory raises doubt on chain of custody
records.text: In a recovery of 20 kilograms of charas, the constable who carried the 1640 sample parcels to the laboratory was not produced and no reason was given. This raised serious doubt on the chain of custody, and the benefit went to the appellants as of right. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1730; Farman Ali v. State.
records.title: Farman Ali v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 498 CrPC: Pre-Arrest Bail Where Post-Arrest Bail Would Follow
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail should not be refused where post-arrest bail would follow
records.text: Where the court concludes that on dismissal of pre-arrest bail the accused would be entitled to post-arrest bail, it is futile to refuse pre-arrest bail and send the accused to prison. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1613.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Reserved Seats Review Petitions: Detailed Judgment
records.heading: Detailed judgment on reserved seats review petitions, with dissenting notes by two Justices
records.text: Detailed 47-page judgment on the reserved seats review petitions, with dissenting notes by Justices Ayesha Malik and Aqeel Abbasi. Per the Urdu summary, review petitions can be heard only by a constitutional bench, and they were allowed in the short order of 27 June. Ref: Pakistan Muslim League through its President Lahore v. Sunni Ittehad Council through its Chairman, Faisalabad and others (C.R.P. 312/2024); Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan; Justice Ayesha A. Malik; Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Pakistan Muslim League through its President Lahore v. Sunni Ittehad Council through its Chairman, Faisalabad and others (C.R.P. 312/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: New Grounds Not in Memo of Petition
records.heading: A party cannot argue a new ground not raised in the memo of petition without court permission
records.text: A party cannot be allowed to argue a new ground that was not raised in the memo of petition, unless the court specifically permits it to do so. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 685.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Additional Evidence at Appellate Stage
records.heading: Additional evidence in appeal cannot be claimed as of right and reasons must be recorded
records.text: Production of additional evidence in appeal cannot be claimed as of right. It is for the court to decide whether a document or witness is required to enable it to pronounce judgment or for any other substantial cause, and where permission is allowed the court must record reasons. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 685.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Deciding Additional Evidence Application Before Appeal
records.heading: An appellate court must decide an additional evidence application before the appeal, but remand may serve no purpose
records.text: The appellate court is duty bound to decide an application for additional evidence before deciding the appeal. If it fails to do so, remand serves no fruitful purpose where the party has failed to prove any nexus with the suit property or justify its possession. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 685.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: Doctrine of Merger of Decree
records.heading: The trial court decree merges into the appellate decree, and execution is governed by section 48 CPC
records.text: When a superior court decides an appeal, whether it affirms, modifies or sets aside, the trial court decree merges into the appellate decree. A fresh execution petition for the appellate decree is governed by s. 48 CPC, so limitation runs six years from the appellate decree and Art. 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908 does not apply. High Court order allowing execution upheld. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 698.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Dismissal for Non-Prosecution After Framing of Issues
records.heading: After issues are framed a suit may be dismissed for non-prosecution if the plaintiff is absent
records.text: Once issues are framed a suit becomes ripe for hearing, and the court may dismiss it for non-prosecution if the plaintiff is absent on a date fixed for evidence. Appearance dates before settlement of issues are distinct from dates of hearing. Dismissal and refusal of restoration were upheld. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 718.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Intra Court Appeal: Maintainability Where Other Remedy Exists
records.heading: An intra court appeal is barred where the governing law provides an appeal, revision or review
records.text: If the law governing the original proceedings provides a remedy of appeal, revision or review, an Intra Court Appeal before the High Court is barred. It is immaterial whether the aggrieved person actually availed that remedy; legal availability of the remedy is what matters. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 713.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Sole Testimony of Victim and Consent
records.heading: A reliable sole victim's testimony suffices for conviction, and fearful passive submission is not consent
records.text: The sole testimony of a victim of sexual abuse, if independent, unbiased, straightforward and reliable, suffices for conviction. Caution and corroboration linking the accused to the offence are needed where enmity or prior grudge exists. Passive submission out of fear, without physical resistance, cannot be treated as consent. Ref: PLD 2025 Islamabad 357.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Revision Dismissed in Default: Restoration under s. 561-A
records.heading: A revision dismissed in default may be restored under section 561-A CrPC on sufficient cause
records.text: A revision dismissed for non-appearance may be restored under s. 561-A CrPC if sufficient cause is shown with particulars, and restoration does not offend s. 369 CrPC as it is not a decision on merits. A second revision against the same order is not maintainable. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 731.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qatl-i-Amd: Failure to Prove Motive
records.heading: If the prosecution fails to prove its asserted motive, life imprisonment is invariably awarded instead of death
records.text: The prosecution need not set up a motive, but if it does and fails to prove it, it suffers the consequences. Where guilt is established but the asserted motive is not proved, the accused is invariably awarded imprisonment for life instead of the death penalty. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 737.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Media Interviews of Accused in Custody Prohibited
records.heading: Law enforcement agencies must not permit media interviews of accused in custody
records.text: Law enforcement agencies must not permit or facilitate media interviews, especially confessional statements, of accused in custody, as this violates dignity and fundamental rights and prejudices a fair trial. Violation is misconduct to be proceeded against by law, and heads of agencies bear responsibility for compliance. The court also called for regulation of the media and deprecated humiliation of citizens at checkpoints. Ref: 2025 LHC 5858; Vishal Ahmad Shakir v. Federation of Pakistan (Misc. Writ 80758/23, decided 10.09.2025); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Vishal Ahmad Shakir v. Federation of Pakistan (Misc. Writ 80758/23, decided 10.09.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: s. 497(1) CrPC: Maximum Punishment Determines Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Where a range of punishment is prescribed, the maximum governs the prohibitory clause of section 497(1)
records.text: Where a statute prescribes a range of punishment (here 9 to 14 years), the maximum punishment prescribed by law is to be considered for the purpose of s. 497(1) CrPC. Ref: The State v. Gul Nawab and another (Crl.P.L.A. 150-K/2024, decided 02.10.2025); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: The State v. Gul Nawab and another (Crl.P.L.A. 150-K/2024, decided 02.10.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry, Gravity of Offence and Rule of Consistency
records.heading: Gravity of the offence alone does not justify refusing bail where further inquiry is needed
records.text: Gravity of the offence alone does not justify refusing bail where the evidence, on tentative assessment, creates doubt and the case requires further inquiry; bail is not to be withheld as punishment. The rule of consistency applies where the accused has the same role as a co-accused already granted bail, after proper evaluation of each role. Ref: Kashif Tanveer v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 562-L of 2025, decided 09.07.2025).
records.title: Kashif Tanveer v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 562-L of 2025, decided 09.07.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Complainant Casts Doubt on Presence
records.heading: A complainant father's unnatural conduct during a brutal attack makes his presence doubtful
records.text: A complainant father who did not intervene, was not injured and made no effort to rescue his son during a brutal attack acted contrary to natural human conduct, which makes his presence at the spot doubtful. Falsus in uno is not applied rigidly, but where evidence has been disbelieved against co-accused with identical roles, the same standard applies to the appellant absent independent corroboration. Ref: User Daraz v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 32-1/2021, decided 25.09.2025).
records.title: User Daraz v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 32-1/2021, decided 25.09.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Individual Criminal Responsibility; No Family Liability
records.heading: Criminal liability is individual and family ties do not transmit accountability
records.text: Criminal liability is individual and family ties do not transmit accountability. A parent is not criminally liable for a crime of an adult child, nor a child for the father's crime, unless complicit through aiding or abetting. Collective or family liability is rejected because actus reus and mens rea attach to the person who acted. Ref: Khadim Hussain v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 974/2025, decided 21.08.2025).
records.title: Khadim Hussain v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 974/2025, decided 21.08.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Old Exceptions to s. 300 PPC and New s. 302(c)
records.heading: Cases within the old exceptions to section 300 PPC fall under the new section 302(c)
records.text: Cases covered by the exceptions to the old s. 300 PPC read with old s. 304 PPC were intended to be dealt with under the new clause (c) of s. 302 PPC. Ref: Asif Hussain v. The State (Jail Petition No. 644 of 2017, decided 18.09.2025).
records.title: Asif Hussain v. The State (Jail Petition No. 644 of 2017, decided 18.09.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absence of Post-Mortem Not Always Fatal
records.heading: Absence of a post-mortem is not always fatal where death from the accused's act is proved
records.text: Absence of a post-mortem is not always fatal to the prosecution if it is proved beyond doubt that death resulted from the accused's act. Examples given are a body thrown into a canal in the presence of eyewitnesses, and a decomposed or burnt body with reliable eyewitness evidence and external medical examination. Ref: Rasool Bakhsh v. The State (Jail Petition No. 296 of 2018, decided 24.09.2025).
records.title: Rasool Bakhsh v. The State (Jail Petition No. 296 of 2018, decided 24.09.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvement and Withholding of CCTV Evidence
records.heading: A witness who dishonestly improves his statement is unreliable, and withholding CCTV footage is held against the prosecution
records.text: A prosecution witness who dishonestly improves his statement on material aspects, or to match the medical evidence, is not worthy of reliance. The prosecution's failure to produce a court report or CCTV footage to prove the petitioners' presence at the spot amounted to withholding an important piece of evidence. Ref: Azhar Iqbal and others v. The State (Criminal Petition Nos. 189, 92-L of 2020 & 1810-L of 2019, decided 02.10.2025).
records.title: Azhar Iqbal and others v. The State (Criminal Petition Nos. 189, 92-L of 2020 & 1810-L of 2019, decided 02.10.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sole Eye-Witness and Blackening of Entry Wound
records.heading: A confidence-inspiring sole eyewitness can support conviction, and marginal blackening may occur at long range
records.text: Quality and not quantity of evidence weighs with the courts, and a confidence inspiring sole eye-witness can safely support conviction. Blackening alone at the margins of an entry wound, without burning, charring or tattooing, may occur even from a long range shot. Ref: Qaisar v. The State (Jail Petition No. 940 of 2017, decided 22.09.2025).
records.title: Qaisar v. The State (Jail Petition No. 940 of 2017, decided 22.09.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Photocopy Documents: Arts. 75 and 76
records.heading: A photocopy has no probative value without proof under Articles 75 and 76 QSO
records.text: A photocopy has no probative value without proof through primary or legally recognised secondary evidence. A document placed on record subject to admissibility must have its authenticity established under Arts. 75 and 76 QSO, and a party must prove its own claim and cannot rely on deficiencies in the opponent's case. Ref: PLD 2025 Sindh 386.

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Scope of IDA 2005 in Family Property Disputes
records.heading: The Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 reaches any forcible intruder but should not criminalise ordinary family disputes
records.text: The Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 is a special penal statute that reaches any person who forcibly intrudes on a lawful owner's or occupier's property intending to dispossess, not only land mafias, if the statutory ingredients are made out. It must be applied so as to deter abuse without criminalising ordinary family disputes, which are better resolved by other remedies. Ref: Abbas Asif Zaman and another v. The State and others (Criminal Petition No. 61-K of 2025, decided 15.10.2025).
records.title: Abbas Asif Zaman and another v. The State and others (Criminal Petition No. 61-K of 2025, decided 15.10.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11(a) CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A plaint is rejected under Order VII Rule 11(a) only if it discloses no cause of action
records.text: A plaint can be rejected under O. VII R. 11(a) CPC only where it does not disclose a cause of action, and only its contents are examined and not the defence. A plaint showing a legal injury, an enforceable right and sufficient factual foundation cannot be rejected summarily. Ref: 2025 MLD 1621; Sajjad Haider etc. v. Syed Ali Rizwan Kazmi etc. (WP-307-21).
records.title: Sajjad Haider etc. v. Syed Ali Rizwan Kazmi etc. (WP-307-21)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Entries and Limited Estate of Female Heirs
records.heading: Mutation entries are not conclusive, and limited estates of female heirs terminate under the Shariat Act
records.text: Under s. 42 of the Land Revenue Act, 1967 no witnesses are required for reporting or entering a mutation, and mutation entries are not conclusive evidence of the facts recorded, so the date of death entered has no evidentiary value. Under ss. 3 and 5 of the West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1962 limited estates of female holders terminate and the property devolves on the sharai heirs. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 914, 2025 MLD 1795.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Circumstantial Evidence in Capital Cases
records.heading: Conviction in a capital case may rest on circumstantial evidence forming a complete unbroken chain
records.text: Conviction, including a capital sentence, may rest solely on circumstantial evidence if it forms a complete and unbroken chain inconsistent with innocence, linking the accused to the offence. If any link is missing the chain is broken and no conviction can be recorded. The death sentence of Zahir Zakir Jaffar was maintained. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 168, PLD 2026 SC 251; Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 467/2023).
records.title: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 467/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage as Primary Evidence: Silent Witness Theory
records.heading: CCTV footage is primary evidence admissible without corroboration if it passes the two-fold test
records.text: CCTV footage is digital evidence and primary evidence, admissible without corroboration if it passes the two-fold test laid down in Ahmad Omar Sheikh. The silent witness theory allows recorded evidence as substantive proof of what it depicts without an eye-witness, with reference to Art. 164 QSO. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 168, PLD 2026 SC 251; Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 467/2023).
records.title: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 467/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Indolent Litigant: Closing of Evidence
records.heading: An indolent litigant given repeated chances cannot be allowed to prolong the matter
records.text: The petitioner was given more than sufficient opportunities and warnings, including last and final chances, to produce evidence but ignored them. An indolent person cannot be allowed to play with the court's process and prolong the matter, because law favours the vigilant and not the indolent. Ref: 2025 SCMR 624, PLJ 2025 SC 643; Muhammad Asim v. Dr. Abdul Hamid Jan and others (C.P.L.A. 277-Q/2024); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Asim v. Dr. Abdul Hamid Jan and others (C.P.L.A. 277-Q/2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 17(2)(a) QSO: Attestation and Promissory Note
records.heading: The attestation requirement of Article 17(2)(a) QSO does not apply to a promissory note
records.text: The requirement of attestation of a document under Art. 17(2)(a) QSO does not apply to a promissory note. Ref: 2025 SCMR 653, PLJ 2025 SC 621; Muhammad Adnan v. Salah-ud-Din (C.P.L.A. 1618/2024); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Adnan v. Salah-ud-Din (C.P.L.A. 1618/2024)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: High Court Cannot Act as Family Court in Writ
records.heading: In a writ the High Court cannot act as a Family Court or decree a suit
records.text: In exercise of constitutional jurisdiction under Art. 199 the High Court cannot arrogate to itself the powers of a family court, substitute its own findings on merits for those of the courts below, or decree a suit. The petition was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 649; Maqbool Ali and another v. Mst. Raheela and others (CPLA No. 1106 of 2024, decided 13.05.2025); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui; Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Maqbool Ali and another v. Mst. Raheela and others (CPLA No. 1106 of 2024, decided 13.05.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Mediation in Maintenance Dispute
records.heading: Mediation reduces cost and delay, and a maintenance dispute was settled after seven years of litigation
records.text: The Supreme Court highlighted the benefits of mediation, which reduces costs, eases the burden on courts and gives quicker resolution, noting a settlement reached in about five weeks after over seven years of litigation. The petition was disposed of in terms of the settlement agreement and the family court was directed to draw up a decree. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 661; Muhammad Naseer Butt v. Additional District Judge, Lahore etc. (C.P.L.A. No. 3519 of 2021, decided 06.05.2025); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui; Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Muhammad Naseer Butt v. Additional District Judge, Lahore etc. (C.P.L.A. No. 3519 of 2021, decided 06.05.2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Time as Essence and Clean Hands
records.heading: Where time is of the essence, the vendee's default and unclean hands defeat specific performance
records.text: Where time was of the essence and both parties understood it, with consequences of non-performance set out in the agreement, the vendee's default within the stipulated time is fatal to a suit for specific performance. The High Court correctly held that the vendee had not come with clean hands. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 685, 2026 SCMR 36; Muhammad Ashraf Anjum v. Sabir Hussain and others (C.A. No. 239-L of 2018, decided 02.07.2025); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf Anjum v. Sabir Hussain and others (C.A. No. 239-L of 2018, decided 02.07.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Review: Earlier Suit Withdrawn Unconditionally
records.heading: Review allowed because the earlier suit was withdrawn unconditionally with liberty to refile
records.text: The review application under O. XLVII R. 1 CPC was allowed because the earlier finding relied on a different withdrawal order. The earlier suit was withdrawn with liberty to file afresh without any condition as to costs. The review judgment was set aside and the appeal remanded to the Single Judge for decision on merits. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 946, 2026 YLR 436; Mst. Bakhan etc. v. Pir Bakhsh etc. (Rev. Appln. No. 3 of 2015 in R.S.A. No. 59 of 1989, decided 19.06.2025); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad; Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains.
records.title: Mst. Bakhan etc. v. Pir Bakhsh etc. (Rev. Appln. No. 3 of 2015 in R.S.A. No. 59 of 1989, decided 19.06.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Eye-Witness Testimony Requires Strict Scrutiny
records.heading: Injured eyewitness testimony needs strict scrutiny, and an injured witness does not always speak the truth
records.text: A FIR registered after consulting a legal brain is viewed with suspicion. Injury to an eye-witness supports his presence but is not conclusive of the truth of his testimony, and the maxim that an injured witness seldom lies is an overstatement where there are several assailants. The death sentence of one convict was not confirmed and the appeal was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 732; Malik Muhammad Imran and others v. State and others (Crl. As. Nos. 63397, 1005, 1200, Crl. Rev. No. 64108 & M.R. No. 134 of 2019, decided 06.05.2025); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Abher Gul Khan.
records.title: Malik Muhammad Imran and others v. State and others (Crl. As. Nos. 63397, 1005, 1200, Crl. Rev. No. 64108 & M.R. No. 134 of 2019, decided 06.05.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eye-Witnesses Failing to Identify Dead Body
records.heading: Eyewitnesses' failure to identify the dead body makes the prosecution case highly doubtful
records.text: Eye-witnesses' failure to identify the dead body suggests they were not present at the scene or did not accompany the deceased to hospital, making the prosecution case highly doubtful. Medical evidence is only corroborative of injuries, weapon and time and does not reveal the identity of the murderer. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 762; Muhammad Arshad etc. v. State and others (Crl. A. No. 78244 of 2023, decided 24.06.2025); Justice Aalia Neelum; Justice Abher Gul Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Arshad etc. v. State and others (Crl. A. No. 78244 of 2023, decided 24.06.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Narcotics: Acquittal
records.heading: A broken chain of safe custody and transmission of methamphetamine led to acquittal
records.text: In a case of 1800 grams of methamphetamine under s. 9(c) CNSA, the police official who conveyed the murasila and case property was not examined, the Moharrir received parcels without a receipt and Register No. 19 was not produced. The chain of safe custody and transmission was broken, the petition was converted into an appeal and the accused was acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 157; Zakir Ali v. The State (J.P. No. 343 of 2023, decided 24.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar; Justice Salah Huddin Panhwar; Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Zakir Ali v. The State (J.P. No. 343 of 2023, decided 24.04.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 512 CrPC: Evidence of Absconder and No Sine Die Adjournment
records.heading: Prosecution evidence may be recorded against an absconder under section 512 CrPC, and no sine die adjournment is allowed
records.text: Under s. 512(1) CrPC evidence of prosecution witnesses may be recorded in the absence of an absconding accused, read with Arts. 46 and 47 QSO, once the court is satisfied of abscondence and no imminent prospect of arrest. There is no bar on recording evidence in the accused's absence and a Court of Session cannot adjourn a case sine die. Ref: 2025 LHC 6151; Muhammad Khaliq v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 53163/25, decided 07.10.2025); Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar.
records.title: Muhammad Khaliq v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 53163/25, decided 07.10.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: FIR: Doubtful Time and Place of Recording
records.heading: An FIR is vitiated where the time and place of recording the statement are not established
records.text: Where the prosecution could not establish with exactness the time and place of recording the complainant's statement and of bringing the injured to hospital, and there is no explanation, the FIR is vitiated and the prosecution case built on it is bound to fall. Ref: 2025 YLR 2472, PLJ 2025 CrC 703; Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. A. No. 39441-J & M.R. No. 163 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. A. No. 39441-J & M.R. No. 163 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness and Dishonest Improvements
records.heading: An injured witness is not necessarily truthful, and dishonest improvements make him unreliable
records.text: An injured witness is not necessarily truthful and cannot be believed merely because of the stamp of injuries on his body. A witness who introduces dishonest improvement or omission to strengthen the case cannot be relied upon. Ref: 2025 YLR 2472, PLJ 2025 CrC 703; Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. A. No. 39441-J & M.R. No. 163 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. A. No. 39441-J & M.R. No. 163 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Evidentiary Value under Art. 46 QSO
records.heading: A dying declaration is admissible under Article 46 QSO but needs corroboration to found a conviction
records.text: A dying declaration is admissible under Art. 46 QSO with no prescribed mode of recording, but is a weaker type of evidence needing corroboration. Conviction can rest on it when fully corroborated by reliable evidence, and it must be truthful, free from coercion and supported by surrounding circumstances including medical evidence of the declarant's capacity. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1876; Rajesh v. The State (Jail Petition No. 243/2023).
records.title: Rajesh v. The State (Jail Petition No. 243/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in s. 489-F PPC: Non-Prohibitory Clause
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC falls in the non-prohibitory clause and bail is favourably considered as a rule
records.text: Offences under s. 489-F PPC fall within the non-prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, so bail is favourably considered as a rule and refused only in exceptional cases such as abscondence, tampering or repetition. The amount involved is not an exception, and s. 489-F is not meant as a tool for recovery. No exceptional circumstances were found to deny post-arrest bail. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1955; Aqeel Ahmed Khan v. The State through Federal P.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 960/2025).
records.title: Aqeel Ahmed Khan v. The State through Federal P.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 960/2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement Executed in Custody: Coercion and Duress
records.heading: An agreement made in custody without free consent is voidable for coercion or duress
records.text: An agreement made under custody or detention may be treated as made under coercion, duress or undue influence if free consent is absent, and is voidable at the option of the person in custody. A contract procured under duress requires restoration of benefits received and making good of loss. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1961; Muhammad Zaffar Khan and another v. Syeda Shumaila Zaidi and others (C.A. 209/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Zaffar Khan and another v. Syeda Shumaila Zaidi and others (C.A. 209/2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Rule of Consistency Applies Only to Equal Cases
records.heading: The rule of consistency applies only where the applicant's case is at par with the bailed accused
records.text: The rule of consistency applies only when the case of the person seeking bail is at par with that of the accused who has already been granted post-arrest bail. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1967; Ghazi Arab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1425/2024).
records.title: Ghazi Arab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1425/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Co-Accused Confession at Bail Stage
records.heading: A co-accused's confession may be tentatively assessed at the bail stage only if independently corroborated
records.text: The evidentiary value of a co-accused's confessional statement is for the trial court to determine at the proper stage. At the bail stage a tentative assessment of it is permissible only if it is corroborated by independent incriminating material on record. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1967; Ghazi Arab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1425/2024).
records.title: Ghazi Arab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1425/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail in Prohibitory Clause: Exceptions
records.heading: In the prohibitory clause, post-arrest bail is limited to the first and third provisos and section 497(2)
records.text: In the prohibitory clause, post-arrest bail is limited to the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC (woman, minor, sick or infirm), the third proviso (unreasonable trial delay not attributable to the accused) and s. 497(2) (further inquiry). Deeper scrutiny of the material at the bail stage is unwarranted, and tentative assessment prima facie connected the petitioner with the offence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1967, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 119; Ghazi Arab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1425/2024).
records.title: Ghazi Arab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1425/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 12(2) CPC and O. IX R. 13 CPC: Scope
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC applies to fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction, distinct from Order IX Rule 13
records.text: Authority on when an application under s. 12(2) CPC lies and when one under O. IX R. 13 CPC lies. Section 12(2) provides a remedy against a judgment, decree or order obtained by fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction, with specific particulars required under O. VI R. 4 CPC, and extends to any aggrieved person. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1936; M/s Mobiserve Pakistan (Pvt) Limited v. M/s V-Tech and others (C.P.L.A. 3824/2023).
records.title: M/s Mobiserve Pakistan (Pvt) Limited v. M/s V-Tech and others (C.P.L.A. 3824/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence Tests; Recovery on Joint Pointation
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain, and joint pointation weakens recovery value under Article 40
records.text: Circumstantial evidence must be fully established, consistent only with guilt and form a complete chain excluding every other hypothesis. Recovery of a dead body on the joint pointation of the accused significantly weakens its value under Art. 40 QSO. Benefit of doubt was given to the accused. Ref: Osama v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 63-Q/2024, decided 18.07.2025).
records.title: Osama v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 63-Q/2024, decided 18.07.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 195 CrPC: Forgery of Document Used in Civil Proceedings
records.heading: Section 195 CrPC applies only to forgery of a document after its production in court
records.text: Section 195 CrPC is attracted only when the enumerated offences are committed concerning a document after it has been produced or given in evidence in a court proceeding. A document allegedly forged and used in civil proceedings, where the offence preceded its production, does not attract the bar merely because the civil matter is pending. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 403, 2025 PCrLJ 1983; Rasoolan Bibi v. The State etc. (WP 82843/23).
records.title: Rasoolan Bibi v. The State etc. (WP 82843/23)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: s. 7(1) IDA: Interim Relief Only During Trial
records.heading: Interim relief under section 7(1) of the Illegal Dispossession Act is available only after charge is framed
records.text: Interim relief under s. 7(1) of the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 can be granted only during the trial, which begins with framing of the charge and not with cognizance. An order directing the accused to hand over possession as interim relief disregarded this stage and was set aside, and the revision was allowed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1919; Muhammad Afzal v. The State etc. (Criminal Revision No. 63117 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Afzal v. The State etc. (Criminal Revision No. 63117 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: FIR Not Signed by Medical Officer at Post-Mortem
records.heading: An FIR not signed by the Medical Officer at post-mortem suggests ante-timed registration
records.text: If the FIR was not signed by the Medical Officer at the time of post-mortem examination, it leads to the conclusion that the FIR had not yet been recorded and was prepared later with an ante-time entry. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1816; Master Riaz Ahmed etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 14068/19).
records.title: Master Riaz Ahmed etc. v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 14068/19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Purpose of Sentence: Deterrence in Multiple Murders
records.heading: Deterrence justifies no leniency for appellants who murdered three innocent persons
records.text: Punishment serves deterrence and reformation, and appellants who murdered three innocent persons deserve no leniency. A lenient view in such proved cases would endanger peace and let hardened criminals escape. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1877; Muhammad Arshad etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 923-24).
records.title: Muhammad Arshad etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 923-24)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Recovery of Weapon Not a Mitigating Circumstance
records.heading: Non-recovery of the weapon is not a mitigating circumstance where ample other evidence exists
records.text: Non-recovery of the weapon of offence on the appellant's pointing out cannot be a mitigating circumstance where ample other evidence exists. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1877; Muhammad Arshad etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 923-24).
records.title: Muhammad Arshad etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 923-24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 340(2) CrPC: Accused Not Entering Witness Box
records.heading: No adverse inference arises from an accused's failure to testify under section 340(2) CrPC
records.text: No adverse inference arises from an accused's failure to testify under s. 340(2) CrPC. On the circumstances of this case the appellant was the best witness to establish the factual position he asserted. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1877; Muhammad Arshad etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 923-24).
records.title: Muhammad Arshad etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal 923-24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Discharge by Magistrate at Remand Stage Set Aside
records.heading: A Magistrate cannot discharge the accused at the remand stage where a custodian complained
records.text: The Magistrate discharged the accused when police sought physical remand, although the complaint was by a Superdar appointed under revenue procedure as custodian of the crops. The discharge orders were set aside, and the matter is deemed pending before the Magistrate for fresh orders. The case involved ss. 63, 167 and 561-A CrPC. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1971; Saif Ali v. The State etc. (Writ Petition No. 7272 of 2025).
records.title: Saif Ali v. The State etc. (Writ Petition No. 7272 of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Four-Stage Proportionality Test in Administrative Action
records.heading: Proportionality is a four-step test applied to administrative and disciplinary decisions
records.text: Proportionality is a four-step test: legitimate aim, suitability, necessity (no less restrictive alternative) and a fair balance between impact on rights and public interest. The Supreme Court has adopted it for administrative and disciplinary decisions, and it must be applied with care where fundamental rights and dignity are at stake. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1916; Muhammad Niaz Khan v. R.P.O. (C.P.L.A. 2283-L/2016).
records.title: Muhammad Niaz Khan v. R.P.O. (C.P.L.A. 2283-L/2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Postmortem and Medical Opinion
records.heading: Delay in post-mortem was inconsequential, but an unreasoned medical opinion on timing cannot be preferred over ocular evidence
records.text: A delay of about 16 to 26 hours in conducting the postmortem was held inconsequential. The medical opinion on the time between injury and death and between death and postmortem was inconsistent with injuries to major blood vessels and unsupported by any reason, so it was ipse dixit and could not be preferred over the ocular account. Ref: 2025 YLR 2472; Muhammad Arif v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Uncertain DNA Report on Alleged Weapon
records.heading: An uncertain DNA report on the alleged weapon leaves the accused's involvement doubtful
records.text: The Forensic Science Agency was not certain that the accused's DNA was present on the iron bar alleged to be the weapon, so that part of the prosecution evidence was doubtful regarding his involvement. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2025 YLR 2372.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Single Accused in Murder Charge: Substitution
records.heading: Conviction of a single accused in murder needs unimpeachable evidence with confidence-inspiring corroboration
records.text: Substitution of a single accused is rare, but a conviction on a charge against a single accused requires circumstantial or ocular evidence of unimpeachable character with confidence inspiring corroboration. The court must assess the intrinsic worth of prosecution evidence and not treat it as gospel truth. Ref: 2025 YLR 2372.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Complainant's Presence at Spot Not Proved
records.heading: The complainant's presence at the spot was not proved, and the FIR could not corroborate
records.text: The complainant's presence was not proved where the eye-witness said he reached the hospital and was told of the occurrence, the FIR was chalked out over two hours after a daylight incident, and the scriber was not produced. The FIR could come on record by secondary evidence after the complainant's death but could not be corroborative evidence. Ref: 2025 YLR 2242.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: FIR Delay of 2 Hours 25 Minutes: Ante-Timing
records.heading: Inquest report silent on time of occurrence suggests the FIR was ante-timed
records.text: Although the FIR was registered within 2 hours 25 minutes, the inquest report did not mention the time of occurrence, which showed the Investigating Officer did not know the time then. This indicated that the FIR was not registered at the time stated. Ref: 2025 YLR 2242.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Autopsy
records.heading: Unexplained delay of eight hours in autopsy is fatal and suggests a cooked-up story
records.text: An unexplained delay of about eight hours in conducting the autopsy, and in submitting police papers to the Medical Officer, is considered fatal to the prosecution case and indicates that the story was cooked up after procuring false eye-witnesses. Ref: 2025 YLR 2242.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses Living 15 Kilometres Away
records.heading: Eyewitnesses living 15 kilometres away without explanation are suspect chance witnesses
records.text: Both eye-witnesses lived 15 or 16 kilometres from the place of occurrence and gave no plausible explanation for their presence, which made them chance witnesses whose depositions are suspect and were discarded. Ref: 2025 YLR 2242.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eye-Witnesses Not Proved
records.heading: Presence of eyewitnesses is not proved where supporting material was not secured and the record conflicts
records.text: Presence of the eye-witnesses was not proved where no cricket equipment, blood-stained clothes or blood-stained earth were secured, and the medico-legal certificate named the deceased's son as the accompanying person although he was not named in the FIR or the witnesses' statements. Ref: 2025 YLR 2492.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Accused Waiting for Arrival of Witnesses Unnatural
records.heading: A claim that the accused waited for the witnesses to arrive is unnatural
records.text: The witnesses' claim that the occurrence took place exactly when they arrived, with the accused waiting for them, is unnatural and contrary to human conduct. The court held that the witnesses were not present and had not witnessed the occurrence. Ref: 2025 YLR 2270.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Closely related eyewitnesses who made no effort to save the deceased acted unnaturally
records.text: Three closely related eye-witnesses who made no effort to save the deceased or restrain an unarmed woman accused acted contrary to natural human conduct. This showed that the deceased was at the assailant's mercy and with no one present to save her. Ref: 2025 YLR 2270.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Agreement: Art. 79 and Art. 84 QSO
records.heading: A document is proved under Article 79 QSO, and the court may compare signatures under Article 84
records.text: Civil cases are decided on preponderance of evidence. A document is proved under Art. 79 QSO, and omission to produce the scribe is not always fatal where attesting witnesses confirm its contents. Art. 84 QSO allows the court to compare signatures, writing or seals and direct any person present to write for comparison. Ref: 2025 LHC 6371; Ali Ahmed v. Zulfiqar Ali (Civil Revision 714-17, decided 15.10.2025); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Ali Ahmed v. Zulfiqar Ali (Civil Revision 714-17, decided 15.10.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 195 and s. 476 CrPC: Forgery in Judicial Proceedings
records.heading: For forgery in judicial proceedings the court may send a complaint or try summarily under section 476 CrPC
records.text: Section 195 CrPC is an exception to the general rule that anyone may set the law in motion and is read with s. 476 CrPC. When offences under s. 195(1)(b) and (c) occur in judicial proceedings, the court may either send a complaint to the competent court or itself proceed and try them summarily under s. 476 CrPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 6349; Agha Faisal Fayyaz v. State etc. (Crl. Revision 93-23, decided 24.09.2025); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Agha Faisal Fayyaz v. State etc. (Crl. Revision 93-23, decided 24.09.2025)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Lambardari State Land: No Proprietary Rights
records.heading: No proprietary rights in state land leased to Lambardars may be conferred under the notification
records.text: By Colonies Department notification dated 17.01.2006, issued in supersession of earlier instructions and still in force, no proprietary rights in state land leased to Lambardars are to be conferred on them. This extinguished the claim for such relief. Ref: 2025 LHC 6259; Muhammad Jahangir v. BOR etc. (WP. 3854-22, decided 23.10.2025); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Jahangir v. BOR etc. (WP. 3854-22, decided 23.10.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Forensic Opinion 'Probably' and s. 118 Presumption
records.heading: A forensic opinion that a signature is probably the respondent's is not conclusive without corroboration
records.text: A forensic opinion that a signature is only probably the respondent's is not conclusive and needs independent corroboration before adverse reliance. The court may inquire into the lender's financial capacity to advance the sum, relevant to rebuttal of the presumption under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Ref: 2025 LHC 6345; Liaqat Ali v. Liaqat Ali Shah (RFA. 8-13, decided 30.09.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. Liaqat Ali Shah (RFA. 8-13, decided 30.09.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Haq Mahr Recorded in Registered Nikah Nama
records.heading: A registered Nikah Nama recording Haq Mahr prevails over conjecture from a prior sale deed
records.text: A registered Nikah Nama recording the subject matter of Haq Mahr carries a presumption that prevails over conjecture drawn from a prior sale deed between the spouses, where there is no pleading or proof of prior discharge. The law does not bar a man from selling property to a woman he later marries. Ref: 2025 LHC 6341; Mst. Saima Rani v. ADJ etc. (WP.11759-24, decided 14.10.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mst. Saima Rani v. ADJ etc. (WP.11759-24, decided 14.10.2025)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: No Civil Court Challenge to Interlocutory Arbitral Orders
records.heading: Interlocutory orders of an arbitral tribunal cannot be challenged in the Civil Court
records.text: The Arbitration Act 1940 reflects minimal judicial intervention and gives no right to challenge interlocutory or procedural orders of the tribunal in Civil Court. A party aggrieved by delay, partiality or bias may seek removal of the arbitrator or umpire under s. 11 of the Act. Ref: 2025 LHC 6277; Lahore Development Authority v. M/s Zahir Khan & Brothers (Civil Revision 48106/25, decided 14.10.2025); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Lahore Development Authority v. M/s Zahir Khan & Brothers (Civil Revision 48106/25, decided 14.10.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Closure of Right to Evidence
records.heading: The trial court may close the right to evidence under Order XVII Rule 3 after repeated opportunities
records.text: After about ten opportunities and clear warnings, the trial court rightly closed the petitioner's right to produce evidence under O. XVII R. 3 CPC and decided on merits instead of dismissing under O. IX CPC. The object of the rule is to protect the process from dilatory tactics, and excessive adjournments were deprecated. Ref: Irfan Rasheed v. Zawar Muhammad Afzal and others (C.P.L.A. 3470/2025, decided 08.10.2025); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Irfan Rasheed v. Zawar Muhammad Afzal and others (C.P.L.A. 3470/2025, decided 08.10.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Denial of Paternity in Maintenance Suit: Qazf
records.heading: A husband denying his minor daughter's paternity in a maintenance suit faces qazf proceedings
records.text: As stated in the Urdu headnote, if a husband in his written statement to a suit for maintenance denies that the minor is his daughter, qazf proceedings will be taken against him. Ref: 2025 MLD 1534; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 01-L of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 01-L of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Written Divorce: Effective Date
records.heading: A written divorce in clear terms takes effect from the date of its execution
records.text: A divorce pronounced in clear, unambiguous terms and documented in writing takes effect from the date of its execution. A written divorce deed with a specific date, validated under oath, fixes that date as the effective date of divorce. Ref: 2025 MLD 1534; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 01-L of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 01-L of 2025)

records.subject: Character Certificate
records.topic: Police Character Certificate: Acquittals and Discharges Not Disclosed
records.heading: Acquittals and discharges must not be disclosed in a police character certificate
records.text: Mentioning particulars of a case ending in acquittal, discharge or cancellation in a police character certificate is against the Constitution and law, as all acquittals are honourable. Such Category-1 matters must be excluded from PRCs unless expressly authorised by law, and their disclosure contravenes Arts. 4 and 14 of the Constitution. Ref: 2025 LHC 6485; Dr Uzma Hamid Siddiqui v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc. (WP. 44024/25, decided 28.10.2025); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Dr Uzma Hamid Siddiqui v. Inspector General of Police Punjab etc. (WP. 44024/25, decided 28.10.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recall of Warrants and Proclamation by Trial Court
records.heading: A trial court may recall warrants and proclamation after the accused surrenders
records.text: A warrant issued by a court can be cancelled by the same court under s. 75 CrPC. An order issuing process, warrants or proclamation is not a judgment under s. 369 CrPC, and the trial court can recall it on cogent grounds after the accused surrenders. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 915, PLJ 2025 CrC 22.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 342 CrPC: Safe Custody Chain Not Put to Accused
records.heading: A chain of safe custody not put to the accused under section 342 CrPC cannot be used against him
records.text: The chain of safe custody of the case property and sample parcels was not put to the appellant when examined under s. 342 CrPC, so it cannot be used against him. The court may examine such material and, if necessary, put it to the accused through a question. Ref: 2025 LHC 6507; Shafqat Iqbal alias Bilalu v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 55608/23, decided 05.11.2025); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Shafqat Iqbal alias Bilalu v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 55608/23, decided 05.11.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution Against Surety: s. 45 CPC
records.heading: A decree may be executed against a surety whose liability is joint and several
records.text: A decree can be executed against a surety, whose liability is joint and several with the judgment-debtor, so arrest of the judgment-debtor does not absolve the surety of payment. The surety may be proceeded against under s. 45 CPC, and unambiguous words in the surety bond are read in their ordinary meaning. Ref: 2025 CLC 1820; Mehboob Alam v. Additional District Judge etc. (WP 29329/20).
records.title: Mehboob Alam v. Additional District Judge etc. (WP 29329/20)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: s. 22(3) Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009: Directory
records.heading: Section 22(3) of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 is directory, and rent need not be deposited before tenancy is established
records.text: Section 22(3) of the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009 is directory in nature. A party cannot be compelled to deposit rent in court until the relationship of landlord and tenant is established. Ref: 2025 CLC 1852; Shabana Parveen v. Malik Mohsin Hassan Rasheed etc. (WP 45912/22).
records.title: Shabana Parveen v. Malik Mohsin Hassan Rasheed etc. (WP 45912/22)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Landlord-Tenant Relationship as Precondition for Rent Tribunal
records.heading: Rent Tribunal jurisdiction requires a landlord-tenant relationship, which the applicant must prove
records.text: The jurisdiction of the Rent Tribunal under the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009 is confined to disputes arising from a landlord-tenant relationship. A person seeking ejectment must prove that the occupant undertook or is bound to pay rent to him as consideration for occupation. Ref: 2025 CLC 1810; Izzat Khan v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 3978 of 2024).
records.title: Izzat Khan v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 3978 of 2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade and Judicial Confession
records.heading: An identification parade is only corroborative, and a judicial confession must be true and voluntary
records.text: An identification parade under Art. 22 QSO must be conducted with scrupulous care and is only corroborative evidence, and the parade in this case was not fair. A judicial confession can found a conviction only if true, convincing and voluntary, free from duress or inducement. Ref: Aziz Khan and Mangla Khan v. The State (J.P. 116/2020, decided 29.09.2025); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Aziz Khan and Mangla Khan v. The State (J.P. 116/2020, decided 29.09.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance Vests Immediately; Heavy Onus on Donee
records.heading: Heirs inherit immediately, and a donee bears a heavy onus to prove the gift
records.text: Heirs acquire ownership immediately on the predecessor's death, and a co-sharer's possession is for the benefit of all. Waiver, estoppel, relinquishment and adverse possession do not apply among co-heirs, and a donee pleading gift bears a heavy onus to prove offer, acceptance and delivery of possession, including date, time and place. Ref: Abrar Hussain v. Mst. Bibi Shahida and others (C.P.L.A. 567-K/2023, decided 29.08.2025); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Abrar Hussain v. Mst. Bibi Shahida and others (C.P.L.A. 567-K/2023, decided 29.08.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Investigation and Inquiry under ss. 4 and 156 CrPC
records.heading: Investigation under section 4 CrPC is distinct from inquiry and follows a cognizable complaint under section 154
records.text: Section 156(3) CrPC refers to the investigation in s. 156(1), which follows entry of a cognizable complaint under s. 154. Investigation under s. 4 means proceedings by a police officer or person authorised by a Magistrate, excluding a Magistrate, and is distinct from inquiry. Exceptional caution is needed where the accused has been in police custody. Ref: Said ur Rehman S/o Syed Akbar Khan and another v. The State through A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P.L.A. 1674/2021, decided 22.05.2025); Justice Athar Minallah.
records.title: Said ur Rehman S/o Syed Akbar Khan and another v. The State through A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P.L.A. 1674/2021, decided 22.05.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. II R. 2 CPC During Pendency of First Suit
records.heading: Order II Rule 2 CPC requires the whole claim in one suit and may lead to rejection of a second plaint
records.text: O. II R. 2 CPC prevents multiplicity of suits and requires the whole claim from one cause of action in a single suit, and it does not stop the court dismissing a second suit while the first is pending. The rule embodies the doctrine of election, and may lead to rejection of plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC without evidence. Ref: Kamila Aamir and others v. Additional District and Sessions Judge and 10 others (Civil Petition No. 3055 of 2023, decided 14.11.2025).
records.title: Kamila Aamir and others v. Additional District and Sessions Judge and 10 others (Civil Petition No. 3055 of 2023, decided 14.11.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: ss. 489-F and 406 PPC: Funds Received by Mistake
records.heading: Sections 489-F and 406 PPC may be charged together, and funds received by mistake may amount to entrustment
records.text: Offences under ss. 489-F and 406 PPC can be charged together. Money credited to a bank account by mistake is not normally entrustment under s. 405 PPC unless there is dishonest intention, but here the petitioner was bound to return it to the bank and dishonestly used it, causing wrongful gain and loss. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 797; Tariq Rehman Chohan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 43725/25).
records.title: Tariq Rehman Chohan v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 43725/25)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail: Hardened, Desperate or Dangerous Criminal
records.heading: A desperate criminal for statutory bail is assessed from the manner of the offence and previous record
records.text: A person seeking bail on the statutory ground may be regarded as a desperate criminal from the mode and manner in which the offence was committed. Relying on Shakeel Shah's case, the court forms a tentative opinion on character from the facts, previous record and the gravity and manner of the offence. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 802; Aqsa Noureen alias Asima Bibi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 34187/25).
records.title: Aqsa Noureen alias Asima Bibi v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 34187/25)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Memo of Identification: No Evidentiary Value
records.heading: A memo of identification has no evidentiary value under Articles 39 and 40 QSO
records.text: It is well settled that evidence of a memo of identification has no evidentiary value, being inconsistent with Arts. 39 and 40 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 807; Nasir Zakir v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.67752 of 2022).
records.title: Nasir Zakir v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.67752 of 2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Additional Amount for Currency Devaluation
records.heading: Specific performance declined, with the vendor ordered to pay additional amount for currency devaluation
records.text: Suit for specific performance was decreed in part. The vendor was directed to pay the vendee an additional amount over the admitted sale consideration on account of currency devaluation, while the relief of specific performance itself was declined. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 1043; Tanveer Mehmood Awan v. Atif Haseeb etc. (Civil Revision-950-15).
records.title: Tanveer Mehmood Awan v. Atif Haseeb etc. (Civil Revision-950-15)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Registered Agreement to Sell Without Consideration; Art. 82 QSO
records.heading: A registered agreement to sell without consideration may be proved, and specific performance may be refused on equity
records.text: The appellants proved that the registered agreement to sell was without consideration and was in fact for payment of an amount due from their uncle to the respondent. Art. 82 QSO may be invoked to prove execution denied by the attesting witness through other evidence, and specific performance is discretionary and may be refused on equitable considerations. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 1066; Saifullah etc v. Muhammad Deen etc (R.S.A.19-14).
records.title: Saifullah etc v. Muhammad Deen etc (R.S.A.19-14)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption: Non-Appearance of Pre-emptor and Talb-i-Muwathibat
records.heading: Pre-emption revision on the pre-emptor's non-appearance and proof of Talb-i-Muwathibat; holdings not stated
records.text: Revision application on pre-emption considering whether the pre-emptor's non-appearance in the witness box is fatal, proof of Talb-i-Muwathibat where pre-emptor and purchaser are real brothers, omission to name the specific portion of the house in the plaint, non-production of the postman, and evidence recorded by a local commission. The post does not state the holdings. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 1053, 2026 MLD 1761; Muhammad Ijaz v. Suleman Asghar (deceased) through his Legal Heirs (Civil Revision-104-15).
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz v. Suleman Asghar (deceased) through his Legal Heirs (Civil Revision-104-15)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Child Maintenance After Dissolution of Marriage
records.heading: A father's duty to maintain his child continues after dissolution of marriage and loss of custody
records.text: The father bears a continuous obligation to maintain his child, which lasts for a son until puberty (longer if he is incapacitated) and for a daughter until marriage. This duty is distinct from the duty to maintain a wife and survives dissolution of the marriage and loss of custody. If the father cannot, the duty may fall on a financially able mother, then on the paternal grandfather. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC 721; Muhammad Imran Baqir v. Mst. Zarnain Arzoo and others (C.P.L.A.5009/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Imran Baqir v. Mst. Zarnain Arzoo and others (C.P.L.A.5009/2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Marriage Below Statutory Age: Puberty Under Muslim Law
records.heading: Under Muslim law a female is presumed to attain puberty at fifteen and may marry without guardian consent
records.text: Under Muslim personal law puberty is presumed at fifteen, after which a Muslim female is sui juris and may marry without a guardian's consent. The Child Marriage Restraint Act prescribes punishment but does not invalidate such a marriage. As the detenue had attained puberty and consented freely, she was at liberty to reside with the petitioner and the petition was disposed of. Ref: PLJ 2025 Islamabad 385.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Broken Chain of Safe Custody
records.heading: Absence of register entries on handing over narcotics leaves the chain of safe custody unproved
records.text: Dishonest improvements by a witness impair his credibility. Absence of any entry in the register or Roznamcha about handing over case property and the sample parcel to the Malkhana, and non-production of a road certificate, left the chain of safe custody unproved. Doubt was resolved in favour of the accused; appeal allowed and conviction set aside. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 232; Raza alias Qari v. State (Crl. A. No. 310 of 2024, decided 18.06.2025); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh; Justice Raja Ghazanfar Ali Khan.
records.title: Raza alias Qari v. State (Crl. A. No. 310 of 2024, decided 18.06.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail in Robbery: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail in robbery is a matter of further inquiry where the accused was introduced only later without source
records.text: Where the FIR named no culprit, the petitioner was introduced only through a later supplementary statement without any source, and no identification parade was held, the case was one of further inquiry under s. 497 CrPC. Bail is the rule and refusal the exception. Bail granted. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 233; Mujahid v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 39389-B of 2025, decided 31.07.2025); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Mujahid v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 39389-B of 2025, decided 31.07.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Seminal Material Not Required; DNA Corroborative
records.heading: Seminal discharge is not required for rape, and DNA evidence is only corroborative
records.text: Under s. 375 PPC even minimal penetration is rape, irrespective of seminal discharge, so absence of spermatozoa is immaterial. Where the PFSA report is inconclusive, the court must assess the other evidence. DNA evidence is reliable but corroborative in nature and does not independently constitute conclusive proof. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 238; Muhammad Rizwan alias Jani v. State (Crl. A. No. 213/J of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan alias Jani v. State (Crl. A. No. 213/J of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appellate Court's Duty to Reappraise Evidence
records.heading: An appellate court under section 423 CrPC must reappraise the evidence despite concessions by the parties
records.text: Under s. 423 CrPC the appellate court must decide the appeal on merits and reappraise the evidence, and cannot avoid this because the accused or his counsel did not challenge the conviction. Concessions or limitations by the parties do not relieve it of that duty, and failure to do so makes the appellate proceedings legally vulnerable. Ref: Tariq Sajjad Khan v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition No.749-L of 2022, decided 30.09.2025).
records.title: Tariq Sajjad Khan v. The State etc. (Criminal Petition No.749-L of 2022, decided 30.09.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 21 CPC: Objection to Territorial Jurisdiction
records.heading: An objection to territorial jurisdiction cannot be taken on appeal unless raised at the earliest opportunity
records.text: Under s. 21 CPC an objection to the place of suing cannot be taken at the appellate or revisional stage unless raised at the earliest opportunity in the court of first instance, and before settlement of issues, and a consequent failure of justice is shown. Where trial of a family suit concluded without the objection being pressed, the defect in territorial jurisdiction was treated as merely technical. Ref: Farzana Yasmeen and others v. Sohail Ahmed and another (Civil Petition No. 3606 of 2025, decided 29.10.2025).
records.title: Farzana Yasmeen and others v. Sohail Ahmed and another (Civil Petition No. 3606 of 2025, decided 29.10.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Infertility No Ground to Deny Dower or Maintenance
records.heading: Alleged infertility of the wife is no ground to deny dower or maintenance
records.text: Alleged infertility of the wife is not a ground for refusing dower or maintenance, and personal attacks on women in litigation will not be tolerated. The husband's allegations were rebutted by medical reports. The Supreme Court upheld the concurrent decisions below and imposed costs of Rs. 500,000 on the petitioner for misuse of the judicial process. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 1039; Saleh Muhammad and another v. Mst. Mehnaz Begum and others (C.P.L.A.354-P/2025).
records.title: Saleh Muhammad and another v. Mst. Mehnaz Begum and others (C.P.L.A.354-P/2025)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Delay in Banking Cases: Technology Based Case Management
records.heading: Delay in banking cases is a governance failure calling for technology based case management
records.text: The Supreme Court criticised the unexplained delay of the High Court in deciding banking cases and held that delay is a structural challenge of judicial governance. It called for a modern case management system with non-discriminatory early fixation, no queue-jumping, age-tracking of dormant cases and judicious use of AI tools for scheduling and triage. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 1043; Abdul Salam Khan v. M/s Bank Al-Habib Ltd (C.P.L.A.88-P/2022); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah.
records.title: Abdul Salam Khan v. M/s Bank Al-Habib Ltd (C.P.L.A.88-P/2022)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Murder of Judicial Officer as Terrorism: S. 6 ATA
records.heading: Targeted murder of a judicial officer for his official duties is terrorism under section 6 ATA
records.text: Targeted murder of a public servant because of his official duties goes beyond private vengeance and falls within terrorism under s. 6 ATA, particularly s. 6(1)(b) and 6(2)(f). The murder of the judicial officer had a direct nexus with his judicial functions, so the conviction and sentence under the ATA were justified. The accused's challenge failed. Ref: Fiaz @ Mansha and Rashed @ Chand v. The State (J.P.432/2021, decided 14.11.2025); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Fiaz @ Mansha and Rashed @ Chand v. The State (J.P.432/2021, decided 14.11.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: S. 161 CrPC Statement of Critically Injured Not Dying Declaration
records.heading: A section 161 CrPC statement of a critically injured person is neither a dying declaration nor reliable
records.text: Where the injured was in a critical condition under anaesthesia and in the ICU, the investigating officer's claim that he recorded a s. 161 CrPC statement outside the emergency ward was disbelieved, particularly with no permission or attestation by the Medical Officer. Such a statement is neither a dying declaration nor worthy of belief. Ref: 2025 LHC 6798; Nauman Ijaz v. The State (Jail Appeal 30048/22, decided 17.11.2025).
records.title: Nauman Ijaz v. The State (Jail Appeal 30048/22, decided 17.11.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cross Version Cases: Further Inquiry and Bail
records.heading: Bail in a cross version case is not a right, but reasonable doubt may justify bail on further inquiry
records.text: Bail cannot be claimed as of right in a cross version case. However, where the cross version raises reasonable doubt about guilt, the court may grant bail under s. 497(2) CrPC because further inquiry is needed to determine who was the aggressor and who acted in self-defence. Ref: Manan Ali S/o Liaquat Ali and others v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl.P.L.A.806/2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Manan Ali S/o Liaquat Ali and others v. The State through Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl.P.L.A.806/2025)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Death of Convict: Appeal Against Restoration of Possession Survives
records.heading: On a convict's death the appeal against restoration of possession survives while the penal aspect abates
