records.text: Under s. 8-A read with s. 8(1) of the Act, an appeal against an order restoring possession survives independently of the accused's personal liability. On the convict's death the penal aspect abates under s. 431 CrPC, but the appeal remains maintainable to the extent of the direction for restoration of possession. Ref: Muhammad Khurshid Khan v. Dost Muhammad Khan (deceased) through L.Rs and others (Crl.P.L.A.562/2022, decided 12.11.2025); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Muhammad Khurshid Khan v. Dost Muhammad Khan (deceased) through L.Rs and others (Crl.P.L.A.562/2022, decided 12.11.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Withdrawal of Talaq Within Ninety Days: S. 7 MFLO
records.heading: Section 7 MFLO applies to all forms of talaq, and talaq may be revoked within ninety days
records.text: Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance uses the phrase talaq in any form whatsoever, and so applies to all forms of talaq including talaq-e-bidat without distinction. The talaq can be revoked within the ninety day period. The post indicates that a wife exercising delegated divorce power may likewise revoke before the ninety days expire. Ref: Muhammad Hassan Sultan v. Chairman Union Council, Cantonment Board Office, Karachi and another (C.P.L.A.5364/2024, decided 28.11.2025); Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui.
records.title: Muhammad Hassan Sultan v. Chairman Union Council, Cantonment Board Office, Karachi and another (C.P.L.A.5364/2024, decided 28.11.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit on Negotiable Instrument: S. 118 NI Act Presumption
records.heading: The section 118 presumption on a negotiable instrument is rebuttable by showing absence of consideration
records.text: Addresses the principles governing a suit founded on a negotiable instrument. The presumption under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 is rebuttable by direct or circumstantial evidence showing absence of consideration. The threshold of evidence varies from case to case, and the post also covers the standard of balance of probabilities in civil cases. Ref: 2025 LHC 6875; Muhammad Anwaar Anjum & 1 Other v. Muhammad Shakeel Sattar (R.F.A. 78871/24, decided 17.11.2025); Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: Muhammad Anwaar Anjum & 1 Other v. Muhammad Shakeel Sattar (R.F.A. 78871/24, decided 17.11.2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Courier Liability: Handing Parcel to Unverified Recipient
records.heading: A courier that hands a parcel to an unverified recipient breaches its duty and is liable
records.text: Under self-collection the parcel must be handed over only after strict verification of the recipient's identity, especially for valuable insured items. Failure to verify identity and delivery to an unauthorised person is a breach of contractual duty and negligence, and the fraud succeeded because of the courier company's breach, so it was liable despite the consumer's own part. Ref: PLD 2025 Lahore 861; TCS In-Charge Regional Office Gujranwala etc v. Muhammad Siddique Ghumman etc (F.A.O.36959/22).
records.title: TCS In-Charge Regional Office Gujranwala etc v. Muhammad Siddique Ghumman etc (F.A.O.36959/22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: CCTV Footage Where Faces Not Visible
records.heading: CCTV footage showing only the back of the culprit cannot support a murder conviction
records.text: CCTV footage that was played at trial and in the court of appeal showed only the back of the culprit and not the faces. It was of no avail to the prosecution and could not be a basis for conviction for murder during attempted robbery. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1742; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (J.P. 213/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (J.P. 213/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Weapon Recovery Without Independent Corroboration; Expert Report
records.heading: A positive firearm expert report loses value where the weapon recovery is disbelieved
records.text: Where no disclosure memos were prepared and no independent witnesses attested the recoveries, the prosecution case was weakened and foisting was possible. With the recovery disbelieved, the positive firearm expert report lost evidentiary value, as it is corroborative and cannot alone establish guilt. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1742; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (J.P. 213/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (J.P. 213/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Inquiry Before FIR: S. 153(3) and S. 154 CrPC
records.heading: A Magistrate cannot order an inquiry under section 153(3) CrPC on a report disclosing no cognizable offence
records.text: A complainant's report only that his son could not be found disclosed no cognizable offence and did not meet s. 154 CrPC. The Magistrate had no power to order an inquiry under s. 153(3) CrPC. Interrogation of suspects without registration of a case was illegal and abuse of coercive powers could not be ruled out. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1717; Sher Ahmed v. State.
records.title: Sher Ahmed v. State

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Widow as Limited Owner: Reversion and Sale
records.heading: When a widow's limited estate ends, property reverts to the last male owner's heirs and her sale binds only her share
records.text: When the limited owner status of a Muslim widow terminates, the property is treated as that of the last male owner and reverts to his legal heirs, so any sale by her is effective only to the extent of her own share. The purchasers' challenge to the daughter's status failed for want of locus standi. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1698; Muhammad Yaqoob v. Saeeda Bibi.
records.title: Muhammad Yaqoob v. Saeeda Bibi

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction on Ground of Bona Fide Personal Need
records.heading: Bona fide personal need of the landlord is sufficient ground for eviction of a tenant
records.text: Bona fide personal need of the landlord is a sufficient ground for eviction of a tenant. The landlord is the best judge of his need and may choose the premises that suit him, without being bound to follow the tenant's dictation. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1691; Salahuddin Ahmed v. Khurram Sultan Abbasi.
records.title: Salahuddin Ahmed v. Khurram Sultan Abbasi

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Identification Without Light Source
records.heading: Night identification without a torch secured in investigation is accepted only with caution
records.text: The occurrence took place at night and although torches were said to be with the witnesses, none was secured during investigation. The eye-witnesses' claim of identifying the culprits could be accepted only with a lump of salt. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1905; Shakeel v. State.
records.title: Shakeel v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presence of Eye-Witnesses: Deceased's Mouth Found Open
records.heading: A deceased's open mouth in the inquest report showed the alleged eyewitnesses were not present
records.text: The inquest report showed the deceased's mouth was open, whereas close relatives present would first close the mouth and eyes. This showed that the alleged eye-witnesses were not present at the time of occurrence. The prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt; appeal allowed and the accused acquitted. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1905; Shakeel v. State.
records.title: Shakeel v. State

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Wife's Maintenance During Marriage Despite Disobedience
records.heading: A wife's refusal to live with her husband does not disentitle her to maintenance during marriage
records.text: A wife's refusal to live with her husband does not disentitle her to maintenance during subsistence of marriage, and s. 9 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 places no such condition. The opinion of the author of Mulla's Mohammedan Law is not binding and courts may deviate from it where it conflicts with equity, good conscience and justice. Ref: PLD 2025 Islamabad 385.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Misuse of Restitution of Conjugal Rights Suits
records.heading: Restitution of conjugal rights suits must not be used as a counterblast to defeat maintenance claims
records.text: Suits for restitution of conjugal rights must be filed in good faith to reconcile, and must not be used by husbands as a counterblast to defeat or obstruct the wife's claim for maintenance or dower. The husband's derogatory language against his wife reflected mala fide intent. Ref: PLD 2025 Islamabad 385.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Six Month Limit for Maintenance Suits: S. 12-A
records.heading: A maintenance suit must be concluded within six months under section 12-A of the Family Courts Act
records.text: A suit for recovery of maintenance has to be concluded within six months as prescribed by s. 12-A of the Family Courts Act, 1964. Ref: PLD 2025 Islamabad 385.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Interim Maintenance: No Art. 199 Petition on Quantum
records.heading: No Article 199 petition lies against an interim maintenance order on quantum
records.text: Section 14 of the Family Courts Act, 1964, a special law, bars appeal against an interim maintenance order. The quantum of interim maintenance cannot be a ground to invoke the High Court's constitutional jurisdiction, and a petition under Art. 199 is not maintainable against such an order. Ref: PLD 2025 Islamabad 385.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Pending Petition Is Not a Stay
records.heading: A pending petition before the Supreme Court is not an implied stay of arrest
records.text: Police must not treat the mere filing of a petition before the Supreme Court, after dismissal of pre-arrest bail by the High Court, as an implied stay or bar to arrest. Interim protection is not automatic and must be specifically sought and expressly granted. Petition dismissed as not pressed. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 866; Zahid Khan and others v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 645-L of 2025).
records.title: Zahid Khan and others v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 645-L of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Child: Adoptive Versus Natural Parents
records.heading: A child's wishes and nine years with adoptive parents prevailed over the natural parents' custody claim
records.text: The High Court set aside the trial court order handing a 13 year old child from adoptive parents to the natural parents. The child's wishes carry weight in custody, and he had lived with the adoptive parents for nine years without complaint. The natural parents had not proved that the handover was temporary and may approach the Guardian Court for meetings. Ref: 2025 LHC 6930; Syed Arshad Shah & 1 other v. ADJ Pasrur District Sialkot etc. (WP 43188/23, decided 28.11.2025); Justice Faisal Zaman Khan.
records.title: Syed Arshad Shah & 1 other v. ADJ Pasrur District Sialkot etc. (WP 43188/23, decided 28.11.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence and Recovery Under Art. 40 QSO
records.heading: On a temporary injunction application the trial court should accept or dismiss it with reasons
records.text: Last seen evidence alone is insufficient, but may be relied on if the chain of facts permits no reasonable inference other than guilt and the accused gives no reasonable explanation. Under Art. 40 QSO a recovery must follow a statement made in police custody and lead to discovery of a previously unknown fact. In circumstantial cases the incriminating facts must be incompatible with innocence. Ref: 2025 LHC 6938; Sumaira Bibi v. The State, etc. (Cr. Appeal No.38037 of 2022).
records.title: Sumaira Bibi v. The State, etc. (Cr. Appeal No.38037 of 2022)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Restoration of Possession: Functus Officio After Order
records.heading: A court is functus officio after passing and signing an order and cannot review it
records.text: Possession was handed to the complainants through a bailiff under s. 7 of the Act without any resistance, and about three months later the accused's brother applied for its restoration. A court becomes functus officio after passing and signing an order (s. 369 CrPC) and cannot review it. The criminal revision was dismissed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1931; Mian Sohaib-ur-Rehman v. Muhammad Bashir (Criminal Revision No. 10045 of 2019).
records.title: Mian Sohaib-ur-Rehman v. Muhammad Bashir (Criminal Revision No. 10045 of 2019)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Cancellation of Anti-Corruption Case: Rules and Pre-conditions
records.heading: An Anti-Corruption case may be cancelled only on the grounds in the Police Rules and its own Rules
records.text: A case may be cancelled on the grounds in Rule 24.7 of the Police Rules, 1934, but the Anti-Corruption Establishment may drop a case only where allegations are not established or judicial action is not warranted yet evidence supports departmental action under R. 10(1)(b) of its 2014 Rules. Revision was allowed and the Special Judge was directed to decide the cancellation report afresh. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1957; Karim Bakhsh v. The State and 8 others (Criminal Revision No. 78 of 2025).
records.title: Karim Bakhsh v. The State and 8 others (Criminal Revision No. 78 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare Prevails over Natural Parents
records.heading: The welfare of the minor is paramount and may override the natural parents' claims to custody
records.text: Under s. 17 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, the welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration, and the court may disregard the father's natural guardianship or the mother's hizanat. Where the minor, now about 13, had been raised by foster relatives since infancy, the orders giving custody to the natural parents were set aside and their application dismissed. Petition allowed. Ref: 2025 LHC 6930; Sayed Arshad Shah etc. v. Addl. District Judge etc. (W.P. 43188/2023); Justice Faisal Zaman Khan.
records.title: Sayed Arshad Shah etc. v. Addl. District Judge etc. (W.P. 43188/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXIX R. 1 and 2 CPC: Order Must Accept or Dismiss
records.heading: A temporary injunction application must be accepted or dismissed, not merely turned down without reasons
records.text: On an application for temporary injunction under O. XXXIX R. 1 and 2 CPC the trial court should either accept or dismiss it and should not use the expression turned down without reasons. The impugned order was set aside and the application was deemed pending for fresh decision. Ref: 2025 MLD 1973; Fahim Ahmed Saeed and others v. Mian Humayun Mahmud and others (F.A.O. No. 81 of 2025).
records.title: Fahim Ahmed Saeed and others v. Mian Humayun Mahmud and others (F.A.O. No. 81 of 2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Transaction With Elderly Illiterate Widow: Burden on Beneficiary
records.heading: A beneficiary dealing with an elderly illiterate widow must prove the transaction by unimpeachable evidence
records.text: Where an elderly illiterate widow transacts without independent advice with a grandson living with her, the beneficiary must prove the transaction by unimpeachable and creditworthy evidence. The 20 year old grandson without income failed to prove payment of consideration or rebut undue influence. Concurrent findings stood and the revision was dismissed. Ref: 2025 CLC 1784; Muhammad Umar Farooq v. Irshaad Bibi (C.R. No. 13867 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Umar Farooq v. Irshaad Bibi (C.R. No. 13867 of 2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Prosecutors' Duty to Challenge Favourable Concessions: Arts. 150 and 151
records.heading: Prosecutors must challenge favourable concessions by witnesses under Articles 150 and 151 QSO
records.text: Where prosecution witnesses made concessions favouring the accused and the prosecutor stayed passive, the court directed Law Officers to remain vigilant in narcotics trials and to invoke Arts. 150 and 151 QSO immediately when a witness deviates. Concessions by police witnesses must not go unchallenged. Ref: 2025 LHC 6970; Shameer Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal.56371/23, decided 19.11.2025); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Shameer Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal.56371/23, decided 19.11.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Safe Custody and Transmission Not Proved
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody and transmission of narcotics is fatal and results in acquittal
records.text: The prosecution did not prove the chain of safe custody and safe transmission of the recovered narcotic, which made its case doubtful and was fatal, resulting in acquittal of the appellant. Ref: 2025 LHC 6970; Shameer Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal.56371/23, decided 19.11.2025); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Shameer Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal.56371/23, decided 19.11.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI CPC: Second Application for Witness List
records.heading: A second application to list witnesses under Order XVI is not maintainable after an unchallenged dismissal
records.text: A second application to list witnesses under O. XVI CPC is not maintainable when the first was dismissed and not challenged, even if relabelled as under O. XVI R. 14. Rule 14 is a discretionary power of the court, not a device for parties to fill gaps in evidence or cure non-compliance with R. 1. Ref: 2025 LHC 7008; Malik Muhammad Irshadfaiz v. Khadim Hussain (Civil Revision-507-22, decided 18.11.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Malik Muhammad Irshadfaiz v. Khadim Hussain (Civil Revision-507-22, decided 18.11.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Ex Post Facto: Conviction Under Later Amended Provision
records.heading: An accused cannot be convicted under a harsher provision introduced after the offence, contrary to Article 12
records.text: An accused may be punished only for the offence on the statute at the time of occurrence, not under a harsher provision introduced later, as that offends Art. 12 of the Constitution. The recovery of charas was before the 2022 CNSA amendment, so conviction under the amended s. 9(1) 3(c) was contrary to Art. 12. Reduction of sentence may be considered after a substantial period served. Ref: 2025 LHC 7029; Sufiyan Riaz v. The State (Jail Appeal.85571/23, decided 03.12.2025); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Sufiyan Riaz v. The State (Jail Appeal.85571/23, decided 03.12.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Experience Criteria: Exclusion Without Legal Basis; Right of Appeal
records.heading: Excluding contract experience without legal basis is untenable, and the right of appeal is substantive
records.text: Excluding contract or daily wage experience when neither law nor the advertisement requires regular employment is untenable and infringes the right to seek public employment. The right of appeal is substantive, and implementing adverse orders before limitation for appeal expires is unfair and contrary to natural justice. Ref: 2025 LHC 7013; Muhammad Amir Shabbir v. Govt. of Punjab etc (Writ Petition-9729-19, decided 26.11.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Amir Shabbir v. Govt. of Punjab etc (Writ Petition-9729-19, decided 26.11.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Victim's Evidence, Medical and DNA Support; Sentence Reduced
records.heading: Rape conviction upheld on victim's evidence with medical and DNA support, but sentence reduced to ten years
records.text: The victim's evidence was not shaken in cross-examination and was supported by medical evidence and an FSA report finding the appellant's DNA profile on her shalwar. Guilt under s. 376 PPC was established, but due to mitigating circumstances life imprisonment was reduced to ten years rigorous imprisonment, with the fine upheld. Ref: 2025 YLR 367; Allah Wadhaya v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 576-J-LD of 2017).
records.title: Allah Wadhaya v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 576-J-LD of 2017)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Natural Witnesses Withheld; Safe Custody Not Proved
records.heading: Withholding natural witnesses and unproved safe custody led to acquittal in a rape case
records.text: The prosecution withheld natural witnesses, the inmates of the house said to have been locked in a room, giving rise to an adverse presumption, and no gun was recovered at the accused's instance. Safe custody of case property was also not proved. The appeal was allowed and the accused acquitted on the benefit of doubt. Ref: 2025 YLR 811; Rizwan Sami khan v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 41759 of 2022).
records.title: Rizwan Sami khan v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 41759 of 2022)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape of Minor: Prompt FIR and Reliance on Child Victim
records.heading: A prompt FIR and unshaken eyewitnesses with a child victim sustained a rape conviction
records.text: An FIR lodged within about three hours of the incident confirmed the presence of the eye-witnesses and excluded deliberation and fabrication. The two eye-witnesses were not shaken in lengthy cross-examination and the child victim was a crucial witness. The conviction was upheld and the appeal dismissed. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1795; Istikhar alias Iftikhar v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 56786 of 2017).
records.title: Istikhar alias Iftikhar v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 56786 of 2017)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mandatory or Directory Provisions; 'May' and 'Shall'
records.heading: Whether a provision is mandatory or directory depends on legislative intent and consequences
records.text: Whether a provision is mandatory or directory depends on legislative intent, ascertained from its object, scheme and the consequences of each construction. A provision is mandatory if omission renders proceedings void. 'May' and 'shall' are interchangeable by context, and where no penal consequence is stated, 'shall' may be read as directory. Ref: 2025 CLC 1852.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Scribe as Attesting Witness; Art. 80 QSO
records.heading: A scribe is a competent witness only if he signed as an attesting witness
records.text: A scribe is a competent witness to a document only if he signed as an attesting witness, and signing as writer does not satisfy attestation. Where no attesting witness is found, Art. 80 QSO obliges the party to prove that the witnesses have died or cannot be traced. Concurrent findings against the plaintiffs were upheld. Ref: 2025 CLC 1982; Kher Din v. Mst. Hayat Bibi (Civil Revision No. 339-D of 2016).
records.title: Kher Din v. Mst. Hayat Bibi (Civil Revision No. 339-D of 2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Qazf: Statement in Court Disputed; De Novo Trial
records.heading: A qazf case was remanded for de novo trial because the evidence was not properly evaluated
records.text: The complainant admitted a quarrel inside the court after the disputed statement was recorded, raising doubt which the Trial Court ignored. It had failed to evaluate the evidence properly and deprived the appellant of a fair trial. The case was remanded for de novo trial and the reference for confirmation was answered in the negative. Ref: 2025 MLD 1500, PLJ 2025 FSC 79; Muhammad Aman v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Aman v. State

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Mulla's Muhammadan Law Has No Force of Law
records.heading: Mulla's Principles of Muhammadan Law is a reference book and has no force of law
records.text: Principles of Muhammadan Law by D. F. Mulla have no force of law, being a reference book only, and do not fall within the meaning of law under Art. 203B(c) of the Constitution. The court declined to interfere in a dispute on change of an adopted child's family name, as the matter was covered by Najaat Welfare Foundation (PLD 2021 FSC 1). Ref: PLD 2025 FSC 18; Mst. Mussarat Fayyaz v. Government of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice, Islamabad.
records.title: Mst. Mussarat Fayyaz v. Government of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice, Islamabad

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Defamation: Allegation of Zina Made After Marriage Ended
records.heading: Accusations of zina made after the marriage ended prima facie fall within Qazf
records.text: Accusations of zina made in a divorce deed, repeated in pleadings and affirmed in court and public after the marital bond ended, prima facie fell within Qazf. Section 14 of the Qazf Ordinance, 1979 on li'an did not apply. The trial judge wrongly dismissed the private complaint as not maintainable. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 955, PLJ 2025 FSC 100; Mst. Sassi Hizbullah v. Junaid Ahmed Khan.
records.title: Mst. Sassi Hizbullah v. Junaid Ahmed Khan

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Polygraph Test and Its Legal Implications
records.heading: The polygraph test: its basis, history and legal implications as an investigative tool
records.text: Explains the polygraph test, its physiological basis and its history, and its legal implications as an investigative tool. The post also states that circumstantial evidence must form a chain excluding every hypothesis of innocence, failing which the benefit of doubt goes to the accused. Ref: 2025 LHC 7145; Muhammad Imran Gochhi v. The State (Jail Appeal. 10692/21, decided 01.12.2025); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Imran Gochhi v. The State (Jail Appeal. 10692/21, decided 01.12.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Misrepresentation and Concealment Before the Court
records.heading: A litigant who conceals facts or misleads the court must bear the consequences
records.text: Misrepresentation before the court strikes at the judicial process, and a litigant who conceals or deceives must bear the consequences. The party withdrew the main suit, continued prosecuting the revision without disclosure and filed a fresh application for prohibitory relief, which showed deliberate concealment and misuse of the court. Ref: 2025 LHC 7119; Wazir Khan v. Tehsil Municipal Administration, etc. (C.R. No.1549 of 2016).
records.title: Wazir Khan v. Tehsil Municipal Administration, etc. (C.R. No.1549 of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Leave to Defend and Ex Parte Orders
records.heading: Leave to defend under Order XXXVII differs for ex parte proceedings and for an ex parte decree
records.text: Against ex parte proceedings, the application to set aside should accompany an application for leave to appear and defend under O. XXXVII R. 2 CPC, and limitation runs only if the plaint was in the prescribed form and summonses were served as prescribed. Against an ex parte decree, a leave application need not accompany it and is required within ten days after the decree is set aside. Ref: 2025 LHC 7173; Muhammad Amir v. Muhammad Asghar (F.A.O. 107-19, decided 03.12.2025); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Amir v. Muhammad Asghar (F.A.O. 107-19, decided 03.12.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Evidence in Presence of Accused: Exceptions and Former Testimony
records.heading: Evidence is recorded in the accused's presence, with exceptions for dying declarations and former testimony
records.text: Evidence must ordinarily be recorded on oath in the accused's presence under s. 353 CrPC. Exceptions include dying declarations under Art. 46 QSO and former testimony under Art. 47 QSO of a witness who is dead or cannot be found. Where the statutory conditions are met, the earlier testimony may be read, ignoring technical irregularities in transposition under s. 512 CrPC. Ref: Riffat Hussain v. Zahida Bibi and another (Crl.P.L.A.1431/2020, decided 25.11.2025); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Riffat Hussain v. Zahida Bibi and another (Crl.P.L.A.1431/2020, decided 25.11.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recording Witness by Video Link: Punjab Witnesses Protection Act 2018
records.heading: A trial court may record a witness by video link under the Punjab Witnesses Protection Act
records.text: Section 10 of the Punjab Witnesses Protection Act, 2018 allows the court to examine a witness by video link, and Art. 164 QSO permits admission of evidence made available by technological advancement. Together these allow the trial court to record a witness through video link when circumstances require. Ref: 2025 LHC 6277; Zubaida Khanam v. The State and 05 others (Criminal Revision No. 66407 of 2025, decided 20.11.2025).
records.title: Zubaida Khanam v. The State and 05 others (Criminal Revision No. 66407 of 2025, decided 20.11.2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 336-B PPC: Petrol Not Corrosive Substance
records.heading: Petrol is not a corrosive substance, so throwing it does not attract section 336-B PPC
records.text: The Anti-Terrorism Court has exclusive jurisdiction to try the offence under s. 336-B PPC. Petrol is not a corrosive substance under s. 336-A, so throwing it does not attract s. 336-B. Without proof of pregnancy, s. 338 PPC is not made out. The post also notes the parameters for recording a dying declaration. Ref: 2025 LHC 7284; Parvaiz @ Irfan v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal-551-16, decided 20.03.2025); Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar.
records.title: Parvaiz @ Irfan v. State etc. (Crl. Appeal-551-16, decided 20.03.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Talaq Under S. 7 MFLO: Ninety Days and Revocation
records.heading: A talaq under section 7 MFLO takes effect after ninety days unless revoked, and non-notice makes it ineffective
records.text: Under s. 7(3) MFLO a talaq takes effect only after ninety days from notice to the Chairman, unless revoked earlier, and the spouses remain married meanwhile. The husband may revoke expressly or by conduct, without informing the Chairman, whatever the form of talaq. Failure to give notice attracts s. 7(2) penalty and makes the talaq ineffective, not invalid. The petitioner could not be prosecuted under s. 376 PPC as the FIR disclosed no ingredients. Ref: 2025 LHC 7342; Jameel Ahmad v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 39/2025).
records.title: Jameel Ahmad v. The State and others (Writ Petition No. 39/2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Quashing FIR: Subsisting Marriage and s. 376 PPC
records.heading: An FIR under section 376 PPC against a lawful husband discloses no offence and may be quashed
records.text: The marital bond between the petitioner and the complainant existed in law at the time of the alleged occurrence, so the essential ingredients of s. 376 PPC were not disclosed on the face of the FIR. The High Court may quash an FIR under Art. 199 where allegations disclose no offence, though not where disputed facts need evidence. Petition accepted and FIR quashed. Ref: 2025 LHC 7342; Jameel Ahmad v. The State and others (W.P. 39/2025); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Jameel Ahmad v. The State and others (W.P. 39/2025)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Collection Without Due Process: Privacy and Art. 9
records.heading: Collecting DNA without due process violates privacy and personal liberty under Article 9
records.text: Collecting an individual's DNA without due process violates privacy, autonomy and personal liberty under Art. 9 of the Constitution. A demand for DNA testing at any stage, particularly to establish parentage, encroaches on these rights, and a judicial order for it without legal backing and consent is more than a procedural irregularity. Ref: Khalid Hameed v. Special Judge Anti Corruption Pakpattan Sharif and others (Crl.P.L.A.106/2023, decided 17.11.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Khalid Hameed v. Special Judge Anti Corruption Pakpattan Sharif and others (Crl.P.L.A.106/2023, decided 17.11.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Conversion of Public or Religious Purpose Land to Commercial Use
records.heading: Converting land allotted for a public or religious purpose to commercial use is unlawful
records.text: Converting land allotted for a public or religious purpose to commercial use is contrary to the terms of allotment and unlawful. Such land carries the character of a purpose trust for the community, and any deviation without competent authority and lawful sanction is ultra vires the trust purpose and void. Ref: 2025 LHC 7330; Province of the Punjab through Secretary Education, Civil Secretariat, Lahore & another v. Darul Haq Trust & others (Civil Revision No.46498 of 2017).
records.title: Province of the Punjab through Secretary Education, Civil Secretariat, Lahore & another v. Darul Haq Trust & others (Civil Revision No.46498 of 2017)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Lis Pendens in Pre-emption Suits: Sole Exception
records.heading: Lis pendens applies to pre-emption suits, with one exception for sale to a superior pre-emptor
records.text: The doctrine of lis pendens applies fully to pre-emption suits, and a pre-emption decree is binding on a purchaser during litigation. The only exception is a sale by the vendee to a person with a superior right of pre-emption, made within the period of limitation for exercising that right. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2095; Muhammad Sadiq v. Additional District Judge, Toba Tek Singh etc. (C.A. No. 636-L of 2012 in C.P.L.A No.1637-L of 2010).
records.title: Muhammad Sadiq v. Additional District Judge, Toba Tek Singh etc. (C.A. No. 636-L of 2012 in C.P.L.A No.1637-L of 2010)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Benami Transactions: Meaning and Burden of Proof
records.heading: A benami plea must be proved by unimpeachable evidence by the party raising it
records.text: A benami transaction is one in the name of another person who holds the property as ostensible owner. The party raising the plea of benami must prove it by unimpeachable evidence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2087; Mst. Nasira Ansari and others v. Late Tahira Begum through legal heirs & others (C.A.41-K/2021).
records.title: Mst. Nasira Ansari and others v. Late Tahira Begum through legal heirs & others (C.A.41-K/2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Jurisdiction: No Evidence Recording; Mutatis Mutandis
records.heading: The High Court in a writ petition cannot record evidence but may vet the available record
records.text: The High Court in a writ petition cannot record evidence but may vet the available record to reach a just conclusion. The post explains mutatis mutandis as with necessary changes made, and records that the High Court disposed of the petitions with undue haste on an urgent motion without appreciating the facts. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2062; Province of Sindh & others v. Amanullah & others (C.P.L.A.4-K/2025).
records.title: Province of Sindh & others v. Amanullah & others (C.P.L.A.4-K/2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Common Intention in Robbery: S. 34 PPC
records.heading: Under section 34 PPC each participant in a gang robbery is liable for acts in furtherance of common intention
records.text: Caution about false implication of family members applies in private enmity cases but not in a premeditated gang robbery. Each participant need not personally inflict the fatal injury, since under s. 34 PPC each is liable for an act done in furtherance of common intention. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2018; Tahseen Ullah; and Salman Khan v. The State (Jail Petition No.611 of 2022).
records.title: Tahseen Ullah; and Salman Khan v. The State (Jail Petition No.611 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inconsistencies as Mitigating Circumstance in Sentence
records.heading: Inconsistencies that do not justify acquittal may still mitigate sentence
records.text: Inconsistencies in the prosecution case that do not suffice for acquittal may still be treated as an extenuating or mitigating circumstance in the matter of sentence. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2018; Tahseen Ullah; and Salman Khan v. The State (Jail Petition No.611 of 2022).
records.title: Tahseen Ullah; and Salman Khan v. The State (Jail Petition No.611 of 2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Delayed FIR and Investigation Before Registration: S. 154 CrPC
records.heading: Investigating before registering the FIR under section 154 CrPC avoids Magistrate supervision and invites abuse
records.text: Examines the scheme of the Code on the First Information Report, which means information recorded under s. 154 or 155 CrPC, where the officer in charge of a police station must enter its substance. Investigating before registering the case avoids the supervisory check of the Magistrate and gives scope for abuse of police powers. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2028; Seeta Ram v. The State (Jail Petition No.51 of 2023).
records.title: Seeta Ram v. The State (Jail Petition No.51 of 2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 91 QSO: Presumption for Confession Taken in Accordance With Law
records.heading: The Article 91 QSO presumption for confessions applies only if taken in accordance with law
records.text: The presumption of genuineness under Art. 91 QSO for statements and confessions before a Magistrate is qualified by the words taken in accordance with law. Under Art. 38 statements to police are inadmissible, and custodial confessions are inadmissible except before a Magistrate or under Art. 40. S. 164 CrPC sets mandatory conditions for recording a judicial confession. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2028; Seeta Ram v. The State (Jail Petition No.51 of 2023).
records.title: Seeta Ram v. The State (Jail Petition No.51 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Duty to Register FIR Promptly: S. 154 CrPC
records.heading: An officer in charge of a police station must register an FIR promptly under section 154 CrPC
records.text: The Court held it a statutory duty of the officer in charge of a police station to register an FIR as soon as information is received, with no authority to refuse or delay under s. 154 CrPC. Unexplained delay lets evidence be managed and manipulated. Copies of the judgment were directed to be sent to the Inspectors General and Prosecutors General. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2028; Seeta Ram v. The State (Jail Petition No.51 of 2023).
records.title: Seeta Ram v. The State (Jail Petition No.51 of 2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: PEEDA S. 13: Competent Authority and Inquiry Report
records.heading: The PEEDA Competent Authority is not bound by the inquiry report but must act fairly
records.text: Under PEEDA the inquiry officer's recommendations under s. 10 do not bind the Competent Authority, and its decision is part of the same proceeding and not an appeal. The authority nevertheless has no unbridled discretion and must act by fairness, sound reasoning and natural justice, failing which the final order is vulnerable. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2071; Muhammad Arshad v. Deputy District Food, Multan, etc. (C.P.L.A.1919-L/2016).
records.title: Muhammad Arshad v. Deputy District Food, Multan, etc. (C.P.L.A.1919-L/2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 115 CPC: Limits of Revisional Jurisdiction
records.heading: A revisional court under section 115 CPC cannot act as an appellate court on findings not perverse
records.text: A revisional court under s. 115 CPC has limited jurisdiction and cannot act as appellate court to replace findings that are not arbitrary or perverse. The revisional court overlooked an application under s. 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 for condonation of delay filed with the restoration application, and the Supreme Court disagreed with its reasoning. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2092; Ch. Fayyaz-Ur-Rehman Khalid v. Amir Javed, etc. (C.P.L.A.1898-L/2021).
records.title: Ch. Fayyaz-Ur-Rehman Khalid v. Amir Javed, etc. (C.P.L.A.1898-L/2021)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Pendency of Petition Is Not a Stay: Remand Orders
records.heading: Pendency of a petition is not a stay, so inaction on remand orders is unjustified
records.text: Pendency of an appeal, revision or petition does not of itself stay the order assailed, as embodied in O. XX R. 1 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1980. Administrative inaction on remand orders because of mere pendency, without an injunctive order, is unjustified and impermissible. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2078; Chief Land Commissioner, Punjab/Senior Member Board of Revenue Punjab, Lahore, etc. v. Administrator Auqaf Department, Bahawalpur, etc. (C.P.L.A.2915-L/2015).
records.title: Chief Land Commissioner, Punjab/Senior Member Board of Revenue Punjab, Lahore, etc. v. Administrator Auqaf Department, Bahawalpur, etc. (C.P.L.A.2915-L/2015)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Competence of Child Witness: Art. 3 QSO
records.heading: A child is a competent witness under Article 3 QSO if tested by preliminary questions
records.text: Under Art. 3 QSO all persons are competent to testify unless unable to understand questions or give rational answers. A child is competent depending on capacity and intellect, tested through preliminary voir dire questions. The child witness PW-2 proved credible and the trial court rightly relied on her. Ref: 2025 LHC 7370; Shahzeb v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 276-J of 2023).
records.title: Shahzeb v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 276-J of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eye-Witnesses: Art. 129 QSO
records.heading: Related eyewitnesses who made no effort to save the deceased are presumed absent under Article 129 QSO
records.text: Closely related eye-witnesses who made no effort to save the deceased or apprehend the assailant acted contrary to natural human conduct, and under Art. 129 QSO the court inferred that they were not present. An accused cannot be convicted merely because she did not explain how the deceased lost his life. Ref: 2025 LHC 7389; The State v. Muhammad Arsalan (Murder Reference No. 01 of 2024); Muhammad Arsalan v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 383-J of 2023); Mst. Misbah Bibi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 384-J of 2023).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Arsalan (Murder Reference No. 01 of 2024); Muhammad Arsalan v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 383-J of 2023); Mst. Misbah Bibi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 384-J of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Alteration of Charge: Recall of Witnesses and Prejudice
records.heading: On alteration of a charge, witnesses may be recalled, and the accused must show material prejudice
records.text: When a charge is altered or added to after trial begins, the prosecutor and the accused must be allowed to recall witnesses and call further witnesses on the alteration. Whether the trial is vitiated depends on the degree of error, and the accused must show material prejudice amounting to a failure of justice. Ref: 2025 LHC 7429; Muhammad Kashif alias Kashi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.10-J of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Kashif alias Kashi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.10-J of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Trial Court Cannot Block CNIC or Passport
records.heading: A trial court has no power to block, cancel or impound a CNIC or passport
records.text: Section 18 of the NADRA Ordinance, 2000 and s. 8 of the Passports Act, 1974 do not empower a trial court to order blocking, cancellation, impounding or confiscation of a CNIC or passport. The impugned order lacked jurisdiction. Ref: 2025 LHC 7483; Abdul Rehman v. The State and five others (Criminal Revision No.205 of 2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. The State and five others (Criminal Revision No.205 of 2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Missing Links in Chain of Custody of Samples
records.heading: Unexplained custody of sample parcels and contradictory dates broke the chain of custody of narcotics
records.text: The PFSA report contradicted the witnesses on the date of deposit of the sample parcels, and the custody of the parcels over six months was unexplained. The prosecution failed to establish safe custody of the recovered narcotic, and the benefit of the resulting doubt went to the appellant. Ref: 2025 LHC 7491; Aman Ullah v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 327 of 2023).
records.title: Aman Ullah v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 327 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Identification: Failure to Prove Light Source
records.heading: Failure to prove a light source in a night occurrence is fatal to eyewitness identification
records.text: The prosecution did not produce or prove any light source at the scene of a night occurrence, so the eye-witnesses' identification of the assailant could not be relied on. This failure was fatal to the prosecution case. Ref: 2025 LHC 7508; Zahoor Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 698-J of 2020, decided 25.06.2025).
records.title: Zahoor Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 698-J of 2020, decided 25.06.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Electronic Evidence: Mobile Not Forensically Examined
records.heading: Electronic evidence lacks probative value if the mobile is not forensically examined or produced
records.text: The complainant's mobile device was neither forensically examined nor produced, and only hard copies of the alleged blasphemous content were supplied. Without independent verification the electronic evidence lacks probative value. Nearly three years' silence and non-production of the device attracted Art. 73-A QSO, and Arts. 46-A and 73 were also relied on. Ref: 2025 LHC 7573; Wazir Gull v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 587 of 2023) and connected appeals.
records.title: Wazir Gull v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 587 of 2023) and connected appeals

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Closure of Complainant's Right to Produce Witnesses
records.heading: A trial court cannot close the complainant's right to produce witnesses whose examination-in-chief was recorded
records.text: A trial court cannot close the complainant's right to produce witnesses for cross-examination where their examination-in-chief was already recorded. The only course is the procedure under law to compel a witness's attendance, so the closure order was untenable. Ref: 2025 LHC 7618; Taimoor Malik v. The State (Crl. Revision No.150 of 2025, decided 07.10.2025).
records.title: Taimoor Malik v. The State (Crl. Revision No.150 of 2025, decided 07.10.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Accused From Column No. 2: S. 204 CrPC
records.heading: A trial court may summon an accused placed in column No. 2 under section 204 CrPC
records.text: The trial court may summon an accused placed in column No. 2 of the s. 173 CrPC report to face trial before any evidence is recorded where sufficient material exists. The investigating officer's opinion that he is not involved is irrelevant and inadmissible and should not weigh on an application under s. 204 CrPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 7624; Ghulam Hassan v. The State and four others (Criminal Revision No.143 of 2025).
records.title: Ghulam Hassan v. The State and four others (Criminal Revision No.143 of 2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 161 QSO: Court's Power to Summon Documents
records.heading: Under Article 161 QSO a trial Judge may order production of any document to obtain proper proof
records.text: Under Art. 161 QSO a trial Judge may ask any question and order production of any document or thing to discover or obtain proper proof of relevant facts. 'Document' is defined in Art. 2(1)(b). Certified copies of a decree of dissolution, the Nikahnama and the CNIC can validly be treated as documents, and the final judgment must rest on facts proved under the QSO. Ref: 2025 LHC 7611; Kaneez Bibi v. The State and two others (Criminal Revision No. 48 of 2025, hearing 30.09.2025).
records.title: Kaneez Bibi v. The State and two others (Criminal Revision No. 48 of 2025, hearing 30.09.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Prompt FIR, Injured Witness and Recovery
records.heading: A prompt FIR, an injured eyewitness and a recovery with proved motive established guilt
records.text: Timely registration of the FIR excludes manipulation, and an eyewitness who bears injuries from the occurrence has a presence beyond doubt. A pistol recovered on the accused's disclosure is relevant under Art. 40 QSO, and Art. 121 QSO is an exception to the rule that the prosecution must prove guilt on its own strength. Ocular, medical and recovery evidence with proved motive established guilt and the plea of self defence failed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 2009, PLJ 2025 CrC 572.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Reduced to Life Imprisonment
records.heading: Even the slightest circumstance can justify converting a death sentence into life imprisonment
records.text: Even the slightest circumstance can justify converting a death sentence into imprisonment for life, and no extraordinary circumstances are required for that change. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 2009, PLJ 2025 CrC 572.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Lis Pendens: Bona Fide Purchaser Bound by Decree
records.heading: A purchaser pendente lite, even bona fide, is bound by the final decree
records.text: A transfer pendente lite is not automatically void but is subject to the outcome of the decree. Even a bona fide purchaser without notice is bound by the final decree, and a purchaser of suit land during proceedings before the Supreme Court acts at his own risk and cost. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2095; Muhammad Sadiq v. Additional District Judge, Toba Tek Singh etc. (C.A. No. 636-L of 2012 in C.P.L.A No.1637-L of 2010).
records.title: Muhammad Sadiq v. Additional District Judge, Toba Tek Singh etc. (C.A. No. 636-L of 2012 in C.P.L.A No.1637-L of 2010)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Lodging FIR
records.heading: Unexplained delay of 2 hours 10 minutes in reporting a murder was consequential and doubted the eyewitnesses
records.text: An unexplained delay of 2 hours 10 minutes in reporting a murder that occurred 16 kilometres from the police station was held consequential. No plausible explanation was given by the complainant, and the statements of the purported eyewitnesses raised serious doubts about their presence at the spot. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2052; Muhammad alias Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 499 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad alias Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 499 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct and Delayed Post-Mortem
records.heading: Unnatural conduct of eyewitnesses and delayed police papers and post-mortem created serious doubt
records.text: Eyewitnesses who did not promptly shift the deceased to a hospital or police station acted inconsistently with normal human behaviour. Inordinate delay in preparing and transmitting police papers and in the post-mortem, together with that failure, created serious doubt about the eyewitnesses' presence at the scene. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2052; Muhammad alias Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 499 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad alias Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 499 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Contradictions Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Blackening, intact bullets and an unhurt co-accused contradicted the ocular account and the site plan
records.text: Blackening around the entry wounds indicated close range, which contradicted the site plan showing the accused 20/22 feet away. Intact bullets recovered from the body were inconsistent with a claimed 12-bore repeater, and the co-accused standing adjacent was unhurt. These improbabilities weakened the ocular account. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2052; Muhammad alias Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 499 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad alias Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 499 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Doubtful Presence
records.heading: A chance witness from another district without plausible reason for presence is highly doubtful
records.text: The complainant who allegedly triggered the incident was spared without explanation, so his presence was doubtful. The eyewitness hailed from another district and produced no documentary proof of residence in the village, and as a chance witness he gave no plausible reason for being at the spot. His presence was held highly doubtful (ss. 302(b) and 34 PPC). Ref: 2025 SCMR 2052; Muhammad alias Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 499 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad alias Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 499 of 2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Murder: Joint Role and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail in murder is a case of further inquiry where a joint role was alleged and no weapon recovered
records.text: Where a joint role of firing was assigned to the petitioner and co-accused, no specific injury was attributed to him, no weapon was recovered and the FSL showed the empties were fired from one weapon, the matter called for further inquiry. The number of injured or deceased on each side is not relevant at the bail stage. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2059; Sher Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1230 of 2025).
records.title: Sher Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1230 of 2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail to Imran Khan in May 9 Cases
records.heading: Post-arrest bail granted to Imran Khan in eight May 9 cases
records.text: Leave was sought against Lahore High Court orders of 24.06.2025 refusing post-arrest bail in eight FIRs registered in May 2023 under various PPC provisions read with s. 7 ATA 1997. The petitions were converted into appeals and allowed, and bail was granted in each case on bonds of Rs.100,000 with one surety. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2013; Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1184/2025); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Imran Ahmad Khan Niazi v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1184/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Converting Plaint into s. 12(2) CPC Application
records.heading: A court may convert a plaint into a section 12(2) CPC application, and the reverse, in just circumstances
records.text: A court may convert a plaint in a suit into an application under s. 12(2) CPC, and the reverse, provided just and fair circumstances exist and the conversion serves effective dispensation of justice. Ref: 2025 CLC 2048; Amina Bibi and another v. Province of Punjab and others (W.P. No. 30762 of 2022).
records.title: Amina Bibi and another v. Province of Punjab and others (W.P. No. 30762 of 2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Standard of Proof in Departmental Inquiry
records.heading: The standard of proof in a departmental inquiry is the balance of probabilities
records.text: The standard of proof in a departmental inquiry is the balance of probabilities and is lower than in a criminal trial. The inquiry officer must still follow the prescribed procedure, observe natural justice and give the delinquent a fair opportunity of defence, and the quality of the inquiry matters more than the length of its report. Ref: Syed Baqir Riffat Gardezi, Ejaz Ahmad (Sub-Engineer) and Abdul Hameed Khan Khosa v. Secretary to the Government of the Punjab (C.P.L.A. No. 215-L, 556 and 557 of 2024, decided 27.11.2025).
records.title: Syed Baqir Riffat Gardezi, Ejaz Ahmad (Sub-Engineer) and Abdul Hameed Khan Khosa v. Secretary to the Government of the Punjab (C.P.L.A. No. 215-L, 556 and 557 of 2024, decided 27.11.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Bench Jurisdiction: Constitutional Bench Matters
records.heading: A matter requiring a Constitutional Bench heard by a Regular Bench results in an order without jurisdiction
records.text: A court cannot pass an order unless competent to adjudicate the matter, and where a court sits in benches the case must fall within the assigned bench's jurisdiction. A matter requiring a Constitutional Bench under Art. 202A, if heard by a Regular Bench, results in an order without jurisdiction. Jurisdiction must be determined at the outset. Ref: Khalid Mehmood v. Pakistan, through Secretary, Ministry of Finance and others (Civil Petition No. 2202 of 2025, hearing 27.11.2025).
records.title: Khalid Mehmood v. Pakistan, through Secretary, Ministry of Finance and others (Civil Petition No. 2202 of 2025, hearing 27.11.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Wakalatnama: No Authority to Compromise
records.heading: A Wakalatnama does not give an advocate authority to compromise without the party's express consent
records.text: Read with O. III R. 4 CPC and s. 22(3) of the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act 1973, a Wakalatnama appoints an advocate to appear and act for a party but does not confer authority to compromise without the party's express consent. The authority to compound or settle rests with the parties. Ref: Riaz Hussain, through Legal Representatives v. Chairman Federal Land Commissioner (C.P.L.A. 962/2023 to 964/2023, hearing 02.12.2025).
records.title: Riaz Hussain, through Legal Representatives v. Chairman Federal Land Commissioner (C.P.L.A. 962/2023 to 964/2023, hearing 02.12.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Evacuee Trust Property Board: Dispute Between Governments
records.heading: The Evacuee Trust Property Board is the proper litigant, and its dispute with a provincial department is not between Governments
records.text: Under ss. 3(1) and 4(2)(s) of the Evacuee Trust Properties (Management and Disposal) Act 1975 the Board is the proper litigating entity for evacuee trust property. A dispute between a federal statutory corporation and a provincial department is not a dispute between two Governments within Art. 184(1), now Art. 175E(1). Ref: Central Government through Chairman Evacuee Trust Property Board, etc. v. Member Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore, etc. (C.P.L.A. No. 1451-L/2024, hearing 09.12.2025).
records.title: Central Government through Chairman Evacuee Trust Property Board, etc. v. Member Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore, etc. (C.P.L.A. No. 1451-L/2024, hearing 09.12.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recovery Proceedings: Missing Daily Diary and Procedure
records.heading: A missing Daily Diary entry and unexplained shifting of proceedings made the recovery case highly doubtful
records.text: Failure to produce the Daily Diary entry of the police party's departure supports an inference that proceedings were conducted at the police station. No proof of ownership of the motorcycle or of the petitioner's possession of the premises was produced, and the shifting of proceedings from the place of apprehension was unexplained. The prosecution case was highly doubtful. Ref: Muhammad Abdullah Tariq v. The State etc (Criminal Appeal No. 159-L of 2021, decided 02.10.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Abdullah Tariq v. The State etc (Criminal Appeal No. 159-L of 2021, decided 02.10.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Protection of Ownership of Immoveable Property Ordinance 2025
records.heading: Challenge to a Dispute Resolution Committee direction under the Punjab Ownership Ordinance 2025; notice to Advocate General
records.text: The petitioner challenged a direction of a Dispute Resolution Committee headed by the Deputy Commissioner as violating s. 8(2)(c) of the Ordinance. The Additional Advocate General stated that the Ordinance was repealed on 18.12.2025 by an Act of the same name. Since interpretation of the law was in issue, notice to the Advocate General was ordered under O. XXVII-A CPC. Ref: Mumtaz Hussain v. Govt. of Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 76106 of 2025, decided 22.12.2025).
records.title: Mumtaz Hussain v. Govt. of Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 76106 of 2025, decided 22.12.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Protection of Ownership of Immoveable Property Ordinance 2025
records.heading: Lahore High Court order on challenge to the Punjab Ownership Ordinance 2025 and its repeal
records.text: The Urdu caption describes this as a Lahore High Court order halting implementation of the Ordinance. The order records a challenge to a Dispute Resolution Committee direction under s. 8(2)(c), the statement that the Ordinance was repealed on 18.12.2025 by an Act, and notice to the Advocate General under O. XXVII-A CPC. Ref: Mumtaz Hussain v. Govt. of Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 76106 of 2025, decided 22.12.2025).
records.title: Mumtaz Hussain v. Govt. of Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 76106 of 2025, decided 22.12.2025)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Registration of Sale Deed Not Deemed Knowledge
records.heading: Registration of a sale deed is not deemed knowledge of the pre-emptor for talab-i-muwathibat
records.text: For talab-i-muwathibat, registration of a sale deed cannot be treated as deemed knowledge of the pre-emptor, because the statute makes actual acquisition of knowledge decisive and constructive knowledge would rewrite the law. Raising verbal cross objections at the revisional stage ought to be discouraged. Ref: 2025 LHC 7822; Muhammad Bashir etc v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 111-14, decided 19.11.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Bashir etc v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 111-14, decided 19.11.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Wife's Withdrawal Statement: Recall for Fraud
records.heading: A vulnerable litigant's statement must be shown to be voluntary, understood and free from fraud
records.text: A litigant's recorded statement is generally given full weight but the court must examine whether it was voluntary and free from undue influence or fraud. When recording a statement of a vulnerable litigant such as a woman in a family matter, the court must ensure it is understood, recorded in a language she comprehends and read over to her, with a literate kin if she is illiterate. Ref: 2025 LHC 7834; Asif Iqbal v. ADJ etc. (WP-9844-24, decided 10.12.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Asif Iqbal v. ADJ etc. (WP-9844-24, decided 10.12.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Remand Not to Be Ordered as a Matter of Course
records.heading: An appellate court should not remand where merits findings were recorded after a full trial
records.text: An appellate court must examine whether remand would meaningfully advance justice. Where findings on merits were already recorded after a full trial, remand only prolongs litigation, and the appellate court should itself reappraise the evidence. The remand ordered on the limitation issue served no useful purpose. Ref: 2025 LHC 7830; Ahmad Nasrullah, etc. v. Shahadat Ali, etc. (C.R. No. 415 of 2018, hearing 03.12.2025).
records.title: Ahmad Nasrullah, etc. v. Shahadat Ali, etc. (C.R. No. 415 of 2018, hearing 03.12.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI R. 1 CPC: List of Witnesses
records.heading: A list of witnesses must be filed within seven days of framing issues under Order XVI Rule 1
records.text: Under O. XVI R. 1 CPC a list of witnesses must be filed within seven days of framing of issues, and other witnesses may be called only with the court's permission on good cause, with reasons recorded. No good reason was shown, and a document should be proved by obtaining a certified copy. The order dismissing the application was upheld. Ref: 2025 LHC 7782; Haji Mushtaq Hussain Shah v. Senior Civil Judge etc (Writ Petition-4874-20, decided 28.10.2025); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: Haji Mushtaq Hussain Shah v. Senior Civil Judge etc (Writ Petition-4874-20, decided 28.10.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence and Remand
records.heading: The appellate court must itself take additional evidence under Order XLI Rule 27 rather than remand
records.text: Where evidence was produced and a reasoned judgment recorded, the case is not remanded for de novo hearing to allow additional evidence. Under O. XLI R. 27 and R. 28 CPC the appellate court must itself take or direct additional evidence and decide the appeal. Setting aside the whole judgment without reversing findings on merits was unlawful. Ref: 2025 LHC 7777; Mst. Bashiran Bibi v. ADJ etc (WP-15728-19, decided 23.10.2025); Justice Rasaal Hasan Syed.
records.title: Mst. Bashiran Bibi v. ADJ etc (WP-15728-19, decided 23.10.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Road Certificate Prevails Over Oral Evidence
records.heading: An entry in a Road Certificate can be negated only by a document of superior legal value
records.text: An entry in a Road Certificate regarding dispatch of case property can only be negated by a document of superior legal value and not by oral evidence. The Investigating Officer and the Moharrar gave consistent accounts of dispatch of the sample to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency, and Ex.DA showed the dispatch details. Ref: 2025 LHC 7841; Naseem alias Seemay Shah v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 68455/23, decided 18.12.2025); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Naseem alias Seemay Shah v. The State etc. (Crl. A. 68455/23, decided 18.12.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Offence Under s. 228 PPC in Court's Presence
records.heading: A beneficiary of an oral gift excluding a daughter bears a heavy onus to prove it
records.text: For an offence under s. 228 PPC committed in the court's presence, the court may proceed under s. 480 CrPC (same day, fine up to Rs.200, with imprisonment only in default), under s. 476 CrPC (summary trial, up to three months or fine up to Rs.1,000, or both), or forward the case to a Magistrate under s. 482 CrPC. Ref: 2025 LHC 7857; Dr Faheem Ikram Butt v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 8188/21, decided 13.11.2025); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Dr Faheem Ikram Butt v. The State etc. (Crl. Revision 8188/21, decided 13.11.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Motor Vehicles Rules: Stand Licence Not Heritable
records.heading: Evidence from an earlier proceeding is relevant under Article 47 QSO only on its stated conditions
records.text: A stand licence under r. 253 of the Motor Vehicles Rules 1969 is a permission and a privilege and not a property right, so it does not devolve on legal heirs on a licensee's death. The proviso to r. 253(2) ties a private stand to the owner's application, and r. 266 gives the Regional Transport Authority power to revoke. Heirs may seek determination of shares in a civil court and apply afresh. Ref: 2025 LHC 7904; Khawaja Muhammad Asif and 7 Others v. Province of Punjab etc. (WP.48034/25, decided 15.12.2025); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Khawaja Muhammad Asif and 7 Others v. Province of Punjab etc. (WP.48034/25, decided 15.12.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody of Samples and s. 161 Statements
records.heading: Section 17 excludes the QSO and CPC from Family Court proceedings, save sections 10 and 11 CPC
records.text: Failure to prove safe custody and secure transmission of sample parcels to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency and deposit of the remaining case property is fatal to the prosecution. Material witnesses' statements not recorded under s. 161 CrPC require extreme caution, and an unexplained delay in recording one gives rise to reasonable doubt. Ref: 2025 LHC 7909; Ashfaq alias Saleem v. The State, etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 43161 of 2023, hearing 10.12.2025).
records.title: Ashfaq alias Saleem v. The State, etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 43161 of 2023, hearing 10.12.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Service of Summons: O. V Rr. 10-A, 17, 18 CPC
records.heading: Disputed gifts that deprive daughters of inheritance may be scrutinised by the courts
records.text: Under O. V R. 10-A CPC a notice by registered post AD is sent with the summons, and the acknowledgment or a postal endorsement of refusal is prima facie proof of service. Rule 17 prescribes affixation with a report, and R. 18 requires the serving officer's report, with the court to examine the officer and declare service or order fresh service. Ref: 2025 LHC 7965; Muhammad Hanif v. Abdul Razzaq (C.R. No. 782 of 2016, decided 10.12.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. Abdul Razzaq (C.R. No. 782 of 2016, decided 10.12.2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift Excluding Daughter: Burden of Proof
records.heading: A press clipping is explanatory evidence under Article 22 QSO and may be considered at the bail stage
records.text: Where exclusion of legal heirs is claimed through gift, there must be evidence justifying the disinheritance. The beneficiary bears a heavy onus to prove the prerequisites of a valid oral gift and special reasons for excluding the daughter, and mutation is not a document of title. The appellate court rightly set aside the trial court's decree. Ref: 2025 LHC 7956; Muhammad Riaz v. Mst. Najma Bibi and others (C.R. No. 1196 of 2023, decided 23.12.2025).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Mst. Najma Bibi and others (C.R. No. 1196 of 2023, decided 23.12.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 47 QSO: Evidence in Earlier Proceedings
records.heading: A court may take judicial notice of a news clipping, subject to relevance, authenticity and reliability
records.text: Evidence recorded in an earlier judicial proceeding is relevant in a later one under Art. 47 QSO only if the proceeding was between the same parties or their representatives in interest, the adverse party had the opportunity to cross-examine, and the issues were substantially identical. Evidence from an earlier jactitation suit could not be used against a non-party petitioner. Ref: 2025 LHC 7931; Razia Bibi v. A.D.J. etc. (WP-3950-21, decided 10.12.2025); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Razia Bibi v. A.D.J. etc. (WP-3950-21, decided 10.12.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: s. 17 Exclusion of CPC and QSO
records.heading: A Call Data Record without voice message or transcript does not connect the accused with the offence
records.text: By s. 17 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act 1964 the QSO and CPC do not apply to Family Court proceedings, save ss. 10 and 11 CPC. Section 13(3) empowers the Family Court to execute its own decree, and s. 64 CPC in any event voids private transfers of attached property by the judgment-debtor after attachment. Ref: 2025 YLR 2806; Mst. Najma Naz and another v. Mst. Farzana Kanwal and three others (Civil Revision No. 2823 of 2019).
records.title: Mst. Najma Naz and another v. Mst. Farzana Kanwal and three others (Civil Revision No. 2823 of 2019)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Disputed Gifts Depriving Daughters of Inheritance
records.heading: Where the drawer rebuts the section 118 presumption, the onus shifts to the holder to prove the transaction
records.text: Disputed gifts that deprive daughters of inheritance may be scrutinised by the courts, which retain power to examine the reasons and justification for such gifts so that no injustice is done. Ref: 2025 YLR 2806; Mst. Najma Naz and another v. Mst. Farzana Kanwal and three others (Civil Revision No. 2823 of 2019).
records.title: Mst. Najma Naz and another v. Mst. Farzana Kanwal and three others (Civil Revision No. 2823 of 2019)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Press Clipping as Explanatory Evidence at Bail Stage
records.heading: Pending civil suit on the same cheques makes a section 489-F case one of further inquiry
records.text: A press clipping is explanatory evidence under Art. 22 QSO and may be considered at the bail stage, where the court acts inquisitorially and can consider material capable of becoming admissible later. It must be read with other evidence, since as sole evidence it cannot prove a fact beyond reasonable doubt, and its cogency is determined at trial. Ref: 2025 YLR 2639, PLJ 2026 CrC Note 167; Samar Abbas v. State etc. (Crl. Misc.-699-B-25); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Samar Abbas v. State etc. (Crl. Misc.-699-B-25)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Judicial Notice of News Clipping: Arts. 111 and 112 QSO
records.heading: Election petition affidavits must be attested on oath, failing which the petition is rejected
records.text: Art. 112 QSO makes judicial notice obligatory for the facts listed, while Art. 111 gives the court discretion to notice other facts. A court can therefore take judicial notice of a news clipping, with admissibility depending on relevance, authenticity and reliability. The post also reports bail granted in a murder case under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: 2025 YLR 2639, PLJ 2026 CrC Note 167; Samar Abbas etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. Nos. 699-B of 2025 and 1362-B of 2025, decided 22.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Samar Abbas etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. Nos. 699-B of 2025 and 1362-B of 2025, decided 22.04.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: CDR Without Voice Message or Transcript
records.heading: An SHO is not an aggrieved person with a right of appeal against a narcotics acquittal
records.text: Call Data Record showing connection of the petitioners near the place of occurrence, without any voice message or transcript, does not connect them with the offence until the CDR is formalised in accordance with law. Ref: 2025 YLR 2639, PLJ 2026 CrC Note 167; Samar Abbas v. State etc. (Crl. Misc.-699-B-25); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Samar Abbas v. State etc. (Crl. Misc.-699-B-25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit on Cheque: Onus to Prove Underlying Transaction
records.heading: A credible victim as sole eyewitness may alone support conviction under sections 365-B and 376 PPC
records.text: Where the drawer denies execution or the underlying transaction and rebuts the s. 118 Negotiable Instruments Act presumption, the onus shifts to the holder to prove the transaction and consideration. The decrees under O. XXXVII CPC on the cheques were set aside. Ref: 2025 MLD 2001; Habal Masih v. Shahzad Vikcy (Regular First Appeals Nos. 18340 and 18345 of 2025).
records.title: Habal Masih v. Shahzad Vikcy (Regular First Appeals Nos. 18340 and 18345 of 2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: s. 489-F PPC Pre-Arrest Bail: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail granted to a juvenile on further inquiry where mandatory reports were not obtained
records.text: Where a transaction gives rise to civil and criminal liability, fraudulent intent must be determined on evidence at trial. A pending civil suit on the same cheques and claimed repayment made the case one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC, entitling the applicant to bail. Ref: 2025 MLD 2005.

records.subject: Election Law
records.topic: Election Petition: Defective Affidavits
records.heading: Article 164 QSO admits modern forensic techniques that are well established and widely accepted as reliable
records.text: Under s. 144(2)(a) of the Elections Act 2017 the petition must annex witnesses' affidavits, which must be attested on oath under s. 139 CPC and the Lahore High Court Rules. Affidavits bearing only an attestation stamp were not verified on oath, so the petition was rejected under s. 145(1). Ref: 2025 MLD 2010; Malik Touqeer Abbas Khokhar v. Malik Saif-ul-Malook Khokhar (Election Petition No. 20093).
records.title: Malik Touqeer Abbas Khokhar v. Malik Saif-ul-Malook Khokhar (Election Petition No. 20093)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Acquittal Appeal by SHO: Aggrieved Person
records.heading: Absence of resistance marks led to rape being treated as fornication under section 496-B PPC
records.text: An SHO who is the appellant in an acquittal appeal under the Control of Narcotic Substances Act 1997 is not an aggrieved person and has no right of appeal against the Special Court's acquittal. Prosecution is conducted through a Special Prosecutor under s. 50. The appeal was also time barred and was dismissed in limine. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 2001; The State through SI/SHO PS Railway v. Mahfia Kausar (Acquittal Appeal No. 451 of 2024).
records.title: The State through SI/SHO PS Railway v. Mahfia Kausar (Acquittal Appeal No. 451 of 2024)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Victim as Sole Eyewitness Sufficient
records.heading: Abduction and rape not proved; a consenting abductee cannot be punished without being charged
records.text: The victim was the sole eyewitness. Her account was consistent with the FIR and unshaken in cross-examination, and her admitted acquaintance with the accused supported the prosecution case. Her credible statement alone could safely support conviction under ss. 365-B and 376 PPC. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 589; Abdul Basit v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Basit v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 812 of 2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Juvenile Accused: Bail on Further Inquiry
records.heading: Mark-up earned in providing services is excluded from the gross amount charged for Punjab sales tax
records.text: The accused was about eleven years old when charged with an unnatural offence against a minor. The Investigating Officer had not examined the circumstances needed to establish mens rea and had not obtained the mandatory reports under ss. 5(1)(b) and 7(2) of the Juvenile Justice System Act 2018. For a younger child, more convincing evidence of maturity is required. Bail was granted on a further inquiry basis. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1279; Muhammad Latif alias Kala v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 1629-B of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Latif alias Kala v. The State (Crl. Misc. No. 1629-B of 2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 164 QSO: Modern Forensic Techniques
records.heading: A plaint is read as a whole and may be rejected if it discloses no cause of action
records.text: Courts must understand and be open to forensic science, and a trial judge acts as gatekeeper of scientific evidence. Art. 164 QSO is the gateway for evidence from modern devices and techniques, provided they are well established and widely accepted as reliable. The petition was dismissed and a recommendation went to the Ministry of Law. Ref: PLD 2021 SC 362; Ali Haider alias Papu v. Jameel Hussain (Criminal Petition No. 513 of 2020).
records.title: Ali Haider alias Papu v. Jameel Hussain (Criminal Petition No. 513 of 2020)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Absence of Resistance Marks: Rape Converted to Fornication
records.heading: An instrument meeting section 4 NI Act is a promissory note and needs no attestation
