records.text: The accused was empty handed, no marks of violence were found on the complainant and no torn clothes were recovered. The ingredients of s. 376 PPC were held not attracted, and the case was one of fornication under s. 496-B PPC. The complainant had not been challaned or charged under s. 496-B. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 662; Muhammad Imran v. The State (Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 374 of 2024 in Criminal Petition No. 725 of 2023); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. The State (Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 374 of 2024 in Criminal Petition No. 725 of 2023)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Abduction and Rape Not Proved: Consenting Abductee
records.heading: A suit for specific performance against an attorney who disclosed his principal; dismissal maintained
records.text: The abduction and rape story was an afterthought, with no recovery from the accused and no marks of violence in the medico-legal report, so ss. 365-B and 376 PPC were not made out. The abductee could not be punished under s. 496-B PPC as she was not made an accused and no charge was framed. The accused were acquitted. Ref: 2025 SCMR 699; Asif Masih v. The State (Jail Petition No. 481 of 2019).
records.title: Asif Masih v. The State (Jail Petition No. 481 of 2019)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Mark-up Excluded from Punjab Sales Tax on Services
records.heading: An available original must be produced as best evidence, and secondary evidence is admissible only if it is lost
records.text: Mark-up or interest earned in the course of providing services is service related, but r. 4 of the Punjab Sales Tax on Services (Specific Provisions) Rules 2012 excludes it from the gross amount charged. It therefore falls outside the taxable value. Ref: 2025 LHC 8073; FINCA Microfinance Commercial Bank Limited v. Commissioner (Enforcement) Punjab Revenue Authority etc. (Tax Reference 16460/23, decided 10.10.2025); Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains.
records.title: FINCA Microfinance Commercial Bank Limited v. Commissioner (Enforcement) Punjab Revenue Authority etc. (Tax Reference 16460/23, decided 10.10.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: A nomination under section 27 does not vest ownership in the nominee to the prejudice of heirs
records.text: On O. VII R. 11 CPC the plaint is read as a whole, and it can be rejected if its averments ex facie disclose no cause of action or the suit appears barred by law, including limitation. For a declaration suit under s. 42 Specific Relief Act, the right to sue arises only on accrual and infringement of the right. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 24; Misree Khan & others v. Abdul Ghafoor & others (C.P.L.A. 81-P of 2019, decided 14.11.2024); Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Misree Khan & others v. Abdul Ghafoor & others (C.P.L.A. 81-P of 2019, decided 14.11.2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Promissory Note: No Attestation Required
records.heading: Mere relationship does not make a witness unreliable, as substitution of the real culprit is extremely rare
records.text: An instrument meeting the four requirements of s. 4 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 is a promissory note, and Art. 17(2)(a) QSO on attestation does not apply, so non-appearance of a second attesting witness is inconsequential. The appeal was dismissed. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 45; Mehr Noor Muhammad v. Nazir Ahmed (Civil Appeal No. 317-L of 2011, decided 06.11.2023); Justice Munib Akhtar; Justice Shahid Waheed; Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Mehr Noor Muhammad v. Nazir Ahmed (Civil Appeal No. 317-L of 2011, decided 06.11.2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance Against Attorney Without Owner
records.heading: An absconder is a factual condition, while a proclaimed offender has a formal status under section 87 CrPC
records.text: The plaintiff sued the attorney alone on an agreement to sell, and later sought to add the owner after limitation against the owner had expired. The question under ss. 12 and 27 Specific Relief Act and s. 230 Contract Act was whether the suit lay against the attorney who had disclosed his principal. The High Court's dismissal was maintained and the appeal dismissed. Ref: PLD 2023 SC 653; Ijaz Ul Haq v. Mrs. Maroof Begum Ahmed and others (Civil Appeal No. 1121 of 2018, decided 16.08.2023); Justice Ijaz Ul Ahsan; Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Ijaz Ul Haq v. Mrs. Maroof Begum Ahmed and others (Civil Appeal No. 1121 of 2018, decided 16.08.2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 76(c) QSO: Secondary Evidence of Documents
records.heading: Observations in a bail order are tentative and must not influence the trial court
records.text: An original document that exists and is available must be produced as the best evidence, and secondary evidence is admissible only if the original is lost. Art. 76(c) protects a person who, despite best efforts, cannot produce the original. The petition was allowed and the matter treated as pending before the trial court for fresh decision. Ref: 2020 CLC 1950; Mst. Balqees Begum v. Additional District Judge and others (W.P. No. 32414 of 2015, decided 24.09.2020); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Balqees Begum v. Additional District Judge and others (W.P. No. 32414 of 2015, decided 24.09.2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Co-operative Societies Act: Section 54 Order and Civil Courts
records.heading: A husband's continued residence or receipt of rents does not invalidate his gift to his wife
records.text: Sections 27 and 54 of the Co-operative Societies Act 1925 operate in a complementary way, and the proviso to s. 54 requires the Registrar to allow a civil court to decide complicated questions of law and fact. A nomination under s. 27 does not vest ownership in the nominee to the prejudice of heirs and is not an unimpeachable determination of title. Ref: 2025 LHC 8107; Rana Muhammad Iqbal v. Rao Khalil Ur Rehman (Civil Revision-178-18, decided 10.12.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Rana Muhammad Iqbal v. Rao Khalil Ur Rehman (Civil Revision-178-18, decided 10.12.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Eyewitnesses and Substitution of Culprit
records.heading: Under Mohammadan Law a presumptive heir has no standing to challenge the donor's gift in his lifetime
records.text: Mere relationship does not render a witness unworthy of reliance where presence is natural and the testimony is firm and supported by independent circumstances. Substitution of the real culprit by close relatives is an extremely rare phenomenon. The post also notes that cases under s. 302(c) PPC are left to judicial discretion. Ref: Shahzad Liaquat v. The State (Crl.A.503/2022, decided 25.11.2025); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Shahzad Liaquat v. The State (Crl.A.503/2022, decided 25.11.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Absconder Versus Proclaimed Offender
records.heading: A dying declaration is admissible without a belief in imminent death, and unproved motive mitigates sentence
records.text: An absconder is a factual condition identified by the police, with warrants issued under ss. 75 to 86-A CrPC. A proclaimed offender has a formal legal status declared by the court under s. 87 CrPC after proclamation, and such a declaration made by due process may be used against the accused to prove guilt. Ref: 2025 LHC 4326; Asad Abbas alias Achoo v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 10141-J/2022).
records.title: Asad Abbas alias Achoo v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 10141-J/2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Order Observations Are Tentative
records.heading: The rounding-off provision must be read with section 22 to prevent denial of pension on marginal shortfall
records.text: Observations made in a bail order are tentative in nature and must not influence the trial court in any manner. The post lists authorities for the proposition. Ref: 2025 YLR 2236, 2025 YLR 2218, 2025 YLR 1951, 2025 PCrLJ 1543 and others.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift by Husband to Wife: Continued Residence and Rents
records.heading: Bail in murder allowed on further inquiry where attendance record and CDR did not connect the petitioners
records.text: In a gift of immovable property by a husband to his wife, his continued residence in the house or receipt of rents after the gift does not invalidate it, the presumption being that he collects rents as rent collector for the wife. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 339; Syed Masood Ali v. Mst. Feroza Begum and another (Civil Petition 552-K of 2021 & 1108-K of 2023).
records.title: Syed Masood Ali v. Mst. Feroza Begum and another (Civil Petition 552-K of 2021 & 1108-K of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Spes Successionis: Heirs Cannot Challenge Donor's Gift
records.heading: CCTV footage not properly produced, played or forensically matched is of no avail to the prosecution
records.text: Under Mohammadan Law spes successionis is not recognised, so a presumptive heir has no right in the property until the owner's death. A donor who made the gift voluntarily, affirmed it in his lifetime and never questioned it leaves his heirs without standing to dispute its validity. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 339; Syed Masood Ali v. Mst. Feroza Begum and another (Civil Petition 552-K of 2021 & 1108-K of 2023).
records.title: Syed Masood Ali v. Mst. Feroza Begum and another (Civil Petition 552-K of 2021 & 1108-K of 2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Art. 46 QSO
records.heading: Where suicide is pleaded, a gunshot residue test of the deceased's hands is necessary
records.text: A dying declaration is admissible under Art. 46 QSO without any pre-condition that the maker expected imminent death, and courts attach great importance to it. Failure to prove the alleged motive was held a mitigating circumstance justifying conversion of the death sentence into imprisonment for life. Ref: Riaz (decd) through his brother Abdur Rauf v. Gulzar and another (Crl.P.L.A.99-P/2019, decided 13.08.2025).
records.title: Riaz (decd) through his brother Abdur Rauf v. Gulzar and another (Crl.P.L.A.99-P/2019, decided 13.08.2025)

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Rounding-Off Provision and Qualifying Period Under s. 22
records.heading: A wife may sue for dissolution or dower where she ordinarily resides under Rule 6
records.text: Every provision must be given effect, so the rounding-off mechanism in the Schedule must be read harmoniously with s. 22 of the Act. It is a substantive remedial tool to prevent denial of pensionary benefits on marginal shortfalls and applies when eligibility is determined. Ref: Employees Old-age Benefits Institution, Lahore and others v. Muhammad Rafique, etc. (C.P.L.A. No. 1567/2025, hearing 09-12-2025).
records.title: Employees Old-age Benefits Institution, Lahore and others v. Muhammad Rafique, etc. (C.P.L.A. No. 1567/2025, hearing 09-12-2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Murder: Attendance Record and Further Inquiry
records.heading: A party may seek forensic examination of a recording, and additional evidence may be allowed at any stage
records.text: The attendance record showed one petitioner at his workplace on the day of the murder, and the company's contrary stance was unsupported by material. With the CDR lacking voice or transcript, the petitioners had made out a case for further inquiry. Investigation was complete and they had been in custody since 17.10.2024, so bail was allowed. Ref: 2025 YLR 2639, PLJ 2026 CrC Note 167; Samar Abbas etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. Nos. 699-B of 2025 and 1362-B of 2025, decided 22.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Samar Abbas etc. v. State etc. (Crl. Misc. Nos. 699-B of 2025 and 1362-B of 2025, decided 22.04.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inconclusive CCTV Footage
records.heading: A judgment-debtor who delayed execution cannot object to payment of a money decree in cash
records.text: CCTV footage from a petrol pump was of no avail to the prosecution where the person who produced it was not joined in investigation or examined at trial, the footage was not played in court for identification, and the forensic facial comparison was inconclusive. Ref: 2023 YLR Note 82.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Suicide Plea and Gunshot Residue Test
records.heading: A vague description of weapons in the FIR casts doubt on the eyewitness's presence
records.text: Where the prosecution alleged murder by firing and the accused pleaded suicide, a gunshot residue test of the deceased's hands was necessary. A stellate forehead wound can indicate a contact shot consistent with suicide, to be assessed with location, weapon and ballistic evidence. Ref: 2025 LHC 5787; Jamroz Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 47572/23, decided 16-09-2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Jamroz Khan v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 47572/23, decided 16-09-2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: R. 6 Family Courts Rules: Territorial Jurisdiction of Wife
records.heading: An FIR lodged after preliminary investigation is a procedural misstep detrimental to the prosecution
records.text: Rule 6 of the Family Courts Rules 1965 lets a wife sue for dissolution or dower in the court where she ordinarily resides. The Family Courts Act 1964 does not prohibit calling a witness not on the list, so summoning the Nikah Khawan was proper, and the medical examination application was unwarranted. Ref: PLD 2025 Peshawar 54.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Forensic Examination of Video Evidence
records.heading: Concealment of real facts by the complainant party made the case one of open gunfight
records.text: A party may apply to a court to send an audio or video recording for forensic examination of its genuineness. By O. XVIII R. 17 CPC additional evidence can be allowed at any stage, so the trial court erred in refusing after closure of evidence. The civil revision was allowed. Ref: PLD 2025 Peshawar 50.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Money Decree: Payment in Cash
records.heading: An eyewitness who escaped unhurt at close range and kept his clothes failed to prove his presence
records.text: A judgment-debtor who delayed execution of a long-standing money decree on flimsy grounds could not object to payment in cash and insist on a cross-cheque. The executing court's order for cash payment was upheld, and frivolous litigation was condemned as abuse of process. Ref: 2025 YLR 1452.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Vague Description of Weapons in FIR
records.heading: A declaration suit against Wajib-ul-Arz entries was time barred, and the entries carry a presumption of truth
records.text: The FIR described the assailants' weapons only as 'Aslaha Atisheen' despite firing from about 20 paces in daylight, and the eyewitness also named no weapons. This omission cast doubt on the presence of the eyewitness and was detrimental to the prosecution. Ref: 2025 YLR 1284.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: FIR Lodged After Preliminary Investigation
records.heading: Where eyewitnesses fail to prove presence, conflict with medical evidence counts in favour of the accused
records.text: The medico-legal certificate showed the victim examined at 5:20 pm, before the FIR time of 5:45 pm, although the prosecution said the report preceded the examination. This suggested the report was lodged after preliminary investigation, a procedural misstep detrimental to the prosecution. Ref: 2025 YLR 1284.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Concealment of Facts: Open Gunfight
records.heading: Conflict between the FIR and the site plan questions the complainant's reliability
records.text: A report by an injured accused, his medico-legal certificate and the eyewitness's admission showed the complainant party concealed the real facts, so it was a case of open gunfight. The aggressor could not be determined, and concealment of injuries to the other side has been considered in favour of the accused. Ref: 2025 YLR 1284.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Presence Not Proved
records.heading: A Daily Diary counter version showed the prosecution suppressed real facts, benefiting the appellants
records.text: An unrelated eyewitness who escaped unhurt from three shots fired at close range, remained standing and did not hand over blood-stained clothes failed to establish his presence at the spot. With no other evidence linking the appellant, the benefit of doubt went to him. Ref: 2025 YLR 1284.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Wajib-ul-Arz Entries: Limitation and Presumption of Truth
records.heading: Few empties, cartridges and marks of struggle indicated a free fight between the parties
records.text: A declaration suit filed in 2000 to challenge Wajib-ul-Arz entries of 1965/1966 was hopelessly time barred. Wajib-ul-Arz is part of the Record of Rights and carries a presumption of truth that needs strong, unimpeachable evidence to rebut. The concurrent dismissal was not interfered with in revision. Ref: 2025 YLR 1017.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Medical and Ocular Evidence
records.heading: No conviction can be awarded for injuries to an injured person who was not examined
records.text: Medical evidence is confirmatory, but where the eyewitnesses fail to establish their presence, a conflict between it and the ocular account counts in favour of the accused. Here the pattern of injuries and the time of death conflicted with the eyewitness version. Ref: 2025 YLR 632.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between FIR and Site Plan
records.heading: Failure to send hair found with the deceased for DNA was a defect in investigation
records.text: The complainant's report alleged indiscriminate firing without specific roles, while the site plan he verified assigned specific injuries and weapons to each accused. The conflict questioned his reliability, and the witness on whose pointation the plan was prepared was not produced. Ref: 2025 YLR 1702.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Counter Version and Suppression of Real Facts
records.heading: Inconsistent accounts of who pointed out the spot cast doubt on the place of occurrence
records.text: A Daily Diary counter version showed an accused was injured in the same episode and the site plan placed him on the spot, so the prosecution suppressed the real facts. The trial court misread the evidence, and the benefit of such concealment should extend to the appellants. Ref: 2025 YLR 1702.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Free Fight Inferred From Empties and Cartridges
records.heading: Multiple firearm injuries excluded the stated manner of firing, damaging the prosecution case
records.text: Few empties and live and misfired cartridges collected from the spot, with marks of struggle noted by the Investigating Officer, indicated a free fight between the parties, although eleven accused were charged. The witnesses stayed silent on that aspect. Ref: 2025 YLR 1702.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction for Injuries to Unexamined Injured
records.heading: Conscious dishonest improvements by the complainant undermine his testimony despite the stamp of injuries
records.text: The trial court illegally convicted the appellants for injuries to injured persons who were not examined. Once an injured witness does not appear in support of his claim, no conviction can be awarded for the injury caused to him. Ref: 2025 YLR 1702.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Defective Investigation: Hair Not Sent for DNA
records.heading: Death sentence altered to life where a labourer killed his wife in sudden heat of passion
records.text: Human hair found in the deceased's possession, collected by the Medical Officer and handed to the Investigating Officer, was not sent for DNA. This was the best evidence of the accused's identity, and the Investigating Officer's reluctance to send it was a factor the court could not ignore. Ref: 2025 YLR 1752.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Site Plan: Inconsistent Pointation
records.heading: Contradictory section 342 CrPC replies do not help the accused, and Article 122 QSO applies to facts within his knowledge
records.text: The complainant and the Investigating Officer gave inconsistent accounts of who pointed out the spot and when the site plan was prepared, and the eyewitness named as pointer was not produced. The inconsistency cast doubt on the place of occurrence. Ref: 2025 YLR 1752.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Conflicting With Ocular Account
records.heading: Medical evidence supported the ocular account, as a struggling victim may change the direction of a wound
records.text: Multiple firearm injuries on the deceased excluded the stated manner of firing, and there were no marks of violence or close-range entries to support a struggle. The conflict between the eyewitness account and medical evidence damaged the prosecution case beyond repair. Ref: 2025 YLR 1752.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Complainant
records.heading: A conflict between medical evidence and the ocular account bears adversely on the prosecution
records.text: The complainant's court statement improved on the FIR regarding the sequence of firing and omitted the firing at the female eyewitness. The improvements were conscious and dishonest, and stamp of injuries alone shows presence but does not make the whole testimony true. Ref: 2025 YLR 1752.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Altered to Life: Sudden Heat of Passion
records.heading: Refusing appointment solely on a past FIR ending in acquittal violates Articles 4, 9 and 18
records.text: A poor labourer with ten children, under economic and mental stress after shifting to a one-room house, acted in sudden heat of passion and not on premeditated design when he killed his wife. Guilt was proved but the death sentence was altered to imprisonment for life. Ref: 2025 YLR 2065.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: s. 342 CrPC Plea and Art. 122 QSO
records.heading: Article 199 requires an aggrieved person showing concrete legal injury and no adequate remedy
records.text: The appellant's contradictory replies under s. 342 CrPC, without evidence on oath under s. 340(2) or proof of absence, did not help him. Art. 122 QSO applies to facts especially within his knowledge, and his flight from fear of police supported the prosecution. The death sentence was altered to life imprisonment. Ref: 2025 YLR 2065.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Supporting Ocular Account
records.heading: A hostile witness resiles to damage the calling party, unlike an unfavourable witness
records.text: The direction of the neck wound did not exclude the presence of the deceased and the appellant, since a person struggling after another injury may change direction. Medical evidence is confirmatory and may be considered where the witnesses were consistent, and here it supported the ocular account. Ref: 2025 YLR 2101.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Section 540-A CrPC allows the accused to be exempted from personal attendance, including acquittal in absentia
records.text: A conflict between medical evidence and the ocular account has an adverse bearing on the prosecution case and cannot be ignored when determining the accused's guilt. Ref: 2025 YLR 2298.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Appointment Denied Despite Acquittal
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC permits summoning an additional witness but cannot fill gaps left by a party
records.text: Refusal of police appointment solely on a past FIR followed by acquittal under s. 249-A CrPC, without conviction, moral turpitude or suppression, was held to violate Arts. 4, 9 and 18 of the Constitution. Acquittal on merit restores the presumption of innocence and denial on that basis was arbitrary. Ref: 2025 PLC (C.S.) 1657; Muhammad Mehboob Hayat v. Inspector General of Police, Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 4903 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Mehboob Hayat v. Inspector General of Police, Punjab and others (Writ Petition No. 4903 of 2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 199: Aggrieved Person Requirement
records.heading: A first section 342 CrPC statement has no effect once further witnesses are examined
records.text: Jurisdiction under Art. 199 is original but subject to the absence of another adequate remedy. Whether a party is an aggrieved person is a mixed question of law and fact, and a government department must show a concrete legal injury rather than a procedural grievance. The consultative process under Rule 8(2) was not shown to have been initiated, so judicial intervention was not warranted. Ref: 2025 LHC 8168; Federal Board of Revenue through Additional Commissioner Inland Revenue Lahore v. Federation Investigation Agency etc (WP 46443/24, decided 29.04.2025); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Federal Board of Revenue through Additional Commissioner Inland Revenue Lahore v. Federation Investigation Agency etc (WP 46443/24, decided 29.04.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hostile Witness and Unfavourable Witness
records.heading: An application to discard recorded evidence is not ordinarily maintainable under section 561-A CrPC
records.text: A hostile witness resiles from an earlier statement to damage the calling party, while an unfavourable witness gives contrary evidence without hostile intention. Under Art. 150 QSO the court has discretion, to be used with care, to let the calling party cross-examine its witness. Refusal to declare defence witnesses hostile was upheld. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 644.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 540-A CrPC: Acquittal in Absentia
records.heading: A USB may be exhibited under Articles 46-A and 164 QSO, and a section 540 application should not be dismissed summarily
records.text: Section 540-A CrPC allows dispensing with an accused's personal attendance when represented by a pleader among multiple accused. The trial court was justified in acquitting the accused in absentia where no prima facie case existed and co-accused had been acquitted on the same evidence. The appeal was dismissed in limine. Ref: 2025 YLR 2433.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Additional Witness
records.heading: Section 265-F CrPC gives both sides equal opportunity to summon witnesses, including those not listed
records.text: The trial court may summon a witness not in the calendar of witnesses where essential for a just decision, but s. 540 CrPC cannot be used to fill gaps left by a party. Where copies of statements and documents were not supplied to the accused at the start of trial, the complainant could not belatedly examine such witnesses. The High Court declined to interfere with dismissal of the application. Ref: 2014 PCrLJ 1504.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Second Statement under S. 342 CrPC
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC confers wide power to examine any person essential for a just decision
records.text: After further prosecution witnesses were examined, the first s. 342 CrPC statement had no legal effect and a fresh statement was required. The eye-witness evidence of the stabbing was not put to the accused in the fresh statement, so it stood excluded from consideration. The prosecution was held to have failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2025 YLR 816.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 561-A CrPC: Discarding Recorded Evidence
records.heading: An accused who lawfully left the country on bail is not an absconder and may be exempted from appearance
records.text: An application to discard previously recorded evidence, alleging tampering with the court file, was held not ordinarily maintainable before the High Court. The applicant had not objected when the evidence was read back or applied to the trial court for correction, and had shown no exceptional circumstances justifying use of s. 561-A CrPC in ongoing proceedings. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1454.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: USB as Evidence
records.heading: A witness cannot be declared hostile during cross-examination, and mere retraction does not make one hostile
records.text: A USB is a device generated through an automated system and may be exhibited under Arts. 46-A and 164 QSO, subject to the opposing party's right of cross-examination. An application under s. 540 CrPC should not be summarily dismissed as belated or as filling a lacuna. The High Court set aside the trial court's order and allowed the application. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 837.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F and S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Witnesses
records.heading: A hostile daughter's presence at the scene was doubtful given her unnatural conduct and residence elsewhere
records.text: S. 265-F CrPC gives both sides equal opportunity to summon witnesses and does not confine the court to witnesses whose s. 161 statements were recorded or who are listed in the challan. Under s. 540 CrPC a material witness may be summoned even if not listed. The summoning order was well reasoned and the High Court declined to interfere in revision. Ref: 2017 PCrLJ 294.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-F(1) and (3) and S. 540 CrPC: Witnesses
records.heading: A withdrawal based on a private arrangement is a withdrawal simpliciter and bars a fresh suit
records.text: Under s. 265-F(1) CrPC the court must take all evidence produced by the prosecution, while summoning a witness through the court is subject to permission and may be refused under s. 265-F(3) if sought for vexation or delay. No bar exists on examining a person whose s. 161 statement was not recorded, and s. 540 CrPC confers wide power to examine any person essential for a just decision. Ref: 2016 PCrLJ 1124.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Exemption from Personal Appearance: S. 540-A CrPC
records.heading: A Family Court may forbid indecent or irrelevant questions and must curb delay in cross-examination
records.text: An accused who twice left the country lawfully while on bail, with his father and counsel appearing, was not to be treated as an absconder and should have been granted exemption. Exemption under s. 540-A CrPC is ordinarily for cases with two or more accused, but may be granted in suitable cases to a single accused even if not physically present. Ref: 2022 MLD 1325.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Declaration and Reliance
records.heading: Pension is a vested right not extinguished by delay in applying
records.text: A witness cannot be declared hostile during cross-examination, and reliance on eye-witnesses so declared was against settled principles. Mere retraction does not make a witness hostile, as the two concepts are distinct. The prosecution was held not to have proved guilt beyond reasonable doubt, with doubt resolved in favour of the accused. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1584.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Presence at Scene Doubtful
records.heading: A chance witness must give a plausible explanation for his presence, failing which his testimony is unsafe
records.text: A daughter of the deceased declared hostile had given a s. 161 CrPC account, but defence cross-examination made her presence doubtful given her unnatural conduct and her residence elsewhere. The prosecution did not show why she resiled from her earlier version, so the safe inference was that she did not witness the occurrence. Ref: 2025 MLD 1544.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal Simpliciter Bars Fresh Suit
records.heading: Under section 149 PPC each member is liable for offences in prosecution of the common object of section 141
records.text: A withdrawal based on a private arrangement, not recognised by the court or reflected in its order, is a withdrawal simpliciter and attracts the bar in O. XXIII R. 1(3) CPC against a fresh suit on the same subject-matter. The subsequent suit was barred by law and by limitation, and failure to challenge the withdrawal order estopped the petitioners. Ref: Sohail Islam and another v. Saadullah Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 5071/2025, decided 05.01.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Sohail Islam and another v. Saadullah Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 5071/2025, decided 05.01.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: Curbing Lengthy and Irrelevant Cross-Examination
records.heading: Separation of powers bars the executive from sitting over a binding judgment
records.text: Unduly lengthy cross-examination with irrelevant questions can deprive contradictions of significance. Under the second proviso to s. 11 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act 1964, the Family Court may forbid questions that are indecent, scandalous, frivolous, insulting, annoying or needlessly offensive. Courts must actively curb delay in family proceedings. Ref: Harris Rasheed and another v. The Learned Guardian Judge and 2 others (W.P. No. 64981 of 2025, decided 08.01.2026).
records.title: Harris Rasheed and another v. The Learned Guardian Judge and 2 others (W.P. No. 64981 of 2025, decided 08.01.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension as Vested Right: Delay No Bar
records.heading: An unbroken chain of safe custody is the backbone of a narcotics case and must be put to the accused
records.text: Pension is a constitutional and legal right of a government employee, not a concession. The right accrues on retirement or acceptance of resignation and is not extinguished by a 13-year delay in applying. The petitioner had over 20 years of service, meeting the qualifying period after the 2001 amendment. The Federal Service Tribunal decision was set aside. Ref: Muhammad Usman v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Finance, Finance Division, Islamabad and others (C.P.L.A. 4065/2024, decided 07.01.2026); Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui; Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan; Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Finance, Finance Division, Islamabad and others (C.P.L.A. 4065/2024, decided 07.01.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Proof of Presence
records.heading: Section 342 CrPC examination reflects audi alteram partem, and material not put to the accused cannot be relied upon
records.text: An eyewitness must establish his presence at the scene through strong, independent and confidence-inspiring evidence. A chance witness must give a plausible and convincing explanation for his presence, failing which his testimony is unsafe to sustain a conviction. Doubt gives the accused the benefit as of right. Ref: Munir Ahmad and Zulfiqar @ Kala v. The State (Crl.A. 11-L/2021, decided 07.01.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Munir Ahmad and Zulfiqar @ Kala v. The State (Crl.A. 11-L/2021, decided 07.01.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 149 and S. 141 PPC: Common Object
records.heading: A motive not reported to police is not doubtful, but death sentence was inconsistent with proportionality
records.text: The common object of an unlawful assembly must be one of the five objects in s. 141 PPC, and under s. 149 PPC each member is liable where the offence is committed in prosecution of the common object, with a nexus between the two. The post also notes that an offence under s. 354-A PPC falls within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Ref: Ashfaque Hussain and others v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 187-K/2025, decided 06.11.2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Ashfaque Hussain and others v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 187-K/2025, decided 06.11.2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Separation of Powers: Executive and Binding Judgments
records.heading: Inability of injured witnesses to identify assailants does not diminish the eyewitnesses' credibility
records.text: Separation of powers is a central guarantee of just government and interpretation of law is a judicial prerogative. The executive cannot sit over a binding judgment. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 17; Ayesha Iftikhar etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 220388/18).
records.title: Ayesha Iftikhar etc v. Federation of Pakistan etc (Writ Petition 220388/18)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Safe Custody Not Put Under S. 342 CrPC
records.heading: Police constables who fired at a motorcar acted in disproportionate excess of their lawful authority
records.text: The accused was not confronted in his s. 342 CrPC statement with the chain of safe custody, including separation and storage of the sample and its dispatch to the laboratory. An unbroken chain is the backbone of a narcotics case, and evidence not put to the accused cannot sustain conviction. The accused was acquitted. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 47; Qaiser alias Aaun v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 24404/2019).
records.title: Qaiser alias Aaun v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 24404/2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Scope and Purpose
records.heading: Mere abscondence is insufficient to maintain conviction without other reliable evidence
records.text: S. 342 CrPC examination enables the accused to explain circumstances appearing in the evidence against him and reflects the principle of audi alteram partem. Incriminating material not put to the accused cannot be relied upon to secure conviction. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 47; Qaiser alias Aaun v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 24404/2019).
records.title: Qaiser alias Aaun v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 24404/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Not Reported to Police; Death Sentence
records.heading: Blackening improbable at the site plan distance and mismatched medical times belied the witnesses' presence
records.text: A motive touching the dignity and honour of a family, disclosed only to the father, is not rendered doubtful by the absence of any prior report to police, and the motive was not artificial or improbable. On sentencing, the court held imposition of the death penalty inconsistent with proportionality and individualised sentencing in the circumstances. Ref: Javed Ali v. The State (J.P. 202/2025, decided 21.01.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Javed Ali v. The State (J.P. 202/2025, decided 21.01.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witnesses Unable to Identify Assailants
records.heading: The deceased's half open eyes and failure to shift him to hospital cast doubt on the eyewitnesses
records.text: The inability of independent injured witnesses to identify assailants, given suddenness and lack of acquaintance, does not diminish the credibility of the eyewitnesses. Judicial notice may be taken that people in society refrain from identifying accused persons out of fear. The conduct was held to fall within s. 6(1)(m) ATA. Ref: Sajad @ Kala v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 47-L/2018, decided 21.01.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Sajad @ Kala v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 47-L/2018, decided 21.01.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Police Constables Firing at Suspect: Excess of Authority
records.heading: Failure to take possession of the cot and blood-stained clothes made the testimonies improbable
records.text: Police constables who fired at a motorcar believing the occupant to be a criminal acted in wholly disproportionate excess of their lawful authority. No enmity, motive or premeditation was established, and the court adopted a third view of the evidence. The case also touches the Qisas and Diyat provisions on categories left to the courts. Ref: Muhammad Daniyal; Bilal Rasheed; Ishtiaq Ahmed v. The State (Criminal Petitions No. 176-K to 179-K/2022 and 1493/2022, decided 21.01.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Daniyal; Bilal Rasheed; Ishtiaq Ahmed v. The State (Criminal Petitions No. 176-K to 179-K/2022 and 1493/2022, decided 21.01.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence Alone Insufficient for Conviction
records.heading: The Anti-Terrorism Court tries section 336-B PPC, but petrol is not a corrosive substance
records.text: A person named as a murderer usually becomes scared and conceals himself to avoid police torture and detention. Mere abscondence is therefore insufficient to maintain conviction and sentence without other reliable evidence. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 105; Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1096 of 2024).
records.title: Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1096 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Contradicting Ocular Account
records.heading: A section 161 CrPC statement recorded without informing a Magistrate cannot be a valid dying declaration
records.text: Blackening on all wounds was improbable at a distance of 10 or 11 feet shown in the site plan. The medical officer's times of death and post mortem also did not coincide with the time of occurrence in the FIR. The conflict between medical and ocular accounts belied the presence of the prosecution witnesses at the site. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 105; Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1096 of 2024).
records.title: Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1096 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: A Call Data Record without company attestation or tested voice transcript cannot prove a call's contents
records.text: The deceased's eyes were found half open in the post mortem and inquest reports, which the court said could not happen had eye-witnesses been present. It was also not understandable that eye-witnesses did not shift the deceased to a hospital 45 to 47 minutes away, which cast doubt on their presence. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 105; Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1096 of 2024).
records.title: Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1096 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Investigation Lapse: Cot and Clothes Not Taken
records.heading: Cross-examination only to impeach a wife's character does not test her evidence; second marriage proved section 2(iia) ground
records.text: The complainant said the body was carried out of the forest on a cot, yet the Investigating Officer took possession of neither the cot nor the blood-stained clothes of witnesses, and the prosecution gave no explanation. The testimonies were held improbable and unsupported by the record. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 105; Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1096 of 2024).
records.title: Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1096 of 2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 336-A, 336-B and 338 PPC: Petrol, ATC, Pregnancy
records.heading: The party relying on a transaction with a pardanashin woman must prove her free will and understanding
records.text: The Anti-Terrorism Court has exclusive jurisdiction to try an offence under s. 336-B PPC. Petrol is not a corrosive substance under s. 336-A PPC, so throwing it does not attract s. 336-B PPC. Without proof of pregnancy, an offence under s. 338 PPC is not made out. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 134; Parvaiz @ Irfan v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 551-16).
records.title: Parvaiz @ Irfan v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 551-16)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Recording of Dying Declaration
records.heading: Legal heirs step into a deceased landlord's shoes, and one co-owner may seek ejectment alone
records.text: A statement of the injured recorded by the Investigating Officer under s. 161 CrPC, without intimating the nearest Magistrate, suffered an illegality that vitiated it. The dying declaration was also not put to the accused under s. 342 CrPC, so it could not be considered against him even if lawfully made. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 134; Pervaiz alias Irfan v. The State (Crl. Appeal 551-16).
records.title: Pervaiz alias Irfan v. The State (Crl. Appeal 551-16)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses; CDR Without Voice Transcript
records.heading: Interference in an acquittal appeal is narrow, and remand must not let the prosecution strengthen its case
records.text: Call Data Record without attestation by the cellular company and without a forensically tested voice transcript cannot prove the contents of a call. Without independent corroboration of their presence, the eyewitnesses were chance witnesses whose evidence was suspect. Failure to prove the place of occurrence is fatal to the prosecution. Ref: 2026 LHC 17; The State v. Sheikh Muhammad Awais (Murder Reference 304-22, decided 13.01.2026); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: The State v. Sheikh Muhammad Awais (Murder Reference 304-22, decided 13.01.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Cross-Examination on Character; Second Marriage; S. 2(iia) DMMA
records.heading: Terrorism requires violence to advance a cause or intimidate, unlike ordinary crimes with private motives
records.text: Cross-examination of the wife that sought only to impeach her character and embarrass her did not test her evidence. The husband admitted non-payment of maintenance and a second marriage during the family case, establishing the statutory ground under s. 2(iia) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, which the courts below failed to adjudicate. Ref: Mst. Naila Javed and another v. Nasir Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 3767/2025, decided 12.01.2026); Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Mst. Naila Javed and another v. Nasir Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 3767/2025, decided 12.01.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Pardanashin Woman: Proof of Sale and Mutation
records.heading: Section 27 ATA proceedings against an investigating officer attract the fair trial guarantee of Article 10-A
records.text: In transactions involving pardanashin or similarly placed women the court exercises heightened caution, and the party relying on the transaction must prove it was entered into with her free will and understanding, as laid down in earlier cases. A mutation is not a document of title and the underlying transaction must be proved when it is questioned. Ref: Muhammad Ishfaq and another v. Salma Begum (C.P.L.A. 4878/2025, decided 08.01.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Ishfaq and another v. Salma Begum (C.P.L.A. 4878/2025, decided 08.01.2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Legal Heirs as Landlords; Ejectment by One Co-Owner
records.heading: In specific performance, equity looks at whether performance was intended within a specific or reasonable time
records.text: On the death of a landlord his legal heirs step into his shoes and the tenant must pay rent to them once notice is served, without fresh tenancy or attornment. One legal heir and co-owner may file an ejectment application alone without written permission of the others. Depositing rent in the name of the deceased landlord was untenable. Ref: Muhammad Ramzan (deceased) thr. LRs and another v. Muhammad Tasleem and others (C.P.L.A. 1054-K/2023, decided 09.01.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan (deceased) thr. LRs and another v. Muhammad Tasleem and others (C.P.L.A. 1054-K/2023, decided 09.01.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal and Remand: Ss. 423, 428 CrPC
records.heading: Talb-i-Muwathibat requires a clear declaration of intent to pre-empt, not a mere expressed desire
records.text: Interference in an appeal against acquittal is narrow because of the double presumption of innocence, and is justified only where the judgment is perverse or shockingly misreads evidence. The power of remand under ss. 423 and 428 CrPC must be used with extreme caution and not to let the prosecution strengthen a doubtful case. The High Court was held wrong to order remand. Ref: Muhammad Fareedon Rehman v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 460/2025, decided 13.01.2026); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Muhammad Fareedon Rehman v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 460/2025, decided 13.01.2026)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Definition of Terrorism; Ordinary Crime
records.heading: A Muslim wife's right to maintenance is not conditional on rukhsati
records.text: An act is terrorism when violence or its threat advances a political, religious or ideological cause, or is designed to intimidate the Government, the public or a section of it, or to destabilise society. Ordinary crimes with personal or private motivation remain distinct from terrorism. Ref: HC Rana Tariq and others v. The State (Crl.A. 119/2021, decided 23.01.2026); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: HC Rana Tariq and others v. The State (Crl.A. 119/2021, decided 23.01.2026)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 27 ATA: Fair Trial and Art. 10-A
records.heading: Section 27 ATA proceedings against an investigating officer attract fair trial guarantees
records.text: Proceedings under s. 27 ATA against an investigating officer result in a criminal charge within Art. 10-A of the Constitution, so fair trial and due process apply. A summary trial still requires a clear accusation, opportunity to plead, cross-examination and defence evidence. A show cause notice with informal questioning is incompatible with Art. 10-A. Ref: HC Rana Tariq and others v. The State (Crl.A. 119/2021, decided 23.01.2026); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: HC Rana Tariq and others v. The State (Crl.A. 119/2021, decided 23.01.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Equity and Time of Performance
records.heading: Specific performance: court examines whether time of performance was intended to be essential
records.text: In specific performance cases, equity does not rigidly adhere to the express terms of the contract. The court examines the substance of the agreement to see whether the parties intended performance within a specific period or within a reasonable time. Ref: 2026 SCMR 36; Muhammad Ashraf Anjum v. Sabir Hussain and others (Civil Appeal No. 239-L of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf Anjum v. Sabir Hussain and others (Civil Appeal No. 239-L of 2018)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-i-Muwathibat: Declaration of Intent, S. 13
records.heading: A mere expressed desire to pre-empt does not prove Talb-i-Muwathibat
records.text: No specific format is required for declaring intent to pre-empt, but the statement must clearly articulate an intention to exercise the right. A mere expressed desire to do so was insufficient under s. 13 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act 1991, and doubt about execution of the talbs favours the vendee. Talb-i-Muwathibat was not proved. Ref: 2026 SCMR 138; Abdul Majeed etc v. Haji Haq Nawaz (C.P.L.A. 1010-L/2014).
records.title: Abdul Majeed etc v. Haji Haq Nawaz (C.P.L.A. 1010-L/2014)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Not Conditional on Rukhsati
records.heading: A wife's right to maintenance arises on nikah and does not depend on rukhsati
records.text: The right of a Muslim wife to maintenance flows unconditionally from solemnization of a valid marriage and is a binding legal duty. Rukhsati is a customary practice with no independent legal status under Islamic or statutory law. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1; Ambreen Akram v. Asad Ullah Khan etc (Civil Petition No. 1107-L of 2015 and Civil Appeal No. 247-L of 2017).
records.title: Ambreen Akram v. Asad Ullah Khan etc (Civil Petition No. 1107-L of 2015 and Civil Appeal No. 247-L of 2017)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Role of Amicus Curiae
records.heading: The institution of amicus curiae supports informed and principled adjudication in matters of public consequence
records.text: The institution of amicus curiae is essential to informed, inclusive and principled adjudication, and constitutional courts should continue to institutionalise it, especially in matters of significant public consequence or global relevance. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1; Ambreen Akram v. Asad Ullah Khan etc (Civil Petition No. 1107-L of 2015 and Civil Appeal No. 247-L of 2017).
records.title: Ambreen Akram v. Asad Ullah Khan etc (Civil Petition No. 1107-L of 2015 and Civil Appeal No. 247-L of 2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive: Double Edged Weapon
records.heading: Motive cuts both ways and cannot alone sustain conviction where other evidence is disbelieved
records.text: Motive can be a reason for the offence and equally a reason for false involvement. If the ocular account, weapon recoveries and medical evidence are disbelieved, the accused cannot be convicted on motive alone. Ref: 2026 SCMR 182; Azhar Iqbal and others v. The State (Criminal Petitions No. 189, 92-L of 2020 and 1810-L of 2019).
records.title: Azhar Iqbal and others v. The State (Criminal Petitions No. 189, 92-L of 2020 and 1810-L of 2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Withheld CCTV Footage: Art. 129(g) Adverse Inference
records.heading: Withheld CCTV footage justifies an adverse inference against the prosecution under Article 129(g) QSO
records.text: The prosecution produced neither a court report that courtroom cameras were not installed nor footage from corridor cameras said to be out of order. An important piece of evidence was withheld without justification, so an adverse inference under Art. 129(g) QSO was drawn against the prosecution. Ref: 2026 SCMR 182; Azhar Iqbal and others v. The State (Criminal Petitions No. 189, 92-L of 2020 and 1810-L of 2019).
records.title: Azhar Iqbal and others v. The State (Criminal Petitions No. 189, 92-L of 2020 and 1810-L of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvement by Prosecution Witness
records.heading: A witness who dishonestly improves his statement is not worthy of reliance
records.text: A prosecution witness who dishonestly improves his statement on material aspects, or to bring his evidence in line with the medical evidence, is not worthy of reliance. Ref: 2026 SCMR 182; Azhar Iqbal and others v. The State (Criminal Petitions No. 189, 92-L of 2020 and 1810-L of 2019).
records.title: Azhar Iqbal and others v. The State (Criminal Petitions No. 189, 92-L of 2020 and 1810-L of 2019)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry and Rule of Consistency in Bail
records.heading: Bail is not punishment: further inquiry and parity with a co-accused favour release
records.text: The purpose of criminal process is to make the accused face trial, not to punish pre-trial. At the bail stage the court makes a tentative assessment without probing merits, and where the case requires further inquiry bail is not to be withheld as punishment. Where the ascribed role is the same as a co-accused's, parity applies. Ref: 2026 SCMR 135; Abdul Mateen Mehboob v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 104-K/2025).
records.title: Abdul Mateen Mehboob v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 104-K/2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Attribution of Narcotic Quantity to Each Accused
records.heading: At bail, each accused is attributed only the quantity recovered from him
records.text: At the bail stage, unless confidence-inspiring material shows each accused knew of the others' possession, the total quantity cannot be attributed to each, and each is attributed only the quantity recovered from him or on his pointation. The total quantity can be attributed only after the prosecution proves conscious knowledge at trial. Ref: 2026 SCMR 115; Muhammad Daud v. The State thr. Special Prosecutor A.N.F. and another (Crl.P.L.A. 537/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Daud v. The State thr. Special Prosecutor A.N.F. and another (Crl.P.L.A. 537/2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Recruitment Disputes: Service Tribunal as Fact-Finding Forum
records.heading: The Service Tribunal is the first fact-finding forum for recruitment disputes
records.text: Factual controversies in the recruitment process and appointments are to be resolved by the Service Tribunal as the first fact-finding forum. Appellate jurisdiction serves checks and balances by re-examination of orders of lower fora, and judicial power is to serve justice judiciously. Ref: 2026 SCMR 92; Irfan Ali Pitafi v. Secretary (Colleges) Education Department Sindh and others (C.P.L.A. 915-K/2024); Justice Muhammad Ali.
records.title: Irfan Ali Pitafi v. Secretary (Colleges) Education Department Sindh and others (C.P.L.A. 915-K/2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Daily Diary Departure Entry in Narcotics Case
records.heading: Non-production of the daily diary suggests the police party never left the station
records.text: The prosecution did not produce the daily diary showing departure of the police party for nakabandi, though Rules 22.48 and 22.49 of the Police Rules 1934 require reasons for departure to be recorded. Failure to produce it leads to the inference that the party did not leave the police station and proceedings were done there. Ref: 2026 SCMR 87; Irshad Khan v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 219-P/2023).
records.title: Irshad Khan v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 219-P/2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Videography and Photographs of Recovery
records.heading: Police made no videography or crime scene photographs as Rule 25.14 contemplates
records.text: Neither the seizing officer nor other police officials made videography of the recovery proceedings to show recovery from the accused's vehicle, nor took photographs of the crime scene as contemplated by Rule 25.14 of the Police Rules 1934. Ref: 2026 SCMR 87; Irshad Khan v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 219-P/2023).
records.title: Irshad Khan v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 219-P/2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Prescribed Procedure Must Be Followed
records.heading: When the law prescribes a specific procedure it must be followed
records.text: Under the maxim communi observantia non est recedendum, when the law prescribes a specific procedure it must be followed, and any deviation renders the act questionable. Ref: 2026 SCMR 87; Irshad Khan v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 219-P/2023).
records.title: Irshad Khan v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 219-P/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 17-A(3) Family Courts Act: Compound Annual Increase
records.heading: The 10 percent annual increase under section 17-A(3) is calculated on a compound basis
records.text: S. 17-A(3) of the Family Courts Act 1964 is a beneficial provision. Where the decree prescribes no annual increase, or is silent on its basis, the 10 percent annual increase is calculated on a compound basis by the executing court. The Family Court may also prescribe compound or non-compound increase in its decree. Ref: 2026 CLC 12; Saba Gull Shahd and 2 others v. Additional District Judge Faisalabad etc (7340/24).
records.title: Saba Gull Shahd and 2 others v. Additional District Judge Faisalabad etc (7340/24)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 41 TPA: Ostensible Owner
records.heading: Section 41 TPA protection requires proof of ostensible ownership, consent, consideration and good faith
records.text: A person claiming protection under s. 41 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 must prove the transferor was an ostensible owner, the transfer was with the real owner's consent, express or implied, for consideration, and that the transferee acted in good faith with reasonable care. Absence of any ingredient defeats the protection. Ref: 2026 CLC 73; Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93).
records.title: Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Registered Document as Notice; Revenue Record
records.heading: A registered document operates as notice and is not displaced by revenue record inquiry
records.text: Sanctity attaches to a registered document, which operates as notice to the public at large. Mere inquiry of the revenue record is not sufficient to dislodge that presumption, as revenue entries are made for fiscal purposes and are not the foundation of title. Ref: 2026 CLC 73; Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93).
records.title: Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Cancellation of Mutation Without Hearing
records.heading: A mutation cannot be cancelled without notice and hearing to the purchaser
records.text: The revenue officer was bound to incorporate the registered deed in the revenue record and had no authority to cancel the mutation without notice and hearing to the purchaser. The cancellation order was void ab initio and had no effect on the plaintiff's rights. Ref: 2026 CLC 73; Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93).
records.title: Jahangir v. Abdul Ghafoor etc (Civil Revision 485-93)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Lis Pendens: Impleading Subsequent Vendee
records.heading: A subsequent purchaser pendente lite may seek impleadment but takes no independent right
records.text: A subsequent purchaser pendente lite acquires no independent right against the transferor and is bound by the outcome under s. 52 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882, but is not precluded from seeking impleadment under O. I R. 10 CPC. Refusing impleadment would deprive him of defence and offend natural justice. The impleading order was upheld in revision. Ref: 2026 CLC 109; Jamia Masjid Hanfia v. Mst. Surraya Bibi etc (Civil Revision 1133-I-14).
records.title: Jamia Masjid Hanfia v. Mst. Surraya Bibi etc (Civil Revision 1133-I-14)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Discretion under S. 22
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary but the discretion must be sound and reasoned
records.text: Under s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act 1977, specific performance is discretionary but the discretion must be sound, reasoned and not arbitrary, exercised on the facts and terms of the agreement. A stipulation for double payment of earnest money does not bar specific performance. The concurrent decree for the plaintiff was maintained. Ref: 2026 CLC 49; Malik Pervaiz Majeed v. Rizwan Malik etc (RSA 214-15).
records.title: Malik Pervaiz Majeed v. Rizwan Malik etc (RSA 214-15)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 79 QSO: Marginal Witnesses of Pronote
records.heading: Marginal witnesses of a pronote are needed only once a probable defence is shown
records.text: Art. 79 QSO applies only where the law requires attestation, and a pronote needs none, so non-production of marginal witnesses is not fatal where the O. XXXVII CPC defendant shows no probable defence. Where a probable defence is shown and execution is denied, the burden shifts back and the plaintiff must prove execution by producing both attesting witnesses. Ref: 2026 CLC 30; Shoukat Ali v. Abdul Ghafar etc (RSA 245-17).
records.title: Shoukat Ali v. Abdul Ghafar etc (RSA 245-17)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 120: Suit Challenging Mutations Time-Barred
records.heading: A suit challenging mutations must be filed within six years under Article 120
records.text: A suit to challenge a mutation must be filed within six years of attestation under Art. 120 of the Limitation Act. A suit filed 36 to 40 years after the mutations was hopelessly barred, and acquiescence, waiver and estoppel also applied. Ref: 2026 CLC 188; Umar Farooq etc v. Province of Punjab etc (RSA 80638/21).
records.title: Umar Farooq etc v. Province of Punjab etc (RSA 80638/21)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Successors' Locus Standi After Predecessor's Inaction
records.heading: Successors cannot challenge transactions that their predecessor knew of and never challenged
records.text: Where the real owner lived for years with knowledge of the transactions but never challenged them, his successors have no locus standi to question the validity of those transactions or mutations. Ref: 2026 CLC 188; Umar Farooq etc v. Province of Punjab etc (RSA 80638/21).
records.title: Umar Farooq etc v. Province of Punjab etc (RSA 80638/21)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Transfer Contrary to Security of Tenure: S. 186
records.heading: A transfer violating the security of tenure in section 186 may be interfered with
records.text: A government servant has no vested right to a particular posting, but a transfer in violation of a statutory provision can be interfered with. S. 186 of the Act gives security of tenure to Chief Officers and other local government officers, which may be curtailed only in extraordinary circumstances with valid reasons. The impugned transfer notification stated no reason. Ref: 2026 CLC 138; Badar Majeed Choudhary v. GOP etc (WP 19036-23).
records.title: Badar Majeed Choudhary v. GOP etc (WP 19036-23)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Closing Evidence
records.heading: Closing evidence under Order XVII Rule 3 CPC without due process is unsustainable
records.text: Closing the right of evidence and dismissing a suit under O. XVII R. 3 CPC without due process is unsustainable, especially where evidence is already on record or the witness is present. The court should call the witness for cross-examination and record in the order sheet that the chance was given. Art. 10-A guarantees fair trial in civil matters. Ref: 2026 LHC 53; Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited v. M/s Value CNG (RFA No. 66044 of 2025, hearing 12.01.2026).
records.title: Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited v. M/s Value CNG (RFA No. 66044 of 2025, hearing 12.01.2026)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: 120-Day Limit for Order After Show Cause Notice Mandatory
records.heading: The 120-day period for passing an order after a show cause notice is mandatory
records.text: The 120-day period in the first proviso to s. 11(5), replaced by s. 11G(2) of the 1990 Act, for passing an order after a show cause notice is mandatory, as settled by binding judgments under Art. 189. The order was passed beyond the period and the petition was dismissed. The court also criticised departments pursuing settled questions of law. Ref: Assistant Commissioner IR Unit III Zone-Cantt Regional Tax Office, Rawalpindi and others v. Umer Tariq Khan (C.P.L.A. 1990/2025, decided 27.01.2026); Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Assistant Commissioner IR Unit III Zone-Cantt Regional Tax Office, Rawalpindi and others v. Umer Tariq Khan (C.P.L.A. 1990/2025, decided 27.01.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Persons with Disabilities: Employment Protection and Quotas
records.heading: Persons with disabilities are protected against workplace discrimination, including through job quotas
records.text: Authority on protection of persons with disabilities against discrimination at work, including job quotas under the Punjab Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities Act 2022, which replaced the 1981 Ordinance and follows the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, provided the Act's procedure is followed. A copy of the order was directed to Punjab authorities. Ref: Muhammad Farhan v. The Province of Punjab (F.C.P.L.A. No. 16 of 2025, decided 13.01.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Farhan v. The Province of Punjab (F.C.P.L.A. No. 16 of 2025, decided 13.01.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Death of Complainant: Brother Allowed to Appear
records.heading: On the complainant's death the Supreme Court allowed his injured brother to appear
records.text: The complainant having died, the Supreme Court allowed his brother, who was also an injured eye-witness, to appear in the petition for leave to appeal filed by the accused against conviction and sentence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 182; Azhar Iqbal v. The State (Cr.P. 189-L of 2020).
records.title: Azhar Iqbal v. The State (Cr.P. 189-L of 2020)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption Strictly Construed; Burden on Plaintiff
records.heading: Pre-emption is strictly construed and the plaintiff bears the burden of proof
records.text: The right of pre-emption is a clog on the owner's freedom to alienate and is strictly construed. The plaintiff must prove a superior right, that the transaction is a sale, and that the required demands were made. Ambiguity as to whether the transaction is a sale defeats the plaintiff. Ref: 2026 SCMR 54; Muhammad Mushtaq v. Malik Mumtaz (C.P.L.A. 4649/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Mushtaq v. Malik Mumtaz (C.P.L.A. 4649/2022)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Sale Distinguished from Exchange
records.heading: Pre-emption arises only on a sale and not on an exchange of land
records.text: Pre-emption arises on a sale, defined in s. 2(d) as permanent transfer of immovable property for valuable consideration, which excludes exchange of agricultural land for better management. Executing an exchange to avoid a feared pre-emption is not inherently illegal. Ref: 2026 SCMR 54; Muhammad Mushtaq v. Malik Mumtaz (C.P.L.A. 4649/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Mushtaq v. Malik Mumtaz (C.P.L.A. 4649/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blackening Around Wound and Firing Distance
records.heading: Contact or close-range firing causes burning, charring and tattooing besides blackening
records.text: Contact or close-range shots (three feet or less) cause burning, charring and tattooing in addition to blackening. Blackening only at the margins of the entry wound may occur even from a long-range shot, and the wounds showed no burning, charring or tattooing. Ref: 2026 SCMR 163; Qaisar v. The State (Jail Petition No. 940 of 2017).
records.title: Qaisar v. The State (Jail Petition No. 940 of 2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sole Eye-Witness: Quality Over Quantity
records.heading: Quality and not quantity of evidence counts, and a sole eye-witness may suffice
records.text: Quality and not quantity of evidence weighs with courts. The evidence of a sole eye-witness that is confidence inspiring and trustworthy can safely support conviction. Ref: 2026 SCMR 163; Qaisar v. The State (Jail Petition No. 940 of 2017).
records.title: Qaisar v. The State (Jail Petition No. 940 of 2017)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 84 QSO: Court Comparing Signatures
records.heading: Courts may compare signatures under Article 84 QSO but only with great care
records.text: Courts may compare admitted and disputed signatures under Art. 84 QSO, but as a rule of prudence this must be done with great care. Comparison by a judge on his own initiative without an expert is hazardous and inconclusive. Ref: 2026 SCMR 171; Tasneem Abas v. ADJ (C.A. No. 132-L of 2013).
records.title: Tasneem Abas v. ADJ (C.A. No. 132-L of 2013)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant's Suit for Declaration of Ownership
records.heading: A tenant's civil suit claiming ownership does not stay eviction proceedings
records.text: The pendency of a civil suit by a tenant claiming to own the rented premises is not a ground to dismiss or stay eviction proceedings before the rent tribunal. Ref: 2026 SCMR 171; Tasneem Abas v. ADJ (C.A. No. 132-L of 2013).
records.title: Tasneem Abas v. ADJ (C.A. No. 132-L of 2013)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Proof of Tenancy: Rent Registrar Entry, S. 5 of 2007 Ordinance
records.heading: The registrar's entry under section 5 of the 2007 Ordinance is proof of tenancy
records.text: S. 5(1) of the 2007 Ordinance requires a tenancy agreement and s. 5(2) requires presenting it to the rent registrar, who under s. 5(3) enters the particulars and seals it. Entry in the registrar's office is treated by s. 5(5) as proof of the landlord and tenant relationship. Ref: 2026 SCMR 171; Tasneem Abas v. ADJ (C.A. No. 132-L of 2013).
records.title: Tasneem Abas v. ADJ (C.A. No. 132-L of 2013)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence Alone Insufficient for Conviction
records.heading: Abscondence alone is insufficient to sustain a conviction
records.text: A person named as a murderer, rightly or wrongly, usually becomes scared and hides to avoid police torture and detention. Mere abscondence is insufficient to maintain conviction and sentence without other reliable evidence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 47; Imran v. The State (J.P. 479 of 2019).
records.title: Imran v. The State (J.P. 479 of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Weapon and Empties Sent to Laboratory Together
records.heading: Sending the pistol and empties to the laboratory together defeats the recovery evidence
records.text: Where the recovered pistol and the empties were deposited together at the Forensic Science Laboratory, the recovery and the positive laboratory report were of no avail to the prosecution. Ref: 2026 SCMR 47; Imran v. The State (J.P. 479 of 2019).
records.title: Imran v. The State (J.P. 479 of 2019)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 182 PPC: Initiation of Proceedings
records.heading: A Magistrate cannot initiate section 182 PPC proceedings without a written complaint from police
records.text: Proceedings under s. 182 PPC cannot be initiated by a Magistrate on his own unless a written complaint is forwarded by the concerned police officer or his superiors. An Ex-Officio Justice of Peace cannot direct the SHO to register an FIR under s. 182 PPC against a complainant. Ref: 2026 SCMR 77; Ali Adnan Sheikha v. I.G Police (Crl.P.L.A. 147-K/2025).
records.title: Ali Adnan Sheikha v. I.G Police (Crl.P.L.A. 147-K/2025)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Doctrine of Sub Silentio
records.heading: A judgment given sub silentio on the question of law is not binding
records.text: A judgment that decides a lis without attending to the exact question of law raised has its precedential value disturbed. A decision reached without argument, without reference to the critical terms of the law and without citation of authority is not binding. Ref: 2026 SCMR 22; Saad Ali v. FOP (CPLAs Nos. 407-K, 499-K of 2021).
records.title: Saad Ali v. FOP (CPLAs Nos. 407-K, 499-K of 2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Ultra Vires and Intra Vires; Vires of Laws
records.heading: A law is presumed intra vires unless ex facie violative or beyond competence
records.text: Ultra vires means beyond powers and intra vires within powers. A law, rule or regulation may be struck down for want of competence or violation of fundamental rights, or if ex facie discriminatory, but there is a presumption of constitutionality unless it is ex facie violative. Ref: 2026 SCMR 22; Saad Ali v. FOP (CPLAs Nos. 407-K, 499-K of 2021).
records.title: Saad Ali v. FOP (CPLAs Nos. 407-K, 499-K of 2021)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Each Case Decided on Its Own Facts
records.heading: Each case must be decided on its own facts
records.text: Each case must be decided on its own facts, every litigant deserves a fair chance of being heard, and the decision must be founded on the facts of the case. Ref: 2026 SCMR 22; Saad Ali v. FOP (CPLAs Nos. 407-K, 499-K of 2021).
records.title: Saad Ali v. FOP (CPLAs Nos. 407-K, 499-K of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Selective Reliance on Defence Evidence
records.heading: Selective reliance on parts of defence evidence offends settled principles of appreciation
records.text: Selective reliance on certain portions of the defence evidence while discarding the rest is contrary to settled principles of appreciation of evidence and undermines the fairness of proceedings. Ref: 2026 SCMR 122; Umer Jan v. The State (J.P. 554 of 2023).
records.title: Umer Jan v. The State (J.P. 554 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post Mortem Examination
records.heading: Unexplained delay in post mortem examination damages the prosecution case
records.text: A delay of about ten hours after receipt of the body, and almost twenty three hours from death, in conducting the postmortem was attributed to police papers not being supplied. Unexplained delay damages the prosecution case and suggests the occurrence was unseen and time was spent procuring false eye-witnesses. Ref: 2026 SCMR 60; Mushtaq Ahmad v. The State (J.P. 853/2017).
records.title: Mushtaq Ahmad v. The State (J.P. 853/2017)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Nature and Purpose of Law of Limitation
records.heading: Limitation bars enforcement of existing rights and does not confer a right
records.text: The law of limitation does not confer a right but bars enforcement of existing rights after the prescribed period. The maxim interest reipublicae ut sit finis litium expresses that it is in the interest of the State that litigation should end. Ref: 2026 SCMR 190; The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022).
records.title: The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Duty of Court to Examine Limitation Suo Motu
records.heading: The court has a duty to consider limitation even if not raised
records.text: Under s. 3 of the Limitation Act 1908 the court has an inherent duty to consider limitation whether or not it is raised. Ref: 2026 SCMR 190; The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022).
records.title: The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Void Order Not Sufficient Cause for Condonation
records.heading: A plea that an order is void is not sufficient cause to condone delay
records.text: The plea that an order is void cannot be treated as sufficient cause for condoning delay in filing an appeal. The High Court appeal against an award made rule of court was dismissed as time-barred, and the Supreme Court found no justification to interfere. Ref: 2026 SCMR 190; The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022).
records.title: The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022)

records.subject: Limitation
