records.topic: Sufficient Cause and Explaining Each Day's Delay
records.heading: Sufficient cause requires a bona fide explanation of the delay of each day
records.text: Sufficient cause depends on a bona fide explanation, with no straitjacket formula, and conduct is relevant. Concocted or fanciful grounds, intentional sluggishness or lack of bona fides do not justify condonation. An applicant under s. 5 of the Limitation Act 1908 must explain the delay of each and every day. Ref: 2026 SCMR 190; The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022).
records.title: The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: No Preferential Treatment for Government in Condonation
records.heading: Government departments receive no preferential treatment in condonation of delay
records.text: In considering condonation of delay, no extraordinary clemency or preferential treatment is to be given to government departments, autonomous bodies or private organisations, whose cases are to be treated like those of ordinary litigants. Ref: 2026 SCMR 190; The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022).
records.title: The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Maxim: Law Aids the Vigilant
records.heading: The law aids those who are vigilant and not those who sleep
records.text: The maxim leges vigilantibus non dormientibus subserviunt means that the law aids those who are vigilant and not those who are sleeping. Ref: 2026 SCMR 190; The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022).
records.title: The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority v. Province of Sindh and another (C.A. 80-K/2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Maxims: Own Wrong and Ignorance of Law
records.heading: No one profits from his own wrong and ignorance of law is no excuse
records.text: No man can take benefit of his own wrong, so a person who devises a strategy to thwart the rights of others cannot profit from it. Ignorance of the law is no excuse and does not relieve a person of accountability for violating it. Ref: 2026 SCMR 152; Ambreen Akram v. Asad Ullah Khan (C.P. No. 1107-L of 2015).
records.title: Ambreen Akram v. Asad Ullah Khan (C.P. No. 1107-L of 2015)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Super Tax: Vires of Ss. 4B and 4C
records.heading: Super tax differentia held reasonable and permissible under Article 25 of the Constitution
records.text: Short order deciding challenges to the vires of super tax under s. 4B and s. 4C of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001. The differentia was held reasonable and permissible under Art. 25 of the Constitution, and High Court judgments declaring the First Proviso discriminatory were set aside. Detailed reasons were to follow. Ref: Super tax vires cases (Civil Appeal No. 1243 of 2020 etc, decided 27.01.2026); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
records.title: Super tax vires cases (Civil Appeal No. 1243 of 2020 etc, decided 27.01.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Meaning of Title and Entitlement: S. 42
records.heading: Entitlement under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is not restricted to ownership
records.text: In s. 42 of the Specific Relief Act, title means a legal right of ownership or entitlement indicating who has lawful authority over the property as between the contesting parties. Entitlement is construed broadly and is not restricted to ownership. Ref: 2026 MLD 175; Sheikh Anwar ul Haq v. Abdul Ghaffar etc (Civil Revision 31213/21).
records.title: Sheikh Anwar ul Haq v. Abdul Ghaffar etc (Civil Revision 31213/21)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Art. 46(1) QSO and S. 162 CrPC
records.heading: A dying declaration is an exception to hearsay and falls outside section 162 CrPC
records.text: A dying declaration is an exception to the hearsay rule under Art. 46(1) QSO, and it is immaterial whether the declarant expected death. Rule 8 of Chapter 12, Volume III of the Rules and Orders of the Lahore High Court excludes such declarations from s. 162 CrPC. Guidelines on recording appear in the Punjab Police Rules 1934. Ref: 2026 MLD 65; Kiran Ehsan v. The State etc (Cr. Appeal No. 16811 of 2021); Rehana Kauser v. Kiran Ehsan etc (Cr. Revision No. 21349 of 2021).
records.title: Kiran Ehsan v. The State etc (Cr. Appeal No. 16811 of 2021); Rehana Kauser v. Kiran Ehsan etc (Cr. Revision No. 21349 of 2021)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Ingredients of Criminal Breach of Trust
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust under section 406 requires entrustment and dishonest misappropriation or disposal
records.text: The offence under s. 406 PPC requires entrustment, dishonest misappropriation or conversion of the entrusted property, and dishonest use or disposal in violation of a legal direction on the mode of discharging the trust or of a legal contract, express or implied, touching its discharge. Ref: 2026 MLD 187; Phaphi alias Fatima and another v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7172-B/2025).
records.title: Phaphi alias Fatima and another v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 7172-B/2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Absconder versus Proclaimed Offender: Procedure
records.heading: Absconder and proclaimed offender are distinct, the latter being formally declared by the court
records.text: Distinguishes an absconder, who is a factual condition reported by the police as evading arrest and dealt with by warrants under ss. 75 to 86-A CrPC, from a proclaimed offender, who is formally so declared by the court after a public proclamation and failure to appear. A declaration made after due process may be used against the accused. Ref: 2026 MLD 46, PLJ 2026 CrC 359; Asad Abbas alias Achoo v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.10141-J/2022; Murder Reference No.16/2022; Crl. Revision No.13628/2022).
records.title: Asad Abbas alias Achoo v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.10141-J/2022; Murder Reference No.16/2022; Crl. Revision No.13628/2022)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Punjab Ownership Ordinance 2025: Powers of DRC
records.heading: The Dispute Resolution Committee cannot order eviction or restoration of possession
records.text: Under the Punjab Protection of Ownership of Immoveable Property Ordinance, 2025, the Dispute Resolution Committee is a pre-adjudicatory and facilitative body with no power to order eviction or restoration of possession. Coercive measures lie only with the Tribunal under ss. 16 and 17. Preventive orders under s. 9 must be written, reasoned, made after hearing the parties and consistent with any subsisting status quo order. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 18; Ghulam Gillani Aftab v. Government of Punjab etc (W.P. 15267/2025).
records.title: Ghulam Gillani Aftab v. Government of Punjab etc (W.P. 15267/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Interested Witness versus Related Witness
records.heading: An interested witness differs from a related witness and needs independent corroboration
records.text: An interested witness has a personal reason to see the accused falsely implicated and is distinct from a merely related witness. Such evidence must be assessed with great care and requires independent corroboration, and the witness cannot be treated as natural or independent. The post cites 2024 SCMR 1085 on the concept. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 36; Rasool Bux v. The State (Crl. A. No. S-48 of 2023, decided 27.06.2025); Justice Riazat Ali Sahar.
records.title: Rasool Bux v. The State (Crl. A. No. S-48 of 2023, decided 27.06.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody of Case Property: Acquittal
records.heading: Unproved safe custody of the recovered substance or sample parcel results in acquittal
records.text: If safe custody of the recovered substance, the sample parcel or the case property is not proved, other merits need not be examined and acquittal follows. The post also notes that the chain of safe custody was not put to the accused in his examination under s. 342 CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 83, 2026 YLR 1058; Shafqat Iqbal alias Bilalu v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 55608/23).
records.title: Shafqat Iqbal alias Bilalu v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 55608/23)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 300 PPC: Culpable Homicide and Grave Provocation
records.heading: Grave and sudden provocation requires proof that a reasonable person would have lost self-control
records.text: All murders are culpable homicides but only those meeting the conditions of s. 300 PPC are murder. A claim of grave and sudden provocation requires proof that a reasonable person in the same circumstances would have lost self-control, and that the accused caused death while still under that influence. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 1; Muhammad Nouman Shakir etc v. State etc (Crl. A. Nos. 39518-J, 35023 & M.R. No. 170 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Nouman Shakir etc v. State etc (Crl. A. Nos. 39518-J, 35023 & M.R. No. 170 of 2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody: Failure to Produce Registers
records.heading: Failure to produce Registers II and XIX leaves safe custody and transmission unproven
records.text: Where the prosecution gave only oral evidence and did not produce extracts of Register Nos. II and XIX or the Road Certificate, safe custody and secure transmission of samples to the PFSA remained unproven. A positive PFSA report does not cure this omission, as it carries value only if proper preservation and transmission are shown. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 63, 2026 PCrLJ 259; Naseem Kousar v. The State (Crl. A. No. 351 of 2024).
records.title: Naseem Kousar v. The State (Crl. A. No. 351 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Counsel from Mufassil Areas: Condonation of Procedural Default
records.heading: Procedural default caused by counsel from mufassil areas may be condoned
records.text: Courts have condoned procedural defaults in pleadings caused by counsel engaged from mufassil areas. The order striking off the right to file a written statement was set aside and the petitioner was given another opportunity to file it. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 9; Muhammad Waseem v. Rizwana Kousar etc (W.P. 49218/25).
records.title: Muhammad Waseem v. Rizwana Kousar etc (W.P. 49218/25)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Columns 13 and 16: Dower in Cash and Property
records.heading: Cash dower may be agreed in addition to property dower despite column headings
records.text: Parties may agree to dower in cash in addition to and distinct from dower in immoveable or movable property. Column headings in the Nikahnama do not determine the matter and cannot prevail over the intention of the parties. The High Court's reading, treating Column 16 as in lieu of Column 13, would make dower in other forms redundant. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 20; Mst. Fakhra Jabeen and others v. Wasif Ali (Civil Petitions Nos. 768 and 827 of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Fakhra Jabeen and others v. Wasif Ali (Civil Petitions Nos. 768 and 827 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dissolution under DMMA Not Convertible to Khula Without Consent
records.heading: A dissolution suit cannot be converted into khula without the wife's informed consent
records.text: A family court cannot convert a suit for dissolution under the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 into one for khula without the wife's clear and informed consent. Family proceedings are civil and decided on balance of probabilities, on evidence and not patriarchal presumptions. A second marriage without the wife's permission constitutes cruelty. Stereotyping language about wives should be avoided. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 91, PLJ 2026 SC 24; Mst. Doctor Seema Hanif Khan v. Waqas Khan and others (C.P.L.A.3268/2024).
records.title: Mst. Doctor Seema Hanif Khan v. Waqas Khan and others (C.P.L.A.3268/2024)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Advocate's Fee Cheque Against Client
records.heading: Recovery of an advocate's fee from a client lies through civil remedies
records.text: Where a client's cheque for professional fees is dishonoured, recovery lies through civil remedies such as s. 73 of the Contract Act, 1872 and a recovery suit. Criminal proceedings against a client are for exceptional cases only, mens rea must be established, and s. 489-F PPC is not a substitute for civil recovery. Bail allowed. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 75; Syed Basit Hyder Taqvi v. The State (Criminal Petition No.39-K of 2025).
records.title: Syed Basit Hyder Taqvi v. The State (Criminal Petition No.39-K of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Substantial Justice over Technical Compliance
records.heading: Courts should prefer substantial justice over technical compliance for minor mistakes of counsel
records.text: Minor unintentional mistakes of legal practitioners in drafting or filing that do not stem from contumacy or intentional misconduct deserve leniency. Courts should prefer substantial justice over mere technical compliance. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 53; Province of Punjab v. Muhammad Chiragh (Civil Petition No. 385-L of 2021).
records.title: Province of Punjab v. Muhammad Chiragh (Civil Petition No. 385-L of 2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Deficient Court-Fee: Rectification Before Rejection of Appeal
records.heading: The court must allow reasonable time to cure deficient court-fee before rejecting an appeal
records.text: Where court-fee on a memorandum of appeal is deficient, the court must ascertain the precise deficiency and allow a reasonable period to remedy it before rejection. A party who shows obstinacy and deliberate disregard of the law may forfeit further extensions. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 53; Province of Punjab v. Muhammad Chiragh (Civil Petition No. 385-L of 2021).
records.title: Province of Punjab v. Muhammad Chiragh (Civil Petition No. 385-L of 2021)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Absconder in Criminal Case: Civil and Service Remedies
records.heading: Absconder status in a criminal case does not bar civil or service remedies
records.text: The rule that a fugitive cannot invoke appellate jurisdiction in a criminal matter is confined to criminal proceedings. Status as an absconder or proclaimed offender in a criminal case does not bar civil or service remedies. Dismissal of the service appeal solely on that ground was a misapplication of law. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 37, 2026 PLC (C.S.) 233; Allah Diwaya v. Director Education Quetta and others (Civil Petitions Nos. 41-Q and 42-Q of 2022).
records.title: Allah Diwaya v. Director Education Quetta and others (Civil Petitions Nos. 41-Q and 42-Q of 2022)

records.subject: Character Certificate
records.topic: Police Character Certificate: Acquittal to Be Reflected
records.heading: A police character certificate must reflect an acquittal and omit the FIR
records.text: After an acquittal has attained finality, continued reference to the FIR in a police character certificate violates dignity under Art. 14 of the Constitution. The petitioner is entitled to a certificate reflecting the acquittal, and the FIR must be omitted. Writ petition allowed. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 84; Abdul Rehman Faryad v. Government of Punjab through Home Secretary and 3 others (Writ Petition No. 40844 of 2025, decided 18.07.2025); Justice Abher Gul Khan.
records.title: Abdul Rehman Faryad v. Government of Punjab through Home Secretary and 3 others (Writ Petition No. 40844 of 2025, decided 18.07.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Delay in FIR Caused by Police Not Attributed to Informant
records.heading: Delay in FIR caused by police omission cannot be held against the informant
records.text: Delay relevant to the informant's conduct is considered under Art. 21 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order 1984. A victim cannot suffer for delay caused by police omission or negligence in registering the FIR. Courts must examine whether delay is attributable to the informant, who here acted promptly as shown by the Roznamcha entry. Ref: Muhammad Bux alias Shahzaib v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.1021/2021, decided 30.01.2026); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Muhammad Bux alias Shahzaib v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.1021/2021, decided 30.01.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Written Statement in Family Suit: S. 9 Family Courts Act
records.heading: Section 9 of the Family Courts Act allows extension of time for a written statement
records.text: In a maintenance suit, after the Punjab Family Courts (Amendment) Act, 2015, s. 9 of the Family Courts Act, 1964 allows the court to extend time for filing a written statement for sufficient reason. Earlier case law on the absence of a time limit is no longer relevant. The matter was remanded for the petitioner to file his written statement. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 9; Muhammad Waseem v. Rizwana Kousar etc.
records.title: Muhammad Waseem v. Rizwana Kousar etc

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Complainant versus Informant; Addressing the SHO
records.heading: Complainant is reserved for section 200 complaints while an FIR reporter is the informant
records.text: The term complainant is reserved for a person filing a private complaint under s. 200 CrPC, while the person who reports an FIR is the informant. SHOs need be addressed only as Janab SHO, and the Sindh authorities are to ensure lower courts do not call a complainant or informant Faryaadi when calling a case. Ref: Muhammad Bux alias Shahzaib v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.1021/2021, decided 30.01.2026); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Muhammad Bux alias Shahzaib v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.1021/2021, decided 30.01.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Punjab Healthcare Commission Complaint: 60-Day Limitation
records.heading: A Healthcare Commission complaint must be filed within sixty days of knowledge
records.text: S. 23(2) of the Punjab Healthcare Commission Act, 2010 prescribes sixty days from the date of knowledge. Worsening of the injury or later diagnostic findings did not extend limitation, and the Commission rightly held the complaint time barred. No illegality was shown and the Court declined to interfere. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 1; Dr. Talal Khurshid Bhatti v. The Punjab Healthcare Commission (Writ Petition No.1873 of 2022).
records.title: Dr. Talal Khurshid Bhatti v. The Punjab Healthcare Commission (Writ Petition No.1873 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Last Seen, Confession and Recovery
records.heading: An unbroken circumstantial chain justified conviction, with death sentence reduced to life imprisonment
records.text: An unbroken chain was established by last seen evidence, a voluntary judicial confession, recovery of the deceased's dopatta on the accused's pointation and medical evidence of homicidal asphyxia. Minor inconsistencies did not warrant acquittal. Appeal partly allowed and the sentence under s. 302(b) PPC reduced from death to life imprisonment. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 1; Muhammad Wajid v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Wajid v. State

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Welfare and Child's Preference
records.heading: Welfare of the minor is paramount in custody and the child's preference may be considered
records.text: Welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration, and the court may consider the intelligent preference of a minor old enough to express it. The High Court set aside the order giving a 13 year old child to the natural parents and left the child with the adoptive parents who had raised him for nine years. The natural parents may approach the Guardian Court for meetings. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 43, PLD 2026 Lah 332; Syed Arshad Shah v. Additional District Judge etc (WP 43188/23); Justice Faisal Zaman Khan.
records.title: Syed Arshad Shah v. Additional District Judge etc (WP 43188/23)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Burden and Altered Agreement
records.heading: Material alteration of an agreement to sell without the seller's consent makes it unenforceable
records.text: The plaintiff bears the initial burden of proving the claim by cogent and unimpeachable evidence. Material changes to an agreement to sell without the seller's consent make it unenforceable, and specific performance is discretionary. No misreading or non-reading of evidence was shown and the revision was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 35; Muhammad Siddique v. Talib Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Siddique v. Talib Hussain

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Wedlock Policy: Posting of Spouses at Same Station
records.heading: The wedlock policy requires consideration of a spouse's request for joint posting
records.text: A civil servant has no absolute right to a particular posting, but under the wedlock policy a spouse's request should be considered subject to availability of a post in the same BPS. The petition was converted into an appeal and allowed, and the transfer order was set aside as to the petitioner. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 16; Mubashir Iqbal Zafar v. Ministry of Defence.
records.title: Mubashir Iqbal Zafar v. Ministry of Defence

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Limited Admissibility of Disclosure Statement
records.heading: Article 40 QSO admits only that part of a statement leading to discovery
records.text: Art. 40 QSO admits only that part of an accused's statement which leads to discovery of a fact, and the resulting recovery must be tested for credibility and corroboration. The prosecution withheld the best evidence, as no DNA or Chemical Examiner report was produced, and the chain of circumstances was not satisfactorily established. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 36; Zunair Younas and another v. State.
records.title: Zunair Younas and another v. State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: S. 498 CrPC
records.heading: Requiring incarceration is a mere formality where post-arrest bail would follow
records.text: Once the court concludes the accused would be entitled to post-arrest bail on dismissal of his pre-arrest bail application, requiring him to undergo incarceration is a mere procedural formality without meaningful purpose. Authority on s. 498 CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 21; Muhammad Akhtar v. State etc.
records.title: Muhammad Akhtar v. State etc

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Supplementary Statement and Social Media Material
records.heading: Bail granted where implication rested on a late supplementary statement and social media clips
records.text: Bail was granted where the petitioner was implicated in a supplementary statement made about a month late, on the basis of tweets and audio or video clips whose admissibility and value were yet to be determined at trial, with a three day delay in the FIR. The petition was converted into an appeal and accepted. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 19; Ejaz Ahmad Chaudhary v. State.
records.title: Ejaz Ahmad Chaudhary v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing FIR in Civil Money Dispute
records.heading: Criminal law cannot be used to secure speedy results in a civil money dispute
records.text: Using criminal law to secure speedy results in a bona fide civil dispute must be curbed, as police cannot assume the role of a civil court, for example by directing rendition of accounts. Though the High Court is normally reluctant to quash FIRs, the case was fit for constitutional jurisdiction and inherent powers. Ref: 2008 YLR 2695; Zahid Jameel v. S.H.O..
records.title: Zahid Jameel v. S.H.O.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Binding Effect of Federal Constitutional Court Judgments
records.heading: Federal Constitutional Court decisions bind all courts, including the Supreme Court
records.text: A decision of the Supreme Court under Art. 189, as amended by the Twenty-Seventh Amendment, binds all courts in Pakistan except the Federal Constitutional Court. Decisions of the Federal Constitutional Court bind all courts, including the Supreme Court. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 22; Riaz Hussain v. Chairman, Federal Land Commission (C.P.L.As. Nos. 962 to 964 of 2023).
records.title: Riaz Hussain v. Chairman, Federal Land Commission (C.P.L.As. Nos. 962 to 964 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata: Object and Scope
records.heading: A matter conclusively adjudicated by a competent court should not be reopened under res judicata
records.text: The principle of res judicata is fundamental to the rule of law. A matter conclusively adjudicated by a competent court should not be reopened, which maintains the integrity of judicial decisions and public confidence. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 22; Riaz Hussain v. Chairman, Federal Land Commission (C.P.L.As. Nos. 962 to 964 of 2023).
records.title: Riaz Hussain v. Chairman, Federal Land Commission (C.P.L.As. Nos. 962 to 964 of 2023)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Wakalatnama: Meaning and Scope
records.heading: Wakalatnama is a signed document appointing an advocate to appear and act
records.text: No statute defines Wakalatnama, but reading O. III R. 4 CPC with s. 22(3) of the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973, it is a written document signed by the party or a recognised or authorised agent appointing an advocate to appear and act in any court. It confers authority to represent the party. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 22; Riaz Hussain v. Chairman, Federal Land Commission (C.P.L.As. Nos. 962 to 964 of 2023).
records.title: Riaz Hussain v. Chairman, Federal Land Commission (C.P.L.As. Nos. 962 to 964 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance Vests Immediately; No Adverse Possession Among Co-Heirs
records.heading: Inheritance vests on death, and adverse possession does not apply among co-heirs
records.text: Heirs acquire ownership immediately on the death of the predecessor without intervention of any authority. A co-sharer's possession is for the benefit of all, delay in challenging a mutation does not extinguish the right, and waiver, estoppel, relinquishment and adverse possession do not apply among co-heirs. Depriving female heirs is contrary to public policy. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 42; Abrar Hussain v. Mst. Bibi Shahida and others (Civil Petition No. 567-K of 2023).
records.title: Abrar Hussain v. Mst. Bibi Shahida and others (Civil Petition No. 567-K of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Arrest After Addition of Offence: Cancellation of Bail Required
records.heading: An accused on bail cannot be re-arrested after an added offence without cancelling bail
records.text: When the investigating officer adds an offence after the s. 173 CrPC report, the accused on bail cannot be re-arrested without a court order first cancelling bail. The prosecution must apply for cancellation or amendment of charge, so notice and a hearing follow, under Art. 4 of the Constitution. Continued detention was declared unlawful and release ordered. Ref: PLD 2026 Islamabad 35; Arham Abbas v. State.
records.title: Arham Abbas v. State

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Undertaking by Tenant's Counsel Before Court
records.heading: An undertaking given through counsel before the court is binding and enforceable
records.text: An unequivocal undertaking given through counsel, such as to vacate within a specified period, is a binding assurance with the force of a court order and becomes an enforceable obligation. Breach offends the dignity of the court and carries coercive consequences. Ref: 2026 CLC 104; Muhammad Naveed Awan v. Additional District Judge, Islamabad.
records.title: Muhammad Naveed Awan v. Additional District Judge, Islamabad

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Ejectment by New Owner: Filing as Notice to Tenant
records.heading: Filing an ejectment petition is itself sufficient notice to the tenant
records.text: Filing an ejectment petition itself constitutes sufficient notice to the tenant of the landlord's intention to end the tenancy, so no formal intimation notice is needed from a new owner under s. 19 of the Ordinance 2001. The invocation of Art. 199 was held misconceived and not maintainable. Ref: 2026 CLC 104; Muhammad Naveed Awan v. Additional District Judge, Islamabad.
records.title: Muhammad Naveed Awan v. Additional District Judge, Islamabad

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: Recall of Order Blocking CNIC
records.heading: An order blocking a judgment debtor's CNIC was recalled where he was never served
records.text: The order blocking the judgment debtor's CNIC was recalled where the decree holder had given a wrong address, so the judgment debtor was never served. Even under s. 18 of the NADRA Ordinance, 2000 courts have discouraged blocking CNICs. NADRA was directed to unblock the CNICs. Ref: 2026 CLC 156.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Presumption of Correctness of Revenue Record; Ex Parte Defendants
records.heading: Revenue records prepared by public functionaries carry a presumption of correctness
records.text: Original settlement field-books and Deh forms prepared by public functionaries carry a presumption of correctness displaced only by cogent, independent evidence. A decree cannot be granted merely because defendants were proceeded against ex parte when the record negates the claim. The revision was dismissed. Ref: 2026 CLC 141.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Entry Does Not Confer Ownership
records.heading: Mutation entries serve fiscal purposes and do not confer ownership
records.text: Mutation entries are kept for fiscal purposes and neither confer nor extinguish ownership. The plaintiff claiming under a gift deed from his mother failed to show her title on the date of the gift. Ref: 2026 CLC 141.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Hanafi Law: Nieces Not Entitled as Residuaries
records.heading: Nieces are not entitled as residuaries under Hanafi law
records.text: Under para. 61 of Principles of Muhammadan Law, heirs are sharers, residuaries and distant kindred. Where there were no sharers, residuaries take the whole. The deceased's nieces were not male relatives on the father's side and were not entitled to anything, so their objections were rejected. Ref: 2026 CLC 120.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Benami Transaction: Essential Elements and Burden of Proof
records.heading: The burden of proving a benami transaction lies on the party alleging it
records.text: A benami transaction requires an agreement between ostensible owner and purchaser to buy in the former's name for the benefit of the payer, and that the real purchaser actually dealt with the seller. The burden lies on the party alleging benami under Arts. 117 and 119 QSO. Concurrent findings were not interfered with under s. 100 CPC. Ref: 2026 CLC 86.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Sindh Land Revenue Act: Suo Motu Alteration of Entries
records.heading: Board of Revenue exceeded jurisdiction by cancelling entries without required inquiry
records.text: The Member (Judicial-II), Board of Revenue, exceeded jurisdiction by cancelling entries without the inquiry required by s. 44, without adequate evidence under s. 45 and without the safeguards of s. 164 of the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967. Deviation from procedure renders the order illegal, and the orders were held without lawful authority. Ref: 2026 CLC 40.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Offence Abroad: Ss. 188 and 403 CrPC
records.heading: A Pakistani citizen who commits an offence abroad may be tried in Pakistan
records.text: A Pakistani citizen who commits an offence abroad that is also an offence under the PPC may be tried in Pakistan (s. 3 PPC). Section 188 CrPC does not bar an FIR under s. 154, and s. 403 CrPC protection arises only after trial by a competent court ending in conviction or acquittal. Criminal breach of trust was prima facie attracted; ad-interim pre-arrest bail withdrawn and petition dismissed. Ref: 2026 YLR 193, PLJ 2025 CrC 442; Muhammad Irshad v. State (Crl. Misc. No.7151-B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Irshad v. State (Crl. Misc. No.7151-B/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay, FIR, Injured Witness and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Unexplained delay, dishonest improvements and late witnesses weaken the prosecution case
records.text: Unexplained delay in reporting to police harms the prosecution version, and a belatedly recorded FIR gives no support. A witness who makes dishonest improvements, denies an admitted fact or is examined late loses credibility. An injured witness is not necessarily truthful, and medical evidence is only confirmatory. The prosecution was held to have failed to prove its case beyond doubt. Ref: 2026 YLR 266, PLJ 2025 CrC 645; Karamat Ali v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 5394 & M.R. No. 12 of 2022).
records.title: Karamat Ali v. State etc. (Crl. A. No. 5394 & M.R. No. 12 of 2022)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Conflicting Views of Equal Benches: Later View Prevails
records.heading: Where benches of equal strength conflict, the later view prevails
records.text: Where benches of equal strength have taken conflicting views on a question of law, the later view prevails. Ref: 2026 CLC 109; Jamia Masjid Hanfia Attock v. Mst. Surraya Bibi.
records.title: Jamia Masjid Hanfia Attock v. Mst. Surraya Bibi

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 118 Negotiable Instruments Act: Rebuttable Presumption
records.heading: Presumptions under section 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act are rebuttable
records.text: Presumptions under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 are rebuttable and the defendant must rebut them. The plaintiff's financial position is relevant, and a driver by profession lending Rs.1,000,000 was improbable. The presumption was rebutted, the burden shifted back, the Trial Court's decree was set aside and the suit dismissed. Ref: 2026 CLC 30; Shaukat Ali v. Abdul Ghaffar.
records.title: Shaukat Ali v. Abdul Ghaffar

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor with Special Needs: Quantum
records.heading: Maintenance must reflect the minor's actual expenses and special medical or educational needs
records.text: In fixing maintenance the court must determine actual expenses on the minor, the mother's living conditions and means, and any special medical or educational needs, which the father must meet. A family court may fix maintenance higher than the amount prayed for or interim maintenance, having regard to the passage of time. Ref: 2026 CLC 59; Hina v. Adil Shahzad.
records.title: Hina v. Adil Shahzad

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Fiqah-e-Jafria Talaq: Seeghajaat Before Two Witnesses
records.heading: Talaq under Fiqah-e-Jafria requires literal Arabic seeghajaat before two witnesses
records.text: A person following Fiqah-e-Jafria must pronounce talaq in the literal Arabic seeghajaat before at least two witnesses, and without it no certificate of effectiveness of talaq can be issued. The Chairman of the Arbitration Council has a duty to follow guidelines devised by the High Court. Ref: 2026 CLC 1; Bushra Hussain v. Chairman, Arbitration Council, Islamabad.
records.title: Bushra Hussain v. Chairman, Arbitration Council, Islamabad

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Word May as Enabling: Departure from Literal Rule
records.heading: The word may can carry a mandatory meaning where the literal rule yields absurdity
records.text: The word may is ordinarily permissive, but in the proviso to s. 7 of the Ordinance it was given a mandatory meaning. Courts may depart from the literal rule where the ordinary meaning is absurd and contradicts the purpose of the law, though such cases are exceptional. Ref: 2026 CLC 1; Bushra Hussain v. Chairman, Arbitration Council, Islamabad.
records.title: Bushra Hussain v. Chairman, Arbitration Council, Islamabad

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gifts and Relinquishment Depriving Female Heirs
records.heading: Courts must be vigilant where gifts and relinquishments deprive female heirs of inheritance
records.text: Courts must exercise extra vigilance where purported gifts deprive daughters and widows of inheritance. Such gifts and instruments, and relinquishment forced on vulnerable women, are contrary to law, public policy and Shariah. Ref: 2026 CLC 176.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Muslim Personal Law Applies to Succession from Time of Death
records.heading: Muslim Personal Law governs succession from the time of death despite custom
records.text: Under s. 3(2) of the 1935 Act, whenever a question of succession of a Muslim arises in court, Muslim Personal Law applies from the time of death despite any custom then in force. It applies even where the predecessor died before the Act came into force. Ref: 2026 CLC 176.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation in Inheritance Disputes
records.heading: Limitation is generally not decisive in inheritance suits by women and vulnerable persons
records.text: In inheritance disputes limitation is generally not treated as decisive for dismissing suits, especially those of women and vulnerable persons where fraud is involved, and where a parda nasheen lady claims her share in her lifetime. Ref: 2026 CLC 176.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Deed and Thirty Year Old Document: Burden of Proof
records.heading: Beneficiaries relying on a gift deed against sisters' inheritance bear the burden of proof
records.text: A party cannot simply assert that a document is thirty years old, and its contents must be proved by the beneficiary when denied. The burden of proving a gift deed set up by brothers against their sisters' inheritance lies on those relying on it. The trial court's decree was restored and the appeals allowed. Ref: 2026 CLC 176.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: KP Procurement Authority: No Jurisdiction on Executed Contract Disputes
records.heading: The Procurement Authority has no jurisdiction over disputes on an executed contract
records.text: Although s. 35 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Public Procurement Regulatory Authority Act, 2012 allows appeals on procurement grievances, the Authority's jurisdiction is confined to the procurement process. Disputes on interpretation or enforcement of an executed contract fall outside its adjudicatory powers. Ref: 2026 CLC 54.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11(d) CPC: Res Judicata and Withdrawal on Compromise
records.heading: Withdrawal of an earlier proceeding on compromise does not attract res judicata
records.text: Where the former proceeding was withdrawn on an out of court compromise, the High Court's order not recording it did not bring res judicata into play. The plaint was not liable to rejection under O. VII R. 11(d) CPC and the revision by the defendants was dismissed. Ref: 2026 CLC 98.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Compromise During Suit: Three Scenarios
records.heading: A compromise covering the subject matter of the suit has the status of a decree
records.text: A compromise in court covering the subject matter of the suit has the status of a decree. A compromise in court beyond the pleadings, or in or out of court beyond the scope of the pleadings, creates a fresh cause of action. Ref: 2026 CLC 98.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Fresh Suit on Compromise: No Permission Needed
records.heading: A fresh suit on an out of court compromise needs no permission
records.text: As the compromise was out of court, res judicata did not apply and the plaintiffs were free to file a fresh suit subject to limitation, so no permission was needed. The imposition of costs of Rs. 5,000 was set aside and the order modified to that extent. Ref: 2026 CLC 98.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Limits on Cross-Examination: Arts. 146 and 148 QSO
records.heading: Cross-examination is not unlimited and the court may stop indecent or insulting questions
records.text: The right of cross-examination is not unlimited and exists to reach the truth, not to harass a witness or prolong the case. Under Art. 146 the court may stop indecent or scandalous questions and under Art. 148 questions meant to insult or annoy. The judge must act as a vigilant supervisor, relying on PLD 2023 SC 211. Ref: Munir Ahmad Bhatti v. Mehmood Ahmad Tahir Bhatti and another (C.P.L.A.1078-L/2025, decided 02.01.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Munir Ahmad Bhatti v. Mehmood Ahmad Tahir Bhatti and another (C.P.L.A.1078-L/2025, decided 02.01.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Order Directing Registration of Case Set Aside
records.heading: Order directing registration of a case against the petitioner was set aside
records.text: The Chief Justice of the Lahore High Court set aside the order of the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Lahore, directing the registration of a case against the petitioner. The post gives no further reasoning. Ref: 2026 YLR 222; Salman Shahbaz Sharif v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace/Additional Sessions Judge etc (WP 43328/25).
records.title: Salman Shahbaz Sharif v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace/Additional Sessions Judge etc (WP 43328/25)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Non-Production of Complaint Bearer in CNSA Case
records.heading: Non-production of the complaint bearer in a Control of Narcotic Substances Act case
records.text: Authority on the effect of non-production of the complaint bearer in a case under the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2026 YLR 217; Mst. Bisma v. State (Crl. Appeal 664/2024).
records.title: Mst. Bisma v. State (Crl. Appeal 664/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in FIR and Unnatural Conduct of Witnesses
records.heading: Unexplained delay in reporting and unnatural witness conduct make the prosecution story doubtful
records.text: An unexplained delay of about two hours and ten minutes in reporting an occurrence, with the police station five kilometres away, showed deliberation and consultation and weighed against the prosecution version. The conduct of the three eyewitnesses in not informing the police or Rescue 1122 was unnatural and made the story doubtful. Ref: 2026 LHC 945; Allah Ditta v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1566-J of 2019, decided 26.01.2026).
records.title: Allah Ditta v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1566-J of 2019, decided 26.01.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata: Earlier Decision Without Adjudication
records.heading: Res judicata does not apply where the earlier dispute was decided without adjudication
records.text: Where a dispute was decided without proper adjudication and evidence, the essential conditions for the plea of res judicata do not exist. Ref: 2026 CLC 176.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Recovery Container Not Exhibited
records.heading: Failure to exhibit the shopping bag containing heroin creates doubt in the prosecution story
records.text: Heroin was said to be recovered from a white shopping bag which was not tendered in evidence with an exhibit number, and this creates doubt in the prosecution story. Ref: 2026 YLR 217; Mst. Bisma alias Sana v. The State (Crl. A. No. 664 of 2024).
records.title: Mst. Bisma alias Sana v. The State (Crl. A. No. 664 of 2024)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Belated Entry of Century Old Mutations: Revenue Officer and Writ Court
records.heading: Revenue officers may correct only minor errors free of serious dispute
records.text: Revenue officers keep records and may correct only errors free of serious dispute, and ownership disputes are for the civil court on evidence. Mutations sought to be entered a century later, for the first time in 2020, could not be treated as a minor error. A High Court in writ jurisdiction is not a fact finding forum. The petition was dismissed. Ref: Faiz Ullah Khan & others v. Member Board of Revenue Punjab (F.C.P.L.A. No. 137/2025, decided 28.01.2026).
records.title: Faiz Ullah Khan & others v. Member Board of Revenue Punjab (F.C.P.L.A. No. 137/2025, decided 28.01.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: General and Special Damages
records.heading: General damages need not be pleaded in detail but special damages must be proved
records.text: General damages are the direct result of the wrong, are presumed to flow from negligence and need not be pleaded in detail. Special damages must be specifically pleaded and proved. The plaintiff failed to establish special damages and the second appeal was partially allowed. Ref: PLD 2026 Kar 1.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Medical Negligence: Quashing FIR, Bar in KP Health Care Commission Act
records.heading: A special health care law bars prosecution for medical negligence except under that Act
records.text: Where a special law, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Health Care Commission Act, 2015, covers the allegation of medical negligence, s. 19 bars prosecution relating to private health care service except under the Act. The special law prevails over the general law, and the police proceedings and FIR were against the relevant law. Ref: PLD 2026 Pesh 23.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Decree: Husband Cannot Be Compelled to Pronounce Talaq
records.heading: A family court cannot compel a husband to pronounce talaq on a khula decree
records.text: A family court may dissolve a marriage by khula when reconciliation fails, but cannot compel the husband to issue written talaq or impose penalties for not doing so. Directions for written talaq, civil imprisonment and daily compensation were illegal, while the khula decree was upheld. Ref: 2026 CLC 126.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Judicial Overreach Renders Decision a Nullity
records.heading: A decision made beyond jurisdiction is void ab initio and a nullity
records.text: Exercise of power beyond the statutory framework is antithetical to the rule of law. A decision made outside jurisdiction or contrary to established legal principles is void ab initio and a nullity. Ref: 2026 CLC 126.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Declaration of Title Not Available on Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A declaration of title cannot be granted on the basis of an agreement to sell
records.text: A suit for declaration cannot be maintained, nor can a declaration of title be granted, on the basis of an agreement to sell. Ref: PLD 2026 Pesh 7.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Moulding Relief to Specific Performance Against Subsequent Purchaser
records.heading: A suit may be moulded into specific performance against a subsequent purchaser with notice
records.text: Where execution of the agreement to sell was proved and the suit was within limitation, the suit could be converted into one for specific performance and relief moulded accordingly. The subsequent purchaser had notice of the earlier agreement. The High Court modified the decrees in revision. Ref: PLD 2026 Pesh 7.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: S. 367 CrPC: Contents of Judgment in Child Rape Case
records.heading: A judgment convicting jointly without separate heads or reasons violates section 367 CrPC
records.text: The trial court convicted the accused jointly under s. 376 read with 377-B PPC and the KP Child Protection Act without separate heads or reasons for not awarding death or life imprisonment under s. 376(3) and (4) PPC. The judgment violated s. 367 CrPC and was set aside, with remand for rewriting. Appeal partially allowed. Ref: PLD 2026 Pesh 1.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: S. 236H: Advance Tax Cannot Rest on Arbitrary Percentage
records.heading: Tax under section 236H must rest on actual verifiable transactions
records.text: Tax liability must rest on actual verifiable transactions and not arbitrary percentages where the law prescribes none. The CIR(A) and the Tribunal erred in limiting the application of s. 236H of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 to 33 percent of turnover. Ref: 2026 LHC 939; CIR Okara Zone v. Shakoor Ahmad (ITR. 62-25, decided 14.01.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: CIR Okara Zone v. Shakoor Ahmad (ITR. 62-25, decided 14.01.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay: Government Departments Get No Leniency
records.heading: Government departments receive no leniency in condonation of delay
records.text: Delay for each day must be explained with cogent reasons, and limitation creates a vested right in the opposing party. Where counsel appeared throughout, the plea of no knowledge fails. Government departments are treated as ordinary litigants, and internal correspondence among departments is not sufficient cause. Ref: 2026 YLR 178; The Province of Punjab v. Sabir Ali and 8 others (R.F.A. No.10975 of 2025).
records.title: The Province of Punjab v. Sabir Ali and 8 others (R.F.A. No.10975 of 2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post Mortem Examination
records.heading: Delay in post mortem examination suggests time was spent procuring eyewitnesses
records.text: Noticeable delay in the post mortem examination generally suggests a real possibility that time was spent by the police in procuring and planting eyewitnesses before preparing the necessary papers. Ref: 2026 YLR 27; Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021).
records.title: Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blood Stained Clothes of Eyewitnesses Not Secured
records.heading: Failure to secure the eyewitnesses' blood stained clothes strikes at the prosecution case
records.text: The Investigating Officer did not secure the blood stained clothes of the eyewitnesses, which if grouped with the deceased's clothes would have strongly corroborated them. This omission struck at the roots of the prosecution case. Ref: 2026 YLR 27; Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021).
records.title: Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Motorcycle Light as Source of Light
records.heading: Identification at night is doubtful where the only light was an unproduced motorcycle
records.text: The identity of the accused in a night occurrence was highly doubtful where the only source of light was the complainant party's motorcycle, which was not produced at trial. A headlight shining on a person's face would make it impossible to see the firing and its details. Ref: 2026 YLR 27; Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021).
records.title: Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Burnt wound margins contradicting the site plan distance defeat the ocular account
records.text: Burnt margins on the entry wound indicated a shot from about two to three feet, contrary to the site plan distance of five feet, and differing wound sizes suggested different weapons. This contradiction showed the prosecution failed to prove the charge. Appeal against conviction allowed. Ref: 2026 YLR 27; Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021).
records.title: Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive Set Up but Not Proved
records.heading: The prosecution suffers where it sets up a motive and fails to prove it
records.text: It is a cardinal principle of criminal justice that the prosecution suffers if it sets up a motive but fails to prove it. Ref: 2026 YLR 27; Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021).
records.title: Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: A chance witness needs convincing reasons for his presence at the scene
records.text: The testimony of a chance witness is ordinarily not accepted unless convincing reasons for his presence at the scene are shown, and absence is presumed otherwise. Without such explanation his evidence is suspect and cannot be accepted without a pinch of salt. Ref: 2026 YLR 27; Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021).
records.title: Shahid alias Shahidi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.848 of 2022; Murder Reference No.234 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inordinate Delay in FIR
records.heading: Inordinate delay in lodging the FIR speaks against the prosecution version
records.text: Inordinate delay in setting the machinery of law in motion speaks volumes against the veracity of the prosecution version. Ref: 2026 YLR 142; Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024).
records.title: Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Witness
records.heading: Dishonest improvements by a witness make his statement untrustworthy and unreliable
records.text: Dishonest improvements made by a witness to strengthen the prosecution case cast serious doubt on his veracity and make his statement untrustworthy and unreliable. Ref: 2026 YLR 142; Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024).
records.title: Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Recording S. 161 CrPC Statement of Injured Witness
records.heading: Unexplained delay in recording an injured witness's section 161 statement makes it unreliable
records.text: An unexplained three day delay in recording the s. 161 CrPC statement of an injured witness who was fully conscious makes it unreliable, as the delay allows fabrication or tailoring. Such a statement is not confidence inspiring and its value is reduced to nil unless the delay is plausibly explained. Ref: 2026 YLR 142; Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024).
records.title: Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness: Injuries Do Not Prove Truthfulness
records.heading: Injuries alone do not prove an injured witness is truthful
records.text: Mere injuries on an injured witness do not mean he is telling the whole truth. His evidence is relied upon or discarded in light of the other facts and circumstances of the case. Ref: 2026 YLR 142; Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024).
records.title: Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Ocular Account Contradicted by Medical Evidence
records.heading: Blackening and burning at the entry wound contradict a firing distance of eight feet
records.text: Blackening and burning at the entry wound indicate a close range shot within about three feet, whereas the site plan placed the accused about eight feet away. This contradiction between ocular and medical evidence showed the prosecution failed to prove the charge. Ref: 2026 YLR 142; Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024).
records.title: Zulfqiar Khan etc v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.702 of 2024; Crl. Revision No.315 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Re-Medico Legal Examination: Time Limit
records.heading: Medical re-examination is not confined to three weeks and depends on reasonableness
records.text: The three week limit for medical re-examination in a Punjab Health Department letter of 1990 was enlarged to an indefinite period by a letter of 1992, subject to reasonableness in the District Magistrate's discretion as injuries heal over time. The Magistrate's refusal on the ground of twenty-one days was therefore wrong, and a District Standing Medical Board meeting was directed for re-examination. Ref: 2026 YLR 208; Sagheer Ahmad v. Sessions Judge, Kasur (W.P. No.55471 of 2024).
records.title: Sagheer Ahmad v. Sessions Judge, Kasur (W.P. No.55471 of 2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Bail: Delay in Trial
records.heading: Statutory bail cannot be refused for prosecution delay absent recognised exceptions
records.text: Where the prosecution caused delay and the accused had completed the statutory period in custody, bail on the statutory ground cannot be refused unless he is a hardened, desperate or dangerous criminal, a previous convict of a capital or life offence, or accused of terrorism. Mere recovery of money and a motorcycle or criminal history is no ground to refuse bail. Identification of the accused was also doubtful. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 7, PLJ 2026 CrC 92; Sunny Hakim v. The State etc.
records.title: Sunny Hakim v. The State etc

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Recovery on Pointation: Art. 40 QSO
records.heading: Recovery on the accused's pointation is admissible as a discovery under Article 40 QSO
records.text: Recovery of the deceased's dopatta from an abandoned house, made on the pointation of the appellant, is a discovery admissible in evidence under Art. 40 QSO. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 1; Muhammad Wajid v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Wajid v. The State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Partial Acceptance of Confessional Statement
records.heading: Corroborated parts of a confession may be accepted and inconsistent parts rejected
records.text: Where a confession is not the sole basis of the prosecution case and is corroborated by other evidence, the Court may accept the inculpatory parts that agree with established facts and reject the inconsistent or uncorroborated portions. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 1; Muhammad Wajid v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Wajid v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Inconsistencies as Mitigating Circumstance
records.heading: Minor inconsistencies that do not justify acquittal may only affect the sentence
records.text: Minor inconsistencies in prosecution evidence that raise some doubt but do not justify acquittal amount only to a mitigating circumstance, capable of affecting the quantum of sentence alone. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 1; Muhammad Wajid v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Wajid v. The State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Cyber Crime Harassment, Marital Dispute
records.heading: Bail is the rule in a marital dispute cyber crime case outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: In a marital dispute case the Court must ensure the legal process is not used for harassment. The offences fell outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC, the petitioner was a medical professional without record and had been in custody for 2 to 3 months, so bail is the rule. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 25; Syed Muhammad Ali Jaferi v. The State and another.
records.title: Syed Muhammad Ali Jaferi v. The State and another

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 190, 173 CrPC and s. 462-O PPC: Cognizance
records.heading: Magistrate must call for the required complaint rather than return the section 173 report
records.text: An offence under s. 462-I PPC is triable by the Court of Sessions. If the s. 173 report lacks the complaint required by s. 462-O PPC, the Magistrate must ask the prosecution to procure it from an officer not below Grade 17 and forward the case to the Sessions Court under s. 190(2) CrPC, read with s. 230 CrPC, rather than returning the report. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 15, 2026 PCrLJ 1730; The State through Deputy Prosecutor General Punjab, Multan v. Senior Civil Judge and another (W.P. No. 14839 of 2024).
records.title: The State through Deputy Prosecutor General Punjab, Multan v. Senior Civil Judge and another (W.P. No. 14839 of 2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Cross-Version, Injured Accused
records.heading: Where the accused party was also injured, who was the aggressor awaits trial
records.text: A member of the accused party also sustained a firearm injury, later fatal, not mentioned in the FIR. Who was the aggressor is for the Trial Court after evidence. Petition converted into an appeal and allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 28; Sana Ullah v. The State.
records.title: Sana Ullah v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal: Abduction Case, Failure to Prove
records.heading: Prosecution failure to prove abduction beyond doubt led to acquittal of the petitioners
records.text: The only eye-witness named in the FIR died before testifying, no weapon was recovered from the petitioners, no phone recording was produced and a money dispute over sale consideration suggested a concocted story. Prosecution failed to prove its case beyond shadow of doubt and the petitioners were acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 30; Iftikhar Ahmad and others v. The State.
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmad and others v. The State

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Contract Under Duress Void
records.heading: A contract procured by duress is void and benefits received must be restored
records.text: A contract procured by duress is void and benefits received must be restored. Duress is constraint or danger, actual or threatened, sufficient to overcome the mind and will of a person. Such a contract lacks consent under s. 13 and free consent under s. 14 and is void under s. 2(g) of the Contract Act, 1872. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 1; Muhammad Zaffar Khan and another v. Syed Shumaila Zaidi and others.
records.title: Muhammad Zaffar Khan and another v. Syed Shumaila Zaidi and others

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Admissibility of DNA Report as Expert Evidence
records.heading: A PFSA DNA report is per se admissible as expert evidence but not primary evidence
records.text: DNA evidence is assessed under Arts. 59 and 164 QSO. The technician is an expert, and by s. 9(3) of the Punjab Forensic Science Agency Act, 2007 read with s. 510 CrPC a PFSA DNA report is per se admissible. It is expert evidence and cannot be treated as primary evidence. Ref: Sajid Hussain v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 434 of 2025).
records.title: Sajid Hussain v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 434 of 2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis and Post-Mortem Changes
records.heading: Rigor mortis and seminal discharge are recognised post-mortem phenomena
records.text: The judgment explains the sequence of post-mortem changes and treats the presence of rigor mortis and seminal discharge as recognised post-mortem phenomena that are fully explained. Rigor mortis was of substantial importance in determining the controversy. Ref: 2026 LHC 975; The State v. Nadeem (Murder Reference 331-22); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: The State v. Nadeem (Murder Reference 331-22)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Counsel Cannot Tender Documents in Evidence
records.heading: Counsel cannot tender documents in evidence through his own statement
records.text: Under Order XIII CPC counsel may file and present documents, but they must be proved through witnesses or other lawful means. Counsel cannot tender documents through his own statement, and the usual wakalatnama clause to sign and file documents does not confer that authority. Ref: Naeem Niaz Awan v. Additional District Judge and others (W.P. No. 71795/2023).
records.title: Naeem Niaz Awan v. Additional District Judge and others (W.P. No. 71795/2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Promotion From Date of Eligibility: Delayed DPC
records.heading: An employee is entitled to promotion from the date of eligibility despite delayed DPC
records.text: Where the department delayed convening the Departmental Promotion Committee for two years, the employee cannot be penalised for the department's delay and is entitled to promotion from the date he originally became eligible. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 60.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Judicial Interference in Investigation
records.heading: Courts should not supervise the manner of investigation except in exceptional circumstances
records.text: Art. 10A protects fair trial from the inception of investigation, which must be free, independent and transparent and collect evidence for both defence and prosecution. The courts and police have complementary roles, and a court should not supervise the manner of investigation except in exceptional circumstances such as habeas corpus, mala fide investigation or acts beyond the investigating officer's jurisdiction. Ref: Suo Moto Case No. 3 of 2022 Regarding Independent and Transparent Investigation into the Murder of Renowned Journalist Mr. Arshad Sharif, in Kenya.
records.title: Suo Moto Case No. 3 of 2022 Regarding Independent and Transparent Investigation into the Murder of Renowned Journalist Mr. Arshad Sharif, in Kenya

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Recruitment Advertisement: Shahadat-ul-Alamia Marks
records.heading: Marks for Shahadat-ul-Alamia in recruitment depend on the post rules and advertisement
records.text: Shahadat-ul-Alamia is recognised as equivalent to an MA, but marks for it in a recruitment depend on the post rules and advertisement. The advertisement allowed such marks only for Arabic Teacher and Theology Teacher, so a candidate for Qari could not claim them as of right. Ref: Shams uddin v. Govt of KPK & others (F.C.P.L.A. No.338 of 2025, decided 27.01.2026).
records.title: Shams uddin v. Govt of KPK & others (F.C.P.L.A. No.338 of 2025, decided 27.01.2026)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape: Prompt FIR, Victim Testimony, DNA
records.heading: A confidence-inspiring rape victim's testimony needs no corroboration, and here DNA supported it
records.text: An FIR lodged within two hours leaves no room for a false story. A confidence-inspiring rape victim's testimony needs no corroboration, and here it was fortified by positive DNA and serology reports. A bare defence of denial and unproven enmity, without witnesses, carries no weight. Ref: 2026 LHC 1007; Hassan v. The State etc (Crl.A-752-18, decided 29.01.2026); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Hassan v. The State etc (Crl.A-752-18, decided 29.01.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Res Gestae: Art. 19 QSO
records.heading: Res gestae under Article 19 QSO requires a contemporaneous statement
records.text: Res gestae under Art. 19 QSO is an exception to hearsay and requires a statement made contemporaneously with, or immediately after, the act and not as a narrative of past events. The minor victim's statements to a witness who saw her weeping, and to her parents on the same day, were admissible. The Trial Court rightly relied on both witnesses as they were corroborated by the victim. Ref: PLD 2026 Quetta 16.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: A chance witness needs a satisfactory explanation of his presence at the scene
records.text: A witness who would not ordinarily be at the scene but claims to be there by chance must be treated with caution, and his testimony cannot be accepted without a satisfactory and convincing explanation of his presence. Ref: 2026 LHC 1039; Muhammad Irfan and 2 others v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.67701-J of 2020, decided 28.01.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan and 2 others v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.67701-J of 2020, decided 28.01.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blackening Around Wounds and Firing Distance
records.heading: Blackening despite alleged firing from six feet is inconsistent with the prosecution version
records.text: A shot from a .30 bore or 9 mm pistol within three feet ordinarily causes blackening of the entry wound. Blackening was observed although firing was alleged from not less than six feet, which is inconsistent with the prosecution version. Ref: 2026 LHC 1039; Muhammad Irfan and 2 others v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.67701-J of 2020, decided 28.01.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan and 2 others v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.67701-J of 2020, decided 28.01.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Withdrawal of PPSC Recommendation; Probationer Termination
records.heading: The PPSC may withdraw its recommendation and the department may then terminate a probationer
records.text: Under Regulations 26 and 63 of the 2016 Regulations the PPSC may withdraw its recommendation where malpractice or ineligibility is found, even after dispatch. The department may then terminate a probationer without reasons or show cause notice. The High Court has no suo moto jurisdiction in the matter. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 36; Province of Punjab through its Chief Secretary GOP Lahore etc v. Chand Iqbal Deputy Accountant etc (W.P. 13336/22).
records.title: Province of Punjab through its Chief Secretary GOP Lahore etc v. Chand Iqbal Deputy Accountant etc (W.P. 13336/22)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Inquiry, Double Jeopardy, Removal From Service
records.heading: Removal from service violated Articles 4, 10-A and 13 through double punishment
records.text: The Inquiry Officer must ascertain that due process and fair trial under Arts. 4 and 10-A were followed. Past punishment cannot ground a further punishment, as that offends Art. 13 on double jeopardy, and dispensing with a regular inquiry needs recorded reasons. The removal orders violated Arts. 4, 10-A and 13. Ref: 2026 PLC 1, PLJ 2025 Lah 750.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Regularisation of Contract Employees: Departmental Delay
records.heading: Contract employees cannot suffer for departmental delay in deciding their regularisation cases
records.text: Contract employees who completed three years of service and were backed by their parent department cannot suffer because the department, through bureaucratic inertia, delayed their regularisation cases until contracts expired. Under s. 4(1) of the Act such cases go to the appointing authority without reference to the Commission. Ref: 2026 LHC 1090; Muhammad Shahid Sharif & 1 other v. Additional Chief Secretary etc (W.P. 70730/25, decided 15.01.2026); Justice Shahid Karim.
records.title: Muhammad Shahid Sharif & 1 other v. Additional Chief Secretary etc (W.P. 70730/25, decided 15.01.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cognizance of Offences Under Chapter XVII-B PPC
records.heading: Cognizance of Chapter XVII-B PPC offences depends on a complaint by the authorised officer
records.text: Under s. 462-O PPC, read with ss. 195 and 196 CrPC, cognizance of Chapter XVII-B offences depends on a complaint, while FIRs and investigation may proceed. Where a complaint of an authorised officer is before the Court, it may take cognizance without insisting on a separate complaint. Impugned order set aside. Ref: 2026 LHC 1071; Farhan Anwar v. ASJ, Faisalabad and 2 others (Crl.Misc.No.66147-M of 2020, heard 03.02.2026).
records.title: Farhan Anwar v. ASJ, Faisalabad and 2 others (Crl.Misc.No.66147-M of 2020, heard 03.02.2026)

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: NIRC Regulation 60: Dispensing With Evidence
records.heading: Regulation 60 permits disposal on the record but is not absolute
records.text: Regulation 60 of the NIRC Regulations, 2016 facilitates expeditious disposal on the available record, but it is not absolute. The Full Bench remains competent to examine whether the controversy could justly be resolved without evidence and to remand with cogent reasons. Ref: 2026 LHC 1112; Moazzam Haq v. Full Bench NIRC & others (Writ Petition-15919-25, decided 27.01.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Moazzam Haq v. Full Bench NIRC & others (Writ Petition-15919-25, decided 27.01.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage Corroborating Ocular Account: s. 377-B PPC
records.heading: CCTV footage corroborated the child victim and eye-witness in a section 377-B PPC case
records.text: In a s. 377-B PPC case, CCTV footage collected by the Investigating Officer corroborated the child victim and the child eye-witness. Recovery of the accused's clothes from his room was further supporting evidence. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1801; Ahsan Ali Gardezi v. The State.
records.title: Ahsan Ali Gardezi v. The State

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Attorney as Landlord; Personal Bona Fide Need
records.heading: A general attorney may seek ejectment for the landlord's personal need
records.text: Under the West Pakistan Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959 a landlord includes any person entitled to receive rent, so a general attorney with all rights transferred may seek ejectment for personal need. The landlord's affidavit, unshaken in cross-examination, suffices, and he may choose the premises. The High Court should not disturb findings of fact in constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: Mohammad Ziafat v. Tariq Nawaz Khan and others (C.P.L.A.3661/2025); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Mohammad Ziafat v. Tariq Nawaz Khan and others (C.P.L.A.3661/2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Entries Do Not Confer Title
records.heading: Mutation entries do not create, extinguish or confer title
records.text: Mutation entries serve fiscal purposes and do not create, extinguish or confer title. Once disputed, the party relying on a mutation must prove the original transaction by lawful evidence. Government land cannot be lost through lapses or connivance of subordinate functionaries. Ref: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Document Mentioned in Cross-Examination Not Proved
records.heading: Mere mention of a document in cross-examination does not prove it
records.text: Mere mention of a document in cross-examination does not prove its existence or authenticity, and the burden lies on the party asserting a fact. An obligating statement in cross-examination is at best inferential evidence and not binding proof. Ref: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Estopped From Denying Landlord's Title
records.heading: A tenant is estopped from denying the landlord's title and must first surrender possession
records.text: A tenant in possession under tenancy is estopped from disputing the landlord's title and must first surrender possession. A tenant claiming co-ownership by purchase of a share must seek partition in a civil court and cannot resist ejectment before the Rent Controller by raising title. Ref: Nawab Khan & another v. Muhammad Yousaf & others (C.P.L.A.806-P/2018, decided 29.01.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Nawab Khan & another v. Muhammad Yousaf & others (C.P.L.A.806-P/2018, decided 29.01.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Wife Killed in Husband's House: Burden of Explanation
records.heading: A husband must explain a wife's death in his house under Article 122 QSO
records.text: Where a wife dies a homicidal death in her husband's home, he must give a satisfactory explanation under Art. 122 QSO. His conduct is relevant under Art. 22 and Art. 129 permits adverse inference. The prosecution must still prove the offence and the offender, and doubt goes to the accused. Ref: Waris Masih v. The State (J.P.787/2018, decided 21.01.2026); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Waris Masih v. The State (J.P.787/2018, decided 21.01.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: No Mention of Caste in FIR and Police Records
records.heading: Caste, tribe, biradari or conversion status is not to be recorded in FIRs
records.text: The Court directed Inspectors General of Police not to record caste, tribe, biradari or conversion status in names of complainants, accused, victims or witnesses in FIRs and other police records. Departure is allowed only where the investigating officer records written bona fide reasons showing it is strictly necessary. Ref: Arshad alias Billu v. The State (Jail Petition No. 183/2019, decided 26.01.2026).
records.title: Arshad alias Billu v. The State (Jail Petition No. 183/2019, decided 26.01.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Trial Court Record Attached to Appeal
records.heading: A trial court record attached with the appeal need not be summoned
records.text: When the trial court record is attached with the appeal there is no need to summon it, and it is to be considered as it stands. Ref: 2026 YLR 178; The Province of Punjab v. Sabir Ali.
records.title: The Province of Punjab v. Sabir Ali

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence: Source of Light Not Proved
records.heading: Identity is doubtful where the claimed motorcycle light source was not produced at trial
records.text: Where witnesses claimed to see the occurrence by motorcycle light at night, and the motorcycle was not produced at trial while the accused's motorcycle at the scene was not taken into possession, identity of the accused was highly doubtful. Ref: 2026 YLR 27; Shahid alias Shahidi v. State.
records.title: Shahid alias Shahidi v. State
