records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Criminal Breach of Trust, Business Transaction
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail where the FIR disclosed a business transaction lacking entrustment
records.text: The FIR disclosed a business transaction lacking entrustment and misappropriation required for s. 406 PPC. Merits may be touched upon in pre-arrest bail, and the case fell within s. 497(2) CrPC as one of further inquiry. Ref: 2026 YLR 201; Mateen v. The State.
records.title: Mateen v. The State

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Delay in Trial Not Attributable to Accused
records.heading: Bail allowed after over a year in custody with delay caused by the prosecution
records.text: The petitioner had been in custody over one year and two months with no material progress, the prosecution causing delay through absent witnesses. Investigation was complete, he had no previous conviction, and continued incarceration served no purpose. Ref: 2026 YLR 134; Muhammad Riaz alias Bobi v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Riaz alias Bobi v. The State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Production of Police Official Carrying Complaint
records.heading: Non-production of the Head Constable who carried the complaint indicates a delayed FIR
records.text: The Head Constable who carried the complaint to the police station was essential to prove prompt FIR registration and the defence could cross-examine him. His non-production, with doubts about eye-witnesses being at the hospital, showed a delayed FIR lodged after a false story was concocted. Ref: 2026 YLR 116; Imran alias Mana v. The State.
records.title: Imran alias Mana v. The State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Closing Right to Produce Evidence: Fair Trial
records.heading: The right to produce evidence should not be closed after only two effective opportunities
records.text: The plaintiff's evidence was delayed by strikes, leave of the Presiding Officer and adjournments, and only two effective opportunities were given before his right was closed. The High Court set aside the order and allowed one more opportunity on payment of Rs.25,000 costs. Ref: 2026 YLR 20; Ghulam Muhammad v. Rashidan Bibi.
records.title: Ghulam Muhammad v. Rashidan Bibi

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance by Biological Father
records.heading: A biological father must maintain the child once paternity is established
records.text: A child's right to maintenance rests on welfare and equity. Once biological paternity is established, the biological father must maintain the child and cannot rely on technical pleas of legitimacy. The law distinguishes a legitimate child from a biological child, and the claimant must prove paternity by admissible evidence, relying on 2025 LHC 495. Ref: Mohammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor and others (C.P.L.A.5626/2024, decided 18.02.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Mohammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor and others (C.P.L.A.5626/2024, decided 18.02.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Healthcare Commission: s. 22 Inspection and Enforcement Managers
records.heading: Inspection under section 22 and the Enforcement Managers mechanism operate without conflict
records.text: Inspection under s. 22 of the Punjab Healthcare Commission Act, 2010 and the Enforcement Managers' mechanism under the 2016 Regulations are mutually exclusive without conflict. Section 22 is an added tier, and visits and reports by Enforcement Managers in quackery allegations do not breach s. 22. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 675, PLD 2026 Lah 101; Muhammad Ahmad v. District Judge Pakpattan etc (W.P. 23462/25).
records.title: Muhammad Ahmad v. District Judge Pakpattan etc (W.P. 23462/25)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Healthcare Commission: s. 28 Fines by Committees
records.heading: Fines imposed by committees of the Commission do not breach section 28
records.text: The Commission is a juridical person acting through delegates and committees. Imposition of fines by committees it constitutes under the 2016 Regulations does not breach s. 28 of the Punjab Healthcare Commission Act, 2010, which does not confer exclusivity on the Commission itself. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 675, PLD 2026 Lah 101; Muhammad Ahmad v. District Judge Pakpattan etc (W.P. 23462/25).
records.title: Muhammad Ahmad v. District Judge Pakpattan etc (W.P. 23462/25)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Guardian Petition: Ordinary Residence, s. 9 GWA
records.heading: Guardian petition jurisdiction lies where the minor ordinarily resides on the date of institution
records.text: Under s. 9 of the Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 jurisdiction lies where the minor ordinarily resides, meaning settled and habitual abode. The relevant date is institution of the petition, and a later removal cannot divest a court of jurisdiction already vested. Ref: 2026 LHC 1241; Mst. Sosan Jaan & others v. Additional District Judge, Lahore & others (WP No.51854 of 2024, heard 26.01.2026).
records.title: Mst. Sosan Jaan & others v. Additional District Judge, Lahore & others (WP No.51854 of 2024, heard 26.01.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Abatement of Disciplinary Proceedings on Retirement
records.heading: Disciplinary proceedings abate where the servant retires before they conclude
records.text: Under F.R. 24-A disciplinary proceedings abate if the servant retires before they conclude, and s. 21 PEEDA Act, 2006 requires completion within two years of retirement. Initiating proceedings in 2011 and 2012 over mid-1990s transactions without reasons prima facie smacked of foul play. Ref: 2026 LHC 1191; Raja Asghar Ali v. DCO Chairman etc (W.P.12365-16, decided 19.02.2026); Justice Shujaat Ali Khan.
records.title: Raja Asghar Ali v. DCO Chairman etc (W.P.12365-16, decided 19.02.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation: Time-Barred Suit and Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Limitation may be considered even if not raised and a barred plaint is rejected
records.text: Limitation is no mere technicality, since expiry creates a right in the other side. As a question of law it may be considered even if not raised, including at appellate and revisional stage, and a time-barred suit's plaint is rejected forthwith without evidence or issues. Ref: 2026 MLD 162; Muhammad Akram v. Province of Punjab.
records.title: Muhammad Akram v. Province of Punjab

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell: Unidentifiable Property, s. 21(c) SRA
records.heading: An agreement to sell unidentifiable joint khata property is unenforceable under section 21(c)
records.text: Where the property in an agreement to sell, held in joint khata with partition pending, cannot be identified with reasonable certainty, the agreement is unenforceable under s. 21(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Specific performance was refused and refund of earnest money upheld. Ref: 2026 MLD 142; Shabbir Hussain v. Muhammad Shabbir Naveed.
records.title: Shabbir Hussain v. Muhammad Shabbir Naveed

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Summoning Inquiry Officer as Court Witness
records.heading: A departmental Inquiry Officer is not a material witness for summoning under section 540 CrPC
records.text: A departmental Inquiry Officer who inquired into the Investigating Officer's conduct is not a material witness in a s. 377-B PPC trial, as departmental proceedings have no relevance to the trial. The Trial Court rightly dismissed the s. 540 application. Ref: 2026 MLD 118; Muhammad Asif v. Asif.
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Asif

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Further Inquiry, Injury to Lip
records.heading: Post-arrest bail: an unexplained six day delay in reporting a lip injury required further inquiry
records.text: Allegation was a pistol butt blow to the mouth, reported after about six days without explanation. The injuries were under ss. 337-L(2) and 337-A(i) PPC, which are bailable, and s. 337-U PPC, and whether s. 337-U reads with s. 334 PPC is for the Trial Court. Case treated as one of further inquiry. Ref: 2026 MLD 108; Asif v. The State.
records.title: Asif v. The State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: Blocking CNIC of Judgment Debtor, s. 51(e) CPC
records.heading: Section 51(e) CPC cannot be stretched to block a judgment debtor's CNIC
records.text: Clause (e) of s. 51 CPC gives flexibility, but it cannot be stretched to permit blocking a judgment debtor's CNIC in executing a simple money decree. Curtailing his ability to live a normal life was an improper exercise of discretion, and the High Court erred. Ref: Agha Abid Majeed Khan v. Idrees Ahmed and another (C.P.L.A.3744/2023, decided 18.02.2026); Justice Munib Akhtar.
records.title: Agha Abid Majeed Khan v. Idrees Ahmed and another (C.P.L.A.3744/2023, decided 18.02.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Where Fine Is Alternative Punishment
records.heading: Bail should not be withheld where fine alone is an alternative punishment
records.text: Where an offence is punishable with fine alone as an alternative to imprisonment, bail should not be withheld, as detention would offend Art. 13(a), s. 403 CrPC and s. 26 General Clauses Act, 1897, and amount to premature punishment. The Court also stressed prison overcrowding and prompt disposal of trials. Ref: Liaqat Ali v. The State through P.G. Punjab Lahore and another (Crl.P.L.A.10-L/2026, decided 28.01.2026); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. The State through P.G. Punjab Lahore and another (Crl.P.L.A.10-L/2026, decided 28.01.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Suspended Employee: Entitlement to Full Salary
records.heading: A suspended employee remains entitled to full salary
records.text: Suspension is an interim measure and does not end the contract of service, so the employee remains entitled to full salary. Withholding pay without legal authority contravenes Fundamental Rule 53(b). Ref: Federal Board of Revenue v. Irshad Hussain Qaisrani & another (Civil Petition No. 4753 of 2025).
records.title: Federal Board of Revenue v. Irshad Hussain Qaisrani & another (Civil Petition No. 4753 of 2025)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption Price: Sale Price Versus Market Value
records.heading: The pre-emptor pays the price stated in the sale where fixed in good faith
records.text: Under s. 27 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pre-emption Act, 1987 the pre-emptor pays the price stated in the sale where fixed in good faith or actually paid. Only where the price was not fixed in good faith does the Court fix the market value, as a corrective mechanism. Ref: Ameer Nawab v. Wali Akbar (C.A.544/2022, decided 16.02.2026); Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui.
records.title: Ameer Nawab v. Wali Akbar (C.A.544/2022, decided 16.02.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Document Tendered Through Counsel's Statement
records.heading: A document tendered in counsel's statement has no evidentiary value
records.text: A document tendered in counsel's statement, neither by its author nor through witnesses, has no evidentiary value. Ref: 2026 LHC 1296; Javed Iqbal v. Data Chemical (Pvt.) Ltd. Faisalabad (Civil Revision No.13296 of 2023, heard 13.2.2026).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. Data Chemical (Pvt.) Ltd. Faisalabad (Civil Revision No.13296 of 2023, heard 13.2.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness to Pay
records.heading: A vendee seeking specific performance must show readiness and willingness to pay
records.text: A vendee seeking specific performance must show readiness and willingness, implying capacity to pay and intention to purchase. The plaintiff failed to offer the balance consideration in time or deposit it after suit. Specific performance is discretionary and the Court may put the vendee to terms to test his bona fides. Ref: 2026 LHC 1296; Javed Iqbal v. Data Chemical (Pvt.) Ltd. Faisalabad (Civil Revision No.13296 of 2023, heard 13.2.2026).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. Data Chemical (Pvt.) Ltd. Faisalabad (Civil Revision No.13296 of 2023, heard 13.2.2026)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Statutory Interpretation: Plain Words and "Any Provisions"
records.heading: Interpretation begins with the ordinary meaning of statutory words
records.text: Interpretation begins with the ordinary meaning of the statutory words, and construction arises only where they admit of two meanings. The phrase to enforce "any provisions of the Ordinance" covers the entire Ordinance, and equity cannot grant relief contrary to clear statutory provisions. Ref: M/s Sceptre Pvt. Ltd. v. Federation of Pakistan & Others (F.C.P.L.A. No.23/2026, decided 23.01.2026).
records.title: M/s Sceptre Pvt. Ltd. v. Federation of Pakistan & Others (F.C.P.L.A. No.23/2026, decided 23.01.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Admissibility and Value of CCTV and Video Evidence
records.heading: CCTV footage must be proved authentic, and once proved is like a witness
records.text: The judgment considers admissibility of CCTV footage in Pakistan, its foundational requirements and its evidentiary value, including whether it can sustain conviction where the ocular account is rejected. Footage must first be proved authentic, and once proved it is like a witness recounting events. Copies went to the Prosecutor General and IG Police Punjab. Ref: Muhammad Saeed v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal No. 221/2024); Imam Bukhsh v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal No. 290/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Saeed v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal No. 221/2024); Imam Bukhsh v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal No. 290/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recording Evidence in English: Urdu Translation, s. 360 CrPC
records.heading: English evidence must be translated into Urdu at once before the witness under section 360
records.text: The Court directed Punjab judges to prepare an Urdu translation of English evidence at once, before the witness, judge and accused, per s. 360 CrPC, so ambiguities are resolved on the spot. A typographical error in the complainant's cross-examination could not be isolated from the rest of the evidence. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 201; The State v. Muhammad Irfan Pomi (Murder Reference.221-21).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Irfan Pomi (Murder Reference.221-21)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Police Rules Ch. 25: Papers Accompanying Dead Body
records.heading: Police papers must accompany the dead body to the Medical Officer under Chapter 25
records.text: Under Rules 37 and 39 of Chapter 25 of the Police Rules, 1934 police papers and articles must accompany the body to the Medical Officer. Unexplained failure and belated autopsy cast doubt on police proceedings and on the timing and contents of the crime report. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 362; Muhammad Riaz alias Baddi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.748-J of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz alias Baddi v. The State (Criminal Appeal No.748-J of 2019)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Regularisation After Repeal of Punjab Regularization Act, 2018
records.heading: The Repeal Act 2025 operates prospectively for regularisation of contract employees
records.text: The Repeal Act, 2025 operates prospectively. Contract employees who completed three years' service before 31.10.2025 are to have cases dealt with under ss. 3 and 4 of the 2018 Act, and rejections based merely on repeal or contract expiry were set aside for fresh processing. Ref: 2026 LHC 1419; Mohsin Abbas & 40 others v. Secretary Communication & Works (C&W) & others (W.P.214-26, decided 18.02.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Mohsin Abbas & 40 others v. Secretary Communication & Works (C&W) & others (W.P.214-26, decided 18.02.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Schizophrenia and Commutation of Death Sentence
records.heading: Retribution and deterrence presuppose mental capacity, which bears on commuting a death sentence
records.text: The Court considered whether schizophrenia is a mitigating or supervening circumstance for commuting death to life imprisonment. It reasoned that retribution and deterrence presuppose mental capacity, so a person with profound mental illness stands outside their premises. Ref: Faryad Aoun Malik v. The State (Crl.A.105/2023, decided 27.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Faryad Aoun Malik v. The State (Crl.A.105/2023, decided 27.02.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witness: Satisfactory Explanation Required
records.heading: A chance witness must give a natural and probable explanation of his presence
records.text: A chance witness must give a natural, probable explanation of his presence, supported by independent circumstances, and his evidence demands greater circumspection. Consistent findings of innocence in successive investigations, absent proven influence, carry persuasive value and support the defence. Ref: Muhammad Nadeem v. The State (J.P.217/2018, decided 27.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Muhammad Nadeem v. The State (J.P.217/2018, decided 27.02.2026)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: ATA s. 6: Place of Occurrence Not Decisive
records.heading: Under section 6 ATA the test is the object, design and impact of the act
records.text: Place of occurrence alone does not attract the ATA, and the test is the object, design and impact of the act under s. 6. The FIR disclosed no intent to coerce or intimidate, and the version of personal vendetta in the s. 342 statement indicated a private motive. Ref: Khurram Ijaz v. The State through P.G. Punjab, Lahore & another (Crl.P.L.A.1327/2019, decided 13.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Khurram Ijaz v. The State through P.G. Punjab, Lahore & another (Crl.P.L.A.1327/2019, decided 13.02.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absence of Motive: Commutation of Death Sentence
records.heading: Where motive is neither alleged nor proved, death sentence is normally commuted to life
records.text: Where motive is neither alleged in the FIR nor proved by reliable evidence, the normal rule is to commute the death sentence to imprisonment for life. Ref: Khurram Ijaz v. The State through P.G. Punjab, Lahore & another (Crl.P.L.A.1327/2019, decided 13.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Khurram Ijaz v. The State through P.G. Punjab, Lahore & another (Crl.P.L.A.1327/2019, decided 13.02.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody in Narcotics Cases
records.heading: The prosecution must prove safe custody and transmission, and any break is fatal
records.text: The prosecution must prove safe custody and transmission of the recovered substance to the laboratory, and any break is fatal. Contradictions among witnesses, non-production of the site plan and roznamcha entries and the unexplained gap in custody left the case doubtful. Ref: Sardar Muhammad v. The State through P.G. Balochistan (Crl.P.L.A.1339/2022, decided 23.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Sardar Muhammad v. The State through P.G. Balochistan (Crl.P.L.A.1339/2022, decided 23.02.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302(c) PPC: Defence Version Supported by Niece
records.heading: Absence of concert and heat of passion places a case within section 302(c) PPC
records.text: In the social milieu a young girl would not ordinarily falsely allege an attack on her modesty, which lends assurance to the defence version. The absence of prior concert and heat of passion placed the case within s. 302(c) PPC rather than s. 302(b). Ref: Muhammad Tariq @ Billa v. The State (J.P.338/2018, decided 11.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Muhammad Tariq @ Billa v. The State (J.P.338/2018, decided 11.02.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302(c) PPC: Grave and Sudden Provocation at Home
records.heading: Intrusion and stripping of a spouse is grave and sudden provocation under section 302(c)
records.text: The prosecution witnesses suppressed material facts, and the occurrence at the threshold of the convict's house supported the defence that his wife was assaulted. Intrusion and stripping of a spouse is grave and sudden provocation, so the case fell under s. 302(c) PPC rather than s. 302(b). Ref: Riaz Ahmad v. The State (J.P.412/2018, decided 12.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Riaz Ahmad v. The State (J.P.412/2018, decided 12.02.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302(c) PPC: Spontaneous Firing in Heated Altercation
records.heading: A spontaneous single shot in a heated altercation falls within section 302(c) PPC
records.text: The occurrence arose in the heat of the moment from a dispute over crop price, with a single shot fired after an altercation at the convict's doorstep and no premeditation. The case fell within s. 302(c) PPC rather than s. 302(b), which the courts below overlooked. Ref: Mujahid Khan v. The State (J.P.778/2017, decided 09.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Mujahid Khan v. The State (J.P.778/2017, decided 09.02.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Upheld: Brutal Murder, No Mitigation
records.heading: Cold-blooded murder of three persons in daylight with no mitigation justified capital punishment
records.text: Substitution of real offenders is rare where eyewitnesses lost loved ones before their eyes. The cold-blooded murder of three persons in broad daylight, abusing trust and with no mitigating circumstance, justified capital punishment and no interference was warranted. Ref: Muhammad Shafi v. The State (J.P.201/2025, decided 19.02.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Muhammad Shafi v. The State (J.P.201/2025, decided 19.02.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Scope
records.heading: Authority on the scope of Order VI Rule 17 CPC
records.text: Authority on the scope of Order VI Rule 17 CPC. Ref: 2026 CLC 212; Khalid Mehmood & 1 other v. Muhammad Ali alias Tipu etc (Misc. Writ 50314/25).
records.title: Khalid Mehmood & 1 other v. Muhammad Ali alias Tipu etc (Misc. Writ 50314/25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Fraud Between Parties Only
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC does not apply to fraud between the parties alone
records.text: If the fraud is only between the parties, with no fraud or misrepresentation to the Court and no jurisdictional defect, s. 12(2) CPC does not apply. The position differs where a consent decree is obtained to gain the benefit of the fraud. Ref: 2026 CLC 201; Bashir Ahmad v. Shaukat Ali etc (Civil Revision.4749-15).
records.title: Bashir Ahmad v. Shaukat Ali etc (Civil Revision.4749-15)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Summary Dismissal and Evidence
records.heading: A section 12(2) CPC application disclosing no fraud may be summarily dismissed
records.text: A s. 12(2) CPC application disclosing no fraud, misrepresentation or jurisdictional defect and filed to delay execution warrants summary dismissal, and submissions suffice where no complicated question arises. Where facts need determination as a mixed question, evidence must be recorded. Ref: 2026 CLC 201; Bashir Ahmad v. Shaukat Ali etc (Civil Revision.4749-15).
records.title: Bashir Ahmad v. Shaukat Ali etc (Civil Revision.4749-15)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: S. 20 Arbitration Act 1940: Order of Reference Essential
records.heading: An order of reference under section 20(4) is essential before the arbitrator proceeds
records.text: An order of reference by the court under s. 20(4) of the Arbitration Act, 1940 is a sine qua non before the arbitrator proceeds. Without it the proceedings are patently illegal, and the trial court erred in making the award a rule of the court. Ref: 2026 CLC 316; Ch. Muhammad Nisar etc v. Waqar Ali Khan etc (F.A.O. 121-14).
records.title: Ch. Muhammad Nisar etc v. Waqar Ali Khan etc (F.A.O. 121-14)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Public Procurement: Splitting or Bundling of Works
records.heading: No law obliges a procuring agency to split tendered work into smaller contracts
records.text: No law obliges a procuring agency to split tendered work into smaller contracts. Directions were issued, including making the annual procurement plan public within one month of the fiscal year under Regulation 5 of the 2024 Regulations and Rule 8 of the 2014 Rules. Agencies should state reasons for bundling as best practice. Ref: 2026 CLC 357; M/s G.P Enterprises through M. Shafique Butt v. Province of Punjab etc (W.P.69497/24).
records.title: M/s G.P Enterprises through M. Shafique Butt v. Province of Punjab etc (W.P.69497/24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Closing Evidence After Final Opportunity
records.heading: Closing evidence under Order XVII Rule 3 CPC is proper after a final opportunity
records.text: Once a final opportunity is granted with a clear warning and costs, the court must enforce its order strictly. Not a single witness was recorded, so the trial court rightly invoked Order XVII Rule 3 CPC. Ref: 2026 CLC 328; Dr Samia Altaf v. Lahore University of Management Sciences etc (R.F.A.11082/25).
records.title: Dr Samia Altaf v. Lahore University of Management Sciences etc (R.F.A.11082/25)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements and Delayed Autopsy
records.heading: Dishonest improvements and an unexplained delayed autopsy undermine a prosecution witness
records.text: A witness who dishonestly improves his account undermines his veracity. Postmortem about nine hours after the occurrence, unexplained, suggested the interval was used to tailor the story. The motorcycle was not taken into possession, and blackening was possible only within three feet. Ref: 2026 LHC 1457; Afzaal etc v. The State (Jail Appeal.17383/20, decided 13.02.2026); Justice Abher Gul Khan.
records.title: Afzaal etc v. The State (Jail Appeal.17383/20, decided 13.02.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody: Delay in Depositing Charas Samples
records.heading: Unexplained delay in depositing charas samples with PFSA casts doubt on safe custody
records.text: Unexplained inordinate delay in handing the sealed sample parcels of charas to the PFSA casts doubt on safe custody, and the report is not duly proved without proof of safe custody and transmission. The prosecution failed to prove guilt. Ref: 2026 MLD 272; Muhammad Tanveer Tannu v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 571 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Tanveer Tannu v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 571 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 196 CrPC: Complaint Required at Cognizance Stage
records.heading: Section 196 CrPC applies at cognizance and not at the FIR or investigation stage
records.text: S. 196 CrPC concerns the stage of cognizance, so its condition need not be met for lodging the FIR or starting investigation. If the s. 173 report lacks the Government complaint, the court follows s. 230 CrPC and stops proceedings until it is received. Ref: 2026 MLD 294; Umair Altaf v. The State (CrL.Misc.3033-B/2025).
records.title: Umair Altaf v. The State (CrL.Misc.3033-B/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Reporting Crime to Police
records.heading: Eyewitness silence for about three hours was unexplained and went against the prosecution
records.text: The injured was taken to hospital by a police official, so police knew of the matter within about 1 hour 20 minutes. Eyewitnesses staying silent for about three hours was unexplained and went against the prosecution. Ref: 2026 MLD 221; The State v. Ihsan Ilahi (Murder Reference.33-20).
records.title: The State v. Ihsan Ilahi (Murder Reference.33-20)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive as Double-Edged Weapon
records.heading: Motive is a double-edged weapon
records.text: Motive may corroborate the prosecution case but is often a root cause of false implication, so it is a double-edged weapon. Ref: 2026 MLD 221; The State v. Ihsan Ilahi (Murder Reference.33-20).
records.title: The State v. Ihsan Ilahi (Murder Reference.33-20)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence as Corroborative Evidence
records.heading: Abscondence is only corroborative and avails nothing where direct evidence fails
records.text: People abscond out of fear and police torture and not only through guilt. Abscondence is only corroborative evidence and is of no avail where direct evidence fails. Ref: 2026 MLD 221; The State v. Ihsan Ilahi (Murder Reference.33-20).
records.title: The State v. Ihsan Ilahi (Murder Reference.33-20)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Suicide Plea: Stellate Gunshot Wound and GSR Test
records.heading: A gunshot residue test was necessary where the accused pleaded suicide
records.text: Where the accused pleads that the deceased shot herself, a gunshot residue test of her hands was necessary. A woman can commit suicide by gunshot, and a stellate forehead wound suggests contact or close firing but is not definitive alone and is assessed with other circumstances. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 704, PLJ 2026 CrC 120; Jamroz Khan v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal. 47572/23).
records.title: Jamroz Khan v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal. 47572/23)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody of Sample Parcels: Return to Moharrar
records.heading: Unproved safe custody of the sample parcel results in acquittal
records.text: If safe custody of the sample parcel is unproved the accused is acquitted without discussing other merits. A police official unable to deposit the parcel at the laboratory in working hours must return it to the Moharrar and recollect it on the deposit day. Here the parcels stayed with the complainant for two days. Accused acquitted. Ref: 2026 MLD 752, PLJ 2026 CrC 128; Rana Farman v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 71368-J of 2023).
records.title: Rana Farman v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 71368-J of 2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas Recovery: Chain of Custody and Standard of Proof
records.heading: The prosecution must prove an unbroken chain of safe custody in charas cases
records.text: The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, with stricter care in narcotics cases given harsh punishments. Issues were whether an unbroken chain of safe custody and transmission was established and whether the evidence was free of material contradictions. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 134; Waqar alias Vicky Gadehi v. The State (Spl. Crl. A. No. D-100 of 2024, decided 18.2.2025); Justice Khadim Hussain Tunio; Justice Riazat Ali Sahar.
records.title: Waqar alias Vicky Gadehi v. The State (Spl. Crl. A. No. D-100 of 2024, decided 18.2.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Wife Murdered in Husband's House: Burden on Husband
records.heading: A husband must explain the death of his wife killed in his house
records.text: Proof of qatl-i-amd needs the standard of Art. 17 QSO, and where a wife is killed in her husband's house he must explain under Art. 122 QSO. The Court urged the legislature to enact a burden of proof on the husband. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 147, 2026 YLR 658; Fayyaz Ahmad v. The State (Crl. A. No. 10150-J of 2023, heard on 23.9.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Fayyaz Ahmad v. The State (Crl. A. No. 10150-J of 2023, heard on 23.9.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Single Shot to Chest: No Mitigation
records.heading: A single fatal shot to the chest is not a mitigating circumstance
records.text: A single fatal shot to the chest shows lethal intent, and the fact that only one shot was fired is no mitigating circumstance warranting a lighter sentence. The Court condemned killing a woman for refusing marriage as gender-based violence and invoked Art. 9 of the Constitution. Ref: 2026 SCMR 205, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 130; Muhammad Kamran v. The State (Crl.A.91/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Kamran v. The State (Crl.A.91/2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Individual Criminal Liability, No Family Liability
records.heading: Criminal liability is personal and does not pass through family ties
records.text: Criminal liability is personal. A parent is not liable for the crime of an adult child, nor a child for a parent, unless complicity such as aiding or abetting is shown. Family ties do not transmit accountability, as actus reus and mens rea attach to the individual. Ref: 2026 SCMR 217; Khadim Hussain v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 974/2025).
records.title: Khadim Hussain v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 974/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Counsel's Authority to Withdraw Proceedings
records.heading: A pleader's authority under Order III continues until determined and binds the party
records.text: Under O. III CPC, particularly R. 4, the authority of a duly appointed pleader continues until determined with leave of the Court by a signed writing, death, or the end of the proceedings. A party is bound by a statement recorded by his counsel, and a later plea of want of authority fails. Application under s. 12(2) CPC context. Ref: 2026 LHC 1500; Fayyaz Ahmed Tariq v. M.B.O.R etc (Civil Petition / CM-u/s. 12(2) CPC/1969-23, decided 23.02.2026); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Fayyaz Ahmed Tariq v. M.B.O.R etc (Civil Petition / CM-u/s. 12(2) CPC/1969-23, decided 23.02.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness
records.heading: Specific performance requires continuous readiness and willingness and timely deposit of the balance
records.text: Specific performance is an equitable, discretionary relief, and the plaintiff must plead and show continuous readiness and willingness from the outset. The Urdu headnote adds that the balance sale price must be deposited within the time fixed by the Court, failing which the suit is dismissed and later deposit cannot be allowed. Concurrent findings may be interfered with on misreading or non-reading of evidence. Ref: Muhammad Imran v. Ishfaq Ahmed and othes (C.P.L.A.3639/2025, decided 26.02.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Ishfaq Ahmed and othes (C.P.L.A.3639/2025, decided 26.02.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 494 CrPC: Withdrawal from Prosecution and Acquittal
records.heading: Acquittal on withdrawal of prosecution under section 494 CrPC was held a judicial exercise
records.text: Where the prosecutor withdrew under s. 494 CrPC after six witnesses were examined, and the evidence showed no eye-witnesses, unexplained delay of 14 days in nomination and no convincing motive, the acquittal was held to be a judicial exercise in line with s. 265-K CrPC. No miscarriage of justice was caused. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 152.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Special Judge Anti-Corruption: No Suspension in Collateral Proceedings
records.heading: A Special Judge Anti-Corruption cannot order suspension of a civil servant in collateral proceedings
records.text: A Special Judge Anti-Corruption cannot, in collateral proceedings, order suspension of a civil servant. The Judge may recommend an inquiry if misconduct is suspected, but suspension rests with the competent authority, and the officer must first be given a hearing. Directions against the petitioner were contrary to natural justice. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 295-B PPC: Case Property Not Produced
records.heading: Failure to produce the case property in a section 295-B PPC case attracts Article 129(g)
records.text: Where the Holy Quran allegedly torn by the accused was not taken into possession or exhibited, the failure demolished the prosecution case and attracted the presumption under Art. 129(g) QSO, absent a plausible explanation. Benefit of doubt was extended to the accused. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 120.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Leading Question to Complainant: Expunged Question
records.heading: A prosecution question to the complainant on delay was expunged as leading
records.text: A prosecution question to the complainant on the reason for delay in reporting was expunged as leading. The Court noted the question did not relate to a material part of the incident, the omission was due to ignorance of legal technicalities, and the defence could cross-examine. Admissibility of questions is left to the trial Court's discretion. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 71.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Abscondence Not Sufficient for Conviction
records.heading: Mere abscondence is not sufficient to maintain a conviction
records.text: A person named as a murderer often conceals himself for fear of police torture and detention. Mere abscondence is therefore not sufficient to maintain a conviction and sentence without other reliable evidence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 257; Laiq Shah v. The State (Crl. Petition No.607/2020).
records.title: Laiq Shah v. The State (Crl. Petition No.607/2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Single Circumstance of Doubt Entitles Acquittal
records.heading: A single circumstance creating doubt is sufficient to acquit the accused
records.text: A single circumstance creating doubt in the prosecution case is sufficient to acquit the accused. The case contained a number of such circumstances. Ref: 2026 SCMR 257; Laiq Shah v. The State (Crl. Petition No.607/2020).
records.title: Laiq Shah v. The State (Crl. Petition No.607/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Order Based on Compromise
records.heading: An order passed on compromise is enforceable even without a formal decree
records.text: An order passed on a compromise between the parties remains binding and enforceable even without a formal decree, by virtue of s. 36 CPC. The Executing Court rightly entertained the execution petition and cannot go behind the order sought to be executed. Ref: Mst. Asma Begum and others v. Abdul Hameed (deceased) through L.Rs and others (C.P.L.A.4417/2024, decided 06.03.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Mst. Asma Begum and others v. Abdul Hameed (deceased) through L.Rs and others (C.P.L.A.4417/2024, decided 06.03.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Seating Arrangements for Witnesses in Witness Box
records.heading: Witnesses must be provided seating in the witness box
records.text: A witness is not required by law to testify standing. District and Sessions Judges, subordinate courts and Administrative Judges of Special Courts and Tribunals were directed to provide seating in the witness box, as consistent with human dignity and the right to a fair trial. Ref: Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA. 1160/2025, announced 06.03.2026).
records.title: Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA. 1160/2025, announced 06.03.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Joinder of Charges: Ss. 233 to 239 CrPC
records.heading: Section 233 requires separate trial for each distinct offence subject to listed exceptions
records.text: S. 233 CrPC requires separate trial of each distinct offence, subject to the exceptions in ss. 234, 235, 236 and 239. S. 235 permits one trial of a single accused for several offences forming the same transaction, and s. 239 extends the principle to joint trials. Ref: Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA. 1160/2025, announced 06.03.2026).
records.title: Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA. 1160/2025, announced 06.03.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal of Suit
records.heading: A plaintiff may abandon a suit without leave but cannot then sue afresh
records.text: A plaintiff may abandon a suit without leave but cannot then bring a fresh suit on the same cause of action, and cannot withdraw while reserving that right. Under O. XXIII R. 1(2) CPC the Court may permit withdrawal with liberty to sue afresh, protecting against O. II R. 2 and s. 11 CPC. Larger Bench decision. Ref: Mst. Sakina Bi, etc v. Barkat Hussain, etc. (Civil Appeal No.3347 of 2022, decided 06.03.2026).
records.title: Mst. Sakina Bi, etc v. Barkat Hussain, etc. (Civil Appeal No.3347 of 2022, decided 06.03.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Variation Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Minor variations between ocular and medical evidence on the seat of injury are inconsequential
records.text: Minor variations between the ocular account and medical evidence on the seat of injury are inconsequential. An eye-witness is not expected to give a photographic account of every injury in the panic of an attack. Ref: 2026 SCMR 317; Muhammad Ali v. The State (J.P. 541 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Ali v. The State (J.P. 541 of 2021)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Landlord-Tenant Relationship: Rent Controller's Jurisdiction
records.heading: The Rent Controller has no jurisdiction without a landlord and tenant relationship
records.text: Under the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 the Rent Controller has no jurisdiction unless a landlord and tenant relationship exists, and the onus to prove it lies on the landlord. Payment of rent is a sine qua non of that relationship. Ref: 2026 SCMR 208; Mst. Shaista Hussain v. Farzana Naheed and others (C.P.L.A. 5516/2024).
records.title: Mst. Shaista Hussain v. Farzana Naheed and others (C.P.L.A. 5516/2024)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Revenue Authorities and Civil Court Jurisdiction on Title and Fraud
records.heading: Revenue authorities do not decide title or fraud, which lie with civil courts
records.text: Revenue authorities have limited, administrative jurisdiction over record of rights and mutations and do not decide title or fraud. Civil courts have jurisdiction under s. 9 CPC, s. 172 of the Act does not bar adjudication of ownership and fraud, and civil court decisions bind the revenue hierarchy. Ref: Abdullah and others v. Waryam and others (Direct Civil Appeal No. 02-K of 2023).
records.title: Abdullah and others v. Waryam and others (Direct Civil Appeal No. 02-K of 2023)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Conversion of Writ into Review: Remand to Board of Revenue
records.heading: The High Court may convert a writ into a review and remit the matter
records.text: No fetters exist on the High Court's power to convert one type of proceeding into another or remit the matter to the competent forum. Relying on the maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit, the matter was remitted to the Board of Revenue, Punjab to be treated as a review under s. 8 of the Punjab Board of Revenue Act 1957. Writ petition disposed of. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 61; Azra Bibi and another v. Fazakat Hussain and others (Writ Petition No. 3790 of 2019, heard on 4.12.2025); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Azra Bibi and another v. Fazakat Hussain and others (Writ Petition No. 3790 of 2019, heard on 4.12.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Age Relaxation for Sub-Inspector Recruitment: Policy Decision
records.heading: Fixing age limits for recruitment is a policy decision courts rarely disturb
records.text: Fixing the age limit for Sub-Inspector recruitment, open merit or in-service quota, is a policy decision. Courts apply the rules as they stand and interfere only if the policy is patently arbitrary, mala fide or contrary to statute. Petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 68; Muhammad Irshad and 34 others v. Government of Punjab through Chief Secretary and 3 others (W.P. No. 56545 of 2025, heard on 9.10.2025); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Muhammad Irshad and 34 others v. Government of Punjab through Chief Secretary and 3 others (W.P. No. 56545 of 2025, heard on 9.10.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Pendente Lite Transferee Bound by Decree
records.heading: A pendente lite transferee is bound by the decree against the transferor
records.text: A pendente lite transferee sinks or swims with the transferor. A purchaser from a party who lost the suit cannot claim an independent right against the decree or allege fraud to set it aside, and the rule of lis pendens applies. Revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 79; Muhammad Saad Hayat v. Arif Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 242226 of 2018, heard on 2.10.2025); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Saad Hayat v. Arif Hussain, etc. (C.R. No. 242226 of 2018, heard on 2.10.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Forensic Comparison Where Forgery of Agreement Alleged
records.heading: Where forgery of an agreement is alleged, forensic examination may be ordered to resolve authenticity
records.text: Where forgery of an agreement to sell and receipt is the root of the dispute, the Court must use all available legal tools, including forensic examination, to resolve authenticity. The petition was allowed and the trial Court directed to obtain Forensic Science Laboratory opinion on the signatures and thumb impressions. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 100; Muhammad Suleman, etc. v. Muhammad Qamar, etc. (W.P. No. 53343 of 2025, heard on 20.10.2025); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Suleman, etc. v. Muhammad Qamar, etc. (W.P. No. 53343 of 2025, heard on 20.10.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Defendant in Jail: Duty of Court Before Ex-Parte Proceedings
records.heading: The court must order production of a defendant in jail before proceeding ex parte
records.text: When the process server reports that the defendant is in judicial custody, the Court must ensure procedural fairness, in particular by ordering his production from jail and supplying the plaint under O. V R. 24 CPC. Ex-parte proceedings were set aside and the revision accepted. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 107; Abdul Rehman v. Muhammad Ishaq (C.R. No. 50934 of 2025, heard on 21.10.2025); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. Muhammad Ishaq (C.R. No. 50934 of 2025, heard on 21.10.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 382-B CrPC Benefit and Computation of Sentence
records.heading: Remission under section 401 CrPC cannot be exercised without consent of the deceased's legal heirs
records.text: The petitioner sought, by writ, that his under-trial detention be counted against consecutive life sentences after the Supreme Court extended s. 382-B CrPC benefit. The Court observed that remission under s. 401 CrPC cannot be exercised without consent of the legal heirs of the deceased. Writ petition dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 111; Saghir Hussain v. State, etc. (W.P. No. 13501 of 2024, heard on 29.4.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Saghir Hussain v. State, etc. (W.P. No. 13501 of 2024, heard on 29.4.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Regularised Employee: Bar of Art. 212 on Writ
records.heading: A regularised employee is a civil servant and Article 212 bars a writ
records.text: A contract employee once regularised becomes a civil servant, and regularisation operates prospectively. A subsequent order withdrawing regularisation or reinstatement must be challenged through the departmental hierarchy and then the Service Tribunal, as Art. 199 is barred by Art. 212. Petition dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 121, 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1005; Hafiz Ahmed Raza v. Government of the Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 8215 of 2025, decided on 2.12.2025); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Hafiz Ahmed Raza v. Government of the Punjab, etc. (W.P. No. 8215 of 2025, decided on 2.12.2025)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-i-Muwathibat and Talb-i-Ishhad Not Proved
records.heading: The pre-emptor must prove the whole chain of information for Talb-i-Muwathibat
records.text: Under s. 13(3) Punjab Pre-emption Act 1991 the pre-emptor must establish the whole chain of information for Talb-i-Muwathibat, and failing to specify the exact portion of the house where knowledge was gained is fatal. Where Benches of equal strength conflict, the later view prevails. Application dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 124; Muhammad Anayat v. Muhammad Razzaq (C.R. No. 398-D of 2016, decided on 2.12.2025); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Anayat v. Muhammad Razzaq (C.R. No. 398-D of 2016, decided on 2.12.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Mental Health Ordinance: Guardianship Inquiry
records.heading: The Advocate-General's consent is only statutory clearance and the court decides guardianship
records.text: Under ss. 29 and 30 Mental Health Ordinance 2001 the Advocate-General's consent is only statutory clearance, and the Court decides guardianship. Where the Court itself examined the person alleged to be mentally disordered and found no sign of unsoundness, no referral was needed. Appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 132; Mst. Naghma Parveen, etc. v. Public at Large, etc. (F.A.O No. 117 of 2023, heard on 2.12.2025); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Mst. Naghma Parveen, etc. v. Public at Large, etc. (F.A.O No. 117 of 2023, heard on 2.12.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: New Plea at Leave to Appeal Stage; Remand
records.heading: A new factual plea requiring evidence cannot be raised first at the leave stage
records.text: Under Art. 185(3) of the Constitution a new factual plea requiring evidence cannot be raised for the first time at the leave stage. Remand is not routine and cannot give a litigant a chance to fill lacunae, and parties are bound by their pleadings. Ref: Faisal Paracha and Khawar Yasin Paracha v. Additional District Judge etc and Ehtasham Sheikh & others (C.P.L.A. No. 209, 210, 211, 212, 324 & 325/2026).
records.title: Faisal Paracha and Khawar Yasin Paracha v. Additional District Judge etc and Ehtasham Sheikh & others (C.P.L.A. No. 209, 210, 211, 212, 324 & 325/2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secret Audio Recordings: Admissibility
records.heading: Recording a conversation in which one participates is generally not illegal wiretapping
records.text: Recording a conversation in which one participates is generally not illegal wiretapping, whereas recording a conversation between others is. Admissibility of recordings depends on relevance, lawful procurement and respect for the parties' rights, and the complainant's illegality alone cannot be the sole basis for convicting an accused. Ref: Basharat Ali Chaudhry v. Sabir Ali, etc. (Criminal Petition No. 248-L/2016, decided 24.02.2026).
records.title: Basharat Ali Chaudhry v. Sabir Ali, etc. (Criminal Petition No. 248-L/2016, decided 24.02.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness and Children's Testimony Against Father
records.heading: An injured witness supported by medical evidence has special status as presence is assured
records.text: The testimony of an injured witness supported by medical evidence has special status, as presence at the scene is assured. Children are unlikely to falsely implicate their own father for the murder of their mother and sister absent a plausible motive shown by the defence. Ref: Muhammad Amin v. The State (Jail Petition No.190 of 2025, decided 17.02.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Amin v. The State (Jail Petition No.190 of 2025, decided 17.02.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 382-B CrPC Benefit Withheld
records.heading: The discretionary benefit of section 382-B CrPC was withheld given the manner of the offence
records.text: Having regard to the manner of commission of the offence and the convict's conduct, he was not entitled to the discretionary relief under s. 382-B CrPC, and the benefit was withheld. Ref: Muhammad Amin v. The State (Jail Petition No.190 of 2025, decided 17.02.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Amin v. The State (Jail Petition No.190 of 2025, decided 17.02.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal with Liberty and Costs
records.heading: Withdrawal with permission under Order XXIII Rule 1(2) is complete when ordered
records.text: Permission to file a fresh suit after withdrawal may be unconditional or conditional on costs, with or without a fixed time. Withdrawal with permission under sub-rule (2) is complete when ordered, and sub-rule (3) consequences do not follow from non-compliance with its conditions. Where costs are not a condition precedent, non-payment does not affect the competency of the later suit, and time can be extended under s. 148 CPC. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 946, 2026 YLR 436; Mst. Bakhan etc. v. Pir Bakhsh etc. (Review Application No. 3 of 2015 in R.S.A. No. 59 of 1989).
records.title: Mst. Bakhan etc. v. Pir Bakhsh etc. (Review Application No. 3 of 2015 in R.S.A. No. 59 of 1989)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Review Maintainable Where Correct Law Not Applied
records.heading: A review is maintainable where the court did not apply the correct law
records.text: A court must apply the correct law, and if it did not, a review application is maintainable. Review also lies where an important statutory provision escaped notice through inadvertence and might materially have affected the judgment. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lahore 946, 2026 YLR 436; Mst. Bakhan etc. v. Pir Bakhsh etc. (Review Application No. 3 of 2015 in R.S.A. No. 59 of 1989).
records.title: Mst. Bakhan etc. v. Pir Bakhsh etc. (Review Application No. 3 of 2015 in R.S.A. No. 59 of 1989)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Bloodstained Clothes Corroborate Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Bloodstained clothes of the complainant and eye-witnesses corroborate their presence at the scene
records.text: Bloodstained clothes of the complainant and cited eye-witnesses produced during investigation strongly corroborate the ocular account regarding their presence at the time and place of occurrence. Ref: 2026 YLR 361; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Appeal 16787/22).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Jail Appeal 16787/22)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Rent Tribunal to Decide Security and Arrears
records.heading: The Rent Tribunal must decide the dispute on security and arrears of rent
records.text: Under s. 2(b) of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009, the Rent Tribunal was obliged to pass an order on the dispute relating to security and arrears of rent raised in the ejectment application and the application for leave to contest. Ref: 2026 YLR 547; Tanveer Amjad Tahir v. Shahid Mehmood etc (WP.520-25).
records.title: Tanveer Amjad Tahir v. Shahid Mehmood etc (WP.520-25)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Production of Light Source: Identification
records.heading: Failure to prove a light source makes night identification of the assailant unreliable
records.text: Where the witnesses admitted a dark night and the prosecution failed to prove or produce any light source at the scene, their identification of the assailant cannot be relied upon, and the prosecution case fails. Ref: 2026 YLR 293; Zahoor Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 698-J of 2020).
records.title: Zahoor Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 698-J of 2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIII R. 2 CPC: Late Production of Documents
records.heading: Order XIII Rule 2 allows later production of documents on good cause shown
records.text: Procedural law serves justice. O. XIII R. 1 CPC requires documents at the first hearing, but R. 2 permits later production on showing good cause with recorded reasons, which is construed liberally and not to penalise inadvertent omissions. Ref: Muhammad Arif Ch. v. Syed Ulfat Hussain Mashhadi and others (WP.8805 of 2026, hearing 26.02.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Arif Ch. v. Syed Ulfat Hussain Mashhadi and others (WP.8805 of 2026, hearing 26.02.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay of 30 Hours in FIR
records.heading: Unexplained delay of about 30 hours in lodging the FIR is significant
records.text: A delay of about 30 hours in lodging the FIR was significant where the information reached police within about 1.5 hours and the prosecution gave no reason for the delay. The Court called for a cautious approach in evaluating the prosecution evidence. Ref: 2026 YLR 458; Muhammad Iqbal, etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Revision No.41 of 2014).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal, etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Revision No.41 of 2014)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: FIR of Deceased Complainant: Not Corroborative
records.heading: The FIR of a deceased complainant not cross-examined cannot be used as corroboration
records.text: Where the complainant died before his statement was recorded and was not cross-examined on the FIR (Exh.PA), then under Arts. 40 and 153 QSO the FIR cannot be used as corroborative evidence to uphold the conviction. Ref: 2026 YLR 458; Muhammad Iqbal, etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Revision No.41 of 2014).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal, etc. v. The State etc. (Criminal Revision No.41 of 2014)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive as Double-Edged Sword
records.heading: Motive is a double-edged sword
records.text: Motive may support the prosecution case but is also frequently a major reason for false implication of an accused, and is therefore regarded as a double-edged sword. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 762, 2026 YLR 513; Muhammad Arshad v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.78244 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Arshad v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.78244 of 2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Jurah Jaifa: Wound Extending to Body Cavity
records.heading: A wound extending into the body cavity of the trunk is Jurah Jaifa
records.text: Any hurt leaving a mark of wound, temporary or permanent, that extends into the body cavity of the trunk is Jurah Jaifa. The Court explained the torso as the area between neck and pelvis housing the thoracic and abdominal cavities. Ref: 2026 YLR 476; Saeed Khan v. Omar Farooq, etc. (Criminal Appeal No.325 of 2023).
records.title: Saeed Khan v. Omar Farooq, etc. (Criminal Appeal No.325 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sole Testimony of Injured Complainant
records.heading: Conviction can rest on the sole testimony of an injured complainant
records.text: Where the injured complainant was himself present and the doctor observed no fabrication of injuries, no other corroboration is required and conviction can rest on his sole testimony, subject to medical evidence. Ref: 2026 YLR 476; Saeed Khan v. Omar Farooq, etc. (Criminal Appeal No.325 of 2023).
records.title: Saeed Khan v. Omar Farooq, etc. (Criminal Appeal No.325 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 238 CrPC: Conviction Without Charge Under That Section
records.heading: No separate charge is required where the court may alter conviction under section 238 CrPC
records.text: No separate charge was required where the trial Court was competent under s. 238 CrPC to alter the conviction and sentence to the other section. Ref: 2026 YLR 476; Saeed Khan v. Omar Farooq, etc. (Criminal Appeal No.325 of 2023).
records.title: Saeed Khan v. Omar Farooq, etc. (Criminal Appeal No.325 of 2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Accrued Right to Appointment on Death of Civil Servant
records.heading: A right to appointment accrued before Rule 11-A was struck down is not defeated
records.text: On the death of a civil servant, one of the children or the spouse acquires the right to appointment, and application or appointment letter are administrative acts. As the right had accrued before the Supreme Court struck down Rule 11-A in PLD 2024 SC 1276, that judgment did not defeat it. Ref: The Province of Sindh v. Muhammad Rizwan Khan & others (F.C.P.L.A.Nos.508, 591, 346, 347, 348, 589, 267, 593, 130 and 353 of 2025).
records.title: The Province of Sindh v. Muhammad Rizwan Khan & others (F.C.P.L.A.Nos.508, 591, 346, 347, 348, 589, 267, 593, 130 and 353 of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: PEEDA Act s. 21 Proviso: Proceedings After Retirement
records.heading: Interpretation of the proviso to section 21 PEEDA Act on post-retirement proceedings
records.text: Authority on the interpretation of the proviso to s. 21 of the PEEDA Act, under which departmental proceedings are to be finalised within two years of the civil servant's retirement. Ref: 2021 SCMR 328.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. IX R. 13 CPC: Sufficient Cause
records.heading: An ex parte decree may be set aside on improper service or sufficient cause
records.text: A defendant may have an ex parte decree set aside under O. IX R. 13 CPC on showing improper service or sufficient cause for non-appearance. Sufficient cause has no exact definition and depends on the facts of each case, read with Art. 164 and s. 5 of the Limitation Act, and is distinguished from ordinary or gross negligence. Ref: Capital Development Authority (CDA), through Chairman, Islamabad and others v. Dr. Sheikh Muhammad Shoaib Shafi and another (C.P.L.A.2284/2025, decided 23.01.2026); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Capital Development Authority (CDA), through Chairman, Islamabad and others v. Dr. Sheikh Muhammad Shoaib Shafi and another (C.P.L.A.2284/2025, decided 23.01.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 42 Declaratory Decree: Recruitment Merit List
records.heading: A declaratory decree under section 42 requires an existing legal right that is denied
records.text: A declaratory decree under s. 42 requires an existing legal right that is denied or threatened. A candidate has at most a right to fair consideration, and failing the minimum marks under a valid policy extinguishes it, so a claim for inclusion challenges the policy itself. Ref: Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary Elementary & Secondary Education Department, Peshawar and another v. Rozina Abbas and others (C.P.L.A.862-P/2024, decided 18.02.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary Elementary & Secondary Education Department, Peshawar and another v. Rozina Abbas and others (C.P.L.A.862-P/2024, decided 18.02.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Complainant Withholding Source of Information
records.heading: A complainant's refusal to disclose the source of his information dents credibility
records.text: The complainant's refusal to disclose the source of information on which co-accused were nominated, in a case registered against unknown persons, was a serious dent in credibility. The question was not barred by Arts. 143 and 144 QSO, and the later implication became doubtful. Ref: Salamat Ali v. The State (Crl.A.543/2019); Justice Musarrat Hilali.
records.title: Salamat Ali v. The State (Crl.A.543/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Theory: Explanation by Accused
records.heading: An accused last seen with the deceased must give a probable explanation
records.text: The last seen theory is an important link in the chain of circumstances but cannot alone sustain a conviction. The accused last seen with the deceased must give a probable and satisfactory explanation of facts within his special knowledge, and failure may be an additional link in circumstantial cases. Ref: Abdul Razzaq v. The State (J.P.250/2023, decided 11.03.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Abdul Razzaq v. The State (J.P.250/2023, decided 11.03.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Delayed Challenge to Mutation; Fraud Must Be Proved
records.heading: Decades of unexplained delay defeat a challenge to a mutation
records.text: Unexplained delay of decades in challenging a mutation renders the claim untenable. Fraud must be specifically pleaded and strictly proved, and the party challenging an instrument must seek cancellation within the limitation period. Procedural objections to mutation proceedings do not by themselves annul the transaction. Ref: Pir Shah Abdul Haq (decd.) thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Irfan and others (C.A.2148/2019, decided 24.02.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Pir Shah Abdul Haq (decd.) thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Irfan and others (C.A.2148/2019, decided 24.02.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Cantonment Board Employees Are Not Civil Servants
records.heading: Employees of a Cantonment Board are not civil servants and may approach the High Court
records.text: Employees of a Cantonment Board are not civil servants, so the Service Tribunal lacks jurisdiction and they may approach the High Court. No court may decide a matter beyond its jurisdiction. Ref: Executive Officer, Cantonment Board Sialkot Cantt v. Qaiser Mehmood & others (Service C.P.L.A.395/2024); Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar.
records.title: Executive Officer, Cantonment Board Sialkot Cantt v. Qaiser Mehmood & others (Service C.P.L.A.395/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXII R. 15 CPC: Guardian for Suit of Unsound Mind
records.heading: The court must appoint a guardian for the suit for persons of unsound mind
records.text: O. XXXII R. 15 CPC covers persons adjudged of unsound mind and those found by the Court on inquiry incapable of protecting their interests, and the Court must appoint a guardian for the suit. The trial Court may appoint a guardian ad litem even though no guardian has yet been appointed under the Ordinance. Ref: 2026 LHC 1615; Riffat Saeed v. Zaheer Adnan etc (W.P. 1589-23, decided 27.01.2026); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Riffat Saeed v. Zaheer Adnan etc (W.P. 1589-23, decided 27.01.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC Mandatory in Family Court Summary Trial
records.heading: Section 342 CrPC remains mandatory in Family Court summary trial of offences
records.text: A Family Court trying offences under s. 20(2) Family Courts Act 1964 follows summary trial procedure, but failure to record the accused's statement under s. 342 CrPC remains a serious omission because the safeguard retains its mandatory character. The maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit was also applied. Ref: 2026 LHC 1630; Noor Ahmad v. The State etc. (W.P. 7946/26, decided 16.03.2026); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Noor Ahmad v. The State etc. (W.P. 7946/26, decided 16.03.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 204 CrPC: Sufficient Ground to Summon Accused
records.heading: Section 204 CrPC requires only sufficient ground to issue process in a complaint
records.text: S. 204 CrPC requires only sufficient ground, not reasonable ground, to issue process in a complaint, and this differs from s. 497(1) CrPC. A prima facie case is one that can be established if the evidence is believed. Neither ground existed here, and dismissal of the complaint and revision was upheld. Ref: 2026 LHC 1623; Muhammad Latif Khan v. Imran etc (Crl. Misc.13016/26, decided 02.03.2026); Justice Sardar Akbar Ali.
records.title: Muhammad Latif Khan v. Imran etc (Crl. Misc.13016/26, decided 02.03.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Issues Framed on Date of Judgment
records.heading: Framing issues on the date of judgment in an Order XXXVII suit vitiates the trial
records.text: In a suit under O. XXXVII CPC where leave is granted and only the plaintiff's evidence is on record, framing issues on the date judgment is announced vitiates the trial. The Appellate Court should remand if the evidence is insufficient to decide the case finally. Ref: 2026 LHC 1609; Nabeel Ahmad v. Abdul Ghafoor (RFA-292-16, decided 19.02.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Nabeel Ahmad v. Abdul Ghafoor (RFA-292-16, decided 19.02.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summary Suit on Cheques: Compromise Payment During Pendency
records.heading: Compromise and part payment during pendency do not divest the trial court of jurisdiction
records.text: A summary suit on cheques falls within negotiable instruments. A compromise and part payment made during pendency of proceedings is distinct from part payment before institution and did not divest the trial Court of jurisdiction after default and restoration of the suit. Ref: 2026 LHC 1590; Mudassar Aleem Babar v. Rana Nisar Asim (Civil Revision.13854/26, decided 04.03.2026); Justice Syed Ahsan Raza Kazmi.
records.title: Mudassar Aleem Babar v. Rana Nisar Asim (Civil Revision.13854/26, decided 04.03.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Setting Aside Ex-Parte Decree in Summary Suit: Art. 181
records.heading: Article 181 governs setting aside an ex parte decree where the defendant never appeared
records.text: For an application to set aside an ex parte decree in an O. XXXVII summary suit where the defendant never appeared, Art. 181 of the Limitation Act applies, giving three years from knowledge. Art. 164 applies only where the defendant had appeared, and the remedy lies under O. XXXVII R. 4 CPC. Ref: 2026 LHC 1669; Muhammad Yousaf v. Shehbaz Khan (Civil Revision No.504 of 2022, hearing 10.03.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Yousaf v. Shehbaz Khan (Civil Revision No.504 of 2022, hearing 10.03.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Departmental Proceedings Founded on Criminal Case End on Acquittal
records.heading: Departmental proceedings founded solely on a criminal case end on acquittal
records.text: Departmental proceedings against a civil servant founded solely on involvement in a criminal case collapse upon acquittal. Otherwise the charge must be independently provable for the department to proceed. The case concerned dismissal after an FIR with no independent misconduct. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 118, 2026 SCMR 843; Ghulam Murtaza v. District Police Officer, Gujrat and others (C.P. No. 4757 of 2024, decided 23.10.2025); Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Ghulam Murtaza v. District Police Officer, Gujrat and others (C.P. No. 4757 of 2024, decided 23.10.2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Oral Agreement to Sell: Particulars in Plaint
records.heading: A suit on an oral agreement to sell must plead specific particulars
records.text: A suit founded on an oral agreement to sell must plead specific particulars, namely exact date, time, place and names of witnesses. Ref: 2026 LHC 1705; Muhammad Nasir Ghouri v. Ch. Muhammad Nazir etc (Civil Revision-534-14, decided 28.01.2026); Justice Tariq Mahmood Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Nasir Ghouri v. Ch. Muhammad Nazir etc (Civil Revision-534-14, decided 28.01.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Evidence Recorded by Local Commission
records.heading: Evidence recorded by a Local Commission and cross-examined can be considered
records.text: Evidence recorded by a Local Commission and cross-examined by the contesting party can be legally considered where no specific appeal ground was raised against it and no prejudice was shown. Ref: 2026 LHC 1705; Muhammad Nasir Ghouri v. Ch. Muhammad Nazir etc (Civil Revision-534-14, decided 28.01.2026); Justice Tariq Mahmood Bajwa.
records.title: Muhammad Nasir Ghouri v. Ch. Muhammad Nazir etc (Civil Revision-534-14, decided 28.01.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Daughters' Claim for Future Marriage Expenses
records.heading: A father need not pay advance marriage expenses where no marriage is certain or imminent
records.text: A suit for marriage expenses lies only where expenses are immediate, certain and unjustly denied. The law imposes no obligation on a father to pay advance or indefinite marriage expenses where no date, engagement or preparation exists. The petition was dismissed, leaving daughters free to sue afresh when the cause of action arises. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 122; Naseem Mai and another v. Malik Muhammad Shah Aalam and others (CPLA No.2872-L of 2022).
records.title: Naseem Mai and another v. Malik Muhammad Shah Aalam and others (CPLA No.2872-L of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Theory of Last Seen Together
records.heading: Last seen evidence alone cannot sustain a murder charge without convincing corroboration
records.text: Last seen evidence is circumstantial and requires great caution. The time gap must exclude others, and the circumstance alone cannot sustain a murder charge without convincing corroboration such as recovery of incriminating items or a confession. It alone cannot sustain capital punishment. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 126; Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021).
records.title: Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Status of a Chance Witness
records.heading: Chance witness evidence is not accepted without justifiable reasons for presence
records.text: A chance witness claims presence at the scene by sheer chance, outside his ordinary business or residence. His evidence is ordinarily not accepted without justifiable reasons for presence, and requires strong corroboration, depending on the facts of each case. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 126; Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021).
records.title: Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Complete Chain Required
records.heading: A circumstantial chain must be complete, unbroken and consistent only with guilt
records.text: Where the case rests on circumstantial evidence without direct evidence, utmost care is needed. The chain of circumstances must be complete, unbroken, and incapable of explanation on any hypothesis other than guilt. Any missing link breaks the chain. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 126; Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021).
records.title: Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confession: Judicial and Extra-Judicial; Journalist Interview
records.heading: A confession recorded by a journalist while the accused is in custody is inadmissible
records.text: Confession is an acknowledgment of guilt relating to the charge, either judicial or extra-judicial, and under Art. 37 QSO is irrelevant if caused by inducement, threat or promise. A confession recorded by a journalist while the accused is in custody is inadmissible under Art. 39 QSO. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 126; Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021).
records.title: Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Media Access to Accused in Police Custody
records.heading: The court criticised police for giving a journalist access to interview an accused in custody
records.text: The Court criticised the police for giving a journalist access to interview an accused on physical remand and for the airing of the edited interview. It noted that Art. 19A is limited to matters of public importance and subject to reasonable restrictions, and expected regulators to consider standard operating procedures. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 126; Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021).
records.title: Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confronting Witness with Unauthenticated Video Clip
records.heading: A witness cannot be confronted with an unauthenticated video he did not make
records.text: A witness may be confronted with documents he authored or signed, but not with a video he did not make, is not seen in, and denies knowing, where authenticity and source are unverified and no forensic report exists. Refusal was no violation of constitutional rights, and defence may prove it in defence evidence. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 277, PLJ 2026 CrC Note 204; Muhammad Shoaib Hassan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 152 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Shoaib Hassan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 152 of 2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: S. 489-F PPC Further Inquiry
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail allowed in a section 489-F PPC case requiring further inquiry
records.text: In a s. 489-F PPC case where the cheque was returned because the drawer's signature differed from bank records, the matter required further inquiry, investigation was complete with no recovery, and mala fide was arguable. Pre-arrest bail was allowed under s. 498 CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 58; Muhammad Shoaib Kamran v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 10674-B of 2025, decided 4.12.2025); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Shoaib Kamran v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 10674-B of 2025, decided 4.12.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: S. 462-C PPC
records.heading: Post-arrest bail allowed where the ingredients of section 462-C PPC were prima facie missing
records.text: Ingredients of s. 462-C PPC were prima facie missing, no loss to the exchequer had been assessed, police conclusion of investigation does not bind the Court, and the FIR was delayed five days. Bail is the rule, and post-arrest bail was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 54; Muhammad Hanif v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 56619-B of 2025, decided 30.10.2025); Justice Sardar Akbar Ali.
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 56619-B of 2025, decided 30.10.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Offences Not Within Prohibitory Clause; No Evidence
records.heading: Bail cannot be denied on presumptions where no offence fell within the prohibitory clause
records.text: Where no witness statements supported the FIR allegations under PECA ss. 13, 14 and 16 and PPC provisions, most sections were bailable and none fell within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Bail cannot be denied on presumptions, and the petition was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 52; Zahid Siddique v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 3794-B of 2025, decided 19.5.2025); Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains.
records.title: Zahid Siddique v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 3794-B of 2025, decided 19.5.2025)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape of Minor: Competent Child Witness and DNA
records.heading: Conviction for rape of a minor was upheld on a competent child witness and DNA
records.text: Conviction under s. 376(iii) PPC was upheld on consistent ocular accounts, a minor victim found competent to testify, and supporting medical and DNA evidence.
