The appeal was dismissed with modification of sentence, and the death sentence was not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 45; Abdul Latif v. State (Crl. A. No. 1035 & C.S.R. No. 60 of 2021, heard on 7.10.2025); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem; Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Abdul Latif v. State (Crl. A. No. 1035 & C.S.R. No. 60 of 2021, heard on 7.10.2025)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: Cheque Not Public Document under S. 510 CrPC
records.heading: A cheque is not a public document admissible under section 510 CrPC
records.text: A cheque is not a public document admissible under s. 510 CrPC through the statement of the Assistant District Public Prosecutor. The original cheque was not tendered through a witness, so it was inadmissible, and under Art. 139 QSO the Court may direct production. Benefit of doubt given and revision allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 44; Munir Ahmad v. State, etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 44 of 2013, decided 30.01.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Munir Ahmad v. State, etc. (Crl. Rev. No. 44 of 2013, decided 30.01.2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Ocular and Medical Evidence; Delayed Post-Mortem
records.heading: Conflict between ocular and medical accounts and delayed post-mortem indicate a blind murder
records.text: Conflict between ocular and medical accounts, and a post-mortem delayed about 12 hours, indicated a blind murder and that the witnesses were not present. Appeal allowed, the accused acquitted and the enhancement revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 42; Waseem Akram etc. v. State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 10158 & Crl. Rev. No. 19582 of 2023, heard on 15.10.2025); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Waseem Akram etc. v. State, etc. (Crl. A. No. 10158 & Crl. Rev. No. 19582 of 2023, heard on 15.10.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Testimony of Chance Witnesses
records.heading: Chance witnesses need cautious scrutiny and a satisfactory explanation of their presence
records.text: The testimony of chance witnesses requires cautious scrutiny and is not to be accepted unless they satisfactorily explain their presence at or near the scene at the relevant time, relying on PLD 2021 SC 600. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 35; Naseer Ahmad Khan and another v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 06, 127 & Crl. Rev. No. 90 of 2007, heard on 20.3.2025); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch.; Justice Sardar Akbar Ali.
records.title: Naseer Ahmad Khan and another v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 06, 127 & Crl. Rev. No. 90 of 2007, heard on 20.3.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Deliberate Improvement in Witness Statement
records.heading: A deliberate and mala fide improvement in a witness statement makes testimony unreliable
records.text: When a witness improves his statement to strengthen the prosecution case and the improvement is found deliberate and mala fide, his testimony ceases to be reliable, relying on 2010 SCMR 385, PLD 2021 SC 600 and 2021 SCMR 810. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 35; Naseer Ahmad Khan and another v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 06, 127 & Crl. Rev. No. 90 of 2007, heard on 20.3.2025); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch.; Justice Sardar Akbar Ali.
records.title: Naseer Ahmad Khan and another v. State etc. (Crl. A. Nos. 06, 127 & Crl. Rev. No. 90 of 2007, heard on 20.3.2025)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay: No Preferential Treatment to Government
records.heading: Government departments receive no preferential treatment in condoning delay
records.text: In condoning delay, no preferential treatment is accorded to government departments, and generic administrative delay is not sufficient cause. The appeal by the Province of Sindh, barred by thirty days in a land acquisition compensation matter, was confronted on limitation, and the law helps the vigilant. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 113; Province of Sindh through Land Acquisition Officer v. Abdul Tawab & others (C.A.101-K/2022).
records.title: Province of Sindh through Land Acquisition Officer v. Abdul Tawab & others (C.A.101-K/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Daughters' Claim for Advance Marriage Expenses
records.heading: Marriage expenses can be claimed only when the date is fixed and expenses are immediate
records.text: Urdu summary of PLD 2026 SC 122. Marriage expenses can be claimed only when the date is fixed, preparations are underway and the expenses are immediate and certain. A father has no legal duty to pay advance sums for an uncertain future marriage, as courts decide on existing rights and not speculation. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 122; Naseem Mai v. Malik Muhammad Shah Aalam (CPLA No. 2872-L of 2022).
records.title: Naseem Mai v. Malik Muhammad Shah Aalam (CPLA No. 2872-L of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 129 QSO: Non-Production of Driver Witness
records.heading: Non-production of the vehicle driver raised the Article 129 presumption against the prosecution
records.text: Failure to produce Tariq, the driver of the vehicle, as a witness entailed the presumption under Art. 129 QSO that the evidence would have gone against the prosecution, and was fatal to the prosecution case against the appellants. Ref: 2026 LHC 1817; Muhammad Atif and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 62 of 2024, decided 20.01.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Atif and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 62 of 2024, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Falsus in Uno Falsus in Omnibus
records.heading: A witness who lied on a material aspect cannot be believed on other aspects
records.text: A witness found to have lied on a material aspect cannot safely be believed on other aspects, and his testimony cannot be used to convict some accused while acquitting others charged with the same offence, per the maxim falsus in uno falsus in omnibus. Ref: 2026 LHC 1817; Muhammad Atif and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 62 of 2024, decided 20.01.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Atif and another v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 62 of 2024, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXIX R. 2(3) CPC: Violation of Injunction and Sentence
records.heading: Violation of an injunction under Order XXXIX Rule 2(3) may be inferred from continuous defiance
records.text: Violation of an injunction may be inferred from a series of acts of continuous defiance. Proceedings under O. XXXIX R. 2(3) CPC are quasi-criminal, with discretion to attach property, detain up to six months, or both. The Appellate Court exceeded jurisdiction by substituting its discretion without illegality, and later dismissal of the suit is a relevant circumstance. Ref: Muhammad Asif Qureshi & others v. Hakim Ghulam Murtaza & others (Civil Revision No.38 of 2019, hearing 17.03.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Asif Qureshi & others v. Hakim Ghulam Murtaza & others (Civil Revision No.38 of 2019, hearing 17.03.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Transparency in Public Appointments: Art. 18
records.heading: Article 18 requires a transparent, fair and just process in public appointments
records.text: Art. 18 of the Constitution gives every citizen the right to compete for public appointments, which requires a transparent, fair and just process. Appointments even to lower posts such as Naib Qasid, Sweeper and Chowkidar demand utmost care and integrity, and departure from this undermines public trust. Ref: Muhammad Bilal and others, Shah Jee Ullah and others v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, through the Secretary Health, Peshawar, and others (C.P.L.A. No. 3119, 3905, 4824, 4825, 4826 & 4827 of 2025, decided 12.03.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Bilal and others, Shah Jee Ullah and others v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, through the Secretary Health, Peshawar, and others (C.P.L.A. No. 3119, 3905, 4824, 4825, 4826 & 4827 of 2025, decided 12.03.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 167 CrPC: Duty Magistrate Cannot Discharge Accused
records.heading: A duty Magistrate under section 167 CrPC cannot discharge the accused
records.text: A Magistrate to whom the accused is forwarded under s. 167 CrPC for remand, having no jurisdiction to try or send for trial, may authorise detention up to fifteen days and, if further detention is unnecessary, forward the accused to a competent Magistrate. He was not competent to discharge the accused. Ref: 2026 LHC 1989; The State etc v. The Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc (W.P. 61369/19, decided 24.03.2026); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: The State etc v. The Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc (W.P. 61369/19, decided 24.03.2026)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: S. 162 PPC: Trial by Special Judge Anti-Corruption
records.heading: An offence under section 162 PPC is tried by the Special Judge Anti-Corruption
records.text: An offence under s. 162 PPC is always committed by a private person but is tried by the Special Judge Anti-Corruption appointed under the Pakistan Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 1958. S. 63 CrPC was described as a clause of result or consequence, neither enabling nor vesting. Ref: 2026 LHC 1989; The State etc v. The Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc (W.P. 61369/19, decided 24.03.2026); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: The State etc v. The Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc (W.P. 61369/19, decided 24.03.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Christian Divorce: Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Christian citizens may seek dissolution or judicial separation through civil courts
records.text: Christian citizens may seek dissolution or judicial separation through civil courts as part of their freedom to profess and manage their religious law. The courts below failed to examine cruelty and the admitted separation under ss. 10 and 22 of the Divorce Act, infringing Art. 10-A read with Art. 4. Directions issued for circulation and judicial training. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 206, PLJ 2026 Lah 344; Shahroz v. ADJ etc (W.P. 2092/2024).
records.title: Shahroz v. ADJ etc (W.P. 2092/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Defamation Ordinance: Trial by Additional District Judge
records.heading: An Additional District Judge may try defamation cases concurrently with the District Judge
records.text: After the substitution of 'District Judge' by 'District Court' in s. 13 of the Defamation Ordinance 2002 through the 2004 amendment, read with s. 6(2) of the Civil Courts Ordinance 1962, an Additional District Judge entrusted with the case exercises concurrent authority. Trial of defamation cases is not exclusive to the District Judge. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 200; Riasat Ali & 1 Other v. Muhammad Sharif etc (W.P. 34478/2025).
records.title: Riasat Ali & 1 Other v. Muhammad Sharif etc (W.P. 34478/2025)

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.topic: Passport Control List: Mere Registration of Case
records.heading: Mere involvement in a criminal case does not justify restricting international travel
records.text: Mere involvement in a criminal case does not justify restricting international travel, particularly where the accused has been admitted to bail by a competent court. The respondents relying on Rule 22(2)(b) of the Passport Rules 2021 pointed to no guideline or data supporting the placement, and the premise that the petitioner was not apprehended was incorrect given his confirmed pre-arrest bail. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 195; Shahid Javed v. Government of Pakistan etc (W.P. 4166/2025).
records.title: Shahid Javed v. Government of Pakistan etc (W.P. 4166/2025)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Punjab Rented Premises Act: Leave to Contest, Registration, Landlord
records.heading: An unregistered lease beyond twelve months is treated as a month to month tenancy
records.text: The ten day period under s. 22(2) of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 excludes the first day of appearance, by s. 8 of the Punjab General Clauses Act 1956. An unregistered lease beyond 12 months is treated as a month to month tenancy terminable by notice. A Mutwalli who receives rent is a landlord under s. 2(d), so his ejectment petition is maintainable. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 172; Ms Phipsons Company Pvt Limited v. Zahid Moyeen etc (W.P. 1913/2020).
records.title: Ms Phipsons Company Pvt Limited v. Zahid Moyeen etc (W.P. 1913/2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 204 CrPC: Sufficient Ground for Summoning
records.heading: Section 204 CrPC summoning needs only sufficient ground supported by the complaint and preliminary evidence
records.text: Where the allegation in a complaint fulfils the definition of the offence and the complainant's statement under s. 200, the witnesses' statements under s. 202 and the documents relied upon support it, so as to suffice for framing a charge and proceeding to trial, there is sufficient ground for summoning the accused under s. 204 CrPC. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 597; Ihsan Ul Haq v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 38316/2023).
records.title: Ihsan Ul Haq v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 38316/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Defence Witnesses: Ss. 94, 265-F, 540 CrPC
records.heading: Refusal to summon defence witnesses without substantial reason is a material irregularity
records.text: Under s. 265-F(7) CrPC the court shall issue process for witnesses and documents sought by an accused in defence unless the application is made for delay or to defeat justice; refusal is the exception and the violation is an incurable irregularity. Section 540 CrPC allows summoning any essential witness. Refusal to summon the control room operator and Rescue 15 record without substantial reason was a material irregularity. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 472; Majid Javed alias Javed Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 242/2025).
records.title: Majid Javed alias Javed Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 242/2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Transfer of Vehicle Case Property by Excise Authorities
records.heading: Excise authorities shall not transfer ownership of vehicles that are criminal case property
records.text: The Excise and Taxation authorities shall not effect any transfer of ownership of vehicles that are involved in criminal cases or treated as case property. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 436; Muhammad Riaz v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 9528/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 9528/2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 47 QSO and S. 512 CrPC: Absconder's Trial
records.heading: Earlier testimony may be read under Article 47 QSO against an absconding accused
records.text: Earlier testimony may be read under Art. 47 QSO and s. 512 CrPC where the witness is dead or otherwise unavailable and the substance of the conditions is met; minor irregularities in formal transposition are ignored. An absconding accused impliedly waives the right to cross-examine at the earlier trial and cannot insist on strict compliance, since no one may profit from his own wrong. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1139, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 81; Riffat Hussain v. Zahida Bibi and another (Crl.P.L.A. 1431/2020).
records.title: Riffat Hussain v. Zahida Bibi and another (Crl.P.L.A. 1431/2020)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Giving Up Witnesses and S. 540 CrPC in Narcotics Trial
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC governs summoning of witnesses in narcotics trials through section 47 CNSA
records.text: Section 47 of the Control of Narcotic Substances Act 1997 applies the CrPC to such trials, so s. 540 CrPC governs summoning of witnesses, with a discretionary first part and a mandatory second part where evidence is essential. A witness whose statement was not recorded during investigation cannot be examined under s. 540; if already examined, the value of the evidence decides prejudice. Ref: 2026 SCMR 870, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 89; Ameenullah and Khairullah v. The State & another (Crl.A. 525/2022).
records.title: Ameenullah and Khairullah v. The State & another (Crl.A. 525/2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Safe Custody and Chain of Custody
records.heading: The prosecution must prove an unbroken chain of safe custody in narcotics cases
records.text: In a conviction under the Control of Narcotic Substances Act 1997 the prosecution must prove beyond reasonable doubt that the recovered material is a narcotic drug. The analyst's report depends on proof of recovery and of an unbroken chain of safe custody from recovery until receipt of the samples at the government analyst's office. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 89; Ameenullah and Khairullah v. The State & another (Crl.A. 525/2022).
records.title: Ameenullah and Khairullah v. The State & another (Crl.A. 525/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Cannot Be Imposed; S. 2(iia) DMMA
records.heading: A dissolution suit cannot be converted into khula without the wife's clear statement
records.text: A Family Court cannot on its own motion convert a suit for dissolution under the DMMA into one for khula without a clear and unequivocal statement by the wife, as khula rests on her express consent. Where the husband contracted a second marriage in contravention of the MFLO, s. 2(iia) DMMA gives a ground for dissolution that the courts below failed to adjudicate. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 181; Mst. Naila Javed and another v. Nasir Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 3767/2025).
records.title: Mst. Naila Javed and another v. Nasir Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 3767/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal Simpliciter Bars Fresh Suit
records.heading: Withdrawal simpliciter on a private arrangement bars a fresh suit under Order XXIII Rule 1(3)
records.text: A withdrawal founded on a private arrangement that is not judicially recognised or reflected in the order is a withdrawal simpliciter. It attracts the bar in O. XXIII R. 1(3) CPC and precludes a later suit on the same subject matter, which was also time barred. Failure to challenge the withdrawal order estops re-agitation. Ref: 2026 SCMR 757, PLJ 2026 SC 186; Sohail Islam and another v. Saadullah Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 5071/2025).
records.title: Sohail Islam and another v. Saadullah Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 5071/2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Pardanasheen Lady: Proof of Sale Mutation
records.heading: Courts exercise heightened caution where a pardanasheen woman is party to a transaction
records.text: Where a pardanasheen or similarly placed woman is party to a transaction, courts exercise heightened caution. The party relying on it must prove free will and informed consent, that its nature and consequences were explained in a language she understood, and that she had independent and disinterested advice, following the safeguards in Phul Peer Shah, Ghulam Farid and Ghulam Muhammad. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 200; Muhammad Ishfaq and another v. Salma Begum (C.P.L.A. 4878 and CMA 14023/2025, decided 08.01.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan; Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Ishfaq and another v. Salma Begum (C.P.L.A. 4878 and CMA 14023/2025, decided 08.01.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: FIR and Criminal Proceedings Through Attorney
records.heading: An attorney may lodge an FIR and initiate criminal proceedings for his principal
records.text: An attorney may lodge an FIR and initiate criminal proceedings before a court for his principal, and may continue them with the court's permission if the principal becomes unavailable or incapacitated. Misuse through false FIRs or complaints can be met by action under ss. 181, 182, 211, 213 and 250 PPC. The contention that an FIR cannot be registered through an attorney was rejected. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 209, 2026 PCrLJ 638; Mirza Yahya Baig v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 53550/2025).
records.title: Mirza Yahya Baig v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 53550/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Polygamy Offence: Family Court and Appeal Forum
records.heading: The offence of polygamy is triable only by the Family Court
records.text: Trial of the offence of polygamy lies only before the Family Courts under the Family Court Act 1964, and appeals lie to the District Court under s. 14 of that Act. The Court of Sessions therefore lacked jurisdiction to decide the appeal. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 191; Muhammad Asif v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 25041/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 25041/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revision Against Interlocutory Order Premature
records.heading: A revision against an interlocutory order lacking finality is premature
records.text: A court may summon essential witnesses as court witnesses and seek expert opinion, and an appellate court may do so as well. The impugned order was an interlocutory procedural order lacking finality, so it could not be challenged in revision under s. 115 CPC. Revision dismissed in limine as premature. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 165; Mst. Naseem Mai (deceased) through L.Rs v. Muhammad Saleem Anjum (C.R. 10/2026, decided 12.01.2026); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Mst. Naseem Mai (deceased) through L.Rs v. Muhammad Saleem Anjum (C.R. 10/2026, decided 12.01.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Petition: Certified Copy of Judgment Relied Upon
records.heading: A petitioner must ordinarily file certified copies of orders relied upon in a writ petition
records.text: A petitioner must ordinarily file certified copies of court orders relied upon or impugned, and no presumption of authenticity attaches to an uncertified copy. He may file a copy of a certified copy with an application dispensing with the certified copy, or remove and re-file. Order accordingly. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 176; Muhammad Shafiq Shah v. Government of Punjab etc (Objection Civil 100/2026, decided 21.01.2026); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Muhammad Shafiq Shah v. Government of Punjab etc (Objection Civil 100/2026, decided 21.01.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings should be allowed if necessary to determine the real controversy
records.text: Amendment of pleadings should ordinarily be allowed if necessary to determine the real controversy and it neither changes the complexion of the case nor prejudices the other side. Refusal of a limited and necessary amendment under O. VI R. 17 CPC was a material irregularity and a failure to exercise jurisdiction. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 188; Sadaqat Ali Khan (deceased) etc v. Zia Safdar Malik etc (W.P. 1975/2022).
records.title: Sadaqat Ali Khan (deceased) etc v. Zia Safdar Malik etc (W.P. 1975/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Interim Injunction in Defamation Suit
records.heading: Courts may grant limited interim injunctions in defamation suits to prevent irreparable harm
records.text: In defamation suits under the Defamation Ordinance 2002 involving serious and unproven allegations, courts may grant limited interim injunctions to prevent irreparable harm. Freedom of speech is not absolute and must be balanced against an individual's reputation, with restraint that does not foreclose final adjudication. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 194, 2026 CLC 624; Meera Shafi through Saba Hamid v. ADJ etc (W.P. 19774/2019).
records.title: Meera Shafi through Saba Hamid v. ADJ etc (W.P. 19774/2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Articles: Execution and Alternate Value
records.heading: A judgment debtor cannot compel acceptance of alternate value for decreed dowry articles
records.text: Where a decree grants dowry articles or alternatively their value, the judgment debtor has no option to compel acceptance of the alternate value, and the Executing Court cannot force that substitution on the decree holder. The alternate valuation is not a strategic device for the judgment debtor. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 236; Afzaal Bibi v. ADJ etc (W.P. 12039/2025).
records.title: Afzaal Bibi v. ADJ etc (W.P. 12039/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt to Non-Appealing or Absconding Co-Accused
records.heading: Benefit of doubt can be extended to a non-appealing or absconding co-accused
records.text: If the appellate court finds the prosecution evidence doubtful and untrustworthy, the benefit of doubt can be extended to a convict who filed no appeal and even to an absconding accused. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 110; Ghulam Mustafa alias Raja Buledi v. The State (Crl.A. 199/2023).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa alias Raja Buledi v. The State (Crl.A. 199/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Document Tendered Through Counsel's Statement
records.heading: A document tendered in counsel's statement and not by its author has no value
records.text: A document tendered in the statement of counsel, and neither by its author nor through witnesses, has no value in law and no evidentiary worth. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 244; Javed Iqbal v. Data Chemical (Pvt.) Ltd. Faisalabad (Civil Revision 13296/2023).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. Data Chemical (Pvt.) Ltd. Faisalabad (Civil Revision 13296/2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness to Pay
records.heading: A vendee seeking specific performance must show readiness and willingness to pay the balance
records.text: A vendee seeking specific performance must show readiness and willingness, which implies capacity to pay the balance consideration within reasonable time and intention to purchase. The relief is discretionary, and the court may put the vendee to terms to test his bona fides. The vendee here failed to offer or deposit the balance. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 244; Javed Iqbal v. Data Chemical (Pvt.) Ltd. Faisalabad (Civil Revision 13296/2023).
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. Data Chemical (Pvt.) Ltd. Faisalabad (Civil Revision 13296/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Re-Examination Limited by Art. 133(3) QSO
records.heading: Re-examination is confined to matters arising from cross-examination under Article 133(3) QSO
records.text: Re-examination is confined by Art. 133(3) QSO to matters arising out of cross-examination and cannot be used to fill lacunae or improve on examination-in-chief. If new matter is introduced with the court's permission, the adverse party may cross-examine on it. Art. 165 gives the Order overriding effect over the Code. Ref: 2026 LHC 2052; Mst Nasreen Fatima alias Nusro v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 10516/2026); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Mst Nasreen Fatima alias Nusro v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 10516/2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift: Ingredients and Proof of Mutation
records.heading: A valid oral gift requires offer, acceptance and delivery of possession proved by cogent evidence
records.text: A valid gift needs offer, acceptance and delivery of possession, proved by cogent evidence, and a mutation based on oral gift must be independently proved under the Land Revenue Act 1967 and the QSO. Withholding the best available witnesses raised an adverse presumption under Art. 129(g) QSO. Ref: 2026 SCMR 587; Abdul Majeed and another v. Mst. Khalida Bibi (deceased) through L.Rs and others (C.P.L.A. 990/2022).
records.title: Abdul Majeed and another v. Mst. Khalida Bibi (deceased) through L.Rs and others (C.P.L.A. 990/2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cross Version Cases: Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail may be granted in a cross version case where further inquiry is required
records.text: Bail cannot be claimed as of right in a cross version case, but where the cross version raises reasonable scepticism about guilt, the court may grant bail under s. 497(2) CrPC as the matter requires further inquiry into who was the aggressor and who acted in self-defence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 442; Manan and others v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 806/2025).
records.title: Manan and others v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 806/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Reduced: Enmity and Mitigating Circumstance
records.heading: A single mitigating circumstance may justify life imprisonment in place of death
records.text: Where the crime arose from mutual enmity and revenge, a single mitigating circumstance may justify life imprisonment in place of death, relying on 2014 SCMR 1034. The Court considered that a diminished penalty would satisfy the ends of justice. Ref: 2026 SCMR 598; Muhammad Ikram & 2 others v. The State (J.P. 23/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ikram & 2 others v. The State (J.P. 23/2023)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Murder of Judicial Officer as Terrorism
records.heading: Killing a judge because of his official duties is terrorism under section 6 ATA
records.text: The targeted killing of a public servant, here a judge, because of his official duties falls within terrorism under s. 6 ATA, including s. 6(1)(b) and (2)(f), as it intimidates public servants and spreads fear. The High Court rightly held it an act of terrorism and the convictions were justified. Appeals dismissed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 413; Fiaz alias Mansha and Rashed alias Chand v. The State (J.P. 432/2021).
records.title: Fiaz alias Mansha and Rashed alias Chand v. The State (J.P. 432/2021)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302(c) PPC: Qatl in Heat of Passion
records.heading: A single shot fired in heat of passion attracts section 302(c) PPC
records.text: Where an altercation at the appellant's shop led him to fire a single shot in the heat of passion, the ingredients of s. 302(c) PPC were attracted rather than s. 302(b). Cases under clause (c) are not exhaustively defined and are left to judicial discretion case by case. Ref: 2026 SCMR 466; Shahzad Liaquat v. The State (Crl.A. 503/2022).
records.title: Shahzad Liaquat v. The State (Crl.A. 503/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution: Current Value of Gold Ornaments
records.heading: An executing court may direct payment of the current market value of gold ornaments
records.text: Where a decree expressly provides alternate modes of satisfaction, the decree holder retains the choice. An executing court may direct payment of the current market value of gold ornaments if their return is not possible. Ref: 2026 SCMR 494; Shafaqat Ali v. Mst. Zaib un Nisa and others (C.P.L.A. 74/2025).
records.title: Shafaqat Ali v. Mst. Zaib un Nisa and others (C.P.L.A. 74/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Child Maintenance After Dissolution of Marriage
records.heading: A father's obligation to maintain his children survives dissolution of the marriage
records.text: The father bears a continuous obligation to maintain his children, a son until puberty (or beyond if incapacitated) and a daughter until marriage. This obligation is independent of the duty to maintain a wife and survives dissolution and loss of custody. It may devolve on a financially capable mother, and then on the paternal grandfather. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 170; Muhammad Imran Baqir v. Mst. Zarnain Arzoo and others (C.P.L.A. 5009/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Imran Baqir v. Mst. Zarnain Arzoo and others (C.P.L.A. 5009/2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Expectancy of Life as Mitigating Factor
records.heading: Expectancy of life becomes relevant for commutation once the alternative sentence term is served
records.text: The Court examined whether expectancy of life is a mitigating factor for commuting death to life imprisonment under s. 302(b) PPC. It becomes relevant when the convict has served at least the term of the alternative sentence, and s. 302(b) gives the court a choice between death and life imprisonment. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 155; Tahir alias Tahiri v. The State (Crl.A. 9/2023).
records.title: Tahir alias Tahiri v. The State (Crl.A. 9/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Disposal of Death Sentence Appeals
records.heading: Appeal and leave stages in death sentence cases should each take no more than twelve months
records.text: The Court deplored the delay in deciding death sentence cases: a six year delay in the High Court and about seven years before first fixing the petition, over seventeen years in all. Appeal and leave stages should each take no more than twelve months, and all State organs have a duty to act. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 155; Tahir alias Tahiri v. The State (Crl.A. 9/2023).
records.title: Tahir alias Tahiri v. The State (Crl.A. 9/2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC Distinguished
records.heading: Section 249-A applies to Magistrates and section 265-K to the Court of Sessions
records.text: Under s. 249-A a Magistrate may acquit at any stage if the charge is groundless or conviction improbable. Under s. 265-K the Court of Sessions may acquit at any stage where material on record makes conviction impossible and further evidence cannot change the result. Ref: 2026 LHC 2103; Khalid Mehmood v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 18965/2026, decided 31.03.2026); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Khalid Mehmood v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 18965/2026, decided 31.03.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 405 PPC: Entrustment Essential for Breach of Trust
records.heading: Entrustment is the key element of criminal breach of trust under section 405 PPC
records.text: Entrustment is the key element for the definition of criminal breach of trust in s. 405 PPC, implying that the owner hands over property and continues as owner, creating a fiduciary relationship. Failure to pay profit or breach of a promise or contract lacks this element. Ref: 2026 LHC 2111; Muhammad Sarwar v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 69461-B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Sarwar v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 69461-B/2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Specific Performance: Proof Through Attesting Witnesses
records.heading: Specific performance requires proof of the agreement through attesting witnesses under Articles 17 and 79
records.text: A decree for specific performance requires the contract to be proved in accordance with Arts. 17 and 79 QSO. Documents creating financial obligations on immovable property, such as the agreement to sell and powers of attorney, need attesting witnesses, and failure to produce them is fatal where execution is disputed. The relief is also discretionary. Ref: Muhammad Humayun and others v. Taj Bibi and another (C.P.L.A. 1035 and 1104/2022, decided 03.03.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Humayun and others v. Taj Bibi and another (C.P.L.A. 1035 and 1104/2022, decided 03.03.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI CPC: Dismissal of Appeal and Default
records.heading: Mere technicalities that are not insurmountable hurdles must not defeat the ends of justice
records.text: Authority on the procedure for appeals from original decrees under s. 96 and O. XLI CPC, including dismissal under R. 11 and consequences of the appellant's default under R. 17(1). Mere technicalities that are not insurmountable hurdles must not defeat the ends of justice. Ref: Abdul Rehman and another v. Syed Jaffar Hussain Razvi (C.P.L.A. 5179/2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman and another v. Syed Jaffar Hussain Razvi (C.P.L.A. 5179/2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 47 QSO: Evidence from Earlier Proceeding
records.heading: Evidence from an earlier proceeding is admissible under Article 47 QSO only on stated conditions
records.text: Evidence recorded in an earlier proceeding is admissible under Art. 47 QSO only if the proceedings were between the same parties or their representatives, the adverse party had the right and opportunity of cross-examination, and the issues were substantially identical. Evidence from the earlier jactitation suit could not be used against a non-party. Ref: 2026 CLC 546; Razia Bibi v. A.D.J. etc (W.P. 3950/2021).
records.title: Razia Bibi v. A.D.J. etc (W.P. 3950/2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification: No Proof of Light Source
records.heading: Identification fails where witnesses admit a dark night and prove no light source
records.text: Where witnesses admit it was a dark night and fail to prove a light source at the scene, their identification of the assailants cannot be relied upon, and the prosecution case fails. Ref: 2026 MLD 420; Muhammad Zafar Iqbal v. The State (Crl.A. 671-J/2019).
records.title: Muhammad Zafar Iqbal v. The State (Crl.A. 671-J/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal Despite Plea Admitting Killing
records.heading: An accused must be acquitted if the prosecution fails, even where he took a plea
records.text: If the prosecution fails to prove its case, the accused must be acquitted even if he took a plea and thereby admitted killing the deceased. Ref: 2026 MLD 420; Muhammad Zafar Iqbal v. The State (Crl.A. 671-J/2019).
records.title: Muhammad Zafar Iqbal v. The State (Crl.A. 671-J/2019)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: S. 12 Limitation Act: Time Requisite for Copy
records.heading: Time requisite for obtaining a copy is excluded in computing the appeal period
records.text: Under s. 12(2) and (5) of the Limitation Act, the day of judgment and the time requisite for obtaining a copy, being the period between the application and the date intimated for delivery, are excluded in computing the appeal period. The provision does not say that limitation runs from the date of delivery of the order. Ref: 2026 CLC 432; Muhammad Imran v. Shahbaz Ali Khan and others (W.P. 2913/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Shahbaz Ali Khan and others (W.P. 2913/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Child Marriage Restraint Act: No FIR, S. 22-A(6) CrPC
records.heading: Offences under the Child Marriage Restraint Act are non-cognizable and no FIR may be registered
records.text: Offences under ss. 4 to 6 of the Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929 are non-cognizable, and s. 9 requires a complaint by the Union Council and trial by a Family Court. The police cannot register an FIR or investigate, and the Ex officio Justice of Peace cannot compel registration under s. 22-A(6) CrPC. Ref: 2026 MLD 525; Ghulam Abbas v. Ex officio Justice of Peace and others (W.P. 50586/2024).
records.title: Ghulam Abbas v. Ex officio Justice of Peace and others (W.P. 50586/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: A conflict between ocular and medical accounts is fatal to the prosecution
records.text: Pellets were recovered from the corpse although the allegation was of pistol injuries. The prosecution must show through expert evidence that the injuries could have been caused by the alleged weapon, and any conflict between ocular and medical accounts is fatal to the prosecution, with the benefit going to the accused. Ref: Muhammad Imran etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 1035-J/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Imran etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 1035-J/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Court Cannot Enhance Beyond Magistrate's Maximum
records.heading: A Sessions Court cannot enhance a sentence beyond the Magistrate's maximum
records.text: A Court of Sessions exercising revisional jurisdiction cannot enhance a sentence beyond the maximum that the trial Magistrate could award. Ref: Sami Ullah v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 124/2018; Crl. Misc. 1015-M/2015).
records.title: Sami Ullah v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 124/2018; Crl. Misc. 1015-M/2015)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 395 and 412 PPC: No Dual Conviction
records.heading: A person cannot be convicted of both dacoity and receiving property stolen in that dacoity
records.text: A person cannot simultaneously be convicted of dacoity under s. 395 PPC and of dishonestly receiving property stolen in the commission of a dacoity under s. 412 PPC. Ref: Sami Ullah v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 124/2018; Crl. Misc. 1015-M/2015).
records.title: Sami Ullah v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 124/2018; Crl. Misc. 1015-M/2015)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: CDR Not Conclusive; Circumstantial Evidence
records.heading: A CDR shows only use within a cell tower area
records.text: An admission of possession of a SIM does not suffice to rely on its CDR, which shows only use within the area of a cell tower and not who carried the SIM. In a wholly circumstantial case the chain must be unbroken and consistent only with guilt. Ref: Ghulam Mustafa etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 124/2020; Crl. Revision 68/2020).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 124/2020; Crl. Revision 68/2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower, Maintenance from Nikah and Dowry Claims
records.heading: A wife is entitled to full dower and maintenance from the date of Nikah
records.text: After proof of Nikah and consummation the wife is entitled to full dower stipulated in the Nikahnama. She has an unconditional right to maintenance from the date of Nikah, and the dowry claim could not be denied because the husband's family did not attend the Nikah. Ref: 2026 MLD 507; Benish Ghaffar v. ADJ etc (W.P. 1829/2024).
records.title: Benish Ghaffar v. ADJ etc (W.P. 1829/2024)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test Declined: Child Born in Wedlock
records.heading: A child born in wedlock is presumed legitimate and entitled to maintenance
records.text: A child born during a valid marriage is presumed legitimate and entitled to maintenance. An application for a DNA test to determine paternity was rightly refused, as the Supreme Court has deprecated that mode. Laches did not apply to the constitutional petition. Ref: 2026 MLD 507; Benish Ghaffar v. ADJ etc (W.P. 1829/2024).
records.title: Benish Ghaffar v. ADJ etc (W.P. 1829/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Dismissal for Non-Prosecution v. Consigned to Record
records.heading: Dismissal for non-prosecution is a judicial determination and consigning to record is administrative
records.text: Dismissal of a suit for non-prosecution under O. IX CPC is a judicial determination ending the suit for default of appearance. A direction to consign the file to record is administrative only. The lis ends unless restoration is sought and allowed in accordance with law.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 265-C CrPC: Supply of Documents to Accused
records.heading: Supply of documents to the accused under section 265-C(2)(b) is mandatory and not curable
records.text: Section 265-C(2)(b) CrPC requires copies of the complaint, documents filed with it and statements under ss. 200 and 202 to be supplied free to the accused at least seven days before trial. The provision is construed liberally for the accused, is mandatory, and non-compliance is not curable under s. 537, so trial cannot proceed. Ref: 2026 LHC 2301; Shaukat Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 65318/2025, decided 26.01.2026); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Shaukat Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 65318/2025, decided 26.01.2026)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Seized Gold: Restoration and Art. 24 Property Right
records.heading: Denial of restoration of seized gold through arbitrary valuation violates Article 24
records.text: Once the petitioner's entitlement to seized gold jewellery attained finality up to the Supreme Court, denial of restoration through arbitrary valuation deprives property contrary to Art. 24. Melting at the Mint does not extinguish his proprietary rights. Customs directed to return the refined gold bar on payment of Rs 100,000 penalty and to return USD 10,000. Ref: 2026 LHC 2292; Abbas Ali v. Collectorate of Customs etc (W.P. 57129/2022, decided 02.02.2026); Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains.
records.title: Abbas Ali v. Collectorate of Customs etc (W.P. 57129/2022, decided 02.02.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth in CNIC
records.heading: Date of birth on a CNIC may be rectified where the claim is bona fide
records.text: Where the plaintiff's passports had been renewed repeatedly without objection and the suit was not mala fide or prejudicial to anyone, she was entitled to rectification of the date of birth on her CNIC. The High Court in revision set aside the concurrent judgments and directed rectification. Ref: 2011 CLC 511.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth: Documentary Evidence
records.heading: Unrebutted documentary evidence of the correct date of birth entitles the plaintiff to a decree
records.text: Where the plaintiff produced unimpeachable documentary evidence of his correct date of birth and the defendants did not rebut it, the concurrent findings resulted from misreading and non-reading of evidence. Revision allowed and the suit decreed. Ref: 2020 YLR 2266.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth: Matriculation Certificate
records.heading: A matriculation certificate carries a strong presumption of truth in date of birth correction
records.text: Academic credentials carry a strong presumption of truth, and the burden lay on the respondents to rebut the matriculation certificate with reliable documents. Revision allowed, the concurrent judgments set aside and the suit decreed with direction to correct the CNIC. Ref: 2022 YLR 1567.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Subsequent Bail Application After Simple Withdrawal
records.heading: Simple withdrawal of an earlier bail application does not bar a subsequent application
records.text: Withdrawal simpliciter of an earlier bail application before any argument on merits does not bar a subsequent application for the same relief before the same court. As no arguments were advanced earlier and there was no decision on merits, the matter was remanded to the High Court to decide the bail application afresh. Petition converted into appeal and partly allowed. Ref: Muhammad Faisal v. The State through the Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl. P. 496/2026, decided 07.04.2026); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail; Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Faisal v. The State through the Prosecutor General Punjab and another (Crl. P. 496/2026, decided 07.04.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Attorney Transferring Principal's Property to His Sons
records.heading: An attorney cannot transfer the principal's property to his sons without her consent
records.text: An attorney cannot validly transfer the principal's property to his own sons without her express written consent. A cheque payment alone does not prove a valid sale without an agreement to sell or independent corroboration, and the transaction offends the fiduciary obligations of an attorney. Ref: Javed Iqbal and others v. Mst. Farhat Iqbal (decd.) thr. L.Rs (C.A. 852/2025, decided 06.04.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Javed Iqbal and others v. Mst. Farhat Iqbal (decd.) thr. L.Rs (C.A. 852/2025, decided 06.04.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Land After 2022 Repeal Amendment
records.heading: Evacuee land stands transferred to the Provincial Government and cannot be allotted
records.text: After the Evacuee Property and Displaced Persons Laws (Repeal) (Amendment) Act 2022, evacuee properties stand transferred to the Provincial Government for public purposes, and the Chief Settlement Commissioner, notified officer or Full Board has no power to allot or dispose of evacuee land. Ref: 2026 YLR 574; Dr Pir Bux Khan etc v. POP etc (WP 5742/2015).
records.title: Dr Pir Bux Khan etc v. POP etc (WP 5742/2015)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Courts Act 1964: Remedial Statute, Procedure
records.heading: The Family Courts Act is a remedial statute and technicalities should not defeat claims
records.text: The Family Courts Act 1964 is a remedial and beneficent statute meant for expeditious settlement of family disputes. Family Courts should interpret it to foster substantive justice and speedy relief, and not allow technicalities to defeat legitimate claims. Ref: 2026 YLR 760; Fouzia Barkat etc v. Additional District Judge etc (W.P. 16587/2021).
records.title: Fouzia Barkat etc v. Additional District Judge etc (W.P. 16587/2021)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Balance Sale Consideration Where Decree Silent on Time
records.heading: A party cannot suffer where the decree fixed no period for depositing the balance
records.text: Where the decree did not fix a period for depositing the balance sale consideration, the respondent could not suffer for the court's omission, and having deposited it after the appellate injunction was vacated, he could not be prejudiced. Ref: 2026 YLR 779; Rasheeda Bibi v. Arif Ali and others L.Rs (C.R. 665/2022).
records.title: Rasheeda Bibi v. Arif Ali and others L.Rs (C.R. 665/2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Execution of Specific Performance Decree: Art. 181
records.heading: Residuary Article 181 governs execution of a specific performance or pre-emption decree
records.text: No specific Article of the Limitation Act 1908 governs execution of a specific performance or pre-emption decree, so residuary Art. 181 applies, giving three years from when the right to apply accrues. A decree holder in possession who has paid the price need not file execution, and the right arises when the judgment debtor refuses to perform. Ref: 2026 YLR 779; Rasheeda Bibi v. Arif Ali and others L.Rs (C.R. 665/2022).
records.title: Rasheeda Bibi v. Arif Ali and others L.Rs (C.R. 665/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inquest Report: Open Mouth and Eyes of Deceased
records.heading: Open mouth and eyes noted in the inquest report cast doubt on witness presence
records.text: The inquest report noted the deceased's mouth and eyes open, whereas close relatives present would have closed them after death. This forces an adverse inference against the claim that the witnesses were present at the time and place of occurrence. Ref: 2026 YLR 712; The State v. Muhammad Abid (Murder Reference 1/2023; Crl. Appeal 34-J/2023).
records.title: The State v. Muhammad Abid (Murder Reference 1/2023; Crl. Appeal 34-J/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Identification Parade Not Always Required: CCTV Evidence
records.heading: An identification parade is not required where CCTV footage establishes identity
records.text: An identification parade is not a legal requirement in every case. Any fact establishing identity is relevant under Art. 22 QSO, and CCTV footage showing the accused is admissible under that Article and also falls under Art. 164 QSO, subject to genuineness and authenticity. A parade was unnecessary where such footage existed. Ref: 2026 YLR 564; Shahbaz Mustafa and another v. State (Crl. Misc. 15084-B/2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Mustafa and another v. State (Crl. Misc. 15084-B/2025)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Evidence: Science, Law and Case Law Survey
records.heading: DNA evidence rests on STR profiling and requires dependable legal and scientific infrastructure
records.text: Authority on DNA evidence, setting out its scientific basis, including STR profiling, and surveying the applicable law and decisions of the superior courts. It also notes the need for a dependable legal and scientific infrastructure in Pakistan. Ref: 2026 LHC 2371; Muhammad Mujahid v. The State etc (Cr. Appeal 22958/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Mujahid v. The State etc (Cr. Appeal 22958/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Adjournments Under Supreme Court Rules 2025
records.heading: An adjournment in the Supreme Court is granted only on application by the Advocate-on-Record
records.text: Under O. XX R. 2 of the Supreme Court Rules 2025 an adjournment is granted only on proper application by the Advocate-on-Record, and O. XXX Part A R. 3 provides consequences for adjournments without sufficient cause. Counsel were put on notice that compensatory costs may follow. Ref: Abbas Ali Shah v. Misha Zeb Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 245/2026, decided 02.04.2026); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Abbas Ali Shah v. Misha Zeb Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 245/2026, decided 02.04.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: S. 324 PPC: Attempt and Post-Arrest Bail
records.heading: Intention to kill was not apparent from injuries to non vital parts
records.text: Applicability of s. 324 PPC depends on the number of accused, weapons carried and opportunity to complete the offence. Intention to kill was not apparent where the accused caused only injuries to non vital parts despite the complainant lying at their mercy. Post-arrest bail accepted. Ref: 2020 YLR Note 23.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Family Pension for Divorced Daughter
records.heading: Family pension is an earned entitlement and extends to a divorced daughter
records.text: Family pension serves social welfare, and pension law is to be read broadly, as pension is an earned entitlement and not charity. The respondent company was directed to transfer the family pension to the divorced daughter and restore the commuted portion with increases since 2016. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 418.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama: Burden on Husband to Disprove Dower Entry
records.heading: Once a Nikahnama is admitted the husband must disprove its dower entries
records.text: Once execution of the Nikahnama is admitted, the husband bears the burden of disproving its dower entries, and allegations of fabrication or blank signed papers need cogent proof. Failure to seek cancellation or examine the Nikah Registrar's official gave rise to an adverse inference, and the defence was discarded. Ref: 2026 LHC 2395; Aamir Ali v. District Judge, Vehari & others (W.P. 794/2025).
records.title: Aamir Ali v. District Judge, Vehari & others (W.P. 794/2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift, Exclusion of Female Heirs, Limitation
records.heading: Exclusion of female heirs by oral gift places a heavier burden on the beneficiaries
records.text: A valid gift under Muhammadan Law needs declaration, acceptance and delivery of possession, and exclusion of female heirs places a heavier burden on the beneficiaries. The appellate court's hyper-technical approach ignored long possession and conduct since the 1960 mutations, vitiating its findings through misreading and non-reading of evidence. Ref: 2026 LHC 2402; Rahim Bakhsh v. Mst. Bakhsh Elahi (Civil Revision 811/2021).
records.title: Rahim Bakhsh v. Mst. Bakhsh Elahi (Civil Revision 811/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 161 and 162 CrPC: Police Statements
records.heading: Statements to police under section 162 CrPC are not signed and have limited use
records.text: Discusses s. 161 CrPC on oral examination of witnesses by police and s. 162, under which statements to police are not signed and may not be used at trial except as the Code provides. Ref: 2025 LHC 8551; Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 8607/B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 8607/B/2025)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Juvenile Accused: Post-Arrest Bail in Heinous Offence
records.heading: A juvenile detained for a heinous offence is entitled to post-arrest bail as of right
records.text: Citing the Supreme Court, a juvenile detained for a heinous offence is entitled to post-arrest bail as of right, whether below or above sixteen years, if the requirements of s. 6(5) are met. Ref: 2025 LHC 8551; Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 8607/B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 8607/B/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Summary Suit Against Legal Heirs
records.heading: A summary suit on cheques lies against legal heirs to the extent of the inherited estate
records.text: A summary suit under O. XXXVII CPC on cheques is maintainable against legal heirs of the deceased signatory, impleaded in their representative capacity and not as makers or indorsers. They are liable only to the extent of the estate inherited, as the civil liability survives death. Ref: 2026 LHC 2448; Sughra Bibi etc v. Tahir Hayat (RFA 63446/2020).
records.title: Sughra Bibi etc v. Tahir Hayat (RFA 63446/2020)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Withdrawal of Time-Scale Upgradation Set Aside
records.heading: The withdrawal of time-scale upgradation granted to four directors was set aside
records.text: The Court set aside the Punjab government's 2023 withdrawal of time-scale upgradation granted in 2019 to four directors of physical education, restored the benefit and barred recovery. The government's objection to jurisdiction, that the matter concerned promotion, was rejected. Ref: 2026 LHC 2346; Muhammad Sultan Shahid and 03 others v. Province of Punjab through Chief Secretary and 07 others (Writ Petition 53549/2025); Justice Raheel Kamran.
records.title: Muhammad Sultan Shahid and 03 others v. Province of Punjab through Chief Secretary and 07 others (Writ Petition 53549/2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Reinstatement Restores Seniority and Benefits
records.heading: Reinstatement restores the employee's seniority, privileges and other benefits
records.text: When a terminated or dismissed employee is reinstated, his seniority, privileges and other benefits are restored. Seniority is determined with predominance to the statutory provisions, including R. 12.2(3) of the Police Rules 1934. The Government's civil appeals were dismissed. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 401; The Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary Government of Sindh & others v. Raj Kumar Lohana & others (C.A. 53-K/2024).
records.title: The Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary Government of Sindh & others v. Raj Kumar Lohana & others (C.A. 53-K/2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody: Register No. XIX and Road Certificate
records.heading: Failure to prove Register XIX entries or a road certificate makes safe custody dubious
records.text: Neither the investigating officer nor the Moharrer proved any entry in Register No. XIX or produced a road certificate for the case property and samples. The prosecution case on safe custody became dubious, and procedure not shown to be followed is presumed not to have been followed. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 505; Sakina Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 177/2024).
records.title: Sakina Bibi v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 177/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Closing Right to Cross-Examine in Capital Case
records.heading: Closing cross-examination without appointing State counsel in a capital case was unjustified
records.text: Closing an accused's right to cross-examine prosecution witnesses on non-appearance, without appointing State counsel in a capital case, was unjustified given Art. 10 and s. 340(1) CrPC. The orders were set aside, and the trial court may appoint counsel at State expense if his counsel does not appear. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 577; Shahzad Haider v. The State (Criminal Revision 37605/2025).
records.title: Shahzad Haider v. The State (Criminal Revision 37605/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blank Recovery Memos, Inquest Report, Case Property Entry
records.heading: Blank recovery memos and missing case property entries each raise reasonable doubt
records.text: Recovery memos leaving the accused's name blank, an inquest report lacking details of the occurrence, and absence of a Malkhana entry on re-deposit of case property each raise reasonable doubt. The trial court's approach should be inquisitorial in searching for truth. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 768, PLJ 2026 CrC 22; Muhammad Imtiaz etc v. The State (Jail Appeal 24423/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Imtiaz etc v. The State (Jail Appeal 24423/2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Talaq: Effectiveness Under s. 7 MFLO
records.heading: The legal effectiveness of talaq in Pakistan is governed by section 7 MFLO
records.text: The legal effectiveness of a Talaq in Pakistan is governed by s. 7 MFLO, whatever form of pronouncement is used. Mulla's Principles of Mahomedan Law is a reference work and not a source of law. The only exception recognised in Kaneez Fatima is divorce by mutual consent (Mubara'at). The post also sets out s. 7(1) to (6) MFLO on notice to the Chairman, the 90 day period and the Arbitration Council. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 343; Jameel Ahmad v. The State and others.
records.title: Jameel Ahmad v. The State and others

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Actus Curiae Neminem Gravabit: Court Inaction
records.heading: No one is prejudiced by the court's failure to record a deposit
records.text: Where the trial court allowed an application to deposit the balance sale consideration but failed to record it in the order sheet, that inaction of the court cannot prejudice the party. Courts must not act mechanically, and no one is harmed by an act of the court. The petitioner's application for return of the deposited balance had been wrongly dismissed. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 320; Saima Batool v. ADJ etc (Misc. Writ. 57749/23).
records.title: Saima Batool v. ADJ etc (Misc. Writ. 57749/23)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Food Authority Act: Seizure and Release of Case Property
records.heading: A Food Safety Officer's seizure is challenged before the Special Court within seven days
records.text: Explains the three regulatory regimes under the Food Authority Act (Food Safety Officer, Food Authority and Special Court). A seizure under s. 13 by the FSO is challenged by application to the Special Court within seven days. The post also notes the similar provisions of the Cr.P.C. on release of case property during trial or inquiry. Ref: 2026 LHC 2581; Abdul Qadeer v. The State, etc (Writ Petition No.10163 of 2026).
records.title: Abdul Qadeer v. The State, etc (Writ Petition No.10163 of 2026)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Territorial Jurisdiction of Special Judge
records.heading: A Special Judge may take cognizance only of offences within the fixed territorial limits
records.text: Statutes are read as a harmonious whole. Under s. 4 of the Act of 1958 a Special Judge may take cognizance only of offences committed within the territorial limits fixed by the government. Section 6 applies the Code to proceedings under that Act subject to its exceptions. A court lacking territorial jurisdiction cannot ordinarily proceed with a case. Ref: 2026 LHC 2576; Abdul Basit v. Senior Special Judge, Anti-Corruption Court, Lahore, etc (Criminal Revision No. 20366 of 2026).
records.title: Abdul Basit v. Senior Special Judge, Anti-Corruption Court, Lahore, etc (Criminal Revision No. 20366 of 2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Extrajudicial Confession, Further Inquiry
records.heading: An extrajudicial confession is weak evidence and supports further inquiry for bail
records.text: An extrajudicial confession is inherently weak evidence requiring rigorous scrutiny. Where it surfaced only through a belated supplementary statement over a month after the incident in an unwitnessed murder, the case is one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Liberty cannot be curtailed as pre-trial punishment because of the gravity of the charge. Ref: 2026 LHC 2571; Muhammad Zakariya and 1 other v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 2105-B-26, decided 15.04.2026); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Zakariya and 1 other v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 2105-B-26, decided 15.04.2026)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Testimony of Rape Victim and DNA Corroboration
records.heading: A rape victim's confidence-inspiring testimony needs no corroboration and DNA supported it
records.text: A rape victim stands on a higher footing than an injured witness, and confidence-inspiring testimony needs no corroboration to sustain conviction. In a conservative society a complainant is unlikely to expose a minor daughter to a rape trial to falsely implicate someone. Positive DNA and serology reports supported the ocular account, and an unsupported defence of denial and enmity was rejected. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 266; Hassan v. State etc (Crl.A-752-18).
records.title: Hassan v. State etc (Crl.A-752-18)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses and Unproved CDR Without Voice Transcript
records.heading: Unattested CDR without a forensic voice transcript cannot prove the contents of a call
records.text: Mere production of Call Data Record without attestation by the cellular company and without a forensically tested voice transcript cannot prove the contents of a phone call. Absent independent corroboration of their presence at the place and time, the eyewitnesses were chance witnesses whose evidence is suspect. Failure to prove the place of occurrence is fatal to the prosecution. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 290; The State v. Sheikh Muhammad Awais (Murder Reference 304-22).
records.title: The State v. Sheikh Muhammad Awais (Murder Reference 304-22)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed FIR and Unnatural Conduct of Witnesses
records.heading: Unexplained delay in reporting and unnatural witness conduct make the prosecution story doubtful
records.text: An unexplained delay of about two hours and ten minutes in reporting, with the police station five kilometres away, shows deliberation and consultation and weighs against the prosecution version. The conduct of the eyewitnesses in not informing the police or Rescue 1122 was unnatural, and there was no Rescue 1122 entry. These features made the prosecution story doubtful. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 278; Allah Ditta v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1566-J of 2019); Ijaz Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.1567-J of 2019); Bashir Ahmad v. The State, etc (Crl. Revision No.469 of 2019).
records.title: Allah Ditta v. The State (Crl. Appeal No. 1566-J of 2019); Ijaz Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.1567-J of 2019); Bashir Ahmad v. The State, etc (Crl. Revision No.469 of 2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cognizance of Offences Under Chapter XVII-B PPC
records.heading: Chapter XVII-B offences restrict initiation to the specified authority under section 462-O PPC
records.text: For ordinary offences cognizance under s. 190 CrPC may follow a police report or private complaint, but offences under Chapter XVII-B PPC restrict initiation to the specified authority, as seen from s. 462-O PPC read with ss. 195 and 196 CrPC. Where the proceedings rest on a complaint by an authorised officer, the court may take cognizance without a further complaint. The impugned order was set aside. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 330; Farhan Anwar v. ASJ, Faisalabad & two others (Crl. Misc. No. 66147-M of 2020).
records.title: Farhan Anwar v. ASJ, Faisalabad & two others (Crl. Misc. No. 66147-M of 2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Synthetic Milk Transporter as Food Operator: Bail Refused
records.heading: A person transporting synthetic milk by vehicle is a food operator
records.text: A person found carrying artificial milk by vehicle or tanker is transporting it and falls within the definition of food operator. Supplying synthetic milk is a serious offence given the harm it causes to health. Bail was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 273; Muhammad Younas v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 76935-B of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Younas v. State (Crl. Misc. No. 76935-B of 2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Defamation: Exceptions to s. 499 PPC
records.heading: An imputation covered by an exception to section 499 PPC is not defamation
records.text: An imputation that prima facie falls within s. 499 PPC is not defamation if it is covered by any of the exceptions enumerated in that section. Where the accused's case squarely falls within an exception, the act complained of does not attract criminal liability. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 335; Rameeza Majid Nizami v. AD&J etc (Crl. Misc. 23159/20).
records.title: Rameeza Majid Nizami v. AD&J etc (Crl. Misc. 23159/20)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Eggshell Skull Rule and s. 322 PPC at Bail Stage
records.heading: Under the eggshell skull rule the accused is liable whatever the deceased's pre-existing condition
records.text: The eggshell skull rule applies, making the accused liable for resulting injuries and death whatever pre-existing condition the deceased had. Objections on the applicability of s. 322 PPC are premature at the bail stage and fall to the trial court at charge framing and trial. The FIR alleged a direct blow on the head causally linked to the death. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 325; Amir v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 10529-B of 2025).
records.title: Amir v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 10529-B of 2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis and Post-Mortem Phenomena in Murder Appraisal
records.heading: Rigor mortis is a medico-legal indicator of time since death in appraising murder
records.text: The court explained post-mortem changes, in particular rigor mortis, as medico-legal indicators of time since death, and treated the presence of rigor mortis and seminal discharge as recognised phenomena that were fully explained. It also noted that the accused left the witnesses present at the scene unharmed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 311; The State v. Nadeem (Murder Reference: 331-22).
records.title: The State v. Nadeem (Murder Reference: 331-22)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 12(2) CPC and Principle of Merger
records.heading: Authority on section 12(2) CPC and the principle of merger
records.text: Authority on s. 12(2) CPC and the principle of merger, including the judicial interpretation of the ratio of Sahabzadi Maharunisa v. Mst. Ghulam Sughran (PLD 2016 SC 358). The post gives no holding. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lahore 283; Mudassar Aslam & 1 Other v. Awais Hussain etc (Civil Revision 8312/26).
records.title: Mudassar Aslam & 1 Other v. Awais Hussain etc (Civil Revision 8312/26)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Grandfather's Liability for Maintenance of Minors
records.heading: A financially capable grandfather must maintain minors whose father has absented himself
records.text: Where the father is alive but has absented himself and failed to maintain his minor children, and the grandfather is financially capable, the minors cannot be left destitute and the grandfather cannot escape responsibility. Maintenance so granted is outside the bar on appeal in s. 14(2)(c) of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964. Constitutional jurisdiction is not a substitute for appeal. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lahore 294; Nazir Ahmad v. Judge Family Court, Khairpur Tamewali etc (W.P. No.1132 of 2026).
records.title: Nazir Ahmad v. Judge Family Court, Khairpur Tamewali etc (W.P. No.1132 of 2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Territorial Jurisdiction of Family Court: Wife's Residence
records.heading: A wife's residence determines the territorial jurisdiction of the Family Court
records.text: The proviso to Rule 6 of the Rules relaxes the normal territorial jurisdiction in favour of a woman suing for dissolution of marriage or recovery of dower, as the words "ordinarily resides" and "shall also have jurisdiction" show an intention to facilitate the wife. Her residence determines the territorial jurisdiction of the Family Court for matters in the Schedule to the Act. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lahore 298; Mst. Ayesha Nasir v. Aoun Abbas etc (Transfer Application No.68837 of 2025).
records.title: Mst. Ayesha Nasir v. Aoun Abbas etc (Transfer Application No.68837 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata Under s. 11 CPC
records.heading: Res judicata applies even if the relief is presented in a different form
records.text: Section 11 CPC rests on the maxims that litigation must end and that no one should be vexed twice for the same cause. Presenting the relief in a different form does not change the identity of the cause of action or the matter directly and substantially in issue. Res judicata rests on public policy and bars reopening of decided disputes. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lahore 303; Anwar-ud-Din v. Muhammad Arshad (C.R. No.5420 of 2026).
records.title: Anwar-ud-Din v. Muhammad Arshad (C.R. No.5420 of 2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summary Suit on Cheques: Compromise and Part-Payment
records.heading: Part payment under a compromise during the suit does not divest jurisdiction
records.text: A suit on cheques was competently instituted under Order XXXVII CPC. Payment of an instalment under a compromise recorded during the pendency of the suit differs from part-payment before institution, and the compromise and part-payment did not divest the trial court of jurisdiction. The suit was properly restored on default. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lahore 326; Mudassar Aleem Babar v. Rana Nisar Asim (Civil Revision 13854/26).
records.title: Mudassar Aleem Babar v. Rana Nisar Asim (Civil Revision 13854/26)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIII R. 2 CPC: Late Production of Documents
records.heading: Documents may be produced late under Order XIII Rule 2 on good cause shown
records.text: Procedural law is a handmaid of justice. Although O. XIII R. 1 CPC requires documents to be produced at the first hearing, R. 2 allows the court to receive them later on showing good cause and recording reasons. Good cause is of wide amplitude and is construed liberally, as the object is to prevent fraud and abuse and not to penalise inadvertent omissions. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lahore 330; Muhammad Arif Ch. v. Syed Ulfat Hussain Mashhadi and others (WP.8805 of 2026).
records.title: Muhammad Arif Ch. v. Syed Ulfat Hussain Mashhadi and others (WP.8805 of 2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Leave to Defend: Surety Bond Condition Set Aside
records.heading: A surety bond condition on leave to defend must consider the defence's plausibility
records.text: In a suit for recovery on a promissory note, a condition requiring a surety bond equal to the claim, imposed while granting leave to defend without regard to the circumstances of the case and plausibility of the defence, was set aside. The trial court appeared to have treated the plaintiff's no objection subject to costs as a basis for the condition. Ref: 2026 CLC 760; Allah Ditta v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 922 of 2024).
records.title: Allah Ditta v. Muhammad Ramzan (Civil Revision No. 922 of 2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Contract Service Counted for Pension
records.heading: Long continuous contractual service against a permanent post counts for pension
records.text: Long continuous contractual service was ordered to be counted for pension. Civil Service Regulations 352, 361 and 365 did not bar the claim, since a long contractual engagement against a permanent post is neither limited nor temporary. Pension is a vested right and not a bounty, and contract employment is meant for temporary or time bound work. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 253; Federation of Pakistan v. Seema Tauseef and others (C.P.L.A. No. 1380 of 2025).
records.title: Federation of Pakistan v. Seema Tauseef and others (C.P.L.A. No. 1380 of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Wedlock Policy: Posting of Spouses at Same Station
records.heading: The benefit of the wedlock policy cannot be left to arbitrary discretion
records.text: The wedlock policy, rooted in Art. 35 of the Constitution on protection of marriage and family, aims to ensure the benefit of the family, and its benefit cannot be left to the arbitrary pick and choose discretion of the competent authority. Appeal allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 226; Naheeda Aziz v. Chief Secretary (C.P.L.A. No. 1789 of 2023).
records.title: Naheeda Aziz v. Chief Secretary (C.P.L.A. No. 1789 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partial Partition Suit Not Maintainable
records.heading: A suit for partial partition is not maintainable
records.text: A suit for partial partition is not maintainable. A party seeking partition cannot select the more valuable parts of the joint holdings and exclude the rest. Each co-owner has rights over every part of the joint holding, so the whole property is pooled under the court's supervision and shares are allotted fairly by area, location and nature. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 215, 2026 SCMR 941; Shahbaz Khan v. Dowlat Khan (deceased) through LRs & others (C.P.L.A. 281-P/2012).
records.title: Shahbaz Khan v. Dowlat Khan (deceased) through LRs & others (C.P.L.A. 281-P/2012)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeals: O. XLI Rules 11, 12, 16 and 17 CPC
records.heading: Technicalities that are not insurmountable hurdles must not defeat the ends of justice
records.text: Reviews the scheme of appeals under s. 96 and Order XLI CPC, including dismissal for the appellant's non-appearance under R. 11(2) and the consequences of default under R. 17(1). Mere technicalities that do not present insurmountable hurdles must not defeat the ends of justice. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 220; Abdul Rehman and another v. Syed Jaffar Hussain Razvi (C.P.L.A. 5179/2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman and another v. Syed Jaffar Hussain Razvi (C.P.L.A. 5179/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness: No s. 161 CrPC Statement
records.heading: Prolonged silence and no section 161 statement undermined the injured witness's evidence
records.text: Injuries do not by themselves guarantee truth. The injured witness's s. 161 CrPC statement was never recorded and he first appeared before the trial judge six months after the incident. Although failure of police to examine a witness does not bar admissibility, the prolonged silence and irregular conduct, with s. 265-C CrPC disclosure in mind, undermined his evidence. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 136; Muhammad Abras v. The State (Crl. A. No. 655/2020).
records.title: Muhammad Abras v. The State (Crl. A. No. 655/2020)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Improbable Narcotics Recovery: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: A reasonable possibility of the defence version entitles the accused to benefit of doubt
records.text: The whole evidence must be reviewed, and a reasonable possibility that the defence is true entitles the accused to the benefit of doubt as of right. The occurrence place was open and visible, the accused did not flee, and no weighing scales, packets or customer were recovered or associated.
