The site plan was silent on key persons, so the easy arrest and recovery was improbable. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 125, 2026 SCMR 703; Mst. Sabran Bibi v. The State thr. Prosecutor General Punjab (Crl.P.L.A.379/2025).
records.title: Mst. Sabran Bibi v. The State thr. Prosecutor General Punjab (Crl.P.L.A.379/2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Delay in Sending Samples to PFSA
records.heading: Unexplained delay in sending samples to PFSA casts doubt on their integrity
records.text: Samples seized on 19.11.2022 were sent to PFSA on 23.11.2022 without explanation of the four day delay. As the chemical analysis report is the cornerstone of the prosecution, such delay casts doubt on the integrity of the samples, and tampering, substitution or contamination cannot be excluded. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 125, 2026 SCMR 703; Mst. Sabran Bibi v. The State thr. Prosecutor General Punjab (Crl.P.L.A.379/2025).
records.title: Mst. Sabran Bibi v. The State thr. Prosecutor General Punjab (Crl.P.L.A.379/2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: CDR Disproving Presence of Raiding Witnesses
records.heading: Call Data Records placing the raiding witnesses elsewhere raised reasonable doubt
records.text: Call Data Records produced by the accused showed that the seizing officer and the lady constable were located away from the place of recovery, and the prosecution did not effectively rebut them. Bare denial without a second SIM, swap record or explanation was insufficient. Reasonable doubt entitles the accused to acquittal as of right. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 125, 2026 SCMR 703; Mst. Sabran Bibi v. The State thr. Prosecutor General Punjab (Crl.P.L.A.379/2025).
records.title: Mst. Sabran Bibi v. The State thr. Prosecutor General Punjab (Crl.P.L.A.379/2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance on Oral Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A party seeking specific performance of an oral agreement bears the onus of proving consensus
records.text: A party seeking specific performance of an oral agreement to sell immovable property bears the onus of showing mutual agreement and consensus on its terms. The pleadings must state the date, time, place and names of witnesses, and these are essential requirements to prove an oral agreement to sell. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 210, 2026 SCMR 966; Ghulam Ali v. Ali Sher and others (C.P.L.A. 4361/2024).
records.title: Ghulam Ali v. Ali Sher and others (C.P.L.A. 4361/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Dismissal of Civil Revision for Non-Compliance of Orders
records.heading: A civil revision may be dismissed for non-compliance with court directions after repeated defaults
records.text: A civil revision filed by a party can be dismissed for non-prosecution even after admission to regular hearing. Relying on Ghulam Qadir's case, the same principle justifies dismissal for non-compliance with court directions, especially after repeated defaults, where the jurisdiction was invoked by the party and not exercised suo motu. Ref: 2026 LHC 2597; Muhammad Umar v. Hafiz Muhammad Idrees (C.R. No.517 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Umar v. Hafiz Muhammad Idrees (C.R. No.517 of 2018)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Legal Effect of Restructuring of Finance Facilities
records.heading: Restructuring of finance facilities operates as a binding acknowledgment and estoppel against the borrower
records.text: Restructuring is a fresh arrangement of an admitted liability with no new disbursement. It operates as a binding acknowledgment and estoppel against the borrower disputing the debt or its quantum, and the bank need not produce statements of account before the restructuring. A defendant must point out precise discrepancies in a certified statement of account. Ref: 2026 LHC 2620; National Bank of Pakistan v. M/s Hussain Mills Limited & others (COS No.13 of 2022).
records.title: National Bank of Pakistan v. M/s Hussain Mills Limited & others (COS No.13 of 2022)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Readiness and Willingness: Tangible Evidence Required
records.heading: Readiness and willingness must be proved by tangible evidence and not only by pleadings
records.text: A vendee seeking specific performance must prove continuous readiness and willingness by tangible evidence, such as deposit of the balance or proof of financial capacity, and not only by pleadings. The Specific Relief Act, 1877 does not require deposit at filing, but the relief is discretionary and equitable. Absence of such evidence disentitles the plaintiff. Ref: Muhammad Nadeem v. Anees Akhtar (Civil Revision No.581-D of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Nadeem v. Anees Akhtar (Civil Revision No.581-D of 2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Criminal Court Findings in Civil Proceedings: Arts 55 to 57 QSO
records.heading: Judgments on matters of a public nature are relevant but not conclusive under Article 56
records.text: Considers reliance on findings in a criminal case in a civil matter between the same parties under Arts 55 to 57 QSO. Art. 56 makes judgments on matters of a public nature relevant but not conclusive, and Art. 57 makes other judgments irrelevant unless their existence is in issue or relevant under another provision. The post also refers to compliance with O. XLI R. 31 CPC. Ref: 2026 LHC 2699; Ijaz Hamed v. Adila Ijaz etc (WP.11961-16, decided 30.04.2026); Justice Sultan Tanvir Ahmad.
records.title: Ijaz Hamed v. Adila Ijaz etc (WP.11961-16, decided 30.04.2026)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Super Tax: Vires of ss. 4B and 4C Income Tax Ordinance
records.heading: Super tax under sections 4B and 4C was upheld as permissible under Article 25
records.text: Detailed judgment on the vires of super tax under s. 4B and the tax on high earning persons under s. 4C of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, including their application to oil exploration and petroleum companies. The First Proviso was held intelligible and permissible under Art. 25, and High Court judgments declaring it discriminatory were set aside. Ref: Super tax matters (Civil Appeal No.1243 of 2020 etc, decided 30.04.2026).
records.title: Super tax matters (Civil Appeal No.1243 of 2020 etc, decided 30.04.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Stale Challenge to Mutation: Successor Bound by Predecessor
records.heading: A successor cannot claim better title than his predecessor who never challenged the mutation
records.text: A successor cannot claim better title than the predecessor. Where the predecessor never challenged a mutation sanctioned in 1929 during his lifetime, a suit filed in 2007 after about 78 years without explanation is barred by delay. Where trial and appellate courts differ, the appellate view is preferred. Ref: 2026 LHC 2519; Jan Muhammad, etc. v. Ahmad Bukhsh, etc. (Civil Revision No.697-D-2015, decided 01.04.2026).
records.title: Jan Muhammad, etc. v. Ahmad Bukhsh, etc. (Civil Revision No.697-D-2015, decided 01.04.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor as Condition of Remand
records.heading: A father's duty to maintain his minor child does not depend on litigation
records.text: A father's duty to maintain his minor child is absolute and does not depend on the pendency or outcome of litigation. Section 17-A of the Family Courts Act, 1964 does not curtail an appellate court's power to impose reasonable conditions, including continued maintenance, when ordering remand. Ref: 2026 LHC 2529; Faizan Kareem v. Addl. District Judge and 3 others (W.P. No.2021 of 2026).
records.title: Faizan Kareem v. Addl. District Judge and 3 others (W.P. No.2021 of 2026)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Who May Complain Under s. 3 IDA 2005
records.heading: Only an owner or occupier illegally dispossessed may complain under section 3 IDA 2005
records.text: The Illegal Dispossession Act, 2005 is a special law construed strictly. Only an owner or occupier as defined in s. 2(c) and 2(d) who is illegally dispossessed may complain under s. 3, and the complainant must make out a prima facie case under ss. 3 and 4. The Peshawar High Court judgment approving the trial court order was found to state the correct position. Ref: Najma Bibi v. Zakir Abbasi and another (Crl.P.L.A.768/2024, decided 08.04.2026); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Najma Bibi v. Zakir Abbasi and another (Crl.P.L.A.768/2024, decided 08.04.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence Ends on Conviction
records.heading: The presumption of innocence vanishes when a competent court finds the accused guilty
records.text: When an accused is held guilty by a competent court on evidence led at trial, the initial presumption of innocence vanishes. Ref: 2023 YLR 1649; Talib Hussain and another v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 181 of 2022).
records.title: Talib Hussain and another v. The State and another (Crl. Appeal No. 181 of 2022)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Full Board of BoR Jurisdiction and Void Allotment Orders
records.heading: A court asked to implement a void order must ignore it
records.text: Addresses the scope of jurisdiction of the Full Board of the Board of Revenue after the Evacuee Property and Displaced Persons Law (Repeal) (Amendment) Act, 2022. A court asked to implement a void order must ignore it, and allotments obtained by fraud remain open to scrutiny and judicial review. Writ jurisdiction is discretionary and aims to right a wrong. Ref: 2026 MLD 602; Muhammad Amjad Aziz & 1 other v. Full Board No. 1 BOR etc (WP. 46764/25).
records.title: Muhammad Amjad Aziz & 1 other v. Full Board No. 1 BOR etc (WP. 46764/25)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Wife's FIR Under s. 376 PPC
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail confirmed where the wife's rape FIR conflicted with medical and DNA reports
records.text: Where a wife lodged an FIR under s. 376 PPC against her husband to pressure him in a matrimonial dispute, and the ocular account conflicted with the medico-legal report and the DNA report was negative, benefit of doubt may be extended even at the pre-arrest bail stage. Pre-arrest bail confirmed. Ref: 2026 MLD 729; Awon Muhammad v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.68529/25).
records.title: Awon Muhammad v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.68529/25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Court Jurisdiction: Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance 1960
records.heading: Civil courts retain jurisdiction where deprivation of title by fraud is alleged
records.text: Section 26 of the Punjab Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance, 1960 bars civil courts only in matters arising under the Ordinance. It does not bar them where deprivation of title is alleged on the ground of fraud, which falls within the jurisdiction of the civil courts under s. 9 CPC. Ref: 2026 MLD 775; Muhammad Arshad Mehmood etc v. Muhammad Bashir etc (Civil Revision.237987/18).
records.title: Muhammad Arshad Mehmood etc v. Muhammad Bashir etc (Civil Revision.237987/18)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 415A CrPC: Appeal Despite Payment of Daman
records.heading: Payment of daman does not waive the right of appeal against conviction and sentence
records.text: Under s. 415A CrPC co-convicts in a single trial may appeal. Deposit of the amount of daman in compliance with the judgment is not a waiver or satisfaction of the conviction and does not extinguish the right of appeal against conviction and sentence. Ref: 2026 MLD 649; Mehboob v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal-660-19).
records.title: Mehboob v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal-660-19)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 174 CrPC Report and Alternate Charging Under ss. 302 and 322 PPC
records.heading: A section 174 CrPC report cannot support an FIR contrary to the complainant's narrative
records.text: On the basis of a report under s. 174 CrPC, an FIR cannot be registered under a different penal provision contrary to the complainant's narrative. The decision also deals with the role of the prosecutor and the court in alternate charging under ss. 302 and 322 PPC and with the prosecutor's powers under the CPS Act. Ref: 2026 LHC 2859; Syed Muhammad Zahid Munawar v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 531-B-26, decided 02.04.2026); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Syed Muhammad Zahid Munawar v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 531-B-26, decided 02.04.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sudden Flare Up and Free Fight: s. 302(b) PPC
records.heading: A sudden flare up and free fight lacks the specific malice required for section 302(b)
records.text: The investigating officer must examine the plea raised by the accused. The record showed an altercation with mutual resistance, injuries from different directions by different weapons and a free fight. The act was a sudden flare up lacking the specific malice required for conviction under s. 302(b) PPC. Ref: Khan Afzaal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 92 of 2022, decided 08.04.2026).
records.title: Khan Afzaal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 92 of 2022, decided 08.04.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Complainant Appointed as Investigating Officer
records.heading: A complainant can hardly investigate his own complaint with required objectivity
records.text: Appointment of a complainant as investigating officer is not technically illegal, but a complainant is inclined towards conviction and can hardly investigate his own complaint with the required objectivity. Investigation should be entrusted to an impartial official to eliminate bias and ensure due process and fair trial. Ref: Abdul Raheem, Lajbar v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. No.647/2023 & J.P. No.199/2023).
records.title: Abdul Raheem, Lajbar v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. No.647/2023 & J.P. No.199/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Dower in Joint Property Limited to Husband's Share
records.heading: A husband cannot transfer as dower more than his own share in joint property
records.text: Under Mohammadan Law dower may consist of any property, but the husband must have title to transfer it. Where property is jointly held by heirs, a person cannot transfer more than his own share, so a dower declaration operates only to the extent of the husband's or his mother's inherited share. Ref: Noman Rasheed & others v. Mst. Nighat Miandad & others (Civil Petition No. 5073 of 2025, decided 06.04.2026).
records.title: Noman Rasheed & others v. Mst. Nighat Miandad & others (Civil Petition No. 5073 of 2025, decided 06.04.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 12(2) CPC: Forum and Nature of Remedy
records.heading: A section 12(2) CPC application must be filed before the court that passed the decree
records.text: Section 12(2) CPC is an extraordinary remedy to nullify a judgment or decree obtained by fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction. The application must be filed before the court which passed the final judgment, decree or order. Ref: Noman Rasheed & others v. Mst. Nighat Miandad & others (Civil Petition No. 5073 of 2025, decided 06.04.2026).
records.title: Noman Rasheed & others v. Mst. Nighat Miandad & others (Civil Petition No. 5073 of 2025, decided 06.04.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: First Execution Petition: Art. 181 Limitation Act and s. 48 CPC
records.heading: A first execution petition must be filed within three years under Article 181
records.text: The first execution petition must be filed within three years under Art. 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908. If it was time barred, the decree holder loses the right to execute and cannot cure the defect by a second petition invoking s. 48 CPC, which only gives an outer limit once execution was properly initiated. Ref: Rasheed (deceased) through LRs and others v. Muhammad Azam Khan and others (Civil Petition No. 4530 of 2024, decided 12.03.2026).
records.title: Rasheed (deceased) through LRs and others v. Muhammad Azam Khan and others (Civil Petition No. 4530 of 2024, decided 12.03.2026)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mosque as Community Institution: Management Disputes
records.heading: Mosque management disputes should be resolved with sensitivity to the wider community
records.text: A mosque is a sacred institution open to all Muslims and is not the preserve of any particular group. Disputes about the management, use or administration of mosques should be resolved with sensitivity to the wider community, so as to maintain harmony and avoid unnecessary judicial intervention that may disturb public peace. Ref: Khawaja Farman Raza v. Province of Punjab (Civil Petition No. 2774 of 2025).
records.title: Khawaja Farman Raza v. Province of Punjab (Civil Petition No. 2774 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Natural Father's Petition Under s. 7 Guardian and Wards Act
records.heading: A person already a guardian may seek a declaration under section 7
records.text: Section 7 uses the distinct words "appoint" and "declare", so a person who is already a guardian may seek formal declaration of that status. Section 19(b) restricts the court's power at the stage of declaration or appointment but creates no express bar on a natural guardian invoking s. 7, and it cannot be stretched to create one. Ref: 2026 LHC 2900; Fareha v. Asad Bashir etc (WP. 16679/26, decided 21.04.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Fareha v. Asad Bashir etc (WP. 16679/26, decided 21.04.2026)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: PFSA DNA Report: Chain of Custody and Sample Identity
records.heading: A PFSA DNA report requires proof of sample identity and chain of custody
records.text: A PFSA report is admissible per se, but its probative value depends on proof of the identity of the sample-givers and of the custody chain. Where the person who collected the swabs was not examined and chain of custody was unproved, the possibility of substitution or manipulation remained, and with other lapses the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: Shafiq Ahmad v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 565/2023).
records.title: Shafiq Ahmad v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 565/2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Preference for Land Donors in Class-IV Appointments
records.heading: A preferential margin may lawfully be given to land donors for Class-IV posts
records.text: Where land is voluntarily alienated as a gratis grant for public welfare projects such as schools, dispensaries or tubewells, a preferential margin may lawfully be given to the donor or his nominee for a Class-IV post, provided the candidate meets all eligibility, suitability and fitness criteria at par with others. Ref: Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa v. Abdur Raqib & other (C.P.L.A. No.15-P of 2023 & C.P.L.A 132-P/2023).
records.title: Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa v. Abdur Raqib & other (C.P.L.A. No.15-P of 2023 & C.P.L.A 132-P/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Penal Provision Invoked by Police: ss. 320 and 322 PPC
records.heading: The court is not bound by the penal provision invoked by the police
records.text: The court is not bound by the penal provision invoked by the police and must tentatively examine the FIR and investigation material. The words "may arrest without warrant" in Schedule II only mean the offence is cognizable. In post-arrest bail the approach is liberal, as s. 322 PPC does not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497(1) CrPC. Ref: 2026 LHC 2918; Nadeem Abbas v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 4411/B/2026).
records.title: Nadeem Abbas v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 4411/B/2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Disability Quota Posts: Protection of Reserved Posts
records.heading: Unauthorised occupation of disability quota posts defeats the statutory mandate
records.text: Reservation of posts under the disability quota is a rights-based measure securing substantive equality. Unauthorised occupation of such posts by persons not entitled defeats the statutory mandate, and the State must ensure that the benefits reach the deserving beneficiaries transparently and lawfully. Ref: 2026 LHC 2946; Iftikhar Ahmad v. Government of the Punjab, etc (Writ Petition No.8293 of 2025).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmad v. Government of the Punjab, etc (Writ Petition No.8293 of 2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Arts 175F and 185: Supreme Court and Federal Constitutional Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Writ proceedings lie in the Federal Constitutional Court and regular proceedings in the Supreme Court
records.text: Under Art. 185 the Supreme Court hears regular proceedings, while all writ proceedings except rent and family matters lie within the Federal Constitutional Court under Art. 175F. Writ and regular proceedings clubbed together must be de-clubbed and routed to the respective court. Art. 189(1) is not read to subordinate one apex court to the other. Ref: Civil Petition Nos. 1011, 1040 and 1964 of 2020.
records.title: Civil Petition Nos. 1011, 1040 and 1964 of 2020

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 46(5) QSO: Statement Made After Dispute Arose
records.heading: Article 46(5) QSO is not attracted to a statement made after the dispute arose
records.text: Art. 46(5) QSO is not attracted under the principle ante litem motam where the statement was made after the dispute arose, so the statement of the deceased carried no admissibility or weight. The post also considers Art. 64 QSO. Ref: 2026 LHC 2963; Kafia Bibi etc v. Alam Ali etc (Civil Revision.4025-10, decided 20.04.2026); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Kafia Bibi etc v. Alam Ali etc (Civil Revision.4025-10, decided 20.04.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Forty Year Delay in Inheritance Claim
records.heading: Petitioners must justify about forty years of silence in an inheritance claim with cogent evidence
records.text: Courts apply limitation liberally in inheritance matters, but petitioners must bring cogent evidence to justify silence for about forty years, particularly where they did not claim their share after their mother's death. They failed to do so, and the cases cited were distinguishable on facts. Ref: 2026 LHC 2963; Kafia Bibi etc v. Alam Ali etc (Civil Revision.4025-10, decided 20.04.2026); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: Kafia Bibi etc v. Alam Ali etc (Civil Revision.4025-10, decided 20.04.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Bona Fide Purchaser: s. 27(b) Specific Relief Act
records.heading: Subsequent transferees bear a heavy burden to prove bona fide purchase without notice
records.text: Subsequent transferees bear a heavy burden to prove they are bona fide purchasers for value without notice under s. 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. The plea needs cogent evidence and proof of due inquiry into title. Where haste, lack of inquiry or notice appears, the protection fails and the prior agreement remains enforceable against them. Ref: Mian Mohammad Mehmood Ahmed (deceased) v. Safdar Hussain (Civil Appeal No. 168-L/14 etc, decided 04.05.2026).
records.title: Mian Mohammad Mehmood Ahmed (deceased) v. Safdar Hussain (Civil Appeal No. 168-L/14 etc, decided 04.05.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Essentials of Art. 40 QSO: Discovery Evidence
records.heading: Article 40 QSO requires lawful custody, specific information and discovery of a previously unknown fact
records.text: Art. 40 QSO applies only where the accused is in lawful police custody in that case, gives specific information, and a previously unknown material fact is discovered as a direct consequence. Only the part of the statement distinctly related to the discovery is admissible. Art. 40 must not circumvent Arts. 38 and 39 QSO and s. 162 CrPC, and the recovery must be independently assessed for reliability and corroboration. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 222, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 36; Zunair Younas v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.532/2018).
records.title: Zunair Younas v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.532/2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal of Suits
records.heading: A plaintiff abandoning a suit without permission cannot bring a fresh suit
records.text: Larger bench decision. A plaintiff may abandon a suit or part of a claim without permission but cannot then bring a fresh suit on the same cause of action. Under sub-rule (2) the court may permit withdrawal with liberty to sue afresh. The post also states that amendments altering the character of a claim are not permitted. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 177, PLJ 2026 SC 313; Mst. Sakina Bi, etc v. Barkat Hussain, etc (Civil Appeal No.3347 of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Sakina Bi, etc v. Barkat Hussain, etc (Civil Appeal No.3347 of 2022)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Death of Convict: Appeal Survives on Restoration of Possession
records.heading: An appeal abates only as to sentence and survives as to the restoration order
records.text: Section 431 CrPC does not deal with a convict who is also subject to an order restoring possession. Under s. 8-A read with s. 8(1) of the 2005 Act, the appeal abates only as to the sentence and survives as to the restoration order. The matter was remanded to the High Court to decide restoration after hearing the legal heirs. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 211; Muhammad Khurshid Khan v. Dost Muhammad Khan (deceased) through L.Rs and others (Crl.P.L.A.562/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Khurshid Khan v. Dost Muhammad Khan (deceased) through L.Rs and others (Crl.P.L.A.562/2022)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Non-Production of Daily Diary: Adverse Inference
records.heading: Unjustified non-production of the daily diary warrants an adverse inference against the prosecution
records.text: Rules 22.48 and 22.49 of the Police Rules, 1934 require departure of police officials to be recorded in the Roznamcha. Unjustified non-production of the daily diary warrants adverse inference that the raiding party did not go to the place alleged. Together with doubt on safe transmission of samples to the laboratory, the accused was entitled to benefit of doubt and acquittal. Ref: Wajhat Bibi v. The State thr. Special Prosecutor ANF (Crl.P.L.A.2073/2025, decided 13.05.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Wajhat Bibi v. The State thr. Special Prosecutor ANF (Crl.P.L.A.2073/2025, decided 13.05.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Circumstantial Evidence: Unbroken Chain
records.heading: Conviction may rest on circumstantial evidence forming a complete unbroken chain
records.text: Conviction may rest on circumstantial evidence if each circumstance is independently proved and together they form a complete unbroken chain excluding any hypothesis of innocence. A missing link benefits the accused, but a coherent and confidence-inspiring chain is as potent as direct evidence. The courts below rightly found guilt and no interference was called for. Ref: Aftab Zafar v. The State (J.P.136/2025, decided 13.05.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Aftab Zafar v. The State (J.P.136/2025, decided 13.05.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: PFSA Report: Protocols Requirement Directory
records.heading: The requirement to mention full protocols in a PFSA report is directory
records.text: Larger bench. The requirement to mention full protocols under unamended rule 6 is directory, and non-compliance does not invalidate the report or its evidentiary value under s. 36(2) of the Act. Naming the internationally recognised tests in the Explanation to amended rule 6 is sufficient compliance. The judgment has no retrospective effect. Ref: Baz Khan v. The State (Crl.A.43/2020, decided 13.05.2026); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Baz Khan v. The State (Crl.A.43/2020, decided 13.05.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeal Where Decree Sheet Prepared During Pendency
records.heading: Delay by the court in preparing the decree sheet should not prejudice the appellant
records.text: The judgment deals with maintainability of an appeal in a partition suit where the decree sheet was drawn only during pendency of the appeal, after delay in its preparation, and applies the principle that an act of the court should prejudice no man. The civil revision was dismissed with no order as to costs. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 404, PLJ 2025 Lahore 987; Syed Imtiaz Hussain v. Muhammad Hussain and 35 others (Civil Revision No. 830-D of 2016).
records.title: Syed Imtiaz Hussain v. Muhammad Hussain and 35 others (Civil Revision No. 830-D of 2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Single Circumstance Sufficient
records.heading: A single circumstance creating doubt in the prosecution case is sufficient to acquit
records.text: A single circumstance creating doubt in the prosecution case is sufficient to acquit the accused. The post is a compilation of Supreme Court authorities for this proposition. Ref: 2026 SCMR 798, 2026 SCMR 783, 2026 SCMR 686, 2026 SCMR 674 and others.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence and Recovery Under Art. 40 QSO
records.heading: Last seen evidence alone is insufficient unless the accused gives no reasonable explanation
records.text: Last seen evidence alone is insufficient, but it can be relied upon where the facts allow no reasonable inference except guilt and the accused gives no reasonable explanation. Under Art. 40 QSO a recovery must follow a statement made in police custody and lead to discovery of a fact unknown to the police. Circumstantial evidence must be incompatible with innocence. Ref: 2026 YLR 1044; Sumaira Bibi v. The State, etc (Cr. Appeal No.38037 of 2022).
records.title: Sumaira Bibi v. The State, etc (Cr. Appeal No.38037 of 2022)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Burial of Non-Residents in Public Graveyard
records.heading: Barring non-residents from burial in a public graveyard infringes the right to dignified burial
records.text: Barring non-residents from burying their dead in a public graveyard, which is waqf property, is contrary to the injunctions of Islam and infringes the right to a dignified burial. Graveyard land attains a sacred character and its sale or discriminatory restriction is illegal. Petition allowed and the Deputy Commissioner directed to recover encroached graveyard land. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 382; Moman Khan v. The Province of Punjab (Writ Petition No. 5476 of 2025).
records.title: Moman Khan v. The Province of Punjab (Writ Petition No. 5476 of 2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Media Interviews and Confessions of Accused in Custody
records.heading: Law enforcement agencies must not permit media interviews or confessions of accused in custody
records.text: Law enforcement agencies must not permit or facilitate media interviews, especially confessional statements, of accused in custody, as this violates dignity and fair trial. Violation is misconduct and heads of agencies are responsible for compliance. Press freedom under Art. 19 does not extend to false, misleading or defamatory reporting that compromises fair trial or dignity. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 395; Vishal Ahmad Shakir v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 80758 of 2023).
records.title: Vishal Ahmad Shakir v. Federation of Pakistan and others (Writ Petition No. 80758 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Exhumation of Grave Under s. 176(2) CrPC
records.heading: Exhumation under section 176(2) CrPC is permitted only to determine the cause of death
records.text: Section 176(2) CrPC allows a Magistrate to order exhumation only to determine the cause of death in a case of suspected unnatural death. No provision permits exhumation to relieve emotional hardship or access difficulties. As no suspicion was alleged, the Magistrate lacked jurisdiction to allow disinterment. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 436; Mst. Shehnaz Bibi v. Magistrate 1st Class, Sahiwal, and others (Writ Petition No. 3893 of 2022).
records.title: Mst. Shehnaz Bibi v. Magistrate 1st Class, Sahiwal, and others (Writ Petition No. 3893 of 2022)

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.topic: Trial Court Cannot Block CNIC or Passport
records.heading: A trial court has no authority to block a CNIC or passport
records.text: Section 18 NADRA Ordinance, 2000 specifies the grounds for cancelling, impounding or confiscating a CNIC, and the word blocking is not used. The Passports Act, 1974 likewise provides for cancelling, impounding or confiscation only under s. 8. The trial court had no authority to order blocking of the CNIC or passport, so its order lacked jurisdiction. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 388; Abdul Rehman v. The State and five others (Criminal Revision No.205 of 2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. The State and five others (Criminal Revision No.205 of 2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Identification: Distance and Lighting
records.heading: Distance and lighting are the primary pillars for weighing eyewitness identification
records.text: Distance and lighting are the primary pillars for weighing eyewitness identification, as reliability falls with distance and poor light. Given the considerable distance and the improbability of attributing the fatal shot amid indiscriminate firing by several accused, the petitioner-convict was given the benefit of doubt. Ref: Shahbaz @ Gillo v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.750-L/2018, decided 14.05.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Shahbaz @ Gillo v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.750-L/2018, decided 14.05.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medical Evidence Contradicting Ocular Account
records.heading: Uniform wound characteristics indicating a single weapon contradict a joint attack by three accused
records.text: Uniform wound characteristics indicated fire from a single weapon by a single person, contradicting the ocular version of a joint attack by three accused and supporting the cross-version. This conflict created reasonable doubt on the petitioner's participation, and the presumption of innocence requires the benefit of doubt. Ref: Saddam Hussain v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1132-L/2018, decided 27.04.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Saddam Hussain v. The State (Crl.P.L.A.1132-L/2018, decided 27.04.2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Cannot Deny Landlord's Title: Art. 115 QSO
records.heading: A tenant is estopped under Article 115 QSO from disputing the landlord's title
records.text: A person who entered possession as tenant is estopped under Art. 115 QSO from disputing the landlord's title while he retains possession under the tenancy. Until he establishes his proprietary claim before a competent forum, tenancy law governs. An assertion of ownership by purchase of a share does not make ejectment proceedings incompetent, as the Rent Controller has limited jurisdiction. Ref: 2026 SCMR 717.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: s. 337-D PPC: Injury to Body Cavity of Trunk
records.heading: Section 337-D PPC applies only to an injury extending into a trunk cavity
records.text: The ingredients of s. 337-D PPC are attracted only where the injury extends to a body cavity in the trunk. A single injury on the back of the neck is not part of the trunk, so the conviction and sentence under s. 337-D PPC were not sustainable. Ref: 2026 SCMR 715; Stana Dar v. Muhammad Ayeen and another (Crl.P.L.A.71-P/2025).
records.title: Stana Dar v. Muhammad Ayeen and another (Crl.P.L.A.71-P/2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Dismissal of Police Officials for Custodial Torture Despite Acquittal
records.heading: Police officials dismissed for custodial torture cannot rely on their criminal acquittal
records.text: The State must protect the right to life and prevent custodial violence, and illegal detention and torture are never justified. Police officials dismissed for torturing an accused in custody to death could not rely on their criminal acquittal to defeat the misconduct finding. Leave was refused and the petitions were dismissed. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 205; Khalid Mehmood and 2 others v. The District Police Officer, D.G.Khan and others (Civil Petitions Nos. 1041, 1042 and 1327 of 2024).
records.title: Khalid Mehmood and 2 others v. The District Police Officer, D.G.Khan and others (Civil Petitions Nos. 1041, 1042 and 1327 of 2024)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Seven Month Delay in Reporting and Unwitnessed Recovery
records.heading: A seven month delay in reporting and an unwitnessed recovery weigh against the prosecution
records.text: The complainant's silence for seven months, despite family members being at home, weighed heavily against her account of forcible rape. The pistol recovery from a residential house without associating witnesses of the locality violated s. 103 CrPC, so the recovery could not be relied upon. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 187; Hassan Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 90-L of 2019); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan; Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi; Justice Salahuddin Panhwar (dissenting).
records.title: Hassan Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 90-L of 2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Summoning Accused Placed in Column 2 of Challan
records.heading: Accused placed in Column 2 of the challan may be summoned under section 204 CrPC
records.text: Where accused named in the FIR and in s. 161 CrPC statements were placed in Column 2 of the s. 173 report, the investigating officers' opinion of non-involvement is irrelevant to an application to summon them. The question is decided within the parameters of s. 204 CrPC on the evidentiary material available. Ref: 2026 MLD 739; Ghulam Hassan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 143 of 2025).
records.title: Ghulam Hassan v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 143 of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Back Benefits on Reinstatement: Constructive Continuity
records.heading: Back benefits on reinstatement are confined to arrears of pay and emoluments wrongly denied
records.text: Back benefits on reinstatement of a civil servant are confined to arrears of pay and emoluments denied through wrongful dismissal or removal. The intervening period may be regularised by leave without pay or leave of the kind due. The Court formally articulated the doctrines of Constructive Continuity and Vanishing Dismissal for reinstatement cases. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 510, PLD 2026 SC 145.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Courts Act: Special Law Prevails
records.heading: The Family Courts Act 1964 is a special law and prevails over general law
records.text: The Family Courts Act, 1964 is a special law for expeditious disposal of family disputes and prevails over general law in case of conflict. A petition sought to stay family court proceedings on dower and maintenance, then at trial stage, pending a civil declaratory suit. A suit for cancellation of Nikahnama has no effect on maintenance of a wife whom the husband admits in his written statement to be legally wedded. Ref: 2026 CLC 740; Hurair Asif v. Senior Civil Judge/Judge Family Court (Writ Petition No. 3657 of 2025).
records.title: Hurair Asif v. Senior Civil Judge/Judge Family Court (Writ Petition No. 3657 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXVI R. 9 CPC: Local Commission for Demarcation
records.heading: Order XXVI Rule 9 CPC allows a Local Commission to demarcate disputed property
records.text: O. XXVI R. 9 CPC empowers the court to appoint a Local Commission to investigate and clarify the matter before it. Ordering demarcation of the disputed property does not amount to creating evidence for a party, since it only verifies the position on the ground. The orders of the courts below were held to be in accordance with law. Ref: 2026 CLC 782; Mst. Hafeezan Bibi and others v. Nazar Muhammad and others (Writ Petition No. 12400 of 2012).
records.title: Mst. Hafeezan Bibi and others v. Nazar Muhammad and others (Writ Petition No. 12400 of 2012)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record: Evidentiary Value
records.heading: A CDR showing only contact does not establish the accused's location at the scene
records.text: A CDR showing only contact between the appellant and the deceased does not establish the appellant's location at the time and place of occurrence. A standard computerised CDR without the signature of the concerned telecom officer could not be considered or relied upon for conviction. Ref: 2026 YLR 1002; Muhammad Hussain v. The State (Murder Reference No. 267 of 2022; Criminal Appeal No. 63866 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Hussain v. The State (Murder Reference No. 267 of 2022; Criminal Appeal No. 63866 of 2022)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Revenue Entries, Title and Art. 199 Jurisdiction
records.heading: Revenue entries confer no title and Article 199 jurisdiction is unsuited to disputed title
records.text: Revenue entries do not confer title and carry only a rebuttable presumption of correctness. Where the validity of old unimplemented mutations is disputed, the matter involves questions of fact and title that revenue authorities cannot decide. Art. 199 jurisdiction is unsuited to controversies needing evidence. The petition was dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 97; Faiz Ullah Khan v. Member Board of Revenue Punjab, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 137 of 2025).
records.title: Faiz Ullah Khan v. Member Board of Revenue Punjab, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 137 of 2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Admitted Execution: Art. 79 QSO Not Mandatory
records.heading: Admitted execution of a document dispenses with attesting witnesses under Article 79 QSO
records.text: Under Art. 113 QSO, admitted facts need no formal proof. Where execution of a document is admitted, production of attesting witnesses under Art. 79 QSO is no longer mandatory, and applying Art. 79 despite a categorical admission was a misdirection in law. Ref: 2026 LHC 3037; Muhammad Imran Arif and others v. Ch. Muhammad Ashraf (Civil Revision No. 56442 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Imran Arif and others v. Ch. Muhammad Ashraf (Civil Revision No. 56442 of 2021)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Partial Specific Performance and Time Not Essence
records.heading: Partial specific performance is permissible and time is ordinarily not of the essence
records.text: Courts retain jurisdiction under s. 22 of the Specific Relief Act to mould relief and may enforce an agreement to the permissible extent where different parties hold distinct interests in the property. In agreements to sell immovable property, time is ordinarily not of the essence unless expressly made so. Ref: 2026 LHC 3037; Muhammad Imran Arif and others v. Ch. Muhammad Ashraf (Civil Revision No. 56442 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Imran Arif and others v. Ch. Muhammad Ashraf (Civil Revision No. 56442 of 2021)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Cancellation, Refund and Readiness
records.heading: Specific performance is discretionary and needs proof of continuous readiness and willingness
records.text: A plea unsupported by pleadings and proof cannot be accepted, and evidence beyond pleadings is impermissible. Where the predecessor requested cancellation and encashed refund of earnest money, he could not later challenge cancellation for want of notice. Specific performance is discretionary, and the plaintiff must show continuous readiness and willingness to perform. Ref: 2026 LHC 3012; Malik Mazhar Hussain v. Muhammad Ijaz and another (C.R. No. 72596 of 2024).
records.title: Malik Mazhar Hussain v. Muhammad Ijaz and another (C.R. No. 72596 of 2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Life Imprisonment as 25 Years: Expectancy of Life
records.heading: Life imprisonment is deemed twenty-five years for calculating fractions of punishment
records.text: Under s. 57 PPC and Rule 140 of the Prison Rules, 1978, life imprisonment is deemed to be twenty-five years for calculating fractions of punishment. The principle of expectancy of life cannot be invoked on periods below 25 years or by counting remissions, as death row convicts are not lifers and are not ordinarily entitled to remissions. Ref: Sher Afzal and another v. The State through PG Punjab and another (Crl.M.A. 1292/2025, decided 26.02.2026); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Sher Afzal and another v. The State through PG Punjab and another (Crl.M.A. 1292/2025, decided 26.02.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 189: Binding Force of Supreme Court Precedent
records.heading: Only law consciously declared on a question genuinely decided binds under Article 189
records.text: Art. 189 requires courts to follow the law established by the Supreme Court, but only the law consciously declared on a question genuinely decided through legal reasoning is binding. Mere citation of earlier authorities without engagement with their ratio, or a fleeting conclusion without reasoning, does not meet this standard. Ref: Qaiser Abbas; Muhammad Siddique v. The State (Jail Petition No. 390/2018 and Criminal Petition No. 593-L/2018, decided 13.05.2026).
records.title: Qaiser Abbas; Muhammad Siddique v. The State (Jail Petition No. 390/2018 and Criminal Petition No. 593-L/2018, decided 13.05.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sentencing in Multiple Murders
records.heading: Sentencing must not let an offender kill two or three and pay for one
records.text: The Court observed that a sentencing structure under which an offender may kill two or three and pay for one diminishes the distinct value of each human life and undermines public confidence in the administration of justice, and cannot be permitted. Ref: Qaiser Abbas; Muhammad Siddique v. The State (Jail Petition No. 390/2018 and Criminal Petition No. 593-L/2018, decided 13.05.2026).
records.title: Qaiser Abbas; Muhammad Siddique v. The State (Jail Petition No. 390/2018 and Criminal Petition No. 593-L/2018, decided 13.05.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Unproved Panchayat Nama and Evidence Beyond Pleadings
records.heading: Evidence beyond pleadings carries no weight and an unproved Panchayat Nama has no worth
records.text: A new case requiring factual inquiry cannot be set up for the first time before the Supreme Court, and evidence beyond pleadings carries no weight. Oral assertion cannot rebut documentary evidence. A Panchayat Nama not proved through attesting witnesses has no evidentiary worth, and the scribe's testimony cannot cure that defect. Ref: Anwar Ali Shah and others v. Sadiq Ali Shah and others (C.A. No. 1410 of 2019, decided 01.04.2026).
records.title: Anwar Ali Shah and others v. Sadiq Ali Shah and others (C.A. No. 1410 of 2019, decided 01.04.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Delay in Challenging Mutation: s. 3 Limitation Act
records.heading: A time-barred suit must be dismissed even if limitation is not pleaded
records.text: Under s. 3 of the Limitation Act, 1908 a suit filed after the prescribed period must be dismissed even if limitation is not pleaded. A suit filed in 2005 against transactions of 1978, 1989 and 1991 was untenable, as unexplained delay in challenging a mutation defeats the claim. Registration is notice to the public, and long-standing revenue entries should not be lightly unsettled. Ref: Fazeelat Nasreen and another v. Maqsood Begum and others (C.R.P. No. 410/2023 in C.A. No. 310 of 2021).
records.title: Fazeelat Nasreen and another v. Maqsood Begum and others (C.R.P. No. 410/2023 in C.A. No. 310 of 2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Guidelines for Trial Courts on Pleadings
records.heading: The Court laid down guidelines for trial courts on receiving pleadings
records.text: In view of persistent non-compliance of pleadings with the mandatory requirements of the CPC, the Court laid down guiding principles for trial courts on receipt of pleadings, together with administrative measures to maintain procedural discipline, uniformity and quality of pleadings. Ref: Fazeelat Nasreen and another v. Maqsood Begum and others (C.R.P. No. 410/2023 in C.A. No. 310 of 2021).
records.title: Fazeelat Nasreen and another v. Maqsood Begum and others (C.R.P. No. 410/2023 in C.A. No. 310 of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Presumption of Regularity: Official Witnesses
records.heading: Official witnesses attract a rebuttable presumption of regularity unless the record shows mala fides
records.text: Testimony of official witnesses attracts the presumption of regularity in official acts. The presumption is rebuttable and holds only while the record is not tainted by mala fides, procedural dishonesty or departure from the path of justice. Ref: Muhammad Shafi v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 847/2023, decided 04.05.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Shafi v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 847/2023, decided 04.05.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: Executing Court Cannot Reopen Title
records.heading: An executing court cannot reopen title or sit in appeal over the decree
records.text: Judgment debtors who led no evidence before the Executing Court cannot set up a new case at the execution stage. The Executing Court exceeded its limits by summoning revenue record and inquiring afresh into title, effectively sitting in appeal over the decree. Matters that attained finality cannot be reopened in execution. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 638; Abdul Ghani v. Mst. Alam Bibi (CPLA No. 2313 of 2024).
records.title: Abdul Ghani v. Mst. Alam Bibi (CPLA No. 2313 of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Night Occurrence Without Light Source; Improvements
records.heading: Doubtful identification at night without a mentioned light source, with improvements, justifies acquittal
records.text: Where a night occurrence was not supported by any mention of a source of light in the FIR, site plan or eye-witness evidence, identification of the accused was doubtful. The FIR mentioned one injury while the medical evidence showed two, a conflict with the ocular account indicating improvements. Benefit of doubt was given and the appellant acquitted. Ref: 2026 SCMR 729; Amjad Ali v. The State (Jail Petition No. 704 of 2017).
records.title: Amjad Ali v. The State (Jail Petition No. 704 of 2017)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Attempt to Suicide: s. 325 PPC Restored
records.heading: The Federal Shariat Court restored section 325 PPC on attempted suicide
records.text: The Federal Shariat Court held that decriminalising attempt to commit suicide through omission of s. 325 PPC by the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Act, 2022 (Act XXXVII of 2022) is against the Holy Quran and Sunnah. The Shariat Petitions were accepted, the Act declared without legal effect, and s. 325 PPC restored. Ref: Hammad Saeed Dar v. Federation of Pakistan (Shariat Petition No. 03/I/2023 and Shariat Petition No. 01/I/2025).
records.title: Hammad Saeed Dar v. Federation of Pakistan (Shariat Petition No. 03/I/2023 and Shariat Petition No. 01/I/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related Witnesses, Motive and s. 302(b) Sentencing
records.heading: Relationship alone does not make witnesses suspect when corroborated by medical evidence
records.text: Relationship of witnesses with the deceased does not make their testimony suspect, and confidence-inspiring related witnesses corroborated by medical and forensic evidence can support conviction. Failure to prove motive loses significance where ocular evidence is reliable. Sentencing under s. 302(b) PPC is a judicial discretion exercised on the facts of each case. Forensic report linked the crime empties to the pistol recovered on disclosure. Ref: Khuda Bakhsh v. The State (Sessions J.P. 178/2025, decided 13.05.2026); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Khuda Bakhsh v. The State (Sessions J.P. 178/2025, decided 13.05.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report and Fresh s. 173 Report
records.heading: A Magistrate may disagree with a cancellation report and summon the accused
records.text: Where investigation is transferred to another officer after a cancellation report and he finds sufficient material, the SHO must prepare and submit the s. 173 report with the entire record. The Magistrate is competent to disagree with a cancellation report and summon the accused. The High Court set aside the lower appellate court's judgment and restored the Magistrate's order. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 858; Muhammad Asif v. Farmaish Ali etc (WP 31717/24).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Farmaish Ali etc (WP 31717/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cancellation Report Endorsed: No Further Investigation
records.heading: After a cancellation report is endorsed by the Magistrate, no further investigation can proceed
records.text: Once a cancellation report is prepared and endorsed by the Magistrate, the matter stands extinguished and no further investigation or transfer of investigation can proceed unless the Magistrate's order is set aside. As no criminal case existed, the pre-arrest bail petition was not maintainable and was withdrawn and disposed of. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 811; Muhammad Sarfraz v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 764-B of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Sarfraz v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 764-B of 2025)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Report: Safe Transmission of Sealed Parcels
records.heading: A DNA report fails without proof of safe transmission of sealed sample parcels
records.text: In a case resting on circumstantial evidence, the prosecution must prove a complete and unbroken chain of circumstances. A DNA report cannot be relied upon where safe transmission of sealed sample parcels to the Forensic Science Agency is not proved. Accused acquitted. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 875; Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 175-21).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 175-21)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Refusal to Sign Charge Sheet: s. 180 PPC Procedure
records.heading: Conviction under section 180 PPC without the prescribed CrPC procedure is a nullity
records.text: A court may impose only a fine of Rs.200 for such disobedience following s. 481 CrPC, and for a severer sentence must send the complaint to a Magistrate under s. 482 CrPC. Direct conviction and 15 days' imprisonment without that procedure was a nullity. Appeal lies under s. 486 CrPC despite the petty offence bar. Conviction set aside. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 957, PLJ 2024 CrC 813; Kashif Nawaz and others v. The State and others (Crl. Appeal 531-23).
records.title: Kashif Nawaz and others v. The State and others (Crl. Appeal 531-23)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Experience Criteria: Contract or Daily Wage Experience
records.heading: Excluding contract or daily wage experience without legal basis infringes the right to public employment
records.text: Where an advertisement requires five years' experience, including from private entities, insistence that it be regular rather than contract or daily wage experience is untenable when neither law nor the advertisement imposes such a bar. Exclusion without clear legal foundation infringes the right to seek public employment. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 590; Muhammad Amir Shabbir v. Govt. of Punjab etc (Writ Petition-9729-19).
records.title: Muhammad Amir Shabbir v. Govt. of Punjab etc (Writ Petition-9729-19)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Right of Appeal: Implementing Orders Before Limitation
records.heading: Implementing adverse orders before limitation expires defeats the right of appeal
records.text: The right of appeal is a substantive and valuable right. Administrative action defeating it, particularly by implementing adverse orders before expiry of the limitation period, cannot be sustained and is incompatible with natural justice and administrative propriety. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 590; Muhammad Amir Shabbir v. Govt. of Punjab etc (Writ Petition-9729-19).
records.title: Muhammad Amir Shabbir v. Govt. of Punjab etc (Writ Petition-9729-19)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Extrajudicial Confession: Weak Evidence in Capital Cases
records.heading: An extrajudicial confession is weak evidence and needs strong corroboration in capital cases
records.text: An extrajudicial confession is weak evidence and has never been sufficient for conviction on a capital charge unless strongly corroborated by tangible evidence from an unimpeachable source. The confession contradicted the circumstantial evidence on material facts, so reliance on it was unsafe. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 824; Muhammad Dilawar and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 77117 of 2021; Murder Reference No. 223 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Dilawar and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 77117 of 2021; Murder Reference No. 223 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Precautions for Recording Confession
records.heading: The Court listed precautions a Magistrate must observe when recording a confession
records.text: The Court listed precautions for recording a confession, including removal of police staff from the courtroom, ensuring the accused understands he is before a Judicial Magistrate, time for reflection between warnings, assurance against return to police custody, recording answers in his own words, and recording by the Magistrate himself. The statement must not contradict the prosecution case on material particulars. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 824; Muhammad Dilawar and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 77117 of 2021; Murder Reference No. 223 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Dilawar and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 77117 of 2021; Murder Reference No. 223 of 2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Rule 14-F HCR&O: Exhibiting Recovered Articles
records.heading: Recovered articles not exhibited under Rule 14-F cannot be read in evidence
records.text: Rule 14-F, Part-B, Chapter 24, Vol. III of the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders requires physical evidence to be produced, connected with the case and identified through witnesses. The trial court did not exhibit the recovered articles separately or record their numbers, so they could not be read in evidence and the conviction could not be upheld. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 904; Sheraz and others v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 77776 of 2021).
records.title: Sheraz and others v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 77776 of 2021)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Punjab Food Authority Act: ss. 22A and 13(2)
records.heading: The Punjab Food Authority Act offence needs scheduled quantities and a seizure statement
records.text: Under s. 22A of the Punjab Food Authority Act, 2011 the offence applies only when adulterated food meets or exceeds the scheduled quantities. Under s. 13(2) the Food Safety Officer must prepare and give the accused a seizure statement. Its non-production supported an adverse inference under Art. 129, Illustration (g) QSO. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 904; Sheraz and others v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 77776 of 2021).
records.title: Sheraz and others v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 77776 of 2021)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics: Safe Custody and Chain of Custody
records.heading: Narcotics conviction requires proof of recovery and an unbroken chain of safe custody
records.text: In a conviction under the Control of Narcotic Substances Act 1997 the prosecution must prove beyond reasonable doubt that the recovered material is a narcotic drug. The analyst's report depends on proof of recovery and of an unbroken chain of safe custody from recovery until receipt of the samples at the government analyst's office. Ref: 2026 SCMR 870, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 89; Ameenullah and Khairullah v. The State & another (Crl.A. 525/2022).
records.title: Ameenullah and Khairullah v. The State & another (Crl.A. 525/2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 49 QSO: Presumption of Revenue Record Entries
records.heading: Long standing revenue entries carry a presumption of truth under Article 49 QSO
records.text: Under Art. 49 QSO, long standing entries in the revenue record, especially the register of record of rights, carry a presumption of truth and cannot be controverted by mere oral evidence unless proved otherwise by sufficient and convincing evidence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 855; Mst. Addan v. Province of Sindh (Civil Appeals Nos. 13-K and 14-K of 2020).
records.title: Mst. Addan v. Province of Sindh (Civil Appeals Nos. 13-K and 14-K of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Mens Rea and Double Presumption of Innocence
records.heading: Authority on mens rea and the double presumption of innocence
records.text: Authority on the doctrine of mens rea, the double presumption of innocence founded on the principle of innocent until proven guilty, why the accused is the favourite child of law, and proof of guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2026 SCMR 947; Shaista Qaiser v. Altaf Ahmad Khan and another (Crl.P.L.A. 213/2020).
records.title: Shaista Qaiser v. Altaf Ahmad Khan and another (Crl.P.L.A. 213/2020)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Dying Declaration: Art. 46 QSO
records.heading: A dying declaration is admissible without proof that the maker expected imminent death
records.text: A dying declaration is admissible under Art. 46 QSO without any pre-condition that the maker expected imminent death. Courts attach great importance to it, as the shadow of impending death guarantees truth, and admissibility rests on necessity and the sanction equal to an oath. Ref: 2026 SCMR 980; Riaz (decd) through his brother Abdur Rauf v. Gulzar and another (Crl.P.L.A. 99-P/2019).
records.title: Riaz (decd) through his brother Abdur Rauf v. Gulzar and another (Crl.P.L.A. 99-P/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unproved Motive: Death Sentence to Life Imprisonment
records.heading: Failure to prove motive justifies converting a death sentence to life imprisonment
records.text: The Court retains discretion to award the lesser punishment of imprisonment for life. Failure of the prosecution to prove the alleged motive is a mitigating circumstance justifying conversion of the death sentence into life imprisonment. Ref: 2026 SCMR 980; Riaz (decd) through his brother Abdur Rauf v. Gulzar and another (Crl.P.L.A. 99-P/2019).
records.title: Riaz (decd) through his brother Abdur Rauf v. Gulzar and another (Crl.P.L.A. 99-P/2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confession in Police Custody: Arts. 38 and 40 QSO
records.heading: Custodial confession is admissible only under section 164 CrPC or Article 40 QSO
records.text: A confession made to or in the presence of a police officer is inadmissible, even before a Magistrate, under Art. 38 QSO. A custodial confession is admissible only if recorded by a Magistrate under s. 164 CrPC or if it leads to discovery of a fact under Art. 40. The Magistrate must be objectively satisfied of voluntariness, and exceptional caution is needed for accused in police custody. Ref: 2026 SCMR 955; Said ur Rehman v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1674/2021).
records.title: Said ur Rehman v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1674/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Investigation Before Registration of FIR
records.heading: Investigation before registration of an FIR is illegal outside the listed exceptions
records.text: Investigation under s. 156 CrPC follows entry of a complaint of a cognizable offence under s. 154, and investigation as defined in s. 4 differs from inquiry. Investigation before FIR registration, except in cases under ss. 54, 55, 57 or 151, is illegal, which may affect a later judicial confession under s. 164. Ref: 2026 SCMR 955; Said ur Rehman v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1674/2021).
records.title: Said ur Rehman v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1674/2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 540 CrPC: Summoning and Recalling Witnesses
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC powers cannot fill lacunae caused by negligence
records.text: S. 540 CrPC confers wide powers, but as a public trust they may be used only where the evidence is essential to a just decision and not to fill a lacuna caused by negligence or carelessness of a party. They are not to cure infirmities in the prosecution case at the appellate stage. The prosecution had ample opportunity and its failure was sheer negligence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 987; Muhammad Fareedon Rehman v. The State through P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 460/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Fareedon Rehman v. The State through P.G. Sindh and another (Crl.P.L.A. 460/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Heat of Moment: s. 302(c) PPC Instead of 302(b)
records.heading: A sudden altercation without premeditation falls under section 302(c) PPC, not 302(b)
records.text: Where the occurrence arose in the heat of the moment after a spontaneous altercation over the price of a crop, with a single fire shot and no undue brutality, premeditation was absent. The case fell within s. 302(c) PPC, and the courts below erred in convicting under s. 302(b) PPC. Ref: 2026 SCMR 998; Mujahid Khan v. The State (J.P. 778/2017).
records.title: Mujahid Khan v. The State (J.P. 778/2017)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Order VI Rule 17 CPC permits amendment that causes no irreparable prejudice
records.text: O. VI R. 17 CPC gives the court wide discretion to allow amendment at any stage where necessary to determine the real questions in controversy. Amendment should be allowed if it causes no irreparable prejudice to the opposite party and does not fundamentally change the nature of the lis, since procedural law is the handmaid of justice. Ref: Deputy Commissioner, Nowshera and others v. Akhtar Ullah Khan Khattak and others (C.R.Ps. 8 to 12/2024 and connected matters, decided 14.05.2026).
records.title: Deputy Commissioner, Nowshera and others v. Akhtar Ullah Khan Khattak and others (C.R.Ps. 8 to 12/2024 and connected matters, decided 14.05.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Cancellation of Registered Instrument: Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: A civil court may cancel a registered instrument and the Registrar Co-operatives cannot
records.text: The Civil Court has jurisdiction under s. 39 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 to cancel a registered Rectification Deed. The Registrar Co-operatives under s. 54 of the Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 cannot adjudicate fraud, forgery or competing title or cancel registered instruments. Rejection of the plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC was premature and illegal. Ref: 2026 LHC 3085; Muhammad Naseer and 2 others v. Munawar Ali Syed etc (Civil Revision 1373/24, decided 12.05.2026); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Muhammad Naseer and 2 others v. Munawar Ali Syed etc (Civil Revision 1373/24, decided 12.05.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Additional Evidence of Tehsildar in Gift Mutation
records.heading: A belated request to examine the Tehsildar in a gift mutation was refused
records.text: A request at a belated stage to examine the Tehsildar who attested the impugned mutation could not be entertained. Even if allowed, in the absence of proof of a valid gift, and given that the plaintiff was an illiterate old parda nasheen lady not identified by a close blood relative or independently advised, his statement would not change the outcome.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutation by Parda Nasheen Lady
records.heading: The beneficiary of a gift from a parda nasheen woman must prove free consent
records.text: The beneficiary of a transaction with a parda nasheen illiterate woman must prove free consent and that she understood its implications, with independent advice from a lawyer or immediate male family member. A gift requires declaration, acceptance and delivery of possession, and the mutation must also be independently established under the Land Revenue Act and Rules. Ref: PLD 2026 Pesh 53.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Revenue Authorities and Civil Court Jurisdiction over Mutation Fraud
records.heading: Civil courts decide fraud challenges to mutation and revenue authorities do not determine title
records.text: Revenue authorities have limited rectification jurisdiction and their decisions are administrative and tentative, determining neither title nor fraud. Challenges to title or mutation on grounds of fraud need evidence and fall to the civil court under s. 9 CPC, and s. 172 of the Land Revenue Act does not bar this. The civil court's decision binds the revenue hierarchy. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 287, 2026 SCMR 1042; Abdullah and others v. Waryam and others (Direct Civil Appeal No. 02-K of 2023).
records.title: Abdullah and others v. Waryam and others (Direct Civil Appeal No. 02-K of 2023)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Civil Challenge After Revenue Decision: Doctrine of Election
records.heading: Relitigating a revenue decision through a full civil trial is barred by election
records.text: After the revenue hierarchy has decided a matter, a civil challenge should ordinarily be confined to the legality of its orders on the existing record. Relitigating the controversy through a full civil trial defeats the statutory scheme, is an abuse of process and is barred by the doctrine of election. Courts must guard public property against unlawful deprivation. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Art. 14 Limitation Act: Challenge to Government Officer's Order
records.heading: Challenging a government officer's order must be brought within one year under Article 14
records.text: Where relief is sought to set aside an act or order of a government officer made in his official capacity, Art. 14 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908 applies and prescribes one year from the date of the act or order. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Exhibited Document Not Necessarily Proved
records.heading: A document is not proved merely because it was exhibited
records.text: A document is not legally proved merely because it was exhibited, particularly where the mode of proof remains defective. Where the foundation of the claim stood unsubstantiated, the structure raised upon it could not stand. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Protection of Government and Public Land
records.heading: Courts must be vigilant to protect government land against collusive decrees and manipulated records
records.text: In matters of public land, alleged allotments and revenue mutations, courts must exercise heightened vigilance against collusive decrees, manipulated records and proceedings in which the Government is kept out. Government land cannot be taken away on account of negligence, connivance or lapses of subordinate functionaries. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Entries Do Not Confer Title
records.heading: Mutation entries are fiscal records and do not confer or extinguish title
records.text: Mutation entries are maintained for fiscal purposes and do not create, extinguish or confer title. Once a mutation is disputed, the party relying on it must revert to the original transaction and prove it by lawful evidence. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Statements and Mention of Documents in Cross-Examination
records.heading: Mere mention of a document in cross-examination does not prove it
records.text: An obligating statement made in cross-examination is not binding proof and at best is inferential evidence. Mere mention of a document in cross-examination does not prove its existence, authenticity or legality, and the burden in civil proceedings lies on the party asserting a fact. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A.1600-L/2014, decided 20.01.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Doctrine of Election of Remedies
records.heading: A person with several remedies must elect one and cannot later pursue another
records.text: Under the doctrine of election, a person aggrieved by an order or judgment who has several remedies must elect one, and after choosing it may not avail another remedy. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322, PLD 2026 SC 269; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A. No. 1600-L of 2014).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A. No. 1600-L of 2014)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: s. 51(e) CPC: Blocking CNIC in Execution
records.heading: Section 51(e) CPC does not permit blocking a judgment debtor's CNIC in execution
records.text: S. 51(e) CPC allows execution in a manner the relief requires, but it cannot be stretched to permit blocking the CNIC of a judgment debtor in execution of a simple money decree on a summary chapter suit. Curtailing the debtor's ordinary way of life this way was not a proper exercise of discretion, and the High Court erred. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 298; Agha Abid Majeed Khan v. Idrees Ahmed and another (C.P.L.A.3744/2023).
records.title: Agha Abid Majeed Khan v. Idrees Ahmed and another (C.P.L.A.3744/2023)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Denial of Agreement to Sell as Void in Written Statement
records.heading: A fabricated agreement to sell can be denied in the written statement
records.text: Where respondents deny execution of an agreement to sell and payment under it as fabricated and void, they need not challenge it through a separate suit, as it created no legal right. They may deny its genuineness through the written statement. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 337; Asif Ali v. Amjad Ali etc (W.P. 13761/26).
records.title: Asif Ali v. Amjad Ali etc (W.P. 13761/26)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 167 CrPC: Duty Magistrate Cannot Discharge Accused
records.heading: A Magistrate lacking jurisdiction under section 167 CrPC cannot discharge the accused
records.text: A Magistrate receiving an accused for physical remand under s. 167 CrPC may authorise detention up to fifteen days. If he lacks jurisdiction to try or send the case for trial and thinks further detention unnecessary, he must forward the accused to a competent Magistrate and cannot discharge him. An offence under s. 162 PPC is tried by the Special Judge Anti-Corruption. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 363, PLD 2026 Lah 465; The State etc v. The Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc (W.P. 61369/19).
records.title: The State etc v. The Judicial Magistrate Section-30 etc (W.P. 61369/19)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 540 CrPC: Power to Summon Witness
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC allows a Court witness to be examined at any stage
records.text: S. 540 CrPC enables a court to ascertain the truth and to examine any witness as a Court witness at any stage. It has a discretionary part using may and a mandatory part using shall. The court must guard against misuse by parties and exercise the discretion judiciously in the interests of criminal justice. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 388; Muhammad Feroz v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 24 of 2026, decided 19.02.2026); Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir; Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas.
records.title: Muhammad Feroz v. The State and another (Crl. A. No. 24 of 2026, decided 19.02.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Substance Found Non-Controlled by Forensic Report
records.heading: Bail is granted where the forensic report finds the sample non-controlled
records.text: Where 1100 grams of methamphetamine were alleged but the forensic report found the sample to be a non-controlled substance, reasonable grounds were lacking and the case required further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. The accused had no previous narcotics conviction and bail was granted on bonds of Rs. 300,000 with two sureties. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 407; Arshad Mehmood v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 16440-B of 2026, decided 01.04.2026); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa; Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Arshad Mehmood v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. No. 16440-B of 2026, decided 01.04.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Difference Between ss. 249-A and 265-K CrPC
records.heading: Section 249-A applies to Magistrates and section 265-K to the Court of Session
records.text: Under s. 249-A CrPC a Magistrate may acquit at any stage if the charge is groundless or conviction is improbable. Under s. 265-K CrPC the Court of Session may acquit at any stage where the material makes conviction impossible and further evidence cannot change the result.
