Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 410, 2026 MLD 1326; Khalid Mehmood v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 18965/26).
records.title: Khalid Mehmood v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 18965/26)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Secret Audio Recordings: Admissibility
records.heading: Recording one's own conversation is generally lawful but admissibility remains subject to legal standards
records.text: Recording a conversation in which one participates is generally not illegal wiretapping, while recording a conversation between others is illegal. Admissibility of audio recordings is subject to legal standards. Secret recording is an offence in itself, and the complainant's illegality cannot be the sole basis for convicting an accused. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 175; Basharat Ali Chaudhry v. Sabir Ali, etc (Criminal Petition No. 248-L/2016).
records.title: Basharat Ali Chaudhry v. Sabir Ali, etc (Criminal Petition No. 248-L/2016)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Injuries Punishable Under Bailable Offences
records.heading: Bail is a right where injuries are punishable under bailable offences
records.text: Where the injuries attributed to the petitioner were abrasions and contusions punishable under ss. 337-F(i) and 337-L(ii) PPC, which are bailable, and he caused no injury to the deceased, grant of bail is the accused's right. Vicarious liability is for the Trial Court to determine after evidence. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 173; Asghar Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1624-L of 2025).
records.title: Asghar Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1624-L of 2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Abscondence and Other Cases
records.heading: Abscondence or involvement in other cases is no ground to refuse bail
records.text: Mere abscondence of an accused or his involvement in other cases is no ground to refuse bail if he is otherwise entitled to it on merits. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 171; Muhammad Sajid v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 2066 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Sajid v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 2066 of 2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Delay in FIR Caused by Police
records.heading: The victim cannot suffer for delay in an FIR caused by police omission
records.text: Under Art. 21 QSO, delay in an FIR is assessed by the informant's conduct, and the victim cannot suffer for delay caused by police omission or negligence in registering it. The informant acted promptly, as the Roznamcha entry showed. The Court issued directions to police officials, including that Sindh courts must not call the complainant Faryaadi. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 180, 2026 SCMR 1798; Muhammad Bux alias Shahzaib v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.1021/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Bux alias Shahzaib v. The State through Prosecutor General Sindh (Crl.P.L.A.1021/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal of Suit
records.heading: A court refusing permission to withdraw with liberty should not dismiss the suit simpliciter
records.text: Under O. XXIII R. 1 CPC a plaintiff may withdraw a suit or abandon part of the claim, with permission to sue afresh on sufficient grounds. If the court declines permission to withdraw with liberty, it should not dismiss the suit simpliciter. Only the request is refused and the suit continues. Ref: 2026 LHC 3240; Muhammad Aslam v. Addl. District Judge, Shakargarh and others (W.P. No. 8607 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. Addl. District Judge, Shakargarh and others (W.P. No. 8607 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXI R. 35(2) CPC: Symbolic Possession in Execution
records.heading: Order XXI Rule 35(2) CPC protects only legally cognizable joint possession
records.text: O. XXI R. 35(2) CPC, under which joint possession is delivered symbolically, presupposes legally cognizable joint possession. It does not protect persons whose possession is neither joint with nor derived from a recognised title holder, or who cannot show an independent right. Objections on vague allegations of collusion failed. Petition dismissed in limine. Ref: PLJ 2026 Pesh 71; Qaiser Khan and others v. Hamshaid and others (W.P. No. 6141-P of 2025, decided 06.02.2026); Justice Muhammad Naeem Anwar.
records.title: Qaiser Khan and others v. Hamshaid and others (W.P. No. 6141-P of 2025, decided 06.02.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Parallel Foreign Maintenance Orders and s. 17-A
records.heading: Parallel maintenance proceedings are impermissible where a competent foreign court has fixed the same liability
records.text: Parallel maintenance proceedings in Pakistan are impermissible where a competent foreign court has already fixed and is enforcing the same liability. Striking off defence under s. 17-A of the Family Courts Act without addressing that overlap was unlawful. Such striking off is a penal consequence needing reasoned satisfaction of wilful default, not mechanical exercise. Ref: PLJ 2026 Islamabad 170; Muhammad Muneeb Arshad v. Mst. Ammara Mahroof, etc (W.P. No. 5459 of 2025, decided 03.02.2026); Justice Muhammad Azam Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Muneeb Arshad v. Mst. Ammara Mahroof, etc (W.P. No. 5459 of 2025, decided 03.02.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Declaration of Ownership: Proof of Foundational Allotment
records.heading: A plaintiff must prove the foundational allotment by producing the document, not mutation entries
records.text: Plaintiffs seeking a declaration of ownership of land from an earlier allottee must prove the primary transaction, namely the prior allotment and conferment of proprietary rights, by producing the document. They cannot succeed on mutation entries or oral assertions. The High Court judgment was set aside, the lower appellate decree restored and the suit dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322, PLD 2026 SC 269; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A. No. 1600-L of 2014).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A. No. 1600-L of 2014)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Civil Courts and Orders of Revenue Authorities
records.heading: Civil courts should not retry factual controversies decided by statutory revenue authorities
records.text: Civil courts should not conduct a fresh trial to re-determine factual controversies decided by statutory authorities, unless the order is without lawful authority, based on no evidence, jurisdictionally defective or mala fide. The ordinary recourse against a final revenue order is the High Court's constitutional jurisdiction rather than a parallel civil trial. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322, PLD 2026 SC 269; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A. No. 1600-L of 2014).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A. No. 1600-L of 2014)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Exhibiting a Document Does Not Prove It
records.heading: Exhibiting a document does not prove it where the mode of proof is defective
records.text: Documentary material cannot be treated as legally proved merely because it has been exhibited during evidence, particularly where the mode of proof remains defective. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 322, PLD 2026 SC 269; Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A. No. 1600-L of 2014).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Officer (Revenue), Bhakkar, etc v. Zulfiqar, etc (C.P.L.A. No. 1600-L of 2014)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: s. 145 CrPC Order and Joint Co-owners
records.heading: A section 145 CrPC order is temporary and does not determine rights
records.text: An order under s. 145 CrPC is temporary and lasts only during imminent danger of breach of peace, without finally determining rights. Co-owners in joint possession cannot be forcibly dispossessed, and possession of the disputed construction is to be regulated by the Civil Court where the suits are pending. Petition dismissed and leave refused. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 134; Malik Saif-ur-Rehman v. Zahoor Ahmad Malik (C.P.L.A. No. 23 of 2025).
records.title: Malik Saif-ur-Rehman v. Zahoor Ahmad Malik (C.P.L.A. No. 23 of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Police Constable Recruitment: Eyesight Standard
records.heading: Constable recruitment requires 6/6 vision under Rule 12.16 of the Punjab Police Rules
records.text: Rule 12.16 of the Punjab Police Rules, 1934 requires 6/6 vision for constable recruitment. The candidate applied on open merit and not under the disability quota and was found medically unfit. The Court noted the Rules are 90 years old and suggested allowing such candidates to be placed in office work, but refrained from interfering with recruitment policy. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 114; Muhammad Farhan v. The Province of Punjab through Inspector General of Police, Lahore and another (F.C.P.L.A. No. 16 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Farhan v. The Province of Punjab through Inspector General of Police, Lahore and another (F.C.P.L.A. No. 16 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Deficient Court Fee: Specify Amount and Allow Time
records.heading: A court must specify the deficient court fee and allow time to pay it
records.text: Before dismissing an appeal or plaint for deficient court fee, the court must specify and communicate the exact deficiency and then allow reasonable opportunity to make it up. These are mandatory procedural safeguards, and court fee requirements should not extinguish substantive rights where the defect is curable. Ref: 2026 LHC 3064; Rahat Fateh Ali Khan etc v. Syed Haider Abbas (Civil Revision 61279/21, decided 12.05.2026); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Rahat Fateh Ali Khan etc v. Syed Haider Abbas (Civil Revision 61279/21, decided 12.05.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Pistol and Crime Empties Sent to Forensics Together
records.heading: Sending the pistol and crime empties to forensics together makes the comparison result unreliable
records.text: Where the crime empty and the recovered pistol were dispatched to the Forensic Science Laboratory together on the same day, the recoveries became inconsequential, and the positive comparison result could not be relied upon. Ref: 2026 SCMR 891; Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition No. 473 of 2018).
records.title: Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition No. 473 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: Witnesses without a reason for being on the route are doubtful chance witnesses
records.text: A witness who gave no reason for being on the route to the place of occurrence, and a complainant who was not an employee of the forest department but gave no valid reason for travelling between forest offices, were chance witnesses whose presence was doubtful. Jail petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 891; Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition No. 473 of 2018).
records.title: Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition No. 473 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Improvements in Complainant's Testimony
records.heading: A new detail absent from the complaint is an improvement that renders testimony doubtful
records.text: The complainant's mention in evidence of an exchange of hot words, absent from his complaint to the police, was an improvement that rendered portions of his testimony doubtful. Jail petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 891; Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition No. 473 of 2018).
records.title: Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition No. 473 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recoveries Without Independent Witnesses
records.heading: Recoveries made without independent witnesses despite public presence are doubtful
records.text: Recoveries of the ring, wallet and other items on personal search without independent witnesses, though members of the public and forest staff were present, were rendered doubtful. Recovery alone was insufficient to sustain the conviction. Ref: 2026 SCMR 891; Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition No. 473 of 2018).
records.title: Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition No. 473 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Passive and unnatural conduct of eye-witnesses casts serious doubt on their presence
records.text: Eye-witnesses who were the deceased's brother and cousin, neither intervened nor raised a hue and cry, and did not charge the appellant for firing at them despite a common motive. Their passive conduct and the implausible sequence of firing cast serious doubt on their presence, and guilt was not established beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2026 SCMR 921; Muhammad Amjad and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 220-L of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Amjad and another v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 220-L of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Interfaith Marriage: Muslim Male and Christian Woman
records.heading: A Muslim male may validly marry a Christian woman
records.text: A Muslim male may validly contract marriage with a Christian woman, who belongs to the Ahl al-Kitab. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court Precedent Before Federal Constitutional Court
records.heading: Article 189 operates subject to the Federal Constitutional Court's overriding authority in constitutional matters
records.text: With the establishment of the Federal Constitutional Court, Art. 189 operates subject to its overriding authority in constitutional matters. The Court will ordinarily follow earlier Supreme Court constitutional jurisprudence unless it is manifestly erroneous or inconsistent with the constitutional scheme or fundamental rights, and any departure must be reasoned, express and principled. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Registration of Muslim-Christian Marriage under MFLO 1961
records.heading: A Muslim-Christian marriage cannot be registered under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961
records.text: A marriage between a Muslim male and a Christian female cannot be solemnized and registered under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, as that Ordinance applies only to Muslim citizens of Pakistan. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Conversion to Islam: Proof and Essentials
records.heading: Embracing Islam needs only a declaration and recitation of the Kalma with belief
records.text: Where a person openly professes a faith, no further inquiry is ordinarily required to verify its genuineness. Embracing Islam needs no specific ritual, only a declaration and recitation of the Kalma with belief in the Oneness of Allah, the Finality of the Prophethood and the Holy Qur'an. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929: Statutory Framework
records.heading: The Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929 remains in force and applies to all citizens
records.text: The Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929 remains in force in Pakistan under Art. 268 of the 1973 Constitution and applies to Muslim and non-Muslim citizens. S. 12 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 raised the age of a girl child from 14 to 16 years for Muslim citizens. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Alteration of Settled Personal Law
records.heading: Altering a settled personal law requires clear and unequivocal legislative terms
records.text: A legislature intending to alter or abrogate a settled personal law must do so in clear and unequivocal terms. Absent an explicit statutory provision invalidating the marriage itself, the legal status of such a marriage remains unaffected. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata: Finality of Unchallenged Judgments
records.heading: An unchallenged judgment attains finality and operates as res judicata between the parties
records.text: A judgment not challenged before a higher forum attains finality, and the determination made operates as final between the parties on the principle of res judicata. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. No. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Compromise Waiving Minor's Future Maintenance Void
records.heading: A compromise permanently waiving a minor's future maintenance is void to that extent
records.text: A compromise clause barring a wife and minor from ever claiming maintenance or instituting proceedings for it is examined under s. 28 of the Contract Act, 1872, which makes void an agreement absolutely restraining enforcement of legal rights through ordinary legal proceedings. Even if accrued maintenance could be settled, a condition permanently waiving the minor's future maintenance is unenforceable to that extent. Ref: 2026 LHC 3278; Akhtar Hussain Awan, etc. v. Naseer Akhtar Awan, etc. (Writ Petition No. 55956 of 2020, decided 21.05.2026).
records.title: Akhtar Hussain Awan, etc. v. Naseer Akhtar Awan, etc. (Writ Petition No. 55956 of 2020, decided 21.05.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Repeated Suits on Same Mutation: Election of Remedies
records.heading: A third suit on the same mutation is not maintainable after election of forum
records.text: Where an earlier suit against the same mutation was finally dismissed and a later suit was dismissed in default without leave to file afresh, a third suit is not maintainable. A party who elects one forum cannot abandon that election and resort to a parallel forum, a bar attracted by O. II R. 2 CPC read with Art. 114 QSO. Leave to appeal declined. Ref: 2026 SCMR 994; Mst. Safia Khanum and others v. Additional District Judge-II East, Islamabad (C.P.L.A. No. 3939 of 2025).
records.title: Mst. Safia Khanum and others v. Additional District Judge-II East, Islamabad (C.P.L.A. No. 3939 of 2025)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay: Sufficient Cause and Bona Fides
records.heading: Condonation requires a bona fide explanation for the whole period of delay
records.text: Limitation rests on public policy of certainty and finality, and a right accrued by lapse of time is not disturbed without sufficient cause. A party seeking condonation must come with clean hands and give a bona fide explanation for the whole period of delay. Negligence or indolence is not sufficient cause, and negligence after return of proceedings weakens the plea of bona fide prosecution. Ref: T&T Employees Cooperative Housing Society, Islamabad v. Haji Ghulam Hussain and others (C.P.L.A. 3469/2025, decided 02.06.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: T&T Employees Cooperative Housing Society, Islamabad v. Haji Ghulam Hussain and others (C.P.L.A. 3469/2025, decided 02.06.2026)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Lawyers' Strike and Suspension of Licence
records.heading: Suspending advocates' licences for a lawyers' strike was declared unlawful
records.text: The Federal Constitutional Court declared unlawful the suspension of advocates' licences on account of a lawyers' strike. It held that the practice of law is a constitutional right and a licence cannot be suspended merely for taking part in a strike or for appearing for a controversial accused. Ref: Peshawar High Court Bar v. Shabbir Hussain & another (F.C.P.L.A. Nos. 379, 380, 384 and 389 of 2025).
records.title: Peshawar High Court Bar v. Shabbir Hussain & another (F.C.P.L.A. Nos. 379, 380, 384 and 389 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Terms and Intention of Parties on Dower
records.heading: Nikahnama clauses on dower are construed by the parties' intention, not column headings
records.text: A nikahnama is a civil contract whose clauses are construed according to the intention of the parties, and dower terms are determined on settled principles rather than on column headings, which are neither conclusive nor sacrosanct. Courts must give effect to the true intent and read the contract as a whole, and a bride cannot be deprived of her rights under it. Ref: 2026 LHC 3293; Mst. Samira Bibi v. Addl. District Judge and 03 others (Writ Petition No. 5398 of 2023).
records.title: Mst. Samira Bibi v. Addl. District Judge and 03 others (Writ Petition No. 5398 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: High Court Declaring Escheat in Private Dispute
records.heading: Declaring escheat in a private dispute without pleadings or evidence is jurisdictional overreach
records.text: In a suit between private parties over ownership by inheritance and an alleged waqf, the High Court in revision declared the property escheat and directed the Government to take possession. The Government was not a party, and there were no pleadings, issues or evidence on escheat. The Supreme Court treated this as jurisdictional overreach. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 283, PLJ 2026 SC 461; Muhammad Shafique Khan and others v. Madrisa Taleem-ul-Quran Khairul Madaris, Multan (Civil Petitions Nos. 3232, 3287 of 2023 and 5138 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Shafique Khan and others v. Madrisa Taleem-ul-Quran Khairul Madaris, Multan (Civil Petitions Nos. 3232, 3287 of 2023 and 5138 of 2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Diversion of Public or Religious Purpose Land
records.heading: Converting land dedicated to a public or religious purpose to commercial use is unlawful
records.text: Conversion of land dedicated to a public or religious purpose into commercial use infringes proprietary and possessory rights and the public interest, and is contrary to the terms of allotment and unlawful. Such land carries the character of a purpose trust, and any deviation without competent authority is ultra vires and void. Ref: 2026 MLD 921; Province of the Punjab through Secretary Education, Civil Secretariat, Lahore & another v. Darul Haq Trust & others (Civil Revision No. 46498 of 2017).
records.title: Province of the Punjab through Secretary Education, Civil Secretariat, Lahore & another v. Darul Haq Trust & others (Civil Revision No. 46498 of 2017)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 161 QSO: Court's Power to Order Documents
records.heading: Article 161 QSO allows a Judge to order production of documents to discover facts
records.text: Under Art. 161 QSO a Judge may, to discover or obtain proper proof of relevant facts, ask any question of any witness or party and order production of any document or thing. Certified copies of a judgment and decree, the nikahnama and the CNIC were held capable of being called for, with no prejudice to the respondent. Ref: 2026 MLD 972; Kaneez Bibi v. The State and two others (Criminal Revision No. 48 of 2025).
records.title: Kaneez Bibi v. The State and two others (Criminal Revision No. 48 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Decree Silent on Compounding: Simple Increase
records.heading: A decree silent on compounding carries a simple annual increase on the original amount
records.text: Where a maintenance decree provides an annual 20% increase but is silent on compounding, the increase is calculated on the originally decreed amount and not on the accumulated sum. The Executing Court erred in compounding, and the Appellate Court rightly corrected it. Courts should state expressly whether increase is simple or compound. Ref: Muhammad Waqar Wasi v. Mst. Amber Abid & others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3204 of 2022, decided 14.04.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Waqar Wasi v. Mst. Amber Abid & others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3204 of 2022, decided 14.04.2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction: Co-Owner and Bona Fide Personal Need
records.heading: A single co-owner may maintain an eviction petition on behalf of all co-owners
records.text: A single co-owner can maintain an eviction petition on behalf of all co-owners. Bona fide personal need extends to the landlord's children and family members, and the landlord is the best judge of his own requirement and may choose the tenement that suits him. Ref: Najeeb Ullah and others v. Syed Shams-ud-Din and others (Civil Petition Nos. 300-Q, 303-Q to 312-Q of 2025, decided 23.04.2026).
records.title: Najeeb Ullah and others v. Syed Shams-ud-Din and others (Civil Petition Nos. 300-Q, 303-Q to 312-Q of 2025, decided 23.04.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Alteration of Date of Birth in Service Book
records.heading: A date of birth recorded in the service book attains finality
records.text: A date of birth once recorded in the service book attains finality, and no alteration is permissible under Rule 21-A(3) of the Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules. Belated attempts, particularly after availing benefits or near retirement, are declined, and correction in educational record does not automatically entitle correction in service record. Ref: The Secretary, Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department and others v. Muhammad Abdullah Khan (Civil Petition No. 208 of 2024 and CMA No. 354 of 2024, decided 31.03.2026).
records.title: The Secretary, Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department and others v. Muhammad Abdullah Khan (Civil Petition No. 208 of 2024 and CMA No. 354 of 2024, decided 31.03.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Public Interest Litigation: Scope and Pre-conditions
records.heading: Public interest litigation must not serve private malice, vested interest or publicity
records.text: Public interest litigation must be used with great care, and courts must ensure that private malice, vested interest or publicity seeking does not lie behind it. The Lahore High Court dismissed a petition against unannounced power and gas load shedding as unnecessary and a waste of court time, imposing costs of Rs. 100,000. Ref: 2026 LHC 3327; Judicial Activism Panel through Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Pakistan through Secretary etc. (Misc. Writ. 24539/26); Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: Judicial Activism Panel through Muhammad Azhar Siddique v. Pakistan through Secretary etc. (Misc. Writ. 24539/26)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sodomy: Sole Victim Testimony and Absence of Injury
records.heading: The sole testimony of a victim of sodomy suffices if it inspires confidence
records.text: The sole testimony of a victim suffices to prove the occurrence if it inspires confidence. Absence of injury does not preclude sexual abuse, and absence of physical signs in the MLC despite examination within hours does not contradict the prosecution case or negate sodomy. Ref: 2025 LHC 8650; Imtiaz Hussain alias Munshi v. State (Crl. Appeal-420-23, decided 15.12.2025); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Imtiaz Hussain alias Munshi v. State (Crl. Appeal-420-23, decided 15.12.2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recording of Statements under s. 164 CrPC
records.heading: Magistrates must record section 164(2) statements carefully in the witness's own words
records.text: Magistrates must record s. 164(2) statements with care, asking explanatory questions and recording the witness's own account rather than formulaic language. In cases under the 2021 Act, s. 14 must be complied with, including video recording and opportunity for cross-examination by counsel. Sessions Judges in the Punjab were directed to ensure compliance. Ref: 2025 LHC 8639; Sonara Khan alias Sonhara Khan v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 6968-B-25, decided 09.10.2025); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Sonara Khan alias Sonhara Khan v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 6968-B-25, decided 09.10.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail in Non-Prohibitory Offences: s. 161 Statements
records.heading: In non-prohibitory offences bail is the rule and refusal the exception
records.text: In offences below the prohibitory clause, bail is the rule and refusal an exception needing extraordinary circumstances. Statements under s. 161 CrPC are not substantive evidence, and the investigating officer's opinion on guilt does not bind the Court. The High Court gave undue weight to tentative police conclusions at the bail stage. Ref: Javed Iqbal v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 450-L/2026, decided 03.06.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Javed Iqbal v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 450-L/2026, decided 03.06.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 302(c) PPC: Sudden Provocation and Social Context
records.heading: Sudden provocation is judged by a reasonable person in the accused's social setting
records.text: Sudden provocation under s. 302(c) is assessed by how a reasonable person in the same cultural and social setting as the accused would react, not on an abstract standard. Relying on Budhi Singh, grave and sudden provocation, loss of self-control and retaliation before passion cools must co-exist. The conviction under s. 302(c) and the sentence were not interfered with. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 394; Hizbullah v. State.
records.title: Hizbullah v. State

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Paternal Grandfather's Liability for Minors' Maintenance
records.heading: A paternal grandfather with means is responsible for maintaining minors whose father is incapable
records.text: Where the father is incapable of maintaining his minor children, responsibility extends to the paternal grandfather, and the welfare of the minor is paramount. The question was whether the grandfather could be impleaded in the maintenance suit where the father claimed incapacity and the grandfather had sufficient means. Ref: 2026 CLC 673; Amna Fayyaz v. Additional District Judge.
records.title: Amna Fayyaz v. Additional District Judge

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Service and Leave to Defend
records.heading: A plea of non-service fails where the jail superintendent's report confirms proper service
records.text: In a summary suit on dishonoured cheques, the respondent in custody pleaded non-service and delay in seeking leave to defend. The superintendent jail's report confirmed proper service and the plea of incomplete service lacked substance. The order granting leave to defend was set aside and the trial Court directed to proceed expeditiously. Ref: 2026 CLC 794; Waqas Mahmood v. Bilal Mir (Civil Revision No. 46 of 2025).
records.title: Waqas Mahmood v. Bilal Mir (Civil Revision No. 46 of 2025)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Appointment of Lambardar: No Vested Right
records.heading: Physical presence in the village is an essential attribute of the office of Lambardar
records.text: A Lambardar performs quasi-administrative and fiscal functions under Rule 22 of the Punjab Land Revenue Rules, 1968, so effective physical presence in the village or chak is an essential attribute of the office. No vested or enforceable right exists to claim appointment as Lambardar, and revenue authorities must select a person in whom the estate can repose confidence. Ref: Shaukat Ali v. Member (Judicial-III) (F.C.P.L.A. 487 of 2025).
records.title: Shaukat Ali v. Member (Judicial-III) (F.C.P.L.A. 487 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Columns and Additional Divorce Benefits
records.heading: Nikahnama columns are guidance and do not conclusively determine the parties' intention
records.text: Columns in a nikahnama are guidance for the parties and do not conclusively determine their intention, so courts consider the intention of the parties rather than the headings. The High Court set aside the judgment and remanded the matter to the Lower Appellate Court to decide the appeal afresh. Ref: 2026 CLC 580; Yasmeen Bibi v. Zeeshan Ali.
records.title: Yasmeen Bibi v. Zeeshan Ali

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Ecstasy Pills: Dubious Recovery and Discrepant PFSA Report
records.heading: A dubious recovery and discrepant PFSA count entitle the accused to acquittal
records.text: Recovery of ecstasy pills was not from the accused's personal search, there was no proof of lawful possession of the flat, and the PFSA count of pills differed from the sealed parcels described by the prosecution. If any limb of evidence is dubious it can suffice for acquittal, as the prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 130; Mustajab v. State (Crl. A. No. 321 of 2024, decided 11.02.2025); Justice Tariq Mehmood Jahangiri; Justice Muhammad Azam Khan.
records.title: Mustajab v. State (Crl. A. No. 321 of 2024, decided 11.02.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Autopsy and Doubtful Presence of Witnesses
records.heading: Unexplained delay of over two days in autopsy suggests a fabricated narrative
records.text: Inordinate unexplained delay of over two days in autopsy speaks against the veracity of the prosecution version and permits an inference of a fabricated narrative. Unnatural conduct of prosecution witnesses makes their presence at the scene doubtful, and their testimony was discarded in a s. 302 PPC case. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 137; Muhammad Hamza v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 759-J & Crl. Rev. No. 305 of 2023, decided 14.04.2025); Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar.
records.title: Muhammad Hamza v. State and another (Crl. A. No. 759-J & Crl. Rev. No. 305 of 2023, decided 14.04.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Post-Mortem
records.heading: Unexplained delay in post-mortem requires cautious assessment and doubts the eye-witnesses' presence
records.text: Unexplained delay in post-mortem calls for assessing prosecution evidence with utmost caution, and the natural inference is that time was used for preliminary investigation and consultation to implicate the accused and fabricate eye-witnesses. The alleged eye-witnesses did not identify the body at autopsy or inquest, so their presence was doubted. Appeal allowed and the complainant's enhancement revision dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 138; Ayesha Naeem etc. v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 67910-J, 67912-J, 67916-J & Crl. Rev. No. 67907 of 2022, heard on 12.03.2025); Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Ayesha Naeem etc. v. State and others (Crl. A. Nos. 67910-J, 67912-J, 67916-J & Crl. Rev. No. 67907 of 2022, heard on 12.03.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in Post-Mortem and Dishonest Improvements
records.heading: Delay in post-mortem and dishonest improvements make prosecution witnesses unreliable
records.text: Unexplained delay in post-mortem suggests that time was consumed in procuring eye-witnesses before police papers were prepared. Dishonest improvements by a witness cast serious doubt on veracity and make the statement unreliable. Appeal allowed, the appellant acquitted and the death sentence not confirmed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 140; Ghulam Shabbir alias Shabo v. State (Crl. A. No. 412 & M.R. No. 39 of 2023, heard on 29.01.2026); Justice Shehram Sarwar Ch.; Justice Sardar Akbar Ali.
records.title: Ghulam Shabbir alias Shabo v. State (Crl. A. No. 412 & M.R. No. 39 of 2023, heard on 29.01.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Statements to Police: Defamation and s. 499 PPC Exception
records.heading: Information given to police falls within an exception to section 499 PPC
records.text: A statement made to police has not passed judicial scrutiny, and information to a law enforcement agency for action under law falls within an exception to s. 499 PPC, excluding liability under s. 500 PPC. Such a case may be one of malicious prosecution rather than defamation, arising when the statements are repeated before a Court. Mode of trial was the main question. Ref: PLJ 2026 Civil Note 37; Sumera Rasheed v. State and others (P.S.L.A. No. 07 of 2023, decided 27.11.2023); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Sumera Rasheed v. State and others (P.S.L.A. No. 07 of 2023, decided 27.11.2023)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Time Spent Removing Office Objections Counts
records.heading: Time spent removing office objections counts within limitation
records.text: A delinquent party cannot challenge an adverse order at a time of its own choosing. Time consumed in removing office objections is counted within limitation, and if it exceeds the period allowed the matter is dismissed as time-barred. After limitation expires, verdicts attain finality. The civil revision was dismissed as barred by time. Ref: PLJ 2026 Civil Note 38; Muhammad Zafar etc. v. Province of Punjab etc. (C.R. No. 81 of 2021, decided 11.02.2026); Justice Ch. Muhammad Iqbal.
records.title: Muhammad Zafar etc. v. Province of Punjab etc. (C.R. No. 81 of 2021, decided 11.02.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 79 QSO: Scribe and Attesting Witnesses
records.heading: A scribe is a competent witness only if he signed as an attesting witness
records.text: A scribe is a competent witness of a document only if he signed as an attesting witness. While attesting witnesses are alive and capable of giving evidence, a document cannot be used without their evidence. In a suit for specific performance, concurrent findings on evidence are not reviewed under s. 115 CPC and the revision was dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Civil Note 39; Shabbir Hussain v. Muhammad Shabbir Naveed (deceased) through L.R Namely Mian Rasheed Ahmad Qamar Qadri (C.R. No. 441-D of 2018, decided 13.03.2025); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Shabbir Hussain v. Muhammad Shabbir Naveed (deceased) through L.R Namely Mian Rasheed Ahmad Qamar Qadri (C.R. No. 441-D of 2018, decided 13.03.2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Revision Incompetent Where Appeal Available
records.heading: Revision is incompetent where an appeal lies under section 96 CPC
records.text: No appeal was filed under s. 96 read with O. XLI R. 1 CPC against the decree rejecting the plaint, yet the Revisional Court decided the matter. Where an appeal lies under s. 96 CPC, revision is incompetent. Petition allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Civil Note 41; Rana Najam-ul-Abbas v. Mst. Lubna Shamim and 2 others (W.P. No. 2863 of 2017, heard on 09.10.2025); Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: Rana Najam-ul-Abbas v. Mst. Lubna Shamim and 2 others (W.P. No. 2863 of 2017, heard on 09.10.2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Deferred Dower: Limitation and Priority as Debt
records.heading: Deferred dower is a debt that takes precedence over inheritance
records.text: Dower is a binding financial obligation of the husband and a debt taking precedence over inheritance, recoverable from the estate before distribution among heirs. The Family Courts Act, as special law, prevails over the general law, and the case concerned limitation under Art. 104 and s. 14 of the Limitation Act in a suit for recovery of deferred dower. Ref: PLJ 2026 Islamabad 132; Asia Ijaz v. Additional District Judge (West), Islamabad and 6 others (W.P. No. 2561 of 2025, decided 17.02.2026); Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani.
records.title: Asia Ijaz v. Additional District Judge (West), Islamabad and 6 others (W.P. No. 2561 of 2025, decided 17.02.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Lis Pendens: s. 52 and Collusive Proceedings
records.heading: Section 52 embodies lis pendens and excepts collusive suits from its operation
records.text: Section 52 provides that during the pendency of a non-collusive suit in which a right to immovable property is directly and specifically in question, the property cannot be transferred so as to affect another party's rights under any decree, except with the Court's authority. It embodies the rule of lis pendens, with an exception where the action is collusive. Ref: 2026 MLD 898; Sardar Muhammad Boota v. Jaffar Ali (RSA No. 02 of 2013).
records.title: Sardar Muhammad Boota v. Jaffar Ali (RSA No. 02 of 2013)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Charas Bail: Net Weight to Be Determined at Trial
records.heading: Net weight of charas is determined at trial and post-arrest bail was allowed
records.text: In a case of recovery of 1260 grams of charas in two pieces in a plastic bag, the net weight and the applicable entry of the Table under s. 9(1) CNSA will be determined after evidence. Post-arrest bail allowed under s. 497 CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 129; Muhammad Azeem v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 3798-B of 2024, decided 23.09.2024); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Azeem v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 3798-B of 2024, decided 23.09.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Charas Bail: Failure to Video-Record Recovery
records.heading: Failure to video-record a charas recovery raises doubt and warrants bail
records.text: Art. 164 QSO permits evidence from modern devices, yet the complainant and Investigating Officer did not record the recovery of 2000 grams of charas although cameras were available. This conduct raised doubt about the petitioner's involvement and made the case one of further inquiry. Bail after arrest granted under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 132; Abdul Qadir v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 668-B of 2024, decided 12.03.2024); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Abdul Qadir v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 668-B of 2024, decided 12.03.2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Charas Bail: Failure to Video-Record Recovery
records.heading: Failure to record a charas recovery despite a camera phone justifies further inquiry
records.text: The arresting ASI had a mobile phone with a camera but neither he nor the Investigating Officer recorded the arrest and recovery of 1420 grams of charas. Art. 164 QSO permits such evidence, and the omission made the case one of further inquiry. Bail after arrest granted under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 122; Imran Khan v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 1087-B of 2024, decided 28.03.2024); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Imran Khan v. State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 1087-B of 2024, decided 28.03.2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Quantum of Minors' Maintenance and Father's Means
records.heading: The father's means are material to the quantum of minors' maintenance
records.text: A father's past and present earnings and assets are material to the quantum of maintenance, and an adverse inference may be drawn if he conceals them. Maintenance must match the children's needs, previous standard of living and education, and the obligation is independent of disputes between spouses. Ref: 2026 LHC 3358; Sohail Zarar Ali Khan v. Additional District Judge (Writ Petition No. 48803 of 2020).
records.title: Sohail Zarar Ali Khan v. Additional District Judge (Writ Petition No. 48803 of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Does Not Erase Earlier Maintenance Entitlement
records.heading: Khula does not erase the wife's earlier entitlement to maintenance
records.text: Dissolution of marriage by khula does not by itself retrospectively erase the wife's right to maintenance during the subsistence of the marriage or for the period for which she was otherwise legally entitled. Ref: 2026 LHC 3358; Sohail Zarar Ali Khan v. Additional District Judge (Writ Petition No. 48803 of 2020).
records.title: Sohail Zarar Ali Khan v. Additional District Judge (Writ Petition No. 48803 of 2020)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Writ Against Capacity Charges and Tariff: Policy Matters
records.heading: A writ against capacity charges and tariff is not maintainable as policy
records.text: The Lahore High Court dismissed as not maintainable a petition against capacity charges and tariff in electricity bills. Energy policy is for the Executive and Legislature, and Art. 199 jurisdiction is confined to the legality of the decision-making process, not the merits or wisdom of policy. Courts cannot act as regulator or order refund of IPP payments. Ref: 2026 LHC 3378; Ashba Kamran v. NEPRA through its Chairman etc. (Misc. Writ. 32881/26, decided 03.06.2026); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Ashba Kamran v. NEPRA through its Chairman etc. (Misc. Writ. 32881/26, decided 03.06.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: No Revision Against Order in s. 104 CPC Appeal
records.heading: No revision lies against an order in an appeal under section 104 CPC
records.text: Revision is not maintainable against an order passed in appeal under s. 104 CPC. An appeal not under s. 96 CPC was treated as an appeal against an order and was decided as such, so under s. 115(5) CPC the remedy of revision was unavailable. Ref: 2026 CLC 869; Ghulam Abbas v. Ghulam Haider (111493/25).
records.title: Ghulam Abbas v. Ghulam Haider (111493/25)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Will in Favour of Heir; Registration Optional
records.heading: A bequest to an heir is valid only with other heirs' consent
records.text: Under Muhammadan Law a bequest to an heir is valid only if the other heirs consent after the testator's death, and a testator may bequeath up to one third of the estate. Under the Registration Act, 1908, registration of a Will is optional, as s. 17 does not list it and s. 42 only permits deposit. Ref: 2026 CLC 905; Muhammad Riaz v. Arshad Ali etc. (Civil Revision 41323/21).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Arshad Ali etc. (Civil Revision 41323/21)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Third Suit on Same Cause of Action Barred
records.heading: Relief omitted in an earlier suit on the same cause of action is barred
records.text: A plaintiff who omits to claim relief arising from the same cause of action in an earlier suit is barred from a later suit for it. A third suit on the same agreement after two earlier suits were dismissed was barred, and non-disclosure of prior litigation was material suppression undermining bona fides. Ref: 2026 CLC 956; Dr. Tehsin Mazhar Sheikh v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 77145/2019).
records.title: Dr. Tehsin Mazhar Sheikh v. Additional District Judge etc. (Writ Petition No. 77145/2019)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Husband Offering Wife for Intercourse: Abetment and s. 365B
records.heading: A husband who offers his wife for intercourse may be liable for abetment
records.text: A husband who offers his wife for intercourse with another may be liable for abetment under s. 109 PPC, while the wife who complies may be liable for fornication under s. 496B. If he persuades her for a benefit he may be liable under s. 365B, and if she submits under compulsion the act amounts to rape under s. 375 PPC despite apparent consent. Ref: 2026 LHC 3442; Muhammad Ajmal v. State etc (Crl. Misc.-3141-B-26, decided 03.06.2026); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Muhammad Ajmal v. State etc (Crl. Misc.-3141-B-26, decided 03.06.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Deferred Dower Payable on Proved Polygamy
records.heading: Deferred dower becomes payable on proved polygamy under section 6(5) of the MFLO
records.text: Deferred dower becomes payable on proved polygamy under s. 6(5) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. The husband concealed prior marriages and contracted a fourth marriage, so the wife's expulsion could not be attributed to her. She was held entitled to maintenance at Rs. 15,000 per month from 27.12.2021 with 10% annual increase, deferred dower of Rs. 1,000,000 and her dowry articles. Ref: 2026 YLR 1338, PLJ 2026 Lahore 262; Mehnaz Saleem v. Kashif Iqbal etc (WP.2743/25).
records.title: Mehnaz Saleem v. Kashif Iqbal etc (WP.2743/25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Service of Summons: O. V Rules 10-A, 17 and 18
records.heading: Order V Rule 10-A makes acknowledgement of registered post prima facie proof of service
records.text: O. V R. 10-A CPC requires a notice by registered post A.D. with summons, and the acknowledgement or postal endorsement of refusal is prima facie proof of service. R. 17 governs service by affixation after due diligence, and R. 18 requires the serving officer's report, which the Court may verify by examining the officer on oath. Ref: 2026 YLR 1316; Muhammad Hanif v. Abdul Razzaq (C.R. No. 782 of 2016).
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. Abdul Razzaq (C.R. No. 782 of 2016)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Civil Court Suit Bypassing Revenue Hierarchy
records.heading: A party must use the special revenue forum before approaching the civil court
records.text: Where the legislature has provided a special forum with an adequate remedy, the aggrieved party must first use it before approaching the civil Court. The petitioners bypassed the revenue hierarchy, and fraud, mala fide or collusion by revenue authorities was not specifically pleaded, though such allegations must be pleaded with specificity and proved. Ref: 2026 LHC 3523; Mushtaq Hussain Shah (deceased) through Legal Heirs v. The Province of Punjab through District Collector, Sialkot & others (Civil Revision No. 70734 of 2023).
records.title: Mushtaq Hussain Shah (deceased) through Legal Heirs v. The Province of Punjab through District Collector, Sialkot & others (Civil Revision No. 70734 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Hiba: Proof of Offer, Acceptance and Delivery
records.heading: A claim of title by hiba needs proof of declaration, acceptance and delivery of possession
records.text: A person claiming title by hiba must prove a clear declaration of gift by the donor, acceptance by or for the donee, and delivery of possession. Mutation neither creates nor extinguishes title, and where the gift itself is disputed a mutation entry cannot by itself establish ownership, serving at best as corroboration. Ref: 2026 LHC 3516; Imtiaz Ahmad & others v. Abdul Hameed alias Majeed (deceased) through Legal Heirs & another (Civil Revision No. 158 of 2019).
records.title: Imtiaz Ahmad & others v. Abdul Hameed alias Majeed (deceased) through Legal Heirs & another (Civil Revision No. 158 of 2019)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Heroin: Laboratory Report on Chemical Nature
records.heading: Laboratory reports on heroin must give comprehensive details and reasons
records.text: The judgment discusses the chemical identity of heroin and the question of what a substance is if the Punjab Forensic Science Agency did not find it to be heroin. The laboratory must give comprehensive details and reasons in its report, and investigating agencies in narcotics cases were directed to obtain reports with such details. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 997; Naveed Hussain v. State.
records.title: Naveed Hussain v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sugar Factories Control Act: s. 21(b) Report Required
records.heading: Section 21(b) of the Sugar Factories Control Act requires a formal report to police
records.text: Under s. 21(b) of the Sugar Factories Control Act, 1950 a formal report by a specified officer to police is required to make the offence cognizable, so an FIR cannot be registered on an individual's report, and the Deputy Commissioner's comments were no such report. The Justice of Peace's order was set aside for that Act but upheld for ss. 342 and 506 PPC. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 986; Azhar Fazal v. Additional Sessions Judge.
records.title: Azhar Fazal v. Additional Sessions Judge

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Witnesses and Delayed FIR
records.heading: Unnatural conduct and unexplained delay in reporting a confession led to rejection of witnesses
records.text: Prosecution witnesses did not arrest the accused after hearing an alleged extra-judicial confession and did not report it for a week. The delay in applying to police was used to fashion a false narrative, and the conduct was unnatural, so their statements were rejected. Ref: 2026 YLR 864; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Circumstantial Evidence: Complete Chain Required
records.heading: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain pointing only to guilt
records.text: In a case of circumstantial evidence, the prosecution must establish each incriminating circumstance by reliable and clinching evidence, and the circumstances must form a complete chain leading to no conclusion other than guilt. Ref: 2026 YLR 864; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Call Data Record Without Voice Data Irrelevant
records.heading: A Call Data Record without voice data or conversation details is irrelevant
records.text: Without any voice call data or record, mere production of a Call Data Record without disclosure of the details of conversations is not relevant to prove any fact supporting the prosecution case against the appellants. Ref: 2026 YLR 864; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recovery Without Private Witnesses: s. 103 CrPC
records.heading: Recovery without local witnesses violates section 103 CrPC and is unreliable
records.text: Recovery of a pillow was not relied upon because the Investigating Officer joined no local witness, violating s. 103 CrPC, so the evidence was obtained through illegal means and hit by the exclusionary rule. Other circumstances, including recovery about five months after the occurrence, showed a sham recovery. Ref: 2026 YLR 864; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof and Art. 122 QSO
records.heading: The burden in a criminal case lies on the prosecution and never shifts
records.text: In a criminal case the burden lies on the prosecution and never shifts, save for statutory exceptions. Art. 122 QSO is meant for facts especially within the accused's knowledge and cannot relieve the prosecution of its duty. An accused cannot be convicted merely for failing to explain how the deceased died. Ref: 2026 YLR 864; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Extra-Judicial Confession: Weak Evidence
records.heading: An extra-judicial confession is very weak evidence needing strong independent corroboration
records.text: Extra-judicial confession is a very weak type of evidence and needs impartial and strong corroboration from independent sources. Ref: 2026 YLR 864; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Delay in Recording s. 161 CrPC Statements
records.heading: Unexplained delay in recording a section 161 statement destroys its value
records.text: Delayed recording of a prosecution witness's statement under s. 161 CrPC reduces its value to nothing unless the delay is plausibly explained. No explanation was given here, so no value attached to the statement. Ref: 2026 YLR 864; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Report: Admissibility and Corroborative Value
records.heading: A DNA report is admissible and is highly corroborative evidence
records.text: A DNA report is per se admissible in evidence and is a high degree of corroborative evidence that plays a significant role in the safe administration of justice. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 875; Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 175-21).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 175-21)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: Weak Evidence
records.heading: Last seen evidence is weak unless corroborated by independent evidence
records.text: Last seen evidence is weak unless corroborated by independent evidence. Material contradictions between related last seen witnesses, and their absence from the FIR despite alleged earlier disclosure to the complainant, showed an afterthought and rendered the evidence highly doubtful. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 875; Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 175-21).
records.title: Muhammad Arif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 175-21)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Synthetic Milk: Laboratory Analysis Not Proved
records.heading: Conviction for synthetic milk requires proof of intent, production and laboratory analysis
records.text: To convict for preparing synthetic milk the prosecution must prove intent and active production. The seized material was not shown to have been sent to a laboratory for chemical analysis. The High Court gave the benefit of doubt, set aside the convictions and acquitted the accused. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 904; Sheraz and others v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 77776 of 2021).
records.title: Sheraz and others v. The State and others (Criminal Appeal No. 77776 of 2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Non-Production of Inmates of House of Occurrence
records.heading: Failure to produce the most natural witnesses supports an adverse inference
records.text: The deceased's children were admittedly residents of the place of occurrence and present at the time, yet neither the Investigating Officer nor the complainant produced them. Failure to produce these most natural witnesses led to the inference that they would not have supported the prosecution case. Ref: 2026 YLR 864; Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State.
records.title: Kashif Nouman alias Kashi v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Second FIR Order: Misuse of Process of Law
records.heading: Repeated attempts to register a second FIR cast doubt on the complainant's bona fides
records.text: A complainant's relentless attempts to bring the petitioner within criminal proceedings, starting afresh after the High Court suspended the earlier registration order, cast doubt on her bona fides. The Ex-officio Justice of Peace's order directing registration of a case was set aside. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 936; Muhammad Baber v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace.
records.title: Muhammad Baber v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Registration of Case Used to Malign Reputation
records.heading: Criminal proceedings must not be used to malign a person or settle scores
records.text: Criminal proceedings must not become a tool to malign or disgrace a person of distinguished reputation or to settle scores. The complainant had earlier conceded by affidavit that the allegations were mala fide, so the Ex-officio Justice of Peace's mechanical order directing registration was set aside. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 916; Muhammad Baber v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace.
records.title: Muhammad Baber v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Judicial Confession: Procedural Illegalities in Recording
records.heading: A confession recorded without the required safeguards is excluded and cannot corroborate other evidence
records.text: The Magistrate gave only one warning and opportunity for reflection and no assurance that the accused would not be returned to police, with no second warning. Such a confession, retracted at trial, was excluded, and one tainted piece of evidence cannot corroborate another. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 824; Muhammad Dilawar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Dilawar v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Extra-Judicial Confession: Weak Evidence Needing Corroboration
records.heading: An uncorroborated extra-judicial confession cannot support conviction on a capital charge
records.text: Extra-judicial confession is a weak type of evidence and is not sufficient for conviction on a capital charge unless strongly corroborated by unimpeachable tangible evidence. The sole testimony of the complainant's brother, who gave no reason for the confession, did not inform police and was uncorroborated, was not relied upon. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 824; Muhammad Dilawar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Dilawar v. State

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Identification of Dead Body Not Established
records.heading: Failure to identify the dead body makes the prosecution story hearsay
records.text: The body was buried under police supervision and the complainant learned of the death only by seeing photographs at the police station. No effort was made to identify the body, so the story was hearsay and nothing connected the appellants with the offence. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 824; Muhammad Dilawar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Dilawar v. State

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Judicial Confession Contradicted by Evidence
records.heading: A confession contradicted by the evidence and unsupported by independent proof is excluded
records.text: A s. 164 CrPC confession placed the occurrence in a cricket ground not near the place of occurrence, and the postmortem showed no firearm injury to the head as described. It was involuntary, untrue, not recorded in accordance with law and unsupported by independent evidence, so it was excluded. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 824; Muhammad Dilawar v. State.
records.title: Muhammad Dilawar v. State

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Compromise Affecting Minor: Directions to Courts
records.heading: A compromise waiving a minor's future rights is void and needs welfare findings
records.text: Directions issued to courts receiving compromises between parents concerning a minor: a clause waiving the minor's future maintenance or future inheritance rights is void and no bar to future claims. No compromise may be accepted solely on parents' consent, and the Court must independently find the welfare of the child served and record reasons. Ref: Muhammad Waleed Arshad v. District Judge, etc. (Writ Petition No. 54280 of 2022, decided 03.06.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Waleed Arshad v. District Judge, etc. (Writ Petition No. 54280 of 2022, decided 03.06.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 512 CrPC: Evidence Against Absconding Accused
records.heading: Section 512 CrPC evidence against an absconder needs prior proof of the witness's unavailability
records.text: S. 512 CrPC is a special provision and evidence recorded in an absconder's absence is admissible only if the prosecution first proves the witness is dead, incapable of giving evidence or cannot be produced without unreasonable delay or expense. Chapter 15, Part-B, Vol. III of the High Court Rules and Orders requires medical testimony in fatal cases. Ref: 2026 LHC 3617; Taj Din v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal-318-22, decided 09.06.2026); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Taj Din v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal-318-22, decided 09.06.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Exhibiting Documents Through Counsel's Statement
records.heading: Documents cannot be exhibited through a statement of counsel
records.text: Documents cannot be exhibited through the statement of counsel, and mere tendering does not dispense with proof under the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 through competent witnesses. Ref: 2016 LHC 4887; Muhammad Tufail (deceased) through Legal Heirs v. Hawaldar Nek Muhammad (RFA No. 108 of 2016).
records.title: Muhammad Tufail (deceased) through Legal Heirs v. Hawaldar Nek Muhammad (RFA No. 108 of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Cheque: s. 118 NIA Presumption of Consideration
records.heading: Admitted execution of a cheque raises the presumption of consideration under section 118 NIA
records.text: Once execution of a cheque is admitted or proved, the presumption of consideration under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 arises, even for a blank signed cheque voluntarily handed over. A bare denial cannot dislodge the claim. Legal representatives are liable to the extent of the estate inherited. Ref: 2016 LHC 4887; Muhammad Tufail (deceased) through Legal Heirs v. Hawaldar Nek Muhammad (RFA No. 108 of 2016).
records.title: Muhammad Tufail (deceased) through Legal Heirs v. Hawaldar Nek Muhammad (RFA No. 108 of 2016)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Supreme Court Directions on Trial Timelines
records.heading: Trials under the Illegal Dispossession Act must be completed within sixty days
records.text: Relying on Arts. 10-A and 187 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court directed all courts under the Illegal Dispossession Act to complete trials within 60 days under s. 5(2), keep a day-to-day order sheet and record reasons for any adjournment. The Trial Court must proceed despite a challenge to an interim order unless restrained by a higher forum. Ref: Raja Khan v. Suhail Arif Shah and another (Crl.P.L.A. 818/2026, decided 25.05.2026); Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail.
records.title: Raja Khan v. Suhail Arif Shah and another (Crl.P.L.A. 818/2026, decided 25.05.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Nature and Abuse of Process
records.heading: Khula is a complete dissolution and resisting it through baseless litigation abuses process
records.text: Khula affords a woman a lawful exit from marriage, with the wife forgoing dower in whole or in part. Once the Court is satisfied that reconciliation is not feasible and the wife's need is genuine, khula operates as a complete dissolution, and resisting it through false or baseless litigation abuses the process of court. Ref: Sultan v. Mst. Roshi Zeb & others (C.P.L.A. 303-P/2018, decided 04.06.2026); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Sultan v. Mst. Roshi Zeb & others (C.P.L.A. 303-P/2018, decided 04.06.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Safeguards for Women's Inheritance Rights
records.heading: Compromises affecting female heirs' inheritance need heightened scrutiny and strict proof of voluntariness
records.text: Courts and revenue authorities must apply heightened scrutiny to any compromise, relinquishment, gift, mutation or instrument affecting female heirs' inheritance. No presumption of validity arises from execution, attestation, registration or mutation without strict proof of voluntariness, and the burden lies heavily on the beneficiary of the transaction. Ref: Mst. Bibi Amina and others v. Shamsullah and others (C.P.L.A. 143-Q of 2025, decided 04.06.2026).
records.title: Mst. Bibi Amina and others v. Shamsullah and others (C.P.L.A. 143-Q of 2025, decided 04.06.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal of Suit
records.heading: Withdrawal simpliciter is an absolute right while withdrawal with liberty is discretionary
records.text: Withdrawal simpliciter under O. XXIII R. 1(1) CPC is an absolute right of the plaintiff and needs no permission. Withdrawal with permission to file a fresh suit under R. 1(2) is discretionary, and the Court must be satisfied of a formal defect or sufficient grounds. Ref: 2026 LHC 3734; IGI Insurance Limited v. Zaiba Amir & 6 others (R.F.A. No. 2876 of 2024).
records.title: IGI Insurance Limited v. Zaiba Amir & 6 others (R.F.A. No. 2876 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: No Extra-Judicial Harm or Torture of Accused
records.heading: No society under the rule of law can countenance torture of an accused
records.text: No society governed by the rule of law can countenance extra-judicial harm, torture or coercion of an accused. Human dignity, due process and fair trial apply irrespective of the gravity of the allegation, and guilt is determined only by a competent court, never by force or extra-legal methods. Ref: Moazam v. The State & another (Crl. Misc. No. 31715-B/2026); Justice Farooq Haider; Justice Ali Zia Bajwa.
records.title: Moazam v. The State & another (Crl. Misc. No. 31715-B/2026)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Punjab Anti-Corruption Rules 2014: Dropping Inquiry or Case
records.heading: The Punjab Anti-Corruption Rules 2014 provide for dropping unsubstantiated inquiries and cases
records.text: Under Rule 6(6) of the Punjab Anti-Corruption Rules, 2014 an inquiry is dropped if allegations are not substantiated, with referral for departmental action where warranted. Under Rule 10(1) a registered case found unestablished is dropped, with referral after the court confirms the cancellation report. The judgment considers the relation between Rule 24.7 of the Police Rules, 1934 and Rule 10. Ref: 2026 LHC 3781; Muhammad Bilal v. The State and 04 others (Criminal Revision No. 101 of 2026, decided 09.06.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Bilal v. The State and 04 others (Criminal Revision No. 101 of 2026, decided 09.06.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Strict Proof in Narcotics Cases; Malkhana Deficiencies
records.heading: The seriousness of narcotics offences does not dilute the standard of strict proof
records.text: Seriousness of narcotics offences does not dilute the standard of proof, and given harsh punishments courts must insist on strict proof of recovery, custody, sampling, transmission and conscious possession. The Court criticised non-production of Malkhana record, unexplained delay in sample transmission and casual destruction proceedings, and directed circulation of the observations. Ref: Mehmood Khan and others v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1544 of 2025).
records.title: Mehmood Khan and others v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1544 of 2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Secret Cavities in Vehicle: Proof by Vehicle or Photographs
records.heading: Narcotics from secret vehicle cavities need proof by the vehicle or photographs
records.text: Recovery of narcotics from secret cavities of a vehicle cannot be accepted on oral testimony alone. The prosecution should produce the vehicle or clear photographs showing the cavities open and closed, their location and the registration number. Failure to do so creates a serious lacuna when concealment is the foundation of the charge. Ref: Alam Khan v. State (Criminal Petition No. 51 of 2023, decided 09.06.2026).
records.title: Alam Khan v. State (Criminal Petition No. 51 of 2023, decided 09.06.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence and Burden under Art. 117 QSO
records.heading: The presumption of innocence is displaced only by lawful evidence proving guilt beyond doubt
records.text: A criminal case begins with the presumption of innocence, displaced only by lawful evidence proving guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Under Art. 117 QSO the burden lies on the prosecution throughout, and a reasonable doubt benefits the accused as of right. In a death sentence case the Court must independently reappraise guilt and sentence. Ref: Younas Masih v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1042/2025, decided 12.05.2026); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Younas Masih v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1042/2025, decided 12.05.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Recording Evidence Through Video Link
records.heading: A trial court may record a witness's evidence by video link where circumstances require
records.text: The Punjab Witnesses Protection Act, 2018 (s. 10) read with Art. 164 QSO allows the trial Court to record a witness through video link where circumstances require. The complainant's petition was allowed, the impugned order set aside and the trial Court directed to record her evidence by video link. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 493; Zubaida Khanam v. The State and 05 others (Criminal Revision No. 66407 of 2025).
records.title: Zubaida Khanam v. The State and 05 others (Criminal Revision No. 66407 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI CPC: Second Application for List of Witnesses
records.heading: A second application for a witness list is not maintainable if the first failed
records.text: A second application for submission of a witness list under O. XVI CPC is not maintainable where the first was dismissed and not challenged. O. XVI R. 14 is the Court's discretionary suo motu power, not a device for a party to fill gaps in evidence or cure non-compliance with R. 1. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 488; Malik Muhammad Irshad Faiz v. Khadim Hussain (Civil Revision-507-22).
records.title: Malik Muhammad Irshad Faiz v. Khadim Hussain (Civil Revision-507-22)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Attachment of Absconder's Property: s. 88 CrPC
records.heading: Section 88 CrPC attachment must not harass others and co-sharers' shares need demarcation
records.text: Property of an absconding accused can be attached, but s. 88 CrPC is not to be used to harass others. Auction of the whole property to the detriment of co-sharers without demarcating their shares should not have been ordered, and once an order is passed the Magistrate is functus officio. Petition accepted. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 501; Ghulam Abbas v. Muhammad Ijaz (Crl. Misc. 27723/25).
records.title: Ghulam Abbas v. Muhammad Ijaz (Crl. Misc. 27723/25)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Torture and Custodial Death Act 2022: Investigation by FIA
records.heading: Only the FIA may investigate complaints under the Torture and Custodial Death Act 2022
records.text: Under s. 5 of the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act, 2022 only the FIA is empowered, to the exclusion of other agencies, to investigate complaints against public officials, under the supervision of the National Commission for Human Rights. Custodial rape is investigated by the FIA, with the Anti-rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021 given secondary applicability. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 514; Zubaida Bibi v. District Police Officer and 02 others (Writ Petition No. 4926-HB of 2025).
records.title: Zubaida Bibi v. District Police Officer and 02 others (Writ Petition No. 4926-HB of 2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Appeal Against Acquittal by Special Judge
records.heading: An appeal against acquittal by a Special Judge needs the Federal Government's direction
records.text: Where a Special Judge has acquitted, under s. 10(2) of the Pakistan Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958 the Public Prosecutor can appeal only with the Federal Government's direction. Under s. 439(5) CrPC, if an appeal is available and none is filed, revision is not to be entertained. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 511; Vishal Ahmad Shakir v. Mian Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif etc (39801/26).
records.title: Vishal Ahmad Shakir v. Mian Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif etc (39801/26)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Passport of Accused: s. 28-A ATA
records.heading: Regulation of an accused's passport under section 28-A ATA lies with the ATC alone
records.text: Authority to regulate an accused's passport under s. 28-A of the Anti-Terrorism Act, including permission to travel abroad, lies exclusively with the ATC seized of the matter. An order based on a law officer's concession beyond his mandate raises no estoppel. The appeal was allowed and the impugned order set aside. Ref: PLD 2026 Lahore 528; F.O.P v. Sheikh Rasheed Ahmed (ICA Criminal-76-25).
records.title: F.O.P v. Sheikh Rasheed Ahmed (ICA Criminal-76-25)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Suit under s. 77 Registration Act; Death of Principal
records.heading: A section 77 Registration Act suit is confined to the legality of refusal of registration
records.text: A suit under s. 77 of the Registration Act, 1908 is confined to the legality of refusal of registration, not title. A power of attorney ends on the principal's death under s. 201 of the Contract Act, so refusal of registration was lawful. Dismissal of such a suit does not bar an independent suit for specific performance. Ref: 2026 LHC 3741; Muhammad Shafique etc v. Muhammad Shabbir etc (Civil Revision 1378-15, decided 04.06.2026); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Muhammad Shafique etc v. Muhammad Shabbir etc (Civil Revision 1378-15, decided 04.06.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Decree for Declaration: Not Executable under O. XXI
records.heading: A declaratory decree is executed through the revenue officer, not under Order XXI
records.text: A decree for declaration cannot be executed in the ordinary manner under Order XXI CPC. It must be presented to the revenue officer for attestation of mutation and incorporation in the revenue record under s. 42 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967, and the revenue authorities are bound to act upon it. Ref: 2026 LHC 3759; Muhammad Rafique etc v. Province of Punjab etc (W.P. 2857/2019, decided 08.06.2026); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Rafique etc v. Province of Punjab etc (W.P. 2857/2019, decided 08.06.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Ss. 371-A, 371-B PPC: Further Inquiry and Private Raid
records.heading: Mere presence of a man and woman does not attract sections 371-A and 371-B
records.text: Mere presence of a man and woman in private premises does not attract ss. 371-A and 371-B PPC without material showing trafficking, sale, hiring or commercial sexual exploitation. The case was one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. A police raid on a dwelling house without a warrant or respectable witnesses raised concerns under Arts. 4, 9 and 14 of the Constitution. Consensual fornication could only be prosecuted by complaint under s. 203-C CrPC. Ref: Noor Muhammad v. The State, etc. (Cr.M No. 326-A of 2026).
records.title: Noor Muhammad v. The State, etc. (Cr.M No. 326-A of 2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
