records.topic: Succession Certificate Statement Not Bar to Inheritance Claim
records.heading: A conceding statement in succession certificate proceedings does not surrender a sister's share
records.text: A conceding statement made in succession certificate proceedings does not surrender the sister's share in her father's property. Such proceedings are summary and cannot decide disputed title, which must be determined by a civil court of plenary jurisdiction, whose finding binds the court granting the certificate. The appellate court's preliminary decree of partition was left undisturbed. Ref: 2026 MLD 1001; Muhammad Irfan Butt etc v. Aliya Nawaz Butt (Civil Revision 13153/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan Butt etc v. Aliya Nawaz Butt (Civil Revision 13153/2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Reinstatement Restores Seniority and Benefits
records.heading: Reinstatement of a dismissed employee restores seniority and other benefits
records.text: When a dismissed or terminated employee is reinstated, his seniority, privileges and other benefits are also restored. The Court considered seniority of police officers under R. 12.2(3) and R. 12.24 of the Police Rules, 1934. No ground was found to interfere with the Service Tribunal's judgment and the Government's civil appeals were dismissed. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 404; The Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary Government of Sindh & others v. Raj Kumar Lohana & others (C.A. 53-K/2024).
records.title: The Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary Government of Sindh & others v. Raj Kumar Lohana & others (C.A. 53-K/2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Bridal Property Vests Absolutely in Wife
records.heading: Property given to a woman at marriage for personal use vests absolutely in her
records.text: Property given to a woman at marriage for her personal use vests absolutely in her, and ownership turns on the intention of the transfer rather than its name. Unauthorised retention by the husband or his family is unlawful withholding, recoverable before the Family Court, which has exclusive jurisdiction over dowry and the personal property of a wife under s. 5 and the Schedule of the Act of 1964. Ref: Ghulam Habib v. Mst. Shazia and others (C.P.L.A. 5432/2025, decided 04.05.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Ghulam Habib v. Mst. Shazia and others (C.P.L.A. 5432/2025, decided 04.05.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness to Pay
records.heading: Failure to show readiness and willingness to pay the balance defeats specific performance
records.text: A suit for specific performance must satisfy Forms 47 and 48 of Appendix A to the First Schedule CPC. A purchaser who does not show readiness and willingness to pay the balance consideration has no cause of action, and failure to comply with a direction to deposit it renders the pleading of readiness untrue. The trial court rightly dismissed the suit under O. XVII R. 3 CPC. Ref: Amjad Javed v. Maqsood Ahmad, etc. (C.A. 173-L/2020, decided 14.05.2026); Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Amjad Javed v. Maqsood Ahmad, etc. (C.A. 173-L/2020, decided 14.05.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inculpatory Statement under S. 342 CrPC
records.heading: Section 342 CrPC statement: inculpatory part may be read when exculpatory part is false
records.text: A statement under s. 342 CrPC is accepted or rejected as a whole, but where the prosecution evidence is reliable and the exculpatory part is shown false and excluded, the inculpatory part may be read in support of the prosecution. A s. 342 statement is more reliable than a s. 164 judicial confession, as duress is less probable. Ref: Fateh Sher v. The State (J.P. 131/2015, decided 09.06.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Fateh Sher v. The State (J.P. 131/2015, decided 09.06.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 7 CPC: Moulding of Relief
records.heading: Order VII Rule 7 CPC allows moulding of relief flowing from pleadings and proved facts
records.text: O. VII R. 7 CPC allows the court to grant relief not specifically prayed for, known as moulding of relief. The power is an exception to the rule that parties are bound by pleadings. The relief must flow from the pleadings and proved facts, must not surprise or prejudice the other side, and cannot change the nature of the suit itself. Ref: Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary Forest/Environment Department Peshawar & others v. Sher Mohammad & others (C.A. 328/2018, decided 14.05.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary Forest/Environment Department Peshawar & others v. Sher Mohammad & others (C.A. 328/2018, decided 14.05.2026)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: FIO 2001: Auction, S. 15 Struck Down, Objections
records.heading: Questions on auction without sale deed and effect of striking down section 15 FIO 2001
records.text: Authority on the legal effect of an auction held without execution and registration of a sale deed where the Bank never took possession, the consequence of the striking down of s. 15 of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001, and the scope of objection proceedings before the Banking Court. The post gives only the questions and no holding. Ref: Zarai Taraqiati Bank Ltd., Islamabad v. Sher Muhammad, etc (C.A. 232-L/2017, decided 17.06.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Zarai Taraqiati Bank Ltd., Islamabad v. Sher Muhammad, etc (C.A. 232-L/2017, decided 17.06.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Bridal Gifts Are Wife's Property
records.heading: Bridal gifts belong to the wife and the husband cannot subtract from them
records.text: Bridal gifts given to the wife at the time of marriage are also her property. The husband may add to them but cannot subtract from them. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 269.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Bridal Gifts: Husband's Suit for Recovery Vexatious
records.heading: Bridal gifts vest absolutely in the bride and a husband's recovery suit is vexatious
records.text: Barri or bridal gifts given to the bride by the bridegroom and his parents vest unconditionally and absolutely in her. A suit by the bridegroom to recover them raised no material proposition of law or fact requiring issues and evidence, and its continuation was oppressive and vexatious to the bride. Ref: 2025 CLC 937.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Executing Court Bound by Decree: Maintenance Enhancement
records.heading: An executing court must execute the decree as it stands and cannot vary it
records.text: An executing court must execute the decree as it stands and cannot vary or enlarge it. An annual escalation cannot be applied retrospectively to past maintenance already quantified, absent clear language. S. 17-A of the Family Courts Act supplies the mechanism for computing annual increase where the decree provides for enhancement without specifying the method. Ref: 2026 LHC 3857; Rana Tasneem Ijaz through Mehmood Ijaz v. Sadia Abbas etc (W.P. 12390/2026, decided 11.06.2026).
records.title: Rana Tasneem Ijaz through Mehmood Ijaz v. Sadia Abbas etc (W.P. 12390/2026, decided 11.06.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Suits on Citizenship Status: NADRA Preconditions
records.heading: A civil suit on citizenship status requires NADRA's order to be attached
records.text: No civil suit is entertainable on a status question unless NADRA's order, including that of the NADRA Verification Board, is attached, and in doubtful cases documentary proof of status before 1979 under Rule 20(3) of the NADRA (National Identity Card) Rules, 2002. Pending cases get 30 days to comply, failing which plaint is rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC. Parties must first exhaust appeals under NADRA laws. Ref: 2026 LHC 3864; NADRA v. Khalid Khan etc (Civil Revision 106767/2017, decided 18.05.2026); Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani.
records.title: NADRA v. Khalid Khan etc (Civil Revision 106767/2017, decided 18.05.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Teacher Accused of Abusing Student: Bail Refused, School Safety Directions
records.heading: Bail refused to a teacher accused of abusing a minor student, with school safety directions
records.text: The Lahore High Court dismissed the bail of a teacher accused of sexually abusing a minor student inside a school. It directed the Punjab Government to review school safety, vet all staff through police and NADRA records including a Police Character Certificate, install CCTV linked to Safe City, and consider legal responsibility of school owners and principals for lapses in reporting abuse. Ref: Shan Ali alias Zeeshan v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 4453/B/2025).
records.title: Shan Ali alias Zeeshan v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 4453/B/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 10(5) Family Courts Act: 25% Dower Relinquishment
records.heading: The Federal Shariat Court annulled section 10(5) but its decision is suspended pending appeal
records.text: The Federal Shariat Court annulled s. 10(5) and (6) of the Act of 1964 from 1 May 2022, but under Art. 203D(2) proviso its decision does not take effect until the appeal period ends or any appeal is decided, and an appeal was filed under Art. 203F. The dower being prompt dower, the petitioner was bound to relinquish twenty-five percent under s. 10(5). Ref: Mst. Azka Afreen v. Hafiz Umar Yasin etc (W.P. 1221/2022, decided 09.06.2026); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Mst. Azka Afreen v. Hafiz Umar Yasin etc (W.P. 1221/2022, decided 09.06.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conviction on Unedited Video Despite Failed Ocular Account
records.heading: Conviction may rest on an unedited video despite failure of the ocular account
records.text: Failure of the ocular account does not entitle the accused to acquittal, as they may be convicted to the extent of the incident established by an unedited video. A photogrammetric test is needed only where identity is disputed, and is redundant when the defence admits the accused's presence and identity in the video. Conviction was upheld for an involuntary gunshot during a struggle. Ref: 2026 LHC 3900; Muhammad Azam etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 67344/2022, decided 23.06.2026); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Muhammad Azam etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 67344/2022, decided 23.06.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Ashura Processions and Majalis: Licence Only on Peace Threat
records.heading: A licence for a Muharram procession is needed only on a peace threat
records.text: A licence for a Muharram procession is needed only if the police judge it a threat to peace. The Court held that the State, while entitled to regulate assemblies, should adopt a participatory approach in facilitating mourning rituals and public servants should support any citizen holding a majlis or procession. Ref: 2026 LHC 3946; Syed Wasi Haider v. CPO etc (W.P. 7251/2026, decided 19.06.2026); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Syed Wasi Haider v. CPO etc (W.P. 7251/2026, decided 19.06.2026)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Evidence Corroborative, Not Substantive
records.heading: DNA evidence is corroborative, and conviction cannot rest on it alone
records.text: DNA evidence is corroborative and a conviction cannot rest on corroborative material alone. Ref: 2026 LHC 3967; Ghulam Fareed v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 200/2021); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ghulam Fareed v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 200/2021)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Consent and Bar on Converting Rape into Fornication
records.heading: A criminal court assesses consent independently and cannot convert rape into fornication
records.text: A jactitation decree does not stop the criminal court from independently assessing consent, which is an essential element under s. 375 PPC. A prosecution must be tried within the framework of the offence charged, and s. 5A of the Zina Ordinance, 1979 bars conversion between zina, rape and fornication. Conviction cannot be maintained on a different factual premise once absence of consent is not proved. Ref: 2026 LHC 3967; Ghulam Fareed v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 200/2021); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Ghulam Fareed v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 200/2021)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Armed Forces Officer: Forced Retirement and Art. 199(3) Bar
records.heading: Article 199(3) bars service petitions by armed forces officers unless the order is mala fide
records.text: Art. 199(3) bars a constitutional petition on service matters of armed forces officers unless the order is mala fide, without jurisdiction or coram non judice. S. 18 of the Pakistan Army Act, 1952 and Rules 12 and 9C of the Army Act Rules, 1954 empower the Federal Government to retire an officer compulsorily. An officer drawing pension on that basis cannot later challenge it, and the petition was held not maintainable. Ref: Major (R) Muhammad Khurshid Asghar v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence, etc (Intra Court Appeal 116/2019, heard 17.06.2026).
records.title: Major (R) Muhammad Khurshid Asghar v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of Defence, etc (Intra Court Appeal 116/2019, heard 17.06.2026)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-i-Muwathibat: Registration Is Not Deemed Knowledge
records.heading: Registration of a sale deed is not deemed knowledge for talb-i-muwathibat
records.text: Registration of a sale deed is not treated as knowledge for talb-i-muwathibat, since the statute makes actual acquisition of knowledge decisive and the legislature has not provided for constructive knowledge. Introducing deemed knowledge would rewrite pre-emption law. Raising verbal cross objections at the revisional stage should be discouraged. Ref: 2026 YLR 1284; Muhammad Bashir etc v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 111/2014).
records.title: Muhammad Bashir etc v. Muhammad Rafique (Civil Revision 111/2014)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: S. 161 Statement of Critically Injured: Not Dying Declaration
records.heading: A section 161 statement of a critically injured person was not a dying declaration
records.text: Where the record showed the injured, later deceased, was critical, under anaesthesia and in intensive care, the investigating officer's claim of recording his s. 161 CrPC statement outside the emergency ward was disbelieved, particularly with no permission or attestation from the Medical Officer. The statement was neither a dying declaration nor credible and was of no avail to the prosecution. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1051; Nauman Ijaz v. The State (Jail Appeal 30048/2022).
records.title: Nauman Ijaz v. The State (Jail Appeal 30048/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Forged Bail Bonds: No FIR, Proceed under S. 195 CrPC
records.heading: Forged bail bonds call for proceedings under section 195 CrPC, not an FIR
records.text: Filing of forged bail bonds does not warrant an FIR. S. 205 PPC is non-cognizable and listed in s. 195(1)(b) CrPC, so only the court concerned can take cognizance, including on the application of the Reader or Ahlmad. Documents prepared during proceedings under court orders and found forged fall within s. 195(1)(b) or (c). Abettors can at most be charged under s. 109 read with s. 205 PPC. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1037; Tabinda Adnan & 2 others v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 77218/2024).
records.title: Tabinda Adnan & 2 others v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 77218/2024)

records.subject: Cheque Dishonour (s. 489-F PPC)
records.topic: S. 489-F PPC: Ingredients and Burden on Prosecution
records.heading: Section 489-F PPC requires proof of dishonest issuance of a cheque and its dishonour
records.text: S. 489-F PPC applies only where the prosecution proves dishonest issuance of a cheque to repay a loan or fulfil an obligation, and its dishonour on presentation. Not every dishonoured cheque is an offence. The complainant failed to prove the essential ingredient, and a single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1175; Shamim Aslam v. The State etc (Criminal Revision 272/2025).
records.title: Shamim Aslam v. The State etc (Criminal Revision 272/2025)

records.subject: Cyber Crime (PECA)
records.topic: WhatsApp Group Administrator: Criminal Liability for Posts
records.heading: A WhatsApp group administrator is not criminally liable merely for members' posts
records.text: Mere creation or administration of a WhatsApp group does not make the administrator criminally liable for members' posts, and vicarious liability cannot be inferred from administrative status. Liability may arise where the group is created for an unlawful purpose, the administrator himself circulates or facilitates the content, or abets or intentionally participates, or a statutory duty exists. Silence alone is unsafe to treat as dissemination. Ref: 2026 LHC 3997; Syed Abdul Mannan v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 69895-B/2025).
records.title: Syed Abdul Mannan v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 69895-B/2025)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay and Correction of Clerical Error
records.heading: Condonation requires explanation of the entire delay, and clerical correction gives no fresh limitation
records.text: A party seeking condonation must explain the entire delay with a reasonable, bona fide explanation, and counsel's negligence or mistaken advice is not automatic sufficient cause. A correction of an accidental or clerical error that does not alter the adjudication on merits creates no fresh decree and no fresh starting point of limitation. Ref: 2026 LHC 4078; Muhammad Arshad v. Rashid Hameed Warraich (Civil Revision 12456/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Arshad v. Rashid Hameed Warraich (Civil Revision 12456/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Suit Against Dead Defendant: Void Ab Initio
records.heading: A suit against a defendant dead before filing is void ab initio
records.text: Where the sole defendant had died before the suit was filed, there was no defendant and the suit was void from inception. Plaintiffs' ignorance of the death is immaterial. O. I R. 10 and O. XXII CPC presuppose a validly instituted suit and cannot be used to bring legal heirs on record, so the defect is incurable and not mere misdescription or non-joinder. Ref: 2026 LHC 4092; Abdul Aziz (deceased) through his Legal Heirs v. Mst. Ayesha Bibi & others (Civil Revision 6103/2024).
records.title: Abdul Aziz (deceased) through his Legal Heirs v. Mst. Ayesha Bibi & others (Civil Revision 6103/2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Attorney Self-Dealing: Transfer to Relatives under GPA
records.heading: An attorney cannot transfer the principal's property to relatives without prior knowledge or authority
records.text: An attorney holds a fiduciary position and cannot transfer the principal's property to himself or his relatives without the principal's prior knowledge, consent or specific authority. A General Power of Attorney, however wide, does not by itself authorise such alienation. The beneficiary bears a heavy burden to prove express authority or informed ratification and bona fides. Ref: 2026 LHC 4099; Haider Aftab & others v. Dilawar Khan (deceased) through Legal Heirs & others (Civil Revision 31616/2025).
records.title: Haider Aftab & others v. Dilawar Khan (deceased) through Legal Heirs & others (Civil Revision 31616/2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay in Trial: Third Proviso to S. 497(1)
records.heading: Post-arrest bail is a right once the third proviso to section 497(1) is satisfied
records.text: The order sheets showed no design or pattern by the petitioners to delay the trial, and with the prerequisites of the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC met and no exception applicable, the petitioners were entitled to post-arrest bail as of right on the statutory ground of delay in concluding the trial. Ref: 2026 LHC 4127; Ghulam Rasool v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 3529-B/2026); Muhammad Jahangir v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 3737-B/2026).
records.title: Ghulam Rasool v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 3529-B/2026); Muhammad Jahangir v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. 3737-B/2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Female Heirs Excluded by Gift Mutation: Inheritance Restored
records.heading: A gift mutation excluding female heirs was set aside and their inheritance restored
records.text: The Supreme Court set aside the judgments of the lower courts and a 1955 gift mutation by which brothers excluded their mother and sisters, and ordered shares given to them. Inheritance is a legal and Shariah right of every heir that devolves on the death of the owner, and any transaction excluding a female heir demands utmost judicial scrutiny. Ref: Noor Mohammad, etc v. Ghulam Haider, etc (C.P.L.A. 1103-L/2016, decided 30.06.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Noor Mohammad, etc v. Ghulam Haider, etc (C.P.L.A. 1103-L/2016, decided 30.06.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Alleged Love Marriage versus Abduction: Evidence Approach
records.heading: Where a love marriage is pleaded against abduction, courts must inquire how the relationship began
records.text: Where a love marriage is pleaded against allegations of abduction or forced marriage and the parties are strangers, the court must inquire how the relationship began and matured into marriage. Proof through call records or messages is not required by law, but total absence of material explaining the genesis of the relationship is a relevant circumstance. Ref: 2026 LHC 4207; Muhmmad Jameel v. The ADJ etc (W.P. 6494/2025, decided 04.06.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhmmad Jameel v. The ADJ etc (W.P. 6494/2025, decided 04.06.2026)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Demarcation under Punjab Land Revenue Act: Remedies
records.heading: A demarcation under section 117 can be challenged by objection, correction, appeal and revision
records.text: A demarcation by a Revenue Officer under s. 117 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1967 can be challenged. An affected person may object during proceedings, seek correction before the Revenue Officer, appeal under s. 161 within limitation, and the revisional authority may examine legality and regularity under s. 164. Ref: 2026 LHC 4212; Raja Hafeez-ur-Rehman v. Member (Judicial-VI) etc (Writ Petition 161/2026, heard 30.06.2026).
records.title: Raja Hafeez-ur-Rehman v. Member (Judicial-VI) etc (Writ Petition 161/2026, heard 30.06.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Overseas Pakistanis Property Special Courts Act 2025: Object
records.heading: The Overseas Pakistanis Property Special Courts Act 2025 creates specialised forums with strict timelines
records.text: The Punjab Establishment of Special Courts (Overseas Pakistanis Property) Act, 2025 creates specialised forums for disputes over immovable property of overseas Pakistanis, with e-filing, video-link evidence and strict timelines. The preamble shows the mischief addressed and is a guide in construing the substantive provisions. Ref: 2026 LHC 4221; Javed Masih v. Amar Javed and others (Writ Petition 2345/2026, decided 24.06.2026).
records.title: Javed Masih v. Amar Javed and others (Writ Petition 2345/2026, decided 24.06.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Complaints Against Enforcement Authority Officials: Special Act Procedure
records.heading: Complaints against Enforcement Authority officials follow the procedure in the special Act
records.text: The petitioner's grievances concerned officers of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority, so the reported incident fell within the offences in Chapter XI (ss. 24 to 47) of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulation Act, 2024. That special Act provides its own procedure, including ss. 16, 49 and 53, for representation, complaint and registration of cases against delinquent officials. Ref: 2026 LHC 4390; Muhammad Kamran v. Ex-officio Justice of Peace/Additional Sessions Judge, Multan and seven others (Writ Petition 6909/2026, heard 16.06.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Kamran v. Ex-officio Justice of Peace/Additional Sessions Judge, Multan and seven others (Writ Petition 6909/2026, heard 16.06.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Pension Cannot Be Withheld on Audit Objection Alone
records.heading: Pension cannot be withheld on a mere audit objection or unproved allegation
records.text: Pension, gratuity and retirement benefits cannot be withheld on a mere audit objection, inquiry, FIR or unproved allegation. Pension is a vested right earned by service, an audit objection is no final proof of fault, and due process is required before withholding. The respondent was deprived of pensionary benefits merely on an audit objection. Ref: 2026 LHC 4268; Zarai Taraqiati Bank Ltd. v. Athar Tabraiz and another (ICA 24175/2026, heard 29.04.2026).
records.title: Zarai Taraqiati Bank Ltd. v. Athar Tabraiz and another (ICA 24175/2026, heard 29.04.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 31 CPC: Duty of First Appellate Court
records.heading: The first appellate court must independently reappraise evidence under Order XLI Rule 31
records.text: The first appellate court must independently frame points for determination, reappraise the evidence and record its own reasoned findings under O. XLI R. 31 CPC. Mere concurrence with the trial court is no substitute. Failure is a jurisdictional infirmity warranting interference in revision, and the case is remanded to the first appellate court. Ref: Riaz Ahmad Khan (deceased) through Legal Heirs & others v. Rafique Ahmad Khan & others (Civil Revision 30580/2019).
records.title: Riaz Ahmad Khan (deceased) through Legal Heirs & others v. Rafique Ahmad Khan & others (Civil Revision 30580/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 64 CPC: Transfer After Attachment; S. 12(2) No Automatic Stay
records.heading: A private transfer after attachment is void against the decree-holder under section 64 CPC
records.text: Once an attachment is operative, the judgment-debtor cannot create interests in the attached property, and a private transfer after attachment is void against the decree-holder under the principle of s. 64 CPC. Pendency of s. 12(2) CPC proceedings does not automatically stay the decree or execution, which continues unless a competent court restrains it. Ref: 2026 LHC 4435; Ehtasham Haider & 2 others v. Additional District Judge etc (W.P. 27447/2026, decided 29.06.2026); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Ehtasham Haider & 2 others v. Additional District Judge etc (W.P. 27447/2026, decided 29.06.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Appointment of Employee's Child: Accrued Right Survives Rule Omission
records.heading: The accrued right of appointment of an employee's child survived omission of the rule
records.text: The father, a Naib Qasid, retired on medical grounds on 17.08.2009 and the right of appointment for his child accrued then, well before the rule was omitted on 24.07.2024. The accrued right could not be taken away, and the Ombudsman's order and the Governor's appeal order upholding it were lawful and binding on the Board. Ref: 2026 LHC 4459; The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Rawalpindi v. Governor of Punjab, etc (Writ Petition 3540/2024, decided 16.06.2026).
records.title: The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Rawalpindi v. Governor of Punjab, etc (Writ Petition 3540/2024, decided 16.06.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Duty to Summon or Recall Witness
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC makes it obligatory to summon a witness whose evidence is essential
records.text: S. 540 CrPC makes it obligatory to summon or recall a witness where the evidence is essential to a just decision, unless it risks miscarriage of justice. Under Art. 161 QSO the Judge may ask any question to discover proof. The trial court cannot remain unconcerned, and an application for additional evidence cannot be summarily dismissed on the ground that the witness was not earlier produced. Ref: 2026 LHC 4471; Muhammad Hanif v. The State and other (Criminal Revision 144/2026, heard 23.06.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. The State and other (Criminal Revision 144/2026, heard 23.06.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 516-A CrPC: Interim Custody of Converted Property
records.heading: Converted case property is restored to the accused absent tentative incriminating material
records.text: Converted case property cannot be treated as case property on the Investigating Officer's assertion alone, and without tentative incriminating material it is restored to the accused. Interim custody, interim disposal and superdari are used interchangeably, and 'any property' in s. 516-A CrPC covers converted property. The court decides on a tentative assessment of the record. Ref: 2026 LHC 4480; Nisar Ahmad Khan v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 3189/2026, decided 01.06.2026); Justice Tariq Mahmood Bajwa.
records.title: Nisar Ahmad Khan v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 3189/2026, decided 01.06.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Oversight in Producing Bank Documents Not Lacuna
records.heading: Inadvertent failure to produce bank documents is an oversight, not a lacuna
records.text: The object of s. 540 CrPC is to reach the truth in the interests of justice, and recalling a witness or bringing further documents on record is permitted and sometimes obligatory where needed for a just decision. Formally producing, through a bank witness, documents already part of the investigation was held an inadvertent oversight, not a lacuna, which the court may correct under s. 540. Ref: 2026 LHC 4471; Muhammad Hanif v. The State and other (Criminal Revision 144/2026, heard 23.06.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Hanif v. The State and other (Criminal Revision 144/2026, heard 23.06.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Recital of Property Transfer Not Proof of Payment
records.heading: A Nikahnama recital of property transfer does not prove payment or transfer
records.text: A recital in Column 16 of the Nikahnama relating to transfer of immovable property cannot substitute for the legal requirements of transfer. Such transfer must be proved by duly executed instruments and revenue record entries, and absent these no presumption of payment or transfer arises. The appellate court erred in treating a bare recital as conclusive proof. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 448; Irshad Bibi v. ADJ (W.P. 6543/2022).
records.title: Irshad Bibi v. ADJ (W.P. 6543/2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay: Explanation for Each Day
records.heading: A party seeking condonation must explain each day of delay with cogent reasons
records.text: The party seeking condonation must explain each day of delay with cogent and legally sustainable reasons, since rights accruing to the opposite party by lapse of time cannot be lightly set aside. Sufficient cause is construed strictly and does not extend to negligence, inaction or lack of due diligence. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 439; Nasir Mehmood Wattoo v. Muhammad Naeem, etc. (R.F.A. 34392/2023).
records.title: Nasir Mehmood Wattoo v. Muhammad Naeem, etc. (R.F.A. 34392/2023)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Extrajudicial Confession in Unwitnessed Murder: Further Inquiry
records.heading: A belated extrajudicial confession in an unwitnessed murder justifies further inquiry
records.text: An extrajudicial confession is weak evidence requiring rigorous scrutiny. Where it surfaced belatedly through a supplementary statement over a month after the incident in an unwitnessed murder, the case was one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Liberty cannot be curtailed as pre-trial punishment merely because the offence is heinous. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 496; Muhammad Zakariya and 1 other v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 2105-B/2026).
records.title: Muhammad Zakariya and 1 other v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 2105-B/2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 152 CPC: Correction of Clerical or Arithmetical Errors
records.heading: Section 152 CPC permits correction of clerical or arithmetical errors in a signed judgment
records.text: Read with O. XX R. 3 CPC, s. 152 CPC is a statutory exception to the finality of a signed judgment, permitting correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes and errors from accidental slips or omissions. The scope of s. 152 is no longer res integra. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 341; Farid Khan and others v. Hamid Badshah and others (C.P.L.A. 4456/2022).
records.title: Farid Khan and others v. Hamid Badshah and others (C.P.L.A. 4456/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: No Blood Collected at Spot: Place of Occurrence
records.heading: Failure to collect blood from the place of occurrence is fatal to proving it
records.text: If the Investigating Officer did not collect blood from the stated place of occurrence on his first visit, it is fatal to proving the exact place of occurrence. Where the complainant says he told other witnesses of the specific roles he gave the accused in the FIR, a question mark is left on those witnesses' later testimony. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 522; Kashif @ Kashi v. The State (Jail Appeal 40664/2022).
records.title: Kashif @ Kashi v. The State (Jail Appeal 40664/2022)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Evidence: Science, STR Profiling and Case Law Survey
records.heading: Current legislation is insufficient to develop a DNA profiling system in Pakistan
records.text: A detailed judgment on DNA evidence setting out the science of DNA and STR profiling and surveying the law and the decisions of the superior courts. It concludes that current legislation is not enough to develop a DNA profiling system in Pakistan and that a dependable legal and scientific infrastructure is needed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 507, 2026 PCrLJ 1318; Muhammad Mujahid v. The State, etc. (Cr. Appeal 22958/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Mujahid v. The State, etc. (Cr. Appeal 22958/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unexplained Delay in Reporting to Police
records.heading: Unexplained delay in reporting to police raises suspicion, especially with related eyewitnesses
records.text: A delay of one hour and forty five minutes in reporting the matter, with the police station only 13 kilometres away and no plausible explanation, raises suspicion, particularly where the eyewitnesses are closely related to each other and the deceased. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 421, PLD 2026 Lah 649; Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Lambardar: Duties, Residence and No Vested Right to Appointment
records.heading: No individual has a vested right to appointment as Lambardar
records.text: The Lambardar performs quasi-administrative and fiscal duties under Rule 22 of the Punjab Land Revenue Rules, 1968, so effective physical presence and accessibility in the village are essential attributes of the office. No individual has a vested or enforceable right to appointment as Lambardar, and the revenue authorities choose a person in whom the State can repose confidence. Ref: PLJ 2026 FCC 1; Shaukat Ali v. Member (Judicial-III) (F.C.P.L.A. 487/2025).
records.title: Shaukat Ali v. Member (Judicial-III) (F.C.P.L.A. 487/2025)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Baldia Factory Fire: Death Sentences Set Aside
records.heading: Two death sentences in the Baldia factory fire case were set aside on appeal
records.text: The Supreme Court allowed the appeals of the two accused sentenced to death by the Anti-Terrorism Court in the Baldia factory fire case, set aside their convictions and acquitted them. The MQM's appeal seeking expunction of remarks was disposed of as infructuous, since remarks lapse once the judgment is set aside. Ref: Muhammad Zubair @ Chariya v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 178-K/2023, decided 10.06.2026); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Zubair @ Chariya v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 178-K/2023, decided 10.06.2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Disputing Landlord's Title: Surrender Possession First
records.heading: A tenant disputing the landlord's title must first surrender possession
records.text: A tenant who disputes the landlord's title must first surrender possession, as he is estopped from denying the landlord's title while retaining possession under the tenancy. A tenant claiming co-ownership by purchase of a share must seek partition in a civil court and cannot resist ejectment by raising disputed title before the Rent Controller. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 346; Nawab Khan & another v. Muhammad Yousaf & others (C.P.L.A. 806-P/2018).
records.title: Nawab Khan & another v. Muhammad Yousaf & others (C.P.L.A. 806-P/2018)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 295-A, 295-B, 295-C PPC and S. 11 PECA: Scope
records.heading: Section 196 CrPC restrains cognizance without complaint but does not bar an FIR
records.text: Discusses the scope and applicability of ss. 295-A, 295-B and 295-C PPC and s. 11 of PECA 2016, with reference to Arts. 29, 31 and 260(3) of the Constitution. S. 196 CrPC does not bar registration of an FIR and only restrains the court from taking cognizance without a complaint by the Federal or Provincial Government. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 457; Zaheer Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 27057/B/2021).
records.title: Zaheer Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 27057/B/2021)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delay in FIR and Post-Mortem Undermines Prosecution Case
records.heading: Unexplained delay in the FIR and post-mortem undermines the prosecution case
records.text: An unexplained delay of about 3 hours 50 minutes in reporting, with the police station 11 km away, shows deliberation and consultation. Noticeable delay in post-mortem suggests eyewitnesses were procured and nobody was present at the spot. A positive PFSA report on a hatchet examined 28 days later was inconsequential as the blood would have disintegrated. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 429; Muhammad Nazir & another v. The State, etc (Criminal Appeal 42209-J/2023); Abdul Razzaq v. The State, etc (Criminal Revision 31321/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Nazir & another v. The State, etc (Criminal Appeal 42209-J/2023); Abdul Razzaq v. The State, etc (Criminal Revision 31321/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Agent's Fiduciary Duty: Self-Serving Transactions
records.heading: An agent cannot deal with the principal's property for his own benefit without authority
records.text: An agent owes a fiduciary obligation and cannot lawfully deal with the principal's property for his own benefit or in favour of close relatives without the principal's prior knowledge, consent or specific authorisation. Any such self-serving transaction is liable to be repudiated. Ref: 2026 CLC 1104, PLJ 2025 Lahore 1043; Abdul Shakoor & others v. Ghulam Muhammad (deceased) through his Legal Heirs & others (Civil Revision No.950-D of 2025).
records.title: Abdul Shakoor & others v. Ghulam Muhammad (deceased) through his Legal Heirs & others (Civil Revision No.950-D of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Limits on Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings is refused if it changes the nature of the suit
records.text: The court has wide but judicial discretion under O. VI R. 17 CPC to allow amendment where necessary to decide the real controversy. Amendment should be refused if it changes the nature of the suit, withdraws admissions, is mala fide, causes irreparable prejudice, or aims to cure evidentiary deficiencies, and belated amendment attracts heightened scrutiny. Ref: Mehbub Ullah and another v. Mst. Taj Bibi and other (C.P.L.A. 5215/2024, decided 01.07.2026).
records.title: Mehbub Ullah and another v. Mst. Taj Bibi and other (C.P.L.A. 5215/2024, decided 01.07.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Documents: Art. 79 QSO, Scribe and Signature Comparison
records.heading: A scribe of an agreement to sell does not substitute for an attesting witness
records.text: In civil cases evidence is weighed on preponderance. A document is proved under Art. 79 QSO and omission to produce the scribe is not always fatal where attesting witnesses confirm the contents, though a scribe of an agreement to sell does not substitute for an attesting witness. Art. 84 QSO empowers the court to compare signatures and direct any person to write for comparison. Ref: 2026 CLC 1133; Ali Ahmed v. Zulfiqar Ali (Civil Revision 714/2017).
records.title: Ali Ahmed v. Zulfiqar Ali (Civil Revision 714/2017)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Jactitation of Marriage: Proof and Registration of Nikah
records.heading: A jactitation decree was maintained where the Nikah was neither registered nor proved
records.text: A suit for jactitation of marriage seeks a declaration that no valid marriage exists and perpetual silence against a false claim. Where the Nikah was neither registered without credible explanation nor proved through trustworthy evidence, the jactitation decree was maintained and leave refused. Muslim marriages must be registered, and a registered Nikahnama is a public record with probative value. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 352, 2026 SCMR 1401; Muhammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor & others (C.P.L.A. 5626/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor & others (C.P.L.A. 5626/2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Child by Biological Father
records.heading: Once biological paternity is established, the father must maintain the child
records.text: The right of maintenance vests in the child and rests on welfare, justice and equity. Once biological paternity is established, the obligation to maintain follows, and the father cannot rely on technical pleas of legitimacy. Where paternity is disputed, the claimant must prove it by admissible and trustworthy evidence. The child's welfare is paramount and a woman's dignity is protected under Art. 14. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 352, 2026 SCMR 1401; Muhammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor & others (C.P.L.A. 5626/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor & others (C.P.L.A. 5626/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Joint Trial: Ss. 233, 235, 239 CrPC Discretionary
records.heading: Sections 235 and 239 CrPC make joint trial discretionary because of the word may
records.text: S. 233 CrPC requires separate trial of distinct offences, subject to exceptions in ss. 234, 235, 236 and 239. Ss. 235 and 239 permit joint trial of offences in the same transaction but the word 'may' makes them discretionary. S. 16(4) of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021 is likewise enabling and may be read narrowly so as not to displace the PECA forum and procedure. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 217, 2026 SCMR 1647; Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA 1160/2025).
records.title: Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA 1160/2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Cross-Examination of Complainant: Judge's Duty to Prevent Abuse
records.heading: A Judge must disallow insulting and repetitive cross-examination and not remain a silent spectator
records.text: The right to cross-examine is neither unlimited nor unbridled and must be balanced with fair trial and dignity under Arts. 10-A and 14. The Judge must disallow irrelevant, indecent or insulting questions and prolonged, repetitive cross-examination meant to exhaust the witness, and must not remain a silent spectator, as that defeats the QSO provisions on examination, including Arts. 131 and 143 to 148. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 217, 2026 SCMR 1647; Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA 1160/2025).
records.title: Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA 1160/2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Witnesses Need Not Stand: Seating Directions
records.heading: No law requires a witness to stand while giving evidence
records.text: No requirement in the CrPC, CPC or QSO obliges a witness to stand while giving evidence, and prolonged standing, especially in sexual offence cases, burdens the witness and may impair testimony. Chief Justices were directed to issue administrative directions for seating arrangements for witnesses in all subordinate courts and forums. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 217, 2026 SCMR 1647; Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA 1160/2025).
records.title: Maham Fatima v. The State and another (Cr. PLA 1160/2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Daughter's Share and Nature of Mutation Entries
records.heading: A sole surviving daughter takes one-half of her father's estate
records.text: Mutation entries are maintained only for revenue and fiscal purposes. Under Surah An-Nisa verse 11 and Hanafi law, a sole surviving daughter takes one-half of her father's estate, the residue goes to the residuaries (asaba), and returns to the Quranic heir by Radd only where no residuaries exist. Ref: Mst. Ameer Begum and others v. Rahima Khatoon and others (C.P.L.A. 97-Q/2024, decided 07.07.2026); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Mst. Ameer Begum and others v. Rahima Khatoon and others (C.P.L.A. 97-Q/2024, decided 07.07.2026)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Acquired Land Remains Bound to Public Purpose
records.heading: Land acquired for a public purpose stays bound to that purpose despite later transfer
records.text: Land acquired for a specified public purpose stays impressed with that purpose despite later transfer, assignment or judicial sale. Neither the beneficiary company nor any transferee or auction purchaser may change its user without the Provincial Government's prior sanction and the terms of the agreement under s. 41 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, which bind all claiming through the beneficiary. Ref: M/s Adil International (Pvt.) Ltd. v. The Secretary Industries, Commerce & Technical Education Department, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and others (C.P.L.A. 5182/2024, decided 08.07.2026).
records.title: M/s Adil International (Pvt.) Ltd. v. The Secretary Industries, Commerce & Technical Education Department, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and others (C.P.L.A. 5182/2024, decided 08.07.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail under Punjab Fertilizers Control Act, 2025
records.heading: Authority on bail in a case under the Punjab Fertilizers Control Act 2025
records.text: Authority on bail in a case under the Punjab Fertilizers Control Act, 2025. The Urdu caption describes the report as the latest Lahore High Court directions in fertiliser cases. The post gives no holding. Ref: 2026 YLR 1561, PLJ 2026 CrC 545; Muhammad Arshad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 5480-B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Arshad v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 5480-B/2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics Trials: Prosecutors Must Challenge Concessional Witnesses
records.heading: Law Officers must challenge concessions favouring the accused by prosecution witnesses
records.text: The prosecutor stayed passive when prosecution witnesses made concessions favouring the accused. The Court directed Law Officers to remain active during evidence and the s. 342 CrPC statement, to invoke Arts. 150 and 151 QSO at once when a witness, including a police official, favours the accused, and not to let concessions go unchallenged. Ref: 2026 YLR 1430; Shameer Khan v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 56371/2023).
records.title: Shameer Khan v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 56371/2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Safe Custody of Narcotics Not Proved
records.heading: Failure to prove the chain of safe custody of narcotics makes the case doubtful
records.text: The prosecution did not prove the chain of safe custody and safe transmission of the allegedly recovered narcotic, which made the prosecution case doubtful. Ref: 2026 YLR 1430; Shameer Khan v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 56371/2023).
records.title: Shameer Khan v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 56371/2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Relevancy of Judgments, Orders and Decrees: Arts. 54 to 58
records.heading: Authority on relevancy of judgments, orders and decrees under Articles 54 to 58 QSO
records.text: Authority on the relevancy of judgments, orders and decrees, which is detailed in Arts. 54 to 58 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984. The post gives no further holding. Ref: 2026 YLR 1476; Raja Shahid Ahmad v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal 525/2024).
records.title: Raja Shahid Ahmad v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal 525/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal Extended to Absconding Co-Accused
records.heading: A proclaimed offender with a role similar to an acquitted co-accused was also acquitted
records.text: The appeal was allowed and the appellant acquitted as the prosecution failed to prove its case. A co-accused who was a proclaimed offender with a similar role to an acquitted co-accused was also acquitted, as further proceedings against him would be futile and an abuse of process. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1633; Ghulam Mustafa v. State.
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. State

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Case Diaries and Fourteen-Day Investigation: Directions
records.heading: Investigations must conclude within fourteen days and daily case diaries are mandatory
records.text: Maintaining daily case diaries is a statutory obligation, and unexplained gaps and failure to start absconder proceedings undermine the presumption of fair investigation. Investigations must conclude within fourteen days, and delay violates fair trial rights. Supervisory police authorities must audit delays, enforce timelines and consolidated cross-version investigations, and report compliance to the High Court within thirty days. Ref: 2026 LHC 4593; Tanvir Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 32557/2026, decided 19.06.2026); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Tanvir Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 32557/2026, decided 19.06.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Non-Prohibitory Clause and FIR Delay
records.heading: Post-arrest bail is ordinarily granted where the offences fall outside the prohibitory clause
records.text: Post-arrest bail is ordinarily granted where the offences do not fall within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. This applies with greater force where an unexplained seven-day delay in lodging the FIR points to deliberation and consultation, the investigation is complete and no exceptional circumstances exist. Ref: 2026 LHC 4593; Tanvir Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 32557/2026, decided 19.06.2026); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Tanvir Ahmed v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 32557/2026, decided 19.06.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Closing Right to Produce Evidence in Trial
records.heading: Right to produce evidence was closed after witnesses did not appear despite warrants
records.text: Concerns an order closing the petitioner's right to produce evidence after the witnesses did not appear on two dates despite non-bailable warrants and the petitioner left after appearing in the morning. The post also states that where the court finds production of documentary evidence is meant to delay or defeat justice, it must record its grounds in writing and refuse it, otherwise proceed in accordance with law. Ref: 2026 YLR 1073; Taimoor Malik v. The State and others (Criminal Revision 150/2025).
records.title: Taimoor Malik v. The State and others (Criminal Revision 150/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Identification: Distance and Lighting
records.heading: Eyewitness identification reliability depends chiefly on distance and lighting
records.text: Reliability of eyewitness identification depends on estimator variables, chiefly distance and lighting. Reliability falls as distance increases and poor lighting worsens it, and beyond a certain range identification approaches guesswork. Diagnosticity is the extent to which an identification distinguishes the real offender from an innocent person. The appeal was allowed and the accused acquitted. Ref: Shahbaz alias Gillo v. The State (Criminal Petition 750-L/2018).
records.title: Shahbaz alias Gillo v. The State (Criminal Petition 750-L/2018)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Declaratory Suit on Paternity: Legal Character
records.heading: A negative declaration on another's paternity is unconnected with the plaintiff's legal character
records.text: A declaration can be granted in favour of a person whose legal character or right to property is denied by another. A plaintiff who alleges that the defendant is not his father's daughter seeks a negative declaration unconnected with his own legal character, and the suit was dismissed by the Supreme Court. A person may sue to assert he is someone's child if that status is denied. Ref: PLD 2019 SC 449.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confession to Journalist During Police Custody Inadmissible
records.heading: A confession recorded by a journalist during police custody is inadmissible
records.text: A police officer in custody of an accused cannot delegate investigation to a private person such as a journalist, nor may a journalist record a confession, which would usurp the Magistrate's power under s. 164 CrPC. Such a statement is inadmissible under Art. 39 QSO, and benefit of doubt was extended. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 126; Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021).
records.title: Shahid Ali v. The State (Criminal Petition No.53-K of 2021)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: NADRA Cannot Adjudicate Paternity or Cancel CNIC on Disputed Parentage
records.heading: NADRA cannot adjudicate disputed paternity and a competent court must decide it
records.text: The NADRA Ordinance, 2000 gives NADRA no power to adjudicate contentious questions needing evidence, including disputed paternity, and a declaration must be obtained from a competent court. Impounding the petitioner's CNIC and changing her father's name was challenged, and costs were imposed on NADRA and Respondent No. 3 in her favour. Ref: PLD 2021 Islamabad 105.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody of Minor: Mediation and Co-Parenting Settlement
records.heading: The Supreme Court disposed of a custody dispute on a mediated co-parenting settlement
records.text: After the mother's death, the guardian court gave custody to the maternal grandmother, and the High Court transferred it to the father. The Supreme Court referred the matter to mediation, the parties settled on a co-parenting model in the child's best interests, and the petition was disposed of in terms of the settlement, modifying the High Court judgment only to the extent of inconsistency. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 118; Khurrum Javed and another v. Ahmed Bilal (C.P.L.A. 2788/2022).
records.title: Khurrum Javed and another v. Ahmed Bilal (C.P.L.A. 2788/2022)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Judicial Review of Award Made Rule of Court
records.heading: A court cannot reappraise the merits of an award made rule of court
records.text: An award made rule of court binds the parties like a decree, and the court cannot reappraise the merits or rewrite the contract. Interference is ordinarily confined to patent illegality, jurisdictional defect, arbitrator's misconduct or illegality. The arbitrator is the final judge of fact and law within the reference, and absent manifest error the award is not lightly disturbed. Ref: C.P. 64 of 2018, etc., announced 13.07.2026.
records.title: C.P. 64 of 2018, etc., announced 13.07.2026

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Refusal of Right to Cross-Examine: Revisable under S. 115 CPC
records.heading: An order refusing the right to cross-examine is revisable under section 115 CPC
records.text: An order dismissing an application and declining a party's right to cross-examine the opponent's witnesses is a final order as to that application and can be challenged by revision under s. 115 CPC. Whether the case meets the grounds for revision is decided on merits in that revision. Ref: 2026 MLD 1037; Waqar Ahmad v. Additional District Judge etc (Objection Case 151940/2025).
records.title: Waqar Ahmad v. Additional District Judge etc (Objection Case 151940/2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Railway Police: S. 22-A(6) CrPC and Ex-Officio Justice of Peace
records.heading: Railway Police are police authorities under section 22-A(6) CrPC for Justice of Peace directions
records.text: Railway Police under the Pakistan Railways Police Act, 1977 are police authorities under s. 22-A(6) CrPC, so the Ex-Officio Justice of Peace can issue directions against a delinquent Railway Police official for offences under Arts. 155(1)(c) and 156(d) of the Police Order 2002 and the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act, 2022. Ref: 2026 MLD 1061; Khurram Khursheed v. JOP etc (W.P. 3966/2022).
records.title: Khurram Khursheed v. JOP etc (W.P. 3966/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC and Appeal: Distinct Proceedings
records.heading: Section 12(2) CPC proceedings and appeals are distinct and neither suspends the other
records.text: Proceedings under s. 12(2) CPC and appellate proceedings lie in distinct legal domains, so pendency of one cannot be a lawful ground to suspend or frustrate the other. Ref: 2026 MLD 1053; Muhammad Akram & 7 others v. Muhammad Bilal etc (Civil Revision 1079/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Akram & 7 others v. Muhammad Bilal etc (Civil Revision 1079/2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Magistrate: Discharge, Not Release, under S. 173(3) CrPC
records.heading: A Magistrate must discharge an accused for insufficient material under section 173(3) CrPC
records.text: The term release has no place in the magisterial trial scheme of ss. 241 to 249-A CrPC. On a s. 173 report, a Magistrate who finds insufficient material must discharge the accused for reasons recorded under s. 173(3). The Magistrate's entering into disputed questions of fact and ending proceedings at that stage was unwarranted and caused manifest miscarriage of justice. Ref: 2026 LHC 4694; Muhammad Abid v. The State & 3 others (W.P. 30718/2026).
records.title: Muhammad Abid v. The State & 3 others (W.P. 30718/2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Un-Exhibited Complaint Not Part of Evidence
records.heading: A complaint not exhibited at trial cannot be read as evidence
records.text: A document not formally exhibited during trial cannot be treated as part of the evidentiary record or read in evidence. The complaint under the Act of 2005 on which proceedings began was never exhibited, and excluding it caused the prosecution case to collapse. Ref: 2026 MLD 1107; Nadeem Liaqat v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal 35879/2025).
records.title: Nadeem Liaqat v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal 35879/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Statement of Injured Witness
records.heading: A delayed statement of an injured witness weakens the evidentiary value of his testimony
records.text: Timely recording of witnesses' statements, particularly of the injured, is essential to the credibility of the prosecution case. A delayed statement of an injured witness weakens the evidentiary value of the testimony and renders it suspect, and it has been deprecated by the Supreme Court. Ref: 2026 MLD 1100; Muhammad Maqsood v. The State & 3 others (Criminal Appeal 231326/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Maqsood v. The State & 3 others (Criminal Appeal 231326/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness: Credibility Judged Holistically
records.heading: The presence of an injured witness alone does not establish credibility
records.text: Mere presence of an injured person at the scene is insufficient, and the court must assess the intrinsic reliability and consistency of his testimony. Credibility is judged holistically and is not presumed solely because of injury. Ref: 2026 MLD 1100; Muhammad Maqsood v. The State & 3 others (Criminal Appeal 231326/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Maqsood v. The State & 3 others (Criminal Appeal 231326/2018)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Government Bound by Its Own Service Rules
records.heading: Government must follow its service rules while they remain in force
records.text: Government may frame or amend service rules but must follow them while in force. After the notification of 23.01.2020, Sub-Registrar posts were to be filled only by promotion from Head Registration Muharrirs and Registration Muharrirs, so giving additional charge to Tehsildars, Naib Tehsildars and Kanungos was unlawful. The High Court rightly set it aside under Art. 199, and the Art. 212 bar was not attracted. Ref: Senior Member Board of Revenue, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa & others v. Habib-ur-Rehman & others (F.C.P.L.A. 300/2025, decided 03.07.2026).
records.title: Senior Member Board of Revenue, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa & others v. Habib-ur-Rehman & others (F.C.P.L.A. 300/2025, decided 03.07.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Guidelines for Courts on Minors' Rights and Guardians
records.heading: Courts must follow Order XXXII CPC strictly in cases involving minors
records.text: The Federal Constitutional Court issued guidelines for civil and revenue courts dealing with the person, property or inheritance rights of minors. The court must identify a minor party early, comply strictly with O. XXXII CPC, appoint a guardian ad litem under O. XXXII R. 3 after checking absence of adverse interest, and accept no compromise or concession affecting a minor unless satisfied, with reasons, that it serves the minor's best interests under O. XXXII R. 7. Ref: Mst. Bushra Bibi v. Additional District Judge, Bahawalnagar and others (C.P.L.A. 30-L of 2025, decided 09.07.2026).
records.title: Mst. Bushra Bibi v. Additional District Judge, Bahawalnagar and others (C.P.L.A. 30-L of 2025, decided 09.07.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Fraud: Pleading, Proof and Limitation for Cancellation
records.heading: Fraud must be specifically pleaded and strictly proved, with cancellation sought within limitation
records.text: Fraud must be specifically pleaded and strictly proved by reliable evidence, and it involves a finding of fact on the conduct of the party. A party alleging that an instrument was obtained by fraud must seek cancellation within limitation. Relying on PLD 2015 SC 212, s. 39 of the Specific Relief Act applies and the suit must be filed within three years of knowledge of the fraud under Art. 91 of the Limitation Act. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1019; Pir Shah Abdul Haq (decd.) thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Irfan and others (C.A. 2148/2019).
records.title: Pir Shah Abdul Haq (decd.) thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Irfan and others (C.A. 2148/2019)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Presumption of Correctness of Mutation and Revenue Record
records.heading: A sanctioned mutation in the Jamabandi carries a presumption of truth unless rebutted
records.text: Long-standing revenue entries should not be lightly unsettled. A sanctioned mutation incorporated into the Jamabandi carries a statutory presumption of truth unless rebutted by strong and cogent evidence, and procedural irregularities in attestation do not by themselves invalidate an established sale. Relying on 2008 SCMR 1425, belated challenges to mutations where parties remain in possession cannot displace the presumption of regularity. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1019, PLJ 2026 SC 569; Pir Shah Abdul Haq (decd.) thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Irfan and others (C.A. 2148/2019).
records.title: Pir Shah Abdul Haq (decd.) thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Irfan and others (C.A. 2148/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Duty of Public Authorities to Contest Cases Diligently
records.heading: Public authorities must contest cases diligently and counsel's negligence binds the client
records.text: Public authorities must contest court cases vigilantly, and failure to do so breaches their duty. The negligence of counsel is generally treated as the negligence of the client, and engaging counsel does not absolve a party of responsibility. CDA had filed no written statement and did not cross-examine the plaintiff after being declared ex parte. Exceptions exist only for circumstances beyond control such as death or incapacity of the lawyer. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1033; Capital Development Authority (CDA), through Chairman, Islamabad and others v. Dr. Sheikh Muhammad Shoaib Shafi and another (C.P.L.A. 2284/2025).
records.title: Capital Development Authority (CDA), through Chairman, Islamabad and others v. Dr. Sheikh Muhammad Shoaib Shafi and another (C.P.L.A. 2284/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXII R. 15 CPC: Guardian for Suit of Unsound Mind
records.heading: Order XXXII Rule 15 CPC requires a guardian for a party of unsound mind
records.text: O. XXXII R. 15 CPC extends the rules on minors to persons adjudged of unsound mind and to persons found by the Court on inquiry to be incapable of protecting their interests. In either case the Court must appoint a guardian for the suit. The trial court may appoint a guardian ad litem under O. XXXII even though no guardian has yet been appointed under the Ordinance. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 568; Riffat Saeed v. Zaheer Adnan etc (W.P. 1589-23).
records.title: Riffat Saeed v. Zaheer Adnan etc (W.P. 1589-23)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Intra-Court Appeal Barred After Ombudsman Remedy
records.heading: An intra-court appeal is not maintainable after invoking the Ombudsman remedy
records.text: Where a substantive remedy akin to appeal or revision under s. 14 of the Federal Ombudsman Institutional Reforms Act, 2013 is available and has been invoked, the bar in the proviso to s. 3(2) of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972 applies. An intra-court appeal under s. 3 of the Ordinance is therefore not maintainable. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 593; Muhammad Umair Farooqi v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (ICA-130-25).
records.title: Muhammad Umair Farooqi v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (ICA-130-25)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Suppression of Accused's Injuries by Prosecution
records.heading: Suppression of the accused's injuries shows prosecution witnesses were not truthful
records.text: Where the accused were also injured and the prosecution suppressed their injuries, this shows that the prosecution witnesses were not truthful, and their evidence is not worthy of reliance. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1010; Iftikhar Ahmed alias Papu Naseer Ahmad v. The State (Crl. A. 57 & 58 of 2021).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmed alias Papu Naseer Ahmad v. The State (Crl. A. 57 & 58 of 2021)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Solitary Statement of Victim in Sodomy or Zina
records.heading: The solitary statement of a victim suffices for conviction in sodomy if confidence-inspiring
records.text: In sodomy or zina under s. 376(i) PPC, the solitary statement of the victim suffices for conviction if it is confidence-inspiring, relying on 2006 SCMR 1042, 2011 SCMR 1665 and PLD 2020 SC 313. The medical evidence, including the lady doctor's firm testimony, supported the ocular account. Conviction and sentence upheld and appeal dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 177; Aamir v. State etc (Crl. A. 1166-J of 2019, decided 13.04.2026); Justice Muhammad Tariq Nadeem.
records.title: Aamir v. State etc (Crl. A. 1166-J of 2019, decided 13.04.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Theft of Goats, Mala Fide
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail was granted in a case alleging theft of five goats
records.text: Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC granted in a s. 380 PPC case alleging theft of five goats. The FIR gave no distinctive features of the goats, arrest was unnecessary for recovery as a search warrant would serve, and the allegation of mala fide could not be said to lack basis. Confinement would harm reputation to no useful purpose. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 173; Muhammad Nadeem v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 2924-B of 2025, decided 10.09.2025); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Nadeem v. State and another (Crl. Misc. 2924-B of 2025, decided 10.09.2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail Refused: Misappropriation by Employee
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail is an extraordinary relief for innocent persons and was refused
records.text: Pre-arrest bail under s. 498 CrPC was refused in a s. 408 PPC case of misappropriation of Rs. 800,000. Recovery was yet to be effected and no mala fide on the complainant's part was shown. Pre-arrest bail is an extraordinary relief meant for innocent persons. Petition dismissed and ad-interim bail recalled. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 171; Nasir Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 17599-B of 2026, decided 23.04.2026); Justice Asjad Javaid Ghural.
records.title: Nasir Abbas v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 17599-B of 2026, decided 23.04.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 302(c) and 300 Exception 4: Sudden Fight, Sentence
records.heading: A sudden fight with a solitary stab wound falls under section 302(c), not 302(b)
records.text: Motive was not established, there was no previous enmity, the occurrence took place at the spur of the moment with a solitary stab wound and no undue advantage taken. Such a case falls within Exception 4 to erstwhile s. 300 and is punishable under s. 302(c) rather than s. 302(b) PPC. The petition for enhancement of sentence was dismissed. Appeal partly allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 168; Waqas Ali and another v. State etc (Crl. A. 78282 of 2022 & Crl. Rev. 1572 of 2023, heard on 08.04.2026); Justice Muhammad Waheed Khan.
records.title: Waqas Ali and another v. State etc (Crl. A. 78282 of 2022 & Crl. Rev. 1572 of 2023, heard on 08.04.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail After Arrest: Further Inquiry in Abduction
records.heading: Bail was granted where the accused was not named and no incriminating evidence connected him
records.text: Bail under s. 497 CrPC granted in a s. 365-B PPC abduction case where the accused was not named in the FIR and no other incriminating evidence connected him with the crime, making out a case of further inquiry. The object of bail is to make the accused face trial and not to punish him as an under-trial prisoner. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 161; Mujahid v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 10417-B of 2025, decided 18.02.2026); Justice Sardar Akbar Ali.
records.title: Mujahid v. State etc (Crl. Misc. 10417-B of 2025, decided 18.02.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower on Dissolution: Khula and Cruelty
records.heading: Authority on dower on dissolution, khula, cruelty and Family Court discretion
records.text: Authority on a wife's entitlement to dower on dissolution of marriage, after the Federal Shariat Court's declaration on s. 10(5) and (6) of the Family Courts Act, 1964. It addresses the distinction between khula and dissolution under the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, whether cruelty bars the husband from claiming return of dower, and the principles for Family Courts' discretion. Ref: 2026 LHC 4758; Arslan v. Nisha Shahid etc (W.P. 20300/23, decided 01.07.2026); Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani.
records.title: Arslan v. Nisha Shahid etc (W.P. 20300/23, decided 01.07.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Recovery on Joint Pointation
records.heading: Recovery of a dead body on joint pointation weakens its evidentiary value under Article 40
records.text: Recovery of a dead body on the joint pointation of the accused significantly weakens the evidentiary value of such recovery under Art. 40 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1146; Osama v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 63-Q/2024).
records.title: Osama v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 63-Q/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Last Seen Evidence: Requirements and Caution
records.heading: Last seen evidence is weak, needs linking evidence and must be accepted with great caution
records.text: Last seen evidence is weak circumstantial evidence and is not by itself sufficient to convict. The time gap must rule out another culprit, and there must be linking evidence such as recovery or strong motive. It must be accepted with great caution. Delay in disclosure and absence of direct evidence weakened the prosecution case, and benefit of doubt went to the accused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1146; Osama v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 63-Q/2024).
records.title: Osama v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 63-Q/2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dissolution of Marriage: Second Marriage, Dower and Khula
records.heading: The husband's second marriage without Arbitration Council permission established a ground for dissolution
records.text: The wife sued for dissolution on grounds including cruelty and the husband's second marriage, but the courts below dissolved the marriage as khula conditional on forgoing dower. The husband's second marriage without Arbitration Council permission established the statutory ground under s. 2(iia) DMMA, which the lower courts failed to adjudicate. The Supreme Court dissolved the marriage and held the wife entitled to remaining dower of Rs. 1,200,000. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 302; Mst. Naila Javed and another v. Nasir Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 3767/2025).
records.title: Mst. Naila Javed and another v. Nasir Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 3767/2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 141 and 149 PPC: Common Object of Unlawful Assembly
records.heading: Section 149 PPC liability requires a nexus between the common object and the offence
records.text: The common object of an unlawful assembly must be one of the five objects listed in s. 141 PPC. Under s. 149 every member is liable for the offence committed in pursuance of the common object, provided there is a nexus between the common object and the offence, and the conduct of each member is relevant. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1196; Ashfaque Hussain & others v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 187-K/2025).
records.title: Ashfaque Hussain & others v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 187-K/2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Sessions Court First; s. 354-A PPC
records.heading: A person seeking pre-arrest bail must first approach the Court of Sessions
records.text: A person seeking bail before arrest must first approach the Court of Sessions before petitioning the High Court. An offence under s. 354-A PPC is a heinous crime falling within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1196; Ashfaque Hussain & others v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 187-K/2025).
records.title: Ashfaque Hussain & others v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 187-K/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Complainant Withholding Source of Information
records.heading: A complainant withholding the source of his information damages the credibility of the prosecution
records.text: The complainant did not nominate the appellant and refused to disclose the source of information on which other co-accused were nominated, saying only that he had sources of his own. The question was relevant and not barred by Arts. 143 and 144 QSO. Withholding such material information damages the credibility of the prosecution and makes the implication of the accused doubtful. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1056; Salamat Ali v. The State (Crl.A. 543/2019).
records.title: Salamat Ali v. The State (Crl.A. 543/2019)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Deposit of Balance and Readiness
records.heading: Failure to deposit the balance sale price within the fixed time results in dismissal
records.text: In a suit for specific performance, the balance sale price must be deposited within the time fixed by the court, failing which the suit is dismissed and later deposit cannot be permitted. Specific performance is a discretionary equitable relief and not a matter of right, and continuous readiness and willingness of the plaintiff is foundational. Concurrent findings may be interfered with for misreading or non-reading of evidence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1063; Muhammad Imran v. Ishfaq Ahmed and othes (C.P.L.A. 3639/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Imran v. Ishfaq Ahmed and othes (C.P.L.A. 3639/2025)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Attorney Transferring Principal's Property to His Sons
records.heading: An attorney cannot transfer the principal's property to his own sons without express consent
records.text: An attorney cannot validly transfer the principal's property to his own sons without express written consent. A cheque payment by the brother to the sister is not conclusive proof of a valid sale absent an agreement to sell or independent corroboration. The transaction offended the fiduciary obligations of an attorney and could not be sustained. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1119; Javed Iqbal and others v. Mst. Farhat Iqbal (decd.) thr. L.Rs (C.A. 852/2025).
records.title: Javed Iqbal and others v. Mst. Farhat Iqbal (decd.) thr. L.Rs (C.A. 852/2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Chapter X CrPC: Billiard and Snooker Clubs
records.heading: Chapter X CrPC powers cannot be used to shut down billiard and snooker clubs indefinitely
records.text: Billiards and snooker are not prohibited by any law, are not immoral, and do not fall within the protected sphere of s. 133 CrPC. Powers under Chapter X CrPC are special powers for temporary measures and cannot be used to shut down businesses indefinitely. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1395; Muhammad Rashid v. ASJ Sargodha etc (Crl. Misc. 106558/17).
records.title: Muhammad Rashid v. ASJ Sargodha etc (Crl. Misc. 106558/17)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Sperm Fraction and Epithelial Fraction in DNA Analysis
records.heading: Absent DNA in the epithelial fraction does not diminish a matching sperm fraction profile
records.text: In sexual assault samples, differential extraction separates the sperm fraction from the epithelial fraction. Absence of the offender's DNA from the epithelial fraction does not by itself invalidate or diminish the credibility and probative value of a matching DNA profile obtained from the sperm fraction.
