Ref: 2026 LHC 4807; Manazir Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 31263/22, decided 08.07.2026); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Manazir Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 31263/22, decided 08.07.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Infirmity as Independent Ground for Bail
records.heading: Section 497 CrPC recognises infirmity as a separate and independent ground for bail
records.text: Section 497 CrPC recognises infirmity as a separate and independent ground for bail, even in heinous offences, distinct from bail on medical grounds. Infirmity is a functional incapacity from age, congenital limitation or non-fatal disease that makes incarceration disproportionately hard. The court may itself examine the prisoner and grant bail without further medical investigation. Ref: 2026 LHC 4824; Iftikhar Ahmad v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 33164/26, decided 23.07.2026); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmad v. The State etc (Crl. Misc. 33164/26, decided 23.07.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Wife's Claim for Past Maintenance: Limitation
records.heading: A wife may recover maintenance arrears for the six years preceding the suit
records.text: A wife's claim for past maintenance is governed by Art. 120 of the Limitation Act, 1908 (six years). Non-payment recurs monthly and is a continuing wrong under s. 23, giving a fresh cause of action each time. She may recover arrears for the six years preceding the suit despite earlier delay. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 308; Muhammad Aslam Chattha v. Shehnaz Akhtar Zahoor Ahmed and another (C.A. 1413 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam Chattha v. Shehnaz Akhtar Zahoor Ahmed and another (C.A. 1413 of 2021)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Recalling Witness to Declare Hostile
records.heading: Section 540 CrPC cannot be used to fill lacunae or reopen concluded examination
records.text: Under Art. 150 QSO a party may cross-examine its own witness with court permission only when the witness shows hostility, and permission must be sought while the witness is under examination. After the adverse party's cross-examination, only re-examination is allowed. Section 540 CrPC cannot be used to fill lacunae or reopen concluded examination. The application to recall the witness was rightly dismissed. Ref: PLD 2026 Quetta 73.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Substitution Unlikely: Related Eye-Witnesses
records.heading: Closely related eye-witnesses who lost family members are unlikely to substitute the real culprit
records.text: Closely related eye-witnesses who lost close family members, including a mother and sister-in-law killed in the occurrence, are highly unlikely to spare the real culprit and falsely implicate an innocent person. Substitution was extremely remote and beyond the realm of probability on the facts. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1085.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Delay in Trial: Case Management
records.heading: A trial court should use case management to curb delay and bail was allowed
records.text: The accused had been in custody for 2 years and 5 months without conclusion of the trial, with most delay attributed to the prosecution and complainant. The trial court is not powerless under the CrPC and should ensure timely s. 173 reports, fix timelines for producing witnesses and curtail unnecessary adjournments. Bail allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1076.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Special Law Bar: Intellectual Property Tribunal Jurisdiction
records.heading: Intellectual property damages suits must be brought before the Intellectual Property Tribunal
records.text: A specialised forum is better equipped for subject matter involving specialised legal concepts. Under the Punjab amendment to s. 9 CPC, civil court jurisdiction is barred where a general or special law is in force. A damages suit relating to intellectual property rights must be brought before the Intellectual Property Tribunal under the IPO Pakistan Act, 2012, and the plaint was returned for presentation there. Ref: 2024 CLD 502.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Termination for Bogus Identity: Writ and Laches
records.heading: Maintainability of a writ against termination for bogus identity, forum shopping and laches
records.text: Concerned a constitutional petition against termination of an employee accused of obtaining employment through false parentage and a bogus CNIC, filed after multiple unsuccessful remedies and delay. The pivotal question was maintainability in light of forum shopping, withdrawal of proceedings, disputed identity and laches. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 889; Ghulam Sarwar v. District Coordination Officer Gujranwala and others (Writ Petition No. 202526 of 2018).
records.title: Ghulam Sarwar v. District Coordination Officer Gujranwala and others (Writ Petition No. 202526 of 2018)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: LLB Degree and Advance Increments
records.heading: An accounts officer holding an LLB was not entitled to advance increments
records.text: An accounts officer in the audit department of Pakistan Railways holding an LLB was not entitled to advance increments. No benefit under the 1966 Scheme had been extended to audit department officers and an LLB is not recognised under the General Scheme, 1996. The petitions were converted into appeals and allowed. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 862; The Secretary/Chairman Railways, Government of Pakistan v. Tariq Mansoor and others (Civil Petitions Nos. 3651-L and 4648 of 2022).
records.title: The Secretary/Chairman Railways, Government of Pakistan v. Tariq Mansoor and others (Civil Petitions Nos. 3651-L and 4648 of 2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Wedlock Policy: No Vested Right to Posting
records.heading: Wedlock or spouse posting policies create no vested right to posting together
records.text: Wedlock or spouse-posting policies support family unity but do not create a vested right and cannot justify indefinite deputation or posting together as of right. Doing so would disregard the resource-based limitations in Art. 29(2) of the Constitution. The policy is a guiding principle and not one to be strictly enforced by courts. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 852; Mst. Salma Raza v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (C.P.L.A. 760-P of 2025).
records.title: Mst. Salma Raza v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (C.P.L.A. 760-P of 2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Weight of Police Opinion at Bail Stage
records.heading: The investigating agency's opinion on bail is neither binding nor gospel truth
records.text: The opinion of the investigating agency is neither binding on the court nor gospel truth, and depends on the circumstances of each case. The court should not brush it aside unless other cogent reasons or extenuating circumstances justify discarding it. Ref: 2021 SCMR 2011.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Further Inquiry: Tentative Assessment at Bail Stage
records.heading: Only a tentative assessment is made at the bail stage
records.text: At the bail stage only a tentative assessment is made, not a deeper appreciation of evidence. The court considers the composite effect of the incriminating material, including inconsistency between the FIR and postmortem report or ocular evidence unsupported by medical evidence. Discrepancy in the location of injuries and the complainant not being an eye-witness supported further inquiry. Ref: 2021 SCMR 2011.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Rejection of a plaint under Order VII Rule 11 must be exercised narrowly
records.text: Rejection of a plaint under O. VII R. 11 CPC is an exception to the rule of trial and must be exercised narrowly. Under clause (a), cause of action is the bundle of material facts the plaintiff must prove, and the court must not convert the summary scrutiny into adjudication of disputed facts or the merits. Ref: Nisar Ahmed Afzal v. Irfan Qadir & another (C.P.L.A. 3792/2018, decided 28.07.2026); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Nisar Ahmed Afzal v. Irfan Qadir & another (C.P.L.A. 3792/2018, decided 28.07.2026)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Scope of Sessions Court Jurisdiction; Parallel Civil Suit
records.heading: A complaint under the Illegal Dispossession Act is maintainable despite a pending civil suit
records.text: The Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 is a remedial statute, and the sessions court assesses whether illegal dispossession is made out without adjudicating complex civil title. A complaint is maintainable despite pending civil proceedings, and summary dismissal on that ground alone is untenable unless the process is abused. Co-ownership of unpartitioned land does not bar inquiry into dispossession. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 333; Qaiser Jabbar v. Syed Mati Ullah Shah and others (Crl.P.L.A. 1121/2021).
records.title: Qaiser Jabbar v. Syed Mati Ullah Shah and others (Crl.P.L.A. 1121/2021)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Party Who Contested the Suit
records.heading: A party that lost after contesting the suit cannot apply under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: A party that contested the suit through the fora below and failed has no right to file an application under s. 12(2) CPC, and its own mistake or slackness gives no such right. The post also records questions on the High Court's writ jurisdiction to reappraise evidence and the effect of s. 23 of the Registration Act, and notes that registered documents carry a presumption of truth. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 304; Mian Tahir Raza v. Mubasher Ahmed and others (Civil Appeal No. 112 of 2023).
records.title: Mian Tahir Raza v. Mubasher Ahmed and others (Civil Appeal No. 112 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Burden of Proof and Accused's Specific Plea
records.heading: The prosecution is not absolved if the accused fails to prove a specific plea
records.text: The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and is not absolved if the accused fails to prove a plea. Where the accused raises a specific permissible plea, the onus of proving it lies on the accused, who may benefit from any oral or documentary material produced by the prosecution. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 326; Anwar Keneth v. The State (Crl.A. 590/2017).
records.title: Anwar Keneth v. The State (Crl.A. 590/2017)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI CPC: Dismissal of Appeal for Non-Appearance
records.heading: An appellate court may dismiss an appeal under Order XLI Rule 11 for non-appearance
records.text: Explains appeals from original decrees under ss. 96 and 100 CPC and O. XLI. Under R. 11 the appellate court may dismiss an appeal if the appellant does not appear, otherwise it fixes a hearing day under R. 12, and R. 17(1) governs default in appearance. Mere technicalities should not defeat the ends of justice. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1316; Abdul Rehman and another v. Syed Jaffar Hussain Razvi (C.P.L.A. 5179/2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman and another v. Syed Jaffar Hussain Razvi (C.P.L.A. 5179/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct and Doubtful Identification of Eyewitnesses
records.heading: Unnatural conduct of police eyewitnesses makes their identification of assailants doubtful
records.text: Police eyewitnesses in plain clothes and unarmed who claimed to chase assailants at once, after a colleague was killed and others injured, acted unnaturally. Their detailed identification of assailants during a sudden attack was doubtful, and their presence was not established by independent evidence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1390; Ali Imran and others v. The State (Crl.A. 257/2025).
records.title: Ali Imran and others v. The State (Crl.A. 257/2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Joint Identification Parade Unsafe
records.heading: A joint identification parade of several accused is unsafe and unreliable
records.text: Identification parade of each accused must be held separately, and a joint parade of several accused is unsafe and unreliable and has been deprecated. Where the accused are already known to the police or their identity is disclosed before the parade, the identification loses its value as corroboration. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1390; Ali Imran and others v. The State (Crl.A. 257/2025).
records.title: Ali Imran and others v. The State (Crl.A. 257/2025)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption Price: Sale Price Versus Market Value
records.heading: The pre-emptor ordinarily pays the genuine sale price and not market value
records.text: Under s. 27 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pre-emption Act, 1987, the pre-emptor ordinarily pays the genuine sale price under s. 27(2). Market value applies under s. 27(1) only where the price was not fixed in good faith. The post also records that no ground existed for the revisional court to interfere under s. 115 CPC. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1288; Ameer Nawab v. Wali Akbar (C.A.544/2022).
records.title: Ameer Nawab v. Wali Akbar (C.A.544/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: No Caste or Tribe in FIRs and Police Records
records.heading: Caste or tribe must not appear in names of persons in FIRs
records.text: The Supreme Court directed all Inspectors General of Police to ensure that no caste, tribe, biradari, conversion status or derogatory expression appears in names of complainants, accused, victims or witnesses in FIRs and other police records. Departure is allowed only where the investigating officer records in writing a bona fide investigative need. The Registrar is to circulate the judgment. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1384; Arshad alias Billu v. The State (Jail Petition No. 183/2019).
records.title: Arshad alias Billu v. The State (Jail Petition No. 183/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: New Plea at Leave Stage; Remand; Bound by Pleadings
records.heading: A new factual plea cannot be raised for the first time in leave proceedings
records.text: A new factual plea cannot be raised for the first time in leave proceedings under Art. 185(3) of the Constitution. Remand is a corrective power and not a routine device to fill lacunae, and parties are bound by their pleadings, with no evidence admissible on a plea not raised. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1355; Faisal Paracha v. Additional District Judge etc (C.P.L.A. 209, 210, 211, 212, 324 & 325/2026).
records.title: Faisal Paracha v. Additional District Judge etc (C.P.L.A. 209, 210, 211, 212, 324 & 325/2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Setting Up Independent Title
records.heading: A tenant setting up independent title during tenancy must vacate and sue elsewhere
records.text: Where a tenant sets up independent title in himself during tenancy, the lawful course is to vacate the premises and pursue remedies in a competent civil forum. Rent proceedings cannot be converted into a forum for adjudicating complex title disputes. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1355; Faisal Paracha v. Additional District Judge etc (C.P.L.A. 209, 210, 211, 212, 324 & 325/2026).
records.title: Faisal Paracha v. Additional District Judge etc (C.P.L.A. 209, 210, 211, 212, 324 & 325/2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence; Interference in Acquittal
records.heading: Interference in an acquittal is warranted only for glaring errors of law and fact
records.text: The presumption of innocence is the golden thread of criminal law. Interference in a judgment of acquittal is rare and warranted only where the prosecution shows glaring errors of law and fact, such that the judgment is perfunctory. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1390; Altaf Yousuf v. The State through Additional Director FIA & another (Crl.P.L.A. 188-K/2022).
records.title: Altaf Yousuf v. The State through Additional Director FIA & another (Crl.P.L.A. 188-K/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absence of Postmortem Not Always Fatal
records.heading: Absence of a postmortem is not always fatal to the prosecution
records.text: Absence of a postmortem is not always fatal to the prosecution if it is proved beyond doubt that death resulted from the accused's act, for example where the body was thrown into a canal in front of eyewitnesses, or where the body was too decomposed after burning in the witnesses' presence and an external medical examination exists. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1223; Rasool Bakhsh v. The State (Jail Petition No. 296 of 2018).
records.title: Rasool Bakhsh v. The State (Jail Petition No. 296 of 2018)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Joint Property Given as Dower
records.heading: A husband cannot give jointly owned property as dower beyond his own share
records.text: Under Mohammadan Law dower may be any property, but the husband must have title to transfer it. Where property is jointly owned by heirs, the husband cannot give the entire property as dower, and the dower declaration operates only to the extent of the husband's or his mother's inherited share. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1298; Noman Rasheed & others v. Mst. Nighat Miandad & others (Civil Petition No. 5073 of 2025).
records.title: Noman Rasheed & others v. Mst. Nighat Miandad & others (Civil Petition No. 5073 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Nature of Remedy and Forum
records.heading: A section 12(2) CPC application must be filed before the court that passed the decree
records.text: Section 12(2) CPC is an extraordinary remedy to nullify judgments obtained by fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction. The application must be filed before the court that passed the final judgment, decree or order. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1298; Noman Rasheed & others v. Mst. Nighat Miandad & others (Civil Petition No. 5073 of 2025).
records.title: Noman Rasheed & others v. Mst. Nighat Miandad & others (Civil Petition No. 5073 of 2025)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Who May Complain: Owner or Occupier, Prima Facie Case
records.heading: Only a lawful owner or occupier may complain under the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.text: The Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 is a special law construed strictly. Only a lawful owner (s. 2(d)) or lawful occupier (s. 2(c)) illegally dispossessed may complain under s. 3, and the complainant must show a prima facie case under ss. 3 and 4. The dismissal of the complaint by the Trial Court, upheld by the Peshawar High Court, was found correct. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1250; Najma Bibi v. Zakir Abbasi and another (Crl.P.L.A. 768/2024); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Najma Bibi v. Zakir Abbasi and another (Crl.P.L.A. 768/2024)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Who May Complain: Owner or Occupier, Prima Facie Case
records.heading: A complainant under the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 must be a lawful owner or occupier
records.text: The Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 is a special law construed strictly. Only a lawful owner (s. 2(d)) or lawful occupier (s. 2(c)) illegally dispossessed may complain under s. 3, and the complainant must show a prima facie case under ss. 3 and 4. The dismissal of the complaint by the Trial Court, upheld by the Peshawar High Court, was found correct. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1234; Najma Bibi v. Zakir Abbasi and another (Crl.P.L.A. 768/2024); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Najma Bibi v. Zakir Abbasi and another (Crl.P.L.A. 768/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Successive Investigations Declaring Accused Innocent
records.heading: Successive investigations finding the accused innocent carry persuasive value for the defence
records.text: The court is not bound by police opinion, but where successive investigations by different officers, verified by senior officers, found the accused innocent without any shown mala fide or extraneous influence, such findings cannot be lightly discarded and carry persuasive value supporting the defence version. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1323; Muhammad Nadeem v. The State (J.P.217/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Nadeem v. The State (J.P.217/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unnatural Conduct of Eyewitnesses
records.heading: Passive conduct of eyewitnesses and contradictions deprive the ocular account of confidence
records.text: The eyewitnesses, grown sons of the deceased, remained passive while their mother was fired upon, and no independent witness confirmed their presence. Their conduct was against normal human behaviour and their testimonies had material contradictions, so the ocular account did not inspire confidence without independent corroboration. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1323; Muhammad Nadeem v. The State (J.P.217/2018).
records.title: Muhammad Nadeem v. The State (J.P.217/2018)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail Where Fine Alone Is Alternative Punishment
records.heading: Bail should not be withheld where fine alone is an alternative punishment
records.text: Where an offence is punishable with fine alone as an alternative to imprisonment, bail should not be withheld, since pre-trial detention would amount to double jeopardy if only a fine is imposed. Refusal would contravene Art. 13(a) of the Constitution, s. 403 CrPC and the spirit of s. 26 of the General Clauses Act, 1897. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1379; Liaqat Ali v. The State thr P G Punjab Lahore and another (Crl.P.L.A. 10-L/2026).
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. The State thr P G Punjab Lahore and another (Crl.P.L.A. 10-L/2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Prison Overcrowding and Under-Trial Prisoners
records.heading: Bail applications must be decided with sensitivity to prison overcrowding and under-trial numbers
records.text: Noting prisons at 152.2 percent of capacity and under-trial prisoners at 73.41 percent of the population per the 2024 data, the court directed that bail applications be decided with heightened sensitivity to these figures and that trials be disposed of swiftly. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1379; Liaqat Ali v. The State thr P G Punjab Lahore and another (Crl.P.L.A. 10-L/2026).
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. The State thr P G Punjab Lahore and another (Crl.P.L.A. 10-L/2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Mere Mention of Amanat in FIR
records.heading: Mere mention of Amanat in an FIR does not attract section 406 PPC
records.text: Merely mentioning the word Amanat (trust) in the FIR does not attract s. 406 PPC unless the ingredients of criminal breach of trust are otherwise made out. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1379, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 228; Liaqat Ali v. The State (Crl.A. 10-L of 2026).
records.title: Liaqat Ali v. The State (Crl.A. 10-L of 2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Duty of Investigating Officer to Probe Accused's Plea
records.heading: The investigating officer must probe the accused's specific plea as well
records.text: The purpose of investigation is to collect all evidence for and against both complainant and accused. Once the accused raises a specific plea, the investigating officer must investigate from that perspective as well. Here the officer failed to examine the petitioner's plea of a prior sodomy attempt by the complainant party. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1344; Khan Afzaal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 92 of 2022).
records.title: Khan Afzaal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 92 of 2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sudden Flare-Up and Free Fight: s. 302(b) PPC
records.heading: A sudden flare-up from an unplanned encounter lacks the malice required under section 302(b)
records.text: The occurrence bore the characteristics of a sudden flare-up from an unplanned encounter with mutual resistance, supported by the injured witness's admitted blows and the injuries inflicted from different directions with different weapons. The act lacked the specific malice required for conviction under s. 302(b) PPC. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1344; Khan Afzaal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 92 of 2022).
records.title: Khan Afzaal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 92 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of CDR: Photocopy Without Secondary Evidence Permission
records.heading: A photocopy of a CDR without secondary evidence permission has no evidentiary value
records.text: Only a photocopy of the CDR was produced, without any telephone company officer, attested CDR or court permission for secondary evidence, and without proof of SIM ownership or CDR of the appellant's own SIM. The prosecution evidence on CDR was inconsequential. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1261; Sikandar Ali Lashari v. The State thr. PG Sindh (Crl.A.343/2023).
records.title: Sikandar Ali Lashari v. The State thr. PG Sindh (Crl.A.343/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Third Party's Property as Dower Requires Proven Consent
records.heading: Third party property cannot form part of dower without proven consent of the owner
records.text: Property owned by a third person cannot form part of dower without clear, unequivocal and proven consent of the owner. The petitioner was not a signatory to the Nikahnama and the alleged later consent as witness in the Kabeen Nama was unproved, so inclusion of the plot in dower could not be sustained. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1293, PLJ 2026 SC 591; Sher Alam Khan v. Mst. Fozia Tabbasum Afridi & others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 429-P of 2024).
records.title: Sher Alam Khan v. Mst. Fozia Tabbasum Afridi & others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 429-P of 2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt as a Matter of Right
records.heading: A single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to its benefit as of right
records.text: If a single circumstance creates reasonable doubt in the mind of a prudent person about the guilt of the accused, the accused is entitled to the benefit of that doubt as a matter of right and not as a matter of grace. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1349; Shahbaz alias Gillo v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 750-L/2018).
records.title: Shahbaz alias Gillo v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 750-L/2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Eyewitness Identification: Distance, Lighting, Diagnosticity
records.heading: Identification by sheltering witnesses during a multi-accused armed attack was unsafe
records.text: Reliability of eyewitness identification depends on estimator variables, chiefly distance and lighting, with reliability falling as distance grows and light worsens. Identification during an attack by several armed accused firing together, while the witnesses took shelter, was unsafe and scientifically unsound. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1349, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 320; Shahbaz alias Gillo v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 750-L/2018).
records.title: Shahbaz alias Gillo v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 750-L/2018)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 423 CrPC: Appellate Court Must Decide on Merits
records.heading: An appellate court must reappraise evidence and decide the appeal on merits under section 423
records.text: The appellate court must reappraise the evidence and decide the appeal on merits under s. 423 CrPC, and cannot evade this duty because the accused or counsel did not challenge the conviction or conceded points. Failure to do so renders the appellate proceedings legally vulnerable. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1215; Tariq Sajjad Khan v. The State etc (Criminal Petition No. 749-L of 2022).
records.title: Tariq Sajjad Khan v. The State etc (Criminal Petition No. 749-L of 2022)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Super Tax: Federal Constitutional Court Judgment
records.heading: Authority on super tax from a detailed Federal Constitutional Court judgment
records.text: Authority on super tax; a detailed judgment of the Federal Constitutional Court. The post gives no holding. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 168.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chars Recovery: Contradictions Create Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Contradictions in the weight and description of chars gave the accused benefit of doubt
records.text: Twelve kilograms of chars was said to be in ten packets of 1200 grams each, but the packet weights belied this. There was no Roznamcha entry on receipt of case property, no description of the chars in the FIR and recovery memo, and a colour discrepancy on de-sealing. The Supreme Court set aside the conviction and acquitted the accused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1215; Tariq Sajjad Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 749-L of 2022).
records.title: Tariq Sajjad Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 749-L of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Vakalatnama: Implied Authority of Counsel to Act
records.heading: Counsel's implied authority under a vakalatnama binds the client unless expressly limited
records.text: The term act in a vakalatnama is of very wide amplitude. Counsel has implied authority to do whatever he considers best for his client in the proceedings, and such acts bind the client unless express limitations were placed on his authority. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 575; Mst. Sarwat Sethi v. Mst. Khalida Parveen (F.A.O. No. 71 of 2011).
records.title: Mst. Sarwat Sethi v. Mst. Khalida Parveen (F.A.O. No. 71 of 2011)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Counsel's Authority to Compromise or Withdraw
records.heading: Authority to compromise or withdraw litigation is inherent in counsel's engagement under a vakalatnama
records.text: Authority to compromise or withdraw litigation is inherent in the engagement of counsel under a vakalatnama. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 575; Mst. Sarwat Sethi v. Mst. Khalida Parveen (F.A.O. No. 71 of 2011).
records.title: Mst. Sarwat Sethi v. Mst. Khalida Parveen (F.A.O. No. 71 of 2011)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 4 MFLO: Children of Predeceased Son or Daughter
records.heading: Section 4 MFLO remains binding until the pending Supreme Court appeal is decided
records.text: Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 gives children of a predeceased son or daughter a per stirpes share. The Federal Shariat Court held it repugnant in PLD 2000 FSC 1, but under the first proviso to Art. 203-D(2) that judgment does not take effect until the pending Supreme Court appeal is decided. Until then s. 4 is binding law, and the spouse of the predeceased child is excluded. Ref: PLD 2026 Islamabad 164.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 88 and 89 CrPC: Restoration of Attached Property
records.heading: The two-year period in section 89 CrPC runs only after complete attachment
records.text: The two-year period in s. 89 CrPC for restoration of attached property runs only after complete attachment of the immovable property by the methods in s. 88(4). Where complete attachment was not carried out, the question of limitation did not arise for an accused who appeared, faced trial and was acquitted under s. 265-K. Ref: PLD 2026 Pesh 154.

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 21M ATA: Joint Trial of Connected Offences
records.heading: The Anti-Terrorism Court may jointly try connected offences under section 21M ATA
records.text: While trying a scheduled offence, the Anti-Terrorism Court may under s. 21M ATA jointly try any other connected offence by the accused. Being tried in the ATC does not turn a scheduled or non-scheduled offence into terrorism, and it remains punishable under the ordinary criminal law. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1236; Riaz Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 22-K/2022 in CrLP.L.A. No. 184-K/2020).
records.title: Riaz Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 22-K/2022 in CrLP.L.A. No. 184-K/2020)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: S. 6 ATA: Ingredients of Terrorism; Meaning of Design
records.heading: Fear alone does not establish terrorism without the design or purpose in section 6
records.text: Terrorism under s. 6(1) requires an act listed in s. 6(2), the design under s. 6(1)(b) or purpose under s. 6(1)(c), and the intimidating or fear-creating impact. Fear alone is not decisive without the requisite mens rea. The word design looks to the object in the offender's mind, so the test is whether the act was designed to cause the outcome. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1236; Riaz Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 22-K/2022 in CrLP.L.A. No. 184-K/2020).
records.title: Riaz Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 22-K/2022 in CrLP.L.A. No. 184-K/2020)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: Attack on Law Enforcement Officials: s. 6(2)(n) ATA
records.heading: Killing a police official while performing duties qualifies as serious violence under section 6(2)(n)
records.text: The killing or serious injury of a police or security official while performing official duties qualifies as serious violence within s. 6(2)(n). Such harm arises from the official's legal responsibility and not from personal disputes, particularly where an armed attack on accused in custody anticipates police resistance. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1236; Riaz Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 22-K/2022 in CrLP.L.A. No. 184-K/2020).
records.title: Riaz Hussain v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 22-K/2022 in CrLP.L.A. No. 184-K/2020)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Landlord's Personal Bona Fide Need: Settled Principles
records.heading: A landlord's consistent statement on oath suffices to prove bona fide personal need
records.text: Summarises Supreme Court principles on ejectment for personal bona fide need. The tenant's long tenancy, investment and goodwill are irrelevant, the landlord's consistent statement on oath unshaken in cross-examination suffices, the landlord chooses which premises to use, and need not disclose the intended business or prove experience in it. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1303.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Agreement to Sell and s. 17 Registration Act
records.heading: An agreement to sell does not require compulsory registration under section 17
records.text: Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908 requires registration only of instruments that themselves create, declare, assign or extinguish rights in immovable property. An agreement to sell creates only reciprocal obligations and a right to obtain a registered sale deed, so it does not need compulsory registration. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1268.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness, Delay and Co-Sharers
records.heading: Readiness and willingness is judged from overall conduct and not an isolated delay in payment
records.text: Readiness and willingness of the vendee is judged from the parties' overall conduct and not by isolating a delay in payment, particularly where the contract has no penal consequence. Joint property and non-joinder of co-sharers do not defeat the claim, as an agreement by a co-sharer is enforceable to the extent of his share. Appeal dismissed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1268.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 40 and 38 QSO: Disclosure and Police Confession
records.heading: Information under Article 40 QSO is usable only for a distinctly discovered fact
records.text: Under Art. 40 QSO information from an accused is usable only to the extent it relates distinctly to a fact discovered, and not a fact already known to the police. Since two witnesses had already named the petitioner, the confession part failed the test. A confession to police in custody is inadmissible under Art. 38, and no s. 164 CrPC statement was recorded. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1255.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Recovery of Weapon from Open Place
records.heading: Recovery of a weapon from an accessible open place twelve days later is doubtful
records.text: Recovery of the weapon twelve days after the occurrence from an accessible dustbin that had been cleaned in the interval was doubtful. No effort was made to match the blood on the weapon with the victims or to conduct fingerprint examination, so the recovery was unsafe to rely upon. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1255.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Failure to Secure the Crime Scene
records.heading: Failure to secure the crime scene significantly weakens the prosecution case
records.text: Securing the crime scene is a foremost step in investigation that preserves evidence and protects the accused's right to a fair trial. Failure to seal the scene, in a case of murder of a wife and two children, significantly weakened the prosecution case. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1255.

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Pre-emption: Weak Right, Burden, Talb-i-Ishhad Proof
records.heading: The right of pre-emption is weak and the pre-emptor bears the burden of proof
records.text: The right of pre-emption is a weak right and is strictly construed, and the pre-emptor bears the burden of proving the transaction was in reality a sale. Where service of Talb-i-Ishhad is disputed, the postman must be examined and failure to do so is fatal. A pre-emptor must disclose the source of his information on the sale price. Ref: Sultan Ahmad, etc v. Muhammad Azam (C.A.28-L/2011, decided 27.07.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Sultan Ahmad, etc v. Muhammad Azam (C.A.28-L/2011, decided 27.07.2026)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Rectification of Register of Members: No Limitation for Fraud
records.heading: Rectification of the register of members for fraud is not barred by limitation
records.text: A five-member bench of the Supreme Court held that a petition under s. 126 of the Companies Act, 2017 for rectification of the register of members is not barred by limitation where the shareholder was deprived of shares through fraud, affirming 2022 SCMR 1171. Ref: Abdul Razzaq v. Registrar of Companies, Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan Associated House, Lahore & others (C.A. 125/2025, decided 22.04.2026).
records.title: Abdul Razzaq v. Registrar of Companies, Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan Associated House, Lahore & others (C.A. 125/2025, decided 22.04.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 409 PPC: Entrustment as Essential Ingredient
records.heading: Entrustment is the foundation of an offence under section 409 PPC
records.text: A conviction under s. 409 PPC requires proof beyond reasonable doubt of entrustment of or dominion over property, followed by dishonest misappropriation. Entrustment is the foundation of the offence. The prosecution never alleged or proved that the salary was entrusted to the petitioner, so the conviction was legally vulnerable. Ref: Dr Waqar Hameed v. The State and another (Crl.R.P.122/2019, decided 08.06.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Dr Waqar Hameed v. The State and another (Crl.R.P.122/2019, decided 08.06.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Family Pension Not Part of Deceased's Estate
records.heading: Family pension is a personal statutory right and not part of the deceased's estate
records.text: Amounts vested in the deceased in his lifetime may form part of his estate, but family pension is a personal statutory right of the widow and eligible dependents arising on death. It does not pass through succession and collateral relatives cannot claim it unless the pension rules include them. A succession certificate does not confer entitlement to family pension. Ref: Haji Painda Khan & others v. Mst. Gul Indana Bibi & others (C.A.208-P/2015, decided 12.05.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Haji Painda Khan & others v. Mst. Gul Indana Bibi & others (C.A.208-P/2015, decided 12.05.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Counsel's Concession in Court Binds Litigant
records.heading: A solemn concession by an advocate in open court cannot be disowned without evidence
records.text: Under O. III R. 4 CPC and s. 22(3) of the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973, a wakalatnama does not automatically authorise compromise or withdrawal. However, a solemn concession made by a duly engaged advocate in open court cannot be disowned without concrete evidence of lack of authority or fraud, and a party cannot approbate and reprobate. Ref: Muhammad Ashraf v. Akber Ali & others (C.P.L.A.49-K/2026, decided 30.07.2026); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. Akber Ali & others (C.P.L.A.49-K/2026, decided 30.07.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Fraud Must Be Specifically Pleaded
records.heading: A general assertion of fraud is insufficient under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: A bold or general assertion of fraud or misrepresentation is insufficient under s. 12(2) CPC. The applicant must specifically plead and substantiate the exact misrepresentation with cogent particulars, relying on Dadabhoy Cement Industries and Bashir Ahmad, and bare allegations without evidence do not suffice. Ref: Muhammad Ashraf v. Akber Ali & others (C.P.L.A.49-K/2026, decided 30.07.2026); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. Akber Ali & others (C.P.L.A.49-K/2026, decided 30.07.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: S. 4 MFLO: Predeceased Brother's Children Excluded
records.heading: Section 4 MFLO does not extend to the children of a predeceased brother
records.text: Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 gives a per stirpes share only to children of a predeceased son or daughter of the propositus and does not extend to a predeceased brother's children. The concurrent refusal of letters of administration to them was upheld and the revision dismissed. Ref: 2026 MLD 807.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Marking of Exhibit and Photocopies Without Proof
records.heading: A document merely marked as an exhibit without proof has no legal value
records.text: A document merely marked as an exhibit, without being produced and proved through witnesses, has no legal value and cannot be considered by the Court. A photocopy admitted and read without compliance with Art. 76 QSO is illegal, and without formal proof cannot be relied upon. The matter was remanded to the trial Court for fresh decision after recording further evidence. Ref: 2020 CLC 780.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 204 CrPC: Sufficient Ground for Summoning
records.heading: Process under section 204 CrPC requires sufficient ground, not reasonable grounds for believing
records.text: For issuing process on a complaint under s. 204 CrPC, the law requires sufficient ground for proceeding, which is not the same as the reasonable ground for believing under s. 497(1) CrPC. A prima facie case means one that can be established if the evidence is believed. Courts must not lightly accept private complaints under ss. 190 and 200 CrPC. The complaint and revision were dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 557; Muhammad Latif Khan v. Imran etc. (Crl. Misc. 13016/26).
records.title: Muhammad Latif Khan v. Imran etc. (Crl. Misc. 13016/26)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Photocopy of Document Without Proof of Loss
records.heading: A photocopy has no legal value without proof that the original was lost
records.text: Where nothing on the record shows that the original document was lost and there is no order for reconstruction of record by the competent authority, mere production of a photocopy has no legal value and cannot be read in evidence. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 598, 2026 PCrLJ 1515; Muhammad Sabir v. The State (Jail Appeal 14716/23).
records.title: Muhammad Sabir v. The State (Jail Appeal 14716/23)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 27(b) Specific Relief Act: Bona Fide Purchaser
records.heading: Subsequent transferees bear a heavy burden to prove they are bona fide purchasers
records.text: Subsequent transferees bear a heavy burden to prove they are bona fide purchasers for value without notice under s. 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. The plea requires cogent evidence of good faith and prudent inquiry into title. Haste, lack of inquiry or facts putting the purchaser on notice defeat the protection, and the prior agreement remains enforceable against the transferee. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 400, 2026 SCMR 1572; Mian Mohammad Mehmood Ahmed (deceased) v. Safdar Hussain (Civil Appeal No. 168-L/14 etc.).
records.title: Mian Mohammad Mehmood Ahmed (deceased) v. Safdar Hussain (Civil Appeal No. 168-L/14 etc.)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Without Wife's Consent or Election
records.heading: Khula should not ordinarily be granted without the wife's consent or clear election
records.text: Khula should not ordinarily be granted without the wife's consent or clear election where she sued on cruelty and valuable financial rights are involved. Where cruelty is not proved and the marriage has manifestly collapsed, the Court must allow the wife to elect between pursuing dismissal of her claim and accepting dissolution by khula on lawful terms. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 406, 2026 SCMR 1717; Mst. Selab Akhtar v. Quwat Khan & Others (C.P.L.A. No. 4792/2025).
records.title: Mst. Selab Akhtar v. Quwat Khan & Others (C.P.L.A. No. 4792/2025)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Long-Standing Revenue Entries and Third-Party Rights
records.heading: Unexplained delay in challenging long-standing revenue entries renders the claim untenable
records.text: Long-standing revenue entries on whose faith third parties acquired rights should not be disturbed after decades, and unexplained delay in challenging mutations renders the claim untenable. Such entries carry a presumption of regularity and correctness. The High Court erred in reappraising evidence in revision without addressing the s. 172 bar, and the impugned judgments could not be sustained. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 415, 2026 SCMR 1817; Nadeem Akhtar (deceased) through LRs. & Others v. Manzoor Ahmad (C.P.L.A. No. 1086/2019).
records.title: Nadeem Akhtar (deceased) through LRs. & Others v. Manzoor Ahmad (C.P.L.A. No. 1086/2019)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Locus Standi in Constitutional Jurisdiction
records.heading: Locus standi depends on whether the impugned action adversely affects legal rights or interests
records.text: Locus standi is determined by whether the impugned action adversely affects the legal rights, lawful interests or legitimate expectations of the person invoking constitutional jurisdiction. A person divested of an accrued statutory right or prejudiced in civil consequences cannot be denied judicial review merely because he is not the direct addressee or beneficiary of the order. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 422; (Civil Appeals 382-L & 383-L of 2012).
records.title: (Civil Appeals 382-L & 383-L of 2012)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Lawyers' Strike and Licence Suspension
records.heading: Suspending a lawyer's licence for taking part in a strike is unlawful
records.text: The Federal Constitutional Court held unlawful the strike by lawyers and the suspension of a lawyer's licence on that basis. The profession of advocacy is a constitutional right, and a licence cannot be suspended merely for participating in a strike or for representing a controversial accused. Ref: PLJ 2026 FCC 45; Peshawar High Court Bar v. Shabbir Hussain & another (F.C.P.L.A. Nos. 379, 380, 384 and 389 of 2025).
records.title: Peshawar High Court Bar v. Shabbir Hussain & another (F.C.P.L.A. Nos. 379, 380, 384 and 389 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXIX R. 2(3) CPC: Sentence for Violating Injunction
records.heading: Continuous defiance of an injunction may be punished under Order XXXIX Rule 2(3) CPC
records.text: Violation of an injunction may be inferred from a series of acts showing continuous defiance of the Court. Proceedings under O. XXXIX R. 2(3) CPC are quasi-criminal, and the Court has discretion to attach property, order detention up to six months, or both. The Appellate Court exceeded its jurisdiction by substituting its own discretion without showing illegality or perversity. A reasoned order on sentence was directed, considering proportionality and the later dismissal of the suit. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 502; Muhammad Asif Qureshi & others v. Hakim Ghulam Murtaza & others (Civil Revision No. 38 of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Asif Qureshi & others v. Hakim Ghulam Murtaza & others (Civil Revision No. 38 of 2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Death of Drawer and Execution
records.heading: Legal representatives are liable under the decree only to the extent of the inherited estate
records.text: The objection that a summary suit was not maintainable under ss. 29 and 29-A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 was misconceived, as the suit was validly instituted against the drawer, unlike the authority relied on where suit followed death. Under s. 50 CPC the decree is executable against the legal representatives only to the extent of estate inherited by them, which the Executing Court may determine on objection. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 534; Mst. Zubaida Khanam etc v. Haji Muhammad Siddique (R.F.A. 84-13).
records.title: Mst. Zubaida Khanam etc v. Haji Muhammad Siddique (R.F.A. 84-13)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Landlord Status and Scope of Rent Jurisdiction
records.heading: Rent proceedings are summary and a landlord need not strictly prove ownership
records.text: Proceedings under the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009 are summary and do not involve adjudication of complex title questions. Under s. 2(d) a landlord includes a person entitled or authorised to receive rent, so strict proof of ownership is not required. Where tenancy is denied, the person asserting it must prove it, and the Rent Court must confine itself to tenancy, rent, default and statutory grounds. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 468; Muhammad Mansha v. Additional District Judge, Khanewal & another (W.P. No. 18312 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Mansha v. Additional District Judge, Khanewal & another (W.P. No. 18312 of 2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Attorney's Authority to Withdraw Suit
records.heading: An attorney's authority to withdraw a suit is fiduciary and must be exercised bona fide
records.text: Even where a special power of attorney authorises withdrawal of a suit, the agent's authority is fiduciary and governed by ss. 214 and 215 of the Contract Act, 1872. Its exercise must be bona fide, within the mandate and with the principal's knowledge and consent. The orders dismissing the suit as withdrawn were set aside, the attorney's statement nullified and the suit reinstated. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 481, PLD 2026 Lah 708; Fateh Shakeel v. Additional District Judge, Rahim Yar Khan and others (Writ Petition No. 10216 of 2023).
records.title: Fateh Shakeel v. Additional District Judge, Rahim Yar Khan and others (Writ Petition No. 10216 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC After Refusal of Leave by Supreme Court
records.heading: Forum for a section 12(2) CPC application after leave to appeal is declined
records.text: The Supreme Court considered whether, after leave to appeal against a High Court judgment is declined, an application under s. 12(2) CPC lies before the High Court or the Supreme Court. It examined the scheme of s. 12(2), the doctrine of merger and its own case law on which forum rendered the operative adjudication. The post does not give the final holding.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: S. 172 Land Revenue Act: Bar on Civil Courts
records.heading: Section 172 of the Land Revenue Act bars civil suits for correction of revenue entries
records.text: Section 172(2)(vii) of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Act, 1967 bars the Civil Court from entertaining a claim for correction of an entry in a record-of-rights or register of mutations. Where the real relief is rectification of revenue entries simpliciter, the suit is barred and not maintainable before the Civil Court. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 415, 2026 SCMR 1817; Nadeem Akhtar (deceased) through LRs. & Others v. Manzoor Ahmad (C.P.L.A. No. 1086/2019).
records.title: Nadeem Akhtar (deceased) through LRs. & Others v. Manzoor Ahmad (C.P.L.A. No. 1086/2019)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Lengthy Cross-Examination in Family Courts
records.heading: Unduly lengthy cross-examination is discouraged and Family Courts may forbid offensive questions
records.text: Unduly lengthy cross-examination with irrelevant questions can rob contradictions of significance and is discouraged. Under the second proviso to s. 11 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 the Family Court may forbid indecent, scandalous, frivolous, insulting, annoying or offensive questions. Family and Guardian Courts must actively curb delay. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 474; Harris Rasheed and another v. The Learned Guardian Judge (Writ Petition No. 64981 of 2025).
records.title: Harris Rasheed and another v. The Learned Guardian Judge (Writ Petition No. 64981 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Decree: Simple or Compound Annual Increase
records.heading: Annual increase on maintenance silent on compounding is calculated on the original amount
records.text: Where a maintenance decree is silent on compounding, the annual increase is calculated on the originally decreed amount and not on the accumulated sum. The Executing Court erred in applying compound increase, and the Appellate Court rightly corrected it. Family Courts must state expressly whether the periodic increase is simple or compound. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 429; Muhammad Waqar Wasi v. Mst. Amber Abid & others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3204 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Waqar Wasi v. Mst. Amber Abid & others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3204 of 2022)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Belated Removal of Office Objections: Time Bar
records.heading: Failure to remove office objections in time makes the proceedings time-barred
records.text: Where office objections render the institution of proceedings incompetent, failure to remove them within the prescribed time makes the proceedings time-barred once limitation expires. A filing incapable of constituting valid institution within limitation cannot become valid because defects are cured later. The Commissioner's petitions against dismissal of references by the Lahore High Court were dismissed. Ref: Commissioner Inland Revenue, Faisalabad v. M/s. Al-Hamd Cotton Ginning Pressing Factory, Jhang (C.P.L.A. 41-L/2026, decided 31.07.2026); Justice Yahya Afridi; Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui.
records.title: Commissioner Inland Revenue, Faisalabad v. M/s. Al-Hamd Cotton Ginning Pressing Factory, Jhang (C.P.L.A. 41-L/2026, decided 31.07.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wife's Death in Matrimonial Home: Art. 122 QSO
records.heading: Article 122 QSO requires the prosecution first to link the accused with the wife's homicidal death
records.text: Absence of some signs of strangulation, or an intact hyoid bone, does not exclude strangulation, but here the medical evidence failed to corroborate the ocular account. In the homicidal death of a wife at home, the prosecution must first link the accused with the occurrence before Art. 122 QSO can require the husband's explanation, and its application is not automatic. Suspicion, however grave, cannot replace proof beyond reasonable doubt. Ref: 2026 LHC 4903; Tanveer v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 7335/2022); Mian Khan v. The State and another (Criminal Revision No. 26176/2022).
records.title: Tanveer v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 7335/2022); Mian Khan v. The State and another (Criminal Revision No. 26176/2022)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Meaning of Banker in S. 409 PPC
records.heading: The term banker in section 409 PPC is determined by a functional test
records.text: The term banker in s. 409 PPC is not limited to executives, nor does it cover every bank employee. A functional test applies: the property must be that with which banking business is transacted, including customer funds and customer data under s. 27(2) PECA, and the employee must be entrusted with it or have dominion over it by his banking function. Bare custody or incidental access attracts s. 408 PPC instead. Ref: 2026 LHC 4884; Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 76474-B/2025); Muhammad Atif v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 20288-B/2026).
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 76474-B/2025); Muhammad Atif v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 20288-B/2026)

records.subject: Arbitration
records.topic: Estoppel After No Demand Certificate
records.heading: A contractor who accepted final payment and issued a No Demand Certificate is estopped
records.text: Under Art. 114 QSO, a party that induces another to act on a representation cannot later resile from it to the other's prejudice. A contractor who unequivocally accepted final payment and issued a No Demand Certificate cannot revive claims for idle charges or price escalation through arbitration. Ref: M/s Ghulam Siddiqe, Ghulam Habib & Company Pvt Peshawar v. Govt of NWFP (Now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) thr: Chief Engineer & Works Deptt: Peshawar & others (C.P.L.A. 244-P/2016, decided 22.07.2026); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: M/s Ghulam Siddiqe, Ghulam Habib & Company Pvt Peshawar v. Govt of NWFP (Now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) thr: Chief Engineer & Works Deptt: Peshawar & others (C.P.L.A. 244-P/2016, decided 22.07.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail of Foreign Husband of Pakistani Citizen
records.heading: Pending proceedings on the accused's citizenship status are relevant circumstances for bail
records.text: The Federal Shariat Court held s. 10 of the Citizenship Act, 1951 discriminatory for lacking a path to citizenship for foreign husbands of Pakistani women, and an appeal against that judgment is pending. Pending proceedings on the accused's status and issuance of a POC are relevant circumstances for bail, and pre-trial detention in such circumstances serves no legitimate purpose. Ref: Jalat Khan v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P.L.A.894/2026, decided 03.08.2026); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Jalat Khan v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and another (Crl.P.L.A.894/2026, decided 03.08.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC and Repeated Last Opportunities
records.heading: Courts should not repeatedly grant last opportunities, and must record reasons for indulgence
records.text: Order XVII Rule 3 CPC cannot be invoked to close the plaintiff's evidence where the previous adjournment was not sought by the plaintiff. Courts should not repeatedly grant last and final opportunities. If default warrants consequences, the Court should invoke the provision, and where further indulgence is justified it must record reasons and impose realistic costs. Ref: Shakeel Ahmad, etc v. Abdul Ghaffar (C.A.357-L/2013, decided 03.08.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Shakeel Ahmad, etc v. Abdul Ghaffar (C.A.357-L/2013, decided 03.08.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Resiling Witness: Declared Hostile, Art. 150 QSO
records.heading: A witness resiling in cross-examination may be declared hostile under Article 150 QSO
records.text: If a witness testifies in examination in chief in line with his police statement but departs from it during cross-examination to favour the accused, the court may declare him hostile and permit the party seeking it to cross-examine him. The application of Art. 150 QSO is not limited to the examination in chief of the witness. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 942.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: No Retrospective Penalty on Past Tax Assessments
records.heading: New penalties cannot be imposed on past tax assessments without clear legal authority
records.text: A five-member Supreme Court bench, as reported, held that new penalties cannot be imposed on past tax matters without clear legal authority, a tax penalty being an additional financial liability and not mere procedure. Concluded assessments cannot be burdened by later legislation. The tax department's appeal was dismissed. Ref: Commissioner Inland Revenue (Legal) RTO, Rawalpindi v. Khadim Hussain & others (Civil Appeal No. 2480 of 2016).
records.title: Commissioner Inland Revenue (Legal) RTO, Rawalpindi v. Khadim Hussain & others (Civil Appeal No. 2480 of 2016)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Binding Force of Co-Equal Bench Judgments
records.heading: An earlier judgment of a co-equal bench binds later benches of equal strength
records.text: An earlier judgment of a bench of co-equal strength binds benches of smaller and equal strength. A subsequent bench wishing to take a contrary view must refer the matter to the Chief Justice for constitution of a larger bench to reconsider the earlier view. Ref: Commissioner Inland Revenue (Legal) RTO, Rawalpindi v. Khadim Hussain & others (Civil Appeal No. 2480 of 2016).
records.title: Commissioner Inland Revenue (Legal) RTO, Rawalpindi v. Khadim Hussain & others (Civil Appeal No. 2480 of 2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Suicide and Asphyxia Death: Ligature Findings
records.heading: Specified ligature and body findings indicate asphyxia by hanging, deemed suicide
records.text: If the ligature mark is not round the neck, the eyes are closed, ribs are not fractured and hands are not clenched, the case is one of suicide. Such findings point to a very high probability of asphyxia by hanging, which is deemed suicide or unnatural death rather than homicide. Ref: 2025 SCMR 730; Muhammad Ehsan Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 231/2021).
records.title: Muhammad Ehsan Shah v. The State thr. A.G. Islamabad and another (Crl.P.L.A. 231/2021)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Declaring Prosecution Witness Hostile: Art. 150 QSO
records.heading: The Court must be satisfied that hostility exists before declaring a prosecution witness hostile
records.text: A prosecution witness is in the prosecution's hands during examination-in-chief and passes to the defence for cross-examination. Under Art. 150 QSO the prosecution may seek to have a witness declared hostile if he resiles from a previous statement, but the Court must first satisfy itself that the requisite elements exist. The trial Court failed to do so, and the petitioner made out a case for interference in revision. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 722.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: S. 161 CrPC Statements: Limited Use for Contradiction
records.heading: Section 161 CrPC statements are usable only for contradiction under Article 140 QSO
records.text: Statements recorded under s. 161 CrPC are not admissible in evidence except for the limited purpose of contradiction under Art. 140 QSO. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 2222.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Res Gestae: Accused's Statement to Rescue Workers
records.heading: A statement made soon after the incident to rescue workers is admissible as res gestae
records.text: Under Art. 19(a) QSO, a statement made soon after the incident is relevant because of its spontaneity and immediacy, provided it forms part of the same transaction and there was no interval allowing fabrication. The accused's statements to Rescue 1122 personnel, who were not police officers, were admissible as res gestae and aided the prosecution. Ref: 2024 YLR 628.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Attorney's Authority to Enter Agreement to Sell
records.heading: An attorney authorised to sell has implied authority to execute an agreement to sell
records.text: A registered power of attorney attracts the presumption of due execution under Art. 95 QSO. An attorney authorised to sell has implied and incidental authority to execute the agreement to sell, under ss. 188 and 189 of the Contract Act, 1872, unless the instrument expressly restricts it. The High Court's contrary view was not accepted. Ref: Saad Younis, etc v. Ghulam Bari & others (C.A.435-L/2012, decided 10.08.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Saad Younis, etc v. Ghulam Bari & others (C.A.435-L/2012, decided 10.08.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII CPC: Defendant Absent at Cross-Examination
records.heading: Order XVII Rules 2 and 3 CPC govern a defendant's absence at cross-examination
records.text: After two adjournments had been granted and the defendant's counsel failed to appear on the date fixed for cross-examination, the options open to the court were those in Rules 2 and 3 of Order XVII CPC. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 887; Lutfullah Virk v. Muhammad Aslam Sheikh (Civil Petition No. 2849-L of 2015).
records.title: Lutfullah Virk v. Muhammad Aslam Sheikh (Civil Petition No. 2849-L of 2015)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Art. 10-A: Fair Trial and Joint Cross-Examination
records.heading: Joint cross-examination by counsel for several accused is not recognised under Article 10-A
records.text: Art. 10-A requires that an accused be informed of the grounds of arrest, be defended by a lawyer, and be given the opportunity to cross-examine witnesses, explain the evidence and produce defence evidence. Depriving an accused of cross-examination violates the fundamental right to fair trial. Joint cross-examination by counsel for several accused is not recognised, and the court should record who is cross-examining. Leave was refused. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 334.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Denial of Opportunity to Cross-Examine Witnesses
records.heading: A defendant denied cross-examination of the plaintiff's witnesses is entitled to remand
records.text: A defendant who was given no opportunity to cross-examine the plaintiff's witnesses was entitled to remand by the Appellate Court for that purpose. The plaintiff pointed to no illegality, material irregularity or jurisdictional defect, and the civil revision was dismissed. Ref: 2025 YLR 2794.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Eviction on Expiry of Tenancy Not Pleaded
records.heading: Ejectment may follow expiry of tenancy during proceedings without a fresh petition
records.text: In principle an ejectment order can only be passed on the grounds taken in the petition. Where tenancy expires during the proceedings, requiring the landlord to file a fresh petition on that ground would let the tenant linger in occupation and does not suit the object of the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009 of expeditious, cost-effective resolution. Ref: 2026 CLC 1292; Muhammad Saleem Minhas v. Ashfaq Hussain Minhas etc. (WP-2292-24).
records.title: Muhammad Saleem Minhas v. Ashfaq Hussain Minhas etc. (WP-2292-24)

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: Territorial Jurisdiction of Special Judge
records.heading: A Special Judge may take cognizance only of offences within the notified territorial limits
records.text: Under s. 4 of the Act of 1958, a Special Judge has jurisdiction only within the territorial limits fixed by the government and may take cognizance only of offences committed within them. Section 6 applies the Code with a non-obstante clause. A court lacking territorial jurisdiction cannot ordinarily proceed with the case. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 624; Abdul Basit v. Senior Special Judge, Anti-Corruption Court, Lahore, etc. (Criminal Revision No. 20366 of 2026).
records.title: Abdul Basit v. Senior Special Judge, Anti-Corruption Court, Lahore, etc. (Criminal Revision No. 20366 of 2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Private Complaint: Delay and Scrutiny under S. 202 CrPC
records.heading: Delay and lack of a prima facie case defeat a private complaint under section 202 CrPC
records.text: In a private complaint filed about a year after the occurrence, inordinate delay casts doubt on the allegations. Under ss. 202 to 204 CrPC courts must scrutinise the allegations and purpose of the complaint to protect the accused from frivolous summoning. A written complaint should not be lightly accepted until a prima facie case appears, and the complainant failed to establish one. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 557.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Right of Private Defence Exceeded: S. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: Exceeding the right of private defence reduces the offence to section 302(c) PPC
records.text: With no motive and no prior enmity, and the accused himself injured in a sudden fight started by the complainant party, the evidence supported his plea of self-defence, though he exceeded the right. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC was converted to s. 302(c) PPC and a sentence of 15 years R.I. awarded. Ref: Haji Ahmad Bakhsh v. The State (Jail Petition No. 543 of 2021).
records.title: Haji Ahmad Bakhsh v. The State (Jail Petition No. 543 of 2021)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Supersession and Deferment of Promotion
records.heading: Deferment of promotion denotes administrative delay and not a finding of unfitness
records.text: Supersession is the appointing authority's decision, on the Departmental Promotion Committee's recommendation, to pass over an officer for promotion on stated grounds recorded in writing. Deferment denotes an administrative delay and not a finding of unfitness, and may be recommended where, for instance, performance evaluation reports are not submitted or the service record is incomplete. Ref: Faheemuddin Memon v. Province of Sindh (CPLA Nos. 914-K to 919-K of 2023).
records.title: Faheemuddin Memon v. Province of Sindh (CPLA Nos. 914-K to 919-K of 2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Acid Attack: S. 336-B PPC Sentence
records.heading: Acid throwing established under section 336-B PPC merits the maximum penalty
records.text: Where acid was thrown on the victim in daylight inside the family home, the consistent ocular account, supporting medical evidence and positive forensic report established the offence under s. 336-B PPC, which carries a minimum of 14 years R.I. extendable to life and a minimum fine of one million rupees. The intentional act of disfigurement was held to merit the maximum penalty. Ref: Abdul Manan @ Imran v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1718/2022).
records.title: Abdul Manan @ Imran v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 1718/2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Judicial and Retracted Confession in Capital Case
records.heading: A retracted confession needs independent corroboration and cannot alone convict in a capital case
records.text: A confession containing minute, highly structured details of many murders, lacking spontaneity, raises doubt about its voluntariness and truth. A retracted confession requires independent corroboration in material particulars and cannot be the sole basis of conviction in a capital case. Disregarding the allegations' effect on named persons offended Art. 10A. Ref: Ahmed Saeed @ Bharam @ Nagori v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 649/2022 in J.P. No. 385/2019).
records.title: Ahmed Saeed @ Bharam @ Nagori v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 649/2022 in J.P. No. 385/2019)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Compounding of Qatl-i-Amd: Heirs Resiling
records.heading: Heirs who made compounding statements before the Trial Court could not later retract them
records.text: Legal heirs who made compounding statements before the Trial Court and did not challenge them in the High Court could not later retract them. In view of their affidavits of forgiveness and about 10 and a half years in the death cell, the death sentence was altered to life imprisonment under s. 338-E PPC read with s. 345 CrPC, and the appeal was partly allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 480; Sanoober Khan v. State.
records.title: Sanoober Khan v. State

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Inconsistent Pleas: Effect
records.heading: A party is debarred from taking inconsistent pleas that are self-destructive
records.text: A party is debarred from taking inconsistent pleas which prejudice the other party's right and are self-destructive. Ref: 2006 PLC 630.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Written Statement
records.heading: Contradictory and mutually destructive pleas cannot be introduced by amendment of a written statement
records.text: Alternative or inconsistent pleas may be taken, but contradictory and mutually destructive pleas cannot be introduced by amendment. Amendment must not change the nature or cause of action, and mere delay is no ground for refusal. The proposed amendment merely elaborated facts, so the orders of the Courts below were set aside and the application accepted. Ref: 2019 CLC 1432.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Amendment of Framed Issues
records.heading: The Court may amend framed issues unless it alters the nature of the suit
records.text: The Court has discretion to amend framed issues where no injustice results, but not where it alters the nature of the suit, permits a new case or changes the parties' stand through inconsistent pleas. Ref: 2021 CLC 1491.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Alternative and Inconsistent Pleas
records.heading: Alternative or inconsistent pleas may be taken but contradictory pleas may not
records.text: Alternative or inconsistent pleas can be taken, but contradictory and mutually destructive pleas cannot be raised. Ref: 2025 CLC 1382.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder of Wife After Khula: Death Sentence Upheld
records.heading: Exercising the right to khula is protected and the death sentence for murder was upheld
records.text: As reported, the Supreme Court held that exercising the right to khula is protected under Arts. 9, 14 and 25, and a cold, planned murder of a woman for doing so merits no leniency. Relatives' testimony for a crime inside the home cannot be rejected, and forensic matching of shell and pistol was strong proof. The death sentence was upheld. Ref: Waseem Abbas (J.P. 617/2025).
records.title: Waseem Abbas (J.P. 617/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Reduced: Circumstantial Evidence, No Motive
records.heading: A death sentence was reduced to life imprisonment on circumstantial evidence without proved motive
records.text: Where the case rested on circumstantial evidence and motive was not proved, what happened immediately before the occurrence could not be determined, so death was too harsh and life imprisonment met the ends of justice. The Court also noted denial of audience and Art. 10-A, and the prosecution's concession that the extreme penalty was not warranted. Ref: Sher Azam v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Crl.M.Appeal.9/2017, decided 19.05.2026); Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan; Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Sher Azam v. The State thr. A.G. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Crl.M.Appeal.9/2017, decided 19.05.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Does Not Create Title; Pert Sarkar
records.heading: Mutation entries neither create nor extinguish title without proof of the underlying transaction
records.text: Mutation entries neither create nor extinguish title and cannot confer ownership unless the underlying transaction is independently proved. A sale mutation recording no admission by the vendor is weakened, and deliberate non-production of the primary official record (pert sarkar) reinforces the conclusion that the defendants failed to establish a valid transfer. Ref: Ghani Rehman v. Masal Khan (Civil Appeal No. 19-P of 2015 out of CPLA No. 192-7 of 2009, decided 23.06.2026).
records.title: Ghani Rehman v. Masal Khan (Civil Appeal No. 19-P of 2015 out of CPLA No. 192-7 of 2009, decided 23.06.2026)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Super Tax: Adjustment Against Tax Credit
records.heading: Super tax may be adjusted against tax credit under section 168
records.text: As reported, the Federal Constitutional Court held that super tax may be adjusted against tax credit, and that the credit under s. 168 is a distinct recognised right, so a taxpayer cannot be confined to refund. Fiscal statutes are to be construed in favour of the taxpayer. The Islamabad High Court judgment was set aside, the appeals were allowed and FBR was directed to decide the adjustment claim in response to the notice. Ref: CM Pak Limited v. The Federation of Pakistan (F.C.P.L.A. No. 1276 of 2026); Justice Amir Farooq.
records.title: CM Pak Limited v. The Federation of Pakistan (F.C.P.L.A. No. 1276 of 2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Video-Recorded Statement to Police Not Substantive Evidence
records.heading: A video-recorded statement to police is not substantive evidence
records.text: A video recording must be proved genuine and free from tampering under the guidelines in PLD 2019 SC 675 before use. A statement made by a witness to the police during investigation cannot be used as substantive evidence, and this applies equally to video-recorded statements. Ref: 2026 MLD 1244; Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8607/B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8607/B/2025)

records.subject: Juvenile Justice
records.topic: Bail Under S. 6 Juvenile Justice System Act 2018
records.heading: A juvenile may claim bail as of right if section 6(5) is met
records.text: Under s. 6(3) a juvenile accused of a minor or major offence is treated as accused of a bailable offence. Section 6(4) concerns bail on merits for heinous offences, while s. 6(5) gives a distinct ground for bail after six months' detention without conclusion of trial, unless the delay is attributable to the juvenile. Relying on Mehran, a juvenile in a heinous offence may claim post-arrest bail as of right if s. 6(5) is met. Ref: 2026 MLD 1244; Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8607/B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8607/B/2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Police Statement of Accused Inadmissible at Bail Stage
records.heading: An accused's statement to police is barred by section 162 CrPC even if video-recorded
records.text: An exculpatory statement recorded by police in custody, not before a Magistrate, is barred by s. 162 CrPC, even if video-recorded, and cannot be used at the bail stage except for contradiction. Art. 10A applies at all stages. With no other incriminating material, the case fell within further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Ref: 2026 MLD 1244; Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8607/B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8607/B/2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Call Detail Records: Evidentiary Worth at Bail Stage
records.heading: Call detail records at bail stage need corroboration and exclusion of alternative explanations
