records.text: CDRs may form part of circumstantial evidence, but their worth depends on corroboration and exclusion of alternative explanations, since the accused may not have held the phone. With no material that the SIM was registered to or exclusively used by the petitioner, the Court must approach such material with circumspection at the bail stage. Ref: 2026 MLD 1244; Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8607/B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Naveed v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 8607/B/2025)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Notice to Tenant on Change of Ownership: S. 30
records.heading: No notice to the tenant is required on change of ownership under section 30
records.text: On change of ownership, no notice to the tenant is required under s. 30 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009, because filing the ejectment application is itself notice to the tenant. Ref: 2026 MLD 1384; Muhammad Irshad v. Khawar Sabtain etc. (Writ Petition-4274-23); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Muhammad Irshad v. Khawar Sabtain etc. (Writ Petition-4274-23)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody of Narcotic Samples and S. 161 Statements
records.heading: Failure to prove safe custody of narcotic samples is fatal to the prosecution
records.text: Failure to prove safe custody of sample parcels and remaining case property, from recovery through transmission to the forensic agency and deposit in the malkhana, is fatal to the prosecution. Non-recording of material witnesses' s. 161 CrPC statements requires their testimony to be evaluated with extreme caution, and unexplained delay in recording one raises reasonable doubt. Ref: 2026 YLR 1742; Ashfaq alias Saleem v. The State, etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 43161 of 2023).
records.title: Ashfaq alias Saleem v. The State, etc. (Crl. Appeal No. 43161 of 2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Oral Gift Excluding Sister: Burden of Proof
records.heading: A donee claiming an oral gift excluding an heir must prove its prerequisites
records.text: A donee claiming an oral gift that excludes a legal heir must allege and prove the prerequisites of a valid gift, including when, where and before which witnesses it was made. The brother failed to do so, so the sister's share was upheld. A claim to inheritance is not barred merely by limitation, and the revision was dismissed. Ref: 2026 YLR 1912; Muhammad Riaz v. Mst. Najma Bibi and others (C.R. No. 1196 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz v. Mst. Najma Bibi and others (C.R. No. 1196 of 2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution of Dower Decree: Alleged Satisfaction
records.heading: Compromises extinguishing a woman's decretal entitlements made within 24 hours warrant strict scrutiny
records.text: The protective procedural framework of the Family Courts Act, 1964 extends to execution of family decrees, so the Executing Court need not frame issues under s. 47 CPC on a vague document allegedly satisfying the decree. Compromises extinguishing a woman's entitlements, made within 24 hours of the decree and without definite terms, warrant strict scrutiny. Ref: 2026 YLR 1949; Ejaz-ur-Rehman v. ADJ etc. (Writ Petition-9437-24).
records.title: Ejaz-ur-Rehman v. ADJ etc. (Writ Petition-9437-24)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Setting Aside Ex Parte Decree After Divorce Finality
records.heading: An ex parte decree cannot be set aside where the divorce has attained finality
records.text: Where the divorce had attained finality and the wife had remarried and had children, an application to set aside the ex parte judgment and decree was not maintainable, as no effective relief could be given and interference would disturb settled rights. Ref: 2026 YLR 1939; Faisal Imran v. Mst. Shaheen (Writ Petition No. 2706 of 2025).
records.title: Faisal Imran v. Mst. Shaheen (Writ Petition No. 2706 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Executing Court Cannot Travel Beyond Decree
records.heading: An executing court cannot travel beyond the terms of the decree
records.text: Where maintenance was conditional on performance of marital obligations and the wife later obtained khula, the Courts below travelled beyond the decree in execution and ignored the binding effect of earlier orders. The attachment order was vague and passed without hearing. The petition was allowed and the objection petition remitted to the Executing Court. Ref: 2026 YLR 1939; Faisal Imran v. Mst. Shaheen (Writ Petition No. 2706 of 2025).
records.title: Faisal Imran v. Mst. Shaheen (Writ Petition No. 2706 of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Reduction on Assumed Non-Consummation
records.heading: Dower cannot be reduced on assumed non-consummation that was never pleaded
records.text: Where the wife pleaded impotence but did not plead non-consummation, no issue was framed on it, and the marriage was dissolved by khula, the findings of both Courts below treating the marriage as non-consummated and reducing dower were legally untenable. The petition was allowed and she was held entitled to half of the house or Rs. 750,000. Ref: 2026 YLR 1713; Saima Sarwar v. DJ (WP. 5288 of 2019).
records.title: Saima Sarwar v. DJ (WP. 5288 of 2019)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Interim Order on Prisoner's Hospital Transfer and Medical Record
records.heading: The Supreme Court directed a prisoner's hospital transfer under security and production of medical records
records.text: In an interim order the Supreme Court called for the prisoner's medical record and directed his transfer to Shifa International Hospital under security, with a medical board, family meetings and costs borne by the family. The complete medical reports are to be placed before the Court on the next hearing. Ref: Mashal Azam v. Ghafoor Anjum, Superintendent Central Jail, Adyala, tehsil and district Rawalpindi and others (Crl.A.400/2025, decided 18.08.2026); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mashal Azam v. Ghafoor Anjum, Superintendent Central Jail, Adyala, tehsil and district Rawalpindi and others (Crl.A.400/2025, decided 18.08.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth in Matriculation Certificate
records.heading: Alteration of date of birth in an academic record needs unimpeachable evidence
records.text: Alteration of vital particulars in an academic record must rest on unimpeachable evidence. The contemporaneous admission form bearing the plaintiff's signature carried the highest evidentiary value over a later birth certificate. The Courts below had misread and non-read evidence. The authorities also pleaded a bar under s. 29 of the Punjab Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Act, 1976. Ref: 2026 MLD 1397.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Cannot Be Granted Without Wife's Consent
records.heading: A court cannot of its own motion convert a cruelty claim into khula
records.text: A court cannot of its own motion convert a prayer for dissolution on grounds of cruelty into a decree of khula. Even where cruelty is not proved but marital breakdown is shown, khula requires the wife's explicit, informed and voluntary consent. Ref: 2026 CLC 1312.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay in Civil Revision
records.heading: Section 5 of the Limitation Act extends to civil revisions but needs sufficient cause
records.text: After the amendment of the First Schedule (Art. 162-A), s. 5 of the Limitation Act extends to civil revisions under s. 115 CPC, but the party must show sufficient cause. Limitation is not a mere technicality. A delay of 21 days was not supported by any sufficient cause, and condonation was refused. Ref: 2026 CLC 1241.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Adverse Possession by Co-Sharer
records.heading: A co-sharer's possession of the whole property is not adverse to other co-sharers
records.text: Where property is held by several co-owners and one co-sharer possesses the whole, his possession cannot be treated as adverse to the other co-sharers. Ref: 2026 CLC 1299.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Waiting List: Filling Resultant Vacancies
records.heading: Soliciting only one candidate for two vacancies from the waiting list was arbitrary
records.text: Soliciting only one candidate despite two resultant vacancies during the validity of the waiting list was arbitrary and defeated the petitioner's legitimate expectation. The Government of Punjab, with the Punjab Public Service Commission, was directed to devise a transparent, time-bound mechanism to fill all such vacancies from the waiting list. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 982.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Issues, Fraud and Subsequent Purchaser
records.heading: Framing issues on a section 12(2) CPC application is not required in every case
records.text: Framing issues on a s. 12(2) CPC application depends on the circumstances, and doing so in every case would frustrate its object. Fraud must be of an egregious nature on the Court, proved by clear and convincing evidence. No fraud on the Court was shown, the application was rightly dismissed, and the revision was dismissed. Ref: 2026 MLD 1294.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Dismissal Without Inquiry Under PEEDA Act
records.heading: Dismissal from service on show cause notice alone without inquiry cannot stand under PEEDA
records.text: The Lahore High Court held that dismissal from service is not a penalty under the Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability Act, so dismissal on a show cause notice alone, without inquiry, could not stand. The department may hold a regular inquiry into the allegations and decide the petitioner's benefits. Ref: 2026 LHC 5289; Shafique Khushnood v. MS General Hospital etc. (W.P. 6323/26, decided 20.05.2026); Justice Malik Muhammad Awais Khalid.
records.title: Shafique Khushnood v. MS General Hospital etc. (W.P. 6323/26, decided 20.05.2026)

records.subject: Land Acquisition
records.topic: Enhanced Compensation for Non-Litigating Landowners
records.heading: A landowner who accepted the award without protest cannot claim another's enhanced compensation
records.text: A landowner who accepted the Collector's Award without protest, or did not seek reference under s. 18 or pursue remedies, cannot claim the benefit of enhanced compensation awarded to another in independent proceedings. The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is a complete code, and extending the benefit would be judicial legislation, a matter for Parliament. Ref: (C.A.192-P of 2010, announced 20.08.2026).
records.title: (C.A.192-P of 2010, announced 20.08.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Amended S. 510 CrPC: Forensic Reports Retrospective
records.heading: Amended section 510 CrPC on forensic reports is procedural and applies to pending proceedings
records.text: Amended s. 510 CrPC brings forensic scientists within the experts whose reports may be used without calling the maker. It concerns only mode of proof, creates no offence and takes away no right, so being procedural it ordinarily applies to pending proceedings unless an accrued right is impaired. Ref: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State through A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.R.P.89/2025); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State through A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.R.P.89/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Plea of Mental Illness as Mitigating Circumstance
records.heading: The plea of mental illness was not a mitigating circumstance and the death sentence stood
records.text: The plea of mental illness found no favour with the Trial Court and the courts above, and nothing showed incapacity to understand proceedings, instruct counsel or defend himself. It was not a mitigating circumstance warranting interference with the sentence, and the death sentence was upheld in review. Ref: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State through A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.R.P.89/2025); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Zahir Zakir Jaffar v. The State through A.G. Islamabad & another (Crl.R.P.89/2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Proof Under S. 304 PPC and Honour Killing
records.heading: Authority on forms of proof under section 304 PPC and proof of honour killing
records.text: Authority on the forms of proof under s. 304 PPC and the evidence required to prove an honour killing. The post gives no further holding. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1582; Ayaz Adil v. The State (Jail Appeal 6763/25).
records.title: Ayaz Adil v. The State (Jail Appeal 6763/25)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Rigor Mortis Contradicting Time of Occurrence
records.heading: Rigor mortis findings contradicted the time of occurrence deposed by prosecution witnesses
records.text: Full rigor mortis at a post-mortem held 7.5 hours after the alleged time of death was implausible in a young adult in a temperate climate. The medical evidence contradicted the time of occurrence deposed by prosecution witnesses and was in accord with medical jurisprudence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 251.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Absconding Co-Accused Acquitted: Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Benefit of doubt was given to an absconding co-accused who only arrived armed
records.text: The Supreme Court dismissed the petition against conviction but acquitted a co-accused who was a proclaimed offender. His alleged role of merely arriving armed with a Kalashnikov, without taking any active part, did not appeal to a prudent mind and the courts below had not believed common intention. Benefit of doubt was extended and his arrest and trial would be a waste of time. Ref: Salal Ghulam Husain v. The State (Crl. Petition Nos. 647 & 817 of 2025, decided 08.04.2026).
records.title: Salal Ghulam Husain v. The State (Crl. Petition Nos. 647 & 817 of 2025, decided 08.04.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Custody of Case Property
records.heading: The prosecution must prove an intact chain of custody of case property at every stage
records.text: Safe custody of sample parcels and bulk property is pivotal in contraband cases, and the prosecution must prove an intact chain of custody at every stage under Rule 22.16 of the Police Rules and Rule 14-E of the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders, Vol. III. The person who packs, seals and dispatches articles must be examined. Rule 14-F requires production and identification of articles in court. These are safeguards against tampering. Ref: Zulfiqar Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 500/J/2024).
records.title: Zulfiqar Ali v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 500/J/2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Proof of Postmortem Report: Art. 76 QSO, S. 509 CrPC
records.heading: A postmortem report does not prove itself and requires proof under the QSO
records.text: A postmortem report is expert opinion that does not prove itself and requires proof of execution and contents under the QSO. If the doctor is unavailable, secondary evidence is allowed only on the conditions of Art. 76 QSO. Section 509(1) CrPC is a statutory exception for medical depositions taken before a Magistrate, and under s. 509(2) the court may summon the deponent. Ref: Umar Hayat v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 12055/J/2022); Muhammad Hanif v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 10970/2022).
records.title: Umar Hayat v. The State (Criminal Appeal No. 12055/J/2022); Muhammad Hanif v. The State (Criminal Revision No. 10970/2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Third Proviso to S. 497 CrPC
records.heading: Third proviso to section 497 CrPC grants bail after two years' detention without concluded trial
records.text: Under the third proviso to s. 497 CrPC an accused of a capital offence is entitled to post-arrest bail if trial is not concluded within two years of detention, unless the delay is attributable to him or someone acting for him. The fourth proviso must be shown by the prosecution on material. Where the case calls for further inquiry, previous abscondence is no hurdle to bail. Ref: 2026 LHC 5338; Muhammad Fazil v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 1313-B of 2026, decided 24.08.2026); Justice Syed Farhad Ali Shah.
records.title: Muhammad Fazil v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. No. 1313-B of 2026, decided 24.08.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: S. 489-B Versus S. 489-C PPC, Further Inquiry
records.heading: Bail was granted as section 489-B was not prima facie met and section 489-C applied
records.text: At the bail stage only a tentative assessment is made. The ingredients of s. 489-B PPC were not prima facie met, and at best s. 489-C PPC applied, with a maximum of seven years outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. The case called for further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. The object of bail is to secure attendance and is neither punitive nor preventive. Ref: 2026 LHC 5345; Muhammad Sarwar v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 35608-B of 2026, decided 19.08.2026); Justice Muhammad Amjad Pervaiz.
records.title: Muhammad Sarwar v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 35608-B of 2026, decided 19.08.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed Postmortem Suggests Fabrication
records.heading: A postmortem delayed about twelve hours without explanation suggests fabrication
records.text: A postmortem delayed by about 12 hours without explanation casts serious doubt and suggests that the time was consumed in procuring and planting eyewitnesses before preparing the police papers. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 421, PLD 2026 Lah 649; Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Inquest Report: Mouth of Deceased Open
records.heading: An inquest report showing the deceased's mouth open made the relatives' presence doubtful
records.text: The inquest report recorded the mouth of the deceased as partially open. The complainant and witness, being the widow and son, would have closed it first had they been present, so their presence at the occurrence became doubtful. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 421, PLD 2026 Lah 649; Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict Between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.heading: Conflict between ocular and medical evidence on injury location goes to the root
records.text: The eyewitnesses placed the firearm injury on the back of the head while the doctor found it on the lateral aspect of the left eye at the front. This major conflict goes to the root of the prosecution case and supports the inference that the witnesses were not truthful or present. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 421, PLD 2026 Lah 649; Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Dishonest Improvements by Witness
records.heading: Dishonest improvements by a witness make his statement unreliable
records.text: Dishonest improvements made by a witness in his statement to strengthen the prosecution case cast serious doubt on his veracity and make the statement untrustworthy and unreliable. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 421, PLD 2026 Lah 649; Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Chance Witnesses
records.heading: Chance witnesses arriving just before the shot make the ocular account doubtful
records.text: Both eyewitnesses were chance witnesses who went straight from their destinations to the scene where the deceased lay sleeping, and the shot was fired immediately after their arrival. The Court found this very surprising and doubted the ocular account. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 421, PLD 2026 Lah 649; Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. Shahnaz Akhtar etc (Crl. Appeal 58756/2023)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Art. 185(3): Scope of Supreme Court Interference
records.heading: The Supreme Court under Article 185(3) does not reappraise evidence or disturb concurrent findings lightly
records.text: Under Art. 185(3) the Supreme Court does not sit as a court of further appeal to reappraise evidence or substitute its view for concurrent findings. Interference is warranted only where findings are perverse, arbitrary, based on misreading or non-reading of evidence, suffer jurisdictional defect, or cause manifest miscarriage of justice. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 352, 2026 SCMR 1401; Muhammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor & others (C.P.L.A. 5626/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor & others (C.P.L.A. 5626/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Power of Court to Impose Costs
records.heading: Authority on the power of the court to impose costs
records.text: Authority on the power of the court to impose costs. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 352, 2026 SCMR 1401; Muhammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor & others (C.P.L.A. 5626/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Shahzad v. Mst. Ayesha Noor & others (C.P.L.A. 5626/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Qatl-bis-Sabab: Driving Without Valid Licence
records.heading: A driver without a valid licence for the vehicle commits qatl-bis-sabab under section 322 PPC
records.text: A licensed driver causing death by rash and negligent driving commits qatl-i-khata, while one without a valid licence commits qatl-bis-sabab under s. 322 PPC. The petitioner held an HTV licence but no PSV licence needed to drive a bus. That the offence is punishable only with diyat does not itself justify bail. Bail was refused. Ref: 2026 LHC 5349; Riaz Hussain v. State & 1 other (Crl. Misc. 5377-B-26, decided 20.08.2026); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Riaz Hussain v. State & 1 other (Crl. Misc. 5377-B-26, decided 20.08.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Party Who Contested Up to Three Fora
records.heading: A party that lost before three fora cannot apply under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: A party that contested the suit or proceedings before three fora below and lost has no right to apply under s. 12(2) CPC. Having had full opportunity to plead, its mistake or slackness does not confer such a right. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 304.

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Doctrine of Precedent and Art. 189
records.heading: Mere citation of earlier authorities or a fleeting conclusion does not make a precedent binding
records.text: Art. 189 requires courts to follow the law established by the Supreme Court, but only law consciously declared on a question genuinely decided on legal reasoning binds. A decision binds only if it resolves a legal issue and establishes a principle, and not by mere citation of earlier authorities or a fleeting conclusion without reasoning. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 398; Qaiser Abbas v. The State (Jail Petition No. 390/2018); Muhammad Siddique v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 593-L/2018).
records.title: Qaiser Abbas v. The State (Jail Petition No. 390/2018); Muhammad Siddique v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 593-L/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Sentencing Where Multiple Lives Are Taken
records.heading: A sentencing structure that diminishes the value of each human life cannot be permitted
records.text: The criminal justice system cannot permit a sentencing structure that diminishes the distinct value of each human life or lets an offender kill two or three and pay for one, as it would undermine public confidence in the administration of justice. The post gives no further outcome. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 398; Qaiser Abbas v. The State (Jail Petition No. 390/2018); Muhammad Siddique v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 593-L/2018).
records.title: Qaiser Abbas v. The State (Jail Petition No. 390/2018); Muhammad Siddique v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 593-L/2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Photo Account Cheque: Suit under O. XXXVII
records.heading: A Photo Account cheque presented without the account holder gives no cause of action
records.text: Relying on Clause 1.5 of SBP Circular 10 of 29.03.2003, a Photo Account cheque presented unilaterally without associating the account holder, and dishonoured in the holder's absence, gives no valid dishonour. It does not create a cause of action for a suit under Order XXXVII CPC. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 601; Salamat Ali v. Sabohi Naz (R.F.A. 27359/24).
records.title: Salamat Ali v. Sabohi Naz (R.F.A. 27359/24)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Scope of IDA 2005 and Family Disputes
records.heading: The Illegal Dispossession Act is not limited to Qabza groups or land mafias
records.text: The Illegal Dispossession Act is a special penal statute protecting lawful owners and occupiers. Its reach is not limited to Qabza groups or land mafias and extends to any person who forcibly intrudes on property with intent to dispossess or occupy, if the statutory ingredients are made out. The Court stressed that penal statutes should be applied without splintering family unions, with protective family laws as the recourse in family settings. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 385; Abbas Asif Zaman and another v. The State (Criminal Petition No.61-K of 2025).
records.title: Abbas Asif Zaman and another v. The State (Criminal Petition No.61-K of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Leave to Appeal by Pendente Lite Transferee
records.heading: A pendente lite transferee who delayed impleadment is not a proper party to seek leave
records.text: A non-party may be granted leave to appeal only if he could properly have been impleaded. A pendente lite transferee who did not seek leave under s. 52 Transfer of Property Act, concealed the transfer and delayed seeking impleadment or suing for specific performance until barred under Art. 113 of the Limitation Act is not a bona fide purchaser or proper party. The doctrine of lis pendens applied and leave was refused. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 380; Jamil Ahmed and others v. Mst. Zarina Bibi and others (C.M.A. 9923/2024).
records.title: Jamil Ahmed and others v. Mst. Zarina Bibi and others (C.M.A. 9923/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: CNIC Not Attachable by Civil Courts
records.heading: A CNIC cannot be attached, impounded or blocked by civil courts
records.text: A CNIC issued by NADRA is not movable property of its holder and cannot be attached, impounded, cancelled or blocked by civil courts as a coercive measure in civil proceedings. It can be cancelled, impounded or confiscated only by the authority in the manner and circumstances prescribed under s. 18 of the NADRA Ordinance, 2000. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 635.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Compromise Order and Undertaking
records.heading: An order passed on a compromise is enforceable even where no formal decree is drawn
records.text: An order passed on a compromise remains binding and enforceable even where no formal decree is drawn. An undertaking recorded in earlier proceedings and a compromise recorded by the Supreme Court are a binding adjudication, so the executing court could be approached. The petitions were converted into an appeal and allowed, the High Court judgment set aside and the Executing Court directed to conclude execution expeditiously. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 393, PLJ 2026 SC 542; Mst. Asma Begum and others v. Abdul Hameed (C.P.L.A. 4417/2024).
records.title: Mst. Asma Begum and others v. Abdul Hameed (C.P.L.A. 4417/2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Return of Dower Gold Not Paid by Husband
records.heading: On khula a husband can reclaim only dower that he actually paid himself
records.text: On khula, a husband can claim back only dower that he actually paid himself. Where the money for 11 tolas of gold given as dower was provided by the wife's father and the husband could not prove his own payment, he is not entitled to the gold or its value. The wife's petition was partly allowed and the order to return the gold or its price was set aside. Ref: 2026 LHC 5363; Dr. Rukhsana Kausar and another v. Shahid Nazeer and others (Writ Petition No.21804 of 2020, decided 31.08.2026); Justice Rahil Kamran Sheikh.
records.title: Dr. Rukhsana Kausar and another v. Shahid Nazeer and others (Writ Petition No.21804 of 2020, decided 31.08.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Child Marriage: Consent and Welfare of Minor
records.heading: The purported consent of a child cannot legitimise cohabitation under the Child Marriage Restraint Act
records.text: Under the Punjab Child Marriage Restraint Act, 2026, the purported consent of a child cannot legitimise cohabitation, which is treated as child abuse, and her welfare and best interests are paramount. The order of the Justice of Peace refusing registration of a case was set aside and the police were directed to investigate the new complaint. The child was placed with the Child Protection Bureau, with permanent custody left to the Guardian Judge. Ref: 2026 LHC 5390; Muhammad Aslam v. Additional Sessions Judge etc (W.P. 46868/26, decided 31.08.2026); Justice Munawar Iqbal Duggal.
records.title: Muhammad Aslam v. Additional Sessions Judge etc (W.P. 46868/26, decided 31.08.2026)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Rape of Child: Death Sentence Altered to Life
records.heading: A death sentence for rape of a child was altered to life imprisonment
records.text: In a case of rape of a ten-year-old girl at a school, the death sentence was altered to life imprisonment, with the fine, additional six months and Rs. 100,000 compensation under the Anti-Rape Act maintained. Absence of semen in the forensic report does not end the case, and a three-day FIR delay gave no benefit of doubt. The Court also issued directions on police patrols near educational institutions and medico-legal services. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 257, 2026 SCMR 1842; Younas Masih v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1042/2025); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Younas Masih v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1042/2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Unproved Panchayat Nama and Evidence Beyond Pleadings
records.heading: An unproved Panchayat Nama cannot defeat title shown in a sanctioned mutation
records.text: No party may set up a new case for the first time before the Supreme Court if it needs factual inquiry, and evidence beyond pleadings carries no legal weight. Oral assertion cannot rebut documentary evidence. A Panchayat Nama not proved through attesting witnesses lost its evidentiary worth and could not defeat title shown in a sanctioned mutation, and the scribe's testimony could not cure that defect. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 443; Anwar Ali Shah and others v. Sadiq Ali Shah and others (C.A. No.1410 of 2019 & CMA No.7122 of 2019).
records.title: Anwar Ali Shah and others v. Sadiq Ali Shah and others (C.A. No.1410 of 2019 & CMA No.7122 of 2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Suit After Revenue Forums: Doctrine of Election
records.heading: A civil suit after exhausting revenue forums is barred by the doctrine of election
records.text: After the revenue forums were exhausted, the civil suit was a second bite at the cherry, as no jurisdictional flaw or mala fides was shown. A second recourse cannot be provided in their absence, and the doctrine of election also barred it. The suit was rightly dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 469; Zafar Hussain Khan (decd.) thr. LRs v. Mst. Farhana Almas (decd.) thr. LRs & others (C.A.1495/2017).
records.title: Zafar Hussain Khan (decd.) thr. LRs v. Mst. Farhana Almas (decd.) thr. LRs & others (C.A.1495/2017)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Burden of Proof: Art. 117 QSO
records.heading: The burden of proof lies on the person asserting a fact under Article 117 QSO
records.text: Under Art. 117 QSO the burden of proving a fact lies on the person who asserts it. It does not shift until that party discharges the initial burden by admissible, credible and reliable evidence, and until then the other side need not lead rebuttal evidence. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 471; M/s Stallions (Private) Limited, Lahore v. Capital Development Authority (Civil Appeal No.871 of 2018).
records.title: M/s Stallions (Private) Limited, Lahore v. Capital Development Authority (Civil Appeal No.871 of 2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Handwriting Expert Comparison: Art. 59 QSO
records.heading: Expert opinion on handwriting is a relevant fact under Article 59 QSO even if rebuttable
records.text: In a narcotics case, the accused applied under Art. 59 QSO and Art. 10-A of the Constitution to send the recovery memo, complaint and rough site plan to a handwriting expert for comparison with the complainant's handwriting. Expert opinion is a relevant fact under Art. 59 and is not excluded merely because it is rebuttable, its weight being for trial. The Lahore High Court allowed the appeal. Ref: Muhammad Arsalan v. State (Criminal Appeal No. 221/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Arsalan v. State (Criminal Appeal No. 221/2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Scope of Re-examination: Art. 133(3) QSO
records.heading: Re-examination under Article 133(3) QSO is confined to matters arising out of cross-examination
records.text: Under Art. 133(3) QSO, re-examination is confined to matters arising out of cross-examination and cannot be used to fill lacunae or improve the examination-in-chief. If new matter is allowed with the Court's permission, the adverse party may cross-examine on it. The power under s. 540 CrPC cannot circumvent this limit, given Art. 165 QSO. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 628, 2026 YLR 2489; Mst Nasreen Fatima alias Nusro v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 10516/26).
records.title: Mst Nasreen Fatima alias Nusro v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal 10516/26)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Sexual Violence: Credibility of Victim
records.heading: A sexual violence conviction rests on the victim's credibility and not the number of witnesses
records.text: A conviction for sexual violence rests on the credibility of the victim, supported by trustworthy corroborative evidence, and not on the number of witnesses. The appeals of the convicts against their death sentences in the Motorway case were dismissed. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 692; Abid Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 20513/21).
records.title: Abid Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 20513/21)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA: Sperm Fraction and Epithelial Fraction
records.heading: Absence of the offender's DNA in the epithelial fraction does not invalidate a sperm fraction match
records.text: The judgment explains differential extraction of sexual assault samples into sperm and epithelial fractions. Absence of the offender's DNA from the epithelial fraction does not by itself invalidate or diminish the probative value of a matching DNA profile from the sperm fraction. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 716; Manazir Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 31263/22); Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi.
records.title: Manazir Ali v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 31263/22)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Ban on Tobacco and Pan Advertising
records.heading: The notification banning advertisement of tobacco and pan was held lawful
records.text: The Federal Government's notification banning advertisement of tobacco, cigarettes and pan was held lawful, there being no permanent constitutional right to advertise tobacco products. The objection of non-reference to the Council of Common Interests was rejected, and the notification was issued under the Non-Smokers' Health Ordinance, 2002. The petition was dismissed. Ref: 2026 LHC 5508; All Pakistan Markazi Union Pan, Beri, Cigarette, Mashroob Retailers through its President v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary National Health Services Regulation & Coordination and others (Writ Petition No.17594 of 2020, decided 02.09.2026); Justice Rahil Kamran Sheikh.
records.title: All Pakistan Markazi Union Pan, Beri, Cigarette, Mashroob Retailers through its President v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary National Health Services Regulation & Coordination and others (Writ Petition No.17594 of 2020, decided 02.09.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Stay of Criminal Proceedings Pending Civil Suit
records.heading: Stay of criminal proceedings pending a civil suit is discretionary and needs supporting material
records.text: Civil and criminal proceedings may run together, but criminal proceedings should be stayed where the subjects are the same and closely connected, or the civil suit is mala fide. Stay is discretionary, may be ordered under s. 561-A CrPC, and requires material showing improper motive or abuse of process. The accused's likely prejudice is the guide. Ref: Bakhtullah Shah v. Govt. of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (CPLA No. 1560 & 1971 of 2025, decided 24.03.2026).
records.title: Bakhtullah Shah v. Govt. of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (CPLA No. 1560 & 1971 of 2025, decided 24.03.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt: Separate Assessment of Defence Plea
records.heading: Doubt in the prosecution evidence entitles the accused to acquittal without examining the defence case
records.text: Where the accused advances a specific defence plea, the trial court must assess the prosecution case and the defence version separately. If any doubt arises in the prosecution evidence, the benefit goes to the accused without examining the defence case. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1457; Sajjad Ali v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.67614 of 2021); Robina Kausar v. The State & another (Criminal Revision No.44600 of 2023).
records.title: Sajjad Ali v. The State & another (Criminal Appeal No.67614 of 2021); Robina Kausar v. The State & another (Criminal Revision No.44600 of 2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Ss. 395 and 412 PPC: No Dual Conviction
records.heading: A person cannot be convicted of both sections 395 and 412 PPC together
records.text: A person cannot be convicted at the same time of dacoity under s. 395 PPC and of dishonestly receiving property stolen in a dacoity under s. 412 PPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 682; Sami Ullah v. The State, etc. (Criminal Revision No. 124 of 2018; Criminal Miscellaneous No. 1015-M of 2015).
records.title: Sami Ullah v. The State, etc. (Criminal Revision No. 124 of 2018; Criminal Miscellaneous No. 1015-M of 2015)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sessions Court Revision: No Enhancement Beyond Magistrate's Power
records.heading: A Court of Session in revision cannot enhance a sentence beyond the Magistrate's power
records.text: A Court of Session exercising revisional jurisdiction cannot enhance a sentence beyond the maximum that the trial Magistrate could award. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 682; Sami Ullah v. The State, etc. (Criminal Revision No. 124 of 2018; Criminal Miscellaneous No. 1015-M of 2015).
records.title: Sami Ullah v. The State, etc. (Criminal Revision No. 124 of 2018; Criminal Miscellaneous No. 1015-M of 2015)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 155(2) CrPC: FIR for Non-Cognizable Offence
records.heading: An FIR registered in violation of section 155(2) CrPC is void at inception
records.text: An FIR registered for a non-compoundable offence in violation of s. 155(2) CrPC is void at inception. It is not cured by later addition of a cognizable offence before the competent Court takes cognizance. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 567; Muqaddas v. SHO (WP. No 12252-Q of 2025).
records.title: Muqaddas v. SHO (WP. No 12252-Q of 2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Marriage of Girl Under Age: Bail Refused
records.heading: A girl under eighteen cannot consent to marriage merely because of signs of puberty
records.text: A female child below 18 is not competent to consent to marriage merely because she shows signs of puberty. The statutory age under the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 is to be given preference over uncodified opinions of religious scholars, and under s. 375(d) PPC the consent of a girl under sixteen is immaterial. Bail was refused. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 227; Shahid Imran v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 33583/23).
records.title: Shahid Imran v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc. 33583/23)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Transaction with Minor Void: S. 11 Contract Act
records.heading: A transaction directly with a minor is void ab initio under section 11
records.text: Under s. 11 of the Contract Act, 1872, a minor is incompetent to contract, and a transaction entered into directly with a minor is void ab initio and cannot confer enforceable rights. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 478; Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal No. 140-P of 2018).
records.title: Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal No. 140-P of 2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Presumption under Art. 100 Is Rebuttable
records.heading: The presumption under Article 100 is rebuttable and cannot validate a void transaction
records.text: The presumption under Art. 100 is evidentiary and rebuttable. It cannot validate a transaction void under substantive law, cure a minor's incapacity, or dispense with proof where execution is specifically disputed. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 478; Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal No. 140-P of 2018).
records.title: Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal No. 140-P of 2018)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Unauthorised Improvements on Another's Property
records.heading: Improvements on another's property without consent confer no title or compensation
records.text: A person who builds on or improves another's property without the owner's consent acts at his own risk. Such improvements confer neither title nor a right to compensation, and a tenant or permissive occupier cannot claim compensation for them. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 478; Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal No. 140-P of 2018).
records.title: Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal No. 140-P of 2018)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Emails as Electronic Evidence: Art. 78-A QSO
records.heading: Emails are inadmissible without proof under Article 78-A QSO and the Electronic Transactions Ordinance
records.text: In a prosecution for corrupt practices based on an allegedly forged degree, the emails were held inadmissible. The persons who sent and received them were not examined, and no certificate or proof under Art. 78-A QSO or ss. 16 and 17 of the Electronic Transactions Ordinance, 2002 was produced, so the electronic evidence was not duly proved. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1278.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Polygamy Offence: Family Court and Appeal Forum
records.heading: Polygamy offences are tried by Family Courts with appeal to the District Court
records.text: Trial of the offence of polygamy lies only before the Family Courts under the Family Court Act 1964, and appeals lie to the District Court under s. 14 of that Act. The Court of Sessions therefore lacked jurisdiction to decide the appeal. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 649, PLJ 2026 CrC 191; Muhammad Asif v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 25041/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State etc (Crl. Revision 25041/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor: Referral to Bait-ul-Mal
records.heading: Court should refer a minor to Bait-ul-Mal where father or grandfather cannot pay maintenance
records.text: For future cases, where a minor's father or grandfather cannot pay maintenance and the circumstances warrant recourse to Bait-ul-Mal, the Court should refer the person concerned to Bait-ul-Mal. Bait-ul-Mal may then assess the case under its own policy and eligibility criteria and decide the assistance appropriate. Ref: Pakistan Bait ul Mal thr. Managing Director, Islamabad v. Raj Ram and others (C.M.A.1477/2023, decided 24.08.2026); Justice Yahya Afridi.
records.title: Pakistan Bait ul Mal thr. Managing Director, Islamabad v. Raj Ram and others (C.M.A.1477/2023, decided 24.08.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court Appeal under S. 14: Adequate Remedy
records.heading: An appeal under section 14 of the Family Courts Act is an adequate remedy
records.text: The Appellate Court under s. 14 of the Family Courts Act, 1964 can reverse, modify or uphold findings of fact and pass interim orders, so the appeal is an adequate remedy. The petitioner should first apply to the Appellate Court for restoration of his appeal rather than press a constitution petition. Ref: 2026 MLD 1597; Muhammad Muzaffar Hussain v. Learned Additional District Judge, Pakpattan etc (W.P.48792/26).
records.title: Muhammad Muzaffar Hussain v. Learned Additional District Judge, Pakpattan etc (W.P.48792/26)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Gift Mutations: Proof of Fraud
records.heading: Dismissal of a declaratory suit does not by itself prove fraud in gift mutations
records.text: The donees' filing of a declaratory suit and its dismissal does not by itself establish fraud in the gift mutations. The petitioner must prove fraud by evidence before a court of plenary jurisdiction, and the dismissal creates no executable decree reversing the mutations. Ref: 2026 MLD 1580; Zahida Parveen v. District Collector etc (WP. 8516/22).
records.title: Zahida Parveen v. District Collector etc (WP. 8516/22)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: S. 24 Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009: Scope
records.heading: Section 24 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act is not confined to eviction proceedings
records.text: S. 24 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act, 2009 is not confined to eviction proceedings and covers other pending proceedings under the Act requiring payment of rent and dues. Under s. 24(2) the Rent Tribunal can tentatively determine a rent dispute and order deposit. An eviction order falls within the definition of final order in s. 2(b). Ref: 2026 MLD 1548; Naeem Ullah v. Ch Zulfiqar Ahmad etc (Misc. Writ 44946/25).
records.title: Naeem Ullah v. Ch Zulfiqar Ahmad etc (Misc. Writ 44946/25)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Orphan Minors from Uncles
records.heading: Uncles are liable for two thirds of maintenance of orphan minors
records.text: Where the minors' father and then grandfather, who paid interim maintenance, have died, and the minors have no property or insufficient income, their uncles are liable to pay two thirds of the court-fixed maintenance by reason of kinship. The mother contributes the remaining one third. Ref: 2026 MLD 1409; Muhammad Maroof and others v. Mst. Mariam Farooq and others (Writ Petition No.50 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Maroof and others v. Mst. Mariam Farooq and others (Writ Petition No.50 of 2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Withdrawal of Regularisation: Service Tribunal
records.heading: Withdrawal of regularisation must be challenged departmentally and then before the Service Tribunal
records.text: Once a contractual employee is regularised he enters the civil service. An order withdrawing the regularisation must be challenged within the departmental hierarchy and, if the grievance remains, by appeal before the Service Tribunal. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1005; Hafiz Ahmed Raza v. Govt. of Punjab etc (WP.8215-25).
records.title: Hafiz Ahmed Raza v. Govt. of Punjab etc (WP.8215-25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Legal Advisor's Authority to File Revision
records.heading: A Legal Advisor's general authority to defend cases ordinarily extends to filing a revision
records.text: An authorisation to a Legal Advisor to undertake defence of all court cases is broad and unqualified. Ordinarily it extends to filing a revision petition in the High Court against the appellate judgment in the same litigation, unless the order or governing law provides otherwise. Absence of express mention of revision is no ground to reject the revision. Ref: Central Govt. through Collector, District D.I.Khan (now) Deputy Commissioner, D.I.Khan and others v. Tariq Mansoor and others (Civil Petition No. 260-P of 2022, decided 28.07.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Central Govt. through Collector, District D.I.Khan (now) Deputy Commissioner, D.I.Khan and others v. Tariq Mansoor and others (Civil Petition No. 260-P of 2022, decided 28.07.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Resignation Cannot Be Converted into Retirement
records.heading: A Service Tribunal cannot convert an invalid resignation into retirement
records.text: Resignation and retirement are distinct modes of cessation of service. Completing the qualifying service for pension does not make an employee retired or cure an invalid resignation. The Tribunal under s. 7 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Service Tribunal Act, 1974 has essentially appellate powers and, without express statutory authority, cannot convert a resignation into retirement to give pensionary benefits. Ref: Govt. of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary Population, Welfare Department, Peshawar and others v. Mst. Bacha Jehan (Civil Petition No. 50-P of 2022, decided 30.07.2026); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Govt. of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary Population, Welfare Department, Peshawar and others v. Mst. Bacha Jehan (Civil Petition No. 50-P of 2022, decided 30.07.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 52 TPA: Non-Joinder of Transferee Pendente Lite
records.heading: A transferee pendente lite is bound by the outcome, and the decree remains open to challenge
records.text: A transfer during a pending suit is subject to its outcome under s. 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. Where an actual possessor or transferee pendente lite is excluded, non-joinder is a defect, and the decree cannot conclusively bind that party. It remains open to challenge on grounds of fraud or collusion under s. 12(2) CPC or by objections in execution. Ref: 2026 CLC 1490; Nadeem Aslam & 1 other v. Shahid Mehmod etc. (WP. 13156/25).
records.title: Nadeem Aslam & 1 other v. Shahid Mehmod etc. (WP. 13156/25)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Majalis and Processions: Limits of Administrative Power
records.heading: Majalis and processions cannot be wholly prohibited by administrative order
records.text: Holding majalis and processions is a fundamental right and cannot be wholly prohibited. S. 16 of the Punjab Civil Administration Act, 2017 allows the Deputy Commissioner to maintain order, not to impose a total ban. Selective refusal contravenes Arts. 4 and 25, and apprehended law and order risk or police reports alone cannot justify restriction without concrete evidence. Ref: 2026 CLC 1427; Bilal Hussain v. Home Secretary Govt. of the Punjab etc. (WP. 39994/25).
records.title: Bilal Hussain v. Home Secretary Govt. of the Punjab etc. (WP. 39994/25)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Oral Rescission of Written Agreement to Sell
records.heading: A written agreement to sell cannot be rescinded orally without cogent evidence
records.text: A written agreement to sell cannot be rescinded orally unless clear, cogent and credible evidence establishes it. Stating the time, place and witnesses of an oral rescission does not offend O. VI R. 2 CPC. A buyer's deposit in his own account with unproved source does not prove refund of consideration or rescission. Ref: 2026 CLC 1546; Zafar Ali deceased through 11 LRs v. Ghulam Mustafa Chaudhary etc (Civil Revision 33211/23).
records.title: Zafar Ali deceased through 11 LRs v. Ghulam Mustafa Chaudhary etc (Civil Revision 33211/23)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Motor Vehicle Stand Licence Not Heritable
records.heading: A motor vehicle stand licence is a privilege and does not devolve on heirs
records.text: A licence under Rule 253 of the Motor Vehicles Rules, 1969 is a privilege and not a property right, and on a licensee's death it does not automatically devolve on his legal heirs. A privately owned place can be notified as a stand only on the owner's application. The petitioners were to seek determination of their shares in the civil court. Ref: 2026 CLC 1596; Khawaja Muhammad Asif & 7 Others v. Province of Punjab etc. (WP.48034/25).
records.title: Khawaja Muhammad Asif & 7 Others v. Province of Punjab etc. (WP.48034/25)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Depreciation and Reduction of Maintenance
records.heading: Dowry depreciation falls on a husband who evasively denied it, and maintenance may be reduced
records.text: Depreciation of dowry articles during a suit for their recovery cannot be imposed on the wife where the husband's denial was evasive. A father cannot be burdened with maintenance beyond his means, and it can be reduced on adverse change in his means, so the Appellate Court erred in refusing him the chance to prove such change. Ref: 2026 YLR 2051; Mansoor Ali v. Mst. Anam Hussain etc (WP-819-20).
records.title: Mansoor Ali v. Mst. Anam Hussain etc (WP-819-20)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Evacuee Property: Re-allotment After PTD
records.heading: Re-allotment of evacuee property after issue of a PTD is void
records.text: Where evacuee property was auctioned, the price paid, the auction confirmed and a PTO/PTD issued in 1961, the settlement authority became functus officio. Any later re-allotment by the Deputy Settlement Commissioner is collusive, illegal, void and coram non judice. Ref: 2026 YLR 2017; Ch. Abdul Saleem v. Mst. Aziz Khatoon (WP.69-06).
records.title: Ch. Abdul Saleem v. Mst. Aziz Khatoon (WP.69-06)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed S. 161 CrPC Statement of Witness
records.heading: An unexplained delay in recording a section 161 CrPC statement destroys its value
records.text: Delayed recording of a prosecution witness's statement under s. 161 CrPC reduces its value to nothing unless there is a plausible explanation. No explanation was given, so no value could be attached to the statement. Ref: 2026 YLR 1968.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Touch DNA and STR Profiling
records.heading: Touch DNA from skin cells can yield STR profiles capable of matching a suspect
records.text: Explains touch (epithelial) DNA left on objects by skin cells, analysed by the same procedures as bodily fluids. Low copy amounts can now yield full or partial STR profiles through PCR based testing, which can match a suspect with near certainty. Ref: 2026 YLR 1968.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Acquittal Despite Plea of Killing
records.heading: An accused must be acquitted if the prosecution fails, even after admitting the killing
records.text: If the prosecution fails to prove its case, the accused must be acquitted even if he took a plea and thereby admitted killing the deceased. Ref: 2026 YLR 1968.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI R. 1 CPC: List of Witnesses
records.heading: Witnesses outside the list under Order XVI Rule 1 CPC need the court's permission
records.text: Under O. XVI R. 1 CPC the list of witnesses must be filed within seven days of framing of issues, and other witnesses may be called only with the Court's permission on good cause, with reasons recorded. No good cause was shown, and oral evidence of a document is inadmissible, so the certified copy should be produced. The dismissal of the application was upheld. Ref: 2026 YLR 2118; Haji Mushtaq Hussain Shah v. Senior Civil Judge etc (Writ Petition-4874-20).
records.title: Haji Mushtaq Hussain Shah v. Senior Civil Judge etc (Writ Petition-4874-20)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Forged Judicial Orders: Fraud on the Court
records.heading: Forging or misusing judicial orders is a fraud on the court
records.text: Forging, manipulating or misusing judicial orders for personal or institutional gain cannot be tolerated, and the Court must protect the authenticity of its record. Where tampering is used for commercial benefit, it is an assault on the public interest in the judicial function. Later contrition does not displace the need for an institutional response to the fraud committed for the petitioner company. Ref: 2026 YLR 2175.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Appointment of Lambardar: Selection Criteria
records.heading: No one has a vested right to appointment as Lambardar
records.text: No one has a vested right to appointment as Lambardar. Revenue authorities select the most suitable candidate under Rule 17 of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Rules, 1968, considering Rule 22 duties and s. 36 of the Land Revenue Act, 1967, with personal influence, character, ability and freedom from indebtedness as prerequisites. Ref: 2026 YLR 2130.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Female Lambardar: Rule 19(2)(d) Ultra Vires
records.heading: Refusing to appoint a female Lambardar on gender alone contravenes Article 25(2)
records.text: Refusing to appoint a female as Lambardar merely on gender contravenes Art. 25(2) of the Constitution. Rule 19(2)(d) of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Rules, 1968, which makes a female ordinarily ineligible, was held ultra vires the Constitution and of no legal effect. Ref: 2026 YLR 2130.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: PERA Statutory Scheme and Further Inquiry
records.heading: Unexplained departure from the PERA statutory scheme makes bail a case of further inquiry
records.text: The failure of the PERA officials who conducted the checking to lodge a complaint, with the FIR registered by local police, requires examination, as the statutory scheme under ss. 20, 25, 26 and 32 is not a formality. These unexplained matters bring the case within further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC, and deeper appreciation of evidence at bail stage is not permissible. Ref: Muhammad Irfan Asghar, etc. v. The State (Crl.Misc.No.2888-B of 2026).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan Asghar, etc. v. The State (Crl.Misc.No.2888-B of 2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Wife's Death in Matrimonial Home: Proof Difficulties
records.heading: Wives killed in the matrimonial home are hard to prove under conventional evidentiary standards
records.text: The Court discusses how the absence of primary evidence makes homicide of wives within the matrimonial home hard to prove, and the vulnerability of married women in the patrilocal family system. It observes that treating such cases under conventional evidentiary standards lets offences go unpunished, and criticises the inadequate investigation in the case. Ref: Habib Ullah v. The State (Jail Petition No. 41/2023, decided 03.08.2026).
records.title: Habib Ullah v. The State (Jail Petition No. 41/2023, decided 03.08.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder of Wife: Crime of Difficult Proof
records.heading: Murder of a wife in the matrimonial home is a crime of difficult proof
records.text: Murder of a wife inside the matrimonial home is a crime of difficult proof. The Court upheld conviction under s. 302(b) PPC on last seen evidence, matching medical evidence, motive and the husband's flight and absconsion for nearly seven years. Leave to appeal refused and the jail petition dismissed. Ref: Habib Ullah v. The State (Jail Petition No. 41/2023, decided 03.08.2026); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakkar; Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Habib Ullah v. The State (Jail Petition No. 41/2023, decided 03.08.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Territorial Jurisdiction of Family Court: Wife's Residence
records.heading: Family Court jurisdiction lies where the wife ordinarily resides, without proof of permanent residence
records.text: S. 5 of the Family Courts Act, 1964 gives Family Courts exclusive jurisdiction over Part I matters. Under Rule 6 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Rules, 1965, jurisdiction lies where the cause of action arises or the parties reside, and in suits for dissolution or dower also where the wife ordinarily resides. Ordinary residence needs no proof of permanent residence. Ref: 2026 LHC 5645; Mst. Shagufta Bibi v. ADJ etc (WP-6627-23, decided 11.09.2026); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Mst. Shagufta Bibi v. ADJ etc (WP-6627-23, decided 11.09.2026)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Talb-e-Muwathibat: Proof and Informant Witness
records.heading: Talb-e-Muwathibat is not proved by hearsay without producing the informant or proof of death
records.text: A plaintiff who says the person who informed him of the sale has died must prove the death by a death certificate or other reliable evidence. Failure to produce the informant, and reliance on hearsay, meant Talb-e-Muwathibat was not proved. The High Court declined to interfere with the concurrent dismissal. Ref: 2026 YLR 2234.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Land Reforms: Oral Gift Mutations and Ceiling
records.heading: Oral gift mutations excluded from land reform declarations were void, and abatement did not help
records.text: Declarants under MLR-115 transferred land to siblings by oral gift mutations in 1970 and excluded it from their declarations. The Land Commission authorities held the mutations void for land reforms and resumed excess land. The plea of abatement under s. 25 of the Land Reforms Act, 1977 did not help, as the mutations had already been declared void. Ref: 2026 YLR 2212.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Rule of Consistency and Parity
records.heading: Bail is granted to an accused in the same position as co-accused on bail
records.text: A bank branch manager accused of operating a bogus account was held entitled to bail on the rule of consistency, as co-accused in an identical position had been granted pre-arrest and post-arrest bail. The principle follows equality under Arts. 4 and 25. Abscondence is a matter of propriety where bail is a matter of right. Ref: 2026 YLR 2196.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Video Clip on USB: Mode of Proof
records.heading: A video clip on a USB must be proved in accordance with law
records.text: A video on a USB was not admitted or proved in accordance with law. The Trial Court did not decide the defence objection, view it in open Court, take notes, or allow cross-examination, and the Investigating Officer denied any video was produced during investigation. Its contents could not be used against the accused and it was inadmissible. Ref: 2026 YLR 2182.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Malicious Prosecution Versus Defamation
records.heading: A cancelled criminal case gives rise to malicious prosecution and not defamation
records.text: Where the grievance arises from a criminal case cancelled in C Class, the remedy is a suit for malicious prosecution and not defamation. Malicious prosecution needs proof of malice and absence of reasonable and probable cause, while defamation needs publication of a defamatory imputation to a third person attributable to the defendant. A claimant cannot avoid these requirements by framing the action as defamation. Ref: Altaf Hussain & others v. M/s. Bayer Crops Science Pakistan through its Chief Executive Officer & another (C.P.L.A.701-K/2025, decided 07.08.2026); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Altaf Hussain & others v. M/s. Bayer Crops Science Pakistan through its Chief Executive Officer & another (C.P.L.A.701-K/2025, decided 07.08.2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Punjab Rented Premises Act: Leave to Contest
records.heading: Section 22 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act does not permit partial leave to contest
records.text: S. 22 does not allow partial leave to contest. Where sufficient grounds exist, leave must be granted, and where refused the Rent Tribunal must pass a final order covering matters in s. 2(b), including arrears and Pagri. Absence of separate notice of change of ownership did not invalidate ejectment, and Pagri could not be adjusted against arrears. Ref: 2026 LHC 5680; Sh. Aamir etc v. Idrees Javed etc (WP1480-23, decided 16.09.2026); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Sh. Aamir etc v. Idrees Javed etc (WP1480-23, decided 16.09.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Land Donor Policy: Preferential Appointments
records.heading: Class-IV appointments under the land donor policy were not disturbed after long lapse of time
records.text: Public sector appointments must ordinarily be made on merit. Appointments of Class-IV employees under a government policy preferring land donors or their nominees were not unsettled, given the long lapse of time since the appointments. The High Court's restoration of the respondents' appointments was left undisturbed, and the donor's entitlement under the policy remained protected. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1020.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Magistrate's Direction to Police to Investigate
records.heading: A Magistrate's direction to police to investigate fairly is not subject to criminal revision
records.text: A Magistrate's direction merely requiring the police to investigate fairly and in accordance with law is administrative or supervisory in character and not amenable to criminal revision. The pendency of a private complaint in which persons were summoned does not make the police investigation incompetent. Ref: 2026 LHC 5720; Mst. Razia Bibi v. ASJ (W.P.No.1185 of 2026, decided 08.09.2026).
records.title: Mst. Razia Bibi v. ASJ (W.P.No.1185 of 2026, decided 08.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Lis Pendens and Impleadment: O. I R. 10 CPC
records.heading: A transferee pendente lite may be impleaded under Order I Rule 10 CPC
records.text: A transferee pendente lite takes subject to the outcome of the litigation under s. 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, and lack of notice does not take the transaction outside it. Its application under O. I R. 10 CPC was still maintainable and the Appellate Court could allow impleadment. Impleadment does not decide substantive rights, and the basis for ordering delivery of possession was not disclosed. Ref: 2026 LHC 5725; Ch. Hafeez-ur-Rehman v. Mst. Uzma Sattar & others (Civil Revision No.414 of 2023, decided 08.09.2026).
records.title: Ch. Hafeez-ur-Rehman v. Mst. Uzma Sattar & others (Civil Revision No.414 of 2023, decided 08.09.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Civil Awards to Public Servants: Art. 259(2)
records.heading: Article 259(2) permits civil awards to public servants for exceptional service
records.text: A petition against civil awards to public servants was dismissed. Art. 259(2) does not limit public service to unpaid or voluntary service, so exceptional public service by government employees may be recognised within the prescribed framework. Holding public office alone gives no entitlement, and without legal basis no direction can be issued for withdrawal of an award. Ref: 2026 LHC 5657; Ashba Kamran v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (Misc. Writ. 51338/26, decided 11.09.2026).
records.title: Ashba Kamran v. Federation of Pakistan etc. (Misc. Writ. 51338/26, decided 11.09.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Quackery under Punjab Healthcare Commission Act
records.heading: A drug-sale licence does not permit practising medicine, and quackery attracts a fine
records.text: A drug-sale licence permits only sale of drugs and not practice of medicine, and recovery of used syringes with the licensee's admission of giving injections established quackery. The Hearing Committee is the competent authority to impose a fine under s. 28, and voluntary deposit of the fine without protest renders the appeal unmaintainable. The appellate judgment was set aside and the Committee's order restored. Ref: 2026 LHC 5765; Punjab Healthcare Commission through CEO Dr. Muhammad Saqib Aziz v. D&SJ Faisalabad etc. (Misc. Writ.33544/22, decided 14.09.2026); Justice Munawar Iqbal Duggal.
records.title: Punjab Healthcare Commission through CEO Dr. Muhammad Saqib Aziz v. D&SJ Faisalabad etc. (Misc. Writ.33544/22, decided 14.09.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Pronote: S. 118 Presumption and Proof of Execution
records.heading: The section 118 presumption does not relieve a claimant of proving conscious execution of a pronote
records.text: The presumption under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act does not relieve the claimant of proving genuineness when the executant's conscious execution is specifically disputed. Attestation is not essential to a pronote satisfying s. 4. The question is whether execution was proved as a conscious, voluntary act, which differs from proving that a thumb impression belongs to the maker. Ref: 2026 LHC 5775; Mst. Noor Bibi widow of Muhammad Ramzan & others v. Waryam s/o Lal Din (deceased) through legal heirs (Regular First Appeal No.02 of 2017, decided 07.09.2026).
records.title: Mst. Noor Bibi widow of Muhammad Ramzan & others v. Waryam s/o Lal Din (deceased) through legal heirs (Regular First Appeal No.02 of 2017, decided 07.09.2026)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: S. 44 Land Revenue Act: Fard Badar Without Notice
records.heading: A Fard Badar corrected without notice to the affected party is liable to be set aside
records.text: S. 44 of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Act, 1967 requires an inquiry giving interested persons a hearing and written reasons. A mutation or Fard Badar reviewed or corrected without notice to the affected party is liable to be set aside. The Patwari admitted no notice was issued, so the Fard Badar was rightly declared ineffective and liable to cancellation. Ref: 2026 LHC 5749; Province of Punjab through District Collector, Multan & others v. Muhammad Arjumand Khan & others (R.F.A. No.504 of 2023, decided 08.09.2026).
records.title: Province of Punjab through District Collector, Multan & others v. Muhammad Arjumand Khan & others (R.F.A. No.504 of 2023, decided 08.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Transfer of Case to Special Court under S. 12A
records.heading: Section 12A permits transfer of a case to a Special Court despite parent statute limits
records.text: A Special Court cannot assume jurisdiction beyond its parent law by consent. Where s. 12A authorises transfer of any case to a Special Court and sub-s. (3) vests it with the powers of the transferor Court, objections based on the limits of the parent statute lose their basis. The Consumer Court's lack of jurisdiction under the 1997 Act does not bar the transferred lis.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Ss. 94 and 540 CrPC: Lacuna and Essential Evidence
records.heading: Essential evidence cannot be excluded merely because it repairs a lacuna
records.text: A lacuna is an inherent weakness in a party's case and not every omission to place material on record. Evidence essential to a just decision cannot be excluded merely because it will repair an omission. S. 94 and s. 540 CrPC and Art. 161 QSO empower and oblige the Court to seek the truth, and the first part of s. 540 is discretionary while its second part is mandatory. Ref: Shahzad Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Petition No.569-L of 2026, decided 12.08.2026).
records.title: Shahzad Ahmad v. The State (Criminal Petition No.569-L of 2026, decided 12.08.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Relationship and Minor Discrepancies
records.heading: Relationship of eyewitnesses and minor discrepancies do not make their testimony unreliable
records.text: Minor discrepancies about bulb locations or a cart's condition, arising from the long interval before evidence, do not touch the core of the prosecution case. Relationship of the son and nephew with the deceased does not make their testimony unreliable, and the solitary trustworthy evidence of the informant can sustain conviction. Ref: Ali Raza Siyal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 384 of 2023, decided 16.09.2026).
records.title: Ali Raza Siyal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 384 of 2023, decided 16.09.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Police Delay in Registering FIR: Duty of Trial Court
records.heading: A trial court must examine and record a finding on police delay in registering an FIR
records.text: Where the record shows police knew of a cognizable offence but registered the FIR after more than three days, the trial Court should notice that conduct and may proceed under s. 201 PPC if made out. Delay attributable to police is not a mere irregularity, and the Court must record a finding on its cause and take lawful action. Ref: Ali Raza Siyal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 384 of 2023, decided 16.09.2026).
records.title: Ali Raza Siyal v. The State (Jail Petition No. 384 of 2023, decided 16.09.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Belated Challenge to Oral Mutation: Fraud Allegation
records.heading: A challenge to a mutation after twenty-two years on bald fraud allegations is time-barred
records.text: A mutation sanctioned in 1980 was challenged in 2002 alleging fraud and misrepresentation, after an unexplained delay of over twenty-two years and with only bald allegations. The Trial Court and Appellate Court had dismissed the suit as time-barred and unproved. The Supreme Court allowed the appeals, set aside the High Court's revisional judgment, restored the concurrent decrees and dismissed the suit. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1019; Pir Shah Abdul Haq (decd.) thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Irfan and others (C.A. 2148/2019).
records.title: Pir Shah Abdul Haq (decd.) thr. LRs. v. Muhammad Irfan and others (C.A. 2148/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Recall of Ad Interim Injunction for Delay
records.heading: Recall of an ad interim injunction is discretionary where the favoured party delays the matter
records.text: Grant and recall of an ad interim injunction pending the interim application is discretionary, and the Court may regulate its own procedure and decline extension where the favoured party's conduct delays the matter or abuses process. The petition was disposed of with a direction that the trial court decide the interim application on merits without unnecessary adjournments. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 610.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Suit: Refusal of Special Oath
records.heading: Refusal to take a special oath does not warrant an adverse inference
records.text: A court may decide on special oath, but refusal to take it does not warrant an adverse inference, and the Oaths Act, 1873 does not make it conclusive proof of the other party's assertion. At best it is one circumstance among others. The Appellate Court erred in reversing the Family Court's findings solely on the father's refusal, and the Family Court's judgment was restored. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 627.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation for Appeal Runs from Signing of Decree
records.heading: Limitation for an appeal runs from the date of signing of the decree
records.text: Under Art. 156 of the Limitation Act, 1908 limitation for an appeal starts from the date of signing of the decree, and the time between judgment and decree is treated as time for obtaining certified copies. Where the decree sheet was not prepared or signed, the appeal could not be treated as time-barred, and the s. 5 application must be decided by the decree sheet date. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 654.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Police Rules 22.70 and 22.72: Registers XIX and XXI
records.heading: Police Rules 22.70 and 22.72 govern the store room register and road certificates
records.text: Explains Rr. 22.70 and 22.72 of the Police Rules, 1934. Register No. XIX is the store room register and Register No. XXI is the book of road certificates. A road certificate is the formal dispatch document used whenever case property moves between official custodies, such as from police station to laboratory. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 63, 2026 PCrLJ 259; Naseem Kousar v. The State (Crl. A. No. 351 of 2024).
records.title: Naseem Kousar v. The State (Crl. A. No. 351 of 2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Withholding Best Evidence: Art. 129(g) QSO
records.heading: Withholding material witnesses attracts the presumption under Article 129(g) QSO
records.text: In a suit for recovery on a cheque, the plaintiff did not name or produce material witnesses, including her brother and two of the three persons said to be present at payment. This amounted to withholding the best evidence and attracted the presumption under Art. 129(g) QSO against her. The decree was set aside and the suit dismissed. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 601; Salamat Ali v. Sabohi Naz (R.F.A. 27359/24).
records.title: Salamat Ali v. Sabohi Naz (R.F.A. 27359/24)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower: Nikahnama Governs Quantum
records.heading: The Nikahnama determines the quantum of dower, and a later claim to enlarge it needs proof
records.text: Dower terms are primarily determined from the Nikahnama, and a later claim to substitute or enlarge the recorded dower bears a burden of proof. Payment of dower in gold ornaments does not, without more, prove an agreed fixed weight of gold apart from the sum recorded in the Nikahnama. The claim of seven tolas lacked documentary support and could not enhance the relief. Ref: Aamir Mumtaz v. Mst. Hina Hassan and 2 others (W.P. No. 5143 of 2025, decided 10.09.2026).
records.title: Aamir Mumtaz v. Mst. Hina Hassan and 2 others (W.P. No. 5143 of 2025, decided 10.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVI R. 1 CPC: List of Witnesses Mandatory
records.heading: A list of witnesses is mandatory only for witnesses summoned through the court
records.text: Filing a list of witnesses under O. XVI R. 1 CPC is mandatory for witnesses sought to be summoned through the Court. Parties may produce any witness voluntarily even if unlisted, but the testimony must stay within the pleadings and annexed documents. Listed private witnesses may give evidence beyond pleadings. Ref: Waqas Qadir v. Mst. Badra Khatoon and others (Civil Revision No. 102/2025, decided 10.09.2026).
records.title: Waqas Qadir v. Mst. Badra Khatoon and others (Civil Revision No. 102/2025, decided 10.09.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Prisoner's Medical Treatment: Rule 197 Prison Rules
records.heading: A prisoner has no unfettered right to demand admission to a particular private hospital
records.text: The Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978 oblige prison authorities to provide medical treatment and a mechanism for referral to outside hospitals.
