Rule 197 allows removal where special treatment is necessary but does not give a prisoner an unfettered right to demand admission to a particular private hospital. Necessity is determined by the prescribed mechanism on competent medical opinion. Ref: Awais Altaf v. The Superintendent, Central Prison Adiala, Rawalpindi, and others (Writ Petition No.4105 of 2026, decided 27.08.2026).
records.title: Awais Altaf v. The Superintendent, Central Prison Adiala, Rawalpindi, and others (Writ Petition No.4105 of 2026, decided 27.08.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Long March: Fundamental Rights and Public Officials
records.heading: No political party may close roads, and public officials must respect citizens' fundamental rights
records.text: According to the detailed order, no political party has a legal right to close roads, and provincial governments must not use state resources or vehicles for the march on Islamabad. Any public officeholder who violates the fundamental rights of citizens in the Islamabad Capital Territory violates the Constitution and his oath and is liable to the consequences provided by law. Ref: Waqas Ahmed v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Interior & others (W.P. No.4421 of 2026).
records.title: Waqas Ahmed v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary, Ministry of Interior & others (W.P. No.4421 of 2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: S. 77 Registration Act Suit and Death of Principal
records.heading: A section 77 Registration Act suit is confined to the legality of refusal of registration
records.text: A suit under s. 77 of the Registration Act, 1908 is confined to the legality of refusal of registration and not the underlying transaction or title. A power of attorney ends on the principal's death under s. 201 of the Contract Act, so refusal of registration was lawful. Dismissal of an s. 77 suit does not bar a separate suit for specific performance. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 679; Muhammad Shafique etc v. Muhammad Shabbir etc (Civil Revision.1378-15).
records.title: Muhammad Shafique etc v. Muhammad Shabbir etc (Civil Revision.1378-15)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Exhumation and Post-Mortem: Ss. 174 and 176 CrPC
records.heading: A Magistrate may order exhumation and post-mortem in suspicious deaths under section 176 CrPC
records.text: Where the cause of death is uncertain and no medical examination preceded burial, an independent inquiry is required. S. 176 CrPC empowers the Magistrate to order inquiry, including exhumation and post-mortem, in suspicious or unnatural deaths. This is an investigative step and not a finding of culpability, and the petition was allowed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 677.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Condonation of Delay: Sufficient Cause
records.heading: Condonation of delay requires a plausible explanation of the whole period of delay
records.text: Limitation rests on public policy of certainty and finality, and a litigant seeking condonation must come with clean hands and explain the whole period of delay plausibly and in good faith. Negligence, indolence or casual conduct are not sufficient cause, and negligence after return of proceedings weakens the plea of bona fide prosecution. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 500; T&T Employees Cooperative Housing Society, Islamabad v. Haji Ghulam Hussain and others (C.P.L.A.3469/2025).
records.title: T&T Employees Cooperative Housing Society, Islamabad v. Haji Ghulam Hussain and others (C.P.L.A.3469/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Right of Wife and Abuse of Process
records.heading: Khula is a wife's lawful exit from marriage, and baseless litigation against it is an abuse of process
records.text: Khula gives a wife a lawful means to exit a marriage she no longer wishes to continue, at the price of forgoing her dower wholly or partly. Litigation that seeks to delegitimise the exercise of that right through false or baseless proceedings is an abuse of the process of court and an affront to the woman's dignity. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 504; Sultan v. Mst. Roshi Zeb & others (C.P.L.A.303-P/2018).
records.title: Sultan v. Mst. Roshi Zeb & others (C.P.L.A.303-P/2018)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Share of Sole Daughter and Doctrine of Radd
records.heading: A sole daughter takes one half under Hanafi law, and Radd applies only without residuaries
records.text: Mutation entries are maintained only for revenue and fiscal purposes. Under Hanafi law a sole surviving daughter takes one half of her father's estate as her Quranic share. The residue goes to the residuaries (asaba), and returns to the Quranic heir by Radd only where no residuaries exist. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 534; Mst. Ameer Begum and others v. Rahima Khatoon and others (C.P.L.A.97-Q/2024).
records.title: Mst. Ameer Begum and others v. Rahima Khatoon and others (C.P.L.A.97-Q/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Rejection of a plaint under Order VII Rule 11 CPC cannot replace a trial on disputed facts
records.text: O. VII R. 11 CPC is exceptional and cannot replace a regular trial where the alleged bar depends on disputed facts, interpretation of a disputed instrument, the parties' legal relationship or the capacity of the plaintiff. The plaint is read as a whole with pleaded facts assumed correct, and absence of a cause of action differs from failure to prove one. Ref: 2026 LHC 5860; Hakeem Muhammad Irfan Kashif & others v. Hassan Ali & others (R.F.A. No.203 of 2022, date of hearing 15.09.2026).
records.title: Hakeem Muhammad Irfan Kashif & others v. Hassan Ali & others (R.F.A. No.203 of 2022, date of hearing 15.09.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nature of Nikah, Dower and Nikahnama
records.heading: Dower, Nikahnama and the duties of Nikah Registrars under Islamic law
records.text: Authority on the legal nature of marriage and dower under Islamic law, immovable property given to a wife in lieu of dower, and interpretation of the Nikahnama including the presumption attached to it and Columns 13 to 16. It also states that Nikah Registrars who fail in their duties or breach licence conditions should face action by the competent authority. Ref: Mst. Farwa Noreen v. Hassan Ali Agha & others (C.P.L.A.372-P/2019, decided 22.09.2026); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Mst. Farwa Noreen v. Hassan Ali Agha & others (C.P.L.A.372-P/2019, decided 22.09.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Penal Provision Invoked by Police: Ss. 320 and 322 PPC
records.heading: A court is not bound by the penal provision invoked by the police
records.text: The court is not bound by the penal provision invoked by the police and examines the FIR and investigation material to see what provision is prima facie attracted. Ss. 320 and 322 PPC are both cognizable, as the words may arrest without warrant in Schedule II show. Courts take a liberal approach in post-arrest bail, as s. 322 PPC is outside the prohibitory clause of s. 497(1) CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 729; Nadeem Abbas v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 4411/B/2026).
records.title: Nadeem Abbas v. The State and another (Crl. Misc. No. 4411/B/2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Injured Witness: Injuries Not Proof of Truthfulness
records.heading: Injuries on a prosecution witness do not by themselves prove he speaks the whole truth
records.text: Mere injuries on an injured prosecution witness do not mean he is speaking the whole truth. His evidence is to be accepted or rejected in light of all the facts and circumstances, and his narrative must carry authenticity. The post also notes the medical text view that burning can occur where a pistol is fired from within two feet. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 753; Abdul Rehman alias Babi v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.507-J of 2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman alias Babi v. The State (Crl. Appeal No.507-J of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Class-IV Appointment: Preference for Land Donor
records.heading: A land donor or his nominee may lawfully receive a preferential margin for a Class-IV post
records.text: Appointments in the public sector must be made on merit. Where land is voluntarily alienated gratis for public welfare projects such as schools, dispensaries or tubewells, a preferential margin may lawfully be given to the donor or his nominee for a Class-IV post, provided the candidate meets all eligibility, suitability and fitness criteria on par with others. Ref: PLJ 2026 FCC 128; Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa v. Abdur Raqib & other (C.P.L.A. No.15-P of 2023 & C.P.L.A 132-P/2023).
records.title: Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa v. Abdur Raqib & other (C.P.L.A. No.15-P of 2023 & C.P.L.A 132-P/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Revenue Entries: Presumption of Truth, Gift Challenge
records.heading: Mutations and jamabandi entries carry a presumption of truth unless rebutted by convincing evidence
records.text: A bare allegation against a gift or revenue entry, without challenging title before the Revenue Authorities or a competent court and without cogent evidence, cannot succeed in a suit for declaration and injunction. Mutations and entries in jamabandis carry a presumption of truth under s. 52 of the West Pakistan Land Revenue Act, 1967, unless rebutted by convincing evidence. Ref: Abdul Latif and others v. Abdul Jabbar and another (C.P.L.A.155-Q/2022, decided 15.07.2026); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Abdul Latif and others v. Abdul Jabbar and another (C.P.L.A.155-Q/2022, decided 15.07.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Official Witnesses: Presumption of Regularity Rebuttable
records.heading: The presumption of regularity attaching to official witnesses is rebuttable
records.text: The testimony of official witnesses is treated as reliable on the maxim omnia praesumuntur rite et solemniter esse acta, but the presumption is not absolute. It is rebuttable and holds only so long as the record is not tainted by mala fides, procedural dishonesty or departure from the path of justice. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 299; Muhammad Shafi v. The State (Criminal Petition No.847/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Shafi v. The State (Criminal Petition No.847/2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Secret Cavities: Vehicle or Photographs Required
records.heading: Recovery from secret vehicle cavities needs the vehicle or clear photographs, not oral testimony alone
records.text: Where recovery of narcotics is said to be from secret cavities in a vehicle, oral testimony alone is insufficient. The prosecution should produce the vehicle, where feasible, or at least clear photographs showing the cavities open and closed, their location and the registration number. Bare assertions by police witnesses leave a serious lacuna in the prosecution case. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 279; Alam Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 51 of 2023).
records.title: Alam Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 51 of 2023)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Sample Chain: Contradiction
records.heading: Contradiction on who handed over case property breaks the chain of safe custody
records.text: Conviction on recovery of narcotics requires trustworthy and unimpeachable evidence that the substance remained in safe custody and that the samples examined by the laboratory were those drawn from the recovered substance. A material contradiction between the investigating officer and the Moharrir on who handed over the case property was a significant defect. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 279; Alam Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 51 of 2023).
records.title: Alam Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition No. 51 of 2023)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Section 34 PPC: Common Intention Not Presumed
records.heading: Section 34 PPC cannot be applied from mere presence at the scene
records.text: Section 34 PPC cannot be applied merely from presence at the scene or association with the actual assailant. The prosecution must prove through cogent evidence that the act was done in furtherance of common intention, and mere presence is insufficient. The courts below erred in fastening vicarious liability on the armed convict who fired no shot. Ref: Jamshair v. The State (Criminal Petition No.22-Q/2023, decided 25.08.2026).
records.title: Jamshair v. The State (Criminal Petition No.22-Q/2023, decided 25.08.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Overseas Pakistanis Property Special Courts Act, 2025
records.heading: The Punjab special courts Act protects overseas Pakistanis' rights in immovable property
records.text: The Punjab Establishment of Special Courts (Overseas Pakistanis Property) Act, 2025 created specialised forums to protect ownership and possession rights of overseas Pakistanis in immovable property, with e-filing, video-link evidence and strict timelines. The Court stressed that the preamble guides the construction of the substantive provisions. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 756; Javed Masih v. Amar Javed and others (Writ Petition No.2345 of 2026).
records.title: Javed Masih v. Amar Javed and others (Writ Petition No.2345 of 2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Section 489-F PPC: Cheque as Security, Bail
records.heading: A cheque given as security in commercial dealings lacks dishonest intention under section 489-F PPC
records.text: Where the amount found due on investigation was far below the cheque amount and the cheques were given as surety in ongoing commercial dealings, dishonest intention under s. 489-F PPC is prima facie missing. The provision is not a recovery mechanism, the dispute is predominantly civil, and bail under s. 497 CrPC is the rule in such offences. Ref: Farman Ali Khan v. The State & another (Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1448 of 2026, decided 22.09.2026).
records.title: Farman Ali Khan v. The State & another (Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1448 of 2026, decided 22.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Amendment of Pleadings
records.heading: Amendment of pleadings under Order VI Rule 17 CPC is a cautious judicial discretion
records.text: The power to allow amendment of pleadings under O. VI R. 17 CPC is a judicial discretion to be exercised cautiously. Amendment should be refused where it alters the nature of the suit, withdraws admissions, is mala fide, causes irreparable prejudice or seeks to cure evidentiary deficiencies. The court must examine bona fides, stage, delay and prejudice. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 358; Mehbub Ullah and another v. Mst. Taj Bibi and other (C.P.L.A.5215 of 2024).
records.title: Mehbub Ullah and another v. Mst. Taj Bibi and other (C.P.L.A.5215 of 2024)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Judicial and Retracted Confession: Corroboration
records.heading: A retracted confession needs independent corroboration to sustain a capital conviction
records.text: A confession with minute, highly structured details of many murders, lacking spontaneity, raises doubt about voluntariness and truthfulness. A retracted confession needs independent corroboration in material particulars and cannot alone sustain a capital conviction. The headnote also refers to mandatory safeguards in recording confessions and to Art. 10A. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1689; Ahmed Saeed @ Bharam @ Nagori v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 649/2022 in J.P. No. 385/2019).
records.title: Ahmed Saeed @ Bharam @ Nagori v. The State and another (Criminal Appeal No. 649/2022 in J.P. No. 385/2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 540 CrPC and Confession Requirements
records.heading: Closure of evidence does not bar the court from placing the best available evidence on record
records.text: Closure of evidence brings finality, but procedural strictness must be balanced against the demands of justice so that technicalities do not obstruct the truth, especially where crucial evidence exists outside the closed phase of the trial. The best available evidence should be placed before the court. The judgment also discusses confession and when it is vitiated by inducement or deception. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 483; Dr. Raheem Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl.P.L.A.721-L/2025).
records.title: Dr. Raheem Ullah and others v. The State and others (Crl.P.L.A.721-L/2025)

records.subject: Illegal Dispossession Act 2005
records.topic: Directions to Courts Under Illegal Dispossession Act
records.heading: The Supreme Court directed trial courts to complete Illegal Dispossession Act trials within 60 days
records.text: Relying on Arts. 10A and 187 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court issued directions to all trial courts under the Illegal Dispossession Act, 2005. These include completing the trial within the 60 days under s. 5(2), keeping a day-to-day order sheet, recording reasons for adjournments, and proceeding with the trial despite a challenge to an interim order unless a higher forum restrains it. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 472; Raja Khan v. Suhail Arif Shah and another (Crl.P.L.A.818/2026).
records.title: Raja Khan v. Suhail Arif Shah and another (Crl.P.L.A.818/2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Supreme Court and FCC: Arts. 175F and 185 Jurisdiction
records.heading: Writ proceedings go to the Federal Constitutional Court and Article 185 proceedings to the Supreme Court
records.text: Under the present constitutional scheme, all writ proceedings except rent and family matters fall within the Federal Constitutional Court, while regular proceedings under Art. 185 remain with the Supreme Court. Writ and regular proceedings that were clubbed together must therefore be de-clubbed, and Art. 189(1) cannot be construed to subordinate one apex court to the other. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 460; (Civil Petition Nos. 1011, 1040 and 1964 of 2020).
records.title: (Civil Petition Nos. 1011, 1040 and 1964 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Motive: Non-Reporting Plausible; Age and Sentence
records.heading: Absence of a prior police complaint does not doubt a family honour motive
records.text: A motive touching the dignity and honour of a family, shared only with the father, is not cast in doubt by the absence of a prior complaint to the police, as such matters are often unreported. The motive was not artificial or improbable. The convict's age, though not absolving him, is relevant to sentence, and the death penalty would not accord with proportionality and individualised sentencing. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 477; Javed Ali v. The State (J.P.202/2025).
records.title: Javed Ali v. The State (J.P.202/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XIII R. 2 CPC: Delayed Production of Documents
records.heading: No universal rule bars production of documents after examination-in-chief under Order XIII Rule 2
records.text: No universal rule bars or permits production of a document after examination-in-chief. The stage is relevant but not conclusive. The court considers prior disclosure, good cause for delay, consistency with pleadings, surprise and whether prejudice can be cured by cross-examination or rebuttal, exercising discretion under O. XIII R. 2 CPC with recorded reasons. Ref: 2026 LHC 6009; Muhammad Waqar v. Ch. Khalid Akbar (Civil Revision-657-24, decided 16.09.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Waqar v. Ch. Khalid Akbar (Civil Revision-657-24, decided 16.09.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics Cases: Strict Proof and Due Process
records.heading: The gravity of narcotics offences does not dilute the standard of proof
records.text: The seriousness of narcotics offences does not dilute the standard of proof. Because of the harsh punishments, courts must insist on strict proof of recovery, custody, sampling, transmission and conscious possession. The Court deprecated deficiencies such as non-production of Malkhana record, unexplained delay in sending samples and casual destruction proceedings, and directed circulation of its observations. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1606, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 273; Mehmood Khan and others v. The State (Criminal Petition No.1544 of 2025).
records.title: Mehmood Khan and others v. The State (Criminal Petition No.1544 of 2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Daily Diary, Recovery Proceedings and Procedure
records.heading: Failure to produce the Daily Diary departure entry supports an inference the police party never went
records.text: Failure to produce the Daily Diary entry of departure of the police party supports an inference that the party did not go to the spot. Absence of proof of ownership of the motorcycle or exclusive possession of the premises, and no explanation for not conducting proceedings at the place of arrest, made the prosecution case highly doubtful. Prescribed procedure must be strictly followed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1790; Muhammad Abdullah Tariq v. The State etc (Criminal Appeal No.159-L of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Abdullah Tariq v. The State etc (Criminal Appeal No.159-L of 2021)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Execution: First Petition Time-Barred, s. 48 CPC
records.heading: A time-barred first execution petition is fatal, and section 48 CPC does not extend limitation
records.text: The first execution petition must be filed within three years under Art. 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908. Section 48 CPC sets only an outer limit for proceedings properly begun and does not extend that period. If the first petition was time-barred, the defect is fatal and a later petition cannot be sustained under s. 48 CPC. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1785; Rasheed (deceased) through LRs and others v. Muhammad Azam Khan and others (Civil Petition No. 4530 of 2024).
records.title: Rasheed (deceased) through LRs and others v. Muhammad Azam Khan and others (Civil Petition No. 4530 of 2024)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Old Exceptions to s. 300 PPC and s. 302(c)
records.heading: Cases under the old exceptions to section 300 PPC fall under section 302(c)
records.text: Cases covered by the exceptions to the old s. 300 PPC read with old s. 304 PPC were intended to be dealt with under the new clause (c) of s. 302 PPC. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1426; Asif Hussain v. The State (Jail Petition No.644 of 2017).
records.title: Asif Hussain v. The State (Jail Petition No.644 of 2017)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Readiness and Willingness, Deposit
records.heading: A purchaser who fails to deposit the balance consideration cannot show readiness and willingness
records.text: A suit for specific performance must satisfy Forms 47 and 48 of Appendix A to the First Schedule CPC. A purchaser who fails to comply with a direction to deposit the balance sale consideration cannot show readiness and willingness, which renders his pleading untrue and leaves him without a cause of action. Dismissal under O. XVII R. 3 CPC was upheld. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1726; Amjad Javed v. Maqsood Ahmad, etc. (C.A.173-L/2020).
records.title: Amjad Javed v. Maqsood Ahmad, etc. (C.A.173-L/2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Court: Late Objection to Territorial Jurisdiction
records.heading: A territorial jurisdiction objection not pressed before trial concluded is only a technical defect
records.text: Objections to territorial or pecuniary jurisdiction must be raised at the earliest stage, before or at settlement of issues, as provided by s. 21 CPC. Where the objection to the place of suing under rule 6 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Rules, 1965 was never pressed and trial concluded, the defect is only technical. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1743, PLJ 2026 SC 68; Farzana Yasmeen and others v. Sohail Ahmed and another (Civil Petition No. 3606 of 2025).
records.title: Farzana Yasmeen and others v. Sohail Ahmed and another (Civil Petition No. 3606 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Closure of Evidence, Adjournments
records.heading: A trial court may close evidence under Order XVII Rule 3 after repeated opportunities
records.text: After about ten opportunities with warnings, the trial court rightly closed the right to produce evidence under O. XVII R. 3 CPC. The Court deplored excessive adjournments, noted that the CPC fixes no number of opportunities but gives the court discretion, and that the rule protects the process from dilatory tactics. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1613; Irfan Rasheed v. Zawar Muhammad Afzal and others (C.P.L.A.3470/2025).
records.title: Irfan Rasheed v. Zawar Muhammad Afzal and others (C.P.L.A.3470/2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 360 CrPC: Reading Over Witness Statement
records.heading: A witness's testimony must be read over to him under section 360 CrPC
records.text: Under s. 360(1) CrPC a witness's testimony must be read over to him in the presence of the accused or counsel and corrected if necessary. Section 360(2) allows the witness to object to the record, whereupon the Judge, after hearing the parties, appends a memorandum of the objection with his remarks and records the correct version. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 283; Mst. Nayab v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A.1033/2024).
records.title: Mst. Nayab v. The State thr. P.G. Sindh and others (Crl.P.L.A.1033/2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: PEEDA: Absence from Duty and Proportionality of Penalty
records.heading: Removal for 63 days of absence without reasons was disproportionate under PEEDA
records.text: Under s. 7(f)(ii) of PEEDA, proven absence exceeding one year attracts compulsory retirement, removal or dismissal. For shorter absence the Authority may impose any penalty under s. 4, but with reasons and proportionality. Removal for 63 days of absence without reasons or confronting previous record was unjustified. Petition allowed, without back benefits. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1238.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Disability Quota: Section 31, Punjab Act 2022
records.heading: Section 31 requires public sector departments to reserve at least 3% of posts for persons with disabilities
records.text: Section 31 of the Punjab Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2022 is imperative and obliges all public sector departments to reserve not less than 3% of posts for persons with disabilities. The State must make the measure operational in a transparent, fair and accessible manner. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1198.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Colonization of Government Land Act: Civil Court Jurisdiction
records.heading: Civil courts cannot undo fraudulently obtained colony land rights, which lie with the Board of Revenue
records.text: Proprietary rights in colony land obtained by fraud remain subject to s. 30(1) conditions, and s. 30(2) of the Colonization of Government Land Act, 1912 empowers the Member Board of Revenue to undo them. Under s. 36, civil courts cannot enter that jurisdiction. The High Court may reverse concurrent illegal findings under s. 115 CPC. Ref: 2026 MLD 1662.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summary Suit: Judicious Mind Despite Leave Recalled
records.heading: A court must apply its judicious mind before decreeing a summary suit ex parte
records.text: In a summary suit on a cheque, even where conditional leave to defend was recalled for non-compliance and the matter proceeded ex parte, the court must apply its judicious mind to the plaintiff's facts and documents before decreeing. The decree was set aside and the case remanded to impose a condition with one opportunity to comply. Ref: 2026 MLD 1743.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Tenant Cannot Deny Landlord by Setting Up Third Party Title
records.heading: A tenant cannot deny his landlord by setting up disputed third party title
records.text: A tenant inducted by the ejectment petitioner cannot, while keeping possession under that tenancy, unilaterally disown the relationship by setting up a disputed third party title. Rival proprietary claims are for the competent forum and give the tenant no defence to ejectment by the landlord who inducted him. Ref: 2026 LHC 6205; Ejaz Hussain v. Saeed Ahmad (WP-3428-21, decided 22.09.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Ejaz Hussain v. Saeed Ahmad (WP-3428-21, decided 22.09.2026)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA of Collateral Relatives: Limited Probative Value
records.heading: DNA testing of collateral relatives gives only indirect and less conclusive proof of parentage
records.text: DNA testing of collateral relatives, not the alleged parent, gives only indirect and less conclusive evidence of parentage, and courts caution against routine reliance on it without supporting evidence. The High Court's finding for the respondents on official records and witnesses was upheld and leave to appeal was dismissed. Ref: Barkat Khan others v. Banaras Khan and others (C.P.L.A.1157/2021, decided 16.09.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Barkat Khan others v. Banaras Khan and others (C.P.L.A.1157/2021, decided 16.09.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Section 514 CrPC: Show-Cause Before Forfeiture of Surety Bond
records.heading: A show-cause notice is essential before forfeiture of a surety bond under section 514 CrPC
records.text: A show-cause notice is a sine qua non before forfeiture of a surety bond, as s. 514 CrPC is a complete code on due process. A mere notice for appearance of the surety was insufficient, and the forfeiture order was unsustainable for violating the statute and fundamental rights. Ref: 2026 LHC 6160; Muhammad Akhtar v. The State etc (WP. 80586/22, decided 23.09.2026); Justice Muhammad Amjad Pervaiz.
records.title: Muhammad Akhtar v. The State etc (WP. 80586/22, decided 23.09.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Consistency with Co-Accused
records.heading: Pre-arrest bail follows where the co-accused with an identical role is on post-arrest bail
records.text: Where the petitioner's role is indistinguishable from a co-accused already on unchallenged post-arrest bail, denying pre-arrest bail would serve no purpose as he would obtain post-arrest bail on consistency. The merits may be touched on in pre-arrest bail, and an accused with a strong case for post-arrest bail should not be jailed to satisfy the complainant. Ref: 2026 LHC 6166; Ehsan Ullah v. The State, etc (Crl. Misc. No.53729-B of 2026, decided 23.09.2026).
records.title: Ehsan Ullah v. The State, etc (Crl. Misc. No.53729-B of 2026, decided 23.09.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay Bail: Third Proviso s. 497(1) CrPC
records.heading: Bail is available after one year's detention where delay is not due to the accused
records.text: Under clause (a) of the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, an accused detained over one year for a non-capital offence, whose trial is not concluded, is released on bail if the delay is not due to his own act or omission. Failure of the prosecution to produce the prisoner in court cannot be attributed to the accused. Ref: Chaudhary Shahzaib Shamim v. The State through the Federal P.G Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A.1449/2026, decided 24.09.2026); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Chaudhary Shahzaib Shamim v. The State through the Federal P.G Islamabad & another (Crl.P.L.A.1449/2026, decided 24.09.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Injunction Between Co-Sharers in Joint Property
records.heading: A co-sharer may sue for a permanent injunction against another co-sharer in limited circumstances
records.text: A suit for permanent injunction by one co-sharer against another is not barred absolutely and may lie where the act complained of threatens to alter the nature of the joint property or prejudices a legally protectable right. The plaintiff must prove the factual basis for such protection. Ref: 2026 LHC 6340; Muhammad Ishtiaq etc v. Abdul Waheed (Civil Revision-855-24, decided 24.09.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Muhammad Ishtiaq etc v. Abdul Waheed (Civil Revision-855-24, decided 24.09.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Disciplinary Action: Punishment Beyond the Charge Sheet
records.heading: An employee cannot be punished on an allegation outside the charge sheet
records.text: A delinquent employee cannot be punished for an allegation outside the charge sheet, nor can the authority materially enlarge the case after the defence and decide against him without a fresh hearing. The sequence is charge, effective opportunity to defend, then determination on the case put to him. This requirement was not met here. Ref: Muhammad Zulfiqar Abbasi Israr Khan v. The Director General Peshawar Development Authority, Peshawar and others (C.P.L.A.2501/2024 and C.P.L.A.500-P/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Zulfiqar Abbasi Israr Khan v. The Director General Peshawar Development Authority, Peshawar and others (C.P.L.A.2501/2024 and C.P.L.A.500-P/2024)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sections 54 and 52 TPA: Registered Sale and Lis Pendens
records.heading: A claim of earlier transfer needs a registered instrument, and lis pendens runs from presentation of the plaint
records.text: Under s. 54 TPA a sale of immovable property valued at Rs. 100 or more requires a registered instrument, so a claim of an earlier transfer must be backed by an effective instrument or cogent material. Section 52 lis pendens operates from presentation of the plaint, and a transferee pendente lite cannot defeat it by pleading bona fide purchase without notice. Ref: 2026 LHC 6223; Muhammad Iqbal Nadeem v. Mst. Talat Riaz, etc. (C.R. No.1484-D of 2025, decided 23.09.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal Nadeem v. Mst. Talat Riaz, etc. (C.R. No.1484-D of 2025, decided 23.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Non-Suit on Unpleaded Ground, O. XIV CPC
records.heading: A party cannot be non-suited on a ground neither pleaded nor put in issue
records.text: A party cannot ordinarily be non-suited on a ground neither properly pleaded nor made the subject of an issue. O. XIV Rules 1 and 5 CPC require material propositions to be framed as issues. As the decisive limited estate theory was not pleaded or put in issue, the matter required reconsideration at the appellate stage after hearing the parties. Ref: 2026 LHC 6231; Muhammad Aslam Khan & others v. Muhammad Afzal & others (Civil Revision No.569 of 2019, decided 24.08.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam Khan & others v. Muhammad Afzal & others (Civil Revision No.569 of 2019, decided 24.08.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Section 17A(3) Family Courts Act: Annual Maintenance Increase
records.heading: A Family Court may order annual maintenance enhancement above 10% without breaching section 17A(3)
records.text: A Family Court may order annual enhancement of maintenance above 10% or on a compound basis without violating s. 17A(3) of the Family Courts Act, 1964. That subsection applies only where the decree is silent on the rate, in which case maintenance rises automatically by 10% each year. Ref: Sadiq Subhani v. Sadia Urooj and others (C.P.L.A.4959/2025, decided 22.09.2026); Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Sadiq Subhani v. Sadia Urooj and others (C.P.L.A.4959/2025, decided 22.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Review: Restaurant Site, MHNP and CDA Jurisdiction
records.heading: Restaurant site entitlement in the MHNP involves disputed facts for the Civil Court
records.text: In review, it was held that entitlement to the restaurant site, its lease and recovery of rent involve disputed facts for the Civil Court after evidence. The earlier finding that all leases and permissions for restaurants in the MHNP were contrary to the 1979 Ordinance was set aside. The MHNP forms part of Islamabad Capital Territory, and CDA has jurisdiction over building approvals there. Ref: Metropolitan Corporation through its Chief Officer and others (CRP) v. Monal Group of Companies through its Sole Proprietor, Lahore & others (C.R.P. No. 825/2024 & F.C.R.P. No. 44/2025 in C.P.L.A. No. 304/2022, decided 29.09.2026).
records.title: Metropolitan Corporation through its Chief Officer and others (CRP) v. Monal Group of Companies through its Sole Proprietor, Lahore & others (C.R.P. No. 825/2024 & F.C.R.P. No. 44/2025 in C.P.L.A. No. 304/2022, decided 29.09.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Matrimonial Agency Does Not Create Criminal Liability
records.heading: Matrimonial agency is a civil principle and does not create criminal liability for a wife
records.text: The principle of matrimonial agency between spouses is a civil law principle limited to household and contractual obligations protecting the wife's maintenance. It has no application to criminal liability, and no penal statute fastens liability on a wife merely because of the marital relationship. Proof of conscious and voluntary involvement is required. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 457; Mst. Rukhsana Sajid v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 1510-L/2025).
records.title: Mst. Rukhsana Sajid v. The State and another (Criminal Petition No. 1510-L/2025)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Prison Rules: Rule 217(ii) Life Imprisonment Remission
records.heading: Remissions cannot reduce a life sentence below fifteen years of actual imprisonment under Rule 217(ii)
records.text: Under Rule 217(ii) of the Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978, for a prisoner sentenced to life imprisonment the cumulative effect of all remissions cannot reduce actual imprisonment below fifteen years. The restriction is mandatory unless the sentence is lawfully altered by the competent authority. The nominal roll computation of the petitioner was prima facie inconsistent with it. Ref: Suba Khan v. Superintendent Central Prison Mach & others (F.C.P.L.A.833/2025).
records.title: Suba Khan v. Superintendent Central Prison Mach & others (F.C.P.L.A.833/2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Doctors Dispensing Drugs: Licence Under Drugs Act 1976
records.heading: A doctor needs a Drugs Act licence to run a medical store or drug outlet
records.text: A registered doctor may prescribe and provide medicine to his patient but cannot run a medical store or retail drug outlet without the licence required by the Drugs Act, 1976. The Peshawar High Court order halting proceedings was set aside, as writ jurisdiction at the show-cause stage was premature. Ref: Govt. of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary Health Department, Peshawar and others v. Dr. Muhammad Rizwan Rajpoot and others (C.P.L.A.538-P/2023); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.
records.title: Govt. of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary Health Department, Peshawar and others v. Dr. Muhammad Rizwan Rajpoot and others (C.P.L.A.538-P/2023)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Harassment Act: Sexual Element Required
records.heading: Harassment Act proceedings require a sexual element for the Ombudsman to have jurisdiction
records.text: Action under the harassment law requires a sexual element, and not every inappropriate behaviour is sexual harassment. Without it the complaint is outside the Federal Ombudsman's jurisdiction under the Act, though the employer may proceed under its service rules. The President may hear representations against the Ombudsman's decision. The Islamabad High Court judgment was set aside. Ref: Usman Shahid, Aqeel Abbas v. Nadia Sarwar & 04 others (CPLA No. 1011 & 1113 of 2026); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.
records.title: Usman Shahid, Aqeel Abbas v. Nadia Sarwar & 04 others (CPLA No. 1011 & 1113 of 2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Illegality Cannot Ripen into Right by Passage of Time
records.heading: An authority's illegality cannot ripen into a lawful right through passage of time
records.text: An illegality committed by an authority cannot become a lawful right through passage of time or reliance on it. Otherwise administrative error would override the law. The matter concerned cancelled allotments of high-rise flats in Phase-V, Hayatabad, Peshawar, to federal government employees. Ref: Syed Ashfaq Anwar, Sohail Ahmad, Muhammad Sajjad and others v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Housing, Peshawar and others (C.P.L.As.800 & 1581/2023 and Crl.A.383/2023); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.
records.title: Syed Ashfaq Anwar, Sohail Ahmad, Muhammad Sajjad and others v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Secretary, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Housing, Peshawar and others (C.P.L.As.800 & 1581/2023 and Crl.A.383/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Compromise and Consent Decrees: O. XXIII R. 3 CPC
records.heading: Compromise and consent decrees both require the court to examine the agreement for legality and fairness
records.text: Compromise decrees and consent decrees are distinct though similar, and both require the court to examine the agreement for legality and fairness. The post discusses s. 96(3) and O. XXIII R. 3 CPC, and notes that requiring fresh proceedings for each breach of a compromise would defeat the purpose of consent decrees. Ref: Ali Haider Shinwari & others v. Muhammad Qubais & others (C.R No. 351-P of 2026, decided 17.03.2026).
records.title: Ali Haider Shinwari & others v. Muhammad Qubais & others (C.R No. 351-P of 2026, decided 17.03.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII CPC: Legal Heirs Not Signatories of Cheque
records.heading: Legal heirs who did not sign a cheque cannot be sued under Order XXXVII as successors
records.text: Under ss. 29 and 29-A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, liability rests on signing the instrument. Legal heirs who did not sign the cheque or note cannot be sued under O. XXXVII CPC merely as successors, though a debt claim may survive against the estate. Once a probable defence is shown, the burden shifts back to the plaintiff. Ref: Mst. Azram Jan widow & others v. Muhammad Sultan through L.Rs (R.F.A No. 15-A of 2013, decided 31.03.2026).
records.title: Mst. Azram Jan widow & others v. Muhammad Sultan through L.Rs (R.F.A No. 15-A of 2013, decided 31.03.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Pre-1984 Deeds, Art. 115 QSO, Concurrent Findings
records.heading: One marginal witness suffices for a deed executed before the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order 1984
records.text: For a deed executed before the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984, Arts. 17 and 79 do not apply and one marginal witness suffices. A tenant or lessee claiming later ownership must first vacate under Art. 115 QSO. Concurrent findings may be set aside under s. 115 CPC for misreading or non-reading of evidence. Ref: Shahid Sultan Durani etc v. Khalid Mehmood (CR No. 717-P of 2019, decided 08.04.2026).
records.title: Shahid Sultan Durani etc v. Khalid Mehmood (CR No. 717-P of 2019, decided 08.04.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dower Property: Boundary Discrepancies
records.heading: A wife cannot be denied dower property because of boundary discrepancies in its description
records.text: A wife cannot be denied property forming part of her dower merely because of contradictions in the description of boundaries, which may change over time. The executing court may identify the dower property or ascertain the market value of an identical property and order payment of it to the wife. Ref: Shahid Sultan Durani etc v. Khalid Mehmood (CR No. 717-P of 2019, decided 08.04.2026).
records.title: Shahid Sultan Durani etc v. Khalid Mehmood (CR No. 717-P of 2019, decided 08.04.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Section 47 CPC: Executing Court Powers, s. 151
records.heading: The executing court has wide exclusive jurisdiction under section 47 CPC and may use section 151
records.text: Section 47 CPC gives the executing court wide and exclusive jurisdiction over all disputes on execution, discharge or satisfaction of a decree, and it must ascertain whether the decree is fully implemented. Section 151 CPC inherent powers may be invoked where decrees stay unsatisfied through prolonged non-compliance, so that technicalities do not defeat justice. Ref: Wazir Zada Afridi v. Muhammad Akram & others (F.A.O No. 22-A of 2009, decided 04.05.2026).
records.title: Wazir Zada Afridi v. Muhammad Akram & others (F.A.O No. 22-A of 2009, decided 04.05.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Res Judicata: Injunction Suit and Later Declaration Suit
records.heading: An injunction suit does not bar, as res judicata, a later declaration suit by a stranger
records.text: A suit for permanent injunction by one party does not bar, as res judicata, a later suit for declaration of title by a different person on a different cause of action who was not a party to the earlier suit. An objection rejected by a speaking order cannot be re-agitated at a later stage of the same proceedings. Ref: Mst. Farkhanda Jabeen and others v. Sakhi Gul and others (CR No. 584-P of 2023, decided 11.05.2026).
records.title: Mst. Farkhanda Jabeen and others v. Sakhi Gul and others (CR No. 584-P of 2023, decided 11.05.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Common Vendor and Judicial Record Presumption
records.heading: Judicial forum records carry a strong presumption of correctness over oral assertions
records.text: Proceedings, statements and orders of a competent judicial forum carry a strong presumption of correctness and are preferred over oral assertions. Where both parties claim title from the same vendor, his statement before a judicial forum in favour of either party is ordinarily to be appreciated in that party's favour. Ref: Mst. Farkhanda Jabeen and others v. Sakhi Gul and others (CR No. 584-P of 2023, decided 11.05.2026).
records.title: Mst. Farkhanda Jabeen and others v. Sakhi Gul and others (CR No. 584-P of 2023, decided 11.05.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Section 118 NI Act and Art. 129(c) QSO Presumptions
records.heading: Section 118 NI Act imposes a heavier burden on the defendant than Article 129(c) QSO
records.text: Art. 129(c) QSO says the court may presume consideration, leaving discretion, while s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 says it shall presume, which imposes a heavier initial burden on the defendant. As a special law the NI Act prevails over general evidence rules. The appellant failed to prove liability by evidence and the suit was dismissed. Ref: Shoaib Rehman v. Muhammad Ishaq (RFA No. 174-P of 2025, decided 19.05.2026).
records.title: Shoaib Rehman v. Muhammad Ishaq (RFA No. 174-P of 2025, decided 19.05.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Parentage Dispute: Official Records and Welfare of Child
records.heading: Official records are the most reliable evidence in parentage disputes, which cannot be reopened after a decade
records.text: Courts must protect the welfare of minors, and a child's parentage cannot be reopened after over a decade because of later family hostility, given acquiescence. In parentage disputes, official records such as birth registers, certificates and identity cards are the most reliable evidence, with family conduct and long recognition also significant. Arts. 46 and 64(5) QSO are cited. Ref: Muhammad Iqbal v. Abdul Khaliq & another (C.R No. 1431-P of 2025, decided 03.06.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal v. Abdul Khaliq & another (C.R No. 1431-P of 2025, decided 03.06.2026)

records.subject: Legal Profession
records.topic: Counsel's Duty to Assist Court on Jurisdiction
records.heading: Counsel must identify the competent forum and assist the court on jurisdiction at the threshold
records.text: Identifying the competent forum is a primary professional duty of counsel. Filing a suit before a forum lacking jurisdiction, due to a statutory bar, arbitration clause or international immunity, may amount to deficient professional assistance. Members of the Bar must exercise due diligence and assist the court at the threshold on jurisdiction and maintainability. Guidelines were laid down for bar and bench. Ref: Muhammad Ismail v. United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) through representative & another (CR No 282-P of 2024, decided 11.06.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Ismail v. United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) through representative & another (CR No 282-P of 2024, decided 11.06.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: Surety Cannot Withdraw Undertaking
records.heading: A surety for a decreed liability in execution cannot unilaterally withdraw the undertaking
records.text: A surety undertaking for a fixed and decreed liability in execution is not a continuing guarantee under ss. 129 and 130 of the Contract Act, 1872. Sureties cannot unilaterally revoke it after acceptance by the court. Ss. 133 to 139 list grounds of discharge but give no right to withdraw, and under s. 128 the surety's liability is co-extensive with the principal debtor's. Ref: Shahid Gul and another v. Ziaullah Wazir and another (RFA No. 263-A of 2023, decided 18.06.2026).
records.title: Shahid Gul and another v. Ziaullah Wazir and another (RFA No. 263-A of 2023, decided 18.06.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Mutation Not a Title Document: Burden on Beneficiary
records.heading: A mutation is not a title deed, and its beneficiary must prove the underlying transaction
records.text: A mutation is not a deed of title. When challenged, its beneficiary must prove valid entry under s. 42 of the Land Revenue Act, 1967, the original transaction, his full domain and, for a sale, payment of consideration. A co-heir's possession is on behalf of other co-heirs, and concurrent findings may be set aside under s. 115 CPC for misreading of evidence. Ref: Ismail v. Alam Shah etc (CR No. 768-P of 2023, decided 19.06.2026).
records.title: Ismail v. Alam Shah etc (CR No. 768-P of 2023, decided 19.06.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Section 12(2) CPC: Fraud Allegations Need Particulars
records.heading: Fraud allegations without particulars do not justify reopening a decree under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: Mere allegations of fraud, forgery or collusion without specific particulars and cogent material do not justify reopening a decree under s. 12(2) CPC. Issues and evidence are not needed in every such application. The s. 36 bar of the 1912 Act covers only matters within the Revenue authorities' powers. An agreement to sell by an allottee cannot itself confer State ownership. Ref: 2026 LHC 6494; Province of Punjab v. ADJ etc (WP.237725/18, decided 22.09.2026); Justice Hassan Nawaz Makhdoom.
records.title: Province of Punjab v. ADJ etc (WP.237725/18, decided 22.09.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Time Essence, Readiness, Forged Receipts
records.heading: Specific performance: time is not essential merely because a date is fixed
records.text: The headnote covers specific performance of an agreement to sell immovable property under the Specific Relief Act, 1877, time as essence under the Contract Act, 1872 (mere fixation of a date does not make time essential), vendor's failure to perform antecedent obligations, vendee's readiness, and burden of proof under Art. 117 QSO regarding alleged forged receipts. Ref: 2026 LHC 6505; Waseem Hassan v. Muhammad Nadeem (Civil Revision.29310/26, decided 24.09.2026); Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani.
records.title: Waseem Hassan v. Muhammad Nadeem (Civil Revision.29310/26, decided 24.09.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Omitted Heir: Proof of Relationship, Art. 64 QSO
records.heading: Relationship may be proved under Article 64 QSO by an uncle with special knowledge
records.text: Relationship may be proved under Art. 64 QSO by the testimony of a real uncle with special knowledge, and a pedigree in an inheritance mutation does not substitute for proof of relationship. Non-production of the Lambardar raises an adverse presumption under Art. 129(g). A daughter who predeceased her father is not a surviving heir, and her legal heirs' entitlement is determined under the applicable succession law. Ref: 2026 LHC 6516; Dilawar Hussain v. Muhammad Iqbal etc. (Civil Revision.192-17, decided 24.09.2026); Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani.
records.title: Dilawar Hussain v. Muhammad Iqbal etc. (Civil Revision.192-17, decided 24.09.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Proof of Oral Gift (Hiba) Beyond Mutation
records.heading: A mutation entry is not title, and a challenged oral gift must be proved by the donee
records.text: A mutation entry alone is not a document of title, and where an oral gift is specifically challenged the donee must prove the underlying transaction. An oral hiba ordinarily requires declaration by the donor, acceptance by the donee and delivery of possession. The evidence as a whole, including the donor's acknowledgment, must be evaluated together. Ref: 2026 LHC 6525; Muhammad Aslam Khan, etc. v. Nazeeran Bibi (deceased) through LRs and others (C.R. No.560-D of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam Khan, etc. v. Nazeeran Bibi (deceased) through LRs and others (C.R. No.560-D of 2024)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Ex Parte Decree: Article 164 Versus Article 181
records.heading: Article 164 governs applications to set aside an ex parte decree and Article 181 is residuary
records.text: Section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1908 obliges the court to dismiss a time-barred application even if limitation is not pleaded. Art. 164 gives thirty days to set aside an ex parte decree, while Art. 181 is residuary and applies only where no other article does. The governing article depends on the relief sought and the applicant's procedural position. Ref: Muhammad Iqbal v. Additional District Judge, Burewala, District Vehari & another (F.A.O. No.83 of 2018).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal v. Additional District Judge, Burewala, District Vehari & another (F.A.O. No.83 of 2018)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula Conversion Without Consent; Shiqaq Under s. 2(ix)
records.heading: A Family Court cannot convert a dissolution claim into khula without clear and voluntary consent
records.text: Family Courts erred in converting claims for dissolution on cruelty into khula decrees without clear and voluntary consent. As cruelty was not proved but the record showed shiqaq, the dissolution was sustained under s. 2(ix) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 and not as khula. Directions on dowry articles were left undisturbed. Ref: Mst. Zainab Bibi v. Muhammad Waseem and others (C.P.L.A.57/2025, decided 07.10.2026).
records.title: Mst. Zainab Bibi v. Muhammad Waseem and others (C.P.L.A.57/2025, decided 07.10.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Case Property: De-Sealing and Exhibiting Parcels
records.heading: Case property in narcotics trials must be de-sealed, shown to the witness and exhibited
records.text: Case property in narcotics trials must be de-sealed, shown to the witness and exhibited in court. Exhibiting sealed parcels without opening them or confronting the witness with their contents would prejudice the accused in his defence. Ref: 2026 LHC 6660; Ghulam Haider v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal.51392/26, decided 14.09.2026); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Ghulam Haider v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal.51392/26, decided 14.09.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Confiscation of Vehicle: Owner's Knowledge, ss. 32 and 33
records.heading: Vehicle confiscation under the narcotics Act requires proof that the owner knew of its use
records.text: Under ss. 32 and 33 of the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997 a trial court may order confiscation of a vehicle even on acquittal, but only if the prosecution proves the owner knew the vehicle was used in the crime. The record showed no inquiry or proof of the appellant's knowledge. Ref: 2026 LHC 6553; Muhammad Kashif v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-411-20, decided 13.05.2026); Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram.
records.title: Muhammad Kashif v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-411-20, decided 13.05.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail: Further Inquiry and Digital Evidence, Non-Prohibitory
records.heading: Digital evidence cannot be examined deeply at bail stage, and non-prohibitory offences favour bail
records.text: The authenticity and probative worth of documents and digital material cannot be examined deeply at the bail stage. This raises further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. The co-accused was on post-arrest bail, so consistency applied, and the offences under ss. 420, 468, 471 and 109 PPC fall outside the prohibitory clause, making bail the rule. Ref: Syed Muhammad Ashfaq v. The State through Deputy Attorney General of Pakistan (Crl.P.L.A.100-K/2026, decided 24.09.2026); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Syed Muhammad Ashfaq v. The State through Deputy Attorney General of Pakistan (Crl.P.L.A.100-K/2026, decided 24.09.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Registered Title: Weight and Surrounding Circumstances
records.heading: A registered title carries weight but does not bar inquiry into the true character of the transaction
records.text: A registered title carries substantial evidentiary weight and cannot be displaced by conjecture or bare oral assertion. Registration does not bar inquiry into the source of consideration and true character of the transaction where in issue and supported by admissible evidence. The effect is assessed on all circumstances, possession and conduct on a preponderance of probabilities. Ref: 2026 LHC 6739; Nazar Muhammad etc v. Muhammad Shahid etc (Civil Revision-757-14, decided 15.09.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Nazar Muhammad etc v. Muhammad Shahid etc (Civil Revision-757-14, decided 15.09.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Disputed Talaq: Family Court and s. 7 MFLO
records.heading: A Family Court must determine a disputed talaq despite the section 7 MFLO notice requirement
records.text: A Family Court should not decline to determine the disputed factum of Talaq merely because its legal effectiveness is regulated by s. 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. A husband who avoids the statutory process cannot rely on his own non-compliance with s. 7 notice as a jurisdictional veto over Union Council proceedings. Ref: 2026 LHC 6754; Raheel Ahmad v. Tayyaba Haq etc. (WP.3165-26, decided 17.09.2026); Justice Anwaar Hussain.
records.title: Raheel Ahmad v. Tayyaba Haq etc. (WP.3165-26, decided 17.09.2026)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Cancellation of Bail: Complainant's Attorney, s. 497(5)
records.heading: A complainant's attorney may apply to cancel bail under section 497(5) CrPC
records.text: An application under s. 497(5) CrPC for cancellation of bail does not require the complainant's personal presentation, so his absence from Pakistan does not make it incompetent. Safeguards are that the special power of attorney must authorise the proceeding, and the attorney's affidavit must be confined to facts within his own knowledge. Ref: 2026 LHC 6733; Tasleem Khan through Muhammad Imran Khan v. The State etc (Office Objection Diary No.73417/26, decided 02.07.2026); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Tasleem Khan through Muhammad Imran Khan v. The State etc (Office Objection Diary No.73417/26, decided 02.07.2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Unsigned Recovery Memo: Further Inquiry, Bail
records.heading: An unsigned recovery memo and no independent witnesses make bail a case of further inquiry
records.text: In a CNSA case, an unsigned recovery memo, where police officials are named as witnesses, is a material infirmity. With no genuine effort to associate independent persons at a public place, the case is one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC, relying on 2022 SCMR 864 and Arts. 18 and 78 QSO. The Inspector General of Police, Punjab, was directed to correct recurring lapses. Ref: 2026 LHC 6779; Muhammad Afzaal alias Afzaali v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.47324/26, decided 01.10.2026); Justice Amir Ajam Malik.
records.title: Muhammad Afzaal alias Afzaali v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.47324/26, decided 01.10.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Executing Court Cannot Go Behind Decree
records.heading: An executing court must give effect to the decree as it stands
records.text: An executing court must give effect to the decree as it stands and cannot modify it or substitute relief, relying on PLD 2024 SC 960 and 2024 YLR 2505. Family Court decrees are read to advance the female decree-holder's relief. Execution is still a judicial process, and the process must stay within the decree and be directed against the proper persons. Ref: 2026 LHC 6823; Zameer ul Hassan v. Executing Court etc (WP.6916-24, decided 01.10.2026); Justice Muhammad Sajid Mehmood Sethi.
records.title: Zameer ul Hassan v. Executing Court etc (WP.6916-24, decided 01.10.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Non-Affixation of Court Fee: Curable Defect
records.heading: Non-affixation of court fee is a curable defect
records.text: Authority on non-affixation of court fee being a curable defect, and on the interplay between s. 149 CPC, the Court-Fee Act, 1870 and the Limitation Act, 1908. Ref: 2026 CLC 1645.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance Without Registration Stipulation
records.heading: An agreement to sell without a registration stipulation does not bar specific performance
records.text: Under s. 55(1)(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, absent a contrary contract, the seller must execute a proper conveyance. An agreement to sell without a stipulation on registration therefore does not bar a decree for specific performance, and the seller was obliged to execute a registered sale deed. The appellate court's contrary finding was flawed. Ref: 2026 CLC 1627; Farida Khanum v. Abdul Qayyum etc (Regular Second Appeal 694-21).
records.title: Farida Khanum v. Abdul Qayyum etc (Regular Second Appeal 694-21)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Counsel Without Instructions: Service and Ex Parte Decree
records.heading: Counsel stating no instructions is not deemed to accept service, so ex parte decree is liable to be set aside
records.text: Knowledge of proceedings is distinct from due service. Counsel who states he has no instructions is not deemed to have accepted service, so the trial court must ensure service on the party itself before proceeding. An ex parte decree after substituted service without due service violates audi alteram partem and is liable to be set aside. Ref: Ghulam Mujtaba (deceased) through his L.Rs v. Ghulam Murtaza (C.P.L.A.1748/2023, decided 05.10.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Ghulam Mujtaba (deceased) through his L.Rs v. Ghulam Murtaza (C.P.L.A.1748/2023, decided 05.10.2026)

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Cantonment Property Tax: Educational Institution Exemption
records.heading: Charging tuition fees does not by itself make an educational institution commercial for tax exemption
records.text: Under s. 99(2)(b) of the Cantonment Act, 1924 educational buildings were a distinct category with exemption, the conditions of public access and no income applying only to playgrounds and dharmsalas. The 2023 amendment made exemption discretionary. Charging tuition fees does not by itself make an institution commercial, but non-profit character alone does not satisfy non-derivation of income. Ref: 2026 LHC 6899; Lahore University of Management Sciences through Syed Sohail Hussain Naqvi etc v. Director General Military Land and Cantonments Rawalpini etc (WP.180995/18, decided 06.10.2026); Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: Lahore University of Management Sciences through Syed Sohail Hussain Naqvi etc v. Director General Military Land and Cantonments Rawalpini etc (WP.180995/18, decided 06.10.2026)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Demarcation by Revenue Officer: Remedies, ss. 117, 161, 164
records.heading: A Revenue Officer's demarcation under section 117 is open to objection, appeal and revision
records.text: A demarcation by a Revenue Officer under s. 117 of the Land Revenue Act is not immune from challenge. Affected persons may participate and object, seek correction before the Revenue Officer, appeal under s. 161 within limitation, and the revisional authority may examine the proceedings under s. 164. Ref: 2026 CLC 1609.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Free Fight: Exception 4 to S. 300 PPC
records.heading: A sudden unplanned quarrel with injuries to both sides is a free fight under Exception 4
records.text: Where an unplanned quarrel erupted suddenly and injuries were caused to both sides, the responsibility for aggression could not be fixed on either party. The occurrence was a free fight and melee, and each participant is liable only for his own act. Exception 4 to the former s. 300 PPC was attracted. Ref: 2026 YLR 2244.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sentencing Philosophies and Reformation of Convict
records.heading: Courts must consider reformation of the convict before fixing the quantum of sentence
records.text: The judgment discusses retribution, incapacitation, deterrence, rehabilitation and reparation as philosophies of sentencing. Since ss. 324, 337-D, 337-A(i) and 337-F(iii) PPC prescribe sentences extending up to a maximum term, courts must consider circumstances indicating reformation of the convict before fixing the quantum of sentence. Ref: 2026 YLR 2244.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Lumberdars: No Proprietary Rights in State Land
records.heading: Lumberdars acquire no proprietary rights in state land leased to them
records.text: A Punjab Colonies Department notification dated 17.01.2006 superseded earlier instructions and provides that no proprietary rights in state land leased to Lumberdars are to be conferred. The notification remains in force and extinguished the claim. Writ petitions of the Lumberdars were dismissed. Ref: 2026 YLR 2350.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Arts. 102 to 104 QSO: Documentary Terms Prevail
records.heading: Oral evidence cannot contradict or vary the terms of a written agreement under Articles 102 to 104
records.text: Where parties have reduced the terms of an agreement to writing, Arts. 102, 103 and 104 QSO exclude oral evidence to contradict, vary, add to or subtract from the document. The document itself is final as to the parties' intent, and the parties are bound by its terms. Ref: 2026 YLR 2301; Muhammad Arif & 1 other v. Haji Khalid Mahmood deceased through LRs (Civil Revision 45106/23).
records.title: Muhammad Arif & 1 other v. Haji Khalid Mahmood deceased through LRs (Civil Revision 45106/23)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Discharge of Accused in Sessions Cases
records.heading: A Court of Session may discharge an accused where no material exists to proceed
records.text: Even in cases triable by a Court of Session, the Court may discharge the accused where it finds that no material is available to proceed with the trial. Such power is inherent in the Court. Ref: 2026 YLR 2415.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Eggshell Skull Rule at Bail Stage
records.heading: Under the eggshell skull rule the accused takes the victim as found
records.text: Under the eggshell skull rule the accused must take the victim as found. Pre-existing infirmity or age of the victim does not excuse the accused if his unlawful act contributed materially to death. Mitigating circumstances are for the trial court after evidence. Bail refused. Ref: 2026 YLR 2507; Muhammad Shah Meer v. The State (Crl. Misc. 6504-B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Shah Meer v. The State (Crl. Misc. 6504-B/2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Extra Judicial Custodial Killing: Death Sentence
records.heading: Anger over injured colleagues does not mitigate the extra judicial killing of a suspect in custody
records.text: A paramilitary official who shot a fleeing suspect after a bomb blast was convicted and sentenced to death. His sadness and anger over injured colleagues was no mitigating factor, as accepting it would encourage vigilantism by law enforcers. The death sentence confirmed by the High Court was upheld. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1622.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Proof of Murder; Fee of State Counsel
records.heading: A corroborated judicial confession proves murder, and State-appointed defence counsel receive full fee
records.text: The accused's judicial confession was corroborated by recovery of the rifle, a positive Forensic Science Laboratory report, identification parade and eye-witnesses, so the prosecution proved its case. The Supreme Court directed its office to pay full fee under the rules to defence counsel appointed at State expense, even if the convict later engaged private counsel. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1622.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Sentencing Discretion in Qatl-i-Amd
records.heading: Sentencing in qatl-i-amd is a judicial discretion requiring recorded reasons
records.text: Sentencing involves a judicial discretion that cannot be exercised mechanically or on whimsical grounds, and no exhaustive list of factors exists. In qatl-i-amd the court must record reasons, particularly when imposing a punishment other than death, and weigh mitigating and aggravating circumstances carefully. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1622.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance of Minor: Liability of Paternal Uncle
records.heading: A paternal uncle's liability to maintain a minor depends on the facts of each case
records.text: Whether a paternal uncle is liable to maintain a minor after the father's death depends on the facts of each case, and courts cannot legislate to narrow the scope of responsibility for maintenance of a minor. The alleged transfer of the grandfather's property to the uncle during the suit needed additional evidence. Mahnoor Shabbir (2024 CLC 513) was held per incuriam qua the Family Courts Act, 1964. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 767, PLJ 2026 Lah 260.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Talaq: Delegated Right and Ninety-Day Period
records.heading: A wife delegated the right of divorce must give notice, and talaq takes effect after ninety days
records.text: A wife who has been delegated the right of divorce stands in the husband's shoes under s. 7. She must give notice to the Chairman, Union Council and send a copy to the husband, the talaq takes effect only after ninety days from notice, and she may revoke it within that period. A wife divorced under s. 7 is not excluded from inheritance merely because talaq was not yet effective. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1759.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC: Issues and Evidence
records.heading: Issues and evidence are not mandatory in every section 12(2) CPC application
records.text: Applications under s. 12(2) CPC challenge the integrity of a decree and should be decided promptly. Framing of issues and recording of evidence is not mandatory in every case, as the court must judge from the nature of the allegations whether the case is fit for it. Here, the questions of fact and law raised required issues and evidence. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1736.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Evidence Beyond Pleadings; Admitted Facts
records.heading: Evidence beyond the pleadings must be disregarded, and admitted facts need no proof
records.text: Evidence led beyond the pleadings must be disregarded. Facts that are admitted need not be proved. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1658.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Criminal and Civil Defamation: Concurrent Remedies
records.heading: Civil and criminal defamation remedies are distinct but co-existent
records.text: Criminal defamation under s. 499 PPC (punishable under s. 500) requires accountability for the publication, an untrue imputation and intent or knowledge to harm reputation. Civil and criminal defamation remedies are distinct but co-existent, and an aggrieved person may pursue either or both. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1658.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Presumptions and Evidential Burden: Bursting Bubble
records.heading: A presumption creates only an evidential burden on the accused, and it disappears once he explains
records.text: A presumption treats a presumed fact as proved once the primary fact is proved, unless rebutted. Where the statute places no legal burden on the accused, it creates an evidential burden, which he discharges by adducing some evidence without disproving the fact. If he explains, the presumption disappears and the normal burden applies, the bursting bubble theory. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1582; Ayaz Adil v. The State (Jail Appeal 6763/25).
records.title: Ayaz Adil v. The State (Jail Appeal 6763/25)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Documentary Evidence Preferred Over Oral Evidence
records.heading: Documentary evidence is preferred over oral deposition
records.text: Documentary evidence takes preference over oral deposition or assertion. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1639.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Chain of Safe Custody: Charas Sample Delay
records.heading: A Moharrar's admission contradicting the road certificate breaks the chain of safe custody
records.text: In a charas case, the Moharrar's admission that the road certificate was prepared on 17.10.2022 and the sample delivered on 18.10.2022 contradicted the road certificate. Oral evidence cannot be preferred over the document. Safe custody was not proved, the Forensic Science Agency report became unreliable, and the appeal against conviction was allowed. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1639.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: Compulsory DNA Test Without Consent: Arts. 9 and 14
records.heading: A compulsory DNA test without consent infringes the rights to liberty and privacy
records.text: A trial court order directing a DNA test to establish disputed parentage without consent, and without issuing process under s. 202 CrPC, infringes the fundamental rights to liberty and privacy under Arts. 9 and 14 of the Constitution. Genetic data concern lineage and bodily integrity, and public scrutiny of parentage without due process is an arbitrary restraint. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1780.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Change of Investigation After Challan and Charge
records.heading: Change of investigation after challan and framing of charge needs new material and reasons
records.text: Change or transfer of investigation is ordered sparingly, in exceptional circumstances such as unexamined essential aspects, new evidence, serious defects or bias of the Investigating Officer. A change after challan and framing of charge without new material was not sustainable, and the order also lacked reasons contrary to s. 24-A of the General Clauses Act, 1897. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1759.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Complaint Case and State Case: Single Judgment
records.heading: A complaint case and a State case from one occurrence cannot be decided by single judgment
records.text: Where a complaint case and a State case arise from the same occurrence, the complaint case should be tried first, with challan witnesses called as Court witnesses, and the State case follows as appropriate, including possible withdrawal under s. 494 CrPC. Deciding both by a single judgment was contrary to settled principles. Conviction set aside and matter remanded for re-writing of the judgment. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1688.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC Statement Omitted: Remand
records.heading: Failure to record a section 342 CrPC statement may lead to remand and not acquittal
records.text: Complete failure to record the accused's statement under s. 342 CrPC vitiates the conviction, but not every such omission must end in acquittal. The appellate court may remand under s. 423 CrPC for the statement to be recorded and the trial to proceed. The remand by the Lower Appellate Court was upheld. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1666.

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Tribal Sardar: No Legal Recognition for Attestation
records.heading: A tribal Sardar has no legal authority to attest CNICs or certificates
records.text: A tribal Sardar cannot claim legal authority to attest CNICs, domicile or local certificates on the basis of customary status. The Sardari system was abolished by s. 3 of the System of Sardari (Abolition) Ordinance, 1976, which ended legal recognition of the status and its privileges. The case also considered who is an aggrieved person under Art. 199. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 348.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Summoning School Principal to Prove Victims' Age
records.heading: A school Principal is a material witness on the age of minor victims
records.text: In a trial under s. 377-A(1) where the victim's age below eighteen is material, the Principal of the school and college along with the record was a material witness on the ages of the minor victims. The Trial Court was not justified in rejecting the application to summon him. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1801.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Deceased/Incapacitated Employee Quota: Married Daughters
records.heading: Marriage cannot disqualify a daughter from the deceased or incapacitated employee quota
records.text: Under R. 10(4), appointment against the quota for children of deceased or incapacitated employees is a recognition of the parent's service, with children acting as conduits for continuity of livelihood. Marriage cannot disqualify a daughter from appointment under this quota. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1105; (Civil Petition No. 1392 of 2024).
records.title: (Civil Petition No. 1392 of 2024)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal: Time-Barred Departmental Appeal
records.heading: A Service Tribunal cannot summarily dismiss an appeal merely because the departmental appeal was time-barred
records.text: A Service Tribunal cannot automatically dismiss an appeal merely because the departmental appeal was time-barred. As the first judicial appellate forum it must examine the full record on facts and law, including reasonable cause and condonation of delay, and cannot dispose of the question by summary dismissal. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1137.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Jactitation of Marriage and Legitimacy of Child
records.heading: A decree of jactitation of marriage does not make a child illegitimate
