records.text: A decree of jactitation of marriage does not automatically make a child illegitimate, and the presumption of legitimacy stands unless rebutted by proper evidence. The minor was not a party and the decree could not bind him on paternity. The Family Court was directed to decide only jactitation and dissolution, without findings on paternity, if the parties did not consent or approach the Civil Court. Ref: 2026 MLD 1693.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII: Grant of Leave Converts Suit to Regular
records.heading: Grant of leave to defend converts a summary suit into a regular suit
records.text: Once leave to defend is granted in a summary suit on a cheque, the suit loses its summary character and is converted into a regular civil suit. The procedure in O. XXXVII R. 7 CPC is then followed. Ref: 2026 MLD 1743.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Superdari: Interim Custody under S. 516-A CrPC
records.heading: Superdari is interim, discretionary custody of case property under section 516-A CrPC
records.text: Superdari is a judicially developed term for interim custody or disposal of case property under s. 516-A CrPC, which empowers the court to pass such order as it thinks fit. The terms superdari, interim custody and interim disposal are used interchangeably. The release is interim, discretionary and subject to final disposal of the property. Ref: 2026 LHC 6956; Ghulam Mustafa v. The State, etc. (Crl. Misc. 4042-Q/2026, decided 09.10.2026).
records.title: Ghulam Mustafa v. The State, etc. (Crl. Misc. 4042-Q/2026, decided 09.10.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Condemned Prisoner Cannot Claim Conversion After 14 Years
records.heading: A condemned prisoner has no right to conversion of sentence after fourteen years
records.text: A condemned prisoner and a prisoner sentenced to life cannot be placed in one category merely by the period spent in custody. Completion of fourteen or fifteen years gives a condemned prisoner no right to have the death sentence converted to life imprisonment, as that would distort the sentencing scheme. Ref: Muhammad Kamran v. The State thr. P.G. and another (Crl.R.P. 73/2025, decided 13.10.2026); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.
records.title: Muhammad Kamran v. The State thr. P.G. and another (Crl.R.P. 73/2025, decided 13.10.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Salary During Suspension Pending Inquiry
records.heading: A civil servant suspended pending inquiry is entitled to full salary absent legal sanction
records.text: Suspension pending departmental proceedings is an interim measure and not removal or termination, so the contract of service and employer-employee relationship continue. A suspended civil servant is entitled to full salary and benefits for the suspension period absent express legal sanction. Petition dismissed and leave declined. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1090.

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test and Presumption of Legitimacy
records.heading: DNA testing in paternity matters is not to be ordered merely on request or consent
records.text: DNA testing in paternity matters is a serious judicial act, not to be ordered merely on request or consent, and must serve the ends of justice and the child's welfare. The courts below rightly applied Art. 128 QSO and deferred the question until the Trial Court had a complete record. The High Court declined to interfere in constitutional jurisdiction. Ref: 2026 MLD 1736.

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Suit for Possession Without Declaration of Title
records.heading: A suit for possession alone is not maintainable where the defendant disputes the plaintiff's title
records.text: Relying on Khurshid Ali v. Miangul Adnan Aurangzeb (2025 SCMR 34), where the defendant disputes the plaintiff's title, the plaintiff must ordinarily seek a declaration of title with consequential relief. A suit for possession simpliciter on the strength of disputed title was not maintainable. Ref: Abdul Raheem (deceased) through L.Rs v. Government Normal School (C.A. 253-L/2010).
records.title: Abdul Raheem (deceased) through L.Rs v. Government Normal School (C.A. 253-L/2010)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Recording of Prosecution Evidence; Absent Post Mortem Staining
records.heading: Absence of post mortem staining despite a five-hour gap weakened the prosecution case
records.text: Prosecution evidence is produced under s. 265-F CrPC and recorded under ss. 356 to 360 CrPC with Arts. 132 and 133 QSO, with examination-in-chief first, then cross-examination, and re-examination only to explain matters from cross-examination. The medical officer's note of no post mortem staining despite a five-hour gap weakened the prosecution case, and best evidence was withheld. Ref: 2026 LHC 7010; Allah Dita v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal 607-J/2022, decided 08.10.2026).
records.title: Allah Dita v. The State, etc. (Criminal Appeal 607-J/2022, decided 08.10.2026)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Occupancy Tenants under KP Tenancy Act 1950
records.heading: Occupancy tenants under the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Tenancy Act cannot be evicted without due process
records.text: The judgment distinguishes occupancy tenants from tenants at will and traces the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Tenancy Act, 1950 (ss. 4, 4-A), under which occupancy tenants could become owners by seeking a declaration within the period in s. 83, with later extensions. Occupancy tenants cannot be evicted without due process and are entitled to compensation for improvements. Ref: Shams-ul-Haq v. Provincial Government through Secretary, Board of Revenue, Peshawar and others (CR 1292-P/2019, decided 29.06.2026).
records.title: Shams-ul-Haq v. Provincial Government through Secretary, Board of Revenue, Peshawar and others (CR 1292-P/2019, decided 29.06.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Public Interest Litigation on Jail Reforms
records.heading: Recommendations on prison reform include women jails, open prisons and digitalised records
records.text: The writ petition on prison management was disposed of with recommendations, including women jails at Lahore, Faisalabad and Rawalpindi, open prisons for prisoners in the last year of sentence, an electronic prisoner file system, digitalisation of court and prison records and video link trials. A quarterly progress report is to go to the Monitoring Judge. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 800.

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Limitation: Court Closure and S. 4 Limitation Act
records.heading: Delay during court closure is excusable where the appeal is filed on re-opening
records.text: Delay in filing appeals during court closure is excusable where the appeal is filed immediately on re-opening, under s. 4 of the Limitation Act, 1908. The High Court erred in relying solely on Art. 12(5). Appeals allowed on the limitation issue. Ref: Muhammad Akram, etc v. Mst. Nazeer Begum (decd.) thr. LRs., etc (C.A. 348/2018, decided 03.07.2026); Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi.
records.title: Muhammad Akram, etc v. Mst. Nazeer Begum (decd.) thr. LRs., etc (C.A. 348/2018, decided 03.07.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Minor Conviction and Police Recruitment
records.heading: A minor conviction under sections 285 and 286 PPC does not permanently bar police recruitment
records.text: A minor conviction under ss. 285/286 PPC, based on a confession and punished by a fine of Rs.500, does not permanently disqualify a candidate from police recruitment. FIR allegations alone do not establish guilt without conviction. Leave to appeal dismissed. Ref: Provincial Police Officer KPK Peshawar v. Hanifullah (C.P.L.A. 302-P/2023).
records.title: Provincial Police Officer KPK Peshawar v. Hanifullah (C.P.L.A. 302-P/2023)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Decree for Gold Ornaments: Market Value at Payment
records.heading: A decree for gold is satisfied by delivery or market value on the date of payment
records.text: Gold owed under a decree is satisfied by delivery in specie or by payment of the current market value on the date of payment. The decree is limited to the quantity and description established by the record. The executing court was directed to determine the payable amount, and the petition was allowed to that extent. Ref: 2026 LHC 7164; Ambreen Gohar & others v. Additional District Judge, Dera Ghazi Khan & others (W.P. 5648/2022, decided 12.10.2026).
records.title: Ambreen Gohar & others v. Additional District Judge, Dera Ghazi Khan & others (W.P. 5648/2022, decided 12.10.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Partition Suit: Burden of Proving Co-Ownership
records.heading: A partition plaintiff bears the burden of proving a subsisting co-ownership interest
records.text: A partition plaintiff must prove a subsisting co-ownership interest, the burden being on him under Art. 117 QSO. A registered instrument carries presumptions under ss. 35, 47 and 60 of the Registration Act and Art. 90 QSO, but where execution is denied, proof of execution is still required. A mutation is a fiscal entry only. Non-joinder should be cured under O. I R. 10(2) CPC. Ref: 2026 LHC 7072; Abdul Waheed Khan (deceased) through his legal heirs v. Hamid Majeed & others (C.R. 833/2015, decided 08.10.2026).
records.title: Abdul Waheed Khan (deceased) through his legal heirs v. Hamid Majeed & others (C.R. 833/2015, decided 08.10.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Malicious Prosecution Claim After Discharge
records.heading: Malicious prosecution requires proof of malice and absence of probable cause
records.text: A civil claim for malicious prosecution requires proof of malice and absence of probable cause. Where the plaintiff was discharged after investigation and the police acted on credible reports, malice was not proved. The first appeal was dismissed without costs. Ref: 2026 LHC 7266; Peer Javed Iqbal Shah v. Muhammad Mansha and 2 others (RFA 192/2026).
records.title: Peer Javed Iqbal Shah v. Muhammad Mansha and 2 others (RFA 192/2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Certified Copy Delay and Revisional Jurisdiction
records.heading: A late appeal without proof of certified copy dates is time-barred, but revision remains available
records.text: An appeal filed about eight months late was time-barred where the petitioner gave no proof of the date of preparation of the certified copy needed for s. 12 of the Limitation Act. Even so, the High Court has suo motu revisional power under s. 115 CPC. The revision petition was dismissed and closure of evidence upheld. Ref: 2026 LHC 7252; Muhammad Ahmad v. Muhammad Shafi Shakir (deceased) through his LRs etc. (C.R. 62808/2024, decided 13.10.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Ahmad v. Muhammad Shafi Shakir (deceased) through his LRs etc. (C.R. 62808/2024, decided 13.10.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Closure of Evidence
records.heading: Order XVII Rule 3 CPC is penal and must be applied strictly
records.text: Order XVII Rule 3 CPC is penal and must be applied strictly. Where a plaintiff repeatedly delayed evidence despite last opportunities, closure of evidence and dismissal of the suits were lawful. All related appeals were dismissed without costs as an abuse of process. Ref: 2026 LHC 7238; M/s. K. A. Gases Private Limited v. M/s Pak Arab Fertilizers Limited (R.F.A. 253/2026).
records.title: M/s. K. A. Gases Private Limited v. M/s Pak Arab Fertilizers Limited (R.F.A. 253/2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Same-Day Gift Mutations by Illiterate Woman
records.heading: Same-day gift mutations by an illiterate woman without proof of valid consent were not upheld
records.text: Successive gift mutations on the same day, with no proof of valid consent by an illiterate woman in continuous possession, were not upheld, and independent advice was necessary. The petitioner's claim as a bona fide purchaser under Section 41 failed as its conditions were not satisfied. Revision dismissed. Ref: 2026 LHC 7198; Muhammad Sarwar (deceased) through L.Rs v. Mst. Maqsoodan Bibi and others (C.R. 537/2015).
records.title: Muhammad Sarwar (deceased) through L.Rs v. Mst. Maqsoodan Bibi and others (C.R. 537/2015)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Lease Renewal Clause and Ejectment
records.heading: Leave to contest cannot be refused without reading the registered lease as a whole
records.text: The courts below refused leave to contest by looking only at expiry of the lease term, without reading the registered lease as a whole, including Clause 17 allowing continuation on payment of market rent. The tribunal was directed to decide the market rent and the relevance of the arbitration clause within sixty days, with no final ruling on possession. Ref: 2026 LHC 7148; Dr. Zulfiqar Ali Khan v. Additional District Judge, etc. (W.P. 5005/2023).
records.title: Dr. Zulfiqar Ali Khan v. Additional District Judge, etc. (W.P. 5005/2023)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Minors Unrepresented; Identification of Joint Holding
records.heading: Proceedings against minor defendants without established representation are invalid
records.text: Proceedings against minor defendants whose representation was not established are invalid. The courts also failed to examine the 1999 purchase, the revenue record, and whether the property was identified and separated from the joint holding. A suit for exclusive possession without partition raised maintainability concerns. The case was remanded for a fresh trial. Ref: 2025 LHC 8750; Mst. Mureedan Mai & others v. Shahid Hussain Khan, etc. (C.R. 1484-D/2014).
records.title: Mst. Mureedan Mai & others v. Shahid Hussain Khan, etc. (C.R. 1484-D/2014)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Possession and Declaration: Alleged Abadi Deh Restriction
records.heading: A chain of registered deeds was valid, and no legal prohibition on transfer was proved
records.text: The petitioners failed to produce admissible evidence of a legal prohibition on transfer of the house as part of Abadi Deh, and the chain of registered deeds and records from the original owner was held valid. The suit was not barred by limitation or adverse possession. Revision dismissed and concurrent judgments affirmed. Ref: 2026 LHC 7140; Nizam-ud-Din (deceased) through LRs, etc. v. Mst. Khursheed Begum, etc. (C.R. 1122-D/2018).
records.title: Nizam-ud-Din (deceased) through LRs, etc. v. Mst. Khursheed Begum, etc. (C.R. 1122-D/2018)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: MDCAT-2026 Question Papers: Access for Candidates
records.heading: Withholding MDCAT question papers impairs candidates' ability to review and challenge questions
records.text: Withholding MDCAT question papers after the examination impaired candidates' ability to review and challenge questions, and the direction to collect papers lacked clear justification. The court ordered the University of Health Sciences to upload the MDCAT-2026 question papers online permanently for Punjab candidates. Ref: 2026 LHC 7274; Rayyan Shahid Malik v. The Islamic Republic of Pakistan etc. (Writ Petition 3516/2026).
records.title: Rayyan Shahid Malik v. The Islamic Republic of Pakistan etc. (Writ Petition 3516/2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Eyewitness Testimony and Limits of Human Perception
records.heading: Close-range eyewitnesses are credible despite minor discrepancies from limits of human perception
records.text: Close-range eyewitnesses present in daylight were credible despite being interested witnesses, and minor discrepancies in the number of shots were acceptable given trauma and limits of human perception. The medical evidence matched their descriptions. The Court discouraged ocular accounts describing a bullet's travel from barrel to impact. Ref: Muhammad Azhar v. The State (J.P. 424/2021, decided 15.10.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Muhammad Azhar v. The State (J.P. 424/2021, decided 15.10.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Footage: Admissibility and Authentication
records.heading: CCTV footage must satisfy strict criteria of source, integrity and authentication
records.text: Digital evidence such as CCTV footage must meet strict criteria of source, integrity and authentication. Art. 164 QSO was amended in 2023, and such evidence is treated as documentary evidence under the Electronic Transactions Ordinance 2002. Complex forensic enhancement belongs in specialised labs, and indistinct footage requires visual comparison or expert reports. Ref: 2026 LHC 7319; Raja Shahid v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 27357/24, decided 28.09.2026); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Raja Shahid v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal 27357/24, decided 28.09.2026)

records.subject: Pre-emption
records.topic: Zar-e-Soim Deposit on Next Working Day
records.heading: A Zar-e-Soim deposit on the next working day is valid where the last day is a Sunday
records.text: Under s. 24 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act the deposit must be made within 30 days of filing the suit. Where the last day falls on a Sunday, deposit on the next working day is valid under the General Clauses Act. The deposit on 26.08.2024 was timely and the orders accepting it were upheld. Ref: 2026 LHC 7285; Muhammad Shah Zaib v. ADJ Bhera etc. (Misc. Writ 11018/25, decided 05.10.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Shah Zaib v. ADJ Bhera etc. (Misc. Writ 11018/25, decided 05.10.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Delayed FIR, Chance Witnesses and Doubtful Recovery
records.heading: Delayed FIR, chance witnesses and a doubtful recovery leave the prosecution short of proof
records.text: A three-hour FIR delay, chance witnesses unable to explain their presence, inconsistent places of death, inconclusive medical evidence, a doubtful weapon recovery and an insufficient motive left the prosecution short of proof beyond reasonable doubt. The appeal was allowed and the conviction reversed. The revision for enhancement was dismissed. Ref: 2026 LHC 7305; Muhammad Ashraf v. State Etc (Jail Appeal 76339/21, decided 07.10.2026); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. State Etc (Jail Appeal 76339/21, decided 07.10.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Regularisation of Contract Employees After Three Years
records.heading: A contract employee cannot be denied regularisation because the contract expired through departmental delay
records.text: A contract employee with three years' continuous service cannot be denied regularisation because the contract expired before the authority decided, owing to departmental delay. A valid subsisting contract at the time of consideration is not a precondition. The impugned order was set aside and the department directed to appoint the petitioners on regular basis. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1320.

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Sale Through Attorney: Proof of Authority and Consideration
records.heading: A sale through an attorney requires proof of authority, bona fides and payment of consideration
records.text: Producing a power of attorney does not by itself validate a sale of immovable property. The court must be satisfied that it was validly executed and proved, expressly authorised the sale, the principal consented, the attorney acted bona fide within authority, and consideration was actually paid. An attorney holds a fiduciary position. Ref: Mst. Nighat Sultana alias Kherogai v. Javed Akhtar and 31 others (CR 864-P/2019, decided 30.06.2026).
records.title: Mst. Nighat Sultana alias Kherogai v. Javed Akhtar and 31 others (CR 864-P/2019, decided 30.06.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Compensatory Costs: S. 35-A CPC and O. XLI R. 33
records.heading: Compensatory costs under section 35-A CPC lie only with the court of first instance
records.text: Ordinary costs under s. 35 CPC are discretionary, whereas compensatory costs under s. 35-A CPC are penal and vest exclusively in the court of first instance. By the proviso to O. XLI R. 33 CPC the appellate court cannot award them. The direction imposing costs of Rs.50,000 was declared illegal and set aside. Ref: Muhammad Zeeshan Ud Din v. Mst. Rukhsana Shafique & another (C.R. 850-P/2026, decided 01.07.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Zeeshan Ud Din v. Mst. Rukhsana Shafique & another (C.R. 850-P/2026, decided 01.07.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII Suit on Cheque: Proof of Presentment
records.heading: Presentment and dishonour of a cheque must be proved in a summary suit
records.text: Presentment of a cheque and its dishonour are conditions precedent to a cause of action in a summary suit under O. XXXVII CPC, and the statutory presumption cannot replace proof of them. With no return memo or bank record, and the cheque stale, no decree could be passed. Judgment set aside and suit dismissed. Ref: Muhammad Ijaz v. Zia-Ul-Haq (RFA 12/2024, decided 02.07.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz v. Zia-Ul-Haq (RFA 12/2024, decided 02.07.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Power of Attorney: Agency, Not Transfer of Title
records.heading: A power of attorney creates an agency and does not convey title
records.text: A power of attorney creates an agency and does not convey title or interest in immovable property to the attorney, whose authority is representative and confined to the powers granted. The relationship is fiduciary, and whether the transferee took reasonable care is a question of fact. Ref: Saleem Akhtar and anther v. Shahid Saleem and others (C.R. 381-A/2021, decided 16.07.2026).
records.title: Saleem Akhtar and anther v. Shahid Saleem and others (C.R. 381-A/2021, decided 16.07.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Inheritance: Custom and Shariat Act Cut-Off Date
records.heading: Inheritance rights acquired under custom before 6 December 1935 are a closed transaction
records.text: Relying on Ghulam Haider v. Murad (PLD 2012 SC 501), inheritance rights acquired before 06.12.1935 under custom are a past and closed transaction, while rights arising later are governed by the Shariat Act. The judgment also discusses limitation, acquiescence, estoppel, waiver and adverse possession in inheritance claims, and the High Court's duty in revision where the courts below differ. Ref: Mst. Zarin Taja v. Saifullah and others (C.R. 211-P/2014, decided 21.07.2026).
records.title: Mst. Zarin Taja v. Saifullah and others (C.R. 211-P/2014, decided 21.07.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Tatimma: No Unilateral Severance of Joint Survey Number
records.heading: A co-sharer cannot unilaterally sever a parcel from a joint survey number by tatimma
records.text: A tatimma is a revenue device for sub-division of a survey number and not a mode of partition. A co-sharer cannot unilaterally separate a specific parcel from joint property, as consent of all co-owners is required, failing which partition proceedings are needed. The alienation was preserved but severance through the mutation and tatimma was declined.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXXVII: Non-Compliance With Conditional Leave to Defend
records.heading: A condition attached to leave to defend is not merely directory
records.text: A condition imposed when granting leave to defend in an O. XXXVII CPC suit is not merely directory, and continuance of the leave depends on compliance. The general preference for deciding cases on merits cannot dilute it. The defendant was rightly proceeded against ex parte after non-compliance. Ref: Muhammad Ishaq v. Karim Khan (RFA 445-P/2025, decided 11.09.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Ishaq v. Karim Khan (RFA 445-P/2025, decided 11.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Malicious Prosecution: Discharge Under S. 169 CrPC
records.heading: Discharge under section 169 CrPC does not by itself establish malicious prosecution
records.text: Discharge under s. 169 CrPC is not an adjudication of innocence and does not by itself establish malicious prosecution. The plaintiff must still prove absence of reasonable and probable cause, malice and damage. Mere registration of an FIR followed by discharge does not suffice, relying on PLD 1990 SC 28, PLD 2006 SC 432 and 1999 SCMR 700. Ref: Shujahat Hanif v. Mukhtiar, etc. (W.P. 133-A/2024, decided 14.09.2026).
records.title: Shujahat Hanif v. Mukhtiar, etc. (W.P. 133-A/2024, decided 14.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Fraud: Specific Pleading and Proof
records.heading: Fraud must be specifically pleaded and proved by cogent evidence
records.text: Fraud must be specifically pleaded under O. VI R. 4 CPC and proved by cogent evidence, and a vague allegation does not suffice. A claim challenging revenue entries from the 1872 settlement, unasserted for over a century and with no date of discovery of fraud established, was legally unsustainable. Ref: Sain Muhammad v. Patwari Halqa (C.R. 519-A/2026, decided 16.09.2026).
records.title: Sain Muhammad v. Patwari Halqa (C.R. 519-A/2026, decided 16.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XXIII R. 1 CPC: Withdrawal With Liberty
records.heading: Withdrawal of a suit is a right, but liberty to file afresh needs a ground under Rule 1(2)
records.text: Withdrawal of a suit is a right under O. XXIII R. 1(1) CPC, but permission to file a fresh suit is not, and requires objective satisfaction of a ground under R. 1(2). Clause (a) concerns a formal defect and clause (b) other sufficient grounds. The conclusion that neither was shown was sustained, and the writ petition was dismissed. Ref: Muhammad Farid Khan & others v. Faisal Khan & others (W.P. 342-A/2024, decided 28.09.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Farid Khan & others v. Faisal Khan & others (W.P. 342-A/2024, decided 28.09.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Presumption of Innocence; Liability by Conscious Association
records.heading: A court cannot convict on emotion or public sentiment, as every accused is presumed innocent
records.text: A court cannot convict on emotion, public sentiment or religious outrage, as every accused is presumed innocent and the law requires proof. The judgment also observes that criminal responsibility may arise from what a person knowingly joins, supports or facilitates through conscious association with another. Ref: Usman v. The State & another (Cr.A 308-P/2025, decided 04.06.2026).
records.title: Usman v. The State & another (Cr.A 308-P/2025, decided 04.06.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Confession Within FIR Lodged by Accused
records.heading: An accused's admission of killing in his own FIR is inadmissible as a confession to police
records.text: The part of an FIR in which the maker, later an accused, admits causing death and discloses motive is a confession to a police officer and is barred by Arts. 38 and 39 QSO. The remaining portions may still be looked at for permissible purposes. Recovery and conduct in leading police to recovery formed a chain of circumstances. Ref: Jehanzeb v. The State etc (Cr. A 424-P/2025, decided 11.06.2026).
records.title: Jehanzeb v. The State etc (Cr. A 424-P/2025, decided 11.06.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Art. 150 QSO
records.heading: A witness cannot be declared hostile merely for a concession gained in cross-examination
records.text: A concession gained through legitimate cross-examination does not alone justify declaring a witness hostile under Art. 150 QSO. The court's discretion must rest on objective factors such as material departure from a previous statement, deliberate or evasive conduct, genuine surprise and absence of innocent explanation. The doctrine concerns the reliability of testimony. Ref: Jalal Ahmad v. Bilal etc (Cr. Rev 120-P/2026, decided 15.06.2026).
records.title: Jalal Ahmad v. Bilal etc (Cr. Rev 120-P/2026, decided 15.06.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death in Matrimonial Home: Art. 122 QSO
records.heading: A husband must explain a wife's death in the matrimonial home under Article 122 QSO
records.text: In circumstantial evidence the chain must be unbroken and exclude every hypothesis of innocence. Where a wife died inside the matrimonial home, the husband, best placed to explain, had to offer a plausible explanation under Art. 122 QSO. Motive is only corroborative, and failure to prove it is not fatal. Conviction maintained and appeal dismissed. Ref: Habib Ullah v. The State (Cr.A 1216-P/2025, decided 24.06.2026).
records.title: Habib Ullah v. The State (Cr.A 1216-P/2025, decided 24.06.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Compensation Under S. 250 CrPC After S. 203 Dismissal
records.heading: Compensation under section 250 CrPC is unjustified after dismissal of a complaint under section 203
records.text: Where a Magistrate dismissed a complaint under s. 203 CrPC without summoning the accused, an order for compensation to the accused under s. 250 CrPC was not justified, as there was neither discharge nor acquittal. The order was set aside and the quashment petition allowed. Ref: Muhammad Usman Ali Khan v. The State etc (Cr. Misc Q.P 38-D/2025, decided 29.06.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Usman Ali Khan v. The State etc (Cr. Misc Q.P 38-D/2025, decided 29.06.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Production of Police Inquiry Reports: Ss. 94 and 540 CrPC
records.heading: Sections 94 and 540 CrPC let the trial court require production of police inquiry reports
records.text: The word whenever in s. 94 CrPC lets the trial court require production of any document at any stage, and the court may use ss. 94 or 540 CrPC to obtain material documents. Summoning internal police inquiry reports is not filling lacunae. No jurisdictional error was found. Ref: Khatam Jan v. Sher Jan and others (Cr.R 23-D/2026, decided 28.09.2026).
records.title: Khatam Jan v. Sher Jan and others (Cr.R 23-D/2026, decided 28.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Medical Negligence: Surgical Safety Directions
records.heading: The Health Department was directed to issue binding surgical safety instructions to prevent medical negligence
records.text: To prevent recurrence of negligence, the Secretary, Health Department was directed to issue binding instructions within thirty days requiring the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist and signed counts of swabs, instruments and similar items, 24-hour reporting and investigation of never events such as retained surgical items, and trained staff in operation theatres. Ref: Bibi Hanifa v. Dr. Jamila Raza & others (Civil Petition 788/2018 and Civil Appeal 244/2018, decided 20.10.2026); Justice Irfan Saadat Khan.
records.title: Bibi Hanifa v. Dr. Jamila Raza & others (Civil Petition 788/2018 and Civil Appeal 244/2018, decided 20.10.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Open Eyes at Post-Mortem and Eyewitness Reliability
records.heading: Open eyes at post-mortem do not alone show an occurrence was unwitnessed
records.text: The state of the eyelids at post-mortem cannot alone establish that an occurrence was unwitnessed, as open eyes are common after hours through physiological processes. Consistent eyewitness accounts supported by medical evidence prevail over presumptive inferences. The conviction under s. 302(b) PPC, with death converted to life by the High Court, was upheld. Ref: Azmat Ullah @ Motu and Muhammad Luqman @ Gona v. The State (J.P. 372/2022, decided 01.10.2026); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Azmat Ullah @ Motu and Muhammad Luqman @ Gona v. The State (J.P. 372/2022, decided 01.10.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Punjab Sentencing Act 2019 and S. 302(c) PPC
records.heading: The Punjab Sentencing Act 2019 does not apply to capital punishment
records.text: The Punjab Sentencing Act 2019 applies only where penalties involve imprisonment and not capital punishment. The conviction was altered from s. 302(b) to s. 302(c) PPC for a sudden confrontation, and the sentence was reduced to the period already served, over 12 years and 11 months, with Rs.500,000 compensation affirmed. Ref: 2026 LHC 7601; Mehar Farhan v. The State (Jail Appeal 41471/24, decided 15.10.2026).
records.title: Mehar Farhan v. The State (Jail Appeal 41471/24, decided 15.10.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Punjab Healthcare Commission: Inspection and Sealing Powers
records.heading: Power to seal a healthcare establishment needs lawful authority and prescribed procedure
records.text: The Punjab Healthcare Commission Act, 2010 and Anti-Quackery Regulations, 2015 serve distinct objectives. Section 22 is not limited to licensing inspections, and quackery and non-compliance are legally distinct. Anti-quackery enforcement cannot be used to circumvent safeguards on inspection, and the power to seal an establishment needs lawful authority and prescribed procedure. Ref: 2026 LHC 7512; Muhammad Umar Hassan v. DC Lahore etc (WP 49137/26, decided 20.10.2026); Justice Munawar Iqbal Duggal.
records.title: Muhammad Umar Hassan v. DC Lahore etc (WP 49137/26, decided 20.10.2026)

records.subject: Property, Gift & Inheritance
records.topic: Stamp Duty on Partition of Inherited Property
records.heading: Partition of inherited property among co-heirs attracts fixed stamp duty of Rs.500
records.text: Where partition among co-heirs relates only to inherited property, a fixed stamp duty of Rs.500 applies under Art. 45 of Schedule I, Stamp Act, 1899, per the 2012 exception, and not 2 percent of the share value. The orders requiring 2 percent duty were set aside and the petition allowed. Ref: 2026 LHC 7535; Muhammad Sajjad v. The ADJ etc (WP 3302-25, decided 24.09.2026); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Muhammad Sajjad v. The ADJ etc (WP 3302-25, decided 24.09.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Leave to Defend: Unrebutted Guarantee Cheque Defence
records.heading: An unrebutted guarantee cheque defence entitles the defendant to leave to defend
records.text: Where the respondent filed no counter affidavit to the defence that the cheque was a guarantee cheque for a property transfer, the defence stood unrebutted and was not illusory. The parties had to prove their stances in evidence, so leave to defend should have been granted rather than summarily refused. Ref: 2026 LHC 7562; Abdul Sattar v. Muhamamd Javed (Civil Revision 55386/25, decided 20.10.2026); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: Abdul Sattar v. Muhamamd Javed (Civil Revision 55386/25, decided 20.10.2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Thumb Impression on Agreement; O. VII R. 11 CPC
records.heading: A thumb impression is equivalent to a signature, so a plaint cannot be rejected for its absence
records.text: A thumb impression is legally equivalent to a signature under s. 3(52) of the General Clauses Act. Rejection of a plaint for specific performance under O. VII R. 11 CPC on the ground of absence of signature was unlawful, and the case was remanded for fresh decision. Ref: 2026 LHC 7529; Gull Muhammad v. Shabir Ahmed (Civil Revision 603-16, decided 05.10.2026); Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh.
records.title: Gull Muhammad v. Shabir Ahmed (Civil Revision 603-16, decided 05.10.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Service Tribunal Cannot Strike Down Recruitment Rules
records.heading: A Service Tribunal cannot strike down recruitment rules or direct their re-framing
records.text: The Supreme Court restored the Controller General Accounts Recruitment Rules 2014 and set aside the Federal Service Tribunal decision of 17 October 2022. The Tribunal could not strike down recruitment rules or direct their re-framing, promotion is not a vested right, and the Government may amend service structure and recruitment rules. Ref: The Controller General Accounts, Islamabad and another v. Tariq Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 8/2023, decided 21.10.2026); Justice Ayesha A. Malik.
records.title: The Controller General Accounts, Islamabad and another v. Tariq Khan and others (C.P.L.A. 8/2023, decided 21.10.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: High Court Directions Against Police Officer Unsupported by Inquiry
records.heading: High Court directions against a police officer must have a material link to inquiry findings
records.text: The High Court's directions relieving a Special Branch officer, imposing restrictions and initiating disciplinary action were not supported by the court-ordered inquiry, which found his role limited to intelligence reports. Directions lacking a material link to inquiry findings violated due process, and judicial review does not extend to encroaching on executive functions. Ref: Munir Samo (F.C.P.L.A. 2010/2026).
records.title: Munir Samo (F.C.P.L.A. 2010/2026)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Registered Sale Deed: Fraud, Pardanashin Lady, Limitation
records.heading: A suit challenging a registered sale deed after 21 years without proof of fraud is barred
records.text: A registered deed is presumptively valid and its due execution must be proved, but the plaintiff failed to plead or prove fraud or lack of knowledge. The pardanashin doctrine was not made out on the pleadings. The suit filed after 21 years was barred by limitation, as she knew of the transfer decades earlier. Ref: Shaman (decd) through his L.Rs. etc v. Syed Kamran Haider Gillani, etc (C.A. 231-L/2015, decided 20.10.2026); Justice Shahid Waheed.
records.title: Shaman (decd) through his L.Rs. etc v. Syed Kamran Haider Gillani, etc (C.A. 231-L/2015, decided 20.10.2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Execution of Compromise Decree in Family Matters
records.heading: Courts must enforce a compromise decree according to its terms
records.text: Courts must enforce decrees according to their terms, though they may interpret them. Continued residence does not imply performance or discharge of the obligations under the compromise decree. The Family Court's refusal to enforce accommodation, expense and ornament obligations was remanded for a detailed lawful determination after hearing both parties. Ref: 2026 LHC 7662; Mst. Shakeela Bibi v. Additional District Judge, Kabirwala & others (W.P. 14003/2024).
records.title: Mst. Shakeela Bibi v. Additional District Judge, Kabirwala & others (W.P. 14003/2024)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Maintenance Is Continuous and Changeable
records.heading: A fixed decree or compromise does not freeze a minor's future maintenance needs
records.text: Maintenance of minors is a continuing obligation and a fixed decree or compromise does not freeze future needs. The appellate court rightly enhanced maintenance from Rs.4,000 to Rs.10,000 per child per month on evidence of rising costs and the father's capacity. Challenge to maintenance and dowry awards dismissed. Ref: 2026 LHC 7655; Kashif Shahzad v. Addl. District Judge, etc. (W.P. No.3546 of 2026).
records.title: Kashif Shahzad v. Addl. District Judge, etc. (W.P. No.3546 of 2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Nikahnama Stipulation to Pay Rs.5,00,000 on Divorce
records.heading: A Nikahnama stipulation to pay a sum on divorce is contrary to Islamic law
records.text: A husband's stipulation in the Nikahnama (Column No.19) to pay a sum upon divorce is contrary to Islamic law because it unduly restricts the right to divorce. The appellate order allowing recovery of Rs.5,00,000 was overturned and the family court's decree on that amount restored. Ref: 2026 LHC 7655; Kashif Shahzad v. Addl. District Judge, etc. (W.P. No.3546 of 2026).
records.title: Kashif Shahzad v. Addl. District Judge, etc. (W.P. No.3546 of 2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Single Accused and Defence Version: Reasonable Doubt
records.heading: Nomination of a single accused does not itself fasten liability, and the defence need only raise doubt
records.text: That only one accused is nominated is not by itself a determining factor for fastening liability, which must rest on trustworthy and confidence-inspiring evidence. The defence need not prove its version beyond reasonable doubt, but it must find reasonable support in the record to raise doubt about the identity of the assailant. Ref: Behlol Ehsan v. Mehammad Shahwaid (Cr.A No. 781-P of 2019).
records.title: Behlol Ehsan v. Mehammad Shahwaid (Cr.A No. 781-P of 2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Doubtful Eyewitnesses and Benefit of Doubt
records.heading: Contradictory eyewitness accounts entitle the accused to the benefit of doubt
records.text: Medical evidence established the deaths, but participation of the accused was not proved beyond reasonable doubt. The complainant was not an eyewitness, and the eyewitnesses gave contradictory accounts of their arrival and reporting and made no effort to intervene or shift the injured. Relying on 2025 SCMR 45, a single circumstance creating reasonable doubt entitles the accused to acquittal. Ref: Mashal v. The State (Cr.A No. 225-A of 2025).
records.title: Mashal v. The State (Cr.A No. 225-A of 2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Acquittal Does Not Prove Police Planted Narcotics
records.heading: Acquittal on benefit of doubt does not amount to a finding that police planted narcotics
records.text: Benefit of doubt given on contradictions, chain of custody defects and investigative shortcomings does not, without independent and affirmative material, amount to a finding that police officials deliberately planted narcotics or fabricated evidence. Inability to prove a case beyond reasonable doubt is distinct from a positive finding of mala fide fabrication. Ref: Sanaullah and others v. The State (Cr. Misc (Q) No. 04-A of 2026).
records.title: Sanaullah and others v. The State (Cr. Misc (Q) No. 04-A of 2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Proof of Occurrence versus Individual Responsibility
records.heading: Proof of an occurrence does not prove which accused caused a particular injury
records.text: Proof that a violent occurrence took place and that witnesses were injured does not prove that a particular accused caused a specific injury; the court must keep the two inquiries separate. Where the genesis was a dispute over a thoroughfare and premeditation was not proved, conviction was altered between s. 302(b) and s. 302(c) PPC. Death sentence not confirmed. Ref: Nauman v. The State & another (Cr.A No. 76-P of 2026 with Murder Ref No. 01-P of 2026 & Cr.A No. 87-P of 2026).
records.title: Nauman v. The State & another (Cr.A No. 76-P of 2026 with Murder Ref No. 01-P of 2026 & Cr.A No. 87-P of 2026)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Return of Dower Paid by Husband Only
records.heading: On khula the husband may reclaim only the dower he himself paid
records.text: On khula the husband may reclaim only dower that he himself paid. Where the money for 11 tolas of gold dower was provided by the wife's father and the husband could not prove his own payment, he was not entitled to the gold or its value. The wife's petition was partly allowed and the order for return of the gold set aside. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 753; Dr. Rukhsana Kausar and another v. Shahid Nazeer and others (Writ Petition No.21804 of 2020); Justice Rahil Kamran Sheikh.
records.title: Dr. Rukhsana Kausar and another v. Shahid Nazeer and others (Writ Petition No.21804 of 2020)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Constable Recruitment: Eyesight Standard under Police Rules
records.heading: Rule 12.16 of the Punjab Police Rules requires 6/6 vision for constable recruitment
records.text: Rule 12.16 of the Punjab Police Rules 1934 requires 6/6 vision for recruitment of constables. The Court noted that the rules are 90 years old and need revision, and suggested that candidates unfit for field duty but found suitable for office work by an eye specialist should be accommodated in desk posts. Ref: PLJ 2026 FCC 165; Muhammad Farhan v. The Province of Punjab, through Inspector General of Police, Lahore & another (F.C.P.L.A. No.16 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Farhan v. The Province of Punjab, through Inspector General of Police, Lahore & another (F.C.P.L.A. No.16 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC Unavailable to Contesting Party
records.heading: A party that contested the suit through three fora cannot apply under section 12(2) CPC
records.text: A party that contested the suit through three fora and lost has no right to apply under s. 12(2) CPC, and its own mistake or slackness does not create one. The Court also considered the limits of High Court writ jurisdiction to reappraise evidence and the effect of s. 23 of the Registration Act, noting the presumption of truth attached to registered documents. Ref: PLJ 2026 FCC 183; Mian Tahir Raza v. Mubasher Ahmed and others (Civil Appeal No. 112 of 2023).
records.title: Mian Tahir Raza v. Mubasher Ahmed and others (Civil Appeal No. 112 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Guidelines for Proceedings Affecting Minors
records.heading: Guidelines require courts to comply strictly with Order XXXII CPC in proceedings affecting minors
records.text: Guidelines for civil and revenue courts dealing with minors' person, property or inheritance. The court must identify minors early and comply strictly with O. XXXII CPC, appoint a guardian ad litem under O. XXXII R. 3 CPC only after checking absence of adverse interest, and accept no compromise or admission affecting a minor unless lawful and in the minor's best interests, with O. XXXII R. 7 CPC complied with. Ref: PLJ 2026 FCC 188; Mst. Bushra Bibi v. Additional District Judge, Bahawalnagar and others (C.P.L.A.30-L of 2025).
records.title: Mst. Bushra Bibi v. Additional District Judge, Bahawalnagar and others (C.P.L.A.30-L of 2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Maternal Filicide: s. 302(c) PPC and Qisas Exemption
records.heading: Conviction of a mother for killing her children was altered to section 302(c) PPC
records.text: The court considered Islamic and statutory principles on a mother killing her children, including the exemption of ascendants from qisas and the mitigating effect of mental condition and postpartum psychosis evidence. Her conviction was altered from s. 302(b) to s. 302(c) PPC and she was sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment, sentences to run concurrently. Ref: 2026 LHC 8046; Shagufta Parveen v. State etc (Jail Appeal.60078/24, decided 20.10.2026).
records.title: Shagufta Parveen v. State etc (Jail Appeal.60078/24, decided 20.10.2026)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Mosque as Inclusive Place of Worship
records.heading: A mosque is not the preserve of any particular group
records.text: A mosque is a sacred institution embodying unity and equality among believers and is not the preserve of any particular group. Disputes about management, use or administration of mosques should be resolved with sensitivity to the wider community, avoiding unnecessary judicial intervention that may disturb public peace. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 564; Khawaja Farman Raza v. Province of Punjab (Civil Petition No. 2774 of 2025).
records.title: Khawaja Farman Raza v. Province of Punjab (Civil Petition No. 2774 of 2025)

records.subject: Specific Relief & Contract
records.topic: Specific Performance: Proof of Attested Agreement
records.heading: Specific performance requires proof of the agreement through its attesting witnesses
records.text: A decree for specific performance first requires the contract to be proved in accordance with law. An agreement to sell and powers of attorney fall within Art. 17(2)(a) QSO, so the attesting witnesses must be produced under Arts. 17 and 79 QSO, and failure is fatal where execution is disputed. The court must also weigh conduct, delay and surrounding circumstances before granting equitable relief. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 585; Muhammad Humayun and others; Taj Bibi and another v. Shafqat Ali Nisar and others (CPLA No. 1035 & 1104/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Humayun and others; Taj Bibi and another v. Shafqat Ali Nisar and others (CPLA No. 1035 & 1104/2022)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Custodial Death FIR: Transfer to FIA under 2022 Act
records.heading: FIRs for custodial death offences must be transferred to the FIA before cognisance is taken
records.text: FIRs registered by local police under general laws for offences falling within the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act 2022 must be cancelled and the matter transferred to the FIA, provided the court has not taken cognisance. Once cognisance is taken by a competent court, an earlier misstep such as an FIR by an unauthorised agency does not vitiate the trial. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC Note 255; Aftab Mehmood v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.81211/24); Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh.
records.title: Aftab Mehmood v. The State etc. (Crl. Misc.81211/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC: Re-examination of Witness
records.heading: Re-examination of a witness is limited to matters arising in cross-examination
records.text: Authority on whether a prosecution witness whose examination-in-chief and cross-examination are complete may be recalled for re-examination by application under s. 540 CrPC. The Court discussed the scope of re-examination under Arts. 132 and 133 QSO, a right of the calling party limited to matters arising in cross-examination unless permission is given. Ref: The State through ANF v. Kamil Shah and another.
records.title: The State through ANF v. Kamil Shah and another

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Murder of Wife after Khula; Death Sentence Upheld
records.heading: Death sentence upheld for the premeditated killing of a wife who had obtained khula
records.text: Death sentence upheld for the premeditated killing of a wife who had obtained a khula decree. Testimony of related witnesses to a crime inside the home cannot be rejected merely for relationship, and the forensic match of recovered empties with the pistol was held conclusive. The Court referred to Arts. 9, 14 and 25 of the Constitution on protection of women. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1921; Wasim Abbas v. The State (J.P. 617/2025).
records.title: Wasim Abbas v. The State (J.P. 617/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry and Bridal Gifts Are Wife's Absolute Property
records.heading: Dowry and bridal gifts vest absolutely in the wife, and the Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction
records.text: Property given to a woman at marriage by parents, relatives, husband or in-laws for her personal use vests absolutely in her, and its retention by the husband or his family is unlawful. Under s. 5 and the Schedule of the Family Courts Act 1964 the Family Court has exclusive jurisdiction over dowry and the wife's personal property. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1838; Ghulam Habib v. Mst. Shazia and others (C.P.L.A.5432/2025).
records.title: Ghulam Habib v. Mst. Shazia and others (C.P.L.A.5432/2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Narcotics Bail: No Public Witnesses or Videography
records.heading: Absence of public witnesses and videography of the raid makes narcotics bail a case of further inquiry
records.text: Absence of independent public witnesses and of videography or photography of the raid compromised the recovery of ICE, relying on Abdul Mateen. The plea that the accused were already in police custody was not conclusively rejected on the record, including a s. 491 CrPC petition, and the matter was held to be one of further inquiry. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 502; Bait Ullah v. The State (Crl. P. 852/2026).
records.title: Bait Ullah v. The State (Crl. P. 852/2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Heinousness Alone No Ground to Refuse Bail
records.heading: The heinousness of the offence alone does not justify refusing bail where further inquiry arises
records.text: Although the quantity recovered attracts stringent penalties, heinousness alone cannot justify withholding bail where the evidence points to further inquiry. Relying on Gul Manan, mere presence where contraband is found does not establish conscious knowledge or constructive possession, which must be determined at trial. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 502; Bait Ullah v. The State (Crl. P. 852/2026).
records.title: Bait Ullah v. The State (Crl. P. 852/2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: Monal Case: Review of Supreme Court Judgment
records.heading: Rights of affected parties cannot be decided without effective hearing, and an inquiry report is not final proof
records.text: The Court allowed the review petitions of the CDA and Metropolitan Corporation and set aside the Supreme Court judgment of 21 August 2024 to the stated extent. It held that rights of affected parties could not be decided without effective hearing, an inquiry commission report is not final proof of disputed facts, and use of a national park depends on whether an activity harms its purpose. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 435; Metropolitan Corporation through its Chief Officer and Capital Development Authority through its Chairman v. Monal Group of Companies through its Sole Proprietor and others (C.R.P. No. 825/2024 & F.C.R.P. No. 44/2025 in C.P.L.A. No. 304/2022).
records.title: Metropolitan Corporation through its Chief Officer and Capital Development Authority through its Chairman v. Monal Group of Companies through its Sole Proprietor and others (C.R.P. No. 825/2024 & F.C.R.P. No. 44/2025 in C.P.L.A. No. 304/2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Dismissed Employees Treated as Regular: Tests Not Held
records.heading: Restored employees are treated as regular where the departments failed to hold the tests
records.text: The Court ordered implementation of the Supreme Court judgment of 17 December 2021 and directed that restored employees be treated as regular because the departments and the Federal Public Service Commission failed to hold the tests. Employees cannot bear the consequence of that failure. The contempt petitions were disposed of. Ref: (C.P.L.A. No 2118-L of 2016).
records.title: (C.P.L.A. No 2118-L of 2016)

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Nine Months' Service: Permanent Workmen by Operation of Law
records.heading: Daily wage employees with over nine months' continuous work become permanent workmen by operation of law
records.text: The Punjab policy of 29.01.2021 applies to daily wage and contingent paid employees of District Health Authorities. Those meeting its criteria, including over nine months' continuous work on permanent nature duties, attain permanent workman status by operation of law without any formal order. Artificial 89-day breaks cannot defeat this, and refusal orders were set aside. Ref: 2026 LHC 8384; Muhammad Bilal Raza & 11 others v. Govt. of the Punjab etc. (WP. 6349/26, decided 29.10.2026); Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: Muhammad Bilal Raza & 11 others v. Govt. of the Punjab etc. (WP. 6349/26, decided 29.10.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Superdari of Vehicle in Adulterated Milk Case
records.heading: Custody of a truck seized in an adulterated milk case may be granted pending trial
records.text: On superdari of a truck seized in an adulterated milk case, the vehicle's modifications did not appear to violate standards or make it inherently an instrument of unlawful use. The petition was converted into an appeal and the High Court order allowing custody only after separating the tanker was set aside; the owner retains custody pending trial without making material alterations. Ref: Salman Rafique (FCPLA No. 70-L of 2026).
records.title: Salman Rafique (FCPLA No. 70-L of 2026)

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Finality of Consolidation Proceedings in Writ Jurisdiction
records.heading: Final consolidation decisions limit judicial review in constitutional jurisdiction
records.text: Final consolidation and revenue decisions limit judicial review in constitutional jurisdiction, and courts cannot revisit factual details or vary final allocations. The execution court only implements the decree and cannot alter land classification determined earlier. The petition was dismissed and leave to appeal refused. Ref: Mst. Anwari (C.P.L.A. No.2118-L of 2016).
records.title: Mst. Anwari (C.P.L.A. No.2118-L of 2016)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Challenge to 1980 Consent Decree for Fraud
records.heading: A challenge to a 1980 consent decree for fraud over thirty years later failed
records.text: The dispute concerned a 1980 consent decree allocating a Mirpurkhas building in a private partition, which the Education Department claimed was government property obtained by fraud. The 1925 and 1932 resolutions did not explicitly prove government ownership, and the challenge was held to be over 30 years late. The trial court's dismissal was restored and the petition allowed. Ref: (C.P.L.A. No.1130-K of 2024).
records.title: (C.P.L.A. No.1130-K of 2024)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas Recovery: Case Property Doubts and Acquittal
records.heading: Doubts over case property and non-production of the vehicle entitle the accused to acquittal
records.text: Material discrepancies about the identification and repacking of the case property, and non-production of the vehicle from which 48 kg of charas was allegedly recovered, undermined the prosecution case. Benefit of doubt was extended, the judgments below set aside and the petitioner acquitted. Ref: Taimoor Khan v. The State through Advocate General Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Crl.P.L.A.172-P/2026, decided 21.10.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Taimoor Khan v. The State through Advocate General Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Crl.P.L.A.172-P/2026, decided 21.10.2026)

records.subject: Anti-Terrorism Act
records.topic: ATC Convictions for Armed Attacks and Murder: Appeal
records.heading: Direct evidence is essential in murder cases, and participation in violence differs from killing
records.text: Appeal from the Sindh High Court against partial conviction of the accused by the Anti-Terrorism Court over armed encounters and abductions. The Court stressed the importance of direct evidence in murder cases and presumption of innocence where doubt remains, distinguishing participation in violent acts from actual killing for severe penalties. Ref: Imtiaz Shaikh v. The State (J.P.279/2020, decided 29.10.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Imtiaz Shaikh v. The State (J.P.279/2020, decided 29.10.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Medical Negligence: Criminal Liability of Doctors
records.heading: Criminal liability of doctors requires gross negligence or reckless disregard
records.text: Criminal liability of doctors requires gross negligence or reckless disregard, not an ordinary clinical error or lapse of judgment, which ordinarily gives rise to civil liability only. Applying the Bolam test and s. 318 PPC, the acquittal of the doctors was upheld and the petition dismissed. Ref: Amjad Ali v. Dr. Taqdees Naqaish and others (Crl.P.L.A.955/2020, decided 06.10.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Amjad Ali v. Dr. Taqdees Naqaish and others (Crl.P.L.A.955/2020, decided 06.10.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Sending Married Girl to Shelter: S. 552 CrPC
records.heading: Sending a married girl to a shelter without legal authority under section 552 CrPC was set aside
records.text: The Sessions Judge's order sending a girl to a shelter by applying the Punjab Child Marriage Restraint Act 2026, which came into force after the marriage, lacked legal authority including under s. 552 CrPC and ignored her statement of voluntary marriage. The detention was set aside and she was ordered released to reside where she wished. Ref: Sher Baz & another v. Ahmad Sher etc (Crl. Revision.37600/26, decided 01.10.2026); Justice Khalid Ibn-i-Aziz.
records.title: Sher Baz & another v. Ahmad Sher etc (Crl. Revision.37600/26, decided 01.10.2026)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Witness Cannot Be Given Up after Examination-in-Chief Begins
records.heading: A witness cannot be given up once examination-in-chief has commenced
records.text: A witness may be given up before entering the box or after oath, but once examination-in-chief commences, even by a single word, the calling party cannot give the witness up and the opposing party's right of cross-examination arises. Any request to abandon a witness must be scrutinised on merits to protect the accused's right to a fair trial. Ref: Qaiser Mehmood v. The State (J.P.228/2022, decided 29.10.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Qaiser Mehmood v. The State (J.P.228/2022, decided 29.10.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Forum of Trial: Magistrate Invested under S. 30 CrPC
records.heading: Forum of trial depends on sections 28 to 30 CrPC and Schedule II, not on offence classification
records.text: Forum of trial is governed by ss. 28 to 30 CrPC and the eighth column of Schedule II, not by whether an offence is cognizable, bailable or compoundable. A s. 30 Magistrate may try any offence not punishable with death, while death offences and those reserved by special law go to the Court of Session under s. 190(2), and a trial by the Magistrate is void under s. 530(p). Competence to try is distinct from sentencing power under s. 32. Ref: 2026 LHC 8457; Ahmad Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl.Misc.No.49393-M of 2026).
records.title: Ahmad Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl.Misc.No.49393-M of 2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Charas Conviction: Improbable Story and Chain of Custody
records.heading: An improbable recovery story and broken chain of custody entitle the accused to acquittal
records.text: The prosecution story of a 12 kg charas recovery was inherently improbable, there was no documentary evidence of the surveillance and arrest, and chain of custody of the narcotics and samples was not established. Reasonable doubt arose, the conviction and life sentence were set aside and the petitioner acquitted. Ref: Gul Muhammad v. The State through Special Prosecutor, A.N.F. (Crl.P.L.A.1691/2022, decided 27.10.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Gul Muhammad v. The State through Special Prosecutor, A.N.F. (Crl.P.L.A.1691/2022, decided 27.10.2026)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: No Conversion of Rape Charge into Fornication
records.heading: A rape charge cannot be converted into fornication on a different factual footing
records.text: A prosecution for rape must be tried within the statutory framework for that offence, and conviction cannot be maintained by substituting fornication on a different factual footing, as reflected in s. 5A of the Zina Ordinance 1979. A decree of jactitation of marriage does not bar the criminal court from independently assessing consent under s. 375 PPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 774; Ghulam Fareed v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-200-21).
records.title: Ghulam Fareed v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-200-21)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Evidence Is Corroborative, Not Substantive
records.heading: DNA evidence is corroborative and cannot alone found a conviction
records.text: DNA evidence is corroborative and not substantive, so a conviction cannot be founded merely on such corroborative material. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 774; Ghulam Fareed v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-200-21).
records.title: Ghulam Fareed v. State etc (Crl. Appeal-200-21)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Bail on Statutory Delay: Third Proviso to S. 497(1) CrPC
records.heading: Bail on statutory delay is a matter of right where the accused did not delay the trial
records.text: Where the order sheets show no design, pattern or concerted effort by the accused to delay the trial, the conditions of the third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC are met and, with no exception applicable, post-arrest bail is a matter of right on the ground of statutory delay. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 788; Ghulam Rasool v. The State and another (Criminal Misc. No. 3529-B of 2026); Muhammad Jahangir v. The State and another (Criminal Misc. No. 3737-B of 2026).
records.title: Ghulam Rasool v. The State and another (Criminal Misc. No. 3529-B of 2026); Muhammad Jahangir v. The State and another (Criminal Misc. No. 3737-B of 2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Unedited Video as Basis of Conviction
records.heading: An unedited video can support conviction to the extent it establishes the incident
records.text: Failure of the ocular account does not entitle the accused to acquittal where an unedited video film establishes part of the incident, and conviction can follow to that extent. A photogrammetric test is needed only where identity is disputed and is redundant where the defence admits the accused's presence in the video. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 797; Muhammad Azam etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal.67344/22).
records.title: Muhammad Azam etc v. The State etc (Crl. Appeal.67344/22)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Belated Supplementary Statement Implicating New Accused
records.heading: A belated supplementary statement implicating a new accused on vague suspicion lacks evidentiary value
records.text: A belated supplementary statement implicating a previously unknown accused on undisclosed sources, vague suspicion or unverified informers lacks evidentiary value. Arrest relying solely on it is oppressive, makes the case highly doubtful and entitles the accused to bail under s. 497 CrPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 840; Umer Farooq alias Ahtisham v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.39870/26).
records.title: Umer Farooq alias Ahtisham v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.39870/26)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Police Confession Inadmissible: Arts. 38 and 39 QSO
records.heading: A confession made to the police is inadmissible as substantive evidence
records.text: A confession made before the police during investigation has no evidentiary value and is inadmissible as substantive evidence under Arts. 38 and 39 QSO. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 840; Umer Farooq alias Ahtisham v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.39870/26).
records.title: Umer Farooq alias Ahtisham v. The State etc (Crl. Misc.39870/26)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Death Sentence Not Commuted: Motive and Related Witnesses
records.heading: Absence of motive is not an automatic ground for commuting a death sentence
records.text: Absence of motive is not an automatic ground for commuting a death sentence. Here the accused was identified by natural witnesses including his injured son, the killing occurred in the family home with repeated firing on family members including a minor, and forensic evidence linked the recovered pistol to the crime empties. Relationship of witnesses explains their presence. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 326; Khuda Bakhsh v. The State (Sessions J.P.178/2025).
records.title: Khuda Bakhsh v. The State (Sessions J.P.178/2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Life Imprisonment as 25 Years: Expectancy of Life Principle
records.heading: Life imprisonment is deemed twenty-five years, so expectancy of life cannot be invoked
records.text: Under s. 57 PPC and Rule 140 of the Prison Rules 1978, life imprisonment is deemed 25 years, so the principle of expectancy of life cannot be invoked on the basis of shorter incarceration or by counting remissions. Death row convicts are not lifers under Rule 198(b) and are not presently entitled to remissions. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 362; Sher Afzal and another v. The State through PG Punjab and another (Crl.M.A.1292/2025).
records.title: Sher Afzal and another v. The State through PG Punjab and another (Crl.M.A.1292/2025)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: 3 MPO Detentions: Peshawar High Court Restrained
records.heading: The Peshawar High Court was restrained from hearing cases on arrests under 3 MPO
records.text: The Federal Constitutional Court restrained the Peshawar High Court from hearing cases on arrests under 3 MPO and suspended the challenged High Court orders, on the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government's petitions. Notices were issued to the parties and further hearing was adjourned indefinitely. Ref: The Additional Chief Secretary, Home & Affairs Department, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar & others v. Waheed and others (F.C.P.L.A.2392 to 2458 & 2307 to 2354 of 2026, decided 05.11.2026); Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan; Justice Aamer Farooq.
records.title: The Additional Chief Secretary, Home & Affairs Department, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar & others v. Waheed and others (F.C.P.L.A.2392 to 2458 & 2307 to 2354 of 2026, decided 05.11.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Challenge to Old Mutation
records.heading: A plaint challenging an old mutation cannot be rejected merely on the age of the mutation
records.text: A plaint challenging a 1931 mutation affecting inheritance cannot be rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC merely on the age of the mutation, as rejection is allowed only where the claim is clearly untenable without factual inquiry. Inheritance rights under Muslim law do not lapse with time and revenue entries do not decide ownership. Petition dismissed and trial directed within six months. Ref: Kifayat Ullah and others v. Kiramat Ullah and others (C.P.L.A.422/2025, decided 27.10.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Kifayat Ullah and others v. Kiramat Ullah and others (C.P.L.A.422/2025, decided 27.10.2026)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 409 PPC: Proof of Entrustment
records.heading: Criminal breach of trust under section 409 PPC requires positive evidence of entrustment
records.text: Criminal breach of trust requires positive evidence of entrustment in a fiduciary capacity, including who entrusted the property, to whom, when and for what purpose; possession or position alone is insufficient. The witnesses were inconsistent and largely hearsay, so the conviction was set aside and the appellant acquitted. Ref: 2026 LHC 8563; Mansoob Ahmad Shah v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal.210897/18, decided 14.10.2026); Justice Khalid Ibn-i-Aziz.
records.title: Mansoob Ahmad Shah v. The State etc. (Crl. Appeal.210897/18, decided 14.10.2026)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 476 CrPC: Forgery Allegations in Civil Suit
records.heading: Criminal proceedings under section 476 CrPC are not justified by mere production of disputed documents
records.text: The power to initiate criminal proceedings under s. 476 CrPC is discretionary and exercised to serve justice, not private vengeance. Mere production of disputed documents in a civil suit, without clear proof of forgery or perjury affecting the administration of justice, does not justify criminal action. Revision dismissed. Ref: 2026 LHC 8556; Firdous Akhtar v. Azmat Bashir Khokhar etc. (Crl. Revision 65936/21, decided 12.10.2026); Justice Khalid Ibn-i-Aziz.
records.title: Firdous Akhtar v. Azmat Bashir Khokhar etc. (Crl. Revision 65936/21, decided 12.10.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Family Pension of Daughters: Executive Notification Struck Down
records.heading: An executive notification cannot extinguish a daughter's entitlement to family pension under the Act
records.text: Subordinate legislation may supplement but cannot supplant the parent statute or extinguish a daughter's entitlement to family pension through an executive notification. The 2024 Punjab notification restricting family pension, as it affected divorced, widowed and unmarried daughters, was inconsistent with s. 18(2) of the Act and set aside. Ref: 2026 LHC 8584; Zahida Yasmeen v. Government of Punjab etc (WP-26-26, decided 28.10.2026); Justice Syed Ahsan Raza Kazmi.
records.title: Zahida Yasmeen v. Government of Punjab etc (WP-26-26, decided 28.10.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Appointments under Repealed Ordinance Do Not Survive
records.heading: Appointments under a repealed ordinance do not survive unless expressly saved
records.text: Appointments made under the Islamabad Capital Territory Private Educational Institutions Ordinance 2009 did not survive its lapse and replacement by the 2013 Act unless expressly saved. Acts under temporary laws are not protected once the law ceases unless validated by Parliament. Petitions were converted into appeals and dismissed. Ref: (C.P.L.As No.2130 and 2136 of 2023).
records.title: (C.P.L.As No.2130 and 2136 of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Revision against Magistrate's Administrative Order
records.heading: A Magistrate's order for medical re-examination is executive and not revisable
records.text: A Magistrate ordering medical re-examination acts as persona designata in an executive capacity, so the order is not revisable under ss. 435, 439 or 439-A CrPC. The Sessions Judge's revisional order of 15.06.2026 was beyond jurisdiction and was set aside; petition allowed. Ref: 2026 LHC 8471; Muhammad Nawaz v. State etc (Crl. Misc.-6707-M-26, decided 02.11.2026); Justice Farooq Haider.
records.title: Muhammad Nawaz v. State etc (Crl. Misc.-6707-M-26, decided 02.11.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Third Suit: Res Judicata and O. II R. 2 CPC
records.heading: Res judicata and Order II Rule 2 objections to a third suit must be examined on merits
records.text: The Court considered whether a third suit over leasehold rights, rejected under O. VII R. 11 CPC, was barred by earlier proceedings, res judicata or O. II R. 2 CPC. It restored the appellate court's decision, and the trial court must re-evaluate the suit on merits considering the objections of res judicata and maintainability. Ref: Syed Aley Sadquain Naqvi v. Matco Rice (Pvt) Ltd. & others (C.A.353-K/2025, decided 22.10.2026); Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan.
records.title: Syed Aley Sadquain Naqvi v. Matco Rice (Pvt) Ltd. & others (C.A.353-K/2025, decided 22.10.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VII R. 11 CPC: Partial Rejection of Plaint
records.heading: Partial rejection of a plaint against selected defendants is impermissible where causes of action are interconnected
records.text: Under O. VII R. 11 CPC, partial rejection of a plaint against selected defendants is impermissible where causes of action are interconnected, and the plaint must be read as a whole. Selective rejection in a suit for specific performance and cancellation of a subsequent sale deed prematurely adjudicated substantive rights and was corrected. Ref: Rana Muhammad Sher Shujah v. Akber Khan and others (C.P.L.A.3829/2025).
records.title: Rana Muhammad Sher Shujah v. Akber Khan and others (C.P.L.A.3829/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution of Decree against Surety
records.heading: A decree can be executed against a surety whose liability is co-extensive with the debtor's
records.text: A decree can be executed against a surety, whose liability under s. 128 of the Contract Act 1872 is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, and s. 145 CPC makes sureties liable for performance of decrees. The father who furnished surety bonds was liable and the constitutional petition against attachment of his property was dismissed. Ref: 2026 LHC 8604; Gohar Rehman v. Mst. Sadia Bibi (WP.3068-22, decided 20.10.2026); Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf.
records.title: Gohar Rehman v. Mst. Sadia Bibi (WP.3068-22, decided 20.10.2026)

records.subject: Banking & Corporate
records.topic: Security Cheque: Presumption under S. 118 NIA Rebutted
records.heading: A security cheque rebuts the section 118 presumption, so liability must be proved
records.text: A cheque endorsed as a security cheque makes enforcement conditional, and the presumption under s. 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act is rebutted so that liability must be proved. The ledger was inadmissible secondary evidence and no purchase orders or transaction proof were shown. Appeals dismissed. Ref: 2026 LHC 8612; MS Nizami Feeds Pvt. Ltd. through Muhammad Tahir Javed v. Muhammad Ahtisham (R.F.A.51711/25, decided 06.11.2026); Justice Asim Hafeez.
records.title: MS Nizami Feeds Pvt. Ltd. through Muhammad Tahir Javed v. Muhammad Ahtisham (R.F.A.51711/25, decided 06.11.2026)

records.subject: Character Certificate
records.topic: Police Character Certificate after Acquittal
records.heading: An acquittal must not be reflected adversely in the Police Character Certificate
records.text: Upon acquittal the criminal case must not be reflected adversely in the Police Character Certificate, and where proceedings are pending only their pendency is disclosed without presumption of guilt. The Court also laid down principles for antecedent verification in public recruitment, including that mere registration of an FIR is not an automatic disqualification. Ref: Abdul Latif v. Inspector General of Police and others (C.P.L.A.2930 of 2025).
records.title: Abdul Latif v. Inspector General of Police and others (C.P.L.A.2930 of 2025)

records.subject: Labour Law
records.topic: Sexual Harassment: Instructor in Position of Trust
records.heading: An instructor in a position of trust owes stricter duties under the Harassment Act
records.text: An instructor with clinical and academic supervision stands in a position of trust akin to a fiduciary, owing duties stricter than in ordinary workplaces. These include avoiding conflicts, not exploiting authority for sexualised behaviour, maintaining a safe learning environment, confidentiality and honesty in inquiries under the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act. Leave was declined and the petition dismissed. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 530.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Witnesses Not Listed May Be Produced Voluntarily
records.heading: A party may voluntarily produce witnesses who are not named in the list of witnesses
records.text: Only witnesses sought to be summoned through the court must be named in the list of witnesses; a party may produce other witnesses voluntarily. The courts below wrongly invoked O. XVI R. 1(2) CPC to bar the plaintiffs' witnesses present in court, which was an illegality. Ref: 2026 YLR 2511.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Insanity Defence under S. 84 PPC
records.heading: The insanity defence under section 84 PPC depends on mental capacity at the time of the act
records.text: Islamic principles on criminal responsibility are consistent with the insanity defence in s. 84 PPC, as both depend on the accused's mental capacity at the time of the act.
