The court must decide the applicability of s. 84 strictly on law and evidence, imposing accountability where capacity is established but not where the law recognises its absence. Ref: Umar Draz & another v. The State (Crl.A.96/2020, decided 07.10.2026); Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim.
records.title: Umar Draz & another v. The State (Crl.A.96/2020, decided 07.10.2026)

records.subject: Constitutional Law & Writ Jurisdiction
records.topic: PM&DC Power to Regulate Tuition Fee
records.heading: The PM&DC Act 2022 empowers the Council to regulate tuition fee
records.text: Read together, the Preamble, ss. 6 and 9 and s. 20(7) and (8) of the PM&DC Act 2022 give the Council authority to scrutinise, regulate and determine tuition fee, including permissible limits. The challenge of the institutions based on lack of statutory competence was repelled. The court also held that a heading cannot curtail operative language and that beneficial construction may be preferred. Ref: 2026 LHC 8618; The University of Faisalabad through Imran Nazir & another v. Federation of Pakistan etc (WP. 43022/26, decided 29.10.2026); Justice Khalid Ishaq.
records.title: The University of Faisalabad through Imran Nazir & another v. Federation of Pakistan etc (WP. 43022/26, decided 29.10.2026)

records.subject: Limitation
records.topic: Time-Barred Appeal against S. 12(2) CPC Dismissal
records.heading: An appeal against dismissal of a section 12(2) CPC application was time-barred for lack of diligence
records.text: The appellants' application under s. 12(2) CPC against an ex parte restoration order was dismissed and their appeal was filed late. The Supreme Court found no infirmity in the High Court's view on limitation, as the appellants had not diligently pursued their remedy and delay condonation was refused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1995.

records.subject: Tax & Customs
records.topic: Show-Cause Limitation: Misconstruction of Law versus Fraud
records.heading: Misconstruction of law is not fraud and cannot avoid the six-month show-cause limit
records.text: A show-cause notice issued over two and a half years after the transaction, with no allegation of fraud or deliberate misdeclaration and concerning only interpretation of s. 106 of the Customs Act 1969, falls under the six-month limit in s. 32(3). Revenue authorities cannot treat a misconstruction of law as fraud to avoid limitation. The High Court judgment was set aside. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1915; Pakistan State Oil Company Limited.
records.title: Pakistan State Oil Company Limited

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: Acquittal Appeal Allowed: Death by Vehicle, s. 320 PPC
records.heading: The High Court convicted a driver under section 320 PPC on the State's acquittal appeal
records.text: The High Court allowed the State's appeal against acquittal in the case of a traffic police sub-inspector killed by the accused's vehicle, set aside the trial court judgment and convicted him under s. 320 PPC with ten years' rigorous imprisonment. He was also ordered to pay diyat to the legal heirs. Ref: The State v. Abdul Majeed (Crl Appeal-182 of 2020, decided 10.11.2026); Justice Aamer Rana; Justice Abdul Qayyum Lehri.
records.title: The State v. Abdul Majeed (Crl Appeal-182 of 2020, decided 10.11.2026)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: High Court Writ Jurisdiction Abates when Service Tribunal Functional
records.heading: High Court writ proceedings abate once the Service Tribunal is established and functional
records.text: Under Art. 212(2) of the Constitution read with s. 8 of the Punjab Service Tribunals Act 1974, proceedings pending before any court abate once the Tribunal is established and functional. Entertaining a constitutional petition during the Tribunal's non-functionality is a stop-gap remedy and does not divest the Tribunal of its jurisdiction. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1385, PLJ 2025 Lah 669.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: No Right to Appointment without Qualifying Marks
records.heading: No candidate can claim appointment as of right without meeting the eligibility criteria
records.text: No candidate can claim appointment as of right without meeting the eligibility criteria set by the recruiting authority. A recommendation made without regard to failure in the written examination confers no vested right, and the High Court in Art. 199 jurisdiction does not act as selection authority or substitute its own assessment. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1452.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Promotion Policy Clause-21: Officers on LPR
records.heading: Excluding officers on leave preparatory to retirement from promotion consideration is a rational classification
records.text: Clause-21 of the Promotion Policy 2010 excluding officers on leave preparatory to retirement from promotion consideration was upheld as a rational classification. S. 8 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act 1974 gives only a right to be considered, not an entitlement. Petitions dismissed. Ref: 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1371.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Khula: Wife's Aversion and Pending Suit on Nikahnama
records.heading: A wife's sworn extreme aversion requires khula, and a pending declaratory suit does not bar it
records.text: A wife's sworn statement of extreme aversion, with both parties refusing reconciliation, requires dissolution by khula. Pendency of a declaratory suit challenging the nikahnama does not bar or suspend her right to khula. Ref: 2026 CLC 1809; Muhammad Irfan v. JFC & Others (Writ Petition 14118-25).
records.title: Muhammad Irfan v. JFC & Others (Writ Petition 14118-25)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Loan Agreement: Arts. 17 and 79 QSO and Art. 129
records.heading: A loan agreement proved through witnesses and bank statements satisfies Articles 17 and 79 QSO
records.text: The loan agreement and payment of Rs.20,37,000 were proved through witnesses and bank statements, satisfying Arts. 17 and 79 QSO. An adverse presumption under Art. 129 QSO was drawn against the petitioner for withholding witnesses. Revision dismissed on concurrent findings. Ref: 2026 CLC 1830; Muhammad Anjum Sharif v. Nisar Ahmad.
records.title: Muhammad Anjum Sharif v. Nisar Ahmad
